name: Aka
detailed_description: Gardening The farming system is inspired by permaculture, where associations (garden design) and wild animals play a role. Construction It is possible to craft shelter, tools, clothes, or various props. It can help solve quests or just be for a decorative purpose. You will need to gather materials, find objects or win them while doing quests. Relaxation Relaxing in hot springs with monkeys, watching clouds while listening to the ocean waves, or taking a nap on a giant Capybara... Narrative quests Aka isn't a linear game. Meet various characters of all kinds: villagers willing to help, trapped animals, giant monsters, or ghosts from your past who need your help to be freed. Mini-games

short_description: Find inner peace in a small, open-world game. On these carefully handcrafted islands, you can take a nap on a giant monster, feed baby dragons, take care of the fauna and flora... ...but demons from your past might come back to remind you what you want to forget.

_childDocuments_.review: For the people wondering if this is worth it on sale, here is my answer: I don't think so, no. You should not pay money for this game, in any case. I will explain why. This is an unfinished, abandoned product. There are bugs keeping you from progressing or interacting with certain aspects in the game and until this gets fixed - I can't recommend it to anyone. I personally picked it up with the current sale because I wanted to see for myself if it was that bad. Which it happened to be, so I refunded it after finding my first bugs. I don't mind having to reload sometimes, or reverting to a previous save. It can happen (we all know the Sims). However, not being able to interact with things you're supposed to be able to interact with or not being able to enter various aspects of  is a problem. I personally didn't encounter any crashes but I hear these are also common later in the game. There's been multiple reports of these problems which have been ignored for at least a year now, which basically makes this abandonware. Go spend your money on devs that do fix what needs to be fixed and actually care about the finished product.It's really a shame, because the concept of the game is really cool and I would have loved to support it in it's finished, polished state. It is still enjoyable, of course. The art style is beautiful, I am in love with the soundtrack and if you think away all of the things you  do it's simple, relaxing fun, but there's so much to be desired, even apart from the bugs and technical problems. Which bugged me, but it might not bug you, who knows. For example:Characters becoming pretty much statues after you've 'helped' them makes no sense in a game that is about peace and connections. Why revert a character with personality and a story to something that is simply... decoration. It would have been nice to be able to keep chatting to the 'friends' you've made, petting the animals or whatnot. It feels like they put more effort into making enough napping spots than they did the characters, when they are supposed to play a pretty big role. The stories of the character you meet feel... non-personal, rushed, like I am supposed to care for these characters but I missed the reason why and yet I still help them... Only for them to go back to boring statues. What was the point? As of right now the most fun thing about this game is the mini games - which they didn't fix the bugs for so... That's just depressing, isn't it? That was my opinion on this missed opportunity to make something that could've been a real journey to not forget about.Shame on you devs, shame on you.

_childDocuments_.review: I know I am very emotionally weak but this game has made me cry multiple times. It is so wholesome, so comforting, so cozy. I really cannot explain the mixed reviews. This is a small indie game, and of course it has its issues upon release! The developers are so kind and responsive both here and on Discord, and they are taking everyone's recommendations to heart it seems.The art style is something I have never quite encountered before and I could not love it more. The movements, the characters, the world... it is all so, so beautiful and serene. The first time I entered water in the game, I was amazed! I loved it. You can sit and watch the clouds, rest by ponds and enjoy the fish, or play music with other animals in a rhythm-type mini-game. For card or deck-building lovers, there is also a card mini-game!The story is very emotional, at least to me. It is post-war and is all about rebuilding and forgiveness. It is beautiful. I hope that they expand it more and add more dialogue, as I love hearing from the other animals.Overall, the price is more than worth it to me so as to support an indie team and their stunning game. I understand all of the complaints, from the UI text not being as pretty as the game itself to the bugs. However, these are not game-breaking issues to me at all and have not really affected my gameplay experience.Aka is a true little treat.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely adorable and heartwarming game with a rather failed release because the devs weren't finished and couldn't get more time. I decided to give it a chance anyway because I loved the demo and have full sympathy for things not working out as planned. When I was "just going to quickly check if it really is that bad", it took 3 hours before I managed to quit... After another 3-4 hour session, I added it to my favourites. The story is a touching one of past tragedy, its aftermath and hope for the future. Dialogues are often funny and cute in addition to the sad ones. Everything looks beautiful, there's much to explore and many quests to finish at your own leisure. It's a bit ironic that the optional card minigame is the usual damage vs. hit points, but unfortunately for me it's so engaging that I've spent too much time on it to complain XD It's a nice touch that you get extra cards from NPCs as you become friends with them. The controls have been abundantly criticised, but being as clumsy as I am, I don't struggle more with them than in many other games. I've found that a combination of mouse click + drag and keyboard (pressing two keys at once to make up for the diagonal view) works best for me. Inventory management seemed smooth after the update, it would just be nice if the crafting menu didn't close after each item. My main critcism would be that the days go by way too fast for me. I feel like I barely got started with something and it gets dark again - too much like real life lol. There isn't anything that you have to do each day though, so it doesn't actually matter. Oh, and maybe our Aka shouldn't auto-enter doors and prompt loading screens considering how easy it is to end up there by accident in some places... Thankfully waiting times weren't that long even on my second-hand laptop. UPDATE: Just finished the main story (after almost 10 hours, but I'm slow and played the card minigame quite a lot) and wow. This game reminds me of 3 of my older favourites. Most of all I got strong  vibes from exploring the beautiful landscapes and secret caves (oh my gosh I love secret caves), all the non-linear and optional quests... and the somewhat half-baked but still fun farming and crafting and generally a bit unfinished state. The parts about helping spirits move on obviously brings to mind , also exploring different islands, though I found Aka less exhaustingly sad and prefer its wonky controls over actual platforming. The painting-like art style, aspects that only matter for personal roleplay, and the freedom to find your own goals reminded me a bit of , even more of its planned future features (cooking over campfires, minigames, playing music with others though in BoT it's other players). Aka's complete absence of enemies and survival aspects makes it more serene though imo. So yes, things do still feel rough around the edges, but I've already enjoyed it so much that this is honestly my belated GOTY 2022. * * * If you like chill and story-driven games, check out my curator . You're also welcome to join the .

_childDocuments_.review: I really really really wanted to love this game.I loved the Demo, I love the atmosphere, I love the music, the dialog, the story.I really wanted Aka to live out their life in peace.What I don't like is the controls, several bugs, and especially this one game breaking bug that may just be a freak accident.The controls:Keyboard and Mouse controls are pretty spot on. No problems there.Using a Gamepad/Controller however can be a major pain if you're trying to place anything. You'd think the right stick will allow Aka to swivel in place so you can place objects. No. The left stick moves Aka for cursors and item placements in the world. When placing an item, it is extremely frustrating to do it through a controller. Just try putting a chest on a corner near some objects. Each time you move into the correct position, you have to account for Aka moving just slightly forward as soon as you let go of the left stick. Just missed? Moving forward is a bit too much and it'll tell you *red* (You can't put this here.) Moving back turns Aka, no longer aligning the item in it's position. Switching to keyboard/mouse at this point completely simplifies the placement, but I shouldn't need to do that when using a controller/gamepad.The same can be applied to watering crops or picking up items. There is a neat control where Aka, if close enough, will automatically move to an item on the ground and do some kind of action, based on what button was pushed. This isn't even close to flawless. Aka will stop after awhile if the item isn't reached on time or if the item is being blocked by entities that aren't really interactable. If picking up grass, I'm fine with Aka deciding that they didn't want to pick up grass at the second they couldn't reach it. On Keyboard/Mouse, watering crops is great. On a gamepad/controller farming crops makes you want to just give up on growing anything. The entire experience is super annoying. The blue square sometimes doesn't even show up for watering a spot, yet somehow it sometimes decide that you successfully watered the spot intended, some random spot, or not at all. Flies and Gastropods will somehow get in the way of watering crops and picking up crops. It goes as far preventing you from watering a spot for some reason, just because it was in the spot at the time.  Moving to a spot to till needs careful movements, as the slightest of mistakes can force you to till a spot you didn't intend to till. I haven't figure out how to un-till, but now you got a spot there until it takes it away from you in a game day's time.This would be easily fixed if you got a strafing option or at least a way to turn Aka without moving. That right stick isn't doing much...The game breaking bug:This game has cloud saves. I played the majority of my hours on record on my desktop. In game, I'm on day 30ish. I was feeling pretty good about the game despite the bugs above having to switch between two different inputs. I've done so much quests on it already, and I'm pretty happy about the outcome of Aka's life outside the war.All until I decided to switch to my laptop. I downloaded the game, the cloud saves are in, I turn it on and...Weird. I started where I left off, but the dialog that came up in the beginning of the game for that island is being shown. I checked my quest list, and it is empty.I still had all my items, my crops are still there, everything is where I left it. But all the quests and quest rewards are reset. I thought, no big deal, I'll just redo the quests and it'll be kinda like a new game+ right? NO!I quickly learned that while I can go through the areas again and do the quests, not all things are reset. The dragons have been fully fed as soon as I entered the cave, and I received their cards again. All the ghosts are back and I can do most of them. But now some of the quests are permanently locked out. Like there are no dead trees, ruins, items in previously opened chests from last bug-free session (that means no key for that one thing). It's impossible to finish the other quests or make it come out to finish them.I have no choice but to start the game over. I currently do not have the courage to start a new game entirely, since that experience in playing Aka is significantly diminished. This bug means I have to wait until I've almost forgotten about Aka before starting that new session.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10I love this game, I think it's a very fun game with adorable graphics, a deep and heartfelt story, and interesting game mechanics, but I would not give it 10 stars. Let's go over what I liked first.The Story is honestly really good and enjoyable, you learn things about many characters and it can really pull at your heartstrings at some points. I cried multiple times while playing the game! You also meet a great cast of characters and the interactions are very cute.The graphics and the music are beautiful, truly a treat to the eye and the heart. It really does create a very relaxing and cozy atmosphere and both things contribute greatly to what makes this game so great. It is something I definitely recommend for people who're mainly in it for the aesthetics, it's adorable!The game mechanics are varied and interesting. You've got gardening, crafting, collecting, even a card game! All of this combined with the missions give you a lot to do in the game, which is great... until you run out of them, and here's where we go to the negative aspects.There is very little to keep you playing the game after you finish the main storyline. You can continue gardening and crafting things but there's no point to them. The minigames are fun but are not the main appeal of the game. There are no missions, no objectives, nothing to give a little shape to your gaming. Some mechanics are even just a one time kind of deal, like the potions.The game feels unfinished in some regards. The controls (played with a controlller) are rough, and gardening is honestly a bit annoying. There's also a marble game that, for whatever reason, just doesn't work.Overall I truly do recommend the game, I even think it's worth its price tag and found it very healing and cute, you can even play it for a long time if you pace yourself with the quests, but don't expect a game with long-term playability after the main storyline and quests are over, because there's very little to do.

_childDocuments_.review: A retired soldier from war, Aka leaves the battlefield with his war friend Thom to one of the islands in the east, in search of a peaceful life of farming and blissful normalcy. Make new friends, visit the city on occasion, go hiking, cloud watch on beaches, play some music, and find a place to settle down. Just don’t let the ghosts of your past haunt you too much. 5-7+ hours to complete, Aka is a hand-drawn casual farming sim where you play as a war veteran. There are four islands to explore and one city, with two houses you can move into - one being your starter home that’s already furnished. Farming is simple and only really needed for quest progression at the least, the scale of what you want to grow is up to you. Overall, it’s a nice casual sim with optional minigames as well as its own card game. There are plenty of fun things to do while short enough to not be grindy. The only cons I can think of is unlike most farming games, your fully grown crop plants rot if you don’t collect them, but any planted flowers stay.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: What a delightful game!It's a simple and short game for the genre but incredibly sweet and cute, with a beautiful message as well.Basically, the war has ended, and our MC begins a journey to find peace and forgiveness. As we progress in the game, we help spirits close their unresolved issues; there's a bit of farming, a bit of exploring, some musical mini-games, and more. We go back and forth through the islands, aiding others. At points, it may feel like you are just the delivery guy to some; personally, I didn't mind. I enjoyed the exploration and was curious enough about the spirits' stories to keep going.I think it's a good, cute game, though super simple. So, if you are looking for something with a lot more content and much more detail in its mechanics, it may not be for you. Otherwise, give it a go! :DI believe it works well for younger audiences, perfect for the little ones as it's short and simple, introducing them to several mechanics that are not too complicated. The story might be a bit dark since it deals with themes such as war, starvation, death, and injustice that occurred during those times.Loved the music too ♥

_childDocuments_.review: The game is as sweet as promised. If you go into the game with expectations, you will be disappointed, but if you take the game for what it is, you will enjoy it. The storyline is simple, as is the gameplay, but the simplicity feels intentional. The music and the watercolor images enforce that.Other reviewers have commented on the difficulty of the controls and the bugs. I have found some of the movement frustrating. But it's not game breaking. My only point of frustration is one place where you have to jump over gaps in a stone staircase for one side-quest item, but every other part of the game is playable so far.Edit: Several of the bugs were fixed in a patch after this review. Some movement remains quirky, especially if playing with a keyboard and mouse instead of a controller, but it has improved.

_childDocuments_.review: Beware potential spoilers.This is one of those games that I really wish I could leave a neutral feedback for.The style is gorgeous. The narrative is interesting. But asides from the main overarching story, nothing else really goes anywhere... and not in a good inner-peace finding way.The farming and crafting that is advertised is barely even important to the game and incredibly shallow.There is a great system there for crops that grow well next to each other or deter each other's pests... If there wasn't only 7 crops and only 4 of those have any real pest mechanics. Seeds are also random in the world with one guaranteed spot for 3 different seeds that are always the same kind which means walking in and out of a loading zone repeatedly to get a good few... Two other seed types spawn on the ground on two of the other islands. Past that I really had no idea where to get more of any other seeds. There also only seems to be one artichoke seed in the whole game so make sure you look after it and pick up the seed after harvesting. Not that having an artichoke really matters for anything. There is also only one tree so be careful where you plant it. Fertilising crops didn't feel like it did anything either.You can make food. But it doesn't do anything outside of two quests. You just end up with stacks of crops for no reason.Getting into the zen of gardening is all very well and good until you are sitting on stacks of 99 of everything because there is no outlet for your gardening. Even just four of each crop adds up fast and you are given space for a lot more than that. Presuming you can find anymore of the other seeds somehow anyway...You can't leave the crops to be decorative either, they just die. I stopped gardening as there is no reason to tend to them.There are also a few interactions that feel like the start of quests. The bees want flowers but after growing the only flower seeds I ever got and harvesting them. Nothing happened. The flower boxes also seem to be glitched so I can't put flowers in them like shown on the store page. I can't put anything in them.There is an orphan you build a shelter for and they want to help with the island but nothing happens after that...You can bring someone ingredients for a smoothie but it does nothing as well...I thought I would be smart and use a warming potion to go up a cold mountain but I couldn't drink it. I had to wear a hat. This permanently locked me out of a bottle. Not that you really need many potions either... The second island has a lovely alternate farm/home but lacks any of the utility. Instead of having a fully furnished home with bed and bath animations and such, you get your own place to decorate as you want. But... there are next to no decorations to actually craft and the crafted bed has no animation. You also can't make a potion pot or a stove or a mill... You can only have a campfire and go back to the main island for potions and then jump on a train from there to another island to use a mill... It's all incredibly back and forth for no real reason... turning into a game of awkward running between quick loading screens. Sometimes the game couldn't even keep up with all the running and blurred or slowed down when running directly forward or back...The controls are also pretty abysmal, especially on controller. I had to switch to mouse to water and plant stuff. Even then it was pretty janky. Having decorations too close to your farm messed with pathing pretty badly. Even just having crops side by side was pretty bad and that is literally the point of the pest system.You also can't rebind the controls.Again, the style is gorgeous. At least where it is consistent. The cartoon menu really clashes for me and was a bit awkward to use. Though the map screen is the most egregious... It looks like it was all done with one solid circular brush tool... It feels incredibly unfinished.The card game was fun. After you get past the fact their is no tutorial for it. Though there are too few NPCs to challenge. There is also no card tracker to check if you have collected them all.The other mini-game is non-functional so I have no idea if it is any good. You click yes to play and nothing happens.And again, the story is charming. But there are a lot of NPCs that just... don't talk to you or never talk to you again after you've helped them. It feels like a shame your character doesn't make any new connections.On sale it could be a short, chill game to check out. The first hour or two is fun. But it just doesn't feel finished. It's a shame because I really wanted to love this game. The style and premise really appealed to me. Also red pandas are awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased AKA yesterday (April 15th, 2023) when it was on sale here on steam for about $10, after having this on my wish list for a long while. I am very glad I did. I began playing last night at 7 PM, and this charming, heartfelt, emotional yet cozy, calming game kept me engaged until nearly 1 AM, when I had to force myself to stop playing and finally go to sleep. The story line involving a retiring red panda (AKA) dealing with the repercussions with war is both heavy and, delicately, tenderly handled as it turns toward healing both the land and the hearts that live there. The art style balances adorableness and soothing beauty while the music is blissful. I enjoyed crafting and discovering mysteries and hidden areas while working to help the islands occupants and growing my own garden of flowers and vegetables. I especially liked the small touch of learning which vegetables grow well and compliment each other. The ONLY downside to this game--playing on PC--is that the controls and viewpoint make precision difficult. The keyboard controls are not bad, but jumping to certain places, picking up items and gardening/watering can become touchy. In MOST games, this would become frustrating. However, because of the calming, no-rush and forgiving nature of the game, I did not find myself frustrated by it. I just kept at it until things worked out because I was enjoying playing. I will say it the controls are this twitchy for PC, I can imagine it may be worse with consoles. So I would keep that in mind before playing on console. I am so glad I got this game, and I HIGHLY recommend it for anyone a fan of wholesome, comforting, easy-going, casual, cute and lite puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful, but simple game that needs a certain mindset to enjoy. I highly recommend it if you want a cute adventure/puzzle game and temper your expectations. You'll be very mad if you're expecting a traditional "game". I highly recommend playing it blind, because part of the experience was... Experiencing the game, for better and worse.FINAL SCORE: A heart-warmingly subjective 8/10.The game really does a bait and switch with the crafting system and first island feels like it was a setup for a completely different game when it was designed. I expected a survival crafting game with PTSD ghost haunting, but when I realized that wasn't the point of the game, I enjoyed it much more.You have no stress. Time means little, and you don't even have energy or hunger bars. Food doesn't seem to do anything, and farming is more often than not an ignorable chore in such an idyllic world. The minigames are short, but feel good. The card game is confusing until you realize it's Magic mixed with Slay the Spire. There's a funny infinite turn combo you can collect early on, but that's about all the depth it has.Perhaps the metaphor is that we look for goals and challenges, when the entire game is about learning to get away from that and to enjoy life. The stories are simple, yet heartwarming, and I've enjoyed learning more about the world. However, if you're expecting Tolstoy or Elden Ring levels of "between the lines" writing, you'll need to temper your expectations, as even the translation has typos and minor errors that can jolt you out of it.The controls are total jank, but they're fixing it. There's some minor movement/inventory bugs, but not enough to make me throw the game away. I think some quests may be bugged, and the tarot reader has never updated their cards beyond 'save the bees" for some reason.Farming can be frustrating, as you'll collide with the plants more than you'll harvest/water them. The mechanics of farming feel like some thought was put into it, but the lack of an economy or even a needs system makes farming more of a tool to solve quests and puzzles. Mechanically, this is not a good Stardew/Harvest moon game. It's not even a good Don't Starve clone. Don't expect that from this game. Expect a cozy story, a comfortable vibe, excellent music, and a game that expects nothing of you, even if you perfect it and its few challenges. At most you'll get an acheivement. Usually, you'll just get the self satisfaction of a good deed done.All in all, the ludo-narative metaphor, regardless of if this game is "complete" or if it was even intentional, made me pause for a moment and appreciate the time I spent with Aka.PS: Make cabbages less miserable to farm, please!
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: I can't deny that this is a cute game in terms of aesthetics and gameplay. It takes a bit of figuring out at first, but it is a fun little game. I didn't expect the plot to be what it was, but it was good.My only issue with the game is that it can be all out of order, depending on how you play. The quests pop up wherever you happen to roam and pick up, so it could potentially mess up the timeline and/or impact of the plot. There seems to be no clear ending once you complete all the quests, so it feels like it's an incomplete game. There's not anything else to do after you finish the quests and story, which is unfortunate too.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: Has a LOT of potential, but it feels like a student made this tbh. It's pretty buggy, controls are a little weird and everything feels under-polished. It needs someone with a clear creative vision to give this a once-over and make sure all the graphic/visual design is cohesive with the overall style. UX/UI wise: The UI feels especially cheap and underdeveloped, I'd recommend taking another look at it, and creating assets that have a more painterly feel (Like the rest of the world) instead of the minimalist-vector-bubble style. The UI looks like a cheap mobile game at the moment. Font wise: Try a Script, (handwritten) typeface, not Arial, or that other sans-serif you guys have in there. The map needs a rework especially. It's super jarring. Feels like it was made by someone with a completely different understanding of what this game is meant to look like. Your font choices atm are 60% of the problem. Learn as much as you can about typography, and how to use type effectively. I promise that skill will elevate all your design work moving forwardStory-wise: Take another look at the arcs you have with each ghost: Give the player time to get to know them and become invested in their story and relationship with your PC. At the moment, you're only doing ~one quest per character, and being told by the ghost about what happened. SHOW the player what happened instead. As in: Let them PLAY through it. Allow the player to engage enough with the ghost NPCs to actually miss having them around once their gone, you know? I'm not gonna miss that one ghost who told me I left them behind, when I (the player) never actually did that... Like "Bro, that wasn't even me, I just got here, but whatever, yeah" In other games in this genre (spiritfarer, cozy grove, etc) You have the ghosts hang around for multiple days and quests. They slowly remember their stories, or they're slowly revealed to the player as the player earns the NPCs trust. Would be nice to have something built on the island (Shrines/ mementos/ artwork? idk, something to commemorate the ghosts, maybe...) that you can revisit when you miss them. Grief is such a powerful emotion that you can use to affect players with your stories, but for grief to take hold: THE PLAYER HAS TO CARE. Not bad for the price, though. The music's great... it made me want to re-install Spiritfarer. (You can decide if that's a good thing or not)The main character is DAMN CUTE and I want to love this game so bad... but at the moment the writing feels a little immature. Take a look at this video that Local Script Man made on YT about writing dialogue:    Should help point you in the right direction when writing complex and engaging dialogue that your players don't just click through.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. It is beautiful and peaceful but the actual story is actually a rather heavy subject: Survival after war.Aka, the red panda, isn't just retiring to a peaceful island to handle some crops. He also has to face various ghosts from the past, and coming to terms with things that has happened.My one and only complaint, is that I finished the game in 4 hours. Yet for some reason, there is an achievement to play the 100th day in game. I'm on day 35 and there is nothing more to do.  Which means I'll probably spend the next half hour clicking my bed and going to bed just for that achievement and that just isn't cool imo.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of red pandas I was instantly attracted to this game; it combines my favorite animal with a relaxing farm and explore + fullfill quests game!I'm LOVING the artwork and cute animals in this game.I very appreciate the DEV that is hard working on this game and has already fixed some of the most mentioned bugs (less annoying backpack, spawn back home button if you get stuck somewhere). Sure when it released it had some issues, but for me I have had a great and smooth experience so far!

_childDocuments_.review: i knew i wanted this game the moment i saw the cute red panda sleeping on a silly capybaraim very sad to say that this game felt very unpolished :( the artstyle is pretty unique and the characters are very cute but thats it. there isnt much to do in-game. u just go around fetching things. ik the game is pretty short but the story is so vague i could not feel anything for the charactersit's full of bugs and it overall feels really incomplete

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to how others have described the game looks very cute, very beautiful with the cut scenes, etc. However, the HUD, UI, Inventory management for both Keyboard and Mouse / Controller is atrocious. Outside of this issue, the game is a very casual and relaxing "complete this quest" type of experience. I don't actually think it's bad, it just needs some polish and it would be more functional to play, I will adjust this review in the future if attempts are made to make it more or less, less clunky.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: Holy ♥♥♥♥, what an exercise in patience this game is.No tutorial. No guidelines. No indication that the train behind you will take you to a location pivotal to progressing the game. No means to buy the seeds you need, dragging out certain quests. Pointless back-and-forth fetch-quest crap. Controls are clunky, if you so much as *graze* an island on your way to the next you will teleport there instead. Music started stuttering and freaking out after the game was open for an hour. It plays like something unpolished at best and unfinished at worst. It is unhelpful, apathetic, and doesn't seem to want the player to have a decent experience at all.No direction provided whatsoever, no hints or suggestions from NPCs via good writing- for example: "Hey, you found some wheat seeds. If you harvest those, you could make some flour. Flour turns into bread! There's a mill in the city, I believe. You can get there on the train near your place." Nah, why would you include anything like that when you can walk aimlessly around and go from island to island bashing your head against the wall because this game is so pointlessly vague.Some of the writing was compelling, the story had a decent "twist". The music got repetitive, nothing was helpful, the game is littered with bugs forcing restarts. The discussion board is riddled with these bug complaints. I tried to use the Discord link supplied to ask others for advice, but would you believe it, it's expired! Seriously, what a crock.I was so looking forward to this game and all it did was frustrate me to no end. I will run it in the background for the arbitrary "extend the hours people played by putting an achievement in" (I just finished the game at day 23, and you want me to play for 100 DAYS to 100%?? Come off it.)To top it off, the graphics and visuals were weak and amateur compared to the marketing material.Pass on this. I can't believe how annoyed something intended to be peaceful has made me. It would be SO SIMPLE to take this game from negative to positive and I'm deadset shocked none of those changes have been implemented prior to this becoming a PAID PRODUCT.Oh, and the best part? You can't skip the credits. Seriously. The final spit directly to the face by this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a collection of ideas that haven't been fully integrated into a single game.What am I doing, why am I doing it, what is the purpose of these actions I can take, what do these side games achieve?Beautiful graphics, but a bit of a mess and a confusing experience. I really wanted to like it and tried to enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: it's cute with a nice story but was clearly unfinished/unpolished. It might be better to just watch a playthroughI hope to see the devs continue to improve the game post release or make another game that gets more time to be finished properly.There is a good amount of bugs/weird things going on, odd controls, and lack of direction to the point that you need to completely wander around for hours before coming across something important like a ghost. Unfortunately some achievements also do not work properly, with the mountain peak one seeming to be impossible to get for me. The baby dragons were also weird, I would leave food but I would have to push them to the feeder occasionally, and for the second round of feeding I had to place food, leave for a day, then return to see them disappear.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: Aka is a casual life simulation game. The story is quite unusual for a casual game, it deals with the aftermath of a war. It covers highly emotional topics such as survivors guilt, death and displacement. However the game keeps a somewhat positive outlook and the focus is more on rebuilding and working on a better future instead of dwelling on the horrible past.The gameplay consists of farming, crafting and decorating, helping other villagers, resolving the grievances of ghosts and mini-games. During the game you get to experience 4 unique islands and a town. Two of the islands feel a bit empty as if the developers didn’t have enough time to add all the things they wanted.A lot of the bad reviews for this game come from the fact that it launched with a lot of problems. After the most recent patch the issues have been resolved, achievements work, the UI is good and all the quests can be completed now.On the whole I did enjoy my time with aka and would recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: I bought and tested the game, but now I have requested a refund and here are some (quite many) reasons why:- You get a bit of story and then you're there and don't really know what to do, like I'll look around and figure a few things out- but some basic things I couldn't even figure out after almost 2 hours. Like I don't know if I am doing progress at all or what I am working towards or what could even be possible. You gotta be into that kind of stuff I guess, but I actually liked about animal crossing for example that I knew I had to do 3 quests oder get that much currency to buy something to enhance my island in that kind of way. I felt lost in Aka- I played on controller/gamepad and rebinding the buttons was buggy and didn't work- Sloppy movement, very noticable by cliffs, feels like sliding (very annoying when I'm trying to make a garden/farm)- Pause menu just one-colored screen with text- Some music and "Quest completed" pop-ups sound or look like stock-material, like a cheap powerpoint my boyfriend made for a uni class he really doesn't like- Cliff ends and different heights are hard to detect- Some pick-up sounds are weird (like the added reverb to picking up grass)- Pickaxe and hoe sound is awful (like a shovel hitting glass), turned down the sfx immediately- Bad/no reward system, like i do a dozen things for some cat that didn't even want it and he just said thanks, im gonna improve the island now, but he just kept sitting there. Not even a little pop-up- I went to play music with some koala and while i was doing the rhythm-drum-thing aka just kept staring at the koala, basically close enough to breathe into his face, at least a changed pose for that "minigame"/action would've been nice- there is a hole in a wall close by aka's house where you meet a ghost, if you try to move toward the hole, aka just starts glitching out- 2 villagers were buggy on the palm island, i couldn't talk to them- "panic boy", "bike boy" and "strawhat boy"(or hatstraw boy?) are three names i think, doesn't feel funny but unfinished- if you look away for 2 seconds you miss the switch from day to night, doesn't feel smooth and a bit too fast- there are "beans" that just straight up look like peas- I can't equip or use a torch and I don't know how to use the campfire i crafted- you can sit around in many nice spots like on a treestump by a pond but it's difficult to pose him right, because he always went to sit facing away/to a wall instead of the pond + camera and I couldn't turn him aroundbut aka and the concept are both very cute and I think I could have loved it, but those issues bug me too muchmaybe if they fix a good chunk those reasons I'll try it again

_childDocuments_.review: Explore Explore Explore! There is a lot more to this game than you may think. Break, pick up, and click on anything you can to open up craftables, locations, and quests. The game will go over the basic controls. The controls I will admit is a little different than typical farm type games, but I got it down pretty quickly. After you get the basic controls, I cannot stress enough how much you need to explore. The game does not walk you through what to do next, for example if you want to make bread in this game, you will need to travel, same is true for updating your inventory. If you don't travel you will never figure it out. So I recommend taking your time and exploring. Overall I think the game is fun and very cozy.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty and chill game, no need to rush through it. Take many naps, relax while your red panda soaks in the hot spring. Story is on the sadder side, exploring some heavy subjects. HOWEVER, there is jank to the game. Some things will just bug out. One (at the time of playing) annoying bug, was being locked in an interaction - have to open inventory to get out of it. With that said, it's easy to look past the jank and just enjoy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: It can be hard to return to a normal life post-war, so Aka decides to do it by gooing to the relaxing island his old war pal grew up on.I loved the art and character designs in this time. It's very soft and adorable, and while the characters aren't overly detailed, they still felt unique and definitely had character. The different islands you could go to were unique and cool to explore, each having a bit of a different vibe to them.The gameplay was… eh. I really wanted to like it more than I did. First of all, I wouldn't call it a farming game. Farming is a very miniscule part of this game needed for maybe… 2 or 3 quests. Otherwise, pretty useless. You can make yourself food, but eating it does… nothing. There's not much guidance to the game, so you kind of just have to wander and find things. Which is fine, but some essential parts are intentionally a bit hidden. I was still able to find it all without a walkthrough, but the very start definitely felt a bit… hard to figure out.A lot of items are limited in gathering, such as iron, but at the same time, you can only use iron for so many items that can only be made once, so I actually just have. A ton of useless iron sitting around. Certain items can only be crafted for quests that would be nice to have as decorations, such as the candle item. The decorations you can get are mostly just the same handful of potted plants obtained by turning in trash, which felt quite pointless after I was just getting repeats.The game also still has a fair few bugs in it. The ones I encountered were simple, such as after using an action not being able to move forward and needing to sidestep around, but I did see a few game breaking ones in discussions. It sounds like some have been there for a while without being fixed. There were also just a few annoying mechanics, such as moving during an action cancels it. Which can be quite annoying when trying to pick a ton of weeds or harvest all your crops.The story itself was super sweet. It deals with regret and moving on. How sometimes, even if you are at fault, you need to forgive and continue on living. It also deals with a lot of death, so please be warned that it may be a little upsetting, but I didn't find it to be anything too much. Nothing in detail, just awareness of how someone died.A few of the quests felt… heavily pointless. No reward, no story progression. Mostly, I'm thinking of the snowman quest. No spoilers but… man, nothing happened. Not even a playing card.The achievements were overall easy to get, aside from 2 being very grindy - the apple tree and the playing 100 days. I beat the story of the game on day 17. The apple tree takes about 30-ish days to grow. Essentially, I just woke up and went to sleep a lot after finishing the last small quest I had to wrap up post-game. Some of the achievement titles are… misleading, by the way. One says to beat a character in the card game on hard but… a) it was the only way to battle him and b) I think that was the easiest card battle I played in the game. I also got the achievement for making every potion without making the speed potion. The misleading names didn't make it hard, though, just… wasn't expecting to get them when I did.Overall, it was a pretty good game. I'm glad I played it, but parts definitely felt a bit boring. I can't imagine actually playing 100 days without sleeping them away because there's just… not much to do once you beat the story and finish the quests - of which there's not a lot, by the way. So as much as I wanted to love it, this probably gets more of a neutral rating from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: I think the art style for this game is absolutely precious and for that reason I wanted to love it. I did enjoy the first hour or so, but after a while the quests get repetitive and it starts to feel like a chore to go from one area to the next to get a specific item and then go all the way back. My personal obsession with completionism is the only thing that kept me going. The whole game feels unfinished, but I feel like it could have been great. There are plenty of bugs and issues (you can completely lose essential items, for example) and tasks and quests are not always clear. Also, honestly, ♥♥♥♥ the "100 Days" achievement. There is no reason why this game would take you longer than 25 in-game days. I ended up spending 10 minutes sleeping 70+ times in a row to pass the days. If you really want to experience the art and a pretty cute story, then at least wait until the game is on sale, but even then I wouldn't totally recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to enjoy this, as at its core its a charming game. There's a card minigame, music minigame, and the crop mechanics are really cool (certain plants grow well together andd prevent pests)However... there are bugs which stop you from playing entire minigame sections, I started the game up and controller support just stopped working and only worked when I completely reinstalled the game, some encounters bugged out and played multiple times, and some stuff feels unclear to a player. The game is written in such a way that it almost expects you to follow particular steps, for example the tutorial for the card minigame is via a spirit on another island but my first card encounters were in the city, where I was just thrown straight in. Also getting pop ups that you earned cards from talking to characters without knowing yet that there even is a card game is confusing, especially when its not obvious thats what they are.Gardening is also really awkward and it can be hard to target the crops you want to water or pick.I think this genuinely had the potential to be a real gem because the art is lovely, and the canvas/painted approach to the flashbacks is really interesting but it just misses the mark a lot. As I saw another review say, Spiritfarer is very similar feeling in a lot of aspects and would be a better recommendation personally.

_childDocuments_.review: I could finally play a lovely crafting & farming game where I don't have to worry about anything at all; just chilling, exploring and enjoying immersive - sometime quite humorous - conversations with all the different characters.Beautiful art style and music, simple controls and UI, fun mini-games (including a cute card game which I really enjoyed after figuring out the rules. I am very bad at card games btw). I'm 6 hours in and still not bored with it.Experienced not so many bugs so far, none of them affected the enjoyability of the gameplay in a negative way for me.I can't wait this game to be more polished and maybe extended in the future. Definitely worth checking out!

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. The concept and trailer made it seem so much fun and gave me comfy vibes but actually did not at all. I asked for a refund on steam because I did not enjoy it at all. I felt I was struggling from the start of the game. Wished it had clear direction on what to do. _childDocuments_.review: The graphics are decently pretty and some effort went in the story, but the gameplay just didn't connect for me.The whole game just felt kinda...off.It felt more like a constant stream of fetch quests with a few animatics inbetween, instead of the emotional island adventure that it advertises.There is very little explanation about things, for example I managed to play the card game several times before I even got the person that gives the instructions on how to play it.The card game (and other minigames) also feel very out of place with the rest of the game, just another thing to accomplish for the chores that at least isn't a fetch quest.The farming mechanic could've been an interesting aspect, but having to go through several loading screens to review the information regarding it is rather cumbersome, and just plopping down whatever plants next to each other worked just as well.There doesn't actually seem to be a reason to work on getting the plant bonus.I also cry very easily during emotional bits in games, but somehow this game didn't do it once.The emotional parts are very poorly built-up, most aren't even built on at all and just drop a sad thing right smack into your face expecting you to feel sadness, without you having a real connection with it first.Only in the ending was it kinda built towards, but because of the lack of information I had to follow a guide and got that revealed too...so sadly that part didn't hit it either.Maybe someone who just wants to chill and look at the neat visuals could enjoy it, but it's just too little, done poorly.There are several games that do it better, I would recommend you play those instead.

_childDocuments_.review: As others have stated, it feels like an incomplete game and overall clunky. For the price point (even on sale), I would prefer more smooth mechanics and a more engaging story. The pacing, controls, and overall feel of the game just feels off. I'd like to finish it, but at this point, it's just not worth the grind.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game. I wish I could give this a neutral review. The story is sad and interesting. I like the crafting and how you can repurpose trash. The quests are relatively simple and straightforward. I watched the credits roll after about 4 hours. I still had one quest open. You can still farm and decorate to get more hours, but there are no technical objectives at that point. I played on steam deck with no issues. However, controllers are super touchy. Like positioning furniture is such a pain.

_childDocuments_.review: A neat little cozy game that involves some farming, crafting, and exploring to overcome the trauma of a war. Some parts of the game aren't as polished, but overall I really enjoyed my time. The card mini-game is fun, and the music is very relaxing. Give it a try if you want a short, cozy game to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beauty of a game! It's so cute and adorable. If you're looking for a chill and cozy place where you can hang around and enjoy your life, this is for you.Here you can decide if you want to do some gardening, help other villagers or if you just want to lay lazy in the sun and take a nap! Nobody will judge you for being lazy. You decide when to explore the world (secrets are hiding) and you can do it in your own pace.The story is emotional - Aka the main character just came out of the war and now tries to find his peace. He's not the only one that was affected by the war. You will hear more stories when you talk to other villagers.As a player who played all 3 demo versions and now the released version I can say this game made a lot of improvements in the last months since August. No game is bug free so maybe you will encounter one while playing. But it's nothing that won't make the game fun anymore or that you can't enjoy it. And I can say the dev team is one of the most communicative and helping teams out there. If you have a problem or need help you will always get an answer on their Discord. They are updating the game frequently to make this game even better than it is now. <3The controls may don't feel intuitive first. Especially when you play with kbm it's kind of weird and the reason I simply use a controller. But same here - that's nothing you can't get used to it. And I'm also sure that this will change in the near future with another update. :)I love the game for it's atmosphere and would recommend it to everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: I tried the demo of this game before the release date was announced and absolutely fell in love with it. Now that it's fully released, I still love it, but it's got some issues I can't ignore.As you journey to spread your friend's ashes atop a mountain, Aka's heart wrenching story is beautifully woven through the quests you pick up along the way. Various ghosts of your past seek answers and forgiveness from our little panda friend. There are no physical rewards for freeing these ghosts or helping your fellow island residents; the act of doing so seems to be designed as such, and it's honestly quite brilliant. The only physical reward Aka gets is through recycling trash encountered on the islands. Some reviews criticize the lack of a reward system, but given the story, it makes sense and is something I love about it. There isn't a lot of direction given and it does hinder the player quite significantly. One of the recent updates added a way to expand your backpack size, but there's no explanation as to where to find the crafting recipe to do so (spoiler: its in a bookcase in the library). Cabbage is a key ingredient for part of a quest on your home island. However, the seeds can only be found on a different island. The games doesn't tell you this, so if you're wanting to finish one island before moving onto the next, you're going to soft lock yourself. The interface is a bit clunky. When you craft something, your recipe menu closes and you have to open it again for each item you make. Some items like the campfire don't do anything. There is a prompt to interact with it once you've placed it, but doing so does nothing. In addition to this, stacks of items don't work as they should. If you have a stack of 70 grass in a chest and a stack of 30 grass in your backpack, you would expect them to merge for a single stack of 100. Instead, they stay separate. Moving them back and forth to try to get them to merge does not work. You'll be left with two partial stacks and a wasted inventory space. I prefer to play with a controller, but placing an item is impossible with one. You need to use your mouse to get it exactly where you want it to go. Not game breaking by any means, its just annoying.Some Steam achievements are bugged. Despite watching the clouds and hanging out in the hot spring for way longer than is required, the achievements do not unlock. This is a pretty small game, with achievements you'll unlock as you play through the story, so getting all of them shouldn't be an issue for most players. It's frustrating to meet the requirements and not be rewarded for completing the task though.Aka is published by Neowiz which makes another game that I play on my phone (Cats & Soup) so when I found out they were done by the same people, I was very excited. Despite the issues, I love Aka and will definitely come back to it as I want to finish the story. However it desperately needs some interface adjustments in the mean time.TL;DR: Beautiful world, story and characters, non-intuitive interface and some bugs. The price is reasonable for what you get.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: Frankly I have mixed feelings about this game due to it being reliant on its art-style to sell the game (something a lot of indies have in common), but my experience is more positive than negative, even though I went in with a negative bias after reading some of the reviews prior to playing.It goes without saying but the art and music is the best thing about this game currently. In terms of farming or life sim it falls very short as most of the game mechanics, narrative and writing are only puddle-deep for a game that doesn't consider itself early access. The UI is quite plainly the weakest part of this on release as it sticks out like a sore thumb among all the beautiful art. Out of principle I won't refund this game even though it fell severely short of my expectations, as it shows a lot of potential to improve and I'd love to see this become more fleshed out. Even with its massive shortcomings the aesthetic is really carrying its weight and I'd love to see it become more than that.
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely LOVE Aka’s gorgeous art, music, dialogue and story.I particularly love how the design and leisurely pace allow me to really reflect on the sorrowful backstory, and how they give meaning to the satisfying tasks I have to achieve. Sometimes, backstories in games can feel like an afterthought. But here, in Aka, it seems like a driving force, both moving and calming. What an immersive, contemplative and beautiful experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: Not only is the video like being wrapped up in the biggest, softest blanket, it also has a powerful tenderness that helps you self reflect on facing the traumas of your past--whether you were the one causing trauma or the one being dealt trauma. With the wildness that has been the last few years, everyone could benefit from the message this video game share. It was everything I needed as I started a new year, reminding me that a fresh start can start now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenomenal! _childDocuments_.review: My first impression of Aka was how slow and simple the game world seemed. It made sense after I started playing - Aka is a war veteran finally welcoming some peace and quiet in his life, after all. Aka returns to an island where a friend of his, Thom, resides. He is given a place of his own and free to grow his own vegetables and explore the several islands in the archipelago. The world of Aka contains many secrets and details to be uncovered besides the many spirits you are tasked to free (and in freeing each of them, you help Aka confront more and more his trauma from the war). You also get a pet wolf, which is cute. There's also a card game unique to the world of Aka, kinda like Witcher 3's Gwent, and just as fun. The characters in the world of Aka are lively and varied (though I was somewhat disappointed by the lack of 'content', I think this lack specifically was intended by the developers as it wouldn't fit the narrative of the game the devs want players to experience).Personally, I think Aka is good for a single playthrough to explore and learn about the world. There are some tender and tear-jerking moments for sure, but my own experience was marred by the too-hidden areas which required external guidance and the achievement bugs (which are still at present-stage, very bugged). I think Aka could have been better fleshed out or optional paths better highlighted. My having to rely on external help greatly reduced the emotional impact the 'ending' of the game was meant to convey, leaving me to perceive Aka as merely suitable for a single playthrough and naught much else. Still, it's a decent indie game to play at least once. It's not terrible, but it isn't astounding. I did shed a couple of tears here and there though. Overall I'll give this game a generous 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: You can and will finish the game before the apple tree finishes growing. It took less than 9 hours to beat the game. And honestly, that was longer than it should have taken. We all have our moments and when I couldn't get into the boat from the beach, I didn't bother trying the dock. yeah. well. whatevs. Anyhow, for a game that can be completed in only a few hours, I would expect it to be less than $6. It's not. It's $13. Over twice what it should sell for. It really is that short of a game that it shouldn't be $2 less than a much more robust game that can take over 300 hours to get perfection (you know the one). But that's my opinion. I got mine in a bundle, so I may have paid around $11, still too much. Buy this game at 50% off or more, or avoid it. It's really not worth it. Now, the things I liked. There's spots all over the game where you can zen out, take a break, and just space out on the ambiance of the game. That's kinda kewl. The story line is a bit dark; not for kids. The graphics are adorable. Though growing crops or lighting the campfire isn't intuitive in any way, shape or form, once you get it, you enjoy it. It's not tedious and you get seeds for almost every crop you grow. I recommend planting and never picking the flowers. You have no use for them and they're for the bees (they don't suffer if you pick them, it's just a mind trick you may or may not need for your own satisfaction). You do not get seeds for picking the flowers, only the crops. You can fill your farm up with potted plants! Yep, you read that right. Recycling is a continuous thing and you can collect as many potted plants as your little red panda heart desires. If you get stuck, there's a guide. Otherwise there's no other indication of what to do next if you don't happen upon the trigger spot at the right time for the last few quests. Those last few seemed easy to miss because the trigger is in a less frequented area. If you're thinking about this one, put it off until it's on sale. When the price drops below $6, I would absolutely recommend this game, but until then, it's a no from me.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing/completing my playthrough of Aka (or well, at least most of it), I'd say this is a really adorable game yet also emotionally tragic with its narrative, which deals with heavy topics of the aftermaths of war and how Aka has to overcome his burdened past; hence why to help out various ghosts in the game of that being his friends, family, or even other civilians who unfortunately had their lives lost during those dark times. Although, this sort of goes on the whim of trying to move on and find a better future, a place to actually call home and find "inner peace" instead of Aka's past getting the better of him, so there is an optimistic outlook with the direction despite the inner trauma Aka may/most likely would feel. It's fairly simplistic of a game compared to other farming sims, where the farming mechanics and crafting are rather basic in itself and perhaps the mini games are a bit too basic also, it would've been interesting if there was more challenging aspects to the mini games (disregarding the hard mode after completing one of the ghost's quests related to that aspect), but that's more on the nitpicky side. Regardless, I did enjoy them personally like the card game. I do feel with exploring other islands some of the quests get a bit repetitive after a while, however they do in fact go along with the story of the characters and aren't entirely random to throw you off the hook so to speak. Most would say here that the controls are rather janky and some bugs that can be seen here and there, despite the recent bug patches update. I would in fact agree that while I didn't experience many bugs since I bought this game after the release of that patched update, the controls or at least for the jumping mechanic is a bit floaty/janky, but other than its initial flaws, it has its fine moments. Admittingly, it does seem a bit lackluster after you've completed all the quests and the main story line leaving with not a whole lot to do afterwards, but again, it's a fairly simple game from my book and it gave from what it delivered and again is more inclined towards its narrative (not saying that's an entirely bad thing, although there could've been other potential of added features if that was ever possible).The strongest points of Aka would be the character/art design, music, and the story especially, I absolutely loved the character design of the NPCs and the tragicness to go along with it. The story is quite dark for a farming sim, but emotionally touching at best standing by the message of learning to move on forward after distressing events like war. Some NPCs may have been just "there" and I do wish some of the NPCs could've had more in-depth characterization, but they all had their unique sense of charm. Especially towards the end. The other island designs and the characters looked amazing, and fairly adorable and detailed with a lot of the art direction (This may be my personal bias, but I do in fact love animal-based games like this especially with red pandas, so, maybe that's another reason I was hooked to it). The soundtracks composed are really pleasantly beautiful, and definitely goes with the peaceful vibe it wants to have. I did enjoy a lot of my time playing this game, and while some may say it looks unfinished/could've had more to it, I do think that aside from what could've been added/done (such as maybe the other islands could've had more areas to explore), for a small indie game it's amazing from what it is. Or at least, in my personal opinion for a small simple game like this, aside its flaws, is really great. Now would I say it's worth to buy? That would be entirely up to you. If you're into a small indie game of a farming sim with adorable character design and having a saddening yet touching narrative story, I'd say give it a go. But if that's not your thing and are rather thrown off by other reviews that don't recommend it, such as other reasons below of it seemingly unpolished/unfinished, that's totally fine. Once again, entirely your own choice if you feel the need to buy or not buy this game. This review is just basically my own opinion covering on how I personally feel about it. You're free to disagree/agree with me vise versa. I enjoyed Aka very much, while also acknowledging its flaws and what could've been improved if that being a possibility. Genuinely from the devs, I think they did an amazing job with most of Aka itself. I look forward to other games they develop that are similar to this one or even going in a different direction, but games like these really have a soft spot for me. I'd recommend playing if this is right up your ally.

_childDocuments_.review: A relatively short, and I have to say, sad entry in the farming sim genre. That's not to say I didn't know at the start that it was about a soldier returning from the war and seeking a peaceful life in the country, away from all the violence and tragedy he'd witnessed. What I hadn't realized was how he'd be reliving his past and encountering the ghosts of people he cared about right up to the end of the story. This isn't a bad thing, necessarily. It gives Aka a unique feel. But be prepared for a kind of lingering sadness that never quite leaves the game. At present, it still has some bugs. The interface can be clunky, at times, though you do have the option to remap keys, at least. (I didn't, but I never quite got the hang of using "R" for inventory and "Esc" never working like I expected it to.) Some NPCs run out of dialog very quickly, either repeating themselves for the rest of eternity or simply saying nothing at all. And clicking on an object often has the disconcerting effect of making Aka run behind it, rather than pick it up.But hopefully these things will be patched soon. Aka is a good game that took me about 10 hours to play, and like all farming sims, you can continue playing after the main plot is finished. Unlike many games in this genre, it also packs a surprising emotional punch.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to playing this game a lot from the way it looks. It looks so cute and the game play reminds me of Animal Crossing meets Harvest Moon, at least with how it was presented to us however from the little I played, it was pretty difficult to do anything without the game menu popping up whenever I pressed the button it required me to do something. I kept having this issue throughout the entire time I tried playing this game, not being able to make it far in what needed to be done without the menu popping up from pressing the button that it was telling me to press to do something else. Which caused me to rage quit honestly. The style is cute, the characters are cute and the concept is cute. The game itself? lacking. horribly lacking. The controls are sh*t to be honest. I wish I could get a refund for this but it's been too long and now I'm stuck with a game I'll most likely never play again unless it gets a huge update and the controls ect get programmed better. Save your money and watch game plays.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like Aka, I wanted to give it as fair of a chance as I could. So I held off on reviewing. However, after playing it repeatedly over a while, I'd have to say I can't recommend it. To start with the good, the art style and characters are very cute! I liked interacting with them and completing the cute missions they gave. Ok, that's all, now the bad. The game play is very sparse and simple, to the point of redundancy. Moreover, the missions characters give you take seconds to complete, and don't feel worth it. Once you complete a character's mission, there's no point in interacting with them again. The story is also kind of lack luster, and not well explained. The music is good, but hearing the same song over and over gets tired quickly. Overall, I wanted this to be more than it was, but past a simple way to pass time, I wouldn't play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: Aka is a very cute storydriven/ farming/ exploration game, that takes about 4 hours to complete. You have 4 islands to explore and complete quests on, a few ghost NPCs that you can talk to and "release", each with an intividual story to tell. These stories are often surprisingly dark and didn't fit the lighthearted vibe of the rest of the game.Farming is such a small part of this game that it doesn't really matter much, you only need it for a handful of quests.I did feel entertained while playing Aka and never really had any complaints because of bugs or stuff, but there are small things that didn't make the game feel 100% polished. Often you have to click a number of times before you are able to pick stuff up, there are things that you can "interact" with without anything happening, ect. I probably wouldn't recommend buying it for the full price but for a 1€ deal on fanatical or similar this is well worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful and touching game with lovely, cozy visuals, NPCs and soundtrack. It's a really calming and peaceful experience worth playing through. Not too much grinding and no in-game currency which makes the game more chill.However it does feel a bit unfinished since there isn't really much to do after finishing the storyline, I feel that more content would make it better, like more decor or more farming just to make it more playable even after finishing the quests.Overall I would absolutely play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted this game before it released, because the art seemed so beautiful and the whole concept is very touching and wholesome. And let me tell you, these promises were delivered 200%. It is an indie game, and there are some imperfections, mostly related to UI and controls. But the fuzzy warm feeling it gives you is exactly what I was looking for in this game. The music is brilliant, I could listen to the sound track forever. There's a lot of content too, more than I expected there would be! There are fun mini games, such as a rhythm game when you jam with a koala at the beach, or a card game in a cat bar where the cards in your deck depend on the friends you have made on the island. In the same cat bar there's also a piano you can play freely, and it's one of the best ways I've seen this done in a game. On stressful days when I want to escape, I will come back to this game and visit the cat bar to play piano and chill with the cats.

_childDocuments_.review: -Gameplay: 7/10, straightforward, but can be a little clunky at times, fun card game within the game-UI: 5/10, does what it needs to-Controls: 3/10 keys are rebind-able, but not for controller for some reason-Graphics: 9/10 cute lil guys/gals/pals, watercolor and hand-drawn cutscenes-Music: 7/10 Very pretty music, but can be repetitive and bug out sometimes-Overall: 7.5/10 Feels unfinished in some parts, dialogue reads weird sometimes (probably because the devs speak a language other than English) post-game is non-existent sadly (99% recipes are either for quest, not as many for decoration as you'd expect for this kind of game, and some don't even really have a purpose) but can be 100% finished in a few hours, so if you're craving some farming sim action for a bit, it'll hit the spot. I hope to see more games with red panda protagonists :3
_childDocuments_.name: Aka

_childDocuments_.review: Aka is an adorable game with a very heavy message about a war veteran (Aka) and him settle with the ghosts of those he has lost. There is some farming and other quests, but this game can be completed within 4 hours and with all the trophies. There is a multitude of other aspects to the game, but once you resolve the ghosts and finish all the little quests, there really isn't anything to keep you going in this game. It is for sure re-playable, but there is no fishing though there looks like there should have been and no reason to grow crops outside of fun and a few quests that require them and its only carrots, wheat, and cabbage. Beans, Corn, Onions, and Artichoke have no value other than to grow them for funsies. Even the card game is too easy, since I can win with no trouble (I am terrible at card games when it gets super hard).Don't get me wrong. If you can get this game on sale, it is worth playing and enjoying the short story it provides for you, but other than that, there is no reason (other than easily attainable trophies for things like 100 days) to keep you playing. Good art, beautiful music, heavy story subject that I did very much enjoy, but I'd give this a 6/10. I'd recommend playing but I can also recommend other games if your looking for more than just a nice story and something more rewarding to grind away at.

_childDocuments_.review: Aka is a beautifully sad Storygame about trauma, loss, grief and moving on. It has a beautiful Artstyle and Soundtrack and even though I had to get used to the 3D Panda in midst of the Painting aesthetic I still think its a beautiful game. The story moved me to tears more than once as the story of struggling to let go hit too close to home every now and then. The Farming and Crafting System is very cute and a little bit different from other Farming games which is a detail I enjoyed a lot. The game doese experience some bugginess around interacting with characters or things like ladders but that didnt bother me all too much.

_childDocuments_.review: Aka is a really nice, cute game. It is very cozy and the tasks are for the most part very obvious or easy to achieve. The music is also very well done and adds to the atmosphere very well.The story is, without wanting to spoil much, very nicely designed - the end can be guessed but still cost me personally a few tears.A very nice game that you can tell that the developers put a lot of love into it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a oozy little game featuring a little red panda, Aka, who is searching for peace.  He returns to the islands of home and starts to help his neighbours.  I found this a very sweet game. It has farming, decorating and crafting.  Quests are numerous, but there are no time limits.  Some quests have to be completed before more are available.  There are mature themes as Aka has returned from war and has regrets.  The whole game is to help Aka find peace and quiet - sometimes that's taking a nap or watching the clouds.

_childDocuments_.review: i went into this game with a bit higher expectations based off the trailer and was pretty disappointed at the beginning but i gave it more time to form a more constructive review!TLDR; it has a few bugs, seems unpolished. UI, menu, crafting and inventory management needs work. beautiful music and artwork, emotional story, easy questing, overall simple gameplay.yeah there's bugs, i couldn't talk to some of the characters and some of the exploration seems a bit choppy. the farming aspect of the game does have an interesting mechanic(?) but it doesn't seem to have a lot of depth to the rest of the game outside of just doing it because you can. there has only been a few quests that required food items made from crops so farthe UI, inventory management and crafting menu is clunky and definitely needs work. this was probably my biggest disappointment because the dialogue artwork and typeface is really beautiful, but the menu and UI literally uses the most basic font that just doesn't fit into the game at alldespite all of that, there is an extremely emotional story to this game that unveils itself at the beginning and develops throughout. there's a reason why you're there, living out an easy, peaceful life now. i say easy purposefully because the questing in this game is relatively simple: talk to npc, receive quest, fetch item, return and there's nothing wrong with that, it's what makes the game relaxing. i'd say the story of the game shares similar vibes to Spiritfarer, if you're familiar with what that game is aboutlastly the music in this game is really beautiful, there are some volume issues with some of the mini-gamesto sum it up, this game definitely needs some tweaking but it is enjoyable, laid back, cute and simple. i would recommend it if you're looking for something that  like most other farming / life simulator games but also with an emotional story, beautiful music and artwork!
