_childDocuments_.review: I love everything about this game. i'm a huge fan of Terra-forming end Eco restoration games, the almost pixel art is beautiful and adorable, i love the addition of wildlife and the recycling system, i love the the fact that its also a puzzle game, especially on harder levels, you really have to consider things. My only complaint it that there's only 8 levels, I want MORE!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Really lovely game - perfectly hits the mark when it comes to satisfying puzzles, nice art & assets, and an engaging game play loop. I love ecology focused games like this and there are not many. I just started playing the new free update, Vita Nova, and so far I'm really enjoying the new animal system & additional maps.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game now after the vita nova update is incredible. It feels more organic in the way it introduces the animals which is obviously very appropriate for the game concept. If you enjoy city builders of any kind, this is a must try. It is so relaxing but not under-stimulating. Truly hits a niche I haven't found anywhere else. Enjoy new players. You are experiencing this game at what is so far the prime of its mechanics, feeling, and aesthetics.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, Very cozy, low pressure, small amount of strategy, easy to understand the mechanics. It took me 8 hours to complete the game 100% on the easiest difficulty. I only have two critiques. One, the currency system is a little useless. I never once had to worry about having enough currency to place structures, but that could be a result of the easiest difficulty. Two, the maps are for the most part randomly generated and this can create issues where parts of the map can't be accessed by certain structures (like windmills to power the area or monorails to clean the area) so you may need to restart a level because the map RNG make it unplayable or certain flaws with the map weren't clear until the end. But other than those two little things, its fantastic! i highly recommend this game for a quick, cozy play!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Game is lovely, people complaining about price/lack of content probably buy new COD games every year to play only multiplayer. Yeah it seems to be a *little* bit short, but it's an indie game, a unique and beautiful one at that. 25$ is decently fair imo, especially with the replay-ability with procedurally generated maps and 4 different regions. It's a casual, calming, and peaceful game; exactly what I was expecting and looking for :D and most likely will end up with some extra features/abilities/dlc in the future as well, who knows.I was able to figure everything out, nothing was annoying or tedious or seemingly unnecessary, everything seems to fit together and work pretty well. The recycling stage is by far one of the easiest things I've ever had to learn in a game, same with introducing wild life with the sonar, so I don't get what the negative reviews are saying about those mechanics. Overall I've been happy with it, and can relax and just enjoy rebuilding a wasteland. It's neat!Wouldn't recommend for people who don't like casual and tranquil games ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I've played through each region once, and am going through for a second time on the newly unlocked maps. Whilst the game is a little small right now, with only four regions and two maps per region, it still packs a hell of a punch, and I'd still say that this game is definitely worth buying. The complexity ramps up nicely, as the tutorial introduces you to each concept, although in later levels it may not be obvious what to do at the odd point, but just experiment and you'll find the solutions easily.There is a lot of scope for adding many more regions, maps, biomes, and animals to the game in future, maybe even incorporating them into other planets too*, and I hope this is the general direction the devs take with it going forwards. It looks and plays beautifully, and I have yet to come across a bug, or an issue I cannot find a solution to.I give this 7 out of 5; a perfect score.*Aliens?
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Not a 100% completion, but I ran through this in a few hours. It's awesome. It manages to be well paced enough to keep me sucked in for hours at a time while being a chill and relaxing game. I've picked it up here after enjoying the mobile version for a few hours. 29€ is a bit steep considering the content and that the game was probably already funded by netflix, (I may be wrong) but I'm cool with supporting indie devs. I hope new content get added sooner than later
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - the game is nice, but extremely short (at the time of the review I finished the standard campaign). I will probably check it out again in the future to see if there are other planets / mechanics worth discovering.The game is very pretty and relaxing, but the content seems to be lacking right now. There are maps with distinct objectives and strategies, but they do not differ that significantly. Some of the mechanics do not seem ironed out yet so I didn't really feel the need to minmax. ¨Overall it took me about 5 hours to finish (1 difficulty / standard campaign) and I do not feel really compelled to start over (at least not at the moment).I don't mind paying the full price for even just a couple of hours, but some may expect more. And also I am sure there's going to be more content in the future (at least that's my experience with indie games).
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10. Baie lekker!Simple, relaxing, and beautiful game. It is great for a short, thirty-minute gaming session or for a three-hour terraforming romp! And did I mention it's beautiful? I was hooked since the demo and was following this game for months before the release. The finished product did not disappoint. More of the same, which if you put in as much time into the demo as I did, is a good thing. The recurring criticism I have seen is that it is short. There are eight scenarios. Two scenarios for every biome (four biomes - urban, tundra, tropical, and temperate. That said, there is a "hidden" randomly generated mode, of sorts. If you change the landing coordinates in the World Map menu, you can create a slightly different version of each of the eight scenarios. It is not very obvious, though. The other thing is it doesn't seem to have a genuine sandbox mode. I would love an option to be able to play a scenario with all the tools available, rather than being constrained by biome or scenario. And the ability to save individual terraforming projects would be nice, for those of us who are trying to make especially beautiful looking worlds. On a final note, and a more personal one. I spent my childhood in South Africa. I was genuinely delighted to learn that this game was produced there.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A genuine joy of a strategy adjacent, city-builder. In other city-builders you might find yourself building and sustaining... well, a city, this game takes the route of you developing and cultivating a once thriving ecology of several different biomes, now lost in an apocalyptic wasteland. Seeing the desolate landscapes become methodically crafted paradises as you manage your resources, balance the climate, and searching for the perfect new habitat for several animal species, doesn't ever feel tedious. Instead it encourages you to actively improve the way you place buildings instead of just randomly dropping them or overusing them.   Overall a very peaceful indie with clever mechanics and a great soundtrack from a studio that continues to deliver. Btw, these guys made Broforce... I'm amazed at the range. 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is the perfect game to pick up on sale. It's a small game, that you're gonna finish pretty quickly (10 hours to 100% it for me) but what there is here is very well made, polished and satisfiying to play. If you like chill management games, you're gonna have a good time. I just wish there was more of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot more relaxing and casual than I thought it'd be, which was a great treat. I did play in Gardener mode, so I'm unsure about the difficulty of the other modes, but Gardener felt like a good balance. I did run into a few bugs and exploits, such as being able to place multiple buildings on top of each other with the monorail system, but nothing too bad.It can be difficult if you make a mistake with the climate or land placement. Fortunately, the consequences aren't game-ending; you just have to pivot your strategy.I will say though, 100% completion was only rewarded with an achievement, which was a bit anti-climactic. I wish there was a cutscene or something like there was for completing the first 4 islands. The 2nd city island was surprisingly easier than the first, too; it kinda felt like a rushed map compared to the others.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Hesitantly recommending this game.My main problem is it's quite short and there isn't a huge amount of replayability. It took me about 6.5 hours to completely restore the whole world, after which there's just achievement hunting to do. Additionally, the UI can be a bit clunky and the game as a whole is a little buggy.Still, it's a relaxing and fun game, with some great sound and game design. Kinda reminds me of the Spore space stage terraforming, in that you've got to balance the heat and humidity, along with introducing different plants and animals to create a stable environment. That was my favourite part of that game, so this one definitely appeals too.Is it worth £20? Probably not, but get it on sale and you should have a fun 6-10 hours with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay loop of Terra Nil takes as its first assumption that no matter how wrecked, ruined, and polluted something is, it can with the right tools be restored to thriving.  Strategic caretaking and restoration is what this game is about.  I wish it were bigger, I wish it were deeper, I wish it was less buggy, and I wish it was well-marketed enough that a generation of gamers all had to contend with its assertions.  But I am very glad the game exists, and I will be waiting for the next one like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A fascinating gameplay concept that has a potential to create a lot of different puzzle situations interesting to figure out, but sadly the game lacks for content and does no job of explaining its fundamental mechanics to the player at all. I am a big fan of games that await wit from the player and reward him for his clever solutions and unique findings (), however even these games must be designed in a way that promotes such way of thinking by hinting this kind of gameplay by different means. Even for me this process in Terra Nil was frustrating as I've spent almost 80% of total playtime just to find out things in this game which cannot be found by just thinking about possible solutions, which basically is the same problem of explaining the toolkit, so the only viable strategy that you can come up with is just to spam everything you have, if the displayed number is colored green... most of the time, at least. Unfortunately, the game has not only poor metagame, but also poor puzzle design: whenever you stuck in Terra Nil, you'll run out of possible parallel tasks very fast, so you'll be just looking at your screen and begging for help. The game does not give you any hints when they are trully needed and leave you alone fighting with uncertainty. This destroys all the joy of solving puzzles
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking for a nature restoration kind of game for so long. I'm glad I found this game when I was going through a civilization builder game phase.I've found much joy in just restoring nature in this game. It's so cathartic to get the environmental conditions just right for rain or snow to fall, and watching polluted ocean and wasteland be purified by said means is just wonderful.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with an interesting idea. The visuals are nice, really enjoyed transforming the wasteland back to a livable state. It was very relaxing. The puzzles are good. Once you solve everything, seeing the vegetation coming to live and the animals enjoying themselves was worth it. Wish they had this for the ocean in real life as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very..... "think three steps ahead" because you can easily f*** yourself by placing a building down to soon. It really flops at the end... and the middle. The first part is bearable... the first time you play it. Any difficulty but the easiest tries to be a super complex strategy game, but it is highly precise circle based tile placement (tedious and annoying).  Once you get to the mid game, the early game resource comes for free when it rains , invalidating your hard work and time spent (time wasted) in placing all of those structures with pixel perfect accuracy. Mid game (climate and habitat stuff) can be interesting, balancing all of the aspects were fun when I was able to actually figure out what the game wanted from me.,.... but the tutorial was really terrible in explaining what it wants. This is where the "screw up your save by placing something too soon" happens a lot though. (All of the climate structures can only be placed on rocks, so if you didn't move some lava around 20 min ago to make more rocks,  so you can make more dehydrators, and are out of rock spots to place them, then you lose. tough luck LMAO should have thought about that before you knew about it. Terrible experience.)The animal discovering is really unintuitive. Also really annoying that the popups for the discovering don't delete themselves immediately and overlap the game UI. Also, if you are like me and brick your first attempt at a continent, and have already discovered the three easy animals to find, then when you try a second time at the continent you will be forced to discover the other three animals with asinine requirements like "be in range of 20 ocean tiles and 20 forest tiles and have a 900 credit score). this wouldnt be terrible, but by the time you are at the point where you can discover animals the space left to place structures to change the terrain to fit their extremely specific habitat requirements has run out and you are shid out of luck. As for the late game, the whole "recycle all infrastructure to leave" is really annoying and not fun in the slightest. Tedium, really. Game only highlights which buildings need to be destroyed when there are less than ten left, when that highlighting would be super useful when there is a single tile building completely hidden inside a forest. Which you only notice at the end, when it is one of the ten left, then you have to rebuild the infrastructure out there to remove it. I never got to the fourth continent, but the cable car things were more bearable than the boats. Speaking of, why limit the amount of boats / drones that can be placed to one? arbitrarily limits the speed you can disassemble things. pointless time padding. (Rock throwers are really horrible to use, why cant i throw a rock into water? cant i just put a rock down with my cursor or something? or pick them up with the cable cars like you can do with buildings?) TLDR neat idea on a whiteboard, but terrible exectution. Refunded. if you want to paint maps with terraforming, just play Creeperworld 3. That game has way better combat anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: What a refreshing experience! To play a game focused on rebuilding, restoring, renewal and preservation of life.  A short but satisfying puzzle to solve.  Each map offers a challenging terrain with unique building configurations and animal species to discover. I found myself fully immersed with the relaxing music and the gorgeous sounds of nature. If you love the sound of rain and thunder storms, you are in for a treat.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: At ~20 hours I'm about halfway through the main story, but this game had me hooked from the first mission area. This experience has had me weep with joy and celebrate each successful challenge completed without ever tiring. I love the unique mechanics that change depending on the map type. Will write an edit when i've finished the main story.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: As both an Ecologist and a huge fan of city-builders and puzzle games, this game *perfectly* scratches an itch that I didn't even realise I had. I may be barreling through the game quite quickly, which does make me sad sometimes, but I can already tell that this will be one I regularly return to, even after fully completing it. Plus the update notes make it clear they are always updating and adding new features! Any given map is quite quick to play, which these days is a huge plus. I can go through a map after work before making dinner without eating up my entire evening.Definitely one of my top games right now, and I expect it to stay there! 11/10
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A peaceful, uplifting atmosphere, wonderful aesthetics, yet strategically-demanding (unless you choose the more-forgiving Ecologist game mode and just wish to enjoy the greenery grow)., it's about performing the right sequence of turns in the correct order - prepare an area of the earth, cover it with grass, turn some of it into flora using a tree&beehive, and then start a controlled burn in that area (while making sure it's separated via cliffs, riverbeds, or wasteland) to finally sow trees in the ashes. You have limited resources that you gain by performing some of these actions, so plan your steps carefully - however, starting over with your new knowledge is encouraged, if needed. The game's strategy evolves gradually throughout the introductory tutorial, and then gets expanded upon over the three other main story levels. (There are four extra alternate levels, which I haven't gotten to yet). I won't spoil the other parts of the main gameplay, as I believe I had a better experience discovering them alone, at the pace the game presents them. are what really made the game for me though. Don't get me wrong, I'm a Factorio & Paradox player and I'll play by spreadsheets and find it fun, but the aesthetics of this game were a wonderful contrast to those games. This game celebrates ecology and presents it in a respectful and positive way that made it a joy for me to restore the wastelands to greenery. The music is reactive and enhances the peaceful atmosphere even more., this game was a relaxing departure from the usual subset of games I play. , I only spent an afternoon and evening doing the main story (I did all levels first try, though one time I came very close to running out of resources), . It's why I'm writing this review, I loved the atmosphere and design, and I want to support the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible! I played this game with my Twitch Channel and we all had an incredible time. The music is soothing and the sound effects are cute, but the game itself is so calming. IF you love city builders but get stressed when it 'doesn't look pretty' this game eradicates that because once you've got the eco system back, you recycle all your things and leave! I absolutely loved finding the animals in different regions and would love to see more areas in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: it honestly hurts me to say this little about the game but there isnt really much i can say. You get to play whats on screen and more of that.But what started as a small pixelart dream which seemed simple enough to be fun for a while has now turned into an overly complex puzzle... mess.The further you get into it, the more new stuff it unlocks and while on its own this is fine, the amount of times you fail in order to learn a new feature isnt. You can go back on changes made yes but that doesnt help when you are supposed to understand a feature thats been introduced not too long ago. Or when you are supposed to make changes with the new items that you are supposed to understand without having even used the new buildable.This game is... not bad. But it isnt worth the 25 bucks. 10, maybe 15 max but only cause Im nice.If you really wanna buy this game, buy it when its on sale. Which really hurts to say since saw this game way back when it had its earliest demos going around and was quite interested in the full release.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game. For people that want their time respected, there's a lot of options to play it your way and for the price tag, I don't think 7 hours is too little for what you get out of it. People will spend more on delivery fees alone with one door dash meal but will blink with this value? Seems a little odd.But it's pretty, relaxing, and like that it's not feeling like anything is dragged out just to pad the time to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Very simple and yet unique and addicting strategy game. It plays more like a puzzle game than a city builder,It's very relaxing.It will take about 10 to 15 hours to complete everything, and there is a little replayability, but not much.Recommended even if the price is a little steep for the amount of gamepley included.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: What a nice game,As an avid Strategy Game player, this is like a nice sunny walk in the park. It does have it's challenge though!It's just a very nice, comprehensive game about restoring nature, and even getting rid of your own constructions after you reintroduce flora and fauna back to the wild.Coming from ravaged places, battlefield of either ancient times or giant futuristic battles of 40k. This is none of that, no battles, no killing (the occasional floor burning doesn't count... right?) but you really feel great "when a plan comes together" and you see the little deer on the meadow or crab on the beach you just created.I *had* a feeling i was softlocked at the beginning of the game, what it doesn't tell you is that you have to clean the buildings up again, and i kinda had to work around that, but you live and learn, no stress about it!The only thing that annoys me or i would change, is the visibility, it's kinda hard to figure out where something is or "where is *this building* on the map", especially in the tropical area after i created a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of tropical flora, the outlining of where i could place a unit was very hard to see.Otherwise, this game is a very relaxing take on strategy games, don't be afraid to play it though if you dislike strategy! It can be more of a puzzle, the maps are quite small as well so you don't get lost that easily or have to min max or something you would do in a more traditional start game or competitive game.It even has three modes to be more or less engaging gameplay, you want to relax or engage in serious conservationism?I enjoy games like these, well made, good price, nice artwork, and they even donate some of their well earned money!

_childDocuments_.review: Engaging strategy game with nearly airtight gameplay and an interesting concept. Some levels require a restart or second play through so you can plan your environment accordingly in order to get all the animals and hit all the environmental targets. Hardly a deficit since replays of each level are rewarding, but it's the only thing that sets this game back by a hair. 9/10, highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I had a better grasp of the game when I restarted months after my first attempts. Overall, a very relaxing game that is still a bit tricky in the later stages, as you have to be careful with your resources, how you're terraforming the landscapes, how and where you're placing the biomes... But it's always satisfying to watch this once dead land grow back to full health.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Very satisfying experience!  I bought and played Terra Nil right after they rolled out the Vita Nova update - and while I see a lot of negative reviews from people who played and preferred the game before the update - I really loved it.  Yes, making certain animal species happy can be challenging on certain maps, (I'm looking at you Whales!) but for me, I like a little low-stakes puzzle that will jog my mind.  I was able to 100% the current content in about 25 hours - and that includes redoing certain regions in order to scoop up all bonus challenges during a single playthrough.  Definitely worth the price, especially if you get it on sale.Thanks so much for a fun time, devs!  Loved the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique, relaxing, and serene experience.The soundtrack and color schemes are absolutely beautiful. Beyond that simple beauty, there is just enough of a challenge in the puzzle of keeping things in balance to keep me engaged as well.I love the "appreciate" option upon successfully completing a region. It gives you a moment of quiet satisfaction and puts a smile on my face.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I have been looking forward to this game since I played the first free concept demo years ago, and boy, was the wait worth it. It's just as relaxing, detailed and lovingly made as I remember it and hoped it would be. Personally it's a bit of a pity that they dropped the pixel style, but that's just personal taste. The core concept itself is definitely unchanged.The only thing that I found slightly disappointing was the total playtime. As you can see, I'm at 100% after 6 hours, after not being in a particular rush. Personally it's still worth the 20€ for me, I got more entertainment out of it than I'd get out of 6 hours of cinema. Would I recommend it? Yes, if you love to just chill, enjoy watching stuff develop and have no pressure. But don't expect a 100 hour campaign mode to keep you busy for weeks. The one thing I would dearly wish for in this game: a replay-mode similar to Power Wash Simulator, allowing you to watch the desolate landscape turn lush and fertile in fast forward mode after you've completed the level. But that's just a small aside.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is a sweet strategy puzzle game.  On normal difficulty what I've done so far has taken some planning but has been clear what's needed and has been do-able with only a couple of area restarts.  This is a good choice for a relaxing game that still makes you think.The graphics are good and the music calming.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games despite my low hours. It isn't something I'd personally play often because I have other things to do, but as a background thing on "gardener" mode- which is basically this games easy mode- it's pretty fun to just make cool scenery and appreciate it at the end. The rain can be pretty annoying though when you try and burn the grass to make ashy nutrients so you can build arboretums, but then it's just like "sike, f**k you" and just gets rid of your stuff. Otherwise there aren't many complaints I'd have and I recommend it to anyone who wants a challenge on cost management for "civil engineer" mode, for if you want to use your brain a bit on the standard mode, or if you want to chill and make cool stuff on gardener mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant twist on a citybuilder. The game is calm and Zen, so don't expect pressure or high stakes. Bit by bit you reclaim the environment from waste, and the touch of recycling all your buildings at the end to leave no trace is really nice. This isn't a game you'll probably play for 100 hours, but it is relaxing, beautiful to look at, and original. Well worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have the proper words for the things this game makes me feel. Yes, there are only four biomes, and yes, I technically beat it in about eight hours but, everyone, listen to me. It was 8 hours I would gladly pay $25 to experience again, and the value is all in knowing that I can in fact experience it again, in a slightly different way, limitlessly. If you like puzzles, or nature, or beautiful art, or soothing music, or perhaps all four, get this game. On the central difficulty I felt it was perfectly compelling, relaxing while still making me remember I was playing a game. Just wonderful, overall. Make yourself a cup of tea, sit down, and restore a wasteland.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: The Game is very good. No doubt about it. it provides uniqueness and zen vibes after transforming the waste land with lush green environment. Unfortunately, its a very small game. Wish it had more regions to play rather than 4 regions. The small playable content of this game, is not justifiable for the price you pay. One can complete the current playable regions in a very less time.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game overall and very satisfying gameplay, especially once you look at the final product once you restore environments. On the pricier side, but if you have a Netflix account the game is free on mobile and its the exact same game. Looking forward to new content being added to the game and found the bonus alternate levels very enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is gorgeous, thoughtful, thought-provoking, and offers a striking commentary on extraction-based relationship to the land, without miring you in the doom and gloom of apocalypse. Terra Nil's entire design invokes second chances, hope, and being thoughtful and intentional about how we approach our environment. The music and art is phenomenal and restive, and the game, even when challenging, is relaxing to play. I've been waiting for this game to come out for so long, and it has blown away any of my expectations. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game, meant to be difficult as no one said healing the world would be easy.The latest update changed the way fauna works though. It went from these fairly inconsequential tweaks that you could fully invest in for perfectionnism, to a hopelessly frustrating slog of wondering why a deer will not walk east to claim the unoccupied plains for space, why a boar cannot use a flower field as space, next to a forest where there are also bears who do not care for plains but are harder to please so you put flower fields. It just brings the entire endgame to a halt. And this was on the third most difficult map in the easiest region, I don't even want to imagine what it's like in later parts of the game.I don't know if this should be rectified, changed, tweaked... I do like the concept, it's just that it goes from a challenging puzzle to just clicking buttons and saying "will this work?"
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This could have been an easy thumbs up from me, as it's a perfect spiritual successor to Sim Earth.BUT.I couldn't even finish the very first map. Animals have need that I seemingly cannot affect (need more food, more land), which probably can be solved with the sonic beam, driving them to a new place. But I couldn't figure out how to remove/recycle all the buildings, because if you build a recycling plant, it stays there. The only way you can remove it by diggin a riverbed, so the recycling boat could get there, I guess? Or just burn the whole place down, but in that case, I can say goodbye to my animals, which is also a requirement to pass the level.Very frustrating that there are no clear instructions in the TUTORIAL level.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: At first I really liked the concept of the game - instead of building up a civilization/city etc. you are reclaiming the land ravaged by a past civilization (perhaps your own?). What was not fun was the way in which the game unlocked abilities such that there were times where I found that in order to complete the area, I would have had to known what abilities/items were available to me beforehand in order to effectively plan my exit strategy. I think this game could use further development to avoid some "no win" conditions, especially when played on the easier modes. I want to like the game, and played for awhile, but ultimately I was not satisfied by the level of strategy involved and the way the game evolved. I did not feel accomplished in the achievements made. For example, building the ship at the end should have felt like the monumental accomplishment, but ultimately I just wanted the game to end.That said, the book artwork is really neat - I just wish it was more useful in the game itself? It was more a progress tracker that popped up every now and then.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, pleasant, and short puzzle/light strategy game. The art design is lovely, the theme is quite appealing, and the gameplay has some unique elements I haven't seen elsewhere.It's definitely more puzzle-like than city sim/builder-like. The main constraint is that you have a single resource, and each action you take consumes and adds a certain amount of that resources. Each mission has a sequence of different terraforming stages, and your goal is to place buildings in a way that maximizes their impact for the current stage (as well as the next one). The challenge is in planning ahead a bit to avoid running out of resources or blocking your progress in future stages, and I think it works out quite well.I was a bit surprised how short it is, though: there are 4 main missions that can be finished in around 4-6 hours total. Procedural generation and one variation for each mission adds a bit of replay value, but it seems like there's a lot of potential for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game i didnt know I needed, or even wanted. But I am so happy i stepped outside of my normal genres to play Terra Nil. It is a deeply relaxing experience. The atmosphere it evokes through the visuals, music, and audio is serene. Watching an environment devoid of life change into a thriving ecosystem one click at a time filled me with satisfaction. I did not expect to be so moved by a "City Builder" today, but here we are. Thank you Free Lives and Devolver Digital for this wonderful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! This game has grown so much since I first played the demo nearly THREE years ago! I cannot believe it has been that long but I am so ready to be back and explore all the new content.Firstly, I love the new animal system. I think it finally gets them involved in the whole restoration of the area and they are the perfect difficulty; Not too finicky that you have to plan ages ahead but not so easy that its a given your region can fully satisfy the animals needs. I think it really gives you a direction for where to put certain biomes, especially when playing maps after the initial playthrough. Also, the new maps are incredible! I know that many of them have been in the game for a long time but they are all difficult enough that they do really bring a challenge for the player to make sure they plan and efficiently use the leaves to their full extent. I found myself doing regions again to just play through the map again and make more beautiful versions. I rarely found myself really stuck and at most had to restart a couple times after understanding the unique twist of each map.Overall, The game has just become so fun and varied to play now and its still got the replayability just like the demo which had only the temperate map. I remember sitting for hours redoing that one map over and over just because everytime the result for different. Now I have so many more options and I will continue playing this game, waiting for the next updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: If you like to take a step back and play a relaxing "city builder", this is the game for you. Relaxing does not mean simple however, and the system is complex enough to give you a challenge as they are introduced. The game length is short and sweet, and despite lacking more game modes right now it's actually pretty fun to replay levels just for the cathartic experience.The visual style is amazing and the end screen on each level where you can just admire your handiwork is a really nice touch.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a fun little game.The premise behind it is cool (cleaning up polution and terraforming a planet), and the elements they've included (equipment for increasing or lowering humidity, initiating controlled burns, creating rock formations, etc.) each have their place in the various regions that you're tasked with repairing.Once your'e done terraforming and restoring life to what was a wasteland, you get to clean up after yourself by recycling all the equipment you deployed.  Afterwards, you can relax and enjoy the scenery, which is reward unto itself.From what I can tell, there are 4 different continents, each with 2 regions you'll need to terraform.  I was able to complete all 8 regions, and hit a planetary score of 100%, but it required re-doing a couple of regions.You do have to monitor the resources you have available to you, or you can find yourself stuck.  Each piece of equipment you deploy has a cost, and if you don't generate enough resources with your actions, you may get to a point where there's nothing you can do but start that region over.  Not all of the mechanics were extremely obvious, and while the instructions gave you an overall idea of the objectives you need to complete, it's up to you to figure out how to get there.If you enjoy puzzles, strategy, city builders, and helping the environment, you'll likely enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Personal score: 9/10Would I recommend: YesChallenge difficulty: ModerateGame length: Short.. ishReplay value: SomeCritical feedback: Need's more levels. So in the months leading up to it's release, I played the demo for this game for over 17 hours and that was with the base mechanics and a single generated map. I think it's safe to say that I enjoyed it. With the full release came more mechanics and challenges and in the face of so much practice it wasn't hard to adapt to the new input. The alternate maps made for an interesting challenge and manipulating the climate to achieve new goals was fun. Although if I have to give anything like feedback on the game itself I'd say it's somewhat limited. There are 8 maps in total and while each map does change in layout slightly, it does get a little ... samey after the 4th or 5th play through.  I've got the moves down to the point where I can finish all eight in a single play through in like 4 hours tops. Either way, I find I quite enjoyed playing it and would continue to play it whenever I needed something quiet to wind down with. 9/10 needs more levels, would totes play again. XD
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice and relaxing game, although sometimes it can be frustrating that you can mess up a map without a way to fix it. I think there should be a way to recycle buildings from the very beginning on, so that you can get rid of a building that is in the way or some such. The game is designed for the player to replay a phase/map if they mess up. There is not that much content, however. Although the replayability is great because there are essentially 8 different maps that are generated at random and three degrees of difficulty, which you can try to master, it will always be the same type of map. That said, the higher degrees of difficulty are quite difficult and require an optimal playstyle and long-term planning. That is, if you feel motivated to try. My recommendation is to get Terra Nil on sale because 25 € is a little much for the amount of content that you get. I hear they are working on a major content update, so this info may be outdated soon. I'm predicting that Terra Nil will become one of those timeless classics that people will still recommend in a few years time.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun and relaxing. For me, it does have replayability-value. I keep coming back to playing whenever I want a relaxing time. If you're only into problem-solving though, there may be too little content for you as of now. It took me about 36 hours to play through all the difficulties and get all the achievements ( I played slowly, though). If you're looking for a lovely, pretty-looking game to relax  and satisfy you, this is the right game for you. If you're looking for a challenging city-builder, you may be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil has an idea about itself and it makes the game stand out in its genre. It's not your everyday job to save a planet and restore biomes in a way that allows different animals to thrive. It's a resource management game in its early stages, then it turns into a puzzle game with very satisfying aesthetics during biome planting, and at the very end becomes a logistic planner to clean up all left-out technology.I found Terra Nil easy to learn, with just enough challenge on the recommended difficulty to still be relaxing and enjoyable after a whole day at work. At the same time, I feel like this game is a bit short and does not provide enough replayability, but I count on devs to release some more content or maybe Workshop support. [VITA NOVA UPDATE] I love it! More places to fix, better animal handling and new achievements! I can fully recommend this game in it's current state.With that Terra Nil can join my elite group of games to play when I just want to see pretty graphics, fix some puzzles and fully enjoy time spent with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great little game. I generally get overwhelmed by 'city-building/environment-managing' games like this because they're so complex. This game ramps up nicely and builds on concepts as you play. Made it very easy to learn, without feeling like it's simplistic or boring. And turning the theme on its head so that you're Unbuilding a thing, is really cool. Soundtrack and general ambiance is also great and very relaxing.Didn't take too long (~7h) to 'finish' the main game and get to the Credits scene, but there's still plenty of replayability, completionist stuff to work on, and some other bits that get unlocked once you get to that Credits scene. Easily worth the money, in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I set it to "Gardner" mode, which is essentially sandbox mode. Very chill. I love it. I've been looking forward this game.However, it's a little frustrating at times and it's underwhelming for the price. It's worth a sale buy for a Saturday afternoon. The concept is there, and I'm hopeful that we'll see bigger and deeper games in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a joy to play. The Demo secured my future purchase the first time I successfully fixed the climate. Now that I have had the opportunity to complete Terra Nil and its challenges(both here on Steam and on Mobile), I couldn't recommend it enough. The Dev Team has stated they plan on bringing more content once they squash problematic launch bugs(I personally have experienced very few, with none being game-breaking), and I'm really looking forward to what they have in store for us.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I was surprised how short this game was, only 8 maps total.  Still, there are a lot of ways to play a map and I had to redo several maps until I got it right.  I think it was worth the $25ish dollars and I had fun, but I wish there were more maps.  The mechanics were fun and its a really peaceful play through.  I wish there was a casual mode where you can recycle your buildings in phase 1 and 2 so you can focus on making the map and not completing the goals.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought I'd find solace in a chill game like Terra Nil, but boy, was I wrong! Usually not a fan of tranquil titles (about as appealing as watching paint dry), but Terra Nil? It's like a cozy blanket for frazzled gamer nerves. Who knew rewilding the planet could be hilariously zen, complete with chill animals hanging out? Terra Nil's cozy atmosphere, calming visuals, and soothing sounds gently whisper, 'Take a deep breath, you maniac.'
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxing "city builder" style game. The gameplay can really make you 'think', while the music is just chill.  The campaign is a little short, although it does feature both a 'normal' and 'advanced' mode, giving some replayability. I know the devs are continually updating/improving the game, even post-launch - I'd like to see a bit more in the way of different biomes to restore, perhaps even as a DLC/paid expansion.Either way, definitely worth the money if you're into relaxing games and enjoy nature.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fresh take on the city builder genre that is novel and puzzling in the best of ways. This game desperately needs more content, mod support, etc, because with the amount of content currently in the game, you feel like you're just getting started when the credits roll. Great game, but left me yearning for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game. That somebody thought to make this game blows me away all by itself. And they've done a wonderful job of it.It's a very relaxing and meditative game, renewing and replenishing barren wastelands. Afterwards you also get to reflect and enjoy the beautiful landscape you just designed and restored.It does need more content but that's my only minor complaint. It also feels somewhat cathartic that Nilaus, a famed Factorio guru, introduced me to this game and admitted it's like reversing years of pollution from factory creation in Factorio. Quite amusing.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Very soothing and relaxing. The sound track is good enough on it's own to play as rest and relaxation music too. It's very easy to lose track of time here, but enjoy yourself the entire time.The multitude of difficulty options as well as customization of difficulty is a very nice way to give you a greater challenge or a more personal challenge.There could be a few more tools that could be incorporated, such as the ability to rotate the entire map or unlocking all weather machine options instead of just limiting it to per map.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil is a very clever puzzle game in which you need to bring back nature from desolated environments. In order to do that, you have different machines/buildings that will interact with parts of the ecosystem (change temperature, clean the soil, get energy...). Each map has 4 different phases: 1. You need to clean the pollution and bring nature back2. You restore the different plants and ecosystems3. With point 2 done, it is time to get the animals back where they belong4. Finally, with everything done, you need to clean up your mess and remove all your buildings in a clean way before leaving.All this is done within a very nice chill mood. Graphics are good (even if I miss the old pixelated ones from the first demo) and the music makes a lot for the ambient. It is the kind of game for you to relax after a long day or just to spend a few hours in something very good. At the time of this review, I have completed 100% of all the areas in the standard difficulty, but I can see myself doing it all again in max difficulty or even play a map from time to time (they are randomized within the selected ecosystem so that helps replayability).
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nice and relaxing, but has more purpose than most "nice and relaxing" games.  It's fun to watch the ecosystem grow and change based on your choices and you can take your time.  Each area provides new tools and challenges and the randomly generated maps keep it fresh.  You can either aim for the bare minimums to get through each area or take more time to beautify the map the way you want to.  Great game concept.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's difficult creating a puzzle/strategy game that feels rewarding and is also relaxing/chill.  The game felt repetitive and ultimately boring.The game advertises itself as strategy, but I think it's more of a puzzle game.  Each map is a unique puzzle to be solved with some minor resource management.  I didn't see much variety in gameplay in either the game or the demo.If you're looking for a game to get high and play, this is it.  If you're looking for something challenging and rewarding, this is not it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A rewarding solarpunk game, more puzzle than simulation - this is not a "grand strategy" game. I love the "appreciate" mode upon completing a map, and the "zen" difficulty option that more or less allows chill free play. Difficulty setting is purely for personal satisfaction, which is wonderful to see.Accessibility notes: sound not required for gameplay. Some reading (tutorials and level goals).
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil is a unique and challenging game. It offers the satisfaction of completing various puzzle challenges all the while creating a peaceful and lovely environment. As the you bring about life, there are additional challenges to bring about various wildlife to individual biomes.Often times, other puzzle games can cause frustration, but with the calm environment and lovely aesthetic, Terra Nil offers a calm and challenging opportunity to spend time after work.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those cases where there needs to be a "maybe" option. It's a great game and a fun little chill puzzle terraformer. But the price point of $25 is too high. My personal algorithm is $1 per hour of play, and this game really only has about 15 hours of play to it before you would just redo the same puzzles. I got a little more just because I had to keep restarting a map to get the final achievement. It just feels like they could have added a few more continents and combinations of the biomes if they want to hit the $25 price range.Fun game but wait for a sale. $15 feels about right.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Brain numbing experience. it tells you what to do, and you follow it precisely. Over and over and over. "Do this player.... okay... now do this... now do this.... game over." Wow. The game is on rails. there is no creativity, player choice, or anything other than following basic instructions before moving to the next instruction. HUGE FLOP. Im sure morons will enjoy it.REFUNDED!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I'm disappointed by what I feel is ultimately more shallow and a lot less beautiful than I hoped. It plays as a strict puzzle game with definable objectives, made interesting each level only by the introduction of new mechanics. It's not that the puzzle solving loop isn't enjoyable, it is to a degree - but it's also a little tedious and ultimately unrewarding. One of the promises of those rewards is to be left with a gorgeous, sprawling, multi-biome, fauna and flora enriched space... and it just never happens. It never looks as good as it perhaps good and part of that reason is the late stage if the game loop where you need to pick up everything you put down. Doing so (dependent on the tech in the level) re-scars the land in some way. The puzzle itself is quite open ended, so there are many ways to win. It feels easy. Although you may not get all the fauna challenges because again, these are introduced late game and you may not have been building up to the specifics required to scan a zone that includes that combination of biomes. The game would benefit from showing you what you need from the start so that the player had more agency at the start of the level. By late level... you've done what you need to to surpass the first two gates... and unlikely to undo those successes for the third. Plus, as I said... picking up after yourself (a noble message) carries with it its own destructive cost to the game's visuals.It's not as pretty as Dorfromantik. It's not as puzzly as I expected. I expected an emergent game play loop to occur... but that doesn't happen. Ultimately disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: ( full review with screenshots:  )Terra Nil is a puzzle strategy game in which you're dropped into a wasteland and need to build machines to restore the climate and habitat without running out of resources. Each level follows the same basic flow of starting out with a toxic patch of dirt that needs to be cleaned up and covered in grass, then that grass needing to be replaced with more developed biomes like forests or wetlands, and finally needing to both find homes for native animal species and clean up all of your machines. It sounds like a lot, but since your currency is greenery and most machines generate plenty of that when you place them, it's generally more meditative than strategically demanding. The game has four major climates: the river valley, the tropical archipelago, the volcanic glacier, and an urban continental map. Although the core gameplay loop is largely unchanged between these, each has its own features that keep the game from getting stale. The glacier and continents map have very different ways of generating power, for instance, and the archipelago's focus on water and jungle is quite different from the initial valley map. Each climate also has its own tier 2 biomes, like tundra for the glacier or coral reef for the archipelago, and its own set of six animals. Finally, there are different helpful events for reaching climate milestones like certain humidity levels or temperatures, and most maps have their own way of recycling all your machines when you're finishing up. Once you've completed the four main maps, you'll unlock an additional four that remix and combine the ideas of the original set. These largely don't introduce new ideas, but you do get more challenging layouts that use the power generation from one map and the climate from another. One of two of these might be too much to 100% if you're playing this as an entirely meditative game, but for the most part they add challenge without getting in the way of the game's relaxing core loop. Still, it does have a couple of noteworthy flaws. The main one is that it's not always very good at communicating what's going on. I frequently had issues with not being sure why I wasn't allowed to place a machine in certain places or with only realizing that a particular set up wasn't good enough once I was already past the point of being able to undo it. This isn't a huge deal since the maps don't take that long to play and it's easy enough to just start over, but it also could have been rectified with clearer tooltips and overlays. Second, the price tag will be an issue for some people. I feel like the $20 I paid was fair for the 9 hours it took me to do everything, but it's harder to justify if you're just going to do the base maps. A fifth biome or user created maps could have gone a long way here. --------For more reviews, see
