_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous little reverse-city builder with a very simple and effective message. A great example of games with impact and meaning. Value for money is subjective and I completely understand some might say there isn't enough to warrant the price tag, but I think it's just about right.Do play it, whether you pick it up on discount or at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty neat. But it doesn't have that much going for it.It's between a puzzle game and a city builder but both are so weak it's kinda neitherThe game is to use obtuse tools to create a beautiful vista, which works pretty well.It's good for maybe one 3~ hr run through but not much more, so get it on sale6/10 because It should be much cheaper or have more depth
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended as a beautiful, chill game with a unique inversion of the accelerating resource extraction of most games. Excellent stylised visuals, soothing sound design, intuitive mechanics, and a bit of puzzling. I don't normally replay games, but I find myself coming back to Terra Nil.Players focusing on doing the bare minimum in restoration goals to pass a level will probably be unsatisfied and blast through pretty quickly. But, very much in the spirit of the game and its themes, where Terra Nil really shines is when you take the time to meet all the optional targets to maximise biodiversity, make a balanced mix of biomes, and ensure there are habitats for animals (all of which are very satisfyingly visually represented). The fun is in taking a barren wasteland and making it into something beautiful and varied.On hard mode this requires husbanding of resources and thinking about efficiently placing buildings earlier in each stage, with things accelerating nicely (again, thematically fitting) as the ecosystem is restores and begins to work on its own. It is possible to screw yourself over with careless placement of biomes (especially when it comes to animal habitats), but even with that, this is never a particularly challenging game. People looking for a high intensity, high stakes city-building should look elsewhere (Frostpunk this is not - though I do love Frostpunk).As for replayability, each map type has a different combination of biome and tools, and while these are the same each time, the layout is procedurally generated, meaning that the challenge is slightly different every time.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: i really liked it, but it is poorly explained and primarily a puzzle game above all else. it's super fun to carve out rivers and valleys and make hills bloom. i love optimizing the shapes and getting everything lined up. i also played on easy and didn't engage too much with the resource limitations. it takes a couple of tries before you understand what each level is going to throw at you and how it's supposed to work. it feels weird to rationalize "we're restoring this wasteland, let's blast it to hell and then use a bunch of tech to freeze it". but i liked the way the campaign put the puzzle pieces back together in a different order (even if the logbook didn't get updated to reflect the changing missions).  this is really a puzzle game first and foremost, and a message game... not at all. it needs some qol stuff, like monotile ranges when placing rocks and some better transparency when labels are obscuring your choices. but also i just locked in and finished it in two days, so clearly that wasnt enough to stop me.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and challenging puzzle game with the objective of restoring nature via using technology in the first place that need to be re-collected at the end. Only nature shall remain.The artstyle is minimalistic but lovely and create beautiful and colorful environments. The music is calm and peaceful.The only negative thing in my opinion is the currently limited content. I hope we get more maps and tasks in the future.Overall a challenging but relaxing game which feels just lovely to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Update 27.06.: The new update "Vita Nova" improves an already awesome game in almost every aspect. This also eliminates the criticism I voiced during the release (see below). In it's current version the game is very fleshed out and deserves all the recognism it can get. First things First: Let us please take a moment to step back and appreciate, that it´s not the hundred Battle Royale clones out there, but innovative gems like this that push gaming as a whole forward. Terra Nil takes a risk, introduces something new and I am very thankful for that.The game itself is pretty awesome and delivers what the demo promised a year ago. It´s also pretty hard - at least at the medium difficulty I´m playing it at. But I won´t complain because Terra Nil might be too shallow if it where easier. But the gameplay loop of building a basic infrastructure, filling it with vegetation and finally cleaning everything up checks out and is massively satisfiying.My one complaint is that Terra Nil sometimes does not seem to be sure about what kind of game it wants to be. Presentation and scope make it feel like a mobile game, yet the complexity and price tag are the one of a desktop game.While advertised as "reverse city builder", Terra Nil has little to no similarities to city builders and is indeed much more of a puzzle game.And last but not least Terra Nil clearly aims at a "Zen Experience" yet it´s pretty hard and can even be frustrating at times.Perhaps those little inconsistencies are the price we have to pay for Terra Nils innovative approach but I cannot help thinking that it would be an even better game if those design choices would have been made clearer.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: When I first started the game, I had a feeling it might be beautiful and relaxing. I can only confirm that it fulfils these two points completely. The music and visuals underline the relaxing and almost meditative mood of the game and the small milestones within each mission give life to the nature that you are doing your best at restoring. I was honestly moved when I saw the rain the first time and witnessed how the area which I had tried to revitalise with machines was washed down and invigorated by the fresh shower from above.This game deserves to be played on a quiet evening and to be really experienced fully. Thank you to the developers for this.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: "City Builder" is very loose term here. It's more the skin of a city builder and simulation, with the mechanics of a resource puzzle. I've only one achievement left as of writing this, and completed the base game in 6h, extra levels in 9h. So roughly 2.8$ per hour of play, you decide if it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I would personally give this a neutral leaning recommend. The core gameplay on offer is excellent, but unnecessarily limited. I feel as if this game is designed around being modular while offering pretty restrictive campaigns with no custom campaign tools.I played a LOT of the original prototype of this game, and while the game does have more content in some ways, due to the random generation being a lot more limited and honed in makes it feel like less is on offer. I just feel like this game could really have more content with the systems it has.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Neat little inversion of classical city builders. As I like games that create depth with few available actions, it was a fun experience - however, as it stands now, content is very limited and after one complete playthrough any further playthroughs do not provide significant challenges.Fine to get in a sale - for the full asking price it would need a bunch more content and replayability imho.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: When I initially started playing Terra Nil and got through the first three regions, I thought all of these reviews complaining about the price were totally pessimistic (just wait for the "however..."). The fact is: if you're someone like me, whose main hobby is playing games (especially cozy, relaxing games), and you've got $25 to spend today, it's worth the price for the play time. My current play time (7.5 hours) reflects about 81% progress. To put that into perspective, I've completed 4/4 primary regions and 3/4 secondary regions. On average it takes me about 45 minutes to an hour to complete a level, factoring in that I am purposefully playing at a leisurely pace. I am playing to relax and I am playing with completion in mind. Terra Nil is challenging and requires you to employ a great deal of forethought into how you play. I even felt challenged enough playing on the normal game mode that I had to switch to the easy game mode halfway through for maximum relaxation.  I found myself excited to play for an hour or so before or after work, just to decompress. It's also very satisfying watching the landscape you created come to life in such a beautiful way. There's fully animated foliage and wildlife full of personality. It's an extremely lovable game.HOWEVER... My frame rate while playing dipped SIGNIFICANTLY several times. The game got choppy and it 100% disrupted my immersion. I see no reason why this game isn't optimized enough to run smoothly and without issues on my computer. I can run Elden Ring, a million terabytes of Sims 4 mods, and every other game you can think of on full graphics without issue. Terra Nil is NOT an especially large or demanding game and while there may be some underlying issue that I wasn't aware of, it seems like it comes down to optimization. Secondly, I experienced literal game-breaking bugs during the 4th primary region, the Flooded City. Monorails connecting to invisible monorails, inability to place monorails near radiation absorber thingies, yadda yadda. And considering it took me 30-45 minutes to carefully plot out the landscape during the first and second stages of each level, I was PISSED when I got the the third stage and couldn't recycle all my machines. I just had to restart the entire level, after over an hour of trying to make it work. I had to play the entire level with this bug in mind, so that once I reached the third stage I could actually finish the level.TL;DR...PROS:- Pretty- Challenging- Relaxing and satisfying- Good play time (imo)CONS:- Not optimized well enough (poor frame rate)- Game-breaking bugs in later levels - I'd be happier with the price if an update adds additional regionsBasically, wait for an update and a bug fix and it's 100% worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and interesting. The visuals are very pleasing. The gameplay puzzle mechanics are very satisfying. The levels are randomly generated so this creates a small new world to play with and keeps it slightly more interesting. I would love to see some free expansions or DLC to add more levels and varieties of puzzles and challenges. Very fun for me, but also very short.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I would say that the gameplay was pretty frustrating and not very fun. Animals and trees didn't appear by themselves pretty much 90% was created by you which was boring, I thought the game would feel more alive if that makes sense. I thought animals would appear by themselves as you progress, which they did not. You had to place a device down and find circles that matched their needs then they would instantly spawn in and just wander in that specific zone.And also something I disliked was how easy and simple the systems where. It was very easy to complete the maps or levels. The game was fun for around 1-2 hours then I felt how it started to become repetitive. And for the amount of content 25$ is not justifiable. My biggest problem was that the game didn't feel alive at all. What I mean by that is like some games have events that you have to react to and adapt like dinosaurs escaping from their enclosures or enemy camps attacking you. This world did not have anything else but thunderstorms which basically just gave you credits because the rain causes growth. It makes it feel very empty. And like it wouldn't matter if you left your pc with the game open. There is nothing going on.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and charming little 'puzzle' game. Despite not being very in-depth, it does provide casual entertainment and I enjoy playing it on my wind-down before bed. The price may be steep for some but I think it's a good game, and part of the profits go toward a real life conservation effort. Very cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is an extremely chill and relaxing game and it's unlike anything I've ever played. The gameplay mechanics are fantastic, the visuals are stunning and the music is relaxation central - very calm and easy listening.The game has different modes to make it more challenging but even on the 'standard' settings, it's so easy to mismanage your resources and run into severe bottlenecks that'll force you to restart your game. I'd love to see Free Lives add more levels and new challenges though because as best I can tell, there's been no new content since launch and for a £21 game that's 100% free on mobile/tablet (same game!) for Netflix subscribers, it'd be great to see something new to bring existing players back and draw new ones in.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I actually really like the idea of this game, and most of the gameplay. It's just the "pack up and get off the map" phase that's extremely frustrating. First you have to place the recycling units within range of the buildings, and then you have to place the beacons on waterways to summon your drone (which is a little boat that always get stuck and your only hope of un-stucking it is to exit and then re-enter the game) to collect the recycling units (which might be out of range of the drones in which case you need to build a turbine in order to build an excavator in order to build a canal which might also need to have water pumped to it in which case you need to build a pump too. And then all these have to be recycled). I'm glad the game factors in cleaning up your stuff but the terrible gameplay mechanics of this phase just make it infuriating and un-necessarily time consuming. Maybe the ship could just, y'know, collect all the recycling silos you've built as it flies out?
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil is a delightful reverse city builder. As someone with an ecology degree, seeing real life ecological processes (i.e. nutrient cycle and fire cycle) being shown in such a positive way in a game was so so pleasing. The artwork is so beautifully done, hats off to the artists. It's so satisfying to see the world develop for the better as a result of your actions. Some things could've been explained a little better in the "end game" content, but I was able to work it out eventually. Deffo recommend if you're looking for something to occupy an afternoon.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Very restful and engaging, lush graphics. Instead of the imperialistic macho or cash-driven urbanism of the average construction game it's a lush and peaceful eco fantasy with soothing music. It's a shame it only has 4 levels, each of which has 2 sub-levels - it's true that they load random layouts each time but it still gets a bit repetitive, once you've maxed out all 12 levels - which obviously doesn't take that long - there's not much left to do.  Still, I've had a lot of fun and not sorry I bought it. I still play it regularly.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Its spring break, so I woke up this morning to this game being released and accidentally cleared the game in 1 day. I did not play on the hardest difficulty (just the default, which appears to be the middle of three choices), but I restored a planet to 100%. This meant going through each biome at least twice to clear both versions of the missions and random excursions back to to pick up missed bonus objectives and critters I didn't quite set up for first time through. Which brings me to the review, this was an awesome experience. I'm so impressed with the game design, I play a lot of strategy and resource management games and this one nailed it. It was challenging enough that I had to do multiple attempts at several maps, but its so pretty and well paced that it never felt like a penalty to restart a level. You learn what you need to set up your biomes in the right area and you start again. Its an extremely relaxing game and I expect it will be a game I return to regularly when I get burnt out from my normal game grind. 10/10 would recommend. Also you can watch your penguins frolic on icebergs.TL/DR: Game has a simple beauty, great game design, good replayibility.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely really enjoyed this game and I feel like it's good for those who like strategy and want a more relaxing version. Pretty easy to "beat" all the levels the first time around, but the procedural map generation and different strategies made it worthwhile to play everything through a few more times. I can tell I have a few more playthrough's in me now at 6.5 hours and will probably come back to this periodically when I want a palette cleanser and a game that makes me feel like I'm using my brain in a calm way. Def glad to see more games of this type getting recognition! Go team!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice idea and I'm sure it's supposed to be relaxing, but the randomly generated maps shafted me more than once.  So, I gave up after making it to the 3rd part of the second archipelago map, and realising it required elevated land for completion but barely any existed in the map.  When you get frustrated enough to Google it, you find a lot of people complaining that they're unable to finish level X Y Z due to the map.This is a reasonable argument against random generation with no dev oversight, if devs had tailored how each level was generated, it would be guaranteed to have the resources you need to be able to complete it.  Instead, it's purely based on luck, and you need to restart if it's not working out.  Which, after you've had to restart a couple of times, ends up being pretty frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game. It's not perfect, but it's a very fun experience and I'd play it again. The only real problem I have with it is how short it is. But it seems like the devs are working to add more to the game, so hopefully that'll change. Fun, satisfying - not particularly hard, but you still have to think about what you're doing. The animals can be a bit finicky, but they normally sort themselves out with time.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful ecological, didactic and educational restoration game! Necessary for our times and to raise awareness. On the other hand a percentage of profits are donated for the REAL restoration of our world. I hope more games like this one will emerge and even be considered for educating the younger generation. 100% recommended, beautifully accomplished and entertaining. Must win the 2023 Steam Award Sit back and relax.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A cute wholesome game which teaches a valuable lesson and is quite fun. A mix between city builder and puzzle game, this cozy game will leave you wanting for more, which is the only complaint one could have for this game.There are 4 types of levels, then you will unlock 4 more variations of those levels once you "beat" the game. If you want to get the most out of this game, I highly advise playing on the Ecologist setting and trying to get all of the achievements.I bought the game while it was on sale for $19.99, and after getting every achievement I ended up putting 18.9 hours into the game. While some people might think that return isn't great, you can take solace knowing 8% of your purchase is going to the Endangered Wildlife Trust.Overall, Terra Nil is a great game which challenges the mind in just the right way without causing unneeded stress which can be associated with the standard city-builder.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 26/07/2024:There was an update with new content and redone animal system. I very much recommend this game right now. There is enough to keep you entertained for a while. It is still short and I'd like to see some random levels, but I understand that is a difficult technical challenge. ---------This is a very sincere review. I'd like to clarify from this moment that the game is good. I enjoyed it very much, but there are certain aspects that need to be addressed before I can fully recommend this game.Overall, I'd say I'm on the fence between recommend and not recommend, and here are the reasons.I DO recommend the game if: you are seeking a new experience different from pretty much all games out there, you have the money to spare, you like zen games, you like puzzle games, you don't get frustrated restarting the game from zero, and you don't mind the game being short.I DON'T recommend it if: you are looking for a 20+ hour experience, you want variety and replayability, you are on the fence about whether you like the idea or not, and you don't have the money to spend on this game without regretting the purchase.All in all, the game is very fun. There are only four regions/themes/ecosystems, and each one of them presents its own challenges and mechanics. The game has three difficulty levels. I played on medium, and it felt very easy. Don't be fooled; this isn't a completely zen game. It is much more of a puzzle experience with rewarding visuals and sound effects for solving every piece of it. The game does a very good job of explaining the mechanics and guiding you through the objectives. I only felt lost once on the last level, but it was a brain fart on my part.GAMEPLAY: At the start of a level, you recover toxic land and rivers by scrubbing toxins and irrigating the soil to create grass as groundwork for the next phase. In phase 2, you start shaping the land by using machines to create different varieties of biomes, and you're also controlling humidity and temperature while expanding the green land to the edges of the map. In phase 3, you are spotting animals by scanning regions of the map. Every animal requires a different combination of biomes, requirements, and sometimes temperature. There are six animals, and you need to spot at least three. The game is very generous on this end because until you get to this phase, you don't know the requirements, which encourages replayability but in a bad manner. In phase 3, you are also scraping all your buildings so when you leave the area there are no buildings left. After all that, you leave the area and move to the next level while the game gives you a zen view of all you've accomplished.Here's why I won't recommend the game for now: it's very short. I finished it in under 4 hours, and the game is relatively expensive for this length. What I would like to see is more levels. The game doesn't need more mechanics; it needs more variety, more combinations of those mechanics and themes. I would like to see a daily or weekly challenge map with hand-crafted challenges, support for mods, DLCs, and updates. The game has huge potential to be such a big hit if it gets a bit more work. I hope this review gets to the developers because I really want to see this game reach its full potential. If you can, please mark this review as helpful.EDIT 1: It took me less than 7 hours to complete 100% on medium, including the variants of each level. All that is left now is only 4 achievementsEDIT 2: All achievements in about 8hrsThank you!

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil is a strange game. On the surface, it appears to be a city-builder of sorts about terraforming. Then you realize it's a puzzle game about trying to discover how you can terraform in such a way that you can meet different restoration criteria. THEN, after you've reset once or twice, you realize it's actually a strategy game about planning out those puzzle elements in as efficient way as possible. This made Terra Nil a very captivating discovery process as I went from screwing around wasting resources to really understanding how to use my tools to make a very ugly area look very pretty. The more satisfying and relaxing element of watching your dirt ball grow into an ecosystem feels earned and all the better for it.The game is split into several biomes and each of the areas function almost entirely differently, so you get this whole discovery loop about 4-5 times before the credits roll. It's a great gameplay loop and it's also why it's  that Terra Nil has very little in the way of replay value. I still very much recommend the game for the first playthrough, but I'm begging the devs to add in a mode with randomized goals, layouts, and wildlife.(Note: After this review was posted, the game has been updated with a new biome and more post-game content added, which does help with the replayability of content.)

_childDocuments_.review: Not usually one to write reviews, however i have to say this one is an amazing game and a must get for really anyone.I personally like putting things in order and planning my own little empire (usually, as in Civ, age of Wonders, etc), or, in this case, rather the environment. I struggle with ADHD a little bit and its hard for me to relax. This game is so incredibly relaxing i have never seen anything like it, really helped to calm down and it was just all around fun and beautiful.I have now 100%ed the game, all achievements, about 20h of playtime that felt like they were just flying by. I played the entire game on medium difficulty and was only really challenged in 2 levels. I really hope the game gets more content (playing after the first major content update) because the different skill sets and intricacies of the individual biomes are fun to figure out. The bonus goals and planning for each animal with the tools you are given, differing for each level, is just so fun.I love this games message. It is all about environmentalism, but not just mindless at that, it implants the idea of recycling as well. I dont know what to say tbh. Its just a well rounded concept and execution.Its been a while since i played a game that made me feel so good while having fun on the way there. 100% recommend if you are curious, support the devs so there will be more content soon!

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who has not played the game for at least 10 hours did not play it all the way through. It isn't any more repetitive than any game out there. People grumble about the price, but I got to my $1 per hour golden rule, which is a lot more than I can say than a certain colony simulator I bought recently for the same amount of money. Their sound design was ♥♥♥♥, Terra Nil's sound design is amazing. Their complexity was much higher, and thats what prevented me from getting a refund, I had to play a tutorial for 8 hours just to find out how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ their game is. Terra Nil was incredible from the start, and I still haven't 100% completed the game, and it's the first game in a long time that I actually want to 100% on every difficulty. I was so excited for this game, I bought my sister a copy, and she rarely plays video games, and I know it's the sort of thing she would absolutely love. This game is not too short for it's money, kids these days want everything to be free *cough* g00gle evil cyber dystopian overlords. When you look at how many people it took to credit the game, it probably needed to pay everyone involved. _childDocuments_.review: From the creators of  whose high-octane over-the-top pixelly violence and general lack of respects for goon and mook lives are very reminiscent of the same 90'es action flicks they summon through their palette of gruff manly-man heroes weaponized to the utmost degree, comes what is probably the chillest game of the century in the form of an ecological preservation building game.To be precise, Terra Nil is a  - and by that I mean that everything you create, you will eventually have to remove. The goal of the game is deceptively simple: you enter a desolate place, and you must leave it as bountiful and luxuriant as you can, aided in that regard with wonderful gadgets and technologies that we may be in dire needs of soon if trends continue. I'll try to be as apolitical as possible, but all art forms are anchored in their environment, and society is by nature political.[/rant]Looping back to the genre, Terra Nil is the first of its kind (that I know of, at least). Progression is not innately linked to your builds, which is what makes it work after all, but it's also a line that is best treaded carefully. While not hard, the levels are a bit more puzzle-y than they appear; a feat all the more impressive considering they are randomly generated each time.Despite that, the game falls a bit on the short side. At time of writing there are only 4 main environments (with 4 'alternate' environments unlocking once the 4 main are 'fixed'). The interplay of mechanics is interesting, but also perhaps a bit... simplistic? It works very well for game elements, anyways, so that goal is filled.Progression feels like a breeze, which is unfortunate considering the "campaign" is so short, yet at the same time the gameplay loop is best approached in small bites. I haven't finished the main storyline yet because I want to savour it. It really is a cozy and nice game for when you want to feel good after a long day at work, perhaps not for everyone as there is a reflection element, but it is nice to fix things rather than break them, for once.All in all a hidden gem of a game, a small but very polished experience allowing you to 'play god' without being an avatar of destruction this time.

_childDocuments_.review: Full video review here: Terra Nil is an extremely relaxing and enjoyable "reverse city builder"/"environment restoration" strategy/puzzle game. There are three difficulty modes to accommodate all play styles, from those who want to casually figure things out to those who want a challenge that will keep you on your toes.The game mechanics are easy to understand but hard to master. The easy difficulty "Gardener" provides a good tutorial that will teach you the basics, but even on the easy mode I do think there is a bit of trial and error to figure things out (in a good way). The maps are procedurally generated, so every time you start/restart you get to play on a new terrain with new challenges. The art style is really beautiful and well done, and the soundtrack is mellow, blends well with the ambient game sounds, and isn't repetitive.I touch on this part a bit more in my video review, but I appreciate the developers' philosophy regarding the game, and I love that they are donating a portion of the profits to the Endangered Wildlife Trust.This game is 100% worth purchasing for both casual/cozy gamers and those that seek out tough strategy games!Disclaimer: I received a game code free from thee publishers for review purposes, but I played the demo a year ago and sought out this game myself!

_childDocuments_.review: I haven’t done a review in a long time. But with this I wanted to give it a shot again.Short 1-5 Star Rating system:Gameplay ***Story**Music****Graphics****New Player friendly*****Complexity****Overall****The Game is written word, but it is not necessary to read a lot if you just want to start.The Music is inviting from the beginning very calmingly.You can expect a Puzzle game like the Game Dorfromantik but very more intuitive.If you like reclaim and renaturing and learn how eco-systems work, while you are calming down from work with calm music and nice Artwork graphics, this is your Game!Gameplay is easy. The first 2 Levels are very nice, and the difficulty starts getting higher at level 3 with Vulcanic activity. But it was a good feeling to restart and gain some more Knowledge.The Story is poor. I remember the Story from Anno 2070 where the ecology was hit hard.To read the small input in the books makes a good effort to give context.The Music is very nice and seems to adjust slowly to changes you make on the map. BUT it’s always calm- maybe this will change later in the game, but I doubt it.Graphics is super nice and you should check out the pages of the book to see the super cool drawings! The Style is nice and a sweet touch.The Game is New Player friendly even if you don’t read the text you can always watch the small video tutorial if you stay on a building button. It is relatively self-explanatory. 5 Stars for the easy Playability and giving new players a hand.Complexity is also 4 * because it can get difficult at some time. Planning ahead will spare you a restart of levels and to get a perfect result you need to plan far ahead.Overall this will get a 4* Rating because it is super relaxing for the genre and is challenging from time to time. 1 Star is missing because it feels there is Story missing or at least some background for the Ship and buildings and the whole quest in itself. Leave a Comment or reaction and thank you. I will try to write a German review as well.

_childDocuments_.review: As is, the game is very well crafted and challenging. Depending on the map seed you find some maps are way easier than others. At full price it is a little on the pricier end, as the "story mode" is very short, but because of the random nature of the game the different biomes it does have some replay value. I wouldn’t classify it as a city builder as it really feels more of a puzzle game to me. You first put up drones and buildings to restore the map, then once your objectives are in place, you tear down and recycle your stuff and move on to the next map. One thing that completely puzzles me is that the map cannot be rotated. Depending on the map, some buildings can be hidden or determining if your hill will form a river can be completely obstructed on the height of the tile. Many isometric builders allow the player to rotate the map to mitigate this issue and is absent in this game. I think this game would benefit from additional DLC drops as I can totally see a desert biome being super hard and interesting. Larger maps could also provide more of a challenge too. For sure would recommend on sale, but at the MSRP it’s a little steep while I completed the base story in about 9 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: The company advertised Terra Nil as "reverse city builder." I came into the game with expectations of endless hours of relaxing biome building game-play. This isn't that, and It's turned into a short and sweet puzzle game. It's not bad, but I can't recommend this game, because it's not what was originally advertised. Do you like puzzles? Buy this game. Do you like relaxing music? Buy this game. Do you like pixel style artwork? Buy this game. Do you like city builders? Don't buy this game. At the end of the day, I'm glad I purchased the game to support the developer's intentions, I just think the video game community has strict standards about how much content a gamer should get for $25. _childDocuments_.review: I'm always on the lookout for environmental restoration games. Terra Nil is a refreshing entry in the emerging ecology genre. Fun and moderately challenging but a little clunky at times. The different biomes, animals, and plants are cute and it feels good to restore the landscape. Like many others I think the game is currently (3/29/23) lacking content. I found myself wishing there was more to the game such as more diversity, maps, and challenges. Also, the instantaneousness of restoration felt odd to me. It seemed like it should take a while, a progression, or as they say in ecological restoration circles: a succession. Forests and grasslands just popping up instantly felt weird.Anyway, I'm glad the game is out there. Everyone should play it!

_childDocuments_.review: I vividly remember playing Terra Nil's alpha when it first released a few years ago. Even then it was an impressive concept, well executed with much potential. The time really flew by and now here it is, all grown up! I'm very happy with how the finished game came out. While the polish lacks occasionally- a small visual bug here, a heavy performance drop there- the wider experience feels near flawless and is a joy to play. The transition from the original detailed pixel art style to the new vibrant 3D models was also handled very well. I do miss the pixel art and would love to see the full game in that style, but I understand why the change was made and love the new style regardless. In hindsight, my only hesitancy is that I can't help but think the concept is so good that the surface has barely been scratched. As "good enough" as Terra Nil is, it does slightly border on repetitiveness or shallowness at times and more content, depth, and variety would go a long way towards bridging that microcosmic gap between excellence and perfection. I'm really hoping the bar continues to be raised for this budding genre, either through a sequel or elsewhere. In the meantime, though, I am perfectly satisfied with the initial success. Well done devs!

_childDocuments_.review: From a "price to game hours" standpoint this is obviously a huge fail. But this one still gets an upvote for me. Let me tell you why:I value quality above all else in games. I understand that smaller studios have a lower budget and can't deliver always on everything. But sometimes they can craft their game in such a clean and ingenious way that it lends to perfection. Dorfromantic & Islanders are games that have this handiwork in them. As many others have compared, Terra Nil misses in places where those games succeed. It very much copies the sort of 'optimizing puzzle game' game play style with the resource & cost & placement-range-thing. In that i agree, Terra Nil doesn't have the depth.But Terra Nil has a few other very special things. Once you get the third map you realize that you aren't optimizing for points anymore, but minimizing your cleanup process. This and other feelings of discovery and immersion are something that the other puzzle games don't provide.Terra Nil brings with it wonder and emotion where it leaves behind complexity & contrivity.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent little game,  EDIT: They patched it! Thanks devs!I started playing this game originally for an Environmental Ethics class, I thought this would be a great game to make a report on and I wasn't wrong. I appreciate the challenge of each level, even the very first area I had to restart at least once. I've seen a few reviews saying they wish there was a way to move buildings once you placed them and it makes it very easy to screw up, but I actually really like that. It makes you put thought into where you place things and take a lot of consideration into how you arrange your structures.I was a little worried at the start after watching the trailer, I think I assumed the game would be pretty one-note or fairly simple for a strategy game, but I was never so happy to be wrong. I think the amount of leaves (energy, eco-power, whatever your little currency is) given to the player on the mid level is perfect. One thing I had to learn was to stop trying to put grass on each little block, focus on just spreading as much grass as possible. This was something the completionist in me hated at first, before I realized you can get to those pesky little spare blocks once you start adjusting the humidity/temperature to allow it to rain. What a neat system![SPOILERS]Towards the end it starts to really give you a challenge, on one of the final areas, after the quake and the resurfacing of the radioactive material, I had depleted my leaves down to 50 several times, cutting it really close, but founds ways to build my way back and continue cleansing the radioactive material. It was such a good feeling, being able to escape from nearly getting a game over.[END OF SPOILERS]I love the music, it makes me think of Breath of the Wild sometimes, I mean that in the most positive way. Usually I have a podcast on while I play strategy games like this, but this was one game in particular I preferred to just fully immerse myself into.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil was near the top of my wishlist from the minute I played the demo in 2022. The game is basically a reverse city builder where instead of building a thriving city you must revitalize four different biomes by cleansing the toxins from the land and water then you must remove all the buildings you placed to complete each zone.The game has four biomes which are each pretty unique and upon completing them you'll unlock one variation for each for a total of eight maps to play. I finished the first four in about five hours and I expect the next four would be faster since I now I have a firm understanding of how the systems within the game work.While I do recommend the game the price is too high for the amount of time you'll be getting out of it. I recommend wishlisting it and waiting for a sale. A fair price for what the game has to offer right now is $10-15 although there is an indication more content will be added in the future but it's not clear if that will be free or paid DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: While the idea is nice (when you don't think about it too much) the gameplay is a bit slow.Then again to a certain degree that might be the appeal.Game mechanics do not get explained but need to be discovered - which is at times annoying.Humidity/Warmth do not have an realistic effect on the environment which is sad since there would be so much more to discover if the simulation would be better.By now a lot of bugs got fixed and so recently it ran pretty stable.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that this developer created both this incredibly peaceful and satisfying game, and also the chaos filled BroForce, astonishes me.I seriously needed this game at the time, it is incredibly peaceful relaxing, yet still engaging to not bore you. 10/10 would recommend if you're looking for a fun little strategy game to unwind after work!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: The Good. This is an easy game to waste hours on. The Concept of repairing or healing the worlds is nice. It is not difficult.  The Bad. The graphics could use a bit of an upgrade by modern standards. The game needs slightly more depth to increase replay value. Skins for rewards might be a low impact option for this.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This ecological strategy/building game really sucked me in. You're tasked with cleaning up a variety of environments, controlling pollution and radiation, managing the climate, and balancing various biomes. Complexity gradually ramps up as numerous deep systems interact. Once certain environmental goals have been met, you construct self-recycling infrastructure to remove all your buildings, leaving only the natural environment behind. This is a breathtakingly innovative take on the genre, and I highly recommend checking it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: So far,  loving this game.  Premise is that you are required to restore a barren wasteland.  Creating stable environments and reintroducing wildlife. Artwork is great. Sounds are soothing. There are issues with the handbook not matching the situation in the second maps of the four continents but using a little logic and trial and error was able to have success. All considered, a very satisfying game.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil is an environmental strategy game and an amazing educational tool about ecological reclamation. Using advanced eco-technology, you are charged with transforming a barren wasteland into a thriving, balanced ecosystem with a variety of flora and fauna. The ultimate goal is to leave no trace of yourself when it's time to pack up and move on.The hand-painted environments, music and atmospheric ambient soundscape lend themselves to making Terra Nil an incredibly pleasant and relaxing experience. I enjoy how the game demonstrates the finicky nature of an ecosystem when different forces such as humidity or temperature rise and fall. I wish the game would further exemplify these themes as it would introduce a greater challenge than resource management alone.I heavily encourage purchasing this game and experiencing its optimistic message about how conscious change can have a positive impact on the environment. In addition, 8% of all profit from Steam is donated to the Endangered Wildlife Trust, a South African based conservation organization whose core work involves the conservation of threatened species and ecosystems.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous game, cool concept. They're currently working on revamping the Animal Reintroduction phase, which is a good change - they currently have a beta out for the new procedure. There's a wide range of difficulties to choose from, from Zen Mode (no resources) to Environmental Engineer (increased costs and decreased starting resources). I personally find it very replayable, but I could see how others don't.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly charming and relaxing game.  Can't recommend highly enough.  I initially fell in love with this game's demo when I played it during a Steam Next Fest some odd years ago.  So happy to see it finally released!Would absolutely love to see this game get more content with new scenarios, or biomes like deserts.I can see myself sinking in dozens of hours playing these levels to unwind after a rough day.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is a simple, straightforward "Reverse city builder" that allows players to rebuild environments while helping people to relax.  I liked this game because of its simplicity and ease of use, but, the game does feel a little short as if there should be more content, it may be the developers may release DLC in the future or make expansions for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: It's quick, but very zen.  It's deceptively simple, appearing at first to just be a "color the land green" simulator.  But as you go on, it clicks that you're setting up the next phase where you try to accomplish goals and then finally the last phase where you need to remove all the pieces you set up.  The flow encourages you to be thoughtful in where you place things and plan ahead that I think beautifully ties into the theme of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Fun relaxing puzzle game, 100%ed it, each level adding something different to deal with, losing isn't a big deal as restarting and getting back to where you are is easy enough, plus you can just restart the stage of map you are on instead of restarting from the very beginning.  There are 4 level (Temperate, Polar, Tropical, and Continental) and once you beat those it unlocks a varied version of each to play.  Hope to see some more levels/planets(?) or possibly steam workshop support so you can make your own.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: After the demo and then the first level, I was really loving this game. And I really wanted to love the rest too, but once I moved on it dawned on me that the "campaign" really isn't one. There is no progression here, other than the artificial percentage of terraforming, and the amount of landmass available to terraform on the planet is apparently about 2 square miles or so.The tech is locked to each map specifically, so there is no unlocking of tech which you can bring along, the maps have a static and separate (but partially overlapping) tech tree. You get a new procedurally generated map everytime you play a biome type, but forget about learning how to solve a problem on map 1 to get creative on map 3. You get to solve the same problem in exactly the same way, by placing the same buildings in slightly different places, but really, if you've done one level, there is no replayability there.There are map variations, which means that the static set pieces move from being 4 biomes to 4*2 biome/approach combinations. And, no overlap. No grassland with a bit more of a djungle in a corner. No tundra/grassland combinations that requires skills or tech unlocked from the other maps. No interactions between the different animals, they basically just show up and walk around the map making it prettier.It really is a pretty title, and it conveys a lush feeling once you green up the map. But there is no gameplay here of significance. A walking simulator in the shape of a strategy game, but with none of the strategy, progression or satisfaction of solving new problems after the first playthrough of each map. If you are looking for super-casual and good-looking, this might be for you. If you want more than that, unfortunately, nothing to see here.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I truly cannot explain how much this game means to me. It's a brilliant puzzle game, the theme of ecological restoration is fantastic, the visuals are gorgeous, and the whole thing is very thoughtfully designed.I guess the best way to express my feelings on this game is that it is worth so much more to me than the $25 being charged, I've been buying copies for friends. I really want more games like this (and more DLC like Surviving the Aftermath's Rebirth) allowing you to restore devastated environments.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Have yet to beat the game, but needed to give this game its flowers asap.It's an incredible game to sit down and play when you've had a long stressful day. It is the definition of zen.You actually feel like you've done a good thing when you finish a level. Revitalizing desolate wastelands into lush, vibrant biomes full of life.Highly reccomend
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Well, waited quite a while for this game and in principle it is now just what it was in the preview version, only it is 4(+4) levels now.There is not a lot of content in this puzzle game (that's what it is) for 25Euros tbh, I do hope there will be more maps or an editor coming.I do like it even though I am not sure about the replayability. If you compare it to a simple game like Tetris, then Tetris had at least some high score to beat and benchmark yourself against. This one is just over and all you can thrive for is 100% in all levels.Then again, it let's you drift off into some satisfying and relaxing hours of a smooth game.If there is not more coming and keeping the relatively high price in mind, my thumb is down.If they add some stuff to improve longterm motivation, my thumb is up.Will keep it up for now and see where it will end.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun! and the music is super chill to boot. bonus to the fact some of the proceeds are going to plant actual trees. looking forward to additional content :)the undo button reminds me of chess.. once you take your hand of the piece, you can't take it back. part of this game's challenge is to either figure out how to fix your error, or to start over with new knowledge. It may be a short game, but it is super nice to play, brings me joy, and is totally worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for Terra Nil's release since I played the demo a few years back. Its incredibly relaxing and surprisingly complex if you bump up the difficulty. My one issue is by the time I finished each alternate level I was left wanting a little bit more. It certainly has a fair amount of replay value given the random gen maps but I do wish there were maybe 2-3 more zones. Nonetheless I still recommend this wholeheartedly.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: It's really "nice." It's pretty, relaxing, with a great premise. And although I didn't play too long, I was honestly a little bit bored. I was able to complete two games in my time before I asked for a refund. And I really felt like "well, I feel like I've gotten enough of that." I see there's a lot more stuff to construct and learn and stuff, but It's just not quite for me. It's super nice to see the whole map transform with what you're doing, but... After you "reclaim the wasteland," you need to recycle your machinery. Cool, sure, but After it's all said and done, my map looks like garbage, both times.That being said, I will 100% buy this when it's on sale. This is totally something to play when you need to relax, but still have your brain working.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Great game for anyone who wants to lay back and enjoy the ride. Beautiful landscapes and easy play-through. Need 10-20 min to get an idea and start playing. Even on the hardest level game is quite forgiving. Player can modify the parameters of the game to make it even harder if needed.Unfortunately the game only has 1 planet with 3 continents each with 4 maps. This adds to total of 12 maps only. Also game finishes on the map 8 not at the map 12 (although you can continue playing rest of the maps). Find this really dissappointing. So little content for so much money. I know there is DLC but 12 maps as a  full game with 1 planet only?
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute game. It's a little more structured and less open sandbox than I'd hoped, but it's still fun. There are 4 major biomes to repair. You have to complete all 4 of them to unlock secondary sites in each biome. The secondary sites are a little but more like a puzzle to solve. There aren't always the landscape features you want where you need them, so there's a little more creativity involved.That said, I've been playing for ~10 hours, and I've knocked out all 4 regular scenarios and 2 of the bonus sites (and that's with starting over a few times because I'm a perfectionist). I imagine it'll only take a few more hours to complete the last 2. After that, I'm not sure how much more I'll want to play because there doesn't seem to be too much other variety to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil is a sweet little game. It is a backwards city builder, or a city builder asking you to deconstruct your creation. That creation is the restoration of a wasteland to a fertile, diverse wilderness. A great concept, and with fabulous soundtrack and art, it makes for a very rewarding experience to look back at what you accomplish on each map. However, there are two issues with the game. There's no saving in the map you're playing. That is annoying but it leads to a bigger issue. The maps dont take long to complete. There's only 8 maps and 4 biomes (2 maps per biome). In total it's not going to get you more than a dozen hour of playtime, max. Combined with a high price point for the amount of game you're getting is a major drawback. I recommend you wait for  a sale, but it is still a good game.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite short. What you may think is just the tutorial, is actually the whole game. And there is no real strategy involved, because resources are abundant, so it is easy enough to complete the missions alongside all side quests in your first try. The objectives are very linear, you build the required stuff and then you're done.I enjoyed the game, but I am leaning on negative for lack of a neutral review rating, because it lacks depth and is not worth it at this price point.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: At first I came to restore a planet.Then I realised that Terra Nil is an inofficial title set in the Civilization world.The main clue that sparked my realisation was the radiated city.-------------------------------------Overall a fun, albeit short (Read: Not overstaying it's welcome and I want more) little puzzle/thinking game.Great for a quick gameplay session in between rage inducing multiplayer losses in other games.I particularly enjoy how openly the player can attempt and overcome each map, sharing screenshots with friends and watching others play is quite nice since it shows how differently people approach each map.It's a lot of fun to revisit maps to finish previously unearned optional missions or get that one more animal species into a perfect habitat.The game gives me the same kind of feeling when peacefully building up my islands in Anno or parks in Rollercoaster Tycoon.Definitely worth the money for some chill restorations. (Both the planet and my sanity)
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I dont have much Time in this game yet and due to work and real life things i dont know if thats gonna change soon. But I love it. Its amazing. In so many games have I cut down the last tree, used all the Stone on the map to build a great wall, hunted entire species into extermination and have done truly horrible things to get even the last little bit of coal mined (looking at you Frostpunk). And then, in comes, swinging, Terra Nil, the exact opposite of all that. You dont cut down trees, you plant them. You dont collect resources, you help "expand" them, by placing beehives, waterpumps, scrublandmakers and so on and so forth. And as you do well, you start seeing little amimals wandering around the map, which also have their unique desires and needs which you fulfil by.... creating more woods, flowerfields and wetlands. And when you are done on a map, you collect all the buildings you placed to achieve this in order to leave nature as pristine as it was before the first hairless monkey crawled down his tree. It makes you feel really good. When I completed the first level, and the Victory screen was me watching the amimals and nature I  restored, all animated with lots of love (I especially like the beavers and bears), I couldnt help but stare at the screen long enough with my mouth wide open to get an achievement. 10/10 would recommend to anyone who ever dreamed of making the world a better place. Very much also worth the full price, although  I did buy it with a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely little game. It's not the longest of games (finished 100% and all achievements in 9.5 hours), so bear that in mind if you're thinking of buying, but still well worth the price. The resource management is just enough that you need to be aware of it but not too much that it becomes loathsome. The artwork is lovely and the music is just right. It's addictive watching everything come together and going from a brown miserable block to a lush colourful wilderness full of life.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I heartily recommend this game. I was playing the demo years ago when that was released and I've always found it a game I come back to again and again when I want a relaxing puzzle builder game. It can be tricky but not in a stressful kind of way.The puzzles in this game are all related to how can you reclaim the current wasteland given the selected tools while not running out of your building resource. That resource is there more to increase the puzzle aspect rather than increase any sort of stress. There's no time limit for the map you're on and you can restart either the entire map or the current phase, which is very forgiving.Each map provides a different set of challenges to overcome and the challenge difficult increases at a very friendly pace. The first map introduces you to basic game concepts while providing enough of a challenge to pull you in, while the final maps take some thinking and knowledge of existing mechanics to overcome.And in the end, you get to enjoy the fact that you're restoring a planet. Sometimes it's nice to take a break from beating back waves of zombies or hordes of enemies and build something nice. And having just 100% the entire map, I'm super happy with it. And I"ll keep coming back to the game in the future for those relaxing moments when I need them.So if you want something fun, somewhat challenging, but not stressful, go ahead and pick this up and enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty poor performance no matter how you change the settings despite the relatively small map size, low framerate led to a pathfinding error for the recycling boat on the second map I played and couldn't finish the level. Refunded. Unfriendly UX decisions, I've seen the happiest deers bears and beavers dozens of times and not intentionally once. Not difficult to win even on highest custom difficulty, once you get rainfall you can do fire cycles constantly with no temperature or humidity change. It's cool that fire is useful but nobody else has seemed to notice. If you've watched other people play this game and think you can do better, you're right. Not really doing anything more than painting tiles. A reverse puzzle game!Under the fake enviromental aesthetic of watering perfectly short green grass is a game with a serious misunderstanding of it's own message, celebrating humanity's potential to industrially create as easily as it destroys, indefinitely. Dark Solarpunk AF.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I know this game worried people at first launch about the amount of content for the price. But after the Vita Nova update nearly doubling the amount of levels to complete in this game, the game length now is worthy of it's price.With that being said, Terra Nil is a beautiful game. With each level playing out in a similar way, but giving you new tools to circumvent each unique area. Every level feels different, and it's exciting seeing what new curve-balls the game throws at you as you progress through the 4 different biomes.The sound design is my favorite aspect of the game. The music is gentle and unobtrusive, and the sounds all of the different machines make gives an extra oomph to the impact you are having in the wasteland. And by far, the best part of each level is correcting the climate and achieving the first rainfall. I get chills as the thunder rolls in and all the parts of the wasteland that I hadn't been able to hit yet turn green as the most calming sound nature can produce rolls over and brings out the lush environment that you were working for. It's breathtaking every single time.If you passed over this game on launch, please give it a try now. It is absolutely worth your time, and is a great game to jump into if you just need a peaceful evening.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: It was all fun and games until it started bugging. Was unable to make it through the tutorial. Read some other people were having the exact same problem. Ultimately for a game that's supposed to just be a relaxing one-off it required an annoying amount of work to get it to run smoothly. Ultimately I wouldn't recommend, especially given it's price.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: If you love strategy games, have a love of animals and nature, and want to do your part in saving the planet (albeit in a fictional planet setting), then Terra Nil will be the ideal game for you. I loved the game right from playing the demo ages ago, the concept is a simple one: Restore life on a planet that has been destroyed by humans. The execution is wonderful, the graphics are beautiful and the sound design will put you in the right mindset to get your hands dirty. You must power up, clean up, create habits, influence the weather, encourage animals back and then leave no trace of your intervention. It is one of the best environmentally aware games I have played and it is so addictive. I have loved every minute of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun relaxing little game. Music fits the vibe perfectly, art style is great, the sound design of everything is really satisfying. _childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic.  It's calming, challenging in places, and beautiful.  Reclaiming the 4 ecosystems is very engaging and in some missions, unforgiving. _childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: It is a beautiful little game that is a very relaxing city builder. To 100% the game took me just 10 hours, but I enjoyed every second of it. There are an infinite number of maps you could do, but it all boils down to 4 biomes. The real beauty of this is designing your own little slice of life heaven.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil is relaxing and fun. It has a chill soundtrack and an alright gameplay loop, and the focus on restoring nature is a nice contrast to most games' focus on either dominating nature or just killing things. Overall, I give it a 3/5 "solid if you're really into that kind of thing." Unfortunately I can't recommend it, because it has too many bugs. It's quite the mess. I've played 11 hours so far and finally got too sick of it. I'm going to wait to play more until a bugfix update comes out. Here's the ones I can remember off the top of my head:* Animal detector sometimes permanently fails to detect animals, instead giving a weird error message about the state of the map having changed. I haven't found any workaround; once the error appears, those animals are undetectable for the remainder of the mission.* Lowering and raising the temperature on the snow map will make it snow or melt, but only once; after that, it doesn't matter what you do to the temperature, you're stuck with the permanent snow.* Newly-built dredgers don't connect to existing monorail nodes, even if they're in range.* Clicking "undo" after creating the bamboo structure will remove the bamboo forest, but won't remove the structure, meaning the structure is useless for the rest of the mission.* The boat sometimes refuses to traverse pound locks* Snow can fall next to solar amplifier if the solar amplifier was built on snowy ground after it had already started snowing.There's also some QOL and game-design decisions that are annoying.* Rain and snow are far too powerful. The whole early game becomes a one-dimensional race to get to those weather conditions, because they give you SO MUCH money and eliminate the need for toxic scrubbers/irrigators.* Far too few hotkeys. 1234 for the different structure panels aren't enough; I want to be able to choose specific buildings  with the keyboard.* You can't save and quit halfway through a mission. When you relaunch the game, you have to start the mission over.* The third gameplay phase (recycling) isn't challenging, because it gives you far too much money. It's mostly just annoying. The recycling drone is really slow and has weird artificial limits on what they can recycle. I've had to make a Turbine, Excavator (which blew a hole in my landscaping), Calcifier, and lone monorail node just so my FLYING drone can be commanded to recycle the Silo that I had already built.* Insufficient explanation is sometimes given to why certain actions are disallowed. I had to Google why I couldn't burn grass with the Solar Amplifier, and Google again to find out that it can burn the scrub resulting from the Humidity Pylon. This kind of head-scratching "why can't I do this?" confusion happened to me a bunch of times. I'm sure it was covered in the tutorial at some point, but it's a lot of tutorial, and moment-to-moment tooltips and warnings should be given.Finally, It feels more like a $10 game than a $25 one. The campaign is only about 12-15 hours long (I've almost completed the entire thing in 11 hours without much effort nor a single loss), and the gameplay loop is too long, buggy, and irritating to want to repeat very many times.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: What i can say after playing this game is : Accomplishment after you fix the environment.the good :+ fun & relaxing type of game,+ kinda puzzle type game imo,+ challenging in each map with 4 region 'forest, tropical, antartic, & urban' each with 2 scenario (you got 8 map scenarios in total).the bad :- need new map / scenarios / region (like savannah region or rain forest region or maybe desert region),- need a bigger map size imo,- need something to add for a longer playtime and re-playconclusion : great game for a break after industrial-type of game. don't worry about the bad because the dev is on a break after the first launch and already planning to give update / DLC to the game. i give 8.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable and calm game about restoring ecosystems. There are some slight puzzle mechanics that are easy to understand and play directly into the restoration goals of the game. It took me about 12 hours to 100% the game in its current version and that was after replaying some levels after an achievement update. _childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the concept of the game a lot. The way the game forces the player to collect every bit of artificial building from the map before it allows the player to continue to the next map is really fitting. This game has something to tell and it tells it with everything: visuals, music, game mechanics. I consider this game an art piece.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game, I think the concept is great, and I appreciate the environmental goals behind it. The issue is that there just isn't $25 worth of content here. I have 7 hours played, but realistically that's only ~4, since I got distracted by work for a few hours. Considering the first level was the Demo, that only really leaves 3 new levels, and then 4 variations on the original levels. I don't expect to be paying $3 an hour for a game, considering the great value proposition that other games offer. Unfortunately, it's just long enough to get you past the 2 hour refund window, or I think I would have refunded this and picked it up on sale down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT:Took me roughly 8 hours to complete the maps on normal difficulty.And, once you do, more missions unlock and there's also hard mode.I haven't started the extra missions or hard difficulty yet as I write this.I still think full price is well worth it if you enjoy puzzle/strategy games with no stress.ORIGINAL:It's a very relaxing game. It's by definition a strategy game but I think of it more like a puzzle.The game feels polished and the music, sound effects and graphics are all great. I've had zero issues so far.It is not a very complex or difficult game from what I've seen. I imagine the hard difficulty will provide a challenge. Normal, on the other hand, is pretty chill. I don't understand some peoples beef with the recycling.. _childDocuments_.review: Summary: 6.5/10Terra Nil is a game with a beautiful premise, a puzzle design and a lack of polish on the last edges. Overall it is a beautiful game for a relaxed 10 hour completionist playthrough for the decent puzzle and strategy player and likely 20+ for others.Its rather short campaign and four basic puzzle types ultimately do not give it any longevity. A sandbox version with random mixed biomes or a global map with all together with biome borders and temperature regions may have helped here. Like this the game is pretty much done for all but the dedicated gardeners after one full playthrough.A few unsightly bugs (the energy grid of the 4th and 8th map leave yellow borders permanently on the map until reloaded, ruining screenshots) still remain.Gameplay: 7/10The economic reconstruction, be it zen or with resource management, is the games greatest aspect, alongside the little deeds to complete and the biome creation. Alas the optional goals are not exclusive, so a map will still "snow" even if the -5°C are now 35°C and the former requirements are gone. It's a temporary goal to unlock some map flavor. The only major effects are "rain" or "snow" as they help clean the map.The greatest weakness of the game is the artificial tedium of "cleaning up". Clearly there was no problem building the solar collector with zero infrastructure, but removing it takes major logistical hoop jumping to get a "insert recycling puzzle item" there to finally remove it. The most annoying of these are the water drone and the railroad, especially due to the time it takes to deconstruct the railroad as well. This has made people quit (DDRJake etc.) and will ruin those fun that came for the "city-builder" and nature aspect. It feels bad. An additional busy work with little puzzle and more logistic. If this is not up your ally, this game is not for you. Sound & Audio: 7/10Most sounds are well chosen and the gentle music works for the 10-20 hours the game takes to complete. It does get repetitive later on. Some noises like the recycler and the dismantler are horrible and artificial and you will hear them alot. This makes the already annoying dismantlement phase that much worse and compounds a problem the game made for itself. If this was a good choice remains to be seen.Replayability: 5/10Maps have little variety and the SAME rules. The seed changes only the layout. There are no alternative biomes or puzzles to complete, no new animals to try to accomodate with the right mix. There are no new secondary goals, even in secondary regional maps and they aren't exclusionary anyway. There are secondary maps per region (which I count to completion though) and those alter the base riddle to get started (e.g. melting snow with solar collectors instead of lava geysers in the polar fjord). That is all they do. For those that want a short puzzle game with a beautiful result - unless the cleanup minigame forced you to ruin it by digging dirty trenches or causing seismic explosions or freezing the oceans - it will be fine. For those wanting something to really sink their time into, consider this an early intro and hope for DLC. A LOT of DLC for a fair price.

_childDocuments_.review: It's strange. I really like the concept of this game, and I thought the demo showed a lot of promise. However, in its current form, I'm not really sure I can recommend it.Terra Nil markets itself as something of a city builder--I would probably place it more in the category of puzzler. Judging it from that perspective, it's...somewhat average. You shuffle around the board placing a few buildings here and there with ostensibly limited resources to fulfill a few objectives in relatively short maps. Which is fine--but the core gameplay loop doesn't actually have as many compelling variations as I would like. The main puzzles are fairly easy, you go through four levels and you're never really pressured by your "limited" resources to make tradeoffs or meaningful decisions, so you wind up just checking boxes to get the job done. There aren't really any execution problems there, either, meaning the "puzzle" aspect is a bit lacking.So, do the "postgame" puzzles fix what is, essentially, a difficulty problem?I would say not. Sure, they require the player to figure out a few minor tricks to proceed--but everything can be found by poking around at the UI for a few minutes. You don't really need to experiment as much as you need to be observant, as everything is otherwise told to you. Theoretically your resources are pushed a bit more, but in my experience, it wasn't substantial (I think I ended those maps with some ~500 less currency than the main ones, which totals up to maybe 5 buildings. When your resource pool ends with you finishing a map with 2000-3000 currency in excess though, it barely matters).Now, all of that said, it's a fairly easy puzzler game. But the dioramas you create are visually appealing, and the game does have a some zen-like qualities to it. But it's not really what I was hoping to find on the harder difficulties it offered. It doesn't offer quite the same replayability that some of the other, zen-like puzzlers I've played do (Dorfromantik is a good, recent comparison actually. The "resource" you manage there being tiles, and although there are fewer options, technically, it still fulfills the task of creating a pleasant world. And it costs half as much!).Anyway, as I said. I'd like to like the game, but I'm just not sure it's something I'd recommend picking up. Certainly not full price, for the lower-difficulty puzzler content you get.

_childDocuments_.review: I was playing this through my shared Family Library as my partner had bought it, and I love it so much that I bought my own copy just so I could leave a positive review. The idea of turning wastelands into beautifully realised, lush, living environments appealed to me from the outset far more than any city building or farming sort of simulator, and it's such a great game to spend a few minutes on here and there just to de-stress and chill out with making things grow and finding just the right way to restore things to make all the fauna happy.Having played it prior to buying my own copy, I already have all the achievements, but I'm going to start a new profile and rebuild everything over from scratch. I love everything from the visuals to the music to the sense of satisfaction from lining up the irrigators just right for maximum plant growth. _childDocuments_.review: Have been following this game for a while now, and I feel great about this game. One thing that really puts the cherry on top is the music and the sound design. The music reacts to the environment, becoming increasingly more "hopeful" as you progress through the restoration process. The sound of the animals returning and the wind blowing through the lush forest you created is nothing less than extremely soothing to the ear.One of the reason I decided to purchase Terra Nil, is the limited time I often have to play video games I enjoy these days. My sessions tend to be frequent, yet unfortunately short. Terra Nil is really great in this sense, as it is a perfect game to just boot up and play when you feel like it. It doesn't require half an hour to get into, and is something which is easy to just play after work or school. Of course you can play for prolonged periods of time, too!The graphics are beyond stunning. There were a couple performance issues I found in regard to the demo, however these all seem to have been fixed, and the game runs smoother than ever now.
