_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil is very satisfying and generally relaxing to play. The graphics are nice, and it is very satisfying to watch a large stretch of wasteland bloom when you fill a riverbed. The downside is that the content is  limited. There are 4 regions and an alternate map for each region that becomes available after finishing the main regions, and there are three difficulty levels. At only 32 hours I have played through and completed all regions on all difficulties.  It would be great if there were more regions/biomes, or if there were an option for different sizes of map. Or even a "random map" option that would generate a different set of biomes and equipment each time. Or better yet, a map that is a whole world with many different biomes and challenges.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly what I was looking forA chill and relaxing game that at first feels like child's play, but its mechanics keep geeting more complicated. Nothing too difficult though, just a bit of planning ahead. Add to that the "bonus" maps with more challenging scenarios, and it has you hooked for a good amount of time.In terms of visuals and soundtrack the game is gorgeous, you can tell that the devs poured a lot of love and time into every detail. It's been the first game in a while where the post-game replay is something enjoyable.Haven't played a lot to give an opinion on replay value, but since the maps are proceedualy generated, I'd bet you can go through several runs.Definitely enjoyed it and wholeheartedly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely chill world builder. Three difficulty levels to keep me challenged. Took me about 6 hours to finish the "campaign" of three main maps, and I'm still working through the "alternate" 3 maps that are more challenging. I'm hoping for some more content in the form of a few more maps and buildings. Loved the demo and I'm not disappointed in the full release.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Simple and short game about restoring environment without leaving a trace of former damage and the restoration process. The base maps are somewhat easy, while their advanced maps can be very tight budget-wise - sometimes going back 1 step is not enough. Overall I would recommend the game, albeit some FLC content would be very welcome - you could probably finish it to 100% in 2 evenings.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BUY AT FULL PRICE. This game only has about 10 hours worth of content. Game has so much potential and is very fun, but like i said... i played everything to 100% complete (including optional goals) and spent a total of 14 hours on the game... i progressed slow and took my time while playing and still finished it in two sittings. If you can get this game discounted its def a fun relaxing puzzle type game. However, for $25, i shouldnt be completing the game in less than 2 sittings... Could add endless procedurally generated maps for little to no extra effort. I'm not going to refund this game because at the very least, 8% of the cost to buy this game goes to planting trees IRL, so i will support that 100%. Otherwise, i don't recommend this game unless you have $25 extra to burn in your pocket and want about a days worth of entertainment.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: very relaxing puzzle-ish game with satisfying mechanics to play around withthough the price is a bit steep for the lack of replayability and content, the current content are all well thought out with great consideration and effort put forth.there's 4 maps(levels) currently, each with their own unique challange and 4 alternate of the 4 maps mentioned with slightly more challenge. the difficulty isn't mind boggling but also not a breezethe art style is very tasteful and it is satisfying to appreciate the nature you've restored at the end of each level. if you still think the price is too much, wishlist it and hold until a sale, it is a good 4-5 hours of fun (additional if you want to 100% the game but i don't really see why would you)
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely wonderful and probably the most charming and heartwarming game this year. I wouldn't necessarily use the "reverse city builder" title that most publications have been giving it, its more of a puzzle game but no matter what you call it, the game is tremendously fun. There is a very solid core game play loop with a variety of challenges. The only thing I wish for is a little more variety in terrain generation.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: "Terra Nil"? More like Terra Chill. This is the most relaxing game I've ever played and definitely one of the most satisfying.I will say some of the mechanics are a little frustrating and feel unnecessarily restrictive for no reason other than to make you think a few steps ahead. Sometimes those restrictions mean that if you get a bad map generation, you will have a really hard time. I got a archipelago map that I'm pretty sure was impossible due to the cliffs being too far apart for the sun shades. As long as you are thinking of things like that before settling on a map, you're fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: The game is exactly what I expected. A small game where you have to restore ecosystems in barren regions of a world based on real natural environments using methods likely to be used in our current world to achieve your goal and then leave after erasing every trace of your presence. The visuals are charming, every step of the game is clear, the environments are well chosen. Also, it's a very soothing game, you won't be stressed with deadlines, mandatory timed objectives or recurring catastrophes. However, the game is very short. It took me a few hours to complete it 100%. I would really love to see a bigger game with more environments and possibilities based on same principle. Overall a really nice little game, I really enjoyed playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I love Terra Nil. I love Terra Nil so much. I spent many hours replaying the demo and I'm going to spend so many more hours playing the full version. This game is a "city builder" in genre only; there are buildings you must place to develop the land around them, and you have to think strategically about where to place those buildings (because it will have consequences later when you recycle them), but that's it. Instead of building a city, the land has already been ruined, and we're bringing nature back to these barren wastes.You start off in the temperate region (which was featured in the demo), which is sort of a middle ground to get you situated with the controls and objectives, but once you've restored the wildlife there you're off to the tropical, polar, and continental regions. Each region has unique mechanics, wildlife, and resources to keep track of. Maps are procedurally generated, so no two sessions in a particular region will be the same unless you specify exact "coordinates" (basically a map seed) to travel to.The goals in each region are to restore the basic terrain from the wasteland, then develop more complex areas such as forests and wetlands, then survey the landscape for fauna, and finally recycle your buildings and depart the map. Where this gets tricky are with the fauna and recycling. Fauna only appear if certain conditions are met; in the temperate zone, for example, you have to induce a wildfire to create forests, which is simple enough, but bears will only appear in a forest that is on a hill and has a beehive in it. Not all animals are so complex as this, but it's something you may need to plan for in advance. You have to recycle all of your buildings in order to depart the map, but to do so, you must use recycling drones that travel on water with a limited radius to dismantle buildings. This means you have to either be careful about your placements from the start, or devise a strategy to get out of the corner; one such method is by re-destroying a piece of the landscape to create a new riverbed. It all gets really interesting and makes you consider a few different strategies to accomplish the mission.I can understand the feeling that there isn't enough content for the $25 price point. What I described above is basically the gameplay loop that you'll go through each and every time, and after a couple of hours you've pretty much seen all there is to see. That being said, the charm in this game's animations, the message it sends, the unique strategy gameplay elements, the fact that I can sit back after completing the map and just watch nature continue on... this is probably the most relaxing strategy game I've ever played, and those aren't words that are supposed to go together. Not to mention, a part of every Steam sale of this game goes directly to the Endangered Wildlife Trust in South Africa. It's awesome to see a game like this being used to support charities doing this incredibly important work in real life.Before writing this review, I was watching a map that I had finished, and while I was watching, the "Goldilocks" achievement had suddenly popped. It requires that you have three bears in forests at least 10 tiles apart. I was confused, because I had only successfully surveyed for two bears, but while I was watching, another forest I had developed was healing further and allowed a natural bear spawn. Even if that is a bug, I choose not to believe that. The notion that I had created a small forest that was then able to further develop and naturally attract wildlife into it is, admittedly, a really small moment in the grand scheme of my life, but it certainly made me smile. Even after "completing" Terra Nil, I'm absolutely going to come back to it just to play more when I need a moment of calm. If Euro/American Truck Simulators are the zen games of driving, then this is the zen game of strategy.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic title, creative and very pleasant graphics. Very chill title. very good learning curve and intuitive progression, with each level there is something new. only downside. i wish there was more to play. Whilst you can play different seeds of the maps, i would love further biomes. wish-list biomes Cloud top mountainsDesert PlateauDeep ocean (underwater biome)(Devs feel free to reach out haha)
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting for this game for a while and after finishing all of the game and getting all the achievements I would say it was worth the wait and while I was hoping for a bit more content but given the small size of the game team its understandable. I don't think that I encountered any bugs in my playthrough and at least not any major ones you would remember and I am looking forward to future content updates if which I assume will be planned since at the end of the game  but the gameplay now is really fun and relaxing! 8/10 would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the definition of a cozy game. The music is sweet and calming, the visuals are gorgeous, and the gameplay is very satisfying. I love strategy building games, but so many of them are about tearing apart the terrain and leaving things ugly. If you are all about pleasing aesthetics AND optimization, this game is for you. I absolutely love it and hope they keep expanding and adding more levels/challenges.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A refreshingly unique take on the city builder genre! Rather than focusing on infinite growth and expansion, Terra Nil chooses to focus on terraforming the environment. In this context, your buildings are simply a means to an end, not the end in and of themselves. My favorite part is how, once you are done terraforming each environment, you have to remove all of your buildings before moving on. It's easy to imagine a far less interesting alternative: a game which plays like Sim City, but where trees and flowers spring up around your buildings, simply wearing a thin veneer of environmentalism while reinforcing the same expansionist mindset which is destroying the environment. But, by flipping the genre on its head, Terra Nil is able to convey a radically different set of values from other city builders, not only through its theming, but most importantly through its gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is a unique and peaceful game that's chill but also a little challenging at times, like a fun puzzle. It's short, but very, very sweet. It's got great music, cute graphics. It's also well-researched and quietly educational. You'll find yourself Googling "do sunflowers absorb radiation?" The answer is yes apparently!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil is a fairly relaxing game where you reconstitute an ecosystem and then leave without a trace. While the full length of the game is on the shorter side (at the time of writing, I've completed the main campaign and am starting on the alternate maps), the experience is a quaint and pleasant introduction to ecosystem balance. It does throw its own logic aside at points—you can raise the temperature well above freezing and still get snow after you "unlock" it in the mission—but overall the core concept is interesting and relevant to our own bleeding world. All in all, if you're interested in short-form, randomly-generated terraforming sessions with steadily progressing mechanics, this one's a good one to try, though I'd likely wait for a sale given the short nature of the game. Congrats to the devs on the launch! Hope this game gets more content down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I 100% completed the game, achievements and all in about 25 hours. Some people would probably dislike how little playtime you can really get out of this game, but I've never really played a game like this (not one that I remember enjoying, anyway), and I enjoy having a new type of experience from time to time.I love the art! I think that's the main draw for most people initially, including me. Watching the animals do their things and seeing visual differences between ideal and normal biomes is really cool; it adds variety to the visual appearance by the end.The soundtrack is very atmospheric- in fact, all of the sound design in this game is excellent in my opinion. The gameplay loop is enjoyable once you get the hang of it (although the polluted fjord was somewhat infuriating to beat- and the quarry to some extent, but hey, they're the harder modes for a reason).The achievements are fairer and easier to get than I thought they would be. I thought that the "Perfect Location" achievement would be harder to get, but I got it no problem in the Irradiated Sprawl level. There were a couple achievements I got that I didn't think I would get so easily! The only one I really fought with was, funnily enough, getting the 15 lava tiles remaining at the end of the Volcanic Glacier level. It's so easy to accidentally turn all of your lava to stone, especially once you get the snow going.I would really like to see more of this game! For the most part, it's really chill, and most of the levels (assuming you plan ahead) are only stressful for one or sometimes two of the stages of revitalisation. More animals would be fantastic- as much as I love to get all of the animals into each level at once to perfect it, I think having some animals that conflict with others, thus not allowing you to place all of them in one playthrough, could potentially add replayability.That being said, if you're not sure you'll enjoy this type of game (especially since you'll only get about 25 hours out of it), it makes a lot of sense to get it on sale. But, if you know that you like this kind of game, definitely give it a go! (It's kind of a less stressful version of like... Planet Zoo I guess, with the zoning? Can't think of another similar game right now.) I loved the time I had with it, even if it was only three or four days.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I generally dislike strategy games. But something about not trying to genocide other nations, not simulating war, and not making a beautiful untouched area into an urban sprawl hellscape makes me enjoy this one.In fact one of the maps is giving an old piece of urban hellscape to cute pandas.Edit: There's like 10 hours of content in this game. 20 if you play it on hard mode after finishing the game on easy. If you expected Starcraft II from an indie studio, that's on you. I like my developers like I like my men, happy and not suffering from burnout.10/10, would buy again.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great chill puzzle game. There is no time limit so you are at your leisure to solve the environmental puzzles. The puzzles are not very hard which helps keep the game chill. Whenever I encounter a possible failure scenario I either start over or look a little deeper if there are ways to recover leaves, your in game life bar.The ambient sounds are well done and I look forward to getting the right conditions to have thunderstorms. It is a nice treat when a storm rolls in.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Personally I have really enjoyed the concept and mechanics of this game, I enjoy every stage a lot except the recycling stage. I understand the concept behind the recycling stage, but it feels tedious, and sometimes one tile can throw off completing the entire level. I was excited to jump into a 5th level, only to realize that it stopped at 4. The alternate levels differ in slightly more complexity and planning, but do not change much to count as standalone levels. I think some of these reviews are forgetting that 8% of the steam sales go to charity, and , I think it is important to keep that in mind regarding the price overall. Fun concept, mechanics, and gorgeous graphics. The amount of content it slightly shallow. Anyone on the fence should carefully consider their purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: It's so beautiful and relaxing and it made me very happy. Its extremely satisfying to restore the planet. Introducing the animals was very cute and I loved their little animations. I played the game in medium mode on the first play thorough, and it wasn't challenging, so I look forward to playing on hard mode, however I have played this sort of game genre a lot before. In conclusion, if you want to peacefully restore a landscape, this is an excellent game.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic calming environmental aesthetic with fun strategic gameplay that is casually paced. As you get further and further in you find yourself wanting to surpass the goals set out to make your perfect little space of nature. Very appreciative that the studio added extensive more free content to the game, I often recommend this title to my friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Sooooo, I wouldn't recommend this game. It's very complex, even when you do the tutorial. It does a bad job telling you that in order to complete certain things, it needs to be near river beds, otherwise, you are doomed and can't finish the job. There's no warning about it, and it's just that. Then your map is just screwed. I wish there was alternatives, but there isn't. There are other things in the tutorial that are not well explained. Even though there is a "book" to explain stuff to you, it's still not explained well, and it's very confusing.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this game up at launch and I can't recommend it enough. It is such a quaint little game that's very intuitive and really fun whilst also being relaxing. If you like light puzzles with no real narrative and have some concept of mild resource management then this is the game for you.The only gripe I have with the game is that there simply isn't enough. it gives you neat and cool concepts but never really expands on them and they're then gone just after you've learned how to master them. I'd've happily paid twice the money to get twice the game with things going a little more in depth and combining the concepts learned more.All in all though it's a great game that I would 100% recommend despite it being on the shorter side
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A very calm puzzle game about reclaiming the wasteland, where you have a lot of freedom in choosing which strategy best suits you and the situation. Each biome level is spit into different sections which pleasantly change the gameplay flow, making you focus on slightly alternating aspects; reclaiming/cleaning, growing/nurturing, and discovering/observing during a single level.The experience is a very refreshing one, and there is some fun replayability after initially completing the first levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended, with the caveat to get it on sale, not at full price. I spent almost $20 on it, which seems a little steep, I'm glad I didn't spend more.Game is very pretty, the premise is neat, the biome puzzles are engaging.  It's also very, very short. Like, there are 4 regions, and your first play through of all 4 will be less than 10 hours: it took me not quite 7, including having to replay one due to the game allowing me to place something in a location it was impossible to recycle it from and having to start a level over, and leaving the game running while I made and ate dinner.  Granted, I did play at the most chill difficulty, so maybe it'd take a little longer if a harder difficulty required more restarts.  So far I've played one of the "second version" regional maps, and it looks like no new content, just the same regional biomes and animals with a slightly shuffled toolset and challenge based on what you get in other regions the first time around. There's probably some level of replayability but it seems like with so few options it will get stale pretty fast.Also, many of the conceits about how to terraform are just ... wrong. Leaving aside the obvious fantasy ones (), and things like for some reason eagles require ruined buildings and can't use trees or cliffs to roost, there were a number of times where the game required  me to do things and all I could think was "it doesn't really work like that...."   If you want to actually learn how ecology works, please read a book or something, don't rely on what you learn in this game.It's also kind of buggy. Besides the aforementioned letting me place something where it wasn't possible to recycle it (it wouldn't have been possible even with later game tools like the flying recycler since there was no rocks close enough to place any monorails and no way to get any close), it also leaves the outlines from animal scanning on the surface of the water, and the UI lags often, especially when trying to rotate buildings to place them (user input? we don't need it, just throw it away!)  Also lacks some quality of life features like remembering the rotation of an object, it doesn't do this even if you're holding shift to place multiple objects. And, of course, the nice long straight irrigation placement patterns are the  ones on the list....  I basically never used the corner ones except when I didn't care enough to spend a minute and a half waiting for the game to accept my rotate input so I could finally get to the straight ones.All that said it is pretty, and it was fun to rebuild places and see all the tiny little animal sprites move in. Worth getting on sale, don't bother paying full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT:  Looks like the save system has been patched. Happy to recommend if the problem below has been resolved. I really like the game. It's a very relaxed puzzle that starts easy and gets more interesting and challenging in the mid game. I would love to tell you about the late game, but I can't play it because of a game breaking bug that literally prevents me from progressing the game further.My save reverts to a set point in the past every time I close the program, erasing any progress.  Turning cloud saves off does not seem to change this at all. The developers have been aware of the bug for more than 12 months and haven't fixed it. Can't recommend under these circumstances, unless the bug gets fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a delight, I see complaints about being short but frankly not every game has to keep you for hours upon hours, and I'll definitely be replaying some of these maps anyways as the replay value is there. It's chill, beautiful, and above all fun with the optional challenge there if you want to up the difficulty. I'm yet to finish it but I'm in love with almost every aspect, it takes the city-builder and flips it on its head for something unique and joyous. I never do steam reviews but was looking forward to this and haven't been let down so I felt compelled!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Chill, visually appealing game, with nice music... That's it. While there's nothing to complain about directly, its price tag is unjustified. The gameplay is very simple and shallow, and it starts to get repetitive after only 2 hours. Either they lower the price to something closer to 5€ or add a bunch more content, otherwise I don't recommend the pruchase of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Just processed refund for this game.  In first 2 hours I had to research a bug where the handbook was not displaying on the screen.  At first I thought the game was just freezing up whenever it opened the handbook...but no it was there but invisible.  Then I closed and opened the app after dinner and was met with a saved game who's tech had been reset to the beginning.  2 big bugs in first 2 hours...i'm out.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I love Terra Nil. The original NextFest demo for this game absolutely floored me and had me primed for the full version. Once said full version was in my Steam library, I devoured it.With eight settings across four biomes and every map randomly generated, there's some variety in the puzzles you attempt to solve. If you're only looking to 100% the game, that won't take long. Honestly, though, that's not the point of Terra Nil as far as I can see it. Terra Nil is a chill puzzle game that you can replay over and over when you want a little bit of positivity in your life.Turning a barren wasteland into a thriving ecosystem is a fun concept by itself. The little audio and visual flourishes that go with it make Terra Nil stand out.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Highly Recommend if you enjoy puzzle/citybuilder games like Islands or TinyTopia.Beautiful game with a pleasant soundtrack that matches perfectly with the game. Easy to learn, but surprisingly more tricky to master - especially on the harder difficulties. Placement is key, but as is the order in which you terraform. Do something too quickly and you can quite literally burn your progress to the ground.A fantastic chill out game but with the ability to customize the level and difficulty settings, it can very easily make for a challenge forcing you to restart sections/phases over more than once to try different strategies. Unlike other games though; this repetition isn't punishment, but rather rewarding as you explore how the mechanics can work together to produce entirely different results.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice and sweet game. Quite short, but because of that doesn't outstand it's welcome. There are 4 different levels, each different from others. And 2nd variation for each level which, I think, is supposed to be harder, but most of the time it isn't.Basically, a great chill game about doing some restoration to the world with simple strategy elements
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: The Game is telling to expect more with the whole world to recover, in the end its only 3 Areas to manage, and the final Rocket is just vanishing in to nothing? Why? very dissappointing and sudden ending. also the recycle system in the end of every level is tedious and breaks the immersion. in short i expected more.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game instills optimism. It's peaceful and relaxing and fills you with hope for a green future.Play time is (at time of writing) somewhat limited, I've gotten all but one achievement in 23 hours. Absolutely worth the price of admission, though, and I imagine I'll be coming back from time to time to reopen this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil is relaxing puzzle and strategy game. You land on a small spot of wasteland and your task is to return it to a lush ecosystem. Once you are done, your task is to find wildlife and remove any trace of your machines that made the transformation possible.The game is beautiful. I like how each level is relatively short. The strategy component of the game revolves around conservation points that increase when you transform the wasteland into a nice ecosystem, and decrease when you build the machines that make that possible. It is not time-constrained, making it a very relaxing experience.Overall I whole-heartedly recommend buying this game for full price. It is a fun ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Towards the end of the peaceful, soothing, meditative tutorial mission-- it is revealed that the only way to "leave no trace" and finish your ecological restoration, is to destroy the beautiful landscape you've created to make more artificial and ugly rivers, because rivers are the ONLY way to reclaim any buildings you put down.Asinine design decision, completely undermines the vibe and flow of the game. I do not understand why they did this.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable, and unique little puzzle game where you attempt to turn wastelands into thriving habitats by balancing different types of environments in unique regions. With three phases to work through; including, cleansing pollution, rebuilding habitats, and recycling your machines to let nature take over. Its fun to balance a region to fit and complete little optional goals and reestablish animals. It's a unique game that deserves to be experienced.All is not without flaws, and the most glaring is the severe lack of content. With only four regions (each with a post game challenge variant.) It's a very short lived experience, and an expensive one at that. On top of that, the only truly interesting and dynamic stuff happens in the final continental stage. I won't spoil it for players but some stuff actually happens that throws you some curve balls and was really cool, but it sadly only happens in that stage. It would be cool to see more stages and dynamic challenges added to the game, but I can easily imagine these ideas better grown expanded upon in a sequel too. All that said I thoroughly enjoyed my time with the game and would highly recommenced for the unique puzzle lite experience alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT upon returning after several patch cycles and playing 30 more hours:Well, they fixed the killer bugs, and added a bunch of maps, and rejigged the progression system amongst other things. This is, finally, the game that was advertised. Do I still love it? Kind of? The tool availability is frustratingly inconsistent, and it's easy to find oneself out of options to hit a specific milestone and having to restart the phase or the mission entirely to thread the needle. Temperature risen too high for moss to grow? Tough titty, this level doesn't provide temperature cooling climate tools. That sort of thing. Overall, it's fine, and it's good enough to recommend, but it's not perfect.ORIGINAL REVIEW:My recommendation is conditional on some of these bugs getting fixed. Love the game, I've apparently played 9 hours of it, sadly, I've only played two of the four biomes because of a save glitch that wipes all my progress. I've played the same two elements of the game over and over. And they are good! But, having fixed, for now, whatever was going on with my borked profiles, I restarted and then halfway through the first level (again) the guide book popped up and I couldn't close it without killing the process.As I said, I love it, but I can't keep playing the start of it. I'll wait till a patch or two come out, I think.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fresh way to play a game, restoring and reclaiming ecology instead of constant extraction and exploitation that is usually the case. It's peaceful and beautiful and the simplicity adds to it. Variation in complexity would be much appreciated, such as gameplay with more climate parameters or proper consequence for changing things to rapidly. But once again, the simplicity adds to the experience more than it takes away as it is right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: In the video essay "Minecraft, Sandboxes, and Colonialism", Dan Olson points out that there aren't really any games where you revitalize an ecosystem rather than colonize one. These devs seemed to take that as a challenge, as that is the entire point of Terra Nil. Joyful, beautiful, and intuitive (except for the monorail function, at first), I can see playing this game for many hours to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: My greatest take-away from this game is how much in need I am/we are of engaging with the destruction of our planet in a positive, constructive light. This game is just that - a fictional take at restoration engineering which makes actual restoration feel as a not-so-fictional prospective after all. Without undermining the pragmatic issues of actual restoration, I think that some playful space to reinforce hope in the human agent is a welcome and meaningful contribution to the problem.I will not go into details of the actual mechanics since the game is still evolving - my summary on the high level game design is that the game is fully playable, offers difficulty settings which transform the game from a chilled experience to a multifaceted puzzle (where failure can also be a valid outcome), thereby making it accessible for various playstyles, and I will positive comment on the concept of "Appreciate" at the end of the levels for its originality and value. Overall, solid game and solid good vibes. Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Very zen game and much better with the Vita Nova update. The interface on tracking animals is a bit unclear, but as a whole they are much more engaging than previously. Best moment is when moisture and temperature levels enable rainfall and pollution is washed away from whole level. Looking forward to more levels being introduced!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game quickly becomes unplayable because it will not save progress (common problem people post about online, also happened to me). In my version it crashed on the profile page every time it was opened--even after deleting all profiles, still showed as 38% progress on each. Uninstalling and reinstalling did nothing to help, and tech support never got back to me.Amazing concept. I hope someone either makes this game playable or makes one with fewer bugs and a similar concept.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Really disappointing. The whole campaign feels like a tutorial, and I was really expecting to go to another planet after done with missions. No such luck! The whole game is 8 missions, in 4 different biomes, takes around 10h to finish. Not a very good value for 20GBP.The game also feels rather shallow, there's very few interactions or complexities. First 2 phases of cleanup and terraforming are quire fun, and so is finding habitat for animals. Cleaning up the buildings however is not challenging, or difficult, it's just a terrible chore, especially in missions where you have to do it by river. Very annoying game design, that no fun part was easily 2h of the whole campaing time.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxed town builder, but fairly short and shallow. I enjoyed my time with it, but I'd have loved to have more maps overall (there's only 8) and while there's a good variety in how you progress through each one, I'm not sure if it's enough to really justify the overall lack of content. Regardless, it's relatively cheap and when my one complaint is that I want more, I consider it a sign that there's something good there.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I played the free version on itch.io so I had to get the full release on steam.Its a fun and relaxing game, less so the "reverse city builder" that people call it but more of a strategic resource management and object placement game. Overall its not too difficult, has a pleasing and responsive design, and is overall relaxing.IMO $25 is a bit too much, but its definitely worth it on sale, so I'd recommend picking it up at a discount if you're looking for something simple and enjoyable. You can also try the free version first to see if you'd like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhere between a puzzle game and a casual builder. You have limited resources, completing the objectives with what you have can be tricky to figure out. But none of the maps are all that difficult. And they're always randomized. So its more of an efficiency game that a real puzzle. Still fun and the art is very pretty.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: At its core this is a fresh wind and its just a very relaxing puzzle game with a cute artstyle. The idea of going from a wasteland to greens lush land has always drawn and I wish more games in this genre would be made and released.Also I applaud any developer for actually releasing a full game in this day and age.However, for the amount of current content and the time it takes to complete it, its release price of 25 Euro is way over the top. I can name multiple titles that will provide 10x the amount of time needed and have a ton of more content for the same price and a few even way that are cheaper.  The game does feel and look polished but again so do several other games in its price range.So I really, really hope more content will be made over time, until then please take note that the game is short so unless you don't mind spending that amount of money for 10+ hours max of gameplay. I would wait for the price to come down or on a sale.But since its a Full release, works and in general a fun game to play I will still recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the first half of the game (main story) and one of the levels after you finish the main game. I would recommend this game to anyone that likes nature, puzzles, or relaxing games. Its very fun and sometimes very challenging especially in the optional levels. I found myself having to restart several times because i kept spending all my resources on accident. The music is beautiful and compelling, the art style in simply gorgeous and worthy of being framed and hung on my walls. Watching barren landscapes turn into thriving ecosystems is a wonderful feeling and makes me appreciate nature so much more.However ive stumbled into far too many GAME BREAKING bugs to be able to give this game a positive review. In the last level of the main game after spending 30-45 minutes on the map i couldnt finish the game because the mechanics wouldnt progress themselves.  and when these bugs occurred i had to completely restart my game and restart the level to fix it. I also find some of the mechanics lacking self explanations for instance  The price tag is a little high for but i dont mind spending it because ive enjoy just about every second of this game.My final thought is that this game is a work of art but beware the bugs that can cause serious issues. I think the people that say this game needs more to do are greedy. Plain and simple.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: The positive first. The game is a fun concept and I like the art style. I generally find terraforming games very satisfying and I do enjoy watching the different ecosystems emerge as you play. It's fun trying to discover what conditions different animals needed to then populate those ecosystems. This game is cute, but it plays like a demo. The tutorial takes up basically the whole game and it never gets into enough complexity to be interesting--any difficulty is just from confusion with the mechanics. It's often hard to understand why you can't place a building somewhere, for example. In terms of satisfying-ness, it's very difficult to completely detoxify an area, which leaves me with an unfinished feeling.It only took me four hours to complete, which is not nearly enough for a $20 game. There are alternate versions of the levels which might boost that to closer to 7-8 hours, but it just wasn't interesting enough for me to want to.I think if the game were cheaper or longer I'd give it a thumbs up, but as it is now I think you'd be better off waiting a bit and hope that they add more content in future updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very satisfying! Restoring life to a barren wasteland step by step is both, fun & challenging. I finished everything, including the (very cool & interesting) alternate maps in 10 hours, which makes me agree that I would have liked a bit more content. Coming up with new maps with new twists can't be that hard, so I hope for a (free) DLC or some user created content to bring a bit more depth to this little gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A very original, chill puzzle game that disguises itself as a "city builder" but really isn't, which I find is the reason for half the negative reviews here.It's NOT Cities Skyline or Sim City "in reverse". It's not "like other city-builders [you]'ve played before but not as good", because it's not the same genre. Don't expect hundreds of hours of infinite replayability. It's a puzzle game, about 10h long.That being said, If that's what you're looking for, I very much recommend it, the art style is gorgeous, the music chill and unintrusive, the gameplay varied - even though the cleanup phase can get a little tedious - and I greatly enjoyed the overall message of trying to "unfµck the world" then remove ourselves from it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: The game tells you what to do, you do it, and you win. Then you do it all again. I dont really see whats enjoyable about it. Maybe it turns into a puzzle of placing everything in ways where they align in the perfect ways so you can do all the things you want with your space? IDK. I dont like it.Its boring as a sack of old potatos with those disgusting eyes that grow deep into the potato and you keep cutting them out but theyre so deep and theres a ton of them and you keep peeling and cutting and before you know it theres no potato left.

_childDocuments_.review: While the concept is solid and the few levels in the game are enjoyable, this isn't worth anything close to $25. _childDocuments_.review: Genuinely a very fun game, if lacking a bit in content at launch.Pros:- Really good atmosphere and soundtrack- Puzzle aspect of the gameplay is engaging without being stressful- Achievements and challenges provide a bit of longevity with reasons to go back and play levels againCons:- Lacking in content for the price point- Mechanics can feel a bit simple once you know what you're doing- Ending is (imo) a bit frustrating Overall, if it seems like the type of game you'd enjoy you'll probably really like it! _childDocuments_.review: You can read my other reviews What if there was a city builder that wasn't about expanding and industrializing land, but rather restoring nature over map tiles stripped of any properties? That is the question addressed in Terra Nil, built on a super relaxing environment that leaves anyone in a zen state, in a different approach to the city-building and puzzle genre.Terra Nil's goal will be to rehabilitate a planet that is effectively dead and devoid of any traces of fauna or flora. Divided into four areas with different environments, it all starts with an element that makes it possible to generate energy, the wind turbine. In this sense, this element becomes the main mean of building the sub-elements that make it possible to create an environment conducive to the growth of vegetation, with the help of a toxin purifier and subsequent irrigator. With the appearance of water and vegetation, the perfect conditions are created for the approximation of animal life. The puzzle component comes into play when placing all the mechanisms created to create life. For example, the wind turbine only works on top of stones, and the sprinkler only has X number of tiles per area, among others. The same applies when letting the area breathe freely without using machines. The final phase of each level is recycling all equipment.Each zone corresponds to certain areas of the planet, such as a forest area, a tropical area, or an icy area. It is indeed fascinating to see the world come to life in different areas with a simple click of the mouse button. One of the tasks presented to the player along his journey is the need to create the necessary conditions for the necessary flora to grow. Controlling temperature and humidity become very important aspects. Not being a super difficult particularity, it made me repeat the tropical biome since it was necessary to reach a certain percentage of humidity so that the corals could grow.After all the weather conditions have been met, the second phase of each zone's journey begins, the possibility of looking for the different animals. Even if the necessary climatic conditions are met, some animals have specific needs for areas in which to proliferate.Some aspects in Terra Nil are fully explained, but others are learned through experience using various tools. It's not a negative element, nor is the game itself difficult, but it can leave some players a little lost not knowing their next move. It is always possible to return to the starting point and if you spend all the resources needed to build each piece of equipment without reaching the next objective, that will really be the only possible choice.Terra Nil is a super relaxing but short experience. It does have some replayability, with the implementation of different difficulty levels, but just four different zones seem pretty short. However, it is a fully recommended title for fans of city-builder games.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and relaxing puzzle game that's sadly going to be overtaken by "it's short, so i don't recommend" as is the case with most games on steam nowadays.I definitely wish there were more biomes/levels - The game currently has 4 biomes to reclaim, being a river valley, a tropical island, a tundra, and a temperate forest . There could have been more variety here such as a desert, the ocean, rainforests etc. However, given what is there I will not hesitate in recommending it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous game with a lot of potential; I'd absolutely love to see more variation in environments, and hope to see this game grow and grow.EDIT 6/24/2024: I was so, SO excited for the update, and I gotta say, I'm blown out of the water by the beauty and hard work. AND THE BEARS FLOP DOWN IN THE FLOWERS AND ROLL ON THEIR BACKS. 15/10, this is absolutely one of my favorite games of all time, and I'm gonna put it right up there with Journey for its simple, but incredible beauty, music, and atmosphere, albeit a different form.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I saw Terra Nil at GDC last week and knew I should give it a go. Behind this game is a talented and thoughtful team of people who really do care about the environment. The message is not thrown in your face the entire time. This is truly a game about reclaiming a world lost to pollution and decay. About fixing things. There's something about the replayability factor that really makes this game shine. The second I had reclaimed the world I instantly restarted it. I also love that part of the proceeds are going to a wildlife fund. I'd strongly recommend playing this game. Just give it a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: - Epilepsy Warning - When loading into the maps, the game flashes white clouds, which I think are meant to simulating you going up and down through the clouds, but really just come off as flashbangs.- Demo Availablility -There is a demo available on Itch.io. The gameplay is nearly identical, and you can try it out before purchasing this version here.Terra Nil is a puzzle strategy game that has you cleaning up polluted environments and restoring the ecosystem to a self-sustaining state. The game is charming, and provides a reasonable amount of challenge on the regular difficulty. The steps to reproduce a new ecosystems are identical, but the differences in each stage do make each level different enough from each other to not feel tedious or repetitive.I enjoy it. It's calming, peaceful, and the only threat comes from not spending your resources properly, and having to restart the stage.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this game and it didn't let me down. It's a really fun interpretation of the city building/strategy sim. I love the idea of restoring nature and ecosystems. The game has a simple loop and easy to learn mechanics. But it's still challenging to find new/better ways to do things and it feels a little different each time.I'm also a big fan of the art style, graphics, and music! If this game catches your eye then give it a shot! If you're on the fence, then check out some reviews or gameplay footage. I'm very satisfied and still enjoying my time with it :3
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Super relaxing and fun to play. Gotta say though, I 100% the game in like 7 hours (including Achievements).For the price I would say its a bit high. But, If you are a fan of puzzle games and have a green thumb this game will grab you instantly.For those more accustomed to higher difficulty games this game will come off a bit easy. To off set this you have the option to limit your resources in the settings. Much like playing the game with one arm tied behind your back.8/10 - Will play it after 100% just for fun.-1 point for lack of content atm. (The devs. have said they would like to come back and add more content)-1 point for price and rare visual bugs.If more content gets released and the few bugs get ironed out, this game could easily become a 10/10 even if the price stays the same.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is visually beautiful and can be very relaxing just to see the world being alive. But for the price I would not recommend it, the game has no replayability after you cleared it for the first time. The gameplay is very shallow and doesn't offer much variety. I was really excited for the game but after playing it for a while it becomes very boring. You might have more fun watching others play than playing it yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is a great,the artstyle is lovely, I especialy like looking at the little illustrations in the book.(idk if its already i thing but i would totaly buy a paper version :) )The music is chill and soothing, And the gameplay makes me feel good and happy.To me this is a game that can get me trouch a rouch day the only problem i have is that its pretty short for the price as i have completed the game in about then hours (plus the extra levels and achievements).all in all i would recoment this game if you have some mony to spare.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I was addicted from the start with the demo. Fulfills what I like about strategy games without an overwhelming amount of mechanics to manage. Multiple levels of difficulties, including "zen mode" to just chill and clear up the biomes. I would love to see a third variation of the levels or additional biomes in the future, if that's possible, but the randomly generated maps ensure replayability. I've binge-played this all of release week, and I don't regret it at all!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Great relaxing puzzle game, 4 different regions with each having 2 levels of difficulty.Its like a sanbox experience on the lower difficulties and can get pretty challenging on the harder ones, as a lot of other people i think the pricetag is to high for the short experience it offers, wich doesnt mean it isnt a very beatiful experience... If its on sale, a no-brainer, otherwise i would think twice since its really short
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I've been in love with this beautiful game since the free beta version. The full release has updated graphics, a wider range of biomes and varieties of maps, and rebalanced progression and a much smoother difficulty curve. This is a 'city builder' game where every decision along the way and your order of operations are critical to your success, but which is still maintains forgiveness for mistakes as long as you learn from them along the way. At the end of each level, seeing the wonderful restored natural world and hearing the music brings tears of joy to my eyes. It's a worthwhile experience with a lot of replayability  in my eyesSmall wishlist of features:Some of the mini games like using sonar scanning for finding animals aren't very well explained, and I would like there to be a benefit from adding multiple populations of the same animal.More uses for the map wide conditions like temperature and humidity, these were great additions to the game but I want to see even more uses for them besides some extra bonus points.Maps that start small then expand - That was such a cool mechanic in the tutorial and I wish there was a mode that let me develop in stages or would throw new problems at me after I had developed. More natural disasters - The disaster present in the city level was so cool and caused me to re-evaluate my game plan. I wish there were more events like that.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing reverse sim builder. Unlike a lot of other "builders" I felt little to no pressure rebuilding nature. In fact, I'd like to say its really hard not to fail so long as you are smart with your resources. The soundtrack and sounds all combine to give this game a super chill vibe. Definitely one of those that could help you pass the time.Side note: I'd LOVE to see this game get full Steam Deck support one day.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice little puzzle game. I wouldn't call it a city builder, the amount of buildings you can put on a map is too limited for that. It's more about building machines to balance different weather effects to create the correct environments, the more environment panels you spawn the more leaf bucks you get the more machines you can build. It's a satisfying loop. It can be a bit obtuse in you gets more leaf bucks though, and the objectives can feel like a counterproductive chore sometimes. One level forces you to make rocks to grow lichen and won't tell you why the lichen keeps losing you leaf bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I adore Terra Nil. I played it before release at PAX and I was hooked. As someone with unholy amounts of hours in factory building games, this is such a gentle palette cleanser. The one thing others have pointed out is that it is a pretty short game. I'm nearing 100% on it - which i should complete in under 8 hours. I honestly don't mind that. Not every game needs to be 100 hours of playtime. I spend as much as I did on this game to go see a movie that lasts 2-3 hours, so I won't complain about the price for the game. If that's your hangup, wait for a sale and pick it up right away,
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: What a wholesome game, definitely recommend! I can't remember finding myself so positively moved as I was on finishing the first chapter of this game. It's a chill game to play, the puzzles and discovery have kept me quite engaged though, and it gets very rewarding to see the land transformation happening... I got an extra kick when fauna was finally returned :)
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so in love with this game so far. I have a career in environmental science, so I really wanted to try out this game. Not ONLY are the visuals and soft music SO CHARMING, but it's also extremely educational. Learning how to strategize and develop the land into the most optimized biomes is SUPER satisfying. I love how much thought was put into this game to make the play style flow so smoothly without feeling like there's too much hand holding or completely leaving you hanging. You will LOVE this game if you like: nature, science, strategy, and relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed playing this game, however there is a game breaking bug on the final level that completely prevents finishing the game. Many users have reported this as early as April 3rd. However today as of June 17th there is no fix, no time table, or response from the devs other than "I noted it for the team". This is completely unacceptable for a completed paid for game. I'd get it refunded if it wasn't too late.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review:
Terra Nil, from eco-warriors Free Lives (Broforce) and recycled publisher Devolver Digital, presents players with the task of environmental rejuvenation. Begin with the water system, slowly purify the soil, and cultivate pioneer greenery. Embark on more ambitious tasks, restore biodiversity, fix the climate, introduce wildlife, and finally recycle all the structures you used to get there, leaving the environment pristine.

Each region of the game has its own flavour and procedural generation palette. Yet even within a region, no two playthroughs will be the same.

Navigate sprawling, verdant, hand-painted environments where everything but the rocks move and breathe. A meditative soundtrack and stunning audio palette will accompany your efforts.

name: God of War
detailed_description: Enter the Norse realm His vengeance against the Gods of Olympus years behind him, Kratos now lives as a man in the realm of Norse Gods and monsters. It is in this harsh, unforgiving world that he must fight to survive… and teach his son to do the same. Grasp a second chance Kratos is a father again. As mentor and protector to Atreus, a son determined to earn his respect, he is forced to deal with and control the rage that has long defined him while out in a very dangerous world with his son. Journey to a dark, elemental world of fearsome creatures From the marble and columns of ornate Olympus to the gritty forests, mountains and caves of pre-Viking Norse lore, this is a distinctly new realm with its own pantheon of creatures, monsters and gods. Engage in visceral, physical combat With an over the shoulder camera that brings the player closer to the action than ever before, fights in God of War™ mirror the pantheon of Norse creatures Kratos will face: grand, gritty and grueling. A new main weapon and new abilities retain the defining spirit of the God of War series while presenting a vision of conflict that forges new ground in the genre. PC FEATURES High Fidelity Graphics Striking visuals enhanced on PC. Enjoy true 4K resolution, on supported devices, [MU1] with unlocked framerates for peak performance. Dial in your settings via a wide range of graphical presets and options including higher resolution shadows, improved screen space reflections, the addition of GTAO and SSDO, and much more. NVIDIA® DLSS and Reflex Support Quality meets performance. Harness the AI power of NVIDIA Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS) to boost frame rates and generate beautiful, sharp images on select Nvidia GPUs. Utilize NVIDIA Reflex low latency technology allowing you to react quicker and hit harder combos with the responsive gameplay you crave on GeForce GPUs. Controls Customization Play your way. With support for the DUALSHOCK®4 and DUALSENSE® wireless controllers, a wide range of other gamepads, and fully customizable bindings for mouse and keyboard, you have the power to fine-tune every action to match your playstyle. Ultra-wide Support Immerse yourself like never before. Journey through the Norse realms taking in breathtaking vistas in panoramic widescreen. With 21:9 ultra-widescreen support, God of War™ presents a cinema quality experience that further expands the original seamless theatrical vision.

Now they just need to send the other GoW games over... and Bloodborne...So about this game: graphics are gorgeous, story and lore are great, voice acting and music are outstanding, and gameplay is addictive as Hel. _childDocuments_.review: I've never played any Playstation Dad Shooters, no God of War games, and my only experience with a melee combat loop like this is Breath of the Wild oddly enough... yet I've been playing it non-stop for three days straight. This type of game is not what I usually play. I never care about cinematic experiences or good video game stories, because I always thought stories detracted from the gameplay to some extent... not this one. With how incredibly detailed the world is, how amazing the combat is, and how surprisingly cinematic it is, I thought the game would be maybe 5 hours long. I had no idea this was such a huge game when I bought it. I just don't understand how it's possible for a game to have so many quality animations and cutscenes with hours worth of dialogue... and the fact it's all done in one cut with no loading screens confuses me by how the frames never ever drop, and the game is almost bug-free.My only criticism is that the stat-based RPG mechanics feel pointless and tacked-on. I'd personally rather them not be in the game, and instead just stick with progression being purely mechanical, as in the pre-existing additional attacks and combat options. My brain simply does not compute minor percentage stats. The luck-based buffs are a bit better to process, but they should all have a 100% chance of activating. I'd always prefer a 100% chance to have a better dodge than a 40% chance to get damage resistance when taking damage. I'd also prefer to be given certain abilities to reward rage rather than just getting a buff that makes rage build faster by 15%.Overall, one of my favorite games of all time. My eyes and hands hurt, yet I'm still begging for more.P.S.This game feels like a 120$ game priced at 50$... 40$ when I got it on sale. How??? It has enough content for several DLCs worth. The entire Valkyrie quest line has a better story on it's own than some entire games. It really could be a video game's plot, but its entirely optional. There are two entire challenge realms which are also optional, and the side-quests feel like DLC content rather than the time-wasters you'd expect from side quests.SPOILERS:

_childDocuments_.review: Ladies and gentlemen, warriors and wannabes, hold onto your divine helmets because we're diving straight into the epic world of God of War 4! Kratos is back, and he's traded in his Greek mythology for some good old Norse gods and frosty battles. Here are some of my personal reviews on this masterpiece:🛡️ **Graphics:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐Prepare to have your eyes blessed by the gods themselves. Get ready for a lore-laden adventure that'll make you feel like a saga storyteller.⚔️ **Difficulty:** ⭐⭐⭐Listen up, warriors. This ain't no cakewalk, but it's also not like you have to struggle with a small goblin mob (Souls). _childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of the most perfectly crafted games of all time. At points the pacing is questionable, but it truly is a masterpiece. Santa Monica took one of the most insane psychopathic, crazed killing machines and turned him into a more relatable character. The story arch of both Atreus and Kratos from start to finish is one of the best. Since 2018 I've played through this game a few times, and without question I bought it on PC as soon as I could. This is how a story driven game should be crafted. No cutting corners, no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ keeping you from enjoying the fun. It's challenging, exciting, and emotionally invigorating. If you haven't played this game or you're on the fence, you should just bite the bullet and give it a try. The soundtrack, visuals, open world, combat, leveling, progression, dialogue, plot twists, boss fights..this is what every games standard should and should've been set by (since launch). Without question more pros than cons to the game (such as reused boss kill animations to name a con), but I can most certainly look past those points. It's a visceral experience and I truly believe that this iteration of God of War is simply one of the greatest games to have ever existed, and will EVER exist. I'm primarily an FPS player, and typically I don't enjoy games like this...but man.. I can't wait for Ragnarok. Thanks for reading if you got this far.

_childDocuments_.review: "We win because we are determined. Disciplined. Not because we feel ourselves superior." What a game. My expectations were high and they were shattered by a huge magic axe. This game has better writing and acting than many, dare I say, most blockbuster movies. There is something so amazing about watching Kratos and Atreus grow with each other and it is so satisfying to see them overcome each new obstacle. Kratos struggling to overcome his past and Atreus trying his best to live up to expectations and prove himself to his dad. It has been done before but it is such a fantastic dynamic. I had to play this game on very low graphics due to hardware limitations. Despite this there were still many jaw dropping environments. And of course, the combat is fun as hell. At first I did not think I would be a fan of the Leviathan axe and missed Kratos' iconic Chaos Blades but I soon grew to love the axe. The attacks feel so heavy and some of the moves you can pull off are really fun. The first boss battle is one of the best I have ever played and it is so exciting raising the stakes because now Kratos has something to lose. I love quick time event sections because it allows Kratos to do spectacular things that the player could normally never do and it makes Kratos feel that much more resilient and brutal. With all that said obviously I loved this game and it has quickly become one of my all time favorites. Simple story, immaculate characters executed to perfection in an epic journey that I won't soon forget.

_childDocuments_.review: I platinumed this game on PS4 two years ago and havent played it since. I was excited for the PC release because it would give me a good reason for another playthrough along with the performance boost and the convenience of having it on the platform i use the most.Every time i pick it up i have to stop myself because i just keep going for hours and hours. I realise now how overdue i was for another playthrough. Decided to go GMGOW right from the start for the challenge and everything is so satisfying. The story, acting, combat, lore, music, aesthetic and overall feel of this game just has a way of sucking me in and keeping me hooked. I've became so attached to the characters like i knew them for years. Seeing how both Kratos and Atreus grow so much throughout the story is just so endearing, to the point of it being almost on a personal level.Santa Monica studio found a way to make me care so much more about a character that used to be so loud and brutal. Now older and wiser, Kratos shows a lot of vulnerability which gives him so much more depth as a character. Massive kudos.As for the game itself. It's a third person over the shoulder action adventure RPG, which is a nice change from the usual 'far from the player' fixed camera, every encounter feels more up close and personal. Combat is still brutal and exciting with an entirely new weapon: tons of new moves, ways to make flashy combos, light and heavy special attacks along the help of your son that can shoot arrows to keep your targets up in the air. They kept some of the gameplay elements that made god of war great but expanded on them to make the experience feel whole and adds a lot more weight. If you're still not convinced then you should probably watch some spoiler free reviews from people who can describe the game better than i can. It's hard to put my feelings into words when it comes to games i love, i can point out some things that the game does right but the love i have for it goes beyond words. I just really hope you can have an experience as amazing as mine.

_childDocuments_.review: Hard not to recommend this game.God of War is what I'd call the Gold Standard in the genre of Narrative focused, story driven, cinematic ARPG's, in a semi-open world.It boasts great performance, amazing visuals, sound, music and voice acting. The story is great, the lore fun and interesting. The world is detailed and level design impressive, with fairly obvious but decently clever puzzles. The game is semi-open world, meaning that while you will eventually open up the entire map and can go wherever you please, a lot of areas are locked behind story progression, and areas themselves will feature linear designs. It's not Skyrim where you can just climb any rock or mountain. There are invisible walls in the form of un-interactable terrain, so your exploration will be limited.Combat is relatively simplistic compared to many ARPG's, but it's rock solid in execution. It's brutal and satisfying. And while it's simple, you're given a wide variety of tools to customize your combat experience to your liking. While you're limited to two weapons, you can use dozens of special abilities and customize your gear to support a specific style of play.If there's anything to nitpick about at all, it is the RPG elements of leveling up and gear, which are all very straightforward. There's an immense abundance of loot to the point where every skill and ability, and every piece of gear can fairly easily be aquired. Which can lead to the feeling that exploration isn't as rewarding as it could be. The only gear that cannot be easily obtained is locked behind an immense amount of optional side-content grind which feels out of reach for casuals, but I guess is a nice touch for those who like min-maxing and testing themselves with the highest difficulty settings.Every fan of RPG's should be looking to play this game. Especially as it is sending a strong message to Sony to port more games from their console library to the PC.

_childDocuments_.review: Overrated. Cumbersome combat with a way-too-close camera that isn't adjustable, yet tons of enemy reliance on flanking offscreen. It just makes the fights annoying. The animations and visuals are great, but combat lacks the somewhat tactical feel of earlier GOW games. Definitely too much faffing about with the boy, too much story. Some people love games that are just interactive movies, but I prefer the focus to be on gameplay. Everything in this game feels scripted and stiff. Kratos, who should feel tanky and powerful, is a wimp who can only take 2-3 hits before dying. The early hours of the game are a scripted slog and play control feels like molasses compared to other high-end ARPGs I've played. Environments look great, but are relatively boring linear corridors (with the occasional obligatory boring puzzle / loop-around paths) with little in them that is interactive or destructable. To me, despite the high production value, this is a step in the wrong direction for the franchise.

The skill trees and light RPG elements keep the combat satisfying the whole way through.The world and side content are just as well made as the main story line, featuring new characters, features, mechanics and action set pieces. I found myself finishing basically all the side quests by the time I beat the main game, in an attempt just to extend the game even further as I just didn't want it to end.Music and visual presentation are stellar also. The soundtrack really elevates the character and action moments in this odessey, guiding the player in how they should feel so as to best match how the characters themselves are feeling.Long story short, buy this damn game! _childDocuments_.review: This game is stunning! Is breath taking graphics and unbeatable gameplay are only a page in a massive book on things why this game is amazing. The story is a magnificent compelling attribute to an already perfect game, the story draws you in by constantly keeping you on a train of cliff hangers and systems where it make you want to unlock other plots advancing the story, all the while making each and every advancement into the plot as fresh as the previous one. The gritty nature of the story at heart is just a small layer shadowing the deeper lesson of understanding and acceptance of past actions. The game play is utterly brilliant, the fighting mechanics and the abilities are unseen is a franchise about hack and slash, while still retaining the incredibly addictive playability of not only it’s own series but of any game genre of us kind. The blocking in this game doesn’t just defend you from an enemy’s attacks is allowed you to counter damaging them stunning them allowing you to follow up with a barrage of strikes from your weapon of choice. The accessibility of progression in this title is irresistible the rewards that are given for complete side missions and main are more than fair, allowing you to upgrade and progress though a bewitching skill system. You also have your son as a side companion assisting you in battle as well as being a key character in the story having a major effect on the narrative. Your son Atreus can be used to attack enemies from a distance and be used to advance to new room and progress though levels and assists is tricky but fun puzzles. The graphics are unbelievably beautiful, unseen  I’m a game of this type. The miraculous terrain you travel is extremely realistic and vibrant, the surroundings are just down right prepossessing and gorgeous. The Nordic style of the environment is perfect for both combat and appealing to the eye. The water simulation in this game is a almost perfect example on how games have evolved from 2D side scroller to game that are unrecognizable from real life.  The attention to detail is unmatched, it’s clear nothing from graphics, gameplay to the story weren’t rushed. The musical score is also an absolute must when is come to setting the mood. The cinematography is on points making the game one continuous shot not cutting from one scene to the next, it creates a cinematic feeling putting in the actual perspective of the character. All around this game is extremely important in the advancements of game quality, and detail.P.S. I have to also say that this PC port is stellar! We have great options and optimizations is fantastic!

_childDocuments_.review: What else can be said that hasn't already been said by so many others about God of War? It's just SO GOOD and I'm so glad playstation games like these have made their way to PC (I sure hope they keep coming!). JUST BUY THIS GAME - it definitely deserves its fair and full price. On a sale? - you'd be quite mad not to add it to your collection.I haven't been this pulled into a third person RPG since Witcher 3, Red Dead Redemption 2, or Batman Arkham City (also, I've played almost every RPG out there, so just take my word on understanding a quality RPG game). The game is so cinematic; moments that need impact and size carry the right amount of weight, and there's just enough beats between Kratos and Artreus that carry appropriate emotional gravitas without it being overbearing. The Norse mythology and stories told by the characters as as you traverse the map are very engaging, and helps alleviate the silence and chore of traveling. There were so many clever tricks used by the devs to make the game feel relentlessly smooth as it transits from set piece to set piece, fight sequence to fight sequence. On a technical front, this is a near flawless port. On my 3080, running on a 38" 1600p ultrawide, i average 80 - 90 FPS in most sections running Ultra, with occasional dips into the 70s. On my 27" 1440p, I cruise at 120 - 150 FPS. The game play is  butter smooth, but I continue to wish that ports would take advantage of more keys on the keyboard. I experienced 2 hard crashes in all my time playing (so far), and occasionally (particularly at the later stages of the game), I ran into issues where it felt like there was a momentarily invisible wall in front of Kratos and I had to move back to move forward again. Overall, I also felt like there could have been more FOV applied as a default, as the game sometimes feel a little too zoomed in, but this is a very minor gripe.From a gameplay perspective, the game isn't a completely open world third person rpg - it has a story to tell, and the world is a medium to help transit you through the story (which is pretty much how I felt about RDR2, Horizon, and Cyberpunk). A few side quests and lots of collectibles. There are optional maps which are, i think, designed as end-game grinds for the best gear.  Several satisfying and challenging fights with mini bosses. General fights can become slightly repetitive at about the 20 hour mark, but luckily the game almost precisely levels you up and spaces these out so that it never becomes too much of a chore. As long as you open your eyes, you should find everything you need to find as you transit through each area whenever the story allows you to, with side quests helping to take you to the locations that are more optional so that you can grab all the other items there too.What a masterpiece. SONY, I implore you to keep this quality up with your studios and their games, and also to keep them coming to PC (even though I still see it as a borderline scummy business tactic to extend the product life cycle of 2 - 3 year old games).
