_childDocuments_.review: I didn't hear about  until long ago, i think it was around 2019 when i first saw some gameplay and i really noticed people freak out about this game. But i didn't have a console and wasn't really into it at first, so i didnt watch theRadBrad or any other creator do the playthrough.      Fast forward to the 8th of December 2021, 3 days before my birthday, i opened my phone in the morning and did my daily routine browsing through youtube and i see it. God of War PC Release. I got really intrigued by that teaser, 1 minute of perfect balance between action, character presentation and, damn, that soundtrack had me so soooo bad.I love reading and gathering information about the Norse Mythology, seeing that this was a game based on this particular thing got me really hyped about the re-release on steam.So yes, was feeling enthusiastic about this game and i really got to the point where i was watching that teaser multiple times a day, but my worry was that my PC wouldn't be able to run the game.      Days passed by and now it was January, it felt harder and harder to be patient because i really wanted to get to play this supposed masterpiece. Finally, maybe 2 days after it finally released, i bought it and it was time to finally get it started.  100% my favorite game of all time. The game that got me to want to understand the whole francise, to see all the videos online about Kratos and his past, to watch any guide imaginable about how to defeat the current game and do all the smaller and bigger side quests. I absolutely love this game and i feel like i don't have enough time to spend exploring and finding new things myself by playing it as i would like. I enjoy everything about it:        In my opinion its the perfect balace between enjoying the 3rd person action based gameplay, the building story and relationship between Kratos and *gasps* BOY and the history that was being re-written about the Norse Gods and the coming of Ragnarok.        Everybody in this game has a rich story behind them, from Baldur and the drama behind his mother's curse on him, to obviously Atreus that is trying to prove himself and to his father after the death of his mother, and Kratos that feels so scared to get emotionally attached to his son because he wouldn't be able to lose him aswell as he lost everything dear to him before.        The emotional impact of Faye's death has had on Kratos and Atreus is being felt through the entire playthough of the game. Kratos is talking to himself asking what Faye would do in his situation, even saying that he isn't ready and he is not prepared to move forward without her, Atreus wishing that it was his father that died instead of his mom, everything is insanely well written about their story.        Everything looks absolutely gorgeous. Freya's home is the incarnation of the paradise, The Lake of the Nine is a great main location to hover around and take your time to search every little nook and cranny. All the realms having their own feeling, some more welcoming than others. The giants in this game were mindblowing for me. When i first saw Jormungandr and Thamur i became speachless. I've never played a game that gave me the feeling that i am so small comparing to the world around me.       I have't played a lot of games like this one, but the combat felt natural. I didn't feel any awkwardness while fighting, throwing my axe, doing combos and all of those felt amazing and intuitive. Such a good management of the controls made even myself look good while fighting those Valkyries.    as a game and as a francise is the absolute pillar of long term story telling and the execution of the transition from the previous style of the first GoW games to this one is flawless.       I love learning things about this game, i love understanding the lore behind Kratos and the other characters around him, everything about God of War makes me more curious about what might happen next and how Ragnarok is going to affect this Universe.Absolutely one of the all time best, if not the one. 10/10 in my books, can't say anything bad about it.       I just hope Santa Monica Studio try to port all the GoW's to PC someday, so i can not only see the evets happening previous to this modern masterpiece, but to play and experience them myself. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Is GoW overhyped? Hell YesIs GoW a must have? Not reallyIs GoW still a good game to enjoy if you don't know what else to play? YesPersonally I can see how this game has won awards for cinematography, animations and musical score. When it comes to actual gameplay it is an Action-Adventure that mix and matches elements from various, better, games. In the end it feels like an decent functional mix wherein nothing really stands out. It is functional and fun enough to keep you going. However don't expect anything exceptional.This game has a good pace where it switching between story elements, exploration, puzzles and combat. It is a redeeming quality that prevented me from getting bored with any specific element. Environments look amazing and fantastical with plenty of metroid-esque upgrades to find. You'll look for secrets and chests that contain the better gear as well as Health/Rage Pool upgrades. As for the puzzles, finding language cyphers, it all feels like a very simplified version of adventure games that did this better. It is clear inspirations have been taken from the likes of Darksiders, Tombraider and to some extent Uncharted. However they all did it much better and engaging.The original GoW games also contained their fair share of simplified puzzles. So this evolution is in line with that. They were also known for its challenge and brutality with the occasional janky/questionable difficulty spikes. This iteration of the franchise shares similarities in that regard when playing on the highest difficulty. Until Kratos has lvl'ed up to 4-5 he will have to deal with super bullet spongy enemies that take ages to kill. Choosing the right skills too pick up has a massive impact here to even damage the enemies. I personally couldn't be bothered and went back down to Hard difficulty instead. However the choice of skills is not numerous, nor interesting in most cases. They lack the flash and cool aspect the old GoW games had. Here it is more about choosing skills and runes for its mechanical functionality. This means a severe lack in cool combo's as you go through the game. Combat overall is also at a much slower pace. If you take the time to explore instead of rush the main story...you'll also see a lot of recurring enemies for many hours. Which to some people can get quite boring. Yet new enemy types do get introduced the further in you proceed. They also get woven into different combinations to keep the encounters interesting enough to deal with. Also the camera is super zoomed in reducing your overall view of the battlefield. Making your combat positioning very important in order to keep an eye on as many enemies as possible. It feels slow, clunky and not really fun. However it is functional enough to get you through the game.I also find that the 3 profiles for the controller are not great. Each setup has some unintuitive binds to them. It would've been nice if we could keybind all of them as some other ports allow. I've also noticed some memory issues with this port. However it seems there is already a hotfix in the beta testing branch. The developers of the port are on point. All other tech breakdowns for this PC port show nothing but positive things. I can say that it does run pretty well for a few hickups here and there. Which the devs posted about fixing already.When talking about unintuitive and occasionally annoying... The inventory/rune sorting UI is horrible.If you take the time to explore and appreciate the beautiful vista's. Then this game does instill that strong feeling of being on an adventure across the 9 realms.As an Avid Action gamer I am disappointed heavily by GoW and rather go back to playing Nioh 2, Bayonetta or any other action game tbh. For the metroid-esque aspect I rather go and play Bloodstained, HollowKnight, Ori or Metroid Dread. If I wanted more Adventure I'd go play Darksiders, Uncharted or Tombraider. As a more variety gamer It is a decent game with a simplified mix of several different genres while standing out in none of those.

_childDocuments_.review: I elected to play at difficulty level "God of War" - big mistake.  Not because it is difficult, but because of the way the difficulty is created.  If you are a glutton for punishment and rely on luck to win then perhaps it is worth playing at this difficulty level however I regret trying this.  The opponents are the same but the seemingly have MUCH shorter cooldown times on special moves than a god, their health bars decrease less easily than those of a god and they seem to move faster than a god.  Their self-healing is MUCH better than Kratos', and him a god, even if in reduced circumstances.  The opening fight promised epic, the game fights - not so much. When I consider that in his first fight he barefist punches a rock pillar to smithereens in a fight with a god eventually beating the god but he has difficulty punching a dent into an enemies health bar of ?mortal? grunts in a mortal world during gameplay,  Kratos swings a tree trunk to bash an opponent into orbit but his axe strokes are stopped by mortal shields? No way.  The promise of godly powers and the reality of equipment reliance disappointed me.You cannot change the difficulty level if you elected "God of War" so I 'm stuck.  Example:   I'm in the Northri Stronghold looking for a whetstone, I land on a beach and face an Ogre and a Viken/Hel-Viken.  The Ogre throws stones hat curve towards you if you dodge close to the outer paved circle around the fire brazier/bowl.  Why he does not punch the rock to smithereens as he had done before I don't know.  Another example is a fight you have as you enter Helheim and try to go past the locked gate.  You have to climb down a tall spire which has a treasure chest caught in frozen vines halfway down.  After climbing down you  enter a bowl-like arena.  An "Ice-Viken?" appears right next to an huge gap into an abyss, you can stun him fairly easily but then Kratos throws him into the middle of the arena where he recovers instead of the abyss right next to him.  Eventually you wait for a lucky break and Kratos does throw him into the abyss.  The rest of the enemies have many ranged attacks so the combination of Ice-Viken and them is painful to overcome without luck.  I also did not experience the "reduced damage" the tips mentioned that battered enemies would have.  That could be simply a mathematically small percentage of total damage that is actually reduced and is difficult to see in the heat of combat.  It is also frustrating that even weak enemies have ranged attacks that are devastating to Kratos' health whereas his ranged attacks are weak - even against weak enemies.  This reduces Kratos from "God of War" to a simple grunt with godly aspirations trying desperately to upgrade equipment from too ineffectual to barely adequate which, to me, is a great pity.Other than the tedium of repeating fights until you luck out.  Levelling Kratos was fun and made sense if you ignore my previous point that he's a god, not a grunt.  I enjoyed the story and the graphics is GREAT.  The keyboard/mouse combinations were easy to learn and made sense during play and combat.  Character movements and actions are brilliantly done and you can almost forget you are not watching a movie.  The difficulty setting I was unhappy with for the reasons I stated but the combination of enemies at the level I chose was obviously perfectly chosen to give the player the most difficult combination of enemies possible, I can understand that.  One surprise was that the enemies were upgraded during the same fight from level 5 in one instance to level 7, now that was unexpected.In all I love the game even with the issues stated.  It is an old game and my comments are aimed at giving occasional players like myself a heads-up on difficulty level choices.This part comes months later:I finished "God of war" difficulty, hating the fights.  I replayed at "Give me a challenge" and loved the fights, you can actually use all these special moves effectively, as well as strategise some other than "run and dodge and die till you luck out".  The last fight with Baldur was "run and dodge again" but overall - play the game at "give me a challenge" level - great fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I approached this game from the standpoint of a father, expecting it to depict the typical struggles of a child growing up with a harsh, distant and unresponsive father. I thought God of War would teach me about realtionship between a father and son. Instead, it made me look deep into myself.	The main story focues on a journey of father and son through beautiful, spectacular yet sometimes harsh lands based on Norse mythology. However, the journey is just the background to the realtionship developing between the two. 	God of War immerses players in it's world thanks to it's camera, which stays close to main characters and seamlessly transitions to scripted cinematic events. The sound work and music further enhance this immersive experience. The graphics are spectacular.	The gameplay mechanics – combat, exploration, collectible hunts - rely on modern design principles, refined and polished to an incerdibely high level. However, the game fails to introduce any meaningful, innovative gameplay elements. This leads to simplified puzzles that almost solve themselves, as a means of avoiding player frustration. At the same time, the game offers depth and challenges through additional bossfights and light build-making options. The suprisingly wide roster of active skills, further increases player agency during combat.	In the end, the main strength of God of War, it's defining element, is it's writing. The story is incredible, with a narrow pool of well defined characters, each with distinct personalities, goals and interactions that enrich the narrative, creating an unforgettable experience. 	God of War proves that videogames can become artistic masterpieces, telling mature, emotional stories. Most of all, it proves that this medium can successfuly convey a message.	I strongly recommend this game.If you are interested in an overly analytic video version of this review then check out my youtube channel:

You'll be replaying the same areas with new abilities or items that allow you discover areas previously closed off. Not many cutscenes, the story is mainly told through dialogue as you play. There are cutscenes its just not cutscene heavy which I love. The characters chat as you play which is the main source of lore and story telling. Its as good as Laslow in GTA3. The writing is some of the best in gaming, equal to Naughty Dog. Borrows heavily from dark souls when it comes to the Valkyrie fights and button layout. You're not sacrificing gameplay for story. Both are stellar. This is a game that will stay with you long after you finish ng++ (which is required to complete your armor sets). A lot of games have the problem of trying to create a deep story and just come off as pretentious. God of War is full of heart and honesty. It's not trying to be anything. The main character isn't a hero, he's broken and kind of an ahole. He can kill Gods but he doesn't know how to be a father, and instead treats his son like a soldier, all while hiding and ashamed of his past. The best stories don't have a right or wrong, they navigate the grey areas as the characters just try to get by the best they can. Every. Single. NPC. is a fully fleshed out with unique personality that brings a lot to the story. The acting and writing is unbelievably good. It puts most movies to shame. Gear has meaningful stats and great cosmetics. Build crafting is based on mods you apply to your weapon along with enchantmentsI've played this multiple times on Playstation and I had to rebuy it on Steam for those sweet sweet frames. This is one of the greatest games ever made and its about time PC players get to enjoy it.Buy this game. It's worth your time and your money, you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War (2018) is a fantastic action-adventure game that combines intense combat, challenging quests, and a compelling story into one incredibly well packed game. The game follows Kratos, a Spartan warrior who is trying to move on from his troubled past and start a new life in the land of the Norse gods.One of the standout features of God of War are the varied quests. Throughout the game, players will embark on a variety of missions that range from exploration and puzzle-solving to epic boss battles. The Realm Tears, in particular, are a highlight, as they offer challenges that test players' skills and offer unique rewards such as Realm Dust which is used to enhance your gear.In addition to the quests, God of War also features optional intense and thrilling Valkyrie fights. These powerful enemies offer a significant challenge and require players to use all of their skills and abilities to emerge victorious.But perhaps the most impressive aspect of God of War is its story. The developers did an amazing job of weaving together Norse mythology and Kratos' personal journey in a way that is both engaging and emotionally impactful. Without spoiling too much : The relationship between Kratos and his son Atreus is particularly well done, and their journey together is one of the highlights of the game.Overall, God of War is a must-play for fans of action-adventure games. Its fun quests, challenging battles, and incredible story make it a standout experience that is sure to satisfy everyone with a need for Story-Rich Adventure games.

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic release by Sony that transcends the God of War franchise from a machismo hack-and-slash bloodbath into a mature, action-packed epic journey.  We get to see a different side of Kratos, with excellent voice acting from Christopher Judge (Stargate SG-1), with excellent character building and story arc.  The gameplay mechanics are great.  Controls feel responsive, with numerous ways to fight enemies.  Encounters are challenging, especially on the "Give me God of War" difficulty.  The graphics are some of the best on the PC right now, and the game runs well even on older hardware with DLSS enabled.  I had a fantastic time doing all of the side quests and completing the challenges.  I am still not halfway through and have had 34 hours of fun, action-packed adventure.  I have not bought a $60 game that I feel better about with my investment than this one.  Buy if you like games like the Witcher or Skyrim, you may like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War (2018) breathes new life into the iconic series, offering a stunning sequel that reimagines Kratos' world. This masterpiece seamlessly blends incredible features, artistry, and narrative, immersing players in a richly detailed Norse mythology that leaves you craving more.The game's visual presentation is nothing short of breathtaking. , delivering an unparalleled aesthetic experience. Vibrant, detailed landscapes bring the world to life, while the unique art direction draws heavily from Norse mythology, setting it apart from other titles. The smooth transitions between scenes and gameplay create an epic, cinematic feel that will leave you in awe.God of War's gameplay strikes a perfect balance between accessibility and depth. , embodying the weight and power of a god. The Leviathan Axe feels satisfyingly weighty, with each blow delivering tactile feedback. The combat system finds a sweet spot between simplicity and challenge, offering flexible options through unlockable abilities. Atreus isn't just a sidekick; he provides valuable support with ranged attacks and rune abilities, adding depth to every encounter.The game world is a joy to explore. While the progression is linear, you'll find rewarding branching paths that encourage curiosity. A central hub connects to diverse realms, each with its own distinctive visual identity. Between intense combat scenarios, uncomplicated puzzles offer a welcome breather, allowing you to appreciate the stunning environment around you.At its core, God of War is a story about relationships. , driving the narrative forward. Well-developed secondary characters leave a lasting impression, brought to life by top-notch voice acting and dialogue. As you progress, you'll witness the growth of both Kratos and Atreus as individuals and as a family, adding layers of depth to an already rich story. Its blend of stunning visuals, engaging combat, and emotional storytelling creates an unforgettable gaming experience that reignites the spark of Kratos' epic adventures. Whether you're a fan of action games, compelling narratives, or breathtaking visuals, God of War delivers on all fronts, making it a must-play title for any gaming enthusiast.

I don't have the most powerful graphics card (GTX 1070), but the game still looks spectacular even when testing on the lowest settings. Consistently a 55+ FPS running game, though it tanks a tiny bit with highly moving cutscenes.At the time of this review, I'm roughly 30 hrs in, and "nearing the end" for the story. I've done about half of the side-quests, and at no time has the game felt like it was hand-holding the challenge. Especially the Valkyries. I'm planning to 100% the game and update the review when that's complete, but it's been a genuine fun experience so far, and well worth the wait :)EDIT: Another 15 hrs later, and I've 100%ed the game; I decided not to go back for NG+, as the only real difference would be end-game armor that would require basically another 100%ing of it. So you could easily drop 100+ hrs on this game. If you like Norse mythology, are a God of War fan, or just like a ripped dad saying "boy" a lot, get the game. The voice acting was fantastic, combat was challenging but never entirely impossible, and the story that's been set up is something that's a genuine happiness once you get to the end. It's a dad and his son going up a mountain to spread ashes, and they just so happen to kill a few gods along the way - get the game, it's a lot of fun, and very much worth it at any price. Easily a 10/10 game

_childDocuments_.review: God of War has an engaging and well-written story and this story is the USP of this game. There's never a lull in the plot and it made me keep returning to play the game every day after work. World building is very skilfully done and the rewards and collectibles do not feel lame like they tend to do in some story driven action games. The armour system was a mixed bag for me. Even though I kept improving my armour steadily as I progressed through the main story and did a few side quests here and there, I found the higher tier armour to not necessarily look as good or as "legendary" as I had hoped. I wish there was a transmog system where I could put on the highest tier armour pieces I owned with the best stats but visually mix and match the pieces I actually liked the look of. The combat gameplay is satisfying and there is a wide swathe of unlockable moves and runic attacks but it does get repetitive very soon due to the narrow enemy variety. I found myself unable to remember most of the advanced moves I unlocked in each of the weapon skill trees and stuck to only a few of them. Things get interesting if you decide to face all bosses of a certain type in the optional side quests. These bosses can and will kick your ass but do not expect amazing rewards after beating them all. Overcoming that challenge is supposed to be the real reward. The main story boss fights are a cakewalk in comparison.I had no issues with the performance of the game on my PC, not even any frametime stutters which are unfortunately commonplace in modern open-world AAA games on PC. I didn't have even a single crash. The only major miss in this PC port is the lack of customizable FOV. The default FOV in this game is awful and would give me motion sickness during combat until I discovered that I could increase the FOV using a modding tool called Flawless Widescreen. I increased the FOV by 25%, and then everything was good.Overall I was very pleased with the game entirely because of the story and lore and am looking forward to Ragnarok whenever it gets released on PC. I hope Santa Monica does better with the side quests, armour system and main story boss variety in the next one.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War 4 had my attention ever since it was released 4 years ago, but due to it being a PlayStation exclusive at the time, I didn’t get to play it right away. Yet, I was still eager to play it. To be honest I missed the exact point when the port to pc came, so the game lost my focus for a bit. But when the winter sale came around and the sale was presented to me in the prime spot on the front page, I just couldn’t say no.Don’t be scared off by the 4 in the title, it’s no necessity to have played the previous entries of this franchise for you to understand the story. Even without the backstory of Kratos, the story of him and his son is just as touching not knowing what happened to Kratos in Greece. But I do have to admit that some points just hit you way harder when you know the background of some things.In short: I loved the story.You really notice the ammount of effort that Sony Santa Monica put into the characters and dialogue.In the following I will talk about the opening sequence of the game, so if you want to go in completely blind, just skip to the next topicIt is the way the game protrays it's characters and tells it's story, what sets this game apart from others. The best example for this is Faye, Kratos's passed wife and Atreus's mother. You never get to meet her in the game. Neither through a prologe or any flashbacks, yet you get to know her through other people in the world who knew her or when our protagonists talk about her. The further you get in your journey, the better you get to know her. By the end you might even have a picture of her just by the impression she left on the world.Combined with the character development of the whole cast, which doesn't just include the two protagonists, makes this world feel alive. It is seeing brothers grow closer or parents finding lost connections again, that make it feel like this world does not just exist for you to interact with, but it already existed before you and will continue to after your adventure.I think the main story took me about 30 hours to complete if you subtract the time of exploring and doing side-quests in the meanwhile. The side-quests offer an additioal 10 to 15 hours.Since I don't want to spoil any of it, because it is a completely different experience when you go into it blind.On the same notice you have to appreaciate the wonderfully designed world of Midgard and 4 other realms of norse mythology.For those not familiar: Midgard is basically the equivalent to our earth. This is where the main part of the game takes place. Because of that they probably also spent a lot of time on the design of this place. Everywhere you go and every new or hidden area you discover offers stunning visuals and level design. This of course if even more the case in sotry relevant areas since the focus naturally falls on those.Yet, the other realms available to you don't fall far behind in this category. Since I don't want to take too much of the wonder away when setting foot into a new realm, I'll just discuss two of the realms here.The first additional realm you visit is Alfheim. Mianly being lived in by both light and dark elves, it doesn't pose such a great look when you first visit it, but when you leave you get to see a lightfilled world full of life. Even though later on there is little reason to return here except for the valkyries(we'll get to that later), I did a couple times just to take in the magnificent visuals of this place.While you could say that the fighting-system has a bit of a souls-like flare, it yet differs greatly from it. You don't have acces to as many options to defeat your enemies as you might see in other games in terms of weapon variety. After all you just have 3 ways to kill your enemies really. You have the leviathan axe, your fists and another element I will not discuss because of spoiler reasons. Additionally, you can choose between runic attacks, which are more powerful attacks using magic with a cooldown and other skills you can unlock though the skill tree. You also have a rage meter that fills up over time. When activated, you change to your fists and start hammering away at your opponents. This fills up your health and deals significant ammounts of damage. But Kratos himself is no the only one on the battlefield.Atreus poses another big facotr in the combat of God of War. He helps defeat Enemies by stunning them or summoning powerfull spirits. He is even able to interrupt some of the attacks stronger foes throw at you later in the game. This becomes particularly important in the fight against some of the optional end-game bosses.While the game is not as hard as some other titles it is especially crucial on the higher difficulties to master all the aspects of God of wars combat to defeat your foes.While the enemies start off as challenging and varying, they become more and more repetetive later one, since they stop introducing new enemy types at about the mid point of the game.Since we're already on the topic of repetitive enemies, I have to mention the trolls. The first boss type enemy you fight in the tutorial area is one of these trolls. If you have seen the gameplay trailer, you probably know which I mean. While this first encounter is fun and also challenging at times, this fight repeats itself throughout the game over and over again. Even though the appearance of the trolls get varied slightly over the different encounters, the moveset stays mostly the same. This appears all the more disappointing when you take into account that the previous titles of the series was all the more remarkable.Yet, there is a perfect example that you can also handle this incredibly better in the same game.The Valkyries are a set of bosses seperate from the main story line. They are spread over the realms with different levels each. So there are some you can fight early on but for some you should wait until later on in the game. Although in this case they are all of the same enemy type as well, they all pose a unique boss fight, since every Valkyrie holds another exclusive attack, which brings a challenging change into these boss fights. This can also be said about the final of these challenging bosses, because she not only deals incredible ammounts of damage and is the highest level enemy you will encounter in the game, but combines all the moves mastered by the others.This poses a very challenging boss fight and combines all that you have learned in the previous fights.I had a blast with the game. At the time of writing this, I have spent about 50 hours with the game and have aquired all achievements. Yet, I plan on completing the game on "give me god of war" next. This is the game's highest difficutly in which it kinda breaks it's own rules just to mess with the player and provide one of the most challenging expirences I have played yet.The movie worthy story is masterfully written, with seeing this father and son duo growing together, being worthy of the Game of the year award it won back when it came out.I can only recommend to play it if you are at the slightest interested in story games or just wants a challenging combat experience or just to explore this wonderful world.

_childDocuments_.review: Atreus is the sweetest little boy and I want to cry or squeal so often watching him and Papa Kratos. There's so much quiet references and subtext to past games that it's so wonderful. Between Kratos trying to teach Atreus how to be a person to being a warrior, and being a good father in the process. He tries to express affection and holds back several occasions. I grew up with the violent blood for blood, Kratos just being his namesake - the god of strength, might. Now he's having to channel the strength into his most difficult journey yet - being a man. Kratos deserves a soft epilogue, and a full, pulsing story. _childDocuments_.review: SYSTEM:CPU = AMD Ryzen 5900XGPU = EVGA RTX 3080 ULTRA FTW3RAM = 32GB at 3600MHzREVIEW:I've argued with many friends that PlayStation games would eventually come to PC, especially God of War. They all doubted me, but here I am proving them wrong. I'm not an optimistic person so I had no hopes in this ever happening. However, it did and I am extremely happy that I got to experience the one game that I've always wanted to play for years, God of War. I have no interests in owning any console besides the Nintendo Switch which is for family purposes. When I heard about the game porting to PC, I was incredibly excited and had low expectations regarding optimization and performance. Boy was I truly wrong about that. This game runs ridiculously smooth on my system and I haven't encountered any broken bugs, glitches, or exploits to ruin my experience. All of my settings are maxed out with DLSS off on my 1440p 144hz monitor. Depending on the area I am exploring or how much stuff is happening, I am never dipping below 60 fps which are my minimum frame rate standards for a pleasant experience. If anything, my frame rate consists above 80 fps which is more than enough for me to thoroughly enjoy the experience. I am not exaggerating when I say that this game runs not only smooth, but looks incredibly beautiful and gorgeous graphics-wise. I have seen my friends play God of War on their PlayStation 4s and the graphics definitely do not beat the PC version.Many people regard God of War's game play style as a Souls or Bloodborne type game. I've never found myself invested in Souls-like games since to me, it never involved any interesting story or lore behind it. God of War game play is incredibly explosive, fast paced, and methodological requiring players to be flexible and maneuverable such as blocking, countering, rolling, and dodging. I've had incredible fun just beating people down with my fists, shield, or axe in a variety of ways. Certain enemies will require you to engage them using certain weapon sets, but it's not too invasive nor a nuisance. The crafting/upgrading system is this game is basic and generic which is something I appreciate for this game because I am not required to continuously farm a bunch of materials just to craft or upgrade something. What makes this more easier to handle is that you only have to worry about Kratos and his son being upgraded. The crafting/upgrading system contributes to Kratos's power and leveling. Certain builds will emphasize on the type of play style that you want to go for. If you want, you can even find optimal builds online that other players have constructed that may match your play style. The skill system is pretty basic and generic; however, the skills themselves are super awesome because it just adds the experience of intense and violent game play to the game. You just feel like an ultimate bad ass when you unlock these skills because not only are they useful, but their animations look awesome.I am well aware of the story already since I spoiled myself during the release time for God of War on the Playstation 4. The story is mesmerizing with rich characters and dialogue, notably the father-son relationship between Kratos and his son. Other characters are quite comedic, but have interesting characteristics about them, making amusing and unique. I will not say any spoils, so I will end it there. The theme connecting to Norse mythology is interesting and wonderful to learn about when you pick up lore-related items throughout the game. Don't get me wrong, Greek mythology is just as interesting but I am happy to see that this new version of God of War is pairing so well with Norse mythology. Remember that this is a video game so don't take anything too serious or rather, the hypothetical truth. God of War does not reflect 100% of what Norse mythology says according to scholars, books, legends, and so forth, but it does a good job representing it. Besides God of War's story and theme, the atmosphere and scenery is just way too immersive. When combined with the game's other elements as previously mentioned, it fits all together to create a near-perfect game and experience.RATING:After everything I have mentioned, I'd rate this game a solid 10/10. It is an extremely well polished game that contains great game play with an enticing story, theme, and atmosphere to it. For being a PlayStation port, it runs extremely well since lately, other Triple A games on the PC have not been doing well regarding optimization and performance. I guess some can also include story or game play as well? I honestly have no complaints about this game whatsoever nor do I have anything to add to improve the game. Some people may perceive my points regarding the crafting/upgrading and skill system as negative; however, I found these to be perfectly fine for God of War the way that it is. The point is, no video game will ever be perfect because there can always be more room for improvement. This is limited to what technology is used to improve the game and how advanced that technology is. I apologize in advance if I have not covered enough details in my review, but this is what I can only think of so far throughout my experience in God of War. Thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: I find it hard to understand the hype around GoWThe worst thing about this game are the fights which happen to be a significant part of the gameplay. Not only there's just a few different types of enemies, but they have no AI and their arsenal is like literally 2 different attacks. And if this wasn't enough, their design is so poor that I wouldn't be able to call them memorable. The game feels generic, and the story moments that are supposed to make this experience special or at least emotional, are few.Exploration is limited by invisible walls that stop you from falling off the cliff, etc. For most of the time, you'll be running in a predesigned corridor that will lead you to another battle once every 2 minutes of exploration. To be fair, there are a lot of little secrets and puzzles to be found and solved, despite the fact that you'll be exploring a narrow path. Artistic design of the game is ok, but I've seen better.  Character design is nice, but characters are few. Locations look nice, but they tend to be disneyish and by far too colourful. To put GoW in a perspective: Dark Souls 3, or Sekiro offer a far better combat, exploration and more satisfying progress at the price of extreme difficulty.Hellblade has got a grimmer world, better art style of locations and enemies, and deeper, more mature story set in the realms of nordic mythology, but it's  short and depressing.I can understand that some people may find this generic aaa slasher to be the sweet spot, but I prefer games with more character, and I appreciate riskier decisions made by the devs.To conclude, despite all my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ above, GoW is a good game. It's got a few great moments and very few obvious flaws.81/100

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest...I was never a fan of the classic God of War games. I had friends that played them and I tried them out once or twice when they released, but they just felt shallow to me. When I play long narrative games, I sort of need a compelling story or at least a set of interesting characters...GOW 1-3 had some of that, but it felt overshadowed by the spectacle and gore. The best word I can think of to describe them is "immature". GOW 2018 changed my entire perspective on them. It is a work of art and masterfully builds up the main character in a way that the original games never did, but it also wouldn't have worked nearly as well if they had. It's a great standalone story that enriches the original games knowing that this is where they lead up to. It's incredible that Santa Monica studios was able to pull it off as well as they did. Major kudos to them and Sony, and special thanks to Bear McCreary - the soundtrack is breathtaking! It still has flaws (most people dislike the semi-repetitive side quests and tedious fights), but for me, it more than makes up for them with believable characters, satisfying plots, beautiful scenery, spot-on character designs, and lore. Lots and lots of lore (which I loved...I'm a sucker for Norse mythology). Beyond all that, it also brings a fascinating and emotional take on fatherhood that I think many people can identify with. It was unexpected but very much appreciated. To anyone on the fence about whether to buy, I highly recommend giving it a try even if you never played the originals. It was well worth it to me, even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War (2018) is the fourth – or perhaps like the eighth, depending on what you count – game in the God of War series. Set in the lands of the Norse Gods after Kratos pretty much wrecked the Greek world, Kratos has been living a quiet life with his wife and son. Naturally, by the time the game has started, his wife has died – apparently of natural causes – and she requests that Kratos and their son, Atreus, take her ashes to the top of the highest mountain in all the land to scatter them.Needless to say, things get a bit complicated, the Norse gods get involved, and before you know it you are off on an adventure through… well, the majority of the nine realms of Norse mythology, though in truth most of your adventure is in one realm (Midgard, i.e. the world of mortals) with your excursions to the other worlds little more than brief dungeons or series of challenges at most.The game is not enormously long, but it has a huge amount of side content which greatly stretches out its length. There’s a lot of places to explore and treasures to find, but the game is actually a bit short on actual monsters to fight.The problem is, the game actually runs out of new things to show you surprisingly early in its length. While there’s ostensibly a number of types of enemies, in reality there’s only a few actually different types – basically a very fast one that jumps on you, a standard melee trash mob, an enemy with a shield, an enemy with a big hammer, an enemy that throws ranged attacks at you, a teleporting witch, a big hulking ogre, a werewolf, trolls with big clubs, some flying enemies who shoot blinding things at you and then engage in melee, some other flying enemies who shoot things at you and sometimes buff enemies, and trolls.The game shows you all these types of enemies pretty early, though, and as a result, it feels like the game runs out of things to throw at you long before the game’s length ends. It doesn’t help that there’s really only five bosses apart from the trolls (which are very similar to each other) resulting in the game feeling like it is lacking for actually interesting combat content – which it kind of is. You fight some bosses multiple times (for story related reasons, but still) and unfortunately, it kind of becomes old hat by the end. The nine Valkyrie bosses do try to mix things up a bit themselves, and are the most interesting boss fights in the game, but they, too, get repetitive after a while.For all the spectacle that the game has, the game’s combat is honestly pretty mediocre – and that’s very unfortunate, because there is a fair amount of it.This is broken up by exploration, which is okay, but nothing super amazing – it’s pretty standard “puzzles”, but they’re all very simple and mostly are pretty much the same, just “the puzzle pieces are hidden differently”.Really, the only thing the game has to make it stand out from the competition is presentation – but fortunately, it does have that in spades. The voice acting is really good, the characters are fun to interact with (even if Kratos himself is mum about things for much of the game), and if you are a fan of Norse mythology, you can see all sorts of fun references in here, along with the game’s various twists and attempts to make the gods the bad guys (because, this is, after all, God of War, the series infamous for deicide – and while gods do die, you will likely be disappointed by the number, though fans of Norse Mythology will also be able to predict who is going to die and more or less how).The game’s core relationship – between Atreus and Kratos – works well, even if it is frustrating at times with just how taciturn Kratos is, but you can see how scarred Kratos is from his past experiences. The game, then, is about Kratos coming out of his shell a little while his son has to figure out who he is and what is going on. Atreus helps out in combat, and also helps with some puzzles, and while none of it is particularly spectacular in execution it works well enough.All in all, I felt like the game stretched itself out too long relative to its interesting content – it added two grindy sidequests for no good reason, as the combat is not anywhere near good enough to justify them, and it just adds to the length of the game without adding to the main thing that the game delivers on – the story of the relationship between Kratos and Atreus and their role in the world, including Kratos’ own undesired role, as he clearly detests his own nature as a god and fears what his son will be like when he realizes that he, too, is a son – trying to keep things as low-key as possible while avoiding giving too much away.I would have liked to have seen more variety in bosses, even if it led to less side content – in fact, especially if it did so, because the side content was weak while the core story was the strongest part of the game. The game diluted itself too much, and didn’t deliver as strongly on its core promise as it could have.All in all, I liked it, but it reminded me of all of the largest issues that game design has long possessed, with a desire to add in more content, even when that extra content actually diminishes the product instead of adding to it. The actual game is only okay, and it is saved by the execution of everything around it.

At least they nailed it with God of War though, as IMO those are Sony's top 3 franchises.I am really loving the story and the gameplay of this entry to the God of War franchise, it is much more my style than the older GoW games. The graphics are great for a PS4 game and the world/art is beautiful. Excellent set piece battles which are kind of glorified cutscenes sometimes but it doesn't matter to me, it is so intense. I can't wait for Ragnarok to release on PC, hopefully it is up next after Ratchet and Clank (that one also *needs* to be a good port or it just won't sell, but Nixxes is at the helm for it, so it should be pretty good). I definitely would love Ragnarok before the new Horizon game, waaaaay more hyped for it, and it will sell very well on PC if they make it a great port just like God of War got.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I hate the new camera. You have to use a third party software to increase the FOV because they don't give any options for FOV within the game itself, and its just too close to Kratos' shoulder. Enemies are constantly flanking me while other enemies attack from the front, and then when I try to swing around to face the direction the arrows say attacks are coming from, I often end up taking the attack to the side of my face.It is so damn hard to keep track of all the enemies or keep them all on the screen, and its because of how close the camera is to Kratos. I don't have this issue on other third person action games like The Witcher 3 or FF7R.The other thing is all the hidden loading screens. Squeeze through this corridor, duck under this pillar, crawl under this pathway, climb this wall. Wait for the fast travel door to assemble, trek around the world tree. Oh you wanna switch realms? Wait for this 5 minute star gate sequence.It makes backtracking an absolute chore, and its so painfully obvious the dialogue during these sequences is there just to try to fill the tedium it makes me feel more annoyed.Also the resource management and upgrading your equipment. There's so few resources during the first half of the game, I didn't ever know if I should invest in my equipment or hold onto the resources for when I get better equipment later. I found myself constantly pulling up my web browser to look up the stats of the different armor pieces and how many resources they'll take to fully upgrade so I could decide whether or not to invest in them.I was also constantly looking up solutions to the different chests because I would look around for 5 minutes to find the last rune to break, and then when I finally found it and broke it, half the time my reward was a special ability I didn't even want to use because it didn't do enough damage. I just really would rather have had most of the rewards and upgrades and abilities come as rewards after bosses or mini-bosses so the game could focus more on combat instead of adding tedious mini-puzzles on top of the already tedious hidden loading screens and travel time. Which, speaking of travel time, don't even get me started on how much time I spent boating around the damn lake. Or the fact that two way fast travel is locked until the later half of the game.(STORY SPOILERS INCOMING)The story has its emotional moments, but its rather average and predictable overall. They dig in a bit into how Atreus is upset with Kratos' detachment and how he feels Kratos doesn't care, even at one point saying he wishes it had been Kratos who died instead of his mother. But they immediately gloss over it with Atreus saying "But I don't really mean that." So instead of Kratos having to muster up the emotional intelligence to understand how his son feels or forget his pride so he can admit to his son that he's been wrongfully distant, Atreus does most of the work in trying to forge a connection.Later, after finding out he's part god, Atreus starts getting violent and full of himself. But instead of Atreus facing any consequences by, say, getting himself severely hurt trying to fight Baldur or going off on his own or even fighting his own father -- this also gets glossed over when Kratos screams at him in Helheim. And just a minute later Atreus looks at a vision of himself killing Thor's cousin and says "Wait, that's not me. It can't be." Really, the only time Kratos ever has to face consequences for his poor parenting is when his son is sick. (END OF STORY SPOILERS)I also don't like how the sidequest with the valkyries gets locked behind mandatory time sinks. The last two valkyries are in helheim and niflheim -- so you have to beat 5 trials before you can get to the valkyrie in helheim. And in niflheim you can go straight to the valkyrie, but she's in the maze of mist and the mist timer is still active during the fight. So if you haven't gotten any of the equipment that increases the mist timer, you're not gonna have much time to try to complete that fight. So the devs expect you to go through the maze a bunch of times and get all the mist echoes for that equipment first before you attempt the fight with the valkyrie. And at that point in the game, I just wasn't willing to spend that much more time with tedium.After beating the game and deciding I'd had enough, I had 38 hours playtime. 10 of those hours was the main story, another 10 was sidequests, and the other 18 was just travel time - walking, boating, progressing through hidden loading screens, backtracking.It just honestly felt like I spent more time walking/boating around than I did actually engaging with meaningful gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War is a good game. Realistically speaking, it is a story that shows the relationship between father and son, that is, the rapprochement of father and son after their wife-mother died. Something similar to the bonding of me and my father, but without the bonding part...but enough jokes. The atmosphere of the game, the music and the fighting are very well done. There is a lot of lore about Norse mythology which is great, but I would like and hope that in the second part there will be a little more about Kratos and his Greek history and how exactly it all came about. One more thing, the variety of enemies is a bit low. The mini-bosses are more or less repeated, which is a shame. I have completed the game 100% everything except the Niflheim world. An optional world with, let's say, equipment farming. I did that part halfway through just enough to get to the last and best gear, which is more than necessary for the real final boss, Sigrun. That boss in itself is difficult in the range of EldenRing bosses. It's quite frustrating with all the combinations of various moves, and even with the best equipment it does a lot of damage. As for the pefromance game, it runs awesome with 70+ fps on a 2k monitor, RX5700XT graphics card. Which is great from Soni considering that Ghost of Thushima has a memory leak and stutters after 1 hour+ of playing. Good game this.

_childDocuments_.review: The first game that I have actually dumped time into since Skyrim. This game is amazing. From the combat, to the puzzles, to the story. I have already put in over 40 hours, with many more on the way as I go through the realms and start a New Game+. 10/10. This game runs well on my RTX 3070 Ryzen 9 5900HS laptop. At 1440p ultra, i can consistently get 40-60 fps when playing on my TV with a controller. Amazing? No. Good enough? Absolutely. Of course I could use DLSS or FSR or just turn down res/quality, but I'm ok with it on this game. Absolutely beautiful and stunning. The amount of content this game has to offer is immense. With an average of 30 hours of story time, the other realms go relatively unexplored and you may miss puzzles or resources here and there. Once you beat the story and look at the map, seeing 30% completion in Midguard alone goes to show how many hidden areas and side quests there are to do. And that's just in one of the realms. I haven't played with mouse and keyboard, only fiddled with the controls. Honestly would just recommend controller, for me it is just that type of game. The story is put together amazingly well. Honestly can not wait to see what this game has in store for me next! I do wish there were more skills to learn, even older games like Darksiders have way more combat combos. But that doesn't take away from how great the combat is, there is still plenty of options between the 3 ways Kratos has, and you also have Artreous. I would highly recommend this game to Skyrim players, Darksiders players, Dark Souls players, Cyberpunk, Fallout, etc. It is a different take on the RPG story side of things, expanding greatly on the action and adventure parts of it. While not necessarily open world, it feels like it should be considered somewhat open world! Once you finish the main story line, you get access to all of the portal gateways,  and you are free to roam anywhere you want. I see why it is not technically open world, but it is very close to it. Conclusion: 10/10 would recommend. If you haven't played this game, you don't know what you are missing out on!

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a "bad" game, but I would hesitate to recommend. I would say pick it up if it's on sale. It seems like the AAA sheen has tricked people into thinking this is some 10/10 masterpiece.Obviously, the graphics are good, and the interaction between dad and boi is entertaining. I even like how the data logs are written from the perspective of Atreus. It makes it actually fun to read. The stoic man that actually has emotions trope is pretty tired at this point, so that feels tedious.However, the gameplay is what I have a problem with. It feels like a game from 10 years ago. The controls feel sluggish, most enemies feel the same to fight, most encounters have the same format, every area is very on rails, and the amount of exposition in the first several hours is mind numbing. I don't need some in-depth explanation of every glowy macguffin I find. Every time you go into a partial cinematic and the game restricts your camera movement, it feels terrible. They literally make you fight a bunch of enemies in one section and you can't turn around, so if one sneaks behind you, you get hit. If you're in an encounter with several enemies, prepare to get stuck and cheap-shotted to death cause you can't roll through them. And what's an i-frame? You can fire off a special attack, and during that animation, another enemy can just start an attack and kill you before your attack completes.Another annoyance is that the UI is all over the place. There are so many one off submenus to equip and upgrade things that don't seem to matter that much, and the skill tree is just a glorified checklist.Also, the music is strictly mid.This feels like a 6-6.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: No Raw input support for mouse users (EDIT) This has been updated and fixed with the addition of a Precision mouse mode option. It no longer feels horrible to play with a mouse.. It was my biggest reason for not touching the game in over a month. Hopefully, going forward, Playstation Studios' pc ports will have RAW mouse input available at launch.No Exclusive full-screen option (EDIT) - After doing some research, it seems that devs are either not being given a choice or Microsoft is just doing a very good job at selling the idea that exclusive fullscreen is "completely" obsolete. Simply having it as an option, irregardless of whether the new flip model is being used would have been nice. Since it isn't an available option, there's no way to know for sure whether or not we could actually benefit from it, and that's kinda sad. Graphically and mechanically, the game is just as good as it was on console with the added benefit of PC specific performance and graphics options.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War is an excellent cinematic experience with high production values, amazing graphics, decent beat 'em up controls, and somewhat repetitive puzzle design. All in all, I've enjoyed it immensely on PC; however, I have a few critiques. First let's examine what this game does well. The entire game is one shot; there are no camera cut aways (unless you count bringing up the inventory), and the close angle makes the game feel intimate and cinematic. Kratos, the player character, has a long backstory that I, as a primarily PC gamer, was not aware of, although the game will eventually fill you in on some of it. In the opening scene, he's cutting down a tree, one of the last requests of his dead wife, and his facial expressions are instantly readable, and you sense the weight sitting on his shoulders. Throughout the entire game Atreus, Kratos's son, will accompany you, and their relationship is the main focus of God of War. Kratos is gruff, untrusting, harsh, and distant, while his son is precocious, trusting, and optimistic, and watching their characters develop is something I have rarely (if ever) experienced in a video game. As they travel through the realm of Midgard, they encounter a host of gods and monsters, all pulled from the weird, wonderful world of Norse mythology, depicted here in all of its strangeness. Originally released in 2018 as a Playstation 4 exclusive, God of War is gorgeous, its dense environments packed with color and detail. Really, it's amazing they released this title for the last console generation. On PC, it sports graphical improvements, such as higher textures and improved shadows and reflections. Unfortunately, on AMD GPUs, there are occasional frame drops, especially around the Lake of the Nine area. Capping my framerate to 60 lessened the severity of these drops; I noticed a few as low as 54 fps, which isn't very noticeable on a Freesync monitor. Just something to keep in mind, as the experience is apparently much smoother on Nvidia hardware. From a design standpoint, my biggest critique is the busy inventory screen. You can craft and upgrade Kratos's armor, Atreus's armor, and their weapons; additionally, you have several screens worth of skills to buy for both characters with XP. In a game very focused on its characters and immersion, I feel God of War too frequently asks you to pull yourself out of the game world to focus on RPG mechanics that don't exactly fit this type of button masher. Also, as you make your way through the game, you'll find yourself switching between combat, which occurs a little too infrequently for my tastes, and puzzles, which all feature Kratos throwing his ax at something. This puzzle design is a little too monotonous and frequent; I'd much rather focus on destroying dark elves and wraiths. Kratos and Atreus don't often fight more than a handful of enemies at once, and I wonder if this was a design limitation of the PS4 (maybe too many enemies tanked the framerate). These are fairly minor quibbles. If you're looking for a cinematic third person action game, then you can't go wrong with God of War.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough review to write because reading all the glowing reviews from consumers and in media, I feel like something must be wrong with me, but I did not enjoy most of my time with this game. It's beautfiully presented with some of the best graphics I've ever seen and all the actors do a very good job with their characters, but I'm here to play a game, not watch a movie and as a game this just falls painfully short. First, this game loves long repetitive animations and it's going to make you sit through every single one everytime you do anything. At around the 15 hour mark I just wanted to stop opening chests all together. Combat is clunky and difficulty is all over the place. There's a side quest with a series of 9 boss fights that will challenge you, but the rest of the game is surprisingly easy. Then there's the grind. There are two fully optional realms that are designed as challenges. They're silly, they're out of place, they waste the potential of these realms and the grind is so slow in one realm that it probably represented 5 or more hours of my final play time and it was not fun. The world is full of repetitive puzzles and lots of backtracking as certain events happen. Even the main story itself doesn't get going until the end and WOW, that end. It felt like the game was just getting started, there's an interesting reveal and then roll credits. It was so abrupt and the game teases a handful of realms and characters that you never even get to see. If this game didn't have the optional grind realms, if it didn't slow everything to a crawl with it's sluggish movement and combat, and if it didn't have the damage spunge enemies, there really isn't a whole lot to the main experience. This is my first God of War game being a PC only gamer and I'm just not getting what the fuss is all about. It was an excellent looking brawler with mediocre combat and all I see are 5/5 and 10/10 reviews. And the interface, ugh. Don't get me started on the interface. It's one of the slowest, most unintuitive and ugly interfaces I've seen in a while. It has none of the character of the setting of the game and it looks like some cheap mobile design. Maybe at some point I'll have a change of heart, maybe I'll appreciate it more when and if I get to play the sequel, but this game just didn't do much for me. To be fair I seem to be in a small minority here, so your mileage may vary, but I'm here to give you my honest opinion and when it was all said and done, this wasn't the experience I'd been waiting for all these years.

_childDocuments_.review: Conventionally good AAA story-based game. Would recommend it on sale.Some textures can get really grainy - I think it has something to do with looking at them from nearly parallel. Only really happens in a few specific areas, doesn't last super long. I did have one GPU crash about a third through the game, then I updated my drivers and it didn't happen again.Combat is good, but gets a bit stale IMO, so I won't be doing the side content. Estimates online said it would take me 20 hours but I beat it in 15, fwiw. That's not to say the game is too short, if anything I felt like a few missions were just padding the story out for no real reason.The characters are done well, but I wish some of the emotional low points for the protagonists were a bit lower. It's kind of a natural consequence from a hardened father and a literal child, but emotion definitely slips through the cracks more than being out in the open. That's the game's charm in many scenes, just wish it pushed a liiiiiiitle bit further. I feel like I'll remember the vibe pretty well, but there weren't many scenes where I was taken aback.End of the game does a fair amount of sequel baiting. It's a complete story on its own, but if this game is your jam then you'll be annoyed that ragnarok isn't already available.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War takes God of War, mixes it with Norse Mythology and adds a new perspective to it, as well as changing the lore behind the Aesir, and other Norse creatures a little bit (read in the spoiler section).While it's known that Thor, Odin and most other Aesir are arrogant bastards, here you will experience a brand new view from the other side. Combat is smooth, sound design is S+, the characters have depth. Overall, without giving any spoilers I will absolutely recommend this game, if you enjoy Norse Mythology in the slightest!Baldur in Norse Mythology embraces his new gift of invulnerability - here he wants to kill Freya for it. Loki is absent from the lore entirely, until the very end. Jörmungandr definitely does not approve of others, regardless of who they are.Mimir was beheaded by the Vanir, and remained a loyal friend to Odin until Ragnarök.And a lot moreNow - if you're a fan of Norse Mythology, like me, reading this might make you shiver, but don't worry - it's executed really well. Mimir still serves his purpose, Baldur is made extremely interesting, the big Loki moment will get you jumpy, etc., etc.Personally I have two issues with the game however:1. Alfheim took way too long. It was so much mindless fighting into the same one or two enemies over and over again that it became very stale. 2. Atreus after learning that he was a god, became a power hungry, arrogant ass. So far so good - however it ended way too abruptly. You arrive in Helheim, Kratos tells him off once, and that's that. He's just made a huge leap in character development and became wise. Still, that's 2 things out of probably 30 I really enjoyed. Combat is very smooth, the sound design is great, the characters (albeit lore inaccurate) are very charming in their own ways, and after beating Baldur for the last time you don't feel hate - you understand that he is a broken god that lived through torment. He was very compassionate towards Freya at first, as you can see in Helheim. He was no monster. My absolute favorite bit though was Jörmungandr.The sound design was astonishingly well done - the first time shocked me, the second time I thought I remember how unsettling his voice was until I felt uneasy again, the third time I just accepted that I would fall back into my chair slightly. 8.5/10 Alfheim really annoyed me, and there could have been more characters. Though I 100% understand that that was saved for Ragnarök :')

_childDocuments_.review: I am incredibly happy that I finally got to experience this fantastic game, what a ride it was. I knew of the high praise this game had received but I didn't think that it was possible for the game to actually live up to the hype, I was very much wrong and happy to be. This was my first introduction to the God of War series and what an introduction it was. This game does such a good job at getting newcomers settled into the universe, very well done. Even though I've never played the other games, I still got a great sense of history from Kratos's character, he felt like a broken man that has seen a lot in his lifetime and this really adds to the dynamic that Kratos has with Atreus. One element of this game that I worried would be poor were the environments, from the gameplay I had seen the environments showcased were the same looking and there wasn't many new environments that I saw but now after having played the game, I can say that it wasn't the case, there is many different environments and some of them are just utterly breathtaking to lay your eyes on, some of the best looking environments that I've seen in a game recently. Another thing I loved about this game was the lore, there is so much of it and it is so interesting to learn more tid bits through finding things in the world. I was lucky enough to go into this game blind in terms of the story and I'm thankful I was able to because the story in this game was just so damn good, so many badass, touching and philosophical moments and the story was the perfect length. You can't talk about this game without talking about the combat, it is immensely satisfying and it only gets better with upgrades to gear and new weapons. The combat can be challenging but it doesn't feel unfair ever, through trial and error, combat can be mastered and the game does a good job at gradually giving you more challenging enemies. When going into this game, I knew I would probably enjoy it but I wasn't prepared for just how good it would be, it has now become one of my favourite games and I eagerly await the sequel, feels good to now be a part of that hype.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was amazing! It might not be perfect, but it is beautiful, it has an enticing story with some twists and it can be challenging but it is fair. It also managed to give an experience of having a follower that's not a hindrance, only few games can do that (Bioshock infinite would also be a good example). We eventually grow to love the characters and their interactions. The relationship  between Kratos and his son is tense and more often than not, it's a bad example of fatherhood, but it is why the good moments feel so liberating. Also, the voice actors are great in their role, especially Kratos' voice actor (Christopher Judge) who has an imposing voice that always leaves you wanting to hear more, even if the character himself is a man of few words. One last thing, the action is also so fluid that sometimes you wonder if you're in a cinematic or not, which helps you enjoy the world to the fullest. I recommend playing it on a big screen if you can, the world can be so detailed I often stopped to just look around and admire the scenery.TLDRIf you don't own a Playstation so you haven't been able to play this game until now, buy it, you won't regret it.

My only complaint, and I mean only one, is that I only was only able to spend 55 hours to do absolutely everything. If it were up to me, I'd want 250 hours+ of being in these realms with these characters. The narrative, the environments, the dialogue and the gameplay itself is all master-class when it comes to gaming. There was never a single second that I got bored, or thought of getting this collectible/doing this side mission was a chore or bother.It is immersive, gripping and breathtaking, just as Keanu Reeves would say. This is also after 100%'ing Ragnarok as well, and I cannot wait to buy Ragnarok again on PC when it gets a port and do it all over again for that game as well. The series, so far, is one of my favorite pieces of gaming that I have ever played. It is in my top 3 of all time, and is a staple of a game that must be played if you consider yourself any form of 'gamer.' It set a new standard at its time of release for what gaming can be and do. If you haven't played it, I couldn't recommend a better game. Nothing but praise and love for everything this universe has to offer and for Santa Monica Studios for crafting it with love and such attention to detail. Truly a 10/10 game/series.

_childDocuments_.review: Complete playthrough of the game excluding grind took me only 31,5 hours on the highest difficulty (not GOD OF WAR). It only lasted 3 weeks in the real world, so the game definitely pulled me in. Story - 9/10Without spoilers. The plot, to be honest, moved very fast, I sometimes even wanted to stop collecting resources just to find out what was next. World - 10/10The world is amazing, filled with a lot of different interesting things that you want to explore. Especially in this respect the game is greatly enhanced by Mimir as a companion, his stories and narratives are perfect. Combat - 7/10The combat system and its development is quite non-linear, and cool combos can be twisted as you please. And considering that weapons and armor are upgraded as you progress through the story, you don't even have to worry about it, the main thing is to loot a couple of chests with steel around the corner.Post story - 3/10After the main plot I was left with the worlds of Muspelheim and Niflheim, Valkyries, collectibles, and Odin's ravens to trek through.Muspelheim given that one of the Valkyries is there, I closed it out with a bang. Though some of the challenges are overly long, but overall not bad for a trained player as a final overall challenge.The Valkyries are very good, they are as varied as they can be, with their own victory schemes that end up revealing an interesting part of the history of the world.Niflheim is worth visiting just for the Valkyries, otherwise just grind material for nothing (armor, not much there considering I was almost through the game at that point).Odin's Ravens and collectibles are only for those who do not regret their time.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game held back by mediocre combat, controls and bosses. 8.5/10Almost everything else is great about the game: story, characters, voice acting, graphics, audio and music etc were all done exceptionally well. Story doesn`t drown you in details nor makes you try to come to answers yourself, so it hits that perfect balance of storytelling that most games fail to do. Huge props to that. Sound effects and overall immersion is phenomenal and I am really glad I played this game with 7.1 surround sound on.The first thing that I really didn`t like, is how mediocre the combat is. You have to go through a long portion of the game doing the same things and getting a few new skills here and there, but overall it making it not that interesting for a large portion. The first time I actually felt really into combat itself was when I had around 90% of the game completed, which for me is far too late. I did do the most challenging trials with the full potential available which was awesome, but it was really bland before that. Second thing was the controls itself. It took me a long time to figure out how to switch weapons efficiently and do the combos. This was most prominent when you get the other tool at your disposal to use, when all things got so mixed together and was easy to break the chain of attacks just pressing one things on the other side of the controller, because the weapon tool mechanics don`t match one another via controls, so it did happen a lot of times that I stopped mashing enemies because I pressed a wrong button in a 15+ button combo. This is all mostly on me, but they could have made it more simpler to not mix and match controls on both of them.The third and final thing is the repeating bosses. You will only fight less than 5 bosses variants throughout the whole game. It`s always the same ones but different color (element), and its the same when you do it the first time and the 10th, nothing changes except their HP and damage dealt. And almost all of the other bosses that are not repeated are gimmick bosses, waiting for you to do a specific thing that will prop a cutscene to continue on...which was really disappointing for some of them...Overall, a really good game, and one to remember, for sure, but I really hope things above change in the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Subject: A Masterpiece in Gaming - God of War 2018Feedback:I recently had the privilege of diving into the world of God of War 2018, and I must say, it was an extraordinary gaming experience that left me in awe. The game excelled in multiple aspects, from its stunning graphics to its captivating storyline, and I'd like to take a moment to share my thoughts on each element.Graphics (10/10):God of War's visuals are nothing short of breathtaking. The attention to detail in character models, landscapes, and environments is astounding. The game's use of Norse mythology is beautifully portrayed through the stunning design of realms like Midgard and Helheim. The graphics alone make it a masterpiece.Storyline (9/10):The narrative in God of War is a true standout. It's a story of redemption, fatherhood, and personal growth. Kratos' journey with his son, Atreus, is emotionally gripping and takes unexpected twists and turns. While it's nearly flawless, there were a few moments where the pacing felt slightly off, but overall, it's a remarkable narrative.Sound (10/10):The audio design in God of War is exceptional. The orchestral score perfectly complements the epic scale of the game, enhancing the emotional depth of each moment. The voice acting, particularly from Kratos and Atreus, is outstanding, bringing their characters to life in a way that few games achieve.Gameplay (10/10):God of War offers a well-balanced blend of combat, exploration, and puzzle-solving. The combat mechanics are deep and satisfying, making each encounter a thrill. The Leviathan Axe is a brilliantly designed weapon, and the variety of enemies keeps the gameplay fresh throughout. The integration of Atreus as a combat partner adds an extra layer of strategy and depth.Environment (10/10):The game's world-building is top-notch. The different realms you explore are distinct and immersive, each with its own unique atmosphere and challenges. From the lush forests of Alfheim to the desolation of Helheim, the environments are meticulously crafted, making you feel like you're a part of this mythical world.Conclusion:God of War 2018 is a gaming masterpiece that sets a new standard for the industry. Its flawless graphics, captivating storyline, incredible sound design, engaging gameplay, and immersive environments combine to create an unforgettable experience. While no game is entirely perfect, God of War comes incredibly close. It's a must-play for any gaming enthusiast.Overall Score: 9.8/10In summary, God of War 2018 is a shining example of what video games can achieve as an art form. It's a journey that will stay with me for a long time, and I can't recommend it highly enough to anyone looking for an exceptional gaming experience.
