_childDocuments_.review: IN-DEPTH REVIEW WITH NO SPOILERS!TLDR: This is honestly one of the best games i've ever played. The story is rich, the combat is incredible and fully customisable. You can completely follow or discover your own playstyle. The voice acting is better than most Hollywood films. The end game is fantastic and adds a lot to the game. 10/10 absolutely 10/10.Of about 20 years of playing games this is one of the best games I have ever played and I regret not having played it sooner. I'll break this review down to component parts so any gamer can look at the bits that they appreciate the most. 1. Story:The story is absolutely incredible. Rich, detailed and full of twists and turns that nobody will see coming. Anyone who has an interest in mythology of any kind (or even a brief interest) will find this amazing. In the gaming world it might be portrayed as a hack'n'slash RPG but in realiity It's a story about a father and son and their struggles to both develop their relationship between each other and developing themselves both on a physical and emotional level. It's a story about growing with each other with their own independent problems. Sure, their are a lot of cut-scenes, but the immersion is so seamless between general gameplay and story that you barely notice it. Especially with in-cutscene interactions and seamless evolution from fight to scene and vica versa.  You find yourself almost longing for the cutscenes to add even more depth to the story. If you want to play a game that feels like an interactive movie, this is 100% for you.2. Combat:The combat is incredible. As you progress through the world you gain additional stats, moves and prowess as any RPG game does but you really feel as though you're progressing. The move-sets, the weapons, the combat interactions between the characters, as you get more experienced with the combos and almost limitless combos you can tailor it to your play style. After 25 hours of gameplay I still have that moment of '♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I CAN DO THAT?!' when i've combined a certain number of moves. Outside of the amazingly detailed and intricate standard skill tree, you have complete control over your special moves. Want to be a guy who dashes all over combat? Done. Want to be that heavy hitter you just smashes everything to ♥♥♥♥? Done. Want to be that fast spell (attack)-weaver? Done. It's amazingly detailed once you get to grips with the stats of armour and weapons to truly customise your play style which leads me onto the customisation.3. Customisation:Whilst you follow a set skill set in terms of normal moves you can completely customise your stats. Want to be a super tank that has a load of health? Upgrade and attach things to your armour/weapons that give you health. Want to be an absolute glass cannon that specialises in standard melee moves? Go for it! Want to specialise in special moves and cooldown to spam those amazing cinematic moves? HELL YEAH! Want to focus on elemental damage? There's attachable upgrades and armour for that! The insane combination of stats and movesets in incrediby intricate and whilst cater to the casual gamer, can also be a super detailed trial and error style game for what you actually enjoy in your playstyle. In addition to the above, gaining a level of certain stats gives your moves extra benefits for example, if you have a certain level of vitality, after a defined combo you gain extra defense or elemental damage. On the flip-side, having full Strength might give you a giant fire explosion to your combo. The realms of customisation are unlimited. 4 World Map. The wold map is absolutely huge, but doesn't necessarily feel that way. There is so much content in this game but the story and side mission guide you in a way that feels natural. I personally didn't get full fast travel of the map until about 15 hours in. Albeit I did a load of side missions rather that the story but it still felt like the story. All travelling time is fulfilled by additional lore, character interactions and interesting stories that simply add to the immersion of being in this Norse mythological world that don't necessarily add to the main story but might reference somewhere you've been or something mentioned in a part of the story. 5. Quests:I kind of touched on this earlier but the main story quests are amazing. More importantly, the side quests don't feel like side-quests at all. A lot of them have their own dedicated areas that you wouldn't necessarily even see without going after them. All side quests give you advantage such as gaining more powerful gear or talismans (buffs you can attach to armour). Every quest still feels like the main story and you get additional lore from every single one of them. You could even class the side quests as their own lore story it's that in depth.Summary:I could go on but i'll save you the reading. This is honestly one of the best games i've ever played. The story is rich, the combat is incredible and fully customisable. You can completely follow or discover your own playstyle. The voice acting is better than most Hollywood films. The end game is fantastic and adds a lot to the game. 10/10 absolutely 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely phenomenal! It's a true masterpiece, in pretty much every way. The combat is extremely tight and very satisfying to learn and the pacing of the game works perfectly with this. The way they space out upgrades and unlocking new attacks keeps the gameplay feeling fresh and entertaining! Be warned, though, the combat is polished enough to make a lot of other games feel somewhat lackluster in comparison. The art design is also fantastic! This game is definitely eye candy and one where you will probably be using the photo mode frequently. Along with this, the characters are also enjoyable and they all have unique personalities that makes most of them very memorable. On top of all of that, the story is the chef's kiss. You are in for one wild ride of an adventure, with some interesting ways that Kratos and his son are mixed into the world of Norse Mythology. If you've never played this game before and somehow haven't spoiled it for yourself, I highly recommend going in blind, as the journey has many twists and turns that pay off all the better when you don't know they're coming.If you have played this before, then you are still in for a treat. This port is amazingly well done! It looks even better than it did on the PS4(/Pro) and the PS5 (if you have a capable machine) and can run at up to 120 frames, even when maxed out! This is by far the smoothest and most beautiful way to play this game. I personally haven't encountered any bugs so far and everything seems to work as you'd hope, which is great to hear, considering the state many games have been released in over the last year or two (including other PlayStation ports).Now, I will admit there are a few things that detract from this being a perfect 100/100 game, such as a somewhat limited variety of enemy types by later game (they mostly just change the color scheme of previous enemies) and not much variety in finishing moves (each specific enemy only really has one). However, those are pretty small complaints to have, considering how well everything else is done. And this game was also huge in scope and a fresh reboot, so I'm sure the sequel will most likely address these "issues."Bottom line, if you haven't played this game and you want to experience one of the best examples of games as an art form to date, buy this! Don't even hesitate! It's worth every penny and Santa Monica really went above and beyond with this! If you have already played this game? I'd still recommend it if you want a chance to experience it again in higher fidelity. This is a game I think every gamer should experience at some point! (Unless you're one of those people who hate story games for some reason)

_childDocuments_.review: So, picture this: you've got a jacked dude with more muscles than a butcher's dog, wielding a couple of swords, and stomping around in ancient Greece... no wait, Scandinavia... no, sorry, it's both. Welcome to "God of War" - a game where mythologies collide and daddy issues are as common as treasure chests.First off, we have our protagonist, Kratos, who's traded in his Blades of Chaos for a big ol' axe and a gruff demeanor. Gone are the days of indiscriminate rage against Greek gods; now he's a single dad trying to raise his son, Atreus. It's like someone decided, "Hey, let's take the angriest character in gaming and give him parental responsibilities. What could possibly go wrong?"But fear not, dear players, because Kratos isn't just slaying monsters; he's also slaying those dad jokes with the finesse of a master punsmith. You'll find yourself chuckling (or groaning) at his quips as you journey through the Nordic wilderness. "Atreus, why did the cyclops bring a flashlight? Because he wanted to see things from a different perspective!"Speaking of Atreus, he's like a combo of Robin to Kratos' Batman and that know-it-all kid from your high school physics class. He's there to shoot arrows, translate runes, and remind Kratos to moisturize because, let's face it, the dude's skin is drier than the Sahara.The gameplay? Oh, it's solid. You'll be hacking, slashing, and dodging your way through waves of enemies like a hot knife through Skadi's butter. And let's not forget the boss fights - they're bigger, badder, and more epic than trying to explain Norse mythology to your grandma.But what really sets "God of War" apart is its attention to detail. From the breathtaking landscapes to the intricate lore, every corner of this game feels meticulously crafted. And let's not forget about the hidden collectibles; finding them all is like trying to find the meaning of life in a bag of potato chips - frustrating yet oddly satisfying.In conclusion, "God of War" is a masterpiece of gaming. It's got action, humor, heart, and enough dad jokes to last you a lifetime. So grab your axe, polish your quiver, and get ready for an adventure that's truly godly... or should I say, dadly?

_childDocuments_.review: Having already played this incredible game on PS4, I went ahead and started reading some of the negative reviews on PC. From what I could gather, either people were attempting to run this game on garbage hardware and were surprised when something crashed or they had no idea this was a full reboot of the God of War franchise and they were expecting a direct sequel to the original series. I got a few laughs in so that was fun. There's really nothing I can say that would add to what others have already thoroughly exhausted in extensive reviews and praise. _childDocuments_.review: I may not have played all of the previous God of War games, but I have played enough to notice that this one feels... different. I was not expecting to be able to play it, since I have been PC only for a long time now. But I am glad that even Sony can put aside its grudges from time to time (or when money is involved :) )Kratos in this installment feels like a changed man. Older, wiser and no longer driven by anger and revenge. That does not mean however, that this game is short of its signature combat and violence. It just gives it a different light knowing the stakes and the motivations of the characters involved. Purpose, if I can put it that way.The world in this game is a masterfully crafted. The biggest problem of modern titles is gigantic but empty world. This one feels "smaller" but more meaningful. Every part of it serves purpose, so you don't get tired exploring it. The signature puzzles are present here as well. I do not mind them, actually I think they give the game-play some variety. I just had to include this in my review, because not everyone may like them, since they are present throughout the whole game.I am jet to finish some locations and post-game content but in terms of length, this game feels quite short. But that just depends if for you 30+ hours for main quest with detours is a lot or not.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always been a huge fan of Greek and Norse mythology, so this game was a dream come true for me. I thought it would end up crushing my rose tinted memories of this game, but it absolutely held up and more. I got addicted again as soon as I started launched it. The story is absolutely amazing and really sucks you in. It starts off as a simple quest, which soon quickly shrouded in mystery and sensation.Apart from the story, the combat in this game has absolutely everything you could hope for. The combo's you unlock later on in the game, make you feel like a combat expert; even though you'd probably get slaughtered in PvP. And the way the axe returns after you've called it back, just hits the spot.There are few games I recommend as much as this one.

_childDocuments_.review: NO WALK TOGGLE!!!I don't understand how a port can get all the way through play test without this feature being added.  It's ALREADY IN THE GAME but only accessed with a controller.  Please devs, stop doing this.  Sometimes you just wanna walk like a complete bada$$.Game itself otherwise is epic.  Screams of lot's of $$$ to create.  I have played none of the old games but I know they were more action and this is more but saying it's a "walking simulator" is just silly.  Combat is brutal.  I had to turn down the difficulty at one point I have to admit.  Plus it's just brutal animation wise, they didn't go all soft there.Another thing I appreciate where they didn't go all soy man bun is the story.  Whomever plays both Kratos and "Boy" do a fantastic job.  We live in a time where you don't spank your kids, there isn't this idea that you "fear" your parents now.  Now I'm not saying that's good or bad but it most definately WAS the case in the past and "boy" absolutely fears his father.  Even just the way he holds his gaze at the floor shows the respect he has for his father.We see a lot of the past being re-written and I'm glad they kept this aspect or in fact went with it.  Like I say we don't treat children this way anymore but people DID.  The tendancy these days of "touchy feely" is to not even show the past or portray it as it was because of "feelings" or some phony nonsense.  This father is HARSH on his son.  He is so harsh that you can feel how even he wants to break from it and show his compassion but knows he lives in a brutal world and must make his son hardened whether he wants to or not.  I love that.  I love how they didn't wimp out and just make it sappy modern day.  Good on them.Combat is fun and brutal and exploration and puzzles are good.  Overall not sure how you can't enjoy going through this game.  My only negative at this point is the map, it's horrible and useless.I9-9900k 16gb2080tiGot it capped to 90 everything maxed with some ReShade to bring back some colors/contrast.  Few dips but my cards fans barely turn on.  Well optimized.Yes, I'd love to see another God of War that plays like the older games but there IS a place for this as well.

_childDocuments_.review: -Game spends minimal time getting into things.-The final boss fight is probably the one of the best I've ever experienced.-The characters banter and dynamic is fun-Combat is simple, but with enough depth to let you mix things up.-Getting 100% Achievements can be done in a single play through. (Long as you can avoid the map bug)-"Give me a challenge" has the perfect amount of challenge. -If you find any of the main characters annoying, you likely find the game annoying too. -If you haven't played any of the previous God of War games. Some story bits might not make sense. -Lack of Enemy variety.- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -Even if you haven't played God of War, this is still a decent adventure game that doesn't waste time getting into things. I won't lie though, if your unfamiliar with Krato's (The main characters) backstory. I believe you do kind of miss out of the emotional part of the story. Don't let that dissuade you from not buying this tho.My only genuine complaint about the game though, is a lack of enemy variety. Aside from boss enemies, there are probably only 11 different enemies you are going to be fighting. This even includes the mini bosses.  This probably isn't a deal breaker though, means you got less things to practice for.I loved this game, and if you ever played or even watched any of the God of War series. I'd recommend picking this up.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game is amazing, play it. 9.5/10(SPOILERS AHEAD)So I slept on this game hard and didn't play it until only a few weeks ago. My reasons for this that I never owned a PS4 and I had heard that this game was essentially an interactive movie so I put it on the backburner until it felt like the right time to play it. I greatly regret not playing this game sooner because holy crap, this game is amazing and I'll explain why.Story:So, GoW 4 takes place in a whole new mythology, that being Norse. Kratos made a new family in Midgard after the events of GoW 3 and sought to have a quiet, peaceful life until his wife passed away. Her final wish was to have her ashes spread from the highest point in all of the nine realms. So, Kratos and his son embark on a journey to do just that, but face many trials along the way.This story is awesome. It shows us a side of Kratos that we really haven't seen before, that being his quiet and compassionate side. He comes to grip with the reality that the new life he had built is crumbling away and he's pretty much powerless. He also is figuring out how to be a better father to Atreus and you can see that he does love his son, but he's terrified to make mistakes so he comes off as cold and distant. This portrayal of Kratos is emotional and realistic, and I love it. This story will make you feel like a badass as well as making you feel like you grew alongside these characters.Gameplay/Combat:This combat is just fun as hell. It makes you feel like a complete badass as you get unbelievably strong and take down enemies effortlessly that were previously major trials. It's also reminiscent of FromSoft, but nowhere near as difficult so if you enjoy that kind of gameplay, there's something here for you.Completionist Difficulty:This is a pretty easy game to get all of the achievements in as it only took me 60 hours to do so. If you take your time and explore, you'll 100% this game in no time.Nitpicks:There's too many ravens to shoot down and Niflheim is annoying to be in.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing to see God of War find a new home on PC, where it can be enjoyed for years to come. The world is rewarding to explore, the is combat brutal with deep mechanics. The characters, however, are the crowning achievement - impressively scripted and acted. These first party Sony games are a reminder of how good big budget games can be when they aren't built and balanced around ongoing monetisation. Just a team of top industry talent making the best game they can.Everyone should play this.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is mediocre at best and at times very frustrating. Whoever decided to have a melee action game control like a third person shooter should get fired from game development. The camera is positioned over your right shoulder, so it's incredibly easy to get sucker-punched by enemies you can't see from your left, which can get extremely annoying during Muspelheim trials.There isn't much variety in enemy types (hope you like fighting the same troll boss literally 10 times) and there are numerous sections where you're just sitting on an elevator or a boat and wailing on waves after waves of same respawning enemies.Story and exploration are good enough to make up for these shortcomings, though. One of the rare games where I'll slog through the fights just to see what happens next.

_childDocuments_.review: (Played on give me god of war)This game has been one of the most disappointing game I have played in a while. I am convinced that those who say this game's combat is well designed either play this game on give me a story, or give me a balanced experience. The higher you go up in the difficulties the more exaggerated the flaws become. First the camera is absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, it is far too close to be able to see around you. A lot of people have compared this game to the last of us, to the annoyance of the game director Cory Balrog, though this absolutely is a fair comparison. For some reason they have chosen a camera angle and fov suited for third person shooters and decided it a better choice than that of the previous games. The result is finding yourself dying to enemies outside of the view of the camera, instead you need to rely on the red indicators around your body. Though these are a bandaid fix at best since the indicator turning red does not accurately convey when an enemy is about to attack, rather that an enemy will eventually attack in the next few seconds, making it rather difficult to time an evade or dodge roll. This is made even worse in the troll boss fights, the game directors were so insecure with merit of the bossfights themselves, that they decided to add a bunch of ranged enemies around the arena, making combat tedious in the higher difficulties. Combat no longer feels rewarding (result of the cheap deaths mentioned above), no longer do I feel inclined to learn the enemy attack patterns, rather just spam runic attacks and try my hardest to cheese the fights. The straw that broke the camel's back was the geirdriful boss fight. As a result of the  poorly choreographed enemy attacks, it becomes almost impossible to differentiate between her unblockable strike, or her blockable cyclone attack. It would not be as big of a deal if you could just time a dodge role for both attacks, however for the cyclone attack acts like a homing missile one you dodge roll the first hit, making it impossible to my knowledge to dodge. All in all there was alot of potential here, however due to the poorly designed combat, the experience fails at being game play focused and rather jerks itself off with its story.

_childDocuments_.review: The story and character development in this game are phenomenal, the character's are brilliantly acted and mo-capped, amazing set pieces and landscapes, in-depth combat system with a wide variety of things to unlock and utilise to fit your play style, and a gorgeous soundtrack to go with it all.The combat itself though, isn't for me personally. In the context of the story, you're playing as Kratos, who is supposed to be akin to an unstoppable force of nature given what we've seen of him in previous games. I don't personally think the gameplay complements that, as the combat seems to be very "wait your turn, you're not allowed to attack this enemy yet, or interrupt their combat animations (doesn't apply to all enemies ofc)" which ruins the immersion. I think the hack-and-slash gameplay of the previous titles was better suited in this regard.Also not a fan of the artificial difficulty that comes in the form of "levels", as in, certain enemies are just reskins of existing ones you've already fought. But because they've got a higher level attached to them, they suddenly deal a lot more damage and take a lot less from you. This is less desirable than introducing new enemies altogether who are more difficult than the ones you've already faced.Finding better gear also often requires you to go off the beaten path or backtrack to areas you've already been, which can also just shatter the pacing of the story. You can of course, not do that - you have the option to after all. But it comes at the cost of suffering through the increasing difficulty in combat as the game progresses. The Valkeryie bosses are fun and challenging, though also suffer from the "wait your turn" issue I mentioned before. It's fine, I understand that this is how the game is designed - it's simply not for me. Though for what it's worth, I did have some fun with it regardless.Atreus is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying character though. I appreciate what his inclusion in the story does for Kratos's character development, but the character itself? Good grief.

_childDocuments_.review: Tomb Raid (the Reboot) was done 2013. Five years before God of War. It features much better level design, sound design, graphics, fights, stealth, crafting and of course a much better story.The graphics are not bad, but please compare it to the Yamatai temples of Tomb Raider FIVE years before. Compare the puzzle to Tomb Raider. Compare the variety of fighting to Tomb Raider.I can't believe I fell for the hype that God of War is a 9/10 or 10/10 game. Basically it's the poor mans version of Tomb Raider. It's extremely boring, mainly because of repetition and the tunnel design of the levels. Almost every time you know you enter an "arena". There are no different ways to achieve a goal or enter an area: it's always the same boring easy puzzles: throw your axe, climb a rope, open a chest. Fight. Redo. Redo. Solve an easy puzzle. Fight. Start over.The main character is a psychopath. No emotional connection is possible (maybe later). The boy is a stupid fearful psychopath, that only forget's his fear when he kills enemies. Also he loves to storm ahead in the arms of enemies, because he cant remember the last ambush just seconds ago. Sure. Basically the boy only exists to get your character in situations a player would avoid or solve with caution.If THIS is really one of the best games of PS4/5 I honestly am very sad how much depth, story, emotions and of course great level design console player miss in their live.Maybe there will be alter grand emotions and storytelling. But why should a player have to wait for that? Compare the character development to the young Lara Croft in Tomb Raider 2013. You understood her fear, her exhaustion, her anger. In God of War you just understand that the main character is a psychopath, that ravages kills and scorns his son. Yes, yes, it's the "God of War". Well, this is the weakest God of War ever. Super vulnerable in fights (already goes down after two hits by this super draugrs only 3 hours in the game), super annoying when talking to his son, super stupid in his decisions.Why the hell can he smash huge rocks, carry complete trees and lift stone columns, but in his path he is constantly blocked by small rubble, weak crates and some thin trees? Only reason of course: to create tunnel levels.I don't even start to compare this game to the level design of the Witcher games. Tomb Raider is very similar to this game, but it's already so far head of God of War - a five year older game with so much better exploring, climbing and fighting. I would say God of War is a solid 6/10. Ambitious, but badly restricted by the level design and boring because of endless repetition.

The interaction of using Atreus to use his bow to help you fight is a great way to give the player control rather than having a semi-useless and semi-functioning AI follow you like so many games choose to use. The graphics are phenomenal with plenty of varied environments. The game rewards you constantly for exploring.  Having Kratos and Atreus interact in the boat while you are in the boat to fill the time and ceasing the conversation when you get to land only to return to the same conversation  when you get back into the boat is a stroke of genius. _childDocuments_.review: This will be quite a lot of text to read so I will put a TL:DR at the bottom, and this review will contain minor spoilers. So skip to the TL:DR if you don't want any spoilers.As someone who doesn't own a ps4, hearing this game was coming to PC at first piqued my interrest. I heard it was good, friends recommended it to me. So why not give it a try? I played for a few minutes, as minutes turned to hours, and hours to days. After 40 hours of playing within a weeks time, I finished the game on "give me a balanced experience" better known as normal difficulty mode.I went in for the story, with some major points being spoiled thanks to media that randomly popped god of war in my face. But despite about 10% of the over all story and almost every major plot twist spoiled, I still LOVED the story. It is emotional, impactfull and al the more meaningfull if you played at least god of war 3. And understand that Kratos does not see himself as a human or god. Instead accepting he is practically a monster.But being a monster is part of what makes the game fun. Now I am not one for glorifying gore too much. It doesn't shake me, but I don't play a game just because it is gory. But this game's combat can be either fast, medium or slow pased depending on how you play, be it aggressive, defensive or somewhere in between. Having started with my playthrough of a harder difficulty I can tell you that it makes a lot of difference how you decide to fight. But the brutality of the game is also represented in the combat. Almost like you can feel the swing of the axe, the weight of every split second decision to attack, block or dodge.And that weight of combat comes into considderation when you are exploring the game. There isn't just a story to play through. There is a world to explore as well. I hesitate to call it a fully open world since you can't return to every single place, but you can revisit most of them. Or even decide to skip out on certain places. If you want better gear, and to be prepared for what challanges come next. The weight of choosing to push onward, or to take it slow and explore is a heavy one. On normal mode I got to about half way in the story, just to drop it and do every sidequest I could. All of niflheim, all of mushelheim, killing every valkyrie optional boss and doing all dwarven requests I could, as well as a few of the other side quests throughout the world.Playing on normal difficulty I found that exploring made the game very easy. after having finished all of those tasks, the story was a breeze to finish. But in the harder difficulties I can already tell exploring and preparing aren't going to be that much of an option anymore. And more of a requirement.But luckily most of the exploring comes with it's own little stories. Pieces of norse mythology told by Mimir, the severed head on you hip. Or by dialouge exchanges between Kratos and his son. Some sad, some slightly funny. Especially the relation between Mimir and Atrues, kratos' son, are funny. And each one got a little smile or small laughter out of me the first time I heard them.And this mixture of story, combat and exploration make for a wonderfull expierence, where not a second in 40 hours felt boring. And the best part to me? There are 2 more difficulty modes and a new game plus to challange yourself even further. As in normal mode the toughest thing to do must have been the valkyries. And I found myself wishing there were more challanges like that. And I have a good feeling the tougher difficulties will give me that challange I crave. Having found my way comfortably in how combat works, and working on developing my way to play.now for the TL:DR:Over all this game has an amazing story, and gameplay fluidity. The good textures and touching moments help immerse you in a story, where you almost wish you could stand in the world beside the characters. The challanges the game provides along with the amazing combat and exploration feel like just the perfect combination of excitement and relaxation within the game.All round I would highly, HIGHLY advise this game to anyone who loves action and or adventure games.Though if you are going in for the story I recommend not going too crazy on the difficulty for your first playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start with the positive. I swear that I do truly think this game is worth playing, despite my criticisms, and I think the criticisms are worth going into detail over because this game clearly had a lot of people put a lot of care into it, but I think where it fails, it fails in very avoidable ways.I love the writing - pivoting Kratos into a meditation on toxic masculinity and the challenges of trying to be a good father with a troubled past in an adverse environment is all really good. Framing it around the Vanir-Aesir conflict is really brilliant, and all in all I think this is a fascinating take on norse mythology. The visuals are gorgeous and the banter genuinely has its funny moments. I'm really truly invested in Kratos (despite not having played the previous games), Atreus, and their relationship, and the people they meet and that says something. I liked this so much that it powered me through the game despite everything I'm about to say.Sadly, I think the combat is a chore. The game that I want to compare it to most is Lords of the Fallen, which should be a red flag. Just clunky, awkward, sometimes frustrating, rarely rewarding. I have plenty of enemies I dread fighting (Revenants, nightmares, those burrowing things) and none that I'm excited to fight. It's not terribly difficult - you can mash your way through and you can punch above your weight by cheesing with Atreus, but playing on harder difficulty sounds like pointless frustration.52 hours in and I still hate the over-the-shoulder view - it was maddening when I got killed by an unblockable attack that I couldn't see coming because Kratos' back was taking up 1/5 of the screen and a bit of shrubbery behind him was taking up the rest. The weird tank-like way Kratos walks is also annoying both in combat and out with the amount of traversal you do.I never really found much utility in the sorta combo moves - they never really seemed rewarding enough to justify the commitment and the investment of timing in the flow of fighting. The runic attacks are cool but it's hard to tell which is best for your playstyle, then you invest XP in one of them and then you're kinda locked in and many of them are a bit situational so most of them go completely unused. The loot also feels really superfluous - you get tons of it and it's hard to tell how big a momentary stat boost under certain circumstances is actually benefiting you, whether it's worth upgrading something or if you should save your crafting materials. None of these things really detracted from my experience, but they feel like systems with unrealized potential. I haven't played Ragnarok yet and I'm curious if they refined them at all.If at any point the combat seems to shine it's in the Valkyrie fights, where the best way to play is to learn their moveset, carefully read them, and react appropriately. If you like this kind of gameplay, though, just play Sekiro. It is a much better-executed version of the concept.Addendum: Who on earth likes enemies whose primary mechanic is making you wait? Oops, can't attack that enemy because they're underground. Better wait until they attack. Oops, that revenant is invulnerable because my son missed with his last arrow. Better wait for that to recharge. Oops, that dark elf teleported to the other end of the room despite me using the time-slowing ability, just after I committed to 10 seconds of a runic attack I can't abort. Sure glad I'm in niflheim, slowly being poisoned to death.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot bring myself to play this game any further than the moment I discovered the true identity of the Witch in the Wood. By that time, I hadn't played since January 28th because of performance issues, and AMD AND Santa Monica have yet to send us fixes. I replayed it, discovered the identity of the Witch... restarted because I had forgotten how to play to a degree... and I lost all interest.This is overall a great product for a vast majority of consumers. I see that a lot of love has been put into crafting this game and the amount of detail is phenomenal. I cannot deny the effort as a work of art. As a game though... This is clearly not for me and there are many things that prevent it from being enjoyable. While the combat is serviceable thanks to good animation quality and sound, the entire system that is the RPG (looting, talent tree, XP, enemy levels, etc) brings down what could have been a great combat loop. It feels mashy, arbitrary due to its parry, slow movement, and the overall slog that is each swing of the axe. There's no true combo variety that is shown through animations. I don't enjoy the combat as a result. And no, finishing the game and playing through harder difficulties through NG+ isn't gonna make it good. In fact, it only makes the beginning worse due to awful balancing because they clearly designed the game around the Normal and Easy difficulties. I'm forced to play on Normal because the Hard Difficulty stopped me due to one combat room running poorly (performance issues, the game going sub 40 frames per second), having tight corridors and featuring some the worst enemies in succession. It's awful!The linear sections are there for bland exploration, opening chests that reward more stuff for its RPG system that I already despise. There's no true reward for making it through an intense combat sequence. There's no incentive to improve or "get good" at it which isn't a problem in games like other action games, specifically the spectacle fighter. That's excluding the AWFUL camera which can be fixed through patching, but the arrogance of Santa Monica is on full display due to the inability to change the Field of View. It only serves to hide Atreus' teleportation because he does act strange. He's an annoyance in combat due to his constant screaming which isn't a surprise. Plus him having an American English while many of the characters are from the Norse mythos... Yeah, I don't get it.The amount of invisible walls, the over-emphasis on pointless, unskippable cutscenes, false gameplay due to walking and talking, and the barebone gameplay that is the combat for a product of this genre just make me question why this is praised. I get it: it looks good, sounds good, has a personal story about a father and son... the father who already had a family and had personality.I respect the game for what it is, but it's clearly not for me and the minority of players who dislike this game shouldn't be afraid to speak up. _childDocuments_.review: You'll laugh, you'll cry, but most importantly, you'll get super ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pissed off when fighting the damn valkyries.I can't recommend this game enough.Update:So, I made a silly review, seen above, about this game. I have played and beaten this game on PS4 and on PC, but, not long after I beat it and posted my review last time, I got the urge to play it again, since it has a New Game+ feature, figured I'd give that a shot.Now, I always enjoyed this game. I've been a fan of God of War since I first played the OG back in the early 2000's. But, after playing this game again, and doing EVERYTHING, I can honestly say, not only do I recommend this game, but this is easily one of the greatest games of all time.I'm not going to go into extreme detail about why I love this game, it's been out for 4 years, and closing in on its 1 year anniversary on PC as of this writing. If you've heard about this game, you've heard the good stuff. I can promise you, it's all true. This game is a masterpiece from start to finish, it is well worth your time.I have so little to critique about this game. Honestly the only real issue I have with it, that in my mind is an actual issue and not a minor nitpick, is the optimization. Now, you've probably heard by now that the game is very well optimized, and for the most part that is true. Playing on my Steam Deck I was able to get a locked 40 fps and a solid 45-50 fps in most spots of the game. On my desktop (Ryzen 5 5500, RX 6600, 16 GB RAM) I was able to cap frames at 80 and had it run from 70-80 for the majority of the game. BUT, what I'm getting at is there are a few places with some rough frame rate, mostly the Lake of the Nine. At that place I saw dips down to 20-30 fps on my Steam Deck, and down to 30-40 fps on my desktop. Other than that though, the game ran fantastically, there are just a few places where even lowing all the settings don't help the frame rate at all. The game is also Direct X 11 and has no exclusive fullscreen option, which is kinda weird, but what can you do eh?Other than that complaint, the game is flawless. I can recommend this to fans of God of War and newcomers to the series alike. I can recommend this to those who didn't like the Greek Saga of games but are looking for something different. I can recommend this to people who don't even play action/adventure games, because the story and character development is just that good.I spent 30 hours beating this on PS4, I spent 35 hours beating this on PC, then I spent another 50+ hours doing a 100% run on New Game+. This game was worth every second of it, I can not recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: 66 hours if for reference. I have more than 100 hours invested into this game back when I still had my PS4 (RIP my boxy friend). I bought this game again on Steam in 2022, and not until recently did I pick it up. My advice for anyone wanting to play this game to the best of your experience: headphones, Dualsense Controller and 8-10 hours of non-interrupting gameplay. I grew up during the era of PS2 and PS3, with the original GoW trilogy and its prequels (Chains of Olympics, etc). The Kratos back then was just pure rage, and the writings were very basic, very childish. Imagine an edgy 20yo guy directing the 3 games back then. This new GoW, however, is much more refined and mature. The new Kratos is no longer the guy he was back then. For me, having growing up for past 15 years, experiencing all kinds of people and downfall in life (heartbreak, health issue, broke to the point almost homeless), seeing how Kratos grew up resonated with me a lot. This game may not be for everyone, especially those who are looking for a mayhem of hack&slash to smash their keyboards/controllers. There are distinct combos and trick shots to be done in this game, and a much more considerable amount of work to be put in for higher difficulties. GMGOW on NG+ was really giving me a run for my money, but heck yeah was it worth it when I was finally able to put down Sigrun the Valkyrie Queen. Solid 9/10, bar none. From the casting, writings and the cinematic. Where is the last point you might ask? They took away the hunting leveling features in the E3 trailer back in 2016, which upset me a lot. But yeah, had it been there, 10 out of 10 definitely!

_childDocuments_.review: In the 2018 God Of War, you play as Kratos, the former slayer of the Greek pantheon, who now resides amongst the realms of Norse mythology. Despite his past as a rage fueled beast whose vengeance knew no bounds, he has tempered his anger, and now only seeks to steer his son Atreus away from the path he walked long ago. Together they journey to fulfill his wife's dying wish; to have her ashes spread on the highest peak in all the realms. A seemingly simple quest that grows more complicated the closer to the goal they get...This is an excellent game. I had actually beaten it a few years ago, but recently before the PC version was released I got a month of PS Now and played through the three main games(little bonus review for that at the bottom if you're interested), and honestly it made this game's story even more impactful. Without spoiling the other games, I love how they've handled Kratos's growth as character, without having him revert to his same old "so angry he literally can't die" self. Even still, my first time through when I had zero context for the series up until this point, I still loved the story.The game play is great too. It changed from the overly aggressive style of the past games, where getting astronomically high combos was the goal, to a more strategic, almost dueling like approach. Again, this reflects a change in Kratos's character, which makes me love it even more. I also absolutely love how they've replaced your bow in GoW III with commanding Atreus to fire his bow in this game. Atreus in general adds a fun layer to the strategy in each fight. He stuns, he grapples, if he has the right equipment he can toss you health stones. Him and Kratos can even do fun combo attacks together that are always a joy to watch.Overall, even if you haven't played a God of War game in your life(which I recommend playing if you get the time), this is a hard recommend from me!BONUS REVIEW: Feels kinda weird talking about PS Now on Steam but just because I had so much fun with GoW I, II, and III, I thought I'd shout out the service I played them on. Wouldn't really recommend it for your more modern games like Bloodborne, Last of Us and, well, this, but for going through their older catalog it's actually pretty nice. Big recommend if you got the internet for it. Oh, and if you thought I meant review for the games, they're all somewhere between good to great. Some of the puzzles gave me an anuerysm, the QTE's in the first game physically hurt to preform, and there are some bosses that almost cost me a $60 PS4 controller, but the overall majority of my experience with these games were positive.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the God of War series, I was incredibly excited to dive into the installment of the new generation  God of War. Unfortunately, despite its high production values and stunning visuals, this new God of War left me feeling thoroughly disappointed.Let's start with the positives: the graphics are top-notch for its time, and the world design is nothing short of breathtaking. The voice acting and storytelling are also commendable in a way, adding depth to the characters and the lore. However, these aspects alone can't save the game from its fundamental flaws.The biggest letdown for me is the combat design. As someone who cherished the fast-paced, combo-heavy battles of the PS2 and PS3 God of War games, the new combat system feels like a significant downgrade. The once fluid and exhilarating hack-and-slash mechanics have been replaced with a slower, more methodical approach that just doesn't capture the same excitement. The lack of variety in enemy types and repetitive encounters only exacerbate the issue, making the combat feel stale and monotonous.Moreover, the game's attempt to incorporate RPG elements feels half-baked and unnecessary. The gear and upgrade systems are overly complicated and detract from the core action experience that God of War should be about. I miss the days when I could focus on mastering Kratos' moves and combos without worrying about stats and equipment.In conclusion, while the new God of War is undeniably a high-quality production, it ultimately falls short of its predecessors in terms of gameplay. If you're a fan of the classic God of War games and are hoping for a similar experience, you might find this new entry to be a mediocre and disappointing departure from what made the series great.

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought I'd see the day when Kratos, the angriest dad in gaming, would make his way onto my PC, but here we are, and let me tell you, it's an absolute godsend!First off, let's talk about the graphics. I didn't think my computer could handle this level of visual awesomeness. Kratos' muscles have more definition than a Webster's dictionary, and the environments are so stunning that I've started using them as my desktop wallpaper. Who needs nature photos when you can have Kratos battling mythical creatures in 4K?Now, onto the gameplay. Kratos is like a demigod on roller skates - smooth, powerful, and surprisingly agile. The combat feels like a perfectly choreographed dance of destruction. I've never felt so accomplished in button-mashing my way through enemies. It's like playing a violent ballet, and I am the maestro of mayhem.The story is, as expected, epic. Kratos is on a journey with his son, Atreus, and their dynamic is a mix of heartwarming and hilarious. Kratos' attempts at fatherly advice are both endearing and laugh-out-loud funny. Who knew the God of War had a softer side and a knack for dad jokes?And can we talk about the axe? Mjölnir who? Kratos' Leviathan Axe is the real star of the show. It's like a boomerang of destruction. I've spent more time throwing that thing around and calling it back than I have in actual combat. It's oddly therapeutic.The puzzles in the game are brain teasers, but with Kratos' brute strength, they're more like brain smushers. It's a nice change of pace from the relentless combat, and I appreciate the moments of cerebral challenge between all the skull-crushing.In conclusion, God of War on PC is a triumph. Kratos has made the leap from console to computer, and he's brought with him a game that's as satisfying as smashing pots for health orbs. If you haven't experienced the joy of being an angry god on your PC, you're missing out. Five stars, two thumbs up, and a virtual high-five to the developers for making Kratos feel right at home on my desktop. Now, excuse me while I go back to wrecking havoc in Midgard!

_childDocuments_.review: Title: The Goodness of God of War: A Tale of Redemption, Adventure, and MythologyIntroduction"God of War," a video game series developed by Santa Monica Studio and published by Sony Interactive Entertainment, has garnered widespread acclaim for its captivating storytelling, innovative gameplay mechanics, and stunning visuals. While it initially gained fame for its brutal combat and intense action sequences, the series has evolved over the years to offer so much more. This essay explores the many virtues and positive aspects of the "God of War" series, focusing on its character development, narrative depth, and exploration of mythology.Complex Character DevelopmentOne of the most remarkable aspects of the "God of War" series is the evolution of its central character, Kratos. In the earlier games, Kratos is portrayed as a ruthless and vengeful Spartan warrior who seeks retribution against the Greek gods. However, as the series progresses, players witness a profound transformation in his character. He becomes a father figure to his son, Atreus, and grapples with the burden of his violent past.Kratos' journey from a vengeful antihero to a more compassionate and introspective character is a testament to the depth of storytelling in the series. This character development is a reflection of the complexity of the human experience, and it invites players to explore themes of redemption, forgiveness, and the capacity for change.Engaging Narrative DepthThe "God of War" series is celebrated for its intricate and emotionally resonant narratives. The games draw inspiration from Greek mythology and Norse mythology, weaving these rich mythological tapestries into their stories. The blending of mythological elements with a deeply personal and human tale creates a narrative tapestry that is both captivating and thought-provoking.Throughout the series, players encounter a diverse array of characters and creatures from different mythologies, each with their own unique stories and motivations. These interactions provide players with a fascinating glimpse into the cultural and mythological diversity of the world.Moreover, the series consistently explores themes such as the consequences of one's actions, the impact of fatherhood, and the complexities of family dynamics. These themes resonate with players on a profound level, making "God of War" more than just a hack-and-slash action game; it is an immersive narrative experience.Stunning Visuals and Immersive World-BuildingThe "God of War" series sets a high bar for visual excellence in video games. With each new installment, the graphics, animations, and world-building become increasingly spectacular. The shift from Greek to Norse mythology in the latest entry, "God of War" (2018), introduced players to the breathtaking realms of Midgard, Alfheim, and others. These realms are meticulously designed, immersing players in a visually stunning and atmospheric world.The attention to detail in character design, landscapes, and mythological creatures showcases the commitment of the developers to delivering a visually immersive experience. Exploring these meticulously crafted environments and encountering various mythical beings is a source of delight for players.ConclusionIn conclusion, the "God of War" series is not just about brutal combat and epic battles; it is a testament to the power of storytelling in video games. The series has evolved to become a masterclass in character development, narrative depth, and the exploration of mythology. It challenges players to consider profound themes while immersing them in a visually stunning and richly detailed world. "God of War" is not only a shining example of what video games can achieve artistically and narratively, but it also stands as a testament to the goodness that can emerge from even the darkest of narratives.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have played in the last few years if not ever. I have almost no critiques and maybe it's because I have literally just finished the game as I'm writing this but this game is almost flawless.I'll get the negatives out of the way and trust me they are very nit picky. Firstly, when interacting with things the game sometimes wants you stood a certain distance and a certain angle from something before you are given the prompt to interact but this is fairly few and far between moments just slightly frustrating when they do happen. By the time you begin to near the end of the game the map becomes far too clustered to understand what is going on with so many icons and its already poor design from an efficiency stand point, putting visuals ahead of practicality, it is impossible to read. This isn't a huge issue though as you barely use the map with your compass being your main source of direction it's just the cluttered icons can look quite ugly. There are quite a few QTEs that some people may find annoying, personally I am not bothered but I know some people really dislike them but I'm sure there is an option to turn them off. My final small issue is I think the game has a small case of Rockstar syndrome, feeling that almost every mission has to be a brawl, now it really isn't that big of a deal here like it is in Red Dead Redemption 2 but there were a few points during the game where I juts felt like I had been running through hoards of enemies for no real reason. Now that I've allowed myself to complain let's get get to the good stuff. The story is an absolute masterpiece, I will do my best to stay spoiler free. The main focus and objective throughout stays exactly the same and the game will tease you with it letting you get very close then ripping it away again and again. This is what makes the story interesting, these set backs, and the people you meet that may aid you or set you back some doing both even those the very closest to you. Kratos' backstory is very important to many of the driving points of this plot. I do not think it necessary to have had played the previous trilogy but at least update yourself by watching a youtube video as I think many moments would lose their impact if you don't entirely understand what they are referencing. As I'm on the topic of the last games, if you have played them and are worried this game just won't be the same don't worry there are still many crazy outlandish fights to be had. The new camera angle is an improvement for the type of game this is being a bit more slower paced I think it is important you feel more connected with Kratos. They also have a thing where the whole game is done in one shot which is true but it doesn't make a huge difference and is more of a marketing gimmick than anything. The best relationship throughout the game is the one you play. The one between Kratos and Atreus develops and changes so much as both characters grow closer. Certain aspects of the plot do feel a bit weird as the pacing can rapidly speed up but that may have been me not doing as many side quests towards the end of the game.Speaking of side quests they are really impressive. Many of them do repeat a similar structure such as: go to cave, kill big thing, get reward or get thing for spirit, get betrayed or rewarded but there are some real gems in here and some storylines that carry over more than just one side quest and integrate with others. Sometimes they can really slow down the pacing of the game and that's why I stood back from them towards the end just so I could keep that endgame tension without interruptions but obviously you play how you want and I don't think my "I must get every collectable" mentality helped with that as I tend to check every corner of each level.Onto the levels and map design, I think it is very smart and intriguing path they took for a triple a game. It is a sudo metroidvania style which isn't very common in 3D games let alone £50 titles. I think it works brilliantly in this games favour though as you will find areas with things you cannot access then 5 hours later you come back and a whole new section is available. I think the world serpent also plays into this well as he is pretty much a part of the map that moves opening up more areas with more loot. Oh yeah loot there is a lot of loot. From random chests to puzzles to treasure chests the game has a million ways to through "money" and crafting materials at you. The puzzles are never anything too complex unless you are missing parts of your brain like me and have to look it up on youtube. I know the term "crafting" can scare people away but trust me it's nothing intense, you just collect materials that you give to someone else to make you armour and weapon upgrades. The weapons and amour you do craft are really fun and can have some really big visual differences along with stats but a true chad doesn't care about stats just style.I will make a small mention of the visuals but you already know they're good just have a look on my steam profile of some of the shots I took during the game and you can see that it is just magnificent in almost every moment.There you go that's my review on God of War it is 100% worth any amount of money it costs you as it fully lives up to its reputation. As I said at the start one of the best games in the last few years and another brilliant sony exclusive, I hope we get to see more of these on PC soon. Overall: 93/100

I pre-ordered this as I played some of this game on PS4 but never got around to finishing it, so when I saw it was available on PC I jumped at the chance to finish it on my gaming setup. I have an ultrawide 3440x1440 144hz curved monitor, RTX 2080 super and an AMD ryzen 7 3700x, I have it installed on my SSD and was able to play the game on ultra settings with no issues whatsoever. The graphics were amazing, the environments were beautiful and altogether the experience was incredibly immersive. The story was amazing, and really made me feel strongly for what was going on not only to the main characters but the side characters and the backstory/lore building throughout the game.  The puzzles felt natural, and really made you stop and think, not only about timing but also about your surroundings and how to go about taking them on. The enemies scaled well with progression in the game and as the challenges increased you really get to see if you are ready for that area or not or if you need to progress further elsewhere before continuing. The exploration doesn't feel like it isn't part of the game experience like it does in some other games, if anything this game greatly rewards exploration and deep thinking on how to get somewhere or get something and makes it feel good when you can finally get that item later on after you receive a power or weapon needed. Sometimes it felt like it was odd I couldn't get somewhere then the story progressed and it all made sense as to what was keeping me from getting there. and the feeling of getting to that one spot you have had your eye on forever felt amazing. The lore and tales told as the game goes on and you meet certain characters and discover certain things make the game even better, especially if you're into Norse anything and acting/feeling like you're taking part in some of the tales makes it feel even better. The lessons and quotes that are said during the game just make you feel good as well. While exploring and going off the beaten path or taking a breather before continuing the story is still fun and rewarded with items, experience, and resources. The game doesn't punish you for following just the main story line, but when certain things happen in game and new areas open up because of them or you can get to some items because of it, I feel like it added to the game to go and jump into those areas. but your mileage may vary of course. currently I am finishing up 100%ing the game so I may be using guides now that the main story is finished for me. But the game walks you in a way that you don't need them (guides), and it won't mess up the story or gameplay if you miss them, but I feel like this game deserves it so wish me luck. All in all I say this game is a 10/10 in my book and I don't write a review for just any game I play, but this one felt like it was so good it deserved one. especially for a PC port, that doesn't feel like a PC port. I Highly  recommend this game either on sale or full price as its worth it

name: Clid The Snail
detailed_description: In a world where only the distant memory of human existence still lingers, you play as Clid, a troublemaking, eccentric snail who has just been exiled from his home citadel. Joined by a faithful and talkative firefly, Belu, you will meet a peculiar gang of outcasts and find a place to call home. Among this new group of friends, you will discover a newfound purpose: Exterminating the mysterious slug plague that is ravaging the land. Clid The Snail is a unique top-down shooter where character-driven narrative and mindful combat take the center stage. Through Clid, you’ll experience a story about exile, friendship, and betrayal, and live the adventures of a troublesome, unruly snail that doesn’t belong. Explore a treacherous world full of threats and challenges, where strategic positioning, precise gunplay, and enemy behavior are paramount to your survival. Discover the truth behind the slug plague corrupting the world and save the land from ultimate ruin. Get creative with your guns, grenades, and unique snail shells to outsmart your enemies. Use the environment to your advantage and learn to position yourself to emerge victorious. A shy hedgehog, a shaman turtle, a mute bat, a ninja frog, and a one-eyed chameleon: these are the members of Alastor. Return home after each quest to rest, stock up on resources, upgrade equipment, and develop friendships. Get to know these unique characters and unravel their past to find out the key to the story. Swamps, desserts, mountains, islands... Each quest will take you to a new location waiting to be discovered. Help the local residents fight off the slug threat and become their hero! And don’t forget to keep a keen eye: Explore every level in search for extra goodies. Powerful threats await you at the end of each mission. You will need to study their behavior, pay attention to detail, and choose your weapons wisely to survive these dangerous encounters. Shooting isn´t always the answer. Use your weapons and intellect to solve puzzles, find secrets, and progress through the story. Sometimes, the answers are hidden in plain sight…

_childDocuments_.review: I think I like the idea of Clid the Snail more than the actual game. The idea of playing a Gears of War style game based on an anthropomorphic snail is fascinating, but in execution the game feels more like a watered down version of an already watered down tactical shooter like Warhammer: Inquisitor Martyr. Clid could've used an inventory or something else to vary the game play. As it stands, it feels more like a mix between one of the aforementioned shooters and an adventure platformer. There are puzzles, but they don't take much effort to solve. The graphics look wonderful at first glance, but after a while the overall presentation feels muddled and watered down. That isn't to say effort didn't go into this game, but the game got old for me within about an hour of playing. You just use the same sniper weapon with unlimited ammo to kill wave after wave of brainless enemy. There's no strategy, and as long as you lead your targets by keeping a distance and using the aim assist it's basically impossible to die. Of course you get your grenades, and then your little collectibles in the form of pieces of life bar upgrades. The only reason to kill enemies not directly in your way is to get money which you barely need because the most useful weapon has unlimited ammo. This game needed a lot more work put into it to differentiate it from the countless other games that adopt this game play style. I admit I was lured in by the idea of playing as a snail with a gun, but the game play isn't as quirky or unique as that initial concept would lead you to believe. In fact, playing as a snail has no impact on any of the gameplay. You would think you could at least hide in your shell for defense or something, but the fact that you're playing as a snail has no bearing on anything in terms of the game design.Also, something I really don't like is that you get half of the remaining weapons just before the game ends. This needed an extra three or four levels to pad it out- honestly it feels unfinished. The final boss fight is solid though. I think the developers wanted to create something story-driven but forgot that gameplay must always come before story, particularly when advertisements for your game showcase the gameplay as an incentive to buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the game I must change my review from recommended to not recommended. I really hoped the game would become more difficult as it went on, but at no point is the game ever challenging, even when encountering new enemies, they never deviate enough to become challenging. The bosses also arent difficult.What I enjoyed about the game -THE WORLD. I think this was definitely the highlight of the game, exploring a world without humans and populated by highly developed creatures was pretty interesting. I think if the game had placed more focus on the world, and less on the combat (which was already beyond easy) it could have truly been special. What I didnt enjoy about the game -Targeted aim seemed to be broken, and would often cause me to aim in the complete wrong direction, or shots would go inches away from the crosshair.The plot was rushed, you only spend a limited amount of time in each zone or talking to each being, so you never get to have a lasting impression from anything.The combat was very easy and repetitive.currency was easy to come by, and nothing in the shops were expensive, so seems pointless.I think for the game to improve, fast travel should be added. In your room in alastor you have a map on the wall you can interact with, why cant we fast travel and revisit areas to look for things we may have missed?More optimized graphics with more eye candy in the different regions to make them more unique from one another.adjustable difficulty so the game can be at least somewhat challenging.More fleshed out lore of the world and creatures within it, collectables in the world with lore even.So much potential in this game, but just feels rushed and forced, could have been such a great game. I hope if any DLC or future titles in the world are released, they spend more time to fully develop and explore the unique world.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. The world seems really interesting and the visual style is cool, but the sheer volume of particle effects, muddy bloom, lack of contrast, and zero options to tweak anything beyond the brightness and quality, and the general oversight for any reasonable UI/UX design makes for a game far lesser than the sum of its parts.Gameplay is fine. A bit clunky. Mostly due to the randomness of if set decoration will or will not have collision on it and the aforementioned muddy visuals. There were times I had no idea there were several enemies on screen due to the constant cacophony of visual noise. I'd like to be able to see the important parts of this VIDEO game :) The UI is awful. The huge blue and red color splashes make me feel like I'm looking through Vaseline coated frosted glass in a night club and the bright colors hide the important information from being readable in the player's peripheral vision. The "heads up display" is generally supposed to provide quickly readable information, not hide it... Maybe it stands for "Hazy, unreadable display" internally.Cutscenes are a drag. World conversations are great since you can click through at your reading speed, but scripted cutscenes are so damn slow. You hear 5 syllables of meaningless babble and then get to read "Welcome!" for 7 seconds before the next line auto progresses. Even if you had intelligible dialogue skipping forward on a per-line basis would be the best solution.Luckily I only paid $4 on humble for this, so I'm not too upset as that's what it feels worth as an experience. But it's so close to being good that I hope these eventually get addressed. I literally just want to be able to see the game

_childDocuments_.review: l is a twin-stick shooter set in a post-apocalyptic world where humanity has been brought to extinction after a catastrophic event, while anthropomorphic creatures have built their own citadels and need to defend themselves from the slug plague. You play as Clid, a mercenary snail followed by a cute firefly called Belu. After a troublesome rescue mission, they are exiled from their village and forced to look for a new home, which they find in Alastor, a group of outcasts with a mission to exterminate the slug menace. The premise itself is nothing original since other games such as  already feature anthropomorphic animals fighting in post-human environments, but the world building is solid and the gameplay cleverly alternates shooting stages with puzzles and narrative sections.Cid and Belu are a funny duo and both well-characterized, but it’s difficult to connect with all the other characters for how little they appear on screen and this unfortunately ruins a few good twists during the final part of the game. Characters don’t talk but only mumble and you can’t skip a single line of dialogue during a cutscene, you can only skip it entirely. I’m saying this cause it often took me a few seconds to read the dialogue lines, but I still had to wait for the characters to stop mumbling in order to move on with the narrative. Fortunately this doesn’t happen during standard NPCs conversations, which can be skipped at your own pace of reading.As mentioned earlier, the game is a twin-stick shooter with an isometric view. Clid has a good set of weapons and gadgets, which can be purchased from merchants or unlocked simply by progressing with the story. The game is generally easy, with only a few spikes towards the end. Most of the time we will be forced to back away, dodge and move constantly while shooting enemies, so there isn’t much strategy involved and only a few bosses require a change of tactics.Despite the main trailer showing some fast-paced combat, what I found was rather slow shooting, recharging and rolling, which became bothersome at times. The gunplay is pretty decent, but there is still some input lag. Fans of the genre will probably have a hard time dealing with this and the low difficulty, but overall the combat experience still feels enjoyable.The art direction is really great and environments feature different biomes, from desert landscapes to snowy mountains. It’s a pity that the level design is mostly linear and the exploration feels optional. You can only find seeds that can be used to increase your vitality or some chests containing in-game currency, but you will eventually be so rich that it will become pointless.Overall, Clid the Snail is a beautiful and enjoyable experience, but short. While the game is clearly a good debut for the team, it never meets its potential as a twin-stick shooter. The world building puts a solid base with Clid and Belu being a charismatic duo, but everything else is left rough and too vague.

_childDocuments_.review: The year is 2004. At Toys 'R Us you survey the shiny, shrink-wrapped denizens of the gaming department, perhaps accompanied by a parent, or maybe a chum who, like you, is raring to go for a new experience in our favorite of favorite hobbies: Video Games.There's a jingle of coin in your or your mother or father's pocket and you will not be leaving this store without seeing it spent. You glance at Snake Eater, unsure of what exactly goes in in that game; you pick up a display case promoting Prince of Persia: Warrior Within. "Nah dude," your sagacious friend cautions. He is wise beyond his years.Past the stack of empty GameCube boxes and the innumerable advertisements for Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, something rimmed in the Mountain Dew green of an Xbox case catches your eye. It's Clid the Snail. And it's Only on Xbox.You're immediately struck by the cover art. Sure you've seen the likes of anthropomorphic marsupials wield heavy weaponry before, but never before has it dawned on you to consider that a snail--let alone a snail with legs--might festoon his hearty hollow with the armaments of warfare. Your curiosity gets the better of you. You buy Clid the Snail for $49.99.At home, past the glowing architecture of your Xbox's interface, you're enraptured by a sailor-mouthed snail and his Navi-like companion as they slowly, deliberately atomize crazed slug tribesman and conspire with Banjo Kazooie-soundin' critters who, like our titular mollusk, find themselves exiled of their own kind and forced into a ragtag mercenary outfit of gunslingers-for-hire, carving a bloody swath through the scourge of slugs that would infest this strange, edgy, somehow strongly-considered fantasy world our crinkled pal Ulysses Grant purchased us admittance to.You beat Clid the Snail.It wasn't terribly lengthy. You grew frustrated with the game's shotgun simplicity. The trudging, languid pace of navigation (although I guess, for real, you are LITERALLY a snail, so to level any criticism at the actual pace of Clid the Snail's movement is almost providing the developers with the argumentative equivalent of a silver bullet with which they may respond "Well duh, you fool, it's in the title") and the not-always-quite-landing banter between our gritty gastropod and co. Here was a game with flaws. Deep flaws.Yet, for all that one might devastate Clid the Snail for, for its mediocrity or just-passability in most of its gameplay fundamentals, you stop yourself from feeling this self-righteous critic's scorn. You stop yourself because, you realize, Clid the Snail had heart. Clid the Snail HAS heart. Here was a game so warped in its premise yet diligently-realized, scripted by a precocious child yet still hammering at shards of painful truth in its characterizations, and simple in its twin-stick ambitions yet satisfying in its gibbing of slug assailants that, in hindsight, you had Fun. And while you're likely to swap discs for Halo 2 and not swap discs again for some long duration, you won't forget Clid. Sure, his was a remarkably simple journey, propelled by waves of mindless slugs for the slaughter and some uninspired level design that even you, a child, could see was a little iffy. A minor episode on a literally-miniature scale. History will likely not smile fondly at the memory of Clid the Snail the way she may recall the adventures of Ratchet and friend Clank, or the crude quips of Conker on his most baddest of fur days. Heck, Clid might not even stand a chance against Blinx. Or Voodoo Vince!But Clid was a snail with GUNS, for Pete's sake. And boy howdy did he know how to use them.

_childDocuments_.review: Clid the Snail mixes up combat with exploration where you can find seeds to increase your max health along with plenty of chests full of currency that can be spent at the local trading posts to resupply.  There’s nothing terribly original about the core game design; we’ve all done this same stuff in dozens of other games, but Clid puts a unique spin on the design with its visionary creature design and the microcosmic world they inhabit.  There is a fun assortment of weapons that encourages close and long-range combat along with tactical use of the landscape.  There are also some fun puzzle-solving and traversal challenges that require you to navigate these deadly lasers.  And don’t forget about some insanely creative boss fights; that rat with the flamethrower and rocket launcher is only the beginning.The overall difficulty is pretty tame and doesn’t seem to increase as you progress the story.  Boss fights are pretty easy too once you figure out the “gimmick” for each.  I suppose this is a god design for younger gamers looking to simply pass the time.  There is also a lot of dialogue in the game, conversation and exposition, and it’s all spoken in gibberish, which means you get to read a lot of text.  You can skip it with a button press but there is often important info lurking in those text boxes.  Some text boxes will auto-advance while others make you click a button between sentences.  I wasn’t expecting voice acting, but this much reading can really mess with the momentum of the gameplay.  I did appreciate the French accent for Clid.Read the full review at Watch the first two hours of the game at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -

In addition to a delightfully grim environment ready to be explored, players will experience a vast array of weapons, mechanics, and puzzles that will encourage creative and strategic gunplay.
