I was playing on my steam deck and was frustrated from dying multiple times a row in the game I was playing so I went to my library and sorted Great on Steam Deck by most positively rated and this one shot to the top, so I figured OK, I'll give it a shot. Oh. My. God. It is so good. I actually completed the full play-through (not all the achievements, but for me to complete a full play-through is practically unheard of) I was occasionally stumped, but the user base online with walkthroughs are good, and it's pretty easy to figure out where you need to go next. Which is not to say it's easy, it's challenging in a fun way. There are multiple ways to complete most of the puzzles. Failure does not put you back very far, which I appreciate. I could try things and fail and then immediately try a different idea without having to play through a bunch that I've already played through. After the first play session, I decided just to clear my schedule and play all weekend and complete the game. The storyline is complex emotionally if you want to engage with it, but you don't need to. The mystery unfolds elegantly and interestingly. The characters are cute and interesting and their problems are relatable. I think my favorite was the monster in the cabinet. The world-building is top-notch. The graphics are fun and well-built. I have a talent for getting stuck between polygons and not being able to move, and for once in a 3D open world, I did not get stuck once. I would highly recommend this game to anyone who likes cute puzzle games that makes you think and feel. It is not a long game, which I don't consider a downside. There are definitely opportunities for replay with various races and extra credit achievements. My only annoyance is that the Nintendo Switch version is practically impossible to find on a cartridge, and their stupid DRM system makes it so I only buy cartridges for my nephew, which is not a knock on the game but rather Nintendo :)
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: The level design is top notch. The writing and music are entertaining. The mechanics are solid, although you might eventually notice that you are doing the same sort of things in each level. It isn’t a precision platformer though. It’s exploration in an amusing bug-world. I only wish things were explained better in the ending. There’s a lot of well-written dialog in the game, and plot devices, why wasn’t this talent used to wrap it all up? But this feels like a quibble next to the 10-12 hours of a wonderful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a sucker for platformer/collectathon games, and Tinykin certainly delivered. I thoroughly enjoyed playing it!The movement feels good, especially the "soapboard" to move around quickly. (think skateboard, but instead it's a bar of soap 😋) There are even races you can do with it, if you're into that.The art and sound are all very cute. And the soundtrack is nice too. I still have one of the songs stuck in my head. 😁Because of the genre, I wasn't expecting much in the way of story. But I was positively surprised, intrigued and even a little moved at the exposé at the end of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Playing a tiny character in a scaled up approximation of real world locations in one of my favourite types of environmental theming in games, and Tinykin just may be my new favourite. Journeying through all the rooms of the house as a two-inch explorer provides plenty of creative takes on settings that combine regular household objects into a selection of differently themed levels. It takes a smidge of inspiration from Pikmin in the form of the Tinykin, but recontextualises them in a 3D collectathon platformer space to marvellous results.Controls are smooth as butter, art direction is excellent, sound design is satisfying, and the music makes great use of dynamic tracks. Level design is not only visually brimming with creativity, but is laid out in such a way that it's satisfying to explore and get around and rarely leaves you searching high and low for one particular collectable for long. It's quite the feat for stages as huge as they are.Tinykin was one of the most enjoyable 3D platformers I've played in a while and I absolutely see myself coming back for repeat playthroughs in the future. It's quite a testament to its quality when the only gripe I can think of is that it's a little on the easy side.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game was honestly just a ton of fun. A great mix of Pikmin and paper Mario without either of those two games' shortcomings. The exploration is fun, the world is cute, the dialog is funny, and somehow it manages to always feel rewarding. Never once did I feel like it was a hassle to collect every single thing in the game. That to me is a sign of a very good game. On top of that the challenge stuff is so frustrating but also super fun to do. Not normally into that stuff but I don't know how they pulled it off it was very fun in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is a 3D platformer that really manages to scratch that collectathon itch.You will go through six unique zones each packed with things to do in every corner and exploring them is just a delight, it's very satisfying to move around the room which is what you'll be doing most of the time. They really nailed the movement with the soapboard having you unlock rails you can grind on, as well as one of your abilities letting you stack your tinykin into a ladder allowing you more freedom of movement as you progress a level.It takes around 10 hours to 100% all achievements and it isn't very hard to do, I do wish there was an upgrade that helps your track missing objectives after you finish the game or something but I just made sure to fully explore everything before moving on so it wasn't a big deal.There's also extra challenge races that are not required for any of the achievements but are very fun to do and reward you with skins, and getting the platinum medals can be quite hard.(Note: there's a bug where to have some achievements unlock you need to revisit all levels, but it's barely an issue and the only one I encountered)Overall it's just a very solid game, highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing platformer than goes back to basics. It doesn't try to introduce any complicated new mechanics just refines ones that have existed for a long time resulting in this excellently crafted world. Pairing this with a beautifully told story and cute art style makes it into one if the best indie games this year if not one of the best games this year. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I first played Pikmin back in highschool I have always wondered what it would be like to have Pikmin style game play elements in an collect-a-thon 3D platformer. Tinykin scratches that itch perfectly. The movement system in the game is quick and snappy and really emphasizes your ability to chart your own path through the enviorment rather than the other way arround. Tinykin easily stands its own against its contemporaries and has an amazing sense of identity. Tinykin is a must play for all collect-a-thon fans out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin has no enemies, just a few obstacles which you easily overcome. Every time you advance within a new area, you gather a giant army of minuscule creatures, who can either carry heavy items, or build bridges or explode barriers. When you don't command them to do the above actions, they just follow you around aimlessly. Could have been used to push back hostile bugs (those shielded are everywhere!), help with boss fights (there's none) or I dunno - form walls for motion detected sequences (also non existent). Give me a damn challenge! :(The core play of Tinykin is checking all possible corners, ledges, hidden passages and multi level platforms. You never know what you might find - an objective item? a collectible pollen or a nice reference?However. Because nobody and nothing stops you from exploring or gathering story things, the play turns into a boring vacuum sucking activity and tedious search. Attention, memory! Have we checked behind those books? Did we bring that lost animal we spotted earlier? And what about those eggs we thought "oh we would collect them later...", where were they?
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Polished, super cute 3D platformer with a satisfying gameplay loop.As a scientist from another planet, Milo wants to find out where humanity came from. For unknown reasons, his research makes him end up in a 1990s earth house, but shrunk to the size of a bug. He finds said house inhabited by lots of cute talking insects, but also by "tinykin", an even cuter species of tiny spherical creatures. Every tinykin species is very good at one task, for example, some are strong and can carry heavy objects, others can explode, and yet others can stack into ladders. For further unknown reasons, the tinykin really, really like Milo and follow him around, allowing him to use their help to get to otherwise unreachable places and solve problems.Milo sets out to explore the house and unlocks one room after another. He helps the insects with various problems and gets their help in return. When you first enter a new room, you have the liberty to go into any direction and tackle everything in whichever order you like. As you reach new places, you can release climbing and connecting ropes to allow you to later quickly return everywhere, often from a hub in the middle of the room. This makes it easy to move from task to task and also to climb to high spots to check the room for any missed pollen. This pollen is a collectible of which there are hundreds in every room. If you collect a certain amount, you can buy upgrades for Milo's flying suit, allowing him to float in the air for longer and longer times. I'm not sure whether you actually need these upgrades to finish the game, but they do help to reach every place.I had lots of fun playing this and cooing over all the cuteness (one favourite: a bunch of tinykin carrying an object together, with very determined faces and little shouts of "heh! hoh!"). The platforming difficulty was just right- motivating, not too easy, not too hard. I was shortly frustrated in two spots, but that's really nothing compared to the total playtime.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Pleasant collect-a-thon type game with great graphics, gameplay and soundtrack. The only fault is the game is very easy with minimal puzzle aspects, however it was such a pleasure to play that the lack of difficulty can be overlooked. This is the perfect game to play when you want to relax and turn your brain off for a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is a fantastic collectathon platformer, right up there with the likes of Banjo Kazooie, Spyro and Mario Odyssey. It makes good use of its "tiny character in a big world" idea with thoughtful level design and layouts that allow players to easily memorise their surroundings, and incorporate gameplay mechanics inspired by Pikmin, with its eponymous throwable minions, the Tinykin.The game follows Milo, a human inhabitant of a distant planet, who after learning his species didn't originate there, finds his way to Earth in the 90's. Once he arrives to investigate, we see that he's tiny compared to the humans on earth, and around the same size as insects. From here, he meets and communicates with insects, and learns about the mysterious Ardwin, who they revere as a god. From here, Milo encounters Pikmin-like creatures called Tinykin, each with different abilities and properties, and must aid the insect denizens of an abandoned home with the help of these new creatures, all while rebuilding a machine that can return him home. The game has the player travelling across 6 main areas within a regular human house, and finding a machine part in each. These areas will have their own unique mini-story to tell, and in order to get the machine parts, the player has to help the denizens of these areas with whatever troubles they're facing. There are also side-objectives that award the player some mysterious objects, belonging to a museum-keeper, and a whole ton of collectible nectar to find (collecting 900 per area will award Milo an extra bubble to glide with and allow him to reach areas he otherwise wouldn't). So right off the bat, there's a clear main objective, and side content for completionists and fans of collectathons to scour through. Milo can jump, climb ropes, skate on a bar of soap and grind on strings of silk, glide a short distance with his bubble, and throw Tinykin, which are used to solve a variety of puzzles and deal with various obstacles. Pink Tinykin carry objects and push obstacles out of the way, Reds explode on contact with any flammable or otherwise weak obstacles and destroy them, Greens stack on top of each other to give Milo a makeshift ladder to reach high places with, Blues conduct electricity from an outlet to a broken cable, and Yellows form a staircase for the Pinks to carry objects across. The game gets a lot of mileage out of each type of Tinykin, and they lend themselves very well to the exploration-based gameplay of collectathons. They hatch from eggs after being touched, and the more you have at your disposal, the more you can achieve in each area. The Tinykin you find in one area don't follow you to the next, likely to balance the game's difficulty and prevent players from trivialising the puzzles in later areas. The 6 areas, despite all taking place in the same house, are visually and functionally distinct from one another. The third area serves as the "water" area, since it takes place between a toilet room and a bathroom separated by a door, with one side's inhabitants being disturbed by the other's constant partying. And the 5th area is a kitchen with many sponges stacked on top of each other to give the illusion of a grassy field with rivers of water flowing between them, serving as the set-piece to a conflict between a well-meaning monarch and an uprising of disgruntled working-class ants. The way the developers refashioned every-day objects to create these differing insect societies with their own stories and problems to face is clever, and it's the sort of charm I've been missing since games like Clockwork Knight and Chi-bi Robo. While there are water and plant hazards that'll set Milo back to the last place he stood (in addition to fall damage that forces players to carefully consider where they explore), the game has a surprising lack of enemies to fight. Seriously, like an Icelandic man once said, there are no enemies. This is a neutral aspect, one that I'm neither for nor against, on its own, but it's clear the devs' focus was on the treasure-hunting and exploration. So in that regard, I'd say it was a smart call. And again, since the levels have various landmarks and points of reference, the treasure-hunting never devolves into finding a needle in a haystack, even if you have one piece of nectar missing. If you're looking for more of a challenge though, then the aptly-named Challenge Update and its content should suffice. This free update includes timed races across the 6 sprawling areas for the best time, with a medal from Bronze to Platinum being awarded depending on the player's time. They make great use of the areas, and give you a good reason to go back to them, as clearing each one will unlock new costumes for Milo to wear. While the platinum medals teter on the edge of ball-busting, they're still doable and fair enough to make the 100% completion experience worth it, and they made me put the soapboard to good use. The game's visuals are top-notch too, going for a toony impressionistic look. Surprisingly, Milo and all the NPC's in the game are 2D, similar to other indie 3D platformers like Demon Turf and Here Comes Niko! I didn't know what to make of this at first, this being my first foray into these types of games, but having played the game to full completion, I can safely say it doesn't detract from the gameplay one bit, as far as precision platforming goes. I initially played Tinykin on Xbox One via Gamepass, and since it never went on sale after my subscription expired, I got the Steam version. While it meant I couldn't continue from where I left off, it allowed me to play the game at an ideal 60fps, which was easily achievable even on my outdated hardware. I do wish there were a few more graphics options to adjust the draw distance and overall clarity, but the game still looks great as is. The sound design is nothing to scoff at, either. Each object Milo walks or lands on has a distinct, believable sound effect to make the game's world feel more lived-in, from scrunching sponges to the pings of steel cutlery. The game also features an up-beat, whimsical dynamic soundtrack, which shifts and changes depending on what part of an area you're in or how much progress has been made there. No expenses were spared, it seems, and the game has the overall polish you'd expect from a double-A or even triple-A game (ideally, anyway). Very impressive how much care, creativity and attentiveness went into the game, considering it was made by small indie studio Splashteam. My only real criticism is that the achievement for collecting all 6 glide-bubbles doesn't trigger unless you revisit each area. This really needs to be addressed or fixed somehow, as I didn't know what was going on until looking outside the game for answers. Other than that, the game is as close to a 10/10 as you can get, and in the 18 hours I spent doing everything, I was having a blast. One of my favourite games from last year, and easily a favourite among the many in my Steam library. Definitely get the game if you enjoy collectathon platformers, Pikmin-likes, or any games where a tiny bloke explores a human home. It's worth the full price, but it's an absolute steal on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game so far, and if you like Pikmin you will like this game. This game is by no means is a Pikmin clone, but rather takes inspiration from the series. It brings back nostalgia from the collect-a-thons of N64. Tinykin is relaxing until you get to the races, which makes me rage a bit. I highly recommend when on sale or even at full price. 8.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful 3D platformer with elements of Pikmin or the Overlord games.I had a good time playing it and had to laugh quite often. You can't have a bad time playing this gem.There's so much to explore in this game and quite some stuff to collect, but not too much to be overwhelming.Update 11/26/2022: I got a Steam Deck since I wrote this review. Tested it in the Deck, runs without problems.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the world of It Takes Two this game is a must try.Otherwise just an adorable world to explore where you are tiny and the household things are big. I loved the tiny beds and houses the bugs had made of buttons and matchsticks>Music was okay, parkour wasn't hard. Not a fan of the challenge update with time based races but it's not mandatory.The best part was exploration. The world is beautifully made. wish they added a pollen tracker in the end game but even without it easily possible to 100% the game. I loved exploring every inch of the house collecting things. Some achievements are bugged, fixes are there but doesnt show on steam sometimes, sadly.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great if you are aren't a completionist, but tedious if you are. The main problem is that once you backtrack to an area you may get some pointers on side missions, but these are usually not hard to find either way. However trying to completely collect all pollen and tinykin is an awfully frustrating endeavor.you get no hints or rough area for where to search so it may mean you spend 9 complete scans of all your surroundings until you finally find that one pollen you are missing on a shoelace (climbable rope), or that one cluster of tinykin that just was just laying around on the side of the road. I even resorted to video guides for 2 of the levels and followed them around in 5 second intervals because it got too frustrating.Simple things like talking to an NPC and him telling you a rough area to search in, or the objective tracking goggles hinting at the location of collectibles once you found enough of them would have helped a lot but as it is now I regret 100%ing this game. It just wasn't fun.Even more frustrating was when I finally found all there is to find and due to a bug the achivements both ingame and in Steam didn't unlock. This is a bug that was known for years, while revisiting every location of the game seems to fix it, it just felt bad having to do this, it detracted from what little feeling of accomplishment there was.The story was, a little weird, leaves a bunch of things unanswered, some big mystery left pretty much unadressed. This is honestly fine and would make for interesting sequel plot.Speaking of a sequels, I do not recommend this game, but if it ever receives a sequel you should definitely check that out instead. This game was decent, but fell flat in the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games (minor spoilers ahead).Tinykin is an indie casual 3D platformer set in an oversized house with each level taking place in different parts of the house, each one with a special name and theme. The levels have simple puzzles that need to be solved by using the minions you can collect throughout the levels, each type with different abilities, but regardless of the puzzles the game is more about exploring the worlds and finding items to complete quests or gain artifacts.The story isn’t very developed during the game, having mostly just a few cutscenes at key moments, but the lore and culture of each species of insect that inhabits each level is unique. There are also a few other NPCs that give you instructions, requests or upgrades.The graphics are good and the 3D levels have lots of interesting details and objects, and some of them can be interacted with. The main character and other characters don’t have a 3D model, instead they are 2D figures, similar to paper mario, in a stylized and cartoony style. In general, the animations are well done and fluid, from simple movements to the different death animations.The level design also has a lot of depth and verticality, you have to explore the grounds as well as the top platforms located near the ceiling and glide in the air a lot.The music and sound effects are also fantastic. The songs change depending on what’s near you, the creatures sing and rejoice and overall the ambiance is very cheerful. Some platforms also have a different sound when you jump on them depending on the material they are made of, and that’s a very nice detail.Regarding gameplay, and as I have mentioned besides the puzzles there are a lot of items to find and collectibles to get, and if you want to 100% the game you’ll need to get everything. In each level I managed to get the essential items rather easily, but it’s very easy to miss a spot or interactable object and struggle to find the last collectibles you’re missing and they happened to be in most levels. After you complete the levels, there are a few races you can do to unlock cosmetics, and they are also fun, but very demanding, and if you’re trying to get the best medal, every move needs to be flawless.     43 Achievements. 10 hours, but I’ve also got some medals and some of the races. Easy. Medium. While the game is easy, getting every collectible requires persistence and a lot of attention so you don’t miss anything. No achievements are missable, but some can get bugged in the end and might require you to revisit every zone, including the “stairs” and “attic” to unlock. Tinykin a very fun to play indie 3D platformer with a lot of items to find and collect, in levels that are unique and beautifully designed. The music is also a joy to listen to and overall it offers a lot of content and things to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Recommendable on sale only. No less than half-price.Gameplay loop is not rewarding but other than that, what you see is what you get; a casual time waster.For this reason, I cannot give it a thumbs down especially given that I am not giving it a longer playtime.Maybe it gets better. I doubt it, but fair is fair.Platforming could be more enjoyable but again, the main appeal of the game is the puzzle-solving with your kins. I did not go far enough to judge how hard the puzzles can get but again. there was not enough fun/reward for me to justify wasting an indefinite amount of time waiting for the puzzles to get rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game. It's beautiful, polished to a fine shine, each of the worlds feel brimming with things to explore. It also has one of the strongest first levels of any platformer I've ever played. So many little things in this game add up to an incredibly strong experience. For example, the soap-board that allows you to travel more quickly through each level, adds so much mobility to the game. Gliding around the levels is easy and joyful. That's just one example among many that create an excellent game. If it looks like your kind of game, pick it up even if it's not on sale. Just a joy.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A fun cutesy little game. I did 100% it and I would say that took me maybe around 8 hours or a little less to do so. There were some issues with achievement progress not counting but that was cleared up by entering and exiting the levels. Another weird thing about the achievements is that it hides info on what are some rather basic achievements that you may not necessarily run into while playing, such as get eaten by a plant. It has them as hidden in game and on the Steam Achievements page so with those either you stumble into them at some point while playing or you have to look them up at the end to figure out what you need to do to get those last few hidden ones even though you 100 percented every room.I definitely give this game a recommend and I hope to see some more Tinykin content or sequels in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This platformer is an absolute gem that exudes charm at every turn. The art style is fantastic, and the music is simply sublime - I was thoroughly impressed! A standout moment for me was the bathtub rave - it was just too much fun! Overall, Splashteam has done a remarkable job with this game, and I can't wait to see what they have in store for us next. Definitely keep an eye on these guys!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Good music, cute and whimsical art. But a very bland game, just a large collection minigame.Has a few obnoxious gameplay bits, including the inability to choose what type of Tinykin to use, general camera wonkiness while aiming, and soap bar being a little too unpredictable.Would have loved to see some actual puzzles, or the ability to use tinykin for more than just their singular use, very frustrating to not have enough pink ones just because you can't recall ones that are holding something on the other side of the map.I guess I was hoping for something more Pikminesque and got a cute but bland minigame.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This was a super fun collectathon! The movement and transition on and off of the soapboard felt very smooth. I've been able to find most of the collectibles just by exploring but there are some levels that I'm only missing a few items. The only thing I think would make this game a bit more enjoyable (as a completionist, not for everyone) would be an option to enable a Tinykin and pollen tracker once you finish the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game! The setting feels clearly inspired by Pikmin, but the game itself is very different. Tinykin is a collectathon platformer, with some solid movement mechanics conducive to exploration. Your main goal is to go around helping people in these different bug societies, and gathering parts towards the game's main objective. The Tinykin themselves are basically items to help you explore, there's no fighting system and they aren't at risk of dying.The thing I liked most about Tinykin was the level design. There is a ton of creativity put into the design of the world, and there's a lot in it to admire in the small details and in the bigger picture of each area and how they fit together in the game's world as a whole. The NPCs are well written, with a lot of work put into fleshing out their different societies and how they all interact.I had an excellent time finding all the secrets this game had to reveal, searching every nook and cranny to find all the collectibles, and completing all the sub-missions to achieve each level's major goal. It took me 19 hours to beat 100%, though a lot of that time went into these unlockable race challenges. Note: If you 100% it and achievements are glitched, re-visiting each of the game's areas in the same gameplay session should fix it, and won't take too long.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever played a game that is just pure joy? All around fantastic work by the team, from gameplay/movement and level design to audio/music and art/cinematic, it was a magical ride from beginning to end. I was already in love with the demo and this game delivers even more than I could hope for. Beside being an absolute blast for completionist - what a delightful and adorable game it is!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: When I played the demo I knew immediately that it was worthy of a day one purchase. I fell in love with this game instantly and it made me remember why I enjoy 3d platformers so much. This game feels like pikmin but it uses its inspiration for puzzle solving mixed with exploration and is not a real time strategy game. One thing that Tinykin focuses on that makes it stand out from other platformers  that it focuses on vertical exploration combined with horizonal though the former being the main focus, as most 3d platformer tend to be an obstacle course design instead this game has a sandbox style of 3d platforming gameplay to it(similar to mario 64 in a way).It has goodies to collect and that makes exploring make addictive and I consider this to be one of the greatest indie 3d platformers I have ever played. Its art style and animation suits the game's setting as well. My minor complaint is collecting all the pollen which I wish they had a system similar to demon turf where you press L3 button to show an arrow  where you are missing the pollens, nevertheless this game is really fun and makes me glad there are creators that want to make 3d platformers while still standing out from other games in the 3d platforming genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best collectathon platformers on Steam, an incredibly polished and charming game akin to Hat in Time.Always loved the theme of being ant-sized in a human sized world, and Tinykin nails it perfectly. All the small details not only fit their respective rooms, but create a very fun playground. Hidden collectables under a crease in the rug, a wedge of cheese used as a ramp in the kitchen, smart usage of everyday items that always gave me a laugh when I noticed them.Speaking of laughs, this game is FILLED with funny characters with even funnier names. All sorts of references to realworld and videogame names are crammed into almost everything. I'd say thenegative point I have with this game is the painfully annoying 100% completion experience.Most levels have upwards of 1200 pollen (the primary collectable), as you zip-zoom around the levels you're bound to miss some. Not the end of the world, but coming back later to find the 3 pollen you missed in an enormous level with loads of hidden nooks and nothing to help you? Not fun.This could easily be fixed if they implemented something like the recent Spyro remake has; a button that gives you a ping to send you searching in the right direction.Overall a great experience, especially if you can get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Went in expecting Pikmin and ended up with an average 3d platformer with a garnish of Pikmin - a veneer, really. Three hours in, I didn't feel like I was exploring and building an army of minions naturally. Rather, the hand-holding between levels and the lack of meaningful upgrades meant I just couldn't finish this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game. It gave me serious feelings of childhood nostalgia. I love the setting. Your about as big as an ant and you get to explore a normal sized house that's filled with life. Every room has a very distinct feeling to it. The bugs have very charming designs and the amount of references is insane. Gameplaywise you might think: "Oh its Pikmin" but its more of a puzzle-platformer collectathon. The movement feels smooth and the "puzzles" aren't overly tedious. Didn't put a lot of time into the races but the ones i did felt fairly challenging. Storywise the game is fine. Nothing new but still very wholesome with a nice "plottwist". Overall 9/10 wish it had more content (even though i know it has the perfect length).
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: very nice mix of platforming and pikminsuper satisfying to get everything in a map, there's no really hidden things or big secrets but just getting everything is funpretty short game, would recommend buying while on sale for the amount of time it takes to beat it (I played 6 hours and I don't have 100% every map but I'm missing like 20 pollen per map max and got everything else, so like 98% completion)cute style, cute music, cute charactersrecommended for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure: I got this game for free since a friend already owned the game, but he got an extra copy of the game from a bundle he bought.A very fun game... if you get past the intro and the story. This game takes some time to really open up to the player. But once it does it really opens up and is a ton of fun. I would highly recommend this game. Though I did not enjoy the story or characters involved until the very end. The gameplay feels super smooth and nice to control. Though it is weird that the player character is always facing towards the camera and never faces away. I was able to ignore it after a while but at first it really threw me off. I also didn't enjoy the main character's design. I think it's purely a me issue, but to me the main character looks like one of those rich snobby bully characters you'd see in a cartoon, rather than a smart scientist hero.But again overall the game is great. I would have enjoyed some more designs for the bug characters since those were great!

There is a level select in the game so if you miss collectables you can go back and get them (offering even more replayability to the game!)I had so much fun playing Tinykin.  I happened to play it on stream and received a lot of comments how it was similar to Pikmin but I haven't played it before.  The levels are so fun to explore and collect all the items. The little tinykin are so adorable! There's a lot of content in the game - you'll want to go back in the levels to explore all the puzzles and collect everything which gives it more replay value. _childDocuments_.review: Played the whole game on Steam Deck with proton-ge, no crashes or anything like that.  Generally ran well on high settings, with some minor (but not unplayable) slowdown in the last few big areas. This game is absolutely wonderful. On the shorter end of things, took me about 7 hours for a not-quite-completionist playthrough, but they were 7 great hours. There's so much love and care put into this game. Artstyle is super charming, with these nice dry brush textures and these lived-in settings. If you like the micro-scale of games like Pikmin and Chibi-Robo, you'll be absolutely thrilled with Tinykin's rich and varied environments. Not a difficult game but it's not a boring one either, there's tons of charm and the levels are fun to bop around in. Seems like everywhere you turn there's something to discover. Buy it. An absolutely top shelf indie game. My favorite non-Elden-Ring game of 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my! I would lie if I'd say that this game took me by surprise as I played the demo before release but still, oh my! I haven't even been much into "Collect-a-thon" games at all but this one. I can't stop smiling while playing. Moving around the cute/beautiful lvl on a kickass "soapboard" just feels too good. It's a welcome break of all those skill based games. Just have a nice, chilled time while you "GOTTA CATCH EM ALL!" (nope, I never played Pokemon) nor Pikmin.Cute artwork, cute characters, fluid gameplay. I really hope there will be more content (or a sequel) for this little gem. I am not done yet (half through the game I think) but I am already sad thinking about the end. Can't remember I've ever had such a chilled yet fun gaming experience. Being an 41yo old fart I feel like a kid again while playing this game. No worries, no pressure, just fun cruising around. Game runs well on a rather old rig (GTX 970, Xeon 1231v3), no bugs so far (tho I've read about some other players encountered some of).If I would have to mention a little downside it would probly be the fact that it CAN be somewhat frustrating at times if you can't find the last 10-50 pollen but - at least for me - that's not a big deal. 10/10 would hug those explosive cute tinykins again ♥

_childDocuments_.review: Wrote a long review but it got destroyed, so to tldr myself:6/10 The game is carried by its music, level design, and charm. The game is held back by its shallow gameplay, puzzles, and references (and the bugged achievements). Play it if you like collectathons, don't play it if you're looking for something to tide you over until Pikmin 4, as they're about as similar as Super Mario is to Super Meat Boy. Pikmin is all about micromanaging your minions to solve your puzzles, Tinykin's puzzles are a question of "do I have enough of X tinykin?" and the answer is almost always yes.If there were a Tinykin 2 that released as is, I'd only check out the OST. If they released with better/harder/more in-depth puzzles, I'd definitely give it a look and might even buy. Couldn't hurt to also have a collectible tracker when you have <100 pollen left, as that was probably how I spent the most amount of time on each level.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a sucker for 3D platformers, and when I discovered that Tinykin has some elements in common with Pikmin, I was very happy.Here's what I like:- An excellent mash-up of Pikmin and 3D platformer collectathons- Tinykin is a more relaxing experience than Pikmin. There aren't enemies to beat up, you can only get hurt by falling from high places or by staying in the water for a long period of time- If you intend to 100% the game, it may be quite challenging: collecting all the pollens and artifacts, and gathering every Tinikyn on the map are quite the task; moreover, Wasp Races are especially difficult (and fun) to beat the best times in order to get all the platinum medals- Funny easter eggs (spoiler)But, there are two issues about Tinykin:- All NPCs have 30 fps, while Milodane (the main character) has 60 fps. They probably did it to improve performance, but sometimes I find it a little unpleasant for my eyes- Some achievements related to collecting everything may not unlock; in case it happens, just visit every room in the game and then they must pop upIt took me about 8 hours to complete the main story, and 2 more to 100% the game.The best "Pikmin" game on Steam so far, I wish they were more games like this.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinkyin is an adorable 3D platforming game where you go through a house of bug-like creatures and help them help you go home. This game is so filled with charm, from the bouncy art style to the weird characters (many of whom were nerdy references) to the bouncy Tinykin themselves. It's very similar to Pikmin but with more of a focus on exploration than any management or combat. There's so much to explore, and the environments feel so immersive and fleshed out. There are a ton of different challenges, but nothing is missable, so this game is a great pick for completionists like me. I loved my time with this game, and I'd recommend it to anyone who enjoys running around creative worlds and solving puzzles with cute little Pikmin-like guys.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game. I was surprised how fleshed out and great the environments felt. There was lots to do and I loved the sense of scale with all the household objects and stuff, made it so much fun to explore. Game isn't overly challenging other than the races, which I ended up not engaging with in the end as it was just bonus content. You need some really precise inputs to do well on them from what I noticed and it's an insane difficulty jump. However, it isn't essential in any way to beating the game and has no impact on 100% achievements, it is there for those who like speedrunning and an extra challenge. But yeah, other than the races, the rest of the game has some simple platforming that shouldn't be too challenging for most people. But at the end of the day, it doesn't need to be challenging to be fun because I still had loads of fun with this game, as exploring and getting around the environments was a really enjoyable experience. There are a lot of collectables and bonus quests and things to do in each environment which is a lot of fun to do as well if you enjoy that kind of thing. You'll have to try and explore every little area to find them all which can be quite satisfying finding little hidden spots where they're hiding something. However, it can be a mild source of frustration if you are missing just one little thing as the game doesn't provide you with any way of finding them. I think this is probably the biggest and only flaw of the game in my opinion, since it can be incredibly tedious to find one tiny little collectable in such a huge environment. But I really do think the rest of the game makes up for that, and if you explore thoroughly and really take in each place you go to, you shouldn't have to do any backtracking to find anything.Overall, very cute and simple game that can bring a lot of joy and relaxation. The story is also very cute and interesting along with all the dialogues from the characters you can speak to. Just a great world to immerse yourself in. I shall give it a solid 9.5/10 easily

_childDocuments_.review: The game was enjoyable enough for me to roll credits. The art style is gorgeous and movement is fluid. Every stage introduces a new mechanic that keeps things fresh. This keeps exploration and platforming interesting all game long. There are also hidden Easter eggs and references littered throughout the game that are nice to stumble upon.While you don't play games like these for their story, I will still mention that the story felt a bit underwhelming to me. The premise of tiny creatures living and thriving in a giant house is really intriguing, but unfortunately was never utilized to its full potential. The developers did highlight various problems a civilization can run into in every stage, but the resolution of these problems were laughably bad. It felt like watching a history piece on the French Revolution that ends up with everyone actually eating cake.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried Tinykin at PAX East a few years ago, intrigued by a giant sign advertising the "World's Tiniest Man". What I found was an incredibly cute, charming, and creative 3D platformer that has all the best aspects of collect-a-thons and none of the tedium. The levels are all incredibly well-thought out and designed with a fantastic art style, the characters are funny and charming (I love bugs, so all the inhabitants of the game's world being bugs was great), and the light puzzles and challenges were fun, but not overly difficult. The story of the game was also fantastic, the plot was engaging and entertaining, and the mysteries unfolded at a perfect pace- not too slow that you forget things, but not too fast that you figure out the ending before you get there. The game isn't a long one, I beat it in 8 hours, and that's including collecting all the major items and upgrades per level, but not 100%ing them. But in those 8 hours, I had a blast! If you love 3D platformers or comfy games, this game is for you!

_childDocuments_.review: I had never heard of Tinykin before, but I received it as a gift from a friend. This one definitely flew under the radar for me because it ended up being a surprise hit for me!The closest game to Tinykin for comparison sake might be Pikmin, but even then they're very different in execution. The game does have you gathering different colors of the titular Tinykin to use their unique abilities to solve problems and overcome obstacles, but unlike Pikmin, you don't really have to protect take care of them. By this I mean the game has no combat and no hazards that will affect your Tinykin, so once you have them, you don't have to worry about losing them, save for a few types that are consumed upon achieving their function. This creates a very low stress environment which places the emphasis on exploration and puzzles.The exploration is easily the game's strongest aspect. Controls are precise and responsive, with the ability to jump, skate on soap (don't ask), or float with bubbles, in addition to using your Tinykin. Levels are large with plenty to see, and you progress by completing core objectives in each level to obtain a Thing. You also collect Nectar in the levels, which can be found lying around in the levels and also be rewarded for completing side quests and objectives. I actually enjoyed that Nectar had an incentive beyond simply collecting them for the sake of collection, for each level has a Nectar benchmark that once reached rewards you with the ability to lengthen how long you can glide. The levels are all appropriately varied, although some definitely flow better than others as a few of them could be a bit of a slog, especially the 2nd and 4th. Even so, the levels are charming and exploration and collection are rewarding.If there's anything holding the game back though, it's that it's a tad too easy when utilizing Tinykin. That is to say, when you target any object that can be interacted with by Tinykin, it will glow in the same color as the correct Tinykin, and automatically select that Tinykin for you. It makes it so the puzzles feel like they're effectively solving themselves for you; by the end I was just blowing through the levels gathering all the Tinykin I could first and foremost so I could just haphazardly toss them at any obstacle in my path without stopping. This doesn't make the game bad per se, but I didn't find myself as engaged as I could have been if I'd had to use a modicum of thought when solving them. This is especially significant considering the length of the game, as it only takes about 10 hours if you want to 100% the game. The visuals are charming with 3D environments contrasting with 2D Paper-like Characters. The character designs are nice and were fairly expressive, although I admit I can't say I was particularly attached to any of the characters given their role was rather small and only a few had unique models.  Likewise, the music is upbeat and charming as well, perfectly complementing the low-stress vibe of the game and matching the feel of each level appropriately. Overall, the game is a lot of fun, but don't expect to be challenged or need to put a whole lot of effort into succeeding. But if you want a short, low-stress game where you can explore and vibe, then this may very well be the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Really beautiful and really fun, I couldn't put it down and finished it in one day.  It's less like pikmin than it seems, more of a collectathon puzzle platformer.  The puzzles are really simple, and won't give you any friction, but sometimes that's what you want.  Great visuals, I love the shrunk down bug civilization in a suburban house setting, great music.  A+! A breezy and incredibly pleasant time!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is a 3D platformer with a gorgeous visual style, extremely fun and fluid controls, and is very comfy. It seems like it'd be similar to Pikmin, but there's no combat or time management or risk of losing your guys, so it's much more about exploration, and the little guys just help with that. You start each level with no Tinykin, and as you find more in the level, that opens up more paths and objectives to do.The levels are larger than life, and in particular, if you're a big fan of Chibi-Robo like I am, you will definitely love playing this game. The characters you meet in each level and the objectives you have to do for them are pretty entertaining. There's also optional challenge races that are a ton of fun to go for Platinum Medals in. The movement has a ton of depth, and I bet this will be a fun game for speedrunners to optimize.

_childDocuments_.review: is perhaps the best word to describe latest offering, , and not just because of the cute little critters that follow you around. The gameplay is reminiscent of that of Pikmin, which effectively blends together a puzzle-based real-time strategy to produce a unique and captivating experience. Although it is not the first game to feature a mixture of different genres, it does take the concept to new heights of complexity and design.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   The story takes place in an unfamiliar world of characters with balloon heads, saucer eyes, and pretzel limbs. You take on the role of Milo, tasked with finding parts to a ship that will eventually take him home. But Milo’s not alone in this endeavor as little critters called Tinykins are scattered about ready to help him accomplish the task.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   Giving orders to your little companions is straightforward as you only need to throw them at corresponding objects to do their thing. When you witness the Tinykins heave-hoing as they lift up heavy objects and faithfully rally back to you with a blow of a whistle will make you fall quickly in love with your little friends.Some of the puzzle elements early on are pretty simple but do get more complex the deeper into the game you get. Tinykins also have unique abilities and talents based on their character types so make sure to grab as many different ones as you can.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   Watching your babies grab onto each other to form ladders and bridges or act as electrical conduits to connect two circuits together will make you feel like proud parents, and unlike Pikmin, there are no fighting sequences which makes the game ideal for any age group.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   Aesthetically, struts down the PC catwalk as a perfect example of visual extravagance. The whimsical artistic style chosen by the developers has blossomed into a fully 3D world where everyday household items are all realized in stunningly realistic forms. The developers show us the world of Tinykin as a perturbing place where the inhabitants exist to be peculiar, obnoxious, but always funny.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   Each level reflects the changing scenery with lush beauty: a bedroom, a kitchen with an overflowing sink, and a playroom just to name a few. On the mountaintop of cabinets, for example, shiny bits of pollen are perched high above waiting to be discovered as the camera uses effective lateral movements to sweep across the opulent landscape. ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   The graphics are bright and vibrant and each level is littered with all things cute and friendly. The Tinykins themselves are so wonderfully modeled that you actually feel a sense of sadness when you aren’t able to collect and free them all. And despite having literally dozens and dozens of Tinykins on screen, the graphics engine holds up very well without any noticeable slowdown whatsoever.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   The only real disappointment I had with the title is that like any good game, it ends pretty quickly right as it’s hitting its stride. A few more diverse levels to explore would have made this much better. Even with this minor gripe, however, is so well developed that it will stand out against many of the bigger AAA titles out there. Its refreshing gameplay and innovative design will make it go down as one of the best games of the year.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀

_childDocuments_.review: Felt like a mix of an N64 collectathon and a more relaxed Pikmin, which for me means the game is fantastic. It looked amazing and ran great on my old potato of a machine. I also preferred mouse & keyboard in this game which was odd to me.Some negatives:I wouldn't have minded a few more abilities unlocked throughout the adventure and they're wasn't any reward besides achievements for collecting everything, which was disappointing considering how hunting down the last few pollen in a level was always a tedious challenge. Also, a few of the types of Tinykin were only useful as they were required for solving a few puzzles (yellow and blue) and they felt underwhelming. Green was definitely the most useful for exploring and sequence-breaking.Overall though, for a short romp, I loved this game. Definitely interested in looking into the speedrun. _childDocuments_.review: I'm such a sucker for games with a unique art style and a good OST... And this game delivers that in spades. Sure, the game is heavily inspired by the Pikmin series but it still has its own unique charm that allows it to stand on its own merit. I really enjoyed how much attention to detail the developers put into the game (i.e the OST changes dynamically to match whatever section of the level you are on... If you are inside a guitar, the level's theme song would change into an acoustic rendition of the song which made traversing each level really fun to do).  I thought the many references to pop culture was a nice touch to modernize the feel of the game and the controls felt so fluid and natural. My only gripe with the game is that the path to acquiring all the achievements was heavily focused on collectibles which can be a bit tedious given how daunting the scale of the levels can be. Overall, the game is packed with fantastic third-person platforming, creative mechanics, and levels that are a joy to explore... I definitely recommend checking this game out if the genre interests you at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun platformer + collectathon + a bit of Pikmin thrown in. The controls are fun, responsive, and never frustrating. The music and sound design is great on every level. I have really enjoyed collecting and exploring each impressively designed zone.If you like platformers or collection games, pick this up. It seems like most people 100% the game in 10-12 hours so keep that in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: The Pikmin comparisons are hard to avoid, but the game does enough to differentiate itself through its artstyle and charm. It's a low stress, lighthearted game, that wins you over through its joyful world that is fun to explore. Filled with details, that makes you feel the passion and love that the devs put into creating the environments. Importantly, aside from the great visuals, the game plays very well. The controls are noticably smooth and snappy, and I rarely had any moments, where I felt like it wasn't doing what I was intending to do. It's also the perfect length for a game like this. Not that I wouldn't have enjoyed to play more of it, but I believe the duration allows the game to end on a very high note, and feels like its not overstaying its welcome. The music is fun and adds to the charming presentation of the game. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best cozy game out there. An improvement in the pikmin formula, in my opinion. Fast, snappy movement but with relaxed goals make the game a breeze, in a great way. Beautiful art style, wholesome animations, and funny dialogue. One of the best games I've played in the last year. I hope we can see a sequel of some sort in the future or maybe some DLC in the form of more levels to explore and more tinykin to befriend.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: While Tinykin has a refreshing sense of style and brings unique Pikmin-like gamepaly to the PC for the first time, the gameplay elements - the environments, dialogue, puzzles and platforming - are simplistic and lose their novelty too quickly. Luckily the game is short (around 8-10hr) and doesn't overstay its welcome. Tinykin is tagged as a platformer, but its first a "collect-athon" and second a platformer. If that bias suites your tastes, then you'll likely enjoy this. If you are looking for complex platforming and rewarding exploration, look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: What a cute, inoffensive, little game. I played through the entire thing in one sitting and 100% it with very little difficulty. There's no enemies and the only thing you really do is use your movement and tinykins to explore, collect various items and currency, and solve simple environmental puzzles. That may sound negative, but it made for a fun time that hooked me with its gameplay loop. The controls feel great on a controller, though there can be a few times you miss a longer jump due to the slightly odd hover mechanic. You get used to it, but that and the soap-board grind mechanic tripped me up every now and then. A tiny nitpick in an otherwise solid game. I enjoyed my time playing and was pleased that it was only around 6 hours long. Didn't have enough time to outstay its welcome, so it left me wanting just a bit more (which is a good thing). I'd recommend this if you like 3D platformers, mixed with a little pikmin, all tied together with a cute story. Thanks for the fun game, developers!

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game for while and Tinykin is easily one of my favorite games this year. If you like cute adventures with lots of details, this ones for you. Pay attention to how the music and audio changes, all the little stories as you pass by, and small details like walking into the dust. Here is a 100% pollen run of Sanctar for a good sample: I look forward to continuing my adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I need to set your expectations of what this game is:This is a 3D platformer / collectathon. It does not play like Pikmin.Now that you expect a 3D collectathon, let me reset those expectations too: 1. Each large level is played one at a time, in order. You don't generally revisit a previous level except for optional speedrun challenges or for pursuing 100% completion.2. There is virtually no danger of dying or taking damage. You explore, jump, climb, and collect everything in a safe and stress-free treasure hunt. The few things that can kill you, such as fall damage or the occasional hazard, cost you nothing and set you back to your last safe standing spot. Instead of enemies, the world is populated by NPCs, most of which serve no purpose except to drop some cute dialogue. (Once I realized that most NPCs were pointless, I almost entirely stopped talking to them. Many had an attempt at humor, but most of the humor boiled down to a pun in their name or a pop culture reference.)Every level in this game is both visually impressive and structurally fun to climb around on. Every bit of space is made use of, and little hidden areas are everywhere. The gameplay essentially is a matter of collecting Tinykin of various colors which in turn allow you to access key objectives and more Tinykin, until you're able to explore the entire level. New Tinykin types are introduced throughout the game; most don't add a whole lot to the gameplay, but one of the earlier ones (green) is an especially clever idea for an ability for a 3D platformer. (No spoilers ;) )The music is great, the graphics feature crisp 2D character sprites and awe-inspiring environments. Interactive objects are clearly noted by colored outlines and designs, such as green climbable shoelaces or objects that need a particular type of Tinykin. The only interactive objects that sometimes betray your trust are grindable ledges - using a bar of soap for faster speed, you can get even more speed by grinding along ledges, but more than a few times I didn't enter the expected grind and instead fell the cliff. Bummer.Overall, Tinykin is like the bubble-wrap-popping version of a 3D platformer/collectathon. There's no danger and very little difficulty at all. It's just satisfying to explore and find everything. The only exceptions to the easy difficulty are the speedrun challenges: These are pure platforming challenges that route you all over the level with target times for bronze, silver, gold, and platinum. As an experienced speedrunner, I was usually able to get gold on my first or second try, but that certainly won't be the case for most players. For platinum medals, I was pleasantly blown away by how tough the times to beat were! It is seriously rare for a game to expect so much of a player (albeit for completely optional awards). These are like staff ghost times in racing games, and I love it.Anyway, Tinykin is fantastic, but you need to set your expectations accordingly. Also it's only around 5 1/2 to 7 hours long, depending on how thorough you are.

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is an extremely enjoyable platformer collectathon that doesn't overstay and is fun from beginning to end. The controls are tight, the music is fantastic, and there are tons of small things that make the game feel very polished. _childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others Imagine the problems associated with being shrunk down to the size of a tiny insect! Spiders bigger than us! Scary… Fortunately, Tinykin takes this idea very lightly and unfolds an imaginative adventure in a mix between Pikmin and a 3D adventure platformer, with a hint of collectathon, which will surely leave a smile on players’ faces.This title puts the player in the shoes of Milo, an archeologist from a planet called Aegis, who has a dream of finding the origins of the human race. After an accidental teleportation event, Milo finds himself transported to planet Earth in the year 1991. The main objective is to recover elements for the reconstruction of the machine that will take this peculiar character back to his planet. For this, he will have the help of Ridmi, who will serve as a guide, and the little Tinykin, who serve as support to cross the various obstacles presented and that gives the name to this title.Tinykins are extremely useful and the main point in the adventure story throughout the house that opens up while searching for the necessary elements. In each level, there are several types of eggs, which, when you pass over them, give life to Tinykins that closely follow Milo. Each Tinikyn has a color that is associated with a different skill. For example, the pink one has a strength like Hulk, so they are associated with heavier tasks, such as pushing objects or even transporting them from one place to another, while the blue ones, for example, allow you to position a conductive line of energy between two points, giving energy to electrical equipment. All tasks associated with Tinykins are associated with a number of elements, so if you find an obstacle but don’t have enough of them, the best is to explore the level a little more.Exploration is key and part of the fun. Using a soap instead of a skateboard or a flying platform serves the purpose of faster traveling and is somewhat reminiscent of the adventures of Ratchet and Clank. In fact, this title pays homage to different worlds and genres of pop culture. It is possible to see the moon and the bicycle from the movie E.T, Gary, the Spongebob snail, the symbol of Sly Cooper, among others. Explore and discover these delicious details.During the 7 hours of gameplay that I had, until I reached the end of his main story, divided between the main story and side missions, Tinykin presented 5 different rooms in the house, which are naturally associated with 5 different levels. Each division has a different insect civilization with its own ideas and where there is a need to help them to recover the captive object, which is necessary for the reconstruction of the machine. The mix between 3D levels with the paper craft aspect of the main character applies a very vibrant and different look than usual. Imagine a bathroom full of small castles made entirely of toilet paper, or a playroom with an intergalactic story where you can even destroy meteorites.Tinykin is certainly one of this year’s highlights. There’s no great depth, but what it does, it does it in a fun way. Of note are the small cutscenes that are fantastic. Will we be able to have a small Tinykin series in the near future?
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: (psst, if you like this game, play A Hat In Time)A charming collectathon platformer, that captures the 'tiny' theme and runs with it all the way to the end.The minute by minute collecting of tinykins and nectar is crunchy and satisfying. The tasks you are sent out to do are cute, and with just enough variance to stay enjoyable, though it is still a collectathon, so there is certainly a degree of repetition. The artstyle's 2D cartoons in a 3d world works really well (even though once i thought about how Milodane is technically always running backwards, I couldn't unsee it!) and the character designs are great, using qualities of the bugs to build this house world is really inventive! Each 'level' has a distinct vibe to it, and I'd enjoy discovering what the next theme would be each time.In all, this is a good game that is easy to snuggle into an enjoyable couple hours at a time. In the same way it consistently stays a pleasant experience, I wouldn't say it ever really hits incredible highs. But I don't begrudge that of it, I'd say if you're looking for a good collectathon to relax and smile with, this is a great choice!

_childDocuments_.review: It's the spiritual successor to pikman and its great.EDIT: I've finally finished the game. Very charming and enjoyable experience. Never very difficult just a fun collectathon with lots of cute little references in the character names and stories that they tell. My only two gripes with the game, it can be very frustrating finding those last 3 pollen you left somewhere, and the achievements are definitely broken. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best platformers I've played in a long time -- replicating the gamecube platformer era perfectly.As a fan of Katamari Damacy, Pikmin, and any platformer from around those times...this game feels like a love letter to all of it.Each stage is very unique and feels different, while also utilizing the setting of it in a house perfectly. _childDocuments_.review: Supercute and easy platformer that is just so comforting and fun to play. Various tinykins make the moving around the house fluid and fun as well as help with puzzle solving. _childDocuments_.review: While on the surface this game might seem like a Pikmin clone - what this game does, it does very well.  This game is all meat no filler.  It combines light puzzle solving with fun platforming and wraps it in a really polished presentation.  Put simply - I enjoyed everything minute I spent in this game's world.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A joy from start to finish! In the middle of playing Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, I needed something mindless, easy, and relaxing, and this game did all that and more! It's a simple platformer, with no puzzles or skill trees, or alternate routes to take. Just progress through the five areas talking to characters and finding the collectibles. Simple but tight mechanics and a well-implemented concept with the tinykins left me wanting more, but it was definitely short and sweet! Glad I picked this up
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Quality: It feels fun, snappy and quick to play. Even though the floating bubble you use can sometimes be somewhat slow, its still really fun to generally move around. Style: The animations are great! The levels are well decorated, each with their own distinct theme. It makes great use of the "smol" theme throughout the game, such as using a sink leaking to make a waterfall and clips clipped together to make walls. It has a ton of small details like these that really bring its worlds to life.Story: The story feels a bit thrown in, but its core is pretty thought provoking, despite how little it is used throughout the game.The closest thing I could compare this to is a mix of Pikmin and either Astros Playroom or Mario Odyssey. The biggest gripe i have is that there is no pollen (the in game collectable) detector, making 100%ing a bit of a pain, with you having 2 left in a level, making you have to go through every nook and cranny to find it. All n all, I really recommend! It has a charm and life to it that is rare and hard to find, and my entire experience was really positive! Well worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Really great casual experience; perfect if you were ever a fan of Banjo-Kazooie (Honestly got BK vibes throughout my playtime).  Not sure I agree with the idea people have thinking this is anything like Pikmin, but I really think the game on its own has a lot of brilliant ideas.  If the developer ever made a sequel, I would love to see more levels outside of the house setting, even though I didn't think the world overstayed its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet. Fun levels to explore full of pop culture references. The movement is fluid and the abilities are fun to use.The game can become a bit repetitive though, even though you play though several levels, the puzzles don't really change and you end up doing kinda the same all the time.But if you want a cute platformer I would pick this up on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Bajillion times better than I expected. If you are not an APM player, don't worry, controlling the "tinykin" is ZERO hassle, because you don't. They are basically your ammo, it's just cute ammo that walks & follows you around. Using them is a simple matter of aim and shoot. The game always selects the appropriate type automatically. It's a pretty platform exploration game, you are looking all around the big pretty world to find tinykin, and shooting them at stuff to solve puzzles. I wasn't too sure about it from the screenshots & trailers, had this feeling it would be hassle to control, boy oh boy, couldn't be more wrong. A real joy to play. Buy the game, GLHF.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is a great game to sit back and relax with. Whilst the game doesn't feel too long, the biggest challenge is finding all pollen and/or Tinykin (which can be annoying considering there is no guide on where they are) and this may take up most of your time.The soundtrack is fun and the level design is a big plus. Perhaps the perfect game for a child to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game literally feels like it was made by Nintendo, enough said, buy this game ! But I will slightly elaborate further, from marketing and heresay this game is supposed to be a Pikmin style game, whilst true, that isn't the entire narrative of the gameplay feel. Tinykin feels more like a mishmash of Pikmin, with a paper Mario/Bug Fables aesthetic built around a collectathon puzzle-platformer in pretty decently large interconnected hub levels with numerous different things to collect and interact with. It took me about 2 hours to get everything in the first main level and there is supposed to be another 5 after that. In terms of the Pikmin side of this game, you collect different types of Tinykin in each level, with a new type getting introduced in each subsequent level. These Tinykin have abilities that will help you solve environmental puzzles, from the standard pink Tinykin which you use to interact with the environment, to transportation of items, then there are the red Tinykin which you hurl at objects in a kamikazi attack to blow up obstacles to create new paths, or the green ones where they build a step ladder, growing higher and higher the more you obtain to gain new heights! All of these numerous mechanics culminate to create something visually and mechanically delightful, playing this game at 60+ fps just feels incredibly smooth, which goes to why this game feels so much like a Nintendo game, coupled with the fact that I haven't ecperienced any bugs at all, the overall polish for this game shows the developers truly put in the care for this sleeper hit of a title they've created. This game is said to be around 10 hours to 100% and for this price i really do encourage anyone reading this review to purchase and dive into this game, you won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I've yet to finish the game, it seems short but sweet.Usually I don't like this kind of modern 2D cartoon style; bean mouths, flat, no detail. But it carries a nice charm here. The game itself feels very tight and responsive to play. Big, open level design that naturally encourages you to find collectibles and objectives, rather than marking it all down for you. Great sound design and dynamic music make the whole world burst with life. Lots of (optional) amusing dialogue. The main reason I wanted to write this review, before even finishing the game, is to point out a design choice that the developers could've done without. Whenever you unlock a rope or silk-rail to let you quickly navigate to and from various spots throughout the levels, the camera pulls back and strips control away from you. This might be fine if there were only a small number of ropes/rails. With so many of them, however, it's an unnecessary momentum-killer.  Even dumb players don't need the game to explicitly show them that a rope or rail was just created.

_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Pikmin who? No but seriously Tinykin wears its inspiration on its sleeves half, Pikmin half Banjo Kazooie. To explain how "Tinykin" work they are like little worker bees you can command at objectives to solve puzzles, For example making bridges, lifting heavy objects, and destroying scaffolding. and you collect said Tinykin in egg pods that are non-renewable which works in making Tinykin a resource for locking off areas of the map and progression but as a result lacks at combat in the game. but the game makes up for in map design. I do feel that the ways the Tinykin are used gets a little too samey later on if they used more puzzles requiring multiple types being used in tandem, or more puzzles it would fix the problem. but i'd say its made up for in the level design and boy oh boy it's amazing and why I compared it to Banjo Kazooie before, the maps for the most part have no restrictions and multiply ways of being traversed it just feels like a blast to navigate, with you clearing a small chunk of a area at a time and each "mini area" feeling stitched together in the best way possible. but with the unsolvable problem of missing one collectable and not being able to find it for 20 minutes, Although I can't hold that against the game only myself. Still, blasting through a map and knocking out all of the objectives just feels satisfying and you don't have to backtrack to previous areas, if that's a good or bad thing is up to personally preference. That's why i said it's similar, a mix of Pikmin and Banjo Kazooie for resource management and free moving level design. sadly no time management its only to save you time but no real reason not that it needed it to be fair. And now for the menial stuff, First the music is nice and sets the tone nice and I do like the "dynamic music" (It changes depending on what part of the area you're in on a subtle level). The graphics all look nice and fit in despite being 3D with flat (Physical) characters they fit in. Akin to Paper Mario in that sense. I do also like the world building they establish with a religion worshiping Salvior Ardwin (I can't for the life of me tell if it's some joke I'm not getting) and other aspects of the world like how the dung beetles are shunned from the people. granted they're played for Jokes, and the game is humorous with witty writing and all. and the world feels "alive" and you're just a nobody stranded here experiencing it but it never gets brought up after the first 5 minutes oh well. I won't spoil the ending but it does fall victim to the age old "end of game exposition dump" would had been a bit better if there was a bit of build up, but its not to big of a deal you're playing the game for the game play not Shakespeare.  The game is a short but a quality title worth the price of admission and not too hard to 100 percent but be careful if you did everything and some achievements don't show up just enter the areas again and check the menus. I think this game is quite the hidden gem and I think there is a lot of potential for a sequel maybe not in the same setting but either way this team proved they know how to make a great game. for every minor downside it has a major upside. if you like "Collectathons" this will be right up your alley. My final rating is 8.6-8.8. Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it, definitely up there with "A Hat in Time" for best Steam Platformers/Collectathons. The only gripe I have about this game is when using the soapboard it doesn't always snap to edges/ledges as easily as I'd like it to, especially noticeable when doing the races. Took me many tries to platinum every race just because of that. Speaking of races, this game would be a fantastic speed running game, since I've noticed a few small skips every now and then. I would love to see more levels in the future and more types of tech (such as a triple jump, but that may require reworking some levels).Achievements: I got 100% in about 8-10 hours, it's largely dependent on if you find all the pollen (coins) the first time.
