I tend to give this genre a chance every decade or so...play a level or two and then quit fairly bored with my experience.  Something about this game overcame my general disinterest in the genre.  Kudos to the devs for finding that magic with this game that I couldn't find with others I've tried and yet people praised to moon.  8/10  Highly Recommended. Nitpicks:  - I didn't 100% this game.  Maybe you unlock something like this if you do more than I did...but I feel like trying to 100% a level would become extremely frustrating to find those last few things you miss.  I probably 95% completed each level and left it at that.  A system in place to make that last bit easier would be nice. - The tinykin that carry stuff across the room do so too slowly.  This became tedious at the later stages of the game since some of those paths are long.  There's no reason to keep the player waiting. - The story didn't grab me in the slightest.The bottom line is this game is just a joy to play and that's what matters.   Great work.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Played through with my 6 year old and it was a blast. The house layout and ability to keep climbing higher to get a better view was very satisfying. Deserves the overwhelming positive review score. If I had to fault one thing, I wasn't a huge fan of the story, by the end we skipped talking to characters that weren't quest related.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! Smooth mechanics, I enjoyed the slippery soapboard mechanics. This game is a great homage to pikmin!I'd highly reccommend Tinykin as a fun easy intro into 3d puzzle platformers. I get frustrated easily at puzzle games, but the gameplay here is simple and easy to understand, so you can spend your time hopping around matchboxes. The dollhouse aesthetics are my favorite part, it's very cute and relaxing. 10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Very underrated Game, lots of fun!The perfect collectathon to kick back and relax tooonly complain i have is that the activation on the achievements was a bit buggy for meI've gotten them all, but some didn't activate, even though i had done everything necessaryIt was really annoying to not get them after the work i put in, but lucky they showed up after i re-entered the final level
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Really well-crafted game. The artwork and animations are nice, the music is nice and ties into the sound effects. The game plays like a collectathon, but everything is tied to progression or little side quests so it never feels like a chore. Pretty much every character has something to say, which is fun. I went into it hoping it would be more like Pikmin, but it's really a 3D platformer with little friends as puzzle keys.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, it's like taking the Supraland world but without the puzzles and the Overlord minions mechanic without the violence.It has a nice flow that always keep you going forward, it's not very long but also it doesn't overstay it's welcome.It has a very weird ending that doesn't seem to be very on the same page with the tone of the game in general.The only bad thing with this game is the jump feature, the player can't jump high and also the player go down too fast so you need to have lightning quick reflexes to activate the glide feature or you will end below the level you want to reach. More often than not this is a source of frustration that could do with a bit of fine tuning to allow you a bit more air time before dropping you like a bag of potatoes.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game with a slightly new take on Pikmin. Very 3d platform focused but still casual. There are no puzzles in this game which is fine as it makes it more casual, but don't expect Pikmin like challenges.. there is only platforming. Only downside is the game is pretty short, about 4 hours. Going back and attempting to find every collectible takes another 4 hours. They could have done a lot more with the mechanics but decided on a short game. 8 out of 10
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A great little (pun intended) platformer with a neat look, intuitive game mechanics, and a fun time all around.Practically no time is spent on trying to figure out the mechanics because they feel natural and are put to good use. You whizz around the world exploring all the nooks and crannies while naturally figuring out what to do along the way. It's a superb game to simply get lost in the exploration while still feeling like you're making progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is if Pikmin, Banjo Kazooie and Paper Mario had a baby. If you like 3D collectathon platformers, then this is a must buy. Exploring, music, characters, level design, art style and all the sounds in the game work great together. You only really get two abilities besides the tinykin, but they are really fun to use, so it didn't hinder the experience at all. The problems some might have is that the game length is short (only took me 10 hours to 100%) and there are no bosses. Neither of these were problems for me even though a boss or 2 could have been cool. Overall, I would give the game an 8.5/10. I hope they make another Tinykin since this one already set a great base and there is a lot more they can do with it
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and a very fun theme. An extremely casual game, great for a first-time platformers. The only part I found dexterously demanding was the optional 'challenge' update's soapboard grinding races. I kinda hoped there would be more dangerous obstacles or enemies like in pikmin, but the game is designed around a very limited set of tinykin per stage. Since everything you need to 100% a stage is there upon arrival, there is very little reason to not do so leaving no reason to come back. It has all the mechanics to be an amazing game. but the overall result feels short sighted.I want to be able to make more tinykin and bring them between areas. I want more rooms and more nooks and crannies to explore, and reasons to backtrack. Heck, even just giving the current areas an 'act 2' after you get all the artifacts would be amazing as having any reason to go back to anywhere even once would be nice. The one 'out of bounds' experience was too short and was necessary for 100% completion so it didn't really feel special or secret.If you like running around collecting stuff, feeling really tiny, or reading lots and lots of dialogue with little references all over the place, then you'll like this game. Some people complain the game needs a pollen detector, but the lack of one is really the only thing giving you any reason to actually look around the maps. So I didn't miss it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Solid, cute, fun platforming adventure.The tinykin will instantly make you think of pikmin, but they act more like collectibles than an army; the combat and tactical side is replaced with platforming and whimsy; which I am perfectly fine with.The art, world, and music is pretty great, the story is kinda weird but it makes sense in the end. An all around enjoyable experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I feel so bad for sleeping on this game for so long.This game is genuinely one of the best collectathons I've ever played, and with me getting into the Pikmin games this past year, and really enjoying them. I figured it would be right up my alley.As for the negatives I have a small few, I didn't find the music that memorable, and the npc dialog was kinda boring. But for the positives each Tinykin is very useful and none feel underutilized (although I think the red ones are a little too overutilized) the green ones were my favorite as they were super fun to use and add a ton to the vertical platforming gameplay.The game controls really well despite controlling a 2D character in a 3D world. The soap surfing feels really fun especially when you learn how to utilize it to gain a ton of speed. And the gliding feels real goodThe sound design is also great, from collecting the popcorn making satisfying popping sounds making you want to go after all of them (which has a valuable reward) to just interacting with the Tinykin each having their own sets of satisfying sounds depending on how you use them.The museum collectibles could be seen as filler. But since the side objectives to get them were so fun I didn't find any issue with it.Overall this game is great and worth its full price, despite being quite short. But I find that this is one of those games where you can get more out of it with replays and that it ended right when it needed to. Right when they've shown you everything the story, platforming, and mechanics has to offer.Great game. Will be playing again.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I am obsessed with this world that tinyBuild has created. I had played this game on GamePass but re-purchased it on Steam because I wanted to spend more time with these characters.This game absolutely nails the casual and master approach. The base platforming will be doable for gamers of any skill level, however the higher level movement tech and speed makes it a joy to play. Riding on the soap board while flinging pikmin to grab items is a challenge for any skilled FPS player.This is a game I will continue to revisit when I need a fun and delightful break for years to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is an exceptional collect-a-thon style platformer. Exploring the various zones while solving puzzles and traversal challenges is all incredibly fun.The 2D characters and 3D world combo is a jarring at first, but you get used to it. And when you collect all the tinykin in a zone, it's obvious why they did it this way.My only complaint is the bizarre meta-story involving space travel. It just made the first 30 minutes way more confusing than they needed to be - this is actually a very straightforward and accessible game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: 2024 is about me achievement hunting to dwindle down my huge backlog and figured I would do this one since it’s short. So I completed it today and loved every second of it! I’m all about open world RPGs but now all I want to do is play more games like this. Possibly one of my favorite games ever. I want another one!!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loving this game. The movement is so smooth and intuitive, the areas give you lots to explore and do without any piece of them feeling like wasteful filler, and in my entire time playing I haven't noticed a single bug (except for the insects :) ).It ain't Pikmin, with the tinykin acting more like a useful resource than an army of little dudes.The game lets the tinykin sit alongside the movement mechanics rather than being the primary tool in your arsenal. I love riding the soapboard.10/10 epic game
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★☆Positive+ Tight, responsive controls+ Adorable and unique art style+ Will run on a potatoNeutral~ Relatively short (10-ish hours)~ No real side activities to speak of, except for a small DLC that added timed races to the game for costume unlocks~ Story and dialogue was not that interesting to me (but it's a platformer so who cares really?)Negative- No in-game method for finding the last few pesky collectibles (I'd estimate about 4 of my 10 hours with the game were spend meticulously combing over areas I'd already been to looking for the last few pickups...)- Full price of $25 USD is somewhat steep for the amount of content, although the came is crafted extremely well
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, wonderful traversal mechanics but be warned, finding all the Tinykin and Pollen is an exercise in frustration and time wasting. I nearly gave this one a thumbs down as a consequence because what should be a fun "post game" jaunt around completing the stuff you missed before is an awful experience.Hopefully we get an upgrade that lets players detect where the missing things are, until then I'd actually recommend you wait on this one unless you do not care at all about collecting everything in a fashion with doesn't either require watching hours of YT videos or spending some of your limited on this planet travelling around with little progress to show for it.6/10 at the moment, 9/10 if the developer does something about this terrible "post game".
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game because a lot of people said it's like Pikmin.  It's really not like Pikmin, beyond the fact that a lot of little dudes follow you around and can sometimes carry stuff.  The game is a straight up collectathon, more in line with something like Banjo-Kazooie.  I still enjoyed my time with it, but don't go into it expecting it to be a Pikmin-type game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Got this in a gamepack, so no idea what it was. Figured I would give it a try and it is ADORABLE.It's laid back and low stress (except for the extra racing). It's a super cute puzzle games, the art is adorable and the amount of detail in the gameplay and NPCs is fantastic.10/10 would recommend and will be playing again!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I really really enjoyed this, it felt like it takes two crossed with spyro. 100% it was a good amount of challenge without feeling like a grind and overall the game was a good length of play. Although I did encounter an issue where 5 of the trophies didn't award and i had to go into each of the rooms again to trigger them.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun, accessible, engaging, and dynamic with great art, funnier writing than you would think, and honestly some of the most impressive audio I've seen in a game. The attention to detail & the quality of the music is incredible for such an indie title. binaural audio everywhere; different materials create different sound effects when you walk or jump off of them; the environments & characters you are near will affect which musical tracks play as they blend into the music to give you a sense of being the world. Never noticed quite how much audio can have a part in breathing life into a fictional world, but this game really showcases that. It's well worth a play.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Only took 15 hours to get 100%, not worth the full price but good for $10 or less. Overall it was a great game but has a few problems. Finding the last pollen and other collectibles in each area was difficult and wasted a lot of time even while using guides as there is no tool to assist with locating them. A few achievements are bugged and required me to visit every area in the same play session. It appears support has ended as the last update was from just over a year ago, and also disappointing that there were only three or four minor updates since the game was released.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Really solid game! The visuals are really pleasing, and the music is great, so I was sold. The puzzles and sidequests are pretty easy to solve too! The only qualm I have is that there's no gadget or method to make collecting all the pollen easier. I had to use an online guide to find some super hidden spots.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Can't believe it took me THIS LONG to play Tinykin! Such a fun charming cute little indie platformer made with so much passion and love! It's got these sort of Pikmin esque mechanics, but then mixed with a platformer that to me feels a little similar control/game feel wise to the Psychonauts games, and then blended with this sort of Saturday morning Cartoon Network visual and animation style! I love it! I also noticed each level has it's own music where they do the Mario Odyssey thing of having the actions of your little Tinykin sync up to the beat of the song when they carry things. The attention to detail is truly on point. Oh and I didn't even speak on the level design... It's GOOD! Like REALLY GOOD!! Extremely consistent, the spaces feel so well thought out and fun to platform through! They just did such a good job of tying each level together tone wise where it all fits the vibe of each playspace and I love how as you unlock new areas of a big room level, it shoots ropes back to other areas to make backtracking a little easier. They really do a good job of just making a simple, yet elegant collectathon sort of thing where you genuinely wanna collect all the little gold things and collect as many tinykin as possible because it's just so enjoyable and well put together. Hats off to the level designers here! Great game. I definitely will finish this, having a blast so far! Quality games like this deserve your attention! They deserve to get more recognition, so I am leaving this positive steam review to help Tinykin get more attention :) (Also this game is really fun on the Steam Deck!)
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games of all time! The art style is so cute, the dialogue is funny, & the worlds were really fun to explore. Something about being tiny & exploring an environment made of household items felt really peaceful, like you're in Toy Story or in a world you created as a child. As far as 3D platformers go, it's a great one. I really hope for a sequel of some sort, because I wish the game was longer & no other game has felt as similar an experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing negative to say except that it's on the short side, 8.7 hours to complete and 100% the achievements. Others already said it but it feels like a chill Pikmin inside a house without any sort of combat or violence which is very different from everything else I play. I really loved the clever use of household items to build environment and furniture, every part where easily identifiable and it reminded me of 1990s-2000s green toy soldiers games. I can't recall how long it's been since a game had me smiling from start to finish and i'm sad that it's already over.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute game with a cool art style, but its pretty mindless. You collect all these thing kind of like pikmin and you have them do these pre-arranged tasks at specific interactive points. It's very linear as there is really no working things out or coming up with things yourself. You just collect enough of them to fulfill the amount needed and you do that a bunch of times to beat each stage. The stages are cool and varied. The story is nonexistant. It doesn't overstay its welcome. Its just a pretty inoffensive chill game, sometimes things can be hard to find as you may have missed one thing in 1 corner but other than that its fine. Its just nothing special and can be boring. 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Rewriting my review now that I've finished the game 100%. Including all Steam achievements and platinum in all challenges. Bottom line: buy this game, now. Definitely the highlight of my Winter Sale purchases, I nearly couldn't put this one down.It's very fun, not hard to figure out, and it's cute. The levels offer a lot of exploration and you can happily stop there, or continue searching until you find everything. If you like to explore, you'll like this game. The gameplay itself is like a cross between Grounded and Pikmin, and they've done a phenomenal job on this combination.Now the cons: first and foremost, it's SHORT. I'm by no means a pro gamer and I was done to 100% in less than 30 hours. If you only care about enough to get through the main storyline, I don't even know if it'd take you 5 hours total. I really felt that there could have been at least 3 extra levels and an actual ending. The end level is pretty underwhelming, especially after you put so much effort into the ones before it.Second, the challenges (the races) are FRUSTRATING. I get it, they're meant to be hard (if you aim for platinum every time), but there are some serious flaws with the game itself that make it annoying. They're pretty much designed such that you have to snap to grind rails and such, but the collision detection is AWFUL. Half the time you expect to snap to something, you just don't. Half the time you are snapped to something, you mysteriously come unsnapped for no real reason. I understand not everything is snappable, but the things that are, should snap as you'd expect them to, and stay so. This is compounded by the fact that you HAVE to snap in order to make platinum! It's an incredibly frustrating afterthought to an otherwise immensely fun game. Last, you cannot rebind your keys to use E. I've been playing EASD instead of WASD for 30 years so I'm used to games not getting this right. But usually they'll let you remap or they won't. This game does, but it won't let you use the E key for some mysterious reason. I hope the devs see this and make a fix so that other remappers aren't stuck with this problem. There's really no reason in this day and age that a game shouldn't be 100% remappable.Other than that, this game was incredible and I'm so happy I was able to play it. I hope they either add to it or come out with a sequel because I will be on top of it in a heartbeat.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Just an absolute pleasure to adventure through. I apparently blitzed through the whole story. I completed the game in 20min-30min chunks killing time before work on my steam deck! Plenty to see if you're into collecting but I mainly finished the main objectives before going into the next level. The levels are detailed and puzzle solving is fun, kind of easy for me but the music and exploring is what kept me attracted to this nifty title.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This must be the best Pikmin-type game to ever grace the circuit boards of personal computers. If you like exploring and collecting, then this is the game for you. One of those rare games where you don't want to stop playing as you spot something in the distance that needs investigating. Then suddenly it's 2am.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is a wonderful little game. It's got lovely art direction and extremely well done platforming controls. Took me about 12 hours to beat while taking my time collection most everything.It's a cozy game by design, and I never actually felt challenged, so keep that in mind with your expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Buttery smooth gameplay, wonderful graphics/art direction, and an amazing soundtrack. The gameworld is fun to explore because of all the fun little details (especially if you like seeing miniature versions of real-world stuff), and charming characters. Tinykin is extremely well-polished, especially for an indie game. About the only negative I can say is the game is fairly void of challenge, though admittedly that can also make it a nice game to play after a long day at work/school.Also worth pointing out, this game's similarity to Pikmin is mostly aesthetic. Tinykin is strictly a platformer, rather than a strategy/puzzle game like Pikmin.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable aesthetic, collectathon that takes me back to Banjo Kazooie, and occasionally tricky platforming that isn't so unforgiving. The Pikmin-esque Tinykin mechanics are pretty fun as well, and not as tiresome as I found Pikmin to be. There seems to be some kind of lore going on that I'm interested in finding more about
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Top-tier 3D platformer. Very kid friendly and fairly easy, so not everyone will enjoy this, but I had a lot of fun casually exploring and collecting. The sound desing really shined here, I loved the variability in the music and all of the various sound effects, the level of polish here is really awesome. If you like 3d platformers and don't mind if they're a bit easier and smaller, definitely pick this up and give it a try. There's a lot to appreciate.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, but a bit different than what I expected,This is a 3d platformer with lots of verticality (which I love) with a tiny bit of pikmin influence. For some reason, I though this was a pikmin clone. But honestly, I think it would be better if it focused even more only in the 3d platforming.I say that because all of the stages have a similar loop. You have to go around the stage doing small and big tasks to complete the stage. But in order to do those tasks, you need lots of tinykins. That means that at the beginning of each stage, you won't have much to do besides exploring in search for eggs. There's a point then that you can stop exploring and simply focusing on the objectives, because the number of tinykins is already almost enough, and the rest will come while exploring for the objectives. I wish there was a better balance to that, because the beginning of each stage felt a bit boring.The second thing I disliked, also in relation to the pikmin aspect, is that for the big objects that you command you tinykins to carry, you do not actually command where they need to go. They already know the path. That put me in a situation some times where I found the goal of a task before even knowing what the task was, and my tinykin would bring the object to the right place. I think a better solution for that would be to let me command the tinykin carrying heavy objects.Other than those two points, the game is phenomenal.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun and chill experience.The gameplay and contols are crisp and on point. You will be rushing through the levels in no time. The collectibles are motivating goals, also you see where you already have been. I can really recommend this game as "small game which you play to make a break from the other big game"
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A lighthearted puzzle platformer version of pikmin, and this time your lil friends don't get hurt!(except the ones that want to ?) The puzzles are fun, the story and writing had me smiling, and most importantly the movement is great. Love the artstyle, and I wasn't even watching things on my other monitor while I played like I expected. I just listened to the nice soundtrack and had fun. In fact, I liked the game enough to stay up...2.5 hours past bed to finish and 100% it.Sidenote btw, if the surprisingly challenging races are keeping you down, they're optional. They're for fun outfits and the thrill of mastery, won't stand in the way of progress or even achievement hunting. Still, I wound up grinding out gold medals just for the fun! It was good, plain and simple, no qualifiers needed. I adored it start to finish, highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Played the whole thing on the Steam Deck, and it was amazing.It's a fun and delightful game that feels like it could've released on the GameCube, and gives me the same nostalgia of being a kid playing a game. Highly polished, and the graphics are just so good. The core gameplay of exploring and collecting things while solving simple puzzles as I went felt very rewarding, and I found myself looking forward to each area as I moved on to the next.It happens for me rarely nowadays, but being able to lose myself in a game and forget that it is, in fact, a video game, means A LOT to me. Nothing while I was playing took me out of the experience. No jumping to the internet to look up unexplained mechanics or puzzles, no grinding out resources or scores, etc. It's been YEARS since I've felt like this while playing a game. Makes me feel young, ahaha.If you wanna re-experience that joy of losing yourself in a simple, but fun and engaging game, then I highly recommend it. It's not a game that'll keep your attention with action or grinding out levels, but you can just sit back and chill out while you explore these fun environments and have a good chuckle at all the references throughout the game.Here's to hoping for more paid DLC, or a sequel! I'll buy anything that gets released for this title.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know what to make out of the game at first. "Will this be a pikmin style of game? Will this be a 3D platformer?"... but once the slow start in the tutorial level was over, the game got its hooks in me immediately!In spite of a fairly nonsensical plot and often clunky controls (GRINDING IN PARTICULAR), Tinykin is the most fun I've had with a platformer in years!The world building and level design were a lot of fun! The collectibles hidden in really smart areas that often had me skateboarding back and forth for hours just wondering where the heck I missed something. Thanks to the many different ways to travel around and the mobility provided by some later game Tinykin, exploring was always a grand adventure. Overall, a very inventive, fun to explore platformer that I can't recommend enough.(Don't get too seriously into racing though. I've screamed screams of despair and I ain't trying for platinum in any race with the state of that rail detection.)
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: What an unexpected delight! It's not a difficult game, there's no enemies and it's pure platforming, but it's incredibly fun, and amusing enough often enough to keep a big fat smile on your big fat face for the duration. The controls is slick and instinctive, the eponymous Tinykin are great fun, and the sheer amount of rewards you get for simply looking in every nook and cranny of each level is wonderful. My only gripe is that the camera has moments where it can't cope, suddenly swinging around when you're mid-jump, but this is certainly only a minor gripe. I think for £21 it's decent value, though I got it in a recent sale and if you can do that clearly it's going to be better value. Recommended for all fans of old-school platforming.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: For a platformer, Tinykin was surprisingly pleasant. You collect little creatures that help you get around, complete several quests, can find other collectibles and explore several rooms in a house as a  tiny person on a soap board.I am honestly not huge on platformers but have played a few 3d ones that were surprisingly fun (here comes niko, etc). Tinykin looked promissing because of the cute graphics and the "overlord" mechanic :D Tinkin is a lot like Pikmin in the way you can collect and use little creatures.Some of the achievements are a bit buggy, some are very very annoying and because of the more time consuming ones (find the last 3 of 1200 collectibles you need in this level), the game slightly overstayed its welcome. Other than that i truly had a blast playing tinykin!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: + Scale / Environment+ Exploration~ No map- Puzzle Difficulty (too easy)I really enjoyed this game.  However, there is another game very similar that is better, called Supraland.  You don't have the Tinykin to help you, but you upgrade your tools, and they pretty much do the same things to assist your movement/etc.  The difference in the games is, the puzzles are real puzzles, where you actually have to think.  Both games have great exploration.   Tinykin is really missing, and maybe I just didn't find it, but the end game should give you a Tinykin that helps you find the missing collectibles you missed during the initial play through.  Armed with that, I would  have absolutely 100%'d the game.  As it is now without this tool, it's not all the much fun looking for those isolated items.  Tinkykin also has no map.  For the most part it wasn't necessary, but there were times it would have been nice to have some way to mark where something is, so I wouldn't have to hunt all over to re-find an item I had seen and forgotten its location.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly satisfying 3D platformer collectathon. Interesting characters and unique story. But who cares about all of that...Really, I compare all of these modern 3D platformers (A hat in time, yooka-laylee, etc.) to Super Mario 64 and the golden era of Rare.Super Mario 64 and Banjo-Kazooie are the grandfather and godfather of 3D platforming. And with a bar set that high, I think this game still pleases. For reference, I loved Hat in Time and found yooka-laylee derivative.With that context set, I highly recommend this game. Also, play with a controller and on a TV preferably. At least, that's my suggestion.Update: After taking roughly 12 hours to 100% the game (could be faster with rushing), I have to say this one of my favorite 3D games ever. The addition of the racing challenges and intriguing story really round this game out. I can't recommend this game enough to fans of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing Pikmin in 2001 on the GameCube, back when Nintendo were still doing anything original. You play as a tiny astronaut, and you convince little coloured aliens to follow you around and lift / fight normal-sized (huge by your scale) objects and enemies in the Gulliver's Travels-style world around you. Well, this is exactly that - except that it's on PC and not made by Nintendo (and there's no combat). The whole thing is really polished. It's not hard at all, but it's so well made and engaging exploring the huge rooms of the house. It's split into 5 main levels, one in each room of the house, and each room has a group of insects that you need to help.- Just generally really well made, with lots of attention to detail and no bugs. What a rarity these days!- Runs well on the Steam Deck- Each room has a main objective, and a bunch of "side-quests" to help individuals with tasks like carrying things or finding stuff- Good controls- There's a soap board you can skate around on to move quickly- There's a method to see any missing objectives in each room- Big beautiful maps, really excellent level design- As you progress through each map, you unlock fast travel in the form of little spiders shooting webs from one side of the map to the other that you can surf along- The only minor let down was the end of the game. Honestly, I just didn't get it. There's a 5 minute set of dialogue at the end of the game that supposedly explains the whole thing, but it didn't make any sense. Thankfully it has absolutely no impact on gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: i liked it so much that i bought the supporter edition on steam even though i beat already it on xbox game passgreat art direction, atmosphere, sound design, ost, and just an overall fun little 3d puzzle platformer that kept me smiling all the way throughit might not be everyone's cup of tea, but please do check it out
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This is a delightful and relaxing platformer/collect-a-thon that took me about 8 hours to fully complete (minus the new racing minigame and the associated outfits). Using various Tinykin to move objects, build towers/ramps, and explode through barriers, players explore an early 90's house filled with puzzles and secrets. While the levels have to be completed in a set order, each is very open-ended, and this freedom makes the gameplay feel both engaging and relaxing. I was even incentivized to find all of the pollen (the main collectible) and Tinykin in each level.If I had to make some minor complaints, I would say that the glider bubble sometimes turns off if the game things that you touched the "ground" (elevation doesn't matter), which led to some annoyances with jumping/gliding. I also found that the later puzzles requiring the ramps to be tedious, since these occasionally required me to stop what I was doing and babysit my tinykin. And while I can't really count this as a negative, the story is fairly thin. The dialogue is charming enough--there's just a lot of it that I ended up skipping.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I went into this fully expecting janky controls, a subpar story, and an unfinished, unpolished product with a mostly empty world. I was wrong. Really wrong.Things I think inspired this game: Grounded, Pikmin, Banjo-Kazooie, and Chibi-Robo.The controls feel great. Everything is snappy and responsive. It's not overly complicated so it's easy to remember which button does what. The controls anticipate your actions so no need to switch your tinykin around. They obviously spent a lot of time fine-tuning every aspect of the controls. They don't include some of the annoying aspects about Pikmin, like your tinykin can't die and you can't leave them behind. They automatically follow you everywhere, which is nice and allows you to focus on your tasks.The music has been fantastic and I found myself head-bopping to it as I went through the levels because it just hits right. It's all dynamic, so as you move to different areas of each world, it changes and as you make progress, it'll also change.It's a collectathon. To 100% it's pretty challenging but to progress, it seems fair.I haven't finished the game so I can't comment on the story but so far, it's alright. Definitely not the focus of the game, however, all of the worlds are full of characters with quite a bit of charm. And almost every nook and cranny is filled with something. I haven't found too many "missed opportunities" in terms of level design. Speaking of level design, they've really used all of the space. There are quick-travel zip-line type things all throughout the levels that take you from one edge of the world to the other both up and down making traversal really nice and easy as you progress through the worlds. You won't find yourself spending a bunch of time wandering back and forth to do things.It's a short game. I'm a little more than half-way done and I've spent about 4 hours playing, so I'm guessing 6-8 for completion and about 8-10 for 100%. I think that's a good length for it considering what it has to offer.TL;DR If you like platformers and pikmin, play it. It's worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Great platformer. Really enjoyed the level design and art, and the controls are tight. A few achievements are a bit buggy (need to revisit every room to complete despite being "done"), and the game is unfriendly toward finding missing collectibles (no tracker or counter to help find them), so be careful with that if you plan to 100% everything.Looking forward to more if they make any more!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Like a cross between Banjo Kazooie and Pikmin. It's just a delight to play, and bursting with charm. Tinykin basically has it all. The game play, good. The movement, fantastic. Level design, amazing. Sound design, environmental design, character design, story. Everything is great, and it creates such a fun experience. Highly recommended if you like 3D Platformers. It is only about 6 hours long, though it took me almost 10 hours to get all the achievements, which, admittedly can be a little finicky. Honestly, the game felt longer than 6 hours (in a good way). The levels are very dense and make great use of the space.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely charming and cute game. Not challenging in the slightest, the only real challenges youll face here is the typical collectathon-ness, like missing 5 collectibles and spending an hour scouring a level, or forgetting to turn in a mission, etc. The race missions, moreso the Platinum Medals, are probably the most challenging part of the game. The soundtrack is good, the art is great and the cutscenes are amazingly animated, the dialogue is charming and funny, and theres a plethora of odd references scattered across the game. Overall extremely cute and well-made, a solid 8-10.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I think I had high expectations and after playing I was a little disappointed with the game. It's an easy game and doesn't challenge me to do anything new. And the story and lines could be funnier. And I only now I did realize that this game has no enemies, no fighting, at least until now, and I thought it had that too before playingThe game is good in terms of gameplay, graphics and the environment created, which is cute and where everything is cute.But despite being a beautiful game, it's not as an intense experience as I thought.I recommend this game for anyone who really likes platforms or simple games where you run around exploring the world levels and collect cute little creatures spread around the worldMaybe I will finish this game over time, but for now I leave a negative review
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Only cracked the surface of this short but wonderful gem. I was worried I wouldn't like it sense I am not the biggest fan of modern platformers but it's brilliant. Riding soap around like it's a skateboard, little minions at your command, cartoon graphics are great and the nostalgia of exploring a house in the 90s. I heard it's a bit short and that's the only real valid complaint I can see but on it's own merits and knowing it is short. I give it a 9/10. If it had great voice acting to match the cartoon, probably a 10 but it has that annoying cartoon mumble garble chat while you read conversations. I have never been a fan of that.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is wonderful! Its a wholesome exploration/collection focused game where you play a tiny man running around a giant house helping a society of bugs. There's no health or combat, technically you can "die" but that just resets you to the last safe platform so you can try again. The levels are all based on rooms of the house so if you can see an objective then you can find a way to get to it, there's no set strategy and you are free to clear rooms in a nonlinear order. When you reach a hard to reach area you often get a shortcut or zip line to move around even easier. The Tinykin that follow you around feel like friends and they give a little cheer when you complete an objective. The music and graphics are excellent and I had so much fun playing that I decided to run around a bit and explore even more after I had finished. I would recommend Tinykin to everyone as it was an absolute joy to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice game, with good cheery music and nice designed levels each with a separate theme. It is not overly long and the puzzles are not that difficult (usually it is more of the "how do I get there" kind). The challenge races that are unlocked once a level is done are a nice little addition to add a reason to revisit a level, but the time requirements are a bit too strict so it is hard to get the gold medals required to unlock the optional costumes.  It would have been nice to have a tool at the end of the game to find the odd little guys that you could have forgotten.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: It is always appreciated when there is a new minion game. It is unfortunate that there are so few. Tinykin is a welcome addition. It is not difficult. The environments are nice and detailed. There is a lot of exploration for the map size. The story and characters are interesting. The only things I have the problem with is the "skateboarding" mechanic. I enjoyed the ability to grind, but it feels like it could be incorporated more. Especially with the races added in, the skateboarding could feel better. Also some of the achievements are broken. The game is fun and warrants another, but with better movement!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is a 3d platformer, collectathon more than anything else.I had a the pleasure of playing Splasher earlier this year, and now Tinykin, I'm now very excited for anything Splashteam puts out in the future.The obvious comparison is Pikmin, and there are a lot of similarities, but tonally, it's very different. There is no challenge, no time limit, no dying, no messing up, nothing. You get more and more Tinykin, and they'll be your best bud forever. Each level adds a new mechanic, movement feels good, and the world is very imaginative (Honey I Shrunk the Kids-esque). I think the game is very satisfying to play, feels good to grow in size and collect varying items.I only negative I really have to say is if you're going for 100%. There's basically coins around the map, and there's achievements to get every coin on every level. I basically ended every level missing 6 - 100 coins and there's no help to find them. So you'll wander around the map until you find the last few. It's not *as* bad as other games, because the levels are fairly open so obviously missed coins can be found by scouting up high, and the hidden ones are probably near other bigger collectibles, so if you're missing an envelope or quest item, the last few coins will probably be found along with it.Overall, I would definitely recommend to anyone who enjoys old school 3D platformers, collectathons, or Pikmin enjoyers who want to avoid the stress.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10.Visually, game looks amazing. Stunning environments and very creative layouts.Gameplay is like pikmen but no combat and more puzzles.pros:1)Exploration is one of this games biggest strengths. Even though each level is "open world" every area in each level serves a purpose. A lot of games have open areas for you to explore but theres nothing in those areas to entice players to keep exploring. This game has many collectibles and easter eggs for you to find in areas making explorating fun. Developers knew what they were doing when they put down collectibles in each area. 2)cute story and characters. I really like the different personalities each species brought3)All of the tinykins felt good to use and was used thorougly in the game4)movement is soooooooooooooo good. Using the  to glide around feels soo nice. Platforming feels great and everytime i would miss a jump or something it never feels like the game is at fault, but my own skills. cons:1)100% all collectibles!  is incredibly tedious in this game. Levels are big with many elevating platforms! Its like finding a needle in a haystack especially if youre missing like 5 of them by itself and there is NO upgrade or dowsing machine to find the last collectibles you need. if you want to get the  then you dont need to collect everything which is nice i guess, but i like collecting everything. makes my brain feel nice2)I kinda wish there was a map or at least a layout of each level. Especially when im trying to 100% collectibles. Game kinda fixes this by allowing you to go in first person mode and see key items, but id like to see a layout to see what areas ive been to so that I dont end up backtracking again. Also there is no indicator when a tinykin is carrying a collectible and is stopped cus a path is blocked. At least Pikmin had a system where the character would say something like "oh no!, the pikmin cant move anymore" to let you know that you need to clear an obstacle. 3)Tinykins ai. Unlike pikmin, you cannot purposely choose a tinykin to throw; the game will automatically chose a tinykin for the appropriate sitation and autoaim you towards the objective. This becomes very annoying when two objectives with different tinykin are right next to each other as the game will sometimes freak out and move your camera around while throwing your tinykins causing you to miss your shots
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game, I haven't had this much fun on a 3D platform adventure in awhile. I hope they make a sequel because my only compliant was that I 100% it in under 10 hours but I loved every minute of it. The gameplay is smooth and each level is well designed for what you would think to interact with it in a honey I shrunk the kids style. The little guys help you but this isn't a combat game like Pikmin and you really won't care because of how enjoyable it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: To be true with you, I didn't really enjoy Tinykin to it's fullest. I'm still recommending this game though, as I realise the issue here is more on my end than of the game. It has the basics for a 3D-Plattformer nailed down with its super tight controls. The moveset, control and momentum of your character all feel right and make just going from A to B a breeze. Now why didn't I personally enjoy this game then you might ask. Simple, I felt like there was a complete lack of challenge in the game. There is no combat (okay that one doesn't matter as combat sucks in most 3D plattformers), no time trails in the main campaign and failing a jump either means you just gotta climb back up or you respawn right next to the death pit you fell into without any consequences. The Puzzles are mostly just solved by throwing your TInykin at certain objects until the nessesary number is met. But on the other hand if a cozy and chill game is what you looking for without beeing to challenging, this game is a fantastic pick.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: The game is short but I found the time with it very well spent, as it was what I hoped it would be. There is no time limit here, no fights or danger. You can die, but you will just respawn just at the point you were at with nothing lost. I loved just to run around and explore the well made levels, full of cute little characters. It is a game to relax and not one to find a challenge. I very much enjoyed that.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: as compulsive a first-playthru 100% as ive ever had. intoxicating level design the likes of which i dont rly know what to compare to...spaces are contained and heavily layered, a large emphasis on vertical traversal and pure density. the loop that scratched my brain so much was that by the end of the level, u have truly completely mastered the space...hard acquisition of knowledge, opening an overwhelming web of shortcuts, receiving a new bubble (a rly clever and well considered mechanic that brings more dimension then the expected double jump) , and ofc this all dovetails amazingly with the tinykin themselves, the acquisition of which presents steps towards new navigation of the space. and the bubbles are acquired thru the pollen...the two most common collectables are enticing primarily because of the expansion of movement they promise. the little challenge races are the most flawless bow on the experience of each level i can think of, and some of the best most joyful stuff i will take away with this. not that there isnt already a lot here obviously...very charming, p funny sometimes, sensory splendor obviously, and sometimes u just need to climb out of a Giant Toilet into mountains of toilet paper where lil bugs have made cozy homes. this is what games r all about baby!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: On the surface, tinykin seems like it's just going to be an indie pikmin, but it's honestly a lot more than that. While you control a bunch of little creatures, I think that this game has a very different feel to pikmin. There's a lot more focus on specific puzzles and traversal versus the survival feeling of pikmin. Tinykin feels really good to play and the worlds are fun to explore. I have some issues with it feeling like it eats your jump and some platform collisions, but it's a really fun game that I would recommend to all. Though I do not recommend 100% it, you are expected to find all collectables without any way to see the like last 3 you missed.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a pretty neat game. Overall it's relaxing to play, and there's no combat or boss battles. I appreciate this for cozy games like this. It's got a classic exploration + collect-a-thon gameplay loop, so if you like that, go for it.Good:- Nice to look at- World is fun to explore- Fun movement- Good performance on steam deck- Cute aesthetic- Races are a fun challenge- Lots to collectNitpicks:- Some of the controls could be streamlined. Having the option to toggle soapboard instead of holding the button down would be nice. (I accomplished this with Steam Input though). - Soapboard ledge snapping can be finicky. This mostly matters during races- I wish you could use your binoculars while on top of a stack of green tinykin- Trying to track down the last few tinykin or pollen in a level can be hard. This only matters if you're going for 100%, though.- pressing start or select forces you off of your soabpoardBad:- The missions could be more varied. It's usually just "go get that thing from up there", or "plug this thing in for me"
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is part 3D platformer collectathon and part Pikmin, and if that combination sounds up your alley, it's definitely worth picking up. If only one side of that appeals to you, maybe watch a bit of a let's play before deciding; the platforming controls are not as fluid or varied as something like A Hat in Time or a Mario game, and there's not as much strategic depth to the uses of your Tinykin as there is with Pikmin. But the combination is such a unique take, and it's full of aesthetic charm, so I still had a ton of fun with it.
