_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: After playing games where times counting down, dying causes frustration, and the pain and suffering is just to much to handle, there comes a time where I get a meditating game and this one was perfect. A calm and relaxing game just when I needed it most. If you are stressed or on the verge of breaking your PC due to a stressful game, but this game and play it. (Sable was the last game I played like that, highly recommend that one as well).
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Harkorn Back to the Good days of hearing the PS2 START UP.Hit me with childhood Wimsey.It's not left me at all.Exploration of a colourful home feels like a dream of colour and Crisp 2D on 3D art style that makes it Different on all other's in the 3d Platform Space.It's not Pikmen 3 in terms of management and Careful planning with it's creatures, but that's good because it flows as smooth a soap down a strand on nylon with it's platforming even when making harsh falls.Explore,Feel Joy,Collect.If you like 3D platformers then it's a Must.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Cool little game which squeezes an enormous sense of scale (almost vertigo inducing) out of very ordinary spaces. Nice, soft fetch-quest style puzzle solving and quick respawn if you fall too far. The only thing I would say against it is that it can take you a while to track down every last collectible and side-quest object, as the special view mostly only indicate where to go to complete a side-quest, it does little to help you find the objects you need. Other than that though, this is great fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: To get it out of the way, the game is short, like really short (as of writing this I 100% the game on the current version).  Despite that, the game is still a blast to play; mixing both a Pikmin style and classic collectathon 3D platformer game play with  a Paper Mario-like art style.  If I had to bring up any complaints, the game is very short (6-10 hours), can be rather easy/repetitive at times, and doesn't give any real way to easily locate the pollen that's scattered throughout the levels which can lead to mindless searching (could have reduced the game play time by at least 20 minutes if it had a way to more easily find the more hidden collectibles).
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: As a preface I played this on the Steam deck and steam seems to have a hard time counting time played.Game took about 7 hours and 20 min to finish but said I had played it for 74 hours. (My guess is that steam still counts time even when the steamdeck is off if you didn't quit game to desktop). And when I tried to give a review it didn't let me until I installed it on pc and it reset time played.Tinykin runs great on steam deck, Even better than a regular controller because the back buttons feel really natural for actions in this game.The game itself is really fun. It's chill and cozy. Music is fantastic, art style is charming. The controls are very responsive. The bugs are endearing. Totally recommend for anyone looking for a 3D platformer.Cons:-Game really needs a pollen tracker and tiny kin tracker (Maybe unlock for the goggles after you finished the main objective in the level?) I would love to 100% the game but I do not want to spend 20 minutes searching every nook and cranny to find that 3 missing pollen.-Milo is as bland as a white sheet of paper, he could use some personality.Top shelf game!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful short-but-sweet puzzle platformer where you're given a bunch of tasks and objectives in big expansive feeling levels and allowed to just take your time combing through it all. Absolutely lovely stuff, cannot recommend enough. Awesome music, wonderful sound design, adorable character design. Don't pass this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little game that was enjoyable through almost all of my ten hours. Reminds me of Pikmin (obviously) with a mix of more classic 00's platformers. The puzzles and platforming is relatively simple and forgiving, but it provides just enough of a unique spin and game loop to make it all feel special. I also played most of this on my Steam Deck, which ran flawlessly.My only minor complaint is for achievement hunting. One of the collectibles (the pollen) can be hard to finish on each level simply because there are so many. On several levels I was missing just 6 out of 1200 pollen, and I spent a fair amount time trying to find that last bit. I ended up looking up some YouTube videos to finish out two of the levels after I got tired of it. If there was a small additional feature that pointed you in the general direction of the remaining pollen (like after you hit the first benchmark to make the brew for Sikaru) that could cut down on the frustration.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Really cute and cozy 3D collectathon with minor pikmin elements - it's definitely the former first with the latter more being tools and -occasionally- carrying stuff around, but it does the 3D platforming side so well that the relatively downplayed mechanics aren't a problem and honestly overemphasizing them too much may have dragged the game down anyways.The game looks gorgeous, the individual levels are all -huge- and full of stuff to collect, each took at least an hour or more to fully clear - plus the designs are all so creative, repurposing rooms of the house for different environments and giving each a unique feel along the way. Add in the escalation of tinykin types that enhance your ability to explore or solve puzzles and the game never gets stale or tedious - it's not super long in the end with only five and a half levels, but what's there is really good.And Milo feels great to control, plus the soapboard and glide bubble mechanics open up a lot of platforming possibilities - and especially the green tinykin as well, they also significantly change the game when you start getting them. Not every mechanic is perfect - the "tracker" goggles are virtually useless and the yellow tinykin can get a bit annoying to go back and forth between building different bridges but it's like, tiny nuisances at most.I dunno, I don't think this game is gonna blow your mind, but for what it is, it's really charming and really damn fun, just an all-around pleasant experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game that took me just a little over 10 hours to 100%. Well worth the price for a fun and silly adventure with tiny little bugs for companions.If you grew up with Pikmin 1 and 2 this WILL scratch your itch for a pikmin game. While there is no combat there are plenty of dialogue, puzzles, and collecting to give you plenty of things to do in this wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A real charming collect-a-thon with an excellent take on the whole, “a bug’s perspective of a human’s home”.Each level delivers a great sense of scale that’s satisfactorily populated with things to do and places to visit. Completionism comes naturally with how tempting it is to investigate any intriguing landmarks or uncover the next secret nook. The layout of each room does a fantastic job of letting the levels be very open-ended without being too complicated or disorienting. Time flies when you’re sucked into the cycle of seeing an interesting new side area, making your way over to it in style, and then rummaging through that area for trinkets until yet another path catches your eye. The music is quite catchy as well, and I’m always a sucker for clever use of "audio middleware” where elements of a musical theme seamlessly change to better match your local context.Tinykin is just generally a blast to play. It’s got good, wholesome platformer energy that’s never more demanding than it needs to be. It’s got a clever blend of intrinsic “Ooh, what’s over here?” and extrinsic “Give me all the gold orbs” motivations. I might not recommend trying to 100% complete the game, but I do 100% recommend Tinykin for a few relaxing sessions of methodical clean-up and spatial reasoning gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I played a portion of the demo at Pax East and really enjoyed the concept and game play. I finished the demo at home and was really excited to play the game when it came out. I am almost done with the game and I really enjoy looking around and trying to gather everything and speaking with the bugs along the way. I do really wish there were more side quests and games while looking for keys because I feel like getting through the levels go by fairly quickly. I really hope that there is a second game because I have enjoyed this one so much <3
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty fun Pikmin-like puzzle game. You're a space explorer that teleported into a 90s house. The twist is you are the size of a bug and the other bugs have developed a society across many rooms, complete with a religion worshipping a previous tenant of the house that has gone missing some time ago. So uncover what is going on and get back to your ship by solving a number of rather simple exploration puzzles aided by cute and eager to help Tinykin critters.The game will take you about 7 hours to beat, and a few more to 100%. It's pretty fun and leisurely, but lacks that sense of accomplishment you'd get from Pikmin where unlocking shortcuts and planning what you were going to do next was an actual challenge.Plus surprisingly enough the game makes you be a scab during one of its levels (the one where ants are protesting because they don't want to bake a cake for a religious ceremony so it falls on you to do it). Kind of jarring for there not to be an option not to be a strikebreaker. At least everyone is happy in the end, but still...
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A total triumph of a game.  Combines some of the best collect-a-thon elements of Banjo Kazooie/DK64, combines them with the Pikmin'esque followers, takes out all the annoying/irritating fun-blocking elements from those games - and leaves a true polished gem.  Really tight controls so you always feel in control, charming graphics, and great NPC dialogue filled with winkwink references to lots of pop culture games/tv/film. The only negative is that it will leave you wanting more because its so good and easy to play through in a few sittings.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is actually a really good 3D platformer that kinda came out of nowhere for me. While I haven't finished the game yet what I've played so far has made it a favorite of the year.It really captures that simplistic exploration/reward gameplay loop in a semi-big level that I think a lot of modern 3D platformers miss. They didn't even need any form of combat, that I've seen yet anyway, to accomplish this.Anyone that's comparing this game to Pikmin in any way is doing the game and potential buyers a disservice. While the game does feature some surface-levels similarities, they are simply superficial and shouldn't be taken as "this game is just indie Pikmin" like one could say for Bug Fables is for the Paper Mario franchise.Buy this game if you're looking for a light-hearted 3D Platformer based around exploration. I'd say don't buy it if you're looking for that high-intensity army and time management of the Pikmin series. Because you're simply not going to get it with this game.Bonus Points for the game working right out of the box for Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most charming games I've played in ages. Fun and cute art style combined with relaxing gameplay. It's not anything too hard or challenging, but it is genuinely fun to explore the world looking for every last collectible to get that 100%. Tinykin satisfies an itch for someone like me who likes to explore every nook and cranny of a level, and brings me back to the days when 3d platformers were more common.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game. Rarely do I ever just play a game from start to finish within a day or two but this game is something special. While it's true it has some similarities with PIKMIN, they are only slight. Certain tinykins have specific abilities and you use them in a very specific manner to solve some environmental puzzles or other tasks. What the game does different however is take away the more tedious micromanagement of the PIKMIN titles. The little guys just do what they do and a task requires x amount of them and often you have to use several in tandem to complete tasks but there's no stressful combat or timer involved.Tinykins is also a fairly competent 3D platformer. The controls are tight and responsive. The levels are incredibly designed, honestly they impressed me with their density and size despite the fact that I am a bit of an old school platforming fan dating back to the 1980s when Mario first debuted. The game is a near perfect sandbox collectathon with only some minor issues.Problems tend to come from the sheer size of the levels and trying to remember or find where objectives are. At one point, the little guys had carried an object for me but I didn't see where they went. The game showed me where they ended up but I hadn't been there yet.  Eventually I found where the item was but a QOL fix to make that item show up with the visor would have helped. That's basically all the game needs, some QOL fixes. Amazing game, I truly loved this experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: From start to finish, this game has charm and the thrill of finding everything in every little nook and cranny. Some day one achievement bugs, but if you think you have everything, try just entering every room again and it should pop up with the achievements. Also if you think you have all the tinykin, go to the ending sequence in the attic and it should pop the achievement once end cutscene plays. Wonderful game, would love a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with this game.  I finished it in probably 9 or so hours, since it doesn't seem like the time I spent on the demo (the entire tutorial and first level) is added to the Steam Game Time calculation.  Luckily, all of my progress transferred over without any problems when I bought the full game.  I loved the puzzle solving, and I felt like the game was long enough that I felt like I was able to feel like I really understood my options for interacting with the world, without becoming frustratingly padded out.  If you're not into collect-a-thon platformers, you probably won't enjoy this, but this game was engaging and compelling to an extent that genuinely surprised me.  The story was decent, and I'm normally a very story-driven player, but I just couldn't wait to explore each area and see all the different ways I could use the Tinykin to get to new places.  I found the controls fluid and responsive using a controller, and almost all of my deaths felt like my error and not the game's fault.  I really hope this becomes a series.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting for this game quite some time now and even played the demo every single time it was available because it was super fun! Now we have the full game and it's even better with some of the best visuals out there and great gameplay. If you like collecting stuff this game is for you that's for sure and it's super cheap as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the best of Super Mario Odyssey, Pikmin and Overlord combined. I haven't been able to stop playing it since I launched the demo and quickly bought the game, which carried my progress over from the demo.This game just wants you to have FUN. There are so many tiny aspects to this game that are so rare but much appreciated: unlimited sprint immediately, platform mechanics that aren't picky, constant unlocked shortcuts to make exploring levels easier as you move on, etc. They all add up to just letting you focus on the fun aspects of the game: puzzle solving and exploration.

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is what I like to call a "Well rounded game", yeah you might find a few little details that could have been more polished but overall the game is just PERFECT.Before I get into those few little detail I would like to list every aspect that makes the game really good:-I got to play a demo of it a few months back and at first it gaved me the "Pickmin vibes" with it's own flavour.Now after completing it I can confirm my thoughts on that matter, yeah you get those vibes but Tinykin it's completly it's own thing and offers it's own dynamics especially when you take in count the level design of the game.-The duration of the game is on point, exactly what the gameplay mechanics could give is what you get since there's no "extra" tastless content in this game. But in case you want to play around with it's mechanics just for fun you can always comeback to it and go for a 100% in each level or just explore new ways to aproach the levels. Having that nice duration for the main story and offering that replay value feels awesome (I completed it in gamepass first and then got a key that I might use to exploit that replay value through steam)-The controls are smooth AF and once you master the soapboard you can find yourself running around the levels at an awesome pace despite of how huge they are.-The story is interesting and know where to put it's efforts to catch the attention of the player to keep it engaged.-Visually the game looks amazing, the art directtion it's outstanding. I really dig the combination of the few art artstyles used (2D-ish character design, with cartton elements in a 3D world that's filled with little details).-Well optimized, run correctly as I expected taking in count my PC config, but the important thing here is how SMOOTH it felt during my gameplay experience.-Many more positive little details.Just a few negative details:-The electricity gameplay mechanics sometimes it's a little bit "meh", the concept is good, interesting and works great when it come to "how it is implemented in the world", BUT sometimes it can feel bad when you find yourself having to completly stop the rhythm of the game and start making a row to carry electricity just to end up seeing that you've arrenged you "bois" incorrectly and they can't reach the cable they are supposed to connect to.-A few times the gamera got crazy when getting into tiny spaces instead of taking a good angle (not a big deal tbh, but I wanted to include this)Conclusion: DUDE, buy it. Awesome game.Here you have some footage of my walkthrough:

So when i found out it came out on the 30th i was super excited and directly got it and had played thru it in one playthrough. _childDocuments_.review: I'm only partway into the game so far- 100% completed the first two levels, and working on the third, but I wanted to leave a review to hopefully boost this game as much as possible! I haven't seen nearly enough excitement around one of the best collectathons I've played in years. Tight controls and great level design, mixed with charming characters and fun dialogue, and a delightfully fun atmosphere. I was hooked ten minutes into the free demo, and have loved every minute since. To fans of the genre, this is absolutely worth the buy.

name: Lost Ark
detailed_description: Embark on an odyssey for the Lost Ark in a vast, vibrant world: explore new lands, seek out lost treasures, and test yourself in thrilling action combat. Define your fighting style with your class and advanced class, and customize your skills, weapons, and gear to bring your might to bear as you fight against hordes of enemies, colossal bosses, and dark forces seeking the power of the Ark in this action-packed free-to-play RPG. Discover a World Brimming with Adventure Explore seven vast, varied continents and the seas between them to find vibrant cultures, strange and fantastical beasts, and all the unexpected marvels waiting to be discovered. Delve into the secrets of Arkesia, prove your might in battles and raids, compete against other players in PvP, travel to distant islands in search of hidden riches, face packs of enemies and colossal bosses in the open world, and more. Your Odyssey Awaits Splash into massively satisfying ARPG-style combat and progression as you quest, raid, and fight on the scope of an MMO. Whether you want to play solo, in groups with friends, or matched up with other adventurers in the world, there’s an epic adventure waiting for you. Fight in the open world or delve into chaos dungeons, go head-to-head in expert PvP duels, test your mettle on epic quests, raid against bosses big and small, and hold your own in the fight against the Demon Legion to reclaim the power and light of the Lost Ark. Define Your Fight Lost Ark offers easy-to-learn features with unexpected depth and room for customization. Hit the ground running with pick-up-and-play action then take control of your combat with the unique Tripod system. Unlock three tiers of customization for each of your abilities, giving you powerful control of exactly how you fight. Lost Ark’s ever-expanding roster of iconic classes—each with their own distinct advanced classes—offers plenty of room to explore until you find the combat style that’s just right for you. The same goes for other features: as you continue your journey, you’ll find non-combat skills, crafting, guilds and social systems, and other rich features that bring the world alive. Whether you want to skim along the surface or dive deep into the details is up to you. ACCESSIBILITY FEATURES: Personalize your adventure with accessibility settings before game play. Enable numerous options including chat text enlargement, color blindness filters, photosensitivity mode, toggleable camera shake, and subtitle settings to create your optimal experience. Define your audio preferences with settings for volume controls, mono sound, stereo sound, and surround sound. You can also adjust game inputs via input remapping options and mouse/keyboard control settings. Lastly, define game inputs via input remapping options, and make sure no message is missed with chat text-to-speech and speech-to-text.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another MMO. It's unengaging, the character design for the women is neckbeard cringe—every woman is wearing high heels and run like their arms are made of noodles (as a mage at least), the areas and enemies are forgettable. Every enemy that isn't a boss waits for you to kill them like a target dummy.  Spam n' StunlockYou're in a world of pain if you don't enjoy mindless button pressing. That's all this really is, the later game dungeons seem to be fun, but you either have to spend money to get a character to that point in the game, or grind through the worst story to get to the better parts of the game. It's like the developers' egos can't understand that maybe they should just make a series of fun dungeons to play with friends; instead of trying to write a story that was written by a squad of sixteen yearolds. It's completely unnecessary and lacks any self-awareness or irony in this day and age. The ability animations are neat.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently 50 on 3 characters (played a little bit with 2 alts after 2 free powerpass) , ilvl 556, roster lvl 35 and game is alright, some positives some negatives: (76 hours played)Pros:- Way above average graphics and effects (played on max settings). I played a lot of MMORPG and can say that its the best looking one that I played. Also, I liked character model/face personalisations, you can make cute characters ;)- Decent main story, but I liked the side stories more (some island quests were interesting). Compared to other MMORPGs, the story is above average, not innovative, but will not make you bored (best button is still g though for some less interesting stuff)- Very Good combat (nice effects, sounds, satisfying ect). Combined with the graphics and ability designs, I think that it makes the combat less boring compared to other MMOs. You should really try it some abilities feels good when you use them and awakening abilities too.- Nice boss fights (decent challenge for some guardian raids or Abyss dungeons), not your average MMORPG, when you can do mechanics and dump all your abilities, sometimes repositioning and interrupting your stream of abilities (DPS loss) is better than taking damage from bosses (limited healing and respawns), so it makes combat less braindead. - Game will be more challenging faster than your common MMORPG because leveling is very fast. It takes not a lot of time to be 'max level' (50) 20ish hours for me, but I got sidetracked a lot, but 20 is nothing compared to other MMOs.- For me voice acting was good, some say it is bad, but I liked it. The dialogue is a bit weird at times though, probably because of translation errors.Cons:- Honing system (RNG based system for upgrading gear) is bs, if the ressources to funnel into were not time-gated (daily/weeklies) it would be fine but RNG + time-gating is too much.- Boat travelling simulator, if you like alt-tabing when auto-moving your ship, then spend an amount of time doing island quest for gear mats (you will need to do that in order to go around time-gating for your first character), you will either be during that time a captain as a part time job or you will alt-tab to watch a Youtube video and not realize that your auto moving ship arrived at destination, but the destination had a hazard and when you come back, well gg ship is stranded and go to the nearest port = waste time, but at least I can finish my video. Also, if your pc takes time loading in zones, then gg because you will spend more time on a loading screen than playing the game (even thought it was fast for me it was annoying af because there is a lot of fetching stuff in other zone for quests = lots of loading). - Pay 2 Win for PvE not for PvP : Basicly you can buy mats for upgrading your gear and thus your ilvl from the cash shop. I saw people argue that it is not P2W and more Pay to convenience/to progress, for me I don't care because I like wasting my time, but I will let you decide. _childDocuments_.review: I was excited for this game for almost a decade. When I heard it was finally releasing here I was so excited until I heard AGS was managing it. I prayed that they could just do one thing right and I was wrong. To make a long story short, this game is not worth it. If you want some more details I will tell you why: This game limits you on traditional MMO gameplay. Yes, RMT and P2W is a big problem, but why are people doing it? To play the content. The content that is locked behind hourly, daily, and weekly barriers. The few dungeons and raids you can play you will be locked out of for the week and only find a small amount of replayability without any rng rewards. The farming/grinding aspect of MMOs has also been gated, it's in a "chaos dungeon" you can do 2 times a day to farm exp, items, and gold. It's a great concept, but standalone it is insufficient. I have played this game thoroughly and am at the point where I just want to get on to raid and do a dungeon, but I can only do 1 dungeon and to progress to do more content I have to grind through weeks of not really playing the game the way I would like to. I want to play an MMO that I can sink time into, explore a world and do stuff in. Lost ark is not that game, you will get to end game and be reduced to sitting in a hubzone and queuing for content. The little story content and exploration there is doesn't last long or give much reward, dungeons in the outer world have no replayability outside of getting mokoko seeds. They could easily make end game versions of dungeon content they have and amazon could release most of the content to us, but instead we get a IV drip of updates and an old game that's not even up to date. Don't waste your time. Lost Ark is currently in the point of it's lifetime where it's pretty much like BDO or a P2W mobile game, Amazon will still profit from this but the game is essentially dead. It is feeding off of a community of addicted whales who are in a rat race and competing for GvG and having fun with their social groups they've bonded with. PvP is a joke not even competitive, I get on after 3 months and absolutely stomp. The PvE and PvP is awesome in this game and it's nice to dabble in once in awhile, but don't invest any money or time you could use better elsewhere on this. This is not a game you should think of investing your time in building a character in to last you years. This game will not last long.Lost Ark is essentially a PvP focused game by design with PvE content as well. The game is designed to be mainly lead by the PvE which is limited and then carried by PvP or extra content in the meantime, but when you manage it the way AGS has you ruin the potential for any PvP community to flourish, the community burns out trying to consume content they can barely handle and we get this mess. Lost Ark is a combat focused game, it's meant to be highly challenging and have intense responsive combat similar to BDO or the old Diablo games. Those bones are still in this game and you can still find a bit of it in PvP, but the PvE experience has been watered down and ruined. The carrot on the stick used to be the challenge of this games combat and content, now it's just getting your gear score up to be in a top guild or play some content and then cry for a week that there is no content because the game has truly missed it's target audience and community has been spoiled and ruined by amazon letting RMT proliferate. Meanwhile, Amazon is chokeholding content to make a profit off of "new" update hype like most people don't realize the updates are old and were available at launch. Amazon knows they have a great wonderful game and they're doing everything they can to milk you and anyone that plays this game in insidious ways. The game is purposefully designed to make you fiend for the content that Amazon won't release to us and further more they have let the economy completely be taken over by the RMT rates so if you want to play fr, open your wallet or progress painfully slowly and gain gold at a rate which you can't afford the current prices at because the gold you just earned is worth a lot less than you actually are aware. DO NOT SPEND ON THIS GAME.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ark has incredible art design and good aspects of a decent MMO, which pains me to say that I will uninstall and stop playing after this review. I have given my pro's and con's and my personal reasons listed below.The Art direction is gorgeous and is not just some cookie cutter MMO trying to cash in on Diablo's success.Lost Ark has a unique art direction of melding different types of geographical settings from rural villages to eastern lands and structures, to mystical and magical forests, and pulls it off strangely enough.The story honestly did not capture my interest, but the cinematic scenes are incredible to look at most of the time, especially when you get to Rohendel and hit item level 460 and play a dungeon that warps the background like the movie inception. Really cool stuff. You can tell the developers are trying their best with what they have.Unfortunately for me, this is were the game turned into a nightmare. In order for me to obtain new armor sets, I would have to complete the abyssal dungeons, which is like a dungeon, but with "Raid" mechanics (especially once you hit 460 item level).These represent dungeons that you have played thus far through the story, but with a twist. They are harder at 340 item level and up, but I was completely thrown off when raid mechanics started to show up for the bosses at item level 460.Up until now, I was not introduced to these type of mechanics, which would be fine if it did not have a party wipe when the mechanic fails. As a new player who is trying to learn, it is frustrating to run into this wall and have to rely on random players to help explain the mechanics, which did not help me at all.I can only suggest to have NPC's talk during these battles and have the NPC's explain the mechanics through text and voice if possible. This can help avoid the situation for players such as myself that have to communicate with random players, where their communication skills are not their strong point. As it stands now. I will not be playing Lost Ark. I would consider it if they balance the raid mechanics by having the mechanics introduced to you earlier so your not going into matchmaking blind.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to have an enjoyable gaming  experience and  appreciate all the hard work that was put into it, then I heartily recommend you jump in.  It's an ARPG with an MMO GUI and its all Free! The only thing you're paying with is your time.However, this may depend on how good your attention span is.  If you are looking to speed through this game while not appreciating the aesthetics of it, then this is not the game for you. You would be better served by playing something that has a 30-60 hour play through time.Yes, there are cash shop items, but this is not a P2W game. The cash shop items are aesthetics or to make things a little easier. That's it.   You'll start off choosing a class and then test the advanced versions, and be locked into that advanced version trajectory within 10 minutes of starting it. The ability to redistribute your skill points to the various skills offered in the advanced skill tree to test out other play styles is a boon.If you're like me and want to hit every quest and side quest along the way you will then spend about 100 hours on the first continent alone. After that there are plenty more islands and continents to explore. If you played LoZ: Windwaker, the sailing portion of the game is akin to that. These lovely locations are gated by level and gear level requirements. Add in world events, PvE and PvP experiences, plus gearing, upgrading, crafting et cetera, all things MMO's have become known for and there are a plethora of things to do.If you decide to tackle this with friends, ensure you're on the same server. Characters and items cannot be transferred between servers. So sit back and relax. Solo it, join a party, create your own guild, and explore the beauty of Arkesia. And remember, the Tooki king is a thief and a coward.

_childDocuments_.review: So the game has been poorly managed by Amazon so far. Ranging from garbage excuses as to why they can't fix certain things, to just straight up ignoring player concerns like true capitalist Chads, it's not a good look.That being said, if we choose to ignore the poor direction from Amazon so far, the game itself is real solid.It's got good momentum during the leveling phase. If you've ever played an MMO before, you're probably all-too-familiar with the soul crushing 'leveling phase' that everyone has to go through unless they spend money to instacap a character. Running back and forth between the same set of NPCs for an hour or two per region of each large 'zone' some dozen times over for possibly weeks on end gets to be monotonous as hell, and most people that would quit the game will do so during this phase. Bonus awful points if the story is also ♥♥♥♥♥♥, so we don't even have anything to smile about while we are slowly dying inside.I'm happy to report that Lost Ark has found a way around much of this misery. The way they do their quests is entirely 'forward facing'. You very, VERY rarely go backwards to revisit the same area. So you rarely speak with the same NPC twice, with the exception of periodically reporting to large hub cities amid a cluster of zones, (And those NPCs often become rapport NPCs, so getting to know them a bit more is kind of okay.) You pick up the quest from NPC A, do the quest actions in a nearby area, and then turn the quest into NPC B on the other side of said area while picking up a continuation quest from NPC B, or the next quest from NPC C further down the road. It's brilliant, and I'm wondering why nobody ever thought of this before. This forward momentum curbs the dullness, making you feel like you're making good progress at all times during your leveling.And you really are making good progress, since this is easily the fastest leveling phase I have ever seen, by far. If a *casual* player chose to skip all the side stuff like hunting for collectibles, doing the extra dungeons, or heck - skipping over all the easily identified side quests (main, world, and side quests all have different colored markers!), they could get to level 50 within a few days. I am NOT kidding. It really is just that fast. Coupled with the ARPG-esque gameplay (it's an isometric view with combat closer in style to Diablo than WoW, as a comparison) and the leveling phase is actually - dare I say - enjoyable? Ah... that might be a stretch for some. But it definitely didn't suck!The price we pay for that fast forward momentum, though, is that the story is mostly nonsense and difficult to follow. You don't stay attached to any set of NPCs for too long, so you probably won't ever acquire a sense of identity with them, and the legendary Arks amount to little more than pretty MacGuffins. If you don't know what a MacGuffin is, long and short is that they have no functional purpose (for you, especially) aside from 'they're gonna beat the big bad guy at some point'. Pity, but that's just the type of game this is, I guess.After leveling is the vaunted endgame phase that is also present in all MMOs. And this one doesn't disappoint. There's lots of unique things to do, between horde busting stages, boss killing, challenge tower climbing, collection hunting, further questing if so desired, a plethora of rapport NPCs to explore with their own little unique story lines (wanna help a Queen play hookie?), various endgame character systems, guild ♥♥♥♥ to do, and more... yeah, you're never really gonna be wanting for activities unless you're the hardest of cores. It's real nice!Not to mention, character building is quite enjoyable. It's a 'tiered skill system' instead of a linear or split 'tree' of skills. So among three tiers, the first tier might let you do one of either regenerating MP on hit or increasing damage dealt to struck enemies, while the second tier might increase the AoE of a skill, change the angling of its hit box and increasing range, or even switching it to an entirely different element while supplying a powerful damage buff. Etc, etc. This means you can create unique loadouts for many situations to maximize your punch in various content. And there's plenty of other endgame-esque customization systems I won't get into here - they're even more complex and involved.And finally, possibly the best part of this game's appeal: the Roster System.What is the Roster System?Essentially, it's taking various meta mechanics like an 'account level', collectibles, and other stuff, and making them account wide instead of character exclusive. This also means that any benefits you get from those things... such as stat increases...Apply to EVERY character you've made, or will ever make.The Roster System is genius, and I've never seen anything quite like it. The flexibility we get from this system is staggering, and MANY of the things you do on one character will seamlessly transfer to every other character you have made or will ever make. And the ways the system functions (you have 'Roster Levels' that increase stats for everyone, while also an individual character level, for example), not only encourages alts, but actually *empowers* them and makes them far more enjoyable for a lot more people. There's extras in there I haven't even gotten to yet that make leveling and even endgame go much faster, so that you can make entirely new characters and get them up to speed at mach 10. It's so wonderful that I'm now thinking MMOs should just make *everything* 'account bound', so people can freely swap between classes at will and enjoy even more of their games. Lost Ark has certainly put us on that path.Putting it simply: if WoW implemented a roster system tomorrow, it would probably save their sinking ship in a heart beat. This ♥♥♥♥ is that good.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start this review by saying that the core of the game is amazing. Hands down the best combat in any ARPG, very engaging. Wonderful skill animations and sounds; on top of all that the class designs are TOP NOTCH.BUT.... unfortunately, this game is FILLED with bots. _childDocuments_.review: I don't normally make reviews for games, but I am taking a little time to just say a few of my opinions on this one. This is an MMO (No ♥♥♥♥ Sherlock). I think if you look at any games in this genre, you're going to be expecting some level of grind. Whether it fighting bosses over and over for specific drops, giant raids, maxing out weapon levels/damage, etc. These are all part of the MMO genre. You CAN pay to progress if you WANT. You do not need to pay if you don't want to, it just means it'll take you more time to get to whatever item level you want to get to. Just because you have bad luck, does not mean it's a bad game. Yes, at the higher Tiers, 3% chance to level up an item to get to the next item level sucks, but playing an MMO is not a race. Of course there are other parts of the game where it's actually a little irritating like the who card system that is pure RNG where you  only get a few selection chest, but overall, if you enjoy the grind MMO then you'll just play this casually and you won't have to spend any money. Just save up the materials weekly, batch hone and move on.If you want to play a game where you can be a chad in a game after playing 300 hrs or so then don't play MMOs, they are not for you. Like honestly, these games are suppose to last LONG term. if you're in a rush to be in that top 1% of players then you're gonna have to be super lucky or spend a lot of money to progress, but it is not a must. Funny thing is that the PvP in this game is literally not item gated either, you just have to learn match ups and learn to play your class correctly. So in that aspect I am sure no one is complaining. I think that AGS/Smilegate can definitely do better in being transparent with their plans with this game with the content release 100%, but as a whole, I think this game has an okay base if you want to play something you can casually play. Like I said, if you're looking to immediately or easily become a mega chad in an MMO, sorry to break it to you, MMOs are not the games for you. Also, the F2P aspect of this game is more friendly, but you have to be patient and not rush. (I hate failing any honing in this game) I still play F2P in this game and I mean eventually I'll hit that 1400+ but Im not in a rush, this game literally came out in NA/EU 2 months ago..... like give it time. HOPEFULLY in a year or so it'll catch up content wise to the KR/RU counterparts. You can wait to play this in a year if you want to do that, but if you don't mind a slow grind, this is fun. I know a lot of people are comparing this with FF14 as well, but remind you that that game has been out way longer in NA than this game, give it time. Also, don't compare this to an ARPG please, the top down view is literally the only similarity. Like the fantasy and all that maybe, but one is literally a full game and an MMO is something that keeps on having updated content so... yeah.

_childDocuments_.review: After the last road-map that was released I can no longer recommend this game to anyone for a couple of reasons.1. I read that some players spent around 800$ for a full set in the color that they wanted in other regions.2. Slow-drip class releases. All classes are already available in other regions and some classes were even available in the beta, so all that Amazon needs to do is activate them. However, they will take one and a half year or so to release them all (1 class per two months). There is no reason to delay releasing more classes apart from milking the community for money. So, if you like to play the game with a class that you might have seen from other regions you might have to wait for more than a year to do so.3. If you want to pay for a premium battle pass (which is 15$) there is no option to simply just pay for it with money. You have to pay 1500 "royal crystals" but there is no option to buy 1500 royal crystals. Your options are either to buy 1000 crystals bundle (which cost 10$ or so) that leaves you 500 crystals short or 2200 crystals bundle (20$ or so, can't remember the exact price) that leaves you with 700 crystals leftover. And no, there is nothing in the store that is worth 700 crystals, so if you want to spend them you will have to buy more.4. Massive amount of bots. I probably wouldn't be exaggerating too much when I say that half the population are bots. You constantly see bot trains everywhere in every zone. Bots existed in this game since release and nothing is being done to combat them. So, if you are a new player be prepared to only see and play with bots until you get to higher level zones.5. Content that is only released for whales. _childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a new job, Lost Ark is for you! Unlike a normal job where the employer pays you, Lost Ark gives you every opportunity to pay them instead. Excited yet? You'll be expected to donate thousands of dollars AND hours of your life to this new job! Wait, there's more! If you don't, nobody will take you seriously enough to let you do the best end-game content. That's right, not only does this job demand your every waking moment and spare cash, you'll also experience gate-keeping and toxicity on scales you've never before dreamt of! Don't wait, apply today!Snarky sarcasm aside... This is a pay to win game. That is, they do everything possible to make free to play as absolutely miserable as they can. They want to get your cash, and everything about the game is geared for exactly that. However, even if you pay you'll find it's never enough, unless you've spent thousands. I'm serious, it's beyond insanity.I have over 2k hours of play time in, and let me tell you: it's just a non-stop rat race of the same monotonous content. You will have to do the same content so much and so often, if you make a mistake or aren't over-geared for it, other players will express their great displeasure at having to spend an extra 45 seconds of their life in that miserable place because YOU screwed up. It's a toxic community, made so by a toxic game system, which itself is framed around a toxic and predatory monetization engine.The only reason to play this game is for the Legion Raids, which is the only content that provides any actual challenge to players. All the other content is just a grind-fest, some of which is mandatory to get your maximum amount of weekly gold, item currencies, and upgrade tokens that will ensure your further progression. Speaking of progression, you have to advance at least 6 characters in this game, or you'll never keep up the gold generation/farming needed to sustain end-game participation on just 1 character. Which means you'll have to spend a lot of time and resources on those extra characters too. The grind-god is never satisfied.You'll be spending A LOT of time obtaining currencies, and spending A LOT of currency to progress these alts as well as your main characters to ensure you can get gold. What is gold good for? The Auction House. Upgrade items and gear. Perhaps more importantly, you can convert gold into Blue Crystals. That part is important because Blue Cyrstals are the only way you can obtain Pheons.What the heck are Pheons? They are a required currency when buying gear and upgrades from the Auction House to wear on your characters. The gear you wear is what determines your item level. After you obtain the gear, the chance you'll have to upgrade it will be very low - at the highest levels, less than 1% chance per upgrade attempt, with each attempt costing tens of thousands of gold in materials. Your item level is what determines what raids and other content you can participate in. So, Pheons and Blue Crystals are essentially a pay-to-win currency that severely stifles free-to-play progression.How do you get Pheons? You have to buy them from the in-game marketplace with blue crystals. How do you get blue crystals? By spending real cash, or sacrificing massive amounts of the gold you made that week to exchange said gold for blue crystals, just to exchange the crystals for pheons. Every time you exchange one currency for another, the game taxes you through horrible conversion rates or artificially inflated pricing directly for cash.Of course, many players elect to bypass months of grinding altogether by going to 3rd party gold sellers, who operate swarms of bots on every server. These bots have one goal - farm gold. Unfortunately, this has ruined the economy for anyone who doesn't buy gold, and unforgivably, SmileGate / Amazon have been doing the bare minimum necessary to counter the issue. It really seems to me they have zero ability to control their own in-game economy, and if you aren't a long-time player of MMOs/RPGs let me just say that this is A MAJOR red flag. Buying a solid piece of equipment from the auction house will often cost around 100 gold (which is nothing) but it will cost you 25+ pheons, which is worth about $10 USD.You see the problem yet? Even if you had millions of gold, it's not the gold that is worth anything - it's their cash shop pheon and blue crystal currencies that hold real value. Also, throw away any thoughts of making millions of gold easily because the game caps you to less than 50k gold PER WEEK, that is unless you sell your time (and have a grossly over-geared character) to bus lower level players through raid content they no longer have the patience or brain cells for doing themselves in normal groups. Time, blue crystals, and pheons are the real currencies of this game.Which is another point of contention - worthless currencies. There are no less than 2 dozen currencies in this game, at the bare minimum. Maybe as many as 60? I'm not sure anyone has counted all of the tokens, coins, and other crap you need to collect to spend at vendors, but it's just stupid. Almost all of them are unnecessary.There are so many negatives about this game, such as the card collection system, the tedious and monotonous "I'd rather watch paint dry" progression quests and the hellish time-sink of performing those 6 different times on alt characters, the toxic community that gate-keeps every raid or event you'll try to participate in, and so much more.Avoid this game like its a grizzly bear.

_childDocuments_.review: Before the official 2/11/2022 launch, the early access reviews were 96% positive over about 2,000 reviews. This is because those people reviewed the actual game itself instead of the abysmal launch and server issues. If I'm being overly optimistic, that's somewhat of a good thing since it means so many people are so exited to play. These issues aren't to be overlooked, and the devs are already addressing so many issues which makes me optimistic for the future.Lost Ark is scratching an itch that games like Diablo 3, New World and Black Desert Online failed to scratch. This game has so many QoL features that I've wished other MMOs included. P2W is non-existent when leveling 1-50 and after you reach the end game, the things you can buy with real world money to aid your progression do not place you lightyears above F2P players and its not necessary to spend money on the game, your late game progression will just take longer. That is all. There's many different classes to choose from that allow for a variety of different play styles and abilities. The story isn't half bad although it is a "G" spam simulator for sure. There's a lot to do in Lost Ark, leveling 1-50, chaos dungeons, world bosses, hunting for collectibles, etc. There's a lot of different activities to participate in that provide two main things: 1) The satisfaction of demonstrating your builds power and destroying enemies more and more efficiently as you get better and better gear, engravings, cards, etc. 2) The rewards that allow you to continue to progress and get more and more powerful. This game offers great gameplay combined with both long and short term goals to reach. Its right at that point where you progress slow enough to where it feels meaningful, but fast enough to where it doesn't feel like a drag like a game like New World. Its free so its worth a shot. Find a character that seems fun, reach level 25-30ish and if you'll know by then if this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I have 200 hours in this game and am no longer playing it. I got my paladin up to ILVL 580 and just quit. I came to the conclusion that it was not worth my time anymore. Here are my reasons:1. Honing. Yeah I get it. It is what it is and I don't mind the mechanic per se. The problem for me lies in the fact that mats are hard to get especially for your alt characters which my paladin is. Why can't all honing mats be shareable across your whole roster and not just a tiny fraction. Why put weekly limits on the mats exchange NPC? Makes no sense unless there is a specific reason I will get to shortly.2. Island missions and rewards are once per account. This means if your main got all those nice honing mats doing island missions your alts can't. But if this was another game you would be able to share those mats with your alts - oh wait - see #1 above.3. Bots. Yeah this game has a serious gold farming bot problem. Often I would find bots wiping out all the mobs I need to complete a mission. Plus you get the usual gold farm spam messages in chat constantly. So my conclusion is, in order to combat the bot problem, Smilegate severely limited the amount of mats real players can farm for honing. I don't know if this is true or not but it is my impression, and is enough for me to quit even though I thoroughly enjoyed my time in this game. This just points to bad planning and management of this game.If Smilegate asked me for suggestions they would be the following:1. Make all mats shareable across an account's roster2. Allow the island missions to be re-playable per alt.3. Get rid of the auction house and let players who want to trade do so via an external website and in-game messaging/invites.4. Change your revenue model from gold sales to fashion/skin sales. Given how long this games has been out I am surprised at the dearth of options to customize the look of your character. This is how F2P games like Path of Exile earn their revenue.

Further, there is gender-locking. Gunners can be either male or female, but mages and assassins can only be female and warriors can only be male. _childDocuments_.review: Current playtime: 1750 hours.Pros: Best isometric game in terms of combat and skill animations and it's not even close, yes including Diablo 4. There are tons of classes to pick so finding one that you enjoy won't be a problem. All classes have really cool 'ultimate' abilities. You really feel the power jumps after you grind for the end game gear and gems. The classes feel very well done in the end game. I've played and tried over 10 classes.The story cutscenes are pretty epic the first time you play through the story mode.The endgame raids are generally extremely well done and requires skill to clear. It's the whole reason why people continue to play this game.Cons: Super grindy (like every other mmo), horizontal content is really boring (stopped doing it like 100 hours into the game). PvP is basically dead content. No real sense of community, this game is mostly pug content. New players will get gatekept in raids. The entire game is based on the end-game raiding and vertical power / gear progression. Once you understand how progression works in this game, you come to the realization that this game is really shallow in terms of actual content. You start to see all the cracks in this game. You grind dailies for materials to hone your gear. Clear the weekly lock-out raids for gold. Rinse and repeat. That's basically the game. Eventually everything feels like homework. The game devs are aware of it, but nothing of significance has been done to solve this (yet).But people still play because of how polished the combat is.There is alot of RNG stuff you have to endure. Using the market house requires another currency called Pheon along with using your gold. It's a stupid system that is supposed to control gold inflation but it doesn't work.P2W element: Almost everything in this game can be bought with real money. In terms of getting BiS gear, its P2W - but honestly getting this gear is whale-bait and there's honestly no point in whaling in this game as you can clear all content without paying money. If you just play frequently, eventually you will get near BiS gear that is like 90-95% the power of a whale. You have to be a idiot to want to whale in this game nowadays.You cannot really P2W the raiding in this game. If you suck at mechanics, you will wipe your entire team, doesn't matter how much damage you do.

_childDocuments_.review: Characters had some interesting diversity and gameplay mechanics. Loved the boss mechanics and was looking forward to the raid content and had very nice horizontal progression.I can not recommend the game in it's current state. It is swarmed with bots everywhere spamming all the time, whispers, mail... etc. The deal-breaker for me wasn't the long grind, lack of cosmetics or even that there is pay to win mechanics in the game... It was that Amazon hasn't been truthful from the start. I was enticed to play because the KR/RU players were talking about good community and that the divide between P2W and F2P wasn't too bad. However, Amazon removed content that was on patch notes to slow leveling down overnight before pre-launch (I don't want to HAVE TO play 3 alts to level my main up at a decent speed). This, plus a lack of content for gaining materials that was never implemented over from the KR/RU versions made the notorious "deadzone" (1340-1370 ilvl range)  even more extreme and further kept f2p players from doing new content when it was released, while whales easily pushed through it paying. If this was a new mmo experience I'd be a little more lenient with an oops we messed up, but since Smilegate even had a convention showing that this was a fault of early Lost Ark in Korea and we were still given it with less avenues to gain resources shows it was done on purpose and therefore inexcusable. Since then I have also been reading that people have been stuck with perma-bans while Amazon is removing bots... just a sloppy westernization of the game. If you are interested, just wait a few months when they put in the catch up mechanic patches... if the game isn't dead and the bots are finally handled then it may be a more enjoyable experience.

Fights are rare and trivially easy - just walk into any group of enemies and push any button and they all die, zero risk to the player.Also, in that 4 hours I encountered hundreds and hundreds of bots, and not a single actual human player. And all characters look identical because outfits must be purchased via microtransactions.

_childDocuments_.review: This takes just about all the worst parts of MMOs, and presents them in the form of a great looking isometric view similar to an ARPG. Unfortunately, the bad of the MMO genre - boring quest design, endless running between point A and point B just to spam "G" to interact - beats out how fun the combat could be. Dungeons are too infrequent while leveling, and all the leveling content is far too easy even in the "hard" dungeons. There are also timegates limiting access to content once you hit level 50.TL;DR: Only play this if you don't care about wasting 10+ hours before getting to the endgame and running into Pay 2 Progress timegates.

(I lived on West Coast US, and E Coast players had taken over W Coast.  Never was able to get on after work.).  Finally able to get in, a few days ago (June 2022) on an East Coast server, and play.  3/4 game play up till that point wasn't playing the game, it was dealing with inadequate server space (really Amazon?!). _childDocuments_.review: I wanted something to have to hold off till Diablo 4. There's plenty out there, but adding another to that library would be great. This..ain't it. Combat is good, impactful, and skills are cool and well done, but it's way too easy, and you're given a lot of skills out of the gate. C'mon, let me work a bit for those first few.I play a LOT of Final Fantasy, and no stranger to cheesy voice acting and off the wall stories and characters. But by the Gods, this is way too much for me. Not an anime guy, and I have a decent tolerance for Korean story telling, but I can't follow this story. Seems cool from some of the cutscenes, but the voice acting, dialog, and starting character cast just does me in. Might seem drastic, but this ruined the game for me. So much bad dialog, cutscenes that hurt to watch and listen to, takes away from the decent combat system.I understand many people can find what they're looking for in this game, but as for me, hard pass. As a note of performance, the client itself ran fine. Never dipped below 60 FPS even when there was a lot going on. Ran pretty smoothly and never crashed. Pretty solid client from my small playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: If you don't like what you're reading, at least skip to the final paragraph.Whoever is comparing this to LoL or Diablo 3, please stop repeating what your hear from sponsored reviews, which Lost Ark is brimming with. I can't believe how a game can be so hyped up and so incredibly mediocre. At least New World and Genshin Impact had a strong core and modern graphics to back them up.It's so much clunkier and slower, it's closer to a generic point and click MMO than a top-down action game like Diablo. Attacks look nice... they are one 3rd windup, one 3rd active and one 3rd recovery, no animation cancelling, no buffering, you can't change attack/movement direction at any point during an animation. No exceptions. On top of this, besides a dodge with 6s CD, the only way you can go past an enemy is walking around them... I am a huge fan of action combat, but I'd take WoW or FF14 any time over this. Dark Souls has A LOT more fluidity and control - It's meant to require commitment, not to be bad and unsatisfying like this mess.Yes, it has a lot of features to make you play and pay, like pets, mounts, NPC affinity, limited housing, but it does nothing remarkably well. If you want depth, go back to Black Desert Online. Some people sell Lost Ark as an especially F2P friendly game, but you can still buy everything you buy in other MMOs, like VIP, upgrade materials, gold and cosmetics. But hey, the PvP is equalized! With combat so bad, if you care about PvP in Lost Ark, might as well give Tetris a try. It will raise your standards.Unreal Engine 3. Blade & Soul, 2012 before its UE4 upgrade, was arguably better looking than this game. Just like older games, Lost Ark suffers not just from graphical limitations and oddities, but also lots of low quality environmental assets. It looks fine for UE3, though not as good as some decade old titles made in the same engine. The artistic look is not even worth mentioning.Nice - the best and perhaps the only good aspect of any generic Korean MMO - but customization is close to rock bottom, you can't change body proportions at all, not even a simple height or weight slider. You have a handful of face customizations and a fair selection of hairstyles, and that's about it.Read the introduction in this review again. I've played lots of MMOs in my time, tried over a hundred, and this game, while having one of the better production qualities, it's just so mediocre. But hey, it has a big playerbase and it's advertised everywhere, so of course we are here playing it. Right?The only thing I want you to remember from this is that there are other options out there. I've already mentioned some. Some better, some older yet better looking. MMOs nowadays are all money milkers: they only want you to have fun as long as it stimulates their income and they use every trick in the book to get you . I won't stop you from anything. I just hope you come to realize this soon. Trust me, I've been there; this is why I may seem overly critical. My standards have grown after all the bull I've seen. There are some solid MMOs that are imho way, way better than Lost Ark, albeit some P2W, but also with much better story, world building and leveling process that you might love to experience without getting hooked on the repetitive time and money sink called "MMO endgame".

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I wanted to like the game but after all the amount of hours i've put into 3 characters to get towards late game, I can't recommend it. The positives:-The combat is great, everything feels good, i prefer some characters over others but the characters I enjoyed, I REALLY enjoyed. Killing large groups of enemies always felt good, doing a lot of damage against guardian bosses/abyss bosses and seeing high numbers always felt good. One of the games biggest positives-Abyss Dungeons are fun, especially in t3 when you do hard mode, the mechanics are interesting, although once you get high enough where everyone is stronger than the requirements of the dungeon it becomes to easy, but for your first experience it was challenging and fun. They're creative enough and different enough where it doesn't feel like you've already done it before and some of them actually require you to work with your group-Side content is fun, such as collectibles, sometimes it can be frustrating and there is a good amount of time gating, but it makes sense for side content and collectibles, they should take time and some of them can be rewarding and unique. They also bring you to islands you usually wouldn't go to in the normal game and you get to experience different content within that, such as events and quests on the island itself.Cons:Content as a whole - In the end game, you don't really have a lot to do, and yes there isn't all the content from the other regions available yet, but even than when it arrives you don't have a lot to do and i mean MAIN content/End game content, ill try to explain better You have basically 4 things you can do in the end game ,  1. Chaos dungeons      You do these twice a day and you can do them more than that for a small chance at mats/gear and extra mats which       you use to buy main matts that go up in price as you buy more (resets weekly) which is nice but will feel very repetitive       after a while and to me personally the more I did it the less I wanted to do chaos dungeons in general.2. Guardian Raids      You can also do these twice daily (or choose to do them once and end get a rest bonus this also applies to chaos       dungeon) and it'll end up being like 75% efficient, which is what i did with GR's because it felt like way to much work to       do 2 daily especially when I worked on 3 characters, but if your playing casually or semi-hard core than i'm sure you'd       be okay with doing it once a day. Either way they can be fun but in the end you'll do the same GR boss every day until a       new one comes out maybe once a month. Yea fighting the same boss every day on multiple chars. sounds fun right?3. Abyss Dungeons.       I actually find these very fun, I don't really think there's any negative aspect to the dungeons themselves besides the        fact you can only do these one a week, and you can only do ones in your gear score range, anything to low and you        don't any gear/mats. So in the end you do the same 2-3 ones on all your characters 1 a week.4. Abyss Raids.        Once again these are really fun, challenging and require a lot of team effort, especially the legion raids as they release         get harder and more unique while being really enjoyable and feels rewarding. But once again you can only do these         once a week per character.Im just going over base game play, not dwelling into the Marketplace or how you gain income and how you gear up or anything, although i am not a fan of it especially pheons.Say your playing casually and you want 1-3 characters like me, say your 1400 gear score and you can only do the first abyss raid, well you do that on 3 characters, in 1 day, and you do your 3 abyss dungeons on 3 characters in 1 day.Well now? You do your chaos dungeon and guardian raid every day. you do your dailys every day to obtain more matts such as cube or boss rush, thats really all there is. There isnt enough content in the game and the Honing system itself stops you from doing end game content, heres an exampleI had collected 1 months+ worth of materials from 2 other characters sitting at 1355 and funneled it into my main for more than 1 month, before Vultan release to get ready for it, and my main sat at 1400. I bought the basic tier of the battle pass the month prior for the rewards and I spent 6-8 hours a day doing everything I can to get to 1415, after 1-2 months and the day vultan came out, I did everything again i could on that day and went to upgrade and only made it to 1412.5. Well I was basically stopped from doing any new released content for at LEAST 2-3 weeks as id have to gain a lot of materials in order to try to get to 1415. Well say I got 1415, now i have 1 extra raid I can do a week. Theres just not enough content, the content in the game is Make another characterWhich itself has its own problems as its gold expensive to make more characters and requires more time you have to sync into another character which isn't really fun at all. Even if they release all the raids and side content in the game, in the end its just going to be an endless cycle of doing the 4 things you can do, in the end after everything's released, it'll take 2-3 days to finish everything on 3 characters but its still not enough.Sorry the review is kinda everywhere and isn't super conciseTL;DR: Not enough content, besides the fact the main content is making another character to do the same thing every day as most things are locked weekly.

_childDocuments_.review: The game overall is pretty cool and very addictive which is good for an MMO RPG. A lot of people cry about the Pay to Win endgame stuff, but I don't think that It's that bad. I have only spent money on skins which are only cosmetics. And YES Crystalline Aura is 10$ per month and it provides you with many benefits BUT you can play the game just perfectly fine without it. As far as I know, you can unlock everything that is not in the shop without paying any money. So in my opinion the P2W argument is a decent one but not good enough to ruin someone's playthrough. For the quality of the game: The game was made in Unreal Engine 3 and for this engine, it looks better than some MMOs that come out today on other more modern engines. I think the fact that the game is Top-Down is so much different than other MMOs. I generally don't like this perspective in games but in Lost Ark, it works so well. And because of that, the developers don't have to concentrate on the graphics that much and can focus on other more important things. So overall It's a good MMO RPG with a lot of potential but sadly, we are so far behind the Korean region, that the game in the west seems like nothing compared to the east.

_childDocuments_.review: So to start, this review is for NEW players. I'haven't swiped at all in this game except for a few skins and the starter pack I bought 2 years ago. I have a main at Item Level 1620. I have a few alts I like to play that are 1580+.Honestly I really liked playing through the game when it launched with my best friend and getting to raid with my buddies from another game. With that, I can recommend playing the game for the Main Story Quest and then quit when it gets too grindy for you if you're playing solo.If you have a solid 6-7 friends to play this with, it's fun but reaching all the endgame fights will be a stretch for you all till about 6 months in when you can all reliably farm the Item Level content you'll be on for the 6 character roster you'll need for all of the items on the list below.-Gold (Limited per week gain in raids per character (max of 6))-Silver (Limited daily gain per character)-Cards (EXTREME RNG, Massive Pool of useless cards/sets) ****Gatekeeping issue-Mats to hone (Daily limit, more can be bought for gold on the Auction House)-The trade skill mats to hone (Daily limit, Can also be bough on Auction House or recharged through the Cash Shop)-Engraving books (Much easier to obtain through the Auction house now for cheap gold prices, Except newer class engravings)- Engraving Stone (Possible massive Pheon Sink - If you run out, Only option is Cash shop them for a large amount of your weekly gold or your credit card sword can farm them)and last but Definitely not least... -Skill GEMS!!!  ****Gatekeeping issue if not high enoughYou will need to reliably farm all of these on 6 characters Weekly to push for the final endgame raid fights you'll see in about 5-6 months time. Unless you all wish to buy gold from Smilegate to buy all of the other materials JUST to upgrade your Item Level on your armor and weapon. Which will easily cost you over $300 for 1 character to be 1580+ with everything they'll need to raid... Except Gems and Cards. If you want decent gems(Level 9's) you'll have to double that amount of swiping for most class builds. Cards are even worse to swipe for.Gems at current endgame aren't considered good until they are Level 9.  One level 9 gem usually takes around a month and a half to reliably farm with your 6 man roster all over 1540+.(1 character usually needs all 11 gems slots filled) Cards on the other hand are just extremely RNG based and will likely take you easily a year 1/2 to get some of the best ones finished without swiping your credit card.Now Making alts has a horrible set-back for new players. You need to have perfect stat RNG rolled Accessories for each piece of gear with the correct perfectly RNG rolled engravings on them as well. YOU WILL NOT GET ANY OF THE ACCESSORIES YOU NEED DROPPED. I haven't encountered anyone this lucky when they first start the game. So what do you do? You'll need to buy MOST, if not all of your accessories from the Auction House. On top of spending gold to buy these, you also need Pheons for each purchase, which are sold in.... Yes you got it, in the Cash Shop. You will get free Pheons playing the game but this will probably be enough for your first 2 characters accessories/Engraving Stones... If you don't mess up/fail/or want to change your build. You can also purchase these with gold, expect to pay a few weeks of your earned gold in raids to buy the Pheons needed alone.If you can handle doing this for 6 characters with your friends for at least 5-6 months for the grind, you'll eventually catch up to the bottom tier of endgame raiders. Yes the bottom tier.Most Gatekeeping will keep you to only playing with your friends, other than early endgame raids like Valtan/Vykas and possibly Clown, which will take 10-20mins to fill up the other 7(or 3) slots.The only Decent times to jump in with your team of friends are when the game's having events for new classes coming to the West. Which will give you a free PASS on the gear / accessories / engravings needed to progress for 3-4(?) months. (Not including card sets) You'll have this free boost until the event ends and you'll need to have bought all your accessories and engraving books you'll need for your classes build by then for that ONE boosted character.To sum this up, No I can't recommend this game to new players. It is not friendly to people starting the game at all if your goal is to experience the whole game or to join the people who have been playing since the start. Which is almost the only player base that's left playing this game. Early content is already completely abandoned and you'll have to solo it all if you're alone.

_childDocuments_.review: I have heard veterans of this game have at least 4-digits hours in and maybe with 200 I cannot really judge. I went from enjoying it immensely to being bored by it. The core-loop of linear progression to improve your item-level is a lot of fun at first. It's fast paced and rewards you often which creates quite the pull to login whenever you can - at least for me. In addition to that you have a number of quirky and funny quests and a lot of ways of what is called "horizontal progression". That ultimately means there are 100s of ways to keep you occupied, some gated by timed spawns or counters on how often you may do them in a day. With all of it there is an rng-element. You may or may not get what you want from that specific location or activity. Which turned out to be my biggest turn-off with the game. I have not reached what a veteran will call the end-game - maybe that would have been fun. I sit at 1340 ilvl roughly and have very little of what i enjoy and a lot which feels like the ultimate grind-simulator. I came for the hardest raids and dungeons with one-shot-wipe-mechanics. I wanted to do those often and get to know people that enjoy it together with me. You can do these things once a week only. Same goes for the raids later in the game. All of it drops materials that you need to upgrade your gear and as you progress, the chance of a successful upgrade of your gear declines to very low percentages. The horizontal progression and chaos-dungeons, boss-rushes, cubes, towers, guardian-raids and what have you are rush-activities. Go in, rush through as fast as you can, claim reward, repeat with an alt. Goal: Farm as many progression-mats as possible.Now you may argue that i approach this wrong and that i should drive around with my boat, do a lot of islands and enjoy leisurely. This is not the type of gamer I am. I look for a challenge. As the key loop in a game. Not a once in a week activity with the rest being farming. So i must ultimately not recommend Lost Ark. It was a fun initial 200h though.
