_childDocuments_.review: To me, the major issue of this game is its gear progression and how to achieve it. It is a RNG based honing system with pity success, and all group contents are gated behind said system. It respects your time by not introducing any durability or downgrade mechanism, not like other Korean MMOs. But to feed this system, game also demands a lot of your time running tedious tasks to collect materials, in later stage. This game has a long honeymoon period till player reaching gears core 1385. Before 1385, there are various mats injections to help a new player progressing in vertical content. It is casual friendly and I enjoyed it very much. Passing this milestone, player would have to gamble on a 10-25% success rate to reach next milestone 1445. I assume it would be much difficult from there to 1460. At this point, failure of honing is increasingly expensive both on mats and gold, hence previous mats injections wouldn’t make any meaningful impact on gear progression. The designated play style starts to reveal itself. This game is expecting player to maintain 3-6 alts to funnel one main character. I would spend 3 hours per week to finish raids in all my characters, this was the joy. The rest of my playtime was collecting quest items to turn in, and mindlessly farm waves of mobs in all my alts, this made the majority of game experience. It feels like a chore, more so every passing day. All the time sink is to hit one success, +2.5 gear score, approximately every week. If you enjoy KMMO with a RNG honing system, this game could be your crown jewel. I certainly would choose it over BDO. However, if you are in favor of western style MMOs, such like ESO/WOW/FF14, avoid this game IN ITS CURRENT FORM. Rather than playing group raid or Mythic dungeon to progress, you will be doing chore for 1-3 months only to unlock a raid. Judging by the pace the game is releasing its raids, one in March, one in May, another one incoming in June, you will be constantly catching up, to an extent that the chore itself becomes the game, or pay to skip.

_childDocuments_.review: The thing about Lost Ark is, it can be fun. You can have a great time exploring the world of Arkesia and discovering the secrets hidden in all the areas. Combat is flashy, some set pieces are truly breathtaking and is just a game to play and not to think much.The problem is that the game is a mess right now. Servers in Europe are overcrowded making the Login experience a nightmare during prime time with queues of up to 3 hours, matchmaking for endgame activities doesn't work most of the time, Crystaline Aura (A paid subscription service) dissapears sometimes and you are left there without the beneffits you paid for.This game needs time to breathe and Amazon has already stated they are not going to solve the most important problems cause they cant. They will not fix matchmaking, they will not fix the overcrowded servers, so my recommendation to you is wait. Some people will go and tell you "they don't have a problem", which is good for them I guess, but this release was an absolute mess and the worst hit was taken by the people who actually supported the game before it was even released by actually paying for the founder's packs.I hope the game stabilizes at some point so everyone can have a good experience, cause right now is far away from that.Edit with 125 more hours in the game: As many F2P games, the beginning is nice and fun and you get a lot of stuff and you feel powerful. But then you reach the wall that makes you feel like you are not doing enough.You have an incredible array of customization, but there is when the grind happens and the grind is incredibly tedious. They are doing events, trying to counter the negative perception from the players, but the grind is there.You want to upgrade your gear? First grind the materials, only to discover that after a few upgrades, your chances of upgrading a piece of gear drop significantly, meaning you can fail at it. So you have to grind more and everytime you fail a small piece of your soul dies cause why would you add failure to an upgrade system. You can make the upgrade materials rarer, meaning you have to grind more, but make the upgrade be always a success and you remove the frustration completely. Considering you have 7 pieces of gear you can upgrade, just imagine the amount of resources you WASTE.And that is only the progression of your gear. You have so many other frustrating elements, that you realize this is first and foremost a free to play game, where your time is not considered at all. Other games like Warframe, Path of Exile, etc. didn't give this feeling of "time wasted" like Lost Ark does.Then you have certain encounters where have ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ attacks that make the whole experience just not fun. But that only happens when you have played 100+ hours and you are invested in the game. But for me it was the last straw.Unless you like heavy grinding, stay away from it.

_childDocuments_.review: Have never reviewed anything on here, but wanted to for Lost Ark. It's a breath of fresh air among the myriad of MMOs out there. Been playing for the past 24 hours and I'm officially addicted. LA has a decent story -- although, a generic good versus evil premise -- which could use some better writing. But the combat, character building and overwhelming amount of other things to do is where the game really shines. And the creators really put some thought into making unique bosses and monsters that aren't just reskins in each zone you go through. The dungeons don't take too long to queue up or go through. _childDocuments_.review: Had been a pre-launch player after spending a bit for the Silver Founder Pack, but otherwise played with only whatever was available in-game. Played pretty consistently ever since then before dropping the game outright a few weeks ago, so I'll just talk about what I think is most prominent when it comes to the good and bad here.Early on, I would've heavily recommended this game to any starter or veteran MMO fans. Amazing in-combat gameplay that I feel tops the entirety of the isometric ARPG genre. All classes in the game, whether damage, support, or in-between focused, have amazing feel to them, with beautiful sound and serious weight behind all abilities and crazy visuals to boot. These get to take center stage in LA's consistently stunning combat encounters, via dungeons and raids. While it may seem a bit sluggish and lame to many, the story content of LA is also equally spectacular to watch, even if it can be campy or have lulls in between segments, but there are many story climaxes worth experiencing playing from the very beginning to the end. If this were all LA was, then I'd still be playing the thing, and the chance to continue experiencing that amazing gameplay was what kept me going. Until recently though, the grind burnout, plus news for the future of this game, finally put me off from wanting to play again.That's where my final stance comes from, and why I don't recommend this to interested players going forward, especially brand new MMO players. This game burns you out bad, and regardless of people's stances on what the core game grind for powering up is, I just think it encourages bad play behavior to the game populace in general, especially to a Western audience on Global. So much of this game's core progression, leveling your characters, is locked between awful RNG mechanics. Though they've done a lot of streamlining for this since launch, the idea of having to roll against absolutely terrible odds (<5% or lower at late game) on several key gear options (6 armor pieces - with 2 RNG modes a piece) and having to play the game's skill building system "engravings", is just painfully demoralizing and what dropped off a lot of my own friends who used to play this with me. Unless you play a filled roster of characters farming materials daily, you will spend ages trying to meet the level requirements to play the game's star content. Even with the devs adding streamlining features (showering you with materials, "express-passing" select characters to skip low tiers), this hardly solves anything for newcomers to LA with the other dark side of the game, the community. In short, everything in Tier 1 and 2 is basically dead, and even the early-to-mid parts of Tier 3 are also dying out in player participation, which is shame since several amazing scenarios and encounters are in those level zones (Phantom Palace and Alaric abyssal dungeons to name a few). People trying to learn and attempt anything beyond those stages will be stuck looking for fellow newer players, or patient others, to actually participate in the later game "Legion Raids" which basically take the forefront of most players attention. Teachers are far and few for this showy but difficult content, and anyone not teaching or new will not bother accepting other players looking for first-time or low experience players.All-in-all, unless you intend to play LA for the side collection gameplay (which is pretty fun) with no raiding or lategame in mind, you're going to dislike coming to this brand new. And even people looking to focus on those collections will find it hard to do even alone since several aspects of it require others to play with you. And just like Tier 1/2 content, those social areas are also dead or dying too, so no full completions for you. Save your time and sanity, play something else if you're new.If you're not new and thinking about returning to LA, don't. Even the latest Korean news with LA shows almost none of the core issues are expected to be adjusted, with only more of the same coming down the pipe for Koreans and us alike. No amount of new class, raid or summer event announcements could interest me to come back as long as this game's current environment will continue to persist.----June 2024 Update----Half curiosity and half addiction, I decided to reboot the game again after playing several other iso-ARPGs for some time and missing the insane combat and gameplay LArk had to offer before. At the short of everything, I'll simply say, the combat and raiding were as showy and awesome to play and watch as it's always been, so good news there.The rest of it is simply bad news to me and I once again cannot endorse anyone, new or returning, to play LA moving forward, as, like I said before, the future outlook isn't any better by this point. Several new classes and raids have come into the mix over the past year since I bailed, and, while the new classes are fun and interesting, all this potential gameplay is STILL stonewalled hard by the stupidly restrictive progression system in LArk.Primary gear progression, via gear honing, is still absolutely trash at the 1500+ iLVL point, and hell, even 1500 iLVL isn't even good enough to most public groups these days. Hell, old school hard mode content for the first Legion Raid, Valtan, is STILL gated by players playing well above the raid's level requirement, demanding massive overleveling, established card sets, high level gems, and much more. Unless you run a character through an Express pass with support for all those upgrades, you are going to be HARD pressed to find anyone to play, at least in anything PUG. Shoot, I haven't even touched upon the additional layers of gear leveling/upgrading beyond all this nonsense, which, to no surprise, is even more layers of insanely low RNG rates that will just frustrate you to no end.Again, don't play this game. Seriously. This game is a job in itself just to play any of the fun stuff. Stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: I've experienced many MMO launches before, most of them the same, 2-3 hour queues every evening the first few days, some crashes and so on.The positive:- I had no crashes so far and nearly no gamebreaking bugs (game came out 2 years or so ago in Korea so i wouldn't expect less).- They gave a small compensation for their incompetence with the launch (see negative stuff)The negative:- Queues. At least beginning around 16:00 the queues already go up into the thousands, which means a HUGE time to wait. 18k queue? Expect 5 hours (!) until you can play.- Their shop server (the place that not only let's you buy stuff like pets, mounts and so on but also handles if you have an active crystalline aura) is also overloaded. That means that sometimes, your crystalline aura is not active when switching to a character. Also, opening the shop can take a long time (popping up like 6 minutes later without any loading symbol) or just give an error "Shop is under maintainence".- Their community management is unimpressive at best. They could not understand that in EU, people like to play on servers where most communicate in their language, therefore they didn't flag servers with languages. But after the community decided which of the big language groups would go to which server, their CMs happily shared that info. Result: Servers which have an inofficial language are of course even more crowded than the others. Completely unpredictable.- Launch: They decided that just right before the launch they would do a non-critical update, which of course didn't work out as planned. So instead of ending maintainence at 18:00 CET (= planned F2P launch), it ended somewhere at 02:00 next day.Currently, with AGS managing the game, I really cannot recommed anyone to buy it, and even then it is so far only mediocre (although I'm only level 23, so I haven't experienced everything). Story is bland, quests are even blander (at least you don't need to kill 50 x and collect 30 y, it's mostly 1-3, or if you need to collect a higher number the enemies drop a high number), nothing so far really gives it an MMO feeling. Most group activity I had was the 2 world bosses I can reach so far, and there was zero communication or organization necessary for that, not even a group, just players hitting the boss together.

My friends are having a lot of fun with the game even if not all of them are hugely into MMOs and I think that too is a very good selling point that Lost Ark has, it manages to be captivating without losing the essence of an MMO for those who are genre veterans.Only downside I'd say is the gender-locked classes, but the characters are so beautiful that it probably won't bother you too much :)(EDIT: I've played for a lot longer in the meantime and I've reached max level and just finished Rohendel and I can safely say that I 100% recommend this game. The grind is pleasant, the world is amazing and it feels like the game never ceases to surprise you with little hidden things here and there, most of them pretty entertaining and exciting. _childDocuments_.review: Updated!Skip to the end if you want the TL;DREverything is daily gated.Only cheap way to overcome this is to create more alts so you can do more dailies.After a certain alt count, your social life will be gone so it's a very risky gamble.The other solution is to pay to skip or whatever you name it but it is worth noting that no matter how many whales there are, most content in the game is singleplayer except weekly raids. Whales can not really harm you in anyway. They just get to endgame content faster.Edit 2: After playing for another 800h, I can say that whales start interacting heavily with you in terms of GvG events such as: Adventure Island Rushes, World Boss Kills, GvG PvP events. These are the only places whales cause problems to players.They also buy out your equipments for absurd prices and provide money so it is a weird ecosystem. Dislike other mmos like Neverwinter, whales do not manipulate the market heavily. Undercutting is also prevented because you lose a percentage of coins putting your items up for sale everytime. So canceling the posted item is bad.Edit 1: Whales do not manipulate market heavily because you can't really undercut the market or manipulate it without "pheons" and losing money everytime you pull out an item from sale to put it for a lower or higher price.Queue times are really short on almost every content. Only low level field dungeons don't have players in 'em. Because everyone progresses quickly in a few days to next levels.The endless G button mashing (to skip dialogue) during the first 50 levels and 4 continents, the game actually stops giving you intros and tutorials. And rewards you with two character boost tickets so that you can play another class if you don't like your initial one. So the rest is on your shoulders to explore.About PvP: First of all classes are not balanced properly, not everything is equally powerful. Matchmaking is an enormous part of the problem. Enemy team can have 2 sups 1 heavy dps while you have nothing. Also player ranks in PvP are matched poorly. 2 bronze players with 1 gold on each team etc. Its like 1vs1 with 2 minions at some points. I even won a game 2vs3 when a teammate disconnected... So no, I dont recommend pvp of lost ark anymore. Its more of a COPIUM/hope it gets better scenario.So as every other mmorpg, this game wants your daily commitment as you get closer to endgame. But it is less of a grind, more of a tenacious timegated content chasing.Simply put:----------------------After giving up 1k hours to complete almost every collectible in the game and playing 5 different classes, I can safely say thatIf you are not into grind and enjoy solid pvp you should stick with pvp of it.Edit 3: 200+ pvp matches, I can EASILY say it's horrible.If you are casually playing games, 2-3 hours max every day, this is also not bad for this game as your content takes around 1 hour every day + a few weekly events that take longer (unless you have more than one character.)If you want something more traditional where you kill tons of monsters for hours like Black Desert Online, this game is not your thing. It is not that kind of game.Edit 4: I dont even recommend the game anymore. I'm sticking around because I've maxed out everything I possibly could and lost track of real life concerns while constantly trying to catch up with daily/weekly quest rotations before every daily/weekly reset and min/max everything I can so I can survive as a F2P player (But I had to pay for some costumes at some point because I was tired grinding gold for it). PvP never got better, PvE content is being fed with a small spoon that comes every few months. And to get the new PvE contents' gear, you need to kill the same boss for 6-8 weeks continuously. If you have more than one character, it becomes a heavy burden. If you try not to play the game, it feels like you're left behind of your friends and guildies.Legion raids are really fun and requiring your skill but its not worth all this grind. Some may argue that time management is my fault not the game's designs but bear in mind that players will gatekeep you from joining their parties and groups by looking at your gear, level and roster level and even achievements and titles. Apart from all that, wanting to play more than one character shouldn't create such a heavy burden on players' shoulders. Wish the game was handled better than this, wish the chaos dungeons and guardian raids didn't have to be killed twice a day and only once. Wish pvp wasn't so horribly balanced and matchmaking didn't suck.If you still want to play the game, I suggest you don't heavily commit.

_childDocuments_.review: Update (2/13) - I've levelled up 3 more times and the second area seems to have better enemy spawns in terms of health and overall number of them. Combat feels more balanced and I can finally see my Sorceress's spell variants take effect through burning and electrocution. Unfortunately, I still feel very disconnected from the storyline so far, and I think that's because of the fluctuating sense of urgency? One moment, we're dealing with a demon invasion of the first city, then the next everything is suddenly fine after a duel visually similar to HP vs Voldemort in the Deathly Hallows movie.Original review: (2/12)The 70 gigs this game takes up is like 99% graphics and 1% fun.Any enjoyment I could've had was doomed from the get-go since the animations outside of combat are questionable and classes (even subclasses) are gender locked. For example, female gunners are royally screwed since they only have access to ONE subclass out of four. Mages, assassins, and 3/4 of martial artist are locked in as female, whereas warriors and 3/4 of gunner are locked in as male. I'm not going to get into the sexualization argument, though it's worth mentioning that some of the animations for female characters either seem like they hurt or just don't make any sense. (i.e. sliding down a carved stone slope in high heels, which every female class starts with, awkwardly climbing up a ledge, and the walk cycle with excessive hip swaying)Character customization is actually pretty good, and the combat animations are visually satisfying. The story cutscenes for each class have interesting implications and feature some pretty major events, but as I went through each class's backstory, it made me kinda mad that we didn't get to play through those events as our character. Drawing off the mage's backstory specifically, protag is in the middle of an initiation ceremony where she inherits the soul of a long-dead but powerful archmage, then demons show up to interrupt and steal said archmage's soul. Protag gets to go on a quest to protect the city from the demon invasion, then tear through the demon horde to reclaim the archmage's soul. They just tell you all of this and throw you into the subclass test area. After you lock in a subclass, you get to start the prologue which has you on a boat as a mercenary(?) escorting some treasure hunters to a mysterious island rumored to have, well, treasure.Including the prologue, the quests so far have been "go to X place and speak with Y" or "go here and interact/fight these things." I'm not just talking about side quests, this applies to the main questline as well. I leveled up 3 times in a couple hours, enough to get 15 skill points, and since the power scaling is so high for players it didn't feel like any of the spell evolutions impacted my gameplay at all. Normal mobs die in like 1 or 2 hits max, and bosses last longer only because they have like 15 health bars.All in all, I'm disappointed that lost ark isn't as fun as it looks. There's potential in the idea and systems set in place, but... man. If you have fun playing this, good for you, I'm not writing this to miraculously convince you the game is bad. I just found the game lacking after experiencing the above, and if others decide not to play after reading or doing other research, that's their choice.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun. The combat is extremely good, and the raids are interesting. However, it uses a multitude of mechanics which are designed to make the game extremely grindy as well as gambling mechanics which are put in place to encourage you to spend money on the game, including vertical power gain (pay to win) though it is possible to progress without spending money.The game starts as a chore getting to lv. 50, which is where the real content starts. It's very fun for a while as you start playing the end-game content. However, to progress in the endgame you have to upgrade your gear which requires materials obtained from time-gated fights (twice per day) and the more you upgrade your gear, the greater the chance is that the upgrade fails and you lose the materials, slightly increasing the chance of success the next time you try to upgrade. There is also a stronghold where you can research upgrades which slightly increase upgrade chances, or craft items required for raids. These upgrades take time (hours to days) to unlock once you start them, and require energy and materials to begin. Energy has a max and replenishes over time, simply one more time-gate which encourages you to spend money on items to restore it so you can continue researching/upgrading. Resources are gained in a time-sink by going to areas and mining/chopping trees/fishing etc. and uses life energy, another time-gating mechanic to prevent you from being able to farm as many resources as you want in a day. Basically, it uses predatory mobile game mechanics all over the place.The game encourages you to play on your alt characters to do additional daily chaos dungeons (an area where you mindlessly kill hordes of weak mobs) so that you can send the time-gated rewards to your main and continue progressing. Additional alt character slots can be purchased from the store. The entire thing is designed to frustrate you so you'll send them the numbers on your plastic. Generally speaking, I'd recommend playing a different game. This isn't the WoW killer, and it's probably not worth your time.

I have played this game as a casual player (2-3 hours a night) and it's been fine to do and I am around 1440 item level with 0 money invested. Its grindy but just the right amount and fun to grind with friends. I recommend this game to anyone. Now, this is when the negative comes in. Once you reach a high level and get to a higher point in the end game, you are going to get stuck by a pay wall or an grind wall. You will need to grind it out to get materials and GOLD. Gold is hard to get much of and this is an issue. I am stuck because I do not have enough gold to do honing to level up. The grind gets to a point where you  just get annoyed and I am at this point. The season pass you buy as well now doesnt give any gold so cant get it from there either. You NEED to play hours on hours to be able to hone. ALSO, this game is gambling. When you spend gold and materials on honing, it wont be successful  all the time. This means you could spend your real money to level up and not even level up. So that make me not want to spend money in the slightest. This aside, there is still so much you can do without gold but you just cant level up which in my opinion is dumb. I wish we could get gold with challenges and not just need to spend money or hours of time to do 1 honing to not even be successful. TLDR: Play it, youre gonna like it. When you beat the game and you have no more honing materials, you are going to stop wanting to play the game. Gamba game that makes you sad.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Laughably low QoL for a 2022 MMO. I would rather be playing a dead game like WoW, at least it feels like systems make sense. System bloat in this game is on an obscene level and what's funny is how clunky it all is. Even the first event they dropped: you can only do minigame once every two hrs, u get a couple min window to enter mini game. To enter minigame, u need a quest. But that quest is only available to one character at a time. So say you're on at the right time, at the right place, and you wanna do the event. Ope sorry! Your main has the quest in their log, so you can't race. Or maybe it's an alt. Hop through all your characters and search through the congested quest log to see if you can find it, abandon it, hop back over to the character outside the event, pick up the quest, and try and jump in. Hope you did that within 1 minute, otherwise it's another two hour wait for the stupid event minigame. Highly unpolished in lots of regards, plagued by bots, and overall just corny. Generic weeb ♥♥♥♥. The devs cannot seem to be clear on anything. Tons of people are pissed about not getting the reward for logging 20 times this daily reward cycle, because we all assumed that since it said the cycle last till 3/10, we would be able to claim the big final reward on the 10th. 6 weeks of logging in for the mount, basically wasted.You buy a founder's pack, you can't even preview the gear. You have to find a third party model viewer. Then they give out an extra one: how nice right? Except the free one can't be dyed, arbitrarily. The devs are too lazy to correct the right item ID when doing this. This is a perfect example of gross oversight of basic little details. Amazon is making TONS of cash off this game, yet they can't even be bothered to use common sense. Generally, the game is ok. You'll have fun. It's worth exactly $0.00 and will likely become pay to win. There's already reddit posts from people who have played like maniacs that cannot progress their gear fast enough to keep up with content releases. The pain in the ass p2w mechanics scale seemingly exponentially for gear progression; something to keep in mind for those interested in end game/PvE.Fine to fill the time, but don't waste your money. _childDocuments_.review: It's good, it's bad, in an free mmo and a Korean one at that.+Combat is satisfying, skill matters (later), I've heard some people complained about leveling being boring but I decided to go full def as a gunlancer and I enjoyed my time, it was engaging enough to keep me pushing forward.+PVP is balanced, no pay2win mechanics here! At least for now..+Respecing your character is free so you can always try new things out without a worry in the world.+Abilities have tiers and perks which can completely change how they work or their elements. Awesome thing+You can exchange gold which you earn in the game by playing and farming for crystals and then buy crystaline aura (basically a monthy sub) with it and other p2w features. Pretty dandy!+Personally I think the endgame is FUN! There's a lot of collectables, achievements, exploring, etc!+Even though it's not an open world, just big locations, the world map is HUGE.+Character creation is good. Sadly I went with la creatura look because I didn't think I'd like this game. My gunlancer looks like a JoJo villian and he's named Budlightnington.+Game is pretty well optimized! You can have hundreds of enemies on the screen and it just works fine! And I have a bad pc, an old hdd, first gen i5, 8gb ram, quadro p2000 and it runs smoothly!+/-The story is.. good with bad elements or bad with good elements, depends on what you like. Personally I believe the writer(s) like their NPCs, the world and it's lore a little too much, so much in fact that that there's a lot of deus ex machina moments and poorly executed ones at that... they could at least go an extra mile and either make the bosses too hard to defeat or scripted so you just can't win. It's weird to basically two-hit KO a boss just to see a cutscene of you getting your butt kicked. Poor execution here.+/-There are so many mechanics in this game it can feel overwhelming. Some are explained, some are not, over all I think the game does pretty good job with tutorials, but it could do better.+/-Up until level 50 you're basically playing a guide. The game actually starts on 50 level. It's hard to count it solely as a con, because I didn't mind the leveling, for me it was fun, although the game lacks challange. It's not as terribly bad as some games, bosses can kick your butt but it's lacking a bit.. And after getting your first character to 50 you can create two characters on 50 level and completely skip the leveling.+/-There is some pay2win BUT it feels more like pay2buytime and it doesn't affect pvp, just pve. I played Korean MMOs before so I am almost certain it will change and p2w will become unbearable. I hope I'm wrong.-Classes are gender locked. Dumb.-Very little armor variation. Classes just get certain looking armors on certain levels.-You start on 10 level, with 50lvl weapon, a handful of abilities and subclass from the get go. Game doesn't explain what the weapon level does, what is the difference between the abilities and you're being robbed of the feeling of achieving something by leveling up and earning your subclass yourself. I am almost sure this wasn't like that 2 years ago when the game originally came out, it feels out of place. Oh, and also you get a new weapon before you had any chance of trying out the old one. Weird game design.-The amount of things to click on the interface.. oh boy. There's so much stuff..-While the servers are full they are just begging to finish them off and end their suffering, It's bad..-I hate those little parkour sections. It's just a scripted little cutscene of your character jumping or climbing. If there was no gap or cliff there in the first place it WOULDN'T CHANGE ANYTHING, the map would be fine. It's just a huge waste of time, sometimes it looks cool, rarely though. It serves no purpose, you have no control over your character so you can't fail, a completely pointless mechanic. Parasitic design by the book.-Some cutscenes are unskippable if you're playing for the first time. -If the servers are so full that you can't even get into the queue THE GAME WILL CLOSE and you'll have to launch it again so you can check if the queues are there. Who designed this and how does he still have a job?-EU version changed some of the NPCs races to pander to the m1norities. Absolutely hilarious and just as pointless.There's probably more but I can't think of anything from the top of my head at this time.Over all I highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: The positives of the game are that the gameplay and classes are actually really fun and if the activities outside of legions, gearing, and release sch of content was good the game would be great.First the game is pay to win, many players will try and claim that it isnt and there is a cap to how much money you can spend on the game. The bottom line is that people who whale and spend thousands on the game will have an inherent advantage over those who dont. In some cases some content being released in windows where only whales have access to said content and if you dont want to whale you are looking at spending hundreds of hours just to keep the gap between you and releasing content within range. Depending on how lucky you are even spending hundreds of hours may not be enough. The events are all the same in the game and there is very little to actually do in the game currently other than the repetitive chores you do on your main and alts every day. The one saving grace in terms of the content in the game is legion raids which are incredibly fun and continuing forward this would make for a great base for the game to improve with more updates. The problem is that smilegate has decided that a slow release of content particularly class release is the way they are moving forward, meaning if there is a class you want to play that you have seen on the korean version of the game then you may not get to play the class until next year.This game could be great the classes are fun and enjoyable if you get to play the class you want. The legion raids are really fun so far. The game is exploitative and the content very repetitive. This is all on top of a massive botting issue in the game because there are a lot of players who apparently think spending $400 a day isnt exploitative enough so they turn to RMT sites in order to get unlimited in game materials to continuously upgrade and put an even bigger distance between themselves and everyone else.If you are looking for a game with a compelling story this is not it. The story is basically set around different continents and each continent is a copy paste adventure of a different already existing game. Want to replay ff7? look no further than arthetine. Diablo 3 more your style feiton has it copied.Ill continue to play the game since I really have nothing else play and have the hope that smilegate will actually improve the game at a good rate rather than drip feed classes. I wouldnt recommend this game to anyone though and if the game continues down this path ill be gone at the first chance when a new mmo comes out or even the new wow xpac.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm editing this review after I hit 4,000 hours played. Here's the shortest version of it:The leveling/lore gathering portion of the game will take many hours and is very chill. If you like mobbing, gathering collectibles, etc - you will enjoy this. The raiding/endgame portion of the game is intense and fun. If you like a challenging action-based game with required teamwork - you will enjoy this.I have spent less money on LA since launch than my first 10 months of WoW. You can grind out the story and probably even do a raid or two pretty easily for free. If you want a game to entertain you for a while, for no money, try it out.That said, the only reason I have 4,000 hours and don't hate the game is that early on I found a guild full of cool people. We regularly do raids together, hang out in Discord and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and enjoy the shared experience of LA's challenging content.Below is my early review left up posterity:The story is generic fantasy sauce. The mechanics are like Path of Exile and Diablo had a baby, and then somebody decided that was too much loot and too much gameplay depth. The graphics are dazzling and flashy, over the top. The voice acting is just shy of bad. The character models are offensively sexualized.But, at least for the leveling period, Lost Ark is too much fun. These stale ingredients were combined in some crafty old lady's kitchen to create a soup I cannot stop eating. The game throws all this stuff at you and then comforts you, reassures you that it's OK if you don't get it right away. And it's not being deceptive.The story I thought was stale and cliche began to suck me in. Like Squid Game, I thought it was a good way to pass the time without paying much attention and before I knew it I was INVOLVED. The cut scenes and movies that I was eager to skip early on became emotionally intense. The mechanics I rolled my eyes at acquired intrigue as the difficulty went from "you don't have to try" to "you do have a try a little more" and I could see the end game on the distant horizon.If you can get past the fact that most of the playable classes are Chun-Li in bondage gear, this is possibly the best FREE game I've ever played, and a pretty good one to sink some money into if you have it.WIll I be bored with Lost Ark in a month? Maybe, but I won't forget my time here.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: As of today AGS has demonstrated way too many times that even a toddler would have better decision making when it comes to publish a game. The game itself is still one of the best I've ever played. However, AGS doesn't deserve a single player to play their games, so if you decide to give it a go, keep that in mind. I will keep playing myself but will not recommend it to anyone to try it out anymore until publisher changes.The game in itselft is absolutely amazing and a enjoyable experience. The combat is super fun and the story is really good. But lets go over it a bit more in depth with negative points other people are rising.It is true that maintenances on EU use very bad times. Last 2 updates have been around 7-8am UTC which is okay-ish but they definitely should invest into regionalized maintenance. EU population is almost twice as big as NA, so the region deserves at the very least that much.The queues are terrible, that's a given. Like in many other MMOs launch the servers cannot handle more people specially since this game was highly anticipated. They are already including a 2nd EU region because the game architecture just do not allow for any more server capacity increase. I am sad to hear that, but we as players need to realize that this isn't up to change as it would mean literally remake the game from scratch. On the other hand, Amazon should have opened way more servers than what they did at the beggining and not now, inexcusable on their part and the other negative reviews are completely justified.The P2W reviews are, honestly, entitled persons. My personal experience has taught me that the amount of money invested into the game gives so small improvements that you would need to have some problems to spend so much money into the game, and it is a PvE game that is balanced around normal people, not whales, you can play literally anything without paying given you play the game. If whales go slightly faster so be it, why are we really caring what other people do with their lives? PvP is completely equalised, no P2W, nothing at all.The game honing / upgrading system is actually very good in comparison to any other game with a similar upgrade system. Items do not break when u fail, they also don't decrease in level and there is a pity cap which guarantees your next upgrade after a few fails. Hitting that pity is hard, like the first 6 upgrades are 100%, up to +10 it is no less than 80% success... Other games barely have a 50% if you are lucky and they decrease the rate a lot faster.In the end the game is F2P, try it if you want. A lot of negative reviews as I've said are justified, but there is also a lot of reviews that just bring up points that have no real foundation and its just for the sake of leaving a bad review because of entitlement or not wanting to inform himself better. The game hitting daily 1 million+ concurrent players speaks for itself about this game, don't let the Steam reviews tell you anything about a game that's one of the most played on Steam, that is also F2P and that has just released. If needed give it some time and come back at it after a few weeks so most critical problems are ironed out. Hope you can enjoy this game, and if not I hope you can find another game that brings you so much enjoyment as Lost Ark brings to its players.

You will spend 80% of your gameplay literally riding a horse between two checkpoints doing basic tasks for NPCs. The other 15% doing one of the tasks listed below. And the remaining 5% actually doing content that involves fighting enemies. These tasks include the following: 1) picking up random objects and slowly carrying them to a random point 2) moving two feet and spending a 5 second channel time interacting with random things 3) watching unskippable cutscenes 4) being a messenger boy/girl between two NPCs or more 5) Use a 5 second animation emote in front of an NPC 6) getting hit by random enemy's that follow you across the map and hit you during object interaction cancelling your channelThis game is a literal walking simulator. People will say this game improves once you hit level 50, it does not. The fun content in the game is limited. And you progress much faster doing random quests on islands that are more of the same story progression quests I listed above. Even at max level, your gear progression will be locked behind these story quests that are completely unengaging boring content.Friends and I played this hoping the co-op content would be fun. Its not. There are so many dumb quests in the game with minimal fighting when you progress that being in a party is completely pointless. Not only this, but most of the "dungeons" in this game force you to play single player content. The most fun content in the game for co-op are weekly raids that last maybe an hour on your first playthrough of them. You can play Chaos Dungeons together, but its basically pointless. Chaos Gates could be fun, but usually there is so many people everything just blows up often before you can deal damage to it. Guardian raids are the last piece of fun co-op content, but you're limited to 2 per day and they are time gated for 20 minutes each, usually able to completely them in about 5 minutes. So you have a total of 10 minutes per day of fun co-op content with the occassional weekly hour long content.Lastly, there are these island quests. These are incredibly annoying. This game has a massive worldmap with islands scattered everywhere. Eventually you're given welcome quests for these islands. However, many of these islands are locked behind random quests to even start them. The very first island I was given on my welcome quest gave some rewards I needed so I tried it out. Spent 10 minutes sailing to the island only to be met with a "you don't meet this quest completion requirement" followed by the name of a random quest where I have no idea where this quest is or how to start it. This is the **very first** island listed on the welcome quest for islands and its locked behind some arbitrary story quest in the game.This game is just bad. Terrible. Not only is the fun content limited, its locked behind 20-25 hours of the most boring gameplay you could imagine, and requires more boring gameplay to progress past Tier 1 of item level. Don't waste your time on this crap, I regret this completely. This game has absolutely 0 respect for your time.

Lastly the RNG progression really drives it home, 4 days of grind if you fail the RNG to upgrade? you lose all the materials.Pros:- Engaging B-roll content (stronghold, rapport if you into that, etc.)- Somewhat engaging story- Gameplay is pretty engaging- Cutscenes look really nice for a 10 year old gameCons:- Outright whale to win (get to end game in 1 day if you spend money)- Lots of cut content, some diversity quotas and some censorship-- Specific character prologue cut from the game so when characters show up later that "know" you it does not flow- No servers for OCE- Boss can wipe you when they are not even in your screen view so you cannot even defend against it (especially true for guardian raids (basically monster hunter))- Need a good guild to tackle any content requiring a semblance of cooperation- Weak willed at best, toxic at worst community (Never say its your first time at an abyss dungeon or they will just quit)- No respect for the player's time (eg having to hike up a mountain for a quest there isnt a tp point there then have to hike up there again to hand it in)- Bots chat spam and currency inflation- Frustrating way of handling gathering and quest item nodes where they are shared so you have to wait for them to respawn- Voice acting leaves much to be desired for english at least- Cuts off last lines of dialogue if you would end up finishing the quest if it would result in a cutscene or instance change (probs a bug)- Tries to explain mechanics that would party wipe while the boss is attacking and via a dialogue box that shows for 2 seconds while right before it starts.- Poor localization, text can be seen to be cut off due to not enough space after translation where it would be placed in the original language.This game has its highs and lows but its lows get so low that I cannot recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I should start by saying I'm not huge on most MMOs, but lost ark has been an exception for me, I like the gameplay, visuals, and even the story. I'll break down some of my likes and dislikes.Likes:Visually pleasing, the depth of each map is insane, it's not game changing but it's nice to see actual effort going into map design to make each area very unique and pretty/creepy/gross depending on the intended feeling.Combat is so much fun, it definitely boils down to hitting the keys over and over but it definitely feels cool blowing someone up and having them actually ragdoll or explode instead of just having a set death animation.Questing, I cannot praise the way they do questing enough. Having side quest not only be easy but also take you in the same areas as your main quest is insanely cool.so, much, content. I am only level 40 and I've already battled huge army's, faught massive demons, disguised as the enemy, sailed across the see, harvested resources and eat "good" cooking. In engine cutscenes, I am a huge fan of the cut scenes being in engine instead of some fancy movie, it makes the game feel more alive. Story,I like that the story is pretty easy to follow even if you skip the dialogue, the cutscenes will fill you in enough to enjoy them, I still felt like a badass knight fighting for my king in a war even though I skipped alot of the lines.And much much more. But for now, on to the dislikesNPC idle lines,When walking through town the same NPC says the same line over and over and it gets very annoying.The game can be very overwhelming at first, which isn't a huge issue but could definitely disenourage new players.Items aren't super unique, I kinda wished gear would look more unique, I think I've only seen like 4 different looks to a item.Overall my only issues come down to very small details that I can see being fixed in time. I'd 100% recommend this game to anyone feeling like they want to play a new MMO9/10 Needs some fixing but overall my top MMO right now.

name: Not Tonight 2
detailed_description: Immigration Enforcement Case #112: You are under arrest. Unless your friends can cross a broken America, retrieve your identifying documents and stay out of trouble... this is the end of the American dream for you. In an alternative broken America, where capitalism and political greed have taken center stage, your friend has gone missing. Snatched during a protest, Eduardo Suarez has been seized by the authorities, and now sits ready for processing in the Miami gulag. Not Tonight 2 is an American document-checking road trip, fusing a time-pressure RPG with a politically charged, dark comedy where every decision matters. Will Eduardo's friends Malik, Kevin and Mari manage to locate and deliver his documents to Miami in time, or is this the end of the American dream? Three compelling stories, written by a team of diverse authors Make your way across America, making terrifying decisions along the way Work the doors of clubs, churches, race tracks, casinos, and cults Check IDS, while completing a variety of silly, poignant minigames Rhythm games, wizard shooting, serving poutine, assessing religion, checking chickens, and more

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first full playthrough, with some re-loading but accepting imperfect plays. A straight playthrough without any reloading or deaths would probably take about 5 hours. Overall, a true sequel to Not Tonight (and Papers, Please). There is more variation in the mini games compared to the original, which got a bit aggravating as they continued adding more things to check etc. This time, each location has different mini-games/requirements, so even if you hate one of them (looking at you, Montana), it's only for a couple rounds. _childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, writing a review for this game feels weird. I very much enjoyed "Not Tonight 1" and was hoping to see big improvements and expansions of game mechanics. The promotional material with the US map and branching roads especially made me think there would be some kind of choices in jobs and places to visit, maybe even re-playability through different paths in which you could stitch together the story after reaching all of them. Alas the game is painfully linear, but it was made from the same recipe than the first game, so i can still somewhat recommend it when taking it out of the context of being a sequel.The good: Gorgeous pixel art like always as well as fitting music. I encountered no bugs and the game ran smooth. Solid core gameplay à la "Papers Please".The bad: No innovation really. The travel map serves more as a tool to facilitate the plot than any meaningful addition to gameplay. There is way less customization and many of the gameplay additions feel gimmick-y, although they kept me entertained enough. You don't really manage much anymore and I am very sad that they dropped the player agency and time management from the first game. Where in the first game you tried to amass money to get cool upgrades and progress the story, money here is relegated to being something you simply need to get on with the linear levels. I get that they wanted to double-down on storytelling and I also get that the absurd politcal landscape of the US lends itself well to that, but this somehow ended up feeling disjointed and weird. The political message is obvious, as is expected if you played the first game, but feels a lot less poignant and stylish. Having this multiple POV story also takes away the very personnal story that was being told in the first game. I have to comment on the big final judgement as well: It is way too easy and there is no way to ♥♥♥♥ it up. In the first game you had to actually somewhat think and work towards getting the good ending Getting some ressources and making good choices is relegated to knowing pop culture trivia and sometimes choices are just opaque and I felt like I had no idea what I was supposed to do. Instead of clever management of time and ressources you now have to remember names, USA trivia and little visual quirks on character and I do not appreciate that as much. But I do understand the devs are trying to do some things different. It is important to note that this sequel is also somehow a lot shorter than the first game, this is compounded by the fact that a quarter or more of your time in this game will be spent reading text boxes. I just listed a lot of negatives, but I still recommend this game. My personal dissapointment stems mostly from a lack of innovation and a departure of many more complex aspects of the first game, as well as US politics as the story backdrop, something I am just so incredibly tired of as it is just everywhere. The gameplay still makes it a fun ride, but I truely hope they try to actually expand things for the next game and make things more complex and engaging. TL;DR: As a fun little game? I think it's okay. As a sequel? I don't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is inferior to the original in every aspect.Unlike the first game, it is completely linear, and there is no choice about where you are going to work, or if you should skip work. Being unable to skip work implies that your health drops everyday and there is no way to stop it. The only way to recover health is completing MapO quests. However, if you fail these specific tasks, in which it's not always clear what you must do, you won't be able to heal, and you will end up dying because the health drops to zero. In this case, you essentially soft locked and forced to restart from the previous chapter, since the MapO rewards are only received in the end of the chapter and health drops 10 points everyday before that.While health is very difficult to recover, you make money from work everyday and there is no real use for it. In the original game, there was an urgency to make enough money and pay the debt until a deadline as reached. You could also buy useful upgrades for your job as a bouncer. In the sequel, money is only used to buy cosmetics and doesn't help you at all. There is no way to use it to buy items that improve your health, like the heating and the bed from the original game.Most of the plot is inexplicably told through text, so it's up to you to imagine what is happening in the story. Unlike the original game, there are no cutscenes. They have been replaced by a map interface that always shows up when you are not working as a bouncer. This is a really poor choice by the developers, because, while the map looks nice, it has no practical use. You can't choose your destination, because the story is completely linear. I would rather have the visual storytelling of the original game rather than this map and narrative through text that just feels lazy. As a matter of fact, the lack of so many features from the first game in this sequel make the entire experience feel rushed and unfinished.If you are a fan of the first game, I don't recommend buying this one. You would be better off playing something like .

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game an above-lukewarm thumbs up. Regardless of one's political leanings, I believe most people can agree that everything across the board has been exaggerated to the point of farce. And that's okay! Farce in itself is not bad, I found it enjoyable and amusing enough, save for the odd moments where the game tries to take itself too seriously. At one point you have a character grappling with having killed a man/seen a man murdered in front of him, then almost immediately after you're checking the IDs of chickens for nugget processing. There was a lot of hype regarding the diverse cast, but like most everything in the game, the experiences portrayed were all very, very surface-level. None of the protagonists' unique circumstances manifest themselves in a narratively or mechanically meaningful way. The astonishingly uncritical, pretty much all positive portrayal of the "hip" tech CEO manipulating politics and monopolizing everything was particularly baffling, though I suppose they know their market and publisher. (a character toothlessly, vaguely griping every so often about how it's kinda creepy is not substantive)The gameplay's simple: approve or rebuke a given number of folks in a time limit based on the level's criteria, usually with a tacked on minigame. I played on hard mode and only had to redo a few levels, mostly because a few of the minigames were primarily reliant on chance. Engaging enough, if not particularly challenging. These segments are broken up by text segments with the occasional blatantly obvious choice or blatantly obvious inventory decision. The characters in the text portions are mostly broad-strokes; no one's very deep here, not even the protagonists. There's the pretense of having to manage stats and money, but even on hard mode I'll admit I didn't even really have to think about those at any point. You do the easy "action" segments well, pick the obviously correct choices in dialogue, and that aspect of the game will literally never give you any challenge.There are some technical things that could use improvement: Audio settings are not saved between sessions, which is a pain. The delay for text boxes and texts in the in-game phone are a touch long, and needless inventory items linger throughout the whole character's playthrough, perhaps to add some artificial difficulty. Overall, I'd say the game has an identity crisis, I want to like it more because I find the core gameplay loop of the action segments enjoyable, and find farce an underutilized genre. There's a lotta fun ideas and aesthetic designs here! But the work itself and the marketing cannot decide whether it's an all-out farce or a darkly comedic political look at the logical conclusions of real world issues. It cannot decide if it wants to be an adventure game, it cannot decide what it wants its story to be and say, and it cannot decide on what level it wants to engage the player.

_childDocuments_.review: This recommendation is really two-sided, because on one hand I recommend this game, but on the other not really.As from a person, who really loved the original Not Tonight and the DLC, this game was kind off a let-down. It is a good bouncer simulator, but less charming and likeable as the first one. First of all, the positives why I would still recommend the game. The gameplay is still the same, fantastic, ID checking madness. The new location quests give a good challenge to the game, figuring them out is sometimes quite fun (even though some of them are a bit nonsensical). I liked the location designs, they were unique and quite authentic (besides some). The OST is great as usual, great electronic and house music mixes all around, with multiple other genres making an appearance. The gameplay loop is solid as always, some of the new mechanics are really creative and fun (and some of them are an annoying pain). The roadtrip core idea is really interesting and quite cosy, you could immerse yourself into it (for the first roadtrip).Now, the negatives. The story is completely devoid of charm, likeable characters or interesting plot points. Not to mention, that even though the first NT felt somewhere a bit overexaggerated, this whole game feels like that. I don't like when stories reflect the developers' political views and they distort reality to fit their views. The first NT was depressing and overlooming, really immersive in feeling like an outcast in oppressed society. But this story, is just shocking for the sake of being shocking and mocking one certain side, huge dislike. (Also why was club rock music playing in the border, where you literally stopped people from emigrating. The Wall in 1 was authentic, depressing, you could feel the people's pain and this is just ???) Second, some gameplay mechanics are simply annoying or outright broken (looking at you musical tickets). They are not fun at all and just make it hard and tedious of A-ing some of the stages. Also some of the dialogue choosing mechanics don't make any sense and sometimes if you choose the wrong one you have to replay the whole night just for the A mark quest. Also, the absence of the custom character mechanic is just bad. I understand that they wanted to make the game focus around other characters as a normal story, but when the characters are not fledged out or interesting enough, you can feel the sting of it's disappearance. Also also, why were the hotkeys removed? They just made the game 10x more annoying, because of misclicks and whatnot.In conclusion, Not Tonight 2 is a good successor to 1 on gameplay front but stumbles in everything else. I would recommend it as a one-play game if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I've 100% both the first and the second game and personally liked the original Not Tonight way more. The second game appears to be more... superficial? casual? sometimes boring? Not really sure how to describe it.Plenty of challenging "paperwork" stuff got substituted by no-brain mini-games, the ones you could probably encounter in hypercasual mobile products. There are three protagonists, each doing the very same thing but in different cities. Almost each city is strictly 2 identically structured levels (the first one is normal, the second one is with VIP / guest list) and you move through those cities relatively quickly and do somewhat the same stuff all over again (check IDs for the very same issues mostly), but now with a different mini-game to "play". Like hold the button pressed for a couple of seconds to fill the Oxygen container or hold the button pressed for a couple of seconds to fill the car with gas, Or give a person one of the three items depending on their "level". On top of that, two of the mini-games have random mechanics in them, as in you have very little control over the results and have to wait the long animation while the card or the dice plays out. Definitely not something I enjoyed.The story seemed alright, although not as engaging as the one from the first game, in my opinion. I also encountered a recurring bug with the Oxygen refilling mini-game in all of my three Mari playthroughs: after you place the Oxygen Container into the corresponding place to fill it from one of the three Oxygen Tanks, the container might start flowing around and therefore you can't really measure the filling rate properly, because the measuring limit flows stays in the place, while the container filling meter flows around with the container itself.Nonetheless, the game is still OK, but if you were to play both the first and the second games, I think I'd rather recommend to play Not Tonight 2 first for a more casual and mediocre experience and then play Not Tonight 1 for a more deep and meaningful experience (and then enjoy Papers, Please for a really hardcore dessert, hehe).
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: While I won't say this game is terrible, but coming from the first game this one just...isn't it. the progression system lost something. I'm almost through one section of potentially 3 of the game and there have been no upgrades. The timed choices leave something to be desired for many reasons: A. There are multiple screens to click through so you may end up progressing the text and land on a timed choice without knowing. B. Not everyone reads as fast or can process things as fast when they read them. While I didn't have that problem, I know some who might... C. not very friendly for those who their first language might not be the ones that are provided. D. Just WHY? Like I get you might be forcing people to commit but never have or never will like timed choices.I loved the charm of getting to see the inside of the pubs, bars, etc that I visited in the first game as well as getting to talk to the boss and earn double the cash and a prize if I achieved head doorman. I hate that most of this game is done via a beige box full of text and character portraits.  I do understand that the map being the "homebase" sort of place is understandable because of the setting and the story but I feel so very disconnected from everything...and okay I guess in a round about way that does very much describe my experience living in America but idkDo not come in expecting to have more of the charm you got in the first game and usually I try NOT to come at things expecting the exact same thing but unfortunately I'm not a fan of the progression system, how the story is told, the environments, the addition of character portraits, the music or even the bouncer tasks. Beware the wannabe rhythm game section as it comes with 0 forgiveness and laggy timing. It's been too long to request a refund so I will attempt to see this game through and may come with more thoughts as I go along. This game is mostly positive so it obviously was a hit with some but it was definitely a miss for me.Edit: So In fantastic style I'm almost through the second part of the game and I continue not caring much for the bouncer tasks. You have to play hi-lo at a casino to let people in and I was thrown back to my dad playing an ad-ridden game on his cellphone. Also I think another thing that gets me is the tone in this one is much more serious and less satire. Like the subject matter was a serious sort of subject matter in the first one but there was a lot more weirdness and satire going on in that one. I will say that it wouldn't specifically fit with the story they have painted to do that here but IDK. The jobs are teethgrinding, there's no real progression and the story is pretty depressing honestly. This is something I might be more into if I was looking for a game like Not Tonight but...yknow wasn't actually Not Tonight. I wanted more quirky satire but honestly I'm wishing I could go back to before I had more than two hours in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: it's not as good as the first imo. it's more like a visual novel compared to 1, and there are no upgrades to make bouncering easier like unlocking hotkeys or something new like to make people wait in line longer without getting angry. instead i suppose it keeps things fresh by introducing a new gimmick with every bouncer location you get a job at, however these gimmicks are not always good; the rhythm minigame in new york/that other city was annoying, but not as crap as the hi-lo minigame in vegas, or the dice roll ♥♥♥♥ in the vr section and the robots in the 3rd roadtrip story. at least the rhythm tickets relied on skill, i'm not down for minigames based on pure rng and luck.anyway with that said, if you can get it during one of the big sales and you've already played 1, i'd say it's worth getting, just keep in mind it is very short so don't go expecting to get more than 15-20 hours out of before 100%-ing it. however, if all you want is a game like papers please and you haven't played not tonight, buy that instead

_childDocuments_.review: I can't really recommend this game. The original Not Tonight is so much better in every aspect it's not an exaggeration.-The characters were better.-The gameplay was better.-The story was better.You don't spend enough time with anyone to really get to know them, and the core gameplay loop makes it impossible to come to know any of them.Each location has a gameplay gimick that is unique to the area and nowhere else. Except for two mechanics that pop up one additional time. Gone are the mass of papers you need to quickly sift through to get enough people in before times up, welcome Dance Dance revolution.The story is split into three chunks, three acts like the original, each act is it's own story and is almost entirely disjointed from the rest of the acts. Acts 1 and 2 take place simultaniously and you can see the progress the other is making in your current act through the text messages. Act 3 is easily the worst the game has to offer. It's the only act that actually uses the map for some gameplay in avoiding Martyr agents wandering the map that you have to avoid or else get an instant game over. The story was passable, but slowly became absolutely forgettable. I don't like this game, I don't think it's very fun, I'd rather play Not Tonight 1 than play this again

_childDocuments_.review: This is the sequel to Not Tonight. Many differences from the original, but those differences are what make this game unique and interesting. Similar concept to Papers, Please, but you play as three different bouncers, unlike the first game. This, already, is a new concept. At first, I thought that this might make the storytelling confusing, as this game is much more story-oriented than the first game, but no, it was well-delivered and easy to follow. You play as one bouncer (Kevin) until their journey ends, then you play out the other (Malik), and lastly the third one (Mari). Each stopping spot/location has its own unique task on top of the regular ID checking part. For example, you would be providing poutine sauce to customers at one stop, then you would be doing dice battle against bots, and at some point you would be filling gas for people. Overall, it is not too difficult to understand, and there are two guides (English) there to help you complete the game without too much sweat. If you wonder whether this is a confusing concept, I would rather say it makes the game less of a bore, and it is not that hard to understand at all.In terms of difficulty, I played on the regular mode, which is not supposed to be too difficult, and it was actually very easy in my opinion. I personally would recommend this gamemode because anything easier than this might just be way too easy, but it could well be just me for being familiar with the gameplay already. For your reference, I managed to complete every shift but only one without a problem. Customers push over way less often than the last game, which is great as it saves you a few seconds for the next person in line. In the original Not Tonight we had people pushing over almost all the time you deny them, which makes it annoying if you wish to achieve the highest grade for the shift.To conclude whether this game is worth trying if you have already played through the first game, it is a definite yes from me. The gameplay is refreshing thanks to all the new features, and the story definitely plays a huge part as well. Kudos to the developers, you have made one fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is AMAZING I just finished my first complete playthrough of Not Tonight 2, and I am in love. The story is amazing, the game isn't too long or too short. Just overall amazing.Here's my basic rundown of how I think the game is.STORY { 10/10 }OH BOY. The story for this game is absolutely top tier. It's well thought out, the different stages of the game flow together really nicely, it's just an amazing story. I found myself being lost in the story, not being able to just stop playing. I was captivated by the story-line, wondering what's gonna happen next. And frankly, it was super nice being able to see exactly how my decisions affected the story, at least a little bit.GAME MECHANICS { 8/10 } The game mechanics to Not Tonight 2 aren't bad ! You use your mouse the entire game, which isn't bad at all, especially if you're just trying to relax and game. It would be really easy for someone who has never played a pc game in their life to play. The only issue I had, was I could use shortcuts on my keyboard, such as setting a key on my keyboard to pass people quickly. Other than that though, I had no complaints.CHARACTERS { 10/10 }Every single character I met (good, bad, neutral) were all well designed. They all had so much character to them, all had amazing dialogue, and even the lore to the characters was beautiful and neatly made. I have no complaints whatsoever to any of the characters and their designs.WORTH THE MONEY? ABSOLUTELY. I think if you're looking for a new game to play by yourself, go for it. And, as a small streamer, I recommend it to stream. They even have a streamer friendly option for the music, so you don't have to worry about copyright !! It's a small game that could run easily on any pc/laptop (unless you're still using an ancient computer).OVERALL, I think this game is wonderful. I can definitely see myself coming back to play it anytime. Plus, as of this review, I have 8 hours on the game. And that was enough to complete the game completely. So, although it is a short game, and you can probably speed run it much faster than me, I believe it would make for an amazing stream ! Or just a nice short game for you to play if you're trying to relax. And of course, at the end, well all I've got to say is.... Glory to Arstotzka!!!

_childDocuments_.review: And we're back, ladies and gentlemen! This time, our favourite Arstotzkan immigration officer takes over three young fellas from the (remains of the) US of A. I really like some of the levels and ideas, but I feel like the pace of the storytelling doesn't feel right. In the previous game, you have like a month to achieve certain things. Here, you've only got two days and most of them are in the character conversations. I might have to say the previous game's story mechanics are a bit better.That being said, I quite enjoyed the story being told from three different perspectives. It's really a nice addition. I also recognized a few familiar faces from the previous game.I really liked the gameplay and the music I hear in this series of games. It's the main appeal for me, and I'm glad they kept this style. I hope they would make more improvements for the third game (if any).9/10 MapO A Grades.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game is odd. if I an an option for "meh" - I would choose that.I would've spent much less time in the game if I hadn't reloaded a bunch trying to get the "right" things - but it turned out for the most part, not messing up didn't impact anything. A really big thing is that this game has pretty much nothing in terms of accessibility options outside of colorblind mode. If you have any motor disabilities, this game will be incredibly difficult - it almost entirely involves using the mouse and being able to move it quickly, even for tasks that could EASILY allow button presses like the counter, or the drum machine, or the arrows (or similar things in different areas). The story is pretty decent - I never played the first one, but this felt like a watered down Papers, Please - traveling around felt sort of unnecessary, and the traveling in the third roadtrip just got annoying when you had to look at the map and attempt to see all of the lines when people were in the way of them. It would've been better if it had stuck to text and said "Oh, he went north, then southwest, then east" instead of the arrow system. If you're looking for another Papers, Please and really want a similarish game to play, get this.I got the game for $14.99 on the Steam Summer Sale and I feel like I sort of got my money's worth, but it feels sort of... hollow now that I finished the game.If I were to give this a true number ranking (and not the gamer rankings where if it isn't a 9 or a 10, it sucks), I would give it a 6/10, as it was mediocre. It wasn't bad, but it wasn't great.The pixel art was cool and the voices were distinct, so I could differentiate between the characters.

_childDocuments_.review: 3/5 Get it if you want or if you’re thinking, the game is honestly carried by the gameplay and art which are pretty important all things considered. A decent sequel to the first Not tonight, takes place in the USA as it essentially crumbles. Which is ew the USA sucks. If you haven't played the first not tonight you don't need to play it to play this game, but you probably should just play it to get the references and to get a better hang of gameplay. Both games are very reminiscent of 'Papers, please' which I loved they even had a thank you to 'papers, please' and Lucas Pope for the inspiration. Get the game if you really liked the first Not Tonight and Papers, please. If your on the edge just try papers, please first. The story is fine, but lackluster. There is a lot going on for it, all to amount to what I felt like wasn't much. Also way too much dialogue, so much dialogue, it was honestly the biggest thing that turned me off the game. The dialogue was getting a bit repetitive and boring. I do appreciate all the satire surrounding american politics and the current climate of many areas. So many subtle things that were great which were then ruined by the dialogue explaining/pointing out the satire. The loop of checking for different things as a bouncer is fun, they usually cycle in new gimmicks per area which are a gamble whether their good or not. Some of the gimmicks were pretty fun and some were making me suffer like the one where you had to hit according to a beat and it didn't help that it was also somewhat bugged. The game doesn't give you much time to really enjoy any of the fun gimmicks though.  Backgrounds and pixel art are really good, but the profiles are ugly. The backgrounds are all really cool and are one of the things I most anticipated when arriving in a new area. Every area had a new song which was cool and a lot of them complimented the area, but most of the songs were pretty annoying and I ended up muting a lot of them. No voice acting but the characters did make sounds which were super annoying especially Kevin who had a squeaky voice. Somewhat fun, made me want to play the original Not tonight again. Relatively bugless, but there is one issue with the IDs. Since the pixel art isnt very detailed (which would have been fine) some characters will have a slight difference between their ID and it will be very difficult to tell the difference (if the ID is fake or not). I've also gotten plenty of IDs with the only difference being a hat or earrings and they were somehow fake. They also didn't learn from the first game on the denying issue. Kicking someone out for having fake paperwork takes way too long which sucks when you are trying to beat the clock. I remember seeing a review saying that it would be faster to just let someone in and take the penalty than it is to kick someone out which is completely true. You also don't get paid for people you kick out so if you get three fake IDs back to back you could be screwed on some levels which sucks. Either make kicking out people faster or pay us for kicking people out with fake papers.Overall, decent game and a great addition to the paperslike genre. I've named it that and you can't stop me.Theres also no infinite mode? I 100% the game and there is no infinite mode given at the end. Super dissapointed.Also what's with the lighter?? Its the desktop logo and its being thrown by Kevin on the banner, but there is no lighter that plays any important part? Sometimes you can catch people with lighters, but they play no role in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Coregame remains, but is more varied due to new, different minigames. This time, the action takes place in the United States. Not Tonight 2 addresses a number of political issues in its usual sarcastic manner. Examples include deportations, religious fanaticism and land grabbing. In contrast to the first part, the developers now indirectly force the player to actually follow the story: If you don't pay attention to the conversations that tell the story, you'll miss the solutions that are required at certain points to be able to complete an area with "A" - the best rating. Of course, as before, you can load an older save point and try again. Reading helps though ^^
