_childDocuments_.review: This is worth playing if you like games like Papers Please and the first Not Tonight. _childDocuments_.review: Not Tonight 2 is the same as the first game, but fixes a bunch of issues that the first game had, and is a more "clean" experience.If you played the first game, but want more, buy this instead of the overpriced dlc the first game had.The game now has you work only 2 nights per location instead of 5.This small change fixes the pacing issues the first game had, but at the same time it makes the game feel like an arcade adventure experience rather than a "bouncer"-"papers, please" sim, and honestly i prefer this change, HOWEVER, i do wish that they would add a "endless mode" of some sort.The story is fun, it's nice, is it as good or better than the first game's story? well, that's debatable, but a sequel does not have to be "better", however i did ultimately have a better time with this story because of the fixed pacing.The gameplay has more variety, but is somehow easier?? Hard mode is not that hard, and that's sad, because half of the reason why people play "stress-games" is because of the challenge. BUTThe soundtrack slaps, again.very, very, very good soundtrack.Overall, not a very innovative sequel, but still enjoyable.Is it worth 17€?...nah, id value it at 12€.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a huge fan of the first game and this one adds all the elements that I enjoyed from the original plus an increased level of difficulty whilst being able to retain the same humour throughout. I very much enjoyed the additional mechanics of the rhythm based mini-games, different environments plus the recurring characters from the original game. I disliked the random luck based elements (the card hi-low game and the robot battle system) as I felt it cheapened the point of the game a little bit and it made certain goals much harder to succeed, even when choosing the most likely option.This is also a fantastic social commentary (as was the original) on the state of the world in the modern age. Whilst not everyone may agree with the stances being made the satire is evident throughout and they are a group who will happily make fun of themselves to some degree at the same time as talking about a serious topic.I hope to see more games in this style from the developers and it is a great example of how well a small team can put together such a fantastic game, certainly they have gained a fan for life.

_childDocuments_.review: This will be a hard one. The review I mean, not the game. Game is easy, even on medium difficulty; will try hard on my second play through. :)First of all, let me tell you why I recommend this game. There are a few reasons but mainly 2; I enjoyed playing both games and I think it has very high potential as an IP. If I just had to tell about this specific one, the second in the series, the review would still be a recommending one but to be honest, not be by far.If you played the first one you won't need any explanation or tutorial, it is pretty much the same mechanics with the same setup and the same choice of graphics style. Yes there are some new "mini-games" (using "" because the original game mechanic itself can almost be called a mini game), but it won't take you to repeat a level to learn them, maybe you'll get in 1 or 2 people less.If you never played the first one, the game mechanics can be explained as simple as; document check. Check the name, dob, this number, that hologram etc. the game is basically this plus the new mini games.Graphics are OK, not the best pixel art around but is enough for this game as it was for the first one.Story is good. Not as good as the first one in my opinion, but still good. Choices in the story seems pretty meaningless though, except when you take 100 damages from them and die, but it is OK. I have also read the reviews you just read before or will read after this one. I do not agree that the game is woke and that it pushes you to take the decisions that the writers/producers want you to take. Actually, I agree with the part of them pushing you to take some decisions that are right for them. But it is not so weird, most of the adventure or RPG games does it, didn't see many RPGs that you can befriend the dragon instead of killing it. There are some games that player choices matter, this one, like many others, is not a game like that. If you think it pushes leftist agenda I invite you also reviewing any militaristic combat game, historical game etc. with the same glasses on, you will be surprised of the level of ideology pushing in many games. Almost every fiction is on a side if look deep enough, this one uses that as a fun creating element. I would say, deal with it or do not play anything that has an actual subject.Music is great. Nothing to say there. Effects and fake speech sounds though; those makes one wonder if that was really the best they could do. It becomes pretty boring after a while.Is it bug free? Almost but not fully, as no complex software can be. Very acceptable.I bought the game for around 15€ at the launch sale. Does it worth it? Well, honestly, no. I think the price point should have been a little lower, maybe around 10€ or something. It took me 10h to finish the game and I read that for some it took only 5. Yes I know the 2$ per hour "rule" but I think it is a bit unfair to gamers, we consume a lot, and in general the games are consumed a lot, they should be cheaper. This could have been avoided by a simple design trick, of course I am not the game designer of this game but I will give my personal opinion about how it should have been in the coming paragraph.If you had the patience to read until here you are probably questioning how is this going to turn into a recommended review? Well I can tell right now; it is the gameplay. It is repetitive, it is same same, but it is brilliant. I can say that it very quickly captures you and brings you to that immersion level which only happens while playing good games. The immersion that makes you easily get out of the negative mood you were in just before you clicked the shortcut of the game. This game requires a high level of focus or you will fail. Yes, there are similar titles around, but believe me, as fan of genre, this one is good. Is it the best one? No, the best is the original one, Papers Please, but this series is close second. Although the flow of the first game was better this one is also very captivating and fun. I would never understand the choice of making us play mini games max 4 times from a design perspective, but it still works, you don't get bombarded with new tricks to learn as it is short. I think if they would have made every city 4 or 5 games instead of 2 they would have built a game that takes longer to finish, would have time to award the player for learning the mini games, would have a more balanced story/game ratio and then maybe a 16€ price point would also be more reasonable. There are some other game design choices I have difficulties to understand but I think it would be going in too much detail for a Steam review.In short the game is good, it has it's shortcomings but it is fun to play. I won't go and tell you to play the first one instead of this one; NT and NT2 both deserves your time and money. Maybe wait for a sale on this one, but get it and play it, I am almost certain you will enjoy it if you are already checking these reviews to decide.

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor to the original "Not Tonight".  We're not dealing drugs to make money, though there's definitely some shady stuff in which to get involved in the former USA.  If you're left-of-center politically, I think you'll appreciate this game's story.  It's definitely not shy about who its audience is in that sense, and I find that comforting.If you found the first game too hard to enjoy, fear not, because the sequel has a range of difficulties from "CASUAL" to "HARD", where CASUAL is not even really made to be a challenge at all.  You can just go through the motions and see the story stress-free.  Easy adds a little bit of pressure, but certainly not tough for anyone experienced with the first game or with "Papers, Please".One thing I'll warn you about, though.  You cannot take a day off and rest to recover health, and working always drains some of your health.  The main way to recover health is to complete Map-O quests, so don't think of them as optional things to do for a branching choice.  Think of them more as things you REALLY need to complete in order to complete the game, unless you're on casual difficulty.The game has occasional stark and disturbing themes, as well as occasionally absurd and humorous scenes, not to mention an enjoyable reference once or twice to those who enjoyed the original game.  There are times where the game clearly doesn't mean for you to take it too seriously, and there are times where you cannot help but see the seriousness in it as it hits home on something sadly all too real.Replay value isn't super great, as the game follows the same general progression regardless of your choices.  However, there definitely is some replay value when it comes to trying to complete the game on higher difficulties, trying to collect all the achievements, and trying to purchase all of the outfits.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot to say about this game, so much that it's difficult to organize my thoughts, so I'll begin with the more basic stuff and move into the more complicated critiques I have. This review will contain spoilers for the game, as I'm analyzing the themes of the game; TL;DR I really do recommend this game but I have notes for the developers and writers!Gameplay: A simple deviation from the Papers, Please formula that emphasizes speed over multi-factor testing with linear "travel" segments between them. As one of the three of our Millennial main characters (Kevin, Malik, and Mari) you're meant to take bouncing gigs through a gig economy-style app to make enough money to travel across the fractured states of America to collect documents to rescue your friend and comrade, Eduardo. It's impressive how well the developers managed to shoehorn the Papers, Please formula of gameplay into a wide suite of different locales: throwing in chickens depending on their age and hormone requirements, doing stat-based RNG battles with robots between letting in actual customers, playing a hi-lo card game with potential entrants to a casino, it's all genuinely inspired. My biggest criticism is the lack of space on the document-processing screen at the bottom, which can lead to some annoying clutter, and the RNG components of some of the gigs mean you're not entirely in control of how well you'll do, but overall, this stuff is great. Meanwhile, the interspersed driving/conversation segments lack some variety in how to approach a problem, but ultimately it's solid enough to reinforce the themes of the game that I don't mind.Aesthetics/Music: I *LOVE* the look and feel of this game. It uses the same pixel art style of Papers, Please, while adding a fun, colorful, and vibrant twist to it, even if the locations the characters are placed in are dour (turning the brainwashing facility into a literal theme park is a great idea). The music uses a variety of modern EDM, reggaeton, hip-hop, and R&B, which is probably more suitable for a game literally taking place in alternate-universe 2022. When the soundtrack comes out, I'm definitely checking it out on Spotify or YouTube Music.Story/Themes: Okay, this game gets a lot of things correct and a few minor things incorrect. America is divided between two factions along the North and South (pretty much the Mason-Dixon line of the Civil War) with two factions: the Alliance (proper liberals, inclusivity without justice) and the Martyrs (authoritarian conservatives, nationalistic and dogmatic). The game critiques both factions, with the Alliance being too focused on compromise and civility politics to focus on the threat of insurrection via liberal democracy, and the Martyrs wielding their power to silence dissent and induce complacency. As a critique of American politics in 2022, I think this particular dividing line is highly effective. However, (and this is where my criticism comes in), the CEO of MapO, a tech company that gives you reward drops for completing missions along the way, rises up in the good ending to help reunite America in a technocratic facts-and-logic unity. The game is tongue-in-cheek about this being a "good" ending, but I would think given the other progressive messaging in the game that you would be able to sidestep this conclusion with the hopes of sparking a more progressive, leftist movement. How this is a part of the good ending is difficult for me to grasp and wound up leaving a bitter taste in my mouth, but I'm assuming it's for the sake of appealing to the broadest audience possible, your Twitter leftist gamers and your Elon Musk stan gamers.Ultimately, I'd give this game a 7/10. If you liked Papers, Please, political commentary included, then you're gonna have a good time bouncing people in Not Tonight 2.

_childDocuments_.review: The devs are back with another satire piece that combines comedy and real-world topics in a super engaging puzzle game. Whilst many elements of the first game are present, such as the checking of ID's and some familiar characters (the cone hat is a staple), the challenges and levels are fresh and encourages creative thinking to pass them. The visuals are also gorgeous and the music matches perfectly. So far, my favourite parts are not only the new methods for passing each day (changing each time to keep things from becoming too autonomous) but also the fact that problem solving goes beyond the game (a perfect DC run requires you to access a selfless website plug from the mayor).If you enjoyed the first game, this is a fresh take on a new location with new political satire and a good mix of old and familiar play-styles to keep it exciting.

_childDocuments_.review: The classic Not Tonight formula feels pretty fun even after playing the first game. It constantly feels like there are clarity issues, such as "Do the Martyr agents count as cowboys" and what to do with the tickets in Orlando Day 2. It takes somewhat too long to let text messages on the phone go through, and game overs just feel frustrating (especially since one wrong binary choice can cause it near the end of the game). Improvements could definitely be made.The pixel art style is nice with its vivid colors and high levels of detail. The music feels alright, though I don't have anything to say about it because I'm not a music fan. Most of the voices feel fresh and not-annoying, expect for Malik's voices which sound a bit too much like actual voice.It's probably just unfortunate timing, but I feel like I've been hearing a ton everywhere online about the US "tearing itself apart" and I just feel like something new is appreciated. Still, the story feels interesting thanks to its interpretation of that idea, and I appreciate the sections between roadtrips with the Miami guards (they remind me of Paper Mario). Overall, the stories are pretty well written and quite captivating.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I loved the original, not tonight 2 kinda misses the mark. the first had more charm in the recurring characters (at least as far as I can tell at this point in the game) and the game play built on itself. I find myself disliking the gimmicks for each location as they don't really add a whole lot to the game and can be frustrating at times. I see how they wanted to build on the original, but if you really enjoyed the first and just wanted more of the same (as i did) this isn't going to be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely incredible game. Imagine Papers Please but outside clubs. The story is huge, the music and map is beautiful. Could play this forever. Highly highly recommend. Finished in a day and already 5 stars just for the chickens and Dave. This is done so well. Everything was thought out and planned amazingly. Could not favour this any more
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: An all around inferior sequel to Not Tonight that still manages to be engaging enough to be worth playingA nice fresh cast of well-written characters with some contrived usage of old favourites from Not Tonight. The way the story is told works well, with the three story-arcs for each character each being interesting and unique. The ending gives you that warm fuzzy feeling from saving all your friends, but ultimately doesn't feel dramatic or impactful to meThe wide variety of mini-games kept the game feeling fresh all the way through, and made the game feel more varied than it was challenging (compared to say, Papers Please, where there's little variety but the level of challenge just keeps going up). I don't consider myself particularly good at this genre of game, but on the default medium difficulty I got bonus 2 every single night, and only got fined for mistakes once.The main let-down of some of these mini-games was that they were entirely luck-based and counted against your performance for the night, and the side quests, which is a monumentally stupid design decision that fortunately doesn't matter unless you're trying to go for all achievementsSpeaking of the side quests, they were a welcome addition, though to me it feels stupid that you're not told explicitly what you have to do for a given quest, then either have to redo a given area if you didn't accidentally get everything, or just try and luck out enough times to get the A grades necessary for the good ending of the game. Personally, I just used a guide to tell me what I needed to do to pass the quests, as I found it frustrating to be given low grades for making ambiguous dialogue choices or outfit decisions incorrectlyFollowing a guide also had the added benefit that I wouldn't mess up dialogue choices that could lead to a game over and repeating a night. As far as I can tell, the only way to work out the right choices is through trial and error in a couple of sections (e.g. )I miss the money pressure of Not Tonight and the drug selling & bribing mechanics that you could opt into to get more money for the higher riskSo yeah, overall, an interesting twist on Not Tonight that I don't think worked out that well in the end, but I was still happy to support the devs and put in the relatively short number of hours required to beat this game
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the first game, you will definitely love this one! There is no repetitiveness whatsoever and you get to process people in a new way for every new place you go to. They have improved the game compared to the first one and have added more game mechanics into it. I had a lot of fun and time went by so fast, I wish it was even longer!
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Contrary to some opinions I felt that Not Tonight 2 surpassed the first game in the series in many ways. It brings back the same addictive game play while adding in a significant amount of variety dependent on your place in the game. Not tonight 2 brings with it an intriguing world, lovable characters, and a combination of subtle and overt witty social commentary. I am so excited and hopeful for a third title. Fans of  will LOVE the little tie in at the very end.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nothing short of a RIDE from start to finish. Where Not Tonight 1 could be more sober at points, Not Tonight 2 is often absurd, but in a deeply captivating way that led to me playing through the entire game in one sitting- and will likely have me coming back again at some point in the near future. I recommend going into the game blind, and playing the first game first for context/contrast if you haven't already. It's a real journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Not Tonight 2 is pretty good, but overall I think the first game is better.NT2 tries to do a similar story to the first game concerning nationalism and facism, but it's also a lot sillier and the constant tone shifts are much more jarring. There's a few parts that are genuinely disturbing but like, also sometimes you have to play a rhythm minigame to accept tickets or shoot wizards out of the air. Even putting that aside, the narrative feels much weaker. It's really unfocused in what it's trying to say. In general it's presenting a capitalist dystopia run by corrupt governments, but also your primary ally is... a megacorp. Who the characters seem to think runs the nicest city in the country. Huh??? There's more, but I won't spoil it.But going back to the minigames: if you found that NT1 was too repetitive, this game fixes that. You only work at a location for 2 nights before moving on, and each place has a different gimmick. The gameplay is overall tuned better than the first game. I never felt like I was facing a huge difficulty spike out of nowhere like I did on some levels in NT1. But moving around so much also means you don't get to know characters for as long as you do in NT1, which is a bummer.If you've never played a NT game, get the first. If you played the first and want more of the same gameplay, give this a shot, but maybe on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: I loved papers please and the first not tonight. This one is more of the same, same gameplay mechanic of playing a bouncer at a door, this time with a dystopian america in the background.  If you liked the previous games you re likely to enjoy this one. The first games are, in my opinion, better. Playthrough is about 10 hrs.  As a negative point, there is a lot of uninteresting dialogue, and slow mini games, and some waiting time until the character moves to the next city.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel that I didn't know existed, but glad it does. The game play is similar to the other game, but has a lot more added gimmicks that increase difficulty to an extent. I will say I am annoyed that their isn't any sort of free play or endless mode yet because replaying specific story chapters could get a bit tedious, but I can forgive it for that. While all the recent political references may date the game going forward I think it can still serve as a time capsule for the time period. I can see the political references turning some people off, but personally I don't think the game takes itself too seriously in the way it uses them. At specific points I will say that it becomes very clear that the game expects you to disagree with a majority of the old fashion boomer beliefs of the Martyrs, but like I said I don't think its that serious. It's a committed dark comedy that is supposed to make you think about what it would be like if the USA fell because of recent events and I can honestly say it is definitely one of the more unique stories I have seen in a while. The ending also gave me some hype for what the future may hold and I can't wait to see what comes next.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Not Tonight 2 is a solid B+. I enjoyed it more than the original. The general gameplay loop is the same, clearly inspired by Papers Please, where you simply compare documents under ever-increasing rulesets.I felt that the original Not Tonight was too grindy. The gameplay loop rooted you to the same venue generally for five shifts straight. Rather than making me feel like it was perfecting my playstyle, I just got bored. I meant to go back and give it another go, but instead gambled on Not Tonight 2, and I'm glad I did. Any given "job" in NT2 is only repeated once before you're off to another location to learn a new mechanic. Even better, the mechanics don't always stack, so I never felt overwhelmed. The pacing was perfect, and I was hooked for the gameplay start to finish.The story is against the backdrop of the United States being split into warring factions, and it's heavy on political themes. It's also heavy on tropes and stereotypes in all directions, with even the main characters relegated to having a couple characteristics each and that's it. I didn't expect top-tier writing from Not Tonight 2, but I also didn't expect it to be that trope-heavy and cringy. It's fine as satire, but lacks any semblance of subtlety. If you're not the type to use the word "woke" unironically while blathering about who's ruining the country this week, I don't think you'll be upset at what you read here. I just don't think it'll provoke anything close to a thought during its entire playtime.Luckily, the gameplay, music, and graphics more than make up for the story's heavy-handedness. If you're on the fence about Not Tonight 2, I say it's worthy of a buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Immediately Purchased this after playing Not Tonight, and honestly was worried it would be the same game-play/ different characters. BUT, it was completely unique while still keeping the integrity of the first game which is what got me hooked to begin with! It still has the beloved ID checking Mechanics but every job is different with special requirements to the location. Also, added QuickTime events within dialog, testing memory and information collected along the way in your inventory. It has a board game feel to it, mixed with great characters from the original game and new ones too! The multiple perspectives of each of the main characters along the way really tie up the story beautifully. Almost as Beautiful as Sean Shawn Shaun's Singing.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: What a strange game.I'm glad they tried to fix the problem the first game had with it being too repetitive by adding gimmicks but they went WAY overboard with the gimmicks. Most of them are decent but some of them are absolutely dreadful like the cult names or musical tickets. Also, having stats like morale and health for this type of game seems pointless.As for the story, it's just... bizarre. Stuff just randomly happens with little rhyme or reason. I like that there is dialogue choices but sometimes it just feels random as to whether or not it was the right decision. Playing as different characters between different roadtrips makes the story feel incoherent and a mess to put together especially since the game itself is linear.Overall, as someone who didn't enjoy the first game, I enjoyed this one more although that's mostly because this game frequently adds new gimmicks to prevent staleness. I wouldn't recommend this as a 'sequel' and more as a standalone experience. If you really want to play it, wait for it on sale as a small recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely do recommend NT2 to anyone that has played the original, but I think NT1 is a better game overall. NT2 both improved and regressed in certain areas - I did enjoy just how many locations you get to visit in NT2, with new mechanics for almost every job that you must complete. it kept it from feeling as grindy as the original, and all the pixel art was so beautiful! it also has great humor, just like the first. however, two of my favorite things about the original was the shop & the music, and I was disappointed by those things in NT2. I at first was intrigued by the concept of the quests and their purposeful vagueness, but it got really frustrating to not entirely control replenishing your health or morale(i liked the decision making of having to work or not in NT1). i missed having a house to decorate! it would have been cool if you could have bought stuff for your car(s). also, all of the music in NT2 felt rather same-y to me? in NT1 i really enjoyed the massive variance depending on the theme of the place you were in, even if i didn't enjoy the songs themselves, but in NT2 there were several moments in which i was confused by the song choice matching the location. yes, NT1 is more laborious to get through, but you feel more connected to the journey and more in control. i sense that it was perhaps the point to make NT2 feel more out of your hands, but after a certain point it goes past enjoyable for me and just feels unfair/tedious. I ended up doing ok with my first blind playthrough, but wouldn't say I enjoyed this game enough to return to (all of the dialogue quizzes/meh music/route taking just built up a lot) but I would definitely replay NT1. they're very different, and i'm still glad i played it, but not stoked with some of the changes they chose to make. regardless, you can see the love that went into this game! i loved the ending bit :)
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: After playing 4 complete runs in this game + some other hours on epic games I think I have enough hours to finally review this game:I absolutely love the map, the mission diversity, the dialogue choices that sometimes matter and some quality of life changes such as the level only starting if you press the play buttonWhat I do not like:-Luck based levels, such as the LA level or the San Antonio level-You cannot move all the items in your board-You cannot use shortcut keys like in the previous gameBut I think overall it is a great succesor of Not Tonight
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect Management game that also has an incredible story like the first game Little Decisions can have a lot of meaning in the game showing how well the team made this gameWhile obviously inspired by other games they Recognise that and still do what they can with the game to the best of their abilities
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Not Tonight 2 is such a stark improvement on the first game. There wasn't a single time that I felt disinterested in what was happening.The story was fantastic! It was a lot less despairing than the first game. It really leaned into a style that was a great mix of fun and disturbing, rather than downright depressing, and it really worked for it! I found it way more engaging to play as friends who were trying to help their friend escape rather than being entirely alone. The way all three roadtrips interweave with each other was perfect; the choice to make it a roadtrip rather than staying in one city was definitely an excellent choice. As a non-American, I found it was also nice to see different facets of America written into the story; each city was so unique and yet at the same time completely American. It really set it apart from the first game.Words can't describe how happy I am with how the gameplay was implemented in this game. In the first game, the mechanic was tedious and it felt like it was dragging of for the sake of longer content. Not Tonight 2 had a perfect balance of introducing new mechanics while also keeping the game fresh. I love that you only had to do 2 nights minimum per city because it felt like the perfect amount of time to learn a new mechanic and master it without wearing the player's patience thin. The pacing of the game was just sublime; I'm buzzing with how much I geniunely enjoyed it.The art style and music were more or less the same than the first same. Completely sticks to the overall theme, style and feel of the game, but nothing too standout. I really enjoyed the addition of the polaroid portraits though, as it gave the characters a face and made me feel more attached to them.Honestly, Not Tonight 2 is so damn good I would just skip the first game altogether (unless you really want to see the easter eggs). The devs really leaned into their own style with this game; anyone who loves this genre would not regret picking this one up!
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably my first actually review of a game lol.***spoilers below***Overall 8/10The story is great, it's refreshing how they used separate characters but stayed within the same universe/style of Not Tonight.  I had a lot of fun playing this game and it was an amazing sequel to the first. Also, the soundtrack is way better than the first. The music goes along great with the venues you work in. Very minimal bugs, which is nice. I love playing games that are made by small developers and are done well. This game was extremely fun, with new and interesting challenges. Btw Dave is starting to grow on me.However, there are a few reasons that it's not a 10/10. I am not a fan how they took away customization. There is minimal customization to your character. Being that this is more of story driven game, I understand which is not a huge issue. I did miss not having an apartment to upgrade to take care of and so on. The one thing that really turned me off was when you hit the last road trip portion of the game. I understand the political satire of the Not Tonight universe (which is hilarious) which led me to buy this game. The first two road trips had a clear mission, and came along some awkward and funny situations that involved political satire. The last road trip, seemed to try harder on getting a political point across rather than being satire. It was over-the-top, to the point where it was not funny and straight bashing. The writer of that road trip makes it clear that they are extremely "left wing" and feminist. In the future I would like to see the political satire continue but staying within satire format. I play video games to have fun and to escape reality, not to live in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Finished in 11hrs. A good game with the same humour as the first. Looking forward to a third! There are some difficulties with accessibility during some of the gigs as some of them are really tricky.There are some glitches/bugs with the checklists. I still managed a playthrough but if you're going back to tick things off - bare that in mind.There are some bugs/continuity/spelling issues during the last scene (which felt like padding tbh) - I can't figure out where to send a bug report so if anyone knows, lmkSimple but addictive & a good one dayer :) Happy Bouncing!
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you were a fan of the first one you'll be pretty satisfied here. There is a some what more elaborate story, but the visuals and game-play remain pretty much the same. Won't go too deep into this one as if you want more of the original, this does the job. _childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the first game, then this is more of the same good quality entertainment. Fantastic music, great pixel art, fun characters and interactions, and a fairly addictive play loop that manages to change just enough every few nights so as not to out stay it's welcome. The game is simple but effective, where it chooses to throw new concepts individually at you rather than consistently add more and more onto the pile like Papers Please does. This makes it a lot more chill and 'easier' without too much of the Brain Hurty, but still fun.There are some cons, however. Some that are personal opinion, and some that are able to be fixed. The main few negative bits of feedback are:- Many Bugs. While my first playthrough was relatively painless, I've found on replays that I'm encountering multiple game breaking bugs. They're usually solved by quiting to desktop and restarting the night, but it gets frustrating when you need to keep restarting every 30mins to an hour and then having to replay the night because the game saves BEFORE the night, not AFTER it finishes. In the space of just under 3hrs of gaming while achievement hunting, I had to restart the game 4 times due to the same few bugs.- The night doesn't start until you press the clicker, which is great for prepping, except there's not a queue already waiting for you. This means you'll often find yourself standing around wasting 30 in game minutes waiting for your first customer to wander past, which is punishing on hard difficulty. Would be far better imo to have a people waiting from the start. Plus some processes are just unnecessarily slow and feel sluggish, such as when you defeat a robot, the system wastes several seconds on the animation before you can turn the away.- Speaking of slow animations, while I love the map and travel aspect of this game, the walking/driving between each point can be unnecessarily slow at times. You'll be travelling between states sometimes with nothing to do, just watching a small icon take 20-30 seconds to walk from one point to the next. This is more noticeable on 2nd playthroughs when you've already read all the texts and news.- While the different mechanics can be fun, the ones based solely on RNG (aka casino and robot fighting) can be unfair to the point of frustrating at points. The joys of this game for me are successfully managing and sorting through IDs, and the failures coming from your own mistakes, so to get the ID check right and then still get a warning for an RNG card pull or dice roll isn't rewarding, you're being punished for something beyond your power. On normal difficulty none of these are a huge issue, but on hard they become annoying. I also HATE the dance beat mechanic but that's personal opinion.Overall an amazing little game that I'd recommend to others, especially when it's on sale, just weighed down by a few minor issues that prevent it from being a full on favourite.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent successor to the first game! The stories were well written and the characters were memorable with nice nods to the first game. I played through the game on hard, but still found the game mechanically very easy and never had a problem reaching the second bonus each night. My only complaint about this game is the inclusion of two RNG based minigames. While they have some way to mitigate the RNG, these were the only times I routinely had to restart a level (because I wanted perfect runs which are NOT necessary). I would prefer all mini games be skill based around our observation as a bouncer rather than observing correctly and having fate decide if I pass or not.Overall a solid game that I enjoyed exploring fully! Looking forward to any future entries to the series and loved the nod to the game's inspiration. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and as someone who finished NT, I enjoyed playing through NT2. Not Tonight 2 has a new different stuff but still keeping the same look and feel from the first one. One of the main elements, the various mini games makes each location feel distinct and challenging on their own instead of having more and more stuff to process. The road trip part fits in with the story and looks interesting having to move from one place to another while passing through some events and perhaps listening to some tunes. NT2 also has a bunch of characters both new and returning with the portrait look gives them a little bit of personality and uniqueness to each of them.Like the first one, Not Tonight 2 has that pixel art goodness from each location you work at and the character portraits. Each place has its mini game that makes it unique from each other and gives new challenges. However, as much as I like some of its soundtrack, they don’t feel as stand out as the soundtrack from the first one (which I often listen to at times). Some of the minigames can feel daunting and hard, especially the ones with RNG to them but after two times playing I learn to hang around.There are some things I missed from the first one, like the keyboard shortcuts and each place inside view both I like from the first game but seeing the game, I can see why they didn’t include them in which I’m okay with it. One thing that I love from the game that can be used in NT, is how you can wait before starting your day. It helps the player to review the rules of the gameplay and as a time to prepare.TL;DRNot Tonight 2 has lots of new features while maintaining its charm from the first one. Charming pixel art graphics and various mini games make playthrough enjoyable with different challenges. There might be things that are not as good, but I learn to enjoy them nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel to this beloved game, doesn't disappoint. It allows for multiple "roadtrips" so you can really start to understand the characters. Also it comes across a lot of moral dilemmas that we are currently facing today. If you were a fan of the first game, or of Papers Please you will enjoy this game. It is sure to make you laugh and your heart wrench into your throat in the best way possible. Alliance for Life!
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: I did think the story was a little more heavy-handed and felt less nuanced than NT1, and the story felt a little less compelling because of it, but it was certainly nothing that ruined the experience for me. I thought some of the satirical touches and points being made were still very good. (The negative reviews based solely on the politics make me laugh.)The improvements to the base mechanics of the game with the addition of mini games were really great, and it was nice that they only lasted one or two jobs before moving on. If there was a minigame I didn't like, I knew it would be over after the current assignment. The chicken processing place especially made me really laugh and it had that bizarre quality from the first game that I enjoyed.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Even better then the first, love the updated map look,new mechanics for each place was a blast though missing my short cuts keys I had to get used to. XD And characters were all well done, story was awesome and being american I appreciate the way some of the ridiculous thoughts and horrible habits here were pushed into overdrive so well. Sadly wouldn't be surprised of at least somethings similar to this happens here to be fair.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, If you loved the first or Papers Please you will love this game so much. It has extra things to do almost every single Club to give different players who like different things a moment in the game. It's not as difficult as papers please but it has so much story and side quests. If you enjoy puzzles/papers please you will love this game so much.Enjoy crossing broken america.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, had lots of fun. The minigames definately added more enjoyment however the ones which were randomized felt ♥♥♥♥♥♥ every so often, like even if I do everything perfectly I still get penalized because I got unlucky.The questsystem is fun but every now and then you get one which feels very unintuitive.LOVE the chicken level!The best story is definetly Malik, so if you're questioning not playing though the entirety of the game atleast wait until then, :)Still some bugs- most of them not too problematic, worst one I got resulted in me not being able to hand out any more tickets so I assumed I had handed out enough of them. Afterwards the game gave me a game over and a snarky "seems like you missed handing out some tickets, huh?".Either that one or the fact that I can't start a second "new game" since my character decides to walk on the spot and wont move, soft-locking the game. Not to big of a problem since I can load the game from day 1 on one of my previous games but still kind of annoying.I still really liked it though, a lot of enjoyable characters (Dave's back, and weirder than ever)
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from America myself, This game was really fun and even funnier to play. The Music was killer as always, and having three paths was very fun to do and explore all of Broken America. I had some issues with the Map-o Quests, but it's really just for unlockables, I'm 90% sure you can go through the game without going out of your way trying to solve the vague meanings. The very Blatant  jabs at american culture is really funny, and I do not care what anyone else thinks.  I would still prefer the 1st one over this, but that doesn't mean this is a bad game, I loved this game and might even go for all achievements one day.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed Not Tonight 1, this is [the same but more!] with more story, more puzzles, more interesting mechanics etc. The game does a really good job at introducing a new mechanic and then moving on quickly before it gets boring / annoying. The story is okay (the satire is really heavy-handed) but overall I thought it was entertaining enough, driven mostly by the fun gameplay loop of checking people's IDs which has stayed fresh after 2 whole games. Fun game!
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: As someone that was a big fan of the original game, this game has definitely hit the mark. It has brought over the good things with the last game, such as the art style, some old characters, basic game mechanics and theme, and has introduced a bunch of new ones which justify making it a new game, as opposed to a DLC.Don't get me wrong, this game still has it's problems. For starters, it's auto-saving feature is a bit confusing, which can result in having to re-play some parts. The dialog has timers for answering, which isn't great if you're a slow reader. If you liked to read the text interactions between people mid-game, beware the game time does not pause. And a few other minor inconveniences here and there, but nothing too major.Overall, if you liked the last game and this game goes on sale, I'd recommend getting.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is essentially a "face lift" of the Not Tonight brand. It keeps the core elements and mechanics from the first game and makes them a bit more in-depth and broad. Overall, it's not a dramatic improvement but it still gets the job done of entertaining you for around 8 hours. I don't see myself replaying it because you can guess what the other outcomes would be. Finally, they should have used the main menu font style in the dialogue boxes. The font of the conversations felt like they do not belong to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review:
In an alternative broken America, where capitalism and political greed have taken center stage, your friend has gone missing. Snatched during a protest, Eduardo Suarez has been seized by the authorities, and now sits ready for processing in the Miami gulag.

Not Tonight 2 is an American document-checking road trip, fusing a time-pressure RPG with a politically charged, dark comedy where every decision matters. Will Eduardo's friends Malik, Kevin and Mari manage to locate and deliver his documents to Miami in time, or is this the end of the American dream?
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

name: Demon's Mirror
detailed_description: Demon’s Mirror combines roguelike deckbuilding and a grid manipulation battle system to create a unique experience where Slay the Spire meets Puzzle Quest. Play as one of three trapped souls and embark on a treacherous journey where your worst nightmares lie in ambush! Collect new cards and gain power as you navigate an ever-changing labyrinth of increasing challenges to solve the mystery of the demonic mirror that trapped you here. Discover over 200 cards to create the ultimate deck! Select cards that grant special powers to deal heavy damage to your enemies or set up clever synergies and punishing combos. Get creative and experiment! Combining deckbuilding and chain-3 mechanics puts you in control of the battle! Collect and wield powerful cards to manipulate the grid and unleash devastating combos upon your foes while chaining tiles to attack, defend, gather resources or decrease your enemy’s power. The added complexity brings depth to traditional deck-building, providing a fresh and engaging experience. Encounter formidable enemies and unpredictable scenarios designed to test your wits. Hasty decision-making will lead to certain death. Only by mastering the strategic balance between playing cards and chaining tiles can you hope to survive! No two playthroughs are ever the same! _childDocuments_.review: It's... alright.It combines two of my favorite genres into a competent, delightful package, but it just lacks that  factor that beckons "just one more round!"  The biggest issue I have is the ; fights can take , with some enemies buffing every round or making copies of themselves while you wait for  RNGs to line up: both your card draw and the board draw.  It's like a see-saw where you have the perfect board but none of the cards, or all your OP cards but a board of weak chains.  Eventually you have to start spending your resources instead of wasting turns and taking damage, and most rounds end up with you nickel-and-diming your way through battles instead of those rare occasions where it all lines up.The best feeling about match-3 games is getting killer chains, but they usually only amount to single-turn advantages in this game.  There's very little in the way of snowballing OP combos, and they usually take several turns just to set up because you're too busy dinking and diving just to stay afloat.There's some cool concepts and synergies to be found, but the three characters feel like one or two-trick ponies, making replay value scarce.  It feels a little barren content-wise, and I'd be surprised to see anyone but masochists with more than 20 hours.The game cribs from existing genres and combines them into something unique, but it's just not enough to sustain long-term interest.  It's definitely worth a shot if you're into this mash-up, but I'd wait until there's a sale.  I just found myself wanting to play other games instead of thirsting to jump right back in.

_childDocuments_.review: I already had a lot of fun with the demo and the full game doesn't disappoint. This is not just another slay the spire clone. It combines known elements from Puzzle Quest/Ironcast and Slay the Spire into something special. And most importantly - something fun! Your have to juggle between traditional card play and match 3 puzzles and many cards can manipulate the puzzle grid in interesting ways. It definitely deserves more attention than what it is currently getting.

_childDocuments_.review: I spent a few hours on the demo because I'm a huge sucker for roguelikes and Puzzle Quest/match 3. I *really* wanted to like this but I'm giving up on it.Cards don't feel interesting. Do X damage, or do X + 3 damage or turn these tiles into that tile. There are not many different kinds of tile manipulating cards.There's no mechanism for a board reset like what Puzzle Quest does. Sometimes you'll exhaust your supply of shield and then the enemy throws down a 1 turn hit you for 30 which means you're just gonna get sucker punched for a bunch.Speaking of enemy tiles, enemies love -- and I mean LOVE -- increasing enemy tile damage. Battles are frustrating because strong enemy tiles mean you're pretty much forced to either take a hit from an enemy, or take a hit from a tile. You don't have enough shield to do anything.The green tile is, imo, mostly useless. Some cards do extra damage if you have enough, but it decays off. In most cases they're junk tiles unless you have the card to make them into crystals.Crystals (willpower) are frustrating because enemies are constantly buffing themselves. Meanwhile your main non-card buff has a sharply increasing cost. So while enemies are free to constantly buff their damage tiles, you hit a point where you have to grab, like, 25 or so crystals for your next buff.Crystal buffs aren't that great. I chain together, what, 20 crystals and I get 3 peace (enemy tiles take 3 damage at the start of a turn). Cool. It took like 7 turns to put that together, and in the meantime the enemy buffed their tiles so now I have a 30 damage in 1 turn coming up. Cool.The game seems designed around the lizard because many enemies have counters if you attack them, but the lizard's attack (influence) doesn't count as damage. A good example is The Shell. Absolutely brutal if you're the wolf who only gets raw damage, but trival for the poisoner. Many enemies are like that.I think my biggest issue is that nothing comes close to that Good Build feeling in late StS. That feeling when It's All Coming Together, and you have your synergies. This game it's like, alright, Charged Fireball gains 3 damage every turn it's retained, and...oh hi there, three different damage tiles over 30. Hey game, you realize the board isn't growing, right? ...right?The art and sound effects are nice though.

_childDocuments_.review: It's easy to mistake Demon's Mirror for just another Slay the Spire clone. It's not afraid to wear it's inspiration on its sleeve, for sure, but the interaction between cards and the match-3 board make for something special and unique. You can get really strategic in setting up combos, and you need to because each encounter is tough. I was a big fan of the original Puzzle Quest, using spells and abilities to manipulate the board, and this has some of that feel. Definitely not for everyone, but once you wrap your head around the mechanics, Demon's Mirror is super satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: Fuse Slay the Spire with a chain-3 game, and you have Demon’s Mirror.Key note. Chain-3, not Match-3. With Match-3, you swap the position of board symbols to create a 3, 4 or 5 block. With Chain-3, you drag a line through as many symbols of the same kind as you can, so long as they are adjacent, orthogonally or diagonally. Set aside the chain-3 board temporarily, and Demon’s Mirror follows the Slay-a-like formula closely. # Begin with a starter deck and a starter artefact / trinket unique to a character, which strongly influences what they are better at# Choose your path on a branching map of nodes with battles, Elite battles, rest sites, shops, events and deck manipulation sites# Progress through multiple acts, each act ending in a boss fight# Battles are a turn-based card-playing tightrope of trying to deal damage whilst avoiding taking damage, and wins result in card and coin rewards# During a run, you add, remove and upgrade cards, gain permanent passively run-changing trinkets and single-use scrollsThen what it does differently, which also changes all the card-based play, is give you a 6x6 board of gems, representing attack, defence, a form of power-up and a form of limit-break currency, 4 total. You have the 3 energy points, same as Slay, initially, but you split them between playing cards or creating chains. Each battle turn then presents a tactical dilemma, what is the best combination of cards and chains?Slay has a magical quality of a near frictionless sequence of card-select, drag to target, release, outcome, with immediate feedback and that little dopamine hit that accompanies it. Demon’s Mirror has that, 100%. Everything executes slickly and feels goldilocks, just right. Many turns give you a wonderful little tactical dilemma. On any given turn, you may have choices like these:# Play 2-3 chains but no cards# Play 3 or more cards, but no chains# Split your energy between chains and cardsWhich is the best will also change based on how you can change the board state *before* chaining, through cards – often 0 cost – that destroy, convert or move gems around. You have a LOT of scope for setting up over several turns for a huge attack, for example, by removing other types of gems from the board to create a long chain of attack gems, applying a vulnerable debuff to enemies, and a chain buff to yourself.Many cards can manipulate the board state, and it appears – initially – viable to really lean in to either a card-heavy or a board-heavy deck. The cards and the board interact with each other – a lot – requiring careful thought both in battle and in the overall deck building. Take the learning curve of any deckbuilder – it can be tough initially as you try and figure out what the heck makes a viable deck. This has that challenge AND then the added complexity of the chain-3 side. This is not necessarily a bad thing, but I could imagine that non-veterans of both genres might find the learning pretty harsh initially.Writing this only 3-4 run attempts in, I can say little just yet. There *are* things to unlock, including the core characters and buffs and debuffs that can be applied to an entire run to change the challenge level.
_childDocuments_.name: Demon's Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: One of a kind roguelike deckbuilder.It combines a connect-3 board with deckbuilding. Each turn you have a number of energy, and you spend that energy either on using your cards, or on chaining on the board. Rest follows the typical Slay The Spire formula. Move through the map with battles, random events, deck management and campsites.. 3 classes which have different mechanics. Enemies telegraph their turn, which goes after yours. And keeping your deck thin. It's quite difficult though, even at 0 ascension, so you'll have to use your brain when making your build.
_childDocuments_.name: Demon's Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: The deckbuilder genre is heavily saturated and afraid to innovate from its core formula. This game is fun, but I don't think the tile-matching is enough to overcome what is essentially the exact same problem-solving set in StS.The tile matching is a fun gimmick but the game focuses too much on the admittedly boring cards at the beginning of each run (pay 1 mana gain 4 shield, pay 1 mana deal 4 dmg etc.) and not enough on the games core feature of tile-matching. And I don't think a game where every run all I'm doing is paying 2 mana for 12 shield until I get some cool combos is something I want to ante up for the umpteenth time.
_childDocuments_.name: Demon's Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: Solid card battler rougelike with chain-3 mechanic. The Slay the Spire inspiration is obvious, but the inclusion of the chain-3 grid really adds to the decision making and puzzling out each turn. The game can be quite challenging, and some cards and enemies could probably do with a few small tweaks, but the vast majority of the content and core gameplay is very solid and exceptionally polished. I also want to say that the music has been excellent and card art is fantastic, especially ones with expressions on them; I've laughed at quite a few of them!If you're a fan of Slay the Spire or similar deckbuilders and the chain-3 mechanic intrigues you, this is a solid recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Demon's Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: A superb game that adds a new "gimmick" to the deck builder roguelite in the way of the match 3 board.Careful use of both your deck and the tile board are required in order to progress. The game takes a few runs to get into (I lost my first 3) but offers a good but beatable challenge rather than spamming a select few cards. The tile board also has enemy tiles that if left alone can damage you, curse you, heal the enemy or give them block... as well as a few other tricks on the bosses.Visibly it's pretty and each character feels different thanks to the unique bonuses each receive. Likewise, even the enemies feel somewhat unique with a number of them having special attributes or weaknesses. There's a lot of hidden control to these fights in using the weaknesses and traits against them. One elite does massive damage but is stunned by gaining enough of a specific symbol on the board, the barbed trait deals damage back to you when you attack them with cards but not with tile-chaining, and one enemy will change it's action based on your plays... and that's just a few, and doesn't even talk about bosses. While there are certainly a number of 'regular' mobs, there's still plenty of times you need to pay attention, adapt and actually think about your actions.It also has positive modifiers as well as negative, allowing you to fine-tune the difficulty to your liking.The biggest negative is that there's not a lot to unlock, and I felt I didn't get anything rewarded to me when beating the final boss and watching the credits roll. It would be great if each character had one unique unlock for that... but this is a SUPER minor negative.I'd love to see more YouTubers/streamers cover this game, as I truly think it stands out in the genre and I'd love to see them expand it further.
_childDocuments_.name: Demon's Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: Quite interesting mix of chain-3/match-3 with roguelike deckbuilder. Sharing the same pool of energy, you have to be playing cards and chaining tiles, being the most interesting part of the game deciding which one is more convenient to use and when. The deckbuilding mechanics are pretty default and not that engaging, but you have a bunch of new extra stats to make some use of the more unique part of the game, which I think is a great idea, because it is the more interesting part here.You count with 3 different playable characters so far, each one with different deck and stats, and overall there is a nice variety of different synergies you can build.Be aware though, runs can be pretty long (could take 3 hours depending on your build), so be ready for a long journey.Overall, a pretty solid roguelike deckbuilder 8/10. If you are curious here you have some gameplay
_childDocuments_.name: Demon's Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic and surprising mish-mash of genres. If you're a Slay the Spire fan, this is your next obsession. Three completely unique characters complement a varied and unique gameplay system. The match-3 is fantastically integrated. I only wish that there were more ways for the match-3 to affect the cards. I've had a great time with Demon's Mirror.

_childDocuments_.review: A thumbs up for the game and a sprinkle of #Ad I guess :P A well deserved one though, for an amazing channel/communityBeen waiting to try Demon's Mirror since I saw it played on Esty8nine's channel some time ago, it has been on my wishlist for quite a long time and it turned out to be an amazing game! _childDocuments_.review: I've done several runs now. 2 with all the characters at least, Where the dragon seemed like the character I synergized the most with, being that you get free cards to play when you chain anything, as long as you keep your card requirement low. (Already incentive not to use higher energy cards, VERY BAD, DOESN'T Incentivize experimentation.)The furthest I've gotten is the third world. and I was royally screwed in my first encounter because there were two enemies that wanted to attack for an upwards of about 40 damage and that's literally impossible to block unless you have insane luck.I started getting to the point where if I had low HP and kept getting bad RNG on the board and cards, I'd just slog and end it early so I could start another run where I didn't make the mistake of picking up cool, but very niche cards that I'd never find a use for.The run where I made it to world 3 was one of my worse runs. but RNG kept giving me godlike chains and cards exactly when I needed them. it felt great until the run was over and I realized that this game isn't very skill based. you just get lucky, or you barely scrape by while trying to fight back against your terrible odds, and inevitably die to some BS in one battle because you stalled for too long.I see a lot of people comparing this to Slay the Spire... I wonder how true that really is because I never played it.>The mix of both worlds, Deck builder, and Chain 3 is very VERY well done. it feels good to get a big chain in the first world that just smashes enemies.>There are events that help you out on your journey, and there's a lot of variety. with shops, Treasure chests, upgrades for cards, removing cards, all to help customize the run on the fly.>Every enemy does it's own special thing to the Chain 3 board, there's a lot of different outcomes.>Each character has a unique playstyle that changes the way you play the game.>Characters are objectively worse than others. even though I played the Dragon the most it's probably the worst charatcer in the game.>If you have any cards that require 3 energy you won't use them period, by the time you can, you've already won the battle, and don't need it anymore because the threats are all dead.>Better cards require more energy and more often than not YOU DON'T GET MORE ENERGY TO COUNTER BALANCE THIS.>Most cards are too niche and require such a specific scenario that you're throwing your game if you grab them.>Some cards are so good that if you don't grab them you're throwing.>The game is boring when you're trying to min max and play effectively instead of for fun. (Burn bad cards, force less RNG.)>If you stall out a battle and try to be tactical, you get punished by buff stacking enemies. all enemies often have a means to infinity scale damage and YOU don't.>Some Elites tend to spam tiles onto your board and it makes getting big combos impossible. Setting up becomes tedious instead of tactical.>Trinkets do so little, honestly felt like half of them did nothing at all. And by the time you get one that would have synergized with something, you don't have the means to make it work.>Battling gives you so little in return, you'll get further avoiding all but the first 2 battles in your run with the same odds of winning or losing.>Some, if not most combat mechanics feel like BS. the lack of power scaling for your own character (like permanent upgrades for this run only.) don't exist. you're stuck with the hand that was dealt to you, no pun intended.>You have to get really lucky to have a good run. and you have to beat impossible odds to win.>The game isn't hard, it's unfair. Hades is hard, but fair. Spirit Fall is hard, but fair. Backpack Hero isn't Hard, but it's Fair all the same and can be made harder with challenges.>The game has a Challenge window, but good luck getting to the point where you unlock any of them.>I'm probably not even listing all the flaws for this game.The game has a Challenge window, among those is things that can make the game easier. but like I said before, it's all down to RNG so... I enabled all of them and died to my first Elite enemy. when I've killed 3 Elites in a row without those settings before.Might play a few more runs but honestly this game needs changes NOW.Want a fair game that won't make you feel like you're bad and it's your fault your bad? don't play this game.Want a game that's skillful and implementing strategy can get you a flawless? don't play this game.Masochist? play this game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Demon's Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome idea, very clunky and boring. It makes me irrationally angry that the developer had such a wonderful concept, but somehow managed to make it unfun to play. Costs 2 energy to do the match 3, but you only start with 3 energy? Why doesn't it just cost 1? Why is every single fight tedious and boring? At least the things blatantly copied from Slay the Spire are decent, but it's just not enough to save this game in it's current state. I really hope either this developer figures it out and makes it fun to play, or someone else takes the reigns and makes a fun match3/card game roguelike, because it's a great idea.
_childDocuments_.name: Demon's Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure, the developer of this game is a friend of mine. But that hasn't stopped me from trash talking or giving a bad opinion before.I think this is a really worthy Spire-like. It really gets the ontological side of things, little lore drops and a vague feeling of unease. The tile-matching component slots in surprisingly well and really changes the dynamic of your deck. Cards I would never consider taking in Spire I would take here in a heartbeat. Draw is less important, the tiles are everything. Everyone has a satisfying gimmick for how they interact with the board (and let's be honest, the axolotl is the best. Hours will pass before you realize that you've been chaining those conductor tiles). I'm currently working my way up the difficulty modifiers, but I'll write a full report when I'm done. At a first glance, this is definitely worth your time if you're a fan of rogue-likes.
_childDocuments_.name: Demon's Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the fact that I love Slay the Spire-like games, and I also enjoy a good Match 3 phone game. As you can tell from 5 seconds of video from the game, this is a very close clone of StS but with a Match 3 board reminiscent of the classic Puzzle Quest. Given that and the care with which the game was made, I enjoyed it enough to give it an up rating.On the negative side, I think it's so similar in many ways to Slay that despite the Match 3 boards, I quickly mined it out. There's not much new to discover, and the three classes all play somewhat similarly. That's not to say it's a bad game -- I had a good time, and I'm upvoting it because I love the genre and this is a decent example of it, but if you are only going to play a few games of this type, there are a lot better entries to pick up. On the plus side, the art is pretty and the game is pretty well-balanced, in my opinion. If you are a frequent StS-like player, you'll likely find it to be perfectly balanced; if you're new to the genre, you may find it quite difficult to win. The cards are well thought-out, and there are a variety of builds to try, but a lot of it feels awfully familiar. It's often more fun to have greater diversity of experiences on runs but have a less tight balance -- maybe an unpopular opinion, but that's how I feel about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Demon's Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of these types of games, and since the release of Slay the Spire, the Deckbuilding Roguelike genre has been done to death with the same concept over and over again. There's a few good ones out there, and far more 'meh' ones.Demon's Mirror has been a refreshing take on a genre that's been frankly overdone. A second facet to combat makes things very different, and I've been having a great time with this game. Be warned, however, as this game is NOT easy at first, but that's not a bad thing, it's a fun challenge for veteran players. 9/10, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Demon's Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: I have really been enjoying this game so far! I find the first two characters you are able to play as (All I have played so far) to be very charming and distinct from one another. I adored Slay the Spire and I think this game does an amazing job utilizing elements that are similar to Spire, but also puts a fun spin on the genre. This game is very unique while also having those charming parallels, and anyone who loved Spire will also love this game. Super recommend giving it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Demon's Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: This is Slay the Spire with a Match 3 element provided.  It works a lot like StS ... different paths, creature battles, random events, and campfires for healing, and shops for upgrading.  During battles, the match 3 board allows you to attack, power spells, gain shields, etc.  You draw cards for attack, defense and skills.  Some of those cards can change the board around to allow for more powerful combos.  The enemy can also add bad tiles to the board that you need to destroy or take some serious damage.  Use them in combos to destroy them.  There are mini-games, one of which uses match 3 and cards to gain gold.All in all, this is a pretty fun game!  It does have some bugs and things that I don't understand.  However, There are lots of things to considers as enemies and enemy board tiles have certain abilities that make things difficult.  There should be many hours to this game as I am still working on my first run...

_childDocuments_.review: really fun deckbuilder roguelite. the grid-chaining puzzle elements fit in really smoothly, the art and music are good, and the whole premise is just really charmingEDIT ok i'm 20hrs in and this game is addictive. there is so much complexity to explore, so much depth to the tactics, so many weird trinket combos to try... every run i'm thinking about my next run. the music keeps playing in my head long after i quit the game and i like it. i've noticed a few very minor bugs but they're hardly disruptive and the overall experience is incredibly polished. the art and aesthetic are so delightfully strange and a lot of the card illustrations are downright funny. the board chaining stuff should feel tacked-on but it's so well integrated it just feels right. a real gem of a game, well worth the price

_childDocuments_.review:
Demon's Mirror is the first game to combine roguelike deckbuilding and chain-3 mechanics in a way that creates a powerful synergy between the two. Like other deckbuilders, you battle enemies by playing cards to attack, defend, and gain powers, but in Demon's mirror you also battle opponents by chaining tiles. Certain cards let you manipulate the board in ways that will allow you to create longer chains. Mastering the strategic balance between playing cards and chaining tiles is what will ultimately determine your fate.

Demon's Mirror plays like a combination of Slay the Spire meets Puzzle Quest (but with a chain-3 mechanic).

name: Frostpunk 2
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition About the Game Frostpunk 2 elevates the city-survival genre to a new level. Take the role of a Steward and lead your city through a cascade of calamities taking place in a postapocalyptic, snowy setting. Build large city districts with their string of endless needs and demands. Navigate through conflicting interests of factions that populate your metropolis. As the needs of the city grow and factional power at its core rises, only you can steer the society towards an uncertain future. The world is overtaken by an ever present winter, which makes expansion of the city the only way for the survival of mankind. In order to grow, the metropolis needs resources like coal and oil, just like its citizens require food and warmth. In Frostpunk 2, it's your job to tackle this never ending circle of supply and demand. The number of your citizens steadily grows, making the task of governing them and satisfying their demands all the more challenging. As the Steward you will have to maneuver carefully across the interests of many groups inhabiting the city. People of your city want to have a voice in how you run things. Each faction has its own ideology and ideas for the future, yet they also have one thing in common - insatiable thirst for power. Choose your allies in the Council Hall wisely. The story of Frostpunk 2 introduces a multi-chapter saga set in the frozen wastes. Spanning across the life of the Steward this campaign lets you feel the burden of leadership as you take the responsibility for thousands of lives. At the same time, the sandbox mode called Utopia Builder with infinite play time leaves you room for boundless social and infrastructural experiments. Frostpunk 2 comes with a comprehensive and versatile modding tool. FrostKit will let you create your own maps, models, and scenarios inside the game. Now, only your imagination can limit the destination your city is heading to!
about_the_game: Frostpunk 2 elevates the city-survival genre to a new level. Take the role of a Steward and lead your city through a cascade of calamities taking place in a postapocalyptic, snowy setting. Build large city districts with their string of endless needs and demands. Navigate through conflicting interests of factions that populate your metropolis. As the needs of the city grow and factional power at its core rises, only you can steer the society towards an uncertain future. The world is overtaken by an ever present winter, which makes expansion of the city the only way for the survival of mankind. In order to grow, the metropolis needs resources like coal and oil, just like its citizens require food and warmth. In Frostpunk 2, it's your job to tackle this never ending circle of supply and demand. The number of your citizens steadily grows, making the task of governing them and satisfying their demands all the more challenging. As the Steward you will have to maneuver carefully across the interests of many groups inhabiting the city. People of your city want to have a voice in how you run things. Each faction has its own ideology and ideas for the future, yet they also have one thing in common - insatiable thirst for power. Choose your allies in the Council Hall wisely. The story of Frostpunk 2 introduces a multi-chapter saga set in the frozen wastes. Spanning across the life of the Steward this campaign lets you feel the burden of leadership as you take the responsibility for thousands of lives. At the same time, the sandbox mode called Utopia Builder with infinite play time leaves you room for boundless social and infrastructural experiments. Frostpunk 2 comes with a comprehensive and versatile modding tool. FrostKit will let you create your own maps, models, and scenarios inside the game. Now, only your imagination can limit the destination your city is heading to!
short_description: Develop, expand, and advance your city in a society survival game set 30 years after an apocalyptic blizzard ravaged Earth. In Frostpunk 2, you face not only the perils of never-ending winter, but also the powerful factions that watch your every step inside the Council Hall.

_childDocuments_.review: Really feels like an evolution of the first game in most ways, while keeping most of what I personally loved about it. The first two difficulties feel a little easier than Frostpunk did. I'd recommend starting on Steward for veterans of the first game, but Officer was challenging enough to be fun too. The story campaign is great and I really enjoyed it.There are performance problems but I'd describe it as minor since this style of game does not demand high frame rates, scaling down the settings does help a lot, and I was able to maintain good performance on the medium preset. Just be prepared to lower settings, even if you are running upscaling and frame generation on very high end hardware.

_childDocuments_.review: While not without its faults, this game is enjoyable and looks like a solid foundation for more stories in the future. It seems the developers also listen to feedback and implement user friendly changes, even if they could have taken some of the lessons they learned from Frostpunk 1 and applied them to this game from the start.For example: deposits in FP1 weren't infinite at launch, but they later changed that. The deep deposits of FP2 also weren't infinite at launch, which was a confusing decision to me because of FP1's changes. It seems they had the same realization and have now changed these deposits to be infinite too.
