_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for March 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before April 2nd, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Bayonetta while missing the charm. Soulstice is designed as an action game.  There are long levels separated into arenas.  There’s a scoring system designed for replayability and a ton of mechanics that need to be tried and mastered. While playing Soulstice there were a lot of games that came to mind.  Metal Gear Revengeance, God of War, Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, and even Darksiders.  And Soulstice feels like it’s standing on the shoulders of greatness with its combat system. However Soulstice is missing something important compared to all those games, it’s not one simple thing, but more a style, a presentation, a defining animation, or a character personality that works here.  Solstice just feels like it’s lacking an important part of the DNA of this genre, and it’s noticeable. Pick this up if you like the action-adventure hack and slash, like Devil May Cry, but understand this is a B-tier effort.  There are also a lot of different mechanics at play here, perhaps too many but also it allows players to get engrossed in the combat system. _childDocuments_.review: The game starts out as a decent DMC/Bayo/old GOW spectacle fighter, but slowly becomes more and more tedious as it progresses. The camera during most parts is fixed which can make navigating and finding secrets difficult if you're not used to these types of games, but combat has a free cam so its generally not as big a deal as a lot of people try to make it out to be. Combat feels good initially, all weapons basically have the same type of attack unlocks, alt combo, launcher, air attack etc, with a few flairs, and they're supposed to be better vs certain types and such, but you could get away with just the starting hammer and have very few issues, other weapons are fun sometimes but just feel less consistent then the hammer upgraded, even when used against flyers which its "Weak" to you can just smash them down with the air attack like nothing.Things start to get tedious when you have to juggle red aura and blue aura monsters at the same time, plus have red and blue area denial bombs to avoid, the auras felt neat and fresh originally but turn into light switch flicking busy work as the game goes on. The counter system with the sister is sort of cool, but the timings to achieve certain ones is either too unforgiving or just finicky, there's supposed to be a type where you completely stop an enemies attack, and a type where you slow and delay it, but 95% of the time its just going to be the slow attack, putting points into stopping feels like a waste when you just buff slow as much as you can. Some enemies also have annoying tracking, so you'll slow mid attack then dodge behind to damage some more, but the slow wears off and they auto spin the attack on you anyways, you either have to dodge again or completely move away, neither feels fun considering you've already "dealt" with the attack.The map layout in some stages seems weird as well, there's been numerous instances where, because of the camera you think the obvious path is in plain sight, so you look around for secret areas to the side, only for the "secret area" to end up being the actual path and a point of no return leaving you unable to back track to the obvious path to find any secrets, The worst part of the game I think are the Challenge areas, like the bayo rifts or DMC secret zones, where you have to kill enemies under certain conditions and such, the friendly AI and enemy AI can make certain ones absolutely annoying, they never feel like fun areas to test your abilities or make you think creatively, just more busy work chores to pad playtime.The characters and story are serviceable enough so I'll probably carry on till the end but the experience has definitely soured as my time with it progresses.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprised to see so many negative reviews. I think they do touch on the biggest problem with the game (that being too many enemies in too small a space, each of which require counters and sometimes a different field to be up to even hit), but I think generally a lot of complaints are overblown.The fixed camera is weird but really not impactful, I can't believe there are so many people losing their minds over it (Bayonetta had it too, by the way!). The linearity of the games is again normal for the genre. I personally feel like the combat DOES feel really good, but this last one is subjective.I think this game makes a lot of really smart decisions. The one that feels the best is the fact that the countering is done by a separate entity and thus, unlike parrying with your weapon, you can counter while in the middle of attacking. There are so many reasons why that's such a good choice but I'll just say that's my favorite part of the game.I love the character designs and I think the story is really interesting. Voice acting is so-so. Overall I think this game is really good, with some flaws, and I'm going to be playing it more.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like coming across Darksiders 1 back in the day. You play it, you feel like you are playing a God of War/Devil May Cry clone, but the game actually has a lot of personality and is pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun. This game makes me nostalgic for the classical hack and slashes from the ps3/xbox360 era. The camera angles, the way it plays, the items you get, it all feels like a love letter to those early 2000 era hack and slashes. Buy it if you are nostalgic about them.Edit: Guess this is my fault for recommending it so early. The start of the game is great, but don't let yourself be fooled by it. After a while you are introduced to mechanics that are straight up counterintuitive and go against the design philosophy of the hack and slash genre. Things such as land mines that explode if you are around them too much, spread across the battlefield, making it so you literally can't combo the enemies unless you bait them away from the mines (which are everywhere mind you). Weapons all having literally the same combo but with some properties changed, making combat simplistic and repetitive at times. The camera is not well designed for combat and its a hassle, having to fight against it more than with the enemies.  Overall its a game that had a lot of potential by offering a combat system that is quite refreshing and different from Dmc, Bayonetta etc. never in my life did I expect to see a combination between a hack and slash and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Ikaruga of all games, coupled with an actually interesting story with some of the most interesting main characters I've seen in a game like this. Its too bad that in the end its more annoying than fun. I do believe that this franchise has a ton of potential to grow and I'll follow the devs in case they decide to make a Soulstice 2 with more polish and less ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mines (seriously, who thought that mines in a hack and slash would be a good idea).  I still think that its worth a try, who knows, you might not be as annoyed as I was by some of the mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice seems to have come out of nowhere. I didn't see any marketing for it when it was released and even still after it came out, I didn't see many people talking about it, which is a real shame. I'm glad I happened to stumble onto this game and hope that more do because this game will end up being one of those hidden gems.This is a spectacle fighter, already a very niche genre without many titles. It plays similar to Devil May Cry or the Platinum titles like Bayonetta, Metal Gear Rising, etc. There is one big difference with this one however. You control Briar and Lute, Briar's sister and the spirit that flies around with you. Lute has special powers that can create entropy fields of certain elements (left trigger will be blue, right trigger will be red.) You have to switch between these when fighting the appropriate enemies. Don't worry about remembering them, they'll have red crystals on them or appear like a blue spirit before you can damage them so you don't have to go memorizing a bestiary to remember which field to activate.The combat is really tight. In addition to have to manage which color entropy field you're in, you also get a wide range of weapons as well as dodge and block abilities. Some enemies require you to be very quick with blocks but even if you miss them, you should have time to dodge. You get bonuses for stringing combos together as well as not taking damage beyond just points or leveling up faster, you can even take on a much stronger version of yourself with some huge temporary power boosts within the fight. I really enjoyed the combat overall here.The world is beautiful, particularly the outdoor stages. The indoor areas unfortunately felt a bit repetitive as you progressed through the game where it looks like you're mostly progressing through the same hallways over and over. The camera is static in platforming sections which can, at times, lead to some frustrating missed jumps but you never feel too punished as it usually only takes about 5 seconds to backtrack to where you were. The camera actually works well for hiding goodies. In combat, the camera is free floating or you can lock onto enemies. This is actually where my one big complaint comes in. Some of the arenas, particularly late in the game, are very small. You'll often find yourself in a corner where the camera gets pushed up towards you or maybe gets too close to the enemy you're fighting and the enemy becomes invisible so the camera can focus on you. It can get frustrating when there's a lot going on, especially against stronger enemies since you won't be able to see them start their big swings and know when to dodge. I'm hoping the devs take note of how frustratingly small some arenas feel. I understand making the area small to give it a challenge but the camera work needs some serious work there.That being said, it's still a great game that is absolutely worth your time if you're into spectacle fighters. The story was great, the aesthetic was great, the camera was frustrating at times but the combat was an absolute blast. This game certainly deserves more recognition than it got. I'm hoping they make a sequel and rework the camera a bit, I'd definitely pick it up!
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: It's actually really good at the start, it's a very high quality action game with great environments, lots of skills, enemies with clear tells and different roles to make group fights interesting, and good boss fights that don't drag on too long, basically everything you'd want out of it.Then it introduces mines.The game has a mechanic where you activate a field around you in order to damage objects and certain enemies that you can't hit without having that field active. This works well until the game brings in mines, which respond to the field being active and will explode if they swell too much, heavily damaging you and knocking you away. This mechanic instantly turns combat into an aggravating chore where you have to keep turning the field on and off to avoid triggering mines while fighting, and if an enemy who you need the field to damage decides to park itself on a mine you're stuck just waiting around not being able to do anything until it decides to move away again.I don't think I've ever seen a fun game so thoroughly ruined by a single mechanic so hats off on that one.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely surprise this game is!If you've ever enjoyed a PS2 action game in the vein of the old God of War or Devil May Cry or the like, maybe a Bayonetta here and there, or possibly a Metal Gear Rising and such, you'll feel right at home with Soulstice.It is so rare to get such unapologetically gameplay-centric games of this style in this day and age that I feel like the game could (and maybe should) be appreciated on that basis alone already, but it turns out it is actually pretty damn great beyond that as well!Good presentation (though there is cel-shading involved to some degree, I've come to learn people dislike that approach for some reason); Surprisingly good story (however, if you've read the manga Claymore, you'll probably be able to predict a whole lot of plot points); Very fun, if a bit clunky combat (there really aren't that many combo options available and there is no dodge cancel, but the game is overall rather defense-oriented and wants you to play slow, so that is entirely intentional)There's definitely some jank involved - levels are too long at times (as is the whole game, really), enemies have too much HP, the upgrade resource economy is a bit bloated and there is a clear lack of visual variety here - but it really is very, very competently designed and most importantly: It is a blast to play.Highly, highly recommended - I absolutely do hope more people check this overlooked gem out. All the best and a big thank you to the devs, I genuinely miss games like this and you made a damn good one!

_childDocuments_.review: Seeing so many people compare this game to DMC and other spectacle fighters makes me genuinely consider if those people, and the devs themselves who claim to use those game as the main inspiration for Soulstice, have actually seen gameplay of DMC let alone play it. This game has aggressively stiff combat.Movement is slowDodging is unrewarding and often laggy in executionMost animations have excruciatingly long recoveryEarly 2000s era colour coded enemies forcing you to use specific mechanics before you're allowed to hit enemiesSecret missions that seem to be made exclusively to point at all these short comingsLock-on will focus on the enemy on the other side of the arena instead of the one right in front of youArena barriers are invisible so you'll randomly find yourself in a corner and unable to get outNon-boss enemies shrug off your attacks, while poorly telegraphing their ownInputs are regularly ignored or have weird timings (Have to leave 1/3 second gap between the movement and attack input for the stinger move)Lute as a concept just seems like a convoluted way for damage mitigation instead just making dodging actually usable.Style and gauge are combined meaning if you get hit once you lose all your resources for super moves and whatever this game calls its transformation mechanicSaid super moves can't be used until you complete specific attack strings for the relevant weapon meaning you have to pray you don't get hit while you're doing it.Does the thing Astral Chain did where they assume just because you control two characters at the same time its okay to throw an overwhelming number of enemies encouraging you to just spam the counter button without learning the timings.Honestly was really looking forward to this game, but it genuinely feels like the devs ignored all the progress not just spectacle fighters but games as a whole have made in the past 20 years. Hope it gets fixed in a hotfix, if not, pick it up if you think player freedom is a myth

_childDocuments_.review: Really good action game!Best parts for me are the relationship of the lead characters, the combat, and the visuals. Leads are the two sisters Briar and Lute and I love how their relationship developed throughout the game both with the story and with the gameplay.For the combat, I liked how easy it was to understand but still had depth and challenge to it. Like most big spectacle action games like Bayonetta, this game has a multitude of combos; All based on the weapon in use and how they're used in tandem with other weapons and against varying enemies. But here there's a big focus on using the right weapon against specific enemy types. Even though I felt the levels were kinda bloated, I still think the game did a good job of giving good enemy encounters. And to that point, there's a good variety of fun enemies here to fight.As to the visuals, I think it looks awesome. It's got this nice 3D take on anime. And it all plays even better in motion with all the combos and frantic action of combat. Music was okay. I think the combat track was the only standout of the soundtrack though.Now for the less enjoyable part of the game and it is the actual levels and pace of the campaign. It just felt like it dragged on for too long. After going through the campaign again in a higher difficulty level, it definitely feels faster to go through just because I have all the combos, upgrades, and weapons unlocked. But it still feels too slow paced and going through the campaign the first time was worse. I think a lot of the midgame puzzle platforming could've been cut or maybe just give all the weapons earlier. I don't know really what's a good solution. All I know is that the whole experience just felt like it dragged on. The slow pace also ruined the story for me. In midgame, I had lost interest in the plot and all the villains. The end kind of helped bring me back. But that's mostly because I already cared for the lead characters and I wanted to know how they're story ends.Overall, I think this is an overall great game and I would love a sequel.EDIT: One thing to note though for the PC version. Add in the launch option -d3d11That should force the game to use the directx11 version. the default directx12 version is just a stuttery mess which is a big no no for a fast paced action game.

_childDocuments_.review: +First of all, the camera is classic spectacle fighter, akin to the classic dmc era. This is NOT a bad thing. Its totally legitimate for you to not like a camera type but it does not make it a bad choice. This does not have any fromsoft-esque antagonistic camera.+Every cinematic is framed beautifully. I couldnt stop myself from taking too many screenshots, every single one of these scenes is packed with action and is masterfully composed.+The combat starts a bit barebones, but when you leave behind the early game it really opens up.+This game managed to get right what the dmc reboot did very wrong; the red/blue enemy mechanic is really well done here, it forces you to make interesting decisions in combat but does not prevent you from the enjoying the combat the way you want to.+The point system rewards creativity and incentivizes beying stylish, I really like the addition of the combat actions glossary.+Decent array of enemies and encounters.-The level design is not really diverse, specially in the first third of the game.-Weird difficulty spikes at times, also one or two bosses needed a bit more time in the oven.-The challenges are very hit or miss.-I despise the repentant with every fiber of my being.

_childDocuments_.review: While I want to like this game, the combat just has so many flaws that I have to wonder if the devs have played their own game. A lot of reviews have complained about the camera, and while the camera clearly struggles, I believe the main issue is that enemies have a tendency to rapidly dash away from the player and intentionally hover off-screen. Furthermore, your attack combos have a tendency to knock enemies back - sometimes just slightly too far to follow-up and sometimes to the opposite side of the battleground. This makes it very hard to improvise with combos, since most of your launcher and special attacks have limited range. Your character has a dashing Stinger attack, but it has a tendency to miss - again, sometimes just slipping by the enemy and other times launching you completely the wrong direction. For bonus points, the dashing attack has a time slowdown effect when it impacts, and because of the general enemy mobility you will be spending a lot of time watching your character miss in slow motion.The main selling point of the game is your ghosty companion who fights with you, but I would argue that it is also the worst part of the game. While you can jump and dodge, these both cause you to interrupt your combo so you are reliant on your ghost's contextual counter button to protect you while fighting...except it doesn't do a very good job at all. There are four different kinds of counters and which one she uses is dependent on the attack she is used against. The most common of these counters is the time freeze. The problem? It doesn't actually stop the attack, only delays it for a second or so. At best, this means you have to dodge the attack and lose your combo anyways. At worse, it means getting hit by an attack from off screen because you didn't realize it was still coming. If all these things weren't enough, there's a limit on how many counters can activate in a short time and whether some attacks can even be countered in the first place so sometimes the game doesn't even have the grace to give you a prompt before blasting your character from off-screen.And, to be clear, off-screen attacks are the name of the game. As I mentioned earlier enemies tend to dash rapidly and hover far away from the player. To make matters worse, a significant number of enemies have a red or blue alignment which you can only damage under the appropriate aura. This incentivizes you to hunt down specific enemies but they certainly don't make it easy. They frequently dive away from the player, teleport, or flat out burrow/disappear off screen. All the time your overload meter is slowly ticking up and enemies pepper you with attacks that you can't possibly see coming because of the camerawork.I appreciate that this game exists, and I really do wish I enjoyed it but ultimately I felt like the core mechanics of the game have gone out of their way to be miserable.

_childDocuments_.review: Got it for free on Epic, had to buy it because it was really good and wanted to support the dev.A surprisingly well crafted take on the third person action-adventure genre, the Devil May Cry / Bayonetta / God of War (PS2/3 era) style of action-adventure to be clear, not Dark Souls, absolutely not Dark SoulsStory is good, nothing revolutionary, voice actors could have expressed a bit more emotions IMO, main characters were good tho.Combat is good, very cinematic (you can tone it down if you don't like cutscenes mid battle) with a twist: you control only one of the 2 main characters, the other one act on her own, with the skills you unlock for her, and it has some (yes, more than one) of the most satisfying "Devil triggers" that I ever played, easily putting Bayonetta 3's to shame.Environmentally is a bit repetitive, there's some variation, but the whole game takes place in a single (very big) medieval urban location, so it's acceptable.Overall a good experience that took me 14 hours to complete on a first pass, exploring everything, taking all upgrades, with a NG+ option that lets you cut loose.But that fixed camera......fixed camera is at times really bad, had me rage more than a couple of times...luckily is only there for exploration...

_childDocuments_.review: If you like old-style hack & slash, you can't miss this one.Graphically delightful. Perhaps it deserves a little more optimization, but nothing annoying: the graphic settings offer a wide choice with the addition of DLSS which, if used, does not reveal the slightest difference with an excellent implementation.Very good combat system, you will fight in symbiosis with your sister's soul who has a ton of upgrades (attack, defense, aura and super moves) and will also take care of parrying and slowing down enemy attacks as well as attacking.the primary weapon is a sword that can be upgraded with many alternate moves as well as all other "secondary" weapons that can be combined together in fights.There's a lot of variety in enemies even though the game isn't a souls-like, but the boss battles are challenging anyway. And often they are…big bosses.At the end of the levels your exploits will be evaluated in great detail, from iron to platinum.The game offers a long story that will grab you from start to finish.Really a pleasant surprise between many mediocre titles in a category that I personally love.Give it a chance and you certainly won't regret it.Sometimes in the fights I had the same cooperative feelings that I had with Kratos and his son in God of War :))Really nice game.7.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice: Hack n' Slash Fun with a Sista Twist!Hey there! Just finished playing Soulstice, and wowza, it was an adventure! If you're looking for a game with cool characters, tough fights, and a world full of secrets, then listen up!Sister Power!: The best part? You play as two SISTERS who fight together! Briar smashes enemies with her big ol' sword, while Lute uses her ghost powers to blast them from afar. It's like a super cool tag team, and figuring out how to use their powers together was awesome.Challenge Accepted!: This game isn't a walk in the park. There were times, especially at the beginning, where I got totally wrecked. But that just made it more satisfying when I finally mastered a tough enemy or boss. Learning from your mistakes is half the fun, right?Creepy Cool World: Soulstice's world is dark and mysterious, but in a way that's kinda cool. Exploring these spooky ruins and figuring out what happened was like being in a giant monster movie. Plus, the music is fantastic – it gets you pumped for battle!Camera Shy Sometimes: The game isn't perfect though. Sometimes the camera decided to play peek-a-boo during fights, especially in tight spaces. A little frustrating, but nothing a determined monster slayer can't overcome!Final Verdict: Even with the occasional camera hiccup, Soulstice is a blast! The combat is intense, the world is intriguing, and the story of these two sisters is heartwarming. If you're looking for a game that will challenge you and keep you coming back for more, this is totally the one for you!

_childDocuments_.review: A game more than often compared to DMC but to me feels closer to god of war (old gen). Fighting mechanics and combo are kept really simple on the surface but for good reason as you'll need to master the game to truly feel how awesome the fighting really is.Game forces you to play better to be able to use your power with all it's potential which might not be for everyone as mistake are punishing but once you do master it you'll crush enemy left and right with more power than ever.(For those saying the game is clunky i swear to god they never played the first 3 dmc cause for having finished them recently this game is a freaking master piece in comparison which is not to blame on them since those game are old but anyway)Probably not the prettiest game of 2022 but i personally am charmed with it even with it's flaws (some movement can be really stiff in cinematic but to me are easily forgivable with the amount of great scene).Musics are great and fits really well more than often would make me just vibe with it while being on a rampage.Story and universe is awesome and really make you want to know more about it (at least to me) but won't go into detail to not spoil it.Overall a great game which makes me want more.Pro:- Great combat mechanic, simple yet hard to master and very rewarding once it is- Story and universe enticing and so are characters (shout out to that one npc in a particular scene with a terrible voice actor)- Music that gets you in the mood to destroy everything- Badass and hype cinematics - Great design overallCons:- Invisible walls everywhere are the bane of my existence- Heavily punishing if you make too many mistake in combat which is not for everyone (or just Git Gud) - Camera can be annoying more than often

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly solid game that I think struggles to do its girls justice. On a moment to moment basis, I absolutely adore Soulstice; tight gameplay with an incredible sense of spectacle as you hack and slash through ghoulish hordes. The main gameplay conceit, with one character in charge of dealing damage and the other mitigating it simultaneously, feels GENIUS and feels really well polished. Great weapon selection as well, even if I wish the individual weapons had a unique input/utility a piece. If you're here for an edgy beat-em-up with super well implemented fixed camera, you'll find yourself right at home.Where I struggle a bit with my recommendation comes down to the writing. I just feel like the main duo struggle to maintain a personality outside of their sisterhood. Which, sure, maybe we're not here for the writing, but when the leading women in your game are flagged by either their sense of sisterhood, trauma, or vanity... it just doesn't feel very Girls' Night. Give us a bit more to chew on.I ADORE Briar's Rapture/Berserk forms, though. Keep that energy up forever. More rip + tear girlies forever.I also do kind of feel like the game starts to drag a bit around the middle; just a few missions that feel like they could be trimmed down an encounter or two, that otherwise set the boss fights and truly memorable encounters further away from each other. And those pop moments REALLY pop; there are some excellent settings and engagements all throughout Soulstice, and I thought every boss fight really swung for the fences. After teasing a sequel as hard as they do right at the end, I do hope they can put together a tighter, leaner, meaner game that hits right for fans of sickos women everywhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like the game because I'm desperate for more Character Action Games but this thing is just a mess.Great theme, nice art style, good combat music, okay-ish combat, old fixed angle camera for cinematic effect, a lot of platformings, cutscenes every now and then, if you played DMC 1-4 then you know how it's like.The combat is quite basic, string combos like Bayonetta/Nier Automata with one command inputs (forward+forward+heavy), some charge attacks that are totally worthless, no perfect dodge, no enemy step, only two air combos which is just different combo enders, stinger, launcher, helm breaker that require you to press 2 buttons at the same time because the game use hard lock like Souls so unless you can get comfortable with the default keybind, good luck rebinding it without being awkward or sacrifice some attacks to be able to use B as dodge like almost every action game and the default keybind sucks.Weapons all feel the same, they use the same inputs to do the same things, only a few movesets per weapon and I understand this is only a AA game, there are indie games that has better animations, fluidity, varieties, combos that cost the same or even lower price e.g. Blazblue Entropy Effect. The only difference between weapons is that this weapon is better at breaking armor while that weapon is stronger against flying enemies, that kind of stuff which make me feel like the game is inspired by DmC: DMC which is more like an Action-Adventure game than a true DMC game, there's no freedom in combat, just puzzles and QTEs during combat.Counter system is a mess, your character doesn't do the counter, it's the sister who do it and she doesn't counter immediately like every other game, it's more like QTEs with input queuing so the support character can do the counters without interrupting your character attacks. There are 3 types of counters; slow time, interrupt action and deflect, you'll have no idea which type of counter she's gonna do because you don't counter base on the enemy animation, you have to press counter as soon as it popped up to perform a perfect counter which is near impossible during combat because there are so many things on the screen, enemies attacking you from outside the screen, enemies with uncounterable attacks, managing red/blue field to attack specific types of enemies, managing your field resource so your sister don't become overloaded and disappear for few seconds leaving you unable to attack red/blue enemies and it's not just that you can't attack the red/blue enemies, your attack will bounce, leaving you vulnerable for 1s.Color coding is literally the worst thing you can do in an Action game, did you learn nothing from DmC: DMC failure? You even made it worse by letting the character have a limited resource to counter enemies.Some secret challenge missions feels like they have never been playtested because they are extremely annoying to do and I have over 1000 hours in Souls and Roguelike/lite so I know a thing or two about learning from failures, these missions are objectively worse than the campaign.Level variety is non-existent, I played for around 13 missions and they all look the same, literally, some sections of later missions are just reused assets from earlier missions, I never felt like I made any progress, everywhere I go they just look the same.I don't have much problem with the camera, don't fight it and most of the time it works, lock-on fast enemies can be a bit wonky but fine most of the time. The platforming sections however, I detest them, it's an old and outdated design to keep player engaging. DMC 5 is the proof for good gameplay can keep player engaging without long cinematic cutscenes, QTEs, long dialogues, a game with pure moment to moment action combat can definitely survive in modern gaming.Just go play DMC 3 or Assault Spy and don't bother with this. I'll give them another chance if they ever made a sequel or a new game that's inspired by DMC 5 instead because there are some potentials in this game, it's just that these problems bother me way too much to even finish this game on easiest mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? It is a typical action-adventure game in which a heroine has to keep order with oversized... weapons. We play Briar, a young warrior with superhuman abilities, who slashes her way through hordes of monsters in a completely deserted city full of fire and destruction. She can jump several meters from a standing position, perform a double jump and jump even higher or farther, can fall from great heights without hurting herself, can escape from dicey situations with a dash. At the beginning of the game, she wears a huge sword on her back, which turns into an oversized warhammer at the press of a button. Inseparable from Briar is her little sister Lute, who accompanies her everywhere as a small ball of energy and can actively give support in battle. She also chats all the time. In the course of the game we learn more about the two of them and how they became this fighting machine.In Ilden a tear has occurred that allows shadow creatures to invade the world. Dark beings seize control of the inhabitants, who subsequently destroy everything and turn the city into a field of rubble. So the High Council sends us out to clean up the mess. Actually they send out three of us, three chimeras, fighters with superhuman abilities. But the other two have apparently already left without us. So we end up all alone in the port of the city to go in search of our colleagues and investigate the events in the city. Layton, who is leading the mission, is supposed to help us, but we have to find him first as well.We find Layton relatively quickly, but he is anything but happy to have been given this mission. He doesn't really consider us competent. It also bothers him that we obviously have corrupted blood. No matter, he is still an interesting interlocutor and tells us quite a bit about the background history. He also exchanges splitters we've collected for new abilities and combos for us and our sister, respectively. Layton, who accompanies us out of hiding on our mission, is thus more or less a walking merchant and trainer. Interactions with the environment are relatively limited. We can kill (almost completely harmless) zombies shuffling around, smash crates and barrels, and destroy furnishings to obtain splitters. There are also levers to pull or doors to open in some places. The interaction points are always quite well marked.The battles take place in (more or less) small arenas, from which we can't move during the fight. You can rotate the view with the right stick to keep an overview. We usually fight several (3-5) enemies at the same time, and as soon as enemies die, new enemies teleport into the battle area (until eventually no more come). We can center the view on one enemy so as not to lose sight of him. Briar only knows a few combos at first, but can learn many more combos for the different weapons that can be found as the game progresses. For example, one of Briar's abilities is to fling enemies into the air and then work on the defenseless opponents in mid-air. Kind of reminded me a lot of Bayonetta or Devil May Cry.At the beginning of the game, our little sister Lute only has the ability to briefly stop time around us. This allows us to dodge an attack and in turn pummel the now motionless opponent. As the game progresses, Lute learns new abilities. For example, she can create either a blue or a red field around us for a certain amount of time - and certain enemies or objects can only take damage in the appropriate field. Working well with our sister charges up a special bar that allows us to perform a synergy attack together. Battles end with a result screen (if we survived the fight). Here we get a score and an overall rating (bronze, silver, gold, platinum, diamond) depending on how well we did (how fast we were, what special actions we performed).Is it actually a Souls-like game? After all, the word "Souls" even appears in the title. But the answer is a clear no, it is more of a typical action adventure game in hack and slash style, where we slash our way through countless smaller monsters that can hardly be dangerous to us individually, but should not be underestimated due to their number. Of course, there are also stronger enemies that kill us with a few hits. There is no stamina bar, but Briar can only dash three times before this ability has to regenerate. When we die, we restart at the last automatic save point. We don't have to search for our corpse, we just start over a little further back... though the save points are quite far apart and by no means save after every fight. You may have to do some battles, explorations and annoying jump passages again after your demise. You'll keep finding (sometimes a bit hidden) special portals that lead you to special challenges (for example, defeating your opponents under time pressure and with at least five successful blocks). These challenges can be retried later (from the main menu) as often as you like. If you fail them, you won't suffer any disadvantages, if you succeed, there are of course rewards.The detailed, gritty isometric graphics with countless animations (burning objects, flying sparks, fog, water, rain, flags in the wind...) perfectly support 21:9 as well as 4K. Many short cutscenes (and a few longer ones) provide variety. There were no stutters on my RTX 1070 graphics card - you really can't complain here. Destructible objects draw attention to themselves by blinking. Our heroine gets smaller when she moves backwards in a level, but sometimes almost too small to be able to act accurately.A lavishly produced hack and slash action adventure with good graphics, fast battles against hordes of disfigured, possessed humans or monsters from another dimension, plus huge bosses and a constantly chattering sister at your side - maybe not a masterpiece, but an uncompromising slaughterfest with the new aspect that we also control our little sister at the same time.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is an amazing game with a lot of soul and passion put into it and I love it to pieces. It has similar themes/is inspired by things such as Berserk, but it is completely its own identity and goes off so well. The gameplay is in a similar fashion to games like Devil May Cry and Nier but with its own unique take. You have a variety of weapons to switch between on the fly, have a fun system where doing well in combat increases the unity/bond between the two main characters to allow for stronger attacks/transformations and certain enemies need you to jump between different coloured effects in order to defeat.The world setting and lore is honestly great and made me feel the love for the game behind it all. The story really draws you in and really leaves you wanting to spend more time in the world. The cutscenes in the game are stunning in their animation and really stand out. The two main characters, Briar and Lute, are written incredibly well in my opinion, and are raised even higher by incredible voice acting (both characters being voiced by the same VA as well, yet sounding COMPLETELY different!). The designs of characters and enemies, especially bosses, are phenomenal and the world itself looks absolutely gorgeous despite all the destruction being wrought. The developers deserve so much praise for creating such an experience and I am praying they do more games for Soulstice!!My only personal complaint would be that sometimes, as others have said, the camera can kind of work against you - but it was never something that ruined the experience for me. It ran really smoothly and the gameplay was incredibly fun.tldr: If you are even a bit interested in the game and like games like DMC or Nier, I am begging you to get it and support the developers. Its such a passion project and looks gorgeous, with fun gameplay and two wonderful protagonists that work off each-other so well.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried really hard to like it, but it's just too unrefined for its own good.Moves you unlock should all be basic ones, most are repeats. Some attacks comes out of nowhere as i've found out in a no-touch challenge later in the game. The Red/Blue system is the worst system i've ever encountered in a Character Action, it's pointless.Lock-on is borderline meaningless, it doesn't ''lock'' as much as ''puts a reticle'' on an enemy. SFX are unsatisfying, camera is wonky, also a worst version of the low health DT in DMC2.It like, it takes the worst aspect of every single Character Action game, and somehow has less depth than that Ghost Rider PS2 game, which, great game btw.I dislike being mean on an indie game and all, there's interesting stuff here, but nothing comes together, I'd take less weapons if it meant having more interesting moves for instance. It's just, it's just the most 4 out of 10 game I've ever played, I'm sorry, it's not fun jank, it's just jank.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I would like this game. I didn't think I'd love it. But I'm happy to be wrong. This game is amazing and I had a blast the whole way through. Soulstice follows in the footsteps of other over-the-top action games like Bayonetta and Devil May Cry, but personally I liked the setting and story of Soulstice a lot more. The backstory and lore were interesting, and I really like that even though the levels themselves were not actually that big, the devs made them feel epic in scale with backgrounds that stretch way off into the distance. Obviously combat is the most important part of this game, and I loved it. It was smooth and fast paced with a good variety of enemies. A word of caution though - by the end of the game, combat is pretty hectic with a ton of stuff happening all over the screen. You'll be comboing, dodging, countering, turning 'fields' on and off, watching the unity meter, using synergy attacks, and switching weapons on the fly to use the right one against the right enemy. If that sounds like too much then maybe this isn't the game for you, but if you put in some effort to get to where you can handle all that and come out the other side with a diamond or platinum rating, you feel like such a boss. But also, if you still want to experience the game despite the difficulty, there are some options to make combat waaay easier and accessible to more casual players. A lot of people complained about the camera, but patches have since improved it and I was fine with it. It just takes some getting used to. I think a lot of players feel paranoid initially about sometimes having enemies off screen, but eventually you learn how to pay attention to the counter indicators, and you get a sense of what you do and don't really have to worry about, and what enemies to prioritize first. Also it seems like some players had graphical or stuttering issues, but I can say it hasn't been a problem for me. The game runs perfectly fine on my old gtx 1650 laptop.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is set in a dark-fantasy world with developing characters. Following the journey of two sisters, a cautious handler and fiery reject warrior. Sent to a desolate high city to investigate and clear the way of hostile forces found for the main army. They speak to each other while traveling or  fighting, keeping the silence away. Both changing as the story develops.The gameplay is balanced between fighting difficulties, and brain-dead puzzles. You're provided a red-blue color system to match most enemy types, and a few weapons to counter them. Abilities and Weapons upgrades are acquired by purchasing or completing Trials found throughout the game. Completing a combination attack with the same weapon will trigger a "synergy" attack that does higher damage, and has wider/longer hit box.The OST is a sound of Electric Symphonic Metal, fitting the gritty dystopian particle heavy world that will rotate tracks on fights.  The core cons to the game is it's camera positioning for some portions of the game, and animation locking for specific attacks.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible nostalgia scratcher from games like Devil May Cry and God of War.Story is new, interesting and fun to keep up with.Gameplay is fun, impactful, unique. The Red/Blue aura mechanic is new and a challenging kind of fun. The second character acting as a independent support is great plus the parry system feels very nice, being able to parry dozens of enemies around you while focusing on one or more. The scoring system showing up every battle feels great as an instant reward and as a pointer for wether you're doing good or could do better.The animations and visuals are beautiful, AAA type quality.I was very pleasently surprised.IMHO a true hidden gem.

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice surprise and it exceeded my expectations !Soulstice deliver a good fast paced and satisfying combat system.Honestly chaining combos feels really nice and the last time I enjoyed the combat that much in a game it was with Devil May Cry 5.Of course the combat system in Soulstice is not perfect and it does have it's flaws, most issues will come later in the game though.In the later levels the combat will become quite chaotic with lots of enemies on screen and it can be hard to avoid getting hit by some spinning enemies or AOE attacks.So no the combat in Soulstice is not as good as Devil May Cry, Bayonetta or God of War, it can become confusing and it can get a bit repetitive but it's still really well done.The game also have great characters and monsters design, the animations are top notch and the graphics looks really nice too, there's some pretty amazing vistas to be found here.Soulstice level design is good but very linear, it still does reward exploration and you will get extra items if you take time to explore the levels.Unfortunately the fixed camera angles and some platforming parts can get annoying at times but nothing too bad.Average first playthrough should be around 16-25 hours depending on which difficulty you choose and if you do challenges and explore the maps.If you grew up playing the afformentioned titles and enjoy character action games then give it a shot, pretty sure you won't be disappointed.Soulstice ain't game of the year material but it's definitely a good game knowing it was made by a very small team.Honestly for such a small team I think they did really well and this game feature really high production values IMHO.All in all we get good voice acting, quality cutscenes, slick looking menus and most importantly a great combat system.Now about the pricing, well I think 40€ is a steep price, especially at this time of the year when there's tons of new games coming out.The game is good but considering DMC 5 is now being sold at less than 10€ on sale I think waiting for a discount for Soulstice might be your best option if you are unsure about the game.It's a nice game but it's far from perfect, there are issues and some weird design decisions like how the unity system works, some strange choices in colors which can mess with player visibility.Anyway I have to say congratulations Reply Game Studios I really like your game and I'll be sure to follow whatever you create going forward.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version, this is why I hate the binary 'yes or no' aspect of steams reviews. Do I recommend this game? For the average person, god no stay away. For someone that's a fan of Devil May Cry and wants to play a game like it? Absolutely, but pick it up on sale, this game is far too jank and far too infuriating in its later stages to warrant full price.I beat this game on its normal mode, Initiate.GraphicsThe game has a heavy anime style to it and on the surface it looks fantastic and runs okay. The biggest issue however is that the game only takes place in a single environment... for 20 hours. So you'll be spending 20 hours in the same castles, sewers and monasteries that are all blue or teal. Except the final 3 levels where the game throws you a curveball and makes everything PURPLE. Yeah, not great. This game is already way too damn long, and the fact every level sort of blend into one another does not help one bit. So even though the game looks nice, the lack of variety hurts replayability heavily.StoryThe game has HEAVY inspiration from the Berserk and Claymore mangas, which I'd recommend checking out if you thought this game's story was cool. Claymore is also a story about a mysterious organization fusing humans with other wordly forces to become living weapons, and if they push themselves too far they 'awaken' and become powerful demons themselves. Berserk is present here more in the aesthetics and general vibe of everything instead of actual story content. Briar makes quite a few guts poses on her journey though, so there's that.SPOILERSThe game ends on a cliffhanger with  superheavy sequel-baiting, which is infuriating considering how much padding this game has, by the end of the game it feels like we're only about halfway through the actual narrative, which after 20 hours of fast frenetic gameplay is a bit of a slap in the face. At the same time, I do hope they make a sequel, because this game could really use a further refinement of its ideas and combat. The biggest issue with the story is that there's actually too damn much of it. This is a character action game, not a AAA adventure game like God of War, I'm here to play video game not sit and listen to characters talk for 20 minutes every level. Each and every level is filled with dialogue and cutscenes, damaging replayability severely. LevelsThis game is TOO DAMN LONG. Getting it yet? This game is around 19-21 hours in length on average, which is kinda nuts for a character action game. Most of the ones I've played personally are usually 6-10 hours on average, half of this game, and are usually packed with far more actual story and have a much higher variety of environments to explore. Most levels blend together and don't really feel all that unique, I just beat the game 10 minutes ago and the only levels I remember off the top of my head are the boss levels and the elevator. That's it. I remember 5/25 levels after just beating the game. Oof. CombatThe actual core combat is actually super solid. Hits feel chunky, animations are satisfying, the sounds are satisfying, enemies explode into gore when killed which is fun. You have massive arsenal of weapons at your disposal, including a chain whip, a sword-axe combo, a bow, blade gauntlets, and more. The weapon variety is fun and the combos are cool, but most weapons' movesets sort of blend together and do the same things. This makes switching between them easy, but it also means the only reason you'd ever take out more than just the sword is for the sake of your score, and the fact that enemies have weaknesses to specific weapons.Lute's abilities are cool, but her (aka your) defensive options are severely lacking. When it comes to larger enemies or bossfights, all you can do is use the slowdown counter, which doesn't actually make them stop their attack, all it really does is slow the fight to a crawl and due to the iffy nature of your dodge i-frames, means most fights against larger foes turns into a game of touch-and-go, which is awful. CameraThis games camera is awful. Like im just gonna come out and say it. It's bad. Fixed camera angles aren't the issue here, its more that the camera is so damn far away from the action at times its impossible to tell whats happening. Not to mention, the game expects precision platforming of you with these fixed camera angles, yknow, when you have 0 depth perception??? There was a platforming segment near the end of the game that really drove me nuts because of this, I feel like it wasn't even playtested. A lot of this game's later half feels like that. EnemiesThe enemies have a great variety, which is good. The enemies are also more often than not, a pain to fight, which is bad. You fight way too many enemies, and the enemies have way too much health, turning most fights into incredibly dragged out slogs that can take forever to end. I was only playing on normal, and the time to kill for most enemies was absurd. I thought this meant the health of enemies was shared on all difficulties, which would've been great, but no, I went up to Knight to try it out and enemy health was damn near DOUBLED. It already takes half a year to kill some of the enemies like the summoners, why in god's name would you make that take even longer??? Honestly, some of the par times on some of these fights have to be a joke, I refuse to believe anyone tested some of the combat encounters.Enemies lack any good telegraphs. As you play you get mentally conditioned to see Lute's counter prompt as the indication of incoming attacks, when this isn't shown, you have so little time to react its usually impossible to get out of the way in time. Enemies have such little telegraphing its nuts, no audio cues, barely any visual cues. Even the massive lumbering dudes with the hammers give you less than half a second before they swing, which is just nuts, and incredibly unfair and unfun to fight against. This extends to when they are out of view of the camera, all you get is a red arrow, which doesn't tell you anything, especially if its an incoming ranged attack. You're too busy juggling a million other things to focus on the arrows anyways, enemies need more obvious visual and audio cues, otherwise the combat becomes incredibly unfair really fast. Also they can stunlock you and wombo-combo you into oblivion, which, yknow, that's great. BossesBosses are hit or miss, the first true boss you face in level 14, Jared, is a super fun and satisfying encounter. The next true boss you face, the bird lady, is alright, but she spends too much of the fight running away and she has way too much health, making her a chore to fight. The second-to-last boss is fun, but the final boss. Hoo-boy. Whoever thought it was a good idea to end their game off with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SAVIOR FROM DMC4, ONE OF THE WORST BOSSES IN DMC HISTORY, should be fired or slapped several times in the face for gross incompetence. One of the only times in the game I ever used an item, I just really wanted it to be over with, an absolutely awful fight and it definitely soured the rest of the experience for me. MusicMusic is good, a solid score overall, though my favorite track, the song that plays in the challenge rooms, is not available in the official soundtrack. Please fix. Voice ActingVoice acting is amateur, but you can tell they’re giving it their all. Hammy performances all around, but I give an A for aeffort. Except the bird lady, her VA was downright awful. Layton’s VA was my favorite.  ConclusionThis pains me, because I did have a lot of points where I had a ton of fun, but also a ton of points where this game absolutely infuriated me. The game is far too long, far too padded, and far too janky. I will not be playing this game again, that's for certain. Which is unfortunate, cause I do feel it has a lot of potential. I hope if that fated sequel ever arrives, it fixes a lot of the issues I have with this game as it stands.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fantastic!I was not ready for how attached to the characters I became. There were so many pitfalls the devs could have tripped in but they did an incredible job with Briar and Lute. For example, they NEVER fight or bicker. I can't tell you how utterly refreshing it is to have characters in a bleak setting trust each other like they do - and it feels earned. The gameplay rips. The weapons are cool and versatile with great sound design; and all your enemies explode into nice meaty chunks. Not a lot to complain about. Setting is great. It's kinda a play on the big spooky castle - except an entire city. It gets a little samey, but they mix it up well enough. Soundtrack kicks all kinds of ass. Wish we had more tracks.Camera isn't as bad as many people make it seem. It's an oldschool design choice that carries with it the oldschool problems. The real issue is the lock-on button, which can be unresponsive at times when trying to switch to a new target. The game can be really challenging on harder difficulties. Even when maxed out, one mistake can cost you. The game has got some serious bite which I love.

_childDocuments_.review: I really-really want to like this game, I love a lot of the things it does, but it falls so flat in gameplay that I just can't recommend it.I love the artstyle. I love most of the enemy designs, at least in terms of visuals. The music is great. The characters are decent. The story is alright. I LOVE the fixed camera angles during exploration and platforming, they are absolutely delicious.But my God, the combat is just not good, and combat is what you will be doing most of the time in this game, so it needs to be good. A lot of enemies barely react to your attacks. You hit an enemy with a huge two-handed sword and you might as well be hitting them with a wet noodle with how little they react to it. Secondary weapons don't feel different enough, they all have the same moves, and only real difference between them is the skill price and what type of enemies they deal extra damage to.The proficiency system is also bad because a lot of the times the combat is too frantic to pull off the more advanced combos, especially seeing how enemies don't really react to your attacks much, and since you don't get a lot of opportunity to pull off cool combos you kinda just purchase proficiency upgrades just to deal more damage per hit to specific enemies because otherwise the combat is just gonna be tedious.Also the combat camera is absolutely god awful. Devs had these amazing fixed camera angles that show the entire arena and for some reason they decided to just not use them, instead replacing them with a super claustrophobic free camera that makes it hard to keep track of the entire arena, making the combat even worse as you can't see enemies attacking from behind and stuff. The little warning arrows they put in the game don't really help either.Also the blocking system with Lute is bad. It's a neat concept, but the execution is horrible. It would've been better if you combined the dodge and block button into one, so if you stand still - you block and if you block and move - you dodge, and have Lute be more of a manual thing, allowing you to choose when to shoot her magic blasts instead of it happening automatically. And then instead of having three different types of block you could have Lute freeze enemies on a perfect dodge and stun them on a perfect block, and have her return fire if you perfect block a projectile, not have this weird system where the kind of block you get is determined by the type of enemy you're blocking against. Plus the windows on blocking attacks are so abysmally short, they maybe could've worked with a more traditional block system but they just don't mesh with the existing system at all.Edit: I have re-evaluated my thoughs a little bit on the combat system - it works well for boss fights. Especially when you're fighting the transcended, those fights work (mostly) well with the combat system this game has. But it just kinda falls apart when you're fighting regular enemies, which is obviously something you encounter way more than bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this in one of those Fanatical Bundles a while ago. I really liked the dark fantasy atmosphere in this game. Not sure about the story since I skipped every cutscene. The color switching mechanic became way too tedious for my liking. The fixed camera is annoying but not a dealbreaker for me. Actually, I think It adds a cinematic flair to the otherwise dull environments. My dealbreaker is the fact that bosses that can heal themselves. They already have massive health bars and to just add that nonsense is a huge slap in the face for the "easy" difficulty I was playing on. Common enemies are already extremely spongy. Seems like most enemies took like 20 hits to kill, no matter what weapon combo I used. If you can put up with the above annoyances, you might enjoy this long indie game (at 11 hours I was not even halfway through the game according to guides) but I just couldn't take any more of the spongy enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is a great and polished AA-tier game, but not without its downsidesLet's break it down:1. SettingDevelopers drew inspiration from such mangas as Berserk, written by Kentaro Miura and Claymore, written by Norihiro Yagi. It really shows, especially when it comes to Claymore - what we have is chaos spawns that pose a great danger to humanity and special warrior breed created for the sole purpose of defeating them. What's so special about them, you ask? They are partly chaos spawns themselves! Very dangerous, if you ask me.World is torn apart by those monsters and countless villages and people suffer horrific fate, while it's not even what they should fear the most - The Veil. The Veil is basically, well, a barrier that protects this world from chaos realm, birthplace of all chaos spawns.This sure smells like something I would like, and I was right - I really love this setting. C'mon, it's dark fantasy, after all.2. PlotWell, I will be honest, plot is not something new or unique, it's predictable, although still quite curious and breathtaking in a way. Remember The Veil mentioned above? Usually, just a small quantity of chaos spawns can tear through The Veil, and even they can wipe whole villages, you can fathom what would happen if The Veil is to be torn.The Veil was torn and so chaos spawns rush into this world. But how can this be even possible, how The Veil was torn? What exactly happened here, in Ilden? Find out yourself...I think it's worth mentioning that their story is not quite finished in Soulstice, they obviously have plans for a sequel.3. CharactersCan't say much about characters, there are too few and most of them won't appear until the very end. I feel like they got too little attention and were discarded, aside of a few chosen ones.Chosen ones get some proper developments though.4. Style & MusicStyle is heavily inspired by Claymore and a little bit by Berserk, but still shows something new. Claymore shows almost everywhere - boss designs, special abilities of main characters, some enemy designs, locations.Main character, Briar, is basically a female Guts (Berserk main character). Not a bad thing, not a bad thing at all. I love it greatly!Music? Yeah, about that. It's a little bit unusual to hear electo music mixed up with some epic notes, but it's always used properly and still fits what's happening around you. But also, I love me some epic chorus.5. Locations & Level designThat's where some issues start to appear - locations are pretty, but seem kinda identical. I had a feeling I didn't leave the sewers for like 70% of the game.Locations are mostly linear, but some of them can surprise you.Each level is full of different puzzles and platforming elements, they can be annoying at times, but add to variety of gameplay and it feels nice to do something other than fighting hordes of enemies while you advance further.6. GameplayFirst things first - Soulstice has a system with blue and red auras you can use to destroy crystals that block your path, get some currency or jump on specific platforms. That being said, they also are used in combat - and hooo boy, it's a pain in the ass. Maybe it was a difficulty issue (I completed the game on Knight difficulty), but there were too many enemies and too many of elite ones especially. Elite enemies, you see, have two types, just as well as auras - red and blue. Both of them cannot be damaged without correct aura usage, and that's where the fun starts - red enemies (most of them) spawn blue enemies when they are defeated and you need to destroy blue enemies, otherwise red one you just defeated will ressurect. Now imagine that you fight dozens of red enemies, dozens of blue enemies, you need to block them all, use correct aura and make sure not to overuse it so you can't activate it for some time. Sounds like a bother, right?Weapons. There are seven weapons in total, each effective against certain enemy types, you can freely switch between them and chain combos, it's a slasher, after all. Combos are fine, but main weapon (starting sword) is always with you and has too few combos, which is kinda strange.Devil Trigger? Yeah, we have that! They made it look really cool actually and made sure to make it your last resort - since you kinda go full berserk mode and harm yourself more than usual - you can't block or parry attacks, only dodge them. I won't go into details - see for yourself, it's really cool.7. BossfightsThere are too few "real bosses", they have some questionable design choices but overall they are gorgeous and I love them. Aside maybe one them, I won't tell you which, but this boss is annoying as hell and I spent a few hours beating the crap out of them (there are platforming and illusions involved). What's so gorgeous about them, you ask? Well, they are a walking bullet-hell and melee death threat, and plus, honestly, they are stylish, and I love stylish things.8. Final wordsI think I reviewed everything I had on my mind and I hope it helps you decide on whether you want to pick this game or no. It was a very painful experience, but a very enjoyable one. Will play this game's sequel with great pleasure.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played the first 4 chapters so far but I've really enjoyed it all, as many of the other comments say the game is very similar in style to Devil May Cry, personally the "vibe" it gives me is similar to the first game in the series, which is my favourite, so I was pretty happy with that! Also being one of those weirdos who really liked the first castlevania LOS games the game reminds me of that too, and I like the inclusion of using different fields to be able to damage different types of enemies while managing the meter to do so (not quite the same as LOS, but a similar mechanic imo). If I could make one change it would be to be able to switch out both weapons, instead of just the secondary, however this is only minor.I can only assume that Briar was inspired by the main character from Claymore, mashed with Guts's penchant for spiky black armour, both of these make for (imo) an instantly cool and interesting character action protagonist. (but if not then well great job devs for coming up with a cool design like this!). The story so far hasn't revealed too much, but it seems really interesting so far, and I'm looking forward to finding more out about the world and characters.At first the game was a bit stuttery in the opening section, and turning my graphics down did not fix this, however this problem has gone away as i played past the opening section. I have read that this is an unreal engine 4 problem, and that the devs would need to make an update to how caching is handled by the game to fix this, so I am hopeful that there will soon be an update to the game to fix this issue, as it does rather take you out of the moment right at the start of the game, during what is clearly meant to be an exciting and climactic fight when the game drops it's framerate by half for short periods multiple times.Other than the early game stuttering, the game has been great fun so far, and I'm looking forward to playing more soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you Devs!Not every action game needs to be souls-like, Rouge-like!Don't get me wrong, these can be fun too, but it's been a while since we got one of these more DMC-like games!** Scroll down to the bottom for a note about older Polaris AMD cards performance.This game will take you back to the good old PS2/PS3 days, with some quality of life additions.So, classic level to level progress, stylish combat, ridiculous* slow mo cutscenes, bosses that talk too much and fixed camera angles!*Not as ridiculous as DMC and DmC, but still ridiculous enough.The combat execution itself isn't that complex, but it offers more and more layers and options as you progress, acquire new weapons and encounter new enemies. It is a bit like Ninja Theory's DmC with it's Blue and Red thing.In general it feels really good when you get the hang of it.One of the biggest criticism this game gets is the fixed camera angles, and how it likes to pull all the way back during exploration. For me, it certainly felt pretty jarring as I started off, even though I've played games like this in the past.And I think it is that this game does it a lot more often, and the levels themselves have pretty big spaces.Although later on it didn't bother me as much.As for combat, they give you camera controls, as well as the options to adjust both camera distance and field of view (which you'll need to max out for some optional challenges).The level design while I liked the design itself, visually, they could have used more variety. Like most of the game is just gray, same castle environment. And I get it is the color palette they choose to set the mood, but in 25 hours I finished the game, it got a bit repetitive seeing the same visuals, same lighting.I played on normal and the difficulty felt fair, only one boss in particular annoyed me quite a bit. But there are many difficulty levels, and even easier ones with assist should you wish.Sometimes the combat can become a bit overwhelming, with the number of enemy types and stuff on screen, and I think some enemies could use a bit of balance. Some are way too tanky imo.There is level replay, and hidden challenges to clear, so there a lot to replay and enjoy this game.You get ranks for combat and level clear, but no immediate ranking like DMC (A, B, C....). Instead you get Iron, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum and Diamond. The better your rank, the more points you earn to spend on upgrades.Anyway for a small indie team, and for a new IP, this is really really good! I had a great time playing this and looking forward to more!I paid full price for this and I'd say it is 100% worth it!**Note: If you have one of the older AMD cards, like my RX480, expect to encounter a glitch in one of the levels. Due to a certain particle effect, the game locks itself to 15 FPS in a certain portion of the level. _childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is a 3rd person action game that focuses on fast and frenetic combat with characters and enemies that have a dark anime aesthetic.The cutscenes are good, even if the voice acting is uneven.  I enjoyed the combat as I improved with it and I was invested in the world enough that I would like to find out what happens in a sequel.  I spent about 50 hours to finish the game--and most challenges--on Knight (hard) difficulty without using items.  If you have any interest in this type of game, it is worth at least one playthrough.There are a couple issues I think kept this from being more popular:INFLUENCESFirst, I think it misses the most important features of the games it resembles (and possibly was inspired by).  The combat system is similar to Devil May Cry in that you are expected to keep up a continuous stream of actions against waves of enemies.  You even get a score and rating at the end of each battle, and at the end of each chapter.  Unfortunately, Devil May Cry fans often cite the creative possibilities of the combat as their favorite feature, and Soulstice combos are relatively simple.  You eventually obtain several weapons, but they mostly differ in that each will do more damage to specific enemies.  Otherwise it's just different animations.  They all have launchers, they all have gap closers, they all have delay combos, and they all have air slam attacks...and they all are done the same way on the controller.  You can switch between weapons in mid-combo, but that isn't to use the weapons for different purposes, it's just because it should increase your score.Since the combos are simple, I thought that perhaps the game wanted to be closer to the older God Of War games.  Unfortunately, the God Of War games were more about journeys through interesting levels and epic boss fights, and Soulstice's levels--while interesting to look at--lack much variety (note that this is also similar to Devil May Cry).CAMERA AND CONTROLS Second, the controls have some weird decisions.  Many of the complaints have to do with the fact that the game uses a fixed-camera at times.  This is mostly only between combat engagements, but occasionally for combat as well.  I rarely had any issues with these sequences, and I had very little issue platforming during these segments.The camera issue I have is the decision to keep the camera up close to your character during combat where the camera is free.  Enemies can and will attack you from off screen.  Some attacks have indicators before they pop, but it's still maddening have to constantly try and take the time to move your character to a position and rotate the camera to see important enemies that you may not be currently engaged with, and that is important because......you have a companion that has the ability to interrupt attacks from enemies.  You may be interrupting several attacks in quick succession, and you are trying to attack and dodge with the main character at the same time, so you can't be expected to learn a specific interrupt timing for each attacks.  Instead you get a button prompt on the screen that you want to press as soon as it shows up.  The prompt looks bad on its own, but worse is that because the camera is so close, they have to give you some sort of prompt for off-screen enemies and it's a tiny arrow that I don't think I've ever noticed fast enough.If they had gone the route of the old God Of War games where the camera would usually be back far enough to see the whole combat area, the issue over what you can see would be essentially eliminated.  (I'm also wondering if they couldn't have a distant camera and still have the interrupt button prompt because it would cover the entire enemy...may have backed themselves into a corner there.)The other part of this issue layer is small, but important, and that is weapon selection.  You select weapons with the D-pad, and since there are six that you can switch between, they put two weapons on the left/up/right parts of the D-pad (down is for items).  The problem arises in that they should have had it where one press gives you one of the weapons and two presses gives you the 2nd weapon.  Instead, it depends on what weapon you currently have!  For example, up on the D-pad represents the hammer or the whip.  If you currently have equipped the bow, then one press up gives you the hammer and two presses would give you the whip.  If you are already on the hammer though, one press gives you the whip, and two presses puts you back at the hammer!  You see the issue?  In the midst of combat, I should always be able to do the same button(s) for the same result.  It's an unnecessary complication for a game with combat that requires lots of quick actions.EXTRA NOTESBosses have great visual design and an epic feeling, but were not that difficult.  Note that the first boss, the big archer, is not indicative of what you will encounter later on.  There is much less chasing in all other boss fights.There is a layer of the combat where your companion has to create a particular color field (blue/red) to damage certain enemies.  It starts out feeling like a pain, but as you go through the game you will gain abilities that make using them easier.  You also learn to think of turning them on and off as parts of your combos rather than leaving them on long term, and eventually it's barely an issue.  I don't see it as a reason to not play the game.Another frustrating part early on is that you will feel like you are chasing enemies a lot.  This is another experience that will get better as you go.  Between the gap closer skill you can get for your first weapon, a ranged weapon, and a weapon skill that pulls you to an enemy, you eventually find that getting to enemies becomes less and less of an issue.This game is worth a buy at full price in my opinion, and don't let a few rough edges ruin the enjoyment you can have with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is the closest thing we're ever likely to get to a game adaptation of the Claymore manga, and this is absolutely a good thing. Soulstice delivers on the fantasy of playing a fantasy supersoldier struggling against the source of her own power to keep her sanity, while also managing to create an identity all of its own with a unique blend of influences and aesthetic flourishes. Camera work and grand vistas reminiscent of the original trilogy god of war games, baseline combat reminiscent of Devil May Cry and a visual aesthetic and setting tone comparable to Berserk, it's not wholly original, but still very fresh.It's not a perfect game. Some of the combat encounters are poorly balanced, certain environmental hazards get overused as combat elements and one or two boss fights have poorly communicated mechanics that led to frustrating ends. And the story, while competently put together and compellingly told, isn't going to set the world on fire. But what Soulstice does right more than compensates for its flaws in my opinion, and it gets things right where it counts. The combat is stylish and intuitive, synergising excellently with the narrative relationship the main characters have. Briar and Lute are as dependent on each other as people as they are mechanically, in a surprising and extremely impressive display of Ludonarrative Harmony, especially aided by the smooth and natural inclusion of Lute's mechanics. And the game's half-dozen true boss fights make great use of these mechanics, standing out as notes of powerful spectacle. A standout moment for me being using the phenomenally cool Berserk Mode mechanic to finish off a later boss, an experience I'm still coming down from the high of hours later.If you're into spectacle fighters, Soulstice is a comfortable recommend from me. Hurrah for the return of mid-range developers!
