_childDocuments_.review: After playing the game almost completely (just an assumption) and trying to enjoy the game itself,i cannot recommend the game.The graphics are nice and the overall style is well made.The combat system and combat action is pretty good too.I also like the whole setting, story and characters, which reminds me of Claimore, a little bit of Berserk and DMC.But here are the things that buggle my mind:1) Locked Camera (while out of combat)Im trying to be as objective as possible, so bear with me.Due to the fact, that the camera isn locked while fighting, it's clearly a pure design driven decision.This feature provides a very specific perspective and thus provides partially critical or at least additional informations for the player while walking through the game. If it would'nt be locked, players are likely to miss out loot or other (hidden) content.Using this feature to literally guiding the player through a linear designed game is not an argument and if it's an argument for the developers, it's a bad one.The problem with the locked camera always appears while trying to "explore" the game.Sometimes the biggest challenge in the game are not the fights, but trying to jump on a small levetating platform.What do i mean by that?It happens, that the camera is positioned in a way, that makes 3D-perception and thus depth-estimation very hard.This results in absolute frustation just to try to jump from platfrom to platfrom while beeing vesseled by a limited ressource that sometimes is required to been able to use the platforms as actual (physical) objects to jump on.2) CombatBeen punished for starting an attack but not paying attention to attacks of the enemies is understandable.Provide attack indicators on the enemy or the environment for unblockable, unparryable(?) or that cannot be countered are a huge help.The problem starts, when the player cannot do s**t to avoide dmg from those attacks at all, due to missing delays between indicating an attack and executing an attack.Due to this problem, is faced several messy fights that got very frustating because of their unpredictability and could only proceed in the game due to my own stubbornness and possibly lots of luck with positioning and enemy behaviour.3) Why i stopped playing (highly personal opinion)I hate time-gate events in games.I cannot express how much i hate them because they inevitably cause unnecessary pressure.But what i hate EVEN MORE is when im forced to play over 10mins of progress again if i fail such an event.Yes, I'm not a good player, yes this could all only a "me"-problem, but punishing a player to throw away progress of such a time span is just ridiciolous.And yes, a part of that is related to the first point.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, the game's greatest strength is that it tries to be its own unique experience while borrowing from the hack-n-slashes that it's inspired by, specifically Devil May Cry. Excellent combat, cool visuals and a solid soundtrack round out this mostly enjoyable game. However, poor PC performance, obtuse camera angles, a surprisingly limiting 'colour field' damage system and other moments of jank hurt this experience. It's a good first attempt at creating a game like this, and with some feedback and re-thinking, a sequel could be truly great. If you enjoy the 'character action game' hack-n-slashes (DMC, Bayonetta, Metal Gear Rising, or even Castlevania: Lords of Shadow), then give this a try.Pros+ Cool, gothic visual presentation that's both anime and Castlevania-inspired.+ Fun, pumping soundtrack that vibes well with the action.+ Satisfying combat when you get into it. Each weapon feels good to use.+ Smooth, cool character animations and special combat cutscenes.+ Interesting story with good voice acting, engaging presentation.+ Boss fights are cinematic and challenging, cleverly using all mechanics.+ Enjoyable exploration that's rewarding, whilst building atmosphere for the world.Cons- Game performance is inconsistent at best, and straight-up bad at times. Frame rate is hardly ever stable, even with strong graphics cards and systems.- The fixed camera during fights and camera angles as a whole are not well implemented.- Using completion time as a negative for score hurts the exploration that the game clearly wants you to do; to discover items and secret missions.- The colour field system is very limiting to the combat and hard to juggle when things get hectic. Would've been better as a status effect that you have to manage, rather than a limited range 'field' that you need to get enemies into.- In-game character dialogue becomes repetitive, and it either needs to be less frequent or have more lines recorded.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from the perspective of someone who is new to the hack 'n slash genre, Soulstice was a pleasant surprise. The combat features a variety of enemies and weapons (though there is a great deal of overlap in combo inputs for these weapons, if that matters to you) and enough different systems to manage (Entropy, Unity, counters) to keep it consistently fun and engaging, and it's all backed up by an energizing soundtrack.The game places a surprisingly heavy emphasis on its story and character development, aided by some great cinematics, as a pair of warrior sisters uncover a world-ending conspiracy in the sacred city of Ilden across 25 chapters. Fans of Claymore will be pleased to find that Soulstice proudly wears its source of inspiration on its sleeve, with numerous overt references and parallels to that marvelous manga/anime series. There are nods to other series like Berserk and Warhammer 40K as well.Unfortunately, the overall experience is dampened a bit by the platforming. I found that the combination of a fixed camera (which hindered depth perception) and tight timings on certain jumps made a few sequences frustrating. Thankfully, most of your time in the game is spent either in combat or simple exploration.On the whole, I really enjoyed Soulstice! I very much hope the dev team has plans for a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: it's about time someone wrote a review for this that isn't either a callously phrased "it wasn't for me" or a shallow comparison to other franchises. user reviews were a mistake and i resent gabe newell for making me read through the slop steam gremlins post constantly. anywayit is a side scrolling 3D hack n slash game. what we have before us is a product which does not stand out as fully unique, perfect, or revolutionary. what it does stand out as is adequately designed, moderately priced, and good looking. in the current era of game development and publishing i think people underestimate just how much these AA studios matter and benefit the medium. it is products like this that i never regret buying even if they don't end up having the staying power of the greatest hits of all time.if you enjoy this type of game and the aesthetic speaks to you, you probably wanna play this. that said let me get down and descriptive:you play as a sisterly bond that transcends life and death. you are a super soldier in the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up fantasy military. a nuclear bomb has detonated in fantasy new york and you're the response team. little did you know, exposure to this fantasy radiation makes you become a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up magical girl. also professor layton is there? i understand now why back covers of books are the way they are....the game consists of a pretty tight game flow: traverse the linear levels, gather two types of currency and secret collectibles, while fighting increasingly complex and chaotic battles, and watch some cutscenes in between. you only have one profile, so you can new game+ before finishing the game on a different difficulty.now the meat and potatoes. does it game? does it POP? eh....mostly. let's get the bad stuff out of the way first. camera angles many times. you will have to do tedious platformer puzzles over and over because the stylistic camera and stark contrast lighting will make your spatial awareness fail in the most "OUGH" inducing way. the combat itself is quite nice. you can easily intuit how things work, the control scheme is well thought out, and getting a good score after a chaotic and breakneck fight feels very satisfying, like you did genuinely earn that badge (though the scoring system is still a little inscrutable to me). if you love to REACT FAST and PRESS BUTTONS GOOD you'll have at least a passably good time. you will be pressing a Lot of buttons, fast. the bosses are all fairly unique and well designed fights. however thanks to the chaotic nature of regular encounters they tend to feel a bit types, but i digress. there is also another set of skills which i will get into less as it ties directly into the story. these magic skills work a lot more passively and actually add variation to the game. by making use of a points alignment system, which skills you pick in these categories will have aesthetic and gameplay effects which is pretty cool. some closing notes on other aspects of the game's quality: -graphical fidelity is nice, framerate is stable throughout (i will post my specs below the review). -the voice acting is stellar, if you can stop yourself from blaming the voice talent for some woefully generic lines with hollywood emotions (they're all lute lines. i'm sorry lute. you are the weenie, i still love you)-the art direction is nothing special but very enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - It's a good character action / spectacle fighter game. It's not without its flaws, but it's worth picking up on a sale.For fans of character action games, it's known that major releases are few and far between. Fortunately, Soulstice does a good job of reaching for some of the rather lofty heights of games like Devil May Cry, Ninja Gaiden, Bayonetta etc. The first and foremost important aspect of any of these games is combat, and they've done a rather good job at it for a first showing. There are 7 different weapons, each serving a different purpose and having their own strengths and weaknesses, both in literal "this does more / less damage to X enemy" and "slow + hard hitting vs fast + weak hits" ways. Swapping between them mid-combo is very simple and can lead to some pretty flashy moments. However, the weapons themselves aren't too terribly complex, and there are only a handful of moves for each (which may be a positive or negative depending on your preference). Being able to mix in counters while doing your moves is very satisfying, and makes it so you don't have to disrupt the flow of your attacks by mashing guard or dodge. Dodges in this game do have some generous i-frames, but use the Bayonetta system of "punishing recovery frames with 3 in a row" so you can't just spam it. The enemy variety is solid, and higher difficulties actually mix up the enemy placement rather than just making everything have more health + deal more damage, and I was pleased to see they avoided the pitfall of spongey enemies. They implemented a similar mechanic as the DmC reboot, with red and blue enemies requiring you to put up a red or blue "zone" buff respectively. It is fortunately significantly improved over the DmC implementation, and there are other aspects of that system worked in to the combat to make it more exciting as a resource management element. Even better, there's an option in the Accessibility setting to let the game handle that switching for you, if it's not a system you want to interact with. This isn't a perfect solution, and can get you in some trouble during platforming segments or general exploration, but the penalty for overuse of the buff is incredibly minor.Other Accessibility features include Auto Combat, and Auto Counter, both of which make this a very...well, accessible game if you're struggling. That, combined with 5 difficulty options, means there's a difficulty setting for just about any skill level of gamer. Lastly for the positives, the music is pretty good. It's not something I see myself listening to outside of the game or anything, but it serves its purpose well.As for negatives: there are a LOT of cutscenes. Not just in the story sense, but every time you use your "power up" form, and every time you use the "ultimate" out of it. You can disable the "hold to confirm" requirement, but if you do so, you have to hit two buttons every time you do either one of those things, which is frequent. Additionally, some levels have cutscenes that appear to be hiding loading screens, but do some in a little bit of a gratuitous manner (e.g. you may finish a fight, run a few steps, jump on a platform, then a cutscene plays of you jumping across some more platforms). The story is really nothing to write home about, it's full of lots of CHAOS and CORRUPTION and takes itself seriously. On top of all that, the voice acting ranges from decent to "embarassing for a Power Rangers villain" levels of bad. The main characters are what you're going to be hearing most of the time, and they're fine enough, but there are very few lines and it gets rather repetitive hearing the same ones over and over again. The last downside I have is that the first 1/2 of the game really drags on, and is full of sewer levels and overall just very "samey" environments.All negatives aside, I enjoyed the game. Personally, I don't see myself really revisiting it on the higher difficulties or going for any achievements, and most of the issues I have aren't something that can realistically be patched out. Overall, for a character action game there's a good foundation, and that's very commendable for this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's fine generally, it really is but there's some minor bad points that quickly add up for me;- The controls have questionable stuff, like having a hard lock-on like Souls or DMC but your launchers and your "Stinger" type attack being two buttons pressed together. That makes it impossible to comfortably remap the light attack, which traditionally is on the left face button, but is now on the top. Why? It makes no sense, especially when you get other skills which make you, get this, stretch from the left button to the right button to do an instant parry. It's not possible, who the ♥♥♥♥ designed these controls? Once you get to fighting it devolves further...- The combat's really annoying, the enemies don't take turns like they do even in DMC, they have very badly telegraphed attacks sometimes with vague animations or instant hitboxes that don't match them, especially the bosses. All this while you manage your barrier so you can get invisible/invincible enemies damaged. It gets really egregious when the game has a mechanic dependent on seeing the moves and the button prompt in time to hit it so you can avoid an attack. This all works out really great when put into practice in a crowded room where you can't see what's going on and you're fighting with no eyes which leads into...- The camera. The camera is the worst part. Even if those other systems worked perfectly the camera would ruin it all. It's vomit-inducing. It's actually atrocious and the fact that they pick the WORST possible angles to do the PS1/DMC/GoW/fixed cameras is crazy. It's the worst part of the game and it's ever-present. It affects the combat, it affects the movement, it affects finding bonuses/challenges/items. It's extremely janky in ways I can't word properly.Edit: Scratch that, I'm not gonna finish this and I would refund it if I could. The way the encounters and enemies are set up later down the line is just too annoying. It's hard to see what you're doing, who's attacking, what's blocking your path, and you take free hits only for the game to be extremely strict with its ranks which in turn means you can't upgrade your options, on top of all the other issues. The controls, the camera, the enemy animations, the placement of things, etc. This game is bad, plain and simple, and while a lot of it is the camera, that's not most of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I never do reviews on games, but this work of art really amazed me and had me hooked from start to finish.It has its flaws, like some of the voice acting could've been a bit better, but the overall experience, world building and story really hit home with me and is one of the best gaming experiences I've had in quite some time. Especially in the last 5+- hours in.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: A really surprising well polished game, with that name I was expecting a Souls Like, but learned quick that I was playing a Devil May Cry Like instead, to the point of having even the fixed camera angles.The game is really competent and has a really engaging moveset of weapons, the start is a bit too slow and has a lot of sewer levels that feel samey and clearly padding. Once you get inside the city the game starts getting a bit more varied in its levels, but the asset reuse permeates a bit too much some areas making some levels be a huge blur on your mind. Overall Incredibly fun game though. Clear inspirations from Claymore, Berserk and Devil May Cry 4. The early bosses are terrible, but the main cast is incredibly engaging to fight against, albeit with a couple tough fights that really tire you. If you're fresh out of DMC's to play, this game scratched that itch so well for me that I actually went and beat it in three sittings. This game is pretty hard and I can see people who enjoy cuhrayzee games really feeling satisfied with the level of mastery you can get to with this game.tl:drGun TonfasGutsShierkeBerserker Armor Devil TriggerSpirit Rave mashing with L2 R2Please support this game, the passion and love is clearly felt throughout the entire game. The story was pretty fun to play through and it reminded me a bit of Nier Replicant in tone. Specially Briar's demeanor through the whole thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this hidden gem, huge throwback to Devil May Cry 1 to 3. With the amazing story telling through the memory sections and the cinematic cutscenes, fluid combat, catchy soundtrack, the unbreakable bond the sisters have, and the detailed dark fantasy art direction. I highly recommend this game to everyone and hope that this game gets a sequel it deserves.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: Combat gives good variety between DMC5 combos and Flashy Bayonetta behavior during cutscenes. I also found this game to be a mix between OG God Of War games with different exploration fixed camera angels and a 3rd person Combat action camera like other action games such as DMC.I am still playing the story. So far really liking the banter of two sisters and other characters I've met in story. Atmosphere truly sells the world setting, and game looks good visually. I think performance wise also it is stable enough. As Others have pointed the camera angle maybe an issue for some, for me I got used to it with 90ish minutes of gameplay so not a big deal, still I'd like it to get fixed or have some future mods perhaps?Good game overall for an indie studio :)
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is a great game that clearly has a lot of love put into it, the game has its issues but for the people who give it a proper chance they will find a really interesting and well-thought-out character action game that manages to find its own identity rather than being the DMC and Bayonetta "clone" that people brushed it off as. It's one of the best character action games I've played in recent memory and I hope the team uses the incredibly solid foundation they have created to make more works of this quality.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: The game is incredibly fun and even in normal difficulty, I found it to be challenging. The cinematics are quite good, especially in the second part of the game. The auras system is refreshing and takes a bit of getting used to during combat. The story and the setting are quite good and they were what made me want to play the game until the end. The worst thing I found about this game was the camera, in the beginning, it made me a bit motion sick, I don't really know why, but after 1 or 2 hours, I got used to it.I find this game incredibly underrated and would recommend you getting it if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is a very good action game, what makes it stand out is, above all, its dynamic action, and the fight here is very spectacular. _childDocuments_.review: Had a fun time playing this eye candy -> Good story (had some claymore vibes, each character has their own reason for the way they act). -> Nice graphics (nothing to complain about here, just looks great).-> liked the soundtrack and the voice acting. -> Manageable battles and nice combo system with different weapons and useful companion. -> I really liked the design of the big baddies. -> BERSERK MODE !!!! ---> mediocre platforming sections (in my opinion - I never had problems with the fixed camera angle when exploring, but in a fight.... hmmm... at least you can use the freecam in the fights). ---> Dodging is a bit slow (3x dodging, gives some kind of time penalty, also the lock-on function is not very efficient. _childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: I was hyped for this since it was announced and it's pretty much just like I thought characters are a little flatter than much of what inspires the game but I love the world, from creative use of many dark fantasy tropes like Berserk to the store brand Gastu clones working for a shady organisation which is straight out of Claymore (that's how I'd describe the claymore too, not just the Ashen Knights)combat is pretty tight, with certain enemies requiring a different field from Lute, some people think it's annoying when wraiths (blue field) and possessed (red) are in the same fight but I just enjoy the challenge of switching targets. while Briar doesn't have a range of combos for each weapon like Dante from DMC does she has quite the range of weapons where the limited combos work uniquely for each weapon then there's the berserk mode. good lord the berserk mode. for one thing, it's actually a berserk mode wrenching control away from the player entirely with the only input being trying to make it stop as Briar screams death threats to a detergent or something and murders the rest of the game. the Donovan boss fight didn't stand a chance when I used itfrom the creative use of dark fantasy tropes to some older character action staples that can still age pretty well, Soulstice is  a great use of it's inspirations between death and transcendence a chimera chooses DEATH/10 would turn gameplay into a basic plea for reason again
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: This game gives a great mix of  things I love: Claymore, Berserk, and Devil May Cry. The story was much more interesting than I expected when first jumping into this game. While some aspects of the story may seem 'predictable' it still makes a good narrative to allow room for growth. If you get stuck on a fight I would suggest starting on a previous mission to get some practice with all of your weapons to see what works best on each mob.

_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: (TLDR at the bottom) With the combat and hidden objects ripped straight out of GOW, and the situational mode switching Ikaruga, Soulstice doesn't do much you haven't likely seen in other games. That along with the lackluster exploration and the late game performance issues, one might wonder why i put so much time into this game, and why i recommend it.Graphics: Beautiful particle effects. The levels are modeled well. Its perfectly serviceable and i have no complaints in that aspect.Audio: Pretty good. The music brings the epic score you would expect from such a game, I was never annoyed or muted the audio.  The Voice acting was solid but . . . . sometimes Briar says some things like an English person, and most things like an American. That was weird. It could just be me but it wasn't a huge deal. Also, one time the main duo commented way too much on the level where the building you are in is collapsing. Other than that, no complaints.Story: There are 2 sides to this one. On one hand, the world. The story is epic in scale, with dark powers derived from chaos, A religion that permeates the entire story. It was never able to grab me in the same way something like Final Fantasy X did with a similar vibe to how the evils of the world, affect the culture of it. Most of the characters who inhabit it are uninteresting, which is fine because most are enemies. However, as I faced down the final boss, I was wondering in the back in my mind "Ok but how does this accomplish our goal?". In essense, I was confused. But, there was one shining beacon for me in this story. The relationship between the core duo was fantastic! I have never in my life cried over a video game relationship like i have with these 2 characters and i have played HUNDREDS of games. I mean it. This relationship is probably the best aspect of the game and certainly what kept me going to complete the story to the end. Chef's kiss.Combat:Movement across the battlefield feels fluid and consistent. The enemy designs are all interesting and best dealt with in different ways. Some enemies must be dealt with in incompatible ways while on the field at the same time so you must focus on one before going to the other. There are ranks given out after every battle, with a reward based on the rank you get. This incentivizes strategy, switching between weapons for optimal effectiveness. Fights are fast paces and chaotic so even though you are kind of given a "Dodge, block, or cancel most things" button prompt, it doesn't feel too easy because you are focusing on so many things. To speak about the fields briefly because they are such a big part of the game, You can switch between red and blue throughout the game. Both are able to do different things with the environment and some enemies can only be damaged when their corresponding field is up. There is no beneficial effect of having a field up. Only a way to bypass an obstacle. You have a limited time you can keep a field up, which can be upgraded. This of course, furthers the amount of strategy required during fights. I like all of these things.Exploration:This is the worst part of the game unfortunately and it can't be skipped when replaying. This dread replaying levels to unlock more things. The level design looks cool from screenshots and trailers, however the game takes place over a relatively small physical space. You fight through 6 environments that repeat as the story demands. This means environments repeat. alot. The levels themselves are filled with spots where you think "maybe there is a secret over here?" only to be met with an invisible wall. You can go down that ally but not THAT ally. This means unless you use a walkthrough, you are going to be running into invisible walls like an idiot all the time looking for extra stuff. The levels also seem to repeat themselves alot. No joke, i was using a walkthough to find extra upgrades and i thought one part of the level was a completely different part because it looked so similar. You can really see the reused assets in this game. As a result, its VERY easy to get lost. Sometimes a fight will break out but i would say about 50% of this game is platforming, and using the right fields to unlock/reach the end. Lots of upgrade materials are to be found, but its still a slog.Control Complaints / Suggestions: The combos are dumb. On a controller, it wants you to use Y+A  to use 2 different combos across every weapon. You realize i need to use my pointer and middle finger or thumb, to crab claw my controller? During combat and trying to avoid ♥♥♥♥? Ya i never used that once. Y + Y (pause) Y + Y + Y for your biggest move for the majority of the game? I feel they shouldn't have bound the sword to ALWAYS be X and allowed switching it like the other weapons. This would allow more things to be done with that button. Also move item wheel to (hold) D-pad down to free up that button as well.TLDR: I have complicated feelings about Soulstice. It does so much right, However it also fumbles super hard on half of its gameplay for me. There is a way to make it work and i hope in Soulstice 2 (hopefully) we see alot of its shortcomings ironed out. I want to see this duo again. Its worth it for them alone for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game for free on Epic and beat it on the hardest initial difficulty. I straight up purchased it here on Steam because these devs deserve the support more than 99.9% of the other studios out there trying to push out 'AAA' titles that end up having sterilized games devoid of any 'soul' in terms of lore, story telling, or even quality gameplay.Fair warning, the camera angels are fixed in alot of places, and I am quite happy with that personally because it feels like a callback to older games such as Castlevania: Lords of Shadow or the Devil May Cry and God of War series pre-Viking era.In terms of storytelling the game is like a high quality anime through and through, my only regret here is that there is no Japanese voice over for the whole thing but the English VAs do an amazing job, better than most high budget dubs out there.In terms of gameplay this is a genuine love letter to all the old school hack n slash titles I mentioned above. Once the action starts it doesn't relent except to allow to explore and each encounter feels like a step up the ladder from the last until by the end you are feeling amazed at yourself for pulling off wild combo strings while avoiding an insane number of hits in the thick of chaotic combat.Anyway... the tl;dr of this rant is that the devs care for their game really shows in every possible way and I can only hope this series continues because it is a true joy to play and immerse in.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: Not a terrible game but it’s pretty basic in comparison to other games in the genre, you're better off playing Devil May Cry, or Bayonetta, or Metal Gear Rising, or the original God of War games, or Transformers Devastation, or any other highly regarded hack n slash that i forgot to mention.This game has got lots of weapons that you can switch between on the fly but all of them have pretty limited amount of attacks, every single once has a ground combo, an extended ground combo, a launcher, and an air knock down attack with the same inputs across all of them.The slowdown can also be a bit crazy as the game goes into slow motion whenever you do a stinger or end most extended ground combos. The worst problem of all I’d say is the different coloured enemies that you can only attack if you have a field activated which you can only have on for a limited time before it needs to cool down, there are upgrades to help prevent it from getting to the point of needing to cool down but it doesn’t fix the problem outright.The story isn't anything i could really get invested in either.Pretty disappointing because I really wanted to like this one especially considering how few and far between games in this genre are.(Funny enough for all the reviews complaining about the camera that's actually something i didn't have problems with, although the lock on system wasn't very good.)
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun spectacle fighter with fun weapons, an interesting open ended story and great visuals. There are two problems with the game. The first is that the static camera makes using keyboard and mouse for some of the platforming and combat a bit more difficult than they are with a controller or than they would be with a free camera. The second is that there aren't that many variations in attacks within a weapon but being able to switch between all seven weapons at once almost makes up for that. Still a great game, hoping for a sequel to see how the story continues!
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst Soulstice has it's flaws in places, it's still a must play for any character action game fan.Combat feels great and rewarding to master. Whilst there isn't much in the way of combos, your attacks still feel good to use with great animations/game feel, and you have a wide variety of weapons at your disposal which you can switch between on the fly. Which lends it's self well to the combat system, as battles tend to be more methodical, with different enemy types requiring different approaches and weapons being stronger/weaker against different enemies. However it certainly doesn't force you to use certain weapons against certain enemies. For example, the hammer weapon is weak against flying enemies, however I still find my self using it against them as it's upper cut will launch you into the air, and it's slam down attack will bring flying enemies down with you.As for it's flaws, the ones that stand out are the camera (it's always the camera) and the implementation of Lute's abilities. Lute is still handled well enough, but I feel like it could have been done better. The main issue is how her attack abilities are all automatic, which is never a good approach for these types of games. And that her defensive/control abilities are all reliant on her counters, and the type of counter will change depending on which enemy you are fighting, and what animation they are doing. So in the chaos of combat it isn't really possible to tell which counter she's going to use, so it becomes difficult to plan around it. I feel what would have worked better is if she didn't have any automatic attacks, and if her counter always had the same effect of just blocking an enemies attack, and maybe staggering them depending on the enemy, and if her crown control effects, such as freezing enemies, locking them in place, knocking them in the air .etc, were active abilities you could use.To just add a note about the camera. Whilst it isn't perfect and sometimes does impede the game. I personally really didn't find it to be as bad as many of the other reviews make it out to be. It certainly isn't a deal breaker.When it comes to the visuals, story and atmosphere in general, all of it is amazing. Whilst the game definitely wear's it's influences on it's sleeve, it still maintains it's own identity. It looks gorgeous with a great sense of style. The story is simple yet still intriguing, and the characters feel very well done, with amazing voice acting, particularly Lute's VA's performance is phenomenal, and conveys her character well. The only real flaws when it comes to the game's presentation are that some of the environments, particularly at the start are a bit samey, the OST whilst good, sometimes doesn't fit that well, and they didn't make Briar at least somewhat buff. Which like... come on, come on. She's swinging that gigantic sword around she should have more meat on her bones.Overall, despite it's short comings, I am greatly enjoying Soulstice, and will likely be playing again on higher difficulties and hunting for high trophy ranks.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: The cinematic trailer is misleading. This is a Devil-may-cry-like game and not a soul-like. It borrow's alot of aesthetic character visual design from the Claymore and Berserk Anime/manga series. I found the developer's take on visual to be very nice.  A good game, but I would wait for a sale if you wanted it. Combat is definitely a step down from devil may cry, but its better to rein in expectations as this is at best an AA game as price point suggests. Overall combat is enjoyable with relatively enough depth to it and a good enough assortment of weapons. Much like the the devil may cry games you'll find you might fight with the camera as the camera orientation is already pre determined by the areas/rooms you are traversing. It probably borrows a little too much in terms of puzzles and enemy design from the reboot DMC. Need red colour for red puzzles and blue colour for blue puzzles and the same can be said about enemy types. This colour with enemy types can get annoying to frustrating; it just isn't for everyone. There are 5 difficulties with the hardest difficulties only unlocking as you complete the game on the lower difficulties before it. The hard difficulty called knight is quite hard, so if you think you just want to enjoy the story then play difficulties 1 or 2. The story itself is a personal tale between two sisters and generally the game has a small cast of characters. Fairly interesting story, fully voiced in English and has nice story cutscenes and action traversal cutscenes. My general only gripe with the game is that its kinda short. Probably around 15-20 hours if you decided to play the normal difficulty instead of hard mode. The game ending sort of sets it up like there is suppose to be a sequel, but that'll vastly depend on this games sales figures.Overall performance is acceptable. 3440 x 1440 p with locked 60 fps with mix of ultra and high settings. I was able to also get anywhere from 90 to 120+ fps when adjusted to medium at same resolution. This is on an r7 3800x and rx 7900 xtx. My only problem with this game is that i experienced random crashing when sometimes in the between chapter menu screen; very bizarre as this happened about 3 times total before i finished the game. As overall i did not have instabilities when in the game itself. At MSRP at 45 CAD it is a bit steep for what it is in my opinion. Get it when on sale at least 35% off.

_childDocuments_.review: i really liked soulstice, enjoyed every chapter, although some encounters were caner inducingsoulstice has awesome combat and weapons, enemies are varied and require the whole arsenal to be killed, strong art direction, cool battle theme, and beautiful story this is as close as we can get to a claymore gamei hope we see at least another sequel
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: Combat was enjoyable (though some of the challenges were BS enough that I started skipping them). Progressing through the levels was generally fun, although a few times near the end the platforming got pretty frustrating. I would've preferred the game to be shorter, and less level traversal. The last act was actually really good at this, skipping that stuff and just having it be a fun gauntlet of combats.Story and characters were really well done, better than I expected coming into it. Some nice twists and turns, and I was always looking forward to learning the next tidbit. Character and monster design were fantastic, loved seeing all of them, especially some of the later bosses. World design was sort of samey, could've used more variety through the first half, although the last half got a bit better.Combat is, at its core, pretty simple, but the game kept adding new monsters, new weapons, new environmental hazards, and it clicked pretty well by the end. Monster design was good enough it was easy to tell at a glance, in the chaos of a fight, what enemies were what and who I wanted to target (although the actual targeting was sometimes frustratingly difficult). Still, once I get the hang of all the weapons, it really flowed well and everything felt impactful.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very good hack and slash. You have 7 weapons, one main sword and other 6 that are unlocked during story, each of them are effective with certain classes of enemy. There is a mechanic where you need to activate one of the two available fields to deal damage to an special class of enemy, which can be difficult to master at first, but it is worth learning (you can enable the auto field in the game play assist options if you have trouble with it). I like the parry system, where you press a button and your shade perform the parry, so that you does not need to interrupt your combo. When in combat, we can land charged attacks if we fill the "unity bar", which works like the style meter from devil may cry, that is achieved not getting hit and performing different combos.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: I got it in Humble Choice and was sceptical at first. The camera seemed to be annoying, holding down buttons instead of just pressing them once and pressing a button for each line of dialogue was a little irritating. However, after finishing the game and looking back I have to say it was a lot of fun. It's a hack and slash game and on (at least) normal difficulty, you can play it like that. Mash buttons and slaughter dozens of enemies in a spectacular manner ... and I kinda liked the story.The visuals are not breathtaking but servicable. The game ran perfectly fine even from an HDD. I've been playing with a controller so I cannot say how good it is with mouse and keyboard.I am not sure I would have bought it for the listed price though. I am probably not the ideal target audience. If you like spectacle fighters and are into replaying such a game for better chapter ratings, doing challenges and higher difficulties, maybe you should take a closer look.

_childDocuments_.review: Might finish it eventually but this camera is worst one I've ever encountered in newer games. It's so jarring, angles are bad and worst thing is instant cut to different angle.Combat camera is fine, it's not good but it's serviceable, but as soon as you finish combat it automatically changes to bad one and it's just not pleasant. For some reason it's very zoomed out, and it's easy to lose your character. There is no way to outline them or something.It's just wild because they have working regular camera for combat. Yes, old DMC games had fixed camera. That doesn't mean they had to actually take inspiration from it and somehow make it worse. _childDocuments_.review: Good so far.Gameplay-wise it's like old dmc, fixed camera angles and combo system with launcher etc. The combat system is a little simplistic, several weapons (I have 3 so far) but not many combos per weapons.It runs really great and it's looking quite good, but I'd like some diversity in the levels. _childDocuments_.review: Soulstice----------------------------------Soulstice feels like a blast from the past, with fast, action-packed combat just like the old God of War and Prince of Persia games. But don’t worry, it has some modern twists to keep things fresh.You control two sisters, Briar and Lute, who work together in fights. Briar does the heavy hitting, and Lute uses magic to protect and attack. It’s a fun combo, and switching between them keeps things exciting.The game’s world is dark and gritty, with clear inspiration from anime like Berserk and Claymore. The characters and monsters are big, creepy, and full of that edgy style.Combat is satisfying, with flashy combos and special moves. The boss battles? They’re epic, but don’t be surprised if you get smacked around a few times.Levels are a bit more straightforward, but there are puzzles to break up the action, and exploring for upgrades is rewarding.It’s not perfect—sometimes the camera makes it hard to see what’s happening—but overall, the gameplay is smooth and engaging.If you miss the old-school hack-and-slash games, Soulstice brings that vibe back with a cool new twist.Just be ready to button mash like your life depends on it!Enjoy !!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, loved the atmosphere. The Hack and Slash was great and the cut scenes before the chapters and at the end of the chapters were great. The cut scenes in between the boss battles were interesting too.i enjoyed each chapter as I progressed further. I noticed a lot of people complaining about the bad camera angles but in the end it didnt bother me except for one part early chapters where I kept falling through 3 floors because I couldnt see where to jump. _childDocuments_.review: A potentially great game with a myriad of glaring problems.I really want to love this game and I do think it is a good game, but I think there's just too many issues that make it hard to recommend. 1. It Looks Great. The game is gorgeous with great character, enemy and level designs. Some fantastic visuals and amazing looking moments, though the facial animations look a bit odd most of the time (hint: people's upper lips aren't supposed to move that much when talking), not a deal-breaker just a bit odd.2. The Story is Cool. Honestly the best bit of the game for me and sadly the only reason I kept playing it. I really enjoyed the story and although the voice acting wasn't the best at times, at least the main characters are good.3. The Combat is Half Baked. This is the big one and not what you want to hear from a character action/spectacle fighter type game. There's a good fundamental base that I think a sequel could build on and make some of the weapons feel a bit more fluid and punchier.  Sadly there's not a lot of depth to the combat, all the weapons only have 1 basic and 1 unlockable combo and they're all the same (XXXX or XX - pause - XXX) as well as at most 3 special moves (usually stinger and a launcher), DMC this is not but pretty good for a first game. I also think Lute, your Ghostly Sister, could be built on a lot more. She usually runs on auto pilot, tickling enemies for small amounts of damage but mostly exists to put up colour coordinated fields to let you damage colour coordinated enemies. Red for Red enemies, Blue for Blue enemies. It's not difficult to understand but when you have a dozen enemies on screen it can be a lot to keep track of and ultimately is a very dull mechanic, it could do with being more interactive, maybe instead of just a field that you have get near enemies, it could be a blast or attack that makes them vulnerable instead, would at least feel cooler. 4. The Enemies are Frustrating. Technically still under the combat umbrella but its a big problem. The game has pretty good pacing at the start, beginning with small enemies then drip feeding you bigger and more complex enemies so you don't get overwhelmed and the enemy variety is good. However I think the balance of the game goes out the window in the second half. A handful of enemies have attacks that are just too quick to dodge and can't be countered and it just throws too many enemies of different types and I find it hard to find openings to attack since tougher enemies can't be staggered until you do enough damage to them. Also mines are the worst, every combat that uses the Red mines is awful and unfun.All in all, I would love to see a sequel, I think they could easily fix all the problems and build on what makes the game great in much the same way Devil May Cry has over the years. Sadly I don't think the game has sold that well so I'm not sure we'll ever see one but I do think it is just a sequel away from being genuinely fantastic.Now for some very specific complaints:Weapons. Some are very hit and miss. Sword is good, no notes. Axe is good but very slow sometimes attacks don't link if you don't mash. Bow is awful, it just doesn't feel good, like shooting water and its use cases are few, make it punchier, make it pierce enemies, anything. Chain is cool for what its for, wide attacks on small enemies, though is could be bigger and faster to make it feel better for its intended purpose. Fist could feel Punchier (forgive the pun) but it's supposed to feel strong and kind of... doesn't. Never used the knives. But they did save the best weapon till last; Cannon Tonfas, amazing I want more.Camera Angles are pretty awkward and I often found myself missing jumps because depth perception was very difficult to parse.Berserk mode was an odd design choice. I get it in concept, "Losing Control", it makes sense. Doesn't mean not being able to control your character is fun.Dodging could be more fluid, I think it would benefit from shortening the window between attacks and dodging. I often found myself unable to dodge an attack because I was still stuck in an attack animation with no window to react.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: This used to be a positive review which I'll leave below, but I've done a total 180 on this game and now can comfortably describe it as bad and not worth your time. It's sad to say this.The focus of a character action game should be the combat. The fun is found in doing fun exciting combos against cool enemies in a nice environment. This game refuses to let you simply fight enemies. The game constantly puts up barriers between what should be the foundation of the gameplay. There's always some dumb hoop for you to jump through. You have 2 "evocation fields" you can turn on. It puts a bubble around you and whether you have red or blue bubble up, it allows you to hit red or blue enemies inside the bubble. Red or blue enemies can't be hurt otherwise (outside of very specific circumstances). But having an evocation field active raises a "Entropy" meter and when the meter is filled completely it lowers your score, lowers your special meters and *turns off the bubble for a few seconds*. This meter also fills up when you Counter, Deflect, Slow down, or otherwise interrupt an enemy, meaning you are *constantly* toggling this dumb bubble off and on just to hit an enemy.Further to this, they also put environmental hazards in which react to what field you have up. There are mines that activate if you have a red bubble up too long (so you have to toggle even more) and there are blue mines which only don't explode if you have the blue field up or destroy them (they respawn). So you're forever either herding enemies away from these things or turning on bubble, hitting an enemy two times, turning it off, waiting a second, turning it back on etc etc.It's like the devs are afraid of simply letting you PLAY THE GAME (as evidenced by them removing the demo!). I just want to do cool combos and hit guys with my sword. I don't want to be flipping the triggers constantly just to interact with them.Further issues; there are only two combos with each weapon I've seen so far and they are the same combo. XXXX and XX(pause)XXX. Boring. They make a number of unique weapons and essentially make them feel identical outside of speed. Even the bow is basically just the whip which is basically just the sword because the bow can't hurt coloured enemies outside of the bubble, so you have to get close anyway!Some enemies also have completely unblockable attacks, they're annoying but they are technically telegraphed. Unblockables are indicated by about 1 second of yellow/black flame around an enemy, so you have time to evade. In theory this is fine, but when the terrible, terrible camera and lock-on system get involved you'll be lucky if you can ever see that one's been telegraphed. Getting hit by an unblockable attack that you couldn't see is annoying.There are special challenge rooms like in DMC4 where you get rewarded for winning in a specific way, e.g. kill everything in under a time limit, or survive X seconds. The majority of these are totally fine and normal, but some of them you will fail through no error of your own. Your companion, Lute, fires ranged attacks at enemies completely of her own volition, unprompted by you. When you have to kill only certain enemies first, or only kill enemies in a certain place and your ally forces you to fail a challenge because they randomly kill them, it's f*cking annoying.The absolute core of this game is good, but for a reason I will never understand, the devs buried it in utterly awful gimmicks. I hate that I don't like this game.Original review below.Red flags: when the game became available the devs delisted the demo. After day one they also seem to have increased the price. Make of this information what you will. It's okay. Feels like an early breed character action game (think more Devil May Cry 1 than Devil May Cry 5). The combat is fun and stages have a grading system like Bayonetta. I don't truly understand how the combat grading system works, you seem to get points based on things like hitting an enemy in the back instead of doing multiple varied combos, some fights I seem stuck at 5x multiplier and I can't for the life of me figure out why it won't go higher, but I likely haven't read enough on it I guess.Platforming is clunky like dmc 1,camera is absolutely atrocious. Unforgiveable. Voice acting is unusual. Game is perfectly playable and overall I'm enjoying it.

_childDocuments_.review: Badazz. You like the original God of War? Boom! Here ya go! Graphics are very clean! No stutters / frame drops. Runs very smooth. Interesting characters too. Played 90 minutes and I am happy to find out more. IssuesI had to force the game to accept 4k by using NVIDIA Control Panel. IrritationI cannot figure out how to turn off subtitles. Two hour refund is more then enough time to figure it out. Do not sleep on this one (Please read below for updates). UpdateThe camera can be a b****...  Another Update!I am now late in the game with still some to do (making this list as I go). One thing that has me dumb founded is the parry system. The main parry option is Lute. Briar (MC) younger sister (blue ghost). Issue I am having, there is either certain attacks or she just randomly just doesn't help. So the devs were nice enough to allow parry on a weapon. But so far, it really is just ONE weapon. Sadly, for me, it is the worst weapon at that (Gauntlets). One of, if not the, slowest weapon. I rarely use it if at all because of the hammer. Really though, my issue comes with giving it parry. The sword is the only consistent weapon. You cannot remove it as an option. It is always sword plus one. Whats driving me mad is the sword gets by far the least amount of upgrades then any other weapon. All that said, my question is why on earth did the devs not have the sword parry? You could look at it like a trade off, not a lot of combos, but you can parry. Heck in some of the cinematic you literally watch Briar use her sword and block... So I just sit there, wondering why I cannot do that. I doubt this will be adjusted, but if you're a parry feign as myself, I would personally give up on this idea. Dodging is your main source as Briar.. However, this is limited to, two side steps and one roll. The roll locks you into place for about two seconds Point is, there really isn't an option that feels satisfying. Dodging is very limited, forcing you to get cozy with those gauntlets, all the while Lute just doesn't seem to care at times. Be nice to have an option that assists by keeping the combat going. Help keep the fight running smooth. To top it off, there is no attack cancel. So once you start a combo, its going to finish. Until an enemy has had enough of you and hits you. Ruining the entire combo and your Unity. To summarize my point, when it comes to your defenses, this game is sorely lacking. You may think it wants you to be aggressive. Which I do not mind, but that cannot be the case. I'll explain more down below in another point. Swapping weapons. Using a controller the left, up and right directions of the Dpad is a weapon slot. Each slot gets two weapons. I noticed if you swap to the second weapon for that direction, then swap away and come back, it doesn't save. So you always have to press twice to get the second option. It would be nice if the last option used was saved. In a hack and slash, every second counts towards the combo. The Dpad being on the left side, it is on the side of your movement. Swapping weapons means you're not moving. Unless you reach over with your right thumb, but then you're not swinging your equipped weapon (face buttons). Too cumbersome in my opinion to not have it save. Later game enemies get BEEFY! Taking a load of hits (granted I am playing on the hardest difficulty offered for the first play through, which I do NOT recommend). I hate to say it, but there not all that fun. In fact, most really ruin the flow of combat. It's like the game is trying to turn into a SoulsBourne without that high of damage output from the enemies, extremely limited dodging from you and a fixed camera. So Devs, please, either unlock the camera, unlock the dodging, parrying, or tone them down a bit. Altogether and it can almost get you to punt your controller... I haven't! And won't! But I have thought about it. No lying on this review no sir.I've also got to admit. I wasn't against the color coded enemies / fighting at first, but I have since changed my mind. This mechanic requires you to use Lute and put either a red, or blue aura around Briar to be able to attack and kill the red / blue enemies. In my opinion, this is used FAR too often. I would easily say 90% of fights require this. I mean, I get it Devs, it uses Lute. But she already is our parry / block system. This WILL annoy you. Why? You ask.. Well, for example. There are red and blue mines in this game. They work opposite of each other. Blue mines require you to use the blue aura and it stops the mine from going off and damaging you. However, the red mine goes off if you use the red aura around it. Now take a red enemy and place them on a blue mine... This ladies and gents is what I like to call, "f***ed". No matter what, you WILL take damage if you attack. Even after the mines go off, they come back. So no, you cannot cheat. Keep in mind, if you're not attacking, you loose Unity (your special). If you are hit by anything, you once again, loose Unity. This sucks. Period. (Aggressive Fighting)Poor, poor Lute. Look, I like the sisters. I like their coming of age, under dog story. But man, I cannot lie. If I rated the sisters now, before beating the game, I can already EASILY say Lute is by far the weak link. She holds Briar back too much. Lute can get exhausted while fighting. She can be forcefully taken by the game to go rest if used excessively. She does warn before this happens, but I promise you now, there is so much going on, you will not hear her at times. Loosing her at the worst moments. When gone, there is NO way for you to hurt red or blue enemies. Granted she is gone only for 6/8 seconds, but still! That is a long time in a HACK N SLASH! You cannot hack, NOR slash. You are truly stuck if there is not a neutral enemy in the arena with you. Most the time, there isn't in the mid to late game. So you're stuck running around till she comes back. All the while you're loosing, say it with me..... Unity (I know you nailed it you Chad you). I hope they fix this because it can be mind numbing. Heck I too have to go rest after some of these fights dealing with Lute. All this does is stop you from being aggressive when you need it most. Tracking! One of the parries Lute uses is her freeze ability. Does just as it sounds. Before an enemy unleashes their attack, Lute can freeze them in place. Nice. Then comes the time you're one on one with an enemy, so there isn't much else to look at but them. You parry/freeze them and discover YET ANOTHER design flaw. When an enemy unfreezes they, no joke, snap back to you finishing the move they started. Meaning, you freeze them, go to flank from behind to keep that combo going, they unfreeze, instant 180 attack. And I DO mean "instant". The attack is now coming at you even faster because it is already half way complete. This game is blowing my mind on so many bad levels. Why is this a thing? If I could parry (with the sword) or attack cancel, I still wouldn't like it in a HnS game because of how hectic it can get, but okay. You gave us the tools, I just have to use them. This means when you freeze, you are allowed another 1/2 hits then the only option is RUNNING. Because a hit IS coming. Ruining, once again, that combo meter. This, in my opinion, has to be patched out. And finally, another MAJOR issue. If you do pull off combos and fill up the Unity meter (FINALLY!), you will unlock special attacks called Synergy. Each weapon has one. Once achieved, the game will focus in on Briar as she pulls off the move. Cool as hell cinematic and I love doing it! However, there is one huge flaw. Enemies do not freeze in place. As the game takes control away from you and Briar attacks, the enemies are free to move as they see fit. This INCLUDES the enemy you're attacking. They just WALK OFF during the move every time. Meaning some of the move, does zero damage. FINAL in comments.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game on hard difficulty, experienced the full story up to the post credit scenes and with all that said, I do recommend this game. Its not without its flaws, some of which are very annoying, but if you're a fan of stylish action and anime inspired designs, you're in for a good ride with this one.STORYThis game with its story, character designs, world and even gameplay takes heavy inspiration from Japanese games and anime. With regards to the story, if you're a fan of works like Berserk, Claymore and dare I even say, The Witcher, I think you're gonna like this. Its not the most complex plot in the world, but its enjoyable enough to keep you hooked from start to finish. The ending was really good and they caught me off guard with one of the big reveals too. I think its fair to say they were on the right track with this fantasy world they created here. The world building was pretty good too and I liked the little touched like characters wishing each other well in the name of the three heroes of their land. Unfortunately though, I feel the pacing is way off and especially at the middle part of the game, I feel it drags on for too long. Yes, I did dive into this game on Hard difficulty right off the bat and that would result in a longer time to complete the story, but I still think they could have trimmed the game down from 25 chapters to maybe 20. 26 hrs felt like way too long for this story for me.GAMEPLAYCombat is fast, flashy and Briar, your main character, moves with a lot of finesse. There are a lot of weapons to unlock and the animations for all of them are stunning! There are also a crap-ton of powers and skills to unlock. I sometimes wished there was a more extensive combo list like in DMC, but it was still really impressive the many things they were able to add in this aspect.Unfortunately, there are some issues with gameplay. First, forget about all the dope looking monsters in the game (I would get to that in a bit), the camera is your number one enemy. Many times, it messes up your flow by getting hooked on walls and honestly, I didn't find the enemy lock that much useful, especially in situations where you get overrun with enemies (And trust me, you would). Also, there were quite a lot of instances where I got attacked from behind and it just left me like, "How the hell was I supposed to see that???"Enemies here aren't playing around though and they will hand you your butt especially on tougher difficulties. There is the option to counter here, which i love, but sometimes it doesn't appear and the enemies just hit you anyways. The platforming is fine at best because not only are your controls stiff mid-air, but in some scenarios, the game doesn't make it easy to jump from one block to another in a 3-D space because it's hard for you to tell what position you're at relative to the platforms (or absence of one) beneath you.The upgrade tree is good, but kinda expensive though. You can reset your choices to try different builds, so that's good.But with all that said, there is still a lot of fun to be had here with many challenges, move sets, weapons, enemy types and upgrades you can add to your style of play. AESTHETICSThis game is beautifullllllllll! It's sont fully lip synced and some facial espressions can look a little off, but this is a AA game so I'm not really bothered. Actually I'm hella impressed cuz DAMN, they really got the art style down. All the characters look very well modelled, the environments are very detailed and my, my, the music is a dreaaaaaaaaam! I'm so in love with the music here that I wish it could easily be found to stream. It is available to purchase here and I do recommend it, but I just wish it was a bit more accessible. Still, it's way too dope and you'll love it if you're a good fan of electronic music.I still can't wrap my head around how beautiful all the character models in this game are, especially the enemies. They are just so intricately designed and are nothing but the product of pure talent.Unfortunately though, the environments, while very detailed do very little to distinguish themselves. Don't get me wrong, you CAN tell when you're in a different location, but only if you focus. There isn't really a change in colour the palette until the end and for a very long time, you'd be stuck with nothing but dark grey brick walls and maybe some ice.Nonetheless, this game looks and sounds beautifullllll! I think this is where they really hit the mark!PERFORMANCEIt was okay for me. I played it on medium to high-ish settings on my 3050 laptop at a near constantly locked 1080p 30 fps. I could very much push it to 60 fps, but you don't really need that for this game, so I saved my SCREAMING laptop some stress. Overall, it was alright. Not the most optimized, but good for me. Your mileage may vary depending on your setup. I only have a 1080p 75Hz monitor, so almost anything works and looks fine for me with my setup.OVERALL SCORE - 7/10I really do recommend this game and although it's not perfect (Far from it actually), I still think it's very much worth your time at a good price. I had very few rage moments with this on HARD MODE and that's a lot coming from a guy who can easily get enraged at video games. I got this game as part of a Fanatical bundle and think you'd be happy if you get it at a good price. THANKS FOR READING THIS VERY LONG REVIEW AND I WISH YOU ALL THE VERY BEST! HAVE A WONDERFUL DAY!!!

When it does require you to utilize other abilities, it can tend to make some combat encounters into a bit of a chaotic mess.- The missions, while certainly fun to play through, feel much longer then they need to be, often continuing on even after I reach points that seem like good stopping points.These don't make the game unplayable by any means, it's still a decent time, but I still feel as though these aspects could've been refined a bit more.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the name and the obvious Berserk reference, this is not a Souls-like. Instead take your mind back to the classic hack-and-slash games of older generations such as the original God of war and Dante's Inferno and you're on the right track. With the DMC/Bayonetta style scoring system and the game's mechanics of using fields of effect to attack possessed or wraith enemies, you must use everything in your arsenal to beat the hordes coming at you. With a massive arsenal of weapons and supported by your spirit sister, you fight through a city on the brink of destruction, facing corrupted humans, wraiths and possessed, while you lose your own humanity the more you fight.  Level up your weapons, unlock new moves and build your spirit's abilities as you see fit with collected resources as you face greater foes, harder challenges and solve more complex puzzles. This is a game with a brilliant blend of fast-paced anime style action, a dark/grim, end of the world setting  and the conflicting duality of morals between the two sisters, generates a great foundation for the story. Granted, the voice actors in parts are a bit cheesy and the story is a bit basic, but the lore is rich and the efforts of the devs shine through the fog of its draw backs. The fixed camera when traversing through this world is obscuring at times, but it is necessary for the cinematography the devs have intended. The graphics are great and a real step in the right direction for high-res skins with the cell-shaded foundation for character models. Awesome level design and the fixed camera helps to guide you through the destruction of the landscape, yet the invisible walls can pull you out of the world from time to time. The views at times are breathtaking and the ever-escalating challenge of the enemies will have you on the edge of your seat and hyped up to go back into the fight if you fail.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much cool stuff in it, there are multiple accessibility toggles such as color blindness mode, font size change, and other features that give off a good first impression. The move-list is basic and easy to perform thanks to the addition of visual cues and controller rumble that facilitates the learning curve for moves that have a “pause/hold”  (e.g. X,X,(hold), X,X,X ). And it is a good thing that the inputs are easy since main characters will have up to 7 weapons by the climax of the game, making it comfortable to return after a long break and refamiliarize w/ the gameplay. But by far, MY FAVORITE thing in this game is their implementation of a Devil-Trigger Mechanic called “Rapture Mode”, where you have to raise your stack up hit counts and raise what is essentially your Style Meter to unlock the prompt to do the equivalent of Bayonetta 2’s Umbran Climax. Before the release of this game(and after playing the demo), I was hoping to encounter great boss fights, and y’know what?!  it definitely delivered a lot of spectacular bosses. It’s cool that the devs draw inspiration from Berserk, Claymore, DMC, Bayonetta,  and Astral Chain, unfortunately, they also carried some of the flaws from all of those titles(along w/ flaws of their own). Such as fighting red and blue enemies in ‘DmC Devil May Cry’, teleporting enemies that breaks the rhythm and combo, and just like how this game has the best DT mechanic, it also has another DT mechanic that I’m not a fan of, called “Berserk Mode”, where the characters automatically attacks the foes in an invincible state and all the player do is align the left-stick with the direction of the prompt and mash a QTE. Although this is a personal thing, I dislike that I can’t deselect items in my D-Pad and get my score docked due to accidentally using a healing(or any other) item, especially when I’m playing a Character Action Game.Other than that, I only have mixed feelings about some other aspects, the most divisive point being the fixed camera, though I’m fine w/ it since it is used to direct the player to their next objective along with making the shots look cinematic, but it is a problem for platforming sections. Also, when you enter a fight the camera is free, there was only 1 fight that was fixed camera and it was fine. Most of the issue w/ the camera is the same problem as other action games where they make you fight in tight spaces, and you have to put in the effort to avoid getting cornered by your foes. Controller remapping is cool but not ideal due to certain inputs requiring you to press 2 buttons at the same time, and therefore you need to get used to something approaching the default controller scheme.In short, I love this game, despite moments that frustrated me, it is one of the biggest surprises of this year for me. AND I WANT A SEQUEL REAL BAD.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the Boomer Shooter of character action games.There's a lot to find charming here, but most of it will likely come off as clunky or aggravating, especially if you aren't coming to it with a predisposition for PS3-era action games. You've got a "main attack" that feels mostly like a combo filler, a "secondary attack" that mixes things up, and a dedicated Counter button where your ghost sister will block or debuff enemies when counter QTEs appear. The main gimmick here that might make or break things for you is using your ghost sister to deploy red or blue fields in order to interact with environmental objects and attack specific enemies. So the idea is for you to be wading into it mashing out combos and dodging attacks while also playing the support role for yourself.  You're being pushed to articulate the bond between the two sisters yourself through combat asking you to master maneuvering these two characters as one. It won't be for everyone, but there's something neat there.My only real gripes are that changing the controller layout doesn't seem to apply until you back out to the main menu, and the environments so far can be pretty bland and repetitive.Oh, also there are plenty of barrels and crates to break for shinies.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, game's kinda fun. Not very far into it right now, but combat feels challenging enough to feel mostly satisfactory. Exploration is a neat feature, bit of trial and error, another decently challenging aspect that I find myself somewhat interested in. Really pretty backgrounds; I love the vibe, how it feels like a healthy combination between Dark Souls and Final Fantasy.But this game is so pointlessly complicated and nuanced.Camera angles are wonky as hell. Not a fan of the constantly changing angles when running around the environment. Makes it complicated to look for the environmental challenges and hidden treasures/pathways.The incorporation of the fields is clunky and anti-climactic. Cool for exploring the semi-open world, boring while in combat. Functions like a resource bar while in combat, but you get the ability to extend its duration while in-combat almost right away with the first tier of talent points, so it removes almost all active tracking of the mechanic.Not being able to buy talents when you accrue the currency for them is kinda pointless. Can only purchase talents while in a shop or between chapters. To be fair, though, there are a few checkpoints scattered throughout the chapters, but I find it to be an obnoxious form of pacing the game's talent tree functionality. What are the developers intending with this feature? Why disallow talent point accumulation without the checkpoints?Lock-on functionality is bizarre. It's incentivized to focus a single enemy because you can only see their health bar when you have them locked on, but it creates the worst in-combat camera angles. The game is very high mobility, so there's a lot of running around/aerial combat/etc, which blows for the camera if you're trying to fight locked on. You're forced to turn off the lock-on feature and then reposition yourself in the arena, but once you do that, good luck finding the target you were focusing before.I'm finding the challenges to be the most infuriating process in the game so far. Researching answers online will only give you paper knowledge; executing them in-game is either impossible or the dumbest ♥♥♥♥ ever, which detracts from the game's combat system. For example: The perfect counter challenge. It was somehow impossible to complete even with high reaction timing, so the way I managed to overcome it was clear out all other enemies until there was only one, and then stand completely still and mashing the F key until it almost broke in order to obtain my "perfect counters". For a game that has extremely high mobility, what's the point of mandating a "perfect counter" system if the only way to accomplish it is by standing stationary?Having similar issues with the synergy attacks challenge. The combo is supposed to be [left click + left click + pause + left click x4] when the icon in the upper right hand corner "merges." It's a resource bar that's not tracked in the game whatsoever. I've only ever accomplished a synergy attack coincidentally, never intentionally.Maybe it'll get better with future talent tiers being unlocked as the story progresses. Maybe. If it does, I'll change the review. But so far, this game has potential, but isn't impressive mechanically.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated Review - 12/10/2023:This game popped up in my mind multiple times throughout the year since I did want to know how the story played out. So I buckled up and pushed through the garbage encounters to thankfully not see as many terrible ones past Chapter 17. Did end up finishing the game and liking how ridiculously messed up the characters became as you got closer to the truth of what happened. Delightfully twisted insanity going on here. If they do manage to get the green light to do a sequel, I may play it and pray they do away with the messy red/blue swapping battles since it does get really tedious having to do that on the fly so much. The main combat itself is good, just need to tweak or remove the extra baggage that was holding it back.Previous Review:Plays like old school Devil May Cry, without the heavy emphasis on humor, which is honestly a good thing. The story takes itself seriously and only has the occasional quip here and there that I welcome since I feel Devil May Cry leans way too far into the comedy that it can be cringe at times, even if it is fun to watch.After progressing further into the game, I have encountered some truly frustrating enemy variants and combat scenarios. The most frustrating enemies are the ones that play keep away with for the entirety of the battle, making the battles take longer than they need to. There are also large enemy types that produce multiple enemies when defeated and if you fail to kill ALL the enemies they spawn, the larger enemy will revive itself, drastically inflating the battle length to a frustrating degree. Does not help that the enemies that are spawned have the same color as the environment, bright blue, making them really hard to find on the field, which is wasting your time in such a terrible way that are you likely going to get at least 2 enemy revives before you can finish the fight.Then there is the annoyingly stupid traps that get involved in the battles, forcing you to switching from Blue to Red fields every couple seconds to prevent the traps from exploding in your face while fighting enemies that can only be hurt by a specific colored field that so happen to trigger the traps on the field since they have the same color, or different color, depending on the trap in place. These type of combat scenarios are downright nasty and stupid.I cannot in good faith recommend this game anymore after seeing how immensely frustrating the game gets the further you progress into it. it started off good and balanced with some nice enemy types, but the game just got worse and worse over time, making things way too frustrating to even be considered fun anymore. The constant issue of being unable to see an enemy attack coming while there are multitude of other things happening around you just becomes to ridiculous.

_childDocuments_.review: You know how Frodo's journey in Lord of the Rings took a year or something? Soulstice's approach would be to show you all of it... This game has no editing. The game proved me wrong on two fronts:1. While I was starting the game I thought to myself why don't more spectacle fighters come up. It sure feels like a winning formula: DMC, Bayonneta, Metal Gear Rising, the old God of Wars and even Darksiders all received at least positive critical reception. Would be hard to mess this up. Soulstice messed it up. It's not a disaster, it just feel so poorly thought out. 2. After the opening chapters of the game I though this took heavy inspiration by Ninja Theory's DmC. After a couple of more chapters I realized this is what a game that would've inspired DmC would've looke like. It's unbelievable that a game 10 years newer would be so much worse.The main problems of the game are that it lacks spectacle and colors, environment diversity, the story is poorly told and the dialogue is most of the time pointless and the game is faaar toooo loooong. These problems would not be so apparent if the game wouldn't drag itself out and show some restraint. The combat is functional and wouldn't be terrible, but the enemies you fight have no discernible identity.
