_childDocuments_.review: I’m not sure why, but it feels like this game has received very little attention (which is unfair because it’s really good). I would compare the gameplay to Nier Automata, if you took away the drone/shooting mechanics. It has that single player 2-in-1 vibe from Nier also (or like GOW/A Plague Tale/TLOU) since you mostly play as Briar but Lute is partially controllable, too. The structure of the game is similar to Bayonetta, where you get a rating for each battle that you complete. I wouldn’t compare the two much beyond that though, since this is more hack and slash and less beat ‘em up, and all my opponents so far are roughly the same size as Briar (player character). No fights with screen-filling monsters. The story is somewhat interesting, but not amazing (at least so far, for me). The world is intriguing, as I’m learning about the lore. It kind of seems like it’s set in medieval times or maybe beyond that…like the dark ages, but in a world with magic and demons and whatnot. So far, I’m enjoying this game and hope it gains more popularity. I’ve been playing it on Steam Deck, initially I was struggling to get the game to hold 30-40fps, but after the last update, it’s virtually locked to 60 with everything set to low, except AA and textures set to high, @720p with FSR on balanced. Very impressed with the performance now.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it. It's a mix of Bayonetta/DMC/Darksiders. But it's not perfect and does have some jank and other things that hold back the game from being good to great. +Good story. +Voice acting and writing.+Cool weapons, combat and skills.+Weird, creepy atmosphere.+Difficulty settings.+Qol toggles. +Beautiful environments. +Linear.  -The game starts out pretty rough- no skills, weapons, etc. and the extra weapons don't come soon enough.-Camera angles and/or zoom during non combat can make it difficult to figure out where to walk or jump next. Some extra lighting to show where to go would be wonderful, or even gps waypoints in game would be nice too. -Unlike Bayonetta which had some varied levels to break up the action, in this game there's a couple running segments (which would be great if your character would autorun), but the worst ones are Lute missions where you just slowly float around following the arrow and listen to more story beats. -Story does get a bit long in the tooth in the last few chapters. Hopefully the devs haven't finished work in this game yet. It would be great to see more camera improvements and other refinements to the layout of skill tree, etc to tighten things up a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: I need Briar to step on meOkay, now for my actual review:Soulstice is going for a LOT clearly. The amount of ambition and content on display is nothing to scoff at. It's a double A game that would have fit in perfectly well coming in around the PS2/PS3 era, and it does that surprisingly well. If you like Devil May Cry and want more content like that, this is an easy purchase in my opinion. It's not without issue, but it's fun enough, and has enough going for it that's unique and is really doing it's own thing quite well. The negatives:-The voice acting is inconsistent. It's hard to fault the devs, since of course, they are based in Italy, but Briar in particular is particularly inconsistent during 'struggling' scenes or ones where she needs a broader vocal range. It's not bad, but it's clear the direction for the english actors isn't the best. Lute though honestly kinda killed it.-The camera is pretty inconsistent. During fights, especially when they let you free cam, it's quite difficult to see anything. I think the cameras during exploration were used to surprisingly good effect though.-Kind of a slow start, this isn't too big of an issue, but it took about as long as my playtime is to start getting fights that had any sort of challenge to them. It's not an inherent issue, just something worth mentioning.-Targeting can be inconsistent, and the lag after a triple dodge is NEEDLESSLY punishing. Especially when you can use the rollstab infinitely and go an absurd distance. Positives:-Character designs, I **LOVE** women with big swords. I need Briar to beat me up-I actually think the story is somewhat compelling. Normally stories like these don't really do anything for me, but I found myself at least mildly interested, genuinely that's a feat to behold for my ADD brain. -The combat feels pretty good, I tend to strongly dislike games that have a 'grading system' after you finish combat, and I wish I could just turn that off, but it's not too intrusive, as little as it seems to actually fit with the world. Something more melancholic would've fit the game better, but it feels like the combat designer and story designer were very much two different people. Maybe it's to show Briar is a creature of combat? Idk, but it feels kind of ill fitted either way.-The sister mechanic is very neat. It seems genius both as a feat of character design AND gameplay where she protects you mid-combo etc. Very cool, used well, and I think the ghost/color matching enemies are foreshadowed well and allowed you to practice that mechanic in a safe environment first. Kudos.I think the game is good, and deserves more praise. It's not perfect, but if you go in with the notion "This is like a PS3 era action game, jank and all!" You'll probably have quite a bit of fun. Anyway, the devs are lucky I'm not giving this a negative review, because they didn't mail me a Briar figurine yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed ReviewPros:🎵 Music: The music in this game is the unsung hero, weaving a spell that enchants and captivates. It's a saving grace in an otherwise tumultuous journey.🎬 Cinematic Bliss: I can't help but applaud the high-quality cutscenes that unfolded like a movie. Each frame was a visual feast, showcasing the artistry that went into their creation.Cons:👾 Sturdy as Fort Knox: My excitement turned to frustration as I faced enemies with health points that seemed insurmountable. The relentless onslaught of spawned adversaries turned battles into a chaotic frenzy, with no joy. Honestly, way too many on the most narrow spots.⚔️ Combat: The combat system, my oh my! It's like trying to dance in quicksand. Mistakes are brutally punished, and the limited combo options per weapon make achieving any form of fluidity an uphill struggle.🗣️ Dialogue: The narrative fell flat with poorly written dialogues that left me yearning for depth and connection. It's disheartening when a game fails to draw you into its story.🌐 World: Exploring the game world felt like navigating a maze with no surprises. The lack of camera control added insult to injury, restricting my view and engagement with what should have been a vibrant environment.🦄 Enemies: Where's the variety in enemies? Facing the same foes repeatedly became monotonous, robbing the game of the excitement that diverse adversaries bring.In the end, my journey through this game has been a mix of awe and frustration. The captivating music and stunning cutscenes couldn't quite salvage the overall experience marred by clunky combat, uninspiring dialogues, and a world that felt more like a narrow corridor than an expansive realm. It's a tale of unmet expectations and missed opportunities.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game on Knight mode.This game is the dark souls 2 of character action/spectacle fighting games.Other action games ask  "how well can you react and pay attention to enemies and their queues"This game asks "how well can you play stiff character action while also controlling your environment"this game feels stiff in terms of combos. A lot of animations go on for too long and cant be cancelled into dodge or a parry. the DmC devil may cry idea of "oh you can do two hits of this combo and finish it with a different weapon" is novel but it makes a lot of the combos short, where as in other games its more fun to see a combo continue because of different moves. Theres some other moves that you can do to avoid knocking enemies out with a different weapon finisher, but there's like idk 3? that keep the combo going.This game keeps the stagger punish of hitting the wrong color gets you punished. when DmC de removed that stagger idea because NO ONE LIKED THAT. on top of this, the game also adds environment hazards that punish you for using the wrong colors and not managing them properly, and this wouldnt be so bad if it wasnt for the constant knockback. The sewers was one of the worst spectacle fighter levels I've ever dealt with.But after the sewers those things are gone and now the only thing left is the enemies, and they're fine. none of them are really annoying, its only when they get in the way in the middle of different colored auras.anyway this game is alright and it does a lot to filter out players in the sewers, none of the bosses or enemies get as bad as the boss in that area lol.final score: play a ps2 game instead/10

_childDocuments_.review: I personally like fixed camera angles and their retro feel, or the way they're used to subtly show the way forward to the player. But Soulstice uses it very poorly, either making it simply uncomfortable and a nuisance, or trying to make you observe the backgrounds (which look quite good, don't get me wrong) in a game where all your attention should be focused on your character.The combat feels dull and too simple and easy, not varied enough. The levels seriously lack legibility. The UI/UX is just weird, why would you make me confirm I want to proceed playing after the loading screens are finished? The story is yet another Dark Souls wannabe, with your classic high-medieval-fantasy "ooooh there's a whole mythos to this corrupted land only you can save, but it is obscure and not meant to be understood fully, and we'll keep throwing sterotypical fantasy words at you to keep you hooked", which is proof that they have not understood what is so good about FromSoftware's (and Miyazaki's) storytelling. Although, they can't be really faulted, as few developers actually have.All in all, many glaring flaws make Soulstice feel like an amateurish work -- which it is. It is not actually bad, don't get me wrong; it can even be enjoyed by most people who aren't as nitpicky as I am (being a game designer myself definitely does not help). It has true potential, and I hope the studio keeps making games and perhaps even a sequel, in order to relentlessly improve upon what they make. It is their first work, and is far better than one should come to expect from a first endeavour, in many departments so. I simply didn't enjoy it enough to keep playing, but I really recommend you try it out for yourself and see if you can look past the lack of polish :)

_childDocuments_.review: Received from humble bundle code.The gameplay is genuinely mind numbing. This is shockingly boring even for a hack and slash. One dimensional combat and janky controls to the point that I can only assume this is a console port, or made specifically with controller in mind. Which would make sense given the controller diagram in the loading screens.There is almost nothing positive I have to say about this game, the intro cutscene and fights are extremely generic exposition followed by a bunch of flashing lights and poor fight choreograph. Then into a boring, flat looking environment on some docks where you're presented with the automatic camera. The camera/controls are horrible, no camera control at any point other than combat, and even in combat it feels terrible. While 'exploring' what little there is, the camera automatically snaps to various angles depending on the area you've entered. This feels terrible and is visually jarring. The combat mechanics are also massively hampered by how strongly each action locks you into an animation. Everything you do, from dashing to attacking, to countering etc all lacks agency. All of it locks you into a momentary animation and ruins the flow of combat. The combat in this game boils down to pushing a button, and then waiting for a bunch of flashy lights to happen on screen before you're allowed to push the next button. The performance as well is somehow terrible for such a visually simple game. Although the fidelity of textures and effects is reasonable, the performance impact isn't. Both loading screens and gameplay peg my pc at 99% GPU utilization. Running this game at medium/high settings, especially in combat with just a few enemies on screen results in about 100 fps at 1440p, with a 7800x3d and a 3090. With DLSS quality enabled, the lights and reflections stop looking specular but you have to live with the blurry result of dlss, on top of the incredible 0% performance impact. Somehow the developers of this game managed to implement resolution scaling in such a way that it has zero impact on performance. My gpu still sits at max util, with the same fps in world and in combat (300/100). Not to mention running hotter than in any other game I play, games like apex legends or overwatch at maximum settings still net me a consistent 200+ fps with sub 50c temps. While this game runs inconsistently at best and nets a 65-70c core even on water. The story also seems extremely generic and poorly thought out. Like a 15 year old's first attempt at writing a fantasy, unaware that they've been influenced by other, better works. If the game was like 15$, I might give it a pass for being visually competent and thematically consistent but at 40$ it is just generic and offensively boring.0/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is a strong entry in the Devil May Cry / Bayonetta style of games. Strongly recommended.The game stars Briar (a human knight styled after Guts) and her ghost sister, Lute, who fight as a pair in a third person action game.  This review will assume readers are somewhat familiar with the genre.Slight spoilers to follow: The two character system is very cool.  It plays well into narrative character interaction and battle mechanics. Briar does most of the fighting, but Lute helps control the battlefield through powerful magic counters and a field that allows exorcism of wraith enemies.  Each of them has their own customization with Briar focusing on weapons and Lute on magic, which appears to be fairly deep. This feels VERY similar to DmC games (has Stinger equivalent, many XX, wait, XXXX combos), with 7 total weapons.  The weapons feel good and have their own niches because of both movesets and a light rock/paper/scissors mechanic.  Some of Lute's counters are hard counters and others do a time stop field that adds complexity to the game as the enemy will eventually unfreeze and finish the attack.  Just like other games in genre, you’re rewarded for not being hit, good combos, etc.  Enemy variety is substantial and most are very fun to fight. Like DmC, there are red and blue enemies and environmental puzzle elements.  This system is vastly improved, as it has a clear in game lore reason for existing, and the color swap is a magical aura set down by Lute that can be rapidly toggled. This game has one of the best “forbidden powers” I've seen.  If you tap into Rapture mode, you get increased speed, damage, and a modified move set, etc. temporarily.  If you go Berserk, you stop controlling Briar entirely, who begins an assault that will certainly overwhelm the  enemy, and instead shift control over Lute who tries to make sure she doesn’t permanently become a monster. This gameplay implementation peerlessly sells the power fantasy of tapping into a dangerous power to win a battle. This has a chapter select mode which also shows how many hidden items / challenges are left in each map, which helps with completionism. I recommend this game for every DmC / Bayonetta fan. It’s an interesting new entry in the genre which takes strong inspiration from existing games but sets itself aside through the 2 character mechanic.  It is also cheaply priced from launch.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very solid Devil May Cry-Like action game that deserves to be played by more fans of the genre. The combat mechanics are simpler than most games like this, with all the weapons having the same 2 combo strings and button inputs to juggle enemies and do the other attacks, but they all feel different enough from each other that I don't mind. The unique mechanics they bring to this game are interesting and set it apart from the rest. Only being able to defeat certain enemies when they're in a particular aura is the biggest difference and takes some getting used to, but to me the coolest aspects are related to the game's different versions of devil trigger. First there's Rapture, which feels like a standard devil trigger-like status, but you get different finishing attacks when you exit this state depending on what abilities you spec the character Lute into on her ability tree. I really liked this, as it made me feel like experimenting and changing up my play style. There's also a berserk state you can enter when you trigger rapture and your health is very low, where you play a quick time event to keep Briar from being taken over by the corruption in her and she just wrecks everyone. I'm not a fan of quick time events normally, but it was pretty satisfying to go berserk in the middle of a fight that was giving me trouble. And then there's another status you get much later that gets into spoiler territory so I won't elaborate on it but I also thought it was pretty cool.The story is good, better than it needed to be for being in an action game like this, and I was surprised by how much I liked the characters, especially Layton.It's not a perfect game - the environments do get pretty repetitive and I feel like a few of the middle chapters could have been cut out entirely without detracting from the plot at all, but if what you want is some slashy fun then those things don't matter that much anyway. There are also some very light puzzle mechanics that gate your progress through some levels that I could take or leave, but they never ruined my experience.I started on the hardest difficulty available from the beginning, Knight, but I eventually decreased it to the "normal" difficulty, Initiate, because the harder enemies later in the game felt too spongy to me, and I hadn't yet invested in all the proficiency upgrades for the weapons that make them more effective at countering certain enemy types. So, I would recommend people start on the lower difficulties, or if you really want to start on hard mode, invest in the proficiency upgrades as early as possible before you get all the additional moves for them so when the harder enemies start showing up more often it's less of a slog.To all the people that bought this game but gave up on it - give it another shot!  According to the achievements at the time I'm writing this, 73.3% of people who own this game have beaten the first chapter, but only 34.4% have gotten the achievement for meeting Donovan, which is in chapter 4! Out of 25 chapters! It gets better people! You don't even get your devil trigger ability until you beat chapter 5 and that's when the game settles into its groove! Give it another chance if you like other action games like this and I'm sure you'll get more enjoyment out of it, even if you don't wind up liking it as much as I did.As for me - I beat the game, had a great time, and I hope they get to make the sequel they set up so clearly at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: You Play as Briar and Lute, Sister whose village were ravaged but the evil Corrupted and Wraiths, due to foreseen circumstances during the invasion Briar the older sister was injured which corrupsted her into becoming a curropted as well. The only was to save her was to become a Chimera; Those who are sworn to defeat the vile curropted by the orders.. Or it seems. After a while both Briar and Lute are sent to close of "The Tear" which has spread Chaos around one of the main Cities/Castles of the world. Join then as they uncover to truth in this action packed adventure full of challenges .  Do you enjoy the fast-paced action of Bayonetta and the chaotic weapon switching of DMC series, with the tad annoyance of the Blue and Red system where you can only attack specific enemies who are inside of the aura like the DmC series of needing to use the right weapon for those enemies. This game will be right up your ally. As you progress you will unlock a total of 5 new weapon (with 2 already unlocked) for a whopping total of 7 Weapons to switch and around and make combos. As you dodge and block your way in battle, your meter will slowly build up where if you wer to finish a combo, a cinematic attack occurs for high damage. As you also continue to play you will unlock two new special skills but using this could ruin you ranking system if you are wanting to get the best rank through the game, know when to use them and you got the game's core mechanic all set! I for one enjoyed the environment.. at the beginning, it later got a little too stale with how often you visited the sewer, castle bridges and indoor the castle area. Later levels have this awkward blue tint due the whats is going on around the city and it just gets a little tiresome. Character design can be hit or miss, and can make it or break it for some people, i for one did not have an issues and it really gives off the indie charm.  Performance can be a little hit or miss. there has been time while playing the music could not keep up and ended up being a little choppy, cutting in and out. Load screen were also a weird one where even with and SDD or a NVME it felt like it wouldn't load as fast as it normally should, but i don't really care about the load screen, game me enough to take a small sip of coffee as i wait.Now comes to the next big thing...  It reminded me a lot of the first DMC game where it would show an area at an angle and it could look a little weird, but i for one am already use to this. I have played multiple game with these kinds of camera angles to know what would happened when it switches. As long as you continue to hold the direction you were face when it does switch over you character should continue to move the save way unless you made an sort of adjustment when it does happen.There has only been 1 occurrence where this was an issue during a boss fight, but it did not make it too much of a problem. The camera isn't trying to fight with you, and its definitely a great artistic choice.

_childDocuments_.review: AA games have always been great, and Soulstice is no exception. There are way too many low-effort indie games and definitely too many complete, absolute GARBAGE, money-grabbing, buggy AAA games. AA games on the other hand usually bring the best of both worlds.Soulstice is a very polished experience similar gameplay-wise to games like Devil May Cry or Bayonetta, but more focused on story. Fortunately, the story, characters, writing and voice acting are all very good. The game is also quite long (around 20 hours).The combat is quite enjoyable, you can feel the weight of your blows and there are some interesting gimmicks, like the two color-coded barriers used to defeat some enemies and your Shade, Lute, who can help you with both defending and attacking. There are some aspects of the combat that I would change, like shortening the recovery time for some actions and how focus works, but overall the combat is a very strong part of Soulstice, especially later on when you get used to it and you unlock more skills for your weapons and Lute.It seems like the most controversial thing about the game is the camera. I assume that people complaining about it missed the best era of gaming. However, I understand them when they say that a normal 3rd persona camera would've been better. I personally did not mind the camera for the most part. The only exceptions were some platforming sections when it was difficult to judge the distances and one or two fights when I got locked into a corner. It DEFINITELY is not a good reason to disregard this game.Graphically, the game looks great, especially the environments. The character models are stylised so they should not look dated even in a few years. I saw some people reporting performance problems, but fortunately I did not experience any. The game kept smooth 60 FPS throughout the whole game.The thing that I dislike the most about the game is the fact that the developer removed the demo version. That is a very suspicious thing to do, and I strongly disapprove of it.Taking everything into consideration, Soulstice is a solid action game, definitely worth the price, especially if you compare it to GARBAGE $60 AAA games that I would not play even if I was paid. I hope that the remaining flaws will be fixed in the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is a game of gorgeous visuals, a touching love story between siblings, and ridiculous hyper violence, dashed with body horror.The locked camera, when it works, feels like the best of Bayonetta or Dante's Inferno. Like all games of this genre, however, late game enemies dashing in and out of the camera will start to demand a level of "reads" from the player that can be frustrating.The hyperviolence is over the top. Your claymore turns into a sledge hammer mid combo, your tonfas are also cannons/flamethrowers, and the demonic enemies rip off their own body parts to use as weaponry. Flowing between your absurd weapons and stringing the combos together becomes satisfying as the game rewards the "cool" style of play. Also, being graded in every encounter does spark the desire to push for diamond each fight.The story is simplistic but respectable. Our protagonist carries the guilt of her dead sister both figuratively, and literally as her ghost is the second protagonist, and your spiritual half on this anti-demon crusade. The demons corrupt people, and our protagonist is a warrior of the church (Also corrupt) struggling to push them back. Enough ground work is laid for a sequel, that I would jam, if it ever arrived.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with Soulstice. The world, while HEAVILY inspired by Claymore, manages not feel like a simple knockoff, but instead builds something original and engaging. The only problem is the length of the campaign, which starts slow and drags unnecessarily at the mind point while repeating too many times some fights. Luckily it rapidly picks up its pace in the last third, and then ends with a bang. The gameplay is like an old style DMC, with a fixed camera, quick weapon switching and the addition of a red/blue mechanic like the DmC spin-off. I didn't mind the camera, it added a certain nostalgic feel to this and made finding secrets pretty fun.Graphically, you can tell it's no a AAA game by the lack of environment variation, the repetition of many segments and the lackluster quality of some models/animations in cutscenes (poor Layton). Still, the game has its own style and most of the times it manages to look cool and stunning.The voice acting is very good, as are the sound effects. The score is appropriate, but it doesn't have any "banger" that stuck with me after playing. Overall it's a great game, and is definitely an excellent pick when discounted at around €20.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the game story I can safely say I have no intention of coming back.I like the story and can see a lot of it inspirations.  Thats about the only good thing I can say about it.  That was enough for me to push through for one play through...Outside of that...  The camera system is something ripped out of the PS2 era.  Its clunky and unrefined.  By design it obscures certain things you might want to pick up, but it also makes any platforming or puzzles a flat out pain - not to mention when you are in an enclosed space with 4 2 story tall enemies that literally block the camera and you can't get an angle above the arena so you can actually see.  ♥♥♥♥♥♥ camera angles also makes it difficult to judge distance, making any jump more difficult than it needs to be.The sewer puzzle deserves a thumbs down on it own. Combat is repetitive.  There are a handful of enemies, most are jokes to handle... and then theres the electric shade.  Hard to stun, teleports frequently, constantly emitting a damaging aura.  To summarize, general enemy design ranges from bland to frustratingly.  Mix that with resource management and a god awful camera and you find yourself ready to drop the game with less than an hour left in it.  Bosses are OK though.  Wish there was more to them(all bosses repeat the same pattern until they die).Platforming and movement is fine... when not being actively hindered by the camera.  You've got all the staples.  Double jump, air dash, ground dash...  As mentioned above the camera is actively working to screw you over, and that kind of makes any platforming flat out miserable though.The world and art design is serviceable.  Its a bit grey, but its well put together.  Shame I can't view it a bit better... Thanks again, ps2 era camera!Sound won't knock your socks off, but its fine.  The battle music gets kind of repetitive, and I wish I can duct tape the character's mouths shut when not in cutscenes, but meh...One last note - if you do play this game turn off rumble on your controller.  You will thank me later.If they fixed the camera system the game would get a recommendation for me.  I could tell a lot of hard work went in to the game, and with a little more TLC it could shine.  But for now... Well, at the very least I can say that I'd be willing to pick up the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Let’s get this out of the way: Performance issues. They are there, but not for very long...After some reading, it seems to be an artifact of Unreal Engine 4; when something is loaded into the game for the first time, I lagged. During the prologue, it was a slide show. I adjusted some settings, restarted the intro, and it lagged for a few seconds, and then it was smooth. Every time I fought a new enemy, and they used an ability I hadn’t seen before, the game froze for a split second, and then smooth again.Review: Soulstice wears its inspirations lovingly on its sleeves: Claymore, Berserk, and obviously Devil May Cry (a few notes of Dragon Age and Darksiders in there as well); but the game also puts in the effort to be its own thing.The soundtrack and voice acting are competent; and the worldbuilding, dialog, character design, and pacing are all top notch. It’s the exact kind of dark fantasy stuff that I like and the boss designs are insane.The DMC style combat is pretty good. Starts out simple, then gains complexity as you unlock more stuff: Easy to do, tricky to master.There is a kind of “snappiness”, for lack of a better word, to the attacks where it tries to pull you to objects it is prioritizing which can be mildly annoying when you’re trying to smash stuff out of combat. *In combat* it’s not a problem and attacks work fine.I played the game with a PS4 controller (you can switch the button readout in the setting) and didn’t like to control scheme at first, but as I unlocked more attacks and abilities, it started to make more sense and grew on me pretty quick. You can change the controls if you want though…In short: I loved it! It’s good. If you like dark fantasy nonsense, mature characters, hack & slash combos, mild platforming here and there, and gradual upgrading like I do, then you’ll probably like this.I’m definitely keeping an eye on Reply Game Studios, and I hope they do more.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not used to writing reviews, but I wanted to give Soulstice a recommend. I had a great time with it.I beat the game a few weeks ago and have only poked around for a minute or two after the latest major patch dropped (1.0.3), so I can't really speak to any changes it made.I'd call the combat distilled character action. All your (secondary/non-sword) weapons have more or less the same toolkit, and the combat encounters demand that you constantly switch between all of them throughout the course of a fight.You don't start out with a lot of weapon and mobility options, and for a while early in the game, it's a bit of a hassle chasing after mooks or trying to hack away at them with a tool that wasn't meant to deal with them. (Regarding mobility, I strongly recommend buying the whip's grapple immediately.)But once you unlock your full kit and fill out the upgrade trees a bit, with the way Briar (the player character) handles, the encounters turn into these hectic, fast and loose free-for-alls where the challenge is in prioritization and maintaining crowd control. Really rewarding to eventually get into the flow of a fight.In terms of performance, I use an AMD graphics card and think that might have caused some hiccups. In the Low Town part of the game, I had to drop my graphics to the lowest settings to get it to run smoothly, and later ran into a really gnarly technicolor visual glitch during a miniboss intro cutscene. Beyond that, nothing that personally bothered me much.I loved the boss and enemy designs, loved the soundtrack, and I'm honestly hoping we get a sequel or story DLC to show more of the world. Good game.

_childDocuments_.review: I just completed Chapter 6, so this is going to review what I've seen and not the whole.I like the game, it is very much a return to Devil May Cry and Bayonetta style games aka Spectacle Fighters.  The pacing in the first chapters is certainly not something I'm accustomed to any more.  I've been playing Dark Souls and basically any Souls-Like that catches my interest over the past decade, so this is a drastic shift of gears.  The Opening gives you an in medias res fight that I believe is close to the final climax.  In that the combat is giving a taste of how it can flow between the two characters.  After that it takes you to the characters entering the city via the Docks.  Outside of combat, you are allowed to explore from a stationary 3rd person perspective.  This is directly reflective of the 1st Devil May Cry game and I think several others from the time frame, Resident Evil 1 through 3 might be the other big example.  Inside combat, you can move the camera around your character or lock on to a specific enemy.  I believe both will be necessary as some enemies have moves to disappear from the battle or speed away and break your lock on.  I think the make or break for personal experiences is going to hinge on whether you like the grading that the game is presenting you.  Each combat is given 4 scores, Combat Moves/tricks, Timer, Damage taken/done, and an overall rating.  The end of chapter collects all of these scores into a total, as well as present a blacked out medal for an optional fight that was missed.  I know the end of chapter rewards upgrade currency for story and I think it gives a bonus for good scores.I think the upgrades are expensive, but I would guess I'm 1/5th through main story progression.  Rewards and costs could get inflated later.

_childDocuments_.review: 🎀This title needs sequels, a trilogy. No dlcs!I loved it from start to finish and it took me back to the Bayonetta days, more for reasons of how the game is told.Soulstice is very reminiscent of the Claymore animated series that introduced me to my son, seeing all the episodes together.I would say that although completely different stories, there are very marked references such as transcendence itself.🎀In Soulstice there are two more crystals, in Doran and Rheim, in the final movie, even in the movie after the credits there are many confirmations and many doors open to a possible trilogy, this title must definitely expand, Briar and Lute are transcended both in one being?Briar is sure, Lute I don't know, but I'm very fond of both, two completely different characters but with a very deep bond.What will happen next? A dlc would be too little and it wouldn't be enough to finish/explain everything, the story is much wider and longer than it seems.🎀The ending of the game makes it very explicit that after the portal in Ilden closes, two more open, one on Doran and one on Rheim as mentioned above.Briar and Lute are quick to face whatever challenges arise in these cities. Then, a new character shows up on final movie, Kordelia the Reaper, in the employ of Lord Dugal and with the stated goal of killing Briar and Lute.Dugal is the real problem and he doesn't deserve to exist after what he did.🎀I think Soulstice was designed to be a trilogy. It would work great if each game would focus on one of the three sacred cities.For example:Each city can have a unique aesthetic and layout, a perspective that is less resource intensive when split across three games than crammed into one. By focusing on just one city like with the first game, Reply Game Studios can fine-tune the look and feel of the city and keep the whole game somewhat coherent.🎀I really think this is intended as a trilogy, but I also think Reply Game Studios is waiting to see what the reception will be for this game before fully committing to a second one.Whether or not Soulstice gets a sequel sort of depends on the player base.The reviews are very positive and this title really deserves a lot.I absolutely want the series to continue.🎀Small additional notes:Graphically beautiful and clean, light engine because the game has been programmed properly, satisfying and fast fights but you get the best trying to create combos by changing weapons, ok no spoiler about transformation.The semi-fixed camera during exploration, and mobile during fights never bothered me, as some mentioned having had problems with it.I tried to explore everything well in 26 hours of gameplay to look for as many collectible and secrets as possible.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an awesome game! I don't get why the ratings aren't much much higher! _childDocuments_.review: I decided to buy this game on a whim because I had just finished Evil West (which was also great) and I was itching for more character action goodness. I had already seen some gameplay and I really like the visual style of the game but I kind of ignored it when it released (boy was that a mistake).I was not expecting this game to take such huge inspiration from og DMC games (DMC1 and 3), with things like fixed camera angles (which I love because it brings me nostalgia from early PS2 games), secret challenge missions, multiple weapon types to upgrade, new moves to unlock, a combat system that allows for creativity/freestyling (and ranking system), good enemy variety and designs, and probably the cleanest looking artstyle I have seen in a while.This game has exceeded any expectations I would of had and so far the game is on par with games like DMC 3, DMC 5, Ninja Gaiden Black/2, Bayonetta1/2, God of War 1-3 (original series)...etc. The wide shots of the world look beautiful, and the combat effects are very nice looking too without getting in the way. I'm just finding very little I don't like about this game, and the quality is what really surprises me.Pros:+ Visuals and Art-style are beautiful and a very clean looking.+ The animations and cutscenes are very smooth and look really nice.+ Combat is very unique with the addition of your sidekick and the synergy attacks (they feel really really good).+ Combat variation is excellent with you always unlocking new moves or getting a new weapon.+ Enemy variety is great and the enemy designs look great as well.+ Very classic DMC feel to exploration, with challenge missions to find, and character upgrades to find.+ Good pacing, and good balance between exploration and combat.+ Good voice acting+ Great cinematic cutscenes, with good animations, and over the top action like a DMC or Bayonetta game.+ (So Far) The story is engaging and making want to find out what happens next+ I actually like the fixed camera angles, because it reminds me of the PS2 era of the character action games.+ I have NOT experienced any bugs or crashes in the 7hrs (at the of the review) I have put in.+ Good atmospheric music along with some banger combat themesCons:- The Lute assist mechanics could have been explained a little more because early on I was a little confused on how to use her defensive mechanics.- Performance is decent but when performing the over the top super moves the framerate can drop a bit under 60fps (Specs: RTX 3080, Ryzen 3800x, 16GB RAM, Win10).- Enemy hit/stagger animations can look a tiny bit stiff at times (being very nitpicky here).Overall this is an excellent hack n' slash character action game. It actually surprised me how polished and how clean the art style is in this game, especially coming from an AA developer, that from my knowledge, was their first big project. If I did not look into the Devs I would have assumed it was from a AAA studios (that is how polished it feels and looks). It holds up with the best of em imo and the inspiration/passion oozes from this game, from the obvious Berzerk inspiration of the main character design to the DMC style level design. If you love the original DMC games (1 and 3) or just like character action games with fun and deep combat systems this game is 100% worth a try. I could not recommend this game enough!

_childDocuments_.review: To the Point======================Mid tier AA beat'em up with some frustrating gameplay choices that keep it from being great.Beaten on Knight (hard) difficultyGood Stuff====================- The minute to minute combat is good and with a game like this that's really all that matters.- The weapon variety, while sort of standard to these DMC kinds of games, is still pretty solid - Unity mechanic - This may be a deal breaker for some but the game rewards you for playing well and switching weapons. When you do well for long enough you do a super move and later on unlock a Devil Trigger like super mode.- The designs - Its a souls-like world thats well fleshed out with lots of interesting looking creatures and characters inhabiting it.Bad Stuff=====================- The Unity Mechanic - I know I just said this was a good thing, and it is, but it's like invisible how good you're doing, they should have a bar or somehow make it more obvious when you're in a unity state.- The fields - Like DMC ( the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Tameem one with DONTE) there are red and blue enemies at points in the game you need to kill by generating red and blue fields, however these don't last forever and can turn off from over use, which leads to the next point...- Emnity - This is the mechanic that turns off the fields I just mentioned. It builds slowly when a field is up and eventually maxes out, shutting down for 5 seconds or so. Later upgrades will, for some reason, cause it to fill faster. These abilities are used automatically so in endgame you can find emnity filling to fast for you to stop it and losing the fields for a short while. You can lower emnity by hitting enemies inside the field but it's nothing compared to the emnity generated by these abilities. I was constantly toggling fields on/off in endgame.- Damage - you do very little of it on hard difficulty and enemies are like sponges, could be I just don't know how to play but some of these fights took forever- Combat Penalties - This is a personal one, I'm used to being docked points for using items etc. but this game actually penalizes you for using the Devil Trigger Super Mode. I don't understand why you'd only let players use this mode when they're playing well then take points off for using it.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice : By Triple F"Soulstice," developed by Reply Game Studios and published by Modus Games, is a dark fantasy action game that takes players into a world torn apart by monstrous forces. At its core, "Soulstice" is an action-packed journey about sisterhood, sacrifice, and redemption. Players control Briar and her sister Lute, who are merged into a powerful entity known as a Chimera, tasked with defending humanity against monstrous entities called Wraiths. The game draws clear inspiration from titles like Devil May Cry and Nier: Automata, bringing stylish combat, impressive world design, and an emotional narrative to create a memorable experience that appeals to fans of hack-and-slash and dark fantasy genres.The game’s combat system is the heart of "Soulstice," balancing fluidity, complexity, and strategic depth. Players control Briar as the main physical fighter, with a range of weapons and combos at their disposal. Lute, on the other hand, exists as a ghostly presence that assists her sister with defensive abilities, crowd control, and support. This dual-character mechanic is unique and requires players to balance offense and defense, with Lute capable of interrupting enemies or casting shields while Briar unleashes powerful melee combos. The interplay between the sisters’ abilities becomes essential, especially in higher difficulties, and adds layers of depth as players master the synchronization of their attacks."Soulstice" emphasizes versatility in combat, allowing players to switch between different weapons mid-combo, unlocking new moves and abilities as they progress. Briar can wield a range of weapons, from heavy hammers to quick, nimble swords, each of which has its own strengths and can be swapped in real time. This variety keeps combat fresh, as different enemy types require players to adapt their strategies and experiment with weapon combinations. Coupled with the need to manage Lute’s support abilities, the combat system is both intense and demanding, rewarding players who take the time to understand each weapon’s nuances and the timing required for combo chains.One of the most interesting aspects of "Soulstice" is its Unity system, which tracks the sisters’ synchronization in battle. As Briar and Lute work together seamlessly, a Unity meter builds up, allowing players to unleash powerful synergy attacks that deal devastating damage to foes. However, if players miss attacks or mistime Lute’s defensive moves, the meter drops, weakening the power of these combined abilities. This mechanic encourages precision and rhythm in combat, challenging players to balance both offensive and defensive strategies to maximize damage output. As Unity builds, players also gain access to a “Rapture” state, which grants temporary boosts in power, adding an extra layer of intensity to the game’s most challenging encounters.The setting of "Soulstice" is equally impressive, taking players through a dark, Gothic-inspired city filled with ominous architecture, sprawling cathedrals, and haunting landscapes. The art direction is a standout feature, creating an atmosphere that feels oppressive and tragic, reflecting the sisters’ struggle against overwhelming odds. The environments vary from decrepit streets to cavernous ruins, and the color palette of muted grays, blacks, and blood-red accents adds to the sense of foreboding. The level design is mostly linear but allows for some exploration, with hidden pathways, collectibles, and optional challenges that encourage players to delve deeper into the world. These details add to the immersion, giving players the feeling of being trapped in a decaying, hostile world.The narrative in "Soulstice" is surprisingly emotional and centers around the relationship between Briar and Lute. The game explores themes of sacrifice, family bonds, and the cost of power, drawing players into the sisters’ journey as they grapple with their unique existence as a Chimera. Throughout the story, players witness flashbacks and moments of introspection that reveal more about the sisters’ past and their connection to the larger conflict. Voice acting is well-executed, and the writing, while occasionally leaning on fantasy tropes, does a solid job of making players care about the protagonists. The stakes feel personal, and the story is driven by the sisters’ bond, making it more compelling than a typical hack-and-slash narrative.Visually spealing, "Soulstice" combines a striking aesthetic with smooth animations that enhance the overall experience. The design of the Wraiths and other enemies is grotesque and imaginative, giving each encounter a sense of dread and intensity. Despite its overall dark color scheme, the game uses lighting and particle effects effectively, especially during combat sequences where powers and spells explode with vivid detail. However, performance can sometimes stutter during more crowded battles, particularly on older hardware, which may slightly break immersion for some players. Overall, though, the game’s visual presentation is polished and evocative, amplifying its dark fantasy appeal.All in all, "Soulstice" is a refreshing take on the action genre, combining fast-paced, combo-driven combat with an emotionally resonant story. Its dual-character mechanic is unique, challenging players to master a complex, rhythm-based combat system that balances aggression with careful timing. While its linear level design may not appeal to players who prefer open worlds, the game’s immersive art direction, engaging story, and intricate combat make it a compelling experience. "Soulstice" stands as a strong entry in the hack-and-slash genre, delivering both style and substance in a world that is as haunting as it is captivating. Fans of dark fantasy action games looking for both challenge and narrative depth will find "Soulstice" to be a rewarding journey.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Skip to the last paragraph.When the trailer for Soulstice was first released you could say I was pretty excited. I thought "A story heavy souls-like game with a female protagonist and interesting partner mechanic?! Count me in!" I got my first copy for free from Epic but didn't get around to playing it till more recently when I received a second copy from Humble Bundle. Upon looking a little more into the game I realized it was hack and slash and not so much a souls-like but I wasn't too worried about it. I thought it'd be a nice break from Elden Ring and maybe take me back to my early days of hack-and-slash games on the PS2 and Gamecube. So while I was excited I came into this game without any real expectations, yet, it still disappointed me. The intro cutscene was a little unclear and a huge info dump. MC's voice acting is pretty bad and the shade has issues enunciating some words but is great otherwise. The dialog reads like a Discord conversation rather than characters who live in this grim-dark world. Cutscene after cutscene after cutscene. I like visual novels, I like episodic series, and short animations but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ LET ME PLAY THE GAME! Cutscenes upon entering combat and mid-combat even with trash mobs. Cutscenes where your character fights and runs around the stage you were on not really doing anything you couldn't have just so MC and the shade can talk which they COULD do without the cutscene. With all the cutscenes I'd think the animation would be a little better as well or maybe they'd lean into a low frame rate style as you see in claymation. Semi-regular stuttering on higher-end hardware. Camera angles were abysmal. The combat is salvageable but as it stands it doesn't feel snappy and is just kind of there. You often have to press the target button multiple times to target an enemy even if it's the only one on the field and goodluck target swapping. To supplement the slow boring combat I tried using the "dodge" as a dash but it isn't designed to be used as a gap closer so it still didn't feel quite right. Tool tips don't always tell you what button to press and the ability names don't match up with the button layout. Finally, the 'knight' mode is the highest difficulty available to a new player and it felt like I was playing in a training mode with incoming damage disabled on beginner bots.I would take more time to better explain and condense this mess of thoughts but I'm running on fumes at the moment.I REALLY want this game to be good and if they at least addressed the combat issues and excessive cutscenes I'd be happy to continue playing. But, as it stands I don't feel this is worth its $40 price tag. You're better off picking up something like RWBY Grimm Eclipse while it's on sale to scratch that early to mid-2000s hack-and-slash itch.

_childDocuments_.review: Played on Epic, decided to give it another shot since I got it from Humble this month.This game VERY badly wants to be Devil May Cry, and it does not actually do a very good job of it. The locked camera angles outside of combat are mild annoyance, but as a result of this locked camera there are invisible walls EVERYWHERE except in the specific locations that have secrets. The combat is aggressively okay, though I found the counter system to be extremely inconsistent. I may have simply been doing something wrong, but it felt as though sometimes I would only get .2 seconds to react to an attack, and other times I would get several seconds to react to the exact same attack from the exact same enemy. The weapon variety is fine, but everything you unlock later isn't really useful except in niche scenarios, so you just default to the sword/hammer weapons you start with 99% of the time.The story is alright, but just doesn't really leave an impression. There's a few too many cutscenes that last longer then they have any right to, but it's inoffensive.tl;dr do not but this game at full price, get it at a steep discount, and don't expect it to blow you away. This is a game specifically and really only for fans of the genre

As some have said the camera is funky, in battle you can lock on to enemies and the camera will stay on a target, which helps, but for the most part the camera feels too far out. The game itself looks pretty, I felt at times the animation was kind of sub-par The world is colorless, but I guess that's just my own personal qualm. I'm not sure if the entire game takes place in this "abandoned city of the dead" so it makes sense everything is sterile and lifeless. Combat is reminiscent of DmC and bits of Bayonetta, you'll fight enemies and get graded on your performance. You're also graded at the end of each chapter with a score based on your time and how well you performed. The game being $40 is kind of helpful, I don't personally think it would have been worth $60If you like these kind of games, can overlook the slow combat, 30 FPS cutscenes, funky camera, stutters/animation, then there might be something here for you. They phoned in the (what I think is) the second half of the game, and Ive lost all interest. Between that and the game problems (below) I just dont care....  I really want to give this a positive review, and until about half way through the game it DEFINITELY was a fun and engaging game, with a few bits of jank that werent show stopping. The action is fun, and when it combat it switches from a cinematic view to a normal camera. There are hidden spots, upgrades, excellent atmosphere and interesting enough story....***And then I hit the middle - later part of the game (where Im at now)*** And OMG its starting to get annoying. A couple of the challenges are just ridiculous and nearly unachievable, whereas the others are fun. I thought they were there to train you in advanced techniques, but nooooo, they are there just to frustrate with arbitrary goals that you mostly would not use in the actual gameplay.Now Im finding the following:* the camera starts getting BAD during combat* Some areas DO NOT drop the cinematic camera any more while trying to fight enemies. * Very narrow areas for combat, with big drops, which mean climbing back up to keep fighting* The camera will automatically pull away from where you are looking, when not locked on to something.  * Lock gets lost randomly and easily.  * The parry button and mechanic is just AWFUL, and hard to manage when doing everything else required. And I cant work out a better button layout that still works.  * Pulling off the combo attacks is nearly impossible because you are being hit so much you can never build up enough affinity (again, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ camera does not help). And I have the upgrades to slow it down from being lost* Im noticing less sense of direction - the goal (avoiding spoilers). Previously there was a real sense of the world failing and we needed to get to the goal, and save people. But these recent levels just feel meh - generic burning houses we have seen before. Same bridges and gates and buildings. Same stuff scattered around the streets. It does not feel any different than about chapter 3. Just more stuff on fire. * It feels like they started to rush and cut more corners the further the game goes on* Even the random dialog is starting to get repetitive and annoying

_childDocuments_.review: So I had to drop this game. The combat itself is pretty good at a baseline. It reminds me of every action game I have played, which is actually a positive. Ghost girl can do cool parries also. The way they mix their story with the gameplay is kinda cool. Like your character is essentially part monster but if she gives into that monster side her life ends. The gameplay reflects this by using that monster side as a sort of devil trigger. I dont know how i did it but i gave into that monster side too much and it gave me a game over, I thought  that was neat. But the problems this game has get worse the longer you play. Lets start with the progression. You can upgrade weapons and abilities in this game which is pretty standard but a lot of weapons have similar moves. However the issue starts when you realize that those moves are also more expensive. What hurts EVEN more than that is that the game has a ranking system (Think Bayonetta or DMC)which factors in time per level. The lower your rank the less currency you get for moves. The levels seem to want you to explore but then lower your rank for doing so? The nail in the coffin for me was the colored enemies. At first they werent that bad: Put up the red/blue field then hack n slash your way through. But this field will break if you keep it up too long. I upgraded this meter and found ways to lower it through those upgrade but after a while it didnt matter. I would run around dodging waiting for this meter to go down and basically playing a waiting game until i could fight again. But some enemies were beefy by this point so it didnt matter.

_childDocuments_.review: Ganna comment about the combat in this review.It's bad in general. There is an aura system where there are 2 auras and you can activate 1 at a time to be able to damage certain enemies, which is a big pain when you encounter the types of enemies that need both auras at the same encounter, combined with bad movement abilities( which are hard to execute for some reason), hard to kill and stagger enemies, super moves locked behind long chain attacks and combo meter which goes down by a lot when you get hit making super moves a luxery. your ghost sister can help you with defenses and other stuff, but it's not enough to make up for the absurd power of enemies. You have diffrent kind of weapons, but they all have the same moveset; dash infront, launch up, launch down, and a long combo. There is a transformation, it's strong but not fun. It's just spam the attack button until you explode.You can't control the fight in this game, enemies will recover and start pressuring you at some point.Tried the transcendence update for a bit, and it looks like they havent learned much. Unlike the other 2 transformations, it stays for some time, you can cancel the form when you want to, and the form has some combos. However Filling it up is risky. You need to stand and charge in the middle of combat and it takes some time to do it, u may need to do it 2 or 3 times. It's like Dante's SDT, but even the SDT is easier to fill and to use.The game has 3 transformations and none of them are good, one for spamming buttens, one with too mant cinimatics and can't play with it, and one that is a chore to get to use.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was pretty uneven experience, sometimes was awesome... sometimes bad...It takes a lot of inspiration from old God of War and DmC (Ninja Theory one, not the GOOD DMC) with some Berserk inspired aesthetics.- The story is intriguing and pretty unique, the mystery is unfold through the course of a game and main cast is written well with Briar and Lute in the spotlight.- Quite impressive for such a small team to pull out AAA graphics, it has a realistic look with stylized characters.- Soundtrack is pretty decent, it's composed with atmospheric ambiance and blood pumping combat tracks (I only wish there was more of them).- Unique combat, Briar controls like a standard melee character but with Lute as a companion that has a lot of offensive and defensive abilities with plenty of synergies between sisters.- The camera is your constant enemy. It works inconsistent during combat and exploration. I have never seen more clunky lock-on system, sometimes is just impossible to lock into exact enemy you want to follow. I hope this will get patched as it was the biggest issue of this game for me.- Color coded combat with flying enemies. Huge pain in the ass to deal with them, makes bow weapon most of the time useless, some types even teleport constantly which makes you run across arena back and forth all the time.- Inconsistent enemy telegraphs and Lute defense. You never know if you can block/parry attack with Lute or you have to dodge them. To make this more annoying, some enemy hit boxes are huge that even perfect evade distance won't escape it.- Game is paced very uneven. There is a lot fat that could be trimmed to make this game shorter but much more enjoyable experience.Despite flaws that mostly can be fixed with patches, I recommend giving Soulstice a try if you are fan of spectacle action fighters. I also hope this production will be successful enough for sequel to be made because I am eager to see what might happen next.

_childDocuments_.review: Utmost sighs. I really wanted to like this game, but the game seemed determined to convince me otherwise. The combat is fairly competent enough for what I believe is this studio's first game in this style. Which is a long-winded way of saying it's just okay. It clears the (low) bar of No More Heroes combat, and falls short of DMC1 combat, which falls short of every other DMC game except 2. Of the four weapons I unlocked, none of them felt very distinct from each other. Lute's moves were interesting in concept, but poorly executed, since all her attacks are mapped to the same button, so she's basically a glorified QTE robot. I will be a contrarian and say I don't mind the color coding, since it's a neat way of keeping you cognizant of combat. Would be even better if the camera weren't a tad sluggish. So, I was hoping that the game could make up for the mediocre combat with anything else, which it couldn't. The level design from all that I played, up to about chapter 8, is very repetitive and dull. You'll be seeing a whole lot of blueish grey ruins throughout your adventure, and not much else, (it sticks out a lot more to me since I just played Dante's Inferno a few weeks ago, a game stuffed to the brim with diverse and lively environments and levels). This wouldn't be too bad if the levels weren't so obnoxiously long. The longevity wouldn't be obnoxious if there was much to do in these levels. There's not. Outside of the token three to four battles per chapter, there's some trivial platforming (with invisible walls to hold your hand as much as possible), and occasional crystals to destroy for currency. Ultimately, the biggest sin of the game is its length, what should be a five-to-six-hour game that's stretched out much longer than it needs to be because quantity over quality is the name of the game these days, sadly.

_childDocuments_.review: Clunk fueled nightmare with too much focus on weird and un-fun aspects of gameplay. Saw the trailer for this game and thought it looked insanely cool. Grabbed it on sale, because I was a little bit cautious. At first it has some cool call backs to classics like Devil May Cry, but that get's tired really fast. The combat tutorial that's supposed to "wow" the player into the game was just like being given an invincibility star, and then being told to mash buttons until everything is dead. You unlock new moves by picking up currency in each chapter, but simple things like a combo ender from a launcher aren't a baseline ability? Your sister is a cool idea, but in combat it really just amounts to mashing out the block button any time it's on screen, and forget about perfect guarding if you're trying to play the game even slightly casually. You also have to activate a number of gimmicky combat mechanics to make your shade seem more effective, but if you're not managing a number of poorly designed looking gauges you lose the ability to do anything with her for a period of time. I'm obviously in the minority on this game, which is good, because the environments, and the artstyle are really incredible. Hopefully if this game gets enough attention the devs can iron out all the needless complexity and bring back a more distilled hack and slash adventure experience. For now it's just too much work, for no real reason. Also if you're going to get voice actors who sound as good as these ones, write something good for them to act! Just because it's a style of game born in the cringe infested waters of the 1990's does not mean you have to write the dialogue like a preteen focus group high on Twilight, and vape juice. So much potential.

It takes inspiration from the Devil May Cry/Bayonetta/Platinum Gmaes shenanigans and made Soulstice their own. It has your bread and butter hack 'n slash with good range of difficulty(I'm getting my butt kicked, and loving it)The voice acting... *insert Pacha meme*The voice acting is incredible. The voice acting expresses the emotions of the scenes beautifully. Soulstice is 2022 GOTY for this alone. With a better budget they could have made it shine better than most AAA games. The non-player co-op is a really cool idea and I have enjoyed this concept greatly while playing the game. This also adds a layer of difficulty.Speaking of layers. Soulstice layers mechanics quite well. It really pushes your ability to pay attention. An ability I lack, but I am chugging my way through it well enough.Finally. The music. The music is great as well. Budget things considered. The music feels like it takes a lot of inspiration from the old school Devil May Cry. A mix of high action, and atmospheric vibes.Overall a small project with a lot of passion, and a lot of soul poured into it. Soulstice is one of those rare few that pay for itself. Soulstice is what AAA titles should feel like.

_childDocuments_.review: I like to style myself as a writer, but I do not have enough words to say how much I loved this game. The world is so full of lore and detail - the weapons, the people, the monsters, the places - it feels completely fleshed out and everything has a reason. There's even lore-backed explanations for why/how certain game mechanics work and the limitations on them. Every fight, every chapter, every challenge is ranked from lowly iron to lofty diamond based on score, time, and damage taken, with respective medals for each. If you loved the Claymore anime or manga, you'll love this game. If you loved the earlier God of War or Devil May Cry games, you're probably going to love this game. As someone who doesn't often play fixed-camera side-scroller style games, the only problem I ever had with this game was down to depth perception. Where targets were and where attacks would land, and one specific bit of parkour. With not one, but TWO difficulties locked behind completion barriers, there's plenty of replayability and opportunity to push your limits on getting timing and resource management right. And that's not to mention the over a dozen challenges to test your limits. I would absolutely recommend this game to everyone. Amazing story, wonderful gameplay, and a surprisingly detailed setting, considering how desolate and ruined it all is. It was 100% worth every penny, and I can't wait to sink more hours into it, completing the harder levels and working for higher scores. Absolutely stunning. Aside from my issues with depth perception, I really have nothing bad to say about the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but it's just not good. Bad level design (long grey hallways of generic fantasy britain), bad game mechanics ("counter" being context dependent and the most common type not even stopping enemy attacks, just freezing them for a second, they still attack after the freeze) poorly functioning lock mechanic, many pointless game mechanics. Each trigger is bound to a color change that does nothing but allow you to interact with objects and enemies of that color, blue and red. They are on a shared timer. That is so artificial and pointless it's actually disgusting.Some elements they did well - the pause type combos have an actual pause and vibration for combo timing, while some they did poorly - the classic "stinger" move that is meant to quickly get you back into a fight launching weaker enemies. Overall aggressively mediocre and core elements (everything ghost partner related) executed so poorly as to actually hold the game back from being good. The dual protagonist thing was what sold me on the game as well, because that could have been used for a unique or at least more fun and stylish combat system, but instead actually makes the game worse.If you haven't played metal gear rising or devil may cry, play those instead. This is a depressingly mediocre clone.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my biggest problems with games is not copying, it is when they copy poorly. If one is aware of the reputation of Euroshmups, this game is the Euroshmup of the Stylish Action genre. Ill-conceived, overly-complicated mechanics; unnecessary skill-trees; more thought put into the plethora of accessibility options than making a camera fit for this genre; too much focus on story and ineffectual attempts at characterization; and boring enemy design. Also, cinematic sequences are anemic and sluggish imitations of stylish choreography found in that Capcom/Clover/Platinum pedigree.I played through three missions to fight the first boss, and was rewarded with a fat, armored giant wielding a hammer... so that's a perfect zero on the originality scale. This enemy plays like a mid-boss who gets demoted to mook status mid to late game. If we're generous and count Bayonetta's tutorial Prologue as the first real level, then the second level gives you the equivalent of this guy (whom you kill with a cool cinematic finisher), along with a preview fight for the upcoming boss, and level 3 starts with a Jeanne fight. In the first Devil May Cry, you get Devil Trigger in second mission and the third mission has you fighting Phantom, an enormous spider-scorpion hybrid made of magma and stone. We're 20 years out and the grand-daddy of this genre is still regularly schooling newer entries. Imagine scoring lower on a middle-school math test than your knuckle-dragging, missing-link ancestors who scrawled on cave walls with charcoal. Another example of taking without understanding is Soulstice's prologue chapter: an in medias res fight where you have a bunch of upgrades and no idea what you're doing other than waling away. In a metroidvania, this might allow you to sample your eventual power level, or introduce you to mechanics you will need to be thinking about when you come across environmental puzzles later on. If your game has diverse skill-trees, you can experiment and decide what you want to invest in going forward. In an action game, this confuses you because you're about lose 90% of this and gain it back in a linear fashion. It also rushes you through the encounter, so any real experimentation is out. Other than learning which button attacks, this level does fails as a gameplay segment. It hints at your "Devil Trigger", but I only know that because I've seen the anime Claymore, and I had no way of telling if this was having an in-game effect at the time or purely cosmetic.If you've never played Devil May Cry or Bayonetta, go play those. If you have played those, you're unlikely to put up with the fumbling missteps of Soulstice. If you're absolutely all out of stylish beat 'em ups, are you sure? Have you tried Fight 'N Rage? It's reeeeeally good. Have you tried Marlowe Briggs? It's a lot more entertaining. Have you downloaded an emulator and played God Hand? Fine, fine. After all that, you could do worse that getting this game for $10, maybe $15 on the outside, if you're desperate. It firmly sits in that 5 or 6/10, just squeaking into the mediocre but playable category.As for the lore, I just want to say that there's homage, there's wearing your inspirations on your sleeve, and then there's sub-contracting your story out to your favorite Japanese manga-ka without telling him. Soulstice is pretty firmly in the latter category. Too bad the budgetary saving created by this five-finger discount didn't go towards better voice acting.

_childDocuments_.review: I am changing my review for a second time after beating the game and am going to cautiously recommend the game. It is a really cool experience with a lot of love put into it in a genre that doesn't get many releases. Learning to deal with the camera and the enemy combinations that make scenarios fairly chaotic (with said bad camera) takes time and a willingness to put up with frustration... which just won't be worth it for many. I have kept my original review with my original criticism (most of which was alleviated with control scheme changes and learning to play this game as a true hack and slash and not a spectacle fighter. The game is more about threat management than stringing together combos and you just have  to accept that)Original Review: I really wanted to like this game but the camera and lock on system are truly a disaster. Also every 20 seconds there is a cutscene to interrupt the flow of gameplay (said cutscenes are disappointingly 30 fps).For good aspects. the art direction is cool if a little monotonous. The characters look great. When the combat flows (which wasn't too common in my case) you do sometimes get that zen feeling from other genre greats. The game ran well on my PC as well.I think this game is having a hard time deciding if it wants to be God of War or DmC and it lands in no man's land and it really doesn't feel good to play.My fixes: So based on reading other reviews I disabled vsync and that did indeed make the cutscenes better. I personally limited it to 60 fps on a 240 hz monitor so the screen tearing is "mostly" unnoticeable.Secondly. I use the following controls to make combat manageable (and dare I say sometimes fun haha). The goal of this scheme is to acknowledge that the lock on sucks and to instead keep your fingers on the sticks. Unfortunately I was only able to accomplish this with a controller with back buttons so I could jump and dodge with A and B on the back of the controller.A - JumpB - dodgeRB - Base attackRT - special weapon attackLT - Lute actionL3 - Blue fieldR3 - Red fieldThe rest of the buttons don't really matter. Note I have LB as lock on but I don't really use it so LB could be used for dodge or jump but you would still be one short without extra buttons :(

_childDocuments_.review: Giving the game a negative review because Reply Games Studios is ESG-compliant.Criticisms and suggestions:Dialogue - Remove the need for a speaking character to finish his/her animation before switching characters. Ideally make all dialogue continuous, with the option to pause if need be. If not, allow the characters to move during their dialogue, but let said movements continue during the next piece of text. For reference, Darksiders 2 comes to mind. TL;DR: make the the dialogue more seamless and smoother.Camera - Don't be afraid to zoom out more, especially during combat. Low-angles are great for cinematic shots but they can get in the way of traversal sometimes; and - Open up the environments a little more if need be. They look great, and nobody is going to notice if the streets are a bit wider just so the player has a better time fighting enemies.Combat - Needs anim cancels in more attacks. As a hack-n-slash, responsiveness is key. Follow-through on attacks are more important in soulslike games.  - Take control of the camera away from the player and instead spend time framing the combat arenas well. For reference, God of War 3. - And on that note, I'd suggest attaching directional-dodge to the right analogue stick. That way it can be functional all the time and not just during combat. Getting that tiny camera-move input from the right stick frustrates a lot more than not having it at all. - Stinger + dodge with every weapon, not just the sword (as in, Dodge+AltAttack, not just Move>Move>AltAttack). - Force Wraiths (and off-screen enemies) to move into the player's FoV before they attack. Alternatively, frame the combat area better (see above). - Increase the hitboxes for crystals and random corrupted humans walking about. Of all things, these shouldn't be a trial to hit.Music - Electronic was the wrong way to go about combat music. Orchestral or metal would have been better fits. Not saying EDM-adjacent music can't match the mood of the game, but it fell short in this case.Lute's Fields - Make them more diegetic. Make the colour drain or the field vibrate as Lute reaches Overcharge and remove the need to look at the icon on the top left. The vocal queue is fine. - Using the fields in combat is an interesting idea. Unfortunately, it should have been simplified. Ideally, the enemies that can only be fought with fields should have a 'shield' system instead: the wraiths should become corporeal for a few seconds after the blue field is activated (like the Sirens from God of War 3 when exposed to Helios' head) and the 'red crystal' enemies should have a breakable barrier (like the Abomination boss) that allows the player to deal damage for a few seconds. The fun should be in the fighting and the combos, not in juggling the active fields.Other: - Just found a feeble fillament by accident. Make them more obvious once you're in their vicinity. They blend too easily with the monotonous blue-white cityscape.Overall, a very flawed game with some fun combat. Difficulty is inconsistent, and you'll often find that bosses are easier than elite enemies. Becomes boring and monotonous before long.
