_childDocuments_.review: The game at best is mediocre and while I normally wouldn't bother with a review for a mediocre game, there's a couple things in it that make me have to recommend against getting this game. One of the first challenges you find in the game is to do 5 perfect counters within a minute. That wouldn't be a problem, if they actually gave you more than a milisecond to get a perfect counter in. They have such a high requirement to get it in that if you don't press the button the INSTANT the prompt shows up, it doesn't count. I had to stop trying to depend on them showing the prompt and had to go by enemy movements and guessing on when the prompt should show up to hit the button before the prompt even showed up and only by doing that could I actually get a perfect counter. That mechanic alone is enough for me to give this review, but there's one other thing that I find to be a terrible design decision: the reward system. You are given no way to improve your attack power between chapter 1 and 2, yet they some how expect you to do more damage in chapter 2 and due to you not having increased attack power, your score suffers, when your score suffers, you get less rewards, when you get less rewards, you can't get more upgrades, when you can't get more upgrades, you can't do more damage... it's a perpetual cycle leading to you getting and worse and worse score and an awful design decision. Similarly, they also force players to rush through the game because the timer is always counting while you're playing, even when talking to NPCs or exploring. Yet you're also supposed to explore to find all their challenges and such.Also, I don't like fixed cameras, they're never in a good spot.

But, you can't do that when enemies are off-screen. I was tryhard around Act 3 until 4 (my difficulty for first playthrough was Knight), thankfully I spent bit time to explore or destroy environments for upgrade points.The good stuff? Visuals, characters, the story, and when it comes to the hack-n-slash thing (especially Chapter 19: Ascension was satisfying for me). Best to stay focus during combat. Starting a new diffculty after first playthrough won't reset all your status and points, but the enemies are tougher, so New Game+ maybe (?)With all that, I still give a thumbs down because of the gameplay not entirely enjoyable. 1st playthrough was Knight and 3rd was Transcended difficulty. _childDocuments_.review: The balance of the kingdom is compromised and now it is up to you to save it. You play as Briar, someone granted superhuman strength and resilience with the help of Chimera. Explore a dark world brimming with mysteries and master a combat system filled with fast-paced action and grand boss fights that reeks of the inspiration from Devil May Cry and Bayonetta. With a unique arsenal of upgradable weapons that can be switched on the fly or insane combos, it is time to unleash and plow your way through this dark story to find out the truth behind it all.While I do believe there is a good game hidden in here, it is definitely not ready for the Steam Deck. We were warned by the developer that it wasn't optimized for the Steam Deck, but people are still going to wonder how it runs! Soulstice struggles to hit 30 FPS and when it does, it still has stuttering issues. On top of that, it will require a lot of power to stabilize that 30 as much as possible, which we felt drained way too much (20W). I did want to make mention that changing the settings did require exiting and re-opening the game for the new settings to take effect. This generally isn't a bad thing, but there were no prompts that the game needed to be restarted for changes to take effect or anything. Just a small oversight, but one that I want to make note of.I can feel a good game trying to get out, and I think it would shine on the Steam Deck, but it just isn't ready yet. We were warned by the developer, but I wouldn't call this one yet. The game does implement DLSS, which means it COULD have FSR 2.0 implementation later down the road. On top of that, we submitted a couple questions to the dev team about Deck support, we will update the review and our article once we hear back. I believe there is a good game underneath all of this, but since we are rating solely on Steam Deck performance, I would wait on this one.

Plays like old God of War mostly with a hint of DmC(yes the reboot) and some Bayonetta combat segment rankings(but with tight Bayonetta 2 time, why? I wanna have fun comboing). That being said, I did get this for free on Epic but decided to buy this on Steam because there is fun to be had and there is a great show of effort. _childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is direct proof that in gaming, looks aren't everything.  Sure, in order for a game to be considered one of the best, the graphics have to be there, but the gameplay and design need to be there, too.  The fun needs to be there.  The whole package has to be complete for the game to have, well, soul.  Ironically, Soulstice lacks soul.  Plotwise it's a B-grade anime style affair with a girl carrying a sword shaped club (seriously, it doesn't have sharp edges, it's like they got a midjourney like AI to design the main character).   Actually that's what most of the character and enemy design for the game reminds me of. Usually at this point I'll embark on the technical defects in the game... I can't do that so much here, there's 4K graphics, a lot of tweaks and customisability, colourblind modes, pretty much everything you could ask for. This is a sloppy, lazy console port with terrific graphics, but some of the shallowest, most mindless and definitely unenjoyable gameplay imaginable.  Combat is a dry, third person brawl where skill is irrelevant and button mashing is king.   You'll spend your time doing some light platforming and pretend-exploration through the nicely presented, linear, boring levels. The real killer, the worst part of this... no mouselook or true mouse camera control.  What a joke!  Do we look like console peasants?  Fixed camera controls like the ones in this game are a direct limitation because consoles lack the processing power to render complex 3D scenes properly... yet the developers here, instead of just designing and optimising their game to work properly on real PCs and not gaming appliances, decided to inflict those limitations on us. As a result, the game is very, very unpleasant to play as you twiddle around imprecise and changing direction and perspectives that the gamer has no control over.  I have no idea how console peasants survive under those conditions, but the best part is, I just don't have to put up with them. There's a story to the game, but the gameplay itself is so painfully poor that I just couldn't get into it.   They want $40 for this, and that's not okay.  $40 bucks spent wisely would get you several older AAA games with far better gameplay than this, with money to spare. It really is such a shame that so much development money (and time and talent from the fantastic artists and 3D graphics guys) was wasted on a bland, joyless button mashing train wreck that seems to have been designed to entertain 8 year olds.

_childDocuments_.review: A very decent PS2 era DMC type action game. I enjoyed this game despite its faults. The combat feel is actually good. The main character can switch between a heavy Berserk-like claymore and a more Dante-eseque broadsword and it's conveyed well enough in the weighty feel of the attacks. There are of course other weapons each with their own unique uses, but my point is the action feels right and good. So many action games never achieve that. Hitting enemies has appropriate feedback.But also in general the game looks solid. The environments can kind of be a drag, as they are samey. Yet when the game wants to have a visual set-piece it can muster up the energy. The character's berserk transformation sequence is a beautifully rendered manga-inspired infusion that looks to capture the Berserk manga's pencil shading during intense moments, and it does it well. It may be AA but in general, the presentation and production values put some major studios to shame. Cutscenes look good, monster design is interesting, the final bosses especially look great.But it sits at decent to me because:The core gameplay is good, but the camera and lock on truly do remind me of the PS2 era. Static camera angels I can deal with, but a camera and lock on that feel like they have no idea what they are doing during battle is a harder pill. It just kind of leads to some headaches as there is a lot going in combat.It throws a lot of enemies at you, but also your astral sister kind of plays crowd control. So during combat enemy attacks will put up a qte essentially that you press the button that corresponds to your sister where she blocks, counters, and stops the attack. Which adds a neat lawyer as it helps fans of these games that complain about attacks not being visible.  Well, here you stop them and then have a clear amount of time to position and dodge. It puts emphasis on that and it's smart because it never feels like your stopping the attack.But your sister is also shooting astral laser attacks that you upgrade for her to even more, so lots of light show ♥♥♥♥ towards the end of the game.But a less smart choice is color coded enemies, but see it's not even like you switch to red or blue weapons, you turn a blue or red area of effect where enemies have to be in that area to fight them. For example, if the blue enemy is out of the field, your ranged attack won't damage them until they are in your blue aoe stance. So thats annoying.What's really annoying is the possessed enemies. Red enemies are possessed and when you defeat them the blue ghost comes out and you need to take them out before they "repossess" the red enemy and bring them back. This is for most enemies later in the game and sometimes multiple ghosts. But that means you have to switch stance(hoping your gauge is not empty) and quickly kill them. That's made hard by the ♥♥♥♥ lock on though. So there were plenty of annoying moments.The story was ok.....like it does come off as a story the writer came up with when they were 16 and thought fantasy ♥♥♥♥ where the religion is evil is still edgy..But they are very invested in their world and characters which is admirable, but I don't know if ending on a huge big "the adventure is not over" type ending is a bit silly.Good game though. I enjoyed it. I like PS2 era action games and this is of that ilk.

_childDocuments_.review: Although the game sometimes fights itself with a not always reliable lock on system and a lot of knock backs with a not always reliable gap closer, the combat is by and large fun. I won't even pretend to understand exactly what I should have been doing in fights, but switching weapons and finding openings for the special attacks was engaging. Nice to play a game with two characters that actually feel like they're fighting together as well. Having a block/counter button that didn't fling you over to other enemies was a pleasant change of pace from the more usual Arkham style combat. I don't have a lot of experience with Dmc, Bayo or anything else, so maybe the game isn't as mechanically deep as those. Was a blast playing through on the highest initial difficulty though. The story isn't anything terribly new if you're familiar with other dark fantasy works, though the world building and characters did enough to differentiate themselves from similar works. Briar and Lute were endearing and have some nice growth over the course of the game. It was very nice to hear a different VA compared to the usual suspects, just for a change of pace. A lot of really neat views of the city as you travel through it. The scenery is a little limited by the location, though the environments do change as you progress. I'll be hoping to see a sequel somewhere down the line. I am invested in the sisters journey now and it'd be a shame if this is all we ever got to see of them.

_childDocuments_.review: I have quite mixed feelings about Solstice. While the story turns out more interesting than i initally thought, there are some flaws that have wasted my enjoymentCombat works well. Mechanics are introduced one by one, and are intertwined as you progress. It is a beat em all that does its job, rather accessible. But it does lack variety, despite the 6 secondary weapons Briar wields. Their respective upgrades (bought at the shop) unlock new skills, dash, air launcher, slam, and a long combo that is nearly unusable most of the time. And that's it : all weapons actually all the same skills to use. Once i realized that only three weapons actually mattered, despite each having their own strategic advantages against certain enemies, all the others were forgotten on the spot. Also, switching between them during the fight is kinda awkward. On the other hand, our ghost sister, Lute, has a large skill tree, all passive abilities, with which we easily see the increase in powerExploration is another sigh-inducing point : the sole purpose of exploring the city (read "corridors") is to find health upgrades. otherwise, everything looks the same from the first chapter to -nearly- the last.But the worst abomination of this game is the camera. Derived from the old Devil May Cry, this atrocity will never be at the right place. Even set at the max speed, finding enemies is a challenge, as enemies will turn invisible if the camera is too close, or unreadable if too far, which both happens too regularly. Lock doesn't help as it tries desperately to juggle between moving targets, and fighting without the lock will make many fights terribly hard, as some wil lrequire to target a specific enemy.The camera is really the one thing that drove my patience to zero, despite the OK game Soulstice is

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this game it seems to be strongly inspired on Berseker and Claymore manga, I heavily recommend to check it out if you like both of these sources, If you like Claymore over it, even more. The gameplay is based around old school Hack and slash games of the ps2 era, with of course, updated graphics, amaizing cutscenes and polished artistic departure, involving around the idea of grimdark anime.Pros:-Visuals and cutscenes.-Good variety of weapons and skill three.-Narrative is strongly based on Claymore.-Good finishers and different ways to break trought the enemy lines.-Great main boss fights.-Multiple ways to aproach different enemies, synergies with weapons and switching is required during combat.ConsThings to improve:-Some semi-boss fights feel a bit unfair, excesive lower enemies attacking at the same time as the semi-boss (Abomination felt really bad, since his attack range is huge and the timing is hard to read when you use the freeze counter on him)-The parry system works most of the time, but the game doesn't properly explain what is a perfect counter (its blocking with "B" before the enemy starts an attack animation, NOT later)-The afinity system between the sisters, sometimes can be annoying due the multiple enemies at the same time attacking you and aoe effects from bigguer enemies. Also it doesn't work to much if there is only one enemy with small or non consecutive counter openings (takes more time and its harder to fill the bar, if you have to move around the bigguer attacks and they don't let you stick near them to make chained combos)-The weapons chained combo it's most of the same for every weapon, but there is complexity in to know when to switch between weapons or make more complex air combos. (But also mention that the air combos give less afinity within briar and lute, so most of the time you gonna stick to the ground to apply these combos, with a few exceptions like the bigger panthoms that you find during the second half of the game).-One of the main flaws for me during the gameplay, It was that lute skill tree can be a long run problem if its not revised and take the correct upgrades. For example, any hability that increases entropy can be a potential bottleneck for you. If you don't go for a overload build and you take to many of these skills, you can be stuck on boss fights due that the entropy will be always at 70-80%, so you can't mantain lute energy field for more than 4-5 seconds, leaving you in the middle of the fight doing nothing at all until lute recovers and let you attack again (This is kind of horrible in a hack and slash dynamic, were you have to be constantly attacking the enemies). So you have to check other options for lute (prioritize the ones that reduce entropy), and also at the end game it's heavily recommended to complete the distance counter for hight level enemies, this lets you counter even boss heavy attacks or projectiles.-Transformations, (this section has slight spoilers and my main problem with the game)I enjoyed playing this game overall, and the themes presented during the history were great to follow up. Sometimes Briar was too edgy and lute was overreacting, but it's ok for me. The gameplay is enjoyable but a bit frustrating at times (the telemetry of the enemy attack after being frozen by counter is hard to read), the main boss fights are huge and I see the dedication and love to make this game possible. I hope for the best if a second chapter can be reached at some point.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Chimera May CryIn a dark, Gothic fantasy universe, humanity struggles against the creatures of Chaos, commonly referred to as “Wraiths”. These blue energy beings cross over across the Veil, and their mere touch is enough to turn hapless humans into mindless, bloodthirsty Corrupted. Sometimes a Corrupted and a Wraith join together and become a red coloured Possessed. In order to fight these spawns of Chaos the adepts of the Triarchy- the 3 gods that separated Creation from Chaos and created humanity-have commissioned the Order of the Ashen Blade to create Chimeras- a symbiotic union of a human Knight and a ghostly Shade. The Knights can heal deadly wounds with ease, double-jump and dash, and hit evil things with sharp and pointy bits of metal. The Shades can manipulate Chaos to create colour-coded Fields that make both Wraiths and Possessed vulnerable to the Knights' weapons. You start the game playing as a novice Chimera made up of knight Briar and the shade of her sister Lute. A massive Rent into Chaos opened up over the holy city of the Lightbringer (one of the 3 gods of humanity). Along with several other Chimeras, Briar and Lute must investigate the source of the Rent and find a way to close it, killing many different enemy types in the process. The game is a typical character-action game, complete with scores for each encounter and varying fixed camera perspectives. Basically think Devil May Cry 3, but more anime. Briar starts with 2 weapons- a sword and a warhammer, and can unlock 5 additional weapon types as the game goes on- a gauntlet, a bow, a whipsword , dual daggers and powered gun/gauntlet hybrids. Each weapon has a moveset that needs to be bought, but they have identical button inputs. Different weapons are more effective against different enemies (gauntlets smash armor, whip and daggers do better airborne damage to bring down fliers, etc). And in addition, Wraiths and Possessed can only be harmed when the appropriate Field is active- and Lute can only keep a field going for so long (until you get upgrades for it). Altogether, this creates a neat twist on the traditional character action combat system.  The game's version of Devil Trigger gives Lute a  sped-up and increased damage form- but if you trigger this when you're close to death, you Frenzy- your damage increases, but unless you successfully perform QTEs, Briar goes Transcended and then it's Game Over. Combine this with some neat boss encounters, bonus challenge rooms, a ranking system and a VERY anime and unnecessary convoluted story, filled of twists and betrayals (that show up seemingly out of nowhere) and you end up with a surprisingly compelling experience. I did not experience any bugs or crashes. The game has platforming and puzzles (typically you need to destroy colour-coded crystals to clear obstructions, or find levers to open paths, nothing complex), and the game takes place largely in a very similar environment- the various districts of the destroyed city are largely samey-looking, so there's little real environmental variety. Some platforming depends on Lute's fields making them visible, which is a timed thing, so those can get annoying. Overall, though, the run on Normal difficulty took me about 25 hours, trying to explore every corner of the level- and I still didn't find about half-dozen of the Challenge Rooms, so there's plenty of content. Anyone who is looking for a good Devil May Cry clone and likes dark Gothic settings owes it to themselves to check this game out

_childDocuments_.review: "Another Transcended walks the land" is the message that pops up when you fail to revert Briar from berserk state.Solstice excels in character design and world building, it would have been great to explore world prior to **events** of game, but alas, ravaged version it is then, there are lot of areas that felt that they had potential like audio/boss tracks and a ton of controversial game mechanics, first of all, the weapon combos for default great sword are lacking (only 2 combos for what it briar's lore weapon). the weapons each have its own strength and weakness and the game  you hard if you use wrong weapon in wrong place. and the fields are overused to extent of me raging cause LUTE CANT HOLD THEM FOR 5 SECS WITHOUT UTTERING "I CANT HOLD THEM FOR LONG", maybe its just me not finding upgrades but, the color coded enemies makes the game feel more like a puzzle, this in turn makes player focus on solving the puzzle rather than focusing on "style". A huge amount of mechanics crammed into a character with lot of "ifs" attached to those mechanics. The boss battles, most of them are meh, but the ones that stood out are the archer one(would have been better if not for handholding mechanics), nemisis (visuals were gorgeous, the fight itself is meh tho), and final boss (harbringer?, mainly cause, the backdrop was amazing and fight was also pretty good relatively, i see devs took a huge inspiration from DMC 4's savior fight)I liked the whole "claymore/berserk" vibe and the cutscene that plays out when you activate berserk is just **chef's kiss**.all in allPlot -- 6/10Gameplay -- 5/10 (are fun, but get tedious fast)Immersion  -- 6/10 (lets see how immersive it gets when you get triple combo'd by enemies from across the arena)OST -- 6/10 stands out at times, could have been betterBugs  -- 8/10 -- it crashed on me few times at a specific spot, had to search for fix online.Grind -- 9/10 -- game is quite generous with its currency Character designs(special) -- 8/10 -- especially transcended designs.Final verdict: 6.8/10 (worth playing if you are bored or need a case study for your game design class)

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is a DMC/Bayonetta-like action game (Hack and slash? Character action?), and I recommend it. Despite its flaws, the core gameplay is great. Weapons/enemies synergies work well: you need to always choose the right tool for the job when you're approached by different types of monsters. This, together with the blue/red aura weaknesses/hazards, makes the combat always fun and engaging. The problem is on the camera, in certain battles, it's a pain in the ass. The shonen-like story is enjoyable, and I liked the main characters and their bond. Level design is sometimes weak, mainly because of invisible walls. But the levels are still better than the ones from Devil May Cry 5, and nobody complained there. Some of those were linear and mindless like an arcade shooter. Difficulty scaling is good.

_childDocuments_.review: This game must be a fever dream or some collective delusion, even more for Berserk fans.So I bought this game the moment I found it out, come on... A game with a female Guts with schierke being soul-bound (Lute, I find her incredibly likable, at least for me) with a Devil may cry 3 gameplay/menus and a lot of skills customizations, and a good dark story, what more I could ask for? And this game is completely shadowed, I found it just because of a random video on youtube, and this game was released some months ago and no one, I mean no one talked about it, like 'What?!' (Some marketing problems I guess) I know the game has flaws, like the camera is not so good, the same problems with old DMCs (The newest patch seems to have helped the camera a little bit), and some performance issues (I hope they can fix that) But I have seen some reviews on Steam that would just hate the game for no real reason, like a guy said that the enemies would not feel the hits, like they stood there tanking everything, I must be playing other Soulstice than this guy because the fights felt really good, like the enemies seemed to feel I lot of pain while I dismembered them with a huge sword or crushed with a hammer. Also, someone said the combat was boring and slow, REALLY? I can do a lot of stylish combos (I don't even have all those skills/weapons available yet) while dashing, fighting, jumping, and parrying (Lute) all at the same time, how is this slow? smh. All about this game feels surreal, If you like Berserk/Claymore, you will love this guaranteed, Soulstice and the developers deserves way better, I have the feeling this game will age like fine wine, and I hope this community grows.

_childDocuments_.review: Played only a few chapters, but I can feel the charm of the game. As many other reviews mentioned similarity to anime/manga Claymore then the collection of orb (red/blue) for skill/item purchases akin to DMC. But the camera are fixed at 2.5D for platforming, while only during other times outside combat the camera follows your character when you move.  Full camera controls for combat in non tight space fights and that's the weakest part of the game. Same issues with the latest Valkyrie game, due to the free camera control fights with mixed range enemies from close, mid, long range and flying enemies can be a chore. Both thumbs are used on movement and camera/enemy lock while your primary attacks are X & Y with B to deflect. Without back paddle buttons controllers, early gamers not used to it would probably  be"All Thumbs". The background settings is nice too, just a bit confusing within buildings where every other background platform seemingly to be climbable but not. Still, I can't fault that since DMC seems doing that well enough. Now the good part is it's really enjoyable to play and the voice actors are really good. Graphics are quite good though I feel the art would be better off with anime like  cel shades. Overall if one is prepared to get used to the "All Thumbs" controls, it will be way better then most games in the same genre. Looking forward to what this dev can come up with next with more simplified control mechanics. 7.5 / 10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great for fans of the Berserk and Claymore mangas, It's gameplay is a fun hack and slash similar to Devil May Cry with a world, characters and story inspired by the two previously mentioned mangas. The game has many interesting mechanics that are present in both puzzles and combat. The combat itself revolves mostly around chaining combos without getting to build up a meter that allows you to unleash powerful attacks, and when filled allows you to enter a berserker like state where you are able to attack rapidly with much more powerful blows, though this state is locked at the beginning and will be available by progressing through the game. In combat your main defense is your shade Lute, in response to enemy attacks you can time a button press to counter, doing so also builds up Lutes meter which if filled will stun her making her unable to perform actions. The game contains many different types of enemies all of which fall under one of three types, Corrupted, Spirit and Possessed. Corrupted are standard enemies which will take damage without a barrier activated, spirits can only be harmed while you have your evocation field activated. Possessed are similar where you will need to have your banishment field up to harm them, both these fields build up Lute's meter over time. Overall I do recommend this game even to those who are not fans of Berserk and Claymore, as long as you enjoy hack and slash games that is, personally I would give this game a 8/10 though I might be a bit biased as I am a huge fan of Berserk and Claymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Early impresses are good. The main character reminds me of the anime Claymore, especially in her OP corrupted mode that the game has hinted at in the opening cut scene. You can't have both. Combat feels fun, weighty. Seems like there's much to unlock and expand your opportunities for combos, could even replay challenges to get better scores DMC style and probably grind for currency this way. This is inspired by and scratches the same itch as DMC, Bayonetta, old God of War games. Happy that I bought this (on the current sale of 25%~ off). No refunding for me, I like it.Update: picked this back up 1.0.4 update has really improved the combat camera and so this game is much more enjoyable to play. The update also mentions performance improvements. This also is running much better on my Steam Deck. Might have something to do with updating my Cryoultilities to 2.0 and applying all it's tweaks but either way this can be played on the Deck at 40hz with a low/high mix and quality FSR. Pulls 16~ watts at TDP 9 and GPU pinned to 1100. Full credit for gameplay improvements to the 1.0.4 update, good job devs!

_childDocuments_.review: It gives me strong DMC 1 vibes. Yes DMC 3, 4 and 5 were more stylish then the first one but I liked the music and the atmosphere in 1.Soulstice triggers this nostalgia for me. Some may not like the static cameras, man even I have some problems with it here and there. But I personally won't miss it. _childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is a capable atmospheric dark fantasy hack'n'slasher.  The dark, grim, and gory environment with well-executed if chaotic combat fill a void for me that's been left empty since Reaper of Souls, maybe even since the gory spectacle that was Travincal back in the day.  The static camera takes some getting used to but ultimately is easy to work with and does a fantastic job of showcasing the world's art.  Combat is fast and unforgiving but nuanced; i-framing through attacks and popping counters while tossing grotesque monsters around is very satisfying.  Bosses are challenging, relentless, and cinematic encounters.  The story is mainly delivered passively during gameplay and is engaging with an acceptable voice over.  I have very few complaints about this game and those few issues are minor compared to how many things the game gets right.  I wholeheartedly recommend it (if you're a fan of grotesque monsters, gory combat and piles of corpses littering the world that is).

_childDocuments_.review: The main, and really only issue I'm having so far is, it crashes somewhat frequently, which is a little frustrating because it can cause you to lose some progress.  Besides that though, it's a pretty good game and the graphics are pretty decent without running too hard on my PC.  The setup is a little different from most of the RPG's I've played.  Instead of just continuing through the game constantly, it has chapters that you get scored on individually as you progress through the story, and you can play and replay them if you want to in order to earn a better score.  I haven't quite figured out what the score is going towards yet, but I honestly don't really care.  I'd recommend playing this with a controller, rather than a key board (but to each their own).  The buttons are also easily map-able for the controller, which is convenient.  I'll update this and review the actual story, either after I finish, or decide it's no longer worth finishing.  With the amount of story lines along with every chapter in each story, it appears to be a pretty long game, so it might be a while.

_childDocuments_.review: A game which you can feel the developers poured their love into. For fans of Devil May Cry, Berserk and Claymore. This is obviously an AA title, so you won't find the kind of polish you might get with Devil May Cry or other similar games. But that doesn't matter, because it does exactly what it needs to do and maybe even more. The combat is fast and satisfying. The story is surprisingly deeper than some would expect. Likeable characters. The only flaws I could think of are: -the overall campaign could be a tad shorter. There's a lot of padding. -combat, even if satisfying, can feel a bit clunky, sometimes. Need to get used to the timing of attacks in order to properly cancel into other action. -the world, even if beautiful, gets a bit repetitive after a while. Other than that, it's definitely worth it for anyone who enjoys the very unused genre of character action games. Also, finally amazing to see such a good Italian game on the market. I hope they'll get enough recognition to work on more projects.

_childDocuments_.review: In terms of the combat and general gameplay in Soulstice, it will probably feel quite familiar if you have played the Devil May Cry or Bayonetta games. As in those, progress is split up into distinct chapters, where you explore through a mostly linear path, encountering combat and light platforming challenges and uncovering secrets. You are graded on your damage output, combo variety and efficiency at the end of each combat encounter and chapter, with high grades resulting in bonus rewards. In addition, various sub-weapons can be unlocked and upgraded, each of which is suitable for a different class of enemy.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is a game that looks and plays like games in the early 2000's brought to the modern era with action packed combat and soundtrack to keep you going in this unforgiving grim but well designed unique environment. God of War and Devil May Cry comes to mind. Also this game is pretty long and you can easily get over 10 hours. I remember feeling like i made a ton of progress only to find out i was on my way to reach halfway into a game. Take breaks if you need it.Story is pretty interesting and it sets itself up well enough that you will want to know more. Though of course there are stuff that are left unanswered. You do meet a fellow called the Observer and through him you can get a bit more on what's going on. Wish this was used a bit more as i liked the conversations while you take a break from combat. 8/10If you played older titles like God of War (not the 2018) or Devil May Cry series then you know what to expect. The game has it's own twist with skill tree. It's a linear experience and i'm ok with that. It's got a beginning, middle and end. It's a chill game if you just what to play something that isn't live serviced or you play infinitely. I initially thought it would be another souls game but no.If you played games like the older God of War or Devil May Cry series then you will know what to expect going into this game. Not sure what else to add... Oh yeah the camera and the targeting may or may not be annoying during combat fyi. Some boss fights later on started to be better over others and changes things up a bit. 9/10I played this game at 1440p on an Rtx 2070 Super and it ran fine at 60 to 140+ fps with no issues with Dlss on the quality setting. Was averaging i think around 100-120 fps at least. The only time it felt a bit janky was a the very beginning but afterwords it was fine. It's possible you might experience fps lost in some level where the game just throws so much at you with tons of particle effects. 8/10Soundtrack is really good. It really get intense in many boss battles and some important ones too. 9/10Visually this game looks great but i'm not sure why it didn't have Rtx since you do a lot of exploring. Would have made it look even better for sure. The cutscenes are also well done. Character models look ok except for 1 but it's nothing lol. 7/10For the price 45 CAD Monopoly money i think it's a fair deal. The game isn't quite AAA but it's good enough if this type of game interest you. Again it's a linear experience but you get a lot of out it. If you like God of War or DMC or anything that's similar then you probably will like this one as well. I left a lot out because you should experience it yourself. _childDocuments_.review: Solid game with a great combat and combat system. If you are looking for a great hack and slash game, Soulstice will keep you entertained for ~20 hours straight. The combat is smooth and really fun, allowing to try different combos with a wide variety of weapons. The story keeps you engaged, as you uncover secrets and plot twist along the way. However, the game has some flaws. The camera system is a bit outdated and might be annoying in certain situation. Also, the color-coded system is something that I personally find really tedious. Luckily, the devs added a setting that triggers the fields automatically. Unluckily, it also lowers the scores at the end of the level. The level design is linear and doesn't give too much space to exploration (although this isn't necessarily a bad thing).Overall a great experience. I suggest giving it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10While I do like the game and finished it , there are some serious problems that could hinder you in your enjoyment of the game.1.) Combat: The combat does make fun but only when you master it. Isnt that the case in almost all action games ? Yes but not to this extent like in this game.There's this mechanic where you can execute certain synergy attacks if you dont get hit and uphold a combo for a certain time. With it the combat feels fluid and you can get cool executions but without it you have limited options , especially at the beginning of the game. And that leads to the second problem , there are far too few combo variations in my opinion.You have 6 weapons but with each you get the same combo each time and need alot of resourcers to buy them. Even worse is that you have to upgrade each weapon up to 3 times for just a damage bonus that doesnt give you any extra combos ,purchasing these over the combos just doesnt feel rewarding at all.2. Story and Cutscenes) I like the concept of the main characters very much , especially how it affects the gameplay aswell. Thats the best thing about this game. The effect the story has on the gameplay. I just love it. The presentation of the story is rather bland though. The animations inside the cutscenes feel mechanical and the voices dont let you feel the gravity of the situation. It sounds like they recorded all the voices at the same day with the same emotion. Throughout the game it never really changes sadly.But I really like the settings , the overall story and the bond between the sisters. I hope that they learn from the game this time and hopefully make a sequel where they improve on it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game far exceeded my expectations and I highly recommend you give it a try before simply listening to reviewers.Combat: DMC style, character action combat with scores for each encounter and level. Plenty of weapons and combos to learn and slowly unlock throughout the course of the game. The twist here is you control two characters, one directly and the other indirectly.Story: This is the star of the show. Both main character performances are outstanding and the overall plot has far more intrigue than this genre of game typically carry.Camera: A controversial subject and is where most of the review complaints are about. _childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty ok 3rd person action game in the vein of DMC, not a whole lot of games like that on Steam, and although it has some issues i think its good enough to warrant a buy.Combat:This is the main issue of the game, see you get quite a few different weapons throughout your play through, and these weapons are your basic tools for the enemies you face: whip deals more damage to basic enemies, hammer is good against shields and fist is good against armor etc etc. The problem is you will face enemies that you are missing the weapons for early on, dont fret too much because the difficulty doesnt ramp up until about half way into the game, but on the higher difficulties you might struggle on your first time.Here is my suggestion though, if you start on the lowest difficulty things will go much smoother. I had never played any game like this before and it helped me immensely. This also helps with the other problem it has, that being the blue and red colored enemies. It can get pretty hectic and only being able to hurt some of the enemies that are surrounding you is a big pain, but on the lower difficulty they will have less health and deal less damage so that helps (also you can increase the difficulty mid play through when you have all the tools and some upgrades).GraphicsPretty good. Unreal engine is put to good use in the art style they chose and the main characters in particular are well done. There are a lot of samey hallways and rooms but the vistas of the city are great. I did enjoy the way they went with the enemy design, a lot of crystaline monsters that look very cool mixed in with a lot of fleshy monstrosities, very cool designs. There are some lip sync issues though on one character when he has his close ups but that was the only issue i noticed. Overall nothing to complain about with some standout boss fights but a lot of mediocre areas. MusicLove the orchestrel stuff and the boss music is sometimes rock mixed in with some synth and electronic. Its somewhat different for a fantasy type game but i really liked it and it definitely gives the game its own style. LengthA bit too long overall in my opinion, there are quite a few sections that i think stay past their welcome, the sewers comes to mind, but the end of the game certainly feels like it accelerates quite a bit which is nice, but would have been nicer had the pacing been a bit faster for the beginning and middle chapters. Theres also a few puzzles that were a bit annoying but only a handful of them that i actually remember so not too bad. Final ThoughtsI think they designed this game to be played through multiple times on different difficulties. Unfortunately this is not obvious to a new player but putting down the difficulty really helped me get through it and overall i enjoyed the story and characters. Combat is fun too once you get all the weapons and some upgrades. It can be hectic but also a good time. To me this was 40 dollars well spent, in this age of studios buying (and closing down) smaller studios i enjoy when a AA game actually turned out pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: DMC in a fantasy setting with a touch of dark souls for flavour, but definitely a little harder. 	Briar and Lute’s journey through a city damned by chaos is a good one. The game play is fast and furious, and the story is very interesting. Graphics are good, sound can be a little odd at times though, including a few voiced lines ending prematurely or not playing. 	The game play is definitely more involved than DMC. Blocking is a required skill alongside dodging, as will cycling through weapons. The move sets are limited and very similar for each weapon, requiring liberal use of multiple weapons to keep your score up. Each weapon is also tailored for fighting specific types of foe. The barrier system also adds another layer to combat that can required fast switching to be able to hit targets. It makes for a fast-paced combat that while it has a slightly higher learning curve than the DMC titles, is still a riot to use.	The Stage has been set for a sequel, and I am definitely looking forward to it. Overall, if one likes the hack and slash style of DMC, this one is definitely worth getting.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Soulstice is a great game with a few flaws, which did not prevent me from having overall, an enjoyable experience. Soulstice is a spectacle fighter in the veins of DMC/Bayonetta. While its combat doesn't quite reach the complexity of aforementioned titles, it does get quite busy when stuff opens up. There's quite a few weapons that get unlocked for you, which seem to be a bit of a focus in combat. All weapons have strengths and weaknesses to certain types of enemies, so you gotta switch them around often. Also, while weapons have similar inputs for combos, you can switch them on the fly in each step of the combo and continue with the move that should be at that combo step of the weapon you switched to. Combined with launchers, air finishers and a few unique moves on some weapons, this does offer some matter of complexity if you really wanna get into it. As the game’s unique twist, you play alongside a "helper" which provides passive and active help. With timed button presses you can slow down or repel enemy attacks. You do need to get used to this, since slowing down a telegraphed attack doesn't negate it completely, but makes it attack later, often more unexpectedly than if you tried to dodge it normally. It does offer a small bit of freshness to combat, as you can predict where the attack is gonna land and reposition yourself to continue attacking. Passively, the helper will attack enemies on its own and occasionally counter enemy attacks that you missed, this one sometimes does more bad than good though and I wish it could be turned off. There would be instances where I would want to just dodge a specific enemy attack, but it would get randomly slowed down, throwing me off a bit. You also have two types of fields that you can temporarily activate and make specific enemies vulnerable to your attacks. Combined with a skill tree that has various passive perks and abilities that can slightly modify most of these mechanics, you do get a pretty decent combat system that gives enough stuff to keep track of for you to stay engaged.There are moments where camera puts a damper on things, it's actually somewhat weird, since in the beginning of the game, in most of the combat encounters you are given free control of it, while in the latter parts of the game, arenas where you fight have a locked or semi-locked view, which where it really can get annoying. Especially considering that if you use lock-on in those areas, sometimes it does move the camera at more angles (occasionally at pretty weird ones though) than without it, which asks, why not just give you free control of it in the first place. Also, if you have teleporting enemies in your game, when they teleport, it would be better to automatically disengage lock-on rather than suddenly flip your whole view around. I recommend not shying away from using supportive items if you happen to get yourself in a sticky situation due to the camera, it's not a solution per se, but it can help alleviate some frustrations.Graphics / design wise I'd say is where the game shines the most. The game really just looks gorgeous. Design-wise, obviously, a lot of inspiration was drawn from Berserk and Claymore, which I'm quite a fan of. So I really enjoyed it in the form of it being a way to get more content in the style of those works. The environments are pretty detailed and portray a dark, morbid atmosphere really well. Unfortunately, there is not much variety in locations, as you are mostly confined to a specific area. It does make sense story wise and on the upside it does make for an immersive experience of you traveling through a huge city one step at a time. For example, there's a great bridge connected to a city which is considered an impressive marvel in the lore and it takes a while for you to travel through it, you have to go through a prison and a guard post located in its undersides, which gives you a sense of how big that thing actually is. While some more variety could definitely be implemented, I'd say developers did a good job with constraints they probably were working with. Overall, the game is done very cleanly and neatly, performance seems fair and I haven't encountered any bugs in my playthrough.Story starts slow, but I'd say, if you give it a chance, you will find that it escalates pretty well and in the latter parts of it, it kept me pretty engaged. Even though there's only a few characters in the game, they use them well and I really liked getting to know more about them throughout the game. There doesn’t seem to be too many music tracks, but they are good, maybe there’s nothing that particularly stands out, but they serve their purpose well. More ambient tracks fit well with the atmosphere and the main combat track has a nice beat to it. In the end, despite its strong stylistic inspirations, the game began to feel like its own thing and I really got sucked into its world. If there’s a chance a sequel might happen I will be all up for it.

_childDocuments_.review: For one, I was really excited and looking forward to this game ever since I saw the previews. I am a lover of action games, specifically action RPGs, but I also enjoy character action to an extent as long as I like the characters and design, and certainly do with Soulstice. I have also played plenty of DMC, Bayonetta, etc., nothing too surprising.The atmosphere, art, and presentation really unite and hold the entire package together by themselves. Character and enemy designs are all fantastic, and the settings are moody and beautiful. Even all of the bold close ups of the characters in cutscenes failed to betray much of any blemishes and that honestly impressed me, full stop. Indie, AA, AAA, whatever, doesn't matter, I was simply impressed. Overall, a visually stunning piece of art, and major props to the devs for sticking to their guns and going all in on some of their character designs and moments. You know what I'm talking about, and it is a rarity. Thank you.Unfortunately, and with a heavy heart, things fall apart for me in the , and I am writing this days after finishing and giving myself time to mull it over rather than go in with raw emotions. I'll start off by mentioning that I played through on Initiate difficulty, which is the middle of the 3 initially available and the recommended tier for experienced players of the genre looking for some challenge; That's usually how I approach any new game, as I just want to experience the baseline recommended gameplay and enjoy the overall experience first before I go nuts with achievements and mastering things, even if it's too easy. Spoiler alert, it was definitely not.To preface the following, I have not read very much in terms of other reviews and thoughts yet, so these critiques are all from my personal experience in a vacuum after completing the story on Initiate difficulty.Maybe this is just a really unpopular opinion and that's fine, but I strongly feel that , and I mean this in the most respectful and hopeful way possible for the devs if they are reading this; There's already a lot going on by the time you get to the middle of the story, and that's not even when you've unlocked all the weapons or seen all the environmental mechanics and enemies.I actually LOVE action games with lots of depth and crazyness. I mean, I was addicted to fist weapons in Nioh 2, and the skill ceiling doesn't get much more blissfully insane than that in an ARPG; That's a title with a fair number of mechanics too. I have been playing these sort of games for a very long time, but I'm not exactly fond of fumbling with all of the pretty much mandatory combat systems stacked on top of each other in this game. More to the point, I didn't particularly find the "challenge" worthy of the difficulty or the enjoyment I got.The stark difference between Soulstice and something like Nioh is that you don't  to interact with many of the numerous systems in Nioh as they are extra and optional. I'm not knocking Soulstice for having necessary systems by any stretch, I'm just saying that there are sometimes too many other things going on around them that muddy what I feel could be a more crisp experience while still remaining challenging.To be clear, I love all the weapons, they are all very fun and very cool looking. I love the entropy system concept with the dual fields that you manage, and it's obviously integral to the everything. I love the unity system and synergy attacks, they look straight up DOPE. The parry/counter system is cool, sometimes a bit cumbersome and other times really flashy and satisfying. The controls feel good and responsive (except the double-tap analog stick dash attack that can be very difficult to execute at times, when there is a perfectly good double-button-press combination on a few weapons). And here's the thing, I loved the boss fights. I really did. They were big and fun, and the combat felt great in those situations.Literally every other combat situation, which is the vast majority of the game, is where my issue lies, because ALL of these systems are coming together to bombard you with the responsibilities of frequently swapping between 6 different secondary weapons with their own strengths and weaknesses (3 of them require double-tapping the d-pad), maintaining two resource-sensitive entropic fields in order to even interact with certain enemies, enemies that require swapping from one field to the other just to chase around and finish them off, environmental hazards that can really mess you up depending on which field you have up (or none), constantly worrying about parrying/countering/slowing tons of attacks coming at you from all directions, dodging uninterruptible and slowed attacks, trying to build Unity for your best attacks but having it get severely depleted when taking any damage, and dealing with a camera that requires locking on to see health bars but greatly limits your field of view and requires constant toggling or awkward swapping between tons of available targets.I think the thing that really throws the biggest wrench into this pile of systems is the variety of enemies that can be thrown at you at once. Some of those combinations are really nasty and require all of these responsibilities to be managed to the max and in quick succession or you'll be in trouble. This is on "normal" difficulty as well. Even if "easy" is much less punishing, there is still a lot to manage and that is a fundamental issue in my eyes. I can  of see an argument towards not needing to use every single weapon, which sometimes is a fair case to make, but some of them are just WAY better at dealing with specific situations.Again, it's not about being too simple or taking away the fun and reward of combat depth, it's about knowing where to draw the line. I don't have any specific suggestions at the moment for the current build, but I hope this will at least be taken into consideration.I want to end on a positive note and say that I really, really like this game, and I will definitely be looking out for post-launch content like DLC, or even a sequel would be amazing. Admittedly, even if the combat hasn't changed much down the line, I will still probably be checking out any future releases, which is basically saying Soulstice has earned a fan in me just based on how well presented it is. , I really can't stress enough that I feel there is some work to be done about the things I mentioned, and I would be very ecstatic to see that happen in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's a quick(er) summary of my thoughts on the game. I would highly recommend reading my full thoughts on it in the steam forums (), since steam reviews have a 8000 characters limit and I had much more to say than that.Soulstice is a good game that takes inspiration from classics like Devil May Cry, Bayonetta and God of War. Despite that, it manages to carve a unique identity with a surprisingly good story and characters, an interesting lore and world, and a very competent fighting system that unfortunately gets marred by some poor design decisions. Regardless, for a first try from a relatively new team on the genre the result is nothing short of spectacular, and I see huge potential in them if they iterate on the ideas. I'll lay down my remarks and although the negative outnumber the positive, rest assured that in reality the game is good, it's just that I point the small flaws deliberately while I paint the positive aspects with a broader brush. Also I'll double down on checking .For starters, it has solid fundamentals although the color swapping mechanic just turns a lot of combats into a chore. Used sparingly as it was in the first few hours was fine, but it was taken to its limits as the game went on. This kind of "variety in gameplay" was tried numerous times in other games, including the infamous DmC reboot, to overall negative feedback, so I don't understand why it was used here. It generally just adds a layer of frustration and instead of making the game more varied it makes it more limited. What should be strategic thinking turns into annoyance. In other games of the genre, you initially have to understand how the enemies work to formulate a strategy, and once you have it it's time to put it in practice with your skills in pressing the right buttons at the right time. But a color swap mechanic does not require skill, it's just a layer that ADDS on top of what you're thinking instead of a broader mechanic that EXPANDS what you can do. Once you see a red enemy, you press the red color, and once you see a blue one, you press the blue. There's no actual strategy, just a "monkey says" prompt. But there are specifics on what makes it a bad design decision (detailed on the forum post).- Normal/red attack on blue enemies (ghost type) just make your weapon go through them, but a normal/blue attack on red enemies (possessed type) makes your weapon bounce, making you vulnerable. So your only realistic option is to kill the red enemies before the blue ones - but then some red enemies liberate blue enemies that HAVE to be dealt in a timer.- Since your red/blue bubble is limited, Bow is basically useless against colored enemies.- Bombs that activate according to color used are hard to see in the arena when the camera is spinning around. It feels like the thinking was that a good challenge is removing the chance for the player to use all the cool stuff they gathered along the way. Your gear and abilities are genuinely fun and thought out, so it pains me that a lot of combat situations actively discourage you to use them, or have a huge detrimental approach to your abilities. Examples (detailed on the forum post):- Flying enemies that CONSTANTLY fly away from you.- Teleporting enemies that make your camera get like Dante's party: CRAZY!- Enemy shields that basically can only be dealt with the right color and the hammer.- Most enemy attacks DO NOT have distinct sound cues for attacks, making it impossible to know what they're doing offscreen.- Your weapons have clearly defined strengths and weaknesses against enemy types, again limiting what you can do.- Bosses are weak in design/strategy up until the last three.- Exploding enemies: just... no.Some other miscellaneous problems:- The game definitely overstays its welcome. The stages are long and with "break the crystal" puzzles that are inoffensive and time wasters.- The backgrounds hardly evolve over time.- The game arccloses, but it is an incomplete story planned for sequels (lots of loose ends).- Sound effects are generally weak or lacking.- Except for bosses, enemies lack variety in design.- Stage 17: An enemy that stays out of the battlefield can shoot projectiles at you, making you randomly have to dodge. The worst battle was against two scorpions and a huge-arm dude, since all of them have silent projectiles (the arm dude being a giant undodgeable - but jumpable - wave). It was so frustrating that I almost stopped playing the game altogether.- Stage 21: There's a timer and if you die/time out, it's off to do the entire stage again. Which is weird since the stage clearly has a midpoint where the timer resets, so why isn't it a checkpoint? The final platform session was the only time the fixed camera was REALLY bad, throwing your perception off just enough to miss the platforms.So after all this, what to love? Well a lot actually, or else I wouldn't be writing this essay.+ First, as much as I complained about the combat, it IS good. It is so good in fact, that that's exactly WHY I wanted to NOT have all those hindrances and actually just enjoy it, think about combos, vary my weapons, study enemy patterns, etc. When there's not a lot of BS going on it's incredibly fun! And to be honest, more often than not you'll find good combat scenarios with interesting enemy formations.+ Upgrades feel meaningful, varied and unique, especially Lute's.+ Although long, stages are actually fun to explore, and more often than not offer a lot of rewards if you venture outside the main path!+ You really feel like you're playing with both sisters.This accomplishment is a feat in itself, and although I think it isn't perfect, I think this can become much better realized in a next game.+ I loved the supercombo/powered state mechanic. It does incentivise you to play well and not get hit, and to think about the trade off between having access to your super move you can use only on certain occasions, or deal a lot of damage at once but lose the super combo. It's skill based risk/reward, but this sometimes gets shot down by the unfortunate battle blemishes described above.+ The fixed camera is done astoundly well, and IMO combat should also be in fixed camera like old school GOW. But unfortunately the camera is the biggest complaint I'm seeing online, so chances are in a next game the devs will ditch it, which is a shame. I hope they stick to their... Guts (yeah had to say it)!+ Background, although repetitive, is gorgeous. As are the character designs for the main characters and villains.+ Story and characters are very well written. The sisters really convinced me that they care for each other, which is honestly rare in video games. Nudity was tastefully used, and it pains me that there is still so much stigma around it with people complaining or pointing out "boobs" as if it's a forbidden thing and not just part of the human body. The villains are very convincing in their motivations and all of them are kind of tragic in different ways. Even your merchant dude goes through a lot of twists and turns. The lore is intriguing and in a way, very original. The setting has the proper mood too! Voice acting is excellent as well. Corvo was done dirty tho+ Nemesis and first Harbinger bosses are excellent and probably the best enemies in the game. They're varied, have multiple phases, and great attack patterns. Even if Nemesis sometimes bonks your head with an unseen boulder. I wish you fought them more times through the campaign.+ Music during battle really gets you pumped up. Thanks for reading! And don't get discouraged by my review, if you like action games (especially the classics), chances are you'll like this game! Here's hoping for great things from this team!

Worse yet, the tight spaces make the already wonky camera even harder to maange.-Teleporting enemies are terrible. Is there someone on the dev team who enjoys chasing them around the stage? If so, it's probably safe to say that joy is not shared by vast majority of the audience. Sure, there's solutions like the whip's grapple mechanic or the god-awful bow that's useless if the enemy isn't within range of the field, but it's probably not a good idea to have this enemy ability if the player doesn't have an easily accessible movement option that can cover large distances like Dante's Air Trick.-Many enemies have attacks that aren't telegraphed enough. _childDocuments_.review: Review edited 1/10/22Review edited second time 4/10/22This game scratches that DMC/Bayonetta itch perfectly. It does use the same kind of stationary camera we saw a lot in the DMC series up till DMC V, which you'll see the people review bombing it talk about as though fixed cameras were part of a coup that overthrew and killed their families and took their lands, using them to grow potatoes for fries to make use of their unending streams of salt.The core gameplay loop is fantastically well done, with various quality of life features as the cherry on top. As an example, I've always struggled with delay attack combo timing (i.e. X, X, wait, X, X, X), but in this game your weapon will flash once the delay combo is ready to execute. The hits are meaty and satisfying to deliver, and your counters allow you to easily turn even the most frightening enemy into a helpless victim once you figure out the right timings for each of the horrid monstrosities.The physical sister, Briar, handles a majority of your damage dealing, while the ghostly sister, Lute, handles your defensive abilities. This means that counters and deflections will not interrupt your combos as they are, technically speaking, done by someone else, rewarding good reflexes and inputs with an unrelenting output of damage while your enemies are stunned, slowed down, or otherwise unable to attack you. There are a few color coded enemies that require you to use Lute's abilities to make them vulnerable, which provides a challenging but not overly infuriating change to fights when they appear, having to balance your damage output and not exhausting little Lute's limited energy supply.Lute herself has a massive skill tree that allows you to fine tune how you want her to perform, as well as giving her extra abilities like auto-counters if you miss one, or altering how her auto attack affects enemies.A very interesting mixup to the usual formula is that perfect counters are not done the moment an attack would hit you, but rather the moment an enemy is starting their attack. I thought it strange at first but I found myself enjoying it thoroughly, keeping me alert through fights to catch enemies winding up before the prompt appeared.The weapons all play and feel radically different, giving a fresh air of variety to gameplay as you swap around them, from the slow but heavy swings of your default alt weapon to the rapid, unending flow of attacks from another you unlock. The audio design for some could have used a bit more OOMPH, more noise to their impacts, but that's just me being nitpicky.A common complaint I've seen is that the environments are a little samey and this IS true, but there is a lot of environmental storytelling if you pay close attention to the various set pieces.The game continuously throws new mechanics at you as you go. An enemy that requires one of Lute's powers to damage, but later on you face it alongside a landmine that needs another power to deactivate, turning fights into complex dances as you switch between your weapons, counter everything being thrown at you, and turn enemies into mulch with a well placed combo.Like many games in this genre, we have a sort of Devil Trigger mode that unlocks fairly early. This mode removes the color-coding requirements from enemies and lets you perform an extreme amount of damage at anything unfortunate enough to stand in your way. Something the game doesn't explain all that much is that the features and abilities of this mode are altered depending on what abilities you've slotted in on Lute, allowing you to choose which one fits your style better. We have the balanced one, pure aggression, AoE Crowd Control Central, and Full Regen as far as flavors go. I heavily encourage anyone that gets this game to experiment and find the one they enjoy most.Now, having completed the game, I am prepping to Platinum this game, knowing full well that will require going through at the highest difficulty. The final boss leaves a bit to be desired when it comes to the fight itself, in my opinion, an unfortunate constant in this genre of games. The story was on point, the dialogue was greatly written, if a bit oddly pace at times, and the ending sets up for a sequel. I adored this game, and I sign off this final edit to my review telling the devs, bravo.Score at 2.5 hours: 7.5/10Score at 9 hours: 8.5/10Current score: GIB SEQUEL/10 (But for real take your time with it.)

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an odd mix for me. I enjoyed the story beats and how the game uses aspects of the story to influence the gameplay, and it was overall an okay experience. But when you compare it to other Hack n Slash games like DMC 5, it feels a bit unsatisfying. All the weapons the same base combo, while combining the heavy button with the jump gives a few different attacks based on the weapon, but that's about it. I never really felt too compelled to try and mix and match combos, and on the off times I did, it didn't feel very impactful. The story, however, I very much enjoyed the whole way through. It was nice progressing through and getting the backstory and interactions of not just Briar and Lute, but the whole cast as well. I think my biggest issue though, comes from the gameplay as a whole. Brair's Rapture form that you get early on looks awesome the first few times you use it, and the game translates the fact that she is on the edge of loosing control of her power really well. However, that means the when actually controlling her, I don't feel like I'm doing much besides dashing and spamming the basic sword button until it's time to do the super-ultra-mega-special attack. This feels even more obvious with Berserk mode, which literally has you having no control of Briar, and instead you try and bring Briar back to her old self while the game autoplays Briar's strongest form for you. And the biggest issue with all of it is that it's based on Unity, which gets built up only by playing perfected more often than not. Getting hit at all can mean a big chunk of Unity lost, which just leaves me thinking that the power-ups are just a "Win faster" reward for playing perfectly. I would say watch gameplay first if you're interested to see if it's right for you. Or if you just want to see the story, then absolutely just watch a playthrough, as I think the story is the game's best part. Overall, I had a good enough time, but I can't help but see the cracks in the gameplay and where things could have been better executed.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice reminds me a lot of the 2000's to 2010 era character action games such as Devil May Cry, Bayonetta and God of War. While the game certainly has some issues along with plenty of small things that could use some more polish, I enjoyed it a lot more than I expected to and was positively surprised that it avoided many of the usual pitfalls that a lot of the combat focused games often run in to.Fans of the genre will find the structure of the game very familiar with the story being split in to missions which are either boss encounters or longer missions with very limited exploration which feature "arena" based encounters where you enter a room and a number of enemies or waves of enemies spawn in. Your performance in every encounter gets ranked by your score (combos etc.), time taken to beat the encounter and damage taken - which then gets calculated in to the end ranking for each mission.Combat could be described as stylish, fun and chaotic although sometimes to its detriment as the visual clarity often gets completely lost among the amount of enemies, spam of visual effects and the awful camera - which along with the target locking/tracking that has trouble keeping up with faster enemies are the biggest issues the game has.Enemy variety and boss encounters were both among the positive surprises, although in the latter portion of the game some of the encounters do feel like they drag on a little due to the sheer amount of hp some of the larger enemies have and boss encounters get interrupted by short cutscenes slightly too often.Game features 6 weapons in addition to the basic greatsword and while many of these have situational uses, some of them simply were just so much more fun to use than the others. Fists, bow and daggers for example felt very bland and as if they needed something more - and there were definitely times when I felt like the basic greatsword should have had a complete moveset instead of just a couple combos.Another positive surprise was the art style of the game, monster and boss designs were awesome and while the environments had some pretty vistas the overall environment design suffers a lot from the repetition.That being said I had a lot of fun with Soulstice and it took me roughly ~17 hours to beat the game on Knight difficulty which is the highest difficulty available when you start a new game but for those looking for more challenge and replay value there are 2 unlockable difficulties (one for beating the game on Knight and one for beating it on the difficulty that unlocks after). I would definitely recommend Soulstice for the fans of the genre, although you may require some tolerance for bad camera and some lack of polish.

Traversal uses a , which gets annoying and can turn you around until you get used to it. In combat, the camera is also fixed awkwardly and targeting enemies barely helps, if at all. At the very least, your counter UI still pops up at the edge of the screen if an enemy is attacking from behind the camera. It's not the worst thing ever, but it takes adjustment especially so since it's not the norm in character-action games.There's a reason DMC and Bayonetta both chose to use an  situated neatly behind the character 99% of the time. _childDocuments_.review: Took me 17 hours to complete the game on Knight Difficulty.Boy was that a ride. And not one that's over. The completionist within me won't let me leave those achievements unobtained.TLDRThis game does not disappoint in any areas. Story telling is slow to start off but perfectly paced by the end of it.Combat is fast paced and unforgiving throughout the game. Just the way I like it.The music works well though I did find that it just stopped playing during some encounters.And the replay factor is certainly there.Long version.I'll start with the greatest point of contention with this game. The fixed camera angles outside of combat. Yeah. Okay. In some areas they made platforming a chore. But that's 2% of the time at most. The other 98% of the time, I honestly didn't notice the camera at all. It's dynamic when you're moving in tight spaces and it has a wide enough field of view to see what you need to see. Secrets especially.Next up. I have to mention the challenges.Yeah. Very Bayonetta inspired. And just as infuriating as well. Thankyou for digging up that memory devs. You did good. But the 2 hours I spent finishing the ones I found were worth it in the end. Upgrade materials are always welcome. And the ones I missed won't stay hidden for long.As for gameplay. I can honestly say that this is one of my favourite combat systems in any action game. Fast paced dodge heavy combat that forces you to pay attention to everything on the screen and off the screen to stay ahead was a thrilling ride. Controlling both characters at once might have been a pain at first but once I got used to the timing of it, the only thing stopping me from finishing every encounter hitless was my own skill level.Oh. And a note about weapons. The sword doesn't have any proficiency upgrades, it's damage is fixed from start to end. Which means that none of the enemies increase in difficulty later on. The game just throws different enemies at you and mixes them in with the rabble you've been fighting thus far.Now, the art style is most certainly anime inspired. The large eyes, the black outline on objects and characters, the frozen crystals that looked like they were taken straight out of DMC. It was a beautiful game from start to finish. (Aside form the sewers though. No amount of detail or artistic influence can make a sewer look good.)And for a game that takes place in a single city, the diversity of the level design and the wide areas of the battle arenas were a pleasant surprise as I got deeper into the game. And the way the option paths are so easy to miss makes exploration a worthwhile endeavour despite the linear nature of the game. Oh. And let's not forget the bosses.The first few are rough as you don't have the weapons they're week to yet or the skills needed to slow them down. But when they appear again as regular enemies later, you'll know what to do.The later bosses were something else though. The mechanics behind their fights were sound. I never felt like I took a hit that I didn't deserve. Their designs were outstanding. The level of detail was top notch. Their scripting was on point. Never left themselves open unless I made an opening. Their arenas were always the right size and shape for the boss. Nowhere to hide or cheese them. You had to fight them head on. And the... boob physics and oddly upward facing camera angles were a thing... Okay. Someone must have been horny when designing that one.Honestly, if I had to pick one thing that I didn't like about this game, it was that the sound effect added to Lute's voice occasionally made it hard to understand the first word she was saying. Her voice fades in an out like an echo. A few syllables get lost at times. But the subtitles sorted that. Maybe it can be patched. Who knows.All in all. This is a AAA game from a very surprising source.The developer is indie. Very indie. But this was stellar. And for the price, a bargain.Thankyou very much for all your hard work devs.And please, please, if you make a DLC or a second game, let us play as Sabre...
