_childDocuments_.review: This game wears all of its influences on its sleeve. If Soulstice were a Venn Diagram, it would have Devil May Cry, Berserk, and Nier overlapping each other. If any of these interest you, give this one a shot. If you like two or more of these, you may be in for a treat. The game plays like a character action hack-and-slash, a la Devil May Cry and you may recognize some familiar movesets from those games. Comes with its own arsenal of weapons mapped to D-pad, so there's room to add variety to combos in a similar way style switching did for DMC. The partner-system reminds me of the Pods and Grimoires in Nier with an Ikaruga flair. The character design screams Berserk , so if you ever wanted to play a black knight with a huge sword this may be one of your few options.Camera angles seem to be a common complaint here. Having played DMC with its Resident Evil-esque fixed camera I was already used to it, though some levels have tight spaces that make the camera go haywire when locked-on to enemies. Developer seems to be accommodating of accessibility features, so hopefully this leaves room for updates or ironing out issues others had with resolution and framerate. Overall first impression from playing the demo and the first couple stages of the game, not a bad outing from a "AA" game developer.Updated: Finished the game and the above sentiments remain mostly the same, though some extra pointers. The camera issues did start to become more noticeable as they snagged on environments and certain arenas. Dev has stated they are working to address this, which is a good sign. Target switching can be a bit of a hassle in more frantic fights and can make prioritizing more difficult than it should be. Later chapters can drag on, outstaying their welcome after a while. It seems that Reply is aiming to make Soulstice into a series, so my suggestion for the future titles is to vary up the environments and cut down on chapter length to make stages more distinct and memorable. Overall, I think this a promising first foray for Reply, with room for refinement. I give this one a Platinum for the effort.

_childDocuments_.review: After about an hour of gameplay, I'm finding the game a bit generic and repetitive. But I'm not complaining because the gameplay is what I was expecting and wanted in a game. I just wish it ran better on Steam Deck, but even on lowest settings it stutters. Hoping to see better combos & weapons going forward. A lot of the action can take place far away and be hard to see. Not some great decisions over all, but the story seems like it may be interesting if not very deep and I respect what they were trying to do with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished it yet, so I will come back to this if I remember it, but for now, I have to say that I AM HOOKED! The graphics are amazing, the story is very enticing, the atmosphere, omg the atmosphere is captivating, and the combat is very well designed, like, really, you can tell they put a lot of effort into making the combat fun, exciting and I think they managed the rule of thumb, which is "easy to enjoy, challenging to master".Did I also say that it runs SO SMOOOTH, and my laptop is certainly not the greatest gaming equipment. As for the camera, it's pretty comfortable once you get used to it, though it might seem weird at first.I LOVE THIS GAME ALREADY! And to think I only learned about it a few days back. What a gem, really. I highly recommend this.Edit: After finishing the game I can say with absolute certainty that it is one of the best game's I've ever played. The story get's better and better, the gameplay is incredible, I can't wait to master it, and the graphics and voice acting are gorgeous. As for the difficulty (this might interest some folks), instead of just making the enemies spongier, Soulstice makes you go up against stronger types of enemies, like MGRR. I really like this approach.Also, the second time you play the game, you have the option to skip the "memories" (pieces of the story) completely, something that I'm sure some folks will appreciate.Best game I've played all year.

_childDocuments_.review:
The balance of the Holy Kingdom of Keidas is compromised when powerful, feral creatures known as "Wraiths" invade from the other side of the Veil, threatening to consume the living. The "Chimeras", hybrid warriors born of the union of two souls, are the only ones who can protect humankind.

Briar and Lute are two sisters who have been reborn as a Chimera. The transformation has granted Briar superhuman strength and resilience, while Lute, who was sacrificed in order to bind her soul to her sister's, has become a ghost with mystical powers. Voiced by Stefanie Joosten (Metal Gear Solid 5), Briar and Lute are sent on a mission to reclaim a city in ruins that has been ravaged by the Wraiths, only to discover that the Order they belong to has a far more complex plan in mind.

Explore a dark world brimming with hidden mysteries, master a diverse combat system, and inhabit the dual forces of two sisters in a coming-of-age fantasy story with fast-paced action, vicious enemies and breathtaking boss fights.

name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo
detailed_description: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo is a surrealist point’n’click graphic adventure. Mr. Coo is stuck in a weird, nonsensical world, and he needs your help to get out of it -but first of all, he needs to find all his pieces and be whole again!- There might be some philosophical strife behind all this nonsense, but with all the chaotic monsters, crazy robots and one-eyed ladies, it’s kinda hard to say. With an astounding and colorful hand-drawn 2D cartoon art, and a surrealist and whimsical story, full of absurd humor, wacky characters and crazy situations and innovative puzzles, The Many Pieces Mr. Coo is a fresh take of the graphic adventure genre that will bring together veterans of these gamers and newcomers alike. Mr. Coo and this game are creations of the acclaimed artist Nacho Rodríguez. 2D animator and director, Rodríguez has been nominated to the Goya Awards for his short film “A lifestory”. He also was lead animator of the game O.zen at Ubisoft. Mr. Coo is one of his most celebrated characters, having appeared in several hilarious short films. A fresh take of the point’n’click graphic adventure genre Astounding hand-drawn 2D cartoon artstyle A surrealist, whimsical world, symbolic and full of meaning – but also heartwarmingly silly! Meet wacky and lovable characters like the Giant Chicken, the Faunus or the One-eyed Woman Lots of absurd humor. Look, we already told you there are giant chickens, we can’t stress this enough

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely charming and it feels like The Neverhood except with puzzles that don't totally suck, but the game is buggier than a roach motel. Once the titular mechanic of having you control different body parts shows up I've run into several game-breaking bugs that have softlocked the game, and with only checkpoint saves, forced me to replay whole parts over. I was genuinely enjoying this game so I want to give the dev some slack and not to refund the game yet. It sucks to have to say this, but stay away from buying the game right now until these bugs are addressed. If they do I will definitely revise this review to a recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: The game is incredible, but currently it's unplayable. The puzzles that involve several pieces keep forgetting the state of the off-screen piece, the clicking zones are off-target, and everything ended up freezing at some point. Whenever you do something out of order (which you tend to do in a point-and-click adventure when trying to figure things out!), it just unravels. That code needs rework. Not to mention that the game has checkpoints after short animations and none between huge puzzles.This thumbs-down is only to inform the developer of the problems. Once they're fixed and I can actually finish the game, I'll happily change my review — the animation is stunning and the world quirky in the best way possible.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a triumph, and a tragedy.To be entirely up front, my only two criticisms with this game are that the demo accounts for a full 30, maybe even 50 percent of the game. And; The puzzle design can occasionally be strange, with the clunky lack of a UI and the hand drawn animation, (gorgeous as it is), occasionally limiting options in a scene.Everything else about The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo is worthy of praise. The characters, the strange world, the minimalism, the satisfying interactions... All of it is absolutely wonderful, and worth experiencing...... but there isn't enough of it to be worth 15 bucks.If the artistic vision of Mr. Coo is the triumph, the modern landscape for gaming makes the tragedy. This is a desperate recommendation for anyone who can afford the entry price, but for most, there simply isn't enough content to pay for. In an ideal world, 15 dollars wouldn't be any barrier to entry for such a work of passion as this game, and the money would help fuel even more glimpses into this strange land that Mr. Coo inhabits. But as it is, and I struggle to avoid this description, I feel almost disappointed in the game purely because there wasn't more of it.The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo is a wonderful game held back by the harsh reality of being a product. Were this a YouTube animation, available to free, it would likely be praised to hell and back by everyone who saw it. Instead, it is trapped on Steam and demanding an entry price, which will inevitably drive people away. And that is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shame.If you have the money to spare, and don't mind the short length of the game, then by all means support it. Otherwise, if you're curious and on the fence, perhaps wait for a sale. And no matter what, keep an eye on this talented artist to see what else they produce.

_childDocuments_.review: + the smoothest animations ever+ awesome old time cartoon visuals+ fun, absurd plot+ unconventional solutions to puzzles that fit the world+ nice visual story telling + fun music+ in-game book with hints (quite well hidden at times)+ you can collect concept art once you're done- puzzles not always intuitive- quite short for the price (insane animations kinda make up for it)- clicking controls don't always feel accurate (trying to click something but it only works if you go a bit below the object)- when pausing the game, you might see an icon that look like an "i" on a piece of paper. those are not hints. those are the credits, making you lose the progress since the last checkpoint when clicking on that.some people experience bugs. those were the ones I noticed:- sometimes arrows show up, indicating that there's another area, when there actually isn't anything- two of the concept art papers were invisible for some reason. I could only find them by closely following a tutorial, where they weren't invisible.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, let's get this out of the way first. Like the great majority of the reviews here, I gotta praise the animations. I haven't seen hand-drawn animation in games a lot, and here they are really fluid and just fun to look at.Graphics are also fun too, you switch from these whimsical animations and drawings to some off-putting montages that seem inspired by Samorost.However this game has some big bugs. Sometimes, Mr.Coo's pieces don't follow each other in between rooms, which softlocks the game. Sometimes, if you click too fast, the animations either get skipped or they play in the wrong order. I had a few times where the camera wouldn't focus on one of Mr.Coo's pieces when I chose them.Most of these bugs could be fixed by restarting the levels, and that's a can of worm I'll into in a bit.Let's talk gameplay. It's a point-and-click game, so expect some levels of moon logic in there. However in some cases, mainly at the end of the game, it really pushes it. There often isn't a visual cue that may point you in the right direction. Worse, the solutions to a good chunk of the problems require you to time clicking on things right. It's not a problem in itself, until you remember that the animations can play out of order and as such make you fail for no reasons.The only checkpoints you'll get are when you complete a levels. If you have to reload the levels for whatever reason, well congratulation, you'll have to repeat the same steps you did to get where you were and THEN hope the game doesn't break along the way. It's not the worst, but it absolutely kills the moodFinally, there's the end boss. You are on a timer to figure out the solution. Said solution requires to click on a random thing, at a precise time, or you fail. And if you fail, you have to wait 20-30s each time as the game needs to play cutscene. Oh, and its also not the real end to the story. Seems the game is gonna be separated into either chapters or into whole new games.Final verdict is that this game is cool, but it doesn't hit the sweet spot in terms of puzzle difficulty and has some uncommon but game breaking bugs.Wait for it to be real cheap if you're interested. The animations are what mostly props the price up, but as a really short game, ~20$ is an absurdly steep price
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a game designed by artists. It's visually amazing, and the world and characters are incredibly expressive and whimsical. But the style is overshadowed by bafflingly poorly designed puzzles and moments of dire UX that left me clicking randomly on anything that could maybe be clickable (Because there is no indication of anything) and searching for the hint book. If the game is meant to make no logical sense, that's fine, but maybe it shouldn't revolve around puzzles. It doesn't work if players can't actually understand why what they are doing is correct, there is no logical deduction, it's nonsense, and that's not fun, it's aggravating.

_childDocuments_.review: I was pretty excited about the game but once I actually played it I just didn't have fun.The animations are gorgeous, but everything relating to the game is simply broken. Sometimes literally. I encountered numerous bugs such as getting stuck on repeating animations, not being able to press a button, disappearence of all sounds and some other little things.The puzzles themselves are very unclear at times. I know this game is very abstract and that's the point, but it doesn't help when you need to kick some pillar and you don't even know that this pillar is interactable. You need to use some mechanism but it just doesn't work. Why? Because some cog rolled away and the game didn't put an emphasis on that, showing you some pretty animation of a weird creature instead. Also, you somehow should've made the connection that one object in one room relates to another object in another room. I refused to continue playing once character just ceased to interract with an object I clicked on. The puzzle was time-based and when I lost, I had to watch the same animation 4 times in a row. Not to say that at start I didn't even know what I needed to interract with - I had to use a guide.Many pieces of Mr. Coo is so abstract it  hints to play it. But when hints straight up tell you what to do it just becomes boring as I don't actually figure out the solution myself. I am thankful the game puts it on player to reveal the whole solution or just a part of it, but I still felt like I got robbed of some experience when I didn't understand unclear sequence.I really wanted this game to be great because I know how hard it is to make all these animations. The attention to detail is honestly astonishing. But when we talk about the game part, it's just awful and not fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the game so much, it clearly had a lot of heart and was so cute and funny. Really stunning visuals and animation with a great soundtrack to boot. The game is a little less than an hour, so you're mostly paying for the amazing animation. I can't wait for the next chapter to release!NOTE: There are many bugs like not being able to switch to the torso if it was in a certain spot, the cursor disappearing every so often after a switch to the body which causes you to restart the puzzle, and the second to last cutscene did not play when the legs were in a different spot as well.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give this game a mixed rating, I would. Though its more like "Mixed-Positive" if anything.Right off the bat, this game is challenging at times. While I'm not an amazing pro point-and-click player, some of the puzzles did have my brain whacked around a few times. I used the very in-depth hint system about 3 times. Most of the times I would just randomly guess the right combination correctly.Only 3 hints for the entire game doesn't sound that bad, but when you take into account the game is less than 2 hours long, it's something. Yeah, the game is pretty short, but in their credit it is significantly cheaper to compensate. Even cheaper on sales! I'm no price:length ratio gamer guru that requires all my games be 10 cents or more per hour, but I was kind of surprised that it just... ended.Even though some of the puzzles were confusing and the game short, it infinitely makes up for it in terms of animation. This game has amazing animation, every little thing so perfectly blends into each other, and the creativity! One second you're chasing after an apple in a present and the next you're inside a chicken egg. Every scene I didn't know what to expect, because anything could just morph, with beautiful transitions and all, into another thing with little to no correlation. The kind of games that constantly get you off guard are really great.I did have my fair share of glitches, especially with characters and animations playing late, teleporting, and such, but it's not game-breaking.  In all- it's a great game with eye watering animations, with a few rough spots here and there. Overall, it's fun!
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: I would highly recommend getting this game on a sale. The base game is roughly 2 hours. There are so go back incentives but I dont have much interest in them. The game itself is a beautiful testament to hand drawn animation as well as great point and click puzzles. Puzzles are challenging but there is a hint system to supplement any frustration without having to pull up a website. I really did enjoy this game but the runtime in my opinion does not line up with the price point. Again catch this game on sale. I know you can beat the game within the steam refund window but dont do that, support the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: Impressively surreal and imaginative use of hand-drawn and claymation animation that reminds of the surreal dark animation back in the 80s and 90s. Due to it being essentially an interactive movie where you can only click on one thing to continue the animation, there is some pixel hunting having to be done and some quality-of-life features like highlighting interact-able objects would go a long way, but the puzzles are particularly creative and cute. It's relatively short at just over an hour which makes sense with how painstakingly bespoke the animation and production is, and it ends on a very wholesome musical note.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game is like watching an old animation like "Tom and Jerry", the opening scene is amazing. The protagonist is like Scrat from "Ice Age Village" with his obsession with apples. I was impressed by the expressive soundtrack and the exaggerated style of presentation. Most of the controls are mouse click based, and the detailed hints make the game relatively easy to play, and the achievements are easy to obtain. Although the overall flow of the game is not long, I feel satisfied with its quality. I hope the production team will bring more excellent works in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: Having done some traditional animation, I'm well acquainted with how time-consuming and how much of a precise art it is. If for nothing else, get the game to watch and rewatch the gorgeous flowing shenanigans in this surreal world.The puzzles and solutions make VERY little sense (which is the only thing lengthening the game), but that's par for the course for point-and-click adventures, and I appreciate this game just leaning into it. Don't ever feel bad about using the hint book. The gameplay is rocky and had some breaking bugs, but tell the team and they're quick to fix them. Utterly unique and looking forward to any future work from these artists.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: After a recent patch, the mouse pointer is indeed functioning properly now.Leaving my original comment below the line:------Not a review but a purchase warning:Not recommended to get because the product is broken. A point and click game with a non-functional mouse pointer. It's that bad.The mouse technically works but the cursor is hidden, and the in-game cursor doesn't respond to mouse input. You can move the in-game cursor if you have a controller plugged in, so it's not completely unplayable, but why would one want to do that with a perfectly functional mouse? This bug has been in the game for nearly a year, it seems.Also, each scene swap is interrupted by an out of place loading logo, even when installed from SSD. You can clearly understand that the scenes were meant to flow together seamlessly, and in fact, the demo worked fine in this regard. This significantly impacts the experience.In addition, there's something I just found out while scouring the forums for technical advice. There is a statement from the author and main artist of the game saying that the publishers released the game without his approval, and he never intended it to be sold in this state.Even if it's on sale, avoid purchasing this until they sort it out

_childDocuments_.review: The Many Pieces of Mr Coo is a game I found through YouTube, and hoo boy. What a surreal little adventure it was!This stylish point and click has you taking control of a small yellow dingus named Mr Coo, solving a series of surreal puzzles to get to the end. The beautiful, hand-drawn levels are accompanied by a neat jazz soundtrack, and the puzzles require you to think and multitask, controlling Mr Coo's pieces to get them to work together and solve the predicament they're in. This took me a little over two hours to complete, and I enjoyed every moment of it.

_childDocuments_.review: It may not stand out as a click and point game but the vivid animation is top-notch, bringing so much fun and laughter to watch the journey of a cute and likeable character.No words are given but the story is very understandable. It is not unusual for a click and point game to not include any words, usually such a game contains several unrelated levels each serves as a small puzzle but The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo dare to involve mystery, scientific, time leap etc to a complete story. The puzzles are well developed just like its animation, I had no trouble solving anything by myself for the first half, the 2nd half was more challenging. My favorite is the head/leg work together to get the chest key, that trap door/moveable brick was a smart design, I had to watch a walkthrough to pass but it is logical, just hard to guess. luckily there are limited items to interact with and most puzzles are not torture.My complaint is glitches. I quit the game rightfully however when I got back, the save file was gone and I had to start from the very start. Then I decided to finish it in one run and upon finishing, I don't get any achievements including those in the game process. I'm not an achievements collector but I'd like to have what I've earned. If you exclude the extra time I spent into the game the actual gameplay should be around an hour, making The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo not a cheap game but doesn't change the fact it is fun to play. I have high expectations for the upcoming sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Curious little game with passion and charm put into the animations and music, with a surreal world that brings me back to the days of The Neverhood, albeit short with some obscure puzzle solutions. I do feel for the creator, Nacho Rodríguez, who had his work published early without his permission, which left the game filled with bugs and cut content. Regardless, I do hope to see Nacho's continuation of Mr. Coo, as a sequel has been teasedWould recommend if you're a fan of traditional animation and peculiar point-and-click games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes no sense as a puzzle game, very little logically follows the thing before it. If you want a game where you spend hours randomly clicking around the screen until you find a very, very specific sequence of random events that somehow allow you to move to the next series of random events, that are so outlandish, that you just spend the entire game reading the hint book, and following it picture for picture, until you figure out wth is going on (if you ever do). Then this is the game for you! The only redeeming quality is it has a fantastic whimsical art style which I very much enjoyed. Too bad it was used to create such a mind numbingly frustrating game. Oh and did I mention that the last puzzle you are doing this while timed???? I feel like I was punished for trying things during that phase. The only other quality to this game is that it is short, so your misery won't last long.

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I'm not a point-and-click type of player, but after seeing the trailer for this game, I knew I had to get it.I'm also not really a puzzle game person either, but even with some of these being absurdly difficult for me, I've still been having a really good time with this game so far just for the animation alone. It almost feels like an interactive movie, in a way. Might update this review after I finish the game (if I remember, I usually just make these once lol).Update: I now have 100% in this game, and I do not regret a thing putting time into this game. Once you know all the puzzles, playing through the full game is like watching a short film, except being able to interact with the puzzles and things around. It's well made, though there are a few bugs; only two of which I found forcing me to quit to the main menu.Pesky Bug #1: After you have your legs, if you leave your head in the spot where you got the bottle of eyes and have your legs run back through the clock, the game softlocks on the head.Pesky Bug #2: After you finally unlock the torso, if you lead your legs into the lava and are prompted to the hourglass, once you click out of it, the torso will be gone. You can still "switch" to your torso and have it run through the clock invisibly alone, but this will softlock the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Art reminds me of Bone (comic book) with the cute art style, yet has dark places. Fairly short game that can be completed in about 3 hours or so depending on how quickly you can solve the puzzles. Does have replayability for extra concept art which is worth it to me since I like it so much. I only had some frustration with a few scenes when trying to click to execute . The biggest forte is absolutely the animation. So fluid, so beautiful. I usually like to click past the loading screen when booting up a game the second time, but I was compelled even by how the logos animated and let it all run normally. Puzzles weren't terribly frustrating but weren't overly easy. When you get stuck, there's a hint book floating around that you can investigate to help move things along quicker. I'd recommend against it if you can since it is so short, but if you want the story, there's no harm (minus not getting an achievement for not using hints). Glad I played! Need more games like this
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: This is the closest thing to a "playable cartoon" that you're gonna find. Other reviews correctly point out the brilliant animation and wacky/weird scenarios. There seems to be some disagreement about the puzzles. I didn't find them to be particularly difficult, but I play a lot of point and click games and I get the weird logic that's often involved. So if you're not a big fan of this genre, you may get frustrated. However there is a pretty good hint system that allows you to reveal the solution in sections, as opposed to simply telling you the answer. This game had some controversy when released and suffered some poor reviews as a result, but it played 99% perfectly for me. One time I was unable to back out of the hint book and had to restart, but this wasn't a huge deal. Overall, if you're an animation fan and like point and click games, you should definitely give this a whirl. If you're intrigued by the animation but don't care for puzzling, the hint book will get you through the game. (Or you can just watch a playthrough.) I hope the developer isn't discouraged and makes a sequel with more sophisticated puzzles. I'm so glad there are still people out there making unique, creative, and beautiful games like Mr. Coo!

_childDocuments_.review: it's a fun little surrealist animation, but it's not a puzzle game--because there's no logical cause and effect, you can't use deductive reasoning to figure out how to proceed. It's also VERY short, and buggy (I finished the whole game but wasn't credited with a single achievement, and I had to try one segment four times because the game wasn't recognizing my clicks at a critical timed component).The art and animation are innovative and interesting--but they're unskippable, even if you've seen them already. Which is really frustrating when you're having to repeat sections due to the game bugging out.Overall it was more frustrating than fun, which is a shame because the animation was cool.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start off by saying that the animation and artstyle look absolutely incredible. I had a lot of fun watching everything move and interact. Also seeing the creativity in how the world works was fascinating. I was also fortunate enough to not run into any bugs.However, the gameplay is severely lacking. As much as I enjoy exploring the wacky world that they built, it is way too nonsensical and unrealistic. It feels like there are no rules or logic at all and things just happen for unknown reasons. Because of this, its nearly impossible to figure anything out by yourself since you don't know the cause and effect of anything, leaving you to constantly rely on hints, which defeats the whole purpose of a point and click game since you aren't able to figure anything out on your own without being told what to do. (ex. You're supposed to go under and into a clown head in order to activate some kind of tv thing with a lever in order to attract a cage with 4 giant legs thats holding your torso. This actually happens in the game and there is no way you would know that without using a hint) This kind of stuff would work great in an animation, not a video game. (yes I know this guy makes animations which are really cool btw)On top of that, I beat the game relatively quickly, so there isn't that much gameplay at all.I think the game would have been more fun if hints were harder to get since they're so important. If the hint book was harder to find or just straight up inaccessible unless we solve something (using real world logic like a cage and a key) then it would make the game more interesting. This is just a suggestion along with my opinion.Although I enjoyed the visuals, I would not recommend purchasing this game.TL;DR: Beautiful visuals, short game time, bad gameplay

_childDocuments_.review: This game is, by a large margin, one of the prettiest and best animated games you will ever find. The puzzles can be frustrating sometimes but that's the spirit of old point and click games: trial and error. In that regard, it's perfect. In the animation and art department, it's also perfect. My one real criticism is that it is incredibly short. It's about a 2 hour experience with stuff just kind of happening. I enjoy the weird, strange, and almost whimsical nature of the entire thing. However, just as you think you're about to learn what's going on the game ends pretty abruptly. Leaving it feeling like a paid demo of a complete game. In addition there are still some bugs with the product. It's not anywhere near unplayable but you can expect to lose audio or the game to freeze and you may have to reload the current part that you're on. It also does not seem to do full screen nor are the aspect ratios perfect. TL;DR gorgeous game with even better animation, there are some puzzle mechanics that may frustrate people, and it features story that leaves you just as confused as the titular Mr. Coo. _childDocuments_.review: Woah, that was one heck of a surreal ride.It's a very interesting experience. A short and very artsy-fartsy thing that at times is a complete and chaotic fever dream. It has awesome animation and design. Really. It looks groovy as all heck for the most part. The imagination it takes to come up with the series of events that play out is quite something, for sure. I love it. The music fits, and is equally bonkers. The gameplay is dead simple, you point and you click to solve puzzles. No real items to combine, no inventory. It's as basic as it can be. The puzzles are surreal as well, but very easy to figure out despite that. Click things to see what they do, and go from there. Just follow the game's logic. You'll be fine! There's even a hint book if you get stuck. There isn't that much in terms of puzzle solving for the hardcore adventure fan, but it's not really the point here either, in my opinion. Just enjoy the ride.It has some glitchy moments and janky pathing and sure could use some more polish. It froze on me one or two times.I recommend it overall, but beware that it's quite short for the asking price. I would wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: At its core it's a near flawless experience that's bogged down by a mountain of annoying little craplets (small pieces of crap) that could very well be ironed out in the future like the small resolution issues, things flickering sizes/in and out of existence, the background for the boiler room and (most infamously), seemingly random glitches that halt your progress and make you quit to the menu. Those issues are things i wouldn't mind in a much larger, less visual game, but in my mind it has similar issues to Stray, because the presentation and brevity of the game is what makes it so appealing, so those setbacks are a lot more major than they'd be in most other types of viddie game. it's also at a pretty steep price for a game so short so I think it needs an extra layer of polish to really warrant that price. There are worse deals out there though! we live in a world where you can buy "luigis green garden gamecube remastered for the switch" for $60.I still think that the game is absolutely gorgeous and very funny, the designs for all the characters are so creative and they all implanted themselves directly into the deepest part of my little brain : ), the puzzles are abstract but pretty fair once you've surveyed your surroundings, and the game even has a nice little hint 🅱️ook to help you when you're lost!Definitely a good game but it's held back from being great by a few minor things that could easily be fixed with an update.

_childDocuments_.review: This thing is a borderline surrealist masterpiece. There's a bunch of weird technical issues that bog it down, and the puzzles are really arbitrary and often have no logical through line, but the animation and overall experience is stunning.I will say though, yes, it's as technically messed up as others have highlighted. I just love it too much not to give it a thumbs up. Here's some of the stuff I ran into, despite this game being roughly a half hour long if you know the puzzle solutions. - The cursor became unresponsive the first time I launched the game, which turned out to be due to a controller being plugged in. This game doesn't have controller support, so I don't understand this. - I had to stop playing halfway through the game, but did not have my progress saved for some reason. - Many camera behavior issues, causing 4th wall breaks where the camera would pan from one background scene to another instead of cutting. - Once the game got locked up when I ran out of a room. It just never loaded the next background and I had to reload. - Many weird issues where for some reason the legs/head would just move without input. Or it wouldn't let me switch between them, causing many later puzzles to be much harder.To cap this off though, yes, despite all of that, I love this thing. It's small, striking, bizarre, wacky, and beautiful. I will say though, the puzzles are often very obtuse, and I used nearly every hint in the game. I would honestly say this would be even better if it had more animated sequences, more set-pieces, and less puzzles, but regardless, this is a great little art piece.

_childDocuments_.review: Very eye-catching visuals with some mysterious characters that I would really like to who they are and what's their background, but since it's "to be continued", you won't find out at this point.  The game seems to have a strong story behind it, but it's early to say without seeing the end.Beside the interesting animation and puzzles, there are some technical bugs the developer team need to take care of.  Also it was shorter than my expectations, but again, it's "to be continued".
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Gorgeous animation+ Incredibly creative and appealing imagery+ No inventory to combine random items together+ Like a playable animated short from a film festivalCons:- Very short (<1 hr)- Not always clear how your character will interact with the environment ("moon logic")- One puzzle requires timing to a frustrating degree- Switching between Mr. Coo's pieces isn't always clear in its feedback
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on this game, one one hand the animations are pretty great and creative, it's wonderfully weird. But the puzzles are the typical, click on everything and hope something happens. Sometimes you can guess what your next step is, but in many cases it's not really logic involved, not even moon logic, it's just random things happening for the sake of beeing random, and I don't think that makes for a especially good gameplay experience. It's also dreadfully short, you can run through it in less than 30 minutes if you know what you are doing and most of that time will be animations. I don't regret playing of buying it, but for the current asking price it's a bit steep. This is one of those, "recomended at +50% off"-games if you care about price at all. I'll leave a thumbs up, but it comes with caveats.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted this game originally because how beautifully animated and creative it is, puzzles are clever but there were certain ones that are a bit difficult since there's no real indicator for them. Game is pretty short but imo its pretty good! I only ran into one bug that nearly made the  stage nearly impossible to beat because the chick and Mr.Coo disappeared If you have that happen just leave the stage and return to it. Enjoyed the experience regardless.  Now, I can't help but to constantly think of  Zach hadel's voice and noises for Mr.Coo which made the experience x10 better.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but very fun. This game is pretty much an interactive animated short with a run/play time of 30 Minutes, and ends with a "To Be Continued" ending, setting up either future games in the series or DLC. But whatever they do, I am looking forward to it. This game is allot of fun, and if you are a fan of "Point and Click" adventure games and animated shorts, you will like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

Timed puzzles are frustrating and sometimes we had the right solution but kept clicking the wrong bit. The last bit could be a bit scary, but not really. But overall I really liked it. That's it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of the Mr. Coo series since it was public on Nacho Rodríguez's website, so I was really excited when I saw the new game of Mr. Coo on Steam!It's been a long time since he created the last amazing animation games before this game, and absolutely this game is still really awesome.I love the idea, story, animation and everything about this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: An intriguing, adorable and fascinating point-n-click with a lovely surrealist art style. Gorgeous animation accompanies a fun and quirky soundtrack; the two blend together in a beautiful fashion. It is a decidedly short game (even with my lack of experience in the genre, it only took me about two hours), but I do not think that this is a point of criticism. The amount of effort that went into the game justifies its short length; art of this quality takes an enormous amount of time and effort to make. Not only that, but it is implied If you appreciate what you are seeing in the trailers, then I cannot recommend this game enough. We all should support creations like this that uplift independent animators and unique ideas. You will not be disappointed!
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: The art and animation in this game is so charming and great, I love it!I recommend this game to anyone who enjoys fun art styles an characters, even if you aren't a fan of point and click adventures, I still think this is worth it.There were some glitches, but nothing that reloading the checkpoint didn't fix, you can read more about the development issues and ongoing patches to the game on the artist's social media accounts.This game was a lot of fun to play with someone and solve the puzzles together.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: My Best Descriptor for this game is "What if Felix Colgrave made a point and click adventure game?"It's fantastically drawn and animated, all of the gestures and animations have lots of energy and the tone is very wild and grabs the attention like little else. The use of light and perspective is used very well early on and while not very long everything here is lovingly done and an absolute treat to behold.Being a point and click, 60's acid trip puzzles to solve and while in hindsight they're quite straight forward, the toon force logic being employed means that the answers can be quite obscure. However the game knows that this may be a problem, and there's an ingame hint book should you ever feel stuck for longer than you'd like.Puzzle design isn't flawless, but it's an animated trip that didn't try and skimp on gameplay and I can't help but respect the creativity and craftsmanship that went into this game. It's a bit on the expensive side for such a short game, and if you're short on cash this isn't going to entertain you for days on end, if you can afford to fund bizarre and unique experiences, then I recommend The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure what some of these reviews are saying about bugs? I didn't encounter a single bug in my play time.As for the game, it's colorful, fun, wacky but very short. I would suggest to wait for a sale to play it or buy full price if you want to support fun projects like this that showcase good 2D animation. I like to support titles like this that make use of traditional animation so this was worth it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: A surreal little game that is just as much a video-game as it is an animated art-piece. The game is quite short, but well worth the reasonable asking price in my opinion.Pros:1) Hand drawn 2-D animation that has been beautifully put together to create the game. Truly a feast for the eyes.2) Silly, fun humour that is enjoyable to all folks of all ages.3) Fairly decent puzzles.Cons:1) As is the case with point and click games, a couple of the puzzles feel a little obtuse, but it's not too bad, simply clicking around will let you access the solution eventually. If not, there is a handy hint book that pops up as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: What a festive romp! Inventive, startling visuals, hugely imaginative, funny, beautifully rendered and the most fun I've had in awhile. Not just in gaming, but in LIFE! Combines cartoons, live action and animated elements seamlessly and it includes a built in hint system. Bravo! The best part of the game comes at the end with three wonderful words..."To be continued..." To Mr. "Nacho" and his team...I totally GET IT and can't wait for more! You should all be very proud! I'm standing at my desk applauding, and don't think I'm not!! Thanks for the great ride!
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! I can't remember the last time I've played a game with so much creativity. If you know what you're doing, you could get through this game in ~30 minutes. But in that time, you would be treated to such wonderful and vibrant art. This game is a joy from start to finish. Even if you're not interested in point-and-click games, I would still recommend playing through this just to have the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: Mr. Coo is more art project than "game" game, a decade (plus!) long effort filled with amazing hand drawn animations in a surreal world that brings me back to the days of watching Liquid Television too young drifting off to sleep. Interactions are minimal -- it is essentially an interactive cartoon where you're clicking on interactions in order to advance to the next scene -- and while the game can be completed in 30 minutes (90-120 realistically on a first play) it's just a nonstop visual assault of charming artwork. It's unfortunate to hear what happened to the creator with regards to the publisher and his wishes but Mr. Coo is an essential addition to any adventure game collection and fan of traditional animation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but oh so very sweet. The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo takes me back to my youth when I played The Neverhood for the first time. Beautiful, surreal, and inspired. This game may not appeal to everyone. The story is purposely absurd with puzzles just as illogical. You have to think outside the box to solve them and just roll with its eccentricities. It's not a very difficult game. There are hints placed throughout, but I was able to finish it without using them. This is a game best played in one sitting for the appreciation of the stylish animation. The mix of art styles and creative character designs are genuinely awe-inspiring. The soundtrack compliments every interaction on screen like an old Looney Tunes episode. Games today often try very hard to be seen as high art often at the expense of the experience, and rarely succeed. This game will likely be snubbed for more self-serious works which is a shame because this has far more artistic merit in its presentation alone than many of the $70 titles that came out this year. It's a clear labor of love and I can't help but feel compelled by it. For the obvious amount of effort put into the stunningly animated hand-drawn art, I say it's worth the price. It should only take around two hours to complete, but I enjoyed every minute and I found the puzzles could be challenging at times. My only grievance is with the cliffhanger ending making it not feel like a complete experience. It left me wanting more. People are seriously sleeping on this one. It deserves far more attention in my eyes. I give it a high recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun short game that's just straight up eye candy. Although, I feel the game was a little too short as the entire gimmick the game is named after, only plays a part in the game half-way through the experience. But it was fun and the cutscenes are beautifully animated. I've also heard people's experiences with glitches in the game but through my playthrough, the most I got was the legs kept playing the run animation on repeat until I made a command that cancelled it. This game is great for those people who loved The Neverhood and wants a new fun animated point-and-click.EDIT:I forgot to mention a major glitch I encountered:For some reason, I never gained any of the achievements. I don't know if this'll get patched out later but I beat the entire game and didn't earn a single achievement.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: One of the biggest criticisms of point and clicks is that they tend to devolve into moon logic puzzles, so I must give props to the devs in making a point and click game that avoids that despite the setting itself being pure moon logic. The animation and artistry is absolutely beautiful and worth the price of admission for it. The game is like going through a modern art museum, except replace the pretentious fart-sniffing and money laundering with actual talent and craftsmanship.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: A very short, very odd, but very interesting/entertaining point and click. The first twenty minutes, absolutely incredible. The puzzles are fun, engaging, and well thought out. Nothing too out there for puzzle solutions. Animation is top notch, I'm still shocked at how vivid some of it is. Storyline...not really sure what's going on but consider me engaged. Mr Coo in particular, likable, appealing, feels like an instant mascot. There's a giant baby chicken mount. A thinking man ogre like thing. An eye monstergirl thing. A evil (I think) crocodile tar monster, and some old...bearded geezer creature who seems to enjoy hitting everything in the vicinity with his cane. What's not to love? Second half of the game is considerably weaker. You go from multiple odd and captivating worlds of madness and cartoon logic to a toymaker's labyrinth. At least I think that's what it was. The puzzles get significantly more complicated and downright frustrating as well. That final timed "Puzzle" in particular. Any semblance of sense in that thrown out the window. Thankfully there's a hint book. I was stubborn, didn't use it. Half my playing time was figuring out what the hell I needed to click on, having to see the same failure animation over and over. Sure shock value the first time, by the twentieth time maybe Mr Coo can be just fine as a pair of legs and a head. Game's plot feels like a drug trip. My only complaint, it's very very short. Completed the entire game in about an hour. I would still recommend simply for the animation quality. I'm looking forward to seeing more from this developer and animator. This game in particular, good stuff. I'm still...lost I suppose in what I just played. It's kept me awake at night, at times it feels like I hallucinated most of it. Like...really what happened!? I'm confused and scared! What's the lore? Mr Coo just wanted an apple, why are there two ethereal beings involved attempting to twist and contort the world in their own way? Who's the villain? The crocodile salamander thing? The old geezer with a cane? Mr Coo? The giant mechanical spider!? Why does music calm it down!? Why is everyone dancing at the end!?  I think the storyline has some deeper meaning, I know it does I'm too stupid to see it. Maybe more will be revealed someday. We can only hope.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to get this game almost immediately after watching my friend start it on PS5. If you like weird cartoons and good art, and don't mind possibly getting softlocked, get this game.Beautiful, short, brilliantly-crafted surreal experience. Part interactive cartoon, part absurd puzzle, part adventure. Lots of bugs (which the devs appear to be working on), but I was able to complete the game. Post-game content was executed in a pretty lackluster, frustrating/confusing way.I wish as much care was given to the gameplay/dev as was given to the animation, music & sound. I wish the game was much longer, but what's here still had to take a painstaking amount of time and work. Seems like it went through some strife in development & some content was cut (check the artist's statement or just look at the community threads for more context).I hope these things are addressed, but if the trailers/art look compelling to you & you don't mind some possible frustration with functionality, I would still recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Point and click games from the old Windows era (like DOS-95) are some of my favorite things for their unchained creativity and unique animation styles.This game has ALL THAT FLARE with its own sense of classic animation. At no point could I have predicted anything that would happen. Every puzzle figured out was rewarded.Absolute instant treasure and I await more.It is REAL SHORT though, so be aware of that. Its about the journey.

I enjoyed it thoroughly, especially for the price.  - It was not free, I paid retail. The downside is that its a bit on the short side, but that is not to say it was a quick or easy game as it was neither quick, nor easy. there were a few parts that required repetitive actions which was slightly disappointing, but not horrible.    I am looking forward to part two !!

There were some parts that were a little annoying, but the solution is usually the most simplest option and I was just overthinking it.It is pretty short though. _childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: For what it is, this little game is great. Perfect? Very far from it, but as of now it is a worthwhile (Albeit sometimes very janky) little experience. You can tell that there is a lot of love and creativity that went into this- but not a lot of game making experience. Wonderful animation that carry the game, and some pretty cleaver puzzle idea- but on the other half there are layering issues on occasion as well as numerous other bugs and glitches. Then a few of the puzzles (Especially the last sequence of the game) feel like you are just brute forcing a lock by trying every combination of everything you can click on. All that being said, despite the glitches and jank, I loved this little experience and am excited to see what else they can come up with.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: Beautiful, imaginative, and fun point-and-click adventure game! While very short, I would recommend this game to pretty much everyone. Its only downside is that it occasionally requires quick reflexes and coordination – thus making it harder for people with decreased motor skills to enjoy. (I played this game with my mouse, and am thus unaware of how it plays using a controller!)Pros: - It’s so nice to look at! I didn’t get tired of Mr. Coo’s movements, even though none of the game’s cutscenes/transition animations are skippable- Hints book prevents getting stuck, without spoiling the puzzles- Does not overstay it’s welcome. Cons: - The game, (like many immersive art experience games), prioritizes looking good over pragmatic game design.- Some parts in the game require reflexes and coordination that not all players will have. (2 occasions to my count )- It’s easy to reach the right puzzle solution, but fail to execute it because of the position of the character in relation to other objects, or badly timing a click. - Imaginative and absurd solutions to puzzles make the ‘use no hints’ achievement a little mean, forcing achievement hunters to choose between the optimal game experience and doing a second run to get the achievement. - Strange pacing – the first half of the game flashes by in short, rapid pace levels, while the last half is just one stage!This game is as close as I’ve ever gotten to playing a movie. Gameplay and Cutscenes blend together seamlessly, and the puzzles are kept short enough that the game moves on before you can become bored or frustrated with your surroundings. The inclusion of a Hints book helps to prevent any irritation from strange puzzle solutions, and instead turns nonsensical puzzle solutions into a fun discovery! The Many Pieces of Mr Coo works hard to avoid the pitfalls of most artistic games. Unskippeable cutscenes are kept to a minimum, it is possible to skip some steps in navigating once you’ve figured out the steps once, and every part of the game is kept bite-size and small to prevent the player from getting confused by unimportant details. That being said, it doesn’t succeed completely. There are plenty of small annoyances in this game, from Mr Coo pushing an item in the wrong direction because you weren’t standing in the right place, to the Hints book only being available in specific spots – but they were not enough to break my enjoyment of this game. Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a perfect counter example for the "graphics in games don't matter" argument. There wasn't a single puzzle that felt super satisfying to complete. I often found myself just going "oh, I see. I didn't guess that." But, tbf, I don't play a lot of point and click games so that could just be me. Even though the puzzles were awful, I still stuck through the game. Something about the visual presentation and the atmosphere in this game was immensely compelling to me. So if it looks like a game you could vibe out on, give it a shot. I hope that this dev continues whatever mad story he has cooking up
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good stuff, but the base game is too short to justify its price and the hint books just straight up give you solutions to the puzzles. Plus there's alot of bugs related to clicking things, sometimes hovering over things just won't register, otherwise it's a completely unique experience filled with the charm of an early nineties point n click adventure game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic point-and-click puzzle game. I'd argue the "adventure" part doesn't apply here, as it flows more like an interactive film until the last section. But that doesn't prevent this from being a worthwhile play, you're still interacting more than watching. Once you get used to the pixel-hunting, and embrace cartoon logic for puzzle-solving, the game shows its wonderful execution of creativity. Short and sweet, I loved it.It seems a tad buggy, however. On the last section Mr. Coo's legs kept replaying an interaction animation and I couldn't cancel it, so I had to reload and redo some steps. There are a few other areas of untidiness in that section, like how the camera strangely cuts just a few centimeters to the left when interacting with the window outside the prison tower (seen in a Steam screenshot). Or the cage's lock that just disappears when you free the torso of Mr. Coo and start the next puzzle. This game is very polished for most of it, showing a clear care for consistency and pacing with how even loading screens don't take you out of the scene, so these things stuck out to me. My only general complaint would be the resolution discrepancy; some assets are hi-res, others very low-res. Not a be-all end-all matter, though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely short n sweet game. Its a point and click alright, with puzzles that are genuinely really clever and some interlock with others, I like that its not convuluted like some point and clicks like the Neverhood. The animation is really lovely too, one of the best parts. Aside from a few bug it's great !
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: "The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo is a must for gamers who like adventure games and point and click. The art is amazing and surprises at every moment . Mr. Coo, has a lot of personality, charisma and is super fun. It is a very enjoyable adventure with replayability with the collectibles the second time you play it. In short, it's a perfect combination of art, animations, mechanics, humor and fun. You will love it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: Every frame is a painting in this utterly surreal point and click adventure game. The slapstick comedy and wacky hijinks are here in full force, and the 2D animations paired with with a delightfully strange art style make for an incredibly enjoyable time I was sad to see finish.I'm extremely grateful for the hint system, as some of the puzzles had me scratching my head, but that didn't stop me from thoroughly enjoying this game. It took around 2 hours for a first-time blind playthrough, though there are a ton of secrets I've learned I can go find now, so you can easily squeeze another few out of this. For the price of a single movie ticket, it's more than worth the asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review: Straight to the point, if you’ve got the money, I’d recommend experiencing it firsthand!It’s VERY short, which is a shame, but VERY worth it! I loved the story (what little we were shown), and all the cast.!!!SPOILERS BELOW!!!But just when you’re getting into it, the game cuts you off with a “to be continued.” I’m willing to wait, but I do wonder if the continuation would be of the form of a dlc, another game, an updated chapter format perhaps? Either way, well worth the price of admission if you’ve got the spare money and just want a short and sweet and goofy game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Many Pieces of Mr. Coo

_childDocuments_.review:
Mr. Coo is stuck in a weird, nonsensical world, and he needs your help to get out of it -but first of all, he needs to find all his pieces and be whole again!

There might be some philosophical strife behind all this nonsense, but with all the chaotic monsters, crazy robots and one-eyed ladies, it's kinda hard to say.

With an astounding and colorful hand-drawn 2D cartoon art, and a surrealist and whimsical story, full of absurd humor, wacky characters and crazy situations and innovative puzzles, The Many Pieces Mr. Coo is a fresh take of the graphic adventure genre that will bring together veterans of these gamers and newcomers alike.

name: V Rising
detailed_description: Experience a Vampire Survival Action RPG adventure like no other. Awaken as a weakened Vampire after centuries of slumber. Hunt for blood to regain your strength while hiding from the scorching sun to survive. Rebuild your castle and convert humans into your loyal servants in a quest to raise your Vampire empire. Make allies or enemies online or play solo locally, fend off holy soldiers, and wage war in a world of conflict. Seize your destiny! Defy Dracula! Rule the night! Now with native gamepad support and a reimagined interface, prepare for action-packed, hands-on gameplay! A Gothic Open-World Explore a vast world teeming with mythical horrors and danger. Travel through lush forests, open countryside, and dark caverns to discover valuable resources, meeting friends and foes alike along the way. Traverse the world with vampire comrades or hunt solo as you pillage villages, raid bandits, and delve into the domains of supernatural beasts. Fear the light - Rule the night Stick to the shadows during the daytime, or the burning sunlight will turn you to ashes. Roam the night and prey on your victims in the darkness. As a vampire, you must quench your thirst for blood while planning your strategies around the rising and setting sun. Raise your Castle Gather resources and discover ancient techniques to uncover forgotten knowledge. Use your newly acquired insight to build a castle to store your loot and grow your army of darkness. Personalize your domain, exhibit your vampiric style, and make sure to craft coffins for servants and friends. Strengthen your castle to protect your treasure hoard from vampire rivals. Compete or Cooperate Travel alone or explore the world with friends. Fighting side by side with other Vampires will give you an advantage in the fight to conquer the greatest threats of Vardoran. Raid other players’ castles, play the diplomat in the game of blood, power, and betrayal, or craft an indomitable retinue of insidious allies. Compete or cooperate - the choice is yours. Master your Vampire Learn and master an arsenal of deadly weapons and unholy abilities. In V Rising, you aim skillshots and dodge projectiles using​ precise​​ ​WASD controls ​and cursor-based​ ​aiming - no click to move. Tailor your vampire to fit your play style by combining weapons with a variety of spells earned through vanquishing powerful foes. Find and master your personal, perfect blend of sword and sorcery to become the ultimate nocturnal predator!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get this game. If you're like me, you'll lose all track of time and destroy your sleep schedule.Dota-style combat but with tighter controls and more precision, a fully-fleshed out experience that is totally fine single-player, and has tremendous risk and reward in multiplayer. Brutal mode is everything it claims it is, the bosses WILL filter you if you aren't willing to try different setups. Don't stick to one weapon, get used to swapping between multiple weapons to take advantage of their varied weapon abilities for mobility, i-frames, range, or unit phasing.9.5/10. -.5 for a gear score system, the only lazy design element.

_childDocuments_.review: ----------------------------------------------------------------------93 Hours Update Below (Spoilers):----------------------------------------------------------------------I am revising my review to a 2/5 after getting to the end game content. I am going to finish this game because I am so close want to complete it; however, I wish I had not started playing this game. Everything I said below is still applicable, in addition:1. The Monkey's Paw - This game's design is "we will give you this, but it using it will make your life harder in a different way". Examples below. Nothing in this game feels like straight progress, instead the game play just changes to be equally frustrating in a different way. This sucks and is not a rewarding design. I hear some folks saying "its just game balancing bro", but game balance should feel like giving the player a higher skill cap as they progress. You get better at the game, the game gives you different ways to be better at the game, you start to tip the balance slight in your favor through your skill acquired through game play. All my complains below cannot be overcome via skill, they are instead hard coded mechanics in the game.    A. "We will give you a super fast horse, butttt you can be shot off it of extremely easily".    B. "You can trigger cool effects on a perfect parry, but 75% of boss moves ignore parry and hit you anyways".    C. "We will give you amazing end game amulets, but you can't fly around with them in bat form even in PvE only".    D. "We will give you human form, but you're extremely slow and the sun will probably burn you and cause you to drop human form and aggro the merchant you were just trying to trade with. Oh, and high level merchants often have Paladins and holy people nearby who can see through your disguise".    E. "We will give you bat form, but its only usable at night, which is 60% of the game".    F. "We will give you servants but they will take 24 hours to collect what you collect in 15 minutes"...this is after the time sink of grinding for higher gear sets for the servants.2. Frustrating Forced Skills: The game's design follow this logic: "Hard is fun" - True. "Unfair is hard" - True. So, "Unfair is fun" - False. Boss mostly can only be dodged and not parried...but you can only dodge every 10 seconds, so you have to sacrifice weapon or spell abilities to have additional mobility.3. Minion Builds Not Viable: They just die too quickly even with a build focused on buffing them. 4. Enemy Spawn Locations: Level 54s will spawn into level 20 areas and wipe you early game, making progressing so difficult.----------------------------------------------------------------------Original Review Below:----------------------------------------------------------------------Overall, this game has a strong start but there are several annoyances that build up over time. 3/5, there are better games to spend your time on and the only reason to play this is if you have a good community of friends. This score could easily be brought up by addressing some of my points below.The Good:1. Building: The system is literally flawless. Everything works exactly how you would expect. Flawless.2. Crafting: Grouping items together by requiring a certain floor type is a stroke of genius. It helps players organize the production line of their base into logical units.3. Base Progression: Again another flawless aspect of the game. What you need to get to the next tier of crafting materials, weapons, or gear is very obvious.4. Combat: 80% of the time combat is rewarding. "Parries" feel great and the skills are mostly varied and feel different enough that cycling your skills keeps the combat fresh.The Bad:1. Enemy Scaling: Extremely punishing. If a boss is 10 levels ahead of you, the game adds an additional modifier to make you do less damage to them and them do more damage to you. This fundamentally means that the game's progression isn't linear, but rather a series of plateaus. You are *not* rewarded for getting 1 or 2 pieces of gear at the next higher level because of this artificial difference modifier. You are only rewarded when you get all 4 pieces of armor and all weapons to the next level. You get a huge power spike because you overcome the artificial level difference modifier...then you have to grind all the way into the next tier of gear for 10s of hours either crushing everything or getting crushed instantly. There is no in between.2. Gear Grind: All or nothing. Mostly addressed in the previous point, but worth saying again: you must get your armor + weapon to the next tier entirely before trying anything higher level or else you will get crushed. This sounds simple but realistically means that you spend 10-20 hours between tiers either getting crushed or crushing everything instantly.3. Vincent the Frostbringer: This Act 2 boss fight opened my eyes to what the game thinks "harder" means. When you do a parry at just the right moment, on everyone else it freezes them for 3 seconds, like just the skill says it should. On bosses it does not freeze them. It doesn't even stun them or interrupt their attack, so one of your two skills are useless in the boss fight. This is true for all bosses. Vincent also has a move that makes him invincible for a few seconds as he just holds up his shield, which is harmless enough. However immediately from that move he does into an offense uninterruptible skill that is ranged which goes so far out that you cannot run out of the radius meaning you can only hope to doge the 5 projectiles he shoots out. This sequence takes about 15 seconds and sucks as a mechanic.4. (Spoilers) Human Form: *This whole section could be addressed by just not making human form unnecessarily slow.* You eventually get a human form so you can go into town and interact with certain merchants without them freaking out about you being a vampire. This is very cool. The problem is that this specific form has been made to be so slow that it is impossible to move between shade fast enough to not get burned as you're approaching the town...which means you have to approach town in your vampire form and just pray that no town NPCs see you and aggro on your vampire form as you approach, then you have to start your transformation into human form near town, which takes about 6 seconds of being completely immobile. Shade moves in the game fast enough that you could start transforming, shade moves, then you start burning before/as your transformation completes, which causes you to take damage, which makes you turn back into a vampire, so now you have to try the whole process again.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10	We played this game purely for PVE, so this review only covers that aspect of the game.IMPORTANT: If you plan on playing PVE, go and look for some recommended game settings, the games default for PVE makes it quite grindy and adds completely unnecessary wait times!What is the game? It’s an open world crafting, survival game where you play as a vampire and your goal is to defeat a WHOLE lot of bosses. There isn’t too much plot going on, but what’s there is enjoyable. What’s good? There are various biomes with different resources and enemies, all part of a vibrant fun world. Especially in the early hours exploration is fun. The resources can then be used to build a base and that is where the game shines the most. The base building is exceptionally fun, has a lot of options and with a little effort you have a unique, visually pleasing vampire castle! In this castle you will do a lot of crafting, with many different workstations, all nicely animated. The game introduced a system where you need to put crafting stations of the same type into specific rooms of your castle, giving you a great incentive for a more complex layout, that as a system is superb! Hopefully other games will adopt this feature! You can craft a lot of different weapons with different, distinct  move sets and learn to cast various spells, all with some option for improvement/customization or in case of the weapons with stat/bonus variations.Throughout the game you will go out and fight bosses in order to unlock new blueprints, spells and vampire powers. This is the second part where the game shines! Especially in the early game, the bosses with their unique personalities and fighting styles are a blast and you will look forward to every fight! Every now and then, bosses will have unique features or mechanics, and the fact that the devs resisted reusing those systems excessively is a testament to their understanding that something being unique makes it amazing!Lastly the game has a fun blood mechanic: The type and quzality of the blood you drink from npcs increases your combat stats. So drinking from a 5% worker is a lot less useful than an 80% warrior. Trying these various classes and ensuring a steady supply of high quality blood is another fun part of the game and adds massively to the “vampire feel”What’s bad then?The games progression through crafting and even the unlocks is very linear. You will be doing more or less the same for your whole playthrough. This will be especially exhausting in the second half of the game, where travel times, boss hp and resource collection times increase, only to keep a number high enough that allows you to fight the next bosses. A number that means no real change to your gameplay. That is because the game uses a system where your gear level determines your strength. The more your gear level is below the level of an enemy the less damage you will deal. This further narrows your path through the game world since fighting bosses is often not a test of skill or player adaption but numbers. The system is certainly a matter of taste, but for us it was what kept the game from being amazing, especially in the second half.Abilities: Your characters cooldowns are … bad. Why this specific complaint? Because it felt bad. Getting hit by boss’s attacks you can’t dodge because your dash has an 8 second cooldown feels bad. Having every ultimate being more or less the same damage/use because you always have 120 seconds cooldowns feels weird. Despite having many abilities in the game, most of them feel too similar to each other, even across the elements. A little less with more variation and maybe a touch more customization would have been much more fun! Milestones: Is said before, you will be doing the same more of less throughout the whole game. This is also because most milestones unlock just better or different versions of things you already have. Once again, this becomes especially apparent in the 2nd half of the game. Vampire powers: Some of these decisions here are probably more important for PVP but PVE wise, they are insane. (Here are a few of my thoughts) Almost all vampire powers should be a lot more responsive. ALL transformations are waaay to slow. I wanna USE these things, turn mid run into a wolf, then a toad and jump over a wall. Instead I have 4 second channel times interrupted by any form of damage. Not being able to upgrade the speed significantly is boring. Transforming back when taking damage is annoying. The rat is pretty useless. The frog’s leap almost adds nothing movement wise. The horse steers like a drunk oil tanker and you fall off when taking any damage. Summoning it takes a millennium. The spider adds pretty much nothing gameplay wise. I like the idea of the human form, but it would have been fun to somehow charm humans in that form. Currently its just: Shopping, but SLOW!Conclusion: It is a fun game, it had the potential to be amazing …

_childDocuments_.review: The best games in life, are genre-defining masterpieces in a category of their own. V Rising accomplishes this.I've recommended this game to friends that haven't played games in 10+ years and they have absolutely fallen in love with it. Having played nearly every game that exists within the scope of the Open World Survival game genre, V Rising finally accomplishes what they all set to do, in its own unique way. For one, this is the only Early Access Game that is nearly feature complete and you'd have no idea it was still in Early Access. Haven't ever encountered any bugs or gamebreaking issues, like you do with many, many others in the EA stage. The PvP is unique and skill-based, albeit does have level scaling so can make it difficult to beat higher level players. But when you're matching levels, it's very possible to 2v1 someone if you have a smart build and play well. The PvP can also be forgiving or hardcore, which is nice to have the option for in a game that's heavily focused on PvE.As far as PvE goes, the bosses are truly fun to beat and a challenge, without being overwhelmingly difficult. Each biome's art style has its own unique aspects and bosses to match the theme. You always feel like you're progressing without ever feeling like it's a slow grind. Overall, 10/10 and can't wait for full release. If you're on the fence, you won't regret it.
