_childDocuments_.review: I have been following the game for about a month. I wish I picked up the game the day it came out but due to circumstances I picked it up about 4 days after release.So far, the game is extremely satisfying. The top-down view isn't for everyone, but if you have experience with MOBAs or Diablo you'll enjoy the isometric style of game play.The survival aspect was a twist I wasn't expecting to be handled well, but it actually works. Most survival games the day is your friend, makes life easy. In this game... CURSE THE SUN! THE DAY IS MY ENEMY!Progression: You are a nobody starving vampy, and you gotta craft basic gear, then unlock technology to give yourself better gear. There is a 'gear score' system which determines your player level. You gotta kill bosses to unlock certain crafting stations and abilities which is the only real wall in your progression. You get one 'movement' ability, 2 regular spell-like abilities with one ultimate spell ability, plus whatever abilities granted by your weapon type you have equipped.  Seven total abilities max (when you have a 3-ability weapon which is determined by the material used to craft it, Iron at a minimum). This is the sum of your 'abilities', and it is simple but elegant, because most of the bosses you kill give you new ones that you can pick and choose at your whim. You are also not locked into your choice, and may switch them, so long as you are out of combat. For base building, thematically starting from nothing and then building my castle in the wilderness feels really fulfilling. I do have to stress picking a good location to build your base, and consider where you put your heart as this has ramifications in PVP and decorating (didn't really think those two would correlate but they do). The downside is that you don't truly get to experience the entirety of your customization options until you finish the last objective/beat all of the bosses (aside from DLC stuff, which I have not purchased).The hunger mechanic... maintaining your blood pool so you don't starve is pretty important. That's the straight forward part of the hunger mechanic, but there's more.You're a vampire, so you gotta drink blood from things to stay alive. If you are hungry any blood will do, but if you want certain abilities... well, each creature in the game has a type of blood, and a quality to it. The type determines a set of bonuses unique to the type... such as 'creature' or 'brawler', or 'rogue'. You can imagine the type of blood provides unique bonuses... and most of the abilities are pretty straight forward if you are used to RPGs. The quality determines how many of the bonuses to your character you receive... and let me tell you 100% blood types are rare (almost 70 hours in and I've only seen two 100% blood types, one rogue and one warrior), but they're the only ones that grant you the full power of a blood type, at 100% you get a % increase to all bonuses of the blood type.However, if you get hurt and you don't have a way to heal, you may spend your hunger pool to heal your character.... This leads to some painful decisions early on when you are not used to the attacks of the mobs you are fighting... spending your blood pool to heal versus having increased damage and movement speed, etc... I think it's quite balanced. Later on when you know how to move around and stuff, you realize using potions to heal is ideal to losing your blood type bonuses. This is somewhat related to the blood mechanic, but in the main tutorial quest-line later on you'll be able to get vampire servants from enchanting your victims, taking them home, and putting them into servant coffins to make into thralls. The higher % of blood you turn into servants, the more benefits they reap you when you make them work for you. You should try to get more servants as the passive benefit of getting materials you need is extremely useful.The 'first' thing, which I list as the last thing is discovering stuff in your game world, the 'research' or 'technology' found in games like Conan: Exiles or Ark isn't locked by level, but merely by your research material. Sometimes random mobs drop tech in book form, which you may turn in at your relevant research desk/study/etc... If not, you need to collect paper/scrolls to turn in, which will give you one 'random' research.  You should always turn in books first, then use the paper/scrolls, as you don't want to accidentally discover a tech before you use the book. If you already have a piece of research unlocked, throw your book in the Devourer for spare paper/scrolls... you'll know what I am talking about.TL;DR Vampire game fun. Suck the blood, damn the sun, make castle big and elegant. Kill all the bosses.Would recommend for a buy of the base game. It's worth it, and I don't feel an urge to buy the DLC. I also rent a 10 man server and we all split it for $15, which we haven't even hit our first month yet.

_childDocuments_.review: A great survival game with Moba-like combat and a solid aesthetic. Leans more towards the survival Rust feel than Valheim. Well worth the price.The sunlight mechanic is terrifying and I love it.Some of the V Blood targets have had really fun mechanics/phases so far, and the way multiplayer allows you to hunt down V Blood targets together and everyone benefits from the unlocks is also great. It's a shame the loot is shared though...I think some main-quest progression requirements could be made a little clearer as there's a few stages where it's like "Make this thing! You need X material, but it's only made by the thing you can't make yet so you're gonna have to raid camps and hope it drops!".Only in T2 at the time of this review but the current game loop feels like it's lacking a little fun loot feel, needs more "Ooo a shiny research book/schematic/furniture/skin" to change things up between raiding for iron, hearts and scrolls.I also think it'd be great if you could craft using materials that are in your castle's storage. A few small QoL improvements like this would really polish up the game nicely.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game on Brutal, PVE, with a friend. We are halfway through the second act. I'll update the review if any of my opinions change.Challenging and fun bosses. Many survival crafter games front load their challenge, and then after you have your base and needs met, it turns into a grind-fest. This game balances that near perfectly. The challenges ramp up well and I'm not getting bored with the grinding, thanks to mechanics like thralls. I'm always excited to beat the next boss and unlock new materials and abilities that we need to keep progressing.Any complaints I have are minor nitpicks. A few parts of the game are very dialed in, primarily (I think) because of the PVP aspect of the game. There are times where I wish I had more freedom of movement on the map...you are never going to weasel your way in or out of a place...you either can or can't. Same with building. Lots of building games you can get kinda janky with it...which, oddly, can be fun. Sometimes I wonder...can't I just build the balcony out over...nope, no go. Its either acceptable placement or not. Also, fishing is just unfun. You can't do it passively (well, your thralls can, but not you personally) nor is it very active. Sometimes its just 15 seconds of sitting, followed by running to the next fish spot, then sit, then run, then sit. I wish it was fully inactive or fully active, instead of occupying this weird middle ground. Inventory management is GOOD but could be better. As far as I can tell, there is no "lock" feature to keep items in your inventory. e.g. I wanted those flowers, but they sorted into the chest automatically. I also would sometimes appreciate a way to lock items OUT of my inventory, e.g. I am farming iron, but I keep having to throw fiber on the ground to clear space in my inventory.Again, despite taking up more space in my review, these are MINOR nitpicks. If we had stars, I would  give it 4.8/5. Top tier gaming experience so far!

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhere i read that this was like Valhiem meets Masquerade. That is kinda spot on. As most EA games go, this one is very polished for this stage. The crafting seems pretty in depth and they said they plan on adding more, they building is pretty straight forward and easy to do. They just need to add some more tool tips when you have to hunt down V blood for recipes. Most recent hotfix helps with that.For the price you will definitely get your value out of it.OK: Now after 60+ hours i can say that this game is a must buy. The progression system is tied to crafting and hunting creatures with special blood. Very unique and fun aspect!The clan system allows you to completely share resources, benches, research and basically everything but a coffin!The building is a lot more in depth than I originally thought. As you play and unlock more items, I found myself making more rooms and redesigning my castle to accomodate. (again because vblood are item level locked for preview from the altar, you cant plan everything ahead)I have yet to PVP, but feel it has a turn of the millenia Ultimate Online vibe. (think Albion) You cant teleport if you are holding materials, so you have to risk teh run back to base.As far as servers go, you can adjust a lot. Like Ark, you can set a single player experience to give more resources, NPCs have half health and you cstart with lvl 30 gear. Just as examples.This is one of the few games that made me stay up till 3am because I kept uncovering more fun stuff!

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is fast paced and quite fun. Lots of variation with the weapon skills and magic skills. The building and aesthetics of the game are both excellent and require a bit of forethought. I do wish I could pitch the camera up just a little bit more as I find myself staring at the top of my screen most of the time while I'm travelling. The progression feels slightly grindy but it's completely configurable and even using the defaults I enjoy working for my progression. Oh and sunlight. Dodging the sun by jumping between shadows is actually quite fun and adds a new spice to combat when you're fighting during the day. I feel so much stronger at night because I don't have to keep out of sun spots that'll quickly fry you.I only have a complaint or two around the inventory management. I wish I could specify the exact amount I want when I split. The quick split is nice and I appreciate having it but sometimes I only want 8 planks from my chest. I shouldn't have to split stack of 200 8 times and send the rest back. My last inventory desire is if there was a quick stack to fill an existing stack but not move more than that. I keep a stack of wood, fibre, rocks, hide, etc in my chests and the rest get refined. I end up filling up with a ton of extra stacks when I just wanted a quick inventory dump to move the smaller stacks of stuff like the gems, plants, whetstone and paper.All and all it most definitely doesn't feel like an early access game and with friends I could see this being pretty damn fun.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game.A great game that is. This title doesn't follow any kind of structured linear story-line, but does reveal itself through killing bosses in different acts. Game play is solid with top down combat that mixes in melee and ranged physical attacks and a combination of different weapon abilities and spells. There are now different armor sets that will influence your stats in different ways that will impact your preferred play style. Music is fitting, but not anything ground breaking, and writing and dialogue is somewhat limited outside of your interactions with bosses and emotes that you can do.The game play loop is satisfying. It mixes in some very light survival-esq mechanics in terms of gathering and building and this in turn influences the ability to craft and alter equipment and weapons which make you more powerful. Building up your castle, your main headquarters so to speak, grants you more recipes to craft different things which allow you to explore further into the world, opening up new enemies, items, and fast travel. The 1.0 release introduces new armor varieties which have different stats. This really opened things up in terms of combat because now you can focus on different play styles like crit, spells, and weaponskills. The game builds on top of itself in a slow, methodical, and precise way. There is a gradual and satisfying increase to your power and reach as you unlock new recipes and defeat different enemies and bosses which opens up more of the world. Bosses and enemies are great, and there wasn't any that stood out as not designed well or unfair, in 1.0 that is. Previously the final bosses in the game, specifically Adam, were intended to fight with multiple players, which can really make solo or duo co-op players feel left out as that particular boss can be brutal. Balancing is better in the full release so this isn't as much of an issue, as myself and my co-op friend we're able to complete the game and all of it's bosses in it's entirety, although the actual final boss is pretty brutal. Music is there within the game, but isn't anything that stood out. I can't speak any further on it as it didn't move me to tears or anything. The writing and dialogue is sparse, but very fitting for the characters and world setting. Much of the story can be explained in the quips that come from their fights and the comments they make. In terms of technical issues, I encountered no major bugs or glitches that impacted my mechanical or visual play through, so objectively speaking it was a flawless experience. Final thoughts:Ultimately, I ended up spending way more time in this game than I thought I ever would. I bought this on a whim based on a random recommendation from a friend, with no real investment outside of that. This quickly become one of my most played games in 2023. It's a great experience, with a solid progression system, good game play loop, satisfying boss fights, and a straightforward building system that can lead to some very impressive castle showcases. I can recommend picking up this title at any price, final rating: 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I'm not sure where all the 'hate' is coming from and the mixed reviews. Maybe they were playing pre-early access and the game had more issues. My experience thus far playing a few hours on release has been very smooth and the game is super fun. No real bugs so far. Running a 3080Ti @4K and it's consistently 70+ fps. It's definitely already worth the $20. I'll be playing with a group of friends for sure.It's got a Valheim meets Path of Exile meets Diablo vibe, but certainly has it's own unique character and gameplay. I like the progression--similar to Valheim with making different specialized workstations and gathering resources in different tiers. The game will make you work, make you explore, make you fight and hunt specific people or creatures to progress, but it doesn't feel too limiting or linear. The building is solid. The structures and designs are beautiful. Mechanics are intuitive and smooth. Feels snappy like Valheim with a few little things they could improve. Combat is a little basic atm, but I think that's more due to my level and limited skills, etc. Using specials livens things up. The hotkeys are intuitive and responsive. Your basic skill set starting out is dynamic enough to not be boring, but after a couple hours I'm looking forward to introducing new moves to my repertoire. Environments and atmospheric elements are amazing so far. Feels pretty rich. I'm excited to see other 'biomes' and villages/towns. I've never been a huge fan of Vampire themes, but I'm already a fan of this game with how they've combined different genres and ideas into something special. Early-access, only $20, and just a few hours into the game, I'd give it an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: + Decent combat system+ Nice building system+ Good graphics and the whole atmosphere is very pleasant+ The world looks alive since NPC fractions are constantly moving and interacting with each other- No way to bind skills to ctrl + button is ridiculous- Character movement speed is so low that makes you think about him as a disabled person, not a vampire- Castle core can not be moved, castle can not have 2 cores even if you can build them - which breaks the good impression about the building system- Standard settings don't allow to teleport with resources, so you spend a lot of time just running- Standard settings make you take damage from the sun, thus 50% of the game you are just standing afk waiting for the night- Bosses will run back and heal to 100% at any random moment. _childDocuments_.review: the game is really very fun but some issues do irk me. mainly the very very slow speed of crafting which really stagger the abillity to build up a base which would otherwise be much funner. the long feeling cooldown on the dodge move which in a regular dungeon crawler like diablo or torchlight wouldn't matter as you are expected to tank hits to a degree but in this case with the wide attack arcs and fairly high damage makes smart play feel really slow, would also love the abillity to equip more than 2 spells and an ult.both of those complaints are derived from the game's design around servers and online survival games which really it is more related to something like Rust or even Project Zomboid than it is to something like Torchlight, so complaining about the solo play experience is kind of unfair on that front. that being said, obviously crafting timers dont tick when you are not in the game which made it so i just AFKd in my box for like an hour to get some resources to help build up my base. the world settings are quite extensive so alot of this is adjustable but the default is a VERY slow game which will likely be the introduction until a player goes to the settings and starts adjusting their solo world. this is a survival game, not a looter really.the core is SUPER solid, i strongly recommend this game. it has alot of room to grow but im enjoying it quite alot until then.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this game is fun but also aggravating as hell due to random game mechanics. I've only played PVE so far on a private server so have no comment on PVP-related interactions. Overall building/crafting mechanics are interesting. Base building leaves a little to be desired with square/based mechanics; at least Conan you have angled pieces. I think they try to make this up with lots of decorations, but meh. Nothing can compete with Valheim's base building unfortunately (despite it tanking performance and that game itself being abandonware). Combat is pretty interesting; feels like a mix of Diablo and Demon Souls a bit. Overall fun but some fights/creatures will aggravate the hell out of you due to perceived balancing issues at the moment. Having your horse get stuck on seemingly nothing frequently, having to turn completely around back out because you're 1 pixel too close to a tree root and then resume your course (which when being chased means you get hit several times and sometimes die). Horse mechanics in general feel clunky/slow and kind of annoying to use. Feels like driving a large boat.The flame archers are way overpowered for their gear level. Absolutely ridiculous damage is taken from these things, it does more damage than many bosses AOE attacks around the same level. Yes you can dodge it fairly easily or dash out of the damage zone, but it still seems oddly overpowered. Gear level assessment seems to have no correlation with unit strength. I've had my lvl 66 vampire get his ass handed to him by units that are in the 50's in gear level, then later will steamroll through lvl 65+ units. I think the algorithm for determining overall gear level/strength of the unit needs adjustment as I'm finding it is not helpful in determining what/who I can fight I just have to try fighting everything and remember who is actually strong.Field of view. Ok I know this is a top-down game, but I still feel like my visibility is handicapped because of this. Running full speed on a speed 11 horse feels like driving 150 mph on suburban streets I have almost no time to make turns. I am getting better but routinely just run into trees or rocks trying to make a turn and have to back out and try again. In general non-horse movement feels similar - I never experienced this feeling playing Diablo or other top-down games but this one just makes me feel like I can't see enough.Some boss fights are borderline impossible to solo; yes I'm sure you can beat them with enough practice but get ready to swear a lot. It's been a while since I've had a game aggravate me to the point of rage quitting but this one has nailed that mechanic. This game will 100% piss you off sometimes. If a boss is difficult, have a buddy join to help - it makes the game significantly easier. Overall seems like a promising title that will be fun with more done with the platform and more balancing. I offer the critique above as I'd like to see those areas improved.

_childDocuments_.review: I keep forgetting this is still early access! It's quite realized already and very fun.I love all the forms you can take, the various vampire folklore nods and the ability to customise your playstyle with all the powers and weapons. I play solo PvE and the bosses are often a bit of a challenge, which I enjoy.However, I do feel like when I'm done maxing out my gear and when I kill the last boss, the game is going to lose the replayability for me. I might spend some extra time redecorating my castle, and that's it. I hope the final version will have more areas to explore, more bosses to kill and more stuff to unlock. The servant missions are insanely long - it could be understandable if it was just real world time, but they take 24 hours of in-game time. Also, each gear level only has one type of armor - it'd be great to have multiple options to choose from, like with every other aspect of your equipment.And my last, very personal complaint is that I was very excited to unlock toad form, but it doesn't really do anything and that's a bummer. I wish it could at least jump up a hill, or do tongue attacks, or croak, or anything.Those complaints aside, I still find this game very fun and I do reccomend it

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game kind of blind with no context other than it just kind of looked cool from the pictures. After sinking 20-30 hours into it so far, I can say this is honestly a great game and a breath of fresh air! I'm currently taking my time going through a "Normal" play through, exploring everything, taking on every boss at a comfortable rate. A few bosses I've admittedly asked for help with, but that's fine. There are a few different ways to play this game. You can absolutely play solo if you want. You can join a clan (though I haven't figured out how), and you can also play on a pvp server (which I'll try out down the road, probably after a 2nd play through). The bosses can be very challenging, and from what I've heard, the last boss may be overtuned, though I can't comment on that yet.. Haven't been there. There are plenty of youtube guides on every boss, so if you're stuck, there's usually a strategy out there that could probably work for you. I've found that there are a couple bosses you can very easily cheese your way through first try just because of how their mechanics work paired with the environment in which you fight them in.If I had one complaint, it's honestly the music. I don't play games at a particularly high volume. I can clearly hear everything as far as combat, voice dialog, and sound fx, but for whatever reason, the music is super low.. and I honestly didn't even know there was music in the game until about 12 hours in when I was playing at night while it was quiet and I sort of heard something while standing in my castle while I was doing something out of game. After turning it up a little more, I listened for a few minutes. It's nice and moody, but it could use some adjusting. But, that's an ultra-minor complaint.Pros:+Challenging Bosses that all have relatively fun mechanics to learn+Castle Building is incredibly rich with decorations and mechanics to improve crafting efficiency. (Don't get too hung up on your first castle, you'll most likely end up moving it later anyway)+Combat is simple with 2-3 spells from a pool of around 40 spells which can be made more powerful with a range of gems. Spells and weapons are hot swappable at anytime. With average cooldowns being 6-8 seconds.+Best vampire themed game since Vampire - The Masquarade: Bloodlines+No EXP grind. EXP is not a thing in this game. Gear score dictates your power which may or may not be ok for some people.+Crafting is pretty simple. Most things being unlocked from simple boss kill progression.+PVP is optional.+There are ZERO MICROTRANSACTIONS. You bought the game, you got the game. There's some castle building cosmetic dlc's, but they're completely optional and don't alter anything other than cosmetics.Cons:-Challenging bosses may be 'too' challenging for some. I've seen some people spend a few hours on one boss because they didn't want to ask for help.-Travel can feel slow for a while. If someone is able to cheese you through the Styx fight to gain Bat Form, it is an absolute game changer for travel and makes everything else more enjoyable.-Resource heavy game. To be fair, it is a crafting game. You'll need to farm a lot of resources to continue progressing through and building better gear. There's times where it's fine, but other times it feels like a chore. Thankfully, you can subdue humans to become your servants and send them on missions to mitigate this minor annoyance.-Music volume is very low even with music volume slider being at full.-Tutorial takes you far, but does not fully explain things as you unlock them. You may be alt/tabbing a lot, reading their wiki for more context a lot of stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've played this year.  I was surprised at how good it was.  The environments, exploration, combat, bosses, base building, etc.  The base building is intuitive and polished.  The blood mechanic is interesting and unique.  I found the bosses to be fairly challenging.  The progression system for gear and base building relies on your boss progress.  You kill a boss, you get the ability to craft new things (and thus new gear at certain points).  After over 100 hours, there's still things I haven't done in the game such as finding all endgame weapons and raiding.  But I can definitely recommend this game to those who like survival / build games.  There's a lot more to this game than I initially thought and is well worth it for the price if you stick with it.

_childDocuments_.review: By far the best survival crafting game on the market, and it's not even close. Much like Stunlock's previous game, Battlerite, a moba-esque pvp arena, the combat is exceptional and well balanced, and where the game shines most whether you play pve or pvp. If you're a gamer and want a good challenge, play brutal, it's a blast, and often times requires you to rethink your strategy and prepare/practice fights. There are many, varied and viable ways to play the game which gives it great replay value.The survival elements serve their purpose and are good. Not amazing, not bad. The progression feels good. The most tedious thing, and it really isn't too terrible, is grinding research so you can unlock your consumables and weapons/armor. The base building is really fun and you can do some really beautiful things, I've seen countless castles that people have poured hours into and it really pays off.The game is really designed for pvp and it shows sometimes ( the endgame rift incursions can get crowded sometimes on pve, not a huge deal), but you can pick pve and still have the time of your life. If you go that route, I'd look for a server with no wipes as wipes are kind of pointless on a pve server.100%ing this game and nabbing all the achievements has been one of my favorite gaming experiences in a long time. I hope it continues to receive support. Stunlock has a tendency to produce games with phenomenal gameplay and systems, but move on to the next project and abandon them years later. It is what it is.Having played countless games in this mix of genres, this game stands on top. Endgame pve content is incredibly satisfying and fulfilling, Solarus, Adam, Dracula, all well designed and fun to beat.

_childDocuments_.review: I am currently at my first base and got like eight or so boss NPCs down. So pretty much still at the start.Thats my resume so far:Pros:- The combat. It feels so natural. After some time adjusting to the controlls it felt very good.- Worldscale. The map seems big at first which it is but you can soon travel reasonable distances in good time. Given you dont get sidetracked.^^- Basebuilding. Also took some adjustment but then it just clicked and it is very satisfying to unlock new pieces and I even did some cosmetic stuff which realy amped up the base.- Character power. You are not just a beefed up vampire lord and can kill everything. You have to earn your power by defeating bosses, doing quests, crafting better gear and fighting smart. After you did so you feel stronger instantly.- Grafic. I liked the Vallheim grafics but they were a bit too chunky for me so this just the right amount of more quality added. You got your glowy eyes but thats it with fancy stuff. The colours dull. Like the night you live in. Even the snow areas have that slight little dirty touch to it.Cons:- learning courve. You have to plan your moves and have a strategy when facing bosses or even bigger camps of foes. For some thats a positive thing for others it might be frustrating to have to run from a boss to start it new.- Its not necessary for fortnite-player. The pacing is slower. (a pro for me)- Tracking. Once you start to track a boss it can be irritating on how long you have to travvel to get to it. You get used to it and kinda expect the boss to be in certain areas. At first I got irritated from that.I probably would not play it alone. Currently playing it with three friends and we all realy enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a little late to the party, but it's the best party I've been to in a long time. TLDR - This game is amazing, period, let alone as an early-access title. It offers and engaging and generous amount of content (100+ hours) to enjoy solo or with friends, even if top-down, survival or sandbox games appeal to you. I clocked 18 hours on this game during my first two days of owning it, which apparently, isn't uncommon. The marketing for it doesn't really do any justice, hence why it took me so long to actually get it.  But IMO there's something for everyone here. Do you wanna immerse yourself in a beautifully designed environment, enjoy a thematically rich adventure as a lone vampire, building strength to defeat challenging foe, take helpless people prisoner, charm enemies and SHAPE SHIFT? You can.Do you wanna chill out and seek the perfect spot to construct an ominous and aesthetically pleasing gothic castle, unlocking designs and furniture to perfect your home/dungeon. You can.Do you wanna enjoy all of that with friends? Or perhaps while meeting new people on a PvE server. Or more competitively on the PvP servers? Absolutely can.This game is like Rust meets Diablo. But becomes entirely it's own through it's charm. And for those that LOATH the camera angle  in V Rising. (Because I've seen that as the main complaint) The community has got you. There are some very popular mods, namely, the camera mod that allows you to shift the angle more than default game mechanics allow and even let you experience it all first person. Which gives the game a Skyrim feel in most circumstances. I hope they continue to create content for this game and bring in more players. There is HUGE potential here. And for the $30 price tag WELL worth the buy.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: The Format of the game is an open world survival action rpg with a goal of reclaiming your rightfully owned places from the last boss of the game. The game has a good balance of Survival through the creation of your castle and combat that complements the open world.If you played Battlerite, then the combat will feel right at home but if not. Let's just say that it is engaging enough to make me actively look for hard foes to test my skills.The progression is semi-linear like Terraria where you choose which target to pursue with the goal of fighting the very last boss. And the game revolves around these core mechanics. You gain skill points by killing them and you get to choose in a set Tier which skill to unlock, allowing for a flexible build early in the game and throughout your gameplay. Getting these targets is also the way to unlock certain crafting recipes and tools to further empowers you gear or to make your Castle more better. Most bosses in the game will be in set places that make sense (eg. early boss that is a bomber can be found in a quarry) and so on. It is thematically correct and cohesive story wise. But other boss also roams and can be accidentally meet on the road and such, making for a dynamic world to play.Now talking about the bosses, they themselves are pack with cool mechanics that make you quick to your feet. All of projectiles in the game are non-homing so it gets to a point of just playing dodgeball with an enemy. Almost all of them have unique mechanics that sets them apart to each other. Making the encounter fun.There is more to talk about but all in all I will say is that this game is perfect for solo, co-op, or pvp centric players to get.

_childDocuments_.review: V Rising‘s gameplay is what you’ll get when you mesh Valheim‘s survival gameplay together with top-down ARPGs like Diablo. The early game is harsh. My vampire was still weak from the years of inactivity, and there’s a lot of survival stuff that needs to be done, such as hunting enemies for crafting materials and building my own castle. Combat animations might look slightly janky at times, but the controls are fluid and fun. Castle building is pretty cool and reminds me a lot of The Sims. The game has a lot of potential, with a solid concept and interesting gameplay..
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: On the surface this game seems like a new change for the survival crafting genre. Looking at the game more deeply the more it takes away from the fun that it can achieve. While I was only on a PvE server, due to trying it out, I spent longer than 2 hours looking for a place to call my base and there was not one spot to even put down just a Heart. Every time that I approached a flat hilltop it was blocked off due to someone wanting control of that whole hilltop. If you want to try this game out for yourself. Try it with co-op and not online because if you do it will take its full potential that people are expecting and flush it down the toilet.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: No offline solo play, must always have an internet connection to play and therefor no way to pause at all. Constant stuttering especially in combat. Only played an hour and already had to grind like crazy to build basic things. For curiosities sake, I went and watched a streamer who had played over 20 or so hours and the grind was even worse. Mobile timer mechanics that artificially lengthen game time. I won't be surprised when they start selling microtransactions to make those timers disappear, just like a mobile game. There is literally zero need for them in this game other than preparing for payments to remove them.All that means a big no from me.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: AVOID AVOID AVOIDrubbish game, I get thematically that vampires cannot be out in daylight, but there is nothing you can do to advance day time, and nothing to do during daytime, so its just an arbitrary wait or a game of hop the shadows, every time the sun rises.add to this boss fights that allow the boss to re-heal way too quickly, imagine waiting outside a camp until sunset, you work your way in picking off all the bandits, you finally meet the boss, you whittle down the bounties health to almost none and some poxy vampire hunter rocks up just at the critical moment, you retreat and they chase you into the woods, you kill them make your way back to the edge of camp, and the sunrises, cue another 15 to 20mins sitting in the shade waiting to repeat the whole thing over again.dull, tedious, boring rotten game, total waste of money.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic.  I am not a big fan of hard boss fights, but the combat is so responsive I feel like when I am killed it was because of my mistakes and not mechanic BS.  The progression in the game is extremely addicting, constantly teasing you with the next tier of gear or ingredients and keeps you moving through the areas of the huge map.When it comes to moving around, the various forms are really great, and the scattered teleporters not allowing for transportation of certain items forces you to run where you need to go (you can always steal a horse if they are around which is also fun).There is no real story in the game so far, I get the original focus of this game was PvP and everything else around it is dressing.. but some more story would have been nice for us PvE players.  This gave me big Legacy of Kain vibes, but not having the nice narration from the character  when he reaches important locations was a bit of a letdown.This game has me hooked.  I am really looking forward to updates and hope the game is a success and devs can keep adding content like No Man's Sky has been doing.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: V Rising even in early release manages to hit a pleasing balance between hack'n slash, exploration, and castle building, resulting in a game that keeps pulling me in any time of day ! (Though I happen to have a lot of free time on my hands which explains my fairly quick progress through the game).I also never really feel hitting a wall - should I be blocked in a situation, there is always a way to solve the issue especially when dealing with bosses. Maybe you need to consider other spells and weapons. Maybe you should upgrade your gear ? Is that enemy really necessary to face right now ?My only critic would be regarding the lack of lore - the bit we do have only leaves us eager for more... That being said, it is still an in development game.I generally am cautious around early releases, but this one has definitly proven worthy of the investment.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: "V Rising" presents a captivating blend of action, strategy, and survival set in a dark fantasy world where players embody the role of a vampire lord seeking dominance. It's a game that immerses players into a realm teeming with danger, where every decision made can either elevate or jeopardize their quest for supremacy.At its core, "V Rising" revolves around the player's endeavor to construct and expand their own castle, a stronghold that serves as both a sanctuary and a symbol of power. This aspect of the game introduces elements of city-building and resource management, requiring players to carefully allocate resources, construct buildings, and fortify defenses to fend off threats from rival vampires and other hostile entities that roam the land.One of the most intriguing aspects of "V Rising" lies in its interpretation of vampire lore. Players are thrust into the role of a vampire lord, endowed with supernatural abilities and an insatiable thirst for blood. This premise opens up a wealth of gameplay possibilities, from hunting unsuspecting prey under the cover of night to commanding legions of undead minions to carry out their bidding.The game's mechanics offer a delicate balance between solo and multiplayer experiences. While players can chart their own path through the game's vast, procedurally generated world, there are also opportunities for collaboration or conflict with other players. Whether forming alliances to tackle formidable foes or engaging in PvP skirmishes to assert dominance, the multiplayer aspect adds depth and unpredictability to the gameplay experience.Visually, "V Rising" impresses with its detailed environments, atmospheric lighting, and meticulously designed characters and creatures. The world feels alive, brimming with untold secrets waiting to be uncovered and challenges waiting to be overcome. From lush forests to desolate wastelands, each area exudes its own distinct ambiance, further immersing players in the game's dark and foreboding atmosphere.However, despite its many strengths, "V Rising" is not without its flaws. Some players may find the game's progression to be slow-paced, particularly in the early stages where resource gathering and base-building activities dominate gameplay. Additionally, there may be balancing issues or technical glitches that detract from the overall experience, requiring further refinement and optimization by the development team.In conclusion, "V Rising" shows considerable promise as an innovative addition to the survival strategy genre. Its unique take on vampire lore, coupled with its engaging gameplay mechanics and immersive world-building, sets it apart from other titles in the genre. With continued updates and improvements, "V Rising" has the potential to captivate players and establish itself as a standout title in the gaming landscape.**Rating: 8/10**

_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Hear me out: it's got the exact feel of Valheim, where you're exploring, building your base up from scratch, and slowly working your way up through types of materials by beating bosses and learning new ideas/researches/recipes. You start with ugly wooden palisades, and then you're working your way up to being able to mark up rooms, multiple floors, enormous gothic statues, and a blood rose field of flowers. Also horses. I haven't gotten to the horses, but there are horses, and I am ECSTATIC.The Palworld bit comes from the servants mechanic. You grow your army and your personal servants, who will autonomously go off and get things for you. You're not catching things a la Pokemon, lol, but the autonomization is what I'm thinking of here.Also, Diablo, for the camera angles.Despite not being a cozy game, it is a game I've been playing on my SteamDeck in my soft, cozy rocking chair, working toward getting the castle of my dreams. I'm digging it SO MUCH. My castle's an absolute mess, but I just moved it, which honestly is a REALLY cool mechanic. The spot I picked wasn't great, honestly, but it'll get the job done till I move again and find a better spot. The fact that you can just move your castle heart and have all of the items kind of pop into a UI thing for placing down without having to worry about tearing your base down, or destroying anything you don't want to destroy. It's really great.Originally, I was kind of amused that all of the DLC is just vanity stuff for your castle... but I get it. I totally get it now. I've seen the Castle Tour videos.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: After 147 hours of play time I finally set this game down. My hat is off to the developers for making such an enjoyable game. The final boss, Solaris, had me pulling my hair out when I died on the 30th try. (Use a fire resistance potion) The combat was extremely fair and every part of the game can be accomplished if you are a solo player, it just takes a lot of practice. After beating V Rising, I continued to perfect my castle and gear up my servants. Once everything was to my satisfaction, I felt comfortable enough to move on. You know its a good game when you have a hard time saying goodbye. However, I have left with a sense of accomplishment and felt at peace jumping into my coffin for the last time. Thanks for the awesome journey, this game was my "go-to" for the summer of 2022. Looking forward to more in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I played this for the first time with the 1.0 release and had a great time with it. I played solo pve, and didn't have any interest in pvp.Pros:Combat feels really fun.Tons of bosses, each unlocking something new.Easy understanding of your next goal as you make progress.Build a cool castle, decorate it as much as you feel like.Many customization options for the difficulty, crafting, and building.Slight cons:I would have preferred a bit more forgiving default options like teleport with materials and faster refining without making changes.  But it's not that big of a problem, they give you the freedom to edit whatever you want in the settings.Overall I enjoyed my experience a lot.  Definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: After 100+ hours in this game, I managed to beat all the bosses, made the bloodkey, and finished the game with all 3 soul shards. Built 2 castles with 250 tiles maxed each, designed, etc. rare servants strong weapons. Everything there was to be offered, I explored.So how was the experience? Bit grindy I must say, but it was a pleasure. The crafting was tough, specifically getting the scourge stones for dark silver. I ended up putting my workers to gather the scourge stones mainly, but eh. The game itself was insanely fun, with each boss fight feeling unique. I spent 9 hours on the gonecrusher or whatever his name is. 9 hours of constant defeat until i realized that you can just use a reaper to go invis everytime he does his ult to buy precious time.The atmosphere of this game was my favorite however. With the ability to not teleport with items, it forces you to go out and explore the map, coming across cool things such as rock golems and tree ents or what they are called. wild wolves that give you 100% creature along the way are a gem, giving you sun resistance if you need it.Each main boss fight, gone crusher, solarius, and winged horror was insanely challenging, specifically for me who decided to do this all solo. But it IS possible, with preparation. The soul shards you obtain are very good as well giving you a much-needed boost for fights. This is only early access too, and Im very impressed with it so far. It's not overwhelming and the game is plenty of fun. Unfortunately about the castle feature though. 1 story castle looks like poop from above in bat mode. But the devs also realized this and will release a multi-story castle feature in the future. I'm looking forward to everything the devs will have to add to the game. Money was well spent here. A more in-depth story would also be nice. It's clear that there is the foundation to some lore here. All we can hope is that this game goes well.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd call it another Valheim in that it's similar in genre and the fact that it's getting little/no updates, but it's not as good. I do not believe this game will go anywhere at all, for a game using assets from the EG store it's taking way too long for content updates. Not a bad game, but needs lots of work and more content to become fun. Hope the dev team proves me wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't been addicted to a game like V Rising in a long time. I am mostly a solo player but I do play with a friend when he is online, the experience solo and multi are both fantastic thus far. _childDocuments_.review: I can't classify this game too well, but a rogue-lite isometric adventure game just about sums it up. The environments are beautiful, everything has value and purpose, and there's even some end-game gear grinding potential for you MMO players.Not a huge fan of the PVP, as it's sort of just social engineering on a server or positioning correctly until one idiot gets caught out, but if it's happening early on in the game's progression and a server's lifespan, you can screw over the progression of other people and become a dominant server faction, so, there's a lot of motivation and consideration for it in early stages of the game.If they could find more ways to diversify that phase of the game with different abilities, or alternative gear, this would be a near perfect game.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: No PvE endgame experience and terrible community.Great game that is fun while it lasts in the PvE experience. After you defeat the final boss, there is literally nothing to do except redecorate your castle. But that gets a little old pretty quickly, especially considering it has no effect on gameplay, and there are no interactive aspects to it like in some life simulator like The Sims or Animal Crossing.The real endgame is supposed to be the PvP experience, and in theory it sounds really fun, with clans battling it out to raid each other for precious resources and powerful shards, but in practice it's a pretty lame griefing experience. I rolled on a brutal PvP server after beating the final boss on normal, and most of the experience has been griefing by gangs of high level players who seemingly have nothing better to do than harass "noobs" as soon as they come out of the starting area. I was literally camped outside my wooden palisades by a high level player for two hours. He stayed glued to my front door until I opened it, ran right in, and stole all of my low level loot. As a high level player, he has no use for low level materials, so he was doing it just for fun. I complained about it in general chat, and most people were sympathetic to the griefer, saying it's part of the game.So overall I would call the PvP experience in this game a petty crime simulator lol. After that I quit and moved on to the next game. So it was fun while I played on PvE, but because there's no endgame there I could not recommend buying any of the DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: There are many things I could say about how I feel this game could be better than it is.   Some of those things I expect to get addressed via updates over time.  Some not.Yet V Rising is probably the finest survival/crafting multiplayer game I've ever touched, and it scratches a deep itch I had for a vampire game I can "live in".The world design, bosses, NPCs, weapons and abilities all have been loved and cared for by the developers in ways that can be felt in the experience.   Not everything is viable in the PvP meta, but everything feels distinct and interesting.  The standard game balance is best if you embrace the vampire RP, prowl for quality blood at night, and take your time building up your castle.  Don't make the mistake of overlooking the incredible PvP that is available here.  It's not perfect, but it's not common to see a survival game with PvP so thoughtfully executed.   I hope V Rising becomes famous for it, and acts as a beacon to steady other game developers hands when they give this genre a shot.I'm looking forward to future updates, but I've incredibly satisfied with what I've already played.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty much what's advertised - Fight stuff, bulid a castle, gather all the things. _childDocuments_.review: Great PvE content feels meaningful and challenging. Base-building is fun, immersive, and satisfying in both graphical and accomplishment sense. Large map is great for PvP content and static waygates, dual coffin respawns, horses, and player-made waygates help keep it from feeling "too big" or overwhelming. Gear progression is quite balanced and rewarding, you don't feel too weak or too strong for content unless you are drastically over or under geared. Bosses have fun mechanics and provide challenging fights - there is a list you can pick and choose from instead of a linear progression which I really enjoy. Overall one of the top games in the genre for me, definitely try multiplayer if solo play hasn't been much fun for you - its quite different with friends/enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: I've gotten a good amount of fun out of this game, but it's still not even remotely close to being done. Devs did in fact improve a number of issues between early access and now- that's great. The game still has no replayability from the perspective of someone who has only done PVE. Gearing up requires little to no thought and each gear upgrade feels as though it looks the same as the last. Weapons are only vaguely visually distinct between upgrade tiers as well. Ability choice is largely the same between trees- two ranged moves, two defensives, 2 aoe options of some kind, a directional ult or a defensive one- but Chaos gives ignite and Blood gives leech! You don't notice any of that in the end. World exploration is better than it was in terms of world size, zones are either unremarkable or ugly, and flora variety as well as seed collecting is a terribly huge pain in the ass. Farming Stygian Shards is terrible, painful even. It's here in particular where mob variety feels at its absolute weakest. PVE basebuilding is pleasant enough, though you're left constantly hankering for more decorative options all game long. Unfortunately 30+ decoratives are locked behind needlessly expensive DLC(4 of them). In addition to this, once you do finally unlock all things decorative, I would describe a feeling of the game already being over. And even then, the last few available boss-locked placeables are so laughably unimaginative or far too late in their arrival that it hardly matters. Nearly level 90, everything long-since unlocked, my gear doesn't have a single good chroma tied to it, three bases built out of boredom- time to fight Dracula! It's the only good fight in the game. What would I change overall? Add more systems beyond the limited resource crafting we have. More decoratives is awesome but there aren't really any meaningful things to place them around in the end. Three different versions of the same desk rendering it's predecessor obsolete each time feels... questionable? And this happens several times. Make upgrading gear feel rewarding, and actually make decent looking sets with good visual variety. Increase the difficulty level across the board. Spend some time contributing to the basebuilding parts of the game even more, maybe even consider implementing a server option to allow people to connect bases that are already basically on top of each other. Add meaningful options for different building blocks, pillar designs, outer wall designs that are weathered or varied. Consider adding greater NPC variety- it sucks that none of them are really voiced. Not even shopkeeps? Anyways. Give it another couple of years, and if the studio hasn't abandoned it by then, maybe it'll legitimately be worth playing more than once.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting blend of top-down ARPG and Survival/Crafting. This game has more going for it than meets the eye, and does a good job of capturing some "Legacy of Kain" nostalgia while combining it with "Conan Exiles" levels of base-building and slave-breaking. I've not gotten far into the game as of yet (just enthralled my first human and am in the process of converting him into a bloodsucking minion,) but for a title that is still in Early Access, there's quite a lot to do. Definitely take a chance on this one if you can get it on sale.*Edited For Gloomrot*Wow. This game just got exponentially better. If the free Gloomrot expansion is any indicator, this dev deserves major praise for dedication and QOL improvements. They have made an already enjoyable title into one of the best survival/crafting games I have played in a long time. My hours played should reflect this. Granted, the new content spikes the difficulty significantly, but it also fleshes out the world of Vardoran to a level that really jives with my personal tastes. I am excited to see what the far eastern territory (still grayed out on the map) will eventually be, and I hope they continue to drop in more lore goodness. Seriously, what happened with Dracula?

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:- Combat is fun, interesting, and decently challenging. Enemies feel like they use actual tactics instead of just walking at you at attacking. Bosses can be pretty tough but can be overcome with practice and build choice.- The aesthetic is superb. I absolutely love the art style. It perfectly captures exactly what I want to see in a Vampire RPG. It's appropriately dark, but does so in a way that doesn't sacrifice visual clarity.- The building mechanics are fresh and interesting. I really like the concept of certain buildings receiving bonuses for being in a separate, designated room for their type. It gives you a mechanical reason not only to expand your castle, but also to organize it in a way that makes sense from a sort-of-roleplay point, too. You can still smash everything into one big room if you *really* want to, but you'll miss out on bonuses that make it more efficient to make separate rooms and organize. I love that it gives incentive on building something that feels more like a grand castle and not, like, a META base build in Rust. - Two "official" PvP modes as well as a PvE mode let you pick just how good you want it to hurt.- LOTS and LOTS of customization options built-in to server settings; gather rate, craft rate, and stack size are just parameter tweaks when setting up a server. There are PLENTY of other options to let you tailor a server exactly how you like.The Bad:-   It was a ping issue. Even then, that server was at around 160-180ms ping (I was playing with friends across the pond) and that was the only issue I noticed. I'd say the game handles higher latency very well! After moving to a low-ping server, the issue disappeared.- My BIGGEST complaint about the game is the random tech unlocks. It's not  since all the most important tech you gain by hunting down and killing bosses, but it's still very annoying to be stuck on a boss and farming research materials hoping for gear upgrades but getting every base decoration first. I would very much prefer being able to choose what to unlock, even if they increased research cost to balance it out.The Weird:-   This makes more sense as you progress, can't really explain why without spoilers.- Blood type and quality is FAR MORE IMPORTANT than it lets on. Certain types are useless at low quality but feel overpowered at high quality. For example, a good type at high quality will let you stomp a boss that you've been struggling with otherwise.  This one is still mostly true. The game could benefit very much from some sort of in-game info that gives more detail of how the blood mechanics work and how important it is. The balancing makes more sense now; some blood types are going to be better for you in the early game but others will outshine them as you get better gear, but early on you should care less about the type and more about the quality. Later on when you unlock more and better weapons and settle into a build, then the synergies with certain blood types becomes more apparent - and important.-   I'm taking this one back, mostly. The pacing can still feel out of whack when the first handful of missions only take a few minutes each and then you hit one that takes several hours. The thing is, those missions aren't  your progression - that comes from killing bosses. The missions are just to help you along in the early game, introduce features and mechanics, then later give you a nudge toward your next steps.Other Stuff: - Material requirements for the mid- to late-game items look daunting at first, but they're far easier than they look. You just need to explore to find the good spots and utilize game mechanics (Waygates, cave tunnels, servants) and it's not much of a grind at all.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good within the limited scope of what it does.However,1) It has ZERO potential for shenanigans. It's a very heavily regimented game, meaning that every little thing is tightly controlled and you can't use any abilities or mechanics in ways that the devs didn't predict and intentionally include. That means less exploits, which is good, but it also means no clever combos, no hilarious interactions, no spectacular fails, less replayability, and a lot less interesting mechanics. I believe the game would have benefited greatly from keeping players on a longer leash.2) There's nothing left to do once you've beaten Dracula, outside of PVP. Just raids on other players' castles, which are inconsequential anyway because if you've beaten the boss you already have everything you could want. The ONLY limited(depending on server settings) resource to fight over is the soul shards and they aren't that great, especially since they limit your shapeshifting and lock you into one ultimate ability.3) Some choices were made for the sake of increasing difficulty that do so in annoying, uninteresting ways. For example, one V Blood just has a damaging aura so wide that it stretches most of the way to maximum render distance and applies a permanent Chill effect. Slows you down by 25% and makes you vulnerable to freezing solid. No way to negate it or escape it without the boss leashing and resetting. Sure that increases the difficulty, but it's just not fun. There are always better, more interesting ways of increasing difficulty, even in "Brutal" mode.Overall it's worth checking out, but I certainly won't be playing it for much longer. (My listed playtime includes multiple early access playthroughs.)

_childDocuments_.review: Wouldn't recommend this for solo players, but can certainly see how fun it'd be with a few friends to go through once. Another title I wish there was something more then a yes/no recommend system since this really is divisive on some of its content. Even as frustrating as some of the fights were the game is still great and i'd like to see what they move on to next.Played on a self hosted server on brutal and it was a slog in almost every aspect. Boss difficulty is all over the place, with some being absolute pushovers and others in the same bracket as the pushovers taking 10+ attempts to down, Adam and Dracula both were like 2 and 3 hour fights respectively. The way aoes/danger zones are displayed is atrocious and often misleading, where you can either be in the circle and not take damage, or vice versa, just not a fun learning experience when the rules constantly change. Again though, with a group the fights are undoubtedly much easier since you can have more build variety.If you do plan on playing through this solo, at least on brutal, i'd recommend maxing all the resource generation/no limits to fast travel/craft time and tweaking the day/night cycle so you're not forced to wait times that are made for an online pvp focused game, it's way to long and arduous on default settings for a singleplayer playthrough. The progression and even the combat in the game felt really lacking(giving players another ability slot would have greatly increased variety imo, but i'm sure balance things on the pvp side), gear upgrades rarely felt impactful in a way where it was exciting to get upgrades, the exception for this would be trying new weapons and eventually getting the legendary variants with unique bonuses. The amount of RNG on jewels/and the randomly rolled weapons is absurd and some way to target craft/refine them should've been added. The blood system and capturing people is great, but what's not great is a 35% chance to brick a prisoner at 1-2% blood quality increases. Despite getting 7+ 95%+ scholar bloods I never got further then 98%, it is maddening that there aren't other ways to increase quality. Just so much of the game is built around the multiplayer pvp aspect that playing it for anything else you can see what was sacrificed to add in bloated playtime and inconveniences meant to create attrition. The castle building stuff is super dope for people that want to get creative, not something I personally had an interest in though.

_childDocuments_.review: The short: Gloomrot a decent continuation, but it's still a slow experience that's missing several key elements and still too reliant on RNG.Pros- Making your own Gothic Castles is awesome- The visuals are cool and atmospheric- The Boss fights are fun and creative- The healing system is, better, in that the game has one now- The animations are amusingly extraCons- The Player Character is still painfully slow- The Gloomrot update broke the Territory systemV Rising Still Needs: - Greatly Trim the cooldowns- A way to grow your character (leveling system?)- More appearance options (endgame characters tend to look identical) - Enough different Equipment to have more then one Build- The ability to equip more spellsThe Long:  This is an update to my review after playing the Gloomrot update.  The main issue remains that your Vampire is very, very, miserably slow.  This is a problem as the game frequently feels like a bullet hell, expecting you to manage many foes and projectiles at once.  In other words you have to take a lot of forced damage, which makes the clever boss battles feel cheap. This is not helped by the fact that your only dodge ability is on a criminally long cooldown.  In a hectic Diablo style game, no one wants to be waiting 7+ seconds for your only way to move semi-quickly to come off a timer.   In point of fact all the player ‘s cooldowns are way too long.   Dying while desperately waiting for one of only TWO spells your allowed to equip to be ready is very common.    I know some will say you get four spell slots, but that gets us into 'accurate, but misleading' territory.  You can equip two spells, one dodge and one ultimate.  While it's nice that we can pick what type of dodge we want, it's going to be used only one way 90% to 100% of the time.  And the ultimate Spells have such a massive cooldown that I tend to forget it exists.   So yeah, if you were hoping to be a Vamp Wizard, not so much.  It's ok Stunlock, really.  We have a big-ol keyboard fulla buttons, you can let use equip more at once without confusing us.  Healing is slightly improved and being able to modifying ones weapons and spells is nice, if highly limited.  That said the lack of any kind of leveling system still feels like a deliberate mistake.  Many is the time when you will die feeling like your too low level for the current area, which of course you are, always.   Now you can get better with better gear, but there isn’t very much of it.  Currently the largest problem is that all character builds will be near identical.  Gear dictates your stats almost exclusively and there’s very little of it.  Both stats and gear.  You can garner short term buffs from drinking blood, but the value of it is far too random.  Heck items  that raises your speed tend to do so by 4% to 7%.  Is that a joke?  You take the most languid Vampire ever to be; and buff their speed by less the a tenth!  How can anyone be expected to notice?  As if to rub this in, the base game harshly restricts fast travel.  Teleporters are spaced far apart and unevenly.  Heck, they can't even be used if you have resources in your inventory.  Never mind that an over-full inventory is one of the best reasons to want to fast travel.  Now you can get a horse not far into the game, and they're fast-er, but they control like, like, like something that's always running into walls or getting stuck in the geometry.My advice is build an actually leveling system for your ARPG and put right at the top under options ‘speed increase’.  Not a percentage, but flat values.  It will massively improve the play experience.

_childDocuments_.review: (NOTE: My review refers to the solo PVE experience, I haven't touched any of the PVP elements of the game.)V-Rising is an isometric, top-down game with some light RPG elements, a plethora of boss fights and base-building.In V-Rising, you experience life as a newly awakened vampire, hungry for powerful V-Blood and conquest across the land of Vardoran. You start a new game rising from a forgotten crypt and immediately start your journey by cleaving through skeletons, crafting basic gear and establishing your base. For players of games like Valheim, the progression will be somewhat familiar. Track down and kill bosses, known as V-Bloods, to extract their power and gain new crafting recipes and spell points to unlock new abilities. The progression system is an expansion on similar concepts as I believe the game has something like 70+ bosses, each with unique stategies and difficulty levels. The RPG element of the game is fantastic. There are a variety of weapons and spells allowing for a wide range of customising builds and playstyles. I personally favoured the whip and longbow with some healing and chaos magic for some DOT. Attribute increases are determined by your gear, which also determines your gear level. This is an overall level for your character; the higher your gear level, the more bosses you are able to face. Taking off your gear takes away your gear level. Base building is a delight. Create your own castle to your liking by going to a plot anywhere on the map and place your Castle Heart to claim it. Rooms can be customised and decorated with special floors and walls giving bonuses to particular crafting. For instance, a room surrounded by walls and a door with the Forge flooring gives a quicker crafting time for items within it and reduces the amount of resources required for recipes. The lighting and ambience is amazing, you can create whatever kind of vibe you want for your castle and the community has a lot of talented builders who make some really cool builds. You can even construct a prison to house any hapless humans who become ensared by your dominating gaze.Speaking of blood bags- er, I mean ... 'human beings', each mob in the world will have a Blood Type and a percentage attached to them. Consuming the blood of different mobs will grant different bonuses. For example, a Brute blood type will grant you life leech on hit, whereas a Rouge type will offer critical chance and movement speed, with higher percentages offering more bonuses. This encourages even more experimentation in builds, as well as incentivising going out to capture high blood type enemies and to also convert them into servants, able to go out into the world and bring back resources.As mentioned above, this game can be played in PVE or PVP. I have only ever played solo PVE but the game does have a lively PVP scene with clans and official servers. I can highly recommend this game based off the solo experience however, so don't feel like you have to experience the PVP side, although it does make this a different game (in a good way). Ultimately, I've had a hell of a time with V-Rising. It is in my opinion one of the best Vampire games out there. Highly recommend for anyone who has any experience in survival/crafting games or for those looking for a bit of an RPG boss rush.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game most wonderful! I was looking for a vampire pvp game and I got one! If you enjoyed diablo, sims, minecraft, poe, and those types of games, you will enjoy this one!! I will disclose now that I only played on the pve servers. Gameplay: After spending a good amount of time getting my vampire exactly how I wanted her (their customising area is so fun!!) I began my adventure!! Starting out, it was a little bit hard to understand how to survive, but you catch on quite quick! Mostly you avoid the sun, hop to shady areas and not engage more than you can handle. Next steps to progress in the game were easy to follow like who to tackle next, which area to explore next, etc. This game to me was relaxing with the right amount of adventure if you wanted it!! I enjoyed the pace of the game, and I can't wait to see more! Other players: If you like making fast friends, stick to the pve servers!! That's the only mode I played, and still got the action I was looking for with all the fun creatures and bosses to hunt. I thought this deserved pointing out, since the community is small right now, it's easy to make friends!! Bugs: I didn't encounter many bugs, and even when I did they didn't make or break the game they were very minor. Castle Customisation:I'm most excited to share with you about the castle customisation ... interior decorators - this one is for you!! I could play endlessly decorating my friend's houses and my own!! You have full control over the design of your castle, where walls go, carpets, tile, windows, you name it!! You get many furnishings, curtains and all sorts of fun stuff to work on. It seems more like and end game thing as you have to use resources to build your contents, but it's fun to farm a little bit and grab what you need. I should mention the material earned to farming ratio is sublime. I'll post a video soon on the decorating in V Rising!! DLC:The DLC was worth the purchase. I really like customising my characters and the dlc let me have features not everyone had. I especially liked the red 3 tailed wolf I could turn into :)Give this game a try and have fun!! :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a dream come true! I needed a game to keep me captivated during my semester break. I didn't even notice the time fly by, it's that good! The graphics are stunning, the bosses are unique and challenging, and the overall there's so much to do and unlock that it really kept me excited about what's next. Someone mentioned that it's Diablo meets Ark: Survival Evolved, and that's exactly what it's like. I really love the blood purity mechanic where sucking the blood of different beings has different effects. There are many spell classes you have access to (Blood, Unholy, Frost, Illusion, and many more) and so you can mix and match spells from different classes to fit your preferred play style or to defeat a specific boss. You have several forms that you can change into (vampire bear, wolf, mouse and even a human etc.) for different purposes. You can enslave humans, equip them with armor and weapons and send them on hunts to get you resources, or simply trap them in a prison to feed on them. You can ride horses, each with different stats. You can fish. And plenty more. I haven't even touched on the crafting system yet. So yeah, definitely recommend...
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Speaking ONLY from PVE perspective. - The progression is incredibly solid, with objectives tied between eachother but not to point where it becomes too linear.- The bosses are really fun and challenging depending on the difficulty you are playing.- The base building aspect simply works well.- The aesthetic of the game is cool as hell if you like castlevania and gothic stuff.Playing it in 4 player coop hosting a dedicated server on my own PC. The game gives you complete freedom to customize the way the game is gonna play using config files. We bumped the enemy stats and now every boss is a challenge where we need to prepare our builds, consumables and coordinate some skills to be able to win, we are having a blast. Also need to point out the huge improvement that was adding the variety of armor sets in 1.0. It improves a lot on the 'RPG' aspect of the game and makes your character and build feel more unique.In conclusion: For PVE only, the game feels solid implemented. Edit the config files according to your preferences and you will gonna have a good experience. Feels like the item stacks are bad? Increase it. Don't have time to smash rocks to grind into stone bricks for hours? Increase the gathering and refinement rates. Create your own balancing and enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Then let's get into it!Cozy, spectacular and unique implementation.I was expecting a Diablo-style gameplay, but as it turned out, the game has survival elements that define a large part of the game.You are a vampire who has abilities, you can drink blood, you burn in the sun so you have to walk in the shade if it is not at night.You build your own castle, get the things you need for crafting / equipment production.The better equipment / weapons etc are varied, so you don't always have a wooden sword in your hand, but always a new piece of crafted clothing / weapon with a different look.Clever, good concept and good implementation.And a huge plus point is that you can set the difficulty for yourself in a unique way and the world settings.You can play on a server / just with friends or even just solo.Although it's not my game, it's not a bad game at all!I can recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, and the recent massive content update (for free I might add) definitely makes this game worth it. Even playing solo could easily cost you hours of your life. The massive map has a lot of diverse areas, and the base building has continued to be refined. The developers are clearly passionate about the game, and I don't feel cheated out of the dlcs, because they aren't pay to win or pay to unlock lots of new features, they are mostly cosmetic or related to base building aesthetic, which works perfectly for a survival multiplayer game like this.2 things I think would make the game better though would be better camera controls (a way to reset the camera to face a direction, a way to lock the camera, etc), and (though this may just be personal preference) a way to make the basic claws viable, like some way to strengthen them or something.
