_childDocuments_.review: (Review based as a Solo player) At this time I cannot recommend this game unless some changes are made. The game is fairly good in my opinion and I could go on about the numerous things I like however as my post is for not recommending I will focus on the negative.This game seems to have been designed for multiplayer. So no matter how much you enjoy the early parts of the game you will eventually hit a wall in which you find yourself saying ah crap this is too much work for little enjoyment. Resources - at the start you will find that you progress at a fairly steady pace and get those little rushes from progressing however once you have your basic base setup you realise you will basically be doing non stop grinding for materials.They say you can get your servants to go out and get resources and loot for you however it boils down to send them off on mission wait for timer to receive a small amount of resources. In the 2 to 12 REAL WORLD hours it takes them to get back I could have got multiples of time more resources on my own.Servants - Again going to back to my opinion that this was designed mainly for multi player is that Servants main role in the game is to guard your base from attacks from other players however on a PVE server or if playing alone then they are pretty much useless.Yes you can send them out on missions however to get such little reward for the amount of REAL WORLD hours and as a solo player it only counts the hours you are actually logged on.As a budding Vampire lord I expect my servants to *cough* actually serve me. I don't understand why human servants need coffins as they are not vampires. I don't understand why I can't tell my servants to gather near by resources to myself or a selected area and I don't understand why I bother equipping my servants if they can't follow me around the map and protect me or assist in killing a boss. In the end of the day I end up being the servant who collects these people, gets materials to make armour and weapons to equip them for them to be nothing more then moving decorations.If someone from the company reads this please allow the servants to have more life and control options so that they are actually do what a servant is meant to do.All in all I think it is a great game so far with potential but the way it is now you might as well label it an MMORPG

_childDocuments_.review: **Overall Rating:** 9.5/10I've had the chance to play both before and after the release, and I'd like to share my experience in the PvE hardcore mode post-release. My primary input was a gamepad, occasionally switching to keyboard and mouse for building.**Gameplay Experience:**The hardcore difficulty feels overtuned, providing very little room for mistakes when fighting bosses. It's manageable if you dedicate around 4 hours to learning the movesets, adjusting your tactics, spells, and sometimes weapons. However, the game penalizes you harshly for mistakes by reducing your max HP, which means that after a split-second error, you're left with 20% HP and can only heal up to 30%. The Dracula fight, with its four phases taking about 20 minutes, is brutal and not for everyone.**Building and Design:**Building your castle is genuinely enjoyable. There are many nuances, allowing you to design and construct your base just the way you like it. I strongly recommend focusing on creating a proper castle and making it a home. 😊**Additional Features:**Fishing is quite skippable as you can have your servants bring you fish. There's a lot of variety in character building, with 7 types of blood, 4 types of armor, 11 weapon types, 36 spells, and 12 ultimate abilities.**Cons:**- The Dracula fight is too long.- Official PvE servers restrict you to only 3 floors for your castle.- The max HP punishment for taking damage is harsh.- Soul shards prevent you from flying on PvE servers, and there's no shard buff on PvE servers.**Final Thoughts:**Overall, I give this game a 9.5/10. Despite some issues, the game offers a rich and engaging experience, especially if you enjoy building and character customization.

_childDocuments_.review: After I sinked in around another 150+ hours into this game, I can only give ideas for future updates.For me, this game hits the sweet spot betweem a sweaty souls like experience and a somewhat chill building sandbox.I'm currently writing this before the 1.0 release, so I have my hopes up.If you are hesitant to try this game, let me give you a quick rundown on what you can expect:-Gorgeous music for all the available regions-a well designed combat and crafting system- *magic *-an atmosphere that you can feel, when you play this game-a really cool and supportive communityBut, all the good things that are here, I have to say some disappointing qualitis, at least from my part:-When it comes to boss fights, the music is not diverse enough. For the first 2 playthroughs, I accept the came music for battles/boss fights, but after the 5th or 10th replay, it will get repetetive. So I would fancy a bigger variet of music for normal battles, theme songs for bosses, etc.-Abilities and magic. Now, I know that in 1.0, the magic system will be reimagined, but I'll share my viewpoint on this game system so far. It's cool that we got the physical attack enhancing spells, and I found it neat that there are exactly as many schools of spells as gems, but I think it would be more fun (from my perspective) if we could mix abilities together, or to add combos into the game. What I mean is, that you could mix the blood projectile with an unholy one, and get a new ability that does both spell type.-World building. For me, and I am sure for many more theorist, we need more lore. What happened to the vampires, how did they become, and stuff like that. I think it would be pretty cool if we could find some old pieces of paper or a diary of some sort, that let us theorise about this world.-The ability that we cannot add mods through steam workshop. This might be a permanent or temporarly thing, but I think it would spice up the whole game, if we could add costum mods, like weapon skins, music, etc. If not, that is understandable as well, maybe this is just a me problem.Overall, this game deserves every last penny if you are looking for a fun and somewhat challenging vampire survival game. A solid 9/10 for me!

_childDocuments_.review: I have played a fair bit on PvE but I can sort of guarantee this game is going to die, very rapidly, at some close point in time. The PvE has some fun to it but i could think there is only going to be only that much fun when you grind most of the times places you already know how to deal about.PvEThe game opens fair and it is fine to have a tracker for your progress in forms of quests. I liked the parts where it told you to do something but you don't have the materials for it. So you go "oh ok, I need to craft it" and then you realise you don't have the station for it and go find out where to get it. That is fun forcing your brain to think a bit.On other note I do not understand why the number of resources needs to be this ridiculously high. Is this game trying to be a mobile game to give you some sort of dopamine attack from seeing big numbers that are as quickly depleted? The game maybe is much easier with servants doing some of the more boring tasks but then what is left for you? Going and killing the same guys over and over again before you jump to the next tier of items and enemies? PvPI will just tell that anyone that likes Rust can pick this up but don't think you can have some cheeky traps to defend your base when you're not there. Don't think about defending your base either if you are a solo player. The only servers that are alive are for recommended parties of 3-4 and duo PvP servers do not exist at all.If you find yourself in a 2v1 situation I can tell you can be ready to kiss your ass good bye because this has some battlerite in it but it's worse and you will NOT outplay your opponents. There are either spell or weapon skills that will straight up stun lock you for enough time for the other player in the party to push his attacks out. No, you cannot use counter if you are already stun locked by a skill. Every character is server sided. You will have difficulties to aquire new skills because most of the times the boss battles take so long, someone else will join and they will most likely kill you for your loot. You need to kill the kneeled boss to get the rewards.This game is only 2 days old by now but I see it as a failure because I can tell it is supossed to be PvP focused. With the lack of possibility to outplay your opponents but to brute force them because they have better gear score is horendous game design. No faints, and combat locked behind your 3 weapons attacks(2 with copper weapons), spacebar to dodge, 2 spells(there is a lot more to chose from) and 1 ultimate abillity that you will not see for a long time. A bored top player could walk up to you and destroy you for funsies. I will keep playing this game on PvE because I cant refund it anymore. The idea of Stunlock-studios having expertise in really fun combat system is not visible for me in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The blood endures. The blood nourishes. The blood also powers my lights, far too many crafting stations, and the very stone itself. Dracula was kind enough to get himself killed and you have been brought back from the near extinction of the vampire race. It is an ignoble enough start. A once great vampire left punching trees and grass to craft the most basic of weapons. If you do not have a stomach for crafting than steer clear of this game. For there is crafting, much of it. A straight linear path of it with a tightly locked level of power that refuses to deviate for even a moment. There is an argument that the game would have been more enjoyable with a more ARPG approach to loot but that would be a whole other game. As it is, the game is mostly about exploring a well made if rather empty world of various biomes. The majority of your time is spent harvesting resources to bring back home to keep the refining and crafting grind going. The rest of your time is spent hunting...V Blood.V Blood contain the essence of Dracula and you must hunt them all down to obtain their dark and secret knowledge...of how to make carpets and bookcases. All progress is locked tightly behind this. The V bloods themselves are a delight to battle and feel as if they stepped out of another much more interesting game. It is almost at odds with the rest of the tone of the game. At its core, V Rising is a fun game with friends but probably an absolute ordeal alone. A sometimes schizophrenic and sometimes immensely grindy game but still fun nonetheless. If you are feeling starved of the red. Be sure to try it.

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing beats running through Dunley Farms and hearing a farmer screaming "Vampire!"This is a great game for vampire lovers with tons of fun combat and non-combat abilities you unlock by defeating awesome boss enemies, some of whom wander the world seemingly in search of vampires like you to hunt! You get to track these bosses down and take their V Blood to become even stronger!You also get to build, personalise and expand an awesome castle - filling it with your crafting stations and chests (and bookshelves once you unlock them) for all your treasures and resources! On top of practical items there are plenty of wonderful purely cosmetic decorations you can add to create your own unique vampire lair!Very easy to get hooked on! Great sense of accomplishment and satisfying combat that rewards skilled players! A great game for a great price and its still in early access, I'm personally looking forward to seeing this game grow and progress!Cheers for Stunlock Studios for giving us the vampire game we always wanted!

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, noble creatures of the night,Allow me to share my boundless enthusiasm for the newly risen gem of digital darkness: V Rising. With the long-awaited release of Update 1.0, this game ushers in a new era of vampiric experience that ensnares us all.From the first glance at the newly illuminated lands of Vardoran, the heart of every night wanderer beats with exhilaration. The developers have crafted a universe with unparalleled artistry and dedication, teeming with secrets and dark beauty. The visual splendor and atmosphere are a true feast for the senses, transporting the spirit to another realm.Update 1.0 unfurls a plethora of new content and enhancements, making the game even more captivating. New abilities and weapons enrich every vampire's arsenal, while the revamped user interface brings unprecedented elegance and user-friendliness. This update introduces thrilling quests and challenging boss battles that will test even the oldest and wisest among us.Noteworthy is the introduction of new multiplayer elements that strengthen the bonds between our dark brethren. Joining forces, forging alliances, and conquering the world together adds depth and dynamism to the game, making our vampiric existence all the more fulfilling.In this new era of V Rising, brimming with innovations and improvements, we find a refreshing revitalization of our eternal night life. _childDocuments_.review: Vampire games are in short supply, and thankfully this is one of the better ones.It's a vampire survival game, so you do vampire stuff, drink blood, and have a good time. You can play this in multiplayer, but I recommend bringing friends along. Honestly most of the battles are challenging and entertaining without being too much to conquer if you're by yourself, the Castlevania crossover is a fun little tidbit and Simon Bellmont lives up to his reputation, and if anything about the game personally doesn't sit right with you, you can adjust just about everything from the server settings to make gameplay easier or harder for yourself. I will give a warning to people who like me do not have friends to play this game with: there are some bosses that were not balanced with singleplayer in mind. I'm sure someone with enough practice and who's skilled enough could overcome that, but I personally hit my limit right towards the end of the game. I tried turning the difficulty down just to be able to experience the combat but aside from a lower damage output, the bosses didn't really change much and I was still stuck at that point. Maybe a 'get good' moment, maybe a 'fight the boss until you learn all their mechanics and die a few hundred times until you win' moment, or exactly what it felt like it was meant to be: a "bring all your friends, cause this is going to be a tough one" kind of fight. Ultimately up until that point, I've had easy fights that left me with my ego feeling inflated. I've had tough ones where I survived with about 1 hp more than the boss I just killed has by the end of the battle. I've struggled, sweat like a pig as I tried for the fifth time to kill a tough boss. After the full release when I lost my save and had to start over, some bosses I struggled with a lot wound up being ez claps because of how well I knew their mechanics, and others that I remembered as being easy I let my guard down around and got smacked around as a result.This game has a lot of content, and you can spend a whole lot of time in it and not get bored. There's almost always a new challenge and up until I hit the limit of what I could beat by myself (f*cking Adam) there was always something more to reach for and look forward to. EDIT: it takes a lot of time, effort, and getting good but you can in fact solo every boss in the game. The sense of achievement is worth everything.I definitely recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game, especially considering it's early access. Super polished, beautiful world to explore, and exceptional gameplay mechanics. I'm really impressed with what Stunlock has created here and bought the extra packs to support the devs. I'd love to see more content in the future.1. The map is pretty big so there's tons to explore. The different areas are unique, making it fun to progress to new stages.2. The artwork style is gorgeous. I loved creating/customizing my character and crafting the armor sets. Favorite by far is  The way the capes swish, the hair movements, all of it is so beautiful.3. Base building is some of the best I've experienced in any game. The detailing, design, and how well it fits into the vibe of the game is still so satisfying even after playing for hours and hours. There are quite a few crafting stations, which does create some hassle running around your base to make what you need, but honestly each station is so fun I ended up not caring.4. The power-ups and weapon abilities are really fun to obtain and experiment with. I think there are spells/weapons that are better than others, but it's still not a one-size-fits-all situation because they each have benefits in different situations. I enjoyed that aspect as well because it added variety and required you to plan which tools you'd need for areas/enemies/boss fights.The only drawback I've kinda struggled with is the movement speed. There were so many times when it was just excruciating how slow my character was "running". Most of the time it just feels like she's jogging through molasses. When you get to  which makes getting around the map easier, but that didn't solve the frustration of slow movement during boss fights or slowly jogging to get around my (probably too big) base. Once you unlock  moving around your base gets a little better. There's also magic relics, but you have to select just one and I preferred the spell boosts to assist with combat (because I suck) over the small boost in speed.That's my thoughts! I still have some end-game content to get to but thank you to everyone who made this game so amazing. To potential players, definitely worth buying.

_childDocuments_.review: First of, this is not a Dungeon Crawler game (e.g. Diablo), like it may seem. This is a survival game, more similar to Valheim. But it is one of the best survival games I've ever played, and it's crazy to think it's still in development.This game has everything I like in this type of titles:- A deep and well layered world, with tons of enemies, bosses, and biomes.- A robust progression system that doesn't cut you from the experience by making you grind endlessly for resources, and at the same time, it feels rewarding for everything you accomplish.- A well designed building system, with tons of decorations (I haven't unlocked every decorative item yet).Instead of looking for food and water, you need to drink the blood of your enemies in order to survive. This also gives you certain buffs depending on the type of blood and it's "puracy". You can also recruit any human and make it your servant, and send him to fight and collect things for you.There are a lot of magic spells to obtain by killing bosses, and 4 types of melee weapons (that I've discovered so far). You can move more freely during the night, since the sun can easily kill you, and even if this may seems trivial, I think it makes a difference on how you play this game compared to others. I'm sure there are more things I've yet to discover, and I cannot recommend this game enough. If you like survival games, give this game a try. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is scratching a pretty nice itch, but it does get too grindy to enjoyably solo as you progress.The game focuses strongly on the base-building early on (this may be a Pro, or Con depending on the player), but you can put more of your focus on exploring the world. There's a few pretty good systems in place that keeps the world feeling alive, even when playing solo. I like the random patrols, encampments with different resources, and V Blood spawns (think of them as Elite enemies) that will incentivize exploration. Levels are tied to the gear you're wearing, but it ends up working out fairly well as you always have a pretty clear objective to progress.V Rising pulls through with very good mechanics; the skills are interesting, and boss fights are uniquely engaging from each other. For me, it's almost exclusively held back by the reliance of multiplayer at this point. I would love to see the studio make a pure ARPG as their next game, with more reasonable scaling that doesn't rely on a team. Even with the sliders, the experience isn't quite what you would expect.

_childDocuments_.review: tl:dr; Game starts off great with PvE focus, but gets dogsh*t after/in about act 3. If you're looking for a nice "open-world" "sandbox" with bosses etc, play, idk, Valheim, I guess. Boss damage/HP and add scaling is just stupid. I played it a bit during EA and had a full run and kill of the main boss (on normal) after full release.First things first: We played on a self-hosted server with PvP disabled, teleport restrictions disabled (because come on...) and general drop roll multiplier set to 1.2x-ish (work, family, you know the drill) **BEFORE** we knew about the greater stygian shards farm ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ We played with 3-6 people on/off and in a single clan.May contain spoilers.I won't say anything about the visuals or anything, if you're reading the reviews you're already mildly interested in the title, so go for it. We also didn't encounter any game-breakers or bugs in general, despite the choices made by the developers.The first few acts, namely 1 and 2 and most of 3, are well paced and there is always something to do. Basebuilding is fine, upgrading by swapping workbenches is questionable, but as you get the materials back, that's fine too.Getting the first research done is "alright", but that is where it starts. You either have to hope that the higher level research drops the item you want, or hope that RNGesus likes you. If not? Go farm materials to unlock it. Oh, you didn't want the whip but the chest piece for your full set bonus? Nah, fam, my bad. Go back to farming.The Greater Stygian Shard Farm is also just plain crazy. Not the farming itself, no, but the RNG again. You're playing an ice buid and need an ice bow? Good luck spending ~1500 Greater Stygian Shards on an lvl 30 weapon. Oh, it has illusion? Tough luck. You finally found one? Lovely. Now go craft a new base bow, upgrade it and use it to finally craft the lvl 30 weapon. No, you can't use the lvl 26 weapon you've been crafting and upgrading for the last few days. Let me be clear: the bosses are a mess. The first ones are fine, but the spider boss is a disaster. Scaling is a joke, and as many people have already said, this is a very movement-heavy game where you need to actively avoid attacks. There's only one movement spell with an 8s CD, which is ridiculous.The closer you get to the end boss, the weirder it gets. Some random mobs out in the wild seem harder than a few of the bosses.The end boss is just...no. We were fully equipped, legendary weapons, potions up, gear according to playstyle, and we were on gear level 90. It's just if you hit a wall. With a truck. In full speed. And miss me with "gIt GuD". Yeah, you're right. The last boss is 100% a "gitting gud" thing, but not from the players' perspective. It's about scaling and the amount of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ it serves out. We tried multiple times with different approaches, including solo.We did it, but holy ♥♥♥ cow, not again. Also, bosses healing as a mechanic in a boss fight where the players deal 40-ish damage and the boss hits you with 100+ normal attacks? Yeah, that's not a good idea.Anyway, if you like to mix things up with the rates or aren't planning to play solo or with PvP enabled, give it a try, but be warned. The game's okay, but they lost focus to the PvE crowd midway through.

_childDocuments_.review: This is essentially a top down Valheim-style survival game structure with the combat of Battlerite/Bloodline Champions and the (optional) multiplayer/PvP mechanics of Rust. Overall I would definitely recommend it if you liked any of those games. Valheim: For context, this means that the overall macro loop is that you go out, fight enemies, kill bosses, and in doing so get the ability to craft new stuff which is stronger. So similar to Valheim (or Terraria, though without the big NPC focus). Hit tree, break tree, get wood, make thing. Find boss, kill boss, get ability, get stronger. That kind of thing. Surviving mostly involves feeding off enemies, but it isn't like you'll be struggling to stay alive. The main thing is that enemies you feed off of give you different buffs, so finding ones which give good buffs is important. You can also use up your blood to heal, which will mean you'll have to feed again sooner (and potentially lose a good buff!), but might be needed. I think it's a nice way to integrate it in without making it feel punitive -- sort of like Valheim's food system. Base building is required insofar as you need to have crafting and resource processing stuff to make weapons to fight with. E.g. you need a workbench, and then you need a sawmill for planks, furnace for ore, etc. etc. It even borrows from Valheim in little ways -- e.g. stone giants will break trees while you fight them similar to Trolls. Two ways it is dissimilar: (1), the base building is not as intricate. If you want to build a super crazy castle, this might not be the ideal game for you. (2), the exploration is a bit less involved. There are cool and varied biomes, but it is definitely more combat focused and so far there has not been a moment like sailing in Valheim for the first time. Battlerite/BLC: The actual combat and moment to moment gameplay is a top down action game based heavily on skillshots. If you ever played either of Stunlock's earlier games, it is just like that. If you haven't, imagine if someone made a MOBA, but then gave it incredibly good skill-based combat and stripped out everything else -- that's basically what Battlerite was. Its fights feel super dynamic/fun -- even though it might look like Diablo on the surface, the combat has quite a bit more depth imo. For example, when you autoattack it will root you for a second, and if you are using a ranged weapon it will be a skillshot which you have to lead and which can miss. You deciding when to attack etc. actually matters -- you're not necessarily just spamming left mouse. Bosses have a variety of attack patterns which shift through fights. As you kill bosses you will steal some of their abilities which you can then equip. You have 1-2 weapon skills, two abilities chosen from a wide list which could be skillshots/counters etc., an ultimate, and a dash. So you can get a decent amount of build customization in the abilities you choose. You can also tailor your equipment a bit, but that part is a bit less impactful than ability choices so far.Rust: And then there is the Rust style PvP aspects. You have a base which you can lock off from enemies using a resource you get from killing stuff. You can also raid other player's bases and kill them. I haven't played it in PvP so can't really comment on it beyond that. I imagine it would probably be fun given that Battlerite was fun.Overall, the main reason to play this is the combat I think- I don't think any other "survival" game comes close. Stunlock has always made games with fun combat, but I think this makes them much more accessible. Being able to experience the really fun skill shot combat of Battlerite in a chiller setting is incredible.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the game as soon as I bought it a year or so ago. Its only gotten better. oh my goodness has it gotten better. Can't wait for release. Pros: Great combat / Great bosses / Great castle building. The castle building is by far the best aspect of the game. There's nothing so satisfying as having a hidden three story castle with tinted windows and spooky foggy courtyards overlooking the desert city or the werewolf town. You get this mad rush of power seeing all your minions lounging about.Cons: Resource stacking. By far my biggest gripe. Needed to create a custom world to get over the issue. Needed to do the same for crafting times. I was here for the building and completely taken in, but the normal worlds actively fight you whenever you're in the flow state. Also, bag space. I wish there were custom worlds where I could increase my own character's inventory. The added crafting bags are a nice addition, but still not enough for all the different resources in my opinion. Haven't tried PVP. Couldn't even imagine someone breaking my marvellous masterpieces. I'd love to see more castle options at full release, though I understand there are technical limitations. _childDocuments_.review: V Rising is an exceptional game that masterfully combines elements of action RPG, base building, and survival. The game invites you into a dark, immersive world where you can build your own Dracula-like manor and defend it against rival vampire clans. The base-building mechanics are both creative and satisfying, allowing you to craft a unique fortress that reflects your style.The ARPG elements add depth to the gameplay, with a variety of combat styles and abilities that keep encounters exciting. The survival aspect adds another layer of challenge, as you must manage resources and fend off threats in a hostile environment.Overall, V Rising is a fantastic experience for fans of these genres, offering hours of engaging gameplay and the thrill of becoming a powerful vampire lord. Highly recommended for those who enjoy a blend of strategic base building, intense combat, and survival challenges.

_childDocuments_.review: I am playing V Rising with customized settings suiting my disability limitations.How I love games which offer such great customization within the gameplay settings. One way or the other it can suit anyone no matter limitations or needs.Another important thing to mention is that the game got much better for me after I installed the Modern Camera mod and enable its Action Mode (in the keybinds). With it I don't need to hold a mouse button down to turn the camera and it makes it feel more immersive.V Rising is a great game with a nice bit of lore. The boss fights can be challenging but that's where the settings can be adjusted (among other things as well). It has a nice base building system with some good additions for decoration. Also without the need to buy any of the DLCs. They are mostly there for you to support the devs if you so choose. They do not change the game in any way possible.The game looks great and has a good enough character customization options. I would have liked to see some more unique loot with a small chance to drop. Then there would be another reason to grind, besides for mats. Similar to how it is in Diablo II. Maybe some extra unique recipes as well.Such mixed with the base building and crafting, the world and looks, would be a lovely mix.

_childDocuments_.review: I cant recomend this game at the current moment due to some development decissions that might change later, or not. Its fun at the beginning (youtube will tell you all about that, so go get an idea about the ups) and the frame for a good game is already there. the first few hours will be fun, yes. To get nearly enough resources to get my castle walls going i spend hours going back and forth to the copper mine. building several smelters to get anything going. hours... Once i reached iron it was triple the time, just for walking. Want to join a game with someone who came to it later? well, bad luck. start from nothing.- Gear = progression. and some gear gives you 1 lvl. but needs farming of hours. without certain bosses no progression at all. how to progress if a boss is just hitting to hard and no new gear can be made? _childDocuments_.review: **Update 05/20/22**Great game, WELL WORTH the $20 asking price. PLENTY of items/style/utility items to build an expansive castle and also turn it into a vampire version of farming simulator if you wish (not required to progress). The skill trees are well thought out and balanced for very specific game play (2 man or 4 man team of players that are ALL in the same "clan" - clan size limited to 4 players. Your skills DON'T effect anyone NOT in your 4 man clan - so those seeking healing open world PvE boss fights and being support is a NO unless they're clan members (i.e any shields, heals, buffs you apply will never apply to any player not in your 4 man "clan." There is no "making a group with non-clan members either." ALL content scales to your gear level, and amount of players that show up for very important boss fights - meaning you might have solo'd a boss fight while at that boss' current level - but come back over leveled or with multiple people and it will multiple the boss' skills, HP, stamina, and if they summon minions - turbo charge it (i.e the boss will summon 40 minions instead of just 10).PvE This game is built entirely around group PvE and Group PvP. The  PvE solo game play is doable the first 5 hours, after that pray your progression is locked behind killing bosses that require multiple people. However, you can only be "in a group" with your clan members (like a guild - 4 man max cap). So if they aren't online and available to help, you will be blasting global chat for anyone to help you. Even on PvE this can hose you over. (i.e you advertise for help to kill boss - people answer and ask you to guide them to the boss - they hang back and let you take the aggro - you die - they finish off the boss - they drain the boss' blood and get the unlock and leave you to revive and do a corpse run. Additionally only 4 players can drain a downed boss and whoever starts draining the boss first ends the boss. This means if you need to be revived or are a distance from the boss - a random player that joined last second could drain the boss before you get there and you miss out.PvP Servers (great content!)PvP is typical early adopters just sitting around chain killing newbies and camping required progression choke points to farm free resources from lower levels and spamming the typical "quit then" responses. Servers are low level (like 40 players) so not a lot of help or ability to turn the tide against those being toxic and abusive (talking about actual toxicity - not getting killed in PvP or getting ganked because you went out solo and got 4v1'd.PvP 4 Player servers are legit fun and worthwhile with a 4 player team, it is a lot of fun. ONLY if you have 4 players online grouping together though. Expect your bases to be ransacked when you log off and for teams to 4v1 target specific players for full loot items that might be better than theirs, only to turn tail and run away full steam. Typical full loot gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I like this game a lot, but it needs some work.PROS:-Fun core vampire gameplay mechanics.-Great looking WoWesque art style-Lots of fun planning out castles.-Combat is decently varied and challenging.-Large updates seem to be on the way.CONS:-The map gets old quickly once you've been through it.-Not much variety in equipment.-Definitely needs progression balancing for single player.  At a few points during single player progression, I felt I had hit a bit of a wall without other people.  On that same note, single player really revealed that there needs to be more ways to bridge these gaps, as well as more for the player to engage with and more ways to do it.-The core game and world are there, and polished too, but it feels like there are elements missing from both the mechanics and the world itself.  The world feels empty and predictable after a few hours.-In relation to the "Large Updates" mentioned above, it just leaves a bad impression on me when a game in Early Access (which means UNFINISHED!) states they are releasing "Free DLC" to an unfinished game.-We need more hands-on community engagement during the Early Access period.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game to play with friends. I tried PvE solo and it's quite fun. _childDocuments_.review: TLDNR: Fun to play, but I fear after unlocking everything the gameplay will feel boring, at least on PVE servers.The game isn't what I expected. I started playing this with a friend on a local hosted PVE server, so we don't have to worry about enemy players or castle decay.The core mechanics are straight forward and fun. Unlocking new stuff by finding recipe books and tracking down boss enemies and monsters is a very interesting mechanic, much better than having an EXP system. Avoiding the sun and drinking different blood types for various buffs, also is interesting and feels fresh. You also unlock many different spells, which help to roundout the build and play style you like.The building system also works great and they also found a way to make sure, people build multiple rooms for benefits, instead of just one big room with everything slapped into it. You still can do that, but then you don't get the benefits.Overall everything seems to be okay, but for some reason I think the gameplay falls a bit flat. I see the core design is made for PVP, and PVE is just an option, that loses some features, without adding new ones. But I don't like PVP, neither do I want to login consistently, just to avoid the castle from decaying. Right now, I can't really tell what the game is missing, but I think it's the unlocking and upgrading system itself. Just grinding through the unlockable recipes doesn't feel satisfying enough. What happens, after I unlocked everything? How long does it take to unlock everything? What other goals do players have on a PVE server? Will just the grind extend to a shear endless grind, so it artificially stretches the gameplay?7 hours on the clock isn't enough to give a final review to this game, so I will keep playing with my friend and most likely edit this, if I feel like it deserves it. Till then, the rating will be positive, because so far we enjoying our time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game. The bosses are well-designed, the base mechanics are solid, and the pacing is great. The vampire theme and surrounding content are exactly what I expected and more. The game is not overly long, nor does it have too much grinding, although there is a bit. I fully recommend it.The only thing that could be improved is the item management. While compulsively counting and sorting can be great, but it takes too link. I wish I didn't have to either:A) Waste 5 minutes every time I return from an expedition, saving the loot in the right chest.B) Drop things wherever, then waste 5 minutes every time I want to know what to farm or craft something, looking for the ingredients or figuring out what I need.A system to give all my loot to a servant and have them sort it out on their own would be great. After all, I'm a vampire with servants!The game would benefit from better communication. Without spoiling, the final boss spawns something that helps you, but we initially thought it didn't and beat it to hell.Overall, the game is highly enjoyable and well worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Best combat system I've played in ages, simple enough to understand with a great depth and enjoyable learning curve.Overall great game, very promising.-------------------------------------------------------------------------Unfortunately after release the devs did nothing to address the teaming issue that plagues every official serverJust like the last update, servers will be dead in a couple of weeks because they will become a huge group of 10-20 people playing together preventing everybody else from doing content and zerging them, generating unbalanced fights, where a huge group outnumbers a duo, in a server that was supposed to be duo.Great game idea, great execution for the most part, but the lack of a solution for the teaming issue makes this game only worth for the PvE.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Stunlock Studios' game seemed cool from trailers, but after 8 hours I figured out that, it's mostly grinding - searching for recipes, ingredients, more grinding, more ingredients then 90% of your buildings are for even more detailed grinding. The cycle repeats.Pros:> Impressive graphics> Innovative ideasCons:> Excessive grinding> Demands too much time and effort> Repetitive gameplay> Solo play can be boring> Online play requires dedication and has risks> Daily log-ins feels obligatory> Static world, potential boredom after first playthrough> Unstable servers, risking progress loss on someone else's server closure> Formidable difficulty in soloing bossesPros include great graphics and ideas, but the cons pile up. The game demands too much time, gets repetitive, and can be boring solo or too hard online. Daily log-ins feel like a chore. The static world may get dull after one playthrough, and shaky servers risk losing progress if someone closes their server. Soloing bosses is too tough.Been into Stunlock Studios games for a good number of years. Usually, I don't do negative reviews, but this grinding got me. Looked promising in the trailers, but after 8 hours, it's mostly just grinding. Good graphics and ideas, sure, but the downsides are a lot. Takes up too much time, gets boring doing the same stuff, and playing alone is meh. Online is too tough. The daily log-ins? Annoying. The world doesn't change or randomly generate, so it might get boring after one go. Servers are iffy – if the host closes, you lose your character. Bosses may be too hard to solo resulting in multiple deaths.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version:Simple to play, hard to master, fun to experience and pleasant to look at. All you could ask for a game to be good with very few flaws holding it back.Long version:This is one of the few survival games that manages to hold my interest and I believe I know why. While fans of hardcore survival games like The Forest or Rust might find it underwhelming at the start due to the lack of needs your character has, only needing blood to outright survive. However, this soon stops being an issue, as the game teaches you that blood types of enemies and the quallity of the blood can have benefits that are replaced when you feed, so often you'll want to seek out particular prey instead of settling for survival (for example, high quallity blood from a worker will help you gather more resources, while warrior and rogue's blood can help you in battle and animal blood will help you travel faster). The game also has a night and day cycle, which matters to you due to your vampiric nature. Standing in the sun for longer than a couple of seconds will set you ablaze, dealing more and more damage the longer you go without shelter.On top of that, not only does the game demand you construct a base to have any amount of progress, but said base is extremely demanding in terms of resources. Furthermore, instead of having a more abstract objective like Rust or a single minded mission like The Forest, your final goal in V Rising is to dominate and become as powerful as possible, which is where one of my favorite mechanics comes into play.Sprinkled around the world are bosses that you will hunt down and kill. These bosses all have unique mechanics and give you different things when defeated, like blueprints for weapons and gear, unlocking workbenches you'll need to make, new building parts to construct your castle and, my favorite part, new powers for your vampire. All of these are extremely useful and sometimes even necessary for you to move forward in the game.In addition, other players can join your clan and pool their resources with yours to have larger castles and more power, which you'll need because a vampire is nothing without domain and, to hold said domain, you'll need to be able to protect it from other players. The game limits this with the necessity to craft keys to either destroy or take over other players castles, so it's rare that you'll lose your hard-earned castle to some whelp who snuck in while you were gone, but even when that happens, you can also have keys with you to take back what is yours and your allies'.Overall it's a really fun game with interesting mechanics!

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, this one was a miss for me, for one simple reason.It does not respect your time.I played this solo, so that may affect the above statement. I played offline, on standard settings. The combat is fun, the base building is awesome, the world map is expansive. But. Everything.. Takes... Forever....I think, during my time, I spent about 90% of the playtime watching my character repeatedly smack a rock with a mace, or a tree with an axe, or an ore vein with a mace... If I wasn't doing that then I was watching my grinder make bricks out of the rocks, or the sawmill make planks from the wood, or the smelter make.....Anyway, you get the point.Further still, it just seems like the game is trying to waste your time. Smacked a rock for 20 seconds and picked up some stone? Now you cant use the way-gates, have fun running for 15 minutes to get back to your castle. Why??? Nothing interesting happens on the way back, I just turn into a wolf and follow the compass. 90% of what you pick up (and ALL crafting supplies) disable the use of way-gates (fast travel).This would be OK if the world was interesting. But there are no quests, no unique encounters, no visual story telling. Just random patrols you can run straight past. If you are going to pointlessly make me run 15 minutes with no teleport option, at least make it fun.I addition, the boss fights quickly become time sinks, taking, literally, hundreds of hits to down a boss on normal. One of the worst feelings is wailing on a boss for 10 minutes, dying, then coming back and seeing them on full health again (after running back to them for 10 mins).Also, you can't craft from your storage, so if you want to build some new armour, have fun running around for 5 mins to collect all the materials from your various storage chests, then another 5 mins to put them back.It is frustrating as it could have been good, without these pointless time sinks. I suspect a lot of this is to 'balance' the multiplayer, but as a solo player, it is all frustration.Add to that there is no story, no world building, no cut scenes. It is a pass for me. On a sale perhaps, but even then, only if you have a LOT of time to kill..!

Actually, when I initially got the game upon release, I wondered why it was so under priced, considering the amount of content that was presented to me out of the gate. 20 bucks entry fee? IMO, that's a friggen steal for a game in this genre.My only recommendation is to bring some friends, because the demand for crafting recipes can be somewhat steep, along with some of the stations taking a good bit of time to pump out product. _childDocuments_.review: This game has great potential but in my opinion it has 3 major problems (two are interrelated) that mean I cant thumb it up. The problems for me are 1) the grind 2) linear progression 3) frustrating boss fights I really like the concept of combining isometric POV with survival and vampire lore. Progression is interesting in that you cant really grind to progress in this game and progress is tied to your gear rather than your character. However this is also where the issues start for me... You MUST take on bosses to progress as killing them unlocks new abilities and blueprints that essential things are locked behind. The problem is that some boss fights are insanely hard even when well over their level and often you need to kill a lot of enemies around the boss to even get into a fight with them. You also need to avoid sunlight since you are a vampire, so taking on bosses will need to be done at night. However because you need to clear enemies to get to the boss you often need to get started during the day, so you are dodging sunlight while grinding through dull enemies to get to a frustrating boss fight you may well lose many times over. Sure you could say 'git gud' but it appears others suffered this same frustration. Even worse, bosses will ENTIRELY REGENERATE their health in seconds mid battle, should you step back a few feet and they get just out of your reach. So you lose all your progress in seconds and this feels very frustrating and is unforgivable in my opinion. When you go through this many times over it starts to become a chore as you may need to grind for say explosive ingredients to gain access to the boss, kill many surrounding enemies and time this all around daylight only to die very fast and have to repeat it again and again... sighThere is no other way to progress so if you are stuck on a boss that gate keeps items you need to learn... you have zero alternate progression options. There is no way to grind your way through, you take on frustrating bosses who completely heal themselves in seconds, or you don't progress. Anyway... I love the graphics and sounds on this game, though the performance can get a bit dicey around your base etc but this isn't unusual for survival type games. It pains me to thumb this game down as it is a great concept and is probably the most complete early access game I have played so far. I got 45 hours gaming so far which is less than a dollar an hour for entertainment - a metric I base value on with games. However I am close to just giving up and stopping the game as the grind and frustrating bosses start to feel un-fun when I just want to explore and build an awesome base but I am struggling to go through another frustrating chore of an infuriatingly hard boss fight. This also limits any replay value for me as I know that next time I play it there will still only be tedious boss fights to progress through the game and why would I want to repeat these frustrating encounters again in the future?So much potential but so frustrating and limited progression wise :(

I haven't yet tried out the PvP servers, strictly PvE until I learn how the rest of the spells work. I adore the soundtrack and the atmosphere of this world. My only gripe about this game is that I wish there were more cosmetic options, and to add to that, there should be a cosmetic slot for your armor. Also, I don't think you should drop your hat/helmet on death, it should stay on you just like your armor does. Other than that I think this game is really fun and I'd recommend it to any of my friends who are into vampires or dark fantasy. It kinda feels like Diablo but with survival and crafting elements.

_childDocuments_.review: For a long time, I was put off buying this game for a few reasons; I'm not that into Vampire-related things (Twilight ruined it all), other top-down games like this such as Cryofall really struggle with appropriate power-balancing between players in PvP, and I'm jaded from buying too many games which ultimately end up ruined for different issues.That aside; V Rising does things very well. The game is incredibly well polished. Certain survival aspects are dealt with in a unique but not irritating way - for example "food/drink" for vampires is of course blood, so that's one thing you need to focus on. But by having different 'blood types' and within those types even a percentage of purity that gives more bonuses, that's a really awesome way to handle the whole thing.The skills are very well balanced especially for PvP; with the (subjective of course) "best" ultimate skill being available at a very early stage, things like this help to give everyone at least a fair bit of balance rather than allowing the disparity between the highest levels and lower levels to be insane. A lot of games completely fall apart with this aspect.To top off the character-based stuff, the building system also has a ton of uniqueness and quality of life aspects such as Waygates to teleport to pre-existing areas (managed by having certain items NOT teleportable so you do still have to risk a run back to base), and even now in-castle teleportation to help you move around your castle better.It would be impossible to sum up the depth of V so far, at 48 hours I've just scratched the surface, but it's clearly so far a game that is ran by an extremely competent game developer, and it's getting to be a rarity nowadays.Hats off to Stunlock for their work so far, looking forward to future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: They delete all progress on major updates. Well, the year is almost up, why is half the map still greyed out?When you send your servants out on missions, these missions take from 4 to 24 hours.This time only counts down while you are actively playing.The rewards are terrible.Seriously, who designed this?This game is not designed well for single player. Single player is an option, but it's designed for multiplayer.Which is bizarre, because I've heard a lot of complaints from the multiplayer side of the game too.My advice? It's 2022 and the vampires still haven't worked out this feature.V risings blood system is a bad time.To get 100% blood quality, you need to be EXTREMELY lucky with RNG.Then you need to get them low health and then drain their blood without killing them.To get a prisoner, you need them to be really low health, then escort them all the way to wherever your base is without teleporting.This is utter ♥♥♥♥.I actually just closed the game because I was having an awful time.I was bored.Utterly bored.I was going from area to area looking at their blood quality, which shows as a percentage by their healthbar. _childDocuments_.review: I will break down this review into several sections, pros 1st then cons, then my reason for not recommending this game.Pros.Novel new concept with vampires, not just same cookie cutter game setup most companies or pumping out these days.Combat, fun and interesting, although simple, it works and works well. Graphics, good for a top down type ARPG.Negatives.Story, not much of one.Grindy, like unneccesarly grindy and wastes your time by burning real world time to craft items. Literally most all this game revolves around is grinding items to build the next tier or gear to then defeat a boss to then be able to craft the next higher tier of gear...BUT that next tier for gear will require all kinds of silly materials just to build the crafting station that can then build the gear plus the gear will then require its own materials PLUS real time to craft them...like seriously built to waste your time. Instead of playing there are often points where you might as well just leave and go do something else while the real world timer counts down...complete waste of time for the sole purpose of wasting time and is a major negative to a casual gamer like myself who cant devote hours and hours to stupid fetch quests and materials.PVP, the reason I play most games any more has two flavors in this game...the normal flavor is that no one wants to PVP because if your loose the other guy can then take all those silly mats you have been grinding for forever and its just not worth the risk to fight...so most every one just tries to avoid open world combat or runs away. Next smaller flavor is gank squads of higher lvl players that camp out in lower level areas just to grief...not that common but kinda silly when it happens. If this happens just leave and come back some other time.In short I cannot recommend this game is it feels like they took the cheesy ideas from mobile gaming and made the game use real world time to craft and complete items and is a complete waste of my limited time. Also this game is really not built around anything but grinding and crafting at this point...all others concepts like combat, pvp, exploring, all that is secondary to waste of time grinding. In short unless you really really like chopping down trees, hitting rocks, and killing the same mobs over and over and over just to get some mats that then take real world time to craft into something...I recommend you pass or get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This Game is SUPER fun! and the creativity inside of it is AMAZING! I have played on several servers, and done several restarts / wipes. Here are my takes on the Pros and Cons of the game:Pros:-Super fun abilities / combat-Building your own vampire base is really exciting and fun to do! -Bosses are challenging, and rewarding-Shape shifting is such a fun mechanic Cons:-Durability loss on death is pretty intensive, and leads to a lot of grinding of resources. After a couple of deaths you're pretty much better off just making new armor / weapons- Sun Damage starts extremely high and builds up ridiculously fast-Fire damage with out the resistances will do everything but 1 point of damage and needs to be nerfed- Maps and bosses are all the same, replay-ability is very low since maps aren't procedurally generatedSome tips I would find interesting to improve game-play:- Soul shards auto reset if not taken by a different clan after a certain amount of time.- Blood moon effecting more than just the player, but also effecting the world. introducing mobs that only come out during blood moons, or certain resources that are only out during blood moons (that turn into aesthetics for the castle)- Changing the paper press to be a boss unlock instead of a research unlock. (maybe taking the place of the holy resistance potion boss unlock and having the holy resistance potion an advancement unlock)Overall, even though the negatives have a bit more explanation over the pros, I highly recommend this game. I could hardly put it down for the time I was actually playing it. but after a few server wipes and replays the game gets very repetitive and burns you out. 10/10 would very much recommend this game, is well worth the $20 price tag. the DLC cosmetics are super nice in game and worth the purchase as well, if you're looking for a little bit more eye candy on your character and base building!

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna sugar coat it, the travelling system is ass. I played for 12.3 hours and probably two hours were eaten up by walking.But this is probably on purpose. Many people are comparing this game to "Valheim but with vampires", but I think it is also accurate to say that the developers were also going for "Rust but with vampires". Which gives a lot more credence to how you traverse the world, considering it was meant to be played with friends, AND against other players that are in the same world. BUT, I am an adult, I don't get much time to play games, especially with friends, and I definitely don't have time to deal with griefing players because I am solo.So, I play solo, on a private server. And this is where V Rising could improve a lot.When you go across the map to collect resources that are end game resources, your only choice is to walk back or find a cave that transports you closer to your castle, which is not exactly easy. And you walk SLOW in this game, I'm talking from one side of the map to the other is 10 minutes of JUST WALKING. And if you are like me, you set up your castle in the starting area because that's what the game was seemingly telling you to do.I understand the reasoning for the travel system when I think about it in context of a it being similar to Rust. BUT, you are giving the players to chose "private play", the sames rules and guidelines don't work well for private players.How could they fix this? Add an ability at gear level 35 or 40 or so that allows you to teleport with resources. That's it. I saw another reviewer say "V Rising does not respect the solo players time" and I feel 100% the same way.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review after playing an additional 50 hours past my initial review. Scroll to bottom of original review for update.Bought this game because I am a fan of survival sandbox games. Here are a couple things you should know before making a purchase for yourself.1. Progression is EXTREMELY linear. Meaning if you get stuck somewhere, there is not alternative option for progression.2. Progression is split into two paths. Killing bosses to unlock upgrades. Or doing research to unlock upgrades. These two paths are still linear. They kind of alternate. Your first upgrades will be from a boss, then your next upgrade is from research. Then another boss. Then more research. Etc. But research is based on finding random drops. Meaning that player progression is not only extremely linear. But it is also tied to RNG.3. The game is obviously balanced for co-op play with friends. The amount of time spend grinding for resources to build a castle take way too long as a solo player. It's fine if you have friends. Because the game is obviously balanced that way. But if you're playing alone be aware that solo play is a huge grind fest. I do not recommend this game in any way to someone wanting to play solo. There are servers out there that have increased loot drop rates. So if you are a solo player. I recommend you try one of these servers. But it somewhat limits your options on what servers are comfortable to play on.4. The boss mechanics are extremely poorly designed. Many of the bosses can be easily cheesed by circling a rock or something. While on the other hand if you actually try to fight them head to head, they seem pretty unbalanced usually.5. The game simply has a lot of bugs. At one point found a 100% blood quality worker. Hurray, right? Time to take you to a prison cell. Nope your invulnerable. My swings go right through you. Lame.5.B. I don't know if it is just this one particular spell. But the blood shield spell (cant remember its name). Just wont activate sometimes. Honestly I don't know if this is a bug or if I simply dont understand one of the game mechanics. I could hammer away at the button, even when out of combat just to try it. And it simply wouldn't cast most of the time. If I held down the button it would eventually cast, somewhere between 3 to 5 seconds later. No idea why this is. But I am fairly certain this is a bug.5.C. This is probably a problem with Latency. But while all my other spells besides the one mentioned in 4.B would cast properly. They often missed their effect. Like lets take the poison shield or the chaos shield. I would cast. Take damage, Never see the ability pop up. And not get a skeleton to spawn for the poison shield or return bolt of the chaos shield. However, this only happens when I cast at the EXACT same time I get hit. If I pre-cast it works fine. Which is why this particular item might be latency issue. I cast the ability, but the attack is already behind the shield by the time it pops up. Still the ability goes on cool down so you just wasted your ability. Super aggravating.You watch youtube videos and they talk about how polished the game is or whatever. Well that has certainly not been my experince with this game. To me this is the most poorly designed game I have played in a long long time. 99% of my time in the game has felt like I was fighting the game "mannerisms" rather than actually fighting other players or NPC enemies.All that said. Personally. Even if they fix all the above. The game is still not a good game. It has ZERO depth besides the PVP aspect. If you play PVE you are going to get bored in less than 3 hours. The PVP does seem pretty fun though. I haven't yet played enough to get into raiding, not entirely sure I will stick with the game beyond this point either. But I got into a number of fights on the road and they seemed pretty fun. I think I would probably enjoy castle raiding, but everything else about the game just makes the whole experince a huge drag. Like I am torn between continuing to play so I can do more PvP, and just absolutely hating the game design. Like. It is REALLY REALLY BAD.So.... Overall. I DO NOT recommend this game if you plan to play solo. I DO NOT recommend this game if you want an enjoyable PVE experince. I DO NOT recommend this game if you are not willing to put up with some really janky game systems, or whatever, honestly I don't even know what to call some of the games problems.I would recommend the game to someone who is interested in PVP and has friends to play with, but would caution them against taking all the youtube reviews and whatnot talking about the game polish with a grain of salt. The game looks great. But honestly doesn't work very well in many ways. Way too linear. Zero depth. And just LOTs of problems.***** Added after putting another 50 hours into the game.I still would not recommend this game to someone who wants a single player experience. I am still not a fan of the design of most boss fights and feel the balancing is simply wrong for a single player experience.However, you certainly CAN finish all the PvE elements solo, including all of the "raid bosses". Just be prepared to grind a bit beforehand. I personally found a server with double loot drops which significantly helped with progression and made playing the game much more comfortable as a solo player. So if you do plan to play this game solo, I would recommend a high loot drop server.However, I will say that the PvP is definitely a good time. After completing all the PvE content I spent a fair amount of time roaming popular areas and killing people and really enjoyed it. I never really got into raiding bases. Loot become pretty unimportant once you reach the endgame (at least on the non-full loot server with 2x loot drops that I mostly played on). You can just send out your servants to gather everything you need to keep yourself repaired and supplied with potions. But lurking around in rat form (because it hides your player name and health bar), and killing unsuspecting victims who happen to be in the area was quiet a bit of fun.Overall, I still wouldn't recommend this game based on the idea of it being a survival sandbox game. I think it barely fits with that genre. And I still wouldn't recommend it to solo players.However I am changing my recommendation from a No to a Yes. Simply because the endgame PvP is actually quiet a lot of fun. And I feel like most people who come to this game are probably looking for a PvP experience over a survival experience anyways. And although I never did figure out what was wrong with that blood shield spell (yes, it is still acting funny last time I tried it in combat. I honestly think maybe I just don't understand something about it), I just never use it anymore. it seems that the spells that I did end up using for PvP function quiet well. So... (shrugs).

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: It's... passably fun. An unenthusiastic thumbs up. Meets expectations but exceeds none of them.Longer version:I want to like this game more. It's styled, smooth, and doesn't feel unfair during pretty much any point of the game. But it doesn't... excite. It scratches the itches for building, but then doesn't really go beyond the minimum. The gear is.. uninspired, just a formulaic progression track that is a set of evenly stepped paces with no personality or style choices. It's a straightforward "get higher numbers, to beat the higher enemies, to get resources, to get higher numbers" rinse and repeat.I want to love this game, but every time I play it I end up mindlessly looking for "the next step" because it's all very laid out in front of you, with no reasoning beyond gear checks and recipe locks. Why can't I smelt iron? Because some bandit king needs to be beaten, but why? There's not a recipe for iron, you put iron in the smelter and it... melts... you don't need to know how. But here we are....I find myself comparing it to games like Valheim or 7daystodie, and in some ways, it does better. The weapons have skills, they let you be fluid in combat, highly mobile, and really change up your spells and how they function... but then... to what end? It all feels arbitrary, fruitless, because the next thing down the line has better numbers, so you're just going to drop some things to build them all over again.I play PvE, which is probably a bit part of it, I don't like having my ♥♥♥♥ stolen, I have a job, a life, I don't have time for starting over again and again. But the only joy I got really was hunting for high quality humans to nab and turn into followers, because it was more dynamic, the only check was my own cunning, restraint to not kill them, ability to pull them out of a group, and then snatch them away. But then... that was only to push the numbers game in my favor more.I want to love this game... but I just... can't... find anything to latch onto, it's like all the mechanisms are there that should make it a blast to play... but then there's no satisfaction, just... replacing one grind for the next grind, over and over.

So much fun...And then, time to farm again to repair your equipment, rinse and repeat.Most people who left a positive review have under 40 hours of playtime, meaning they didn't even play 1/3 of the game.If you don't plan to finish it and drop it around the 20 hours mark, then it's for you (and you're weird), if you plan to finish it, you'd better have nerves of steel.

_childDocuments_.review: The game every survival sand-box wishes it could be on launch of early-access. I'm floored. There are a number of amazing components that are huge, but the real winning components are the tiny pieces of detail the Devs worked in, like the true-to-folklore mechanics that remind you that, while you are a very powerful undead creature -- you have rules to play by. Little things that tickled me that I noticed:* Grass that doesn't get sunlight because you are blocking it out with magic bone fog with wither over time. I REALLY hope this was intentional, because holy heck I was impressed.* The assets are all lovingly made, and it is easy to make castles that look like something you could find in a AAA title.* The floor tiles have randomized dirt and grime for the workshop, so it doesn't just look like repeating tiles. Had this been a full release, it would have garnered a 9/10 for me. I am so excited to see what is coming next. I'm a huge vampire lore fan, and this just hits all those good buttons for me!

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I love the game, the idea and the concept.  it is a unique take on something that has been ingrained in our history, Vampires and people hunting vampires.  But then you might ask, well why the negative review,   For one simple reason, a game that is currently in active development and has a status of "Early Access" with *PAID* DLC, leaves a bad taste in my mouth.  Sure, on day one they released the Founders pack DLC which, at the time, and still at this time is valued more than what the game is.  And yes, I won't deny it either, I own the founder pack DLC.  So Again, why the negative review with the release of the new DLC?  Here is why; Someone took time out of the active development cycle of the game to make something that they could then turn around and monetize.  Sure it's only cosmetic items you might say, But who says that later they won't go further,  Who says that they won't slow boil us to the point where we end up with a pay-2-win cash-shop, or pay-2-win DLC?  This is what ARK: Survival Evolved did, then later invalidated that purchase with the release of other maps which included the DLC content.  We need to tell developers that this type of predatory business practice is unacceptable. So To Stunlock Studios, DO NOT release any more paid DLC while your game is in Early Access.  FINISH your game as you intended.  DO NOT cut content in an attempt to monetize it now.  If you want it in the game for the 1.0 release, great, add it.  But DO NOT do this again,  The players are watching you and they will quickly abandon you if you continue down this path.  At this point, Players would rather pay more up-front for the price of admission to your game knowing that they get the full experience that you intended instead of tacking things on like you are now.

_childDocuments_.review: V Rising puts an interesting twist on the resource gathering, base-building survival game. Your character is a vampire who is damaged by the sun and must either only go out at night or stick to the shadows during the day. To progress, you must kill bosses to unlock recipes for stations, materials, and abilities. V Rising's bosses are each unique in that they generally have a different specialty related to the recipe they unlock. For example, Clive the Firestarter unlocks a recipe for explosives. While V Rising's ideas are unique and the game has lots of potential, much of that potential is squandered by the game's execution. Boss fights are retardedly difficult, even with more than one player. Much of the difficulty stems from all your abilities being locked behind an animation. For instance, your character has a healing ability in which you can sacrifice some of your blood for health. However, the healing animation takes so much time that it is rendered practically useless. When your character does finally begin healing, the animation must continue uninterrupted. If you get hit, you instantly stop healing. There is also a craftable healing potion. But, like the healing ability, your character must complete the potion's consumption animation to begin healing. Also like the ability, the potion immediately stops healing you upon damage. V Rising's camera mechanics are also poor. The game's default camera controls require you to hold the right mouse button to move the camera's angle. Fortunately there is a mod that makes the game's camera functionality much better. Unfortunately, it seems that the developers can easily implement or have already implemented and are just not enabling the camera settings that the mod allows you to use. V Rising's poorly executed mechanics make progression nearly impossible at certain points. I was essentially stuck in a mid-game rut, unable to kill the next bosses I needed to progress until a friend and I discovered and began using the camera mod.This brings me to my next beef with the game. The developers have made poor choices with the game's execution, and neither they nor the game's community seem to care. Simply put, the community is AIDS. The game's official discord server has channels for feedback and suggestions. However, if you provide any even slightly negative feedback or make any suggestions that would even slightly alter the game, you will be ♥♥♥♥ on. It is unclear whether the developers are actually involved in the discord server, but if they are, they are only seeing an echo chamber affirming every poor decision they made with V Rising. To be clear, I enjoy the game overall. I love V Rising's progression system. I think the game has some great ideas. V Rising should have exploded in popularity. The only things holding the game back are its ignorant developers and cancerous community.

_childDocuments_.review: It is like they mixed crafting/building games with RPG and made you the bad guy. It is not for everyone and I strongly suggest watching a video of someone playing to see if it is your kind of game but so far all my friends that I have suggested the game to ended up loving it so much they bought a copy. That being said not much end game outside of PvP and the building is extremely restricted. An example for what I mean by restricted is that you are limited to 2 floors in your castle at default and super limited in tile placement as well. Those problems can be fixed by running your own server and customizing the rules (castles can be built up to 6 and floor tiles can be set to 600). Starting over after the update was a bit annoying as well but once again being able to change the rules when I made the server helped a ton with that issue (allowing you to set free crafting/building, make it more materials drop, speedup crafting, allow teleport while holding materials, slow/stop durability loss, and more). You can even set it so that your castle heart does not use the blood essence as often or disable it completely so that putting 1 in there will make it last forever (so you no longer need to worry about logging in once every few days just to feed the heart). Sadly there is no way in game to change those settings for a server that was already made (the only way to do it is to leave the game to edit the files manually or do some file juggling with a new server setup with the rules the way you want). In the end the game was worth what I paid for it, and I would recommend it to others with similar taste to me (thus the reason I suggest you watch videos of people playing/building in the game 1st to see if its something that looks good to you) but only as long as the price is below $35.00.

_childDocuments_.review: First game review I have ever felt compelled to make, purely because these devs deserve all the support we can give them. I have been playing Vrising off and on since it went into early access and have spent many hours (300+ as of this review) on it start to finish. So Ill get right to it with the pro's and con's. For clarity I have only played this PVE and solo so if PVP is your focus I cant help you there.PRO's: - Straight into early access this game could have been considered complete from the start.- Visually gorgeous and unique environment, love the art style and consistency.- Combat is super intuitive and flows well in PVE, its just punishing enough to be satisfying when you do win, and magic schools and weapon variety are pretty good. (even better with the recent Gloomrot update(pistols are my new favorite)- Paid DLC is all cosmetic only.- I love the survival aspect of dodging the sun and maintaining blood levels.- MASSIVE open world soft-gated by your equipment/power level (Think Valheim).- A good mixture of enemy variety, each area has their own melee, ranged, magic, brute, and animal enemy type etc.- The game play loop is fun going from your base out into the world, stuffing your inventory with resources and loot then returning to your castle, build, chill, pick your next boss or location to raid and repeat, slowly growing in power and wealth.- Speaking of castle building, its easily one of my favorite aspects of the game and its again even better with the recent Gloomrot update. - Its the only vampire game that for me satisfies that become your own Dracula kind of fantasy.Now... the cons -Its a pretty real grind for resources and they have fixed some of the RNG soft blocking of progression that used to bog the game down when they added the markets where you can by missing research recipes, but it is still pretty grindy.-Performance does drop a bit the longer you play the game but its not to bad and it has gotten better recently. - I'm an RPG lover and I do wish there were more ways to interact with the game world. You cant sit in your own chairs/couches for example. Pretty much if its not a crafting station of some kind you cant really interact with it. All you got is emotes and as a solo player there's not much use in them for me.All in all the game is overflowing with love from the devs and they really give life to this genre that is seriously lacking in newer additions to the vampire-theme game market. If you like the classic vampire mythos and a Valheim/Conan exiles type progression system with a Path of Exiles/Diablo control scheme than I say please give it a shot and support these awesome devs! :D
