_childDocuments_.review: V Rising is a great game, I strongly recommend. The game focuses on game play over lore. it is definitively an action survival style game with arpg influences. You must build your castle to make progress, and spend time in the dangerous world fighting to survive while gathering materials and defeating numerous bosses. What the game does not provide in lore it fills deep and wide with extremely deep and rich world artwork and extremely tasteful and artfully integrated vfx.It can be played solo or in groups and seems to scale bosses in a very fair way with cooperative play. You can get through the (PvE) game without deeply getting into builds, but also you can take the time to combine powers and items to increase the strength of you character substantially. Similarly you can get through the game without going too deep on most mechanics, but there is also a lovely poetry in the most effective combat motions and timings. The game has a good progression in difficulty without too much of a big ramp in any particular spot.The changes from the first release to Gloomrot were substantial, well chosen and executed and welcomed by the player base while positively contributing to most of the aforementioned gameplay aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that made me play in long sessions, 6-7 hours almost, something that a game hasn't done to me in a very long time. The game is definitely special; it is very unique, and what makes it so unique are the mechanics it offers. These mechanics, like different types of blood giving you different buffs depending on the quality of the blood, are genius. There are so many mechanics like this that keep you engaged, trying to perfect every minute detail.The art style is also really good. The characters are well designed, the bosses look great, and different regions feel distinct and unique in their own way. They look incredible, and that brings me to the world. Exploration is perfect here; you do it a couple of times to know what's what and then become familiar with the world. You now know what each region provides. The world is also perfectly sized, not feeling too dense or stretched. Another great thing is how alive the world is, with different factions and creatures fighting each other, making it super immersive.Farming resources doesn't feel tiring and is actually fun. You also have a way to farm resources passively, which makes sense, as you progress you don't want to be farming lower-value resources, etc. The combat is another plus point of the game; it feels epic. The abilities are new and fun, looking and feeling great. The combat is smooth, and battles feel great because of this. You also have a wide variety of skills to choose from depending on the situation and your playstyle. The bosses are fantastic. Each one is incredibly unique, and nothing feels repetitive at all. Boss battles are fun, hard, and super satisfying once you beat them.I also have to talk about the progression in this game. This too is very unique. Levels depend on gear levels, abilities can be switched, and you have multiple weapons, ensuring you are not tied down to a particular class. The game actually encourages you to be flexible. The bosses also give recipes that you need to progress. The building mechanic is also amazing, giving the right amount of freedom to build the castle the way you want while still fitting it into this world. There are enough styles and building options to create a unique castle of your dreams.Lastly, while creating a server, this game gives you complete control over your experience. There are settings to change and adjust literally everything. Don't want to grind too much? You can increase resource output by a lot. Want a more challenging experience? You can simply increase the bosses' health and reduce damage. That's the level of customization this game allows, something every survival game should be doing.This is easily one of the best games I've played this year, and I can't recommend it enough. This game has set the standards so high for survival games and made me realize what a perfect survival game looks like. Amazing combat, linear progression, incredible bosses, a solid building mechanic, and a beautiful world to lose yourself in.That being said, why is it not the perfect game? Because even with all this, the bosses didn't seem properly balanced. There were some bosses that were insanely hard when you tried soloing them but got steamrolled with 2-3 people, and there were bosses that felt impossible even with 2-3 folks. Another example would be bosses being super easy with no preparation at all, and with every buff the game could offer, the boss would still be crazy hard. This disparity is the only problem I have with this game, but that shouldn't stop you from playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Solid EA game, offer many hours of fun - However EA is VERY clear in the game, lack of customization and a very linear progressing makes the game feel slow and repetive. Its a solid start, no doubt. But WAIT a bit and give the devs time. Thats why im giving it a "NO". V Rising offers many great hunts, adventures, bosses and beautiful polished areas. It however lack a lot of customization when it comes to items. you litteraly go a gear level up each time. you repeat the same progress EVERY time. Craft a workbench, kill bosses for recipes, craft the gear and now repeat that 4 times. the game only has 6 different weapon types. Each has a unique style. To some this is perfect, however as a player who has been into RPGs since 98', the lack of customization just kills it for me. no exciting loot drops other than recipes - YAY ohh wauw! The game feels unbalanced and you'll die a lot. Expect many hours of running back to your corpse for each time you encounter a new boss. I did many of them Solo and im only missing the last 8 out of 37 I think. Many servers have castles everywhere and you wont be able to create your own. _childDocuments_.review: [Edit]A Diablo-esque, but every Loot item is identical.A crafter, but with only one item to craft.A Simcity builder, but you must play Fortnight to learn new buildings.An RPG, but you better be watching Netflix if you want a story.A rather petty waste of time.The problem is that this game ISNT what might be expected.It ISNT Diablo where you are creating/finding your preferred loadout. Loot isn't variable, and all advancement is locked behind boss kills. A google search will tell you exactly what gear you will own at any point in the game. There is quite literally just one option at every stage.It ISNT a gear-crafting game. You don't have a choice in crafting. New items are buildable only when the game allows you to, locked behind those boss kills. Crafting is in lock-step with progress. There is no flexibility or alternate pathways at all.It ISNT an RPG. There isn't any story, and no rationalie at all.As an ultimate sop to all the above limitations, you can modify the server settings to create whatever difficulty mix you want. But all you are really doing is reducing the difficulty of boss battles. Nothing else matters. But if the battles are too easy, then you will discover that the game has no content whatsoever to keep you entertained.So, unless you like the constant unending struggle and the 'git gud' approach, then I suggest you do this:Set the server settings to max out all tech, and mark all bosses defeated. Have fun building a castle. Delete the game. It isn't enough.[Original]SOLO PLAY REVIEW ONLYSo I'm playing solo in my own PvE world, and the game is a mix of great and awful. The genre, the graphics, the setup, the building - all top-notch stuff. Well worth a play and a look, and really fascinating and fun.Can you hear the 'but' coming?The game timing is off-target for solo. To kill a boss, you might want to clear mobs and terrain, you need some good blood which might not be nearby, you need to do all this before daylight, and you need, you need, you need. Coupled with the sad lack of healing options the timing complexity forces too much focus on the setup, and too little on actually enjoying the game and the combat. If you get any element of the timing wrong, it can totally invalidate your setup, and with no alternative option you often end up standing behind a tree waiting for the next night - totally and utterly wasting my available IRL time, which is a horrible design element unavoidable as part of the solo experience.I've played to the end of Act I, and I am becoming aware the game is totally on rails. The construction of equipment and abilities is locked behind bosses, which means that my fundamental loadout power tier is locked in. I can go looking for iron, but I cannot smelt or use it, which ruthlessly locks off other pathways to success. Comparisons to literally any other game of this genre creates an unflattering image for V Rising. Spell book options exist which is nice, but equipment is totally gated, and weapon choice is so narrow to be no choice. I hope this will change in later acts, but I'm not really hopeful given the careful and unfailing lock-down so far.So I'm left with an awful feeling that I'm going to be wasting a lot of my time waiting around doing nothing, in what is otherwise a beautifully crafted world and concept. Standing behind a tree is a bore, and there's nothing else to usefully do in that time. Yes, one third of your play time (in certain circumstances) can be spent in another part of your house doing the ironing. That waste of time colours my perception of the game irrevocably, and it is a total shame to be exposed to this outcome.For the solo experience to mean something more, it needs a few options : allow time to pass more rapidly (meditate, sleep, whatever), give an in-combat heal option (multi-player can have one person take the 'time' to drink a potion, whereas single player there isn't the gap to wait the interminable delay while you unstop the bottle, shake the bottle, lift the bottle...oh, you got hit already? - or allow a companion to enable off-tanking while guzzling your potion), lower the respawn timing to to allow at least a second chance after a failed first attempt. The number of bosses I've fought while I watch mobs and terrain re-spawn into the space I'm fighting is a laughably awful example of the one-size-fits-all (except you, Mr Solo) game design.Worth a play, for sure. But I've got to the point I'll try a boss a couple of times, and then just resort to the console codes to avoid getting frustrated by the game design. I just don't care to spend the time to bother. That's never happened before in a game, and my enjoyment and emotional link to the game are shattered as a result. I really would like to see what happens later, its just I can't say I care about the gameplay any more. It's like watching a netflix series while you are in another room o your house - just going through the motions but not really invested.What an awful thing to discover in what could have been a top-tier and defining experience in diablo-esque games.

Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. _childDocuments_.review: When I first heard of this game it instantly caught my attention, I have always been a fan of crafting survival games and the thought of a vampire twist to the genre was too hard to resist. Of course, being that this game is Early Access I was very hesitant to buy it... even if it was only $19.99. I started reading some of the reviews and a very high volume of those reviews claimed this game was not only very hard but also an extremely long grind and coming from a game that I have invested over 4000 hours in and still nowhere near end came content I ended up not buying this game... That is until it went on sale and decided to bite the bullet.Despite what most of the reviews said about this game it was not as hard as they made it out to be. There is a lot just a lot of different survival mechanics to this game because you are a vampire. For example, drinking blood is the key element to surviving this game you don't have to monitor thirst, hunger, or sleep. Another survival mechanic of this game is sun damage. Which I am not going to lie was really annoying at first because it made me scared to explore far away from my base out of fear, I would get stuck outside, but it didn't take long for me to get comfortable running around in the daytime as trees are very strategically placed so you can always find some sort of shade and protection from the sun. Now as far as the grinding aspect of the game I personally don't think this game is a grind whatsoever, but I may be a bit biased coming from a game where I would need to spend 200+ hours training a single skill to reach end game content for that skill.Now let’s cover some of the things I did like about this game and the things I didn't like about this game. So, starting with the thing I did like about the game. The gameplay of this game reminded me a lot of Diablo mixed with a little League of Legends both are games I enjoy. As far as the crafting a building aspect of the game it is very simple and easy to grasp. The leveling system in this game is very strange your level is determined by the items you have equipped and even though this felt odd at first it really helps progress the game very quickly if you don’t fixate on gathering resources. Finally, the combat in the game is super engaging and required you to learn boss mechanics and be strategic in your moves as well as the environment around you. Overall, I think the game has solid core mechanics.Now let’s talk about the things I didn't really like to much about the game. So, one of the things that I absolutely hated is the lack of guidance when starting out the game. You are basically taught how to attack and do basic item crafting. Which that alone took me almost an hour to figure out where to find the crafting menu which is hidden as a tab within your equipment menu. The tutorial is basically a little popup window in the corner that never goes away telling you to do generic things like cut trees or mine, as well as craft certain thing with no explanation why. Almost everything in the game that you craft must be unlocked via killing a certain boss or by researching books that are randomly found while exploring but the game doesn’t tell you this you have to figure it out on your own. So, this tutorial window will literally have you losing your mind telling you to craft something you haven’t even unlocked yet. Which is not an issue at all but when you are new to the game and have no idea what is going on it makes it very easy to quit and never look back. Fortunately, there were some great YouTube videos out there that really helped me understand what was going on.Now because this game is Early Access, I am forgiving them for all the learning pains cause by lack of information given to the players. After watching a player made tutorial this game was nothing but fun and I would totally recommend this game to anyone looking for a unique semi open world craft survival game.Recommendations- If you don’t plan on playing this game consistently every day or every other day let me save you the headache and tell you to make a private game. Bases in this game are on a timer require blood as upkeep so if forget to refill you castles heart with blood you will lose your base as well as all items you have stored inside the base essentially meaning you will need to start all over.If you play on a public server, try to stay on one of the official servers as most players can pay to host servers but a lot of times they’ll stop paying and have them shut down and you will lose all progress in game.

_childDocuments_.review: As somebody who played the game since launch I believe I can firmly say 10/10. This is early access and day 1 we had 40+ bosses...a year later we get a whole RE-VAMP with more enemies and bosses. This game takes the best of the games we love and makes them into one. There is tons to do ... GRINDING is going to be a must. I only play PVE and I never find myself short on battles to undertake. The search for 100% blood is REAL after the update...and the ability to increase low level blood is literally like Russian Roulette... Are you feeling Lucky? Building in this game had become extremely detailed from the floor tiles... to wall paper all the way to curtains and pictures. Literally Live your best VAMPIRE fantasy here. All playable content is free.. the only thing the DLC offers are cosmetic so no PAY TO WIN here.   I love the combat being skill based and the ability to play how you wish, you can go primarily physical or if you want you can throw spells at people left and right! And the devs pushed this even farther by allowing Gems for your abilities. And best part.. all of the gems are Random so there is always a chance of that GOD roll Gem out there. _childDocuments_.review: VRising is a weird game. A weird game that I can recommend very highly, but that I would definitely say isn't without flaws, especially when playing solo. It's a game that's almost fighting against itself, which is very ironical given what your final goal is supposed to be.This game is MEANT to be experienced in multiplayer first, and some of the designs for that purpose seep into the solo experience in a roughly negative way. There are ways to mitigate and improve the solo PVE experience, like disabling teleport limits, and decreasing crafting times, but there are some core aspects of the game that can't be changed and hurt a lot in those regards.For example, respawning will not let you use your own castles as respawn points, even if you own multiple waygates/coffins (unless it's the last coffin you've slept in), and even if you can actually use said waygates as fast travel locations from any other fixed waygates.Respawning will then make you wait for a full 5 second animation, which then will require you to wait another 5 second to transform or get a mount, just to start moving towards any destination after death. This is on top of an already present 5 second counter on death, plus screen transition. So that's roughly 20 seconds wasted doing nothing.And respawning, you will do very often. Especially in Brutal (which I've done the entirety of the game on). Not only will you have to wait those extra times just to be able to move, but you will often have to traverse on foot/horse for quite some distances, plus clearing out camps, as they have the potential to hinder some fights, unlike what you'd expect with boss designs inspired by Dark Souls. Imagine if in a souls game there was no fog walls and you had to clear every creep, otherwise they'd participate in the fight? Yeah, that's this game at times.And speaking of boss fights, this game is shining brilliantly at those, when they're good, they're insanely good (I'm still in awe of how the final boss was done), but some can be really frustrating, especially in how the mechanics are stacked. Some bosses are very methodical, with proper tells, where some others are more chaotic with AoEs thrown everywhere. Late game bosses are both at the same time, which can lead to some really unfair situations, with no possible ways to escape.The Shard Bearers, (final fight excluded as it actually dealt magistrally well with this upcoming issue), are some of the worst fights in the entire game, not due to the mechanics they present, but on how they are stacked together. There are a lot of really crazy good mechanics on paper that stack themselves with the boss or with another mechanic, but not necessarily with all of them together, and unfortunately, the Shard Bearers do stack all of them at once, sometimes to the point of just being an RNG fight. Solarus and Adam are the worst offenders of this. The problem with them isn't necessarily the fact of "being impossible", but rather "being possible if the worst never happens", which it will very often be happening.There are also a weird "balancing" decision around certain boss attacks that don't necessarily make sense. Magical AoEs and lasers counter counters. Understandable, as they would be way too strong otherwise. However, they state "Melee and projectile attacks" as what they block, and certain bosses will outright ignore these words. Tristan is an example of this, which made a very enjoyable, methodical fight into a frustrating die and retry on his third phase.But again, when the boss designs click, they click very hard. There are some creative ideas, some memorable designs and some things that newer game creators should take notes of. That final boss fight should be in any masterclass on boss designs.Not only did it deal with one of the worst parts of the game (the frustrating backtracking/clearing for retries), but every single move is crystal clear, every single part has a clear counter, and even though chaotic patterns are present, the methodical attacks will almost always let you have a way out if you keep your cool (unless you blew up your dash/counter too soon). This was one of my favorite boss fights of any game of all time, and hands down the best fight of the game.So do I recommend this game? Yes, of course I do! It's a fantastic package that will give you a lot to do either solo or multiplayer (though it's highly recommended to play multiplayer for a lot of the mechanics to "make sense, bosses are generally really enjoyable solo). If you're seeking a challenge, it'll definitely give it to you.However, keep in mind that it comes with its quirks, and that some of these quirks keep fighting against each other leading to some very frustrating moments. But still, definitely get it, it deserves a full completion!PS: For the devs: Please make a toggle for specialized storage to behave like unspecialized chests for quick stacking, for future players! Sorting inventory with specialized storage was so bad I actually had to resort to using lower tier unspecialized chests to quick stack out things (while separating wood products/stone products/metals, for example)!

_childDocuments_.review: I am someone who has played this game since early-access launch, and has played exclusively co-op or solo (as in, no PvP).I love this game, and sincerely whole-heartedly recommend it to anyone with a taste for open-world survival and Vampire games. A bizarrely specific niche, but one that clearly needed fulfillment. The game is clearly intended for online survival/PvP, but it is completely enjoyable solo or with friends privately.If playing solo, playing on normal is totally acceptable and sufficiently challenging. For co-op and additional play-throughs, definitely turn it up to the harder difficulty. I also personally recommend setting custom-server options to make constructing buildings free, but increasing the cost of making gear - this will make building a base more fun and tolerable, but still give you real reason to go harvesting resources. Do not be afraid to experiment with the different weapons and spells; most of them actually rock in different circumstances, and you will likely find that some bosses are better handled with alternative weapons.I want to make some recommendations to the developers, for future updates or DLC;1) Vampire hunters being wandering foes makes sense in the PvP environment, but I think it would be great if there was an option for co-op or solo servers for the vampire hunters to, in some way, actually track or randomly attack the players. I am sure that AI castle-siege mechanics are not really feasible, but instead it would be cool if there were some kind of regional heat mechanic where if you upset the populace enough you get vampire-hunter hit-squads after you, or maybe the natural patrols get stronger/larger/more common.2) I need Rapiers. Honestly, if you locked rapiers behind a DLC or something, I'd buy it. Similarly, I think it'd be sick to add Katanas as a weapon type. (Rapiers would probably act like a more light-weight spear with a built-in parry move, Katanas a kind of charge-up weapon.)3) I feel like it is an obvious missed-opportunity that we cannot place iron maidens or guillotines anywhere in our castles. I respect that the game needs to maintain a T rating, but it'd be sick to just have the items as cosmetic decorations. Similarly, please give us 'pile of gold' type decorations (and/or 'treasure-pile' floor tiles). I need to fill up my treasure vault like Scrooge McDuck.4) After defeating Dracula, it'd be cool to have a good reason to go on hard-mode V-Blood hunts. I would hesitate to give them weapon-shard drops (as it would detract from the need to do rifts) - but a motivation (outside of "it'll be fun!") to do additional extra-hard boss hunts would be nice. (edit: Maybe combine 3 and 4 here; maybe defeating v-bloods end-game unlocks bonus decorations? Like trophies?)Anyway,You knocked it outta the grave, Stunlock.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing this game for very little, i have just started it but i dont feel like giving it up at any moment. I have never been someone to like MMORPG's or such because the insane amount of hours farming seemed tedious to me and the leveling not as rewarding as it could be. This game though? Its a whole diffrernt story. The first thing i noticed is that you couldn't move your camera freely. So at first it was a bit uncomfortable for me to always be seeing my character from above instead on having a free camera to move around. Now i see that it is actually mre convinient since you can see the hitboxes better in combat. Now once you've done the tutorial and entered the forest you'll start building your castle. Now when i first saw that, i paniced since i have never understood MMORPG's base building system. But honestly... This game made it so easy for me and rewarding through time, you'll unlock vampire abilities such as transforming into several animals or being able to mindcontrol humans and turn them into minions. Which makes the game a whole lot cooler since you can get that "Dark Lord" fantasy experience which i personally always wanted.Another thing which is important to take into account is that the farming isnt as tedious as you'd expect, since you can always postpone your current quest to go on hunting for blood (there are several blood types which you can obtain from mobs, each mob has a different blood *quality* percentage, the higher the percentage, the better the quality and the stronger the buffs you recieve upon drinking that blood). You can become a Tank, DPS unit or Glass DPS unit, as well as a "creature" which you can obtain from animals and has buffs that increase your survival chances (resistance to sun, increased defense from attacks, walkspeed increase...)Its never tiring to play the game and there are also cosmetic dlc's that allow you to add a bit more style to your castle, animal transformations and your equipment. All in all, the game is great, it hooked me up right at the start. I greatly recommend it. - PD: Excuse me, my english is not the best, i know, thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: You want a yes or no?  Yes.  With a friend.  I always say that though.  It's a coop game, get a friend to play it with.If you're still reading, you're craving detail.  So... let's say it's kind of a top-down craft-and-survive game, except you're playing as a vampire, so there's a few interesting quirks.Being out in daylight is risky, though the shade thrown from a tree is enough to stop your delicate gothy skin from sizzling.  Various opponents have different blood types which, depending also on their "quality", gives your character some passive buffs when you tap in for a sip.  I'm making it sound almost like tapping a tree for sap.You'll do research by knocking over various enemies, you'll find resources you need for upgrades through murder, and your progression is basically charted strictly through your gear.  There's no experience points, so grinding doesn't do much of anything except stockpile resources.  There's just your kit, and the targetted assassinations you've made, and that's it.I own two other games similar to this one:  Core Keeper and Scrapnaut.  None of these are remotely as combat-intensive; this game rewards you for using timely parries, dodging, and evasion and it feels like it's got a nice bit of action to it.  It's possible to take on powerful foes but miscues will be severely punished.The default game mode is PvP, though.  Find yourself on a PvP server, and other players can attack you on sight, and judging by the moaning on Steam's forums, it doesn't take a great deal of time to be completely outclassed in the game.Or you can do as I did:  Run the game yourself, get your wife on, build a pretty castle and murder fools for their wine and cheese boards... and skills.  Mostly their skills.And for that, we got a game that looks nice, plays quite smoothly, and will be enjoyable for awhile.  For the price I paid for two copies, it's got the full 1.00 thumbs up here.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game. Was a 9/10 but act 3/4 bring it down. Due not I've played this solo five times now PVESince playing in early access I had the following complaints:Blueprint/unlock systemDurability(and more but they got resolved)I was hoping in the 1.0 version they would fix this but I feel they made blueprints worse and unchanged durability.The blueprint system is designed so bizarrely late game. Enemies drop the same amount of schematics as they do paper. But you need more schematics... why? Bosses are too high level to comfortably fight, but also you unlock the final research desk later act 3. Why? To be a similar level to these bosses you need unlocked blueprints. It's just baffling why the slowdown exists in act 3 when all the other acts feel fair and balanced for this. Additionally while their is more armor, it now takes quadruple the amount of time to unlock one set because there are others. Why? Why not give players a chest-plate blueprint that unlocks all chestplates. Then they choose what buffs they want. I feared this would happen when they were teasing 1.0 and it happened. Give the players more choice but sike, you need to grind another 4 hours to get that choice. Just throw on some random sets and be happy.Durability. This game does not need it. I don't understand why it exists (Okay for the shards it makes sense and I like the way the durability works for that as well). The fact that I don't feel like playing because my armor is about to break, is a problem. I don't want to leave my castle out of fear of pants breaking. I don't want to fight bosses or enemies because my durability will go down. It boils down to: too expensive to repair, and it stuff breaks way too fast. While fighting Dracula I went from 100->0 and was dealing 7 damage to him afterwards. The fact that is possible is horrible. The challenge should be the boss, not my gear suddenly breaking. I quite literally cannot think of a single reason this feature is in the game. The simplest solution would make durability cheaper to repair, but the core problem is still there. Like max out costs to like 4 of each item, not 7.Devs, I'm genuinely curious why you designed these the way they are. Not even in a condescending way, I want to know why, and what changes you've made to them already. I praise this game for being one of the few games out there, where the challenge is fighting the boss. Not  to the boss, not dying and  all your gear so you have to run naked to it. When you die, you can get right back to where you were (if I ignore durability). Like Valhiem has a repair system (which I do really like) that forces you to upgrade workbenches to utilize. This game doesn't have that. I'm curious what the devs have to say cause it might make me understand and appreciate these systems more cause currently I do not.TLDR: 8/10. Durability shouldn't exist, and act 3 blueprint system has sucked since at least gloomrot. If you want to look at the best grind/durability system in gaming, go look at Terraria. This game makes a lot of steps forward but these two back really make me want to give up when I play.

Between waiting for the Sun to go away, or mats to refine.Combat makes me feel like I just played Dragon Song on guitar. Early Access blues. _childDocuments_.review: I see that this is a good game for a lot of people, but... Not for me.Personally, I think the combat is very clunky and boring.The world is not interesting. It is small. You are basically just another beast in the forest, not a character, and there aren't other characters you interact with.Loot suxx a lot in the beginning - killing enemies is super boring because of it. Based on videos, loot improves a lot after many hours into the game, but it still doesn't seem great.The inventory is small, and running back and forth your base is yawn. You will always find items that disable teleportation for you as long as they are in your inventory. Which makes life super tedious.Half the day the sun is up, and will kill you if you are out in the open. I find this mechanic super, super annoying.Gathering is boring: it takes long, finding or exploiting a node does not feel rewarding.Your containers at the base are small, which would not be an issue, if they were all connected into one common inventory. _childDocuments_.review: Building gothic style and being a Vampire, yes please!You can do it alone but the bosses are hard if you do, and you kinda need the gear.The games beautiful, mechanically you're a vamp, sunlight = bad for you but you can tolerate a little. You can send out we will call them hirelings, but if you make a private game, it will take forever for you to make one, unless you want to join a current server but then you have pvp. The waiting time spoilt this aspect for us, but the builds are nice, and theres interesting items to create and how you style your build is up to you. Lots of planting and things to make. _childDocuments_.review: This is from a solo player in a private PVE server, default stats.The game starts fine and I had fun beating some bosses, some of them are really unfair and the end game is doable.. Is it fun tho at that point? No it's not.By now you lived through the constant spawning in your back, bosses that walks around paths go out of aggro and refill their HP inconsistently, bosses that spawn ads and ridiculous fast tracking attacks, chests that despawn while looting it and then you arrive to the final region to be welcome with Riflesman who makes you're mount irrelevant with their aim bot, mobs that shield and heals and you gotta farm in that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.So comes the problem with the gear and farm, it's all unappealing.You will farm Paper (50\1), Scroll (75\1) and Schematic (100\1) more than you'll ever imagine. Because in this game you must unlock everything through those items (the numbers on those item are the ratio for 1 unlock). The worst is it's in a form of a gatcha game, everything is random, from weapons to wallpapers to torch to floors to windows.. and there is ALOT. And to finish with the gear you so effortly farmed.. the only thing you should look forward is iLvL and Damage upgrade. I mean that game has only 2 Epic Set ( Mid and End game ) that included stats on them and they are (+4% movement speed, +4% attack speed) and (+6% movement speed, +6% attack speed). Not sure what was the point other than giving me hope I was gonna be able to make somehow a build but there is no such thing.The only positive thing I can give is that I really had WAY more fun building my castle. Yet again I would like to vote between a Yes and No, but it really got more frustrating than fun at the end.PS. Many hours accumulated were AFK.

_childDocuments_.review: V-rising is overall pretty decent (B-/C+ range). The fighting mechanics are FAR AND AWAY the most interesting part. You can figure out some interesting combos between the spells and weapons. Some of the bosses are quite difficult and interesting. The graphics are pretty good. Overall, the materials balancing and building leave quite a bit to be desired compared to other games (e.g., Valheim, Icarus). The servants can basically play the game for you if you have a dedicated server setup.Some suggestions/changes:-Castle raids would be interesting for PvE-Dying & respawning should drop your weapons and armor otherwise it's not very punishing-Horses should be able to drink from wells instead of giving them water sacks-The crafting patterns for the research (scrolls, schematics, paper) should come much earlier in the game. I never once needed the wood dust.-The need to enclose the special rooms with the floors makes the castle building pretty boring-V blood should fill your blood pool with good blood.-The carpet is terribly frustrating to use-There should be more variety of armor-Headgear should be more than just decoration-Some weapons should have de-buffs against certain types instead of just buffs-More special abilities for weapons are needed-Several of the crafting stations are good for ~5% of the game until you get the better one (why not just upgrade them?)-Some of the early game materials (e.g., copper) should still be needed later. Once you leave the Farbane Forest there is literally no reason to go back.-Crafting armor/weapons/potions should not take more than 5sec. I can understand waiting to craft basic materials but the rest are a kick in the pants to wait for

_childDocuments_.review: Embrace Your Inner VampireV Rising is a top-down PvP vampire survival game that sinks its teeth into players with a unique blend of fast-paced combat, survival mechanics, and immersive world-building. Developed by Stunlock Studios, it offers an addictively fun experience where you can live out your darkest vampire fantasies while honing your skills in both combat and crafting.Combat: Fast, Skill-Based, and ThrillingThe combat in V Rising is a standout feature. Skill-based and engaging, it keeps you on your toes as you dodge, strike, and drain the life out of your enemies. Whether you're facing off against other players in PvP battles or taking down powerful bosses in PvE, the fluidity of combat makes each encounter feel rewarding. You have a wide array of abilities, ranging from swift slashes to devastating vampiric magic, and timing is everything. Mastering your vampire's moveset is both challenging and fun, adding depth to the gameplay.Survival, Crafting, and Building: Satisfyingly DeepThe survival mechanics are surprisingly well-balanced, blending resource gathering, crafting, and base-building into a cohesive experience. As you stalk the night, you'll need to gather materials, craft better gear, and expand your gothic castle. Building your fortress is a key part of the game, and it’s incredibly satisfying to shape your dark domain, from basic structures to intricate dungeons that reflect your vampiric grandeur.The crafting system is deep but accessible, making progression feel meaningful. Whether you're creating new weapons or brewing potions to enhance your powers, the crafting loop keeps you invested without feeling like a grind.Community: Surprisingly WelcomingIn a genre often notorious for toxic communities, V Rising stands out with a much more approachable player base. PvP interactions are intense but respectful, and the online environment feels a lot less hostile compared to other survival games. Of course, you'll still have competitive moments, but there's a sense of camaraderie among vampire players that makes the experience enjoyable. Whether you're teaming up with friends or joining forces with strangers, the online community is surprisingly positive.Final Thoughts: Grab a Friend and Become VampiresV Rising offers a unique take on the survival genre by fusing it with vampire lore and skill-based combat. The game excels in providing a fun, immersive experience where you can truly feel like a powerful creature of the night. Whether you're crafting, battling, or building your dark empire, the game has something for everyone, and it’s especially fun with friends.If you're looking for a survival game that combines intense combat with satisfying progression, and a community that's less cutthroat than most, V Rising is a bloodthirsty delight. Grab a friend, sink your fangs in, and embrace the night!

_childDocuments_.review: So far i've got 600+ hours in the game and i can say i'd give a fair interview.Is the game worth its money? - Yes, even more rightfully so if its on saleI live under the ideology that if you play any game over 100/150+ hours is worth its moneyDoes it feel expensive? - Maybe?.. if you start comparing the cons to triple A games that are on winter/summer sales.All im saying is at this point for 35€ people start to have expectations and im not saying thats not a bad thing since players like to see the updates moving forward in their direction.The game has enormous space for improvement given the state thats in and considering now that we barely know what are the game's plans people are worried as they feel theres nothing to do once you beat Dracula (final boss) or organize your selfs some content and fight other players at pvp servers. In my opinion the game is in the fragilest state on which direction is gonna go, considering the game's value price went up when it became fully released. (and yes we're grateful for the few months heads up dont get me wrong)Here's some pros and cons i can give to the players and the devs to maybe consider something worth thinking, yet along implementing.- Interface once you launch the game needs ridiculous improvementMost of the players dont think about the approach they want to take in game but rather take the passenger seat and have expectations until they feel familiar with the game mechanics and designs. Imagine you're new player, you decide to play multiplayer and all the sudden you're supposed to be filtering and searching for servers not knowing what you're getting into (let me cook). It simply feels like you're launching game without knowing much while the official servers are mixed with the private ones and somehow its "distinguished" by adding some small icon on the side into the chaos of servers hosted. This needs priority of its own, official servers should be at the top and private servers on a different board since the game is being promoted trough this first sight and should say "HEY, we're in control, this is the norm, we invent the meta, and all these other servers are by other people making their own thing since they can choose to close it anytime THEY want". You want gamers to feel welcomed and somehow it doesnt have that, the game does not land you directly to its play and i would simply say.. if its not in direct sight, people who haven't played the game WILL NOT KNOW WHAT ANY OF THOSE OPTIONS MEAN SO THEY CAN UNDERSTAND THE NORM in the first place and just like that.. imminent lost of interest. Make the game more interface friendly.-Gameplay and designOnce you launch the game theres PLENTY of stuff to be surprised by .. the map is big, the bosses are well designed, on brutal mode its even making you even more invested to think "will i even make it? and then when you screw up, thinking (what the ....? the math aint mathing?) .. but turns out you're just bad as you take the approach more serious" and i like the unique approach that the game it self within feels like its alive as the environment is interacting with its own environment. A rare approach and it feels good for once as an observant to take uppon the opportunity of its self (yes bosses can kill even other bosses). You can do so much as improvement in building at your castle, transferring it completely to another location (well done on devs behalf for that by the way), while hunting for materials and chasing challenge on bosses and just like that, you snap your fingers.. 2 weeks of gaming are gone thinking "waiting a minute..!!". Hats off for that and thats how you know the game is good without implementing any micro transactions nor adding any specific gambling adictivity in it but rather letting you think you can do it with alternative ways on approaches. The cosmetics did an okey work as im pretty sure people would want more of it on long term improvement. For those who dont know, the DLCs have nice cosmetic stuff to be thinking about as every player has its own taste.Now the multiplayer side feels you're in shallow waters, depending on which mode you want to play (PvP or PvE). Tho we're grateful to have it, i rather talk about something that feels like missing in both of them so everyone can get my idea.The most annoying, if not the biggest frustrating thing they both share is the fog of war. Imagine coming to a pvp/pve server and wasting up to 2 hours so you can learn there is no space as the "abundant" info by the server isnt clear how many spots are actually taken so you have to waste time on your own. That on it self is a big turndown. Let devs do the math how much waste of time per person is wasted by searching a place on their servers as players are struggling to figure out where they can place their castle hearts! ITS NOT RIGHT and it needs fixing! (i dont care if people start getting defensive and start disagreeing on this with me by telling me how else this mechanic can be avoided because we all know its bad and it has to get fixed because nobody benefits from this as the map is permanently unlocked once u see it!!).-The PvP side lacks objectiveness (as they are currently now 2) one being the endgame bosses shards hold by players as shards and the events happening in the recently added zone. The option to chase players feels like activity you as a player need to make on your own and its fun untill you get bored out of it few times. The meta is oriented around taking other players heart down and breaching trough walls till u get it. Something thats really bothering is the stairs which are unbreakable as experienced players build walls of stairs so they cant be taken down to even enter its making even more annoying, so it feels like being stripped off out of an option. There is coloseum and other places that have nothing but space but im pretty sure theres space to add some minor rewards as in like when carriages start if someone wins a pvp fight or something that gives 1 hour of increased stat (some mini reward that cant be crafted but rather obtained trough participating where winner gets more, looser gets less to motivate them going at it.. im throwing wild ideas) but we need it rather than players coming up with their stuff for castle beaches ONLY.-The PvE sides lacks connectivity, unless you're in a clan, you cant heal others to help eachother, body blocking on spells is a thing so you dont deal damage on the boss but rather 0 damage to the target standing in front of it and you're starting to think im better off my own, people having trust issues of inviting you to a clan since you have imminent access to their entire goods, and you feel the fear in global chat as these things cripple them feeling insecure, unable to help someone with the research to help on a progress faster by coming from another server.. one thing i can THANK YOU FOR, IS FIXING THE ISSUE WITH THE PRISONER STEALING where people greef. I've also spoken to a lot of people in the pve servers and A LOT (i mean really a lot) of them agree that experience would improve mildly far if theres /pvp console command (player to player fight flagged only) in the pve servers as you ask for consent if the player wants to be taking pvp action or having just a zone where pvp is allowed. I simply dont understand the necessity of to why make a separated server for pvp no raids, where it only splits the players for it when you can kill two birds with one stone. Yes, theres too much work for it but its for the right cause.. it brings the community with a better interaction. But ofc. all these perspectives of mine are just a mere suggestion as far as advice goes by so devs can decide whats truly a priority. None the less, an awesome game that requires attention to small details which need fixing and objective matters that can attune it into an amazing pvp experience (not that it isnt but theres always room for improvement).Hope to see more

The game hasn't had new gameplay added for a long while, and it does become very stale because of it. _childDocuments_.review: From my PVE perspective with 200 hours of play on default settings:Fun game early on, love the building aspect too and I'm sure many will enjoy it but,Game is very grindy and that get's boring fast. I just eventually gave up.A lot of time is spent just organising and moving resources.Character feels weak for being a vampire.Movement is painfully slow for being a vampire.Daytime is incredibly annoying as sunlight kills you which means some things you'll have to wait till night time before doing them, or attempting them again. This can frustrate you when farming stuff or fighting bosses.Bosses are overturned and the last 3 are almost impossible to beat solo if you are not very skilled at these type of games. Most bosses summon tons of help and heal themselves so many times over that it's not a fun experience in any way but rather a test of patience to how much spammy and unfair disadvantages you can endure. Plus some attacks just seem unavoidable. Also if there are other enemies that happen to walk by they will happily join the fight and try to kill you. There is no way to heal instantly, heals are used slowly and work over time and stops working as soon as you take damage, making it near useless with the hard bosses. If the healing alone was improved somehow I suspect this would change my opinion so much on the boss fights too.Your level is determined by the gear you have and a lot of it is locked behind bosses. So if you are struggling with a certain area of the map or a boss there is nothing you can do or improve or level up to make it easier if you already have the best possible gear available to you.Many abilities / spells / ult's are useless.Changing forms is painfully slow.Cooldowns on abilities, especially dodge is too long and can make boss fights incredibly frustrating coupled with the already slow movement.Game has a lot of potential but the above mentioned really ruined the experience for me. It's fine in the beginning but get's progressively worse to the point of becoming a chore and just boring. I ended up spending more time just building stuff in the end. But, tbf, I guess for the money it's ok..but not great. I wouldn't want to start over though...

_childDocuments_.review: Decent survival action game with a flavouring of RPG combat, although somewhat under-cooked in each aspects of its undertaking.The game's presentation is great. Although the setting itself isn't unique, featuring very standard fantasy genre trope creatures, set pieces and designs. There isn't anything here that you haven't seen in other fantasy games, but this time you are playing as a vampire, so your castle exudes very Gothic styles and furniture. The graphics are nice, the lighting works well and night and day are remarkably different experiences visually. The only major dissonance here is really the use of low poly character models for the bosses and enemies, visually clashing with the detailed world assets.There is a decent amount of foliage and clutter, and each biome feels distinct enough from one another to encourage exploration and provide diversity. Sound design is decent, although nothing too memorable.Moving on to gameplay, the strengths and weaknesses are more pronounced. You play as a vampire with explicit goals of hunting down special bosses that award you new blueprints and powers on defeat. Similar to other genre staples, you can either use an altar at your castle to create a tracking trail that leads to the boss, or you can simply head to the area and find them as they are either always in an arena or have a set patrol route.The bosses are varied enough to feel fun, although the first half of the bosses are simply just enhanced mobs, and the last few bosses are where it gets more interesting and challenging. There is a need to plan the time you engage these bosses, as the game's day night cycle means that in the day when the sun is out you can possibly be caught in an arena basked in sunlight, which casts a deadly ray on your vampire that can quickly finish you off.The castle building is decent, and utilizes a gridbased expansion and construction system. This means that you can quickly build structures and alignment is easy, though it also means that the more avid builder might feel limited. There are a decent amount of crafting stations with your standard forge, woodwork, chemistry and sawmill, and a few other specific stations that involve blood refinement. Where the base building gets unique is the introduction of prison cells that allow you to lure charmed NPCs with a high blood quality back, imprisoning them and turning them into livestock. There are a number of farming stations available, although the steep material costs involved to even begin production of other materials can be off-putting. Crafting is one of the weakest points here, and while its generic tiered weapon crafting system is serviceable, the problem of the material acquisition rate rears its ugly head often. As an example, the mid game to late game crafting utilizes a lot of scourgestone in almost any high end crafting materials. Scourgestone is either found in graveyard areas, or crafted with a set of lesser materials that are still specific to find. Almost the entirety of your progression will be locked by scourgestone production rates, while other materials accumulate well into excess stacks. After the scourgestone drought ends, you will run into the next issue, scrolls, which are needed to randomly unlock a blueprint on your research desk, hoping for armor and weapon unlocks even as the RNG decides to unlock a furniture blueprint instead.All these crafting woes lead to a massive grind for resources, one that can only countered by playing in larger coop parties or if PVP, raiding other castles. There needs to be more loot spots or more enemies and loot drops per spot for some materials, especially ones that bleed into multiple recipes.The combat is quite engaging, it allows you to pick two spells, an ultimate and you have three weapon skills preset based on what weapon you are using. There are some neat combos here, and the telegraphing and real time evasion of attacks provide for a rather fun combat system that you can get better at with play. Much of the spell options are however, locked behind boss kills, and there is no other customisation which means that most players you encounter would be running similar builds that lack variety. You can select a class in essence by drinking blood from a creature or human of a particular class, and the quality of the blood determines how much buffs you receive. While interesting, it turns into a micromanagement game that can become annoying later on.Loot is mostly restricted to more materials for crafting, and bosses do not drop unique gear outside of the one or two that do early game. Gear scales upwards with pure stats, so a higher level sword does nothing but increase your damage, and adds nothing else. This bland tiered gearing system can rear its ugly head later on when you begin to feel like there is a lack of motivation to earn new gear.The game does have a lot of potential and is a blast to play with friends, but at the end of the day it feels like a lacking title that only slightly innovates from the standard genre tropes and then completely stops and doesn't take the game further. The systems work well together, but they do not work at the levels needed to make the game stand out. Early Access, keep an eye, decent for its price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an instant timeless classic. Was looking for something to fill the void until the Satisfactory update 6 release.  Even with Update 6 out now, i still haven't been able to put down V Rising. Setting up a dedicated server for me and my friends to play on was easy. Game mechanics are very well thought out. The developers put a lot into the UI as well. Seems very intuitive, by games for gamers.  Game is nearly perfect and still in Early Access. V Rising is the newest addition to my all-time top 5 games. My only complaint is that I can't explore the world in first-person. There is probably a mod out there to do this. Not even sure how combat could work that way, but for admiring your castle and screen shots it would be a cool option. Castle building and converting humans to your vampire servants is very cool. I love this feature. One of the coolest things in Conan Exiles was capturing and enslaving thralls. This is very similar, but in addition to converting, can capture and keep imprisoned as a blood bank. One castle for production of all goods and one to build a massive prison. However I changed the rules to allow 5 castles each on my server. The blood system in the game is really cool too. You get certain types of bonuses depending on the type of unit you consume, as well as different tiers of advanced abilities depending on how pure their blood is. 100% blood is awesome. When your blood pool runs out, you have to feed again, and blood abilities reset with each feeding. A whole cupboard filled with vials of 100% is game changing. Game is really fun solo, but Bosses are challenging and progressing through technology is impossible without defeating and drinking the blood of the bosses. It's nice to be able to team up with friends to take down bosses. Clan members basically share all resources and can build too. They can also learn all your technology, just by visiting your research table and clicking on items. Easy to power-level new players to get up to speed quickly. A full clan can make 8 castles total, 2 castles each if 4 members per clan, all shared. And the grind is really fun! It is possible to make grinding fun, just takes a talented dev team to pull it off. V Rising is all about the grind and its fun and rewarding. At first I was almost turned off by the art style. Thought the vampires looked kinda dumb, but it has grown on me. I love it now. Also highly recommend the game on triple monitors, because of the camera angle I see lots of resources off to the side I never would have spotted on one monitor.

As he realized that this might not happen, without any explanation or warning, he simply disappeared with the game server and Discord. Hours and hours of play to waste. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game, which makes this so incredibly frustrating. I spent three days playing this with friends, and none of us had a shred of enthusiasm in our voices after maybe hour 2. Just became a constant slog of asking how to make progress and getting back an answer that made me miserable because it meant I had to play more of this game.I don't like PvP games, so I played on a PvE server, and I think it's great that you can do that, but I feel like large swathes of balance decisions are made for PvP, which makes PvE unnecessarily miserable. Combat in this game is mindless, slow swinging at enemies that can chunk the hell out of your life and dodging on an EIGHT second cooldown at a Diablo-style camera angle. It's worth mentioning here that I also am not a Diablo fan, but at least in Diablo you had skill trees, and could make some kind of a build for your character. I was hoping this game would have some skill-trees to explore the different kind of vampires you could be, but that's not the case. You gain powers (and gear recipes) by tracking a target and then taking a long walk to find the boss, (sometimes the bosses will move so much they'll lead you away from their arena, and they'll notice they're out of bounds, and reset the fight, gaining all HP back)  and have a slog-fight with them until they die and you can drink their blood. Once you get their power, you'll realize "oh my god, I have to replace one of my abilities because I only have two ability slots." Two ability slots for magic does allow you to take a first attempt at a boss and say "actually I think I want this defensive skill instead of this ranged one" but that's more akin to finding a solution to a puzzle than it is making a character that works for you. Also, weapons have skills, but you get them by having that weapon be a certain material-level. Copper is the third tier of weapon, which gives you the first weapon skill of that weapon-type. Crafting takes so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ long. I don't know who looked at the speed at which items smelt in Minecraft and decided it should take ten times longer (recipes often take 60 seconds) and be split up across all the different rooms in your house. To craft some of the more useful items, you use a workbench, but that workbench will craft items for cheaper if it is on a Workshop Floor. Items including your armor, which is made out of materials that you use at the Tannery, or the Loom, which are both machines that receive that same efficiency bonus if they are on a floor that matches their type, just like the workshop, leading to me having to walk a full circuit around my base whenever I want to craft anything, because I wouldn't want to put a Workshop in my Tannery, because then the armor would cost more material because I made it in the Tannery where I keep all the armor materials, rather than the Workshop, where I keep the Woodworking things. I'm already steamed enough having to lay all this out, but just one more complaint. The blood system. Blood is the way you heal, even if that healing is only worth doing out of combat. When starting or respawning, you have the "Frailed" blood type, which gives no bonuses. You can drink the blood of most enemies, giving you their blood type, i.e. "Creature," "Warrior," "Rogue," etc.  These come at varying percentage-based levels (1% blood will give you nearly no bonus but is still worth it if you desperately need blood, 100% blood gives you all bonuses and buffs them) and are overwritten whenever you drink another blood, making all blood types merely passive, temporary bonuses that are doomed to be replaced next time you step to the sidelines to heal, consuming your blood, so you need more blood for next time you heal, so you sup upon the nearest Deer (Creature, 7%), losing the buffs you got from defeating and feeding from someone who had a blood type of Brute (57%). I hope this game can become better, I really do. But until then I will be refunding.

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely refined formula and refreshing take of the Valheim-like survival genre. It's got it all:- Day night system that encourages the player to do different things and prevents "burnout"- Extremely flexible, elegant, and extensive building mechanics- Solid and fun combat mechanics- Great enemy variety and challenging bosses with unique patterns- Beautiful world with a great sense of progression and pacing- An immersive lore and setting that meshes perfectly well with gameplay. Let's you roleplay to your hearts desires. Mind control your lowly human servants in your lavish vampirian castle, and imprison high quality humans and drain their blood for your enjoyment. ("You really fEeL like a vampire")Haven't been this addicted to a game since age 10.

_childDocuments_.review: The potential is there but the game has a ton of issues, which are well documented in other more competently written reviews. Not really worth the time nor money in it's current state especially if you plan on playing solo. I feel like the player numbers for the game will drop drastically once all the new players brought in by streamers and initial positive reviews realize how quickly the current gameplay loop becomes stale and extremely linear. Linear progression is a cardinal sin in open world survival games, it completely goes against the 'approach things however you like at your own pace' appeal they have. This is especially noticeable on the default server settings, due to how there is a sizable amount of grind involved and how that grind is artificially extended by time gates (looking at you 1h50m servant conversion timer) and how it's extremely easy to be set back an hour or two on PvP servers with ganking a plenty and no safeguards in place for high level players camping low level bosses or breaking into barely complete wooden bases with explosives or the utterly busted siege golems. TLDR;

_childDocuments_.review: Please ignore negative reviews. If you like games that feel like Albion Online (without the guild wars and constant PvP) you will probably love this game. Its your basic survival game, gather resources, build a castle, create weapons and get your gear score up to go into more dangerous places to progress your quests as well as gain access to create better equipment. You can pick up some weapons/armor, but its pretty rare. You will be crafting almost all of your things. This game is very centered around crafting and building up your Vampire Castle. I recommend playing on the PvE servers if you want to enjoy your time with friends without the constant worry of getting ganked. You will instead fight bosses together, ride horses together, and overall have a great time together. Definitely give this game a chance. _childDocuments_.review: Not terrible, but the whole premise is strange. As a vampire(millionaire) I feel that the entire project of building a cabin in the woods is beneath me. Why can't I just steal what I want? Character progression is on rails and entirely equipment based, but the equipment is simple and boring without randomization or interesting traits. Combat is OK, but heavy reliance on cooldown timers makes the game play like a cheezy MOBA, but with character control far less precise due to the very poor camera system. Base building is grid based and more constrained than I expected. The world is lovingly crafted and held my attention for a while. The game is well coded, stable, good performance. A good game overall, I can understand why people like it, but for me it doesn't do anything well enough for me to invest myself.

_childDocuments_.review: V Rising is not an EA product, let’s make that clear. The content already there could easily be considered enough for a full release. Plus, haven’t notice many bugs in my playtrough. The only thing is the I.A, kinda dumb, but not super dumb neither.I play alone and yeah, the farm and repetition is kinda absurd when playing alone but, it’s very relaxing and satisfying, so, on PVE server, you can easily play on your own and spend dozen hours( if not hundreds) chasing all your victims, while building a nice chateau for your vampire.Crafting is easy and intuitive, interface is neat and well organized, nothing much to say about that aspect. The point of view (from above your character) is, sometimes, confusing for the building part of the game but you get use to it quickly, nothing to worry about.It’s really a good action game with a nice crafting and survival layer put on top of it. Survival is not too invasive, which is nice, but present enough to key you on your toes in certain key moments (during fights or on the verge of a new day). Beware of the sun.The action part is really cool, and I think that’s what people love the most about the game: combats are fun, varied, and not that simple: you are weak and most enemies are powerful and will kill you very quickly.  That’s the main difference between V Rising and another survival with combat: the combat is good and a bit more “tactical” than the other ones.It’s cool to see “classical vampire aesthetic” for once, you really feel like some Dracula fighting to recover his/her power, the sense of progression is really well paced and very satisfying. Building is cool but limited, I don’t really care, I’m not a good builder, but you can create a nice comfy lair for your lord if you so desire.The heart of the game is sure PVP, and that can be a problem if you can’t find a nice group to play with. PVP is bringing one more layer of Stress in your expeditions, but you will be quickly overwhelmed if you play alone. Nevertheless, PVE servers are sufficient to have fun for a few dozen hours, which is more than enough for the price tag.The only thing I miss is  a sense of discovery and exploration of the world itself. It’s, for as far as I know, almost non-existent at the time and the world is kind of bland. No caves, no secrets, it might appear after, but, for now, it’s just a map with enemies on it to give the suck or resources nodes.Overall, a very good example of how to create a satisfying gameplay loop with ingredients we all know. They said that the the current build is far from their final vision about their game. It’s nice to know but, to be honest, the final game could be what we have now, it would have been widely sufficient for me. If they add more content or systems with time, it’s a good thing but you can dive into this one right now if you like crafting games and survival, it has enough content (and is polished enough). You’ll have a great time solo and a fantastic time in a group on a pvp server.  But you can def play solo, don’t worry.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, one of the best survival open world games that I have played! Acceptable grind. Ofcourse more fun if you have friends. But I don't have friends. Graphics are very nice considering it's a top-down game. The fact that you are a vampire, makes the day-night cycle special to you and it is quite balanced with addition of blood moon. The PvE elements have their own beef with eachother, so you can always be creative and use the environment to your cause. The character creation is decent enough but don't expect Conan Exile level to set the size of your wee-wee and boo-boo.As I said the grind is decent and leveling system is fair. So by the end of the day you will not be smelling sweat and piss all over the room.I would rate it 8/10. -2 deducted because I don't have friends and I want to take it on developers. Please fix!UPDATE on 01-Jun-2024: +2 added back because you can play Single-player if you are a poor miserable ♥♥♥♥ who doesn't have friends, just modify settings to make it suitable to your play style so this game is really cry-proof and sweat-proof if you want to!So 10/10! _childDocuments_.review: Title: V Rising: Immersive Dark Fantasy at Its FinestIntroduction:V Rising, is a PC video game that has taken the gaming community by storm. This dark fantasy title is a perfect blend of immersive gameplay, stunning visuals, and captivating storytelling. In this elaborate game review, we will delve into the various aspects that make V Rising an absolute must-buy for gamers seeking a rich and engaging experience.1.Immersive Dark Fantasy World:V Rising presents a meticulously crafted dark fantasy world that will leave players awestruck. From the moment you step foot into this gothic universe, you are enveloped in its haunting beauty. The attention to detail in the game's environment, architecture, and atmospheric effects is truly remarkable. Every corner of the world is teeming with secrets, mysteries, and lore, ensuring players are constantly engaged and eager to explore.2.Unique Vampire Gameplay:One of the standout features of V Rising is its innovative vampire gameplay mechanics. As a vampire protagonist, you have the freedom to choose your playstyle, whether it's stealthily lurking in the shadows, engaging in fast-paced combat, or using supernatural abilities to manipulate the environment. The game offers a wide range of vampiric powers and skills, allowing players to tailor their character's abilities to their preferred playstyle. This level of customization adds depth and replay value, making each playthrough a unique experience.3.Base Building and Resource Management:V Rising seamlessly combines action RPG elements with base building and resource management mechanics. As a powerful vampire, you have the opportunity to establish and expand your own castle. Building and customizing your lair not only serves as a personal sanctuary but also offers strategic advantages. Manage resources, recruit minions, and construct various facilities to enhance your powers and bolster your position in the world. The base building aspect adds a layer of depth to the gameplay and provides a sense of progression and ownership.4.Engaging Narrative and Quests:The narrative of V Rising is deeply immersive and captivating. Players are thrust into a morally ambiguous world filled with political intrigue, conflicting factions, and ancient rivalries. The game presents a web of intricate relationships, allowing players to make impactful choices that shape the outcome of their journey. The quests are thoughtfully designed, featuring memorable characters, well-written dialogue, and morally ambiguous decisions that challenge players' perspectives.5.Cooperative Multiplayer:V Rising offers an engaging cooperative multiplayer experience that allows players to team up with friends or other players online. Together, you can explore the vast open world, tackle challenging quests, and conquer formidable foes. Cooperative gameplay adds a new layer of excitement and camaraderie, encouraging collaboration and strategic coordination among players.6.Stunning Visuals and Audio:The visual fidelity of V Rising is simply breathtaking. From the hauntingly beautiful landscapes to the intricately designed character models, the attention to detail is evident in every aspect of the game. The atmospheric lighting, particle effects, and dynamic weather systems contribute to the overall immersion. Complemented by a hauntingly atmospheric soundtrack and immersive sound design, V Rising creates an audiovisual feast for the senses.Conclusion:V Rising is an exceptional PC video game that successfully merges dark fantasy, innovative vampire gameplay, base building mechanics, and cooperative multiplayer into one unforgettable experience. With its immersive world, rich storytelling, and engaging gameplay, V Rising is a must-buy for gamers seeking a deep and captivating adventure. Prepare to be enthralled by its dark allure and indulge in the power of the night. Welcome to the world of V Rising!

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game! The boss fights are really fun and each one unique, the base build is simple to figure out whilst having quite a few designing options giving creative freedom, and there are alot of fun options to switch up your fighting style with different weapons (each having their own attacks), spells and ultimates. They have really done a good job at including the classic vampire things as game mechanics such as not being able to walk in the sun, being vulnerable to garlic and silver as well as having to search for blood. I've seen people compare it to valheim and in some ways there are for sure similarities but I'd say this game is more enjoyable because its less grindy (you can get servants to help you farm for stuff) and the different weapon abilites and spells makes fighting better in this game imo. I'm excited to see where this game will go as it develops but its already a really good game! I've played it both solo and with friends and its fun either way. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game.  Time will tell if they do the usual "survival game abandonment" thing but for an early access release it is very polished and full of content.  For perspective, ~5 of us have been playing on a private dedicated PvE server and we are almost 40 hours in and getting near the end of the PvE content.  I'm sure you can rush much faster, but being able to enjoy 40+ hours of PvE only content in a game like this is a very good sign.Jumping into a public server with PvP would only open up things much more... if the PvP rules were setup and balanced correctly.As long as the developers continue to improve the game, add some more quality of life features and flush out the content and balance this will be a great game to play.   My main concern is that they release the game as 1.0 with the content we see now and call it done forever and abandon the game.  I think a game like this would really benefit from continued support, more added content, new  areas to explore, harder content to push, dynamic events, raids, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't quite what I expected, even having seen people play the game.BAD:1. It's ALWAYS ONLINE, even single-player. Not a deal-breaker for me, but still sucks for people with spotty internet.2. You can LOSE YOUR PROGRESS if you don't continue playing, because your castle "decays" in REAL TIME whether you are logged in or not and REQUIRES MAINTENANCE. This can be attenuated through settings when starting a "server", but those settings cannot be adjusted after starting the server. I don't like games that make you feel OBLIGATED to play or you'll LOSE EVERYTHING.3. The default settings force you to WASTE A LOT OF TIME IN TRANSIT in a way that adds nothing to the gameplay experience except you dying sooner in real life having watched your video game character auto-run along a path because your inventory is full.3. The game doesn't really have an "end-game" and it's really just a series of upgrades and objectives that will take you 30+ hours to complete on your first attempt. No real story to speak of either.GOOD:1. You can fix most of the bad parts of the game by changing settings at the beginning. These settings can only be set ONCE, however, and cannot be modified afterwards without starting a whole new game.You will probably start your game over once or twice as you try to figure out what settings work for you. MY SUGGESTIONS: Turn "portal bound items" off, set "crafting rate" and "refining rate" to 1.5, and set "castle heart decay rate" to 0.1. This will make the game significantly more enjoyable & will make it much easier to not lose all your progress if you don't play for a bit!!!Also: Play with friends!
