_childDocuments_.review: This game is very Reddit. From the cringe dialogue to the “progressive” themes, it’s pretty clear which collective of stereotypes were responsible for making this game.You would think such a lighthearted and casual game about delivering mail through a stylized whimsical forest wouldn’t suffer from these issues, but then you’d be subjected to read the caterpillar fire off dozens of few-word dialogue lines in quirky 2023 meme-speak, or listen to your character’s remarks about capitalism during a delivery with the landlord that acts like what every Liberal Arts major assumes they act like.I’ve rolled my eyes so much over the past hour and a half I’m pretty sure you can see my optic nerve. If you’re a Tumblr enthusiast or have a few extra bucks you saved buying your soylent in bulk, this game’s definitely for you. If not.. this game’s not worth it’s weight in Reddit gold.

_childDocuments_.review: Yikes, I spent money on this game?I saw the review score, screenshots, perused the steam store page, and put it on my wishlist. Bought it half a year later without thinking too much of it and now finally playing it, I'm just disappointed. - The full controller support is an absolute lie or at least incredibly unwieldy. I gave up trying to navigate the menus and options with the controller entirely after fiddling with it. - This game is apparently only 2 or so hours, asking quite a lot for a $20 price tag. I would expect a lot from the game if that is the case but...- This game looks and feels super amaetur-ish. The 2d art, setting, dialogue, and other cozy aspects are pretty cozy but where the game actually takes place isn't great. Maybe you can chalk it up to bad optimization since the game looks ugly at medium settings but still doesn't give good performance. The animation is absolutely awful. You'd think with the majority of your actions being walk, run, jump, and glide, they would animate and feel great but they don't. It is pretty cozy but there are much better alternatives at a better price point. I regret paying any money for this game personally and I'm not sure if I would play it if it was free. I don't think I would be so harsh if not for the price tag. Charging $20 in general opens the game up to a lot of criticism as opposed to $10 and sets up expectations for the consumer that this game fails to meet.

_childDocuments_.review: This is really something that has very little substance. I am just glad I got it as part of a bundle, so in perspective, I paid it few dollars.The game is non-existent... It is advertised as cute relaxing game where you go around delivering mail and interacting with people, creating some sort of connections; but the game itself has really very little about that.The map has no way to orient yourself; so you walk around and have to learn where each person is. The first thing you are told is to talk to someone to deliver this mail. and off you go without any reference about where to go.You then talk to the first soul on the street and this person is not exactly that great in giving you even an idea of where to find that recipient... It is like whoever designed this city hate so much any sort of addressing system, but still wanted to create a mail system.So you wander around for a bit, meet more people, which are the most obnoxious characters you may find around, and have very little cuteness (nothing like the images you see; one person is literally so in love with his money that borderline grotesque), which will give you mail to deliver.So... You find those folks and you think your job is done? Nope... Then you become a helper and need to find stuff for these people to help them. So what is this game? A delivery game? A helper game? A mix of different genres? Can't really tell because it does not do a single thing straight and end up just being confusing and approximate.Controls are fine, graphics is very simplistic, and remind me of the first Unity games from 2018; not sure if the game is made for adults or kids or what not, but I have hard time to get the actual target for this game and what they were going for.I was expecting some sort of relaxing cozy game, from what I saw in the trailer; where you deliver mail in this forest environment to strange folks, but it ended up being like a colorful version of conker's bad fur day without the nasty stuff, mixed with animal crossing and another 10 different games.No offense, but I am not sure what this game is supposed to be, and really do not appeal to me at all (and I play a ton of relaxing games; that people would call boring, mind you).4 out of 10 for me; avoid even at a discount; there are other platformers; and if you want to deliver mail and talk to people, buy Lake instead

this was itching at the back of my mind as i kept delivering stuff to other characters that had no idea who greg was or making side quests(of sorts. fetch side quests). but by pure luck mid-game...you see, the platformer action in this game is quite bad/annoying/imprecise and the "gliding" thing very frustrating. i found the only "person" in town who knew where the fella would be(while i wanted to glide somewhere else and ended up landing on there) and THEN understood that the delivery i thought would be the first was gonna actually wrap things up. like, with no chance to go back and do other stuff or in general still have access to the sandbox. it ends ENDS the game.this game would really really benefit from a map(with options for showing where characters and items are) and better controls. 2-3 ish hours go by and you finally feel more comfortable doing miracles with the sorta bad platforming + controls and at this point actually knowing where characters are, and the different areas get clearly defined in your head. the game feels even better!!! too bad, it's the end, you've finished your "dialogue arc" with the critters, the sandbox/world starts feeling void and all you can do at this point is go after completionist stuff(IF you want and haven't already), then "greg". and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ are the very last few additional things hard to find, with both the lack of a map and still uncomfortable-ish movement mechanics. i think the devs were going for a simple experience with replay value, but I feel like there's none unless idk I get more amnesiac from yet another concussion. had one recently. anyway, well that wraps it up. It's a flawed but cute...game...thing. love love love the music in it. hope they work on updates, patches and so on later. also, you can tell it was done with lots of love and dedication regardless, it really shows, and I look forward to seeing the devs' next works!

_childDocuments_.review: is a very easy action-adventure/platformer in a fantasy setting. The protagonist, who is a Mail Scout, delivers various parcels and letters from and to residents of a small valley. The story is completely linear and there is only one ending. The character customisation is reasonably well done - name, gender, hair and skin colour, and the outfit can be chosen at the beginning, while during the game, there are several mushroom hats to find. The chosen appearance is shown both on the 3D model and the 2D sprite. All abilities, such as gliding and double jump, are available from the start and it is very easy to use them. The controls, while not rebindable, are generally comfortable, with both WASD and arrow keys being assigned to movement. The world is of reasonable size, almost fully open from the start, and does not have a map, though there is a quest journal and an unlimited inventory. The quests involve finding items or NPC on the map. The protagonist auto-dialogues away upon interacting with an NPC. While the writing is lovely, the lack of interactivity in dialogues is not. The graphics and visual style are very clear and expressive, with the characters and interactive items being reasonably easy to notice (the NPCs have exclamation marks above their heads and the items sparkle or rotate). The music is present and not annoying, and there is no voice acting. The game has only 1 save slot, which auto-saves the progress frequently, so the only option for save file management is Windows Explorer. Though, as mentioned, the story is linear and short (3-4 hours for all quests), so, unless one really likes the very well done platforming, one playthrough is all it takes to experience everything the game has to offer. I have encountered only two minor bugs (an invisible NPC in the epilogue and the collectibles unlocking incorrect hats).Overall, I would recommend the game when it is on sale. The lack of dialogue choices, rebindable controls, and save file management are more unappealing than the length of a playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: My son got this game for me for Mother's Day.  I do like cozy games, and I thought the art style was cute and promising, so I gave it a shot.  The pluses: I played for about an hour, talked to several characters, and explored the area a bit.  The art is great.  I really enjoyed the cute customisation possibilities.  I love the creativity with the little backpack and the envelope gliders.  Each character was fun, really catchy drawings.  I never found Greg, but I liked the character looks of the ones I did find.  I enjoyed the scenery and I really got a kick out of the old-style animations during the dialogue.   It wouldn't have been my choice of game at the outset because it appeared to be what it is: a bunch of fetch-quests, my least favourite side-quest.  That said, they were cute. The music was pretty good for this style of game, as well.     The not so pluses:  Really horribly glitchy, and the dialogue is frankly just *painful*.  The art is fantastic, but the reading killed it.  It's like reading a Discord chat typed by semi-unconscious 10 year olds, only less dynamic.  Way too much slang, no punctuation or capitalisation, and just zero personality because of the overabundance of l33t-speak or otherwise lazy writing.    When I say glitchy.... I kept getting stuck in the scenery.  Under mushrooms, behind flower stems, etc.   I appreciate having a pop-out button, and I know programming isn't the easiest thing to do.  However, it gets old constantly having to reset.   I didn't have any crashes, but I only played an hour, so.  Overall: I think this is a great start for an entry-level programmer.  There's the seeds of a really great game, and a clear intelligence and creativity behind the concept.  That said, it's not there yet, especially not at this price point. I encourage the creators to keep going! But I don't recommend buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: You're a mini mushroom-loving elf who delivers  to all the animal townsfolk! Each of them have a unique personality and they're very endearing :) Incredibly cute and silly humour with positive, meaningful messages! This game has that fairytale and cottagecore aesthetic down perfectly! The artstyle is hand-drawn with very calming colours! The soundtrack has about 14 songs and matches the whimsical forest adventure vibe perfectly! It's just super adorable & cozy with a great mix of 3D platforming! You can bounce on mushrooms and glide off the tops of flowers, hills, rooftops or bridges to travel around the differently themed areas of the map! You have to genuinely think about how to get to some places and secrets, since the world is gigantic compared to you! Helpful quest, item collection and achievement tabs with tooltips to show you what something might be for or how many of an item/action you still need!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall very cute but there were a couple bugs that were quite annoying.The mouse cursor kept bugging out wich made it pretty hard to move the camera properly. I could do it by holding the button down and then moving the mouse but the movement speed was inconsistent and it got tiring to hold, adjust, run into the screen borders, let go, move back to the middle, rinse, repeat. Restarting the game did solve it but it happened often enough that I couldn't be bothered towards the end.Then next, to unlock hats you can collect mushroom samples and give them to an NPC. It was a fun minigame but on the last round of mushrooms I couldn't hand them over. I had the samples, the NPC had the icon that meant I could progress in the quest but every time i spoke to the NPC my character claimed I hadn't found them yet and got told what to look for again. I really wanted to see the red cage one, but couldn't get it unlocked. I gave it a second and even third try. You can't give them earlier than they are asked for. They do disappear from the inventory but it doesn't unlock the corresponding hats. Giving all the mushroom samples at once doesn't work either, the NPC just won't take any of them when you do that. To be fair though, the hats you CAN get are really cute and you do have something that matches with every outfit.Now, the ending was triggered without me doing the required task. I don't think there was much I missed with it (I was just supposed to move to another location) but it was still annoying. The VERY end wouldn't let me talk to all the NPCs. They were all too close together so I kept talking to the same NPCs while i couldn't get the others' dialog. Eventually I triggered the credits because I didn't realise that I was too close to the NPC you're supposed to speak when you want to leave. So yeah ...I would still say I enjoyed this. The game is really cute and cosy, the lore is fun, if a bit sparse at times (looking at you, Worm-Man), it can be a bit tricky to reach all the places and gather the collectibles but all of it was doable with checking out the terrain a bit so that was challenging in a fun way. Despite the bugs being annoying they don't make the game unplayable. The mouse bug is bad but to be honest, in my first playthrough it only happend once and was an easy and quick fix. It did get really persistent on my last but clearly that isn't something that always happens. My best bet is that I clicked too fast since I skipped over everything then and the game lagged behind and then didn't remove the cursor from my screen anymore. It's cute, it's fun, I'm happy.

_childDocuments_.review: This is just a fun, colourful low-poly fetch quest/collectathon style game where you play a mushroom capped postal trainee sent out to deliver a message to an unknown character in an unknown location, and along the way you will meet many animal characters who will bombard you with letters to deliver to other characters as well as a series of fetch quests to fulfill their requests.In terms of positive features, the game is just plain fun and a delight to play, the world is just big enough to require you to explore without overwhelming you with too expansive of a playground (believe me, you'll have a hard enough time as it is remembering where all the characters are!), and while low-poly, the environments are still a pleasure to roam around, especially the quite accurate flower types.As for some negative, the character art (not the in-game polygonal, 3-d models, but the 2-d artwork used during conversations) is rather bland and even a bit ugly.  Additionally, the gliding/jumping can be janky and difficult to maneuver with.  Oh, and some of the dialogue is too twee by half......throttle back on the obnoxiously cute stuff folks, before someone barfs on their moniters!Still, while it can be a little (or a LOT!) too cute for its own good, it's a nice, cozy diversion from longer, more serious games (and all achievements can be fairly easily obtained just by progressing through the game without elaborate and complicated/time-consuming wankery).Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games (minor spoilers ahead).Mail Time is a short casual low budget exploration/walking simulator game where you play as an apprentice mailman that needs to make deliveries between several different characters, but you’re not a human but a small gnome that will have to explore a forest where everything is bigger than you, even flowers and small objects. The other NPCs you interact with have the same size as you but are different kinds of animals, with their own personalities and hobbies.The game engine is 3D with simplified and oversized object models. The game world is cute, colorful and beautiful but rather small. The conversion screens have 2D drawings of the characters and speech bubbles like a comic. The game also has a character editor with many different options regarding clothing and the items you use. The music is calm and very relaxing and helps setting the mood of the game, but like most low budget indies it doesn’t have voice narration, unfortunately.The gameplay is simple: you talk to the characters and they will give you tasks, but to be efficient it’s better to get several requests at the same time and do as many in one trip around the world as possible. There are also several different types of collectibles to get but if you get to vantage points and look around you can spot most of them and I didn’t need a guide to find any of them, just explore every corner, the game world is not very big.   23 Achievements. 2 hours Easy. Easy, exploring the world carefully and completing every sidequest is enough to get every achievement. One of them didn’t pop up when I expected it but I got it at the end of the game. Other reviews said that there are no missable achievements but just to be safe it’s better to get all the collectibles before completing all the quests. Mail Time is a short casual low budget walking simulator that looks cute and charming, set in a world that is fun to explore and with some collectibles and side quests to complete. While targeted more at children it can be enjoyed by everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: 4h 1/10 1 No, but you don't need a guide No No, since the new patch the game has no missable achievements anymore.  Not really, the 15-minute gliding feels a bit long but easily doable No Only 1 that is for delivering mail within 30 seconds, but can be easily done at the start of the game or later on when going from the "upstairs neighbors" back to the person you originally came from, as it is just a jump down No No No difficulty option No unobtainable achievements anymore after the patch that released June 2023In Mail Time you play as a mail scout on their first job. Before you start you get quite some options for designing your main character, which was already so sweet. And when the game starts you're very soon on your way to delivering your first mail. The game drips with humor and cuteness right from the start! I loved to just go to high places to just look around this beautiful world, as well as to glide down.Mail Time is an adventure game that doesn't give you any time limit, you can just enjoy the game, take your time to look around, and explore the woods. So it is stress-free, which is a bonus in wholesome games. You have to deliver mail to multiple animals that live here.. and maybe not only mail but also some other stuff. You'll get to know the animals and their storyline even in the short interactions you'll have with them. I would recommend reading the dialog, as it is full of funny punchlines and asking questions of general conceptions. And I won't spoil the story but let me tell you that it has an important and wholesome message. So play Mail time and get soaked in cuteness and wholesomeness!Mail Time has a very nice achievement list, and it comes down to just completing everything there is. You can go back after finishing the game. This changed in a patch that got released in June 2023. This makes that probably only one missable is delivering a mail under 30 seconds, but since this can be done right at the start of the game, I would not call this a missable achievement.

_childDocuments_.review: After 8 hours of playtime, I have officially finished and completed this game. I'll start out saying that it is your typical cute and cozy video game. If you enjoy cozy games just in general, especially cottage core aesthetics, you'll probably enjoy this game.However, I wouldn't call this game relaxing, at least it wasn't for me. I'd say it was 60% relaxing. The game needs to incorporate a map system to make it easier to find all the people you deliver mail to. Without having one included I had to look up fan made maps as well as YouTube videos to try and track down some of the characters, or even to just remember where they are from where my character was standing at the time. This was frustrating to me and added a lot of extra unnecessary time to my game play that I didn't enjoy. The game would be so much smoother if a map system was incorporated with little character icons of where you need to head to next. After about the 6.5-7 hour mark I *finally* was able to kind of understand the lay of the land.. but for such a short game it shouldn't have taken me that long to figure out. Despite all of this I do think the game is an interesting and somewhat fun play. But the lack of map system really made the game kind of unbearable to deal with. If you are okay with going at a snail speed most of the time in such a short game then I recommend it. If you lack the patience or are bad at direction in video games then this one is certainly not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Now i dont write review usually...but for this i had to.Its a cute short game you can finish in under 3 hours but 20 euros are way too expensive for it.. I got the game for like 2 euros as a key because i wasnt willing to pay full price. 5-10 euros are fine, 20 is a ripoff for a buggy unfinished indie game. Compare it to Stardew (another cozy indie game) its priced at around 15 euros, cheaper, and has hundreds or thousands of hours of playtime. Donut County is cheaper as well (almost half the price) and is another cozy more puzzle-focused short game. Hand drawn indie game is one thing, 20 euro price tag another. I see the effort of the devs but this is too much.BUGS:- The game is very buggy, sometimes glitching out and movement input doesnt work anymore until you repeatedly talk to someone and the controls reset into letting you move.- Theres controller mapping included for xbox/playstation and even switch but they dont work sometimes either..you have to mess around with it since there arent any 'connect controller' or 'switch to controller' settings. - Other people complained about game breaking bugs where they cant pick up items anymore as well..IMMERSION:Apart from that some visuals or texts are breaking the immersion.- Soks (the caterpillar's) antenna has a different color in the Sprite vs in the actual 3D model. - Kaz (the Raven) speaks french from time to time (in the english version, idk about other languages) and that would be fine if it were a few simple words, but he speaks full on french sentences..without there being a translation in a letterbox after or in a smaller font below. - Some of the quests are unfinished. You have Soks talking about the Frog controlling worms, yet when you talk to the Frog about it he wont say anything, nor does Soks follow up on this.You cant expect a global audience to speak a language they didnt put the game settings into.OVERALL:The game itself is cute and some of the dialogue is really funny. I mean where do you get an angry Caterpillar calling you dumb and about to throw hands or a schizophrenic hallucinating Rat that sniffed too much gunpowder? Plus you got a literal Forest Mafia scamming an egotistical capitalistic Landlord Cat out of his money. Yet, again, 20 euros is too steep for a game like this. The game is fun, although buggy, unfinished and short. If you do get it, i'd advice waiting for a sale or getting a cheap key. View the devs like the capitalist Cat ingame if you want. Its a good analogy. However for the price and sometimes gamebreaking bugs i cant recommend it in the current state. The devs stated they were finished working on this game, so i dont expect any future updates either.

_childDocuments_.review: i really wanted to like this game. I bought it expecting an experience similar to that of Lil Gator Game or Here Comes Niko, but with a sort of foresty aesthetic. I'm not sure if it was due to my expectations or what, but this game ended up greatly disappointing me.The visuals are okay, I thought the art was very well made and cute, and the character designs felt unique enough for each one (with the exception of the bunnies). Other than that, the environment and artstyle looks like something out of a children's picture book, which I don't think is a bad concept at all, but definitely wore itself out towards the end of the game.The gameplay left a lot to be desired. The movement of the character feels very floaty and slow, and with no faster way of getting around other than just walking, it can get pretty annoying. In terms of the game itself, its a mere series of fetch quests around the map. Talk to this character, give this character something, now go back to that first character, you get the idea. I don't think a game like this is a bad idea if it's done right, but the gameplay was the exact same throughout the entire game and by the end of it it just felt tedious.Speaking of which, this game is short. I managed to finish it in less than two hours (I will not be refunding). Granted, I didn't go the extra mile and grab every achievement and get 100%, but with there being no postgame, or map or hint system or anything to help you track down any missing collectibles, I felt no desire to try for completion.And then there's bugs. a lot of them. This game might be one of the most broken games I have ever played. about 4 times during my 1.8 hours of play my character would randomly sit down, get back up, and then I wouldn't be able to move at all, forcing me to restart the game. Achievements and whatnot were constantly popping up covering the entire screen as I was trying to talk to the NPCs, which I would have to get rid of so that i could focus on what the NPCs were saying so that I didnt get lost on where I was supposed to go. The soundtrack being dynamic as you're in different ideas is a fine idea on paper, but it's way too obvious when a track stops and starts, with the previous area's track cutting off and the next one's starting as if you had crossed an invisible line.Overall, this game had a lot of potential, but unfortunately fell flat in quite a few areas. And 30 NZ dollars for such a short game is damn near extortionate, so if you were looking to get this game, my advice would be to wait for a sale.I do, however, greatly appreciate the landlord slander.

_childDocuments_.review: A cozy little indie game that puts you in the shoes of a tiny postman that has to traverse a small town in the midst of a forest. The art style is charming as is the music. Gameplay wise there is room for improvement. Gliding is slower than walking, the camera does not follow the player instantly when jumping which results in constantly jumping out of the viewport and you can not sprint or gain speed in any way. There is a button to walk slowly though, for whoever wants to go even slower... Your tasks are either delivery or fetch quests, nothing more, nothing less, so be prepared to traverse the same paths a few dozen times. All in all a cozy wholesome game with basic but serviceable gameplay that does not outstay its welcome. 3.5 out of 5 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm kind of torn on my opinion of this game, keeping in mind that this game was made by a single person (that also seems to be their first game?) it's definitely rough around the edges. Platforming has a playable amount of jank there's no game breaking bugs that I experienced but it definitely has a unpolished feel to it. Character Dialogue was also completely insufferable in my opinion, almost every NPC in this game talks like a child. PC dialogue also feels very unnecessary, I would have preferred the PC to remain silent as having a character named after myself, that I designed myself is "saying" things that do not reflect my feelings in the game. I don't mind the fetch-quest gameplay loop, however be aware that is what the game consists of. The world design is very charming and I enjoyed exploring the map. I think it's a great first attempt at a game and I look forward to any future projects by the developer.All in all though, I would not recommend this game. Had I the opportunity to refund it I would have done so after the first 20 minutes (I bought this game in a bundle)

_childDocuments_.review: I have a fair amount to say. As others have said there are a LOT of bugs, I would clip into walls, see thru the map, and have button inputs break all the time.Here are a few smaller issues that were not resolved before launch:-no input cancelling after speaking with an NPC, if you button spam like i did you will talk to a NPC 5 times before you get the hang of it-random icons in the background of the menu, cant interact with them-small freezing when you interact with pause menu buttons/saving especially-UI badly designed in general, this is clearly an aesthetics over gameplay game-NO MAP (in a platformed exploration delivery game???)-you can double jump in the air but its never told and possibly a bug-only can start unlocking skins after meeting skins NPCIn general this game suffers from a lack of bug testing and general thought. As an example, every mushroom hat skin collectible turns into a letter, addressed to the mushroom Bat NPC. These letters show up on the overlay(that covers up the screen) and show the icon for the Bat NPC. So naturally, you walk up to the bat so they can tell you...."OOooo no its the signpost to the left of me to unlock the skins!" Why. The letter was addressed to YOU, not the signpost. It's little stuff like this that just build up, especially when the gameplay isn't anything to write home about. I even played the demo and found the trailer of this game on Wholesome Direct. It was much better as a smaller game, and I think it should've been broken up into separate areas, also bc it isn't the best optimized and my computer was loud playing it.(NVidia 3060 Super)I also don't know how to say this but others have mentioned this as well. The writing....its very juvenile. There's a lot of dumb references and hating on landlords and a rude caterpillar that's fighting worms?? Are these supposed to endear me to the characters? I have no idea. There's also a very "LOLXD random" humor from the early 2010's that's in every character. The few standouts are the cute lil girl that likes stars and our mentor Susan that's constantly annoyed with our childish actions and I gotta say, I relate to you Susan.Overall this game isn't that good from its very foundations. If it goes on sale and you don't mind cringe dialogue, float platforming and annoying fetch quests, you should try it. I was drawn to this game because of it's art style, but as you can see I didn't even last a whole hour. I actually wanted to stop at the 30 min mark but I pushed myself. Overall cute but not entertaining. I'd recommend Smushi Come Home over this.TL:DR: 2/10, cute idea, needs a lot of work, dialogue is bad

_childDocuments_.review: The game is worth the $2 I paid for, I rate it positively ONLY because it is cheap. The graphics are cute, which is the main reason I made the purchase and the only merit I found in the game. In the game you are a micro-creature living in the woods and delivering letters for the residents. The first letter is for Craig, instead of telling you where this guy is you were told to "ask around and go figure out yourself" It feels unwelcoming, which is entirely the opposite of the warm environment. The wood is not a relatively big place but it has lower and higher platforms, swamp, tree houses and farm places that could be some problem memorizing locations and who's who/where since no map is offered. I think devs might think it is fun to be an errand boy to run around and to discover hidden places like the cave behind the facade - but not for me, mostly because 90% of the time is spent on the road and 10% are random dialogues. Besides, the mechanics could be better: You can find a bat that requests mushrooms and you have to manually select what you've collected, because if not, even if you have everything they won't count and the mission is left unfinished. I played half an hour and achieved half of the achievements. This game could be okay for kids, or for someone who only cares about the cute characters and graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game so much! After finishing the game, 100% achievements, I just cant recommend it. TL:DR its a rough, unfinished, wonky fetch quest game. The only reason I finished it was because Im a glutton for punishment and I wanted the 100%Its cute, the artwork is cozy, but the game feels very rough and unfinished. The port to PC is bad. The controls are wonky (you cant even click on things properly or move your character with any precision), some scenery in the environment is missing. You cant walk over small ridges, like from ground on to a bridge, without jumping. You get stuck CONSTANTLY. Your little person will also sit after about 7 seconds of inactivity, so when you try to move, you have to wait for her to stand up again. Its cute the first time, but after the 10th time its extremely annoying. The dialog is odd and its amusing sometimes, but lots of it is kind of disturbing and weird. For instance, all thru the game your little person is calling her boss Mom and Janet. The boss is her mother but your person is trying to act grown up and call her by her real name instead of 'mom'. At the end of the game, Janet says shes not her mom... what the heck? Also, the dialog goes on and on and on and on... You have to click thru dozens of chat bubbles to get thru one short interaction! Its tiresome and clunky and too long. AND THERE IS NO MAP!! Thankfully someone online drew a rudimentary map so I didnt get lost as much. If they had put more work in to this game and polished it and made the dialog better, it would be a good game. The way it is rn, it isnt.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid, fun cozy game!I really enjoyed my time with Mail Time. It took me about 4 hours to finish and I loved every second of it!The OST was amazing, and I could see myself enjoying it outside of the game. The writing was absolutely amazing. Full of little jokes and just absolutely a blast to read through. I didn't feel like skipping any of the dialogue in this game, which is great! And the art style was absolutely ADORABLE. Really gives it the cute, cozy feel.The performance was really good - I only ran into one area where the frames seemed to dip a little bit (around the multiple water falls) but even though it was noticeable, it didn't detract from the enjoyment I got from this game.I have a few criticisms about this game. One is the navigation of the menus are a little wonky on a controller. The sliding bars made it so I couldn't move to the other side of the menu unless I moved down off of them. Two, when using a controller and changing the buttons (like switching joysticks, etc..) it doesn't update the controls in text. I accidentally turned on the switch joysticks option and was really confused because it told me to move L stick, but L stick was moving my camera and R stick was my move.I did run into a few bugs but again, nothing that really tainted my overall opinion of the game.  - It seemed that sometimes my mouse wouldn't "lock" into the screen so I wasn't able to just move my mouse to change camera direction. This seemed to get fixed by reloading the game from the menu or when there was an 'achievement' in the game that you unlock or a collectable you pick up.  - The 'Express Delivery' achievement/badge didn't unlock when I delivered letters under 30 seconds. Possibly because I unlocked other achievements during these letters so perhaps there's a bug because of that.  - I can't quite remember the name of it but the achievement/badge that requires you to collect all 9 mushrooms I couldn't complete because I wasn't able to talk to Toph when I had the last mushroom. They just repeated dialogue and it didn't give me the option to 'turn it in'Again, these small bugs really didn't detract from my experience and I would 10000% recommend this game to people looking for a really chill, cute, fun game to play through.
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: This is a cozy game where I can kickback to fun dialogue and achievement / patch hunting. The character customization was nice and the artstyle overall is really cute- the textures and graphics give good brain feels. This is definitely not much of a true platform but there's enough of a puzzle to still be entertaining. Definitely a heartwarming adventure I'd return to. Cons: That being said - I have to return to the game in the future because of the amount of game-breaking bugs that make it impossible to truly progress at the moment. Some character's are difficult to locate - ie, Kaz and Greg - with minimal hints from the other characters. I both enjoyed and absolutely hated that there was no map or UI hints on where to find people because I'd spend 15 minutes wandering around the small map just trying to find a single person. I imagine it was a creative choice to make the world feel larger but it was frustrating at points.Now the bugs... there were so many bugs that made frustrating to continue. Bugs that I personally encountered included the patch "Express Delivery" never being rewarded even when completing a delivery in about 5 seconds, Topher's Mushroom Quest, Daisy's broken speech indicator, unable to hit the "Wooo" button so the graphic stays across my screen infinitely, and I also had issues with items not being given to continue questlines. I know in the patch notes that some of this was supposedly fixed but I continued to have graphical errors around Egbert and quests not completing where I did not feel confident in continuing further in a new save out of fear of spending 3 more hours to find out other bugs were also not fixed.Then there's the price. By the point of being 3/4ths of the way through all content, collectibles, and taking my time, I was 2 1/2 hours in. The game doesn't feel like its worth $20 USD when it can be 100% completed in a couple hours and there's very little replayability since the map and quests remain the same.Overall, I do tentatively recommend the game because it hits all the wholesome cozy feels that are perfect for sitting down wrapped up in a blanket after work and the Dev seems to be trying their best to fix the bugs but at this point in time I am unable to complete the game until those bugs are fixed. I look forward to hopefully returning in the future to enjoy the game to its fullest.

Simple fix, no?Sometimes when she speaks to a person, the game soft locks the moment the conversation ends. _childDocuments_.review: I cannot deny having fun playing this game, though at times I question if it really should count as a game; it's perhaps closer to a "jumping simulator". The game loop consists solely of fetch quests, each triggered by completing the previous fetch quest and introduced in a flurry of dialogs that are both very fluffy and also decently humorous. All this is set in a fairly small but entirely open world, where "paths" are mere appearance and you can go anywhere that you can jump to. The jumping mechanics include double jump and glide and almost remind me of the early Spyro games. The real mark against this as a game is that it offers near zero challenge. I mean some of the jumps are tricky and a few times you might have to repeat them when you miss, but in large you just wander around talking to people you meet along the way; many or most will have a pending quest completed when you do, OR will launch into a new quest. So it all feels a bit aimless and very low stakes. But the same could be said of many walking sims, and this is a bit more challenging then those, as there is actual platforming, at least to take shortcuts etc. And in the end, if it's on steam, and you have fun playing it (yes to both) it's a game. So I  guess that's what this is.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game as part of a Humble Bundle and was very excited for it. I love mail delivery games and this one is so darn cute. The art style and writing is so charming and also inclusive (pick pronouns instead of gender, lots of skin colour choices, other characters have diverse body types, there's queer romances, nonbinary characters, characters with multiple pronoun sets etc). The gameplay is overall really fun, playful, and adventurous, except some of the quests are really drawn out. Especially Kaz is a massive pain since they are located out of the way of everybody. And the game sends you their way more than 6 times, which gets tedious and annoying. The fact that there’s a “joke” at the very end of the game about having to return all the way to the start really doesn’t land well when the game actually does do the overly tedious fetch quest for real. Also for a full release game that has been out for over a year, I experienced an unprecedented level of bugs and visual glitches. There was floating rope, flashing text on a badge message, clipping, freezing of the character etc. For a game at 20€ price point, this is shocking. While I overall found a lot of joy in this game, and think it is a truly charming world and set of characters, I cannot really say I recommend this full price. Get it on sale or in a bundle if you really want to play it in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: While it's indeed quite wholesome and charming, as indicated by the cutesy forest aesthetic and whimsical creatures, Mail Time is not afraid to tackle deeper themes and subjects like mental health (anxiety, depression), capitalism (a literal fat cat!), and more. There is a criticism that can be made for "wholesome" games that trade on cuteness and positive vibes but might not have much meaningful to say. But thankfully Mail Time is deeper than that in the storytelling department. It's because of this and it being a 3D platformed and a mail delivery game that reminded me of Lake and A Short Hike. It's frequently funny too, and the characters are well written with arcs to them. I particularly liked the artist raven and the racing turtle's struggles with perfectionism. It's also similarly short, at 3 hours. I also appreciate the level of customisation and inclusivity on display. An easy game to recommend and could end up as one of my GOTY contenders!

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 8/15/2024The problems that caused me to give this a negative review have been corrected, it seems. I can now fully recommend this game.Edit 05/05/2023The way I abruptly came to endgame was the result of 3 bugs the devs are aware of and, according to them, working on. There are several major bugs to work out as well, so I'll keep checking back to see if there are any updates on that. If they fix the problems, I'll change my review, but right now, it reflects the state of the game I played it in and which is, to my knowledge, still the most recent version.---I was enjoying it immensely until it forced me to the end of the game and if you hit continue after sitting through the very unskippable credits screen, it doesn't let you continue to get the quests you missed. It forces you to completely restart your game for 100% which is not typical of platformers.I was having such a good time, but this has completely ruined it for me and I'm just incredibly stressed out.I will change my review if this problem is fixed in a later patch since I was a KS backer but I consider invisible Points Of No Return and the inability to get 100% on a single playthrough to be massive dealbreakers. This would be important information for me to know if I were a customer, it entirely turns me off to games. Especially since I'm a streamer who specializes in 100% playthroughs.Edit: A productive suggestion would be to add a confirmation screen asking the player if they've done everything they want to do. It's pretty standard for PONRs to have such confirmation screens so it'll immediately tell most players that there is no going back once they hit OK. If that were present, I'd have just hot "No I'm not ready yet" and completed the rest of my quests.There were other minor bugs so I'll check back on this game in a week and see if this problem is fixed, then I can given it a proper review.

_childDocuments_.review: I both liked and disliked this game. I liked the premise of the game and its whimsy. I liked the character customization and LGBTQIA+ representation (no, it is not so in your face as one <cough> homophobic/transphobic <cough> review claims. It is simply there, existing just as normally as people of any identity do). I really enjoyed exploring the small world of this game and finding all the hidden items and characters. I so badly wanted to be able to positively rate this game because of these things, but I did have some minor and major issues with the game that prevent me from being able to do so. One of the minor issues I had with the game is that a certain section of the world can be very difficult to get to, and figuring out how to get there is not intuitive (at least it was not for me). I also frequently came across the annoying bug of being stuck inside of the ground, a wall, or an object upon loading up a save or just by clipping through things. There is a debug feature in the settings that allows you to reset your character for such instances, so this to me is also a minor issue. The major issue for me is that the game is broken. Can I technically finish the game? Yes. But can I complete the game? No. The character Toph is broken which means there are several quests and achievements that I cannot continue and accomplish. The game is also extremely short. If the game were not broken, I could have completed it in about an hour, an hour and a half. I do recognize that only one person is working on this game and that fixing the bugs mentioned takes time. It is a gorgeous game and even with the minor bugs and issues I really enjoyed playing it. However, in its current state, I cannot recommend this game be purchased at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Mail Time is a very entertaining and aesthetically pleasing game, it is one that took me a little over an hour to complete (Simply because I was fooling around and exploring within the map) But overall it is cut and dry. However, I do have a few criticisms/Critiques for its contents. Firstly, I don't think the game is worth 20 bucks. for that amount of money, one could buy games like Cuphead, or Little nightmares which include so much more depth and game play, content and more. I would say perhaps 5-10 would cut it but for as much as the player receives, it's a little much. secondly, the game could pass off for someone above the age of ten and up but the age range of the game doesn't exactly make itself clear with the multiple nasty jokes in the game. I'm all for a good chuckle now and again but it's good to clarify what sort of an audience that you are hoping to sell to so others can steer clear if that's the case, even if some of those jokes fly far over their head. I think a cool addition to the game might include a week of practice within the village, running mail to the residents with a small rental home or cabin the player can return to. Maybe add a shop, some customers giving the mail scout coins or a tip for their speedy delivery which the protagonist can use to purchase things to help their pursuit or create a more flashy outfit of their preference. I think this would much better fit the price while providing more content. Within the week of the scouts training, they unlock new areas of the map and must fulfill tasks or even partake in small games or puzzles to accomplish their goals and eventually deliver their primary letter. Maybe add different characters or choices that the player can make, maybe have a crush or two they may encounter, I think there is a way to make this game really flourish with a few additions and a nice polish. Anyway, thank you for reading, I had fun playing this game and would love to see more.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game about delivering mail, so it shouldn’t be surprising that it is a fetch quest game. I expected that there will be maybe some other things to do like minigames, platforming challenges or something else. But no, this game is only 2~ hours of fetch quests and dialog. For me the game is not worth full price. I got the game luckily in a bundle. That is something to keep in mind before you get into the game.+ The world looks charming+ I found the dialoged and characters fun+ Character creator (where you can pick your pronounce) + LGBTQ+ characters and characters that use they/them or mixed pronounce + Very cozy vibes - Gameplay gets very repetitive and has no variation- No mini map, making the world navigation confusing- 2 h ~ for a 20 bucks, with very repetitive gameplay is pretty steep- A lot of BugsBugs go from small things to what seemed to be game braking bug where the game didn’t think I didn’t deliver a letter and I couldn’t progress the game. Luckily after restarting the game few times, it fixed itself. Or after every dialog in the second half of the game I was unable to move and I had to open the menu to get control of my character again. Another small nitpick is that side worm plot was unresolved, what felt weird because all the other characters plots had an ending. And I had troubles getting to the high bride area. I did not figure out the main way there and just kinda forced my character up trough jumping and things I was not supposed too. Also, there are there are ropes that are hanging from nothing in one of the main areas what looks weird and very cheap. Conclusion:The game is cute and cozy. I think it is worth the play, I had my fun with it, but personally I do not find it worth the full price (50% of sounds like a good price). I think a lot of people will also get bored with the game. I wish I could give this game neutral rating. I do lean towards negative rating based on the bugs and issues I had with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cozy game! It's probably a 1-day kind of game if you've got the time. I got the game on sale from a bundle website, so I'm very happy with the cost-to-enjoyment ratio. The game supports Mouse and Keyboard, as well as game pads. The most unintuitive control is that you press Shift to walk, because running is on by default. Other than that it's got your standard WASD keys, with a double-jump and glide function. Lots of little parkour options with little trinkets hidden on top of things. The music starts out a bit loud, but it can be turned down. Plenty of helpful choices in the options menu. The gameplay is straight forward: meet the characters, complete fetch quests, find all the hidden objects, 100% the game. No danger, nothing scary, no rage inducing things that keep you stuck in one area for hours. Just a cute slice of life platformer game with a simple story.... Apart from the one thing, but you'll find that out after finishing Irene's quest line. I had an issue where one of the achievements didn't unlock during gameplay, but by the end of the game credits, it had unlocked itself, so that worked out fine. If the devs ever make a sequel, I'd be interested in seeing where the mushroom capped gnome goes next.

_childDocuments_.review: As anticipated, this fetch-quest cozy game has adorable art and music that is calming to match. I love some of the leftist leaning values in the dialogue, especially surrounding landlords. The default being gender neutral pronouns immediately made me happy, even though I do go by she/her. A nice touch to encourage everybody to join the cozy fun :) Some cons, I have been having bugs where the mouse loses control of the camera. Top's interact button distance seems smaller than the other animals and often doesn't pop up unless you're at a very precise angle. For an indie game that just released, these are super fixable and I'm sure will be adjusted in time. I do think the game needs a map; despite the word not being very big my memory isn't stellar so this could be added as a toggled feature for accessibility. There were a few other minor items, like platforming in certain areas being a bit awkward, but overall the ability to move around is good. I'm also at end game, running into a bug where Toph doesn't recognise the samples I have in inventory, and is stuck in a dialogue loop. It's unfortunate - I'll have to replay large sections to unlock those achievements that I technically have already done. I didn't see any colourblind modes, which would also be nice for the shining objects, but I would not be the ideal candidate to test that. The field of view can be adjusted, though there's no motion smoothing settings, the game doesn't inherently have a lot of movement as you walk, so it's relatively accessible anyways. It's on the pricey side for a cozy game and amount of content I've seen so far, but I am not that far into the game, so I will update when I get closer to finishing!EDIT: About half the bugs have been resolved. I would anticipate they are all sorted if you restart the game now rather than try to go back for the last details.

_childDocuments_.review: ...So...what's the bee's purpose again?Okay sometimes I do get tired of violent and depressing, some would call gritty, looking AAA video games. Need a break from having Keanu Reeves messing around in my head and pirating around in space. Sorry haven't played that new D&D game yet. AAA games are expensive and don't have the budget to play them all when new and still developing. Also getting more into H games. If you have to ask what an H game is, you're too young to play those. But you're the perfect age to play a game like this. You can be 5 years old or 5000 years old. This is what we would call 'for all ages' or 'for everyone' game. There's no bad adult mojo anywhere here minus whatever is taken out of context on purpose.So now it's MAIL TIME! Adventure Time comes on next! See what I di...nevermind this is one hell of a cozy cottage core experience taking on a role of a child's first day and assignment as a Mail Scout. The real thing is more horrifying with hot mail trucks, guard dogs and armed thieves, but you're a Mail Scout in a vary safe and temperate forest neighborhood delivering one mail but end up delivering 53 mail. That was my count anyway. I believe I did everything in game but not 100 sure on this. Did discover a voice in a giant well for starters. Are you raising an army of worms down there? Are you a reference to a certain necromancer in Elder Scrolls? You are...the king or worms...down there. Or queen. Or they/them whatever.Won't spoil anything and it is a vary short and sweet game. The map isn't Bethesda's smallest world map big at all. Not too much to explore and discover while it is a game about exploration. Minus the cave that was a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥' awe moment. But to me it's more of a visual novel platformer. I know sounds wildly new! Like a visual novel, it has no real challenges, competitions or combat. Game's not about punishment and reward. It just tells you a story and nothing more. BUT! you don't just read you can move around and explore a map while using a giant mail as glider to get around and collect whatever for everyone else or just clean the place up. I'll give hints on the kind of stories that are here. There's a love story, a story about the dark side of capitalism...so tired of this cliche but yeah it has this, and there are...'super friends'.Can write vary long reviews but will rap it up here. This is not for masochist players(still maybe Markipliar might play this one day) or players who want a more traditional gaming experience involving a real reward and punishment system. The only challenge here would be a speed run. The game is meant to be comfy with a kettle of tea and plate of toast. Just relax and enjoy the ride.Games like this can be a prototype or inspiration for whole new styles of gaming. Video games don't have to be all about competition and challenge. Games can also tell a story or be more of an interactive movie/TV show. And this feels more like an interactive animated kids movie. With that it would be more of a simulation rather than a video game.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent cozy wholesome game with fantastically charming and funny dialogue. The characters are all wonderful, even the capitalist  cat (mostly because he's very adorable). Honestly, would love to be besties with the dialogue writer because clearly they get me and my brand of humor perfectly.The character creator isn't anything crazy expansive or groundbreaking, but I think it offers a good variety of cute options for a fairly small game. Some menus -- specifically the hat-picking one -- are a little clunky to navigate with controller, but I didn't run into anything game-breaking. As someone who's just awful at platformers, I was able to fully complete this without too much trouble, so that's a big plus imo.Also, yes, it's basically a big game of fetch quests, but of course it is because you play as a mail delivery person, so if you're not a fan of that I'm truly not sure what you're doing looking at this game to begin with lmaoThe only complaint I could have with it is the very minor fact that some items you pick up don't seem to have any use. Part of me wonders if they're just to characterize the MC as a  collector of shiny things because it feels really on brand lol, but at the same time I have to wonder if it was part of some other planned quests that didn't end up in the final game.All in all, very recommended if you like little comfy silly games where you take stuff all over the place to make cute characters happy.

_childDocuments_.review: Way too expensive for a game that you can very easily 100% in less than 3 hours. I should have known that it wasn't going to be a nice relaxing little game when the first thing they ask for are your pronouns. It was way too many veiled political statements. Was it cute? Sure? But the creators seem to have a big problem with capitalism (it was brought up several times), which is ironic because, considering the insanely high number of Kickstarter backers they had and the fact that they charge such an absurdly high amount for such a short game, they are clearly benefiting from capitalism.  At the end, they mention that wealth should be redistributed. I wish they would redistribute the wealth back into my pocket because this game is not worth the cost. _childDocuments_.review: Mail Time is an adorable, relaxing cozy 3D platforming game with a relaxed storyline. I enjoyed the game, yet it does leave you asking for more sometimes, with certain areas of the game feeling unfinished. It feels rushed, almost as if there was a deadline the developers didn't quite reach.The game is incredibly short. It took me 3.3 hours to complete the game to 100%, and that is INCLUDING me leaving the game open while I did other things during it. It is certainly not a game I would pick up if not on sale.There are bugs within the game which really should have been sorted by now - for example, dialogue and characters becoming invisible on the screen, or your character becoming frozen after a dialogue scene. Also, there's no minimap/map? Which feels incredibly strange given how big the area to explore is.However, despite its issues, it's a fun game, with likeable characters and easy controls.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice, relaxing game. You play as a new mail carrier delivering to the creatures in the forest. As your are doing so you end up helping them with tasks so that you can accomplish your goal, and also make sure everyone is happy with their service.The game mechanics are straightforward and the tasks you need to do aren't very complicated so you can get through them relatively easily and quickly. It is a short game, but its peaceful and exactly what I needed at the end of a long day.
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: This is a silly game and I love it to death, it takes the simple concept of a game about delivering mail and turns it into a well-made 3D platformer with charming dialogue. The controls are extremely simple, it's WASD to move, mouse for camera, spacebar to jump and hold spacebar to glide, but I couldn't imagine the game being any more complex. The gameplay itself is nothing to gawk at, the dialogue taking centre stage over platforming, there is still constantly fun and engaging platforming.I can't help but dedicate a paragraph to the environment alone, while the graphics are nothing to gawk at, you don't need to be in awe by the amount of pores on the models when the artstyle more than makes up for this. The design of the people is so cute, the player character is cute, the little houses are cute, everything in this game is SO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CUTE. I'd sell my soul for a triple-A game with this artstyle and quality. Sometimes I'd just look into the horizon for a few seconds and just smile. The flower forest, while being a bit of an overdone trope, is still amazing, and the bamboo section near the end of the game is so cute. Speaking of that, I love that stupid capybara, and every other character in this game, if I had an ounce of artistic creativity I'd mail in some fan art.While I can keep going on about how great the game was, how much I love it, I do have to admit that it's a really short game that I was able to 100% in one sitting, and for a price-point that's a bit over the 25 hour masterpiece OMORI, and a bit under Minecraft, you'd expect a bit more than two hours of content, but the game is so charming that I can't help but recommend this to anyone who can afford the price, this is probably one of my favourite games of all time because of the dialogue alone.If you're someone like me who uses the words "trinkets," "methinks," "perchance," and ":3" you have a 100% chance of liking this game, and if you don't I will personally come to your house to deliver some "mail."9/10

_childDocuments_.review: So I wish I could rate this as a maybe for a bunch of reasons:Pros:-cute story- there's all sorts of life lessons they give you and even stylistic choices in language that I find super funny-cute aesthetic - the bounciness---that alone is so friggin funny and cute. I love that we bounce and soar through the sky with our mail glider. The world too is unique and shows different layouts and/or seasons as you explore. The art style is both cute and cozy which honestly is so nice to interact with in the world. -world is super fun to explore - like above the world is pretty big with so many mushrooms to bounce off of, cliffs or other heights to glide off of, and places to explore that are just cute or even beautiful. Its honestly amazing.-some of the characters are funny or interesting to interact with - there are so many amazing characters and most of their dialogue is unique, cute and even sometimes funny. How they project their emotions too is so nice as you really get a feel for the conversationCons:-lots of bugs--like to the point they have a reset button that you need to google to see where it is in your book since its not in the typical settings menu. That kind of interrupts the immersion of whats supposed to be a relaxing and cozy game.-there's no map and the area is kind of large--if you're directionally challenged like me this can make things complicated and sometimes even frustrating-some of the characters are just too friggin annoying, like eye rollingly so. Doing multiple quests for some of them can definitely be a downer. Other than the few cons I think this game was trying it's best to be a unique and cozy game--and it did for the most part which is why I'm recommending this. On the other hand though if the cons outweigh the pros for you then by all means avoid this game. For everyone else I recommend this game more if it's on sale and not at full price due to the glitching issues alone. All in all though, funny and chill game so definitely check it out if you want to.

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable little collectathon style game about a young gnome girl on her first official mail delivery. Although things do not go quite as planned, many friends and adventures are had along the way.It's important to know that this is not a long game. My initial full run clocked in around 5 hours and some of that was me making my character and later getting mildly lost. The controls are pretty darn simple as you can jump, talk to people.. and that's about it. Holding down jump or hitting it a second time will open your glider which is invaluable for reaching some places.You meet people, they may have a delivery request of their own, and explore the cute woodland area which has clearly seen Human activity at some point despite the small village the animals have made. I love the style they went with and how nice it all looks. One of my favourite places is Kaz's little cave behind the waterfall - an easy place to miss cause it's not obvious.My only real downside/complaint would be that there are two sets of items, bottle caps and gems, that seem to have no purpose at all. Scratched my head for a while before looking around online to learn they have no use besides collecting them. Perhaps the dev will update them someday to be useful. I've love to see more like this, though, maybe in a larger setting with more people to meet.

_childDocuments_.review: Aesthetics--Visuals: Truthfully, the best component of the game, easily. It is so. darn. CUTE. I love my little mushy girl, I love the little animals, and I love the overall vibe. There was also plenty of visual variety to help distinguish areas at a glance. 10/10Sound: Nothing super outstanding, but the music fit the general vibe and was somewhat memorable. Sound effects were satisfying. 7/10.Gameplay—Mechanics: About as straightforward as it gets for a 3-d platformer. I'll admit it took me a while to get comfortable with moving around, and the map was quite overwhelming at first. Not to mention how much the letters added up! Considering how linear the game was, a bit more guidance in terms of where the heck I was going would have been nice. But, by the end I had fun finding everything. It did end just on time, as things began to feel repetitive. 13/20Value: For what I paid, it was a fair value. I got this game 50% off, and played about 2 hours, so about $5 per hour. But at full price? Not worth it. 5/10Overall score— 35/50. C. Whether or not you want this game is solely based on your mood and what you value. If you are willing to spend $10 for 2 chill hours, then this game is for you if it's on sale. I feel satisfied with my purchase, but I wouldn't at full value.

_childDocuments_.review: Aight so this one is a curious type.Normally one might hear a game discussed as somewhat repetitive in moment-to-moment action, with its story and writing maintaining the attention of the player in the moments where tedium overstays its welcome. Mail Time suffers from that problem, to a degree, but in a very interesting way. In essence, Mail Time is a walking simulator that ties its story beats together with light platforming, doing so both to temper the pacing and engage you in the world itself. You'll go from character to character and back again, ping-ponging between correspondents to learn more about their interactions and help this little woodland community run smoothly. The twitter of this neighbourhood is genuinely fun to enmesh yourself into, and the web of letters among the inhabitants gives you a genuine sense of place not only as some delivery they/them, but as the scandalous town gossiper.The issue with this though, is that the writing struggles as a component in a larger video-game. Moving through the small size of the world sets that dreaded sense of tedium in far faster than even the game's short length can tolerate. The term 'platformer' in all honesty cannot be applied to this game. It isn't a collection of challenges that involve movement to solve, rather a world to walk around in that uses 3D platformer-esque controls to explore. In appearance, a platformer, but in function, gameplay, and mechanics, it's a walking simulator.  This is where the game's greatest flaw comes into play. A genuine walking simulator uses an incredibly linear progression of narrative set-pieces to hold player engagement despite an absence of challenge. With Mail Time, Narrative set-pieces are reduced to (very well-written and compelling) chapters in a webtoon, with the time in-between being spent repeating the same route of travel over and over again to further the story. The sweet and authentic antics of these animals is inanimate when added into an example of interactive entertainment.This could all be fixed if, ironically, the tedium of mail delivery were further embraced. The game would dramatically improve if, instead of wearily bouncing between pen pals, letters were dropped off and picked up during the player's daily delivery route. Characters would be less frustrating to fulfill the demands of and more balls would be in the air with multiple one-on-one spats building tension at a pace outside of the player's immediate control. Instead of that, Mail Time plays as it does.Another thing, though: save for the tree canopies so tall that they almost never enter your field of view, none of the plants are animated. Not a single blade of grass or flower sways from wind or pushes against you when brushing past. That, and the foley work for the player's movements are overly quiet even with the corresponding audio setting at max. These two missing components hollow out the world's otherwise lovely art style, and have given me the first instance I've seen of an environmental uncanny valley. I want to stress though, that the effort on display by what appears to be a single person is absolutely incredible, and I'm genuinely excited to see how the lessons collected from this project help further their future work. Near every great developer started with a first project that was troubled in some aspects yet incredibly exciting in the promise it held. Kela, you the developer. I highly doubt you'll read this. In the unlikely event that you do, I wish to say this: Pressure can turn dirt into diamonds, or it can turn diamonds into dust. I've had the privilege to see what you're already capable of. Go get 'em, kid.

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game as part of a Humble Bundle and it definitely was one of those games that I enjoyed from afar, but had no intention of buying. Now that I've completed it, however, I would say that I recommend this game! (Albeit, maybe while on sale.) Mail Time is charming. There are a few really memorable moments, the premise is simple and repetitive, and the game runs alright.I was a huge fan of the Frog Detective series for its humorous dialogue and I have been waiting for a game to come along and scratch that same itch. Mail Time is not that game. There are definitely some standout characters (Soks my beloved) and a few banger lines, but the writing is just sort of good enough for the most part. I had a handful of really good laughs and smiles, especially by the game's end, and that was enough to make me feel like it was worth my time.I encountered a small handful of graphic bugs and points where the game was just laggy out of nowhere, plus your character's movement is a little... wonky. I played on a Switch controller, but even when I started out on mouse and keyboard I could tell that movement in the game was going to be clunky. There were no issues as far as getting stuck in weird places and I had a lot of fun cheating the game with it's weird jumping actions. Not the best, but had a lot of fun anyway.I really had a good time with the game, even if it wasn't perfect. Luckily, the lesson of the game's story is that it's okay not to be 100% perfect 100% of the time. It felt like a warm hug and I could tell that the creators were just grateful to make a game they loved. And that was enough for me, too <3

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very wholesome, relaxing game. I wouldn't say it's the best game ever by any means, but if you just want to unwind for a while, then you could do a lot worse. The appeal from the game mostly comes down to finding the animals to deliver mail to, some platforming, and reading some humorous dialogue. It by no means is Shakespear, other reviews seem put off by it, but I found it charming rather than annoying.There is a lot of running back and forth between different people delivering letters to progress each group's individual stories. I could see this getting tedious in the long run, but the game is overall fairly short, even when completing everything 100%. I enjoyed the different environments, the cave was my favorite, and finding the fastest route between them all was fun as well (though I am partial to optimization, so perhaps this is something few people would enjoy.)If you can pick it up on sale and just want something wholesome that occasionally provides a chuckle, then consider Mail Time. It's cute, wholesome, and just has good vibes all around.

_childDocuments_.review: Wasn't a huge fan of this.  The art style is okay, but I found most of everything else about the game frustrating.  The two biggest putoffs for me were the writing and the gameplay.The writing is just...a bit too Gen Z for me.  Lots of fragmented sentences, slang and pop cultures references.  I don't have anything against kooky characters, but I guess I just prefer them to speak in full sentences.  I guess I'm officially old.The gameplay is...well, it's a fetch quest and nothing but a fetch quest.  Go deliver this letter to this person, but wait before you can do this you have to deliver a letter from them to another person.  Oh no, now that person wants you to deliver a letter from them to someone else before they'll let you deliver the second letter.  And on it goes down the cascade.  The entire time is just one long cascading fetch quest and none of them involve anything more interesting than "Here's where this person is, go find them and get more busywork."  If I wanted the runaround, I could just walk down the street and talk to a bank.

_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: Pleasant. Calming music. Friendly tone with a happy forest atmosphere. Light exploration with maybe a little too much backtracking (the landscape has plenty of cliffs, so getting around involves climbing the same hills a lot). Satisfactory and sweet all around, like taking a chomp out of a delicious pastry.However, like some pastries, the price can be a little much for the brief happiness you get out of it. _childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: Mail Time is an open world 3d platformer about learning to be a mail scout, making friends, and earning badges.Despite having a  different art style, it really gave me a similar vibe as A Short Hike.It's not super challenging, but I had a relaxing time exploring, helping people (animals), and gliding around the forest.
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cute, very short game. Even with running around all over, you're probably not going to spend much more than three hours on the game. The map is small, which ends up being a bonus because you have to run back and forth and back and forth on different quests. (And I still managed to get lost, but that's a me thing, I definitely struggle to navigate any kind of in-game map without an overview map.) Which brings me to one of the few cons of the game: There's no overview of the map. It can be confusing to navigate on your first mission because while there is a path, it branches off and goes up into the trees and down into the flowers, and so on. It can be difficult to figure out where you're supposed to go to find various NPCs, or find an NPC again when you need to go back to them for the next part of their quest. It would be nice if there was an overview map or NPC tracking to figure it out. But that's a pretty small thing, and it definitely doesn't impact how much I enjoyed the gameplay. The storyline is simple, but each NPC is cute and unique and has a fun personality, and their own storylines are fun to see play out. There's no in-depth changes, but it doesn't really need it. The game doesn't pretend to be anything other than it is: a simple, cute, casual and cozy play. Also, it's super easy to 100%. I never 100% games!
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: A short and cute game. The deliveries require a bit of backtracking, but nothing too bad. I enjoyed looking for the collectibles as well. I had issues with an achievement not popping, but it did after I finished the game, so no worries. The achievements are pretty easy to get, just be careful not to finish the game early.
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: There are a couple of rough edges that could be polished a little (like sometimes when I got an item for delivery I'd be frozen until I either talked to the NPC again or until I paused, hit b, and unpaused, using a generic xbox style controller; also the game doesn't tell you that if you jump and tap a at the top you'll effectively double-jump which is the only way to get to the battery afaik), and there appears to be an unused asset or two (the bottle caps seem to indicate they should be a delivery but don't seem to be? also feels like there should be more to that well, and those gems are random as nitwit flubber oddment tweak), but all in all the game was fun.Oh and the last mushroom got moved after the guides were made so you won't need to use that first updraft to get to it... look around the edge of the platform that has the first updraft.
