_childDocuments_.review: I spent a leisurely 3 months playing this game, with a total play time of 10 hours.Unlike Inside and Limbo, I didn't feel any urgency or trepidation for the character.  In fact, during the early stages of the game I found it difficult to engage with the character or to care about Lana’s plight. After all, it is a game of puzzles, and feels more like a puzzle game then either of the aforementioned two games.The early puzzles were easy to solve. The greater challenge was finding how to reach the shrines – that was until the game progressed further. Eventually the puzzles increased in difficulty. I stepped away from some of them to think through them. They were certainly not impossible but required some good thinking.As for replayability, I will probably give this one another play some time, just to try to gain some missing achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: "This game possesses several noteworthy aspects that contribute to its overall appeal. Firstly, the visual artistry is commendable, boasting stunning backgrounds that capture the player's attention. However, I found the designs of the main character and her sister to be less impressive, which slightly detracted from the overall visual experience.Secondly, the inclusion of a companion creature, be it a cat, dog, or monkey?, adds a unique charm to the game. The interactions with this little creature enhances the overall gameplay experience, creating moments of endearing connection between the player and their virtual companion.In terms of gameplay, the focus primarily revolves around platforming puzzles, which are engaging albeit relatively straightforward. While the mechanics are basic and occasionally repetitive, I never found myself growing bored, although I wished for a bit more complexity to deepen the challenge.One aspect that did pose a challenge was the use of a (possibly artificial) language for the main characters, which initially put me off. However, as the game progressed, the dialogues became sparse, allowing me to overlook this aspect and immerse myself in the gameplay.In regards to the game's duration, it's worth noting that the overall playtime is relatively short, clocking in at around 5 hours for the main story. However, completing the game to 100% may require additional time and effort, making it suitable for players seeking a moderate yet enjoyable gaming experience.In summary, while the game may have its minor flaws, such as repetitive gameplay and peculiar language choices, its captivating visuals, endearing cat/dog/monkey-thing, and overall charm make it a good choice for those looking for a heartfelt and relatively brief gaming adventure."

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw a trailer for  a year ago, I was immediately engrossed by its mysterious world, mainly due to its vividly colourful presentation. I knew I wanted to dive into this experience full of glamorous landscapes and menacing wildlife that have their natural habitat interfered with by emotionless machines. Perhaps it is an over-explored theme at this point, maybe even slightly exhausted, but it can still make for an intriguing journey if done well, and my first impressions were quite positive.Sadly, that did not last long.Even though  introduces a bunch of solid premises, it never builds upon them, as if it was afraid to actually reach its initial vision and rather preferred to stay in some kind of wishy-washy safe zone that is perhaps sufficient enough – not being inherently terrible – yet still is rather monotonous and uninspired to keep my full attention. It feels like it is doing the bare minimum and counts on making up for it with marvellous audiovisuals—and that hurts both the narrative and gameplay.Let us start with the storyline first. On a distant, foreign planet, Lana and her relatives enjoy a relatively peaceful and harmonious way of life with nature. Needless to say, it does not last long, as their world begins to crumble with a sudden invasion of hostile robots, which kidnap everyone they spot. Thus, Lana’s goal is simple: to find her close ones and free them before it is too late. Sure, probably no one will praise such a premise for its unimaginable creative spirit, but I would say that it is adequate for this kind of game, and nothing stops it from being told in a captivating way.Moreover so, when a cute, cat-like being called Mui joins your adventure. Both of you are on the run, after all. Unfortunately, there is barely any narrative interaction between these two characters; their relationship does not grow. They simply stumble upon each other and continue forward, whilst any hint of possible development is only present at the very end. Instead, it focuses more on the background of both humans’ and robots’ origins via environmental storytelling, which is done well for the most part. I do not mind that – I welcome it, in fact – but it completely overshadows Lana’s character and journey. Therefore, any emotional scene or a possible sign of development feels rather superficial.Where  actually shines are its abovementioned visuals that beautifully portray each new environment you visit, making them distinctive and lovely to look at. The playthrough’s overall flow profits from that tremendously, helping with the feeling of discovering something new each time. And to give credit where it is due, these vivid visuals are perfectly complemented by a top-notch sound design, mainly by an astounding soundtrack, whose charming compositions pepper up many encounters. But it is more than that, as various natural sounds, Lana’s made-up yet inspired language or droids’ tones help with building up the atmosphere, as well. This audiovisual pinnacle was the sole reason I was still somehow semi-motivated to progress further, as at certain moments, it felt like a relaxing odyssey.Alas, the gameplay does not manage to use that – or the said premises – to its advantage and instead drags the experience down with a repetitive and simple loop. That is especially regrettable due to its short length of three to four hours. Now, the issue is not necessarily the fact that it is relatively easy to play nor that the puzzles do not require much thinking—the problem is that there is barely any variety. Any obstacles in your way, whether it is enemies or puzzles, are reused far too often. To make matters worse,  shows most of its tricks within its first half, so the latter chapters fail to surprise, with one exception, and feel the same. That is more astounding, given the fact that your companion Mui is often required to help you. Yet, its presence mostly wearisomely revolves around dropping down a rope for you, whereas you move a box or lift a platform. Any longer or more elaborate interactions are rare, which is a shame.These shortcomings arise from the presentation, too. For example, while you will spot quite a few machines in the background, you only keep engaging with just two types during the encounters. It seems like a waste to come up with various models and then not use them for imaginative and exciting situations, perhaps not introducing them as a foe to avoid but as a platforming section. The same can be said about animals. I mean, one would expect some varied wildlife on a distant alien planet, yet you keep hopping into a bland take on boars and some slime-spider things. The heavily promoted large creatures are barely there. Thus, nature feels lifeless, even though it should not be that way. And the fact that you actually kill  animals than destroy robots undermines any kind of harmonious message this title wished to promote. What a weird decision.So, while the journey and core of the game are perhaps somehow solid, it all feels so basic that I barely found any enjoyment in it. Perhaps if it focused more on the actual journey, I would like it much more. At this state, however, I was bored halfway through, and nothing that happened later on changed that. Simply put,  stagnates since its very beginning and fails to deliver on many fronts. Still, it can be somehow enjoyed as an audiovisual spectacle, but I would advise waiting for a sale for that.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw the trailer for this game a few months ago and was intrigued by the visuals. And the game definitely does not disappoint in this aspect! Planet of Lana is a very aesthetic game with beautiful backgrounds and rich colours. The sheer size of the robots in the background, combined with the music gives the game multiple “highlights”. In some instances, I wished there would have been more cutscenes so I could have taken in the full picture without having to react to the enemy attacks. (An option to skip the cutscenes would however be helpful for those who want to replay the game for all the achievements.)But as visual astonishing the game might be, it isn’t completely without fail. The animation of Lana is very detailed and very fluent but the more the puzzles start to rely on good timing the more the animations got a bit annoying. Lana pulls herself up ledges and only starts moving again when completely standing. So if you are even a few pixels late, you cannot outrun the enemy view. Also, if you jump off just one pixel to early you will not reach the ledge. At least it was for me – but maybe it was just my controller as others seem to be praising the precise platforming. But the game is very forgiving and only sets the player back to the beginning of the puzzle or to the midway point of the puzzle. However, if you wish to finish the game with no deaths you might have to learn to jump pixel perfect.The puzzles themselves are not to hard an in some instances were not really a puzzle and just a timing game. Something I didn’t mind as you can let the visuals better sink in when you aren’t frustratingly scratching your head wondering what to do next. Most puzzles are solved by using your little companion. Even though Miu doesn’t say much you just have to like the little fella. Lana herself is also very likable and the voice actor did a good job relaying Lana emotions, whispering to Miu when enemies are nearby and sounding sad when calling out to her kidnapped sister. Personally, I would have liked to stay in Lanas village a bit longer to actually start caring about her sister and the villagers. The story itself is also very basic, but I haven’t seen a game portray the story with such good visualisation. Everything is conveyed though the backgrounds and character interaction so no boring text dumping and unnecessary “on the nose” conversations. There is also a "music theme" throughout the game. I wish they would have leaned more into the music theme as the two puzzles which were slightly related to the theme were my favourite out of all puzzles. The game is also not very long. I finished it in one afternoon (~5 hours). This can be seen as a positive as you can easily replay the game to go looking for missing collectables (shrines) or as a negative as there isn't much to do apart from trying to reach 100% steam achievements after finishing the game.All in all, I would definitely recommend the game if you are looking for a fun but short game. I would give the game a solid .+ stunning artwork+ great soundtrack+ likable characters+ easy puzzles+ no unnecessary lengthy texts (no text at all, just visuals)(+ short game)- Sometime to depended on pixel perfect timing- No deep emotional connection to Lanas sister and therefore slightly missing reason for the player to by invested in the actual mission(- short game)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good.That's the last time I write a review saying I personally disagree with a review someone else made.I got angry in heat of the moment, and it bit me.CONTEXT: If anyone cares, I wrote a passionate review heavily disagreeing with a negative review. so I deleted it after properly thinking about what I said. I didn't say anything bad or insulting, dw lol. Off note, it's not clownish for a person to disagree with someone that you agree with. And people providing their own reasons for liking a game makes both sides (negative and positive) helpful to people who are thinking of spending their money on a game. Applying to any game, not just this one.Pros:- Cool concept.- Art-style is beautiful (obviously).- You get to pet Moi.- Environments felt unique and well designed.- Character and animal designs are really well done.- Story was wholesome and awe inspiring.- Soundtrack was great (loved the motifs).- In my opinion, as repetitive as the stealth sections can be, there were some new things added with each environment, which helped refresh a little.- Visual storytelling was really good, especially with the abandoned ship.- I did like that Moi (your little buddy) helps you with puzzles. I thought that was pretty unique gameplay- Runs really well (for me at least).- It feels like a breath of fresh air in a sense. Since this game 'get's in and get's out' with what it's doing. Personally, I think too many games try too hard to make their games lore so unnecessarily deep and 'vital to learn' to understand whats going on. With this game, the story is simple. And I love a game with a simple story from time to time.The gameplay is good enough, has the basic necessities. Run jump, crawl, pet, etc. Basic side scroller stuff.Cons:- Stealth sections were repetitive, didn't really bother me, but I can see how that would be an issue for other players- Human models admittedly look a little weird IMO. They almost don't fit to me. Moi and the animals looked good. The humans just looked a little soulless.- There needs to be a sprint button. The game felt really slow at times when it didn't need to be.- The final stretch was a tiny bit less intense than what I felt this game needed.- I do get why people are not a fan of there being only one collectable that only offers lore. It personally didn't bother me, because I just like the hunt, but I do see why people don't admire it.- This game is a tad overpriced. For what you're getting out of it, I don't view it as entirely worth it's price tag. To fix that, I think this game could've offered more variety in gameplay and puzzles. Take that and make the game a bit longer, then the price tag would make more sense.The puzzles were kind of easy. Which can be seen as a good or bad thing. If you want an easy experience (puzzle wise), then you're in luck here. Although I wouldn't recommend this as a beginner puzzle game due to it's price tag.Overall, the game is good, and I would recommend it. Compared to back then, I do understand a lot more now on why people don't like this game at all to now. My initial review was 9/10. But now it's  a 7.8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's a fan of the travelling from left to right puzzle/platformer genre; this game feels lacking.If you compare it to games like Limbo/Inside the puzzles are almost nonexistent. There were only two puzzles in the whole game that actually made me recognise they're a puzzle and stop to really look at what it was I had to do. Everything else was just going through the motions. Though games like Limbo/Inside managed to also have a sense of tension, a kind of unease to push you forward, even just a curiosity about the world that makes you want to see more. I'd even say the Far games (Lone Sails and Changing Tides) manage to capture a sense of almost panic, pressuring you to succeed. Where Planet of Lana I just never felt any real engagement from the game, no reason to feel like I wanted to see more. The game just feels slow without that special something to make it stand out. The game also does the telling the background story through the... well background. Finding collectables to explain whats happening in the world but, it all feels very surface level. You can ignore the collectables as it's very easy to predict the plot just from a few hints the game drops early on. There's no twists, no turns, just what you'd expect it to be.If this game existed in a bubble where there was nothing else like it I'd recommend it, but if you compare it to similar games I just can't recommend it. It's just it feels like there are a lot of repeated scenes and puzzles to stretch out what little play time it has. There's even a few slow panning scenes with emotional music with nothing really happening just to admire the scenery if that's the type of thing you're into. Oh there's even some QTE sections which, for me, kinda killed the tone of the scenes. Like there's a scene from the early trailer but it's not gameplay it just has some button prompts plastered over the top of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is an art-first, gameplay later experience. This doesn't quite mean it's a walking simulator. The puzzles, while simple, are substantial enough to hold player interest across chapters. Gameplay feels like a mishmash of Inside, Hob and Far: Lone Sails. Controls work fine. The end game has a couple of challenging platforming & navigation sections but they're manageable. Including a no-death achievement however is counterproductive and unnecessary for a game of this nature (see also Bramble: The Mountain King).The visuals, painterly and gorgeous, will take your breath away. Wishfully intentionally uses a minimalist art style for characters to redirect attention toward lavish background set pieces (forests, caves, oceans, deserts) because PoL is about the journey, not the one who takes it. Takeshi Furukawa's sublime score substantiates this. The atmospheric compositions are engrossing and distinct musical motifs mark key moments. 'Horizons' is devastatingly beautiful.PoL's characters use a unique language which is a pleasure to acquire through context; the protagonist Lana often uses 'iimo' (stop) and 'olai' (follow/come) with her animal companion, Mui. Mui is unbearably cute and playing PoL will make you want a Mui of your own. Don't say I didn't warn you. The overarching story centres around the intersection of technology and nature, which, in my opinion, is overused in fantasy media and especially games (see RiME's sentinels). Despite this, and the short playtime, PoL has a message that's worth pursuing: even the corrupt can be healed through great personal sacrifice.

_childDocuments_.review: Think of this as an experience rather than as a game. Enjoy the beautiful watercolour visuals, solve some (admittedly pretty basic) puzzles and discover the story... all the while being serenaded by a stirring soundtrack. It might only be around 4 hours long, but I very much enjoyed my time spent with Lana and Mui and don't regret buying this at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: What an unexpected gem. This game is a stealth masterpiece. It'll be accused of lifting from Playdead's successful approach, though to me that's just a huge positive. It goes a much more uplifting route with a charming natural ambiance, and it unashamedly wears its heart on its sleeve with anime influenced cinematic storytelling, superb sound design and soul-stirring music that punches several tiers above its weight class. I'm as jaded as they come and usually unimpressed when I'm being emotionally manipulated, but this game does it so well that I got emotional and weepy like a girl multiple times. 😂 The gaming world needs more of this kind of stuff. 👍
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous graphics and great music; the story and the actual game is a bit lacking.The game is beautiful and in a fairly unique way; it has a nature-vs-machine theme, with natural scenes represented with painting-like aesthetics and machine scenes looking like blocky 3D models. It works really well. Unfortunately the actual game is not that fun - a puzzle platformer with fairly repetitive puzzles, especially in the first half of the game which is just a random series of scenery changes (forest, mountain, underground, forest again, mountain again etc), each with a string of similar puzzles, with no real sense of progression or story arc.Overall still worth a play (it can be finished in 4-5 hours), but it could have been a great game and ended up merely an OK one.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful little game - it manages to deliver the wholesomeness and cuteness it tries to project, with a deep message .I wouldn't buy this thinking of it as a puzzle game, but rather some sort of interactive movie/adventure.  Baring 2/3 scenes, the game doesn't require any thinking or posses a challenge whatsoever.Very original idea, and I would say 20€ is a fair price.  Congrats to the devs!Also, .

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and can't recommend it enough.If you liked or loved LIMBO, INSIDE and to some extent even GRIS, this game is definitely for you.The hand-crafted art is gorgeous and breathtaking, the soundtrack is tender and monumental at the same time, the puzzles manages to be both a part of the world and offer gameplay beats that challenges you as a player while also, slowly, evolving the bond between Lana and Mui.Carefully and tastefully crafted. _childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool. Great narrative experience with stunning visuals. Gameplay is fairly simple, but game is doing a great job from a user experience point of view. It reminds you what actions are available if it looks like you're stuck. The game draws your attention to important stuff by having the characters look there too. This could work as a pretty introductory game for someone new.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: As side-scrolling adventures go, it's a good one.  A great one?  Debatable, but still very much worth your time.It's got some competition; many years later both Limbo and Inside still loom large in this field and indeed they will take some beating, for me at least.What Planet of Lana has in buckets is twofold - one is the sheer amount of polish and love that has been invested in it.  It looks amazing with a classic colour palette, visual style and sense of journey.  The second thing is the animation, which deserves a point of praise all of its own.  While I get a *lot* of Conrad Hart from Lana herself (and that's not in a bad way at all), it's the, ahem, guests and their machines which feel so well painted and designed, they move incredibly and a big hats off for that.As a game I spent around 5 hours all told, enjoyable hours at that.  From Lana's seaside fishing village, the land of sand, the underground and so on, before being welcomed to the machine.  The levels are distinct and all look great.If there is one criticism I have, it's the variety of gameplay throughout that isn't all that varied.  The puzzles, which take up the lions share of the game, are good.  Not too tricky that one must find a youtube solution, but just enough that you might have to spend a few minutes figuring out what you've got and how to use it - a sense of progression was welcome and kept me going.What I missed though, and maybe Inside has spoilt me, is a set-piece.  I can bring to mind any number of scenarios from that game many years later but for Lana, I can only think of one about 3/4 into the game and perhaps another which uses music and sand.  Both of these were very good but I couldn't help feeling, as I sent Mui to another ledge to knock down another rope, that I'd like to be on rails experiencing something a little more cinematic, just a couple more times would have done it.Anyway, great game well made and all involved should be proud.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little game that will take about 3-4 hours to play through. Nothing ground breaking, it's pretty run of the mill in terms of story and mechanics. I also felt there were some parts which were surprisingly short lived and not fleshed out. But it's as pretty to play as seen in the trailers. So if that's your bag and you're happy with the price, I'd recommend playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short puzzle platforming side scroller with a story to tell. You'll set out to save your village and meet some interesting friends along the way. In some moments I felt the easy puzzles were a little too repetitive, but right about the time I was feeling that way a new puzzle type would show up to keep things interesting. I beat it in about four hours but I didn't collect all of the things. I'm sure if you pushed through it you could beat it much more quickly, or take your time and play it a few more times to go and collect all the hidden things.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous little cinematic platformer adventure, that's the very definition of short but sweet. Stunning visual style that looks like a painting come to life, the wordless storytelling is lovely and the adventure compelling through and through. Mui is adorable and deserves all the pets. An absolutely sublime score by Takeshi Furakawa pretty much seals this as a very memorable journey well worth taking. I would be interested in seeing more in this universe.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a beautiful game, the art direction is top notch and so is the music and sound design.The game is short but feels long towards the end due to a repetition of hide and seek scenes that don't feel necessarily new. They also introduce QTEs because some people seem to enjoy them.That being said, it's an emotional journey and the relationship with Mui abd compagnon control is what gives this game its uniqueness and cuteness.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I don't remember when I saw this game for the first time, but I still remember that I was instantly captivated by its charming graphics and a setting that filled me with intrigue. I tried the demo at one of the past Steam Fests, and I knew it was a game I was going to love. Planet of Lana will take us along a fantastic odyssey, putting us in the role of a young local girl and a cute creature; they will be the ones who’ll rise up in the face of adversity and try to put an end to a looming threat.The  is one of those that are not told, but shown, and follows the adventure of Lana: a small villager of the colorful planet where the game takes place. At the beginning, we’ll find ourselves in her village, where we’ll gradually learn the basic controls while we follow another villager playfully. Abruptly, we’ll observe how some huge objects fall from the sky in the distance, and soon we’ll witness the identity of these phenomena: some giant robots that seem to have invaded the planet, and who promptly kidnap the rest of the villagers, leaving Lana all alone. She will try to chase them, making her way through the wooded paths of the area, until she runs into the other main character: a curious and adorable little black animal, like an ink spot with white eyes and little ears, who will accompany us and help us from then on. With this new companion and following the same goal of finding the villagers, Lana will travel through this planet full of secrets from the past, dangerous fauna, interplanetary enemies and beautiful landscapes. It's a story that I really enjoyed from beginning to end, even though it's not of the conventional type (being non-narrated), and has several moments that range from adorable (thanks to our beloved little animal) and captivating to tense and exciting; it's a concoction of emotions that I gladly soaked up in, and it's ending left me super satisfied.The  is that of a side scroller, where we can move sideways and jump on some platforms along the way. The controls themselves are very simple, since in addition to the arrow keys we will have some interaction keys, such as activating mechanisms. However, the twist that gives this game to these mechanics is that we can ask our adorable little friend to help us, giving him indications of what we want to do. For example, tell him to activate a switch that we can't access, throw us a vine to climb, or stay somewhere in particular to attract the attention of the enemy. The use of our cute companion is the key mechanic of the game, and we will have to help each other to advance, since sometimes it will be up to us, as Lana, to activate these switches to be able to meet the little one again.As expected, there are several puzzles of different types, but most of them are very simple and give way to organic progression; and, although perhaps some make you think more than others, I feel it is unlikely to get stuck in one of them. Among these puzzles we’ll also have stealth scenes, moments where we can move machinery, and even send the cat (I don't know if it's a cat but well, the word came out of my soul) flying around in drones to activate distant mechanisms. On the other hand, not only will we have to deal with invaders, but also with more hostile wild creatures that want to eat us (or our little friend). Even so, there are not many direct encounters with enemies, but rather we’ll have to avoid them, although from time to time you can defeat some of them; what I mean is that there is no combat per se. Truly a creative section, somewhat simple in some aspects, but extremely entertaining; I want to add that in some moments there are quick time events, but those who are not fans of this mechanic can disable it in the game's options menu.The  are beautiful, drawn in a very aesthetic and colorful style, like watercolor for backgrounds and environments, and more detailed for some areas, characters and enemies. The scenes that you can observe in the distance help to create a very fictional atmosphere, showing us from desolate fields and cemeteries of giant bones, to jungles that hide vestiges of imposing civilizations that fell with the passage of time, and give an air both beautiful and catastrophic. I can say that everything mixes together very well, from the leaves on the trees and bushes, to huge robot creatures looming on the horizon, and these differences blend together to show us a welcoming and captivating world, but that has its dangers when you look for them.The , on the other hand, is a delight. Once again I fall in love with the music of a game, which has several melodies of all kinds, such as the tense classical violin tunes, or more relaxed ones with a piano or guitar. There is one song in particular that features vocals, and that detail always gets me; I loved it. The sound effects and the voices of Lana and the little creature just fit, and although they speak in another 'language', they express their intentions very well. The atmosphere that is created between the visual and sound section is excellent, going at a pace that balances the various moments of the game perfectly; two sections that shine on their own, but together they stand out so much more.In , Planet of Lana is a game that radiates effort, with very elaborate and carefully done sections, and that generated many emotions in me. I experienced super tense moments that made my skin crawl, realizing how immersed I was in the moment, and others that made me smile, like when I noticed how Lana talks in whispers with the little creature when there are enemies nearby; it's a detail that may seem simple, but I found it very cute and that it made sense. I found the animations of both our eared ink blob and the enemies, especially the robots, to be very elaborate and detailed, and I liked the puzzles quite a bit even though I'm not the biggest fan of them. I loved the cat (I know I don't know if it's a cat, let me be, but it's incredibly adorable whatever it is) and Lana, and I adored accompanying them on their adventure. It's a game that left me very satisfied with everything, and I totally recommend it to those who want to experience a charming sci-fi odyssey.

_childDocuments_.review: I've come to call these type of games 'adventure platformers', of which classics such as Another World, Flashback and Inside belong to. But even though this one doesn't bring anything new, it's serviceable enough for the genre.It should go without saying after watching the trailer that the animated art design is quite charming. Unfortunately that's the best I have to say about this title as everything else is fairly standard. The story, controls and puzzles all feel very familiar compared to similar games. All of which left me feeling a little bit bored and disappointed, leaving me with not much else to add.Don't let my play time fool you as I clocked a bit up on the Steam Deck. After playing this I'll say it's done well, especially for fans of the genre. However, with the indie space being what it is, there is a lot of stiff competition out there that have a lot more to offer. So maybe on sale if you are a die hard fan looking for a new 2D action/adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting for this game for quite some time, especially because it reminded me in its mechanics of a long time favourite - "Another World". A few hours into the game I´m happy to say that the game has delivered. Beautifully drawn, lovely soundtrack and a story that so far sounds promising. Lots of interesting puzzles and also lots of opportunities to die in many different ways despite the seemingly kid-dish appearance :-)  Loved the gentle introduction/tutorial that introduces some of the basic actions, but also the remaining ones, while not explicitly mentioned, feel very natural and are easy to discover. All in all - great game.Update: Ok, so I've finished the game now (4 hours or so) and I stand by what I wrote. A nice cinematic experience, story was satisfactory (although a bit cheesy at certain moments). For sure I hope we have a sequel soon :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana, is a stunning and immersive experience that stands out as a piece of art in the world of gaming. This cinematic puzzle adventure takes players on a heartfelt journey through a vibrant, colourful world brimming with both charm and danger. The game's visuals are nothing short of breathtaking, with every frame feeling like a painting rich with color and detail, creating an atmosphere that's both captivating and otherworldly. The contrast between the lush, beautiful landscapes and the cold, mechanical invaders enhances the story's emotional impact, making every moment feel significant. Planet of Lana excels in its unique companion-based game play, where the young girl and her loyal friend must work together to solve a variety of puzzles that are cleverly designed and diverse in their challenges. These puzzles are not overly difficult, making the game accessible and relaxing, yet engaging enough to keep you invested. The use of stealth and wit to navigate dangerous situations adds a layer of excitement and requires thoughtful strategy. The story, which spans galaxies and centuries, is both epic and intimate. It is a tale of harmony disrupted by a faceless army, yet it remains a story of hope and resilience. The narrative doesn't dwell on war but instead focuses on the beauty of the planet and the journey to preserve it, giving the game a refreshing and poignant perspective. Playing Planet of Lana is a truly relaxing and enjoyable experience. The controls are intuitive, and the pacing is perfect for those looking to unwind and immerse themselves in a beautiful world. The game is a brilliant blend of art and adventure, making it a must-play for anyone who appreciates well-crafted games. In conclusion, Planet of Lana is an absolutely brilliant piece of gaming. Its gorgeous visuals, compelling game play, and touching story make it a standout title. Highly recommended for players of all ages, it is a testament to the potential of video games as a form of art.

The puzzles aren't terribly hard but can give some frustration. There isn't any combat perse, but super intense moments occasionally that get your heart beat going. _childDocuments_.review: Quick and simple: If you don't mind spending 20 bucks on a game that you complete in 5,5 hours, go get it. Otherwise wait for a sale and still go get it.Here's why:The graphics are gorgeous. You can basically stop every 5 minutes, take a screenshot, and you got yourself a new desktop wallpaper.The soundtrack is really nice, too. Not exactly a banger like Frank Klepacki's Command & Conquer music or Ben Prunty's FTL soundtrack, but still solid. And it fits the game's overall atmosphere perfectly.The gameplay is the usual liniear platforming and puzzle solving thing in the likes of Limbo, Inside, Abe's Odyssey and so on. Straight forward, nothing too complicated, nothing too fancy, but it still gets your head scratching from time to time. Especially coordinating your and your pet's abilities to solve some areas is quite fun.The story / environmental storytelling works pretty well for me, too. I won't spoiler anything here. There's no dialogue except for the made up language, there are some discoveries, there's room for interpretation. I liked that.And here and there the game just pressed the right buttons to make my cold black heart feel some genuine emotions. Well done, game, well done.Overall I can recommend this game. My only complaint would be that it's too short. I would have loved to see more of that beautiful world. But as someone with very little time for gaming nowadays I have to admit I do appreciate a short and well crafted game that can be experienced within a couple of evenings.So yeah, go get it, already!

_childDocuments_.review: The game offers a wonderful experience. _childDocuments_.review: I'm an old gamer and games that are intense button bashers are not for me any more. What I do like is originality and emotional engagement from a game and this definitely hit the spot for me. Yes, it has standard platform mechanics that, thankfully didn't demand rapid button pressing sequences to get through a level, but the story was lovely. What touches us emotionally is highly a individual thing and depends on our own personal back story  and this one made me cry just like Papa and Yo and Gris did. It's a beautiful thing when a game reaches into your heart and engages with you beyond the superficial layers of yourself and Planet of Lana is one of those. I don't often finish a game these days but I did finish this one and will play it again in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed playing the game, but it felt like it dragged on despite being less than 4 hours of content. I felt zero motivation to go back and find all the collectibles. Majority of the time you're just walking to the right, and the few "puzzles" the game offers are relatively similar to each other. The game only really has cinematic action scenes to offer which are admittedly very well done, but my PC seemed to struggle with some sections despite it being fairly high-end.They put a lot of time and effort into the visuals and audio but the gameplay was severely lacking. Also the idea that they would even consider asking players to complete this game deathless is ridiculous. The controls aren't nearly tight enough to consider this a platforming/combat challenge.If you buy this, just sit back and enjoy the ride.. it's basically a movie.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SUPERB, from art direction to music and puzzles.Flawless ~4-5h of fair challenges in gorgeous environments interacting with characters that evoke their own personality by the way they look, move and sound. MOOD - You are the whole game on a run to save your brother under danger from unknown creatures. Despite that, there is no fear evoked but a climax of alertness, as well as many moments of tenderness and epic scenes (v.g. facing a colossal spider or running in the desert).- Character design and sounds play a big role in creating a link with the characters: cute dialogues in an unknown language (soft in danger, loud otherwise), the tender responses of your companion, or even the broken bones when the protagonist falls fromhigh.STORY- Story is explained without words, making you part of it. It is simple but good enough for a platformer, and it gives meaning to running the whole time and hiding and sorting robots and creatures. - Some disperse elements give a bit more depth to it, but do not open questions, provide a complex narrative or offer alternative paths or ideas. The story is simple and superficial.- Don't play this game for the story, as it is not its focus nor it is worth discussing it. Characters are plain, do not evolve nor have an interesting story behind them. They are not defined by their actions, complex personalities, or their own story, but by how they look, move and sound.GAMEPLAY- Every level feels new and requires more and more complex mechanics. It combines environment elements with a coordinated action of you and your companion. Timing becomes important after the mechanic has been introduced and tested by the player.- Giving orders to your companion and controlling robots and mechanical elements of the environment adds a lot of fun to the game.- Puzzles are fair and make sense. There is a little challenge, but no frustration. It is rare that help is needed, as the design and rhythm at which mechanics are introduced make it easy to follow.- Puzzles are dynamic. There is a lot of hide and seek and distraction involved in many puzzles. It requires good timing, but not infuriating precision. - Each new enemy character introduces different mechanics and approaches: the way you make them move; how they make you hide or run; how to tease or control them; the effect they have on the environment (v.g. changing water level)...ART- All levels have a very nice color palette, and there is a variety that is big enough to not get bored.- New creatures keep being introduced, all of them with their unique design style, sounds and mechanics. It is not just how they look, but their mechanic and essence that is different.- Animations are very fluid and give a lot of personality to the characters, which have a unique look and behavior, in the way they look, move and sound. - Character design is great, and varied enough. Each new character is unique for a specific reason and adds a set of game mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Since everybody insist on comparing this game with Limbo and Inside, this is how I came to play it, and I my negative impression is mostly based on the comparison with Playdead's two games. Also after almost 3 hours of tedious play I couldn't bring myself to continue, so I didn't finish it. Like in Limbo and Inside the puzzles are very simple, however the story and environment are much less interesting. There is no sense of mystery at all, fiew from the characters interactions (it's obvious what will happen with her sister at the end), and absolutely none from the environment. Always the same rocks, the same trees, the same setting that has nothing to tell us but "I am lush and wholesome Ghibli-palette nature". This kind of game is the 2D equivalent of walking simulators, there is no gameplay so the story better be interesting. Imagine playing Firewatch or Death Stranding but the story is not interesting?  That's basically Planet of Lana.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana has the flavour and gameplay of the 'INSIDE' platformer game. Puzzles are more easy but I don't blame it, on the contrary. The nature is colourful, bright (instead of dark in 'INSIDE') and full of mysteries, a la Spirited Away (japanese animated fantasy film). Graphics are gorgeous, very atmospheric and immersive. Xbox wireless controller is well supported. A joy to play. A masterpiece. Kudos!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This is not the game I thought it was going to be. While I knew going in that this seemed to be lifting some of it's aesthetic from games like Limbo (which I've also played and enjoyed), the character of the game and the pacing of it's gameplay do not always match up.It's understandable that Lana and Mui have to put themselves in harm's way, but so many puzzles involve Lana and Mui using themselves as bait to lure away the robots or boars or something else. Not only that, but many of the puzzles can only be solved by Lana running headlong into the maws of death, just so I can learn what the pattern is that I'm trying to break.Which is to say; the puzzles have such tight tolerances as a means of creating tension, it actually takes me out. More than once, I've had to put the controller down, not because the puzzle was hard and I wanted to get it right, but because to succeed, I have to be throwing Lana and Mui-shaped dolls into the shredder. My girlfriend asked me to stop streaming the game, because of how unfun that tension turned out becoming.The oddest thing about this is that this is not remotely necessary. The game has more than enough atmosphere to keep me playing and there's already plenty of moments of tension for me to get a feel for the tone. The puzzles are just designed needlessly tight with not enough margin for error to the point that you think that you did it wrong, when you did it right, you just didn't do it slightly fast enough.I hope I will finish the game, but I have to discourage others from buying it. Some puzzles are like running into a wall and with no clear solution, until you've killed the small child character on screen enough time that the game deigns to let you pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so cute and so fun! A lot of games like this are plagued with god awful controls/unresponsive character movements that lead to frustrating wacky ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but everything is really tight and well designed here. I really enjoyed my time with this game and even felt encouraged to 100% it, doing so in just 4 or so sittings. My partner watched me play this whole game and she loved watching it even more than I did playing it!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a puzzle platformer comparable to games like INSIDE both mechanically and in length. The art is beautiful, the soundtrack is gorgeous, and the story relatively simple, but holds emotional weight. The puzzles never become overly challenging, but there were a few that made me think. I found the game relaxing and enjoyed my time playing it. I will likely go back to find all of the hidden secrets. The soundtrack is worth the price alone. YUP
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game.The art style and music are just beautiful.The game is basically a sidescroller comprised of small puzzles, that you solve with the help of your cute little companion (cat?potato?both?).Sadly the game is a little bit on the short side, clocking in at about 4 hours. I would have loved to spend more time in this world.Nevertheless it was worth every cent.If you like Puzzle Jump 'n Runs like Inside or Limbo, this might be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I'm conflicted. I want to like the story, I want to like the ending. But there's just not enough to tie it together. Gameplay is not this game's strong suit, aside from some QTE cutscenes there are  only one or two challenging sequences, everything else is your standard analyse patrols and evade kind of difficult. So naturally the focus for this one lies in visuals, story and music.You can tell a lot of passion went into the graphics and music. The kind of beauty you see on the screenshots persists all the way through with some heartfelt soundtrack to go along that, no complaints there. Now let's talk story. I believe a strong combination of the 3 aforementioned factors can create a truly investing experience that can make you feel something for the characters and maybe even shed a tear during emotional points. Planet of Lana has a solid idea with a good start and end to the story but has connected these 2 points with a flimsy little string. Maybe you can dig up some lore in the little details but on my casual first playthrough things were just.. happening. There were some very vague clues dropped here and there but ultimately I had no idea what I was doing until I apparently was in the final boss room. Various interesting plot point questions were raised throughout my run but the game only ever grazed the surface in terms of explanation and rather spent more time showcasing pretty visuals. This wasn't helped much by the fictional language (which isn't bad per se, don't get me wrong) used in this game. Now I'm not saying I want a 15 minute lore dump sequence but some more clues sprinkled about as to why these machines and lifeforms act the way they do really wouldn't have hurt. Regarding the ending, it is well done and I do want to like it. But there was a certain lack of world building and I ended up feeling like that one office handshake meme for not really knowing how I just saved the world. At the end of the day being good in almost all other aspects it can certainly be enjoyed by most people but if a strong and cohesive story progression is as important to you as it is to me then this isn't your game.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into to Planet of Lana very hopeful. Smooth as silk and just as shiny, with music to match. Beautiful set pieces abound. But beyond that, I didn't walk away from the basic 4.5 hour runtime with any lasting impressions.The encounters are what you'd expect from the genre. The story didn't give me anything new, (but that may just be because I play and watch too much sci-fi).If you're totally new to the genre and the themes, AND you've already played Inside and Limbo, then you might enjoy Planet of Lana.For $20 though? _childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a beautiful side-scrolling adventure that follows a young girl and her cat on a search for a lost friend. Lana witnesses the destruction of her village by an extra-terrestrial invasion and manages to escape. The rest of the game is traversing a variety of landscapes with natural challenges (chasms, hills, etc.) while evading the invaders (death ray drones, mechanical spiders, etc.).  You also find alien machinery to puzzle out and use as you make your way. The game feels a bit like LIMBO or INSIDE but has less violence and seemed a bit easier.  Your alien encounters are interspersed with long walking sequences that provide respite.I am not a cat person, but I could not help cheering for Mui - Lana's feline companion who responds to her commands and has special powers. Lana is 'the last child standing' and the cat provides friendship and assistance. All dialog is in a fictional language but the game manages to create strong emotions about love and joy, fear and loss. It also does a good job of creating an atmosphere of true menace when Lana is at risk.Typically, I do not excel in this genre. However, Planet of Lana was manageable. A couple of the evasion scenes are quite tricky as you coordinate the movements of Lana and Mui to survive. My timing failed more than a few times before I finally hit the magic combination and moved on.For me, the hardest task in the game was when I had to load Mui on a drone and fly him about without killing him. The drone controls are very wonky and keeping the drone steady without sending Mui into an electrified wall or industrial fan was quite daunting.  After several days, Mui survived my drone piloting and we were headed towards the final chapter. There is no true 'boss' battle at the end. However, there is a QTE-like exercise which almost gave me carpal tunnel. I played with a controller but there was still a lot of button mashing.The game autos-saves frequently, after each collectible (10 shrines to locate) and each major scene. Although there are some exceptions, progress on incomplete puzzles is not saved. Failure usually meant starting from the beginning of the exercise. SIgh...The art is beautiful, the music is passionate, and the story is sweet. If you don't mind some running, jumping, climbing, and stealth, then I'd highly recommend this game. Completionists have their work cut out for them... 100% requires that you survive the entire game without dying (a lofty goal, indeed!).

_childDocuments_.review: Lana is clearly inspired by Inside and similar games, and it does a good job of living up to its inspirations (but it's no Inside, which I consider a masterpiece). Lana has beautiful graphics and plenty of different biomes, so the visuals never disappoint.The story reminds me strongly of Somerville, another game clearly inspired by Inside and similar games. I think the Somerville story is quite a bit stronger, but the Lana story is interesting and has some unique elements like the relationship with your "helper." The story is straightforward, but enjoyable.The gameplay is much stronger than a game like Somerville, but not up to the level of Limbo/Inside. There are plenty of puzzles, so this is not a walking simulator (except for a few interludes), but the puzzles are not challenging and are a bit repetitive. The secret shrines are fun to find, but don't give any additional lore or endings.At 5 hours for nearly 100%, this is a pretty short game, but I enjoyed it and recommend it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a great piece of visual storytelling. It is, of course, extremely beautiful - this should not go unsaid, but really, a lot of games are. What really gives meaning to Planet of Lana’s beauty is its worldbuilding. It’s not pretty for the sake of it, it’s not an art exhibit either, it’s a whole meticulously thought-out world. From the vibrant colors of the forest, to the dimness of the swamp, the bareness of the desert and the black-and-white factory level, the game’s visuals mean something.As for gameplay, I had a very good time with it. It has enough puzzles and platforming to remain entertaining and is by no means an auto scroller, but it manages to not be about its challenges - ie. the element at the forefront always is the visual storytelling, as it should be in my opinion. I do have a gripe with like four levels in which the relative jankiness of the controls made them a chore to go through, but aside from those I had a great time and especially appreciated how many elements you could interact with - from Mui to the boxes to the water level to the robots, etc.Planet of Lana is a relatively simple and straightforward game, which is 100% worth experiencing.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana a cinematic  puzzle platformer with some quick time events and some precision jumping. The game play is solid but nothing spectacular. The puzzles are too easy for my taste, and the platforming is less about mastering a system a system of play as learning what buttons the game wants you to press when, an issue with cinematic platformers going back to Out Of This World.Why do I still recommend the game? Because of the CINEMATIC part of this Cinematic platformer. The music, art direction,  backgrounds, and cut scenes are of exceptional quality and show the strong influence of Miyazaki and Spielberg. This team and story may have been better served by making a film rather than a game, but when the film part of a game is of this quality, it deserves notice.   The alien monkey cat is really cute, too.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a gorgeous cinematic based 2D platformer centered around a girl whose planet has been invaded by robotic aliens.From the presentation aspect, it excels in its art style akin to games like Inside but much more colorful and full of life. So many times I had to pause in my track just to take a screenshot that might be a desktop wallpaper candidate. From the rustle of grass to the particle effects, the art direction is really well done.It's also worth mentioning the soundtrack whose melodies play a key part in setting the scene for enemy encounters, mood changes and plot developments. With the main tracks played by violins and actual lyrics, the game doesn't shy away from showing it off particularly in some transitions throughout the world, making us feel like a part of Lana's journey.Then there's the gameplay that controls similarly to others from this particular genre such as the old Prince of Persia games or Limbo. The player must take into account the delay of their actions shown through the animations while solving the accessible to somewhat clever stealth puzzles that are sent in their way. While in my experience none of them were particularly troublesome, my biggest gripe came with the flawless achievement (beating the game without dying) which goes against the trial and error nature of some of these obstacles.Regardless, a playthrough of it can be enjoyed by both the player and their viewers. For its price I'd say it is worth checking out even in the midst of a great year for game releases.

It's a fine balance and I'd certainly prefer Lana's approach over other games I've played that get too challenging, taking me out of the narrative and sometimes leading me to give up.Well worth the 5 or so hours I put into it!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a mixture of an interactive novel/movie and a puzzle platformer. I finished the game in just over 5 hours and it was neat, but not really satisfying. For me it feels like by trying to mix three genres, all were done okay to good but none fulfilled their potential / promise.Story: The story is cute, the visuals GORGEOUS and it has a few unexpected twists, but its rather straightforward / predictable most of the time. There is no dialogue so its mostly environmental story telling. In some cases this is done really well, and I could order things I'd seen at different times into the narrative, but it still felt lacking in detail and depth. It is also quite slow paced, even when there's no puzzles; many sections are just walking through wonderful graphics.Platforming: The platforming has beautiful animations but pays for that in precision. That makes puzzles often tedious. Sometimes you can play as other entities than the player in the game, which I always found a lot more fun than playing & moving as Lana herself.Puzzles: I did have several satisfying aha moments and I really liked how each section of the game added a few new mechanics that changed up the puzzles. My deal breaker is that, while It is mostly easy to figure out what to do, it's then difficult / tedious to actually do it. I found the vision cones of enemies a bit ambiguous, fall damage hard to estimate plus had the above troubles with the not-so-precise platforming.Accessibility: In my opinion, it's straight out rude to provide a warning for photo-sensitive viewers at the start of the game but no accessibility setting to turn it off, nor a second warning before it happens. It was only one scene in the final cut scene so it wouldn't have been so much work and an ambiguous warning at the start is extremely unhelpful and seems more like a legal protection than actual care or consideration for photo-sensitive gamers.In summary, this game relies heavily on its amazing graphics and beautiful music, but the game play was not very satisfying to me, and the story not as gripping as I'd hoped. It's still a pretty good way to spend a couple of hours on the weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: - Beautiful Game. Optimistic and light in genre full of solemn heaviness.- Simple, yet solid story carried through by wonderful world-building and lore.- Doesn't over stay its welcome and drives forward. There isn't really weak part of the game.Cons:- The movement is rigid. You're given all the tools you need to complete the game, but you definitely feel how limited it is.- Its definitely a "first game" not many chances were taken with game play or presentation and even though its a completely satisfactory game, it can leave you wishing Wishfully Studios had allowed themselves more room to be creative and experiment with new or unfamiliar mechanics.Planet of Lana is a great addition to the PlayDead style narrative-driven side scroller. It approaches a genre mostly comprised of somber, macabre and stark artistry from the complete opposite angle and gives you a optimistic, lively and vibrant world to traverse. It keeps the tradition of using the camera to really show case the vastness and beauty of the game from time to time. You'll find yourself hitting the screen shot button more than few times.As the title states, it is an odyssey (in about 5 hours). Unlike its peers, its fairly straight forward with a definable beginning, middle and end. Though the story is simplistic, its wrapped in pretty enthralling world building that boast a fun blending of humanities and classic sci-fi.The music is good, maybe not Bastion or Spiritfarer good, but definitely notable. I'd put it a step down from Inside. It is also very important for game play, keep your ears open and pay attention to what you hear!The controls are simple and while it gives you everything you need overcome all the challenges Lana faces, you'll definitely feel the rigidity of her movement that will leave you wondering why they just didnt add sprinting or why she can only jump a foot off the ground. The double sided puzzle solving with Mui is very fun though and though the limitations make actions themselves feel stiff, the responsiveness allow you to correct mistakes as they're happening if you're quick enough.Most of the puzzles are classic platforming with just a couple of hint/deciphering puzzles. Nothing to write home about, but enjoyable none the less. There were definitely times were I made it harder than it had to be because I forgot a key piece of information (despite it being reemphasized through out the game) or because I didnt believe I could jump the distance needed (again, the movement gives you everything you need. Believe in Lana, you can jump that gap or reach that ledge without doing any cheesing)As far as technical stuff goes, I had only one noticeable hick up and that was loss of frames during the Coastal Town level, which is a little puzzling for a rather undemanding game running on a high-end PC. This was only momentary as you dont stay there long, but definitely caught my attention. I'm not sure if Wishfully intends to do a optimization pass on the game, but if they dont Im sure that issue will be addressedOver all this, is a great little game and a wonderful first impression by Wishfully Studios. Their artistic abilities cannot be overstated and while I enjoyed the story in Planet of Lana I hope that they spread their wings a little more and allow themselves as much creativity with the plot as the do their lore crafting. I enjoyed my time and I think others will too. If anything we'll all be yearning for that simple life in lush beautiful world.

_childDocuments_.review: This game can be summed up as:"Mom can we play Inside?""No honey we have Inside at home"Inside at home:I am almost completely 50/50 for loving/hating this game.Pros:Absolutely gorgeous game. Provides an immense sense of scale, with towering titanic enemies moving past in the distance, and beautiful vistas stretching to the horizon. Absolutely wonderful to look at.The lore is sparse but very interesting and immediately understandable through very little communication, which is very impressive and well done. This is very much a "show not tell" game. You can pet the companion, which is always nice, and overall the game has a very cute feel to it.The cons:The character has only one speed of movement, and it's not agonizingly slow but it's far from fast. This game desperately needed a sprint button. The enemies are all much much faster than you, which if done well can heighten the tension of a game, but unfortunately instead of tension I got frustration.  There were also multiple periods of just walking and looking at the background, (including an odd out of place 4 minute music interlude) no puzzles, no interaction, just hold the left joystick to the right. Get ready to hold that left joystick to the right *a lot*. With how simple a lot of the puzzles are this game is almost a walking simulator. There's a ton of puzzles that require almost frame perfect timing, and with your character's movement speed, enemy patrol patterns and save points, those three elements often combine to equal waiting for upwards of 30 to 40 seconds to retry a frame perfect moment, missing, dying and getting reset and having to wait 30 to 40 seconds for another chance at a frame perfect moment.  None of the puzzles were *super* complex, but were however difficult to solve due to timing and platforming. This often led to me having solved the puzzle logically in my head, but then needing to execute in real time, and dying over and over due to requiring frame perfect jumps or timing enemy patrols.There was a huge amount of repetition, it seemed like they made you send the companion up a cliff to toss down a rope to you at least 30 different times.If it were longer than it is I wouldn't recommend it. But if you get it on sale it's fun to kill an afternoon, if a little tedious and frustrating. But I'd rather play Inside.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a breathtakingly beautiful adventure game with a cinematic focus. Featuring simple, but clever puzzles, awe-inspiring landscapes and a poignant soundtrack that culminates into a memorable sci-fi odyssey. The protagonist is a young girl named Lana who lives a pleasant and comfortable life within a small community. Unbeknownst to her, a looming threat is becoming nearer, a threat that will destroy the harmonious balance between mankind and nature. Before long, the tranquillity is abruptly shattered, and her best friend Ilo is taken. The village is in shambles and malevolent robots have taken hold of everything she once knew. This begins Lana’s adventure to pursue the robots and find her friend, but she does not face the journey alone. It is not long before she meets a small and adorable creature named Mui. Mui becomes Lana’s companion for the remainder of the game and plays a fundamental role in the gameplay. There is no dialogue, as the characters appear to speak a fictional language, but the narrative is told through the beautiful surroundings, landscapes, soundtrack, and the tone of Lana’s voice. The story is not something entirely new, moreover, similar stories have been told many times, but it provided more than enough intrigue and mystery to keep me interested.  It is a story about friendships, courage, and cooperation. A heart-warming tale that mixes the essence of these themes, and thrusts them into a puzzle, sci-fi adventure.Before going into detail, the gameplay is more on the simpler side of adventure-puzzlers. If you are looking for something challenging, something with multiple different solutions to puzzles, or a game that may leave you stumped for a few minutes, this may not be the game for you. Planet of Lana excels with its graphical beauty and atmosphere, and whilst its gameplay is not bad by any means, it is not complex.Gameplay is almost solely based on companion-style puzzles, light stealth elements and platforming. Lana cannot directly attack the robots, so she must sneak past them, hide in long grass, and utilise Mui to reach higher places, hit buttons and so forth. Mui must be directed to stay or follow, chew through wires, jump up to a certain spot and more. Timing is typically the biggest challenge with these segments. I did feel that developers aptly introduced new mechanics as the game progressed, expanding players options so it never felt repetitive. Mui learns a myriad of new skills and Lana uncovers new ways to control the robots. There is no inventory management or puzzles involving picking up objects and the simplicity helps keep the game in motion. Becoming stuck on a specific puzzle would feel out of place to me, as this would ultimately deduct from the wondrous atmosphere that the game oozes. The game is also very forgiving and autosaves frequently. If a robot spots Lana or Mui, unless blocked, it will automatically kill them. Despite being heartbreaking to watch Mui die, there are no real consequences to this, as you will just respawn almost exactly where you died.The entirety of Planet of Lana mostly follows the same formula of companion style puzzles, however there are some quick-time events splattered in latter sections. The ending of the game also felt unusual and slightly out of place, but I can only deduce that the developers were trying to do something different for the finale, and it wasn’t too jarring to negate the game's previous accomplishments. There are also some collectable shrines to be discovered throughout the levels, but this is the only extra content the game offers, and these are also linked to achievements. I did not find all the shrines, but I still took approximately 6 hours of playtime to finish. Stopping momentarily to soak in the gorgeous environments surrounding me. However, I have seen some people reach the credits in 3 hours or less.  Bugs were very minor and scantily impacted my experience, however there were enough to be noticeable. During a scene that is supposed to be a swell of emotion and triumph, the foreboding eerie music from the previous scene was still playing, detracting from this moment entirely. In retrospect, this ill-matching audio only happened this one time. Another bug that I encountered a handful of times seemed to be caused when trying to exit an animation too quickly. Resulting in the character staying in a statue, unable to interact with objects or jump, just stuck forever in a T-pose until I reloaded my save.Undoubtedly the most standout feature is the gorgeous visuals. With a plethora of motley landscapes to trek across, ranging from deserts to lush green forests to barren caves and factories. Another impressive element that cannot be fully appreciated from screenshots alone, is the excellent camera and cinematography. Despite being a side-scrolling adventure, Planet of Lana does not feel limited by this. Often in large-scale areas the camera will pan or zoom out, giving an entirely different view to players. There were never any issues with this, it never felt unresponsive or awkward, it just worked, and it worked flawlessly. I also must mention how utterly delightful Mui is. The small cat-like creature bounds gleefully at Lana’s heels throughout the game and is simply adorable.Whilst there is no dialogue, the soundtrack matches the level of quality seen in the visuals, aptly capturing the highs and lows that Lana encounters. Understandably so, as this original soundtrack was composed by Takeshi Furukawa, a highly acclaimed composer known for his work in  and many more. Six hours whilst taking my time but can be completed in as little as three. Yes, the developers also recommend this. Being a linear puzzle adventure, not really. However, there are some achievements and collectibles that may warrant a second playthrough for some.Planet of Lana is a gorgeous cinematic adventure game that when combined with its emotive soundtrack, radiated beauty in every scene. Puzzles are not too challenging but had a great balance in difficulty and were an adept medium in storytelling. Being  debut game is an impressive feat, and I am eager to see what else arises from these developers.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, and judging by the player reviews, you might like it yourself. And if so, great. But I do want to say that how much you like this game might depend on your experience with other cinematic platformers and other tearjerker games.Basically, this is a standard game of its genre, except the puzzles are simpler (I was stumped only once), there are a bit too many "keep running to the right while you see scenery, for dramatic effect" moments for my liking, and it tries to jerk tears in predictable ways involving an alien that you adopt as a pet, which follows you around and becomes required for puzzle solving. (If it dies, you lose.) Can you guess what happens to the alien later? Yup. Can you guess what happens AFTER that happens? Yup. But if you've never played a cinematic platformer before, or a game which tries to jerk tears, then this is a good place to start. Because it still does these things well enough. Graphics are beautiful and downright stunning at times. The story is told through the environment and occasionally cutscenes without dialog that only zoom in the camera, if that, as the characters emote through animation. The camera freezes in place when in a puzzle or action zone to fit all of it on the screen, until it's completed, which is a feature I really like: basically, the camera moves when you're traveling, but stops to show everything that's important when you need to solve a puzzle or evade an enemy. Being a cinematic platformer, you move almost like a real human, with movement limited to climbing and dropping down, jumping only as high as a real (albeit athletic) person, and pulling and pushing things - or controlling other things remotely. And giving commands to your pet, for the game's many puzzles which require the two of you to work together.It's a competently made cinematic platformer that tries to make you cry a few times. But I've played games that  jerked real tears, and this one just made me roll my eyes in annoyance and think, "I get it, it's supposed to be sad." That's not their developers' intended effect, but I'm sorry, the storytelling just didn't work for me. I never felt attached to Mui, the little animal you adopt for a few hours. And I know everyone talks in a made-up language, but their language seems to have like ten words total, which I also find hard to take seriously.So, just keep in mind what you're getting if you decide to buy this. If my complaints are about things that wouldn't bother you, then hey, buy this game and enjoy it more than I did.

I found myself wondering if I was playing a game or just watching a glorified slideshow of vibrant backgrounds. The story tries hard to be poignant but ends up being as flat as a pancake, leaving no emotional impact whatsoever.It’s hard to believe that a game with such gorgeous visuals could be so utterly forgettable. Planet of Lana is a beautiful waste of time, where you’re left staring at the screen, wishing you could shake some life into this lifeless shell. If you’re looking for an engaging experience, keep looking—this is not it.
