_childDocuments_.review: This is a spectacularly beautiful game.  The protagonist, almost anti-hero, is relatable.  You "feel" with the character.  This game makes me think of Prince of Persia and Flashback of the 1990s, but with a emphasis on beauty and the story.  I am taken aback with the detail, the wind blowing through the leaves, the butterflies, birds, little fish, etc.  The monsters are unique and the puzzles are challenging, but not so hard as to be irritating and annoying. This is by far one of the best side scrollers I have every played!  It's that good!!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. A through-and-through adventure full of memorable magical moments enriched by beautiful music and breathtaking aesthetic. Puzzles were simple yet they always force your brain to think in a certain way. My only criticism would be the QTEs though they do serve a unique narrative purpose. Just didn't enjoy them gameplay-wise.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: It's a simple enough 3D side-scroller puzzle platformer. It offers a pleasant soundtrack and engaging atmosphere. It does have an interesting story delivered without words. One thing to note though, in the first 2/3rds of the game there is a lot of "walking right" in between puzzles. In the later chapters walking does tell a story, as do most visuals you encounter in the game. I enjoyed it, even though I rarely buy side-scrollers. The secrets you collect are part of the storytelling device, so make sure you collect all of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what I would label as a "simple masterpiece." It's not anything groundbreaking in game design or story telling, but it's just so well done and so simple. The graphics and art style are amazing. It's a very simple art design with more minimal detailing that looks clean yet beautiful. The sound design is also incredibly well done and really helped pull everything together into a more immersive experience. The story was done without any spoken dialogue or written text, yet it was both cute and very moving throughout the whole journey. I felt really attached to the characters and kept wanting to see more of where the journey was headed. The end of the journey was so captivating it had me in tears (not going to say if they were happy or sad tears). Not many games make me feel much emotion, especially the way Planet of Lana did.The game isn't very long; it can be completed in several hours. The gameplay itself is simple. Jump platforms, solve puzzles, evade enemies. The puzzles are not too difficult but sometimes will make you think a little bit which adds a feeling of accomplishment. There's no combat, but you will have to figure out ways to evade enemies or they will straight up kill you.If you like any of these things mentioned you will probably like this game. I felt so immersed, I usually have videos or live streams on the background when I game, but I had to keep pausing it for this game just to experience what was happening. The sound design and art style played a huge part in making things so captivating. I would put this up there with games like Outer Wilds and Stray, which are very different games, but similar in the sense they have a unique art style and unique way of telling a story which breaks out from the typical gaming standard.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that "PlayDead-Like" makes any sense as a moniker is a testament to the strength of that studio, and this comes closer to the ludo-narrative impact and polish of Limbo and Inside than almost all of the many puzzle platformers inspired by them.If Somerville played like an awkward and arrhythmic imitation of what makes these games tick, Planet of Lana manages to feel like a beautiful celebration of the form, despite the narrative playing things somewhat safe and the puzzle design being merely "strong" to PlayDead's "inspired."One of the nicest side effects of narrative puzzle platformers being insanely hard to execute at this quality is that they almost never drag on or overstay their welcome in a market filled with live service "forever games" competing to become your next habitual lifestyle...Fans of the form should enjoy Planet of Lana today while dreaming about the third PlayDead game of tomorrow.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: - You love story focused games- You love beautiful whimsical worlds- You enjoy clever simple puzzles - Don't mind a game in the 3-5 hour range- Are a fan of both INSIDE and Ghibli- You want tremendously difficult puzzles- Prefer crunchy mechanic focused games- Aren't a fan of games where the main reward is the story- Nothing about the world portrayed in the trailer sparked curiosity in youI love an infinite AAA game that you can pour years of your life into without ever scratching the bottom as much as the next person. Sometimes that's what I want, sometimes I really just want to be somewhere else for weeks at a time, to have an experience that I know will always be there with something new for me to do.And sometimes I want Planet of Lana.I've been desperate for something to scratch the INSIDE itch since it released years back. Planet of Lana scratches that itch with a more adventurous upbeat tone that still has a fair smattering of dark spooky moments. The puzzles aren't going to make your head explode but the way your companion is integrated into them leads to some super clever and satisfying solutions.Plus the composer worked on The Last Guardian, the music really really makes the game and helps reinforce that wondrous feeling of adventure.it also has some of the best alien wildlife ambiances I've heard in a while. Each location feels like it's full of very diverse alien creatures, most of which are conveyed through sound alone.I had a great time, some very tense moments, some very tender moments, some slightly frustrating moments, overall well worth 20 bucks if you meet the above criteria.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game in all aspects. Reminded me of Limbo, crossed with the golden oldie Another world, in its earnest simplicity and visual storytelling.Mechanically, the game plays spectacularly. The controls are well thought out and precise, and the environment almost always communicates clearly about what options you have in every situation.The visuals... Oh the visuals. This game is extraordinarily beautiful, especially when you see the environments in motion. Together with the music, and the unwaveringly cute voice, giggles and squeaks of the main heroine and her pet make for an excellent game atmosphere.Overall, the game is exactly what I hoped it would be - light platforming, some light puzzling and an excellent story told entirely in subtle visual clues, so your mind is free to fill in details.Overall score: 11/10.(The extra point is because YOU CAN PET THE PET and it's super satisfying! :-) )
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: The artists did a wonderful job with this game... but that's really the only praise I have.The puzzles being so repetitive was honestly one of my most minor criticisms (in fact, I thought they were pretty good for the most part). The whole idea of the story in this game just felt so lacking and dispassionate: you have this beautifully painted world invaded by robots, but as you progress through the story, it becomes clear that the natural dichotomy of nature vs machine which one might expect to be explored in a game such as this, is actually too complicated for the storytellers to bother with: animals (aside from your eventual companion Mui) are portrayed largely just as """bad""" as the robots themselves (and ) and in the end,  There seemed like a lot of potential for lore in the shrines and the "communication" with the machines, especially in , but in the end it turned out to all just be an effortless tack-on perhaps for the collectathon minded.The creators wanted a world reminiscent of a Studio Ghibli film. They achieved the beautiful paint, but got lazy with everything else. I was very disappointed in this game, and would not recommend it. If you want a puzzle-exploration game that is actually inspired and full of heart, I would recommend a game like Tchia.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful game that takes you on an atmospheric adventure of friendship and brevity. The story simple yet well told even though there is not a single word spoken in any language you speak. Whilst playing you discover a fantastic world full of fascinating creatures. You can feel right into the characters and you might shed a tear or two.The game plays similar to  or , but in a much brighter, colorful way. It is way more forgiving than LIMBO and less just running than INSIDE, yet you get a fair amount of just running, which I'd say is the only downside to this game. The puzzles are easy and logical, the shrines are not too easy to find but also not unfairly covered and if you tread carefully you might even manage to not die on your first run - although I'd recommend a backup copy of your savegames, just in case. It reminded me on a simpler, friendlier version of . I played through it all in about 5h and it's a game worth to be played for atmosphere alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: What a little treasure of an indie game.I thought Planet of Lana was a creative masterpiece. It had light puzzles, a fantastic soundtrack, and incredible storytelling; my favourite combination in a game.The puzzles kept me engaged as a player, and weren't too difficult  in that they would lead to frustration. It struck just the right balance for me. As a video game music fanatic, the OST was a must for my VGM playlist. The music truly immersed me as I trekked through the story.As a sci-fi nut, I was fully-engrossed in the story. It had all the pieces I needed to love it.I highly recommend this game to those who love story-rich light-puzzlers.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game overall.Positives: 1. Art is amazing, animations are cute, the world is alive with small animated details. The story is clear and easy to follow, while also developing over the course of the game and revealing nuance. The music can be relaxing, but also tense at the right moments, and I liked the original songs.2. Puzzles are usually interesting and varied, especially because you play as two characters, Lana and Mui who each have their own strengths and weaknesses. Puzzles generally have one solution and can't be exploited. Only 1 or 2 puzzles stumped me, but not so much that I needed to look up a guide. I only feel like I solved 1 or 2 puzzles in an "unintended" way.3. SPOILERS: "Boss battle" at the end is pretty fun.Negatives:1. I only really have one. At times, the game seems to drag needlessly. I understand the more cinematic moments that show the great lengths Lana goes to save Ilo, but sometimes puzzles are repeated verbatim or there are long sequences where extent of the gameplay is holding the right arrow. Some (few, but still worth mentioning) of the rooms seem repetitive, rehashing the same puzzle with no added story or gameplay element. Then the next room the puzzle will make me think about the environment in a completely new way, which is awesome. I just want less of the former and more of the latter.It's hard not to compare this to INSIDE, and if I were to do that, I would have to say INSIDE is the better game. However, this game is quite good too, but I have more here to criticize.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to go with a light recommendation for Planet of Lana. There are a few stretches of this game that could have been trimmed down big time. It feels like it's about an hour too long. There are only a handful of types of puzzles that you and your little cat/alien buddy named Mui solve, and there was a point about an hour and a half into it where I just wanted to feel some kind of progression. It was just the same puzzles over and over again and that section definitely overstayed its welcome. It picks up again around the middle, but then it falls into that same pacing issue a bit towards the end, but the third act pretty much overall, is really nice and emotionally satisfying, and really saves the game. But, there are definitely a few badly paced, repetitive chunks. Sorry but I need to go on a little tangent here... any RedLetterMedia fans might be reminded of the movie Nukie (a terrible 80s b-movie that they watched and was referenced in their videos for years). I only say that because really all the main character does is call out for her sister ("Elo!!!!"), and the opening of the game there is a section where they are calling out to each other over and over, ("Lana!" "Elo!!" "Lana?!" "Elo?!", etc etc)  and it just immediately reminded me of Nukie, which gave me a laugh. If ya know, ya know...With that said, the art design, the score, the sound design, and the narrative (which is all visual storytelling) are all top notch. There are defintely several moments of real beauty, awe, and emotion, and I have to give the game a lot of credit for engaging me in that sense. If you enjoy these types of games (this is very similar to something like INSIDE, which I loved), then I would definitely recommend this. Definitely stay away if these artsy platformer puzzle games are not your cup of tea.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a captivating masterpiece that seamlessly blends stunning visuals, an engaging storyline, and thought-provoking gameplay elements. Set in a mesmerizing hand-painted world, the game takes you on an emotional journey alongside a young girl named Lana and her loyal companion, a small alien critter named Mui. Together, they navigate through a beautiful yet perilous universe, unraveling the mysteries that lie within.The game's art style is a breathtaking work of art, with vivid colors and intricate details that transport you to a realm of wonder. Each frame feels like a carefully crafted painting, bringing the world of Lana to life with every step you take. The atmospheric soundtrack complements the visuals perfectly, immersing you deeper into the enchanting experience.But it's not just the aesthetics that make Planet of Lana compelling. The gameplay mechanics are equally impressive. With puzzles to solve and obstacles to overcome, you'll find yourself challenged while still feeling a sense of tranquility. Instead of focusing on fast-paced action, the game encourages you to take your time, observe your surroundings, and approach each situation with a calm and collected mindset.The game has also great support for ultra wide resoltuions: Planet of Lana is more than just a game; it's a work of art that transports you to another world. It provides a sanctuary where you can escape the chaos of reality and immerse yourself in a beautifully crafted universe. With its rich storytelling, stunning visuals, and serene gameplay, this game invites you on a journey of self-discovery, reminding you to appreciate the beauty that exists in both the smallest moments and the grandest landscapes.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, combines some of the best parts of classic puzzle-platformers like Flashback and Abe's Oddysee with heaps of unique charm of its own. Only criticism/suggestion is, it'd be nice to have a "hold jump to autojump when you reach the edge of the platform" option in settings, for those who like the puzzles but not the precision platforming
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what would happen if Hayao Miyazaki had been tasked to make a game like INSIDE or Limbo. If that sounds good to you, then you can't go wrong with this game.I admit I'm a complete sucker for games that tell a complex story solely through visuals and subtext and this game checks those boxes beautifully. If there is one thing to criticize it's the game really is too easy. The focus here is on visuals and storytelling rather than challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game I like it more than any individual aspect of it can motivate but the balance is perfect. Nice scenery, non verbal storytelling. Don't expect anything too complicated in the gameplay or storytelling.I Introduced platform puzzel to my 4 year old daughter with POL and she loves it. The puzzels are too tricky for her but the platform aspect offer a good challenge which means we can play together. We had fun and now wife replays it with her (wife never played games) Works great on steam deck and with external controllers. 9/10 for casual gaming or introductory platform puzzels.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, game recognizes ultrawide resolution, but does not handle it well. Sky textures are too small and there are visible borders on the sides. Music is fantastic, the game does not live up to it.The puzzles are not meant to be solved using thinking, rather find an object to push or pull, and here you are. No brain required. Control is a bit slow in response, what can be annoying, I understand that sprite has to take action from current state, but it could skip some frames to get immediate move.The "puzzles" sometimes do not deserve the name. Avoiding a beast by hiding in the grass can hardly be called a puzzle.The game is nicely done, has a great music, graphics can be a bit annoying with "wind simulation" that looks like through the looking glass, every leave moves in the same plane. Seems overthinking can be an overkill.Has potential, but does not present a challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! The game was amazing and I enjoyed the companion of a cat helping me in the story. The fun adventure from start to end was epic and fun challenges the game offered plus a puzzle to solve. The graphics are beautiful as well. I used an XBOX Wireless Controller which was great playing this game. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: My name is Lana and that was the sole reason that I became initially interested in this game. However, that being said, I was overjoyed to find that this filled an INSIDE shaped hole in my heart. I love 2D platformers, such as Limbo and INSIDE, especially of the abstract / surrealistic variety. This checked all my boxes. Stunning artwork? Check. Gorgeous soundtrack? Check. Abstract and avant-garde execution? Check. Bonuses: You get an adorable cat companion that you can pet. Also, there are some moments that really hit hard emotionally. I got teary eyed a few times. There is a plot line, yes, but the game definitely urges you to use your own imagination while you go on the journey of unraveling the plot. In my opinion, the plot was loose and very abstract for most of the game, but towards the end, everything came together and everything made sense. The game is 90% about the journey and 10% about the actual plot. Like I said, by the end, it's very obvious what the whole journey was about and everything starts to completely make sense. I highly recommend it. It's such a relaxing and chill game that's embedded with occasional moments of tension and dread. Definitely kept me on the edge of my seat. The game had a slow start for me, but once it gained traction, I couldn't put it down. I finished it in one sitting and can't stop smiling and gushing about how wonderful it was.

She loved the little monkey companion "Mui"I didn't care much for the button-mashing moments.  It could have been cool to use the controls to evade in depth while riding the robot.  Instead of just a button-mashing sequence.Overall, it was a fun game,  I like that it doesn't take a commitment of your life to finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful but short puzzle-platformer with some good art and a fun story. In many ways, it feels a lot like a lighter version of the Playdead games Limbo or Inside, both in terms of the difficulty and content. I wish it were a little bit longer, with more numerous and varied puzzles, so I'm not sure I would recommend it for full price, but it was well worth the few bucks I spent on it during a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely would recommend! Mui is best space cat. Soundtrack is outstanding. Story and visuals are cinematic! This is a gem and (as of mid 2023) probably one of my fave experiences so far this year. Summing up the gameplay as a 2D, side-scrolling puzzle-platformer doesn't encompass the way the game makes you feel as you move through the world. The puzzles are well-designed, and (especially for folks who've played other games in this vein, like Limbo, Inside, and even Little Nightmares) there's enough that feels fresh and works your brain in some great ways. There'd be times I'd be stumped for a minute, but it always felt great to figure out the timing or order of what they were hoping for me to do. The story is told without words, although there is VO that you'll be able to loosely translate as you play (and a language to decipher). I feel like I have a solid theory of what happened from my first play through, but I'll definitely be playing again to hone my thoughts a bit more, as there's a lot of mystery to uncover!

_childDocuments_.review: If you boil it down, Planet of Lana is mostly a walking simulator with some light puzzling and a couple of QT events throughout, its not a hard game, and its not overly long either.But MAN, the story, the world building, the visuals, the sound design and the incredible score just elevates what could be a pretty pedestrian experience to something truly unique, almost cinematic in quality.I cannot recommend this game enough, it is, quite simply, fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game,  I don't so much recommend it as not *not* recommend it.  But I can only give it a thumps up or down, not a "meh," kind of handwave. TL;DR:+ The game is pretty, colorful, sentimental and whimsical.  The art and music are fantastic and it has a good 'feel' to it. - It feels like a more colorful and sentimental but ultimately lesser version of the game Planet Alpha.  I spent MOST of my time playing through going, "Yup. Feels like a Planet Alpha ripoff."  I try not to make direct comparisons to other games while playing because I think that even similar games with a lot of overlap can provide rewarding experiences!  In a somewhat niche market of sidescrollers like this though, it brings nothing new to the table and generally offers less than its competitors...more of which named below.  The Likes:The graphics are whimsical and very pretty at times.  The sound and music is very well done :)  The 'story' progression is nicely told through scenery and observation.   If you've had limited experience with these types of games (others being Limbo, Inside, Planet Alpha, (arguably) FAR: Lone Sails etc) it'll probably all feel very novel and charming!  Dying (which will happen a lot no matter how careful you are as  you sort through things) is a zero penalty affair, which is good for this sort of game.  You typically start back with little if any progress lost.  Controls are simple and the required button pushes are often labeled for anything more complicated that jumping.  You WILL NOT find yourself getting stuck or hung up because you can't remember the buttons for a specific action.  If you've never played a game like this before, it's a good primer to the genre :)  Now the criticisms:   Total gameplay if you take your time is probably 6ish hours?  I have 9.5 hours logged but think I left it running in the background while I ran errands somewhere so the timer's a bit off.   If you liked it enough to play through it again and search for all of the secret locations you'll clearly get more out of it.  ....but understand that a normal runthrough will only last you an evening, maybe two. ...not much in the way of puzzles. There were a few which made me scratch my head for a minute or two, but most of the game involves virtually identical types of simple setups to navigate through.  "Instruct your companion to climb up there and throw the rope down.  Climb the rope."     "Hide in the grass, find a way to get the robot to get on the other side of you, run to the next hiding place."   Often LITERALLY identical setups.  There is very little variation. The flow of the game can be frustrating.  Almost every bit of terrain you'll encounter throughout the entire world will require you to jump and climb with little deviation.  No casual jumps which allow you to keep moving at a regular place while providing variety to the terrain and ambiance..   Just lots of completely unnecessary standardized up and down and ups and downs as filler which can feel very unnatural as you move through the world.   Transition between playing and cutscenes feels awkward and also upsets the flow.   Instead of shifting naturally from character movement into the cutscene, the screen goes black and comes back...but it's the exact same kind of animation and camera control as the game.  I know it would have required a bit more effort to move seamlessly from one to the other and there are limits to the time and resources devs can put towards things.  ...but it bothered me every single time it happened and devs from other projects have done it pretty well. The 'story' itself...if you've never played any other similar games, is somewhat charming.  To me it felt like a less involved version of Planet Alpha with fewer puzzles and less interaction with the terrain and surrounding world in general. Overall: It's a cute game with a bit more sentimental/whimsical feel than most of the other games I've referenced .   ..but that's ALL it has setting it apart.  Given my play history with other similar type games which I feel did almost every element of playstyle better than this one, I can't really recommend Planet of Lana.  BUT.  I can't in good conscience *not* recommend it just because I think that many other games have already done almost literally everything this game set out to do and did it better.  It's a decent game and despite what I consider an overall lack of creativity and over-reliance on the same few tricks, clearly a lot of love and effort went into it and it shows.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely, wonderfully crafted masterpiece. It's fun, relaxing and enjoyable. I love how the gameplay and visuals are inspired by timeless classics like Pitfall, Another World, Prince of Persia, Flashback and Loom. The game is pretty forgiving and allows experimenting with different ways of solving its puzzles. The companion mechanics was a genius touch. Overall an incredible experience that doesn't overstay its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game a lot. It's a beautiful cinematic platformer with an excellent soundtrack, fun puzzles, and a heartfelt story. This is an example of how to tell a story with no dialogue. The speech featured here is in a probably fake language, but the message is clear nonetheless. The presentation is the highlight here. The visuals and soundtrack mesh perfectly. Its art direction reminds me of Studio Ghibli with the vibrant colors and cutesy models. Despite being 2.5D, the environments have a lot of depth to them. The backgrounds are full of detail and showcase impressive scale making the world feel huge. There are moments that feel like I'm watching a good animated movie.As is typical of the genre, there are chase sequences, semi-realistic movement, puzzles, and one-hit deaths. It's not a difficult game at all and can be beaten in a single playthrough. The controls are tight and platforming isn't as complicated as some other cinematic platformers like the old Oddworld games. Directing the companion is simple and easy to do. It's also very adorable and you can pet it whenever. There's a good variety of locations like underground caverns, the swamp, a desert area, and a high tech facility.I don't have many complaints, but I thought the quick time events were out of place. I'd prefer more gameplay or just another cutscene. The final boss is rather lackluster. You just time some jumps and do an easy QTE. I also found the repeated fade to blacks distracting and odd since it fades to black before a cutscene plays following whatever you were doing in gameplay. Nonetheless, I think it's a great simple game. It's definitely style over substance, but the style is really incredible and the substance isn't bad. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This is made by an Indie Developer, and so I definitely give this game a high score probably a 9/10. I look forward to the next episode in the series. It's a mix of a walking simulator with some light puzzles, some nice music, and a cool heart warming story.Pretty good game with at least six hours of content. I'd recommend playing through this with some friends or some young kids if you have any. There are puzzles that aren't too difficult, some platforming challenges, and a pretty cool Sci-Fi flavored storyline. There are no words or reading in the whole game, so anyone of any age should be able to play along with you as you run through this. The only challenge would be one part, which is a mathematical puzzle that involves binary, and I think that will be probably be the most challenging part.I had a good time and enjoyed the storyline. It warns about flashing lights, and that's mostly at the end of the game besides some bright flashing when you launch the game. I have some eye sensitivity so I really wish games had an option to turn off bright flashes, but it didn't bother me too bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Some sort of alien arachnid army has descended on the planet and is abducting all the life forms, but to what end?  Naturally, it’s up to Lana to save the planet, and she’ll need to work in tandem with Mui to sneak her way across the planet, defeat the alien threat, and save her people.  Sounds like a video game to me.Overall, the gameplay can best be described as generic with a few moments of brilliance thrown in when it comes to a few of the puzzles and stealth sections.  There is no combat.  Stealth is a priority and discovery often equals death, but the generation checkpoint system saves before nearly every possible thing that could kill you.  The real standout feature is the co-op moments between Lana and Mui, clever in design and seamlessly integrated into the environment and architecture so they don’t seem like busy work.  With simple commands you can order Mui to sit and stay or come to your position.  You can also point him to specific spots, which comes in useful later when Mui needs to hit switches, cut cables, or ride around on a hacked security bot.Everything else is pretty standard platforming with running and jumping and crouching through low passages, swinging and climbing ropes, dragging boxes around to use as steps.  What sets all this apart though is the incredibly clean and sharp graphics.  My 4090 was crushing this at 4K 120fps with everything maxed out and it looked incredible.  The storybook art style and the expert use of parallax layers including a prominent black silhouette layer in the foreground creates a convincing 3D environment and a wonderful sense of depth in every scene.  They could have used some more unique locations.  The forest, mountains, and desert themes seemed to run on a bit long.Planet of Lana is a one and done adventure offering a quality experience for a great price and is scalable for just about any PC that still plays games, but on a high-end rig, this was like playing a Studio Ghibli movie.Read the full review at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This game either should have been about half the length, or it needed a lot more puzzle ideas.The visual style is done quite well, especially the environmental art. The soundtrack is great, although it is a bit limited, and the main theme gets used way too often without enough variation. Kudos to the story being shown as opposed to told, and the emotional moments are sold well. However, while I'm all for letting a story breathe and a sense of pace, some story moments linger far too long. Several story sections each needed to be trimmed by a good 20-30 seconds as they went on long after the emotional impact and on to the point of annoyance.Lana - the protagonist whom you control - moves relatively slowly. That isn't necessarily an issue in a cinematic puzzle platformer such as this, except the game doesn't have enough interesting content to fill its length. Lana's movement isn't fun in itself, so environmental storytelling moments that are drawn out for too long as you saunter past, or coming upon the same puzzle elements being reused far too often, or moments where you're running through environments with nothing particularly interesting happening are all amplified. The puzzles are, for the most part, quite simple to figure out, but some have surprisingly tight execution timing windows for this type of game with this type of movement, and having to redo any of those puzzles after failing can feel like a slog while Lana jogs slowly along.The pace finally picks up a bit in the final act of the game, but even then it's not all that quick, and the rest of the game (~75% or so) needed to be edited down considerably to at least come close.Planet of Lana does several things very well, but the overuse of the same puzzle elements repeatedly and too much time spent with nothing new or interesting happening in both gameplay and story make this a game I can't recommend. I'm someone who enjoys a great soundtrack and an interesting story with emotional impact enough that it can make up for only having decent gameplay, and this game left me annoyed and frustrated by the end. There are way too many other puzzle platformers that are far more worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: AVOID | LACKING | MAYBE | WORTHWHILE |  | UNMISSABLEPlanet of Lana is an action-adventure puzzle and platformer game. It's definitely more in the cozy and atmospheric camp, making it somewhat akin to Firewatch in the style and walking simulator aspects, but it also reminded me quite a bit of Voyage given the juxtaposition of nature and technology, and the overall look of the game.I thought the storyline was quite interesting (though I'm predisposed to like games centered on female friendship). It reminded me of an updated version of War of the Worlds focused more on the human aspect of such a catastrophe. None of the puzzles were particularly difficult, though a few took me a few tries to figure out what I was supposed to do. The controls were good, though not being able to change direction while in the air is a pet peeve of mine in platforming games, and that was implemented here. The game looks great and clearly choices were made to make it stylistic, which I appreciated. The game took me just shy of 5 hours to complete, and I suspect most people would finish in 4-6 hours. I think the price is slightly too much given the length and replayability (I suspect for most people, this is a one-and-done game), but I certainly don't feel ripped off or anything. While I don't think Planet of Lana will change your mind if you don't already enjoy puzzle/platformer/action-adventure/walking simulator games, it's easy to recommend if you want a mostly relaxing foray into those genres for a few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: A Heavenly Planet: Experiencing the Planet of LanaHaving just put down my controller after completing the first chapter of Planet of Lana, I felt immediately compelled to share my experience with this masterful piece of art.From the moment I plunged into this enchanting odyssey, I was bewitched. The game, steeped in emotion and intricately layered with profound storytelling, is a deep dive into the intersection of art and gaming, much like its spiritual predecessor, Limbo. But in Lana, we find a sharper edge of sentiment and soul that adds depth to the entire experience.Planet of Lana tells its story through gorgeous hand-drawn visuals, arresting backdrops, and a wonderfully ambient soundtrack that pulls you into its heart. It's not just a game; it's a lovingly crafted world you get to inhabit and explore, painted with such exquisite care and detail that you feel its breath, pulse, and ebbs and flow.Indeed, where Limbo often leaned into its atmospheric gloom, Planet of Lana chooses to embellish its poignant narrative with vibrant and contrasting colors, imbuing a sense of hope and determination in the face of adversity. The characters are fleshed out not through text or dialogue but through expressive animations, leading to a rare empathetic connection in most games.The puzzles in the first chapter are wonderfully designed, cleverly woven into the narrative, and never feel obtrusive or out of place. They challenge the intellect without leaving you in utter despair, allowing for a gratifying sense of accomplishment after each solution.Yet, what truly sets Planet of Lana apart is its emotional undercurrent. This is where the game raises the bar, transcending from being a mere atmospheric puzzle platformer to something profoundly human. Every interaction, every obstacle, and every quiet moment of reflection resonates with raw emotion and touches the heart.Never before have I felt such a gamut of emotions in the first chapter of a game: excitement, tension, joy, fear, and an overwhelming sense of empathy and connection. The way Lana and her pet interact and communicate evokes strong emotions, making their journey profoundly personal and their triumphs and setbacks ours.In conclusion, Planet of Lana stands on the shoulders of the giant that is Limbo and reaches for the stars. Its captivating narrative, unique gameplay, and mesmerizing aesthetic make it a game that demands to be experienced. It's an emotional tour de force that is as heart-rending as beautiful. If the first chapter indicates what's to come, I can confidently say that Planet of Lana is on its way to being a modern masterpiece.

Suits the game perfectly, so kudos to the composers/producers on that. This flows through to the artwork as well. It's a beautiful looking game.What I would love to see from Wishfully in the future is a game similar to this (minus the secondary character control) is basically this game, but with Metroidvania movement. Double jumps, dashs, dodges, coyote systems, jump buffers, the whole nine. Or just some of it. Now, Metroidvanias are my favorite genre, so of course I would wish for more features such as that, however, don't let that discourage you from this game. I know Inside had a sprint (or maybe Limbo did?) but either way, this game is 100% worth it. You'll find yourself getting lost in the story, the beauty of the atmosphere, and so much more. Definitely give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a love letter to Flashback (1992) and it's EXCELLENT. _childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a whimsical journey through a land of many faces where you control the titular Lana, a girl trying to find her lost sibling amidst a mysterious alien attack on her home. The game will feel quite familiar to fans of Limbo and Inside, as the puzzles and even terrain are quite reminiscent of those titles. The gameplay is engaging and the soundtrack is cinematic-level good, providing players with an enjoyable 4-5 hours to sink themselves into the world of Lana. Planet of Lana’s story is a simple one, but not one I’ll get into here. The game gives you a brief tutorial where you’ll familiarize yourself with movement, stealth, and actions, before plunging you into the story’s inciting incident first-hand. During your journey, you’ll be accompanied by an adorable cat-like companion Mui. Mui can assist you with puzzles and overall traversal, and they provide some much-needed company in a game almost devoid of any other characters. The game’s various environments are gorgeously animated and teeming with life if you know where to look, and seeing the levels transition from lush and green outdoor areas to cold and dark industrial areas serves as an organic and visual reminder of how far you’ve come. The game truly is beautiful to look at, and I don’t think I’ve taken as many screenshots of any other game than I did with Planet of Lana. Some real wallpaper material stuff. As mentioned, a large part of the game will be you solving puzzles (typically with Mui), and though these aren’t brain-busters, they did give me some trouble here and there. My only gripe with them is that there are some puzzles where you need to control a drone, and the drone controls like a cat on ice skates. Beyond that, the puzzles eventually present their solutions after a bit of trial and error, and I wouldn’t call any of them impossible.Planet of Lana also features an absolutely stunning soundtrack, one that would (at least for me) rival some AAA soundtracks. It’s available on Spotify so if you loved listening to the music scoring your journey you’d be remiss not to check it out.Overall, Planet of Lana is very much worth your money. Viva indie.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana, a game blooming with personality. A game so beautiful you'll get lost in the background, foreground, creatures, music and sound design.The gameplay feels similar to "Inside", another sidescroller, but with a horror setting and no companion.Planet of Lana borrows the movement and feel of the character, but everything else is so unique.The artistic style of the game is simple, but the color choices and fluidity of the animations are so polished that you sometimes forget you're playing a game. Controlling Lana and her companion feels very natural, the devs did an amazing job. I was never frustrated because of how the game handled, no complaints in that department at all.I took a dive into the negative reviews to see what reasons people had for disliking it, and it was like i expected.People disliked the puzzles (Granted they are a bit easy) and the long stretches of enviroment. I get why people would prefer having more "Game" and less "Art and music". But that's the trade-off that comes with making a game this artistically beautiful and immersive.The game is more about taking in the sights, exploring the beautiful and mystical world along with your companion. If you want a lot of gameplay and interactivity with lots of input; this game may not be for you. But if you're fine with just sitting back, relaxing and enjoying this gorgeous world and it's cute characters, i think you'll have an incredible time. I sure did.I bought the game on sale for 10 euro, but i would've absolutely paid 15 euro. I personally think 20 euro is a bit steep, but i get why it's set at 20. A LOT of work has been put into Planet of Lana, and it clearly shows. My only complaint is that it wasn't longer, but i think that if it was, it would've felt dragged out and lose some of it's charm. So i'm glad the devs stuck to what we have here.Thank you devs, for making a game so unique and refreshing, and thank you for letting me experience it.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. Soulful pastel art that reminds me of the FAR series, layered on top of a barebones but meaningful story, and with far more of a focus on music than I first realised. It's still engaging puzzle work with surprisingly punitive timing for such a graphic and story-driven game. The movement is a little slow and unenjoyable at first, but I got used to it and found I liked the added challenge--and realism--of a (deliberately, I surmise) clunkier movement system. Less patient people might get bored, but for me the game itself was never a chore and even if it was the ending would still have been absolutely worth it. Short but sweet.Brilliant game.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana - 10/10If you enjoy puzzle games such as Limbo & Inside, and are also a fan of Ghibliesque art style, Planet of Lana is the game for you. I absolutely enjoy a good puzzle game, especially a good side scrolling puzzle platformer, so it’s no surprise that I fell in love with Planet of Lana the moment I picked it up. I will admit, a typical issue I come across in similar games is a lack of narrative. It might be just a ‘me’ issue, in that I struggle with interpretive stories, but Planet of Lana did a wonderful job in creating a clear storyline. The story itself might not necessarily be unique, but it is still incredibly heartwarming and gripping all while accompanied by beautifully stunning visuals. There is no dialogue, narration, or subtitles, but the characters speak a made-up language and have so much emotion in what little sounds are made. We begin our journey in, what looks to be, a small fishing village. Villagers are going about their  usual daily routines as children, in particular Lana and her sister, run through the village for a bit of fun. As they reach the outskirts of the village, invaders from the sky begin capturing everyone in the village, including Lana’s sister. Lana begins doing whatever she can to reach where the invaders have taken her sister, which includes hiding from and manipulating the surroundings to avoid capture. Along the way, she finds the cutest companion and they continue on this journey together. For me, Planet of Lana was an absolute 10/10. Once I picked it up, I couldn’t put it down. The story, the art style, the narrative, the soundtrack, all came together to create a beautiful game filled with such incredible emotion. I’ve seen a few reviews mention it’s not worth the price point at $19.99 because of its short length. However, I strongly disagree because a shorter game done right can be so much more rewarding than a 30 hour game with a bunch of filler. So if you have been questioning whether to pick this one up, I’m here to highly recommend picking this one up!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever played any of Playdead's offerings, like Limbo or Inside, you'll know exactly what to expect here. It's a puzzle platformer where you, mostly, run to the right doing puzzley platformy things. There's little to see in PoL that you haven't seen in other genre entries; you'll push crates, swing on ropes, jump around and engage in rudimentary stealth. PoL has a couple of unique mechanics of its own, but nothing particularly special. Still, it does all of these things well enough and feels fluid and responsive to control.In terms of narrative it's relatively straightforward; you play as the titular Lana who's planet is invaded by a mysterious force that is kidnapping her people (including her best friend). Thus, the journey to rescue them, and figure out who these invaders are and what they want begins. There's no real dialogue in this game, the characters speak in a made up language and you get the gist though context and actions. Since you have little time to get invested in Lana's human friendship before the kidnappings, the game deploys the age old device of a cute animal sidekick to provide most of its core emotional elements. It's all fine and there is a bit of lore to discover and decipher too.So it sounds like Lana is pretty middle of the road? Well, yes and no. What sets PoL apart from its genre peers are its gorgeous Ghibli inspired visuals, super fluid animation and stellar audio design/music. This game is an absolute treat to behold whether static or in motion and it sounds fantastic too (special shout out to the beautiful vocals).So while PoL may not be the most mechanically interesting game out there, and other games do many of the same things, as an experience its more than the sum of its parts. If you like these sorts of games, this is one of the better ones. If you've never tried one this is fine place to start. Oh, and like most games of this type it's relatively short, expect between 4-6 hours to complete.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is an absolute visual masterpiece. The world is exquisitely crafted, with every frame resembling a stunning piece of art.  The simplicity of the gameplay mechanics makes it a breeze to play, allowing players of all skill levels to enjoy the journey without any stress or pressure. It's a truly relaxing and tranquil game that offers a much-needed escape from the chaos of everyday life. If you're looking for a visually breathtaking and easygoing adventure, Planet of Lana is an absolute must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: My closest comparison to this game is the movie WALL-E: A visually gorgeous, emotional, larger-than-life sci-fi odyssey, told through minimal dialogue. And it's just as good.I'm seeing some criticism of the relatively short game time for the price. But here's the thing: This is not a game about getting max playtime or losing yourself in complex puzzles. Think of yourself as buying a ticket to see WALL-E on the big screen, in all of it's beautifully drawn and animated glory. It's really not about the puzzles - they are there to advance the story, to serve as obstacles our protagonists encounter along their journey.No movies you want to see in the theater right now? Spend your Saturday evening curled up with your PC, and experience this masterpiece. (And FWIW, I used the keyboard controls just fine - no need for a controller.)
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to play a short game that just has you working with the environment around you then this is for you. If you want a bit of puzzles, no combat, some semi skilled jumping maneuvers, you will enjoy this. The scenery is beautiful in this game. The music is lovely. the monsters aren't too scary, and you have a cute little cat-like companion. I nabbed this game on sale because I wanted a something small to play through. I was hoping for some deeper story involved. I would rate it a 3 out of 5 stars. It's not awful in any means, but it's not something groundbreaking. I personally like my platform puzzle games to have deeper lore involved, ones that I can scan through the internet finding others creating theories on, solely based on a game that's under 20 hours long. That doesn't have that, in fact, there isn't much chance for multiple play throughs. Yes, there are some collectibles and achievements to grab if you so do wish to go back, and you could one day play this again, but overall it isn't one you can keep playing over and over finding new amazing things each time. It's a good game, if you were already interested in it you won't regret buying. I would suggest buying on a sale though, as this game can be finished in a day or even one sitting. It's under 10 hours and that was with me dying and trying to figure some stuff out when playing. I don't regret purchasing in anyway, I just felt it was super super short, even for my already expectations on it being a short game.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely brilliant, amazing and wonderful experience.  Not just to play this game, but to explore this world and go through this amazing journey!  The visual and environmental story telling is some of the very best I've ever seen!!  The more of the world you see the more you want to see. _childDocuments_.review: Nice cinematic platformer. It's like Inside, but in a more positive mood, with blue sky, green trees and a cute alien pet. _childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a wonderful, heartfelt adventure. The art is beautiful. The characters are compelling, even with the dialogue being in an alien language. The puzzles are satisfying, never too difficult, and the movement is smooth and graceful. I found myself really affected by the characters' stories by the end, and it did make me cry a bit (oh happy tears)! There is a good sense of mystery and wonder as you explore and progress, and also real danger. Warning that there is a lot of traumatic circumstances in this story, and a lot of children-in-danger scenes (watching yourself die can be tough), and the stakes are high. I expected a cute, pretty adventure, so I was surprised by how intense it can be. So go in prepared for that. They do spring some quick-time events on you with limited warning, so be ready for that as well. All-in all, this is a wonderful, inspired story that is worth your time! Some of the visuals at the end are downright brilliant.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re looking for an adventure game that will captivate your heart, mind and senses, Planet of Lana is a perfect choice!The first thing that I noticed about this game is the breathtaking artwork! You share this adventure with a small companion that you befriend on your journey called Mui, and by combining both of your unique abilities, you overcome obstacles and progress through the adventure. _childDocuments_.review: 2D platformer with puzzle elements, gorgeous graphics, orchestral soundtrack and visual storytelling.In a little village, Lana lives with her sister Elo. One day, they witness machines falling from the skies, and then, Elo and all the villagers are abducted by these machines. Only Lana can escape.She sets out on an epic journey to find her sibling, and on the way, she encounters and befriends a friendly little cat-like creature she calls Mui. Together, they follow the trail of the machines. Many times, they have to evade machines and overcome obstacles, which requires the player to coordinate both characters: Lana can jump, pull objects and operate machines, but on her own, she can't reach the same high places that Mui can. But she can command Mui to go to specific spots, to stay or to follow, to press buttons, etc. These puzzles aren't overly tricky for the most part. The platforming, too, is quite doable - you don't have to jump with pixel precision to get from A to B, nor do you have to do pull off complicated maneuvers.I enjoyed the detailed and beautiful graphics and the music (although IIRC it seems mostly absent from the middle part of the game). The relationship between Lana and Mui was cute to see, also because Mui is animated and "voiced" so adorably. The story was interesting enough, with some impressive or touching scenes here and there. All in all, a nice little game.

It quicly becomes boring and like someone else said you at some point you play just to finish it so I just stopped.They should have done a short animated film with this design and story instead.

_childDocuments_.review: 8h 10/10 without save scum trick, otherwise 8/10 1 I wrote  No Yes, there are 2 missable achievements. You'll have to play through the whole game without you or your companion dying.   No No No No No No NoPlanet of Lana is such a beautiful platformer/puzzle/adventure game. You play as Lana and will go on a very stressful adventure to find your missing sister. While something weird is happening in the world with robots who are kidnapping humans and burning their cities. What are they doing with them, where is everybody and most important where is your sister, is she safe? As stated above, the game has gorgeous artwork. Not only is the artwork beautiful but the music and the sound effects are outstanding as well. They make that you'll get immersed into the game quite quickly and you'll be emotionally invested. and believe me, Planet of Lana will pull on some heartstrings. The puzzles in Planet of Lana will start easy. However, they will get more complex the further you get and also will be time/skill based. I heard from others that they found the puzzles easy, but I needed some time to figure some of them out. This might be because I almost finished Planet of Lana in one sitting and was tempted to get a break in between but I was so close to finishing that I decided to just keep going. This might not have helped with my concentration but I was just so emotionally invested in the story. What I have been wondering throughout the game, Lana will shout out for her missing sister during the game, but when she does that at the start of a new area, she doesn't know if that would help her find her sister or if she just told the enemies she is coming. It helped with feeling how hard she tried to find her sister, but my logical brain found it quite dangerous to do so. There were a few small things that I encountered and was less impressed by. For example, some of the loading screens were white, while most of them were black. I prefer black as white is so bright and I don't understand why some of them are even white. Another thing that I encountered quite a lot is that the character movement is sometimes a bit off. I couldn't count how many times I thought I made jumped at the right time but ended up dead because I just barely missed the edge. It isn't too bad as there are quite a lot of spawn points even in the middle of puzzles, but it sucks if you're going for the achievement for completing the game without dying. Speaking about the achievements; a lot of them are story related and can't be missed. For that reason, I would not recommend scrolling through guides or achievement-tracking websites as you might get spoiled. On your own profile, they are hidden, so you won't get spoiled. There are also 11 achievements that have something to do with the 10 hidden shrines that can be found, and believe me, they are really quite hidden. During the game but also after finishing it, you can use chapter select to find the missing ones, and looking up where they are is quite easy as the achievements are numbered. And then there are the 2 achievements for which you need to complete the game without dying. This is so hard to do, not only because movement isn't always fluent, but also because a lot of puzzles require a bit of trial and error, and that isn't possible if you go for this achievement. I understand why they added it to the game as it adds an extra layer of you caring for Lana and your companion Mui but it is brutal. On PC it is possible to save scum your way through this achievement, but on consoles, it is just almost impossible to do this. You will also only know if you succeeded at the end of the game, there is no way during the game to know if you're still on zero deaths. I loved playing through Planet of Lana, it is beautiful and emotional and just amazing. However, I would highly recommend not going for those last 2 achievements to keep your sanity and enjoy the game even more.

_childDocuments_.review: Invaded by a faceless force, Lana witnesses her best friend being captured and whisked away to a destination unknown. Lana undertakes the perilous journey to rescue her friend and stop the evil from spreading. Along the way she befriends an animal companion that helps her overcome challenges.Planet of Lana is a puzzle game in the main, but it does also contain arcade sequences, quick time events, and rather a lot of stealth.Most of the puzzle solutions I felt I had seen before, with a lot of hiding in bushes trying to evade the glare of the enemy, especially at the start of the adventure. Puzzles did get more varied towards the end, with a more mixed approach to game play, and I particularly enjoyed the relationship between Lana and her pet Mui who work together to solve problems. Lana can control Mui and command him to stay and approach. She can direct him to certain places where he can use his abilities, like cutting ropes to help Lana climb rock faces, or hypnotizing creatures to aid in puzzle solving. Lana must be close to Mui to direct him, which can act as part of the puzzle, and I did sometimes have a little difficulty controlling the cursor, as it felt very sensitive in its movement, and with certain puzzles requiring quick movements, it occasionally proved frustrating. I’m probably being a bit picky, but I think it is worth mentioning. Puzzles are very logical, which is always welcomed, and I think they were so logical that they almost felt too intuitive and easy to complete. They still required a little thinking, and I did get stuck on one puzzle and had to look up the solution, but mostly you would just do what you would have done if you were Lana. For me, that made the game appear very realistic and just immersed me further into the story. There are some dramatic sections that require quick maneuvering or quick time events, but they aren’t that difficult, and because checkpoints are very generous, any failures throw you straight back into play, and there are no annoying repetitions.Planet of Lana feels like an adventure rather than a puzzle game with story elements. I have played countless puzzle games where a story has attempted to join together puzzle sections and felt mediocre at best, but Planet of Lana is an example of how a puzzle game and a decent story can have a fruitful marriage.  Beautiful environments, interesting characters and enemies, with camera angles that flatter the scenery and create a luscious landscape that feels alive. Just the way Lana moves are pleasant to watch which elevates game play.There is quite a variety in landscapes from forest and swamplands, to ancient civilizations, progressing to futuristic looking locales. It all looks stunning, especially for a predominantly based puzzle game. Superb special effects sounds immerse you in the drama as it unfolds, especially at the onset which is gripping. There are beautiful orchestral themes playing at poignant moments and scattered throughout the game. There is no voice acting, but the mimicking of voices is done well and does create emotion especially in combination with the dreamy soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is light's out gorgeous. The story is captivating and mysterious. The music/score is near perfect. It's truly a wonderful and beautiful experience. The actual gameplay, however, leaves a lot to be desired. I wish the puzzle diversity and difficulty had increased as the game progressed. It was definitely worth playing through for the art and story alone but more engaging and diverse gameplay would have elevated this game to almost perfect. 7.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful puzzle platformer that focuses on telling a story with no words. At first it seems kid-focused, and overall it's much more of a walking simulator than a puzzler, but the difficulty ramps seriously in the end. (Hint: if you have trouble with the bosses, turn the  quick time events off from the accessibility menus.) All in all, if you love Another World, Limbo, Inside, Braid or Little Nightmares, you'll like this one, despite its lots of filler, err, contemplative moments :) and its gameplay mechanics that feel less fluid than all of these classics. If you don't care for achievements and secrets, you'll probably spend 4 hours on the Planet of Lana.

_childDocuments_.review: Sort of recommend. It's alright. It's cute. If it's your first foray into these sorts of atmospheric 2D platformers, then it's a good intro. Bit simple, bit short (I got an achievement suggesting I was at the final act in under 3 hours), bit shallow, not particularly compelling, not particularly original. With a bit more depth and complexity it could be quite good. The main problem is that all the things it's good at, it doesn't do any better than other games. You want an interesting setting, some obviously hidden lore to uncover, and puzzles that actually feel tense and like they're part of the world? Inside does that far better than Lana. As does Little Nightmares. Lana basically does nothing that Limbo didn't do thirteen years ago. At least playing Inside I was actually nervous of the dogs etc as I was playing, and it felt like I was actually trying to get away. Sure as ♥♥♥♥ not worried about getting away from the robuts in this, cause in all the cut scenes I just run past them and they ignore me. It was a nice departure from the horror aspect that these games seem to attract, but it didn't really do enough with the stuff that WAS different. Make the lore deeper and give me something to sink my teeth into. Make me feel like I'm solving a big mystery as I go along with the little puzzles, that would suit the brighter, nicer atmosphere they've created really nicely.

_childDocuments_.review: is a callback to the first era of indie gaming where every protagonist was a kid (or other large headed individual) in a big scary world, advancing by puzzle-solving and platforming your way to the end.Puzzles, puzzles everywhere, intuitive and easy to grasp, push crates, flip switches and operate machinery to get to the next section.You play as Lana in a world where a robot invasion just took place as you try to avoid the mechanical menace while searching for your brother Elo.I’m a sucker for landscapes, and this game has some breathtaking vistas along a very pleasing artstyle.A perfect game for someone starting out as it nails that visual part with the cinematic flair a first-timer might want.For a 4-hour game some sections really feel drawn out a lot, long puzzling sections that are just a repurposed version of the previous steal the spotlight to what could’ve been a really interesting sci-fi world.It also feels like an old-school indie, but this is a minor nitpick, as to me it may feel the title doesn’t bring anything new, but to someone relatively new to gaming it will be a new way to experience the classics in a new light.For what the game brings to the table I can’t say its worth the asking price, but definitely get it on a discount if you’re in the mood for some classic and simple puzzle-solving with great visuals.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful narrative work with fun and intuitive controls. The world building is exceptional for what is essentially a text-free game experience. The artwork and soundtrack are gorgeous, and the characterisation, while relatively simple, manages to convey a depth of emotion that is genuinely moving. From the very beginning the world is established as a place of natural beauty and simplicity, as the tutorial/intro provides a tour of Lana's home town while following her sister. From there, the story takes a dark turn  Lana's quest  takes you through a variety of landscapes, showing off the beautiful painting/cell-shaded environments, and gradually introducing hints of the history of the planet and Lana's people. There are moments of tragedy and exultation, simple pleasures and existential horrors, obstacles great and small, and eventually the game ends and you're sad because you just want more of everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Steam clocked me at 7.6 hours playtime, but I tend to get up and go wander around while it's paused, so maybe that's a high estimate.  I think for most people play time will be between 5-10 hours.  The game is really pretty, which is a big part of what initially got my attention to buy it.  At times though, the visuals take more of a lead than actual gameplay.  There are a lot of long cut scenes and parts where the character is just running through beautiful landscapes for a distractingly long time.  Only 1-2 puzzles had me stumped longer than the first couple of tries, so for many I think it will feel too simplistic and redundant.  Plot reveals weren't epic or novel.  That said, I had a really nice time, enjoyed the puzzles, visuals, and the overall story. I recommend it, especially if you snag it on sale like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: There are two sides of the coin in this game. Planet of Lana is very casual in both its story and performance. It was enjoyable, and you can easily see that it is friendly to any casual players, as the puzzles aren't too hard to solve and not too easy to get bored. The music and score are incredibly good. However, on the flip side, it's kind of game that you may forget about after two months. I had a great time playing it though, just couldn't help but wish it to leave something more, like Limbo or Inside once did (Can't help but make a comparison with these excellent works). The kind of game that makes you think about yourself, others, and the world around you. Despite all the elements in this game that are full of potential, Planet of Lana still lacks 'something' to achieve excellence—something we might call 'profundity' in both its story and gameplay.Anyway, this doesn't make it a bad game. In fact, it's far from deserving labels like 'Stupid Puzzle Game' or 'Boring.' Especially if you played through to the 'Horizon scene' and still hold those attitudes. I can't help but feel sorry for you if you struggled with your appreciation.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie, my dyslexic self first read the title as “Planet of Anal” and I was deeply confused……and after realizing my mistake, a bit disappointed.It’s like Inside, but outside.This was the first game my daughter beat on her own without any help from me. For her this game will be a core memory. So for that I am thankful for this game. We finished Planet of Lana just last month and haven't stopped thinking about it since. The art style. The music. The foreboding atmosphere. The tension is palpable. I could actually feel this game. Without wanting to ramble, Planet of Lana does things and goes places I never would've expected. It's pure magic.Planet of Lana is a side scrolling, platforming, puzzle game. It was short, sweet, and mildly challenging. The briefest, spoiler-free synopsis is that you play a young girl, searching to find her sister who was kidnapped by strange, alien robots. You meet a companion, a cat, and journey through the world, solving puzzles and avoiding being captured by the sinister robots. You unlock a few new abilities along your way to help you. Visually the game looks great. I wouldn’t go so far as to call it stunning, but the artistic styling was pleasing and the color palate shifts during different segments of the game, especially at the end, was striking. There were a few times where the game zooms out to reveal some really magnificent set pieces. Also the gibberish language made the visual storytelling even more pronounced.Music is so much better than it deserves to be and it’s almost worth playing for that alone. It was great and really helped convey the emotions of the characters. The sound effects were pretty standard, and far from the primary focus of the game. I liked the artistic decision to use an in-universe language with no subtitles. If forces you to use the music and the character’s tone to understand their feelings, and the use of set pieces and art on the walls to tell the pieces of the story was well done and compelling. For the gameplay, the puzzles were fun and moderately challenging at times, but nothing that couldn’t be figured out in a few tries or less. It played like Limbo/Inside and is very similar to Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons in using two characters to open doors to progress through areas. Puzzle design was well executed, but far from innovative and though not amazing, they’re nothing really nothing you wouldn’t recognize in other similar games in this genre. At times though, games don't need to bring anything new to be a pleasant and fulfilling experience to play. My only complaint is that there are times where the controls feel a bit wonky, but it’s hard to elaborate on this without some puzzle mechanic spoilers. This game took me about 6 and a half hours to finish, and was a joy throughout. I think it certainly merits a second playthrough and I wager it would take about 12 to 15 hours to 100% complete the game and achievements. And I actually quite enjoyed that 6-7 hour playtime, it's great to have games you feel like you can actually complete in a busy life.Beautiful graphics! Amazing soundtrack! Captivating storie! It is not the most difficult game though. But I have just enjoyed every second of it. It was a powerful experience for at least one person (me). I had tears running down my cheeks and a smile on my face for the final 30ish minutes. It's not a game that's going to move the Limbo-inspired genre forward. But it was a good time because of the presentation and polish. The visuals, robot designs, and Lana's animation were very well done. The slow pacing also helps you to appreciate the environments and background. There were enough clever puzzles imo that things didn't get stale throughout the game.This shows that good games don't always have to be bigger (like for example a Bethesda RPG) or more complex. To be honest... It owns its place in the most enjoyable games I have ever placed! People need to talk more about these good games, these little surprises. The gaming industry isn't as doomed as how the bleak stuff covered by the media make most think. If you’re looking for a relaxing, low stakes adventure with a few challenges peppered throughout, Planet of Lana is a visually pleasing romp through a strange and intriguing world that’s VERY much worth your time. What are you waiting for?9/10

The graphics are wonderful but what real elevates this game is its amazing sound and music. If i was going to nitpick they could have made the puzzles more difficult and varied. _childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Visually it looks fantastic. I like the mystery of the story up to the point I've played so far.Gameplay wise it's fairly dull. I've been playing it for 1.5h straight so far and it feels like your the actor in a cinematic where you just keep going in one direction. It's interrupted with a puzzle every now and then. Outside of one or two that I've experienced so far, the only challenge they present is to go here, then take a longer way back around to finish it. Most of the time it takes longer to walk to the next puzzle then to do the puzzle.Hour and a half in and the story hasn't progressed at all, other than making a new pet friend that is only used to unsuccessfully add more depth to a puzzle. _childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles/Gameplay 2/10-There were 1 or 2 good puzzles within the game the rest is just really simple content that never expands on the concepts that are introduced-The amount of repeated stealth segments is mind numbing, they have to be added to pad the runtime IDK what other reason-Out of place QTE sequencences-The last Hour of the game virtually has 0 puzzles or gameplayVisuals 8/10+The graphical style is really nice and and the painterly environments are pleasant+A few stand out backdrops that are great to look at-Some of the environments i found interesting were only played in for like <5 minutes and i would have liked to stick around and do some more puzzles within them-Death animations were very lackluster in comparison to other titles where the character clearly just touches some collision box and instantly goes limp, you can just die from touching a monster that doesn't even notice youSound 7/10+ Sounded fine overall with some decent environmental+ I like the jingle+ Enjoyed the sound of the characters speaking and the cat- The vocal song that is played feels really cheesy and on the nose-Multiple cut outs of music and sound effects (IDK if its my computer)Preformance 7/10+Overall preformed nice besides a few audio glitches-My character did not load in one of the scenes after a transition and then black void, upon "reload last chapter" the game crashedStory 4/10+ Plot leads the character to pleasant environments- Very derivative, its visuals and story have been done to death- Nothing surprising or thought provoking in the storyOther- Collectable shrines not rewardingIt took me about 2-3 hrs to beat the game for first time and another 2ish hrs to find the collectables ( alot of repeated slow segments and unskipable cutscenes) Overall Id give the game like a 5/10I enjoyed looking at things but the puzzles were very shallow
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is one of those games that will stick in the memory for years. It's gorgeous visuals are undoubtedly a primary focus here, and are supported by a stunning soundtrack (and a stellar performance by Siobhan Wilson). The whole experience feels fluid in motion and full of heart. Mui is fantastic little companion too.If you're a fan of Playdead's work on LIMBO and INSIDE or Tarsier's on Little Nightmares, you'll definitely love Wishfully's sci-fi epic.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana has done something truly creative and remarkable.Its clever way of connecting diegetic and non-diegetic music is one of a kind.It’s not just combining the two; it’s integrating the simple yet deeply meaningful 10-note core melody into the story, atmosphere and gameplay in a coherent manner, as a NON-musical adventure game.It elevates the notion of “original score” to a new level in interactive gaming.Together with its meticulous sound design, this game is an innovative auditory masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: A game worth playing, a story worth discovering, and characters worth remembering. Breathtaking cinematic shots that put you in the world of Planet Of Lana. The game play gave me an extremely enjoyable experience with ever changing scenarios, tempo, environments, character interaction, and level design.I would highly recommend anyone and everyone who comes across this game to play it. I am very glad I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: is a delightful puzzle platformer with stunning dynamic deep backgrounds, masterful soundtrack and a fantastic story that borrows ideas from multiple sources. Gameplay mainly focuses on your interaction with your companion to solve puzzles and help avoid the menacing creatures that you will encounter on your journey.
