The game is roughly 5 hours long, divided in 12 chapters each with unique environments and hidden shrines to find. Puzzles are on the easier side to ensure smooth progression through your journey. Give this game a try if you like simple puzzle platformers or you enjoyed similar games like  or . [9/10]
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Many negative reviews say this game is too short and too basic, I have to strongly disagree.It took me 7 hours to complete and that is only because once I started, I could not put it down, until I had completed it.Yes the puzzles are not exactly going to challenge any hardened gamers, but sometimes we must remember that kids exist too, and this is perfect for children to learn and challenge their skills while having fun at the same time.The atmosphere, graphics, music and story is jaw dropping and for someone who just wants to escape to another world for a few hours, this is perfect.Oh and yes, I cried...;)
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Very satisfying game. Slick production, animations, character coding for mantling and acknowledging walls and edges is very good, (I'm a nerd who appreciates that 😂). Lovely art style, challenging but also relaxing most of the time. Good puzzles, platforming and a few very well thought out and implemented sequences and camera moves. I'd put it with Limbo, Inside and Sommerville. I got this as a combo with Sommerville and could not be happier with that purchase. Loved it!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: In the early 90's 'Another World' defined platforming adventure games for generations to come. It did so with a sparse palette, no dialogue, and little in the way of exposition. You picked up the story, learning as you went. While 'Planet of Lana' isn't about to redefine a genre, it calls to mind 'Another World' while doing its own thing and telling its own story. It reveals bits and pieces of itself as you play in such a way, that, if you know how to read the scenery, the pictures it paints will leave you begging for more details and letting your imagination fill in the blanks.This isn't a long game, and personally I think the last quarter of the game could do with a couple more chapters, but that doesn't mean I was in any way disappointed. I enjoyed every minute I spent on Planet of Lana, and even if this isn't a game with a lot of replayability built in, that's okay. Not every game needs 3,000 easter eggs, branching storylines and a dozen possible endings. A good story stays with you, and that's what Planet of Lana is: a wonderful interactive story. One I might not re-read five times this year, but I'll probably pick it up again down the road and enjoy it every bit as much as I did the first time. How many games can manage that?
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding game. Challenging, but not frustrating puzzles. Sweet characters and the most outstanding music and sound effects in any game I've played this year. The gameplay is similar to Limbo, Inside and other side scrolling adventures. It's a short game, but you don't feel short changed because the artistry and gameplay is delightful.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Good little snack sized cinematic platformer.Easy, breezy and nice looking. Pretty good music as well.I enjoyed my time with the game - around 5 hours. The story is ok, but doesn't tread any new ground. It's all seen and done before. The game has a lovely, hand painted aesthetic. Environments are sparse and there's not a whole lot going on, but the developers have done a lot with a little. There's a few extra nice scenes that stand out, but they're rare.It's just a good, chill experience that doesn't outstay its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is an amazing game and tells a captivating story. 5-6 hours playtime might sound short, but the pacing is great. The mix of platforming and puzzle works from start to finish while simply looking stunning. Apart from that you will meet one of the greatest companions you could ask for. Don't miss this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautifully drawn, nothing you haven't seen before though.  After a few hours you start to notice some asset repetition though. The plot is predictable from the start and the execution is a bit disjointed.  The puzzles are easy, sometimes insultingly so, and when you finally find a few that seem complex, the game literally gives you the solution for them, because there are too many possibilities and no reasonable algorithmic way to find a solution. It's sad to see really. Another irritating thing is the use of QTE (quick time events) exactly at the wrong time.  Leaving aside the fact that QTE is a dubious concept, in this game it's just used to mask the lack of interactivity.  I guess it's easier to prompt the player to mash a button instead of giving them a situation where they have to dodge etc.All in all, cliché plot and gameplay and not much of them either.  Have you ever had to write an essay and you just add padding to it, and double spacing etc. just to get to the required number of words/pages? Well, this is the gaming equivalent of that. If you want to buy it, wait until it's 75% off or something because this is what it's worth, not a cent more
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely little sidescrolling puzzle adventure game with charm! A bit short for the price (~4.5 hours) so I recommend getting it during a sale.Very linear since it's story-focused, but that was fine with me.During my playthrough I only got mildly annoyed at two puzzles. So I'd say puzzle design is quite good. Even for someone who hasn't played many puzzle games.The artstyle reminded me a little of the Ori games. That was a plus since I absolutely love those games!All in all, Planet of Lana is in my opinion a great puzzle game with a pretty gripping story!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Breathtaking game! Well I loved this experience, especially the creature that follows us around. It looks like a cat and monkey combination, super cute, and given that I'm in crazy love with cats this was very empathetic for me. The sad/crying sounds the characters make when your animal companion or the protagonist die is so heartbreaking! Gameplay criticism: I couldn't stand the checkpoints! _childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Repetitive, slow and becomes boring.  Run, run, run, run, crouch down & go under a ledge, move an object to allow you to climb, repeat this over and over and there is the game. . And that's about it.  Puzzles are OK for a six year old, but not much else. I was greatly disappointed.   Graphics are nice, the sound track is good but shallow repetitive game play is not. _childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing little game with stunning visuals and unexpectedly awesome music and soundtracks, puzzles are simple to solve without any of them being too difficult or frustrating, smooth mechanics and a nice little side companion, story is a bit to the weaker side though ...An overall very good game that doesn't overwelcome its stay and provides a few hours of quality content for what it is. _childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: One of the first times I've actually used the walk feature in a game a lot. The world in this game is too beautiful to just run past it. I stopped so many times to just look at and listen. The art style, all the little details, sound design and music in this are fantastic. Also, if you have a dog or a cat as a pet, just buy the game right now.If you have played Inside and Somerville, some elements and the general direction of the story will seem very familiar to you. Also, the gameplay mechanics/riddles become a little repetitive the further you progress. None of this matters though. I definitely recommend playing this.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Look, the game looks really nice. But first of all, it's definitely not worth $20 for the length (3-4 hours). Secondly the puzzles are braindead easy and worse, they repeat themselves. I don't even mind if the gameplay is easy if it's at least enjoyable and varied, but it's not either. They sometimes introduce a new mechanic, then instead of going further with it, they just make you repeat the puzzle again and then you move onto the next area. It will usually take longer to implement the solution to the puzzle than it does to actually solve it. I mean I've seen better brainteasers in lowbrow games like Atomic Heart or Uncharted. There's no gameplay other than the puzzles, there's no action or setpieces, you just solve one easy puzzle and then go on to the next in a pretty lame fashion. The story is hard to follow, you just see random patterns scribbled on walls and I guess it's supposed to be deep? I legitimately feel like there isn't enough context to figure out what is supposed to be communicated. All I really know, is that the girl's best friend was captured. So the story and gameplay are both severely lacking, can the graphics carry it? Well, no, they can't, there's a lot of detail in the graphics but the level design being mostly a straight line means that even that gets to be pretty tiring. Overall just don't bother, I know it looks tempting visually but trust me, this one sucks.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent, definitely recommended.  The game takes you through several environments as the character uncovers the story.  I think having the sidekick help solve puzzles was a nice touch, and the logic is done very well - Mui never does anything frustrating or unpredictable.   The game relies on stealth and distraction to get around enemies and there are no weapons so if you like to go in guns blazing it may not be for you.  But if enjoy games like Far, Rime, and Aer, this is definitely worth a look.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game during the steam demo event a couple months ago and loved it. As soon as I found out it was released I bought it. I can say without a doubt hat this is one of my favourite game of all time. The score is beautiful and powerful and the graphics are akin to Studio Ghibli films. The pacing was good but having said that I felt it was slightly too short, especially at the end. I guess I just wanted more of this amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game! It's a heartwarming, casual puzzle game set in a beautiful (and at times, bleak) world that really drew me into it's embrace.  It's a really engaging game that makes you want to see it through to the end, not so much for the satisfaction of completing the game, but moreso for the simple joy of just being in the game world.The art-style is just beautiful - I found myself just stopping to enjoy the beauty of the world around me and sharing it with my faithful companion, Mui.  The simple and haunting score is totally in keeping with the beauty of the surroundings - a wonderful combination. It's the kind of game that deserves to be played not speed-run or for the sake of hollow 'achievements' but for the reward of engaging emotionally with it. A realy lovely game that's a good balance - the puzzles are not too difficult (except, perhaps, when piloting Mui on a drone, but that might be just me...) but are still satisfying to solve. I appreciated the onscreen tips about which key or button to press so I didn't have to remember much but instead, enjoy the experience of playing the game. My only real complaint is that I wish it were longer - I could've kept playing it for much longer, especially the gorgeous outside scenes! Speaking of outside, this game felt a lot like Inside (which is high praise as that's a bona-fide classic in this genre). While not as dark or surreal as Inside, Planet of Lana is a more friendly, gentle game but seems to  have been inspired by Inside, not because it's a side-scrolling platformer but more the overall 'lone protagonist vs dark technology' ethos, the level design that somehow feels similar with it's use of noise and the simple, but beautiful art-style. All of that makes Planet of Lana as satisfying to experience as Inside.All in all, a terrific game that I'd recommend to anyone with a heart. I'll miss that little cat....
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game was simply a transcendent experience. The visuals and the motion graphics for those visuals was nothing short of extraordinary. Although the puzzles were almost easy, it made sense that the game was meant to be more experienced for it's story, visuals, and music. Just a wonderfully beautiful game!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, Beautiful music, great story telling without any uneeded explanations, the jump and run, climb and sneak mechanics are done exactly right. It is not very challenging (neither the puzzles, nor the sneak passages) but that doesn't matter to me as much, since everything else is so perfect. Just don't expect a challange like Ori here.Performance is also great (stable 144 fps at 2160p), as it should be on a last generation high end PC, but these days that's sadly not guaranteed.I think it's  absolutely worth the money, especially with that discount at the moment.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Beautyful little adventure. I'm not 100% sure, what actually happened, though. You can disable QTE and i happily did. I lost some gameplay due to that i'm sure. Nice puzzles, not very hard. Great music. Stunning visuals. I actually have an early screenshot of this game as my desktop background for years(?) now. Runs well and out of the box on Linux.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game, beautifully animated, with a gripping storyline. A nice balance of stealth, platforming and puzzle-solving. I loved the relationship between Lana and the cat-like Mui, who must work together to save their companions from the robot invaders. If you enjoyed games like "Inside", "Planet Alpha", and the "Little Nightmares" series, then you're bound to love this. I should also mention the soundtrack, which is perfect and really adds to the game's atmosphere. To be honest, I can't fault this game – 10 out of 10 from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a beautiful game with a touching and heartwarming story! The animation, visuals, and the music is literally out of the world! Probably the best 2d platform game I've played in a long long time 10/10. The developer did a phenomenal job in programming everything, and the story was just touching! I loved everything about it! Totally worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing Planet of Lana, what I could say is that:- The artistic direction is simply stunning, reminiscent of the enchanting style seen in Studio Ghibli films. The visuals transport players to a mesmerizing world filled with beautiful places. - The exquisite soundtrack further enhances the immersive experience, effortlessly immersing us into the game's universe. - The puzzles strike a perfect balance of ingenuity and accessibility, catering to a wide range of players. - And, most importantly, the story is emotionally touching, particularly as it reaches its conclusion.Planet of Lana is one of my favorite games I played this year.Ah and to not forget, you can pet Mui (the cute creature compagnon, the cat-like animal you know ?)
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a very cool, exciting and enjoyable game in which we play as a girl Lana (although I'm not sure that it's a girl), whose parents, as I understand it, have died, and she considers Ilo, her sister, to be the only person close to her. But she, like the entire settlement, is kidnapped by robots. These robots are machines from the planet Earth (the game does not take place on Earth, but on a colonized planet). These robots must protect people from their disappearance from this planet and help them as much as possible, but it looks like a real kidnapping. Therefore, we, in the person of Lana, will be looking for Ilo throughout the game, solving moderately difficult puzzles and admiring the very cool art design in the background, which is not too difficult to draw, but looks very cool, thanks to which, at least for me, I did not get tired of playing. I just admired the background.  The game is not long, I finished it in 4 hours, but I walked away, leaving the game open, so it may take you less time to complete it. But in these 4 hours I admired the game to my heart's content. Many write that the game is stuffy because of walking, but I think this is not true, and this game is made very well and correctly. It is not made to strain your brain, but just to relax, admiring the wonderful views and simple gameplay. In general, I really liked the game, and I recommend it to everyone. Just if you are tired of playing online garbage and want to relax, this is the best. I advise you to play on a gamepad, and with headphones, because the music in this game is something with something..
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphics, a gripping story arc and a soundtrack to die for. Planet of Lana takes you on Lana's journey to be reunited with her sister Ilo and brings you through a range of biomes, where you face different threats along the way. Despite the many terrifying moments, you aren't truly alone and you'll only succeed with the help of a little friend and those you meet along the way. The pacing of the game is just nice, you never feel too bored and actions and puzzles keep you thinking and your mind working, as if you were right there with Lana. What is particularly impressive is how you'll Lana becomes a character you start to care about and empathise with as the story progresses and the developers only used a few nonsensical words( I think).  This is one of those shorter games where that is polished and you can tell that the developers put a lot of thought and love into. It's definitely worthy of your time!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: The whole game is basically a kid's comic book brought to life. The visuals are stunning, the music and audio are extremely well done, and the character designs for everything--people and creatures--are also great.Just like a kid's book though the story is very simple. Honestly the structure and similar gameplay reminds me a lot of Bramble (except MUCH more lighthearted). Really my only major complaint is that the Main Character's animations aren't very smooth, especially when transitioning to cutscenes where instead of naturally merging into it the game "blinks" (fades to black then quickly back in). Also the puzzles are all pretty simple. I feel like they could've done much more with the mechanics they have.Honestly though this is a great game just for the atmosphere of it. I'd recommend playing it next to an open window on a boring, sunny day for the best experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful journey and atmospheric puzzle adventure.Difficulty ★★★☆☆☆☆☆☆☆ (easy logical puzzle with rare QtE)The game is a potpourri of Another World, Oddworld, Far Lone Sails and Unravel. Also Luna and Mui are inspired by companion puzzle mechanics like in Robinson - The Journey (Robinson and the Baby-T-Rex Laika) or Never Alone (Nuna and the arctic fox). So in fact there is nothing totally new about it. But is that bad? No, in fact the whole narration and charm plays out pretty well in its own unique way.* beautiful graphics and artwork* fitting soundtrack* quick time events can be disabled in the accessibility options* cute characters* nice story and atmosphere* not too difficulty riddles and puzzlesActually. This is one of the rare games I don't really found anything that was made bad or was buggy. Of course, there is room for improvements, but all of them seem to be more of a personal taste thing and not bad game design or anything like that.The game is rather short (5 hours for the first playthrough) and does not give a lot of reasons for second run. But neithertheless the game was such a beautiful experience, that any cent spending on it was worth it. If you are into these type of game, it is a clear recommendation from me.Ah... and farewell little horsey, you will never be forgotten. You are my unsung true hero.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said in their reviews, Planet of Lana doesn't break the mould in terms of gameplay, half of the games is pushing your right joystick or key. Movement felt fairly sluggish and some inputs cacked up for me. Having said that, and if you know what your going in for when buying the game, those problems aren't write-offs.The visuals and artstyle, music and simple story are wonderfully executed. It took me 6 hours to finish the game and for the €16 launch price I paid, I'm very satisfied. I would say that the full price is a bit steep, so keep it on your wishlist and wait for a sale if that's a putt-off for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Holy...cow what an absolutely beautiful game! Such a gorgeous art style, incredible music and epic sound design! Oh boy the emotions hit hard as well. This game has so many jaw dropping moments. It's a platforming puzzle game with a beautiful emotional and mysterious story. Such a wonderful experience all around. I don't know how to really express how this game made me feel but there is such an emotional weight to it that you just have to experience for yourself. There are so many beautiful gems in video games and this is for sure one of them. Highly highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Limbo or Inside then you will love this TRUE MASTERPIECE.Played it through in one run. Catching, atmospheric, beautiful piece of love.It is more about enjoying the artwork and go deep into the story, which is not narrated to the player, but you can picture it from the scene and progress in the game. I barely write reviews, this one deserved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This is undeniably a very beautiful game, however it is incredibly simplistic and very repetitive.The story is nice and some of the mechanics are cool but there is far too much running through (stunning) scenery with nothing to do.It's a chill little platformer with some nice content but I wouldn't recommend it
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: The visual and audio experience was overwhelmingly beautiful.  The puzzles weren't too complex, it felt more focused on providing you with the visual and audio aspects of the game, which I found to be fitting for the game play.  There were some puzzles I got a little stuck on, but in reality they weren't too complex and were still really enjoyable!!  I loved that you had to have your eyes peeled for the some of the clues along the way.  The bond you create with your little fluff were wonderful in a lonely world to find your sister.  As I don't want to give any spoilers, I will say this is one of the only games to give me such an emotionally driven experience that made me shed some tears! Highly recommend if you enjoyed games like Gris, Ori, Somerville.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing, epic adventure with some great characters and an interesting story.  An impressive sense of atmosphere and scale through beautiful scenery, voice acting, sound and music, and artistic camera work.  The environments vary from cozy to HUGE.  The puzzles are interesting and fun, and tricky enough that I looked online a couple of times for a hint.  You'll be using a number of skills that you learn along the way.  Some of the more thrilling levels are fast, tense and play out like an action-movie sequence, though most of it plays at a slower pace.The story sort of progresses in bursts, but steady enough that you're never left too long between cut-scenes.  I thought it was paced pretty well.This game played flawlessly for me... I didn't notice any bugs or glitches.  It took me just over 6 hours to finish, though I didn't get all of the achievements.  Feels like good value for the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice and refreshing game. Looks amazing, there are no unnecessary glows and other modern stupidity. I like gameplay, riddles etc. It's perfect for evening slowdown and relaxation. Of course, there are few things that I'd like to be a little different, but it's nothing to write about. I hope they're working on sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: They got the aesthetics right.They got the feel right.They got the story right.They got the music right.They got the controls right.They forgot the gameplay :(It feels like 5 mins of running then a 30 second challenge that's no challenge whatsoever (and I'm no puzzle solver).Imagine "Inside" (awesome game) for 4 year olds..So close to being great but didn't make it for me, sorry :(
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful visuals and a good story. There is no understandable dialogue through the game, with the mystery of the main threat revealed piece by piece through clues scattered through the levels. It is a fairly straight-forward 2D puzzle-platformer, but there are enough visual layers to give it a pseudo-3D feel. It is a fairly short game, with my first run finished in a little over 6 hours, but I still recommend it for those who like this style of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed the pace used to tell the story.There are several scenes where the music and the panoramic views are so well put together.I was able to understand the made up language and the characters emotions when they were using it.Pretty well put together "ridding into the sunset" type scenes.Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: It's basically if Spirited Away was made into a sci-fi adventure. Simple style used to beautiful, atmospheric effect. Short, sweet and doesn't leave much to mystery with the story it tells. Can be finished in 4 hours or less depending on how fast you get through the relatively simple puzzles. If visuals make you feel, the music makes it real. 8/10 since you can pet your little friend.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Came for the vibrant colors. Stayed for Mui.Both the platforming and the puzzles are very intuitive, you will know what to do once you see the bigger picture. There are some QTE-heavy segments toward the end but that should pose no problem if you've gotten that far.The story is simple and heartwarming.The art and music are simply breath taking. I can not praise those two departments enough.Thank you for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: An extraordinary puzzle-platformer game in 2D. This game surpasses LIMBO and INSIDE by a significant margin! The characters, ambiance, and level designs are expertly crafted and highly entertaining. The immersive atmosphere in each level of the game is truly captivating. The puzzles scattered throughout the game are both enjoyable and satisfying to solve. Without a doubt, if you have a fondness for 2D puzzle-platformer side-scrollers, investing in this game is an absolute must.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I am honestly in lost for words for this game, I came in with not much expectations and it blew a hole in my mind to find this gem and play it.The art, music, sound design all adds towards the beautifully crafted atmosphere of a alien place, a place that is not what we used to know. The many cinematic shots, overall consistency of puzzle design that guides the players to harder puzzles, polishing touches like animation, are the proof that is game is made by nothing short of love and passion.I highly recommend anyone with a free evening in their schedule to get this game, sit down and just enjoy this thoroughly.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a visual feast. Every scene is beautiful in its own way. Sound design is also excellent. The puzzle elements are so-so. You've got some pretty good puzzles and a whole lot of filler ones. The ending of the game gets away from the core mechanics in a way that's fine but overall less fun than the good puzzles. Game took about four hours to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: More like Planet of NadaThat's how I would describe it...empty.If someone asked, what would you find very creative and special in this game, I would just say the art, and only in the open and green areas. Because you will spend half the game in the dark caves, which would still be okay, if it was relying on any other values OTHER than art. The game lacks diversity in environment, to at least appreciate the art style. The music was done very well though, to help you grip the atmosphere.Anyhow, as others have already stated, the game also lacks in gameplay elements, with simplistic story, nothing too special in those departments either. So unfortunate.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Unbelievably amazing art, music, style, and story telling! Easy to run this game on a potato machine. The story evokes emotion and makes you think in a way that is original and will make you remember it. Is it perfect... no... but nothing really is. My main gripe is that I feel the there should be some kind of hint system outside of just reminders on how to do certain actions. Something toggle able. But everything else is so good I am willing to give this my extremely rare 10/10 rating.A message to the developer...
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Saw this game on Youtube and loved the art-style.It's definitely worth the price if that's what you care about and I got a good few hours of fun out of the game because of it.Having said that, it's probably the only major selling-point of the game. You can easily finish the game in one sitting.Lana only has a few voicelines and if you actually finish the game in one sitting those few lines will get on your nerves. Especially because they're very predictable.The puzzles are easy to solve. For a puzzle game that's an issue. In this case they're interesting but not challenging at all. Maybe they can add some DLC with more difficult puzzles but if you're looking for a challenge you will be disappointed. If you've got a 49" screen this game will display background shaders/images that do not fill the entire screen.There's a bunch of other games that have this issue (Apex Legends used to have this issue) and it's not game-breaking just a nuisance.TLDR;"Oooh! Pretty!""ELO?! ELO!?! ElO?? eLo?! MUI?! MUI!!!! MiU?! ELO!!! Elo?! eLO!?! Mui!!?""Hmm.. guess I have to move this block again.."
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I would have loved more puzzles and some more difficult ones. That being said, I'm more of a casual gamer so it's alright. The pace of the game is on the slower side which for a game like this I believe is appropriate to appreciate the visuals and the atmosphere. (It can get frustrating in the middle of a long puzzle though). It contains a lot (if not most) of my quality features that I'm always looking for: puzzles, atmospheric, amazing landscape, platformer, storydriven, and amazing music! I'm really curious as to the intent behind the music composed and featured in the game. Also I think Elo could have been utilized more as a character as Lana's motivation.Anyway, would replay for the achievements and understand the story a little more. I would also love to have a chance to revisit some of the cut scenes (without going through an entire level) because they are beautiful! iz solid game :D
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: The most beautiful platform puzzle game I ever played. The story is told without telling it. It enrolls while playing. You can't stop the story until it is done, you want to play further. In the end it sometime becomes a little more difficult, but never to difficult. And some puzzles puzzled me for a while, but I never needed to look something up. Took me about 8 hours, including some time to go back and find some missed secrets.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game enough. It was SO beautiful. The story, the art, the music. It was an EXPERIENCE. I cried at the end but was also so HAPPY! The puzzles were fun and the challenge level grew appropriately as it continued on, I really enjoyed the whole experience. Much love for such a wonderful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Music 10/10- Perfect, nothing much to sayLevel Design 7.5/10- Some levels were duplicated, I can tell that you are trying to make the playtime longer.- Reasonable level designed, to be honest I can also tell that you guys tried to think of different game plays with limited mechanics. - Some cut scenes are perfectly input(running in the desert with the BGM, perfect climax for army bots.)- Game is pretty short, which i only took 4.2hr to finish, but it's well designed I guess. Art asset 8.5/10- Very consistent, I like the color themes.  - Some of the art asset not so obvious to figure out their meanings. Game narrative 7/10-  I would say that this is the story of the transfer of earth-like creatures to another planet and the beginning of a new extension of civilization. The story begins with unexplained sabotage of the previous planet's technological products, causing them to awaken and adopt more aggressive behavior towards all living things. But seeing the creature imprisoned in the machine, I thought it might be possible that the underlying code of this similar technology had been disrupted, causing him to execute a similar code to reproduce the creature. In the end, all are saved by the protagonist's rescue and ultimately coexist with the machine.- not 100% sure the story. BUG- There's one part, when Mui was on a log and I asked Mui to follow me by holding Q, Mui fell into the water and no matter what I did, Mui just wouldn't come out.Suggestion- Giving more hints for the stories. _childDocuments_.review: Once again I wish Steam reviews allowed for more than just yay or nay.I'd give this game a grade of 6/10. It is by no means a bad game, but it paled in comparison to similar titles (specifically, "Limbo" and "Inside")Although much darker in tone, these games have a very similar, rudimentary "run, jump, push, pull, climb" gameplay. But what they lacked in deep mechanics, they made up for in atmosphere, intrigue and environmental storytelling. I can't count how many times those two games made me go "Holy s***!!!" or "WTF is going on here?"."Planet of Lana" doesn't have much intrigue beyond the motivation of it's robot invaders. The planet itself is very pretty (they nailed the Ghibli nature look) but there's a fine line between "serene" and "boring". And while it does have tricks of it's own (you have a cat-squirrel pet that you can send places and have it press buttons or push down ropes) it's not enough to keep it's simplistic puzzles from quickly becoming repetitive. A lot of people complain that the game is too short, but to me it actually felt LONGER than it was.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Such a beautiful little game! From the masterfully arranged, angelic music to the breathtaking and sometimes spooky scenery, this game is a pure work of art! I've never played a game that took it's time to show you how small and insignificant the player character is. It also takes it's time, in some moments, to show off some amazing artwork that truly makes you fall in love with this world. I'd 100% recommend this game to anyone looking for a movie, art show, and concert experience bundled together and sold as a 5 hour puzzle platformer! My whole heart goes out to Wishful studios, especially the art and music team, for making this wonderful gaming experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I don't play games that often, so not proficient at using a controller, but this game starts gently and gradually gets more and more challenging. It rare for me to be able to complete a game, but I managed it with this one.It's not just about shooting everything in sight, and gives your brain a good work out. There's a human interest angle, and a cute "cat" helper.Took me about 65 hours of play time to complete the main game, (with a little help from a walkthrough), but there is an added element of finding 10 shrines, which I'm tempted to go back and look for.  Each "chapter" once completed can be played in isolation. May not be of interest to seasoned gamers, but then again could be quite relaxing. I certainly felt it was worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: A cinematic 2D platformer with noticeable game mechanic influences from Prince of Persia, Out of this World, and Limbo. Character design reminiscent of Star Wars.Very good puzzle platformer with your pet hybrid alien / cyber cat sidekick.Right amount of story, characterization, and pacing.Spectacular environmental and set design and very polished animation and controls.Highly recommend if you like any of the games mentioned above.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore Inside, so if you're like me and you've been waiting for Playdead to release their next game, Planet of Lana scratches some part of that itch. The puzzles can be challenging at times, but are mostly accessible for everyone (I spent an average of around 5 minutes on every puzzle). The art style in this game is what most people are attracted to, and I couldn't agree more: it's minimalism makes for some really pretty wallpapers, and there are moments where the developers want you to take that screenshot.It's a linear story that doesn't exactly invite discussion or late-night thinking, as was the case for me after Inside, but it's an original heartwarming tale that's well worth the experience. Rating: 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: If you like games like Little Nightmares, Inside, Bramble, A Jugglers Tale, or Brothers - A Tale Of Two Sons, than this game is for you and you will possibly have fun with it.The outstanding soundtrack deserves special mention.The puzzles themselves and the controls are among the bad parts of the game. I was never at a point where I was excited about what puzzles will come next, like I was i. E.  in Inside or Little Nightmares,The puzzles are an unfun compulsory task at best, downright annoying at worst. This is due to the design, but above all to the controls. It's really worth emphasizing here that it's a pain in the ass to move Lana. It feels really. really bad.Lana moves very slowly, there is an input lag, especially when jumping, or when stopping and ducking. You cannot steer or correct in the air. For everything, Lana takes a long, endless break. Be it to recover from the landing, to pull herself up, and and and.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game since the first trailer came out. I was not disappointed! Though the game doesn't take too long to complete, it's absolutely packed with stunning scenery, gorgeous music, and heart. The palettes used for each separate area are cohesive and fun to look at. I really enjoyed the use of a conlang (constructed language) for what little dialogue is spoken in the game. The environments and puzzles reveal tantalizing glimpses of the underlying history of the planet. The diegetic use of the game's main musical theme was such a treat! As platformers go, this one is gentle on the player, a great choice for a first platformer (I would say). I finished the whole game and found I had only unlocked 2/10 of the secret areas...and I'd thought I was being thorough! I loved the overall feeling of hopefulness in the game's story. Finally, Mui is one of the most adorable creatures to exist in a videogame (or anywhere)!! Their shape is so cute and their sounds make me smile every time I hear them. How I would love a plush version of the little guy!!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Exploring the world of Planet of Lana feels like stepping into a beautifully illustrated storybook and accompanying the stunning visuals is an immersive soundtrack that adds another layer of depth to the game.The gameplay of Planet of Lana strikes a fine balance between exploration and puzzle-solving. As you guide Lana, the game's protagonist, through various environments, you'll encounter intriguing puzzles that require clever thinking to overcome. These puzzles are well-designed, providing just the right level of challenge to keep you engaged without becoming frustrating.Planet of Lana is an absolute must-play for indie game lovers!

The controls/animations are a little sluggish - but this won't make any of the platforming frustrating (unless you are going for the deathless run...)I took my time with the game(and went afk for an hour or so), so expect a solid 4-5 hours of play. Once done you're done.I got good value out of this game and don't mind smaller experiences, but for some they may find the content available is lacking.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely side-scrolling puzzle adventure game with excellent game design.First of the game is beautiful, I found myself taking many screenshots. The musical score is fitting and pleasant. The level designs are top notch and the puzzles are excellent. I played this entirely on the Deck with no issues at all.The characters don’t speak and most communication is done with chirps and whistles with your adorable little “cat”. I was still heavily invested into the world and its inhabitants due to the fantastic story telling via cutscenes and background scenes.The game introduces new skills or mechanics as you progress and it requires you to implement these skills in later parts of the game. This is solid level and puzzle design from beginning to end.There is some stress as you and your buddy can die but I would still say it is low stress overall. I would still call this a low stakes puzzle platformer. My playtime is fairly accurate with little idle time.

_childDocuments_.review: It is quite lovely, but my friend was saddened by the intensity of the dark events happening in the opening.The atmosphere becomes more beautiful after that again.Controls work flawlessly and intuitively, the puzzles are on the easy side, but are fun to solve anyway.The cat is extremely cute and well behaved companion.Looking forward to finishing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, just, wow. Planet of Lana is so much more than it appears, and that includes after it's been finished. The story that is, at times, literally only told on the walls contains so much potential and intrigue that my brain can't help but construct a wider narrative for the universe of this game. The lack of direct information about certain wider themes allows the story to grow far beyond what we, the audience, are directly shown. It is as if we are given enough information to construct our own sci-fi universe if we want to, but if not, then we are just given a small cool story about saving the day. Make no mistake, nothing feels like it is missing or removed from the story. I was constantly blown away by just how much care the developers put into getting the little things right. This mentality of care is present in every aspect of this game, from the puzzle mechanics to the music, I honestly can't fault anything. But there is one thing that I feel this game truly excels at, and that is guiding the player's emotions through atmosphere alone. There is hardly any dialogue, and what exists isn't complex. The music, colors, graphics, environment, and even the voice acting behind the meaningless babble language of the characters carry so much weight. Planet of Lana is a sleeper among the greatest sci-fi stories of all time. Although it does seem to take a page or two from H.G. Well's War of the Worlds, this game truly crafts itself a narrative and world that is not like any other piece of media that I have experienced. I feel that a dramatic quote from another deceptively powerful game describes this one perfectly. In the words of Alan Wake, "It's not a lake, it's an ocean." This may be a short indie puzzle game, but it is one of my favorite worlds.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Planet of Lana, it has a very nice almost Ghibli like ambience to the graphics. While short at about 4 hours, it never really felt like it overstayed its welcome like some other shorter story-driven games can do, however some running sections definitely could have been shorter. The music is great too and I'm listening to it as I'm typing this review.The game definitely fits into the "Art and Story Experience" category, it features light platforming and puzzling, towards the end of the game it turns slightly more active and you need to learn which way to run and to respond to QTE prompts (which you presumably can turn off judging by the option available).It's never really hard and the save-points are almost always close, so even if you are dead in just one mistake, you will get back to it so soon the mistake will be forgotten almost immediately.A few negative points would be that jumping from ropes and ledgegrabbing can be inconsistent, sometimes Mui will watch you fall from an obvious ledgegrab like Scar throws Mufasa in the Lion King.No crashes or any major bugs was experienced, did experience two smaller bugs but nothing that stopped me for long.I can recommend it for those that want a visually pleasing and not too hard or punishing experience. However if you are after a tighter gameplay-filled game you should probably keep looking.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This game exceeded my expectations of what kind of puzzle game I was going to encounter.Not only are the puzzles intuitive; they build upon each other where you can tell the devs respect the player's gameplay experience.There wasn't any hand holding; I felt there was a healthy balance between puzzle solving and being told an amazing story.I really recommend others to try it out for story alone. It's not too short but worth the price for experience alone with a very satisfying ending.There are a lot of times where the devs give you a moment to just enjoy the soundtrack and scenery.Heck, there's an entire playable cutscene where the music just...hits. You'll know when you get to it later on.This is, I think, the main reason I truly loved the game; it understands the beauty of small moments with respect to the overall scope of the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: A captivating and beatuifully arranged video-story. The puzzles are mostly not too hard or complex (with a few notable exceptions), so mainly the player moves the character of Lana through the flow of the story rather than specific locations. And what a gem of a story is presented here. It is told by emotional expression and graphical concepts instead of words, as the language used in game is purely fictional. But the essence of the respective scenes is ever so clearly transported visually and acoustically even without recognizable conversation.In my opinion a masterpiece of presentation that more often than not caught up so much of my attention that I forgot about the gameplay itself while enjoying the landscape pass by or some little story unfolding in the background.And that is where others might find this game lacking - it took me only about 4h to finish (even with some repetitions) and - as I mentioned above - the puzzles are not too complex.It's a journey, not a challenge. For me, totally woth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful but slightly boring cinematic platformer. Movement always feels a tad too slow.Puzzles felt too easy most of the time. And the story only really gains traction towards the end. Overall this may sound too negative, but if you're looking for something relaxed for one evening see this as a recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I've genuinely enjoyed this little game. Its not long, but its impactful, the graphics are stellar with its Miyazaki-esque muted pastel hues and hand drawn aesthetic, and a rather heartwarming adventure between a frightened but brave young girl and her... pokemonesque little buddy. My only complaint really is the length could be a little longer (devs: Something to think about next time, use the money from this popular game for a sequel that has a run time that gives us a little more.) But I dont think its enough to strongly detract from the game as it does ensure the game never outlasts its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: THIS is what PlayDead should have made after Inside, not Somerville.This reminded me of the first time I'd played Limbo. Inside was good but too much of a direct sequel. I'm so glad to be able to play a game like this both brutal, heart warming, heart wrenching and beautiful. Music is also very orchestral and cinematic. Sometimes a game like this needs to exist for people who need it in the moment and I am grateful. Thank you devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I had a good time with this game. The artwork is nice, Lana and her little pal are super likeable, it doesn't have any annoying difficulty spikes, and it doesn't overstay its welcome. It could have been a little longer, but that's just because I liked it so much. Great game for a chilled Sunday afternoon or two.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Did you like Limbo? Love Inside? Want more of that 2.5D adventure and puzzle solving goodness? Then this is the game for you. The game play here is good and the puzzles are doable but not too hard. You even have a mouse-dog thing that follows you around and helps you solve puzzles.Great graphics and the music is incredible. I hope they release the OST for purchase. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I've completed the story of the game, at the time of writing this and it's been a fun 5 hours (almost). Not sure what to compare this game to but folks will mention games like Inside, Far Sails or even Little Nightmares perhaps in terms of puzzling and platforming but this game isn't as dark as Inside or Little Nightmares, although the mechanics feel familiar.Planet of Lana is beautifully directed with a very cinematic feel at times, gorgeous visuals and great music. None of the puzzles are complicated but there's a nice mix of them across the game.This game won't be for everyone but if you like to enjoy a fairly stress free, beautiful game then this might be it.Minor gripe: I played the game with a controller and there was one section later in the game where the prompts reverted to the keyboard input when they popped up on-screen which resulted in a death but other than that I had no other technical issues with the game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my gosh this is BEAUTIFUL! This feels like a movie you'd want to take your kids to see in the theater! It's like Playdead's INSIDE, but not dark. The art is phenomenal, the music is gorgeous and very fitting for the environment, the story is simple yet captivating. The gameplay is very fluid and I have to say that I never found any bugs. The puzzles are mildly challenging, but never so difficult that they ruin the pacing or bog down the game. Seriously, there is nothing wrong with this game! (However, there are moments where you travel in a straight direction for several minutes, with nothing going on but a scrolling background to look at. The main character, Lana, also walks kinda slowly at times, which makes the game feel more spaced out. I personally found these sections as a time for quiet reflection on the journey so far. I liked them, but if you're looking for a game with constant puzzles or traps, that's not what this is.) So then it really just comes down to taste. Do you like sidescrolling puzzle platformers? Maybe with some cinematic episodes thrown in? Good, you'll love this then!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: A very special game!!!!Every now and then, a game comes along that captures the gamer on so many levels - this game does that for me. In fact, I wouldn't even call this a game. This is art! Thank you to the wonderful developers and music composers for making this beautiful symphony. One of my favourite titles in a while!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! A very intriguing story that could be a movie koncept. Lovely visuals!Not very long, but an nicely developing plot. Played with my six year old who thought it was a little scary at one or two occations, but I think it was mostly excitement. It's not an easily scared kid though. We both enjoyed it very much! I'll replay it a few times to see if I can find more secrets.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game a few days after release and it only took me 4 hours to beat.  The gameplay itself is nothing more than solving some fairly simple puzzles... So this game isn't going to appeal to everyone.With that said, I highly recommend giving this game a shot.  Everything about the game is so incredibly well executed. The Visuals are stunning!(just look at the screenshots). I spent more time than id like to admit admiring the rocks and trees in the game.  The Visuals are so much more than just the artwork though, the level design is superb! The locations feel unique yet connected to the same planet. The story unfolding in the background is another design decision that works so well.  The whole game has a very cinematic feel to it and is worth the price of admission imoAudio: again stellar! From the tactile sounds of the different surfaces to the score and original songs... So damn good.  Little things like Lana whispering commands when an enemy is near or just the many ways she says something like stay.  Gameplay is the only thing that is a bit lacking.  I personally enjoyed the puzzles and platforming but I can definitely see people being upset if they are looking for a puzzle platforming game.  To me this game was a 4 hour movie with some respectable gameplay elements in it.  Planet of Lana is an, emotional, cinematic journey that is expertly crafted and a pleasure to experience
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This is a sci-fi adventure puzzler with gorgeous art, and a beautiful soundtrack. Some of the puzzles and enemies are a little repetitive and there are areas where it becomes a walking simulator, but this was still a win for me.  The cat(?) companion was adorable and used in interesting ways to solve puzzles. Just like in Stray, I felt terrible when I got my little friend killed. Also she cries when you die.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING game!  Worth every penny!  It took me roughly 5.7 hours to play through the whole game.  It is very similar in style to Inside and Limbo, but this one is less creepy and dark.  It is so colorful and beautiful, what else can I say, it is just ART!  I loved the story, the companion, and how the companion was needed and not just there to be cute.  The puzzles were pretty easy, only a few took me a minute or two longer or several attempts.  Towards the end they definitely got a little harder.  I loved how the music would change to something more urgent whenever danger was near so I knew to be on my toes.  The danger was certainly scary in it's own way, but not evil or creepy.  It was such a wonderful adventure I wish I could play it over and over again!  And yes, a lot was left unexplained, but the ending was satisfactory.  I would highly recommend this game to anyone who loves artsy side-scrollers, and some stealth, climbing and timing action.  Oh and although it says it works best with a controller, I found a mouse an keyboard worked just fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of platformer and puzzle games, I went into the game with really high expectations. It turns out, I was probably not the target audience and those expectations worked against me.I think I would have loved discovering this game as a teenager. The art direction is incredibly beautiful and rich. I often times would just try to stop walking left to right and just soak in the beauty of the world. The puzzles are (mostly) very easy and are accessible to younger players. This makes the game accessible to those who find games like Ori and the Blind Forrest too hard for instance.Three small things I felt reduced my enjoyment of the game:- The left to right movement was frustrating in the phases where it was all about soaking in the beauty of the place. I felt somewhat forced when all I wanted was explore more freely. - Some timings of challenges were really tight, making me believe a few times that the solution couldn't possibly be the correct one.- I missed the eight first secret locations only to find the ninth one as my first. I feel like the first secret area should have been more visible, to attract my attention to the fact that there are secret places to be found early on. But maybe I was just too focused on solving puzzles and missed an obvious first secret location.These three points do not make this game un-enjoyable. It's a fun and accessible adventure that can be enjoyed in a few hours. Beautiful !
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game. Absolutely amazing game! Wonderfully crafted, both aesthetically, musically and game design wise. I only wish there were more games like these. Challenging and thought provoking with the right fluidity. Also, it touches on life in general, how you want to live, friendship and even the interaction between AI and nature. My gf gave me this game as a birthday present since she wanted me to have a relaxing experience (I'm normally a competitive RTS player) and this was truly a great gift. Thank you for making this game and I'll be keeping an eye out for the next game you produce. The music was on point and fit the sense of the game perfectly by creating a contemplative and heartful vibe. Grade: 9/10. Need to save the last point for your next game ;).
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I have just completed the story of Planet Of Lana, and I'm struggling to think of a game that has affected me more in 25 years of casual gaming. The story, characters, graphic design, gameplay and music are all beautiful. If you've never bonded with a character from a computer game, that is about to change!POL plays beautifully, has some interesting puzzles that can all be figured out before they get tedious, and has a few boss fights that are challenging without being disheartening. It really hits the sweet spot for new or experienced players alike.The characters are wonderful, and care has been taken to bring them to life with voice effects and gestures that reveal themselves through the game. It's a platform puzzle game, and the character development never gets in the way of the gameplay, but you get a real *sense* of who Lana, Eila, and Mui are.The credits reveal what an international effort this game is, and would love to congratulate everyone who was involved in its creation for such an enjoyable experience.It's OK to have a little cry at the end, honest!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable little sci-fi adventure with fantastic art and music, puzzles that did not bog things down (primarily environmental manipulation, some timed action/QTE sequences), and a story told mostly environmentally.  Satisfying conclusion.  I wouldn't have minded a little more variety to the puzzles, but on the other hand I appreciated never getting frustratingly stuck and needing to seek answers external to the game.  Took me a little under six hours, but I was focused on moving forward and missed 8/10 collectible doodads, so I'll probably revisit things.  I'd advise against rushing -- enjoy the experience.Important: You can pet the adorable alien dog(?) critter.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: A charming puzzle platformer with beautiful graphics and music very much in the same style as Limbo, Inside and Little Orpheus. _childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable as a visual storytelling shorter tale with a great score, art direction, and focus.Cinematic, full of good moments and a cohesive world concept. The platform puzzling is very INSIDE and LIMBO-adjacent, with some interest added in through controlling Mui, the very good cat creature by your side, and gradually gaining more control over the tech/organisms across the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gorgeous game with wonderful storytelling. The game was engaging from start to finish, and somehow managed to make all the puzzles seem relevant to the journey. The puzzles were enough to make us think and keep us engaged, but never punishing and never monotonous. The sound, camera movements, and cinematic sequences really contributed to the overall story. _childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 Beautiful but pretty simple puzzle action.When her home planet is invaded by Amazon's Alexa,  Laaaanaaaah must outwit an army of exceptionally unintelligent AI drones and find a way to turn her pet monkey into a Tesla tower. The graphics and music are great but the puzzles are fairly lacking both in originality and variation. The difficulty doesn't scale much either: if you can clear the first 15 minutes of the game, you will have no problem reaching the ending.  The story, though lacking originality, is good enough for a few well-engaged hours of gaming.Get it on discount and you probably won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This game has amazing artwork, a dreamlike atmosphere, and two main characters that leave you with a wholesome feeling while playing. _childDocuments_.review: The game is very cute and very short. I didn't feel like I had to exert too much effort, and it provided me with a few hours of well-made visual escapism, with stunning visuals and a stunning sound track. Without challenging or lengthy obstacles, it took me only a few seconds to understand the majority of it, and the most challenging parts took less than five minutes of thought and trial and error.The main character is charming, feeling very 'alive' in the world. She reacts in a very realistic way, which adds extra immersion to the game for me.The interface isn't difficult, but it takes some getting used to. Most of the work is done with the keyboard with a little help from the mouse.The enemies are endearing, and it's very easy to figure out how to overcome them. However, they provide a dark undertone to a game that is otherwise colorful and joyful.Overall, it's worth buying on sale. There's no reason to pay full price.Thanks to the creators of the game for a pleasant and straightforward experience. _childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a 2D side-scrolling puzzle platform adventure game, similar to classics like Oddworld: Abe's Oddysee with cooperative puzzle-solving mechanics involving more than one character like in games like Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons.You play as Lana, a young girl whose village is attacked by an army of robots and whose people are abducted, including her friend (or sister?) Elo. Lana takes off in pursuit, and soon encounters and rescues a small, black cat-like creature with glowing eyes, who she names Mui. Mui accompanies her on her quest afterwards. Through the course of the adventure you use Lana and Mui's unique skills to solve puzzles, traverse the terrain, and avoid and escape enemies as you seek to rescue her people.Lana can run, jump, climb ropes, crawl through tunnels, hide in tall grass, move boxes and carts, and later, control machinery through control panels. Mui can be directed by Lana to jump and climb to high places, crawl through small spaces, push down ropes to Lana, push certain buttons  and trigger switches, and later, hypnotize beasts. Neither has any combat skills, and so you must occasionally use stealth tactics to sneak past wild beasts and robot patrols, sometimes using each other as bait to distract the enemy so the other can get by.The puzzles are fairly straight-forward and easy to figure out. None of the stealth puzzles require particularly fast reflexes to complete, and it shouldn't be very difficult for anyone to complete the game. That being said, you will almost certainly die at some point. Which makes one of the achievements in the game that requires a deathless playthrough particularly challenging. The art direction is stunning and the music is very nice too. But the game is pretty short, with my playthrough clocking in at 5 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most beautiful and overall best games I have ever played.First of all, the plot is absolutely amazing. Even though barely any language was used throughout the game, you feel extremely invested. It had me glued to the screen, as I wanted to know what would Lana do next and would she find her people. It is hard to tell what's going to happen next.Secondly, the puzzles are very well thought out. Many of them are easy, others require lots of thought and attention to detail. You never know at what cost a mistake might end up being. And oh my goodness the visuals. At first I was worried that the game was going to be beautiful just in the beginnnig, but every single frame of the game is an absolute masterpiece. This game is quite literally a work of art, considering how much effort and love the creators (especially the artists) have put into it. Sometimes I would just stop doing anything and just look at the background of any given scene. I am fascinated by how cozy and relaxing this game feels, given that the story is quite tragic, and the puzzles felt challenging at times. And yet, here it is. One of the best experiences of my life is playing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not long and not challenging for experienced gamers, it's just very nice to play through. I was hoping to sit out that time without disturbances, but this game has some stupid limitations, which are very common in games these daysThe game stutters due to v-sync buffering. This is not necessary with a proper framerate limiter, which the game doesn't have. Well, there is a 60 fps limiter, but I can't stand the sample and hold motion blur on 60 hz even in a slow side scroller like this. I use a backlight strobing lcd to eliminate motion blur, but I need at least 75 hz, or a rediculously low screen brightness in order not to see flickering. And no, the rivatuner framerate limiter does not help. The time consuming cpu buffering can only be disabled with an in game framerate limiterThe other problem is the anti aliasing. It looks blurry and there isn't an option to disable it. Apparently, 10% of gpu usage still isn't low enough to implement supersampling. And no, I can't force supersampling through the nvidia control panel and set a high vertical total at the same time, which is required to avoid crosstalk when using backlight strobing. In other words: supersampling just needs to be implemented in the game itselfI could have decided to not bother, but it's time for the gaming industry to solve these problems once and for allPlease fix this and I will come back

_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I first saw the game a year ago: it immediately appealed to me with its style and music. Now, after playing the game, I can say 100% - this game is a masterpiece, at least for me. Although the plot is a bit banal and there are some things I would like to criticise the game for, I won't, I just don't want to, because I can see how much effort the authors put into their brainchild. The game charmed me from the first minutes of the game - the drawing and design of the locations, my admiration, and I would also like to mention the music, so much that I fell in love with it. Another thing that is hard to take away from the game is the cinematography: I am particularly grateful for the spectacular and dynamic scenes. Although the game is not without its flaws, it has something that some games will never be able to replicate: it has a soul. Special thanks to everyone involved in the game, my infinite respect. I could have played a lot of other games, but I didn't regret playing Planet of Lana.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a beautiful and simplistic puzzle-adventure game with a charming story and immersive atmosphere. The puzzles are not particularly challenging, but they are well-designed and integrated into the narrative. The game's visuals are absolutely stunning, with a watercolour art style that is both unique and eye-catching. The soundtrack is also excellent, perfectly complementing the game's atmosphere and mood.One of the things that I appreciated most about Planet of Lana is the way it blends puzzles and action-filled scenes. This keeps the gameplay fresh and engaging, and prevents the game from becoming too repetitive. The story is also well-told, and I found myself becoming increasingly invested in the characters (Lana and Mui) and their journey.Overall, Planet of Lana is such a cool game that is sure to appeal to fans of INSIDE, GRIS and other puzzle-adventure games. It is a beautiful, immersive, and heartwarming experience that I highly recommend : ) .

_childDocuments_.review: It might not do any one thing spectacularly (other than looking and sounding tremendous), but every element that makes up this game is so thoughtfully considered and add up to be a great experience.  I do want to highlight some excellent level design though - the puzzles aren't too difficult but they are, how can I explain it, Nintendo-like.  They manage to give you some challenge but be fun and not vague in the slightest.The game does also have a decent degree of replayability too, for those people who might find the 4-5 hour playtime too short.  But even without that, you'll play it again much like you'll watch a great film again.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Not one to normally write reviews on games, but this game is just hard not to. Sure, other reviews may bring up that some of the puzzles are repetitive, or that the QTE's were out of place, but the real pull for me was the art style and the story. none of the puzzles were challenging, allowing for a more open audience. On the QTE's they are only used in 2 high intensity parts near the end, and for me draw me more into the game since it feels like the stakes are higher in those moments (though there is a setting to turn them off if you really dont want them). I definitely recommend this game for anyone who wants a calmer storytelling experience more than an action filled one.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so let’s put this on the table from the outset; the game is short and quite simple. But hey! Some of my most favourite people are short and simple. Well, maybe not my most favourite but i still really like them. This game is kinda like that situation. It’s a really pleasant, enjoyable experience. It’s not challenging but it is light and it flows. It’s also quite a pretty game and there’s no glaring glitches, which is quite nice seeing as many AAA games do. Oh by the way, I played it on the Steam Deck which I think contributes to the experience. So in conclusion;ShortSimplePrettyAnd I paid 10€ which I was happy to pay.

_childDocuments_.review: I love games that don't have any dialogue to tell the story. The characters occasionally speak a few words in their language, but the game never outright tells you what they are saying, and lets you pick up on it through context clues. The story doesn't need more than that, the breathtaking visuals tell more than any words.Overall, a perfect game when you can't commit to playing the same game for weeks, and just want a beautiful experience for one evening.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a stunning cinematic platformer that tells a touching story of friendship and survival.You play as Lana, a young girl who teams up with a cat-like creature named Mui to rescue her sister from an invading army of machines. Along the way, you will explore a beautiful hand-painted world, solve clever puzzles, and bond with your adorable companion. Planet of Lana is a game that will captivate you with its gorgeous visuals, emotional music, and charming characters. It is a must-play for fans of narrative-driven adventures. My score? 8/10 😁
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing I must say is that the art style for this game is lovely, very nice everything. I think the music works, But without a doubt the most memorable music is when you go through the desert and the credits, it's just beautiful. Controlling lana is not as fluid as other games of the style but it's not bad either, as for its difficulty the game has nothing challenging, it is made mostly to be simple and if that is its focus I think it is unfair to criticize it for that. The achievements are easy, most of them have to do with winning the game and finding the shrines. I would say the hardest and by far (honestly I think it's the only challenge in the game) is to win the whole adventure without dying, very difficult.Story is simple and I never understood what the robotic creatures were or where they came from but other than that I don't think it needs a sequel, I think it had a very rounded ending but i won't bother me if they make one. I also think the world of lana from its creatures to its biomes has a lot to give.Very enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is an artistic masterpiece! As well as an emotional roller-coaster! A lot of the triple A companies should play this game and understand the power of core concepts of art! This includes scale, perspective, contrast, color, and so on! The impeccable usage of camera zoom ins/outs to maintain the player constantly immersive and show what needs to be done is impeccable!I disagree with a lot of the comment saying that it is to repetitive in fact! I believe I haven't played a platform with so much diversity in a long time or ever!Only issue I found which is very small is the lack of PS5 HUD controller support (but hardly any PC games have unfortunately) and at times it felt a bit clunky.I am so glad to have supported this indie game!My score will be of 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Keyboard & mouse input is just too awful in Planet of Lana for me to recommend it. It feels somewhat sluggish, but that may be intended, and possibly identical with a controller (I do not own one to compare), so I can give that a pass. However, the inability to rebind keys is a massive issue for someone who does not use the widespread but objectively inferior WASD layout. There are only 7 input keys in Planet of Lana, so it is not that I need the pinkie/ring finger space like I do in typical FPS or MMO games, it is just a fact that muscle memory makes me move left when I intend to crouch. And trust me, you do not want to miss your crouches in Planet of Lana.This aside, the game does have strong positives (beautiful scenery, empathic characters, relaxing tempo), but feels a bit simple both in its puzzles and its storyline. Would recommend for the more casual player who owns a controller.
