_childDocuments_.review: The controls are incredibly sluggish and clunky on kb/m and I couldn't find any rebind settings so that I didn't need to slightly-too-occasionally reach for my mouse. Art is beautiful but controls are slow and sometimes need you to be too precise. Also no second chance when you get spotted by an enemy and the respawn time takes a hint too long.Overall a bit boring, slow, and feels tedious to actually play.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful mix of elements you may know from other games, like Far, INSIDE and Little Nightmares, but all done in a unique way. The world is not as depressing as in other games and feels very alive, especially thanks to the plenty interactions you have with the environment and various beasts you come across on your journey.The puzzles and platforming reminded me a lot of the classic Oddworld games, but far less visceral. In fact, the game aims to find non violent solutions for most of the problems it confronts you with. There have been some unexpected difficulty spikes in the later parts of the game, which could be overcome after a couple of retries. The musical score ranges from simplistic to epically stunning, but always fits and in at least two moments completely emotionally captivated me. All I say here is: That Sunrise. The story in general is very endearing, being a classical hero's journey. It feels a lot like a modernized 80s or 90s childrens adventure story and in my opinion fits any player around the age of 10 or above (Consider that themes like obduction and enslavement are being depicted).The art style is simplistic, but not dull in the slightest. Stunning vistas and wide panning shots show the amount of work and the attention to detail that went into the hand drawn environments, the character animations and the storytelling.The overall production quality is at a solid AA level and the presentation is mostly flawless and very cinematic.Rarely has a game taken me on such an emitional rollercoaster while also being this lighthearted and joyful.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Overall score: 3.5/5It's a good game, but there's a lot of things I don't like about the game, and one of the main themes of these problems is lack or break up of immersion, but I'll include both positive and negative aspects of the things I list.Music - 98% of the time the music is absolutely beautiful. It's incredibly fitting and on-theme with the various locations in the game. I especially love the songs that have a soothing voice with a calm, angelic music.There are, unfortunately, some moments where the music isn't really fitting though. In one moment, a song played that had the singer sing in English. This is immersion breaking because literally no other character in the game speaks English; just their own language, so a song that is only in English is not fitting. The other moment was when the music that plays when an enemy robot is triggered plays suddenly when being chased by an army of them after finding Elo a white room. Other than those two moments, the music is absolutely beautiful.Graphics - The graphics are both very cute and very terrifying. Very cute, because... Just look at it! Mui, Lana, Rauken, Elo, and the environment are cute and beautiful! I especially love Lana's and Mui's design. They're super cute! The environment is also incredibly beautiful. Not only that, the details are also noticeable since they are large enough to notice, so you can notice the beauty while playing!I also said that the graphics is terrifying, because holy mother of God it's terrifying. The animals in the game are extremely terrifying. The rock-hiders, hogs, and spiders are very terrifying, but the scariest one of them all is undoubtedly the big mother spider, because it's gigantic! It's also very fast when it eats Lana, so it's extra terrifying.The spider-robots are also pretty scary, but what I like most about them is that they're basicallyControls - 99% of the time, the controls are extremely good; even on PC. The problem comes with button mashing, because nobody, and I mean nobody likes button mashing. Having to constantly press my fingers on a button is not good gameplay, dude.Animations - 99% of the time, the animations are very good, very expressive, and very good. The only complaint I have regarding animations is the death "Animation." I put air quotes there because there's actually no death animations, so Lana just drops like a Garry's Mod ragdoll, and while it's very funny, it's also very immersion breaking; which is made worse considering that you die a lot, so I think that giving Lana a proper death animation for whenever she falls or gets electrified is really important.Puzzles - The puzzles are honestly not well placed, and one of them is not well made. This game has a lot of sudden difficulty spikes and "difficulty pits," as in parts of the game that are suddenly made easier. This is so bad that I legitimately find the middle and later levels in the game way easier compared to the beginning of the game, and that is really bad. A game is supposed to be harder the more you play; not the opposite. If the devs had switched some puzzles for more fitting levels of difficulty, or make new ones entirely, this game would've been a lot more bearable.I said that one of the puzzles is not well made. What's that puzzle? It's the first music puzzle in the cave, and it's unfortunate too. It had awesome graffiti leading up to it that was very cool, and rich with stories, but the puzzle is incredibly difficult, to the point where I had to watch a walk through of the game in order to complete it. This is the only puzzle out of the entire game where I was basically forced to watch a walk through. That is embarrassing.Story - There are actually two stories in the game, so I'll split this review between "Main story" and "Space story."Main Story - The main story is not really good. Again, lack and break up of immersion is the main theme with all the problems, and this section is filled with that.When Elo got taken away at the beginning of the game, I didn't feel as sad as Lana did in the game. I was still sad, but it wasn't heartbreaking, which is unfortunate considering that Lana lost her sister. I think that if Lana and Elo were together until the middle of the game, it would've definitely been incredibly heartbreaking.The separation of Mui and Lana is not really believable, because Lana just kept running away from Mui. She obviously wanted to be with Mui, but she ran in the opposite direction of Mui. Had the cave been collapsing, this would've been a lot more believable. Bonus points if she cried afterwards.Lana's sleep at the beginning after she witnessed Elo get kidnapped by a robot is unfortunately not really sad. If I was Lana at that situation, I would've cried a lot, because losing your friend and knowing that they might be dead is heartbreaking, but sleep would not have been an option. I would've been too sad to sleep.One last thing. Lana's inconsistent cries for Elo up until the moment where she was transported to the giant robot eye thing is immersion breaking. I think that had Lana cried a little more, it would've been a lot more believable. The cries at the giant robot eye thing was definitely 100% believable.Space story - The space story is absolutely amazing, because there's a lot to think about, with many hows, whys, and whats. You'll be asking questions like, "Why is this here?" "How long has it been here?" "Was it from here? From another world?" "Are these people us?" It's a very interesting story that I absolutely love. It's one of the best stories I have ever seen!So yeah, that's my entire review. 3.5/5. Nice job.

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous art style and my first impressions of the OST were really great too. Mui is adorable.Unfortunately, the story did not grip me and the gameplay was too slow for me. Perhaps it was due to the made up language that did not get subtitled, but I would've loved to see more of the characters and what they were talking about. _childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: A narrative masterpiece, that does so much in so little time.Planet of Lana feels less like a game and more like an... interactive story. There are puzzles to solve and hazards to avoid, for sure, but the core of this experience is the story and amazing visual atmosphere. Every chapter has moments where you can simply sit and rest, and be bathed in incredible ambiance as you take in the carefully crafted scenery. The main reason to progress is to simply see the story unfold, which is done superbly. Lana and the other inhabitants of this strange world seldom speak, and when they do, they vocalize in a unique language (that perhaps can be deciphered if you listen closely). Lana's character is established in a wonderfully quick prelude of sorts, and Mui - her strange little animal companion - feels like gaining the trust and love of a beloved pet as their bond deepens over the course of their journey.And of course, the world itself is fantastic, and ripe with environmental storytelling. To progress is to learn of the incredible history of this world and it's inhabitants, and the threat that now looms over it. It feels like reading an immersive book - you simply want to progress, to turn the page, to see what big reveals await, what challenges Lana and Mui will face. The puzzles aren't too hard, and the story itself is only a few hours long - but what an incredible few hours they are. I can honestly recommend this to anyone who wants a nice, heartfelt sci-fi story, wants wonderfully rich environments to adventure through, and doesn't mind an experience that... really doesn't feel like a "game" in any capacity, in the best way I can possibly describe it.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty boring. You mostly hold the joystick to the side and wait while running to the next little puzzle which isn't really interesting, but takes time to do because you move so slowly and it takes so long to do things like drag a crate or climb up a ledge. I have a feeling they increased the time it takes to finish by adding more tunnels you have to crouch and very slowly move through.You'd probably enjoy this game more by watching a lets play VOD where you can skip to the cut scenes where the story is told. The art is very pretty, and I love the atmosphere. I just wish the game play was mentally stimulating in any way. I didn't make it past the first hour, so maybe it gets better later.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a side scroller adventure game with puzzle and platform mechanics that never develop enough depth to be challanging, yet are sufficiently engaging and varied. _childDocuments_.review: Beautiful story telling! I was very surprised how much I enjoyed it - easily my favorite for 2023. The music score is terrific and seamlessly meshes with the game. _childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: In general this game has a nice and beautiful   backgrounds, with very detailed and alive environment. The soundtrack plays at the right time, making the experience more  immersive. On the other hand, the mechanics are pretty simple, you can just walk, run and move some items. One interesting element is the ability to work together with the little cute puppet, you have to be precise about the decisions you make in order to solve  the puzzle in front of you, because it's not about how can solve it, but  rather about how well you can work together with your puppet  to overcome the puzzle as a team.At the beginning, these  elements make for an enjoyable  experience, but over time It gets boring and stressful. On one side, you're  always doing the same thing , the puzzles are very similar and you don't  feel satisfied  when you solve them, it feels tedious; in order to solve the puzzle you have to go through a lot of steps, just to  solve a small part of it. On the other hand, the puppet becomes an extra weight that you have to carry thought out your journey. I don't know if that was the idea of the developers, but i didn't like it . The main problem is always about the puppet, so there is no any satisfaction in that kind of puzzle-solving.I wouldn't recommend it  as a game programmer who loves to experience game mechanics that give  you some satisfaction when you interact with them or maybe when you overcame a puzzle. The core elements of the game were beautiful, it's more about how the lead designer mixed this elements in a bad way. I feel that they could have  been  combined in a  better way.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I felt this game to the core, the atmosphere, the music and the story. I let myself be lost at parts in the game, I had tears of joy at the end. A beautiful story, set in a fantatsic world, backed by a soundtrack that pulled at your heart strings.I am so glad to have experienced this game. It is now one of my favs and will live rent free in my head and my heart.Buy it and let the game take you away.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing journey! This game is just mesmerizing. The graphics, the music, the story... Wonderful platformer game. I totally fell in love with Mui (you can pet her!). The story is a well known scheme of finding kidnapped sister, but the journey to achieve this goal is full of beautiful landscapes, some action, enemies to avoid and puzzles to solve. I recommend this game for the people that prefer games with slow-paced story telling, because this one is not made for speed-run. Enjoy the scenery, listen to music and find your way to your sister and maybe back home. (10/10)
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This game gave me, for the first time in a very long while, the same sensation of exoticism mixed with excitement that I perceived the first time I watched Star Wars (from which I would say it is heavily inspired), Mad Max 2 and 3, or the first time I read a comic by Moebius.Just like in The Full Void, the animation is clean and detailed, but not rotoscoped, but the graphics here are minimal cell shadings that play well with the bucolic setting, but less so with the machines and the swamp.Where it really shines is the sound department, not only for a John William-esque soundtrack, but especially for having created a simple fiat language, that like many brands from Scandinavia (this game is Swedish) is full of Italian sounds and had it pronounced by Italian voice actors. The effect is a grounding set of spoken words that participate magnificently in the world-building.As a puzzle platformer, the puzzles are mostly easy but satisfying, none of them based on extreme quick-actions except for one scene inspired by Lawrence of Arabia that is so epic though that you will forgive the repeated deaths.The whole game can be finished in less than 5 hours, has no violence, blood or gore and it is primarily targeted at kids, who would thoroughly enjoy an aided playthrough, I suspect.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I felt like this often stumbled short of the potential it could have had; the pacing is severely uneven, the speed of the animations make puzzles grind any sense of momentum to a halt, a couple of the puzzles are way harder out of nowhere, a few of the story bits feel a bit too out of left field and not cohesive with the rest...I think it's fair to say the game leans first and foremost on its strong Ghibliesque art direction, its live orchestra soundtrack, and a lot of concepts that seem striking and evocative at first... and it does draw you in! But it tends to result too much in a sort of "hold right until you see the next puzzle" syndrome sometimes. A few moments are super duper cool, but they are few and far between.With all that being said, this remains a very sweet kind of "cinematic platformer"... if you liked "INSIDE", "LIMBO", and games like that, I think there's a strong chance you'll like "Planet of Lana".I would love to see this team do something along these lines again, while addressing the weak points of this game. I think they'd knock it out of the park.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simple yet utterly beautiful. While many complain that the game's puzzles are easy, I would say that the game has a gradual progression curve. For those who play games daily, sure they're easy. However, I think this game's strength lies in being able to amaze more casual audiences while still giving them a good sense of satisfaction with the game's mechanics. The art, however, is nothing short of incredible. The fantastic use of color, perspective, and artistic talent all come together to create a collage of memorable and striking moments that should capture anyone's attention. Look at the store page screenshots and tell me you don't want to play this game. The playtime is roughly 4-5 hours which some players cite as another downside of the game, but this more constructed and concise experience isn't forcing itself to do things it simply can't. Lana is constantly moving forwards, metaphorically and literally, while keeping the filler out.My only real complaints were a couple puzzle moments that weren't as effectively communicated as the rest and the ending being a little more abrupt than I would've liked. Otherwise there's not a whole lot I can dock the game for. So far one of my GOTY contenders, 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Without any Dialog you understand everything, you bond with the cutest animal on earth, the soundtrack is like heaven for my ears, as well as the art style is for my eyes.I recommend this for everyone, who likes games like inside and little nightmares, even though i don´t compare it with these. Planet of Lana has its own story and experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say that It is not a bad game. I do not recommend it as it is pretty repetitive.It emulates the PlayDead games in an edulcorated way, but lacks the dark feeling of Limbo and Inside.The puzzles are ok, but at the end you fell a little bit tired of them as they are all very similar and with the same kind of enemies.Not my favorite, I can not recommend, but it is a good game for children.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I would compare this game heavily to "Inside".  There are areas where it is on par with that game and areas where it leaves a little to be desired.   First of all, the music, sound design and artistic style are what stand out the most in Planet of Lana.  There are parts in the game that are stunning to look at and, paired with the music, make for a memorable experience.  The story is interesting enough to keep you engaged, and having a little sidekick following along beside you adds to the experience.  Where Planet of Lana falls a little short, however, is in its puzzle design.  I would say that outside of a couple of puzzles throughout the game I didn't find any of them particularly challenging.  Overall, I still really enjoyed this game and would recommend it even at full price.  If you played the game, "Inside", I'm sure you will enjoy Planet of Lana.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Played with my daughters (I play, they watch), and we enjoyed it. Very short (Steam says 4 hours played), but beautiful little gem. The game play reminded me a bit of the old Another World, but less cinematic and more puzzle-like. The art style is simply BRILLIANT - I love the graphics, the work with camera and perspective, the music, the occasional animations - a perfect game to watch/enjoy/be immersed into.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful Game with a fantastic Artstyle, wonderful Music and an interesting Story.And Mui is absolutely adorable <3If you liked Cinematic Platformers like Limbo or INSIDE, or maybe even Little Nightmares, then you should get this Game.Performance was great with no frame drops in 1440p@144hz & you can play it with unlocked Framerate! The pricing is also fair for this type of game, took me 5hours on my first Playthrough.Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: "Planet of Lana" is an enchanting and visually stunning game that effortlessly immerses players into a beautifully crafted world filled with wonder, danger, and emotional depth. Developed by a small indie studio, Wishfully, this side-scrolling adventure captures the heart and imagination with its evocative art style, captivating storytelling, and innovative gameplay mechanics.The first thing that strikes you about "Planet of Lana" is its breathtaking visuals. The hand-painted environments are rich in detail and vibrant colors, transporting players to a mesmerizing world that feels both familiar and otherworldly. From lush forests and towering mountains to desolate wastelands, each location exudes a unique atmosphere, contributing to a sense of exploration and discovery.The narrative of "Planet of Lana" is where it truly shines. The game follows the journey of Lana, a young girl accompanied by her loyal companion, Mui, as they navigate a planet on the brink of destruction. The story is conveyed primarily through stunningly animated cutscenes and subtle environmental storytelling. It tackles themes of friendship, sacrifice, and the consequences of humanity's actions, delivering a poignant and thought-provoking experience that resonates long after the credits roll.The gameplay in "Planet of Lana" combines platforming, puzzle-solving, and light combat elements. Lana's abilities, paired with Mui's mechanical skills, are cleverly integrated into the game mechanics, allowing for a seamless and satisfying progression. The puzzles are well-designed and provide a good balance of challenge and reward, while the platforming sections offer a mix of precision and exploration.One minor drawback of "Planet of Lana" is its relatively short playtime. Clocking in at around six to eight hours, the adventure may feel a bit brief for some players, leaving them yearning for more time to further explore the enchanting world and its characters. However, the game's concise length also ensures a tightly woven narrative that never overstays its welcome.Another aspect that could have been further expanded upon is the combat mechanics. While combat encounters are infrequent, they lack the depth and variety seen in other aspects of the game. A more fleshed-out combat system could have added another layer of engagement and excitement to the overall experience.Despite these minor shortcomings, "Planet of Lana" remains an exceptional indie gem that showcases the power of storytelling and art in gaming. Its emotionally charged journey, combined with its stunning visuals and innovative gameplay, make it a memorable experience for fans of atmospheric adventures.In conclusion, "Planet of Lana" is an outstanding achievement in the indie gaming landscape. It effortlessly captivates players with its stunning visuals, thought-provoking narrative, and well-crafted gameplay. Though it may leave some wanting more, the sheer beauty and emotional depth of this experience make it a journey worth embarking on.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 Would recommend you play this game it is an amazing story puzzle game with an amazing game design If you like FAR: Lone Sails or FAR: Changing Tides then you should 100% play this and if not check those games out as well amazing story but a different design in game it's more an RSM game then a puzzle one and just overall a yes for the price

_childDocuments_.review: I'd definitely recommend this game. It's exactly what it looks like it is. A well-executed 2.5D puzzle platformer that tells its story all through animation and the environment. I was actually surprised at the amount of gameplay mechanics there were. There weren't tons, but it was well sufficient for a game of this type. As you'd expect, the art direction and animation is phenomenal. Every scene and sequence was a joy to experience. It's a shorter game, but that's to be expected of this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This heartfelt and beautifully illustrated and sound designed visual story can be played in around 6-9 hours. Lana is a nice break from some of the darker and more violent games out there. The story pairs thematic elements from sci-fi films like Oblivion with visual styles from animated films like those by Studio Ghibli and nature-centric games like Zelda, Breath of the Wild. The soundtrack and sound design are top notch - simple, ethereal, atmospheric, beautiful. I would definitely enjoy even just listening to the soundtrack on its own.As a side scroller with no fight mechanic or weapons, your objective is to simply survive to the end while making it past the many puzzles and various enemies along your way. You can die, but you simply respawn on just outside where your screen was at, with a few exceptions for major "boss" type puzzle areas where you have to complete the whole section at once. The relationship between Lana and Mui is cute and the ending felt simple, satisfying and heartwarming.Overall I would recommend it and maybe even play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Two years ago, when I first caught sight of the trailer for 'Planet of Lana', I was utterly blown away. My exact words from a WhatsApp message then read, "I am blown away! So very much looking forward to this... This is a world that I want to explore every nook and cranny of... if I can just get to roam around in this world, that would be sufficient." Now, having journeyed through this world, I can affirm that the long wait was absolutely worth it.The moment I set foot on Novo (Planet of Lana), I was engulfed by its vibrant, hand-painted landscapes, evoking the same awe and admiration I feel for the enchanting worlds conjured by legends like Hayao Miyazaki and Makoto Shinkai. Takeshi Furukawa crafted a masterful auditory experience that augmented the emotional depth of the game. This, coupled with the meticulously designed sound effects, made the journey through Lana's world profoundly immersive.Novo is so mesmerising, I often found myself pausing my journey just to admire its sheer beauty, soaking in the ambience, and longing to learn more about its origins. Every relic, every shrine whispering the tales of this world's history left me gazing in silent awe at the mystery they embodied.The relationship between Lana and Mui is a moving narrative that transcends the game's mechanics. Their story of resilience, their unyielding bond amidst adversity has struck a deep chord within me, tugging at my heartstrings at every turn. One particular moment, which I shan't spoil, was a scene where Lana's desperation and her raw emotions towards Mui were so palpably real that I found myself wiping away tears.As I continue to gaze at the glyphs of Novo with fascination, and daydream of owning a Camel Robot of my own, I find comfort in the certainty that Planet of Lana has been an emotional journey worth every second of the wait; a surreal, indelible experience that I will forever cherish.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: A good chill game to relax and play after a long day's work.  This game is very much in the vain off INSIDE and LIMBO but with more of an unfolding story.  The puzzles are not too difficult so you won't get stumped by them at least not for long.   The best is you have a BuddyCat to keep you company on your journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Not as cinematic as expected from trailer, so don't expect experience of Limbo or Inside (like I did). Planet of Lana is slower paced and much more about puzzle solving, but the puzzle variation is surprisingly lacking, to a point, when it got a bit repetitive before it ended. But beautiful anime-like visuals and story still kept me entertained till the end... and your companion is just adorable :D
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I could sum up Planet of Lana as Trine 4 with more emphasis on the story and less on the puzzles. The game is rather relaxing (fantastic visuals/music) than challenging experience, so it's not something that hardcore players will enjoy eventually......so for those who look for a challenge - big nope. For those who look for a story/visuals, or for any casuls like me that likes pretty - yes, 100% recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana | ~6 hours to beatAn indie-ish side scrolling puzzle narrative game with no words, yet still tells a good story and looks beautiful along the way.It’s a Sci-Fi game set on a world where a race of alien robots have invaded the planet and began capturing folks War of the Worlds style. You’ve got to navigate through some not-too-difficult puzzles and use a bit of stealth (with the help of a smol cat-like alien) on your journey to rescue someone and solve some mysteries.It’s what I like to call a great “palette cleanser” game. It’s short enough that there’s no reason to let it sit for months. Long enough to get you invested in the experience.The music is super good, to the point where I’ll be adding the soundtrack to my playlist. I recommend the game. Had a good time with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is surprisingly worth playing. It's worth every single penny. Unlike one of the GOTY Sekiro game I've completed, this indie Planet of Lana has way better story telling, storyline, and music than that easy game of the year. Love how PoL has some unexpected plot twist before going back. PoL also has interesting environments, nice visuals and the machines in the game reminds me of Horizon Forbidden West Burning Shores, especially the Horus. Gameplay has a mixture of quick time events (QTE), stealth, puzzles, chasing scenes, and few short walking sim to enjoy the environments. Best is you can pet Miu, a cat-like character who is also your buddy working with you in the game to overcome obstacles. Love the machine music motifs, reminds me of a Chinese Orchestra classic yaozu wuqu 瑶族舞曲 piece. The symbols in the music sheet is brilliantly done! If you like short games with good story, nice gameplay, interesting visuals, some adrenaline rush, this is the game. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a visually beautiful, touching, and compelling game.The game is reminiscent of many classic games going back decades. The story begins with a familiar trope however what unfolds is a surprisingly engaging and delightfully artistic journey.Due to the delightful art style and the layered visual depth (which reminds me of early Disney animation style), every scene could make a good wallpaper. In fact, I took many screenshots for just that reason!I won't spoil the content of the story although there are many goods things to say about it. Play it for yourself. It's not exactly complex or deep game-play but I found it very pleasant to journey through their world.

Movement and controls were a bit like the very old days of Prince of Persia, in a very good way. At it's heart it is a puzzle game and I found that there was enough difficulty with the puzzles to keep you going. I finished the game in 10 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I took my time with this because I wanted to soak in every detail and nuance. What I experienced was an emotional, exceptionally well told story. The puzzles made my grey matter awaken, the music and visuals took me away to places I would never have imagined and the relationship that developed with my companion had me invested all the way through. Games, no, stories don't come along like this too often. Every single thing came into being in this game and from start to finish I was hooked. Now I am off to rest myself emotionally because I know when I play this again I will be taken through all of it again and I welcome that!

Yes I got the idea in the end (i believe), but still "meh".Most events feel quite random, or too convenient just for making a certain puzzle work,  to pretend it's not just about going forward. Yes honestly it became annoying having to just press forward for 50% of the time. Beautiful sliding landscapes, yes...I wish they could have done so much more with this idea. Sorry!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Promising announcements did not deceive, the game really turned out to be exactly what it was positioned for - a colorful adventure with a heartfelt story and incredible landscapes. Realizing that comparisons with Inside and other games of the genre cannot be avoided, the creators decided to answer with their trump cards, relying on a unique setting, complex puzzle solving together with their cute furry friend, who is either a cat, or a lemur, or all at once. This bet has played, the game feels like an independent work, not a clone. Let the game have some unpleasant moments in places, but they are fully compensated by the spirit of adventure, the overall competence of the plot and the energy of the action.If a beautiful visual can be easily seen already in the promo materials, then how incredible work has been done with the sound design, you only understand when you are in the game itself. It's just incredible. It seems that everything lives and sounds in this pulsating tropical world, each branch is woven into the overall sound palette with its crunch. With the help of sound, the creators control the mood of the player, either raising or lowering the degree; they create the necessary atmosphere, without which the game would have faded. The plot develops smoothly, albeit without giving any surprises, but beautifully combined with the gameplay. Yes, for such a rich world, I would like more diverse species of local fauna with which to interact. Yes, sometimes the movement becomes a little awkward, which leads to inevitable deaths (to get the achievement to complete the game without dying, you need to be furiously careful and even this may not save you). But the game is a pleasure to play, it gives you pleasure to interact with it, which is perhaps the most important thing. You can see that this game was drawn with their own hands, its story was invented by living brains, it is sincere and interesting. And for such an attitude I want to praise, well done!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: (no spoilers)A really cute little story about Lana and her planet getting invaded sparking an adventure for her and a really cute little animal she meets and will become her friend.Positives:- Game is really cute and beautiful, pretty unique, different biomes for different levels, goes from nature to industrial and vice versa, without being too much, it's pretty simple (not in a bad way but like they didn't overdo it)- Puzzles are pretty easy to do but you still have to think- The pet "Mui" that follows you everywhere is so freaking cute and you become VERY VERY  attached to it as it's one of the main mechanic that helps you solve the puzzles, you need to be the best duo- The ending was really nice without spoiling- Game is 4 to 5 hours long depending on how much time you take to do the puzzles- Sound design and soundtracks are AMAZING- Even though there's no dialogs really you can understand what's happeningNegatives:- The movements are pretty slow, which makes the game looks very slow sometimes, but I think it fits the genre- Story could be a little clearer sometimes, it's very "mysterious", I would love to know more about the actual lore- Some puzzles can be repetitive, would've loved to see a bit more varietyConclusion: I'm a sucker for those kind of cute emotional story games/platformers (I love Ori, Arise, GRIS, Limbo, RIME, Kena, Journey, The Last Campfire etc...) so I really enjoyed it. The pet is my favourite part of this game and probably will be yours too, soundtracks and graphics are great, it can get slow and would be great with more lore details, but it's like short and really cute and I had a really good time, I recommend for people who like those kind of games!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. It's only about 4 hours long, but I loved every second of it and for the price it is very worth it. It's got stunning visuals, a beautiful soundtrack, emotional highs and lows, and a pretty good story (considering all dialogue is in an alien language the player can't understand). I want to see this game succeed, because it is truly one of the best indie game experiences out there, and Wishfully Studios needs to make more games. Support them by buying this, you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: The soundtrack, the scenery, the simplicity with gradually increasing difficulty, the bits of story that piece together like an Anthropologists dream, the families being torn apart by some ancient tech that may or may not be from that planet is tragic and gets my curiosity going, its so nice to play without getting overly stressed or anxious about the monsters, machines or puzzles. Overall great game to sit and zone out and enjoy the trip as you gradually make your way through this planet's various biomes.

_childDocuments_.review:
A planet that used to be a place of undisturbed balance between human, nature, and animal has now become something else entirely.

The disharmony that had been in the making for hundreds of years has finally arrived in the form of a faceless army. But this is not a story about war. This is a story about a vibrant, beautiful planet - and the journey to keep it that way.

name: GNOSIA
detailed_description: The Gnosia lie. Pretending to be human, they’ll get in close, trick and deceive, and then eliminate one victim at a time... The crew of a drifting spaceship, facing off against a mysterious and deadly threat known as the “Gnosia” and having no idea who among them is really the enemy, formulate a desperate plan for survival. The most suspicious among them will be put into “cold sleep” one by one, in an effort to rid the ship of Gnosia. Gnosia is a Sci-Fi Social Deduction RPG in which you will engage in discussion with a variety of unique characters, with the aim of identifying the Gnosia among the group. Players will have to use what information they can gather during the discussions to ascertain whom they think is Gnosia and then vote to put them into cold sleep. As you progress, your abilities will improve - but so will those of the crew. As the numbers of crew members, Gnosia, and various “roles” increase, it will become increasingly difficult to determine who is telling the truth. Work in collaboration with or against other crew members to ensure your survival until the end. ・Repeatedly play through “loops”, triggering special events to unravel mysteries in a uniquely original narrative. Certain events will unlock new commands for you to use during discussions. ・Step into a variety of roles to develop different character builds. Your stats will determine how effectively you can sway the group’s opinion or lie, and will also affect your likelihood of being selected for cold sleep. ・Engage with an engrossing and eclectic cast of characters and experience randomly triggered events, each one unique to its subject. Character events will reveal information about your crewmates in the form of special “Notes”.

_childDocuments_.review: GNOSIA is an impressive social deduction visual novel game. As a unique existence in visual novels and Japanese AVG games that cannot be ignored, GNOSIA has won many game awards based on its unique advantages.When it comes to this game, I have to compare it with another excellent Ultimate Werewolf visual novel game on the PSV platform - Raging Loop. This game is different from Raging Loop, which uses Ultimate Werewolf as a story background to render the atmosphere of the game. In this game, the narrative of the story is not purely linear but promotes the story by playing werewolf killing games in the game. The characteristics of the characters in the game affect their actions and abilities in the werewolf killing game. This setting may seem boring, but it can unexpectedly bring a good game experience.The story background and character setting of the game are very avant-garde and full of technology. The music level is not bad either. The biggest drawback of the game is probably that is too monotonous. Repeated cycles will gradually cause players to feel bored, attributes are the most important factor affecting a character's actions, and the gameplay and the level of AI is also the biggest problem of the game.In general, as a rare visual novel with the theme of werewolf killing and social deception, this game is suitable for players who are interested in these elements; but at the same time, don't have too many expectations for the game's gameplay, such The setting will inevitably lead to the later game being relatively boring. I personally think the most outstanding part of this game is the perfect combination of futuristic technology, social deception, Ultimate Werewolf and visual novels.
_childDocuments_.name: GNOSIA

_childDocuments_.review: You might think that "Single player anime Amogus" sounds strange at best. But GNOSIA is a bit more than that. The mechanics are almost completely different, even if the scenario is the same - an impostor on a spaceship, killing the crew one by one, until the they get voted out by the survivors - or kill enough people. That is pretty much where the similarities end; and this is where the fun stuff comes in.Because even though the main format of the game is indeed playing the social deduction game, there's a lot more to it. There's a meta plot, interesting worldbuilding, there are individual subplots of the characters... there's even romance! How can you fit all of that in an anime Amogus? Hah, told you it's a bit more than that.Social is in the name, so you're probably confused; I know I was. So let me explain. I'll be using Among Us as a reference of sorts, but don't worry if you haven't played that.First of all, the game's story takes place in a time loop - every game is one loop. Every loop the roles are shuffled. Who's Gnosia and who's human this time? Well, that's your job to figure out! Or to prevent others from doing so, if you're Gnosia. But how do you figure it out? No - you can't go around and watch the characters' movements, catch them red-handed, going through vents. Everything is taking place in a specific order, kind of like in a board game. The game's split into days. Every day goes like this: First, there's a meeting. The meeting has five rounds of discussions in which the characters point fingers, talk about their roles, use their special skills (more on that later)... and then they vote on who to put in cold sleep (hey, better than being thrown out of the airlock). After that, you get some free time, which you can use to either go follow an event if available, or to improve your relationship with a character. After that, it's time to sleep. That's where people with roles that have actions get to act. That means Gnosia choose their target, for example - only one per day. If they managed to successfully kill their target (not always the case), you get a message who was eliminated, and the next day begins. This keeps going until either all Gnosia are in cold sleep, or half of the ship's remaining crew are Gnosia.No. There are multiple roles available, most of them possible to fill only once. For example, there's the Engineer who can investigate a person once a day, just before bedtime - and they'll know if that person is Gnosia or human. Sounds sweet, right? Well, not only being an Engineer makes you a target, but also the Gnosia can lie and pretend to be Engineer as well. But that's not all - Gnosia can also have a human ally, who can ALSO lie!So often it becomes a game of "who do I believe?". And this is where it gets fun. As you progress, you level up your abilities which for example increase your likelihood to instantly tell that someone's lying, or for others to believe your words more. You have three engineers! Which one's the real one? Which one's Gnosia? How can I tell?In total, there are 15 characters, including you. They always have the same stats and the same personalities... but there are some minor changes in their behaviour, depending on whether they're Gnosia or not. Those changes are generally very hard to detect, so it's better if you rely on deduction instead... or on the behaviour of others.For example, there's this character - Comet. She's not very clever and bad at lying, but her intuition is almost superhuman. She'll be able to detect lies much more easily than others. So if you notice Comet suddenly saying that someone's sus, you know that she probably detected lies. Or she's Gnosia.Then there's Raqio, a non-binary ultra-rational jerk. They can sometimes deduct with 100% certainty that someone's human or Gnosia... but they have a bad habit of suspecting their allies as well. Do you support them? Or shut them down? You can't tell, this twatologist will say that everyone is sus anyway. Unless you have some more reason to think that Raqio's right, or lying... and Raqio's decent at lying!Oh yeah. You're in a time loop, and one more character - Setsu - is stuck in it with you, although they're going through it in a different order than you. Nobody else is aware that this is a loop, and of course you and Setsu are trying to break it. That's the storyline. And in order to find out what you need to do, you need to keep playing the game. I managed to reach the true ending after 131 loops, or 25 hours. So you'll need to play a lot of Anime Amogus to get there. What I'm saying is if the social deduction gameplay doesn't sound appealing to you, then skip this one. A lot of the plot consists of smaller subplots, little events that need specific conditions to manifest, which show you another side of a character or teach you a new special skill. Some of those plots can end in romance... which is sad, considering that at the end of the game you'll loop and everything will be forgotten (although I'll never forget showering with Comet). Some characters will only end up attracted to you if you're of a specific gender, mind (there are three options: M/F/NB). Oh, and many of those events also serve as little windows to the greater world that exists outside of the ship. There's slavery, classism, horrifying parasites, transhumanism gone wrong... but also sentient, uplifted animals and a procedure to turn yourself into a cat? No, no sexy catgirl, actual meowing cat. It's good stuff.The aesthetic and the music complete the entire experience. Women suffer a little from the "same face syndrome", but less than in other anime-style works. I found all characters interesting and likeable, even when they tried to kill me. Perhaps especially when they tried to kill me? Ah, wouldn't go that far.If my messy description of how the social deduction gameplay sounds interesting, then I think you'd like GNOSIA. I got hooked almost instantly; but if this kind of discussion and deduction based thing isn't your cup of tea, then the rest won't be worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: So I want to say that, for sixteen hours, I really really liked this game. But, I know plenty of people are going to give it a positive review, and that people who read negative reviews are mostly looking for a list of things the game doesn't do well to use as an informed purchasing decision. If you look through my experience and think you might be willing to put up with it, definitely do, this game tries something really cool, but the annoying parts are unforgivably annoying. So, the game is a single-player Mafia game like Town of Salem, Among Us, Epic Mafia, etc. To compensate for the lack of actual social deduction, you have stats that you can increase through leveling, which occurs just through playing the game and viewing events. At the start of the game, you're going to be relying on things like looking over voting patterns and seeing who defends who, and making sure to not reveal yourself as an important role too early or else you'll be targeted and killed. By the endgame, though, you basically single-handedly decide who gets voted off each round. The gameplay works, but it's not something that you would like, come back to after clearing the game just to have some fun rounds of Mafia. The gamplay very much exists just to facilitate the story.The story exists in sort of the same realm of sci-fi time-looping realm that some of my favorite other VN's occupy - 13 Sentinels, 999, VRL, AI Somnium Files, stuff like that. However, the overarching story is very light, and character writing is even lighter. There's fifteen characters plus the MC, and each of them have key pieces of backstory you need to learn in order to progress. The way you unlock these is mostly through specific scenarios - you and an ally both survive til the end, you vote off a certain Gnosis who was targeting an ally, you eliminate a certain survivor as Gnosis, stuff like that. These range from very simple to weirdly obtuse, requiring groups of three specific survivors to all be alive at the same time. The signposting here also ranges from pretty obviously clued in (one character loves another character, you need them to both survive) to not communicated to you at all (three characters who have never spoken as a group in any other scene). At some point basically every discussion online leads to "at what point should I start using a guide to help me find some of these?"And at sixteen hours into the game, that's basically where I was. I'd done a fair number of loops where nothing happened, despite me always using the "Key Finder," an automatic settings function that messes with some of the backend values to increase odds of you getting the specific combination of allies you need. If you manually set the number of Gnosis to 3, it could be any three. If the Key Finder sets the number to 3, it will probably pick some pre-determined combination to help you view a scene you haven't seen yet. I only had four scenes left and was feeling pretty clueless, and after looking at the guide I'd realized the only ones I hadn't seen yet were completely random. I'd heard stories of people needing to max their stats to manipulate certain people living and dying and even then struggling to get the very specific setups they need, but I'd somehow gotten all of the really weird ones and was only left with ones that were completely out of my control. Two I got soon after that, one I managed to get after some messing around with settings. That leaves the last scene - one scene left to get. Again, this was my situation at sixteen hours. You might notice my game time is twenty-two hours. For the last six hours I have just been speedrunning loops as fast as possible. The condition I need is to vote a certain character off. Once I do, they have a chance of using a skill, and that's the final scene I need to beat the game. I use doubt five times in a row, we vote them off, and they don't use the skill. For six hours in a row. I don't have all the skills yet, so for the first hour or two I had a list of characters that wouldn't teach me any skills at all, so I would vote them all off first, and then only worry about winning at the end. At some point I stopped caring about winning and only focused on keeping characters who could, again, have a random chance of teaching me a skill alive. After two hours I stopped even caring about that and would just do the exact same thing every round - instantly vote off the character I need, then turn on my turbo controller until the round ends. Four hours of that. For a long time, the steady trickle of admittedly small-scale plot pieces was fun and worth it, but honestly it's long since that point. I would maybe be more willing to see this through if the writing was, as a whole, better, but it's not good enough to keep going. Several characters have involved backstories, but a lot of them are just throwaway one-liners. Most character's backstories are one-note things that never go anywhere and don't feel fun to have learned. One character is like "oh, yeah, I was raised on an AI planet." Never mentioned again, not related to anything happening in the story, but that's still one of that character's five critical pieces of backstory. In VLR, you ended up spending a lot of time with each character and learning their backstory is usually relevant information to the player. Even when it's not, it's usually at least interesting. There's some really good character writing here, but it's mostly condensed to a few characters while the rest are just sort of taking up space. Finding out the final piece of backstory to a character only sometimes results in an actual dramatic scene with some special CG and dialogue, while most characters you learn their two-sentence piece of info and that's it, that's the conclusion to that character's arc. The plot is also nowhere near as involved as a tradition VN either - there's very few crazy twists or foreshadowing or revelations that keep you hooked and wanting to know what happens next. This would be more forgivable if the experience was just shorter, but when it's dragging on in the way that it is it's much tougher to recommend. There's a couple really funny gotcha moments, but if you're coming from any of the games I mentioned above expecting some totally mind-blowing revelations and crazy twists, this is not that game. It's good, but it's not THAT good. To be completely fair though, it seems like my experience is SIGNIFICANTLY outside the norm. While looking through a bunch of "how long to beat" threads, the number I consistently see is 110 loops to 160 loops, depending on how much info you know about what conditions you need to meet. My number of 240 seems convincingly and wildly outside the average range, to the point where if you told me my game was bugged I would believe you. In fact, it seems now like a fair number of people are having trouble getting this event, so it might actually be possible that the game as it currently stands is unwinnable, or maybe the odds are just comically low. Both options are bad. Everyone I've asked for specific advice about how to trigger this event says "damn that's the weirdest thing I've ever heard." Gnosia was a really cool experience up until this moment, which is why I hate to give it a bad review, but like...damn. It's hard to recommend just watching a longplay because the moment-to-moment gameplay ties into the story so heavily, but on the other hand you have to deal with stuff like, uh, this. I'd be more forgiving if the experience was all-around more involved, but the effort to payoff value just isn't there from my personal experience with the game. Like I said, almost everyone else's runs have been way shorter than mine, and I think if my run had ended six hours ago I'd have really liked this game. I'm gonna stop playing until I see confirmation of anyone actually completing the Steam release of this game and I get some actual word that, no, the game isn't bugged, I'm just unlucky.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying that I loved the Danganronpa Series of games, but always felt underwhelmed by the fact that it never was a true "social deduction game", those games had a pre-determined story to tell and nothing you did had any effect on the outcome. It's probably why very few people are fond of the VN tag/genre, because most of them lack gameplay..There are visual novel elements to the game, however it is paired with quite a mechanically deep "social deduction game", where you're pitted against characters with different behaviors (thanks to their intelligent AI). The game expects you to pick up on each characters unique characteristics, some of which can be very subtle, others can be extremely blunt () and this lends itself to making each character feel more "real" in their personalities and the way they would behave. Whether you lose or win, the game doesn't end instantly. Instead you are rewarded with EXP (in which you can level up certain characteristics to help you win) and sent to another "loop", where your relationship with every character and role shifts. One run will never turn out exactly the same, so you'll have to rely on your own deduction skills, abilities and rational thinking in order to survive. With each loop you also get the chance to progress the story, and learn more about characters via VN sections (yes that's where the VN bits pop in). The plus side for most of you who simply care about gameplay is that these sections are short and sweet, so it doesn't take long before you're back into some social deduction action. However, with how strongly written and unique the characters are, you'll WANT to learn more about them and spend time with them- both from an emotional standpoint and gameplay standpoint. Learning more about these characters will help you win loops, and choosing not to do so will simply make your life harder.As for the music, well there's not much to say besides I love it and how unique it sounds- and that the art style is equally as superb. I'm no arts/music major, I simply like what I see and hear here.One more thing before I leave my final rating- for those of you who decide to try this game, don't be discouraged by losing loops. Like every other roguelite, you'll get stronger via levels and better yourself at deducing each character and situation. Trust me, this game is worth the patience.I would honestly recommend almost anyone to atleast try this game out once for yourselves, as I truly believe this game is a unique hidden gem, and my one wish is that more people will notice it and applaud it for what it is. This is the most fun and refreshing experience I've had with a video game for a very long time, and I have the utmost respect for the people who worked on this.For those still unsure, I'd recommend watching gameplay or streams  to get a feel- or better yet bum it off a friend for a bit and purchase it if you like it!The game's a solid 9/10 for me in the 7 hours I've played it, and I can't wait to play even more in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The beloved game has finally arrived on Steam! Described by many as a combination of Werewolf and Among Us with a heavy dose of Anime nausea is a visual novel that surprised me in several ways as I played through it, while its comparison to Among Us is valid with all of its characters being on a space station with one or more of them being an imposter of sorts, that's generally where the similarities end as while this game came out after Among Us, its original release in Japan was way before it became the sensation that it is now, so if anyone is looking for a similar experience they're going to be a bit disappointed.In Gnosia, you play as a faceless protagonist whose only discernible characteristics are their gender, name and whatever symbol or color you decide to associate with them you are soon introduced to some of the characters that you'll be interacting with throughout your adventure, only to learn that some of them are what are known as Gnosia. I can't really divulge too much about their goals without spoiling part of the story but let's just say that they are an imposter of sorts that will kill someone every time the ship goes through warp speed, if you've ever played the game Werewolf you'll be able to see the similarities. As a crewmate you must try to figure out which of your fellow crewmates are lying and put the traitors into cold sleep, after you succeed or fail to find out who the Gnosia is, you'll eventually go through a time loop and will once again need to find out who each Gnosia is but this time with a slightly different group and with everyone's roles jumbled around, these loops act as rounds in the game and are integral to the game's story and they're what allows you to replay the game over and over again.During your playthrough, you will meet all 15 members of the crew including yourself as well as learn about the different roles that each of them could have, besides the gnosia you have engineers who can suss out who is human and who isn't, you have guardian angels who can protect one person per night and prevent them from being killed, doctors can check on anyone who has been put into cold sleep to see if they are actually gnosia or not, AC followers are basically a wild card whose main goal is actually to let the gnosia win even though they are not gnosia themselves, there are characters who will have been on guard duty who cannot be gnosia as the gnosia cannot lie about being on guard duty so you can guarantee that anyone who says that they were to be genuinely human and the final role in the game is the bug, bugs are characters that shouldn't exist in the timeline they are in and if the gnosia or humans end up winning their loop and a bug is still alive its very presence can cause the universe to fall apart at the seams, so yeah, bugs are bad. These roles are explained a bit more in depth in the game but generally no role in particular is overpowered as there is plenty of counter play depending on which roles are in play during each particular loop. Eventually you will begin to realize that while the Werewolf game mechanic of restarting loops over and over again is important it isn't the true goal of the game, what you're actually trying to do is obtain as much information as you can about everyone who is on board the ship and by doing so figure out some of the mysteries that pop up as the story progresses. Going after this information can lead to some unusual situations, including a gnosia member sacrificing themselves in order to save everyone else on board while another may have you and a member of the gnosia working together when something goes horribly awry, the thing is sometimes these tidbits of information only come up if very specific circumstances are met and they aren't always guaranteed to proc unless you know exactly what you're looking for luckily after a certain point you'll be given the ability to automatically have the game set up a loop where a segment could occur making it where you don't have to randomly keep guessing what you're looking for. When going from loop to loop the frustration with the game comes when you're trying to complete these extra objectives and the characters that should theoretically be your allies in this situation does their best to mess up what you're trying to accomplish.If the above doesn't sound like it's going to scratch any particular itches with you, then Gnosia may not be the title for you but for those where the idea of a single player Werewolf style game as you slowly uncover an overarching mystery sounds appealing, Gnosia may be right up your alley!
_childDocuments_.name: GNOSIA

_childDocuments_.review: Gnosia is a bit of a rough little gem - an attempt to take a game framework that relies on human social deduction and interaction and turns it into a single player affair, to largely successful results.At its core, Gnosia is effectively a Very Weird Sci-Fi take on a Werewolf/Mafia simulator, where you play through a number of loops of the game with a variety of NPC crew members present; the gameplay revolves around debate sessions where the crew decides who is a probable Gnosia (the werewolf analogue) and tries to stop them by voting them into cold sleep, while the Gnosia eliminate people off the board each night. As you go through these loops and various permutations of role assignments for the crew, you see a number of events; some give you background on the crew, some teach you skills you can use during the debates, and some flesh out the broader mystery of why you and another crew member are time looping and how to stop it. There's also the complication of a special non-human/Gnosia role known as the Bug, effectively a walking paradox; if the Bug makes it to the end of the round without being put into cold sleep or scanned by an Engineer, they win by destroying the entire universe.  It's an interesting twist to throw a role into the mix that the standard "teams" are both required to play around and address ASAP.In the moment to moment, Gnosia is a fun game. The actual debates can get a bit repetitive in terms of dialogue since there's a relatively limited pool of statements each character has, but the developers did a really great job at actually designing the characters and giving them specific strengths/weaknesses and personalities that you have to learn to work with - and around. One character is incredibly adept at spotting lies but is effectively doomed the moment they have to try to tell one. Another character has high overall stats but is erratically insane so he doesn't use any of them well - but can still surprise you with his skills. Another character has good logical and analytical capabilities but is so abrasive that they'll often get voted out purely because nobody wants to deal with them. Another plays almost entirely on emotion and if you get on her bad side, regardless of whether or not you're on the same team, look out. Learning the character styles fleshes out the debates, because you have to decide how best to handle each round - who's a threat, who's a potential ally and who's just acting weird. If someone everyone tends to hate suddenly has a bunch of supporters this round, they may well all be Gnosia - or if everyone is dogpiling someone it's entirely possible they spotted something about their behavior that you missed. This ties into the fact that you get to choose your own stats and build and decide the approach you want to take; I went extremely high in intuition (spotting lies), performance (telling lies) and logic, but was generally weak in terms of keeping below the radar and lost a bunch of sessions because I made too many folks angry even when I was right about something.  You're not locked in though, with a fairly easy set of criteria to trigger a character stat reset to allow you to change what you feel isn't working.Ultimately, Gnosia is worth a look if you're curious how a well handled single player social deduction game would play out, or if you just like weird sci-fi settings and narratives.  The cast and crew are very interesting and fleshed out well and it's fun to just interact with them even if one of them might stab you in the back the next day.  The art and character design is bright and colorful and neat, and the music is gorgeous and strange with just a hint of friction.  Gnosia plays well and each loop is pretty speedy, and the game has a nice feature where you can have it set specific round parameters that can potentially trigger new events for you to help you progress. It is, however, very much not a visual novel at its core and just uses some of the trappings; Raging Loop is the flipside where the focus is the VN and the Werewolf games are more set dressing.  Approach Gnosia as a cool framework for a set of variable logic puzzles and you'll have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Gnosia is an unbelievably fun Visual Novel style game about surviving on a ship with Gnosia infectees using a Werewolf-style mechanic. The crew must find the Gnosia, the Gnosia must eliminate the crew with each phase taking the shape of 5 conversation-type interactions and then a vote. You can defend allies, call out enemies or even betray your collaborators.Each of the Crew have their own personality and discussion style, be it Raqio's purely logical approach, Yuriko's ruthlessness or Shigemichi being... well... Shigemichi. Meaning you have to truly know and understand the characters you're on the ship with to be able to read them for deception.There is story, with a wide variety of loop endings depending on both what roles you had, who survived and what actions you took, with plenty to do to unlock the mystery of the characters within.The art style is nice, characters are visually distinct and whilst I could've done without Comet's underboob, it really isn't a focus of the game.Gnosia is exceptionally fun and really rather well made. The achievements are also not obnoxious, and I personally had a lot of fun with this.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you know the true rage you will inevitably feel when the collective intelligence of the town hits rock bottom because your fellow townies couldn't figure out a mafia member if h...Wait...Do you know the true rage you will inevitably feel when the collective intelligence of the spaceship hits rock bottom because your fellow humans couldn't figure out a gnosia even if it hit them in the face? Yeah, that. The game is exactly that.It is a werewolf party game with more roles. You play as an amnesiac protagonist who has to piece together information as you go jump through the loops (literally). Since it is a single-player game, the game gives all of the characters unique skills that the player can also learn and outlevel everyone (yes, you can grind). This way, the game offsets the problem that is Artificial Unintelligence so you will not be forced to pull all of your hair but only some locks here and there. My main criticism is the overall weirdness and RNG-based progression system. Yes, there is a tool you can use to maximize your chances but you still have to rely on luck and more absurdly, you will need to betray your own faction in order to get a specific ending. All in all, good game. Much better than I expected, but not a masterpiece that left me speechless.
_childDocuments_.name: GNOSIA

_childDocuments_.review: The main selling point of Gnosia is the absolutely gorgeous art by Cotori. The game is a visual treat from beginning to end. As an actual game, it works, but not spectacularly well. You'll play somewhere around 150 somewhat short rounds of gameplay trying to find the Gnosia hidden among the crew or working with other Gnosia and to take down the crew yourself. There are a few other wrinkles to add complexity but they aren't terribly important. As you go through these rounds, repeating the same loop over and over again, you'll gather information about all of the characters and finally solve the underlying mystery.This hunt for secrets is what makes the game actually compelling to play- especially once you level up your abilities to the point that you're almost invincible and you can lead the debates whatever way you wish. The game does some things behind the scenes to point you in the right direction but whether a round of gameplay will yield anything new or not is kind of a toss up. Raging Loop was a much more interesting way to tell a story like this because it was fully scripted without any of those random elements. Because this one is randomized, you'll hear the other characters repeat the same lines in their debates over and over again and seeing the same general outcomes over and over does get a little tiring. I still found myself getting attached to some of the characters and there are some legitimately emotional scenes. But I can't help but think that this could have been a legendary game with a different approach. I still have a soft spot for it and I recommend it for anyone looking to enjoy the beautiful visuals and spend time with this crazy cast of characters.
_childDocuments_.name: GNOSIA

_childDocuments_.review: Gnosia is basically a singleplayer among us, with a story.There are different roles crew member, gnosia (enemy role), engineer, doctor .                                                                                 You will unlock event search after the tutorial. You can play it to uncover the story, and learn bits and pieces about all the characters.You can also create your own custom games, choose what role you want, how many crew members, what roles to include, how many gnosias (max 6).                                                                         It's a lot more fun than i expected it to be.                                                                                   As for the gameplay itself                                                  You basically are stuck in a time loop, yet every loop is different. The core of the gameplay are conversations. You can doubt, defend, become allies, or the npcs can doubt and kill you too. At the end of the day everyone votes on who they find to be guilty. You can lvl your abilities, and learn skills in order to help you survive and win. Despite being a visual novel, it did not feel like one due to the engaging game mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Gets good after the first 1000 hours! _childDocuments_.review: I'll start off by saying, if you're into Visual Novels purely for the story then this game might be a skip for you.Story bits are far and few between and some come with arbitrarily specific things to do to get to them.The ending while good, did sadly not feel "worth it" so to say.Why am I still recommending the game you ask?Because the combination of the gameplay, story and generous price is absolutely worth it!Personal favorite about Gnosia to me was/is the music, it is exactly what I want from a Visual Novel.Just like Zero Escape and AI, Gnosia has a specific song that will leave you to remember the game and the memories you have of it whenever you listen to it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game before on the Switch (finished at Loop 129) and the best thing I can say about it is that is excels in the uniqueness of the mechanics it uses: while it is true that you are stuck on a loop of days playing a variation of the popular Werewolf/Mafia game, the story/progression offered not only by the events of the game  as the degree of consistency of the characters and their respective personalities make this VN an excellent and easily recommendable experience, as long as you know what you're in for.I believe this latter point on the characters being consistent is very much worthy of praise, considering the circumstances for every loop are 99% randomized . I find it amazingly cool that you can start developing your own biases like being annoyed a certain character has been the Gnosia for 3 consecutive loops, for example.It is also worth noting that, as you will be relying to some degree on luck, especially at the very start (and towards the end), the game can feel slow at the beggining. I recommend playing at least around 25/30 loops to decide if this game is for you, if you are by any chance as turned off as I was in the first few loops — the initial segment of introducing new characters and mechanics certainly does not represent the entirety of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: GNOSIA

_childDocuments_.review: To say that I liked my time with Gnosia would be an understatement. It quickly became one of my favorite games of all time. The very emotional story is accompanied by great characters and an unbelievable soundtrack.The art style seemed weird at first, but as I got used to it, the urge to buy an art book was irresistible. Unfortunately, there is no art book (yet), but hopefully, they'll make one at some point.It's one of those visual novels that are very easy to recommend to genre newcomers, as it's partially an RPG. It's challenging at first, but as you unlock more skills, it becomes progressively easier. The endgame is a breeze, serving the purpose of unlocking various character scenes and exploring different outcomes.I really hope that it'll get a good remaster with voice acting in the future. It absolutely deserves it.
_childDocuments_.name: GNOSIA

_childDocuments_.review: this is one of my favorite games of all time. has your brain been completely and irreversibly damaged by time travel stories? did you play mafia once in high school and got way too into it? does seeing the phrase "among us" used seriously make you laugh? this game is for you. be the most suspicious person in your efforts to point out that someone is very clearly an impostor and get cryogenically frozen for your crimes. be the most suspicious person in your efforts to throw everyone under the bus because you're the impostor and wring your hands as everything goes according to plan, until the dolphin in a space suit reveals she's actually not supposed to exist and the whole universe collapses. these are just scenarios that will pop up in the basic gameplay loop, which, while it can get repetitive, holds a surprising amount of complexity in the individual personalities of each character you will come to understand throughout the game.the story is a whole other animal, and I won't discuss it here, but I will say it made me ugly cry. this is the game of all time. its soundtrack makes my chest hurt. big thanks to my wonderful friend who gifted this game to me. i am now going to probably buy a switch copy just to display. please buy this game
_childDocuments_.name: GNOSIA

_childDocuments_.review: Underrated gem.Very consistent art style, addicting gameplay loop and nice narration. Contrary to some other reviews, I haven't had to spend too much time hunting for events, wrapping up around loop 90, but I still feel compelled to run it again for more gameplay (achievements are requiring to win in some tough configurations) or for any missed optional events. Also the game looks gorgeous: there are absolutely no elements which would look out of place.Few tips, because you deserve something good if you've read this far:- If there is Yuriko, then either make sure that you're BFFs, or plan ahead how you'd get rid of her. She can be a ton of pain to keep around, and she won't hesistate one bit before throwing you under the bus even if you are on the same side. Even more so on the late game, when she gets retaliate: if you desperately need for someone to survive, make sure they don't get hit by it, even if it means you defend Yuriko immediately after she is accused by them. - Raqio is opposite, utterly useful to keep around. Same for anyone universally hated: being able to focus votes on someone may be your only hope in certain situations.- AI never makes two gnosias assume the same role. There are AC follower and bug, though...

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely well done story-rich game. The storytelling had well done twists and turns, and even with the game's nonlinear progression, all the story points fit in well together, like a carefully crafted puzzle. It's also just a fun werewolf/mafia game if you want it to be- very unique singleplayer setup that makes the game play unlike any multiplayer werewolf or mafia game. The world has plenty of life in it. Some people might think 25 dollars for 26 hours of gameplay is a bit steep, but I enjoyed every second, and I still think about the story and carry it with me to this day. A must-have for anyone who enjoys logical rationale.
