_childDocuments_.review: All told, OTXO is quicker than a muzzle flash, offering rapid-fire twin-stick action that is seriously intense. Wrapped in a cool monochrome package and splashed heavily with the blood of your enemies, what it lacks in visual clarity it more than makes up for with an impressive sense of style. The gameplay isn’t built for lasting impressions though; with no long-game to speak of, it’s strictly a ‘how far can you get this time’ affair that harkens back to the arcade shooters of the 80s and 90s. Best enjoyed as a run or two in between more meaty experiences, OTXO is perfect for the Nintendo Switch or the Steam Deck, where you can wile away short commutes with a hail of bullets before slipping your machine back in its holster, ready to let rip again at a moments notice.Full Review:

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourite games of 2023. It is a brilliant symphony of loosely controlled chaos, destruction and violence. The guns feel amazing and somehow sound even better. The control and skill required to excel in such an environment seem impossibly out of reach at first but after a few failed runs where we are slaughtered by random henchman #23b you find yourself acclimating to the chaos and you can feel your reflexes tighten up in real time as you start to perceive Otxo as a violence ballet that you can weave your way through with a combination of the right steps and the right shots. As you fire one guns last bullet into the waiting mass of enemy bodies aggressively persuing your demise you reach down and pry another gun from the cold dead hand of the fallen to continue the cycle of violence onward and forward. Otxo is a murder mansion on the shores of an unknown plain of existence where you will kill your way through countless faceless adversaries that stand between you, a hard day's work and a nice stiff drink at the bar.

_childDocuments_.review: I love twitch shooters and punishing games akin to katana zero and hotline miami (where this game obviously draws inspiration from - even the Midnight Animal HM fan-spinoff that never came to be is referenced in this and in the credits), so I was expecting a lot from this, and had fun with the demo.The kicker though, is that the game has a lot of fundamental flaws that contradict the "quick and brutal" gameplay style the game goes for - with the Drinks also hurting the game in multiple ways.- Enemy reaction time too quick, too much emphasis on either using Focus or waiting around corners. Slows down the game.- Invisible enemies and goo-shooters slow down the pacing too much and are just infuriating to fight- Bad drink rolls ruin can screw over your run- The roguelite elements - gun gachapon and drink importing should actively be AVOIDED (explained later)- too much screenshake - even setting screenshake to 0 in the settings still has screenshake from kicking- frame dips when things get going- pretty much non-existent narrative but w/e- view range is quite limited (let us see further like in hotline miami - it encourages thoughtful planning)- no sensitivity options- sound settings don't seem to work that much - you ears will be blasted either way Funnily enough, the best strat to win this shooter is to NOT shoot (outside of boss fights).You want to actively remove all gun purchased from gachapon through the nun and only leave the starter pistol. You want specific drinks, which as mentioned previously, really makes or breaks runs - so in order to not dilute the drink pool, you want to avoid importing drinks that don't revolve around melee or pistols.For general gameplay, make sure to pick up The One (most important drink), Fat Wallet, Healthcare, Dome 2016, Bloodweiser, Trophy and Roadhouse (anything with healing, kicking, and coins - and avoiding non-pistol weapon drink) - with QoL being Vigor, Sliver, Halo, Cadaver, Bloodweiser, Hair of the Dog, Cliche, Rabid, Roxy, and Animal.For boss fights, you just need to have Dividends (most crucial boss drink), Lightweight, Enlouder and Chenrezig to speed up DPS with the starter pistols - Practiced helps too.Also, avoid any drink with a negative - most of those are dogwater.4/10 - the "core" gameplay is fun - but the best way to succeed is legit to avoid most of the game's core mechanics like guns (you want the single-shot low-rpm pistols for easier use of The One's reflection) and some drinks, with too much hindering on RNG for those key drinks you need to succeed. Plus, having some enemies that are the antithesis to a faced-paced shooter is kinda wack.The biggest negative has to be the enemy reaction time being WAY too high that you have to rely too much on sitting behind corners or using Focus (which is used by the dev as a design crutch to band-aid fix the reaction times being too high) until you have the drinks that let you cheese it all - which again, is RNG dependent.

_childDocuments_.review: OTXO is yet another of literally hundreds of lazy amateur 2D retro top-down shooter/brawlers infesting Steam and lowering the average quality of all video games everywhere.This one is basically a ripoff of Hotline Miami, except somehow the developer managed to come up with even worse graphics... truly an achievement.  It's not only pixelcrap, but it's monochrome pixelcrap.  Except the blood is red because that's edgy and basically because of that the developer is as talented as Stephen Spielberg.  No seriously. In fairness the controls are well polished and smooth and you can customise them... the only thing that made this somewhat acceptable, but only to huge fans of Hotline Miami who wanted more of that but were willing to settle for this second rate ripoff experience instead.From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.While this is on PC, it has all the hallmarks and deficiencies of a console game, from the clunkier than needed control scheme to the less than cutting edge graphics.  There's 10's of thousands of PC games on Steam, and PC gamers deserve only the best.  This might not appeal to many gamers due to the lack of PC-centric design.  It's unclear why this game was never accepted on the video game console appliances it seems to have been designed for.Some of the defects in the game can be attributed to the choice of using the GameMaker Studio construction kit/toolset.  This is a very poor quality toolset favoured by amateur developers as it's cheap and requires little in the way of development skill, but unfortunately has very limited capabilities.  Just as you can't make a silk purse out of a sows ear, you can't make a great video game if you use a terrible engine.  GameMaker Studio is most commonly used to make retro pixel shovelware and cash grabs.A strong argument can be made that construction kits like GameMaker Studio should never be used to make games for profit, as the "developer", Lateralis Heavy Industries has done here.  These construction kits are intended to teach people some of the basic principles of game development, and to make small demos to pass around with friends.  They're not intended to replace to actual work of real, professional game developers.  So it's inappropriate when amateurs try to use these for profit, without any actual, real game development effort taking place.  This doesn't result in products that have any real meaningful value for gamers.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.OTXO has the laughable, eye-watering price of $15 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  For comparison, the $15 asking price for this game could get you games like "Hearts of Iron IV", "Project Zomboid" or "Cities: Skylines".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.  There's also thousands of free, superior quality games on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: An easy recommend if you like the idea of a seriously hard action rouge-like. It has an incredibly strong flow state. My 11 hours feel like 40. I think this is because if you fall out of the right head-space, you'll die in about ten seconds flat. Just beat my first run; at times I was honestly unsure if I would ever manage it. You can't out-grind this game, upgrade your starting stats, or switch to easy mode. All you can do is get better, learn the map layouts, learn the weapons, their firing speeds, how long you have before an enemy turns to shoot you.The game itself is also really well designed, in subtle ways I didn't appreciate at first. There's a good amount of variety in runs. You can't switch between starting characters, but can control what guns spawn in the mansion, and the different perks combine in interesting ways sometimes. Skill is also the same thing as speed, and you need to go fast to keep a combo and earn enough money to out-scale the later levels. This means that not only is there a constant risk/reward, you want to go fast enough to earn money, but not so fast you slip up and die, but also as you get better at the game, your runs become faster and faster until you're practically speed-running the early levels. This cuts down on the tedium of those early levels significantly and makes repeated runs way more fun.An easy recommend for me. OXTO is not a 300-hour game with endless random content. It's the kind of rouge-like more about the challenge, and overcoming said challenge, than endless replays. It is a tight, extremely intense experience which respects your time and abilities, and which I will be thinking about for a very long time.

_childDocuments_.review: OTXO is an incredibly fun game, with some mechanics that I think hold it back from being exactly how I would like it to be. Raycevick has a really good review of this game, so parts of my observations will repeat.Combat is extremely fun, fast and tactical. It is one of those games where you constantly make small decisions on the fly. For example: grab a shotgun to clear a room, then quickly get a sniper to take care of a distant threat, only to switch to an lmg and fire from a distance into a new batch of enemies to draw their agro to keep your combo meter going. The feeling of “OTXO Zen” when all these decisions are made back, to back, to back is great. Guns are great and feel wonderful to fire while remaining different for each other. SCAR is a slow and accurate rifle that can deal a lot of damage at range, while Famas takes care of anything up close, while G36C is a great compromise, while AK47 packs a punch with a low rate of fire… and so on. There are a lot of tools of destruction with almost every archetype of guns present/ The option to get rid of weapons you do not care for before a run is also great. Music is amazing. There is not much to say, listen to it online and imagine you are firing two mac-10s :) in slow motion.The upgrade system is great. You have to be aggressive to get coins that you spend on drinks that allow you to be more aggressive. If you are passive, your multiplier will not be high, so you will lack coins to buy drinks, so you will lack the firepower in later stages. The builds that you can make are diabolical. Pair dual-wielding with increased rate of fire, increased rate of fire when you reload, Increased damage, 25% chance to get back bullets you miss, big bullets and increased damage when you hit an enemy. Then grab 2 vectors and see if there is a God to stop you. Bosses can be killed with 4 mag dumps. Also shooting at a wall refills your ammo, so dumping dual g18 down a corridor is surprisingly cost-effective.My issues with this game are few, but quite impactful.- The first few floors are just boring. OTXO starts at floor 3 or 4. It starts when you have 5 enemies in a room, not when you have 5 of them on a floor. - The bosses are not fun. They are either so easy you can stand in place (inbred basilisk), spammy (abhorrence, the final boss) or annoying (Mr. Manslaughter my God). They usually deal almost no damage…. until they start firing explosives. Then they can erase 2/3 of your health within literally 2 seconds with almost no warning. And since it is a roguelike, dying to such attacks can be VERY infuriating.- And then there is the RPG enemy. A lovely gentleman that fires an AoE rocket that can erase a substantial part of your health. These rockets are fast, often come out of nowhere and can be easily missed in the chaos of the later stages. Also extremely annoying in a game that resets your progress when you die.In conclusion, buy the game, have fun. If you encounter an annoying boss just save, quit and come back to try again. Doom Eternal does not make you feel as powerful as some of the drink combinations in OTXO. Also listen to the OST, it is on Spotify.

_childDocuments_.review: Now I'm not usually a fan of rogulikes, and I cannot stress this enough...BUTOTXO is everything roguelikes should strive to be and then some.  It's everything that topdown shooters or action games in general should strive to be!  The art style, though simple, is visually striking and manages to strike the balance of reusing assets without seeming repetitive.  The soundtrack is so unfathomably good that it 100% deserves its vinyl printing.  The story is a light presence, but it's always there, and from the people you meet, to the drinks you buy, to the collectibles you find, and even to taking a breather to fish for some extra coin; the mansion and its denizens are teeming with life that brushes the fur of a greater narrative beneath the thunderous roar of the weapons and visceral stains of red upon the tile floors.  And the gameplay:I loved Hotline Miami but the instantaneous death did happen to get frustrating, especially during the longer segments of its sequel.  But OTXO fixes EVERY issue I ever had with Hotline Miami.  Your character is no longer made out of paper, your weapons have actual weight, your aiming feels precise, and bullet time is there to get you out of a pinch when you need it.  It demands careful knowledge of your surroundings without being overly tedious, yet facilitates gameplay that always invites those heart-pounding run-and-gun brawls that you should expect of an action game.DON'T THINK.BUY.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Hotline Miami. It’s still THE pinnacle brutal top down arcade twin stick shooter to me. But OTXO comes pretty close to dethroning it. It shares the same core loop of clearing rooms as quickly and as violently as possible, but with just enough extra mechanics and details to make it feel unique. The only things that hold it back are the roguelike genre elements, of which I am just not a fan of generally, as well as some minor criticisms with its visuals affecting gameplay; which are the equivalent of two cheetos holding a door from a battering ram.While the games look very similar, OTXO does not play like Hotline Miami. I had to learn this the hard way when I first started playing. Hotline Miami was all about clearing rooms quickly, memorizing paths and swapping weapons, until you get the perfect run on a level. Aside from the occasional boss and dogs, all enemies were essentially the same. OTXO’s levels are somewhat procedurally generated as far as I can tell, and there is much more variety with enemies and bosses, and none of them are a one-hit-kill. The same tactic of sprinting through rooms and wildly spraying bullets will only get you up to about the first boss of OTXO, and not much further. You’ll have to make use of your other abilities, like bullet time, dodge rolling, melee kicking, and maybe a bit of luck with the bonuses you get from the bar in between sets of missions in order to advance further. And you’ll  to master them in order to see the end of this game because every time you die, you have to start the entire game over from the very beginning.This is where I start to have a problem with the game. There is a story to this game, albeit barebones and not really worth mentioning beyond it being a solid excuse for the insane action, and seeing new areas and bosses will be difficult to tackle for the first time. But my patience wears thin when I lose literally all of my progress while I am still learning the patterns and layouts, and just want to see the conclusion of the game. I don’t have an issue with difficulty spikes or difficulty in general, but I do have a problem with forced Ironman modes. It exacerbates all of the otherwise small flaws in the game. Flaws like how the background environments don’t always make it immediately clear what is traversable terrain, or how some areas are too large and open for you to see enemies before they start shooting at you, or how some random bonuses are clearly better than others and can trivialize runs.At first, these flaws combined with my approach to the game were making it difficult to have fun playing. But the more I played, the more I understood and appreciated what the game was doing both with its gameplay and its surrounding elements. The sound design from the guns to the music is phenomenal, and the unique areas and bosses have a great visual design to them. I love the shattering glass and explosions of papers from stray bullets and bodies hitting the environment like it’s a John Woo movie. When I finally beat the game for the first time, I was completely sold.

_childDocuments_.review: [Short Glowing Review]Game is 10/10.Music, 10Gameplay, 10Features, 10Story, 10.[Long Stroke Review]OTXO is a symphony of death. The music lines perfectly with each level and this would probably be the only game in a long time in which I haven't muted the songs out of annoyance of shlocky easy grabbed music arrangements. Each track is perplexing and quite enjoyable with a plethora of different sounds that make each unique instead of the same garbage with a slightly different tilt.Each level has it's own unique aberration to the normal gunplay. Be it mechanics, enemies and design, forcing you to adapt to each situation while you go through the manor.The gameplay, while basic, is quite addicting and is carried by the design [Less is more]. Easy to pick up, hard to put down. There are intense moments of snap decision making but unlike Hotline Miami a failure is not an instant death. The enemies react to each action. Any door kick or shot creates a window of tension as the AI flanks and hunts down the player. This ontop of the ambiance and music creates a level of tension that is not perpetual/vexing. It sits at the edge of the engagement making each individual level pop in their own way.The bosses are unique, finely crafted and wonderfully bizarre. Each an obstacle to learn and overthrow with precision which is what it should be. OTXO is not afraid to be different at the same time synonymous with shooters of this style. It is not afraid to take leaps where others take small steps. It exemplifies the simple loop with small adage to detail, for example when heavily wounded the pause screen slowly drips blood as if the Wolf is hovering over the note. The overworld is charming with a slight mystique to it and while I wish there was more to do within it. There is enough to satisfy coming back to it on the odd occasion. This is a game with love and design at the forefront. It seeps with cautious flow on the dance of creativity, meticulously bridging a gap of what is known with what is unknown. It is an experience that I wish I could restart with fresh eyes and hands. And it is criminally unrepresented in most gaming circles, had I the power to change such a thing I would in a heart beat.It isn't a masterpiece, but in the flaws it makes a staunch overlap of indie development over AAA slop. If a sequel is planned I would recommend adding more to the bar, improvements to weapons and the Wolf himself. The overworld is the nexus of insight, but the bar is the nexus of home. Would it be that it were developed further I can consider that to be enough to set OTXO apart from the first towards the second.A beautiful game where suffering is a tool of growth as it should be. 10/10, Would summon attack dogs again.

_childDocuments_.review: It takes a few runs to really get it and find the rights drinks (aka power ups). But once you get used to the gameplay and find your favorite weapons, the game gets super fun and you can't wait to start another run after you die or complete one.There are so many weapons, and although they take time to unlock, they really feel different somehow; it's well balanced and interesting. You can customize the game quite a lot with weapons roster selection, and difficult challenges.The game gets boring in terms of visuals and rooms layout, but it's still awesome to play a couple runs from time to time for a big dose of entertainment.Congrats to the devs, because they really made something different from anything else! Of course, the inspiration is Hotline Miami, but it's even faster-paced, chokefull of content, and has way more replayability.I highly recommend, the game is so cheap, yet super cool.
_childDocuments_.name: OTXO

_childDocuments_.review: Otxo (Pronounced "Oh-Sho") is what happens when you trim the Fat of Hotline Miami, smooth out the gunplay, toss in some roguelite elements, and add a generous helping of ultraviolence and destruction.The story of this game is minimal with some system-shock-style lore elemnts through books and log entries, and I like that the dev did it so he could focus on the gameplay, which plays butter-smooth, and brutally-difficult.It doesn't have hotline miami's soul-crushing story, it's glitzy and jarring visuals, or it's smooth synthwave soundtrack from various artists. It doesn't have melee weapons or executions. and doesn't have animated character portraits. But that's Okay.Otxo also, doesn't have door jank, stupid enemies that forget their allies died, the need to manually extend your vision when you point the cursor at an enemy, bosses that die in only three hits, and the hell of trying to sort through ten guns on the ground and figuring out if you can grab the one you want.Otxo's soundtrack is a methodical, paced, hard, dark and brutal style, as if a synthwave artist took inspiration from death metal rather than 80s movies. the closest music comparison I can find to Otxo's Soundtrack is Dawn of Ashes, but even then, Otxo is distinct-enough to where it basically has it's own style. of music.Just like Hotline Miami, the music drives the action, and holy hell is it a banger. If you've ever watched Max0r's videos, you've probably heard a track or two from this game. Otxo does far more than most roguelites I've seen to mitigate the problem of "RNGESUS HATES YOUR GUTS AND SENDS YOU JUNK DROPS ALL DAY,", but it can still fall into this problem. In addition, Otxo shares Hotline Miami's Problem where large open spaces make you prone to being sniped by enemies offscreen. Thankfully, a proper health bar means that you won't die after a single stupid little mistake. but enemies have health too, which means you may have to double or even triple-tap to get a proper kill.Also, one of the bosses before the final boss is famed for being supposedly-harder than the final boss... and I think they're correct in that regard, if not because that boss has SO MANY EXPLOSIVES!If you liked hotline miami, you'll have a good time with Otxo. If you love top-down shooters but hated insta-death mechanics, you'll appreciate Otxo.Definitely recommend, on, or off sale.
_childDocuments_.name: OTXO

_childDocuments_.review: Really slick game.  Some have called it a spiritual successor to Hotline Miami, but besides the aesthetic it is really in a a whole different category.  First off it has randomly generated levels opposed to a chapter story like HLM.  This is a fast and punishing roguelike.  I am not sure how much I will play it, because it is TOUGH AS NAILS.  The gameplay loop is really fun tho and the beats are PUMPIN.  The lack of color aside from the blood makes for some striking visuals.  I def recommend it to fans of the genre of top down shooters.

The randomly generated levels are varied, enemies are aggressive, tons of perks to combine off one another for powerful builds, and there's a ton of weapons to use and unlock. _childDocuments_.name: OTXO

_childDocuments_.review: Hotline Miami is one of my favorite games of all time, top-down frantic gameplay combined with an unique aesthetic and a killer soundtrack make for a memorable experience. However, it doesn’t come without flaws. The game is old and by playing it you realize it has quite the amount of jank (picking up weapons is a chore, the enemy AI sometimes just stops working properly and doors are busted beyond repair) and, aside from S ranking all levels, there’s only so much in terms of replayability.OTXO takes the framework of Hotline Miami and expands on it, adding bullet time, roguelike elements and getting rid of all the junk, while still maintaining an identity of its own.In terms of gameplay, while similar to its inspiration, OTXO takes some liberties making the game even more fast-paced and challenging. By killing enemies you earn coins used to purchase upgrades, the combo meter affects how much you earn. A higher combo nets you more coins, urging players to be fast and actively seek combat instead of playing more passively and safe. Being fast isn’t just for show, it’s the optimal playstyle.Even your choice of weaponry is used against you, through an NPC before the beginning of a new run you can select which of the weapons you have unlocked will appear in the mansion, the catch is that this also influences the weapons the enemy wields. Select only the best performing guns? The enemy has them as well, and they greatly outnumber you. Pick as many guns as possible? The weapon pool is now more variegated but also filled with redundant bloat. Pick only pistols? Time to recreate your favorite John Wick shootout.If all of this sounds too much don’t worry, you’re not a bullet away from death as you have a health bar and you can always roll under a hail of bullets to dodge them or to reposition. Drinking will also help, as the liquors you purchase from the bar will grant you special abilities (such as a rechargeable shield, dual-wielding or blocking bullets with your hand just like Neo). Be warned though, as you progress further the enemies will improve as well and more specialists will join their ranks (e.g. snipers, sticky goo shooters, invisible gunmen), dispose of them and you’ll come face to face with the boss of the floor. While some of them are total pushovers others can and will send you back to the main menu, the game at least is kind enough to grant you infinite ammo to deal with them.Perhaps the most incredible aspect of OTXO is that it was made by just one person, one developer with a clear vision that expanded on an already great game while delivering a unique take. I also want to commend the work that went into the sound design, I’ve never felt this satisfied mag emptying a machine gun and the soundtrack already has a dedicated playlist on my Spotify.A must buy, whether or not you have played Hotline Miami before.
_childDocuments_.name: OTXO

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game. If you crave Hotline Miami but don't wanna play through HM2's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, OTXO is the way to go. Lots of customizability, and incredibly replayable. The main issue with Hotline Miami and Hotline Miami 2 for me is the lack of replayability and how fragile you are. In this game though, both you and the enemy are less fragile. HM and HM2 also lacked replayable levels that weren't tedious, frustrating, or incredibly easy. The bosses are also fun when you learn how to deal with them. I just finished the game on normal and it was fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: one of my favorite roguelikes at the moment! the sound design slaps to the point where almost every song from OTXO is on my workout playlist lmfao. The gunplay is solid, the drinks (obligatory roguelike power-ups) are fun to synergize and not too grindy to unlock. The solo dev, Lateralis, made a different game called Manus Dei, which is kind of a Devil Daggers-like. Not a huge fan of it but its $3 USD so if thats up your alley you can buy that too. As of right now, (steam summer sale 2024) OTXO is 50% off, landing it at $7.49 USD. imo the full price is worth it, but if you cant shell out 15 bucks i understand. _childDocuments_.review: OTXO is a rougelike top-down shooter where you ruthlessly shoot, kick and blow your way through a mysterious mansion in an attempt to free yourself of its confines.The gameplay is incredibly fast-paced, violent and stimulating and the vast arsenal of guns is a treat to play with. Paired with great sound design and a remarkably brutal soundtrack, OTXO is guaranteed to satiate any desires of ultra-violence.The roguelike elements are simple but mostly well implemented. You get coins from killing, the bigger your combo the more you earn, and you spend the coins on upgrades in the form of drinks. These upgrades are plentiful and are bound to make every run unique. I did find the bossfights rather unbalanced however, as some would pose far less of a challenge than a regular level, while others I would never be able to bring down to half of their HP before dying, and it was entirely up to RNG as to which boss I’d face.The monochrome + red artstyle, while an appealing aesthetic choice, does unfortunately result in a lack of visual clarity at times. It’s easy to mistake a window for a wall, an acid puddle for a prop and so on. During one run I had run out of ammo, but due to the absolute mayhem going on on my screen and in my headphones I had not even realised I wasn’t firing any bullets until I had most of my health blasted away.Overall, despite a few design flaws OTXO provides a vicious and exciting shooter experience as well as sensory pleasure, for which I give it a score of 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Hotline Miami gameplay, this is more of that with some rougelite elements. _childDocuments_.review: I'd just like to say first, please, let this and Hotline Miami co-exist. I know Hotline Miami is one of, if not, the most renowned top-down high-risk shooter, but Otxo is a different territory, and the two shouldn't be compared gameplay-wise.I had great fun playing this. Just like in the written logs during the flashbacks that spoke of former Otxo's who fought more and more, getting further and further into the mansion, I felt pure satisfaction getting further, and further. Making those long-term investments to upgrade the bar with more powerful abilities, and of course, the occasional fishing and playing fetch with Roxy. Gotta love Roxy.I found this game in a "find wife" meme, where it had Isaac Clark, James Sunderland, Alan Wake and Elster, if you know any of those characters. After playing Signalis, I became a sucker for "find wife" games, and this game just screams, So, of course I had to pick up this game. The story is told through bits and pieces, and I enjoyed collecting more of those pieces and putting them together. I enjoyed thinking logically of the long-term; a run that I knew just wasn't meant to be, will not be. I easily spent money towards the better drinks that had to be imported, and whenever I could, I always spent money to get more guns and collectibles during those flashback sequences. I will say, after playing all this time, I have learned that there are drinks that are worth grabbing, some drinks that are an INSTANT pick up for me if I can buy them, and there are drinks to avoid because they are just not good. Do what you will with that info.Also, the two characters that stick out to me, is the Otxo of course, but also the nun that's devoted to the Church of Steel. Church figures with guns have always been cool in media. (faith: the unholy trinity >>>) With the Otxo, I've never seen a game that has a john wick-esc badass using old WWI/WWII guns extensively, both as a killing machine and an absolute gangster. I never knew I needed to see the Otxo duel-wield two MP40s but here we are. The M1 Garand gifted to him was such a good style choice to me, it just clicks.TL:DR, Otxo is an awesome rogue-lite with great music, serviceable story, great music, solid gameplay, and great music. We love Cvnka we do we do!

The starting drink you get for free has a massive impact on how quickly you can get currency, with drinks that build your econ early snowballing into a massive advantage and those that don't really limiting your run.  It leads to a situation where the meta seems to be to just reload a bunch until you get a good drink.This problem is compounded by the fishing minigame.  Normally in video games, fishing minigames are a way for you to chagne up the pace of the game and relax for a moment before getting back into the game proper, and in theory this is what the fishing minigame in OTXO would be - it's extremely simple, no skill relaly to it other than recognizing hte water ripple pattern that means it's time to reel it in, and as far as I can tell the actual money value of the fish you get is random.But the fact that it has  means it can't serve its seemingly intended role as a way to chill out from a pretty intense game. _childDocuments_.review: Amazing rougelike. This game has almost everything you would want from a heavily Hotline Miami inspired rougelike aside from maybe coop. Combat is extremely smooth, responsive, and satisfying. Enemy variety keeps things interesting up until the end and through subsequent playthroughs. The slow-mo, dodge, and kick mechanics all blend in the most perfect way that would make John Woo fully erect. And to top it all off you also get a banger dark synth soundtrack and overall amazing sound design to accompany you during your struggles through the mansion. For criticisms there are very few. Mainly the monochrome aesthetic and color palette. While I do like it from a style point of view it can make certain levels blend together at times and feel samey outside of their respective gimmicks. Also sometimes due to blood completely coating the floors of each level (red being the only non-monochrome color in this game) it can be hard to see just how full your blood red health bar is. Overall I highly recommend this game even to people who don't traditionally play rougelikes or top-down shooters. You WILL have a good time, even in failure.

_childDocuments_.review: I've 100% both hotline miami games (not including genocide achievement because it sucks) and when my friend gifted me this game and told me it was inspired by hotline miami i gave it a whirl. It introduces a slowdown mechanic because, to put it roughly, it's your only advantage against the enemies because they are way stronger than you. And I thought to myself that "I've played enough hotline miami I can just blow through this game easy peasy maybe even without the slowdown" and I couldn't have been more wrong. OTXO advertises itself as a difficult game and it does not disappoint. It wasn't lying when it said that the enemies are stronger than you. I don't want to give too much away about how they are but that slowdown is necessary to play through OTXO and I don't believe you can beat the game without the slowdown. OTXO does have some progression but for the most part this game is entirely skill based. Each run you fail you only head back into the mansion with the knowledge you gained from your previous run and the skill you earned from it too. Not gonna cover the gameplay too much there's the slowdown and rolling and there's bosses but the trailer covers the gameplay well enough.My only somewhat of an issue with the game is is that unlocking new guns and abilities its tied to earning coins for your run so if you wanna unlock stuff permanently you would have to sacrifice coins for abilities for you run. One of them is permanently unlocking abilities to add to an ability pool for the shop to randomize from to sell to you. This part doesn't bother me in fact I'm alright with this part especially considering the ability you unlock permanently is applied for your run. It would be fine sacrificing temporary progression for permanent progression but some of the stuff you unlock are collectibles or new guns that can spawn in the mansion which is nice for diversity so you don't have the same weapons but it doesn't improve your odds of winning runs in the mansion as much as spending it on abilities to put it into the shop. It somewhat incentives doing runs to spend a lot of coins on unlocking this stuff and then doing later runs trying to beat the game by spending all your coin on shop abilities after you unlock everything.But don't let what I say earlier discourage you from playing this game I love the gameplay, the ost, the lore (the game doesn't force the lore upon you so it's optional if you wanna get into it), the story is very simple but it makes for a great game. Would definitely recommend to people.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine you're sitting on a park bench with a loved one when you notice a random passerby drop an unusual white mask on the ground. You reach down to grab the mask and return it to its owner, only to be suddenly overcome by an overwhelming urge to put it on. Once you do, you immediately black out - waking up on a strange beach with an eerie manor house looming in the distance.Making your way to the manor house, you meet the friendly Groundskeeper who explains your situation. Your task is simple, if not particularly easy - to get your loved one back, you must make your way through the manor and reach its Heart, killing anyone in your way. This is the premise of OTXO, a roguelike top-down shooter by Lateralis Heavy Industries.Whenever you have a top-down shooter with stylized graphics and cryptic storytelling, it's hard not to compare it to what is in my mind the pinnacle of the genre - Hotline Miami. However, these superficial features are about where the similarities between them end.For starters, OTXO is much more focused on the roguelike aspect of its gameplay. At the start of each run, the Bartender will offer you a choice of 3 free drinks. Each drink you choose offers a specific passive bonus, some of which can completely change your playstyle for that run.As you make your way through the run, the order of the manor sections (except the first one, which is always the Infinite Foyer), the layout of individual levels, and the placement of enemies are all randomized. Also, at random intervals between levels, you may return to the bar or enter a secret room. In the bar, you can spend coins gained by killing enemies to buy drinks or unlock new ones. Secret rooms offer short lore snippets and gacha machines, which award random weapon unlocks and collectibles for 250 coins a pop.The moment-to-moment gameplay favors quick thinking and lightning reflexes. Enemies are incredibly fast and perceptive, and they get even more so as you progress through the game. To even things out, you have Focus - the ability to slow down time, letting you take down entire groups of enemies at once, provided you're accurate enough.I found Focus to be a very interesting feature. On the one hand, it's a clear point of distinction from Hotline Miami, which is more focused on improvising and less on super-accurate gunplay. On the other, the deeper I got into the game, the more it looked like a stopgap measure to balance out the difficulty than a conscious design decision. It's almost as if, at some point, the devs realized that the enemies were too difficult, so they decided to even the odds by giving the player the ability to slow down time.As I already mentioned, OTXO is all about gunplay. The most basic and frequent type of enemy is just a guy with a gun, but the sheer number of available weapons they can carry makes it feel like you're fighting dozens of unique enemies per level. Each will drop their gun when defeated, and you're expected to pick them up frequently if you want to fight effectively and avoid running out of ammo. You can also kick enemies, which is sometimes the best way to handle fast-moving ones.Each section of the manor ends with a boss fight. Boss difficulty ranges from trivial, to soulslike (not that difficult once you figure out their movement patterns), to damn near impossible. In fact, the final boss is much easier to defeat than several preceding ones, another example of the game's flawed difficulty scaling.The best thing you can say about the presentation in OTXO is that it completely nails the vibe of the game. The pixel graphics are minimalist and sharp, in black, white, and red. The soundtrack is killer. The storytelling is cryptic and tinged with surreal horror elements. This is clearly the most thought-out aspect of the game and as a consequence, it raises the overall impression from something that could have been mediocre to a genuinely intriguing experience.Of course, not everything is perfect. I've already mentioned the odd difficulty curve a couple of times, and it gets to be a real problem in the late game. There are ways you can cheese the game (and you'll probably have to at some point) by kiting enemies with loud gunshots and then waiting to shoot them as they cross a corner. However, if you want to clear a full run, you'll need a near-perfect combination of drinks, weapons, and plain old luck, which doesn't leave a lot of room for developing skill and the feeling of accomplishment that comes with it.Ultimately, it feels like OTXO was built around a solid idea and a great soundtrack (which you can check out on the ), with the gameplay added around them to fill in the gaps. Even if it doesn't reach the same heights as Hotline Miami, it still offers an overall pretty solid experience for fans of roguelikes.

_childDocuments_.review: this game takes after HM2 emphasis on gunplay, soundtrack, storytelling and map design and revamps it in a roguelike of 40 segments, and while it does a fairly good job at it, i can't help but find it a bit lackluster and misleading, specially regarding featuresthe soundtrack is really well done and is a solid homage to el huervo and carpenter brut, what bothers me is there are like 5 songs for all the levels (not including boss themes, which are honestly very alike each other), and they can play over again once you reach a new area regarding replayabilitywhile this may seem true, and expanded in impossible mode, i've seen the same room, in the same order, multiple timesregarding atmosphere, OTXO does well creating a world of mystery and leaving little to nothing for the player to explore it, there are diary entries, occasional dialogue and gachapon machines that can give you minor lore details but thats it, you're supposed to feel like you're stuck in a dreamscape in which time doesn't seem to go on and people never leave, but that concept falls short when you realize you can finish the story in less than 40 minutes, when push comes to shove, the story is very well put together, its just not interesting enough to not be forgettablethere are lots of unlockables and for me its where replayability is at, its a very fun and solid game with very interesting features of its own, just don't expect it to be a spiritual sucessor to hotline miami

_childDocuments_.review: It's good. I like it and will keep playing it. There are some flaws and quibbles that make it ultimately "Hotline Miami at home", but hey, the food at home is good too sometimes. Above all, the sound design is great. The music's the pounding, aggressive, berserker-rage electronica you want for this kind of thing and the guns sound powerful and deadly and you want to use them simply because the crunch-BRRRRRRRRRRR-splatter of breaching a room and clearing it out is so damn satisfying. In general, the action is pretty well translated from the mostly melee-focused Hotline Miami concept where guns are a terrifying threat on the enemy and a Mario invincibility star to just delete a couple rooms full of guys while the ammo lasts when you have them, to a more power-fantasy action-movie style idea where everyone has guns and taking a few strays as you push through a hail of bullets is just part of feeling badass. If Hotline Miami is Dark Souls (punishing, puzzle-like analysis of the combat encounters, you're going to die, deal with it), this is Devil May Cry (still hard, but just surviving isn't as difficult - instead the challenge is more to do things fast and stylishly so that you have money to buy upgrades). That said, most of my issues come from the game seeming to not want to break far *enough* away from the HM games. I adore the narrative in those games, and in OTXO what feel like very perfunctory cryptic and weirdly hostile NPCs and journal entries you can read in the environment that have so far completely failed to add up to anything interesting - which leads me to believe that they're here less because there's a story that someone really wanted to tell and more because they were mimicking HM. Similarly, this game does the signature Hotline Miami "The music stops and you have to walk out of the level in silence" thing - but this is hugely thematic in HM, which is straightforward about one thing and one thing only: it wants you to think about how it's a bit weird and kind of messed up that it was just extremely fun to pretend to splatter two dozen guys' brains across their kitchen tile for reasons that are unclear to both your character and you. In OTXO, which is more or less unambiguously going "Whoa, cool gunfight!" (and to be clear, I have no problem with 'Whoa, cool gunfight!'), it's just a chore. Similarly, on the gameplay front, the fact that the combat is gun-driven leads to there being a larger fraction of weapons that are total duds and disappointing to see dropped. The game lets you disable any gun you don't want to see, but that's just admitting that you ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up in my book. Pretty much anything single-shot that doesn't instantly kill (bolt-action rifles, pistols and so on) is so ridiculously outclassed by insta-splatter shotguns and fully auto spray-and-pray options because they more or less require an expenditure of bullet time to aim correctly without getting ventilated by the enemy, who start shooting the exact frame they can see you at the max rate possible. Finally, the two options I've seen for the second boss fight are both okay if less interesting than just rooms full of dudes, but what appears to be the static first boss is an absolute chore that's genuinely less threatening than a room with three regular enemies in it. I have no idea what skill it's meant to be testing or what lesson about the gameplay it's supposed to teach, or generally how you could even get killed by it if you weren't trying to die. Maybe I'm being arrogant and he's necessary to ease in people who don't have 200 hours in the HM games, but I don't see how that could be the case when I found the levels leading up the boss significantly harder than the boss itself. All that complaining aside, this is still ultimately a recommend given the price. Despite some flab and imperfections around it, the core gameplay loop is very solid and there's that strong "Just one more run" feeling that any good roguelike should produce.

_childDocuments_.review: Ufff.  A great game if you're into dying over and over and over and getting precisely nowhere.  I'd give it a negative review if the game weren't so well made, but kudos to the developer, it's stylish, even if it's repetitive, too friggen hard and soul crushing. I tried.. I really did.  I got almost all of the "drinks" available by grinding and grinding.. But when I wanted to play the game properly, the RNG just never offered me good options, or affordable ones.  I was clearing levels with 4.5x, 5x and even 6x multipliers at one point, I was getting so much money, but the bar just always stocked 2 bad drinks and 1 mediocre which was out of my price range.  on ONE run out of dozens and dozens I got two useful drinks, but that got me to "The legionnaire" boss, and the fscking game had the cheek to say "Switch weapons more often to not die!" when I died.  In a boss fightthe one friggen game mechanic that's good (switching weapons) isn't available! Cheeky ♥♥♥♥!  Another time it said "Try hiding behind obstacles" when there's no obstacles in a boss fight, and another time it said "Use focus", when I got killed by a bomb by a boss, IN FOCUS... Grrr.  The game is for people with hundreds of hours to "git gud" (which in this case means learning the layouts and then grinding over and over until the RNG blesses you with some good buffs, but spending the intervening 90+ hours just doing the same thing over and over and over. Now, given that there are dozens and dozens of drinks, most of which are horse piss, it's really rare to get several good options in a single play, so you waste money on pointless trinkets, again grinding grinding grinding to get a gun that's good...  Meh.  This is a really well done game, but it suffers from the age old problem that the developer played it so much it became easy for them, so they ratcheted up the difficulty until it was hard for them, thinking "well, if it's hard for me, it'll be fun and hard for the players".. But that's like a friggen black belt choosing the hardest badass in the dojo, and when the white belts turn up for their first day of "fun karate", they get friggen pasted against the wall whle the other black belts with 100's of hours of time to practice sit like idiots on the side lines shouting "git gud", despite the kids just wanting to have fun and not make a bloody career out of it.  I mean, the game gives you a cool mechanic, focus, and then punishes you for using it by reducing your combos because you take longer.   So you have to take risks.. But again, it's russian roulette. You're probably going to die because either you took a risk, or you didn't take the risk and didn't get enough money for a good buff.... The only problem is that once again the dev has set the cooldown on the combos so crushing that you need ridiculously good reflexes.  The feeling of just sliding right down to the bottom and starting all over again is soul crushing.     The RNG is a pain in the nuts, you can't stack buffs between plays, so once you die, you might get three 'drinks' which are useless, and then you may as well quit and restart.  That's a hack recommended in the forums.  A word to the wise, if people say "Just quit and restart to get a different set of options", you're getting the RNG wrong, and people are finding workarounds for it.The music's great, and the action is fun. But if you have a limited amount of time to play, then this isn't the game for you. It takes a LONG time to get the hang of it, and to find what weapons work.  The RNG of the "drinks" means you can play a dozen games before you get a useful combination, and the drinks that actually buff you only do, like 10%, which is bollox.   The enemies have superhuman reflexes, so you really need the focus, but on later levels, there just isn't enough focus to clear a room, and you always end up being swarmed.  The enemies get tougher and more numerous, so eventually you find yourself swarmed and out of ammo.  If you can kick your way out, that's grand, but that's a sticking plaster cos you're near dead.  You can get lucky and run away, but if you're cornered, it's lights-out and back to square one with zero buffs.I'm sure if I had 100 hours+ with nothing else to play, I'd be able to get further, but right now, I can only get to the third boss who's a bullet sponge and despite learning his 'tells',  I run out off focus too quickly.   I just can't get any further and the game has no 'difficulty' slider.  It's just going to get harder and harder. I think I cleared 17 rooms on my best go, but it still wasn't enough.  So won't waste my time any more.  Give the game a friggen difficulty slider you cowards. Whatcha afraid of? Losing your "hard game=cool" credentials?   Pfft.  Hopefully someone's done a mod to add a less brutal level of difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the Hotline Miami duology there was only one thought in my mind; "I want more of *this*". Otxo was the answer to my prayers, but in spite of that similarity it is an incredibly great game on it's own mileage.Gameplay is at Otxo's forefront, with incredibly stylish and intuitive top-down shooter mechanics that allow you to easily fall into it's flow of combat. Combined with it's refined rogue-lite mechanics, the action is only enhanced by your accumulation of creative perks and abilities. The selection is always random every time, which means that every new run is an opportunity to try another build, and the player agency it gives is amazing. Whether it be the tried-and-true high-DPS and high-HP builds or the more experimental abilities, I found that there was plenty of fun to be had on every single run. Otxo's setting is also very well-done, although only initially. All the plot really has going for it is its intriguing premise, the rest feeling a bit on the shallow, uncompelling side. That being said, all the other elements are simply stellar. Enemies, areas, and bosses alike are all really inspired in both their designs, gameplay elements and it always felt like I had to adapt myself to each one. Some levels allow for high-combos and frenetic action, but the later ones would force you to be patient under threat of being overwhelmed. It just works together really nicely.All in all, Otxo is just a relentlessly action-packed shooter experience that excels in creating a truly random-feeling roguelite experience. Fans of Hotline Miami and other similar games will no doubt find a lot of joy in this game and it's brilliantly innovative take on a classic formula.

_childDocuments_.review: The aggressive, straight forward music perfectly fits to the game's overall style of bloodlust and insanity. Together with the loud, distorted sound design it creates a badass harmony of violence, that scratches all the right spots.The gameplay, once you get the hang of it, feels just right - challening, but just the more rewarding because of that. Every single kill, every room you clear, every stage, boss, feels perfectly satisfying, and as you get better, you get further in your runs, get more creative with your kills, and the satisfaction never stops.Every mechanic, and even some hints, are embedded in the lore in some way, without seeming out of place, leaving you completely immersed in a world that actually feels finished, makes sense (for how bizarre it is), and is nicely glued together.With the roguelite elements, the game is highly replayable, each time with different weapons and perks, allowing to play for hours on end, without ever having to worry to get bored.Overall, 10/10.A shame I didn't know about this game in time for the 2023 awards.

_childDocuments_.review: Would recommend OTXO. super intense gameplay, very little slack. Even littler annoyance, Good game.But there's to be said about it, is there? I discovered OTXO from a video from Raycevick and saw that he also Played SYNTHETIK, and immediately bought it on his recommendation. OTXO is a twin-stick, top-down shooter featuring High speed ultraviolence. Most others liken it to Hotline Miami, but I have never played any of the Hotline Miami games. Which OTXO is said to pull the most from. Going in, my only frame of reference is entirely SYNTHETIK, another top-down twin-stick shooter Featuring High speed Ultraviolence. So if you haven't played SYNTHETIK then a large amount of this review is going to not make sense for you, I really recommend you do though, as I like to see both games as a pair, shifting to one or the other depending on which speed I want to go at. playing both has given me insights into the other. What I'm trying to say is that they go together like PB and J. If you like one of these games then you will like the other. And I will review OTXO as such.One of the immediate differences between the two games is that OTXO has Friendly NPCs that you can talk to, and by extension a story. SYNTHETIK”s by contrast only has a weedly little Preamble before the subsequent 100 hours of android stomping action. That’s not a negative thing by the way, less time between playing and not playing and in both its entirely ignorable. But I appreciate the move by OTXO to have one. And it's probably interesting or something But I still mostly ignored it though because of one thing: It's only told through tiny lore scraps and uncommon dialogue. I've just kinda gotten burnt out on this way of storytelling after the other dozen times of games and media trying to start speculation on vague lore and no good hooks outside of being mysterious. I think it has some good examples of this. But I've come to really crave stories that have some, if not most of the characters who have their plot on screen, instead of being on a note or something, ditto for world building. I don't want to watch a youtube video or a fan-wiki to understand a story.. I just don't want to put in the effort to remember every little scrap of lore anymore. Maybe the final boss clears everything up. But I haven't gotten to it yet. It might sound cruel, but I kinda wish OTXO had a nothing-burger story like SYNTHETIK without the possibility that anything has happened that I don't know about. But this is coming from a place of personal preference, and as I'm writing this I just don’t have tastebuds for how OTXO tells its story.OTXO is incredible in its gameplay though. Which, like SYNTHETIK, is what I'm mainly here for. Truly incredible in every way I can say besides incredibly bad. It is fast, vicious, and kinetic, but it is also incredibly difficult. A dozen hours in and hundreds of hours in a similar game and I still haven't beat the final boss once, or have even seen them. All the other bosses feel so tough that besides the inbred basilisk it still feels like a coin flip between whether or not I'll defeat them. The  Enemies become so numerous and crazy in the later levels that they too feel like an inevitable defeat. But I wouldn't call OTXO overly wrote with its difficulty. I have reason to think that my overreliance on SYNTHETIK’s items and class perks is what causes it to feel so hard for me. OTXO’s equivalent of items (Drinks) have felt weaker on average than what SYNTHETIK’s items already were to the roguelike average. Your only two X-factors over the enemies is your focus (slow time) and some extra health, where in SYNTHETIK you had access to weapons and abilities that very few, to none of the enemies had. This gives OTXO an extreme reliance on its weapons to carry you through the fight, overall there is no number gaming at all in OTXO so it's on you to use each of the weapons to their fullest to get the most out of its combat. All weapons feel good and work great besides the single shot pistols which I never seem to be able to hit with when it counts. The mechanic with the nun is super interesting, like the supply points  in SYNTHETIK but only exclusionary. The dodge roll is also kinda good, but i suspect not using it might be the number one reason i'm losing so much, it's just never clicked that I should be using it more running at the opponents and using cover just seems like so much more useful the rolling at or away from the enemy and getting hit anyways. Same feeling on vaulting is just so niche that furniture is going to be in the exact spot where it is helpful to use over-activating focus to dodge bullets. All of these things I bring up about OTXO aren’t deal breakers by the way. The main gameplay loop is extremely good and well thought out, I really just wanted to highlight some of the very rare annoyances for a more full picture of the game.Is OTXO worth fifteen dollars or less? Its Extremely worth it. But It's a game you can play forever but it is not a game you can play forever. It can become grating when playing for more than an hour or two. It just goes so fast that I end up wanting to play a slower paced game after I'm done playing. This is not a demark, it’s just that OTXO is so good at what it achieves that it needs to be spaced out between other activities. Even if I still prefer SYNTHETIK over OTXO, OTXO is still a strong experience that's worth my time and my money.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;dr: Awesome soundtrack, excellent combat loop, if you liked Hotline Miami, this is a must buy/play.   Hotline Miami was a game that used violence to illustrate the sickening dissonance of violence against living beings in video games and positive reinforcement via scorestreaks, flickering lights, etc. It wanted people to crave and receive dopamine from the brutal murder of other humans. The problem, is that they did a really good job of making it fun.    Otxo wears its top down twin stick room clearing shooter inspiration on its sleeve. It is an improvement over the Hotline Miami combat loop in many ways. And the music is just as phenomenal. The difficulty is a tradeoff in this game, you do not die in one hit but it is a RougeLITE. Which means if and when you die, you must restart the game, and keep ZERO progression. The only thing preventing you from completing the game, is skill and knowledge.    If you're on the fence about buying this game, I implore you to go to spotify and listen to the soundtrack. If it makes you want to violently murder pixelated enemies, then you're going to like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: While inspired on the surface by Hotline Miami, this game adopts the combat and mask effects into a roguelite formula very well while also tweaking the gunplay and traversal of levels to fix the numerous small but impactful flaws with Hotline Miami 2's gameplay loop. Never again will doors block your bullets when you don't expect them to, because they are now only ever "Closed and locked" or "Broken" with no flung-open in-between. Never again will off-screen shotgunners blast you and instantly kill you. The camera system chooses a midpoint between your crosshair and your character, obviating Hotline Miami's use of the Shift-look system, and the health system means it's unlikely that a single shotgun pellet or two from across the map is powerful enough to kill your character.Tired of having trouble switching between a gun and a melee weapon as enemies close in on your position? In OTXO, you are able to kick with middle mouse button at any time, and the kick kills enemies instantly. No knockdown, no execution required, just an instant kill."Mask effects" are superceeded by liquor effects, which you can combine, mix, and match to your hearts content with each run. However, to purchase liquor, you use money dropped by the enemies. The kicker is, you get a combo multiplier if you kill a lot of enemies very quickly and aggressively, and this combo multiplier directly increases how much money the enemies drop when killed. So, these three pillars of liquor, money, and combo multiplier combine to emulate aspects of Hotline Miami's stylish gameplay and unique mask effects, but also go beyond it by providing an in-game motive to fight like hell rather than just an end-screen score that can be cheesed with a boring power drill for executions.The story is alright I guess, nothing like Hotline Miami, but it gets the job done and leaves you wondering more about the mansion while you absorb some lore.If you liked Hotline Miami's gunplay and wished it was a little more refined, you'll love this game. If you liked the melee combat and runs in Hotline Miami, you'll be a little disappointed by the lack of melee weapons, but will find that the kick is a fun and adequate stand-in for that gameplay style (though I miss the sheer aesthetic of running around with a knife or a baseball bat). If you've never played Hotline Miami, you'll really love this game nonetheless.This is the only "bullet hell" type of top down roguelike shooter that not only hooked me in, but actually got me to beat it.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't review every good game, so I've resolved to only write about those which I personally find special.  This is one.OTXO☐ Universal must-try☐ Subjective favorite of mine☐ Captivating ambience☐ Exceptional narrative☐ Exceptional characters☐ Meaningful player freedom☐ An ability to bring friends together plays faster than you can think.  This is a good thing.  Like many rogue-likes, “progression” is about player skill more than unlocks.  So in this game, getting good is a matter of developing the right instincts and reactions.  And once you get there, it feels .Controls respond fast, guns shoot fast, enemies die fast, and so do you.  When you need extra time to think—which you will—focus mode slows time.  And it’s limited, so you better figure out your mess before your focus runs out.I’ve never played , but the crisp gunplay and, well, crisp everything in this game makes me understand why people are fans.While you play, there is an invisible force pushing you forward and lending weight to everything you do.  That force is the sound design.While the soundtrack plays, you have no other option but forward.  It goes that hard.  Guns have punch and power; I genuinely think they sound better than most AAA titles.  And the rush of it all—there really is a rush—has made me laugh out loud after clearing a level.  More than once. is nuts. proves that an outstanding game needs only two things: gameplay and style, nothing more.  It refines these and wastes little time elsewhere.As is typical of the genre, there are items (”drinks”) you accumulate during a run and some meta-progression to accumulate over all your runs.  These are done well, in my opinion.  To be frank, however, they’re secondary.The mechanics and presentation in this game mix into a cocktail that is best injected directly into your veins.

_childDocuments_.review: Been itching for something that plays like Hotline Miami for a while and this scratches that itch. Combat is quick and brutal with a large amount of weapons to pick up from your victims, but is more forgiving than Hotline in the fact it takes a bit to kill you, you can temporarily slow time, and you can get a collection of power-ups to help out. Enemies are diverse enough and boss fights are challenging but not ridiculous. The world building/lore is kind of interesting too. It tries to instill a sense of hopelessness through not only its difficulty, but through its dialogue, readable pickups, and drab collar palate as well. Players looking for something similar to Hotline might be turned off by the rogue-lite features of the game but as a fan of the genre it is really cool to see how this kind of gameplay can be adapted for it.

_childDocuments_.review: While there was initial difficulty in getting a feel for the controls, rebinding everything to a more natural feel made this game a lot smoother and achieved the constant surging of adrenaline that the game is intending to achieve. It's not an overstatement to say that this game is "faster than Hotline Miami", though comparing the two is probably a fruitless task, as OTXO creates its own identity by removing that planning phase in which you try to figure out the optimal movement strategy for the rooms and enemies, and instead primarily has you winging it, and picking whichever door is best at the moment. Luckily, enemies don't hear through doors too, which might be for better or for worse, as for the most part, you'll know exactly what you're in for when you force an engagement. Most of the improvising thus comes from fixing your own mistakes- where you run out of bullets midfight, or can't find a weapon, or didn't account for a particular pillar/obstacle when trying to run away. And while there's a lot more leeway in OTXO  than in something like Hotline Miami as a result of it's health system, it's definitely needed when bullets are essentially real-time. But that doesn't stop that fun panicking you feel when you start getting pelted with bullets, and your health is diminishing. The perk system is also nice- mostly notable changes that, while add up over time, don't make things too overpowered. Ideal for this kind of game, where the gameplay loop necessitates constant danger and awareness. I think the main flaw of this game is ultimately repetitition, though- which is primarily an issue depending on how you play the game. I personally believe that if you approach this game with the mindset of consistently going with the flow, and only taking some time to strategize, this game becomes something special- but less so the more and more you hard-optimize it. But of course, this is a roguelite. You naturally will get better at the game, and figure out the nuances to make each run more and more perfect, which is fine. But I personally would say to not think about it too hard. Just keep trying and improving alongside the flow of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a magnificent combination of a lot of different stuff- so let me break it down:- Roguelike with tons of action. There are some progress elements like buying new drinks and new weapons, but every time you die you start at the beginning.- One of the best OSTs I've heard in a long time. It rivals even Doom Eternal and Rebel Galaxy. (in my opinion)- An intriguing story 'hell' bent on NOT letting you finish it.- The guns actually have a FEEL to them and aren't just sticks making sounds.- The overall sound design from the firearms rapport to even kicking in a door is just brutal and gives you a feeling of... well... brutality.- The NPCs aren't too bad but could have a little more depth to them. (To be fair, I feel like this also could just be the point. They are trapped in the mansion and have been for who-knows-how-long and seem to have given up hope on anything save you) However, the main NPCs you'll be 'meeting' with are hostile.- The enemies CAN and WILL end you and send you all the way back! By this I mean that you're no more powerful than the enemies, save your 'special' ability you get from the mask.- Influences from classic games such as Hotline Miami and movies like John Wick. (I didn't really want to mention these since literally everyone knows that that game and movie were influences to OTXO, but I feel like I should include everything I've experienced and noticed.)- The beginning tutorial is kind of 'meh' but it does do it's job of teaching you how to play the game.- The combat is fantastic and really makes you feel like you're achieving something whenever you clear a room. However, at the same time it still has this sense of danger whenever you mess up or make a wrong descision...- The kick is an instakill (yes I know it's kind of a spoiler, but shhhh) which means even if you run out of ammo (which could only be your fault, mind you) you can still risk it and splatter someone with a superhero kick to steal their weapon.- While this is one of the gripes I have, I think it's weird that enemies can't open doors.-- On the same token, while I also find it weird you can only open doors by kicking them to pieces, I guess it makes sense since you're an action-hero archetype like John Wick (I know I mentioned it again, sue me) or the protagonist of Hotline Miami (you should've expected this connection) Or really just any action movie... Heck, even the Matrix is more than likely an influence!Needless to say, if you don't mind roguelikes and love action games- or maybe you just really like slaughtering groups of enemies with overwhelming power- or maybe you just like the looks of the game- I would HIGHLY recommend you buy this. It's a great game with a banger soundtrack that is sure to be a hit at rave parties or firefights equally!

_childDocuments_.review: *insert review comparing Otxo to Hotline Miami*.Jokes aside, this is a great rogue-lite shooter with some of the most stylish and brutally satisfying gameplay I've seen since Hotline Miami 2. Make no mistake though, Otxo is not trying to be a clone of those games, there are a considerable amount of things that this game does to set itself apart from the rest, such as the randomly generated levels and enemy placements, all the different enemy types, the focus (bullet time) mechanic etc.What this game does really well however are the rogue-lite mechanics. The liquers that act as your abilities throughout the course of your run are implemented in a similar way to other games in the rogue-lite genre such as Hades, with a huge number of abilities that can be mixed and matched to create a variety of builds. The only drawback of this system is that Otxo doesn't really allow the same sort of creativity in builds as a game such as Hades does, which could leave some of your runs feeling very similar to each other, but nevertheless I'm still glad that it's included.Overall, this game rocks in spite of the few criticisms I have with it and I highly recommend it to anyone who is feeling that Hotline Miami itch.

_childDocuments_.review: If you played Hotline Miami and thought ''Man, this game isn't punishing me enough'' then OTXO will gladly beat you down and spit on you until it deems you worthy. Making the mistake of breaking the front door and casually meandering inside one of the rooms will leave you surprised. Your adversaries in these halls of the proverbial baroque mansion have their heads on a swivel, will not hesitate to immediately open fire the second they spot you, and will exploit every single mistake you make to send you back to the beach. The mansion might have lured you in its hellish realm with temptation like a mere wild beast, but the wolf will eventually present its fangs. The more you try again, the more the estate moulds you into a vicious killer. The myriads of weapons previously fired towards you become your partners, the deafening sounds of their discharge melds with the incredible soundtrack, and the brutal combat becomes an elegant dance between you, your opponents, and their bullets.All in all an incredible, very inspired game which lets you fill the gaps of its mysterious setting with your imagination, and one that makes you feel like a complete badass.
