_childDocuments_.review: ***Some light gameplay spoilers belowAt first, this game was a "slightly positive" experience for me. The song style used in the first world (pop-based) was good enough to get me through all of it, but the difficulty of the game was largely lacking. But when I finally reached the last level in the first world - my feelings changed a lot. The song had a very driving beat and enemies were spawning left and right - the game finally showed what it can truly be, and that's when I got hooked. Chasing that adrenaline rush has kept me going; I'm currently on World 7 and having a lot of fun.Addressing some concerns I keep seeing about the game:"It's too repetitive."Aren't all rhythm based games repetitive? DDR, Guitar Hero, all 1000 Rock Bands, Thumper, Amplitude, Crypt of The Necrodancer, Rhythm Doctor,  - the list goes on. All of these are the same thing over and over and over again to different songs. As you progress through any of these games, the difficulty slowly goes up by adding new buttons to press or more notes coming at you, but the core of the game remains largely the same. Soundfall is no different (and that's not a bad thing); the game is you shooting in rhythm at enemies and trying not to die. As you progress, the number of enemies that appear increases and tankier/stronger variants of them make your game harder. The looting aspect of the game helps break up the repetitiveness of playing songs back-to-back and having different characters to choose from is nice too (more on the characters later)."Song choices aren't good for a rhythm game."I agree with this to some degree - World 3 was an absolutely miserable experience for me. However, this is when I learned about the "Metronome" setting that makes a ticking noise play on every single beat. This helped me get through the slower songs and the songs with no definitive beat. I know I shouldn't have to rely on such a function in a RHYTHM GAME, but I'm glad it was included. Even though I agree with the statement above, I really appreciate the diversity of songs that this game has. Every world has a theme to it, and each world has 10 songs plus 3-4 bonus songs that deviate from the present style. I'm currently on World 7 (out of 8 Worlds, I think). That's a lot of damn songs for a $30 dollar rhythm game, and there's a style out there for everyone (World 5 is the best, fight me).Now, for my wishlist in future patches:- Give us a retry button when I pause the game. I shouldn't have to completely leave a song and reload it to try it again, especially with how steep the difficulty is for the top medal/award.- Give us the option to change the "metronome" sound. I'd love to have something that has more base to it rather than this annoying tick. Default options should include, the annoying tick, an actual metronome click, a bass drum, and a clap noise. I think that would help cover all the different styles of music in this game.- Please bring a little more depth into the equipment. Let us craft/merge weapons together. I would love to be able to move attributes from one gun to another. Customizing weapons (at the cost of gold or something), would make the equipment portion of this game amazing.- Let us play uploaded songs with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a huge laundry list of complaints about this game my friends and I made, but that was a lot of work for a product that mostly disappointed me. Just take these points away:- If you came here for a rhythm game, you are actually getting a metronome player over top of music not well selected for a rhythm game and sound effects that are extremely distracting. You only get to play 4/4 or 3/4 quarter notes for basically the entire game.- If you came here for a looter shooter, you are never going to get a satisfying enough amount of loot. You will get 1-3 pieces of loot average per song and they will almost always be irrelevant to you or the gear in the store will be better than it. Also all the loot you get does not truly change the way you are playing in any meaningful capacity.- If you came here for a twin-stick shooter, you will actually find this to be an ok game. However it is bogged down by everything else attached to it. (And too many stationary turret type enemies for my taste)The animated scenes are nice and the graphics are decent. The story is full of cheesey puns that I love but it feels like a gacha game story before the writers realize the game is popular.It was fun for about 3-4 hours then the rest of the time I spent playing it felt more like a slog. I think there was a lot of potential for this idea overall but feel that none of it was executed well enough to keep me playing or recommend this to any of my friends. I did discover a couple new music artists that I like inside so that was nice at least. I doubt I will ever look back at this game again, even if it is well updated, due to the core rhythm gameplay being turning you into a perfect metronome.

_childDocuments_.review: I would love to say that this is one of the most innovative rhythm-type games out there, but has certain problems with the game mechanics itself.1. There's no clear indication of whether the beats get faster or slower. The only indication is the lower beat-indicator which isn't easy to read when you concentrate on tricky enemies2. The game demands you to position yourself for a clean dodge(as enemies can hit you in late off-beats even after an on-beat dodge)3. Some of the colors of enemy projectiles can be almost hidden by your own projectile/action4. Most of the missions don't let you get hidden chests if you wish to want a rank above silver(song ends too quick for you to reach far-away chests), sometimes not even a single item besides the final one.It is surely a good game, and I enjoy it a lot.But there are some loose ends here and there that might knock you over from time to time.

_childDocuments_.review: A rhythm game that never progresses beyond the baseline. The entire time I played, even with greater "intensities" I clicked the same monotonous pattern, but sometimes faster or slower depending on the BPM, regardless of the movement of the actual music. Now that I think about it, the player is just a glorified metronome. It doesn't help that the enemies do not follow the music at all and attack whenever and if its off-beat, get ♥♥♥♥♥♥.Also, missing too many notes complete disables your attack and the ultimate has endlag without iframes.In a good rhythm game, if you turn off the music you should be able to hear the song as you do the inputs. Play rhythm heaven, elite beat agents, muse dash, or crypt of the necrodancer instead.

_childDocuments_.review: i think the game is pretty good. however...it does have flaws that can affect experience playing itthe gameplay, the animations, the different characters, weapons, playstyles, feel right ultimately, they feel pretty solid as far as rhythm games go. i do like how this game lets you add in your own songs and play them.however...that has it's issues.the different music is categorized with different stages, each more or less set for specific genres of music. at times, it works fine and as intended. but other times?the music despite being a different genre can tend to get lumped in with the same kinds of stages, making the custom soundtrack gameplay feel same-y. most of the music regardless of what i added either gave me Cityscape or Volcano.not just that, but the inputs can end up being synched off, or moving waay too fast, disregarding the song's actual tempo. essentailly the game AI-Generates what it thinks you'll play too. that wouldn't be much of a problem if the game allowed players to review the pacing/timing for inputs, and had a way to arrange different stages for songs that don't work/fit with the one it's stuck with.that said however, the game does have promise. the songs that've come with the game are varied and keeping in beat with them isn't all that hard. the different loot having stats like healing, or extra dashes adds to the gameplay experience. and the special weapons have variety to them to suit different people's playstyles.ultimately? it's a competent game, but if you're going in specifically to add your own music and play it, be aware that this game's system is flawed in that regard.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: I think Soundfall is an OKAY rhythm game, but compared to EXCELLENT rhythm games, like Just Shapes and Beats (more-interesting challenges), and Sayonara Wild Hearts (more-interesting aesthetics and story), I don't think I'd recommend Soundfall.---I'm not sure what the value-add is for grinding level-ups & equipment in a rhythm game. Grinding can be useful in games to accommodate different skill levels, but some difficulty settings would probably be just as effective (and there's already a ranking system for people who want to demonstrate expert play). I think an equipment system with bigger, more-discrete bonuses - like Crypt of the Necrodancer's - would be a better fit for this kind of game. Soundfall's equipment system feels more tedious than useful.The gameplay itself wasn't that interesting to me. The world moving to the beat is fun, but Soundfall's combat feels boring compared to Hi-Fi Rush's, for example.Finally, I found the writing to be kind of annoying; very low-budget-Saturday-morning-cartoon-y, both in terms of plot, and in how everything has to have a "thematic" name. To be fair, this is not a game-killer on its own: I'm happy to ignore the terrible writing of most Sonic games, for example, because most Sonic games are joyous to play. But Soundfall was not joyous to play, so the bad writing stood out even more.There's a lot of good polish in this game that shows the devs really cared - UI, quality of graphics and animations, generous timing windows for some world traversal, and the inclusion of multiplayer are all great - but when I look at games that spent less time on UI and graphics but came out better overall (Just Shapes and Beats!), it's hard to recommend Soundfall.

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright. Probably more fun with friends, as im playing solo. About mid way through the 2nd area and only enjoyed about 2 or 3 of the songs so far. The goals to 100% a level are a tad absurd. _childDocuments_.review: 08/27/2023 EDIT: After going through my library and stumbling across this game again, I decided to do a little research. Back in May of 2022, a news article was posted about creating one's own beatmaps. This is, honestly, insulting. This is akin to the dev saying "We're aware there's beat detection issues, but we're not going to fix it. Fix it yourselves." As much as knowing how to make custom beatmaps is nice if the game could properly handle automatic generation, it comes across more as insulting in a "complete" state. I was considering giving the game a more thorough second chance, but not after this.ORIGINAL REVIEW:Bought this game specifically for "Free Mode" (song import) and now I deeply regret it.In terms of the included soundtrack, beat detection is "acceptable" if you can successfully calibrate your display and audio device (which took more than two hours of testing, invalidating refunds), though the extremely eclectic song selection includes a number of off-beat songs that really do not play well with the presumably hand-tuned beat rates no matter what you do.Free Mode, however, is a mess. I've had a static BPM chiptune MP3 start at 4x beat speed, then ~30 seconds in suddenly drop to something resembling what  be acceptable if it were actually on beat, then fluctuate wildly throughout the remainder of the song. Meanwhile, when loading a lossless FLAC of an epic metal track with variable BPM across its movements, the analysis sticks to a single beat rate that only matches about 1/3 of the total song; that's when a FLAC even loads, as anything over a certain size threshold (not fully tested, but LONG FLACs with sizes in the range of 16 minutes / 200 MB freeze the analysis and require force-closing the game to exit). And to top it all off, "for legal reasons" imported songs do not support online multiplayer even if all players have legally-acquired (Bandcamp IS a thing, you know), hash-matched copies of the same song.I can't recommend this game in its current state. It's luck of the draw when calibrating your devices, Story Mode is passable, but Free Mode is in a generally unplayable state; if this were a minor or post-release feature this could be excused, but this is a store page advertised major feature. If this is ever improved, I'll gladly change this review. But for now, I recommend rhythm game seekers pass up this one and instead spend on Beat Hazard 1/2/3, Melody's Escape 1/2, or Metal Hellsinger instead.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this isn't a rhythm game. There are no rhythms in this game, there is only the "pulse" or raw bpm of songs. It is however a game about keeping to the beat. You press the attack button on every beat, even while there are no enemies around because why not.The game has a tedious leveling and gearing system which serves no purpose. I've played 5 hours and I've already experienced all/most songs. The enemies attack patterns does get faster at higher difficulties, but I just don't think the grind is worth it.In a real rhythm game the only way to progress is to improve as a player. Here, it's mainly about how much you grind. And honestly, why should you grind in a solo player game you've already experienced all the content in? It just doesn't make sense to keep playing after you've beat all the songs.In conclusion, this game has a broken progression system which offers little incentive to keep playing.

_childDocuments_.review: (game complete review at 11.6 hours) (short version)All in all I hate saying no to this game I did have fun but I wouldn't suggest my friends buy it for $30.(long version)This is another game I wish there was a 'maybe' button for steam the tipping point for the 'no' review is the price point.Positive factors: The animation cut scenes are well animated.The shooter aspect of this game stays consistently fun with a new trap design showing it's ugly head at each new biome.The music is unique and not repeated during 100 stages of game play.Negative factors:$30 is too much for this game in my opinion, I would wait for it to be on sale for $20 which I think is a fairer price point.Stages repeat... Often, especially when you get closer to the end the snow peaks area repeated the same stage 7 times (at least) this makes game play tedious at times and you can tell the developers were having a rough time near the end.For a looter shooter there is a lot of shooter but the loot is not generously distributed, there is a store but it's rare you'll find what you want/need. To put it in perspective there are 5 elements, at least 5 weapon types, 5 heroes (special weapons),  5 gear slots, and 5 quality levels for each item.  With this many options and you receiving on average 1-2 usually white quality items you're very reliant on the RNG gods by the end of the game, and for most of it you feel underwhelmed.  That is one thing I'd love to see patched would be the drop rate improved by 15-20% games like this / borderlands are fun because of the insane combinations you create with the items received.The game is listed as split screen co-op but when I invited my wife to play on our LAN it sent her to the store page.  The other thing I'd recommend patching is the remote play together capability.  I'm 100% confident this game is 80% more fun to play with friends.Lastly, the end stage goals seem to be game tested by a beta tester who was fully leveled out wearing full legendary items for each stage they cleared.  I don't remember the exact specifics to get the platinum trophy, I think it is not missing a beat, getting at least one extra treasure, and clearing before the song resets.  However, on many of these stages the song often resets even if you're making a b-line to the end goal not to mention doing your best to not be hit (missing a beat) or missing a beat while walking/firing/dodging.  In my personal opinion if you have a trophy system it should be able to be accomplished for w/e level that shows up there initially.  To get even the gold trophy it seems like soundfall was expecting a lot of players to run new game+.  For me I would have much more fun achieving possible goals upon arrival than thinking "well if I play 80 more hours I'll be able to get the 1-1 platinum achievement".  A good model to follow for trophies would be super Mario 3d world where the end stage trophies are skill based vs equipment/level/skill based.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually leave reviews but I think this game is really fun and has a lot of potential, but there are a few things holding me back. Most of my criticism is around the use of imported songs from your own library. The game analyzes the overall BPM more than the beat for individual parts- so there are times when the beat does not necessarily match up with the song. I wouldn't mind waiting longer for the game to analyze a song for a more accurate beatmap to be generated. Maybe it can even be done in the background while you play other songs. Also, not allowing custom songs for online play is a real downside since I want to play them with an online friend.I'm not someone who plays for the story, I'm just here for fun. But I do hope to see hard end-game content that makes it more beneficial to grind out gear. Additionally, it's really hard to see what type the monsters will be before going into a song. And even when I'm playing, I still don't know what type they are.That being said, I think I would recommend this game to someone if they don't mind playing bare-bones rhythm games. The default songs are, IMO, kinda soulless but it's not like they can get popular bands on this without spending too much of licensing fees. Definitely do not pay $30. I bought this for $5 and I think that's honestly the highest I would pay for it in it's current state. Wait for a sale.So, yes, I recommend this game. But with the caveat that it has a lot of growing to do if it ever wants to be worth the $30 price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: What a mess...Nothing in this game is making any sense. Devs did their best into making any song playable, never even questioning if they should have in the first place.The result is what we see right there. The whole game has no soul. Levels aren't fun to play, enemy archetypes are ranging from "These won't ever hit you" to "One frame reaction at 240BPM", and the whole setlist is poorly selected -not saying these aren't good, most of them are. They just don't belong in a rhythm game. Why you may ask? Well, let's take a look at Ownage from Frank Klepacki. Great song, nothing to say about this. Sadly, the song is straight up unplayable. BPM changes, AI deciding that the drum breaks are actual beats and screwing up the beat recognition, more BPM changes, resulting in a Platinum medal impossible to attain without grinding the same level over and over.If you think I'm being picky, take a look at ANY song from World 2 or 3. Orchestral songs, in a rhythm game based only on beat recognition? Really?I could rant for a lot more, but this is not the point. If I'm writing this review, it's because I strongly believe that this game has a lot of potential. So, instead of beating the game's corpse, here's some ideas you may want to take into consideration:- . Fixed songs. Fixed levels. Give some soul to the game, levels that were carefully crafted to fit the song you want to immerse players in. Is the song length an issue because players are not completing arenas at the same pace? Why not selecting a specific part of the song, making it loop until the arena is completed, then progress through the rest? Metal: Hellsinger does this, and it's perfect.- . Some attacks can't be dodged on beat (the best example would be towers from World 4). Why aren't ALL enemy attacks on beat? Some of them already are. Quite unfortunate to not polish them all with the same care.- . I was bored really fast, there are too many levels, too many songs, none have an identity. Dropped the game on World 4, still don't understand how to get better gear other than grinding my account level. Streamlining all of this and making it user-friendly would help with retention.On a sidenote with this point, your game's difficulty right now is just the BPM. That's fine if it's your choice, however... could you please not throw players a 250BPM song on World two out of TEN? Again, player progression.- . The final level of each stage is... a single arena? Why? Two to three arenas like that back to back would make for a great level in this type of game, yet, finishing a world doesn't feel satisfying at all.I would've preferred to like that game, really. The world and animations are quite good. A rhythm game looter shooter sounds fun on paper, but the result really isn't.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game based completely around music, visual design is a huge part of Soundfall's charm. Everything is bright, colorful, and surprisingly pleasant considering you'll be spending all of your time in Symphonia dodging and returning fire. But then, this may also be due to everything - from enemies to set pieces to you yourself - bopping along to the beat. So its music is apparently just as infectious as its art style, and would have to be as any off-beat action is largely ineffective. That is not to say rhythm novices like myself are completely out of luck. Amongst the wide variety of weapons and armor available to collect are plenty that soften the already gentle penalty for missing the beat. Keeping the difficulty down with the aptly named “Warm Up” mode will leave some of the more shooter-based pressure to stay on tempo at a minimum, but as the level of difficulty restricts the level of gear that will drop, that's no permanent solution either. Still, as an aforementioned rhythm challenged individual myself, I was able to use Soundfall's leniency - and its built in metronome - to learn and grow into the rest of what this game has to offer. The main source of the variety Soundfall has in-store is in the world of Symphonia itself. There are ten different biomes that give off a different vibe along with music tailored to suit that theme. This element of progression is more set dressing than an actual change in the state of play with the real flavor being the increasing diversity of Discordians marching against you. There are only a handful of categories, most of which debut before the halfway point, but those base forms give rise to their own alterations in later missions: for example one enemy type charges for a few beats and then fires off a sort of sniper shot, but as you progress, you'll find some will fire off a triple split shot or a triple sized shot. All of which are perfectly telegraphed with arrows showing where the charging shot is aimed for, adjusting those warnings until firing. This design philosophy is what makes the other type of escalating hazard variety, traps, as equally fair and fun as the enemies themselves. But danger isn't the only way Soundfall shakes it up. The wide variety of equipment with an equally diverse set of randomly selected modifiers and the musical genre affinities with their own distinct traits offer the majority of the game's customization opportunities. In practice, these equipment choices are much like the available character choices: each play just similarly enough to avoid knocking off your flow when switching between them while still having strong enough individual quirks to feel like a totally different approach. The game's story follows this same aesthetic by having the oh so different members of your new quintet working through their little quirks together in a way that feels a lot like a Saturday-morning cartoon: any conflict is simple, clean, and gets solved over the course of a single set of missions. The still images and plain text it's told through do add a little flavor and context between missions, but also leave the storytelling feeling a bit like an afterthought. Not that it'll demand your focus, you'll be far too busy harmonizing the unending forces of Discord by keeping the beat, which is perhaps the most child-friendly way a bullet hell game has ever been described.

_childDocuments_.review: Not outright terrible, but just not that good either.It's an interesting concept, fusing rhythm gaming with other genre's, but in this case the two really just don't meld well.The rhythm game part isn't very satisfying and becomes really quite tedious with each level.More importantly I never really felt 'satisfied' while playing. Never felt like I was getting into a flow-state, chaining attacks, dodges, skills, or anything like that. Most of the gameplay is just backing away from enemies and occasionally dodging an attack that you can't walk around or away from.The 'looter shooter/dungeon crawler' part is pretty lackluster and shallow as well. with fairly limited gear options whose primary distinction is the value of their primary stat and not much else. Even with the weapons there's really only a small handful, none of which really do anything particularly interesting and are just each a slightly different method to deliver ouchie points to your enemies.The sound track for the game is honestly pretty weak. A handful of bangers for sure, but most just don't do it for me, and a few of which feel out of place entirely in a rhythm game.I could also get into some of the minutiae of where the game sort of falls apart in certain aspects, from certain animations/cooldowns not actually playing in-time with the beat, some enemies/traps simply being way too fast/accurate, the game not crossfading songs leaving relatively long moments of silence between loops, the game spontaneously changing tempo without warning, repetitive/copy pasted level designs/layouts, the dodge being pitifully short, so on and so on. But reviews do have a word limit and I'm sure more than a few fanboys will just cry of a lack of skill or something like that.Suffice to say that all-in-all the game doesn't do either aspect of it's genre's particularly well or satisfyingly.In the words of Squilliam Fancyson himself; The game is just simply, ""

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, from a rhythm game point of view, the difficulty ramps up enormously after the second area and it's simply because of poor level design and the enemy's hp scaling way too high. It is insane to ask of the player to not get hit, while  shooting at enemies that shoot back, on a tight corridor, while an indestructible tower also shoots at you, and all of this, while keeping the rhythm, because if you mess up even once, your combo doesn't matter, all you are getting is a poor quality medal and poor quality loot too.However if you ignore the rhythm aspect of the game, then the it becomes mind numbingly easy! Simply get a weapon that heals you when you shoot, and that's it. You will heal back during the invincibility frames after getting hit. You should be able to just shoot your way through.I believe it could be a decent rhythm game by simply keeping the enemies as an incoming danger that you can quickly dispatch in a few beats, instead of them dragging on and piling up. And by also adding a better grading system. You might want to keep the platinum medal being very difficult to obtain, but allow the player to still get decent tier loot.

_childDocuments_.review: The core concept is solid. The music sounds great. What draws me to neutral territory is: The game's UI, music, and moment to moment gameplay directly fight against the core concept of the game. UI: Everything is on the far edge of the screen, while your character remains fully centered. Music: Half of the songs do not have a discernible beat; Don't get me wrong, the songs themselves are great, they just don't all make for the best backing for a rhythm game. The two of these things combined mean that unless you have the game's metronome enabled, which means you're not really hearing the music and might as well disable it.The mechanics of Combat fight against the music. Some helpful things here would be: A more centered way to see the beat timing; Such as a closing circle around the player character for beats, and some on-character indicator for dashes or melee swings. Enemy telegraphs "growing" or becoming more "Menacing" with the beats as they pass. As an example for a Line shot - the line starts short and green, growing and turning more red as it becomes closer to firing.

_childDocuments_.review: I have put a lot of time into this game. While it is not perfect by any means, and there are dozens of things it could do better, what you get for what it is, is very impressive.The game has a full story mode that can be played on and offline, single and multiplayer. It supports drop in and out co-op, and the story itself doesn't overburden. It's there to add some flavor, and give some entertainment and purpose between missions. Music puns are plentiful and it's fun to catch all the little references both visually and written. Depending on how hardcore you want to make it for yourself, this can be breezed through in 10 or so hours, or on max difficulty settings can take 20+ easily. The game itself scales it's difficulty if you add more players, too. So if you gather a friend group, it won't suddenly become a cakewalk.It's a music game, so it lives and dies on the Soundtrack. While some people have complained about the song choices, I love how diverse it is. What game has such a range as this? Pop, calypso, Jazz, funk, classical, metal, dubstep, chiptune, rap, symphonic, synthwave, prog.. even ELECTROSWING? I would challenge anyone to find such a wild soundtrack as this. Yet, since they are aimed around the various biomes, it never feels horribly disjointed and out of place. For the trickier songs, you can also turn on a metronome to keep track of the beat if it's hard for you. If you somehow don't like the 140+ songs given in the game? You can even add your own! The game will generate a level and enemies based on the song. It gets it right about 70% of the time, but for the other 30% you can do some offline fixes with manual beatmapping that only takes about 5 minutes once you get the tools. Just search "soundfall manual beatmapping" on YT and you'll find it.The game is controlled entirely through the BPM, and so it does not allow for runs of notes and experimentation within the beat, etc.. But the BPM controls everything. It controls how you attack, how the enemies moves, how the UI and background animates, etc. The BPM is also measured and the entire game will show down or speed up based on it. It would be incredibly difficult to tether all that to an ever changing beat to follow- though a few songs do actually change up the beat mid song. After you beat it, there are more challenges to do, and depending on your skill level you can very easily put in 100+ hours on it. And if anyone thinks it's too easy, just keep increasing the difficulty as you go. This game is tricks you into thinking it's a cute little shooter with it's colorful art- but then will beat you into the ground on some later stages.Things the game falls a bit short on:- Levels can be a bit repetitive at times. It's procedural, so this is an inevitability.- Enemy variety could also be a bit better- Loot variety could be better- Because of the mentioned 3 things above, the gameplay can get "samey"Ultimately though, for a huge music game with randomly generated content, 4 player online and local co-op, a full story mode, great looks, and fun gameplay, it's hard to really go wrong with it!

_childDocuments_.review: The base layer is an average twin-stick shooter with diablo-style loot. The twist is that every action on the beat of the music is greatly enhanced, and every off-beat action is greatly penalized.The main issue is that the game only recognizes inputs on the core beat, rather than anything that matches the music. As a result, it never feels like you're jamming out, but more like you're trying to be a human metronome. Overall it's pretty fun, and gets my recommendation if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, however most of the reviews state the same thing.The repetition is what makes this game quite un-enjoyable. I can play it for 20 minutes or so expecting different results and badass gear, only to be let down by the monotonous, stale gameplay. Don't get me wrong, it's fun for the first hour or so, but you'll quickly understand what I'm talking about after playing it for two/three hours. It's dull, repetitious, and overall just underwhelming. You don't really get any decent rewards for finishing the levels, even if you nail a perfect score. I seem to constantly find gear that's very similar to each other, with little to no genuine difference. Imported songs, especially longer ones take absolutely forever to import-- and like a lot of other people have mentioned, the bpm can be frustrating for more intense songs.I will say that I love the art style and the concept of the game. The characters are fun and somewhat interesting, but I personally don't enjoy the repetitious gameplay. Most levels feel the same with very minor differences with gear being boring and underwhelming. Again, you'll understand exactly what I mean if you decide to pick it up.I personally can't recommend the game unless its on sale or you have a knack for rhythm games. I'm optimistic for some kind of polishing for the gameplay. I can't quite say what would make my experience more enjoyable-- maybe I'm being too harsh?

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 4/5Music: 5/5A rhythm game with variety beyond just pop music makes my soul incredibly happy. 80's techno, classical, pop, metal, jazz, this game has so many options that allows lovers of any genre to find something they enjoy. Not to mention, the ability to upload any song you want into the game and play along with it is such a fun feature! Game Play: 5/5Bullet hell dungeon crawlers aren't exactly my favorite style of game, but the game does those aspects well. Each character has a strength and, when paired with the right player, allows for a fascinating team building and co-operations. There aren't necessarily special bosses (that I have faced, yet) that differentiate themselves from the other enemies, but the levels are still challenging and the combinations of the various enemies attacking at once really ramps up the difficulty without needing a specific boss.User Interface: 3/5This game is fairly straightforward, but there are some aspects that I would not have found out on my own. For breaking down a piece of equipment when you inventory is full, there's teeny tiny text that tells you to hold down space (I think). For changing the difficulty of a level, you hover over the level and hit E. To change weapons, you use the scroll wheel of the mouse (not sure about controller). Things like this, I completely missed and, though they don't affect the game play too much, I wish were more apparent.Story Line: 4/5A story isn't exactly necessary for this type of game, so it's a little lackluster. The metronome is the heart of the world and little monsters want to destroy it, thus requiring you to fight them off? Sure. It's about what you would expect, so it doesn't disappoint me in any way.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: After spending several more hours with Soundfall, I revoke my recommendation. This is a game where the little problems just build up over time until they become unmanageable so I'm flipping my final verdict to negative. I mentioned the annoying stage hazards. Well, the later levels they don't just have one type per stage hazard. They start to add multiple traps. By the last area (the snowy mountains) you have boulders falling on you, slippery terrain, spike walls, floor tiles that shoot spikes when you step on them and laser beams. This in addition to the bullet hell when the normal enemies are on screen. I realized at some point, I wasn't listening to the music at all. All my attention was on stuff that was going to kill me. Yet I was somehow managing to clear the stages, no problem. When my guns misfired, I'd wait a second and pull the trigger again, repeating this until I hit the beat. I've put an unhealthy number of hours into Final Fantasy Thearhythm and Hatsune Miku Diva Project. I've played Elite Beat Agents, Amplitude, Taiko no Tsujin, even the Persona 4: Dancing all Night game. Obscure fair that barely anyone remembers like Mad Maestro, Vib-Ribbon and Guitaroo Man and have even imported Japan exclusive titles like Bakumatsu Rock and IA/VT Colorful. I'm saying this to point out that I know my way around rhythm games. You just can't play a properly optimized music game by zoning out and winging it yet I was able to do that.This leads me to believe that the regular stages have the same problem I mentioned the stages of imported music have: the game reading the beat of the song is just an illusion. Either that or this mix of music and shooter is not a good match. They had to make the music part so imprecise to make the shooter aspect work that they might as well not even bothered. Somethings I said in my original write up below are not true after all. My problem with no loot drops for my preferred character was because the inventory had been filled up so the gear I was seeing at the end of the stage was actually just being dumped. Would have been nice if the game gave me a chance to delete something from my inventory. I only realized when I went into the equipment screen to buy something from the shop and could not buy the item. This is why I hate these loot-heavy games. Inventory management is the worst part of any game and it is a drag when you have to toss eight sets of level 12 armor with different percentages of speed and defense boosts. The inventory space is quite small considering you have to have a load-out for five characters.I also said your combo chain resets if you go too long without defeating an enemy. This is also false. You can deal with all the empty space between rooms where enemies swarm you by randomly firing your guns in time with the beat. That's just kind of stupid. No, you are better off skipping Soundfall. The shooting distracts from the music and the music doesn't work well with the shooting. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------This is a recommendation with some big caveats. A soft thumbs up if you will.Soundfall is a rhythm shooter. You run and gun through the levels matching gun fire and melee strikes in time with the beat. Failure to be so results in attacks doing less damage and several mistimed attacks in a row result in a short but deadly attack cool down where all you can do is dodge incoming attacks.I've been playing for five hours. This game has some pretty severe flaws but it also has that compulsive, one more round quality that music games often have. A rhythm game is only has good as it's track list. Soundfall's is pretty big and eclectic ranging everywhere from classical-inspired instrumentals to JPop to metal and swing. However, I don't find many of the tracks all that memorable so this is quantity and variety trumping quality. But nothing stands out as awful either.The game has a feature where you can import in your own music and play it as auto-generated level. Supposedly, it is able to analyze the song and know when you are matching the beat. I played around with this feature for a few songs and I am not convinced this is the case. It handled songs that tend to not have much variation in them fairly well (I was able to nail a stage generated from Usher's DJ Got Us Falling in Love), but throw something that uses a lot of different instruments and changes tempo and... it's not able to follow the song. It will give you a beat-meter on the bottom of the screen and you can get by just matching button presses to that rhythm, but it's not the rhythm of that song. I guess there is some value to play random stages with your own personalized soundtrack list, but this could have worked better. I've seen some posts where the devs ask you to download a free audio software program and a plug-in to make it work better, but I ain't doing all that. Let's talk about the shooter element. It is adequate, but not more than that. I dislike hate gear-based games where you are showered with new armor and weapons and you have to constantly shift between items where the stat differences are minimal and compare the special features. I find it tedious because you quickly end up with an inventory full of junk. Guess what Soundfall is? One of these. But that is the nature of the beast, I suppose. I stuck to the first character for the majority of play time because she felt hands down the best to control, and I swear that after the third character joined, gear for her rarely seemed to spawn. Most of my upgrades had to be purchased from the shop. It's like they were trying to force me to switch characters. That wouldn't be a problem, but two of the characters control like slightly worse versions of the first girl and the other two are awful to control. I played those two's mandatory stages and decided never again. The arenas are really where it falls down. They are very boring. Really, each stage feels like a palette swap of the previous one. You run down down connecting narrow pathways to reach the wider enemy rooms were you will have to hold off an onslaught before the barrier blocking your progress crumbles. The only real difference between areas are the stage hazards. I think I lost my bonus chains (very important because they determine exp and loot quality) more to getting hit by the stage hazards than I did to enemy attacks. All of them are annoying, but the worst one is definitely the wall lasers. These things will fire three beams out of the walls and you have to time your movement very precisely to avoid them. They are wider than your dash is long so there is very specific timing you need to hit to get past them without getting damaged. I could go on and on and about the small questionable decisions that stack up over time such as how much dead space the arenas have, which wouldn't be as noticeable if your combo chain wasn't on a timer where it resets to zero if you go too long without defeating an enemy, or the lack of iframes on the special attack. Or the fact that they put a story mode in. You can skip it easily, but the fact remains, no music game in history has ever benefited from a story mode. And you have to play at least half of it to unlock all the characters. It might sound like I hate Soundfall. I don't. I do find it enjoyable for what it is: a zippy little distraction good for short bursts of play that could have been much better than it is with some tweaks. It isn't worth the full sticker price, but it's a good time if you can find it for five or six bucks on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It is amazing on concept, don't get me wrong.As someone who loves Rhythm games and Dungeon/Instance Clearer games, Especially with a loot and shoot feel, the game falls short in my personal opinion. The reasons are simple, though I will go into detail to make sure others understand why my experience is important to take into account upon purchasing the game. This is not to say that anyone else's isn't valid, but rather just to give my personal experiences to work off of from someone who loves these kinds of games.First off: The Main Mechanic, and the issue.Soundfall works off of a very timing-heavy (And rapid) combat system, which is non-restrictive to the enemies to the same sense that it is restrictive to the player. Let me explain.When you make a game that requires Beats and Rhythm, the player should be able to hit the notes on the same timing that they need to (Be it enemies in this case, or notes), as to keep with the beat of the song and provide a pleasant experience for hitting those "Perfect" notes. The game decides to do this as the only real way you can attack, however, rather then giving some leeway for misses as getting even slightly off rhythm (Especially in multiplayer) Is an incredibly painful and not fun experience as a whole. Why is it so painful you ask? Well, unlike the trailer where you have four players able to shoot along the screen with no gauge of their actual timings (Thus not needing to focus due to multiple people to deal the damage, nor being able to tell if they truly are attacking on beat as a LOT of the gameplay footage is ONLY on the super moves which DON'T have to be on beat.) you actually have to make sure to match any beat of the 100 songs that the game has, rather then the spam you see in the trailers.Complexity: Engage the Rage.Now, not to say that everyone has this problem, but weaponry preferences aside, the game has a surprisingly few selection of weapons that actually operate differently, Especially early on. Granted, this would be fine in any normal Looter shooter style game, as most guns would operate in the hands of the player in much the same way. We all know Rocket launchers shoot rockets that blow up, and we know pistols for being super accurate at mid range and being the bane of any CS:GO's players existence if they get smacked with the Deagle. But this is something that gets ruined by the main mechanic.You are likely to hear me say this a lot, but to me personally, it doesn't work well with the main mechanic. Each weapon has a "Feature" of sorts, that allows it to be used either in a "Timed perfect way" or a "Held way" For some. Now, in a rhythm game, you need to keep up that press-to-the-beat style, otherwise you get off rhythm. Which is why (90%) of the Held fire weapons, DONT WORK. You have to get a perfect, and hold it for 1 2/3's beats. For some, it can be as little as 1/4th, and for some it be as long as 2. Why is this important? Because this is not only one of the most COMMON mechanics you will find in the game, but it is also the most difficult to keep any form of consistency in. Especially since it is your main, and usually, only attack. Unless you wanna waste all your time leveling your "Super gauge" with damage from offbeat attacks, and swinging wildly to hope for the best. That leads us to our next point.Punishing: Timing, dodging, and the enemies who don't give a ♥♥♥♥.I for one am fine with the souls games, and their level of difficulty. Same with most rogue-likes and their higher jogs of difficulty when appropriate, (EX. Taking too long in Risk of Rain 2 for farming money or EXP can be dangerously risky sometimes.) but this game honestly has NONE of the safe guards nor even level playing field when it comes to enemies. When it comes to levels being played single player, you are almost instantly overwhelmed past the first three stages of the game. This wouldn't be too bad if everything was on Rhythm with you, as that would allow you to easily break past the enemies with perfectly timed shots, and would reward you for getting those perfects. This... doesn't happen.The main enemy type: Discordians (If I remember right) can attack freely, without worry of timing or having to stay on beat for full damage. Again, wouldn't be as bad of an issue if you weren't swarmed with enemies that not only can attack in wide swaths and ranges that require you to focus on not just your rhythm, but your dodging and positioning, but almost constantly diverts your attention because the game is likely to spawn at least TWO enemies of this type, almost per area per level. Whether it be the ones that can tank your shots as you try to move away from the 6 coming after you while you try to stay on perfect beat to not lose your streak, but also to make sure you can kill them before they swarm and gang up on your health bar like its two dogs on a pair of tied socks.Don't even get me started on the dodging. You see, dodging ALSO has to be timed, and is on a cool-down. Didn't dodge right? Get punished for it just as you would the lack of timing you have while your attention is split seven ways to Sunday kiddo. So your dodge is pretty much useless save to get out of the way of an attack, assuming you perfect it and actually get the I-frames you might need to get out of an attack. Again, the issue here is that the consistency really tanks due to the main mechanic. If you could dodge when you needed too, rather then it having to be on-beat, this would be way less of an issue, and the game would actually be rather ok at that point, save for again, the combat solely operating on nothing BUT this mechanic forced into your hands, and no-one elses. Oh wait-Multiplayer: A nightmare for not just you.I will give the creators this, they tried their best to account for lag between individuals by creating a "Sync" option that allows you to time your shots along with your apparent connection to the host of the instance. The unfortunate part, is that it rarely works. I tried to play with a good friend of mine who actually enjoyed playing it just to jam to the music, not really caring about playing the game as much as just [Listening to the music]. This meant that again, while we were actually trying to progress, we struggled in many ways, especially when neither of us, Host OR player two, could land our shots due to the latency issues that the game can't fully account for. I even tested a auto clicker that was set to the beat of the song, counted by the metronome program in the game, and it would still mess up horribly, though I was honest to my friend that this game honestly wasn't for me due to the insane level of things the game expects you to get through.Finally, the biggest issue to me.Looter Shooter: Rarity and the guns of meaninglessness.I am no stranger to the looters and shooters of modern day, or the ones who really solidified it. Things like Borderlands, a First person Looter-shooter made by Gearbox, is a good example of a looter shooter, but to compare this game to that one would be apples to oranges. After all, it is a first person game compared to a angled top down game, and not to mention that this game is a Dungeon crawler! So why not compare it to something that follows the same suit that way. I play a game called "Fate", which was made back it 2005, and you can even still find it on the steam store, along with its sequels that span from that time all the way till 2011 with Fate: The Cursed King. Now, there are some very big similarity and differences for the games innovations to take into account here, as follows.When it comes to Fate, game play can be inconsistent at times, but it is only how the player builds themselves that can cause such inconsistencies. But in Soundfall, with so many differing things to focus on, that consistency it seems to "have" is easily lost.Personal rating: 3/10. Good idea. Just not good execution.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall seems like a good quality game with a decent amount of tracks, game play is interesting and can be challenging at times.My main issue is some levels the beat feels completely 'off', so as it suggests I try using the calibration tool which didn't feel like it made it any better, keeping the beats feeling off, with the only way feeling playable being to play on every second beat.I'd think maybe 'Git Gud' would make sense, but given i haven't had an issue with other rythm based games, or that some levels are much easier to follow at similar BPM, i'd argue otherwise.What adds to that is the lack of 'beat' within multiple songs where there just isn't something to follow aside from the visual metronome (or the audio one if you enable it... but that almost feels like a cop-out for not having enough queues to play without it).If you're using a controller, there is also another factor of the vibration for the beat being just short of the beat itself and no clear way to change that setting.I'd recommend this game for a bit of fun and i'm sure it's going to receive some more fixes given it's only just released.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game - I love rhythm games - but it has a lot of fundamental flaws that make it not particularly enjoyable to play.I'll largely skip past commentary on the dialogue/story under the assumption that anyone really interested in a rhythm-based game is not particularly there for the dialogue/story, but suffice to say that it is not particularly good and often feels like the development team simply felt like they were obligated to insert dialogue in-between stages.The gameplay WITHOUT music is... okay. There's a myriad of weapons everyone can use, and each unlockable character has their own special type of weapon that only they can use and their own special attack. These are the only ones that don't share gear. Weapons and armour have modifiers on them, akin to Diablo or a looter shooter -- maybe this one gives you bonus damage on the beat, or this one gives you extended range, or this one chains lightning to other enemies nearby. There's a few different 'styles' of blaster, from regular single-shots to rapid machine-gun fire to shotguns. Ultimately, though, you are only ever going to want the chain lightning effect no matter what weapon it happens to be on, so this is kind of a letdown. You do get two gun slots, so you could take a hard-hitting non-chain weapon for large monsters and swap to it when the time comes, but... mostly, you just stick with the chain lightning because everything comes out in big swarming packs.The gameplay WITH music is.. it's not good. The game map is spread into sections of 10 stages each, and each section has its own 'theme' - be it classical, metal, pop, country, EDM, etc. If you don't like a particular style of music, that's too bad, because you're going to have to play through it anyway as opposed to it being a single song here and there. This is ultimately forgivable by itself, but the songs that are chosen are often not particularly conducive to rhythm-based play at all. There's lulls, there's thrashing drum or guitar solos, there's beat changes -- but the beat itself is set at the start of the stage and you are expected to always maintain this beat even if it is no longer in tune with the music.Further, a not-insignificant number of stages have songs that are around the 2 minute mark, which gives you barely any time to recognise or appreciate a piece of music that's present before you're on to the next stage. I'm sure a great many of us who love rhythm games can easily, easily think back to games we may've played even years ago and recall the music almost effortlessly -- I can do no such thing with Soundfall. I would be hard pressed to hum anything but the overworld map music, and at no point did I ever feel compelled to replay a stage thinking, "Wow, that was awesome!" It's all just forgettable, which is compounded by the fact that stages are often extremely similar in layout and design, having only rudimentary changes between one and the next in a given section.I like the idea of a rhythm shooter, but this isn't the game to do it with.

Generally didn't like any of tracks in this game too.Soundfall also doesn't do well as game to shoot things, most levels are 1-2 minutes long, levels look samey and it's not fun to play even in co-op.It also has elements of visual novel, but they're extremely short, uninteresting and it would benefit from having better writing or scrapping this completely. _childDocuments_.review: I saw this during a Direct today, and had no clue it existed. But the second I saw it, I knew I had to play it. And so far (1 1/2 hours in) I'm NOT disappointed.It is essentially a mashup of a dual-stick shooter and Crypt of the Necrodancer (or more precisely, Cadence of Hyrule). A bit more freeform than Crypt, but also a bit more punishing if you are off-beat. I don't know if it is my computer or what, but tuning the delay is a bit tough so I am having to rely very heavily on my ears. I can easily see how this game could get overwhelming, as they throw more and more enemies at you. Juggling dashing between attacks is tougher on faster songs, and so far I've not been able to do a perfect run - but that is perhaps to be expected. There really isn't much to guide you towards a couple things - like using the face buttons instead of the triggers for more precise input (at the cost of only being able to do one thing at a time). They also don't explain the overworld map very well, which is needed to start unlocking things. I also think the biome chunks can easily be picked out and start to get repetitive... hopefully there can be more variety in those in the future. And finally, the game really does encourage you to speed through things. Which.. well, is fine, except I want to listen to this music! :) All in all, I would very much recommend it. It's been a while since I've done a blind buy like this. I'm glad I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Soundfall is an ok rhythm game.It looks beautiful, the feedback of the weapons is great, the story is quite goofy and fun (so far) and it offers a bit of customization for your characters. It can be played in local coop, it allows you to import your songs and play levels generated to fit your song. The AI of the enemies is surprisingly good. It is overall a fun game.BUT, it has many limitations that I want to focus on, hoping some of the devs will read this and improve.The stages are separated into biomes, but the stages in each biome feel kinda same-y. The game gets repetitive quite quickly due to lack of innovation. You play in the same maps, with the same assets barely moved around, fighing the same 5 enemies with minor changes. I think the game could be improved by adding some variety in terms of enemies and assets.The level design is very flat, it's often the same rooms connected end to end, very simple to navigate through with some occasional jumps in pre selected locations.The character level is pointless and unfun. You get to level up and receive some weapons and other loot that you would get anyway through quests and by completing stages. Every 5 levels a new difficulty is unlocked and you can play every stage at the new difficulty. Why? I don't know, there is no real reason to soft lock difficulty selection behind character levels, the game is very easy anyway.From my understanding, the loot received at the end of a level is randomly generated from a selected pool of items. This makes the game somewhat grindy if you want a specific weapons or armors, adding that to the fact that the game is already repetitive, that's not a good thing.QOL stuff: the sorting system for songs and inventory is awful, you can sort songs by artist, name and biome but not by genre for example, even though the game states multiple times that the genre of the song will determine what kind of loot you will receive by completing it. You can sort them by "award" which I assume is what I am talking but the game is not clear about what kind of "award" you will be given by completing the stage. You can't sort them by which songs you have played already and there isn't a favourite system to filter out all the songs you don't like. Also for some reason, in story mode you need to hold A to play the selected stage and in general this thing of holding down a certain button is somewhat present in the menus of the game, great, but for whatever reason in free play you only need to tap A to play the selected song, which means that if you spam A at the end of a free play stage to skip through the XP gained screen and each loot you received shown one by one, you will most likely tap A one too many times and end up replaying the same stage. Not a big deal, just mildly annoying but I wonder why.About inventory sorting: it doesn't exist. There are 5 different types of weapons, each can have specific elemental buffs tied to it and they have different rarity and a different tier. They are listed by tier by default but you can't change the order. Also it doesn't let you compare two different weapons (you know, the usual green arrow up if the stat is better and red arrow down if the stat is worse).You can import any song you like, which is great, but everything after that is automatically handled. Often times the game gets the timing or BPM of your songs a bit wrong and I didn't find any way to fix that, which is a shame. I think the game would benefit from letting players create their own levels. Many rhythm games do this and survive on user-based content, such as Osu! or ADOFAI.The tutorial is very incomplete. I only realized after hours of gameplay that you can shoot not following the rhythm of the song, you can shoot in between the lines of the metronome and as long as you are following the melody of the song, it doesn't consider them mistakes and the weapons will deal full damage.I don't think it is worth 30€.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game. So much.The gameplay loop is fun for me, despite how repetitive and grindy it can become.But there's just something... not right with how the rhythms are mapped out.After recalibrating the game several times, I still couldn't manage to maintain the rhythm for extended periods of time.I wanted to chalk it up to having to multitask a twin stick shooter + rhythm game, but it really just felt like all my rhythm game skill disappeared overnight or something. So I jumped to other rhythm games to see if I suddenly became nubsauce again and I was still playing Necrodancer and DJMAX very well.I don't know what it is with Soundfall but keeping the rhythm just doesn't feel right.And when the core distinct element of your game doesn't feel right, well.....File this game under "games I REALLY don't want to flush". _childDocuments_.review: The central premise of the game is flawed.  You click on the beat to shoot, but that plays a new shooting sound so now you've got two slightly offset beats.  Then it's a projectile attack, so it travels a bit and hits something, and that adds a third beat that's randomly offset from the other two depending on how far away you are from things.  Then you're moving and aiming freely, which are not on the beat at all, and you have to respond to enemy movements which are random.  It's a total cacophony.  Even if all those problems were fixed, you'd still just be monotonously clicking your mouse in rhythm like a human metronome for the entirety of the game.  Playing this game, even for a short time, was pure suffering.  I got it in a bundle for $1.67, so I'm mentally free to just abandon ship immediately.  Anyone who paid $30 (!) is locked into sunk-cost stockholm syndrome and has to psychologically justify their purchase in their review.Alternative games: If you're looking for an aesthetic music experience, I'd recommend .  If you're looking for a musical action game, I'd recommend .  You could buy both of them at full price and still be ahead.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay loop is fantastic, with easy-to-use controls and a decent selection of weapons even just a couple hours in; fans of Bullets Per Minute, Metal: Hellsinger, or other rhythm shooters are going to love the way this game flows. Character unlocks are a bit of a slow burn, but not slow enough that you'll get too tired of anything. Music selection is solid, and the game even has custom song support to build the library even further (although be warned that it doesn't always get the tempo 100% right, so some imported songs may drift a bit). Bonus points for integrating music choices directly into the gameplay, with genres and tempos actually influencing the environment, enemy selection, and loot tables of each level, which you can use to prepare accordingly or even select songs from your personal library to grind for items you might need in your own style.Visuals are gorgeous, with vibrant colors and beautiful hand-drawn animations sprinkled throughout. Every biome has a very distinct feel, and the way everything moves with and pulses to the beat really helps get you absorbed into the motion. Some telegraphs aren't quite as readable as I'd like (remember, sniper-flutes fire the beat  the gauge fills) but overall the field is never too hard to keep track of, even in highly chaotic situations.Writing is... certainly a plot. Rather generic isekai couched in musical references. Probably the weakest part of the game, sadly; I find myself speed-reading through cutscenes to get to more gameplay. Not  to be fair, but certainly not holding my interest.Overall verdict: Highly recommended. This is a fantastic genre-mash that does everything it sets out to do and then some.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is kinda strange. You can do all the levels on the lowest difficulty, but the tempo of the song is what's really going to determine how hard it is, since faster-tempo songs are going to make traps and enemies move and shoot faster, and they're much harder to time shots and dodges on than medium or slow tempo songs.That being said, some enemies will fire off-beat, and some traps will too- and sometimes, when the enemies and traps fire on-beat, you'll be at an off-beat range from them but needing to dodge, meaning you'll dodge off-beat and still lose health anyway because only on-beats give invincibility frames.There aren't actually 500s of weapons, there's actually only about 10-12 kinds, each with 5 elemental variants. The special musician weapons don't count since they're only themselves with "cores" that only augment their elements, and mixtapes that also do the same thing, but for that weapon's special ability.If you don't like the song that a level uses, you can turn it off and the metronome on, so, that's not really a problem.What IS a problem is the custom track feature. It requires you to have a specific kind of mp3 of whatever you're trying to import... Which means you need a mp3 version of every song you want to play a level for.... In an age where most of the music we all hear is on Youtube/Youtube Music, Spotify, Itunes, and so forth- ONLINE, not as a file. This ends up bringing people into the worst headache there is: Online/App-based link-to-file converters. Every single one of them has ads or viruses, or opens a random window and downloads some random other file you should go delete, or, like VLC, gets an mrl error that everyone has a fake, non-working fix for. Just let us put in links, then have the game convert it to an mp3 and do its thing. Please. I beg of you.Speaking of, make sure you use songs with a consistant, stable beat that doesn't change during the song, otherwise the system that makes the beat will go crazy, and will alter the tempo when it detects a change in the beats. Sometimes this can be cool when a song has a section of lower tempo, other times it just makes no sense with what the audio's telling you.Levels themselves only get made when songs are imported- all the story mode ones and ones you've already imported (as long as you don't move the file then re-import it to get another level genned) are static, as well as all the level elements and enemy spawns, meaning if you have trouble with a story level, even if it's only on the lowest difficulty, then you're going to have to run it over and over and over with no variation within until you clear it.There are rarity-based loot drops, and the modifiers can be signifigant if you choose to keep the difficulty scaling the way the devs came up with. Unnecessary grind ho! What makes that worse is that difficulty level and medal level (medals are earned at the end of levels based on how perfect you are at the game... I'm not kidding, the highest tier asks you to not be hit, never miss a beat-based action, and never break a combo chain by getting hit or letting the combo meter run out while still getting to the end of the level before the song ends and/or loops. Crazy, man.) affect loot rarity, so, have fun dying and wasting time to get that Legendary of that one single weapon you like with all the modifiers you want to keep doing harder and harder levels! (Though again, you can set it all to the lowest difficulty or whatever you're comfortable with, then play the whole thing, including custom tracks, at that level.)

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, let me make it clear first and foremost that this is *NOT* a bad game. The main reason I have it as "Not Recommended" is because the price-point is too high, for this game.This game functions, is colorful, and fits a niche; which for some will be more than enough. However, where this game falls flat for me (pun intended) is that it very quickly felt repetitive. A lot of the stuff I saw was handled the same way, and the scenery very rarely felt varied enough - to the point that I started going through things without even thinking about them. Not caring to get the treasure chests, and would rather just finish up the stages - so that they would be over. Which is a big warning flag for games that are built around obtaining more loot in stages/dungeons.And, the other thing that actively annoyed me - was the characters never really shutting up. For a game about music, the characters talk way too much before each stage; and sometimes even after. To the point that I started skipping every cutscene and conversation that occurred, because I wanted to see if the next stage would be the one to grab me.But, sadly - none of them did.I will say however, the biggest redeeming quality of this game is the "Custom Tracks" feature. Letting us play to our own music, which is something that everyone can enjoy. This function though was not enough to keep me satisfied to play more than I already have. After unlocking the second character, I was pretty much done.I might still pick it up, and give the custom track stages a play from time-to-time. But, this game simply couldn't hold my interest; despite me loving the concept and wanting to enjoy it.That said, if you see it on sale for only $15 - $20; then go ahead and give it a try. It can be an okay enough distraction for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: you can shoot and dash on the same beat--*BIG EDIT*--I have now hit endgame  and spent some time there so i am now able to dump on this game, there are alot of reviews here and most of them are dumb and wrong in the context of giving people all of the information they actually need to understand if they want to purchase in the context of a long term rhythm arpgFor non spoiler summary for the people who want to experience game mechanics themselves; this is a great game with considerable problems, its fully worth the price provided you go in understanding its flaws IF you can eventually accept them. Good luck, they are not small flaws---SPOILERS AHEAD---More depth:-The game has 142 songs and requires you to complete 102 of them to unlock either of the final two difficulties, in a game where most enemy variants dont even show up on the first two difficulties it is stock standard poor pacing of arpgs and coop games in general expecting players to require far more time then necessary digesting new systems and mechanics, do not play 3-4 songs and expect anything other than very simple zerg enemies, the -Many properties/prefixes/whatever you want to call them on your gear range from ridiculously powerful to literally detrimental, this creates scenarios where some items are ruined by poor prefixes and others are made unbelievable powerhouses from just one (of up to five), this has the huge positive advantage of not just tying worth to only itemlevel and creating a large positive identity for your guns/melee weapons causing them to perform and potentially even feel vastly unique, but means you'll have to accept that not all item prefixes are born equal and you will be hunting the specific properties that any gun/melee type needs to succeed -The core gameplay is a bit wonky, being able to dash and shoot in the same beat is easily the most fun part of the game but it creates some serious balance issues amongst the cast of weaponry -The beatmaps of some songs will feel off and that is mostly because the game needs to give you a consistent beat all the time so gameplay doesnt stop while many songs do not necessarily provide the beat to your ears at the same volume or even pulse, and in some cases will disappear entirely, this is a much bigger problem with imported tracks since most of the music that was picked for this game is fine and is extremely varied in taste/pace/genre so pretty much everyone will have tracks they like and dislike, but its important that if you want music to feel correct you will either need to get used to using audacity to fix it or live with it---BIG SPOILERS AHEAD---Dont read if you aren't happy being told exactly how combat works and the values/power of item properties:-The beat as far as I am aware has NO restrictions on your actions beyond a set duration, melee attacks and dashing cannot be animation cancelled into ANYTHING else and lock you in until the beat ends, but shooting can be cancelled into EITHER of these, this gives you two major options on any beat (unless you use an automatic weapon then you have a third inferior poo option) unless you absolutely want to just shoot and keep walking which is fairly rare and usually doesnt involve combat; shooting and dashing inside of your current beat as your defensive/positioning option, or shooting and meleeing which restricts your movement significantly but obviously gives you massive damage and especially massive burst (at least before any specific item properties)This is a massive problem when comparing your options for play since any automatic weapon (burstfire/sixteener etc) has the gigantic penalty of LOSING damage anywhere from 20-80% depending on how fast your fingers are, what the bpm is and how fast the gun fires, IF you also want to dash in the same beat. Since these weapons are balanced around shooting for the entire duration of the beat and usually even AFTER the beat has ended, if you want your dash or your melee in combination you have to give up shots for it. These weapons are NOT balanced to have to compete for this, and numerically cannot make up for the gap at all, you would need some insane positive properties on an automatic weapon to make it more valuable than a non automatic weapon if you are willing to sit on an APM where you can comfortably shoot+dash/shoot+melee every beat. This take completely ignores that with many weapons (quarterizer is the best example and one of the best shoot+dash/shoot+melee options in the game) can shoot TWICE (or even THRICE in the case of low BPM songs) if you have decent timing and are willing to fire slightly offbeat and probably ruin your ears a bitThe obvious retort is well ignore all this stupid high apm sweaty meta garbage and the guns are pretty close right? no sorry dumb and wrong because in this game legendary armor can roll with a property that gives you INFINITY dashes meaning you can dash every single beat and another ONE of your five armor properties gives you a spastically high 50% damage amplification for the entire next beat after dashing on beat. You can keep this up permanently if you decide to shoot+dash the entire map without thought or decisions while still allowing you to dump massive burst damage with shoot+melee following a shoot+dash. Automatic weapons get to abuse NONE of this and it further skews the problem that if you aren't using a weapon that has synergy with dashing and melee you are giving up both massive dps and mobility, most weapons are not automatic and dont have this problem but its important to mention that if you see automatic weapons in the promotional material for this game and that is why you are buying it that you need to understand that they really suck RELATIVE to other options because of how animation cancelling, the beat and item properties function in this game-Some properties like arrythmic are straight up awful, reducing your bonus for playing on beat and reducing the penalty for playing offbeat, which you never want to do, the times you would ever consider playing offbeat are almost always a scenario that you put yourself in and are ALWAYS negative and to be avoided. This property is not just a wasted slot it straight up makes anything it touches worse, there are other examples of poor properties but this is by far the most egregious, likewise for weapon procs stuff like chain lightning's raw dps is better in almost every case than lifesteal or fire damage over time and usually even delayed damage. There are nowhere near enough instances of a large target with a huge health pool to allow any of these dumb slow procs to deal any damage, and for those that exist swapping to a secondary specifically designed to kill bosses/large single enemies is not a healthy way of balancing chain lightning, it will always be superior until it isnt and you'll just swap to the next best single target option. BadI could write a billion more words on the prefixes that are problem children but arrythmic/on-beat dash damage amplification are the two that make the most waves, doubletime (eighth note swings instead of fourth note, or in human speak you attack twice for I think slightly longer animation time, this is completely mandatory if you want to use melody's sword in the late game efficiently) is another good example where no other prefix comes even close to its level of dps, if you care at all about the arpg side of this game you'll need to decide for yourself if having properties on your gear be this polarizing is a good thing or a bad thing---have fun reading all that lol good game i will continue to play id give mixed review if steam didnt suck fat c
