_childDocuments_.review: Here we go! I loved Soundfall. I'm a sucker for any games that are music oriented. I've played many many MANY hours of Audiosurf and similar games. Soundfall hits all the right spots and 95% of the music is awesome! I have a techno/edm obsession so as you might imagine this is exactly the type of game I'd love. That should also be an indicator as to the type of music you can expect to find in Soundfall. But by no means is it all that genre, although most of it has got the BEAT. I will say, what's great is there's some variety in Soundfall, you get to shoot and slice and dice enemies to a beat with a multitude of different weapons. Now before we really get into the core of the game, I want to say this isn't necessarily a FOR SURE LOCK IN BUY for a player looking for a rhythm based game. There are some issues I've run across. So instead of me babbling more, let's get into the pros and cons of Soundfall! Pros:* THE F*****G music is excellent, as I stated before, most of it is great and it hits a variety of different genres. I replay levels just to listen to the music. Which is why I have 14+ hours in the game and I haven't completely beat it yet. I will say also, that I'd never heard of any of these songs before and I'd only recognized a few of the artists. This may be a con for some, but for me this is how I find new songs and new artists. I love it! * Artistic and visual nailed it here, everything in the game moves to the beat of each song. And I DO MEAN EVERYTHING, background objects, characters, enemy AI and anything you can think of moves to the beat! We, however won't be overheating any video cards with this game. It's a unique look, but I can't say the graphics will blow your mind. * You can play as 5 different hero characters (unlocked as you play the story), each with their own unique melee weapons and ultimate attacks. Everyone uses the same armor and instrument guns but they do give off a different vibe when using them. * For a relatively simple concept, there is a quite a bit of replay-ability with Soundfall and maybe that's why. It's easy to learn and play but hard to master especially on the harder difficulties. * Many different levels and biomes to play. Each (sort of) have their own genre of music and their own unique enemies or hazards. * You can import your own music. I haven't done this yet and I'm not sure how it creates the levels with the imported music but I'm excited to try it and this is a big deal since games like Audiosurf can do that too. MORE REPLAY-ABILITY!* There are medals you can earn each map based on how well you kept the beat, didn't break your beat chain and finish the level before the song loops. Also, each difficulty has the medals too.  * There's coop play, which I haven't tried yet either. Sadly, I don't have any friends anymore, so I play solo.Cons* This is a big issue, a real lack of explanation on a lot things in the game. If you don't read loading screens you might miss valuable info. Some weapons have elemental attacks, bonus damage etc. Who knew?! * Unfortunately, you'll run into the same levels or basically the same levels over and over again. I saw people B***H about this and they gave Soundfall a negative review. Yes, I'm listing this as a con, but only because its ridiculously noticeable at times, especially once you hit the Cityscape area. As in back to back maps that use the same areas. It's obvious and they should have shuffled the map placement up a bit. I find it a tad annoying that's all. * From what I can see, you can only dash with your character up to a certain amount of times based off what your armor allows you to do. So far, I've only seen three times in a row. I'm sure there is a higher number later with better armor. So that means you can only dash, in this case 3 times, within a certain amount of time before it won't allow you to dash again until a cool down period has passed. I find this mechanic unnecessary. If you can't dash to the beat, why even allow you to dash at all, especially when there are areas and enemies that require you to dash! This dash cool down should be removed.* It's WAAAAY too easy to lose track of your character, especially on the harder difficulties and the later levels. You find yourself getting damaged or even killed because you lose track of your character.* There are tons of areas that are blocked with a temporary wall and you don't realize those are even places you can access until you've eliminated all the enemies in the area. There needs to be something visual that let's you know, "hey, you can go here!" That way you don't miss so much.* Even though the song selections are pretty good for the most part, there are some songs that really have me scratching my head. Some that are below 100 BPM (Beats Per Minute) and in the harder difficulties this is ridiculous. It's an incredible hindrance because you have a ton of enemies and you can't do anything but dash away from them because you can't attack fast enough. Something I haven't mention is, when you want to do max damage you need to make sure your attacks are timed with the beat OR you'll do reduced damage and sometimes overheat your weapon. It's simply unacceptable, you can't play the game as intended because of poor song selection.  * There are too many areas on each map that have absolutely nothing. No enemies or chests only dead ends. I've played it on several different difficulties and this seems to be a common theme. There's no real explanation, except to confuse and keep you from finishing the level before the song ends. No real reason for this, add enemies to those areas with loot. * Some character's ultimate attacks throw their melee weapon or shoot from a distance and others attack with it. This I found to be confusing, because you can be attacked and damaged if you are throwing or shooting the weapon opposed to moving with your weapon where you are invincible. AND after you've used your ultimate, you can be hit by an on-coming projectile. There needs to be a grace period so that you are NOT damaged by something that you can't control. It makes it where if you are trying for certain medals in a level you never want to use your ultimate because it can get you damaged. * You are only required to use a new character ONCE and that's when the new character is being introduced. You play as them to acquire their special melee weapon. After that, you never have to use them again. BUT, you still unlock gear and weapon upgrades for them in place of things your character can use. This is kind of a waste even though you can sell the unused upgrades. Two things need to happen. One, you shouldn't be getting gear for characters if you aren't playing as them. Since you share guns and armor, it's not as if they will be under leveled if you switch to a character you haven't played in awhile. Two, if you want the other characters played as well, you need to make them mandatory to use for certain levels. For example, only their unique abilities can kill certain enemies etc. This can easily be displayed on the map menu (requires this character in the party or something like that). That also is perfect so if you are playing coop, you'll know one of you will need to use that character. I know I may have listed several cons, but none of them ruin the game. Mostly, they are suggestions of ways to improve the game. I still stand by my initial statement. I love Soundfall! Drastic Games really impressed me. I hope they keep adding new levels and music. I will continue to play Soundfall, and I hope to see more. If the pros are something that excites you and cons are something you can live with, then Soundfall is a MUST GET GAME! I highly recommend buying this game at full price. That's right FULL PRICE! Why?! Because Drastic Games deserves the credit and the money. They made a fun game and if you are reading this, I think you will think so also. That means two thumbs up for Soundfall!

_childDocuments_.review: Scratches the rhythm game itch.  As a long-time fan of games like Guitar Hero, Rock Band, and Beat Saber, and someone who has put over 1000 hours in Diablo 3 and other diablo-likes, I feel that it fuses the two genres together fairly well.  Some of the beats are confusing, but nothing too hard to wrap your head around.  Haven't finished the game yet as of writing this review, but I don't see myself not finishing it and not coming back to it afterwards, especially with the custom level/song input feature.  Lots of room for different builds and playstyles, but some do feel better than others.  It's all up to personal preference based on the loot you get. It's a good rhythm game, and makes good use of the looter and isometric playstyles, has an interesting story and setting, and features overall likeable characters.  Nothing is inherently wrong with this game, but it is a lot of things to balance, and it gets most of them mostly right.The price point to me feels right.  You get your money's worth, and it is a good time.  From what I've noticed as well Soundfall is frequently on sale, so if the price point is a bit too steep still, it's worth buying on a discount for sure.Overal 8/10 in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that is painfully unrefined at this writing. It is worth getting, even at its current price, but worth playing the campaign only far enough to unlock all the playable characters, then diving into free play (which has everything else unlocked from the start).The gameplay itself is really great. It plays like a fusion of Spiral Knights and Audiosurf or Beat Hazard, with maps tiled together and played to the primary beat of the music. Custom tracks work too, and the results are pretty fantastic with just the right level of difficulty.But the campaign, looter shooter aspects, and most of the complexity the devs added to this formula fit together awkwardly and detract from the experience. It's not for lack of trying: there are reams of dialog, a system that classifies genres of music into elemental affinities that even have their own weapon triangle (!!), and fantastic visuals that feel unpolished but demonstrate the devs' love of the game. But it doesn't add much and severely overstays its welcome, clearly more designed to meet a quota of levels per stage than introduce players to the game. This causes the campaign to act more like filler than the already good game demonstrated by free play.There are other mechanical problems, including songs that do not track well, having to manually divest of older gear one at a time, and having to tell the game that yes, really, I want to play at this difficulty level, but most were minor nuisances in my playthrough. And the core gameplay loop and music are so good that you might not notice or care.There also exists up to four player coop, which I did not get to try yet at this writing. But it exists for those so inclined, and if it plays well, it might be a good option for folks looking to reprise the old coop days of Spiral Knights-like gameplay (to the beat).Overall, a good showing from the developers, but please cut the extraneous parts next time. With a refined looter shooter design, a shorter campaign that let the writers thrive instead of burying them and the players in generic dialog and levels, tweaks like mutators and automatically generated three- or four track sprints, and a few generic features and terms thrown in instead of making absolutely every mechanic into a music pun, the game would thrive on its merits. As it stands, it already does, provided folks skip the campaign and play their favorite tracks instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Soundfall started out decently for me, but the quality dropped as I kept playing. I'm happy with the music selection here, and the look of the game is pretty aesthetically pleasing, but that's where the positives end. It has many design flaws such as lazily designed repetitive chunks of levels, the same enemy types with little variation, loot accumulation and the shop both handled poorly. It doesn't feel all that snappy to control. Another nitpick I have is the melee special attack you can do doesn't even make you invincible. Enemy hitboxes are also very wonky, as others have pointed out. A game like this lives and dies in how tight it is to play, and unfortunately, it's not very tight at all.5/10. Maybe get it on a sale, but honestly there are better options.

_childDocuments_.review: On paper, this seems like it would be a great game. In execution, it is lackluster at best and frustrating at worst. For one, there is little variety in level design and layouts and enemy variety is almost non-existent. What you fight in the first 10 minutes is what you fight the rest of the game. Secondly, the looter aspects are bare-bones, extremely basic, and unsatisfying. Thirdly, there are songs with inconsistent tempos and stretches of complete silence making it impossible to continue to perform actions on the beat, practically forcing you to keep the metronome on permanently. And lastly, the timing window to perform actions seems to shrink the faster the BPM is, making levels with high tempo songs almost completely unplayable, despite repeated audio/visual delay calibrations.Are there any positives? The game has good visuals and the animated cutscenes are cool. I also like that it is possible to add custom music to the game, however the beat mapping is as equally flawed and inconsistent as the rest of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I came across Soundfall a little before release and tossed it on my Wishlist so I'd know when it came out.  I don't usually buy games before reviews are available, but this one seemed like it was tailor-made for me: a looter shooter rhythm game where you can import your own music!  So, I decided to take a chance on day one when only a couple of reviews were posted.... and I'm glad I did!The gameplay is fun and the pacing of battles seems well tuned, which is important in a game like this where you need to stick to the beat and can't just fire your weapons willy-nilly.  The length of each level feels good to me, as it seems to be based on the length of each song -- not too short and not too long (most songs I've played run around 2 to 3 minutes).The loot tends to be more than just a stat stick -- the gear you equip helps you lean into different playstyles.  For example, do you like to stay at long range with accurate shots?  Or maybe you prefer to get up close with a slow, high-power, high-spread shotgun approach.Most of the custom tracks I've imported worked without issue, but there was one where the beat wasn't detected properly.  The devs have posted a walkthrough on how to manually set the beat when this sort of this occurs, but I haven't had a chance to look into it yet.Tip: Pay attention to the loading screens... there is information there that doesn't seem to appear anywhere else in the game or tutorial.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally saw this release on the Nintendo Switch and didn't think much of it. Saw it again on Steam and gave it another peek and I'm so glad I did!!!I'm a huge rhythm game player, I just love music. My spouse has never played any type of rhythm games and I was delighted when he agreed to try this co-op with me! We played for 2 hours straight before he called it quits - not in a bad way! It's his first time playing this type of game genre, so going with music beats to do any combat was very new to him. Can't wait till our next play session of this game! The storyline is very generic but honestly the music and art style is so fantastic! Combat buttons for keyboard+mouse take a bit of getting used to with how your avatar faces all wonky at times during combat. I suggest playing with a controller, it's so much easier. Loot and gear system adds nice elements to the on-beat combat system, plus the character animations when they use different instruments is pretty neat.I loved this so much that I'm thinking of buying it on the Nintendo Switch for solo and portable gameplay! I just hope the system can handle this game, we will see! A little pricey but with the amount of songs this game has I'm sure it's to cover all the licensing much like games such as Beat Saber. If it's on sale I'd say give it a go, worse that can happen is you request Steam for a refund.Love love LOVED IT! 8)

_childDocuments_.review: A rhythm based ARPG with a less overwhelming loot system than most. You play as various instrument wielders against the bad guys, the Discordians. No, they're not 14 year olds with anime profile pictures and senses of humour that can only rival a wet dish cloth. The game has very tight controls and on the higher difficulty settings, the game becomes more of a bullet hell. It can feel like it's 2010 and you're in a flash mob - you're having a great time but then armed forces arrive and (deservedly) begin firing. Anyway, anyone who calls the gameplay basic probably can't handle a 3/4 time signature.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, fresh and wholesome. I'm a sucker for rhythm-based action of any kind, but Soundfall adds a co-op mode to that already exciting proposition, and let's be real, brawlers and shooters are at their best when enjoyed with friends.Soundfall is incredibly generous -- there's tons of levels, each with a unique song, in genres I didn't even know I liked... _childDocuments_.review: This game had a cool concept with a combination of bullet-hell, rhythm games, and cooperative play. I wasn't expecting much from it, but since it was bullet-hell I'd assume it would have some fun mechanics. Unfortunately, there is basically no depth to the levels with it's bare-bone design, and uninteresting enemy design. Most enemies are extremely simple, and basically just shoot and spin. The maps were also generally very basic; essentially you would roam around a linear level that has one random branching path at some point to get a single chest that gives you a few credits and perhaps a weapon/gear. These weapons/gears are a dime a dozen and aside from a new weapon, all of the gameplay loop stays the same.Also, the co-op in this game does not work well. It doesn't read in a keyboard and a controller very well, and you basically need two controllers. It was also just a pain to set-up with both controllers affecting the menus/etc. If you're looking for a chill rhythm game that is also a looter shooter, this is probably your pick. The one feature I found interesting was you could insert your own music, but again it doesn't fix the core issues that the game has in terms of mechanics and progression.

_childDocuments_.review: Gets repetitive very fast. Levels and enemies are quickly recycled and feel very generic. The loot system is also a bit messy: weapons have many stats but they all feel very similar to play. Nothing feels very unique nor forces you to play differently: most of the time, you shoot in rythme while circling around your target, nothing more.The art style is colorful but the action can be a bit hard to read in 4-player coop. The music feels adapted and you might like it if it's your style.If you are looking for a relaxing and straightforward rythme game then this might be for you. If you are looking for a challenging and diverse roguelite rythme game then buy Crypt of the Necrodancer: it's half the price and way more polished.

_childDocuments_.review: Unless they vary the gameplay more, I can't in good conscience recommend the game.The game is beautiful. It has animations. It was well crafted visually. The music is generally quite great. (The first boss song is hard to keep the beat and this coming from someone usually quite musically inclined on average.)The problem is that even for a roguelite type game this is really repetitive. The same tired enemies with the same tired layouts. It needs more variation. I was ready to do the first boss about 4 levels before it was actually presented. I didn't try out freeplay so I don't know how that feels, but I'm not the only one that felt the game was too repetitive. It needs more variance in enemies and layouts. If they do add this down the road, it should be a very low price overall as DLC or simply an update.I have refunded the game at this time, but I'll keep an eye on it.

_childDocuments_.review: So played this for a good while, both with the default music and imported music, and I cannot recommend buying this for $30 when it's like most other basic rhythm games that only "create" beats to follow based on bass. With the default music it's really easy to hear the bass beats and pace you're supposed to follow, but with imported music it's obvious that you can see the engine that's been used for "beat detection" primarily focuses on bass and nothing else especially if you're someone who like me listens to a lot of metal. While the in-game look and design is neat, the menu needs A LOT of polish, it honestly feels like a menu I'd see in a flash game on Newgrounds. The intro cutscene was nice, but there really isn't much more after that to see other than some static dialogue before each stage.And speaking of stages, when you do import music, it's only for "Free Play", and when the game advertises itself on importing your own music but you're limited to 1 mode that auto generates the same type of level and structure, it feels like a bait and switch. So for $30? Not even close.

_childDocuments_.review: If you see a review here with less than an hour of play time saying its boring disregard it. The game's systems are FAR more intricate than one might expect and believe it or not it has a rather steep learning curve once it gets into the REAL stuff. The faster a song is, the more potential for movement and damage output the player has. And they aren't seeing that. The guns that shoot a lot of bullets may feel unwieldy, but thats only when you don't know how to use them. It actually shares a lot of properties with Bulelt Hell games, so if you're into those and you can keep a beat half decent, I'd recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: These people wanted to make some music first, and then a videogame second. They made a game where you have to keep to the beat and then they let some parts of the song legit just lose the beat like the silence when the song ends. With certain other songs the vocals are disorientingly sang on the off beat causing your gun to overheat easily if you time your shots with the vocals. This is an example of how NOT to make a rhythm action game. There's a reason Crypt of the Necrodancer and BPM are so beat-heavy and samey, and it's so that you're locked onto a beat easily. Please let the beat boom through the whole song even if it compromises your song's integrity, I'm here to play a game first and foremost. Also the metronome sounds horrendous.

_childDocuments_.review: This game sounded pretty cool to me at first cus I am personally looking for "something to do" while listening to my music and I haven't really seen any games like that since audiosurf/beat hazard. However, this game really misses the mark.Firstly there's no FLAC support and, based on reading dev responses, it was never intended. That's pretty low for a rhythm based game where a huge selling point is being able to import your own music. This would be like making a shooter game on PC with no mouse support because controllers are popular... Honestly it just implies to me that the devs really don't care.Secondly there's some dumb volume normalization going on that makes it impossible to hear anything without cranking the volume up yourself. When things force volumes to be so low, people turn the volume up too high, and then get blasted when they listen to stuff set at the correct level.Thirdly, a lot of the audio aspects of gameplay do not sync up with the music at all. For example, the default blaster definitely has a bit of audio delay when firing, which really screws with your internal metronome for attacking on the beat. I think this really showcases how screwed up this game is.Avoid like the plague.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE 5/12/22: I just tried co-op for the first time, and it does NOTHING to balance players who are higher level. I am level 15 and I wanted to play with my friend who got the game at my suggestion. I am forced to use extraordinarily overpowered gear, with no option of buying cheaper gear. I cannot start a new save file because there are no alternate saves, I'm forced to play with my high level characters. I one-shot all enemies. In addition, the host is getting level 15 gear drops instead of gear for their level, and they can't even use it.The game is virtually unplayable between people of different skill levels. I cannot recommend this game for anyone interested in co-op, and I won't recommend it until this is addressed.---There are some issues I've run into in my first couple hours that bother me that I'd like to address. Most are design decisions, some may be bugs or mistakes.1) The colorblind mode is not good. It uses a filter mechanism and the different filters are labeled 1, 2, and 3, and none of them help my red-green colorblindness at all. It still keeps all AoE markers some form of red, and the health bars are some form of red/pink. It also doesn't differentiate the health bars from the temporary "health lost" bars, so while an enemy is actively taking damage, it's very hard to tell how low they are because of that temporary bar. Most developers are really bad at making colorblind modes so I shouldn't expect any more, but it's still immensely disappointing.2) They don't actually explain what the "Overdrive" item does outside of loading screen tips. It doesn't clearly say that it's for your Ultimate ability, because they never call your Ultimate ability "Overdrive" and the item itself doesn't say it modifies the Ultimate. Not a big issue, but confusing for the first hour or so. They did a great job explaining everything else so it was really odd to just neglect this particular item.3) They let you unlock and play new characters a mission or two prior to them unlocking their abilities/ultimate, due to the story. This is an odd choice that I feel negatively impacts player fun. Players will almost always gravitate toward wanting to try new characters right as they unlock them, but not being able to use any abilities for a few missions is a big buzzkill. I wouldn't give players the choice of playing the character until their specific mission that unlocks their abilities. There's no reason to kill the fun by letting them play a character with no special features.4) The difficulty defaults to the lowest setting after every mission, or if you move your mouse from one mission to another after changing difficulty. This is minor, but really annoying after a dozen missions and constantly having to quit out of missions when you realize you forgot to move it up again. A lot of extra button presses that the player shouldn't have to worry about. Have the difficulty setting a toggle on the world map and let it apply to every mission they choose while it's set to that.5) The UI is extremely reliant on press-and-hold (or click-and-hold, for mouse users) for many functions. This is, from an accessibility standpoint, problematic. It's not like it will harm anyone directly, but it's commonplace these days to mitigate the amount of rapid pressing (example: quicktime events, etc.) and press-and-hold functionality for players with physical disabilities, or other hand strain concerns. I would recommend the devs revisit UI controls to eliminate unnecessary button  holding, when something like a confirmation dialogue fulfills the same purpose with less physical effort. I know, referring to holding a button as "effort" is weird, but being mindful of disabilities and hand strain is really important.This is all I can think of. I'm enjoying the game, I'll update this review as time goes on. I hope the developers are listening to feedback because this game can become even better with some of these issues out of the way.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing. TL:DR The bad part about this rhythm game is the music they used, aka the selling point of a rhythm game.I like me a good rhythm game, and this game having rhythm as a mechanic hurts it more than it helps. A lot of the music from the main levels don't have a beat strong enough to follow. The songs either fade in or fade out, so for 15-30 seconds of game time you are unable to play because you are trying to follow the beat of near silence, and keep in mind the levels are 2:50-4:00 average time. Or many of the songs don't actually have any instrument or noise associated to the beat, like no drums on the beat or guitar on the beat to follow, so you are following the theoretical beat of the song. Oh but you can turn on the metronome for those songs! Yes, because these songs get better with a disjointed ticking just to make them playable. I've 100% both BPM: BULLETS PER MINUTE & THUMPER, and I can say with confidence that this game isn't worth the time sink for me. I have other complaints with Soundfall, but at that point it's personal preference or fixable UI issues so it's not worth making a fuss over.

_childDocuments_.review: Soundfall is a refreshing fusion of rhythm-based gameplay and action RPG elements, creating a unique experience that stands out in the crowded indie game scene. Developed by Drastic Games, this title offers a vibrant and rhythmic journey through the world of Symphonia, where your success in combat is intricately tied to the beat of the music.Gameplay:The core of Soundfall lies in its rhythm-driven gameplay, where every action—from shooting to dodging—must be performed in sync with the soundtrack. This mechanic is both challenging and satisfying, rewarding players who can stay on beat while punishing those who miss the rhythm. The game features a variety of weapons and abilities, allowing players to customize their combat style, which adds depth to the gameplay. While the rhythm-based mechanic is innovative, it may take some time for players to master, which can lead to a steep learning curve in the early stages.Music and Visuals:One of the strongest aspects of Soundfall is its soundtrack, which is a diverse collection of catchy tunes that span multiple genres. Each level is carefully designed to match the music, creating a seamless blend of audio and visual elements. The art style is colorful and vibrant, with beautifully crafted environments that feel alive with the rhythm of the music. The character designs are also charming, adding a whimsical touch to the game’s aesthetic.Story:The narrative in Soundfall is serviceable but not groundbreaking. You play as one of the Guardians of Harmony, tasked with saving the world of Symphonia from the forces of Discord. While the story provides a decent backdrop for the action, it often takes a backseat to the gameplay. The characters are likable, and the world is interesting enough, but don't expect a deeply engaging narrative.Multiplayer and Replayability:Soundfall offers both solo and co-op modes, with up to four players able to team up locally or online. The co-op mode is a blast, as coordinating with friends adds another layer of challenge and fun. The game’s level variety and the ability to revisit previous stages with new abilities and weapons encourage replayability. However, after a while, some levels might feel repetitive, especially if you’re not a fan of the particular music genre featured in them.Conclusion:Soundfall is an ambitious and entertaining title that successfully combines rhythm mechanics with action RPG elements. Its vibrant visuals, infectious soundtrack, and challenging gameplay make it a must-play for fans of rhythm games and those looking for something new in the action RPG genre. While the story and some repetitive elements may not appeal to everyone, the game’s unique concept and execution are enough to keep you coming back for more.If you’re ready to dance your way through hordes of enemies and save a musical world, Soundfall is well worth the beat.

_childDocuments_.review: I have almost 100 hours into this game. I LOVE this game. I have no intentions of ever not coming back to this game to replay it. I have come back to update my review after having played for much longer to help dispel some of the negative feedback incoming since the game was recently on super sale again.First off, if you don't like or don't usually play rhythm games - this isn't for you! What a shock! But really, this is a tougher rhythm game than most when you get to the higher difficulties. A lot relies on your armor/weapons and how you play around them.Secondly, I am convinced that most of the negative reviews are a combination of several things:-Not calibrating the audio properly. You can do this as many times as you want in the settings.-Having lower end speakers or a lower end headset and then complaining the songs have no beat. They do, and it's perfectly fine. I like most of the music in the game and have had NO issues finding the beat to any of them. I say this as someone who is working on the platinum achievement and has platinum'ed a few songs already. PLATINUM ACHIEVEMENT PRO TIPS: If you are trying to work on the platinum achievement, it's to play 100% on beat (this includes VERY FIRST BEAT AND ON) and NEVER take a hit. No touchy.Load up on the reflective gear and learn to time countering enemy effects back at them so they don't hit you. Also LoSing (line of sighting) and hiding behind a rock or whatever to avoid getting hit.--The ONLY time music will be hard to find the beat to is if you are importing freeplay music. Yes, most songs/music change beat. A LOT. So if you're playing to your own tunes in freeplay, expect the beat to randomly change. The in-game songs are all ONE BEAT the entire time.-Not paying attention to the descriptions on abilities and/or weapons/armor and how they can -drastically- change the way you play the character.--Eample 1: Armor with on-beat dash speed increase = character "sliding". It can actually be quite helpful, but not if you're already struggling with maintaining rhythm.--Example 2 :Armor with off-beat perks ~ no, it's not encouraging you to go off beat. It is a handicap until you get better gear that greatly emphasizes being ON beat and penalizes off-beat play. This should be obvious in a rhythm game that you don't want to play around the off-beat items....--Example 3: Weapon types for character weapons. READ the descriptions. If you're already struggling doing a level or increasing difficulty on a level - don't just slap on a weapon that will change your 3 swings in a row to one big swing etc and say the beat is off. You will have to adjust to how the weapon timing changes. Some of them even add double time slashes and it will feel weird until you use it a few times.--Example 4: Some guns you can hold the button down on and fire a continuous barrage for several beats. Others you have to tap the entire time.-Struggling to find the beat that's there? They have a metronome option that you can set to however u want it. You want it on the whole time? Go ahead. You want it to start if you stop playing for a few beats so you can find the rhythm again? Go ahead. You want it NEVER on ? Do that too!I get sad when I see the negative reviews on this game. I love this game so much, but it's NOT for everyone and I think the cutesy anime style trailers lure people into thinking it's simple. The video trailers also only play the pop songs and don't showcase the variety of music as you change biomes and/or import freeplay tunes.The story is just a very basic 'characters save the music realm' story. And I'm okay with that, because I'm here to play the levels anyway and they did a good job IMO of keeping it short and simple so you can just get to the next level and play more.Anyone who says the game is easy is lying. Look at the harder achieves. You start with songs on warm-up mode and can increase the difficulty from there all the way to lethal.If it's so easy, please show your platinum lethal achievement! <3

_childDocuments_.review: I like Soundfall. It's a good game. But it does fall short in a major way. Note to new players: TURN SOUND EFFECTS OFF!The reasoning: Soundfall expects you to hit buttons on the beat. This isn't new and shouldn't be an issue. The problem comes in the form of sound design. Games like this are made and broken on sound design and my biggest issue with Soundfall is that theirs is bad. Not just bad, but actively annoying to the point I turned off sound effects and immediately enjoyed the game far more. The noises your weapons, dash, etc make are not timed to the music. If I were designing this game I would either make these noises incredibly snappy - so much so that they need not be timed at all - or I would have introduced some small line of code that extended or shortened sound effects to start and end on beats.Unfortunately, the designers of Soundfall did neither of those things and the result is frustrating. If you dash or shoot or slash, you SHOULD contribute to the music. It should be fun, making and enhancing your own little beat. But instead, all your sound effects take way too long, end on a syncopated beat, and generally mess you up. Don't expect to have fun ad-libbing extra sounds to the beat like in "BPM: Bullets Per Minute", which does the snappy 'add your own sounds' well. I don't usually name drop other games in reviews, but I decided to this time so people could go look up what I mean for an example, since it's a sort of niche thing I'm describing. Instead, I recommend anyone playing Soundfall to turn their sound effects off.All that being said, I do like Soundfall if the sound effects are muted. I enjoy playing with friends, and it's rare you see a game like this with local multiplayer, so for that I give it a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: A different take on the rhythm game, it's the ultimate action human metronome simulator! Keep time and act on the beat for more powerful attacks and move bonuses. The premise is simple, but it will certainly take a few rounds to maximize your effectiveness. Mix things up a bit with different weapon types and heroes, all with different abilities. The game itself includes a wealth of tracks in a wide variety of musical genres.While the enemies are more of less the same, each musical genre creates one of a handful of dungeon types that have their own theme and hazards. The art is polished and the controls seem consistent enough. And there's a free play mode, so it's possible to relive a favorite tune or import your own right from the get-go.I'm a huge fan of music-based games, especially ones which allow custom tracks, so this was an easy sell for me. I haven't had any issues playing Mp3, Ogg/Vorbis, or Flac (after support was added). My only frustration is that some styles of music (such as those with uncommon time signatures, avante garde, or strangely, brass bands) confuse the tempo detection algorithm, causing the expected beat to sometimes vary wildly--even on tracks without tempo changes. So I often play with the metronome tone enabled, which helps me stay on beat when things get weird. Overall, I'd recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Every since I bought this game, I've been absolutely addicted to it, while most of my other games are sitting on the sideline.  I just keep coming back to this.  I read the negative reviews before purchasing and still bought it.  19 hours in, I don't regret it (note I did get it on sale).  I understand the comments in the negative reviews and they are basically on point, with two exceptions: 1) I am in the 2nd phase of the game and have started getting a few legendaries with far from perfect play; 2) There is more change in the enemy behaviour and abilities than some imply, though yes they are still variations on the ones you see in the first few stages.  But they make a big difference in play, along with some environmental hazards, etc.  So there is enough variation for my taste (though I was worried it wouldn't be enough variation early on).The thing is, it really comes down to what you want.  Is it repetitive?  Sure, but not in any bad way.  Every game is repetitive in is own way, from big AAA grindy looter shooters to roguelikes, etc.).  What has kept me coming back to this game is the music, the joy of playing a twin-stick shooter to the beat of fun music, a bright and colorful art style.  It is just simple fun.If you are looking for some kind of mechanically deep shooter or something with a lot of complex play & lots of boss fights, etc. then this isn't the game for you.  If you like music and bopping to a rhythm in your chair, and straight-forward pew-pew gameplay than can get quite challenging as you pump up the difficulty, then you will enjoy this game.  Don't come to this came looking for something serious.  Come to this game to enjoy some music, smile and just have pure fun.  In fact, it is the challenging, while still feeling light & non-stressful, approach that makes me love the game.I will agree the story is nothing to write home about.  It is kind of cute, sometimes a bit too much, but it is there and gone.  I wish the art that went with the character dialog had varied expressions.  They are always fixed in generally the same silly grin or overly serious face, even when they are getting exasperated, etc.  You can fortunately turn off repeating dialog when replaying stages (though you could skip it any time if you wanted).  So once you go through it, you don't have to go through to it again.I will also agree that not all of the music is the best choice.  I loved many, liked most, wasn't a fan of some others (but those are the minority).  Fortunately, I don't have to return to those stages if I don't want to.  And I can import whatever music I want (and earn rewards playing them--that is where I got my first legendary).  So you don't have to worry about it once you've played the stage once.I will share that I had trouble at first playing.  It took me a while to realize that variable delay in my bluetooth headset made it impossible to keep on beat consistently.  I kept re-calibrating over and over to no avail.  Once I used only wired headsets, all was good and I could enjoy the game as it was meant to be played.So if what I described sounds like something that you'd enjoy, then you would not regret purchasing this game.  Otherwise, it isn't for you and that is okay.

_childDocuments_.review: Soundfall is a very interesting experience. There is so much about it to love, and yet there are a few things that hold this back from being a truly incredible game. I'll discuss this further.I want to start with the animation. It was so incredibly stunning. I wish there had been more cut scenes just so we could've seen more moments of this beautiful work. The character designs and concepts were really fun, so seeing the animation was just so lovely. In general, the art for this game was awesome. I wish the characters had been more fleshed out, as they were a bit trope-y and didn't go very deep. Regardless, the designs and animation were such a positive of this game.The level design was where the game was a bit weak in my opinion. Many of the levels repeated, or were re-skinned. Now, I wouldn't normally think much of this, to be honest, but because each world had about ten levels or so, it got a bit repetitive. It would've been nice for things to switch up.The music was overall, fantastic. I found so much new music from playing this game and I really enjoyed MOST of the songs. There were a few that didn't tickle my fancy, but that's simply a personal preference. I did, however, find some songs difficult to find the beat? I think it was cause most of the songs followed the BPM and it didn't always 100% match with the flow of the song. I made sure to calibrate my computer as well for lag, etc. To be honest, I think the main reason I enjoyed this game was because I liked being able to zen out and just play through the levels and listen to the music. If you're looking for a decently chill game with a bit of challenge, I think this game could be for you. I'm not sure if I would replay it, but I can imagine going back and playing through some of my favorite songs. There are definitely some flaws, but overall I found it to be an enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun and unique game! I love the idea and it's done well, but there are a few issues that others have pointed out.Some songs change tempo, maybe speeding up at parts or slowing down at the end. This makes the gameplay a lot harder to keep up with, but I did find that turning the metronome on in the sound settings helped.Songs have different tempos. In terms of difficulty, it's not an issue, but it actually makes some abilities worse. I love playing Brite but her shield has a resting period of 4 beats, so for some songs I can use it frequently, but for others, I have to wait longer. It makes the ability inconsistent and frustrating to use at times.Another issue with Brite - why is the resting period 4 beats? If I do a quick shield block, maybe to deflect projectiles or to knock an enemy back, the cooldown should be 3 beats. It's very jarring to have to wait 1 measure and 1 beat until I can use it again.Some people have mentioned that the gameplay gets repetitive, and I do see that a bit. Increasing the difficulty helps by adding new types of enemies, but like I said above, your abilities rely on the tempo of the song, so while more enemies appear that can spam their attacks whenever they want, you're restricted to the tempo of the song.Last quirk - I may be using it wrong, but it seems like the minuet perk doesn't work most of the time. It's supposed to heal you for a percentage of the damage you deal, but on multiple occasions, I've used minuet weapons and abilities and haven't gotten any healing. There's actually a quest to do 2,000 self-healing with minuet and in all of my playtime, I'm only at 100 or so healing. If the healthbars don't regenerate on their own after a period of time of no damage, minuet should proc more consistently. EDIT: According to the known bugs, minuet not activating in multiplayer is a known problem, so a fix should come soon!However, this game is special and there really isn't anything like it out there. I love the different types of weapons and characters that all allow you to create your own playstyle, and it's really cool to get a groove going and wipe waves of enemies out. The aesthetics are great most of the time (but thing can get messy, especially in co-op when your player is pink but all of the enemies and abilities are also pink), I like most of the music choices, and it's overall a very fun game. Hopefully these issues can be addressed in future updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic idea for a game! Unfortunately, not a good execution. Imported music is only local and very rarely (if ever) syncs up the beat properly. If you wanted to play with imported music you would likely have to generate your own beat patterns and import that into the game using external programs.The default songs chosen for this game are not the greatest as a fair number will have unique singing or even silence disrupting the users ability to maintain the beat pattern.This last one is my opinion: I don't think dash I-frames should be tied to the beat. This feature will never be convenient in the chaotic bullet hell of higher difficulties and can only be utilized to dodge very specific environmental AOE hazards. Dashing to the beat should reset dash cooldown or increase dash distance instead. I understand this may just be a frustration that only I experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Backed this game back in 2018 or something. Have been waiting for it for a long time, and it was worth the wait.Can be played alone, but is best played with friends. Fun rythm dungeon-crawler where all actions needs to be done to the beat for it to take best effect which is a cool mechanic I appreciate!Game has its own calibrator, so if your monitor had input lag, and audio is delayed, this calibrator will with it for you to make sure you hear and hit the beat at the same time :)The story is simple and intriguing and progression is good.Multiplayer disclaimer: You wound start with 4 different characters. _childDocuments_.review: I backed this game during their Fig campaign because I love music/rhythm games and this seemed like it would be a unique take on the genre. While the game isn't perfect, it is pretty much what I wanted and expected it to be. The core gameplay loop is pretty basic and can get repetitive, but I enjoy the soundtrack enough to not mind that so much. I also look forward to trying to import some of my own tracks after I finish the main story and see how they play. It seems really hard to get platinum medals on levels (maybe I'm just not that good), and I also find some songs much harder to stay on beat with than others. However, if you are looking for a unique take on the rhythm genre, this is definitely worth trying out. If you love this genre as much as I do, buy it now. If it's not your favorite genre but you are curious, wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is a cautious recommendation.I was able to beat the story fairly quickly, around 9 hours, and the story was amusing throughout along with the characters. Each of the characters played uniquely with regards to their instrument and ultimate, which appealed to me and I switched characters around quite a bit through my playthrough. Each of the different maps felt good initially, but for ten stages per map it always felt like it overstayed its welcome by the 9th stage. There were also a lot of stages on each map that felt pretty derivative of one another.The loot portion of the game I feel needs some tweaking. It doesn't feel rewarding only to get one or two pieces of gear per level on the lower difficulties. That being the case, I didn't feel compelled to play stages at higher difficulties as it felt like enemies were bullet sponges. There should have been a tutorial on the different weapon types as well in my opinion. Lastly, the UI feels a little under cooked.The game is fun and has a lot of personality. The characters and the art direction are definitely the highlights. My enjoyment of the core gameplay loop was definitely diminished over the course of the repetitive level design. I think if you really enjoy rhythm games you could wait for a sale on this title.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I love this new "beat-based" sub-genre that seems to be cropping up. Crypt of the NecroDancer, Mad Rat Dead, Bullets per Minute and now this.There are a few problems I have, such as the difficulty options being stingy late into the game (why do I have to hit the level cap to unlock the hardest difficulty?), some of the music choices were a bit "meh" (especially in Worlds 8 and 9 - they were definitely a bit front-heavy with the good music, as World 1 has my favourite tracks!), plus the enemy variety was a bit basic with you constantly seeing minor variations on the same enemy types in the higher difficulties. Despite all that though, I REALLY enjoyed this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but I strongly suggest you get it on sale.I just finished the game, which for only a 20 hour game (faster if you blaze through without repeating any levels for loot and doing the extra missions) the fact that I'm in the < 1% who did according the achievements should say a lot.I went back and forth on this recommendation, but eventually my love for the core gameplay loop won out, despite the numerous issues. Since the pros should be obvious (fun and unique rhythm based twin-stick looter shooter), I'll stick with the cons and list my feedback/suggestions for the devs.I played every level at the highest difficulty available to me. After the 3rd difficulty no new enemies appear, just more enemies with more attacks and more health. More & more & more & more. There are only 2 unique bosses in the entire game as well, meaning that the end of each biome is just a capoff with sometimes HUNDREDS of the same enemy. Fun? Yes. Interesting? No. More enemy variety, more bosses.There are 100+ songs by default, but they are mostly royalty free. So while there are some good tracks I actually added to my personal playlist, most I would never be able to tell you a thing about again. I know it's costly, especially as an indie studio, but some more unique songs, especially licensed ones or ones made FOR Soundfall, would be ideal.As others have pointed out, BPM trumps all in this game. Which is... not ideal? To say the least. There are times where there are just no audio cues to go on, so you better have perfectly matched your finger to the BPM or start looking at the metronome.  Any song that has lulls needs to go. If possible, manually increase the volume of the beat in existing songs that are not clear what the BPM is being based on.Oh boy, okay, this is where I probably have my largest complaint. First off - If anyone ever gets the "Multiplatinum" achievement, which at time of writing no one seems to have done, then you deserve a handmade trophy from the developers. It requires you to beat every song at the highest difficulty with a Platinum ranking. What does a platinum ranking entail? A. Beating the song B. Beating the song before it loops C. Beating it without dropping your chain (which drops if you don't do an on-beat action in a set amount of time, or take damage), and D. Every button press you do (besides joystick movement) has to be on beat. So basically, perfection on each song at the highest difficulty.Even on difficulty 4 (of 6), the last difficulty you can unlock before beating the game at least once, I sometimes could only get bronze despite being 13 levels higher than the recommendation. Levels seem sporadically planned out, some with so few enemies I could finish 1+ minute early, and others so filled with enemies (and constantly respawning waves) that even though I could room clear in a few seconds there was no way I could get to the end of the song in time.And I'm supposed to do that, at the highest difficulty, while never getting hit and keeping 100% on beat? For every song?? Suddenly Elden Ring seems like a Edutainment game in comparison. Go through each level, at each difficulty, and tune it more appropriately. There are multiple times on difficulty 4 I'd have ~20 seconds to clear the room (according to the progress tracker), but there would be so many waves of enemies that there's no way I'd clear it in less than 40 seconds to a minute.Adding to the difficulty is the enemy design. Most are decent to good. But some shoot quiet projectiles at you, and a lot of them, which can blend in with the music and background. Most of my hits in this game were not from actually making an honest mistake, but more because I just didn't see what hit me. On top of that, some enemies just waste your time. They can block attacks for 5+ seconds before exposing themselves for a few moments to charge you. Try to dodge behind them? They turn with you. You just sit, and wait. Oh, and they have enough health that dumping 20+ beats worth of ammo into them is still not enough. Oh, and your on a timer, if you remember point #4. It's mind boggling. Enemy projectiles should always be loud and noticable. Enemies that just block your attacks no matter what should be changed. Enemy health in general, especially on the tankier enemies, needs to be slashed. I'll keep this brief - The latter biomes just have way too much going on, trap wise. The traps stopped being unique and just became a game of "more, more, more." Compounded with the number of enemies, the enemy health, the timer, and trying to play PERFECTLY, it's just overwhelming. Keep tracks unique, and keep them limited. They should be used as an interesting challenge, not as a band-aid for difficulty.  After all of that, I wouldn't be surprised if you thought I hated this game. But the core gameplay loop is so fun, I just couldn't stop playing. That's why I want it to be the best it can, this game has a lot of potential but just... isn't fully there right now. I hope the developers see this and understand my feedback is in earnest, and I only want to see the game improve. Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game and I can see that a lot of care and love was put into it, but I didn't. The only reason for this is that I don't feel the beat of the song compared to what I get in the game. For me it seems that the bar you are matching the beat on just goes fast, medium or slow depending on the song and there has to be a very noticeable slowdown or a quiet period in the song for that to be reflected on the bar.So for me it's like playing a good twin stick shooter with a nice colorful visual theme with my own selection of songs for the music which is great but then I misstime a few presses and suddenly I can't shoot or if not timed correctly I can't dodge so the main gimmick of the game is stopping me from enjoying it and getting in that shooter transe. While at the same time if I get them correctly they don't seem to correspond with the song (even the free ones included with the game) to a degree where I can get really pumped up and destry my mouse or joystick.It's hard to explain, imagine playing this to Dragonforce which I did and expecting the guitar solo, when it hits all hell breaks loose, a boss or champion appears and you start shooting like a mad man. Instead you get a few enemies if you are in the right spot since they seem to have pre-defined spawn locations on the tiles used for the levels and you have to shoot just a bit faster than you did before, barely noticeable.I like the graphics and that you can import your own songs on PC. The loot and enemies are interesting. Maybe I'm just tone deaf and I don't get the point. I like the idea of games that incorporate music to a larger degree but so far I only really enjoyed Beat Hazard. Still this gets a thumbs up since everything else seems great and maybe my expectations were too high.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, where to start this off...First of all i am a MASSIVE fan of rhythm games. I bought this on XBOX at release, and once i found out PC had custom music, i just HAD to get it so i could shoot/slice up the landscape to my favorite tunes.Overall, this game has a ton of potential and i hope the Devs work on this game more as it gets farther from the release date.There are a few main pros and cons that i like about this game so if i haven't bored you senseless here ya go:PROS:*Great Loot System            -Overall, the variations of guns are AWESOME the "elements" of guns are the various effects are really cool and i don't think there is a single gun that i don't enjoy with the exception of the guns that mitigate the penalty for shooting off-beat (because i am a pleb). The armor, while basic, also has some really enjoyable modifiers. One thing i would change however is maybe have multiple types of armor with different effects rather than just bonus health. It would help to further enhance the differences of play-styles. The weapons are all really cool and i love how each characters weapon functions differently even if its just a slight difference. *Catchy Music (10/10, its a music game)         -The music they choose for the game, is really catchy and it helps make the gameplay more enjoyable. There are a few songs that don't exactly fit but most of them are some of my new favorite electronic songs BY FAR.  There is a little pause before the song starts again that tends to throw players off but that seems to be a common complaint.*Scenery          -THE SCENERY MOVES TO THE MUSIC AND AHHHHHH I LOVE IT SO MUCH.....sorry....i just think its really cool and it gets me into this mind-numbing state where i am just playing the game without even thinking as my leg bounces up and down to the beat while i play.*Gameplay          -The actual gameplay mechanics are awesome and very easy to learn. I love the fact that there is auto aim with a controller (IDK about mouse and keyboard i still use a controller: refer to above...i am pleb). It's a easy to learn hard to master system if you're like me and accidentally get caught up in the mayhem and forget i need to be dodging projectiles.*Animations          -The little animations during parts of the story are really neat and they help enhance the experience ten-fold!*CO-OP          -The CO-OP is seamless and playing local is incredibly fun. I love that for steam when you add a local user they just copy your items so they aren't starting at level 1. (This also means my inventory now has two sets of gear, one that my friend likes and one that i like).CONS:*Repetition          -The levels feel very similar after a while and other than traps and such it feels like it's just playing the same level over and over with a different sound track. *Characters          -I tend to enjoy playing free-play a lot more than the story and i was bummed when i bought this on XBOX to find that i had to progress in the story before getting to unlock different characters (This is a minor dislike i understand why they did it and its not that hard to b-line through the story to get the characters)*Leveling         -Leveling up gets hard asf at a certain point and it gets a bit grindy*Difficulty (Kind-of?)         -The difficulty settings are level locked which hurts if the game is too easy for you yet you aren't high enough level*Conflict of Interest         -The silver badge is to complete the level before the song ends but it also encourages you to explore and find loot zones.....BRUHTLDR: There are a few minor issues and one major issue, but other than that i absolutely love this game. I understand that a game just out of release made by a smaller company is bound to not be perfect, and for how it is so far i am very much looking forward to the future of this game.QOL IMPROVEMENTSFew QoL additions/features that i would like to see added in the future-Choose biomes for custom songs-The ability to level up items somehow (although this can discourage trying out new items)-The ability to save profiles and have local co-op use those profiles (This is just for pc, consoles already do this with accounts)-The ability to favorite songs for freeplay-The ability to enter in the BPM for a song in game (it would be a simpler fix than the current workaround for when a custom song is finicky)- Beat based puzzles maybe?-Terrain that changes with the beat, like elevators, moving platforms etc...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything you make of it. Single player and co-op both feel amazing, the songs are wonderful, even if some may not be your preferred genre, and lets you play how you want -- revolutionary for a rhythm game imo. You can import your own songs and play to your favorites -- even if sometimes you need to create a custom beatmap to make it flow just right. The style of the graphics are pretty yet simple, and bright yet versatile to boot.What I will say is, if you're looking at this game solely on the looter/shooter aspect, make sure the game is for you first. Though you can do a lot of things with your builds in this game, don't expect this to have any hardcore min-maxxing. The game isn't perfect, but for what it is I absolutely adore this game, will probably get even more time than I already have from this game as of the time of this post, and desperately hope for more content/DLC/updates as I want more reasons to play this game! This has been a go-to stress relieving game, and also a game just to sit back, enjoy, and even be challenged by!

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a middle option for reviews, as having only yes or no kind’ve forces you to swing a certain way. So, despite enjoying the game myself and certainly recommending it to some, I’m voting ‘Not Recommended’ in hopes the devs will take notice of some critiques. I wrote down my thoughts, and would be remiss if I didn’t post it and add my voice in the mix in hopes things may change for the better!NOTE: I have unlocked all the characters and put in a fair bit of playtime, but I've yet to beat the 'story' mode, or play online, and I’ll try to keep this review ‘spoiler free’, but I want to lay out my thoughts as I go through the game, as it hits a sweet spot for me and I just HAVE to write a review, and hopefully give others insight if they're on the fence and maybe the devs will notice if this game picks up off the ground. I try to go into detail about my reasoning for things and can be a bit long winded, but if you're fine with all that, read on, else check out my final thoughts at the bottom!Pros:+ The soundtrack, obviously. It’s varied and there’s a whole bunch of variety in genres.+ Soundfall lets you drop right into the entire playlist of the game’s ~100 songs, with the added bonus of being able to import your own. (Note *1)+ Controls are snappy, it feels like a blast to play. The game itself seems very polished.+ A decent variety in character abilities, there's bound to be something there for every type of player to carve their own play style. (Note *2)Cons:-  Some of the equipment mechanics are locked behind rarer loot tiers (e.g. double/triple dash, longer ultimates, more range, etc.) which make the lower tiers immediately feel bland upon trying them out. There is also no infusion/upgrade system to bring your favorite weapons up to par. This leaves players out of luck later when they find a rare weapon at low level.- The game too slowly drip-feeds you exp, mechanics, characters and difficulty, which could bore some players at the outset before things pick up in the late game. Character unlocks are tied to story progression, which makes getting to 'new' things feel a bit sluggish. Plus, if you  play free play and ignore the story, you’re stuck with  playable character. (Note *3)- Levels within the same 'biome' feel samey, procedural generation could be to blame and might benefit from more varied path 'tiles'. For a game with procedural generation, the song is the same, every time, except via higher difficulties, but that only changes the monsters you encounter, not the layout. Every time I know exactly what to expect, and while it can be good for mastering a song in a rhythm game, it does not work well for a grindy looter-shooter with freeform movement and gunplay. (Note *4)* Note *1 - One of the characters is nearly identical to another with some seemingly minor tweaks to their skillset, while not game-breaking, feels a bit underwhelming after playing the others, which are more vastly different in comparison.* Note *2 - The imported song generation can work great on some songs, but is also fickle, as some songs will straight up be off beat on import. Though the devs have posted a third party workaround which is neat, albeit a slight bit convoluted for the 'average' gamer.* Note *3 - I feel the exp curve should be half of what it is, as unlocking higher difficulties can feel grindy and slow. It’s also unfortunate that because of the way the game is structured with power level, lower difficulties become ‘obsolete’ because you gain power over time, so pairing someone new to the game with people who’ve already mastered it just doesn’t mesh well. Unlocking characters is tied to story progression, so while jumping into freeplay play from the get-go is nice, you can’t unlock the more varied characters, so you may as well just play the campaign if you don’t want to import music. Speaking of importing music brings me to my next point.* Note *4 - There is no way to customize an imported song’s biome - Sometimes an EDM song can make a volcano biome (usually attributed to Rock), sometimes a rock song can put you on the beach, or in the jungle. As stated above, most biomes feel samey, and would benefit from a bit more variety of path and battle tiles. There’s also NO way to play the ‘arena’/gauntlet type levels with custom songs. They seem to be tied to the end of stages in story mode, and that’s the only way to play them. Slightly disappointing, as the option to play a wave-based type stage with your own songs would be a very cool addition to this type of game considering you only need to spawn enemies in a designated area, rather than generate level tiles to walk through. Speaking of walking through levels…* Note *5 - The game incentivizes completing a stage before its designated song is over, but there’s also explorable areas off the beaten path that could yield some reward. The better rewards are tied to better rankings at the end of the level, which seems sort of counter intuitive to exploring a level for more loot- Though getting loot this way can also yield rare items, and can in turn de-incentive people to getting good at the song and just rushing for the hidden chests.* Sometimes on the menu songs wouldn't keep previous difficulty, as in I'd start a song on Challenging, and either swap menus or win, then the song would be back at Warmup.* When a song ends, it takes a few seconds to start again, which can throw off players trying to keep a beat against mobs of monsters in silence.* There is no option to ‘favorite’ a song. While not game-breaking, this is kind of a standard in most rhythm games, being able to load up your favorite toons quickly is one of the reasons folks come back. Without it, it feels like a bit of an annoyance. Some quality of life updates would really help this game survive in the long run.* Upon researching, this game started as a backer game on fig.co, there are some stretch goals that seem not yet implemented, or stripped entirely. There’s no DJ or playlist mode, no playable instruments, or new skins for the playable characters, and no Twitch integration to speak of. Either way, it seems the game’s been in development since even before the last part of 2018, so they’ve clearly had time to iron out some kinks, and seem to have some community presence. 2020 took its toll on a lot of people, so perhaps some things had to be scrapped for the sake of putting the game out. Take that for what you will.This game overall has a lot of love put into it, and clearly shows there’s thought behind all the systems and is not only gorgeous and fun to play, but also technically sound, it's unfortunately held back from greatness by some seemingly strange loot/exp mechanics and shallow replay value, that hopefully could be rectified if enough people speak up and the devs take notice. Due to this being a unique, possibly niche game, and an indie developer, I want to be able to say I’ll cut Soundfall some slack. It’s a very good base, and I would definitely look forward to a sequel, though I feel this game might have benefited from being early access or playtested more by their target audience for feedback before release. In spite of that, the game feels polished, structurally sound, and is of decent quality.If you're new to rhythm games, or are put off by the loot system or procedural generation,  I love this game's premise, and it's really up my alley. I personally enjoy it, and despite the ‘Not Recommended’ label, if you enjoy things like Just Shapes and Beats, Crypt of the Necrodancer, Diablo-esque games, or twin stick shooters/bullet hells plus rhythm games,  you can handle the gripes I’ve listed here, I can recommend giving this game a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game, although far from perfect. Just putting up front I actually recommend this game, and if it looks fun you should buy it. The rest of this review I've GOTTA complain though. Just a couple points that are kind of worth noting before you purchase:1. Some of the music is very poorly chosen for a rhythm game. Very early into the campaign you hit a forest area that mostly uses orchestral music that is VERY difficult to follow the rhythm of, and in some cases have BPMs that are ridiculously high that seem to be incorrect and make the game WAY harder?? The choices are occasionally baffling. Most of the music is great though and works great but especially in world 2 so far there are some songs you just have to drag yourself through.2. Importing music barely works. If your song has ANY tempo changes, breakdowns, or anything that takes a consistent hard hitting kick out of the song expect the beat to get thrown off. There's a guide on how to make your own beatmaps that is really appreciated, but it's a hassle and in my experience also sometimes doesn't work at all. You'll create your own beatmap and for some songs the game just will refuse to use it and will instead use the very bad in-game algorithm instead. If you're looking at this to play exclusively your own music, i'm not sure I can really recommend it.3. There's a lot of sound effects that don't hit on the beat and also only really serve to throw you off and make the game less fun. My honest suggestion is before even starting to go into the settings and turn sound fx volume to around 40%, and also enable the metronome to play when you haven't hit a note on-beat in a while. It really helps.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for about 7 hours, and there is a lot that I like here. Very satisfying action gameplay, and I hope it goes deeper the longer I play. The ability to add your own songs is very awesome and I wish more games did that. One of the nitpicks I have is that at the end the the level, the music just abruptly stops, and for a game all about the music, there has to be a more elegant way to fade out the level gracefully. I also know that there is a way to edit the BPM for custom tracks, but I haven't been able to make Audacity work like the Devs did in the video, I feel like they skipped some steps on how to install the plugin. With custom songs, this game is practically endless, and I wonder how deep the rabbit hole goes with progression. Speaking of progression, I do wish there were just a few more variations of weapons, I feel like I'm just trading between two weapon types any time there are stronger ones. Anyway, there are more pros than cons, and I am looking forward to sinking my teeth into the rest of the game. 8/10, would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: As a lifelong musician, I find this game really fun. I'm usually not really into shooters but this one has managed to keep my attention for 6 hours at the time of this review. It's just so satisfying to play! Graphics are nice, singleplayer runs very smoothly despite a lot of stuff happening on screen, and I was pleasantly surprised to find that its soundtrack has many different styles of music. My only critique is that a lot of the songs don't loop properly, so you end up with several seconds of silence in the middle of battle, which makes it incredibly hard to keep the beat if you're playing with no metronome. Also some songs have weird intros/outros where it's impossible to hear the beat because it's just ambiance. I've died many times due to losing the beat because the song stopped playing in order to loop itself. That can be really frustrating. But if you're playing with the metronome on at all times I'd say I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The first time i saw this game was at Pax Australia in 2018/19. It was a beautiful demo of the game showcasing the mechanics and style of game play i would come to expect. The way the game felt then was absolutely amazing, I loved doing everything in the game along to the beat of the music! Shooting enemies, dashing through obstacles, jumping up to different areas, even going as far as to having the character's walking pace matching with the music!Fast forward to 2022, having waited 3 years for the game's final release, I have to say i'm nothing less than amazed at how far the game had come. The story is amazing, the art is beautiful, and the game play is even more fluent than the demo i played those few years ago!Not only that, but the ability to put any song I have into the game, load it up and the game will automatically generate a map for me to play along to the beat of that song just makes it all that much better!Sound fall is a beautiful game for any and all to enjoy! You won't regret getting this!

_childDocuments_.review: This slaps, full stop. If you enjoy Crypt of the Necrodancer and you'd be into a more mobile and fluid take on the concept, well...strap in. I love the fact that it's multiplayer, the story is cute, the mechanics are fun and the added benefit of playing to your own music is really inspired. _childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: This game mixes some really neat game mechanics to create a really fun and unique experience. The core premise of tying all of your character actions to the beat of the song is actually very satisfying when timed correctly. I think this is in part due to the excellent sound design of the game, which gives some really nice audio feedback with on-beat attacks and dashes. Once you get in the groove of it, you really start to feel like your playing a part in composing the song, using the notes from the weapons and dashes mixed together. Overall, I think this is a fantastic game so far. The mechanics and aesthetic are combined artfully into a must-experience package.That said, I do think there are some design elements that feel a little rough around the edges to me. They don't detract from the experience as a whole, but I think these are some things that could make the overall experience of play just a little tighter and feel more complete.1. The cursor for item select is difficult to see with the current ui design. The box-in-a-box-in-a-box thing it has going on could really benefit from a bigger visual distinction between the cursor and the item slots (like maybe a beating red dot inside the selected item or something like that).2. The Gold tracker feels out of place where it currently is. I think it would make more sense to put it near the store page, since that's where its spent.3. Speaking of the store, I don't think it serves much purpose to close the inventory/store page when the cursor is over the current inventory. I think it would streamline the visual inspection of your loot if that panel is just always open.4. I'm not sure if this is an issue later in the game, but it feels weird that the rythmic blaster (a submachine gun) and the scattershot (a blunderbuss) share the same weapon skin when the stable scattershot (another blunderbuss) is visually different from the former version.5. It would really help with item experimentation to have a training area in the menus to try out equipment before setting of on a deployment.6.  The character swap tutorial spoils the whole cast! It should really only have Jax and Melody as the example characters in there.7. Lastly, this is probably a non-issue since it likely only comes up once early on for everyone, but I feel like the prologue cutscene was too terse. It went from Melody talking to her room mate about having to drop her audition to keep her job to a cutscene where she puts on headphones, without some sort of story transition like "I'll think about it later, right now I just wanna not think about anything for a while." or something to that effect. The way it reads to me as it is right now, if feels like Melody blew off a heavy subject with her room mate to go to her own world (literally haha).Anyway, these are my personal thoughts on the first few hours of the game, and overall I think it was a very positive experience. I'm looking forward to seeing what else the game has in store for us players!
