_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Well first off, I don't really play games like these. I usually like playing shorter games that have more instant results with more action. However, as soon as I played the demo for this I was really interested in this world the story have started to carve out. When I started beyong the demo, this entire ecosystem of the world opened up to me slowly through interacting with the environment, people and how the system works. As someone who enjoys a good story, this is definitely one that draws you in. The art is polished and immersive, the characters you bond with stay with you after you finish the game, and the gameplay is quite simple- you select your choice of answers and questions and explore the general area. What still impacts me is the characters- the game makes you care for them and connect with them, and the choices that impact them negatively or positively will affect you as well. There's a couple of moments in the game where I gasped out loud and was stunned :p I feel like after I finished this game, you feel this sort of (good) empty feeling after reading a good book- where you went on an adventure and it finally ends.. and now what do you do with your life? haha Overall really enjoyed this game and I am very hopeful for this studio's next game- I think they're really creating art and I can't wait to see what else they will create in the future!

_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: I've been on quite a Visual Novel binge lately, and I have to say that 2024 has been one of the best years for this genre that has created a genuine impression of authentic emotions, story, and character development, not only with Minds Beneath Us, but with so many others. While the game is extremely slow in terms of interaction time and progression more so than action and adrenaline, if you can stick with it throughout those long sessions, you'll be greatly rewarded with a gripping emotional story. Your choices here have a huge impact on your connections with coworkers, love life, and general interactions with people all around the world, especially with the persons life that you are currently taking over. Everyone has a personality, rather than just being background characters making it feel very real in a sense.On the surface, the game appears to be simple with its expressionless figures, yet they are capable of conveying a wide range of emotions through body language, which is wonderful. Simply put, this is a slower-paced iteration of the Visual Novel genre similar to things like Night in the woods, very engaging, and emotionally connected with your moral responsibility to the authority and yourself in this dystopian society.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: It has typical cyberpunk style of story, where "corporations always win, necessary evil and you're the loser no matter what" etc etc...Not very much of a game as it is practically a visual novel and I can see that it could possibly get boring to some people, since there's a lot of dialogue and no voice acting.But at least in a visual novel, I'd be able to go through entire different routes, but here, although I do get to choose one of two different departments in MC's work with its own quirks for a tiny part of the game chapters, in the end, all the choices in the game boil down to same 4 ending options, no matter what, with the difference being the aftermath of your game choices shown before the credits...And I really wished they made proper CGs or something, since I did like character art shown in the game page, but there's nothing like that in the game...Now I do have to inform, it is essentially a woke chinese game, which is kinda weird, but it is. Nothing too extreme, didnt annoy me too much, except for the dialogue in first 2-3 chapters. The "woke" part is light, but quite typical. While I expected them represented in a game that's set in 2049, LGBT couples get more highlighted in the game, you can withness their confession and talk to them about it, even hinted at almost catching them having sex, but main character and his girlfriend doesnt get as much romance or at all, just few short conversations. Game character art made me think 23 and Nin Situ are male characters, until I played the game to learnt those are female (as of course lesbian) characters in the game's cover art. Every major authority character is a female and of course the male authority characters are one or two and they are the villains, it was kind of funny in a way considering the age we're living in. But none of that made it too bad of an experience for me, what actually pissed me off is when they started talking about politics in the first few chapters, like for real, I get that its a chinese game, but the MCs girlfriend promoting communism was just dumb, props to the game allowing to call that out, but it was pushed aside at laughed at, as if we're just "misunderstanding". Same with other conversations promoting one side of politics over the other, but its being done in a way that almost seems like a parody, a meme or a criticism towards it, considering how idealistic its being portrayed to the point where the characters look delutional, but you can tell the developers want to promote those things to you, but dont realize what they are actually saying or what it means. Once they were done talking about politics, the game felt much better.To top it all off, the game tries sequel baiting. There were things that were left unanswered on purpose.It wasnt too bad, but if I could choose again, I'd probably not buy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: A nuanced and refreshing take on the cyberpunk genre where the priority is not violence and combat mechanics, but rather on journeying through ethical and interpersonal conflicts that make you question your own value systems. Story is well-paced, engaging, and full of wisdom. 100% recommend--this is a GEM. I'll be keeping an eye out for future releases from this studio.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and loved playing out the story that the devs developed. The story, and the things that you find out as it unfolds, is engaging and I loved the concept. It was unsettling enough to make me care about the characters and the outcome of the story. I also loved the art and the combination of 2D and 3D. Overall, I would definitely recommend this game to anyone that is looking for something new to play.With that being said, there are some negatives/cons of the game that did stick with me.I think it's quite evident in the trailer, but this game has NO voice acting, so you will be reading all of the text dialogue on your own. As someone who reads to help myself fall asleep, I will admit that I fell asleep during some parts of the game. Partly due to having to read the dialogue and partly because I was at a boring part. I easily put 10+ hours into this game, so if you think this is going to deter you from playing the game, then maybe don't play it and watch a playthrough if you're really curious about the story.The middle of the game/story is the weakest section of the whole game, in my opinion. Beginning and ending of the game are engaging since you're finding out new information and fighting to end the battle, respectively. However, I think the middle of the game is kind of lackluster and I feel like it's not very memorable. Once you get through the middle, it does ramp up well and the story gets exciting again.This is more of a smaller issue, but when I got to about the last quarter of the game, there was this glitch where characters were disappearing and flickering during conversation. I saw that at least one other person had this issue in the Bear Bone discord, so I hope this is an issue that they patch soon. Closing the game and restarting it fixed the problem. Also, some spelling and grammatical errors for the english version, but again, not that much of an issue.TL;DR: There are some issues, but I think they're minor in the grand scheme of things. Give the game a shot, it's pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: From the narrative and visual perspective, I would definitely recommend to play through the game. Even though it is mostly a book, really. Visual novel would probably be the best tag for this game. However, I do feel a little lied to, as the entire story feels like it's building up to the main character becoming someone bigger and better. We are left at the end of the story going in that direction that I expected to start with. In that sense it was a let down. The real lesson I've learned after first playthrough is that the main character is not you. Without giving up any spoilers, your job in this story is to team up with the main character in this story. Yes, you do make important choices. But all choices that actually impact the narrative are shoehorned into the story precisely to give you the false sense of being the center of it.It's really hard to be satisfied with this story when you're in chapter 4 and still waiting for your character to start being "the hero" of it. Again, despite my disapproval of this decision, I would still recommend the game because its very affordable and it has a lot of positives going for it. I just would wish someone told me before playing that I should not expect to become the cyberpunk equivalent of Captain America, which is literally something the story tells you you WILL become. Just off screen after the end. This felt cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible. I loved the moral questions and situations that this game has the player think through. There were so many deep conversations that I absolutely adored. _childDocuments_.review: It's pretty hard to find video games with compelling and moving narratives like this that make me reflect on my life decisions thus far. Without going into spoilers, I can say that this game is very philosophical, with strictly no right or wrong answers. It will force you to make tough choices. Moral dilemmas will be forced onto you. Sometimes even make you feel guilty for doing the "right" thing. Perhaps there is no black-and-white except for the principles we make for ourselves, and Minds Beneath Us will make you re-evaluate them in uncomfortable ways.It's with this setting in mind that the game's narrative is mostly built around the perceived illusion of choice in the grand scheme of things. Unless you happen to be extremely rich and/or powerful (and you probably aren't, otherwise you wouldn't be reading this), you are nothing. Even the choices you make seem insignificant because the world keeps spinning regardless of your actions, but Minds Beneath Us reminds us to be kind to ourselves and the people around us. At the end of the day, we still matter. We are our own most important person, and it's not necessarily wrong to be selfish. The game's narrative constantly reminds us that the world can be a cruel cesspool, that we inevitably do what we can to survive, sometimes even stepping on others, but also subtly urges us to make decisions with empathy. Because no matter how screwed up and hopeless everything seems to be, we can still make small changes that feel like they mean the world to ourselves and those we love and care about. The consequences of our actions, no matter how small and insignificant, still fully exist in tangible ways that we may not be able to predict. Minds Beneath Us reminded me of some moments in my life when I felt that I should have just ceded control of my life to the whims of fate, only for me to decide to stand my ground in the end. Things didn't always turn out favourably in the end, but at least I was glad I tried. What mattered the most was that I could live with myself and the decisions I made. Accept myself for what I am, mostly. I could look myself in the eye with some degree of pride at least, mixed with some shame. Still proud nonetheless.Admittedly, when I first saw the reviews for this game, I wasn't convinced that it could be so well-regarded with 9/10 or 10/10 scores everywhere. Feels like I'm jaded, cynical and bitter enough to regard everything online with a pinch of salt, what with rampant disinformation, echo chambers and state-controlled media these days. I'm glad I gave this one a chance. I think you should too.  Oh....and there's plenty of unskippable dialogue, veeerrrry heavy on the philosophical, political and anti-establishment side of things with some rather repetitive QTE sequences. Solid translation work from Chinese to English with minor typos here and there....while keeping emotional nuances in dialogue mostly intact. TLDR:   PLAY IT. IT'S A STEAL AT THIS PRICE POINT!

_childDocuments_.review: From the viewpoint of someone who's incredibly picky about sci-fi writing, especially in videogames, this game is a relief.Oh, sure, the art is nice and the characters feel decently written, but what really struck me was how the writers actually put thought into the concepts they came up with. So much sci-fi is essentially an aesthetic skin on an ordinary story, or possibly a clumsy metaphor for something else; Minds Beneath Us is a work that's interested in exploring its premise and examining different what-if angles on this world they've created.Even the little lore drops in the form of magazines and TV broadcasts were thoughtful and presented a setting that felt both interesting and grounded. Offhandedly, a single article mentions that scientists are searching furiously for a reason to say humans are unique and intrinsically special after discovering brains aren't that different from computers. Another article mentions cybernetics as first and foremost a disability issue, which is probably the literal first time I've ever seen a videogame understand cyborgs as disabled people.It's also wonderfully refreshing that the writers have clearly thought through arguments you might actually want to make in a debate. I was amazed to see dialogue options that included things I wanted to say, rather than feeling like I was limited to a set of bland stock lines; I also never felt like the narrative tension depended on the protagonist not wanting to ask questions, which is something that annoys me a lot in other games. Often other characters might refuse to answer or might not give you good answers, but just being able to ask at all feels good.The game does have its weak points. Sometimes you can make choices that feel like the game clearly didn't expect you to make them, such as , and seems to proceed assuming you did something else. The  have the weakest writing. The entire mind parasite premise doesn't ultimately seem necessary when the game really shines most in the parts that could also be experienced by a basically normal guy.Nothing's perfect though, and overall, it remains absolutely head and shoulders above almost all other sci-fi videogames.Subjectively, if you don't like VNs and really need there to be robust gameplay, look elsewhere -- this is basically a VN. It has even less gameplay than a simple point-and-click, which is probably for the best -- it focuses entirely on its writing without trying to pad itself out by making you hunt pixels or collect keys.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely good. It has a strong hook and stays consistent throughoutThe game throws many dialogue options with no 'right' answer, which leads to a very proactive experience. Compared to many Narrative Choice based RPGs, it is usually easy to tell if you picked the 'right' or 'wrong' choice. This game really wants to challenge that. As a result, the overal themes and plot devices end up being very gray.Although chances are that if you found this game, you're already interested in the visual novel style, more story, less gameplay type of experience. The reviews speak for themselves.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: This game has to be one of the best RPGs I've played this year. The amount of thought and emotion put through the dialogues are something else. The questions of morality and how far do you draw the line in what is right or wrong, how much can you give or lose for what you think is the greater good. The characters are well thought out and express their emotions towards choices you make are pretty well done. The characters all have their motives and background fleshed out that makes you care whether or not your decision really is the right thing. It's not everyday that I write a review like this but I believe this game deserves it. Only thing that I would say that's not much of a con is the amount of reused settings. I think it would have been beneficial to have the story go to other place other than just the company and the house about 70% of the time. But other than this minute con, this game is good, I hope a DLC or a sequel comes out for it to further develop the ongoing story! 9.8/10!

_childDocuments_.review: Holllyyy crap. An entire game that sets you with morale choices left and right. Are you a survivor? Are you a pragmatist? Are you an idealist?It sets you up over and over again with lots of little tests to make you actually live into your professed ideals. Little tests: do you sacrifice for the greater good? Do you sacrifice to improve your own standings?  Do you just keep your head down...And then in the final act it sets you with a brutal trolley problem, an "unwinnable" moral quandary that makes you really put your money where your mouth is. When your life is on the line, will you stay on your high horse that you've been riding all game or will you tuck tail and run?Hot damn. Finally a morality system done well.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing The gameplay is simple and intuitive, and the story keeps you engaged very hard. I can't remember the last time that i got so focused in a story-focused experience like i was in this game, i played most of it (around 18 of my 20 hours) in 2 days, and during gameplay overall i was extremely engaged with the story. The worldbuiding is okay. The plot you think you will explore in the prologue actually is not the focus of the story, but that didn't matter much because the actual story quickly clamed my interest and became the focus. Indeed the fact that you are actually some type of player just controlling other person did not came to me anytime except the few moments that you are detached from the character.The vibes, musc and visuals are also pretty good, contributing a lot to the atmosphere and helping the player engage even more with the game. The combination of this and the awesome characters made feel a lot harder then i would usually feel for characters in a videogame.Personally, in a smaller/simpler way, some obvious differences aside, i felt like i was playing some small version of disco elysium. This game does not have a lot of content to speek of (around 20h to 100%, mostly don,t need to play it again to see the stuff you have lost), but the price isn't saying it should have. For the first game released by this developer i think it have a lot of quality.The story was amazing. The characters are very good and have a very nice development (provided you want them to develop, as you can ignore some very important stuff regarding this matter). The whole thing, unfortunely, is a bit short compared to my expectations. I understand that they may had limitations and could not make a game twice the size, but i hope they are able to make some good profit of this game to have the ressources to make even bigger projects. Also, i felt that, except by the side quests, your choices didn't really matter that much. I did not make any stupid things that could obviously hinder the main objectives, but overall i think it didn't make all that much difference. And the endings are all a choice you make in the last scene, witch isn't a thing i actually hate, but i think it would be better to tie these ending choices to at least some of your deeds in game (for example, situ just offer you her mentor's weapon if you did resolve the conflicts in her team).OverallGameplay: 5/10, very simple, but is not the focus anyway, just think they could bring more variety to quick time events, and also bring more puzzle-like sections like the very start in the prologue.Vibes: 10/10, the atmosphere is very engaging, even considering the simple graphics and lack of voice acting, the music is beautiful and the key moments of the story are very well built into the scene to make a breathtaking experienceStory: 8/10, I really made an effort to pull out everything i did not like about the story, and overall i think it had more potential, but is amazing nonetheless

_childDocuments_.review: Really recommend this one if you like playing point and click and/or games that are lighter on gameplay since this doesn't have a whole lot of action. That said the story is fantastic and the gameplay comes mostly from carefully understanding all the conversations and how you as the player react to it. Won't spoil the story but this world is frighteningly realistic in its depiction of unchecked corpo's which definitely fits the Cyberpunk genre. Took about 15ish hours for one play through but it has replayability due to choices you can make so can easily crack 30 or more hours total. Easy recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first review ever. I will keep it brief. I have played all sorts of point and click games. Check my profile if you'd like. This is a wonderful game. Not without it's flaws, but whatever. The story is the highlight. It is thought out, engaging, and evolves multiple times. If you stick around for the conversations that people have if you pass them by, the lore makes everything mean just a bit more, and it's worth it. The game begins with the typical "all events are coincidental" bla bla bla. Look at where the game was created. Draw parallels. You'll figure it out. Explore, exhaust only the dialogue options you like, but don't be afraid to take a risk. Good job developers. You MUST make a sequel, the universe has potential. Not everyone is 100% bad, but no one is 100% good.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Minds Beneath Us is rich in story and kept me hooked from start to finish. This is exactly the game I needed to play right now. Game play is smooth with a few stop and starting motions that are most likely just a part of it still being early days. I love the UI interface with the thoughts, it's easy to understand and has a great design. The overall aesthetic is great with a real stand out to me being the background art, especially of the city. I love the streets and all the little conversations happening, it really adds to the feel of each character having their own lives beyond the plot of the game. All in all, Minds Beneath Us and it's story, characters and the questions it asks will stick with me for a long time and I am so glad I played it.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Finished this game recently and it was absolutely fabulous. I would definitely recommend this game to my friends. The ending was shockingly tremendous yet very sad. That feeling you know you could change nothing and the world still goes on the way it was, it just hurts. The script of the game is what makes it stands out. I like it a lot and it involved many things. Morality, responsibility, justice, etc. The background is set in a futuristic world where AI systems are in charge of almost everything. It's kind of like the Cyberpunk-style world, with all those cutting-edge technologies yet people's life is still rough. “High tech low life” is the foundation of the cyberpunk world. The struggle, the desperation… society was built on people's misery. The AI system needs energy supply, and the cheap, easy-to-get resource? People. The game made it clear as one NPC points it out that humans are actually the most convenient resources they can get. See? Human beings are just a kind of resource, a useful tool for that rotten society. When playing the game, I couldn't help but constantly think of the iconic movie series Matrix. The red and blue injection bottle from the chapter 1. And also using human's brain as energy. All that similarities. I've always liked the Matrix movies and I'm certainly happy to see such a game. I've made so many choices along the way and every decision leads to the ending. What is free will. Does it really exist? I guess some questions are hard to get an answer. Like Delores said in the show Westworld season 3 “Free will does exist. It's juts so f**king hard.” This is life and this is the world we living in. Guess we are not so much different from the people in this game. Words being said that "every road leads to Rome" but the truth is, some people are already born in Rome. Some choices are hard to make, and some people even don't have a choice. This is life. The harsh cruel life.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely goated game. Suprisingly good story, and your choices actually influence the story, not just a bit, but could end up changing the whole course of the game. Your actions can also influence side character's lives, like you can talk a person into confessing for another person. Your previous actions can unlock more choices, the more time you spend learning the story the more options you will have.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Though  it is mostly choosing dialogue options, these choices matter and can have consequences or open up potential paths or choices that impact certain events.Like many stated, I too like how my choices impact outcomes. I also like how some of the characters feel relatable or rather believable maybe? Like the characters to me, and you're welcome to disagree, feel deeper than what I usually encounter in some of video games I've played over the years. Not sure how to put it....Additionally, the soundtrack is wonderful. I especially loved the track that plays when you have to make your final choice at the end. Felt very befitting for that moment.I thank the creators and the their teams for building this wonderful game and look forward for more in the near future God willingly.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun game to play, too bad it ended within just 17 hours of gameplay. I am genuinely impressed by the game developer and hope they will create a better game in the future. There's way too many pros that I am quite sure has already been written by other reviewers, so I am just going to state what I don't like about this game -- the narrative seems to be much convoluted the nearer you get to the ending, I'm sure the writer did a good job, but I don't know whether I am to be satisfied with how the game reached its final conclusion.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect to like this as much as I did, but with its story, characters and artstyle it ended up being one of my favourite games I played this year.I hope there's a sequel and/or DLC for all the questions left unanswered.There are some typos and some weird wording choices in the english translation but nothing major, and it doesn't detract from the experience in any way.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 Great, captivating story with grounded characters as well. I love the way it tackles on heavy issues and their corresponding moral dilemmas. I also love the way how the visuals and sceneries were used to express certain messages. However, I would have appreciated if a choice has been given to me as a player to be or not to be on pure auto-save. Contrary to that criticism however, I acknowledge that this feature was added to add weight to the decisions you make. Asides from that, great experience and great game overall!
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend the game if you are not into choice-making or if you don't like reading, because it's basically story telling.But, WHAT A GAME, I know that was gonna be good, but that's litteraly blow up my mind !So much question, so much of "WOW", "OMG" and "This game I swear", that I some moment needed to think about.I was surprise all along !
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, this game is a visual novel, 85% (or more) of it is reading dialogue between characters, there are some quick time events but they are simple and don't occur often.that said, is a DAMN good visual novel, main story is good and has some juicy  plot twists, writing is exceptional, immersive and made me care for the characters, visuals and presentation are good also.i'm  glad  i stumbled into this game by chance 1 week before launch, otherwise i would miss it.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Utterly brilliant.I love complex, mysterious, choice-driven narrative games.  is up there with  at the very top of the mountain. The 15 hours of my playthrough went by so damn fast and I was so heavily invested in the characters and the multi-layered story that I played most of it in one sitting despite hellish heat in my computer room.The final two chapters had a larger number of spelling mistakes that the earlier chapters didn't have ("Chamleon"), but that is literally the only (small) negative I can think of. Even the fact that the game contained quick-time events didn't really bother me, because they were fortunately fair and really easy (I think) to master, so that they wouldn't become a showstopper. I cannot say enough good things about the graphics, the atmosphere, the dystopian cyberpunk mystery story and, most of all, the characters. What beautiful character design from a writing perspective, with side characters and their stories feeling just as real and alive as the main characters.This is a GOTY contender for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Minds Beneath Us brings together storytelling, beautiful visuals, and interactive gameplay in a way that keeps me hooked from beginning to end. I enjoy sci-fi stories and games that test my thinking and decision-making, this game is definitely one that check out all the boxes and leaves you thinking for a while after finishing it!I was taken bsck by how much I enjoyed it it's a fantastic game. Hopefully the studio creates more games and sequels in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game for almost always giving me the option to say nothing (the option ".........."). As an introvert person, I often prefer let the other person finish their whole argument or opinion before express mine. So this ".........." option is great for me. (some other games though.... force you to choose one option from ones that you all dislike)BTW, great storytelling. A super rare case of cyberpunk style story based on modern tech development (2010+). Love it. 3/5--My own rating criteria: 1: Terrible; 2: Average; 3: Good; 4: Awesome; 5: Miracle.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: saw it in recommendations so I decided why not and played it, had an absolute blastit's a "choices matter" game but leading up to the final choice you have a lot of control and the game lets you go outside the box a few times and it's very satisfyingthe game is very morally grey and it's not always easy for me to pick a side and I think it'll test your principles to some degreenarrative is fairly complex with a lot of good foreshadowing of future stuff in hindsight.I really hope the dev makes other games with a similar style cause this was extremely unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that was so heavily worked on, over the course of 5 years, by a small team of people. I feel very proud of the developers at Bear Bones Studio, for putting something like this out there, that made me think that it was a good game from the start up until the end, and I found little to none as many flaws with this game, as with other games, when I played it. It's vibrant with its locations and designs, comedic with it's moments, and heart-warming in the moments you get to bond with characters and see them grow in the short time you are there with them. As well as being dramatic and upsetting in it's major moments, even towards it's final moments.I have seen people complain about the combat, I really didn't care about the combat, I know the story was the main focus. To me this game feels like it's a final cut on it's story. But to a lot of us, it feels like there isn't enough. Just like other people, I would also like to see more content or a DLC added to this game, because we want to see more with these characters and the world they live in.Besides from that. I truly enjoyed this game. And I highly recommend it for anyone that wants to play something like this. That for once in the reviews I make, I'm not going to make a funny review about it, like I do with other games. Because I loved this game when the demo came out, and I loved it and 100% it after I had finished the full story, So, thank you.10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Superb story, decent twists, amazing world-building, interesting characters, and great art and animation. Very interesting style though, as all the characters have no face.The game does start out very slow, and there's a lot of reading. Things do pick up near the final quarter of the game. The story does branch out depending on your dialogue choices, and there are multiple endings. Gameplay is a bit lacking. You only get to make dialogue choices, walk around, inspect things, and engage in very very simplistic combat.Would love a sequel, and hopefully next time the characters have faces and there's more to do in combat and exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Really amazing diversity of choices and characters have great personalities. Your decisions impact many choices later on, even when I didn't expect it in many ways. Worth the price for a great choices matter story. I would love a Minds Beneath US 2 release with a continuation. Game is about 20hrs long.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Oh I love this game SO MUCH and IT's A TRUE GEM.  The visuals, music, the choices, the long length, the inspectable objects, the not so hard fight sequences, the trials you undergo, the missions, the characters, it's just one heck of a sci-fi game - I recommend Sentience the Android's Tale that's like this but RPGmaker.  The Orwell series and Simulacra are like this but the Orwell series is really like this with no action but a great story.  Personally this has become one of my favorite games.  I only played it 9 hours though I got really emotional about it at parts because it's just so realistic with its metaphors.   If you go to work, this will resonate better with you especially if it's an office.   I recommend Moonless Moon for realistic metaphors and music videos instead of fighting scenes and a short length for one playthrough if you want that but this is about four times longer and less philosophical but these go good together one after another.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible narrative game in a genuinely thought provoking cyberpunk setting. The story has interesting characters and moral quandary's that it spends a ton of time fleshing out and examining from every angle. The game does have action here and there but ultimately the star of the show is the games efforts to consistently challenge the player to take a moral stance on the various issues it's presenting to you and ask you to rationalize your thinking. The only real negative I would call out is the small writing snafus such as rare grammar issues or a letter missing from the end of a word here or there. I know that anytime someone calls out translation errors it can be a bit of a red flag but I want to be sure it's clear the translation is fully legible the entire way through the game and the occurrence of these errors is a rarity and in no way the norm.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game and stared at the wall for a long time.An incredible experience that was worth waiting for for two years (since I first played the demo). Amazing soundtrack (I especially want to mention two compositions that were mainly played during the conversation with Lawrence, I’m extremely delighted), beautiful locations, some quite disturbing (yes, the Cellar with the Matrix vibe, I’m talking about you), characters, you empathize with... All this made every hour of my play the best thing I've done in a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Very detailed, rich cyberpunk-style game with a dark story and an amazing soundtrack. Throughout the playthrough, this game will test your morals and raise many philosophical questions by presenting various situations that happen to characters in the story. Emotional depth is another important aspect, it's filled with moments that will make you question the nature of society and the consequences of your actions. Not to mention well written dialogues, and choices that they have, although most the choices lead to the same outcome, some of them actually alter the story and the ending. I would highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys deep, story-driven experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: As somebody of Taiwanese descent who almost completed his tech-related Master's, this game felt like it was made for me. Minds Beneath Us goes into a lot of hard-hitting topics such as a black-box nature of machine learning algorithms alongside societal issues such as how the poor are forced to do unsafe work to make enough money, or that a company's conditions are deteriorating due to budgets. If dystopias and sci-fi/cyber punk is your jam, I highly recommend this game. The writing is top notch, and it's been a while since I've agonized over various in-game decisions.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: A very narrative heavy game with minimal gameplay elements, but enough to keep you engaged. The story and the characters are the main reason you will want to keep playing this game. I easily became invested after just a few minutes and with each chapter came new revelations and even more questions. Highly recommended if you like dark mystery type stories.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: I personally loved this game. It might not appeal to everyone since it's more of a 'Playable Narrative' with a few action and combat moments. But if you give it a chance, it's very likely you'll get hooked on the story, the graphics, the characters in general, and the exploration of new events/choices and everything else.It's a 2D game with 3D aspects that also stands out for its carefully crafted atmosphere, featuring a beautiful, detailed, and vibrant setting that greatly contributes to the game's immersion.Overall, the game is well-designed, though it has some gaps, as is often the case. I felt they could have explained the most important part of the game better; it came across as vague and even a bit lazy when you think about it. But in the end, it paves the way for improvements in the future (I'm already waiting for a second title, if possible). The exploration is well-balanced, offering a satisfying gameplay experience, and it incorporates many psychological aspects into the gameplay, which adds an extra layer of depth to the game, creating interest and even a sense of responsibility and fear when making certain choices. It's definitely worth giving the game a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Tl:dr This game has fantastic dialogue, colorful characters, a truly impactful choice-system and amazing writing.This game provides a truly engaging, action-filled and thought-provoking experience from the very start to the finish line. The characters are all very well fleshed-out even if they only appear for short periods of the game and all of them feel *real* which is impressive from a writing stand point no matter what.This game has a lot of dialogue seeing how it is a choice-based game, however what most choice-based games tend to fail at I find this game does amazingly, that is it doesn't hold your hand throughout the process, you are left to explore the world, notice hidden meanings and motives behind what people are saying and unlock choices by thinking outside the box rather than just following the set path. The dialogues themselves are truly well written, the interactions between characters feel real enough that you could easily see people out on the street having similar interactions, barring the more deadly and threatening ones of course. What really gripped me personally was that the choices you could make always had consequences whether small or big, but not only for you the player, the consequences affected the character and their life in a way most games fail to realize. A lot of the choices really had me questioning my own morality and doing my best to find a middleground between my own wants as a player as well as what I percieved would be the best for the characters themselves. Overall this was an amazing journey that gave me a lot of insight into myself and many hours of enjoyment, I highly recommend this game to anyone who likes choice-based games with heavy moral themes.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Narrative choice and morality games I've ever had the pleasure of playing. My suggestion... play the game through without resetting the Autosave file. play through it and accept the fate of your choices as if you were experiencing this yourself. there are no redo's in life. treat the choices in this game the same way for the best experience. though this is just my personal opinion. there were times when i did reset but after getting back to that same dialog option... i wanted to know how much my choice at this moment would affect me later in the game.  some choices do carry through to later in the story. The characters are written so well to react like actual people. even closing off dialog and discussions based on your responses. incredibly philosophical and makes you question your own ideals and morals. the dialog options reflect core ideas of people and you will almost always find an option that reflects what you're thinking and the characters respond appropriately. the setting feels alive. there are pivotal moments where paying attention to details makes or breaks certain story elements. exploring is absolutely encouraged and rewarded. analyzing these characters while you play is also a key element to knowing which choices to choose for your own personal outcome. only a few grammar errors dotted throughout but doesn't impact the story terribly. very minor mistakes that can easily be translated to what was intended. Now... time to replay it and see alternative outcomes and see how much foreshadowing was present. also unlock remaining achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Come play Minds Beneath Us. You can:1. Hook up a guy with a girl. 2. Hook up a girl with another girl. 3. Help a gay man sort things out with his adoptive father. 4. Help 2 best friends make up after years of conflict. 5. Expose a corporate conspiracy to , , and thus , for the sake of . 6. Adhere to the bro code when pissing at some urinals.7. Not actually find out what you are exactly.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: The art and music were amazing. I enjoyed the story but many of the character's felt flat, repeating their motives over and over again. Some story lines were discarded midway through and it honestly felt like many of my choices didn't matter. Characters that are so important one minute are never seen or mentioned again. The plot twists were good but they just kept coming over and over again to the point where I couldn't form logical answers because whatever happened was a trick or lie anyway. I enjoyed the game but there is definitely room for improvement for future games by this studio. I appreciated the philosophical messages in this game and I thoroughly enjoyed the world building and characters. The ending was pretty disappointing though.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: I waited nearly 4 years for this game and it was worth all the wait!The art style is awesome. The scenes have so much detail and the background characters give life to the world.While the ending of the game does leave open a few questions and feels a tiny bit rushed at the end, I would still recommend this game to anyone, be it just for the general world and art style, buit also for its characters.The characters are very well written, some cliches are there, for sure, but overall I had the feeling that they are very believable and I was rooting for some and hating others. Which is great :)Please support this team in any way you can <3
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first play-through, and wow. The art and visuals are very stylised and I love the mix of 2D and 3D assets I think it really helps give a sense of scale to the large rooms. The themes and messaging are consistent throughout and honestly, it reminds me of a lot of Cyberpunk 2077 but if you had to play as Johnny Silverhand. It will make you feel awful for the situation that neither you nor your host have control over. Make no mistake just like any good game based in a cyberpunk world, you are just a grain of sand on a beach. There are no happy endings for people like you, not without losing something important. I think this game captures that idea perfectly and doesn't have a single point in the story where I felt bored. Now the ending (or at least the one I got ):I have a feeling people will have mixed thoughts about the ending its sudden, but fitting. You don't really get a payoff, some reactions but nothing like a full epilogue and honestly, I like that. This was never your story, never your body. Does it matter where you came from? What an MBU is? No, I don't think so, if you want a game about an outsider taking over another's body and finding out about the secrets of your existence, this isn't it. I'd compare it more to parastye as this game more tackles what a human is, what thought is, and what gives a life (no matter how seemingly unimportant or how short) meaning.100% recommend for any fans of omniscient readers viewpoint or Parasyte or psycho passspoiler for the ending:
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely surprised by this game. Not my usual as I prefer fantasy role-playing games generally but recently been branching out and boy am I glad I am. So far I'm in the early stages but I'm instantly hooked. I can't wait to explore this game and see my ending and go back and see the other choices. If you like story-driven games this is a must grab IMO. The mystery, the small details I've seen so far, it all is so compelling I lost three hours in the blink of an eye.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: i honestly really love this game i loved the demon and i got the game the day it came out i do wish the new game option was not the highest option in the menu i just lost a bunch of my play through cause of it and that really sucks but imma force my self to try to get back where i was but i just wish the new game option wasnt so high up on the menu
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Story is so amazing i was hooked from the start still going through it , i love the characters the world building the relationships its like reading a very good book or watching a super cool tv show, gameplay wise its super simple you get to make choices though i havent tested how much it matters to the overall story, id totally recommend for anyone looking for a good sci fi storyEdit: finished the game god what an ending i was on edge the whole time, definetly worth a try
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved Detroit Becoming Human, you while love this game. It is not exactly the same but out of all the games I've played I would say this game comes the closest. Your choices can have a major impacts on the story allowing you to see different sides which gives this game lots of replayability. The only thing I wish the developers of this game would add is a story decision plot tree that branches off like in Detroit Becoming Human, or at the very least more chapter checkpoints that you can load into so you can start closer to where certain decisions are made in the story without having to completely replay the whole chapter. Overall this is great game that is perfect for visual novel lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review:
Minds Beneath Us is an adventure about a guy and a data ghost who lived in his head and controlled his body.

After society has become fully automated with AI, a new industry has emerged that replaces the hardware needed to operate the internet with linked human brains. As a result, the most disadvantaged of citizens have had no choice but to put in their bid to sign up, one after another.

Against the stage of this mad society, a mysterious conspiracy gradually unveils.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

name: MXGP 2021 - The Official Motocross Videogame
detailed_description: All the power of Motocross in your hands: the new MXGP 2021 is finally here! The official MXGP videogame is ready to show you what it's made of: warm up your engines and get ready for the most realistic, exciting two-wheeled experience ever! CAREER Strap on your helmet, hop onto your bike and go full throttle on your path to becoming a true MXGP champion. You can create your own team or choose to join an official one, starting from the MX2 category in the new career mode. Your career results will affect game progression, as well as the contracts you can sign with teams and sponsors. LOST IN REALITY Everything is so realistic in MXGP 2021 that it's easy to get confused. More than 40 riders, plus the official MXGP and MX2 2021 season bikes and teams. Sponsors, accessories and all the 2021 championship tracks. Plus three iconic tracks from past competitions: Ottobiano (Italy), Ernee (France) and Leon (Mexico). With MXGP 2021, you'll feel like you're riding your bike instead of watching in front of a screen! MAKE YOUR MARK ON THE FUN Make your dreams come true, letting your imagination run wild with the track editor: choose the terrain type, build the track and customise every aspect of your dream track. Share your crazy achievements online and download the most exciting tracks created by other players. Again, bunch of hours played in '19....now to just bouncing around like gravity is on a smoke break. Then there's the animation of the rider. It only makes sense to pair the Gary's Mod physics with what looks like Raggedy Andy with Moto GP style riding on a dirt bike (I've raced dirt bikes in the past and ride motorcycles on the road, so I have little idea of what rider form looks like). Its hard to enjoy this release when games from over a decade ago did better.Other small things like engine noise are annoying as well. 2 strokes sound like a weed eater, I'm almost thinking that they actually recorded a weed eater. 4 strokes are ok. The sound of the revs just don't match what the bike is experiencing.For a player expecting a realistic outdoor (MXGP/Nationals) style of motocross, look elsewhere. Heck go play 2019. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR - MXGP Pro is much better for racing real life tracks, this game is only (insanely) fun for the track editor.I'll give it a yes, because I am absolutely in love with the track editor. My only complaints in that department are the camera and interface (worked great in the SX games, and it's the same company, right? Just use that...), and it could use more features (although I'd probably say that regardless of what's offered). Other than that, the track editor, with it's real-world-style maps, is crazy addicting. There was only so much you could do with the flat-floored stadiums in the SX games, but building in the hills adds a whole 'nother dimension. Literally.As far as the actual racing/career mode, I don't like it. The physics aren't terrible, I've definitely experienced much worse, but it just doesn't work with the tight, twisty, narrow, bumpy real-life tracks. However, the physics are fine, just fine for the the big, wide, smooth, fast tracks you can make in the editor. The AI is much harder than in previous games as well, without being bulldozers. In fact, if you get lucky and grab a holeshot, you can stay out front until you make a mistake, even if you're not as fast as the AI. They'll stack up behind you instead of running you ever. And, if you collide, it's actually a fair chance between which rider falls, it's not guaranteed to be YOU every single time anymore! It's a very surprising and pleasant change, but now I can't lap the field on 'realistic' difficulty haha. Definitely an improvement if you want a fair, but difficult challenge (and if the physics suit you). Also, even with the graphics turned down some, the game doesn't run too great with all the other bikes out there. I'm using a 3060 12gb, Ryzen 5800x, 32gb ram, and it's still stuggling to get 60 fps, running 3440x1440 with the bells and whistles turned down/off. Just another reason the racing is difficult for me. Runs fine in the editor though.I'd say, if you want to have fun racing on the real tracks, go with MXGP Pro. The physics in that game are some of the best I've come across, as far as a balance of fun/challenging. MXGP 2021 is honestly pretty similar, but something's off. All I know is, in Pro, I didn't have to rewind 30 times because my rider doesn't understand the concept of exiting the inside rut of a tight hairpin, heading in the general direction of the track. Instead, we wanna slide over the rut and likely bounce over all the other ones and off the track, OR we wanna turn WAY too tight and spin a 180 and start ripping backwards.Anyways, If you like to build tracks, buy this on sale. And I'm sure I'll be uploading a few LONG ones if anyone wants to watch for em. My first track is a 4:47 lap time on a 250 haha!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely a step forward from the last game, which was amazing. The physics seem to be completely new, there is actually track deformation that effects the way you ride and the AI are very tough. But all of these improvements have there downsides though, first is the track deformation, while it makes a huge impact on how you take every corner every lap, it sometimes gets absurdly difficult and makes the bike do very strange things like spin out randomly, hit an invisible wall while turning and it seems like you cant really catch the ruts most of the time, you almost just bounce out of them, however it is very fun to actually have to search off the main race line in order to find a smooth line. Next is the AI, they are extremely challenging, but as soon as they get a 2 second gap on you they will begin to absolutely leave you in the dust, I think it has something to do with the track deformation not rendering for them because they are too far ahead? But you can have some amazing battles, as long as you don't crash which at the end of the race if super hard not to do. Finally the physics, they are an improvement, but super frustrating. If you are going too slow through a turn and lean too far you will drop the front end and crash, this can make you feel cheated in some circumstances. Also the swapping physics that every one hates are actually really good. It will get your attention if you land sideways but you also can save the bike as well. Overall the game is great but has a few quirks that can ruin your race and make you very angry, but my advice is to at least finish the 250 season then try to fully upgrade your 450, then decide if you like the game or not, If you liked last years game and want something more realistic then you will love this game

_childDocuments_.review: I find it necessary to express my profound disappointment with the apparent negligence displayed by the developers tasked with adapting this PS5 console game for PC. Their indolent approach is clearly evident in the misalignment of the mouse cursor with the menu interface - a blatant oversight that does little to inspire confidence.Moreover, the imposition of a user agreement, whose terms are relegated to an external website, ostensibly to obfuscate them from the player's immediate scrutiny, introduces an additional level of inconvenience to the overall user experience. Furthermore, the curious decision to commence the game with a tutorial race instead of the main menu, while lamentably commonplace these days, only serves to exacerbate the situation. Regrettably, the necessary equipment to ascertain the functionality and efficacy of "adaptive triggers" and haptic feedback within the game lies beyond my immediate reach, rendering me incapable of conducting a comprehensive examination of their performance. Notwithstanding the aforementioned observations, it would be remiss of me not to acknowledge that one may, in fact, elect to use the keyboard to play. This option ensures that even those who might eschew the use of more novel control schemes can nevertheless derive enjoyment from this gaming experience. Additionally, it is noteworthy that the optimization of the game's graphics allows it to operate smoothly on systems of a more modest specification, thus providing an inclusive experience for a broad spectrum of users.Despite some reservations, I can cautiously endorse MXGP 2021 as a game worth considering. However, it is important to note that my personal preference lies with the 2019 iteration, graced with more vivid and enthralling graphics, albeit perhaps skewing towards an aesthetic that may not fully align with the most stringent standards of realism.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing the game on the hardest difficulty with advanced physics makes getting a single player championship impossible. Why? Because if you lean to the left or right, you quite literally instantly fall over. The AI do things that are literally, and I am not overexaggerating, LITERALLY impossible for the player to do because if you did it, you would crash. Oh, but if you don't do it, you still ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crash.I love this game but at the same time all it does is infuriate me because I KNOW I can win, the game just doesn't ever ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ want me to.In retrospect and after uninstalling the game I will admit things like air physics and general bike handling are VERY good. Hell, even the A.I. is golden. So golden that I really hope Supercross has the same... "dynamics" with their A.I. where the grouping isn't so.. together, but instead spread out. Able to lap other riders. Maybe not on a short race (depending on the length/complexity of the track) but 100% definitely on a medium race and so on.This is a good game. Just like the previous titles they're slowly getting better and better. Clearly there's obvious issues like the fact that there still isn't track deformation, but for me it's alright because the tracks do feel like they get bumpier throughout the duration of a race. No ruts, but still, they're getting there. It's an arcade game, not a simulator. On that note I do think there should be different game modes for realism specifically.Air physics are better; still no free control in air but it's not the worst. Graphics are obviously a bit better than last year, which goes with the gradual increase in game quality that we're familiar with in Milestone games.Again, it's a good game. I recommend giving it at least a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Scripted gameplay. The bikes pivot in the center and any feedback from the road goes straight to lateral grip. Nothing to do with vertical physics. Ever notice how there's no wheel hop or struggle leaning forward when launching? Nothing to do with suspension unless you're mid-corner. To clarify an example: Fast bump will help with the small grooves, but not "extension", which would be fast rebound. Slow bump helps a minor bit for grip in smooth corners and large jumps. And that's all. The animation of the rider also over corrects like a sob at every given chance. Guess that's their way of pretending "speed wobbles". All this really does in effect is remind you to keep 4ft from the edge of the berms or the rear will step out. Doesn't matter if you're on the gas, how fast you're going or if you're even in the air. That rear-wheel steering will be sure to finish you off. And don't bother racing will computer, they drive on rails and reminds me an awful lot of Grid Autosport. The "physics" which are scripted act like the lie of Forza.Okay, rants over. I meant to keep it short, sorry. It might be fun with friends and I really had my hopes up for this game. HDR is also forced on so everything is bleached out. At least it allows full screen though and runs fairly smooth on fps. It certainly is a challenge, but after playing Tourist Trophy, MX bikes and so on, this could've been much better by comparison. I had a lot more for with MXGP2 & 3.

There doesn't seem to be much terrain deformation, but the tracks are already nicely rutted and feel great. The animations and rider movements all look really good and natural, and the whips and scrubs feel nice, although it's a shame they're still not completely free. Graphically the game is stunning, and is easily the most optimised Milestone game I've played, it runs like a dream!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic update. I own MXGP 2020 and this entry is totally worth the price. The track surfaces are more realistic than ever. Real ridges form as you ride (in 2020 some tracks were just flat), water from rain fills in the tire ridges, and weather can really change the surface in a noticeable way.  The riding surface will look totally different by the end of the race. This is something I've wanted to see for a long time.  Actual dirt degradation.  The tracks also have more detail and a more varied usage of 3D space.  Lots of tilts and twists, again moving farther away from the flat feel of past entries.  Controls and physics are challenging but you can really get in a groove once you master them.  The mud and sand each have a unique feel and you can even hear the difference when throttling the rear tires against them. I love it and totally recommend this, for new players or those who enjoyed 2020.

name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters
detailed_description: Grand Master Edition Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters - Grand Master Edition contains the acclaimed base game, Execution Force Pack, Duty Eternal Pack, and Castellan Champion Upgrade Pack. Castellan Champion Edition The Castellan Champion Edition includes Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters, the unique playable character Castellan Garran Crowe*, and the Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate – Daemonhunters Original Soundtrack. *Unlocked through a timeline event in the main story campaign. About the Game Lead humanity’s greatest weapon, the Grey Knights , against the corrupting forces of Chaos in this brutal and fast-paced turn-based tactical RPG. Root out and put a stop to an insidious plot to infect the galaxy with the Bloom , an intergalactic cosmic plague capable of rotting worlds into oblivion. Armoured in faith, shielded by devotion, the Grey Knights ’ very existence is rooted in mystery, enforced with mind-wipes and executions. Experience life in the 41st millennium and follow the journey of these elite warriors in a narrative penned by acclaimed Black Library author, Aaron Dembski-Bowden . SHAPE THE FATE OF THE GALAXY Upgrade your base of operations, build new facilities, conduct research into arcane mysteries and engage in combat missions across multiple worlds to purge the spread. The Bloom corrupts without prejudice; your choices will affect which planets succumb… and survive. FORGE YOUR CHAMPIONS Command your own, personalised squad of Grey Knights ; learn a range of diverse skills and psychic abilities, unlock powerful equipment and specialise your champions into four unique standard and advanced classes. Each of your warriors can be customised with voice, armour and facial options to make them your own. PRECISION TARGETING Grey Knights are an elite chapter of Space Marines and are not in the business of making mistakes or missing their shots. The Precision Targeting system puts you in control of your tactical decisions, allowing you to plan your strategy with confidence, whether by taking shots from afar with sure-fire accuracy, or dismembering and dismantling a foe in brutal melee combat! MUTATING MONSTROSITIES AND THEIR MINIONS As the Bloom corrupts worlds, environments will evolve and erupt with deadly hazards and minions, cultists and the infamous Death Guard Chaos Space Marines will mutate with pestilent boons and blessings, giving them new attacks and abilities. Adapt your tried and tested strategies to overcome unsurmountable odds against towering foes and their servants. CINEMATIC SLAUGHTER Charge headlong into fast-paced tactical combat. Eviscerate and execute enemies up close in gory displays of prowess, or strike from afar with blessed bullets and powerful psychic energies. Use the dynamically destructible environment to your advantage by tearing down pillars or slamming vehicles into unsuspecting enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: The closet comparison most people say this game resembles is Xcom which is pretty accurate. To the mechanics, upgrade systems, and other such things. Regardless of that stuff, is this game good? Well lets start off with some basics before making a final judgement.W40K: Chaos gate starts off with Gaheris fallen into daemon hands and the ship Baleful Edict heading straight towards the planet to fight off the Khorne  daemons. Commander of the ship Agravain along with 3 other Grey Knights are warped into the battlefield. Which starts the scripted tutorial of the game. Shows you movement mechanics, combat and abilities. After the tutorial, Commander Agravain dies along with the deamons and you become the Acting commander of the ship. While on the return trip to Titan, we are contacted by inquisitor Vakir and taken to another system to fight off a plague know as the bloom. This is where the game mechanics open up.You will have a overview of the system you are in and able to begin unit customization, ship upgrades, and research upgrades.Once you start you will notice the ship is extremely damaged. You will start off by repairing your Plasma Reactor, Augmentation Chamber and Augurium as those are priority. After you repair, you are free to upgrade your ship systems. In order to upgrade your ship, you have a resource called Servitors which is needed anytime you upgrade your ship system.The ship upgrade are divided into 3 sections: Support/Defense/Personnel Systems. These systems range from upgrading you ship speed, reduced construction/research timers, ship weapons/shields, and Unit recover/XP/unit slots. Of course all of these are important but you have to pick and choose which are your priority for the moment. For example maybe you want your ship to move faster when traveling or prioritize your units or research. Make sure you spend the early game Servitors wisely.While were are still in the topic of upgrades, One part of your ship has research in which you will benefit from. These are split into 3 different Categories. Bloom research or what i like to call Main Story Research is used to progress the campaign to the next stage. Prognosticars research are used on the starmap and missions. You have a finite resource of 6 you can use on the starmap. These are used to delay the plauge but also provided bonus while in combat for your units. Last is Stratagems which is combat bonuses while in-combat. You can use a max of 4 Stratgems which can ranged from more actions points, healing, and various other buffs.This is the most important part of the game. Your Grey Knight unit composition and customization. Chaos Gate has a total of 8 unit classes, 4 basic and 4 advance.  Each class has their own skill tree to go along with it however you can't max the whole skill tree so you have to choose your skills wisely. . In terms of gear, everything is customized. You can swap armor, melee weapons, ranged weapons, and Throwables/support items. This is fairly straightforward in terms of combat. It plays like a game of Xcom without the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ % to hit chance. The only thing that is percentage based is your Critical hits. If your gun is within range of an enemy you will hit them unless they are behind some wall thats blocking vision. At the start each unit has a total of 3AP (Action points) where they can move/shoot/melee/use abilities. The farther you move, the more AP you will consume. Just like Xcom you will have your partial and full cover. If your in Partial cover, you will not receive the full damage of ranged attacks and full cover will protect you. Enemies have a stun mechanic were if you hit them X times you can perform a melee execution which will buff your units. Enemies will also have armor mechanic, where you will need to break their armor before you deal HP damage. Another mechanic is also Bloom meter. Each enemy turn, the bloom meter will increase by a set amount depending on various factors. If the bloom in the sector is high it will increase but also whenever your units use psyker attacks or abilites, it will also increase bloom meter. Once the bloom meter reaches max on an enemy turn, one out of several things will happen. The enemy will receive attack/defensive/support buffs,  enemy reinforcements will be called in, or your units will be given a debuff. this is completely random what effect will happen. After each mission you will be given a chance to acquire gear through Requisitions. By completing mission objectives and side objectives you can a certain amount of requisitions. Spending these lets you get New Knights, Armor, Melee Weapons, Ranged Weapons, and Throw able and supports. You can upgrade the rarity of items you get through events which will discuss nowWhile on the star map there will be random chances for events to follow. It will range from ship to ship combat to research purposes. These events while may seem good, also have consequences to them. For example you may be able to increase your research speed at the cost of having some of your knights out of commission for a duration of time. Another example is the crew is currently infighting about ship repairs and research. In choosing a side you may increase your ship construction by 50% but reduce research by the same amount. However the big one is the Grand-masters Report which happens every 60 days. The Grandmaster Vardan Kai will request updates on the bloom. These choices are based on the progress with the bloom spread so far on the campaign. Also the choices in this report are very important. Picking the right dialogue can result in some really good buff like bonus XP, 100% Research/Construction buffs/bonus resources and units. On the flip side of it, if your progress is lackluster or pick the wrong dialogue, may experience debuffs such as negative research/construction, may limit your requisitions, Knight recruitment, or handing over of resources. Also have neutral dialogue which will be neither hurt or provide bonus. After the report you can upgrade the rarity of the requisitions you receive by spending. Just note that every 60 days you must report your progress so try to advance the story as you can.If your into Xcom type of game this is definitely your cup of tea. However it'd be poor of me to mention some problems with the game. There is quite a bit of performance issues that will ruin the experience. I had some FPS drops while playing for extended period of time. Nothing major besides that for me but i would wait for some updates before purchasing the game.I rate this game an 8/10. Very solid game they got going here but unfortunately some performance issues to go along with it.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty fun game but it's hampered by some major issues.  My main complaints are the bad performance (FPS drops made it near unplayable frequently) and the time sensitive nature of the campaign. You don't really get to play around with all of the different customization options (gear, abilities, squad combinations etc) since it's literally game over if you don't finish in time.  You can't take your time and try to unlock a lot of cool stuff; the narrative is pushing you to do everything as quickly as possible. Once you do finish, you  can't continue playing after the campaign to enjoy all of the stuff you've unlocked either. I've been through the campaign twice and still haven't had a chance to try a lot of the armor/weapons and even two of the advanced classes. I haven't felt like starting over a third time so I've just been reloading saves, but that's already gotten old. The moment to moment gameplay is fun and I want to play more, but due to the choice to limit gameplay to a single campaign playthrough, I can't see myself playing this much longer.

_childDocuments_.review: Way underrated. 20-ish hours in, this is a beautiful and polished game that I recommend to fans of the genre.Compared to other XCOM-like games, this one feels much closer to Firaxis' game, with many aspects directly parallelled, if somewhat darker and maybe a bit grim. When you scratch the surface though, you'll find many of the less popular aspects of XCOM have been addressed in interesting ways —  • Turn-after-turn missions will become harder by adding mutations to enemies, debuffs to your units or other general hazards, which nudges you against taking your time between engaging new groups of enemies • Some enemy groups (patrols) move around the map, adding another thin layer to your tactics — it's rare, but possible that an enemy group will stumble into your battle with another group if you're not careful. • The skill tree you upgrade your units with is engaging just enough to make you excited to experiment with a different path on few more units of the same class.Those and smaller gameplay and UI decisions, to me, signal professionalism and creativity from the team behind this game, and I love it.I am early on the campaign, so I can't speak about the story much — so far I can't say I'm losing sleep over it, but the sort of earnestness of the characters and I enjoy reading their takes on what's going on, and their occasional banter.

_childDocuments_.review: I have finished the game on the easiest difficulty.The ending of the game was really good. You got to meet characters who are important to the lore.The story was competently told.The voice acting was decent.You have to make difficult choices as the campaign progresses.And the kinds of enemies you’re up against at the end really make you feeling like you’re commanding Space Marines.The game is mostly good but I have some criticisms.The music quickly wears out its welcome. Perhaps more tracks would have alleviated this.When you’re not in and engagement you have to creep your units forward one action point at a time because if you don’t then when you send one knight out the front and he discovers enemies suddenly your other three knights are way out of position and have to spend all their action points moving in order to get close to the enemy. I wish there was some less than tedious method for exploring the map when you’re not in an engagement.When you discover enemies they tend to run and take cover. So you spend most of your action points moving into a position in which you can actually hit them.  Then when it’s the enemies turn again then run away and take cover again. So if feels like I’m playing Ring Around the Rosie with my space marines, it’s frustrating.Earning the Will Power you spend on abilities through kills means your Apothecary has to be killing things in order to heal your Marines and that’s frustrating because he doesn’t have abilities that make him good at killing. So you end up weakening enemies with one unit only to finish them off with you Apothecary to get those precious Will Power points and that feels sad.The Apothecary’s Speed Biomancy skill should be a ranged ability, spending precious action points to move him in to position to cast it is too expensive.Most of the mission designs are fine, but there’s one mission type that made me stop playing on my second playthrough on a harder difficulty. The mission involved protecting units from waves of invaders. The units you have to protect are too far apart. And there are far too many waves of units to kill. I never finished the mission but image that if I did it would have taken well over an hour, a deeply unpleasant slog of chasing down units and killing them.Configuring your Space Marines’ appearance should be one of the more enjoyable aspects of the game. But each cosmetic item is numbered instead of named and you scroll through them with arrow keys. Which one was the cool pauldron that looked like it would suit your Interceptor again? Was it pauldron 7? Time go through the list one a time to find out. There should be a list of thumbnails to choose from instead. This deficiency means I spent almost no time configuring the appearance of my Space Marines which is a shame because time and effort went into the 3D art for those configurations.My last criticism is that, as a results of the way the combat is balanced, the Grey Knights don’t really feel like Grey Knights until the end game. I know that it’s good balance that my Storm Bolter doesn’t one hit kill the cultist because that would be way too easy. But if feels like it SHOULD annihilate the cultist in a single hit because it’s the Storm Bolter of a Grey Knight for goodness sake. So the Knights don’t feel like Knights in the early game.So all in all the game is good but with some frustrations.
