_childDocuments_.review: Game of the year 2022 - The developers should be lauded for creating such a faithful representation of the 40k verse but..The bloom has spread to steam!There has been a malaise of negative reviews cropping up all over the Steam Sub-sector purporting heretical notions that this game is not good. Let us address them here:"The graphics aren't great ...."  Untrue. The attention to detail in the environments are stunning. Textures and effects bring the worlds of the system to grim dark life. What I think people are referring to by "graphics" is the ART STYLE which leans towards the Pixar side of things which in and of itself is purely subjective. Graphics are just fine.performance issues....It's unfortunate that some have experienced this but on a RTX 3070 at 1080p - smooth sailing. Items locked behind twitch stream views...Who cares! Don't want to watch? Then don't. I sure as hell didn't. They're just starting items any ways. UPGRADE YOUR ARMORY and you'll be getting better items before long. Really, it's not big deal. It really isn't. It's an XCOM clone...Yeah it's an XCOM like. How is that a bad thing? Should you not play souls like games because they are dark souls clones?Grey Knights out of action of 20 days after getting shot by cultists....it's unfaithful to the lore...This one is a real doozy. Your grey knights don't go down in one shot by a cultist. It takes SEVERAL shot to bring one down and even then, when reduced to zero health they still get up after 3 turns. In the beginning of the game your strike force was depleted from an eariler engagement. Your resources are low and you are under strength. Just play the game. Level up and invest in those skill trees and you'll be wading through cultists. Just like it's supposed to be.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is as flawed as a game as you can get. I am a great fan of tactical turn based games (XCOM, UFO series, Mechanicus etc) and am a giant 40k nerd so, in theory atleast,  I should be overjoyed playing this game as it strives to combine 2 of my favorite things. It does do that to some degree but what it fails utterly at is being a fun game. Having finished the campaign, I promptly uninstalled it and will not touch it again, barring a major rework or such. The base tactical game is fun and engaging enough and the builds and classes are all varied, or atleast they were until the devs decided to nerf alot of the possible builds into oblivion. These heavyhanded and shortsighted approaches do not bode well for the future of this game. The final mission is the pinnacle of uninspired game design - repetitive, bland, filled with artificial challenge and gotcha moments, a pure reflection of the game in its entirety.To conclude, I am writing this not out of spite, but rather dissapointment in seeing a potential great game ruined by bizzare design decisions and balancing. It is as if the developers are devotees of Slaanesh and derive pleasure from the suffering they inflict on their player base.

_childDocuments_.review: A definite must play. Highly recommended!Warhammer 40k: Chaost Gate - Daemonhunters is one of the best WH40k strategy games ever made. A blend of X-COM and WH40K, it's better than Mechanicus. If you are a WH40k and enjoy tactical turn-based strategy then this game is for you. First of all, it's freakin' gorgeous. The amount of detail in the maps and characters is unbelievably dense. I've caught myself spending moments looking at the detail and textures in the game. Tons of moving bits, everything is destructible and there's a lot of interactive points in the map that you can use to spice up your gameplay. My favorite is the big ol' crane.As far as the Space Marines, they're heavily detailed, have tons of customization and you can easily make them look how you want them to. In addition, their armaments and their buffs are wildly varied and you are constantly picking up gear throughout the game. There's a lot of depth to the systems involved as well. Everything from loadout, to abilities, to the management of your ship and strategems. It can see a little daunting in the beginning but once you get familiar it's really enjoyable. I love how much there is to this...there's been a ton of work put into it. Upgrading your Marines is fun and you have a lot of different ways to take them...my favorite are the teleport/attack combos. Fun stuff!Combat is also fun with more actions and different types of Willpower use and specialized attacks. The Bloom countdown adds a lot of variability and danger to matches. Sometimes you can get hit with some pretty hard stuff like multiple bloom portals bringing in buttloads of fresh enemies. Some may find this too difficult but you can adjust the difficulty at the beginning of the game.There's a few things that need to be ironed out still but I haven't experienced any bugs other than visuals thus far. It feels absolutely solid. Things that bug me are the camera, which doesn't seem to cover the action properly and it gets locked during nme movement. Sometimes during special attacks, it will move to where you can't see the actual action or is blocked by the roof of a structure. They should have a roof -/+ system like the original X-Com because it sucks when you can't see what's happening. _childDocuments_.review: So basicly this game is a Warhammer 40k XCOM clone where you run a group of five Grey Knight Space Marines with psychic powers, and fight against the forces of Chaos (In the base game its , except the tutorial). In the first few hours of game you might really feel that those knights seem very underpowered, you get the feeling that the enemy is way more stronger, however this game unlike the newer XCOM's itself focuses hard on team synergy.The balancing seems bad, but when you start getting aware of possible combos you realize that you squad becomes simply unkillable. For eg. Every of your Knights starts each turn with 3 AP (Action Points, where you can do stuff like shoot or move or hit melee). Now you got one guy who can teleport and hit hard in melee, and then you have a commander oriented knight which gives AP. Suddenly you buff the melee guy which then runs with 8 AP at the start of his turn, which also has a 50% chance to get a AP on something specific like a crit etc., and this guy now teleports arounds the room killing half the army by itself and pumping even more AP into the rest of your squad, resulting in at least 25 AP or even more for one SINGLE PLAYER TURN. I fought a  and brought him to 20% hp in the first turn before he could even do something on Hard Difficulty. So yeah right team composition is key.There are only two different generic missions types, its either kill some patrols, or find some structures on the map an kill them. That is propably the biggest downer in this game, since it gets super repetitive after few missions. The campain missions are only little better, except the bossfights and the final showdown.The map is designed incredibly good, there is a lot of cover and a lot of environment which you can use against your enemy, like exploding ammunition crates or topple a statue over your enemy. This is actually what the game excells in. The enemies are diverse, with diffirent strength and weaknesess which you MUST exploit or you will have a really hard time.The story is OK. . However the characterisation is done pretty good, especially the Adeptus Mechanicus advisor is awesome.I think the idea of this game is superb, but i think that choosing Grey Knights was a bad decision because the have such a limited roster of weapons and armors. I wish to play other marine orders with different doctrines and styles, or even play Battle-Sisters or Aeldari (OMG please) ?!? The other thing is that this games need WAY more different missions styles, because there are only two which are almost the same so we can say only ONE mission type which is boring. This game needs more mission types.P.S. F*** Space Marines give me Sisters of Battle, Craftworlds or Orks :P

_childDocuments_.review: The difficulty curve of this game is too bad.Here let's not talk about whether it is in line with the original Warhammer 40K worldview setting and so on at first. Players are not unable to accept high difficulty games, but the difficulty should have a smooth process, rather than a sudden increase of several times, while the game tells players that this is a "low threat" mission. This is completely unreasonable, and very poor game design.About the enemies in the game.Cultists have the exact same AP as the player (and the Chaos Marines), making them actually do more threat to the player than the Chaos Marines. Due to their numbers, Cultists can always surround and flank players' squads. A rudimentary enemy instead poses a greater threat to the player, which is also bad game design.Finally, if the player is not fighting cultists, then at least the battles can be less ridiculous. Instead of what seems to be some other game with a "Warhammer 40K mod", as it is now.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I feel this game suffers from the "annoyingly/frustratingly difficult" issue.Yeah, difficulty itself is fine and all and can be fun, but this game has some frustrating BS in it that bogs down the fun of the core game. I've been playing on "normal".Not only do you deal with multiple enemies that surround your units, they can be ressurrected and summoned in within just a few turns, or seemingly at random. This means if you don't go straight for the objective you're stuck dealing with a ♥♥♥♥ ton of enemies that just dont die. Doesnt help that these guys dont go down as fast as you'd like. Sometimes it takes just one hit, sometimes two, but then they respawn, hit your units and slowly chip away at their health. Then they set up an overwatch, stopping you entirely unless you want more health chipped away.Need a healer? sure, you just gotta sacrifice more damage for it. And that heal doesnt last, as you just repeat the previous and your units get chipped down to 0 again.This shouldnt be too big a deal, right? Ok but now we add in extra annoying stuff.The objective of the map is the main focus. Kill a specific thing.Ok, cool. Now you're dealing with the above, plus the thing you have to kill which is a damage sponge, and has high area damage attacks with a good deal of range that screws up your units. And in some missions these things have helping hands with the same high damage attacks. Theyre health sponges as well.Ok, now you have 2 of these objectives, far apart from one another, you will certainly lose one or two guys doing the first objective and now you have to do the second with what little you have left.I dont mind difficulty, but this just borders on wasting my time.Unless you go out of your way to savescum you're forced into doing these missions (low danger btw) and cant retreat or redo. If all your guys go down, mission fail, life moves on, other missions get harder.I have other issues with the game besides this, mainly the UI needing a lot of work as it's a bit big and cluttered at times, and I think the mission structure (not being able to just go into a lower-level mission to skill-up recruits) could use some work. My problem with the difficulty is the thing stopping me from enjoying the game however.If you're an Xcom player, then you'll probably like this, but for me this just aint what I was looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the more interesting 40k games to appear recently. I'm very impressed with a lot of the animations and general visuals, even though it is cartoony I think it looks really good. Things start out a little corny, but the voice acting is also quite good. It shows a lot of polish and effort two with things like the knights saying their names when they are picked for a mission. A small detail but one that required effort to go through what I imagine to be a long list of names with the VAs.Game play is extremely reminiscent of XCOM with less RNG in general. This is not a bad choice overall, especially with the grey knights having the upper hand in most 1 vs 1 fights. I do however wish there was more access to straight damage reduction like I think cover might give? These huge swarms that auto hit every attack means that it is extremely hard to pull through without injury unless the mission is a total cake walk. This is sort of a pain, but its definitely managable on the middle difficulties where I have played so far.Also, I'm not sure if this comes up later but so far there seems to be not a lot of classes in the game. Most of the weapons feel pretty similar as well. Im hoping this changes as I progress with things like dreadnaughts, Nemesis Dreadknights, Assassins or any number of other Ordo Malleus units. If not then hopefully the game develops either a modding scene or some DLC to add the missing variety.In reference to the previous two points, with most things feeling pretty similar, the stronger options feel really OP. I hope that they give some of these other seemingly pointless options a reason for existing, because with what there is now, they can't really afford to make some items worthless.I have played through a lot of xcom with all sorts of mods and I have always wanted a 40k version. On that basis alone I can heartily recommend it to anyone that shares a similar interest in these things. I have enjoyed it so far and I look forward to seeing what content is coming down the pipeline (and I really hope there is).Last Item: Just to mention it, there was also a controversy with Twitch drop items at game launch but the devs seem to have walked that back and I haven't seen any mention of Twitch at all in game. If anything this game will be disproportionately punished by all the negative reviews it got from that decision. I made this review early in order to recommend it to others on the fence that enjoy these sorts of turn-based rpg-esque management games. If there are significant changes to my opinion or in any of these areas over time you can be certain I will change this review.Edit 11/28/22 - Stability has improved over time making the game more playable. It still doesnt feel complete and the progression system is a grind, but its fun and runs better overall

_childDocuments_.review: Its good. Has its problems but a very enjoyable game overall. To deal with the elephant in the room. Yes this game is very much Xcom in 40k.  But its also so much more. Xcom is an obvious inspiration point, but the devs added a lot to the mix to differentiate. The enemy design is very different, most enemies are rather reactive, forcing you to act (like suppression, slow  area bombs, etc) and your starter units are much stronger. Also lot of the "roll to hit" parts of the game are gone, Not even mentioning the genius Bloom mechanic. I also genuinely  enjoy some of the animation touches and the VA and audio design is in general really good.  So that was the good. Now the bad. The game runs kind of bad, not super well optimised. And the higher fidelity graphic settings seem to clutter the game instead of actually make it look better. (Also oh my god that greater demon in the tutorial looks horrendous) I had a number of crashes and bugs, usually related to audio or loading. A few animation jitters too. I recommend not alt tabbing at all while playing this game. It gets WYERD,  But once the game is going and running it seems pretty stable. I played games with much worse problems (just the Xcom enemy unknown to start with). Hopefully they get fixed however.  Overall its a fun game. And the story and theme seems to click well with 40K's vibe.Big recommend to any fans of either tactics games or 40k. Pick it up on a sale. Maybe not on full price until they fix some problems.

_childDocuments_.review: Chaos Gate: A great game mangled by a few clunky systems.If you're a 40k fan or an XCOM fan I think this game is worth a try, especially if you get it on sale!The presentation is great. The voice acting, story and characters are all pretty decent.The combat, gore physics, animations, classes, builds are fun and engaging.There are other small, nice things like the enemy designs and the ship building are all cool but I want to dig into what I don't like or things that could have been done better.First, I want to highlight this game's clarity or lack thereof. I found the game a bit difficult to get a handle of and I ended up starting several "first" campaigns because of little things the game didn't explain very well.From little UI design elements, to enemies looking the same and how after 50 hours you never really know what an enemy is going to do. Are they going to shoot you? Hit you with an armor breaking grenade? Shoot you with a plague flame thrower? It's hard to tell with the unit models that all look the same but it can have dire consequences if you don't know what to target first.Then there's the loot system. You can play mission after mission and never find a "good" piece of armor or a decent weapon with decent rolls. I played an entire campaign and I only found 1 suit of "Heavy" armor with movement speed on it (which is really important)The research tree is a little underwhelming. It doesn't really give you any huge bonuses which is kind of the opposite of what you want from a research tree.Long story short, I had lots of tiny problems with this game but I was able to overlook them all and really enjoy a whole campaign with it. I hope this studio continues to work with this IP and learns from this game and makes something even better next time!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who never played a Warhammer 40k game before this felt like a good game to start. I have read the first book of the 40k universe, but still you really don't need to know anything about the universe to enjoy the game. It only add to the immersion, but doesn't  take away for it. Unto the game, this game really makes you feel like you are controlling tanks rather than actual soldiers. Of course they can be vulnerable, but after going in blind, and developing some strategies the game got easier, and more manageable. I won't spoil these, because one of the charms of this game is discovering these tactics, or getting ambushed my multiple squads of enemies in one turn. This is a game that heavily inspires itself from X-com, but that doesn't mean it doesn't have it's original idea. There is no hit chance anymore. Your only defence is attack or going behind cover. Half-cover reduces damage taken by 50%, and full cover by 100%. You can't get comfotable though, because almost everything, maybe everything can be destroyed in this game. It also has a unique way of letting you use the environment to kill your enemies. Pushing a statues to kill a pod? Sure things, here you go fam. Shooting some explosives to push enemies of the map, and killing them instantly? Shoot away!The UI is really well done, although some people complained it is pretty big, although I think that's just the nature of the Warhammer universe, and it really didn't bother me. You have multiple base classes, with multiple skill tree, and later on you get access to advanced classes. At first you need to be careful how to kill enemies, and not aggro more. While this is true later on as well, you will be able to kill dozens of enemies in one turn easily. Music for me felt really fitting, but not really groundbreaking, so it was okayish to goodish. Now comes my biggest issue with this game, which you could have seen some other places as well. The performance of this game is really wonky at times. I couldn't get above 45 FPS on any settings I played, I tried the lowest, the highest, the middle one, custom settings nothing worked. The FPS also goes down the longer you play, so I assume there is a memory leak somewhere. This was really bothering me, and the one thing that kept me playing is the game. Now I have a GTX 1660 TI, and an amd ryzhen 7, which according to the requirements should be enough to run this in a stable manner, but from my experience it wasn't.The other negative aspect of it was that first day DLC, and I wouldn't have had a problem with it, if the performance was better. Instead of designing a DLC, they could have focused on that instead. Pretty annoying.All in all, I recommend you try this game out, but check out the performance first, and if you don't have a good performance refund it. This game for me was a mixed bag, but just because of the performance. If they resolve that this game would rise to new heights.

_childDocuments_.review: Any turn-based tactics game these days will be compared to the XCOM reboots (XCOM: Enemy Unknown and XCOM 2), but this game is actually closest to Gears Tactics (3AP and stun/execution system). This is to its credit, and if you enjoyed Gears Tactics like I did, then this game offers a similarly fun tactical formula with a more fleshed out strategy layer on top.The player and AI take turns commanding all their troops each turn, like in XCOM, Gears Tactics, Phoenix Point etc (as opposed to individual characters taking turns based on initiative, like in XCOM: Chimera Squad, Battle Brothers etc)Each character has 3 Action Points (AP) per turn. All actions cost 0-1AP and can be used to move/attack/activate skills in any order, which offers a great deal of flexibility. Certain abilities can provide bonus AP as wellEvery attack that applies damage is guaranteed to hit (no XCOM-style missed shots). All attacks have a single default damage as well. However, the damage actually applied by an attack varies according to the following:The UI nicely shows you how much ranged damage your character can do to each potential target as you mouse over each possible tile you can move to, which is an excellent featureOverall, having no hitchances completely eliminates frustrating moments of missing 95% shots and adds a bit more predictability in the game so you can focus on other interesting aspects of combatWhen your Knights perform melee crits or special ranged crits with "Precision Targeting", you will have a choice to disable different body parts of the enemy to debuff them in different ways. This varies from enemy to enemy. For example, you can shoot off a Plaguebearer's arm to disable their main melee attack, or shoot their head off to inflict the "Crazed" effect which gives them a 50% chance of attacking their allies each turn. This system is most similar to that of Phoenix Point (minus the manual aiming)Non-mechanical enemies have a "Stun HP", which refers to how much Stun damage they can take before they enter the "Stunned" state. Most attacks deal 1 Stun dmg by default, and the game will tell you if an attack will deal 0 Stun dmg or bonus Stun dmg. All melee attacks on Stunned enemies are guaranteed crits, and if the melee attack has Precision Targeting, there is an additional option to Execute the enemy, which immediately grants +1 AP to all Knights that turn. This enables a fun combo playstyle you can wipe out the enemy force in a single, well-planned turn. Note that at higher difficulties this becomes a lot more difficult as all enemies spawn with higher Stun HPBasically a mana pool. Each Knight has an amount of Willpower (WP) which can be spent to perform special abilities. Killing at least one enemy in an attack usually grants +1 WP to the Knight who made the attack. This system means that most non-DLC abilities don't have any cooldowns (except that you might only be able to use the ability once per turn), while still encouraging thoughtful use of abilities. Note that many WP abilities contribute to the Warp Meter, which is explained nextEach battle has a soft timer, where as the battle goes on and as your Knights use Warp abilities (that cost WP), a Warp Meter is filled up. Whenever the Warp Meter reaches 100%, a random debuff is instantly applied, ranging from enemy reinforcements, reducing maximum HP/WP of all Knights by 1, temporary buffs to enemies etc. Hence, although there's no hard timer in battles like XCOM2 (where you will instantly lose the battle when the timer reaches 0), the game does motivate you to complete the battle as soon as possible, as it gets increasingly difficult as the debuffs stack upEnemies roam about the map in pods similar to XCOM/Gears Tactics/Phoenix Point and have the free "scamper" turn upon contact, where they will take cover, go into Overwatch, or even attack in rare instances. This game mitigates this effect by full refunding all player AP when a pod is activated when no battle is currently taking place. As soon as all active pods have been defeated, all characters instantly reload and regain their max AP as well. The UI also shows a radar icon showing the position of nearby enemy pods that have not been activated yetMany players really hate free "scamper" turns in tactics games. While this game doesn't do away with it, I think this game offers a more forgiving system that doesn't make players feel like they have to resort to the slow Overwatch crawl popularised in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. Moreover, Overwatch distances are much shorter in this game and enemies typically will be well out of your Knights' Overwatch range when the pod is activatedLimited-use "spells" that you can use to heal/buff/debuff depending on what cards (Strategems) you selected before the battle(Steam Reviews have a character limit so this section will be less detailed than the Tactics section)You control a single ship (which you can upgrade) and move between nodes on a Star Map. Time passes as you move and missions appear on the map that follows the tried-and-true XCOM formula of You Can't Be Everywhere At Once. On top of that, many events can happen that basically require you to choose between different debuffs, such as reduced XP growth, limited roster, reduced research speed etc. You're basically fighting a campaign with one arm tied behind your back most of the time, which can be frustrating for some but definitely poses an interesting challenge each campaignYour Knights gain EXP and level up, allowing them to spend Ability Points each level on a branching skill tree similar to that of Gears Tactics. There are 8 classes in total with 4 available from the start. Each class promotes different playstyles and are restricted to certain equipment, though there is some overlap and a bit of flexibility depending on how you level your KnightThis feature kept me  on this game each playthrough. At the end of every battle you can purchase randomised gear for your Knights. Starting from the midgame () you can upgrade the gear as well. The different types of gear and their upgrades can drastically alter how you play. I found that between 2 different playthroughs, how I played each battle varied greatly depending on what gear I had at the time. Every time I play this game I want to play Just One More Mission to see what cool loot I'd getThe devs have continued to update the game with free new missions and enemies. To date there are 2 content DLCs (Duty Eternal and Execution Force), each adding new missions/enemies and classes. I highly recommend playing a vanilla playthrough first to get a feel for the game before buying or activating the DLC. This is especially true for Duty Eternal which many reviewers complain as being unfairly difficultThis is a fun, well-designed, and polished tactics game. You don't need to have any knowledge of the WH:40K universe to enjoy it. I look forward to more updates and DLCs from the devs!

_childDocuments_.review: Very disappointing really...Random squad size of 4 when Grey Knights minimum is 5 which exacerbates the overwhelming number of enemies thrown at you (typically groups ranging from 3 to 14, scale that up to 22 - 25 if you get unlucky with patrols). This with enemies' dramatic scaling in armour values make getting through a mission without critical damage on most of your squad a nightmare. Then we throw the random challenges into the mix and your oddball squad of 4 just seem like Imperial Guardsmen. Probably would have made more sense that way frankly...Nearly all enemies out-range your squad who primarily rely on melee weapon since guns only have a tiny handful of shots unless you spend several points amping a particular role up and even then you need to get out of and then through the minefield of enemy overwatch fields.Frankly I feel like the game needs to be worked on at it's most base level, I feel starting with a squad size increase to 5 and perhaps giving your standard gear 1 or 2 armour pips would be a good start (even Vakir has 2 armour pips - that's equal to current base Terminator armour values! Excuse me?! What the heck!). I also find the Knight level cap of 9 to be annoying when trying to skill up a Knight where you're often falling a point or two short of what would make them actually helpful given everything I've mentioned previously. I think it would be worth raising the cap to 10 at the least. After all that I think we see where it takes us.I understand that the game need to be a bit challenging but this was ridiculous given how good the Grey Knights equipment was supposed to be. It feels like the devs took the XCOM franchise and very literally painted it with what they perceive 40k to be. If these Grey Knights are humanity's last defence against the forces of Chaos we're boned.

_childDocuments_.review: The further you get into the game, the more glaring the issues are with the game.  My biggest issues are with game design.  The game awards various items to you throughout game play, but them has arbitrary events that require to either lose the items you have collected/purchased if you get too many of them or get a very hefty negative modifier.  Also, without giving away storyline, you have to collect baubles to unlock new "team" abilities," but certain combinations of baubles are needed to unlock certain abilities, and abilities are locked behind other abilities in a "tree."  Developers did not check to make sure there is a balance of baubles and so it is very easy to get stuck waiting for a certain colored bauble to show up (randomly) which puts you behind on unlocking abilities at a pace that the game expects players to do.  Also, as you requisitions new soldiers, their skills are already chosen and there is no system in place to allow players to change them to make the soldier useful for their playstyle.  Buy it on a discount.  Not worth the full price./

_childDocuments_.review: This game... Really makes me wish there was a mid option for reviews. I "enjoyed" the game for the most part. The base gameplay is rather fun. But it seems for every positive this game has it has a matching negativeFirstly the game is easy. Extremely so. I started the game on the easiest difficulty because people were saying it is extremely hard. I stopped halfway through that run because I hadnt even lost a single knight. So second run through I go for the next difficulty level up and same thing, easy as hell 99% of fights are over turn one or turn two as the knights just blend through enemies as if they were nothing. The only challenge is that the enemies pile on a million debuffs onto your units, rather then just making the enemies deal more then like 5 damage and have more then 8hp, they decided that they would rather make every encounter extremely annoying as your units get hobbled forcing you to not be able to reach the enemy so you waste a round doing nothing, Or completely disabling all spells (Somehow? Like seriously how does a bell make up to 5 grey knights unable to cast spells???), Or literally everything plaguing your marines so you have to have a million cleansing abilities or servo skulls. But probably the most annoying thing is that by the end of the game literally every enemy reduces your knights armour, or entierly bypasses their armour. On both my runs I went for things that increased armor alot, turns out that was all a waste because everything ignores armour. Seriously one grenade hitting your squad and suddenly your 4 terminator armored knights are now equal in protection to a normal power armor knight. Not that it matters because the enemies die immediatly from a stiff breeze assuming you have a functional brain and can spec your knights out effectively. I didnt even look up what the meta is or anything, I suspect if you do you probably will take literally no damage as everything crumbles in your pathWhere the challenge of the game comes from is the absolutely absurd RNG in the game. I suspect if you are very unlucky you could die by day 100 through absolutely no fault of your own. Your knights can just up and vanish due to events "Oh you have a level 9 knight that you love. lol hes just dead now not through combat through a random event!". These happen constantly and have zero skill to them. And random events that damage your ship can happen constantly. To the point in my first run I ended up with a ship almost completely destroyed entierly through random events. I of course maintained a massive stockpile of servitors on my second run and that mostly fixed that issue. The way mission spawns seem to also actively screw you over. It seems impossible to actually reach all 3 that spawn most of the time, and half the time you can only reach one. This makes it less of a be careful with how you deploy your knights and more of a "Well you can only reach one mission anyways may as well only have a A team and no backups because when will you ever need a B team". Turns out you ABSOLUTELY NEED A B TEAM. Two of the final missions basically are impossible without a decent B team. Luckily I had a few decent ones but it was extremely annoying. Speaking of the missions. These are sometimes fun but spoiler there are exactly 4 types of missions. Seed carriers, Bloom spawn, Bloom Spreaders, And boss fights. These get stale fast, and worse they get LONGER not harder, they get LONGER later into the game. You go from needing to kill one seed carrier to needing to kill 3 seed carriers spread across the whole map. Needless to say the fact that the game doesnt really spawn more units or really make you face anything tougher then two terminators in these missions. Well yeah its just annoying to the point 90% of the time I am in a mission I am not thinking on how I could beat it, but instead how I could cheese the map to get it over with faster. Saving teleportation abilities to cross gaps or teleport past enemy patrols. Its just not fun, zero challenge in these random missions and they just drag way too long. There is also no way of skipping enemy actions, you can speed them up but the animations still play out and enemies all have to move individually. Same thing with your knights. It takes like 5 minutes of just watching your fat ass knights jog their way across the map one by one to actually get to the fight. It would be WAY more fun if every mission just had one objective and that objective was actually hard. Rather then a million scattered easy as ♥♥♥♥ objectives that you clear in one or two turns tops. The enemy variety is also a bit lacking. There are like 3 demon types that spawn, and 5 marine types, along with 2 cultists. They are pretty basic, the only interesting ones are the 2 big terminators that have unique abilities. Unfortunatly one of them is just straight ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ allowing ALL UNITS to bypass the armor of your knights. As said earlier this is just annoying. But really it is rather unfortunate that you dont see any of the more unique demons or more threatening marinesBuilding a squad is very fun, there is alot to do there and is probably the most enjoyable part of the game. The problem is ITS 110% RNG. There is no way to pick what you want ever, you cant craft items, you cant choose upgrades, and you cant even pick what knights you want. I beat the game once almost twice, I still havent seen a librarian. Not even once show up as a recruitment option or a reward. I havent gotten to play with a librarian. The worst part is the completely RNG weapons give so many cool unique builds that would be awsome to mix and match if you could craft your own or modify weapons or just actually pick from a option of 4 at least. By the end of both of my games I had upwards of 40 requisition points because I simple never got any decent equipment rolled that I could actually use past a certain point. The game would massively benifit from a crafting system, and a level system that let you start with basic strike marines and spec them into paladins or librarians or purifiers down the line. It also feels like the game is missing a commander. You are the commander but you never actually join the battle. Having a main character Captain or Librarian that you can spec out with various team buffs would be very coolThe ending and post game are bad and none existent respectively. Slight spoilers but nothing major. The final boss is sort of interesting but over all is way too weak, the only good part about it is that you get to play the best character in all of 40k (Fight me) Kaldor Draigo. Unfortunatly Kaldor is a MASSIVE PUSHOVER, he has like 2 unique abilities and is overall weaker then a single paladin. Half the health and basically no armor. Seriously what? Like really why did you make him weaker then a level 9 paladin? He 1v1 mortarion in the past and a million demons, but no hes straight trash that has to be protected by your random marines. Probably the worst part is that you dont even get to kill off the main sorta bad guy Kadex, like sure you kill him but no true death for him. Come one Kaldor is right there with the titans sword just have him kill off the annoying bastard. Kadex isnt even a major character, he doesnt even have a model on tabletop. It would be so easy to have Kaldor just say ♥♥♥♥ this annoying ♥♥♥♥ and banish him from existence. And finally you dont even get a final chapter master report, not even a final "good job you get to keep the ship and stuff". Or a triumphant return to TitanAlso post game content. Why isnt there any? You have Khorn daemon models in the game. Just like have a gauntlet type deal where you fight them in randomly generated missions along with nurgle units and hell since it seems like they make new units as if its nothing (Seriously literally made Khorn models for the intro that you can skip and they never show up again) why not flesh out the other gods for this sort of mode as well?

_childDocuments_.review: ETA: several "oh wow that's new after 50+ hours" but not always in a great way. sometimes in a "that's never worked like that before but i haven't been ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in 30 minutes so to hitler's personal hell with the core mechanics, i guess."don't worry about mechanics, enemies take less damage at more than half range! oh he's in close range? no debuffs or cover? eh ♥♥♥♥ it, -1 damage anyways!move a few spaces outside a bomb radius? that's no fun! get hit anyways and then blown sideways toward the enemy rather than away from the bomb!plot out your route to make sure there are no dangers in your path? _childDocuments_.review: Too many people compare this game to XCOM. It is FAR more akin to Gears Tactics and makes me realize that not everyone plays as many tactical/strategy RPG games as I do. It's an amazing genre - go play some more games than just XCOM. HMU if you need recommendations. Overall I have been enjoying the game. I like the art, the music, the ability to literally disarm your enemies, and once you get the first healing upgrade and to around level 3 things really start to open up.The first part of the game IS pretty rough on you (I had some salty words on stream about it NGL). If you just push through that and stop thinking of this game like "Hide in cover" XCOM it really grows on you. There's a lot fun to be had here. I think so far Teleport Strike is my favorite ability. Man that one is just awesome fun to use. The only mechanic that irks me still (at least as of writing this) is that when you Overwatch you step OUT of cover. I got shot a lot needlessly figuring out when Overwatch is (and is NOT) helpful. Final note: You don't have to kill everything. In fact you RARELY have to kill everything. Focus on your objectives and then GTFO. I know that's a different mindset than some of you are used to in this type of game and it's a bit of switch. Once you make that change though... it's fun times ahead!

_childDocuments_.review: One day this could be a great cross between 40k and X-Com.Today is not that day. The game is hella janky as it stands.Cover is very wonky. People will shoot you from below while you stand three tiles back on an elevated ledge. Overwatch will not trigger on people running backwards and forward through it - except sometimes it will. Enemies will shoot you from positions you were certain were safe. You won't be able to shoot them back.And then there are the missions.Spoiler Alert: The first time you take the inquisitor out for a mission you have a nice long slog through constant respawns. Get to the end and you have a long fight against the toughest nurgle fellow so far. Kill him and all that's left is to channel the inquisitor on his altar. Oh wait! It turns out you need to channel for 6 turns while fighting off waves. What a lot of pressure! What a long tough mission... and then. You realise that despite explicitly positioning your inquisitor between two gigantic plague towers so that she's channeling on the altar and not getting hit by them... they just seem to hit her anyway. Every turn. For a bunch of damage . And corrupt her. But wait! She can't take actions! The game has locked her channeling! Just standing there taking massive damage but you cant walk her away. Can't stop the ritual. You desperately drop all of your remaining heals on her. It's a miracle you have any left after this giant slog of a mission. You try giving her armour but this stuff pierces right through... of course. Turn after turn the out of range towers smash her and she dies, Enjoy that kids! Some great design there. I genuinely don't know what they want you to do. Perhaps sit wailing on the two towers for a number of rounds before sending her in? But that seems kinda insane. They're basically scenery. They don't move. They're tough as hell. Why would you waste the time? You know... if you don't have to.I'll say this much. No human being has play-tested this campaign through from start to finish because I'm really not that deep in and already there are some glaring issues... Give this one a few good patches because right now, you'll want to punch the screen.

_childDocuments_.review: Greetings as always!  Today we’ll be looking at “Warhammer 40k: Chaos Gate – Daemonhunters” which is not only a fairly long title but also a sequal of sorts to the original Chaos Gate.  I am a huge fan of tactical turn based games (X-COM) and even a bigger fan of 40k so this game seems like an easy recommend and it is but it’s still good to suss out as to why.  Let’s discuss.The Final Frontier:  At the core this is a tactical turned based game; more commonly referred to an X-COM style or a Tactical RPG and the genre thankfully shines through heavily.  You deploy four brothers of the 666th chapter of the Emperor’s finest onto a grid based battle field cleansing heretics and Daemons in turn based combat.  Knights get action points to move, attack or use special abilities and one nice thing is that you can activate in any order and go back and forth between Knights to create a lot of combos.  The graphics and sound design is definitely 40k, adopting a more comic or stylized visual aesthetic.  The story, being nothing special in 40k terms, is still definitely a serviceable story itself.  Even though I feel most fans of the setting will see every twist and turn easily.  Mechanically you get more of the same.It’s a Space Marine:  If someone just called this X-COM 40k they’d be more or less right on it; though the game does borrow heavily from other games of the genre it still brings a lot of new things to the table.  Warp Bloom creates a soft timer of sorts as the longer you take and the more pskyer abilities you use the harder the mission becomes.  I absolutely love this mechanic, I hate timed missions and having this middle ground is elegant.  The minions of the Plague God also can gain mutations, buffs that can be cleansed from them that add another layer of complexity in the game.  The game overall is focused much more on melee and just being overwhelmingly aggressive which can be a huge detour for most games of the genre.  One of the biggest changes however is the lack of percent to hit, you either will hit and do damage 100% of the time or your target is behind full cover or out of line of sight and you will do zero damage.  There are crits in the game, which is a normal percentage chance but the target can be more or less vulnerable to crits which is a neat addition.  There was one really big mechanic that sounds interesting but just became tedious; I just wish it was the only gripe about the game.Deploy the C.A.T.:  This is an amazing game but it has a few small flaws and one major one.  One of the smaller annoyances is that you can’t chain activate, if one of my Knights is mid move and I just want the other Knights to move I have to wait till the animation is over; also having to manually remove gear to complete deeds is also equally tedious, it would have been a small mater to just ‘deactivate’ their bonuses.  These alone are only small gripes that only costs me time.  The major one is the communing system.  You can have your Brothers commune with your fallen to allow them to respec or gain more ability points.  This makes sense in the fiction and sounds cool but the overall ‘grind’ needed to accomplish this is annoying and really breaks the immersion of the game.  I do not have issue with communing with the fallen to provide these bonuses, it is thematic and interesting.  I don’t even care that to gain the most of out of this I have to sacrifice a max level Knight.  My problem is how long it takes to kill the Knight, it’s easily done on low and medium missions (as these can be done with well equipped Knights missing a member) but you end up having to kill a Knight over 7 missions.  Why not just let me send them on a ‘final stand’ mission or something.  It may sound like I’m making a bigger deal out of this than I should and probably is true it just really stuck with me.Okay, aside from the communing function this game is an absolute great addition to any X-COM or 40k enthusiast library.  My only request is that I’d love to see more of the 4, I’m tired of seeing Nurgle everywhere.  Where’s my Patron God (Tzeentch) or She who Thirsts?  I know they would be hard to create in this format but I think it would be amazing DLC.  Anyway, highly recommend.  Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game.  I like how I'm not punished for aggressively moving troops toward exploring the map and being ambushed after spending activations when the enemy takes their turn.  My action points can be refunded to me prior to starting combat.  It's an immensely enjoyable feature for me.  The other part I really like is how the stunning and execution mechanics work together to (again) refund action points, creating a potential whirlwind of destruction. Wonderful! You don’t see this in many tactical strategy games.  These features combined help to enhance the fantastic mythos of the formidable Warhammer Space Marines. I think that my greatest dislike of this game is a minor one.  The interface is a bit clunky.  A lot of clicks.  Not a big deal, but this could be improved - for example: in the mission start “teleportarium” screen, it might be helpful that if I click on a weapon, armor, or wargear that it takes me straight to that particular loadout screen.  Or if I click on the name of the warrior, it would take me to the warrior’s summary screen.  Enhanced tooltips on the teleportarium screen with popups that describe that particular piece could be useful.  Just something that helps to reduce clicks and provides more information on a squad-level view of what’s equipped by the whole squad on one screen.  Again, these are minor quibbles for me.Overall, it’s awesome.  The growth and development of troops is top-notch.  A true pleasure to play through this game.  Well done!!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I think the game still needs some optimization work. The framerate on some levels drops as low as 10 from 60 during the enemy turn in particular. I have a suspicion this is Denuvo related. Further, even for minor wounds, the wound recovery time is way too long and needs to be balanced better. I have had some at 40+ days for minor wounds. This means you cannot use the same character and build them up as per the RPG element of the game. The audio in-game is very good, but not outside of it. The story doesn't make much sense lore-wise either. So while the author is, in my opinion, qualified, I am left wondering if it was double-checked by somebody more familiar with the lore? The interactions between the Imperial factions stand out to me as lore-breaking in particular. Special mention to the outrageous price for two items, one character and all the twitch loot you can get by watching streamers for hours on end. I think they need a better marketing department, to be honest. Charging people so much for things that should be in the base game is not acceptable. Full review:Do you like X-COM? Do you like 40k? On paper, this should be the game for you. Overall the gameplay is good, though wound recovery time needs balancing. 40+ days for minor wounds isn't acceptable. I mention this as even weapons that lore-wise would damage Aegis Armour rarely do so regularly. This would be forgivable if wound recovery did not take so long.  Some of the abilities that show up at random are either useless or absurdly powerful. Due to being randomized, they often affect mission outcomes greatly. Imagine fighting through a mission that was super hard, only to know you likely have to reload and hope that ability does not spawn again. This is incredibly frustrating. Otherwise, I think the game is very good; though I'm not too fond of cover being up to 100%, I think it should be capped at 80-90%.Sound-wise, the voices and battle sounds are great. Honestly, they are some of the best I have seen from a 40k game. Outside of battles, minus the voice acting, it is subpar. This takes away from the immersiveness of the setting. I had hoped for better. Story-wise, I think several missions come across as filler and do not contribute meaningfully to the story in any way. When you have the Inquisitor, Astropath and other characters written so well, it sucks having to grind through meaningless missions that do not contribute overall. Dawn of War 2 at least had missions that were grindy, but there was a purpose overall to do them. Here it feels like you get a small reward, but that is all. I would like to see that improved. The interactions between the Imperial factions also needs to be improved as well. Performance-wise, it can be all over the place. My system is high-end, so getting frame rates as slow as 10 on the enemy's turn is not great and takes away from gameplay. I note this only happens on some maps, whereas others are near perfect 60 across the board. I would hope the developers optimize it some more and hopefully remove Denuvo. Finally, one cannot neglect to mention the marketing team deciding to make players watch over 10 twitch streams for items. Who thought that was a great idea? Further, the items + characters in the special edition could have easily been included in the base game. Neither adds anything meaningful to the experience, as far as I can tell.In conclusion, I would give this game a 7 overall, but it is a 6 due to the crappy marketing and value for DLC proposition. I hope the devs know that this would be a solid game with more optimization. Perhaps market it better next time? Buy it on sale.EDIT: The Devs were kind enough to give the community the twitch items in an upcoming update. I am bumping my overall score to 6.5/10. It is good to see devs listening to the community. Now please remove Denuvo.

_childDocuments_.review: So I never post Steam reviews but after putting in some time on this game I felt I had to warn people NOT to buy this. This is my review after 30ish hours on normal difficulty. Initially, I was having fun looking for an XCOM-like and boy did it scratch that itch. I'll start by saying that on the positives that the tactical side of this game is extremely fun. The missions play out like a more aggressive XCOM, the Knight classes are well designed and balanced and each mission has tension and more often than not that the line between sweet victory and catastrophe was a one move difference. Now for the negative. This game's random event system is utterly broken, unbalanced, and unfun. This makes the strategy side of the game a complete dumpster fire. The game withholds information from you and peppers you with so many random events that you are constantly digging a hole in the sand as it relates to managing your ship. Here's an example. After the Craftworld mission (basically beginning of Act 2) I got three random events in a row, the first was a cryptic message about my construction being disrupted for infinite days until I "resolved" a situation. There was nothing in any of the menus about how to resolve that situation (e.g., special mission, repair) so my halted construction project stopped 1 day before completion. About 35 days later I received a message that I had failed to resolve the situation so my construction would continue to be delayed (current project knocked back to 10 days), hull integrity -1, gun batteries down. Great. So more projects stacked on top of each other to get back to 0. Then, another random event this time an enemy ship encounter. I had to board the ship otherwise I think any other action would have been an instant game over. I complete the mission by the skin of my teeth and it's fine. Then a THIRD event. This time there's sabotage in the ship and my ship immediately suffers -1 integrity (my ship is now at 1 life), my reactor is down so no construction can happen, my gun batteries are still inoperable, my current construction project is now cancelled after spending ~45 days trying to get it done. I opt to send knights to investigate after consulting a guide, which seemed like the least negative impact (3 knights inaccessible for 10 days). Now I'm basically one random event away from a game over after 30 hours based on random events that I have not enough information to successfully navigate. This game is too frustrating to recommend. I may slog through, but I would recommend you save your $$ and time.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game on Legendary. First play through on Regular was super fun, and I learned a lot. Love the story line, the graphics, the voice acting, but most of all, the tactical combat (like Xcom as everyone says) combined with the strategic pressure building relentlessly. The music is repetitive, like all of these games, but I frankly don't even notice it any more. Like Gears: Tactics, it looks like you'll be completely overwhelmed, but somehow, if you figure out the sequencing of your knights and their abilities, you can often pull it off. In the 2nd play through at Ruthless, it was pretty dang hard but I somehow squeaked through. I discovered the trick of standing on the bloom warp and sometimes being able to stop a reinforcement squad from appearing. I learned which weapons and armor were worth spending precious requisition on, and I avoided certain builds for abilities that I didn't use very often. I got to try a few of the harder classes to recruit: Chaplain, Librarian, Paladin. At the end of game 2, I read some online guides and realized I had been missing out on some other tactics, like making Interceptors into melee machines instead of primarily using them for fire support as I had done originally. I learned about how to really double down on certain knights' strengths and rely on passive equipment and auto abilities much more, instead of active abilities that suck up WP and limited supply items like grenades. So in game 3 in Legendary mode, I was much more picky on which weapons / armors I would pick up. I got a lot more knights from the missions instead, so I could send a squad of knights to battle for some of the strategic encounters. I still didn't quite sequence the ship construction correctly - should've focused on getting to the 50% faster construction ability sooner. I never used an Exterminatus, but maybe I should have. My Morbus level got to 3 when I finished the game, but it felt a lot riskier at the time.Though I've spent way more time on Xcom 2, I dare say I love this game even more. I am itching to restart a new Legendary game to see if I can do it better / faster. I really didn't know for 99% of the Legendary run through whether I could live through the final Boss battle. Turns out I had a little more buffer than I had thought, but I was definitely swearing and sweating through the multi-hour fight.Awesome game. Great job developers. I hope there's a follow-on game where I can continue using my killer knights and all that equipment painstakingly curated and upgraded.

_childDocuments_.review: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters’ focus on clarity and aggressiveness allows for a calculated, more active approach to its tactical battles. A varied enemy roster that consistently outnumbers you coupled with the Bloom’s effects make each fight feel like a battle against the odds. This feeling extends to the campaign as a whole, your barracks consistently housing Knights recovering from their wounds earned in painstakingly won battles.You’ll need to use abilities creatively to compensate for your smaller numbers, even if the Grey Knights you control are walking tanks you’ll slowly grow to recognize them thanks to their detailed customizable armors and powerful abilities. The plague trades outright ruthlessness for a steady advance across the sector, asking you to always weigh a mission’s rewards against the affected planets’ corruption levels.Even when you do get a sense of the rhythm of its battles, there’s always something to keep you on your toes, making Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters well worth giving a shot if you’re a turn-based tactics fan..

Scrolling feels jerky.-	Readability of the maps and characters is not good, the art design itself is OK-	The UI looks very soft. It seems like it is designed for FHD and does not scale to 4k. _childDocuments_.review: So much of a wasted potential.Interesting story, unique lore, turn-based X-COM like gameplay, beautiful graphics, new mechanics - I was so excited at first hours of gameplay.But now, after playing almost 20 hrs I will just drop this nonsense. Games are about fun, not about frustration, when unbalanced difficulty spikes on normal (!) difficulty level just force you to witness constant failures of your squad even when you try to play carefully. I had never such experience even on hard level in X-COM.- a lot of enemies. And when I say a lot - it means that you sometimes can literally cook dinner when you wait until all enemy units make their turn, return back and they will still do some moves. _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. Everything looked so good, and the story seemed interesting. I was excited to see the mechanics of the game at play in the 40K universe. Sadly this is one of the more frustrating turn based tactical games I have ever played. For some reason the developers of this game thought it was a good idea to omit a few simple but essential elements. Such as the ability to know what the limits of your squads vision are, or any kind of indication as to how much of the fog of war will be revealed when you move your squad around the map. This leads to you being constantly thrust into ambush like engagements. Even when they give you an indication that the enemy is close you can very easily trigger combat prematurely, because of not knowing where the edges of your vision are. During combat if you use Over watch your supposedly elite Spacemarines will step fully out of cover in order to cover the field of fire you setup. Seems like elite super soldiers would have figured out at some point this is a bad idea. When engaged with enemies good luck knowing what sort of range they have on their attacks, because this game gives you zero idea if you are walking into range of your enemies attacks. The simplest solution? A superimposed preview of movement, and ranges for weapons as well as seeing the edges of the squads vision so you know how much of the fog of war you will reveal. The same goes for the enemies. Scroll the mouse over a known enemies position so you can see what their effective range is. The worst part is that they will give you this kind of information if it has to do with AOE attacks like grenades and other explosive elements on the map, but not anything else. Sad to see what could have been an outstanding game hamstrung by poor choices by the developers. I am not sure I will ever pick this game up again. If you don't mind putting up with the aggravation and frustration created by these bad developer choices then play away.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Finished the campaign. Pretty mediocre, by-the-numbers story, but it had some interesting settings and I love all the Warhammer eccentricities and verbosity. Grey Knights have been my favorite faction for some time so I was eager to play a game that revolved around them. I am EXTREMELY disappointed this game didn't have a playable Dread Knight in it. I wanted that so bad. I expected it.As for gameplay, the first few hours were punishingly hard, but after it became painfully easy. I had 2 Justicars stacking extra AP on one crit % Interceptor with an Apothecary for heals and it was ggez. Most bosses that allowed one turn KOs were just that. At least until they balanced the game and nerfed the ever-loving heck out of that strategy. It's still OP, just not as OP. I only leveled my 4 primary knights and when I got to the last mission and found I had to run two sets, I was a bit screwed as I only had 3 other knights in total. Despite that huge handicap, I still won, handily, but it was the hardest fight of the entire game. I really enjoyed the last battle. Made the last 25% of the game, which felt like a grind, worthwhile. That's how OP this strategy was.If you're a Grey Knights fan, I highly suggest playing this game. _childDocuments_.review: I beat Chaos Gate: Daemonhunters - played halfway through on Ruthless then restarted after learning about some dumb gotcha moments and beat it. This is a positive review but I'd recommend waiting for a sale price, personally.(Relatively low number of hours is due largely to using cheatengine's speedhack to play the game at 4x speed - it's sloooooooow paced by default)Like most good Warhammer games it's really held back by being a vehicle for Games Workshop's lore instead of taking advantage of the things the IP is known for, like designing and painting your own armies. I understand the lore reasons why they went with Grey Knights but because you're forced to play Grey Knights, you can't recolor any of your armor or customize soldiers much and you're locked into everyone being a psyker.But there are other ways this sucks even more - like every X number of days you have to give a report to your Grandmaster. This can go a number of ways - but one example is that since the Space Marines are all ascetic weirdos he'll do things like berate you for stockpiling resources (seeds), and demand you hand over half or all of your resources. You can choose to say "Nah, I'll keep them" but then this entirely locks you out of earning new gear until the next Grandmaster Report (which is ~4+ missions away), and the game autosaves immediately after your choice (and only keeps one autosave slot). So a number of times throughout both playthroughs I unexpectedly got locked out of earning new gear and oof that sucks. Another thing he will berate you for is claiming too much gear from missions that you're not actively using - if your inventory starts to fill up, he tells you what a bad space marine you are and demands you hand over random pieces of high level gear, with similar penalties for saying no. There was never any indication that this would come in the future or that I should limit what I take, and since I had no idea what gear I'd want late-game I just took everything that seemed interesting.Another way the game ♥♥♥♥♥ with you like this is with soldier death and advancement. If a soldier 'dies' they get a Critical Wound. After too many Critical Wounds, they die permanently. At any time before they die permanently you can retire them to get a Requisition bonus. The obvious gameplay avenue here is to retire any soldiers that reach 1 Critical Wound because you get resources for them and they're about to die permanently anyway. Well, once you get one of your marines to max level, you learn that you can respec their skills or gain additional skill points on them... but it requires 'communing' with permanently dead marines. So late game, I hit max level on my first playthrough and find out I had no way to respec or gain bonus skillpoints because I never actually let anyone die. Then I had to restart and game the system by intentionally hiring marines whose sole purpose was to eat up enemy hits and die an actual death so that later on I could mulch their corpses into bonus skillpoints for my party. This all sucks because you're punished on a gameplay level for lore fluff reasons and the accompanying gameplay mechanics are just bad and frustrating.All of that being said, by late-game my marines definitely did feel like invincible space marine ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who could shrug off a thousand suns, on Ruthless by late-game the Marine:Enemy ratio feels much more appropriately space-mariney, with engagements often being 20+ enemies closing in on my 4 marines and my marines dispatching them handily. It felt too easy toward the end because of how absurdly tanky your units get but that was also probably my fault for continuing to grind out bloom missions to get powerful before taking on the Reapers - by the time I fought them I basically just dogpiled them, ignoring all their gimmicks and killing them in a couple turns each with overwhelming damage output. Since I restarted to kill level 1 marines off to turn into bonus skillpoints later I took advantage of it and maxed out a couple characters' entire skill trees :v:Overall I enjoyed it a lot, it was some of the better tactical strategy RPG combat I've played and the production value is high. Great presentation, marines feel weighty and punchy. The Strategic layer is extremely shallow compared to even nu-XCOM and the way it handles strategic resources is frustrating at best, and the entire time I felt kind of sad at all the ways it was held back from being great just to tie into the IP lore.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an example of older games being better than the remakes. In the original UFO: Enemy Unknown game, the computer controlled aliens were moving around the map, regardless of the player's movement. In Daemonhunters and other new XCOM games, the computer controlled aliens don't move around the map on their own. The location of the aliens is visible on the map, and there's no surprise effect. And the aliens start moving only when the player gets near enough to them. That makes the game unrealistic, and is a major let down, since the original game released in 1994 was better. This game is a copy of the XCOM-series after all, so why not copy the most realistic game of the series?There's no PVP in this game, that I'm aware of, so avoid buying this.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good (if quite flawed) XCOM-like experience, I would give this game a borderline positive recommendation at this time, but there are lots of small frustrations detracting from the experience itself.TL;DR before I rant? If you wanted a Warhammer XCOM, or you played the original Chaos Gate and somehow still have interest over 20 years later, you will enjoy this. If you are someone who doesn't particularly care for Warhammer, perhaps coming from an XCOM/strategy background, I'd say put this somewhere low on your shopping list.Now, on to discussing my qualms:1) Mechanics are not well-explained, and the schizophrenic UI layout doesn't help. For instance, it is explained that wounds are applied to characters who return from a mission at less than full health, but sometimes they'll still be applied to characters who return at full health, is this intentional? If so, why is there no explanation? Wounds also seem overtuned, really. Should a character missing 1 health at the end of a mission really suffer from a -3 health debuff for 1 full month?2) Graphically this sits right in the uncanny valley, they've gone for something between cartoony and realistic which has resulted in horror every time a character moves their mouth. I don't expect a fix for this, but damn Complex, in future pick a lane.3) The 'story' really feels like an afterthought. You're given some explanation as to why you're in this sector doing what you're doing, but then the missions are just "Planet X: area of interest, kill all enemies" with no explanation or tie-in. Why is killing these 10 cultists on a random area of a random planet going to resolve anything? How am I advancing the plot, what am I actually doing other than pissing in the wind?4) The character upgrades... I took one look at the skill-trees and my eyes glazed over. Poor UI strikes again here, making it difficult to glean what path you want, which ultimately doesn't matter as all of the upgrades are really underwhelming, +1 DMG to a specific move etc. Choice seems quite limited.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes and No.  Daemonhunters is a great isometric X-Com-style game, but it suffers from a measure of Darkest Dungeon Syndrome, heaped upon a failure to properly represent the characters you are portraying. Daemonhunters has many wonderful systems in place to engage you, including of course its excellent tactical combat, refitting of your cruiser, and research of The Blight plus the beneficent abilities that will help you fight it. It uses an Action point system of very tiny scope i.e. 3 pts. per unit to divide amongst movement, interactions, attacks, and special abilities. The totality adds up to make a very good game. BUT...  ... The game hammers you. The Warp Surge mechanic - a timer that bestows all sorts of negatives upon a player, from plagues to weakenings to reinforcements - is an omnipresent tiring thing that always has you under the gun... rushing from A to B to C. As such, a player does not have much luxury to employ certain stratagems, like luring enemies into an area full of destroyable architecture. You have to bull-charge forward, and the more effectively you do that, the better. Some researches, some cruiser technologies can help. Still though, you never get a break, and the aforementioned bull-rushing is almost  your best option. That aspect plays into the main gripe with Daemonhunters.  You aren't playing Grey Knights. As an appreciator of the lore we are immersed in either from dabbling in tabletop days or from playing the MULTITUDE of Warhammer 40k games out there, many of which are quite good, you understand the place Grey Knights have in the Empire Of Man: Grey Knights are the most potent cloned stock of engineered warriors, the most dedicated, augmented by their super-human psychic abilities. They are the demon-hunting special forces from amongst the special forces of the Space Marines of the entirety of The Imperium. ... in Daemonhunters you are no better than a regular Space Marine with a couple of interesting psyker traits. In 40k lore, Lasguns and Stubbers (conventional ballistic weapons) are at the low end of the tech pole. Plasmas, Meltas and Bolters (gyrojet round weapons) are at the high end. From the very beginning of the game, you are confronted by hopeless human Cultists with primitive Stubbers. You should wipe the floor with them.  These Cultists will out-range you, pin you, lay low your psychic shields, strip your vaunted elite armour, and tear you a new one. While playing you will fear the appearance of run-of-the-mill Chaos units, nevermind anything like a plague priest, a vehicle, or a buffier demon. You play in constant terror and dread of such. Compromises were made to make a (good) challenging game that works. And it works very well. But the compromise always rubs you the wrong lore way: these are trusted Marines who have occasional superior tech and interesting powers, not at all the Grey Knights of 40k lore. And that reality constantly gnaws at you, especially as entirely conventional Chaos enemies pound you into the earth. One who knows more than I about 40k lore put it this way: a single Grey Knight wouldn't be challenged by 3 to 4 Cultists and their Stub-guns... he'd be sweating against 500 Cultists. 500. Daemonhunters always feels off because of that. I played up to point X on Normal. The combination of that lore scope and the unrelentingly brutal treatment of those aforementioned mechanics made me quite decisive about abandoning my Normal Campaign in favour of starting a new Easy one, whatever such a setting may bring. Just not interested in  so much, Darkest Dungeon-style. Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters is still a great game, just not quite what it should have been.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated Review:This game is fun, and I generally hate this sub-genre. I decided to give it a try and am going to allow an exception in this case and say I love this game.One piece of advice is to check your marines traits to see what they are inclined towards, since these are unique rolls to each character. After playing through the tutorial once I now disable the tutorial and restart the campaign until I get at least 1 marine I like. In my case I re-rolled an Interceptor with Omnissah's Chosen which will allow me to fully min-max this character, even more important since I'm playing my entire team around having a pimped out melee Interceptor. I'm planning to roll augmetics as many times as possible since he will double their effect. For your opening build I suggest either 3 Judiciar 1 Interceptor with maxed WP on the Judiciars for Honour the Chapter to feed into the Interceptor. OR you can go 2 Judiciar and 1 Apothecary with the Interceptor. The apothecary is only there for Iron Arm to buff the stun on the interceptor so you can chain executes. 3 Judiciar is more of a 'sure thing' but the Apothecary addition is more fun in my opinion. You can sub out a Judiciar for either a Chaplain or Librarian later; both have their merits with Chaplain improving the rewards for Executes, and Librarian making it easier to execute with a very good aoe stun spell.For some reason, I haven't had a game hang since I started playing with Grandmaster mode (this game's name for Ironman/ forced auto save only) disabled, which is weird, unless they have since patched it.The game is fun and I haven't had another campaign ending bug and am now on my second campaign. I decided to restart on Legendary since I felt I had learned enough on my first attempt on normal to do it properly. The game is pretty brutal but I found normal to be waaaay too easy. The AI in this game is pretty bad so the only way it's going to challenge you at all is if they have such insane overwhelming numbers that they can walk into you and eventually kill you if you don't play well.On Legendary, you're often fighting 15+ enemies which at least means you get punished for every misplay.Original review below:Fun game, would thumbs it up but for some reason, like many games in this sub-genre, it has issues where the game gets hung during the enemy turn. Basically every Turn Based Tactical RPG I've played had this problem, not sure why Developers can't figure this issue out.For me, the game got stuck on the third mission but my friend was like 15 hours deep before it happened to him. We are both playing on Ironman mode (autosave only) so this means our campaigns are ruined. My game got permanently frozen when the Cultists were revived.Game is good but you must be able to save scum to avoid this bug ending your campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: + W40k setting+ Xcom-style turn-based combat, but with its own improvements+ atmosphere+ many options for customizing weapons and character development+ challenging campaign- minor technical problems- the side missions are too much the same at timesThe tactical game from the small Complex Games team surprised me. Games from the W40k universe are often weak titles using the strength of the brand, but Chaos Gate is one of the few exceptions. The game is strongly inspired by Xcom, but it goes its own way with its own improvements and the result is very good. The player takes the reins of the Imperial ship Baleful Edict of the Gray Knights Astartes chapter. Instead of returning to the home Titan, the damaged ship is taken under the command of the Inquisition and tasked with investigating the Chaos infection that has broken out in the sector. The basis of the game is tactical combat, where the player takes command of 1-4 marines, who perform story or side missions to reduce the spread of infection. For start, 4 classes are available, each with its own development tree. 4 prestigious classes will be added later. The combat system is based on AP, which are basically 3 per turn and can be used in any order within the turn and characters, and the variety is also enhanced by the possibility of using the environment to eliminate opponents. Requsition points are earned for successfully completed missions with the option of a bonus challenge, which can be used to obtain new recruits, weapons and equipment from the chapter. As a basis for operations, strike cruiser serves as a base, which can be improved in various ways.The game is challenging, of course the most fun is in the form of one save, grandmaster mode, when you need to be very efficient and careful, because it is not a problem for an inexperienced player to fail in the campaign even after dozens of hours. The knights themselves are haed and killing them is not that simple, but injuries are frequent, which subsequently reduce their maximum hp in missions or make their deployment completely impossible. The game also randomly loads events that mostly affect various parameters of the ship or crew and sometimes generates very unpleasant challenges.Enemies and their AI is very straight forward, but not bad. Their counts and types are put in play gradually and story bosses spice it up.Chaos Gate is a very good game that I can only recommend to fans of XCOM and similar tactical games .8,5/10
