_childDocuments_.review: Daemonhunters could be described as a game that gets better after you sink ~10 hours to it, which by itself makes it very difficult to recommend. Combine that with some severe or even game breaking bugs, the miserable slog through repetitive missions for the first ~10 hours along with bland combat - i'll be blunt here, this is a pretty tough sell for 45€/$ in its current state.Game suffers from an extremely frontloaded difficulty curve and much like the recent XCOM games, campaign gets easier and easier as you progress further. So what makes the first ~10 hours such a slog? In my opinion this is a combination of few things: - Mission duration in the beginning of the game is far too long due to the Grey Knights being utterly pathetic at level 1-3.- Early research & construction take too long- Leveling total of 8 knights to level ~4 (the level it roughly takes to get your build started) takes too long- Game holds back the access to "advanced" classes for far too long.Once you break past those early stages and progress a little further you arrive at sort of a golden zone where you have decent builds, better gear and enemies start to appear with some more advanced abilities as well. However it does not take long before you start to become more and more powerful, eventually being able to dispatch enemies with ease...Unfortunately at that point I was already really bored of the game due to the lack of mission variety, while there are some story missions and special missions, the regular missions that make up the bulk of your playtime consists of only 2 mission types: Kill seed carriers or kill big plants - no matter if you introduce new enemies, repeating the same two missions over and over and over again is woefully inadequate to keep the player interested throughout such a lengthy campaign.For now I would recommend keeping an eye out on what aspects of the game get worked on in the patches, perhaps in a few months time it will be in a better shape and if not, then at least likely you'll find it sold on a discount if you still wish to try it.

_childDocuments_.review: You know. I've done a lot of testing in this game by now, and I have to say I think it fails pretty hard. It tries to be X-com, but it takes out certain rules, and changes things that were there for a reason.There are less tactics in this game. I'll try to explain a general overview of what is wrong with it.In X-com there is a chance to avoid fire when you are in cover. In this game, all hits are automatic and cover just offers you damage reduction. I'll get to why that is a bad thing in a bit.Enemies tend to completely outnumber you in this game. They are weak compared to you, but I don't think the developers really know what action economy is. If every enemy hits you, they are all guaranteed to do at least some damage. Through no fault of your own, you can end up in situations that screw you over. Why? This game has random events. A patrol you are not aware of somehow sees you through a wall while you are fighting another encounter. Or a warp gate opens up which spawns in enemy the game doesn't really indicate clearly as to when these reinforcements will show up, just that they will at some time. You can quickly get completely overwhelmed by the sheer actions of so many enemies and worse yet, this can even happen when you are fighting far more elite enemies, that actually aren't significantly weaker than you, especially during early game. The game is focused around being defense as far as I can tell, but you are actually rewarded far more, for being almost recklessly offensive and just killing as fast as possible, while spamming heals. While this doesn't make the game impossible to beat, far from it, I feel like the design leaves for far less strategy compared to a game like X-com. This game kind of forces you into a corner, to play a very specific way.There are also other problems. This game doesn't run as well as it should, the graphics are passable, but the faces just look awful, and the game has Denuvo, which I am pretty sure they didn't mention until after release, and is likely causing the slowdowns. I'd probably not have purchased this game at all if I had realized it had Denuvo to begin with as I know for a fact it tends to cause problems. I've experienced it in other games, and had to use cracks on my legal version, to remove Denuvo, just so I could play the game, so don't tell me Denuvo doesn't cause it.All that said, I think this game is a good first attempt. There is a lot here that is quite nice, and I like the customization. The art style isn't really Grimdark, but it's not bad either. I think with a second entry if they change some things around they can have a much better game.Also, is it just me, or is Nurgle like... The enemy in the majority of Warhammer games now days? I am getting really tired of facing the same enemy in every game.(Oh. And the other reason I mentioned the auto hits, and action economy, is because the recovery time of units in this game, is absolutely atrocious. If they were going to do auto hits, they need to really balance that out as it is way easier to get a wounded soldier in this game, than something like X-com.)Edit: If you play on easy difficulty, nothing above is relevant. As I have found so far, the game is laughably easy. It especially helps that you now one shot most enemies, which makes it far easier to manage the enemies action economy. I tested easy just a little, but it felt kind of like X-com 2's zombie like enemies I can't remember. Except without the mechanics that let you keep shooting as long as you one shot them. I actually think that X-com2 mechanic would be quite good in a game like this one, considering Grey Knights would basically walk all over most things I've seen in this game so far. The only real exception being traitor marines. Except... Grey Knight are all Psykers and would still walk all over them.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is the first time that I'm going to change my verdict from recommended to not recommended.I had big hopes for this one. I love XCOM, and the mix of XCOM and Warhammer 40k sounded really good. Having watched the preview gameplay and reviews, I decided to preorder Chaos Gate Daemonhunters. It was a bad decision.First of all, preorder cost me around 40 euro since I chose the version with the DLC - thought that it would give me some story, customizable items, anything? Nah, you get a character with some items. Paying 30% of the price just to get a character is very bad market practice.Next is the gameplay itself. This game is a literal copy of XCOM 2 in terms of research, building, soldier loadouts and abilities. And I don't mind it. What I mind however is the terrible gameplay on the battle map. I liked the idea of going through systems and purifying the plague nests, but battles are another thing.Bloom meter or whatever it is called is such a bad mechanic. It gives your enemies buffs or gives you debuffs, and that would be fine, except it fills up quickly... VERY quickly. Around turn 5/6 the bar is filled and by this time you are probably fighting two groups because it is impossible to isolate the groups - spawns are designed in a way to force you to fight two groups at once because the detection range of your marines is big.At this point NORMAL difficulty turns into LEGENDARY. You essentially end up fighting around 10-20 enemies with 4 space marines, whereas half of your enemies are pox minions that do nothing except waste your AP points. Even if you do win the battle, it probably cost your soldiers their health, and because of that, your campaign is ruined.That is because the wound recovery time is absurdly long. Your soldier walked through a small bonfire? Unlucky, he needs 50 days to recover despite the fact that his body was made to withstand literal gunshots. This forces you to use less-experienced soldiers, but as the game goes on, the difficulty is higher and the enemies get tougher. In my last mission I was forced to use one healthy soldier with 16 health and 3 wounded soldiers with 6 hp each. Obviously I lost. You barely get any soldiers, if you do it is after you win a battle and these happen every 20-30 days or so.I'm not even going to mention the twitch drops scandal because I'm too tired for this.Overall, I'm just frustrated. I really like the idea behind the game, but mechanics are just so so bad and frustrating and because of that there is no fun. I have faith in the devs of this game, so I'm hoping that the game will get patched and receive mod support and hopefully, in few months it will be playable and enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the campaign and it was good. Cool bosses, better plot than expected and a nice mix of ship management, map navigation and of course the tactical combat.Chaos Gate iterates on the XCOM formula and some of these ideas actually rock.- 100% hit chance: After having played WH:CG, I don't want to go back playing XCOM anymore with the RNG frustration. I much prefer this system here. - Pod Alarms: In XCOM an alien pod can screw your whole team. So usually, you advance slowly, go overwatch a lot and try to not trigger them at other times. In WH:CG, you can see near pods positions even before they see you. That way you don't have nasty surprises. Also, if you aren't in combat and discover a pod, you get all action points restored, so you don't have the XCOM issue that you may already activated everyone and now just watch the alien run you down. And lastly, usually the enemies are still fairly far away. Instead of always overwatching you sometimes just want to approach and activate aegis shield instead. On the whole, I found this pod system superior and more forgiving than XCOM, so I didn't feel pressured to save scum so much.- Interesting crits: Melee crits don't only give more damage, but also interesting effects like bleed, disabling abilities, etc., which is especially important in boss fights. That adds an extra layer to the "just damage" play style that XCOM sometimes asks for. Hitting enemies also count their stamina down until they hit 0, guaranteeing a crit and for non-bosses even an execute to restore your action points. This system allows chain combos to extend your troop turn. Great idea.- Timers: I hate timers in XCOM. But that's because you can lose a whole mission with it. WH:CG does timers right. You'll hit them multiple times during the missions and they trigger negative conditions. But not game breaking ones. So yes, you are pushed to hurry, but it's no drama if you need longer. There are even stratagems to stop the timer for several turns.- Equipment upgrades: Somewhat comparable to XCOM, but most good items allow upgrading different aspects and can feel different later even for identical base items. For example, my Librarian had a specialized bolter for stunning enemies while my Apothecary used one that could pierce armour.- Character customization: You start with bases classes and get access to even more later. Within a class, you have several ways to build it. The skill trees have some overlap, but I didn't mind. Leveling up was fun and it's almost unfortunate that you can only take 4 of your nice warrior collection to battle. Then again, sometimes you need to bank them to recover from wounds. Taking them to battle anyway is still possible and the hit point penalty is acceptable.- Difficulty: I played on Merciful and it was the way I like it. You can tell the game wants to be played on a harder difficulty though. There are upgrades for improving your critically wounded troops with augments and even commune with fallen comrades. I only had two critically wounded champs over the full campaign, so that system didn't even apply. Fine with me. I did restart two missions and save scummed a bit, but way less than in XCOM. Again, no RNG!I don't really enjoy the WH universe, too gritty. However, it was a welcome change that you don't only have supportive folks around you like in XCOM. In WH:CG, my first briefing with my boss went pretty grim, haha.I feel a bit weary after having finished the campaign and won't rerun it, but the game delivered what I hoped it would.Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy turn based tactics despite really, really disliking X-Com, the granddaddy of them all. Daemonhunters had potential, but around the 15-20 hour mark there are some massive difficulty spikes. More importantly, there are far too many enemies placed on the maps and the maps are far too large. You can easily go multiple turns without engaging in combat, then get a squad of space marines wiped out by a handful of cultists and mobs. The game started with a great concept, only to be marred by updates and tweaks to make it more difficult and more of a pain than it's worth to play. Watching the AI take turns and destroy your squad for a solid couple of minutes, only for your turn to last a minute tops, is a waste of time. At no point after the 10 hour mark did the game feel remotely balanced. If the entire game is an uphill battle, it isn't fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The concept is great, the execution needs significant work though. The difficulties are almost nonsensical in how punishing it can be. While games like this do tend to be on the more difficult side, the amount of punishment your characters will receive is almost constant, while the amount of damage they can take feels very minimal, which is odd since they're space marines. They feel like they're as squishy as an Imperial Guardsmen. 100 pox walkers wouldn't touch a space marine, let alone a grey knight, yet if you're not careful in the early stages of the game, you can lose a marine to 1 or 2 pox walkers. The other thing that makes the "difficulty" setting feel like it either wasn't tested or simply doesn't work right is the amount of RNG in a map. The enemy seems to be able to call-in endless reinforcements, and the plague marines seem to be able to just heal whenever they want, even on the "easy" difficulty, the RNG can make the experience a slog to get through. If things just don't go your way, you're better off restarting the mission until you get it right or just abandon it all together. The game balance really feels overwhelming at times, where one wrong mistake means you've basically lost the round.You'll find that your characters are constantly chasing the objective to keep up, and complete the mission before the game spawn too many enemies for even a space marine to defeat. Weapon balances don't make any sense unless it's simply to make the game more difficult and unnecessarily tedious. A trashy cultist auto-rifle of stubber does more damage than a storm-bolter, Plague Marines can just hang out in psychically charged promethium fire and only get a little warm. There are annoying mechanics that allow stationary enemies to just get free, incredibly powerful attacks on your characters with almost no recourse and they're harder to kill than most of the actual enemies. Their range of attack is also probably close to if not double the range of your own characters. The Purgation Marines you can field have a laughably short attack range, making them nearly useless considering how much you have to move characters. The design makes the Grey Knights and Space Marines as a whole feel significantly weaker than the lore, and even other games in the same universe suggest. While I expect X-Com clones to be difficult, it feels like they made this hard in all the wrong ways. It's frustrating. Developers completely ignored lore to make the game more difficult unnecessarily. After the time spent with the game, I can only come to the conclusion that the developers think a Space Marine is just some normal guy with cool looking armor on, because that's what the Knights feel like.It's not a bad game, but it's also a far from good game and not worth the $40.00 price tag. If you're interested in this game, wait for a sale, a very big sale. It would ironically feel like a much more consistent, and less frustrating experience if you simply changed the Grey Knight characters into Imperial Guard, at least then their lack of starting abilities and generally weak feeling characters would make sense. There's not been a great representation of what a Space Marine is in a video game since the 40k Space Marine game released over a decade ago, and I'd love to play another game where a Space Marine feels like an actual space marine. Your low-level prisoner in Warhammer Darktide is going to feel much more powerful than a Grey Knight in this game. I want to like this game, it's just doesn't do itself any favors. The presentation isn't bad, it looks like a 40k game, they look like Grey Knight Space Marines, except at the end of the day the game doesn't play like you're a Grey Knight, or even just a Space Marine. While the game looks the part, at the end of the day it certainly does not play the part of a Space Marine well at all, and to a frustrating degree.

_childDocuments_.review: I have shelves full of 40k minis and hundreds of hours of in the Firaxis XCom games. So this seems like the perfect game for me. Which makes it particularly disappointing that I'm just not having fun. The main problem is that there's basically just one mission to play. Walk across the map while having your resources slowly ground down by swarms of enemies and a constantly ticking timer of hostile passive effects. Kill something at the destination. Repeat a couple times. Sometimes there's a timer. You will play this mission a lot. Often 4-8 instances for each research unlock, and research doesn't do much to change-up the dynamics of the fight. New enemies unlock, but they're all similar Nurgle units with more hit points on top of the same tricks. It just becomes a chore.Other issues:- As best as I can tell, all weapons are unlocked form the start. Makes sense from a lore perspective, but doesn't make for much progression. If you work really hard you can get the same gun with +2 damage on a critical hit. Yay?- New recruits usually come pre-leveled. Which is necessary for them to stay relevant, but the game assigns them skills when you buy them. Even at the start, you're often getting level 2-3 guys with 4-6 skill buys that lock you into a build you may not want, preventing you from customizing your squads in a way that fits your playstyle.- Maps are littered with environment effects that you can use to help even the odds. Which is really fun. Unfortunately, encounters are random and you can't really control where they happen. So you seldom get an opportunity to actually trigger these effects. Plus, once you get beyond basic enemies they don't really do enough damage to be worthwhile anyway.- Every enemy seems to have three action points, just like your squad members. Even basic cultists. Since you're nearly always outnumbered, often by 2-3x, you may have to sit through 30+ elaborately animated actions each turn with nothing to do but wait. - Enemies overwatch far too much. This seems to be a way of balancing out all the actions. Otherwise, the would too easily swamp you with attacks and kill you off. Usually the overwatch with one or more of your marines in the fire cone without bothering to fire one them. This bogs everything down into an uninteresting movement puzzle. - Oh, and enemies often get to act immediately as soon as you trigger them. Not just moving, but buffing or attacking and, of course, going into overwatch. So there's no way to start an encounter with any sort of workable plan.- Overwatch is nearly useless for you, though. The range is shorter than standard weapon range and in a narrow arc for which you can't control the vertical. It's usually blocked by terrain and often difficult to judge where the blockage will occur until you're setup. If an enemy does trigger it, you throw out a few desultory shots and then give up without doing meaningful damage to anything but trash tier enemies. - Enemies are slightly too tough relative to your ability to do damage. For example, I once caught a cultist with a heavy stubber with no cover on easy mode. I shot him with a 4th level purgator armed with a relic psilencer. This was not enough to kill him. Why? Similarly, plague marines all have at least three points of armor regenerating each turn, better than grey knight terminator armor. They will often get more from warp surge effects. Killing each one requires slowly grinding them down over multiple actions.- The net result is like playing in quicksand. The AI gets an almost endless wave of actions, each slowly wittling down your resources, while you only get twelve most turns, which quickly disappear to movement and the need to attack multiple times to kill one basic enemy. Then it's time to wait again while the AI takes its actions. Rinse, repeat. Sorry, that was longer than I intended. I actually think this is a very good game, and clearly a lot of people really enjoy it. There's clearly a lot of skill and care that went into designing the characters and levels. It's just not a game that I can really enjoy, for all the reasons listed above.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: I have one hour of playtime, the rest is waiting on the Enemy Turn..Seriously, at times there are so many enemies on the field that it's visually confusing and headache inducing. My cpu* has never been hotter. Screen is so busy it looks like bright vomit. Performance dips down to 5 fps.. This game seems to be playing itself.  I played about 10 missions on both Standard and Merciful, and did not see any difference between the two difficulties. I have played a ton of turn-based tactical games and this one is the most imbalanced, by far. I don't think it's possible to play this purely tactically, it only seems to favor a blitz style combat. Core gameplay is loss mitigation and triage. You can expect to find yourself simultaneously pinned down, suppressed, marked, overwatched (from multiple angles), standing in poison or fire or both, plagued, hobbled, blinded and stunned, with no AP. You will be outnumbered, outgunned, outmaneuvered, outclassed, out-armored (that one is the most annoying and inexplicable to me), and surrounded on all sides. This is a disaster management sim. It may have translated better as an RTS. Devs are listening and updating, but so far the fixes have been insufficient to make the game playable or fun. They said they reduced the number of enemy spawns in update 5, but honestly there are even more. 6 spawns per incursion, said they lowered it to 4, but there are now 10, as if they stacked instead of subtracted? I don't know. It sucks.The Grey Knights and the 40k style are really good, I love it. But it seems this was made for 40k fans alone and not tactical gamers. One last note: The tutorial is a 3/4 party wipe. Not even kidding. edit: Support Ticket and dxdiag sent per dev suggestion.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. Although I was slow getting into it, it is a great quality 40k game, and there are precious few of those (and I own most of them).As an XCOM type game, I like it a LOT. It doesn't have quite as much going on as something like Phoenix Point, but you have many, many options in combat, and what happens in battles makes sense. I never liked the original percentage based hit formula because it would often be just stupid, like shooting something at near point blank range and missing because you only have a 98 percent chance to hit. None of that here. You can clearly see what result your actions will have before you commit to them, and there is good strategic depth. I rarely if ever feel cheated by the game or that my loss was simply bad luck instead of bad tactics.On the 40k side, it is pretty good. I read quite a bit of lore and some of the books, and it feels right as a 40k game. I've heard complaints that your Grey Knights aren't as strong as they should be lorewise...maybe those people just haven't gotten far in the game. They are pretty weak at level 1 or 2, but by end game, a single knight is wiping whole squads of enemies in a single turn, so they aren't THAT weak. It has to be balanced as a game, and generally, your knights feel like the badasses they are supposed to be. The game presents plenty of the challenges, and the story is good and fits well with the series.The two biggest issues I have are how randomly punishing warp surges can be, and the general ridiculousness of injury recovery until you invest in the medical upgrades for the ship, but these are small issues clearly meant to balance challenge and game pacing, and they seem to have been a little smoothed out since launch. Optimization is slightly lacking. I had to reduce graphics to medium in order to smooth the game, but honestly, it looks great on medium anyway, so it wasn't a noticeable loss of anything.I greatly, greatly want to see more DLC and campaigns added. There is a LOT of Nurgle in this game, basically its all Nurgle, and some variety added would greatly help. If you like a better version of XCOM, you like 40k, and you want to bash demons with a team of cracked space marines. Then this is your game.

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game so far. I think I finally reached the point where the game actually begins : Do not be fooled, this is not XCOM. There are no missed shots and you can see how much damage you would do from a new location before moving there.For example, pod locations are shown to you if you get close - so you're not surprised by them. All of your units get all of their action points refunded when combat starts and ends (end also auto-reloads everything - ah the little things sometimes feel great)There are multiple ways to gain action points. Starting from buffs and auto-skills to executions - use them.In this game, use Willpower - it's easily replenished. Cons : Performance could be better. and Inventory / group changing interface is awful (Change a grenade? - follow these simple 10 steps!).tl;dr : Great game!RANTING;

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game for three hours all I can keep thinking is "I wish I was playing Mechanicus".I really wanted to like this. I love 40k and I love xcom-style turn-based combat. And the idea of playing Grey Knights as fight chaos with customisable marines really ought to be awesome but somehow this game ruins this opportunity.From a gameplay standpoint, the UI is extremely confusing. Between battles, the game doesn't do a great job of explaining the different options. It runs a tutorial mission and then offers XP progression but doesn't explain what the different classes do so you're making decisions without really understanding the consequences. In battles, it's not always clear what uses what Action Points and you're making basic mistakes because it's not obvious that the action will end that character's turn. None of this is helped by terrible graphics. I'm not sure if it's the art style or the way it's implemented but its really difficult to differentiate between your marines and make sense of the battlefield. The camera pans and moves in a non-sensical manner. Regularly I've been in battles where you take a ranged fire action and the camera will pan behind a wall so you can't see anything. But worst of all, you just don't feel like you're playing Grey Knights. These are supposed to be amongst the baddest of badasses in the galaxy. Not just Space Marines, but the toughest, hardest, Space Marines there are. In the intro, you see the Commander go toe-to-toe with Greater Daemon of Khorne. So why is it that a few rounds from a cultist and my guy is down to less then half health? I get that you need to make the game a challenge, but if you substituted the Knights for Imperial Guard it would be more realistic!Everything that Chaos Gate does, Mechanicus does better. Much better: from graphics, gameplay, story and music there really is little point in Chaos Gate unless you really want a game where you get to kill Nurglings.

_childDocuments_.review: Even if you took away all the trappings of the WH40K universe Chaos Gate would still be an excellent turn based strategy game.I expected an XCOM clone but was pleasantly surprised to discover that the tweaks that Complex Games have made to the formula go a very long way to making the combat feel unique. i.e. the extensive use of environmentals, the general lack of RNG and the aggressive playstyle encouraged without the use of game-ending timers.The sound design is overall quite spectacular. Weapons feel impactful, Bolters sound punchy, Space Marines sound like big stompy Space Marines without coming across as slow and clunky. My only complaint is that some of the enemy dialogue seems a little weak, especially compared to the Space MarinesVisually it's very pretty, it somehow captures that Grim Dark feeling despite having a very saturated colour palette. If anything it makes it feel like tabletop figures come to life. Some of the lighting is particularly impressive and explosions in particular are quite funIf you have any appreciation whatsoever for the grim dankness of the 41st millennium then I wholeheartedly recommend this game to you.If you have no idea what Warhammer is then I'd say this is a good place to start and I'll still recommend this game to you

_childDocuments_.review: A battle worn strike unit is forced to fight on.  This had everything to feel like X-com but it removes a lot of the rngness and innovates. You are always balancing on a knife's edge. Grey Knights are super soldiers able to cast magic, but in 40k magic comes from the demon realm, which causes it to attract demons. The more you use your magic superpower the faster the "demonic intervention" timer will count down. This knife's edge design is repeated throughout the game, your choices constantly have consequences in the wider picture.This is far less rngness than Xcom, shots will always hit, but range and cover offer flat damage reduction, armor blocks all damage until it is overcome and regenerates each round. Your action points are refunded after clearing an enemy patrol or upon discovering one, completely removing the slog of taking 3 turns making sure everyone is loaded and moving inch by inch.This is a really fun game, that does not pull it's punches, you'll be met with challenge after challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to the negative reviews that claim the game is too difficult. It really isn't. After you learn how each class works and how they synergize with others gameplay gets pretty smooth. You'll learn when you can push forward and when you need to fall back, which makes this game so much more engaging. You'll have enemies thrown at you left and right at times, you have to analyze your surroundings and create strategy on your own. There are even ways to pump all your resources into one marine to wipe entire squads with just one person. The tutorial really needs some work, it misleads you into thinking you can play recklessly, they don't really showcase real strategy. Yes, you can run in guns blazing, but only circumstantially. I'm almost willing to say this game is better than X-Com. Mainly because if you do things right, you completely turn the tides of battle and you're not really a victim of rng when it comes to this game. My only real complaint about this game is the dlc. It's hot garbage and not worth it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: If you played Battletech, you'll probably see many similarities. As the XCom comparisons miss on a couple aspects: 1) RNG is nowhere near as brutal in this game as the XCom franchise. Either for you or the enemy. If you miss a shot, you took one at someone in cover. Same if they miss. In general, your Grey Knights will do more damage. Be hardier. And can wade through chaff with relative ease. But the AI has brutes of its own. And will use the hordes to whittle you down until you walk into them. 2) The tools you have in the beginning have all the essential gameplay elements you'll see throughout the game. Unlike XCom, where you unlock bigger squads, new types of weapons and methods of attack, in this game, your tactics will be decided by the mission. And your gear by the character build. Which you'll probably have a strong idea of when you see what each character's trait and class are. There's more variation than the game tells you. And that's good and bad. Good because it rewards you for investigating the systems and becoming familiar with the mechanics. Bad because the game could do a better job of telling you some of these items. For example: Character Traits. Nowhere are you told each character has one of these. And if you don't hover your mouse over the center of each character's progression tree, you would never know it's there. The gameplay is very good. The story is solid. The music is YMMV. But I like it. The interface is Unity engine style. Which is another reason I say Battletech is a good point of reference. As both are Unity games. The game doesn't have near the performance hits of typical Unity fare though. So hats off to the developers for that. All in all, a solid game anyone who likes either Warhammer or Tactical RPGs should enjoy.

That mission with the imperial guard where you have to protect the four bases, more of that please, here's some ideas.Hold The Line - Hold a trench and repel waves of enemies.Under Siege - Hold a single fortification and repel waves of enemies.Dual Battles - The final battle was epic, where one squads action impacted the others, made it feel like a war, more variations of this would be great.(These missions can all include Imperial Guard too)Speaking of Imperial Guard, I would love if in a future DLC, this was the unit you could recruit. _childDocuments_.review: If you've read some of the Warhammer books and understand how brutal the universe is, then you'll have a good impression of what to expect. It is not Mechanicus where your Tech Priests become insanely strong, it is not Dawn of War with Hero characters. The intro mission sets the tone, and you becoming commander is not a fluke but a veiled reminder of the universe you are entering.Overall the progression of your knights into killing machines are awesome to see. But the chaos gods have an answer to everything you try prepare for. Luckily additional classes become available later in the campaign to assist in dealing with the ever increasing challenges you face. I will say that the difficulty increases steadily with your own power growth and it is only in the last 25% where you might have confidence knowing you can finish missions cleanly and efficiently. Beware that the closing 10% will quickly destroy all that confidence and personally I loved that twist of desperation. I honestly thought I would have to reset my 2 hours of final mission at several points.The story does a good job explaining the ever increasing difficulty and desperation of the gameplay. I was also surprised more than I thought I would be at the turns the story decided to make. In Xcom and Mechanicus the story is somewhat easy to read before hand, but I must say I was pleasantly surprised at what the writers decided to do with the story and how the characters felt genuine.If you understand and enjoy 40K and enjoy turn based strategy, then this is an awesome game. Replay value is there, but after the amount of time I put in in my first campaign I'll be taking a break. But I can see where there are ways to replay and take different paths with the classes. Way more variety than the other titles mentioned earlier. And on the sale price it really is a no-brainer.

_childDocuments_.review: Gotta be my favorite 40k game. The story is gripping and by the end I found the weird, 2010 Gmod style animation to be endearing. I really like the ability, in this game, to collect and maintain a reliquary of unique and named weapons, armor, and wargear. Daemonhunters is also quite bug free for a modern Warhammer game...I played through the campaign once on normal difficulty and found it to be quite fair, maybe a little on the easy side, but only after it had been earned through research and leveling of knights. There's definitely replay value in this title and I'll be revisiting it soon.It has a good hours-of-gameplay-to-price ratio at full price and, on sale, it has fantastic value.Also, you get to play as the coolest Warhammer faction, the Greyknights. Honestly I think you can pretty much fit the entire Grey Knights Codex into this game, and you have a Strike Cruiser! Where are my dreadnoughts and DreadKnights! _childDocuments_.review: I am very glad to say that I really enjoy this game and I can't stop playing it! Experienced a lot heavy crashes about 5 times out of my 50 hrs play time, specially after starting the mission after I completed assigning my strike force. Fortunately, there were a lot of auto-save functions after each of your selections in-game so that you can just reload your game when it crashes. And also the application always starts-up regardless of the heavy crash and did not corrupt your saved games unlike other games.- Yep I knew that WH40k should be bloody and gritty. I also initially thought that this game seems "way too clean" not enough blood, grit and weathering. - But the game already have all of those details. the graphics shader was just too bright/colorful(?) or something comic-like or overwatch-like. Still way better than League of Legends graphics in my game standards. A dark, gritty, and bloody graphics mod should be made available soon. Personally, I think the graphics fits the board game origins of it.- Yep I knew that it only takes 100 Space Marines to conquer Earth against its United Earth Armies.- Yep I knew that Space Marines are genetically engineered Super Soldiers like Captain America but came equipped with Vacuum sealed Space Powered Suits made out of Ceramite, an armor made out of a combination of Cement and Metal.- Yes, I was frustrated seeing that a regular human soldier with firearms can just kill a space marine, not just a space marine but a Gray Knight, an elite spec-ops army of the Emperor dedicated on fighting the Army of Chaos with magic powers in the shadows.- But I also knew that the lore was very difficult to translate and balance in a game so give the developers a break. - Don't get me wrong it can be done with proper writing, planning, and time or just introduce it as an easy mode in the game.I did not played the WH board games nor do I own the model kits (but I do own some JoyToy articulated and highly detailed Blood Angels Death Company figures). I am a huge fan of Starcraft and ever since I saw the Astartes/Space Marines knowing that they pre-dated Starcraft. Since then I knew that Starcraft and all its races was based on or ripped-off from the Warhammer franchise. But unlike Starcraft, the Warhammer franchise was extremely and painfully mismanaged with very poor business decisions made in the past. By now Warhammer should have been bigger/popular than both Starcraft and Warcraft games that was based out of it. Warhammer should have been bigger than Starship Troopers, Star Wars, and Star Trek. With multiple CGI or live action movie trilogies or movie-verse and various game styles made out of it. Yep, very painfully mismanaged. Originally I came here just to support the WH40k franchise knowing its possibilities and was surprisingly satisfied with the gameplay. Coming from my all-time favorite turn based games like Disciples 2 and Tactics Ogre: Knights of Lodis.But I have these few nitpicks or proposals that the developers can help improve in the game in the near future:1. Do not limit the screen rotation in just 4 corners. It could have been dynamic since this is a beautifully colored and detailed 3D graphics game. A complete camera 360 support should have been made available like the other 3rd person action games.2. The game was extremely detailed and the current Zoom-in limit was still a bit far. The player should be able to zoom-in and see all those beautiful and wonderful character designs and details while in the game map. 3. Yes I am aware of the Character Info screen, but even that it was only limited to the front view. The player should at least be able to rotate the character in that screen.4. More Mouse control support in the settings. The user should be able to rotate the map using the mouse, zoom-in and zoom-out. The accept and decline function currently was a great touch.5. The unit HP HUD was severely underutilized. Other than the selected Unit HP it could also already show the unit Ammo Capacity, Action Points, and Warp/Will Points. thereby allowing the players to clear out some screen clutters and show the complete  beautiful game map and units with less screen clutters. 6. The Character customization screen should have mouse scroll support for an unlocked manual zoom-in and zoom-out. A and D keys should also be supported in rotating the character.Regardless, overall I'm very satisfied with this game. Already looking forward for DLCS like:1. An Ultramarine version or various different Chapters selection.2. Other races defend against Gray Knights invasion or invade a planet fighting Kriegs and etc. A complete reversal of this game.3. A new story or new game exploring the Emperor Origins from the Thunder Warriors, The Hunt for each Primarchs on different galaxy sectors, Horus Heresy, and so much more!

_childDocuments_.review: 30 Hours in I can say this game will give you some good enjoyment for your money if you can handle some teething issues with optimization and some rough-around-the-edges balancing. This game emanates WH40k-ness, so much that everything looks 100% like the miniatures, and does a good job at doing its own take on turn based tactics. My Review is based on the highest difficulty.The gameplay is XCOM but with RNG only extended into the positive, which means you always hit if your enemy is in line of sight and not in full cover, but crits can happen that allow you to disable enemy body parts. Some classes have abilities with 100% to make this system usable in your tactical calculations, the same goes for the value to apply or resist negative effects. All of the classes are useful and there are lots of party compositions that work out, I found it highly enjoyable and the game also invites you to experiment even on the highest difficulty. Some damage abilities heavily fall off during late game, though.The difficulty curve of the game is kinda weird, while you are likely to get challenged by early game enemies, and very much so, the game becomes easier in mid-to-late game when you have some equipment and can abuse the execution mechanic to get six or more actions per turn. While you navigate your ship, the Baleful Edict, through space to mission locations random events can happen, and those I found the most annoying. I lost my best Purgator to an action that didn't even say he was in danger, and when you send Knights on a mission the game does not let you choose which ones, so you might lose your entire squad to some random event, which is unacceptable. This was easily the part of the game I consider most unfair, since in some situations you just lose no matter what you choose and it's not made clear how some actions will affect the outcome of an action. If you enjoy a good turn based tactics game with WH40k atmo and lore you will have plenty of fun here. If you're unsure, wait for patches, it can only get better from hereon out.

_childDocuments_.review: I have several complaints. But I wanted to first touch on the difficulty "issue" some folks are having. I am very much someone who likes a game that isn't frustratingly difficult. Because of reviews, I played this on the easiest setting. It's been ridiculously easy. I don't know what people are doing that makes it seem too hard for them, maybe I've just been around strategy/tactical RPGs for longer, but full cover giving 100% damage protection is bonkers strong compared to basically any other similar game. Using units appropriately and making calm decisions in combat and the galaxy map helps too.Now for my complaints: There's not much randomness in combat.. but they put that all elsewhere. Random weapons, random new troops, random encounters on the galaxy map, random (seemingly) responses doing random things for events. I've gotten so I save scum less for missions and more for events on the galaxy map.Gear organization is terrible. Not being able to sell or scrap items is annoying too. (So much so that when the monthly visit insists I give up some of my unequipped stock, I don't even hesitate.)There's a decent bit of variety in the maps. But mission types, enemy types... those don't change a whole lot. And it's ALL Nurgle. Which is the theme, but there's so much in the WH40k universe to tap in to...Lastly and most importantly, there's a LOT of QOL stuff that is in other similar games but not this one... Two speeds for enemy turns: Ridiculously slow, or too fast to figure out what's going on. And there's only 1 for yours: Too slow. Even outside of combat you have to manually move every single Daemonhunter manually, complete their animation, before you can move the next. And there's no way to speed up their movement. There's also a LOT of unskippable dialog. Every mission starts with some unwitty banter between the main crew of the ship about the mission. Even when it's the 37th time you've done the exact same mission.Would I recommend it? If you like 40k as much as I do, especially both Nurgle and Daemonhunters, definitely. It is a lot of fun, despite its shortcomings. But I would defintely not buy it for its full price, I got it for about 10% of the normal price.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like Imperial Guard Simulator, except you're cosplaying as Grey Knights.Did you know regular bolters do more damage than storm bolters?Did you know that human cultists are more durable than space marines?Did you know that Chaos Marine armor is far superior to what Grey Knights wear?If you enjoy watching the finest of the Astartes hit a regular human with a force halberd and repeatedly fail to kill him, this is the game for you.It's actually not a terrible tactics game, aside from the clunky UI and slow animations and transitions, but it manages to make the Grey Knights feel grossly incompetent at every turn. Power armored marine took a punch from a one-armed cultist? Wounded for thirty days. Cultist crouching behind a box? Essentially invulnerable to ranged attack. Every mission type requires you to push push push relentlessly, so you spend most of your AP trying to catch up to enemies who spawn in by the half dozen, then fall back into cover to shoot you to pieces. Because yes, human cultists are better marksmen than Grey Knights, their rusty stubbers outranging even your purgators.Hence Imperial Guard simulator. Were I running a dozen lasgun monkeys, I'd understand how digging gribbly cultists out of their cover could be a rough fight. Instead, I'm watching terminators get punched and take damage.The ideas in it are interesting, but this is a game where their only ideas for challenges are to put a timer on every mission and reward you for bringing fewer soldiers. As a result, every fight plays out the same: rush forwards at full speed, because the enemy gets more actions than you and is almost guaranteed to use several of them to fall back, drawing out every fight so the bloom can spawn in more of them or buff them to insane levels. The devs response to this was to nerf the mobile classes.

_childDocuments_.review: I started this game on legendary and am very familiar with playing turn based tactical games on thier hardest difficulties.I have seen this game compared to xcom and I don't think thats fair, this game is different and better imo for taking out all rng chances to hit your enemy and putting rng into events, stages, rewards, units starting passives, random negative debuffs in a stage called warp surges and optional objectives on stages for more rewards, etc. This alone gives your units more agency and control over the effect you have on the battlefield while maintaining a different experience everytime due to the rng placed in other places as mentioned in the last sentence and just to make a small note, the mini cut scenes of your marines breaking down doors and what not gives a real cool feel to the game. There is also ship management, tech research and other outside of combat choices you make that can further strengthen your gameplay or possible weaken it depending on your luck adding another layer of depth to being successful. The progression of your units is mainly a skill tree and there gear combined with global abilities called strategems that can be used on any unit per battle and a unique system of possibly augmenting your units to have better stats when they die and brought back to life which I believe there could be more here but its adequate for most. I do really like the game but there are very punishing mechanics, soo much that to avoid them is a profound advantage but cannot always be avoided because of rng, think darkest dungeon kinda. If a unit loses 25% or more of there life anytime in battle, even if you heal it back, they receive an injury that lowers max life for x amount of days which makes it that much harder to avoid getting a critical injury the next mission if you use and so on and so on almost snowballing, this combined with my inability to properly read how the enemy ai acts, I almost wonder if some rng plays a role, caused me to save scum on multiple occasions to avoid every getting critical injuries although I was playing my first time on legendary that should be expected I would think. The skills trees have maybe 2, maybe 3 real ways to build your unit and if you don't build them that way, your in for a bad time and as well not all units are created equal, you will find that your interceptor will carry your gameplay and supporting him with buffers is one of the best ways to play, I wish there were more options so I didn't feel like a meta slave so much although I have heard the expansions open up more playstyles due to releasing more unit classes. Not all mission are created equal either some missions will have you ripping out your hair because of the difficulty spike when if it had been a different mission you would have steamrolled it with your eyes closed, I can only believe that either balancing was not done or it was intentional so that you have to make the choice of wether the mission is worth doing. This all leads to basically the game will punish you alot for lack of knowledge, not looking up a guide, I was fortunate enough to figure out on my own what would be some of the best skill tree choices on units and what units were the best to invest in on my own as well as best ship upgrades but found myself needng to lookup alot of stuff about the game in order to not "screw up" my game on my first playthrough from where to position prognosticators because you could never anticipate the map would get larger or not to research a certain tech to give yourself time to get stronger before "the next chaptor".TLDR The game is great, offers adequate customization although only a couple real paths for the most success, takes the rng out of the attacks and into the outside world and enemy although enemy ai seems difficult to predict, and if your playing for a challenge know you will be punished for a lack of knowledge that the game does not provide you until it's too late.

_childDocuments_.review: I like it. I was never a hardcore Warhammer 40k Fan, so i know not a lot about the Lore and stuff, but the Gameplay is pretty solid, reminds a lot of a combination of Xcom and Gears Tactics.  Most Negative Reviews i have seen are somewhat bound around the twitch dops (which YES, is a real no go, but they changed their mind and will give them to everone, so that point is gone at this point in time, AND "Grey Knights feel to weak , they should be true elite and never die", which i can not say is true at all. Again, NO idea about the lore, but compared with Xcom, your Knights are pretty tough IF you play carefully. Standing in the open and eating 5 Attacks : You probably survive, but : Bad idea, that dude is in hospital a long time (you can use him, but with reduced HP ) But if you use the Cover, especially full Cover, they will probably not even take s singe HP-Damage.  I am not very far yet, however, like 10-11 Hours in the game.The game uses NO %-based ToHit System!, you (nearly) always know how much damage you will do at least (you can crit and deal more).  But don´t be fooled, its still VERY hard. I play on "Standard" Difficulty (2 out of 4), and Ironman Mode, and some encounters are really tought. However, there are a lot of clever mechanics in the game that allow you for some "thinking ahead" planning. (e.g. you can see the enemie "pods" positions and where they will move (but not what exactly awaits you), and uncovering a pod, when you are out of combat, will refresh all your Knights AP , so no more "move with 2 Units, and then dont move an inch further than that because you might trigger something. That really helps with a more aggressive approach, as you actually "save" Turns without risking Knights due to "ups, last guy with 1 AP triggered the pot, i guess i am screwed" moments. And if all goes wrong, you have a lot of Skills you can use to turn the tables, most of them are pretty powerful/useful

_childDocuments_.review: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters isn't perfect but it's fun and has a ton of heart and atmosphere.  It can get aggravating to wait for the computer to make all of its moves, most notably at the end of the game when it has 20-25 units on the board, tactical play at that point can become tedious and repetitive. But overall the game is engaging, immersive and, as I mentioned above, fun.  If you're a fan of the X-Com reboots and Warhammer 40K in general than this game is for you.  The art direction is great, the lore is on point and the campaign is interesting and full of twists and turns that do the writers a lot of credit.  I should mention that the designers opted out of the frustrating RNG combat model used in X-Com.  Every action's outcome is predetermined and you can see what that outcome will be before selecting the action you want, no more missing at point blank range, hallelujah.  The game has a lot of re-playability and I can see myself playing through it a second time.  A solid 8 out of 10, have fun, stay alert and keep your boltgun handy.

_childDocuments_.review: Rewriting this review now that i've finished the game. I will say the most important thing about this game is the story is actually really quite good. It's more compelling than most other games in the xcom style and if you really enjoy 40k, is a must have. The game game is not without flaws. Most noteworthy is the cinematic animations. They leave a lot to be desired, but you can almost forgive them considering just how many there are. A big thing about this game is it is surprisingly long. Everytime you think things are about to wrap up, you find you've only just peeled one layer of the onion. That is not something you see in xcom games, almost ever.The major issues I had in my previous review are still present here. This game is HARD. I love xcom games. I consider myself fairly seasoned with them, but i had to lower the difficulty on this to "normal" putting this title on the same level as "hard" or "very hard" for other xcom titles. The upside is the game builds in a lot of benefits to failure. Knights won't just randomly up and die, they take a critical wound instead. Once a knight has too many, they are actually dead. Even then, once dead you can use them to gain extra talent points for another knight, or respec that knights talent trees. Not to mention, with each critical wound knights gain bonuses... so really it is important to simply embrace failure, in a way. I can't emphasize it enough though, the best part of this game for me was the story that was told. I thought I was able to predict what would happen, but I never could. Really cool experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The base game was enjoyable enough on hard during my first play though, but the DLCs destroyed that experience. Duty Eternal ratchets up and skews the difficulty of the base game and non-DLC missions with zero tools to counter balance it. No additional weapons or armors, permanent armor destruction by enemies, more aggravating warp surges and unbalanced elite units. Oh but you get a wildly inferior Techmarine as a liability you have to swap a competent squad class for? ♥♥♥♥♥♥' ridiculous. Devs refuse to listen to what the community wants and Execution Force repeats the same mistakes that Duty did. I could deal with watching some turd with a stubber outshoot a transhuman super warrior because of balance reasons in the base game, but not with how inconsistent difficulty has become now, because no one finds that fun. Its just lazy to constantly not evolve beyond the lazy crap a lot of devs do; bullet sponge enemies, kneecapping your units, 4 soldiers/3 AP, etc. I was hoping they'd move past this common developer mistake when making a squad based 40k game.

_childDocuments_.review: While there is a lot of fun to be had playing Chaosgate, the game needs to get out of its own way. You are constantly being pushed forward in the story, with very little control over what you actually do. Random events pop up often and almost invariably penalise you for making the "wrong" choice, with no way to understand the consequences of your choices before you make them. I enjoy the action in the game, and it looks pretty good, but I've also taken to keeping a book next to my computer to read while the enemy takes their turn. In my first play through (failed the campaign) I finished the first half of Rabbit Redux by John Updike doing this. I hope that this game is developed into something better than it is because at the moment it is a fun X-Com clone weighed down by punishing and grindy mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: The only gripe I have is that it's a bit unbalanced. Decided to play on normal, and got my ass completely kicked for the first few hours of the game. Managed to not lose any Knights, but got incredibly close many times. I decided to go for the 'purple' boss first first, and it took me roughly 3 hours and many, many restarts to finally beat it. However, after this, the game became a too easy. Once you've got a good interceptor and a few justicars with AP boosts, the rest of the game is a breeze. Every subsequent boss fight was done after literally 1-2 turns, by simply beefing up my interceptor to hit as hard as the Emperor Himself.The art style took some getting used to, and it's oddly reminiscent of Fable of all things, but it has its charm. The animations are gorgeous, and working out a good plan of attack is very satisfying when it pays off. Recommended on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has solid foundations, but currently it suffers from unintuitive UI, several bugs which can ruin the experience (permanently disabled stratagems with no explanation in my case) and grindy missions in the later part of the game which are (in my opinion) more of a chore than fun.Reporting bugs is such a hassle. After creating an account you can't report right away, you have to wait a period. After starting a report, I took my sweet time gathering screenshots, and saved games to archive and send them for review. The page forgot what I had written as a description and steps to reproduce. I wrote everything again, submitted and got an error message "We are sorry, but the issue could not be added to the system", no further context. It will probably be a good game after a few patches in, but currently, I would wait a bit before buying. _childDocuments_.review: It's a great tactical rpg with plenty to love. But in this review, I'll focus on the negatives other reviews have listed rather than the big positives. If you like tactical rpgs, you'll probably like it. A tiny bit about myself: I adore turn-based strategy in all forms it takes. Though I've never managed to finish any X-Com game. I take my time with them and eventually something new comes along before I can wrap up my 100+ hours campaign.The twitch drops are forgettable. They're all simple T1 gear, and none of them have particularly exceptional looks, either. They give 10% crit chance or +1 crit damage. You will get similar and better gear the moment your missions start rewarding gear (about 1h into the game). The pre-order hammer and book are more substantial, but hardly overpowered. You get similar gear about 4-12 hours into the game, depending on how hard you rush the requisition upgrades that boost your loot drops (it's a very simple system).I like them. The enemies are somewhat cartoony, but that seems adequate, given that they're Grandfather Nurgle's jolly hordes. Your knights look badass and not cartoony at all. The simpler graphic style also means you can easily tell at a glance if enemies have mutations (a system that makes basic enemies more dangerous as the game progresses), and that you can play it very well on weaker hardware and have it still look fine. I play on max on my desktop and on minimal on my ♥♥♥♥♥♥ old laptop, and while max is prettier minimal still looks pretty decent.I've played on normal difficulty so far, and while it took me a few missions to get used to it, the game seemed straight forward enough once you get a hang of the mechanics. Basic enemy cultists hurt a lot if you're out in the open and they have the numbers advantage, but once you realize they waste their action on a really weak punch if youstand next to them, and that their guns deal next to no damage if you're in cover, you very quickly figure out how to dismantle encounters. Another important trick is to realize that once you kill the last enemy, your entire squad immediately reloads all weapons and recovers full action points. So you use up all your ap to heal and reposition before finishing off the last enemy and then immediately move to trigger the next encounter. It's possibly to finish some of the easier missions on smaller maps without the enemy ever getting even a single turn, once you levelled your guys a bit.If a knight takes even a single point of damage, they suffer a "minor wound" after the battle. If they take more than half total hp in damage (regardless of healing during the mission), they suffer a major wound. If they go down, they suffer a critical wound. Minor wounds reduce max hp by 3, major wounds by 6, critical wounds by 9. Your average knight has 14 hp (though it's fairly simple to get them to 20+ total hp around my current playtime, and presumably even more later). Wounds take from 14-60 days to heal (depending on severity and some RNG). But here's the thing. Nothing stops you from continuing to use an injured knight. And if they are, say, recovering from a major wound, suffering another major or minor wound wont extend their recovery time at all. A critical wound will, though. So it's a system that incentives not letting your knights take too much damage, but not overly punishing if they do. The max hp reduction hurts somewhat, but is far from a run-ending handicap.I have no idea where this comes from. The UI gives you all the information you need during a mission with very few clicks, and I've never really noticed it "getting into the way". The only minor gripe I have is that you cant go directly from the gear screen to the skill tree or swap to another knight's gear screen without first having to exit out of the gear screen. But that's not really that much of a problem?

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to “screw you gate”, the warhammer 40K game where you will get rewarded with punishment and annoyance on top game difficulty. The game itself tries to be a X-COM rip off with not even a close match to the delightful work that the X-COM remaster had.  While X-COM has a fast-paced campaign where mistakes can be really punishing, this game skips all that and even if you make good decisions and you manage to keep everything straight for some time, it will still kick your nuts, because screw you.  The game fancies an artificially created difficulty with the “ warp surge” mechanic, which can basically hinder you every few turns, or buff the enemy every few turns, this is on top of the fact that all enemies usually have much more range than you, they are also  more than you, and practically all enemies have one or more special skills (which can combo with the mentioned buffs or debuffs) The game campaign also aims to bother you at every step, for example: Are you doing well? Have you stocked hard earned samples that you pretend to convert into much needed upgrades for your equipment? Well, what about we take half of those from your hands because of no bloody reason? That’s nice of you, grand master. At least the storytelling for campaign is not bad, plus this is a Warhammer 40k game. To make a general balance of the game, I would say:  Cons: Learning curve is steep and punishing, get ready to start over a couple of campaignsCombat feels a penance because of the horrible design of the mechanics, especially the warp surges. It feels like as if they could not get to balance the game and as it felt “too easy” they artificially added the Warp surges to make it artificially harder. Campaign would be ok if all the events were not just to screw you, some of them REALLY HARD You need to mostly “live off the land” because better gear can be only obtained based on the planet you make the missions, and the missions trigger randomly, so you may not be able to make a truly polished build for your characters I think they saw how bad this was and changed it when introducing the assassins and the dreadnought, but that is too late for the main body of the game There is a game mechanic to “enhance” your characters, but requires them to be mortally wounded, which makes them unavailable for a very long time. At the start of the game, you don’t have many characters and they heal really slow, causing that if you get them some mortally wounded, you might find yourself in a situation where you can’t complete missions  PROS:  It is a Warhammer 40 K game with a very good ambience, they really got the lore right The story is interesting, and it is well told The boss fights are fun, quite fun, to be honest To wrap things up, if you are not into BSDM, just try to avoid the game because it mostly feels like a torture. If you decide to get the game, absolutely not worth to buy at full price, wait for discounts.

The early game was more difficult for me than the late game, after upgraded gear, leveled-up Astartes, and special classes were all on-hand, enabling different tactics and synergies. It can be interesting to try different combinations of classes in a squad. Personally I favored using Interceptors and Purifiers.Things I did not like: - The character animations are often distracting. Lunete's "expressions" are probably the best example of this. - Vakir and Lunete are obnoxious. Lunete adds nothing to the game other than Mechanicus "representation", if you will. - Ball was dropped with respect to the soundtrack. There's some great Warhammer-themed music & ambiance here,  but it's mostly tucked away in ship locations/menus that you don't spend much time in. What you do hear the most is the generic "marching"/"prepare for batlle" music, which becomes grating very quickly. I grew to hate it. The combat music is also repetitive and not very good. It's a far cry from what Guillame David created for WH40K: Mechanicus,  sadly. - Combat missions become repetitive chores. Not enough variation in mission types. - It takes much too long to get access to good gear. By the time I had 30+ grimoires I only had three decent tier-3 Terminator power armor sets for example. - Plot is forgettable and somewhat ridiculous.  - Final boss battle is a slog.

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t think I’ve played a game that feels so similar to X-Com, yet plays so differently. Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate – Daemonhunters looks like X-Com and dialup up to 11 with the breach sequences, but absolutely punishes you if you take a wrong approach to combat, and the errors compound quickly. Its base difficulty is fairly high, and with its unintuitive gameplay mechanisms and clunky UI can lead to frequent campaign restarts (or at least going back a few saves). Recommended for Warhammer 40K fans, or those who like tactical turn based combats who don’t mind frequent difficultly spikes.You play the role of a newly elevated Grey Knight commander, leading his decimated ship and forces back to Titan when an Inquisitor intercepts you and “requests” the Grey Knights assistance with stopping a demonic plague (the bloom), from spreading beyond the current subsector that it has been detected in. This is the start of a much larger story, and involves many well-known characters from both the Grey Knights and Death Guard, and what you think could be a major battle turns out to only be the start of a much larger conflict between the two opposing factions.I found the story good, choices you make affect gameplay and squad readiness significantly, it doesn’t go against any of the settings established lore and having to manage relationships between the main characters on the ship (who are often at ends with each other) while constantly fighting running battles, random events and reinforcing you current squads gives the feeling of always being 2 steps behind the enemy and severely under resourced. The 8 troop types you can pick all have abilities that align to the tabletop game, and give you fairly free reign in how to develop your squads. Losing experienced squad members can be devastating (at the time), but at least you don’t lose their equipment and the game does have mechanisms to get you up on your feet quickly if you invest in the right technologies. If you are fortunate enough to have the right resources on hand, you can exterminate planets, which is very much in line with what the grey knights and inquisition would do.Gameplay is similar in most regards to X-COM titles, though differs enough that you can easily set your campaign behind if you play it like X-COM. There are a few instant game over conditions, which requires careful management and progression of resources and research. You can’t always avoid the events that cause additional damage to your ship, and need to keep a handy stock of servitors (resources used to upgrade rooms), and possibly planet destroying missiles if you don’t want to do the Morbus mission that seem to constantly appear. Failing a mission isn’t a game over, though the squad will be in recovery for an abnormally long time, and it can lead to the death of a marine, and is more likely to happen on a Morbus mission (where enemies are constantly reinforced) or during a bossfights where there are instant death pits and you have to choose between mobility and firepower. The actual missions are where the largest departure from X-Com is felt. You have free reign to pick any 4 squad members before deploying, including their equipment and weapons. Gameplay has you generally performing 1 of a few mission types (these do get repetitive quickly, even if the terrain and layout constantly changes), which either involve killing 1 large well protected target, killing 3 wandering targets then surviving for a few rounds, or defending priority targets from multiple waves of enemies. Increasing levels of corruption increases the resistance found in stages, the available buffs enemies will have, and you are punished every few rounds by a debuff that hits your team or a spawn of additional enemies for you to fight, which is a kick in the pants as the games already difficult enough without handicapping you more.The game doesn’t seem to know if you it wants you to play cautiously or hard and fast with your Grey Knights, punishing you every few turns, but also really wanting you to hug cover and avoid taking any damage all at (or at least only taking damage against armour that regenerates every turn). Enemy patrol usually consist of between 1 to 6 enemies, and they all activate together. You generally want to be stunning enemies to unlock a execute move (which then gives the entire squad another turn), or if killing the patrol isn’t an option using precision attacks to perform critical hits (which then allows you to remove an attack or inflict a debuff on the enemy). It’s another kick in the pants that enemies regenerate from these easily enough, undoing your planning. Overwatch takes you out of cover, making it practically useless (unless you are only left with enemies who will melee you), and the units you really want to overwatch with, can’t (Purifiers). On the system map, you can control the routes to each planet to take on bloom missions. Each mission advises you of what your rewards will be (either in weapons, armour, new recruits, resources or requisition), as well as the mission type and it’s a fine balancing act between going for the mission that has the correct rewards vs what you can reach before the missions expire (the planets corruption increases). You can also purchase ship upgrades, research abilities (that either help in missions or help further the story), and upgrade and reequip your recruits and equipment. This is also where you will death with Death Guard fleet missions, random events, and receive your regular dressing down from your grand-master. Most of these events generally have a negative impact, which can start taking its toll on your campaign, but on a positive note it does fell like there are hundreds of these and they don’t seem to repeat (even if they are random).The game does a great job in animating the corruption of Nurgle across the stages, with increasing corruption warping each stage more. Enemies look great (though each enemy type is exactly the same), and battle damage is shown against the enemies. The execute (instant kill) moves are very cool, and the different bosses are varied, have vastly different attack patterns and offer a good challenge. The animation of enemies and units busting through the environment is great, and the environment is mostly destructible (cover can become very rare in prolonged firefights).This is a nightmare to play on normal, you would have to be masochist to want to play this in the hardest settings. _childDocuments_.review: I would love to recommend this game, I've tried very hard to like it and in many ways it has a lot going for it:+ The audio is great, both effects and music.+ Character design is generally good,if slightly too cartoonish for my taste. + The combat is weighty and satisfying. + The decision to remove chance to hit RNG is great. Sadly, I can't recommend the game, and wish I could get my 80+ hours and money back, for the following reasons:- RNG has been removed from chance to hit and instead injected into every other mechanic in the game, resulting in frequently, brutally unfair encounters and enemy spawns that take it from satisfyingly challenging to a pointless waste of time.- Optimisation is non-existent in this game. It runs poorly while looking mediocre.- Environments are very similar and consist of 1 or 3 template arenas that get randomised slightly for each mission. - The unit upgrade tree is full of choices that aren't meaningful, or sub-optimal and will get you killed.- The game is more stressful than fun. Like many people, I play to relax after work. The chance that I will get steamrolled in any given mission due to unlucky enemy spawns, or warp events, is totally off putting and will make me want to play anything else 9 times our of 10. TLDR - I wish I could go back in time and never have bothered with this game. It's an un-optimised mess that's full of petty mechanics designed to ♥♥♥♥ on your day, rather than present a genuine challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that tries to copy X-Com but makes everything worseIn a nutshell, its neither a homage to nor an improvement on X-Com, it is an attempt to cash in on its fame by producing a badly thought out, player unfriendly shadow of its older brother.It is fair to compare this game to X-Com, there is actually no other way to talk about it, since it is a a blatant copy of that game. That would be fine, that is how business/ the gaming industry works. It would be even better, if Chaos Gate built on X-Com and made improvements on its predecessors issues. Instead they try to hide their kinship by making menus and interfaces different to a point they are just confusing. What this game does wrong- unnecessary tutorials that stop the flow- no tutorials where they are actually needed- confusing menus (no overview of all the ongoing construction, healing, research at once)- confusing interfaces (Ability overview of a Soldier... an experience)- UNSKIPPABLE CUT-SCENES- UNSKIPPABLE ANIMATED ACTION-Sequences during gameplay (Moving your ship from one sector to another give you a 10s window to contemplate your lifes choices while watching your ship activate the chaos engine for the hundredth time, the same way... wanna throw a grenade, better prepare for a 5 sec animation of the grenade flip, wanna go through a door... oh boy, better get strapped in and check out the funimation of your marine breaking it down every single time...)I played about 10 hours and got more and more frustrated. I cant remember ever quitting a game I invested so much time in, this is a first. (In retrospect, I also quit the new attempt on reinvigorating homeworld)

_childDocuments_.review: This is a turn based tactical game like XCOM, like XCOM, if your Grey Knights end the battle with wounds, it takes an absurdly long time to heal them, while you are under a timer to cleanse more planets. This provides the fun aspect of having your higher level units recuperating, forcing you to either use under-leveled Knights to tackle the next mission, or using the hurt Knights and risking them dying. Even on the easiest difficulty, its pretty stressful. The Apothecarions arent able to heal every turn, which makes the above situation worse. I rage quit XCOM 2 every time I try to play it. This game seems to take that frustrating aspect of the game and bring it wholesale into this. I really enjoyed the accessibility options that Mechanicus had, had the option to make is stupid easy, basically turning it to a guided tour of the game. This, unfortunately, does not have that. I get that a lot of people love XCOM 2 for its difficulty, and that's cool, you do you. I do not enjoy games that piss me off. I play to relax and chill, maybe have fun stomping enemies.Difficulty aside, the graphics are great. The cutscenes are acurate to the lore of 40K. The game has a little cartoony aesthetic to it, which is unique. Music is good, just not Mechanicus level of good. The Grey Knights are insanely powerful in the lore, but here, a Chaos Cultist can kill your massive Grey Knight with a dinky pistol if they get enough shots in. No glitches seen yet, however the Kill Cam can clip oddly into walls during the close-ups and you just stare at a wall while your Knight turns the enemy into chunks. If they add accessibility options into this on an update, I would highly recommend this to everyone that enjoys 40k or XCOM 2. As is, it's difficult and frustrating on the easiest setting.
