_childDocuments_.review: There are some traps at the start of this game and I can see how a lot of people with only a couple hours of play time would come away with a negative impression. They're not wrong.While XCOM 2 is the single biggest influence on the game and clearly the starting point of the design, it mixes in other modern games like Gears Tactics and has enough ideas of its own that you'll be very frustrated if you try to play it just like XCOM at the tactical level. The game does not introduce you to its systems well either. Not from the perspective of a new player, and very much not from the perspective of an XCOM veteran who's chiefly interested in the things that are different. Cover, overwatch, armor, RNG, critical hits, action points, movement, skills, etc. are all quite different and need to be re-learned. Optimal play patterns are very different in this game compared to the games that inspired it.At the same time, while in many ways this game is devoted to the 40K lore, the developers treated it as only a suggestion when they were tuning the early-game combat and progression. If you come into the game with lore based notions of how tough Space Marines are, and expect that power fantasy out of the gate, you're in for a rude surprise. Cultists with mere slug-throwers are going to damage and sometimes wound your marines, even those with terminator armor, with one or two hits. Your level one and two guys with the entry level gear, despite looking, walking and quacking like Space Marines, are closer in power to XCOM recruits you need to keep behind cover. It feels bad.The far-from-purely-cosmetic pre-order kit, the cheat-code marine in the special edition and the twitch drops all leave a bad taste in the mouth as well.But if you can get through those bad initial impressions, and engage the game on its own terms, there's something really special here. The game isn't just copying other tactical shooters, it's in conversation with them, mixing things up in some very interesting ways. The combat systems they've changed largely feel like improvements and after the rough opening, fit well with being elite Space Marines. The skill trees and the gear system allow real builds to emerge. As these builds start to take shape and you personally start to master the game's systems, the power fantasy kicks in and then some. Your squad of marines will be able to roll through tough encounters with some real momentum, not getting shot at all, or only getting shot when you intend to on troops with enough armor to shrug it off. At the strategic level, it feels even more like XCOM 2 out of the gate, but finds its own identity as the game goes on with constant and interesting tension in your choice of missions and how to spend your resources. The interplay between tactical and strategic are great, with the strategic often asking you to take extra risks and leave your comfort zone in the tactical for some extra resources.The story is better than anyone should expect from a game like this. In the now familiar pattern, it starts with XCOM and finds its own voice from there. Like XCOM, it's told largely by your supporting caste in your HQ. Unlike XCOM, there's some real tension between the characters and you make decisions that have real, if sometimes opaque, impact on your campaign. The writing and voice acting are solid. Cut scenes are fully voiced. The interactive dialog has about one sentence per paragraph getting voiced. My one complaint in this department is that that one sentence isn't always the first sentence of the paragraph, creating some real dissonance where you either need to just listen to their line without the context of what they were supposed to say before it, or try to read their response as written while ignoring what they are saying. It's a baffling choice in an otherwise very well produced story.This game is not without flaws, and they are unfortunately very front-loaded in the experience. But it's loaded with love for the genre and setting, and some real ambition to be its own game and create new thrills and challenge, even for those like me who've taken many a lap around its tactical shooter predecessors. There's a reason, I think, for the disparity between the near universal critical acclaim and the mixed player reaction. Critics had to get through the opening to write their review. Normal players are under no such obligation.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - PASSABLE: 6/10Same gripes as most of the players. Marines are fragile, ranged weapons hardly have range, 4 member squad limit, it also follows XCOM style of gameplay instead of staying in line with the first Chaos Gate game.Yeah, I'm one of those salty Gen Xers that's been playing 40k since "before it was cool", so I'm a little more opinionated than some other fans. The first game was one of the best 40k games ever(still available on GOG, btw). This feels like more like XCOM than Chaos Gate. Enemies move in clusters which once spotted break up into individual units. It makes the most important part of your strategy positioning your team before combat starts.Cover is broken. You either have 100% chance to hit, or 0%. If you are behind low cover and use overwatch, works fine. If you are in high cover and use it, your knight will peal out to the side of it, completely exposed, instead of just peaking around and still using the cover.Armor is a joke. Your power armor has a rating of 0 standard, where as the Chaos marines have 2-3 standard. This means all damage is done to your health(more on that) with basic power armor, where as Chaos marines have 2-3 points that regen every turn.Fragile marines. If you stub your toe, or scuff your knee, expect to have 2-4 weeks of recovery time for the most minor of injuries.Ranged weapons. A cultist with a an autogun has better range than your highly trained knight with the best weaponry the Imperium can build.Strategy is lacking. With only a team of 4, and limited range it just turns into a scramble to find cover every turn. Especially with an enemy that goes into overwatch with more range than you.Personally, I've never been a huge fan of Grey Knights, but that's just me.If you're a 40k fan than you'll find some enjoyment of this. If you're looking for a strategy game, just do XCOM, which does it better. Hopefully the devs will fix the armor issue, reduce chances of being wounded, and balance out the ranged weaponry.

_childDocuments_.review: Ehh, it is ok. Good cartoony graphics and smooth game play but that is about it. I found a bug in the first few minutes - I could not start repairing the ship, I had to save and reload (thanks to the info on the Steam forum). The game totally ruins the effect of playing as the very tippy tip of the Emperor's spear when a lowly cultist will easily kill one of your Grey Knights. You do not have the feeling of being powerful at all. None. Zero. Zilch. This game needs an injection of something thrilling. You need to feel powerful, you need to feel like you are doing something. The game cut-scenes and battle maps do not convey the awesome universe of 40k. The huge scale of slaughter, the huge scale of buildings, the huge scale of war.  I would love to mow down cultist, but the game mechanics are built from basically one on one combat. Every character in the game is almost on par with your Knights. The missions need low level troops that you can slay with a few mid level units mixed in. This would increase the scope and scale of the game and add some excitement. My Knights want to spread the Emperor's light, but the game decided a half dozen cultists should be a match for my Space Marines. There are some choices in the game, but you always (and I mean ALWAYS) feel like you are playing exactly the path the developers want. It is the illusion of choice. The interface is clunky. A lot of "ok" or continue buttons are fairly small and appear in the bottom corners of the screen. The first time I loaded a battle I didn't see the button and I thought "wow this is taking a long time to load. The game needs more chances to skip cut-scenes. In general it is not good UI design, but the UI is smooth running.A cultist with a rifle, cowering behind a barrel will make you question your life and your Steam buying choices.Edit 1: The more I play, the worse it gets. I just realized that the super cultist slackers have way more armor than my Space Marines. What the...Edit 2: The game revolves around giving your Knights only short range options and all of the enemies long range weapons. This game needs mods bad. Bad. Please mod this horrible game. Shorten the enemy ranges and give the Knights more armor and longer range attacks. Before someone says, "Well the game just has a hard difficultly level...". No. It is not clever or good game design to just lower the stats on one side and raise the stats on the other side. That is laziness. The core of this game is just lazy design. Edit 3: 2 more bugs found. 1. When I restarted a battle, the game did not display the special objective, "Glorious Deed" (?)(it was "do not use willpower"). I am so tired of this game, so I said you-know-what to the game (I told it what I thought of its parents and where it could stick things) . I beat the mission using every power I had anyways. The game displayed the COMPLETED bonus objective in the mission summary screen and gave me the points. 2. My game now freezes at the end of day 164. I get a feeling that the game want to load an event, because some of the UI goes away, but some of the other buttons can still be pressed. Needless to say, I told the game you-know-what again, just to see if it helps this time. *as a note: I realized that this game is just a cash grab by the developers, so I did try to get a refund, but I ended having a slightly long play time. It was rejected by Steam. We need a "game stinks, tried to get a refund" tag.I feel the Chaos Gods sucking the life out of me the more I play it.

_childDocuments_.review: X-com in 40,000 universe.  It should have been great, but Chaos Gate has serious flaws that mar what could have been an excellent game.  Firstly, user interface and strategy; what should take one click takes three, there are to many nested menus, research and construction seem unnecessarily opaque and the requisition system is complex for no good reason that I can see.  Lastly the voice acting is, odd.  There are frequently paragraphs of text with only one line voice acted.  I found this much more irritating that I thought I would.  A quick word on the graphics, they are not bad but they feel not right for 40,000, they are cartoon a bit like someone put a world of Warcraft style filter on the game, its personally but I prefer the gritty realism style in the 40,000 universe.Secondly, the difficulty spikes are massive.  Its not just a case of the game being hard but that it goes from being easy to incredibly hard from mission to the next.  This is not challenging but poor balancing and mission design.  To go from a difficulty of (out of 10) 2, 3, 1, 9, 3, 2, 10 feels uneven, punishing and off putting.Lastly, performance.  I have a pretty beefy machine with a 3090, and the not only is the performance sluggish, especially on the enemy turns, but my rig sounds like its trying to take off and fly.  Am sure this will be patched at some point soon.To sum up this is an amazing premise with solid underlying game play marred by what feels like a very rushed release and muddled design.  Hopefully this will be a great game in 6 months time but I wish I had waited until them to buy it.  I would recommend that you hold of purchasing at least until you read feedback about the next patch.Hope you find this helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I’ve really enjoyed this game, and I can understand some of the issues people have with it, but none of them have really applied to me. Performance wise the game has run fine for me, and I have an rx 6500xt (yes, that awful thing) paired with a i5 10400. No stutters as of yet, but that may be how I’ve optimized my settings, etc.As far as difficulty goes, it’s fine. There’s no shame in playing on the minimum difficulty. A knight being lwounded isn’t the end of the world either. There’s ways to mitigate the damage you take as well as many forms of healing up your lads to minimize the time spent to recovering from wounds.I see a lot of complaints about the encounters being poorly balanced or your knights not feeling as strong as they should, And to a degree some encounters can overwhelm you, but taking out 6 enemies in one teleport strike or scatter shot or executing a whole blight hauler because it was stunned does not feel weak. I enjoy the decision making the game offers, there really are no right answers, only really less incorrect ones if you can understand what I mean.The game definitely has its issues, but seeing as how the devs seem to be working to address them, I’d recommend this game, and say that it’s worth a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: XCOM meets WH40K, the right way. I found the mix of game systems and risk/reward management inherent to keeping your roster of marines healthy to be enjoyable. The AI can be very clever and punishes bad or risky plays very hard. There is no 'aim %' system, so everything is based off of range and no/half/full cover systems, and it works well. Every class has a ton of skills you can level up and build into, there is a wide variety of gear and wargear to equip on your guys, and you will be forced to try out a variety of things due to getting wounded and having to take backliners often. Certain skills are of course overpowered compared to others, but finding out what is good and what isn't is part of the fun.A unique aspect of the game would be the manner in which each mission unfolds thanks to the warp timer causing random effects that can seriously change how you approach a situation, such as spilling a swamp of poison between you and the enemy, randomly giving mutations to enemy troops that make them much more dangerous, spawning in reinforcement squads, depleting your casting resources, or evne giving all the enemies a huge armor stack for a turn. It makes for some very wild twists in missions that I find very welcome and in character for the setting, considering it takes place in the middle of a demonic incursion into the sector.My one small gripe so far is the very punishing wound system that results in a lot of downtime for team members, from pretty routine amounts of damage. However, if I had been able to use an A-team the whole way I probably would have complained about that instead. Some people take issue with the cartoony style of graphics, but I actually like it and think it suits the setting. I've played enough 'realistic' 40k games to last a lifetime, and this take on the aesthetics is refreshing and welcome. Despite the graphics, the story narrative is spot on setting wise, and fairly engaging, especially for a WH fan.Overall I would say a lot of care was put into this game. It does the source material justice and is also decent from a gameplay perspective. Yeah it has its quirks and some aspects are not executed all that well, but I can say its a good game and mean it. Doing a blind run has me fully engaged and interested in learning how to make the best squad possible, and it feels like all the information and resources I need to do that is in the game itself.

_childDocuments_.review: I would sincerely warn against picking up this game. It's probably about as good as XCOM: Enemy Unknown was, it certainly does not hold a candle to XCOM: Enemy Within or XCOM 2, and War of the Chosen leaves it in the dust. There are times when it feels like this game is a stealth Early Access release and it was just put out to get funding to continue development. On the good side it has solid production values for this game. Nothing is cheap looking, though they skimped on VO, probably paid Andy Serkis a lot of the voice budget. There are a few issues with the maps and getting stuck on them, which would be fine if they were procedural but there are no procedurally generated maps in this game, just lots of handmade, which doesn't excuse knights getting stuck. There are apparently lots of stability issues, but I haven't run into many or any of them as far as I can recall. So it looks and sounds like Warhammer 40K but that's about all they get right, which is a big chunk, but not the biggest chunk. Though it is very lore unfriendly mechanically. This game is a mess tactically and the sweeping balance patch they pushed a week after the game released is indicative of this. The development team is not well managed or too inexperience to know how they want their game to feel when playing it. All the while I played it I couldn't nail down what kind of experience they were going for. The game puts you up against a lot of weak enemies overall but enjoys buffing them with impunity, but a grey knight can't kill an unbuffed guardsmen with a power sword. There are times in the early game where rapidity is rewarded, being able to roll through the place shooting up guardsmen and engaging in glorious melee with chaos marines, but then the AI is badly designed so after a few missions the boring doldrums of combat start to sink in. The AI is way too defensive, but the devs didn't balance it right so if they actually made them aggressive they could just throw bullets at your guys and kill you every time. So your best bet is actually to retreat and pull there stupidity into your overwatches, because they can only turtle when they see you. Your knights themselves are fairly bland, both in your ability to enjoy some emergent storytelling with them and form attachments a la XCOM or even customize them. Mechanically they're also boring. Instead of letting wargear and equipment define a character's abilities they put it all in the character sheet which is nine rough sections with very few interesting or fun abilities. Most of the sheet is just increases for more standard fair. All of this culminates in a boring as dirt experience. You're sending four bland knights against mostly twenty four of the same units over and over. You'll most likely win in the end but you're not moving fast enough or doing enough damage to the enemy to make combat flow so it just because entirely based on meta safety plays and minimizing damage because the super soldiers of the imperium can be put in the hospital for near a month by being smacked by the butt of a chaos guardsman's gun. The game even tricks you at some point into thinking you'll get more enemy variety type but it's just different stats for the same mobs over and over. They've made 40K boring. There's not a lot of mission variety. You can be stuck for five minutes at a time (fast forwarding enemy turns no less) watching the enemy move all their pieces the same way. The strategy layer is boring as well. There's little interesting or game changing to research or engineer. There's a lot of vital stuff sure, but nothing that makes it worth it as your better gear is held behind randomness and an entirely different system. The board is unfair at the best of times and most of the random strategic events are straight up punitive with little reward to be had. It is a boring, mind numbing exerperience, and nothing seems to be able to say it. My recommendation is to wait for a DEEP sale on it if you have to have it, otherwise I'd hope this game gets an almost from the ground up rework, hopefully with some actually good revisions, I'm talking No Man's Sky, start totally over or give a lot of free updates to add in at least some other enemy types, maps, or a reworked gear and abilities system because while this thing has a good framework that's it. And that framework is only good for about ten hours of novel gamepaly but the experience is burned through faster than the planetary defense garrisons on any give world in the imperium. I expected better.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of 40k, but they've been very hit and miss regarding licensing their properties to developers making average or subpar games. I am happy to say that this is not one of those games! It plays very similar to X-com, but uses the Grey Knights perfectly! The story and combat feel fantastic and authentic to the 40k universe. The knights stomp through terrain (especially when in terminator armor!) and there's a high emphasis on melee combat! I'm really enjoying it so far and would highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys 40k, turn based tactical strategy games or ideally both! (like me!)

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time enthusiast of turn-based tactical games, this was a huge win for me! You can tell it is made by a team that loves Warhammer 40K lore. There is tremendous variety for skill and gear builds, as well as team compositions. The developers struck an excellent balance of making your Grey Knights feel incredibly powerful, yet sufficiently challenged by the mass of foes that you will face.The biggest issues I experienced with this game is that the map variety becomes stale and familiar by the time you reach mid-game, but all other aspects of the game were more than fun enough to make up for this!

_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I was sceptical as a lot of Warhammer games fail to live up to their potential but Chaos Gate is awesome. If you liked Xcom's style of researching and upgrading your ship to provide benefits for battle you will be at home with this. It took a couple of hours to get used the systems of the game with what the resources do as well as in the battles managing the bloom with your warp abilities and how to execute criticals to replenish AP but now I feel like this game is great. I am playing on easy with ironman on and still it can be a bit of a challenge as enemies can spawn in and overwhelm you fast, but as I have learned the game I feel the challenge is fair and rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, I just wish it had more than 4 controllable soldiers at the same time. _childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the game so far. It's super hard and can be overwhelming at times. Below is a list of things I've enjoyed and I think need improvement. SPOILERS as I discuss game mechanics and systems and I don't want to spoil anything for anyone. Things I really enjoy:- Basically follows the same format as XCOM in regards to missions, you have the story ones that are spaced out and then you have the randomly generated battles in between. -Research options are really neat and really helps you turn the tide against some of the game mechanics-Lots of classes that have their own purpose/role-Wargear with different modifiers and effects -Combat is fun to watch, seeing my knights slash cultists in half never gets old-You really need to think about each decision you make, you only have a squad of 4 knights on each mission, sometimes the odds seem impossible but it is doable! Weigh all your options! -The Central hub that is your ship reminds me of Starcraft 2! You can talk to the characters and do all of your upgrades and research! I really love this aspect of the game-The characters are all unique, I enjoy the story they've made, and the voice acting is well done-UI us very easy to follow and look at-Warp Surge keeps each map spicy by adding random negative events for the player-Lots of enemy variety and mutationsThings for improvement:-I really enjoy the difficultly of this game, but sometimes it's insane and it's an endless snowball, I think some balancing can be done to better enhance the experience. Reinforcements are sometimes too much-Needs some kind of system that lets you see how big the map is going to be. Some of the maps are massive and I feel it would help the player prepare properly before entering a mission if they knew the map size-Wounds take a long time to heal -Flamethrower I feel needs to be better, it's so short range and it has very limited use in a mission unless you are TOTALLY swarmed-Performance could totally use some work, that seems to be common with most games these days though.-Some classes are much better/useful then others. Can't imagine running a squad without an interceptor as an example.Overall I think this is a fantastic game for Warhammer fans, it's not perfect, It's brutal, but I hope the publishers and the devs keep pushing the game forward with updates and adding some new enemy factions hopefully! I do believe people are being a little hyperbolic about their gripes with the game. It does have issues but they can be ironed out with time. The devs are receptive to player feedback and I hope they continue to work with the community to make this game better!
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this but be warned, it is not easy. I remember back when these games first came out, it was a relaxing fun game to play. This, to me, is not that. It is hard, you have got to micro manage your team, your ship, your everything and all in all it is just an annoying second job.Sadly it makes the Grey Knights, arguably one of the strongest Space Marine Chapters, feel very weak. Again, it is not a bad game at all, it's made well the story is good, it's just not a game I can enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: A few things.First of all, this game is great fun. XCOM crossed with 40k is a match made in heaven. I basically bought this game because I wanted to experience the power fantasy of commanding humanity's finest weapons: the Grey Knights, and this game delivers very well on that. The overarching narrative of the game is great. Very simple, but very effective. All NPCs are extremely well voiced and are actually interesting; with my personal favourite being our resident Tech Priest.The art style is really nice, the environments are exceptional, and the animations and art assets (especially our Grey Knight terminator armours) are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ perfect. The only issue I have experienced thus far, is that this game is EXCEPTIONALLY punishing. I started my first play through playing on normal difficulty, and man - the game ♥♥♥♥♥ you up real good and fast. As I said, I bought this game because I wanted to play as the most overpowered chapter of the Astartes and experience the power fantasy of them wrecking ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ left and right... I have no shame in saying that I dropped the difficulty down to easy to achieve those ends. Even then, if you forsake tactics in the name of a more run & gun approach on this difficulty, you will find yourself outflanked, outmaneuvered, and outgunned a vast majority of the time - which is great. For what I wanted out of this game, easy difficulty is perfect (it'd probably be more considered 'normal difficulty' in other titles. Game is very punishing.)The game has various spikes in difficulty too. For the first 3-4 hours, it's pretty smooth sailing. Then, you start to experience a vast array of various hard hitting units that give you a pretty rude awakening that you better stop ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around and start approaching your missions with actual tactics.Great fun, I enjoy this game a lot. Hopefully you will too.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: the game is just too repetitive and slow paced without having the tactical depth of Xcom, mechanicus or other turn based games.I want to like the game but I can't. And despite how incredibly aggressively people defend the game it has blatant flaws when compared to others in its gameplay genre and price bracket.The game takes aspects of Xcom and Mechanicus, but doesn't reach the peaks of either. The result is a mediocre turn based game with a Warhammer skin. The devs are clearly passionate about the universe and its great to see nurgle corruption and the greyknights in physical form.Positives--40K one of the best in depth sci-fi settings there is and its great to see more stories being made in this universe and this game is a masterpiece if you compare it to the disgrace that was Dawn of War 3.- decent customisation/wargear options; you get to use maybe around 50% of the Grey Knights lore arsenal albeit everything is incredibly nerfed.Cons-- game is incredibly clunky from top to bottom, the levels are contantly filled with unskippable audio and camera lock sections and each mission starts with arbitrary commentary from either your fellow grey knight, onboard inquisitor or Mechanicus representative. This would be a great bit of extra flavour if it didn't directly slow down gameplay.- combat system: while the basic stepping stones of turn based combat is there, the game lacks the finesse of Mechanicus or Xcom. Particularly in the way you have no means of gauging enemy detection range and you can't squad move your guys so you will often get enemies randomly spotting you through walls then having full movement and overwatch setups without you being able to do anything in return- this 'cinematic combat start' phase will also have the enemies ignore any overwatches of your own so there is no opportunity to set up ambushes outside of just pointing guns at one of the inevitable portals that shows up.-wound system; while a more hard-core injury mechanic is by no means new or unwanted in space warfare in this game it's a lot less hardcore or tactical and comes across more as just another ticking debuff that you have to deal with while you let time pass in space. Your super armoured terminator put their pinky toe in a campfire? -3 to maximum health for the next 30 days.- pacing: The game is slow, your turns are slow, the cinematics are slow, your ship is slow even as you begin to upgrade it, healing is slow, using the menus in your ship requires constant dramatic camera effects that further slow just issuing the next construction project, you can't fast forward anything except 'enemy turns' which barley ups the speed at all. Even outside of combat you cannot issue more orders until the previous unit has fully finished (unlike similar games that let you Tab to the next troop while the former continues their move order.)you can't skip in-misison dialogue, you can't skip animations in space, you can't skip cinematics of a portal appearing, you can't enemy intros, you can't skip combat intros, you can't skip your dude kicking a door, you can't skip your camera zooming to stare at nothing for a while because one of your knights sensed distant enemies, you can't skip the arbitrary event of the bloom bar going up.These are all very small things but when it all stacks together I can honestly say more of the gametime involves just sitting around waiting for animations/dialogues to progress than actually playing the game.The balancing of Lore and game balancing: Outside of a third person horde shooter; there is essentially no way you could ever make a game featuring Greyknights that is remotely close to lore accurate, this is just the reality of having to nerf people in order to make gameplay that works. However in this games case many expected gameplay to perhaps exclusively involved fighting demons who are the primary foe and actually dangerous adversary of the grey knights; while there are certainly many demons and greater demons in the game there is also plenty of trash fodder that just add to the length of combat without bringing anything interesting to the table. A constant bombardment of random cultists who know what grey knights are (?) and are able to serious wound terminators with autoguns creates a weird feeling. All the while you are dealing with random debuffs hitting you constantly and being seriously hampered by chaos taint even though you are the force specifically known for their ability to ignore and surpass such corruption.In many ways this game should have been an Inquisition game; you play as inquisitors hunting corruption dealing with the politics and management of your campaing as you go, your soldiers would have much more customisation options and it would make much more sense in both gameplay and lore aspects that your troops have incredibly limited movement and combat abilities. It would make more sense that you're constantly having to babysit the normal dudes getting injured by nurglites and the rarity of specialised nemesis weapons would reduce the feeling of seeing an elite space marine faction be nerfed into the floor.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game at first view, and was definitely interested in it. However, after a few hours reality reared its ugly head. The slow but ugly truth was that no matter what you did, you started falling behind. Spread missions, the wounding system which I thought was absolute BS and some creatures were not balanced compared to others. Can become a good game with some slight tempering, but as it stands, the game could use a second look. I loved the graphics and the core of the game itself  so for people who could look past my comments, this is quite possibly a fun and maybe even a good game. A give the recommend, because the game was not ♥♥♥♥ enough IMO to warrant a do not recommend, since the foundation was properly build and executed.

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna try and be short:It's not a tactical game, it's more like a card game or a puzzle game; you are given option to create combos to get more OP and cheese the game, and you either do that or you die horribly by trying to play tactically.Taking cover, advancing slow and steady, flanking and anything else that should sound smart to do is the worst possible option in this game. Instead you have to focus on the skills that give you more AP, more chance to score critical hits, which allow you to stun and enemy and then execute him, when you execute an enemy you get free AP so you have more chances to kill enemies before they wound you.Yes, your Grey Knights will suffer grievous wounds from basic autoguns and stubbers, and you can't really play safe because most missions after the first 2 or 3 become rush-based, where you want to achieve your objective before you get swarmed in debuffs(the Bloom mechanic) and reinforcing enemy troops.TL&DR: Do not buy this expecting it to play like Xcom 1, Jagged Alliance or an actual tactical game, you have to research the skill tree and the stratagems to get the stuff that makes you cheese the game, like a deck building game.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I'd almost recommend it, but not quite. I really like the setting, but this isn't really a lore rich game. Compared to Mechanicus, which is similar, there just isn't as much going on here story wise. The combat is a decent x-com like but it doesn't do much new. After a while it starts to feel really similar form mission to mission. I also found the difficulty a little all over the place. It can be hard to figure out what will work without a lot of trial and error and when things go wrong they tend to keep going wrong. I feel like if it was just a bit better I'd have really liked it but as it stands I just can't quite recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not bad per se, OK graphics, sound, OK voice acting. It is pretty brutal difficulty wise, which is not a bad thing, I like the challenge, but it get repetitive very quickly. Boss fights feel unfair considering it takes two hits with the power sword to kill an unarmored cultist, each single demon and chaos space marine takes a team effort. This is my biggest gripe  with this game, it punishes you hard for making a wrong decision but it does not really reward you for good tactical play, the best you can hope for is no critical wounds. Story is interesting but not very compelling. Overall Grey knights don't feel like demon slayer powerhouses they supposed to be, which is sad. On a bright side, upgrade tree is very nice and offers a lot of tactical options. The variation of classes and weapons , including weapons visual aspect is great, but in the end it all comes down to doing same thing over and over, struggling to survive on every map. I think it would benefit from rebalancing, enemies, making them hit harder but also go down easier, this would push players to utilize more skills and environment and plan ahead better with less frustration. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely unbalanced, couple of missions go easy, then i got three impossible to win any of them. Had to lower the difficulty (game does not allow change difficulty during same campaign), but even on easiest it is terrible - ten or more missions in a row with not even get knight injured, then totally overwhelmed with knights on 8th and 9th level with tier 3 equipment under my control. Good idea combined with low balancing skills of developers. Sad. Someone said that the developers changed difficulty in some of previous update, for some reason make it harder. Then, great job guys, you ruined your own game! And yeah, I am little pissed right now (actually a lot). :)
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: Love 40k but hate, you know, dice?  Probability?  Chance?  Then THIS is the game for you!  Love Space Marines but hate, you know, THEIR ARMOR?  TOUGHNESS?  LETHALITY?  Then THIS is REALLY the game for you!  What's better than fighting enemies that NEVER MISS YOU, LITERALLY, than fighting them with space marines (Grey Knights at that....) in power armor that does ALMOST NOTHING to mitigate AUTOGUNS, whilst getting exponentially outnumbered both tactically and strategically?  (Oh there is PLENTY that is WAY better than that, but I won't spoil it...)Now you too can experience the absolute THRILL of COMPLETELY FORMULAIC combat, where there is no point in ever taking a calculated risk, ever, because you know exactly what the outcomes are going to be, without question. I'm an addict so I'm going to reinstall this but if you are also, listen- stick with your staples.  This one gets in your veins fast like XCOM...but it hurts WAY more and has a way shorter half life.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: What if X-COM 2 was a good game without needing mods for that?That's pretty much the question answered by Chaos Gate in those early hours for me, so far.They have better implementations of pretty much exactly all mechanics of X-COM and X-COM 2 that bother me.Like the turn limits that result in an instant gameover - here they cause mutations that increase the difficulty instead, makes a lot more sense.Or the awful, awful pod mechanics of XCOM - here the enemies are not the only ones that get a free turn when a pod is activated.Or the boring RNG-fest of accuracy. There's no accuracy mechanics here. You still have some rng in the form of Crit Chance and similar, but there's no missing the target; neither for you nor for the enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: Chaos Gate makes Grey Knights cool again!!!This game is redefining hoe a turn based game should work. The mechanics are so much better and fine tuned than any other turn based game I've played.And the story and build up is great. Great voice acting and a interesting plot. If you are into the Warhammer 40k lore you will enjoy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone who isn't a massive fan of 40k.It suffers from the same problem that most games based on 40k have, a sub par studio gets the license and depends upon the draw of the property to make up for what is otherwise a mediocre or even bad gaming experience.I've run into some bugs, none game breaking. Did have to restart once, but luckily auto-save had my back.The game designers don't know what they are doing when it comes to balance, so you get a only get 4 dudes to face endless waves of baddies in every mission.And that's the entire game folks. You learn quickly to prioritize certain targets because failure to do so is an automatic loss. Every type of pox walker is capable of reviving all dead enemies as new pox walkers, so if you didn't kill them all, you didn't kill any of them. Get the bloom tree quick, or it will churn out plague marines. Oh, and just spotting it brings in a wave of chuds.For a game that is meant to be sort of sandbox-ish, this is a problem. Missions are a slog, and take way too long. It's as bad as Mordheim was, with the only up side maybe being, you can save scum if you really like to do that?This isn't a good game. Takes like 7 or 9 clicks to change one piece of wargear. To much clicking during missions too, not enough hot keys. It's a poor copy of x-com. Unless space marines get you hot and bothered, don't buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: This game has alot going for it and great potential, however I've run into a couple of problems.Just to clarify I've been playing RTS and turn based strategy games most of my life, so I hope my opinion will help.Pros: - Great cinemtaic combat animations, you can see care has been taken with them. Great voice acting for the most part- A linear story that still allows you to feel you're steering it's direction through in game choices.- The fun logistical challenge of managing your time and resources between your ship and Grey knights, it gives a true sense of desperation and urgency, couple this with event decisions and it adds weight to every choice you make.- A new  style of gameplay that awards aggressiveness not seen often in the turn based genre, forces you to really think about your next move.Cons:- UI seems a bit much for me, there are options to turn some components off but there is just far too much going on.- Enemies never seem to stop coming on most missions, and do too much damage. Little cultists can leave a big dent in you with machine guns even with Terminator armour. I was only playing on normal and I'm used to playing Turn based games on the hardest difficulties. Safe to say I wasn't feeling like a Space Marine.- Wound times are far too long, especially for how easy they are to acquire. 40+ days to recover my grey knights, after I had to make an in game decision it increased their recovery time by a further 50%- Buggy in some places, there are freezes and FPS drops. Doesn't seem well optimised atm but I'm aware this is an issue that will likely be fixed. I've had no crashes yet.Summary:In conclusion Chaos Gate has alot going for it, it's tried to break the mould and be different from other turn based strategy games and it's working. Enemies defintely need their damage or numerity tweaking, it needs some quality of life improvements and optimisation. But at the foundation is a really good game that you can tell has been made with care by people who love Warhammer.I hope this helps 🙂
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, having finished it once and now going for the rest I can safely say that this is one of the good W40K games.If you like W40K and X-COM then it's an absolute no brainer to get this.I'm not sure about full price. as well as the DLCs, but on a sale the basic game is a blast for fans of the above.Gameplay is pretty good for a turn based game (and you won't have the 99% miss chance).Visually it's its own cup of tea. Nothing amazing that will make your jaw drop in awe, but the direction they took on the design is still pretty satisfying.What shines the most though for me is the story. It is absolutely awesome for someone who likes W40K. Starts of slow and picks up the pace with some twists and the usual futility that humanity faces in this franchise. For a sale it's a must buy, for full price I'd still recommend it.The only reason I'm giving it an 8/10 is because of some fps drops I experienced (rare ones) and some crashes.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: I'd only recommend this to hardcore 40K fans.If you already own XCOM 2 this game will only piss you off as many bugs in this game have already been fixed and done better with the prior mentioned title. There is no mod support. I'm not sure what these devs were thinking but if they dropped a mod kit and opened the game up they'd more than likely increase sales by 30-40%. A ton of issues this game  has is already solved in XCOM 2 a decade old game. If there were mod support here the game would have triple the attention due to 40k fans. Unfortunately it doesn't.Again, there is no mod support.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that throws a lot of Nurgle's Daemons at you, and gives you a lot to fight them with. Build your forces the way you want. No compromises in the form of, you can have this, but then you can't have that BS. You can play with all the toys in the box. Just know that all the balls in this box are big.Positives: Combat is fun with difficulty settings that scale from easy to a good challenge on legendary. AI is pretty good. Lots of interesting build/strategy options.Negatives(mostly minor): UI is a mess. Lack of mission variety can get repetitive. Non-combat map navigation is tedious. Camera options are claustrophobic. Selecting units obscured by terrain/other units not as intuitive as it should be. The extra cumbersome "win a mission without Master Crafted equipment," only serves to destroy the games momentum. Game occasionally hangs up. Opportunist Achievement bugged.Neutral: Individual missions can be very long. Note to self: Use stratagems6.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended. Take the X-Com formula and put it on steroids. The talent trees are more diverse, then add it unique weapons, items, armor sets, etc. If you ever thought X-Com was punishing, this game pretty much says "hold my beer." Every fight, every action is vital to winning the campaign. I'm about half way through and every minute that goes by I am just trying to make it another event, another minute of not dying, lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: You do not feel like a psychic super soldier, you feel like a tin can using wrapping paper for armor. Almost every single enemy will have double or triple the amount of armor, they can all out-range your knights, they're virtually immune to any status effect you might want to put on them - there are just so many things that detract from the fun of this game that it's infuriating. Want to use your knight's powerful psychic abilities? F**k you, it increases the bloom and pumps negative effects for your team every two to three turns. Want to use your Inquisitor's even more powerful psychic abilities? F**k you, she's wounded for 63 days so you can't - even on a mission where she is fighting side by side with your knights. Want some requisition to recruit a knight, get a better gun or upgrade your grenades? F**k you, the Grand Master just took some away because you're ugly and he hates you. Want to take your time and build up the strength of your knights, your ship and your research? F**k you, hurry the f**k up and go do those timed missions before you LITERALLY FAIL THE ENTIRE CAMPAIGN. The early levels are abundantly easy, but the more bullsh*t the game throws at you, the more ridiculously tough enemies, terrible status effects and random game encounters, the more obnoxious it all feels. Missions become long, grueling slog-fests, where the longer you take the more you're f**ked. I've spent over an hour on a level, just to have the Inquisitor die to a random blight drone shot from halfway across the map and the mission fails. The graphics are good, the levels look detailed and varied, the customization is killer, but the game play itself just becomes tedious and frustrating. I've put a fair amount of hours into this game, and it's weirdly one of the few games where the longer I've played, the less I've liked it. It's good for a Warhammer game I suppose, considering that's a pretty low bar anyway, and it delivered on some things like customization and graphics, but the game play is just not there. It's more like an infuriating chore than a game where you're supposed to feel like you're commanding demi-gods.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. If you're a fan of XCOM style games you will love this - if you're also a fan of Warhammer 40k then you'll love this even more. This game takes a lot of the tedious parts of XCOM and improves on them. When you end a combat encounter your grey knights reload on their own. Except on certain battles when you encounter an enemy the turn restarts and all your units get their full AP back to make their moves. The stun system is interesting and let's you approach situations much differently than XCOM's creep and overwatch. This game is definitely worth the pick up at full price. I do not recommend the Castellan Edition though.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: It's great, similar to XCOM 2, but very different at the same time. You are the boss, but numbers are quick to overwhelm you, the game mechanics are nice. With DLC's/Mods it will get better for sure. Nice amount of randomisation. Could maybe use some more maps? Not too sure how many times I have seen the same ones/how many I have yet to see.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game. And I would definitively have given a thumb up, if that was an actual sequel to the cult game Warhammer 40K: Chaosgate from 1998 developped by Random Games Inc.So, the biggest fault comes with the name. No big deal would most say. So why do I freak out?Simply put, there are two kinds of Warhammer Games:1) The ones who follow somewhat the Warhammer rules (Shadow of the Horned Rat, Dark Omen, Space Hulk, Chaosgate 1998, and so on) and offer the real immersion. They are the best imo.2) Those who are under a Warhammer License but mimick some other game or license dynamics. You've got good and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ things there. And Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters belongs to the good games from the second category. It is actually a very good XCOM-like game and I enjoy it for that. But else, compared to the dynamics of the original Chaos Gate:- it lacks a proper squad number of units (5, not knowing the Grey Knights, I don't know if they actually are based on a 4-units squad system). It might seems weird to some, but overall I don't like that much games where you control only 3 or 4 characters. I had always a preference for 5+ playable-at-a-time characters games. It just feel more real.- you control only 1 squad. in 1998 CG you controlled more and more squads as the game advanced in plot, with vehicles (unfortunetaly a bit buggy or not adapted to the maps, but there was potential there for a sequel).- the ambiance of Daemonhunters, true to the XCOMs, is too much comics/funny-wise for my taste. 1998 CG was a lot darker and I prefered that.- Musicwise, Daemonhunters does not hit a spot by me. 1998 CG did. And it was a looong time ago. And still it does if I am to believe the comments of some retro-gamers).So, dear developpers, why did you actually manage to no deliver a sequel - probably condamning at the same time any future hope in that regard -  and still used an existing name? Lack of inspiration?You did a good game, don't get me wrong, but you killed my hope for a much promising sequel to the 1998 version of Chaosgate. Yes you did. And for that only reason I give you a thumb down.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR at the bottom.Initially I was afraid that this game would be yet another half-baked, poorly designed or just straight up bad that would fall in among so many other Warhammer 40K titles. And am I glad that those fears were unfounded.So for the most part I would say that this is an enjoyable game, it has some lesser issues that I would mostly write up as potential quality of life patches down the line.Now for the parts that most people would like to know before buying a new game.If you do not enjoy games that are primarily very heavy on turn based tactical squad management, like XCOM and Phoenix Point, then this is not for you. However, if you do enjoy this type of gameplay but dislike XCOMs RNG heavy system then you are in luck. This game works fairly straightforward as the game has done a good job using both some RNG but also relying for the most part on raw numbers.For the most part the game works with very specific numbers. For example, base weapons tend to do 4 points of damage and half cover reduces the damage partially whilst full cover negates damage entirely. Now the interesting part here that I found is that the only "misses" you get are from shooting at something that either is protected or hiding behind something that will negate all your damage. If you get shot from the side of a full cover but it is not a straight 90 degree angle you will get partial full cover. This will usuallly reduce the damage by half.Most of the effects are fairly simple and straightforward too, Damage over time effects are 2 HP/turn and the parts that are RNG are usually related to one specific stat. You will over the course of the game aquire gear that lets you increase a specific stat quite significantly. For example there items that starts with a small stat boost of 15% and this number is the actual chance it will happen. Later on these items at their third tier will give you 50% boost. You can read about most effects and mechanics from the settings menu which can be handy since the game does not always straight up tell you what something will do if you forget.For the most part I felt like I was in control of what RNG I wanted to potentially to happen since the game uses the different classes to let players specialize their strike force. The only real RNG that you do not have control over are what potential gear you will get from missions. You will be able to control the odds of what quality each type of gear you can get but you can't control what specific item of that category will show up. Which can be a little frustrating if you are looking for one specific equipment upgrade but you don't get it.Overall I do enjoy that much of what happends on the screen is based very much on how the player decides to move forward. The game does a good job of instilling a sense of urgency as the game moves forward and even at the best of times you will not be able to get all missions that pop up, At most you can reach 2 out of 3 missions. But careful selection and patient planning will earn you a victory.As for the difficulty I do feel that on my first run I went for the 2nd hardest, Ruthless, and it was hard but not insanely so. I eventually had to accept defeat and abandon that run due to my own poor planning. My 2nd run was on normal difficulty and I found it to be too easy. I also played with the Grand Master mode enabled so I guess it made things a little bit harder. It essentially lets you only have one autosave and no manual saving. So every decision does need to be made carefully. On harder difficulties you will find out that the main reason you are about to lose is not because one or two enemies are absolutely OP, it is usually because you spread out too much and attracted the attention of more than one enemy group.In the end I do feel like the developers made a good job of instilling the sense of frustration of having to work with what little resources you have. It also offers the player a very good way of making the most of out each combat engagement by rewarding careful planning.Storywise I have to say I really enjoyed it. I kept thinking about the story as I progressed and I do love the curveball they put you up for. I will not discuss any details but all I can say is that I feel the characters you engage and interact are well made. They play their roles and keeps your immersion intact. With some slight bumps that are related to certain condition specific events. They may break the immersion but I personally found them to be more funny when they did and they are not game breaking.TLDR: XCOM like game with WH40K theme. Fight as your way through the stink lord's legions as you try to contain a pandemic on a massive interstellar level. Good gameplay with well balanced RNG and hard set numbers systems.

_childDocuments_.review: A really great W40k game that is almost ruined by a terrible doomsday mechanic and an awful last level. I highly recommend W40K: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters for a joyous, crunchy expedition through the Grimdark universe featuring the ever-badass Grey Knights. This is a wonderful, turn-based strategy game that slows down the hectic pace of many other similar games and makes you focus on approach, skills, and having a good plan. The story is excellent, audio and voice acting are very, very good and enjoyable, and the graphics convey the dark, nasty world of W40k. You choose from a myriad of classes to work with in combat, and spend your time stomping through legions of Nurgle. I really appreciated that the game can be paused at any time, even during cutscenes. The game is divided into two parts, which is combat with the Grey Knights, trying to hold back "the Bloom" and ship management, where you can upgrade your facilities, weaponry, shields, etc. Both play an integral part as you zip around the galaxy trying to extinguish the heretics. You bring a squad of four Grey Knights into combat, and having a diverse group of gear and abilities will serve you well. Each Knight is rank 1-9 (leveling system), with the higher ranks having more access to abilities. There are also some neat augmentation mechanics that occur if your Knights fall in battle. Don't let them die too often though!There is also a Stratagem system which serves as accessory powers and abilities that you can "bring" into battle with you. New Stratagems are unlocked as you progress through the campaign and offer things like healing, resistance for the squad, teleportation (bring this one!), etc. You start with one but can have up to four. There is a Research mechanic as part of the ship management, where you can unlock new Stratagems as well as bonuses from your Prognosticar, which is essentially a psychic boost to a number of planets on the map. Highly recommend that you research this more. Many great things can be said about this game, but I do want to share the glaring issues: 1) You can get totally screwed with dialog choices - while I appreciate that it is an adventure and not every outcome can be known (or should be shared) but you can get absolutely hosed with losing resources, units, or even taking damage to your ship by choosing the wrong option. 2) The Doomsday mechanic is asinine and is a huge annoyance.  As you are combating the bloom, certain planets will explode to a Level 5 threat, which means they have a chance of triggering Doomsday. This can only be avoided by traveling to that planet and doing a very, VERY tedious combat mission to hold off "the Morbus." This mechanic isn't really explained and it is impossible to avoid. I wouldn't mind if you only had to do that mission 5 times, but it keeps coming up again, and again... and again. I eventually would just reload my save until I got a version that didn't include a "Morbus" mission because I grew so tired of them. 3) The final mission is absolutely awful, is extremely tedious, and goes against the general mechanics of the game meaning on a scale of 1-10 for fun, it is a 0. You create two squads of four and have to hold off *spoiler* and *spoiler* but you are given no insight into what you will be doing within the mission, what types of gear to bring, you are not given access to the hard-earned Stratagems, and the enemies essentially race past you to the teleporter rather than engaging in combat. This was almost game-ruining for me. 4) When you recruit a Knight, they came with a few skills pre-selected. I found that many of my Knights came with skills that didn't make any bloody sense. Take a bit to research the strengths of your classes and pick and choose carefully, even if you have to respec. The respec mechanic sucks, so be warned.To avoid those three things, I recommend keeping a few save files going within your campaign. One in space where your "state of the game" can be safely kept, and then a few in-combat saves. That way if something goes sideways, you can at least get back to where you wanted. I appreciate that some players are more hardcore and find that cheating, but I wanted to have fun playing this game, and in general, I had an absolute blast. The final mission is total crap but the journey, progression of your Knights, and ripping through hoards of Nurgle never gets old! I found these links to be a great resource! Happy hunting!Event guide - Class guide -

_childDocuments_.review: PROs:Compelling gameplay with a strong 40k theme. You always feel like you're making interesting choices with your squad, including how to outfit them for each mission, optimizing their passive trait and resting them after taking injuries. The optional challenge mode for each mission, which offers more rewards in exchange for suffering a penalty such as not being able to crit or only being able to field 3 knights, feels rewarding and keeps things feeling fresh. The ship truly feels like it's limping around held together by string while you push for the most optimal upgrades. Research is well-paced and requires some resource-gathering during missions. Dialogue is often very meaningful and leads to lasting bonuses or penalties.Customization is strong, with armors and weapons having their own models, multiple voices to choose from, and more. Devs listened to community about locked Twitch rewards, which is a good sign. Attention to lore is much, much better than most 40k games.CONs:The UI could use some work; pop-ups showing more stats and details about equipped items would be appreciated. Sometimes overwatch cones and explosions can happen on odd planes when there are objects intervening, causing you to miss.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely one of the best 40k ever made. The gameplay is fun, challenging and rewarding. The combat itself reminds of X-Com in many ways while still standing on its own.Characters have access to various abilities and weapon options, yet there's no one specific build for any class that would stand out above others, all abilities have their uses as do weapons so you can't really make wrong choices on what you choose to go with. There's also plenty of decisions and challenges thrown at you between battles on the campaign map, you can't save every planet, you have to pick and choose what'll work the best for you and deal with the surprise obstacles thrown at you once in a while.I've played about 35 hours now and I'm starting to get close to the end but there's still missions to do. And I'm playing on normal so that should give some indication of how much gameplay there is.If this is the "X-Com" of 40k by Complex Games, then I can't wait to see their "X-Com2". The core gameplay is solid and fun and I think there's a lot of potential for expansions and sequels.And while I understand why the Grey Knights are the stars of the show in this game, I'd love to another chapter represented in a sequel, just to add into the gameplay choices and politics between the battles. Having to deal with all kinds of Imperial factions, planetary governors, other chapters and so on would really add an interesting layer to the campaign itself.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm a huge fan of XCom (I have over 500 hours played across XCom and XCom 2) and also a MASSIVE Warhammer fan (former table-top player, with somewhere north of 3000 combined hours spent on Total War Warhammer series, Battlefleet Gothic, Dawn of War series). So for me I admit this is VERY much in my fan-boy sweet spot. I can recognise that the game has it's faults - the difficulty curve is quite hard and the interface isn't the cleanest (working out how much ammo, or a Knight's avg Crit Chance and Damage when out of combat is quite painful).But so far I'm REALLY enjoying it. Thematically it works great, the voice acting, VFX and sound are all top notch. Gameplay wise I'm finding the synergy between team member skills works VERY well, and I often find myself playing each unit to their very specific set of strengths, and using their abilities in tandem - is if very rewarding when you do this to chain together a number of complementary abilities to wipe out an enemy pod in a single turn! I think the only worry is that it could end up being a little repetitive in late game as the mission variety is a little narrow - I'm personally hopeful that future DLC is going to add additional races, campaign features, and potentially RPG elements in future to keep it going for those multiple playthroughs.

_childDocuments_.review: Start up xcoom on hardest difficulty for the first time, even on the first mission you gotta pay attention to make it through with all your dudes alive. You're actually *playing the game* the second you start it up.So far, Chaos Gate, I'm over an hour in and I haven't started playing the game yet. You're forced through a tedious tutorial where you don't learn anything because you're not thinking about anything you're doing, it just "click here" over and over, may as well have watched a video. Then I play the first "real" mission, literally just click on the enemies with zero thought, make it through with zero damage done to any of my guys - with ZERO tactics or planning or thinking involved at all, just clicking on max distance movements into zero cover until I see enemies then clicking the enemies without thinking. Second mission, same thing. There's no *game* here so far. "oh, b-b-but the game starts, uh, several hours in - past the refund window!" yeah, dude, whatever. If I'm not having fun and wanting to see more almost 2 hours in, the game's never gonna be. Oh and I had to restart the game top be able to start upgrading my ship because of a UI bug, because nobody's able to launch any games these days without so many bugs that you start stumbling over them right away.As for the campaign experience, presumably an important part in this single-player game, it's written like a saturaday morning cartoon. I dunno if that's appropriate for the Gey Knights, and I realize WH40K is an inherently cartoony setting, but this is too close to "intended for children ages 2 to 6" for my taste.So. Gameplay is awful. Writing is meh. Aesthetic is pretty damn awful as well. Again, it feels like a saturday morning cartoon, not like the over-the-top ever-so-grimdark setting that is WH40K. If you found yourself fighting Diablo 3-style unicorns and carebears that would feel entirely appropriate for the aesthetic of this game. Wildly inappropriate for the aesthetic of WH40K. _childDocuments_.review: First off:If you like XCom (or Gears Tactics, Phoenix Point, Battle Tech, etc) then you might check it out, at least the first 2 hours will help. You will find enough similarities and some things a bit twisted. I like it, the start is a bit much handholding but as soon as you can decide for yourself, it really is fun.The Gameplay:As a Vet-XCom player i thought i knew how to get to work. I set up my fine overwatch line and keeped my distance ... and i had a really hard time. Those mighty Knights feeled more like pushovers. The Damage was meh, the Overwatch-Range freakish short and everthing that is fun pushes the warp timer ahead (that means if that "doom clock" is on 100% you get some nasty suprises - never a good one). Soooo, if you take to long or play with your abilitys ... oops, here they come and eat you alive. My Sickbay was full, getting a clean & healthy Knight to work was hard.Then i changed my tactics. Being aggressive, jumping to the front, hacking and slashing and learning the auto-funtions of some of your dudes (Support-Fire in example). Suddenly the pushovers DO have some weight. Now i don't care that much about the warp-timer, because the enemy is toast till then and sometimes i welcome it, because more Dudes to kill, more XP to get.The Story:I don't care about stories in games. Gameplay always trumps Story. There are exceptions (Plague Tale, Last of Us (1&2), etc). So i'm suprised that i'm still interessted in it here. It won't win a Oscar anytime soon, but for WH40K Game, i like it. The Voices are solid (even if they later only speak one sentence but have four sentence on screen). The SFX / Music / GFX:I like it - mostly. The GFX is a bit comical, but still grim, the animations are fine. The explosions and physics effecs are really nice to look at. The Music is very good, very dramatic, gothic - pushing the atmosphere higher. The SFX ... well, shooting, slicing and even the Knights yadda yadda is ok. But some of the enemys, oh boy. Cringe as Cringe can. I hope there will be mods later, i need to erase some of those enemy voices ... Terrible.Short Pro List:Good Turn-Based Combat,Nice GFX, MusicDeep (enough) things to fiddle around (Shipresearch, Toon abilitys, Outfitting, etc)Short Neg List:If you are new to the genre ... start on the lowest difficulty or prepare for pain - maybe check a guide or two(why is this a Neg? Because the game could teach that better. No biggie for a Vet, but, it can be hard even for them!)Not everything is voiced, thats a bummer - but no deal breaker.The Game presses hard on your rig - my pc had a hard time to keep the temp low. It got better after a patch, but, huiii.The Voices of the crazy dudes .. i really hate em. Terrible. :)The UI before the fight will have you make many, many clicks. Take your time.Thats it.I'm happy with the game and looking forward to still fight for the Emperer./salute

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played for 19 hours, and have only done 7 or 8 missions, so I'll edit this recommendation based on more gameplay, if necessary.  Even those 19 hours are misleading; I played the first mission on easy mode, unintentionally, so I started over on Standard mode.  Then I made several bad decisions due to not understanding how the various mechanics work (their documentation / explanations are very terse), and decided to start over again.  So I'm only half as far as you might expect I am.I am not a Warhammer or Warhammer 40K fan; I do have some residual resentment towards Games Workshop due to their pricing model and some of their business tactics within the miniatures hobby, it's pretty low-key.  I don't dislike either of their main franchises; I just don't know much about them.Even without knowing the lore or the backstories, I'm still enjoying the plot and story elements of the game.  Actually, one of the reasons I've only played 19 hours is that I found the lore and references so interesting that I started reading 'Eisenhorn', one of the most-often recommended series in the extensive line of 40K novels.  I've been enjoying reading that during some of the time I otherwise would have been playing the game.  I'm normally enough of a snob that I wouldn't read an RPG tie-in novel, or usually even a franchise (Star Wars, Star Trek, etc.) tie in; the fact that 19 hours of game play convinced me to give one a shot is pretty impressive.  The mechanics are X-COM-worthy.  The action point and willpower economies are fun to manage, even with the limited amount of control I have with level 3 characters and a single strategem; I can see how I'm going to get more and more tools to manage both in-battle currencies in the future.  There is a Ship tech tree, and a Research tech tree.  Each marine has their own individualized Ability tree; I believe what they did was define a bunch of mini-trees, each one of which can be placed in the North, South, East, and West positions relative to your starting point in the center of the tree.  I also believe they came up with similar mini-trees that could slot into the NW, NE, SE, and SW locations, and I think that which one goes into a particular marine's final tree is at least partly determined by which of the "primary, N/S/E/W" trees are on either side of it.  In any event, it makes each marine distinct, and with the same class and the same level, two marines can play completely different roles.It plays well with both gamepad and mouse-- I use the gamepad while playing on my laptop in bed, and the mouse when playing on the PC with my widescreen monitor.My two significant complaints so far are:1. As ridiculous as this sounds, there's actually no way to inspect the battlefield.  You always have one of your marines selected, and anywhere you place the cursor is in relation to some action that marine would take-- moving, firing at range, teleporting, healing, whatever.  You can't hover over something that looks like it could be just artwork, or could act as effective cover, or whatever, and get a name, or a description of its effects.  This is super irritating.  Even if you could get all the info you need while having a marine selected (and I don't think you can), it's needlessly awkward.  It would be so simple to just have a button you can press when a square is highlighted to get information, but there isn't.  It would also be normal an convenient to have a button you can press which would outline items of interest in some color, like movement penalties, what kind of cover it supplies, etc.  2. I can't figure out how to re-read the text that appears on the screen-- sometimes in battle a message will get displayed in a or edge of a screen that I'm not looking at, and by the time my eyes track over, I only have a moment before the text disappears, and I'll miss part or all of the meaning.  Similarly, in the Options, I have Combat log turned on; but I can't find any way to view the log, which I'd *really* like to do.

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review - As a fan of the old school x-com games and someone that used to play Warhammer 40k as a kid I love this game so far, the graphics are solid, the music it atmospheric and the level designs make me wish my battlefields as a kid looked like this. There have been a lot of hit and miss Warhammer 40k games over the years and I have to put this up there in the hits section along with Space Marine, kill team and Dawn of War Soul Storm. The game play is similar enough to other tactical games like the recent x-com remakes and gears tactics that fans of strategy games can quickly jump over even if they are unfamiliar with the lore, and the game play is also simple enough that 40k fans who might not be familiar with turn based computer games can jump right in. However, game just doesn't know how to balance itself. Again, your knights will feel like paper until you get very late game gear and abilities. One of the most common enemies is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ plant that acts as a high range, high health, high damage mortar that cannot be stunned or disabled. You just have to ignore every enemy and bum rush it, or wait a long time to draw out enemies. Keep in mind the game debuffs you randomly every few turns with the "warp surge" mechanic. The straw for me is when I complete the month, get an "Grandmaster Report" where I can upgrade stuff. Great.Except no. Every report is a penalty to you, where you basically get condescended and then they demand even more resources, for no payoff. It's literally a resource sink. The amounts taken increase as the game progresses. At a certain point I had to give up some knights for a while. Only, it didn't tell me it'd be for THREE MONTHS. And they didn't let me choose.
