_childDocuments_.review: Picking up where the first game left off, Submerged: Hidden Depths is a third person, casual survival game where you and your brother arrive at another sunken city only to find that there is a “Mass” that has killed all of the inhabitants and taken over the city. It's up to you and your brother to find out what happened and you need to find a way to fix it.Pros:Simple controlsExcellent graphicsWell optimizedNon-linearMystery unfolds as you playCons:Sometimes your character can get stuck on the stairsMuch like its predecessor, Submerged is a fun, relaxing game that will keep busy for awhile. After playing the first game, I knew what to expect, but I didn't anticipate the story to be this engaging. Each time you complete part of the story, a short cinematic movie will play filling in a few holes. Before long, you come face to face with the “Mass”.I didn't have any technical issues with the game but I did notice that on occasion, your character can become stuck on a set of stairs. One time, I was so hopelessly stuck, that I had to exit the game but when I came back, I was unstuck fixing that problem.At the time of this review, Submerged: Hidden Depths was selling for $29.99. This game is much longer than its predecessor and the story was very solid, so I found it to be well worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: The basic gameplay is similar to that of Submerged: you explore the city with your boat, climb certain buildings to complete objectives, and after each objective, a cutscene is played and the story progresses. There are many improvements though. The graphics is improved, the scenery is more varied, the puzzles are more complex (but still not difficult), there are more kinds of collectibles, and now at some places you play as Taku.There are some things I liked better in the previous game, mainly the map design. There, the city looked more organic, the main missions scattered around different parts of a forest of buildings. Here, each mission takes place in a building that's surrounded by a cluster of other buildings, with the rest of the map being much more sparse, mostly empty space. This makes the map look more artificial, more like a series of video game levels and less like a real city. Similarly with the weather, on one part of the map it always rains, on other parts it's always sunny.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first Submerged and Hidden Depths did not let me down. It captured the essence of the original game and improved upon it. You return to a new submerged city which is beautifully crafted in exquisite detail. From the interiors of the ruined buildings to the sweeping vistas, it is just incredible to behold. You control a brother and sister who are restoring the city by fighting the dark forces at work. This is done by locating seeds and restoring a network of 'green' to replace the blackness.While the main mission is to restore balance by locating and planting seeds, there are a host of collectibles for achievement hunters. Outfits, points of interest, signal towers, salvage (boat parts and items), and the pages of history which complete the story. My favorite is the wildlife. There are creatures on land and at sea and it is really fun when  you encounter them (especially when a large one surprises you by coming to the surface of the sea!).There are limited voice overs that are done in a native language (with translated subtitles) and the story is told through pictographs with translated captions. The sound track is a delight to listen to and really adds to the wonder of exploring the watery world. The game world is very open with somewhat linear paths through the buildings. This is helpful because there are big interiors to navigate and it is easy to get lost. You have a map that builds as you travel and a telescope for spotting items of interest. There is also an optional compass on the interface which is quite helpful (although I discovered it late in the game). I used a 'grid search' method to traverse the entire map and it took just over 20 hours to find all collectibles and reach 100%.For me, the controller worked best (although keyboard/mouse can be used). This gave me more control with boat navigation and I crashed less regularly (luckily there is no penalty for boating into a structure at full speed!).  The characters do a lot of leaping and climbing but no actual platforming is required on the part of the player. You simply move ahead and the character does what is needed to navigate obstacles.The game autosaves as items are collected and you have the option to save on exit. A single save slot is used. If you get turned around in a building, it is possible to restart the current area. All items you've collected are retained and you can go back through, searching for missed collectibles from the start of that area. There is also a fast travel option that becomes available as you work through each major building.If you enjoy exploration and scenery, then I highly recommend this game. If you missed the original Submerged, I'd play it  first (although Hidden Depths is stand-alone).  This will give you double time in the wonderful environments created by Uppercut Games.

Got stuck on textures while exploring a few areas such as around the big hotel building. No checkpoints so, just had to restart the whole area. Cool looking game though and it's simple enough so that you don't have to learn a whole lot of game mechanics before actually playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Miku and Taku have drifted around the world as outcasts, never allowed to live with their own kind due to Miku’s gift after she was blessed by an unknown entity that allows her to bloom flowers and grow plant life. Drifting for a long time over the endless ocean, the siblings discover an abandoned city whose residents have mysteriously vanished in the aftermath of an unusual disaster. Investigate the disappearances to learn what happened, explore the beautiful world around you, and decide if this is a home worth settling for. 5-10 hours to complete, Submerged: Hidden Depths is a gorgeous, post-apocalyptic open world exploration game with fun puzzles and a charming atmosphere. A sequel to Submerged, Hidden Depths is a massive improvement in every single way; musically, graphically, and environmentally. Not only are there now outfits and hairstyles to collect, you have a base that you can improve, a garden to grow, and treasures to discover! Taku is also now an available character to play in some areas, and the interaction between siblings as they explore another sunken city is very well done! I genuinely could not stop taking screenshots and it was difficult to narrow them down to a few to post. While the storyline is admittingly almost as confusing as the first game, it’s still worth picking up and playing them in order.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 6.5/10I felt that the story was very lackluster compared to the first game, even though both are very minimal. While it would seem that the sequel is a continuation of Miku and Taku's story, I felt that it didn't add anything to the series and wondered why a sequel was even necessary. That being said, the game wasn't horrible, but I did find myself getting bored more often than not. My biggest issue was that the game felt very janky at times, despite having a pc that is more than capable of running it....characters getting stuck in the floor, boat spinning out of control after using fast travel, huge lag spikes when using the boosters...those were the main ones. And despite loving the first game, I couldn't really get into this one.Graphically, it's still pretty and has plenty of detail. Exploration is relaxing and at your own pace. If you must play it, I'd suggest waiting until it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just going to say that I immensely enjoyed the first Submerged and even though it was left open-ended, I definitely didn't expect part two to be coming. However, as soon as I was thinking about replaying part one, here comes part two. And it gets way, WAY better. The story, the gameplay.... all of it! It seems everything that was lacking in the first installment (although in my opinion, nothing was lacking) was taken into consideration and polished to perfection. First off, this game is absolutely beautiful and for a screenshot lover it's a real gem! The navigation is better, the locations are better and of course the "antagonist" came out simply perfect! In addition, the story is fantastic and it made me realize how much I have missed the main characters. Trust me, you WILL want to complete this with full achievement - it's so rewarding. One remark though, if you accidentally end up in a spot you're not supposed to be in you will get stuck and it will crash the game. Just use fast travel to get out so you can continue. Last but not least, when you just happen to hear a certain growling noise above you at some point - do lift up your head and try not to fall out of your chair. Just saying. Yes, I'm classifying it as a jumpscare :)

_childDocuments_.review: There’s a wealth of post apocalyptic games that go out of their way to kill you so it’s nice to play one that doesn’t. Submerged: Hidden Depths is billed as a “non-combat third-person “relaxploration” adventure” and it delivers exactly that. The world is a colour rich environment of a sunken city and the remains of an old world now mostly underwater which finds our sibling heroes Miku and Taku making their way through the ruins looking for bits and pieces of lore, animals, and most of all the “seeds” that might bring salvation to an otherwise destroyed civilization. Submerged is primarily a story of two siblings, Miku who obtained mysterious powers from her contact with the “Mass”; which is a plant like growth that has wrapped itself around the left over buildings of the past, and her brother Taku who is just trying to take care of his sister and keep them together. The general goal is to find and collect the “Seeds” at various locations and plant them to help heal the “Mass”.The general gameplay is fairly straight forward as you make your way to various mostly submerged buildings. You’ll sail, climb, and zipline your way to collect the seed and various other collectables to unlock some backstory, progress the story or find other elements of the world. Exploration is key to find some of the more hidden paths that lead to cosmetic pieces that unlock ship or clothing cosmetics as well as finding collectible flowers or encounter some of the animals that are still around. The remnants of past technology are seen everywhere as you climb, jump, or take elevators upwards and onwards to find the “Seeds”.Taking the seeds and planting them in their appropriate place will help heal the mass and progress the story forward. The nice open world aspect and fast travel unlockables make it easier to return to places where you might have missed a book, or unlockable piece. Yet even in this colourful environment there are reminders everywhere that an apocalypse took place, from the sunken city, the decaying runs overrun with plant-life or the human like plant echoes of people who once lived or survived only to be consumed and left their nuclear like shadows made of plants.It’s a beautiful example of indie games that leverage story telling and a familiar situation in a different way. The music is often soft and understated as you progress while it can also ramp up with events that take place over the course of the game. Eventually as you get to other areas you’ll find some extra interaction using your boat to tow or pull down elements to help you progress in your journey but none of these are especially puzzling and just add to the experience. There is a story to be found and a relaxing trip to take without the urgency of things trying to end you. Though I will admit I missed some of the collectables in some of the areas that I’ll end up going back for as I wrap up my own playthrough, but for the purposes of this review I’ve enjoyed the time I’ve put in so far. If you’re looking for a break from the usual open world exploration types I would certainly recommend Submerged: Hidden Depths as one to take a look at. There’s a welcome amount of depth to be found wrapped in some easy gameplay and a wonderfully crafted world. Also there are whales.

_childDocuments_.review: improves on every element of the earlier title while still feeling like an organic continuation of the beloved original. Everything has been tightened and polished to raise the bar yet again on what a relaxing exploration game should be. Specifically  adds an immersive audio layer that I found a critical tool for exploring. (The sound effects and music are perfect.)It was incredibly satisfying to continue the story from the first game and to see how the world evolved in essentially real time. Gameplay (and music!) alternates between Miku & Taku as you explore, which felt meaningful and added to the surprising variety of environmental styles. In fact, now there are even cosmetic options to unlock (hairstyles, clothing, boat style). The world this time around feels much bigger, and much more vertical. There are more puzzle elements than before (namely bridges and switches), but everything still feels just right. That all acrobatics (jumping, swinging, climbing) are all done by simply moving forward makes this game a great fit for players of all skill levels. launched with rebindable controls, Steam cloud support, accessibility control schemes (mouse only for MKB, one-handed for controller), color sensitivity options, good graphical control settings for UE4 (no FOV due to auto camera in certain sequences), and devs have been responsive to community discussions. That Uppercut Games backported several of this game's improvements to the first, now six-year old  is a good demonstration of their ethos.I am hoping for a few quality of life changes eventually (auto throttle, disabling cutscene skipping warnings, quieter insects), but at launch the game is in excellent shape and I look forward to spending many more hours exploring the

_childDocuments_.review: In the years and years I've had Steam, I've only ever "completed" a game once, by getting all the achievements.  I'm not really given over to that sort of thing.  This game is the closest I've come to that.  Let that be a measure of how strongly I liked this thing.This is not a game that requires hand-eye coordination.  This is not a game that has any sense of urgency.  This is really about exploration.  Exploring the world reveals snippets of story and cosmetics to dress up your character.  I'm not moved by the latter, but the bit of story and all these ruins sucked me right in, though I'd only play it for an hour or so at a time for long-winded reasons I'll leave out of this review, because I'd like to keep it under a megabyte in length.Anyway, this game isn't at all cruel about the tidbit collecting.  If you're patient, if you look through each corner, if you take all the alternate forks, and if you pay attention, you'll find them all without stress.  A distinct sound plays near collectible items.  Just listen. And in listening you'll hear the work that went into this game's audio: the footfalls on diamond-plate catwalks, calloused hands grasping wooden poles, annoying pigeons making their annoying pigeon noises, and so on.And, of course, also look.  That's the point, I think.  A lot of effort went into this little sunken, ruined city.  The colours are bright and saturated, the style a trifle cartoonish, and maybe the city doesn't quite make internal sense to me in a few places but that's a terribly trite complaint.  I can believe people lived amongst the ruins, years ago.  Now it's desolate and it's terribly lonely.Mind you, maybe I like ruins.  So here, a city that was built up so long ago the people who made it were called "ancients".  A civilization sprung up around the ruins, building little nests and walkways amongst the ruins, sticking them to the outside of office towers like 2x4 barnacles.  Then this second society was also driven out.  You're in the crumbling aftermath of a double-extinction event, and there's not another soul in sight.There's a couple minor issues.  A trite one:  I'm not the most fond of playing as young teens.  Well, I'm a zillion Internet years old at this point, so you can get off my lawn.  And occasionally, my character got stuck on some terrain.  In all cases save one, I was able to jiggle my way free.  A quick-travel back to base, and back to my exploration solved that problem effortlessly.With what I think was remarkably thorough investigation, I've found all the game's secrets (save one), solved all the puzzles, and unlocked all the cosmetics, in a bit over eight hours.  But if you judge a game strictly on a time/money ratio, you're doing yourself a disservice.  A flight in business class costs more than flying economy, but there's no doubting it's a better experience. But then maybe crawling through ruins doesn't move you as much as it does me.  Either way, here's an experience I kind of regret I waited this long to get, before jumping in.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: An immensely enjoyable (and relatively stress-free......though perhapsstress free) exploration, puzzle platforming and collection game, sequel to the previous "Submerged".  I had a great deal of fun navigating the ocean looking for mutated fauna, points of interest, wreckage for power-ups for the boat, etc.  However.......the game is not without its flaws.Positives:*Graphics*  Colourful, vibrant, eye-pleasing.....all these adjectives apply, and even on my increasingly out of date graphics card (1050 TI), the game still looked great, and more importantly, played great (although there were some frame-rate drops, to be sure!)*Gameplay*  The central gameplay loop of boating around and exploring ruined buildings in this drowned world is downright addictive, and I had a blast......but I'm also going to ding the gameplay a bit below....I had a minor and a major kvetch.Meh:*Music*  It's not bad, truly its not, but neither is it great.....just rather mid......and even a little cheesy sometimes.*Gameplay*  If you have played the previous game, than there really isn't much other than a new gameplay mechanism that you haven't seen before........even the story chops/beats are quite similar.  Now I know that as I sequel it sure should share some thematic and gameplay DNA with its predecessor, but this is REALLY derivative of the previous game.  I didn't mind TOO much, because I really liked the first game, but the similarities became a little been-there-done-that after awhile (IMO).Negatives:*Gameplay*  It sure it fun.....but it's  easy.....I know, I know, I usually love easy games, but there are numerous platforming challenges here with beams to balance across, gaps to leap, etc etc and they all amount to "push forward to win".   You literally cannot fall.  Now, this absolutely allows you to explore with a sense of wonder and awe and not have to worry about plummeting to your doom (ever!) which does have its upsides, but there were so many awesome challenges that looked great from a puzzle platformer perspective that 100% (IMO) lost a little something for being impossible to screw up; as I said, once you're on the beam, just push the arrow keys (or WASD, whatever) in the right direction and the character automatically leaps over gaps, balances on thin beams, etc.*Story/Narrative*  The problem with having an open world game with true freedom to explore any location you want in whatever order you desire, is that the story-based objects that will unlock the background of this region to you the player can be accessed in any order.........which means that you will possibly (and it my case, absolutely!) unlock story/background information in such a way that you know the middle and end of the story first without knowing what came first, totally robbing the narrative of any sense of story progression.  You will eventually learn the whole tale, but ask any reader; would it matter to you if you read the last chapters of a fantasy novel first, followed by a chapter or two from the beginning, then read the middle chapters, then perused the remaining opening chapters?  Of course it would.  Sure you eventually get the whole picture, but it is more or less drained of any narrative heft.Regardless, the game was still fun and enjoyable, so I'm going to recommend it, just be aware that it does have some hefty flaws.Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Its similar to the first game but the parkour/platforming has been significantly nerfed from what I remember. In this game you can't fall and you can't miss jumps etc. Actually you don't even jump in this game, instead you just point the character in the direction of the jump and the character handles the timing. Maybe the first game was the same but for some reason I remember the game-play being a little bit more hands on and engaging, while here the game is arguably a little bit too chill and laid back.  Apart from the parkour the other aspect of the game-play is just exploring the map and finding the various collectibles dotted around. Its enjoyable enough and doesn't feel tedious or grindy. I guess probably a big reason for this is that the game looks gorgeous and so just sailing around and taking in the vistas is entertaining by itself. In fact the game is so pretty you might spend more time taking screen-shots then playing.There are also little bits of story sprinkled in and you can unlock more with collecting items but the story is not really the focus of the game as far as I can tell.Overall recommended if you want something relaxing.

_childDocuments_.review: Sequel to a great game, that's definitely bigger. Is it better? I think that's questionable.  Let's get the obvious out of the way: the game is gorgeous. The best way to describe it is “baroque”. Everything feels more ornate, more over the top; there's options to collect sets that let you alter the look of your boat, as well as Miku's hairstyle and outfit; you can collect flowers and dredge up relics to set up a museum and a garden in your home base; the building you explore feature pressure plates,  and levers to make you progress. It all seems far more elaborate. However, these elements, while neat, also make the game more streamlined. To add an animal  or landmark to your Journal, you need to approach it and hit the “interact' button. The level design has gotten far more linear, with paths more colour-coded and only one or two paths visible at the time. None of this is bad, but it reduces the organic feel of discovery. The buildings where you can find optional diary pages (replacing “secrets” from the original) are also clearly  differentiated from the other buildings. This removes the frustration of searching everywhere, but, again-makes the experience feel more guided, rather than free-form. There's also 10 lookout towers that reveal (some) of the nearby collectibles. It's not particularly overbearing, as most of the things it could reveal I'd already spot with the looking glass (and finding engine upgrades is the most annoying part of the game anyway, so any help is welcome), but I can see this annoying people. Overall, the improvements in the sequel are a mixed bag. However, it carries the relaxed exploration vibe of the original, and its a visual feast.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: 5 hours and finished. Can probabl put in 1 hour more for finding all stuff. This is little more than an explore the map "game". No jump or other buttons. Just WASD and it plays itself. Thumb up for a short relaxing and non-frustrating, time. Not woth more than 10€.Better of with Kena: Bridge of Spirits which is a really good exploration game, cute and with some combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nothing. It has no noteworthy characters, shallow story, no gameplay, borderline no writing. The only thing it has going for it is pretty graphics which I guess was enough to warrant the very positive rating it has. My main issue with this game is the gameplay, or more so lack of. Its an exploration game where all the places to explore have a single path you go on without engaging at all. You simply press a key in the direction you wanna go in and your character does all the jumping, vaulting, climbing. There are no puzzles as everytime you come across anything you can interact with you just interact with it and thats it. The sailing gameplay would be decent as the boat has good weight to it, if it wasnt for the fact that its buggy and doesnt register you already pressed W to go forward. Also whenever using your telescope while sailing your boat stops, there is no momentum and its super annoying.All in all this game is all about graphics, aslong as it can jingle those keys infront of you and you dont get bored for 8 or so hours you are good to go. If you are looking for any actual exploration or gameplay this is a hard pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game and great sequel. The basic concept is the same, exploring interesting world and collecting various items, without dying or time pressure, while listening to great calm music. Compared to the first game, Hidden Depths has  (besides other things):- better graphics- more complex puzzles- more items to collect- more developed story- lots of quality of life changes (fast travel, area restart, "All nearby objects discovered" info, etc.)Ten hours of pure joy and I still have to find that last boat upgrade and last animal.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't really reviewed any games before, but felt the need to on this one.I finished the first Submerged game a week or so ago (and also quite enjoyed it) then jumped straight on this one, and have to say that it is a massive step up. Improvements in all the right places and they managed to make the world look even more gorgeous - Just the water alone was so beautiful to look at. The postcard mode is perfect for capturing SO many screenshots (though I found it to be a touch buggy on ziplines, but still usable). The extra little options for customisation were also a really nice addition.This was the perfect game for me to just sit down and relax for a while. Exploring structures and is somewhat set to a locked path (with some extra areas for the collectables which I love), this did mean that a lot of the exploration was just holding w (no need to press space to jump over a gap for example), but I didn't mind this in the slightest. Also no combat but a game like this I feel didn't require it at all, and a lot more content would be needed in the game to make it worthwhile.I also quite enjoyed how the story was managed. Cutscenes weren't overused and there wasn't much talking, but the visuals and subtitles plus story notes in the journal made it enjoyable to follow.Overall thoroughly enjoyed spending time sailing around to find new areas, exploring all the buildings, and completing the achievements. Somewhat simple to play, but really pleasant and beautiful.I highly recommend to anyone looking to just chill out for a few hours and explore a beautiful world.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 | Truly amazing | Beautiful Scenic Views | Phenomenal. This game is truly majestic. The first game was a delightful wonder to experience and the second in the "series" is just such a wonderful continuation & delight to dive into. If you've not played the first game I highly recommend doing so first. It's not an overly long game and should make sense upon experiencing that story as this game follows up as the two siblings appear to be older. There's a ton of collectables and plenty of ocean to navigate and explore whilst either focusing the main story line OR just experience freely yourselves.Massive thank you to the developers for this game, I'm super grateful to have experienced this and hope to finish it 100% one of these days as it's such a soothing, relaxing wonder. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Basically the same relaxing game as the previous. You explore, you enjoy the scenery, and you collect things. If I needed to search for a gripe I'd say there's a small invisible wall problem, the boat boost should last longer, and a couple of the creatures are a little tough to find, but I'd really have to stretch to actually be annoyed. _childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: A nice and straightforward exploration game. I didn't realise until I completed it that there is another Submerged game that came before this one so I'm not sure how it compares, but I liked this one on its own as well. The game is pretty short and easy, but offers some lovely visuals and relaxed exploration. I recommend playing with a controller.I would overall rate Submerged: Hidden Depths a 7/10. It's relaxing, pretty, and accessible. I also managed to get it for a very worthwhile price. It could, however, benefit from more variation in its gameplay and encourage more input from the player. I would wait for a sale, especially since even 100% takes less than 10 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend this at historic low price or in a bundle, but not near retail price.  Platforming may be completed in as little as 3-5 hours unless you get stuck like I have on getting further at the locations where two seeds are.  This is a platformer with lite parkour, an occasional simple puzzle, and its an open world only in that a boat happens to be used to go between the different platforming areas on land: 10 seeds to put in trees and various other diary locations.  Other than that, there's a good amount to collect by boat including landmarks, boat upgrades (read: max seconds of boost), and sea animals.  There's no dialog, but there are some cutscenes between seed unlocks, and when a matching set of 4 collectible diaries is found then it tells a local story.  Make the black stuff go away and spread flowers and green stuff, even the planet seems like a flooded foregone conclusion - Its a different take on environmental-centric stories.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: This was a most colorful game. I enjoyed a change of pace from the hack and slash games. I really enjoyed the exploration and solving the puzzles. I wish it was even longer. It was mysterious and relaxing. The graphics were so beautiful and colorful. The only down side of the game was during game-play at times it would stutter and the character would get stuck and couldn't move. I ended up saving/going to the menu and reloading. That usually fixed the "stuck" situation. It happened a total of three times in the whole game. Other than that, the game was smooth running. I hope there will be another Submerged game since I enjoyed this one so much.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Submerged Hidden Depths it's a nice sequel overall, but it has some of the problems the first game had (performance issues when loading new terrain and using too much transitions cutting the rythm of the gameplay), I'll explain myself better later.But appart from that the story is short and interesting, the visuals of the game overall are really nice, there's some good extra exploration to do after finishing the game, the music is really really really good, and the gameplay mechanics are an improvement and expansion of the ones the first game had. In general the game feels good, solid and enjoyable.About the problems...yeah...there are a few really really short moments where the game feels strange, there are some actions that don't have any animations, I DON'T KNOW WHY wouldn't they put the effort in it since this game would be a lot better without all the transitions placed in those little moment that literally put a barrier between you and the world of the game this kind of details that break a little bit the gameplay experience are hard to accept in my opinion when this game isn't "new" since it's been for more than a year on "Stadia". It feels a little bit odd paying 25€ and not seeing those things that despite of being "little"/"stupid" are there but not being adressed by the devs in this rerelease of the game on steam.But as I've said, those are little details and especially if you liked the first game you'll love this one with my only real concern being that the price it's a little bit high.Here you have some footage of the game:

I'd recommend this for anyone enjoying exploration games with some light puzzle work.  Or even those just wanting a game that is   relaxing and not stressful.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: This game seems like it would a fun game where you just chill out and explore but it has so many technical issues. In the one hour I played I crashed three times. _childDocuments_.review: Nice chill game, pretty graphics and a cute little story. The message can get very heavy handed, nature good, technology bad, we get it. _childDocuments_.review: Submerged: Hidden Depths is a great sequel to Submerged. It is very well done and is a great game in it's own right. It's a third person atmospheric adventure game set in a flooded world. The world graphics are beautiful, the way the light reflects off of the water, the half submerged buildings and statues make the world come alive and it's gorgeous. There is very little dialogue, so the stories of what happened to the world and Miku and Taku are told through drawings that look like cave drawings and the actions of the characters. It's a very interesting way to tell the story and it's extremely well done. The music is awesome, the game controls very well, and exploring the water world is a lot of fun. The climbing and jumping from ledge to ledge is very well done, along with the switches and pulley systems that transport you real fast. Overall it's a really good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Coming upon a half-submerged city overtaken by a strange plant-like growth, a sister and a brother take it upon themselves to discover the secrets of the city and its past inhabitants to find out what happened.  Encountering obstacles along the way, the siblings will have to face off against the unknown if they want to discover the secrets of the hidden depths.Submerged: Hidden Depths is a third-person puzzler with minor platforming aspects in the gameplay.  Here you explore a half-submerged city, looking for clues as to what happened to the previous inhabitants by boating to different areas to solve minor puzzles, collect numerous collectibles, and enjoy the scenery.  The environmental puzzles are not difficult, and the game seems more focused on exploring and taking in the view than it is to challenge you…which leaves ample room to enjoy the game.The two stories of Submerged: Hidden Depths are told in tandem; the story of the city and the story of the brother and sister and these tales are told without words but instead with a curious picture language.  However, unlike the previous game, captions are provided when the story segment is completed so you can enjoy the story instead of trying to puzzle out the pictograms.Items to find, besides completing the story items, tend to be items that help tell the story of the city, provide upgrades to your boat, and more so, provide different skins for not only the main character but your boat as well.  Additional items to collect include viewing all the different animals as well as finding strange relics from the past.Controls are easy and the game takes over for some difficult areas such as swinging, jumping, and holding on to cliff faces.  Basically, you point the character in the right direction, and they take care of it themselves.  Areas where the characters can perform these tasks are well marked so you aren’t trying to hop a cliff for hours only to figure out that you couldn’t do it anyway.  You won’t accidentally fall off or drown, but simply have to find your way from point A to point B.  For some players this is a negative aspect of Submerged: Hidden Depths but understanding this type of game and what the developers wanted me to get from it, I didn’t have a problem.Achievements are attained by completing the game and finding many different sets of collectibles.  All collectibles can be found by simply exploring the map.  Additionally, you can continue to play after completing the game to get the rest of the collectibles that you may have missed during the first playthrough.You do not need to have played the first Submerged to enjoy this one, but I highly recommend playing both games.  The vistas are beautiful, the story captivating, and the puzzles, while easy, allow the ability to enjoy the atmosphere without fear of getting stuck.   Submerged: Hidden Depths is for those who have played the first game, those that love exploration and finding collectibles, or for those who may have a hard time playing other games where you must be precise in jumping or climbing activities to progress.  All in all, my second journey to the watery world of Submerged left me completely satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game. I finished the previous part and enjoyed it for what it is. It does have some technical issues (geometry isn't perfect and you can get stuck in places you shouldn't, significant framedrops are common, input lag and camera are annoying) but I see it as a something to chill down and relax by. It is a nice game to introduce your child to gaming. There is no violence, challenge is nonexistent, you can't get hurt and it looks and sounds just nice.For those who played the original Hidden Depths: it is basically more of the same. Yes - there are some mechanics added, but nothing important. Map size is more or less the same, so is movement. You explore seed locations and watchtowers as a girl and diaries locations as a boy, but they differ only in the way they look.I wouldn't (and didn't) buy the game full price, but if you find it discounted to about $5 I think you might get enough fun in it to justify spending this money.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: An improvement on the first game in almost every way. The graphics are improved a good amount, especially the lighting. The clutter (amount of stuff present in the world, plants, animals, structures, etc.) is significantly improved, adding depth to the world.The level design is also more interesting than in the first game. There are far more mechanics to interact with. Though this is somewhat hampered by the obnoxious paint on everything you can interact with.The story is generally more interesting. Still, I wouldn't say it's great.The cinematography/art direction... absolutely 10/10 beautiful and the art style is magnifique. There was never a time where I was confused by the camera angles like in game 1. The entire game feels like it was the perfect manifestation of what the devs imagined. It's such a unique feel.7/10 Definite improvement on the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Elements of arcade but not quite. Only slightly platformer/parkour, and only slightly puzzle because neither get really hard enough to count as a definition in Hidden Depths. Explore and find things, which are out in the open, almost makes Submerged an exploring game. Each of 7 locations unlock a chapter of the story, but although linear in it's message, they can be found in any order. So for me it's a solid explorer. Atmospherics add to the prettiness of the game world, and a sense of the passage of time is implied in a mist that slowly builds without creating any kind of urgency. Explore at your own pace and aside from the 7 seeds, you can finish without finding any side items. I really liked the way you can climb structures and then use a telescope to spot treasures from up there, and how collectibles add to your home/base.So very much a Peaceful Explorer game even if it has some menace to it in the vertigo inducing climbs and a lurking "Mass" monster.Like the original game, Hidden Depths is a story with that post-apocalyptic feel to it. Where human, greed or something caused us to fall. And for the depths, metaphorically to open up and swallow us in punishment. And so you must make that selfless sacrifice to undo the evil. Usual stuff really.And for the plot aspect of the game, it's being much a copy of the last, and not being that long, that immersive and re-playable. I'm tempted to mark Hidden Depths down as But although hard to identify with, the characters are likeable. The scenery beautiful and the soundscape is credible and pulls off a credible post apocalyptic feel.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: 9h 2/10 1 Yes,  No No No No No No No No difficulty option NoSubmerged: Hidden Depth is a sequel to an already really enjoyable game but this one is even better. The game felt more fun and it looks and sounds so so much better than the first one in this series. You play as a brother and sister that try to save the world from a "sad" plant. There are no enemies in this game but you'll explore and climb on all kinds of obstacles. The game has the option ( which is on when you first start the game) to highlight areas you can interact with red, to make it easier to know where to go. I only have one con and that is that the game had a lot of stutters for me. Like once every 2 to 3 minutes or so. I couldn't find any pattern why the game did that and turning on VSYNC or lowering the graphics didn't help. Gladly there is no combat in this game, so it wasn't that bad but it sucks for such a beautiful-looking game. Submerged: Hidden Depths has no missable achievements. There are a lot of collectibles and I would suggest exploring everything you can when you're close to it, but don't worry about missing out on anything as there is a free roam option after you finish the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: is a stand-alone sequel to the award-winning Submerged which was released in 2015. This colourful new adventure game follows a brother and sister as they explore the ruins of a sunken city and does not require knowledge of the original game in order to enjoy it.It is a wonderfully immersive and relaxing experience that strikes a nice balance between allowing players to roam freely while still providing some rails to aid progression. There is no shortage of things to collect and do and the vibrant and varying environment is a joy to explore. The narrative is perhaps a little lacking but this does not detract from the enjoyment too much. There is a lot on offer here and I heartily recommend this game to anyone looking for an exploratory adventure game that doesn’t demand too much!My full review of this game where I discuss gameplay, narrative and styling is available on
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: First, prettiest thing ever. Second, it brings the feels; playing this game is an emotional experience, like a really good holiday. Third, it's clever and filled with interesting content - lore, backstory, art, details. Fourth, it's quite a different experience than any other game I've played; it's neither a narrative railroad nor a blood-drenched meat grinder, and despite the level of detail it doesn't cause my system to fall over or even wobble. It's a voyage of discovery, and one I will both remember and return to.Oh, and no offence to meat grinders. I love gibs as much as almost anyone, but this is a refreshing change of pace from that. And while I was gifted this game, it is a much-appreciated member of my library.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: It's really big jump since last game. The fast travel, graphical improvements, story that you don't need to actually figure out what happened cause It's already written and a lot of other things but I must say the story didn't really went with me. That's only thing that I didn't really like. The Giant and other creatures are cool tho.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I love post-apocalyptic settings and the sort of 'nature has reclaimed the world' sub-setting is quite rare.Graphically the game is.. almost gorgeous IMO.It's a tad empty everywhere the player can't go, but otherwise I think it's lovely to look at.Lots of greenery and some decent water effects.And the character models are well done as well.It's always nice to see a girl-next-door protagonist instead of the usual supermodels.Audio-wise the game does a good job as well, the music is nice and relaxing and the sound effects are perfectly serviceable. The fishing up a relic tune is heavily inspired by Zelda if I'm not mistaken.I would compare the gameplay to the 3D Prince of Persia's, but without the.. tension since you can't fall, die or fail.Gameplay basically consists of driving a boat to a location and then at the location it turns into a climbing action-adventure with some minor puzzle elements.The boat is actually quite fun to drive, which it's definitely not in every game.And that's all the gameplay really.There is no combat or anything remotely difficult.I vaguely recall the term 'relaxploration' being bandied about and that's not inaccurate.The main 'problem' the game has IMO would be that it's a tad dull.It's fun in relatively short chunks, but it's not like it grabs you and won't let go.Other than that I'd say it's a good relaxing indie game and a slight improvement on the first one.I would love to see more of the world though.Something like a Fallout or Subnautica style game where you learn more about the world.That's my favorite part of Fallout, finding out how the world came to be and little stories about how life was before, during and after the calamity.So would I recommend it?If you enjoy some casual platforming with zero chance of failing with some minor exploration, sure.It goes on sale quite a bit and with large discounts, so definitely wait for one of those though.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: This is Submerged 2. To make it, they took a game that uses a lot of stereotypes / clichés to tell a heartwarming story (Submerged 1), and applied deconstructivism to it, completely killing the atmosphere. They destroyed it so thoroughly that I would actually love to hear how this abomination was created. So what are some of the changes between S1 and S2?I could go on but will leave it at that.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I feel very conflicted about this game and I appreciate the designers are trying to create a more relaxed gaming experience. However in trying to do that I feel that they have crossed a line from relaxing to just plain boring. The 'puzzles' in the game are beyond simplistic, most gameplay revolves around collecting things, the thin story is nothing you won't have already heard before and open world despite some efforts, still comes across as lifeless and dull.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: The first Submerged was a very relaxing exploration game, quite enjoyable if a bit too simplistic in gameplay. This sequel takes the same type of gameplay and overall structure and improves upon it in every possible way. If you enjoyed the first game then this is simply better in everything. It's bigger, better, more beautiful, it has more things to do and see and it is a very very nice adventure type of game.I am not into collectables and that kind of stuff and I finished this at 100% because of how much I was enjoying it. There's no enemies to fight or kill, it's all about exploring and platforming. It's relaxing, it's beautiful and it's fun. Very recommended.Oh, I played this and the first Submerged in VR using the UEVR mod. It plays absolutely perfect with both games and it makes the game even more beautiful than it is when played flat. The views alone almost makes it worth the recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: This is, to me, a beautiful walking sim with lots of casual puzzles to unravel.  Nice music, and there's no pressure because the characters never do anything that would harm them.  You can't make them walk off a ledge or anything dangerous.  Have you seen the movie Annihilation?  The part where actor Tessa Thompson's character walks through a yard full of plants shaped like humans?  There are parts of this game where you find plants like that.  Very haunting stuff, in a nice way!  I think this game should appeal to old gamers (like me) who just want to relax and meander through a fantasy world, like having a coffee break.  This game seems like it would also be good for those who are new to 3D open-world stuff.  Anyway, you can't go wrong playing this while bundled up on a cold night with a cup of cocoa.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Submerged Hidden Depths is as beautiful and epic as the first game: Submerged.  The story is just as wonderful as the first....adding more to the journey of Miku and Taku who are brother and sister. There are some changes. The graphics are more updated. You play as characters, switching at various points during game play. There are new collectibles that allow to change different styles in boat, clothing (Miku only) and hair (Miku only).  Other collectibles include finding different items left over from a preflooded world, There are 9 flowers to collect that Miku can change in her hair. Journal pages tell the story of the city and that of Miku and Taku.  There are creatures to discover as well.  There are sites of interest as well to discover. Use the telescope to locate various sites and items to help find them on the map.This is an adventure puzzle game.  There is no fighting.  Though set in a flooded world there is no swimming. Use the boat for transport between areas. Walk, climb, and jump.  Use the elevators and rope slides to get around on the buildings. You cannot or will not die or fall at all.  Just guide the PC in the direction you want to climb or walk and it will go.I recommend use of game controller. But the keyboard and mouse it good too.  Use which ever you prefer.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice looking game, but you can tell very quickly if this game is going to be for you. It's pretty much a walking simulator, there's no platforming, heck, there's no jump button. It's pretty much just walk til you can pick up a seed and the drop it where the game tells you to via contextual button press. I looked to see if it'd change, and it really won't. There's simply zero reason this game should cost $30. Even if you're a fan of pretty walking simulators, there's little chance you'll find it a good value. Unfortunately I got it in a bundle, so can't refund it. Really look at some gameplay before you buy in. It's a very particular kind of game for a particular type of gamer.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I can see how hardened gamers, if they were to play this, would rush through it, and see how fast they could finish. But take your time and savor the beauty. I don't even want to watch walk throughs! It seems to have a lot of places to explore, and discover. No falling. No Dying. No Bosses. Beautiful world. Beautiful calm music. Lots to discover and collect. No specific way to correctly choose. Just go your own way. Exploring every nook and cranny will give results.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely, stress free game of exploration. You can't die and nothing can really harm you. The brother/sister relationship is explored as you explore this very pretty world. Takes about 8 hours to complete at a leisurely pace. Completion is maybe 10 hours. So much to like about it. Reminds me of another game "Sable" which takes about 25 hours to complete (also recommended).
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for the embargo on Submerged to lift because I've been dying to tell people about it. I love Waterworld settings and there aren't enough of them! Exploring Submerged is a fantastically relaxing way to spend your time after a long day at work.  The devs coined the term "relaxploration" for Submerged and I honestly can't think of a better way to describe it. Love the waterworld setting; the scenery is incredible. No pressure, just exploration.For more niche curation, follow me at:
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle platformer for those who aren't good at puzzle platformers, but want to play them. No skill required for jumping and climbing. The puzzle aspects can be challenging though, as the "stories"  and "designs" are hidden in some clever places within the ruins of the buildings. Those who like collecting games will enjoy these too as there are animals, artifacts, and boat upgrades to find in the ocean parts of the world. Don't be fooled by the tag "walking simulator". These games are much more than that. Also the artwork is just stupendous, especially in this second game.  The first game is good, but this one brings everything up several levels. Wonderful. Beautiful. Chillaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Follows on from the previous installment that stays true to the original open world puzzle exploration. Very much an upgrade that doesn't lose the charm that the original version has to offer. 7/10Average completion time: 8 hoursNumber of achievements: 14Difficulty: casualReplay-ability: done in 1 playthroughOnline playerbase: N/A
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the first then this is pretty much the same but in a good way with some new features. Fast travel helps for the completionist.  The tower levels I feel are designed better. The brother segments are just padding diversions that adds to the game's length. The story lore has been interesting so far. If you didn't like the first game this 2nd game won't change your mind. If you're new I don't think its necessary to play the first one and can just jump to this straight. Hope that helps.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxed exploration game with light platforming and puzzle elements (no combat). You play as brother and sister trying to rid your world of black mass and solve the mystery of where it came from. Sail your boat around the ocean, stop at different landmarks to clear out the black mass. Find collectables as you explore: journal entries, outfits, hair, boat styles, flowers, relics and boat power ups. There's not loads to do, but the world looks very pretty and the music is nice. I enjoyed my time exploring and sailing around.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I can't express how much I love this game. I play all the big titles, but when I want to chill, my three favourite tags are: open world, exploration and collectathon. This game blends those three elements perfectly in an absolutely beautiful environment with a compelling story. I loved the first game and loved this one just as much. I wish there were more games this.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, this game is exceptional. The only problem I can see here is that I think I'm not really capable of doing it justice in a review. Rushing through it would be missing the point.Playing it while looking up a guide would be missing the point.And if you intend on playing it in one or two gaming sessions, and then go off to the next thing... you probably should rethink things through.Make it last. Give it your attention. Enjoy it, and enjoy yourself if you can. This is a beautiful and precious experience that is to be savoured.This shouldn't be something you play to kill time, or to pursue some weird feeling of satisfaction you sometimes get when completing some kind of checklist which is, for all intent and purposes, unrelated to the actual experience.This game possesses such a dreamlike quality and sheer beauty that you rather should want to treat it (and yourself) very gently and take your sweet time with it.Personally, I stuck with it for a good month. During the cold, dark, and dank winter of 2023/2024. Playing an hour or two, here and there. Coming back to it. Not playing when I knew I couldn't give it my attention. I had a blast. Whenever I could play, it always made me smile and feel good. And I hadn't taken as many screenshots in a long while. This is one of those rare gems that made me feel like 100% completing it, which I did. I estimate it would take a normal person around 10 hours to play through this game. This is a 10 hours game. I'd say any number you hear that is less that this is ludicrous and should be subject to question. I spent a good hour AFK, so personally my total playtime is 12 hours.When it comes to the soundscape, the soundtrack and sound design for this game was created by legendary video game composer Jeff Van Dyck. Which I think a majority of people would know from his outstanding previous work on the soundtracks of "Rome: Total War" and Medieval II: Total War". The music is beautiful. Mainly, you have a string quartet. Which is often joined by a piano. Then, at the opposite of that on the spectrum, so to speak, you sometimes have what I'd call tribal percussions. All of it merges wonderfully with the scenery and the gameplay experience.What's more, the game is confident enough to know when to be quiet, sometimes. And to only leave you with silence and environmental sounds, which is something I appreciate very much.I've read in another review that the author wished there was 15 other Submerged games, and I agree. This is wholesome, this is soothing, this speaks to our sense of discovery and wonder, and is making us feel good in all the good ways. And I sure wouldn't mind more of that.Thank you for reading me, have a sweet day. This game is a gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe I got hooked with a pure exploration game such as this, but after a few hours in, it became one of my favorites.Definitely not a game for everyone, as it lacks combat or any sort of danger. It has very simple controls, and it places you into a "Sandbox" world to explore, while following a small story. It may not be much, but it's amazing visuals and the attention to detail, are enough to motivate you to keep playing. For me, this is a perfect "Stress Relief" title, so if you're into this genre, you should definitely give this game a try.However, I can not recommend this game, to anyone who has issues with heights!
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Submerged is a great example of a game that does what it sets out to do and doesn't overstay its' welcome. This is a near perfect example of what I want out of a game, especially an indie game. The gameplay is somewhere between a walking simulator and a 3D puzzler (but basically no puzzles - that's just how the controls are I would say). There is a decent sized open map that's beautiful and invites exploration on your boat, and then smaller areas where you can adventure on foot that are more or less exactly linear. The required areas have some side paths to get collectibles, lore, but the side areas are a straight shot. The thing that really sells this game for me is it's just an experience. The graphics are pretty and keep revealing more and more details as you go, from a day-night lighting that didn't need to be as nice as it is, to the general feeling of every area being so very unique and handcrafted. The sound and effects amplify this sense.Just a quick edit to add: I'm not sure why, exactly, but the game looks MUCH better in-game than in screenshots. Some processing or subtle motion or something, but yea.If you went straight for the required story parts, didn't do any collecting, and just powered through, you could probably beat the game in 3 hours, but I don't know what you'd get out of that. The fun is in the experience you get from being in the world and exploring. My negatives, such as they are, would be that no optional minimap on the boat ends up taking you out of things sometimes. On top of that, the watch towers are pretty useless, and the last few collectibles (especially animals and boat upgrades) you pretty much HAVE to use a guide for, unless you want to spend an extra hour on JUST those 3-4 things. Aside from that, the game was friction free, and has a lot of quality that much bigger, much better funded games lack.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Submerged: Hidden Depths is a wonderful adventure game that revolves around the story of a brother and sister lost in an abandoned city. The world around them is attacked by a black plant and it's your task to free it. It has an open world with a lot of locations to discover. You can freely explore it and drive around with the boat to find additional relics, upgrades, flowers, species and so on. The graphics are beautiful just like the soundtrack and the game is very relaxing since there is nothing that attacks you. You solve small puzzles and find your way by climbing and jumping through the old ruins. Simply amazing and very immersive. Also the climbing and vaulting mechanics work so well, I wish all games would make them so fluent.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the original Submerged so was really happy to see this release. The story flowed very well with lots of places to explore and collectables to hunt. I finished my playthrough on twitch with about 75% of the optional items collected and was happy to see the developer let's you explore the game world after completion to finish your collecting and nab those achievements. This is something all games with tonnes of collectables should do so props to Uppercut for that.The game looks great graphically with relaxing music and good sound design. My only wish is that the games cutscenes had more ambient sound other than just music playing but that is a minor gripe.I only encountered one problem during my playthrough where an item needed to open a path didnt spawn. However after saving and restarting the game the item was in the expected place and I was able to continue. I see this has already been posted in the bug forum so it will likely be resolved in a timely manner.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Submerged: Hidden Depths is a superb non-violent game focusing on the exploration exploits of sister Miku and brother Taku. Interestingly, the enviable athleticism of the characters are reminiscent of the original Tomb Raider; (without the wild animals, trigger-happy humans or deathly falls...). The well-written story line reflects upon the greed of humanity - I won't go any further as I don't want to drop any spoilers. The graphics are also excellent. It was fun exploring the key ruins for the relevant artifacts for the story to progress, though this had to be done with due diligence and perseverance in order to find everything. Lastly, I was surprised that though I had indeed completed its prequel, Submerged, some time ago, I had not written any review - this too, was an excellent game and what prompted me to buy Submerged: Hidden Depths. I must play the prequel again and hence provide a review. In summary, Submerged: Hidden Depths is no less than an outstanding game which I would recommend to anyone with a keen curiosity and some degree of patience re exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: this game was so awesome! i enjoyed the first but this one is a massive glow up. i admire the concept / story line especially in contrast to the first. the side quests were really enjoyable & i appreciate that i always had something interesting to do because i do get bored easily. i really liked the specific collectables, especially the relics for my mini museum. i liked changing my person's style to my liking based on what i picked up. i even liked the home base. had i of known that i could continue playing after the main story-line had come to an end i wouldn't have been so eager to get everything though & probably done the main story before being pedantic about getting everything else. this game is so beautiful & colourful. it's cool how it's set in a completely different time & place with such unique-looking animals. my only critique: this is the second time "multiplayer" has been tagged in a game i was interested in that doesn't actually offer multiplayer so i got hyped to play it with someone. we both got it & right before we planned to play i found out that this wasn't the case. i still would have got it if this wasn't the case, it was just a bit frustrating because i put it off playing even though i was really excited.  luckily the game made up for it pretty quickly. i think they do it to reach more people but games shouldn't do this even if it's the last tag. i think i've learned my lesson this time.edit / after thought: if they ever came out with a third it would be cool if they ever came out with another submerged game that has filtering or boiling water & gathering then harvesting food at the home base. there should be an option to dry food to take with you. they should stick to being combat free but further the survival aspect while remaining a relaxing play (so can't actually die but perhaps need to be taken back to base to recover or just become not so agile. a new environment while sticking to the water theme would be cool. they should actually do a local multiplayer option where someone plays the brother & someone else plays the sister. i think there should be an option to go swimming below the water. keeping the ideas of the story of them & the story of people (secrets), clothing / accessory styles, collectables & some sort of relic (for mini museum) continued would be cool too. lots of colour and plants that glow at night would be great. maybe even a cute alien-looking pet. the idea of having different places to carry out a main quest and side quests should be key as in prior games.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful little gem!If you are looking for action and adventure, this is the wrong game. This is all about exploring and lifting a curse from a submerged land while you're at it. There is no skill needed to play this game, no pressure, no fighting. This game is for people who want to spend some time in a beautiful environment, feeling wonderfully at peace while enjoying the scenery.The characters are adorable, the music is soothing, the environment is gorgeous. If you delight in well-made water in games, get ready for a treat.I don't understand why people are complaining about maneuverability of the boat - you can do a 360° turn on the spot - try not going fullspeed when you want to go around a corner. Besides, if you're trying to complete this game as fast as possible, you're missing the point. This one isn't for speedrunners. This one is for people who want to spend some time in a peaceful environment where nothing will hurt them.If you're stressed out and need a bit of a break from reality, this is a mindsoothing digital holiday spot.I have one criticism to make, though: Whoever committed the abominable design crime of the black on white text should be ashamed of themselves for not doing their job in an otherwise lovingly made game.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: A nice-looking game about exploration and collecting different stuff in the rare setting of a flooded megapolis.It will not provide any challenge at all, so this game would be a good choice for a chill weekend or evening unwinding. There are some problems with optimization - the game will stutter a little bit after loading, at the central hub, and when using spyglass, even on high-end hardware. There are also some missing animations; the game will show you a black screen when doing certain actions, like grappling gates or getting on/off a boat.Despite these minor flaws, the game has given me a couple of pleasantly spent evenings.P.S.A piece of advice. Do not place a seed in the socket if you intend to collect everything there is at the level and haven't done this yet. If you do, you will be automatically transported to the central hub and will have to come back and traverse the location once again to find the missing stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is very similar to the first game which I would call an "On-Rails Climber". The music and the visuals are great even if the gameplay is repetitive. For achievement hunting, you will be able to do everything in one playthrough in about 7-8 hours depending on how careful you are with the puzzles. You might need a guide if you miss a collectable.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: So Submerged: Hidden Depths is definitely an improvement from its prequel. It builds on the mechanics already existing and polished the already established ones.The game is just as fun to explore and is overall a pretty chill experience.However theres a few things that could be better.Facial expressions during cutscenes would have been huge for a better storytelling.Cosmetics for both characters. Felt a bit weird that only one seemed to have any sort of progression.Personally i wish there was less empty space/animals. The sense of loneliness, feeling like i was roaming through a big empty city, were things that made feel a bit creeped out but also intrigued to what might have happen.Overall it was still a fun and relaxing game to play. Kept the charm of the first one and hope to see more projects from the devs
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: A sweet game about a brother and sister looking for a home in a dystopian world stricken with corruption; this game is full of different floras, faunas and cosmetic styles to collect, document and exploring a vast sunken city surmounting a trusty motor boat.The game is beautifully level-designed, as each islands you explore is really fun to traverse and conquer once you reach the goal. I really enjoyed my time playing as both the siblings in a small game restoring the power of nature over malice, listening to heartwarming and soothing soundtracks Submerged: Hidden Depths has offered.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: It's an incredibly gorgeous looking game and plays great, at least from my 22 minutes of playtime, the game really pulls you in!But unfortunately for me, I don't plan to keep the game as the game can't accept any input of any keys from my keyboard or controller, unless I go online, and for a single-player offline game, this is unacceptable... _childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: This is an engaging game, with a great soundtrack and truly lovely visuals. The puzzles are solvable without too much back-tracking (though I'm yet to find two of the collectables - a boat part and a creature).  It is usually very clear where you need to go to be able to complete each ruin / site.  I have enjoyed playing it very much and will be replaying in the future.There are a few negatives, though. - Navigation: A couple of points that shouldn't put players off, but require a tiny bit of persistence and willingness to retry-- There are some sections where it isn't clear where you can go, which form a bit of a blocker. For example, in some ruins, you can cross the water which you cannot do in others. -- There are locations where you need to be a bit more precise in where you go, to ensure you are in the right spot to climb from.to. However, once I started looking at the need for precision as a layer of added challenge, it became part of the game rather than detracting from it.- The story: There is a strong environmental message that is a bit at odds with a game designed as a relaxing exploration puzzle. Like the first game, while ultimately nothing bad happens, there is an increasing sense of tension as you move through the puzzles until the final resolution. (Everyone will have their own views on whether this detracts from the game, or not)/
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Nice story the graphic is quite good, but there are glitches and yes there are areas where you will shuffle around trying to find the area you can walk on, climb on or cling to kind of breaks the flowI also had quite a few instances of the camera suddenly changing the viewing angle abruptly again kind of breaks the flowthe full price is a bit to high get it on sale
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Submerged Hidden Depths is a very nice sequel to Submerged. I thoroughly enjoyed both games. Hidden Depths is beautiful. Every piece of it. The water, the foliage, the flowers, and the art style fits so well in this world. The collectibles are also fun to collect, but they do not pose a hard challenge. The story is as simple as the prequel, but I think that is a good thing for these games. The music is calming as well. The only neutral thing I have about the game is the climbing and platforming is automatic, so there is no input for you to enjoy and mess up. I wish there was more, but it works well enough. The only negative I have is that you can get stuck on a lot of corners while walking. My suggestion is to not cut any corners and take stairs head on. Other than that, this is a fantastic game. I can see why people were upset when it came out at the price point that it did. I suggest this game on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Great chill game. I remember playing it on Stadia prior to its closure. Im glad I got to play and finish this game on Steam. Very atmospheric. No deaths. Open world and the achievements are 100% doable with the guide. There are no missable achievements. The quests are easy to follow and the cosmetic unlocks are easily attainable. Recommended you play with the controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: YEheeees. Really liked this game.Controls are easy and the game is really focused on the exploring and not so much, or not at all, on puzzles. Yes, the game could have been made more challenging, but I really loved the chill exploring pace of the game. Loved the change of scenery when seeds had been replanted. Story was interesting and I really liked how the history unfolded by collecting diaries. Overall fun exploring chill game.Only the music was a little disappointing. Yes it was pretty, but very inconsistant. It would play for a moment and then slowly stop and there were a lot of random silent moments. Apart from that the game was great. Definitely recommend for a chill short exploring game, with no puzzles, combat or any other activity except for climbing and sailing.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: In my two hours of playing this game so far, i hit invisible walls so many times that my face hurts. That's not how open-world exploration adventure game should work.Feels like they did not learn anything new about design after Submerged 1. S2 is extremely linear, puzzles are not even puzzles: put a stone (that's heavier than you character, yet they can carry it with ease) in a specific spot, pull a lever, pull a gate, pull a bridge, etc. Climbing is linear too, a bit of branching for collectibles, but in general there is ony one way of going. Climbable things are obvious due to guide-coloring (you can change guide colors), When you "complete" a landmark you get automatically teleported to base, so if you have any collectibles left there, welp, go back and go around it again. Feels like even devs realised that it's almost impossible to miss collectibles due to game's linearity.And the most frustrating thing is that the world itself doesn't feel lonely or mysterious, they did something to the atmosphere so it feels generic and boring. There was THE MYSTERY in the first game, it was fun and exciting to find new lore, new landmarks, encounter othe *things*. Here, the only true mystery is MC's dreams, but even that feels a bit heavy handed.And those ♥♥♥ invisible walls, there are parts of landmarks that look explorable, you character clearly should be able to get there, they look interesting yet NOPE. Invisible walls galore.Technically it is more advanced game than S1, but for some reason it feels like it a step back.I desperately want to like this game as i legit liked the first one (100%'d it). But alas.The only reason i could recommend Submerged Hidden Depths is if you are researching open-world design, this will be a good example on how not to do it.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Edited to add : since this elevator bug seems to be very unusual, in case anyone else is stuck because of the same problem, here's what I had to do to keep playing. I tried creating a new game but that wasn't enough, there was the same bug in the new game. I deleted my save files manually, deactivated the steam cloud save, reinstalled the game: once I had that blank slate, I was able to start a new game where the elevators worked. Of course this means I lost everything I had already done on my first playthrough, but I was able to complete the game on that new save.--Review:There are bugs that make completing main objectives impossible. (Can't activate some elevators.) Characters also get stuck in terrain, stairs in particular are dangerous traps for them.Considering that 95% of the very simple gameplay in this game is climbing, using stairs and elevators, etc, it's a major issue.Too bad because I loved Submerged and Submerged Hidden Depths is also quite beautiful.

_childDocuments_.review: I was not reading for how gorgeous this game looks. With so many modern games deciding to apply movie filters, being really dark for ambiance or using pixel-art, it´s sometimes easy to forget how good modern graphics look when devs make an ephor to allow the colors to shine. The design itself of the emviorement and the characters can only boost the visuals of the game, and it´s accompanied by fantastic light effects.As for gameplay, this is a pretty child exploration collectathon with a short story that is going for vibes rather than difficulty or complexity.
