_childDocuments_.review: 5/10 the people that tagged this game walking simulator nailed it 3.3 hours to finish the game and i didnt try to speed run it. I was poking around and enjoying everything, the way it looked at least11/10 game looks AMAZING!!!!6/10 music2/10 gameplay wise it is a pile of garbage. no real exploring or free roam outside of sailing aroundNo way to get hurt at all in this game from what i can tellBoat upgrades just give you a little bit more boost timeThe game auto does everything for you…. _childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, story rich sequel to the first game. _childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed, but leaning towards recommending since the game works. Just wish it had more story. Likes/Dislikes lists will be below for a quick read, because apparently I have more to say about the game than I thought I did.Feels like a simpler/smaller version of the Legend of Zelda: Windwaker. If you liked that game (I did), you might like this.I'm someone who is pretty story-focused when it comes to most games, and I just felt like this one's writing was too barebones. There's a few cutscenes and a some dialogue, but not as much as I was expecting. I get that this might be to encourage exploration to find out more about the world and what happened, but just wish the main storyline had more substance.The main characters, the siblings, feel human and flawed, but are also interesting (for what is given). I like the dynamic between them as well.If you're looking for something fast-paced and intense, you will want to pass on this. I personally liked the simpler gameplay, but it does get a bit repetitive after awhile. Thankfully, the main game took me only about 3 1/2 hours to complete, so you don't have to suffer long.There's no combat and you can't really die, so it's a good game to play for people that might not play many games, or just don't want to worry about things while playing.The game shines the most with the environments and being user-friendly. There's waypoints for everything, and climbing only requires you to move the joystick (if you played on a controller). The game also lets you know if you collected everything in the immediate area which is nice as well.Glad I got it on sale and glad I played it, but I probably won't play it again.- Simple gameplay.>> Climbing is easy. After the Uncharted games, I really don't feel like dealing with climbing all the time anymore. - The boat is easy to control.- Good sound design.>> Lots of walking, but the footstep sounds are (for a lack of a better word) satisfying, especially on wooden planks.- Equal respect from the writers between the brother and sister.>> Actual gender equality and not the BS that most media thinks it is? How ground-breaking!- Collecting things.- The animals.- The environments.- Not enough story.- Gameplay gets very repetitive.- No voice acting during cutscenes.- The ending seemed too sudden.- U.I. could be better.>> Subtitles are black text in a white box.>> When you collect writings/books, it takes up quite a bit of your screen for a few seconds.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Charming and whimsical, not the greatest challenge but that's not the point of the game.Lovely detail and interest for those who like to explore and for completists.EdIt: Completed including all achievements (animals required a guide!) in just under nine hours. Will play again fairly soon as it was so enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Submerged: Hidden Depths is a really beautiful post-apocalyptic, adventure game and a great sequel to the first submerged game, okay the story. It has been a few years since the older sister saved her younger brother's life and nearly died from it, but only for her life to be saved by the mass a mysterious entity that is responsible for the world they live in.Now both siblings arrive to the old city of their ancestors a place that was abandoned due to their greed, foolishness and abuse, now the two siblings desperate for a home go to the old city in order to reclaim it and to rewrite the wrongs of their ancestors.Alright then the likes, the story is really good it's a bit bigger than the first game’s story, now I’m not saying the story in that game was bad, it was just a pretty simple story of a sister trying to save her brother, even those we did get snippets of a larger story with collecting all those pages. But here not only do we get to find out what happened to the world and answering questions I had in the first game, I also really enjoyed the story’s themes of growing up, nature and the greed and selfishness of humanity and learning to let yourself get help, I also really enjoy that the story’s world is also told not just through the little pages but visually as well but I'll get to that in the levels, anyway it was all done very well.The gameplay is very good, while it is generally the same as it was in the first game I.E climbing, platforming and getting to the top here it's a bit more flushed out and spectacular, like we're hop from platform to platform, swinging, climbing and sometimes solving some environmental puzzles, I also really like the part where you pick up this magic green ball and as the character walks around, flowers start to sprout from her it reminded me of Okami.Also we're encouraged to do exploration because the pages you pick up that tells the story of the city is scattered throughout the world, not just in one building so it gives incentive to explore like the first game. I also enjoy the fact that we can also play as the brother like there are these mini levels where you can get a picture note and instead of playing as the older sister you get to play as the little brother, it was an interesting concept, although I will say I do wish it was used a bit better but I'll get back to that in the dislike.The graphics are really good better than the first game; they are more vibrant colors and shading that really pops out especially with nature taking over the city. Compare that to the graphics in the first game, they weren't bad but they were more toned down, but here it's all bright and colorful feels more alive more visually stunning compared to the first game’s graphics and colors.The levels are very good, the game is open world but each building you go to acts as a level, just like the first game, but here it's more visually appealing, it's not just some dark greens and browns with a bit of scenery, no here there's all kinds of greens, reds, blues and purples, there are also little encampments showing that people used to live here after the apocalypse and what it was like to live in this place with stairs, pulley elevators and little bedrooms, you really gtt to feel for the place and each level stands out from one another.The two characters are very good I really love their sibling dynamic they play off of each other really well and we find out a little bit more about them as characters like the brother, we really only got to know the sister in the first game but here we get to know the brother a bit and find out that he's caring, strong, quite adventurous and loves his older sister.The music was very good each track was well made and fits the whole game very well. Also the extra bits for the game was good, like the pictures/notes in the first game you can collect pages that basically tell a story through visuals, but here it's improved where if you collect four pictures it actually not only shows you a story but also tells you it. There is also these little shells and flowers in the main levels and if you collect them you can get cosmetic things, like for your boat or your character. There are also these items that you can dredge up from the sea, like an old coffee maker, a camera, typewriter, old toy and old ship items they don't really add anything to the game other than just some fun things to look at and collect.Alright then the dislikes, there are some bugs, but nothing really game breaking and can be fixed with a quick restart. Now as I said we also get to play as a brother, but the problem with that is that the brother’s move set is essentially the same as the sister’s except for one key difference with the girls plant powers, I don't know I feel like there should be some things that the brother can do that the sister can't.Also speaking of plant powers I do wish the girl’s plant powers could do a bit more like maybe creating bridges and stuff out of plants, I don't know maybe all that could be explored in another sequel if there is ever going to be one.Alright then now that I told you all this Submerged: Hidden Depths is a really beautiful post-apocalyptic, adventure game and a great sequel to the first submerged game, with a really good story, really good gameplay and really good graphics, so I recommend this game, especially if you like the first game then you're definitely going to love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, the music was great, gameplay simple but fun and there is plenty to explore and secrets to find. The game initially can appear quite daunting in size but when you get used to the boat mechanics, map and the world layout, exploration is much easier. The game doesn't hold your hand in telling you where to go which means you are free to explore as you wish. The downside to the game really is the lack risk reward other than venturing off the predetermined pathway of each building to possibly find a collectable item, The boat cannot capsize, you cannot be injured and there are no trial error restart sections, however, the intriguing narrative, art direction and general charm of the characters and world perfectly balances to create a fun and relaxing experience, in fact i am impressed in the amount of immersion for such a small dev team. I definitely recommend this game for all ages, perhaps some will find more longevity out of it than others however it is still a worthwhile experience until the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Very beautiful game, with wonderful graphics and music. Fun, relaxing and enjoyable. One of the best I played these last 2 years. Excellent for those who enjoy some easy playthrough without risking all the time of being eaten, chased, falling, dying, hurting, fearing for your life, killing and so on. If you like these things, there are other games for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Very atmospheric, with a nice soundtrack. Although I have gotten snagged on a few pieces of scenery, I was able to free myself without having to close the game. I played the first game quite a while ago, and this one has a very similar feel to it. I would suggest that you play the first game for the backstory, it adds to the immersive quality and gives you a good introduction to the characters and the lore.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece that everyone should try at least once, definitely worth the asking price, one of the most moving experiences you're likely to find in gaming nowadays. If you haven't played the first game, i highly recommend checking that out as well, as this won't really make much sense without playing it, although it can still be played as a standalone experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend this game! First one was a slog and kind of tedious, but this time the game design, being still very constricted for an "open world", has better flow and different mechanics that make the experience more enjoyable. Graphics, animation and music are wonderful. I love the non violent mechanics, but for a game based in the exploration the way you solve the climbing parts doesn't feel organic still. There are even more collectables than in the previous game, being a boomer I didn't care at all for all that junk and it looked tedious to walk back full levels looking for things in the corners while the game limits your movement. Sometimes the extra objects were close to your hand but the restrictive game design forced you to take long detours. A Zelda BOTW approach with total freedom, everything walkable, even in the boat parts could make a third part glorious. The story is... well... terrible. Characters acted overemotional and said weird things and everything ends dope for reasons. The first part story wasn't the big thing, but made more sense. I still recommend the game, it's a short, nice experience and improves the experience of the first one by far,
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and relaxing exploration game. You boat around a post-apocalyptic sunken city climbing the ruins of buildings and collecting things. You can't die and you can't lose. I loved it.I've played the first entry in this series and the developers have improved on every aspect of that game. A postcard feature enables you to take clutter-free screenshots while you play, an innovation I wish other games would implement. The visuals are amazing and the UI is mostly intuitive. I hope the developers make more Submerged games.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and chill game that did the "sequel" thing well.  If you played the first one and enjoyed it, this is for you. Audio & visuals are great; similar mechanics and items to collect with only a few of the collectibles being in areas that had to be hunted for. It also ties in the story and was overall a joy to play for a few hours.If you are looking for a challenge - this aint it. No combat, no difficult puzzles - just a beautiful world to explore and the devs did a great job of rewarding that exploration with bits of the story, skins, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful, atmosferic and captivating, although it's a short, simple and easygoing experience. If you played the first submerged, you will be glad to know that the exploration is expanded, and once you have reached the end of a puzzle (after you get a collectible), developers added shortcuts to the beginning, so there is no unnecesary backtracking.Also, the graphics are phenomenal, they really fleshed out their vision in this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games perfectly made for VR (UEVR mod).   The world, water, effects, everything really beautiful.   Boat is super easy to steer, exploration and understanding of what is going on is very direct, no fear of dying (that I have found yet).  Will definitely be coming back to this.   If The Falconeer and Abzu had a baby, it would be Submerged.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: This is a simple exploration game with a brief story.  If you are looking for something casual, yet captivating, then this is the game for you.  I managed to get about ten hours of game time out of it.  I really enjoyed the first Submerged game and so I decided to try this one out.  I was not disappointed.  Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow, this game had gone under my radar, and I had never heard of it until it popped up on a random game review site as being on sale. I went to check out the store page, and was sold on the absolutely gorgeous water animation.The game really is beautiful to look at, the entire environment has a similar feel throughout, but that doesn't make it any less stunning. The characters themselves are quite nicely done as well, and even though they don't speak, you can tell the subtle emotions they convey through their facial and body expressions. From a visual point of view - this game nailed it for me.The actual gameplay itself is fairly straightforward. You have a boat that you can sail around in, using your telescope to spot points of interest, need to find the "main islands" I suppose you could call them, where you must restore them by returning the seeds to their rightful places. Most of the puzzles are fairly simple, and the segments are fairly linear with collectibles being slightly off the main track (though you can do the islands in any order). But it was still enjoyable to play as a chill experience, so I don't have any complaints there.There are a couple of occasions where you get stuck against an invisible wall, and one time I manage to get myself stuck out of bounds and unable to move back out of it, but that was the only real bug I noticed throughout my time with the game.The collectibles throughout the game are fairly easy to find with your telescope, or using the viewpoints to mark them, the only real difficult ones are the animals, but mostly they can be found by travelling near the main islands. Nothing is missable, as the game opens back up after completing the story and you can revisit any island at any time, which is nice.All in all a nice relaxing experience that I would definitely recommend - especially if you pick it up on a good sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I love games in which you don't have to fight or kill and can just explore. This setting is very  unusual and beautiful. You can speedrun this one in 1-2 hours, or spend 8-10 hours watchin beautiful sunsets, searching for unusual animals or finding out this place's history. Boat is pretty difficult to steer - there're big waves and inertion to consider. Sometimes it adds realism, sometimes it's annoying.Main heroes can - make 2 meter jumps by their hands, while hanging over 100-meter building; drag around stones half their size. Buut they can't step over a rope railing, no no no. )
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Submerged hidden depths is an adventure game that has no enemies and no deaths, it’s a purely exploration game.The world is filled with a black plant and the locals are turned into plants themselves. Miku and her brother are determined to find a way to free the land and the people of the plant curse.Like the first game the story is limited and mainly focuses on exploring and finding items across the flooded world. The game looks great and is much more detailed than the first game. It was a great game from start to finish, and the climbing and movements were improved upon.A great relaxing game 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed this game. It's beautiful yet eerie at the same time. 2 civilizations lost, the one that inhabited the city before the flooding and the one after. You find journal entries along the way that unravel the history of what happened to the second group of people while trying to stop or, in a sense, heal the "black mass".
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful world, compelling if vague story, and simplistic but rewarding exploration mechanics. However like the first game it doesn't really have any replayability. Once you're done platinuming it which will take about 5-7 hours total, there's no real reason to go back aside from the vibes, since nothing changes and there's no alternate paths.It's just more Submerged, and that's fine by me.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't even know that sequel existed! It was first released as a Stadia exclusive, dabbled there for more than a year, then quietly appeared on other platforms. That's why there are so few reviews on Steam.Both this game and its predecessor are very kids-friendly; there is no combat, you can't really fall or hurt yourself in any way. Gameplay-wise it's a third-person walking/boating sim with climbing sections.i greatly enjoyed the setting and story of the first game; it was quaint and fresh. The sequel is basically more of the same, with some improvements. Most of the clunky charm of the original is sadly missing: environments are much prettier and less repetitive, but exploration is severely dumbed down; no more figuring out obscure paths to tiny ledges, no more branching ways, no more eerie emptiness. It's like developers didn't know what else to do with such a simple concept: instead of expanding and iterating, they simplified it even more and filled the world with cosmetic collectibles instead of actual content.Gameplay is almost identical to the first game; you are sailing around the city and climbing sunken buildings. There are new directional sound and visual cues for collectibles and key items, that make finding them even simpler; new wildlife to meet and new story to untangle.Now we have a new multi-leveled hub where all the collectibles go. The hub design is frankly gorgeous; I just wish it was more interactive. The visuals are lovely and significantly improved. The world is brighter, much more detailed and obviously inhabited in that weird diorama-style. The props are sometimes baffling; for example, there are So. Many. Dishes. Everywhere. Former inhabitants were OBSESSED with stacking plates!Character animations are even more fluid and satisfying than in the original game. Now you can control Taku too; you still mostly play as Miku here, but automatically switch to her brother in select locations and for the story purposes. Similar to the first title, all character lines are voiced in a lovely quirky language which sounds like borken English. I mean, you can literally understand it. It's a cute detail, adding to immersion, as if the language has evolved and changed over time. The music is less impressive in this sequel, but still very decent.As with the first game, there are two sub-stories - of the siblings and of the city. While the former is fine and mostly tells us about what happened to them after their previous adventure, the latter is where the devs really dropped the ball. Instead of a tale of a multi-layered apocalypse, we now have what amounts to "hurr durr progress bad" hot take. I suspect it was supposed to be a cautionary tale of overconsumption; if so, it was poorly conveyed. Sometimes you see details which are surprisingly too dark and morbid for this bright sunny world. That one hairdryer in a bathtub full of grime... things like those are a tad too much, and clash with the overall tone of the game.There are performance problems, too. The game mostly runs smooth, but there's intermittent nasty stuttering and frame drops while exploring with the boat (loading chunks of the city? Looks like bad streaming issue). There are also annoying fade to black moments before cutscenes start.Other than that, everything is seamless and quite polished. Recommended for casual and peaceful exploration experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I played and wrote a review for the original Submerged back in 2016, and I have to say that I was very happy when I saw a sequel come out. The original game, though short, felt like a relaxing lore puzzle that I was tasked with putting together. The fact that it lacked combat or a fail state was exactly what my frazzled nerves needed at the time.Seven years later, I purchased the sequel at another time when I could certainly use the mental break. Life is once again more stress for less rewards. But does Hidden Depths hit the same sweet spot that its predecessor did back when I needed it most?I could prettymuch hit the same notes now as I did in my previous review: The game is all about exploration with intuitive parkour. For your efforts, you are rewarded with amazing views of the flooded city and bits of lore to piece together. Only this time around, the Devs have improved upon the old formula. Instead of you piecing together the lore from pictures, each strip of four pictures tells you exactly what happened once they're put together. It's helpful, though a bit disappointing to someone like me who preferred putting my imagination to work.The complaints I had for the first game seem to have been eliminated. The boat controls a lot better this time around. The camera still repositions itself sometimes but not so often as to be a nuisance, and can be easily repositioned when needed. I'm using an Xbox One controller now and haven't had any issues with the character navigating the environment. I also wear glasses now to signify the passage of time.In all seriousness, Hidden Depths is quite similar to the first Submerged, but with a different location and reason for exploration. I won't spoil the ending of the first game, but in this continuation of their travels, the girl and her brother are now trying to heal a city covered in corruption with the hopes of finding a permanent home. The amount of collectibles has been increased but is not unreasonable, and the feature includes customization options for the sister, the boat, and their main base. Once again, the paths up and down the buildings seem fairly linear with only a few deviations for "secret" items. Ultimately, though, you'll end up getting everything if you just pay attention to the map.The price tag seems a bit steep for a game that doesn't appear to be that much longer than the original. However, supporting Devs does often mean paying more than something is worth. I recommend this game to anyone who, like me, doesn't have anymore time in their day for frustration, but greatly desires to see the sights and feel the sense of accomplishment that comes with gaming in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: A former Stadia exclusive, this is a gorgeous and easy exploration platformer and collect-a-thon with an abstractly told, but poignant story. It's more about exploring the environment and has no combat, but it's also chill and an enjoyable place to be in and can provide a good number of hours if you want to grind out all the collectibles. Not for everyone, but I liked it.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice looking and relaxing game, but the best part is how userfriendly it is.Smooth controls, clear level design, skippable animations, I didn't get stuck a single time.[ It's all in all just very pleasant to play. A bit short to buy it at full price, I got it for 2,50 and that was a very good deal.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: the game keep crashing for no good reason.But other than that, the game by itself isn't that bad, except for the fact that there basically no challenge, You can't die, there only one path to follow in big red painted marker and you can't walk outside of it. (like the first one) your brother did keep his scar, but for some reason your arm now have some root on it and flower even grow on it, witch has nothing to do with the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: First, I highly recommend the original Submerged game. Go play it, if you haven't.I can't recommend this follow-up, though. It's clearly been made with care, the graphics are nice, and it plays smoothly. However, it is a bundle of missed opportunities. I want to explain without spoiling the actual content so I'm going to be abstract in case you want to see for yourself.- The core of a story is there but it's not pushed far enough. Because of this, it feels slapped on rather than tightly integrated. What you're supposed to do is obvious but, unlike the original, your motivation for doing it is lacking.- There's an issue of mild mcguffins. You need to find and repeat the same process with many of them, they play a small role in the resolution of the story, but, without the support of good narrative, they just look placed rather than organic.-  The main game-play is platforming but it's all essentially done for you. Everywhere you can go is marked and you don't actually control the jumps. In a game with more going on, this might be welcome but here it just makes the player feel like they don't need to be there. There is already a visual effect in the game that triggers when you get close which could have been used to "reveal" areas where you could jump or climb. - This point goes to the previous two. I'm not suggesting that the game should have integrated the notions of health or damage but could have used failure/restart from checkpoint to add tension (there's none to speak of in the game). The mcguffins could easily have created an environmental hazard. This would have both served narrative and created more interesting game play.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: You get a lot of what you probably expect such as exploration, climbing and looking at beautiful dilapidated world. But if feels like there's less room for exploration. It's more straightforward in it's level design. When I read the title I hoped that it had diving. But doesn't so the title does not make sense.Also I find it weird that the sister got younger and brother older. They also look different. Graphics are improved but it does not add to the game style. It probably even take away the charm that was present in the original.Story seems completely superficial and makes little sense.You'll probably enjoy it if you liked the original. It's not a bad game. Just beware of its shortcomings.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.user: I am the cream of the crop!
_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic sequel that beats the first game in every way. The only thing that annoyed me in the first game was the ugly running animation and here it looks solid. The visuals are really good, the gameplay is simple and there are a lot of collectables. If you like beautiful walking sims and parkour, you will enjoy this.Time to finish: 4,4 hours
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, if you're looking to waste a couple of hours just playing.This game is extremely similar to the first submerged game. So much so, that I was questioning myself at first, if I hadn't already played this game. It's basically the same thing: go out in your boat and look for diary pages, lookout points, upgrades for your boat, relics and seeds to fix the blight that is infecting this water world. The only difference with the first game is maybe some of the graphics and the storyline is progressed a bit more. It's a fun game to play if you're bored on a rainy day. Don't get me wrong: it's beautiful and the puzzles can be fun, but it also gets repetative and after a while I felt like one of those test animals that is made to solve mazes over and over again as part of a laboratory experiment.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice little game and a clear improvement over its predecessor.  The ending was rather anticlimactic and could have used something "extra". For a moment, I was thinking something similar to the game Ico would happen where near the end new gameplay elements are introduced. But that wasn't the case.Apart from that, it's a calming and relaxing game. The exploration could be a bit smoother. Swinging between bars is a bit annoying and activating all the lookouts doesn't reveal every item location. I didn't like that.Nevertheless, I enjoyed it and hope there is a third game in the series that is an equally big step up like this one has.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I've been enjoying Submerged greatly. Great artwork and environment, I like the way the story is told through the collection of pages from books hidden all around. It's an exploration, puzzle, platform, collection game in a 3D environment, so many of my favourite games all in one. It's a very zen game, so if you'd like something to relax to and spend a few free moments on, this will do you nicely.The one question that comes to mind thought that bothers me, and I wonder if it bothers anyone else who's played it, but... am I the only one that is annoyed that the brother doesn't get upgraded costumes when they are unlocked?  Miku gets a new look, even the boat gets a new look, but Taku has to do with his patched up bloomers and no shirt.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Better than the first one, but still a mediocre experience.  I appreciate that it delivers what it sets out to do: give you a simple, easy exploration experience, but the minimal story, lack of dialog, and repetition makes for a dull game.  It's pretty, and at 90% off it is a bargain, but it still is just a so-so game.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very relaxing exploration game. You mostly go around on a boat towards points of interest, uncovering the history of the post-apocalyptic city you're in. It has points of interest where you get off the boat and platform around to find hidden items and books that display what has happened in the past. There are also a lot of things in the water that help improve your boat or creatures to discover. It doesn't have combat. As you play, you will sometimes be the boy or girl, mostly the girl. The girl is all about secret finding so you should be VERY observant when you play as her. The boy's role is very simple and he only needs to find one book and he's done until the next point of interest. At each major point of interest(green orb on map) there is an orb to locate and place in a specific spot in that area. Keep in mind that when you place the orb, you're immediately taken back to the "hub", so be sure to gather all the items before you place it.All in all a very relaxing and fun game for those who like to wander and like the water as I do. If you liked the 1st game, you will love this game. It's a sequel to the 1st but you don't need to play the 1st to know what's going on. You'll just have a deeper appreciation for the characters, that's all. There is no carry-over from the 1st game to this 2nd game.I just bought this gem on hella sale for $3. ENTIRELY WORTH IT!Highly recommend! Enjoy the pretty blue water!
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with this game, the atmosphere was on point. I did find myself reflexively using the wrong controls, which just led to me redoing things, but that was it. Some of the collectibles can be insanely hard to spot, but that was half the fun. I'd definitely suggest this to anyone who enjoys a relaxed atmosphere and not pressure gaming :)
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed the first game in this series - mainly because of its relaxing game play and 'cannot die' element.This sequel is just as soothing - though considerably larger. The graphics are superb - even on "Ultra" settings on my aging GTX 1060. I like the idea of collecting things being optional - you can finish the game without needing to find all the 'hidden' objects (flowers, relics etc.) - or go back to look for them once all the seeds have been restored.I got this 90% off in a Steam sale - at which price it's an absolute bargain.It's not perfect though. There were a couple of times when I got 'stuck' in the scenery, at which point my only option was to quit to the menu and continue straight back in - at which point I was magically 'unstuck'. It was irritating but easily resolved, so not a game-breaker. One design element that I did find very annoying, however, is the way the game takes you back to the start location every time you successfully place a seed - meaning you then have to navigate via the boat to your next destination. This soon becomes tedious (particularly if you were close to where you wanted to go before the game moved you) - even with boat upgrades.Whether the changes in this sequel make it better than the original is open to question - but it's certainly on an equal level.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: This is the urban version of Moana. You and your brother (Maui) go island to island on your boat trying to restore the lands from corruption. You then see the angry monster responsible for everything and ultimately restore the heart of Tafiti and all is saved. Definitely has major Moana vibes but Moana has more action.Having said that its actually a fun game with a small story that is relaxing. Its simple puzzles and no danger. Would spend 3 bucks for this.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and melancholic adventure about two siblings exploring a ruined city in a flooded, post-apocalyptic world. I didn't play the previous Submerged installment, so maybe I missed some lore or backstory about the cataclysm, but the game works well on its own.You have to scale and search buildings, from skyscrapers to industrial complexes, in order to heal the environment and to learn about the city's (and your) fate. The gameplay is easy and relaxing, you don't have to time jumps and you cannot fall; all you have to do is to find your way through ruins (which is also easy since you are helped by visual cues and sounds).Note that despite the title, there are no underwater scenes or missions.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I had initially found the first game on the Nintendo eShop and had no idea that a second game had been released in the meantime.  This game just so happened to come across my recommendations, and this started me playing through the first game again, just so I had more information when I started this one.  This series has definitely found its place on my Favorites list, especially with everything it has to offer.  The storyline of this game is a lot more comprehensive than the last game, which I appreciated.  The previous game had no words or voices, other than the language of the game itself, so a lot of the storyline needed to be interpreted by the player.  This game did have the same language to voice, but this one at least introduced an actual storyline about Miku and Taku in addition to the story of the previous inhabitants of this area.  Going to the voiced language, some of the words did sound vaguely comprehensible when listening to them speak.  While there wasn't as much to interpret in this game, I really appreciated having a storyline to actually read along to.I was super excited to see that the story still followed Miku and Taku, and that Taku had now fully healed from his injury in the first game (albeit with a very noticeable scar).  I was even more ecstatic when he became an actual playable character in the game, switching between him and Miku for the playthrough.  I loved getting to see their relationship change through the game too, getting the backstory before they found the city as you finish each area.  I also appreciated learning more about the people that had lived there prior to the game and the relevance it had to current events.  The soundtrack was similar to the previous game, but I felt it had a lot more depth to it than the previous game.  It didn't feel like the same song looping over and over, which fit a lot better.  This game also had musical tones that helped to find the collectibles, which was fantastic.  With how well hidden some of them were, having that hint definitely made it a lot easier to find all the items.  The gameplay itself was the same as the previous game: you don't have to worry about dying, or taking hits, or falling off of buildings.  You neither gain abilities nor do you need to.  It's a very relaxing game that focuses entirely on exploration and storyline, with the added bonus of looking for the collectibles.  This is a fabulous game to play if you need something to relax to because you get to explore without worrying about much except for missing out on collectibles the first search of a building.  In addition to the musical hints of the collectibles, you also got visual queues, like the water bubbling viscerally in the area with a trinket or the flash and glow of other collectibles in an area.  You also get the glow of the new Animals, the ones produced by the Mass, so it makes it easier to discern some of the underwater creatures.  This has a very easy gameplay that anyone could figure out fairly quickly early on.  Moving on to the achievement sides of things (being an achievement hunter) I love the fact that so many more achievements and items were added into this game that weren't there before.  One of the biggest struggles of the previous game was locating the boat parts and story pages.  Towards the end of the game as I was finishing my achievement hunting, I was getting increasingly more frustrated in not being able to find some of these items, and this game made it a lot easier to find those.  The introduction of the Lookout towers was fantastic because it added some locations into your map, but also gave you a vantage point to find locations for the trinkets, boat parts, and other story pages.  The panoramic view it gave also was beautiful and gave a wonderful view of everything that was nearby.I absolutely loved this game, and I am so glad this made its way to my recommended games page.  It was worth the playthrough and the money for sure, and is certainly going to be one that I end up playing through again.  Highly recommend playing through the first game and this one, just to get the full experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: omg i loved this game. it was like lara croft without weapons, climbing up vines, jumping, handing onto walls.  but you never ever fall or die, something i prefer as it's much more relaxing to play. no shooting, no killing, no dying, nada. the boat navigation was a little annoying at first, but i think that improved as i found a few boat upgrades, and then steering the boat became very fun. just remember you can go backwards with the controller using the LT, left trigger. that got me out of some stuck positions. on that note, i did get the lead characters stuck and unable to move dozens of times. that was bad, and i thought i'd have to give up on the game, but then i realized i could save and restart the game, and i was free to move again. it would be nice to clean that up though. oh, and i read in discussions a clever way to get free from stuck is using the fast travel feature on the map. you auto go to another location and you are free (hold down X button on the controller after clicking on a new location in the map).anyway, great game, very satisfying, absolutely gorgeous graphics, fun animals and birds to find. i'm glad i spent a little more than i usually do on a game to experience this one.  i'm giving this game 5 stars out of 5, not something i do lightly. i strongly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Good: Nice exploration, puzzle, and collection game. Strong guides exist if needed, and can free roam after the main quest is completed to get anything you missed.Bad: No run function on land (and boost in boat is limited even at full upgrades), not even a cosmetic-only jump animation button (even Pirate/Wizard101 have at least that),  no "return to boat" teleport option so if you want to return to the entrance of a current dungeon you have to fast travel away and come back, and the "seeds" (really a misnomer for lack of a better term or better understanding I'd guess) will magically re-plug themselves if you leave before restoring them, which I learned the hard way on my last one.Ugly: No forum (at least at time of post, it's under complete lockdown and no posts can be made by players at all, it doesn't even refer to a Reddit), and IMO the story would've been better if the sister had been the one described as being uncomfortable with the situation and the brother had been the one offering reassurance that she was still herself, cause as-is it comes off indistinguishable from her being basically mind-controlled.Also, remember there is no a combat to speak of. Not even the obvious (by midgame) endgame "boss" is a fight.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Couldn't find one whale and one boat upgrade. Might come back for them. It wouldn't require replaying. The whole game is basically going through mazes (awesome ones) and picking up collectibles and fixing the drowned city while you're at it. Love this game. Amazing world building. Relaxing. Good stuff. Gimme more.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Zelda: The Wind Waker, if the entire game had no combat and was just the sailing part, with those random sunken treasures and those tiny islands that have one or two solitary things to find via platforming. Very simple game, there is no way to jump, fall, "take damage", or really, have any kind of challenge. You are essentially running through mazes, but if the mazes had no dead-ends. But the graphics are pretty, and the audio is lovely.Don't play this if you want anything other than exploration and collectibles.Time taken to 100% achievements: 7 hours
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically the first game with much improved visuals. A peaceful, uplifting collectathon that anyone can play, where nothing will try to kill you and you can't miss a jump. You just sail around, do some climbing puzzles that require literally zero skill, and take in the beautiful post-apocalyptic vistas. It risks feelind kind of boring and repetitive after a while, and the story as you uncover it is rather frivolous and derivative, but at the same time it does not outstay it's welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes it's good to play a game that's 'easy'. In Submerged: Hidden Depths, you can't miss a jump, you can't drown, you can't die. It's about exploration - sailing out across the seascape, amongst the crumbling buildings and ascending a number of beautifully realised climbing frames (skyscrapers and assorted other structures). There's no combat, and although finding every collectable may tax you, a gentle forward motion will see you to the end credits.But that sounds like damning with faint praise - I really enjoyed Submerged: the relaxed pace, the feel of zipping a boat along the water, the satisfaction of the parkour and the ferreting out of hidden objects. You'll already know if the nature of the game appeals - but if that's the case, then rest assured it does what it does well.PS: Also special mention for the imaginary language spoken at points throughout, which I thought was a fun touch as a kind of "English after the apocalypse".
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Nice relaxing adventure, the main thing to take from this game are the visuals, the world and atmosphere. There is not much gameplay to speak about, platforming is simple, you cannot fall down, there is no combat and puzzles are just as simple. But you will be in a place of zen while exploring the world.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little sequel to the original Submerged, pretty much more of the same gameplay (climb buildings to get stuff) with a little more puzzle solving but it's still very light. The story has Miku and Taku exploring a submerged city that is corrupted by a strange black mass, and as they explore they discover the reason and how to cure it through the images and symbols that are revealed (if you did the first game and translated the symbols then you can use them here too, though the only downside is that they do provide an english translation when you find each set of four which somewhat takes the fun out of it - would be nice to have the option to disable that!). It's a enjoyable game to play with lots of picturesque photo opportunities and cool landmarks (and more of the great soundtrack), and I thought the end was pretty worthwhile too. If you liked the original game you'll like this too!
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very chill and allows you to wander around to locate the items needed to restore the world.It has a good story line. No fighting; just exploration and seeking out the items. It follows the same as the previous game, but with a new adventure :)This game is for anyone that enjoys a game without fighting, but something that offers a great story to learn through exploring!
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it a lot more than the first as it is much longer and has way more mechanics and things to collect. It's a great little game and if you were to collect everything, you would be here for quite a while. The length of the first game was around an hour and this can be completed in around 3-4 hours and the aforementioned collectables are also a factor so that could easily add at least another hour on top.It's a fun game, it's very slow paced and has a nice variety of things to see and do. It's like an evolution of the walking simulator and that is by no means a bad thing!
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely qualified recommendation. I actually would NOT recommend for most people, unless you really like relaxing exploration with absolutely no challenge or combat or strategy or crafting or much of anything at all except just collecting a lot of stuff. But as a mindless way to kill a few hours, it has a unique charm that is all about the atmosphere. While there is a lot more stuff to collect in this sequel than there was in the original, I don't really like it as much as the first game. The solitude and mystery of the first game was compelling, despite the shallow gameplay that made it feel more like a technology demo or proof of concept than a fully fleshed out game. This second game adds a lot more embellishment to that shallow gameplay without really making it any deeper. It's not so much about exploration and discovery as simply completing a bunch of lists. And you're no longer alone, and the story is more explicitly explained in ways that detract from it's eerie mystery. But for all that, I feel compelled to experience it nevertheless. It's a unique and fascinating world, just begging for the right author to make it really come to life. I love the idea of game purely about exploration without combat and <shudder> boss fights. But this misses the mark and has essentially become a hidden object game without any puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Fun adventure, with strong atmosphere and sound. Both the first Submerged, and this sequel have had an impressive ability to make me tense and on edge despite knowing there are no threats during gameplay.Personally, I preferred the bioluminescent lichen style of the Mass from the first game more then the floral vine style in this one. It felt more mysteries and unclear whether it was a good or bad thing. Combining that with the lack of readable text or understandable language, the first game felt more like a spooky mystery. But flower vines? Pop culture has us all equating green & Flowers = Good, Black & red glowing = bad. It just felt more black and white, which is less interesting to me. Add in the text explanations for the pictographs, and there’s not much left to speculate about.Still the overgrown city and water graphics are gorgeous. I can totally understand why they added in a postcard mode. This game is built for screenshots.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: My review: good and bad. Overall, I'd say it's great, and if you liked the first one the second one would be enjoyable.The good: improved graphics, improved polish, improved design. This really feels like the devs going a step up in skill from the previous title. Everything is prettier, moving around feels a bit better, I didn't feel as lost trying to find all collectibles in the game, and just the entire game was improved overall from the first one.The bad: ... thus it feels like a more polished iteration of the 1st. Movement is still clunky "go here, do this, you can't actually fail beyond needing to backtrack" stuff, which disappointed me at first before I accepted this was only slightly improved from the first title, because the better animations made me feel like this could've been a more free-form parkour system. Instead it's game 1 mechanics again but the animations and graphics are better, and some 101 puzzle elements of "push button, retrieve block, do something here to open a later path" implemented.Overall: I'd say it's good, but I can imagine scenarios easily where it'd be hard to recommend: would be hard to recommend as a series, as people would be better off just playing the new one, and I imagine there would be plenty of people dissuaded by the lack of "new" to the game. It's improved, but nothing is especially new to it, beyond very simple puzzling mechanics that didn't really improve the experience from the first game, and maybe a couple cosmetic story-related things that change as you progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: so I found out a little too late that this is a sequel, so Im just finishing this then going to play the first one. But I have had trouble finding a decent solo game to capture me and pull me in. I've been on a multiplayer only kick and this game has me in its grip. The visuals, the music, the gameplay. All so simplistic yet beautiful, very good game to sit down and relax with or start your day on. HIGHLY recommend, whether you played the first one or not. Use the steam summer sale as a chance to grab both.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game!  I loved Submerged, too!  Just: yum.  I waited until there was a sale as the price tag, while totally worth it, was still just a little high for me in general.  But I'm so happy I finally have this game.The environment is exquisite and the attention to detail in the imagery is amazing;  the beautiful accuracy in how everything  naturally "moves" is astounding, as well.  Both games in this franchise are stunning.  I will add that I like that I can't fall off a ledge or miss a jump - that can make a game that's tagged as "relaxing" a lot less relaxing, for me.  There's plenty of challenge finding ways around, discovering, getting out of an area you somehow got yourself into - always knowing you'll find a way, or if you have to, you can get out by "transporting" somewhere else.  There are a lot of new features compared to the first game, both in the game play and storyline, all of which I think work well.The  addition of different "styles" is fun, too.  So long as make up and nail polish and mousse don't enter the picture...!  I consider this and Submerged to be among my favorite games of all time.  And I was around when Myst first came out and I've played a LOT of games since then, so that's saying a lot!I'm not finished my first go 'round yet - I'm taking it slow and really exploring.  Like with the first game, I know I'll be replaying this one just for the exploring fun and beauty of it.  I recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed the first game and picked this one up as soon as I finished it. It has improved on everything in the first one and added a bit more variety. The environments are more interesting to explore, being able to see beneath the surface of the water was great, the added puzzles that weren't too difficult and a variety of collectibles made me keep playing until I 100%ed it. It even made me go back to the first one to appreciate the drawings and the story of what had happened and finish 100%ing that one as well.Very peaceful enjoyable experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: This is Myst for a new generation.  Stunning visuals, enchanting lore, stirring music, and loads of content across multiple island environments and even on the open sea will totally captivate players and keep them playing for many hours.  Intuitive controls. no combat, and visual puzzle design make this a joy for kids and parents alike.  Fun for the entire family!Watch the first hour of gameplay at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: OKAY so after thinking on giving this game a good review because besides the frustrating sailing and a couple of glitches I was enjoying it so far and I truly like it BUT I was just one seed away to finish the game when my boat got stucked in a building and there was no way of fixing it so I had to start my game all over again and that's just so wrong I can't give this a good review. Watch out if you decided to buy it because even tho is sure a game with so much potential the development is obviously controversial.  I still would recommend it as in playability/story since I truly love but yeah.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: A nice small game.  Like a novella or a palette cleanser.  My life is plenty busy and I don't have much energy for serious gaming.  Submerged HD was great for me.  A low-stress visit to a beautiful world.  A little pathos, and some exploring.  Some light parkour without any real stakes (you can't fall and getting lost is fairly difficult).  Good for a spin.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a fan of platformers or 3rd person games, but this one, and the first (Submerged) ... well, you have to play! It's not a traditional platformer. You will have to find your own pathing and that can be tricky sometimes. It's apocalyptic, but still family friendly. A game to play at your own pace, or to take a break from games with violence and destruction.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Both of the Submerged games are perfect examples of game design as an art form. Know upfront that they are non-combat, exploration games with light puzzle elements. You cannot die in either game and there are no time limits to worry about. Hidden Depths improves on the first game in every way, such as quality of life changes (more things show up on the in-game compass, you can fast travel between more points on the map) and the environments and music are simply beautiful. Your "home base" is much larger, and there are more collectables such as flowers and artifacts you can use to decorate your home, skins for your boat and I think even skins for the characters (I haven't unlocked any of them yet but I see them in the menus). If you enjoyed the first game, this one should be an immediate purchase. I hope the devs keep them coming. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: 100% completed in a bit over 8 hours. It was one of the best 8 hour gaming experiences I have had. The game is beautiful, and the exploration feels organic. The soundtrack is where this game really shines. Do yourself a favor and play the game with surround sound. Collectables, quest objectives and basically everything in this game have their own sound effects, which are projected in 3D space. It is extremely satisfying to collect things, as all of it is displayed in the hub area as you collect it. So over time you create a home for the kids you play as. Cannot recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful adventure. Stunning visuals. Interesting storyline. Lots to explore in this stunningly gorgeous waterworld. Easy controls with KB/M. Even with my 2+ yr old desktop PC (albeit with a strong video card), the game, with all grfx options set to max and set to 60 FPS, this game is very well-optimized and, as mentioned, looks absolutely breathtaking. Pleasant music background, too. As someone online noted: this game is "relax-ploration" at its best.Worth every penny. I've only fully explored perhaps three areas in the game so far and cannot WAIT to explore the rest of the submerged areas. Do not wait to buy this beautiful game.-----Edited to add: I finally experienced what some others have also experienced: very quick, slight hiccups when using the boat on the water. Only happened twice to me, and these were practically instantaneous. But for the sake of honesty I thought I should include this in my review.---Updated in 2023: finished this gorgeous game over a year ago. Still enjoy fast-traveling from place to place or sailing around on the waves. Great game to play to waste some time once you've finished it, as well. Still recommend this game wholeheartedly.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: I actually really liked the world of Submerged, the water was fancy, the individual locations were nicely designed as well. The climbing and switch puzzles made of vines, ladders, switches, bridges, etc. were interesting, sometimes even challenging. Many puzzles are quite different from island to island, though they did have repetitive elements in them over time.The level design wasn’t boring yet because of this, but I did wish for more surprises and more unique features here and there. So I kind of see this area with a laughing and a crying eye. So it’s more like mixed, but still in the upper range.The story behind the game develops quite slowly. There is a great mystery, but it takes quite a few hours before this starts to unfold and for my taste, this was a little too lacking in involvement. The tension is rather gentle. Okay, the developers want to put relaxation and release in the foreground, but at least in the story area, this could have used a little more energy.The relaxedness in the design of Submerged Hidden Depths is a double-edged sword, occasionally one wants a little more action or a little more surprises and dramatic twists. And should you fire up the game when you’re already a bit exhausted or even tired, it can easily become so relaxing at times that it makes you even more tired and want to go to bed. Submerged 2 is more like a yoga game here, it can relax and bring inner peace, but sometimes it can be a little exhausting.Enough grumbling, because all in all Submerged 2 offers a nice, unique concept. It clearly stands out from the usual action mush. And it’s quite pleasant to play such a peaceful and cozy game. But the balancing act between relaxed and boring is difficult and certainly not suitable for all kinds of players. And if you have to search some places 2-3 times to find everything, it becomes sometimes rather frustrating than funny.I definitely had fun in Submerged: Hidden Depths. I enjoyed it and I think I will finish playing it as well. However, I can only play the game for 1-2 hours at a time and then I personally feel like picking up something else, something with more story and action.For the price of about 25 euros or dollars, Submerged: Hidden Depths offers a special experience, relaxation, and cozy gameplay. It is technically well implemented, looks pretty, and offers exploration puzzles that stimulate the brain. Unfortunately, in some areas, the balance between relaxing and lame is very much on the fence.I would like to give this mix a basic rating of 75%. For minor problems with the dubbing of the cutscenes and the annoyance factor with the unwanted backporting, I subtract 2%. However, both can probably still be fixed easily.For the courage of the developers to go with their “Relaxploration” a completely unique approach, there is a 5% bonus from me again on top. This brings me to a final rating of 78%.And clearly, if you can’t stand to be without action, drama, and danger, then this game is not for you. But if you are looking forward to a calm and relaxed exploration, then you will get a beautiful world here.EN DE
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

_childDocuments_.review: Boat, climb, interact and explore in the beautiful ruins of a sunken world.
_childDocuments_.name: Submerged: Hidden Depths

name: Thirsty Suitors
detailed_description: Battle Your Exes. Disappoint Your Parents. Find Yourself. The year is 199X. The power fantasy is BEING A ROMANTIC TRASHFIRE IN HUMAN FORM. The final boss? Your TERRIFYING GRANDMOTHER. It's about to get MESSY. Outerloop Games presents Thirsty Suitors - a stylish, chaotic, heartfelt interactive drama about first loves, family, friendship and forgiveness. It will make you laugh. It will make you cry. It will make you want to text that one ex... Yes. You know the one. Confront your hot but toxic exes in spicy fully-voiced PSYCHODRAMA BATTLES. Reveal your messy break-ups through NARRATIVE COMBAT mechanics which put a new twist on the turn-based RPG. Taunt opponents to discover their emotional weaknesses, and exploit them! Enrage, shock and impress your exes, or flirt with them to throw them off… Try to win your parents' approval and AVOID EMOTIONAL TRAPS in over-the-top cooking segments full of delicious South Asian recipes. Skate, grind and wall-run away your COMPLICATED FEELINGS. Find yourself as you return home to the small town of Timber Hills - full of gossiping aunties, parental expectations and the consequences of your past mistakes. As JALA - choose to be a HEARTBREAKER, STAR or BOHEMIAN - your THIRSTSONA affects your combat build and shapes narrative outcomes. Each battle in Thirsty Suitors is a chance for growth and reconciliation - but how you get there? That's up to you.

_childDocuments_.review:
From Outerloop Games comes Thirsty Suitors - a game about culture, relationships, family pressures, and expressing oneself.

Can Jala handle her demanding parents, reconcile with her exes, and mend broken friendships in time for her sister's wedding? Will she be ready for the impending visit of Paati, the family's terrifying and judgmental matriarch?

Through the game's story, Jala will confront her exes in cinematic, turn-based battle sequences.

name: FLOW
detailed_description: Check This Out!!! About the Game WARNING / Developer Warning: FLOW is not a fully fleshed-out project, and is on Steam for Archival Purposes. With that being said: This is a SHORT exploration game. Please go into this game expecting to spend your time exploring. This game is an exploration game that explores dark themes. You will need to interpret the text in the game to your own degree. With that being said this game is more of an art than an interactive experience and we hope you enjoy. Wake up in the shoes of Flo, a 19-year-old, and explore a strange and wonderful world. You can only access this strange world through Flo's nonfunctional computer. The more you explore, the more of the truth behind the world you will find... but be wary: You only have 1 Week to find out what's really going on! FLOW, at its core, is an exploration psychological horror game. You go behind the scenes of Flo's mind. This gives the game a very bleak and foreboding atmosphere. Explore a mysterious world filled with brightly colored enemies, and discover a forgotten history by navigating through the lively and mundane. CREDITS: Dallen Larson / Adam Helquist / jijigri / Lucas Ferreira

With an embedded design of DDA (dynamic difficulty adjustment), players with differing skill levels can intuitively customize their game experience and enjoy the game at their own pace. [SCEA]

name: The Star Named EOS
detailed_description: Follow the stars, to where the past and future cross paths. The Star Named EOS is a story-rich puzzle adventure built around photography. Explore a beautiful hand-drawn world as you photograph some of the most precious yet fleeting moments in life. As you recreate photos from the past, you will slowly uncover the truth of a family mystery, and the love hidden within fragmented memories will eventually become clear. As the young photographer Dei, the player sets off on a journey following in the footsteps of his absent mother. When he was a young child, Dei received letters from his mother on her travels. They always included a beautiful picture of places she visited. But one day, Dei notices something strange in the photos that threatens to overturn everything he's ever believed in. With the guidance of his mother's voice ringing from deep within his heart, he takes the first step on a journey to discover the truth of his mother's absence... Experience a harmonious mixture of beautiful hand-drawn art and engaging puzzles as you embark on a journey of reminiscence. By recreating old photos left to Dei, uncover a long-forgotten truth about the past. A fully-voiced experience to fully immerse you in the world of The Star Named EOS. Interact with a beautiful hand-drawn world. Enjoy highly detailed panoramic scenery. Discover puzzles and items hidden in the panoramic scenery Uncover the truth with engaging puzzles that tickle your brain just enough.
about_the_game: Follow the stars, to where the past and future cross paths. The Star Named EOS is a story-rich puzzle adventure built around photography. Explore a beautiful hand-drawn world as you photograph some of the most precious yet fleeting moments in life. As you recreate photos from the past, you will slowly uncover the truth of a family mystery, and the love hidden within fragmented memories will eventually become clear. As the young photographer Dei, the player sets off on a journey following in the footsteps of his absent mother. When he was a young child, Dei received letters from his mother on her travels. They always included a beautiful picture of places she visited. But one day, Dei notices something strange in the photos that threatens to overturn everything he's ever believed in. With the guidance of his mother's voice ringing from deep within his heart, he takes the first step on a journey to discover the truth of his mother's absence... Experience a harmonious mixture of beautiful hand-drawn art and engaging puzzles as you embark on a journey of reminiscence. By recreating old photos left to Dei, uncover a long-forgotten truth about the past. A fully-voiced experience to fully immerse you in the world of The Star Named EOS. Interact with a beautiful hand-drawn world. Enjoy highly detailed panoramic scenery. Discover puzzles and items hidden in the panoramic scenery Uncover the truth with engaging puzzles that tickle your brain just enough.
short_description: The Star Named EOS is a story-rich puzzle adventure built around photography. Recreate compositions of past photos to uncover the truth of a family mystery. Experience a harmonious mixture of beautiful hand-drawn art and engaging puzzles on a journey of reminiscence.

_childDocuments_.review: Pass-time game, puzzle, graphic adventure, well-curated story, emotions, hand-drawn.Dei is a talented young photographer, but something is missing from his memories in his life: he wonders what happened to his mother who disappeared during her travels.Determined to fill this hole, he rereads the letters he received as a child and looks at the photos of the places he visited.He embarks on a long journey in the footsteps of his missing mother, guided by her imaginary voice, he will discover the truth and how much love he felt for his beloved son.Beautiful, deep plot full of emotions accompanied by an evocative soundtrack, capable of making us identify with the protagonist.Ideal for those who love searching for landscapes and photographic details, we can zoom, move and find the fleeting moment to create artful photos, as many as we want up to 80.The gameplay is based on focusing on certain objects that have memories for Gods and overcoming the puzzles; the clues are scattered throughout the location, sometimes it is easy while other puzzles are more difficult.The graphics are wonderful handmade, they envelop us with their sweet colors and seem to convey to us the sweetness and tenderness of Dei's mother.If you like to dedicate yourself to collecting, in each location take a good look at all the objects: there are 3 hidden stickers, use the camera, zoom in and take a photo, it will be placed in a special album of memories.I recommend a well-made product, rich in art, creativity, which will involve not only the mind with the puzzles. but also the heart with positive emotions.Must try!
_childDocuments_.name: The Star Named EOS

_childDocuments_.review: From the creators of Behind The Frame, a game centered around painting.. comes The Star Named EOS, a game focused on photography. While the game only takes around 2-4 hours (depending on you solve the puzzles), the story is both touching and bittersweet, The art style looks quite the same with Behind The Frame, and now features voiceovers in English, Japanese (日本語), and Chinese (中文), adding depth to the experience. I play with 日本語 VO and it was a legit deadass.It took me 3 hours because I got stuck on a puzzle that I didn't fully paid attention to and this doesn't include unlocking all the achievements. However, I really loved the puzzles. Some were easy and some were challenging but not frustating. And you will use the camera to solve certain puzzles. I also appreciated the small details in this game, such as how the background picture changes to match the chapter theme when you return to the main menu. Also, they put some easter eggs from their previous game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Star Named EOS

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because I loved the feel about it, the design and the story. I also bought the game because most of the player feedback said that the puzzles are not that hard. So I (female 59 years) and my husband (73 years) sat there for long periods of time, tried to click whatever we could, and had no clue how to solve the puzzles. If you have very little to no experience with this kind of games (I usually play survival, simulator and city builder games) those puzzles are HARD. Also, I'm not very thorough and most often don't see things. Having to scan every tiny corner feels tedious to me. So most probably this game is not for me. Though I hate to write a negative review I felt I need to add it for others like me who don't have much experience with games like this. The puzzles are only easy for those who are experienced.
