_childDocuments_.review: I really want to give this game a good review. I love the survival crafting genre, but there are A LOT of improvements that have to be made to make this game more enjoyable. But let's start with what I DID like. (Keep in mind that I'm a pretty casual gamer, so complaints about difficulty may be less warranted.)PROS:-The music is nice. It's relaxing when it needs to be, and epic when it needs to be. Fitting all around.-Collectibles make the game more interesting to play, and there are more incentives to explore.-The weapons are pretty cool so far. -Most of the boss fights are pretty fun. Ghorm gave me quite a spook when I first saw it, not gonna lie.-I love the durability system. You don't have to toss out an item that breaks, you can just repair it at a station! No wasted materials here!-The concept of an ancient underground energy as a plot point is very interesting. Can't wait to see where it goes.-Overall very cute concept with a solid art style.CONS:-PLEASE do not make me craft ten thousand tiers of crafting tables. It's a pain in the butt to have to hunt down materials to upgrade. Wood, tin, iron, scarlet, it literally never stops. I have two rooms in my base dedicated ONLY TO CRAFTING STATIONS. It's utterly asinine. Other survival games like Minecraft and Terraria tend to leave three main crafting stations for common items like weapons, tools, and armor. Maybe a few extras for things like potions and magic items. -The grinding is exhausting. ESPECIALLY when you have bosses that require items to summon them. Namely one of the titans in the Early Access. You need ten pieces each of four different ores that require you to explore different biomes on opposite sides of the map. It's a chore. Straight up not enjoyable.-Some of the enemies are ridiculously overpowered, even when you have the best armor and weapons available. -Some of the bosses are enemy spam/bullet hell. Please don't.EXTREMELY FRUSTRATING:-Supposedly a softcore character does not lose items upon death... Uh, they do. your ENTIRE INVENTORY OUTSIDE YOUR HOTBAR is lost and you have to retrieve it. No. Just no.-Boss items take a ridiculous amount of ore to make. Some of which, RNJesus does not make it easy to find. It should not take 45 pieces of ore to craft a freaking egg. Some games such as Terraria only require five of a particular item, maybe ten of another. And such items are much easier to find. SUGGESTIONS:-Game rules such as keep inventory--hunting down your items after you die is a pain in the ass when you die on the very edge of the map and have to make a LONG trek just to retrieve them. -Game difficulty settings--I am a pretty casual gamer so if you intend to make the game this difficult I'd very much like to play on baby mode.-Tone down the enemy spawn rate during boss fights.-Consider nerfing the titans a tiny bit.  Their fights don't need to be that hard.OVERALL:Early access is literal hell. I'm optimistic about the full release. I understand Early Access is just testing your demographic and receiving feedback on how to improve. Hope my review helped. Because as it currently is, Core Keeper makes me want to fold my monitor twelve times. Unfortunately had to request a refund. I will consider buying it back once the full release is out, IF some suggestions are honored.

It is absolutely phenomenal.----------I almost didn't buy the game because it is in Early Access. I'm so glad I did though. It has been a month and I've put 115 hours into the game and I'm not stopping there.The game has a lot of similarities with many of the other survival-crafter games out there, but has so much to offer. _childDocuments_.review: Core Keeper is a solid sandbox exploration game.The gameplay loop is similar to that of Terraria: explore the current biome, gather the ore there, make equipment from it and kill the boss or bosses for the area.  Then you repeat that process for each new area you encounter.The base of this game is good but it needs more meat.  They have done a good job filling the world with neat stuff to find but most of it isn't too interesting yet.  I want to see more armor sets, weapons and usable equipment.  Giving certain weapon types a charge attack was a great idea.  I hope they'll give every weapon type something like that.The game isn't perfect though.  The skill tree is a cool idea, but some of the choices you have just aren't worth taking.  They're either too situational or have such a low activation chance they're never worth taking over the other option.  I hope once the map is done the developers will rebalance the skill tree so that all the choices are fun and interesting.The other nitpick I have lies with how difficult it is to find the game's special one-off locations.   The gameworld is very large so finding certain special places without using the wiki and/or tools the community has made is down to dumb luck.  The game is kind enough to offer locators for most of the bosses so I'd like to see something similar for each biome's special locations.  I like discovering cool optional stuff in games but I don't like having to play "find the needle in the giant haystack" multiple times to unlock the coolest stuff in the game.Is the game worth $16?  If you like this kind of game, definitely.  The average length of a playthrough (ie killing all bosses) takes about 50 hours.  Patches during early access have been substantial with the developers delivering what's promised on the road map.   I am interested to see what else the developer plans to add once we reach the end of the current road map because given proper polish and additional loot to collect I can see this game becoming very good.

_childDocuments_.review: The progression of the game is very confusing at first but once you beat the first three main bosses and get past the wall this game is fantastic. I found myself comparing this game to terraria quite a bit initially but now that I've played more of it, it is an entirely different game with it's own unique mechanics. that being said, i'd say it's much more difficult than terraria, pretty much no matter how much progress you make it feels as though you're never truly safe while exploring new areas. The biggest downside of this game in my opinion is probably the lack of unique weapons and equipment, there's only a handful of items for each "class" in the game which is a negative in my opinion because, to me one of the most exciting things whilst playing a game like this is getting fun new items to use at each stage of the game and furthermore having a variety of different items to choose from based on your play-style. perhaps the worst of this is summoning because there are only  3 summon weapons in the entire game and the only real difference between them is their attack mechanics they all fundamentally do the same amount of dps and only exceed or fall short of each other in specific scenarios. Regardless I think this game is a great addition to the open world survival craft genre and I'd recommend purchasing if you are looking for something fresh with a fairly high level of difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game but there are just way too many features that only exist to annoy you and waste your time. For some ungodly reason this game has durability, it's not even that hard to repair tools, it just exists to force you to make long treks back to your base to repair your stuff or you sacrifice ~3 inventory spaces of your already overflowing inventory to carry the repair bench, scrap parts, and bars. This wouldn't be bad if it had a teleportation system like Terraria, but if it does exist, you unlock it way too late into the game for me to have ever seen it.Aside from durability the game is just in general boring. Every enemy feels the same of either: thing that melees you, or thing that shoot you from a distance. Maybe it gets better later game but every time I make it past the bosses of the first 3 zones, I lose all motivation because the game turns into a grindy slop where you spend a long time just mining to find the resources you need or the items you want. Far too many of the good weapons, armors, rings, etc. are enemy drops or found in special rare structures. In my most recent playthrough I wanted to go ranger so obviously you get the ranger armor right? Wrong, this set and far too many other items in the game aren't craftable. The first set of class armor can only be obtained as random drops from boxes or enemies. I found plenty of mage and summoner armor but it took hours to even find a second piece of the ranger armor, by that time I gave up and just beat the first boss without it. These class sets drop from the first boss so I expected to just get the final pieces from refighting it but I would find out after that that hope was near impossible.Another place where the game lacks is bosses. Many important class items can only be obtained from bosses, if you come from Terraria you may not bat an eye because you just just refight the bosses until you get the item you want, right? Nope, the only way to resummon early bosses is to buy the summon item from a merchant, these summon items aren't cheap. You won't be able to afford fighting them many more times before you need to give up because you're broke and lack the item you wanted. Considering that most of these items have a less than 10% chance to drop, the barrier to refighting it disgustingly high.In the end I just can't recommend this game. When I first played it when it came out the grindy aspects were expected, but after 2 years of updates nothing has improved and the game is still the same boring grindfest it was in the past. If you want to try an top down Terraria style game, Necesse is 1000 time better.

_childDocuments_.review: Aquatic titan is not a well designed boss if all it does is spit an ungodly number of tornadoes at you that suck you toward them, limiting movement thus making it so you can't outmaneuver them easily if at all, and then get three shot with no hope of recovering using healing items. 'Course this is as a single player mage with a max level pet, fairly decent stats grinded out, and gear that is supposed to be at level with this boss rather than overcompensating by venturing into arguably more dangerous areas that are sequentially after this boss. Lest I'm missing something, it's a new and unhinged mechanic to have to resist bullet hazards sucking you in. And if they're stacked up or you get combo'd because you didn't react fast enough to falling into one and getting pulled into others, GG you die with no hope of healing. And if this is only a midgame boss? I actively shudder to think what the end game bosses are going to do.Everything else is a well done and a fairly well constructed experience up to this point, yet it feels awful to keep dying to the same boss and then have to grind out the materials you need to resummon it because it killed you. It's not the only boss that does this, had I perished to two of the required bosses before this I'd have to resummon them as well. Only the first two bosses, Glurch and Ghorm, and a couple of optionals so far, the larvae queen and the toxic slime, don't require an item to summon them or to rematch if you die on the first fight. The toxic slime actually required a bit of thinking because healing in its arena is off the table and the slime slows you down, but that's surmountable. Having to grind out materials for a rematch? That will always feel awful. I know the ever comparable Terraria does that too and it's not excusable there either.So either bosses need rebalancing or after they've been successfully summoned once you need to be able to refight it without expending more resources. Provided the expended resources are difficult or otherwise time consuming to acquire.Core Keeper can do so much better than this.

_childDocuments_.review: I found that this game had a lot of grinding and a slow item progression system, which was fine for the most part. However, I had a problem with the gameplay between the third boss and the fourth boss. If the developer doesn't rework this section of the game, I think a lot of players will stop playing after beating the third boss. The issue is that the gameplay between these two bosses is just not as enjoyable as it could be, and it can be frustrating for players who are trying to progress through the game. Additionally, I found the character job feature to be largely useless, despite the fact that it grants additional skill points and items at the beginning. This is because it requires five skill points to unlock new abilities, regardless of your character's job. This means that you'll need to grind for skill points in order to unlock new abilities, which can be tedious and time-consuming. One potential solution to this issue is to adjust the skill point requirements based on the character's job. For example, a miner character might require three skill points for the mining skill and four skill points for the running skill, while a cook or gardener character might require six or seven skill points for those skills. This would allow players to specialize in certain areas and make the progression system feel more balanced and fair. If the skill point requirements are the same for every job, you will eventually reach the same level of progression as other players, which can make the game feel less unique and rewarding. It could also enhance the experience of playing with other people, as players could choose different jobs and work together to progress through the game. I would recommend that the developer consider implementing this change in order to improve the overall gameplay experience. Despite these issues, the sense of accomplishment that comes with slowly working your way up and unlocking new items may still make the game enjoyable for some players. Keep in mind that this game is still in early access, so there may be additional updates and changes in the future. Overall, if you enjoy games that require a lot of grinding and have a slow item progression system, this game might be worth giving a try.

_childDocuments_.review: My overall thoughts: Great game, simplified progression compared to other survival craft games, very chill and emphasizes teamwork in terms of resource gathering in multiplayer, a must buy for fans of Terraria.This, however, is a review of the updates the game has gotten since I last played in early 2023:TLDR for the 1.0 update they added new classes, mage integrating old items into itself, and warlock adding completely new items. However, the mage class suffers from these old items not changing enough, the warlock class just doesn't have enough items at all.•Upgrade TableThe progression has been reworked to use an upgrade table to keep whatever gear you want viable up to end game, its a system I love since it lets you play with whatever weapons you want, but it feels like I should be able to make this table at the start of the game as opposed to mid game. I'll bring this up again for the warlock class where it hurts the most.•New magic system and classMagic staves are now their own class instead of being ranged weapons, The issue with this is that not enough impactful magic gear has been added to the game, and the few staves that used to be rare sidegrades to guns and bows are now their own class and thus everyone needs them to upgrade magic - the loot tables are not built for this, you will need to a boss for hours to get 3 players staves, an issue we have not run into with any other weapon class. This will also be revisited in warlock class.•New warlock classA new type of weapons called summoning tomes have been added along with gear and class. The issue with these is in that they only have 3 tomes compared to magic's 7 staves or any other classes' 20-ish weapons. The first tome you get is pitiful, equipment can only help so much when the weapon does terrible base damage. You get this tome in the first 10 minutes this is the ONLY tome for the entirety of the early game, or about 10 hours. This means if you're a pure warlock, you will deal the least damage on your pure build team and by the time you can make the weapon suck less with the upgrade table, you can also just go get the other 2 tomes. So you are given a choice: Do you want play it safe and grind for hours to upgrade your starter weapon that you've already spent a third of the game using? Or do you want to play the slots and hope you get a lucky drop for either of the two other tomes before eventually upgrading them? THESE ONLY OPTIONS FOR THE ENTIRE GAME, THERE IS NO WAY TO CRAFT ANY WARLOCK GEAR OR WEAPONS. Now, what was I yapping about warlocks in the magic section for? Well, if you want to be a warlock but don't care about mixing and matching, you will gravitate towards staves since a lot of warlock gear also gives you magic damage, which means a mage and a warlock will HAVE to grind bosses for staves - something that is still balanced in loot tables as a rare novelty item as opposed to a core weapon.TLDR for the 1.0 update they added new classes, one integrating old items into itself, and the other adding new items. However, one class suffers from these old items not changing enough the other just doesn't have enough items at all.Now obviously I still love the game and highly recommend it, but I'm very disappointed that the new features in the "1.0 full release update" are clearly incomplete and will need "version 1.1" or "version 2.0" just to make them actually fit in the game.Let me know if you disagree with anything, I wanted to get my thoughts out there while they're hot, but I've only made it to the ocean so far and haven't heavily used the upgrade table, though I do love the concept and expect to love upgrading my items.

XP is earned per action performed (IE, mining blocks is +1 xp gained, same withing melee, fishing,... etc). There is no colony sim management, but there are NPC merchants that spawn the same way they do in terraria. Speaking of which, the game is filled with many easter eggs and references to other popular indie survival games such as terraria and deep rock galactic (not sure if DRG counts as indie). Nostalgic 16-24 bit visuals, ambient BGM, and impressive ray tracing (shimmering water is a little too blinding in large open space, take caution here). Highly recommend for what it's worth, game has immense potential comparable to minecraft's earlier days.

_childDocuments_.review: Before buying this game, I saw many people comparing it to the legendary games of Terraria, Stardew Valley, and Minecraft. having played all three of those games, my friend and I decided to give this game a chance, and sadly, we were disappointed.The game lacks charm. The soundtracks of Terraria, Stardew, and Minecraft immediately hook you, their aesthetics are wholly unique and have personality, but Corekeeper feels bland. The environments don't feel compelling or interesting like Terraria, the art style doesn't compare to the uniqueness of Stardew, and there is no early expression of creativity like Minecraft.In the early game, combat is very boring. Whereas in Terraria spacing, knockback, and the mechanics of weapons are essential to the combat loop (even with the copper sword you start with), Corekeeper's enemies are incredibly easy to dodge and boil down to just spamming left click with no flair. Progression is very meh. My friend and I found tons of copper in the starting biome with the occasional gold/tin, but we didn't know where to go to get more, better ore. Whereas in Terraria and Minecraft, the progression is clear to the player after finding better stuff mostly when digging downward, or like Stardew's community center where there is a clear goal to chase (with a compelling reason: to restore it to its former glory).Anyways, whoever compares this game to Terraria or Stardew Valley is smoking good zaza, because this game doesn't hold a candle to it. Go play those games instead if you haven't already, and if you have, this game will likely disappoint you.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: Highly recommend to anyone who enjoys Minecraft, Terraria, Stardew Valley, or other mining/ exploration/ base-building games! Good for casual and challenge-driven players alike, even in the exact same world!Later game 4-player Co-Op does tend to lag a bit sometimes as of 12-28-2022, but hopefully the devs of this early-access game are working on optimization.Very fun game! The Good:The Co-op multiplayer is perfect for a small group to hop in and out of anyone's active game. The Skills encourage players to specialize and benefit from each other, which allows the more casual players to safely chill at the base while more adventurous players can challenge enemies or find cool things to bring back! Even the chill skills like Gardening and Fishing give players unique combat powers that will have the more combat focused people BEGGING the gardener to come help them with the next big boss!Single-Player gamers will still have a ton to do without feeling held back by lack of diverse skills from multiple players. Everything is doable at skill level 1 so long as you can get the proper equipment or technique down.Bosses are still challenging, and preparation and planning are very much rewarded. The world is BIG and different with every playthrough, with scenes and enemies mostly unique to each different biome. Difficulty scales at a very nice pace as you progress, new resources are fun and new and useful, and GOOD LUCK exploring every nook and cranny! I'm still finding new things in the beginning Dirt biome after all this wild exploring and 4 bosses defeated!I find myself comparing this game to Minecraft all the time, and in that way Core Keeper simply removes a ton of the headache-inducing Minecraft aspects. Light levels only help you see, as enemies spawn from removable and replaceable floor tiles. Minecarts are FAST and DON'T collide with people going opposite directions! Tools can ALWAYS be repaired. Players have a map and mini-map built-into their GUI. Chunk loading is not a thing in Core Keeper, your farm will keep growing and drills will keep drilling no matter how far away any player is. Death is very forgiving; players respawn with their equipped armor/accessories and hotbar, and the rest of your inventory is placed into a conveniently marked tombstone that restores your items EXACTLY as they were (so long as nothing new is occupying that slot). Biggest perk for me is that NOTHING despawns! I left a giant mushroom lying on a tunnel floor 2 hours into the game, and went and picked it right back up around hour 40!The Bad:While the game encourages base building and putting down lots of torches, it seems like even with graphic settings turned lower on a moderately powerful PC, if 4-player co-op is running, lag gets to be an issue around mid-game. My group suspects that all of the flickering torch animations, growing vegetables, farmed mob spawns, and different decorations all in one place are what's causing the major lag issues. Restarting the host world and re-joining helped a bit.We have attempted removing torches and limiting mob farming to only slimes with some success on reducing lag. Hopefully program optimization is a high priority for the developers, but Core Keeper is still in Early Access so only time will tell. When playing on single-player or working away from the base in co-op, the game runs pretty dang smoothly. It's specially smooth when your game is still limited to the first three major biomes.Overall: GREAT game! Ton of Fun! Maybe try to get by with fewer torches than you want to reduce lag, but otherwise the game runs pretty well on even older/ weak PCs.

_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Corekeeper is really cute and fun. It is similar to Terraria in terms of progression with the angled top down view of Stardew. Each person can choose a "background" for their character that gives them specialized items and boosts to certain skills early on which is a really cool idea. That doesn't mean, however that people are stuck with just the activities they specialize in. You can level up any skill and do whatever you want, allowing for total freedom. When my friends and I all downloaded it, we pulled an all-nighter accidentally because it was just that fun. I'm very excited to see where they go with this game!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a brilliant example on how polish makes a product shine above others. _childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Core Keeper has a pretty fun gameplay loop of collecting, building, repairing, kind of like Minecraft. It's less open than Minecraft though with objectives to complete and areas to unlock. I think I'd prefer a game closer to Minecraft in this style, but Core Keeper's combat is more fun. I found myself wasting hours playing...digging...collecting...building...but then I sold my PC and it was refreshing to stop playing. If they ever release an update to support Mac, I'll probably check it out again, but for now I've had enough of the repetitive gameplay loop.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun game that's beautifully crafted and a lot of fun to play. Also the multiplayer stability is really hit and miss, and the method of joining another players game doesn't make any sense. Entering a random case sensitive code with a fairly hard to read font is annoying enough, but then to top that off the code doesn't always work, often requiring the game to be restarted to get things working again. Sometimes multiplayer games can be stable for a few hours, other times (more often that not it seems) the network issues are unbearable, kicking you off every few minutes. These issues seem to persist both over internet and with LAN. It's a shame because it's otherwise a good game. I might have even recommended it if it didn't kick you out of an offline game for some "Lost Network" bug or whatever it said. Just enraging.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a buyer beware video game purchase!Game Review:After spending almost 30 hours on the game; the game offers barely anything interesting to keep you hooked after the initial tutorial of the sand box area. Whether you are playing alone or with friends; the game punishes you for staying on a single task for too long, whether it be building, adventuring, or farming materials; you are constantly being nudged to do something else whether than just having the option or freedom to do what you want with ease.By nudging I mean: - If you fail to keep your hunger in check, the debuff will lower your health far enough that even the easiest of monsters will be able to kill you regardless of armor. Your hunger bar burns quite fast to the point that even the free mushrooms you gather to cook; will not be enough. Forcing you to build a farm as fast as possible. However... by the time you do manage this; the hunger bar's demand is greater than what you can produce. To make matters worse, the skill tree you are offered is painfully slow and to unlock the hunger-control talents; you need to spend well over 5 hours just farming and planting; which anyone would find boring even in co-op.- Should you decide to AFK for any reason due to real life reasons that grabs your attention; apparently "hunting parties" as I was told will spawn and kill you on the spot. While death has no repercussions when playing on normal mode other than walking back to collect your stuff; this deteriorates the incentive of playing the game over time as you get further and deeper into the game.The game also fails to explain on what is considered a "punishment" and what isn't; much less hint it. I didn't find out until later from the community discord for this game; that having "Zero" food energy for your character and your farm animals; would not kill you; even on "Perm death" mode. Making half the talent tree, cooking, and farming; almost completely pointless that it never justifies the grind required for it. The crafting system is also just "bare bones". You are pretty much stuck with the basics of what is required for PvE combat but when it comes to "Building/decor" its laughable on how limited your customization is. Which is to be expect for a 2D environment but you'll soon end up running a bunch of "mods" from other players just to fill that missing gap.How... any of the previous game reviews said that this game is a "fresh" approach to heighten survival; is a bold face lie. There is no punishment in dying. The only thing this game offers is just constant running back & forth to grab materials, crafting tons of food, and burning tons of hours trying to level up a horrible skill tree; just to access tougher bosses.Speaking of bosses, the combat system pretty much has a very unbalanced progression. Once you get past the three tutorial bosses; side bosses and end game bosses pretty much become a "job" in trying to solo and as you get further & deeper into the game; the developers have set up the difficulty bar to be done in such a way that you are flat out punished for not having any friends or just playing with others. Making the replay value nearly non-existent as the game ages.The traveling system is terrible, if you die; you have to use a minecart system you made to travel back to your corpse. Depending how far you've traveled out; it could take over 10 minutes to reach your death stone. You can create a "bed" to make the respawn less painful but... should you want to travel out from your base; well... there is no quick short cuts.Too make matters worse... the community formed with this game is extremely toxic. If you make any mistakes or try to compare the game with previous gaming knowledge on how to tackle this so-called "survival" game; you are constantly told that you are not to compare previous gaming experience to this one as its considered unfair in expecting a working game to function as intended based on common sense. Suggestions made to improve this game or "quality of life" ideas; are met with ridicule and disdain. You are often hazed to the idea that you are considered "Stupid" for not looking at a cheat sheet or guides on how to play the game dismissing any real reason to approach this blindly or as a veteran gaming player.In conclusion:Due to how shallow & empty the game offers in content via sandbox; you grow extremely bored after the first six hours of gameplay. You are often told to use "mods" from other players to improve the game's experience but... seeing the store demands 16-18 dollars based on your purchase area; doesn't justify the developer's lack of depth in providing content after so many years has passed. Regardless if this listed as an "indie game"; its plain and clear the game is designed to be a quick "Cash grab".If you spend more than $5 on this game, you've been tricked.

_childDocuments_.review: Core Keeper seems as if mechanics from multiple other well-known and mostly successful games were put together, without really having grasped what made those other games successful and fun to many people. It has mining, fishing, farming, exploration, survival, crafting and much more, but most mechanics feel like they were just implemented to check them off a checklist without really integrating them with each other to create something new and interesting. Some mechanics even make the game feel overly tedious, such as the infinite, dynamically generated game world, which calls for extensive and regular travelling in combination with the sheer amount of semi-useful stuff to pick up while exploring and the comparatively limited and uncomfortable inventory and storage handling.Instead of including more gameplay mechanics from other games, the developers might be better off taking a look at gameplay refinements the other games received over the years. Maybe those refinements were put in place for good reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming open world RPG not too dissimilar to Terraria and its clones but from top down perspective which i far prefer.+ Progression is intuitive and easy even without any map markers or anything else. Its done really well here.+ Bosses are fun and difficulty seems well balanced even though i have to say as a ranged character you will have much easier time with some of them.+ Combat is interesting, how weapons, magic, barriers etc. work is all done very well.+ If you like building bases you will love this game. There is so much decoration and options its actually amazing. + Great and varied visuals. Tilesets are interesting and shaders look pretty cool.+ Weapons and other gear are varied and interesting. Every tier brings more to the table and they have unique abilities and set bonuses.+ Exploration is solid, i especially liked how tiered it was and there was some thought put into it.+ Overall this is a solid Terraria like RPG/exploration/building/crafting game i can easily recommend.+ Pricing is fair, takes about 30 hours to beat if you dont focus much on decoration and building. + Music is excellent.+ Co op works well and was the main draw for me. A lot of fun with friends.+ Classes are cool, i liked summoner and ranged combat the most. Leveling is easy to understand and never gets in your way.- Weapon selection could be better for some classes. There is heavy focus on melee, decent ranged variety but summoners only get three tomes which you dont even need to find and have no idea about if you dont check wiki.- Traders in this game suck. They never sell anything really interesting like cool armours or weapons.- Story is bog basic and theres not much to it.- Definitely has a lot less content than Terraria has. Maybe 1/3? While there are some drawbacks i think this is a great game especially in co op. I liked how chill it was, never took too much effort to do anything and most importantly it never felt like it dragged.

_childDocuments_.review: Core Keeper is an absolute gem in the world of indie games, offering a refreshing blend of exploration, survival, and crafting that keeps you hooked from the very start. The game masterfully combines the charm of pixel art with deep and engaging mechanics that cater to both casual players and hardcore survival enthusiasts. One of the most impressive aspects of Core Keeper is its expansive, procedurally generated world. Each new playthrough feels unique, with vast underground caverns filled with secrets, resources, and dangerous creatures. The sense of discovery is constant, as you dig deeper into the unknown, uncovering hidden biomes and ancient relics that add to the game’s rich lore. The crafting system is another highlight, offering a wide array of tools, weapons, and structures that you can create to enhance your survival experience. Whether you’re building the perfect base or forging powerful equipment to take on formidable bosses, the game provides a satisfying sense of progression and accomplishment. Multiplayer support is seamlessly integrated, allowing you to team up with friends to explore and conquer the depths together. The cooperative gameplay adds a new layer of strategy and fun, making it an ideal experience for groups.

_childDocuments_.review: 40 hrs so far and for the most part, Ive really had a good time. I do feel like the game suffers from an identity crisis. Does it want to be an open world survival like Minecraft, something casual like Stardew Valley, or more of a Boss a Rush type of game?The postive thing ia that you get a little bit of all 3, but the negative is that you have to deal with game mechanics that intentionally slow you down.Example, Trying to farm Wool, but you can only do it every 10 real time minutes. Bosses that have a cooldown before they respawn. Or farming for the 3 upgrade materials, Emearld,Ruby, and Sapphire which take forever without a Mob spawner. If you can look past the obnoxious grind for materials, I think youll enjoy your stay here. Alot of these materials arent necessary until later in the game depending on how fast you push into the next zone.Boss are cool. Lots of sets and diversities. The upgrade station allows all early gear to stay relevant if one choose to upgrade them. Looking forward to future updates. _childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely bare bones at the moment and I keep seeing comparisons to Terraria/Minecraft/Stardew, but I'm just not seeing it. This game doesn't have the challenge of Terraria at release, because there's no real danger in the game until the outer ring, and that gets minimized very quickly. The bosses so far are very easy to cheese and get confused when more than one player is involved. There's no immediate threat like in Minecraft Indev 0.31 so you have no drive to do anything. Why make an enclosed area when there's no threat. Just plop a work bench down anywhere, any threat can be easily mitigated by just ripping up the spawning grounds. Even in 0.31, you had drive to stop enemies from spawning which lead you to getting wood and coal for torches. There's also nothing creative to do other than set up a rail system to reach the outer areas. The perspective keeps you from making anything interesting. There are no castles to design, no cottages to build, and I don't see people being able to make art like in both Terraria and Minecraft.Food is currently directionless, unlike in Stardew at release. There's no reason to even experiment because just filling your hunger is enough of a benefit. There's also no economy like in Stardew because the NPCs don't do anything other than sell things you can easily get yourself, boss summons, or a blueprint for a weapon. Those summons are pointless too. Why would I re-fight a boss for rarer gear when there's no threat? You might get slightly more damage output, damage mitigation, or a minor special effect, but currently those are not necessary and they won't ever be necessary if they continue with the same game play loop.The only reason I'm doing this comparison is the shear amount of people constantly bringing up all three of those games. I've seen people stating "don't you remember these games at launch?" Yes, yes I do, other than Minecraft, they were released as completed games. There was a lot you could do in Terraria at launch, and Stardew was a fully completed game at launch.Core Keeper could be a really good game later on, but there is a lot of work to do, and people constantly bringing up the "the big three" of this genre are not helping anyone. It's annoying at best and disrespectful at worse.

_childDocuments_.review: Core Keeper is a decent game, but it doesn't really stand out in any way. The story is almost non-existent. The crafting system is ok, but doesn't coordinate as well as it could. For example, farm animals provide one type of good. You don't typically need many of these goods and they don't really coordinate into something more complex. While early game ores let you build a large number of tools and buildings, the later ones are much more limited. Crafting stations could've been combined or upgradable to save space too.The gameplay is decent overall. I don't feel like the fighting is a strong point, but it's not a bad one either. You get several options for playstyles, though some can feel a lot weaker or stronger unless you've really optimized your gear. Most gear is found by RNG though as the craftable options are quite limited. So you might need a wiki and patience to find what you need.The late game started to feel tedious to me. Lots of wandering hoping that whatever material I needed would eventually drop - and the world wasn't interesting enough to make the grind fun. It'd probably be better in a group though. Also, many bosses require spending resource to create an item to fight them. If you die, you need the item again. I prefer boss fights where you don't have to waste a bunch of time just to have the right to fight them again.Overall, it's a fine game if you've got time to kill or don't mind grinding, but it's not amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: I heartily recommend this game. After 88 hours and beating all bosses, it definitely scratches that Terraria itch. The graphics are gorgeous, the music is fantastic, the gameplay is solid, and the progression is interesting. It is not perfect by any stretch of the imagination, but as a 1.0 project that seems to be taking a page from Terraria's playbook, it has a VERY exciting future. Unlike some games that I wait after release to "let it cook" because they aren't finished, Core Keeper is a completed game, with tons of content, but with lots of room to grow. It will be fun to return to this game after some updates, DLCs, etc. and see how the game develops. I'm looking forward to it.

_childDocuments_.review: I would say this game is a mixture of 70% Stardew Valley and 30% Terraria.The game takes a lot of inspiration from both games but it fails to develop its own identity.You have the cute pixel art style and the progression through the different ores to upgrade your weapons and armor.There arent any tutorials or npcs ( at least i didnt find any in 1 hour of playtime) who tell you what to do or where to go.Being a sandbox game with little to no help for the player can work if there is good visual storytelling or an ingame encyclopedia but the little text over items are not very helpful. I also dont think that the gameplay loop works very well for this game because nobody played Stardew Valley and thought that the gameplay in the caves was interesting or very enjoyable. Stardew Valley is successful because it has a great story and good npcs. The success of these games does not depend on the gameplay but heavily on its story. In this department the game is lacking a lot.I dont think this is worth checking out at least at this stage. If the combat gets an overhaul and there is a lot of new stuff added to the game it might be worth looking into but at this stage the game just feels very generic and boring with very obvious inspirations. The performance is also very questionable for a game that has a pixel look. I put some stuff in my base and had like 30 plants and my fps went under 60.

_childDocuments_.review: Wish Steam had a "meh" option. For an early access game, it's not the most offensive thing out there, but it's so freaking generic that it kind of hurts. _childDocuments_.review: The game is entertaining for a while, but it has bugs that need to be fixed--but haven't been fixed for ages. FPS is terrible even at low settings--using tons of GPU intensive effects for a pixelated graphics style is dumb. 'Cattle' do not respawn, so if one of them glitches through a fence and goes missing (a known bug), you'll have to create a new world and start it over. Gold exists but has very limited use. Fishing is a pain and becomes tedious very quickly. Sad to see a game with so much potential turn into another early access money grab with no consistent follow-through. The whole point of early access purchases is to help developers fund the game, but the developers are selling merch now which indicates that they are just milking profits and relying on influencers. Best to save your cash until you start seeing consistent updates.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fine game. People like it. I'm just not one of them. Consider this review a drop in the bucket.This game is a management nightmare. You end up with 30 different tables/anvils/crafters that all have some unique crafts that you always end up needing. There is no centralization. The ability to draw items out of adjacent chests while crafting is brutally undercut by the waking nightmare of organizing this mess. Minecraft and Terraria showed how to manage this a decade ago. Make a crafting menu bigger than a 2x6 grid. Make tables include the contents lower in the tree.The having the map open while travelling feels mandatory due to the zoom and scope of the world. That is fine. You can not interact or attack while running with the map open. Explored areas have no transparency options. An almost good idea that fell on its face.You need to craft four tables and setup a generator to power a lumber mill... to make a plank of wood. One plank per 10 seconds. 40 planks for a special map table. You need this table just to know the currently explored map. This is a terrible. A living hell when playing multiplayer. When you have people screaming their heads off about getting jumped by a dozen miners, and they are a mile into the unknown... Either turn this feature ON or OFF for the server. Gate keeping it is terrible.The game is fine. It is a fine 2012 game. It looks great. It has a lot of character and unique designs. I have played dozens of early access survival crafting games. The fundamentals are rough in a way that will never be addressed. Technology scope will increase. You will get more mechanics and tables. If the above does not bother you, then the game is up your alley.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game. Did not finish every side boss but completed the main story. It wasn't a rush but I avoided grinding as much as possible. I think there is a little balancing between the classes and the grind is a little tedious but you can clear the game in hard with most of your skills far below max level (Think my highest was 65/100). The graphics are good, boss fights are interesting, and POI's make the maps memorable. That being said the biomes are a bit too large for me (Perhaps options for a small world or the like), end-game boss locators take a little too long to grind for, durability is too small for the HP pools (might be a hard issue), and skill exp is a bit steep (though again this isn't the most impact). Overall as a base it is a fun game, and with updates and mods, it can go from a good game to a great one.TLDR: Good Biomes, Bosses, Mechanics, but needs some QOL and is a bit grindy esp. towards the end game.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: It really hurts to rate this down, but I'm pretty disappointed by how my time playing this shaped up.To get some things out of the way:First, this game is gorgeous. The art, both visual and audio are incredible. The design is seriously immaculate. I really love the vibes this game offers.Second, it is really addicting until it isn't. It grabbed me in a very similar way Terarria did, which is both positive and negative in my review.The thing is, this game is obviously inspired by and clearly pays homage to the titanic product that is Terraria. So I cannot but compare the game to Terraria, and that is where the problem lies. Terarria is a game that is GREAT solo, and is EXCELLENT with friends. This game shapes out to be incredibly boring solo, and I can't say how it plays with friends, but I imagine it is much better.Here's the problem, the grind to progress is absurdly boring, absurdly long, and there is barely a feeling of movement along the way. Getting through the basic early game bosses was fun. Like Terraria, it hit that feeling of exploration while also offering a fair few items to play with and see which way you'd want to play. Unlike Terarria, after you get into "Hard Mode" the game grinds to an absolute complete and utter halt. You are presented with MASSIVE biomes that are so incredibly large, that your only way to locate the boss is grinding out arbitrary boss locator icons, which is miserable solo.What's worse, is that you also need to grind out the item that summons the boss.What's worse, is that by the time you've done all of the above, 90% of the items the boss will drop are world drops that are common to the biome. Killing bosses in this game is actually pointless most of the time beyond the fact it progresses the story. After spending 30 hours getting to the sea titan, I had not received one build defining drop. Not one. Every single drop that did define my build was a duplicate I had already acquired from a basic enemy. In Terarria, every single boss drops items that can define or improve a build. Every single one.This would be something I could potentially overlook if the itemization in this game wasn't so boring though. There is no point in the game where basic tier white items with a single stat aren't still dropping. In fact, said Sea Titan, the 8th boss I had fought, dropped one. Beyond the obvious question of why a boss is dropping single stat items, why are they even a thing in the game past the first ten hours?There are a lot more smaller, annoying aspects that bugged me (insane mob density, map size, no feeling of ever clearing a map, bizarre overly complex generation, boring boss fights, copy pasted boss fights) but I don't want to make the review longer than it already is.Point is, just play Terarria. It's a better value, and it's a better time regardless of your friend count. It respects your time, always has a sense of exploration, and the content is simply just more enjoyable. If you're bored of vanilla Terarria, and think this will scratch the itch, just play the Cataclysm mod.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with a lot of content even in early access, I liked digging around and finding big open caves to explore, even though there wasn't exactly anything to find. Some of the bosses were pretty difficult with the gear I had at the time but I never struggled to the point of frustration, I just felt like I had to prepare a little more and then I could beat it. Most of the skills level up as you play, and most of the perks you can unlock are useful and worth working towards.The only thing I would complain about is the fishing, it's not particularly fun and is tedious to level up.

_childDocuments_.review: Terraria's exploration had Starbound, and now Stardew Valley's mining has Core Keeper.Core Keeper is a very unremarkable (though initially somewhat charming) caving game. You mine. You make tools with stronger ores. You keep mining. Maybe you build a little house somewhere. You start a farm to feed yourself. It just keeps going.From the player perspective, the game feels very uninspired, and there's not much to keep you going. I've spent nearly a day's worth of time playing this game, and I don't have much for it - armor and tools with higher numbers and different colors, and more enemies with higher numbers and different colors.It's a soulless process, and I recommend you neither pay money for it nor spend your precious time on this planet playing it. Spend time with your loved ones instead, because unlike samey mining simulators, they won't be around forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: I have never reviewed a game on steam as I am selfish for my own time, but I believe you seriously need to have a warning before you decide to start this game. I recommend you check the wiki to fact-check my information if you do not believe me, or look for videos.I have played it for 45 hours. We started as 4 and ended the game being 2 as we wanted to "complete" it.I did not enjoy the experience: many people here describe the game as a survival/craft game similar to Terraria / Minecraft / Don't Starve.This game is nothing like the aboves: it is empty in its core.Combat is uninteresting with very limited movesets. All weapons pretty much do the same thing.There are only 3 different summoner weapons in this game.There are only 7 mage weapons in this game.Melee patterns are the exact same, all the time. The same spear/axe/sword you find early game will have the exact same pattern late game.Coop experience is flawed: the only way to upgrade health permanently in this game is to consume almost-unique items found randomly in biomes or very late through boss fights drops and fishing.There are 8 in the game. (I am excluding the christmas-specific item)4 are biome specific, so you could not obtain them twice, meaning only one person in your coop could have the increase. In our world, we only found 2 of them as well as they are tied to biomes in game. The biomes are extremely large and you do not need to explore them entirely (would take a while and ressource-wise not necessary)There is a slime boss in the game early on that has only one attack pattern: a jump towards you.You will encounter a reskin of this boss 4 times in the game, and the pattern is always the same: a jump towards you + one unique pattern per slime reskin.Other bosses are pretty bland: the Shaman is probably their best boss design.The titans are going to be very disappointing: each titan has the same pattern as the last one with one additional clone.On hard difficulty, you will die from regular mobs attacks post early game in one hit. This may be tied to the fact we did not have the chance to get many health upgrades.This does not make the game challenging though: it makes it really tedious to play.Food cooking / farming experience is not fun, but necessary to do in order to have stats buffs (movespeed/damage) or any form of health regen if you have the chance to survive a hit from an enemy.I would seriously recommend checking out the skill tree to understand what kind of game this is: the "skills" are ALL passives and are extremely boring. They are a % increase to a stat or a chance to proc an effect that gives you a %increase to a stat. Unlocking a skill is not exciting in any way.Overall, the mining & exploring core loop is not very fun or interesting as there is not much to discover by exploring: the weapons upgrades are the same things with higher values (+dmg).There a lots of "cosmetic" biomes found without interesting loot/chests/rewards, which is probably what attracts some people in this game. For a sandbox aspect, I would much rather play modded minecraft or Stardew Valley as a cosy game rather than this.I still do not understand why and how it was allowed that cosmetic items like herbs are destroyed by our attacks on mobs. Whilst exploring, there is so much inventory clutter createdPlease make sure to put a timer when you start the game to ensure you can have it refunded after you play it a bit. What you experience at the beginning doesn't improve but fades more and more through the rest of the playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is really fun for the first few bossesas soon as you get to "hardmode" after the great wall you just do the terraria ore progression over and over againthe bosses are alright but the combat is just too flat to really feel satisfyingthe constant need to farm resources and manage your food level gets annoying quicklymagic weapons are just ranged weapons without unlimited ammo (mana is an issue) + the tradeoff of losing armor for magic barrier is just not worth itthere is currently only THREE summoning weapons and EIGHT mage weapons in the gameendgame bosses are really tedious to find and their scanners are fairly expensivethe concept of durability is just stupid in this game. it literally costs almost nothing to repair your tools and gear so you might as well just remove that system entirely and just keep the reinforcement systemportals should not have a cooldown.the skill trees are way too tedious to levelenough whining here are some prosthe game is fairly self explanatory, you dont need a wiki to play through it allautomation feels satisfying aesthetically the game looks really good, great boss designs visuallycustomizeable world gen loot tablesnot a lot of guidance allows for exploration and surprise ambience is really cosy and chill music

_childDocuments_.review: A friend of mine who knows I like this kind of game (Terraria, Crea, etc) got this for me. The idea of turning Terraria into a top down, semi isometric dungeon crawl is pretty cool. The beginning is easy enough. Dig around, make stuff, dig and make stuff. Things start to get annoying once you have made all the normal copper and wood stuff. Then you realize that tin is super short of supply. (of the 300 or so ore I found 9 were tin, the rest were gold and copper. Gold isn't useful until much later.) Finding enough tin to make the upgrade table is just not a fun process. You will probably end up running into mobs that you can't handle despite full copper armor. You might even run into a super slime (I managed to avoid that but jeez that thing is huge). The nth time dying to a series of mobs that are too hard to fight (one had many hundreds of health, another had nearly as much.)  was enough to chill my enjoyment of the game.I would definitely sideways thumb this if there was an option for it, despite my own misgivings. If you love Terraria you will play this and recognize similarities. You might enjoy it. It certainly was fun for a few hours before the grind set in. And I do respect that the game is by a small developer house, not some gigantic AAA producer.The graphics are fairly awful btw. I don't love pixel graphics in general but Terraria's definitely is the way to do it. More antialias, less fuzzy lines would make it a lot less ugly. That said, graphics are typically the least important aspect of the game unless they interfere with the game play and they don't here so I would not base my no on that. Just a note that you might or might not like them. Overall: buy it if you have a fondness for survival crafting games. Be aware that combat is twitchy and not well tuned to be fun. And it seems like there are game balance issues, especially with creature difficulty vs resource availability/tech upgrades. The lack of a ranged weapon option at the beginning is especially egregious as it somewhat leaves out the ability to kite enemies. I'd give it a 4 out of 10 stars with a definite eye on improvement over time since it is still Early Access.

_childDocuments_.review: Once you start, it's very hard to stop playing, very addicting and lots of to do but doesn't tell you what to do and lets you explore on your own pace.Relaxing, grinding (not too much and this is configurable), fighting bosses, looting, pets(!), crafting, fishing, cooking, farming, herding, it has it all.Multiple classes to start from, but you can switch when ever you want or use multiple classes to combine your own fighting style.Same kind of game like Necesse but deeper and better imo.Whole heartedly I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't bad but I can't recommend it until it's at least out of early access and the automation system is actually fleshed out.What makes these kinds of games fun to me is the automation systems that the player will unlock and figure out throughout the game. The problem is the electrical system used for automation doesn't have much to it yet, and in some cases if you try to use it you get punished for it. There's a leveling system in this game, but it takes far too long to level up skills. I have a little over 100 hours at the time of writing this and only 72/100 levels in farming.I tried to use the automation system to automate my garden, but there is no way to automate planting or watering which takes a long time. Harvesting can be automated but then it won't count towards leveling your skills that already level far too slowly AND you won't benefit from any perks the skills would give you.At this time the game is like playing Stardew without sprinklers or upgraded watering cans. Or like playing Minecraft where the only things red stone can do is open doors. It's not bad, until you get to the late game and feel like you don't have anything to show for it except a fancier sword.

_childDocuments_.review: I've dumped so much time into this game, it's roped me in and I can't escape.My first impressions based on the name alone was that Core Keeper was a mixed procedurally generated dungeon crawler, tower defense style game. I regret to say I judged a book by it's cover.Akin to Terraria, Core Keeper takes a boss-centric, mining-and-exploration heavy approach to progression and didn't miss the mark when making procedurally generated worlds fun to BE in. Core Keeper, on it's launch, also already rivals Terraria in terms of customizable character progression AND cosmetics. It has a unique upgrade system, making gear relevant even into the end-game akin to, but further developed and integrated, than Starbound. Some might even compare elements of these systems to Stardew Valley. In particular, the leveling system rewards you within skill trees related to your various tasks, which may be grind heavy at times. But, this is more than made up for by it being so gratifying to have multiple viable options to choose from in not only a multitude of skills, but ways to play the game. It has an absolutely eye catching art style, which although maybe said too often about pixel graphics games, is completely true here. It's simple, but highly polished and refined. Core Keeper is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good. If you like things like Terraria, Stardew Valley, Starbound, even Minecraft, you should get it.The main focus is on combat, but there's a decent variety of build options and non-combat activities that can each help you get stronger in their own ways. I haven't played multiplayer yet, but it seems like that's where the game would really shine. The graphics are nice without being too demanding, I've had very few glitches, and I think I'm about halfway through at ~52 hours. I probably could have beaten it in 20, but I like just exploring and farming and such. There's also an in-game mod manager that I haven't really checked out.There are kind of two unofficial class systems in the game, and each person could play their own specific build. Outside of combat, you might focus on fishing, farming, crafting, building, exploration, and/or automation, all of which are helpful to the whole group in their own ways. In combat, you can focus on melee, ranged weapons, summons or magic (or a mix of whatever you like). In single-player, I've been taking my time and exploring each of the non-combat systems (except automation, but I'll get there).The biggest disappointment so far has been the lack of weapon variety for a summoner/mage playstyle. In 50+ hours, I've found 3 simple summons and 5 staffs that shoot some kind of ball that does damage on contact. I guess those classes were added really late into early access, so hopefully they get more love but we'll see. I haven't played melee or ranged yet, but the weapons I've found seem to have a bit more going on. The problem is that I've played a lot of Terraria, and the weapon variety there blows this game out of the water. It's probably not fair to compare a game that's been getting updates for 10+ years to one that just came out of early access, but it's still something I've found lacking.My other issue might be a limitation of the top-down, grid-based style, but some of the biomes get pretty samey after a bit. There are a ton of handcrafted 'scenes' scattered around, many of which are really cool. The space in between is often completely indistinguishable from 100 other places in that same biome.Overall it's a really solid little game. Well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game, but it doesn't really explain any of the necessities for how to play. It's community driven in the sense that the game is basically incomplete, and doesn't teach you any way to advance. You MUST consult external resources, otherwise it's conceivable to spend years playing the game and not knowing what to do next. This can be done well, but I don't feel that core keeper manages that. Games have done this style before, but even in the case of a game like terraria, they literally have a guide NPC to give you direction. He spawns with you initially, and the game's very design encourages you to do things that will make progression click. You build a house for your character to survive the night, and suddenly the guide moves in. Core keeper lacks that direction. It's a mining game. At no point is there any semblance of something that would force you to build walls and a house. You can just dig out a cave for your work stations. You don't even need doors, as long as you remove the tiles using a shovel. So, in that way, the game is requires either familiarity with the genre, or an inhuman amount of patience and curiosity. I would recommend it for experienced players, but even then the progression is slow and clunky so I can't give a whole-hearted endorsement. The best way I can describe it would be "imagine if stardew valley wanted to be terraria, but wasn't."

_childDocuments_.review: I did a full play through with a friend in a single seed to 100% the game in a little over 120 hours.  The progression of this game is fantastic and the crafting system is easy to use/follow.  Go-karts, Boating, PvE, PVP, boss battles... I was never bored playing this game as there is always something to do.  The customization you are allowed to make in game is endless (painting, flooring, walls, farming, automation, mob spawning, etc.).  Essentially you need to defeat certain bosses to gather parts to power the core, which will unlock more of the available map.  There are also optional bosses, ALL of which have fun mechanics and I recommend trying all boss fights.  The appearance of the game to me was appealing, giving almost a retro feel to the game.  This game felt like it took great aspects from other games I've played and put it into one.  Very fun game, definitely recommend it.  Things I've learned/tips:1.)  Using the Map - to place the Icons, select the desired icon and click the middle mouse button on the map to add; click on same spot to remove.  Mark boss fighting/summoning locations to find easier later on.2.)  If you want to customize flooring that doesn't allow it to be painted; put a "glass floor" on top of it, then paint it.  May find a color you like w/ that pattern.3.)  Create Scanners to find bosses, sooo much more convenient than blindly running around the map.4.)  Save the figurines you collect.  There's a way to "power" them to have them spawn that type of mob; they do not drop loot, though still grant exp for your skill ups.5.)  You have 3 different gear sets, recommend binding those sets to hotkeys.  Some fights may be much easier if/when you switch armor sets/tactics during the fight.Hope the above helps, enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: It's sideways Terraria with a top-down digging exploration that may remind older gamers of Dungeon Keeper. It also incorporates a major Stardew Valley feel, with farming elements. Later, there's a dash of Factorio, with basic mining automation and electronics.It's very polished for an early access game (as of version 0.3.3). I only had 2 random crashes, which lost no progress. And I think I only saw one glitch (an invisible mob).It's got a whole lot of content already: 46 hours worth of core progression, for me. That's playing almost entirely alone. Although it was definitely a bunch more fun when a Steam friend joined my world for a bit, near the beginning.I was able to defeat all the bosses solo. But there was a bit of a learning curve with that. And I had to cheese the last two using environmental... adjustments; the spike trap is a rather core gameplay mechanic, at this point.My biggest criticism is that a few of the biomes feel dead and boring: particularly the stone area, after one's been through killing everything, nothing seems to respawn there.The movement and combat is not intrinsically as fun as a side-scroller. And a *lot* of the mechanics and content are very clearly derived from Terraria (and Minecraft). But the change in perspective, various novelties, etc, were enough to keep me engaged. Just about. Having not played a similar game for a few years.Overall highly recommended. Either to play now, or to wait until the next couple of bosses are released. Presumably with a whole lot more content besides, given the rate the devs are currently pushing out updates.[Edit: 120 hours further in!]So, after checking out some YouTube, Steam community and Reddit content, I realised I'd entirely missed 2 optional bosses, hidden away! Plus a load of higher end and rare gear. So I jumped back in (for lack of any other game I can currently be bothered to pick up)...The game becomes wildly time consuming, searching the vast swathes of map (alone). And in terms of levelling up the skill-tree of your character, through grind the various activities. And catching the less common fishes, etc.Then I got into aesthetic builds. Reorganising my base for more optimised crafting flow. Experimenting with wood auto-farms and enemy mob spawn mechanics. Plus making a couple of guides to apprise players of the lesser known aspects of NPC housing and, today, the wildly expansive cooking system - currently there's 1785 unique dishes can be made!The chunky pixel graphics have grown on me even more; I feel like this might be the most pretty retro graphics of a game I've seen. Particularly in parts of the wilderness, with the water shimmering there.And I've revised my #1 pet peeve: the clumsiness of fine interactions (on PC). It's trivially easy to break the wrong thing, like the punching the floor off, instead of harvesting a veg, or picking up a torch, or mine cart, or mining a wall. All the same interaction. And it auto-targets something else off to the side, sometimes, even when your character is looking at what you want to do. Sometimes even when that thing is highlighted! So hopefully there might be some refinements there. But either way, I'm fully hooked into this game and community, now.[Edit: over 400 hour in.]Short video review here!:

_childDocuments_.review: You should definitely play this game - but not right now. I did enjoy the majority of my time in Core Keeper, but I was constantly haunted by the game's immense unrealized potential.If you do decide to play, do not play on hard mode. It is an artificial difficulty increase, 1.5x enemy health, 2x enemy damage, 1.5x more loot from bosses. You will get one tapped constantly while you whittle away enormous health pools.This game is best enjoyed blind. Stop reading here if you don't want any spoilers. This unrealized potential reveals itself in many ways - missing QOL pieces, massive gaps in the game's content, significant oversights in the game's progression, and poor balance.The majority of enemies and bosses are simple copy/paste jobs of one another. I completely understand wanting to stretch the assets you do have as far as you can, especially seeing as the first times you encounter an enemy type or boss type it's very exciting and cool. It's just that once you fight the same boss with a new color palette a third time with an extra gimmick, or you enter a fifth new biome with, you guessed it, the same enemies as everywhere else just wearing a new hat and mustache, it gets to be too much.From this point in the review, I am going to start complaining and whispering maniacal montras to myself in a corner,The game tries very hard to push you toward playing a hybrid ranged/melee character. As a resident mage in every game, I was punished for my choice this time. Don't get me started on summoner. There are 32 melee weapons and 20 ranged weapons, compared to eight magic weapons and THREE summon weapons. In the entire game, THREE? The last of which being a mid-game item? Phew.99% of the time, when you find a new armor set, or ring/necklace, or even an off-hand item, you'll find yourself saying "that's it? that's all that does?"After a point, it just becomes insulting, or at the very least unsatisfying. A ring that gives 19 armor eh? That'll take a good 15 damage off the 1100 damage attack from this boss! Oh I only have 800 HP using the strongest buff I can find while using end game equipment so the boss will instantly kill me no matter what? Score!!Guess I should have gone for the 90% dodge chance build (which is also absurd).I like the mechanic of leaving automatic drills on huge ore deposits, I really do, but there are three problems:1. They give way, WAY too much ore. So much that, as soon as you are able to leave drills on a deposit, mining it yourself is a waste of time.2. The electricity should not be free. In the future, generators should require fuel or something.3. The drills should probably require some sort of maintenance, whether that's just a simple durability system or whatever, I don't know.Fishing is not a very fun use of time. Maybe that's just me. Fortunately you're never really required to pick up a fishing rod. Farming was fun. I wish there was a faster way to plant seeds.Game needs more NPCs, and also they need to be killable or at least movable manually. One escaped his habitat and started wandering my base so I basically tortured him for 10 minutes before deciding he was immortal. Why can I deal damage to them if they cannot die? Are the merchants the true gods of Core Keeper? Let me put the bearded man into a cattle box for safe keeping. Or on a leash so I may drag him back to his eternal prison.Sequence breaking the game is trivial. You can use an early game grenade launcher and bombs to run to the outer ring immediately upon killing the first three bosses. The enemies in the outer ring are annoying, but tolerate them for long enough and you'll find yourself with bombs that will obliterate nearly any block and armor that you'll probably never get rid of.I ran halfway around the outer circle and got enough materials from scrapping excess armor that I was able to skip to the final tier workbench not long after speaking with the core the first time. I would say this actually contributed to my enjoyment of the game, though.Especially considering that even with the huge skip in progression, the mid-game enemies and bosses still removed all my bones from my body a hundred times. I can't imagine what build the game WANTED me to use on these opponents. Lightning round of things I liked:It's beautiful. Combat works pretty well, hit registration issues are rare. Trying to min-max your build is fun. Skills level at a pretty fair rate mostly. Instruments and the music doors are so cool. OST is fire. Lots of funny multiplayer moments. Multiplayer is smooth. Farming is fun. The sex scenes were good. The world is full of interesting set pieces and constructs. Bases feel very cozy. Every biome is visually distinct and are a joy to look at and explore. Multiple boss fights are seriously cool (azeos and the first time you fight a hydra are my favs). Overall, I am very excited to come back later down the line. I hope there are plans to continue development beyond 1.0, as I know this game can without a doubt become a 10/10.One last gripe, I hope when I come back that I don't use the fireball staff for 15 hours again. Also I hope the chaos staff gets some kind of change or just turns into a sidegrade - the best in slot magic weapon should not have the chance to just make you instantly unalive yourself and your teammate every time you shoot.Thanks for reading, cowboy.  See you at the leather club meeting this Thursday.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: kind of like Terraria. It's a fun game and I recommend it if you like digging/exploration kind of games with rudimentary combat.This game satisfies most of the same itches Terraria scratches, but with several differences. Lots and lots of digging to find ore to gradually beef up your character, fighting bosses that gate content, building farms for mob drops and food, fishing, etc. That's pretty much where the similarities end. Equipment takes durability damage and needs to be repaired pretty frequently. Farming crops is more reminiscent of Stardew Valley requiring you to till the dirt to plant seeds and maintain a water level in your watering can. There is a very basic talent tree and makes you want to experiment with different things, or look up build guides on youtube.Regarding areas for improvement: - Some boss battles. One in particular, somewhat early on is more challenging than the others. There used to be a way for the player to effectively remove one of the mechanics from the battle, but it has been patched out of the game, requiring the player to find another way around some of the annoying mechanics. It's just a very dull encounter that feels like something you have to do just to progress. No real fun in it.- Playing on hard mode seemingly has one benefit only: more drops from bosses. Doesn't seem worth it seeing as how everything in that mode gets more HP and hits way harder. If there were more benefits to even out the hard mode difficulty slightly, or various exclusive mob drops, it would be fun to take on the challenge. - There is no way to transport the various liquids in the game to fish in apart from digging extensive trenches back to your main base. The way around this is to have multiple bases in the different biomes. [EDIT: this has been addressed with the addition of water buckets to transport liquid.]This review is based on the early access version, so I'll try to update when ver 1.0 releases. Overall it's a lot of fun and I see myself spending many more hours playing Core Keeper.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR I love this game. Best 15$ I have spent on a game in YEARS. If I knew how good it was back then, I would have payed 100 for it. So I have finally beat this game. After nearly 100 hours of game play. Some of which was spent in a friends world, but most of it was just mine. I thoroughly enjoyed every aspect of this game. The farming, the crafting, mining, fishing, the different combat styles, everything. The music and art is top tier. Every zone is a breath of fresh air when it comes to music and design, and it brought the atmosphere of each zone together in a way that not many games are able to pull off. I absolutely loved all of the boss fights. I did end up having a fairly cheesy build that made a lot of them a lot more trivial than they should have been, but because of this I am genuinely looking forward to playing through again, but with a much less cheesy build. I honestly had no idea what the final boss was, and literally finished it 5 mins prior to this review. I would like the genuinely thank the minds behind this game, the people who brought it to life in such a beautifully crafted way, because I believe this is easily a top 10 game I have played in my 25ish years of playing games. So thank you very very much Pugstorm. This is a solid 100/10 for me, and I genuinely hope that more people get to experience the simplistic bliss that is this game.
