_childDocuments_.review: This is game is amazing. It's basically Terraria from a topdown view, which (in my opinion) makes the map so much bigger than in Terraria. The world generation is really nice and has a good number of settings to it as well. What I really liked in particular though is the story behind the world you navigate. Each biome has its own set of structures that each tell their own stories of who might've lived there/used it. The bosses in this game is what truly amazed me though. The slime bosses were very basic (although I liked the Terraria reference to king slime), but the bosses that I really liked in particular are the hydra bosses. When I first saw these bosses spawn in I was amazed at the animation of these bosses for a game that has pixel graphics. I also really liked that each time you kill 1 of the Hydra bosses, their soul fights alongside the next hydra boss you face, making you eventually fight 3 hydras. Although this game is great, there are aspects to this game that I think need improvement. First off, why are there so many different crafting stations? You start off with a workbench for regular crafting, a furnace for smelting ores and an anvil for crafting gear. But then you have an automation table for automation like conveyor belts and drills, a bait workbench for creating bait for fishing, a carpenter table for decorations, a jewelry workbench for necklaces and rings and a lot more crafting stations. The one that ticks me off the most however is the glass smelter and glass workbench. The glass workbench is only there to craft with glass which in my opinion is mostly useless since you don't need glass to look through a wall since this game has a top down view. And the glass smelter is hilarious. It only lets you smelt sand into a glass piece and that's it. It's things like this that make me wonder why the glass smelter was even added in the first place. Why not just add this recipe to the furnace? And better yet, why don't you just add most of these recipes to crafting tables/furnaces? Why do I need to fill my base to the brim with 20 different crafting stations just so I can get the 1 item I need and then never touch it again? I get that you need to lock certain items behind something for the sake of progression, but you couldn't have made something like a crafting scroll that you can find after like defeating a boss or just exploring the world to unlock the recipes for certain items? Another thing I really didn't like is the gardening mechanic. On the surface level gardening is fine. You plant stuff, it grows pretty quickly and then you  harvest it. Easy. But it is when you start making bigger farms where the main problem starts to arise. Planting things takes forever on a big farm. There's no automation for planting crops, so you'll have to do it manually. This wouldn't really be so bad if I could place more than ONE seed at a time. But since I cannot, it really just discourages me from farming at all, which disappoints me since I like creating giant farms. Hopefully they expand on farming and specifically automated farming in the coming updates.And lastly to top this already too long review off is the baffling summoner class. When I found out that there was a summoner class I was excited, since I like being a summoner. Although in my experience very few games actually manage to pull off a fun summoner class. So I was curious how the summoner class in CK is like. After playing through the game and checking the wiki to make sure I wasn't hallucinating or really unlucky, I found out that there are only THREE different summoning books of which one is almost completely useless (which also happens to be the highest leveled one of the bunch). But there is plenty of cool looking armor for the summoner class. Why? There are 32 different melee weapons, 20 ranged weapons, 8 magic weapons and only 3 summoning weapons. Really? On top of this, something I really didn't like (and this also applies to most magic weapons) is that you have to get these weapons from exploration or killing enemies. You cannot craft magic weapons. You have loads of different crafting stations for very specific things, but couldn't make one for magic/summoning items?And that's my review. Great game with some flaws, but definitely addicting. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is a good game, however it does have issues which can make it stale at times.Pros:+ Great art style and overall aesthetic+ Good spread of skills (fighting, fishing, mining, farming etc.)+ Gameplay is nice, similar to stardew valley with a larger focus on combat.+ RPG elements where skills level up through use+ Bosses to kill+ Discovering new recipes is satisfyingCons:- New patch repair system means you can no longer use salvage and have to use ores. This would be fine, however ores are not all that common, tools are expensive and break quickly leading me to not use tools, especially when high mining skill can make bare hands decent enough.- Exploration/mining can be dull as you have to tunnel everywhere making finding new areas a bit of a chore. On top of this, ore locations are highlighted so you know there aren't any surprises for you to uncover in your exploration.- melee combat purely relies on kiting making each encounter just a hit then run away experience which is not very satisfying.- Skill trees really only offer stat bonuses. It would have been nice to have abilities or more interesting skills that allow you to lean into a certain playstyle/build more.- Very little driving force to make you progress. Hunger is easy to beat and mobs won't invade you so you don't need to upgrade your base and only need better gear to beat bosses.Overall this is an early access game with a lot of potential. I am confident that more things will be added and am excited to see where the game goes hence my positive review. However until I either get some friends or the game systems become deeper I will probably not be playing much.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game per se, but I cannot give it a recommendation either for a few reasons in it's current state. The main issue Core Keeper has right now is that it doesn't offer enough variety with it's gameplay. It's the same gameplay loop you're asked to do over and over again, with the same tools every single time, enemies that play by the same rules and bosses that are very one dimensional. The game runs out of steam around the third boss, which is sad because it's a pivotal moment in the game's story and progression (at least they try to make it look like that), but what you get instead is you are asked to do the same thing you were doing so far, again.I will make a reference to Terraria here to try and explain what playing this game is like in it's current state: Imagine the very first version of Terraria and how barebones it was. Then take away everything that isn't the underground layer and leave only a few pieces of findable loot and unique things. Now you have an idea of how simplistic and basic this game is in terms of the gameplay loop and what is there available for you to do as a player.So, what does this game need to actually be interesting and have more staying power? As I said: variety. That can manifest in multiple different forms: More weapon and tool variety to make combat more dynamic, different objectives other than "kill the next boss", more interesting loot and unique things to find to give you feed your spelunking drive, different kinds of progression other than dig-new ore-same gear but stronger stats-repeat, new gameplay systems that give you things to do. There is so much design space here that the devs have luxury of choice in what they want to work on. Any of this would make the game significantly better. And the best games in this category (like Terraria) have absolutely all of it and then some.As it is right now, you might get about 10 hours of gameplay out of it until you arrive to the point I've mentioned when the repetition starts to wear on you. I've played the game two times so far, and it stopped being fun around the exact same point. The way the game is being developed right now, I don't think this is going to change, adding higher tier content is not going to change anything if I never get to it in the first place, what Core Keeper needs is a proper midgame section when ti opens up with possibility and varriety, not an infinitely stretched early game with the same gameplay loop. And I hope the devs realize that, because it would be a shame for a game with so much potential to remain in it's current, gimped form.

_childDocuments_.review: Started playing this game because it reminded me of Terraria, another game I love, and now I have become addicted. I could roam around in this game forever and find fun details and spots.2. The gameplay hits that sweet spot of not being too hard but gradually ramps up in difficulty, while still being insanely fun and rewarding. It's also a lot of fun to make new builds for your character and test out all of the different kinds of fighting styles.3. I cannot get over how much I love that this game takes place underground. It reminds me of how I usually end up living in the caves whenever I play Minecraft. It's so fun and unique.4. _childDocuments_.review: -The game is sorely in need of a way to automate seed planting, like a seed cannon or seed disperser because it takes me 10minutes just to plant my seeds on my current field, and that's 10minutes that I could be out exploring the world.-Coins don't stack, so I have 4 chests literally just filled with coins.-You can't see what's in a chest at a glance, so you always run around opening each of your chests just to find the material you're looking for.-You can't craft from nearby chests, which is sorely needed.-When you want to destroy an item, it takes two clicks into the trash box, when it should only be taking one.-The price for items/materials isn't displayed, until you take it to the merchant, which is terribad.-The game is for sale in ruzzia.-The regional pricing in the 3rd world is disgusting.-The skill system can be improved a lot and you gain nothing anymore if one of your skills reaches lvl100, so you literally waste experience at lvl100, instead of that experience being passed to other skills.-The game has seasonal content, which is always bad since the devs spend development time on something that players will only 'enjoy' for a few weeks out of the year, and that development time could have been spent on permanent content instead.I'll play the game more during the EA period but right now the game has too many missing QoL features which makes the player's life difficult, and the crazy regional pricing & ruzzist support push this game even further into the red.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you liked Terraria and need a new game to play, play this.At the time of writing this (version 1.0), it'll probably take most people around 50-100 hours from start until the final boss, going in blind or mostly blind. One huge plus to this game is the ability to let you do that; everything is fairly intuitive, never felt like I had to go to the wiki in order to figure out how to do something.It's a fair critique to say this game has less content than Terraria and I'd say that's probably true, but you also gotta remember Terraria has been out since 2011 and has had tons of updates since then. The way they've laid out this game you can definitely tell they've set it up to receive plenty of updates in the future. And even if you just do your 1 playthrough and stop, $20 for 100 hours of fun isn't exactly a bad deal.But for those who are still enjoying the game after they've beat all the bosses, there is still time to be spent in optimizing your character re-farming bosses for rare loot, trying out different builds, and customizing your world in general. Also tons of different world settings you could try out if you wanted to test out playing a new world or a harder difficulty.If you don't know too much or haven't seen too much content on this game and you're considering getting it, I'd recommend going in blind. This game has a lot of little details and surprises that lead to cool moments.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Huge potential, as many have probably said, game is VERY much like terraria, but not in the "oh terraria has this but better" way, its familiar, but has something new to offer that can't be found in terraria. With that out of the way, this game has potential to become one of the greats in terms of survival/crafting multiplayer. I appreciate how easy it is to start a world, copy one code and have a friend join a game, looking at you minecraft. As for the gameplay itself, it offers fair and ramped up challenges as you move along in the game, the more bosses you defeat the more powerful you must become before facing the next. Crafting can be pricey but as is the nature of crafting games; at first it'll be tough to get rid of your items, but soon you'll be drilling the ore cluster and have hundreds of said ore. On top of that, a skill tree, personally one of my favorite upgrade aspects in video games. My only complaint, I wish it was a longer list, but if it there was more upgrades perhaps the points should be a bit less between upgrades, fishing can be grueling where as running and gardening will be a breeze. Combat is simple, but still thrilling, when you first start off even the basic slime can be a bit scary. This is also one of the first games where an ax or bow is much preferred to a sword as they tend to lack range, which is interesting to see. As this game gets more updates, and more content, new biomes, new mods (there seems to be a fostering community for it which is awesome to see), new items etc., I could easily see this being right next to terraria, or even surpassing it in quality. Amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh Gosh! I'm really torn how to rate this.  There are so many great things and aspects of the game, but a few fundamental aspects that make this game a no-go from the obstacles I encountered.Pros- What a great way to imagine and build.  I had fun creating and making factories, railways and other structures.  I could have done more and invested in hours of creativity.  It's pretty much the skys' limit in what you want to make. The sounds and pixel art is really good.  Love the sounds in the game.  Great variety of biomes and much exploration. Major CONs-  This game is made for CO-OP play.   The problem I ran into is I found it really difficult finding a group that I was able to fit in their terms of their world.  Many wanted mic's and I can not have one since I'm in a room with other people.  There were timezone issues where they want to be the admin, but turn the system off and you can't access until they are on.  I find a group and they discontinue their save and all is lost.  So I tried solo and once I began fighting the last 3 titans, I ran into a progression problem.  In order to fight the titans, you have to find rare gems to make an object to summon them; that appear random and maybe 20% of the time.  You will spend 2 -3 hours to find them, if you are lucky.  I think the Developers should have created a merchant that sells these Gems.  This is a stupid aspect that I called it quits.  Unless you have a lot of free time, don't play this game ALONE!  Because of this flaw, I have to rate this a no-go.

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gem of a game! I'm a still astounded by how much content Core Keeper has, but still manages to feel fun and refreshing (and the music is awesome as well). I'm inredibly glad that Malugaz received the spotlight he deserved as one of the game's best bosses.My only complaint is the way boats work in this game. The game has lots of ways for the player to refine and upgrade their respective builds, yet half of it is pretty much useless when fighting on boat. Pets don't spawn (even the flying ones), which usually can be a huge damage source against bosses. Off-hand items are obsolete except for their buffs, so using a shield to block attacks is also not possible. The Speeder also barely feels faster than the normal boat and slows down a lot as soon as the player chooses to move into a different direction, which is the major reason for me dying during the Atlantean Worm fight.Despite that, Core Keeper is a great game and I highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a beautiful soundtrack; including my personal favourite “Azeos’ Wilderness” making me want to pack up my entire base and move just to have the biome music. The placeable items, walls and floor options allow for a lot of creativity - both practical and non-practical. The bosses and entities in the game offer variety with how you interact and fight them, so you need to plan your hot bar equipment before heading out for an adventure. While it can feel like a bit of a grind to get higher tier gear and become stronger, there’s a lot to do and explore alongside that: battle arenas, dungeons,  discovering ancient ruins - heck I even find farming fun in this game and I often dislike farming sims/farming genre games.It’s a lot of fun both with friends and solo. I’d recommend at least giving the game a try as there’s many more updates and features coming in the future and the community and devs are interactive and wholesome.

_childDocuments_.review: The  is clear without hand-holding, but you're free to do whatever you want; Follow the clues to tackle the next challenge, or rush straight to the  and yolo.The  mechanic feels good. It's a buff system in disguise. Each raw food item has a stat buff and you can cook any two raw foods together to make buffs that work for your character or build.Characters have  like Terraria or Valheim. You can make a new character per world, but you don't have to.There's  for the green-thumbs that has a really nice feeling skill progression. Combining skills, tools, and equipment to make even a little go a long way.The  is almost the crux of the game in a way. The progression path is led mainly with breadcrumbs in the crafting system; find a new item, craft a new thing, now you can find even more items or defeat even more enemies, repeat. And crafting is separated into different tables which allows builders to really go to town on bases. Which leads to...There are so many  options; walls, floors, sub floors, lights, furniture, decorative items, equipment stands / item pedestals, etc. You can even paint some of the blocks to really let your creativity shine.For the animal lovers, you can  for fun or for crafting ingredients. You can find  eggs around the world or from boss drops to have a little companion in your travels. There's also the  skill tree if you absolutely must have the maximum amount of critters following you around. There's fishing. If you know you know. It's way less stressful than Stardew and an excellent time sink for if you just want to hang out and wait for some ore to smelt.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10. I give this game a lukewarm yes.For the price, I would recommend other games such as Terraria, Valheim, and Stardew Valley as they have way more content to enjoy and a more rewarding experience. This game is in Early Access, so there are still elements to be added, but the overall core gameplay cycle (ex. explore new biome, farm resources, kill boss) is unrewarding and therefore boring. The game is very grindy, but doesn't reward the player adequately for all their hard work. Bosses will drop items that are significantly worse than items you can find on basic mobs. The boss fights themselves are ResidentSleeper. The main goal of the game is to kill the bosses and outside of that there isn't much else to do. So if you are a goal-oriented player, then I think you'll find the experience lacking and un-fun.The positives are that the game isn't buggy ~ especially considering its Early Access state. The graphics are cute. And playing with friends is fun and makes the game playable. There's a lot of potential with interesting elements like pets, shopkeepers, and automation. If you buy this game, I don't think you'll hate it. I don't think you'll love it either though.

_childDocuments_.review: At the start I was blown away by this game.It was a good time with friends. However After I went past the inintal 4 - 6 hour mark I started to notice this game was a bit hard. Bigger mobs would come out of nowhere and 1 shot you , the map is so big you end up miles and miles away from your main hub (yes u unlock teleporting later on) however I find it very tedious to explore to far as it was so boring having to back track to each zone. Combat was sometimes unresponsive and attacks would miss for no reason. being ranged is much easier but only after you have found a decent ranged weapon.Crafting items is fun and so is the food, that aspect of the game is enjoyable. However farming to make better gear is not. Then there is the boss loot. The unrewarding boss loot that is not even better than what you are using most of the time.The tech tree is also difficult to explore, as I have been stuck on Scarlet or the lack of for quite some time. The 3rd boss me and my friends simply cannot kill. We lack the firepower. Bombs do nothing, and all of our weapons tickle it. It has way too much HP and the constant acid on the floor and spawn of mobs is just impossible for us to deal with.Yes other players have managed to do it, but we are a group of casual players who do not invest that much time into games unless we really enjoy them.Unfortunately my friends have moved on and I am reluctant to play with randoms on a discord server. So for me it is now a single player experience and it is just awful as single player.The base building is fun and the mechanics are there for a solid game.  It is fun to build a base it still has charm and there is a good game here.But it needs balancing for single player asap.There needs to be a casual mode so me and my friends can get back into the game with massively reduced monster HP and upscaled damage and health for players and the option to turn off the food mechanic.In its current state I cannot recommend this game. I will update as the game gets updated but right now there are better crafting/survival/co-op games out there that value your time.*Update*Development team have update the game and it has now gone into full release. I will update the game based on my gameplay of 1.0

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. You'll find a lot of elements from other great titles like Valheim, Ark, Zelda, Stardew Valley, Diablo, Minecraft, Terraria, Harvest Moon, Animal Crossing, Forager, etc. It's a balanced mix of mine, grow, gather, and hunt. As you find relics, kill baddies and bosses, you'll get to upgrade and customize everything along the way. You can run up to three armor sets at a time utilizing various rings, necklaces and offhand gear. This allows you to change stats and abilities on the fly for various enemies and tasks. It's a huge world and it easily accommodates the 8 player option to venture with friends. There's only been a few visual bugs and a handful of times items around the base decide they don't want to stay in place. It's just a matter of breaking the ground with a shovel, replacing it, and laying your item back on it. I'm sure it'll get patched at some point. It overall feels like a polished and very finished game compared to a lot of titles that have released in recent years, so if this is just early access, we're off to a great start!

_childDocuments_.review: It's early access, things change. Just remember that. As far as people claiming your garden will wither away since you don't get enough seeds back, your base chance to get them back when harvesting is 75%, the very first 5 points you have to spend in the gardening tree add another 25%. You will not run out of seeds. As for the repair changes that lots of people complain about, the required resources needed to repair are exceedingly low, you will spend very very little time gathering stuff to repair your items.As for the game itself, it's $12, you can rush through the bosses in probably under 15 hours, but you can also work on leveling your talents, or make a world with friends, or just explore. I've played every day since it came out, and plan on continuing to do so.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is a gem, it delivers what is says.at early access it's all ready a lot of fun to play, mining stuff, building a nice base and protecting it from enemies.starting a small farm, then expand it and reap the rewards (farming bomb plants will prove worth the most when you get your npc's)the biomes are fun and need a different approach when you reach them.some of the enemies will nearly kill you with a single hit some will surprise you by hiding in a bush, then eventually learn how they fight, adapt, kill a bunch and collect the loot.the further you progress, the more new things there are to discover.i like the leveling, its done really good but at early access could use a bit of tweaking.players that don't level their chars, will still be nearly useless in the "harder" biomes.it means putting in the work, actually pays off, equipping a new char with tier 5 gears will only allow them to level up a bit easier.at early access there are 5 tiers of craftable equipment, then when u reach tier 5, there still is better stuff available...and also, there are 5 bosses i'm aware of, but i suspect i have not encountered all of them yet...playing together up to 8 players really adds to the fun, but at early access it does need improvement.it encourages to create multiple worlds.replay value is highcreativity has a lot of spacei enjoy it alot!well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: I did not like the game, the game play felt tedious and somewhat pointless, and during my 8 hours in the game I have not seen anything I have not already seen in other games (by and large).  This is the main critique. Could have forgiven bad inventory management if the rest of the game was engaging.There are 2 years old threads when people request an ability to use items directly from inventory that got completely ignored.  This problem is exacerbated by a couple of other QoL (or absence of there of) decisions:- Since I cannot use from inventory, I want to reserve a hot bar slot for these, so I do not need to swap. Just open inventory, put in the empty reserved slot and use. However the game insists on filling the hot bar with whatever is looted next so this does not work- Infuriatingly, when you swap an items between inventory and hot bar and close the inventory, the old item remains attached to your mouse pointer. You cannot ESC or another keybind to put it back to the inventory. If you left/right click it is simply dropped to the ground. You need to re-open inventory again, put the item back there, and then close the inventory. ESC here would have worked nicely (or better yet do not keep the item attached to the pointer, or make a toggle if some one really fond of it this way).This may seem trivial, but this is a problem that I have every few minutes in the game. It gets old very, very quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game!!!Valheim meets Path of Exile meets Zelda.As a fan of Valheim and Path of Exile, this game totally hooked me even though at first the pixel art wasn't really my thing. However after about an hour I felt like the pixel art was charming and now after dozens of hours I LOVE THE PIXEL ART!!!It has a similar progression/crafting system to Valheim, which the devs even stated was their inspiration for the progression system. Yet it's even more in depth than Valheim. Each new biome and boss require strategy and upgrading your gear and cooking better food along with some forethought as to how to approach the fight and even how to manipulate the terrain prior to engaging the boss in order to give yourself an advantage. And of course the combat and isometric camera angle reminded me of PoE a little bit even though it looks more like old school Zelda at first glance.The boss fights themselves are intense, especially if you play on hard mode which is quite hard in the beginning stages of the game. Each boss has interesting and challenging mechanics and it's chaotic at times but still the mechanics themselves are very 'readable' with good visual clarity unlike one of my favorite games of all time Path of Exile which while being incredible itself lacks visual clarity and it's one of the biggest downsides to that game (unless you use a broken build and trivialize the endgame bosses, LOL... but back to Core Keeper).Man this game totally grew on me to the point where I got my buddy to try it and at first he was like "meh, I don't know about these graphics" but then after about 30 mins he was loving it as much as I do. Being in a group (up to 8 ppl can play co-op) is even better than playing solo although solo is enjoyable as well of course.Do yourself a favor and pick this game up. It's great and yet another great example of how much better indie games are nowadays on average than most AAA titles with bloated budgets and 100's of devs. Fun is fun and no amount of "investor capital" and massively over-staffed studios can manufacture fun any better than a few dudes with passion and focus. Just buy the game. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Core Keeper is a delightful indie title that masterfully combines the charm of pixel graphics with the excitement of exploration. The art style is vibrant, detailed, and perfectly fits the atmospheric biomes that range from lush forests to eerie caverns. The music complements this aesthetic, creating an immersive experience.The gameplay shines with its variety of bosses, each offering unique challenges. The thrill of exploring new areas and stumbling upon unexpected secrets keeps the game fresh for hours.However, the game could use some balancing. Warrior melee builds dominate with their damage output and survivability, making them feel overpowered. Meanwhile, summoners and wizards struggle to keep up, often requiring more effort for less reward. Additionally, some skills demand an overwhelming number of points to unlock or upgrade, which can feel like a grind.Despite these shortcomings, Core Keeper is a fantastic adventure for anyone who loves exploration-driven gameplay with a retro twist.

_childDocuments_.review: On its own merits, Core Keeper is a solid and very visually pleasing game that takes a "quality over quantity" approach in its design. 1.0 is a much better game than it was during early access. It can be very fun and invoke a great feeling of adventure and discovery— the wonderful visual design of many of the later biomes makes suffering through some slow grinds feel worthwhile. I have criticisms, but they are mostly only comparisons to the big titans of the survivalcraft genre, and thus not very fair to the great work put in by pugstorm on this game, or in the spirit of the experience they have planned out for their players. _childDocuments_.review: I wish there was an in-between button again. I do and do not recommend this right now. I'm on the fence for sure!I am at university and I hold 3 positions there voluntarily, which keep me quite busy! As such, I don't have much time to game - I'm sure this is true for many of you. This game, from the 2 hours I played, quickly told me it would require a lot of time to get up and running. From the amount of travel you need to do from A to B, to the amount of terrain manipulation to make things efficient respectively. Whilst it is fun to do this, I just don't have the time to manage it all and I want to play in my off-time.Generally, graphics were nice, concept is nice, and it all ran perfectly fine. The UI had a few minor issues in that if you were not stood exactly pixel perfect, you could accidentally hit the wrong square and delete your torch, or whatever. This happened a lot to me within 2 hours game play, and I'm sure it's just a practice thing, but equally it could do with a bit of tweaking maybe.Also, and this one REALLY irritated me actually, the floor and wall tiles are completely individual, even if they are both, "Stone" or whatever. So, you dig the floor and get, "Stone Floor", and "Stone Wall" for the wall. This is annoying because it takes up extra inventory, AND the floor is incredibly tedious to manoeuvre - If you dig floor, it leaves a literal hole behind you can't walk in, and so I just found myself juggling floor tiles for no reason.. In my mind, it would be incredibly easy to have materials as just, "Stone" etc. You place Stone in a hole, and it fills it in to become 'Stone Floor'. You place Stone on a floor and it effectively adds on top and becomes 'Stone Wall'. You dig/mine the Floor/Wall and you simply get 'Stone' back. I feel like this would make building and inventory management MAHOOOOSIVELY better. This, ultimately, is just a side point though.

The first hours feel like a grind where you first dig countless 1-wide tunnels until you finally find a small cluster (1-4) of ore, only to realize that the game has this tedious tool durability mechanic that forces to you take an almost equally long walk home to repair your pickaxe. Its a chore that doesn't feel rewarding at all, and leads to walks taking 50%+ of time spent in the game. Apart from some crates with the usual items, the only interesting places are few randomly scattered rooms which unfortunately do not contain anything radical, just several crates and low level crafting equipment.The weaponry, at least until in the copper-tin-iron tiers are just differntly colored items with slightly better stats. As of the time I'm writing this, we couldnt even craft a different bow (there is one model randomly dropped by chests though).The cooking seems nicely executed with several recipes, but these are more or less only  combinations of the precursor item's stats (more speed, more damage, ...)Bosses have annoyingly small operating ranges, and if one player accidentally drags the boss slightly away (or the boss randomly changes aggro to a nearby player), that boss resets to full health. That occurs regardless of any other players who never left the zone.That said it's EA yadda yadda so let's hope that this game gets the radical makeover it needs to stand out .

_childDocuments_.review: So with the release of the 1.0 there came a slew of patch notes that many of us in early access hadn't heard about or were expecting. The biggest ones was the gutting of the endless map, the removal of the fishing mini-game (i know that's a controversial one but it was one of my favorite things) and the tacked on magic system (still no clue WHY it wasn't tested in EA but...)The Map getting limited makes it smaller. SO much smaller. I'm pretty sure the entire dirt biome in a Classic world was the same size of the entire three zones inside the unbreakable wall. Gorm the Devourer had to be made smaller (The big worm thing from the above trailer. Hes like...1/4 his old size) and exploration feels so much worse when you realize how much less there is to explore.For the Fishing Mini-game, I'm biased but I personally loved it. Just simple pattern recognition, sit there, and relax. I know a lot of people didn't like it because it kept them from grinding up to 100 as fast as possible, or because they couldn't slow down for a few minutes, or simply because they just don't like fishing mini-games. I understand its removal is overall a positive for most people, but what makes me the most upset is that it came with no warning. No notice, no communication, no polls outside of a discord (assuming they did one there, i don't join too many discords due to personal reasons) they didn't look at maybe revamping how fishing exp works (easiest way would be to double exp gained when catching fish at active fishing zones, hell just fishing at those whenever you see one is an easy way to keep fishing even with your other skills) but no, lets just nix the entire thing. I guess the auto-fishing mod is going to get more popular since the system isn't worth interacting with now.Speaking of systems, Magic is OBJECTIVELY terrible. It basically boils down to "ranged, but with extra steps." The new magic guard is neat and is kind of a balance between dodge and armor, but its not strong enough to carry you very far, especially in multiplayer with how much harder enemies hit. (The fact it ONLY on gear an doesn't go up with skill level or other skill trees doesn't help its case)The Magic system took a few range staff weapons an made them their own skill system, but they're bad. They go shoot, shoot but bouncy, shoot a few, shoot or explode, and shoot.AND, unlike ranged, your LIMITED in how many times you can shoot by a mana pool. It just doesn't feel worth it, and the devs lack of creativity when compared to most of the game is shocking.Staff for tethering to an enemy and dealing damage over time? Nope too creativeStaff for laying traps at your feet that attack enemies who step on them? Nope too creativeStaff for a chain lightning spell? Nope too creativeStaff for healing allies or self? Nope too creativeIt's just not a system worth levelingSummoning is actually decently enjoyable, despite the devs having tacked it on at the last second. (There are only THREE summoning weapons) The first and earliest weapon you get summons a little ranged bat that lasts 30s, and if your running around with melee or ranged its a nice little helper, shooting at things. If you get summoner gear, you can summon more than one, which sounds good on paper but their targeting of whats hostile and whats not still needs to be worked on (surprising.) The fact they cost mana to summon isn't an issue if you're just relying on the one, but when your limit goes to 3 or beyond that, you're mostly running around trying to get your attention deficit helpers out onto the field. An easy fix would be having the mana cost of summons passively go down the higher the skill level is (the tree is fine, don't change it) but until a change happens its basically worth using as a side skill, not a main play style.While I'm happy to see an EA game leave EA, a few baffling changes that SHOULD have been looked at in the EA long before 1.0 was on the map are dulling this gem of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember buying this game for my sister a few years back. Didn't think much of it at the time, but I thought it would be a nice gift for her. I remember seeing her playing it from time to time, the message indicating that she'd started playing it popping up on the corner of my screen. There was always a certain small pride in seeing that, because to me it meant that she was enjoying my gift.Last September she committed suicide.After everything had more or less settled down from that, I sat down and booted up her computer. All that was on there was Chrome, Steam, Word, and a few games. One of them, of course, was Core keeper.She had played this game to pieces, clocking over 170 hours and owning practically everything the game had to offer. She had used every square inch to its maximum potential, and was making ridiculous amounts of loot. It was only then did I see just how much she loved my present. No other game she played quite captured her affection as much as this one. None of her friends really knew about it, however; it seems like she preferred to keep it to herself. Like it was her own little bit of heaven she could turn to whenever she wanted.And because of that, I can't help but smile whenever I play this game.I cannot recommend it enough; every bit of hard work the developer put into this masterpiece shows in every single aspect. The music is catchy and memorable (I'll often find myself humming certain tunes from it), the world feels lived-in and natural, and the gameplay is incredibly laid back and enjoyable. It's hard to stop once I get invested in the game; minutes can easily turn into several hours. And now, with the multiplayer beta, I play for even longer with my friends, each of us dedicated to our desired jobs. Most of all, however, we're all just happy to be together.

_childDocuments_.review: SOLO NO GO! May be better in a group. Bro, I have run into a wall. Progressed all the way to solar ingots (final crafted gear I can see), but have not found the bosses, and do not have the mats to ping them either. The travel is terrible, and the mobility never got better. Slow plodding forever. In Terraria you are zooming around like crazy in the 30+ hours I’ve played this game, but not here. You just walking the same speed, with even more annoying obstacles. Even with rail the distances and amount of exploration required puts you well off the beaten path. Leveling XP is too slow! I am in solar gear, yet still in level 5 melee! I was having trouble with poison and slippery slime, so I built huge farms… two slimes after an hour GTFO!Devs, you have something good here, but the balance is completely rancid for a solo player! _childDocuments_.review: This might be the worst game of this genre type I have played. At the very least in hard mode, the scaling is bad; you gain little to no stats over time so things stay the same for the most part and older mobs will do nearly all of your health in 1 hit. The boss fights are very poorly designed. I dont think they playtested any of their boss designs as some of the later bosses have a few patterns that are trivial to dodge however they have such a significant amount of health that you spend 10 minutes repeatedly breaking shields to kill them which is just honestly boring after a few minutes. The final boss is completely unfairly designed as attacks can spawn directly on top of you with no warning and will 1-shot you completely, making it just an unfair and unfun experience on top of having absurd health and shield values. The overall design of the game is nice and the graphics are nice, but the combat is severely lacking and it shares almost all the traits of terraria with such a worse implementation of them that I cant help but think its a shameless ripoff of terraria with no intent to make a fun game as they have clearly not played it themselves.

_childDocuments_.review: As an early release, it very much shows. The game plays fairly well if you only play in small bursts in a solo world/with a friend, but the state of the dedicated server shows just how glaringly bad this game is programmed. There is seemingly no memory management, and a game is hard capped at utilizing 4gb of memory, dedicated server or not. This would be fine in most games that purge items and enemies, but this game does neither. A server cannot exist for more than a few hours before hitting the cap and crashing, and there is no way to notify people on a server of an impending restart to mitigate this. The complete lack of basic server functionality shows this game is still needing a lot of polish before its release, and they just announced they are going 1.0 in Summer 2024. This suggests the dev team has utilized early access as a means to finance the game, something Steam actively tells devs not to do (but doesn't stop), and are pushing 1.0 to get financing from consoles for either continued development or dropping support entirely.I do not have high hopes for this game's future, even if I enjoyed the first few dozen hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I know this has been said by many people before, but the first chunk of the game is great. The first three bosses and charging the core kept my friend and I so engaged, we thought we'd found the next terraria, or at the very least a new game to dump dozens of hours into. That was until we we dropped the walls. Everything after the walls are dropped is an absolute slog, ores take forever to find/mine, finding bosses requires ungodly amounts of digging, and everything is SO expensive. What had once been a fun experience turns into a grinding/waiting simulator. You'd think that the massive open world that's put before you would be just as interesting as the small pocket you'd already seen, but the truth is that it's just a giant shallow set of biomes. Everything outside the walls is interesting once, then becomes samey really quick. The bosses are a mess too, the locator items have to be made first, and then the spawn items take forever to grind for, so if you lose, you'd better enjoy spending the next 20 minutes getting more resources to make another spawner and travelling all the way back to the boss arena. There's clearly a lot of content beyond what my friend and I have achieved so far, but the grind necessary to get to the each of the next steps is really starting to drain our interest in the game.This is just a few of the many gripes I have about this game, and I hate to leave a bad review on it, but without some series quality of life changes and major redesigns, I don't see this game succeeding.

_childDocuments_.review: After beating first 3 bosses i have no interest in continuing to play. At the moment i can't really recommend this game.My main gripes are:1)Biomes are boring. There is nothing interesting to biomes. Biomes are mostly walls of various durability and pocket of mobs, sometimes slowing slime or damaging acid puddles on the ground.2)Mining is tedious. While i know there is a way to automate gathering from nodes that scattered about, i got bored and stopped playing before made to the point where i had the tech required.3)The game is grindy. Skills are levelled solely by hitting/wall/vegetable or in case of fishing playing some tedious minigame.4)Perks are boring. They mainly consist of +% to damage, those that add something more are mostly "Stand still to get +100% to crit", there are no perks that affect gameplay in any meaningful extent.5)Progression is boring. It mainly consists of "get ore> smelt ore> craft workbench> repeat for the next ore". Even worse recipes are not inherited from previous tiers of workbenches. They are still required to process/use material from lower tiers.6)Smelting ores takes a long time (27 seconds for a scarlet bar). Why? I genuinely don't understand this. There is no automation prior to this ore. Even if there was, what the point? This isn't MMO that needs to waste players time with useless waiting.7)Automation come into game too late. When i got crimson ore i already was getting bored from tedium of gathering and smelting ore that i needed up to that point. Even then Crimson ore takes too long to process without automation.8)Combat is boring. For melee it mainly consists of hitting something few times and the running/dashing away to avoid attack. For ranged it consists of shooting something then running around waiting for the  to finish, making having more that one gun useless.9)Worst of all mobs have a "anti cheese" mechanic where they start to regenerate health if they cant get to you or you are attacking from outside their attack range. Why? Half the fun of these games are making mob farms or otherwise automating the combat. I would have understood if bossed had this, but not trashmobs. This is only decision i consider truly moronic for devs to implement.I genuinely have a hard  time understanding why this get so much praise.

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: This post contains spoilers.  is a magnificent sandbox RPG game that is a wonderfully intriguing experience, albeit with a few drawbacks here and there. I want to give a shoutout to my friend Boss Door  for putting me on it.I will say that I found the  story of getting isekai'd (more or less lol) into this massive sprawling cave system a bit lackluster. The game doesn't  quite hit the mark for me in terms of story in my opinion, however, the more you sat to truly  on things, the more it wonderfully opens itself up. For example, (spoiler alert: this is about a later area of the game)  Some of the various "scenes" (random areas with a structure or 'thing' going on—you'll know what I mean once you encounter one) provide insight on the lore of the game, and many of the items are descriptive on the context surrounding them, or what they pertain to. There's honestly just so much to enjoy about it, and I am engrossed by the often subtle approach to showcasing lore that the game has. I will say that it is not without its occasional ambiguity, and I do think that the story isn't particularly a mastercraft . I also think that the main plot could be brushed up on .In terms of gameplay value, I absolutely endear Core Keeper. I think it does very well for what it is (again, with the occasional drawback here and there—but what game doesn't?). It has plenty of sandbox elements which allows you for many ways, shapes, and forms of having control over your world. You can build massive, sprawling bases underground. You can construct railway systems that will take you from one end to the world to the next. You can build fully autonomous factories that harvest, process and automatically store resources for you. I think this game is absolute methamphetamine for autistic people. I DO think that—while allowing plenty of options—some of the choices made available do fall somewhat short. For example, you can only make very simple mechanisms. Even the more advanced farms are more-or-less just upscaled versions of the same small farms. I'm specifically a big minmaxx kind of guy, and I understand that the game is meant to appeal to a wider range of audience for what it was, so it's not the BIGGEST grievance of mine. I do think that—regardless—the game would stand to benefit from more advanced systems for the more technical side of the community (don't even get me started on mob farms with their "spawning chunks"... why allow the player to pick up spawner tiles and make the system ). I also think the  farming mechanics feel a bit dull since you need to manually plant everything, though it isn't the biggest deal since you can auto-water with sprinklers and harvest quite efficiently with an upgraded hoe. I also find the fact  We also don't talk about fishing in the game. However, please don't mistake my grievances with the idea that  has "poor" sandbox elements, though. I still absolutely love what it allows you to do, and some of the bases I've seen made by other players are amazing. There's so decorative options, and you can really make some beautiful things. Coupled with the drastically varying environments, and you have so much potential for building cool things. I think that  handles its progression kind of weirdly. Did you know that—at the time of this review—an iron pickaxe is actually the strongest handheld mining tool? If you upgrade it to level 19 (the maximum level allowed), it has the highest raw mining damage. You can also bypass a lot of "standard" progression by fishing in biome-specific waters—simply brave an expedition, bucket the water, and take it back to base. You can fish from it infinitely to get the biome ore without having to risk mining in the biome! Now, to be fair that is entirely avoidable and you aren't mandated to having to do that. However, I think that the way  handles combat progression isn't .  In "Hard" difficulty, you reliably can get 3-4 shotted by some of the enemies—even with the best gear. Not to mention some bosses can nigh-instakill you in some ways. I know it's supposed to be "hard" but it frankly felt unfair that you had to be so vigilant about enemies and bosses. It almost felt as if you NEEDED to have , which obsoleted about 90% of the rest of the potential offhand items . I also think that the way the classes are balanced are weird. You may have heard it from many other reviewers before, but magic and summoner tends to get the short end of the stick. Melee—while impractical for many bosses due to how many of them deal melee-based damage or fire projectiles "from" their bodies—is still a DPS powerhouse and is balanced in that aspect. Ranged forgoes a decent amount of damage for the safety of firing from afar. However, melee and ranged don't use "stamina" or "ammunition" respectively—I think that's honestly a massive quality of life decision. But magic and summoner use mana and don't quite nearly have the DPS to justify their "cost". Summoner especially quite literally only has 3 different choices and the minion AI isn't the best. All of the balancing surrounding weaponry aside, I think fighting the bosses is a cathartic and thrilling experience. A lot of them are quite difficult, in fact. Some of the difficulty spikes of the bosses are a bit insane, but I actually quite like the additive difficulty—it makes the eventual accomplishment of defeating the bosses so much more rewarding. The boss fights can be tense, stress-inducing even, but I honestly find them such a joy to accomplish and beat. I also think some of the enemies are really fun to learn and try to anticipate. For as many issues that I've found with the game's combat systems, I still thoroughly enjoyed much of it. While my review might come across as overly-critical, I still thoroughly enjoyed the game. It's beautiful, scenic, comprising of a rich atmosphere, and satisfying, grueling battles. I'd write more, but Steam has a review word limit. I would highly recommend this game, though—it's the beautiful underground brother of Terraria with a beautiful OST and tens, if not hundreds of hours for you to sink into it. I wish the best for this game and I can't wait to see it evolve.

_childDocuments_.review: Exploration: Fantastic (I really loved the Biomes)Progression: Fantastic (until towards the end of the game)Music: Fantastic (I will be listening to this OST on Spotify)Combat: Fantastic (It gets fast and intense)Gear/Loot: Very Good (The loot that they have currently is great but there is not much of it/It's the same thing just better stats)Sound Design: Very Good (Sometimes there are audio cues from monsters that play multiple times at the same time making it loud)         I strongly recommend this game if you like exploration/isometric combat (especially if you like Terraria). The pacing and progression of this game is fantastic.         I had a solo world and character for when my friends were offline and while I enjoyed playing with friends there was something magical with exploring the deepest dankest caves and biomes while being alone. It created a terrified feeling of what is hiding around the corner that will kill me next.         I played on normal difficulty and while some fights were easy because I progressed past them I still enjoyed all of the boss fights. The final couple of boss fights were pretty tough.         I have pretty much nothing but high praise, but there are a couple of things that I noticed that I hope gets fixed down the road. The final two biomes did not really have much going on in them. the second to last biome felt fine, but there was not that extra push to keep exploring once I realize there was really only one thing to do outside of getting the ore and getting out. The final area felt like it was rushed or the devs felt like they needed one more biome to make the game bigger. While I like the visuals and the encounter in that biome, it felt really empty once I realized what it was.         With those minor complains out of the way, I really hope these devs stick with the game and continue to progress the game/fill up the current map. They have plenty of space to work with with adding new things to do. I will keep my eye on this game going forward and will immediately jump back into it if they release new content.

This was a nice surprise.-  It’s satisfying to use minecart rails and cruising around with the boat.-  The game is a bit of a grind. Most of the time you will be searching for X in area X. -  It’s kind of a hassle and not too much fun at the start. Gets better later on.-  Could use more advanced features like automation.-  The game could use some more advanced chest management features like in Terraria. And some connection issues/low fps but not too often.If you don’t mind grinding for some specific resources from time to time to progress it is a satisfying survival game. _childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: 1/29/2024With numerous updates adding new features that smooth out the overall gameplay, especially with the QoL change to the multiple crafting stations being able to craft all tiers below them, the game has become significantly more enjoyable. There's a lot more variety in equipment, and the inclusion of pets and more unique collectables adds a lot more colour to the adventure. We've been surprised multiple times over how many new offerings and quality of life changes there were to play with since we last played.Sadly, the game still feels very on-rails after the initial starter bosses, but it's a very enjoyable game these days with much more to find than before. I can definitely recommend the game now, but it still could use some more of that same level of variety in exploration introduced toward the start of the game for its later areas, as well as more unique items/weapons to find at each tier to allow for more playstyle diversity.-(OUTDATED) Old Review:It's a bit checklist-y after the inner ring of bosses, even though it started out incredibly promising. I have more issues with the overarching game design than I do the direct gameplay, and it's really souring what would otherwise be really enjoyable.Really felt like a worthy Terraria-esque RPG where progression doesn't just go in a straight line and had a lot of cool things to discover at your own pace, but it kind of hits a wall (ironically) after you open the literal wall in the game surrounding the inner circle.Once you're beyond that, progression feels incredibly linear, with a pretty defined path of which bosses to fight or where to go because of how dangerous everything is. That, and materials required to tech up are found in specific biomes leading up to one another. Any attempt to skip or explore beyond the intended path at this point gets stifled by strict game design discouraging exploration through limiting your options.After playing for long enough, you also kind of realize there isn't anything unique to really collect that does anything noticeable besides useful passive bonuses. As far as weapons go, they all feel pretty much the same, and there's no creative magic like Terraria or wacky weapons to find like modded (or even vanilla) Starbound. Just some speed/scaling variations but no particularly differing movesets/summons/gimmicks. There's almost nothing to differentiate players' playstyles, especially when playstyle-relevant things like dodging/shielding or role-encompassing stats are strongly dictated by the resource/tech tier you're currently in, too.Building leaves very little to the imagination as well, with most essential components to a base being made irrelevant by other things in the techtree or just requiring too many things something else also needs- so they end up crammed in the same room as each other instead of encouraging us to sprawl them out elegantly. The inventory management leaves a lot to be desired as well, as managing chests and limited space even with upgrades feels frustrating when moving large amounts of items. Not to mention that the game has an incessant need to fill your inventory with valuables that do nothing but sell for currency, yet there's so many of them.I just can't recommend it. It starts out strong but the direction feels a little confused. It could change, but for now I just can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game and very much enjoyed pouring hundreds of hours of my life into it, and plan to do more in the near future. I finished my Normal mode playthrough and am just about to clean up and finish my Hard mode playthrough so I think I am just about qualified to put what I've gathered thus far:The game's storytelling is incredible. At the very beginning, you are thrown into a room with roots, dirt walls, and an inactive core, and even though nothing is explained to you, the design of the game is so intuitive that I went a really far ways into the game without even needing to look anything up on the wiki, which is incredibly rare for this style of game.I can clearly tell that the game was balanced incredibly well... for normal mode. I can feel myself getting stronger in a directly proportional relation to how much effort I put into growing my character, and the dopamine hit is insane as I walk into an area and get to participate in a mini bullet hell, only to come out on top. I think that that is a big part of the charm of the game.I love the way that food was implemented. There is an incredible amount of variety that comes with the choices you are allowed to make as a player when it comes to what you eat. I'd say that after 30 minutes of playtime, food becomes less of a hindrance and more a huge part of what gives this game its character. When I say that I can feel my strength increasing directly based on how much effort I put in, the food system plays probably the biggest role in that. There is no limit to the amount of buffs that you can have on your player, besides the amount of effort you are willing to put in to coordinating them. One caveat that I will note here- I play with the Keep Farming mod, which allows me to reliably fill up my tummy with a variety of Golden Crops really reliably once hitting farming 80, so my relationship with the food system isn't *entirely* vanilla.This does bring me onto my next point. The Mod Integration is also a really cool thing to have as a default setting in the game. There is no alternate version of the game to download or anything, or a third party to manage all the files through. Everything is hosted natively, and many of the mods exist solely to improve the game in ways that I think the base game could benefit greatly from. For some examples of mods that I really appreciate and why:-Keep Farming: Pretty self explanatory, allows me to take Core Keeper from a game where you can garden into a game where you can Farm, which is a huge difference. I do think that the game could benefit from a way to create more seeds from the ones you have planted (Maybe increase base seed reclamation % by 5%, so at Gardening 25 you get 105% seeds from crops?), especially since getting more seeds in huge quantities is pretty tough at all stages of progression.-Placement +, I think its called. I have a giant base in my hard mode run, and without this mod it still wouldn't be finished. Increase the scale of placement and shovel actions with keybinds and then alter greater parts of the world with it. This small QOL mod played likely the biggest part in shaping my experience in my latest playthrough.-Faster Minecarts: The world is infinitely large. Minecarts don't get any faster than the one obtained in the Forgotten Ruins. I think this is pretty self explanatory, as it keeps Minecart tracks both relevant and useful to the player, especially as the slower minecarts typically aren't fast enough to avoid getting killed by the Tentacles in the Sea or the Assassins in the Desert.Anyways, there's far more to this game than the modding, and I love every single thing about it, besides one important, glaring one.One of the complaints that I saw in the Core Keeper subreddit a couple of days ago was that the Bosses in hard mode were so incredibly easy and the mobs were too hard, and that one of the devs was confused by this since they hear a lot that the bosses are too hard, and the mobs are easy. I agree with both of these, and it stems from the fact that Hard mode is definitely in dire need of some balancing assistance. I get that its hard difficulty, but that is no excuse to be getting consistently 2-shot at EVERY stage of the game. The slimes in the dirt biome deal a good chunk of health, but its nothing to really worry about. I stepped foot into the clay caves and got dropped immediately into dangerously low health by a single spear, dealing 130 damage in a place where there are not many options to increase the health pool or armor stat of the player. I immediately hid back in my base and fished for a while to gather some resources and try again. Despite preparing, 2 shots still would've killed me, just for stepping into the second area of the game.This is a constant story throughout the whole game. From what I can see, Normal difficulty is balanced so that by the time you make it into a new biome, a roughly equivalent amount of hits will kill you based on the relationship between your Max Health, Armor, and enemy damage. The thing that really changes the game is the enemy mechanics, which makes for a game that doesn't get more damaging, just more technical at a rate at which the player can pick it up.This balance falls apart immediately on Hard Difficulty. If you had 80 points of armor on Normal, and an enemy deals 150, you'd take 70 points of damage. That's fair, as it gives you as the player room to make mistakes and still feel like you are growing in strength. In Hard Difficulty, the damage doubles. This seems like it should be fine as a difficulty increase, but in practice the amount of damage taken is far more than double due to the fact that none of your defensive stats become more effective. With 70 points of armor, you don't take double damage from an enemy that deals 150 in normal, you take something closer to triple due to the fact that your defensive stats consistently lag behind in all stages of the game.At no point in the game can I feel myself as a player getting stronger, just that I am barely holding on. Just as enemies in the Clay Caves 2 shot me, as so enemies in the Forgotten ruins, the Azeos Wilderness, the Sunken Sea, The Desert (to an extreme degree) and the Shimmering Frontier (at a point where it just feels insane.) Whenever engaging with the combat system gets you sent home every 10 minutes, players are incentivized to play defensively at all times, and are punished for spreading their wings. This led me to a gameplay loop where I would play a little bit in the zone to find a boulder, hide in my base and upgrade, and then run to the next zone and do the next. By the time that I had gotten to the point where I was running out of upgrades to do to my gear, I was still getting killed almost immediately by random events outside of my control. I think that if the damage stats were identical on paper as it got processed through your defensive stats, and THEN got doubled, instead of being doubled already when it ran through, the difficulty would be a lot more consistent and manageable for players such as myself (i.e. 300 damage - 70 defense = 230 damage vs. (150 damage - 70 defense = 80 damage) x2 = 160 damage. I think this would be far better as, in late game areas, I'm consistenly taking what feels like 5-6x the damage from enemy attacks, instead of the double I was told to expect.Besides the (imo) poor balancing on the hard mode side of things, the devs have put together an incredible game that is filled with some of the best gameplay and most enthralling visual storytelling I've ever encountered in a game, and for incredibly cheap at that. Definitely recommend.Oh and, dodge chance maxes out at 90%, but defense only blocks up to 75%. Was this intentional?tl,dr: Incredible game, immediately became one of my favorites of all time. Could use some more QOL, Hard Mode balancing is wack (or personal skill issue tbh), but still a 9.9/10 normal mode.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this with 20 hours in and having bought CORE KEEPER just after 1.0 release.This is a NO SPOILERS REVIEW!!====VERDICT=================!If you were the type of person in STARDEW VALLEY that would spend most of their time in the mines and exploring, CORE KEEPER is for you!!============================!CORE KEEPER has great pixel art polish: It has cute art, character, enemies, and more, coupled with amazing reflection and lighting tech that makes the world feel alive.The music is very calming and doesn't bother.The controls are intuitive and are easy to pick up, and can be comfortably played on both controller and keyboard&mouse setups.CORE KEEPER shines very bright when you bring someone with you, and it's very easy to do so, with "Game ID" sharing. It's easy to hop in and out of a game at any time, and ingame chat support makes it easy to communicate.The gameplay loop revolves around EXPLORATION and expanding your crafting options. EVERYTHING you do in the game will accrue experience, even moving around. You'll get points and then you can spend those points into a three tiered talent tree that accomodates your favorite playstyle. CORE KEEPER also makes it easy to reset your skills in case later on you want to try something new with your skills. Even FISHING in this game will translate to combat buffs eventually, a passive way to encourage players to engage with ALL aspects of it.As for gear, you have the option to switch between 3 different sets: you can gear up for adventure, for mining, for gardening, or whatever mix you choose to be. Fighting playstyle is malleable, with melee, ranged, magic, minion, and with each player getting pet companions that excel in different areas while having randomized skill trees out of a specific pet type pool.I recommend not watching any trailers or media and just jumping into it! There are so many things to discover, and really, the sense you get from discovering what each thing does, and how to best use them, will make for hours and hours of fun!It has native MODDING support with community pumping out incredible work that increases accessibility, adds quality of life features, and explores different map seeds.It has been a long time coming for this game, having spent a lot of time in early access, and I can't wait to see what the developers and the community have in the future for it.Let's roll, Keepers!!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't leave reviews often, but I felt like I needed to leave one for this game.If you like stardew, Minecraft, and terraria, You'll like this game. It's like Minecraft and terraria had a child with the looks of stardew. (which is something I've been wanting since forever).Pros:+ stat system is excellent + challenging bosses+ Swift/Smooth controls and combat that feels amazing+ procedural generated worlds that feel expansive (and maybe really expansive, cause I still haven't reached the edges yet)+ you can save and quit wheneverCons:- Work benches aren't upgraded, instead you build a new one with new materials and it doesn't contain the old recipes from the old work bench; So you're going to have several workbenches and anvils of different types placed in your work area.- Not much if any filler content between bosses. (no quests, objectives, etc. at least that I've encountered).- Wall and floor materials are separate, so you can't use a wall to fill a hole; You Can't craft flooring from it's wall counter part either, so you'll have to dig a hole to fill a hole. (this is just based on my exp. you may be able to, I just haven't encountered it yet).--------------------Something I hope gets added is some NPC objectives like "bring me a mushroom for X coins" or "fight 10 slimes for X amount of coins". Just so players have something to do that isn't digging, fishing, or combat.Its pretty great for an early access game! It's a nice game to relax with, definitely worth the 12.99.---------------------I'm 8.9 hrs into the game right now, and I'm still not bored, nor have I ran out of content (this may be because I am taking my time and exploring, not speeding through everything). About 7-8.0 hours into the game is when I finally took on my first attempt at the first boss.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the same gameplay loop, that is dig, build new work stations, new gear, kill the boss, repeat. You may have heard this from Terraria, except that game has more enticing combat than this. Analogy: This is the start of hardmode (in Terraria) except, you have to make a new forge and anvil for every ore you find. The best part? The digging takes longer and longer the farther you progress. You go from walls taking 3 or so hits to break, to progressively taking more hits to destroy. I'm at the point where you require scarlet ore, and the walls take 10 hits with my iron pickaxe to break. I seriously question the developers insight in thinking this was a good idea.Did they even play test?Yes you can say to use the rock and stone ring set, yes you can say to reinforce your pickaxe. But I simply dont understand where the numbers come from. The small boost from the reinforced pickaxe to brings 10 hits to 7, and with the ring set 7 to 4. I believe the damage number is just there for show.I also question why feel the need to add more rings and jewellery to this game, if the developers expect you to only use the  rock and stone ring set. With the amount of time bloat this game has, you would expect it to be a live service subscription based game. The mining speed is unnecessarily predatory.I bought this game on 40% discount and still felt like I had overpaid. The only consolation was that the start of the game was good with the first boss. But after that you realise that the game no longer has any innovation and it is the same repetition but increasingly more time consuming. A grind to consume your soul. The only difference is the scenery which has, admittedly good artwork and lighting. Bosses can't be repeated, albeit I've heard they can later in the game, therefore if you get bad loot, gg go next, start a new run. Items intended to be sold (valuables) sell for nothing, only 10 - 50 currency, where as figurines (this is an item designed to be a base decoration) sell for 200. The pet you buy at the merchant does more damage than any weapon you can find pre-scarlet ore.This game is very questionable, and is in Early Access for a reason. I hope the developer can make the game more reasonable to play, as I apologise, but I do not find sitting at my desk, holding the mine button for 10 seconds just to destroy a single wall, which I need to mine thousands of, just to find hundreds of ore in that area to progress to the next stage, enjoyable. If you are brain dead and enjoy games active 'idle' games, then please, try this game out. This game might be the one piece you were lacking in all your life.But as for the rest of you, look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: This game seemed unremarkable when i first encountered the early access, but i was quickly charmed by the gameplay and especially charming graphics~if you like Terraria, this is a must-try! I love the innovative map generation thats kept in rings, which makes it really fun to explore in all directions! Even the building aspect of the game surprised me, because from first glance it seems that you dont have many options besides your average brick and hay walls, but the generated structures and painting option offers alot of variety to cook up some absolutely beautiful builds (not to mention the gorgeous gernerated builds all across the world, i love stopping by these and taking screenshots)!The ore progression is not too slow, and also not too quickly overcome, and i like the creativity with the in-game metals after you get past gold.The combat is fun and not too clunky, and the upgrading of weapons into late-game is something i wish other titles would do as well.HOWEVER:There are two gripes i have with this game, and they are a kind of annoying thing to deal with...The first being the durability system. In my opinion, these just straight up consume more time than you should be needed to put in. It become annoying real quickly, especially when you're working on large scale builds (there is a skill in the mining tree that lets you regain durability points when mining ore, but its not broad enough to fix the issue, like with weapons or armor for example).There have been one or two cases where my armor broke through a boss fight, and i had to take a larger  break in order to renew the items i needed to beat the boss...Speaking of bosses, there comes my other main gripe with this game. and unfortunately, this one really stings. Call me a bad gamer but this thing needs a desperate rework. Im talking about Omoroth, the boss residing within the sunken sea. Let me ask you this, if you die to a boss, you probably try to get back there as soon as possible to give it another shot, right?Well, unfortunately, with Omoroth, that can be pretty difficult. His arena consists mostly of water, and thus, making a boat to fight him is essential.Sure, you could cover the entire area in walkable tiles, but Oh-Oh, you didn't account for the tentacles that spawn, which break tiles in a 2 by 2 area wherever they are summoned. And he summons *alot* of tentacles, Pair that with his absurdly unfair vortex attacks, and you have the recipe for a downright unfair and unfun Boss, thatll force you to go on a major collection detour to get another boat, or tiles, if you die to him.Unfotunately, Omoroth in my eyes takes this game down quite a few tiers.Despite that though! I still love this game!!! Its charming, its cute, its well-packed full of stuff, but not at all overbearing, and not too grindy whatsoever! in my opinion, 7/10, and a deffinate recommendation to people who love sandbox games and terraria lovers!

_childDocuments_.review: Alrighty, I can do this in a 3 bullet list:- If you have friends and like playing crafting/exploration procedural RPGs. Go Go Go! It's a lot without help.- If you're a completionist, avoid, unless you have a Frankenstein-level boner for these kind of games. PSA: I do not have said boner for this game. Seriously, I employed years of macro knowledge and still took 80+ hours to 100%. I could have done it faster, sure, but only by sucking every ounce of fun out of the game.It does have some beautiful bosses though, and some wonderful biomes, and a ton of cool different gameplay options that I think really pushed the boundary of optimizing your little world. That was a feel, but it only lasted as long as me and my friends had vertical content to consume. Everything after that felt like a massive grind.
