_childDocuments_.review: I came to this game expecting a Terraria or Minecraft like experience (Like a block based, base builder combat thing) and first impressions were solid. Fun gimmicks and varied environments made the first 5-10 hours fly by, especially with a friend on board. The progression was obvious and didnt require a wiki to survive. The bosses werent anything special but made good milestones (even though you can over gear and stomp them).However, when you beat the opening few bosses, the world opens up massively with a bunch of new environments and this is where the game loses most of its fun. The environments you gain access to are massive, repeating areas with little gameplay and enemy variety with these vast, sprawling dungeons with nothing interesting to offer as a reward. No cool weapons or armour, just random supplies. On top of this the game just gets unnecessarily confusing in what drops what and where. There is no rhyme or reason to some of these things like a card thats wiki description indicates you might find it in the desert. Not a 0.02% chance to drop from breakable items in a specific small biome. Similarly the armour progression is confusing as like in Terraria you can spec into ranged, melee, magic and summoning however the sets that improve these stats are rare drops from enemies rather than having dedicated crafting options. My friend who went ranged got stuck in the dilemma of using armour that was outdated or using armour that had no benefit to his class but meant he would die in 3 hits instead of 2.The next problem is the downtime that this game has a serious problem with, especially later in the game. Some of the later ores in this game take 32 seconds to smelt 1 bar which wouldnt be so bad of the economy for these bars wasnt so scuffed with weapon and armour sets requiring 40 bars at time. Everything in this game feels like the timer is bloated. I think the item that sums this up the most would be the portal. The Portal is a near necessary item for returning to farther areas but the requirements are ludicrous. 100 bars of 3 different ores along with wood planks that also take time to cut and then once the thing is built, you have to wait 10 minutes for it to activate. And for games that have similar timers like Stardew, the main difference is you can leave the bars smelt and go do other things with your time whereas in this game the only thing you can do is either wait or go mine more ore to spend more time waiting.This game has so much potential and I overall recommend the first couple of hours but this game turns into a massive grind so be warned. And the game is finally seeing progress towards a semi easy to work with inventory system

_childDocuments_.review: Let me tell you the story of how I said "I'm not ready for another 80-hours-game" after finishing Baldur's Gate 3 and then put 100 hours into Core Keeper.It's a game that sucks you in and it needs no tutorial for it. You just go out, explore, dig, craft, fight and progress through the game quite organically. One of the best aspects of the game is that it's not grindy at all - very uncommon for these kind of games. The soundtrack is awesome, the pixel art is cute and the surface reflections are gorgeous. Core Keeper has interesting biomes to discover, bosses to fight, a nice item system and even basic automation. Which I recommend to use since inventory management is an issue (but bearable for me).One of the few games I restarted right after finishing it. You can start a new map with the same character or inherit your old map with a new one, besides starting completely over, of course.

_childDocuments_.review: 1.0 just released and I gave it a try, and I'm rewriting my review. The thing I enjoyed the most about this game is exploration, especially secret areas like the royal tombs. However it does get a little old after I've seen almost everything each area has to offer. Overall the experience was alright, not mind-blowing, but it's an okay game to kill some time with. I'll probably play it again some time in the future whenever I feel the itch.I feel like this game has so much potential but there are so many aspects of it that are so lackluster. It's such a shame. It's the kind of game that doesn't have enough to get me fully invested but pretty cozy to play for some casual gaming.Here are some things that I wish were included in the game or could be improved upon: -Quick-storing items to nearby chests. I was playing with a controller and inventory management has been such a pain. -More weapons choices. Melee weapons have such close range that I didn't even bother with them 'cause it's just too dangerous.The fireball staff is just so much better than bows that I've been using it all the time since I got it early game. The summons don't do much so I stopped using them when my pet got strong enough. The weapon design just lacks certain creativity. Combat gets boring when I'm using the same staff 95% of the time because of how good it is. The upgrade system sounds like a good idea at first but then it just gets boring since it means I'm still using the same thing. No ability upgrade or extra perks or whatsoever. Only the number grows bigger and bigger.-Cooking lacks creativity too. Being able to cook with any two ingredients sounds great but it really isn't. I just end up stuck with 3 or 4 dishes with my preferred buffs and don't bother to make anything else. I think it would be great to have like an advanced cooking station that allows you to cook certain recipes with better and more interesting effects.-Enemies don't despawn. It's especially annoying when you're visiting an area that you haven't been to for a long time, then you're gonna find the entire place crawling with enemies. There might be a limit to how many can be spawned in to an area, but I'm not sure.-Something to stop enemies from being spawned near my base. There's this new giant mushroom enemy now and it freaking destroys blocks. It's such a pain that I can't keep my mushroom farm the way it is. -Collection system. Something like a museum or whatnot for all the insects, critters and treasures I find. I don't think there's anything you can do with the bugs you catch except for feeding them to the animals but I could be wrong. It's kind of a shame that there are so many different critters for each biome but not much to do with them.

_childDocuments_.review: Thanks to the change in the repair mechanic from scrap parts to partial recipe costs a lot has changed, rare items like the mining grenade launcher are no longer priced posessions but something that will inevitable become useless since there's no way to repair them without recipe materials since they aren't crafted. You can forget spending your first of a higher tier material you worked hard to get on your favorite tool, why bother till you can get lots? it's just gonna break and need stuff you barely managed to scrape together instead of scrap, ducktape and prayers.  Since ores are a finite ressource, you will be forced to mine ever further out just to repair your gear , overtime reducing progress speed because a portion of your gains will be spend on repairing your tools. _childDocuments_.review: the whole game is basically early hard mode terraria, just working through ore tiers over and over. It gets kinda dull and this game could be made a lot better by changing up how you get ores and better gear. For instance maybe one of the ore tiers you get by killing enemies or finding chests. Digging through walls that take a full minute to break over and over is pretty awful. there is also items you need to craft armor sets that the game doesn't explain in the slightest how to get, so its easy to get lost. Plus you could just move on to the next ore tier and hope the next set doesn't have the same ingredients. fishing also kinda sucks in this game. its original how you catch the fish but that doesn't make it fun. plus, fishing rods aren't cheap to craft and the reward you get from them is very limited. also the basic swords for ore tiers are way under powered for how risky they are to use. Its not a bad game, but i would really like to see these issues addressed before a full release.

_childDocuments_.review: So, Core Keeper, is it worth it? You're probably thinking that, if you're looking at reviews before buying the game. Short answer: If you like building bases, exploring, and enjoy progress, then I would say yes. The game offers a nice progress system, and allows for a simple multiplayer system for coop. If you want to know more, you can keep reading.Having a feeling of Stardew Valley and Terraria, You start in a dark cold cave world, filled with mysteries, creatures, and bugs worst of all. You'll have to diggy hole your way around to collect various resources for progressing against a various amount of bosses.Although the game has a fun unique experience, you should know that there are issues that I have to address. As I write this review, the Desert of beginnings update has been out for not too long, so things might change. So firstly, my biggest issue is that although the game has lots of content as it is, none of it is really fleshed out. Let me give you an example:The game has different transport systems such as minecarts, boats, and cars. Despite what you think, they are very basic, as in you can only use them to move around, and don't offer extra inventory space or use to make moving unexplored regions easier.-Minecarts are simple, yet they ask a lot of resources for how little use they offer. It's best to use other modes of transportation.-Boats are currently the most useful for simple navigation, but there's only 2 variants, one of which is quite expensive just to go faster.-Cars are the most recent in the game, and offer more than the 2 others. They have 3 variants. The first one, being the primitive car, can be found in the world, and is overall the weakest. Second one is all about turning good and having a quick top speed. Lastly, the third one is way too fast, which I personally find impractical, since you can't really react in time before crashing into a wall and getting butchered by 9 daggers in the back (you'll know when it happens to you).Despite this, it is just an example of what I think the game has issues with. It's best that you do not base your entire view of the game on it. The game still has a lot to offer in terms of entertainment, with plenty of updates to come. I hope to see you all out there exploring the deep dark caves of Core Keeper.

_childDocuments_.review: The game doesn't autosave and it has spiralled me into a progression depression twice now.Corekeeper doesn't fail as a game, it has a charm akin to Terraria. In Corekeeper you grind endlessly to level up your skills and get gear, I'd say the majority of the game is spent on this. Which in itself isn't the worst, many games do this. The problem is that the game only saves whenever you exit your world, so if the game ever crashes for any reason before you save and exit, you lose ALL your progress; in your world and character both. And while it doesn't crash all the time, when it does it is DEVASTATING. I've lost countless hours of progress to this issue, I am beyond infuriated.For me, until they fix this issue Corekeeper is simply too risky to invest your time into at the moment. Just play through Terraria instead.

_childDocuments_.review: A must have for Terraria fans, Stardew Valley combat enthusiasts, people looking for a game to play with friends, or anybody looking for a challenge! Core Keeper is very charming and beautiful but also quite hard at times. Has a bit of automation for people who are crazy about that, but its not fully necessary to finish the game for people who dont like that (me), the most complex being needing to know how to drill big ore boulders. Also lots of customization and base decorating options, and awesome scenes that can be found randomly around the world that makes exploration refreshing every time you have to go out.The only downsides, in my opinion, are that: It can get a fair bit grindy at times, but I think this can be avoided when playing with friends. Also the inventory management can get a bit tedious. I would also love to see more weapons, especially more summoning books or stronger magic things. Looking forward to this game getting updates or DLCs!!

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game more than I actually do.  I played both during first release during early access and after 1.0.  The game is a fun, casual, survival/mining romp up until you get passed the content that was available at initial release.  The grind significantly increases, the new biomes actively work to be "unfun," and the bosses at that point are miserable.  It is simply not fun having to grind up 200x of various not-so-easy to get resources that take forever to refine just to build one important structure or even a faster version of vehicle. It's also not fun getting to a water biome where it's safer and easier just to build land bridges because going out on the water with a boat will inevitably end with you needing to build a land bridge to get your body/boat back.In short, much of the newer content is padded out with grind/difficulty rather than anything unique.  Once you've done a few iterations of "find new biome, get new flavor of ore, beat boss" you won't find much else offered.  The early game will make you think otherwise because you get mazes, puzzles, and other scenes that give you hope that your experience will be varied going forward.  Sadly, if anything, it gets simpler as you go.At the very least, I would suggest the developers seriously consider the cost of late game items.  Requiring rare drops for upgrades, hundreds of resources, or drop-dependent items just for one try at a boss, is not fun.  Many items need to be re-balanced to feel meaningful and purposeful in the game.  Choosing to try the warlock/mage class will lock you out of many crafting options because you simple cannot craft magic-relevant armor or weapons and the ones you find are of limited use (e.g., summoned mobs barely engage enemies, staves that can blow you up as fast as they can enemies).  Lastly, there are a lot of seemingly "unfinished" ideas with crafting benches that could give this game a healthy boost.  Automation could be a lot of fun but there is little point with the available tools provided (need load balancing at the very least).In short, I'd wait for the developers to refine the game further before diving in with your friends.

_childDocuments_.review: review based on 1.0 Sadly I lost my motivation to finish the main story after 40 hours. This game starts really great and promising but becomes a grind boredom after the first 3 bosses. ///// Negative highlights /////- The wizard / summoner class is unplayable due to the difficulty bump after the initial 3-4 bosses. the summons are not strong enough and with the summoner gear you die from any mob with 2-3 hits , for me specially the desert area became unplayable as summoner. I dont want to kill extra bosses just to maybe find better gear for these classes. I found myself forced to switch mid game to melee and  just lost interest.- The digging and exploration is not rewarding at all like in Terraria for instance. And as soon as a Ore boulder is found there is no real need to explore , you just grind Ore and wait for the drill so you can purchase / improvve gear, become strong enough for one boss, just to start over again.- Enemy variety way too short. Each biome maybe 3-4 enemies, becomes boring quickly- Weapon variety also short, focusing on main story you will skip probably most of the uinteresting weapons. The main story is grinding enough so I the extra grind to get maybe some better gear was pointless to me.- Mining cart system: after 1,0 there are portals which can be moved around, so the mining cart experience became useless and should be rethought- the NPCs are useless, they dont even defend themselves on an attack like in Terraria, it feels very boring as they just walk around///// Positive highlights /////- simple crafting / harvesting / fishing system for casual play- nice pixel art and Envionments- No dialogues at all if you dont want complexity, just straight to the bosses/// OVERALL ////If you loved Terraria and want a similar game and if its at a cheap price, I would recommend it. Just keep in mind it gets very boring at mid game and the motivation to keep going goes very low.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks cute and fun on the surface but underneath is a hilariously unbalanced and anti-fun grindfest. There's a point where some bosses are literally unbeatable with skill. You just need to spend hours grinding for higher stats or making specific builds, It feels much less like a game and more like a puzzle at that point. I'm sure part of our issues came from playing on hard but that's another problem in it's entirety. When I think hard I think "can be overcome with practice and more skill". Not whatever this is. We specifically struggled with the boss "Omoroth". It's sad because the core gameplay is fun, the visuals are beautiful, the soundtrack is good. But the balancing and grind are just godawful and feel like they needlessly prolong the game. We loved the experience past the first three bosses,We typically enjoy hard games. Unfortunately this games difficulty doesn't come from requiring more skill but requiring more time and knowledge, which is just not fun. Again it'd be acceptable if time and knowledge were a substitute to make it easier for those struggling and not a base requirement.All in all I believe the game's worth keeping an eye on. At the moment the gameplay just starts to deteriorate past the 5 hour mark.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game combining elements of Terraria and Stardew, Lots of ups, some downs. Exploration:Great and rewarding given there are unique points of interest to find, 1 of each in a world. Beautiful biomes and designs. Utilizing minecarts, conveyor belts, teleports, nothing feels "too far".Combat:Rough at the start, but felt fluid after getting a dash.  Weapons felt kind of lacking, maybe just compared to Terraria, cant wait for more.Bosses? Meh. of the 17 only 4 felt Unique and interesting Progression:Almost all boss summons are cramped into one UI making it awkward to find the order.Upgrade progression doesnt feel right. You can get to endgame gear after 3 basic bosses. Hope they implement Ores connected to bosses.Skill leveling system is great, putting offensive stats in farming/fishing/mining/cooking gives more of a reason to do them even for the group's "Warrior"XP gain rate needs some kind of progression, as of now crafting with dirt gives the same (1) Xp as with crafting with endgame ore. Most skill's grind boils down to: "Autoclicker"Building/Decorating:99% of things you see in the world can be picked up, and used as decoration.Giant bug Carcass? Sure it will look good in my garden!Alien Meteorite Egg? Give it!It being 2D "limits" the possibilities, but hey, that never stopped Terraria build artists!

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like Terraria takes a step back from 2d action adventure with a dash of crafting and goes instead top-down full crafting open world.  Combat is serviceable, progression is the usual 'kill the bosses to progress' style gating.  Good for kicking on a podcast and whiling away some time, but it is screaming for something more to it to give it a bit more identity.  Also, for the love of god devs, if you give us a teleport home item, make it create a 1 time return portal.  We had this banged out all the way back in the Diablo days, making me walk all the way back across a quarter of the world to where I was mining when I needed to dump inventory is a step back in the wrong direction for pointless padding, especially when I have to build the dang things and they are 1 time use.TL:DR - If you like Minecraft and Terraria, this will scratch a lot of the same itches.  Good for podcast binging, but you'll need the podcast because it lacks some identity of it's own here.

_childDocuments_.review: Played for the two hours beating the first slime and game never grabbed my interest. Everything felt really grindy and item management felt like a chore. Maybe better with multiple people but lacking any local coop or remote play together features.1.0 Update- I played for another 6 hours on the free update on a new 1.0 world. I still found it grindy with small inventories and having to constantly return to base to put things away. I searched for two hours for tin, found lots of iron and gold, before I finally broke down and looked online for where to find the stuff, turns out there is a specific biome you have to look for in a specific direction. As far as I know there are no hints for this in game at all and extremely frustrating. Maybe add a core craft where it can point you towards the tin and iron biome like the boss finder?I made maybe 8 different crafting benches but didn't use any of the automation or drill mining stuff because I didn't know if it'd be useless soon? I found one warp teleport and if those were all over I wouldn't need the mine carts to get around and with the craftable warp to base item you can soon not having to worry about returning to that track spot. I wasn't sure how the drill worked on the large rocks if I had to sit around and wait for it to complete, if the ore vein ever disappeared, or if the items it mined up disappeared if I wasn't there. For the conveyor belts I also didn't know if they worked when you were on the other side of the map like in other games. Overall I don't think it's bad but I just didn't enjoy it and still feel it must be balanced for multiplayer because I found it extremely grindy.

_childDocuments_.review: Wildly positively surprised and impressed by this game. Absolutely love the retro graphics with modern fluid movements and dynamic lighting. Has the elements I love from games like Harvest Moon or Stardew Valley, without the daily time constraints or stamina limitations. Character creation gives incentive bonuses to choosing roles for characters, making multiplayer more of a role-playing environment. _childDocuments_.review: I couldn't currently recommend this game for people who have played games like Valheim, Terraria, Stardew Valley. My chief criticisms: - The mechanics are done better in other games- This game doesn't have enough content yet- Some of the content is boring and unrewarding, especially the two dungeon types (larval and fungal)- Game seems too easy, including bosses (just spam bombs and drink health potions)Having said that, the game is on the right track. The music is wonderful, and they've managed to make a completely underground game pretty bright and interesting. I think with new updates they could pad this out and make it a very playable game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing since it was very small, while the game is ABSOLUTELY huge (and the biomes are bigger than my future) what makes the game great are the devs. The devs listen to players and their critiques and they're constantly striving to make the game better, which is seemingly challenging for alot of games nowadays. That was a huge highlight for me, all the little things inbetween the big updates were generous. I told myself I'd post a review once I got the perfect achievements (did I mention how happy I was once they added achievements?) the randomness of trying to find the points of interest or the key places are.. rough. (I walked past the eye shrine about 6 times before I found it) Then I'd get angry and come back and garden fiercely. I appreciate some of the bosses having locators because without it, I would not have found some of the bosses (especially Azeos since the wilderness and desert and beach are HUUUUUGE Biomes)All in all, I definitely recommend this game.It's a fun little time spender (my 300 hours say hello), it's not taxing on the PC or the wallet.Buckets are coming (as I cry since I dug from the beach, desert and wilderness to my base) :imfine:There's always new content coming in some way.Glow tulips are shiny. <3The game is fun with friends, the base building has potential but still plenty to go. You can create as much or as little as you want, there's no requirement. The bosses aren't challenging enough to be strictly difficult (I say as I've never dared go to hard mode) and the soundtrack is soothing.

_childDocuments_.review: First - don't let the hrs on record be an indicator of the grind involved.  About 2/3's of my played time has been OCD related developing/changing my base, acquiring EVERY item in the game to display on pedestals, etc. etc.  That is not to say there is not countless hours worth of content to experience just playing the main content.  I picked this up shortly after their first EA update a few years ago and have been hooked every since.  A great example of a game where the devs have a continued passion to make a great product and iterate/update on it, listen to community feedback and (because I feel it needs to be said given the state of much of gaming) don't feel the need to push an agenda and then complain when their game fails.  The volume of content released during EA has been nothing short of remarkable, consistently updating their living roadmap and I look forward to all Post 1.0 content.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game is trying really hard to be the next Terraria. But its just lacking substantial content. Art style is nice, and the early game play loop is fine. But it gets repetitive really quickly and you end up in end game so quickly that you realize that there is barely anything to explore and ultimately do. Performance in this game is also not ideal but acceptable for a early access title. The grindy skill tree is mostly devoid of any choice, and is so grindy that I cannot imagine the effort needed to even see the later skills of the trees.For now I suggest just waiting until more content updates unless you really want to play around with what is essentially a demo of a game. Recent updates like the new desert biome haven't brought me back into the game as I expect its more of the same fluff that the water biome had. The boat mechanic was such a joke that I just ended up building land bridges instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game, I just finished the first boss and I thought I would write down my initial impression. It reminds me strongly of Keplerth It also reminds me of Minecraft and TerrariaOne of my favorite features of this game is it is absolutely pitch black underground and if you don't have a light source you can't see anything. Some games will make it really dim without a light but not this game. Definitely makes the first boss more terrifying as it keeps smashing your torches; plunging the world into darkness.The cooking setup is fun, so far it seems you can combine any two ingredients and you will get a unique food item that looks like a combination of the two and gives you bonuses from each part. I'm looking forward to finding more seeds and experimenting with all the combinations and seeing all the different artwork.Skill trees are a fun idea and I like being rewarded for all the endless mining with something tangible. All in all I'm enjoying the experience. There are lots of little hints in item descriptions that suggest things to try like building a room and encouraging specific people to take up residence Terraria style.But truly the best part is it's early access so who knows what other fun features will be added!

_childDocuments_.review: I actually like this better than Minecraft for reasons I don't fully understand yet. It seems perhaps more streamlined or less confusing. I'm playing this with my two kids, aged 7 and 9 and it is complex enough to keep me, a 40ish year old man entertained, but easy enough for small children to grasp. Unfortunately there is no split screen type co-op, but that is understandable imo because otherwise you'd be tied to the same area or the screen would be too small. The upside is this motivated me to smash together a couple of old PCs into a new frankenstein gamish. It is an interesting evolution, from iPad kids, to playing on PC with Xbox controllers, and now eventually somewhat with the mouse. At least they're seeing it is way easier to navigate and aim using mouse rather than the controllers. Anyways, we're currently 4 hours in and having a blast. There is enough decorating and building for my daughter, enough exploring and fishing for my skittish son, and enough logistics, organization, combat, and complexity to keep my adult gaming sensibilities fulfilled. That's a pretty tall order if you think about it, and it makes sense why this game has such great reviews. Another benefit to the devs (and Steam for that matter) to this more cheap co-op game is now each kid has their own Steam account, own PC, and own copies of Core Keeper. Nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Review at Patch: 1.0.0.7Hours Clocked: 70.7Face it, if you are into this genre you have probably already played Terraria, Necesse, and Don't Starve (Together). You have probably clocked hundreds of hours at the least and like me you were hungry for more.I have checked in with Core Keeper since it first became available, stopping at the first titan that was originally available. While I enjoyed myself then, I really wanted to wait until the game was fully released before I dove in. Since then, I have doubled my time in game and for good reason.If you are new to this style of game, the premise is simple. You start with little more than a backstory and a mysterious set of statues. I will touch on the backstories in a moment, but essentially you are now tasked with getting your bearings and eventually downing all the bosses in order to get home.With that in mind, let us return to the backstory you can choose at the beginning.  From professions like Fisher, Explorer, Chef, Fighter, Mage, Warlock, etc you are getting a small bump to start in that  path. Some get early gear, and if you are going to min/max or speed run, these choices matter a little. No matter what you choose, you can do all of it.As you play, you will accrue skill points just by doing "that" action. Your mage finds a sword and now you have decided melee combat is the better path? You will earn the respective points as you go, so mage start or not, you are not stuck with that choice. Conversely, if you find a sweet mage staff, you can go back to slinging magic or decide both is a fun option.As you level up, every so many skill points will move you up a tier. This lets you choose an associated perk and instead of being cumbersome, it is small stat boosts to lean into your style of play. In Co-Op this means you can lean into being the group farmer, or generalize and do whatever. No one tree is overpowered or underpowered and getting skills as you go means your character is always adapting to how you are playing.That said, there are also pets you can get that will also get skills in the same manner. These pets can buff your stats to further specialize your character, or to round out other skills. For example a melee oriented player might want a pet to buff their movement speed and pick a pet that buffs that, or they might choose a pet to buff their ranged attacks for when melee is not ideal.Combat for the most part is attacking with one click, but some weapons do have an alternate attack. Otherwise, it breaks down to simply dodging or attacking. There is enough depth that a mage will play differently than a melee, but shallow enough that playing with friends does not require them all to be able to clear a no hit run in a souls like.In addition to all of that, food and potions further specialize your character. Add in a variety of weapons and armor, and you will find there is a lot you can mess with but not get bogged down.Exploring the world is mostly gated by gear or skill. While a boss is not gated, you might find tackling them in a mild order is easier if you are geared up with the materials found in that biome. There are a lot of good looking biomes, and while some enemies are common like slimes and cavelings, there is enough variety that each area does not feel like a reskin of the last one.Last but not least, builders will find lots of options to decorate, design and paint their new home. You can transport a biome's block, water, and decor to suit your tastes. Want to theme it? Go for it. Want to make a cozy fishing hole? Absolutely. Want to make it a dystopian hellscape full of monsters? Yep! There are even traps to farm them.Overall my recommendation of Core Keeper is Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: FANTASTIC GAME! Picked this up with my GF and we love this so much! _childDocuments_.review: So the game isn't completely bad, but if you believe reviews saying it's like Terraria, you'll be disappointed. It's not an adventure, it's a farming and mining game.After almost 2 hours I still haven't found anything interesting in progression or exploration, the game felt like chores. I'm not going to wait another 2/5/10 hours more just for a chance that it might get better.This is purely as if the Hill-top(mining) farm from Stardew was the whole game. It's just tedious mining, planting, and hoping you'll be able to automate it soon so that you can go look for something more fun to do.Terraria was about the mystery of exploration and treasure hunting. There you always expect treasure with unique materials, gear, new unique weapon. Entering a new biom you can always expect some new materials for crafting and (mini)boss or special event. With that gear you want to always try something new, something different and not just next tier set.Here it's all missing. - Get wood - craft wooden gear, then get copper - craft copper gear, get iron - craft iron gear. There is no horizontal progression, only stats upgrades. There is no variation or side-grades, or character building beyond choosing a class. You get a class specific set with a set bonus, which is like 1/3 of total set's power so you really don't want to mix it with anything else. - Combat feels boring. You have 3 basic classes with boring weapons; melee, range, magic. Weapons in each class don't have much variation and all feel the same. Summoner might not exist at all with how awful it feels: resummon pet every ~20 sec, broken AI that constantly stops attacking, pathfinding issues, needs a full set buff and 3 minions to be close to basic mage staff. With summoning frequency and amount of mana it requires, you can’t really mix it with mage.- Exploration is extremely boring. There is no interesting or unique loot, ruins only give the items that you could craft on your crafting bench. Just points of interest with increased quantities of the same materials. - Farming feels extremely clunky and tedious. You can't hold the mouse button to till the soil since it will then automatically turn it back to dirt, and you can only till the adjacent block. Plants growing time is in a weird spot where it is too long to just keep planting, gathering, and planting again with new seeds, but it's also short enough that when you are done planting and crafting, it will grow just a few minutes after you leave the base to explore. So there's a lot of time your farm is not growing.- The UI, controls and missing QoL features just make it feel like an early access game. Interactions are a mix between cursor aim and character position, interaction range is extremely limited, so you often have to adjust character position just to interact with something in front of you; inventory is tiny and not in an interesting way, you can't lock or favorite items, controls for splitting stacks/moving/equipping etc. feel random and unintuitive. There is a lot of unnecessary text with an awful font. Hunger system is very annoying with very little use. You have to constantly cook and eat, but the buffs are barely noticeable.

_childDocuments_.review: Seriously, if you have ever liked any of the relevant survival games from Minecraft, onwards, buy this game. I first played Core Keeper in early access (I'm talking EARLY access when it first launched on steam) for about 14 hours. From day 1 the foundation for game was entertaining and fun, but didn't necessarily feel like it stood out yet. Fast forward to the launch of 1.0 and I'm honestly fascinated. This game has so much charm. I'm in my 20's now, and Minecraft launched when I was about 10 years old. Growing up, MInecraft was that game that really got me excited about gaming as a whole and opened my eyes to how magical a quality game could be. As I've grown up there have been many great games that have brought innovation to the Minecraft-like, survival genre. Terraria, Starbound, Stardew Valley, and to an extent Satisfactory come to mind as titles that really stick out. This game draws inspiration from all of those games, all while putting it's own wonderful spin on it. Core Keeper removes little inconveniences that are common through out these types of games, but delivers these quality of life features in such a natural and seamless way. For a small example: Tools have durability, but it doesn't feel like nuisance, because the materials to repair them are the same no matter what tool you repair. Additionally, with a couple of extra materials you can double the durability of said item and make it stronger.  Crafting stations draw resources from chests that are placed next to them. Shortcuts and hot keys are readily displayed in menu's so you don't have to stumble around inventories. The pixel art is so cozy and full of character. The sound design is peak, the music is stunning. I can't quite put words to why, but this game gives me the same feeling I had when I played Minecraft and Terraria as a kid. So basically digital crack, delivered in a warm, pixelated, apple pie. TLDR:Exploration is rewarding, mining isn't a chore, as you do things in game, your character levels up. There's loot that feels meaningful, armor that looks cool, unique bosses, pets you can tame and level, gear to collect, and I could go on. All of these features feel well thought out, and created with intention. This game combines elements of Minecraft, Valheim, Terraria, Satrisfactory, and Stardew Valley in a way that is seamless and beautiful. If you have ever been a fan of any of those games, do yourself a favor: skip buying starbucks for a few days, and buy this game. These devs have made something truly special.

_childDocuments_.review: When i saw this game i immediately fell in love with the graphics. Those lightning effects and reflections - simply amazing.At first i enjoyed exploring the game, but the deeper i went the uglier it got (not visually), leaving me with no desire to play until most of the issues i have are fixed.Here are the issues:1. World is too big, and there is no setting to make it smaller. I once decided to find a piece for a sword recipe, the one in the jungle. But after seeing how damn huge that jungle is i just gave up. Biomes also get very repetitive because they are so big.2. Ore deposits are not infinite, making you move your whole drilling and automation setups, and there is no option to make those deposits infinite. Hey devs, why don't you add a soil depletion system for farms? So that farmers would be forced to move their farms every once in a while. I bet it would be fun.3. Hotbar is anti-handy. For example, to plant seeds you will have to remove all your potions and stuff from hotbar, put your seeds in there, plant them, then put your stuff back on the hotbar. Same thing you will do when building. Every. Single. Time.4. Classes and combat sux. I've played with several people in several worlds, and most of them were playing as ranger. Because the rest of the classes simply suck!As a warrior you will see one swinging animation the whole game, mages constantly have no mana, summoner is a joke without multiclassing (and devs are not sure whether he is ranged or melee). There are some failed attempts to make a rogue.Only ranger is the strongest and the most interesting class.Btw the game has almost no active skills. Such a boring and disbalanced combat system in a game where you constantly fight.Those are the big four for me, but there are a lot more minor issues. Like "valuables", or huge unnecessary amount of food recipes, or tedious unproductive fishing. Why you can automate farms, but not fishing, if you need a lot of fish too?And all that can be fixed with a series of QoL and balancing patches, it's not like the game needs an overhaul.But until those patches arrive, i'd stay away to avoid the bitter taste of disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: The first hour of the game was confusing with little in the way of a tutorial to teach you keybindings or even how to interact with the UI. This continues into the main game with no clues on things like "What the heck are these monuments I spawned next to?" or even basic stuff like how to find your way into what ends up being a linear progression. If you happen to choose the incorrect direction to travel, you may spend hours drudging through content that is intended to be above or below you because you simply don't know what you're supposed to be in for. This is a criticism toward the entire genre, but I do feel this game does it worse than similar titles like Terraria. I quit having fun before I even found the tier 2 ore. I still played through more progression tiers with time between sessions getting longer, and sessions themselves getting shorter, until I just quit before finishing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, even with only being at 0.5.3 of early access.  It got almost a hundred hours out of me before I meandered through all the current boss content... and there's STILL plenty more I could be doing if I wanted.  This game is basically Terraria but in the Stardew Valley perspective/graphic style and with Stardew style farming.  I can't wait to see the animal update coming out soon and to find out where this game goes from here. Well worth the $12.99 price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Early game Core Keeper is absolutely a blast, to be honest. I'd go as far to say as it's nearly perfect. Those first few biomes feel wonderful, have plenty of enemy variety, and lots of options for weapons and armor for all the classes. After making the outer wall fall, the wilderness was also, in my opinion, nearly perfect. They filled that biome with plenty of content, equipment, scenes, and enemy variety.This is the issue. Everything past the wilderness feels incomplete, and a bit empty. Visually, all of the biomes look incredible. However, the enemy variety continues to shrink as you continue through the biome, and gear becomes more scarce for summoners and mages. It ends up with you being in the passage, where they are only two enemies, minimal structures, and one boss. Funnily enough, the final boss isn't even in the endgame biome. Why?The game is not worth playing through to the end, as there isn't enough content to satisfy the part of me that enjoys survival games. I'd rather play Necesse or Terraria until the developers add more content, or until significant overhaul mods are developed for the latest version.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: This is very much just your usual adventure survival game, nothing very unique to see here, but i wouldn't consider that a bad thing. For a game just released a week ago in early access, it is extremely well polished.It is very much a laid back kind of experience, but so are most other games of its genra so its to be expected. Again, if you know you enjoy games like minecraft or terraria, this one will be right up your ally.Can also be very repetitivePerformance... I mean look at it, it could probably run on an actual toaster. (As a side note, the framerate does seem to be somewhat limited to 80fps in some scenario's, but it seems to be rather an engine limitation instead of the game actually being demanding).Get some friends and try it out. Its a good time waster if you can't find anything to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: I heard that it's like Stardew Valley and Terraria, so I bought it because I thought I'd like it since it was meant to be similar to Stardew Valley. I had some reservations since I didn't enjoy Terraria, but I thought I'd try it out anyway. Unfortunately, in the short time I've played, it feels like a purely underground Terraria and I've not enjoyed it. Also, the game drops you in without much to go on. At least Stardew Valley has the basic opening of your grandpa leaving you his farm, and you turning up and being welcomed in, told to introduce yourself to everyone, etc. Whereas this just drops you in it and leaves you to get on with it. So, unfortunately, I don't recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: We have Terraria at home, the Terraria at home:It's relaxing and pretty in both visuals and music, but it's shallow and repetitive. I would say to buy it on sale. I couldn't help but think: "Why am i not just playing Terraria right now?" It wears its inspiration on its sleeve but I feel it to be quite inferior to what it attempts to emulate.Towards the end of Terraria the game throws exploration and adventure to the wayside and becomes more of a boss rush, around after you beat The Golem, i personally find that to be the weakest segment of the game, Core Keeper runs out of mystery and exploration quickly in a similar vain. I don't mean to only compare it to Terraria, i believe that even in a vacuum i would find the gameplay loop hollow and pretty unsatisfying. Adding to that: a pillar of this genre, that being gear progression, is lacking and inconsistent with random spikes in power coming from normal mob drops and having hard earned/crafted upgrades being meager in comparison.Farming and fishing are too tedious for the rewards they give. Cooking is a fairly useless buff and money printer, too bad money isn't useful for much and its so plentiful. Also, a word of warning: don't bother going the summoner class like i wanted to, it's half baked, tedious, and there are much more viable, fun options.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game for Early Access. It's similar to Terraria but for a top-down perspective rather than a 2D one. The biggest thing I don't like about it is how insanely rare some items are, and how much players need to grind to max out their skills (especially fishing). It is still in Early Access so the issues the game has will likely be fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing Core Keeper about a week ago and all I can say is that I like the game a lot. It's a fun co-op game where you and your friends can build a base, slay enemies and just have fun exploring the map. I think it's very addicting and since it is still  in early acces, also very promising to be an even better game with lots of content! :)Can't wait for what the future of this game will bring.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying it so far, minecraft and stardew vibes from some aspects which I love. Been playing co-op and it's fun exploring with someone/building a base. Nice music and love the pixel art. The bit of story that I've seen so far is interesting. Excited to see what more will be done since it's early access. _childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: The music is phenomenal. Game is ok. It outstayed its welcome a bit for me.Unusually good:- Music. Probably the main reason I enjoyed it so much.- Tasteful shaders. The water looks beautiful.- It has a wide variety of mechanics, which keeps things interesting for a while. Meanwhile, it manages to stay relatively casual.Could be better:- Could've maybe used a bit more story, because I'm not that compelled to go everywhere to defeat all bosses. It worked for me in the beginning when every new biome was exciting, but eventually it all felt samey and the intrigue faded long before reaching the end.- Limited inventory space is always a pain if there's a large amount of useless items. And in core keeper, those items permanently clutter the floor and you loot them automatically. I initially had some fun getting bigger inventory sizes because every item felt valuable and I had to make decisions on what to keep and what to leave behind. But later into the game it turned into a constant nuisance, because my inventory was full 100% of the time, no matter the size, due to the perm clutter. I always had to drop something to pick up a new item, to only find out that it's probably just another useless item.- Dropping all your stuff when you die and having to walk back to pick it up is... never fun? It has tendency to snowball, because you get more and more impatient, trying to rush back to the place where you died, and you die a lot more often when you're impatient. There are other ways to increase the stakes that don't have such a annoying & boring punishment. I'd rather lose half my stuff in the non-protected slots and be done with it.- Even though the music is beautiful, it fades out and starts from the top if you walk out of the biome for a few seconds, which is a bummer when it's not clear where the biome begins & ends and you do it accidentally. This happened to me frequently.I think everything else is decent. It's not my favourite genre, but it still kept me entertained for quite a while. I played Terraria a decade ago, and this felt like a step up.

_childDocuments_.review: i really enjoy this game i play it 1-2 hours daily the music is soooooo relaxing and good its crazy and the biomes are so pretty  and the game play is very nice i would totally recommend this game plus the price is just crazy good only negative thing i would say about this game is the world is huge but very empty and very few enemy variety so i get bored very quickly once you have gotten all the newest ores and gear but this game is early access so i am sure they will constantly be adding new content so this shouldn't be a problem at launch but for 15 its just crazy good price totally worth it plus gives them the money to add so much stuff they want to add :)

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't a full release yet. Mage and summoner "classes" are barely a single class together, and are honestly just a reach in calling them fully enacted classes. Especially since the summons are paltry wastes of mana that don't target anything. Terraria made summons actually good, let alone making magic viable compared to just ranged. Top end there is no real reason to equip anything but the final drill, as it just kinda does everything and never breaks while doing it. The devs have managed to make their full release feel like this game is just a knock off of everything else in its field, it doesnt have enough appeal or character on it's own to get people in. It's a look alike for terraria meets stardew, that can't be either. Not really close to either. Core Commander needs a craftable or purchaseable scanner. Full stop. Needs more work, needs the dev's to be serious about "adding classes" if they bother to come back to flesh out their work at all.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something that has so much going for it.yet I can't say in good faith that this game is well designed.A lot of design decisions by the devs feel like they saw it in another game and slapped it in this one, take for example; hunger... Hunger in this game is the most actually baffling decisions i've ever seen in a video game, it feels like 'oh minecraft has hunger, lets add hunger' even in minecraft the hunger system doesn't need to be there, its just there to give the illusion of depth, so why is it here? I'm fine with hunger in games if its done so in a strategic way that assists the vision of the game (don't starve), but core keeper fundamentally misses why features like that are included in games.Fun fact this game has durability, why?... I honestly don't know... Like i see why its a feature with the tools, but does your armor have to break aswell? Again it's just another shallow feature that feels tacked on.A thing that is actually a genuinely severe issue, unlike the things that i spoke about prior, the progression. The progression system in terms of its ores is incredibly linear (at the beginning), basically each biome gets a different type of ore and you have to get these ores in a certain order, each biome has a different type of stone that gets progressively more difficult to mine even whilst your tools are getting upgraded...In addition every single tier of ore gets its own crafting station meaning your base is entirely filled with crafting tables... Doesn't it seem obvious to have a system that is backwards compatible? like what? Terraria has such an elegant crafting system that just makes sense (although requires some wiki searching unfortunately). I just don't get it...This game is secretly 3d, probably explaining why it isn't as performant as you'd expect from initial impressions, so with this massive hit to performance... they do nothing with it and put a pixelation filter over the game's camera... Core Keeper, you have the potential to be a hybrid 2d-3d game, imagine if the camera could rotation along an axis keeping the same angle to the player similar to Realm of the mad god, do you know how actually amazing that would feel? how that would look in trailers? Realm of the mad god did this like 11 years earlier and granted, that game's artstyle is significantly worse, but that one single feature will never wear off to me because of its utility in topdown games like this to understand your surroundings.What do i like about the game... I only managed to get through the first three bosses and did a bit after that, it was an nice feeling seeing the world expand, the bosses I fought were ranging from pretty good to enemy spam, uhhh... Soundtrack is serviceable. It's art has a strong identity of its own..... uhhhhhh...Okay I'm gonna be honest this one's hard to be significantly positive about, I did have fun with it at times but it's really hard for me to go in with a clear mind at how bad some of the decisions are.I think Core Keeper is a case of wasted potential, it has such great fights, ambience, art... But is significantly flawed at its core, ruining everything that makes me take this as a keeper.(okay i'm sorry for that one lmfao)

_childDocuments_.review: Core Keeper has a ton of pros IMHO compared to its cons.  It feels as though Stardew, Valheim, & Factorio had a baby and called it Core Keeper.  Assuming you're not looking for a first or third person style 3D modern-looking adventure, and you like the general crafting-survival genre,  could be right up your alley!TBH, I really had to think about the 'cons' list above.  The devs fix glitches pretty quickly that do arise, and release great content every couple months.  Like I said in the BLUF, if you like this genre, you won't be disappointed in Core Keeper.  It took the farming satisfaction of Stardew Valley, mixed with the crafting/survival/biome-bosses/progression of Valheim, mixed with some automation of Factorio/Satisfactory.  There's literally a little bit of several great featuresets baked into one little Early Access game.  And honestly, it doesn't even feel like Early Access, especially compared to several other full-release games out there today.

The unique bosses which usually require a few attempts to figure out.The amazing pixel art in 2D isomorphic with wobbly 3D cave walls. _childDocuments_.review: All the best parts of Stardew valleys mines and Mine crafts adventure feelingI love the skill trees, controls, pixel art (its amazing!), and music! The natural progression to finding new things to grow, kill, and craft also felt really nice! Gives each player their own unique way to play so you don't have to make the world too easy or too hard. You can get a fast pass to role? class? Job? specific skills but seems you can level anything you want just by doing it. I love that your character's stats and items carry over from world to world! You can get a head start in a new world with friends or make a solo run much easier. Will see myself putting many many more hours into this with and without friends!

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 45 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single farther to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 18 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just, watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. loaded into the game, made my character and world and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my son many happy memories

name: Stray Blade
detailed_description: CHECK OUT THE NEW DLC 'VALLEY OF STRAYS' JOIN US ON DISCORD! About the Game Prove yourself in this action-adventure and master intense combat while exploring the ancient ruins of a mysterious civilization. Legends tell of Acrea the Lost Valley, a wild and overgrown place but unmistakably powerful. You found this forgotten land yet died. Time passes, and miraculously you are brought back to life. The price you pay: You are bound to this land. Regain your freedom and embark on the quest of restoring balance in this ravaged and war-torn place guided by your trusty companion, Boji. Explore towering throne rooms of giant god-kings and long-lost cities. As you uncover their secrets, prepare to face even deadlier foes. Get ready to explore a world that is constantly altered by your discoveries and the waging forces! Set off for an unforgettable adventure. Embark on an unforgettable journey and discover the story of Acrea and its ancient legacy. Discover the whole history that turned the peaceful valley into a place of war and death. Use this knowledge to destroy the relics of the past and restore peace in the war-torn valley. Change is part of your journey where every victory leaves a mark in the world. Time keeps moving forward even if you die. Revisit the places of former victory and experience the changes you brought to the world. But beware! Your actions will lead to even greater challenges. The hyper-responsive combat system allows quick reactions and precise attacks to fully control the flow of battle. It merges strategic anticipation of enemy attacks with split-second blade-to-blade reactions — the High Noon of melee weapon combat. Encounter the God-Kings that ruined the land in the past. Bring their legacy to fall and free the land from the shadows of the old era. Harvest their powers and use them to unravel the mysteries of Acrea. New domains are waiting to be unlocked. Both the adventurer and Boji have individual talent trees. The Adventurer is a fighter who gains experience through battle, whereas Boji is a craftsman who increases his experience by finding pieces of ancient lore. Acrea's colorful world ranges from overgrown city ruins to frozen caves and winding canyons. Together with your companion, explore the deepest corners of an ever-changing world bristling with adventure. Every discovery holds treasures. Find rare materials, recipes, weapons, lore pieces, and beautiful places.

_childDocuments_.review: Classic example of a kickstarter being overambitious - The first 1/3 of the game (First major zone) is amazing, so many weapons to play with (20+).The remaining 2/3 of the game contains a grand total of 6 weapons and all the same enemies, but recolored. The boss fights are decent but there's only 4 of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game horrible to a point you would want to call it hot garbage? - NoIs it a good game - also no. Had a great potential to be something cool, yet either the budget or talent of the studio was not enough. Starts pretty nice - there's a world to explore and everything looks nice. You check out the combat and it feels ok: you exchange hits and dodge at right moments -> this gives you stamina boost. Yeah, I see where this is heading. Then you discover there are dozens of weapons. Maces hit hard, spears are reaching far, daggers are fast & crit, etc. Oh, and all those floating glowing stones in the sky and locked doors. Hmm... It's pretty clear I will use those to move around, so I need to find and unlock some abilities first. Nice!Exploration feels great, revealing the maps and finding secrets - satisfying. Man, this game feels good. Why all the negative reviews, I wonder? Couple of hours in the game you start to notice stuff. Like why all the enemies feel the same? You got knights, bugs and rats. Several variations of them, yet still. Why different spear weapon acts like if you didn't even change the equipped one? What's up with all the items dropping from enemies? I got tons and tons of them, even after crafting everything I could, yet my inventory is full of junk I never use? Maybe it'll get better as I progress?Couple more hours in the game you unlock multiple new regions and guess what? Copy the above and paste it here. Everything stays the same: enemies, surroundings, loot... The scenery doesn't change a bit. But you also notice even more problems - performance issues, bugs, bugs and bugs again. There are plenty. You can get stuck in textures just jumping around props. You can make enemies teleport around and insta regen health if you kite them out of the spot where designers meant them to spawn and operate, you can kill a mob and spawn their loot in the sky above you. And more. And more. And more.Finally, you open your abilities and that is the last drop of your patience: there's a bunch of glowing-portal-like rocks floating around, connected with beams of light. They serve as "grapple" points so to say. And to get to one - you press R3 (to focus on the spot), hold Lb and press Y to teleport to the stone. Guess what? It's so random that at some point it's just insane. You could be standing 1m away, 5m away, 4m to the left, 13m to the right of the thing and it won't highlight. Do a step in a random direction - "Ok, oh. You may use it now". LIke how was it supposed to be? Feels broken to the core. Summary: this is a game that totally deserves it's current Mixed rating. Full of bugs, poor game mechanics implementation, poor AI, poor variety of species and combat equipment. It has a decent exploring element and a somewhat good level design (if all the game features would work properly). Could be your game, yet for me it's just disappointment and frustration the further I play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game taught me to pay less attention to steam reviews. Yes, the game needs some patching in some aspects, but really only minor things. Also I have seen the reviews say it has a almost nonexistent story, with less that 2 hours of gameplay... Story, music, combat, progression, weapon variety, beautiful envriments (truly),custom difficulty settings - I love it and fully recommend, if you are willing to look past a few performance issues. _childDocuments_.review: I do like this game, combat is satisfying and exploration is always rewarding, but as of right now, its bogged down by technical issues. Performance is bad, seems to take a huge toll on my machine running basic effects, and there are all kinds of bugs and glitches. I think I'm softlocked out of progressing in the skill tree, because skills are passive and unlocked by mastering the various weapons, but you have to craft the weapons first. After I hit the halfway point I straight up stopped getting blueprints, so I can't craft weapons. There were moments were the controls became straight up unresponsive, which is a huge problem for timing based combat. I want to recommend this game, I think its a good idea and I would like to reward smaller yet ambitious titles such as this, but I simply can't when there this many problems.

_childDocuments_.review: This game sneaked upon me from nowhere, and without a friend's recommendation, I'd have never even found out about it. So far, it pretty much feels like a souls-inspired take on Fable/Kingdoms of Amalur, with easy to grasp yet somewhat difficult to master stamina-based combat with parries, dodges and poise break. The world is visually attractive, and there's tons of stuff to discover while hunting for the next boss. Really fun surprise so far!

_childDocuments_.review: I very rarely make reviews but this game i felt deserved some positive ones considering the amount of complaints it had. I think there's a problem with how players treat souls-like games and that is because a lot of them expect those games to be well... Souls games and so they create for themselves those high expectations like every above-average quality souls-like game should be as good as it was made by Fromsoft themselves.While personally I appreciate any and all different approaches to this kind of games that makes them both similar to Dark Souls and also different from Dark Souls and let me tell you Stray Blade does a lot of things right but most importantly it really is fun to play. So now that i know the gameplay is fun lets get into more detail.World/level design - Aside from your classic exploring - which the areas are beautiful and they also can change drastically with your progression through the world and it's interesting and cool to see how the things you do influence the world. Tells you a lot how powerful the original dwellers of the valley were.But aside from that It feels like Stray Blade took a page from DS1 and made the world map a fun convoluted mess of interlocked areas - where you explore an area and move on and further on you discover a shortcut/gate/vine/bridge which leads back to the previous area except where in DS you would meet there the same enemies and environment you did on your first go through the area in Stray Blade the areas change, sometimes you will se Golden Order move in on a turf you yourself cleared, sometimes you will see wild animals nest up in the Order's former camps - you may also find some loot that previously wasn't there. I really enjoy that because unlike Souls' world this one isn't dead or dying and thus it's subject to change and in story it's cool and makes sense that when Farren blazes a trail and clears out an area - some faction follows his in footsteps finds decent ground for camp or stronghold and sets up.Tl;dr - Backtracking can be fun and good if done right which Stray Blade does.Story/lore/characters - It's likely that the story is not the main focus of the game and yet it's not lying forgotten in the dust. I enjoy the fact that Farren despite his general skepticism and loner mentality expresses genuine curiosity about the area and the history - as a proper adventurer should. It's a very natural way for the player to learn the lore and the history of Acrea - Farren being an adventurer and Boji being a local and it's also natural way to break the ice between Farren and Boji. Which i do also enjoy the dynamic between the two, i enjoy how much personality they both display in anything from Farren being revived to them smithing a weapon/armor together. Even though i saw the forging cutscene tens of times at this point it's still fun to watch.I will not talk about lore too much, because naturally better to find out by yourself but i will say that Acrea isn't huge, decorated with weird visuals, metals and ornaments purely for the aesthetic. A lot of what you see while exploring has to do with the original residents and the elements and metals that they used, the more you learn the more things start to make sense.Combat - I heard all the complaints about Stray Blade's combat and apparently soon it's getting a bit of a rework so i don't know how relevant my opinion here is going to be but here it is anyway.First off I am a Gothic 1 and 2 veteran so your combat would have to be really really bad for me to have problems with it. As it happens personally i really do enjoy Stray Blade's combat, i like the amount of weapons i can get, i like that mastering each can boost my character - i think it has something to do with the fact that Farren is a melee weapon nut as much as i am - i also like that i'm better with some weapons and i suck with some other ones. I do actually find it a little weird that some red attacks that don't look to heavy(animation-wise) can't be parried, i think most enemy attacks should be able to be parried, maybe some elite enemies and bosses should have red attacks and that's that.I would also enjoy more killmove animations with different weapons as some of the different weapons share the killmoves - but that's a minor thing that's purely aesthetic, doesn't lessen the combat fun.Which as a final note on combat/killing end of the game - the killmoves are cool, extremely fun and make winning that much more satisfying.To sum it up i believe Stray Blade is a great game as a whole, one of my favourite souls-likes in fact and i'm gonna support and shill it every chance i get and with upcoming updates and fixes it will potentially become even better as even i have to admit that few things like camera work could use improvement.My two biggest complaints would be clunky feeling cameraAnd lack of photo-mode.I highly recommend this game if you're looking for fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Blade is a souls-like with heavy focus on the story/characters and weapon variety. It has unusual system of progression where you unlock passive upgrades for your character by mastering various weapon types, this technically forces you to use every weapon you find which is a double-edged sword as one one hand you have a decent variety in armament, while on the other you're often forced to use a weapon you might not like just to unlock a damage or health upgrade for your character. Entire combat system is heavily melee focused as there are no ranged weapons and you only have few magic abilities that are story-related. Average playthrough should take around 20-25h. I've waited till latest patch to write this review and unfortunately I can't recommend the game in its current state. It does run better than it did on launch but that's only because the game was shipped in a very bugged state. For a souls-like game, a genre where timing and precise inputs are crucial the gameplay feels very clunky and unresponsive. It doesn't help that you often have to face multiple enemies at once with some of them attacking you from range, a design decision that makes the game even more frustrating given the lack of precise input. The game's performance is also quite odd, even when not much is going on the screen the game fully utilizes my R7 5800X, which is a sign of poor optimization.Hopefully the developers can solve at least some of these issues, they are quite active on Discord and open to feedback so there's hope for improvements in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable hidden gem!To get the bad out of the way, performance should be better relative to my hardware.No big deal, but I have to lower more settings than I should.Visually I find it very appealing, reminds me of good old Amalur.It´s not open world, but the hubs are big enough to make for rewarding exploration.Combat is challenging but fair. Fortunately other game mechanics, e.g. the progression, are not "souls-like".There is no harsh penalty for death, just retry and keep leveling up as you do.I like it when games respect my time. ;)Lots of different weapons to unlock, and the game makes you use each of them at least for a short while.Cut short, Stray Blade is a nice Action-RPG with a bit of Souls-DNA.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: A solid open world game, maybe a bit rough around the edges, but neat ideas like clearing out a location of enemies lets the world evolve and other enemies take over, sometimes building new things for traversal.Ran into a small bug that was annoying me a bit, so headed over to the game's Discord and asked about it, got help directly from the devs and solved it quickly. _childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game.  It's dripping with ambiance, and there is a huge amount of potential, but alas it goes mostly unused. The two biggest gripes I have about the game:- the 3 factions, there's little to no backstory about them -- what are they doing in Acrea?   What is their origin? fleshing these little details out a bit helps immensely. (granted there's books / notes which hint at these things, but it's not enough)- for a game that hinges so much on exploration and finding secrets, the way the map and compass currently work makes it far harder than than needed.  What do i mean?1. face a direction2. open your map3. You'll now notice you are not facing the direction you were facing in step 1.  I'm going to be shelving the game until this bug is fixed.. c'mon guys, bugs like that should never have made it out of QA.

_childDocuments_.review: Verdict: On one hand the game is fun, on the other finding new collectibles and fighting the same enemies for 20 hours is beyond dull. Get it on sale if you are into action RPGs, stay away if you want something souls-like +Steam trading cards (7 drop, 13 to make a badge)Steam achievements (52, 46 base game and 6 DLC, a lot of collecting things)Visually beautifulThe landscape is gorgeous at times Solid execution animations A lot of work was put into the story and how you learn about the world There was a lot of care put into the worldArmour sets and weapons are beautifulWeapons feel different when it comes to their light, heavy and special attacksCombat is not half-bad itself and you feel the weight of your weaponsColour palettes for your armour are quite nice Voice acting and soundtrack are enjoyable to listen toThe few bosses the game are well put together -Levelling is a lie - level up means 1 skill point and 1 new weapon blueprint drop from the first human enemy you encounter 90% of my deaths were due to falling into the abyss Serious lack of enemy varietyI got stuck in loading several times after dyingThe story is pretty much the most basic fantasy I have ever seenThe pacing is off - with exploration it took me 5 hours to meet the first boss and 2nd one was 5 minutes after himI have no idea what is going on with the sounds as it sometimes plays combat queues including parry soundThe game uses 'increase X' without telling you what that means, hence making informative decisions impossible Armours have armour/dodge stats, but once again without explanationsStory bits = stop and listen,  you can either skip everything or wait for 5 minutes on a spot

_childDocuments_.review: I tried this game when it first came out and thought it was aesthetically pleasing, but there were some performance issues, and the combat at the time was not the greatest. I'm so glad they went back, revisited it, and altered the core gameplay to what it was to what it is now. I think what they had was a cool concept. Parry blue attacks. Dodge red attacks, but combat in between that was not as rewarding. Now it plays very fluidly, they have indicators where poise breaks are going to be on enemy attacks, and each weapon feels really cool. The finishers are absolutely amazing. The voice acting in the game is great. My only gripe is that the lack of pauses between commas and periods causes the character interactions to not seem very lifelike. Either it is the voice actors are not given a full script, reading and acting sentence by sentence, or that between each sentence a new "cutscene" is produced that may load too quickly. Which that honestly isn't a big issue. The story is cool so far, and it's a really cool take on an RPG with light souls-like elements. If you are a Souls fan and are looking for a game, just note this is very light in that category. There isn't much of a loss when you die, the real souls-like elements are just the combat, memorizing enemy attack patterns, dodge, parry, and stamina consumption. They do a lot to make the game their own. It amazes me how little attention this game has gotten. I'm really glad I gave it another go. I understand how it may have been hard for the devs to want to alter a core gameplay mechanic, and I just want to thank you all for putting the time and effort into reading and listening to both the community, and providing a top-notch game that I hope get's more traction soon. It's much deserved.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. There is a deep love at the core of this game. I felt that.I play a lot of games. I tend to enjoy an open-world experience with a little bit of platforming, as long as it includes stuff u get from the game as mechanics. That is not all, but the rest is not relevant to this review. This game, from its entry to you, does not pretend to tell you anything you haven’t heard already and cuts right to the chase of the character’s heart. Goals are established and you understand what it is you are to do. There are no side-quests or countless lost minutes searching for what it is you set out to do via a “journal page”. You’re very aware of what to do, and if not, there is helpful tiny staff guiding with magic fingers to guide your clueless ass to which area you are supposed to look in. It’s not embarrassing as that same character will play on the world around you.That said, this game is horrible on my ADD, undiagnosed, at this point because I will find myself filled with child-like amazement at what is next or actually noticing a crevice that leads to another area the map doesn’t show. The map is seductively chaste in its disclosure of info. You are not burdened by weight mechanics, or fractions of % increase in stats when you find items. The mechanics, at core, are present and work well. The game has not crashed on me yet. I highly recommend this game to those missing the heat or excitement from the early days of Fable 1, or those that have been sold this same journey, lone chatacter vs the world, with less effect, on other indie titles.In the end you have to at some point give credit to 505 games for putting weight behind this title that might not have got the polish that is delivered to you on day 1. Are there bugs? Yes. Does it really impact your play when you lose nothing when you die? No. Can you play it on your potato? I currently can’t upgrade to windows 11 due to my hardware, so yes, if you have a recent gfx card and all else, it runs as smooth as butter. Is this a souls-game? I am no expert, and am quite dumb at moving my character around, but this has no resemblance to that genre other than a dodge mechanic? This has more similarity to Kingdoms of Alamur:Reckoning than that. A lot of fresh talent looking at these games these days without the memory of anything other than a blockbuster reviewing these hidden gems, I think, results in the “mixed” review status.If you have fresh eyes on this game, try it. It’s not as hard as you may hear and it may run on an older system hoping for a new adventure.
