_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished a full run yet, but I'm enjoying myself immensely. Absolutely everyone hates us and our economy is barely functioning, but we found space!wheat, the forests are talking to us, and my scientists managed to unknowingly take out a Borg ship recently (and I am very proud of them). It's amazing. I love it. It's got its rough patches, though. Off the top of my head: DLC issues, typos, missing chunks of text, options sometimes failing to unlock, and poor or lacking explanations for most things. My  beef however, is the absolutely  text with no real way to increase the size without throwing the entire UI out of whack and shoving text blocks partially off-screen, which doesn't help matters at all, actually. This is a very basic accessibility feature and it needs to get fixed, quickly. My SECOND biggest beef is probably the tutorial being so barebones you're basically better off ignoring it entirely and relying on tooltips and your AI assistant to explain things to you, and even then a ton of tools are left with no explanation at all. Trial and error will get you through, but it can feel like you're being wrenched out of the game a bit when you're having to guess how basic mechanics function. I'm willing to gamble with my in-game decisions, sure, but I also feel like I should have the basic information the game clearly expects me to have to make those decisions, and if the game expects me to have information then it needs to make that information available. It's cyclical. Overall, a very fun game that clearly loves its source material, but it needs some serious polish. Recommended to most, with some reservations.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying this a lot, but there are some criticisms that I hope will be addressed in updates:1. Some obvious lore stuff. Star Trek doesn't use terms like "voidships," and I'm not sure what those are yet. The game's "authenticity" - appearances by characters like Picard, Worf, Dukat, etc. are why I bought this game. There are obvious terms like "quantum slipstream" and "transwarp" in the Star Trek universe that could explain advanced forms of faster-than-warp travel.2. Bajor doesn't seem to be "working" the way it should. In my Federation game, I went to war with Cardassia, destroyed their station, and landed troops. But I can't seem to find a way to "annex" it. Perhaps because Cardassia fully occupied Bajor earlier in the game. Anyway, it's a bit frustrating to be sitting in a system with your troops all over it and not be able to tell the Cardassians "this is mine now, or I'll destroy all of your fleets again." Oh, and about that station? Pretty sure there was a whole show about the space station in orbit of Bajor, and it did not look like "generic minor state space station 01." 3. Geordi. Poor Geordi. He'll never get to join his friends on the Enterprise-D. Why? I'm fresh out of anomalies. I found tons of them before I unlocked the Enterprise-D, but once I finally paid that alloy cost, the anomalies seem to have dried up. Now it appears that I'm effectively locked out of those campaign objectives. Maybe make it so you can unlock him by scanning debris from battles? That seems a lot more reasonable. Either that, or find some way to create low-reward anomalies that can be done later in the game. There's too much content locked behind the "Geordi wall," like the Defiant and Enterprise-E, so lets pull a classic move and give him a way to roll under the door.4. Poor Romulans. I had no idea how to get that carrier ship I was supposed to have to save those guys. RIP5. The tutorial absolutely brain blasts you with information. It's a little overwhelming to a new player. I figured things out, but, oof.So overall, I'm really happy with the experience. Frankly, I'm just glad that someone is making a game based on my favorite TV shows. I'm excited to do more, but after putting about 8 hours into my first playthrough, I'm hitting these bumps that show that maybe a little more polish could go into the authentic 90s trek experience the game wants to offer. If you can't tell by my profile, that's a pretty big deal (I hope I find the D'Arsay archive sometime soon!)Personally, I hope the game has a big future. I'd love to see Gamma Quadrant and Delta Quadrant DLC, or special scenarios or modes where you do things like fight the Dominion War with mission objectives based on episodes like "In The Pale Moonlight," or command Voyager on its journey home. There's a ton of potential here. Even though I've found my experience to have some rough spots, I'm really hopeful for the future of this game.Edit: Oh, one more thing. The lack of voice clips from Picard, Worf, Data, etc. is a big miss. I'm not even looking for original VO. You obviously have the license. Slap some clips of dialogue in there for appropriate moments.

_childDocuments_.review: This promised a solid throw together of Birth of the Federation and Armada. Classic Star Trek Strategy games that some of us grew up with fond memories off and the prospect of not compromising one over the other in a grand strategy concept using the Stellaris engine great I was sold as soon as I saw the teaser trailer and some of the initial screenshots.I gave it a solid few hours of game-play to get a feel for it and all I will say is this had all the potential to be a great game, but the more I take time to reflect on this it just seems like a rushed effort to get something out there quickly to get some cash back.You can see so many areas where some real thought has gone into the game and the story but in most cases it tapers off into what started off as a good idea but then quickly drops to a disappointing end.I think having the four main powers in the Alpha / Beta quadrants is a good idea and makes a lot of sense for the time frame set but then not including the option to play as some of the mirror powers is a serious oversight and again flags my point about this being a rushed effort. A lot of the effort seems to be a case of taking what Stellaris offered and changing it to be Star Trek relatable but they didn't ask the question if it was needed to begin with for it to work and really strip it down to the basics. So far most of the nod seems to be in-favour of a faction management title more akin to a jumped up Birth of the Federation game but the nods to Armada which is what hooked me more are painfully lacking. Throwing some notable TV/Film ships into a game and passing off a very basic ship combat element which can only happen in a star system is just terrible. There is a massive cannon element to ships in Star Trek especially in the time frame that this game starts from and grows into and this has simply been barged to one side just to make four factions with an equal amount of ship tiers. Bravo! You've literally learnt nothing from Star Trek as a franchise not mention one of the many criticisms of Armada which was also modded to the nth degree. I'm genuinely curious if they actually tested this game out in the wider community prior to release and if they did what feedback they got as given the reviews of this game on Steam and wide press because they all say the same thing disappointing or they loved it but you'd have to have played Stellaris before hand. That latter point this the problem for this game and it shouldn't be like that. Don't get me wrong there were times I found myself enjoying this title and wanted to go back for more but I quickly ended this once one of the day one bugs kicked in, or the gameplay came back to ruin my enjoyment, immersion and general fun which were just replaced by frustration.At the end of the day I might come back to this game I might not it depends how things pan out for it in the future. I suspect that this will have a cult following by some and end up one of those titles that just fades away into people libraries. Mainly as I feel that it will need some serious dev time to correct the draw backs and oversights made.I think if they took this back and built this up more on a Total War level of gameplay I think they would have been on to a winner. For now however a franchise that lends itself perfectly to RTS/Grand Strategy game play will need to wait until this sorts itself out or something better comes along. Until then this game isn't fit to lend itself to the Star Trek Franchise.

I will continue to play, but like i say, I recommend waiting for a sale.** Update **Thinking on this further, I do not believe that purchasing this game is worth it. _childDocuments_.review: I sadly have to not recommend this game.While there are a few likely fixable issues such as bugs, annoying pirates that really just force you to have fleets near everything or loose an outpost, a less than perfect UI that is somehow much worse than the Stellaris original, my chief complaint is actually the Star Trek bit.You have 4 Empires - Federation, Klingons, Romulans, Cardassians. Leaving aside the weird idea of Cardassians as a major power, that's all you can play. All else are minor Empires. Their start positions (aside Bajor) are entirely randomized, as are many systems, so you get strange things like Trill being on the far side of the Romulan Star Empire rather than between UFP and Cardassia. Not that it matters much - they're largely inconsequential aside offering a minor conquest or integration target.You start at around the time of the Khitomer Incident. Despite this, you can only build Miranda-class ships. If you're lucky like me, you might get the USS Cerritos from Lower Decks shortly thereafter - just that ship - and 30 years later you build your first Intrepid. Somewhere along the line you might complete the Enterprise mission goal and get the Enterprise-D. Only that one, no other Galaxy-class ships. Another 30 years, and you get... Excelsiors. Right now I'm well past Picard-time and have just upgraded (?) the Enterprise-D to the E with another mission. This mission also unlocked the Defiant-class (the class, not the specific ship) which is the equivalent of a Stellaris frigate and weaker than a Miranda. I'm also finally researching the Galaxy-class. I have been told the Sovereign exists but haven't seen it, nor any other classic ships aside those - well, and the Oberth science vessel.Onwards - equipment. I'm sorry to say that space combat looks nothing like any of the shows. _childDocuments_.review: I love Star Trek, honestly there aren't enough games made about Star Trek that are playable in a grandiose way that aren't 10 or 20 years old, so for this simple fact alone, Star Trek: Infinite was really a surprise--especially when you consider the fact that it's set in the early Next Generation era, which, barring Kirk, is perhaps the most beloved other era.There are, however, a number of glaring problems with this game; firstly, to do with the implementation, more than the use, of Star Trek IP; and secondly, to do with the mechanics of the game itself. I'm on my probably eighth run, this time at Ensign level, playing as the Klingons, after a successful run with the Federation on Cadet difficulty.Implementation-wise, the game is heavily biased towards the Federation; this is the human starting race that most Trek fans would be familiar with. And it's also the one that I probably have the most beef with because it takes you right out of the historical setting of when the era is set versus when you are able to afford certain things. For example, you don't get access to the Enterprise unless you stockpile 3000 alloys. In early game, this is particularly difficult, as you need to invest in different currencies in order to stabilise your economy in order to generate said alloys. And in the meanwhile, you need to field science vessels in order to explore the galaxy. The problem is, the Enterprise *is that ship*, or it should be, the first ship that the Federation gets access to in order *to* explore. Giving the Federation a slightly bigger advantage, yes, but given that it's just *one* ship with a lot of firepower on a mission of peace and exploration, it'd immediately fit better with the whole Federation aesthetic. The other gripes I have have to do with the types of vessels that get unlocked in what order; clearly showing that the Devs, although they maybe pored over the various Wikis in order to grasp 'what makes Trek Trek', didn't stop to think that the intrepid-class star ship was designed for deep-range exploration, not entirely combat. And it was one or two generations *improved upon* the old Galaxy class starship with its use of neural-gel packs as kind of giant GPU/CPU hybrids. The Miranda and Nebula class ships would have been a better option, because they fit the timeline - and the old Excelsior class ships, which *did* get some action in the Dominion war, are actually old refits which are better suited to being fielded alongside the Enterprise *before* they start producing more galaxy-class starships. Putting the intrepid after these advancements, and then substituting the constitution-class ships for defiant-class ships (which were *specifically* designed for encounters with the Borg) would have been *chef's kiss*, followed by the big old sovereign class as a game-ender.What the Implementation lacks, even to do with the Federation specifically, it more than doubles down on when it comes to the overall mechanics of the game. Which, let's be fair, to anybody who hasn't played Stellaris (or, at the very least, the most recent patch of Stellaris) are very bamboozling and totally unfamiliar. My experience with Stellaris, in the early days when they had 3 types of interstellar travel, prepared me for 'Warp Logistics' (which is an old throwback to wormhole technology), but what I wasn't prepared for were districts. I find districts very difficult to manage. Especially when they cost a lot of money to build in the early game when resources are scarce. And what I find very counterintuitive sometimes about the expand or die mentality that is Infinite/Stellaris, is that it punishes you economically for building practically anything. To the point at which I had to disengage with my second attempt as the Klingons because somehow they hit a massive energy credit deficit that was getting difficult to manage *as an empire that should be focussed on conquering its enemies*!That said, the devs continue to work and rework the game, improving it with regular updates. The sad fact of the matter is they're now starting to push modders in their dev updates as a way of promoting how the game, instead of being polished at launch, can be better optimised *through those mods*, which clearly demonstrates a lack of commitment to the project itself, as well as an overall rushed state of affairs with its launch. So why do I recommend this game? I love Star Trek. I want to see more Star Trek IP. I think that what they've got here is definitely heading in the right direction, and while it does have a steep learning curve, and it doesn't always specifically adhere to the show that I know and love very well, it does scratch that Trek itch that very few Trek games can do these days. I'm fully expecting to see Paradox implement two big DLCs, probably the Borg as a playable race, which, to be completely honest with you, should have been accessible from purchase (honestly the only reason I kind of bought it), and the Dominion wars.

_childDocuments_.review: I have over 1,000 hours in Stellaris, probably over 100 of that in the fantastic mod, Star Trek: New Horizons.I was interested to see how Paradox's "official" Star Trek spin on Stellaris would compare to the existing game/mod combo.I am a sucker for anything "Star Trek," so should be a pretty easy sell to convince me a Star Trek game is something that is worth my time/energy.UNFORTUNATELY, as this seems to have been abandoned by the devs, I cannot recommend purchasing the game until/unless it gets a little more TLC. As it is, it is nothing more than an broken promise.Details follow. . .The pros:1. It just works - really, I had not major bugs or gameplay issues and most of those issues mentioned by others seem to have been patched out quickly. Compare this to ST: New Horizons, which is still constantly playing catch-up as Paradox releases update after update for Stellaris--it is a great mod, but there are recurrent issues due to the ongoing fluctuation in mechanics and re-balancing of the base game.2. Content seems very consistent with established ST canon - as a die-hard Trekker, I really appreciate a game that is respectful of the series that have been produced to date. This game, IMO, does an excellent job recreating the TNG-era galactic atmosphere in the Stellaris format.Mixed bag:1. Early progression is interesting/late progression is boring - the gameplay loop and all the various aspects of management, as with Stellaris, are engaging (if you are into the grand strategy/(micro-macro)management genre. It is demanding on your attention until you establish an advantage (technologically or otherwise), and then it is up to the pre-established gameplay mechanics to limit your runaway hegemony over the other galactic powers. Stellaris, has established a great number of late-game mechanics (mostly available through DLC) that keep things changing and challenging you all the way to your eventual triumph or defeat. This game does not yet have this rich buffet of political, technological, espionage-oriented, etc. mechanics. It runs out of steam after a certain point.Cons:1. NO UPDATES SINCE DECEMBER - yeah, I think this might've gotten caught up in the whole "Embracer" thing. Ugh. That sucks, because I think this could easily have been the next "Birth of the Federation" if Paradox would have just given it a minor iota of attention.2. The scope is quite limited - you only have the one galaxy to play in (no galaxy generation options, as there are with Stellaris). This kinda makes sense for ST: Infinite 1.0, but with further development this game would definitely benefit from--nay, require--more ability for the players to fine-tune the starting parameters for the game they are about to spend hundreds of turns playing.It also starts in the TNG era, which to me makes less sense than a grand strategy game encompassing all of Federation (or Romulan, or Klingon, etc.) history. The extant mod already does this quite well, incorporating canonical events from all the shows.As it is, you can only play as a few galactic powers, whereas with the mod, you can even play as a minor power like the Kazon (though why you would want to, is beyond me). Admittedly, if the mod did not exist, the game's limitations would not seem so glaring. But in its current state, with a better alternative available, this just seems like a half-finished game which may never be completed--as a result of poor prioritization of projects, rather than irreparable problems with the game itself.This game could be decent if it got a little support from the developer. The longstanding curse of universally mediocre Star Trek games apparently continues unabated, well into the second decade of the 21st century.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a lukewarm fan of Stellaris. I wasn't in love with its anthropomorphic animal factions and generic setting.Star Trek Infinite, as a 4X game, is worse than Stellaris, but its fantastically improved IP makes me optimistic for its future. I'm looking forward to where the developers take it.–In detail:I loved the Mission tree. The game gives you goals, in the form of a small branching tree similar to Hearts of Iron 4’s National Focus trees. The Federation mission tree rewards you with an Enterprise-D, a unique ship capable of research and combat. Once built, you get six specific missions to complete with the Enterprise, each rewarding you with a “graduated” member of the Enterprise’s crew, who joins as a Faction Leader. I was partial to Troi, who became my lead diplomat (or envoy), and Data, who became one of my best Science Ship captains.I appreciated the smaller-form, hand-designed galaxy. Star Trek: Infinite gives you the lower half of what seems to be a medium-sized Stellaris galaxy. It’s still procedurally generated, but less so than Stellaris. There’s a design to the galaxy. Personally, I loved smaller Stellaris games, and I prefer hand-designed content over procedural generation, so these are great steps in my opinion.Star Trek: Infinite draws content from the Rick Berman period of the 90’s-00’s, but mostly focuses on The Next Generation. We don’t see anything from The Original Series, Star Trek: Enterprise, or the rebooted classic period.The game is far from perfect. There are bugs. The AI of other major powers is poor. The End Game Crisis never seemed to trigger in my game. Content gets a little sparse as the game goes on. I’d have preferred a deeper internal politics system for the United Federation of Planet, and a deeper character system. I’d prefer better voice acting, especially for the Klingons. No sound effects or music are brought in from the shows, and what we have in the game isn't very good. (Compare, for example, the early 00's Star Wars: Rebellion, which made excellent use of Star Wars' voiced dialog, sound effects and music.)– I enjoyed my 20 hours. I'd love for Paradox to apply this same treatment for other IPs: In many ways, Star Wars is a much better fit for Stellaris than Star Trek. Dune or Foundation would be interesting, and I would absolutely love a Crusader Kings 3-based Game of Thrones game.This is a tentative, qualified recommendation, assuming that Paradox is going to come through with a patch and content update for the game. For me, it was worth $30, and I’d recommend it if you’re sort of like me: If you like 90’s-era Star Trek and you thought Stellaris was at least “okay.” I hope it's financially successful for them, as I'd love to see it improved and expanded.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me first immediately state I can see the Devs clearly put a lot of work in this game, the artwork and designs look top notch.However the problem is the fact the game itself is at odds with its own heritage.As someone who loves both Star Trek and Stellaris, I feel that the devs sadly have made the game lose touch with its own roots.I am well aware this is based on Stellaris and while I do not see a problem with that at all, the issues start with many of the choices on how to balance both sides out.The governor system from Stellaris was perfectly fine for example, putting them on ships which only buffs one planet in specific ways just feels clunky at best.So I started mostly ignoring them altogether.Another example is piracy, since Stellaris got rid of alternative drives years ago for sake of balance piracy is very predictable.Send a lot of trade through unprotected systems and you will sooner or later have pirates pop up there, though they aren't more than a nuisance usually.Instead the devs decided to make some random Nausicaans come at random and trash your systems.So why is that a problem?First of all it pretty much means, and I am not kidding, in my game I had to dispatch fleets every 5 minutes just to keep them at bay, because if they trash your system you will lose it and when that happens you lose that system unless it contains a planet, so they decided pirates use the same mechanics as the Stellaris endgame crisis.And sometimes there is not even enough time to intercept them, and there is no solution either, because if you build a starbase in that system they just pick another one, which thanks to Warp they do not care how deep inside your borders it is.This also extends to diplomacy where the Klingons and Romulans just after Khitomer started becoming best friends, I really feel the Devs should have made this more realistic.And then there is the speed of in-game time, which while working perfectly fine for Stellaris, does not work in Infinite.It immediately became a meme for my friends and I that I got Data, which not even 5 minutes after becoming an officer died of old age.In general when you're dealing with a franchise that has named characters, you have to adjust your game so they don't die off like that, maybe fallen in combat sure, but having TNG suddenly span hundreds of years like that just feels weird.And speaking of Data, the mission system inspired by EU4 is nice on paper, but its execution felt bad in the game.I got stuck on multiple roadblocks, I cannot get Bajor because the Cardassians integrated it and I could not help the Romulans, their supernova happened while I was stuck on not having enough trade treaties.For some reason when the game considers you too strong, they refuse to do trade deals with you. So I was never able to get to the point where I could evacuate the Romulans, so I failed that.So while those missions were an interesting idea, Stellaris as a base is too random for it to work properly and it does not feel good getting stuck like that.So in the end with those issues and many more gripes, I did not feel really engaged with the game much because I was hoping for a more roleplay like experience with a Stellaris flair, but as stated the game is at odds with its heritage.Overall I hope eventually the devs manage to change those things to make more sense, then I would of course adjust my review. But until then I just cannot recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be good, perhaps great but I feel a lot of work needs to be done before it should have been release on a lore and game play perspective. Posties: it is filled with trivia and lore that is accurate, the voice acting is superb and the art work is amazing. It is a beauty to look at and it is worth the price alone. Also the narrative is great and responsive when playing with options you would not see in Stellarais I hope the custodians implement some of them. Being able to assassinating leaders or running sabotage mission due to coveting the populace with brilliant idea. Also able to add districts is a much great game play method that should be implemented in Stellaris as well.The negatives: the game is balance for early Stellaris, which is a problem when gathering resources for the game does not provide the player a chance to gather as many materials as Stellaris due to planets being smaller and fewer resources you can mind from space. One wrong building and you have to spend 10 minutes working to fix your economy to stop it free fall, especially when it comes to energy credits. Also there is a lack of depth as you do not get as many ships to play with, technology being very straight forward, and lack of things to do after the mid-game and before and after the crisis. It also hurt it has some game breaking bugs or things allowed. For example, Bajor being assimilated by the Cardassians with a Federation that cannot declare wars to iberation to free planets from Cadrassian control. Along with no anomalies showing up to prevent completing of the Federation mission tree on the Enterprise. Not to mention getting certain mission within year 10 before you have a chance to research technologies to allow for more options in the game. Finally, there is just not enough factions to play with and lore is lacking in areas.So here are some suggestions I feel would greatly improve this game:1) Re-balance nearly everything to create more diversity. Starting with varying technology and ships to give players more options. In addition, I recommend planets on average have more directs, and/or gather mroe resources to making it easier to mange then a pain. I also suggest allow cruisers to serve more as mission all capable as science, construction and ambassador ships when traveling alone to be with lore. 2) Each faction start with cruisers, destroyers, frigates and corvettes and are research better versions and more diverse ships hulls to be able to make a diverse fleet. Like in the cruiser section fro the UFP, the starting is the Constitution as a close range ship and Excelsior is a mid range ship, and later research Promethus for close range combat, and Akira is a long range artillery ship.3) Removing the aging mechanic and the ability to die due to old age for key characters tied to mission tree. It was pain to get that point only for the missions tasks and make sens for some to die of old age (like Data). In fact, with how costly it is to get commanders, I suggest leadership is unlock through research and the person gains someone from the shows, video games and books to fill the role immediately once research.4) Resemblance the AI so they are more likely to diversity their one planet so they easier to assimilate instead of sending the economy into free fall doing so (which is necessary as any of the factions, especially the Federation). Also makes it easier for the player to convert the planet and allow them the empire to remain relevant as they are not running low on materials.5) Add more diversity in game play like the mission tree should be expanded. Like have more then one hero ship with missions and expanded tree. Also tradition tree could work to diversify with possible 2 more branches at least for its a case of more is needed.6) Remove trade and research agreements only viable for empires of equal value. You will quickly outpace other empires, and it removes a good way for factions to gain resources and increase likable to assimilate them.7) Add not only factions but also different game mod. Right now it only has four with making them more or less balance to each other. I think that is a mistake and should make a lore version with power being very different to reflect their actual versions. See below for example.8) Try to not only add factions but maybe change them up so they feel like their own and really stand out while increasing replay for different play styles. Again, see belowFor example:The UFP could take from their lore and by the 24th Century is the largest faction with vast territory rich in resources and a number of home worlds with various species. In fact they have not only four found species, but also the Betazeds, Bolians, Caitians, Denobulans, and Saurian as already assimilated members, with five multirace colonies. For species the UFP know and enticing for membership is the Trill and Bynar. They are also the most advance among the four and wealthiest. However, they are least developed and focus with few additional colonies and planet districts distributed evenly to not lack. In fact, you get penalize for trying to focus planets into one resource planet as the UFP wants each planet to be able to survive on their own with planets only focus on making specialized in specific rare materials, research or training worlds. There military is diverse but small for a empire its size so its player job to expand the Fedeartion and build it up to be a great power before others decide to try to take chunks out of Federation space early game.The Romulans is if playing as a tall empire. They have a small territory but unlike the UFP a highly focus economy to maximize returns, large number of cruiser size and up ships, and highly defended territory. However, they start off as isolationist with only after reaching a certain military threshold can they communicate and conquer outside their the empire. They also lack the smaller ships so they can be vulnerable to small fleet if you don't get first strike outside cloak. They are also the most sneaky and get the most spy master and bonus from spying on other species, specifically in acquiring technology and resources. Also the Romulans should have the Remans on their moon as a slave species with possible others as well.The Klingons, they start off the largest faction military and the most developed planets being the oldest empire. However, they also get the least from their own resources and research for being a warrior species. To compensate, they can be very charming and intimidating when meeting with other species, so they can get far more in trade deals, research agreements, and vassalize other empires. Meanwhile, species assimilated in their empire and more productive as well. As the Empire, you want to make friends with the more technologically advance UFPs or Romulans while vassalizing smaller powers which the player starting with the Orions (resources and trade vassal) and Ferasan (research vassal) from the start.Finally the Cardassians should be hard mod for players. They are smallest and least of all the other empires. However, as the under dog, so they deal more damage against stronger players, especially in their territory and are good in all areas instead of the focus areas like the Federation, Klingons and Romulans. So they best not get the attention of more powerful factions or they will face the consequences.Factions they need to add or think about adding: the Dominion, Tholian Assembly, Gorn Hegemony, Tzenkethi Coalition, and Terran Empire.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: 6/16/2024The game has been abandoned completely. Go buy Stellaris and download the Star Trek mod!=======================================================================It's 'Good'  but not great.- As a Star Trek game, this is pretty good. It has tons of flavor, high quality models, stories, etc. It feels like a Trek game.- As a Stellaris game, it is slow. Deadly slow. It's not about expansion and empire building, Infinite is more about telling a story and doing missions inside of a Star Trek universe.If you are a Stellaris player, you will enjoy this game. But you will be missing on more recent Stellaris type features and depth. Infinite is definately not a copy/paste of Stellaris. The dev's have made this their own thing, but it feels really flat compared to Stellaris.When I say it is not a copy/paste, it's almost like they took Stellaris. Took out a bunch of features (or refinements) Stellaris has and then put their own Star Trek spin on it. It's not bad, Star Trek fans will love it. But it's not great, Stellaris fans will get bored.If you were to say this game compete's with Stellaris, then you'd be wrong. Infinite is more about telling a story, running the game a 1.0x speed or slower and letting things play out.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoilers: This will be lengthy.I've played stellaris and now I have played Infinite. There is definitely a lot of differences.One: there is a glaring difference in playability, you are always bound by a pre-set game design that limits a lot verses stellaris. I get that they want to keep this almost like true trek, but adding a random universe setup will do the basics a wonder. Further, there isn't any settings to change for this game. You can't set the crisis difficulties or the amount how things are set up.So if you just want a conquest game, or an ethics game, you cannot change the settings to give you that option. I was winning as the klingons, and then out of the blue within like...40 years, the federation pulled a win of ethics out from under me when I had looked and everyone had 3 ethics like me. I was completely surprised.Two: Computer systems in the game messed up my designs pretty horribly upon getting to the Vorcha class (Tier 4 ships). In stellaris, it tells you the effective ranges that the computer will stay at for longest ranges of shooting. (like artillery, line, and point blank.) Another issue with the computer for tier four ships, You only get "Stay at longest ranges" as an option. Which made my ships sit outside their own weapon ranges and be useless upon fighting stations. (so tier 3, 2, and 1 ships were the ones fighting the stations effectively where the tier 4 just.... sat there... Very Frustrating.)Three: They hinted that the Nebula ship was in with artwork at somepoint, sadly they don't have that ship in the game. They did say they might put in the option to making the ships have optional skins, but really... I feel they are leaving this to modders. Which is highly frustrating to me. On top of that, while claiming to be going canon, they muddled up the order of ships. Further, they are using I believe the avenger style miranda looks instead of the classic miranda that we usually see.Four: Star bases are different in this game verses stellaris. You can build any number of them and it seems to be ok, verses stellaris having you research more starbase amounts. This is probably because of how the warp works for ships being able to attack any system within the FTL limit.Five: It feels like the same missions go across the factions, so it doesn't feel unique like the stellaris beginning story arcs. Maybe it is located in certain areas, because I played the federation, and then klingons, and conquered Sol... But I got a few missions from the federation playthrough.Six: There is not much variation with the ship builds. You don't get to pick different hulls that make different builds per say. Birds of Prey have 1 small weapons slot and 2 medium weapon slots. Mirandas have 3 small weapon slots and 1 medium. (Tier 1 ships) It felt like there was classes of ships in stellaris with the hull picks (where one is a picket class, one a torpedo class, one is a basic class, etc.) It would be nice if they used different ships for this design. (but using such minimal ship designs makes this currently impossible at this time.)Seven: Some of the race missions requires you to be a friend of X empire, like the klingons, in order to progress down its mission ark, you must be friendly with either the federation OR the Romulans. Which if you weren't paying attention before, and went to war with both, it is a pain in the ASS to get to be allowed to complete this missions. Literally ANY war you do, drops both the empire's views of you and you have to wait FREAKING FOREVER to complete missions. Making the game kind of stale.Eight: I have YET to see the end game crisis. Which is supposed to be something to worry about. (Which I doubt seeing how I completely dominated in the game.(Nine: (and probably my last point.) I think I missed the research tree for the exquisite minerals, so it seems like you cannot buy them? Someone correct me if I am wrong, but on my playthrough, I could not buy any dilithium for my better buildings. Very frustrating.Now, on to my actual review on the game.Graphics are pretty standard and they look nice. Very stellaris. Many of the icons is stellaris. If you want to play a sandbox game, definitely play stellaris over this game. There are so many things that could be improved with this game that they are indeed going to let the modders do the work for them. It is unfortunate that this will eventually be just abandonware.Core issues with the game:There is no true flexibility, if something happens, too many of the quest lines get broken. If a character dies, dead quest line. Everything seems to be super interconnected where If you go to war, all of the major empires will have extremely long lasting negative views of it...making say the klingon mission tree fail completely or take far to long to go through.There is no way to change the win outcome, so if an empire beats you on civic wins, you have lost. (yes, you may continue to play through, but its still considered a loss.)There are far too many bugs right now. Infact, as of this day, there's an advice bug that will not remove the tutorial advice, removing the whole U.I. on the right hand side. VERY FRUSTRATING.Concerning ships, the most iconic ships are in (arguably) especially on the federation side, but only has Galaxy, Excelsior, Miranda, Intrepid, and Sovereign class ships are actually in the game. In a latest statement, they pretty much said they are going to let modders fill in the gap. This screams Abandonware to me, and that they are not invested in giving their player base exactly what they want...and want the modders to do the work for free. I am highly disappointed in this outcome.  At this time, I cannot endorse this game. I may update this review at a future time, but as it is, I think the most polished game is stellaris with the mod new horizon for a star trek themed Stellaris. I do not normally want to give a game a negative review, but today is the day I was super agitated by the U.I. bug that was caused by the latest update, and last friday's dev report.

_childDocuments_.review: Although there are enough changes that make this a different game, to the point where you can say that if you like this, you might not like Stellaris, and if you like Stellaris, you might not necessarily like this, and because I like Trek, I like Stellaris, and I'm not bothered one way or the other about DLCs, I was on the fence about a 'Yes' or 'No' for this game. Overall, the graphical representations of the IP give a general 'Star Trek' feel to the game, and as a Stellaris player, it was easy to pick up and deal with the new or different mechanics this game offers. There are, however, many QoL features in Stellaris that are frustratingly absent in this game. Manual Empire Capital relocation, or Autobuild for Construction Ships are two good examples.In the end I decided to give this game a 'No', and since it's essentially a Star Trek skin on another game, I want to focus on thae Trek rather than the actual gameplay.The Federation starts with the 4 founder races. There are no Remans. Not at the start, and not later on.I got Janeway as a special character as part of a Borg storyline. Great, except I was playing as the Romulans.People can and will debate the inclusion itself of the Hobus Supernova, but in the game it's utterly unavoidable. In every new game. the Romulans will lose their capital after about 40 years or so. If you've played Stellaris, you'll know why this is might be a problem. If you're a Trek fan from before 2009, albeit for different non game related reasons, you'll also see why this might be a problematic thing to put in the game from an immersion perspective.There are a few notable exceptions, like Singularity Cores for Romulans, but for the most part, everybody gets everything technology wise. In short, there is one tech tree with very little individualisation for the different factions. Romulans can research and use Phaser Cannons, and the Cardassians, Plasma Torpedoes. There are a lot of events and 'quests' to do as you play through the game, which is really good. The trouble is that a lot of them either don't make any contextual sense for where you are in your current game, or else flat out happen in the 'wrong' order.The game is set just after the Khitomer Massacre, and the 4 major powers start off well established (4 colonized systems), yet only the Miranda (or equivalent) class size ship (Stellaris Corvettes) are available at game start. This is partly due to the Tech Tree having been borrowed from Stellaris. It works well there. It's problematic for a Star Trek game based in a particular era. In one game, I unlocked the Enterprise D before I'd researched even the second tier of Starship. Disappointingly, this is the Intrepid Class. Read the first line of this paragraph again.The whole game is oddly specific about so many things, yet really not when it comes to others. Romulus has to die, but can then use Phaser Cannons. Like... is it a 'canon' based game or isn't it? The Borg didn't speak to me like they do in the trailer. I had to... ugh.... read... 'Resistance is futile'.In the diplomacy screens, each Civ (majors and minors) only have one line. The Klingon guy sounds like Brad from accounts - even if you have the preorder Klingon language DLC.There's not a great deal of major Trek related issues. But there are an absolute mountain of minor issues that add up to an overall 'Trek-like' experience... kinda. It's a little too Stellaris and a little just not Trek enough for the whole thing to feel off.So... I played 32 more hours since posting this review, most of that time in multiplayer. I'm feeling very uninspired by subsequent patches. I understand that they're busy fixing more critical problems that should never have been part of release, and I haven't played since 1.0.2, but nothing they've patched so far touches anything that goes anywhere near what I feel are the underlying issues. It's still a 'no' but the more I see, the less on the fence about this verdict I become.

_childDocuments_.review: My disappointment with Star Trek: Infinite knows no bounds. With high hopes of immersing myself in epic online PvP battles set in the beloved Star Trek universe, I eagerly booted up the game, only to be met with a slew of unresolved issues that quickly soured my experience. Save your warp cores and set your phasers to avoid – this game is a lost cause.

_childDocuments_.review: Not getting crashes like some of the other people here but the game itself has many other issues. I will make many comparisons to Stellaris as they're practically the same game, the few differences between them are not enough to distract from this fact.The events and focus system have wonderfully made art and overall well written text, sometimes might be a bit off but they are in Stellaris too occassionally, with so many events they can't all be incredible and some of them have to be mundane things too. The Klingons had one where they had to challenge themselves to create the most deadly tea and drink them as a challenge event, because only Klingons are the best tea testers! apparently, which I found pretty amusing.Unfortunately, there is some clearly being reused from Stellaris, like the floating Tree of Life I think it was called, here it's "Space Tree". It feels lazy reusing things even if the text content and buffs are slightly different. Why not change it in the smallest way and make it a space bush? maybe a giant space fruit? a derelict ship covered with space fauna? perhaps not the best suggestions here but you see the point, it's not hard to come up with similar but different ideas rather than reusing old ones.The thing I noticed first when playing. The UI is not great and as with Stellaris, absolutely sucks above 1080p, I play at 1440p and the icons were ridiculously small hidden away at the top to the point they're very easy to miss. Otherwise the UI has been redesigned to look very clean and minimalist but as a result you can't tell when things are clickable buttons or just informational icons; the fleetpower overlaps with your faction's coloured slash on the fleet icon so it's hard to read; some buttons are coloured like your faction  others are grey , options hidden within options which you'd never know if you hadn't looked already and so on. It's weird how many issues with the UI there are. The 3.1 Stellaris version they based this on didn't have most of these problems. It feels like they made the UI worse unintentionally whilst changing it as an excuse to make it feel different. Do it properly or don't change it please, we already know it's basically Stellaris anyway so all it's done it make the game more frustrating to play.Generally the typically seen Trek weapons like Phasers do more shield damage whilst others do more hull damage, for the most part it seems that Torpedos are the hull damage for when shields go down. This is fine in itself but I wish the weapons were less extremely biased one way or the other, Phasers have a +100% to shields and -75% to hull... but we see Phasers blow ships in half when shields aren't protecting them so the negative seems too high.There doesn't seem to be traditional Disruptors or equivalent plasma weaponry in the game for the Klingons or Romulans to use, their ARE weapons with those names but they do not function statswise or visually like you'd expect them to based on the lore rather they function like they do in Stellaris, Disruptors having pen etc. Also, no spiral wave Phasers/Disruptors for the Cardassians. Overall seems to be majority generic Phasers at multiple tech levels, some variants. Of the 8 or so I tested they fire almost identical  not beams. I could have missed the beam weapons but this is TNG, they shouldn't be that hard for me to find, most ships had beams in that Era. The 15+ phasers are mostly different tech levels rather than different weapons which is to be expected, there are too few other types of weapons which are useful and fit in the lore though. Again, I could have missed some but I used the console afterwards for the sake of testing and  of the weapons unlocked were more of the same with the odd unique weapon, no Klingon Disruptor pulse cannons etc.They could have each faction start with statistically similar weapons with different visuals  but instead we all use the same thing. Torpedos are slightly dissapointing and done better by mods IMO. I've personally made, subjectively speaking, better lore accurate weapons myself so I'm unsure how they ended up with what they have here. I'm just someone modding for fun but these are professionals.The worst part about weapons is that they didn't use Star Trek sounds or something close to them which is stranger still when considering this is officially licensed. They're half Stellaris sounds while the rest are egregiously  high pitch whirr sounds or another annoying to hear sound effect. It's not at all what Phasers, Disruptors or any other Star Trek weapon has ever sounded like. They immediately pull you out of any immersion when your ships open fire because it doesn't sound like you're playing Star Trek.The music isn't particularly crazy or memorable  it is competently done and does sound like what you'd expect in a Star Trek game, I haven't listened to the whole soundtrack so there may be some more bombastic sounding combat music I missed but from what I heard it was much more calm overall, giving you a more chilled out experience as a result if that's what you're looking for.The ships are all recreated well and at the detail level you'd expect for a 4x game . The biggest problem with the ships is that they majorly lack in variety, there is no alternate types of equivalent frigates/cruisers/battleships etc, you literally get one of each and that's it per faction. Keeping elements of the modular system from Stellaris so we can kitbash our own Warbirds or Federation ships with different Nacelles/Saucers etc would've been cool and added to build diversity.Klingons for example use the same model for the Governor, Spy and maybe the Transport ship. The Klingon equivalent to the Stellaris Cruiser is literally the same ship as the Destroyer, just made bigger with 1-2 extra parts that glow on top of it. They could have modelled one of them as the TOS D7 and gave it some greebling for detail on the hull to make it fit in and look older. Instead we have 2 K'Tingas which takes the limited roster down even further visually. It's also difficult to tell the Starbase levels apart at a glance for the same reason and there's only a few levels, yet still they look too similar.Performance seems to be no worse than Stellaris and might be slightly better due to the smaller fleet sizes. I can run it at x8 Supersampling via Nvidia's Control Panel like I can Stellaris and it runs 165FPS easily on a 3070 at 1440p. You'll be CPU bottlenecked not GPU, as expected.I was one of the people arguing that for the price it's a fairly large amount of content and I still think it is, however what's here is just not enough to make you want to play it OVER the game it's based on, even if you don't own that game already, Paradox is competing against themselves and losing.Game looks cleaner and more minimalistic but it's to the point it's a detriment and lacks the depth you'd expect from a standalone game. The usability issues with the UI and lack of depth in ship builds got frustrating to the point I wanted to go play Stellaris instead. I'd advise to  Base Stellaris without DLC is a more complete and fun experience IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: I am now about 50 hours into the game and I really cannot concur with all the negative fuss spread in the reviews.Yes, the game is still a little bit buggy. And yes, it is unfortunate that Paradox has discontinued development of the game. And yes, why should you play Star Trek Infinite when you can also play Stellaris?However, for all the hardcore Trekkies out there, this is THE game we have been waiting for 25 years, ever since Microprose brought us BOTF (Birth of the Federation). Being a clone of Stellaris, Star Trek Infinite is a grand strategy space game beautifully embedded in the Star Trek universe. It's nothing special, but it's fun to send Jean Luc Picard and his Enterprise on missions and to see all your little Star Trek ships, that you know so well from the shows, in space combat action.The game has a very steep learning curve and a really bad tutorial, so getting into the game takes quite some patience and time. Bugs are existent, bug none of them are really game breaking.Bottom line: I would not hesitate to recommend this game to every single Trekkie that is willing to invest a lot of time to see a major power in the Star Trek universe to grow and expand. Everyone else is probably better off with the original, namely Stellaris.My verdict: for Trekkies: 9/10, for regular strategy game players: 6/10.Engage!

_childDocuments_.review: I think that I gave this game a fair chance, but there's just too many inconsistencies (many modifiers and values feel like they were decided on the fly with nobody to check if it felt consistent), there's too many stuff from Stellaris that was simply reused without being changed (some species even have Stellaris traits, like the Nausicaans). It even gets in the way of the "love for the setting". They achieved balance between the 4 main factions in the worst ways possible (emptying Denobula and Rysa, for instance).Overall this game reminds me a lot of Imperator. The interface itself doesn't feel very good (because it's so small with unintuitive icons), the gameplay gets in the way of immersion instead of facilitating it. In the end I don't really feel like I'm playing Star Trek, I find myself just blobbing. The new features aren't exactly compelling either - spy ships and governor ships are annoying to micromanage, missions trees are very limited, galactic tension would be a nice idea if it wasn't so anecdotic. There's some stuff I tried to do but couldn't because the buttons didn't work or it just created new issues (I ended up downgrading the Bajoran station as Cardassians because rerouting the trade route didn't work like it should). I wanted to see if I could vassalize a minor faction through purely diplomatic means so I sent an envoy, then I did the same mission 4 times to boost relationships, reaching the max level. I saw no new options, but the minor faction sent be treaties that I didn't even have access to and that did nothing (a migration treaty and a "protection" treaty that seemed both directly borrowed from Stellaris, but did nothing here and didn't appear as listed on the diplomatic interface), and that's it. No way of knowing if I need to unlock something, and I don't even know what I'm supposed to do with a minor faction.The only stuff that really works is the gameplay that was brought in from Stellaris, but I can just play Stellaris instead.Now it doesn't mean that everything is bad and there's potential... but I'm not going to force myself to play this game, and I'm not going to use my love for Star Trek as an excuse to forget everything that doesn't work well in it. I wish a jolly good time to people who like this game and good luck to the devs. But I think it's important to say that this game doesn't offer a streamlined, polished experience for now.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay:I find the gameplay of "Star Trek: Infinite" disappointing. Although it presents itself as a complex 4X game, it comes across more like a very limited and incomplete RTS (Real-Time Strategy) game with some 4X elements. Despite the uniqueness of the Star Trek universe, the lack of robust implementation of 4X elements could reduce the game's appeal for fans of the genre.Technical Issues:The numerous bugs and technical issues could pose a significant obstacle for a smooth gameplay experience. These technical flaws could be particularly frustrating if they significantly hinder or even prevent the progress of players.Comparison with Stellaris:Engine and Aesthetics:Both games share the same engine, which could lead to similar gameplay mechanics. The aesthetic implementation of the Star Trek universe in "Star Trek: Infinite" could be appealing for fans of the series. However, I think that the game doesn’t offer much new in terms of innovation or unique gameplay elements.Unique Features and Gameplay Structure:Although "Star Trek: Infinite" offers some unique features and a structured gameplay experience with clear objectives and missions, these elements might not be enough to significantly distinguish it from "Stellaris", especially considering the reported technical issues and the perceived lack of gameplay depth.Overall, I find that "Star Trek: Infinite" receives mixed reactions from players and critics, with technical issues and the perceived lack of gameplay depth being highlighted as major points of criticism. The similarities with "Stellaris" could be both an advantage and a disadvantage, depending on the personal preferences of players and their experience with both games.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a die hard Star Trek fan, so when I learned of new Paradox Trek game, I was very excited!When I first saw the gameplay reveal, it was clear it was going to borrow a lot from Stellaris, but after getting a couple of hours into the game now, it's clear that it is, unfortunately, a re-skin i.e UI, same mechanics - everything...right down to the construction ships.Now if you're a Trek fan, will you like this? probably. However be prepared for inaccurate continuity. The game starts with the Khitomer massacre and the events around the TNG episode "Yesterday's Enterprise". However, the Federation is only a small power and you start as though the UFP has only just been formed. So, unlike Stellaris where you expand from a single system out, you control of the 4 founding members but you find established cannon planets like Risa are unsettled planets (which breaks from the timeline too), therefore, they need to be colonised.Would this have been better to start just after the Star Trek: Enterprise finale? and develop the respective "empires" from their?Also, starships can't initiate first contact on their own either, you have recruit diplomats to do the work that a captain would usually do, so you have to sometimes put this on hold until said diplomats are free to do so whilst they complete other tasks etc. The game looks great, but it feels disjointed from the Trek universe so far, so I'm hoping it gets better soon and that Paradox work to distinguish this from Stellaris, and give it it's own personality, rather than having a "copy & paste" development plan. It would be nice also to see empires such as the Romulans and Kingons take on their species traits more too. When I get a Romulan ambassador asking me to open a trade deal and share technology for peaceful means, I get a little suspect (because it's the mid-24th century in the timeline, and they wouldn't do that) especially after they've just wiped out Khitomer, and especially as this event in cannon plays such a huge part in the Star Trek universe.So would I recommend it? Yes. BUT...it needs a lot more work to give it a truly unique Trek experience - as well as making it a lot more different from it's similar predecessor. Paradox have a plethora of amazing Trek content out there to draw from, but we don't even get an LCARS UI. Please, PLEASE make this MORE of a TREK experience.

_childDocuments_.review: For now, not recommendable.Not because of bugs, glitches or anything that I understand are being immediately addressed, but for failing to faithfully portray the iconic Star Trek franchise. I frankly don't care that it's based off of Stellaris - I even think that Stellaris is the closest starting point for what Star Trek: Infinite should be.The endlessly repeating "Search for life" popups are the constant reminder that it *IS* just Stellaris, with different faction names. Those popups were the best opportunity for exploring lore and posing the existential questions that the Star Trek shows have accustomed their viewers to. But they just generically repeat whatever Stellaris did, once in a while swapping a word for a recognizable Star Trek techno-babble. The A/B choices of random events are so generic, I don't even understand what part of the universe they're supposed to support.Really, it's in its Narrative Design that this game truly fails to deliver.System Design-wise, there were only a couple of mechanics that needed an overhaul to feel like we're playing in the ST:TNG universe:- Meeting new civilizations: just needs 10x times more of it - that's what Star Trek shows do every episode! And it shouldn't be a research project unless it's an exotic civ like the Borg. Just meet and greet - this was a cool feature in Stellaris, but has absolutely nothing to do with the Star Trek universe. This research project could have easily been replaced with a "first contact action" that's available to a flagship, and to governor ships perhaps, with fresh new options and outcomes.- Fleet range and Highway Nodes: just, no! Hyperlanes work in Stellaris universe and the devs were right to change them, but it needed to be changed in a way that's coherent with the universe! There's no excuse for coming up with the concept of "Node Highway" when Star Trek already gave us the concepts of Transwarp Conduits and the concepts of Wormholes. Just use those two! And if fleets needed operational range for balancing purposes, just make it consistent with a universe where Ships go "where no man has gone before", no where they go to their neighbors and call it a day because they're homesick.- No adaptation of the research system. If there's one system that needed to be invested in, it's this one. Techs are just randomly queued like in regular Stellaris. They're not even faction-dependent, so you have Federation techno-babble when playing as a Klingon. -.- This feature is by far the largest infringement on the lore.I sooo wanted to love this game and lose myself in this game. But I absolutely don't.I love ST, and I love Stellaris, but I just hate how they come together in this product.

The Federation have a massive mission tree and the other powers? The Cardassians have like 9 missions, the Federation have like 20 and get free warships (Enterprise and the Cerritos). It's really questionable, this whole thing. They should have, especially for a 4 player only multiplayer, made parity in terms of content between the empires.And it's a shame because there are good ideas here that could have made this a really excellent game. A sort of Star Trek version of "Gihren no Yabou" where you had all of this rich lore to work with and the player has access to all of these officers and characters from the series and not just a bunch of randomly generated characters, where you could make Janeway captain of the Enterprise D or whatever, that would have been really cool. But that sort of game doesn't work if you are using Stellaris as a framework because the core of the Stellaris experience is randomisation and fleet battles that are WAY too big for most of Star Trek outside of a Borg episode or a movie.Furthermore the Stellaris tech system is way too granular for Star Trek. You're giving the player so many choices in terms of weapons and there is no way for the player to rationally comprehend these differences without deep diving into the stats. It's not even a good system in Stellaris: designing ships doesn't work if you don't have turn based tactical combat so the player can get meaningful feedback on their designs. And in Star Trek, this idea doesn't make any sense at all.And all of this feedback is meaningless because this game is never going to get the overhaul it desperately needs to be anything more that a depreciated Stellaris clone. It's not a mainline Pdox release, so it will get like two "expansions" and thrown onto the junkheap. Pretty standard fare for the titles Pdox publishes (Hell, Lamplighters just came out and they've already disowned it.)Just play Stellaris' New Horizons. It's different but largely comparable to this.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit half-baked right now. A number of things they should have addressed before launching this.- Modernize the UI, I have to upscale it to a pixel mess on 4k. Feels very dated. Just a color swap and no official looking menus such as LCARS.- No official music, it's a pretty big deal. If you spend the money on the brand don't get cheap on the iconic music, obtain official music licenses. - Number of bugs, missions that get stuck or enemy ships I cant attack because they are locked to some sort of story trigger that wont fire.- Lack of official Star Trek species. I'll see an occasional reference to a real Star Trek race but there was no reason for randomly generated races when there is so much actual lore to pull from. It does feel like certain ones were initially left for DLC.- It's a bit overwhelming for players who have not recently played Stellaris. Many systems should have been turned off and introduced over time, juggling 17 different resources is unnecessary. It would have been much better to start with a single solar system and expand like Stellaris. It feels like i'm just loading someone else's save game and they are several hours in.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that is not quite the Star Trek experience I was looking forward too, and too much like Stellaris, which I already own and love. The issue is this feels like Stellaris and not enough like it's own game. I'm happy they brought back the warp drive (which was in the original Stellaris until they tweaked it to include only hyperspace travel between stars), but the ships are not multi-purpose like they are in Star Trek, and instead follow Stellaris' formula for specific ships for construction, science, and military. While I understand this as a way to play the game, I was hoping for the versatility for ships to take on whatever role is needed, like how Voyager (Intrepid-class) was a science vessel, rather than purely a military ship in Star Trek Infinite. And yes, I know you can get the Enterprise-D and it can both fight and explore, but I feel like this should have been the norm for all ships, not the exception.The time of when the game starts also messes me up as well. The game seems to primarily try to aim for the Next Generation Era and afterwards, skipping when the Federation was first founded and also the Original Series era as well. There are alot of star systems and aliens missing from the game as well. And while I understand that adding them would up the scale of the game, it just makes the Star Trek universe I'm trying to play as feel incomplete.I guess that's how I would sum up this game: incomplete. It has the potential to be a better game, but it was developed off of Stellaris and marketed to Star Trek fans as something new. However, it's not unique enough to be it's own game yet. When playing this game, I want to feel like it's a Star Trek experience, not a Stellaris one. If I wanted to play Stellaris, then that's what I would do.

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely a solid sister-game to Stellaris, as it's made with the same engine. The IP has to stay alive, it's an important cultural pillar and I choose to support it.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, it is similar to "Stellaris", which should not be a surprise.A little bit less complex but still with a lot of depth. I don't understand why some people complain, that it should have been only a DLC to "Stellaris". Making it an independent game gives it more freedom to add later "Mods" or DLCs of its own and the game itself is reasonably priced (similar to a DLC but you don't need to pay extra for Stellaris).  The map is awesome because you border with the other "major powers" in the center but you still have enough space to expand outward.I love that you are not restricted to "star lanes" but that there is a range for your "none-science-ships" which can be extended through technology and star bases. Later you will discover some kind of "Highway" that lets you travel bigger distances from one side of the galaxy to the other. This together with nebulas makes the map more interesting. The "Balance of Power" system is a great way to see where you stand compared to the others and I saw that when one got too big the others acted accordingly. The game has a lot of Star Trek content (events) and the mission tree adds to the immersion. I have not seen a "Tech Tree", maybe it will be added or someone will make a "Mod" for it.Documentation about the mechanics in the game, either through an encyclopedia or a "wiki site". There is a nice little tutorial in the game, which does a good job of explaining some basics without putting you off, but later you want to be able to look things up.

_childDocuments_.review: No, I can't recommend the game. And not just because it's a reskin of another game. Because there's just not much there to it. There's only one galaxy size and one galaxy type, and it's pretty small. You can never explore the gamma or delta quadrants. Game play amounts to sitting around and waiting for events much of the time.It feels like a demo to the game they should have made.And I'm already seeing political stuff in the game. In before "Star Trek was always about politics!" No, not like this. For example, there's one 'event' where a colony becomes a matriarchy and it just magically solves all problems for it. That's it. That's the event. Compare that to the TNG episode about a matriarchy where they're executing people for having traditional relationships. Two sides to every coin etc. (Update: now they are riots on that planet because their polices are too gender "binary". It'd almost be an improvement if it were riots for any other reason, but no Cardassian in Star Trek ever expressed any ideas similar to gender theory. Really, you're making a TNG-era game. Stop inserting modern politics.)Also, now there are Cardassians of every color. Because I guess "gray lizard people with spoons on their heads" was too difficult a description to follow. Not every faction needs to be a mirror of Earth and its interracial politics. Some can be, you know, alien.That stuff is the bridge too far for me. Not because I disagree with the politics of the devs, but because it's not like Star Trek was. I disagreed with the politics of most Star Trek writers and I still loved the show. Because they were good writers who knew how to justify their beliefs and didn't just beat everyone over the head with them. But if a game is sold to me based on nostalgia, I'd expect them to try to make it the way Star Trek used to be, not the way modern politics would have liked it to be.Speaking of stuff that's not like Star Trek btw, the weapon effects and the music are not like Star Trek. You'd think they could have gotten something that at least sounds similar for the music, but it's very generic.So, yeah, this is not for me because it's simplistic and not like Star Trek. Maybe some mods will fix it, if Paradox doesn't take them down, since I know they're famous for doing that.

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek: CANCELLEDDO NOT BUY, THIS IS CANCELLED.I refunded this game, despite being a huge fan of both Stellaris and Star Trek.It didn't feel like a finished or polished game. MEH), Species 8472, the Xindi (a current minor empire....), the Gorn, the Tholians, the Breen, the Dominion) and let me customise the galaxy (I always play the largest possible galaxy with the greatest number of AI and minor species in Stellaris, because the game feels rich and alive that way).I will revisit this in the future, to check the state of the game, but for now Stellaris and the Star Trek mods will more than satisfy this particular itch.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE this game.  I am a Stellaris fan and have been playing it for years through all the major updates.  Stellaris is a great game and has amazing mods to make it a passable 4x game with Star Trek elements.  What I mean by passable is that Stellars is a great game in it's own right, but even with the mods it never felt like Star Trek.  Just a great game with a Star Trek skin.  Then, Star Trek Infinite came along.  I was skeptical at first, especially with the mixed reviews.  But  "WOW!", this game really feels like Trek.  It is more simple than Stellaris, but still much more complex than most other 4x games.  I like the balance.  I like that it uses resources from Trek.  I have played for a few hours and already feel like I am playing in the Trek universe that I love.  The biggest problem with the modded Stellaris version "New Horizons" is that after a while it bogs down.  Too much detail to enjoy after your empire grows to a moderate size.  Since Infinite is more simple, it is more manageable with larger empires.  The interface is cleaner, everything seems more polished.  So, big thumbs up from me!  Hope you try and like it.  Oh, and I haven't hit any bugs yet ... they have patched it a few times, maybe most of the bugginess has been addressed in the patches since release.  If you're a 4x fan and a Trek fan, this should be a great game for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Having always been a Trek fan, and remembering ST Galaxies i was looking forwards to playing this game...Sadly the game is a disappointment. Although its graphics quality and smoothness are not an issue, the important factor - game play, is where it fails miserably. It is disjointed. You start with an already established set of borders, wars and all manner of other things that appear to be happening without you even gaining your bearings. The tutorial is unclear/indecisive, it does not give you clear instruction on button direction or control options on screen - and there are lots of buttons!Every 30 seconds or so a message pops up, giving you barely time to read the previous. None of the research trees or tech seems to have a point, its difficult to be sure what resource you are spending.The game tries to hard to micro manage everything but does not give obvious indication as to what (if anything) has changed when you do build/change/create/research. When a discovery is made, whether its a anomaly, star system or random event you jump to that place without seemingly being warned.War is declared. I haven't even established contact and already we are at WAR.Didn't notice any bugs in the game which is great but unfortunately it all feels very rushed, almost as if it was just a after thought to rake in cash.Normally ST is a no brainer for me, i am straight in, but this time its a no from me.GR is probably rolling in his grave, my advice, give this one a miss and look at Galactic Civilisation 3 maybe.

_childDocuments_.review: It's base game Stellaris with Star Trek candy coating. People complain it's a little slow; But, you can adjust that in the settings and also turn the game speed up. 4X games are slow by nature. It doesn't currently have the complexity of modern day Stellaris which I actually see as a good thing as I long for the streamlined previous versions of early Stellaris without all the bloated mechanics added in that game to justify capatalist DLC bloat. We haven't had a "good" Star Trek focused solely on ships and space exploration in what like 25 years? So, I'm quite happy with this release. Sadly, many special interest parties with their particular single issue gripes seem to be the loudest detractors to this game that was sorely needed to continue the franchise in the strategy gaming market. I dearly hope for at least a few good faction DLC's. Paradox please don't abandon us!

_childDocuments_.review: Really damn good game so far. However, you have to treat it like a campaign for Star Trek the Next Generation, instead of a sandbox game like the original Stellaris. I find it much more enjoyable than just playing a random Stellaris star race since you know what your role in the universe is - especially if you like Star Trek and know stuff about the lore.Otherwise, I think the art & music is great, and increases the immersion of being there controlling one of the four different factions. This is probably Paradox's best release in years, to be honest, so hats off to the devs (). Can't wait for what they cook in the form of DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, here we are.Sadly, the company had a very strong template here to make something unique and appealing, for not only Star Trek fans, but also the fans of the Stellaris game aswell.In the end though, they missed every single mark they could've aimed for.The game itself feels like a quickly rushed out of the gate Early Access.From the design down to things like actually the missions to finish the game.Sound alerts telling you you have lost a high ranking officer when your leaders gain a new level.War score not being possible to achieve even if you are bombarding the enemies planets.Blunders when calculating the scores for Victory conditions.The list goess on.This, is another prime example of a company riding the wave of a new hype theme (In this case Star Trek general resurgence).It's never been playtested, riddled with bugs and obvious blunders, and generally just a horrible design.Most of all this truly feels like a mod of Stellaris, that got abandoned half-way through its design.I cannot advice people anything else then simply to stay away from this product.

Still, that's a minor issue that I can get past because this game ticks all the boxes for me and I look forward to many more hours being invested in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge Star Trek fan and a huge Stellaris fan.  I've got 2,100 hours into Stellaris.   Unlike most of the negative reviews, I'm capable of reading and it was very clearly and officially stated this game was based on Stellaris.  It wasn't just a "rumor", it was right on the official announcement.  So, this shouldn't have been a surprise for anybody.  Initial impressions is they've delivered on giving it a Star Trek feel so job very well done on that.  If I didn't have 2,100 hours into Stellaris, I would probably be declaring it fantastic right now.  The problem is I do have 2,100 hours into Stellaris and not having Stellaris's QoL improvements is painful.  Don't get me wrong, if I try to pretend I've never played Stellaris, it's a great Star Trek game which is a void that badly needed filling IMO.  If you're coming in as purely a Star Trek fan looking for a strategy game, you're probably going to love it. But if you're a Stellaris player, staring at both titles in your Steam library, Infinite is a tough sell.  Given Paradox is publishing it and it's based on Stellaris, I expect both mods and DLC to follow in quantity as per the norm, so take that as you will.However, I'm not talking about DLC or mods, I'm not even going to touch those subjects.  I'm talking about things like the improvements to science ship automation and adding construction ship automation.  Infinite is basically missing out of years of Stellaris QoL improvements and that makes for a rough sell/transition for Stellaris players because it basically feels like you've stepped into a time machine.  You find yourself going "How did I used to have to do this, I forgot".  Or "Oh, man, I forgot we used to have to do this manually".  I mean an hour in I'm going "I forgot how much I hate researching anomalies stops auto-surveying".  I love current Stellaris' option of auto everything on science ships.
