_childDocuments_.review: Stardate 2365.07.23..A combine Romulan and Federation offensive has pierced the boundaries of the Cardassian Union. Legate Dukat, at the helm of the glorious navy that fights our foes and brings death to our enemies, has blunted their offensives. The Romulan offensive was smashed in the Trelka system while the Federation was blunted over Bajor. Actrium, taken early in the conflict, has been liberated. A status quo achieved, but a victory for Cardassia no less!Now, our intelligence tells us that the Romulans have made treaties with the Klingons who now advanced against the Federation, striking deep into their territory. In this peace that we have gained, we will grow stronger as our enemies weaken themselves. In the end, we will be the true victor, we will achieve greater heights! For Cardassia!=========================While pretty bare bones compared to Stellaris, which has the Star Trek mods, this official title is still fun. I was worried about when I saw only four factions as playable. There had been no dev diaries, to my knowledge, of minor factions, yet I was surprised. I saw Betazoids, Bajorans, Nausicaans, and Idanians as minor factions with one Ferengi outpost thus far. The game is pretty optimized and looks gorgeous! The colors, the UI, the music, and more all were given quite the detail.Now, certainly Stellaris has the leg above considering all the DLC and updates, but for a start, Infinite has the potential and solid foundations to become a great title in its own name.For 30 to 40 dollars, you get what you paid for. But, that doesn't mean it's so raw that there isn't much to bite. There is certainly room to grow and improve. It is a good foundation for potential and for what could become an absolutely amazing game. Keep it up, Nimble Giant and Paradox!

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike Star Wars - or Marvel - or DC or most massive multimedia IPs - Star Trek established a... different formula for itself back in the day.Ever play Birth of the Federation (Master Of Orion) ? Bridge Commander (various Totally Games flight sims) ? Elite Force (Quake) ?Knockoffs of popular games with a Star Trek© skin??Long ago - when the internet was young - this is what CBS/Paramount would  when they wanted a 'Star Trek©' game. Rent the IP out to a mid-tier developer - give them a fractional budget - and hope something platinum came out of it. It led to a lot of stinkers - granted - but it occasionally led to something truly special.Though, what it usually generated, was a 'fine' product.This is that.It's fine - it's serviceable - it's a neat little strategy game and if - like me - you're opposed to the idea of having to buy a huge amount of DLC to play one of the Stellaris mods then this might be for you.If you like strategy - then this might be for you.If you like Star Trek - this IS for you. You, like me, will tolerate the unstable launch and diet Stellaris for what it is to get even  in this universe.Buy it - let's see if we can support this game enough to get proper mod support (and by that I mean the STEAM workshop) and maybe a Dominion and Delta Quadrant DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: It just wasn't fun.As a player of Civ and Total War titles, I like to think I have a fair grasp of 4X mechanics, but this being my first true Paradox game, everything fun and engaging about those other titles is absent in this.  The battles are dull, uninvolved affairs of watching a red and green bar slowly slide one way or the other, totally absent of any interaction by the player.  The economics are obtuse and opaque, with an unnecessary number of resources to balance against one another.  To make matters worse, engaging in diplomacy actually hampers you.  The best way to play the game is not at all -- just let the AI kill each other and watch as you slowly rise to the top of the leader board.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit torn in recommending this.It's the first week of release. And there's a number of bugs and glitches on things. And a few design choices that will hopefully be re-balanced. And if you're willing to overlook that, it can be a pretty fun game. If you've played stellaris:It adds some interesting mechanics with the Federation empire that feels in line with the Star Trek cannon. The resource system is similar, but different enough to be interesting.There's a branching "Mission" tree which grants bonuses and adds some narrative goals (Though it's a bit broken at the moment)It's not as in-depth or fleshed out as Stellaris (Which is to be expected, Stellaris has been actively updated over 5 years or so)The map feels smallerIf you've not played StellarisIt's a pretty in depth strategy game where you manage an empire.There's some story elements in it, but it's not character focused. And events can happen randomly. Think choose-your-own adventure book rather than epic novel.It'd like to say it's a diamond-in-the-rough waiting to be polished. But I'm not sure if that polish will ever come. I hope it does, this has the potential to be great. Until then, be prepared for some jank if you do decide to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I have now played 13 hrs of the game.   While you cant play the other races within ST, they are there.    As the Fed, you can integrate them, as the other starting races, you can conquer them for their civics.   The anomalies need work.  I so far have repeated 2 of the anomalies in the same game with only 13 hrs of play.   How you get the enterprise is interesting as well(I wont give it away).    But I dont like how they do it for 2 reasons.   1, its not the true enterprise D.   Its based upon the tech level of the shields, weapons, etc.   So its basically just a named ship, and an expensive 1 at that.  The traditions are interesting, but make no real sense for the FED.   The ascension perks are decent, I actually liked some of them for the FED.   The research tech so far is a little under whelming.   Now mind you, I havent tried the other races yet, but for the FED, they are not unique in my opinion.   Maybe I havent gotten far enough down the tech tree to see, but to me they seem cookie cutter.  Example, there are no bonuses to diplomacy which the fed is known for.   There is no real tech dealing with the prime directive nor any reason to follow the prime directive as the fed either that I can see.  Also, as the fed, you are interacting with the Borg way to early for the tech tree limits.   If they are starting in this time frame, then some of the tech should already be there.   Also, starting in this time frame, where is the Federation Council.   That should be a big part of it, and they are not to be seen.  Star Fleet Academy seems to be just a building on Earth, nothing more.  The game has potential, but right now it isnt.   Dont get me wrong, I will continue to play it to see if I am missing something later in the game, but I just dont know.For me, play Horizons or Civilisation for Stellaris.   More you can do with those mods and alot more immersive.   What they are doing is gearing the game towards dlcs.   I can see it now, a new race every 2 or 3 months at 12.99 a pop.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a labor of love, in two ways. The devs putting the heart into this game, and the player having to fight the game to enjoy some Star Trek. A very soft "not recommended" from me. Though I don't feel it was a waste of money as Paradox games usually age like wine, I do feel too frustrated to play again in the near future after just 11 hours and 1.5 games. Pros: Where No Man Has Gone Before: The artwork, setting, and attention to detail here are amazing. It's clear the devs have a love for Star Trek that shines through every aspect of this game. Tomorrow is Yesterday: It's Stellaris lite. I've got a ton of time in Stellaris and I've been playing since release, but sometimes the game gets a bit bogged down. It's nice to jump into a game here and not have to deal with a lot of the bloat of starting a game in Stellaris. Lower Decks: Much of the Stellaris engine fits very well in the Star Trek universe and about 80% of the game just feels great. My first five hours felt like a breath of fresh air and just felt Star Trek. Neutral: Deja Q: It's a Stellaris reskin. I don't think that's a bad thing, but you should absolutely be aware of that going in. Hollow Pursuits: The focus trees are a fun addition to the game but are not super fleshed out. Basically a button click for things you were already gonna do. Looking forward to expansions on the concept like in other Paradox titles. A couple times events and focus tree items got jammed up and impossible to continue. If you don't keep on them then key leaders will die from old age before you can complete the line and this will hard stop those events and focus tree items. Unsure if this is working as intended or not.Cons:The Menagerie: Deeply frustrating events. The events in war are exactly the same in all four empires (I assume, they were identical between UFP and RE). And boy are they awful. One of them is that one of your fleets just straight up disappears. This only triggers during a war. It absolutely lost me a couple wars early game when one third of my military just vanishes. Then there are a number of events that occur over the course of the war that are seemingly intended to tell you how the war is going, but trigger randomly. Star Fleet troops are in the middle of invading Cardassia, their fleets burning in space, Bajor liberated, and I get an event pop up titled "We are losing this war." There are at least three others like that that seem to be an attempt to give some flavor to war but are not tied to reality and seem to pop up at random.  I, Borg: Unfinished events like the *spoiler* that seem to hint towards bigger events that never trigger. I played a full game as the Federation and it was so boring after the first half. Once you eclipse the other powers they essentially stop participating in the game. The Federation (correctly) can't claim systems and generally can't be aggressive. This is good from a lore perspective but essentially means the last 200 years of gameplay is Microsoft Excel simulator. Also there was a bug that made it impossible to assimilate minor powers into the federation. Schisms: Diplomacy sucks. This was always a complaint of Stellaris but is unfortunately severely highlighted in this game, especially if you're playing Romulus or UFP. The UFP is relegated to a purely reactionary force on the galactic stage since you can't do anything. Spying also sucks which means playing the Romulans is like playing the Klingons or Cardassians but painted green. Face of the Enemy: Enemy fleets are really jump happy. The enemy will have a half dozen military fleets jumping around your systems like a squirrel on crack. They don't do anything but sit on the edge of the system not engaging with your starbase (even when they could easily defeat it) and jump away as soon as you enter the system. Makes war a very frustrating endeavor.Turnabout Intruder: The pirates make me want to put a phaser in my mouth. They will randomly jump into your systems and early game you cannot repel them. They destroy your starbase meaning you have to reclaim the system and also takes 1,000 each of the basic resources away from you. This is devastating early game and there doesn't seem to be a way to do anything about it until late game when you can repel the fleets or find the pirate system and ask them pretty please to stop. This is what finally broke me into using the console to just delete the fleets as soon as I see them. They're infinite though so it's a temporary measure at best. Balance of Terror: I have literally never seen the AI employ a cloaking device despite the fact I know it's in the game. Shades of Grey: All the factions are boring are seems to be kneecapped by being crammed into the Stellaris engine. I've already elaborated on the UFP. Romulus has an event pretty early game where the sun explodes. It's fun from a lore and universe perspective but even metagaming and preparing for it it still absolutely wrecks your economy. I haven't played the Cardassians or Klingons yet. I think both probably lend themselves better to the engine as they are more conquest focused empires but I'm not very optimistic after the UFP and Romulans. The Trouble with Tribbles: It's pretty buggy. I know that's par for the course these days but still.~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Edit: Got the itch while watching DS9 and reluctantly played another campaign. I played as UFP all the way to 2650 and got a victory. No material changes to my review but some observations:-Couldn't complete a focus tree because of a bug. It said I didn't own a system that I clearly did. Deleted the starbase and rebuilt, donated the system and retook it, nothing fixed it. -Even as Evil UFP you can only claim three systems at once. I had to spend a couple hundred years chipping away at the other powers despite the fact I could have conquered them all at once. -The borg are the worst. I clapped the "end game crisis" before mid game. I didn't even use all my fleets. -The other three powers are way too diplomatic. The Klingons, Romulans, and Cardassians never even attempted to conquer minor powers. That's like the Cardassians whole thing and the other two should at least be more aggressive and treacherous respectively. -I threw everything into liberating Bajor very early in the game. Bajor responded by hating me and forming several treaties with the Cardassians. I guess Kai Winn won in this universe.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not one to often review, but the people who take to this complaining that it's "just a Stellaris reskin" are wrong. There are definitely some similarities, but there are enough other mechanics to make things interesting. Yes, I'm recommending the game, but there problems.For one, the game definitely needs some polish that it evidently didn't get before release. For example, when I go to my envoys to see what they're doing, I get the base game code for integrating a new species into the Federation. "vol_INTSPE##" or something like that. I also see that in diplomatic modifications. Today I completed the mission to save the Romulan people when their star exploded and it was like "compmis_ex" +200. Another is "warp_agreement_yes".... Which I don't even know what a "warp agreement" is. (It's not open borders, that's a separate thing.) I figure a patch or two will fix some/most/all of that.For all that, I've been playing the Federation of Planets, and I've gotten to explore a large amount of official timeline and I've decided to do the whole "benevolent Federation" thing. It is possible to make the Federation into a conquering police state by fulfilling different missions in the tree. I haven't touched any of the other three factions, so I can't say what their mission trees look like. Science is handled in a way that I quite honestly like, with just "Science" being generated and applied to all the trees equally, instead of getting specific amounts of society/physics/engineering, though the tech tree is done with "cards" shuffled into those three groups just like it is in Stellaris.There is a complaint that ship advances come far too slowly, and I have to agree. I'm five hours into a game, and I only just got the second ship class. They're equipped with weapons that were FAR more advanced than what they actually had in the show. I'd rebalance those mechanics if I were them.I'm a trek fan, but only from the tv shows and the movies, and I've really enjoyed what I have so far, which is not the complete story. And only from the Federation of Planets side of things so far.Someone in one of the reviews says that the map is always the same. That's not true. The map is slightly different in its initial setup (and does change slightly from playthrough to playthrough, even when you don't alter the settings.) But you do get the basic, Federation to the South, Cardassians to the West, Klingons to the East and Romulans to the North, with the Romulan Neutral Zone making up a significant portion of what would be the Federation Border. The map outside the starting area is different for every playthrough. The map is somewhat less than lore accurate, mostly to prevent the Federation from having a MASSIVE advantage. If the map were lore accurate, the Federation would have empty space to the "North", the "South", and the East, in the North or South depending on where the Cardassian Union is placed on the maps. Even the "lore-accurate" maps aren't all consistent.Yes, I have some complaints about the UI, and I had to work the graphics for about ten minutes to get them to look right on my very small display (I have a 13-inch Macbook Air so it can be tough to do that, but I make it work with all the other Grand Strategy games.) And there are some crashes and some weird things that have happened (some combination of buttons reverted my graphics to what the game originally set them to that was all wrong, and I had to save and quit and come back to fix it.Finally, the music is much more Stellaris than Star Trek. Sometimes you hear a little note or three of Star Trek in there, but if you're expecting to boot it up to the Star Trek: The Next Generation/DS9/Voyager theme, you're going have to do it yourself (it's not hard if you own the music), or wait for somebody to mod it.If you're hesitant about it, go ahead and wait a few days for some of the kinks to be ironed out, but if you're able to look past some of the warts, and you want a Star Trek Game, I would recommend Star Trek: Infinite.

Voice acting is cringy, its riddles with bugs, and the UI and empire management systems feel like it was built off a version back in 2016. It makes Imperator Rome look polished and AAA in comparison. The fact that so few people heard about it due to poor advertisement, and that there was a media embargo on it, speaks volumes. The whole thing just feels like it was thrown together with minimal effort, attaching a few memorable empire names here and there, and thrown out the door to rake in some extra cashits a shame as I was so excited for a Star Trek themed Stellaris game, but I think I'll stick with the mods available for now.Maybe I'll come back to it in a year or so, but I'm worried it will end like Imperator Rome. Such a damn shame :(

_childDocuments_.review: Update 10/18/2023:I've uninstalled the game but didn't ask for a refund. As I logged back in, after playing Stellaris, I was again frustrated by the distance created with the Stellaris quality of life updates. So much was manual again, among other things!The Star Trek connection feels even more forced than my short initial play time. I don't think that Starfleet only ever had 1 type of ship (I don't count construction or science - though that's a whole other problem). Maybe there's a way to get there, but there seem to be several issues:1) The core Stellaris mechanics are not suitable for an established universe that doesn't match those mechanics2) The core current Stellaris quality of life mechanics are not available in this variation, which makes it hard to play when compared against its own predecessor3) The game doesn't match the emotional depth of the Star Trek universeNote, I believe this is my only review on Steam at this point, which is due to the importance of both Star Trek and Stellaris for me.Original:I know it only shows minutes playing on this game, however, I have played over 7,000 hours on Stellaris, and I am a huge Star Trek fan.I was very much looking forward to Star Trek with the Stellaris engine with the best of both worlds (like Spock :) ), but that's not what I felt happened here. _childDocuments_.review: If you like Star Trek, then you will like this game. If you're a Stellaris or Paradox fan looking for Stellaris 2.0 or something similar in terms of scope and depth, you'll be disappointed. This game is a re-skinned earlier version of Stellaris that has been watered down and streamlined, with some new features added from other Paradox games like the mission tree from EU4 or 'galactic' tension from HOI4 and so on to spice things up. The gameplay is relatively simplistic compared to Stellaris, and there is not much to do besides play each of the four factions once or twice. The Federation has an alternate history mission tree, for example, that you could decide to play. The alternate path allows you to go on the offensive and attack other civilizations, where normally you would be stuck behind a purely defensive role. Besides that, each game will feel relatively the same, although there is some small RNG like where certain minor factions spawn and how the galaxy generates. Outside of that, though, it will feel the same in each playthrough. I would suggest playing with friends to make the game more interesting, but there is only so much to be done in a game that only allows you to play as four factions. It is as if you were going to play HOI4 but only could play Germany, the Soviet Union, the United States, or Japan, and had only one or two paths to play for each nation.The game also currently has a number of bugs, although I haven't encountered any and I haven't gotten any technical issues either. The game for me has worked seamlessly so far so I can't comment on those issues, but be aware of them. For example one reviewer was soft-locked out of continuing the end-game story line.In the end, this is a fun game to pick up if you like Star Trek. You'll recognize the characters and the lore, and the random events that pop up you will be able to recognize from episodes of the shows. That alone will be enough to keep you going through a playthrough. If you're not a fan of Star Trek, you'll probably find a lot of the core gameplay shallow, and will be disappointed in the relatively small scope of the game (you only get to play in half of a relatively small galaxy, for instance). If you're a Trekkie, I would pick it up. If you're not, I would wait until it is on sale to give it a go, or get it to play if you have a friend group to play the other three factions with.

_childDocuments_.review: It is, quite literally, Stellaris with a Star Trek paintjob. So this means that if you play Stellaris, you already know how to play this, for good or for ill. I love Stellaris and I love Star Trek, so I'm personally happy to have the two combined, but it comes with some BUTS.It's Stellaris, BUT you don't get the whole galaxy to play in. Alpha and Beta Quadrants only.It's Stellaris, BUT it's not a procedurally-generated galaxy ENTIRELY. It's got four big pre-set empires who are all rubbing borders with each other, but the rest of the (again, only two quadrants) galaxy is random.It's Stellaris, BUT you can't make your own empire. You're Federation, Romulans, Klingons, or Cardassians. And that's it.It's Stellaris, BUT when you recruit Galactic Paragons they treat them like any other leader (seriously, Spock is a "promising young recruit"?)It's Star Trek, BUT Xindus and Denobula are unpopulated, and the pops are not in the Federation, despite being in the Federation borders. I'll admit this one bugged me as a lifelong Enterprise fan.It's Star Trek, BUT there's no LCARS UI. And the sound effects seem kind of...generic.It's Star Trek, BUT there's a total lack of minor empires (they don't have to be playable! But we have the one-planet species we can get missions from, why not sprinkle in a few larger empires, too? Where's the Breen? Where's the Tholians? Where's the Xindi? Where's the Suliban? Where's the Gorn? Where's the Kelpiens? Where's the Caitians? Where's the Orions? Where's the Saurians? Where's the Edosians? Where's the Pakleds and Pakled Planet? Where's the Elachi? Where's the sentient gas clouds?If you want the "species of the week" aliens where they get somebody from the local Shakespeare company and throw a single rubber forehead on them, yeah they've got you covered! But if you want the more complex, more interesting designs? You're outta luck.)And on the topic of "everybody's just a human", where's the TOS planets where they're just Romans or cowboys or gangsters, but IN SPACE? Grab some of those old period drama costumes out of storage and let's see what Sigma Iotia II's been up to since Kirk! Seems like a slam-dunk for a pre-FTL species. If you're gonna do the basic aliens, you might as well go ALL-IN.It really needs some varied start dates, too. Like Crusader Kings. Starting at the Khitomer Massacre is fun and all, it's a time we haven't really seen much of, but it'd be nice if we could start in the ENT period, or TOS/SNW, or even Discovery (the Klingon War would be a challenging start date that could provide opportunities for a divergent, more militaristic Federation!) Because that's the thing about Stellaris, it provides OPTIONS. There's a reason it's a decade old and still going strong. Because it has variety. This game......... doesn't. And that's fine, I knew what I was getting into, but I WILL get bored of it eventually and go back to Stellaris. Because Stellaris is always fresh.It's a fun game, and I hope it survives a long while. But is it for everyone? Your mileage may vary. I recommend watching and reading the dev diaries before buying. A lot of negative reviews seem to be people complaining about things we already knew about, weeks in advance. If not years. Because, again, this is Stellaris with a fresh coat of paint. If you don't like Stellaris, you're not gonna have a good time. And if you DO like Stellaris but don't like the restrictive nature of playing in a pre-defined galaxy, you should probably not play a game set in a pre-defined galaxy.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of both Star Trek and strategy games. This game is a good blend of both.Negative reviewers want this game to both more and less Stellaris. This, to me, is a mistake. The game is approachable for players who are newer to the genre, and it foregrounds the Trek universe. Many of the game's discoverable anomalies and events mirror Star Trek episodes. They're cleverly written and help to build the immersion.Players who expect the game to perfectly match the Trek timeline will be disappointed. With so many canonical events, some of them fire out of order or in ways that are anachronistic. These misalignments are occasionally jarring, but I can't imagine the difficulty of keeping characters, events, and conditions appropriately locked together while still giving the player freedom.In its current release, the game has some bugs, most of which are only a little annoying. Dismayingly, my current save file (35 hours in) has become corrupt and unplayable. I expect these kinds of errors will be remedied in patches. Though I can't continue my current adventure, it was fun along the way.As with most other Paradox releases, this one will no doubt have scads of DLC: playable factions, events, mechanics, and more. I'm excited to see what comes. For now, though, I'm happy to have purchased and played this game. Is it perfect? No. But I can't wait to boldly go again soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Tentative recommendation. While it is unpolished and somewhat buggy, I think it demonstrates particular strengths over Stellaris itself -- the set galaxy encourages a very different way of engaging with the other powers, and certain new mechanics like crew being a resource, are something Stellaris itself could stand to port over.The biggest weakness of the game is that it is built on a significantly older branch of the Stellaris engine, with a lot of aspects and issues that Stellaris itself simply doesn't have. It's a fun twist on Stellaris, has a nice Star Trek coat of paint, but it'll only become great if it is polished and fixed up over time.

I've unlocked the Galaxy class in the year 2430. At that time it should actually be like 70 years old. I've yet to be able to research the Defiant or the Sovereign. The game could be very good in the future but for now it really needs a lot of polish.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't bad, but it isn't really a simulation of the Trek universe. If you just want to play a Trek themed game of stellaris, this would be a premium version of the trek total conversion mod. Its good looking, has lots trek art and stories, and if that's what you want I think this is actually worth it. However, for me I have decided to return the product as there just wasn't any mechanics that felt tweaked enough (or at all) to fit the trek universe. Personally, I really wanted ships to operate more independently like they do in Star Trek. Example of something cool they could have done with ships: Assigning a captain to each ship, and then an admiral per group of ships would have been much more interesting. The ships could have been off exploring and conducting missions (opportunity for more story) within a designated area and then recalled when combat is happening. Unfortunately, ships really just operate like they do in Stellaris. So they just sit around. The combat is also boring because of this and not very Trek. Other weird things like being able to just go to war with Cardassia with the sole goal to humiliate them as the Federation. No real effort to simulate the world of politics in the Trek universe. The map is also streamlined, making it seem kind of oddly shaped especially if you are familiar with Alpha and Beta quadrants.Overall, its just not really that immersive if you know the lore of Star Trek. But if you want a premium total conversion mod of stellaris, this could still scratch your itch. Follow me at

_childDocuments_.review: Should my opinion change as I intend to revisit this game in 6 months,  I will update this review.In a nutshell I do not recommend this game. It isn't ready in its current state. In fact for the price paid, it's absolutely daylight robbery.There are several things I am pretty upset about;1 - When playing MP some of the diplomacy options between you and other players are permanently greyed out. You cannot do certain things with them, no matter how long you improve relations. This seems to be deliberate over a bug. Why? If me and a friend decide to play coop and then fight it out once we're the last 2 standing, whats the problem with that? Why have the game prevent that? Makes even less sense when you consider the Federation and Klingon's were allied anyway during the show....2 - Lack of ship / stations designs. It's Star Trek, we were never going to have the customisation Stellaris gives us, fine. However, a full tech tree unlock gives you 5 ship classes to play with, 1 defensive station, some weapons that fit in universe but the majority just don't, and ZERO effort on providing a adequate name pool for said ships so you end up with "U.S.S. Name XIV" for a ship name, which is absurd. Not only that but the Defiant isn't even in the game. So they either lied (and continue to lie) during their promotional campaign, or it's only available behind some sort of paywall that I don't have access too. Either way, I won't be purchasing anything more to support this product. 3 - You're expected to micromanage EVERY planet you colonise or conquer? I started to lose track at 20, and the universe has hundreds. What the hell.Overall, it's bad. They could have taken Stellaris, gave it a face lift and injected the Star Trek in to it and released a fully complete game with all the lessons learnt from Stellaris already baked in. Instead they've taken version 1.0 of Stellaris and gave us the bare minimum so they can fleece the fan boys some more with DLC's. The sad thing is people will STILL pay KNOWING they're being fleeced. If you want a Star Trek strategy game, buy Stellaris when it's on sale, download the Star Trek mod and play that. This is a waste of your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy, unless it's very heavily discounted. _childDocuments_.review: The Good:  - A Star Trek Grand Strategy Game, the first since Birth of the Federation way back in the day - Uses the Stellaris engine, so players of Stellaris will be able to easily pick up and play - Star Trek related events and story missions - Uses a Hearts of Iron style mission tree, which can lead to ahistorical playthroughs i.e the Federation going bad, or the Cardassians being cooperative - Graphics and music immerse you in the Star Trek universeThe not so good - It's an earlier Stellaris engine so there's still some irritating micromanagement i.e governors and spies have their own ships and you need to move them around. - As your chosen power expands things can start to feel bloated, lots of micromanagement, and it doesn't feel very streamlined The potential - This is the base of a new game, but what it could become with future patches and DLC is exciting! - The Mod community could do great things with this game Overall: A good, though not amazing, game that starts to scratch that Star Trek grand strategy itch with lots of potential. 7/10 (if that potential is realised, that score could very easily go up!)

_childDocuments_.review: This game has potential. But that potential is not yet realized. My review might change in the future if they implement enough changes. But as it stands now this game is more frustration than it is fun. Here are some of the key problems:1) It feels too much like Stellaris. Now hear me out: I -love- Stellaris. One of my favorite games ever. But to really soar this game needs to leave Stellaris behind. One good example of this: In Stellaris you have to work to research large and larger ship sizes. You start at the bottom, and work your way up. That shouldn't be the case in Infinite. This game starts in the TNG period. Not TOS, or pre-TOS. There is no good reason why each side should only have the smallest ship size unlocked. And of course the ships they picked are questionable in some cases. Intrepid over Excelsior? Yeah... For the UFP at least, they should start with Miranda, Excelsior and Ambassador unlocked from the start. I would also have updated models in the future that replace older ones- same rough size and cost, but better/more features. Think upgrade the Miranda to Steamrunner, as just one example. 2) More divergence between factions. This is where I think the game can really shine over Stellaris. Make each side feel truly unique. Don't simply give them some buffs or incentives towards certain playstyles. Really differentiate how each should play and then reinforce/reward that. The basic building blocks of this are there, it just needs more. 3) More interesting systems and space objects. Star Trek lore is filled with all kinds of possible encounters. There needs to be unique system, there should be more types of space creatures or other things for you to interact with. 4) "Mid" factions. I am talking about a handful of factions that are in between the major 4 and the minor powers. I am talking about the Breen, Gorn, and Tholians, to name a few. Use them for "mid-game" events or other challenges as the game goes on. 5) Bugs and Balance- both need work. Some is already being done, but more is needed.

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek: Infinite SpreadsheetsIt's Civ-in-space with a (quite pretty) Star Trek skin. It pretends to be a Star Trek game that honors the lore, the universe, and the peoples of 90's era Trek, but is only 'skin' deep. Edit: Apparently it's Stellaris, which I do not play because I do not find it enjoyable. Too bad; I thought this was a new game with some of Paradox's 4x mechanics ported over. I guess it's more of a poor mod for an old game, like season one of ST:Pic. (Android Picard; give me a break. *slams head on desk*)It's pretty enough, but last-gen graphics. Starships are pretty static 3d models with some lens flare. Maybe it gets better, but I'm probably not going to find out.The promised story-line is as easy to find as a genetically modified Suliban. I assume it's something to do with one of the multiple mission logs... but you know, just assuming here.No achievements unless you're on "hardcore" mode, so you weak-willed non-Klingons may not seek glory. What a joke. Star Trek was about exploration, not 'hardcore' shi... whateverThe game has real depth and seems to have a lot of care put into every tooltip. The voiced tooltips are horrendous though... I mean it didn't stop even when I exited to menu and started a different game. I'll be honest, this game has some potential but I couldn't make it through the first 2 hours before I got seriously overwhelmed by the bombardment of tips. Aaand the game is unplayable without some guidance in the beginning because there is simply too damned much going on all at once. Put it like this, when I started Civ VI, I skipped the tutorials because you know, SIX, and I beat the nuts out of the first 5, so get on with it already. This is NEW and not intuitive, yet. So, huge learning curve to even begin to discover if it's enjoyable in the mid or late game stages. WHERE IS MY STORY? For real though, there's no objective goal beyond trying to figure out what each of the very tiny (ui scaling sucked) icons does or doesn't do. My god this game's ui is a mess.I won't refund because I will support any game that is Star Trek in hopes of more of them, but this game needs some serious work on the user experience side of things. If there's amazing graphics, show me them! if there is a great campaign, then put it in my face and let me play it! If you expect me to spend 2 hours figuring out tooltips just so I can start my first mission, say so and then piss off back to the Gamma quadrant.So disappointed I feel like I'm watching the first season of ST:Discovery again.

_childDocuments_.review: It feels a bit rough at times, which is not totally surprising for a Paradox launch? Some of the tooltips are not clear, and not all the things I remember from Stellaris are working the same way in ST:I, which makes for an occasionally frustrating experience...HOWEVER, it feels like a really good branch off of the mainline Stellaris platform? Like, we have Warp drive again rather than starlanes, which is a huge change. The starting zone is pretty fixed, with the good ol' cluster of Romulans, Cardassians, Klingons, and the Federation all together... each with "advanced starts" relative to Stellaris. Warp drive and multiple starting planets (partly to accommodate the Federation's multiculturalism) are better than the starting setup for Stellaris where it can be easy to get locked behind someone else's set of starlanes.No, it's not BOTF... but I feel that people have overly fond memories of the clunk factor in BOTF's turn-based setup and Civ-lite style.This is still a "simplified" Trek, not built for the minutia of 20 classes of Starfleet Frigate through multiple eras of TV shows and movies and video games... so if you're going to be irritated by a limited flavor of Starfleet, play Cardassians or Romulans.Like Stellaris, the potential is there for a launch title. It's an inexpensive Paradox launch title as well, especially given the license and the feature set it lifts from a later-stage Stellaris branch. For as much as the Astral money grab annoys me as an expensive Stellaris DLC, ST:I feels like a very inexpensive start of a Stellaris-like experience.Buy in for the potential and the Warp drives.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this, but it feels like such a shallow game that I think I'm done with it after one run through.  The game doesn't pace correctly (I was able to unlock the Enterprise-E before Galaxy Class ships, which is weird) and there's a lot of just plain bad gameplay.  Minor factions ask for the same mission to be done over and over.  In my game the Naussicans were pirates but had a double secret base somewhere (at least two of them) and I couldn't stop them.  It didn't matter, but it was annoying.  The Borg Queen beat me because I wasn't paying attention, then just camped (completely inert, no hostility) on a node and basically ended the Borg questline entirely.  The Cardassians assimilated the Bajorans pretty much 10 minutes into the game for me, so that questline as Federation just didn't work unless I wanted to play the Mirror Universe I guess.  If they're meant to have a quest where you recruit them and have some cool stuff locked behind it, maybe they shouldn't be able to be soaked up by the Cardassians before Sisko is even born.  I know, I know it's a game.  It just isn't a very good one when it kicks you entirely out of the environment of the game by giving you major questlines, and then chopping them off.  Space combat is Stellaris.  If you've played it you know how it goes. Make big stacks and watch them win or get decimated. Oddly, there's an "effective warp range" mechanic that's annoyingly frustrating and definitely not in line with how things work in Star Trek.  The whole space highway concept is a very poorly implemented restriction on just having ships fly through space.  I don't get the point of it, there could have been a better way to implement an influence sphere or other restriction on where you can settle planets that doesn't also stop your military from going wherever they want.  (it's also what stopped me from defeating the pirates I think, I had to assimilate two minor factions just to be able to get TO the base that I thought was going to end the pirate threat once and for all, which again did not actually do anything to stop them).   If a science vessel can get to a system, why can't my 144 Galaxy Class ships with longer range do it? I just wanna kill pirates! Also, just to make things worse, there's absolutely nothing for a win screen other than "u did it, good job" and exit the game.  Pretty disappointing.  I just conquered the entire galaxy, sort-of defeated the Borg and made friends with 10 insignificant civilizations, and all I got was this lousy t-shirt.  Maybe it'll be fixed up and worth playing after a few patches, I don't know.  I just know I spent 22hrs on a broken game that wasn't all that much fun for a whole lot of it.  I would probably play it again without the bugs, even though some of the gameplay isn't all that great, but for now it's just not something I'm gonna spend another week of my free time on.

The game is based on Stellaris, which itself isn't the issue, they just haven't adapted the systems to this game very well, random research really doesn't work for this game Combat is awful, just a chaotic mess, no rerouting phasers, power to shields or even the ability to attack aft or forward shields just click a massive blob of ships at their blob and win or lose, absolutely shocking that they paid for the licence but haven't any of the sound effects or even the sound track from the shows. There's also no voice acting for the Hero characters, no 'engage' when clicking on the Enterprise.They should've scaled the combat down so you could have smaller more meaningful engagements such as the tense cat and mouse submarine warfare from the show maybe something similar to Home world or Battle fleet Gothic?. There is a severe lack of ship diversity so you can't really specialise ships into certain roles. Can't really seek out new life and new civilisations you just find neutral worlds and get met with a bland diplomacy screen were they repeat the same phrases again, works in Stellaris as it's more open ended but this is meant to be a tighter narrative why can't we get unique missions from them like the t.v. show were we solve a dilemma or something. Also a massive lack of unique events in the game a massive issue when you're mainly staring at a screen waiting to happen.More time was clearly spent on the federation which makes me think that maybe they should've made them the only playable race to begin with, released the game in a more polished state then added the others to play at a later date.The game does have some good qualities, the developers seem really open and receptive to critique and have regularly been patching issues. Bear in mind that they are mostly patching silly Q.A. oversights with a few understandable bugsAs a Star Trek fan you'll most likely enjoy it but you'll be constantly asking yourself 'why did they do that that way?' and 'why is that not like it is in canon?'Really depends if you want an alright game now or wait for MAYBE a good to great game in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: After time has passed and updates have been released, I would like to say that this game is definitely one of my most favorite Star Trek/Space 4X Grand Strategy game! Stellaris still being my number one favorite though but Star Trek Infinite is climbing up to become second!There is a lot of complaints of this game being Stellaris. But it is not. What people fail to realize that Stellaris was built to be solely about Stellaris, nothing else. Not Star Wars, not Stargate, not Mass Effect and definitely not Star Trek. Are there total conversion mods that turns Stellaris into those games? Yes. But that does not make Stellaris a Star Trek Game or a Star Wars Game, etc. Stellaris will always be a Stellaris game.Star Trek Infinite is its own game. Does it have elements of Stellaris? Of course. Developers were given permission to use Stellaris to build this game. But there are obvious differences that this game has compared to Stellaris.Then there was the hiccup at launch. Who is truly surprised that games come out buggy at launch? It's lately been becoming a thing, which is annoying indeed but at this point, it should be expected. Cyberpunk, Pokemon Scarlet/Violet, Starfield. And more. Did the Developers hop onto fixing the hiccups at launch? Their response to fixing the game so that players can play it, was quite quick.And what others also fail to realize, is that it will always take time to flesh out the bugs, iron out the kinks, and make the game better over time. Stellaris wasn't perfect at start. It was great, but over the years, the developers improved it to where it is today and it is so much better than it was at launch. 25 tile planets...crazy border gore...multiple FTL options that was slogging down the game for most people. Again, the developers spent years improving Stellaris to where it is today and thus have the experience and tips that they could offer to the developers of Star Trek Infinite to help improve it more quickly.But these things do take time.Overall, I was quite excited when this game was announced, very excited when it was launched and not as disappointed as most people were and definitely was not shaming the game either after playing it for the first time. I know improvements will come, and I do quite enjoy the game as it is now and cannot wait for more! We all know there's going to be DLC in the future but I am quite excited to learn what they have planned for the future of this game. Perhaps they could offer a preview to a roadmap?Take my review as you will, it is my opinion after all and if you do not agree with my opinion, that is your choice and it will not alter my opinion or my review of this game in any way.Edit:Unfortunately the latest announcement states that the continued development of this game has ended. Likely due to Paramount but no one will ever know.BUT there is enough for the modding community to keep the game alive! And I for one, who have plans for this game in a group I am in, I too plan to keep this game alive. Games that have been cancelled have been revived and development returned to full force. I hope some day, that too will happen, with Star Trek: Infinite. I refuse to give up hope and no one will take that away from me.Live Long and Prosper!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very disappointing. I went in with very low expectations, and even those weren't metI have completed one full game as the Federation, achieving a diplomatic victory. What I can say is good about the game is the addition of new victory conditions is nice, and a feature that Stellaris unfortunately lacks. Also, some of the UI presentation is excellent, and I like some of the unique concepts (like warp logistics range), at least in concept.But then there's all the problems. The first is the parts of the UI that aren't polished to a shine. The galaxy map is nice, but the alert icons are odd. Ships in transit to reinforce your fleet? Expect to see the icon Stellaris uses for federation XP decreasing. The alert icon stellaris uses for your federation level increasing is also used wrong (although I'll admit I can't remember for the life of me what they use it for).Then there's the voice acting. This might be the most egregious design decision in the game. There's such a comically low number of unique voice lines that I can't take the game seriously. What lines they have don't match Star Trek at all. The Klingon male diplomacy screen voice spoke more like a Ferengi than a Klingon, and only ever said one thing. Every female voice is unbelievably high pitch, and again, only has one line on the diplomacy screen. But the problems aren't contained to the diplomacy screen, because there's a severe lack of alert sounds too. Leader just level up? You'll get the alert sound for a leader dying. Diplomatic proposal rejected? Leader died alert. Sometimes even construction queues finishing would give the leader dying alert sound. That one sound effect was  I always had to check and verify that a leader hadn't died constantly. I know voice acting is hard, and it isn't cheap, but is it too much to ask for unique alert sounds? For women to not sound like a cartoon mouse? Even the Klingon voice pack from my pre-order didn't make the Klingons on the diplomacy screen sound Klingon.Ship design and space combat are also severely lacking. Having every faction just use phasers is already a bit of a simplification. But if they're having the different weapon types be so limited, how come they didn't put in the effort to make the weapon effects look accurate to the show? Only spinal lance phasers are beams for some reason, and it's nearly impossible to distinguish a photon torpedo from a phaser array, since the phasers shoot little red-orange bursts instead of coherent orange beams. The worst part is, base Stellaris can make battles look more like Star Trek using just lasers and missiles, why weren't those effects used more? The weapon progression is similarly absurd, starting you from Enterprise era technology, 200 years after it would have gone into service in the timeline. I'm not normally one to nitpick on canon things, but it's really hard to take this game seriously when I don't even have torpedoes when the attack on Khitomer happens. So many weapon types have such low accuracy that it's just not worth using them.The Borg are nowhere near threatening. I don't know if it's just because I've played a lot of Stellaris, and the basic settings were just too easy or what, but I completely wiped the floor with the Borg. They didn't kill a single ship of mine during the crisis. I stopped them at the source. And based on the missions, it seems I was behind on tech. The missions seemed to expect me to have Sovereign class ships before the Borg arrived, I didn't even have Galaxy class ships yet. I have no clue how much I need to turn up the crisis difficulty to make the Borg challenging, but if the expectation is to have 15 Sovereign-class ships before they arrive, I don't think the slider goes high enough.The worst part of all of this is that the core gameplay concept isn't bad. There's clearly a good idea at the core of this game. But the game concept is so unsuited for the Stellaris engine. I knew this was a Stellaris reskin going in, they're certainly not shy about it, and I can understand why using a pre-existing game as the basis for this makes sense. But using Stellaris as the basis for a game set in a time frame of about 100 years at most is just bad use of the engine. Stellaris mods like New Horizons work by using the full 300 year length Stellaris is built on, and running you from around the launch of the NX-01 Enterprise, through to the events after Picard. At its core, Stellaris is built for those kinds of generation-spanning stories, and the way it implements researching tech and exploration and planetary development reflects that. Star Trek Infinite is not a generation-spanning story. It is set in one era of Star Trek, with tech that never develops beyond about 30 years from the start of the game, but to give the progression Stellaris relies on, it tries to squeeze the entire history of Star Trek technology into 30 years, on only TNG-era ships.Star Trek Infinite would be a better game if it was built like Birth of the Federation, on the framework of a more traditional 4X like Masters of Orion, or even Endless Space. Instead, we have a lackluster use of the Stellaris engine and gameplay, for a story that doesn't fit, and that warps the whole reality of Star Trek to make anything even almost work.If you're looking for a true Star Trek experience in the style of Stellaris, I unfortunately cannot recommend this game. Try out the existing mods for Stellaris instead, Star Trek: New Horizons (my personal recommendation), or the more streamlined Star Trek: New Civilizations. They're more worth your time, and somehow have better voice acting than this officially licensed game.

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek Infinite, stellaris's trek flavored kindred.rating 9/10first i will start this review by naming some of the current issues with the game that the devs have been informed of and are looking for fixes. ~there are some crash to desktop issues primarily involving firewall permissions, and MAC OS~DLC authentication issues that can cause some bugs~loading screen issues related to specific systems which the exact cause has not quite been pinned down. im starting the review with these because of the mixed reviews rating steam currently has listed for this game, to explain that these issues are painfully clear to the devs and have been reported ad infinitum in their discord server and they are currently working on patches to fix them ASAP. onto the actual review nowPros: ~a healthy balance of exploration, strategy, combat and planning. unlike infinite's big brother stellaris, infinite has a markedly higher focus on the logistics side of things, stellaris feels significantly faster because all of the mandatory content  of stellaris IE the primary gameplay loop of explore>colonise>conquer>explore repeating, is distributed into the new logistics systems. this game is not stellaris, it is not a clone with a trek costume on. it has unique mechanics that require additional attention and slow the overall march of the game down. you MUST focus on all fronts or you will fall behind~beautiful visuals and artwork~incredible attention to detail in how systems interact with each other which ends up rewarding careful planning in powerful ways~a basic but comprehensive tutorial to properly introduce a new player to all of the above systems~a nail on the head star trek theme. no expense was spared in detail or design making an overall authentic accurate star trek experience encompassing DS9 VOY and TNG star trek eras.cons:~the game could be considered very slow for some people, especially for people who like the more combat oriented feel of stellaris~infinite is not what i would call "easy", individual mechanics are sometimes simple and sometimes intricate but learning to balance and use them all continuously is taxing mentally and if you arent used to that level of depth or detail infinite will almost certainly run away from you occasionally and leave you reeling to correct some problemsi give infinite a 9/10. any "complaints" i have come down more to nitpicking than genuine criticism. the game fleshes out all of its mechanics, provides a lore accurate and friendly star trek experience mixed with the fundamentals of stellaris with its own evolution on the original concepts that create something entirely new. the devs are also incredibly responsive on all levels and immediately set out diagnosing day 1 launch issues. final verdict: if you dont mind some bugs and troubleshooting buy it now. its certainly worth the full price tag if my pros section interested you. if you would prefer to avoid bugs for now, give it a few days and watch the game in the store or your library. once the launch issues are ironed out infinite will be a masterpiece experience even for new players.

_childDocuments_.review: Consider this game as the starter box of Star Trek Ascendancy, with Cardassian expansion, if it was put into PC game format. Where the tabletop game does have replay-ability in how it is set up each game, this is where this game sadly lacks that variety. The devs, wanting to retell the TNG to VOY timeline, have made the galaxy a set piece, the board does not move or change, only what territories are snapped up by each of the other races though after a few games the AI can get predictable. Like many others have stated prior this game has the "potential" to become something greater, something more, if given the green light to get out, let's say, the Dominion as a playable but also end game crisis. This would affect all other races and add to their mission trees and what can and can't be done.However in its current form, from what I've played on a previous machine for a good 50+ hours that sadly aren't synced to my current steam account, the base game gets too samey after too many games, as I stated before the galaxy is a set board that doesn't change or alter all that much. Sadly I think, for a while, this game is being sidelined for something else as prior to release there really wasn't much in the way of gameplay footage or youtube previews, but plenty of previews for the pre-order/deluxe content that would be available. So I can only assume there's no credible news on further expansion on the game and we shouldn't have to rely on the modding community to upgrade and finish off the starter game.This does sound like a contradiction doesn't it? That I recommend it yet talk about it in a negative light. The game in its current state is good for someone wanting to play Stellaris BUT are overwhelmed with how complicated that game has become now with all its expansions, as this game's engine is Stellaris 3.0. Not too difficult to get the ideals of the 4x empire building down but also allows for bringing in more mechanics later on. The devs right now are playing their cards way too close to their chests with this game, like they did with previews, and as it stands, with some extra free or paid content thrown our way in the coming months, I could easily throw in a good 10+ hours a week for a decent thorough playthrough, maybe a multiplayer game too, but this won't happen. Buy this if you want a diet-Stellaris with a star trek theme, but do not buy it if you're looking for a Birth of the Federation 2. C'mon Devs, give us something for this game. There's obviously a lot of time, effort, artwork, and thought that's gone into this game wanting to recreate the TNG-timeline and beyond, but as it sits here it looks like a dead shelved game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Half-baked at best, frustrating and disappointing. I should have just played Stellaris instead of wasting $40.I have been looking forward to Star Trek: Infinite for months. I'm a big fan of Star Trek and other Paradox games. I start with that to say, I'm really bummed out by this game. Here's why:It's only vaguely Star Trek themed. It lacks any identifiable Star Trek music, not even in the launcher or during loading to get you hyped. The UI isn't LCARS or Cardassian or anything you associate with Star Trek, it's all just leftovers from Stellaris.But worse than that are the UI and help systems. They don't surface vital information on 90% of screens where it's relevant, instead you have to visit one screen, remember a piece of info and click over to another screen where you need that info, which closes the previous screen. It's incredibly cumbersome. God help you if you're making decisions based off more than one or two pieces of information at a time!The help systems beyond the limited tutorial is non-existent. You get through the first phase of tutorial and then there are friendly narrations on each menu screen explaining the purpose of that screen. Unfortunately, those narrations only provide a high-level overview, when what you really need to figure out this game is detailed descriptions of each game mechanic and the terminology. Many complex games (even Paradox's own games) give you tooltip pop-ups when you hover over key terms. No such luck here. Most games at least have a glossary or central help hub where you can go to read about various terms, mechanics and concepts. Again, not here! Ominous alerts will pop up claiming that something bad has happened in your empire. There's no indication as to what consequences that might have or what mechanic of the game it relates to, just a simple button that says "OK". It's one of the most miserable learning curves I've experienced in a game, simply because there's nowhere to turn for information.It seems buggy. I keep getting false alarms about losing people important to the empire, but I've lost no one. Some buttons don't work when they seem like they should and, thanks to the poor communication from the UI, I'm unsure if it's because I don't meet the requirements or a bug. I have missions in my log that seem to have objectives, but no buttons available to complete them, like some other missions do. The good news is I haven't run into anything game-breaking, but that might only be because I've played a few decades of in-game time.There are other complaints but those are the big ones and you already get the idea. I would recommend putting your $30 or $40 into a high-interest savings account and letting it grow to $70 so you'll have the cash for when some other company takes a real run at making a grand strategy Star Trek game, rather than a half-assed reskin of their existing game.

Even getting around the fact that the federation has canonically have many more ship designs, you could work around it by using the alternative design feature that Stellaris has had for ages to change the flavor of ships the other factions have, this is not a new problem, and it was fixed by mods and even Stellaris has fixed it. The pacing of the game is rather poor and unless RNG is in your favor, your mission tree is pretty much locked behind it. Speaking of which. Why is Denobola and risa uncolonized? These are major planets in the Federation... There is so much wrong with this game, that more time and forethought could have went into it. _childDocuments_.review: In a word: Disappointment.This game feels at it's core like a cash grab -- Stellaris with a focus on Star Trek? Sounds great! The issue is the scale of it is very... empty. The Mission trees sort of feel less like they're giving you options for historical/ahistorical Trekky fun, and more like they're just a veiled tutorial guide for what direction your focus should be, such as Klingons starting with the task of literally just making two space fleets and an army, then giving them a leader each, and beefing up your overall fleet power to an arbitrary number -- after which it goes on to very similar tasks, all of which are effectively leaning toward 'make big fleet/army' with minimal effect and equally minimal effort. After playing about halfway through Klingons (most of which I spent fighting my terrible economy), then about halfway through Cardassians, I got bored. _childDocuments_.review: Caveats:1. I have Stellaris and much of the DLC2. I have not played the existing Star Trek Mods which are freely available and highly toted by others3. I have picked this up on the pre-order and played through to just shy of the 2hr limit as I contemplate a refund. Star Trek: Infinite is based on the Stellaris UI/Clausewitz engine. It behaves and feels much akin to Stellaris. The downsides to this, and granting this is a new game, is that it feels like Stellaris after they removed some FTL options and before they got some actual polish updates into the overall system.The interactions, Star Trek shell notwithstanding, feel VERY sterile and underdeveloped when compared to Stellaris (again DLCs and longer development history notwithstanding -- this is comparing to other historical iterations of Stellaris).There is currently only a single stock medium map -- with systems/empires placed at incorrect locations relative to cannon. There are Governor ships instead of just using a Governor in systems (why this is a thing vs. how other leaders operate (both within Star Trek: Infinie and when compared to regular Stellaris)  I cannot fathom). A planetary/system Governor should simply be assigned to a planet/system -- having them fly around on ships relative to a science vessel akin to their anomaly missions to trouble shoot the empire is certainly not intuitive and seems illogical (relative to how other leaders operate/are assigned and relative to Stellaris proper).No racial customisation also "feels odd". Yes it is Star Trek: Infinite but it's not very infinite if you can only play as one of 4 major Star Trek empires and must be shoe-horned into certain behavioral traits 100% of the time.I had hoped that Star Trek: Infinite would be a "rebirth" of Birth of the Federation (one of my favourite 4x games - Star Trek notwithstanding). However, even Birth of the Federation BOTF (released ~1999) at release had 5 major factions (they also included the Ferengi Trade Union) vs. Star Trek: Infinite starting with only 4.BOTF did lock you into certain ships, traits etc. but it still feels more polished and intuitive. Star Trek: Infinite currently lacks either the raft of options available in Stellaris or the polish and nostalgia of BOTF.I remain very disappointed with this title/launch. The overall vibe being the taking of a much loved IP and a relatively popular and successful back-end (Stellaris/Clausewitz) and smashing them together with the least amount of input possible (I am not saying that is what was done, I am saying that is how the product feels/behaves after 1.8hrs of playtime).Will this improve over time -- very likely in the short term.Will this have continued publisher/developer support -- debatable given the clear competition vs. Stellaris proper and the lacklustre state at launch. I'll be holding out to see developer responses over the balance of the refund grace period -- without going over the 2hr limit to try to gauge how this may improve, however, for anyone who does not already have Star Trek: Infinite in their library, this is NOT a buy -- wait to see how things develop and/or wait for a substantive (minimum 30%) sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This review will be a bit atypical for me, it will be rather short and mostly a summary.Total Score: 4/10It's a barebone representation of the Star Trek IP with some nice little nods to the stories and events, however unless someone plays this game for the flair and looks for a rather tame challenge with lots of bugs and exploits left behind, it's a no go. The events are further reskinned for all factions and only a handful of them have unique choices for the faction... or rather the text for the choice is different (implying it is the RP choice to make).There are mods for Stellaris, they are much better and they cost nothing. This game allows people with old PCs to play a bit of "Stellaris Lite" which is one redeeming quality I guess. It is playable from start to finish with all achievements in working order - sadly not self-evident in all Paradox games (Imperator). That is another reason why this is a working game.The AI is atrocious, can't handle their own planets and ruins the endgame (Coup wars need the target to be stable to coup and overcrowded unemployed planets of minors lategame make this impossible), and will lose 9/10 wars due to sheer incompetence.Even on higher difficulty most people will outtech and outgun the AI which is unable to build proper ships. The Romulan ships which are supposed to be terrifying in lore are a joke ingame. They got balanced with very low HP and huge weapon slots early game... when no weapons aside of Phaser for them exist and the meta is S/M mines and cutter beams. They get ransacked in every run by Klingons and Cardassians... unbelievable.Exploits like the "eternal" puppet state spy extraction for example allow a Romulus player to get 2000 ore, alloy, energy + 150 Influence per vassal per year for NOT assimilating it. That's more broken than the easy low difficulty smear campaign influence farm of spies. Romulans also "clone" 1 pop out of thin air with each successful spy mission. In a weird horrid way, in a players hands the weak ships are the only thing balancing this broken faction. A gift the AI is unable to work with at all.The AI is mostly an "artificial insult" to GSG veterans. Completionists can get their fill here, people that like some shallow Trek IP can get their fill here, people that can't normally support Stellaris with their CPU can get their fill here.For everyone else, this is a cash grab and Paradox seems unwilling to renew the contract with the studio to expand on this commercial failure. There is little hope in the community that this game doesn't get axed.O7 commanders, pay respect, fly safe and let it crash.

Occasionally it will shoot photon torpedoes but they don't work against shields so... There is a lot more I could list here but I'm not trying to completely nitpick this game.  My suggestion is to skip it, or at least keep an eye on it to see if it gets some much needed updates. _childDocuments_.review: Grand Strategy will start to take hold in every major genre brand in the future from Star Wars to Babylon 5, but for now Nimble Giant E, takes its shot at the classic brand Star Trek, with Paradox's classic backing. Took a fast look at what I liked, and what I did not.What I enjoyed:Stellaris: Using the same UI presentation, this navigates very similar to Stellaris and that may not be a bad thing if you enjoy that kind of UI game play. Presentation; If you love Star Trek, then this will be a game you may get into. Icons, Music, Aesthetics, Characters, Models, and sounds.Micro Managing: Following a story mode and mission sequence, you will manage everything from ships to officers, planets. as it takes small segments of other games and places them in this one.Expandable: The base game is just that, a base game confined to 4 factions, but this will be a DLC expanding picnic. Camera: Easy camera movementsLearning Curve: icons everywhere, but easy navigation once you know where everything is.Visuals: Wonderful cut shots and graphics give you the feel of the genre it honors.What I think needs improvingFragmented: A lot of ideas that don't quite execute the way the game wishes. Officers that you assign, but have no true uniqueness. Things too automated, and like Endless Space, upgrading ships you never see.Story: Is in the dynamic teasers, but in game its just point and click. You never feel like you are part of the movie. Galaxy Far Far Away: What is the point of doing all this wonderful modeling and effects if you play the game at a vast distance. There is a reason Third Person works. Terrible decision.Speed Up: Some gaps of waiting for things to happen that even speed-ed up, can make you wish you went to the distance. BOTF: Though not truly Birth of the Federation, an old turn based game that had a more speed up game play of move and effect. The end development of this game maybe a mutated complex version of that one.Faction Rigid: For a game that wants you to control the destinies of these faction, you are restricted to their events and stories. Defined roles. No Minors: No minor faction game play for now. Combat: Could be more creativeFinal initial take: Grand strategies are very complex and time consuming and I am not sure there is enough here to keep players invested long term. It will all come down to what this game looks like a year from now when patches and future dlcs extend the content and alter what does not work. Star Trek Infinite is truly for Star Trek fans, but those who are grand strategy lovers may find it unpolished and fragmented. I give it a positive review for the hard work these developers do in making these games a reality. It will be interesting to see what this game looks like after a year. See the video game play above discussion to see if this game is for you. My initial score 3.0 out of 5

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek: Infinite may have started as a Star Trek themed Stellaris mod but it grew to become a full fledged game on its own. While most of its 4X mechanics (exploration, warfare, planet admin, research) are built on the Stellaris vanilla experience and easily recognisable by Stellaris players, ST:I sports many additions and reworks that feel both thematically and mechanically appropriate: mission trees, galactic tension, faction specific event chains, more nuanced spy game, faction UIs are the most immediately evident.Aside from a few bugs, mostly fixed in the days following launch, I think this is all in all a great experience both for Stellaris players looking for a more flavoured and railroaded game and trekkies looking for a solid strategy game.Looking forward for prolonged support and expansions + reworks.UPDATE Mar 2024: Game is quickly reaching abandonware status, keep that in mind when you consider buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid Star Trek strategy game. I had been missing something like this since the legendary Birth of the Federation became unplayable. ST: Infinite had launched with a few rough edges and stability issues, but the development team is engaged and active and have addressed the most important of these.The 4 "factions" to choose from (The Federation, Romulan Star Empire, Klingon Empire, Cardassian Union) play differently enough in the early and mid game to make for a distinct experience which is enjoyable. The late game is a little less distinct as the balance of power gets lopsided and overwhelming brute military power can resolve most challenges. It is very playable as of the date of this review, gives a Star Trek feeling strategy game to those who have wanting just such a thing, and it is improving as the developers continue to work on it.The developers are coy on the question of additional content and won't comment on DLC but I'm hopeful that substantial changes are still to come. Either refining and enriching the experience of the 4 factions or adding playable factions or both. So, ST: Infinite is solidly playable as it is, and fingers crossed for more content.Note: For people not approaching this with a Stellaris background the game mechanics can be daunting and may be a turn off. I know I had a hard time with it until I looked up some videos of playing guides and a few reddit threads, which allowed me to make sense of things, improving my experience greatly.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: It seems like the future of Star Trek: Infinite is looking bleak. AFAIK the Devs have sadly already been laid off... so this will slowy fade into obscurity...  I still leave my positive review up because I did have my fun in the 32 hours or such. But I also totally understand all the complaints etc. the community and real Star Trek Fans have (I myself just know Star Trek but I'm not really a true fan in that sense) and I stand behind them. Sadly this game will now just go under and there won't be any updates or new content.... They really had a good shot here but yeah.. Paradox in recent years is disappointing more and more and I don't think the future will be better with/for them.If you were always unsure about trying Stellaris because of it's complexity then Star Trek: Infinite is a really good entry for it. It's a smaller scale and you can learn a bit easier and don't get as overwhelmed as with Stellaris. It also might helpt that it's set in the Star Trek universe so some people might even have a better connection with the game. I tell you first what I don't like. I also would've rated this game "Medium" instead of I recommend it or not. It's almost 2024: - change resolution; restart the game- change Fullscreen to windowed(?); restart the game- change gui scaling; restart the game- GUI scaling doesn't just use a vector file that "gets bigger" but it kinda zooms in (like in stellaris) and makes the UI look choppy, pixelated edges and low quality (that's 2015 era problem, or earlier)- The introduction tutorial sometimes skips a text/voice in the middle of it- The introduction feels awfully similar to the one of stellaris.- as many have said, it feels like a mod to stellaris; I do hope that they will add DLCs and Updates that make this game stand out more and can be called a real standalone game. - i can not play in true "windowed" fashion - it's still fullscreen but just without borders... it's like borderless window and windowed make no difference... I want to play the game in a 1920x1080 res window on my 3440x1440 monitor, but I guess that's not possible in the 2023 (somehow, miraculously this started working after starting the game again for the third time or something..)- ah cmon! Why is the ironmade mode setting hidden in the campaign settings screen? I didn't even bother checking it out at first because I wanted to go straight for ironman and only just now noticed that you have to enable it there first. Why? Why isn't it immediately visible that it is disabled or enabled... played through the whole night and wondered where the achievements where and thought it's a bug... welp - restarting the campaign for th third time nowWhat I like: - it isn't as complex as Stellaris (complexity is nice, but sometimes I just want to "relax" and a less complex game can be nice too)- I like the themed art-style etc. of Star Trek and how you can have a "true" Star Trek space game here- I really like the models of the ships and Starbases they look really well (they looked worse in some trailer I saw so I was worried a bit - for example I don't like zooming in to look at the ships in Stellaris because they look so weird)- Mission tree so you can follow a path and don't feel like you don't have a goal; it's mostly about making your own story, your own adventure, do what you want - but I somtimes feel lost because of that and I like that I can at least follow something, something to achieve and follow a goal. I hope there'll be more mission trees coming etc. - I like the Events as of now- the events are really cool and fun and everytime I start playing I end up staying awake the whole night...
