_childDocuments_.review: After much thought and deliberation, I believe Star Trek: Infinite deserves a 9.5/10. Although not without its flaws (somewhat clunky war system, poor documentation, etc.), I have had a great experience with the game after 17 hours. The gameplay is very engaging and I have been delighted by my playthroughs so far.Frankly, I'm as shocked as you are. Given Paradox's poor showings in recent years, I had no faith that this game would be any good at all. Joking aside, the development team should be commended on their ambitious take on the 4x genre. They made a great choice to focus on the TNG-era. We all love TNG and it avoids a lot of the cringe of more recent Star Trek media (ST: Picard, Discovery, etc.). The art direction is wonderful and respects the work others have done, while appropriating it into the Stellaris formula. The playing the warlike Klingons feel very much like Klingons, the ruthless Cardassians feel like Cardassians, and so on. I especially enjoy the influence and officer mechanics. The AI is a challenge without becoming overbearing. These are essential aspects to the game that make it worth my time.Is it what I wanted?I wanted Birth of the Federation 2. I knew I wouldn't get that, but I am convinced this is the next best thing. Infinite is a brilliant Star Trek experience from a group that loves the franchise. It is more than worth the cost of admission. Given a robust patching schedule and reasonable DLC (Dominion, please), I think it will become *the* go to Star Trek game for years to come.Kudos to the devs and Qapla'!

If you own no other space strategy game and you want a Star Trek game like that, then this is good and much better than the highly overrated BOTF. If you own Stellaris and play Star Trek New Civilizations mod that is basically the design of this game. Not overly complex like New Horizons, runs well, generally good gameplay dynamics. However this thing does things that a Stellaris mod can't do. Such as how ships travel is much more like Star Trek and how agents are used is more fun IMO than Stellaris. The bespoke events and things like that are not much of an upgrade, especially not over Star Trek New Civilizations mod for Stellaris. STNC is a much more complete Star Trek experience even considering that you have hyperspace lanes instead of warp and all that. The main thing with this game is I hope development continues because there is a lot of potential here, especially with mods. I think this is overall a good game and i'd recommend to buy it simply to make sure development continues, this will probably be the future focus of Star Trek modders.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently I cannot recommend this game as there is so many issues.1) Gameplay: It feels "empty". We have some Minors, the most I don't know from Star Trek (ST) btw. They are just there, but I don't see how they contribute to e. g. the Federation like with an unique ability. They don't have any unique traits or whatsoever. Assimilate them, repeat. That's it. The other Majors are even worse. In my last game Klingons were calm, Romulans were calm, Cardassians were calm. As for Federation, the gameplay is sooo boring. Only here and there pirates are attacking and somehow the BORG, but that's it.2) Science:A complete mess. If you are playing Federation at least you can research things (too many things). But a major issue is the complete randomness of junk inventions. Why do we have weapons never seen in ST? Why do we have 10+ different weapon systems? Complete useless. In my last game shortly before 2400 (end of game) I finally could research the solar panels for star bases? Why not earlier? This doesn't make sense at all. You have to research photon torpedoes. Not mark VII or so, the basics ones. While I like that scientists have some research traits, it is annoying to switch them acc. to what is currently researched for the bonuses.3) MapI know that only alpha and beta quadrant are covered, but it is still a complete useless non-ST map at all. In addition, there is a certain amount of anomalies you can discover. So after a certain point in time there is no benefit to uncover every star system at all. The random factor of resources is annoying. Sometimes you have only one system with Dilithium. The other rares are...super rare.4) EnterpriseWhat exactly is now the purpose of the Enterprise D (and if you are lucky E)? It is a science ship, ok, and can make some buum buum. But that's it. The missions are ridiculous. Some are super easy, but finding three fights is more a challenge. You can't even put some other ships to the Enterprise, so it is highly dependent of a proper fleet IF someone is attacking. No "real" missions available, sad.5) EventsWhich events? In the ST New Horizons mod at least you have a bunch of events, but here - NOTHING. Ok, you have this stupid Romulan star system sh1tty thing (I hate this Kelvin? timeline), but even after - nothing happens. It doesn't matter at all. Bajor? If you don't attack Cardassia, they will assimilate it - no prophets, no worm hole. So empty, so boring.6) IntelligenceWhat is the purpose of that? You spend sometimes 10 years with a certain mission, but then, booom mf, you mission failed. Hahaha.7) ShipsWe are starting with something like "Miranda" (lol), and then, due to the crappy science system, maybe you can research for Intrepid, Excelsior (!), or Defiant (which is crappy to the power of 10). Yes, in STNH we had too much, granted, too many versions of subversions, but at least some kind of logic and canon. Here, we have developers not knowing what was there in the 24th century.Taken together: It seems like this is a premature version of what could be possible. On the one hand it is not as complicated as STNH, but on the other hand it is too "empty" to have fun. Also, in my opinion the Devs started as ST fans, but then the team switched and now we have Devs who don't know anything about ST. Shame on you. And Paradox: if you have plans to bring out 1000 DLCs to make it playable: GFY.

_childDocuments_.review: Too many bugs and bizarre creative decisions have made this pretty disappointing overall.The bugs are everywhere, from flavour text missing in pop ups to buttons that inexplicably do nothing. There are developer notes showing instead of in game text and empire names missing from situation reports.I can overlook these as paradox tends to work these out. What I can't overlook are the choices made by the game's designers...You get access to a tiny roster of ships and (for the Feds at least) the order that these ships are trickled in just makes no sense. You start with the Miranda, an old ship. The next ship you unlock is the Intrepid, a very new ship. Then you unlock the Excelsior... A ship almost as old as the Miranda. Really? A game designed by fans, for fans? That's utter nonsense. You can unlock the Enterprise D fairly early on but it's the only Galaxy Class you get access to for a huge chunk of the game, if at all! The frequency that a new class of ship becomes available is so slow, it makes fleet management pretty boring. I've finally managed the right research to unlock the Excelsior class... In 2390! That's like a century later than in the shows. I unlocked the Enterprise D decades earlier so have a Galaxy Class flying around decades before a ship that came out in Kirk's time!Minor races are a mixed bag with their portraits with some being very generic and some having unique ones, but they all play the same in game. The major powers are flat out boring and far too friendly. There's no intrigue and cold war taking place, everyone is friendly. I've seen 1 very brief war between the Romulans and Klingons, where nothing really happened.Such a wasted opportunity. It needs more ships with realistic release dates. It needs some character with the minor and major races. The vaunted mission tree is actually very limited with only 1 real decision to make for the federation (peaceful Vs warlike) and even then is not really that in depth.This needs some real work. It just feels very unfinished from a design and polish perspective.Now it's been completely abandoned which should be treated as fraud. The game's unfinished, people have paid money for it and they're not going to bother finishing it. At least offer us all refunds to make this right!

_childDocuments_.review: I've had an absolute blast with the game so far. The artwork is stunningly beautiful, from still images and the soundtrack to the ship models and stations. The events throughout the game are engaging and pure joy for existing Trek fans (speak up Wesley!), and the minor changes they've made to fit better with the Trek universe doesn't go unnoticed - trained officers being a tangible resource is a particular favourite of mine.While heavily compared to the Trek mods for Stellaris in terms of variety and price, comparing Infinite to existing Star Trek games such as the Armada series shows a clear progression in official Trek content and finally brings Trek strategy back into modern gaming without relying on fanmade mods.My only qualm with the game is the small selection of ship classes. It makes total sense that they have so few - while the Federation have a plethora of designs to pull from, for every class you introduce to one faction you have to substitute it into 3 more factions with their own designs. And while they've done an excellent job of giving us iconic designs that make sense for the time period, it still leaves a bit to be desired. Even just small craft such as shuttles and other hangar craft would make a nice addition to flesh the game out.Overall, a great experience as a Trek fan and I'm looking forward to any future expansions that we may? receive. (Borg DLC? Please? Pretty please???)

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Stellaris about 40 minutes. I've played this game for 80 HOURS. Here is why...I KNOW THIS LORE. I've watched all the TNG, DS9 and Voyager multiple times (like a familiar album). So yes, essentially this game is fan service.  MY TL;DR  is as follows...If you play strategy games and love 90's Star Trek this game is a  MUST OWN and might actually be the best Star Trek game ever made regardless of era. If you dumped a ton of money into Stellaris and don't care about the lore, don't buy this game, it wants to be what you already have and will seem inferior. If you like JJ Abrams Star Trek play Starfield.Game mechanics:  (from what I can tell are like Stellaris...just read every other review?)Took me at least the tutorial and an abandoned play-thru to get used the mechanics. I'm a 24+ years Civilization II - VI vet;  Firaxis still holding my strategy heart with the XCOM franchise, CIVs and also still Alpha Centauri that i play via GOG.  Since this game can be paused at anytime, strategies can be set up as you wish while you micro-manage your empire and it's not turn based but you can get it very slow. There are only 4 starting faction choices  (which kinda took me back back to the old Warcraft III days for me (Undead, Human, Orc, Elves)...each one having a distinct yet familiar play-style. Since there are a multitude of NPC factions that can be controlled, integrated, or destroyed AND every faction besides starting factions, Bajorans and Betazoids are random in terms of placement each time I've played, there is some def rplay value here.The mechanics are def playable, but a bit clunky. and you kinda gotta grind out to figure out, per empire, the best way to distribute, increase, control and establish your agendas. Since each starting point has a combination of static elements with random starting resources, elements, planets etc, it allows for a same-faction-play with different outcomes / preparedness / and adaptability for the scripted encounters.I'm not really sure how the sound effects are and the soundtrack is since I turned them off so I can binge-watch episodes of the series represented in the game on a second monitor while I play. The graphics are like nothing crazy... I'm running a 4070 RTX GPU with a i7 12700 intel CPU so I'm having zero issues running this graphically but checks your specs first i guess. Seems like they made a game that many systems can handle. This game is really my type of fan service. I'm a 90's Star Trek fan and this is hitting the spot. It's not perfect: it does have the feeling of play-testing (i've submitted at least 5 crashes as of couple weeks of playing) but i feel if the bugs and some game clunky mechanics issues are worked out, it will be a high watermark for the Star Trek franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm confused about the reason for this new Star Trek game's existence. We already had a fantastic total conversion mod for Stellaris called Star Trek: New Horizons. It offered a deep and engaging Star Trek experience with unique events, mechanics, playable races, and a challenging gameplay loop.This new game, however, feels more like a modern version of the classic Birth of the Federation. It lacks the variety of playable races and complex mechanics found in New Horizons. There's also minimal story unless you specifically choose the Federation faction.In its current state, I wouldn't recommend this game. While future updates and potentially expensive DLC packs might improve it,  it's unlikely to reach the level of depth and polish achieved by the free Star Trek: New Horizons mod for Stellaris.

_childDocuments_.review: Most CRAPTASTIC "Star Trek" game that I have ever played. No Player's Manual is complete BS. (No wiki either) Having to put a governor in orbit of a new colony for TEN FRACKING YEARS to complete an inauguration ceremony is complete BS. Waging war against an enemy empire for several years while obliterating 80% of their territory only to have the war suddenly end and you get ZERO territory for your efforts because you did not click a magic button on some magic sub menu before the war started is complete BS. (Casus Belli is complete BS. The victor makes the rules. ALWAYS.)Enemy ships that escape at the last second is complete BS.  Somehow massive structural damage never disables the navigation or warp drive systems.The entire colony building and district allocation system is complete BS. You need food so you create agricultural zones but NO they would rather starve to death than farm because they were trained for white color work, not blue color work.I love Star Trek. I love 4x strategy games. I HATE this game and most likely so you will too. Far too many HIDDEN RULES that are not explained by the cursory tutorial and they cannot be bothered to publish a game rulebook.You won't know how bad this game gets until it is too late to refund it so . . . just don't buy it. You will  probably be happier that way. I know I would be.Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: Stellaris with a Star Trek skin, and some bugs.  I've been thwarted on the Borg storyline twice because the mission spawned beyond my warp range. Then they overran me 20 hours into the game because I didn't complete the earlier missions, and because they went beserk before I had adequate fleet size. I finally was able to defeat them once and for all, then the game froze when too many popups happened at once (my biggest complaint about Infinite and Stellaris). That requiried a PC reset. I mean, why torture yourself? It might be a good game eventually, but right now it's frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: I never really played Stellaris. The number of resources to manage was intimidating, the sheer number of stuff to do (as typical for Paradox games) was overwhelming, but since this was Star Trek I had to give it a try. And even with what little I've played either title (and I've since fired up the ST: New Horizons mod for Stellaris), it's clearly true what they say. The mod has way more. More races, more quadrants, more complete overhaul (like all the resources have faction-specific names, different UIs for each major faction, Star Trek soundtracks through mods, etc). Really the only good thing they've done here is some of the events and artwork. It's in the most alpha of alpha states and now that's how it will stay since it's  it's dead. This was after just 7 patches and 13 hot fixes made over the course of one week shy of two months after release, with the last on 12/5/23. That's right, this game got just 7 weeks of support before being killed.It's flabbergasting to me how little was done here. Things like faction-specific UI and more complete renaming of things from Stellaris would have been pretty cheap to do. Clearly a project that was in trouble for some time. I never really liked Paradox since they DLCd you to death with about every title. But this experience really proves to me that I really, really should stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: In its current state ST: Infinite gets a thumbs down from me. It tries to distinguish itself from Stellaris, which is the framework this stand-alone DLC is based on, and I call it deliberately a Stellaris DLC, as that is what it actually is, but in the end it fails in many areas. 1. The framework ST:Infinite is based on is an older version of Stellaris. Many years of Stellaris improvements are missing and painfully absent, especially quality of life elements. 2. ST:Infinite tries to distinguish itself successfully in some areas from Stellaris, but unfortunately in many areas this adaptation feels forced, just for the sake of being different from Stellaris and by doing so, it gets worse or feels clunky and not thought through enough. 3. This came up in many discussions/reviews before me and people won't like to hear it, but the fan made Star Trek conversion mod: "New Horizons" is in my opinion far superior to ST:Infinite. Horizon might lack on the graphical design side, but when it comes to depth and fun factor, it beats ST:Infinite by miles. So you have a mod out there that does the Star Trek conversion far better than a paid stand alone version, which is actually painful to see. 4. ST:Infinite has a lot of bugs and issues at point of release, to a point where it is not really enjoyable,5. I was hoping for a game that tries to innovate and feel more like a spiritual successor of "Birth of the Federation" and "Star Trek Armada", which the devs themselves said they wanted to aspire to. But there is nothing that reminds me of the good old games like Birth of The Federation or Star Trek Armada. It falls short on all fronts.

_childDocuments_.review: Having waited for the successor to 'Birth of the Federation' for 20+ years, I'm happy Star Trek: infinite has arrived. It certainly does scratch that itch for me.I was never able to get into stellaris, as it was overwhelming with the decade of development and expansion packs. It was just too complicated.'Infinite' makes things a lot easier with some systems completely dumped from stellaris, as it wouldn't make sense in the star trek universe. Along with my passion for all things Star Trek, this made my life easier to get into the game. Further quality of life stuff like handing planet micromanagement to the computer (once you've selected the planet's speciality), reduced the stress of managing the empire, less tedious for me.All this helps me enjoy the story of the game and the in-game events. It's fantastic to carve out your own little episodes of star trek, while trying to conquer (peacefully of course :P ) the galaxy.I'm running this game on a geforce 1050 (2gb) video card at 1440p, and it runs just fine (75fps on galaxy map) ...  but we'll see if it chugs at end game chaos.It's a great game for its price. I hope it is successful, as I would love to see other empire's in the game, like: 'The dominion', krenim imperium, Breen confederacy and Orion syndicateI haven't had any crashes, and if there have been bugs, i wasn't paying attention.See you all out there, in the stars :)

_childDocuments_.review: This one is really hard...  It's...  alright...I was excited for this game when I first heard the announcement for this game.  Star Trek themed Stellaris?  Sign me up.But this is where is kind of hard.  Stellaris is a great game and Star Trek Infinite is built off of it.  The core gameplay is the same game you have probably played before - not much has changed.  I was hoping that Nimble Giant were going to diversify the factions a bit more, however what you get is basically a slightly dressed up custom empire from Stellaris with some mission flavor built in and a custom EU4 style mission tree for each faction.I can see you liking this game if you are a hardcore Star Trek fan.  Even then, the game will only meet you halfway.  Yes, there are Ferengi, Bolians, and Nausicaans in the galaxy, but there are many more major species that are no where to be found.  And while I understand that the game probably wouldn't be able to fit all the vast species of the Star Trek universe, some omissions seem very glaring.  No Remans?  No Orions?  No Gorn?Most of the issues will probably be fixed with patches and dlc, but what is here is good - just not better than Stellaris if you already own that.  I mean, this isn't going to flip your skirt up.However, the artwork and design looks amazing.TL;DR - It's basically Stellaris 1.5 with a little bit of Star Trek.  And I really need to stop pre-ordering games.

_childDocuments_.review: Concept is cool, how it plays is pretty good...  but the bugs ruin it- Steam Deck can't get past the race selection screen, because that screen blanks at low resolution (workaround by messing with UI scaling)- "The federation has lost a true hero", plays every few minutes... Its annoying because it's false alarm 95% of the time.- Android Data died at 84 years old doing research, someone forgot to plug him in overnight- The Enterprise is broken/immobile in combat, 3 battles it has:    1) sat outside it's own firing range and just taken damage without moving    2) parked itself ontop of the borg cube (maybe taking friendly fire)    3) had to retreat 2 of 3 times because it sits unmoving at point blank range- Jean Luc died- Every minor power greets you and then gives you cause to go to war with them even if you give them a money gift (why??)- Redemption mission is broken for me, maybe because I started research with less time left than the research was expected to take- Clicking on one ship at a time bumps the other ship out of orbit with the cube, have to go up to galaxy map select 3 fleets and then move them to the cube... - There's more stuff, but these are just the ones off the top of my head.Bottom line: way too buggy, wait a few months for it to get patched and go on sale, then buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been holding off making this for awhile, guess there's no time like the present. Star Trek Infinite is a decent game, Nimble Giant is trying its best to make it better and modders are adding mods to make the game even better. The mission tree still needs a little work but at least it presents a challenge, Currently you can play one of four major factions in the Alpha and Beta Quadrants: United Federation of Planets, Klingon Empire, Romulan Star Empire and Cardassian Union.At present the UFP has the bigger mission tree with a story arc that has you make a serious choice, you can either stay true to the Federation's ideals and free Bajor or you can empore Section 31. Romulans are the best at espionage, Klingons are of course war-like because their philosophy is based on honor in battle. The Cardassians believe in military control and subjugation, all four factions are interesting to play and each gives a different perspective on overall gameplay.A current minor issue is of course the time-gating of ship tech but devs are working on it, 100+ years to unlock the Sovereign Class does seem a bit much but I'm still having fun with the game overall. I do recommend this game to Star Trek fans, please give it a chance and enjoy the TNG era of the game's timeline. Have fun with friends in the multiplayer and swap ideas on management and economics as well as fleet control and strategy. It's fun playing by yourself but better with friends.Live Long and Prosper

_childDocuments_.review: The Good: This is a glorified Stellaris re-skin with a slight stream-lining on a few mechanics. If you are into 4X games and you always wanted to play with a star trek skin, this is for you.The Bad: This is a glorified Stellaris re-skin... with that there is limits on how lore-accurate this can be, thus while its wearing the skin and feels like a familiar, its alignment with star trek fades quickly below surface levelThe Ugly:1) The war system is completely broken, you can out right dominate your opponent, kill all their fleets, take most of their planets, with no victories to their side, and still have the war end with you being the loser - and after the war everything you occupied is gone again.2) the "logistics warp range" mechanic is not only applied in a rather nonsensical manner, it also breaks your chances in endgame content.3) some things haven't been translated from Stellaris to Star Trek (for example the shipyard you need for your largest ships keeps saying it needs to be build on a citadel - a station type from stellaris that doesn't exist in star trek.4) for some reason a lot of dialogs had the wrong sound played when they opened.The Conclusion:it can be a fun game to play, but is currently dealing with a few issues that can also make it a bit annoying - I'm sure they will patch those out eventually, and for the price the game is a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a real shame that I have to not recommend this game, but given there are some really good Star Trek mods already out for Stellaris, this feels like a major downgrade for a paid title. The gameplay is what you'd expect from Stellaris, in fact, it's almost 1:1 to it, and what's worse it's a super old build of Stellaris without some of the great updates that have happened (i.e. having a ruling council, needing a scientist to lead each branch of research, construction ships not able to auto-construct) That said, where you'd expect this game to really shine - the Star Trek lore - is really poorly implemented. Here's just a few examples of the immersion breaking gameplay:-You'll get the opportunity to build the Enterprise-D, but Will Riker will exist as a separate "admiral" level character that can't be assigned to the Enterprise-Captain Ben Sisko appears but without the Defiant-Janeway can return, but will be commanding a generic, random science vessel "The Fearless" instead of Voyager. -Data can be recruited but is a generic SCIENTIST slot character, who also can't be assigned to the Enterprise-Spock makes an appearance, but not as an Envoy They really clearly just rushed the development of this game and didn't take time to truly create a Star Trek game, but instead, reskin as quickly as possible old Stellaris and its event mechanics. Instead of overhauling the ship system and having hero ships that have multiple officer slots, to recreate that feel of crews like the Enterprise, they just cobbled things together. What's more, you start with Miranda-class vessels and then will randomly get further patterns via research instead of having a tree to follow to unlock later, less anachronistic designs, unlike both ST mods for Stellaris where you get ship patterns based on the stardate.TL:DR: It will wow you if you're a Trekkie for about 30 minutes and if you already own Stellaris isn't really that much of a change to warrant spending money on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is effectively dead, and is still a buggy mess currently. Unfortunate, because this game actually got rid of a lot of the bloat that Stellaris had from years of DLC, and some of the new mechanics like the warp range were better. Not launching with scaling difficulty was a mistake. Without it, the harder difficulties just becoming surviving the first 30 years with min maxing, at which point it becomes impossible for you to lose because the AI can't keep up. With the scaling you can set it up so that the AI is strong enough to contend later, without having to use the same build all of the time. It's pretty clear that they were going to try to add a bunch of factions in as DLC later to keep the money train going, but they forgot that you actually need players to do that.

_childDocuments_.review: When I got this game, I went in expecting to be a little disappointed by what I found.There are some issues that I ran into. Day 1, there were UI scaling issues (I have my main display set to 150%) but that was easily fixed (but this could have been fixed). There are some notifications which don't make sense (like the Cardassian Union assimilating itself, apparently). The leader for the Trill Assembly has seemingly gone on vacation in my game. But none of this actually stopped me from playing the game.You play one of four galactic empires from Star Trek. Note that while it may help to complete goals in the Mission Tree, this isn't required for victory. A lot of the things you need to win come from researching technology in three areas - Physics, Society and Engineering. You don't progress along a tech tree, instead the game will give you several random choices of things to research.It can be a bit of a research roulette, but I found that if I stacked up research bonuses and made sure my empire was generating lots of beakers, I was able to progress quickly enough to eventually get the technologies I wanted. For a while there, I was trucking along with the Tier 1 reactor on my ships (one step above the starting reactor) which didn't let me power a lot of things, especially on the starting ship class.Speaking about stuff you can add to your ships, there are a few things which bug me, like how small quantum torpedoes need tetryons to build but medium and large don't. There also isn't a massive difference in damage done between small and medium torpedoes, but that isn't a big deal.You also need to manage the rest of your empire too. The populations (pops) of your colonies have needs, and you also need them to make resources for your empire. One of the mistakes I made early on was not adding enough mining and energy districts.Speaking of districts, if you feel like you made a mistake or, you assimilate a minor power who have a bunch of districts you don't need, you can replace them with other districts, but you will be making the pops working them unemployed. I realised late that this was a bit of a problem, so it led to a crime problem. Whoops. I eventually added some buildings which had jobs which they could move to. Having a governor working on keeping the crime in check also helped. Crisis averted.All in all, this game has plenty to keep an aspiring galactic ruler busy. I haven't played the multiplayer part so I have no idea how good that is, sorry.Is it a good Star Trek game? If you suspend your disbelief, yes. One of the mods that I noticed on the mods page for this game is one to stop Data dying from old age. So, that's a thing. Also, the sounds and music don't exactly do well to sell it as a Star Trek game. But they aren't awful, either. Except for the ambient sound in the galaxy map. Either there are too many sound layers or they're too loud, which led to me turning the ambient sound slider down to almost zero.Overall I'd give it a score of 7.5/10. 1 full point off for the UI scaling issue, and then half a point off each for other problems.

_childDocuments_.review: On the whole I love the idea of this game. my biggest gripe is the fleet centered ship combat. Star Trek isn't about massive amounts of ships. It's about the captains and officers of individual ships. I know that the Stellaris engine was used to make this game. but I really hopped it would get a way from the fleets of ships and have individual ships. In the shows, if you had 2 friendly ships in the same system, something major was going on there. Large fleet battles don't happen very often in star trek, and rushing to gather large fleets makes you care nothing for the individual ships. This game has the ships, it has a system for notable people, it just needs to be reworked. Ships are major investments that shouldn't be mass produced, they should be major investments that a civilization puts a large part of their wealth together to make. Ships should be built slower, you shouldn't have as many, and they shouldn't be controlled in fleets. If you have 10 star ships they should be out and about, patrolling your space, exploring, not all clumped in one system because if you split it up your neighbor will have a stronger fleet than you. Also, this games fighting needs some options. Federation ships will destroy their enemies if they have to, but they would much rather disable them. if there is going to be single ships, there should be an option to disable enemies. This is just my gripe about it though. As far as the game goes, it could used some tuning and patches, but I'm still going to give it a thumbs up. Most Trek games gloss over the part that the Federation doesn't kill every thing it comes into contact with, look at Star Trek online, you literally have to kill everything level up in that game, stunning is weak debuff in land combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Thus far, it's exactly what I wanted out of a Star Trek 4x game.  ---------....6 hours later....Playing Federation.Have liberated Bajor.About to help evacuate Romulus before the sun explodes.  Good:  -It is a love letter to fans of the TNG/DS9 era.  I AM the Federation, and I feel like I am.-The mechanics are different enough from Stellaris to feel fresh-Looks absolutely beautiful.  I literally just sat there watching a construction ship build a starbase for 5 minutes when I first started up the game.  -The diplomacy feels a lot more involved than Stellaris ever did.-You get to run around with the Enterprise.-Music is good.Feedback:  -While I agree with the devs reasoning behind not flooding the game with ship classes... having played it now, I feel like it does in fact either need a few more ship classes, or at least they need to have you unlock the classes they do have faster.  I'm 6 hours into the game and I still only have 2 ship types.  -A few glitches here and there, but nothing game-breaking... mostly a few voice notifications that are popping for the wrong events.  -The espionage system, while more involved than Stellaris (good), is bit obtuse.  You keep getting this "silent alarm tripped" event, which apparently is supposed to be your signal to do an anti-espionage mission with your spy ship, but the game never tells you that, even in full tutorial mode.  -I feel like research needs to be a bit less random in spots.  Right now I've unlocked two different types of disruptors for the Federation, and still don't have photon torpedoes.  Overall, I'd say it's at least 8.5/10 as is, and it can only get better as they patch things and adjust stuff like research weights.As of 11/21:  Devs have put out a lot of fixes and respond well to feedback.  Gonna call it a 9/10 now.

_childDocuments_.review: God I wanted to love this game.  I love Star Trek.  I love Stellaris.  Unfortunatly this game needed more time in the oven, breakdown below.1. Borg are a letdown:  The Borg make there presence known early, but before you know it the Borg which are the "endgame crisis" are dealt with quite trivially.  The game starts in the 2340's and by the 2390's the Borg are dead and gone.2. Attempts to stay true to the "original" story get in the way more than they help:  Events will happen only because they happened in one of the shows, not because they make any sense given what is actually happening in your play-through.  The Maquis will show up, despite no demilitarized zone with the Cardassians existing for example.  The Borg will show up and kidnap Picard... despite the Enterprise being on the other side of the quadrant from the Borg.  I'll spare the list of examples, just know they continue.3. Game systems don't mesh well: The normal give and take of Stellaris just doesn't exist here.  Where you normally need to decide where to focus in Stellaris in this game you can just do everything from the jump.  Make a big fleet, send out a ton of research ships, research welll, etc.  There is no real decision you are making and at a certain point I just started ignoring my economy because it didn't matter.  When I wanted to do something I would have enough resources to do it, and if I didn't want to do something right then it could languish on the vine until I did and be fine.  This is because of....4. No one is there to stop you:  The other powers just leave you alone unless you start something, and why would you?   There is plenty of room for everyone to expand for centuries so there is no reason to fight over resources like in Stellaris.  With no need to fight, and plenty of smaller powers who pose no threat to you to trade with, you can just ignore the other "major" powers entirely.  There is no reason to fight.  There is no reason to talk.  Every major power might as well be playing their own game of solitare.5.  Bugs:  There are a lot, like a lot a lot.  I'll spare the examples, check reddit if you want some good laughs though.TLDR;  Like I said on the start, this needed more time in the oven.  You can see what they were going for, but nothing comes together in the way it should for this to be recommended by me.  Get Stellaris, find a good Star Trek mod for it (there are several) and check on this game in a year or two.  Paradox has a history of working on games for years after release so here is hoping they can salvage this.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent game.  Most people now a days would rightly compare this to Stellaris (same developer, same Paradox mission tree, basically the same late game "crisis," etc.). I don't have Stellaris but I've seen a few videos, etc. on YouTube and would tend to agree.  For me though this is the RTS version of Birth of the Federation from several decades ago.   BoF was turn based and had a better auto-management of planet specialization and a better empire-wide application of intelligence services.  The late game lag in STI is very reminiscent of the late game lag in BoF (which was the result of a memory leak they never bothered to patch, not sure what STI's late game lag issue is but it's there).  BoF also had the Ferengi Alliance as a playable empire and a much greater ship variety.  Hopefully STI will roll out some decent additions and pace the development better and add more minor / major factions.Regardless, it's a decent enough game for the price at the moment (assuming Paradox doesn't do their usual twenty to thirty DLC packs at $10 - $20 each, if that's the case check out Sins of Solar Empire and find the Star Trek Armada 3 mod, doesn't have the spy-craft or the diplomacy aspect of STI but has a better pacing of technology and development.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the quickest I've refunded a game from a publisher this well known.The game immediately installs a third party launcher when opened for the first time without user permission or action, this is mildly annoying at best but when the launcher doesn't work it's a tad more aggravating. Working around it means changing the launch options to point directly at the game executable with an additional "%command%" option so it skips the launcher.When you're finally in game there are then numerous bugs and crashes. If you run the dev exe (infinite_rd.exe) it pops up the error logs and these are constant as it seems to be trying to load missing assets etc. Also has issues with running in full screen, which is the default, necessitating a change to windowed fullscreen... basically just bugs all round.For what is essentially a Stellaris DLC on a very mature engine with no significant changes or updates this is pretty shocking. I'm also not sure why this is a standalone game, perhaps due to licensing? To justify the price? So it can have its own billion DLC items added over time?Whatever this answer is I'd give this one a miss. If you're a hardcore Stellaris fan just get the trek mod for that game.

_childDocuments_.review: Just a quick review, a handful of day after launch. Yes, this game feels a lot like Stellaris, for obvious reasons. I don't know if I would have been happy paying 60, 70 dollars for it, but i think it is priced appropriately for what it is, I'm having fun so far, and I am sure that it will get even better with time. This game really brings me back to playing Birth of the Federation (which really needs a true, turn based sequel...). I'll be playing this over Stellaris for a while, no doubt.Recommend for Trek fans, or for people who want something similar to Stellaris but with a different feel and more consistent lore.Bugs I have seen so far: A pop migrated to my colony, Specialist class... and after a while assigned itself to the Ruler class, despite there only being Worker class jobs available.Later at that same colony, I migrated a Vulcan there to take the open researcher spot... but the Vulcan decided he wanted to be an entertainer, and let the Klingon take the researcher job. Like... what??? Please have pops prioritize jobs they are good at, devs...Had a governor who didn't gain the investigator trait when they should have, so now I have no way to resolve the special project which he wanted to check out.Diplomatic missions which require a spy ship to go into a minor power's space seem to have the spy ship bug out, entering and then immediately leaving the space without performing the mission, which certainly throws a wrench into diplomacy...Minor design flaws:  It becomes way, way too hard to find anomalies once you get a few years past game start. Their either needs to be some sort of tech or special project to find them, or maybe the minor races shouldn't be able to trip whatever flag it is that stops us from being able to find them, or something. Yes, this is super annoying because I need them to get the Enterprise-E...As the Federation, the event which triggers focused on the Romulus system triggered WAAAYYY too early in my first game. I get that these events are locked to the official timeline or anything, but.... I have 0 chance of completing it, because there was just no way to integrate a second minor power in time. For the record, the event is going to trigger about 10 years before it fired in the official timeline. That hurts.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most notable aspects of "Star Trek: Infinite" is its captivating setting, where the Star Trek universe and Stellaris intersect seamlessly. The concept of a dedicated Star Trek strategy game is undeniably appealing, as it promises to deliver an experience that fans of both franchises can relish. The prospect of immersing oneself in the Star Trek universe through gameplay is an exciting one.However, the main setback for "Star Trek: Infinite" is its technical performance. It's disheartening to report that the game is plagued with numerous bugs and issues that sets the overall experience, to self destruct. These technical hiccups, ranging from missplayed audios, stuck missions, stranded fleets and ghostly increasing resource consume, makes it very difficult to fully enjoy the game in its current state.I cannot, in good conscience, recommend purchasing "Star Trek: Infinite" at this time. While the idea licensed content and original material, behind the game is promising, its execution leaves much to be desired. It's clear that the developers have a long road ahead of them to rectify these issues and deliver a more polished and enjoyable experience for players.That being said, there is still hope for "Star Trek: Infinite." In the far, far future, with dedicated effort and ongoing development and a convincing modding community, it is possible that this game will reach its full potential and could even go beyond. "Star Trek: Infinite" could eventually become our all gamers source of joy and a worthy addition to the Star Trek gaming legacy.In conclusion, "Star Trek: Infinite" is a game with great potential, but it is currently hindered by technical issues that make it difficult to recommend. It is my hope that the work will continue and these problems get solved, eventually providing a gaming experience that lives up to the excitement of its concept. Until then, potential players should exercise patience and monitor the game's progress in the hope of a brighter gaming future in the Star Trek universe.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Infinite

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of Star Trek The Next Generation, Voyager, Deep Space Nine, or Picard, DO NOT BUY THIS GAME. You will be SORELY disappointed in their extreme lack of attention to detail and disconnection from the franchise they attempted to cram into a reskin of Stellaris.The game timeline is all screwed up, events take place out of order, classic technology isn't in place when you start the game, recognizable ships are not in, territory that should be part of the Federation is not... This game is all kinds of BAD.For starters, you have to research very basic things like photon torpedoes and phasers, which were invented in the 22nd Century by the United Earth and by the early Federation in the 23rd Century respectively, so we should have the blue TOS phasers and photon torpedoes minimum at game start. I can see upgrading the blue phasers of TOS to modern orange ones as part of TNG, but those were also installed on various vessels as early as the Motion Picture era.Quantum torpedoes (blue) and transphasic torpedoes (yellow) were the ones introduced in the 24th century, trying to combat the Borg.And speaking of The Motion Picture, where are all the Excelsiors in this game? They were EVERY-FREAKING-WHERE in canonical TNG. As I see it the Federation should have access to those at the beginning of the game, just as we do the Mirandas. After all, they're both from the TMP era, which predates TNG.Hell, they even had a few modernized Constitution-class cruisers still active as sector flagships early on in TNG. Hello, Battle of Wolf 359? Admiral Hansen's flagship?So we start the game with NONE of the appropriate technologies or ships for the era, just replicators. If this is "a sop to gameplay" then they need to strongly reconsider the era in which this game takes place. It would be far more at home as a TOS-era, TMP sub-era game, NOT a TNG-era game, as that is when the game territories, playfield and tech aspects make the most sense.And the Romulan sun exploding is an event in this game, but it occurs WAY too early. By the time the Romulan sun exploded, the Odyssey-class was available canonically! Does anyone remember the USS Verity from the tie-in novel? That's long after the Enterprise-E and approaching the -F! So if they're going to give us that event, then they should also be giving us the Verity from the novel/Odyssey-class from Star Trek Online.Between that and the fact that they didn't even bother to give us the proper territory (Denobula, Risa, Betazed and several others need to be colonized in the game when they should be in the Federation already, the Nausicaans should be known as well) and random, rapid timeline progression unconnected to the actual date in-game, these developers do NOT know their 24th Century Star Trek lore. Not TNG, not Voyager, and not Deep Space Nine. They don't even know their Picard, which was WAY past TNG and the Enterprise-E.They are vaguely aware of the overall events and major cast of characters of TNG, DS9, VOY and PIC, and they know how to make a simplified, reskinned copy of a game (  ) but they are clearly NOT fans of Star Trek The Next Generation, Star Trek Voyager, Star Trek Deep Space Nine, OR Star Trek Picard.I highly doubt they've seen a single episode of any of these series, maybe just the opening title sequence but nothing more than that. They probably just looked at Memory Alpha for all their details instead of actually watching the show.In Developer Log One, the devs claim this was a "passion project", they claim it was meant to be inspired by titles such as Star Trek Armada and Birth of the Federation. After playing the game, all I can say is that that statement is "a whole load of BULL!""Passion" is more like "pathetic". Both of those games have actual gameplay, are well-paced and the events happen pretty much when they are supposed to. I should know, I play both Armada and Armada 2 currently!There's literally not a thing in this game for the developers to be proud of. It's a clone of Stellaris with a Star Trek paintjob and a few bits of Trek lore sprinkled in.What they did with this game... it's like trying to attack a starship with a stick. What you end up with in both cases is an epic, epic failure. These developers shouldn't be proud, they should be ASHAMED. They are clearly quite DISPASSIONATE about Star Trek, and this game is an INSULT to the entire history of the franchise.This game is a waste of money - I wasted mine, and wrote this review so that you don't have to waste yours. It's not worth twenty dollars and ninety-nine cents plus tax, it's worth precisely zero dollars and zero cents. If I could get my money back, I would.However, since I'm past the 2-hour refund time for this game I will continue to play it, but as someone who is actually passionate about Star Trek, and ESPECIALLY 24th century Trek, I can pretty much guarantee you that you will find a better version of this by playing a free Stellaris mod. Don't spend your money on this.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR -Fun, but incomplete. I give it a thumbs up because I'm 30 hours in and still enjoying it, which is sort of a benchmark. Still in my first playthrough as the UFP, not finished with the mission tree (but close). The good:- Smooth experience with minimal micro-managing (I have 25 colonies, which I see to for 3 minutes every 1.5 hours).- Being fully licensed, the characters and ships you expect to see are here, as well as some story lines.- They did not give up on the random events and mysteries from Stellaris, which is nice to see.- No time travel s***, thank god.The bad:- Mission tree is very basic and has a couple of choke points (Bajor and having the Enterprise do just about everything in order to upgrade it).- Other factions are locked into a timed action (Cardies will always attack Romulans, peace out, then attack again).- Galaxy feels a bit small, I get it's 1/2 of it but make that half bigger...- Wars are not well made, winning a war and choosing DMZ will lose you territory.If you're not a Trekkie, I would wait for a couple of updates and a good QoL mod to pick this up. If you are, then you already own it lol

_childDocuments_.review: So, I really wanted to like this game. I played Star Trek Armada and Armada II, Stellaris, and many other strategy games. If this was an early alpha I could recommend this game. In its current form I cannot recommend this game. There are just aspects that are missing. You are honestly better getting stellaris and just getting a star trek mod. Pros:* Ships look good. * Each faction is different* Art Looks fine.* It has mostly Stellaris gameplay. * The Lore is fun.Cons:* Some of the stuff is hidden in strange places. - For example, as the federation there is a way to claim a system. It just isn’t as intuitive as the other three factions. * Missing basic features- Why can’t I let my science ships just auto start anomalies like I can in Stellaris? If there is a way, then it is hidden going back to my first point.* The UI IS SO BAD!- Okay, even the devs acknowledge this problem. The text is just awful. There is a mod that was shown to help with this problem but this should be fixed sooner rather than later. We shouldn't need a mod to fix it. * Only 4 factions- You got Federation, Romulan, Klingon, and Cardassian and that is it. This is a bit disappointing as I would hope for the dominion, breen, borg, and more factions. I know this game just came out but we have models for minor powers, why can’t we use those? I would hope this isn’t part of some DLC money scheme. Which brings me to my next con:* You can’t make a faction- You are stuck with 1 of the 4, which I understand. This is a Star Trek game and so they want you to play one of the main factions. Why can’t we have the option of playing a minor faction that have ships like the Klingons but look like Romulans? (Remember when Klingons and Romulans had similar ships?)* Only one map- I wish there was a choice to play the star trek universe with different maps other than the same map over and over again. * Lore- While lore can both be a positive and a negative for this game, I have to put this as a negative here. The map is boring. I wish there was the ds9 map. The Romulans get screwed. They took the thing where they lose their home world and bam they get hurt hard pretty quickly. Romulans, regardless of the difficulty, seem to be always losing. * Pirates- There is nothing wrong with pirates. I know some people would like it if they could be turned on and off, but I am fine with them. I actually like the pirate feature. Now here is my complaint about them. My problem with the pirates is that the warning for them get lost in the notification for everything else. I wish the notification would show in the center where you get notifications for needing to do research, traditions, or your tree. * Ship problems- Not every ship in factions are equal. The Klingon bird-of-prey cannot have shields…. WHY? Also just the way you get ships from a lore perspective is strange. For Federation you get the Miranda class and then the intrepid? Why? Then you get the excelsior class? Why? Klingons are fine but the federation is just awful. * Mission Tree- I like this idea but some of the stuff is not really intuitive. I think the mission tree could be more refined. For example, with Enterprise you have to do missions. Which means you go to minor factions and hope they give you a mission that the Enterprise can do instead of the 6th one where you have to repair another of their ships that broke down like some cheap car repair business.* Borg- The borg would have been a fun thing but instead of them feeling like a mid-game or late game crisis like in stellaris, they feel like a minor event quest. You do some minor things and it is over. * Romulans- I have to mention this again. They are the worst faction. They have a slow population growth and they lose their home world. I feel like I am kicking a person while they are down every time, I deal with them. ALSO, they need to build little singularities for their ships and I swear they treat these things like oil in a car because at times you just start going in the red. Why? This is such a poor mechanic that I tend to always leave troops on the ground and then when I need them to invade, pull them up, fly them over, and then invade. All the while I am going through singularities like it’s coffee or something. * Loyalty- This is so stupid. I cannot fathom why I would lose population in my federation to go to the Cardassian and become slaves and then die there. WHY? I really dislike this stupid population loyalty system.

_childDocuments_.review: I purposely waited for the latest patch to be pushed out (and played on) before posting.  First off, I'm a devout Star Trek fan and was excited enough about the Star Trek Infinite pre-release teaser to pre-order the expanded package.  To me, I don't mind helping support another Star Trek software attempt since "Birth of the Federation" was the last Star Trek strategy game that appealed to me, but evey "long game" eventually crashed due to how big the game had gotten around Turn 220+.  Star Trek Infinite appears to take that "long game" scalability into consideration if the player has the patience to stick around for it. Despite the bugs and very frustrating issues in the first week after go-live, I believe Star Trek Infinite has a lot of potential once more fixes are pushed out.  Having played in the first week (before patches) and the second week (after patches) the second round of patches has made a huge difference in game play flow, reduction in frustrations (Data dying of old age? Inconceivable!), and select actions that now "work" like they're supposed to.  Is it perfect yet?  No, but neither was Crusader Kings II or Europa Universalis IV during their initial releases either.  As a licensed Star Trek offering (in theory), I would have expected more Star Trek-themed music, but most of us are in this for the game play, and how well the game mechanics actually work.  Disclaimer: I have never played Stellaris, so I have no basis to compare Star Trek Infinite to the Stellaris mods.  And Star Trek Infinite does have the potential to grow and refine itself as more of the remaining underlying issues get resolved.   My one hope:  effective patches get completed to the base game "before" the roll-out of DLCs, please!  One more thing; every other Paradox game has the "Pause" key on the keyboard functioning for a quick "pause/unpause" shortcut for players, but not here?

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a Star Trek fan.  Not a convention Trekkie, but I like the shows and watch them, often.  I also love Stellaris.  And I'm of the generation of kids that saw the first advertisement for "Birth of the Federation" in CGW and waited years for it to launch.  Then it had bugs I never was able to resolve with my meager teenage funds.In other words, I had every expectation in the world and I had no expectations at all.  No clue what that means?  Then you haven't been playing Star Trek video games long enough.  I read the reviews,  They were mediocre-to-bad.  I waited.Over the holidays, I finally picked it up.  It is great.  Will I complete more than one mission-centric play-through for each race?  Yes, but very little unless there is a solid DLC or mod community.  There have been complaints that the "canon" events always occur at the same time.  I'm okay with that - those events make the Star Trek universe what it is.  That said, it would help for replay, especially in the event that there is no DLC or long-term support for this game, if it was possible to turn those events off entirely or randomize them among the species,  As-is, after three lengthy games in various factions (UFP, Klingon, Cardassian), I feel like I have one more in me (Romulan) before this goes back on the shelf waiting for some DLC, a good mod, or a sleepless night with TNG playing in the background.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  This is an unfinished game, do not buy yet.I'm a long time fan of Star Trek, and Stellaris is my most played steam game of all time, so I'm pretty much the ground zero target audience for this game.  What we get for the purchase price is a pretty enough Star Trek mod for a version of Stellaris which is several years out of date.  The gameplay is fine.  The story elements are okayish.  The graphics are very pretty, although puzzling in a few places (like, no LCARS?  Seriously?).The biggest issue with the game is its pacing.  It rushes through TNG's story elements extremely quickly.  It feels like we've barely gotten started, and suddenly Romulus blows up...  There's no tension with the Cardassians, and suddenly Bajor is conquered.  There's exactly one short little event for Locutus, and then the Borg invasion bugs out and doesn't launch properly.If this were a DLC for Stellaris for $20, it would be a great deal.  But at the price of a full game, it's an unfinished, shallow, and buggy mess that I cannot recommend.  Come on Paradox, you're better than this.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Stellaris clone.Worse, it's a fork off of one of the earlier versions of Stellaris, where you could DEFINITELY feel the jank that had to get patched out. And oh boy, the jank absolutely shows here. The UI scaling feature is completely borked, it makes some screens overflow off of your monitor. The game kept crashing on startup for me until I did a full reinstall. The UI is also, frankly, terrible in general. There's too many buttons that don't actually list what they do until you hover over them, which is absolutely dreadful for a game that's all about clicking on buttons to do things.Like open menus.And honestly, I don't really like how the game plays. There's way too much crap you have to micromanage. It's way more tedious than regular Stellaris. Like, hell, they actually managed to make espionage more tedious than in Stellaris. Originally, you'd just send your envoys over to spy. Now you have to recruit spies and physically fly them into enemy systems to perform espionage, and nine times out of ten your spies get murdered when the AI sends a fleet over. So that system's pointless and I have no idea why they'd implement espionage like that.They split governors off into their own little ship class too, so that's another thing you have to micromanage. Governor happens to be halfway across the quadrant when a special timed project pops up specifically requiring one? Welp, guess you're screwed. And on and on it goes. Pick this game up if you're a Trek fan, but just get Stellaris if you're in it for the 4x experience. Stellaris has way, way more features than this game does, it actually manages to be less jank, and it's got a modding community to boot.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Infinite

_childDocuments_.review: So having played through a Federation "campaign" well towards the end of the tech tree, the pacing in the game is terrible. The majority of the quests are supposed to be done quite early, I never managed to upgrade the Enterprise as anomalies disappeared and Troi's counter kept resetting.... I didn't even have the heavy transports in time to rescue Romulus as you can't focus the tech tree towards specific goals, you have to research what it provides. The fact you cannot change your war philosophy as Federation also makes late game combat more difficult (and terribly boring), because it's relatively easy to out tech your enemies just after the story completes, as that's when you finally have enough resources for your colonies to upgrade well, and unless they attack someone you are protecting, they won't engage you and you can't claim territory from them. The ship scaling and pirates are totally bananas compared to both resource production in the "early game", specifically for alloys. There is no reason I am using Miranda and Intrepid ships before the Excelsior class, no reason why fleet size is so restrictive relative to power (the pirates attack you with 2.1k dmg fleets and you need at least three or four fleets in the early game to defend against them), and if I can fly the enterprise around, why can't I build other galaxy class ships.... The idea behind the game is sound, and it could have been a lot more fun if they had scaled the time/resources/ships more appropriately. I would really hope there will be a balance patch to fix the pacing a bit but given the price of the game I doubt one will come. NOTE: I have not played the Stellaris star trek mod before, so this is only from playing Infinite.

name: Still Wakes the Deep
detailed_description: STILL WAKES THE DEEP is a return to the first-person narrative horror genre for The Chinese Room, creator of critically acclaimed games such as Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs, Everybody’s Gone to the Rapture, and Dear Esther . You are an offshore oil rig worker, fighting for your life through a vicious storm, perilous surroundings, and the dark, freezing North Sea waters. All lines of communication have been severed. All exits are gone. All that remains is to face the unknowable horror that’s come aboard. GAME FEATURES Explore a stunningly realised offshore oil rig in 1970’s Scotland that evolves throughout the story World-class visuals, audio, writing from award-winning studio The Chinese Room Star-studded cast of voice-actors: Alec Newman, Neve McIntosh, and more World-class, haunting soundtrack by Jason Graves Six hours of terrifying gameplay Brace yourself for a symphony of action, trepidation and awe LIVE THE HORROR An immersive disaster story aboard an authentic North Sea oil rig Face a terrifying, unrelenting foe Pray that, one day, you get to see your family again Experience the beauty and ferocity of the sea, as it rips apart one of humanity’s strongest structures and its steadfast crew ESCAPE THE RIG Avoid, distract, and sneak around in best attempts to survive No weapons. No powers. Just your wits and determination Run, climb, and swim through the flooding corridors and storm-lashed outer decks Struggle for survival, as one wrong step could be your last

_childDocuments_.review: For better or worse, people can be pretty down on "walking simulators", but this has the special sauce that will make you believe. Beautiful environmental design, voice acting that doesn't make me sigh (really love Finley's voice actor), and just enough spice in gameplay and mechanics to fly you through the 5 hour playtime without a hitch. It makes me think about the days of "interactive fiction" where games were "wrote", and this is probably the end result of what they hoped to make one day.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, here we go. I think SWtD is a game worth playing. It's hauntingly beautiful lovecraftian body horror. If you're afraid of the water, heights, or claustrophobic, you're going to pee your pants. The rig is amazing, I enjoyed all of the characters and I shed a tear or two. The level design felt linear, but that isn't necessarily a bad thing. It reminded me of SOMA in a way.That being said, I didn't find it super scary. Maybe I'm just too used to these games, as I'm a career Horror Enjoyer(tm). I thought the encounters in the beginning were spooky (Gibbo, since I never saw him, and Trots since he was the first) but after all of the monsters had the same mechanic (throw a thing and crawl while they're distracted) I was just kind of tense, not necessarily scared. What I did appreciate was that checkpoints were often, so you didn't have to replay a ton if you failed. The game also didn't take me very long, and other than a few achievements there isn't really any replayability. The characters were fun. I liked the voicelines, I liked the dynamics of everybody, and I super appreciated the subtitles translating some of the things for me. Overall, this game has an amazing atmosphere and I would recommend it if you've got thirty bucks burning a hole in your pocket, but otherwise, wait till it's on sale. 8 screwdrivers out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is a first-person horror game developed by The Chinese Room. Set on the Beira D oil rig in the North Sea during 1975, it offers a beautifully crafted juxtaposition of manmade, natural, and supernatural elements.Atmosphere and Tension:The game excels in creating a sense of place. The oil rig feels remote, claustrophobic, and oppressive, yet it also holds warmth and life. The lived-in spaces reveal much about the characters, and the authenticity of the world is easy to buy into.The writing is beautifully nuanced, incorporating perfectly deployed profanity, and the performances from the cast are stellar.Narrative and Gameplay:Electrician Cameron McLeary (Caz) receives a letter from his wife, urging him to come home. But duty calls, and he faces a day filled with escalating disasters.The game balances horror with a human heart, gradually allowing unknowable forces to take hold. While the linear structure might disappoint some, the strong atmosphere compensates for it.Visuals and Art Direction:The grim period setting of the Beira D oil rig is brought to life with gaudy fabrics, grubby linoleum, and meticulously recreated details. The artistry captures the bleakness of the rig while infusing it with life.Conclusion: Despite some hand-holding, simple puzzles, and a short story, Still Wakes the Deep is an atmospheric, tense, and gripping experience that I fully recommend. It’s a journey into horror with a very human touch.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Having played one or two of The Chinese Room's previous titles in the vain of horror, I'd been looking forward to this release, after suddenly seeing it revealed at a game-related-showcase. Getting my hands on it thanks to a friend, I'm left rather surprised, to be honest.I wanna get the game's biggest negative aspect out of the way right away, it's very overpriced for how short it is. This game should be maybe $20 bucks at the most. So absolutely buy it when it goes on sale.Now, as far as the game itself goes, I love how much of a cosmic-horror blend it ends up being. It's very easy to bring it up and compare it to something like Outlast, but the differences SWtD introduces are in its design. On the surface, it's rather comfortable, similar, in the sense it's a tense, cat-and-mouse-style horror game. However, its levels, interiors, are all designed to ensure the hiccups in your progression are *player* caused, over Outlast, where it'll suddenly put an enemy in front of you to stifle progression. SWtD emphasizes on being more quiet, cautious with how you navigate around its horrific creatures. The level design is also designed to cut out as much backtracking while in one space as possible, while continually evolving and reshaping already explored spaces throughout the games progression, giving some variety, some worldbuild-evolution to the spaces you'll bumble through. The voice acting was my absolute favorite part of the whole experience. You're robbing yourself if you don't play it in the United Kingdom English version. Every character felt very, *very* grounded to the story and their ever-changing workplace. They carry the continuity, the whimsical-ness, the stress, the terror and anguish across the games duration and do not drop the ball once, stellar voice acting across the board. I also learned quite a lot of new words :). The one instance where I wish Steam had, or maybe in this games case, used 'Cosmic' over the 'Psychological' tag, as the game does a good job leaving you in the unknown about its horrors, allowing you to really ponder and create your own thoughts, your own ideas. I like it when a horror game has unexplained-horrors-beyond-comprehension, and leaves that open the entire time. I can identify some of its psychological elements, but the games main, central horrific(s) feel deeply rooted in a cosmic-aspect. I really liked this game! It's honest about what it wants to be, and kept me dialed in with all kinds of immersive-downtime beats, somewhat adds to the compounded foundation that is many an Outlast-esq, by including new ways to parkour and shimmy around a decrepit and constantly evolving oil rig.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's make something clear, first:I don't play games like this very often (horror games, where you can't fight back). While I really like a well written story, I always want something more - an arsenal to shoot or slash the enemy, skills to distribute and/or choices to make - to use and/or to do.I'm most likely not the target audience, and if games like this are more to your liking, than maybe my points will not be as relevant for you. I will try to focus on objective stuff, so this review might end up being more useful.The very short summary of the game: you are on an oil rig, and something goes wrong, and now you'll have to survive.The visuals, the atmosphere and the voice acting is freaking awesome! The many little noises that you can think of are all there. Waves and rain from the outside, metal structures making noises - it's all done very well - I felt like I was there. The visuals of the game is great. The "grayness" gets you into the game's atmosphere immediately, and never let's go. The character models look good, and the enemies look very disturbing (I mean this as a positive). The only negative I can say (if I really wanted to) is some design of the "bad stuff" reminded me when some graphics weren't finished in a game, or when the models clipped - mostly in older games. In this games case, it wasn't a bug, or anything like that - it just reminded me of those things. I'd have gone with different (more "fleshy") design. But this, I'd put in the nitpick category.The voices got me liking the game from the first lines! Literally every voice actor and actress done a top notch job, and I really liked the accents! They conveyed the emotions - the panic, the hope and the despair - perfectly. Also, the voices and noises coming from the enemies enhance their creepiness. Made me want to get away even more.Now, get to why I can't recommend this game after praising it: IT'S TOO SHORT!Since there are no choices in the game, there is only one ending (as far as I can tell). There is no replay value - you can't change how to approach challenges, enemies, neither who to save or let die. Which is not a bad thing in itself. But then the game/story should've been much longer! I got the game on a sale for 26€ (with VAT) and even that feels much higher than what playtime I was able to put in it (and I was really not trying to rush). At full price you'll get 6-7 hours of gameplay for 36€. While it's pretty, that's irrelevant, if you can only play it for this long. The game either should be much cheaper, or they should've put in mechanics to at least create the illusion of choice and different outcomes (or actually provide multiple endings). I can sink in several hundred hours in games where I can create different builds and/or have different outcomes because of choices I can make. If I'd tried to price those like this game, they would cost thousands.I can't recommend this game, it's too short. I will still check the devs upcoming projects, because they sure as hell have talent - just either make them cheaper or longer!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, truly one of THE best horror stories in a game that I've played in a long time -- unfortunately it's constantly marred by poor game design and a lack of QA. A+ story, C- Gameplay. It kills me to have to set this as a "not recommend". The voice acting and world building is top notch, and the atmosphere is perfect. I really enjoyed the characters and the body horror was perfectly grotesque. Sadly, the most of the actual game mechanics simply felt entirely "tacked on" last minute to me. It feels like it would be a great filmThe game is absolutely FILLED with bugs, with several of them even being game breaking. There were countless times where I found myself infuriated with the controls failing to register properly - near the end I was gritting my teeth through it just to finish up the story. This probably has the worst swimming mechanics I've ever had to deal with, and I even had to spend a full hour doing my own QA testing just to try to figure out how to get around a game-breaking bug regarding an underwater ladder jump. I was frequently glitched through views, or straight through guard rails (to my death) several times. Many of the settings menu options simply don't work at all, which is crazy considering that should be the simplest mechanic to verify. On top of that, the level design is incredibly simplistic with simple paths and very little actual game play. It's very much a walking simulator -- which I normally tend to love ...when I don't feel like I'm having to fight against constant bugs just to make progress.As a result, it felt like I had to actively fight the game just to complete the story. The game mechanics actively dragged me out of it simply because they were so broken. It really got worse the more I went on, so perhaps they focused more on the first half of the game during testing. I DEEPLY wish that I could recommend this game, but with the current glitches I feel like I have to tell people to wait and save their money until the developer spends the time fixing the bugs. These bugs should have been solved before launch -- it's a full month later and they haven't fixed anything?

_childDocuments_.review: In the 1970s salty Scotts are turning into haggis monsters on an oil rig that is about to fall into the ocean. It's up to one man (good with the "leccy") to set things right.Still Wakes the Deep is a short but polished "walking simulator+". There are simple QTEs, jumping, swimming, stealth, and chase sequences. It's entirely on rails with little-to-no freedom to explore the environment but that is fine for the type of game it is.The visuals are good with a wide variety of upscaling methods supported, including DLSS and FrameGen. Audio is fantastic, not just technically but also the quality of the voice acting (although I did start to feel like same two or three swear words are used a little too often throughout the script).It took me a little over 4 hours to beat the game, with the only replay value being missed Steam achievements. Such a short playtime at $35 USD off-sale is a big ask, but with that having been said, I got it 10% off during the first week of release and I liked it enough that I do not regret having paid nearly full price. At the time if this review it is on Game Pass, so check there first.
