_childDocuments_.review: Eh, its a Chinese Room game, what else to say? If you didn't hate Machine for Pigs, you probably won't hate this one too, on a sale. If you want more from a horror game than just some visceral imagery, you should look for another one.It has a nice story and characters, atmosphere, good voice acting, but it is just a walking simulator. It has a few H&S and chase sections, but it would be disingenuous to call them tense. I initially wanted to give the game a negative review, just for how appaling the monster encounters are, but decided that it would be unfair. Especially considering that i didn't HATE anything else about the game.Visual and sound design of monsters is good, but the danger they present is an illusion. The game has no health or other damage system, so the monsters just instantly kill you on contact. You are not worried about spending recources to recover, so there is no tention from that. You also have no inventory and all of the puzzles are usually 1-2 steps long and do not require items that you can lose. The encounter sections are generally short and consist of you crawling from one hiding spot to another. So you have little to no tention from losing progress. The only thing left to scare is your own perception of monsters. Which crumbles to dust the moment you climb into a hiding spot.You see, monsters literally cannot harm you when you are inside a hiding spot. I found that out in the first encounter with a real monster, Trots. I was sitting inside a wide open cabinet, about a meter away from the monster, flashing the light directly into his mug, and he could not do anything to me. The monsters generally don't react to light, so you can safely crawl around with your lights on at all times. Even if you are noticed, you can hop into a hiding spot, put hands over your head in a triangle and say "I'm in a house!". They will growl and cuss, shake their hanging intestines in front of you but they will leave you alone. Later in the game there is a moment where a "hiding spot" is an elevator shaft with a wide open door that the monster could easily fit through, if it was a better horror game. Back in Outlast, Chris Walker would drag me out and rip my head off if i tried something like this.Besides Machine for Pigs, i was also reminded of a little game i played years ago called The Sexorcist, which had the exact same issue. Except the "monster" in that game was leaving traps around, you had multiple item-based puzzles around the house and only 3 lives to complete them all. An H-game with pre-bought assets made me feel more tense than a horror game by Chinese Room, because there was something to lose. If you get killed in SWTD, you are put at the exact same place. I think if you put monster encounters in your game you should put even a little effort into it, so it doesn't look like it was made out of begrudging obligation.I guess it is unfair to focus so hard on the monster encounters to the point everything else seems to be ignored, but had little reason to care about anything else. I don't feel that the characters are in danger, because i don't see the monsters as a danger. And i couldn't care less about the characters because i can't tell 90% of them apart. I remember Addair, , Rennick, , Roy and Finlay, who i assumed to be a guy for about half the game. Everyone else, including the main character, seems to be the same "wee Sco'ish bas'ard" who might as well have the same voice actor. A good voice actor, mind, but nonetheless.Like i said, it was supposed to be a negative review (and it clearly is), but writing it i realised that monster encounters are the only thing i didn't like about the game, and frankly the only thing i had anything to say about.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Spoilers.Very straightforward horror walking simulator, you can't get lost, you can't branch off, there's nothing to collect, just walk from point A to point B and flip a switch like you're told while evading very avoidable monsters.The coolest parts being the designs of the meat oil monsters, kind of gave me a 1999 House on Haunted Hill meets The Thing vibe, and the big twisty oil tendrils themselves and what they were doing to the station was very cool. The execution of the story kinda falls apart aside from that, you're literally just running around plugging holes while finding out literally NOTHING about what is going on. What should be an environment that lends itself to isolation very well (being an oil rig out in the middle of the ocean) never ends up making you feel scared or vulnerable because you're in constant communication with crew mates, meeting them and crawling around extremely talkative monsters or hallucinations who never shut up so the horror vibe never really settles in.The game starts getting coolest right before the end, like, right before the end. You don't get an explanation as to what's going on, what the thing that got drilled up was or why it could twist and warp solid metal and create recursive windows, not even a hint, and you don't even meet satan at the end (or whatever IT was) so the story just sort of slams shut with no real satisfaction for the player or anyone slightly curious as to what the hell is going on.The voice acting and script was good though, likeable characters.If it was a quick little twenty dollar horror experience I'd give it a positive rating. With how barebones it feels at $40 I can't give it a good review, especially when it only takes around 5-6 hours to play the game (it didn't take 10 hours to beat, I just left it on overnight).

_childDocuments_.review: Im torn and still wish steam had a middle option between good and bad.If you take your and try to explore... you 99% of the time dont get rewarded. So if people say they finished it in about 3hours, yes you can finish it in that time or even less when you do the second run to get all the achievements but when you really actually play, read, look around and allow yourself the time to experience it... even if you end up being disappointed cause walking around a bunch of corners and backtracking is pointless except for when a phone rings, your first run can be 4-6hours. Adding the retries of sections cause you dont know where the hell youre supposed to go, the game bugs out on you or you think the game bugged out but its just a scripted scene where you have to fail and swim instead of climb... reloaded the game 3 times just to realize you have to fail the QTE...This game is basically QTEs everywhere. Walking sim with some stealth and basic, walk there, activate that, no riddles or anything hard. Voice acting is great, the scottish accent is... fun but holy hell every sentence is filled with curses and swearing. I do want to ask the person who decided the achievements, how exactly they thought it was fun or helping to play in a language you cannot read at all... if it was the voice overs that changed that would be one thing but not being able to read instructions is just ... who came up with this dumb achievement? Overall the visuals and atmosphere are really good and the setting sure is different from alot of horror games. The game does not offer free exploration of an oil rig, the game description is kinda misleading there.Maybe the price is set a bit too high for a experience of this length but some other games also charge 60-80 bucks for a 6hour game but 35 for a 4hour game still feels a bit too much. The game has 0 replayability and the only reason to do so is getting all the achievements and increasing the playtime this way. At least the game is not a cheap jumpscare festival or turns into a gunfest midway.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is a captivating and immersive experience that masterfully blends atmospheric storytelling with intense, suspenseful gameplay. Set on a North Sea oil rig in 1975, the game plunges you into a harrowing tale of survival and mystery. The hauntingly realistic visuals and sound design pull you into the eerie, isolated environment, making every creak and shadow feel ominously real. The narrative is rich and engaging, revealing its secrets at a perfect pace, keeping you on edge throughout. With its strong character development and deeply unsettling atmosphere, Still Wakes the Deep is a must-play for fans of horror and narrative-driven games!It's a 10/10 from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Best game I ever played! No, do not ask why I have so many hours on it-Jokes aside, I rarely get motivated to play games. I am usually someone who doesn't enjoy mainstream games and only play a handful of older games.However, after seeing a Let's Play of this game, I was hooked. Even if I am extremely afraid of Horror Games, my interest for this game was big enough to dare playing either way.Aside from playing I started drawing a bunch of Fanart for the game, explored the games files to find hidden details, spend a questionable long time messing with Muir (don't ask)- and learn about the making of the game.(Also waiting with excitement until the Artbook gets shipped out next year!! I don't regret preordering it)Not sure how to describe how much happened thanks to this game. I was extremely fascinated with everything. I started chatting with a bunch of folk from the community and it has been an absolute blast. The last months were extremely stressful for me, which is thankfully over soon. But having a game where I can relate with the characters helped a ton to get through this time period. Playing this game multiple times didn't even get boring for me, okay maybe a tiny bit. But I found new ways to make each playthrough really fun.Not to mention how I somewhat got rid of my burnout that my workplace gave me. I am currently trying to put the lore together with others on discord, while recording a bunch of my playthroughs for a future video maybe? Also learning a bit more about blender (to mess around with the models) and finally being more motivated to draw humans, which I am usually too nervous for. Graphics are great, story/dialogue has me invested enough to want to stay up and be miserable at work tomorrow to see more, and the setting is amazing. One thing I really love is that so far a lot of this is actually taking place during the day which is rare for most horror games. So far the monster designs have all been The Thing levels of body horror and while the scare sequences definitely feel on rails that's just how it is with the genre of chase/unarmed horror. Stuff like Soma or Outlast was a lot more open ended with how you handled hunts but it all still boiled down to run and hide while completing an objective then have a chase, this game just cuts the fat with that and gets on with the story. Seen people say it takes a bit out of game play to give stronger set piece moments, but lets be real the hide and seek loops of other chase horror games aren't really deep enough to offset a good experience and I like the faster pace in this. Moving from one thing to another and not spending 30 minutes under a bed makes you feel like you're actually on a time crunch to figure out a solution to your situation.Overall strongly recommend. Glad the games getting good reviews and hope with the success of this we see more devs try their hand at eldritch horror and deep sea/oceanic settings.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game is at least 95% crawling or swimming through contrived obstacles for no reason. That's not an exaggeration, it's literally true. The ending is stupid and not only thoroughly unsatisfying but genuinely frustrating. The game never explains itself, even a little. It's nothing more than a very short, linear "crawl now, jump now" mess with a garbage non-story.This is just another stupid game with characteristically stupid design and plot choices (e.g. "You stay here. I'll get to the lifeboats alone and then come back for you, tripling the time and the risk for no rational reason. We definitely should not both go right now together, even though this plan makes zero sense whatsoever.")Just another game that makes you hit the right button at the right time -- basically QTEs -- while you zip through a contrived maze that is absolutely unrealistic.Just another game with ladders that lead to cramped crawlspaces in an incredibly unrealistic way, and with filing cabinets and the like stacked in a thoroughly implausible way for no reason other than to create a pointless maze.And yeah, I'm running for my life to escape a monster trying to kill me, and yet for some reason, the best I can do in this scenario to move a laundry basket that blocks the exit is to gently move it ever-so-slowly, as if to avoid waking a hummingbird. Or how about that my top running speed is around 3 MPH?This nonsense reminds me of how, in Days Gone, the ultra-fit protagonist somehow becomes tuckered out after running 10 steps, even when trying to escape a horde of zombies. This is just contrived, low-effort gaming mechanics trash. It doesn't entertain me, it infuriates me.The swimming mechanics are infuriatingly difficult, even when they work as intended. And at one point, I lost all control of the character while underwater. My hands were out in front of me, but I couldn't move, no matter what I tried. I just had to wait to drown.And the monsters are , ffs.Stupid game. Boring and predictable. The ending -- which comes rapidly since the game is extremely short -- is also senseless and frustrating, and makes everything you did up until then completely pointless. Alternative ending scenarios are easy to imagine but are not even brought up.And the game doesn't even begin to explain what caused all the events depicted!People like this game for the same reason that people raved about the Model T automobile in 1908: There's nothing better on offer. Sort of like how there's nothing on TV but absolute trash, more absolute trash, and just plain trash. The plain trash looks good by comparison. But it's still just trash.Here's a clue, developers, and yes, I know you don't care: STOP MAKING IT SO CONTRIVED!Edit: Cute sarcastic comment, Liam. How "incredibly detailed" should my review be, given that the game has hallmarks that I hate? If you went out for dinner at a restaurant and found a turd in your soup, would you detail everything about your experience, or would you focus on ... oh, I dunno ... the turd?

_childDocuments_.review: Please keep in mind there may be spoilers in this review, I played the game in "story mode"!Plot: You are working on an oil rig as the electrical engineer, you get called to your boss's office and once you leave his office a bit afterwards you will experience the main game, any further explanation of the plot may spoil it.An Absolutely Amazing Game!Amazing Atmosphere!If you like hair raising games then try this game.Just Incredible Graphics & Story.If you are looking for an action game this is not it, well let me explain, there is lots and lots of action, there is plenty of action, but if your thought was fighting and shooting monsters then this is not it, here you evade the monsters and hide.Gameplay consists of advancing the story and avoiding death whenever it shows up in various forms. I know I already mentioned this but the ATMOSPHERE! OMG they f'ing nailed it!The only downside is the game is not terribly long, I used about 5 hours to complete it start to finish but it definitely did NOT feel short even if it was. This is because the atmosphere makes the experience feel way longer than it actually is.If you are unable to watch horror movies maybe don't play this, let's say if you can stomach the "Saw" movies, you know the guy called "Jigsaw" then you can stomach this, ok maybe "Saw" is a lot worse but rather shoot too high than too low haha.The game can get emotional at times, especially further out in the game.The game is super casual in that you don't have to be Micro Jackson Himself to play it, unlike other games like Starcraft 2/Age of Empires 2 DE/Warcraft or LOL/Dota 2. If your micro skills are that of an actual potato you can still play this, especially since if you die you just load from the last save point which usually is not far behind, so you only play a few seconds to get to where you were if not instantly.Obviously it was not without it's flaw(s)1) Sometimes when you pick up throwables and then crouch you will be locked in crouch and can only de-crouch by dropping or throwing the item you currently have in your hand.2) The game is not as optimised as you'd want it to be. In the menu alone I dropped frames.In game I had decent frames at maxed out settings (1920x1080p monitor) without framegen or upscaling but it would sometimes drop my frames down to 110'ish which is still very playable given 60 is the minimum for playable but I wouldn't have minded a game that ran at 144 fps instead of 110'ish in some areas. Sure I could upgrade from the second best graphics card to the best graphics card (rtx 4090) but that card is absurdly costly. If you wanted to see how my PC ran on the game please look at the link below. Yes you can upgrade graphics card and turn down settings and use lossless scaling (costs about 7 bucks on steam) and maybe a lot more things but what I am getting at is that at the end of the day it would be really nice to NOT have to do these things. Would be really nice to play it natively without worrying about fps. And yes if my pc case had more or better fans then my CPU & GPU would perform better.2 TL;DR) If you play at 1080P at MAX SETTINGS and doing so WITHOUT NEITHER framegen or upscaling and your system is 32 GB DDR5 (speed 6000) RAM and CPU is 7800X3D and GPU is RTX 4080 Super then you will get 90-100 fps in most areas.To wrap up this review:Amazing Game, the game's high points are Graphics/Story/Atmosphere.This game gets the Adventure Archives Score of:6/10Cards:[Story] + [Horror] + [No Combat] + [Realistic] + [Emotional] + [Easy]Want to see a FULL PLAYTHROUGH? _childDocuments_.review: "Still Wakes The Deep" is one of the best narrative horror games I've played in a long time. It's set on a dangerous oil rig in 1970s Scotland, and the attention to detail in recreating the setting is impressive. The graphics, powered by Unreal Engine, deliver stunning visuals and effects that truly capture the atmosphere of the rig and its surroundings.One of the standout features for me was the sound design. With high-quality headphones, the game's immersive soundscapes drew me in, allowing me to hear everything from footsteps to the howling of monsters and the creaking of the rig during a storm.The game does a fantastic job of conveying the power of the sea during stormy weather, making the waves feel incredibly realistic and the environment truly immersive.The story is more of a narrative horror experience rather than a survival horror game like Outlast or Amnesia. It's like being part of a movie, taking you on an emotional journey filled with intense and eerie moments that will keep you on the edge of your seat.While 'Still Wakes The Deep' is a highly recommended horror game, it's worth noting that it's relatively short in length. However, the compelling story and characters make it a worthwhile experience for any horror game enthusiast.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lovely horror experience. It had me on my tiptoes for most of the playthrough.From the story to the enemy design, the game looks and feels amazing to play. I found Caz to be a very enjoyable protagonist and the story was captivating.The game isn't perfect though. It is very graphically intense, which makes it look absolutely gorgeous and it excels at creating beautiful environments, but it also means that lower end machines won't be able to run it. Make sure your machine meets the requirements, and preferably even a little better than that. This does not take away from the experience I had while playing this game. Still Wakes the Deep is a beautiful story-driven game that is sure to go down as a new classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is a game that perfectly embraces the philosophy of "less is more." The simplicity of its mechanics works in its favor, allowing the story and atmosphere to take center stage. There's no need for complex systems or convoluted gameplay —by keeping things straightforward, the game lets you fully immerse yourself in its beautifully crafted world.The graphics are stunning and serve as the perfect backdrop to the growing tension throughout the story. The level design is intuitive and well-paced; I never felt lost or unsure of where to go next. I liked the character development, and the well-written connections between the characters that added depth to the narrative. Also the voice acting is another standout feature!In all I really enjoyed the game, and hope for more in the future! ^^

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5 - GoodThis is perhaps the best walking simulator you will ever play. But it is a walking simulator, you're very much on-rails and there's minimal gameplay mechanics. It's also quite short, my playtime includes over an hour of fiddling with the graphics to get a smooth frame-rate. The high points of this game are the atmosphere, graphics, audio and story, everything there is top quality. Use headphones if you have them for extra immersion.One thing they should improve is to make it easier to optimize graphics. There's no medium or low presets and all options are set to Epic by default. Your frame rate is likely to suck when you start the game. My best recommendation is to set Shadows to Low as this setting is the main FPS killer, and shadows on medium/high don't even look that good (curved objects have jagged shadows lol). Also reduce the UE TSR upsampling if you need to, putting it to 80% made a world of difference to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Bit overrated. Honestly middling in a way that makes me disinterested in getting into talking about it. So in short;On the plus side it is pretty in places(particularly around the entity), monster design is nice even if the horror doesn't really work, the sound design was excellent, and I like that I could play in GaelicBut many visual glitches, clipping errors and so on. The voice actors are doing their best with what they have but the dialogue is cheesy and tired, story is by-the-numbers stuff, characters rote and shallow, movement mechanics frustratingly slow and clunky, AI is a bit buggy and the distraction & throw mechanics frequently don't work, nothing you do as a player matters, very linear, arbitrary roadblocks everywhere, no real point to looking around or exploring. Maybe its because I live in Scotland that the novelty of seeing tartan carpets or hearing accents isn't carrying it for me. I bought it in the sale, but still refunded. It is a profoundly ..almost okay.. game.I'm sure some people will excuse its shortcomings because that's just how the genre works, but I've played plenty of similarly linear narrative-led horror games that didn't have these issues, or were executed in a way where it didn't matter as much - because unlike here, there was more substance to stop these being the defining parts of the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: You play the role of Caz, a guy who flees to a Scottish deep-sea oil-rig to evade police after beating someone up.  While drilling, the rig uncovers something straight out of a Lovecraft tale.  (I was disappointed that we never learn exactly what it was.)  Will our hero (or anyone else) escape the rig?  Caz is sure going to try.This was an interesting, albeit short first-person horror game, but I didn’t care for the ending.  The game was very linear with clear indications of where to go and little to explore as the environment was rather barren.  The visuals were good and the voice acting and ambient sounds were amazing.    In fact, they were the best part of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially unsure whether I would relate to this game based on the trailer, the protagonist and setting being so opposite to myself. However, I loved Everybody's Gone to the Rapture and Dear Esther so I decided to give it a chance and in the end I'm glad I did. First things first, this is definitely not your traditional walking simulator. This is more a mix between walking simulator, parkour, horror, and a stealth game. If you were hoping for a relaxing, little to no game mechanics type game, this isn't the game for you. There's some sections of parkour that felt unintuitive or tedious. There was such an excessive amount at times that it took away from the immersion. But overall, it did add to the sense of danger.That said, everything else about this game is a top notch cinematic experience. The voice acting, music, and sound effects is once again top of the line as The Chinese Room is known for. The visuals are immersive, beautifully made, and perfect for the setting. The real sense of danger and feeling hunted, the eerie feeling throughout... this is another work of art rather than merely a game. Even though I didn't feel that I could relate to Caz and his backstory much, nor the others on the rig. I couldn't help but to really feel their experiences and relate to their emotions the further along it went. The voice acting is very well done and convincing. I finished the game feeling impacted by it which prompted me to write this review. So, I definitely recommend this experience if you like this type of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I had a feeling this game was not going to be ok but I still wanted to give it a chance. Unfortunately, it was still lacking substance. After knowing the game's mechanical limitations, it felt like repetitive and in the end I just wanted to get to the end of it to see how everything will unfold. I wish I had a weapon or somthing to shoot or blow up or maybe some food lying around I could eat.

_childDocuments_.review: "Still Wakes the Deep" has actual human characters, throws you right in the middle of the drama, and moves at a brisk pace of an old-school disaster movie. Wait, what? The Chinese Room, to me, is synonymous with walking slowly ahead while disembodied voices talk to you. Usually all the interesting events have already happened, and the player is just there to ponder on the story they've missed out on. I know Dan Pinchbeck is credited and all, but "Still Wakes the Deep" just doesn't feel like his game at all. At one point, I found myself climbing a burning helicopter wreckage suspended hundreds of meters above open sea. This is Uncharted stuff, how's that a follow up to "Dear Esther"?! That said... I never particularly enjoyed The Chinese Room games. I mean, they were FINE, but I didn't REALLY like them. "Still Wakes the Deep" I find a lot more enjoyable specifically BECAUSE it feels more human and less cryptic. It seems to have lost the poetic pretense of previous games, for better or worse. There are no monologues. It's... Really, it's kind of a standard horror story, but The Chinese Room nailed the oil rig setting, nailed the atmosphere, nailed the sound design, and made me buy this tale wholesale despite some tired cliches. It's really quite good. The gameplay is very linear though; there's a lot of walking, running, swimming, pushing switches, and hiding from monsters, but the levels are structured like one continuous corridor. On the bright side, it means the game is quite accessible and pretty much anyone can enjoy the story. And I recommend that you do, if you find the premise interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there were more games like this.I love games that have a very unique feel to them, an atmosphere that entrenches you into the world, and a beautiful self-contained story. I read the IGN review for this game beforehand (the one that rated it a 6/10) and thought the critiques sounded stupid, so I wanted to give this game a try and see if they were wrong. They were. I disagree with basically all of the negative things they said.The sound design is amazing. The environment is beautiful and feels like an authentic real oil platform that actual people are working on. The horror elements are tastefully done and unique. The story and general feel reminds me of The Thing, with a crew of professional in complete isolation trying to survive from some type of unknown horror they don't understand. Probably the only gripe I have is that I personally find it hard to take people with thick Irish accents seriously, so there were a few moments of dialogue in the game that I found unintentionally funny when I think I was supposed to be scared. Regardless, solid 9/10. Give me more stuff like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes The Deep is a game that I have been looking forward with a lot of hype since it was announced and I can safely say it did not dissapoint!First thing I want to say is that an Oil Rig is a very under utilised environment in almost any video game! Given its secluded nature, its large size and clostrophobic interior - it honestly makes for an amazing environment in almost any video game but it really works in a horror like this one.I loved so much about Still Wakes The Deep: Overall I loved Still Wakes The Deep, it ticked every box for when it comes to an amazing single player narrative driven game and the grotesque horror was the icing on the cake!

_childDocuments_.review: So I've played this for like an hour and I gotta say: Don't buy it. It is literally just a pacifist obstacle course with intense music masquerading as a survival horror. If you don't believe me WATCH all trailers and that is literally about everything in this game so far (minus any fights because I don't think there are any. Really). You'll also notice the player never has any items in his hands... probably because there isn't an inventory system, let alone a combat one This game consists of: 0) Locked doors on an oil rig. -Hope you like finding another way around!  1) Making you 'jump', 'crouch' and 'interact' in a painfully predetermined fashion with little variation or creativity. The controls also feel somehow very appropriate yet poorly mapped in a way you can't really change. You can pick up things in your hands but you can't really do much with them as I recall-No inventory system, health bar, crafting, etc... Just you.-I mean, you'd think a survival horror on an oil rig may involve more creative use of things around you, but nope. Just run through hallways and down stairwells.2) "Narrative" cut-scenes that go from being kinda watchable to quickly feeling like they are strangling you on your couch while you debate whether to skip them or sit there listening for 3 minutes (you can't move during them)NOTE: They all end in you going on a fetch quest because 3) Despite what the trailer says, there actually isn't any fighting (at least not so far, 1 hour in). -No signs of me having an inventory or being able to punch, kick, swing, shoot. So dumb.4) All the scary parts are heavily manufactured as if they are just interactive cut-scenes that are banking on intense graphics and loud music to be fun.Maybe just go buy an identical but much better game like "Alien: Isolation". -That game at least makes you think you can shoot things because it actually gives you a few guns, a clear opponent, simple but immersive survival mechanics and all the fetch quests you could ask for. -It also has an alien!-Asura's Wrath is dope too if you like interactive cut-scenes, fun story and cool game styles.Basically I would maybe pay $10-15 for this. Great graphics (but needs optimization) and awesome voice acting, but nothing really... gameeeee. I wanted a video game, not a $40 story.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Big heads up, this game is solely focused on story and immersion, the go to term people would use would be "Walking Sim". There are some gameplay elements beyond just walking around but they are very surface level. HOWEVER, the story, atmosphere, sound design, and definitely the voice acting more than make up for the shallow gameplay. This is a game you turn the lights off and play alone with noting in the background or on the other monitor.I was expecting a longer game however, I was also expected a different kind of game and in hindsight after beating it, the game would feel a lot worse if it went on longer. If you beat the game in one session like I did, the game might drag on a wee bit at the end but thankfully not too much.On to the actual review, good story  , and phenomenal voice acting. From the start I was completely engaged and that continued until the very end. The game play leaves something to be desired however this being a story focused game and the length of the game, it is more than acceptable. The price might be a bit of a pain point for some people so I would say wait for a discount if you really want to play it but I must insist, this game is ABSOLUTELY worth playing. 7.5 / 10And one last thing to remember Caz, Jesus loves you, but everyone else thinks you're a ****
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: A story driven horror masterpiece that felt like anything but a boring corridor-walking simulator. Immersive in dialogues and acting, gorgeous in sound and image, I loved every second of it.It has this taste of cosmic, unknowable horror in a realistic setting without sacrificing its mystery to squid-like demigods' names and long dead american writers. It smelled like cinematographic, arctic horrors and submarine despair without being a soulless copy. The characters felt true, respected by the writers and the actors. Kudos for making me love the scottish accent. It's short by today's standards and expectations, even though I felt a hint of replayability. However, I'd take that sort of games for double the price anytime, considering its quality and the emotions it left me with. It's fluid, challenging enough, simple but varied without repetition, well paced, well written, well acted, well crafted.A shame that sort of solo experience is so rare nowadays. Thanks for this journey.A future classic and already up there in my "all times best" lists.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is a unique narrative-driven game that immerses players on an oil rig in the North Sea. It blends exploration with psychological horror elements, creating an unsettling atmosphere that keeps you on edge.The game features stunning visuals and sound design, enhancing the eerie ambiance. Players navigate the oil rig while uncovering its dark secrets, encountering haunting imagery and thought-provoking storytelling. The sense of isolation is palpable, as you confront not just external threats but also the internal struggles of the main character.The pacing is deliberate, allowing the tension to build up slowly as you piece together the narrative. And it does a very nice job making every discovery you come across feel significant.Overall, Still Wakes the Deep is an engaging experience for fans of narrative exploration and horror, offering a haunting journey that lingers in your mind.

All in all, 6/10 for me, if this was cheaper in the 15-20 dollar range I wouldn't have any complaints but 35 is way too much right now. Wait for a sale before you buy.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the worst horror games I've ever played.... with that being said, this could've been one of the best horror movies I've ever seen. Most good horror games contain but are not limited to: unsettling atmosphere, decent puzzles, little interactions with friendly npcs, and good scares. Still wakes the deep has almost none of this. The whole game feels like a very linear walking simulator, you're always on a path, no secrets, no crafting, nothing, you're always walking until you hit a monster. The game has some sneaking around but it only lasts 5 minutes before a character dies and you go into a chase sequence, and most of the time the chase sequence is in one straight line. There was basically nothing suspenseful or scary about this game. I beat it in 4 hours and I will admit, I'm a coward. It took me 17 hours to beat resident evil 7 on normal mode, so if it took me 4 hours to beat this game, it'll take you 2 hours. Now when i said this game would make a great movie, its because the voice acting is the best I've ever heard and the story is pretty decent but my entire play through I couldn't get over how amazing the voice acting was. Unfortunately that's the only good thing this game has going on. Every interaction you have doing anything is unnecessary. Every time you pull a switch you press f to interact and then w,a,s,d depending to flip it which just wastes time. The game itself is just a huge waste of time. Buy it on sale just to experience the amazing voice acting.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully sculpted game, top notch voice acting, and smooth as butter gameplay. Only once while swimming up through a hatch did I get stuck, glitched in the floor. A quick checkpoint reload put me back about 15 seconds. Checkpoints are very generous, so repeated deaths aren't bothersome.I always enjoy a game with regular characters; no special powers or unique skills/abilities. Caz is just your average guy with dogged determination in a horrible situation.The game is a puzzler at heart. It never felt overly challenging, especially the parkour. The only times my progress was impeded was due to me turning off the repeated prompts feature, so I didn't recognise the odd interaction that I'd done somewhere else prior. If I could do a first playthrough again, I'd also turn off the yellow paint directional markings for an added challenge.I think the only thing that let it down slightly was the avoidance system. Throwing objects to distract often felt like it wasn't working, or was just not even necessary. The achievement for throwing 50 unique throwables doesn't seem like one you'd ever get naturally. I doubt I picked up even half of that. I started by trying to carry items in case needed, but the crouching, standing, or squeezing through an obstacle automatically drops it, so I gave up quickly. As for hiding in lockers, other than the first time I was prompted to try it, I never had to use it. There was simply never anything near me to even require it.It's not a very long game, but it's pretty polished and an overall, very enjoyable ride. Recommended to use headphones for the ambience. Enjoy :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: ""SPOILERS""WE NEED MORE. this is hands down one the best story driven horrors i have played since "the last of us" one and two. The story and voice acting is amazing and that sense of isolation being stuck on an oil rig in the middle of the ocean really digs deep into your head when playing. Seeing some of the best members die in the story really added a sense of guilt and dread when they couldn't be saved. I'd love to see another game based of Caz's back story, the fight he got involved in and the relationship between his wife and kids. the story touches on this but i would love to see more, and play the story. best horror game i have played so far in 2024. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those occasions I wish there was a "Meh" or "I guess" option.TLDR: Not great not terrible. Worth it for 15 bucks or so. So the game is 60% navigation (which comes down to just "find the closest yellow thing and interact with it") and 40% "Hide from the monster", which is just Alien:Isolation Lite. The monster is dumber and the areas are way scaled down, both in size and complexity. And then towards the end they spice the gameplay up with "find the yellow thing while hiding form monster". The two standout elements are the location (not sure if this is an accurate depiction of an oil platform, but it is certainly beliveable) and the voice acting  - good, thick Scottish accent and expressions, a delight to hear. If you are new to this genre, buy Alien:Isolation instead, which is a much better game for the fraction of the price. If you played all the good games in the ganre and want some more, I guess buy this, but wait for a deep sale - the game is not worth more than 15 bucks or so.

_childDocuments_.review: What a banger of a game. When i first saw this game revealed i thought this was something perfect for my taste if it would be how i'd imagine and here we are, i just played through the game and what can i say, it is exactly how i imagined it to be.Quality is top notch, if it's Graphics design, Audio design or the excellent Path visualizations to keep you in the flow, everything just works well hand in hand to give a spectacular movie like experience.Also here is finally a game again that is very short compared to most games but the more amazing.It's really nice to see all the temporal upsamplers included if it's TSR, XESS, FSR etc. without them i would have played at 20-30fps and massive input lag but with XESS i got pretty much the same experience but with fps locked to 45fps flat on my 1080Ti and 3840x1080p monitor which made the game feel much smoother but noticing almost no visual degradation.The one thing i'd say wasn't all that nice was the amount of quick time events, they are generally very intuitive so they feel very natural which lead me to lock in my buttons for new quick time events before they showed up due to the nature of the task, but the amount of equal quick time events is getting a little repetitive overall i feel.Overall, if you're a fan of horror games with monsters and maybe you liked John Carpenters "The Thing" then this is THE game for you!@TheChineseRoom @Developers @SecretMode awesome Game, you tried something new and you nailed it so thank you for that ! :)

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:Its a beautiful game first of all. My favorite parts of the game is it still keeps everything a mystery and the player knows nothing why. It has some lovecraftian elements obviously, and Im glad they didn't have like some large sea creature come out of the sea end credits, that wouldve ruined it for me. so thank you for not doing that. I love nautical horror, its my favorite next to scifi horror. The oil rig is an amazing setting and I cant beleive it hasnt been done before. To my knowledge. The setting of it all is amazing, the atmosphere and environment is PEAK. The story was great imo, made me a little emotional near the end, some characters felt like they got too easy written off. Scottish people need more in the spotlight. Love em'Did enjoy the subtle hints of madness like the environment looking a bit different than it should.If you love nautical horror, The Thing (1982), Alien Isolation (Not game mechanics, but mood of dread), and never getting answers and leaving it up to the interpretation? This game is for you. I highly enjoyed it.The Bad:You are working on an oil rig that is falling apart, can we please have more creative ways to get past obstacles instead of pulling a lever or flipping a switch. Maybe some more creative alternatives. Also way to many conveniently places boxes or such to stop the player going a certain way. Perhaps some alternate routes to a place would make it feel more freeing to the player. There are enemy encounters but they feel way too easy, it was hard to have anything perceived as a real threat in this game. Felt like our character would've gone mad a long time ago. he was hella resistant. The Ugly:The main enemies you encounter; your fellow crew. I'm sorry, but I think making us more emotionally invested so we feel bad for them. Instead we are clearly given the A-holes and they are the ones that turn. So we don't feel bad for their fate. I think that would affect the player more, bad things happening to good people. Maybe have a moment in the game they seem more human? Maybe about to kill the player but resist their madness, to REALLY show they are still there and don't want to hurt the player but cant resist for much longer. And maybe do it more like alien isolation, the encounters felt way too scripted rather than AI in the game. What I would've changed: -Alternate routes so it doesnt feel so linear- More emotionally Invested into good people turing into beasts- The dead disfigured people maybe moaning, twitching, and etc. Making it feel like the could be the next threat after us. - More creative ways to get past paths or obstacles- Im not particular too fond of madness elements, but for this game I expected it, and was a little disappointed there wasn't much in here. Id make the player question his surroundings or actions. An unreliable narrator. - Maybe a little bit more lore about the company; why that drilling spot was chosen. Mainly wanted to know more about the company itself. Conclusion:The game has amazing atmosphere and story, just think it could've done more to tug at heart strings and madness elements. Story superb, gameplay is good, but it shows it had more potential and didn't. Environment gets the highest rating, I LOVED the environment. great job guys.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the movie The Thing by John Carpenter, then this game is made for you. It is clearly an adaptation on a petrol station in the outskirts of Scotland. The atmosphere is incredibly immersive. You are immersed in an incredible atmosphere !!!Frankly, I recommend it. It makes you drool. It's great, the story is great. Bravo, great game !!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is definitely one of the best games I've played recently. Perhaps the best in the horror genre. Although it is basically a walking simulation, the fantastic atmosphere created in its interesting universe, the best voice acting performance I have seen recently, sound effects, visuals (especially on the body horror side) that regularly manages to give you fear and tension instead of resorting to instant and cheap scares makes this game definitely a praiseworthy job. Body horror aside, creating a Lovecraftian piece of horror is a very difficult and respectful task. Many of the works created in this genre usually turn out to be disappointing, for me at least. I do not need to say that The Chinese Room succeeded it at this point but I want to praise them again because I felt the value and importance and love they attached to their work in every second and part of this short game they made. By the way, this game being short is a good thing. Otherwise it would get boring quite fast due to its repetitive gameplay and I think it ends exactly when it needs to. It does not offer much challenge, it is not hard at all and for horror enthusiasts I can safely say that this is basically like "Entry to Horror 101" but who cares? It is a damn fine game. I highly recommend it to people who are especially into body horror and Lovecraft.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a game!I'm not usually a fan of horror games, I've managed to get through some like The Medium and Alan Wake 2, but others like RE: Village and Alien Isolation were too much for me. However, I do love "walking sims" with great stories (like Firewatch, The Invincible, Edith Finch), and this game delivered exactly that.The setting and atmosphere are superb, and while the core of the story isn't particularly novel, I loved the way the narrative played out, and that was helped by some incredible voice acting and dialogue.On top of that, the attention to detail in the environment is outstanding, the graphics are great, and everything was tied together with a brilliant soundtrack (I’m actually listening to it as I write this).The ending was so impactful that I just sat watching the credits roll. And by doing so I inadvertently saw how many people and how much work went into it. That actually gave me a better appreciation of the high price tag, although I still think €35 is a bit steep for a six-hour game. I picked it up on sale and would recommend others do the same.All in all, this was a very memorable experience. I'm glad I pushed through the horror elements to play it (I think I'll even give Alien Isolation another try now). I’m excited to see what they put out next and I'm looking forward to trying some of their older titles like Everybody’s Gone to the Rapture.

_childDocuments_.review: MEAT! HORROR!It's so strange to play a game that features a mega-structure that I can practically see from my window. Let alone hear familiar accents & language! I only learned after playing it in English that there's a Scottish Gaelic version! Yes!Despite some technical issues getting the game started and the game blasting my computer until the whole thing shut down, after lowering the graphical settings it behaved for (the majority of) the rest of the playtime. I'd suggest lowering the quality a tad just to give yourself the FPS to enjoy your surroundings. I barely noticed the difference between epic & high. Anyway! _childDocuments_.review: This was kind of a running simulator but my goodness the level designs were perfect.   First off, I appreciate them not putting things to find as many games do now days to encourage exploration (and possibly time padding).  It helped keep the flow of the game focused  and I really appreciated that.   It made it way more immersive and enjoyable. I really give them props for having the flow of the player instinctively laid out.   No wondering where to go.   The direction of where to go was laid out perfectly.    May not be for some people as not a challenging game.     It wasn't really scary either as I never was scared of dying that much.   However, it didn't take away from the experience and I really enjoyed it.   The oil rig setting was really cool and I wondered how much it looked like in to an actual one in real life.   Kudos to all those who worked on this.  They did a great job.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate that you can only recommend a game or not, it's really a hard choice with this one. On one hand, at it's heart it's got a decent narrative, has well-detailed environments, is good at creating a feeling of tension, and is above all else superbly voice acted.On the other hand, that decent narrative is stretched really thin - at best, it would make a good single episode of television (probably not even a movie's worth.) It's about four hours, two of my six hours of playtime were a break/pause, and by the end I wanted the game to be over. The walking simulator/exploration became monotonous, and had about three hours of 'oh no the thing you need to do is over here, go here, do this, etc'. Some of the 'monster' designs were more laughable than horrific - think giant-head MODOK from the most recent ant man, with more tentacles and less butt cheeks. Lots of chromatic tentacles/viscera. I wish they had gone in a bit different direction with the monster element, it would make for some good cosmic horror but doesn't quite get there in this game. Some of the 'The Thing' comparisons are apt, at least in tone, but not quite. I would recommend it if it were shorter and cheaper, and wish there was a so/so option which I'd have chosen for this.It's an achievement to make a game at all, so kudos to the developers. Bravo again for the voice acting. Graphically, it was fine - environments were great, character models and lip sync/animations less so, but traversal overall (which is the bulk of the gameplay) was alright. I didn't hit any game breaking bugs, and there was no UE stutter/shader compiling nonsense - it worked. A lot of loading screens for such a small map that reuses areas so many times, but they were brief load times at least. For some reason I also only had High and Epic options for the graphics, and the motion blur was atrocious before some tweaks to the upscalers.The biggest complaint besides the length is the HOW DID THIS GAME RELEASE LIKE THIS bug relating to the subtitles. Yes the scottish accents are thick, but I wanted the subtitles off. Every time you move to a new area, every time you die, every time you even open the page with the subtitle options (even if you're just passing that page to get to the graphical options), the subtitles turn back on. I spent probably 20 minutes of my playthrough turning off the subtitles, which by the way, are not even directly capturing what the spoken dialogue is - they change some of the words for I'm guessing clarity? English with an Accent to English is not a translation that is necessary. Either way I assume (and hope) the subtitle issue will be patched out quickly.It's maybe worth watching an edited playthrough eventually for the story, but in the meantime if you want a similar game I'd go with the Dead Space remake or Calisto Protocol - similar vibes, but cheaper and better overall. (FWIW, I'm also kind of skeptical of some of the glowing reviews that popped up here immediately with early/free copies..)

Excellent sound design and voice acting. In terms of optimization, I played on ultra settings at 1080p with DLSS (DLAA), the game ran at a stable 60 fps, and I didn’t notice any drops.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: There's cheap horror, and then there's this. Still Wakes the Deep is a stunning atmospheric visual experience, and if you're into story-focused psychological horror, definitely pick it up. The well-crafted story paired with excellent voice acting and sound design keeps you immersed and engaged all the way through, and while it's not the scariest game out there, there's a near constant underlying sense of dread that is incredibly effective. It's not littered with cheap jump scares, and the creature encounters are actually chilling. This is probably a good one if you're trying to ease into the horror genre. So yeah, this was horrifying and I loved every second of it.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 The most technically beautiful UE5 game so far, fantastic art design with absolutely stellar environments and character models, with very Cronenberg-like enemies. Gameplay is quite smooth, and a "Story" difficulty is offered if you, like me, don't enjoy the survival horror genre, which significantly eases up on enemy AI in stealth sequences. Controls feel crisp and the traversal punches above its weight class. The story is just enough to move the plot along, with few strong emotional notes, and a satisfying conclusion. For the price and size of the project, it feels more like a 9/10 - if you like cosmological horror, this is certainly worth your purchase, especially at the price it is offered.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: A relatively short, but rewarding horror experience. It's a very Lovecraftian inspired horror game and nothing you haven't seen before in terms of main story, but the writing is very witty and elevates the entire experience. The setting is interesting, the atmosphere is very immersive and there's a few areas that are beautiful in terms of design. I ran into a few bugs and soft-locks that were annoying, but you have a "restart from checkpoint" button that works very and you're given checkpoints frequently.Overall, surprisingly solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! I'm nearly through it all and may come back to update if something life-changing occurs, but this game is one I would recommend 100%. It features well-developed characters, has some great humour at times and is set in a unique environment--an oil rig, which opens the doors for platforming, dark metal corridors, and a very unsettling atmosphere at times. What I really like about this game is that it's actually a horror set in the day, which also gave me a false sense of security at times, but the horror was still very much there regardless of the lighting. It's very forgiving and has great attention to detail with fun achievements that I will definitely collect with a second playthrough! I won't say much on the story as I am not done yet and also don't want to spoil, but I'm greatly enjoying it so far ^-^ Only issue I had was with FPS, but I'm unable to say whether it's just my set-up or the game, so take that with a grain of salt! It improves by lowering the graphics settings anyway :)

_childDocuments_.review: Very engaging story, a few points could have greater clarity, more info about people other than Caz, Suze, and Roy would have been nice so that we could get more attached to them and understand their motivations. i.e. Knowing that Finlay has a child or more about Brodie. The ocean looks fantastic and the 'thing' looks stunning! The  also look great.  design and animation were a bit disapointing in comparison. A few graphical elements seem prone to errors: A lot of the ropes/tethers that are meant to flap in the wind glitch and jitter quite oftenMultiple instances of vibrating or floating chainsLighting and shadow glitches occasionally- especially when entering/emerging from water.Caz's arm and shoulder would occasionally stretch across the cameraNot the most engaging gameplay, but there are a few sequences where it really shines. My biggest issue was that there were multiple instances where I got 'soft locked' due to glitches- this wasn't a big hassle as checkpoints are fairly numerous. I shall list the instances I can remember for reference:Blocked into room by an immovable object in the doorway.Blocked into room by  which was stuck in the door.Character got stuck in a small gap between platforms and was unable to moveCharacter's head got stuck on the 'thing', could not move and screen was covered in the proximity effect which made it harder to realise I was stuck.Upon returning to a checkpoint, quest progress had reverted but I was unable to interact with the item required to progress it again (reloading the checkpoint again automatically progressed the quest to the correct stage)Really great accessibility settings, with a story mode and a normal mode. Subtitle settings are very in depth. I made use of the anti-motion sickness settings which worked wonders. Many other settings were available also, including; colourblind settings, a reaction window slider, closed captioning, and a flashing light toggle.A game with a great, engaging story which is well worth playing. While it does fall short in a few areas, I wouldn't let that put you off. Additionally, if the progress halting glitches I encountered get fixed, I would say that this is a very high quality game!

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen a lot of people give this game flak, and to me it's completely UNwarranted...The game is fantastic for what it is.Amazing voice acting,fantastic scenery,terrifying environments.People are closed minded in using 'linear' (nearly 4 hour game) as a insult clearly are looking in the wrong direction when it comes to a game that they want to play. I think that its linear path is quite refreshing, and that it's about 4 hours is fantastic for people who aren't willing to spend 100+ hours on a game.I have played this 2 times already, once on my own and steam clocked me at '3.8' hours after completion, and the 2nd time was when I streamed it for my mates, and they said they all felt gripped to the story and loved it saying that they felt attached to the characters, even crying when particular ones died. _childDocuments_.review: Looks great, runs great (even at 5160x2160 DLAA + FG) and the immersion from the audio and script is really excellent. As others have said, The Thing in game form. If you like horror in general, then this is s short escape into a game location you've never played before, and likely never will again. A unique experience.It's UE5, so some half decent GPU hardware is needed for the Epic settings, but the steam version has all the upscalers and there's also a mod for FSR3 Frame Gen now for those on non 40 series RTX cards so you can tweak the best performance easily enough now.For ref, my 12700KF and 4090 pull 75fps average without Frame Gen at 5160x2160 DLAA or over 100fps using Frame Gen.  Using DLSS Quality at 1440P is the best experience and you get the higher framerate too for lower cards. You can use DLSS Performance at 4K for equally excellent visuals.There are some menu bugs like subtitles not disabling, and DLSS Quality not remembering (at least for me anyway) but if you're using DLAA or 4K with DLSS Perf, then this isn't an issue anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly I want to say I don't regret my decision to buy this game, although I really think it should be closer to the €20 mark than €35... But I was happy to support a group of indie devs and it definitely does have many redeeming qualities.Starting strong with this one, the environment in this game is pretty amazing to be honest. You're on an oil rig off the east coast of Scotland and it's very well made. I probably stared at the ocean for 15 minutes in total throughout different sections of the game. Hallways feel cramped and the deck feels dangerous. Overall really well done.This is sorta where things start taking a bad turn. You play as Cameron (Caz) McLeary and you're a "leccy" on board this ship. I feel like they tried to give some characterisation to all the characters at the beginning of the game when you go to the canteen for breakfast, but like a lot of things in this game it was very half baked. Dinnae really find myself caring all too much about anyone except for Caz' best friend Roy who's a sweetheart. The best part aboot all these characters however, is how AGGRESSIVELY Scottish they all are. My friend watched me stream a portion of this game and legit had no idea what they were saying at some points even with subtitles, which I found hilarious.And here is where the majority of my issue with this game lies. God where do I begin. It tries to do the whole Amnesia hold to push open the door thing except it doesn't do it on the doors, it does it on the same yellow valves to stop steam every second room you walk into, and they're not even hidden they're literally right in front of you. Some gates have padlocks on them so you hold lmb and d to break it (this probably happened at least 15 times), some ladders require you to pull a lever down (lmb and s) you get what I mean... There's a climbing system in the game except it's also very half baked and mainly consists of hold rmb, hold w, wait for random explosion to make Caz lose his grip, hold lmb until he regains his grip, listen to him say ♥♥♥♥ a few times and move on. Pretty disappointing ngl, no room for creativity or freedom. There's some swimming sections with water rising around you as you try to reach an exit door or the likes but again very half baked, I forgot to mention wherever you go has that typical yellow paint so it's literally impossible to lose unless you go out of your way to try and find something interesting which there never is.The cat and mouse with the monsters boils down to watching them move on a set path and moving from crouch high hole in wall to crouch high hole in wall until you reach your destination, sometimes you might throw a hard hat or a wrench but it genuinely isn't even necessary. The chase sequences are also pretty mid I think I got a little spooked the first time but beyond that they all sorta play out the same. Half baked freezing mechanic (whenever Caz gets cold there's always a heater right in front of you), half baked fire mechanics (there's always a fire extinguisher within 10 meters), half baked attempts at pretending you're the only one doing anything of substance or use (My friend made a great point when he said this game would have worked way better as an Until Dawn style game), just overall very undercooked mechanics and motives with little to no complexity.Couple this with some of my pet peevs in video games in general but especially horror games, ie. a ridiculously slow sprint speed and doors which magically unlock when you complete your objective and yeah, found myself getting kinda tired of it pretty quickly.I would really struggle to give this anything above a 6 to be honest. - Environment- Scottish people being Scottish- Pretty much everything else- The page claims there's "6 hours of amazing gameplay" but I'm sorry I see basically 0 reviews with more than 4 hours of gamplay clocked in and close to an hour of it is spent holding lmb or rmb and a movement direction6.0

_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I won't say much besides that this game, from the horror and scares, to the narrative and acting, to the music and visuals, excels in practically all that it tries to do. Don't expect a twelve-hour-long, game-play focused roller-coaster, but that is not what it is attempting to do, and that does not make it any lesser of an experience. It is easily one of the most riveting story and horror games that I've played in recent memory, and I won't spoil the experience by writing more about it. The rig really feels like an actual place. An intricate place filled with lovecraftian horrors. Likewise the characters are quite human, and thus very relatable, something that's helped along by some excellent voice acting.It also doesn't overstay its welcome, but progresses at a brisk pace, but without feeling rushed. Rather the pacing is just right.Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: The best horror survival experience I have barely emerged from in a long time. I am glad to see that The Chinese Room has persisted for all these years and that they are still making titles in this vein. SWTD is terrifying as much for recreating the sense of being in the midst of an industrial catastrophe as it is for its faithfulness to the Lovecraftian tradition of tentacles from the unknown and the otherness of body horror. The game looks beautiful and the puzzles and problems to solve are engaging and challenging without being frustrating. The voice acting is equal to the strong story. Both serve to add a degree of emotional intimacy which make the characters believable. Considering what happens, the realism of the game is staggering and terrifying. I personally ended up being more scared of the Rig's unstoppable self-destruction than anything else, but the tentacles from beyond and mutant crewmates are fearsome to behold. 4.5 out of 54 out of 49 out of 10A+Highly recommended.Play!
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: A truly beautifully written narrative game. I enjoyed it tremendously, and recommend it to anyone who is interested. It's short but its story, voice acting, and setting make it well worth the heart break of having to let it go too soon. My only wish was that it wouldn't end, because I truly was engrossed throughout the game. It was so good I had to give it a second playthrough right after the first so I could 100% it. Thank you The Chinese Room for this masterpiece, I knew I could trust you after Dear Esther and you certainly have not disappointed me. Good luck in your future endeavors, I will be waiting patiently and with great anticipation.PS Edit (because I forgot): Please, please Chinese Room, patch in the option to remove the yellow markings/paint for objectives and progression. Thank you again.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game that has constant chases this isn't the horror game for you. I originally saw a clip of the monster in this game and was instantly hooked not knowing what it was really about and ended up purchasing it. It starts off getting a little bit of insight on the main character and why he is on the oil rig. Not to get into spoilers so I won't, but this game has many instances where you're constantly in tight spaces, swimming in pitch black water, trying to not drown from said water when it forces you to route out an escape so you can get some air, walk along beams that are high up, and some occasional monster interactions. The only complaint I really had was I wish I could enjoy it longer and with how the ending goes. The ending isn't bad, but before the end credits roll around you realize that the main character could've had his happy ending all along and unfortunately wasn't able to have that. The voice acting I thought was great as well I definitely enjoyed his voice lines and how much this character had to go through. I've read some things saying this isn't for everyone, but I would say just for the story and atmosphere I would rate it a solid 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Canny recommend enough, beautiful & heartbreaking story. A mixture of Annihilation and NOPE (Two movies I adore) but on the open ocean, I'd say. _childDocuments_.review: When I bought the game, I had a different idea of what it would be like. For this reason, the gameplay disapointed me quite a bit and was having a mostly neutral to negative experience throughout. It was only after the end sequence that I had the realization that Still Wakes the Deep is a whole different type of experience and my first impressions towards it were a result of my own lack of understanding of it and its genre. The game is just a vessel to a story, your own actions are secondary. So the right mindset when approaching this title is to have in mind that you are not playing, you are experiencing its events.Granted, even with that being said, the gameplay could be improved exponentially with simple changes as it suffers a lot from simplicity, lack of options, lack of actuall puzzles, too much QTE where you simply press a single button to perform an action and above all of that, the game is crushingly linear and you are not rewarded for exploring. The level design is simple and repetitive. And even for a story based game, that is a big downside since, like I mentioned, minor tweeks and a slightly different approach to the gameplay could result in a big improvement. To summarize all of that, the game is not challenging at all.On top of that, there are a few ridiculous moments, one in particular where the character is unable to open a door, only to recieve a call where the person tells him to kick the door in order to open it. As if you "just unlocked door kick" because someone told you to. At that moment I couldn't help but feel like I was controling a complete idiot. Oh, and you never get to use that again. That one scene is the only moment where you get to kick a door in order to force open it.Another downside is that the game doesn't seem to understand some of its strenghts. The outside area, where you get to experience the oil rig is one of the best settings I've ever seen in a game, and I can safelly say that this is not only my subjective opinion but it's objectively true since it's not something we get to see often in a game and is very original for that matter. Not only for the industrial look and feel but also the fog and the open sea in the distance. The game, however, underutilizes this setting for some reason, and instead, 80% of its runtime is spent indoors, where the environment is just as generic and blend as any other game. The type of environment we've seen a thousand times before. This is a decision that I simply can't understand.With all of that out of the way, it's understandable why I was not having a positive experience. But all of that changed and the game redeemed it self with the final sequence. That was honestly so touching, sincere, emotional, and beautiful that my entire view of the game suddenly switched. It almost brought me to tears and I'm not lying. Not only it was a blast to experience it also changed my understanding of what the game was entirely about and made me feel like I had just experience a true work of art. The dialogs are so well written and the voice acting so magnificent that I actually felt like these were real people.I will most likely not play the game again, but I am for sure going to watch the ending on YouTube many many times again in the future. Congratulations to the amazing team responsible for this production.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: This needs to be said, it is a small experience at least for what I'm used to.But it is a good one, the atmosphere, the voice-acting, the soundtrack, the story itself, pretty beautiful or not I guess you know.But I would recommend waiting for a sale that makes it at least less than 20€ since it is a small game like 5.5 hours for me probably less on average.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only at the point where sh*t is starting to hit the fan, but this is really excellent so far! Wonderful to hear Scottish accents and lingo in such a high production game and the characters seem very fleshed out. Audio presentation is outstanding and really ramps up the tension. Visual presentation is also phenomenal with the material and lighting work being stand-outs.Unfortunately there are some of the typical UE5 performance hallmarks with jittery pacing of frames even when the average frame rate is above 60, the 99% frames will be down to 20-30 sometimes. Hopefully it's something they can sort out. Also it would be great to have a slider for the amount of motion blur as the default UE5 is way too much, but turning it off completely highlights the frame pacing issues.Very minor gripes tho for what is looking like it might be one of my favourite games of this year! Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of games like Everybody's Gone to the Rapture, Gone Home and What Remains of Edith Finch, so when the The Chinese Room announced Still Wakes the Deep, I was completely hooked on the concept. I love the idea of a horror game / story set on an oil rig cut off from the mainland, and the incredible cast, location and sound design combine to create a really immersive experience, albeit a relatively short one. The game is "on rails" a lot of the time, but I really appreciate how the developers had a strict idea of the type of game / story they wanted to tell and executed it perfectly. There is a super high level of authenticity with how the 1970s oil rig is portrayed, and graphically, the game is absolutely stunning. The gameplay leaves much to be desired, but the narrative experience more than makes up for what this game lacks in the actual "game" department. Story 9/10Gameplay 6/10Graphcis 9/10Sound Design 10/10Soundtrack 10/10Overall: 8/10

_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is one of those rare horror games that is 1. Well written 2. Pretty scary in parts and 3. Emotionally resonate. The wheel isn't being reinvented here by any means and in fact the tasks you're completing can get a bit repetitive (probably the games biggest flaw). What you get though is a compelling story that plays out something like The Thing but on an oil rig and everyone's Scottish. There's so much cultural flavor in this game from the Scottish angle of it all that it does add a sort of quirky charm to the whole experience. But that charm is cut HEAVILY by just how bleak and horrific the game is. I think it's well worth 30 bucks and 6 hours of your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good game. I don't whole-heartedly recommend it as I cannot both pickup and carry objects while interacting with doors. It makes things very awkward to have to chuck something I was carrying through a room and then be able to interact with a door.It also has the issue of making you press too many buttons for a given interaction that these sort of games with not a lot of activity going on tend to do. Its like budget QTEs, which are already bad enough on their own for how haulting they can be to a scene. If you don't have gameplay, then don't make me press a bunch of buttons for the sake of keeping my attention. It just halts my immersion to have to figure out which random button you want me to press. The ambiance is good, even if the people's interactions to seeing monsters, psychotic breakdowns, and fleshy masses are somewhat reserved and unbelievable (if I saw a fleshy mass made of my coworkers, I wouldn't just chuff and walk past it like it was a gnarly spider at the zoo). I will revise this review at the end, I hope it improves. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this creation. A game? I wouldn't classify this as a game, more like an experience. The price at max should have been 24.99. You will experience this story in around 3-6 hours depending on the individual.Pros: +Setting - I liked the setting, minus the layout. +Plot - The story pulls you in well enough to keep you going out of curiosity. +Voice Acting - Honestly this is where Still Wakes the Deep shines! +Visuals - Recommend playing @4K with the best settings. Cons:-Pacing - Things move quickly in the first 10 mins, but slows down to an abysmal crawl. -Ending - All that for nothing! -Design - Lord almighty i've never been so annoyed. Conclusion:It's a walking sim, plain and simple. Play this once, enjoy the story. Honestly though, this became so tedious to play. The design of the Oil Rig after about 40 mins drove me crazy. By the end of the game I was begging for it to be over. With every path you must follow there is something painted yellow, even still with that I spent at least an hours worth of time just trying to find where to go next. Don't get me started on the swimming. I know people with no legs that walk/run/swim faster and smoother than this character does. Jesus! Everything you do, you get the same exact animation with no variation at all. I mean a small and simple detail like that could have made this a better experience. We spend the majority of the game looking at everything, you didn't think we'd notice the copy + paste animations. Honestly, if it wasn't for all the nonsense of the mechanics & design, you could finish this game in about a hour and a half. It's not bad, but it's not good either. Wait for this to be on sale under $20.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: If I push all the way through a horror game it means I really liked it.Still Wakes the Deep takes the best things from the Amnesia-games and Alien Isolation and combines it into a neat, compact game that is dense with detail, real good checkpoints, stunning visuals and top notch sound design... AND a good story. on top you have f-bomb-dropping scottsmen - what is not to like?If you like body horror like "The Thing" or "Virus" and the dread of being defenseless and only being able to run & hide, then you will like this.it is rather short so maybe consider this when buying. average is supposedly 5-ish hours.

But it is priced as a AAA game. Pick it up in 6 months when it is on 75% sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know where to begin, everything about this game has me stunned.I've never bothered writing a review on steam as i haven't come across a game that pushed me to take the time and post.But this is it.The story line, artwork, characters, soundtrack, soundfx, voice & acting, the SUSPENSE, I don't have a single issue or even a negative point with the game.
