_childDocuments_.review: Real cool UE5 horror game, with the right amount of suspense and action. Altough it is very linear, i never really felt bored, because the oil rig is constantly changing and you revisit some places.What really stands out in this game are the voice actors. The voice acting in scottish (i presume, i had to use the subtitles because i didn't understand everything) is absolutely fantastic and makes the game more than worth it, because you really feel immersed to the maximum. I also liked the monster design.My only gripe with it is, that i wish it was longer and i could see more of the various lovecraftian horror. The ending makes absolutely sense and is kind of beautiful, but i just wish there was more.But that's the thing with lovecraftian horror. If there are a lot of explanations, you understand everything and theres a typical hero, it isn't really lovecraftian horror. The charm comes from just accepting that there are things, that are better left unexplored.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game and Voice Acting. The "infection" is horrifying to look at, along with what it does to the people sadly consumed by it. short and simple, environment looks incredible, really loved the entire oil rig thing. The atmosphere throughout the game was superb in my eyes. The moments of claustrophobia in tight spaces, chases and all of the above made this game feel so very real. _childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lot more moving than I expected. The memorable characters are well written. Let's break down the experience (but spoiler-free!):Still Wakes the Deep is a glorified walking simulator (there is even an achievement by the same name). There is no combat, no inventory, no chapter select. It's a very straight-forward experience. I don't find these to be cons. I think the notion that you can't fight your way out of a pinch adds to the horror survival aspect. It also cements the fact that you're just a regular guy. An electrician. That said, the game is very forgiving even on the "normal" difficulty. The QTEs aren't hard at all, and it's overall easy to navigate your way through the rig, even if you change the settings to limit things like yellow paint, and button markers.The game is 4-6 hours for those who're just looking to get through it, and 6+ hours if you're trying to 100% it. You can completely 100% it in one playthrough, but I wouldn't recommend it as one of the achievements require you to play it in Scottish Gaelic. The language will still be in English, but the UI, menus and so on will be in Gaelic. I personally recommend a blind run at first, and a quick clean up afterwards. The good thing is that certain multi-step/collectable achievements carry over.I was impressed to see a game with true Scottish Gaelic, and an overall good horror experience, and emotional story. I definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: This could have been John Carpenter's "The Thing" on an oil rig, but the horror beyond space and time is overshadowed by the main character's regret over his poor life choices, which makes sense; your agency is a breadcrumb trail of slathered yellow paint leading you all the way to a climax with zero payoff.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I will go with a negative review on this one, I truly was looking forward to play this but...overall it was an average game which i lean more into the negative review instead of the positive. If steam had a middle option that would be my pick.Strong points of this game is the good visuals and the great voice acting.Not scary by any means, just freaky especially when the story begun to uncover. Then it became a bit repetitive and i dare to say boring. Go there and do this grab that and fix this type of gameplay, hide from the monsters and throw an item to momentarily sneak away, you get the idea, that's the entire gameplay.I enjoyed the voice acting way more than the game it self is all I will say.I encountered three times some wierd glitches that soft locked me momentarily from proceeding the story further and required from me to reload the checkpoint. In all of these three times it took me quite a while to realise that im facing a soft lock glitch so I lost quite some time going back end forth until I figure out that i need to reload those checkpoints, so the game has some technical issues. I finished the game in under 5 hours despite that issues. Price is questionable,maybe arround the 14.99 range would be an ok one time experience,so better wait to grab it on a sale. I really don't see my self replaying this title again.Pros: 1)Great voice acting👍          2)Good visuals          3)At times very good ambient and             inviromental soundsCons: 1)The game starts strong and fall off              really fast.          2)Boring gameplay.          3)Some soft lock glitches in my case          4)Really repetitive game after a              while that made those 4+hours to              feel like i was playing way more          5)Boring story that made zero sense               in the end.I would recommend this title only on a sale at 10-15 bucks for a 1 time experience then uninstall and forget.The only memorable thing on this game is the voice acting.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time lover of games of The Chinese Room, picking this up the same day as realising they released another game had me approaching it with a lot of excitement and expectation. For the most part, it met it. Characters, voice acting and setting were all superb, really going well at building an immersive environment and a set of characters I can really believe in listening too, similar to Everybody's Gone to the Rapture.Enough eerie and creepy moments happen to keep an intensity up, with the only annoying spots being a few issues I had with how the platform-like elements handled, and getting myself through some of the story points. Not up there just as high as previous work, but still a fun romp and worth a look if you like their previous stuff, with having a bit more action this time.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Ok yeah, I just liked this one. The scenery was cool, the game was pretty, and some of the mechanics just felt really fun. There are parts where you need to hide which weren't my favorite, though I didn't play around with it too much to find out more tbh..  The story isn't super original either; you'll find it relates to other media like The Thing or Annihilation - You've probably seen this story before is all I'm sayin. _childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Came here looking for a similar experience after A Quiet Place and I'm glad I found this. I haven't even seen a monster yet and this is way scarier lol. I found a comfort in the blindness of the quiet place monster. I find no such comforts here! It doesn't help that you get a tutorial popup "Press x to look behind you", indicating that you should be looking behind you now? Scary af lolThe graphics are way better here as well, seemingly. This game lets you use DLAA Character models look great, the acting is great too. Nice to hear a different accent than what we usually get.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, it's short. It's linear. The puzzles are barely there. It has almost zero replayability. However, the setting, acting, story and pacing are all so good that I don't regret buying the game. Even for someone like me who is a wimp when it comes to horror games, there's that "I'll just get to the next section" pull that saw me actually finish it. The horror sequences are mostly laid out in such a way that you can get through them first try if you think them through and don't do anything dumb. A couple of sections need a tweak though; I died a bunch of times due to one stealth part requiring a lot of trial and error, and a later swimming section saw me fighting the controls more than I'd like, but it's mostly fair.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game, great storytelling with a very captivating narrative that will keep you immersed for some time. The characters have a lot of depth and it's easy to get invested. The horror was never made cliche with too many jumpscares, the missable phone calls of desperation were honestly a nice touch to make you believe the madness was actually happening. The only drawback is the game is a bit short, I would love to see more put out by the developers. The price tag may be a bit high for some but keep in mind you are paying for an immersive experience. Even in the short time of play I still felt like I got my value due to how much enjoyment I had. Keep making games like this guys, it shows you cared about what you made.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: "Still Wakes the Deep" is an atmospheric horror game that immerses players in a haunting and claustrophobic environment. Set on an offshore oil rig, the game masterfully combines tension-filled exploration with eerie sound design and unsettling visuals. The narrative unfolds slowly, building a sense of dread as you uncover the mysteries lurking within the rig. While the pacing may be slow for some, it enhances the overall experience, making every moment of terror feel earned. Fans of psychological horror will appreciate the game's ability to create fear through atmosphere rather than cheap scares.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really good. The unique setting was really refreshing. The horror and atmosphere were terrifying. I'm so glad they had an easy difficulty or I just wouldn't have been able to do it. Every horror game should have a wimp mode. I do wish it had a little more interactivity like small puzzles to break up the platforming and stealth/chase sections. That's my only grief with it. Perfect length for the experience as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: This was a well crafted video game with a strong framework. The horror element was good but didn't over stay it's welcome (Never explain your Lovecraftian horror, I say). The voice acting was on point and the story telling never gave me a reason to roll my eyes. During my play through I never ran into a glitch that took me away from the experience so kudos to the dev teams for that one (Name a game you can say that about now and days). This is not a challenging game and my playtime ended up around four and half hours which I appreciated as well. _childDocuments_.review: Good horror games are difficult to make. "Still Wakes the Deep" is certainly one of them!After a mysterious accident on an oil rig in the middle of nowhere, it's now up to you to find the rest of your crew - and escape this nightmare. "Still Wakes the Deep" is a story of survival, but by no means a survival game. Level design is strictly linear, and game mechanics barely extend beyond movement and object interaction. Quick events will occasionally test your reaction time, picking up and throwing items as distraction is as complex as it gets. No fighting, no inventory, no HUD. The focus is always on you and your surroundings, your experience.But damn, what an experience it is! With its exceptional quality in graphics and sound, "Still Wakes the Deep" is able to create a feeling of realism and immersion, tension and fear - and ultimately horror - that is unmatched.Whether you make your way through abandoned crew quarters, flooded machine rooms, or destroyed maintanance areas, environments are packed with detail. Textures look super realistic, often used and worn down. Lighting is on point, accentuated, rich in contrast. Your flashlight may certainly be helpful in darker areas, but it'll never reveal enough. Water effects, from the wild ocean to heavy rain puring down to rain drops collecting on windows, consistently impress. Having to dive into muddy waters or escape raising water levels is definitely something else. Adding to the immersion, your actions are fully animated, from rotating valves to opening vents to picking up phones.Then there's that constant creaking and rattling of the oil rig. The heavy waves crushing against the legs. The unnverving screams in the distance. The sound of your footsteps, your breathing and groaning, your swearing. The mysterious and unsettling music in the background. In "Still Wakes the Deep", sound plays a significant role in conveying fragility, a place on the brink of collapse - and a place of danger.And damn, you gotta be charmed by the unique scottish flair of "Still Wakes the Deep", from the setting to the soundtrack to the absolutely brilliant voice acting (subtitles recommended).I do recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Very short for the price (I spent at least an hour of my playtime not actually playing), but on the whole a high quality experience with horror elements and some subtle but distinct mechanics, most of which are well done, such as flashlight flickering and fading when pointed at monsters, meaning you never really get a good look at just what is hunting you, the ability to look behind you when fleeing so you can appreciate the drama of the situation instead of just hearing crashing noises behind you, and a parkour system which, whilst limited (the game is linear after all) does help sell the tension of the situation as you deal with death-defying situations.I wouldn't say it's a particularly good pure horror experience though, as it lacks enough openness to feel like failure is likely. Monsters are easily distracted in the same manner every time, so getting caught is unlikely during stealth sections. During chase sequences the game feels tense but not terrifying as the game is so linear there's no real risk of getting in an unwinnable situation, just hold the sprint button and point face in direction away from enemy.Story good, gameplay okay, sound design and visual design excellent (except for a few minor continuity errors where the devs either forgot or failed to realise you could see them). My only real story criticism is there's no real "aftermath" sequence where the outcome of the events of the game can be seen from an external perspective which would help put the events into context.

_childDocuments_.review: Short experience that you can enjoy on a weekend afternoon. Here is a short list of likes and dislikes in my opinion:Likes:-> There is no denying the game looks beautiful and you can see that care was put into the design to make it feel like a logical map and layout. Textures are crisp.-> Lighting was really good and the flashlight effect really sold the horror in some dark areas.-> Unique setting for a game like this. Felt like a breath of fresh air.-> Characters were modelled excellently and the voice acting was superb. I really enjoyed the banter between characters and the Scottish accents. A small elaboration on this point: Sometimes in horror games humour is used in dialog but can feel out of place due to the situation that is unfolding. I felt that these characters however had realistic dialog and always acted in a somewhat believable manner.-> The game does not have a lot of mechanics which is fine for this type of experience as the game does not overstay it's welcome at all. If the game was longer then I would have had a problem about the simplistic controls and traversal.-> the body horror was pretty cool and some set pieces in rooms were excellent. I however did not find the designs to be very scary. It is perfectly fine for this game but still feel that few games did body horror as good as deadspace.-> No major technical issues which is very much appreciated. I found one or two visual bugs but nothing game breaking and performance was solid.Dislikes:-> My dislikes are more aimed at the story than the game play. The concept of this game is really cool and unique but I felt they could have done a lot more with it. For instance the lead up to the "event" was really quick and felt rushed. Here I actually would have enjoyed a level where you just did a day of work on the rig and met more characters than the ones in the canteen. Also I felt somewhat disappointed that that you did not experience anything under the waves and ocean beneath the rig. I would have loved a section where you had to go down in one of those diving pods beneath the rig.-> My personal biggest complaint about the story is at the end of a casual play through I still did not understand the "horror" entity. Overall still highly recommended if you like short horror experiences as well as eldritch and body horror genres. I also got the game on sale which makes it more worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had a nickel for every time a body horror story on a oil rig and the man sacrifices himself for his wife and daughter, I'd have two nickels. Which isn't a lot, but it's weird that it happened twice. A game like this depends on the writing. Unfortunately, it's not very good. The prose is fantastic, but the plot and themes are a mess. There's no subtlety, and the writer makes sure hit you over the head with their metaphors. Dear horror writers, you do not need to tie a personal metaphor to your story. It's not all negative, I do like that the alien was never explained and so much research was done to make it feel like you are actually on the rig. I'm also sick of stories about how a man has relationship issues and sacrifices his life to prove his love for his family.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to write a negative review of a game so much work went into. [Edit: so I'll call this a neutral review, particularly with the devs so responsive.] The 1970s industrial style was cool, the setting was novel, the story was well-written though not particularly engaging for me. The voice acting was good except that the protagonist didn't sound nearly as scared as he should have been in a lot of situations. The music was apropos, though I won't be humming it to myself going forward. Although the Police song Synchronicity II went through  my head the entire time I was playing it. (Now, that's a trippy music video.)But, this game was  a 5-hour experience for the price of a 20+ hour experience, even on sale. Replayability is low because the game is mostly on rails and once you know what's going to happen, I just don't see the point. The monsters were annoying but not very interesting to me. There was no point at which I was scared, although the only game that ever scared me was Outlast, so maybe that's just me. The gameplay is a combination of walking/running like hell simulator, light parkour, very basic stealth, and some weird extra keybinds for gripping ladders and clinging to things that of course you would cling to regardless.I could say that I wish it were longer, but I actually wouldn't have enjoyed 15 more hours of it. Still, it's nice to see something different. In general, and from this developer, most of whose other games I've also played.

_childDocuments_.review: This Horror Game Hits DifferentI really liked this. The setting itself is awesome. The oil rig looks (to my untrained eye anyway) very authentic and really adds to the game, it is a truly great setting for a horror game. In fact, even before things go wrong it's a great setting to have a walk around in. Not many of us will ever experience being on a working oil rig. It is super cool to walk around in. The characters and the voice acting are great too and very authentically Scottish. The language on display here might be more horrifying than the actual horror content, these rig workers do not hold back and their authenticity grounds the game and location really well. This helps the plot too as I really did root for some of these people to survive... others not so much, some people are just meant to be food lol.The story is actually one of the very (very) few I've been able to properly follow in a modern game, partly due to the runtime (just over 5 hours for me) and partly to the story not doing anything stupid, it all flows very nicely and everything makes sense, in a horror context anyway.This game is different to other horror games, this has a class and an integrity to it somehow. This is a really nice, very well made piece of gaming right here, well done to the hardworking and talented devs at The Chinese Room.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I write anything, I just want to say up front, that even though my review is negative overall, I don't do it lightly and it does not mean that this game is a 100% no-no from me. It has plenty of positives and many subjective matters, so please feel free to read more for more details and of course consider opinions of others.I really wanted to love this game, I saw some youtubers praising it, I was all the awards and grades on the steam store page, I love the lovecraftian themes and cosmic horror - this game had all the things going for it to be one of my favorites. I immediately decided to buy and play it. And I was really torn between adoration and confusion.First of all lets take obvious out of the way - the game is gorgeous! Visuals are amazing, the setting is very interesting and not commonly seen (atleast for me), a lot of work and love was put into the environment and a thought out layout of the rig. The atmosphere, the rain droplets on the window, the wind and the shiny oil, it all looks just stunning. The voice acting is second to none. The authentic accents give the game so much character and authenticity, even though I am not a native English speaker and it would be hard for me to understand everything without subtitles, I am glad that it was done that way. Makes it all feel so much more real. The overall development and pacing of the story feels nice, the environment gradually changes, everything that can go wrong does go wrong and the game has some nice surprises. But also this is where one of my main issue with the game begins.While being really well paced the game is also extremely short. I finished my first run at about 7.5 hours, and I was going out of my way to read everything, listen to everything, soak in the atmosphere of every room. Someone who would want to just breeze through the game would do it in less then 5 hours. Short and sweet is not a problem in and of itself, but considering the price of the game, which is 35USD at the time of writing, it is a lot to ask for 5-6 hours experience, which is also worsen by following points.Some of the things from gameplay standpoint feel not very polished and sometimes straight up buggy. While I have not encountered anything gamebraking, I had couple of just annoying and immersion-braking issues. The worst offenders are some of the bosses. Not to spoil anything, their movement and their limbs feel very buggy at times, several times one of them got stuck in some corner giving me and easy pass. Many character animations feel jittery and abrupt, especially when transitioning between jumping and climbing, and some throwable objects just get stuck in tight spaces so I have to restart from the checkpoint. Nothing is too crazy, but considering that the game is that short, it is a shame that it is not more polished from that perspective.Another thing is more a result of a general trope of horror games, but it is still annoying as ever. Many time you will see barricaded doors and passages that are magically opened after a cutscene, many way too convenient accidents, some trivial looking obstacles are impassible and some much more imposing ones are easily completed because they are marked with yellow paint (which to be fair can be disabled). At one moment the game teaches you that you can kick the locked gate open, but it never used in a gameplay ever again. Considering how much effort was put into creating the rig and all the attention to details, such moments feel really strange and videogamy.Being so short does not help the story either, in some cases. There are a lot of characters. A lot. And they all have names and some feelings to them. But the game does not let you get to know them very well. You just briefly get a chance to see some of them during the intro, and after that you mostly hear them on the phone or hear about them from other character. The only problem is that you have no chance to remember who is who and who has what name. It is very confusing that game keeps repeating their names to you but you had no time to attach the face or a character to that name. This is a real missed opportunity. Only couple of characters can be remembered, and only because you interact with them throughout the game constantly.The story is a very subjective matter. What I can say is that it is a very personal story but not very deep or very detailed, a lot of it left to imagination, a lot of it is needed to be read between the lines. Don't expect much explanation to what is going on. It is more about the journey of a character. I will leave it for you to decide if it is a good or a bad.The gameplay is also subjective. I am not a hardcore horror game player and it was ok for me, game does not rely on too many jumpscares, "boss" encounters do not happen too often (considering game's runtime) and they are on the easier side, but it is not a bad thing for me, Many more experienced and hardcore players will probably find the experience lacking, but it was quite nice for me.In conclusion, I want to say that unfortunately I can't recommend this game with clear conscience. It is not a single issue, it is just a lot of small problems and details adding up together to be too much. If it would be a cheaper game I would definitely recommend it, but considering it's price, runtime, and combination of issues I have to do the "thumbs down".

_childDocuments_.review: My personal review of this game, I am not afiliated and didn't received this game for free.“Still Wakes The Deep” by The Chinese Room is a captivating psyhological experience that takes players on a thrilling journey of events through a collapsing oil rig, witnessing an unknown horror that emerges.The game features a closed environment world, you need to navigate through darker corridors, rooms filled with horror events and a gives you a thrilling vibe that will make you immersed.Visually, “Still Wakes the Deep" is simply stunning and was developed in Unreal Engine 5. The lighting system is something that I fell in love with from the beginning, lights are simply amazing and enriches the horror experience overall. In some areas I actually turned off my flashlight, just to experience the overall stunning illumination.The sound complements the gameplay perfectly, enhancing the overall immersive experience and aligns with the vibe making you feel you are actually there.The story follows an electrician named Cameron "Caz" McLeary who is trapped on a damaged oil drilling platform in the North Sea in 1975, having no ways to escape while being pursued by a mysterious monster under harsh weather conditions.Although at the time I am writing this review, I merely have a couple of hours of gameplay, with no doubt I can say that this game is a perfect thrill for any horror fan out there.Overall, “Still Wakes The Deep" is a must-play for fans of horror games and not only, offering an unforgettable experience with an interesting vibe. This game actually reminds me of SOMA and if you liked that game, you will like this one as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great visuals, great voice acting, great dialogue, but that's about it. The actual gameplay and plot of this game, which I consider to be the most important aspects, are borderline nonexistent.The game is so linear you're functionally traveling through a tunnel for the entire game, there are no elements of exploration. Early on the game teaches you that you can hide in a locker and then it's never needed because the couple of stealth sections are so thin and quick that there's no point. It introduces a heater mechanic and then that is pointless as well.You know everything about the plot in the first 30 minutes of the game, and there is no character or narrative development past that point. You just get told to go to the next destination and flip the next switch for 5 hours and then the game is done.Any aspects of horror are also incredibly weak. _childDocuments_.review: Updated after completion:Aesthetically, Still Wakes the Deep is like the book version of Annihilation; so it's like a cross between the movie adaption of that book and John Carpenter's The Thing. It's gorgeously horrific and they did an amazing job with that.Also, the game is set on a Scottish oil rig with a full cast of Scottish characters that are very well voice-acted, which really helped the personality of the game stand out. There's even an achievement for playing the game in Scottish Gaelic, which I'll do on an eventual replay.The game is mostly a character-focused atmospheric horror walking sim. It follows the typical horror story formula, where the main character's fight against the external threat is a metaphor for his own internal struggle (Caz's selfish, juvenile behavior killing his marriage). So the story follows him trying to save himself while simultaneously learning that he needs to change as a person to save what matters to him. There's nothing too notable about the story; it's pretty straightforward, although all the characters are engaging and I never found myself hearing/reading a name and wondering "who was that again?" like I do in many games. I personally would have liked a higher emphasis on the mind-altering affects of the entity, Lovecraft-style, but I think the devs wanted to stick with the human story more-so than the alien one.The gameplay itself doesn't do anything especially original. It's your standard "use the monkey bars to cross the broken walkway, then shimmy along the ledge", "find the valve to shut off the steam to get through the corridor", or "throw the can to the corner of the room to distract the monster while you sneak past" but I didn't find anything too tedious or confusing. There's enough punchy moments to keep you engaged, even if you don't really have to exercise your brain to solve any problem. It's more about making you feel engaged in the moment and story than making you solve some unrealistic convoluted puzzle. I didn't mind the simplicity in this area.If I had any gripes here, it's that the actual horror sneaking scenes were too simple and easy. I think some small level re-design could have made these activities much riskier and therefore more visceral and engaging. Even just removing every other safe spot on a route would have helped. I really didn't feel much threat during those levels.One thing I surprisingly liked was that THERE ARE NO COLLECTIBLES! I didn't realize until this game how distracting it is to be constantly searching behind every box and under every bed for a secret shiny to read. This allowed me to focus on the environmental storytelling. Some people may not like the absence of secondary objectives, but I felt much more immersed without them. And since the atmosphere, characters, and monsters are what make this title stand out, I'm glad they stuck to the core objectives. There are still notes and other things to read, but they're just for atmosphere, such as the dart tournament bracket sheet in the rec room near the beginning of the game, but there's no "4/10 notes found!" popups or anything.I recommend going into the game options and reducing the environmental hints. The game is linear enough and hopefully the change will have that same effect as the lack of collectibles, where now you're looking around for a way to go rather than scanning for yellow stains. And plenty of path markers remain yellow on the reduced mode anyway.Lastly, this is just an aside, but I'm still not sure what's up with those heaters you have to use sometimes. There's only a few in the game, but you can't progress until you've warmed yourself up at one. It feels like some cut content, where they either intended them to be your save/rest areas (there's too few of them for that) or they initially wanted to add the challenge of making you freeze if you didn't warm up fast enough (you won't). They just seem oddly out of place as it is.Tl;dr It's a great Scottish horror walking sim. Some of the best monster design and environmental storytelling I've ever seen, especially if you're a big fan of movies like The Thing, and the human characters were better than in most horror games. Don't expect anything too original from the gameplay itself; it's a story game first and foremost, but a pretty good one.

_childDocuments_.review: ➕ It's The Chinese Room - so the VA direction is stellar as always!➕ The visuals and overall look of the game looks great, definitely a glow up for the developer!🟣 Short length, around 4 hours.🟣 Does feature enemy encounters, even though there aren't that many of them and they aren't that complex.🟣 The writing does work at some level but keep your expectations low,.🟣 As of patch 1.2 it's relatively stable experience without many bugs present.➖ Overall rhythm and feeling of engagement, especially from the story perspective, slows down to a hault half through the game compared to pretty strong introduction section. You might start feeling exhausted from the lack of breathing room between somber atmosphere sections that the gameplay throws at you. Really linear experience.➖ Lots of gameplay padding with underwater swimming sections, valve shutting, fuse swapping, ladder climbing and vent crawling. Overall the gameplay is full of inoffensive short set pieces that don't really do much for the player, it's shallow but it doesn't want you to think it is. It's really cute that each level contains a map for the place but after 2 hours you'd start to ignore it, since the path is marked with bright yellow elements that always leads to the objective.I can't recommend it nor do i hate it that much and the price does bite the wallet a bit. It's an underwhelmingly safe experience with a strong opening section.

_childDocuments_.review: Bit of a mixed bag, but all in all a very solid horror walking (and running, and swimming, and desperately holding on) sim. More exciting than their previous work, with absolutely top-notch atmosphere and acting.Cons? The third fourth of the game really does start to drag - you wind up doing a bunch of maintenance tasks in a row and it starts to feel like you're just going about your day on the rig, doing some more busy work while cosmic horror inconveniences you.The story also didn't land as well with me as it did with others - halfway through I was loving it, and actually said to myself "thank god they aren't doing a ham-fisted emotional character arc and are leaving this guy's backstory as quality set dressing as the horror unfolds." Then by the end they have gone full-blown morality tale, dude's actually  So that was a bit of a letdown, and really did wind up spoiling the great Industrial Accident atmosphere and theming they had going at the start.Last point on the death of Regardless, it's strong points are still very strong. 7/10 above average horror game from someone who doesn't usually like them. Had the potential to be a 9/10 if it was shorter with some different writing beats, but that's life.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always wanted to play an horror game set in an oil rig, something about being isolated in a critical situation. Still Wakes the Deep is a strong narrative driven game where you are a blue collar electrician, stuck in such a nightmare scenario where you go around trying to find survivors and of course, escape!This game has many interesting settings mixed into one, where you can find strong inspirations coming from the movies "The Thing", "The Blob", "Leviathan", "Underwater" and even a non-horror one, "Deepwater Horizon" for the catastrophe of the oil rig.SWTD is mainly a walking simulator and it has a few interactions to be had, like flipping switches and turning valves. You have many "run for your life" escape sequences and hide from monsters situations. The visuals, sounds and voice acting are all spot on very good. The oil rig itself was impressive looking and a treat to explore when you can that is.The game is VERY linear but you do have some opportunities to explore a bit but not enough in my opinion. I found the catastrophe happening too fast and I wish you could had done some more "blue collar" work around with the other oil rig crew but it is not the case.The story is minimal since you don't know much WHAT is causing the catastrophe besides some strange otherwordly "skin filaments" hanging everywhere. I wish you could get to know more about the origins of the "entity/ies" but again, story is minimally explained.Game works very well for Ultrawide screen but as of now, it doesn't have a FOV option and at times, the in-game view is a tad too close. No bugs or technical issues encountered in my playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Listen,I really like the game. I do. I think the premise is quite unique; you can see the foundations upon which the story, creature, and visuals have been lovingly built, while retaining a very unique personality. The characters are very endearing, due in great part to the voice actors. Unfortunately I found the gameplay a little repetitive at times, and possibly buggy? Which made it drag by the third act, which is a shame, because this is also where the art direction truly shines, and the character relationships become ever so ripe for exploration. The ending feels... almost like a betrayal to the themes of the story that made us connect so deeply with the characters and root for them. Undeserved tragedy, unearned nihilism, that felt familiar coming from the studio but maybe disconnected from this particular story. The Chas I was told about and the one I witnessed helping his comrades were completely different, and though my stay with him was brief, he as a protagonist utterly convinced me he was deserving of a more layered finale.TLDR I think the game is worth experiencing, though maybe not playing. Watching it or getting it on sale is much recommended; ending is a Little Flat. :/

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game from The Chinese Room. Still Wakes the Deep is probably the best survival horror that I have played. It certainly has the best depth of characterisation and story. The location, a dilapidated oil rig, is unique and a great choice. The rig drills through something it shouldn't have in the deeps. A creature, enormous and multi-hued, begins destroying the rig. It has multi-coloured tendrils and stretches up from the sea floor to overwhelm the structure. The workers who are caught by it are transformed into horrific, bloated body horrors. You are one of the few survivors. You manage to work with others to try to save yourselves by saving the rig. As the game goes on, the entity takes over more and more of the rig and destroys more and more of your friends. The level design is excellent. The graphics are also outstanding, as is the sound and voice acting. And again, the script is great, especially for a horror title. I strongly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game. Streamed the entire story in 1 sitting. The story was entertaining, the visuals and environment were fantastic. Audio was on-point too.Only real complaints I had were:First, the game is rather short for the price. 4-5 hours and that's with quite a lot of messing around and dying.Secondly, it would be nice if you could turn off the Yellow for the game. It marks every single path you have to take through the entire story with yellow tape, lights or paint so you have to really try to get lost and even then, it's mostly linear so you can't go far. But if we could disable the Yellow help lines, it would add a bit of a challenge, especially during the "chase" sequences. It leaves no mystery as to where to go to navigate the rig.Lastly, Not so much a complaint as it was just an annoyance. But in a game where everyone is telling you "Hurry, you have to get to blah-blah or we're all going to die" and "The place is falling apart, get to the such-and-such as fast as you can", and then proceeds to have dialogue with characters for 5-10 minutes of just filler, took me out of the panic for time mode. I ended up skipping more and more dialogue sequences as the game went on because listening to someone yammer on for 10 minutes after they tell me how much of a hurry I need to be, made me care less for the characters and not feel rushed at all. "With my dying breath, I'm going to talk to you for 20 minutes about nothing, make you think I died 3 times, while I continue to talk, and the entire place is on fire and falling apart around you....but please hurry!" lolThe last 2 were more personal preference than anything. But I did enjoy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is a really good and satisfying "Eldritch-Bodyhorror-Type" Game which is worth your time if you havent played it.Story 5/5The Story is really good, it is written so well and especially through the end it picks up and gets really emotional and engageing with it really catching your feelings. The Intro of the game helps so much because it sells the different characters to you, you will go "Oh man I talked with that guy before" or "No no no not him/her" many times and thats all because of the immersive intro. The Voiceacting is really great, Emotions and intentions of the characters are so clear because of this, you really feel emeressed and engaged throughout the 4 hours of Gameplay. The Voiceacting of the monsters is so good, from the pleading for help to the screaching and moaning. It gets so uncomfortable sometimes because you most of the time hear the entitys before seeing them. Graphics 4/5The monsters and the rig are really well made, getting you emeressed and creeped out with a feeling of dread. Beatuiful sceneary mixed with grey - almost hopeless looking - Graphics really sell the game and what it wants to create. I recommend playing with "film grain" on as it sells this dirty old 1975 look even more.Gameplay 3/5This is the biggest flaw of the game. Sometimes jumps or events really felt sluggish and not coordinated. This gets frustrateing sometimes but I can look over it for the most part. The swimming feels really bad, slow and all around just no polished. I sometimes felt like my inputs didnt do anything as the character barely moves underwater. The Controlls are the biggest weakpoint of the game.But the Horror, oh my the Horror. It is not in your face, it dosent need jumpscares to be scary. It just used these eldritch and deformed beings, you get really uncomfortable and start feeling the dread as you see one of the monsters. The story also gets really uncanny as u just feel hopeless throughout the whole game. This game is really good, it is worth the money and worth the time. If you have 4 hours to spare then please give this game a try.3,5/5

_childDocuments_.review: This game was absolutely BEAUTIFULLY done. The score, the visuals, the characters, the acting & the enemy design were all amazing. I do think it's worth the money, simply because of the amount of heart you can tell was poured into this game on all aspects. Big thank you to everyone involved, I absolutely adored this!

_childDocuments_.review: As with all Chinese Room games I've played the story telling is immaculate. Visuals, voice acting and sound are most impressive. Controls are a bit finnicky and could be smoother, especially during swimming sections. At times you had to find the exact spot in which a button prompt would enable and to do that under stress of drowning was true horror, my goodness gracious, I almost quit out. At a point or two I also got caught on seams in the environment and had to jump over them, if you're too fast you may start talking over yourself having triggered 2 voice lines simultaniously, and once I got into an seemingly infinite death loop, but the game sorted that out itself thankfully (well coded, ty, devs). There are also a great deal of accessibility option aside from all other standard options. I am unsure about the FPS cap though.The murky waters here with oil ontop are the true highlight to me, immensely terrifying.I appreciate the realistic details, such as going down on all four to traverse beams, as any sane person would in real life. None of this idiotic balancing on 2 legs when your life depends on it. That you also have to warm up on heaters after being submerged in ice cold water, thank you, you don't survive those temperatures for long. The banter between crew mates was fun too and added much life to the story.It's really really good existential horror. Walking sim, I don't agree. I got turned around some, especially in water, and so you can actually get lost, if only for a short while, even though, yes, the game is linear. There is some platforming, QTEs, stealth sections, chase sequences, all of which you can fail and die to, but no, you cannot defend yourself in hand to hand combat in any other way than to struggle free if the option presents itself. Some people just like to call anything that don't have gunplay walking sims. Like Outlast, or Super Mario.Story is open for some interpretation so if that annoys you more often than it intrigues you and makes you think, maybe stay clear. At the heart of it it's about acceptance I would say. If you like Alien, Lovecraft, John Carpenter and David Cronenberg you may very well enjoy it.*Playing again the sound design is possibly the best I've ever played in my life and def the highlight of the game*

_childDocuments_.review: A game’s linearity or lack of exploration paths doesn’t necessarily make it bad. If you’re griping about these aspects, you might just be playing the wrong game. Maybe it’s time to look for something more in line with your preferences.Overall, this game holds its own. It boasts a compelling atmosphere and excellent voice acting, and the main character is refreshingly human, with realistic reactions, limitations, and concerns.However, the ending is where it stumbles. It feels bland and abrupt, which unfortunately drains some of the joy from the experience. The main antagonist remains unexplained, and the attempt to create emotional depth with family flashbacks falls flat, making for a rather anticlimactic conclusion.If there was an option like "recommend, when on sale", I'd use it. There isn't, so I go with "wouldn't recommend".

_childDocuments_.review: OK, I really hope people read this so they know what they're getting into. despite the negative review, the game is fun. but its just not worth it at this price point. wait for a bigger sale for around 15-20 bucks in you're equivalent not the 45 i paid(so 50-60 percent off). they're a few reasons, but the primary one is this took a little over 3 and a half hours for me to finish (i also probably could have finished it faster if i didn't get stuck so much) and after its done its done there is no reason to play it again, at this price point i want more value from it.i am more than happy to admit the sound, visuals, and story are pretty good and well worth a buy. but the second reason not to buy this at full price is the gameplay. it makes it so bland to the point it probably would have been better as a walking sim. the puzzles are pointless, the obstacles are easy, and the only thing that will give you challenge is the level design which can be so confusing and needless. as immersive as the story was for me the game portion completely took me out of it. it feels like the game portion was very much an after thought of the story. i hope people find this useful for my overall experience 5.5 angry scottsmen out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part, Still Wakes the Deep is a fantastic horror game. The only thing that would've cemented it as one of my all time favorites would have been monster encounters that were more varied and frantic rather than running down linear corridors.The voice acting and sound design are phenomenal, the environments are terrifying and hypnotic, and the monsters are grotesque and unnatural. The tension was intense all the way through with brief, well-earned moments of levity when the characters joke with one another amidst their seemingly hopeless situation. The developers succeeded, I think, in making the characters' situation feel so damn real. Wonderful game. Really hope The Chinese Room considers making more horror games in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm pretty conflicted about it.Still wakes the deep is a short experience(I've finished it in like...4,3 hours) with clear inspiration from Lovecraft's stories. The short duration can feel a bit lacking, but given the lower pricetag(40 instead of 70) it can be understood, in a way.Pros:-Beautiful visuals-Scottish accents makes the game pretty unique in terms of dub(play with the british dub for full experience)-The big bad of the game makes you constantly ask yourself what it is.-The layout of the oil rig is incredibly detailed, giving the player a constant sensation of being in a real place.Cons:-A bit lacking in mechanics, being pretty much just an experience-The threats feeling too easy to overcome, becoming less threating the deeper you go-Too little context to certain things said by some characters, leaving you pending for more infoSo, to leave this short...I enjoyed the game for what it is, i think they could have gone with a more maze like map in some areas, to make the player feel more trapped i guess, but probably that's just me7+/10

_childDocuments_.review: The atmospheric density is unreal. They borrowed just the right amounts from various inspirations like John Carpenters "The Thing", Creative Assembly's "Alien Isolation" and Frictional's "SOMA". In the story department the Chinese Room doesn't need too much input, being responsible for storytelling masterclasses like "Dear Esther", "Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs" and "Everybody's gone to the Rapture". I'm not through yet, but I rarely have an emotional response like this to a game. I'm freezing cold, despite it being summer. I can literally feel the raw north sea peeling off the warmth from my skin, creeping under every layer. This is what I want from a lot of games, but rarely get. I don't want to discuss the price. If I have a good experience, I actually don't care if this could have been 10 bucks cheaper. A lot of triple A games may bind you for a hundred or more hours, but will never achieve that level of atmosphere and immersion.Also, as a Type 1 diabetic myself, the whole storyline around Roy hits on a very different level. I'm sure it's the very first time this disease got representation/ a storyline in a game.

I often would try to explore every area I could in the hopes of finding collectibles or lore and never really found anything, it usually just turns into dead ends.The sound design is INCREDIBLE. The cast did an amazing job and that sweet sweet sound design of the environments and enemiesHowever, the problem starts when you're supposed to *feel* for these characters because other than 2 lines of dialogue with them at the beginning you never really get to know them AS PEOPLE. _childDocuments_.review: First up, the positives. The game looks gorgeous, plays very well, the soundscape and especially the voice acting is top notch and especially in the first part of your adventure, it's an absolute treat and it's a joy to get to new areas, explore them, learn about what's going on.The negatives though, I feel personally, outweigh the positives. The game is extremely linear and the storyline is predictable, lacking in any real depth. I think the linear aspect of the game pushes you so hard to go in a single direction always, there is a single path forward and you either follow that path, or you won't progress. And because a lot of the environmental troubles you face are going to be repeats of the same thing over and over, going over ledges, crawling on beams, swimming from one spot to another. The actual gameplay gets stale because it's not a hard game, the enemies aren't hard, most of the troubles you meet are quicktime events where you hold or press buttons to overcome them.The enemies as well, sadly don't have a lot of variety, they are creepy and cool the first time, but then you're faced with two situations, you either run away from them as they chase you, or you sneak around while distracting them by throwing stuff.What I really miss in a game like this, is being able to make choices, perform actions that change the outcome of certain situations, even if the end result would be the same, it would be really nice if you're not just moving from place to place doing exactly what the story needs and nothing else apart from looking at stuff, reading up.Would I recommend this? Probably a slight yes over no, but mostly for the first part of the experience and the character development that happens there, that stuff is great, everything else beyond that is just going through the motions more and more with every area you go to.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on an impulse with no prior knowledge and I'm chuffed that I did. As someone who has been on Scottish oil rigs before in my work life, this game really was fascinating.Without giving away too much about the story / gameplay, it's an incredibly linear experience. You are defenceless for the entire game in the sense of never receiving a weapon to fight against the enemies with, so it's purely reliant on stealth. If you've ever played games like Amnesia, Alien: Isolation or SCP: Containment Breach then you'll know somewhat what to expect. The plot, Lovecraftian btw, manages to keep realistic enough to not completely blow your suspension of disbelief. I personally didn't like the ending, but that's probably just me. There is a small side-story that adds a bit of background to the protagonist but otherwise it is, as I said, linear. Interactions with the monsters aren't free-roam; you'll interact with / arrive at the thing the plot tells you to, an enemy will appear in a cinematic scripted fashion and you'll sneak/run away, you enter a small "safe" area and get a new update to the plot, rinse and repeat. The game could've done with something of a larger exploration zone / free-roaming possibility of the entire oil rig in-between story beats (à la Ishimura in the Dead Space Remake).The horror is great right from the get go due to the belivability of an accident on an oil rig, but a lot of the main horror is in-engine. Cutscenes rarely show the monsters up-close, they're mostly only shown properly in gameplay (as such jumpscares are often unintentional) which is an incredibly immersive thing imo. The audio and sound work is genuinely one of the greatest I've seen; the MC often comments/reacts vocally regarding specific things that happen naturally / dynamically right in the heat of gameplay which makes it feel almost like a cinematic experience than anything.9/10, would jump in the North Sea again

_childDocuments_.review: Hear me out!  I loved so many aspects of this game!!The voice acting was great, the banter was spot on! I really enjoyed exploring it all before the main event.The gameplay wasnt for me, the paths overall were very linear and so much is in the dark, with a torch you are viewing the game with tunnel vision.  There were points where I couldn't find my route and was killed repeatedly by being trapped or chased down by a monster.  Times like that the feeling of frustration outweighs any joy or fear or feeling that the game is supposed to generate.  The game itself ceases to be scary after a while. _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game but it just isn't very good. I'll try to keep it as spoiler free as possible but there are too many issues that add up to ultimately being a 2/5 game at best. Starting with the good. The voice acting itself is very good, and the environments are occasionally very pretty and almost always quite atmospheric. Now for the bad. The story is an interesting concept but is not executed well. The main character makes next to no decisions for himself and is just doing what hes told all the way to the end of the game. The supporting cast also will make nonsensical decisions just so the can end up in the right spot for the plot when needed. I will cry at most emotional moments in games and movies but I felt nothing during what should've been a pivotal moment. Basically take the plot of The Thing (1982) but make the characters only try to escape rather than ever fight back in any way. This causes the story to fall flat for me despite having a solid core idea. The first time you see a monster it's quite unsettling but be prepared to see essentially that same design for the rest of the game with the exact same gameplay loop of move from hidey hole to hidey hole. You'll also get a good long look at each of them causing them to lose any real sense of unease or fear. The pathfinding is also hilariously bad at times and I'm pretty sure monsters got stuck on the environment more than once letting me casually complete a section. The game also misuses mechanics that would fit in a more open design like a classic resident evil game. You will occasionally unlock doors, lower ladders, and close valves to shutoff spraying fire or gas leaks. There is also a one time use mechanic of being able to kick open a door. Now the misuse of these mechanics come from the fact that this is a linear game with zero back tracking so if you have to lower a ladder you aren't unlocking a shortcut back, you are just momentarily inconvenienced by hitting a button literally next to the ladder you are going to climb. Every blocked path is unlocked within feet of the block adding nothing to the gameplay except making you press X or hold right trigger and then tilt the left stick. I've seen a handful of complaints about all of these things but the vast majority of people seem to not have any of these issues, which truly surprises me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was excellent, one of the best atmospheric walking simulators I have ever played.Positives and Negatives:+ Jaw dropping gorgeous graphics.  The game ran perfectly on max settings 4K on my RTX 3070, which was interesting because on the forum some other people have been having troubles. Maybe its my beefy i9 CPU or 64gb Ram I am not sure. + The sound design was also fantastic, from the howls of the ocean waves to the howls of the monsters, everything was quality and felt big budget.+ The game moves at a brisk pace, there are no difficult puzzles to get stuck on or get frustrated+ The voice acting is superb, like a Hollywood movie+ Again, art direction and level layout is jaw dropping.+ The jumping and platforming sections were done right. Many FPS games do this wrong and these sections are usually frustrating. In this game the difficulty is perfectly balanced, fun and exhilarating.+ As with the platforming sections, there are a few stealth sections that were super tense and fun. I usually do not like stealth in games, but this game nailed it.  Perfectly balanced difficulty.- I beat the game in just 4.5 hours and actually tried to take my time with it.  So for some players this may be an issue because of the price per length of the game. - The subtitles cannot be turned off as of July 2024, this ruins the immersion and atmosphere of the game a tiny bit - The ending was anticlimactic and felt rushed.Rating: 9.5 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic vibes and you can tell an enormous amount of effort went into making the setting feel authentic. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty good horror adventure. Not particularly scary as you see and hear the monsters way too much and get desensitised to them extremely quick. Kind of a shame really. The story was pretty interesting. It doesn't tell you very much of whats going on so you're kinda left to interpret it yourself, which I quite like.I'm surprised no ones done a horror game based on an oil rig before (they might have done but I cant think of any). This one feels like a mix between The Thing, Annihilation and The Colour out of Space. If you've seen the latter title you'll notice a lot of visual similarities which is cool. Cosmic horror is hard nut to crack in any medium really. This is one of the better ones out there. My main gripe is that it is a little too short for the amount they ask. They could've done Alien: Isolation on an oil rig. That game was 17+ hours of pure tension and fear the first time playing. And it was fantastic the whole time. and still is to this day. This is more like 5-6 if you take things very casual. Imo that's way too short. There's no pandering or any "modern audience" stuff in this either which is great. I play games to escape real life and have fun; not to be lectured to. So that was a nice change of pace. Just as a mention I am getting a bit tired of Unreal 5 engine games running like absolute crap these days. Even with a 4080, if you don't turn on DLSS and Frame Generation their games run pretty bad. Somethings going on here with this engine and its getting annoying. I cant imagine the performance for people with less powerful GPU's. A lot of Unreal 5 games are like this these days and they should run that bad. Even with expensive hardware you pretty much have to have these cheap performance settings turned on to get a decent framerate alot of the time. The graphics are also really nice too. The sea shader they've used reminds of Sea Of Thieves at times (not as good though) but one of the better looking choppy sea shaders I've seen. It adds very much to the immersion of where you are with its crashing wave sounds. Speaking of sound, that is a standout point too. It's generally fantastic. I cant express how important sound and music is to a genre like this and it nails it.All in all this is definitely one of the more decent horror games we've had in a while. If my review has been worth anything of merit, I do very much recommend it. I just wish the game was longer than it is.

_childDocuments_.review: I caught a glimpse of Still Wakes the Deep on a livestream and thought it looked pretty promising but sadly it turned into probably the most disappointing game of this year so far for me. Here's the pros and cons based on my opinion and experience with the game:pros:-offers a very unique and fitting setting for a horror game (in theory)-great voice acting and sound design-good graphics-really good performance despite my old setup; I didn't encounter a single stutter, freeze, crash etc.-didn't run into any major bugs during my playtimecons:-the game progression is strictly linear and also pretty repetitive with barely any optional stuff to find besides some phone calls and the remains of your dead coworkers (feels like a "walking simulator")-while the "monsters" look pretty disgusting the game fails to deliver the actual horror feeling; usually a good horror game catches me really quick but most of the time I just felt bored or indifferent since I didn't have that feeling of being chased or in danger and there were barely any jumpscares-predictable and repetitive quick time events-pretty shallow storytelling: during the game you're gonna find out why you ended up on the drilling rig but there is zero explanation to what is actually going on; no background information about the spreading abomination and the ending just left me sitting with a big questionmark in my head-despite literally walking through most of the game I finished it in just a little over 4 hours which is extremely short for a 35€ game

_childDocuments_.review: Giving it a thumbs up due to Steam's silly binary vote system but this one is a definitive "meh" vote from me, in actuality.It's a fine game for what it is, but ultimately I was somewhat disappointed. I'm familiar with the genre but this one just didn't grip me in the same way that others such as Firewatch did. The story was impactful and it most certainly takes center stage here, but I didn't feel that invested in any of the characters. I had hoped that the gameplay would pick up some of the slack but alas, it was devoid of any mechanical variety. Using a screwdriver and pulling levers is as complex as it gets.The game was buggy but it was nothing too unforgivable considering this was an indie game that just launched. My only major complaint was the subtitle bug in which the subtitles reset to the "On" setting every time you re-enter the Audio settings menu, enter a new area, or reload a save. I am easily distracted by subtitles so this really broke my immersion in a game whose sole purpose is to immerse the player.I'm not here to dump too much on an indie game, but this one didn't scratch much of an itch for me, personally. On the plus side, the setting is brilliant as is the Scottish culture and atmosphere. If you suffer from thalassaphobia or megalophobia, you're in for a hell of a time!

_childDocuments_.review: if you're here just for the visuals and some atmosphere, give it a try. But it's not a good horror game and not a proper story.Level design and visual design in general are awesome. Monsters look terrifying and disgusting, the platform itself is designed very cool throughout the whole game. It's also incredibly easy to navigate, even though yellow marker paint is by now a very lazy cliche, it helps a lot in this game, especially in some underwater sections.Voice acting is also incredible, all of the voices match their characters and the actors clearly put a lot of effort into it. as in Lovecraftian horror I expect a story to be the main part of the experience. Here the story is almost nonexistent. It is linear to the point where the only action that looks like it could make some difference ends up being completely useless. The story revolves around a simple guy with his simple problems, and there is no character development at all. The lore doesn't exist as well: half of the characters almost ignore the fact that chunks of cosmic flash fill up the platform up till the last 15 mins in the game, and you as a player end up having tons of questions about this Thing, but the game doesn't even try to answer them. Some dialogues look as if they were chatGPTed, while the others are just trying to be overly emotional and make you feel something about deaths of poor-written characters who you don't really care about. Hiding my fav example of this game's writing under a spoiler here:Horror parts are not really there as well. The monsters are dumber than the one from Amnesia:The Bunker, so it's very hard to feel threatened. Cosmic horror in this game ended up being less unsettling then depiction of oil platform falling apart for quite boring reasons as fire, flooding and explosions. As a film, Still wakes the deep would be a great disaster movie but a very weak horror.On top of that, controls are sometimes weird, it takes time to get used to holding a button for the character to climb the stairs and sometimes it still doesn't work properly making you restart from the nearest checkpoint. I honestly wanted to enjoy it after waiting for the release so long, and up till around 5-6 hours in I was going to give it a positive review, mentioning the shallow narrative but overall great experience. However, after finishing it, I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely leave reviews nowadays, but I am doing so now because Still Wakes the Deep was a lovely experience and deserves praise! I tend to be a sucker for narrative-heavy horror games, and this game is no exception. With a unique setting and an absolutely marvellous cast and performances, this game really knocked it out of the park for me. It carefully balances horror and story-telling, leaving you wanting more - but the game does not outstay its welcome, and it ends when it knows it has to. The gameplay is simple, and there is not much that you can do as the player to directly combat the events of the game - which is good, in my opinion, especially for this genre. This leaves an ever-lingering tension that lasts throughout the piece but also creates a slow and steady rhythm for it. You are a sufferer of the events - not the controller. This might not be everyone's vibe - if you are looking for something that focuses on gameplay more than narrative, this might not be your kind of cake as a result. If you are someone, however, who wants to get attached to characters and loves experiencing the story with them, I guarantee that you will love this game. Crisp high five to all the people who worked on this project; your love and dedication show.

_childDocuments_.review: I've just emerged from the depths of "Still Wakes the Deep," and I'm still catching my breath. This game is a masterclass in atmosphere, wrapping you in a claustrophobic blanket of tension from start to finish. The plot had me hooked like a fish on a line, reeling me through its twists and turns.Now, I've heard some folks grumble about the game being too linear, but for me, that's part of its charm. It's not trying to be an open-world extravaganza - it's a focused, narrative-driven experience that knows exactly what story it wants to tell and how to tell it.Speaking of focus, let's talk about the game's length. It's short, sure, but it's all the better for it. There's no filler here, no padding to artificially extend playtime. Every moment counts, every scene builds on the last. It's like a perfectly paced thriller novel - gripping from page one to the final chapter.Visually, this game is a feast for the eyes. The developers have worked some serious magic here, optimizing the game to run smoother than a well-oiled machine. It felt more like controlling an interactive film.It's not all smooth sailing, though. There are a few bugs in the code (please fix the fusebox first, when the game tell you), but they'll be fixed in a patch coming this July. The enemy AI could use a bit of fine-tuning too, though if you're as fused in the story as I was, you might not even notice.My one major gripe? The main character's inability to climb over closed doors outside on the rig. It would be nice too have some visual obstacles, that prevents him to do so.Despite these minor issues, "Still Wakes the Deep" is a triumph of atmospheric storytelling. If you're a fan of narrative-driven games that prioritize mood and plot, you owe it to yourself to take the plunge. Just don't be surprised if you find yourself holding your breath along the way.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

_childDocuments_.review: Worth $10, not 30.Would refund if steam allowed it, absolutely not worth the price and I feel scammed.Not a video game, a railroaded story with 3 sections of actual gameplay that boil down to "throw object to move AI monster".Any idea that you are in danger from a monster is thrown out the window on second appearance once you realise the monsters will never catch you if you simply hold forwards, and thus all fear is removed from the game.I see people praising the story. This is an average story with completely arbitrary story beats designed to pad out the game which all feels incredibly pointless, which SPOILER: turns out it was all entirely pointless and you are even told as much at the end of the game. There is no point to this game, it is sold as a lovecraftian, eldritch, psychological horror when in reality it is a poorly told story utilising body horror and using the label "lovecraftian storytelling" to disguise the fact they could not be bothered to actually acknowledge anything that goes on in the story. _childDocuments_.review: As much as I wanted to like this, I did not. My main takeaway is that unfortunately the game is kind of just....boring. Or at least it was for me. I usually really enjoy games like this, but my runtime is a big tell here - I kept pausing the game and walking away for a bit to do chores or do a bit of work or something to break away from the tedium of actually playing this game. The game itself is actually about 4-5 hours long with 6 hours being a very meticulous playthrough. There are a few excellent things here, but at the end of the day I was very glad to be done and was left feeling pretty unhappy with the game.Obviously, the game is beautiful. While I don't think it matches the stunning presentation of Senua's Saga, this is a good showcase for UE5 graphically. The game is incredibly demanding as well, putting my new 4090 through it's paces I was barely getting 60fps at 4k ultra until I enabled DLSS/DLAA/RR/FG - the full suite of goodies - which landed me about 100+fps consistently. I feel like the games upscaling technology options are needlessly complicated and poorly explained however - DLSS in particular is an umbrella term for a few different functions, and the game allows layering of those in a weird way that makes it difficult to understand exactly how it is behaving and what is functionally flipped to on. Don't even think about trying this on a Steamdeck or ROG Ally - it's not gonna be a great experience I don't think. The sound design is equally great and really nailed the atmosphere - no complaints there. Presentation is by and large stunning.But then we dig into the meat of the game and this is where things fall apart for me. I, personally, IMO, found this game more often than not really boring to play. It's just not fun to ENGAGE with. I know it's a walking sim - I get that and it's a genre I normally like, but my goodness this game tests your patience with moving you one tedious task to the next and they are all strung together with the same janky and unsatisfying parkour that at times gets so ridiculous that it actually robs from the game. Random Scottish dude Nathan Draking his way around the deteriorating oil rig really takes a lot away from the games more grounded attempts at pulling you into its world. Even the sequences where you have to deal with monsters are really heavily scripted, but to the games credit I don't deny many a buttcheeks were clenched while darting towards a hiding place right as you are noticed by an entity. But the game really only serves up a few of these moments, with an equal number of entity encounters being just holding sprint and running down a hallway with no real fail state. Next up, and this one stings me the most, is the story and in particular the games attempts at telling a grounded tale of people with day to day lives. Look, everything here is very authentic on the surface - genuine Scottish actors being genuinely, if not a bit stereotypically maybe, Scottish. It's all executed with savvy. But for me none of it mattered - I didn't spend enough time with these people or learn about them in any meaningful way. Even Roy, who is the protagonists best friend and probably tied for most prominent secondary character in the game....you have 3 brief conversations with him. The game does a pretty bad job setting up the people to act as the lattice for the subsequent drama. Almost every single character moment fell flat for me save maybe one or two. I feel like the game would have been far better if it had leaned into the protagonist being a newbie on the rig who hadn't formed any friendships yet, and focused on him and his story instead of fracturing so few moments between so many characters.Lastly the crux of the game, the entity. It's cool. Maybe not particularly creative, but cool. Very traditional Lovecraftian vibes, unknown motives and bizarre behavior that leave you wondering. Its effect on the crew, who serve as the actual functional threat, is pretty much spot on with "The Thing" type behavior, which again while not particularly creative was cool and definitely a bit freaky. I can think of a few more interesting ways they could have ended the game, while keeping the protagonists final actions intact, but that's a minor complaint. It ends about how you would expect it to, no surprises there and by and large that's OK I suppose.Still Wakes The Deep felt to me like a game that is less, not more, than the sum of its parts. Nothing is mechanically wrong or broken, but it's just all so bog standard and at times uninteresting that without the quasi photo realistic veneer of UE5 I am not sure the game would be getting the same reception that it is. No doubt though, damn, those graphics. I feel like games like Layers of Fear have done this sort of thing in a much more interesting and engaging way. However, if you've played Layers of Fear and games like them and are looking for more than this might still be worth a try. The game clearly clicks with some people, so there may be something here for you to find. I personally however only really found shiny graphics masking what ended up being to me a pretty boring experience.Also, while not a horror game exactly, another release earlier this year that is pretty much this exact type of game but executed waaaaay better is "The Invincible". Check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is a fantastic cinematic experience. It is a beautiful game with marvelous environment design. The game does a tremendously good job of making the player feel small and weak within the massive oil rig. The visuals, sound effects, and weather effects all complement the narrative, which is as distressing as each cranking corner of the slowly deteriorating structure. The voice acting is also brilliant, with each character feeling alive as you descend into madness throughout the story.However, the linear progression is too limiting for the overall experience to be truly satisfying. Still Wakes the Deep is essentially "The Thing" on an oil rig, but it lacks the absolute horror that the movie delivered and fails to offer anything that encourages the player to explore more. It’s a shame that such a gorgeous map feels underutilized simply because the player is forced to follow one path. As someone with a low tolerance for scares, I was disappointed to find very few genuinely frightening moments. Although the monster designs were wonderful, neither the psychological horror nor the scares lived up to expectations. Even in the darkest areas, the monsters felt too easy to avoid and applied almost no pressure. It is almost as if SOMA failed to turn its encounters into frightening experiences.
