_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is the latest game from The Chinese Room, known for their critically acclaimed title "Dear Esther." This marks the final game written by studio founder Dan Pinchbeck. Set in the mid-70s, the game places players in the shoes of Scotsman Cameron McLeary, an electrician on an offshore oil rig, who is evading the police after a drunken pub brawl.The opening scenes introduce the beautifully rendered setting of the rig and its superbly voice-acted inhabitants. However, things soon go awry as the drill awakens an eldritch beast from the depths, threatening the rig's structure.Players must navigate the wreckage using first-person platforming to escape. As some crew members transform into monsters, McLeary must hide and run from his former friends to survive. The game predominantly offers a walking simulator experience, with players moving from one section to the next, interacting with environmental items, and occasional light stealth sections. Routes and interactables are clearly marked with the "yellow-highlight" method, making navigation straightforward. Those seeking in-depth gameplay should look elsewhere.Instead, the atmosphere and story are the highlights here, particularly the audio. While there aren’t many major twists, "Still Wakes the Deep" keeps you hooked throughout its roughly four-hour runtime. However, the lack of notes or similar items to discover along the way is a missed opportunity to flesh out the other crew members more.On a technical note, the game ran well on my 1080ti and Ryzen 5 1600X with FSR3, though I encountered an issue where the game would crash during a couple of loading transitions. Apart from this hiccup, I managed to achieve a decent frame rate of around 60-100fps.Overall, The Chinese Room has put significant effort into creating an edge-of-your-seat walking sim with good world-building and a fantastic cast of characters. It won’t be for everyone, and the higher price tag may deter some, but if this sounds like your cup of tea, I definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I ultimately regret buying this experience.I say "experience" because that's what it is: A playable story. The actual "gameplay" of this game is very light, but that's okay! This is a great story, the best voice acting since RDR2, awesome graphics, and a fantastic setting for a horror experience. I really love the natural unfolding of events, in particular. It's kind of like playing Dead Space, but instead of finding the Ishimura after all the chaos, you get to actively see the chaos unfold. I really appreciate that the game has characters other than the player until the very end... that they don't surface after the event with everyone already dead....But $30 is simply too much for this.I would recommend this at $15, maybe $20. To be clear, this offers a 4 hour campaign with zero replayablity. And unlike Scorn, I don't think I'll be thinking about this a year after playing it.I think these devs are great, and made a great product. However, I can't ignore the fact that I beat this in an evening, and am now going to uninstall it, probably never to install it again.Note: I'm keeping this review as "Recommend" since I do ultimately recommend this, just on sale a year from now.

_childDocuments_.review: A simple in scope, short but wonderfully crafted horror game.Key takeaways, charming voice acting (love a good Scottish accent), compelling narrative, detailed environments that feel 'lived in' and enough variety to keep it relatively fresh.Horror / game-play mechanics are common enough; avoid nearby enemy and escape to safe areas to continue exploring in a linear fashion.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is a great entry into the horror genre, more specifically centered around themes such as body horror, Lovecraftian elements, claustrophobia and thalassophobia. You play a character down on his luck working on an oil rig off the coast of Scotland, before the rigs drill hits an unknown entity that sets off a chain of horrific events that results in both the crew mutating, as well as the oil rig itself distorting. While being set in an environment as industrial and bleak as an oil rig, some of the cosmic horror elements in the form of the entity itself bring a slew of strangely visually pleasing aesthetics to the game, despite being hostile and quite frankly disgusting.The story elements are well done, as is the voice acting; it’s fairly uncommon to hear British and Scottish voice actors in a game, but in a strange way it adds a level of authenticity to the games storyline in my opinion. The main character is likeable and the writing is very authentic to the Scottish. You’ll hear a lot of swearing and banter between the crew, and a lot of colloquialism that I personally really enjoy in a game.The horror elements are great, the body horror specifically is quite magnificently gross, yet you can’t help but take a look and really examine the brutal transformations that the entity causes on board. I found myself going out of my way to find most of the dead (or not dead) crew members to see their fates. Most of these dead crew members are essentially either set pieces or hazards, but there are a few notable enemies that force stealth sections. I didn’t mind them too much but some areas did get frustrating, as the enemies movements are actually very hard to predict as they moved around the areas like giant legged spiders almost.In terms of the gameplay, we’re really looking at loop that incorporates walking simulator elements, light parkour and a few stealth sections between, with some very minor puzzle elements of remedial tasks like turning switches off or moving carts out of the way of your path. At its core, it’s a pretty basic game and mostly an enjoyable horror experience, but due to this I can’t really imagine doing multiple playthroughs. Despite that, I would 100% recommend this game but only perhaps during a sale and not for full price – it’s a short experience but a good one nonetheless.Excellent voice actingOriginal concept and settingGreat visuals and weather effectsNot much replayabilityA little on the short side
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes The Deep was one of the more refreshingly dreadful (in a positive way) psychological horror games I've played in recent history, due largely in part to developer The Chinese Room's awareness of the importance of building an atmosphere within your game universe. While the game plays as your standard walking simulator, and at times has its frustrating set of chore-like responsibilities, it serves as a reminder that horror should have a creeping sense of dread attached to it inherently in order to be effectively immersive. Creature design paired with a well-crafted story, tense atmosphere, and unsettling overall vibe make this one of the more highly regarded horror experiences of 2024. Not necessarily for people who require a high-octane jumpscare attached to their horror.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game that had me sitting with bated breath multiple times. I almost wish they did fixated more on the psychological thriller theme rather than the horror aspect. The voice acting was great and the graphics really helped immerse me in the game. This game is more setup to be a playable movie than an actual game, which helps sell the experience. God I wouldn't want to be on this oil rig.For the Devs, 2 notes.1. I think the game would benefit from having interactions more varied to keep them immersive rather than competitive. For example, the grip option should probably be repetitive button pushing so you aren't just holding two triggers and waiting. Having the interactions so similar took me out of the animation and I think held back from what you were looking to achieve.2. The flashbacks should have more moments like the end game. There was a difficulty getting attatched to the characters so it was hard to care what happened to them. A little more interaction from the player or more interactive scenes might help resolve that problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Where "Everybody's Gone to the Rapture" was a slow and dialogue-heavy narrative, "Still Wakes the Deep" is a fast and very linear disaster experience.  The writing alone is excellent enough to save the game from its lack of environmental storytelling and unconvincing "survival horror" elements.  Don't get wrong, the whole package still works.  It's just unfortunate the developer went full-blown "action narrative" vice letting us slow down and explore the oil rig and the characters more.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: **Spoilers**Great graphics and I like the consistent game mechanics. The quick-time events become instinctual very quickly. I played the story mode and the game was still challenging but not difficult. The one part I did not like was not being able to save Roy and not having the choices/speed impact the story. I wanted to get Roy's insulin as soon as he mentioned it in the very beginning but there was an invisible wall in the direction of the cabins. The story/game progression is very railroady, there is only one path you can go and the game will not let you go the "wrong" way. But in some areas, it still allows for minor exploration, but this does not effect gameplay, only the ability to get achievements. Still a great game overall. 10/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible unknown adversary and survival game so far. Lovecraftian in the sense that the horror is in the fear of the unknown, but set in a partially contemporary environment.... No boredom! I am playing at boy scout level and have managed to get myself killed on several occasions. I am perhaps one of the older players. My family ran a marine salvage  company and I was able to spend school holidays on the salvage ship on the north Sea moored over a wreck being recovered. The feel of the wind, spray and the shipping forecast that was very important at the time made my hair stand out at the nape of my neck. Rather like being in a movie. I am going to try this in vr using UEVR when I have finished. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game thinking it was gonna be another walking simulator like Amnesia: a machine for pigsWhat I got was one of the most dreadful stories I think I've ever witnessed, the writing is so damn real, the characters feel like real people and not witty teenagers spouting off random witty catchphrases everytime they escape death.This game almost made me cry, it made me laugh, and of course, it scared the ♥♥♥♥ out of me.Good on ya Caz
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the game. Took me a bit over 6 hours to finish it and I think it's the right length for this game. The pacing is great except in the middle where you have to keep fixing the generator and you start to ask yourself "What's even the point of this?" but it all comes nicely together at the end when they directly address it in the story. And the story itself was fine but the thing I liked about it, it did the cosmic horror right. And the whole game felt like playing through a movie because it was so focused and the acting was good.It's basically The Thing on an oil ring (even the protagonist's name McLeary is similar to Kurt Russel's MacReady) minus the paranoia. Instead of an alien posing as human, there's some kind of growing presence infesting the ship and changing the crew members. The flesh growing between the walls of the rig reminded me of biomass in System Shock 2.The graphics are top level, the environments are full of detail and the monster animation is great. Like I already mentioned, the acting is very good for a video game. The dialogue and the banter between workers felt real and they speak Scottish with so much slang that you'll have to rely on English subtitles for translation lol. You'll interact with a handful of characters throughout the story but I only cared for one of them- your best mate Roy. Expected he would turn into a monster at the end and fighting him would be heartbreaking but that never happened. Perhaps a missed opportunity. You see your wife in the flashbacks but she always acts like a total ♥♥♥♥♥ so I didn't get why he wanted to go back to her so bad, I thought the monsters were a pleasant company in comparison. Such a weird decision to put happy memories where she was actually somewhat charming only at the very end of the game.The sound design is fantastic. They built a miniature oil rig to capture the sounds of the environment. The cries and the screams of the monsters are creepy as hell and getting chased by them was nerve wracking at times. But after sneaking around them for a while and playing hide and seek, the scare factor began fading away.The game is extremely linear and there's no room for exploration. Pretty much every door that you don't need to go through right this very moment will be locked. I thought the use of the color yellow to guide you worked perfectly in this case as that's a color heavily used on the real oil rigs in similar fashion so it's actually subtle but then they kept adding yellow paint and yellow towels hanging out of the hiding spots and it became annoying and immersion breaking instead. There's a constant feeling that the devs are holding your hand throughout the game, even solving puzzles for you. You see a typical looking puzzle in this genre and it seems like you're gonna have to figure it out but it is just window dressing. The solution to the problem is always right in front of you, and all you have to do is press interact and the character will solve it for you. . It would be much more satisfying if we'd have to engage our brains a little. A couple of simple Frictional style puzzles would do wonders for this game. As it is, it seems like the devs have no faith in the players. Everything you do in the game is sort of realistic so despite of all the supernatural stuff, I only had to suspend my disbelief during some of the platforming sections. There were a couple of jumps that I don't think even the best parkour athletes could make - you'd break your arms catching yourself while dropping from such heights. And this guy starts breathing heavy if you run for just 4 seconds but at the same time he has incredible agility, upper body strength and endurance to climb for hours.There were a couple of scenes where the sights of eldritch horrors actually looked very beautiful and awe inspiring (accompanied with music, which I only really noticed during those scenes). These were some of my favorite moments.For me it's  despite how damn linear it is. If you're into cosmic horror, you will love this game. setting and the atmosphere cosmic horror done right realistic visuals and fantastic sound design great acting and believable characters good pacing too linear, almost on rails doesn't require any thinking  In the latest patch they added a toggle for reducing the yellow markers.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't really have any expectations for this game. I did ponder the idea of buying it, and thankfully, my friend gave me a glowing recommendation. I am thankful for it because I believe this game deserves nothing but the highest accolades for narrative-driven horror. Still Wakes the Deep is a love letter to the claustrophobic nature of John Carpenter's The Thing, from the immense body horror, tightly packed space of the Beira D Oil Rig taking the place of Outpost 31, and most importantly, the well-rounded cast of characters making this Scottish rig feel like a grim but lively environment. The story is otherwise a horror-drama that is just The Thing on an Oil Rig, which by no means is an insult, it's quite perfect, especially since very few games have tried to replicate that outside of the official Thing game and Distrust.For its 6-hour length, you will see things so uniquely bizarre that I honestly will plug the concept artist Jef Wall here:  I really wish we had a model viewer since the few monsters you do run into are so heavily covered in darkness or fog that you can't appreciate it that well, so hopefully that link can satiate that interest. On the other end of that, this game does feature moments where you need to face monsters and honestly, their scripted sections that don't last long and are quite easy to navigate for the most part, so for people expecting a Mr. X situation you don't need to worry, everything is purely situational and that's honestly fine. This is a narrative game, first and foremost, and it's some of the best writing I've seen for a game of this nature. I cannot recommend it enough; it's a truly anxiety-inducing experience that is definitely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: This is a breath of fresh air. In time of survival games flooding the market with the same rinse and repeat approach to a world with now story in it, I'm glad to have these little treasures to keep the creative story telling side of things alive. It is a bit on the short side, but I the story was fantastic. I actually cared about what happened to all of the characters. I can't wait to see more from this team.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I have thalassophobia yet I love these games even though they terrify the hell out of me. This one is fantastic and the inspirations are obvious. This has all the makings of a cult classic, voice acting, dialogue and story are all incredibly well done and the atmosphere is absolutely dreadful in all the best ways. The chases sequences really get the blood pumping and the visuals are just stunning
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Simple horror, (Go pull this lever/start the generator while hiding from the monster.) STUNNING visuals & sound design.They really took advantage of UE5. Great voice acting, horrifying lovecraftian monsters, although the narrative focus on the protagonists personal issues without investigating the behaviour, purpose, effects or origin of the main monster by the end kind of left me with blue balls.Main downside for me is the game play is so linear and simple (With a literal yellow paint trail leading you through the whole game) It may as well have been a movie, but it was a great experience none the less.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, not great. The setting and atmosphere is really fun and unique. The gameplay is pretty simple - very basic puzzles and a lot pressing buttons when prompted, and very much on rails. This is a level or two above a walking simulator, but it was fun enough to play through. I'd get it on a sale though, price is a bit steep for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: This was a genuinely scary experience, in a good way. I am someone who finds the entire concept of an oil rig terrifying by itself - a flimsy little platform out in the middle of the sea, at the mercy of elements, I'm a little sick just think about that. Introducing a Lovecraftian horror into that already terrifying setting? What could possibly go wrong? XD
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: The voice actors, graphics, monster design, story... Everything has been wonderful. The problem? There are moments in the game, when you are in the outdoor area of the building, that it is almost impossible to play it with terrible lag. I've tried to lower everything to a minimum and nothing, it keeps going in fits and starts. This obviously breaks the immersion and it's VERY frustrating to play like this.However, in the interior areas, the game runs wonderfully smoothly with all the graphical options maxed out.It's obvious to mention it, but I have a gaming computer with a lot of power, and I've never had a problem running the newest games so I know it's a game thing, which me off more. In addition, the duration is very short...I would have finished it in less than 6h if the lags had allowed me to play it properly instead of making me pause it for hours until I remembered I was playing it.PLEASE, this game has a lot of potential and I can't wait to see what else you have to offer us in the future, but this game is not worth almost 40 dollars... I seriously thought about returning it, but I think it's important to support you and help you improve. If the outer area played more fluid it would be wonderful, please fix it
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I am normally HORRIBLE at horror games. This one was absolutely beautiful and the story was well written. I definitely had some big spooks but I really enjoyed how I wasn't able to get lost. There's a pretty clear path to follow as you go through the game which I enjoyed. (Again I'm normally pretty bad at spooky games so this was nice) Definitely worth it and lovely story.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful game! The story is very well written, the voice acting (especially the lead) is superb, and the musical score is (as always with their games) mesmerizing. There were a few moments in the middle of the game where some of the game mechanics became a little repetitive but there was always a new story progression around the corner which kept me motivated to keep moving forward. The Chinese Room have perfected the art of creating beautiful worlds and telling well-crafted narratives and, for me, their games are obviously crafted with love and passion. Buy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I could not walk away from this game until i beat it, the story captivates, the art is amazing, the shower was fun to stay in for a bit. As someone who has played so many horror games to the point where jump scares are predictable this game kept me on the edge of my seat, it still had some predictable moments, like a brightly illuminated exit sign down a dark hallway. I still jumped out of my seat a couple times! If you play it i recommend you beat it, the story is worth it, and the game isnt too hard! Amazing job devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING, DO NOT USE FSR 3 IN THIS GAME OR YOU WILL EXPERIENCE CONSTANT CRASHES AND FREEZES! Still Wakes the Deep is a fantastic, linear, story focused horror game that tells an amazing, emotional story, and provides stressful and fun gameplay. The visuals are fantastic, the sound design is amazing, the voice acting is superb, and the experience doesn't overstay its welcome and tells its story within a crisp 4-5 hours. Totally worth the money to support this team and the fantastic game they made.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep succeeds in creating both a wonderful cast of characters that will have you hankering for an Irn-Bru before you know it and a truly unnerving bit of ambience in its quieter moments. However, the magic quickly runs out if you happen to peek behind the mirror, resulting in a great character story mired in a somewhat generic and needlessly gory B-movie. While I do recommend checking it out and playing it in Scots Gaelic (massive props for adding that, Chinese Room), it may not be worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I think a self written quote perfectly sums up this game in all it's form of what has easily become my best game of the year, hell, decade so far:"And it's there at a choice that you made, that in the midst of it all, all the rage, fury, anguish and agony that one wonders, if you had of turned a different way, spent a bit longer in the shower, said your goodbyes - that something would've changed. Just to know you got to spend just a few more moments of time with them."It is - to date, the second best video game story behind Red Dead Redemption 2 for me which now says a lot and hits home almost too closely in it's own way of story telling that hurts, but makes for a game that we rarely see in a world of hurried scripts and bugged messes.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I will start off positively saying the games graphics, sound, voice acting, and atmosphere was top notch, especially using an oil rig as the environment which is definitely underutilised in horror. Also the monsters retaining some of who they were as theyre yelling out, hunting you was amazing. I really wanted to love this game as it was recommended a few times as being a GOTY contender and after seeing the trailer having "the thing" type monsters I had high hopes. Problem is those monsters barely play a role in the game. Youd expect them to be a bigger threat, sorta like outlast, but you can easily sneak by them with little effort and other characters talk about them as if they're a minor inconvenience or not even monsters at all. You dont even get to see what most of them look like as you never get that close. Even when they kill you its instant with no type of unique execution, which i found disappointing. Most of the monsters look like meatballs or a giant head with lines coming off them which i couldnt take seriously. I also kinda expected the game to have multiple endings or choices to give it some replayability but its linear with little in the way of collectables to help world building.As much as I dont regret buying the game since i do wish to see more games like this, just with a little more depth. I cant recommend it as youd be better off watching a playthrough of it and maybe read some lore as youd get the just of the experiences
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I was recommended this game by a friend. The game looks great. I'll start by making that clear and that there is something positive to say. Scary? Not so much. There were some moments of suspense but for me that quickly subsided with just how linear the whole game felt. Like, I could have played the whole game by moving forward only. Chased by a monster? Just dip under the nearest counter top you'll be fine. And if you do get caught by a monster, it's instant-death with a blurry death screen so it removes any of the immersion. Story? I felt it was lacking. Ok so you're on an oil rig, there's some kind of monster/alien you drill into, and then the ending is abrupt. There are no consequences, no choice, and no real character building. No real explanation into the monsters/aliens and the protagonist's main story about being away from family was just rushed and irritating. I was disappointed. I think they could have done so much more with this such as1) Given the monsters the ability to pull you out from a hiding place if they see you go in 2) Given the monsters unique kill animations 3) Given the player choices and consequences 4) Explained the aliens/monsters more  And MY GOD does this game love: valves, ladders, and ledges! If you are tempted to play this; make it a drinking game and see how long you last with just those 3 things. Then you can add: fuses, opening padlocks with a screwdriver, and randomly placed phone calls.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: A truly fantastic cinematic horror game, perhaps the best one I've played in a long time. Awesome monster designs, excellent dialogue that can be legitimately funny or heartbreaking at the right times, and great narrative pacing. I'd compare this game more to the likes of Soma, where there is actual gameplay elements like sneaking past or running away from monsters, throwing things to distract them, etc. but the main draw is the atmosphere and story. To me, this game is the perfect culmination of all the narrative games the Chinese Room has made in the past. Heavy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is a fun yet honest by-the-books horror game experience.Gameplay-wise the game does not present a lot, as it's mostly fueled by typical parkouring and basic stealth.With the game instead focusing on cinematics and story priority, which isn't inherently always a negative. But it is worth a mention.A lot of the body-horror present feels most strongly inspired by that of Carpenter's The Thing and Annihilation from 2018.And what I really like is how the game takes awhile to build-up the monsters before ever seeing them, which makes it immensely rewarding when it is you finally do. Which is furthermore is also topped with the glimpses of humanity present within the monsters themselves as well, and of course the gorgeously grotesque gore galore.There was sadly a short part of the game where I got pretty hardcore stuck on, as I had no idea how to progress.Luckily, the developers commonly roam the Steam Discussions and were quick to happily help me out. Very awesome! Thanks!Also Scottish is funny.Anyways, the game is pretty good but in the sense that I don't foresee it reaching anybody's top 10s this year.You can play it and be over with pretty quickly and feel nicely satisfied -- some probably in a single session or 2 -- with yet very little motive to ever really return to it or think of it again. That's not inherent criticism, those games are needed in the industry. But it is still worth being considered.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Cool atmosphere. Kinda like the Carpenter's the thing. However, i think the game play systems are simple enough to call this a glorified walking simulator. No difficulty from the monsters, no puzzles, no health very very linear. A few of the encounters are on rails chases.  I enjoyed this game but for 35 dollars its wayyyyy too simple. Id say its 15 dollars too expensive.Cant recommend for the price
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: 8.75/10I LOVED this game.I beat it in 5 hrs on my first playthrough, standard mode. Let's talk about it! SPOILER WARNING!! This is going to be a long one, buckle up! <3Pros:- The story is very well written, easy to understand and relate to, and felt grounded and realistic for the game world. It wasn't over complicated, which I think actually added to the game because you aren't trying to split your focus between a complex story and the scares which take most of your attention in this game.- Gameplay was great, smooth on my rig, with no framerate or lag issues- The horror was BRILLIANT. I never once got bored or expectant of the horror or the scares. From start to finish, I was on the edge of my seat and did not know what to expect.- The monsters felt unique, even though they appeared somewhat similar in model. They weren't overemployed and though there were calm moments, I feel like the scale of chase/evade to free roam time was pretty fair and balanced.- I LOVED that you got to know which monsters were where, and at points I was going 'ohhh don't you dare send me back to Engineering, I don't wanna see Addair!' xD Which was great.- The strategies you needed to employ for each monster felt challenging, and I had to stop and put thought into my next move before taking it, and when I did die, I had to reevaluate my moves. In one scenario against Addair (changing the fuse box in Engineering cage), I died probably 5-6 times trying to go 10 feet to a door. The BEST part of this situation for me, was that after I got to the door and closed it, I walked ten feet and realized the beast was waiting for me in the NEXT DAMN ROOM. That was brutal, and I felt like it flipped the script on the traditional 'hide/run/rest' cycle of horror. We have been trained by horror games to hide or run and once we reach a door or a checkpoint, we get a few moments to rest where the music is light and we can let our heartbeat come down - BUT that moment where I opened the next door and found him there, and immediately had to go back and hide was one of the most brutal things I have had a horror game do to me in a LONG time. It was a nice sequence break that kept me on my toes. (Addair was honestly my fav monster, and I also hated him the most xD I was so thrilled when he burned LOL)- The map was very well utilized! Despite returning to the same areas several times, they were different each time, and I never felt like I actually learned the map because it kept changing and molding as the iridescent goop (as one of my stream viewers called it) took over. I had to find new ways to get around the monsters and form new strategies for the same area because it had changed since I was last there. This made the horror 10x better because I wasn't just running down the same hallways (even though I technically was) and looping the monsters because I knew the map, I had to relearn the rig at least three times, which was scary, but great!- The graphics and art style was beautiful. The world felt REAL and lived in, the map was (to my knowledge) fairly realistic in terms of an oil rig, and I didn't feel 'pathed' as you might say. Yes, this could be considered a form of walking simulator because there isn't much to do besides run/hide and open doors, but I never really felt like I was on a single straight roped off path like some games feel. I felt like I was exploring an oil rig, and even if I couldn't walk around the map freely like an open world game, I didn't feel guided like a carrot on a stick, I was exploring in the bounds of a falling apart oil rig, and it felt genuine. I felt like I was in control, which made it all the more scary, because I was making the choices, and I suffered for my mistakes.- The sound design was top tier. The noises of the rig, the monsters, and the ocean were very realistic and horrifying. The atmosphere it created was bone chilling at times, especially for the under rig sections and pontoon sections. There's more atmosphere than music, but I don't think that took anything away from the game at all. I actually think it suited the game to have less music and more just natural sounds of the rig and ocean. The Leg areas and Pontoon areas were brutal for me because they were so SILENT xD That scared me way more than creepy music would have.- This might not be a 'Pro' to everyone, but it is to me; this game plays PERFECTLY on Thalassophobia and Vertigo.Cons:- The story could have been introduced a little better at the beginning. Why are we there? We don't really find that out for a while and it left me with a slight disconnect. Also, the connection between Caz and Roy was not established very well. I felt nothing when Roy died. I felt more losing Brodie and Finlay because I spent the whole game talking to them and experiencing the horrors with them.- There were only a couple graphical issues, specifically where you got out of a cutscene. Both of those were when the cutscene was showing a monster coming up behind you and you had to run. One was with Trots or Addair, I think? The other was with Rennick. The one with Rennick got me killed TWICE in a row. Basically, when you come out of the cutscene, it turns you back around, so you're facing the monster. I already had my run going, so the moment I came out of it, I ran smack into Rennick instead of running away like I had been before the cutscene turned me. This isn't a huge horror killer, but it did break my immersion/horror/tension when Rennick killed me twice in a row before I got myself turned the right away and barely escaped him from the time I lost to the cutscene turning me.- A couple of the controls were a little buggie (though it may have been user error?) The 'leap forward' while swimming did not work for me at all. I followed the on screen directions and it never worked. I was using keyboard and mouse, so maybe it's just an integration issue. Despite this, I never once drowned in the underwater sections, so I didn't suffer for this issue. The grab and grip mechanics failed a couple times when I KNOW I was pressing hard into my mouse buttons. I am unsure if that was scripted or just a control bug.- The run speed felt... awkward? While I know you aren't supposed to be able to outrun giant monsters, I sometimes felt like I was moving through quicksand (even when not injured). This MAY be purposeful, but I died more than once in places where I should have been able to make it to a safe space or door.- The volume was a little hard to get right - meaning I wasn't actually sure which meter the monsters were tagged to minus the global meter. It was a little hard to get that balanced right - and as someone who uses earbuds, that did present me with a challenge when the monsters were right in my face. They were WAY too loud, but if I turned down the global setting, I couldn't hear anything, so I felt almost handicapped. Maybe add a volume slider for the monster sounds, or make it clear which one they are tagged to for headphone users? That made it really hard to find a good balance between 'i'm scared' and 'my ears are blown out, you just ruined the horror for me', but honestly, it was only a major issue in a couple sections, mostly with Addair in Engineering.- This is specifically about Addair in the Engineering room with the fuse box - I got stuck under the stairs to the door out beside the fuse box cage. Addair was literally on top of me, and would not move or go back to his patrol path despite me being silent. Even when I threw objects to pull him away, he would not move. I ended up having to let him kill me once because it felt like he was bugged there after 10 minutes of just waiting and throwing stuff across the room. I am unsure if this is a bug. Overall, I had a BLAST playing this game* If the Dev's want footage of any of the bugs I mentioned above, let me know, I streamed my playthrough on Twitch, so I can provide timestamps to see the issues I had.- LitaCakes

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this was excellent. I'm about to say a lot of stuff that sounds otherwise, but hear me out. This is one of the best things I've played in years, you just need to meet it on its own terms to appreciate it.This is probably the most linear game I have ever played. It's more like a movie. You control the camera. You move around and interact with limited objects. You succeed or fail at the tasks it puts in your way (usually you don't fail at them more than once, mind you). You execute very basic QTE type reactions in order to stop yourself from falling or getting caught. You don't solve puzzles, per se. The only portions with any degree of choice (other than "die" or "don't die") are brief stealth encounters. So, how is it possibly any good?It's a great, proper-Lovecraftian horror movie I watch/played over the course of a few hours, and once I realized what it was, I loved every minute of it. It's got a great sense of authenticity, its characters are believable and extremely well acted. The cast gets whittled down to a core group pretty quickly, and I found myself caring about the fates of those who survive the initial mayhem. It doesn't over-explain anything, and it builds toward some of the most epic and unsettling visuals I've seen in a game or movie, full stop.I imagine its core design/philosophical direction will put certain people off. For maybe the first hour of play, I bucked against its full dismissal of exploration or choice -- but having completed it, I'm fully convinced that this design approach was a strength. This game maintained narrative momentum where most games completely fail, and narrative momentum was the whole point of this game. By in large, this narrow and cramped gameplay just serves really cool way of expressing this particular story (as well as being thematically appropriate for the setting, come to think of it).Why be a game at all, and not a movie? This has proven there is something that really grounds you in the experience, just controlling the camera and limited inputs. Being at the controls keeps you engaged, seeing through the character's eyes keeps you immersed. Hearing his voice in your head keeps you emotionally invested. All that does largely serve the horror here. That said, it's worth noting there were a few moments where the gaminess of it took me out of the narrative. Most notably, I found the on-screen prompts for QTE-type interactions annoying. There are no complex button combo QTE's here, but I did find that looking at a prompt during a dramatic moment undermined the drama a bit. There were also moments where choices may have improved the horror a bit, by adding an element of uncertainty. When you know your only available option is to move forward along a pathway, it somewhat undermines the threat of the monster chasing you -- all you have to do is keep moving forward (your only option), and you're fine.Overall, though, this was fantastic. Strong recommend, as long as people know what they're getting into. Again, meet it on its terms and you'll love it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where I wish I could put an intermediate rating.Don't get me wrong, I loved the game. The graphics are good, the storytelling is top notch, the flow of the game, everything about how it feels and plays is good. Except for one crash which I blame on overreaching with my graphic settings and a few places where you can wedge yourself and get stuck, there are no glaring issues I encountered. The generous checkpoint system turns death or getting stuck into a momentary delay, and the crash only set me back thirty seconds or so. And the voice acting  turning a good story into a great one. (If you like Scottish people.)But with all good things, there is the other side of the coin. The game is expensive for what it is. 35$ for normal price, and -10% on steam summer sale bringing you close to 30-ish is steep. This game feels more like a movie with its story focused linear game-play, which hurts for this cost considering there is no replay value. Even on it's 'survival' difficulty, the game is not hard (Though I don't really see a problem with that).Even if it was at a nice even 20$ i think it would be much more reasonable, but in the end I bought it, so who's to say. The problem stems from that watching the game, and playing the game, offer a very similar experience, and finding a internet personality you can stand and watching them play this would offer the same feeling at no cost to the end user.In the end, it is a lovely game made with passion. If you have the money, and want a good four to five hours of game-play, this is the game for you. I can certainly say that I enjoyed it, though I hope the developers have some steeper sales in the future to allow more people to enjoy this fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: While not the longest or most complex game of its kind, Still Wakes the Deep truly stands out among the crowd in evoking a sense of place and person. The accents, the writing, the VA performances, and the sound design all come together to create such an intense sense of being in a singular place and time that I truly got lost in it, and found myself thinking in Scottishisms for a week after finishing the game ("I'm good at the leckie"). The biggest criticism I have of the game is that I found the "metaphor" or symbolism of it too... simple, or not really present enough. Horror as a genre is all about representing fears from reality and taking them to the extreme, and I found the messaging here a little too obvious or straightforward. "Rampant capitalism and environmental destruction bad." Which don't get me wrong, I agree with as a sentiment, but it felt so... surface (pun not intended) level here. Similarly, the tragic ending could be spotted half a million miles away. Ultimately very little here surprised me, which doesn't make it bad, but I was hoping for something *more*.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve just completed the game. Before I swing back around to get the achievements here’s my review!I will start by saying I’ve been a fan of The Chinese Room back since Dear Ester, and that survival horror is a guilty pleasure of mine - so there might be some unconscious bias involved in this one boys, but I’ll do my best!The setting of a grubby 1970’s oil rig lends itself perfectly to a claustrophobic horror experience. The rig itself feels like a character in the game and the old girl certainly starts to get worse for wear as the story progresses.After an initial meet and greet with the crew an ‘event’ leaves us tasked with going into the guts of the rig and saving our friends and coworkers as we quickly realise there’s something unseen going on.Often times the player character questions why it must be him who needs to undertake the life and death missions, even sarcastically pushing back at times. I liked the self aware nod and realism of this. Too often the everyman-hero in the game is willing to dive in headfirst into danger without a word or complaint.The decor, lighting and ambience of the rig are fantastic inside and out. The music and sound effects all add to the overall impact of the experience.As for the horror sections, they generally consist of short-ish set pieces. The player only needing to evade the threat for a large room and few corridors at a time to be safe. As opposed to say an Outlast where the player must evade for long periods of time before reaching ‘safety’. On the subject of ‘safe zones’ they are pretty frequent. This will surely be a plus for players less than enthusiastic about being chased relentlessly to their wits end, however for more experienced horror survival players it could feel overly generous.The game is well paced, not too long, not too short, the breaks in the tension felt well timed and as the story progressed I found myself being really curious as to how it would all end.There are some jump scares that will play well with streamers and the game is suitably gory enough to satisfy the 90’s horror fan in you.I would recommend this game for any horror enthusiasts, as a very reasonably priced enjoyable evening or two of terror!

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely review games, but this?This is cosmic horror done The voice acting is superb, the atmosphere is on point, and It genuinely terrified me, which is hard for horror games to do to me. The Thing meets Color Out of Space, with a healthy dash of absolute terror that comes from hearing the distorted insane ramblings of your co-workers as their corrupted husks they once called bodies slaughter their friends. Lovecraft thought that being able to describe, or quantify such horrendous creatures and concepts detracted from them.This proves him wrong.Buy this game. _childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one and it makes me wish steam had a neautral option. The best way I could describe the game is that its not really a game, its almost a visual novel. The entire game bright yellow paint guides you absolutely everywhere and the game doesnt have anything that remotely resembles a puzzle. Its also incredibly short, taking only 5 hours to finish with me exploring every nook and crany. So all that said really the only thing this game has going for is the atmosphere and the story and are those really enough to carry a $30 game?Yeah actually, in this case it is. Unreal Engine 5 is used to its full potential to create a visually impressive and moody enviornment. Combined with the incredible monster design and the stellar voice acting this game managed to hit alot of their major emotional beats perfectly. I would have liked if we got more time with our main cast of characters, even a few scattered text logs or audio logs would have helped, but overall I found myself caring for most of them and when the credit rolled at the end I can honestly say I felt something. _childDocuments_.review: This is a MASTERPIECE of exploration, narrative story-telling, immersive game-play all gripped in the clutches of a terrible horror from which you must escape.  A lot of people say it takes around 4 hours to complete, but I've just come through the other end after 23 hours (for reasons below).  I think the game is worth every penny and not at all over-priced.The pace of the game is fantastic.  Some sections allow for exploration, some for battling the environmental dangers, and some for 'other things'.  I found it a huge relief that quieter sections interspersed the high-adrenaline horror sections.  There are two game-techniques used that are sometimes seen in a negative light: the yellow go-this-way clues, and the paths of no return.  But in THIS title, both were needed (and appreciated).  The rig is so vast and detailed, you'd simply be lost in minutes without these clues, especially as destruction ensues, and when a route you've taken closes behind you, it reassures you're headed in the right direction.Checkpoints are saved frequently so a reload is never too far away from where you were.  This is probably a good thing because I managed somehow to get stuck on one of the weights in the leg of the oil rig and had to reload (this was the only glitch I encountered).  Death can be fairly frequent because climbing and jumps and such are human-paced - you're no batman in this!  You'll manage a jump like someone who is dressed in heavy waterproofs, and who is tired, scared, injured.  Same with running - you're no Usain Bolt!The graphics are simply mind-blowing.  I can't praise them enough.  The entire oil rig - it's vast, detailed, it feels accurate to every section, platform, pipe and valve (I wouldn't of course KNOW this, but it feels it).  The reason my play time is so long is two-fold: firstly, spending an amazing amount of time just taking in the environment and exploring, admiring the craft and workmanship that made something feel SO real...   Secondly, having to, um, drop the screen for a bit until I was brave enough to move on!  Repeatedly.You see - I LOVE oil rigs, but I don't love horror!And so the rest of this review is here to help my fellow cowardly players!  I'm going to describe the sort of encounters you might experience (in spoilers) so you can decide for yourself if this game is a good one for you...These first spoilers simply describe the type of horror sequences (ie the gameplay involved, whether there is killing, sneaking, running).  There are no story spoilers.If you want to know where the scariest part is, then read the next spoiler.    Only read if you need this to help you through horror sections!Still Wakes the Deep is an incredible immersive experience.  If horror isn't your thing but you REALLY like the look of the story and the setting, it's really doable.  I had to think long and hard about whether I could play this (other games like Dead Space are a total NOPE for me), but in the end I had an absolute blast and am looking forward to a replay now I know exactly what happens where!

_childDocuments_.review: The meticulously designed setting and the credible, well-acted dialogue give the game more realism than you usually find in games of this kind. In my opinion, it's closer to Everybody's Gone To The Rapture (big surprise), Layers of Fear or Outlast than to SOMA, Firewatch, Tacoma or Gone Home, all of the latter I liked more. For my taste a bit too simple and overpriced, but worth the time if bought on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: WOW, incredible game. Feels good to play, looks good, and I mean, the voice acting is just top notch. Great voice actors just do so much for the immersion of a game. This game did a great job of sucking me in, with the ambiance, and great voice acting, it made me forget I was looking at a monitor. Has some pretty scary moments too. As a pretty seasoned horror-gamer, it takes a very well made experience to get me creeped out. The story is well laid out as well. Very interesting, and did a great job of making me care about the characters. A common complaint people seem to have with this game is its shorter run time, but it took me 7 hours to beat, and, personally, I find a lot of games try to justify their price with filler content or drawn out segments, and they tend to suffer for it. This game doesn't do that, and I appreciate it. Also only experienced one minor glitch throughout the whole thing, and WOW is that rare nowadays.Long story short, this game is easily worth what it costs, and it excels at nearly everything its trying to do. This shortish game left me feeling vastly more satisfied than 99% of AAA games today, proving to me that it really is an indie world right now.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn about how to review this game. It's one of the ones that really makes me wish steam had a more nuanced rating system. The story is incredible, the character acting is unparalleled, sound design is flawless, environment is beautiful and immersive. Several scenes are horrifying, depressing and terrifying all at the same time (in a good way). I was extremely invested in the story and the fate of the characters.The gameplay is effectively absent. It barely feels like a game. 90% of the gameplay is traversal, which is never challenging but occasionally frustrating. There are a few stealth sections which are pretty solid. The interactions with the environment are super trivial and becomes extremely repetitive (pull down to open, press l2 to balance). There are no player choices to speak of. I assume when a game is labeled "lovecraftian" there's going to be some investigative component. There isn't. It really is just traversing the environment, and not in a challenging way like Mirror's Edge. It's just walking and responding to prompts. I expect replay value is basically 0.I certainly don't regret playing the game. But, for a 4.5 hour cinematic experience, I would definitely recommend waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Dan Pinchbeck is my favorite writer, and my biggest artistic inspiration. I've been looking forward to this game for a very long time, and I think it is well worth the wait. The atmosphere and character of the world that Pinchbeck builds is stunning -- both visually and narratively. I don't think that it's as profound of an experience as  or  but it's still compelling throughout, and the ending is just as emotionally impactful as the rest of his work (seriously, this guy knows how to write a good ending).For what it's worth, I've already played this twice in the past twenty-four hours, and I think I liked it even more on my second playthrough. I'm sad to see that Pinchbeck has left The Chinese Room, but I hope that he keeps up the great work, because I'll play any game or read any book that he writes.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent presentation (visuals and audio) but absolutely nothing special. I appreciated the human aspects of the story; the characters feel like real men in a bad situation. The script and voice acting are solid (even if some of the characters, like the boss, come off as cartoonishly over the top).Unfortunately, the game is insanely overhyped. It boils down to a relatively short, completely linear, on-rails experience with little actual *gameplay* (just pressing a button here and there to interact with a lever or a phone or door, etc). That might be fine if there was more atmosphere or if the scares were more intense, but it's pretty "meh." Any sense of dread just comes from the protagonist's desire to escape, not because the monsters or atmosphere are particularly scary.Not really a horror game, more like a prolonged obstacle course on an oil rig where you'll occasionally get annoying game over screens. I didn't find it to be worthwhile, but maybe you will.

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5/10. I played this game on my bro's Xbox on GamePass, and then came home and bought it here so I could own and support it more directly, if that tells you anything, but I might be a little weird.I admit my expectations weren't extremely high, because I wasn't sure what to expect from The Chinese Room.The first thing I want to call attention to is how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ excellent the voice performances are. It absolutely nails the setting, an oil rig in the North Sea, manned by a bunch of Scots. The accents / dialect / language are impeccable, you will probably need subtitles if you are an average English speaker. The story gets pretty emotional and the voice deliver on that.The game is fairly linear, but that didn't bother me in this case. This game does a lot with its horror set pieces, and never relies on cheap scares. The mystery of the antagonist in this game is at once chilling and compelling. Without spoiling too much, if you like  you should love this.It's pretty short at 4-5 hours, but I would happily pay $35 for this experience, maybe more. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. I have never fallen in love with a game so quickly, or connected so well with the characters before. I'm not a huge fan of playing horror games (in fact, I've never really played any before), but this one really caught my attention. The entity, the mutations, the setting, the voice acting, the interactions of the characters were all so  interesting. I so desperately wanted them to live, and the ending was so brutal but also important. I loved the story, and I don't mind a linear game. In fact, I like it more than an open world environment where I don't know where to go and I'm just wandering about for hours aimlessly. I had a little trouble with the controls at times, but it didn't stop me. My only huge gripe, if you can call it that, is knowing I will never see more of these characters and this story beyond what's in this game. I so wish I could see more of them in some way or the other. I loved how they talked to each other and wished I could see more of them, especially prior to the events of the game. The oil rig setting was so fascinating. The game itself played like an interactive movie, which was very enjoyable for me. This has somehow become my favorite game and I will play it more in the future, just to enjoy the story and characters again.

_childDocuments_.review: Generally not recommended. Maybe for select few, but with some major caveats.I know Unreal Engine is the most accessible tool for small studios, but I wish it would be dropped altogether. UE title almost always means stutters, performance issues, and bugs... No matter the hardware.I'd only recommend this title to a very specific person. There isn't exactly a surplus of Lovecraftian nautical horror out there, and for me.. the relatively short length was a plus. The atmosphere, art direction, music, and voice acting all impress. As a game? Not so much.The gameplay is the biggest disappointment here. I can only turn so many valves and switches before I just wish I was watching the game on autopilot. The movement is some of the clunkiest I've seen. You know those dreams you have where your brain can't really simulate what motion and gravity feel like in real life? When your punches feel like they're in slow motion? That's this game. Climbing, running, jumping... It all feels like you're stuck in peanut butter.In the end I loved the setting.. The rig is undeniably a character itself. You really do start to become familiar with every rivet by the end of the game. The artists knocked it out of the park here, despite the UE shortcomings.Pick this one up (on sale) if you want a bite sized horror experience. Or just watch a stream. You won't be missing much in the way of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow what a ride! This is one of the few games that kept me thinking about it during the day. The environmental sounds and the voice acting is absolutely fantastic.Also the environmental puzzles although light I found to be a lot of fun.What really makes this one special to me however is the story. It feels like those guys know each other for a very long time. The way they interact and how the story progresses is authentic and believable. I was desperate to know how the story unfolds. I had a few graphical glitches here and there but nothing serious. For a just released title it ran fine for me.It's a bit short for the asking price but I'd rather enjoy something short but intriguing. What brings it home is one of the best and memorable stories I've seen in a game.Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: - I really enjoyed this game. If you are a fan of Lovecraftian stories and you like good writing and good characters, I think it's definitely worth your time. Mechanically it's pretty basic walking-sim/survival horror fare. Sprint, crouch, pick up items and throw them as distractions, and multi-input interactions to open doors and activate machinery. Some Pros:I love the setting (a Scottish Oil Rig in the mid 1970s) and I really appreciate the voice actors' performances. I'm not someone who cares about "representation" in media, however it was really cool to hear so many accents and voices from regions of the UK that you don't see (hear) very often. I also very much appreciated how the subtitles translate the slang and Gaelic into more common English for us non-Scots. The environmental design is fantastic. The game does an incredible job of invoking all sorts of discomfort and phobias; I have never before felt this hesitant to swim through water in a video game. The story is very good and I won't spoil anything. It tells a very human story amidst this supernatural disaster. All the characters feel real and (for the most part) likable. The monster design was very unique and straight out of nightmares. They also do a great job of not showing you all that much for quite a while; the first encounter is terrifying because you only catch a slight glimpse of the screaming thing chasing you.Lastly, I think this game is  in as much as what is happening is unknowable and has very disturbing implications. So many games these days follow the trope of "slap some tentacles on it and call it Lovecraftian" without  of the themes or ideas that are what make cosmic horror so interesting.Some Cons:The game is  linear. That is ok with me as the writing and pacing are so good that I didn't feel too robbed of a good time. However, there were a few moments where the on-rails nature of the game clashed with what I wanted to do. I'd find the occasional invisible wall, which felt very out of place considering how claustrophobic and narrow so much of the environment normally is. Probably the worst moment for me was when I thought I was being clever by turning off a flame valve, luring a monster into the path of the fire, and turning the valve back on and the monster just clipped right through the flame with no effect at all. This was extra annoying when later on . There were a few moments that took me right out of the game and shattered the immersion. Here are a few examples: one time I went the wrong way when evading a monster during a sneaking section and the monster saw me, but couldn't get to me. However, I was totally cornered and had no way to escape or distract the monster, so after about 3 minutes of waiting, I just walked into the monster to let it kill me so I could restart the section. Another time I goofed up a platforming segment and fell to some scaffolding I wasn't supposed to be on. There was no way off the scaffolding and no way to fall of it to my death, so I had to restart from a checkpoint. Lastly, there was one chase sequence where I was supposed to jump AND GRAB onto a ledge, but I didn't realize I needed to try and grab it until the prompt popped up for <1 second and I fell into the sea.Lastly, I don't think I'll replay this game even though there are, apparently, quite a few achievements that I missed. It was a really good ~5 hour experience, but I have no desire to go back and do it again since I know how it all ends.

_childDocuments_.review: If one were to be cynical,  could be described as a script the player walks through,  obeying the odd on-screen prompt to clear obstacles, until the game is over and leaving no incentive to play it ever again. _childDocuments_.review: *mild-spoilers ahead*I've agonised over my rating - but Valve only lets me provide a binary response, so.. well here we are.Firstly, some parts of the game are fantastic. The sense of place and time - I could smell the stale tobacco that's permeated every inch of that tartan carpet and stained the formica. I'd have happily paid to just walk around and explore the rig. The combination of the desolate exteriors with the endless sea and the claustrophobic interiors let the story wind through the small environment with some variety. The middling things - the story and the characters.As many people have said, it was nice to have some proper Scottish characters and have them well voiced.I did not for one moment however, care about a single one of them though. They're drawn with some very broad strokes (Will the guy with National Front posters, be a nice chap? *strokes chin*). There is the clearly special NPC you're meant to care about (we know this as you have conversations that don't just tell you to go somewhere) - and that ends precisely as expected. I felt infinitely worse about my horse in Ghost of Tsushima.The plot was 'fine' - but not novel and didn't really take anything off in any unexpected direction. After 'the incident' happens, you'll find yourself asking a question that takes the game until the last 10 minutes to surprise you with..The poor.The game is very very linear. Walk/Jump/Swim forwards and aim for the yellow thing.I saw in another comment that they were planning on allowing the yellow to be turned off - that won't help. Whether the yellow is there or not, there's always only one way to go. Without it you're just going to have a more frustrating time finding the single place you can go and bouncing off a lot of invisible walls. Initially I'd got excited when spotting what looked like options ("Do I carry on forward, or duck into that tunnel?") - but there's never an actual choice. A subtle branch spotted simply means the main path is about to be a dead end, or the story will be taking you back through this area. There are no superfluous areas to explore - don't waste your time looking. Follow the yellow. The plot is entirely driven by MacGuffins - Character X will tell you that you need to go to Y, to press something to make Z happen. The character will be behind a window, on a ledge, on a phone, have to remain seated to press a button (as the game clearly doesn't support two characters interacting). Once you realize nobody can ever follow you and every movement that isn't you is scripted, then being told to go and rescue somebody.. well you know it's not happening. There's going to be no cluster of survivors path-finding across an open deck to a rescue vessel.I think there would have been a great 2 hour game, which you rattle through without engaging your brain. I think there could also have been another game, where you spend hours free-roaming the rig getting to know your colleagues, delving into back-story and performing menial rig-tasks, before it all kicks off.What we got here just feels a little imbalanced. Despite the length of my whining, I did enjoy the game and am glad I bought and played it.If you can get this in a sale and come into it knowing what to expect (and what not to expect) - it's a fun experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing about Still Wakes the deep, don't listen to reviews, play it yourself, i can guarantee that you will not regret it.From the casts Incredible voice acting to the oil rigs layout and beautiful design structure,As someones who's been out to an oil rig the depth of detail is astounding such as safety pins through the release lines in the lifeboats, to the sad depressing canteen where shift patterns only able to see the same people over and over again. SWTP enraptures story telling, sound design and visual stimulation. Look if your looking for an action packed game this probably isn't for you which is okay.However if you want to feel like part of a family, be brought into this world of SWTD where your seemingly carrying out an ordinary day until something goes disastrously wrong and you genuinely feel the fear of the MC then i cannot recommend this game enough.Beautifully made.Beautifully written.A Beautiful piece of Art.Congratulations Chinese Room & Secret Mode. You really have broken the ceiling with this fantastic video game.10/10Note: Being called the C word in Scotland is very normal, culture init.

_childDocuments_.review: A well executed immersive survival horror.It delivers everything, what the genre is strong at. The environments are absolutely beautiful and gameplay-wise, well designed. You'll be able to explore the area or always find maps of it before... the game puts you under stress. :)The sound design is top notch. The acting is very well done as well. The dialogues are very well written, although the drama didn't really hit the mark for me. Machine for Pigs was way more memorable for the drama and mood elements, than this one.It would spoil stuff if I went into specifics, but the level designers deserve a medal, for they recognize, that level layouts could spoil gameplay features and it shows, that they take that into account.The monsters are creepy as hell, visually very well done! The throwable item mechanic is bad. For one, I've hit extremely large hitboxes on props multiple times, which prevented me from throwing items far enough. The other terrible factor is that crawling, "shimmy-ing" in narrow spaces, climbing waist-high objects make you drop your held item. You can't open/close a door in this game while holding a mug in your hand. Also an immersive game means, HUD should be minimal. Overall, the game delivers well on this aspect (you can disable elements), but interaction icons are too big and aren't positioned on the edges, where they should be. Also, while holding an item, the game constantly shows two huge (smallest setting) icons saying "LMB throw", "RMB drop". This info should be a one-time tutorial, then leave them out from the HUD entirely.Underwater controls aren't good. Quick-Time Events underwater is done even worse. Those areas really dropped the fun factor of the game and it didn't manage to climb back enough by the ending.If you like the genre, I'm pretty sure you're going to love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished it. 3.8 hours and I wasn't "sprinting" through the game though lack of collectables or anything of the sort added to that. Pros: Good initial premiseGreat voice acting/cast Good pacing and tense momentsBody Horror. Feels very "Colour out of space" for the first hour or so. Cons: Areas felt reused (a lot)No elaboration on the "event" whatsoever. Not even notes or in game text (compared to something like Dead Space or Bioshock this leaves a kind of hollow experience) Ending was a bit cliche Extremely simple gameplay loops and a little repetitive. Performance wasn't great. IDK what that 3D resolution slider is but that's where ALL your frames go. 50% I could get 120 fps on a 3080. 100% I could barely get 60. Rest of the options did nothing in terms of performance cept maybe lighting and shadows. Conclusion. Wait for a big sale. £30.00 for shy of four hours gameplay without replayability isn't a good deal. This is the kind of game you give to someone that doesn't mind a slower pace of game with extremely simple controls/game loops. Perhaps a relatively new gamer looking to try a horror game as the game has no combat, crafting, skills of any kind.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my second review, in truth. My first one was negative because i was... hit badly by the ending. Someone closed to me decided to unalive himself, and what happens at the end of the game truly brought back negative emotions.But that's a "me" problem, it was not the fault of the game. The game is good. It has excellent atmosphere. I liked it, and the recreation of a sea rig is just wonderful. Moreover, i have a bit of a soft spot for scottish and australian accents (the latter are not in this game).A dev also answered kindly to my admittedly quite emotional first review, and this has value. They didn't deserve that.And the memory of my friend doesn't deserve that i act dishonorably.The game is good, if you like horror walking sims with light puzzles and occasional stealth sections.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually a fan of horror or psychological horror games, but I decided to give this one a try. From the moment I started playing, I was completely hooked, largely because of the captivating story—I just had to know how it would end. The graphics, atmosphere, and sound design are exceptional, adding depth to the experience. The ending left me feeling empty and deeply sad. What an incredible, emotional journey in such a short game!
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: 100% recommend this game to anyone who wants an experience. The visuals are stunning, the soundscapes are amazing, the atmosphere is incredible, and the voice acting is beyond a doubt some of the best I've ever heard in a game. Anyone who wants a big bombastic game with lots of combat and exciting action? This probably isn't for you. This is an environment you want to invest yourself into, and all-around a great environment to become immersed in, and if you're playing this expecting a fight-for-your-life monster-killing action game then you're doing yourself and the game an injustice. Love the characters, love the story, love the atmosphere, but don't ask for something it's not advertised as.I do have to mention though, as much as I love the experience I had with this game, it was shockingly hard on my PC to run. Despite having at least the recommended PC requirements, in most cases better, I still had to turn down all the graphical settings to the lowest I could stand, and I was even then getting occasional frame jumps and big lag spikes, all while my poor PCs fans are running like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ airplane the entire time - especially noticeable while entering the deck (perhaps the water graphics?) and ESPECIALLY whenever there were a lot of moving parts or people on screen. I'm incredibly grateful for my noise-cancelling headphones, else the PC trying to take off would've absolutely drowned out the game audio. Despite all this, I did still enjoy my time playing, but it was often distracting to be having to pause and wait for the lag spikes to pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: It has disappointed me quite a bit. It's not a bad running or escaping simulator, but it doesn't stand out on anything. When I finished it, it left me quite cold. _childDocuments_.review: I was so excited when I heard that this game had come out and I had no idea it was being developed. I absolutely loved Dear Esther and Everybody's Gone to the Rapture.
