_childDocuments_.review: Worst horror game 2024.Story rich is fine, but when it's all there is to a game, it should be good. It doesn't deliver here. It's another awful retelling of psychological horror great SH2. Protagonist with inexplicable dark past he either won't admit/remember as the world around him changes to the whims of a spiritual power punishing people for their sins and general humanity for it's hubris. It's been done before, and infinitely better. The great mystery of SH2's story was how it told its story through subtly, this game throws it at your face without any nuance or grace. Then this all brought down to even more understandable and relatable terms to just any judeo-christian deity so it's just another angry god story, instead of a character finally coming to terms with his past and what brought him to such a decision, it's just an guy being punished for him being an actual terrible person.Game play could be nonexistent and I'd probably have more enjoyment from just a visual novella. Interact with X place at Y oh no, don't get seen by Z. But making collision and the game eating inputs any task now becomes a chore.The voice acting is fine, it's just a real tragedy they had to act out this horrendous story, apologies to the voice actors.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a supernatural Eldritch Horror, survival type.  You cant fight back against enemies, but you can distract and run.  The environments were creepy, the enemies the same.  There were jump scares and audio elements that added to the creep factor.  7.1 surround headphones were WILD for this; the audio slaps.The game is very linear in its progression.  Yet, you will occasionally retrace your steps or enter parts of the map that you have traversed before.  Just know... if you dislike linear level design and game play on rails this may not be for you.The story events were pretty engaging and the reason for calamity was mysterious,  It def fit an eldritch horror / alan wake-esque altered world event scenario.  The voice acting was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ phenomenal and really made the characters seem believable.  The accents also sounded genuine and not forced.Graphics, visuals, and lighting effects were also very well done.  They weren't so good that I forgot I was playing a game, but the environment design / lighting / textures and shaders really made me feel like I was navigating an oil rig heading for disaster.I only had a couple small issues with getting stuck in the environment and I simply reloaded at the last checkpoint.  My biggest complaint.....  I wanted more.  I need more of this story.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Its a pretty linear game, narrative focused with some light puzzles that even an idiot like me can solve. (thank goodness), The horror is pretty good, not many games actually make me jump but this one managed to a few times, I played it with my mom passing the mantle of playing between deaths and she enjoyed it as well, Great story, great horror, great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: THIS IS ONE OF THE BEST HORROR GAMES I'VE EVER PLAYED! It's got a nice mix of story, horror & stress momentum. I don't know WHAT the **** people are complaining about and how being "linear" is a bad thing. How come we haven't learned from big gaming studios who make this huge games that run like crap, have tons of glitches and have no heart and soul? Heart and soul is what this game A C T U A L L Y  have a LOT of - and you can tell! Some of the puzzles were a bit "Huh?" but nothing that made me get stuck for more than maybe a few extra minutes. Visually it's simply stunning, lighting and design is amazing, the audio design and the voice acting is superb and there's nothing really for me to complain about. Oh actually, SOME of the first person animations were a little bit funky, like climbing things, running etc. But it was such a minor thing for the most part I didn't pay attention to it. I spent around 6 hours in this game, and I did not think that I would dive in my second session and cry over some story related events - but I did. Such a great journey. Maybe gaming in 2024 isn't dead after all.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one you have to know and want to play before buying it. It is a walking simulator and it is a short game. I clocked in around 4.5 hours, worth the time spent, for sure, whether it's worth the asking price is up to you.It is certainly good, it is well produced, the sound design and voice acting is phenomenal, the story is good, the animations/facial animations are very well done, it's all quite impressive. Unfortunately, as I said, it's a walking simulator and that's what you'll be doing for the majority of the game, walking and QTEs, decently made and satisfying QTEs but QTEs all the same. I think there was potential for a better game here, as there always is BUT what is on offer right now is a really great experience that clearly has been loved to the bones and worked hard to fruition.I recommend it with the caveat that you HAVE to know what you're in for, it's a really good movie that you get to play, don't expect a revolutionary game but expect a worthwhile time investment.

_childDocuments_.review: "Still Wakes the Deep" is an atmospheric horror game that excels in creating a deeply unsettling experience. Set on a North Sea oil rig, the game's claustrophobic environment amplifies the tension as you explore narrow corridors and dimly lit rooms. The narrative draws you in with a sense of isolation and helplessness, where every creak and shadow adds to the eerie atmosphere. The game's visuals and sound design are top-notch, effectively immersing players into its grim, mysterious world.While the pacing can be slow at times, especially for those expecting more action, the game shines in building suspense and delivering moments of heart-pounding terror. It’s more about exploration and psychological horror than combat, which might not appeal to everyone, but for fans of games like "Amnesia" or "SOMA," it’s a hauntingly captivating experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Do not spend $35 on this. At most it's worth $5-$10. It's interactivity is almost nonexistent, requring you to press two buttons to show the next animation it wants to. And the most horrifying fail states merely reset you 10 seconds earlier to avoid The Thing.I managed to make it to just under the refund time limit, based on the raving reviews of the story, before I decided an unreal engine demo with QTEs wasn't worth it. Then I watched a playthrough to see what they're raving about. The story is a very GAMER (derogatory) view of manual labor. You are the one smart guy on any job site, an electrician. You're missing Christmas and New Years with your wife and daughters because you're the kind of POS who actual gets in physical fights with people. ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan because the communists, fascists, and superiors (who are dumber than you) you work with push too hard to meet the alien corporate office's production demands. So begins your slogful journey to escape the horror of an oil rig. The lovecrafitian horrors you must avoid to make it back to your wife are the communist, fascist, idiot boss. Coworkers driven mad by the horrors of drilling on an oil rig. _childDocuments_.review: The ocean waves hide darker secrets than the stars can even imagine.A fine line between classic Lovecraft, where the common people are forced to confront the indescribable, unexplainable unknown. Recite what you saw and be declared deranged.Mixed with a beautiful, more modern edge, where even the most bizarre can make just a sliver of sense through human connection.An excellent, narrative-driven horror game that plays smoothly with light stealth elements and breathtaking environments. Every part of this story is highlighted by its fantastic art direction, where darkness gets warped by bright, colorful lights and the reflection of the water that sneaks into the cracks of the decaying oil rig that's surrendering to the weight and forceful invasion of a mind-and-flesh-bending organic monstrosity.And it wouldn't be fair to leave the amazing cast of voice actors unmentioned, as they put a beautiful, cherry red, satin bow around the delightfully horrific package that is Still Wakes the Deep.I don't want to spoil too much, I just want everyone who's even remotely interested to take their own dive into this fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good horror game overall with a good story and characters. The art and sound really carry the game, and give you the feeling of being isolated on an oil rig that's falling apart. Can't really say it does anything new or unpredictable though.I would say the low point of the game is the monster encounters, they kind of suck balls. Considering how little gameplay is in the game, this could have been a place they put special attention towards, but it's incredibly lazy. The monsters just patrol back and forth and you just go from cover to cover. If you're seen, you just instantly lose. Yeah that's right, the monster doesn't attack you, you don't have any health, it's just you're seen, and you reload. So basically instead of having a confrontation with a monster, like a horror game is supposed to do, these stealth sections are just playing Metal Gear for 5 minutes. Actually even Metal Gear is more tense because you have player agency when you're spotted, that's what makes it engaging. In the walking sim horror genre, The Chinese Room games seems to nestle comfortably between the highs like Frictional's games and the lows like Bloober Team games. If you like their previous work like Machine for Pigs, you'll like this, it's a similar sort of deal. They have all the elements there, they just need to spruce up the gameplay and give you more options for how to play.

But I could listen to that back and forth banter between the workers and Caz for hours and hours.Really appreciate the read of this game as Cronenbergian. Lovecraft never had an eye for human behavior, while Cronenberg is all about the icky parts of human nature.David Cronenberg protagonists are often characterized as somehow "incomplete" or "inadequate" in some way, a deeply flawed and too-passive person.Caz is a great Cronenbergian main character, because despite trying to get everything right, you can just feel he's doomed.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes The Deep is a first person action adventure psychological horror game which take palce on an oil rig in the 1970's in the North Sea. You play an electrician named Cameron "Caz" McLeary who has to navigate and survive the weather and monsters after an incident on the rig. The GoodThis game really surprised me from the jump, the story is amazing and the horror aspect of this game really draws you in. So many elements went into this game to make it feel the a great survival horror. Level design is unique in its own way and the characters well created to help the story and not basic, they grow and change as the story progresses. Unlike other horror game it does just what you need it to along with the simple puzzles that add a nice touch to the story as well. The location and setting for everything was really satisfying and I loved the funny/witty dialogue that comes with the characters. The BadPart of this game did feature some bugs and issues unfortunately. At the begging of the game audio bugs and even some movement issues did plague me for a few minutes. During the game specifically the running sequences i noticed some lag but nothing to major. Optimization overall wasn't terrible but the game did run a little hot on high settings but nothing to crazy.Overall Thoughts And Score Still Wakes The Deep was an amazing experience truly from start to finish. I loved the story and they way the game played out and how characters really played a part in helping and hunting you. This game really makes you feel like your watching a horror movie just in control of the character in its own unique way. You get immersed in trying to solve the mystery and help save others. Id highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a nice fun paced survival horror game. This game takes around 4-5 hours to be but overall that to me felt perfect in time length to go with the cost of the game.Score 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's important to stress out of the gate that this might not be a game for everyone, it's quite short and the mechanics are straightforward but it's an absolute masterclass in good acting, likeable characters and atmosphere and environment doing a ton of heavy lifting. With a game like this, you're going in for the experience more so than the gameplay and it certainly delivered for me personally. I found the setting and characters to be a refreshing change of pace. It was especially nice getting to hear some Scottish and British voices that weren't just cartoonish cliches dialed up to 11. The characters and actors felt relatable and I genuinely enjoyed a lot of the patter and found myself chuckling along on many occasions. The presentation and performance were also very impressive for me. I'm running a 4080 and a 7800x3D and I was able to comfortably run on Epic settings at 1440p with DLSS balanced and frame gen turned on hitting around 100fps most of the time. Baring in mind, the higher settings are using ray tracing for the reflections, GI and I believe shadows and maybe ambient occlusion. In spite of all these heavy settings, the game feels very fluid and I never felt like the game was chugging at any time and the visual returns are generally spectacular. If you can get over the short runtime then it's well worth checking this one out because it's a really neat and refreshing experience. More of this type of thing please Chinese Room!

_childDocuments_.review: I write this as someone who's played and enjoyed the Chinese Room's original brand of minimalist, narrative-driven gameplay. The studio has undergone major changes through the years, and Still Wakes the Deep is proof of that. Not just a "walking sim," this has a modern, cinematic flavor. Unfortunately, I was very disappointed. If this game were priced more modestly after some polishing, I could possibly recommend it, albeit with massive caveats attached.Other reviews have mentioned it, but the amount of convenient yellow signposting in the level design really is beyond excessive, making the game unintentionally amusing rather than intentionally horrifying, regardless of the excellent atmosphere. There are also many repetitive interactions throughout, such as breaking locks, turning valves, and opening vents. When you're forced to see the same animations over and over again, it easily comes across as padding. Additionally, I felt no tension in the sequences of danger involving pseudo-platforming and stealth, because they require too little of the player. Even for something that obviously aims to be straightforward, there can always be new elements introduced to replace old ones. Occasional QTEs with the same button prompt during a climb aren't exciting, and neither is tossing objects to distract an enemy. Perhaps a handful of times--not repeatedly over the span of 4-6 hours. I found it strange how areas contain several lockers to hide inside, yet I never had to. Lastly, this point isn't as significant, though staying within the subject of level design: Areas being separated by loading screen doors contributes to a pace that feels less immersive, given that it's another repetitive interaction you're sitting through. I was often underwhelmed to realize I didn't accomplish much and I'm already getting funneled into the next area.On the technical front, I encountered several bugs, a few recurring like the double black screen after dying and reloading, and not being able to grab onto a ladder until I walk away and approach again. In one particular stealth sequence, the enemy got stuck near the objective, allowing me to waltz past and get a nice smell of his tendrils. Besides the bugs, I think the controls could use some tweaking. For example, when crawling through a tight space, you crouch to initiate the animation, but the game makes you stand when coming out the other side. It's tedious to re-press the crouch button during stealth sections.Although I miss the flowery writing from the Chinese Room's previous games, and the story here doesn't have as many thematic layers to it, I was still engaged thanks to sharp dialogue and great performances by the cast. Despite all my complaints, I did have an otherwise convincing physical presence in the setting, connecting with the protagonist. The fact he has a full body and casts a shadow helps, too. If TCR makes another story-driven game, I encourage them to rethink how they balance storytelling with gameplay. As other titles have shown, you can be cinematic without being passive, and you can be minimalist without recycling.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, after four hours of playing (with some breaks in between), the game has been really good. It's not quite what I was expecting after seeing some favored YouTubers talking about playing it, but it is still a great game.I do want to point out, the game has a Standard and Story mode option for gameplay. I noticed a lot of Reddit reviews stating the story mode takes out chase scenes and having to sneak or engage with the enemies--it does NOT. It only limits how difficult these encounters are. So if you saw the reviews stating story mode is a walking sim that your grandma can play for the story line without having to rush like I did, they are wrong. This isn't a search and find or collection based game--it is a walking sim in a lot of ways, but there are encounters where you do have to sneak and sometimes run away. I noticed a lot of comments stating there are only three of these events in the entire game for story mode--that is also not true. At three hours in (not knowing how close to the finish I am), I have already had six encounters on story-mode. Not exactly what I wanted for a story mode option as, after reading reviews, I was hoping to be able to relax and not severely panic during chase scenes (IRL personal issues), but it isn't too terrible. I do want to add after finishing the game at 11.7 hours, there were more like 10-15 chase scenes in total. You can try to sneak through many, but several still end in a chase regardless of how well you sneak. There are some jump scares where you have to press whatever button is specified. There are many events where you have to run through obstacles to escape areas, both during chase scenes and areas that are, not timed, but you do have a short period before disaster hits if you're not quick.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is a technically impressive, but narratively unfocused, horror-themed walking simulator. I was entertained enough that I played it all in one sitting, but I don’t recommend paying full price. I got it around 40% off and I think that’s a fairer value.The game’s setting is astounding in scale and attention to detail. It’s one of the most immersive games I’ve ever played. The oil rig is this monumental structure that feels as big as a small city. You will feel so small playing this game.Music, voice acting, and sound design could not have been better, and I mean that. The dichotomy of live strings and vocals with a huge mechano-synthesizer was a pleasure to listen to, and really kept me hooked. It intertwined seamlessly with the industrial noise going on all around you. The character’s voices sold me on their stories immediately, the passion and authenticity in their delivery was balanced very well with the actual script. Speaking of characters, I want to thank the design team for making these people look normal. They look like people who work on an oil rig. They’re not fashion models or Overwatch characters.The gameplay itself is barebones, because it is just a walking simulator, but I was very focused on the narrative and environment. I found it quite refreshing that there was no lore bits or collectibles, you just… play the game. While I do find the level sequences quite short (usually under 10 minutes), the result is that a real full game released in 2024 using Unreal Engine 5 is… just over 10 Gb. Astounding.I found the story to be simple and pretty predictable, but reasonably well done. There’s not any real character development, as too much of the player character’s backstory is exposed in the beginning, but this is more survival focused with elements of a backstory rather than a Genuine Emotional Journey. The characters make a few decisions and things happen, good enough. However, you do not make a decision. Not once. You are railroaded through the entire game, aside from the very beginning where you explore a small section of the map and meet the crew. Every single doorway not directly related to your current objective? Blocked, broken, locked. I mostly didn’t mind this in the moment, to be honest, which is why it sits here as a neutral point. But on retrospection, it would not have been much extra work to hide some horror or a short optional passage behind a door you have to make the decision to open. The game is not scary. Like at all. I get scared pretty easily in games that I’m not even half this immersed in, and the reason is, as nicely as possible: The monsters look unfinished.I do appreciate that the thing that takes over the rig, this indescribable Lovecraftian entity, does stay that way the entire time. It’s not hinted at in a series of journals, no one tells you a folk tale their Mammy told them when they were wee, no one even really comments on how it looks both inviting and incredibly dangerous.But the monsters you encounter all look like chewed bubble gum. They have some distinguishing features, but they’re basically without rhyme or reason. Extra eyes, extra arms, antlers (in the ocean?), and a few of them have gut-tentacles they use to get around. One of them is different, but its design is so bad I laughed out loud at it when it started chasing me. Utilizing an approach like Shadow over Innsmouth, where they are more subtly disfigured into having fish-like features, would have been much more effective, because they would at least resemble the characters you meet in the first part of the game. In fact, most of the gore, gut meat, and other viscera strewn about the place looks like it’s from a Playstation game, and it’s 10 times more noticeable when you’re running Ultra graphics and the environment around you might as well be coming from a GoPro. All my pulse increasing experiences came from the environment. Missing a jump or having to swim through dark and creaking machinery underneath the rig were much scarier than being chased by an under cooked meatball. The only time I felt scared by “A Creature” was the 1st section, where you are avoiding it through meandering corridors blocked by pipes. I was fortunate enough to not see it at all, to the point where I thought it was just pre-scripted sounds and dialogue. It does have an actual in game model, but it looks like nothing. Overall, the game is ambitious. A lot of the more material aspects of that ambition are realized, and while the shortcomings are noticeable, they didn’t hamper my enjoyment that much.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely recommended. If money's not an issue, buy at full price, it's genuinely worth it. This is an absolute gem of a video game, and one of those that stay with you long after the credits roll. Here's some remarks, if you're curious why I hold it in such high regard: Direction and design are positively outstanding. First time in a very, very long time, that I have engaged with a work of art, which truly understands cosmic horror - as a pure notion, and not as a deflated buzzword for 'tentacles from space'. The story is very good. It's engaging, the characters are memorable  and the setting is meticulously crafted. The rig feels lived in, realistic and interconnected in a shockingly immersive way. Some beats are simple and well-written, others introduce ambiguity and let the terror slowly seep in through the gaps in what you know and understand. Playtime is exactly what it needs to be. First playthrough took me about 5-6 hours and it included precisely zero seconds of downtime or padding. Subjectively, dedicating another hour or so to the buildup in the first chapters would be great, but if it were to come at a cost of anything else, then I don't want it. The gameplay surprised me with how involved it was. Promotional materials may or may not give an impression of a glorified walking sim, but that's just not true. You really do feel like a part of this game's world. Various threats can be usually dealt with in rather open environments, making the challenge fun. Of note is the remarkably competent inclusion of button prompts (that, for the first time in their history, make sense in context of what you want to do). I lost count of how many times my body physically tensed up to do something along with Caz, even though I was just supposed to press a button or two. From a technical standpoint, the game is quite tight. It ran okay for me, and while there are some small infidelities and a bug or two, they didn't take daway from my experience. One bit of jank towards the end of the game got me a bit upset, but I can't guarantee it wasn't user error. Quality is pretty high all throughout. The hraphics are really something special. I couldn't help but stop and marvel at them a whole bunch of times - literally, just stop and stare at the surroundings, sinking it all in. Framing is excellent, possibly on the level of Dishonored 1, and the environments feel 'made', rather than simply 'designed' or 'crafted'.  The audio is fitting, well made and immersive. Music doesn't overstay it's welcome, while the churning waters, the howling winds and the industrial ambience remain center-stage. Also, a word of caution: this game does audio cues. Pay attention to what you are hearing.

There is very little interaction beyond that, you just do some mild parkour, hide a lot and turn some valves and push buttons. The monsters yo hide from are a bit scary but that's it.

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous visuals, sparse story, tedious gameplay.There's like 80% less story than Everybody's Gone to the Rapture, and a lot more thinly-veiled busywork (go to this area, turn this knob, hide from this monster). There's no emotional payoff for any of the characters, despite the superb voice acting, because there's little of them to get invested in. I didn't even know one of the characters was my brother until . In Everybody's Going to the Rapture tragedy emerges in the intersection between the alien and the human, between two wounded beings locked in mutual misunderstanding. In Still Wakes the Deep, the alien is a mere backdrop for human tragedy to unfold, but a tragedy with no substance nor development (unlike in Soma). The game opens with the protagonist's reason for working on an oil rig, and ends without further elaboration. The majority of the narrative is being told to go somewhere, to fix something, for someone; and the gameplay involves climbing ladders, crawling through vents, and turning valves. There's neither a compelling story, nor compelling gameplay. I just don't know what the point of this game is.No wonder the creative director left. RIP The Chinese Room. You weren't the best, but you were better than this.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: One part Alien Isolation, mixed with the Thing and Deepwater Horizon. This was easily one of the best horror games I've played in the last year. Some people may not be a fan of how linear and simple the gameplay is, but if you're looking for a short, expertly paced horror game, this is it. Definitely worth picking up if you're a horror fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: If you're on the fence of buying this game, do it.The story, characters, and environment is absolutely amazing. Despite it's potentially worrisome price that many are very reluctant to give into, it is potentially one of the best games I've played so far in the year. The amount of passion and creative work that went into this project shows. While the game may not be the most terrifying or expansive horror game its ability to create mystery around the unknown  is very impressive for such a small scale and relatively short story. The characters truly feel real. The voice acting for this game is some of the best I've heard in a very long time, the emotion and expressions of the characters really do make you feel apart of the story. This games' immersion was something that completely blind sided me (American) as the Scottish accents and dialect was something I feared would take me out of loop, however, I found it to be quite the opposite.Despite it's great attributes there were still some areas of problems. many levels did feel repetitive and very linear while not necessarily being a bad thing it was somewhat disappointing. Still, the developers did a great job of making these moments feel mostly natural despite the lack of exploration.Without spoiling much more I highly recommend this game. Whether you're a fan of indies, horror, or great stories this is a must pick.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like the idea of this game started out as a passion project but turned out very mundane in every aspect (story, gameplay and art). It does not come close to, let alone surpass, any existing literature in any manner. I was hoping we would get at least a different take on the thing style horror but it rather feels like a very cheap copy with family issues inserted. The gameplay gets redundant very fast. Even the basic mechanics of cat and mouse style running away gameplay feels choppy and not engaging. Then you realize thats all there is to the gameplay, absolute disappointment there. The art potential of an oilrig in the middle of a storm seems boundless but they somehow managed to make that boring as well dont ask me how. All in all, It feels like the drive to make this game ran out very early in development. Leaves much to be desired.Edit: "the thing" here refers to the movie The Thing (1982)
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: While a little too "on rails" for my liking, the presentation is fantastic and I'm a sucker for body horror. I was brought to tears a few times from the VAs performances. While you may feel the price is steep for the 5-7 hours you'll get out of it, I still highly recommend this title, especially if you love  or  minus the action.My biggest praise for this title is the fact that progression felt natural, the flow from scene to scene didn't hold my hand.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap this is exactly what I want in a horror game.  Superb acting, good writing, no battery/match hunting, and the monsters are rare enough to always keep you on edge without annoying you.  I loved that the threats were otherworldly and somewhat defied description.  I have no critiques of this game!  Grade: A++
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: The story and art design goes hard. Color-coded leveldesign (follow the yellow trail), lots of climbing and jumping, especially in a speedrun... To some extent, the design reminds me of the sewer and ship levels in Mirror's Edge. The antagonist is the Dead Space corruption that shines in "colors, unlike any known on Earth", really a fantastic game! The story got me hooked, and I even cared about some characters. Nobody has ever made a game set in the UK during the 1970s recession.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: THEEEEEEEEEEE game of the year. compelling narrative, divine characterisation, a beautiful utilisation of re-entering zones for different reasons, avoiding different obstacles and sound and graphic design that makes you feel like a scottish oil rig worker in the 1970s dealing with marital issues and also career issues. JUST SOOOO FREAKING COOL. I LOVE YOU THE CHINESE ROOM!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: SO we ended up finishing this in one sitting. The price is so so worth it, especially if you're a fan of SOMA or Alien Isolation.the sound design is fantastic. you can heat every clatter as things move about ship. I love the way this game keeps you on your toes with it. The voice acting takes the cake though. everyone in this is amazing, you can hear the weight of the days events in their voices. some moments are absolutely heartbreaking too, i cried a couple time. _childDocuments_.review: Audio-- 7/10 not immersive enough, sound field-surround tech missing.Graphics- 8/10--- looks silly when looking down, but quite immersive sceneryGame play--2/10-- Nothing to do, no puzzles, no sneaking, just annoying QTE which are glitchy in some partsVoice actors- 10/10 some of the best out there, too bad the characters do not create a bond or connection.Story- 9/10 solid horror story,. Simple and effective. Around 4 hours long7.2Get it for a short nice story, when in discount. Do not expect a challenge but a short story.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Thoughts after beating the game:This game is good enough and short enough to be completed in one sitting (4-5 hours).Obviously very reminiscent of 'The Thing', which no doubt it took inspiration from, narratively.In a sea of ♥♥♥♥ horror game stories and settings, the story and setting of this one stand out.The characters rapport and narrative direction of the game are easily the best parts.Levels are fairly linear and I think there could have been some improvements on the complexity due to the already maze-like and vertical nature of an oil rig. Maybe make it worth exploring by adding achievement-tied collectibles tucked away in corners to reward the explorers?Game feels more like you're playing through a movie than a survival horror experience, minimal gameplay mechanics so don't pick it up if you don't find that compelling. If you do like narrative driven games, I wholeheartedly recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: The narrative was very unique and actually sucked me and my chat in rather than most horror/thriller games that are just the same storyline and are very predictable. My only wish would be that the story was longer as I was left wanting more! Definitely would recommend especially for people who don't enjoy severe horror as the storyline will make you want to play!
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Alien Isolation meets the Thing "walking simulator" that meets survival horror in a great way. The graphics are spot on with grand set pieces only becoming more beautiful as the game continues. Additionally, the voice acting is some of the best I have ever heard. It is quite short, however, and can be completed in one sitting. The game's atmosphere is outstanding, a mix between a steel, lifeless 70's industrial normalcy and  horror. The characters, even the ones who have few lines, feel like real people, helped by amazing voice acting. (It's so great I had to mention it twice).Overall the story of Cameron "Caz' McLeary and Cadal Oil's Beira D oil rig is told masterfully and finds the right balance between abject horror and sadness.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: A solid game telling a sad personal story while also stuck in a scary and dangerous environment. Having just finished the game I'm left a little down, but glad to have experienced the whole story.There's no major boss fights. You mostly need to know when to run and when to sneak around. The visuals are really good and I took way too many screenshots, the sound and music is really good too. I feel like I know too much about Oil Rig layouts and operations now.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Still wakes the deep is a incredibly authentic SCOTTISH horror experience (i am personally Scottish so i find this very entertaining) BELOW THIS POINT THERE MAY BE SPOILERS I HAVE BLACKED OUT EVERYTHING I CONSIDER A SPOILER BUT I MENTION THE PACING AND LENGTH OF THE GAME + TALK ABOUT HOW THE STORY IS PORTRAYED (NO SPOILERS REALLY AS I DON'T TALK ABOUT ANYTHING THAT HAPPENS)The actual horror itself is inspired by a few things the main noticeable ones being   The games story is Phenomenal in my opinion While also being very LAYED OUT / on the nose, what you see is what you get if get what i'm saying which is not a bad thing in my opinion as it is done very well. Another big positive i would like to mention is EVERY Character feels like there is a story to them but not in a forced way, it feels like they are people doing their job just like you which i think is very neat (plus the funny Scottish banter is amusing).One thing i will say while not necessarily a negative, is that it is VERY linear like there are next to know other paths you can go the closest thing you get to breaking away from the set path is looking around for some lore or other random things (it doesn't feel this way though) at least not until later in the game. Now this COULD be seen as a bad thing BUT personally i think it is a good thing for the game as first and foremost the game is a story to be told, AND ITS A DAMN GOOD STORY although because of this linear structure i feel they decided to not make the game that long (i completed it in around 6 hours this is with me doing most of the optional things) and i feel this is because they feared the game play would get boring since it is kinda just sneaking about NOW personally i think they could have taken it a bit farther. ALTHOUGH i understand why they didn't and i still really enjoyed my time and the ending. but i do kinda wish there was more and  anyways the reason i mention this is for 2 main reasons1. it's kinda short for how expensive it is2. it is lacking in replayablity because of how linear it isHaving said that I really like this game even though i normally prefer more free less linear games and don't regret spending money on it IN FACT i would do it again honestly I may even replay it just because of how good it is even if there won't be a lot variance from my first run that is how strong the game is as a experience in my opinion.a few things i wanna rate---------------------------voice acting = 10/10writing/story = 9/10visuals/setting = 10/10music = 10/10 characters = 9/10 (there are some reaLLY good ones but i feel like one was slightly half baked / needed more screen time other wise i feel it was 10/10)horror = 8/10 (some parts are TRULY horrifying and the cosmic horror that is there is on point both beautiful, horrifying and beyond my comprehension lmao but as i mentioned earlier it was slightly untapped in my opinion + in the last few parts of the game a lot of the tension towards the main threat had felt less scary having said all of that if you like cosmic horror or interesting settings/characters or even body horror (and silly Scottish banter) i would recommend playing this game at least once it is worth the money BUT if you are not willing to spend that much it is understandable.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review:
STILL WAKES THE DEEP is a first-person narrative horror from The Chinese Room, creator of Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs, Everybody's Gone to the Rapture, and Dear Esther. 

In STILL WAKES THE DEEP, you are an off-shore oil rig worker, fighting for his life through a vicious storm, perilous surroundings, and the dark, freezing North Sea waters. All lines of communication have been severed. All exits are gone. All that remains is to face the unknowable horror that's come aboard. 

Search for your crew and help them survive if you can. Run, climb, and swim through the flooding corridors and storm-lashed outer decks. Face a terrifying, unrelenting foe. And pray that, one day, you get to see your family again.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

name: Bramble: The Mountain King
detailed_description: Bramble The Mountain King takes you on a gripping and unsettling journey through stunning environments. Take on the role of Olle, a young boy setting off to rescue his sister, kidnapped by a dreaded troll. Not everything in Bramble is exactly how it seems - in this strange land with creatures big and small, you must be careful when to approach and when to hide. Many hungry and spiteful beasts lurk in these forests and caves. Watch your step.... Call upon the Spark of Courage, an enchanted fragment granting the gifts you need to endure the pitfalls and trials in your path. Defeat the horrid creatures you encounter in different and unique ways. Be warned, courage without kindness can take you down a dark path. Adventure as Olle, a brave boy who sets off to rescue his sister. A beautiful yet dangerous world to explore. Encounter twisted, mythical creatures from Nordic folklore for epic-scale boss battles. Tense, heart-pounding moments with hi-end visuals to match.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a 10/10 for its genre and a 8/10 in general. It's a horror puzzle platformer like Limbo, Inside, and Little Nightmares and is a top tier addition to this niche genre. However, players should be warned, that content warning is NOT for show. This game gets DARK! The atmosphere is 11/10 and is by far the strongest selling point of this game. This includes sound, lore, music, monster design (especially good,) and setting. It's not the highest graphic game, but it doesn't need to be. This game is Horror in it's purist form. There are no cheap jump scares (though a boss entrance at one point did make me jump.) This game relies purely on the situation, the environment, and the monster design to instill disgust, horror, and dread in the players.Also, to be honest, I'm not entirely sure this game wasn't an excuse to use a really nice remix of "In the Halls of the Mountain King" in a boss fight.Negative Points (Nitpicks):-The sound the young gnomes were given is overly cute, and is fine the first time. However, they get annoying fast and by my third time hearing them I understood why everything wanted to eat them... Thankfully, they're only around for the beginning of the game.-At a few (maybe 3) points in the game awkward angles on paths made keyboard navigation annoying. These were really the only unfair deaths in the game. Basically, I had to slow down and inch myself past a few paths or fall to my death when it was clear those points weren't meant to be a challenge at all.Extra Notes:-♥♥♥♥ Lillemore-Lemus and the Frog are real ones
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: 4/10, I sort of recommend this game but not at the current pricetag.I loved the gorgeous atmosphere, which is the game's main selling point, but the game fails to reach farther than that. Somewhat janky platforming, stiff animations and forced camera angles makes for a generally unpleasant experience. The devs seem generally inexperienced rather than lazy which is something I personally can respect. They obviously spent a lot of time on the graphics and sound. I acknowledge the potential of the game and I hope that it has been a good learning opportunity for the devs.I personally don't think that the game is worth 30 usd in its current state but at the same time I would not want to dissuade anyone from purchasing the game if they are really into it.My final thoughts are that it's a worse Little Nightmares but it makes excellent use of nordic folktales and mythology, a theme you'd be hard-pressed to find much of in the gaming community.For anyone who likes the aesthetic of the game I reccomend searching for the name John Bauer, the artist which this game borrows a lot of inspiration from. You can even find some of his paintings within the game and the character Tuva is based on a character from his paintings (Tuvstarr).Shoutout till hen som lade in 1 kilo mjöl postern XD.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely hate to do this. I love games like this. I like that this is an indie game and I hate having to downvote a game someone clearly put a lot of time and effort into making. That being said, this game was the most repetitious and unengaging knockoff of little nightmares that I have ever played. The story is relatively unconnected and the level design is far more akin to a walking simulator than anything else. The checkpoints were pretty unforgiving in the sense that you are forced to redo the most boring, unengaging "puzzles" over and over again because you jumped the wrong direction or your ankle got clipped by whatever bad thing is being shot at you. I play challenging games. But there is no reason for a game like this to be so challenging. The final boss was so redundant and frustrating I couldn't stand it. It was just time consumption for the sake of ensuring this 4 hour experience wasn't a two hour experience. There were several parts of the game that were unnaturally elongated so that it wasn't too short. Most of the horror is shock horror with no real depth to it besides, "I murdered a baby, here's it's corpse" or "check out all this gore". It lacked any real depth. I get they were going for the Grimm fairy tale, disturbing, vapid story-telling, but it just can't keep my interest for the whole 4 hours. I forced myself to beat this game, I was done with it about an hour and a half in. $30 for this is HIGHWAY ROBBERY. I got it on sale and I still feel like I was scammed.I really don't understand why everyone is so in love with this. It's shallow and boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the puzzles, the art was incredible, the controls left a little to be desired (if you are working with a keyboard like I was), and although I'm really not one for the Horror genre...this left me breathless in all the right ways. it wasn't mindless gore and blood (though that is included) it's an in depth story based in many folklores and sad tales. Worthy of all the praise and worthy of a hearty replay! Gorgeous all the way around - well done indie games, Merge has made a masterpiece!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: As far as walking sims go, this is probably one of the better ones, but it's still just very, very little interesting content considering the price tag. Had I not gotten it from a friend, I'm not sure I would've finished it. Most of the game is just walking around with some admittedly pretty cool visuals, it's when the game tries to be more with the few boss battles it features it lost me completely. I admire the effort, but they really just feel like they're wasting your time more than acting as a real roadblock in the way of the main goal. Whole thing could've been condensed down to maybe 90 minutes. There's also some very, very light puzzle elements, but it's mostly just sticking the peg in the right hole, so hardly even worth the footnote I've given it. The story books spread around are pretty interesting though.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Gentle, contemplative, mysterious, at times sinister, incredible textures, rich and captivating fairy tale story, wonderful physics and mechanics, beautiful lighting, surprises around every corner, wondrous creatures and monsters, intriguing but approachable puzzles, dream-like atmosphere, innovative movement scheme, lush flora with depth and convincing nearly photo-realistic presence, amazing sound design in all dimensions, calmly familiar without forcing an over-wrought style, a sensitivity that pulls the heart strings, scary and intimidating antagonists, at times deeply nightmarish in a Looking-glass manner, enticing game play, and simply Gorgeous in every way. Kudos.I would love to Beta test ANYTHING these Devs make to be a part of the process, because I fully plan to purchase every title they create in perpetuity to support these astonishing artisans.I am blown away by how lovingly crafted this title is. My cup runneth over. This is the most beautifully rendered game I believe I may have ever seen. 100/10 stars. BUT this is not an easy title.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly i expected more from this. The high praises and reviews set my expectations really high, but in the end the game was just ok, nothing more. If you're a fan of little nightmares or other 'creepy' games, then pick this up. However if you're looking for a great puzzle platformer for either the puzzling or platforming, then i don't know if this game can satisfy those needs. It's not really a great horror game either because it's more disturbing/disgusting than it is scary. The story then remains as the determining factor for this game and once again i felt that it fell short. This is subjective ofcourse, as many people seemed to have liked the story. The visuals and OST are a real treat though and the game is worth experiencing on that merrit, just not at this pricepoint.The platforming in this game is pretty basic. The character, being just a little kid and all, controls pretty poorly. The walking speed is slow and he doesn't jump very high. This makes sense but doesn't make for particularly engaging platforming. It works well for the stealth sections though, which were the highlight as far as gameplay is concerned. However the stealth is also pretty barebones. There's no distractions you can cause to confuse the enemy, just waiting until they've moved on so you can get a move on. There's also puzzles to do but these were very basic. They were never particularly creative or challenging, just a small obstacle to overcome to move to the next area or avoid detection from the monsters.Speaking of monsters there's a handfull of 'boss fights' in this game. They vary in quality but all of them suffer from the sluggish controls so they're mechanically simple to compensate for that. Thematically they're great though, each boss behaves and looks vastly different. It's just on the actual gameplay front that they fall a bit short. They're also quite creepy for sure, but not scary. In fact there's not a single scary area in the game except for one tiny section in a dark house. This part was tense and the one i'd consider true horror but this part was only a few minutes long. The rest of the game is more unsettling or disturbing than it was dreadfull. I had hoped for more parts akin to what little nightmares does so well.The story was pretty dark, especially that of the background characters and monster backstories. However the main narrative, despite a few dark moments, feels like a lighthearted fairytale in comparison. Without spoiling anything the ending left me dissatisfied, as if the whole game amounted to nothing. The voice over that narrates the whole experience was great though, all of the audio is. The sound effects, voice acting, monster noises and music were all great and the strongpoint of the game in my opinion. The visuals were also very striking but only from a distance. Whenever the camera came closer the game lost it's visual flair. Most of the times though the setpieces and scenery worked, and the game had a consistent artstyle that had some dreamworks accents sprinkled on top.At least the whole experience ran pretty well but for that price it'd better. I had some minor bugs such as the character getting stuck on some geometry but for the most part it's fine. The clunky controls were more of a nuissance though, they made all the gameplay a bit stale and the narrative didn't strike me enough to keep me engaged over this dull gameplay. Had the game played better, had a more memorable story or been much scarier then i'd be satisfied but as it stands i'm not happy with my purchase. Most people seemed to enjoy it though, so chances are pretty high you'd enjoy it too, it just wasn't for me so it gets a thumbs down.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble the Mountain King is a hidden gem that deserves to shine. I'm utterly captivated by its exceptional visual storytelling and seamless gameplay.The visuals in this game are nothing short of breathtaking. The artistry and attention to detail in every scene are simply mesmerizing. The way the story unfolds through the visuals alone is a testament to the developer's creativity and talent.If you're searching for a game that excels in visual storytelling while maintaining an easy-to-pick-up gameplay style, Bramble the Mountain King is the perfect choice. It's an absolute joy to play, and I can't recommend it enough!

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful landscapes contrasting against unsettling sights really set the mood for this game. A wild adventure tugging you between feeling excitement to dread, fearing what you will come upon next and yet not being able to look away. The story is so interesting to me and I love the Scandinavian fables/myths that are apart of this game. The music is at times breathtaking and other times haunting, complimenting the scenes you come upon perfectly. I truly enjoyed this game and was sad once the adventure came to an end.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: If you love games like Ico, The Last Guardian, and Little Nightmares, you will fall in love with Bramble: The Mountain King.  If you've never played any of those games, but love Brother's Grimm type stories, horror movies, and puzzles, then you'll love it, too.  This game is beautiful both in scenery, plot, and music.  The bosses are very fun and a good level of challenging.  I wish my computer could have handled the game at it's full potential; I had to play it on the lowest setting, but it was still breathtaking.  The game did a wonderful job of not using unnecessary jump scares to create a feeling of suspense.  The creators did a wonderful job at making it so that, inevitably, even the brightest scenery is no longer safe.  While the game only took me 6 hours, and apparently others 4, I would say it has some replayability... though, mainly for the items you forgot to pick up during your first playthrough.  I bought it on sale ($27) and would say this game is worth it; you can feel all of the amazing effort the creators put into it.  I give it a 9.5/10, mainly because twice I had to restart due to falling into a void... but that's easily fixable.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Well. I think it's a bit tricky to decide whether I would recommend this or not. I personally bought this solely for the art style and nordic myths, and I got what I wanted. It was delightful to see familiar folklore creatures like Näcken and Skogrået come to life as beautifully designed bosses. You can tell a lot of love went into character design and some of the hauntingly beautiful scenes in between. Couple of scenes in the game made me gasp in awe for how striking they look. Camera angles made it look like a movie, and the narrator really enhanced that "living in a storybook"-kinda feeling. I really enjoyed seeing all this. However, I didn't enjoy playing through it as much. Clunky controls, mediocre at best puzzles, very basic platforming where you only die because of the clunky controls and tricky angles.. It felt like the actual gameplay was an afterthought and main focus was in the visuals. Some things are clearly not thought through: you can insta-drown in a puddle but walk through a waist deep stream. You're taught to throw the light in the beginning, but sometimes it just shines and sometimes it flies when you do exactly the same thing. Basically you never know how your only weapon works and how far it can reach. You can also run, kinda, but not always, and while you can't climb a big rock you can climb up a straight wall apparently because it's rusty.It also felt like the platforming parts were just thrown in there, they didn't feel very connected to the world and lacked meaning. They stood out from the otherwise beautiful and atmospheric world in a negative way, because they were often dull, generic and lacked detail. There's an interesting contrast between gruesome and beautiful in this game, but an annoying one between looks and playability.I would recommend this for the visuals and usage of northern myths, but I can't recommend it overall as a game. I don't regret buying it and I enjoyed it for the parts it was made great and pushed through the rest because I wanted to see more.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has it all: timed sequences, poorly implemented keyboard controls, tiresome multi-stage boss fights, pixel hunting, one-hit stealth and worst of all, trial and error sequences, in which it is impossible to know what to do until the character has died several, or perhaps dozens, of times. Contrast this with games such as Saturnalia or Ctrl Alt Ego, in which the failure state keeps the player in the game, while teaching them at the same time. Much like Little Nightmares, the 3d fixed camera often makes it difficult to know where the player character is, so plenty of deaths are caused by failing to move at exactly the correct angle. The game is clearly designed for controllers and should probably not be played without one. It’s surprising that the studio were able to do so little with so much, as parts of it are beautiful, and the music is great, but all of it is undermined by its gruelling, repetitive gameplay. The storybooks are nice but the artwork within them is jarringly cartoonish. It would have been nice to have some kind of encyclopedia as in Black Book, to learn more about the myths being used. More time in the world away from the tedious running and jumping would have made the game a more complete experience, but as it stands I’m very glad it was no longer than it was.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is a dark fairytale based on Nordic folklore. It's a story about a younger brother in search of his older sister who got kidnapped by a troll. During his search he comes across all kinds of fantasy creatures, some friendly and some dangerous. If you are a fan of games like Little Nightmares you will love this game as well. Great presentation, design, sound, music and atmosphere. It's basically a platformer/puzzle game with some bossbattle mechanics here and there while facing of the evil creatures of the bramble forest. At times this game can get really, and I mean REALLY dark in its themes and does not shy away from gore and gruesome acts. This game doesn't have a M (18+) rating for nothing. Personally I loved the setting and the tone and with it's 4-5 hour runtime it's a nice little fantasy horror game to lose yourself in. Some parts of it are truly beautiful, even more so because of the dark parts. 8.5 out of 10, highly recommended if you like these types of games, just not for the faint of heart or people who do not like children getting hurt.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so first things first. I played this on the Rog Ally so will start this review by saying overall how the game was on the handheld. It ran smoothly for the most part. I ran it initially in "silent" mode to conserve battery. About an hour in a started getting glaring frame drops so switched to "turbo". The game ran between 30 - 45fps from there without many issues at all. A small number of occasions it dropped down to 15 -25 fps when there was much going on on the screen. Seems linked more into the light stone you find and use in the later parts of the game. As for the actual game: an absolute masterpiece. Do not let the art style fool you, this game is a fairytale from Swedish (I think) folklore that is deep, dark and disturbing. You play as Olle, a young boy in search of his kidnapped sister. The gameplay here is very simple. The game is very linear (I would have preferred some exploration personally) and plays very much like a platformer/adventure game. It does have elements of combat which is also very simple that is used in the boss, which I must say were very fun and unique, albeit easy. I certainly get the feeling that they did not want to make the game too hard, which works well. There are some very light puzzle elements here, collectable figures and story books that you can find that add the depth and the lore outside of the narration. The characters in the game first off are silent and the game is narrated beautifully, akin to someone reading an old fairytale. This was absolutely fantastic and really helped pull you into the story and the world. It really sets the tone from the off. Graphically the game is gorgeous, yet simplistic (in a nice way). The lighting is used incredibly effectively. The colours and characters pop out at you. Without spoiling anything and if you haven't seen anything of this the game is incredibly dark and grotesque and the overall designs are top notch. The game gets progressively darker the further you get. It starts out colourful and playful but quickly takes a sinister turn. This game has some truly terrifying moments. The sheer size and scope of some of the things here in comparison to Olle is breathtaking. A final note and something worth mentioning is the sound design and in particular the musical score. It's 10/10. The folky instrumentation and the breathy vocals add such an atmospheric layer to the game. It accompanied the visuals and storytelling in a way that I can only sum up as sublime. This game sits at "overwhemingly" positive and it's clear to see why. Whether you love horror, walking sim, platforming, story, this game is something to be experienced. At £10 it's an absolute bargain. My gametime is around 8 hours though some of that was on pause. The game is a 4 or 5 hour run through, give or take on how much you try explore/collect and how much you die. I highly recommend this game. It's crafted with such a love and care that the AAA and even some AA devs really need to sit down and look at themselves after playing it themselves. I hope we get more from these devs like this in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR : Little Nightmares, but on Nordic folklore steroids. I wish they also gave some to the controls.Exploring the captivating world of Nordic folklore myths was an absolute treat, and I loved how they blended in with the narrative. Speaking of the story, while the main plotline didn't leave me in awe, the "side" stories packed a powerful punch. Moments like The game offers a nice take on horror, making it appealing even to those not typically drawn to the genre. The atmosphere is well-crafted, transitioning from eerie to gory to downright disturbing. Special shout-out to The game's aesthetics are nothing short of beautiful, and the level design melds perfectly with the world. You don’t feel like following an obvious, linear path laid out in front of you.The boss battles have some original and cool concepts, cleverly executed and staged for maximum impact. The game has a pretty slow start; the first 30/45 mins are kind of boring but then it gets gradually better pretty quick.While the level design is nice, it can also be tricky. Occasionally, perspectives can lead to unexpected falls, and moments when you think you're safe behind a rock or something, but surprise, you are not.The major downfall, though, lies in the controls. They feel somewhat stiff and, coupled with the level design issues I just mentioned, they led me to several frustrating deaths, briefly pulling me out of the immersive experience.Overall, it was a very good experience. I recommend it and I would give it a strong 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Review video link: Bramble is a brilliant blend of Nordic fables and real-life horrors that does not shy away from dark themes. The game also features a host of characters with layers of complexity; they are often neither all good nor all evil.The game represents the power of courage in the face of fear - the power that comes from loving someone so much that you are willing to face the beasts of your literal nightmares. A puzzle platforming adventure that is as heart-wrenching as it is heartwarming.

_childDocuments_.review: "Bramble" hits all the classic tropes of the cinematic platformer: a child in danger, fantastical world, basic platforming and puzzles, and most importantly: a super dark tone that is rarely motivated by narrative other than to place a defenseless child in peril.I give this a very tepid recommendation mainly for its cutesy, slightly generic fantasy aesthetic slamming into an incredibly violent and grim Witcher 3-esque world. There's something compelling about that, if to only tell a mid-grade, dark, R-rated fairy tale. Play it for the Scandinavian folklore vibes, as Swedish as husmanskost salted fish.Pros:- A lot of compelling and creepy fantasy imagery- Plays with scale and size in a unique way that makes you feel truly tiny in a vast, unknowable world- Amazing score, top notch- Short length (matches thin plot)- The picture books you can find. Lovingly illustrated and voiced.Cons:- Extremely dark and violent without a compelling narrative to accompany such a decision. Feels cheap and downright exploitative at times- Platforming can be sloppy at times- Boss fights with unclear mechanics, especially the last one, can lead to a lot of cheap deaths and restarts- Very, very, very linear without much mechanical depth or narrative drive

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is as gorgeous as it is horrifying, with surprises lurking around every corner. _childDocuments_.review: Bramble masterfully balances two contrasting atmospheres; one moment, you find yourself in a serene and enchanting world with little creatures and so much light... only to be thrust into a sinister and gory environment the next. This dynamic shift keeps the gameplay immersive and intriguing, as you never quite know what to expect around the corner. However the gameplay could use some improvement, particulary with the camera angles. There are moments when this plus some not so responsive controls can really become frustrating, detracting from the overall experience. Despite those setbacks, the engaging story and the atmospheric design make it a game worth playing. I reccomend giving it a try!

Bramble is a dark Nordic fairytale that is presented as a bedtime story. You have to sneak past various monsters to try and save your sister. The story and the lore was interesting, and rather brutal. It's not a game for kids at all.  The graphics, art and music make the game beautiful and very atmospheric. The puzzles aren't too difficult but also not so easy that it's boring. Just the right amount for this sort of game where the story and the lore are the important things. It's quite short, taking me just over 7 hours to complete, and I'm by no means a speed runner so you might be quicker. So I got it on sale and it was worth it. It was like being in a puppet theatre - minus the strings - it was lovely.There were unexpected and sudden turn of events that kept me on my toes - sometimes in fear, sometimes in horror, sometimes in laughter.I highly recommend you grab this game AND THE SOUNDTRACK. _childDocuments_.review: My Review of Bramble 🌸Although Bramble has some beautiful scenes and music throughout the game, it also contains very dark moments. Some of the bosses I encountered gave me goosebumps, but I was ready for the intense experience. Besides the bosses, there were disturbing scenes that I'm not going to mention here, but it's worth noting that these might be hard for some people to handle.The game itself felt like playing inside an old storybook, reminiscent of the tales our parents used to tell us, like "Jack and the Beanstalk" or "Hansel and Gretel." This aspect was very cool from my perspective. The music in the game was beautiful, the story was compelling, and the boss fights were very enjoyable. It kind of reminded me of "Little Nightmares," but a bit scarier with more engaging boss fights.Overall, I do recommend this game, but I suggest watching some videos about it to see if it's your cup of tea.

This kind of game is exactly why I love Indie developers. Lots of love, effort, and hard work put into the game to create something amazing.

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, this game does have Little Nightmare vibes, but I personally believe it's even better, It brings Nordic folk lore, a sensational music score, stunning visuals and the most emotional journey of death and discovery, wrapped up in a gritty old burlap sack full of incredible boss fights, timeless story telling, brilliant voice acting and the most compelling game play I have seen to date! This small studio has blown lid off these grim, horror, adventure games, there is nothing really quite like it, I do hope this isn't the only Bramble title they make! Because I'll be following Dimfrost to my grave! Horror games lately are all jump scares and cheap frights, Bramble makes you feel truly creeped out and on edge, with unexpected twists around every rock and thorn, the world is immersive, beautiful, dark and full of exciting puzzles and monsters. A true masterpiece you need in your collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game didn't realize how much time i put into this game because i was just so into it. I stayed up playing this game until 3 am and finished it this morning. ( of me writing this ) 10/10 would play again the story, Music, Characters, bosses and world is just amazing and sometimes you get confused but not for long the game is really good at leading you to where you need to go. game is really pretty too but also REALLY REALLY DARK I should have realized how dark it was going to be but I still enjoyed it none the less! RIP GNOME BABIES

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is a hidden gem in the action adventure game genre that shines among the likes of Little Nightmares and Limbo. With a story heavily steeped in Norse folklore, the game does an excellent job with it's visual and narrative storytelling, keeping the player constantly hooked throughout. From the little details in the visuals, the soundtrack, the story - everything just flows so well together and is such a treat to behold! The game is roughly 3 - 5 hours in length, but make no mistake, it still leaves quite the impression when all is said and done. Highly recommend experiencing for yourself!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10. Wonderful visuals, Scandinavian folklore which is great to see used so well. Enchanting soundtrack. The story is superb too.However, all this was almost ruined for me because of stupidly difficult boss fights. I wasted so much time on them :(Please add an easier level of difficulty for casual players like myself in the next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly well done. To me this was mostly an interactive story with a STRONG atmosphere. The gameplay mechanics were at times tough because I am so used to moving a camera, but that tradeoff is well worth it. Every bit of creative, artistic detail comes together brilliantly in Bamble. The soundtrack, the level design, the cinematic camera angles, the storytelling. If folklore interests you and you can stomach a bit of horror, don't skip this short yet powerful game!

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning relaxing not creepy at all non-horror game 8.5/10The soundtrack and sound design was phenomenal. I could really feel myself being in the environment, listening to every single sound around me. Also, to my surprise, the art and lighting is looking absolutely amazing With the nice play of motion blurs and other effects that are constantly setting up the screen, any given moment could become a wallpaper. The game also handles camera movement really well, giving the player multiple perspectives to play from (not just a regular side scroller/top down)The gameplay delivered, it was well paced, kept me on my toes and knew when to give me a moment to breath. Fighting off each enemy was unique while still letting player react to what they've already learned Some areas gave me literal chills and I was really creeped out. The formating of the story was also well done, as it slowly unravels itself.Cons: At some points while holding the light I had fps drops and stuttering (it ran perfectly smoothly everywhere else). I wouldn't recommend it to someone who doesn't control movement that well, as the constant camera position changes change "which way is forward".

_childDocuments_.review: This is not necessarily a game that's frequently scary, more commonly it is unsettling or disturbing with many cute and whimsical moments interwoven.Be aware this is basically an interactive story, if you're looking for rich gameplay or choices to make this game is not for you. The controls are a little clunky, but it is enchantingly beautiful in both light and dark moments, it doesn't censor itself in any way (rated 18+ for a reason). The puzzle, stealth and platforming segments can feel a quite basic at times, but they're not frustrating and are usually simple and short with many checkpoints.That being said, I had a great time. It's not necessarily a game I would play replay, but it makes for a very enjoyable experience due to its phenomenal atmosphere and its unique setting of nordic folklore.If you enjoy horror and appreciate atmospheric games, this has my recommendation for sure. If you enjoyed the horror elements in The Witcher 3, then this is absolutely the game for you.If suicide, satanism or infanticide are triggers for you, you better play something else. Stereo sound also is basically a requirement.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is puzzle platformer similar to games like INSIDE or LIMBO by PlayDead while also using many elements (particularly the movement and traversal) from Bandai Namco's Little Nightmares. This game takes the strongest elements from all of these games (maybe a little too much in some areas) and makes them the main draw for this game alongside it's Scandinavian folklore art design and storytelling. Now, let's get into the Good, Okay, and Bad of this game.GOOD: VISUALS, MUSIC, AND NARRATIVEThis game is just a visual and auditory treat. If you are a sucker for Scandinavian folklore, fairy tales, or viking legends, this game will not disappoint. This game is punching way above it's weight in terms of graphical fidelity and art direction, which makes sense since Dimfrost Studio's previous game, A Writer And His Daughter, had some really high fidelity models for items and some nice lighting as well. It's been a long time since I've looked at water and thought: "Damn, that's nice looking water". This game also knows when to be scary. Since this is based on some really classic fairy tales, they know how to really frighten to inner child within. This game also has some beautiful and haunting music from Martin Wave and Dan Wakefield. They know how to really bring out both the cheer and fear within classic fairy tales, since they are meant to be both enticing and daunting at the same time. As for the story... oh man... it far exceeded my expectations. Typically, whenever a game opens up with a "Content Warning", I usually roll my eyes since it kind of takes a lot of shock away from me when I suddenly see the "Dangerous Content". I think a game like White Shadows really did a number on me for this exact topic regarding Content Warnings since I found their depiction of "Dangerous Content" to be very underwhelming. Bramble: The Mountain King... holds back no punches when it came to their subject matter. You will see very young children get mutilated, dismembered, and eaten alive. The amount of blood and gore in this game can be kind of nauseating in a good way. Now, for the story itself. I don't want to spoil it, but I will say that while the characters don't really talk, instead some NPCs have their dialogue described by the narrator, they give a good amount of character development to Olle, our protagonist, which needs to be experienced from start till end. There were some moments where I was genuinely shocked at what this little kid did, sometimes heinous, sometimes gross. He may not be the most developed character, but he has really good progression. Even his sister gets some progression, but it is mostly epilogue progression; the typically: "This character changed because of what you just watched, The End!" Kind of progression. This game is a visual, musical, and even partially emotional treat.OKAY: ANIMATIONIt is hard to find something that is just "okay" for Bramble: The Mountain King. But if I were to give it an okay on anything, it would have to be animation. NOW, before you disagree, I find the environment to be much better with animation that character models. I think that the character models unfortunately have a "Stiffness" to them at moments that can be kind of hard to ignore. Strangely enough, I only feel like this stiffness occurs in cutscenes rather than gameplay, since the controls are tight and the animations are really consistent and flow good when playing. But the cutscenes just have strange pauses and locking of limbs at times that is hard to explain without you seeing it. This is just okay since it didn't ruin the experience, but it was hard to ignore. But that environmental animation is top notch! Give the environmental animators a raise!BAD: COMBATI should start by saying that I do like some of these boss battles. Skogsrå being probably the best and is made even better for being a mid-point boss. Mountain King himself is also pretty fun with how he switches up his movesets mid fight, keeping you on your toes. Now, this is the thing. These bosses are really well-designed, but the amount of options you have in combat are extremely limited. Now, you might be thinking: "Well... it's a puzzle platformer!" True homie, but honestly, I would've preferred this either be shaken up just a little bit to spice up combat encounters (Don't want this to become an action platformer now do we?) or they just remove it entirely and make the combat a puzzle. But they want you to be engaged in combat since these boss fights give you a 3rd person perspective and have you aim at targets to shoot. It feels really... clunky. Like... trying to play a battle royale on your phone kind of clunky (I know what I said, I have no shame!). So I'm more favoured towards removing combat than enhancing it, and what they did was something... executed poorly.So overall, this game is an easy must play. I would put this next to Little Nightmares in terms of good puzzle platformers, but not as high as INSIDE since that game has just the best atmosphere I've seen in a game. In fact, I should mention that there are a lot of elements of both INSIDE and Little Nightmares you'll notice in this game if you've played it. Especially the scene in INSIDE where you fully encounter "The Pulse". If you know, you know. Congrats Dimfrost Studio on an excellent game!
