_childDocuments_.review: I thought this would be a good, creepy game after trying the Demo. After completing it, I did not expect how violent, bloody and dark it got. And it blew me away. It's got that feeling of the old kids/family fantasy films of the 80's... just bloodier.Fantastic game. Short but not too short. Can't recommend highly enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow the word I'd use to describe the game is "honest" and I'm not sure why.It feels like the developers really cared, but were limited by time or money to give it that final spit-polish to really make it shine. That is not to say that it's bad, looks like crap or anything like that, the quality is there but you just notice little things here and there that maybe should've been ironed out. The character doesn't move quite right when climbing diagonally, seems they forgot to detail the background in that one location, sound doesn't quite line up in that one cut-scene. Little things but they do add up to make the game feel a bit unpolished.Now that's said, the game is quite good. It really nailed that nordic fairytale aesthetic, the music, atmosphere, all of it, a real treat to see the old folklore from my childhood brought to life like this.I will say though, I'm glad I got the game at a discount, for just about 4h of gameplay, it's quite pricy.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game! Too short but the story is a great and the ambiance is AMAZING. They really lean into the fairy tale element and show a very gruesome depiction of the evils that exist in those stories. Definitely not meant for younger audiences or those that are averse to horror and gore. Some themes were extremely dark but their stories must be told! I would definitely play this again and I hope to maybe see a part 2!

_childDocuments_.review: This is my GOTY. Highly recommend.The music and graphic are beautifulThe difficulty is perfect.It's linear. No backtracking.It's not easy for a game to scare me (jump scares don't count), but some boss gave me the chill.It's more emotional, violent and gore that I thought. Do not underestimate the trigger warnings at the beginning if you are sensitive.It took me around 5 hours to complete it. It went fast.I was expecting a side-scrolling puzzle/platforming game with an implicit story, à la LIMBO or INSIDE. That's not it. The camera angle changes often, and there is a narration and a backstory (beyond "the brother has to save his sister").It makes me want to learn more about the nordic mythology.

_childDocuments_.review: It has wonky physics and creepy af main character model, but other aspects is great: near-perfect length, variety of situations and locations, beautiful atmosphere, simple enjoyable puzzles, strange charactersMany people can say that's like Little Nightmares spin-off, but for me it's more superior from gameplay and story perspective. So if you like Little Nightmares, horror games, grim tales and Scandinavian\Northern stuff - buy it. I played Bramble first time on Switch and even there game runs okay and looks fine. On PC or more powerful consoles this game is beautiful
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo, purchased the full game, and played it all in one sitting. The pacing of the entire game was very well done, going from story to action to puzzles to drive the whole experience forward, never staying doing one thing for too long.The puzzles, including stealth sections, were clever and interesting without being too hard or too easy. They never took very long to solve, but they felt satisfying to figure out.Like the puzzles, the boss fights are also very well done and balanced. Sure, I died quite a bit trying to figure them out for a first play though, but it never felt like it was too brutal nor was I left wondering what to do.Scattered throughout the game are some storybooks. I absolutely LOVE these storybooks! The art is just wonderful, and somehow the pages feel like they have weight as you flip through them. Kudos to whoever worked on them!The overall visuals of this game can be amazing at times. There were moments when I had to pause and look up what engine this was running on because there were some scenes that made me think it might be UE5 (it's on UE4). I usually do not like film grain and depth of field usage in video games, but it served this title well. I found the controls to work well using a wired xbox controller. Performance was great - no UE stutters here.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Overall fantastic game.  It has a pretty extreme range from cute to disgusting and gorgeous to dismal and terrifying.  The storytelling and folklore is exquisite.  The music is great, especially the main pieces and it ends with a very familiar piece, for most people I'd imagine.  The gameplay is light exploration and platforming with a few brief puzzles.  Nothing overly challenging and yet failing is part of the journey and was quite entertaining in a lot of cases.  There are a few boss encounters that were fun, but again, not too complicated.My play time was just shy of 4 hours without any searching for the collectibles.  Even with the brevity, there were a couple of sections in the second half of the game that could have been cut down by 5 minutes and I think the game would have been better for it.  An excellent way to spend 4 hours if the trailers look intriguing to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Women... am I right? Remarkable game. It's crazy how this game can go from a innocent, cutesy game one minute and then a gore-ridden, nightmare the next minute. I highly recommend it. Lots of trial and error though. Plays ok on steam deck. If you do end up playing on the steam deck, set the graphics to medium but still be prepared to dip into the mid 10's ffps from time to time.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: The Mountain King offers a delightful adventure that captivates with its engaging story, immersive atmosphere, and stunning visuals. The easy puzzles make it accessible to a wide range of players, though some may find them lacking in challenge,i kinda liked them, it stands as an enjoyable experience worthy of a solid 7/10 rating.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game. The mix of Nordic folk tales and horror was the clear highlight of the game.The gameplay was only ok, though. Bramble was clearly inspired by Little Nightmares, but must say I found it a bit less successful in both gameplay execution (lack of LN polish) and atmosphere. For some reason I found LN's world more disturbing and unnerving and the story was somehow more interesting as well.Still... Bramble is good as well and definitely worth a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy little nightmares, you are going to love this game.Obsessed with this game. Beautiful music, graphics, and story-line. The way the game incorporated Nordic folklore to tell the story about a brother's adventure to save his sister was incredible. Not recommended for the faint hearted or younglins
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I always loved short & sweet games and this is one of the better ones. Not much to add. Visually it's among the best thanks to photo-realism provided by UE. The soundtrack is great, my favorite part is in the last boss fight. The story is good, nice little Nordic fairytale. The gameplay is good enough and definitely accessible for beginners, but nothing major I haven't seen before.Technical side is good, but not amazing. The game is under 5 hours long and yet I've ran into 3 bugs where I had to reload my save. The ultrawide support is officially non-existent, because it would mess up the artistic vision, so we get black bars. What art. UUU removes the black bars, but doesn't fix vertical scaling in cutscenes and even some gameplay scenes even when I added a line into the config file to enforce proper scaling. Get with the times, devs. UW is the future, ESPECIALLY for cinematic games like yours.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: WOWOWOW! Absolutely hooked from start to finish. Beautifully haunting atmosphere created from the mix of gorgeous graphics and piercing sound design. Neat little puzzles throughout that aren't impossible by any means but aren't mindless and dull. Above all however. The story, the way it's presented and the pacing are just fantastic. One of those tales that I couldn't wait to finish but that I didn't want to end.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game took me by surprise. Even knowing, that this game is not light hearted, before I played, the story is one of the most horrific games I have ever played. And in this case that's a compliment.Bramble reminded me very much of Brothers-A Tale Of Two Sons or What Remains Of Edith Finch, with a graphical design, I found to be very close to Unravel and its sequel. That said Bramble stands very much on its own feed and is very much worth playing,Same as Brothers or Edith, Bramble is more about expieriencing the story and very light on its mechanics. Everything is easily solvable, but well done and mechanics are rarely redundnand. Bramble offers sth. new in every puzzle or fight, which never gets boring, while at the same time having a difficulty that is always easy enough to not distract from the main goal of the game: its story.As mentioned it gets really dark, but there are good character developments, interesting character interactions and the scandinavian setting, offers sth, I haven't seen before and apreciated very much.Overall highly recommended how likes a lot of quality in an overall short playtime and doesn't shy away from some really dark places.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Not only is this game beautiful graphic wise the music and lore surrounding it astounding. The designs for enemy and allies in the game are beautiful, I wish we could unlock the models of your foes and friends alike to appreciate it better, especially if you are running for your life from some. There is some incredibly dark content in the game, however it plays very well into the horror adventure. Over all it left me wanting more and I look forward to whatever game is released next by these amazing folks.

_childDocuments_.review: A fixed camera angle! Wow. I'm really been missing such a thing in modern games for quite awhile. I'm so ♥♥♥♥♥♥ tired of solely over-the-shoulder 3rd person player-controlled cameras or just another cramped first-person camera.I'm so desperate for another fixed-camera game. And this game has quenched my thirst for the time being until I begin to get desperate & claw at my neck until I begin to spray blood again.I love fixed-camera games.Also, the gameplay alone is so good.Much like games like , your movement is pretty basic yet snappy. The gameplay instead more-so being applied to how your character, Olle, interacts with the world through its unique, ever-changing ways to constantly have you enthralled in the game's magnificent gameplay.You never know what's next, what next to expect. Every area feels completely different & individualized by their personalized mechanics or themes. One area will  feel the same as the previous or upcoming one.This why short games are so unbelievably good, as they allow to cramp all its good stuff within a 4/5 hour long package, keeping the player constantly engaged and excited to experience the next part, instead of spreading the excitement out so thin by same-y experiences.It's like a huge pie but most of it is crust with only a few, yet delicious strawberries placed about. Absolutely lessening its impressive size, making the much smaller yet more delicious pie to be so much more noteworthy compared to its counterparts.Anyway, AAA open-world lite-RPG rant is now over.Moving on... I think one of my favourite moments in the entire game actually pretty late into it.I'll have to spoil a bit, but I think it's a worthy exception of such.But essentially there's a part where you wander into an abandoned house from the lowest floor. You see a staircase & a huge empty room only blocked by a wooden box that you can crawl over & through.Okay, cool.But walking up the stairs leads you into a nearly pitch-black attic with stray holes spread all-over it. And in the attic it's home to many enemies. You can either lure these enemies to accidentally fall into the holes by luring them or try to avoid them when crossing this area.It'll be hard to get by them because the area is so claustrophobic & cramped with enemies.But if you instead lure the enemies down into the holes... and you thereafter fall into said holes too while attempting carefully walk over them by balancing on small wooden logs... then you'll now be stuck in the huge empty room from the floor below, desperately trying to muster through a horde of enemies to the exit blocked by the wooden box that only you can climb through.That's such a perfect encapsulation of risk/reward game-play, where you try to balance enemies both above & below as to minimize risk in both areas as much as possible to your personalized will, that will possibly have consequences if you misjudge yourself.♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that's just amazing. I sat there with gauged eyes & hanging jaw the second I left that area. WOW.The bosses in this game are so good that they deserve their entire dedicated section.Each boss-fight plays out entirely differently, helping establish their individual characterization through their fighting style & methods; and also keep the game-play new & ever-changing.I don't want to spoil any bosses, as they each are so impressively unique & shocking that by merely describing them will ultimately desaturate & degrade first-time impressions from this that will  be reading this.But straight-up, they're all so good...I adored every one of them.My  complaint with literally any single of them would by the "skull" boss (not spoiling anything beyond that) & how I felt it could've benefited from adding an additional & new phase; and thereafter shorten their first phase, as it is a little too same-y after awhile & underwhelming considering their wonderful visual character design.Still though, the rest of the boss-fights vastly make it up for this sole underwhelming boss-fight.I don't even feel comfortable describing it as "underwhelming" as it's still a pretty alright boss-fight, it's just that stacked up against all the other boss-fights it sorely lacks behind, sadly.But with fights like the Nøkken one & the last boss-fight... yeah there's just no way all of them can stack up equally. That's to be expected.I also just adore how a lot of the boss-fights based on actual folklore & fairy-tales have actual in-game collectible fairy-tale books explaining their history in great & honest detail.All detailed with gorgeous artwork & great voice-acting.It's these small things that just greatly enhance so much of the game, especially to those who may not know all these creatures & beasts since they possibly don't interact with so much mythology/folklore/fairy-tales as peeps like I do.It's really hard to talk about this game & review it.Because almost anything I have to say would end up being constituted as spoilers, since so much of the game greatly just benefits and relies on the act of surprise. That's why I have had such a hard time trying to actually write a review for this game.Still, I hope I did it quite fairly for this gorgeous & wonderful experience.Utmost certainly one of the greatest games I have played this year.It deserves every bit of praise that it has received so far + more.Please check this game out if you haven't already!

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so this will be my first ever steam game review, and for a good reason.♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, this game is a pearl. Went into it, starting to expect a kids game, thinking "what the hell did my buddy recommend me?" - 20 minutes later, I was switching between being in awe, melancholic, and terrified all at the same time. The game plays on norwegian, swedish and finnish folklore, which caused it to affect me deeply as a norwegian. Lots of my childhood fear were now brought to life, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ are they well done and terrifying. On the other side, the game looks and sounds freaking incredible. The songs nearly brought tears to my eyes a few times, and several times I had to stop up and just watch the screen, because of how beautiful it was. Story wise, it captures the player and makes you emotionally invested in it - who doesn't relate to sibling love, and fear of losing someone you love? The controls are the only thing I can criticize at some point, but it didn't nearly ruin my experience with it.TL;DRVisuals: 10/10Sound & Music: 10/10(The Huldra bossfight and final bossfight music is EEEEPIC)Fear, fright & jumpscares: 7/10Story: 7/10Controls & gameplay: 6/10Staying true to norwegian, swedish and finnish folklore: 12/10. This game is truly worth the money. Total playtime around 5-6 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is a rather unique horror adventure game set in a gorgeous atmospheric fantasy world, with a more narrative driven experience, along with it's mixtures of puzzles, boss fights, folklore, and other interesting design decisions. This game, is a very unique experience overall that was captivating from start to finish. I have not played a horror or horror-like game this good in years, and that's really saying something, coming from someone who has tried many different horror and horror-like games over the span of many years. Honestly, my only, tiny, issue is that the ending, although good for what it is, and I understand why the ending is the way that it is, it does feel slightly anti-climatic even though I don't think it's a bad ending by any means. That, and sometimes the overall scale of the world can be a bit confusing at times, but at the same time, that is being done deliberately and to great effect and I also understand why the overall scale of the world is the way that it is. Either way, these issues are rather tiny to such a degree, and I don't even see those issues as real "issues" myself, so this game to me is a 10/10. This game is definitely a must play.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain KingI have a little over 2 hours in the game right now and thought I would share my opinion on the game for those on the fence about buying it. The game takes you on a very 'Unique' adventure of a little boy names Olle, trying to find his sister who was taken by a forest troll. You go through many challenges on your path in trying to locate her, and almost everything is trying to eat and or kill you. The creatures and the lands of bramble are so vibrant and beautiful, but yet so dark and frightening. Its not secret that the world is so different and amazing and sets itself apart from other games. I mean, you can really tell by playing from the start the devs put their heart and soul into making Bramble. I think of this game sorta of like limbo in a way, same concept, but much more beautiful, and gory using today's hardware.  I will honestly say that this game so far has exceeded my expectations and I am so glad I am able to experience this adventure. If you're on the fence on wanting this game, do not wait any longer. Its worth the full price tag, but get it while its on sale! You will not regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely worth the money. Despite its short runtime, Bramble provides a delightful yet darkly twisted fairytale with beautiful art and fun puzzles. _childDocuments_.review: Bramble compels you to keep going, challenging enough to give you minor frustrations for a casual gamer, but makes you keep trying. The puzzles are easy to work out enough. Battles are easily grasped and you make it through hoping to see more.Visually, this game is SPECTACULAR, both breathtaking in it's beauty, and with flip side darkness that makes you grimace.The folk tales it is based on are amazing, and you can see from what folklore stemmed many versions recognisable to me, and those that were brand new to me. Music and songs worked wonderfully with the atmosphere. It was both paradise and hell, I commend the artists with the highest praise- we were given quality that even goes beyond most high ranking game companies that sometimes can't get anything right on launch.This game is not for the faint of heart though; please take heed of the warnings they give; they are meant to be harrowing and they are, yet do not be afraid to venture - there are lots of moments of light and hope throughout for a respite for the gamer. Just bear in mind you will see things that may upset you.Story wise it is simple, but the journey is what makes it lovable. I never at one point lost immersion, and this is a game I FULLY recommend to anyone, and a game I will be playing again. I look forward to what they offer next.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble The Mountain King is one of those hard games to describe, mainly because it's far more about atmosphere and outlandish spectacle, than it is about meaty game-play.  It may also require some familiarity with Scandinavian folk-lore, as this covers quite a few things that seem to have no connection with each other and so just come over as filler encounters to pad out an otherwise pretty slim narrative.A boy wakes up in the middle of the night and his sister is missing. For some reason the game doesn't explain, she has rather stupidly gone running off into a forest absolutely jam-packed with giant monsters that make no attempt to hide their existence, despite her seemingly being ignorant of them being real and quite unfriendly. He sets out to find her, and once he catches up, they have a really nice old carefree time of it running about in the beautiful outskirts of the forest and playing hide and seek with some very cute gnomes.Then a giant troll comes along, pops the poor little gnomes like they were adorable zits, and yoinks your sister into a bag so he can go feed her to the bramble king. Now, it's unclear why she was even out there in such a dangerous location in the first place, given that it took all of about 5 minutes walk to go from being in a tranquil gnome village and finding themselves  in some serious sh*t.To me the plot boiled down to: My sister is a free-spirited f*ck-wit, or some kind of mentally sub-normal thrill-seeker, who got into easily avoided trouble for no good reason at all, but hey! ho! Looks like you gotta go rescue the dozy muppet. Along the way there are flesh-eating trolls and giants that allow for a large sense of scale in it's set-pieces, and some measure of dread. There are evil forest spirits, malevolent entities, and the dark twisted forms of dead babies. It's a magical mystery tour of that cultures most grim and gruesome tales, but the actual terror is fleeting, as it's never backed up by mechanics with much depth to go with the visual grandeur.Back in the days of the playstation 2 it was impressive seeing the likes of God Of War 2 doing humongous menaces that would smash through environments as they tried to grab the tiny player character. And then again a console generation later on the xbox 360 when Batman Arkham Asylum had you tripping your head off under the scarecrows fear gas, in hallucinogenic sequences. Only, by then it was more about how they managed to get this absurdity into a relatively "normal" game, rather than being impressed by the scale. Seeing it in 2023, albeit with glorious graphics and superb ambience, is somewhat weak given that there is very little difficulty or involvement backing up the spectacle. It's great that an indie studio can now produce titles that match 20 year old console titles, but not so great that they still can't beat 20 year old game-play, never-mind the fact that things like GOW / Spiderman are on pc with massive increases in both the action and the scale since then.  It's like "my first horror game for children" in terms of the tone and challenge, yet is pretty gory and disturbing when it comes to the content. Platforming is straight-forward, as are any puzzles, and it all just comes down to being engaged by the story and the visuals.And, yes! It looks sublime and evocative when it comes to telling this grim fairy-tale, but at 5 hours length to complete and with few sequences that are anything more than a simplistic minute or two of tension that quickly dissipates, well, it's a bit hollow. The only time these sequences take more than two or three attempts to finish, is down to slightly awkward fixed camera angles and some poorly sign-posted things you need to do.If you took a bit of the whimsy of Ico, then chucked in the scale of God Of War or King Kong, and then tried to mix that with Amnesia The Dark Descent (by quite literally nicking one of it's set-pieces and repeating it rather witlessly twice) you'd have some sense of the various things this is mashing together. You can take inspiration from other games, but at least do it as good as them, or preferably even better. This does neither for about 95% of it's run-time. That Dark Descent set-piece that it cribs? It was in first-person and had you trying to wade through knee-high water as an invisible enemy chases you. It was intense and scary, precisely because the point of view limited what you could see. You could briefly distract this enemy, and then the game would deliberately slow you down by making you have to turn a wheel to open a vertical door until you could get under. It knew how to terrify and how to turn the screw to sustain the tension.The developers here, do not. They do it in third-person, which inherently weakens it's potency to begin with, and it then just goes nowhere after that. You can see the threat moving around under the surface, and you just run to the next safe spot. Repeat this about four times and you're done. Having done this underwhelming sequence once, they repeat it again later without any changes whatsoever. It's probably more irritating for me because I played Moons Of Madness only a few weeks ago, and guess what set-piece it too is cribbing in an equally lame fashion...Yup!! The exact same one! Nor did I think it was any good when The Beast Inside nicked it and tediously repeated it, or Bloober Team with their dreary Blair Witch game.The Evil Within did a pretty good job though, but the point is that I can reel off oodles of titles that are "inspired" by this idea and then only do a pish, cheapo knock-off when replicating it. The one time that they do a genuinely good "boss" sequence it's still riffing on ICO and has maybe, I dunno, two whole minor differences between how that games final boss plays out. This is, what? 20 years later?To some this will feel fresh, but to me it is stitched out of other games that were done better, and this folklore was explored in more frightening titles such as "Unforgiving: A northern hymn" / "Through the woods" / "Apsulov". It is visually stunning and incredibly well-realised when it comes to the presentation, but as a game? Well.....what's here is engaging enough to pass the time, and nothing more than that.Every so often it does something creepy, every so often it does something where you're like "wow! indie games have come a long way technically". Yet, looking back at it, looking past the production values....it never succeeded in being pant-sh*ttingly scary, or ever sustained those moments of dread. The reason why is that any stealth is basic, the chase scenes are too short and easy, any other type of challenge is pretty straightforward, and when they do find an average level of success it's just repeated again with minimal changes.So, on the one hand: It's good if you're new to whatever you'd call this toothless "cinematic" kind of "action" and "horror", but on the other hand....it's a nothing-burger of a game in a nothing-burger genre. I love games like Limbo and Inside, and in some ways they are just as vapid as this when it comes to the game-play, so I do understand the appeal. If anything it's the potential for this to have been a "proper" horror masterpiece, like Amnesia The Bunker, that makes it somewhat more disappointing. They do have game-play here, but it's done at such a low level as to be equivalent to crossing a 3d platformer for babies with a walking simulator "horror" experience.  I don't regret my time with it, or the money spent, but having finished it, ooh, I dunno, half an hour ago, I can't name one sequence where it blew me away beyond the artistic and technical side of it. At 5 hours for £25, and seemingly with little reason to replay it (such as a branching narrative, or things to discover) it's good enough for a recommended, but only just for certain players, and most definitely not recommended for action or horror seekers.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so far my favourite game in 2023, the story and art is phenomenal. There are moments that are extremely horrific but its perfectly balanced out with moments of pure beauty. The last time I played a game that nailed the balance between those two was Elden Ring. Bramble was able to be a nostalgic reminder of childhood for me, it created an experience that I too felt like I was Olle, a child. Exploring the world in innocence and curiosity, experiencing wonders and magic but unspeakable horrors too. I loved each of the storybooks and getting to hear the lore behind characters, it just added to the experience of the game. Onto my experience in regards to the game play:I would've loved to see more collectables, I am a bit of a loot fiend but i felt like there was so many places that there could of been an area for more lore, interactable objects, collectables or just something?? I felt like it took away some of the experience because as a child there is this natural curiosity to see and experience but there was limited things that you could interact with or find. There was a point where I thought that the boss fights/encounters where going to be recycled throughout the game, however I was pleasantly surprised when that wasn't the case. Some elements where defiantly repeated, but not overly so that you get sick of them. I found that each boss fight a unique experience, some being harder then others obviously but overall really fun and exciting. My only criticism with this game, which is also why some of the boss fights/sections where so hard. Is the inability to judge angles properly, in certain areas because of the set camera angles it is quite easy to accidentally jump a little to far to one side and die. Which isn't necessarily a problem unless you are trying to get the "survivor" achievement; which is to complete a play through with no deaths or restarting levels. It makes that achievement practically impossible because its so easy to die in some areas.My only other issue, which I'm not entirely sure if it was the games fault or just an accidental corruption of save files. but I had gotten to the end of the Troll forest and ended up getting off for the night. However, when I came back the next day my save file was gone and I was only up to the nearby forest. So it set me back like 40 mintues of playtime, I was kinda devastated.I am excited to see what the game devs bring out in the future, I would love to see a Prequel of these two siblings when they are older but from Lillemore's prospective, and as a potential way for more lore or collectables she has diary that she keeps everything in.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is a 3D platformer, set in a dark Scandinavian fairytale setting, featuring Ollo as he sets out to find his overly adventurous older sister in the nearby surrounding area, featuring forests, swamps and plague villages full of mythological creatures from Scandinavian folklore.The game is best played with a controller probably, but the platforming and control schemes drag the game down in several areas, where the controls fight the fixed camera angles, not to mention the boss fights random patterns, leading some fights, in particular the final one, as a bit of a chore. Further joked by the developers adding a ultra hardcore no-death playthrough achievement, making you wonder whether they ever played their own game themselves or just added it for laughs.That's not to say the game isn't worth your time, it clocks in at a bit under five hours, and so it doesn't overstay its welcome. And the game drips atmosphere and feel all the way through those five hours.On the note of the atmosphere, given the prevalence and importance of the lighting in this game, it's unfortunate that the game doesn't offer Ray Tracing.

More of an experience than a game but it hits the mark.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ delight. I had so much fun during my playthrough, and I cannot recommend it enough.I am waiting for part 2 and the DLCs if they are expected in the future. I'll buy them all.- Art design and in-game artwork. I cannot emphasise enough just how pretty this game is. It's vibrant, it's cute, but it can also be quite frightening when it intends to be. The books we discover throughout the game deserve a separate mention; they are beyond beautiful.- Soundtrack and sound design. The melodies and the overall sound design were lovely. The narrator lady telling the in-world tales and myths did a terrific job. SPOILER: - Map design. I had zero issues navigating the world, including time-sensitive moments like chase sequences.- You can ride a hedgehog.- The hedgehog leaves almost immediately after helping you.- One (1) confusing puzzle moment. I meant it when I said I had zero trouble navigating the world. However, there was one (1) instance where I died an embarrassing amount of times because I was genuinely confused about what I was meant to do. That particular puzzle involved pigeons, and that's all I'm saying here.- Too little lore. I wanted to get more out of the world. The tales we get from books in different areas are fantastic, but I wish there were MORE. I want to know more about our protagonists, about creatures inhabiting the land. Everything looks magnificent, and I wish we could've gotten more of that "everything". Sadly, we only get one story per location.- Where is the mother??

_childDocuments_.review: a perfect spooky season experience! I rly enjoyed this game~ it came onto my radar after seeing it featured in one of Jacob Geller's video essays, Games That Won't Leave The Dark, and i'm so glad i picked it up.this is a very grim and unsettling horror adventure through a beautiful & terrible world woven from Scandinavian folklore. first off, the visuals are absolutely stunning... everything is so lush, and the camerawork is so cinematic, every scene is just such a joy to experience. the love and attention given to even the tiniest details, like how a flower head bobs when you bump into it, the grazing moose you just catch in the corner of the screen, the raven flying by the window... it's just very magical. the textures, lighting... everything, so pretty. the way they utilize depth of field, the sense of scale and camera placements pleased me over and overthe sound is also wonderful, with some great sound effect work, very fitting & at times very lovely & haunting music (& yes the final boss music choice was absolutely fire hehe) and the vocal effects in particular stood out to me, they were so well done. the narrator also does a fantastic joball of it boils down to an incredibly immersive experience, one that gives you small tastes of the light before plunging you back into the horrors of the dark. I was delighted with every new terrible and/or beautiful thing that i came across- and they don't hold back! some pretty gruesome and twisted things are about in these woods, so be sure to check the content warnings. this is more of a disturbing and unsettling horror game as opposed to one that serves you jumpscares thankfully, as i'm not a fan of those, too scaredy cat /ᐠ｡ꞈ｡ᐟ\this game has offered me so many things that will forever be in my memory, esp a certain point where things got veryyy psychedelic and liminal, i truly tripped out for a few moments and then was buzzing with excitement! there was another wonderful, violently musical scene that i really loved, just so much good stuffthere was more gameplay to this then i expected, which is both a pro and sometimes a bit of a con. there are some puzzles, which are fairly straightforward yet usually satisfying, and then there are a variety of things like chase scenes, stealth sequences, some targeting and a handful of quite inventive boss fights, some of which could get a lil tricky, particularly the last one. other than that there's a lot of just traversing from one place to another along with some simple platforming. there's enough variety here that it never rly grew repetitive, tho i do wish there was a lil less stealth, but it's alright, it's very suiting for what's goin on.as far as the story goes, i went in expecting a kind of abstracted, myth-type approach, and that is indeed what they're going for here. there are actually kind of a collection of smaller stories/myths throughout the journey in a way, and there are these absolutely stunning books you can find at different points that i loved flipping through, with beautiful illustrations and narration that give more context for the things you're experiencing. one thing i was happy about is how much they got you to care about several of the characters, even with no dialogue and for ones that didn't get much focus.aphantasia-wise, this is a very linear game so no worries there, the cinematography guides you from place to place in a very satisfying way. none of the puzzles were reliant on visual memory so that was also smooth sailing. fully accessible for meeeethe only reason i'm not rating it 5 stars is simply just that a few of the gameplay elements were a bit clunky at times, even slightly frustrating in a cpl instances, and i feel the pacing & ending has a bit of room for improvement, but yeah i highly recommend u check this out if u want a dark fairytale experience <3 a very unique piece of art that i will definitely return to~

_childDocuments_.review: The game is atmospheric, whimsical and amazing visually.  There are some odd fixed camera moments and the plot seems to omit too much leaving chapters to seem barely connected and the player wondering if parts were somehow skipped.  The adventure is amazing but goes from being a smooth, storybook experience to playing an annoying side game.  The aspect that makes this review negative is that there are several bad choices at making the game challenging.  The boss battles really ruin the game.  I didn't enjoy one moment of any boss battle.  They are way too long and tedious.  Sometimes, the last boss battle especially, you will get killed only because you can't see your character or tell what the enemy is doing. (the screen is concealed by effects, do I duck or jump?  The concept that all games need boss battles is antiquated and they definitely didn't need to be in this title.  My guess is that too many ideas where applied to the game resulting in a game trying to be too many things.  The energy put into the boss battles should have been used to make the story longer.    The character's walk and run speed has so little difference it is barely noticeable.  Some puzzles you are thrown into with no real preface hinting at what or why you are even needing to solve it.  I would really be excited for a sequel if I knew that the aforementioned issues had been considered.

_childDocuments_.review: This is like experiencing one of those surprisingly dark fairy tale stories that are meant to scare children for yourself. In this case, it's heavily based on Scandinavian folklore. In many aspects, the game plays and feels very similar to games like the Little Nightmares series or Limbo/Inside, with the big difference being that you get much more of a concrete narrative here. And I actually quite liked the story of this game, which is rather rare for me. The highlight, of course, is still the atmosphere that really turns this into a captivating experience. We can thank the great looking visuals, music, sound design, and voice narration working together for that.But it wasn't a huge surprise for me that where the game struggles is the gameplay itself. A lot of the game consists of soaking in the atmosphere while solving puzzles that barely can be considered puzzles and doing platforming that can barely be considered platforming because they are so simple and easy. The “boss fights” are mechanically not very complex and often consist of dodging 2-3 different attacks. But I still really enjoyed them for the visual presentation and just for how climatic they feel.I feel like the game could have done more in terms of gameplay, but the atmosphere and narrative really carried it, making this overall a great experience for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd been eyeing this game for a while and ended up purchasing it as part of a bundle with two other games for a grand total of $12. If you wanted to buy this game I certainly would not recommend spending more than that, as there's really not that much here, and I found what content there is in this game to not be nearly as compelling as most of the reviews seem to indicate.My experience with the "horror platformers" microgenre is pretty limited. I played "Little Nightmares" a year or two ago and found it pretty frustrating to play, if visually interesting. My opinion on Bramble is pretty much the same, though I think Bramble is an overall worse game. I haven't played Limbo or Inside, which I gather also fit into this genre.I found the first half of this game to actually be pretty enjoyable. It offered some diverse (if unchallenging) forms of gameplay outside of the platforming. The platforming, at least to start, worked well for me. By the second half of the game the difficulty spikes rather suddenly with some incredibly tedious boss fights, and the wheels start to spin in place on the gameplay in general. The game starts repeating its least compelling mechanics and hence loses its sense of freshness. Visual design and presentation slips very dramatically. A good chunk of the back half is spent in a generic medieval village running/hiding from generic zombies. It is gray and totally unmemorable. This is a pretty big problem for a game that is, at most, 5-6 hours long.On the platforming. Your player character moves a bit like a boat, very floaty and imprecise. Which is fine to start. The platforming challenges are initially very generous. (Little Nightmares also has  the "floaty" platforming but by contrast, required a degree of precision that made it more frustrating than fun). By the second half of the game this generosity wears off and you're essentially playing a different game. This feels like an artificial difficulty spike for the purposes of dragging out the experience.The first half of the game has quite a lot in common with the "walking simulator" genre. There are a few relatively cozy puzzles and other challenges interspersed with some creepy imagery and dreamlike atmosphere. The problem is when the back half of the game decides it wants to be a "real game" and the lack of precision becomes frustrating as bigger challenges are put before you. There is a boss midway through the game that really epitomizes this shift in design philosophy. I understand that the game needs to become harder/darker as it continues, but with little on-ramp and generally poor controls, this difficulty spike felt needless and artificial.This game's narrative and theming left a lot to be desired. The story-book folklore stuff is neat to start, but the game does not really do enough with it for me to feel like its particularly memorable. There is nothing particularly interesting about making fairytales gruesome for the sake of making them gruesome (sure, some fairy tales are actually gruesome, but usually in the service of moralizing to children, something that is totally absent here). One of the dumbest choices the game makes it delivering narrative both through "story-books" you read in game, as well as voice-over narration that comes and goes. They should have stuck fully with the voice-over or bothered to animate more cutscenes. What makes the "story-books" fail as a narrative delivery mechanism is largely that they occur *after* boss fights. They exist to explain the "lore" of the boss you just defeated after you defeated them. This choice really demonstrates that the narrative and world here is an afterthought. Transitions between areas are likewise abrupt and unsatisfying. Really, what I see here is a series of set-pieces the developers created with very little concern for how to tie them together. The dream/nightmare/fairytale/folklore conceit allows the developers to play pretty fast and loose with overall coherence in this regard, but nonetheless I was continually confused by certain basic elements such as scale (you literally change size relative to your environment between segments for no discernible reason), narrative cause and effect, and overall plot themes. All of this would have been totally fine had there been some kind of larger arc to follow (emotional, thematic, story, or otherwise) but its really just a series of discrete experiences tied together with the barest suggestion of a story.Maybe this genre isn't really for me. I initially found this game to be quite charming because the world design and relative ease of gameplay and variety of challenges and mechanics. For a five-hour game to totally run out of steam in the back half and devolve into narrative/gameplay incoherence is pretty unforgivable. Extremely so when you are asking $30 full price.

_childDocuments_.review: The very first thing to point out with this game is the control issues... On the Steam Store page it indicates FULL controller support and under that full controller support for Xbox controllers. However; when after the game is purchased and it viewed in your library, it then changes to "Mostly playable with your controller... The game is playable, but may show incorrect glyphs or require a keyboard at some points." With that in mind, this game to me is best suited to be played with a controller due to the platforming and having to move diagonally in many instances, which I think is much easier to do with a controller.  I used a Playstation 4 controller and the first night I played it, it showed all the correct buttons on the screen. The second night, it showed the Xbox ones. This was peculiar but not a major issue for me. What almost caused me to refund the game on the first night of playing was not being able to move at all at random times when climbing netting up a tree. It took me a while to try my keyboard for those situations just to move left or down or whatever direction was needed. This was extremely frustrating at the start of the game, which is where it seemed to be at it's worst. So my caveat for others is that if you choose to use a controller, be ready to use your keyboard at times, especially in the beginning of the game. The glyph issue happens in many games as most don't seem to support designating which type of controller is being used so that is not much of a complaint on my part, but would be nice to see improved. After that mini rant, the game itself beyond control issues, is very good. The graphics at times are amazing, the story telling is done very well. I appreciated the game taking time after a sequence of intense events to stop and open a book and recap the story. That was excellent for pacing and retelling as it is sometime hard to decipher the story when one is busy playing through action scenes. The story itself was interesting and unique. Audio effects were good overall. Game play mechanics were exactly where they should be for a game like this - diverse enough but not overwhelming where new ones are constantly introduced. As others have mentioned, the game is somewhat on the short side, so waiting for a sale would be a good idea as it is likely a one play through game. Overall I would definitely recommend the game, just with noting the control issues for those wanting to use a controller.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King - A Captivating Journey Through a Dark Fairy TaleBramble is an enchanting experience that beautifully blends stunning visuals with a hauntingly immersive narrative. From the moment I stepped into this dark fairy tale world, I was captivated by its rich atmosphere and intricate design.The game's graphics are truly breathtaking, with lush landscapes and meticulously crafted environments that draw you in. Each area feels alive, filled with details that enhance the storytelling. The sound design complements the visuals perfectly, creating an eerie yet captivating ambiance that keeps you on the edge of your seat.The gameplay mechanics are intuitive, allowing players to fully immerse themselves in the story without feeling overwhelmed. The puzzles are cleverly designed, providing just the right amount of challenge while seamlessly integrating into the narrative. I found myself genuinely invested in the protagonist's journey, experiencing a rollercoaster of emotions as the story unfolded.What truly stands out in Bramble is its ability to evoke feelings of both wonder and fear, reminiscent of classic fairy tales but with a unique twist. The blend of folklore and fantasy elements creates a rich tapestry that is both familiar and refreshingly original.Overall, Bramble is a must-play for anyone who appreciates beautifully crafted games with deep storytelling. It's a haunting yet beautiful adventure that lingers long after you've put down the controller. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is a solid, short game.  It is, however, a prime example of how the "thumbs up/down" system is flawed and should be replaced with a number system of some sort.  I enjoyed the game for what it is: an INCREDIBLY short, captivating fable with gorgeous graphics and intuitive game play.  It is just so short that I can only, in good conscience, recommend it if on extreme sale.  If you just sit down and play with no interruption, you will complete it in 6-8 hours.   THE GOOD:-Stunning graphics and haunting imagery-Easy to learn and master game play-Horror done well (I still jump in my chair every time a bear trap I didn't see gets me)-Several checkpoints so you never have long to get back after a death-Fun, engaging boss battles-It's just fun!THE BAD:-"Death my camera-angle" - annoying and punishes players for no reason-As stated, really, REALLY short story line-100% linear with no true replayabilityI am giving this game a thumbs down because I am so torn and want to offer some balance to the reviews.  You will beat this game in a single afternoon, easily.  That is the driving factor in my recommendation.  However, if you don't mind the hefty price tag/hour played, the game is definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I sometimes wish there was some sort of mid tier for reviews, the game looks stunning, creature design is really neat, the stories and mood are interesting and the music is pretty and atmospheric. I also liked how brutal it could be as weird as that sounds lol. But This feels all dragged down by the actual gameplay, it feels quite clunky and stiff. It very much looked like a game I should play with a controller but I noticed that at certain points the controller just did not work or respond. Buttons to interact with items would disappear forcing me to restart sometimes (I noticed there is a softlock patch out rn, this might have fixed the issue I was having), left or right control stick would not work but only when I was climbing on cages for some reason. Just a few odd bugs here and there causing me to switch from controller to kbm at random points. Those problems aside, the gameplay generally is not very deep and it doesn't need to be but it does help when it at least feels good/smooth. Which it did not. Puzzles feel very resident evil-y, very basic and not sure if they even add anything to the experience aside from more playtime (Which is not a lot). I even found myself overthinking them quite a lot but it was always the most simple solution. The game is also weird about its own rules sometimes, mostly when it comes to water. Usually going into the water means death but there were times where the character could swim or the water was just undeep but you are unable to see if it is or not. Overall, beautiful game, would simply not rec because of the gameplay, short playtime combined with the pricepoint. If you care less about that it's a great experience and the dev is worth keeping an eye on.

_childDocuments_.review: This would have been a better movie than it is a game.The "gameplay" is very lacking there are puzzles but they are like jigsaw puzzles in the sense that there is only one right answer. No room for player creativity, its not easy but its challenge isn't very exiting and often comes more from design desions then gameplay mechanics (an example of this is the point of view camera changing while your moving which messes up your movement.)Little Nightmares 2 is a similar game to this and I kept thinking back to this while playing it and came to the conclusion that its because of the constant point of view for the player. You learn the speed of your character, how hight/far they can jump. _childDocuments_.review: Bramble : The Mountain King is, at the same time, one of the loveliest and most terrifying games I've played. The way the story of every encounter is told through a story book just before or after you first meet them is a genius way of introducing the player to the fairytale, then show the horrifying reality. This game made me want to read more through Swedish mythology. The scares were so incredibly well done, like seeing Pesta in the distance before even having heard of her. Really, really well done, and I'd recommend this game any day.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best games ever made. To start off, the story is amazing. It is like the Brother's Grimm but a bit more disturbing, and not relying on conventional tales remastered into video game form. On top of that, while it did seem to stress my PC out a lot, playing on the highest settings made everything beautiful. The art in itself was awesome, and there were times when I was playing that I felt scenes could make amazing backgrounds or even pieces for an actual wall. The music too was also perfect, and at every turn it was there at just the right moment to kick in and give atmosphere.  When it came to the actual game-play, it must be said that a lot felt unoriginal. Being a fan of indie games, the stealth stuff felt all too familiar to others I have played before. However, there is only so much it can do differently when many predecessors have come before it. As far as this critique goes it is minimal, and may be a selling point to see these tropes used in a new setting. Further on game-play, while this too is super polished, there was one thing that really annoyed me while playing. This was how janky the controls are. There were many deaths that felt unfair simply because I could not get the controls to do as they were supposed to, or to get the character to move right. A lot of platforming sections felt awful because of this, but it is also super easy to look past given patience. Another thing, although rare, were the small bugs.  These bugs were minimal though, and took nothing away from the game. In short, it cannot be described how good this game was. While it is not perfect, as nothing is, it should be considered one of the best things to come out, and everyone must play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I loved this one.The contrast of the beautiful settings and idyllic music with the very very dark themes is woven beautifully.  From Sylvan forest to the bloody trolls' den to the halls of the mountain king, it felt like I was immersed in a Nordic fable, and the soothing, calm narration only made it more so.   Be warned, there are a few scenes that play out in this game that are not easy to stomach; I won't spoil the game, but please heed the warning that comes with this title if horror isn't your normal cup of tea.  The game is a roller coaster of emotions. The one negative I have is the combat or, more specifically, the targeting, a minor gripe, but it is rather clunky and was the cause of my failing some of the combat sequences.  TLDR: great graphics, narration, and soundtrack.  If you liked Little Nightmares and love Nordic fables, you will love this. But be forewarned that graphic violence might turn off some people.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: is a fantastic atmospheric platformer set in a world filled with dark and twisted Nordic horror folklore. This game is very immersive, has beautiful environments with interesting creature design, some unsettling horrific sequences, a wonderful soundtrack and a forgiving checkpoint system (you can only can get hit once and then have to start all over). The boss encounters are very unique and has some interesting mechanics thrown in. The story can be completed between 4 to 6 hours which includes searching for hidden figurines to be collected in each chapter.  The only negatives would be the janky controls, slow character movement speed and forced camera angles. Other then that, the overall experience was enjoyable especially during the platforming sections and boss encounters. For those of you who loved , I would not hesitate to purchase this title. [9/10]

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game. The story is the big selling point to this game. It is very immersive and the storyline is very emotive and sometimes very scary, being based in Nordic folklore. Despite any frustrations I had with the game, I continued because I wanted to know what was going to happen. I think it would be a hit with anyone who likes dark fairytales and horror games. The one thing I will say it is deceptively very cute in the beginning and part of me mourned that there wasn't more of messing around collecting up cute gnomes and meeting friendly giants. But it gets dark VERY quickly. And when I say dark, I mean really dark. At one point you are wading through entrails, you witness ritual murders and infanticide and by the end you are so desensitised to the literal dead bodies hanging everywhere that they become part of the background. And when your character dies (I died a lot), you get close up shots of this 7/8 year old boy literally being eaten or ripped in two etc. It is not a game for the squeamish, though the developers do have a content warning at the start of the game. I must admit at one point I was like "what else can they literally throw to terrify this child?" and then lo and behold, plague zombies made an appearance. Now onto the visuals, the actual backdrops are quite detailed and I enjoyed the art style. The actual player character isn't so well characterised and can be a bit jerky but it didn't detract too much from my enjoyment of the game. I think it is pretty good for a game of it's type. Playability is where I ran into some difficulties. The puzzles were great, I loved the problem solving and the platforming aspect of it. It is a pretty linear platformer, with very little variation apart from whether or not you manage to collect the statues or not. However, some of the stealth/fight scenes were a bit frustrating because there is literally only one way to do them and sometimes that is not immediately apparent and there is no room for error at all or an alternative way or route to doing it. I tend to play more open-world games like Hogwarts Legacy, so this might just be because I changed genre but it was frustrating sometimes to have to die a few times before I perfected a particular sequence because the margin for error was so incredibly small. I salute anyone who manages a run through without dying - I died a lot, particularly towards the end! Also, your player characters skill in certain areas seems a bit shady - you have to suspend belief that the kid can stab a monster but drowns the minute he hits water or dies straight away if he falls over, with no recourse to quickly recover from your mistake. Another thing to note is that the final boss battle seemed disproportionately hard compared to the rest of it. Some of the boss battles were based around a combination of skill, stealth and pattern recognition and you got the gist of it after a couple of run-through's. Usually you expect a final boss battle to be a culmination of all the skills and patterns you've mastered over the course of the game and other boss fights, thematically some of it tied in - like the flowers play a big part - but suddenly, pattern recognition goes out the window because the game style evolves into predicting your possible moves and targeting you that way, rather than you knowing where to go because you've observed the fighting style pattern. Also, the hitbox for the Bramble Kings weapons are really big compared to previous fights - the weapon doesn't need to hit you to kill you - you automatically die if the weapon is anywhere near you. This meant that it took me quite a few goes to succeed in the final battle, I am not a seasoned gamer though so it's possible veterans of this type of game will have a different experience. I just feel it's important to note because this is a game that might appeal to more casual gamers as well who like to pick up storyline rich games for cheap in the sales like me. Overall, I did really enjoy this game, mainly for the storyline. It does have some flaws but if you are looking for a challenge or something distinctly adult, this might be a good pick for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The mountain king takes from games like little nightmares and Inside but instead of the dark backgrounds of little nightmares and the muddy art style of inside, Bramble combines beautiful scenery seamlessly with the more dark and horror themed parts. Seriously this game doesn't miss when it comes to visuals. Every part of the game nails the visual aspect. It's not just the bright jaw dropping parts that stand out, it's the creepy and occasionally brutal moments as well. Usually you can see glimpses of the next boss in the background if you look carefully and it ads to the general uneasiness you feel. The only part i thought felt off is the character models, they look a bit like dolls and so don't really fit in with the realistic graphics. Also the movement can feel a little stiff and animations are a bit jittery however nothing too major. The camera movement and positioning are god tier and really adds to the incredible scenery. Lastly i think there could have been for verity when it come to boss design, the first half of the game it's the same twisted troll looking dudes. One with a lamp, another with a violin and one with a skull mask, this improves after you get to the succubus lady, and i get that the troll dudes are important in Nordic mythology/folklore but still some verity would be nice. Gameplay is simple move forward and occasionally solve a puzzle or fight a boss much like the games it took inspiration from but now you can move in full 3D not just the left and right of inside, but don't get it wrong it's still a linear game with one path to take. Speaking of taking inspiration from inside you know that part where you have to move from cover to cover, avoiding those sonic booms pulses? well this game uses that idea 3 different times, they are all different in some way to keep it interesting but still a little much in my opinion. You get a get a shiny rock in the beginning of the game to use as a light, then later it becomes your weapon to fight bosses. This is a cool way to keep things simple while still having some sort of combat that doesn't need more than one button. Another difference from the others games is that they didn't really have boss fights. Bramble has a more mainstream style to the boss fights, that's not to say it's bad, in fact i thought some of them were pretty cool and interesting but in most cases you just shine light in there eyes a few times then win.The game is really very good and definitely deserves some awards. There is no real big complaints apart from that price. As of time of writing it been out for a few months and i'm sure it will go down in price eventually at full price it's £25 for a full 4 hour game is asking for a lot. It also lacks the replay-ability. Little nightmares had new game + as well as tones of hidden stuff to look for and inside had a few collectables that unlock a secret ending and is a 1/3 the price of Bramble that only has a few wooden statues to get to only see for a few moments before the games ends. But that's up to you, £25 for 4 hours of a great game or wait for a sale? i'll leave that to you.

_childDocuments_.review: this horror medieval fantasy game tells the story of a little boy who’s looking for his sister.it’s very similar to little nightmares and to INSIDE in the sense that it’s a horror puzzle game and that you can only go one way: it’s straightforward, and small & simple puzzles need to be solved in order to continue. besides, there are bosses that need to be killed to be able to follow the story, and things to be collected if one wants to be more familiar with the lore.what makes it different from them is the ambiance and the setting. while INSIDE is set in what looks like a dystopian black and white society, and little nightmares is set in places that are way too proportionally big for the main character, Bramble is set in a dark medieval world with mystical creatures and a lot of pagan mythology.but what makes the three of them amazing games is that they are not horrific for the sake of causing fear. Bramble, specifically, is a tale about how love can conquer everything. the brother, the protagonist, will face any horrible creature and even defeat/save a cursed king in order to find his sister.the music is amazing, the graphics are beautiful and the design overall is enchanting. the story is what moved me most than anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble is a gem! It's one of the best games I've played. I only wish it could be loger.It's charming, atmospheric, dark, very dark at times. It's quite scary sometimes, but idk if I'd call it a horror game.Most of all it's absolutely beautiful! The scenery, lighting, camera work, sound and music are all stunning.Light, shadow and depth are gorgeous, very well composed in every frame.Visually and in terms of immersion or feeling for me it's a masterpiece.It's not the longest game (finished in ~8hours) but I don't hesitate to recommend it. Money very well spent.The weaker points like some rare, harder boss events, (one in particular) where you need a bit of luck and will probably replay a few times... do not change my overall opinion.Some details that might be important to you:It's mostly about the story, but it's not a walking simulator.It's not a "gamey" game, no combos, no numbers.Parts of the game play  like a 2.5D platformer, others are more freeform 3D, but the camera is always fixed, only rotating or on a fixed trajectory. This is what makes it very cinematographic.It runs great as well, on my 1080 ti it usually stayed over 80fps, always smooth with no hitches.If there's ever a sequel I'll surely check it out.My hope is this is the Witcher 1 of the Bramble series :)

_childDocuments_.review: I already know that I’m going to be the unpopular opinion and I don’t expect to get any fans from this review, but I can’t help but feel like a lot of the aspects of this game that bothered me are being overlooked in lieu of the graphics. Story: The atmosphere of the game is well developed, and progressively becomes more ominous as the story progresses. Even though this is a horror-lite style of game, that relies heavily on gory visuals to unsettle the audience. It was nice that the story was voice narrated. This helped to reinforce the idea of having a story read to you. Pacing: The game is relatively steady depending on how easily the player overcomes different types of obstacles or boss fights. The somewhat janky controls for the character’s movement often lead to frustrating delays by not responding well to player input and command.Visual: It’s obvious that Dimfrost poured a lot of their attention into the visuals for this game. It’s beautiful. I don’t dispute that at all. I can’t help but wonder how many people can play this game on high or ultra graphics like it is supposedly intended to be seen. The average gamer doesn’t have high end graphics cards and so they’re paying for this gorgeous game they can’t fully enjoy because it won’t run without lagging all over the place. The animation style is well selected and fits the game. Soft, fantasy-feel, and creepy. And don’t forget all the inclusion of gore details from wading through intestines and other internal organ refuse, to repeatedly shanking a demon woman in the heart (100 times in a row for an achievement) and having blood spray all over a little boy’s face with every stab.Audio: The ambient music seems to fit the setting well enough. In contrast, I absolutely hated the screeching and squalling of the little gnome children. It hurt my ears and grated my nerves to the point where I had to turn the sound off when I interacted with any of them that were crying. Like forks scraping across a ceramic plate, oof. Gameplay: I noticed the reuse of mechanics in the game. It’s not a long game. The same use of hide from the light, hide from the sound, hide from the troll, hide from whatever is overused. There are lots of things you can do in an adventure game, add in more variety! That same thing is employed in at least three different areas and it’s only a four-hour long game. The lack of variety is really disappointing to me. As I mentioned before, the ability to control the movements of the character was more than a little loosey-goosey at times and downright infuriating in some instances. I feel like if the controls had been tightened up a little to be more responsive on the interface, perhaps that would have been a little less irritated when the character repeatedly ran in a direction I wasn’t aiming.I will say that the “boss fights” are very well done. Those are unique (mostly) and I thought they are clever and in theme with whatever is going on at the time in game. Kudos there, awesome job. Wish the innovation of those battles was brought to the rest of the passive gameplay. Accessibility: I will say this, Dimfrost did step up and put in an option for colorblind people. And not just one option, but several different types of colorblindness. Very cool of them to do that. They also had subtitles available for those who are hard of hearing or just like subtitles, and an assortment of languages to choose from for which the game could be played. Conclusion:I can’t shake the feeling that the developers leaned too heavily into the graphics and neglected the gameplay and controls part of this game a bit. Perhaps a few more hours of polishing would have really made a difference. The price is about $30 dollars for a four-hour game. That’s a bit rich for my blood. I won’t be recommending this game unless you really don’t care about the price, and you want to stare at something pretty. The story is alright. The boss fights are great. The gnome children cries are absolute torture for your ears…Overall, the game is very attractive, but I ran into a lot of hangups that really rubbed me the wrong way. Don’t get this game unless it’s on deep discount. 4/10Bonus:Does the game have achievements? Yes.Are they tedious/impossible? There is one that is tedious but depends on how much time you want to spend trying to get a perfect run.Are they fun/worth your time? All except the “perfect run” are relatively reasonable. As for the last one: In my opinion, life’s too short.Are they easy, playthrough only achievements? No, perhaps a handful are story related. Many are collections you have to look for, and a few more are random things some players might get without trying if they enjoy playing around.Other: There is chapter selection if you want to hop back though the chapters to get to an achievement that you may have missed without having to replay the whole game. That’s always nice.Liked the review? Looking for more? I'm a curator! Check me out:

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I hope you get this game at a discount because you get 5h of gameplay tops. I think the game is really average that's why I can't recommend it. I graded it 24/40 based on gameplay, music, graphics and plot. The gameplay in particular can be very frustrating at times, kind of similar to Little Nightmares, if you don't land on the precise pixel then you slip and fall or just die. There's no healthbar in the game so anything kills you in just one hit, in this respect the game is very unforgiving. Also the "puzzles" are a joke. Is this what people call puzzles in 2023-2024? Just matching the shape or looking at a picture and highlighting things? Why bother at all? The so-called puzzles are for young kids but the game itself is horror so I'm confused. The graphics are the strongest point, although when it zooms out a lot then the picture really doesn't look special. Overall if you're into this genre, I highly recommend Little Nightmares. The gameplay is also frustrating at times but at least the environment is more engaging and the plot weirder.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game really excited. I saw a clip online and it had gotten my attention immediately. It's hard to identify just one problem with the game that made me dislike it but there is a few things I will point out. The gameplay is slow. It's partially due to the fact your character is slow but also that there's a lot of downtime in between the good parts. There's a ton of cutscenes which slow it down even more. From what I played, the controls are iffy at best but there's a lot of platforming. I would die over and over again just trying to make one jump because the controls were so wonky. There's a narrator that talks for a lot of the game as well and while I like her voice and her voice acting, it feels off to me. I think a reason is that the game is supposed to be a cryptid based horror game and the narrator takes me out of it. It struggles with knowing whether or not it wants to be a mysterious storybook themed game and a creepy horror game. The one thing this game fails to do is to bring me into the world. The visuals are amazing and I liked most of what I saw, but the controls weren't fluid and it was frustrating failing at basic platforming because of how the game controls. I tried both keyboard and mouse and controller and neither one worked out.I do plan on eventually going back to the game to finish it, because it does seem like there's a lot of content here and I hoping that maybe there's a patch or two that will help against my complaints. I did edit this review to further explain what I was talking about and fix some typos.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: As anyone with a little interest in fairy tales and legends will gladly tell you, the original stories are dark. Not a little dark, but bleak like the cold dark nights they must have been told in. And I'm surprised to see that Bramble holds on to that darkness and never lets go. Yes, there are cutesy bits with gnomes and hedgehogs - but the gore and horror is full on display here - with a beautiful cinematic art direction and marvelous narration. But you know what has me the most impressed? That aside from all the eyecandy it's not just a tech demo or a walking simulator - there's a proper game too! With several different level designs, challenging puzzles and excellent boss fights. The final boss had me sweaty palms and cursing but I managed, and the feeling of victory was glorious! Haven't had that often before. Anyway, TL;DR: recommended on all levels! Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: absolutely loved this game, the story behind the folklore is super interesting and graphically it's a beautiful game, the only annoying thing that holds it back from being perfect is the physics and the controls can be a bit awkward and jank sometimes, e.g. not grabbing onto walls when its supposed to, falling off ledges easily, getting caught between objects and clipping. but don't let that stop you from playing this gorgeous game, 100% recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

It's sadly a short game so only expect between 4-6 hours at most for one playthrough but that didn't affect my experience in a negative way. The story of this game was a dark yet powerful journey which kept the progression feeling like a continual process rather than dragging on. The camera shots & cutscene's were phenomenal for an Indie game. A LOT better than some AAA games these days visual-wise. The gameplay is pretty straight forward with platforming, simplistic puzzles, slight combat & avoiding enemies/boss fights. The ONLY reason I didn't give this a 10/10 is because some of the boss fights felt a little bit...stale. Some times too basic, generic concept BUT it also fit well into the game and the style of the theme. I also wished the game was a little longer but oh well. Maybe DLC? :)Definitely recommend. Worth the full price but hopeful for DLC in the future (?) - Support these Dev's. <3

Difficulty is Easy to Medium (there's not a setting, this is just my estimate based on battles and platforming. The puzzles are ridiculously easy). _childDocuments_.review: I love the atmosphere and story in this game. The story is utterly captivating as you play and watch Olle grow through his journey into the dark night. The art is stunning, the story is full of dark whimsy and fantastical creatures. You can truly tell that the developers put their hearts into this.The graphics and controls are decent though at times may be a little stiff or awkward, but the developers made the game forgiving in regards to this so it's only a minor inconvenience at most. Like getting used to the controls on any game or having to repeat a small section because your timing was off. Definitely would recommend this to anyone who likes Nordic or Gaelic mythology and stories about the Fae. Also would recommend it to anyone who enjoys a linear creepy story that feels cinematic.
