_childDocuments_.review: This really is the fairy tale for little German children. There are many things in the woods and only a few of them are nice. It's mechanically passable platforming and passable combat. The major feature is it's fully fledged environments visually. Which makes this a very good play through for a single time.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: The Scary bits are really tense and can get your heart going. The atmosphere goes from peaceful and joyous to an unrelenting grim without hesitation. A beautiful game with a good fairy tale story. It can be beaten in one sitting, which I really enjoyed. I got the whole experience and I liked it. I was not bored for any of the game play. The voice acting was spot on. The music was also very well done and matched the game perfectly. Give this one a look if you are into some Nordic Lore and fairy tales. However, the content warning at the beginning of the game is no joke and there are some seriously grim moments so take care.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I saw a short portion video on this game and figured I'd try it out..SO glad I did. This game is beautiful. I started playing this morning and finished by the evening, so yes it is a short game but damnit...it's so freaking goood. 10/10 recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game is gorgeous.  I 'grew up' on WoW, Castlevania, horror and fantasy movies and games.  The world is just flat out amazing. _childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: As a swede, this was a magical experience! Great atmosphere with stories from the childhood.The something, in the , gave me extreme chills, that was a  one. _childDocuments_.review: Good and traumatizing. The story is really good if you like Germanic folk-lore dark fantasy stuff, this game is prime for that. _childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed a lot of the more intense moments of the game and had a blast playing the more alert sections. Great soundtrack and, northern forclore accompanying the game's atmosphere.It's a game I highly recommend to experience BUT you could get it from Game Pass. You will finish it in 1 to 2 days. The only reason to replay it is doing the Survival achievement that has you play the game without dying or restarting the game. (in theory) as you can fool around with that achievement.Having said that, the controls are iffy at best. I have played with the controller, not the keyboard and mouse and most likely is better made for that, but still, the camera angles, the motion blur, locations that are bigger than they needed to be without serving a purpose and abysmal controls make me rank the game lower than I should have had.You have to fight the camera and controls for some reason, and instead of navigating the tense moments evading the boss, and playing around, the movement is sometimes weird, and you will miss jumps or moves that you would have not missed in any other game.It's a bad blend of 3D where 2D would have worked better.I agree with the comments that the movement is pulling the game down, but storywise, visual presentation and atmosphere is an amazing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Truly amazed by this game. _childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I thought it was really boring and requested a refund. It seemed to just be doing random things. Like a shuffled playlist of random mythology situations. _childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, because the things it does well it does VERY well. Incredible art direction, beautiful imagery, and good voice acting. The boss fights are satisfying and the gore is well rendered and adds to the dark tone.But where it succeeds as an experience it fails as a game. The puzzles are extremely easy, to the point of being tedious. They aren't even that long, but just the fact you have to do them at all feels like jumping through hoops because the answer is immediately obvious, every single time. Some puzzles also get repeated, which feels odious when they were already so simple to begin with... The gameplay is basically on rails at all times (barring bossfights), with the direction the camera is moving telling you where you should walk 100% of the time. There is only ever one solution to any obstacle the game throws at you, and almost always only one path to take in any given situation, so the ability to control your character starts to feel redundant after a while.It makes me sad because it cant help but think its a huge a missed opporunity. For example, there are multiple situations where you need to 'find' a key or a handle to get past an obstacle, but instead of hiding it behind a challange or puzzle, it will literally just be a short walk away from the door you need to open or winch you need to pull. You walk over, grab it, bring it back, and get past the obstacle. It just made me wonder why they bothered separating them at all.It's not really a walking simulator, but the interactive elements often feel so secondary to the experience that they might as well not be there. If you just want to watch a movie, you'll probably enjoy this - I was hoping for a more engaging horror/puzzle experience, so I didn't.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Really captured the feel of playing through a fairy tale with how gorgeous the visuals look and the different encounters/puzzles the game puts you through Also a small heads up: the game is really gruesome and bloody even tho it might not look like it at first glance, just to let you be aware of that
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: You are thrown into a beautiful and suggestive world, only to soon find out it is but a lie. There were many different ones and they were all incredible.I can only praise the studio for how well polished and complete Bramble was, I will be looking forward to their next game.

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Absolutely stunning little game. Highest recommendation to anyone, especially people looking for something fun to get into over a weekend, fans of Nordic folklore, platforming, and games like Limbo/Little Nightmares/Inside.The premise of the game is simple: you're the little brother who needs to find his big sister after you got separated in the forest. On your way, you'll encounter different places and creatures, whose backstories are being told through narrated picture books you'll find along the way. These will also allow you to slowly piece together the background of this world, what happened to it and why.Gameplay wise, this is a linear 3D platformer. None of the platforming was too hard, but the environments were varied and the platforming always engaging. I did have a little difficulty sometimes when they game required fast jumping at some angles, but that's due to me playing with a keyboard and so having to rely on WSAD only for movement. Aside from platforming there are puzzles, which are - again - engaging but easy to understand and follow through. As a result, while these allow you to remain engaged and bring some variety into the game, at no point has it felt like hitting a wall and having to spend any significant amount of time to solve it i.e. think Little Nightmares/Inside, not Myst.Is it scary though? Depends on what you find scary and your threshold. For me, it was definitely creepy at times, and I admit there were 2 parts where I squealed like a.. completely normal adult. Yeah. But at no point did I feel like it's too much, though. Also, I very much appreciated the scary sections/encounters being peppered in sporadically, with many different types of gameplay in between, so that it never felt tiresome or overwhelming. So even a scaredy-cat like myself was able to play through everything and have lots of fun!One place where the controls got a little more demanding were the boss fights. There's several of them marking the end of each section, and while they are not difficult, each has its own skills and you need to get familiar with and counter their skills. But in the end, as with the rest of the game, even this part is geared towards a visual and gameplay spectacle more than it is about telling you to "git gud", so no need to worry about the difficulty!And a'propos the spectacle - this game is an absolute masterpiece as far as the visual experience is concerned. The environments are extremely detailed, aimed at creating an unforgettable atmosphere. While each map is linear, usually with a single path forward, there are secrets and collectables to gather along the way as well. The amazing visual experience is elevated further by the amazing OST. It matches the scenes before you perfectly, enhancing the feelings each place wants to evoke. It also serves very well during boss fights, building up the tension and the mood of the fights. On that note, the voice acting by the Narrator is truly amazing, especially given how none of the characters actually speaks by themselves and we are only told what they said by the Narrator, as if she was reading a book to us.Overall, the game is quite short (it took me 6 hours to finish it, in a day no less!), and oh is it sweet! Even my partner who's not usually interested in this type of games couldn't help but look over my shoulder as I played. If you're looking for something to take your mind off of things, to transport you somewhere and offer a gripping experience - this game is it! Once I started playing I simply could not put the game down and I have absolutely no regrets in spending a large portion of my weekend free time on it!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of artsy grimdark indie horror games like Little Nightmares or Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice, you will LOVE this one. It is dripping with atmosphere and has simple yet engaging gameplay. It feels like you are playing a fairy tale as a video game, being ensconced in both Nordic mythology and elements evoking the Grimm stories. Wonderful experience and I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend the game.1. There is no real story, no interesting narrative or coherent lore. It's like RPGs in the 80ies: A bad guy (the mountain king) captures your sister and you have to rescue her. Thats the story, it does not go deeper. On the way to the king, you pass through independent episodes in which nothing is really told and in which you don't meet or interact with any interesting NPCs. There are boss battles in some episodes and after a successful fight, at best it is explained who it was and what their back story was.2. Camera work is bad in this game. And because the camera movement also changes the avatar's direction of movement, you have to constantly adapt the direction of movement to the camera movement. This is often unsuccessful and you slip off a plank, fall down or jump off it. The avatar dies unnecessary often because of that, especially if you play with a controller.3. The boss fights are bland and repetitive with a preference for triple repetition.4. The avatar remains colorless. There is no character development. There is just one scene that tells us a little about the protagonist's inner life.5. There is one scene in the game that is very disturbing and really inappropriate for an entertainment medium.6. The avatar is a child and you have to prepare the see the child die often in multiple brutal ways. Don't take the trigger warning lightly. The game mechanics are designed to see the child die often. In principle, the game is a negatively creative way an encyclopedia of various ways in which a child can die or be brutally killed.The violence against children is not even the core problem, the problem is that the game makes nothing out of it. It's just a world in which the most brutal violence is practiced against children. The game does not work discursively with what it depicts, it does not go beyond what it shows graphically, it ultimately does not conduct a meta-discourse about itself, as other games with drastic depictions of violence do (cf. The Last of Us Part II). And that makes it repulsive and boring. Which is a real pity: an interesting meta-discourse would probably have cured the mediocrity in the other areas.In contrast to this game, I can recommend to have a look at two other games that do a lot of the things right that are wrong here. One game is Tunic, which can be described as Zelda meets Dark Souls. This could be for those who like a bit more combat-oriented gameplay. The other is Stray. Less combat-oriented, but with the cat a character you simply have to take to your heart right from the start. A cat exploring the world and doing cat things. :)

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A great game for those who like nordic mythology and horror. I loved the story, the voice of the storyteller, the graphics and especially the nordic mythical creatures. _childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Overall, 10/10. A beautifully dark game with a satisfying story and refreshing gameplay experience. After about 6 hours, I can say Bramble is worth it - but get it on sale. I like to put in at least an hour per dollar I spend on a game, and you probably won't get 30 hours out of this unless you replay it.Graphics & Sound Design: 10/10Gameplay Experience: 10/10Story: 10/10Combat & Controls: 9/10NPCs + Characters: 10/10Bug-free: 10/10GRAPHICS & SOUND DESIGN. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. The Swedes know how to make a game. They put in my favorite sound in the world - külning - and I was sold. I kept commenting on how beautiful the ROCKS were, not to mention the trees, grass, everything. It's gorgeous, and they place the perfect things in the perfect places so you just enjoy every square inch of the game.GAMEPLAY. This is honestly one of the most refreshing games I've played. They change the camera perspective every so often, a small detail that adds so much to the fun and keeps it interesting. Bramble is a game for gamers; throughout the game there are things to interact with that you wouldn't expect - keep an eye open for little surprises! I read everything, interacted with everything, even translated the words on signs because they were so immersively designed. You will get sucked in.You will also cry a lot because it will scare the ♥♥♥♥ out of you sometimes. Especially when you meet Näcken...STORY. My god. Dark and eloquently told in the form of a storybook, and expertly woven to make your heart bleed. There is so much pain in this story, so much love, so much to overcome. It made me cry, and that always means it was good. The coolest part? Not a single character speaks. When you can write a compelling story without a single line of dialogue, and still evoke emotions...you've done well.COMBAT & CONTROLS. Combat is hella fun. It's a simple system, but inventive - and the bosses are challenging enough to be satisfying when you beat them. This goes for the puzzles and parkour too! The controls are easy until you need to use all your fingers at once, so you might want to use a controller. Otherwise, I was able to play through pretty effortlessly with keyboard and mouse.NPCs & CHARACTERS. Beautifully designed and memorable. I love that the names are Old Norse in origin, too!BUGS. 'Nuff said. 0 glitches, 0 hitches. Plays smoothly.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble is a horror game similar to Limbo or Little Nightmares but if flows nice and easy, everything you have to do is very well shown for the most part and there is not too much of the trial and error common in the genre.The story, music, graphics and environment are very good. _childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed this game and I recommend it to those who played the Little Nightmares games. I wouldn't say this game competes with Little Nightmares in any way, but it's pretty hard to play this game and not acknowledge their similarity (and so I will).Bramble: the Mountain King (BTMK) has upwards of 18 chapters, although it feels more like 14. Each chapter is brief, but they're completely unique and almost each features a "boss fight" of some kind. The game can be beaten in around 5 - 6 hours, and I beat it in 9 hours after getting 100% achievements and writing an achievement guide (check it out!) simultaneously. For this reason, I would say the game is overpriced and more of a $20 game, but I'm not complaining. The art direction is good. The character design and the environment design are great, but the mythology is what makes this game stand out. Each character in BTMK is based off of Nordic fables, and the acts they carry out are dark and demented. Despite encountering the characters only briefly, they are what makes each chapter so memorable. Their tie-in to the main story is fitting, and it's impressive how many meaningful characters you experience in such a short time. Compared to the Little Nightmares games, there isn't really any guessing that has to be done for you to understand what's going on. This is nice, but when you finish the game, there isn't really more for you to do. There's no reason to go look up a lore breakdown or start a discussion why characters behave the way they do because, well, there isn't really any mystery. One thing I really loved about Little Nightmares were the metaphors the designers placed throughout each level, and how they helped foreshadow the story. To put it bluntly, BTMK just lacks that level of depth.From an achievement hunting perspective, this game is very, very accessible although not particularly fun. The majority of achievements are for collecting figurines, so I wouldn't say the achievement hunting experience adds anything to the story of the game. Some are creative, but if you're looking for another "perfect" game to add to your steam profile — this is an easier pick. However, once achievement is to beat the game without dying (which I hate). I personally don't see a replay-ability in this game, so this achievement is a huge chore. All in all, fun game, worth a buy, but consider wishlisting it until there's a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Bramble: The Mountain King! The music was definitely one of the highlights. It really added to the immersive experience of the game. The camera angles were also really well done, allowing you to feel like you were really there in the game. And the story was so captivating, it kept you engaged the whole time. It's always great to find a game that captures your attention like this one did.I loved it so much that I went back and completed all the achievements. Highly recommend to any horror game enthusiast!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I know that this is a pretty stereotypical review for a game, but I don't know how else to describe how fantastic of a game this is. The graphics are great and it's really cool that it can be changed. The game has a stunning world, story line, and the boss fights are really interesting. It's honestly amazing how the game ties in folklore. The sound design and soundtrack were also top tier for me. Sure, there are some issues like how sometimes I would have to pause the game and come back in if I couldn't crouch or use the light, and I got stuck in certain places and had to restart from the last checkpoint, but it was all fixed pretty easily. Overall, I seriously recommend playing the game. (Also a certain boss theme at the end of the game was fantastic so I recommend playing with headphones in an area where you can listen to it really well.)
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I do not understand the outstanding positive reviews for this game at all... I was hoping after playing it more I'll understand but sadly not. It was a chore to get through and found myself just wanting it to be over.Cons:- Extremely boring- Tedious cliche boss fights- Horrible game play mechanics- Very short for the price- Feels like an older generation game- Uninteresting storyPros:- Nice world design- Soundtrack- ArtworkI don't post game reviews, but felt compelled now since this is getting so much praise. _childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Alright listen. I don't post reviews often but this was worth writing a review to. Buy the game. Do it. The music is re-imagined classical music... gave me goosebumps and chills the art is also beautiful. If you like dark fairy tales/ Grimms' Fairy Tales then this is your game. Its a plat former and its pretty forgiving. There is attention to detail when it comes to the story, music, and graphics. I would very much say that this is my game of the year. It took me about 6.5 hours to complete the game but I'm sure you could probably get this game done in about 4 hours or so. I got this game on sale for $11 in a bundle with 2 other games. It was basically a steal. Keep in mind that this game revolves A LOT on story. It is very much a story telling game. It doesn't challenge you mechanically in my opinion so if you are looking for a game to challenge you in that regard this isn't the game. However, if you want a beautiful yet grim story telling fairy tale this is THE game. It did not disappoint me.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I would say this game is almost perfection. I love the graphics and the art style, the soundtrack is wonderful, the rendition of the song "den blomstertid nu kommer" with the artist Bjoern is fantastic, I was surprised to hear this song in a game, for swedish people it's very recognizable ,but it absolutely fits the atmosphere and the environment. Also the storytelling is so good. It's impressive how they make all graphics, sound and story work together so well. Besides all this, the gameplay is actually good too. It reminds me a lot of the Little Nightmare-games, and Limbo.The gameplay is simple and I think that most players will get into it easily, the puzzles are mostly easy to solve, but that makes the story move forward too, you will never get bored because you're stuck for too long. It's also pretty directed with camera angles that make you understand where to go next. There are more challenging scenes with some of the bosses, but thanks to the generosity of checkpoints you rarely have to redo a lot of the stages you already passed. I would guess most players will finish the game in 5-8 hours, so don’t expect to have weeks of challenging gameplay. However, the game is totally worth it, it’s more comparable to the feeling when watching a beautiful movie, except that you’re a part of it. But commonly these days many games have so much better stories than most movies from Hollywood. As a swedish person I recognize many of the characters from tales, and creators thought of so many details that it makes me happy. What surprised me is how the first part of the game is so cute and the second part is so violent and dark, it’s a difficult balance but it gives lots of depth to the game that I love. However, I would have liked them to also make a censored version of the game so that I could let my son play it, because I know he would have loved many of the stunning scenes and the puzzles, but some scenes make it difficult to play with a child.9/10*I played the demo first, then I purchased the game at once. I continued to play from where the demo ended. After I finished the game I realized that the demo starts after ⅓ of the game, so I was happy to find out I had ⅓ more to play. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game is slightly slow to start. I’m new to games (and not very good) so I’m still learning the basics but this short game provided me with fun, difficulty and the skills to transfer to other games.I’ve put lots of screenshots on the game page for an insight into the game. Really good game and really happy I’ve finished it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Solid story and cool atmosphere/monsters. This would be a great animated series or movie. The graphics were good but the constant camera weirdness and overdone depth of field really stopped me from enjoying or appreciating it.The game play is really bad. It's tedious, a walking simulator, and some of the worst "puzzles" I've ever seen. There was one good puzzle at the very end, that is it. Most of the time if I was stuck it was because I overthought a puzzle or couldn't figure out what the game wanted me to do (the latter most often). The last two boss fights are good, the rest are either too easy or tedious and annoying. This game is worth buying at a $15 price, definitely not a $30. I don't feel like I was robbed, just disappointed in what I got. It often tries to be artistic and creative, sometimes succeeds, but I was so bored with the game play that I wasn't impressed with the parts they did well. It felt like getting a bad meal and trying to savor your drink out of pity.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

The boss battles are challenging, and the puzzles and obstacles are fun enough, but there is a lot of blood and guts and putrid rotting things. _childDocuments_.review: Bramble is a single player third-person game that is based off of Scandinavian folklore. You play as a small boy named Olle and you travel through the forest looking for your sister. You will encounter many unlikely friends and gruesome enemy's in through your journey. There are also some puzzles and even boss fights around the forest that you will have to get through to find your sister. -"Awe this game is so cute and wholesome! :)"-"WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥♥-"-"I just... I killed it... I am a murderer... Oh god..."This game is pretty complex controls wise, sometimes you fall because you don't actually know what key to click (I died multiple times to this ungodly fate). However, if you want to jump straight into a game with some complicated controls, sometimes frustrating bosses as well as very graphic and horror themes scenes, you will enjoy this game! But if you are super super new to gaming and don't want anything challenging then I would not recommend this game to you until you become more familiar with your controls.The game play is mainly you going through the story you are leaded through the various paths and such. You collect little figurines that have no other purpose then that they are super cute and they are achievements. Most of the game play however comes from the boss fights and various puzzles you will have to solve throughout the game. Which are somewhat simple however if you die a lot you will become super frustrated (like I did).In my personal opinion the graphics are absolutely gorgeous. Its mostly realistic, though sometimes the graphics are a little bit buggy. The music that comes with the scenery and boss fights are also extremely incredible making for the player to become super connected and present with what is happening in the current moment.The community seems nice though I have not interacted with them personally. I have only seen videos and posts that have been posted to steam.You can play however long you like however, realistically it only takes around five hours to complete. I personally do not think it has a lot of replay-ability. In my opinion I really loved this game, the story and soundtrack absolutely are up to par with what I personally enjoy playing. After I get most or all the achievements however, I probably would never play this game again. Doesn't mean that I do not recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: People who liked Inside, Limbo, Little Nightmares, etc will be very happy with this. What differs are its heavy emphasis on story, some light boss fight sequences, and its use of a more 'dynamic' camera that pans and rotates around set pieces, rather than adhering to strict 2.5-D viewpoint like the others.Good things about Bramble TMK:• Brilliant set pieces, lore, storytelling + environment • Like playing a Grimm's fairy tale• A roiling, brooding, restless soundtrack ranging from exotic to horror film-level scary• Seriously the music is amazing, almost like its own character.Things that are not so great about BTMK:• Pretty awkward controls (intentionally)• Depth perception can be an issue• More trial-and-error than I prefer (it is endemic to the genre but still)• Pretty short but doesn't end too soon.• Boss fights are not that fun imoThe good outweighs the bad by far. Only negative is its length; I think at 6 hours the reg price is a little high but not ridiculous. I got it on sale for ~$9 so I'm happy, it was a very odd and original experience. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Clearly a lot of love has been put into this but I can't recommend it. It has some nice ideas with pretty environments and lovely music, but it's seriously marred by poor character models and animation (the stuff that isn't mocap), imprecise mechanics/platforming and egregious game design. About 70% of this game is dedicated to hard-fail sequences (ie you make a single mistake, you die, you start over eg chase sequences, stealth sequences etc) which wouldn't be so bad if the mechanics and platforming were well-implemented but they aren't, they're just janky as hell. As a result I found it more frustrating than enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I found my playthrough of Bramble to be really enjoyable. It took me just under five and a half hours to complete it with 29/30 achievements. That being said, here we go. Positives:-The game's aesthetics are beautiful.-The music perfectly fits the game's atmosphere and mood.-I really enjoyed the lore and the story and as as result I found myself looking forward to each new chapter-The collectible storybooks were a wonderful addition and really added another layer of depth to the world. -The bosses were extremely well designed and detailed. Negatives:-The controls can be a little unresponsive with MnK. There were several times where I tried to pull out Olle's light and flash it and it just wouldn't happen-A bit of a walking sim, which may not be a negative if you really like those!-There was a specific part in the swamp that actually made me little uncomfortable, involving a baby and a puddle. Again, that's just a personal issue subjective to each person. Overall, I give this game a solid 7/10. Would recommend Just exercise caution if you're sensitive to child abuse.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is Little Nightmares if it was based around Scandinavian folklore.And... that's pretty much it. The gameplay features light platforming and puzzling and it looks drop-dead gorgeous.The only gripe I have with it is that the monster designs aren't really that clever, but they make up for it ten-fold with their set-pieces and boss fights. Especially Pesta. Plus, it's folklore. Every monster in folklore looks the same, so it gets a pass.If you're a Little Nightmares fan that wants to play a game with a little more culture behind it, pick up Bramble: The Mountain King and try not to punt the gnomes.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it because it was on sale, looked fairly interesting from a mythological perspective, and had a horror-like element to it.  The game starts off pretty slow and wont pick up for a few hours.  I'm still not sure if it's a dream, myth, or reality...within a dream, myth, or someone else's reality.  It plays like a cross between Paper Mario and A Plague Tale; one minute you're wallowing through sunshine, flowers and grass, the next, you're wallowing through bloody, discarded innards.  The camera works against you at times, and sometimes are punished (die) for being exploratory.  You'll die a lot just because you're not entirely sure what the game wants you to do.  Unfortunately, there doesn't seem to be a lot of replay value, maybe just to go back and get some achievements, and the boss battles, which were actually a lot of fun.  The background music of the final boss alone made the purchase worth it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Lets start with the obvious, this game is absolutely gorgeous, the level of details is simply amazing.The atmosphere is eerie, giving you a feeling of dread and uneasiness at all times (reminding me of the Forest Temple in Ocarina of Time), way to make me feel nostalgic!And i really commend the developers for using Scandinavian folklore as an inspiration, even for things spooky.There's to many games with horror elements, and it's way to often random monsters, or merely amalgamations of things perserved as scary or discomforting, and it's getting tiresome at times.So this is a fresh new take i'm all for!I'm still mesmerized by this game, it certainly lived up hype and praises it got, and i would highly recommend it to just about everyone that feels like they're up for a grand adventure!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to first say I purchased this game on sale for about $12 USD. At this price, I am pretty satisfied with my purchase, I paid about $2.40 per hour of playtime I got out of this game. It is beautiful, it is fun, and it all goes together very well. It is also extremely dark in every sense of the word. Do not let the trailer fool you, some f***** up s*** happens in this game. The puzzle elements were fun, but not very challenging which was a negative for me. Since puzzles were not hard to figure out, it oftentimes felt more like an exploration (walking simulator) game than a puzzle plat-former. I do not know if I think this game is worth the full asking price or not. There is virtually no replay value besides to snag achievements you missed on your first run, if you missed any at all. I did greatly enjoy the story and all of the Scandinavian folklore that was woven into it and the world in general. I found the final boss battle to be exciting, but it was still not very challenging. This game is interesting, as the story clearly announces this is a game for people who can handle dark mature topics, but the game-play itself is quite simple and will provide little to no challenges to most individuals. All in all, I thought the game was unique and I am glad I played it. If it is on sale, I definitely recommend picking it up if it looks cool to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I am simply in love with North Mithology and the way this game depicts the monsters and creatures. Every chapter has a boss fight of its own that is unique to the challanges Olle has to face. I also love the fact that throughout the gameplay you get to see Olle changing himself, growing up, maturing  You get to learn the story of The Mountain King alongside with Olles own story. The few collectibles are also fun to discover and the fact that each monster/boss has its own story explained makes you fall in love with the legends itself. Definetly give it a try!

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic little game unlike anything else I've played. Bramble: The Mountain King's probably most similar to Little Nightmares in terms of its gameplay, but it borrows ideas from older cinematic platformers like Another World and Heart of Darkness as well. This isn't to say that the game doesn't bring its own ideas to the table because it certainly does, primarily in the form of its dark fairy tale aesthetic heavily inspired by Scandinavian myths and legends. This is a short and sweet game for sure, lasting only about 4-5 hours, but that feels like the perfect length for the kind of experience it's trying to deliver. If you're a fan of Little Nightmares and cinematic platformers in general, you won't be disappointed. Lovely game.

_childDocuments_.review: AVOID | LACKING | MAYBE | WORTHWHILE |  | UNMISSABLEBramble: The Mountain King is an atmospheric horror-adventure game based on Nordic fairytales - think Midsommar meets The Witch, but aged down slightly (children's fables can be kind of messed up, huh?) in game form. The game follows a young boy searching for his sister and navigating a fantastical and often deadly world of gnomes, shapeshifters, trolls, etc. The game is rich in lore and very well-paced. That said, it is quite linear with only one real path to progress. This works well for the game and isn't a negative, in my opinion, but I do think it's worth mentioning. The soundtrack is absolutely beautiful and the environment is lovely too. Having  play during  is nothing short of epic. I think the game struggled at times with allowing for smooth navigation of a 3D world on a 2D screen. This isn't unusual in my experience, but it was frustrating to e.g. jump off something and look like I would be able to land the fall, and then wind up wildly off base and die. That said, the game has chapter select and frequent checkpoints which made it so I didn't have to redo large sections when this happened. Additionally, the game took me about 4.5-5 hours to complete, with my remaining time doing achievement clean-up (~1-1.5 hours). For its listed price, I think it's on the more expensive end for what you get, so while I absolutely recommend this game to those interested, I highly suggest waiting for it to be on a steep discount.In summary, Bramble is a compelling narrative-based adventure game the positive aspects of which are amplified by things such as an incredible soundtrack, creepy atmosphere, and nice artwork. While expensive, it's worth picking up if you're at all interested provided you can get it on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: It started innocuously, attempting to converse with pine cones under the cover of night, playing hide and seek with infantile sprites, and herding living blossoms into a pen. But within an hour, the adorable pine cones revealed their wild, aggressive faces, the dwarves with newborn voices began falling into steel traps set in the forest, and the innocent boy I was controlling was cleaved in half with an axe. Not much time passes before we are suddenly left on our own, feeling fear of the unknown, succumbing to the loneliness of the protagonist searching for their sibling. Minute by minute, it gets worse. The greenery of trees and the scent of spring give way to the redness of fresh blood and the stench of unidentifiable innards. Carefree hopping on soft mushroom caps turns into wading through entrails and sequences of agility where we try to avoid painful and brutal death.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy cinematic platformers like Little Nightmares or Inside, there's a good chance you'll enjoy Bramble too. Like those other titles, this is a short but sweet experience that combines light platforming, stealth and chase sequences and very little direct combat. The similarities don't end there; Bramble's dark fairy-tale narrative is often very bleak in tone, though it mixes the lighthearted and the grim to great effect. The are moments of stunning beauty in Bramble but also of visceral gore and horror (this isn't one for the kids!). The environments look great, coming close to photo realism at times and the creatures of Nordic folklore that stalk you are fantastically designed and suitably terrifying.It's important to come into Bramble with the right expectations. This is more an experience than a game. It isn't mechanically interesting or complex, it isn't challenging and it isn't going to take you long to finish. But if you're looking for a straightforward, linear adventure with great visuals, audio and atmosphere, this is well worth a look.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Overall i can highly recommend the game if you're into surreal/fantasy experiences, especially if you find folklore even just a bit intriguing. _childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad, but I don't understand the 'overwhelmingly positive' - the whole experience is just a bit 'meh'. Some of the mythology feels compelling, and at times a really cool atmosphere is generated. Where the game suffers is the horribly repetitive gameplay, which literally consists of basic movement, timing dodges, and one attack, and the clunky controls. The boss fights aren't engaging, they're just long. Same for most of the puzzles. All in, it's a fine experience, but nothing special. More than anything, it made me wish I was playing Little Nightmares instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game with stunning, photo-realistic environments and cinematic visuals. Not too hard to play if you're not so great at games (like me), while still containing some interesting challenges and puzzles so that it's not just a walking-simulator. The story is simple but great, with a wonderful use of folklore characters and creatures.The biggest flaw of the game I would say is its fixed camera angles. While it's great for storytelling and capturing the beauty or horror of the environment, it can make gameplay very difficult when trying to maneuver obstacles or estimate depth at times. I think about 50% of my deaths were because of the camera angles.Overall, would highly recommend it if you love fantasy horror that makes use of folklore.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: --- BRAMBLE: Ivy Climbing Simulator ---In a similar fashion to many other Little Nightmares fans, I went searching for similar experiences.Bramble caught my eye as a potential winner, and I really wanted to like it, but it falls short on several levels.First off, the visuals and soundtrack are excellent, there is no faults there and I commend the work done in that regard with the highest praise.That being said, unfortunately the gameplay is downright boring at best, and tediously infuriating at worst.- Movement is far too sluggish to keep pace with the environments sprawling areas.- Do you like CLIMBING IVY? YOU'RE IN LUCK BECAUSE IT"S OVER HALF OF THE GAME.- There are pointless quicktime-like events and input presses when just letting the player control the character normally would've served the immersion better.- The constant camera angle switching is disorienting and not in a good way for horror. Too often the environment is not readable, the camera is always cutting out important information, and the constant camera switching becomes a nuisance rather than a desired effect.Overall, it feels like they would've been better off at making a movie rather than a game.Side Note: Stopped playing at the 4th chapter due to the really bizarre and lazy insertion of occult/satanic imagery and ritualistic ideals. I understand the games inspirations, but it still feels incredibly dated and absurd to see these things in horror nowadays. It's overdone in horror and it breaks immersion; it's comical at best and spiritually bankrupt at worst. Neither serve game play or world building well.5/10Bramble could've been something special but is drastically held down by the intrusive camera, molasses game play and stereotypical uninspired horror tropes.Bonus Note: The gnomes sound design is literally just a pitched up baby crying and throwing a tantrum and it's pervasive whenever they're around. I don't know what doorknob thought that was a good idea.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. the graphics and audio are breathtaking and really draw you into game-play. The horror is immersive and skin-crawling however defiantly check the trigger warnings. The platforming and parkour isn't too hard or too easy. The enemies gradually use new mechanics as you play and are original except for one enemy which was reused once. The boss battles are challenging but not frustrating and are a good length of fight. you get to ride a hedgehog and idk how they did it but that little guy is adorable. All the character models are amazing looking and the hostile creatures are honestly really intimidating or scary. The voice acting is superb and you really care about the protagonist. now my critiques. The story line is fine but fairly generic and the game halfway through stops being fighting creatures in the woods and throws you into a huge arc which i found to be fairly similar to a lot of other games. Same goes for the ending. I personally would have rather that the game stayed like the first half where you meet fun creatures and battle folklore tales instead of travelling to a mountain to free a king from a curse. That being said I still really enjoyed the story. the baby gnomes are SO ANNOYING when they cry and they don't just cry for a bit and then stop they cry and wail until you save them and it fully makes you not want to save them but you have to.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried my best, but its a poor imitation of little nightmares. I find it hard to relate to the story or the character: you play a young boy who attempts to rescue his kidnapped sister from mythological Nordic creatures. But everything you do, see or experience is barely connected. It feels like it is a series of wacky adventures in a dark fantasy world. One time you stumble on a cemetery with zombies, then you find a witch in a swamp, then you just walk through a river out of blood, scary? Not really. It doesn't have to be connected, but it just feels so artificial. It is missing sounds, atmosphere and perspective. Same with the "puzzles" which should belong back to any 90th game: "oh there is a hole in the wall and next to it lies a lever", "oh there is a door with a triangle, circle and cross on it, which ingredients for a spell do I need to combine to open the door?" Those puzzles just bring you back with your thoughts wandering of what you'll have for dinner.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10A very dark and fun game.Inspired from little nightmares and others.Makes you feel very emotion that is possible (joy, sadness, fear, disgust) The game really makes you think and i love the Swedish folklore aspect, I wish more games do this.The only issue i have is the achievement to not die for the entire run through of the game. it is almost impossible and a lot of the time you die from slipping of a log because the game does not lock you in a 2D direction even though you can only walk 2 ways on the log, This makes you fall and die and restart the game. So they should remove the achievement, fix the controls a bit or make it easier to earn the achievement so that only 0.3% of players earn it.But overall, What a game.

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I am writing this review after like a month of not playing it, but managed to have time to type this review so it may not be so accurate. From public opinion this game is by far a great game, but I say otherwise. It's not a horrible game, it's actually a work of art, but there are some major concerns I had while playing this game. To me it seems the original plot of the story kept changing because the creators of the game kept getting more cool ideas and kept squeezing it all together into this small game which ended up making the game's plot very confusing. I started wondering what I am even doing at many parts while playing the game because the story just wasn't it. Aside from all the cool scenes, it's a confusing story game. From trolls to demons like with magic powers to who knows what, the plot wasn't consistent and at times I'm left wondering what is even going on. -- SPOILERSThere is a part of the game which the player climbs what I presume is a light house and at the top is this crystal like thing which you touch and you get this 1900's horror-like clip which I found so irrelevant to the game, whys it even in the game?There were way more annoying/confusing stuff, but I have forgotten since I haven't played it in a while.Aside from that, one of the many things which I found annoying was some of the sound designs. They are either too good for the game, don't fit the game, could be better, or whatever. One example is the little gnome creatures we start helping at the beginning of the game. Why did the creators of the game find it necessary to make them weep, yap, and make noises like little children. It was one of the most annoying things I had to listen to while playing the game.To me this game's story and plot is utter garbage, the only thing keeping people playing this would be the scenery, art, and visuals. I do not recommend unless you are looking for a game with cool effects and such.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. The mix of atmospheric adventure, puzzle platformer and horror with with a story rich folklore topic makes this indie game absolutely fantastic. To be fair, i was quite surprised by the unexpected turns this game took, and yes, it was a roller coaster of emotions, but that is, what I like in a game. With all the unfinished games coming out, Bramble stands for a change. I got more than I asked for and/or expected. I personally struggle with the controls here and there, but that has never been my strong suit. I might see how it goes playing with a controller. Overall, I do recommend this game! Epic Boss Fights, tricky Puzzles, lovingly created characters and bold Horror Elements make this Game must-have.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble is a triumph of sound design and art direction. The world is brilliantly brought to life through Martin Wave and Dan Wakefield's sensational score (namely the arrangement of In the Hall of the Mountain King), and extremely well done camera work.The game does show a few rough edges such as clipping issues and frame dips, but stands tall amongst the linear horror/adventure genre with gameplay that is simple, at times challenging, and constantly innovating on itself. This is an easy recommendation for anyone who wants a tight 4 hour experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A combination of  puzzle/cinematic platformer gameplay and  panic horror, wrapped up in Nordic folklore themeing.The gameplay is varied enough that it kept my insterest trought the 4 hours of my playtrough. Some people think the game is too short but I feel like the lenght is just perfect, making it any longer would have just made it feel padded out. There are already so many awesome moments and setpieces in the campaign. Graphically, it's obvious that it's a smaller indie game but the environmental design and atmosphere are superb and more than make up for any visual shortcomings. is a very charming and memorable experience. It's competently made and clearly with a ton of passion. If you like horror and don't mind the occasional cinematic moments, It's definitely worth a playtrough.

_childDocuments_.review: I got drawn in by the beautiful graphics and magical concept, especially as it brings nostalgia and comfort to a swede. But after about an hour I just felt irritation during pretty much the entire game. The constantly shifting angles makes it difficult to follow along with the controls, sometimes you can't even see that it's a new angle you need to follow leading to death. Not to mention that the rules of the game seem to change as you go on, one moment you can't stray of your path if you try and the other the tiniest misstep sends you to your death. It's also confusing what the game wants you to do because the map is too undefined and unclear about the next step. Many levels I've had to retry an annoying amount simply to understand what my goal even is. I strongly considered getting a refund after an hour because of all these reasons but the positive parts made me at least want to finish it. I wish I had just gotten the refund and spared myself the stress.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Although it's short I think it's a must play for anyone that's into horror (or even a good story).I love that (norse) mythology is an essential part of this game and the lore isn't overbearingly deep but still very emotional and if you read all the books you can find out way more about the backstories of the characters. Although it draws inspiration from norse mythology, the designs and lore of the characters are changed for the game and I think it fits well into the universe.It feels like a movie with the amount of (long) cutscenes but they aren't really annoying like other games where you just wait to play again (And tbh sometimes they were a bit of a relief).The combat is rather easy (mostly dodging and a bit of aimed attacks) but it's fine because the focus is on the story (although some hitboxes were a bit ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥). It makes sense that there are no difficulty settings.You get casual and safe introduction to mechanics that you need later on where you're not safe anymore."Level" design and the general pace is fairly simple and often times repetetive but usually not in a disruptive way.The game has beautiful music and it's used very well to create an amazing atmosphere.In general the sound design is excellent (sometimes I couldn't tell if it came from the game or from inside my house) and sets the whole tone of the game.You can feel this especially when there is nothing concerning on the screen but the music becomes more unsettling or disappears and you feel very unsafe even when everything looks normal.The game has beautiful visuals (especially the lighting) and design choices of characters and environment are great.The camera placement is so good - some perspectives are placed like how you are perceived (e.g. the camera is inside a house and you're observing yourself through the window).This makes you feel vulnerable and watched all the time (afraid of what else is lurking around and watching you).You are so small (also literally) and at times you can see the whole background and the vastness of the landscape in contrast to your fragile tiny self.This choice of design is excellent since the camera forces you to watch the background, making you wonder what you're suppose to look at when it centers your view there.It makes you feel like there is something out there and it should be something to look out for feeding into the idea of not being safe at all times.It's unbelievably immersive and in addition to that I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ loved the gnomes & LEMUS! and I genuinely cared for them (RIP little cage gnome and that one gnome that walked into a bear trap).Apart from the beauty of this game it is also genuinly terrifying.Anytime a new "monster" came, it was horrifying like you actually had to run away (it was a genuine threat, not just in game).I was terrified everytime I heard them approaching, I didn't even want to move.They managed to create a perfect balance between the scary parts and the wholesome parts (loved the hide and seek btw, cutest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing I've ever seen).Everything is in place and has its right to exist in the game (nothing is too much) and I thank the developers for not purposefully stretching the game.There are little details you can easily miss but when you look around (e.g. in the background) and manage to catch it it adds so much to the horror factor and the feeling of unsafety.What's an interesting design choice is that you only get little hints before the bosses come (the wooden figures)and you only get to know the stories (or even names) after defeating them, it makes the first encounters so much better and terrifying because you don't know what they are and everything clicks only after the fight.You begin to feel safe in the cute segments (in the beginning) but you essentially realise that nowhere is safe. I think this game has a "Little nightmares" feeling to it and even some similar mechanics. So if you like that game you will enjoy this one.You can feel that there was so much love put into it.Seriously you could write a whole essay about this game and there are probably a lot of things I've missed but I don't want to go that deep, I already got carried away.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible Nordic fairy tale, complete with the entire scope of lore that is, at all times, beautiful, repulsive and captivating. If you are a fan of stories around frightening trolls that eat children, benevolent forest creatures, whimsical gnomes and malicious kings, you will love this game. It is easy enough for just about anyone to pick up while providing a challenge that doesn't make you want to beat your head into the wall. I strongly recommend playing this with headphones as the sound design is absolute top notch. I do also recommend playing with a controller, as others have mentioned. It feels a lot smoother that way. The content can be very heavy at times but anyone who has read the old school Nordic folklore will tell you that these things were just a part of life and/or myth. The Skogsra in particular was breathtaking - there is a good reason she is their mascot, so to speak. I truly recommend this for anyone who is looking for a quick, narrative driven folk story that makes you just a liiiiittle spooked and leaves you dreaming (or having nightmares) about Scandinavian bedtime stories for days to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how people are finishing this game in a few hours and I wouldn't want to if I could.  The scenery and story are so beautiful and I wouldn't want to rush it. It's more of a lovely fairy tale with a few scary moments.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautiful The controls are very intuitive It encapsulates the Scandinavian aesthetic perfectly runs flawlessly EDVARD F****NG GRIEG The soundtrack is from out of this world! It's one of the best i've ever heard. The game is extremely short [3-4 hrs] It misnames a few mythical creatures. Despite the run length, some fights are clearly just there to add playtime and add no value to the story. The camera angles can often cause you to fall and makes maneuvering difficult.Ultimately, i'd recommend the game for anyone with an afternoon to kill that enjoys games similar to Inside, Little nightmares and limbo. As the vibe and gameplay style is very similar and clearly draws inspiration from all of the aforementioned titles.The music is phenomenal, and adds real cultural spice to the game to make you really feel enveloped in the culture while playing. Hell, they have Edvard Grieg, you can't beat that.The story is nothing crazy to write home about! Very basic stuff, and it's really more like travelling through many mini-stories with one bigger story that you're actively progressing towards at the same time. If you enjoy Scandinavian culture, or even are Scandinavian, this game is 100% for you! Easily worth the price!Bramble The Mountain king is a fantastic game for any adult and despite a few issues that only some Norse folklore nerds will notice, it's a fantastic game with astounding visuals and an aesthetic that will blow you away!

_childDocuments_.review: It took me about 4.5 hours to complete what is possibly one of the absolute best releases of 2023. Where do I begin to talk about what this game gets right?1. Phenomenal sound track. No matter what you were doing there was very nearly appropriate music or ambient sound to accompany you. The final boss's theme music is definitely my favorite, please make the ost available everywhere. 2. Incredible environments in every chapter. The world felt so genuine, and each environment helped me build a great internal picture of the Bramble world. The vibrancy of one setting contrasted with the melancholy of another didn't feel like a change of pace or deviation, it all flowed naturally together. 3. The Bosses. There was not a single boss fight where I did not have fun. Every boss had their own unique combat style, and very rarely it felt like mechanics were being reused. 4. The story. The overall story was so captivating. A young boy trekking through a harsh and unforgiving world to find a sister that for all he knew was dead, encountering so much that would dissuade anyone who wasn't a protagonist away from adventure and still persevering. The constant conflicts and hardships that young Olle had to endure made for an incredible story of growth and sibling love. 5. The variation in game play. It wasn't all platforming, and it wasn't all combat, and it wasn't all stealth. It blended different game play styles quiet well. My only gripe would be that it was so short for the amount of story building that could have been possible. The Digital Art Book even talks about some scrapped ideas that seemed like they could have been fun. Of course, if scrapping those ideas meant that the game would pace better, that was a good decision to make.

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't finish this game which kind of sucks since I really wanted to like it. I made it up to the plague witch and then decided I was done, not because she was super hard but because I didn't care anymore and I finished by watching the game on youtube to see what I missed. I was expecting this game to be heavily inspired by Little Nightmares and it was but not in the best way. You'll definitely receive Little Nightmares flashbacks while playing, both from the sheer numbers of gnomes and some of the puzzles.The game has real boss fights and this is really not a good thing. The throw/fire mechanic is clunky and the controls aren't the best either. Also, you make your monsters a lot less scary once you make us fight them instead of being forced to flee from them. The game's horrifying scenes are well done and satisfyingly intense but the game doesn't really generate fear very well. The bosses are all pretty easy too. The game keeps going back and forth between wanting to terrify you and wanting you to appreciate the beauty and wonder of the magical world. It does an OK job at the former and it badly fails at the latter. The landscapes are consistently beautiful or at least, they are very impressive when they want to be. Unfortunately some of the 'stages' are not impressive by design. These areas especially the swamp and the village are intended to be mostly about the banality and gruesomeness of ordinary death so they don't take advantage of the amazing art work delivered at other times. The last level is amazingly put together, the artwork is like something out of Dark Souls. The artwork I saw during the let's play of the final level was so good that I considered going back and finishing the game. The game keeps you on a very tight leash and there's basically no exploration at all. You just wander from scene to scene.The story is not very good. It feels unfocused and we don't really find out any connection between the big bad and our quest until the very end. The story is at its best when dealing with the trolls. When it tackles other concepts and monsters, it loses its footing. The story is chalk full of DEUS EX escapes which get frustrating after a while.If you liked Little Nightmares, I won't say don't buy this but maybe wait for a sale.Spoilers:The troll scenes are probably the best parts of the game. The rest is kind of hit and miss. The Huldre (They call her a Skogra) fight is cool as is the 'lake fiddler chase.' The Pesta is annoying but I give the game prompts for her visuals. If you look carefully, you can see her watching you from the distance long before she shows up to fight you.My favorite parts of the story are the early parts with the trolls but the game is actually pretty solid as long as we're hiding or running from a colossal monster. The Mountain King himself, the main villain, has really no connection to the kids. So when you actually fight him, there isn't much invested in the fight, especially since at that point you're not sure if you can still get Lillimore back.The Huldre boss and the Swamp witch were both interesting because they made me wonder if maybe I'd made a mistake in killing the Huldre and letting the baby die and was now on the way to the bad ending. I did some research and there is only one ending. You can't save the baby and if you show Huldre mercy, she just kills you. So everything the game tries to do to make you feel guilty is just annoying. The Huldre being the one that Tuva calls you out for crossing the line on really feels strange. She's not a sympathetic monster. We know from her backstory that she kills people without hesitation or remorse. She's more human looking than most of the other monsters and more attractive than the trolls but that's about it.  It just feels weird that the game tries to make you feel guilty for killing her.

_childDocuments_.review: h1] Bramble the Mountain King: Great atmosphere, (Mostly) great bosses [/h1]Bramble the Mountain King is an excellent dark fantasy adventure that is worth looking into if you like horror games and platformers like Little Nightmares.  There's generally a nice juxtoposition with how beautiful and how horrific the game can be at points.My main critique with the game is the random difficulty spike which really only crops up at the end.  In the fight with the Mountain King, there's a point where he slams his hammer on the ground and the vibrations cause stalactites to drop from the ceiling.  Normally, the stalactites are marked before they'd drop with a shadow, but sometimes the shadow would be too subtle or outright bug out of existence.  So, out of everything the game threw at me, that was my only real complaint.All in all, this game was a fantastic way to learn about Norse mythological characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is truly a work of art and absolutely worth a play. It takes an incredibly unique and intriguing perspective on horror and plays extremely similarly to Little Nightmares and Inside. While Bramble is great, it certainly isn't perfect. At times it does suffer from clunky controls, minor bugs, and can feel tedious at times. Personally, I felt that it could have been 1-2 chapters shorter. Overall the game doesn't feel scary, as much as it feels tense and disturbing. Despite these things, Bramble overcomes all of its shortcomings with great artistic direction, an awesome final level, lovable characters, and a great soundtrack. I'll definitely be one of the first people in line for Bramble II and have my fingers crossed that a sequel is in the works.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like games like Ico, Brothers A tale of two Sons, Limbo or those sections in God of War where you are scaling/avoiding giants? If so then you are likely to enjoy Bramble: The Mountain King.This game gets very DARK in places with some mature themes and is NOT for kids.Graphics of humanoid faces are just ok (they went for stylised/doll looks), however the graphics of the creatures, monsters, forest and background areas/details are excellent. Well above what you would expect for an indie title.HDR is not natively supported (even though it would be a great game for it with its contrasts between light and dark areas) and I cannot recommend Windows auto-HDR as it creates a noticeable black crush/film grain type look in darker areas. SDR still looks good though, so would recommend using this if you have an HDR monitor (especially if its an OLED panel like an LG C1, alienware AW3423DW monitor etc).Gameplay involves exploration, light puzzles, light stealth, and light combat sections. Progression is linear (this is not open world).Without getting into spoiler territory there are many "boss" sections (that often involve means other than combat to resolve), with just the one boss that I would consider "annoying", however there are also 2-3  boss encounters which I would consider great (one of which is likely to make a few top 10 lists with the way its handled).Difficulty could be considered Easy-Medium range (this isnt Elden Ring/Sekiro), with nothing designed to road block you for long.Completion time should range from between 4-7 hours for most people who don't use a guide and just explore naturally as they progress.Music is great. Voice acting is mainly limited to the narrator, who does a great job (storybook segments are a stand out).Performance wise it ran at 4k 120fps Epic settings on a high end PC (even when using DLDSR to go to 2.25x it stayed above 60fps). Unreal Engine game but seems very well optimised (no stutter struggle for me).A great indie game from an indie studio and one that punches well above its weight.If I had to assign a score/rating: 8.5/10 or B+

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is thematic and atmospheric and the art isn't too bad.  However, the game play leads something to be desired.  It is essentially a puzzle game, and many of the games are ok, when it comes to finding hidden objects or doing some series of action in order to proceed.  My main problem is when they have "action puzzles"  where you are being chased or searched for or something, and you have to do some kind of timing relative to other moving things in the game.  And the reason why these are a problem is because the sum total of your movement controls are WASD, spacebar (sometimes) left shift to sprint (sometimes) and left ctrl to crouch (sometimes).  Not only are these loosely controlled, but you're watching the character from third person and you can't always see "what they'd see". Sometimes the character himself is entirely occluded by scenery.  But what is even more irritating is the camera, which swings and wooshes around cinematically, depending on where the character is standing in the scene, and the directionals are tied to the camera and not the character.  So the character may be walking down a plank over a river, and suddenly the world wooshes around him, and he falls steps off into the water and drowns immediately adjacent to the plank walkway.  This is further confusing because sometimes the character is on a path and will follow it as long as you're hitting a button that is comparatively forward to the scene.  So add this to action, time pressure, time, and "dangerous" activities (all together) and rather than being exciting and tense, it becomes tedious as you die over and over while trying to both determine the necessary sequence to get the character to go the right way, and also manage to operate your left hand in a contorted series of maneuvers to accomplish that.This would be a lot easier with one or more of the following: Driving with the mouse, steady point of view from behind or over the shoulder, directionals relative to the character's position rather than the camera, camera rotation around the character controlled by player, consistent control actions from scene to scene, instead of them being so context dependent.Now, I know any of those are going to screw up their cinematic artsyness, but they would make the game play more tolerable.

_childDocuments_.review: A linear adventure following a brother and sister who disobeyed their mother and ventured into the forest after dark. At first, the world they've found is full of wonder, but the story gets darker, when the older sister is kidnapped by a troll. The young brother needs to brave the dark corners of the land to save his sister. The gameplay is largely linear, with a few collectables strewn along the levels. The camera is fixed-angle. There's some climbing, a lot of stealth-puzzles (where you need to move from cover to cover, avoiding insta-death line of sight), and even some combat. There some truly memorable enemy encounters, and the many influences of Nordic folklore are very impressive.  I honestly expected the game to be yet another 2d platformer about a small child lost in a dark world, so what this turned out to be truly surprised me. Bramble is steeped in old-school design, but it is a wonderful title nonetheless, with truly memorable encounters, and a wonderful mix of puzzles, combat, stealth and platforming. One of the most under-appreciated titles of the past few years.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Would never have played this game on face value but I got intrigued when I saw it nominated at the horror game awards.What I discovered was one of the scariest games I've played in many years! As charming as it is terrifying, this short and sweet game is a must play for any horror fan looking for something different.It's quite a linear and short game but you'll be on the edge of your seat for the 4-5 hours you spend in this twisted fairytale world, it never allows you to let your guard down and boasts some of the creepiest looking beings I've seen in a game, even Geralt of Rivia might have second thoughts about hunting some of these bastards.If you like Little Nightmares you'll LOVE this! Makes that game look like Pikmin
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This is a difficult one. Overall I liked this game, but I don't think it is "overwhelmingly positive" good. So it is not really a negative review, rather a neutral  one. I liked fairy tale books, music and overall visual design of the bosses.But on a mechanical level it felt a bit rough. Very straightforward levels, one intended path (you leave it, you likely fall to your death), all boss encounters are kind of variation of the same few gameplay ideas. I also really didn't like the look of "human" characters. I think I get, that the idea was to make them look really innocent and childish contrasting the grim and cruel world. But to me they just look like characters from a garbage third grade CGI animation.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! One of my top 3 indie games of this year. 8.5/10Beautiful graphics, absolutely stunning, arty and trippy scenes and some genuinely scary, tense and haunting moments. I played the demo a while ago and was really excited for the official release and it didn't disappoint. The directing of the story and visuals were a 10/10 for me. The combat was good (sometimes a little awkward) and the audio paired with it created fantastic atmosphere (especially the 'final boss') great use of music - very fun.It was such a stunning and immersive world, and the horror aspects were fantastic!I enjoyed that this game didn't hold your hand. You have to figure out somethings for yourself and when your facing enemies, this adds a great level of challenge. My only issue was that the controls and game play were a little bit annoying at times, I often found myself slipping off of surfaces because of the camera angles and the clunky turning of the character. At one point, I died about 6 times because I kept slipping off a stationary platform when I jumped onto it. _childDocuments_.review: As a Swed I'm a bit biased, but let me tell you this.Bramble: The Mountain King transcends mere gaming and immerses you in a captivating narrative based on Nordic mythology. Reminiscent of the genre exemplified by Little Nightmares, this experience intertwines a compelling story line with breathtaking artwork, accompanied by amazing orchestrated musical scores the game successfully sets and sustains the desired mood. Usually horror games goes the everything is horrible route, but Bramble goes darker and darker and then light again, which gives the gameplay high peaks and low valleys. While it contains fewer unsettling moments than Little Nightmares, Bramble: The Mountain King possesses its own unique charm. It's truly captivates the player from start to finish!Pros* The game is STUNNING both in the 2D & 3D assets used & the environmental design.* The soundtrack is amazing (I've been listening to Blomstertid by Martin Wave & BJORN several times after the play through).* It flawlessly captures the essence of the Scandinavian aesthetic.Cons* At times aggravating checkpoints.* Sometimes misguides the players spacial awareness with the set camera which results in failed jumps.* Short game time.* Many puzzles but few are truly challenging.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game! As a native Swede it was so refreshing to see some proper Swedish lore and environments. The horror elements are on point, the environments are amazing and the SFX/Soundtrack is damn good! The art is on point (lots of John Bauer inspired stuff), great voice actors and designs. HOWEVER, some of the puzzles was super weird and the auto-lock on system could have had some work before release. I was also bummed out by the weird depth of field, motion blur and grain combined with very very dark areas and it was hard to see what you were doing half of the times. Luckily some amazing individual posted a solution to remove this in a ini file under Windows/Users/(Your user)/AppData/Local/Bramble_TMK/Saved/Config/WindowsNoEditor and then open the Engine.ini file with notepad, and add this text under all the text in that ini file:[SystemSettings]r.MotionBlur.PreferCompute=0r.DepthOfFieldQuality=0r.MotionBlur.Max=0r.MotionBlurQuality=0r.DefaultFeature.MotionBlur=0r.Tonemapper.GrainQuantization=0r.Tonemapper.Quality=0I feel like these graphics settings should be added into the game, and hopefully the devs will in the future. Another thing that other people are complaining about is the price, but I think 30 EUR is more than fair, this world is currently on fire with inflation, we're all trying to get by, especially smaller dev companies. And I'd much rather pay 30 EUR for this game than giving EA or Ubisoft 60, 70, 80, 100(!) bucks for some other half-baked non-ambitious game. 8/10. Strongly recommend!
