_childDocuments_.review: It is easy to recommend Bramble: The Mountain King (which I'll hereafter refer to as simply "Bramble") if you are interested in it for non-gameplay reasons, and that is presumably true if you are reading this review. Judged purely for its game design and gameplay, however, it has some problems.Playing Bramble feels like being part of several dark fairy tales (European fairy tales, specifically Nordic Swedish ones). Some of my favorite moments from the game were terrifying, as I was a young boy trying to escape some scary monster. You should also be aware that some moments are also genuinely horrifying, and the content certainly pulls no punches (despite the playable character being a child this is certainly not a game for children).The environments are beautiful, and sound design and music are also fantastic. The human characters felt uncanny valley-ish to me, but nothing bad enough to ruin the immersiveness of the experience. It was easy for me to get lost in the experience when some of the gameplay elements weren't getting in the way.A large portion of the game's runtime is more of a "walking simulator", where you won't really have any agency besides proceeding on the path that the developers have created. Even the camera and invisible walls prevent exploration in most cases; you definitely are not encouraged to stray from what the developers want you to do (although there are some achievements that require exploring off of the main path, which feels a bit strange when the game design so actively discourages that).There are traditional game elements, however, but I didn't find most of these particularly fun. Most of the game sequences in the first half felt like wastes of time to me (in the sense that the puzzles and action sequences weren't really difficult or rewarding; I would have preferred just keeping things as an interactive story), and most of the game sequences in the second half felt more frustrating to me than fun. Bramble isn't a difficult game, but there were sequences where I actually died an embarrassing number of times, with a large percentage of those times being in ways that felt frustrating.I think that possibly my biggest complaint would be the camera. The aesthetics of camera shots have clearly been given priority over gameplay. I don't actually mind that, and think it was a good choice for this game! But the problem is that gameplay has been created that doesn't take this into account, and then as a player you are asked to do things that are challenging _because of the camera_, with the punishment being swift and severe. (A curious sidenote: It is honestly amazing the number of times that the game expects you the player to walk off some ledge and drop down without having any way to see what is on the other side or how far you are dropping. Early in the game this was just amusing to me, but I just decided to trust the developers. As the game progressed, however, I accumulated more and more deaths that were a result of me walking off ledges or jumping the wrong way because I couldn't judge depth or direction, and then these frequent and intentional drops of faith became more and more stressful.)That's not to say that the gameplay is "bad" (and, to be fair, there were some puzzles and one boss battle that I did enjoy). Instead, it felt like a pretty average indie game, with what I would consider mistakes that I might expect from designers without much experience. I think that the mediocrity of the gameplay was made more frustrating by a few things: 1) Everything else in the experience was so good that the gameplay weaknesses felt jarring, 2) the sequences with frustration and insta-death took away from the tension and atmosphere, and 3) since so much of the game was already a walking simulator it felt superfluous to introduce game mechanics that weren't particularly polished or fun.Bramble reminded me of Little Nightmares in several ways; it felt influenced by it, and had some of the same strengths, but also some of the same weaknesses. Like Little Nightmares, however, I am positive that what I will remember from Bramble when I look back on it in the future are all of the good things, and the frustration will fade. I am definitely glad that I played it.If you look at a trailer or screenshots of the game and think "that looks like something that I would like to play" then I think it's pretty easy to recommend. It absolutely lives up to the promise of getting to experience being part of a dark fairy tale! You may also experience some gameplay frustrations, but the positives easily outweighed the negatives for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is a 3D horror plattformer. It's story is set in Finnish folklore and mythology so the content warnings are justified for sure.I came across it because I was looking for indie horror games. It certainly bloody and gory. The atmosphere, camera work and music are fantastic. I thought that the people at Dimfrost learned from Little Nightmare's weaknesses especially in regard of the camera. Although I enjoyed the game's atmosphere and story I didn't find it scary most of the time - except for one boss fight that surprised me how amazingly well it was designed and that I found actually spooky.My subjective pro and con about Bramble: The Mountain KingPro: I love indie games and I especially love it when creators take inspiration from their local mythology and folklore.Con: Horror games have more difficulties in creating an intense atmosphere if they strive for realistic graphics and for realistic light and shade, imho. The game has a lot of cutscenes. They are well placed but every now and then they made me think that perhaps Bramble would have shone even more as a movie. Since this con is a very subjective view of mine I would still recommend it to anyone who likes games like Little Nightmares.

_childDocuments_.review: The tutorial is subtle and easy on the eyes. The game uses the very known and common WASD scheme for KBM that makes everything very intuitive. The controller is equally simple but users may face incompatibility issues that require driver updates.The game disregards having a UI; you rarely pick up items or have to interact with your inventory. It tries to minimize the immersion breaking feeling that a bad UI can bring, so it chose to have none. Sometimes a prompt can be seen on screen, sort of a QTE, but not really; in this case, they are quite visible and on your face, as they should be.The graphics and art style are mesmerizing and unique. The contrast between adorable and grotesque results in a very artistic duality that may cause a reaction in the player.Flawless sound design with sound effects impeccably chosen and implemented. The right sound at the right time often resonated as a living part of the game environment; sounds were perfectly selected, designed, and curated to give living things more life. Superb music choices that give an opportunity for exploration into the world of great Swedish classics like ‘Dem Blomstertid Nu Kommer’ that will remark the contrast in the game’s dichotomy even more. The sound design, in my opinion, is simply perfect.The game’s nature has the player explore many different environments within the game’s duality. Cute and vivid in colors and life, you wish to delve in, juxtaposed to macabre and gorey scenes you wish to end asap. Navigating the game’s environment in full immersion is truly an experience. The way the atmosphere is set up is such a great statement for good game design.The characters we meet in our journey are mainly derived from John Bauer’s works and Sweden’s mithology. As for the game’s polarized nature, the models design swing like a pendulum between adorable and grotesque, from smiling gnomes with lovely laughter to evil trolls with cruel facial features ready to chomp on you.All 3D models are evidently carefully crafted with great attention to detail that does not break the idiosyncrasies of the overall artistic style of the game. This style is very pleasing to the eyes. It might be the mix of realistic proportions with the at times cartoonish stylization, perhaps, but there is something unique to this style that I can’t really put into words; it is simply lovely and mesmerizing.This is where this game truly shines. The game has the player follow a story through stories. A great narration will have us navigate several mithologic or folkloric tales of the northern lands while we struggle to achieve our goal of finishing our own journey. The stories are told through classic narration, environmental exposure, and in-game events. The narrator, Nola Klop, will lend her incredible voice and interpretation skills to accompany Olle in his, at times, lonley journey to meet Lillemore and other creatures. You will also find fable books and diaries to complement the game's exposure and narration.This being said, the game is great at what it is; the story telling is split into chapters, like any good book, and has the player follow a  .The game’s pace is at first slow, then picks up and fully launches you into the experience. While at first glance, the game may seem adorable and cute, . The scenes this game hides within can be extremely heavy on the heart. Newborn babies get killed, extreme gorey scenes and sudden death animations out of nowhere. I would not suggest playing this with your nephew, niece, or younger siblings. Some themes pictured in the game are potently sorrowful and woefully charged, with extremely graphic content to go along with them. Gampelay is as simplistic as it gets in a story-driven game.Follow Olle on his adventure through lesser-known Nordic folklore and defeat several iconic figures. Do so by solving puzzles and avoiding dangers to tip-toe your way to the next area. There is no great gameplay with incredible gear combinations, nor is there some challenging mechanic for resource management or fighting technique to be learned. You are Olle, a little child in a fantastic world, and this is his story., what its genre is, and doesn’t try to be anything else; it is a great example of interactive story-telling where the player's hand is held through the whole journey to discover a great tale of ups and downs, of fear and laughter, of nature’s dichotomy in beauty and brutality.If you do not like games like  or , then this is not your game. Bramble directly feeds on this genre of interactive story-telling; if you want some action-packed game, move along; this ain't your style. From the many Scandinavian folklore and ghost stories to John Bauer references, the game puts the player against many different creatures and bosses, always following a contained narrative. One of my favorites is Pesta, the personification of the plague, and Skogsrå, the gorgeous devil-tailed shapeshifter.Each boss belongs to a specific tale, being it’s defeat the end of said narration. Going from one boss to the next and walking through its story is a great way to learn more about Scandinavian lore. There are half a dozen bosses before the end.The bosses included in the game are [spoilers ahead]: I feel like in 5 hours I have completed the game and seen everything it has to offer. I took my time in every little scenario and felt like I saw everything, good and bad, although I missed some figurines. The game’s length must be one of its biggest flaws, but I feel like it ends in the right spot. Artificially lengthening the game might have led to a boring outcome.There is absolutely no reason to replay the game once the veil of mystery has been removed. I’d like to have more excuses than simple achievements to dive back into the game’s gorgeous worlds. Sadly, there is no incentive to replay at all, and obviously, there is no ‘New Game +’ concept.Replaying the game forces you to go through the same slow-paced sections, with close to nothing to explore aside from the already-heard tale. When the player abandons the establish path or ryhtm, the enemies may bug out and scripted events may lose their impact. Like walls exploding by their own whill instead of zombies breaking them because they left after you stood still4.Some animations are a little flawed and stutter, but that’s just me nitpicking.Camera angles sometimes behave strangely. If you do not go the way the game wants you to go, the camera can flip out and confuse itself into a buggy scene.Limited or absolutely no power over the story. At least, several endings would’ve been nice to have.Short game with no replayability at all. Buy it when it's on sale.The art style and narration are flawless and enticing.If you like interactive story telling, this is your game 100%.The game contains some serious gore and grotesque content that may not be appropriate for younger or more sensitive audiences.I’d say this game deserves attention, but 30,00€ might be a bit much for a 5-6 hours experience. Sadly, the game suffers from the "one use only experience" syndrome, and this conditions my conclusion for the game’s worth in money.

_childDocuments_.review: They really put time and effort into this game, I am in love.The graphics are incredible at such a small game size. The amount of compression here is insane while keeping visual appeal, that was the first thing that astounded me. Now to the game play, I went ahead and grabbed the demo, wanting more info before I bought the full game. Let me tell you the "Demo" is not your ordinary run of the mill demo offered. You actually get a whole bunch of content for 100% free and it showcases all of what you need to see to want the full game. Let's just say after beating the demo I instantly bought the game and art book as I fell in love.The music and overall aesthetic of this game is it's true charm, the game developers ability to make you feel small in a massive world is incredible. The POV while running is dynamic while cameras do track and follow, you are not limited to how you wish to play or run around. The mastery in design and art style is a wonder, every page in the art book or in game is drawn with love and attention to detail while holding close that familiar medieval style we all love. Befriending giants and saving children from certain death is always fun too haha, this game makes you happy then instantly sad then happy. It's a whirlwind of emotions and a true masterpiece to play, I will not spoil that for anyone.The monsters and lore of this game is everything I have always wanted in a video game.My rating:Graphics: 8/10 beautiful (Game could be larger to accommodate ray tracing, and added textures etc)Story: 10/10 (Nothing needs to be done here, everything is a joy to play)Movement 8/10 (some jankiness, but hey it's too be expected, jumping mechanics are a tad sticky and not as responsive as I would like, It did not keep me from being able to move fast though, Just takes some learning)Horror!!! Is it scary?: well for me yes, and no. The lore is beautiful paired with amazing gfx and story telling. You will be scared though at certain times, aka jump scares that made me throw my juice at the wall XDOverall this game is worth the price point 100% It is a fair $ for what you receive. (Note to developers)I would be interested in seeing an online game mode or 2-4 coop mode to play with friends. Another game mode could be 5-10 people fighting 2-3 giants in a lake etc. Great game guys! can't wait to see what's next!

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game. The backgrounds are beautiful, atmospheric, and memorable, featuring gorgeous Scandinavian forest landscapes in all varieties. The character designs look like they're straight out of a John Bauer painting, and the music is highly atmospheric Scandinavian folk music, ending with a great rendition of In The Hall of the Mountain King by Edward Grieg.The story varies from cute and wholesome to horrifically dark. I think maybe they could've cut down on the gore a little, as it felt pretty excessive at times, especially during the troll section early on in the game, though to be fair, the horror of it is pretty accurate to the old and very dark fairytales it borrows from. This is an aspect that I think will turn a few players off the game, though, so keep that in mind if you're considering buying this game. The small boy you play as can also get chopped in half if you're not careful while playing, so it's definitely not a game for the faint of heart.As a Norwegian, I was pleasantly surprised to see that this game doesn't only features Swedish folklore, but also a few creatures that are exclusively Norwegian, such as Pesta and the Mountain King himself. The designs and backstories for Näcken and the Skogsrå are also a nice mix of both the Swedish version and Norwegian version of the creatures, which I quite liked, as it takes the best of both worlds, while still keeping it instantly recognisable to people familiar with either country's folklore. It also isn't afraid to veer a little bit away from the original fairytales, as the main story surrounding the mountain king is a completely original one divorced from the original myths, but it works well.There have been a number of games over the years based around Scandinavian folklore, but no game has done it as well as Bramble, which really nailed the atmosphere and storytelling, and provided fun gameplay to accompany it.

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing experience.Bramble: The Mountain King kept me hooked from start to finish. It's one of these rare games that not only keep their momentum until the end, but also ramps up to a fantastic grand finale. Every chapter was a fresh surprise, and always brought something new and interesting to the table in terms of gameplay and story. It might start calmly, but Bramble soon takes a completely different route than what you'd expect. I genuinely did not expect the story to develop in the ways it did, and it was so much fun to explore the many ideas it brings to the table.The production quality of Bramble is absolutely amazing. This game is truly gorgeous, and it knows it. The excellent camera work and beautiful scenic shots/interludes show off the amazing world it takes place in, with so many different environments and settings. The music is incredible and works great with the atmosphere of the world, growing and fading in perfect sync with your progress (that last boss fight, oh man). Bramble sounds as amazing as it looks, and that's not something you always see. There are little nuggets of lore and foreshadowing scattered all over the place, waiting to be discovered by the keen-eyed, and the excellent narration wraps it all up beautifully.I appreciate the well-thought pacing of the game. I clocked about three hours and I think this is just about the right length for a game like this. None of the levels feel like they drag too long, and the variety of mechanics and environments help keep things fresh and interesting throughout the playthrough.The game is not entirely free of issues, though. The player physics and the controls can be a little glitchy sometimes, especially when you need some precise movement, and this led to some frustrating deaths that felt really bad. This wasn't often and definitely isn't a deal breaker, but until it's patched, be prepared for some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ moments here and there.I also had multiple moments where the fixed camera and level design made it very unclear where I should proceed next. Again, nothing serious, but it could use a little more work.You know a game is really good when the credits start rolling and you're devastated. Bramble did exactly this to me. It's one of these gems that leave an impact on you, and you can really feel the love and passion the team put into this title. I loved every moment of it and I highly recommend it. Well done, Dimfrost! I can't wait to see what's next from you.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble is an A+ storytime wrapped in simple game mechanics, and takes quite a bit of nerves to stomach through some scenes.To start off, Bramble is NOT like Little Nightmares. The atmosphere and theme are where the similarities begin and end. Little Nightmares relies heavily on parkour and platforming, and opts out of potentially traumatizing you by stylizing a lot of their gore and horror. Bramble goes for the complete opposite. It wants to lull you into a promise of a dark fairytale puzzle-platformer, and then hits you over the head with realism that's oftentimes not for the faint of heart. On top of that, the platforming mechanics often inconsistent and pathing unclear.HOWEVER, as soon as I understood that i will be playing a storybook, and not something like LN, everything clicked. Bramble transports you to a time when fairytales were meant to teach children that the forest is not a playground. That curiosity kills the cat, and that creatures who live in the woods will most likely kill you. You are an outsider in a breathtaking ecosystem that will never be your home (a subversion I REALLY enjoyed).You play as Olle, a little boy who snuck out to explore the forest with his adventurous sister Lillemor. Everything starts off fairly tame, but as soon she gets herself into trouble, the story begins to show its dark and twisted underbelly. The story is, ultimately, never losing hope despite how dark and difficult life gets. Olle is forced to grow up in such traumatizing ways, and the fact that he's a silent protagonist ON TOP of being a child makes the experience so much heavier on the player.To end this haphazard review, let me highlight my favorite aspects based on which I'd recommend the game:1. The graphics are great, the atmosphere shifts super well throughout the game. The devs really play around with lighting and level design to tell the story.2. The narration is top-notch, wish you could choose Swedish to complete the experience <33. The folklore. That's it. Just. Wow.4. The camera work is a dead giveaway that this was intended as a storybook experience more than a platformer. The camera angles shift with every new scene, like in old Resident Evil games, for example. It really enhances the cinematic experience of everything you do. For me, this one shot in particular, where the camera is positioned as if you're someone inside a house looking through the window at Olle (while you're running around with him) was what hit the nail on the head.5. Last but not least - the boss fights. Oh my god, their design gets better and more visually striking as the game progresses. You never know what to expect with each boss, and it's all the more exciting when you experience the fights. The final boss fight accompanied by the soundtrack is done like a proper culmination of the entire journey. All in all, Bramble was the kind of game I really needed to play, and I'm thrilled that I did. For those who like dark stories and heavy themes, it's perfect, but for those hoping they'll get puzzles and platforming exactly like Little Nightmares or INSIDE, you miiiight want to scale down your expectations. Bramble is more about the story and atmosphere, bogged down by platforming bugs and inconsistencies that might frustrate you, especially if you're playing on a controller.

_childDocuments_.review: Not quite a real game, not quite a walking simulator. But frustrating all the way.This game really wants you to dislike it with it’s sluggish controls, unrewarding gameplay and unpolished design. All the Nordic folklore stuff don’t get to shine properly in what feels like a cheap student work.The game can’t decide what it let’s the player do, and what it doesn’t. Right down to the last action.Even the best part of the game, the graphics, are often murky and ill designed. They are bad at conveying where the game wants you to go and what is relevant and possible. This turns many parts of the game into learn-by-dying nonsense.The concept is all over the place. At times it’s so sappy and cutesy, it’s sickening. It feels like a children's game teaching toddlers how to use a controller. But then - BOOM! It turns into an unnecessarily bloody gore-fest and everything is way too dark and disturbing for kids. Who is this for?In the middle of the game, in the swamp chapter, you momentarily forget the horrible gameplay, and even get a little invested in the atmosphere. But by the end you’ll be swearing this game to the ground.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you remember when you were a child and someone read a fairy tale to you? Do you remember experiencing the story you were hearing vividly in your mind's eye? Replicating this feeling is what this game wants to achieve, and it succeeds beautifully at it. There's not much to manage as there are no skills, abilities, perks, etc. All you have to do is experience a story and feel like you're living it. Fair warning: Even though the story is clearly inspired by fairy tales of old, it is not for children. This is Brothers Grimm fire, brimstone, pest and cholera kind of fairy tale, not the Walt Disney kind. There's a fair amount of gore and horror elements in the latter half of the game.In today's sea of samey games, this one convinces by being unique and memorable.

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful, light-hearted romp through Scandinavian folklore. Ignore the red flags and red herrings, and just enjoy a merry adventure with the likes of playful gnomes, adorable little hedgehogs, kindly old librarians, and friendly stone giants. Do a bit of boating with a friendly old woman, take swimming lessons with one of the ladies who likes to hang around, enjoy a walk in the forest with an enchantingly lovely companion, or play tag with some of the villagers who like to give hugs. At the end of your adventure, enjoy a meal with the king himself, who is sure to be impressed with your cutting wit and shining personality.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: the Mountain King is a fascinating and dark fairy tale bathed in Norwegian folklore. This is a narrative, linear experience that will take you close to 6 hours in your first play through as long as you're not gunning it to the end.  The visuals are spectacular and the gameplay is simple. There are are puzzle, platforming and combat scenarios throughout the game that don’t feel samey.  There are collectables to discover if you take your time exploring the world.I played it twice, back to back.  I thoroughly enjoyed my first play through, but got nothing out of the second.  There is no replayability outside of looking for and collecting the remaining collectables and going for 100%.  I played it through a second time to get more of my money out of it because I knew I would never go back in after that initial 6 hour play-through.Recommend on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very beautiful game. The environments are amazing. There are a lot of interesting details and references to Swedish folklore, not just in boss encounters but also in objects around the world. The sound design is absolutely fantastic. Both sound effects and music is top notch and immerses you and is even incorporated into the fights.There isn't much story to speak of. It feels like the "story" is more of an excuse to guide the player through the environments. It's still ok though, but it's definitely not a story driven game. So if you're looking for an interesting story this isn't the game for you.Gameplay is the thing I have the most issue with. The first half hour to an hour feels mostly like a walking simulator. The controls feel clunky at times and the camera angles sometimes feel awkward. For example, having depth when camera angle is more or less in a platformer perspective but then you can still miss a jump because you're "too deep" into the platform without being able to see it.Overall a good game and fun enough to play. It's not super long (3-4h) but considering it's made by a small indie studio it's very well made. I only wish there had been a bit more of a story and not just an escort from one Swedish folklore to another.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is a dark linear adventure game that is has some light platforming and puzzle/stealth mechanics. The game isn't overly difficult but it's all about the journey through a horror setting. The game is absolutely gorgeous, awesome soundtrack, and super interesting story based on Nordic fables which I didn't know about. It was cool going through it and learning some interesting fables for the first time. There's not too much game play but it works great for what it is. It kind of reminds me of a game like Inside except more of a 3D setting for it. It's really dark and is not afraid to show some gruesome deaths. It's short and sweet. I definitely recommend this if you're into darker theme adventure themes, it's really great.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Now this this review may sound like I didn't enjoy the game I did though. I keep telling friends they have to play it that it's beautifully made and the story is great but with any game, we all have problems with it and isn't that what reviews are for to say what we thought? As some reviews have said the movement was kind of clunky. The sprint is no different from just walking I found. It also took some time to get out of movements which kind of sucked during battles. As well as lining up shots sometimes wasn't that smooth I found. I also wish we had more interaction and exploration with the other creatures but that's just people, it is a horror game but trying to keep them alive at times I found added to it. Though I feel like the story lost itself along the way. At one point I forgot we were looking for his sister after you deal with the trolls. We got back to it but there was a long point when you hear nothing or are shown nothing of the main goal. Even just showing you are going the right way to reach that goal like evidence that troll went that way to remind you the main goal is getting her back. Even have the storyteller talk about her more to remind you. Again I did love this game I'm trying to work on the not dying achievement now.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a loveletter to Scandinavian folklore.It is bright and joyful, and it is grotesque and cruel. The story is about Olle and Lillemor, two siblings living in medieval Sweden. It starts with a fairytale about Bramble the Mountain king. Their mother warns them that if they go out at night they will be taken by the bramble. So they go out, of course. On their adventure they encounter creatures like gnomes, cloudberry people, trolls and even zombies.The boss fights are very cool and unique, the soundtrack is amazing and the visuals are stunning. The only negative I have to say is that the controls and camera angles felt janky at times, but nothing gamebreaking. Well worth a try, I havent enjoyed a game this much in a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this one. Playing through the dark folklore stories and seeing them play out as you ran through them was amazing. Creepy and beautiful. The music and sound design were also top notch, and really pulled you into this world. Glad I picked this one up and definitely recommend giving it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: An Unforgettable AdventurePrepare to be transported to a world like no other in "Bramble The Mountain King." This grim adventure, inspired by dark Nordic fables, offers a gaming experience that is truly extraordinary. As I delved into the depths of Bramble, I found myself captivated by its unique and awe-inspiring world.One aspect that truly stood out was the game's exceptional music. At times, it evoked such powerful emotions that it brought tears to my eyes. The orchestral masterpiece, including the mesmerizing "In the Hall of the Mountain King" by Edvard Grieg, added depth and intensity to the climactic end boss fight, where the music elevated the epicness to new heights.Throughout the game, I couldn't help but develop a strong sense of protectiveness towards the main character, Olle, and his sister Lillemor. I found myself deeply invested in their journey.Having Scandinavian friends in my community added an extra layer of enjoyment to the game. Their knowledge of folklore and music enriched my experience, allowing me to appreciate the game's authenticity even more. The attention to detail and the incorporation of cultural elements made "Bramble The Mountain King" feel like a true homage to the Nordic heritage.One of the game's greatest strengths lies in its ability to seamlessly blend cuteness and beauty with the grim and dark. It's a delicate balance that Dimfrost Studio executed flawlessly. The juxtaposition of charming aesthetics with grotesque creatures and haunting environments created an atmosphere that was both enchanting and chilling.I'm eagerly anticipating the future games of Dimfrost Studio. Their ability to craft such an immersive and unforgettable experience in this game left me hungry for more. I can't wait to see what they have in store for us in their upcoming projects.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. This game is stunning!! From the level building to the dark fairy tales made real. Has a kind of "Little Nightmares" feel to it, but within a more serious tone. The game pulls no punches and can be quite dark (and sometimes terrifying). Is a fairly short play-through, but definitely worth the ride. Will remember this one for quite awhile.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed this game with about 15 hours in, and honestly just wow, this game is so beautifully crafted and the story telling is amazing. If you're a lover of horror mixed with folklore/fantasy, 10/10 recommend getting this game, especially now with its very cheap Steam sale price.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this to be an incredible experience overall. I was completely captivated from the start until the end. _childDocuments_.review: I had so much fun playing this game. The setting is beautiful - as is the story, the music and all of the lore. It really draws you into this world of madness and cuteness. I appreciate that the story is somewhat made up for interpretation and that it let's your imagination fill in the "gaps" of the story. Me being a Swede makes me appreciate this even more since it's set in Sweden and with all of the nordic folklore, it was really fun to see. If I should compare it to other games I've experienced it's like a mix of "Inside", "Senua's sacrifice" and "A plauge tale". All really great games, so it gives you an idea of how well made this is. It's not too challenging, and also not too easy. I feel like they balanced the gameplay really well for making both beginners and more advanced players able to enjoy it. The contrast in this game is a big reason that makes it scary and really unsettling. It goes from being adorable to really gory in a second, and it works. I loved to be part of this world, even though I'm really glad I do not have to live in it and don't have to meet those creatures. _childDocuments_.review: This game is my Game of the Year.If you're a fan of narrative-driven game with spooky stories, folklore and a love a good puzzles, look no further – Bramble: The Mountain King is the perfect game for you. I found out about Bramble through a TikTok showcase before its release and I immediately added it to my wishlist.The brilliance of the music and sound design cannot be overstated – I loved it! It really establishes the game's atmosphere. The artwork and visuals are not just aesthetically pleasing; they expertly set the stage for the immersive experience. The use of light and shadows really work well, you're cheerful one minute with bright colours and light... and then... well... you get the point.I've played through it once and watched others on Twitch and YT play through it too because I can't quite get enough of seeing people react to the gameplay. I've been genuinely recommending it to everyone I know. This game satisfies the itch I've had for a unique horror/spooky experience, and the story having folklore adds a wonderful layer.I'll be looking out for more from Dimfrost, for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble is a great new entry in the cinematic platformer genre, becoming a natural successor to games like Limbo, INSIDE, Unravel, Little Nightmares (etc.) and their fathers ICO and Shadow of the Colossus. This time though, the game takes a step in the 3rd dimension again, making it a full fledged 3D platformer.All of the above mentioned games play a role in being sources of inspiration for Bramble, some more directly than others. Often times you'll think "Hey, I've seen this scene in <insert game from above list>". But the game does also enough of its own things to stand out from the others:- the well executed cinematic tracking shots as you walk through the insanely beautifully designed nature of sweden- a greatly told story referencing nordic myths and fairy tales narrated through voice acting- some of the most detailled gorey nightmare scenes we've yet seenAll of this is embedded in very lighthearted puzzle platforming, very easy and thus not distracting so your eyes can enjoy the many details of this world. The 3D gameplay doesn't involve many unfair jumps, and the checkpoints are very briefly seperated. There are also surprisingly many boss fight, but they are also not very difficult, so the frustration factor is very low. Also the boss phases do have checkpoints.Thus this also comes with a warning: If you seek a challenge in games and get bored easiely with shallow gameplay, Bramble might underwhelm you. For the rest of us, the path of cinematic platformers could not have a better entry today. Bramble foreshadows what's possible with games becoming a playable piece of artwork.I'll gladly return to the world of Bramble often, like the other games in my list above. If you feel the same, this game is definitely for you!(Time after first credit roll: 4.9 hours)

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is a horror game focusing on themes of Scandinavian/Nordic folklore. And for me, it is a fresh idea mainly because they added a "culture" themed to it. It's not just a "horror" game. It's a retelling of a world yet terrifying portrayal of Nordic folklore and what it means for a kid that had to experience such gruesome tragedies and graphic imagery just to survive. And to look for his sister, means he had to endure harsh environments as well. This game might be short but it was decent. The story writing might be plain and easy to anticipate but they still delivered through scenery,ambient, and musical scoring. The eerie silence, the dreaded environment, and the sound especially when they played "In The Halls of the Mountain King" I just lost it. The thrill is there. All of it, was a nice touch of perfection to me. It really captured the accuracy of every folklore while maintaining a balance of saturation and horror. With that I mean, even if it's a folklore they didn't overdo it. They didn't gave them exaggerated powers. They stayed true to the resource materials. It's a game that are meant not to be feared but it was meant to be educational, to impart a knowledge from another culture. To be able to absorb a material through games is such a wonderful experience to learn new and appreciate things in life. Soooooo, props to DIMFROST for making this wonderful game. I just hope that some other indie devs will follow your creative steps to also commit and do their own version of BRAMBLE. I give this 8.5/10. <3I might platinum the game but not at this moment. I need to prep myself first for a no-death run. HAHAHA

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved my time in this game and it was a treat to finish. The game has a demo and I think that is an excellent way to see if the game is for you so I do recommend trying the demo. I really enjoyed the gameplay, just moving through the zones felt great. The atmosphere and music were absolutely top notch and it did tonal shifts absolutely masterfully. Crawling through blood and guts, everything seeming just depressing, dark and cruel and I start to get the feeling this game is just a dark dark game and nothing else but then suddenly I am in a beautiful forest with the most amazing tranquil music playing. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I so rarely leave reviews on games, but I thought this one warrants one.  This game is absolutely breath taking.  I'm not typically one to fawn over beautiful graphics, however both the graphical fidelity and general art direction of this game is positively stunning. The storyline and horror elements are expertly crafted.  Basically, I am mostly parroting what other reviewers have said previously, though it is certainly all true.On one hand, $30 doesn't seem like a great value proposition for a game that I completed in just over 4 hours.  However, I am going to be thinking about and talking about this game for quite some time I think, so I am going to say that it is absolutely worth it.  If this game goes on sale, it is an absolute no brainer, but if you don't have to worry about spending $30 and are looking for a game that will fully immerse you in a dark fairytale universe and bring you nearly to tears ... please buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: You get to run around in a magical Scandinavian forest as a miniature human while looking for your missing sister. _childDocuments_.review: A very atmospheric experience. Thematically, it's occasionally "heavy fare" and should only be enjoyed if you're in a better mood. Unfortunately, the keyboard and mouse controls are sometimes off, so there's a certain potential for frustration. In the end, you get a few very sophisticated hours of puzzle fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding game! The artistic direction is breathtaking and I really enjoyed getting lost in Bramble's world. Scandinavian folklore has always been a bit mysterious and I feel like the developers have really managed to transcribe it correctly, including the magical yet enigmatic and slightly horrific side of it. The only problem I had is with the camera mecanic and my own depth perception, which are both kinda broken imo, and sadly that means that we quickly find ourselves falling into the void for nothing, knowing that the game camera is not very friendly on top of that is sometimes frustrating. Beyond that, 12/10 would recommend. Also, I don't know if before arriving at the Butcher, the stone statue in the water is a reference to The Groke from the Moomins but in any case I saw a little nod to Tove Jansson's character and loved it~ I will definitely come back to the game to try the flawless run and earn the last trophy I don't have. GJ Dimfrost!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game a lot. Great music, beautiful environment, engaging story and a really cool adventure. Very creative. _childDocuments_.review: Incredible from start to finish. I'm a huge fan of mythology and this game did not disappoint! _childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game was absolutely fantastic! I found myself saying "I already love this" without even leaving the first room you spawn in on. What instantly captivated me was the use of fixed camera angles, the atmosphere, and the beautifully talented narrator. At first I found myself thinking the puzzles were too easy, but as the story progressed, I got deeper and deeper into the atmosphere and the world around me so that I didn't care about how easy or difficult it was, I was too busy being captivated. I commend how this game doesn't shy away from blood, gore, and harsher topics. Sometimes games limit themselves by trying to appease everyone. By not doing that, I was able to continuously be surprised by the curve balls the game threw at me. Some small things that I appreciated that this game did was: Not have any cut-scenes or continuation scenes after dying (the game simply fades to black and immediately spawns you back in, no need for excessive waiting or clicking), the fixed camera angles were both unique but also expertly placed so that I wasn't aggravated when trying to maneuver, and I especially appreciated how it locks you in place when walking over single lane objects (like planks and tree limbs) (one of my biggest faults with fixed angle games is how easy it is to fall off small objects but this game eradicates that).I can't recommend this experience of a game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: What an awesome game, you can tell how much work and love was pour into this. The story is simple - a boy is searching for his lost sister and on the way meets all kinds of creatures from Nordic mythology. it started as an innocent fairy tale, but turned out to be quite brutal and gory. Even as the protagonist is a young boy, this is not a game for children.To sum it up:+graphics are really beautiful, attention to detail can be found everywhere.+soundtrack - well done!+the story - what the protagonist will go through...no spoilers though+cuteness meets brutality, a contrast rarely seen in other games+bosses are quite enjoyable as well-game length is just about right. I finished it in less than 5 hours, but I didn´t explore much and missed many achievements-the protagonist is weak(as can be expected, considering he´s a child) and can die very easilySo do I recommend it? Hell yeah! This is one of the best indie games you will ever have the pleasure to come across.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Set against the backdrop of a Nordic land plunged into darkness through the actions of a grief-stricken King, the game is as a fable told to the player via gentle narration as we guide the hapless Olle through multiple trials on his quest to save his sister. The loop of play is simple enough: move from one area to the next, wisely avoiding various traps, pitfalls and trolls as you go. Lightweight boss fights serve to break each bite of the story into chapters; from confronting a drowned musician who insists on trying to yeet us off the rocks and preventing a deranged midwife from entreating rituals that result in deceased infants to repeatedly stabbing a very naked witch without a prompt to stop, as well as being forced to avoid the sharp ends of very large pieces of cutlery ourselves, it's fair to say our Olle is having a seriously bad case of the Mondays.While it's not a triple-A product in the conventional sense of the term, I guarantee you Bramble looks every bit as good as one. The environment is, in stark contrast to games such as Little Nightmares, Limbo or Inside, full of colour and life. Verdant grassy meadows sway around Olle while sombre notes ring out and gnomes adorned with red pointy hats struggle in the surroundings, sometimes joyfully, more often fearfully. Indeed, sweet and peaceful downtime emerges between the horrors of Olle's tale but it is short and ultimately uneasy. Importantly though, it serves to highlight what Olle is really fighting for: not just his sister's salvation but peace for himself as well as the other creatures and beings who inhabit this strange land. Far from actually being a caricature of an anxiety-ridden child, the very journey he embarks upon proves that he is much more alike his sister than the narrator initially lets on.The only complaint I can reasonably level against Bramble is that it's a very short game with little replay-ability: I personally would do perhaps two play-throughs at most, three tops, even that much would likely only be for streaming purposes. However in my view this is worth the cost of purchase, especially so if you enjoy playing adventure games of this style.

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Worth every minute and every penny. Phenomenal storytelling, environmental design and soundtrack. Very nostalgic since it had a lot of lore and music reminiscent of my childhood, thanks to growing up in Sweden's beautiful countryside; where the forests and fields are splendid during the day, and quite... unpleasant during the night. If you're fond of Swedish folklore and mythology, this will be a golden gem for you. I was careful to avoid spoilers, so little did I know how perfect it would be to play Bramble: The Mountain King during Midsummer Eve. Wonderful coincidence that really set the mood.

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Wow... I am speechless... I was expecting a good game, since the reviews were so good... didn't look up anything before playing.... I regret now not buying it the first time I saw it, just to give my immediate support to the dev team. I was absolutely blown away. Everything, from the visual design, sound design, ost, story, mechanics, the pacing (how it goes from a hippie nature trip to brutal gore horror in seconds), even umm, BOSS FIGHTS? Like I know this isn't a type of game to actually have good boss fights... but somehow they are perfectly done. Not to hard, not to easy, great music, great scenes, great backstories, fun to play... I am shocked by this game in the best way possible. If you enjoyed classics like Playdead's Inside, or Tarsier's Little Nightmares, this is a must. If you didn't, first re-evaluate your life choices, and then still get this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Remarkable, weird, and creepy game. It is a great re-telling of a few folktales that combines many different mechanics and styles in a way that actually really works.At times it feels like:Limbo/Inside (and has some issues of the latter (i.e. you gotta die a few times to figure out a puzzle - it is very hard to not die on your first encounter with many levels)); Plague Tale; Agony; Harry Potter Games (the ones that came out in early 2000s); Witcher 3 (especially Swamp Chapter, but more);Ori;Hellblade;But it never feels derivative - Bramble manages to add an extra spin on each of those "tropes/references" and be a great game in it's own style.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that the soundtrack of the game is PHENOMENAL, It perfectly fits into the Nordic/Swedish aesthetic of the game and conveys intense emotions during every scene. The environment is gorgeous, especially in the first two chapters. It's mesmerizing and mystical, with every location and view that could be saved as wallpaper. Though yes, the game can be quite brutal and cruel, the game has a lot of stories to tell about Nordic folklore and I was touched at some moments. With all its beauty, it's still a horror game and it was pretty darn spooky. So if you have the guts and the heart to give it a try, it'll be worth it (especially with headphones).

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a proper grim fairy tale.Plays like Little Nightmares, but is completely unique in its own right. Love the world and troll folklore. Makes me want to play more Scandinavian set games. Every part made me question how this world works, what is artistic choice and what is real. _childDocuments_.review: I am happy that I bought this game, I think it's awesome! :)(Got it on sale, so I wouldn't pay the full price, tho. :/)The story is captivating and it's cool to have the narrator do all the talking.With that said:The voices of the little dwarf people were so annoying to me, that I had to turn down the volume. :xIf they were ment to be annoying - 10/10, well done.I honestly was surprised how dark the story actually got and how they displayed it, so if you're into that, do play that game. :)I know, that there are trigger warnings in the beginning of the game, but still... - had many games with those kinda warnings and they did not deliver.I was emotionally invested and it was the right kind of horror & suspension for me. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most incredible gaming experiences I've had. The graphics, camera angles, music, story telling...every single bit of this game is truly a masterpiece. _childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Two words: totally impressed. After starting to play a few minutes of Bramble: The Mountain King, I told myself I'd make a review for this game after my playthrough - yet it became immediately necessary during the part where I heard one of the songs of the game, "Blomstertid", man - I was literally taken aback by emotion hearing it, simply the most beautiful music I've ever heard in a video game, even if short - and came to a realization, although I have yet to finish the game: in spite of its' tiny flaws (that don't prevent from enjoying it), this game has something really special and wonderful to show and give.What caught first my attention were the graphics though: an incredible care and sense of detail were brought to them, the beauty is visually omnipresent too, although counterbalanced by some necessary darkness and gloom, the game having some horror elements - by the way, it seems clearly inspired by old fables, a bit like Hansel and Gretel, but with . . . a gory side to it by what I saw, so I couldn't say Bramble would be for kids: there are explicit depictions blood and cadaver meat included here : )Otherwise, as for the "bright side" of the game's art, when it's cheerful and joyous, it really is: bright colors, vivacious elements of nature, and strange beings / animals taken straight out of a tale give all of it an enchanting vibe, the graphics and music finding a cohesion and coherence that is near perfect. My only small gripes with the graphics were that the textures / renders looked a bit "plastic" and old sometimes in my opinion, nothing shocking nor preventing from enjoying the game's beauty, but I think the devs could have done an even better job with the renders, even if easy to say. Otherwise, it's just an incredible work of art, in which you can feel all the love and attention poured into it, so can't criticize that much.The gameplay is very simple, nothing demanding nor difficult to get - I'll be honest, I have yet to go on with the game, so I don't know if it gets much harder after, but so far it's really not challenging; and even with this rather "easy" aspect, I got hooked from the start of Bramble and couldn't let go of my controller until I decided to make a review. So as for the gameplay, no noticeable thing to say, aside that the difficulty makes it welcome to any player, and it renews itself enough to keep the player captivated from the start and after. The only flaw I encountered with it was that sometimes the movements feel a little slow and stiff, but absolutely nothing gamebreaking.Well I wish there were more games like this on Steam! I first started it by default, without knowing that much what I was getting into, and was more than "not disappointed", I was surprised and amazed - so frankly, I'd recommend Bramble: The Mountain King to any player (over 10 yo maybe lol) who wants to play something different and refreshing - because all inspired from some old fables it is, it simply reactualizes all of that kind of folklore into an indie game offering a little journey between light and darkness, with a  personality of its' own, and a remarkable one at that - fully recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review:
Bramble The Mountain King takes you on a gripping and unsettling journey through stunning environments. Take on the role of Olle, a young boy setting off to rescue his sister, kidnapped by a dreaded troll. Not everything in Bramble is exactly how it seems - in this strange land with creatures big and small, you must be careful when to approach and when to hide. Many hungry and spiteful beasts lurk in these forests and caves.

Call upon the Spark of Courage, an enchanted fragment granting the gifts you need to endure the pitfalls and trials in your path. Defeat the horrid creatures you encounter in different and unique ways. Be warned, courage without kindness can take you down a dark path.

name: Storyteller
detailed_description: Storyteller lets you build stories using a visual language. The goal on each level is to make a story that fits the given title by placing settings and characters that react to each other, creating a narrative through their relationships. Storyteller's comic-panel design and charming animations allow for experimentation within the framing of its many stories: just drag and drop characters to see how the story plays out! Play with a library full of characters and themes, heroes and villains, dragons and vampires, infidelity and revenge, love, lies, madness, and more! Use the blank canvas to manipulate secrets and desires, slay monsters or terrorize people with them, betray lovers or bring them together. You know how the stories go — but this time you are the author.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a cute side scroller type puzzle game, where you have to take a phrase and then turn it into a dramatic scene. You go through a mix of storys and even have some easter eggs in the end. -"Muhahahahaha murder."-"Do I really have the patience for this?"-100%'s the game "Yes... yes I do."This game is definetly fit for any new gamers who are looking into a puzzle game that is more simple. The nice thing about this puzzle game is that you are not in a horror setting or in first person so you can have a super chill experience while also making cute love stories... or murder scenes.The game play itself is pretty simple. You just drag, drop, and rearrange items that the game provides in order to create a scene. Not much else to it.I love the simple 2d style that these graphics offer, its easy on the eyes and its honestly really cute to watch the characters little faces. For being 2d and only really seeing them from the side they are very expressive little guys. The book itself is a little more detailed then the characters, but I overall think it compliments the style of the game and truly makes it feel like you're in a book. This game is single player, however, from what I have seen of the tiktok community and the steam community everyone seems very friendly and willing to help if needed. You can realistically play for as long as you want, however, If you only do one playthrough, with all the content, its only about 3 hours worth. Overall I did really enjoy this game, it made me laugh and had funny little plays that go along with it. I hope they add more, I feel like there wasn't loads in this game and there could be so many chapters to add or even some sort of "sandbox" option where you can use any characters or scenes to create your own story. Also I would say this game is child friendly, so if you want your children to get into puzzle games this could be it. -

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I'd like this game, but unfortunately it disappointed me on multiple levels.Let's get the good out of the way - the art style is very nice. The characters are cute and vivid. The poses they make in the stories are funny and cute. The idea is also pretty interesting. Build a story that adheres to the title. I don't think I've ever seen this concept done before, which could lead to some unique experience.Unfortunately the game is first too simple, then it becomes quickly too obscure to be enjoyable. At the start you get kind of tutorial levels, where the solutions are pretty obvious and short. They slowly teach you what all rooms you can use do, and you figure out the rules for the game. At least part of the game. Because it mostly focuses on fantasy/fairy tale theme. Fairy tale theme is pretty well designed with tons of rooms and characters, which provide many interesting interactions.The other themes you encounter over the game are very barren. There's a bit of bible, a bit of murder mystery and I think 2 or 3 horror themed levels. Out of 60. The non-fairy tale themes suffer by being too simple compared to what you learned previously with the fairy tale levels.Overal the game is also very easy. I got trough all 60 puzzles in less than 2 hours, which includes all alternative endings. The game has pretty useful marker next to each chapter, which shows if everything there was done. The main menu is very slow to navigate, but yes, the marking is useful. You need to watch page turning animation each time you want to change the chapter, and you cannot jump to selected chapter. If you left something unsolved in chapter 3 it will take you a long time to navigate there from chapter 13.Then after you solve everything you unlock some additional puzzles, that have special twist on existing stories. It's much harder, especially since it takes some time before you figure out what the new character can do. But it's still kind of fun. But then there are "stickers" which you can collect by doing something specific. Those stickers are a terrible idea. You cannot unlock any of the stickers until you finish the game - even if you do the things required. And while each sticker has a hint what needs to be done - you usually can do it only in a single level. Which of the 60 levels? Well, hope you remember which level had which characters and items, because the game won't tell you. So have fun looking for a level where you can actually do those sticker thing. It's too obscure, so I'm pretty sure 100% of players who get there will just use a FAQ. Leave the hints, add at least info on chapter where it can be done. You don't even need to provide exact level... As it is now the table of contents names of each level are very cryptic, and don't really make the player recall what the level was about, so the stickers are just a big pain.Next thing is a big issue - the translation to Polish, where I tried to play initially, is pretty bad. The titles sometimes are mistranslated, leading to completely different meaning, and/or impossibility to solve the level. One of the levels was translated to "Old sad dog dies happy". Wait, how can the dog be sad and happy at once?! I had to switch to English to learn it's "Old Heartbroken Dog Dies Happy", which actually made sense. The game also had narrator disabled by default in Polish, so I didn't hear the reading of the original title. I didn't even know there was a narrator until I switched to English.Finally, even the most developed fairy tale theme is VERY limited in the amount of characters and rooms, and their interactions. It gets repetitive very fast. At some point most puzzles had the same solutions, pretty much. Especially the gun related ones in murder mystery were just obvious, and it was not about finding a solution but just executing the same moves again.Overall the game had a potential, but even after squeezing everything out of it I didn't feel like the game clicked with me. I then though - who would it be good for? Puzzle game fans will be underwhelmed by difficulty, and people not into puzzle games will be irritated by the late-game. And then the game is pretty expensive for the shallow experience it provides.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short, relaxing puzzle game about crafting a chain of events using the provided sets and characters to fulfill the title of the "story", with some additional challenges thrown in after the first set of puzzles are completed. The game can sometimes require some trial-of-error, but it's mostly logical. Say, the goal is to have one character poison another, so set up a love triangle, give the third wheel poison, and have one of the lovers drink the poisoned wine, all of it made easier by only having three characters, a "love" setting, a "poison" setting, and a "wine" setting available for use. Not exactly difficult, but later challenges, where multiple conditions have to be chained together in the right order, can get a little tricky.Overall, it's a pretty fun game, with three caveats: it's short, the stamp-collection challenges don't tell you which puzzles you need to tweak to gain them, leading to more trial-and-error, and moving between the "chapters" is slow and clunky, and you'll have to do it a lot while looking for the right puzzle for the right stamp. Unfortunately, even with all of that obvious padding inserted into the game for the sake of increasing the play time, the game is still extremely short. Using some hints on which stamps corresponded to which puzzle, I 100%-ed the game in just three hours. Doing it without hints would probably take longer, but even so, I think it would clock out at 5 hours tops, and it has zero replayability.It's not exactly a great price/content ratio, but it's a unique experience, and I've spent 15 bucks on dumber things, so I can't really complain. All of that combined, I would give this game a lukewarm recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Take on the role of the storyteller in this innovative puzzle storybook game.Storyteller is developed by Daniel Benmergui for Annapurna Interactive.The game opens to a beautifully illustrated storybook, separated into chapters. Each chapter has a number of titles which the player must create the correct sequence of scenes to enact the title. Players create scenes from a limited assortment of images (scenes and people), as in a comic book like setting. Every element of the narrative is fluid, allowing you to change and rearrange scenes and characters at any time. The timeline is also dynamic, so changes made in earlier panels apply to panels after them.Puzzles increase in length and complexity as you progress through the storybook.Definitely recommended for fans of puzzle games.Pros:* Beautifully illustrated* Calming soundtrack* Innovative puzzle gameplay* AchievementsCons:* Price is a little high* No trading cards7/10 (due to being a little overpriced)

_childDocuments_.review: With a unique art style and a very tongue-in-cheek kind of dark humor, Storyteller from developer Daniel Benmergui and published by the always amazing Annapurrna, asks the question: what if there is more than one way to tell a story?A puzzler with a flair for the macabre, each story invites the player to figure out how the main theme unfolds. Placing characters into situations just to see what happens to them is oddly satisfying. And don’t let it fool you into thinking everything is easy. Some of the pages took repeated tries with entertaining results. The number of times I said “whoops, they’re dead again” was not little.The animation of each character is delightfully wacky, and their expressions are spot on. It’s easy to get lost in Storyteller for a few hours, and still want more.

_childDocuments_.review: I was drawn in by the extraordinarily creative demo and immediately bought the game as soon as it came out, only to be let down by the sheer lack of content. It really sucks because I feel like there is so much more you could do with this concept and they barely explored any of it.It's really cute, and fun for what it is. But for ten bucks, I recommend you get it when it's on sale, or if/when they add much more content and better puzzles in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the reasons why I like Indie Games is because they are innovating the industry - AAA games will push forward with hardware and tech but Indie will lead with creativity and originality; whether it hits or miss is another thing.in this case, originality hits successfully and it's refreshing to have something new to play.You get one line of text each page, which tells you the expected outcome and in some cases, a condition(s) getting to that point. And then you add in how you think the story played out.Keep in mind though that this is a puzzle game and not a sandbox story-maker (which would've been interesting to see how that would've panned out), and in most cases, there is one solution, but the game does feel great when you stumble on surprise twists to that criteria.Only 2 issues: price and length - the solution would be that one problem fixes the other, but I'm not sure if there will be more to this than what is there now, so perhaps buy it on sale, but it is still worth a buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Annapurna continues to impress me with the games they publish - always creative, fun and innovative.  Storyteller is a short game with a unique concept.  You have a text prompt of what the "story" should show and various figures or settings to create story panels out of.  The goal is to arrange these in a way that matches the given prompt.  There are also on some of the stages, alternate story prompts to "discover" by playing around with the characters and settings.The entire look and feel of the game is fun and playful, and while I didn't find much of this challenging (I did 100% the game in about 4 hours) I still had a great time and considered an evening well spent.  Also huge props to the people or person in charge of sound - the sound effects were minimal but effective and enjoyable.  The only complaint I have about this game is that not all of the stages have alternate stories to tell.  And they are not marked in any way to indicate that.  So without looking it up, you wouldn't know if playing around with the panels would get you an alternate story or not.  I'd much rather it said on the stage that I'd uncovered 1 of 3 stories or 1 of 1 stories so I didn't waste any time on ones that didn't have that.The long and short of this though is that this game is super fun and creative, and while I don't personally think 14.99 is a good price point for this game, if you can get it on a sale as I did, it sure made for a fun evening.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR the game is short but very fun so i personally didn't mind the price.i really enjoyed this game, i've been looking forward to the full release for a while and it was very fun. the art style is cute and overall the game is well-polished. there were a few puzzles which stumped me for a bit, which i consider a good thing! i didn't feel like it was repetitive, you had to achieve different results in each chapter and some are harder than you would initially think.i also liked how there are subtle differences between the characters, for example edgar and lenora are indifferent to the poison without a reason to use it, while isobel shows interest in it. i thought that was a nice way to make them each unique in some aspect.i know a lot of people are upset about the game being short for the price which is why i'm writing a review in the first place. i did feel a bit sad when i got everything completed in only 2 hours, but i think the game was worth the $15 dollars. i had a really fun time playing it, and it's well-made with a solid art style and no bugs. and most important for me, it made me smile and laugh like when i discovered the "frogs kissing" achievement, while still giving me a challenge (that final puzzle got me good). i also think this would be a wonderful game for kids.it might be unlikely but i do hope they release more content for this game because it is such a fun idea and there are so many more stories out there to take inspiration from.

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant idea, fantastic execution, super cute artstyle ...... BUT ...... unfortunately way too short. I only used outside help for finding the level with the last achievement I was missing. Anyway, the quality of this game is absolutely top tier, which makes it even more of a shame that it feels like the first chapter of a 10 chapter game. But like many others, I felt sort of cheated by the price and the game length.It's not even a game you can play again and get a different experience. You play it once and you've seen it all. _childDocuments_.review: I have to say I mostly agree with the other reviews of this game. Overall this game is still decent: the art style looks great and the mechanism of the game is very engaging. Still, I looked forward to this game for a long time, and this final product just... does not seem to be on par with the amount of time it took to develop and the price it is at.As others have already pointed out, the biggest problem is that the overall content is lacking. Even after spending a good amount of time playing around with different combinations of characters and backgrounds, it took me less than 3 hrs to complete. If you dedicate yourself to the plot it would take even less time. There is no eastern eggs, no secrets. Once you finish it, you finish it. It feels abrupt and truncated. Also, towards the end of the game, some of the individual stories just seem to lose the creative designs the earlier stories get. There was one story titled something like "waiting" where you basically just put the only two characters in all 6 panels, with the same background, and that's it. Like, what is the point of that lol. I really hope that the devs would consider updating this game later on. Either add more stories, or perhaps just give each story a few more panels (i.e for a story that is completed within 6 panels, give players like 3-4 more blank panels after completion of the game), so we can explore more combinations of stories.But for now, I wouldn't really recommend getting the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I can not recommend this game.First of all: Graphics, music and the style of this game are very charming and I like it a lot. The idea of an more "open" puzzle-game by solving stories and experiment with the different logical and narrative plot elements are very good and I really wanted to like this game.But the longer you play the game, the more you realize that it has a better idea than execution. First problem is, that you dont have the ability to experiment freely with the narrative elements. Instead of getting more and more narrative elements, characters, props and scenes, you are limited to 1-3 elements of each. Within that scope you can experiment with this elements and its quite fun sometimes to see what happens if you switch the different elements and characters. But especially the later puzzles are frustrating and it seems that your freedom of experimenting gets more LIMITED over time instead of getting more options to solve the puzzles. How cool this game would have been if the developer just said: "Here, you got a bunch of characters, all scenes and props you unlocked so far, now solve the puzzles within the logic of this story". I would LOVE this so much.But instead, you get limited. And some solutions of story puzzles are just there to make it extra hard for you to solve them(maybe so you dont be able to finish the game too fast?) Mostly you just have to think as mean and as cruel as possible to solve the story. So its not that wholesome it could be. Often you need to think "Oh...how bad, cruel and ruthless this character needs to act, so solve this puzzle?" One or two times this would be fun too, but at the later puzzles you have to do this too often and it gets boring very quickly.Another problem is, that the logic of the game is not correct or understandable at some point. In a later puzzle you have to match the exact gender(male instead of the female protagonist) to solve the puzzle, although there was no reason for it, because their roles where totally interchangable.Overall I am not happy with critizing this game. The idea is great, the animations and character designs is adorable and the way how to interact with the panels, characters and such feels so nice and makes a lot of fun. But in the end this game is too limited. Instead of being able to experiment with the story elements, it is just like any other puzzle game: You have to find the correct answer, just the way the developer want you to find. If you want to do it your way, it will fail. Even if the game suggests, its based on real world logic and you can solve the puzzle by using this logic. At the point the illusion of an free puzzle game fades away, the game is a lot less fun and feels very very limited. And it lacks a "free mode" too, where you could make your own story based on the panels. This would be so nice, especially for kids, to experiment with and make their own stories. Maybe even share it in social media and such.The game has so much potetial, but it doesnt use it in the end. So I can only recommend the game for people who want a short puzzle game experience, that is slightly different from other puzzle games. If you hope you find some great innovation in gameplay, you will get disappointed unfortunately. :/

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting, avidly, for this game for 15 years, since it was first announced on the author's blog and won the Nuovo Award for innovative game. I was a huge fan of the flash games  Daniel Benmergui made and Storyteller was the absolute pinnacle of everything he'd done before then. I bought Fidel specifically to support the author in the hope of Storyteller one day being released. I was absolutely overjoyed last year to finally play the Storyteller demo. And that demo was amazing. Absolutely everything I'd hoped for. I was so excited for the game to release. The trouble is, the demo felt better than the full release.  I am so disappointed with how short this game is.  I wandered afk, and also the game crashed, and I still managed to finish the game in well under 2 hours. A lot of the scenarios were ones I'd already played in the demo. I absolutely hate leaving a bad review, especially on release day, but I'm so saddened by this. The core gameplay mechanic is fantastic. The game concept is great. The demo was great.  But what's been released just doesn't feel complete. I'd so many hopes and I'm just sad.I really, really wanted to love this.  I had a lot more fun with the demo.There's less replayability here. It feels less like making an actual story and more like just solving a puzzle with a limited solution. There wasn't the same feeling of having this cool innovative toy to play with that there was with the demo, where you could go back and replay everything, and experiment with the story changing the outcome. It feels like it's lost the essence of everything I loved about the flash games, and the demo, and I'm so sad about that.  I'm really hoping that there'll be extra content released.
