_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR --> The Plucky Squire was less of a main character than I wished.----------------------Well, this was... more underwhelming that I expected. But maybe I expected a bit too much.The Plucky Squire (TPS) is exactly as you see on screens and trailers: you take control of the main character of a fictional kid's storybook who eventually gains the ability to leave the book's reality and also progress his adventures in the "real world", in a beautiful 3D. The game features 10 chapters with a Zelda-ish system of both combat and puzzle-solving, and during them you also will do some minigames that are basically throwbacks from classic games. While the premise is very good, and the artstyle is absolutely gorgeous, this is pretty much where it ends for me. By the time this review is made, the game is worrisomely buggy (and I will update my review if this ever changes). Not only game-breaking sequence happen (at some point my characters were DUPLICATED on a screen, causing all sorts of weird stuff happening), but also full game crashes. Moreover, for whatever reason, replaying a chapter from the Chapter Replay option doesn't allow you to save, and it is like this BY DESIGN since a prompt box appears telling you that before you jump into a chapter. I honestly don't know how this felt okay to anybody. Aside from technical issues, my absolute biggest problem with the game is that it treats you like a complete idiot. Despite focusing a lot on puzzle-solving areas, the game literally prevents you from solving anything on your own. Characters will give you all the hints BEFORE you can even start trying to figure out anything at all. It brings the "let's make sure noone gets stuck" to an extreme I haven't seen before. This goes along a very childish story that will not give you many surprising or unexpected events.The game's difficulty is laughable too. I don't know why there are two sets of difficulty when the "hardest" one is completely trivial all the way through. Every single enemy and wave can be easily dealt with by simply spamming the sword attack, and in case you lose health they will start dropping hearts very, very often. Finally, the game's variety also drops down after certain progress. At the beginning you will be presented with many different things you can do and you might get excited to see how this will go on. Well... it barely does. Some new mechanics are presented later on but they are more lacking or just less interesting. The final chapters catch up a little bit, though.Overall, I can see a target audience for this game being kids, but even kids might feel discouraged about how much everything absolutely given right away here. It is not a bad game by any means and I wish Steam, once again, would allow me to give a neutral review, but right not and at a 30-euro price tag I felt this game ended up below my expectations.

The game as a whole isn't all that difficult, but there are a couple of quirks that make it much rougher an experience than I'd have liked.The main adventure and puzzle aspects work great and feel creative, but I just ran into one too many freezes, glitches or slow texture loading during my playthrough that irked me some. _childDocuments_.review: I made one key mistake in the lead up to this game, and that was coming in with the assumption that this game was much deeper and mature of an experience than what is honestly marketed as. But that's entirely on me, because this game absolutely nails everything it sets out to achieve. It has impeccable art direction and it understands children's writing, being very pallet-able but never talking down. And it has very much the same approach to puzzles, ensuring all the pieces are clearly laid out, but never condescendingly directing.The game is however incredibly linear. If like me you had thoughts of having every page of every chapter eventually at your disposal or an overworld map to freely explore akin to its obvious zelda inspiration, you would be mistaken. Every chapter has its set pieces and designated pages to explore. And it uses those pages well, often in very interesting ways. Similarly the world outside of the book is very linear, and you will only ever have access to obstacles pertinent to the current chapter. Its yet again something that caught me off guard for reasons that would be very hard to explain without both spoiling the game and giving my interpretation of the themesThe puzzles, minigames, and combat, while all greatly competent, also are not hard. All of this leads to the obvious conclusion that the game with the very kid friendly aesthetic is very much made for kids. A design philosophy that I'm always 50/50 on. A good family game does not have to be one with a low skill ceiling. However I'm also not one to glorify the regrettable and intentionally frustrating design decisions of games of the past, and understand that not every game is going for a Link to the Past type learning curve that taught a lot of us how to play video games in the past, especially if the game is trending to be accessible for children under 7. In that case this game is absolutely fantastic. If you are a parent or a cool Uncle/Aunt with the fancy Steam Deck or Gaming PC, this is a must buy even at this price. But, while I still think this is a great game for all ages, even adults, its length and relative difficulty leaves me to say you might not get 30 dollars worth of personal value from it, and therefore might want to wait for a sale. Unless of course you just pop of for chill, wholesome, cute things, then its 8 hours of pure bliss.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: The Plucky Squire has a charming art style and a novel concept but is too concerned with making sure the player is never stuck to give them a chance to do much of anything on their own.The art direction for this game is really strong and was a large part of what kept me playing to the end. I really appreciate the effort that went into making the characters look good both hand drawn and as 3D models, the mix of art styles to represent different genres and media, the lighting that really emphasizes the time of day on the desk, and the way the music fades in and out between the desk music and storybook music as you move to or from the book. I also really liked the narrator and having text pop up on the page further cements that you are playing out a story in a book. The mini-games also help add some variety and was the other part of the game I continued to look forward to as I played. Mechanically, the game has everything it needs to be a competent top-down Zelda style game, including tools that play into the idea of being able to pop in and out of the book, but it stumbled on the execution.There is nothing wrong with having a generous hint system, especially in a game that is clearly aimed at a younger audience, but it is a problem when one is not allowed the option to figure things out on their own. Far more often than not, when you gain a new tool or encounter something you haven't seen before, the game will take control from you, explain what you're looking at and how to deal with it, pan the camera to exactly where you need to go, and for good measure mention that there is an npc you can talk to if you get stumped. The combat is also problematic because mashing the basic attack button is almost always the best answer even in "adventure mode."
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: It's not like this is a bad game. But it's incredibly underwhelming in terms of what i had expected. From the trailers we had been shown i had though this was gonna be a zelda like adventure game the likes of link to the past/link between worlds, where the outside world was gonna be the major focus and you manipulate your own book/world by doing stuff and maybe other books and stuff were gonna be the dungeons. However that is not the case at all. Instead this is an incredibly linear and handholdy puzzle game with a relatively short amount of actual game to play. I was shocked when i was in chapter 5 out of 10 after less then 2 hours of gameplay. And while my total amount of hours ended up being a little bit over 7 hours, that was with me searching for hidden stuff, which i gave up torwards the end of the game when i realized there is no way to visit locations from previous chapters. It didnt help that it felt like i was on autopilot for half the game cause characters keep interupting you almost constantly to comment on whatever just happened. You picked up an item? "Goody let me explain" okay, fair enough. You picked up a collectable? "Goody let me explain" okay, i guess. You solved a puzzle? "Wow great going" okay thanks but please just let me play. You picked up another collectable? "Goody let me explain" Come on, i know what it is a short pick up message is enough don't halt the game again and again for this. You solved another puzzle? "Wow great going" PLEASE JUST SHUT UP AND LET ME PLAY! You screen transitioned? "Oh wow a new environment! And that looks like a puzzle up ahead" *cutscene plays showing a puzzle you haven't even gotten the chance to walk up and inspect on your own* "Gee i wonder how this will work" Can i just have break... can i just have one break? Again this feels incredibly handholdy and almost like their artificially stretching gameplay time.The Puzzle Solving itself isn't even bad, there were a few that i thought were really smart and used neat ideas. But a lot of it feels like you don't even need to use your brain, its just "you know how to do thing, so go do thing" which again constantly gets interrupted by characters commenting either before or after the puzzle or both. Imagine slightly less annoying fi from skyward sword. It also doesnt help that at the date of this review i've experience multiple bugs, like things not loading correctly after dying, environmental items suddenly not being interactable anymore, picking up box and it getting stuck in my character.TL;DR: Overall i'd say it's not worth its current asking prices of 30 bucks, its too short, too linear and doesn't deliver much in return. This is not to say it was an awful game, but more on the mediocre side. Definetly would say if you wanna grab it wait til it's atleast half off. That's the highest i'd pay for it if i could go back.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral option...So basically it is a game with unique visuals and interesting mechanics, but that's it.I hoped for an Adventure Time-, Gravity Falls-, Gumball-, Flapjack-like experience where tone and humor are a bit more mature and don't match the artstyle, but here you can expect what the visuals show. Too childish for my taste to be honest.The mechanics would be great and it would be good to find out for yourself how to solve the puzzles with the toolset you have, but the game just simply feeds you the solution every single time (except for maybe 1-2 occasions).The graphic is really nice both for the 2D and the 3D parts, I haven't seen more beautiful pages of a book in a game before and the music is enjoyable too, matches the tone of the chapters really well.The story is like 8-9 hours long which is not much considering that it is very easy. The enemy variaty is okay for this lenght.I wouldn't feel good if I gave a negative review for the game as it really is well made, just not my cup of tea and also I find the 30€ price tag a bit high, for this lenght and experience I would find 20€ more appropriate.

_childDocuments_.review: This game would be perfect for my 6-year-old kid (which I don't have). I have had it on my wishlist since forever and was hoping for a fun, diverse gameplay. Just when I started to feel a little impatient about the currency farming with the bushes and trees, I started to become excited again when I found out I could get out of the book.However, the story does not mostly carry on outside the book. It becomes repetitive even after 3 hours of gameplay. If I wanted, I could have just walked around and hit trees for hours just to buy skill upgrades.Now, I understand being able to change the pages of the book to travel from one page to another, though it does start to become long and tedious since I need to be at a certain spot to change the page. It's a lot of walking considering how frequently I do it. The game includes parts where you need to move the words from one page to another, which can only remind me of Baba is You. Having played that game, this just feels like an annoying task considering how often we need to do it.Although the art style is a winning point, I doubt the gameplay will ever be. Some may have purchased this game with hopes of reminiscing their experience with It Takes Two. Instead, The Plucky Squire is far too limited and redundant to attain a similar or better level of success. It might be hyped for the moment, but not for a long time. Maybe, what is missing is an 'adventurous fun' kind of touch. It does not feel the same as launching It Takes Two, Little Nightmares, Grounded, Another Crab's Treasure, Hypercharge: Unboxed, Fall Guys, Dave the Diver, etc. I found these games I named to be pretty fun (some of which following a similar 'cute', 'childish' or 'human world' style. The mechanics are pretty basic; you can dash, jump, hit, throw your sword, etc. Bosses don't require a mastery of mechanics though. I've played games that were frustratingly difficult for me, but this one was frustratingly easy. That said, I would rather use similar mechanics and launch Fall Guys to troll 12-year-old kids.I'm going to finish the game nonetheless because I'm a sucker for achievements: P---UPDATE: I am not going to finish this useless game. I have never felt so much inner rage for a game that is so full of narration EVERY second. I kid you not. I was already getting super pissed that I couldn't just go straight to the boss and finish the game. Who wrote the dialogues for this game? Trust me, none of that was necessary.I admire the artistic effort that went into this game but GOSH, just because I selected Story mode doesn't mean I bought this game for a stupid bedtime story. 50 % of my hours are from the dumb narrations, 10 % are from the bugs that forced me to reload the chapter or from the last checkpoint (7 min ago), 30 % of the game is walking back and forth like an idiot and I can't even tell if the last 10% is worth calling gaming. Enemies offer zero variety. It's always the same damn thing. You can always effortlessly kill enemies. HOWEVER, the final boss is INCREDIBLY difficult for the sole reason that it gives you a rhythmic challenge where you have to click buttons at the right time. It lasts so long before you actually do end up landing a hit! I just wanted to rip my head apart. This is such a lack of consistency, especially when it comes to the distribution of levels of difficulty.A little heads up if you are buying this game: farming currency has proven to be especially useless later because you end up with too much money and you only have scrolls to buy in the shop starting mid-game. That just means they ran out of ideas.Music can honestly be better. The game looks so "lively" but the music can just make the whole experience boring or, at best, mediocre. Even at some point, it started to feel depressing. That's one of the reasons why I feel like the atmosphere of the game is truly a weak point. Somehow, we always get shot into random environments with random quests with no real correlation to the storyline or to the objective whatsoever. I don't know what the goal is? Why are we just constantly doing quests to unlock random doors and all? Did we need all those weapon upgrades? Not at all. A waste of time.I cannot even fathom doing this game twice (story mode and adventure mode) to get both achievements. I guess my patience ran thin mid-game. DO NOT get this game!---Maybe there is a better world in some unidentified dimension where this game can be significantly improved with:- varied enemy attacks and fighting style- automatic saves every time there is a dialogue or just a save button!- FIXED BUGS FIXED BUGS FIXED BUGS FIXED BUGS- removal of unnecessary narrations/dialogues (I cannot stand one more second of the worm in the post-its talking and saying the obvious)- removal of all skills from the shop and make them into something you earn from boss kills- ability to upgrade skill level with the accumulation of XP from killed enemies- removal of health drops from enemy kills- repurposing of the shop such as to sell potions for health or boost attacks- reduced amount of time it takes to turn a page -a better mechanic for getting in and out of the book- better music in the first biome and in the area where the MC saved Violet- a better use of the cycle between day- and nightime (in real time, it does not take that long to read a book and it felt pointless. Moreover, nightime had too many shadows, I could hardly see in some corners)- better puzzles because they are simply linear and it is impossible to get something 'wrong', hence making them tentative- replacement of the sorry-of-an-excuse skills that Crash and Violet have. They were super underwhelming, especial Violet's. She said she was going to perform magic, and I expected magic. Whatever happened in the game was not it- include a skip button for dialogues and cutscenes- merge dialogues and cutscenes to reduce the intervals of said things- more involvement from the MC's friends because they are useless and just follow me around when they could have just done something to help (can't we incarnate them during the 'exploration' as well? not just during boss fights?)
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with excellent graphics and art. The minigames were enjoyable diversions but didn't get in the way (and are skippable). Shame the main character has to be just another blank slate though. Would love Jot to have a personality. The writing is mostly good and the narrator is good enough. The sword upgrades are almost entirely useless and worse than just mashing the attack button in almost every situation but not a big deal. I really wanted to see more with the re-writing mechanic but what was there was fun. I would love to see a sequel some day.

_childDocuments_.review: Positives: Beautiful art direction, especially with the 2D elements. I love the unique style of the art too.Negatives: The writing is bad. Kind of reminds me of the Star War prequels type of bad writing, for example, you are introduced to your friends but not in any sort of fun or interesting way. You're just told that they are your friends and that's the end of the story. They also reuse words constantly, I hope you like the word "plucky" because you're going to hear it like 10,000 times throughout the story as if they don't know any other words or adjectives to describe anything.The gameplay is just awful and far too easy. People will tell you this game is meant for little kids and that's why it handholds so much but I've been a little kid and this would drive me absolutely insane if I was playing this as a child. No kid wants to be paused every five minutes to be told how to play basically. When they're not holding your hand, basically all you have to do is swing your sword like once and everything is dead. Even little mini-games that you hope will be fun will last like ~10 seconds and it's basically impossible for you to lose.I know I got the product for free, but if I didn't - I find it overly expensive. $30 for 8 hours of subpar gameplay is a total ripoff. It's a buggy mess too, includes gamebreaking bugs that will stop you in your tracks. I kind of expect this problem with Devolver products honestly but still - it's a problem.The game feels like some artists got together to show off their skills/display their art and they forgot to actually make a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a charming platformer with a cute story and characters. What really got me was the music and the atmosphere. A wonderfully unique world bouncing between 2D and 3D. The achievements were fun to get! The one thing I have to say that may deter people is that it does have its bugs. _childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game so badly. It's got so much style & a unique concept. But ultimately it's very shallow. It has a very strong emphasis on story which in itself isn't a problem, but it's the main focus with little game play in between. It introduces concepts & mechanics that are hardly used & never gives you an chance to breath constantly cramming story & exposition down your throat. Also you get a couple of sword abilities that you'll rarely ever use because your basic sword attack for some reason is so much more powerful that it's not even worth wasting your time on spin attack, jump attack, or sword throw. A handful of decent puzzles, but overall underwhelming if you're over the age of 13. Clearly a children's game. The game also has a tendency to freeze on Steam Deck. I had deleted that comment from this review after changing to lower graphical settings, but still experienced freezing.Edit: It's unfortunate that Steam only has a recommend or don't recommend option. I would very much recommend this game for young kids. My 6 year old daughter is loving it. However given the Steam platform demographic is typically older people, for this platform I will keep my review as don't recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: I only made it halfway through the game, so take this review with a grain of salt. While I do think the game has a cute art style and charm to its world, the gameplay feels very monotonous and boring. I was really excited for this game, but at $30, I feel like I was let down a bit. I would suggest getting it on sale !!
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is riddled with bugs, to the point where getting softlocked happens far too often. In the first four chapters alone, I encountered so many issues that I genuinely question whether the game was properly playtested at all.On top of that, the handholding is excessive. Nearly every room has dialogue interruptions explaining the simplest, most uninspired puzzles, leaving no room for the player to figure things out on their own. It's frustratingly dull and undermines any sense of challenge or discovery.It’s especially disappointing because this was one of my most anticipated games of the year. Sadly, it turned out to be a really huge letdown and one of the most boring games I have probably ever played. The only redeeming quality of this game is its art style, which is admittedly really cute and well done. However, the gameplay is deeply flawed, making it hard to enjoy the experience.I can’t even recommend this game for children, as the excessive handholding and constant interruptions, not to mention the bugs, make it more frustrating than fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: Painfully dull.Plucky Squire is visually impressive and has a strong core premise but is held back by boring gameplay, an anaemic story and very little substance.It would be easy to pin it as a 'good game for children' but its insistence on holding the player's hand by pointing out solutions and constantly interrupting the flow of play by spelling out the next objective suggests it espouses the creativity and wonder of children but doesn't trust them to apply it here. On numerous occasions control is taken away to pan over the area, have an NPC point out what to do 'oh? those two keyholes look like we need two key. i think theres a key to the east and one to the west!' and then, to really drive the boot in it has a hit system for some reason. All of this is even more confusing as the puzzles are straightforward with very few moving parts, so why so much explanation? The combat is much the same with each enemy taking only a few hits and offering no strategy so to speak in defeating them. Even when you misstep and lose life the game hides hearts EVERYWHERE meaning there is no stakes. Goes without saying that there is a death system but it immediately starts you on the same page, so why even hard it.But maybe you can move past that and want to indulge in the storybook world and 3D spaces. Well, they are fine...You spend very little time in each area with not much depth to each. It really emphasises how well games like Katamari, Pikmin and Tinykin did to create a miniaturized toy room and how much this does not.Ultimately, The Plucky Squire is incredibly underwhelming. It assumes very little of children and the player and a more cynical person might look into the constant emphasis on how GOOD the Squire is as a franchise within the text as fairly self-congratulatory for what is a forgettable title.

_childDocuments_.review: I think “style over substance” is a phrase that is frequently overused by game reviewers and video essay youtubers alike. However, it does work well in summarizing how I feel about The Plucky Squire. It’s got all the correct ingredients, but none of the seasoning and intrigue that would make it a truly excellent experience.Puzzles and GimmicksThe dynamic between switching between and interacting with the 2D and 3D worlds is a genuinely interesting gameplay twist and it’s a real shame none of the puzzles that involve you switching between the two worlds ever go beyond the surface-level. Upgrades like the stop and bomb stamps and being able to flip pages to move stuff in the environment are super technically impressive and definitely wowed me. However, I couldn’t help but see the missed potential as when I continued to progress through the game I realized the gimmicks never went beyond that initial spectacle. You can see visages of a good game bellowing under the surface, but the game is just so sanitized and so afraid of letting the player fail or get stumped that it just ends up feeling empty.Controls and BossesThe entire game is generally way too hand-holding. Even during enemy encounters, the game just showers you with so many health pick-ups that you’re probably never going to see a single death screen during your playthrough. And this isn’t a compensation for any flaws in the general game-feel. No, the game controls absolutely fine. Switching between 2D and 3D feels natural. I had no issues during my entire playthrough as your basic combat controls feel great; it is almost too great as no enemy is really going to give you any trouble. On that note, a lot of boss encounters have a unique gameplay-style where the game has you switch game-genres. Sometimes you’re playing a Punch-Out! Style boss fight and other times you’re playing a Puyo Puyo knock-off. These boss encounters are great and were a highlight during my playthrough. The only gameplay-style I didn’t care for was the stealth segments. They felt stiff and unforgiving that feels antithetical to the rest of the experience. They feel unnecessarily and are such a minor portion of the game that it feels like a waste to have them at all.Story and PresentationThe game’s story is also nothing to write home about. You have a set of two additional party members that stick with you during most of your journey. However, since the Squire is the only character that can jump between the 2D and 3D worlds, they don’t get to do much. Most of their screentime is dedicated to their characters' arcs of needing to “believe in themselves” and “need to prove themselves.” It is a super basic characterization that felt kinda hollow and didn’t move really get me invested in the game's characters at all. It doesn’t help that many of the cutscenes involve the physical book having to flip the page every single time there was a scene transition. It’s novel and quirky at first but it does eventually get old and slogs the pace down. It’s a shame too cause presentation-wise, the cutscenes are the biggest showcase of the unique art-style that defines the game. Each cutscene does a great job in selling the premise of a children’s book come to life. To add to that, the presentation is basically flawless. I love how the 2D segments look and plopping between the 2D and 3D sections is basically seamless. The 3D sections are also really well done. The desk is a fun area to explore and I kind of wish the game took place in more 3D locations so that the game could fully showcase the fun setting. It’s just a shame that the game's flaws do end up hampering my final enjoyment of the story and presentation.Most of my issues with Plucky Squire might stem from the fact this game is clearly targeting a target audience that is way younger than I am. It’s probably a great game for your kids. But even most children’s media has something for adults to latch onto. This game has so much potential with its excellent premise, gimmicks, and presentation. It just needed to plunge deeper into its puzzle design and a slightly more difficult experience for me to get the most out of it. I hope that the developers take this feedback this game is getting and put it into a sequel that expands upon this game’s strengths which may give us a truly great game experience when the potential is fully realized.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: On the one hand, the game is a bit of a victim of the hype it has generated since its first public presentation, but it's impossible to forgive its catastrophic pace.In the 2D phases, the game constantly takes the player's hand away in favor of incessant dialogue phases on every screen. It's a pity, because there are some good ideas and varied gameplay phases that are fun in theory, but neither very deep nor very fun to play in practice.A Nintendo feel on the surface, but very dull in the end.What's left is a superb art direction, but it's no match for the systematic dialogues that break the pace and the bland gameplay phases.Not bad, just bland.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely charming!Everything in this adventure feels so well thought out, from the intuitive puzzle design, to the unique boss encounters, to the seamless transitions between 2D and 3D gameplay. The story are characters are wonderful, and the art style and storybook-like presentation carry everything so well. The length of the game feels very satisfying, with no extra padding trying to artificially extend it.As an adult, I totally love this game, and had I played it as a kid, I know I would've been absolutely obsessed.Ran into a couple minor glitches, but the autosaves are frequent, so never lost more than a minute of progress.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: A celebration of art in all of it's forms, The Plucky Squire is as much a homage to picture books and video games as it is to painting, writting, sculpting, it's ultimately a story about creativity.It is, however, a very, very casual adventure, filled with minigames and perspective changes at every turn to keep things interesting,  many of them homages to other games in the medium, all brought a smile to my face, but this means as a pond it is both incredibly wide and incredibly shallow, anyone expecting any depth in it will be disappointed, but I have to say I do not share the opinions of most reviews saying the puzzle were too easy and handholdy, I was stuck for a while in quite a few of them, not an hour or so, but definitely a reasonable amount to get the noggin joggin.If there is one thing I disliked though, it was the combat, namely how Jot has all kinds of different abilities he can purchase at the shop, but all of them deal less damage than just mashing the attack button, with enemies dropping health every second kill, mashing you way through combat is much more effective than actually trying to engage with the secondary skills. Combat can be easy and still engaging, see the decades of 3D Zeldas out there, but there is a structure to it, and this ain't it.The Plucky Squire won't set the world on fire with new ideas, but as a celebration of everything that came before and hope of what has yet to come, it is a good reminder of how fun videogames, and art in general, can be.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I want to love the game it is just a very slim experience. Beautiful art style but that's all the game is. _childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to the plucky squire for a very long time and I would say that my expectations were definitely met. _childDocuments_.review: The core of this game, clear to anyone who's seen a trailer, is of course a playable picturebook, with the amount of narrative and dialog you'd expect from that kind of medium. When it becomes interactive, the environments are contained within two pages, which lead to the next pages, so don't expect branching paths or an open world.The twist is that you can leave the book and explore the outside, 3 dimensional, world. The desk on which the book is lying is only slightly more open but mostly a space to obtain tools to manipulate the book from the outside, allowing for some innovative gameplay. Puzzles aren't terribly deep but feel fresh thanks to the varied gameplay both in and out of the book. As opposed to what you might have read elsewhere (Kotaku, cough), the dialog doesn't spoil any puzzles. But there are optional hints from a character named Minibeard.You don't travel alone and each character has their own unique gameplay. And depending on the occasion, the main character may adopt different playstyles as well. On the surface, it's a classic Zelda like but there are also rhythm, stealth, arcade puzzle, boxing and shooting elements to it so it's a mix of genres and a love letter to gaming calling back to its roots, and drawing innovation from the meta gameplay that contains all those varied elements.The execution of what the devs set out to do, with its whimsical art and writing, tight controls and polished gameplay, would be flawless if it weren't for some technical issues. Framerate is not as stable as one would hope and especially towards the end the rate at which you might encounter progress breaking bugs increases (hopefully this will be ironed out with patches). But the auto saves are pretty frequent so you can just quit and start again, without losing much progress. In the rare cases where you have to do stuff again, it will be much faster once you already know what to do.Being a UE4 game, this works with praydog's UEVR mod. I recommend to not set the decoupled pitch option (which usually is the first thing you want to do) so you don't have to look down at the book which is an awful strain to the neck. Both the frame rate (I reduced the quality setting from the default epic to low and render resolution to 80%) and some of the camera perspectives will test your VR legs so I don't recommend this as your first VR game. But if you can play it, the game's little big world really shines in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game thoroughly but the fact that it didn't let you do your own thinking and instead took your hand guiding you to everything was a bit underwhelming. Also I missed some scrolls and for some I have to replay the whole game with a new save, not good. It would be a good addition to indicate on which chapters you're missing a glitchbird because I really don't know where are the missing ones I've got left.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: I was hyped as ♥♥♥♥ for this game in the lead up (so much that I decided to drop the $30 on it day 1), but sadly that hype was too much and now I'm a little disappointed. Idk, it's charming and not bad, but it feels like a lot of other Indie games where it seems dope as hell but it's kind of just *shrugs*. Plucky Squire is mainly a Zelda-like (I guess?) that has 2D gameplay, and some 3D gameplay. It's all very serviceable and the main neat stuff this game does is the puzzles that revolve around "meta" stuff of books. You can swap *certain* words around to change a gate from "closed" to "open" (etc.). Or there are puzzles revolved around turning the pages or gravity affecting stuff in the book from tilting the pages. There are also quite a lot of gameplay changes from an early Punch-Out boss, to Super Bust-a-Move, to side scroll jetpack shooting, and a rhythm game too. These are fine and work, just feels like it spreads itself with all this.FINAL BOSS SPOILERS:The final boss reuses 3 of those minigames I mentioned and ♥♥♥♥ man I don't want to play Bust-a-Move or Punch Out! You didn't give me enough time to learn how to play Punch Out or Bust-a-Move! Don't make it the final boss! Thank god you can skip minigames and those count because I hated that ♥♥♥♥.FINAL BOSS SPOILERS OVER/Overall, this game is charming, has a beautiful 2D artstyle, and serviceable gameplay, but it is not really what I am left slightly disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: The Plucky Squire is such a breathe of fresh air, and with such an imaginative adventure that easily blends 2D and 3D gameplay. This game is a true standout to why you should invest more time in playing indie titles, because these developers have created an amazing game with such passion.The game's unique art style is very well done, both in 2D and 3D presence. The narrator does a nice job explaining the story of the hero of and his challenging journey with friends to take on many foes ahead.The gameplay is a perfect balance of challenging and rewarding. The puzzles don't overstay their welcome and offer a nice break between chapters. The pacing of the game overall is smooth as well, transitioning seamlessly through chapters of a book.The game runs very well, I haven't experienced any issues on my end, and the soundtrack compliments the vibrant world in a lovely way. Overall, this game is a clear love letter from the developers who have been working on this project for a long time. Be sure to support them as The Plucky Squire is an absolute gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: This is the perfect casual gaming experience that anyone will like. The story does not overstay it's welcome as the game is only 10 chapters. You do have two story options with 'adventure' and 'story' mode. Story mode is a very casual experience, adventure is a tad harder. Graphics are incredible and the transition between 2D and 3D is flawless and integrated in the game perfectly with the puzzles and collectibles. Puzzles are pretty simple, maybe a couple head scratches for a few minutes here and there. Collectibles are simple with artwork (50 to collect) and 'glitchbirds' (10 to collect). Some can be pretty hard to find, but it's fun. You do have a chapter replay once a chapter is beaten if you miss anything.Combat is super super simple. You have a few upgrades to have new combat moves and more damage, but it isn't anything too crazy. The bosses are where the game shines more and when the game evolves more into just your standard 'attack with a sword' game it's really fun.One of my favorite games of the year and can see myself playing it every once and awhile after initial completion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I'm playing this on Steam Deck LCD. It runs smoothly. Love the artistic style and narrative story presentation of this game. My kids and wife enjoyed it also.I just wish it was a bit longer as I didn't want for it to end already. Also the boss mini games were you need to hit the things that the boss is throwing at you is a little bit lame, wish they added more mechanics into it, it gets old after a few fails.At first I was bit hesitant on buying it full price, was thinking of waiting for a sale. After watching a bunch of reviews online, decided to buy it already. It was worth every penny.  Overall, I highly recommend The Plucky Squire.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: This could have been a great game.  It is a very cool concept marred by poor design and bugs beyond belief.  It’s hard grasping the fact that a game this buggy passed Beta testing and quality control before its release.  The gameplay is overly simplistic and lacks any sort of challenge.  You are given two difficulty options - Adventure and Story modes.  Adventure mode is supposed to offer a challenge, but there is pretty much no challenge.  The auto hint system that is built into the game can’t be turned off, so you are pretty much guided by the hand throughout the game.  Instead of introducing new abilities or weapons and letting you figure out how to use them, the game tells you exactly what you need to use a weapon or ability on in order to progress.Next, the glitches and bugs are so bad that they, several times throughout the game, cause the game to freeze completely or slow down so much that you have to reboot your game system and restart from your last save.  This is utterly maddening.While not a $60 AAA title, this game is not worth its $30 price tag.  At best, it’s a bargain $10 game designed for five year olds.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this, I really did, but found out rather quickly after you are able to leave and re-enter the book that I'm just not having fun. Might be for some folks, but it's just not for me.The art direction is phenomenal, the game sounds amazing, the concept is unique and very inspired... but it's just not fun. Feels very slow and the start takes quite awhile to get through, combat is bland and doesn't offer much, and overall while the whole mechanic of being able to leave the book and manipulate the pages is really a great idea, the game fails to capitalize on this concept in a meaningful way beyond leave book -> move to different part of book -> enter book again. On top of this the game feels the need to stop you in your tracks to toss dialogue at you almost constantly grinding the flow to a total standstill.Wish it brought more to the table but what is here just isn't fun enough for me to want to keep going.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: Aesthetic and concept are cool. But, that concept isn't explored at all beyond the story book and kid's desk. All other usages boil down to minigames that are uninspired at best, and mostly tedious. The combat has nothing to it. The only useful upgrade is the sword throw, which trivializes most fights. The puzzles could be interesting, if the game didn't have extreme railroading and spoil area solutions upon entry. Hell, I started looking away from the screen during dialog in hopes of getting some small sense of discovery. There are some mechanics with the book that could be interesting, but they're never really explored or combined beyond their initial introduction. Confusingly, the final boss uses none of these mechanics and is just a boring collection of reused mini-games. The game is extremely linear with very little exploration. Even within that linearity, the flow of the game is constant interrupted due to unimportant/uninteresting dialogue.I also have to mention that I experienced a few bugs. Nothing that really ruined the experience, but there were 3-4 times where I had to reload the game and lose progress due to being soft-locked. I finished it because the art team clearly put a lot of love into this game and I hoped it would get better. But, I'm walking away with a bad taste in my mouth and I regret spending $30 on it. That being said, I expected a cozy Zelda-like with unique art style. I now realize that this game may be intended solely for kids. If that's true, then I'm not the target audience. But I still can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: The Plucky Squire is a charming, fun indie game that brings a fresh twist to platformers with its seamless blend of 2D and 3D gameplay! It's like a playful mix of classic Mario mechanics with some extra flair, and the transitions between perspectives keep things exciting. The visuals are adorable, and the level design is creative, making it easy to get lost in its cute, vibrant world.That said, while the story is sweet, it doesn’t dig too deep—it’s more about the adventure and gameplay here. If you're a fan of indie gems that offer unique twists on familiar mechanics, this one’s a must-play. We need more games like The Plucky Squire.

The game is a lot of fun but I can not recommend it when a game breaking bug still exists

_childDocuments_.review: In spite of the stellar art direction I cannot recommend the games:- it takes controls away from the player all the time - it is very restrictive, even disabling tools for no reason half of the time- it has a lot of softlock glitches. I wanted to finish the game but after 4 softlocks that forced me to reload a chapter I don't care anymore.This is my first negative evaluation on steam. But the glowing reviews don't match my experience sadly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely stunning, a real technical achievement in blending 2D and 3D so seamlessly. The trailer captivated me, and I was genuinely excited to dive in.The gameplay itself is decent—nothing groundbreaking, but that's not necessarily a flaw. There's a good variety of modes that kept things interesting and fun when I was actually allowed to play.  Unfortunately, the game seems determined to pull control away every 1-2 minutes, forcing you to sit through cutscenes or dialogue that feel endless. I don’t mind a good cutscene, but when they’re this frequent, and the characters or story lack depth, it becomes tedious. I play games for the interactivity, not to sit through endless exposition.The game doesn’t trust the player to figure things out, constantly hand-holding through every new mechanic. This kills the joy of discovery, leaving little room for the player to explore or uncover secrets on their own. A bit more freedom and faith in the player’s ability would’ve made this a far more enjoyable experience.It’s disappointing to say, but I can’t recommend this beautiful game despite its immense potential.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: This game felt like it was made for eight years old children. I don't know if it was intentional or accidental.The non stop narrator comments with drawing mini cutscenes butcher the entire dynamic and flow and you just start to yawn.The first boss fight felt very boring and repetitive, you do the same actions for too long, no cliffhangers or unexpected mechanic changes.Audio design felt weak, the music is too cute and childish while sound effects constantly missed opportunities to make funny gags.It felt like those generic TV cartoons which little children watch all day.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: The Plucky Squire is a charming action-adventure game with a lot of potential, though it falls short in a few areas. The 2D sections are beautifully designed with clean, vibrant graphics, making them an absolute delight. However, the 3D segments feel somewhat generic, resembling a typical platformer. The game is highly linear, with only one solution to each puzzle, and often feels too hand-holdy as NPCs and camera cues frequently provide hints unprompted.While the puzzles, such as those involving words to alter the story, are creative, they are quite simple and designed for a younger audience. The game features various minigames and cool ideas that don’t overstay their welcome, but the low difficulty level means that combat can often be solved by simply swinging your weapon, making the upgrades feel largely unnecessary. Upgrades feel underwhelming, mostly offering two special attacks and basic damage boosts, which don't add much variety.In terms of accessibility, The Plucky Squire shines with options like jump assists and invincibility, and even lets you skip some minigames if they are too hard. The story largely feels predictable and underwhelming... up untill the like last third of the game. Then finally it gets more interesting and even gameplay gets somewheat challenging. However, The Plucky Squire has no dialogue or scene skip, making replaying for collectibles a chore.Ultimately, The Plucky Squire is filled with style but lacks the substance to fully deliver on its ambitious ideas. It’s a fun, family-friendly experience, but might leave some older players wanting more complexity. Worth playing, but perhaps at a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: Visually the game is stunning, no complaints there, but the game play is very lacking. Puzzles are incredibly easy and combat might as well be non-existent, you can spam attack and are almost always guaranteed a health drop. I was hoping for there to be more minigames to pad out the game play, but they are few and far between.Overall, i liked what i saw on screen, it just bored me by the second hour. I'd definitely recommend this game to those with small kids.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: Frustratingly mediocre and less than the sum of its parts. I had been hoping for something halfway between Supraland and Evoland; playing with the physicality of the storybook and the desk with a few cute motifs of other games and genres for variety. The Plucky Squire hits those notes occasionally, but most of the time it's extremely trite puzzles that are both fiddly and simple, and with a variety of NPCs that shout out the answer before you get the opportunity to even look at the puzzle. The presentation and structure speaks to a lack of confidence in the game, as barely a moment goes by without a reference to another piece of media to distract from the token combat and platforming. The game is also incredibly short, only a few hours long but still feeling padded with repeated puzzles and slowly dragging carried objects from area to area.This game had a lot of potential but every mechanical gimmick and every story beat was already done better in Chicory, and the base gameplay was perfected 30 years ago in A Link to the Past. There's nothing here that you haven't seen before, and the gestalt feels cheap rather than celebratory.Edit: I somehow forgot to mention the incessant softlocks and glitches. Catching on geometry, puzzles not uniformly acknowledging completion, unclear objectives, and seams between map tiles causing ugly pixel gaps.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: Was pretty hyped for this game overall but with the amount of softlocks I experienced and had to troubleshoot I’d say wait until it’s updated and fixed or on sale. Overall ok story, pretty creative and I love the art style but the amount of softlocks and bugs I had to deal with completely killed any momentum it had going for it while playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute and charming game clearly made with a lot of heart and passion. I absolutely loved the mixed media look, how styles wouldn't match but the game would blend them, it was so fun! It's definitely a game intended to be easy for kids to play, there's next to no challenge here and minigames are skippable if you want to. If you're looking for a visual treat and about 10 hours of enjoyable story, or if you have young children who want something cute to play, definitely pick it up (maybe on sale)
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: The Plucky Squire is one of the best indie games of 2024.I followed the game's development since its reveal and having played through the game, it is exactly what I expected - a wonderful and joyful adventure that took me back to a much simpler time.The art style was something that I was immediately drawn to. I was concerned that the game would be all style but no substance but that turned out to be not the case at all. The gameplay variety is something that can easily last for another playthrough - there is plenty of combat, puzzles, minigames and collectibles to keep you busy. The presentation, again, is fantastic to look at and a joy to experience. Jumping between the painted storybook and the 3D world is not only creative but pretty memorable.The game launched with a few frustrating technical issues and bugs but some of them have already been addressed. I just wished though that we wouldn't have to fiddle with some outside software to cap the framerate - because of this, screen tearing was an issue that affected the game's presentation but overall, I didn't mind it too much.Nevertheless, the Plucky Squire easily earns my wholehearted recommendation even at full price!
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review:
The Plucky Squire follows the magical adventures of Jot and his friends - storybook characters who discover a three-dimensional world outside the pages of their book.

When the malevolent Humgrump realises he's the villain of the book - destined to lose his battle against the forces of good for all eternity - he kicks the heroic Jot out of its pages and changes the story forever.

Jot must face challenges unlike anything he's ever seen if he is to save his friends from Humgrump's dark forces and restore the book's happy ending.

Jump between 2D and 3D worlds in this charming action adventure - solving puzzles, boxing badgers, flying with a jetpack, and enjoying many more delightful and surprising mini challenges as you become the hero of a living storybook.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

name: Lies of P
detailed_description: You are a puppet created by Geppetto who’s caught in a web of lies with unimaginable monsters and untrustworthy figures standing between you and the events that have befallen the world of Lies of P. You are awakened by a mysterious voice that guides you through the plagued city of Krat - a once lively place that has been poisoned by madness and bloodlust. In our soulslike, you must adapt yourself and your weapons to face untold horrors, untangle the unfathomable secrets of the city's elites and choose whether to confront predicaments with the truth or weave lies to overcome them on the journey to find yourself. ・ A DARKLY ELEGANT AND CRUEL WORLD Unearth the secrets of the city of Krat – a place soaked in the style of the Belle Epoque era which once thrived due to its puppet industry and now sees its streets covered in blood. ・BATTLE WITH TWISTED INSTRUMENTS Develop a unique combat style to counter vicious enemies and terrain by weaving together dynamic weapon combinations, utilizing the Legion Arms, and activating new abilities. ・WHAT’S IN A LIE? There will be times when you will be confronted with choices where you can give comfort to others in sorrow or despair by lying…or you can choose to tell the truth. Carve your own path. ・A CLASSIC REIMAGINED Experience the beloved fairy tale of Pinocchio reinterpreted as a dark, grim narrative that allows players to discover the secrets and symbols hidden within the world of Lies of P.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say, I was pleasantly surprised by this game. After it was first announced, I never looked up any gameplay, I was already sold on it with the Souls-like and steampunk aspects of the game (i'm just a sucker for those things). _childDocuments_.review: Completed "Lies of P" - An Exceptional Soulsborne Experience!The atmosphere throughout the game is incredibly immersive, and the music, especially during the final arc, is mesmerizing. The story is absolutely epic, with each character perfectly voiced and portrayed.The game's difficulty is high, with the final act being the toughest. I faced numerous challenges against Laxasia and the subsequent two bosses. Even the final boss presented a significant challenge.Overall, a definite 10/10 experience.Note:- Have many achievements left but I think I won't continue the NG+- In every universe, I'll aim for Ranni the witch

_childDocuments_.review: As a passionate gamer, I recently completed "Lies of P" and was thoroughly impressed. The game stands out with its meticulously crafted gameplay mechanics, which are both intuitive and gratifying. One of the highlights for me was the vast array of weapon choices and combinations available. This feature not only added depth to the combat system but also allowed for a personalized gaming experience.The overall gameplay was exceptionally smooth and linear, a design choice I greatly appreciated. It provided a focused narrative path that kept me engaged throughout my playthrough. The game's pacing and structure were well-thought-out, contributing to an immersive experience.However, no game is without its flaws. I noticed that it was possible to 'cheese' most enemies, a tactic that, while useful, sometimes diminished the challenge and excitement of combat. Additionally, while the main storyline was captivating, I felt that the game could have benefited from a few more side quests to enrich the world and its lore.Despite these minor drawbacks, "Lies of P" is a stellar example of what modern gaming can offer. It brilliantly intertwines intriguing gameplay mechanics with a compelling narrative. For its ambitious design and execution, I would rate it a solid 9/10. This game is a must-play for anyone who appreciates a well-rounded and engaging gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: After about 34 hours put into this game I would like to get my thoughts out there.Pros:-Bosses are by far the best aspect of the game. Every boss is varied and deep with it’s moveset that it is satisfying to conquer the challenge. None of them feel the same and each have their own learning curve.-Level atmosphere is immaculate. Every area has a different feeling to it, whether it’s the city, forest outskirts, opera theater and more. Each look incredible and enemies fit the tone of each area.-Combat is satisfying to master. Using dodges, deflects, and tools to slay enemies feels great and impactful. The variety of weapons and moves you can use is great to see and think about how I can modify my weapons to fit my build. Most weapons can be dismantled to create different combinations of weapons and handles to make a new moveset.-Fable arts are SICK. Having different moves you can activate for things like crowd control, stagger, multi-attacks and status effects feels like a fantastic addition to the combat. -Legion arm is great. Each arm has a different feel to it and feels great to have for status effects and new moves. It’s like Sekiro’s Prosthetic but limited to one tool until you upgrade it. Personally, I like fire, but it’s not a “one size fits all” situation.-Story is unique and dark. The characters feel attached to the world and setup the tone well. However, i’m not much of a story guy. (Side note: Gemini just feels like a narrator; like his dialogue felt more like exposition than anything else by just explaining what we see. Small critique.)Cons:-The level design is too linear. Don’t get me wrong, the individual levels are very dynamic and interesting, but looking at them as a whole is too linear. Once you have fully explored one area, you have no choice but to defeat the boss because none of them are optional. There are mini-bosses that are optional but big bosses that have specters to use are not. This makes the game less dynamic in it’s design because you can’t get any extra weapons or upgrade material beyond the area you are in. If you’re stuck at a boss, the only things you can do are grind Ergo or re-spec your build; that’s it. It also ruins build crafting because if you want to use a certain weapon that’s in the end game, you can’t get it any sooner and you have to beat EVERY boss before it.-Bosses are hard. This goes back to the linear level design. If you are stuck on a boss, you can’t upgrade your weapon or tool beyond what the game allows you (Like getting the next tier of upgrade materials for your weapon). You could be stuck with a +6  weapon (or +3 boss weapon) with no option to upgrade further because the material you need is beyond the boss. If you’re stuck then you have to grind Ergo or change your build which you can’t even do until slightly beyond the mid game (The 8th main boss, I counted the Mad Donkey). Your upgrades DO MATTER because resources are limited, except for weapon upgrade stones (but you still are limited by the stone tiers). -Some mini-bosses are unskippable as in you can’t just skip to the main boss. A smaller issue but I just find it stupid that I'm forced to fight a tough enemy rather than it being something optional that I can do to increase my character’s power. However, not all of them are unskippable.Small changes:-Make the pop ups for items obtained and written notes toggle-based instead of timed. Like I’m trying to read everything and suddenly it disappears. Also, sometimes I am celebrating after beating a boss that’s been kicking my ass for 2 days and everything I get from it disappears. I know for items there’s a system that shows new items which is great, but my point still stands for notes.-Some death dialogue gets cut off when you die to a boss/mini-boss because it mutes the audio. Have the audio still be heard while the death animation is happening because I want to hear it.Overall, Fantastic game. It may take me a while but I want to get all the achievements. Despite my issues above, a great souls-like game. Great world design, great combat, great weapons, and great bosses would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. It has obvious similarity to other games in this genre but has added its own unique flair that makes it a truly memorable experience. The weapon crafting and legion arm mechanics allow for some pretty cool builds and the weapon durability was honestly quite fun to manage, this is helped by the very fluid and flashy animations. The score and sound design were lovely and really added to the experience. Lastly, the story was great, it had a lot of heartfelt moments and was happy with the ending I got. Though I will say the latest weapon that they gave to players on start does trivialise the early game. This wasn't really a problem for me as I enjoyed being stronger than the enemies and would have just maxed out another weapon like I do in other games so I can stay ahead of the content. And, like with other souls-likes there are bosses that are more annoying than others but nothing that can't be overcome with a spec change.Regardless, I look forward to whatever they bring out next for the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing take on the souls like genre. Guarding/perfect guarding are your go to for defense while dodging and side stepping is situational but can be very useful. Damage mitigation is substantially more effective compared to other souls like games. Enemy variety feels like its in a good spot. Only had one small bug my entire playthrough and zero performance issues.The game isn't perfect but definitely worth a try for souls like enjoyers.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: It was everything I was promised and more! Can't wait for the DLC or sequel or whatever they have planed next for P! I care about him very much! I love the aesthetics, the NPCs have interesting stories, loves the music, just an incredible game, and I need more!(Spoilers ahead) Unhinged praise aside:Not to sound shallow but... It would be nice if P had an outfit that felt truly his. The one he begins in was reflection of his father's expectations and desires, something for a puppet, a tool, not for an actual living being, a real, independent person; and all the others either belong to someone else or represent an affiliation to a faction he doesn't really belong too, including the one in the promotional art and cover. Maybe he'll grow more into himself and get an outfit of his own in a future protect? I hope it comes with different haircut, his final one looks... IDK, tragic? It just doesn't look good on him TBH... Also:The animations for when we try to do something but don't have items or legion takes too long leaving P too open for damage.The weapons getting stuck in the environment is just annoying...Chipping a HP bar to 0 only to find out there's a more is... I don't even have words... Please, in the next one just make it like you did with the champion: You get halfway, there's a short cut-scene, and then we go to the second phase. All that aside: 9,7/10 Definitely recommend to any souls-like fan. It has been eating at my brain since I got it and I'm about to finish my second round, might go for a third!
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: I love the part in which P said "it's time to lie" and then lied all over place and, somehow, that is the requisite for the best ending.Absolutely stellar level design. The developer understood that a souls game is made or broken by its encounters above anything else. The reason why dark souls 2 is considered the weakest of the series while having excellent mechanics and levels is simply that the encounters sucked, which shows that even from software sometimes fumbles. Apart from a couple of areas (and like I said, it's not like the originals were flawless), Lies of P manages to maintain every encounter fun to figure out.The only bad thing I want to mention is how there are no major secret areas and bosses. During a normal playthrough, you will most likely explore everything. It's a linear, streamlined experience, which is not necessarily bad but makes me wonder why this aspect in the original souls games is often glossed over. In Bloodborne, a small part of an otherwise late game area can be accessed by getting killed by one particular enemy. There are several optional bosses, all of them of high quality. None of this is present in lies of p. Save from one final choice, every boss you kill in your first playthrough is also every boss in the game.That said, this game is extremely replay able and I'm on my second playthrough with a completely different build.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: Cannot recommend this one enough.  It's the closest thing to a Fromsoft game any other studio has come.  Meaty, deliberate combat mesh with a superbly interesting setting.  The way quests work is much more straightforward as well.  Music and sound top-notch.  The weapons are incredible, and had me tinkering like a mad puppet.  Count me in for DLC and a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: Simply wonderful game. Whether you are a souls veteran or a newbie looking for a way into the genre, this a must. for the obligatory Bloodborne comparison. If Bloodborne is close to a perfect reimagining of the lovecraftian tale in game form, this would be the equivalent to Pinocchio's tale. Somehow its able to retain the sweetness and kindness of the original fable, while pitting you against nightmares and then some.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: Its a pretty game, there are very few faults that I noticed in the less than 30 minutes I played. However Elden ring spoiled me. I absolutely refuse to play a game without a map. I did this with the surge series and realized it makes me absolutely miserable, it kills any and all replay-ability as well as being able to pick it back up with ease down the line or if I don't binge play it. There are so many quality of life things missing, no crouch, no jump, always will be straight lines essentially and thats just disappointing. the game lacks the ability to sprint without using stamina when no enemies are around and a game without a map that is a cardinal sin since now you're being punished for exploring and trying to explore while always having to stop and go is just irritating.I'm not saying this game is bad, some of its qualities would be cool to have in Elden ring like durability to force others to use more weapons instead of their favorite like 4. If you want a souls like game sure this might scratch the itch but realistically you might hate it if you enjoyed Elden ring due to its very major QOL items missing. In ER I hated that they never included a quest log so its hard to remember where you leave off down the line, in this game if you aren't the type to play one game until completion you'll likely hate it as much as I do and I really wanted to give it a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! By far the best souls-like game I've played not to be developed by FromSoftware. I'd personally suggest to refrain from summoning for help on the boss fights (at least in the first play through) as I cant imagine you getting that same hit of dopamine when you finally defeat the ones that you've spent hours on.  Hoping to see more games of this genre from Neowiz in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels like a super generic souls-like.This whole experience was so incredibly boring. I'm having trouble understanding why people rate the game so highly. The level design:Basically one long corridor with some diversions here and there but none of these go much further than just around the corner for an item and back again. If there's a crossroad and a path takes longer than 10 seconds then it's guaranteed to be the main path and you should go back as you've missed an item. Part of why this is a problem is that you'll never miss upgrade materials which means the upgrading of weapons might as well just be a checkpoint mechanic. Why do I have to go back and upgrade manually if the game knows exactly when I'll find what item? I've never played a souls-like that has such predictable shortcuts and save spots.My biggest problem is that this creates a lack of any exciting areas and absolutely no secrets. Enemies:90% of the enemy variety is basically a zombie with a puppet reskin. The movement and attacks are all very basic and direct and the same enemies keep reappearing over and over. Later on something happens to them and they'll be recycled with a new skin...When you do meet a special enemy, just run past them as you'll be guaranteed a save point and then just go back for the enemy. The uninteresting trash mobs make going through the corridors a real bore. Bosses: I'm not a big fan of the parry in this game but that's OK. I think because I'm not good at parries it makes for a less pleasant experience. I understand this is a skill issue so I don't mind. I found 3 bosses in the game to be memorable. Souls-like (besides fromsoft games) that I think are more interesting than this include:Nioh 1+2The surge 2Lords of the fallen 2014 (yes, really)At least this was better than Code Vein...I'm not saying the game is bad perse and I'm happy that other people enjoy it so much. I just wish I knew why.6/10 for £50
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: Nails the feeling of a FromSoft game with enough unique mechanics that make it stand out from the rest of the imitators. The upgrade system and the weapon blade+handle system give a lot of options to make your playthrough unique, and the different arm abilities are interesting and fun. Basic enemies can be a cakewalk but the elites and bosses are where the combat shines, with a heavy emphasis on perfect parries that feel amazing to get right. As these games go this one is very linear but the story is well paced and uses the linearity to its advantage, being more straightforward than many of the games it was inspired by. I'm excited to see where it goes (currently on Ch4 boss) and have no hesitation recommending this to any fan of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely one of my favorite games to come out in recent times. I've had a surge to play any games that are Souls-likes & I don't know what it is, when it comes to Lies of P.But this game specifically; has became a comfort game for me personally. Considering how many times I've beaten it, tried out different build from Dex, Strength, & even Arcane niche builds. It's just been really fun running the game over & over again. Every boss is pretty nice that makes of the gameslist, except for in my opinion. The only ones I don't really likes in all honesty when it comes to facing again in runs is Nameless Puppet, and Corrupted parade Master. There is like two others I can think of but I forgot their names but yea. Not every boss is a favorite but it's nice to know that most of them are great to fight against. I'm just glad I found my favorite Souls-like, even though it's not made from FromSoftware. It's still a great alternative if you're not a fan of any of the titles there. But that's rare to hear from anyone who is a fan of this Genre in general. Got it on sale cuz I put like almost 200hrs into the game and learning it on Game Pass.Thought I get it on sale for 42$ and once again. Enjoyed my time with it, beat it in one day. 11hrs run with me taking my time. Got the Rise of P ending because that's the best ending and apparently; the canon ending to the game's story. If you're a Souls fan, check out this game. It's worth your time, and do so before the DLC arrives!
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: Best soulslike hands down, not much difficult as I expected hearing people here and there but I guess people just can't play this game lol. Only boss I didn't really like was S.M. but after the first playthrough I've done it first try everytime so I guess there's not much to say about that. Story is ok, I mean it's pretty obvious where it is going from the start but obvious is not equal to bad, I liked the story <3Get this master piece, enjoy it and praise the wrench!
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantasic souls-like.The fact this is the developers first shot at a game like this is mindblowing because it blows basically all others in the genre out of the water. From presentation, gameplay, combat, boss/enemy design,.. 10s across the board.Only small gripe I have is the linearity of it. The zones are ( mostly ) not interconnected and all have kinda the same structure. It gets a bit obvious after a while. But who cares if literally everything else is amazing?ABSOLUTELY worth the price. I cannot wait for DLC and for the next game in this new series.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: This game does not just wear its inspirations on its sleeves, it wears them plastered across its face in neon flashing lights. But rather intentionally, NEOWIZ has opted for a particularly compelling pairing of inspirations and executed on each beautifully, and most importantly, faithfully.Would recommend for fans of souls games and/or wooden puppet folklore enthusiasts.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: The best souls-like game you will ever play (as a 3D and that stuff of course) it has all of the good challenges that you want in terms of bosses and the in the overall genera. Most of the hate that people have is because the game does not make you rely on dodging the whole time, parrying is a really important aspect in the game. So I would give it like 70% of the game is parrying and 30% of it is dodging. The game also introduces many new mechanics and ways to modify yourself that were not in FromSoftware games. So overall I give the game 9/10 and maybe 10/10 taking the fact that this is the first game of this studio and this is the only legit souls-like game that you can play.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: You know when you're looking for some new Soulslike content and you only find trash...well Lies of P just made it possible!From now on i will look forward to what these devs are cooking for us. Very fun and attractive game. Nothing wrong to say about it so far. After 10h in.The gameplay is a good mix of Sekiro and Bloodborne in my book. The block mecanic makes you want to stay engaged with the boss in melee and get those sweet fatal attacks.I'm not a 10/10 guy so now i'd give Lies of P an easy 8/10. Very good!
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: Before playing Lies of P, I was very skeptical on whether or not it would be worth it. The instant I fought against the first mini-boss, that all changed. Lies of P is GOLDEN if you like the older-styled souls games (Bloodborne, Dark Souls 3, etc). It implements multiple systems that were used in previous souls game and so much more! The level design so far is genuinely amazing and feels very similar to the shortcut-system used in DS1. The combat feels great and though it's not as flashy as Elden Ring, it is still very VERY exciting. Lies of P is an amazing game and I highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys the Soulsborne games.

_childDocuments_.review: I had so much fun playing Lies of P and I can't wait for the DLC! I'm just going to highlight some of the key aspects from this game if you want to know more. Bosses: There are some mean puppets ready to kill you in this game. Fortunately, instead of just being there holding your p-organ waiting for your turn, you are a very active participant in the fights. Are there some bosses with really long combos? Yes, but in addition to blocking/dodging you always have the option to parry them and build your stagger, or getting some space to throw some consumables (they are really strong in this game). With some exceptions, I also appreciate the lack of sparks, clutter and visual noise in the fights which makes it easier to understand what the bosses are doing. I could do without some of the 2-phase bosses, just give me one big health bar please. Levels: The levels are mostly linear with secrets hiding here and there, but you will rarely get lost. Some late game levels can get a bit boring or rather dull-looking, but there is a lot of variety in the environment and the enemies you encounter. While there is an order you follow while you experience the game, you can at least know that your fighting level/knowledge is where it is supposed to be. Combat: It's simply the best part of the game. Weapon arts, weapon mods, legion arms, consumables, parrying, blocking, dodging are all tools that make your experience feel tight, fast and fun! There are so many little details I could describe as to way I love this combat system (like hitting a heavy to stagger) I think it is better if you experience it for yourself. Difficulty: Overall, this game is challenging, but it is so worth it in the end. If you get stuck at some point, try your consumables, and use your specter (the game will shower you with the material needed to use specters). As you play, there is also a way to "strengthen" your specter, but it is unlocked around mid-game. Until then, learning the timings and watching other people fight the bosses is the way to go. Now, my good boy, go finish the game and then join your fellow P-heads as we wait for the DLC.
