_childDocuments_.review: After beating the game for the first time and having progressed halfway through new game plus I think I'm ready to talk about this game.For those who just want the short version, do I recommend this game? If you like souls-like games (although I hate that tag for various reasons), then sure. The game is difficult, but not extremely difficult, most fights and situations feel fair and it has a very satisfying combat system. The story is a nice little twist on the source material, and although it seems basic for most of the game, it really does take a very nice and satisfying turn, specially if you get the "true ending". And the art direction is honestly gorgeous most of the time. So yeah, it deserves all the praise it gets., this also means it is a difficult game, or more difficult than the mainstream games today. If you do not like challenges DO NOT GET THIS GAME. I've had a friend talk to me about how he really wants to play this game because it looks so good, and I've had to talk him down from doing it since he told me he only played 10 minutes of Bloodborne and he hated it. If you feel like that, give this game a pass, or play the demo (I really love that it is an option) and be the judge of if the game is for you.And now for the long part. This game gets the "souls-like" tag from Steam, which is a tag that I usually despise for several different reasons, just like metroidvania. Because it doesn't really tell you that much about the game most of the time, and people just write them off as copycats most of the time. But this game is probably one of the few that I would say it is fair to compare to the souls series. This game heavily leans on their formula and took all the right cues and game design philosophies that made the Fromsoftware games great, while trimming all the fat and clunky parts of them.This game has all the classics like "does not open from this side", poison swamp, surprise miniboss, traps, ambushes and boss weapons... So it has this very nostalgic and familiar feeling if you've come from that series. But like I said, it actually improves on the formula by adding some very nice quality of life changes and improvements that I seriously don't understand why From hasn't done them before. Like giving you a hint on how to continue sidequests by marking the checkpoint they are closest to, letting you reset your build as many times as you'd like with an unlimited resource, only catch being it gets more expensive the more times you do it in a single playthrough. Helpful in-game tutorials and all the mechanics are explained in a guide tab in the settings menu. Lore items that do all the worldbuilding so you don't have to rely on item descriptions alone, you don't have to run too far to rematch bosses and they leave your money at it's door in case you want to do something else before trying again, and so on and so forth.The bosses feel like they were designed specifically for this game, and never felt "cheap" or unfair (except very few exceptions from certain attacks, and some pre-patch health pools), unlike Elden Ring where it feels they introduced Sekiro style bosses in a system where they don't work so well. Speaking of which, this game feels better to play more as a Sekiro style game than a souls one. Most of their mechanics heavily encourage you to use their "parry" system since you are extremely rewarded by doing so, and unlike other souls games, you CAN parry basically everything (I still have to test some attacks). Besides, it's less expensive stamina wise, you can break weapons doing it, you deal stagger damage to enemies and if you are early you still can block the attack and recover the chip damage with another parry (with the right upgrade). On top of that it's just really satisfying compared to just dodging.They also made the consumables VERY worthwhile, unlike in souls games. They might even be slightly broken, but that gets compensated by them being a bit expensive, so you are basically throwing money at enemies to make things easier, something the game is very good at. Although there's no online play, major bosses have the option to summon a specter, which with the right buffs can basically solo some bosses, there's no penalty besides having to use a consumable that is easy to farm, and that later on you can just buy.I could really go on, and on, about the positives about this game, like how the weapons feel and are very interesting and unique, it's assembly system, Fable Arts... But I think you already get the point. It's good.But even the most critically acclaimed games have their flaws, and this game is no stranger to those. For one, some places in this game really needed some good landmarks, since it's very easy to get turned around sometimes and not know where to go. There's some puzzling level design sometimes, for example: in the Elysion Boulebard, there's a place where you can deploy a ladder that lets you skip a whole house full of enemies, it feels like a backwards shortcut, like you were meant to climb the house instead of going down. It's as if they flipped the level design in that one, it's not bad, it's just Another issue I have with the game is the whole timed decision system, it just doesn't add that much to the game. I would like to have some time to think about my answer before just doing it, any other choice does let you do that a lot of the time, so why some of those are on a timer? Maybe it's an artistic decision to make you feel the pressure of the moment, but the presentation of those options already achieve that making you feel like it's a major choice, so there's not that much of a point to stress people out with a clock. Some enemies are able to parry you, which is fine, but some can do it while you are already attacking them (like in a combo) triggering an instant counter-attack, which makes them extremely annoying to fight. As a game designer myself, that is a TERRIBLE idea, you discourage the player from doing damage, and you force them to drag on the fight a lot more than it should if you have a fast hitting low damage weapon. It's as bad of an idea as giving a boss i-frames in the middle of a fight. A better solution would be to make it always dodge out of your combo or get hyper-armor instead of parrying you, like most of the enemies do so you don't stunlock them to death.Another big problem in my opinion is that they don't really do anything with new game +. It's just the same, but with everything scaled up, just like in Elden Ring and Dark Souls. But that's something it's been proven to be a huge letdown. Dark Souls 2 and Armored Core VI have a way more satisfying New Game+ experience, with different events and enemies being exclusive to a second run. It just gives you more of an incentive to play through the game again, instead of just completionist cleanup. I could point out some more issues, but they would be very nitpicky at that point. I honestly think this game can be an absolute classic, and I can't wait to see more, like DLC or even a sequel in the same universe.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat it. 7.5/10. It does a few things well. But I can't recommend it since I really stopped having fun about half way through, I only finished because I paid full price and do enjoy this genre of games. The overwhelming issue though is that fighting in this game is frustrating for the wrong reasons. Every single enemy, and I really do mean EVERY single enemy in this game, relies on the same style of attacks: long build up, awkwardly long pause, and then insanely quick execution of attack. It makes dodging and parrying literally impossible unless you are already familiar with the enemies movesets, and even when you know their movesets - you will miss parries because the time to react is so ridiculously small. It's not so much a matter of parry window being too short, its that the attack happens so fast you don't have time to react. Other souls games do have this style of attacks as well, but they don't rely on every single enemy using them.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid soulslike with some inspiration from Bloodborne, though you do have to approach it on its own terms and not expect it to be exactly like other games.Few criticisms:- The puppets are a cool enemy type but they all but disappear in the second half of the game in favor of generic goop monsters which aren't nearly as cool or interesting. Huge shame imo.- A lot of bosses (Green Monster, Black Rabbit rematch, Laxasia, Romeo) have a very easy first phase and a rather difficult second phase which share little or no moves, which made me feel like I was wasting my time grinding through the first phase just to get a few shots at the second phase a lot of the time. Would have appreciated the bosses to be tuned a little better in this regard.- Story feels a little messy and confusing sometimes, being told "go here" without any real explanation for it, things just happen without a clear explanation, etc. There are several different crises in the game world simultaneously and it's not really clear how and why they are connected. While *most* of this makes sense in the greater context of the story, it still feels like a lot of the time I was confused as to whether something was supposed to be mysterious or supposed to be clear and I just missed some dialog somewhere. This results in things just feeling a little half-baked and disjointed at times, and in me not really caring about a lot of very important characters like Sophia, Simon Manus or Gepetto.- In fact, almost all characters other than Venigni and Arlecchino feel pretty underdeveloped.- Level design is a little bit underwhelming. Especially Arche Abbey just feels a little arbitrary, confusing and gamey. As the game takes place in a city I would have appreciated a somewhat more connected and coherent world map.Good points:- The weapon system is a lot of fun.- Variety of different possible builds and approaches.- Parrying feels good and satisfying, the Bloodborne-style 'rally' mechanism is also at its place here making it less punishing to attempt parries.- Bosses have quite some variety in general.- The game is nice to look at.

_childDocuments_.review: Personal Rating: 8.5I struggled a little during the first two hours of playing due to my decision to go with a strength build even though I usually focus on agility builds, but after I got the option to change weapons and especially when I had the option to combine my own weapon my interest and joy for the game gradually increased. While parrying in the beginning still felt very punishing and very unrewarding in the beginning during boss battles you really learned how and when to parry and when you then finally did a perfect parry it at least felt good even though it didn't have an immediete impact on the enemy. It's also quite fun to note that if you parry someones weapon often enough they can actually break, which also works during boss battles. In general I would say the game is quite challenging and definitely had some bosses where I struggled for around 2 hours before I eventually beat them, however I also have to add that they just recently nerfed some bosses and boosted the helper companion that you can summon for boss fights which should make it easier when you are truly struggling. The map design is also really well made, the passages always feel manageable and the next shortcut is usually not too far away when you are out of healing potions. Some spots are a little bit too predictable especially when you are not new to the genre, but there were still some parts where I got jump scared by an enemy or where something unexpected happened.The story was also decent, even though I'm not usually too interested in the plot. Sometimes you will be asked for a decision in a quick time event. Even though I disklike locking myself out of certain endings or scenarios most decisions were rather reasonable and it is not too challenging to assume what kind of impact ones decision would have.I would definitely recommend the game if you like Souls Like games as it should provide you with a solid 20+ hours of gameplay. It personally took me around 25 hours, but I also made sure to collect and explore everything which is quite doable due to the linear setup of the map.

_childDocuments_.review: ***9/10***If someone told me FromSoft made this game, I would have believed them. This is the only soulslike I've ever played that met the quality of the actual Souls games, feeling like a true successor to Bloodborne. While most boss fights don't feel as difficult as From's, that's not necessarily a bad thing. Each boss is a spectacle in its own right, and the more gimmicky ones are incredibly fun to fight. The OST is so much better than it needed to be, you can feel the amount of time and effort that went into each track, especially in the collectible records. The weapon assembling mechanic is great, increasing your available weapons exponentially each time you find a new one, granting an insane amount of build variety. It's super easy to respec your character whenever you want, so you never feel locked into one build, and there's no need to worry if you level up an unnecessary stat by mistake. The game has Sekiro's parry, Bloodborne's rally, and a connected world akin to Dark Souls 1, among other things from From's games, making it feel like a celebration of the genre in the best way possible.If you're a fan of Bloodborne, or any Souls game, this game is a necessity.Now it's time for me to grind out the rest of the achievements while I wait for DLC or a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I've beaten the game, I want to give a more detailed review. To be clear- this is overall a very well made game. My negative review is tentative, and hopefully I will change it into a positive one in the future, but that depends on if the development team is willing to make slight quality of life changes that would drastically improve the enjoyment for the player. This game does a lot well: the level design, the aesthetic, the music, the weapons, the various "legion arms," all of that is great. However, I do genuinely think this is the absolute limit of difficulty that Souls fans are going to be willing to put up with.The lack of animation cancelling and the unnecessarily tight perfect guard windows are incredibly frustrating, both things that Sekiro does better. There are decisions in this game that come across as oversights at best and spiteful at worst. The deflection system comes across as overly punishing with red attacks not being able to be dodged as it's entirely arbitrary as to what can be i-framed and what can't. There are also an over abundance of red attacks in comparison to Sekiro where they felt more special and thoughtfully placed. Another issue with the deflection system is how inconsistent it is in conjunction with grab attacks- while unblockable attacks glow red to let the player know to either perfect guard or avoid the attack entirely, there are also grab attacks that need to be perfect guarded or avoided entirely that don't glow red, and the only way to figure that out is to perfect guard the very first time it appears or to be punished for something you've never seen before. Another thing I hate is how the game tends to break its own rules- the guard break system in particular. Normally if you posture break a boss it slumps down so that you can get in a critical, but the second rabbit boss fight the big brother does a crazy flailing swing when you "guard break" him (literally going against the name of the mechanic) to get in a few cheap hits on unsuspecting players that could cause an unfair death. This also happens with Laxasia and it's just a cheap surprise. The worst instance of this ways throughout the whole game, big enemies falling down don't have a hit box as they collide with the floor, but the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Door Guardian boss does, and his head hitting the floor actually killed me, causing a huge chunk of my time to be wasted. And why are we still doing the weapon upgrade system? Of all of the things to copy from Souls, this is the worst. How can I be expected to experiment with different weapons if I have limited and expensive upgrade materials? If the game is also going to include a weapon durability system (which is pretty harsh in comparison to something like Das1 or Das2), then at least let me change weapons on the fly without worry of how upgraded a weapon is. Lastly, I hate the withered health. Losing stamina to blocking is trade-off enough, and it's obviously just something from Bloodborne the devs wanted to shoe-horn in.

_childDocuments_.review: My original review further down is from when i had 16 hours in the game, after playing the second half in the game, i have changed my opinion drastically. This game is centered around the parry mechanic, you're at all times MEANT TO be better off parrying attacks (you interrupt (up to 20 hit combos), you take no damage, you can break enemy's weapon, you add to enemy's stagger and work towards riposte, there are attacks that are undodgeable and the dodge is overall short and ♥♥♥♥), but that is far from the reality. The parry system has countless flaws:- Different timings depending on context (staggered, poise broken, blocking, not blocking, attacking, rolling, using consumable) and every single one of them changes how long does it take to activate the parry frames- Enemies might telegraph, but in the Elden Ring style: seconds worth of frames of windup, then 10 frames of attack which tests your reaction time - the telegraphing is worthless- Enemies have AoE attacks and "body slam attacks" which means you have to parry as they approach an arbitrary distance away from you, you can never know and punishment for failing is: your parry timing changes, you get hit usually twice, you get debuff stacks that usually mean you have to disengage and the 20 hit combo continues- If you want to keep your parry timing consistent, you have to stand in neutral where you will just get grabbed by attacks you can't parry (the game does NOT notify you of this in any way) - Dodge roll is just laughably useless, there are attacks that are undodgeable on purpose, then there are attacks that are undodgeable due to the dodge mechanic being terrible (no matter how you dodge the attack loops and hits you anyway) - Exploring the world was great in the first half, but in the second there's just the same 5 enemies again and again one of which is a guy with a gun who shoots you off all the ledges you don't just fall off because this game loves taking away your controls, so you just watch your character walk off the ledge and when you get your controls back, it's already late- As mentioned in previous point, the game takes your control away all the time.. you get hit too hard? can't do anything until fully recovered, used consumable? can't do ♥♥♥♥ till your character is done rubbing his tummy how good it felt, you walk into bossfight and want to apply buff to your weapon? nah the block input doesn't count despite you still holding it.. you wanna roll then immediately heal? well you better press that heal AFTER you regained control.This game had potential and the first half of it was brilliant and beautiful, but the moment the bosses start testing your understanding of the game's skillset, you ran into the problem that you have to play around the game's stupid decisions, instead of going with the flow.. this game has one of the worst takes on parry i've seen in my life, which would be fine if it wasn't the core mechanic of the game. It's close, but still so far. You can't subsidize combat with the style in a game about combat, sorry. Original:I'm a fromsoft veteran, middle of the pack challenge runner (SL1/"flawless" endurance runner), played DS123/Se/BB/DeS/Thymesia/ER and plenty other games.. guess that's my bona fides, this game is amazing, the new features, the changes to the relentless world of fromsoft games and the artstyle and performance are all working well together. The poster child feature is ability to combine handle/blade of any "non boss" weapon into a new thing, with an ability to shift the handle towards the build you want to play stat wise (alphabet scaling SABCDE), which leads to some crazy looking and feeling weapons that allow you to strategize and or just have fun on a boss with a dumb looking creation, it just kinda works. I don't personally use all of these, but the game has: - Sekiro style prosthetic ranging from a punch to a cannon- Souls style elemental resins (with a guaranteed one per life for free)- Summons for bossfights- Weapon arts (one for blade one for handle)- Consumables/Throwables/replenishables- Souls style gearing (4 pieces of gear, 2 weapon slots to alternate, up to i believe 4 "rings")- Passive tree unlocks allowing you to for example trade extra estus for more damage/defense/magic - Bloodborne-sekiro hybrid combat (perfect guard - hurts opononent, block takes some HP and makes some regainable, no block just takes HP)The bossfigts are varied, unique and hit the classic archetypes: Gank squad, multi phase, backstab cushion, parry festival, endurance survival, gimmick, "run away or perish", and many others. You won't struggle to find interesting battles and cool tools to take them up with. Areas are interconnected and close up on themselves, reusing bonfires like what people love about DS1s world, but way more and way better. Just like DS1 the world is not interconnected, but the areas loop on themselves which gives them a lot of character and sense of direction, because personally i remember where i am based on how i got there and if a zone has 10 shortcuts, i have many ways to get many places. This game in my opinion wears it's inspirations proudly, taking from the best and while unique and separate, joining the other greats from FS on the list of my beloved games. The art is breathtaking, LoP is beautiful.You can't be a woman. 0/10

_childDocuments_.review: (Score and summary at the bottom)I want to preface this review by saying that before I played Lies of P, I have never finished, or even made it to a boss of any of the other Soulsborne games I tried. I played the beginning of Bloodborne at a friend's place a few years ago and got destroyed for a few hours without making it to a boss though had fun learning the game, and I also own the ps3 version of Demon's Souls, which I stopped playing really early on as well, and after having finished Lies of P, I'd love to revisit at some point.I'm a bit of a literature guy and love games that tell darker retellings of classic literature (if you haven't played Alice Madness Returns, 100% recommend that game) so seeing this game retell the story of Pinocchio, it caught my attention, even with many reviews stating this game is harder than any other Soulsborne they had played.The story for this game is so interesting, with a memorable cast of characters that you truly start to care about as you progress through the game. Each character brings something to the table, and also subtly hint at information that'll make more sense later on. The tragic world presented here is top tier and the environmental story telling is some of the best I have seen.Now for the meat of the game, the gameplay. I've heard Lies of P described as Sekiro and Bloodborne combined and having watched videos of Bloodborne, and picking up and finishing Sekiro after finishing Lies of P, I think that's a fair description of the game. This game is brutally hard and the best advice I can give is be patient. Because the devs are evil and made most of the enemies puppets, the arms on swings will wind up 4 or 5 times and then just snap onto you. Enemies will constantly fake you out, delay attacks, attack much sooner or later than you'll expect, the variety of encounters in this game is fantastic and makes every new area you explore so much fun. I don't wanna spoil encounters for those who want to enter the game blind, but I'd say the challenge in this game for veterans of the Souls-like genre is that NEOWIZ knows how you like to play and they basically give you the finger. I actually think me entering this game with no experience in the genre helped because I didn't have a set play style and habits for tackling games like this, so ironically, a game that challenges the most hardened Soulsborne players may be easier for folks who are new to the genre! Though having picked up Dark Souls 1 after finishing Lies of P and Sekiro, it saddens me that the "parry everything" strat isn't nearly as viable in DS1 so in a way I ended up developing habits that'll make Dark Souls even harder for my first time playing which will be interesting to see as I progress that game further!The music in this game is absolutely beautiful and the use of vinyls in the hotel to help Pinocchio gain his humanity is such an interesting way to use music in a game. Also the use of lying throughout the game makes for interesting story beats as well. It's established early in the game that puppets cannot lie, Pinocchio being the exception, and I enjoy this different take on the classic story since I know I put spoilers over the last paragraph, and if you haven't played this game, I highly encourage you to enter this experience as blind as you can in regards to story, because this is one of the best I have seen in a long time.Lies of P is going to get a 10/10 and I am extremely picky with scores, but even with a few minor flaws like back stabbing being a bit finicky, Lies of P is one of the best games I have ever played and I loved it so much I immediately started playing Sekiro Shadows Die Twice and finished it. If you have the patience to learn this game's systems, you'll find probably the best Souls-like game not made by Fromsoft, I'd argue Lies of P may actually be better than some of the Fromsoft games. There's so much more I could cover in this review like the creative weapon assembly system, the immaculate level design, and the incredible boss fights, but I think these things are best experienced for yourself. 100% buy this game right now, it is absolutely worth it!

_childDocuments_.review: After patch the default movement was greatly improved. It was less demanding now so I can finally wholeheartedly recommend this game.It has stunning art, out of this world music, beautiful story, and lovable characters. It can be a bit off-putting at first because the combat logic has some unique ideas that souls veterans need to learn and not just play it like *insert souls game here*. The weapons and combining system are extremely varied and a excellent innovation.The progression of this game is very linear, and that comes with 1 problem.Limited weapon materials that only come in at absolute end game already.You can't get unlimited special weapon leveling material even after NG+, ending in discouraging trying different weapons. Despite this oddity, the game is worthy of the new indie souls-like darling reputation it has, and swiftly joining one of my favorites.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautiful, but lacks some important polish as far as mechanics are concerned. It seems like the game wants you to chain parry in a way inspired by Sekiro, but doesn't let you combo into a block from an attack, or vice versa, but imperfect timing leads to chip-damage and soulsian-esque guard-breaks. Learning a boss's move set is forces a slow and methodical rhythm, but the fights themselves demand a fast and aggressive play-style in order to win. Looks great, and is mostly fun. But much of the time, it feels like the game forces you to suffer, rather than forcing you to get better.You don't get hyperarmor, which makes slow strength builds very annoying to run. No hyperarmor is also a major issue with this game's "groggy" mechanic. It requires you to either perfect parry or pressure the boss until their health bar turns white. It's at this point that if you land a fully charged heavy attack that you can finally land a major blow in the form of a "fatal attack." Bosses can still attack you during the 4~5 second window, and will always interrupt your charge if they connect, as you don't have and can't get hyperarmor.Just buy it on sale if you really want to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game, if you like souls-likes you will enjoy this game. Take a page from Capn Jack Sparrow; sometimes the best strategy is to run away to fight back (literally, dodge an attack or tap the dodge to backstep, then run away, and run back in to punish works for a LOT of bosses).The game takes some time to adjust due to its own mechanics being slightly different (no generous roll windows, no poise, skim amounts of hyperarmor on heavy weapons), but it gets much smoother as you play more. I definitely recommend having a quick weapon and a slooooow weapon on hand, some enemies can be spammed to death and others you can abuse the small amount of hyperarmor at the end of meaty charged heavies to chunk their health.Anyways the game is like others have said: it's hard but fair, and once you figure out the unique mechanics you'll really love smashing puppets

_childDocuments_.review: This game hits you with the hardest final boss of all time: Jokes aside, I like this game a lot. Every ounce of skepticism I felt due to the silly premise of a Pinocchio soulslike was shed once I actually got a feel for it and saw just how earnestly the team behind this game took its premise. Not shallow in the slightest, neither as a soulslike nor as a Pinocchio inspired story. The mechanical depth behind the combat mechanics and upgrade systems are on par with any Fromsoft game. The perfect guard is especially satisfying, staggers and guard breaks net big damage, and everything in general just flows nicely once you get the rhythm for combat that hits hard with excellent sound and visual design to back it up. Everything I could ask for in a tough as nails soulsy experience is here, and they achieved that visions better than many contemporaries with the same goal.One minor complaint: their "if it ain't broke, don't fix it" attitude towards mechanical inspiration sometimes leads to some somewhat contrived decisions that border on uninspired references from time to time (drop down a tower/well with planks bit, swamp with ballistae, 20 second long boss runbacks, a couple annoying crystal lizards, etc. etc.) none of it really bothered me beyond an eyeroll here and there at what they must have considered "classic" obligatory add-ins. That said, this game still does enough unique stuff and has a different (but good) feeling to it, so I can forgive a bit of copycat little brother behavior. The P-Organ upgrade system is pretty cool and the internal parts > armor is a nice way of letting you stay fashionable. The indicator of how many souls are on your bloodstain are nice, quest location update indicators are a godsend, alongside a bunch of other smaller original details I liked. Here's my only serious complaint: why don't they let you get any of the rabbit masks as a wearable costume? Ok - genuinely though, I found very little to gripe about. The coin fruit thing maybe? I dunno. It's a mechanic almost exclusively for folks who need partner AI assists and to respec. On principle I think the timed resource thing is... weird? But it's so vestigial I've only used it for a single respec, so there's nothing to be mad about.I could say so much more but I think anything that could be said already has. I liked pretty much every boss, even the lame ones were passable. Lies of P passes the "would play again just to fight the bosses" bar of this style of game which is often the place that so many others fail. I would play a boss rush, for sure. Also worth mentioning, characters were compelling, def got a few good gut punches - as a story of creation, humanity, love, life, and death (as many stories are) Lies of P could have been as shallow and forgettable as any other attempt, and yet it all felt simple yet sincere. You could tell each character had a solid theme and arc where they make you love (or love to hate) them from the first minute and over the course of only half a dozen interactions can tell a full, meaningful short story. Which is to say, you could tell someone who actually cared and felt things for what they were writing did so.Anyway, halfway though NG+ now to finish up achievements and I'm still having a blast. Saw some folks complain about the difficulty of it and it's been pretty breezy. Bosses have a lot of extra health but normal enemies are not annoyingly spongy, so you can still blaze through zones on the retread and then you just have a tougher boss that demands stronger execution of the skills you've built up - no issues imo, love it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice "Bloodborne at home".Developers haven't simply checked all boxes for a "modern Soulslike game" (although, quite a lot of game design decisions look like they were made just because "you gotta"), they truly brought some new ideas, some of them quite bold, like the weapon assembly system or attacks that completely ignore i-frames.But of course, if you have played Souls/Bloodborne/Elden Ring you would notice a myriad of direct borrowings from there, some of them almost outrageously straightforward, like "talk to coughing people behind closed windows", "very nimble swordswoman that undresses in the second phase, calls herself a sharp-edged weapon of some other person and has some infuriating combo-attacks", "character named Manus that has an enormous hand" and so on and so on. It is not bad per se, it's just... Confusing?But all of these strange things aside, that's a solid and VERY polished game that is fun to play, intriguing to listen to and is generally well done.Nice job, guys, looking forward to that teased sequel :)
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: Lies of P is probably one of the best (if not the best) SoulsLike there is.I have heard many people complaining about that characteristic, stating that it is almost plagiarizing From Software but I have to disagree. Many games have tried to tread the line of trying to incorporate many elements from different SoulsBorne games, but I think Lies of P manages to take the best from every game while adding its own spin to it.The developers are still working on the game and taking feedback from players, and while obviously some of the flaws won't be addressed, they have listened to our voices and adjusted Boss health and damage scaling and other QOL issues. With a DLC and more games of the same "Expanded Universe" I am really hopeful that the few things can be improved will be worked on, to give us a trully unforgettable experience.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often write reviews for games. If there was ever a game worthy of it, Lies of P would fit the bill. As a huge souls-like fan, this game scratches every itch. Engaging and complex combat. An interesting and wonderful world to explore. A heavier emphasis on story than most other souls games. It is rather linear, which i believe to be a positive, allowing the story to unfold exactly the way the developers had intended. To many, this game will be perceived as "Hard" and "Difficult", they are not wrong. The parry mechanic is something to get used to, especially if you are coming in with expectations from other souls games. However, once you get the grasp of the combat, a true feel for it, there isn't anything quite like it. The element of "Git-Gud" resonates through this game. Once you have, a far greater appreciation for the overall combat can be had. The bosses in particular are memorable and interesting. After sometimes several attempts, you can learn some of their move sets. The feeling of perfectly parrying their combos is just straight up addictive. After playing through this game 3 times already, I have no doubt it will be a journey that I come back to time and time again. Each time I walk through those train station doors, the words that come to mind are, "Another fine day in the city of Krat!". I am ecstatic to see what will come from NEOWIZ in the future, especially with the upcoming DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: simultaneously the most forgiving and yet difficult take on the genre I've ever seen: The game wants you to parry, and it gets very exacting with the timing very quickly, but there's so much QoL stuff and polish on top that it's hard to feel mad about when I botch a parry and get summarily comboed to bits. _childDocuments_.review: The combat of this game will be familiar to most people who've played any of From Software's soulslikes, it blends a mix of Bloodborne and Sekiro to create something that can stand on it's own.Neowiz added their own flavour to the combat with the ability to mix and match weapon blades/handles to create unique weapons with differing movesets and stat scaling.The legion arm adds further combat customisation in allowing you to have devices such as a grappling hook, flamethrower, lightning fist, etc. The fable arts that are tied to weapons are their own spin on weapon arts from DS3 and skills from ER, but in my opinion they have much more impact than those games.The only real negatives I would say about the combat is, sometimes hitting a block sounds and looks the same as hitting a perfect block which can be confusing in the heat of the battle when you aren't expecting to take damage. The other problem is that dodge feels mostly useless until you get the upgrade that lets you dodge a second time in succession, thankfully it's fairly quick to get it.I've played most soulslikes that have come out over the years and enjoyed a lot of them, but Lies of P feels like the first game to truly capture the essence From Software brings with exploration in their games. While this is very linear in that there's really only one path of progression, it still has the very satisfying shortcuts to lead back to rest spots and items hidden in hard to see paths.One of the things I love about From Software games is piecing together the story of the world through exploration and item descriptions.This game does it very well by following the same ways of discovering story in both item descriptions and npc dialogue.I don't think the writing is as well done, but it's still great.My only real complaints is if you pay attention, especially in the first few areas, they tried to make the city look more dense with lots of buildings but they are the same bakery and book store repeated throughout. While this is really a minor issue it does show a lack of attention to detail in some regards.Oh boy.. I suck at gank fights, absolutely suck at them. But once I learnt that you can perfect block to break even bosses weapons, the game opened up quite a lot for me. I would say most of the bosses are extremely well designed and have beautiful set pieces with very cool attacks.The difficulty at first was quite rough as it takes a bit to get used to how tight the perfect block timing is, but once I did it got a fair bit easier. There were a few bosses I still struggled with but I was trying to go a heavy chungus weapon build at first which I was finding I wasn't able to follow up on staggers fast enough. After a while I swapped to a lighter weapon and again found the game go a lot smoother for me.For those that want it, most of the major bosses in the game allow you to summon an AI companion to help you in the fight.In a 2023 miracle, this game ran exceptionally well. I never dropped below 150 fps with all settings maxed and DLSS on Quality. Quite often I would hit my refresh rate cap (240hz) in doors which made the gameplay feel a lot smoother.The game itself is quite beautiful and there we many moments where I would stop to take in the scenery.Overall I'd say this game is a must buy for any soulslike fans, or even check it out on gamepass if you have it. It's by far my favourite game of the year so far and I'm excited to see if the devs make DLC or a new game similar.

_childDocuments_.review: A very difficult thumbs down here because the theme, story, customisation and fresh ideas are absolutely fantastic.The blaring problem is the unforgiving perfect block chance when enemy attacks are already too random to the point where you have no idea what they are going to do. They either have a delayed attack that lasts 5+ seconds, causing you to stand there like an idiot and wait for a perfect guard, or they attack in .2 of a second. Normal blocks reduce your damage taken and give you a chance to recover it back, but most of the time you get hit by something else to negate your recovery. Yes you can dodge attacks and use items, but blocking is highly prioritised so you can stagger and do serious damage. On top of that, some enemies lock you into combos that seem like you can get out of them or block follow up attacks and when you desperately try to, you can't. Instead they will often just kill you and it's insulting. I do not want to be repeatedly bashed into the ground with a shovel because I failed to dodge or guard a common attack.The combat needs to be more refined for me to consider playing it again. It has great moments, but for the most part it just feels clunky and awkward at this stage.

_childDocuments_.review: Being the first attempt from this company on making a souls-like game, this is very well crafted and works incredibly well.I bought it in pre-purchase and had no problems whatsoever thrugh the entirety of my playthrough. I liked the story and NPCs with their stories, which is overall way more explained and understandable compared with Fromsoft titles.The combat is also very enjoyable, all enemies have understandable attack which and the variety is enough but not overwhelming so in time you'll start to become more and more capable to deal with them.Also becoming a master with parry is king here, if you put the effort to pull often perfect parry you'll feel very good and it will help you succeed.Certain bosses are very hard, no joke but it feels good when you overcome them.Also I like the customes and the Arm - Weapon Combination is a very interesting choice for sure, and deaths are more forgiving than traditional Dark Souls which is a plus for me.There are though some areas of improvement, and the best part for devs is that you could make an easy check list to keep in mind for the sequel. An example could be that certain attacks are a bit cheesy or simply too fast for the general pace of the game, or the skill tree could be more refined to have additional interesting choices, also the mix and match weapon system could be more interesting and favor veriety rather than raw-power.Certain maps are very cool to exsplore but in the end the game is quite linear like zone1 -zone2 and so on with a central hub where you find all npcs. I like a central hub but I hope in the sequel for something more like Dark Souls1 in terms of zones connection with more freedom to go around.Overall, I think a 7 to 8 / 10.

_childDocuments_.review: I was buying this game to get a discount Fromsoft game, but what I found instead was truly special in ways I did not expect.Lies of P wears its inspirations on its sleeve, so it is easy to assume that many people who think about buying the game (and reading this review as a result) want to play something like Bloodborne and are contemplating if they should buy this one.This review is for people like that. I have 100%ed every FromSoft game including Bloodborne, so the described experience might be completely different for a new player to the genre.Let's cut to the chase - I think Lies of P is a much better game than Bloodborne. Before you leave a clown award on this review, please give me a moment to explain.Before we start, it is important to note that I absolutely love Bloodborne. But, in my opinion, people really tend to overhype it for what it is. The main game Bloodborne has 2 or 3 good bosses with literally every other boss being "strafe right hit R1". Bosses like Paarl died without me even understanding what just happened. Lies of P avoids this issue completely, and nearly every single boss (with a single exception, looking at you Chapter 10 gang) feels amazing to fight.It scratches the same itch as good Sekiro bosses do. You get into this flow state where you can parry attack after attack and it just feels incredible. Bosses in Lies of P rarely die on a first attempt. Game really demands you to learn the attack pattern of each boss and perform well throughout the whole fight.If you are a newer player I think Bloodborne will be a much better starting point. Lies of P is rough. I would even go as far as to say that this is the hardest souls-like game I’ve ever played. But as usual, you have your options. Summoning NPCs to draw boss aggro away, using absolutely busted throwables, or a shield-hand will make the experience a ton easier if you are looking to tone down difficulty a notch.While the level design in Bloodborne might be less linear, it kinda feels homogenized to me. The entirety of Yahrnam just feels the same, I can't name any non-DLC area that isn't a city or a forest. At the same time each area in Lies of P feels distinct to me. It might be more linear, but level design is equally as great. A bunch of nooks and crannies to explore, secrets to find and shortcuts to open.One of the biggest issues I have with Bloodborne that this game avoids is the lack of gameplay variety. Sure, trick weapons are cool and all, but not being able to change your build to try out new weapons funnels you into using just a couple of weapons during your entire playthrough. You don't get enough upgrade materials to upgrade some random weapon on a whim and play with it for a while.Both of these issues combined resulted in me playing the entirety of Bloodborne start to finish with a cane-whip thing because it felt like the most effective weapon at nearly all times. Sure, I might’ve found something better along the way, but I couldn’t risk spending precious upgrade materials to check out the weapon at its full potential. Lies of P is extremely generous with weapon upgrade materials but strikes a perfect balance where you wouldn’t be able to upgrade everything under the sun immediately either.While might not seem important, it’s the little things that add up during the playtime that decide your overall enjoyment of the game. For example, the fast travel system in Bloodborne is horrible, zones are split into different fast-travel objects with no images attached to names of locations, and sometimes it's infuriating to try and remember which place was which. I don’t even have to mention the fact that healing items not replenishing on rest.Lies of P, on top of improving everything I just mentioned also goes the extra mile by having a bunch of QoL stuff, like training dummies in the hub to check your weapon damage and movesets, tells you when a certain NPC wants to talk to you, and reminds you where you picked up that quest you just completed so you don't have to teleport around the entire game trying to remember who wanted this bottle of wine you just found.Both games have great stories, but I liked the story for Lies of P more. This point is completely subjective though, more so than everything else. Characters in Lies of P were interesting enough for me to come back to Hotel Krat to listen to what they had to say each time a new dialogue became available. There’s just something so magical about the Hotel, the music, the ambiance, I just can’t get enough of it.At this point it might sound like I just hate Bloodborne, but no, not at all. I think it was a brilliant game, but isn't a gift from gaming Gods that many people make it out to be.Is Lies of P without faults? Of course no. Some of the boss attacks aren't clearly telegraphed, the difficulty balancing can use more work. The endgame is rough with chapter 10's gank boss absolutely sucking and climbing the tower in the end being rather tedious. However, these issues don't stop the game from being absolutely fantastic in my opinion.Overall, I don't think most people would ever agree that this game is better than Bloodborne simply because of how iconic Bloodborne has become over the years. But for me Lies of P is so much more. Such a beautiful game, really didn't expect it to be this great when I was buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: The key to a good game of this style is fairness in its cruelness.  The game is never fair.  My main complaint is the stagger mechanic and lack of i-frames in your fable attacks.  You get all these cool abilities, along with the ability to perform fatal attacks, but they are all TRAPS.  End game bosses will blast right through any attempt to use your fable attacks, wasting them.  Charging to try and get a stagger...dream on.  It all comes down to luck to see if the bosses will decide to be merciful when it reads your inputs.The fights end up being a chore with trying to perfect parry for 90% of the time, to get two swings off.  Also this means the game favors fast weapons versus the cooler large slower weapons.  I couldn't imagine trying to use something slow against Nameless Puppet.Otherwise mini boss enemies are just unrelenting damage soaks that just become a chore to defeat.Overall, game ambiance is great, story is better and more defined than most soullikes.  Music is A+++.  But the combat system makes this a solid do not recommend until either implementing a better dodge roll, or some kind of enemy stagger that stops them from being non-stop swinging whirlwinds of death and destruction.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a love letter to Bloodborne, and it shows - not just in the combat or the aesthetics, but also in the many references scattered throughout the game. These guys have done an excellent job replicating many of the successful systems of Fromsoft games, which means the gameplay is pretty fantastic. However, this isn't anything new.The real novelty for this game lies in its concept - you literally play as Pinocchio, from the fairy tale, seeking to save  Krat from a horde of demonic puppets. I don't want to spoil much, but let's just say there is some thought provoking commentary on the nature of human consciousness in the age of artificial intelligence.I finished NG at around 25 hours. Well worth the $40 sale price I paid.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely  this game. This is my favorite souls-like game to date, and honestly the level of polish of this game is comparable, if not on par, with some of From's finest works.Despite the fact that I'm no stranger to souls flavor combat, having finished the Dark Souls trilogy/Bloodborne/Elden Ring,  that I'm playing the game after various patches and improvements for combat have been introduced, I still got my ass handed to me so many times during this game--almost all of which, I should add, are very much fair fights. Nearly every time I fall to a boss, I will know exactly what mistake I made, and why I failed. It's a tremendous task to make boss fights difficult but still fair, and Neowiz had done an absolutely phenomenal job with their designs. What I particularly enjoyed about the combat system is the sheer flexibility of it: from the weapon assembly system to general approach to encounters, this is truly following the Souls' spirit of "use anything that will help you survive", and perhaps even more effectively implemented to a degree, just by its obligatory melee style and the sheer enemy difficulty. As I got deeper into the game, I found myself actively seeking out different play styles and strategies, utilizing all my resources, trying out all the weapon arts and attacks, learning to rely on something other than dodges... Because my old tricks that carried me through all the Souls games no longer suffice. I'm once again presented with challenges above my current skills, and I have to work  to overcome these obstacles. Nearly all the endgame bosses got my heart racing like I'm facing the Fume Knight or Nameless King once again, and that. Is. AWESOME.The level design is also fantastic. It's no DS1 (but let's face it, DS1 is going to be one of its kind for a long, long time), but the shortcuts placements, enemy allocations, and the developer's clear mindfulness of player attrition are outstanding. This is a game that has been tested and played extensively, and all the balancing efforts are very clear even to a lay person like me.Oh, and did I mention the art direction? The costumes, the weapons, the art pieces, the general atmosphere--gorgeous. Just absolutely gorgeous. And the music... oh the music. Let me just tell you, that first time I listened to the record in Hotel Krat reminded me of my first encounter with Gwyn. I still get goosebumps just thinking about it. I also love how each record's description is a small story all onto itself--I got teary eyed many times just reading them.I can go on for days just to pour out my absolute adoration for this game, but if you're a Souls like enthusiast, or just a fan of ARPGs in general, you should definitely give this game a shot. It will not disappoint.

_childDocuments_.review: A very worthy edition to the Souls-like canon, with possibly the best feeling combat of any I've yet played outside of the actual FromSoft games. It's probably closest to Sekiro in terms of pace and aggression, with a focus on parry timing and dodging over blocking and tanking. Tons of weapons to play with, and that's before you start to mess with a very cool system of mixing and matching blades and hilts to create bespoke ones to suit your build/preferences. I did ultimately end up using a boss weapon for most of my playthrough, but I still appreciated the smorgasbord of stabbing, slashing, and crushing implements served up to me.The Legion Arm system was a fun addition, calling to mind Sekiro's Ninja Tools by providing combat tricks at the expense of limited ammunition. That said, I did rely almost entirely on the Puppet String, the first Legion Arm given to you, as none of the other options ever really seemed to match up to the simple utility of pulling an enemy to me or me to the enemy.The setting is very well realised, making great use of the  styling in the nebulously-European city of Krat. The costumes are excellent, for the Fashion-Souls enjoyers, though I would have liked the option to mix and match outfit pieces. I will offer the mild criticism that the game is very linear, with levels mostly boiling down to being a corridor to the next boss fight with a few short diversions along the way. There's none of the sense of connection between areas of Krat that you would find in Yharnam, to use the obvious point of comparison.Finally, you can pet the cat. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a small miracle. It's a wonder that this team from South Korea made such a polished souls-like game their first try. They somehow managed to exhibit more insight and understanding of what makes souls-like games tick than nearly any other game in the genre. This game could stand on its own and compete with the FromSoftware games. Perhaps the most remarkable thing about it is the atmosphere and the distinct sense of style. The world and the characters that inhabit it are dripping. It has the design maturity of a TV show that's in its second or third season and just coming into its own. The most comparable game to it aesthetically might be Bloodborne. The aesthetics are different but they are the same in having achieved a profound and unique artistic vision that shines through every aspect of the game, from the world and character design to the soundtrack and just the cohesive unity of the story, world, and game play.  The art direction, level and boss designs are very creative and compelling. I wasn't expecting the story to be anything great, but not only is the story pretty good, it unexpectedly got me in the feels!This style and atmosphere could not have been achieved by merely copying an art style or graphics from another game (as some people suggest). Both Bloodborne and Lies of P achieve their characteristic style from their creators' unique visions.  The same could be said about the combat mechanics. Although it unabashedly borrows from the games that inspired it, no mere copy/pasting could have produced the expertly unified mechanics it takes from Sekiro, Dark Souls, Bloodborne, etc.  It manages to be both derivative and uniquely its own thing at the same time - a mark of originality!I look forward to whatever these guys do next in this genre because they have proven that they have the spark of inspired game design.

_childDocuments_.review: I am so happy to see this game where it is at. This has been one of the games I was waiting for years to play and was really not disappointing once it released. The demo got me scared since the dodge mechanic needed some work but it was fixed!This game has really grasped what makes a souls like a souls like. By all means it is not perfect, there are improvements to be made such as way too many 2 phase boss fights and to many recurring "obstacles" like bridges going to break under you.BUT the combat... HOLY SCHMOLY. It does take a minute to get used to but it feels like the perfect bacon after you get the hang of it, nice and crispy. I am so excited to see where this takes us with neowiz and I am really hoping that DLC or a new souls like game from them comes soon.

_childDocuments_.review: My Game of the Year without hesitation. Magnificent, with immersive gameplay, a dark atmosphere that will make you feel lonely and desperate in a nihilistic world that is not without reminding our current times, where technology has destroyed society. While dystopic games often fall into clichés, Lies of P surprised me many times, making the experience less linear and more organic.As for the gameplay, I don't know why some people say this is harder than Elden Ring. I personally found it less difficult; if you choose a weapon specialization, it's extremely fair. The variety of mechanics make the fights satisfying, and the bosses are quite interesting and different from one another.I didn't know NEOWIZ & Round8 Studio before playing this game and I will be sure to keep an eye on their work. Hugely talented developers. Thanks a ton for offering us this gem of a game. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: Looking back on games from the past decade, this is one of the few games that truly captivated me and challenged me to the extent that I was invested in every piece of world-building dialogue and would constantly look at the wiki for more insight on the game's mechanics. Bloodborne is probably my favorite video game of all time and this game doesn't just pay homage to Bloodborne, it took the baton and is holding it up high 8 years later. This game takes that Lovecraftian, Cosmic Horror genre and twist it into something new. It pulls you into a universe that will both frighten and excite you. Every detail of this game is incredible. This game developed a formula for copying all of the best parts of the Souls-like genre and added its own variables that we didn't even know we were missing. The dynamic between parrying and dodging is much more engaging than simply just dodging or holding a shield out in front of you. And I do think the gun parrying from Bloodborne was a bit tricky to get a hang of and didn't really work against the larger bosses. The Quartz system makes the game feel more like a traditional RPG were you're really advancing through victories and exploration, rather than just clicking 'Level up' until the game is over. The weapon system is immaculate and I have a feeling, with the new update coming out this month, that there will be so many viable options in the creative space they provided with this system. The music is beautiful and honestly I actually sat there and listened to pretty much all of the records for like an hour straight. The main bosses are almost all 9/10s. None of them quite as hard as Orphan of Kos or Mikaela, but they are all consistently difficult (with the exception of a small handful). The characters are dynamic and interesting and the story is wonderful - And it's given to you up-front. No need to scour YouTube essays explaining the tiny scraps of environmental story-telling that were given to you throughout the 40-hour play through. But the story is still deep and even after playing the game multiple times you will catch things that you didn't notice prior that will surprise you. Overall, I would seriously recommend this game to any Souls-like veteran or anyone who wants to try a Souls game that has a bit more showmanship than the originals.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played many non-FromSoft soulslike games, but this is definitely the best one I've played so far. I have some nitpicks, like why arent we allowed to level up at the stargazers through most of the game, why Fable isnt recharged at stargazers, why grab attacks arent properly telegraphed, and other small things like animations being a bit odd and the parry timing being a bit weird to get down a lot of the time as a result. Overall these things are pretty inconsequential and I imagine smallstuff like this getting ironed out in the sequel if it happens. Difficulty isn't too bad in my opinion, there was no boss I was stuck on for any considerable length of time. I am playing post-nerf cause apparently a number of bosses got nerfed, so that may be a factor. Progression is very good in the early game with rapid level ups, but slows to a crawl in the late game. Overall I had a very good time with this game, especially once I got the Twin Dragons sword, that thing's special parry attack saved my butt so much in the late game and it made me feel like a god when I pulled off risky parries, shutting down a boss's entire combo string. Using that with the puppet string made me feel amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game, but not the god-sent Bloodborne II people are making it out to be (so far). A bit easier than From's games as well; I've died three times (again, so far), once to a boss and twice to clutter that wasn't breakable, and I'm past the third boss. So make of that what you will.In terms of the new mechanics, I've not used them too much, but the ability to 'augment' (for lack of a better word) P with new abilities is nice, and looks like it has a lot of potential. I also like the addition of a 'shinobi prosthetic', to help diversify builds and play-styles.One gripe I have (and this may change as I get deeper) is a general lack of enemy variety; most common enemies look very similar, and their attack patterns are almost identical, with some few exceptions. As annoying as ranged enemies might be, fighting the same enemy repeatedly is just boring. The bosses and minibosses are fine and all, but the stuff between them can be kinda meh. Again, I do recommend the game, but don't go in expecting it to be better than if it came out of FromSoftware. Easily, Lies of P is one of the best soulsborne games from another studio, but it does lack a bit of that Miyazaki flair.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and interesting game brought down by a terribly restrictive combat system.Because it has unreliable clunky controls that lock the player into actions without the ability to frame cancel, as well as an incredibly punishing parry system coupled with enemy combos that ceaselessly stretch and interrupt, one is forced to learn fight patterns and parry with only few viable attack windows to exploit. This makes most fights an uninspired slog. Even basic enemies feel like fighting an 8-bit era boss where pattern recognition is forced on you. Parry, parry, parry, attack. Parry, parry, parry, attack. Wash, rinse, repeat... It isn't overly difficult, just claustrophobic and boring. With so many weapon combinations and abilities it would serve the experience far better to have a more fluid combat system that allowed for more creative exploration.A shame really, as the game is close to masterpiece levels of execution on everything else. The story is a delightful combination of Isaac Asimov's I, Robot mixed with a fable from Brothers Grimm. The customisation is deep and rewarding. The art style and music are gorgeous with an immersive quality rarely found. For the sequel hopefully the combat mechanics can become as refined as the time period the game emulates.*Edit: It gets by on style and depth. Having now beat the game, I really did enjoy the characters, story, and immersive setting. The teaser at the end hinting where the franchise is headed just nudged it over the edge of a negative review into a positive one. That said, the control scheme really is disappointing. I would prefer even more difficult enemy encounters with unrestricted combat if it meant not playing checkers while the enemy plays chess. Having to choose whether to attack, parry, or heal while an enemy unhindered by environment, sluggish animations or stamina requirements slashes your face gets old fast. In the end, I cared enough about the characters and what happened to them to power through the entire game. As such, I have to give the experience a passing grade.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm paranoid every time I see treasure now.Such a great game. Fun combat system that feels very tight. Difficulty feels very well-scalled throughout the game. Lots of interesting and unique weapons. Sometimes, it feels like the game lacks in "standard" enemy diversity. They make up for this by creating lots of different scenarios & environment to keep you on your toes. This game also LOVES to throw constant curveballs, both in gameplay and story! Such a well-crafted experience, I just wish I had more! Lies of P is very much worth the price. Great job.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a phenomenal game. A true masterpiece. And it most certainly deserves your attention if you are in any way interested in the "souls-like" genre. This may be a hard pill to swallow for some, but in many regards I think this game just raised the bar for FromSoft... you know, the pioneers of the genre!The environments seem to be inspired by the Batman Arkham series, Resident Evil 4, Bloodborne, and Dark Souls. The gameplay is truly exceptional. The combat is incredibly engaging, satisfying, and punishing at the same time. This game not only understands the elements of the genre, but also innovates and adds its own twists, substantially augmenting and elevating the experience in the process. I think this game stands heads and shoulders above all other souls-likes (Ashen, Thymesia, etc.). If someone told me FromSoft made this, I would be inclined to believe them! That is a monumental achievement for Neowiz.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw the trailer for Lies of P, I didn't really think much of it. The idea of a Soulsborne game set in the world of Pinocchio seemed very far fetched and wacky. But to my surprise, the game was well made and I found myself enjoying it a lot. The combat is nice, and the addition of being able to swap your weapon's blades and handles opens up plenty of room for experimentation. If your a fan of Dark Souls and Bloodborne, I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is Amazing, if you are looking for a souls like with atmosphere, solemn music, relatively versatile combat, and a pretty clear story line, but is still different from your typical from soft game, this is the way to go. I can't explain how excited I was for this game to come out because of having perfect blocks, and all the other different mechanics it introduced into the combat system that allowed you to adapt to enemies. Even from the demo, there was never a time where I felt that the bosses were repetitive so there was almost no one combat style fits all for the whole game. While it does borrow mechanics from Blood borne in terms of propagating a more aggressive play style, you will slowly but surely learn that not all bosses can be approached in the same manner, and it will take some time to learn their attack patterns, so at least for me when reaching end game patience was KEY, meanwhile in the beginning it wasn't as much of a worry. Overall a damn amazing game that kept me enthralled throughout my verging on 60 hours of game play, and definitely something that any souls like fan who isn't afraid to fail should try. Can't wait to see more amazing games from this studio.

_childDocuments_.review: This is genuinely 10 times better than I expected it to be. I have been pleasantly surprised by almost every aspect of this game. It's beautiful, the concept is weird but works, the combat feels responsive and solid, and the bosses are varied enough and have interesting designs. There are only two things that I am not so fond of: parries and dodging. Parries don't feel rewarding enough; I can get 10 perfect parries in a row and am not rewarded with a riposte. That seems odd, and the timing is pretty tight. As for dodging, it's by no means bad, but I'm often left wondering why the quickstep doesn't move P further. Maybe I'm too much of a Bloodborne fanboy. In any case, this game is great fun, and I genuinely think it's the best souls-inspired game to date. I think it's worth the full price, but if you're skeptical, don't hesitate to pick it up when it goes on sale.* EDIT *Now that I've beaten the game, my thoughts have changed a bit. Lies of P is absolutely amazing! Round8 has made a true final boss that is up there with some of my favorites that From has put out. I won't spoil it. It was so nice to see so many souls-borne references littered throughout this game, from bosses and their attacks to weapons to level design—really well done. On another note, the music is just so appropriate for the atmosphere of this game. Feel is such a great song to hear at Hotel Krat. I sat and listened to it more than a dozen times in my play-through.As for my original critiques, quicksteps work fine, and my problem was mainly visual, so that went away with time. Ripostes are simply not a big part of this game, so don't expect to get them too often. Perhaps that makes them more exciting when they do happen. Also, this game feels much harder than most Souls games. That may be because it's new, but as for now, I would say returning to this game, as I certainly will, will see me dying to more areas and bosses than everything except Bloodborne if I include chalice dungeons. I am very excited for the DLC/sequel that is teased upon completion. Buy it, don't quit.

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the best game released this year. In my opinion this is the closest thing to Bloodborne II that we have been asking for. _childDocuments_.review: Not only one of the best Souls-like game ever, but one of the best games of the year. After three complete playthroughs and finishing NewGame++, I have loved every minute (no matter how frustrating some of these bosses can be...) The challenge is rewarding, different weapons offer different playstyles - not to mention the ability to mix-and-match weapon heads and handles, unlocks a whole world of possibilities. The voice acting is phenomenal, and the story is moving. The gothic world building is beautifully executed. Very much looking forward to DLC or sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Lies of P is polished and extremely well made and optimized on a technical level; it looks absolutely amazing and it runs extremely smoothly and well, with minimal drops in frame rate even during things like large explosions that would cause most games to drop frames.But on a gameplay level, Lies of P is very much Bloodborne with a bit of Sekiro thrown in, and the story is mostly just Pinocchio Bloodborne in Belle Epoque France. The gameplay and story don't have a ton that's very new or interesting to offer people who have seen FromSoft's games, so the question of whether it'll be worth the asking price is mostly just: "Do you want a polished but somewhat unoriginal Soulslike?"If you're fine with a less original game with a good level of polish, you'll like this. If you're looking for a Soulslike that does something new, this will probably be pretty milquetoast. Ultimately I did enjoy my time with it but kinda forgot half this game pretty soon after putting it down, and don't think I'll replay it too much or too soon. I would ultimately give it a recommendation if you like Soulslikes though.

_childDocuments_.review: I am revisiting my review after playing ng+ and ng++ and replayed the game to ng and ng+ second time. I played each update from the start. Saying that this game is like incredibly good. Before updates their was alot of complaints about difficulty but even before the updates the game was incredibly fair and always gave you tools you needed to fight any boss let that be a Electric type of weapon to deal damage on puppet types or throwables to deal with gank fights. The boss roster is incredibly strong as well with i think outside of sekiro might have the best boss line up quality wise in souls games in general. Very fun combat loop as well with parrying/blocking and dodging.But you might be wondering what makes this game stick out  compared to other games like darksouls or bloodborne. Besides its more Bioshock like aesthetic its very linear in level design which is really up to you if you dislike that or not since i believe some people might enjoy linear and less confusing/Convoluted layout (and i know a decent amount of people have been turned off by the souls series for being as confusing/convoluted and this is a great game for people who want to play a souls game but not get a headache and need a wiki to find stuff) It also has alot of good QOL (from elevators resetings to tell you when you can level up by turning your ergo blue their just alot of good QOL that doesnt make it a hassle) and brings a unique weapon system i haven't seen in a souls game which is a combo system for handle and blades. Blades are the damage/attack type/ Elemental/ and range/speed with each blade having its own fable art. While the handle defines the attack animation and has its own fable arts and their around 29 Handles and blades that are all interchangeable. Their also weapons that are 1 piece which are boss weapons are their really fun to play from a sekiro like sword to the range of puppet ripper. Their so many weapon choices that really its up to you to find your favorite and stick with it lol. The story is also really good but does suffer from some meh translation but most of it is fine just 1 off issues here and their. the ost is really good. Like REALLY good from the boss OST to the music discs you can collect. Lies of P has alot going for it. If you enjoyed Sekiro and or bloodborne combat i 100% recommend this game to you! If your wanting to get in to souls games and couldn't really get in to dark souls i recommend you try lies of P as it easily one of the more casual takes on the souls genre thanks to alot of its quirks.

_childDocuments_.review: This might just be the best non-FromSoft soulslike out there. The core combat mechanics are rock solid and consistent, the additional layers on top like weapon customisation, skill tree and legion arms are all excellent and interact with one another well. Art direction is likewise top tier, meshing the puppet theme seamlessly with Gothic horror.I knew all that coming in and was not disappointed, but what I didn't expect is the story to be so well thought out. It's a perfect mix of immediately engaging intrigue, nuggets of hidden lore waiting for you to find, and clever tie ins to the original, also very brutal, Pinocchio story by Carlo Collodi.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad that I decided to do some catching up on my Steam library. Otherwise, this great game would continue to collect dust without the chance it deserves. Bloodborne at home vibes, except, not really when you get into it. Lies of P is unique enough to have its own identity. I found the story engaging to the point that it spoilt my mood when I went for the "bad ending". The "good" one is rather bitter-sweet but it still was a nice change after the former.As for the actual gameplay, it's snappy and satisfying. The deflections are quite reminiscent of Sekiro. There are several systems on top of regular combat which create a decently complex and cohesive whole. While the game is very linear, there are opportunities to do some rewarding exploration. There is also a fun mechanic that allows assembly of weapons from two parts - for example, you can take a greatsword's blade and stick it on a dagger's handle, and this has big gameplay impact. Unlike FromSoftware games, Lies of P has more meaningful NG+ cycles (at least up to NG+2), where additional character progression opens up.Personally, I didn't find any boss music to be very memorable, which is a shame, however, there were still good pieces sprinkled here and there. You should also watch out when the game tries to kick you into NG+ as you might want to do some things to wrap up the ongoing playthrough.All in all, I regret not playing it sooner. This might be the most polished Souls-like out there.
