_childDocuments_.review: I will start saying that this game slowly grew up on me. I didn't enjoy every session I played, because it's a very hard game. My own frustration was a bigger part on this more than the game's shortcomings. Sometimes it actually was unfair, even though the game teaches you to be on your toes at all times. But most of the time it only felt unfair. And that was because I was just not familiarized enough with the game's mechanics. So here're some tips to enjoy the game:1. DON'T rush it. Let your brain learn its foundations well, because even when there's new stuff coming at you, there's always way to respond that has already been taught. 2. Take breaks. Trying too hard in this game will be the end of your enjoyment and patience.3. If you feel frustrated when you are about to play I would recomend to play or do something else.4. I would really recomend to take your time with bosses, even if you die many times, because there's no greater feeling than overcoming the challenge. Not every boss is great, but there are many that are good and some that are excellent. There's an effort to be made in order to not compare it to the souls-like series (which is inevitable for the many things it borrows or even exactly copies from them) there's a very rewarding and beautiful experience behind.Now try it for yourself and have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I don't go out of my way to review uh...anything. Literally the only 3 reviews I've ever done on this account in 13+ years on steam are joke Batman reviews when I was drunk.So Lies of P. It's good. Hell, it's great. I'm not gonna do some lame copy paste review of it's graphics and ♥♥♥♥. Lemme just tell you what's good and what's not so good.Combat's great. It's bloodborne with some Sekiro sprinkled on top. Yes you have to perfect parry. Yes the perfect parry window is 2 frames and that's not a lot. Yes there are other ways to achieve a perfect parry like fable arts (Special moves). Yes your dodge does still have iframes. Be aware you can and SHOULD dodge sometimes and space yourself away from some attacks. You don't need to perfect parry everything and in fact you shouldn't.The game also has a lot of interesting combat ideas, like being able to break apart weapons and re-attach the blade to a different handle to give a weapon the damage/speed of the blade, but the scaling and moveset of the handle. I am disappointed this idea ended up pointless in my run because the boss weapons are OP and not able to be broken apart, but perhaps that's an area to re-examine in the future. I -also- enjoyed being able to adjust the scaling on weapons. That was a super interesting mechanic. Instead of some weapons just fundamentally being better because they were graced with S scaling, you can adjust how a weapon scales by 1 level (From like B to A or A to S)Story is really good too. Thankfully not as spread out over 10,000 item descriptions like in FromSoft, though some plot points could probably have used more explaination, like why the Puppet Frenzy actually happened. But it's got enough intrigue to make me go to the next area to figure out wtf is going on, and if you're aware of the original Pinnochio text you'll recognize a lot of the names and references too. Voice acting is hit or miss. I like MOST of the character and MOST of the dialogue. And then there's Gemini. I do not understand why Gemini is here. We're in a dark, miserable, desperate place on the last edge of hope and he's just kind of weirdly lighthearted and goofy, to literally no payoff. Why did he mention losing memories? Why were we told he'd grow with us? Absolutely do nothing character that could have been left as a lamp.Music and graphics are good, I'm not really a great judge of that but it does look and sound nice. Find an audio engineer or someone who cares about graphics for that I guess.Exploration is a bit lackluster, the game is decently linear and any alternate paths you take will fairly quickly end up as a dead end with a few items. There are some secrets strewn about, but after getting to the final boss I found I only missed 3 things total, which is surprising for a game like this. I could probably boot up DS3 right now and find a weapon or item or path I've just never found before.So is it good? Yes, it absolutely is.

_childDocuments_.review: ---note my review is bias due to my experience with dark souls games/franchise.---Put very simple: Awesome story, Extremely soul-like and I mean that in a good way. I'm a big fan of the dark and twisted spin they put on the well known story of pinocchio. The new story really adds to the experience as it let's you enjoy the soul-like gameplay in a refreshing new way. So in a sense, you get to enjoy 2 things at the same time that is old already known, (the story of pinocchio and soul-like gameplay), and experience them as brand new. Therefor, I would rate the story and gameplay as following:Story: 8,5/10    Gameplay: 9/10 The story and Gameplay gets a -1 due to some aspects of the game design which leaves me a bit wanting. The story also gets a -0,5 from me since, while it was great it was not perfect. Simply put without spoilers I wanted a bit more details/story telling than what we got. The ending was really good but a bit more elaboration further onto the climax/plot twist would have been very nice.Game design: 7/10-1: If you are a hardened soul-franchise player like me, this game is rather easy. Only the optional final boss was a bit of a challenge. Also, the game is too forgiving with checkpoints. Meaning, in dark souls you usually have to fight your way through a range of enemies to reach a boss, and then fight the boss with what ressources you have left from your last checkpoint. However, in this game you will almost always recieve a checkpoint right at the entrance to the boss.-1: You can only customize your appearance cosmeticly, meaning you don't get varies sets of armor to choose from and select in slots like head, body, arms and legs. You do though get many different and cool full body costumes to choose from with 2 slots beside the full body, hat/mask and face(glasses and such).-1: There is pretty much no way to fight ranged. There is no archery or magic in this game, which means you can only fight as a melee class. There are different melee fighting styles though, but all in all I miss a bit more variety to choose from.Summary:All in all, I really enjoyed this game and I can't wait for the DLC and sequel. Very excited for what comes next.

_childDocuments_.review: The game combines many mechanics from other souls type games and add some nice and interesting new ideas into the formula that I hope to see more in the future of the genre, however there is a reason the different mechanics were not in separate game previously. The perfect block, block and dodging mechanics all being equally stressed makes boss designs a bit harder to balance especially when this is a linear game (in other souls like if you feel stuff you are usually able to go somewhere else to grow if needed or desired)The lack of an ability to see how far we have raised an enemy's stagger bar makes perfect blocks feel weak and even when getting the groggy indicator, bosses may be in a combo making it impossible to land a fully charged heavy attack, making fights feel stolen from the player. They should have made it so we could see this bar rise are we damage and block and once filled just have them be open for a critical hit without needing to do a heavy attack.Secondly, in sekiro they have a separate bar from the players HP that rises when mistiming a block to allow for the player to learn more during attempts. Additionally, the perfect block from my tests (which may be flawed but did the best I could) looks to be 5 frames long when looking at footage back, if I blocked 1 to 5 from before a hit, I perfect blocked, if I did 6 or more frame early, I blocked normally. Sekiro had 12, so this is an extremely tight window and sekiro still had a separate bar from HP so this is double punishing. Not to mention many fights have extremely fast fury attacks that from beginning to move to attack and hitting the player, it takes so few milliseconds that it is toward the top end of the bell curve of human reaction time, thus requiring not to react to it, but to be hit by it and trial and error how early before the move starts to block. There are also graphical issues and pop ins and some lazy asset placement, but the combat itself feels like it is trying to combine styles that were separated for a reason and lack pieces of said mechanics that were needed. If you enjoy the game that is great! but imo it needs tweaks that can't be added via a patch but hopefully improved if a equal is made.If you are new to this type of game, regardless of whether i think this is a good game or not, I do suggest starting with a different souls like game as this is quite difficult with not many ways to easy a difficult boss like others in the genre have (i.e. exploring a different area to grow stronger and progress at the same time)

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down, a masterclass in souls-like games storytelling - I dare say even surpassing FROMsoft, and I'm an avid fan of that type of nitpicky easter-egg based stories. Less is more, and just a litte bit of structure goes a long way - all games in this genre, including FROM, should take notes, because this is currently the pinnacle of souls-based games stories. Difficulty can be a bit jarring, especially towards the end, but trudging through it really payed off. I don't say this lightly, but this game can easily be called a masterpiece and not many games can reach this praise, at least not in my book. Congrats to the devs for taking souls-games to the next level and proving that there's more to the genre than just haphazardly throwing bits of lore here and there and calling it a story. Soundtrack is out of this world, artstyle is on point, ambience and atmosphere are AMAZING, enemies have variety, bosses are not rehashes, combat and weapons are ingenious, scope is just right and I absolutely adore the setting - very much looking forward to the DLCs, sequels and what other fairy tales we'll get to explore.Towards all the negativity aimed at the difficullty, especially by the self-proclaimed "veterans" around: even though I've finished all Dark Souls, Elden Ring, Bloodborne and other souls-likes - I can safely say that I do not consider myself a great souls player by any means - I'm a sword and board scrub and could never get consecutive perfect parries in these type of games (reason why I never even started playing Sekiro in the first place), thus aiming towards dodge builds mostly. But the difficulty here felt just right and even finished this on NG+ which is a first because of time restraints -  but what worked for me is taking a different approach where i got stuck - what worked a lot of times was going full on aggro with a very fast technique scaled weapon (usually Etiquette), Aegis equipped for easy parries and less than 30% weight for quick recovery and dodging, with a bit of physical resistances on (lose some of the equipment to reach the weight threshold if needed). And just pushing through...again...and again...and again. In the end it all payed off. Thanks for an amazing  experience. Truly.PS: Also has the best damn weapon in any soulslike so far: a freaking umbrella.  didn't stand a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: This games has everything that makes Souls great:On top of that you get a very special way to customize your character and build.Weapons consist of two parts: Blade and Handle.The Blade determines the durability and damage type while the handle determins the moveset and scaling. During your playthrough you will find a lot of very different weapons of which you can mix and match blades and handles to your liking which helps to make combat feel fresh and engaging. There are no weapon requirements and both blade and handle come with their own "Fable Arts" that can be performed by using Fable Meter, generated in combat. Defensive stats aren't bound to how your character looks but rather unrelated items in their own slots with their own specialization. That way you can just choose your favorite outfits without sacrificing any combat viability.They even slapped a skill tree on top to make sure you can lean more towards the playstyle you like.If you are a fan of the Souls-Series, Bloodborne or Sekiro, you will have a great time with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: 8.7/10 - Fantastic-It's a shame that it's a set character, I always prefer to see a character creator. -Unfortunately the game comes together best in NG+ but NG is still quite good. Mostly owed to late-game rewards, such as final boss weapons and certain cosmetics making the game overall more enjoyable. This can also be considered a very fortunate thing as it means the reward structure pays out, and it gives you reasons to replay the game. -Combat is great, but I would have liked more fluidity for things such as swapping weapons and legion arms. As it stands the animation is slow and feels very clunky if you're not literally doing nothing else at the time, making it very difficult to effectively change tactics while in combat.-Puppet String is love, Puppet String is life. That thing will stop any mook enemy dead in their tracks and enable powerful jumping attacks with the potential to stagger even the burliest enemy types. The other Legion Arms are also pretty good for what they do, just not AS good.-A very small parry window makes it difficult, if not just annoying, to attempt to parry enemies with jittery and delayed attacks. Of which there are many, making the risk not quite equal to the reward in many cases. It can still be very effective and satisfying for bosses with more rhythmic attack patterns however.-Mostly solid to really good boss design. A lot of 2-phase bosses makes for encounters with a lot of meat on them. Most crucially it ends on a high note, with the final boss being the decidedly best in the game, something I can't recall happening since I played Sekiro.-A select few enemies are incredibly dumb and I hate every fiber of their stupid being(non-bosses). -Level design is competent, but there is a slight over-reliance on enemies sitting around in obscure corners waiting to ambush you and nigh-indistinguishable weak floorboards that constantly break away under your feet until you grow paranoid that every bridge or wooden path you see will self-destruct once you step on it.-Side-content such as character stories and treasure hunts are a good diversion from main progression and have satisfying rewards. There is a good amount of hidden treasure in each level to keep you curious and alert to anomalies in your surroundings. A much better motivator than aforementioned ambushes and floorboards.-Waifu is cute. Wholesome. Must protecc.-Side-kick Gemini is a stand-up guy and mildly amusing, managing not to be overbearing or plain annoying.-Setting and aesthetic is neat, though the choice of puppet enemies can make combat frustrating at times. And though it's a small part of the overall plot "World Expo Gone Wrong" is a cool hook. -There was never any reason why the "drop your exp/currency" mechanic should have out-lived the Demon's/Dark Souls series, but I guess it's what everyone does nowadays... so, that's okay I guess?

_childDocuments_.review: If Sony ever destroys whatever ancient, demonic bonds prevent it from authorizing a Bloodborne remaster/PC release then Bloodborne will likely peak Lies of P on the "take the Soulsborne format and run with it" throne.Until then, Lies of P seems fairly secure. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: not perfect and not sub-parLevel & World Design:  The world is very linear. It's not much of a bother, but it's still notable. The level design isn't anything spectacular and the shortcuts can seem oddly placed, but it's still well serviceable and basically a non-issue if you don't expect FromSoftware quality there. The world isn't very memorable, it's just not forgettable either. It's no Lordran or Yharnam by any means, but it does feel like a mapped out place. Its believability and memorability are maybe a few steps below Lothric more or less.Polish:  The bosses aren't anything crazy and are mostly just fine. They don't feel like they were completely play tested and polished, but it's not too bad. There isn't much to be amazed by with the bosses. The animations aren't bad, but they feel just a teeny bit sub-optimal. The combat controls feel perfectly fine and it's systems are well integrated, though. There's no core issue with how the game plays.Balancing:  It is slightly off. Health bars can seem too large sometimes and other times you may be steamrolling through. Sometimes you come across an enemy that's oddly troublesome and sometimes it's perfectly fine, and sometimes it seems a bit out of place. A lack of attack speed isn't compensated well enough to make those weapons as viable. Parrying doesn't reward you as much as expected for the effort, and it's not too difficult or useless. And sometimes the difficulty of a boss comes out of nowhere when compared to the area it's in. There's no major issue.Progression: Very enjoyable. There are absolutely no complaints here. You level up in the standard D&D inspired way as well as a separate system that is more specific with what you're doing, and it is satisfying.The game is definitely within the comparison bracket of the FromSoftware titles, and can be preferred over a # of them without it being any sort of hot take. There's no reason not to play Lies of P if you like the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: ---{Gameplay}---☐ Bland and mundane☐ Mildly technical☑ Technical and engaging☐ Above and beyond---{Story}---☐ No Story☑ Rich lore☑ Engaging ties with the player☑ Compelling Characters---{Difficulty}---☐ Easy☐ Easy to learn, hard to master☑ Moderate☐ Difficult☐ Difficult to learn, difficult to master---{Game Time}---☐ Short (1-10 Hours)☑ Average (10 to 30 Hours)☐ Long (30 to 50 Hours)☐ Very Long (50+)---{Replay Value}---☐ No replay value☐ Some☑ High replay value☐ Infinite replay value---{Graphics}---☐ Terrible☐ Moderate☑ Excellent☐ Noteworthy---{Sound Design}---☐ Poor☐ Average☑ Excellent☐ Innovative---{Voice Acting (if any)}---☐ Awful☐ Decent☑ Amazing☐ Award worthy---{PC Requirements}---☐ Low☑ Moderate☐ High☐ Demanding---{Bugs}---☑ None experienced☐ Minor bugs☐ Noticeable but manageable☐ Game-breaking bugs (Completely unplayable)---{For the Price}---☑ Worth the price☐ Get it on sale☐ Not recommendedA Souls-borne game based on the story of Pinocchio, but that’s where all similarities end. A twisted take on lies, where instead of becoming our downfall, lies become our way of achieving humanity and protecting our companions. Compelling characters, easily digestible lore, and likable and evil characters alike. The main character P seeks to save the city of Krat from the mad puppets only to fall in a rabbit hole of an even greater evil. Pros: Smooth gameplay, fast combat and perfect blocking system is where action combat is streamlined together for the most satisfying gameplay experience.	Rechargeable pulse cell (heals) during combat, a nice way to reward the players who excel in combat and make use of the Perfect Parry system it has saved me many times during critical moments. Custom weapon set-ups, high replay value, humanity system, sound design, P-Organ system.Cons: Camera issues in critical moments: This was infuriating at times, when you are cornered by a large enemy and the camera shrinking into itself making combat near impossible and you end up in a stun lock and are unable to escape. Stats have a significant efficiency drop-off after a specific level which makes leveling useless after a certain point. Maxing all stats at 100 will be not much different from 50s across the board. TLDR:Despite some issues I had during my experience they were significantly next to nothing compared to all the positives. I normally don’t go out of my way to plat a game but this game is different and heading into NG+ ill be finishing the last few achievements. All in all, this game is amazing and having played DSIII, I’ll say this with confidence: Lies of P is the best non-From Soft game ever. Highly recommended, even at full price, it’s worth every damn penny. Overall rating: 9.4/10

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Soulslike games not made by FromSoft. If you wanted something to scratch the Bloodborne itch, this is it. Cons:  - Durability is a thing, but it can be restored with a infinite use grindstone in your inventory - When you have "Souls" to recover after death they are drained away as you take damage, but can be recovered if you kill the enemy that damaged you. - Dodging is basically worthless until you unlock the ability to chain them together and to dodge from a downed position, and even then Enemy Fury Attacks don't allow for Dodge I-Frames anyway. - If you exchange one of the "Boss Souls" for an Amulet instead of a Weapon you get locked out of a Cryptic Vessel Solution. (Frozen Feast)Pros: + Weapon Handles and Blades can be mixed and matched to your liking, as scaling and swing style is determined by the handle, and damage and damage type is determined by the blade. + "Souls" are dropped outside of boss arenas so you aren't committed to finishing the boss fight. + Parrying is very fun and works like Sekiro in a lot of ways. You can break enemy weapons by parrying enough times. + Stagger attacks can be triggered by parrying or damage, and it shows you where to stand to start it. + The level design is fantastic and they provide plenty of unlockable shortcuts in each area making traversal a breeze. + The graphics are beautiful and really scratch the "Victorian Gothic" itch. + Runs great on my machine. No crashes, and only 1 notable bug that only happened once and was fixed with a reboot. (I died to a grab and the game did not send me back to the "Bonfire.")Overall fantastic game, even most of the cons are nitpicks. Buy this game when you can!

_childDocuments_.review: Last year when Lords of the Fallen came out I was one of the lucky (or unlucky depending on how you look at it) creators that got early access to it. Because of this I blasted through it largely impressed with the visuals but disappointed by the lack of difficulty overall and the godawful performance. It also has by far the least impressive final boss I have ever faced in any soulslike. I made a video saying as much, and that video got 3 kinds of comments. 1. People either agreeing with me or just angry and disliking the game/whining2. People disagreeing with me and cursing my family for trashing on the OBVIOUS game of the year (lol)and uh3. People ignoring the video entirely and telling me to play Lies of PI am very thankful for that third type of comment because without them I might have missed out on what was easily one of the best games that came out last year and one of the only soulslikes that I personally think is anywhere close to the weight class of capital F Fromsoft titles. There's an incredible amount of enemy variety for a soulslike thats genuinely impressive. Every new area has unique enemies both in terms of visuals and moveset. Lies of P also does something that'll have Fromsoft fans *seething* which is uh... they uh... they tell a story? Like actually tell a story, not just "story" hidden in item descriptions. I enjoy that about the Souls games, but its nice to just have the story be direct and straightforward sometimes rather than relying on the wonderful VaatiVidya to know whats going on lolNow while exploration is a lot more linear in Lies of P than Fromsoft titles, it actually contributes to shortening the gap between my personal favorite part of Souls titles; the f*cking amazing boss fights.There's almost no stinkers in this game, every boss is designed to push you in a direction and test how you engage with the mechanics. You can either deflect or dodge and its not only fun to perfect both but enemy types and bosses exist in the game that nudge you towards using one or the other as a defensive tactic and eventually there are enemies that throw down the gauntlet and incentivize using both for different attacks which tests your ability to read whats being thrown at you and then responding appropriately. This game is pretty difficult by the end, but the slow curve and ramp up to that final secret boss is amazing. Noah Caldwell Gervais has a 2 part series of video essays on Souls games (go watch them he's great) and he talks a lot about how there's difficulty customization in terms of the build you choose even if there isn't an "easy, medium, hard" on the main menu. You can use magic and tons of consumables or run in naked with a big club, the choice is yours.Lies of P gives you so many options that if you are really struggling with the core gameplay, you can amp yourself up 20 different ways and use a bunch of different tools that each boss is specifically weak to in order to really set yourself up to win. The empowerment of the player in this game is more than any other Soulslike I've played and its great, theres just so much at your disposal. Lies of P was not my game of the year, not the BEST game this year, for me, but it was probably the game that I had the most fun with. Don't sleep on it.

_childDocuments_.review: LIES OF P is a high-quality Soulslike that I recommend wholeheartedly. That being said, it doesn't have indirect easy modes like FROM SOFTWARE games do (eg., co-op, overpowered weapon arts, cheese tactics, etc.) and you can't outlevel the content like you can in Team Ninja games or Elden Ring. In other words, it's probably going to be way too difficult for people who haven't spent hundreds of hours in these games.PROS:- game looks & sounds gorgeous- it's very well optimized (runs great on 1080p, high settings, on GTX 1070, Ryzen 3700X, 16GB RAM 3200MH/z)- huge enemy and boss variety- gameplay feels very tight and well executed- game is pretty long (30-40 hours) - story is interesting enough- levels are linear, but well-designed and with enough variation to keep things interesting- overall a really good game- it's like a love letter to the Soulslike genreCONS:- gear variety seems pretty limited. You can't see any of the gear except weapons and cosmetics on your character. I'm playing as a robot, why can't I change other limbs except for my left arm? It seems like such a missed opportunity...- there are massive delays on almost every attack, yet the attacks themselves come out incredibly fast. With perfect block timings being as tight as they are, this means your reaction time probably won't make much of a difference: you'll just have to die to a boss over and over until you learn the timings by heart. This often makes bosses and elite enemies feel cheap and annoying to fight against, but don't get me wrong, the combat is still a million times better than in 99% of 3rd person action games ever made. - the camera is zoomed way too close during some boss fights, so you'll be getting hit by super-fast attacks from off-screen. super annoying- there's no magic, ranged combat, or real build variety. You'll play a melee build that's focused on blocking and dodging, and that's about it. This greatly reduces replayability.- the levels are very linear. Again, not a problem on your first playthrough, but it also limits replayability.- the devs have started nerfing the difficulty, which wasn't necessary IMHO, but your mileage may vary.TLDR: If you're a Souls veteran (a REAL veteran, we're talking hundreds and hundreds of hours in these games) this game is a must play. If you're a Souls newbie/casual, you may want to leave this one for later.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I regret to change my previously positive review of the game, but I feel an ethical obligation to do so. I believe Shigeru Miyamoto once said that you should never be prevented from completing a game because of a prior mistake, and while LoP does not formally make completion impossible, I am certain many players will find a certain point in the plot insurmountable.At the point I mentioned, the game removes your ability to fast travel, to fully respec, and to buy most consumable items. This is before a boss, and there is no warning whatsoever. I anticipate fan rejection of what I've said, so please check my achievements: I beat the boss. It  took a few tries, but I did so. I am also a veteran player of this genre, and I do not expect every player to be able to match that. 'Git gud' is not a response to a flawed game. Asking $50 for a game you may have to hard reset 2/3rds of the way through is not acceptable. The developers made a catastrophically bad design choice, and I will remain a negative review on LoP, regardless of its many other high points.Original review follows:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------So Lies of P is a good game. I want to stress that, and I'm going to highlight the highs first.1) The records are some of the greatest music ever encountered in a game. They are just perfect, that sweet, melancholy, aching sort of composition. I invite anyone to hear Feel and not think about the people they've cared about most, and yet lost. I invite anyone to hear Fascination and not just feel the pain of life drawn up and exposed, like someone expertly massaging a knot in the back muscles.2) The bosses are good! They're quite good, they're nice.3) The opening levels are great, just fantastic design.Okay. I really like this game. I wanted it to succeed, and it's a miracle it did. These are the things that don't work:1) The level design past the first third is awful. If the designers didn't want you to simply run past every encounter, I have no idea what they were doing. If they *did* want you to run past every encounter, that's awful. That's just bad. The frustration of every level will ramp and ramp and ramp for artificial, stupid reasons, and you just have to roll with it if you like the game.2) The bosses aren't amazing. I required no more than three tries on any boss so far, and I'm near the end game. Most bosses I one shot. This ties back into complaint #1: the difficulty of this game is bad design, not legitimately interesting design. You won't find Friede or Orphan or Malenia (so far, in my experience). You'll get a *ton* of Abyss Watchers-esque fights. Just so many. None of them are as good as Abyss Watchers, or Nameless King, or any other 2HB From boss you want to name, but lord will you have to fight them anyway.3) The story ain't great. It's fine, but it won't scratch that weird itch. _childDocuments_.review: My time with Lies of P was exactly the intense and gratifying experience I hoped for. While the game broadly functions similarly to the best the souls-like genre has to offer, Lies of P‘s tweaks and refinements are so masterfully planned out and implemented that they make every moment of gameplay a pleasure. _childDocuments_.review: While FromSoftware's IP has spawned a smattering of clones and inspired many others, the most successful of which never travel too close to the sun. While games like Hollow Knight have seen great success with only light inspiration to great acclaim, others that attempt to mirror the quixotic appeal of Dark Souls and Bloodborne too closely end up feeling like cheap copies, whether or not that's fair to the game. In that sense Lies of P has an immense hurdle to climb, in that it will inevitably be compared to it's contemporaries that it's not shy about drawing inspiration from. I'm pleased to say that it excels, and even surpasses in some ways, even though it fails in others. The fundamentals are where the game shines brightest. While it's easiest to compare Lies of P to Bloodborne, it's combat system is a mishmash of Elden Ring/Dark Souls, Bloodborne and Sekiro. From Bloodborne comes the "hop" dodge and the "rally" system. While the traditional dodge roll is still present, the snappier Bloodborne hop is, and has served as a new demarcation point for faster, more aggressive enemies, and this is no less true in Lies of P. The rally system, which was Bloodborne's method of rewarding aggression by allowing the player to recuperate lost health through attacking, instead applies exclusively to chip damage acquired through blocking. The chip damage and stamina attrition acquired from blocking can be avoided entirely however from the "deflection" system inherited from Sekiro, in which a block timed to be raised just before you're struck negates stamina attrition, chip damage, and damages the opponents "posture". "Deflection" in Lies of P is dramatically more challenging that in Sekiro however, this is due to the removal of an "activation" period for raising your guard which made tapping the guard button a common tactic for procuring a deflection. Simply put, when you let go of the button, you have no parry frames, and you must allow your guard to return to a neutral state before raising it again in order to procure a deflection. This effectively removes the mashing element of deflection entirely, so that the player absolutely must know when the attack is about to connect, and the luck element is gone. I suspect the timing is also more strict, but without intricate knowledge of frame data I would merely be speculating. While deflection is often the most rewarding defensive option, as it accrues posture damage, avoids damage, and doesn't penalize your stamina the way a dodge would, it is also the most challenging due to the aforementioned changes, and it isn't *always* the best option. This is in part because breaking posture doesn't automatically segue into a riposte state the way it does in Sekiro and Elden Ring. Once enough posture damage is accrued, you must strike your foe with a charged heavy attack. This is a thoughtful change as landing said move requires so much time and commitment that often necessitates the kind of lateral positioning only a dodge can provide, but setting aside from that specific use case, just like in Elden Ring, basic attacks and especially heavy attacks accrue posture damage instead of being the sole province of deflections. The reason I take so much time to illustrate the nuances of Lies of P's combat system is to explain that each mechanic has been carefully considered to take every Fromsoft game's core combat mechanics, and intertwine them in a way that creates a better overall system than any individual Fromsoft game has accomplished. This is the game's strongest suite and the sole attribute that exceeds it's contemporaries even when others pale, so it deserves a proper hearing. More can be said about the game's "fable" system, the mixing weapon components, and the innate weapon skills, but for the sake of brevity I will simply say that Lies of P has a meaningful variety of weaponry without becoming too cluttered with hundreds of weapons only superficially different from one another in the way that Elden Ring was. Lies of P's second strongest suite is it's boss design. I don't profess to be the ultimate gamer, I have plenty of experience with the Fromsoft suite of games, and nonetheless plenty of the chapter bosses required dozens of attempts for me to complete. The difficulty curve was a smooth curve rising to a maddening crescendo. Although as a heavy weapons enthusiast, the "modular" combos where it's never entirely clear if I have a safe window to attack *can* seem cheap and unfair, I understand this is a cross I chose to bear by wielding a giant hunk of steel.Up until this point I've had nothing but good things to say about Lies of P. It's combat system, it's array of tools and weaponry, it's challenging pulse racing boss fights. With all that said I'm afraid that's where the game's strengths end, and the rest ranges from middling to outright bad. While the aesthetics as it relates to combat are superb, and the bosses are great, the common enemy design never graduates past the bland array of harmless mooks that meander around in modest groupings. These enemies are fine at the start of the game, as you're only gathering your bearings by that point, but by the time I'd gotten my footing they were nothing more than a conveyor belt of zombies marching into my charged heavy attacks. Outside of boss arenas, the only real challenge exists with "elite" or "miniboss" style enemies, but even they became helpless prey to my giant sawblade around the midway point of the game as each charged heavy attack sent them reeling.If there's a single red line I could draw that differentiates the Fromsoft games from their clones, it's the level design. Fromsoft at their best are experts at crafting winding interconnected areas that're in equal parts convincing, branching, challenging and varied. The level design in Lies of P checks absolutely none of those boxes. The most you can expect from Lies of P's level design is a solitary side path that dead ends or loops around to an earlier point, perhaps with a radiant ergo fragment or a resistance ampoule waiting at it's end. Each area a rectangle populated by a smattering of chattering puppet butlers wielding candlesticks or tacky looking petrification zombies bursting with turquoise goo, occasionally punctuated by an elite enemy who is the sole possible threat of death around any corner. Each time you might expect a level to meaningfully diverge paths you're met by an indestructible, impassable stack of luggage. Regardless, the streets of neo London still look beautiful replete with gothic architecture and enough tattered furnishings to make a convincing looking area. The metro stations, exhibition hall, opera house, and lower income neighborhood all look pleasing albeit very similar, and none offer much more in terms of actual navigation than what I've already explained. Occasionally you'll walk across narrow rafters and be ambushed by hiding foes, but never enough to make you mutter more than an "oh". This is truly the red line that distinguishes Fromsoft from it's aspirants. In Lies of P, much of the game is just a freeway that leads to your ultimate destination: a boss arena. Anywhere outside of Lies of P's Neo London is totally bereft of any creative vision. The muddy rural swamps, caves and the lategame aztec temple like structure could be lifted from any JRPG in recorded history and nobody would tell the difference. Around the time you revisit Neo London ravaged by earthquakes and strange ergo infused formations, fight recycled bosses infused with petrification to augment their moveset, and navigate a remote island temple that's comprised entirely of sandstone brick rectangular rooms and ramshackle wood structures it becomes clear that the developers started to run out of steam around the latter part of the game, but thankfully they have enough to give the game a good sendoff with 3 great bossfights at the tail section. Overall, an easy recommend albeit it's flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never wished there was a "neutral" option on Steam more than I do now. This game is fun for a solid ten hours. The flow of combat is nice, learning the parries is rewarding, and the visual designs are usually amazing. But then the cracks start showing. First it was just an enemy that can stunlock you unless you have a specific upgrade. Then a boss where you can't tell the difference between turns and attacks. Soon you'll realize that you've spent more time running back to a boss than you have fighting it. Then they added a four phase gank fight that really just wasn't fun even when I won. But the experience that really pissed me off was getting locked in a corner by an elite enemy, with each hit adding a status effect that hamstrings your healing while the camera refuses to show me what's happening. I'm likely going to finish my play-through and maybe try for a few achievements, but you should probably just go play Sekiro again.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished Lies of P, and i found it a masterpiece both from objective and subjective perspectives.    THE. AWESOME. ART. Above everything else, not just the graphic detail, but the artistical concepts behind. Scenarios, aesthetics, all that. It could have been made with worse overall graphics, and still, for me, would be SO AWESOME as it is now. Specially i love the aesthetics of some late-game area/s so reminiscent of certain historical periods/areas, without entering into spoilers (besides the obvious general asthetics of victorian era, that also are so cool).    The narrative can be so unnecesarily poetical and it is a beautiful how it acompannies the theme "Lies-Truth" and the process of "Humanisation" (which, ironically, the recovery of lost humanity is an ever-increasing artistic theme in modern art because of the dehumanizing effect of modern society). There are some scenes (mostly side-quest scenes involving NPC interaction) that are instilled by so much love and evoking so many deep feelings...These cinematics are developed to a professional-Oscar-prize-winning-movie. Also, the main story narrative evolves alongside the game, giving at each step more and more insight into the worldbuilding and the protagonist, and creating tons of poetical moments that, without any need in such a "souls-game", evokes immense beauty.    Genuine/innovative defensive mechanic. On one side, the mechanical idea of block-but-attack-to-recover-health vs parry-and-keep-staggering trade-off as the main survival mechanic is genius; most of the last years souls-like were based on the need to time the defensive input since it is a "1 tick" input (i.e. rolling in dark souls series, parrying in sekiro, and other games as bloodborne and nioh the same, to name a few).    Weapon personalisation as means of player-driven-personality expression. Quite awesome that players can tailor their weapon by assembling-dissassembling, and most of them work for any build thanks to an early mechanic to modify scaling, similarly that last bit to previous souls games. The freedom for each player to tailor their weapon is by far more satisfying than the ability to tailor the character aesthetics (in the end, everything bends in front of the narrative, so it is fine to play along with it, considering how well done it has been done).    The length is appropiate, and THIS is important. I was afraid of a burnt-out, but it took me around 30-35 hours (taking my time savouring some beautiful art-scenarios and taking screenshots :p) and it is perfect (for instance, Elden Ring was criticsed negatively at its moment due to being relatively long to beat the full story and sidequests, taking around 80hours). It is true that some levels and areas go in and out without noticing, but for anyone that sees this fact as a negative one, i would ask "Are you sure it would be better an area if it were twice as long?". This answer rarely is yes, and only it is for very specific areas for each players, according to each personal tastes on scenario-art &/or area-specific enemies.Bottom Line: I beat Lies of P in a single walkthrough. I left Dark Souls 3 at its moment in the half. I ended frustrated with Elden Ring being too long (still i enjoyed it and replayed it along time, though). However, considering the "overall playing experience", the souls-game i've ever enjoyed the most playing it has been THIS GAME. My congratulations to the whole team.Love <3

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. I like the game, but there are a few obvious oversights. I'll give this game a 6.5/10 and here is why.While the mechanics themselves are quite solid and the combat is enjoyable, there are a few things I would like patched. 1) To be able to select a specific language with a different language's subtitles. Shouldn't be hard to do. Secondly.. I like to keep my inventory tidy, so I regularly throw out items I don't think I'll need in the near future. In Code Vein there was a simple and good system: Put in box, disable auto-refill. Exactly that feature is missing here. That is an absolute dealbreaker for me. It feels like a punishment to have the game vomit items into my bag over and over. Even just a symbol of what has auto-refill and what has not would be a helpful start.The atmosphere certainly gives me the right kind of vibe, however (keep in mind, I've only played 3.5 hours so far), the enemies are.. how shall I put it.. their AI is too simple and their health bar too low. I love RPGs with stat upgrades, but from level 1 an enemy was 3 hits and after upgrading a good 8 levels, its still 3 hits. That tells me, the initial value either is too low or the upgrade system in itself quite meaningless. Devs, if you read this, it gives people a good feeling if they level up and suddenly everything becomes a bit easier. If you want the exact opposite, to make players slowly realize, that leveling is meaningless.. well.. congratulations. You managed to do just that in only 2 hours.As for the AI, it feels like "the easy way out". Even bosses use the same basic AI: See enemy, ready weapon, charge in a straight line. It shouldn't be that simple. Where's the love in the details for bosses? Even that human boss fight, you can literally just side-step him and repeatedly stab him in the back.To sum it up, story and atmosphere are solid, the hits in battle feel solid as well, however the enemy scaling, level-up system and quality-of-life features still need some work.

_childDocuments_.review: Steam Deck performance was great. I played with a locked 40 fps with FSR2 Quality at 12 watts. The game can also run at 60 fps with some dips to 50 fps. At the time of writing, Lies of P is classified as Playable, but I think it should be Verified. I saw no bugs/glitches, but the text size in the menus are kinda small. No spoilers here, great game. Completed it twice and it was just as fun the second time as I continued to experiment with weapon combinations. One playthrough takes about 20-25 hours, but probably varies quite a bit from person-to-person.Round8 did not try to hide the FromSoftware inspiration and down right mimicry in some aspects. What they copied was executed very well and did not feel like a budget version at all. If someone told me the developers at Round8 had ties with FromSoftware, it would sound believable. Despite taking several gameplay mechanics from multiple different FromSoftware titles, it was still able to create its own unique identity. The combat feels great. Every player character animation has a slight pause afterwards and input buffering is included. This may feel clunky to some, but I enjoy the harder commitment to an action and the required deliberateness of each button press. While the game heavily encourages the player to perfect guard, the use of guarding, dodging, and spacing from attacks provides a great mix of viable options in fights. The perfect guard sounds great as well. Being able to break weapons from multiple successful perfect guards was super cool, and a fun way to reward to player for nailing the timing. I also think it justifies implementing the player character's weapon durability mechanic. While it may feel tedious at times to repair your weapon, it's only fair that if boss weapons can break, then so should yours. I will not say too much about the boss fights to avoid spoilers, but I just thought they were unique and were simply great! Weapon customization was one of the best mechanics implemented in the game. It made finding new weapons much more exciting since you get to try out new blade and handle combinations. In souls games, finding new weapons can sometimes be disappointing because of stat requirements or because it scales better with a different build. This issue does not occur in Lies of P because due to weapon assembly and handle modifications, making exploration feel more rewarding.I liked the character progression system through the P-Organ. While the abilities you get are not super unique, was a nice addition to make P stronger outside of just leveling up. The progression system through the leveling system was not very interesting and I don't feel like there is much distinction between choosing between motivity, technique, or advance since you can alter the scaling on handles anyways. I think the weakest part of the game is the level design. I wish there were more hidden areas or branching paths to make exploration more fun. Overall, I still found the level design to be just ok.The gold coin mechanic felt out of place. Overall, the way this was implemented was strange, but I didn't find it problematic as this whole mechanic can be ignored. The rewards for trading gold coins also seemed underwhelming since most of them are specter buffs. Similar to FromSoftware titles, the summons used in boss fights completely trivializes them, but I'm still glad it was implemented for those who would still like to experience the full game, but struggle with bosses.I found the the most of the dialogue options to be uninteresting, but giving the player the option to lie is cool.I did not find the Legion arm to be interesting and often found myself forgetting about it. I wish Geppetto would stop calling P a good boy.9/10. Extremely excited to see more from this studio in the future. And no, this is not [FromSoftware Title] from home!

_childDocuments_.review: A true love letter to Bloodborne and Sekiro, and a must-play for fans of the genre with high-octane action guaranteed to get your P-Organ going, this is by far and away the best non-FS Soulsborne game bar none.If you told me that it was FromSoftware, Inc. that made this, I wouldn't have batted an eyelid. In fact, I would have said: "I'm glad the optimisation is so much better here than in ER." Such is the attention to detail, the quality of minute-to-minute gameplay and world traversal, and the closeness to the intangible secret sauce that is Soulsborne, that characterise Lies of P. It is not easy to adapt a timeless fairy tale into something new, much less a Soulsborne video game. But the coherent narrative NEOWIZ has crafted here - fleshed out through scraps of lore tucked away in a beautiful and broken world that is satisfying to explore and inhabited by a memorable cast of characters - had me taking the story seriously throughout and even convinced me to seek out all its choices and possible endings. This is a narrative that is grand and knows it, and its lofty ambitions are more than fulfilled by how mechanically tight it plays, how gorgeous everything looks, as well as one of the best soundtracks I've heard in games in a long time. I liked this game so much that I purchased it on Steam after playing through the first ending on PC Game Pass; I want to support developers like these and to see more games of such quality. I knew nothing of NEOWIZ before this game, but now eagerly look forward to whatever they put out next (a sequel was teased, with a different fairy tale perhaps!). You all have done astounding work here and should be proud. Now, please release the soundtrack. Fighting!

_childDocuments_.review: So as someone who's played DS1, 2 and 3, Sekiro and Elden Ring, I was expecting this to be more of a low effort clone to piggyback off of the success of the fromsoft games.However, especially in terms of atmosphere this game is definitely able to stand on its own two feet. but also the gameplay is satisfying, it looks good, it controls well and the weapons are varied and interesting. I do tend to not have an idea where I am in a level and this game doesn't relly help that. The areas are tight and (at least for me!) it is hard to have an actual idea where I am in relation to Stargazers (this game's bonfires). An in-game map (at least a rough one) could've gone a long way for me. All in all I certainly recommend it to fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: The design is pretty cool, weapons are nice, enemies have a nice variety. Combat is where it misses, a lot of the fights are pretty one mechanic oriented (you either NEED to dodge everything or parry everything), which takes a bit of the fun, also a lot of core mechanics are locked behind a skill tree that if you dont realize you will have an even harder time. A lot of enemies (mainly elites and bosses) have mulitple hits combo, to the numbers of 10 or more, that along with the bosses not being too well designed in the atk movement part makes it really hard to understand those, and make it so any hit you take becomes at least half of your hp bar. If you love melee you might go beyond that and enjoy the game, my fun ended when i had to deal with bosses mood swings between 3-4 fury atks in a row, multiple of those 10 hit combos just because yes and the need to grind a lot to buy resources for each try (resources like bombs and "enchants" for weapons are almost mandatory), so it kinda loses the fun factor and learning process of the game if you need to constantly grind to try again, also there's a spectre that if you wanna use, you need a limited (time regenerated) resource, which is kinda absurd lolAll an all the game is a nice try, but some core mechanics missing, the bosses not being fun and the need to grind to try again just breaks it for me

_childDocuments_.review: Having played this till the trip of returning to the original maps, with more than 134 hours of Elden Ring and hours for all of the Dark Soul episodes (all done), I think I need to voice some opinions for this rough diamond:Firstly, I think people are too harsh with this game when comparing it with Elden Ring or Dark Souls 3. Remember, before these two, From Software also struggled with Dark Soul 1. I still remember the times I played it lol. It was fun, sure, but it was a mess, with janky systems & lots of unfair fighting arrangements that have only been fixed at Dark Soul 2 & 3. So it would be fair if we treat this game like Dark Soul 1, and honestly, if we compare like that, I believe Lies of P has done better than Dark Soul 1 in a lot of aspects, from graphics, to the sound & the atmosphere, also the fighting system.And about fighting system, I see a lot of people complain about the weapons being clunky, too slow and not break the monster efficiently like in Dark Souls (lol!) I believe it's only because you guys pick the wrong weapon choice or/and haven't learnt how to assemble the weapons. It only took me a few tries to realize how weapon works. And currently I still use heavy weapon fighting style with Bone-Cutting Saw Blade & Krat Police Handle, and have made it passed the Green Monster (the only one I struggle with so far) So watch some video guides about weapons & learn how to invest in stats correctly!The only thing I am not too pleased with Lies of P now is the lack of choice for heavy fighting style. I have tried combinations but only a few truly fits, mostly coming from the poor variety of weapon movesets & Fable Arts. So I do hope they make Patch about this rather than the bosses, minions, Amulets or Capacity or some things like in the recent Patch. I find hard bosses are engaging, rewarding since I have beheaded a lot harder ones in From Software's games. And I believe many Veteran players also feel the same as me.Oh yeah and also I think the developer should add the Multiplayer like other reviews have stated out, it would be more fun!Overall, good game, not excellent, but definitely good! (8/10)

_childDocuments_.review: Friendly reminder that this is my opinion and if you disagree with it and really like this game. Good for you. I do too. I am just expressing my opinion like the people who do enjoy all of this game. I Just have a difference opinion.Lies of P is a insanely solid souls like game. At its best I honestly like it more than Elden Ring. Why the thumbs down? Because this game has one of the single biggest drops I have ever seen in a game. The quality from the first half to the second is insane. Combat spoils will be below. I will not be discussing the story but boss names and combat mechanics will be discussed as well as area spoilers. Off the bat first half of the game? Insanely good. Boring but solid level design with beautiful world building, story, art design, music, and sound design. I like the first half of the game outside of a few stinker boss fights as much as I like DS3 and as much as I like the the few low spots of Sekiro ( the absolute peak of souls games don't @ me) Its good. The core combat is great and the QoL mechanics such as damaging giving you flask back or putting the souls out of the boss arena are amazing. The levels are fair and not full of the Dark souls staples that I really don't like such as death traps, ambushes, enemy spam , etc. However, around the second half they fired the dev team and brought in John Dark souls himself to fill the game with more and more unfun BS. Games enemy Variety was already lacking but now it is 90% the same "faction" of enemy. Levels go on for way too long especially the final area. they spam the same couple of unfun status affects that either do DoT or insta kill you. How engaging... Enemies around corners? Absolutely. 90% of them. Whats that? You want more enemies? We got you. There's a part where there's two enemies around both corners of the room and one in the center both with stun locking ranged movies. Awesome. Its not hard. Its just not fun. I die to it one time then never again. Every once in awhile? Sure. But 6-7 times before the next bonfire? Awesome. 20-30 times in the last area. Now its getting frustrating. The loot goes from being plentiful with 1/10 being good meaningful loot to 1/100 being important so you feel like you are wasting your time. The areas filled with nothing also increase wasting more of your time. Mini boss enemies that dropped loot in the first half? ♥♥♥♥ it, Give em double the health and throw two of them down with no loot drops. I am going to list the locations and my ranking of them so you can see when the game falls off.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great soul-like for beginners.  It starts off fairly easy, but continuously gets more difficult.  The areas are pretty straight forward so you don't have to worry about getting lost.  The stargazers(bonfires) and shortcuts seem to be placed perfectly to create a challenge getting there the first time, but once you know what to expect on the way they are easy enough to reach.  The game also gives you multiple options to overcome challenges such as legion arms, summons and elemental weaknesses, but never forces you to use them.  Overall, as someone with limited Souls-like experience, I really enjoyed this game.  I have also heard vets of the genre have really enjoyed it as well.  one of the best games of 2023 so far imo.

_childDocuments_.review: To all new players, you are not playing bloodborne nor dark souls! I see many people getting frustrated because they think they can overcome the game by smacking everything on their way while also relying on a fixed build they feel comfortable with. Lies of P encourages adaptability, imagination and pattern recognition. Hallways are getting too narrow? better off switching to a smaller weapon for now, enemies on this area are too fast? modify your weapon to a better suited combination, the game has so many options for you it can feel overwhelming some times, and that's without considering the extra layer of possibilities when including the different legion arms with their own abilities and character traits.Adapt your play style, experiment with different weapon combinations, use your consumables!One of the absolute best titles to make use of souls-like mechanics out there; the game is absolutely gorgeous, they really went all the way with the attention to details, a beautiful looking game from start to finish. One of the best level design I've experienced, not only visually but also making Krat a joy to traverse; its unlikely you will ever feel the need to rush through an area first time exploring and shortcuts are conveniently well placed. Tons of unique and variant enemies with their own combat patterns, also the enemy placement is excellent, with enough surprises here and there, but never punishingly unfair.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to give this game a good review but It falls just short for me.Using big weapons hinders you.Enemies attacks track almost twice as fast as in other souls-like games.Enemy attacks are very often huge silly strings of sweeping attacks which devalues positioning as a game play choice.Larger enemy (Usually bosses) can have some or all of their animation off screen or covered by their body making it hard to read.Fury attacks change the perfect block and health regain system from a great alternative to simply dodge rolling everything into the 'Correct' way to play. limiting play rather than expanding it.The above issues have in my eyes lead to two of my preferred methods of playing a souls-like to be unavailable in Lies of P. _childDocuments_.review: This is probably my favorite soulsborne game that has come from outside of FromSoftware. If you're a fan of those games, you will almost certainly enjoy this one. The level design and world-building is fantastic. The voice acting is excellent. The story, while not as overt as a standard narrative game, is also not as oblique as the stories in FromSoftware games. You don't have to read item descriptions to know what is going on. Also, there are some great quality of life features in this game, such as character icons on fast travel points, that help you figure out where to go to complete optional side quests so you're not wandering around aimlessly trying to find specific persons of interest if they've moved.The combat is solid mix between Sekiro and Bloodborne. It has the rhythm-blocking mechanic and enemy stamina drain of Sekiro as well as the offensive healing mechanic of Bloodborne. I thought it was a great blend and was able to get into the swing of how the game operates pretty early on. There's a nice variety of enemies and damage types, and some of the boss fights are epic (and brutally difficult).I highly recommend this game to any fan of the soulsborne genre. It's money well spent, even at full price. If you can get it on sale, that's just icing on the cake.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best souls likes to exist, differentiate itself with mechanics, have a great story, and achieveable and fun to achieve achievements for 100 percenting.the mixing, matching, early game, late game, and preponderence of useful items (throwables with stats, easy use cleanses, stealth pot, bleeds, resistances, auto proc the stagger from range) and meaningful upgrades (speccing into multi, charge attacks, blocking, weapon swapping, etc)truly a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ masterpiece. i dumped 75 hours in over 3 play throughs, and im just wishing i could do ng+4 or higher and fight just the bosses. But after 3 runs through it's a bit of a slog to run through the areas with all the long animations for ladders, stargazers, etc. less of an issue your first time when it's all still cool and you're not just booking it for the boss and quartz.The boss pacing is fun and fair with good move sets that can be learned extremely quickly. throwables are like ranged heavy attacks and very useful. you can choose to do more damage via grindstones and speccing, or you can take a defensive tactic and up your ability to guard and regain or have auto perfect guards for a period of time.I just can't say enough good things about thisgame.DOWNSIDES:1.some animations are long, 2. looting you cant just dismiss the item popup and itlocks you out of other actions,3. if you beat an area boss before returning to NPC's you end up invalidating quessts. For examples: A) the church girl, must return the coin to her b4 the boss fight or it fails.B) eugenie, you MUST do the cryptic vessel before talking to her after trismigistus.4. the semi hard cap on stats is rough as you go to higher play throughs. you end up trying to pick a weapon with the MOST combined scaling regardless of which trait it's in, although most are somewhat similar. So at higher NG's you feel a bit annoyed since you can't make anything outrageous with one stat to carry it (reg-ng+2 this works fine, i also did not farm any ergo).5. the legion arms are pretty poorly designed by and large. The good ones are so fun it makes the mechanic useful still, but....one dies fire. one dies shock. one does acid. or you could just, ya know, attack them... more for limited resource runs. aegis? you have a non perfect block unless you time it. and the whole thing is so slow. why would i dedicate time and effort learning that? boss amulet pluss perfect block into heavy is so much faster and staggering. Puppet string, unique, cool, fun, useful, i used this through NG+1. Itll hit for 2,000 eventually. even so, that ends up being pretty risky a large amount of the time and isn't vertical, still so good though. The other good option was eagle eyes. building distance and just pumping 2,000+ damage into the targets for free from range or as you disengage a boss and often getting a stagger as they run at you for you to go in on? insanely good. I would have liked to have seen better designs for these. make the fire one move you around, make the electric one speed you up after getting a charged shot off, make the shield an auto perfect into HUGE damage. Make the mines..... not suck complete cheeks. Do not invest in the mines. you can only have two out at a time and it does about as much as eagle eyes. Terrible.\10/10 game tho, a necessary and wonderful addition to souls/sekiro/bloodborne/P type genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Lies of P is very satisfying to play on a moment-to-moment basis and offers an addictive sense of progression in your personal skills as well as the story. If you want to play a """souls-like""" then play this. While this game borrows very very heavily from its predecessors, it executes each mechanic far better than any of From Software's games.One of my main critiques is that there are a lot of two-phase boss fights where if you die in the second phase you have to redo the first before you can try again. This gets exceedingly tedious, particularly in the penultimate fight of the game, which gets boring after the first couple of times you beat it since all of the boss's attacks are very samey and drawn out, and its health pool is predictably bloated. Lowering the required number of parries for the boss's weapon to break, then concluding the first phase if the player manages to meet that requirement could rectify this issue. To be clear, the boss's weapon shouldn't remain broken in the following phase. As it is, the enemy weapon breakage mechanic is very underutilized, which is a shame since it's a really fun addition.The fourth boss needs some polish. There are some faulty hit boxes,

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely fantastic Soulslike which gives some of From's best work a run for its money. While I don't think it surpasses Sekiro or Bloodborne which it draws most inspiration from, I think it's stronger than Dark Souls 2, 3 and Elden Ring. What a miraculous game. That this team was able to distill so much of why these games work in their first outing, I will never understand. So many cool build possibilities, a world dripping in baroque pestilence, bosses that were uncompromisingly spectacular from a gameplay perspective and a narrative feast for the eyes. Elden Ring made me think I was getting a bit tired of this genre, Lies of P has shown me how much deeper the well goes.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a huge variety of enemies and plenty of toys to cut them down to size. The mechanic of making your own weapon is really unique. Every Handle and Blade has it's own weight, damage, and Fable Arts. I thought I was going to just stick with the first weapon presented to you, but soon realized that was not going to pan out. I switched out my small Wintry Rapier blade for a big Bone-Cutting Saw, while keeping the handle. The result is fighting the same style, but with more range and slower, but more powerful attacks. The Fable art included was a double slam attack that absolutely decimated enemies. There's no consequence and nothing lost with weapon assembly. You can mix and match to your heart's desire. Be sure to scrounge every corner and merchant for new weapons.There is a LOT of creatures in this game. A vast enemy variety to my surprise. From the screenshots, I thought it was just going to be mechanical puppets and such, but there's at least 30+ enemy types that kept me on my toes. There is an abundance of jump scares from freaky monsters that took me by surprise. Or just not even a jump scare, just some weird new abomination hobbling towards me from a dark hallway, leaving me to wonder, . And don't even get me started on the bosses. You think you've seen the worst of it, and then you open a tremendous door to some horrifying beast.The setting is Steampunk done right.  From a glimpse, you may see it as aping BloodBorne, but you couldn't be further from the truth. This is 1800s Victorian style Steampunk in a dark and corrupted style. Bleak factories, automated machinery, and eccentric characters with wild facial hair. This all comes together with the wonderful soundtrack. You'll hear a lot of it throughout the world or playing on record players. A beautiful orchestra of sounds and opera music to juxtapose the dark world of puppet monsters.In short, the game is  The first playthrough took me near 31 hours to complete doing everything. NEOWIZ really did something amazing here.

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that an unknown studio from South Korea whose only other game they made is an MMO speaks volumes to the dedication and appreciation the developers have to the Souls genre especially to my all time fav Souls game that is BloodborneA world that comes alive with stellar sound designs, thrilling fights, and an engaging story not found in most Souls gamesDifficulty is a suggestive thing. I know a lot of the complaints for this game is that it's too hard + even harder than the Souls game or that it's unfair.I found Seikiro to be harder than this game as Lies of P gives you a whole array of tools and mechanics to help you on your journey once you figure it all out.As for the unfairness, you need to throw away your Souls knowledge and understand that this a completely different game with it's rules and mechanics And when the game combats click for you, you'll just have a nonstop blast overcoming the next challenging fight like I did There is some things that keep this game from being perfect (the running back to the boss after getting killed, the perfect parry window being very tight [though it also click for me], the extra dodge abilities being locked behind the upgrade system, 2nd phase difficulty spikes)But for their 1st major AAA game, Studio8 blew it out of the park and have a formula they can make improvements upon for future entriesCan't wait to see what else the developers have in store in the future for this universe that they have created

_childDocuments_.review: My overall experience with the game has been fantastic. I like the artstyle, the characters, the soundtrack and most importantly Combat coupled with the artstyle is the most important part of souls-like games. When combat is executed perfectly it feels like you are a well-oiled terminator killing machine. From perfect parrying, dodging, charging and then delivering a fatal attack on an enemy feels good, if you actually can. The perfect parry window is  small and coupled with almost every enemy delaying and in some cases even holding their attacks until they are close enough to hit you can make you feel frustrated. I wish the perfect parry window was longer or while you are parrying you can let go and parry again to hopefully get that perfect parry. Currently you can't because you are semi-locked into regular parrying unless you roll away.You have no poise, the enemy however does have poise and this creates situations where you are charging a heavy attack but some regular attack by an enemy interrupts it. Can you imagine using a 3 bar fable art and right before it connects with an enemy it gets interrupted by a regular attack. Goodbye 3 fable art bars, it was nice knowing you. This also creates situations where if an enemy attacks fast enough (and they do) and they have an attack combo of 5-10 you can be stunlocked into death.This makes me wish some animations for the player were shorter than they are. The unnecessary loss of control during the buildup of an attack or after an attack has already landed. I've already hit the enemy why is my guy trying to twirl his damn weapon or holding his weapon out just move please. This also makes me wish the player attack animations had a slightly longer reach. The amount of times i thought my attack would connect with an enemy with some weapons that should have longer range and then they didn't was ridiculous. This paired with the fact that almost every enemy has a longer or far longer reach than you soured some fights and made me cheese them with the wrench fable art.The weight system could solve these animation gripes IF weight actually mattered. There is almost no difference in playing light weight, medium weight or heavy weight. The only things that change are your stamina refill rate and your rolling speed. You should be able to run faster or swing your weapon faster at lighter weight but no.Some P-Organ upgrades like the extra dodge and dodge from the ground should be available by default instead of locked behind upgrades but what do i know.It also doesn't help that the saintess statue that allows you to respec your levels, P-Organ and Legion upgrades unlocks roughly in the middle of the game. Weapon upgrade materials are also kind of rare, expecially for special weapons. Want to try out a new weapon? Oh you didn't save your upgrade materials? Too bad, you're punished.The difficulty is here and there. Some encounters with mini-bosses or elite enemies are harder than most of the bosses. Examples are: The mad clown before the opera and the electric version in the swamp, The crazy clown in the arcade cellar and abbey. both the mad clowns and the crazy clown in the abbey can be bypassed by running past them if you so choose to. The crazy clown in the arcade cellar however cannot be passed until you defeat it. I had more trouble with the crazy clown than ANY of the bosses or mini-bosses/elites before it. Let's also not forget the other elite that you encounter in the arcade cellar and malum district that does that very quick spinning attack.I've been hearing people say that  is difficult and it is, because it is the first boss that has 2 phases. Some attacks are very fast and painful but there are plenty of opportunities for counterattacks.I've been hearing people say that the king of puppets is difficult and it is. Phase 1 is fine, Phase 2 is also fine until the half point where the boss launches a multi-hit combo attack at you while chasing you down. This can be frustrating because being stunlocked and watching your character die because you cannot do anything is not great. Despite this there are plenty of opportunities for counterattacking.I've been hearing people say that the swamp monster is difficult and it absolutely is. It was the most frustrating fight in the entire game until then and continued to be the most difficult fight right until the second last boss. Phase 1 was fine, Phase 2 however significantly reduces the amount of counterattacking opportunities not only because the boss is very fast but because the boss has extra delayed attacks and will quickly launch into another combo of attacks. it is also a very quick and mobile boss.If you thought these bosses were difficult then  will make them seem like warmups. If you thought the previous bosses were fast, this boss is quite literally lightning-fast. If you thought the previous bosses hit hard, this boss will murder you. If you thought the previous bosses had stingy counterattack opportunities, this boss will fly halfway across the arena away from you into the air and attack you. it is doable but damn if it wasn't the most difficult fight in the entire game.And finally the final boss is more annoying than difficult due to long-range sweeping attacks and AoE zones that appear in the middle of the map and where the boss is at set intervals.The one encounter that i personally feel like was absolutely spot on was  because not once did i feel like the boss had ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ range, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ speed or ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ combo attacks. If i got hit it was because i made a mistake. Despite all this i however had a great time playing through it the first time and will be doing a NG+ playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best souls-like I've played 9/10.-Beautiful design: Seriously, the world artstyle is amazing and depending where you are on the game the hotel will start changing , like your nose on the wall painting , really good details . -Combat: Perfect blocks feel SO GOOD. Unlike most Souls games, hits feel powerful and slow, but landing that perfect parry is euphoric. Especially the fatal attacks, they feel incredible.-Weapons and builds: Mixing blades and handles to change scalings is awesome , Literally any weapon can be viable, which is super fun. Plus, the Fable Arts add another layer of customization. And resetting Paragon with gold coin fruits just lets you experiment builds all you want. The Legion arms are cool too, this game just nails build variety.-Rich story: Your choices, your lies, your humanity, all shape the story and lead to different endings. It's dark, sad, and depressing, but in a good way. The cinematics are great and you get attached to the characters, so the ending hits hard.Bad stuff-Camera: It NEEDS more options. Stop rotations, adjustable FOV, especially for big bosses. Not seeing their attacks because they're off-screen is annoying.-Level design: 70% is amazing, but the other 30%… ugh. Annoying enemy placement that blocks paths or pushes you off edges. Not cool nor fun.-Body blocks: This is the WORST. Jumping enemies cornering you and getting stuck with no movement or visibility? Died to this SO many times. It happens everywhere, stairs, corners, even under bosses! Getting stuck under a boss after a perfect block is just unfair specially with the swamp boss.-Artificial difficulty : Some bosses are super annoying with faking attack animations , NG+ you literally get 1/2 shot by almost everything , grabs are super annoying on some bosses , the game has a lot of artificial difficulty implemented but if you get used to it you'll clear the game with no problems.Things to keep in mind-Difficulty: It's HARD. If you're new to Souls games or a casual, get ready to learn about perfect blocks, if you don't learn you're not going anywhere.-Linear: No Elden Ring freedom here. Stuck on a boss? You're stuck until you beat it , no cheeses , no get OP early , no ergo (xp/runes) farms , no going around the world for different bosses that are easier.
