_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I watched the first trailer and then played the demo a few months ago I knew that I would enjoy Lies of P.. and that I would probably die a lot, just like in other souls-like games I have played like bloodborne and sekiro. INDEED!!, Those gave me a hard time too.The game itself gives off a unique aura. The puppet conquered streets, the abandoned houses, the people our protagonist meets during his journey, all of those elements give life to the game.You are free to make your own choices. You can either lie or tell the truth, it's all up to you. However you should know that sometimes your decisions have consequences.Another interesting aspect of the game is the weapon system. There are 2 types of weapons. Normal weapons and special weapons. Normal weapons are divided in 2 parts, a handle and a blade. You can disassemble and and reassemble different handles with different blades to create different combos and fable arts. Fable arts are unique skills for each handle. Special weapons on the other hand  are weapons you can obtain by using the rare ergo you acquire from defeating bosses. They cannot be disassembled but they have their own set of skills.I find it very satisfying whenever I perform a perfect guard, and whenever I break an enemy's weapon, and even more when I perform a fatal attack and completely destroy them! The game provides the player with many means to attack and protect themselves. From potions that heal ailments to grindstones that allow weapons to deal different damage types, you can use many different means to protect yourself, or move to the offensive.Finally, I really enjoyed this game's music, not only the one from the boss fights, but from the records that can be found in the various places of Krat too.

_childDocuments_.review: While playing this game, I had only one thought in mind: "WHEN WILL IT FINALLY END?".Pros:* Exceptional optimization* Music* Engaging plot* Victorian style of the gameCons:* PRICE - The game seems super overpriced. I regret purchasing it without a discount. It costs as Elden Ring but doesn't even offer 25% of its content variety. * Much of its content feels borrowed from Dark Souls and Sekiro; the game doesn't seem to introduce anything groundbreaking in terms of game mechanics.* The bosses are underwhelming. It feels as if they were designed solely to ♥♥♥♥ player. After defeating them, I felt empty, especially since I've completed all the Dark Souls games I saw interesting bosses.* The game is super unfair. Blocking, blocking, and more blocking - the game doesn't give you flexibility in how to beat a boss. There's an incredibly short window to block an attack, making these some of the most challenging boss fights compared to other souls-like games.* When you defeat a boss, you might discover that there's a second fight where the second phase has 100% HP, deals more damage, and has more HP than the first phase. Technically, that's fine. BUT when you notice that SIX separate bosses follow the same pattern, it's incredibly annoying.* Camera during boss fight sometimes plays against you* Tunnel locations * Hidden stun scaleI'll re-play in DarkSouls but in Lies of P definetly no!5 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm past the refund so I'll maybe stick through to the end. Lies of P is just not for me. Everything.. I mean just about EVERYTHING pauses before hitting P. FromSoft did this first I believe and I remember laughing because it got me. I did not expect it and got popped (of course) thinking touche FS. But the issue with making just about EVERYTHING pause is it kills the flow of combat for me. Keep in mind the pause can be a quarter of a second, half a second, three quarters of a second, maybe even a second or two. It, as it is designed to do, warps the combat flow. But Neowiz banked on this. I actually read a review for this game that said "bLoOdBoUrNe iS oN pC"... Not even close. That game had combat that flows, Lies of P, gets frustrating. Fights take longer and these Devs had zero issue giving the boss a nice chunk of health to boot. So for me, it becomes tiring. I think these work best when the hits hurt, but the swings come at a rhythm pace. I understand an enemy or two maybe even A boss fighting with the pause style, fine. Take Sekiro as an example. Instead of slow, slllllower and sllllllllllllowest. Sekiro goes fast, faster and fastest. You know what else goes fast? Me in bed. Kidding... kind of. But your heart rate. Slow feels like I want to get into the combat, but instead I am waiting for something to happen too much and find myself constantly standing on the edge but never having the rush of the fall. Kills it for me. When it comes to bosses, at this point you already know. You have your, 50% health switch up combo boss, your 2 stage boss (new form resetting health), you getting jumped by multiple bosses... As someone who does not use the specter (NPC help), once again, tiring. Dragging out an already dragged out fight. Neowiz literally sat there, looked at FromSoft and said "YEAH! But lets go one step further!" Instead of the normal, block till you loose all stamina option, Neowiz goes a new route. You have the normal i-frames (which is fine), but you also have a perfect guard. Which is just blocking at the last second. If you do not, you take damage every single time (1/3 of the damage I guess). They even lie to force this mindset. We all know the red attack (in game called fury attack). Red = dead. So roll out? NO! You can "ONLY perfect guard". This is a lie. There is an entire room, hallway, road behind you. You can dodge back but the rubber band is STRONG with these. So be careful if you go to dodge. Main issue with me is sometimes the fury attack is too fast. Not so much the attack but by the time the game gives the warning (turns red) the enemy is already falling on you. Although rare, it can happen. And again, even if you hold guard down, full damage if not a perfect guard for fury attacks. Now on to the levels. They are extremely linear. Which isn't the worst imo. But if you get on a boss and get stuck or tried and want to switch it up a bit, well, keep fighting him because there is nowhere else to go. I hate to say it but all Neowiz did was take an established IP and told FromSoft to hold their beer. So far I've only gotten what I call the SoulsBourne Rush one time. When you start feeling the rush by barely squeaking by with a amazingly last second parry or dodge 3/4 times in a row and the hits are too close for comfort but you got it and eventually it leads to the W. Once. I had that one time so far. Issue with these parry only kind of games is once you have the rhythm down, you're done. I KNOW for a fact the game sometimes has an issue with button commands. Hitting the attack or dodge button two/three times before it does anything if at all. Not all the time, but brace for it.  Graphics are nice. Acting is good and music is great! But the one thing I need more than anything is lacking imo. The combat. I truly wish devs would stop trying to either copy directly from FS or even worse, find ways to make it "hArdEr" for no reason. This INCLUDES how you turn OFF the game. Seriously!? It is not the worst game ever, by no means. But when combat is your bread and butter it seems weird you go with the slow build up with a fast swing or fast build up but a slow swing. These are purposely put in just to trip the player up non stop. Mix that with the usual line up of bosses. 1 V 1, 2 V 1, 2 stage V 1, BIGBOSS V LilP... And yes, the big bosses will push you around taking the camera with it. Its all here! Same ish, different game. Shame devs don't sit back and look into why Maria (Bloodbourne) is the #1 boss of all time (IMO). No gimmicks, no massive chunk of blob taking up your screen or camera, no multi stage health bar. Just a one on one fight, someone your size and the hits kept coming while in a beautiful setting. BB REALLY needs to come to PC. If you get Lies of P, go for the sale. Sadly, you may be hours in until frustration builds to irritation so refunds probably wont happen.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game, please do not listen to the people spouting the terrible opinions about it. I give it a solid 9/10 and deem it "must play" for anyone that enjoys these types of games. I urge the developers to beware of trying to appease the people complaining about certain difficulty aspects of the game. Don't lose your identity by chasing a larger audience. Just continuing improving on your game and the sale will continue to come. Some feed back from me personally: some weapon types could stand to see some improvements, particularly the more nimble weapons especially during boss fights. The issue I encountered frequently was they simply cant compete with the larger heavier hitting weapons in terms of effectiveness due to the additional chip damage you take when blocking attacks and the fact that you are frequently pushed out of range when blocking to get any significant punishes off even when perfect guarding efficiently. On top of that, the lower attack rating makes it require more perfect guards to break poise of the the attacker. All these factors combined just means you have to perfect guard more often, are punished far more heavily when you miss it due to additional chip damage and when you're counter attacking you do less damage. I would like to see additional benefits bestowed on these weapons to close the gap between them and the large weapons for a better variety of viable options to choose from during these excellent boss fights. A great start is making the parry fable arts for the weapons more instantaneous (far less wind up) but in exchange it should cost fable arts meter weather you land it or not, and perhaps make it cost more fable arts meter so builds that focus on this play style also have to use quarts more heavily on fable arts meter upgrades rather than increasing their cell charges putting emphasis on on precision but offering big pay offs if you master it. Like if you made the fable arts for these weapons more powerful and made most of them reliable gap closer combo starters options that can be used during combat rather than a heavy handed stagger punish that takes a aot of time to complete (which most are) this would give this weapon class a different identity from the slow methodical play of block and punishing that the larger weapons offer and accelerate at.

_childDocuments_.review: Lies of P is a successful souls-like for many fans, a decent product considering it's their first game in this genre, but sadly they took way too much inspiration from the original creators of the genre and just didn't quite manage to reach where I would've loved them to be, above Nioh 2 or The Surge. It's a game that has an incredible start and then just throws it all away into the garbage in its late half...👍 +Great atmosphere for the first half of the game+Amazing soundtrack👎-Horrible late game in terms of everything-Way too many shamefully copy-pasted mechanics that don't click wellLies of P is a unique "retelling" of the story created by Carlo Collodi, a twisted version of puppets and humans. Without spoiling much, the gist is, the world has managed to harness some form of, let's call it a mineral, called Ergo, which gave life to automatized puppets. Thus began a new age in Krat where to game takes place, where puppets and humans lived quite happily on the surface of things and not so much behind the curtains. You awaken on a train and you are shortly thrown into a city dominated by murderous puppets which somehow lost control and killed almost all the humans. You soon meet some interesting characters that will help you on your journey, characters which are references from the original story of Pinnochio. As you can imagine the main aspect is the "Lie" mechanic, which takes form in the game as a dialogue choice. You'll have plenty of dialogue choices where you can either lie or tell the truth. How these choices impact the game is for you to discover. Overall, it's certainly a messed up story, with some twists here and there and it's without a doubt far more cohesive than what From Software gave us, but it isn't something I'd say I like or love. It was fine, it did its job and that's about it.Story rating: 7/10Lies of P is certainly in the top of the best 3D souls-like games, but that aint saying much when it comes to my own tastes. The Surge and Nioh 2 are still the only ones that came close and even surpassed in certain aspects, a few From Software games. Lies of P would be somewhere in the third place, but far from the first two. It tries to be too many things and it doesn't succeed well in either. It tried to be Sekiro by forcing players to perfect guard all the enemy attacks, but most enemy animations are absolute dog sht and to make matters worse your character model has a far bigger hit detection than its body as most bosses and enemies will hit you even tho visually their weapons did not actually touch your body. You can dodge, but the game does not have any i-frames which means it's absolutely useless and you'll always get hit unless you upgrade your dodge and get a certain amulet late in the game. That along with stiff animations and movement, most of the time you have no choice but to rely on the dodgy perfect-guard mechanic or the simple guard mechanic. Balancing is also way off, as you progress more in the game, enemies become tanks and you remain a two-hit target practice. Stats feel useless and are just barely helping, the game has blitz, fire, and toxic damage which you'd think impacts certain enemies, however, the impact is incredibly minimal. I had no trouble dealing the same amount of damage with blitz to human enemies compared with fire. Toxic is the most useless of the three. Weapons are also incredibly weak and if you loved playing two-handed weapons in souls or other souls-like games, I have bad news for you. As I mentioned before the game tries to be Sekiro in its mechanics, which means almost all bosses and enemies will attack you quite fast, so fast that you will barely have time to hit them with the incredibly slow two-handed weapons. You can do 2 times the damage with a one-handed weapon compared to a 2-hander and you'll still have time to guard/perfect-guard. The game also has a stance/weapon break mechanic, and certain enemies and even bosses can get their weapons damaged if you perfect guard them A LOT of times. It's mostly useless and their weapons will still deal almost the exact same damage. Stunning them is worth it as most enemies can get stunned and then you can deal insane amounts of damage. Besides the usual stats that you level up such as health, stamina, etc. the game has a unique skill tree where you can further upgrade your character. Sadly it's half-assed like most of its mechanics aka half of that skill tree is useless. There is a unique mechanic, but I wouldnt exactly make it a selling point, you can disassemble most weapons and combine their handles to create more unique weapons but almost all handles have the exact same stats and besides having having different attack animations, it really doesnt do much and you'll use it only a few times to make yourself one good weapon for most of the game. Gameplay rating: 7/10When it comes to the soundtrack, I have to admit I was quite impressed considering it's a sorta indie/AA game. The music especially in some boss fights is phenomenal just as good as peak Souls games. The voice acting was surprisingly good as well.As for the sound effects, they're all pretty decent, nothing that stood out. Audio rating: 8/10The game runs perfectly, no stuttering, no performance drops and it's almost entirely bug-free which is quite rare these days. To be fair, it's a very linear game and a lot of the environments are not very good-looking. Looks good for the first half of the game and then the devs just threw it all away and got very lazy as the late half has the most boring and uninspired-looking locations you've ever seen. To make matters worse it seems these devs lack a complete understanding of what sets From Software games apart from the rest of the pack. It's not just the gameplay, but the level design is a HUGE aspect and as important as the gameplay, the way it's masterfully crafted, a 3D metroidvania with tons of paths and secrets to discover. Lies of P fails in this regard, as most of the game is as linear as Resident Evil 4. It's not really a bad thing, but an almost 40hour souls-like game where you mostly just go forward and sometimes circle around a bit? Not a good look especially once you're in the late game as the game seemingly just won't end. Graphics, performance and tech analysis score: 7/10I initially did not feel like giving it a thumbs up as the game has a lot of poorly done enemies, locations and even boss fights and it just doesn't do anything to set itself apart(again, the handle/disassemble thing was not as deep or unique as you might think) like Nioh 2 did with it's incredibly unique gameplay or The Surge with it's awesome limb mechanics. It's a good first attempt, better than most, but not quite as good as many praise it to be. Get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not play this game if you're expecting quality combat.  The combat system is lazily implemented with parts stolen from other souls like games with zero thought or care to how those parts interact.  What you end up with is a slow as dirt playable character who can't react and enemies and bosses who are fast enough you need to react.  This turns the game into a slog where the only option is to throw yourself at something ad nausea until you learn the fight inside and out.  The game also forces you to utilize the parry mechanic that derives difficulty from unnatural animations that have randomly placed pauses in an effort to "trick" the player.  Additionally, some animation are simply not visible to the player due to the size of the boss.  This is on top of a parry system that drops inputs and often times just doesn't work.  Many times where I am pressing and holding the guard button and nothing happens as you get hit for the full amount.  This game's setting and story would have had it sitting at the top of the genre but instead it will be known for its lazily implemented combat system.Edit: List of things I've noticed since this review... more dropped inputs, often time the block just doesnt register.  Enemies can spin on a dime to face you mid attack motion making the dodge mechanic useless.  Seen my weapon pass right though enemies with no damage registered numerous times.  Just lazy, lazy development which is a shame given the story is interesting.edit edit: just asked for a refund for this game.  The glaring and persistent issues with the combat system make the story not worth seeing such a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: More ,,straightforward" or should I say linear level design and storytelling than other souls-like games, but this is definitely a good one. Nice atmosphere, nice visuals, OPTIMIZED well enough which you cannot say about many of the newer game titles. _childDocuments_.review: A lovely souls-like, perhaps one that does not spend effort in innovating as much as it does refining and distilling the beloved elements of the genre. The player is equipped with the hugely powerful perfect block mechanic from Sekiro, reasonable i-frames on a step-dodge, and a balanced blocking system that rewards confidence and tempered aggression. The story is engaging and, thank god, not hidden behind item descriptions, loading screens, or (needlessly) missable npc engagements. The game is a blessing for the FOMO player in all of us, with reminders and visual indicators for optional npc questlines. The bossfights have short respawn approaches and fair health bars. I found the movesets of many enemies to be less fluid and intuitive than Sekiro; the first experiences with most enemies that couldn't be stunned lock resulted in needless damage taken or death. I do consider this a flaw, but not an insurmountable one. It is only as much a flaw as you are unenthusiastic to die and try again. In my experience, the game is fun and tight enough that a handful of deaths in the process of improvement didn't bother me any.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece.  A brilliant take on Pinocchio, if the world was a dark fantasy filled with twisted puppets and shattered humanity.  The lore is both easily accessible and hidden away - allowing players to easily understand the overarching story but rewarding exploration with a surprisingly deep story set against a metaphysical backdrop of, "what does it mean to be a human."This game is absolutely the best souls-like game released that wasn't made by FromSoftware.  It draws heavily on FS's past titles for inspiration but also innovates in key ways that I felt dramatically improved on a few things I always struggled with in souls games.  The two highlights of this system are the weapon assembly system and the empty pulse cell mechanic.  Find a cool weapon you like but it has an annoying moveset, or scales with the dex stat instead of strength?  Well swap out the handle and it now is a dex weapon with the same moveset as your old weapon!  This game uses pulse cells as the healing item, and when you fully exhaust all of them, then damaging enemies allows you to refill the last cell technically infinite times.  This let me clutch moments against tough bosses or continue through world areas without having to rest to restore my health items.  Such a small quality of life change that made such a difference.The world design is brilliant, and each area feels distinct and hand crafted.  Despite cool interconnected areas and unlockable shortcuts, the game is very linear, which can be a turn off for many players.  Personally, I found it refreshing as I always knew where to go and each area felt specifically designed to show off the amazing environments.  Bosses are another highlight, with a minor caveat.  Each boss was both fantastic and fantastical, and some were quite a visual spectacle that was sometimes lost by my panicked blocking and focus on the boss.  The latter half of the game does throw annoying dual phase fights repeatedly against the player, where the boss starts slow and ponderous and ends up fast and deadly.  This was entertaining, to a point.  Sometimes I would perfect my phase one technique but struggle in phase two, meaning each death was an annoying restart of a phase I had already mastered.Despite these annoyances, the devs carefully provided a number of difficulty modifiers to help players.  Most bosses have a summonable NPC specter to assist, drastically reducing the fight difficulty.  In addition, throwable items are wildly powerful and spamming even a handful of them into a boss make huge dents in the healthbar.  Deciding whether or not to use specters or throwables is up to the player, but they can be very helpful for those who don't want to spend multiple attempts memorizing attack patterns for perfect parry retaliations.Final Note - recent patches have adjusted readability on many enemy attacks and added a few unlockable abilities as base kit (like dodging from prone after being knocked down) which further makes the new player experience a bit easier!  Don't miss out on this game, I fully recommend it even at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review:
You wake up at an abandoned train station in Krat, a city overwhelmed by madness and bloodlust. In front of you lies a single note that reads:

"Find Mr. Geppetto. He's here in the city."

Play as Pinocchio, a puppet mechanoid, and fight through everything in your path to find this mystery person. But don't expect any help along the way and don't make the mistake of trusting anyone.

You must always lie to others if you hope to become human.

Inspired by the familiar story of Pinocchio, Lies of P is an action souls-like game set in a cruel, dark Belle Epoque world.

name: A Little to the Left
detailed_description: Sort, stack, and organize household objects into just the right spot in A Little to the Left, a tidy puzzle game with a mischievous cat who likes to shake things up! Puzzles hidden among household objects Multiple solutions make for intuitive and satisfying puzzle design A puzzle unique for you every day with The Daily Tidy Delivery Perfect for casual puzzle game fans and those who get a jolt of satisfaction from a well organized space Feel free to skip levels with the 'Let It Be' option, and choose when you want to tackle certain messes Need a hint? A little or a lot? With a unique hint system, you control how much of the solution is revealed in each level. Which way should the clock hands point? How to arrange the eggs? Who put so many stickers on this fruit?!? Come enjoy a calming world in an observational puzzle game with surprises around every corner. Featuring charming illustrations and surprising scenarios, A Little to the Left is satisfying and curious with over 100 delightful puzzles to discover. Keep your eye out for a mischievous cat who has an inclination for chaos! In the Daily Tidy mode, you’ll get a puzzle delivered EVERY DAY with variations on our favorite puzzles that’s unique to you. Find all the solutions each day to earn fun badges! If only tidying in real life was this rewarding. Want that festive joy in July? Feeling like a fright in May? A Little to the Left now features a puzzle Archive, granting permanent access to the formerly limited-time seasonal levels. Now enjoy messes based around Xmas, Easter, Halloween, and more, no matter the month. FEATURES: Over 100 unique logical puzzles Quick-to-solve puzzles make for satisfying gameplay Intuitive drag and drop controls A puzzle unique to you delivered each day with The Daily Tidy Delivery Multiple solutions Charming illustration Atmospheric sound design A mischievous (but very cute) cat Funny and playful, great for all ages!

_childDocuments_.review: I have had my eyes on this game for quite a while, I think I first saw it on a wholesome direct and it felt like someone had made a game specifically for my weird enjoyment of menial virtual tasks. I thought it would just be a nice little organisation game, something satisfying. But it's also a fantastic puzzle game! I don't think it's super hard but I've had to take time to think and I absolutely love that for some levels there are a number of different ways to solve them and you can go back to get the other methods. While I think you could probably work your way through the game pretty fast there seem to be daily challenges coming out, at least a year is planned for this it seems so there's a lot of content. So if you want a chill and not too tricky puzzle game (at least what it seems like from the early levels) I really think this game is worth your money.Also the art is super charming, the music is chill and my silly little reptile brain gets pleased by ordering things nicely.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming and enjoyable! I can feel the love put into the game from every ounce of content, my only real gripe would be that there is, very minimal replay value. _childDocuments_.review: This is the type of game I adore.  I have played Unpacking, a similar game, on three different systems because I like them so much.  I was hoping this game would give me a similar experience, of satisfying puzzle solving and a cute environment.  While it delivers in the environment, sound design, and visuals, the game itself feels unpolished in a way that I felt I needed to review.  While most of the puzzles are solvable with some patience, others require a near pixel-perfect adjustment or clicking to get the game to recognize the solution.  The hint system is helpful at times and completely unhelpful in others.  In the  one of the hints is for a completely different, previous puzzle.  I have dyscalculia, and relied on the hints in several levels because of it, and when the hints were broken or the game would not recognize the correct solution, it led to immense frustration.  I streamed the game to my partner as I played, and they shared my frustration - being unable to tell if you are doing the puzzle wrong or the game is bugging does not make for a relaxing puzzle solving experience.  Were these kinks worked out, I would have loved the game.  As it stands, I cannot recommend it, and I say that with great disappointment.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: [EDIT] Just so you know, the last DLC is riddled with bug, and instead of making an announce so you know that X level is currently bugged, they do so in a discussion so they don't tarnish their release with "warning it's bugged". This will honestly affect my review of the game as a whole, it's an unacceptable behavior to hide what is happening and leave you searching for half an hour just to avoid to have an announcement which would let you know that this and that thing aren't fixed.I have some difficulties to judge this game, even though I bought it at release and played along the dailies and specials. Dailies are actually my problem and what is making me want to give this advice : Buy this game on sale.A Little To The Left is a cozy puzzle games which will allow you to relax and even scratches that itch of "I want everything to be ranged in this specific order" as it's the point of it. The whole game in itself is satisfying, as I said, it scratches that itch and does it properly all along its numerous levels.HOWEVER, if you're expecting the same for the dailies, prepare to be disappointed. The dailies are no others than a little selection of those puzzles you already solved with random items coming from other puzzles, but it's only a few of those puzzles on repeat over and over again, which means that this itch that brought you to that game is now tainted by the fact you already did those 10 puzzles in repeat (I honestly think it's more around 7 identical puzzles all week long) but there is no novelty beside that today you'll be sorting pasta instead of leaves. I do appreciate the addition of specials for Christmas and Easter, but I would love even more than instead of those 10 puzzles, every single one of them would be added little by little so you don't feel like you're doing the same thing every day for the sake of getting your achievement, because at some point, it becomes more that than scratching an itch. You already know the limited set of dailies and it's "one more thing do do" rather than being surprised by this one puzzle you didn't have since a while.So this is my plea to the dev : You promised dailies, dailies there are but doing the same set 100 times is honestly not a pleasure. Your puzzles are already made, so add them little by little to the dailies instead of serving the same annoying set of sands to sort by range of colors and then by shape which I seem to get 3 times a week and got me away from the game for quite some time. The material is there, pretty please, make the dailies fun and not a pain.

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left advertises itself as an "tidying simulator" and that is true for some of the puzzles. I enjoy the way all of the objects feel and sound when moved and how they all snap into place; it's very cathartic. However, I think a game like that comprises of only that would get old quickly and luckily the creators of this game seem to agree. You quickly learn that many of the levels can be solved in multiple ways, and that's where the secret genius of A Little to the Left is unlocked.The game, especially over the course of its expansions, morphs into a puzzle game about recognizing logical and visual patterns. Since the game never gives written instructions on anything, you're really forced to sit there and scan for the little details in items. I was frequently blown away by comically tiny details such as the lines on a mug because you realize how intricately every item in the game was sculpted to make these patterns line up. Not all of the puzzles are amazing at this, but when A Little to the Left is at its best there's not many other puzzles games quite like it. Don't boil this title down to a "wholesome cleaning game"; it's a lot smarter than it lets on.

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable for people who like sorting objects like myself. This game kept me from completely losing interest as a whole and made me feel better when I felt like my life had no meaning. Like, it is literally just a game, but it really did help me get back on my feet.Additionally, my save file was bugged for a while and I corresponded with the Max Inferno team and they put so much time and care into helping me out and solved the issue in about a week. _childDocuments_.review: After a little over four hours of gameplay, I can say that while I have played more exciting or technically impressive games, I have rarely played one as charming as this.The game is exceptionally lovingly designed, and everything is coherent and fits well together. The music is also just right for a puzzle game, neither too intrusive nor too dull.A bit about the gameplay: You move from puzzle to puzzle, with most puzzles taking place on a single screen. Sometimes you need to arrange objects in a specific order, other times you have to recognize hidden patterns. With a bit of thought, you can always find the solution, and some puzzles even have multiple solutions! I find it particularly enjoyable to discover which alternative solutions the game demands. The graphic style is reminiscent of hand-drawn artworks and is not only very atmospheric overall with a beautiful color scheme, but it also allows for fatigue-free puzzle solving, as the screen never feels overloaded or 'loud.'Overall, you can tell in every corner and almost every puzzle that this game wasn't made just to make a quick buck but that a lot of heart and care went into 'A Little to the Left.'If I had to criticize anything, it would probably be that the controls are sometimes a bit finicky, but so far, that hasn't detracted from my enjoyment of the game.In some puzzles, a cat decides it wants to join in and cause some mischief. And just like with a real cat, you can't be mad at the virtual pet because it's too cute (cat owners will know what I mean!), even though you usually only see its paw :)All in all, it's a very fun and at the same time very relaxing cozy game, full of clever puzzles whose difficulty gently increases as the game progresses, and imaginative ideas.If you like puzzle games (and cats),  supporting the charming developers and giving the game a chance is a no brainer for me!(If you don't like cats, by the way, that's okay too ;) )
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A nice and relaxing casual experience, if a bit short (as of this review, I have fully solved every puzzle in the game except for the stupid candle one. _childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game fairly close to its release date as I and a friend were highly anticipating it after seeing it advertised to us several times. Unfortunately, we found the advertisements to be fairly misleading. We were anticipating a mostly sorting-based game, only to find it to be a relatively small portion of the game (like the drawer levels). We each finished the game, mutually agreed "well, that wasn't what I'd really wanted or was expecting" and never played it again. Gave it the fairest shot I could. And then some time later they release a DLC for more levels like what they were advertising in the first place... lol.This game is relaxing and the art style is pleasing. I did enjoy the puzzles that were like what was being advertised. If this game were entirely about putting pens and screws into their right spots, I would have ten times the playtime. The later levels in particular I found to be progressively less enjoyable, although there are uninteresting puzzles throughout. I can't find it in me to recommend others spend like $20 CAD on a relatively short-life puzzle game with hit-or-miss puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Such a wonderful and relaxing game. The art is beautiful and sets the moods for the game. Kudos to the team for continuing with the daily and seasonal challenges as well, that's a lot of work and it is done so well!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Simple puzzle game that either requires no thinking at all or the aim/solution is obtuse. Some enjoyable segments, but mostly the puzzles were not satisfying to solve. By far the most annoying part of the game is the daily puzzle mechanic, where you have to wait 24 hours since the completion of the last daily to unlock the next segment. You can only unlock one daily per day (they don't 'store up' the unlocks) and 100% achievement completion is locked behind doing at least 100 of these things, with an achievement requiring a 30 day streak as well. All of the dailies are reiterations of the same puzzle types you play in the main game. Making you log in repeatedly for over a month really soured my impression of this game, not going to bother 100%ing it. Wouldn't recommend paying full price for this game considering over half of the 'content' is time gated.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hoping for something to tell a visual story like Unpacking...  And what I got was a very simple, hand-holdy "puzzle" game where you just move things around until they snap to a spot, and then keep trying different items in different snap-to spots until you hear a chime.  Repeat ad-nauseum.  Which is a shame, because the visuals are lovely and I LOVE knolling and organizing.  After the third "put these pencils in order" level I got bored enough to quit.You also cannot re-map key bindings.  From what I played you likely won't have to use the keyboard, but there was one level that my mouse just couldn't get something to move far enough to snap-to and chime so I had to use WASD to complete the level.  I am not a WASD keymap player for accessibility reasons.  So this game is potentially not accessible to some players if they need to use the keyboard and don't or can't use WASD.I'm disappointed!

_childDocuments_.review: This was a game that I had happened to find on a video through Youtube Shorts, and I thought it had been interesting.  I love to organize, and it seemed like a creative game!  It didn't take long for me to figure out what game this was and purchased it.  The game itself has a cute little hand-drawn charm to it which is what also drew me in, the puzzles soon captivating me.  Each puzzle was unique with a few different repeats, and there were even a couple puzzles that had a few different ways of solving them!  I really enjoyed how much it got my brain to thinking about different matches.  Every chapter was also different too, like the food-themed one, or the workbench chapter.  There were always items I didn't think really belonged in a couple items, but to be honest, everyone has some sort of random junk in their drawers on occasion.  The Special events for the Daily Tidy was also a cute little addition and I loved how different those were!  It brought in some of the knowledge you gained from previous puzzles, but also brought in new ways of solving things.The music was soothing, though it did get a tiny bit monotonous towards the end of my achievement hunting.  The only time I remember the music changing was towards the end.  Personally, I think it adds to the relaxing atmosphere and can't think of anything else that could be played while you go through the puzzles. I just wish that the hints for the puzzles were a little better about explaining what needed to be done.   Erasing the lines to reveal the hints were cute, but I struggled with learning what to do with some of the puzzles we were given.  However, this is a tiny issue in comparison to all the good things the game does.I personally enjoyed this game a lot and definitely recommend it to anyone that enjoys organizing or just needs to kill a little bit of time~  Definitely worth the purchase!

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is a delightful, stress-free experience perfect for those who find joy in tidying up and organizing, all within a beautifully crafted and relaxing world.Offering a soothing, orderly escape from the chaos of everyday life, the game invites players to sort and organize household items, turning mundane tasks into satisfying challenges. The simplicity of arranging books, kitchenware, and office supplies based on size, color, or shape becomes surprisingly addictive, especially when a mischievous cat adds playful disruptions.With over 75 puzzles, the game gradually increases in complexity, requiring more thoughtful solutions as you progress. While the early levels are straightforward, later puzzles introduce more abstract thinking, making each new challenge feel fresh and engaging. The game’s warm pastel visuals and soothing soundtrack create a calming atmosphere, encouraging players to take their time and enjoy the process.Despite a few puzzles that might feel a bit obtuse, the game’s hint system provides gentle guidance without giving away all possible solutions. The inclusion of a “Daily Tidy” feature adds replayability, offering new puzzles every day.Overall, A Little to the Left is a tranquil escape, perfect for those who find peace in putting things in order. With its gentle challenges, relaxing visuals, and calming soundtrack - it offers a stress-free escape into a beautifully crafted world where the simple act of creating order brings satisfaction and peace.It's asking price is pretty fair, but I'd personally get it when it is on sale. It regularly goes on sale for under $10 and is totally worth it at that price point.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

Great game!

_childDocuments_.review: is an unorthodox puzzler in which for 4 or so hours, you sort knifes, power tools, chess pieces, stars and shadows into perfect little formations. All while avoiding the nefarious motions of your overlord kitty, hellbent on destroying your attempts at neatness. It is a calming, casual experience that I found occasionally quite difficult, mostly since the latter stages lack the logical basis of earlier ones. You can never truly expect what comes next, sorting flowers by colour or turning tires into sugar, and it makes for a constantly entertaining and equally perplexing series of solutions. Solutions which, without the help of a friend (honourable mention to James) I would not have found. But don't let that put you off, if you can't figure something out immediately, the game doesn't penalise you in any meaningful way for skipping it or using the hint system.  The only game I can compare this to is , which similarly has you sorting items into neat stacks or layouts, sporting the same cosy atmosphere and colourful look. But it's definitely more a defined puzzler than that game.  While  has multiple solutions, this game mostly has just the one. But if you liked that game, I imagine you'll like this too. Anyway, this is one I really enjoyed and implore you to try. It's well worth its asking price despite it's relatively short length. These are, to me, a kind of "best of" collection building on the main games more conventional sorting, space efficiency puzzles. One's where you match up, and slot things into their rightful places. But expanded with additional functionality, namely, drawers and cupboards can now be opened and closed to reveal more stuff inside. As a result, they are bigger and often take a little longer, so while there might be only 25 levels, trust me it is a lot. My favourite being the box that continually opens with secret compartments the more you put into place, a puzzle inside a puzzle. But all of them were great and flowed perfectly from one another, even brandishing a return of the evil kitten in the form of 4 interlude levels. It took me a little under 2 and a half hours to complete (the DLC), which is outstanding considering the price and quality. So if you buy this game, buy all of it.

_childDocuments_.review: A little to the left is a good game, but I don’t think everybody will feel they got their money’s worth. The game promotes itself as a relaxing, organizing puzzle game. _childDocuments_.review: I sincerely think it's not fair that you've added demanded daily play achievements for 100% completion. Can't recommend it for that reason alone, even if the game itself is short and sweet.EDIT: It appears that a developer has responded to this review. Please do understand that while I did enjoy my time with this game, I cannot support daily grind achievements. While there ARE many people who enjoy daily tidies, there are people who DON'T at the same time. By adding these, you're locking several players out of 100% completion.What if somebody isn't able to get to their computer one day? A 30 day grind achievement is REQUIRED for 100% completion, and if somebody misses a single day? Boom. Done.I'm sorry, but I still do not think these should be in the game. By rewarding fans of the tidies, you have accidentally created a situation where you've locked several people out of a complete experience. My genuine suggestion is to at least remove the DAILY ones. The 7, 14, 30 ones. These lock a HUGE majority of individuals out of the achievements at hand.Please do keep in mind, I am a fan of what is here, and I would legitimately love to give this game a positive review for the gentle puzzles and serene atmosphere. But I'm sorry, I just do not think it's justifiable or correct to have these achievements on hand.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, no.  There's no rhyme or reason to the organisation in this game, and I LOVE to organise according to rhyme and reason.  Any job I've been in, I've inevitably been the one to go back and straighten up messes left from before my time, because it's a constant presence in my mind until I fix it.  But you're going to annoy the h e double out of me if you come along after I've arranged it without any help from you (and I do mean that, I refused to use the hints, because this is the kind of game that really shouldn't need hints) and suddenly you have all KINDS of ideas on why the way I did it is wrong. _childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, but rather short.  I enjoyed most of it, but there were some issues that bothered me, and maybe worth considering by those wanting to buy it.  The biggest problem I had was that the puzzles don't have any introduction as to what you have to do to solve them.  On many puzzles, this is the biggest challenge.  Once you figure it out, the solution is trivial.  I am not fond of this genre.  I like a challenging puzzle where the rules are given to you and you spend your time applying them to solve the puzzle.  Anyway, there is a hint system, which can unstick you and there is also a "let it be" button to skip. I used both.  In a few cases, as far as I could tell, the puzzle was solved , but it wouldn't move on, so I used the latter button. Despite my annoyance with some aspects, I still recommend it heartily.

_childDocuments_.review: If we ignore the Daily Tidy achievements, which are the epitome of worthless padding just to grind out a number (100 days of the same 10-12 puzzles? _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I mean this is really good, for some people like me. The art style the gameplay is good but for general gamer like me, I might complete this game too fast, I ran out of level to play really fast (I complete the entire game 100% in 5 hours including DLC) So it would be more interesting if dev add more levels or make the level more complex taking more time to complete. Compare this to other games, it's too easy. Nonetheless it was a really good experience.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay/art style scratches the itch of appreciating the beauty and design of everyday objects. Adding the chaotic cat energy honestly enhanced this calming experience and gave it more life. I'm currently playing the Seeing Stars DLC, it's really fun how the solutions were kicked up a notch and encourage you to explore even more. Thank you for creating and sharing this game!!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for A Little to the Left to come to iPad since the game first came out. Decided to wait no longer and am playing on my PC and laptop. I knew I would love this game and it does not disappoint! I started in the archives and some of the first puzzles I did were pretty tough and stressful but I have since gotten in the flow and do find it very relaxing. After studying solutions when I just could not figure out what to do and reading some 'Tips & Tricks' blogs I now know what basic kinds of things to look for. So happy I broke down and got A Little to the Left!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: In general, I very much enjoyed this game. I found many of the puzzles to be quite clever, if a bit obtuse at first. I appreciated the multiple possible solutions for each puzzle. And I, for one, actually really appreciated how no puzzle actually has a stated end goal within itself. It is just presented and you have to figure out what you are even attempting to do, which I think is really the puzzle at its core.I think my one gripe with the game, outside of its length vs. cost, is the fact that the difficulty of the puzzles doesn't seem to progress in a logical sense. A lot of the earlier puzzles are easier ones, but you will occasionally run into one that is leagues harder than the previous few, and you will wonder where this difficulty came from. And yes, even though there are chapters, the puzzles within each chapter don't even follow a difficulty progression. This could be just the way I looked at the puzzles and your experience with them may differ ever so slightly, though.That being said, I enjoyed the trickier puzzles and only wish there were more of them.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I felt this game was too short. It was cute but I kept waiting for that moment where I could get lost in the game. The entire game went by and that did not happen for me. Some people will like this a lot. This is the type of game I do usually like to play but something about it was just off for me and I feel like I wasted 3 hours of my time with this. If you like puzzles you will probably like this. I'm disappointed because it looked so cute.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A delicate blend of: cute, elegance, challenge, elegant design, and cat memes. The game is woefully short, but it makes up for it with a delicate charm. I found most of the puzzles to be "easy", in that it was clear what the game wanted you to do and how to do it. About 5% of the levels and additional solves required a bit of savvy but not in a way that would be frustrating for the user. This game was oddly calming for me while I've heard others say that the game feels frustrating. There is no time pressure here; take your time and find new ways to look at things. On a final note, I found the game's music to be mesmerizing, even luring. Any puzzle fan should have this game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking for a relaxing but satisfying game after Unboxing, and this looked very similar. You basically just click and drag objects until they are in some kind of "satisfying" order, like arranging books in height order.The first few levels were easy, but satisfying. Then the game quickly devolved into really confusing levels where it's not clear at all what you're supposed to be doing. For example, there's a level with a calendar and a pack of stickers with flowers, dots, squiggles, etc. Some stickers have already been placed on the calendar, so you need to figure out which days you should put the rest of them on. After a while of not being able to figure it out, I went to the forum, and someone said that you just have to put a sticker every 9 days. Why? I don't understand. What appointment does anyone have that is every 9 days?? How is the player meant to figure that out???After a few of these puzzles I was becoming genuinely irritated. I don't mind paying a lot for a niche indie experience but I'm probably just going to refund this one.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely such a charming, cozy organizing game. I feel like I chewed through it so quickly, but having a 'daily tidy' makes it worth it to keep going back for a little brain teaser. I also love that there are a few puzzles where there are many different ways to solve it! The music is calming and a really nice background to a lovely charming game. Plus there is a fluffy white cat who WILL cause problems while you play. Hope there will be more DLC to come, because I demolished the Cupboards and Drawers so quickly. If you get this, maybe limit yourself to one puzzle a day to really savor the game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I was interested in the game after playing the demo, and I like the game, but if you're looking for a similar experience to Unpacking this might not be it. The first chapters hit that vibe for me, but the later chapters have more "there is only one solution" puzzles, and some of them are just kind of confusing. Though I don't think any of the puzzles have any completely out of nowhere solutions, sometimes it does feel like you just have to do what the game wants despite finding another satisfying way (and there's still one puzzle solution I cannot figure out the logic behind, but only that one) I was hoping for more multiple solution puzzles, but they only make up about a fourth of the campaign puzzles. Also the ending was weird and I think it went on for a bit too long, but it was very pretty.I recommend the game still, it's a very relaxing and pretty puzzle game. The majority of the puzzles are good, and there's a cute cat.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say I’m glad I bought this on sale. The art direction and the idea behind the game are great. The execution was lacking for me. I found myself to be increasingly frustrated because more often than not the goal of a puzzle was not clear to me and even if you’ve understood the goal there’s little to no indicator if something quite literally needs to be placed just a little further to the left or right to be considered correct. This caused me to rearrange whole puzzles even though my initial solution was correct but the game didn’t recognise it as such. After a while it also became quite repetitive. I wish there was a neutral button but I can not in good faith give a thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: There's really not a lot here to justify purchasing this at full price. The levels are pretty repetitive, with mechanics running old after awhile. The daily tidy's are really misused, and you'll find yourself doing the same levels over and over, meaning the one thing pulling you back goes stale quick. Also Whenever I open the game the DLC for it appears in my shopping cart, so I don't like that.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. It was sold to me as a really satisfying and zen game about organising things. A part of it is, and those parts are fantastic. The art is simple and cute. It has all the right parts to make it a great game. But it isn't. To much of the game is increasingly difficult and obscure solutions to, what should be, simple puzzles. Do the developers expect me to sit on those leaf levels (especially the second one) and trial and error the solution? Without giving to much away for people that do what to try this game. This "puzzle" involves selecting the right items out of everything or it resets. Normal games have visual indicators or patters to assist this. This game said no to that. Why are those blank screen and random item "puzzles" like that? I thought it might just be like a timed thing where you can move on after playing with the items for a certain amount of time, or that there was some sort of picture to build. No. There is a picture to build...a hyper specific picture...with no reference to it...and everything has to be specifically placed or you won't get the level. Honestly, I never thought a game about organising would need a walk-through, but this game does. It is also super sad to see the walk-through's with explanations for the solutions to the "puzzles" being "I have no idea why this is the solution, it just is." I think that is the problem. The "puzzles"exist to stump you and be different. Not to scratch the itch that organising brings. The game does have hints though....and by hints....I mean they give you the answer. I'm assuming because even they know that some solutions are too stupid and complex for anyone to spend time figuring out. To be honest, I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone that wants to have a relaxing time. There are better games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: After getting 100% of the achievements, including the DLC, I'd say it was pretty good. Definitely worth it if it's on sale and you enjoy simple puzzle games. Nothing super challenging but I don't think that's what the devs were going for anyways. The daily tidy achievements were a little tedious so that might bring the score down a little if that's something you care about.In the end though, the overall experience was a solid 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to give this game a negative review--this is another case where I wish Steam had a "meh" button in addition to thumbs up/down.When I heard about this game, I was very excited to play it. I've always been obsessive about organizing stuff, so it sounded perfect for me. But somehow...this just isn't quite it.My number one issue with the game is actually the setting. It seems to take place in some Martha Stewart dreamscape: nothing but houseplants, seashells, pretty rocks, and household objects. Weirdly enough, there is basically zero overlap between the things I actually like to organize in real life and the things I get to organize in this game. There's no level where you re-indent all your code, or where you get to redo the cable management behind the TV, or where you have to guess what screw goes in what hole as you put a smartphone back together. So I really couldn't relate to the overall scenario that much.Another issue is how boring most of the puzzles are. The solution to half the puzzles is just to sort by color. And if not that, then just sort by size, or make the shapes fit with each other. There are only a few really tricky puzzles that call for any lateral thinking at all. A handful of the levels don't even have a single, correct solution; you just have to . It's more of an color-acuity test than real puzzler.I was also let down by the level of interactivity. You can click and drag to rearrange stuff on the screen--and that's it. You can't attach parts together, break things, fold things, turn parts over, etc. So most of the mechanical, kinesthetic joy that comes from disassembling or fixing stuff is lost. It especially stings in the tool-themed chapter; you get a screen full of bolts, nuts, and wrenches, but can you put the nuts on the bolts, maybe using the wrenches? Nope. They get organized in some sort of cafeteria tray, same as the seashells and paperclips from before.I was also unimpressed with the audio. The music is very repetitive and not very good. There is one track with this one arpeggiated piano chord, and it just goes up the scale, down the scale, up the scale, down the scale...I had to put the game on mute when I came back to replay the levels for 100% completion. The sound effects for picking up and moving objects around are also much too loud; the effect is often pretty jarring. If you move stuff around too fast, it turns into some kind of extreme ASMR.And there are some other careless details besides all that. For instance, many levels have more than one solution. After finding one solution, I always wanted to try to get the others (sometimes they are painfully obvious). But the game automatically boots you off to the next level, so you have to exit to the level select and pick out the level the hard way. Another example is the daily puzzles; I think they are automatically generated from maybe 5 or 10 possible templates. The solutions are the same every time, so after a couple repetitions you can solve them on sight. Not sure how this is supposed to retain my interest.Still, there are a few things I liked about the game. The narrative with the cat is a cute way to tie the different chapters together, and there are a couple of memorable puzzles in the mix. The art style is consistent and fits with the rest of the game, and it's a nice, focused experience. I can't deny that it held my attention for long enough to finish the game and do some achievement-hunting (the devs promise that the broken ones will be fixed in the next update). I'm sure some people will like this game much more than I did.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Fun fun fun! This game is soooo cute! I love the vibe of the game. You're not only solving puzzles but you're tidying up the home and you're seeing how the simple story progresses with the kitty. Super cozy puzzle game. I love the DLC and I LOVE the daily tidies! _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I really love the concept and I had it wishlisted for a year or longer and played the demo. The only thing that really bugged me is how finicky some of the puzzles are..like I'm looking at the hint doing exactly what it says to do and it won't clear the puzzle. _childDocuments_.review: okay, ive replayed this game so many times, and i Still enjoy it. love the dlc and the puzzles are fun. love that there are multiple ways to solve them as well. the one issue i had was with the hints where it only showed one solution to the multiple solution puzzles. but they have finally updated that so it shows hints for All of the possible solutions. 10/10 would recommend this game. tempted to buy it on mobile so i can play it more but for now, im satisfied to replay these levels again and again.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I sure do love my animals. This game made me realize how even though my animals frustrate me sometimes, especially while trying to keep a tidy home, I love them unconditionally - - all the way to the moon and back. This is a fantastic game for anyone who likes to fixate on things and maybe thinks they're a weirdo. The daily cleaning mini-games will become a ritual for me before going to work or doing homework. Exercises like this get my brain in the right mood and focused. It's also amusing to play while sharing your screen with a friend, so you can share how weird you are about how you organize or solve puzzles. The art style and music are phenomenal. There are a couple of levels where some of the noises of the puzzles are a bit grating, but other than that; I had a fantastic time playing through it.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great for those who prefer lite puzzles over organizing. There are some puzzles where the solution is a satisfying way to organize (like sort this drawer or stack this neatly), but the vast majority feel somewhat arbitrary (especially the multiple solution ones) with not great cohesion on game progression. There are a small amount where the solution feels random and obscure, but most just aren't satisfying for me who expected more of an organizing game. Additionally, if you're going for any of the Daily Tidies achievements, it gets very repetitive;  the developer has responded there are 15 with minor variants on each. Lastly, some of the snapping is finicky and can be quite maddening.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Now obviously my opinion doesn't matter in the grand scheme of things, but I didn't like this game. I saw it thru to the credits, sans DLC, and got several of the Secret Version answers to the main puzzles - got the rest with outside help guides - but I felt no desire to go in again and again to do the Daily Tidy's, nor buy the DLC (which seems a bit overpriced, imo, at half the game's price again, for less than half of the main game's content, each). Nor, crucially, to attempt any of the other, technically-possible achievements. Which is a real rarity for me. I do, often, play games I don't wholly enjoy to 100% completion because that part IS satisfying for me. I knew right away that would not be the case here.Many of the puzzles frustrated me in that they were VERY FINNICKY with where exactly the object needed to be placed to count. I got really gritted-teeth and hunched-shoulders about it, as I got closer and closer to the obvious clear solution... and yet couldn't force the game to recognize that I HAD the right idea in mind! And the final credits stack, ughhhh, that was HORRIBLE for my shoulder tension. A stacking puzzle on a timer?? Whyyyyy.... Why did it feel worse than Tetris, to do that section? Tetris gives me an anxiety-spike, yes, but not nearly to the degree that puzzle did? Perhaps I was extremely nervous for the jumping kitty... Perhaps just any hint of animal in danger makes my internal alarms go bonkers, even if totally 2D and fictional!And I'm not even a very nervous person! Usually, it's totally manageable, and only goes crazy before I do a performance, or take a day trip to a new location, or something like that, something that makes sense. This? Did not make sense. I didn't like it. Therefore, I don't recommend other ppl have that experience! I suppose what this game was really missing, that would ACTUALLY have made it feel relaxing to me, is a sense of ATMOSPHERE. I felt like I was just walking between desks at a school, being quizzed on how to clean up this particular person's messy desk. I didn't feel like I was in the same house the whole time, and I didn't feel like the cat - huge part of the branding - lived in that house, either. It wasn't even there every time, so I didn't feel like it was a character, or companion, or part of the scenery... Felt like a randomly-appearing stage hazard. So, overall, the game felt like it was missing a sense of cohesiveness. Didn't create a vibe of a singular place, and didn't go minimalist enough to seem like it wanted to be JUST a puzzle game. Seems like it aimed at two targets and failed to synthesize them. To me, at least. That saying of 'chase two rabbits, catch neither' comes to mind.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I've had my eye on this game for a long time since I first saw it in a Wholesome Direct, and I only spontaneously bought it + the DLC the other day. I have since finished every single puzzle, including the ones in the DLC and the ones from the Daily Tidy archive. I enjoyed this game a lot more than I thought I would!! This game has no explanations for the puzzles which can be frustrating, especially if you're someone who needs clear requirements/rules. But!! I find that the charm point of this game is being able to experiment with different possible solutions. The music and the sound effects also rock :-) I look forward to future Daily Tidies and DLCs (maybe??) because I loved all the puzzles in the Cupboards & Drawers DLC a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this game to someone who doesn't like how open ended things like Unpacking or House Flipper etc are. If you want a ton of short low-key Warioware-ish puzzles with specific answers to find you'll have a great time with this. Unfortunately for me I think I prefer something more open-ended. Sometimes I didn't like the organization methods chosen, or the categorization felt really strange or counter-intuitive to me, and there's no allowance for that in the solutions so it started to just get frustrating. I tried to go back to it again more recently and had the same issues, so I think this one's just not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Im going to be completely honest, I saw this game on TikTok as well as from various streamers. It seemed like a pretty chill game. I went onto steam and noticed how it was like $15 and thought that was an okay price for such a chill and stress relieving game. I literally finished both the original game and the DLC in around an hour. I spent al most $20 on a game that can only be played once to enjoy. I am so disappointed in how short this game is. Yes, Im aware of the "daily sorts" but they are usually so short and are quite literally copies of other sorting levels. I cannot believe I spent $20 on this game let alone paid any money for it at all. This is a game that could be purchased on the app store for like $2 if not for free. I do not recommend this game. Save your money and literally just watch someone play the 20 levels this game provides.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic and simple little puzzle game that I totally wish there was more of! The art style is fantastic and it's really satisfying when you complete a puzzle. The puzzles could be a little too simple for some, but to me that just means more people can enjoy the game without getting frustrated, especially young kids.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I am sad to leave a poor review of this game.  Conceptually, it's very cute, and I greatly enjoyed the majority of it.  I have two grievances.One is that it felt like there was a tangible decline in the puzzle quality as the game went on.  There was an acceptable amount of redundancy, I would say - although you can only straighten photos or sort junk drawers so many times before the novelty wears off - but some of the puzzles were genuinely frustrating.  A few of them made no sense to me and required hints and I have no idea how anyone would have ever figured them out without them; there were also a few instances where I just clicked around randomly to find interactions with items that were not at all obvious and I don't feel like that's good design.  The frustrations I started to feel in the second half of the game took a lot away from the enjoyment I got out of the first half.My second issue - the larger one - was playtime/content.  Even with the struggles I had, I completed the base game in 3 hours.  I am glad I bought this on sale, but still don't feel it was particularly good value for the money.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely way to spend an afternoon. Really clever and satisfying puzzles, with clear mechanics that prevent the game from getting in the way of the player. I hate when you are playing a puzzle game and have the solution but abandon it because your attempts to implement the solution fail due to clunky mechanics. Sometimes puzzle games have an issue with not lining things up correctly or things failing to register. That doesn't happen here- if you haven't gotten all of the solutions yet, it's because you actually haven't figured it out.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and charming but pretty short. Though there are the daily puzzles so I hope those add to the experience. Some of the puzzles are quite satisfying to my sillly little brain. I kind of hate the constellation and the snowflake dailies cause its annoying to do 3 of them and I wish they were less repetitive but ofc I don't expect them to program a new puzzle for every daily
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect if you're looking for a calm little game with no stress and no expectations except making things tidy. There were a couple I had to look up solutions for, I will admit, because the lack of instructions made it a little frustrating to figure out on my own, but the ability to skip levels and come back later is a wonderful solution to that challenge. Highly recommend for a chill, short game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I have yet to partake in a Puzzle Game that is both most delightful and a tad challenging to master upon first attempt, yet retains the capacity to be both serene and gratifying in its play. Should one find pleasure in the art of arranging common objects of daily life in varying manners, then verily, this game is most assuredly suited to thee!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: It definitely didn't pass the dollars to hour requirement. Some games pad their score by simply having such a memorable experience that a short time is enjoyable.This ain't it.The puzzles were mostly just too easy, but were held back by the fiddly method of executing the solution. I'd often be right, but I hadn't nudged the object into the correct pixel, which eventually led me to check hints to verify if I was the moron, or if the game was the moron (it was the game).
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A polished, humorous, and good-natured puzzle game for the compulsively organized. It has just the right amount of puzzles, with only a few that made me look up the answer and groan "oh come ON." More often they were very satisfying. You just have to sit for a few of them. Take a deep breath. Live in them a while. Don't rush (it's not that kind of game). Highly recommended if you find great pleasure in straightening things on your desk or find pleasure in neatly mirrored patterns. The DLC is also really good.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really nice and calming game to play. There is a DLC that I have yet to play, but its just really fun to play with the music in the background after a long day of school or work. I highly reccommend this to people looking for a chill puzzle game (especially if you like organizing and/or cats)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this. Okay, some of the levels might seem a little unclear to start with, but there's a hint available. For the most part it's soothing and very playable. Being neurodiverse, this one lands in all the right places, it's so calming and pleasing to create order out of chaos, and recognise patterns. Not sure why tidying up a cutlery drawer or toolbox is so much more pleasing to do in a game than in real life, but there you are. On some levels there's more than one way to solve the puzzle, and there's a daily puzzle each day to continue playability. MORE LEVELS PLEASE as I clearly need this in my life. Can I suggest the "my messy wardrobe/closet" level, the "organize my sock drawer" level, the "omg, the basement" level and the "hell, no - craft room" level?!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: mixed bag for me. there's some solid puzzles here and there but also quite a few that feel clunky and unsatisfying. and the daily tidy feature shouldn't exist, especially since there's achievements tied to it. nobody is going to do 100 daily tidy's by waiting 100 days. there isn't even 100 unique daily tidy's, there's about 15 or so, which makes me question why they even bothered.not a fan of the achievements that require clean playthroughs as well, since they contradict other achievements. for example, one requires you to skip a puzzle, but another one requires you to complete the entire game without ever skipping. why.the music is alright, gets repetitive after an hour or two. the best puzzles are definitely the cupboards & drawers ones. a little to the left's biggest strong suit is the visuals though. it looks great.

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing game, but it get's a bit repetitive after some time.
