_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly addicting. Each level is challenging enough to keep interest, but not too hard as to cause frustration. The result is satisfying every time, without fail.The graphics are fairly simple, but the items all move with such fluidity and grace. All items have a fun sound when you move them. In conclusion, don't let the simple look of the game lead you astray. This game is perfectly and carefully built, and I would play it 1000 times over if I could.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Is very good, soothes that autistic/nd anxiety, very satisfying to get everything to be just right. Fun figuring out "okay i solved it how i would do it, now i have to figure out the other 5 ways to do it". art style is nice and relaxing. you get to pet the cat. played through the whole thing in a couple of sittings. wish there were more chapters, or that the daily tidy came with multiple puzzles
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly good hidden gem! The puzzle is simple to understand (no text explanation needed) but take time to solve the riddles. The art style is great and relaxing, sounds and music is chilling. Control is exceptionally smooth and it never break any puzzle no matter what crazy move tried, very well debugged. Story is simple and plain, but it is not a must for a good puzzle game.The overall experience like "Rusty Lake" series with lighthearted world. Totally recommended to all puzzle games lovers!Score: 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Ran through the whole game in 6 hours. Not sure if it's worth paying full price for 6hrs of game play, but I bought it on sale 40%off and I'm glad I did. It was fun and really lovely visually, cute themes and clever puzzles. I was pleased with the difficulty of the puzzles and the solutions. If I had to nitpick, there were 1 or 2 solutions (through the ENTIRETY of the game) that dissatisfied me. The replayability (ie "daily tidy") doesn't really keep me playing the game imo; I'll probably drop it until the dlcs go on sale.Overall 8/10 (on sale)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really enjoyable game; very chill and relaxing with some humor, too. With the recent update, you get a nice little chunk of content; and the daily tidy is a nice little, daily, calming exercise. If you can pick it up at or under $12; it's definitely worth grabbing. If you like cozy games, it'll probably be worth it at any sale prices.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A little to the left is such a relaxing game. The game play is super smooth and enjoyable. It's also really long which I like, and the puzzles can get pretty challenging at times with the alternate solutions so it isn't really easy to finish in one play through. I would recommend this game to people who like 'cozy' games like Unpacking.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game that's exactly as advertised. You organize stuff, some levels have multiple solutions and other puzzles I was lost on, but they're mostly relatively simple. There's also hints if you ever get lost. I heard there will be some more puzzles and I'm very excited for that, however I do wish there was more variety in the daily tidies as you're supposed to do 100 for the achievements (possibly more if you miss the consecutive for a month). I really liked the easter egg event having different puzzles, like putting the glass back to match the patterns, I really loved those puzzles. Otherwise, calm cute game and you get to see a little menace kitty and who doesn't love that?
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! It's so satisfying to put everything in just the right spot... Some levels are super easy and obvious, and some are quite challenging, especially the ones with FIVE different solutions... So it's a nice blend of difficulty. All the cats are fun as well! I showed the game to my mom (60s) who DOES NOT play video games (okay, except Dr. Mario 64), and she played several levels in one sitting! My kids like it as well. It's a super chill way to relax in the evening!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Good puzzle game. Took about 3 hours to complete -- which IS short, but I feel very fair for the sale price I nabbed it at. Great aesthetic all the way through. Puzzles had a very satisfying range of difficulties, with more than one way to complete most and some pretty novel solutions. Some stumped me a while, some were quite obvious. All were fun.Really enjoyed this, all the way through the adorable credits.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I have OCD... Opened the game i thought it was going to be very relaxing...I was wrong, the amount of times i got mad during this and there was only one shoe etc etc uncountable..Meanwhile my bf laughing at me and couldn't control himself. so i guess the recommended is to give your loved ones a laugh. but it is still a good game and I loved the art work.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, and comfy, and unfortunately maybe a bit overpriced for how short it is.  The puzzle backgrounds could do with a bit more visual indication of where to put things sometimes too, instead of just being barren but having clearly designed 'slots' stuff will snap to.  Overall though it's basically exactly what it looks like on the tin, so if it seems interesting to you, you're probably the target audience.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for an unpacking game this is not it. I saw some videos that made it seem like it was but there are very few levels that give that vibe.  This is a puzzle game. I love puzzle games though however, some of these puzzle seem impossible to figure out with out looking at a guide. One specific level that comes to mind is the one with sea shells where you have to put them in a pattern and maybe I must missed something but you could have sat there for hours trying to figure it out and still got the pattern right. If you like brain teasers, really hard ones, from time to time this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: When going through some mental difficulties, I found this game peaceful and comforting. I wish there was more, especially of the DLC desks and drawers. The music, colors, different puzzles all had a calm atmosphere and were extremely satisfying to finish. As of now I play each day for the daily tidies but I played through it more than twice, even knowing all the solutions. It was that calming.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is a comfort food of a game. It's good at teaching the player how to play it and building difficulty in a fairly steady ramp. It has enough variety too. it's hint system is well thought out and the ability to skip a level is a relief. It has depth with the ability to find different solution, the DCL and the daily puzzle. Both the graphics and music are charming. It knows how to surprise. And, in the end, it's a bit of a love story.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is a charming puzzle gem. Arrange household items in logical ways, with some puzzles offering multiple solutions for a satisfying challenge.  The adorable visuals and relaxing atmosphere make it a perfect game to unwind and unleash your inner organizer. The main campaign takes about 5 hours, with DLC and daily challenges adding even more content. Highly recommended for puzzle fans!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game was very cute, cozy, and relaxing. I loved the simple puzzles and appreciated that some puzzles can be solved multiple ways (and need to be completed EVERY possible way to complete chapters). The game took me around 5 hours to complete, but I haven't played the DLC nor completed every achievement yet. I'll likely come back to the game in a few months when I've forgotten the answers to do a new playthrough. Even though I really enjoyed this game, for only 5 hours of game time, you may want to purchase it during a sale :)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend the Seeing Stars DLC to anyone who likes A Little to the Left and is prepared for more of a challenge. Overall I enjoyed these puzzles very much. Many of them have 3-5 possible solutions, requiring a lot of creative thinking and pattern recognition. There were a few that were frustratingly ambiguous - such as the pizza level that could've had 15 or more reasonable solutions, but somehow we had to read the devs' minds and only pick four. As others have mentioned, I had a few issues fiddling with items that wouldn't click into place but this is the same problem I had in the main game and I know how to deal with it by now. It didn't stop me from getting all 100/100 stars (with a few hints and a lot of trial/error). But if you're not looking to strain your brain, maybe stick with the Daily Tidies and steer clear of this DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Very pleasant and simple puzzle game. Haven't had such a calm time with video games in a long time honestly. Solutions are well explained through hints you can use if you get stuck and most of the levels you can just outright skip. The only two things I dislike are the plant symmetry puzzles and the daily tidy achievements. The plant symmetry puzzles are horribly explained, difficult to keep track of, and can easily soft-lock you even once you know what you're doing. It's not very fun in the slightest and more annoying than anything. This could've been easily fixed by avoiding locking selections permanently once made and instead highlighting the ones you want to keep. That way the outliers that grow back can be easily identified and if you select one by mistake you can simply undo the selection. The daily tidy on the other hand is a perfectly fine feature by itself, but what really sucks is that the achievements require you to go on  and check in for  That's just stupid. I personally will probably do it anyways just cuz I find this game very fun, but grinding achievements aren't fun.As long as you aren't achievement grinding and skip the second plant symmetry puzzle, it's a very relaxing and fun experience. Definitely would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: this is absolutely my type of brain rot game that kept me busy all day. Bit short but I'm happy there's daily stuff too. Pros: The first time my brain has been calm and focused in so long. Super cozy, and relaxing.Cons: Some of the lvls were absolutely confusing but not impossible! Took me 6 hours to complete ☻♥

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute and fun game! I love that they have mixed in easy, medium, and hard puzzles throughout, rather than just getting harder and harder. There are multiple solutions to most puzzles as well, making it even sweeter because you can do a puzzle 2-3 times, looking for a different way to solve it each time. Last, but certainly not least, the kitty! It makes this game extra cute and its cheeky behaviour makes this game unique.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty and fun puzzles. Some are a bit finicky - I had some trouble with the laptop one and had to manually reopen the game and do the puzzle again for it to complete. Otherwise, its a really fun experience, especially like that there are sometimes more than one way to complete one puzzle as finding a different angle is sometimes more challenging than a new puzzle entirely!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I love the concept. But unless quite a few more chapters and levels are added it will unfortunately lack replayability. I bought it when it was on sale and still think it was a little expensive considering what you get. Finished the game including all solutions and daily tidy in a couple of hours and since I now know the solutions it will be quite awhile until I can enjoy it again. I did however try, and it wasn't nearly as fun.On the plus side the game perfectly balances chill and cozy with a little challenge on a few levels. Most of the levels are a breeze but highly satisfying and once in awhile they'll give you a little brain teaser.If the game included more puzzles it would definitely be in the top tier of my cute, chill and "kill-an-hour" games so I'm crossing my fingers more will be added so I won't regret my purchase.If you do however love puzzle organizers and are okay with completing the game in 2-3 hours, I can recommend "A Little to the Left".Might add, haven't noticed any bugs and I love the cat.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favourite games. It is SO fun to play. It's the kind of game I wish I could get a lifetime supply of, but at the same time it is good that I don't because I would just play it non-stop. I would forget to feed myself. I would not sleep. I would just play. I absolutely recommend it if you like organizing stuff and/or if you're neurodivergent.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a delightful, calming, cozy little game. I love to play to unwind after a long day of uni coursework. The graphics are so fun, and I love how accurately life with a pet is portrayed. Seeing little illustrations of the devs' pets in the credits was such a sweet little easter egg, too! I got the DLC, too, and I have zero regrets. 10/10, would highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Great soundtrack with some cool puzzles. Very satisfying to play. Some of the puzzles are a bit too rigid with their requirements to solve them and aren't fun, some are almost too easy. My favourites were the ones with multiple solutions, often one or two would be obvious to me but the third would have me scratching my head trying to figure out what I was missing (and trying to program my brain not to obsess over the previous solutions I already figured out). It's not a very long game (unless you want to commit to doing the daily puzzle over and over again) but it's cute and definitely cozy.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: You looked a trailer and this game seems fun, relaxing and meditating? Nope, it doesn't. I have check reviews before buying and have some misleading thoughts, but now I get it too. It's just another boring hard-coded sorting puzzle game, but with good marketing, nice graphics and "cute" cat.First of all, this is not how "Full controller support" should work. Can you imagine mapping mouse cursor directly to controller joystick movement? Does this seems absurd to you? Well, developers saw this as a good idea and implemented it just like this."Puzzles" are rather boring and sometimes counter-intuitive. In first color crayons puzzle I sorted them in opposite direction and guess what? IT DOESN'T COUNT. After that and a few more puzzle I just realized that this game nor fun, nor relaxing. My whole experience and expectations for this game was ruined not because I'm too dum to sort this, but because I can't sort thing in a way I like.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I felt like I was watching baby sensory videos partway through and the feeling only increased the longer I played.Clips online that piqued my interest contained the most interesting levels, arranging woodworking tools using what appeared to be a random series of nails on the wall, organising a medicine cabinet where everything aligned perfectly... I had expected most of the puzzles to be as complex as these. Instead, it was mostly lining things up one after the other by size. Perhaps worthwhile for a young person (It feels rude to say child, but there you have it) as worthwhile edutainment, but not for someone seeking a challenging puzzle game.It is beautiful, I will mention. The art is minimalist in an incredibly appealing way, but I feel the art is what misled me, in part, to believe the game was aimed at a 'mature' audience (for lack of a better term). Still, kudos when they are owed.Would I recommend it? Well. It's a good tool to teach children logic, or for someone who just wants to move things around on a screen. And frankly, that's about it.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited to play this game cuz the concept is cute and it looked like a satisfying game but it's also surprisingly harder than it looks. There's been too many times where I've given up and had to cheat the answer which takes all the relaxation away. Like how am I supposed to know in what order the cat knocks over things? And it's not water, wine, plant, broken pot, lamp I can tell you that. Some levels feel like they have no indicator as to what the solution is. I feel the games solutions are sometime TOO conceptual. This game is kind of a headache...
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adore this game. Just spent a good 2 hours getting lost in the ordinary-ness of it all. The game doesn't rush you, the graphics are gorgeous, and it feels damn rewarding after spending some time on a puzzle to see it line up just right. It's such a fun time, worth every dollar and the occasional cat is lovely. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great if you love puzzle games. Some of the puzzles are harder to figure out than others, of course, and the game offers a hint system. There are daily puzzles, the Daily Tidy's. The art style is really cute. It's a very relaxed and relaxing game even when a cat starts swiping at your neatly placed items. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fluffy puzzle game that makes you feel so accomplished when you finally find all the solution to the level. Well, to be fair I had some frustration with the game mainly with the level that had all these tools you need to hang, it wasn't that fun. The rest of the game tho -  and also the event dailies are really cute. (And the cat is so beautiful YOU CAN PET IT!!!)Overall if you want to poke your brain a bit to try to find some patterns - it's a game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I very much love this game, it hits me right in the autism in the right way and is satisfying to boot. The style is cute and most of the puzzles are fun! (Tho personally I find the make a symmetrical pattern from random item ones a bit dull, I'm one for more defined results) Overall I'm looking forward to the dlc!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure I would recommend buying the game at full price, but if it goes on sale for 9.99 or less than I think it would be worth the buy. The game is definitely satisfying, but that's it's biggest plus side, so if you don't care much for challenging gameplay and just want to relax, it's a worthwhile purchase. It feels like at least 10 or 20 puzzles were thrown in just for the sake of increasing the puzzle count (as an example, a few just involve rearranging three objects in order.) I would much rather have seen half as many puzzles that were challenging and well-thought out, but I cannot complain too much as there were at least 4 or 5 puzzles in the game that had me stumped for a few minutes. The "Daily Tidy" doesn't offer much in terms of replay value, but I can at least appreciate the developers' attempt to giving the game some sort of long-term playability. I would love to see a game that focuses solely on the compartment-sorting puzzles, as these ones (particularly the shed) felt satisfying to work through and solve, as well as being some of the only puzzles in the game that I didn't blow through in 30 seconds.All in all, this is a cute game that I would highly recommend grabbing for under 10 if you can, but only expect a few hours of playtime total.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun for relaxing by yourself. However, I turned this into a drinking game with my friends and it made it so much more fun. You need to play on 2 separate devices split into 2 teams. For every 3 stars that your team gets, the other team has to take a shot. It starts out really easy, but as you progress, not only do the levels get harder, but you also get drunker and thus thinking of solutions also becomes harder. [You can change the amount of stars needed to take a shot depending on how drunk y'all want to get]
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Full experience can be described with the following GIF , kidding; more or less 😄 The game is a lot of straightening, ordering, colour coding and stacking - all while your cat is playing games and knocks them over. Not going to lie, it does get a bit repetitive, no matter how much the developers are trying to spice things up with DLCs; the game’s goal is the same tidy-up and variants of few puzzles but with different objects. There is not much story-wise to it, although for perfectionists its a bit of an extra tasks and thinking caps are needed. As there is no per-se story to the game, it does get a bit boring; I’ve been finding myself taking breaks for few days between playing the game. Sometimes the puzzles are a tad frustrating; for what might look tidy to you it does not for the game. At the end of the day after all the in-game tidy, there is the real-life hose to tidy up too, right 🥲. But if your OCD is not triggered a lot during the day or already have an organised house, definitely try this game. Its a somewhat no-brainer (if you are not going for achievements ) that does not require a lot of effort, just a bit of attention and desire to organise. As a tip, I would buy this when it goes to sale; though some might argue there is value for moneyFor achievement lovers these are not too big of a hurdle to obtain; majority of them can be obtain by going through levels and finding all the possible solutions. But as always, if you struggle a bit ( as I did for few achievements; figuring out what to do with those damn boxes took ages, felt stupid), these articles are a great resource:

_childDocuments_.review: I don't care if it's not your style. You WILL PLAY THIS GAME FOR THE END CREDITS! I SWEAR SEEING ALL THE PETS AND THEIR NAMES HAD ME SOBBING ON A SATURDAY NIGHT. Thank you for allowing me to yell at you. <3 xx (also this game soothed my ADHD but it also bugged me, so do with that info as you wish. But the end credits made all of the frustration worth it).

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and charming puzzle game. The style and polish of the game is very relaxing and I highly recommend it!There was only one puzzle that I couldn't figure it out, the one with the skull in a box, which I don't think I would've ever understood. Otherwise I found most puzzles satisfying!I love that the dev team is actively paying attention to feedback on the community page which lead to changes like reworking of the achievements. I had given up on 100% when I originally played because the daily tidy achievements were kinda insane. But 100 is very doable with some patience :) Or by changing the clock, but it was a nice routine to pop onto the game for a minute or two and do a daily tidy.Looking forward to the DLC!

_childDocuments_.review: some of the organization puzzles seem impossible at first since everything is just chaosbut then you start and make progress little by littleand eventually you just,, do itand that feels greatis it cliche to say "this game taught me..."idk,but it didsmall steps can add up to a long journeyof course i knew that before, but this silly little game (especially the dlc) made me actually feel it on a level i can grasp

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, A Little to the Left is a fun game. I do feel like it was not marketed well, however. A lot of the marketing surrounding this game called it a simple, relaxing, organization game. It was compared a lot to Unpacking in that regard. However, while it does have those elements (especially in the early levels) it is a puzzle game first and foremost with very specific solutions. As a puzzle game, it's pretty good, though some of the solutions (especially in the DLCs) are extremely obscure. I commend anyone that can figure out every solution without a guide or using the hint system because I certainly could not.However, the hint system that is implemented is VERY good. I really like that you can erase just a tiny bit of the hint to get an initial idea of what to do instead of being given the entire solution. That helps the game not feel quite so frustrating. The music is very calming and nice. The sound design overall is spectacular in this game and adds to the simpleness of the game. It does make for a nice cozy experience, once you know what you're actually getting.My biggest complaint in this game were some of the achievements were ATROCIOUS to get, but they have since been nerfed and made easier. Once upon a time one of the achievements required you to do the daily tidy 365 days IN A ROW. If you missed a day, you had to restart for an entire year. It was madness. I believe the new biggest consecutive streak you need to obtain is only 30 days which is vastly more manageable, and so I won't dock the game for it anymore.All in all, I still recommend this game, but only if you really like puzzle games. There are very specific solutions needed for these levels and it's not as much of a free form experience as I had been led to believe in the advertising. It still makes for quite a nice experience in the end!(But devs, please stop adding achievements to the DLC. The DLCs are fine, but I don't want to have to keep spending money to keep my 100% badge. PLEASE.)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the experience and blasted through it, some of these really got me thinking haha Especially when there are several solutions :DGreat cozy game, I totally recommend if you like organizing puzzles and are looking for a game you can play in small sessions when you've got a few minutes to spare. Though, be careful it can be addictive...
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute little game about organizing, with most puzzles being very satisfying to solve, a pleasant ost and a really cute cat; turned spiritual awakening/acid trip with a really cute cat at the final level. The only thing bringing this game down is its  short runtime of approximately 3 hours (finding all possible solutions) and  of unintuitive solutions for some of the single solve puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: If you saw your favourite streamer or tiktoker play this, they were probably on a level neatly reorganizing items into a shelf. This is because those levels take the longest but are the most satisfying to us OCD viewers. Don't be fooled as there's only a handful of those levels while the rest of the game is frustrating as hell.Certain levels have multiple solutions to which you'll have to reattempt them for a full clear. However, once you've solved the first, the game doesn't let you quickly reattempt it and shoves a 1/3 star in your face. Now you'll have to interrupt the flow with a slow animated menu just to retry, yet the full solutions are just wack. Maybe if you have the patience to solve puzzles, you'll be rewarded in time, but I'm here just trying to get to the darn levels which sold the game for me. It's frustrating beyond all hell as the hints don't provide full coverage and when you do google the answers, you just roll your eyes and think, it's not worth it.The relaxing tag is a bait. Skipped every level till I got to the ones I wanted. They've acknowledge why their game is selling well yet has some negative reviews, so the DLC addresses that which is exclusively organizing cupboards and drawers. I'd say keep waiting till the front game is dirt cheap, then get the dlc to sate that initial social media video that got you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely little game, perfect for when you need to relax and don't want to think *too* hard about puzzles. The sound and visual designs are wonderfully cozy, and I love the kitty who seems determined to mess up the perfect organization! I imagine some might find it annoying, but as someone who's had cats for almost my entire life it is a very cute - and accurate - inclusion. So many times in my life have I been working, and said "put this over here - no, this over here - stop playing everything, I'm trying to organize this in a specific way!" The cat in this game is significantly less irritating than real-world ones can be, haha. The game does get a bit convoluted as time goes on, with the final puzzles not really feeling that tied down as plausible actual organizational challenges that you might encounter in the real world, but they're enjoyable nonetheless. :)

_childDocuments_.review: The game is appealing in colors, vibe, etc.The game has a fun narrative, which while simple, I found very enjoyable.The game has good puzzles.The game is relatively short. _childDocuments_.review: Really cute and beautifully made. _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely cute and fun little game, with responsive devs who are dedicated to improving the game. _childDocuments_.review: I wish I bought this on sale, as it doesn't feel like value for money at $17. _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: The game was slightly disappointing because a decent portion of the levels (30 %?) wasn't satisfying or relaxing as you'd imagine, but rather annoying or frustrating. The issues I had was that sometimes it was hard to tell where to place things in order for them to be counted as organised (some of the pencil levels, for example), how to use them (e.g. open the box for the skull or q-tips), sometimes even with the hints I was unable to figure things out (for example I still don't understand what the idea behind both of the solutions for the nine rocks level was; had to watch a walkthrough for that), sometimes I knew what to do, but it was really difficult, tedious and/or unsatisfying to do it (e.g. the picture level (the pictures kept coming back to their original positions no matter how much I pulled them up to be levelled), the hanging tools (really hard to figure out where to put things), cardboard boxes, vines and snowflakes levels). Another thing I didn't like was how long the transitions between levels took and how user-unfriendly they made it for you to repeat a level while not having completed the rest of the levels (in order to get all of the stars) - it was so annoying, at one point I just gave up and went back to the multiple solution levels after I completed the campaign. Another issue I ran into was that after I solved all of the levels, I wanted to get two of the achievements for using no hints or skipping so I replayed the entire game without using any of that (which took at least 2 more hours of gameplay), only to get neither of the achievements, which was very annoying.However, despite all of this, for the most part I had fun. Many levels were super satisfying and relaxing and I really appreciated the option to skip a level or get a hint (for free) - that helped a little bit with the dissatisfaction. The art style and chosen colours were also very pretty, the animations looked really nice, the sound design was great too and helped a bit with finding the correct spot for things (on the other hand, I wasn't fan of the music so I turned it off pretty early on), I loved the cat interludes and little jokes. The part after you pet it and it appears laying in different positions was the highlight of this game for me, so cute and wholesome. I think there are some things about this game that could be made better or fixed altogether, but as it stands right now, it's still a nice game and I recommend it to anyone who enjoys puzzles and/or organising. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because my favorite vtuber HATED IT.I had a lot of fun with this game.  The puzzles were challenging, but only rarely frustrating. _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is one of my favourite cute cozy puzzle games. I'm usually not big into pure puzzle games, I prefer if it's puzzle elements mixed into something else, but every now and then, I crave something nice and relaxing to throw the 3.5 braincells in my head that are not perpetually busy with being either anxious or stressed at some problems with no needless clutter.And man, is this game perfect for that! It's literally about fixing clutter, and it does so in a very adorable way. The puzzles are all about finding patterns and bringing order into the chaos that happens in life. Sort stuff, that's all there is to the core gameplay loop. Boxes, mugs, trinkets, paper, buttons... all the paraphernalia of life, drawn in a simple, but very cute style, with the occasional cat thrown in. It sounds boring on paper, but it's surprisingly addicting. Especially because for most puzzles, there's multiple solutions and figuring out all the possibilities is a whole lot of fun. Is this the greatest game of all time? Nope. Is this a super relaxing cozy puzzle game that tickles my brain into actually cleaning up my house after playing for a while? Yes, absolutely! I would recommend this game to my mom, who is slowly graduating from Candy Crush to actual, proper games, and to everyone else who likes chill puzzle games with cats.

_childDocuments_.review: It is frustrating but in a good way. I enjoyed getting mad and trying to figure out what they wanted me to do. _childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is a spectacular game. I originally only saw it through YouTube shorts, and it looked very interesting at the time. But overall the puzzles were very good, and I was engaged through every single one. The soundtrack for this game is very beautiful. I enjoyed listening to it while playing the game, and it kept me in a very relaxed state.In summary, A Little to the Left is an excellent game that has magnificent game art, with very relaxing/interesting puzzles, and a beautiful soundtrack.Art: 8.5/10Gameplay: 9/10Soundtrack: 8/10Cost: 6.5/10Overall Score :  8/10

_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitly not a game for everyone and you probably need to be in a specific state of mind while you play it. Some levels are honestly infuriating but most are fairly straightforward, there are a few puzzles, especially in the last chapter, but most is just figuring out in what different ways you can sort the objects or make patterns. If you would like it or not, can probably be answered in one single question, - Do you organize your stuff at home in specific patterns. If your awnser is "Well yeah, obviously. Who doesn't!", then pick this up, However if you awnser is - "No, what kind of question is that, why would I do something like that", then no, you will hate this game. Me? Yeah i'm in camp A, so I did enjoy this game for the most part, but I do think the last couple of levels where kind of terrible to be honest. Especially the last one, it goes on forever to the point that you start to wonder if you are doing something wrong.

Then there's the puzzles with the pentatonic chimes as you make progress, just absolutely delightful to the ears.The only issue I have with this game is that there are two particular puzzles in the daily tidy that just annoy me every time they show up. The spider is purely subjective, I just don't like the sounds it makes. But the snowflake tidy takes so long to do; what normally takes 30-60 seconds to just do as a daily routine becomes more like 3-4 minutes of futzing about until its solved. All the other daily tidies are quite pleasant, it's just that those two in particular are bothersome for me.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was something I could do in return for the devs of this game beyond just having written a good review. I'm hardly sure where to even begin. With no exaggeration, this game has actually saved me from breaking down multiple times. I've struggled with near impossible levels of anxiety for quite awhile now, I spend many nights panicking until I passed out from exhaustion. Many medications have been no help in dealing with my panic and while therapy does help it is a slow process through small wins. This game has helped me calm down many times during those long nights, when I had originally thought there was no end for the panic in sight. The soft yet satisfying sounds are never too overwhelming, the music is very calming, and since you can always just pass on a puzzle I have never felt any sort of pressure while playing. I cannot recommend this game enough, I never thought a game without a major story would mean so much to me. Even after finishing practically everything in the game and its dlcs I find myself replaying levels to soothe myself. I can't thank Max Inferno enough for this incredible game.

_childDocuments_.review: -  A Little to the Left is a gorgeous game dripping with mid-century Realism. Many of the levels and their contents look like they were ripped directly for a 1950s home ec textbook-  The use of color is also nice. I liked how most levels used a restricted palette, giving each a screen print sort of feel-  While the soundtrack wasn't bad, it did feel a little out of tune with the visual style. Given the artwork that harkens back some 70-80 years, I would have expected the genre of the backing tracks to follow suit. While they are a pleasant mix of dreamy synth, ethereal piano, nicely varied percussion, and playful back-and-forths of plucked and bowed strings, the style feels contemporary and out of place-  I rarely feel motivated to mention sound design, but A Little to the Left does a great job in this regard. The various clinks, whooshes, clatters, and scrapes you'd expect to hear while shuffling various objects around are faithful and instantly identifiable. It really does capture the auditory experience of rummaging around in a messy drawer for a book of matches- I don't wander into the "cozy organization puzzle game" world very often, but unlike the last one of these I played (Unpacking), there's not really any attempt at storytelling. Just clean, organize, and watch out for - Although the vibes are indeed mostly cozy, I bumped into some frustration when trying to figure out some of the alternate solutions to certain levels. Those wound up crashing the party enough that I wound up using a guide when I circled back to 100% the game. Some of the solutions are fairly insipid, and I don't know if I would have gotten there naturally (looking at you, pen level)- Your enjoyment of the game is wholly dependent on how much you enjoy this style of gameplay, and perhaps the tasks of tidying and organizing as a whole. Do you find it meditative and satisfying? Then you're probably going to enjoy this experience, especially with its pretty visuals. Do you find it boring and frustrating? Then don't even bother considering- The gameplay can be almost wholly described as "click and drag object to correct spot". Beyond that, you occasionally stave of incursions from your luxurious Persian cat- I don't have any compulsive need to organize, so I'm probably not gonna revisit this one- I'm still undecided on how I feel about this sort of game (not that I've played many of them). All I really have to compare it to is Unpacking. While I liked the unspoken narrative of that title, I kinda hated the "puzzles". With so few restrictions, I found myself mostly piling up garbage into technically correct positions and moving on to the next level. A Little to the Left, on the other hand, gives you the satisfaction of feeling like you're actually solving a puzzle by adding set solutions, but the lack of any motivating pretense means that the whole experience feels a bit pointless. It made me wonder why I was bothering to tidy up my virtual cutlery drawer when my real one is a jumbled mess. Oh well. At least it motivated me to finally reorganize a few of my actual kitchen's messy cabinets- I feel like I write this on a lot of point-and-click games that I wind up playing on Steam Deck, but the same thought applies: the trackpads are sufficient, but M/K would have been smoother- . A passably satisfying experience with some pretty visuals and slick foley work, but little more. I mildly enjoyed the organization gameplay, but if you don't, you're going to have a much worse time

_childDocuments_.review: You know how in life you want everything in order and then everything is perfect? Well, nothing in life is like that! _childDocuments_.review: Got this game on sale, but it's still way too over priced for what's nothing but a far too long series of the exact same ♥♥♥♥. The 'puzzles' are hardly even puzzles; the solutions are either arbitrary and make little to no sense at all or are mind numbingly simple. It's literally nothing but sort by; size, shape, or colour. Playing with my toddler sister is more interesting, even for what's meant to be a relaxing game. But, it's not even that relaxing because, as mentioned, the other half of the puzzles have no logic to why the solution is the way it is. It's also not interestingly illogical, there's nothing 'surreal' or intuitive about it at all. The cat also doesn't 'shake things up'; it just pops up at the end of the level and screws the pieces up, and then the game proceeds to the next. If you want a relaxing, cosy game that actually has something going on, just play Unpacking. It's a similar price, sure, but it can actually be fun to play when you just want to sort and wind down for the evening, and has an actual story, small as it is.

_childDocuments_.review: What sets A Little to the Left apart from other puzzle games is its intuitive and playful design. The game's charming illustrations and surprising scenarios add to the overall appeal of the game. Whether you're trying to figure out which way the clock hands should point or how to arrange the eggs just right, there's always a new challenge waiting for you in A Little to the Left. One of the most delightful aspects of the game is the mischievous cat who likes to shake things up.But perhaps the best feature of the game is its accessibility. If you don’t like the puzzle or you are completely stuck you can simply skip it without any harm to progression. But if you still want to finish the puzzle, you can get as much hint as you desire with the game’s awesome hint system where you can erase a sketch of the puzzle gradually to figure out what to do. And finally, the game has no time limits or jumping puzzles which all in all makes it a perfect game for gamers such as myself!Overall, A Little to the Left is a must-play for puzzle game fans and anyone who enjoys the satisfaction of a well-organized space 😄

_childDocuments_.review: “A little to the left” is both a phrase that I hear way too often when helping my mom change furniture around in her house, which she does at least once every couple of months, and the name of an I know I joked about the whole furniture thing, but honestly, I’m pretty sure that precise scenario is where the developer got the name of the game from. You see,  with the very first level being all about fixing a picture that needs to be tilted just a little to the left. I see what you did there, devs! Honestly, I love the name of the game. It fits.But what DOES it fit into, exactly? What is the full package? Well,  You have a level select screen with over 75 quick levels that give you a variety of objects that you need to organize within whatever frame the level provides you with. If you get a bunch of books side by side, for example, you’ll know you’ll probably have to shift the books around to organize them in a way that makes sense, be it by size, cover design, whatever. On another level, you’re given stickers to apply to a calendar, or stamps to apply to letters. Whatever the case,  The worst were the ones that just gave me an empty space and a bunch of objects. In those, you’re supposed to arrange the objects in the right way, except as far as I can tell, there’s only one way to find out the correct arrangement, and that’s via trial and error.  The game does try to alleviate this by having a kind of a snap effect to an object when you put it in the right place, along with a DING sound that plays, but for me, that was simply too inconsistent to rely on. Well, I say hint because that’s the name in the game, but the truth is the hint is actually the entire answer of the puzzle, but it’s displayed in a way that can be a hint. It’s quite brilliant, really. Let me explain. The answer is basically written in a notebook, but scribbled over. You can get an eraser and erase all the scribbles, which reveal the puzzle’s answer. However, if you only want a hint, you can choose to erase just part of the scribbles, and reveal just a bit of the answer. This way, the player has full control over how much help they want, and I find that to be pretty cool. Basically, you complete a puzzle and you get a star. However, if you complete a puzzle and you see there are two or more stars to get, that means there is another solution to your level. Just like with the puzzles, the solutions can also be unintuitive sometimes. However, in this case, not even the hint will help you, as the hint only shows you the answer to one of the solutions. The rest is on you.  In a game as simple as this, in which you play by clicking and dragging your mouse, that’s mostly okay, but this fact can generate some confusion in some areas, such as the stars. I’ve seen players for example who thought these stars were ratings, and that they were being too slow/doing something wrong. If you finish all the content of this game and want more, fret not:  so at least once a day you can hop back in and do that. In this vein, the game is very relaxing.  The game is very good at making you feel like your worries are melting away… if you don’t get frustrated at some of the puzzles. For me, the puzzles varied wildly in quality, with the best ones being very intuitive and a nice challenge in figuring out how to accomplish your objective, and the worst ones being the ones in which you have no idea nor clue what you’re even meant to do, or, even worse, the empty space ones in which you know what you have to do but have no way to tell which object goes where in the game’s preferred organization. Thankfully, I found more intuitive puzzles than I found the other type, but there were still many more of the latter than I think should have been.If you think you’re okay with this caveat I mentioned, then you’ll probably find this game very relaxing, much in the vein of Unpacking, if you played that. But if you tend to get frustrated when a game wants a different solution than your perfectly valid one, or upon feeling that a puzzle might be unfair… then it might be best for you to steer clear of this title. For me, I had a good time, even with the frustration. Certainly commendable work, especially for a 2 person team. If you do pick up the game, I do hope you enjoy it. And if you want to talk about the game, I’m always down to chat! You can find me just a little to your left. … I’m so sorry. I’m actually probably thousands of kilometers away but I really wanted to make the joke.

_childDocuments_.review: A game by OCD's, for OCD'sPros:* Excellent escalation of puzzle difficulty, with some humor tossed in to break up tension.  Puzzles are generally that of organizing objects and/or clutter, but usually the underlying pattern to follow is not immediately obvious.* Great music and effects.Cons:* Since the whole point of the game is to discern the underlying pattern of each level, and some levels (not most) can be a little twitchy on recognizing your success, I went a little mad trying to fine-tune what I thought was a valid pattern... only to rage-quit, look up the solution, and find I was waaaaaaaaay off.TL;DR: 9/10 if you like puzzles - else, avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta give it up to the marketing team, because I was so excited for this game. And then after buying it on release day, I was like "Oh wait, this is like a million other puzzle games."Put the leaves color order. Make the spoons go smallest to largest. Turn the clock until a shadow in the background matches.I've played that game. I've played that game a hundred times. Any game under "puzzle, casual, relaxing, cute" is going to be this exact game. The marketing made it seem like it reinvented the genre. It didn't. It's a "puzzle, casual, relaxing, cute" game. You hear those tags, you know exactly what the game is. ... And you don't really expect it to be $15 (and no discount on release day). Also, needing to get things pixel perfect is annoying. A lot of puzzle games will say "Ah, you're 92% of the way, we'll just jiggle everything a little for you to get it perfect, you obviously know the answer." It genuinely felt like it was every a good fourth of the puzzles in this game I would get the right answer, not proceed, look at the hint, see the hint was the answer I did, and have to jiggle everything around for a solid minute trying to get it *exactly* where they needed to be. Genuinely, my playtime is as long as it is for this exact issue. Specifically from the postcard puzzle, where I had the correct answer for 30 minutes and it just wasn't "clicking" into place. It was Unpacking in spirit, but not execution. I wanted to put things in a drawer the way I wanted to.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is a game about finding satisfaction through organization. It is only sometimes a puzzle game. I think my biggest gripe with it was when I judged it too critically through the lens of a puzzle game. That said, some of the tasks are immensely satisfying, some are tedious in that you know exactly what has to be done but don't really feel like doing it - either because you feel the end result won't be particularly pleasing to behold or because getting there requires a non-insignificant amount of tedium. I think in terms of the balance, though, most of the tasks are rather satisfying.I do think that the daily tidying challenges are a bit of a mistake - they tend not to add a whole lot extra to the game and are essentially a roadblock for 100% achievement. They are usually just subtle remixes of the same challenges done before. All in all, I think this game is both fresh and satisfying, and do recommend it as a purchase (the DLC is also quite good too)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Some fun puzzles, but many levels have very arbitrary answers. Controls are not great - have to get objects to "snap" in place, and usually it works, but sometimes it's annoying to get to work, and that takes away from the game experience. I've seen quite a few people advertise this as a cozy, organizing game, but it is very much not that - it is very much a "puzzle" game where you try to figure out what the developers thought would be an appropriate arrangement. I would have expected more content for the price - the daily puzzles are nice, though, for after you play through the regular game; however, I have played some already (3 hours in) that are just the same as the in-game content. Nice concept in principle, not the best execution.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I've never had a game anger me so much but also make me so happy at the same time. _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Decent variety of puzzles and amazing art style/graphics. _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A great organizing game ! Without the pressure of a timer, it honestly helps me go through the levels faster since I don't have to concentrate on anything other than the patterns and placements. _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be so good, but it falls short. Some levels are intuitive enough that they make sense, but somewhere between "half" and "most" of the puzzles don't give any indication at all of what you're supposed to do. For example, one level gives you a handful of pencils of varying lengths. The natural assumption is that you are supposed to arrange them in order based on their length, which is true, but what the game gives you NO indication of AT ALL is that you're supposed to . Another example is a level where it gives you a bunch of envelopes with some stamps. Again, with NO indication of what you're supposed to do, you have to just click around the guess, Turns out, you . Another level has you stack papers on top of each other, but then a very similar appearing level wants you arrange them on (invisible) hot spots around the background. There's nothing distinguishing those mechanics.So this game is basically just "click around randomly until you find the invisible hot spots." It seems like they are supposed to be puzzles for you to figure out, but forgot to include the actual puzzle.The "hint" system gives you the full answer (at least on the levels I used it on), which is definitely not a reasonable thing for a game like this that gives no indication of what you're supposed to do.I don't generally bash on games where it's obvious I'm not the target audience, because I don't think that's really fair. In this case though, I *am* the target audience, as far as I can tell, and enjoyed the few levels that made sense.  2/10, A for effort. If the UI were fixed to provide indicators for where the invisible hot spots are, or even indicators about what each puzzle is supposed to be, maybe a riddle or something, the game could be so much better.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Its cute, fairly simple and an overall good time! The game does have its downsides, and isn't entirely perfect.If you like puzzles, colorful aesthetics, and cats this is for you, but some levels are hard/impossible to complete, even when doing exactly what the game wants you too. Some of the achievements are also buggy, so buyer beware if you want to 100% this game and its dlc. I'd give the game a 7/10, as the dlc being a bit of a mess, and some of the main game levels not working ruins a bit of the experience for me. It's a cute game, I just wish it worked a bit better.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: There were a few levels in A Little to the Left that I really enjoyed. But I was hoping for more organization gameplay, like Unpacking, instead of just another basic puzzle game. Most of the level have nothing to do with organizing or fixing anything. You just fumble around until you figure out what the puzzle wants you to do. I'm not a fan of these types of games and feel they never really hit the balance between providing a challenge but also giving you enough information to go on.If you like an average puzzle game where you have to figure out what the game is actually asking you to do before you can even attempt to know the answer, this is probably for you. But even still, it's definitely overpriced. This would be better around the 4.99usd mark.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A cute and enjoyable puzzle game with lots of content! My only complaint is that some of the puzzles are tedious, not complex. _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: generally good game. some puzzles feel repetitive and there's already not much content in the game. that being said, the art style is very cute and the puzzles themselves are fun and rewarding to complete.i'd give this game a similar review to unpacking's- if its on sale, go for it. if not, it might not be fully worth it.i was able to finish the game in 4ish hours, if that helps anyone with perspective.

_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: While only about 3 hours of playtime, I had fun with A Little To The Left. For me, it's at its best when it's a puzzle game - the levels with multiple solutions in particle encourage some creative thinking. The levels about organising a large collection of objects are satisfying, too.Where it falls down is levels which have no puzzle whatsoever (the constellations level and snowflake level in particular come to mind). These levels go from feeling like a puzzle based on a chore to being a chore. In addition, The Daily Tidy (alongside being the bane of all completionists and achievement hunters) pretty quickly became tedious for me. Daily Tidies based on good puzzles don't work (because you know the answer), but if they're based on non-puzzles (the last two Daily Tidies were constellations and snowflakes) then they're even more tedious than the original.Speaking of non-puzzles, some levels simply involve arranging a bunch of stuff so there's symmetry, but the actual pattern you choose doesn't matter as long as the symmetry is there. This wasn't clear to me, and I think I only realised this was the case after completing all such puzzles with hints.In addition, there's a few places where inputs seem finicky. You have the right solution, but you placed something slightly wrong or turned something a few degrees too much and the game doesn't acknowledge the solution (I think my biggest problem with this was on the alternative solution to the tomato cans). That said, this is rare.As a final complaint, for a game where the coolest part is replaying levels with multiple solutions, the game always forces you onto the next level when you complete a puzzle for the first time. So if you want to replay it while it's still fresh in your head, you have to exit to the menu and reload the level.Overall, this game is still excellent, I just wish they'd focused the experience more around the 3 Star levels and levels involving mass-tidying. Still a great game, highly recommend it while on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a satisfying game. It is cute, cozy, and has a good soundtrack. It is visually appealing and the level breakdown makes it easy to play for a short or long sitting. Did I expect to get emotional when beating the final puzzle level? No, but call backs to previous puzzles, motivational music, and a familiar friend all came together to make me tear up. A simple, thoughtful game that builds on what you've learned earlier. Sometimes challenging, but never so much that you quit and want to never come back. Eagerly awaiting more DLC, this was well worth the inexpensive investment.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: super lovely relaxing game. i found some puzzles frustrating at first because i didn't really know what to expect and i was too stubborn to look at the hints. it's a game i've played through 3 times now and i really do enjoy it. i love the daily tidys but i just wish there was so much more content lol. i'd prefer maybe a dlc that allows more creative freedom? i adore the dlc even more than the game itself but i would really like a dlc that allows us to decide where things belong rather than having to get everything in the perfect place. hope that makes sense o.o anyway, super lovely game and will probably play an endless amount of times!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is a nice, relaxed puzzle game. There's no pressure from a timer or any other reason to rush, and that's good. Because honestly some of the puzzles are downright un-intuitive.I found I either needed to use a hint, or mess with stuff for a good while on a level before something "clicked" and I suddenly got what I needed to do.The game has a good number of Steam achievements, providing decent replay value. But added replay value comes from the Tidy of the Day, which is a nice way to not have to engage the story, but still take on a quick puzzle.I recommend A Little to the Left, as a relaxed but challenging puzzle game with a cute story and relatable premise.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Any and all satisfaction from arranging things was lost due to the irritating UI: - Having to watch the animation of my completed levels play in its entirety before being able to select a level to go to. - Spending more time trying to get the item to fall into the EXACT place in order to complete a level, when visually it was already correct. Spent more time on some levels spamming left click to try and find the exact pixel it needs to line up to despite already finding the solution- For some reason, despite releasing an item, sometimes it would continue to move out of the position I'd placed it in, resulting in having to once again find the EXACT location- Solutions are vague and arbitrary, which became more annoying the longer the game was played

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the game for a bit now, and the lack of any communication on what is expected for the "puzzle" and the fact that hint is just an answer, really makes the game not enjoyable. Love the cat paw its usually unexpected.)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game expecting it to be a cosy little tidying game, since that's what it's advertised as - It is not.I really wanted to like this game, because I love what they're trying to do, but it's just too frustrating for all the wrong reasons. I can deal with a tough puzzle, I'll be the first to admit I'm not very good at them, but the game does a terrible job of explaining the logic of puzzles. The only way to get any idea of what the logic is, apart from guessing, is to use the hint function.Maybe if I'd have known what kind of game this actually was going into it I'd have received it better, but it's advertised as a tidying puzzle game. I didn't think that meant brain teasers and matching up images with their reflections to a hyper-specific level.All in all, this game barely scrapes a recommendation because it's something different and has plenty of fun moments, but only if you enjoy brain teaser puzzles. The whole tidying thing is honestly secondary, and that was the whole reason I bought this game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the levels are incredibly satisfying, especially in the DLC. The art style and sound design are both very pleasing. _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game a little while ago after getting it in a humble bundle, and I thought that I'd leave I review! _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I've never found such an infuriating game. _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: An atmospheric organisation game with a few puzzle elements but predominant focus on satisfaction and aesthetics. _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed organizing a big number of objects in different compartments. Those are my favorite levels and I really wish there was more of them. I even got the dlc hoping to get more but it didn't really satisfy me. Most of the puzzles are very short and simple and it's a little disappointing.Despite all of that, I do recommend it. The art style is lovely, the music and sound design are wonderful, most of the puzzles are well made (although lacking complexity most of the time) and the way hints work is very creative. I also liked figuring out the puzzles that can be solved in a number of ways, even if sometimes it was a bit convoluted.I just wish it was longer and more complex.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Really cute and fun puzzle organization game! I bought this after I finished Unpacking and I finished it over the span of a few days. I played it to take my mind off things and to ease anxiety. Not gonna lie though, some puzzles were hard for me and it could get a bit frustrating, but luckily, there's Hints and an option to skip the level. If I got too frustrated, I just closed the game and continued it later. I love the cat aspects and think the music and sound effects are really cute and satisfying. For harder levels, or levels with multiple ways to solve things, I streamed the game to my friends on Discrod and we figured them out together, which was really fun!I highly recommend this game! :)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Good Game, wait for a sale tho- If you are really debating on buying the game and want to know if its worth it- its not worth 15 bucks, I will be honest. The game has nothing necessarily bad going for it, but don't let the 75+ levels fool you like it fooled me. In total, there are 80 actual levels you can do, and some have different solutions to them. Though I would say that some of the levels are wayyyy too easy, and some are way too hard. It goes from organizing 5 colored pencils in the order of a rainbow in 5 seconds, to hanging up different tools on a wall based on where the nails are which took me like 15 minutes to figure out. Its about 2-3 hours of gameplay. With little repeatability. The game can genuinely be more picky on how to organize things than you would think. I personally think it would be way better if you reorganized everything in the way you wanted, and then said you were finished with the level, and continue to the next. Then at the end it could show you all the before and afters, and you get that feeling of having cleaned or fixed the mess to your liking, and not having to do it the way the game wanted you to. Maybe like an alternate game mode like that, idk. The art style and sound are really really nice though, I am personally a huge fan of all the little noises it plays when you interact with all the different items on all the levels. I like the sound of satisfying noises so if you are the same then this game definitely is nice in that field. Also the daily tidy thing is nice, but it just chooses a random level for you to do, so you are just repeating a level you've already done if you beat the game. So they take like 5 seconds to do. I would say this game is much more like a 5/10 dollar game as is, but I do think the devs plan to add more levels in the future, which is cool. Game itself is fun though, and a good 75-80% of the levels are satisfying to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: It's nice and cozy, I like it :). The art style is cute and fluffy, the lil cat is adorable, and the puzzles are very satisfying and relaxing. However, the daiky tidy's SUCK. One quick tip for these though, just change the time on your pc over and over :)Overall 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: If you like relaxing and cozy games- and puzzles tickle a part of your brain- this is the game for you. As your cat does cat things (messing up cabinets and breaking vases) you get to organize every drawer and cabinet to satisfaction. It doesn't end there! Plants, picture frames and more all need your expert organizing eye to put them back together.  If you've been wanting to organize but want to be able to walk away whenever this is a perfect substitute to cleaning up your personal space.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: 10h+ 4/10 1 (if you don't use the hint system) Yes, I would highly recommend  No Yes, achievements like "not using the hint system during the whole campaign" and "Using the hint system on every level"  Yes, doing 265 daily puzzles (And one achievement for doing 300 on consecutive days Yes Yes Yes, for a few achievements you have to solve the daily puzzles on consecutive days with the highest one being 300 days in a row No Yes, you have achievements for using the hint system all the time and for never using it NoI have such a hard time writing this review. On one hand, I adored the game, I had such a lovely time playing it. It was wholesome, fun and with moments frustrating because some of the puzzles with multiple solutions and not being able to figure out the other solutions. The game has a great hint system, but that will only show the main solution, not the others solutions.  So for people who love organizing/cleaning in games, this is a lovely one and I would highly recommend it. For achievement hunters, it is a totally different story. With the promise of this game kinda expected a relaxing achievement list. The ones where you have to do something special at a specific level and completing all the levels with all solutions would be the type of achievements I totally would expect and was ready for. Sadly it has so many frustrating achievements as the one to use no hints during the whole campaign as well as to use the hint on every level, but the worse are the 365 dailies and the 300 consecutive dailies, especially that last one. I believe it is possible to "cheat" a little bit on this by changing your computer time, but I'm not up for those types of challenges. Especially when you can get totally stuck and start over when one day you aren't able to solve the puzzle of that day. The developers have responded to  about how crazy the achievements are and that they will think about maybe redoing some of them, so that gives a bit of hope. For now, if you enjoy puzzle games, especially when there is some sort of organizing involved, I would highly recommend this game as it is a lot of fun! As an achievement hunter, I would for now wait and see what the developers will decide to do with those very tedious achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game with the entirety of my heart.      🏆 Overall Rating     ★★★★★     🎮 Gameplay      ★★★★★     🎨 Graphics      ★★★★★     🎵 Sound Design      ★★★★★      ↩ Replay Value      ★★★★★      😧 Difficulty      ★★★★☆      🖥️ PC Requirements      ★☆☆☆☆ If you're like me, you've heard nothing but good things about A Little to The Left, and that is for a reason! The art design is stunningly adorable, beautiful, and polished, the sound design is nothing short of a chef's kiss, and you can tell that at every turn the creators put so much thought and effort into every little detail. The puzzles range from simplistic to challenging and this is furthered by having multiple solutions to various puzzles! It helps you to think inside of the box, outside of the box, and all around! Every time you figure out the solution there is a euphoric feeling of accomplishment (and perhaps a bit of embarrassment from learning you were overthinking the entire thing)!The replay ability is incredible as well. Not only are you able to go through and play the entire game (and DLC) after just a little time away, but you can also play specific puzzles that particularly piqued your fancy. There is also the addition of "Daily Tidy's" which will keep you coming back day after day! This is hands down my favorite comfort game and I genuinely thank the creators from the bottom of my heart.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad puzzle game. But the emphasis should be on PUZZLE. Due to the marketing I was expecting a more zen experience like unboxing. So much of the game offers itself as "organizing, with multiple solutions for puzzles, and sometimes a cute cat to fuss with". My experience was more "increasingly obtuse puzzles meant to stump you on purpose, and a cat that appears largely once you've beaten your head against a puzzle and solved it just to mess it up on purpose". It's a cute game, I don't entirely regret getting it. But it was NOT remotely what I had wanted going into it. Which is a shame, since the first few puzzles hit that satisfying spot. But it soon turned to 'there is one RIGHT way to do this' solutions, and I found myself struggling to interpret what the creator thought was a "satisfying" solution versus what I thought looked appealing. By the last chapter, all the stages are metaphysical challenges (spoilers : one has you moving a mirror to arrange items specifically how they appear in the reflection, in order to match) with hard "there is One Right Way to solve this" answers. I hadn't bought this looking for a game that was "oops all adventure room point and click game puzzles". I wanted something more like Unpacking that perhaps had solutions but freeform and relaxing enough to not feel like I was fighting the game just to finish it.Also, that tupperware end scene went on for WAY too long.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I have always loved puzzles, but A Little to the Left has cemented that love as a key aspect of my personality. This game has whimsy, complex puzzle, and the daily challenges keep you coming back - daily! The DLC has done a great job continuing the interesting puzzles while keeping the pesky (and sweet) cat there at your side.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Parts of the game play is cheeky and unexpected, with really cute use of subtle storytelling. I pretty much can't get enough of the colors and how adorable all of the illustrations are. I'm trying to pace myself because it's all a little too engaging lol. Like, I could just mow through all of the puzzles like a bag of chips. My only complaint is that I wish none of it had an end. Give me more of everything please!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely delightful little game. The puzzles are satisfying and imaginative (and sometimes have more than one answer!) I appreciated the hint/let it be options, which ensured that the few levels I got really stuck on didn't stop me from progressing or detract from the enjoyability of the game. The illustrations are bright and cheerful, and the music is cute as well. The daily tidy is a nice way to get a little fun out of the game every day, too. If you like to sort and tidy up, this one's for you!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, challenging and satisfying game. I really can't get enough of it, and I'm sure my friends are tired of hearing me talk about it. The overall design is very charming, with an analog vibe and a pleasing color palette. The gameplay is seamless, especially since they added the replay option on the puzzle end screen. It's nice to be able to immediately replay a level for the puzzles with multiple solutions without having to exit and scroll back to it through the menu. I love the concept of the Daily Tidy, and it's always fun to have a new puzzle to play every day. Because the puzzle formats are (understandably) repeated in the Daily Tidy, sometimes it can be a bummer to get a repeat Tidy that has an easy solution when I'm in the mood for a challenge. Looking forward to any and all future expansion packs!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is perfectly priced! You get so many levels, and you can also do Daily Tidies. For those that try puzzle games and always get frustrated, don't worry about this! I'm incredibly impatient with puzzles and I loved every bit of this game. Never ever got frustrated. DLC is also amazing if you're craving more.It's also great for those that have ADHD and want to help get rid of the feeling of executive dysfunction. It's a good leeway to cleaning irl. Makes you ease into organizing your desk, or cleaning your kitchen counters. Very good game!
