Plus there's only two of them in the base game and only one in the daily challenges. Aside from that, I loved the whole game. Very chill vibes with puzzles that can be challenging without being frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great aesthetics and starts off with reasonable progression in concepts and difficulties. I found it absurdly charming to begin with, though the music got really repetitive really quickly. Unfortunately, as with many logical puzzle games, the logic behind some of the solutions was difficult for me to follow. I got to a point of frustration where I had to walk away, and when I returned, the frustration levels didn't really go down. So this isn't a game for me, but if people like puzzles that don't do a lot of hand-holding and works with items found in most houses in fun ways, this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I've enjoyed the entire game, except for the achievement for doing daily tidies - those were annoying, largely because they were so repetitive. In doing 30 consecutively, you learn that there really aren't even nearly 30 different versions.The reason this review is negative is, the devs add achievements for DLC, every time they add new DLC. They argue in reviews that it's because steam doesn't let them add the achievements to just the DLC (true), and the achievements add soooo much to the game! Except 1) they don't, and 2) even if they did, just add in-game achievements for that.This game is basically made for completionists, but then the devs add extra achievements, seemingly just to ruin your completion and make you buy the DLC. I can't think of any other reason they wouldn't exclusively use an in-game achievement option for the DLC in particular. It's sad, and I honestly wonder how many people buy the DLC just to keep their achievement progress.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam offered middle-ground reviews, this is a maybe. I RECOMMEND the game if you really think you'll like it and if it's on sale. I DON'T RECOMMEND the game however, because there simply isn't enough content for the price, some solutions are repeated multiple times and some puzzles are super finicky. It's cute though and the idea was good!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Review from someone with ADHD:the positives: it looks cute. the negatives: I played 5 min of this the refunded. Why would this game ever be $14.99? It's like if they took House Flipper, cut all of the graphics out of it, and then just gave up puzzle variation. This should be an app game for $5.00 bucks, that would make sense. But $14.99 for what, 75+ puzzles of just organizing things? What in the hell is that? I'm sure this was truly relaxing for some people but oh my god to me it was just anxiety producing seeing these mismatched items and then putting them in ways that felt, clunky and bad. If I wanted to clean things, I'd pay 2.50 for a ticket back on the train and clean my room, why is this a game? At least in House Flipper you have like, a house to complete, so you can see how it's changing over time, and you get excited about the next power washer section, stuff like that. You know what this made me feel like? It made me feel like I was drinking boba with the tapioca at the bottom, and you have to get all the tapioca balls in the straw or you feel anxious. At least I do. But in this case you solve it, and then you just jump to getting more of a mess! There's no "look at all these fixed things you did" it's just, hey you are anxious about this messed up area, you put things either next to or onto things, then you get a star and then go to the next mess. Don't play this game. Please. And if you have ADHD, man I hope you can enjoy this, but this game at this price just made me reallly annoyed. If this was $5.00 this review would not have been as harsh.

_childDocuments_.review: A cute selection of organizational-type puzzles. It's a relaxing chill-out game for the most part, but some puzzles had me stumped for a good while. Thankfully, you're able to skip levels and come back to them if they're too challenging. There's a hint feature as well, but I feel the hints just gave away the answer outright instead of being a small nudge towards the answer. I was expecting the cat to really mess up the puzzles in my playthrough, but they seemed more of a cameo for quick mischief! I didn't mind it, but I would have loved an alternate difficulty where the cat would have made you find the alternate solution, or something similar. Overall I think it's worth playing until the end, because the final puzzles were my favorites. The game doesn't stop after the main campaign though - multiple puzzles give up to 3 different solutions, and there's a Daily Task to check out every day as well. I think it's a really charming game for puzzle fans and worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a calming way to indulge my habit of adjusting things until they're *just right* and is easy to play in small bites that doesn't take time away from tidying my actual home. I love that they continue to add new content, including the recent DLC, the seasonal Daily Tidies, and the Archive that allows me to visit levels I missed.

(Around 13 euros normal. 10 euro on steam summer sale 2023)To then add a DLC that is half the price of the main game seems unfair to me.But even with this in mind, I still think it's good.Grab it when the price goes down or when a big sale hits.

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute and relaxing puzzle game. The music is really calming, I could listen to it on repeat completely independent of the game. The puzzles themselves are very visually appealing, and present enough of a challenge without being TOO MUCH of a challenge, you know? I also love that there are multiple ways to do several of the puzzles instead of it being one and done, there's so much creativity put into the solutions. At first I was a bit disappointed that the Daily Tidies are repeats of puzzles you have done, I thought they would be new puzzles introduced daily but tbh I understand how unrealistic that was. I still enjoy doing them for the achievements, and it's definitely helping me to get in the practice for the perfection achievement hehe.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to do this review after I completed all the achievements, but since the dlc ruined that and I refuse to give more money to this game, here it is.I like puzzle games, I really do. I am a big fan of the Professor Layton games; I have played all of them. Those games are known for having a lot of really good puzzles and some bad ones that you cant possibly follow their logic. This game has some really good puzzles that make you feel really good for figuring them out, and a LOT of bad ones that are even worse than the worst puzzles from Professor Layton.The repetitive nature of some of the puzzles only worsen when you have to solve them multiple times and even worse when you have to do them again and again and again with the daily puzzles that simply change the assets. I honestly cannot recommend this game because each time I played it, I just ended up frustrated by how it was.If you like it, that is wonderful it just means I couldn’t enjoy something you did. And in the end that is more important than anything else. I just didn’t enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are equally cute and frustrating. Half the challenge for the puzzles seem to be making very minute changes to pieces until the game finally deems the answer correct. The puzzles shouldn't need to be pixel perfect for aligning things. Towards the end of the game, there are "puzzles" where there is no logical solution. The puzzle is simply "make this look aesthetically pleasing, as arbitrarily determined by the game devs". Even if you use symmetry and make it look nice, if it's not in the exact layout that the devs, arbiters of aesthetics, deem correct, you won't get credit for it. These are less puzzles and more a mind reading activities. There's no real problem solving.The other frustration is the controls. The control scheme only allows you to drag items, so no rotation or anything like that. The game then decides whether an object should be oriented differently or not. Many times, you're left hunting to see where the game wants you to start a puzzle (waiting for the object to "snap" in place). I've also had issues where an object will reorient itself, leading me to believe it was correctly placed. When I picked up the piece again, it would revert to its original orientation and not switch back. I don't know if collision from other objects caused this, but it lead me to believe a piece was placed correctly when it wasn't even facing the correct way.Another small, but bizarre design choice is the main menu. You click the "play" button, expecting the game to take you to your current/last puzzle, like virtually every other video game created in the last two decades. However, for this game, "play" apparently means "new game" because it starts you from the very first puzzle. You actually want to click "levels" and then scroll through tens/hundreds of puzzles until you get to where you were last. I wanted to like this game, but it needs some polish.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is a very casual and fun organizing game. I really enjoy the levels where you put items in specific slots, but I like the variety in puzzles. The achievements are fun, and I think that having more than one way to complete some levels adds a challenge, but still keeps the casual flow of the game. The daily tidy seems to be a nice add-on, allowing for a "new" daily puzzle to scratch that organization itch.If you enjoy puzzle games, then this one is totally worth it. I did get it on sale, but I think I enjoyed myself enough to say it's worth the price for those who truly enjoy putting things exactly where they belong.

AAnd especially notable are all the developer animals shown in the Credits. So overall a perfect Game.I personally have 3 Problems, but those are completionist related. 1. The no Hint Achievement is placed further below the use a hint achievement. So because of this i used a hint on purpose to get the achievement and later deeply regret because i will need to wait some time till i can go through the game again without getting bored. I would just leave the: let it be achievement and use a hint achievement away, then a clean walkthrough would also be more interesting to achieve.2. Having Achievements for the DLC is cool, but that they are placed in the main game again means: i have to buy the dlc to get 100%.3. Having Dailys in a short puzzle Game is a big no go for me. _childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly pretty game with each level having a lot of visually striking and unique objects to try to organize.The main issue is that the puzzles start becoming absurdly esoteric after a bit with my personal experience being seeking out a guide or activating a hint before reaching my own solution or repetitively dropping everything randomly until an audio cue played or the object snapped into place which never felt satisfying.I honestly wouldn't be too perturbed by how backed into a corner some solutions are if the game gave more levels multiple stars to collect as SOME progress is being made, but very few actually have multiple solutions and require finding 'THE' way.At least there's no punishment or downsides for hints and you can always skip a level, but with how short the game is it feels like a waste, and as someone who likes 100%ing as I go along it reached a point where it got annoying.The price is also rather a lot more than what I'd expect with all this in mind and would honestly see it working more as a visually striking paid mobile game.If you're looking for a cute yet complicated puzzler then feel free to try it out, but the advertising of it being satisfying begins fading the further you go which drags down the art when worked into a full product.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If logic puzzles are your cup of tea, give A Little to the Left a shot. Just make sure you read lots of reviews or watch a let's play or two so you get a good sense of the game's difficulty before buying.  If you're looking for a more dollhouse-like experience similar to Unpacking, skip this one.Many of the puzzles are fun and give you a sense of accomplishment when solved. Others are IMPOSSIBLE to figure out without hints (thank goodness for the 'ding' and items snapping to the grid as self-corrects), making the game more frustrating than fun. I stumbled my way to more than one solution before I even knew there were actual hints available in the pause menu. Even then, I didn't always understand what I did to get the puzzle right. I suspect many of you are smarter and far more patient than I am, so your mileage may vary.As other players wrote, the demo doesn't set the right expectations for the the difficulty of the full game. The art style and music are lovely, and the levels that allow you to sort, order and organize just so are a blast. Less enjoyable are the rage-quit worthy-logic puzzles scattered throughout an otherwise chill game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: If you are the child of a hoarder you will love this game, especially the DLC. It's a bit short for the price IMO, but it's indescribably cathartic to be able to organize the scenes into something that makes sense. Do not play if you hate cats. This game loves cats. Some "levels" in the DLC are not actual puzzles, they're just pictures of the cat and the "solution" is to click on its head to pet it. You can skip these with the "let it be" button, but it feels a bit cheap that maybe 5 of the expected challenges are actually just cat simping. "Daily tidy" is a nice feature and I do enjoy it, but sometimes it's just a partial reskin of existing levels from the main game.Overall I don't recommend this game if you're one of those poor chaps with only a few fivers you've gotta apportion between entertainment and food for the month, but if you've got loose pocket change this is the place to spend it. Also if you still have issues from your hoarding parents give this a whirl- it's way cheaper than therapy and it's got really lovely sound effects.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I feel bad not enjoying this one. I love these kinds of relaxing puzzle games. However, I found a few aspects tedious that were growing a little more obvious over time.Some puzzles have more than one solution, but the hints are rigid. At least, I think so anyway, I did not see a way to get a hint for an alternative solution. So if you solve a more challenging puzzle but can't figure out the second or third solution, you're left either flailing or giving up. There were a few puzzles as well where I could see a potential solution, but it wasn't a solution that the devs had considered so it doesn't work.But these were relatively small issues. The one that made me stop and put the game back was the soup can labels. The solution was obvious, yet it wasn't working. I finally gave up and checked the hint, and...I was right. I had been a pixel off of the exact positioning. It had multiple solutions, and I realized then that I probably would not be able to 100% this game. No hints for the alternative solution, and armed with the knowledge that it would have to be pixel-perfect I switched to the next puzzle. Solved it easily, but then found that some of the alternatives that I was coming up with weren't working.It's not a good fit for me. Only some of the puzzles have a clever "aha" moment, and the game has a few intentional moments of making a mess. It might be a good fit for you, so I'd say give it a try and if it doesn't click after an hour, it isn't for you either.

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game! The basic content had a variety of ordering puzzles from super easy to medium difficulty, in which you have to pay attention to the details. The daily tidies continued to bring me back to the game every day, determined to get up to 100, but I wish there were even more of them. I really appreciated the newer DLC puzzles that were all medium difficulty but with more complexity. I hope they continue to add more of those levels. :)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful calming game that weaves a small but sweet plot line that brought a smile to my face. My cat joined me for a playthrough and it genuinely enhanced my experience. Although the overall length of the game isn't 50+ hours, I'm of the opinion that games don't need to be long to be enjoyable. If you enjoy puzzles and organizing (and cats!), this game should be on your wishlist.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game for its beautiful graphics and the different levels and styles of puzzles! It is very relaxing, though if you play for too long at one time, you may find it starts to get a bit tedious/boring (though this may be due to my ADHD). This game is most relaxing if you try to limit play to a specific amount of time per day. Overall a beautifully designed game!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing cozy game. Perfect for procrastinating actually tidying up or just continuing if you already did so. It is obvious this was a labor of love game for the dev team.The art style is minimalistic, the colors are pleasant to the eye and the music is relaxing. Perfect for a little breather from real life responsibilities.The puzzles themselves aren't that hard to figure out, altho the alternative solutions aren't always the most obvious (the third solution for leaves took a while for me). The pacing they created with puzzles is amazing to me since I didn't know that was possible to do. I Love what they did at the end or rather with the puzzles at the end, it gave me a great feel good high.While I do recommend this game for those who like puzzles and get a kick out of making things tidy, I must say I expected more content out of it. Its a solid 4 hour game (i did all the puzzles including the multiple solutions in this time frame) and for the price it's at i feel like it should have been more content to it, so i recommend getting it on sale if you are used to getting more than 4h of gameplay inside of this price range. That said it does have daily puzzles that are different everyday and work up to achievements that give it more replay value, since base puzzles stay the same.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This has to be the most satisfying game I have ever played! No pressure, relaxing music, organising things to be just right, and a surprising amount of replay ability. You can get through the whole game relatively fast but some of the extra stars are hard to get right away. I love the Daily Tidy as well, makes me want to come back everyday to see what puzzle is showcased. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: thought id love this game, but it really got under my skin, the hints are just the answer and sometimes the puzzle makes no sense. it wanted me to mess up the paintings with out any rhyme or reason, and the hint didnt make it make any more sense.  i gave up on the game not cuz its hard but annoying and repetitive the calendar and sticky notes with scribbles came up like twice before i got to do any kind of sortingi wish refunds were a thing
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I found the DLC to be more fun than the actual game. The game itself is very calming and keeps you occupied with fun puzzles which I enjoyed, however the price is way too high for this kind of game. The game itself can be finished in a couple of hours and then there really isn't anything else to do. The replay value of the game is low as it is just puzzles you solve once (or twice if you want to get all the solutions). I definitely recommend getting it on sale if you're planning to buy it, but overall the design and music of the game is great and it is a cute idea. In my opinion, there should have been way more levels and more to do in the game besides the daily tide. Some of the levels are also not puzzles at all and just require you to click a few times on the screen which was disappointing. The organizing levels with the cupboards and drawers from the dlc were by far the best and there should have been way more of them. Was quite disappointed in how quickly I finished the dlc (within an hour).
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so satisfying when you get to organize the little trinkets. The cupboards and drawers DLC is by far  my favorite, and I really enjoyed seeing all the cats throughout. I will say it did get a little frustrating on certain levels, and some I was just downright baffled. But overall, I think this is definitely worth the play, and a great game to hop onto at the end of a day.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: An immensely satisfying game with plenty of replayable potential. Some of the levels were relatively easy, and I have yet to find alternate solutions to some. This game is relaxing and fun to play, even my mom found it relaxing, and she has difficulty passing the tutorials of most games. This is an excellent game for people of all ages and skill levels and makes you feel good.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: The art is really charming and I like the puzzle design. I get tired after doing a puzzle or two and so I only play for a few minutes a day at most, but I feel like that's how this game is best played. It made me sad to see so many people complain about the price; I feel like it's well worth full price for an entirely hand drawn indie game that's very unique and whimsical. The creators did an amazing job.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get it twisted, I  this game. The art is fantastic, the music is relaxing, and the controls are great. The price is a little much for how much content there is in the game. There is a daily play mode, where a new puzzle is unlocked each day, but after finishing the game in two sittings, I'm not sure I'm going to bother coming back to play a level that will only take 3 to 5 minutes to complete.I'm not saying that the price is exorbitant or anything, but for what the game is, and how finicky some of the levels can be with precise placements, the price is a touch high.If you are willing to spend $15 to fill a single afternoon playing an organizational puzzle game, then do it. _childDocuments_.review: There are a bit too many moments where you're doing it right but one thing is off by the tiniest increment so it doesn't count and you end up going over a million other things and then looking up a walk-through (or taking a hint) just for it to tell you to do the thing you tried first for it to suddenly work, which is INCREDIBLY INFURIATING. A good example is the level with the balls in the paintings. literally didn't do anything different it just suddenly worked after I looked it up, I hate that level so much.Other than all that this game is great and I'd fully recommend it to people (at least the first four chapters, the fifth one is kinda weak in comparison and... just not really fun). I'd especially recommend it if you're a neat freak or have some amount of OCD (Which I'm sure I probably do) as then the way the game thinks just sorta makes sense and you're likely to see the solutions pretty quickly (except in the fifth chapter, it sucks).

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, and I think it has a lot of merit. The game's style is really cute and very well crafted. It is visually very strong and what drew me into the game to begin with.However, I just can't say the same about the puzzle design. I understand it is first and foremost, a puzzle game where you have to find the "catch". But it advertises itself as a relaxing organisational experience and it's not really that. Some puzzles only have one set answer even if you can craft many different ways to organise the scene.I found myself frustrated as I can't figure out why my answer wasn't correct, after a few times of feeling this way I just couldn't keep playing. The real answers are too abstract and sometimes feel arbitrary. Sometimes I would just stumble upon these "real answers" randomly because of the items snapping into place and playing an audio cue.I think a way that could make this game feel better to play is allow more and looser answers to all puzzles. Let the players experiment and find all the possible solutions. When I'm done with a level, instead of moving me forward, let me retry and fiddle around and see what different and abstract answers I can make up.The "let it be" option is a good design choice but feels unsatisfying to click when I've made my own answer.I feel like the whole time I'm cleaning someone else's house with their rules instead of my own spaces which makes the game feel tedious unintentionally. It's a cute game if you like abstract puzzles that look pretty, not really for those looking for a zen and carefree experience.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: "A great little game to relax with." At least that's what I thought until I saw the repetitive daily tasks and positioning puzzles (clover and leaves from trees) that can't be solved with logic. So the game is too boring for me. If these "puzzles" had been at the beginning, I would have refunded the game immediately.

_childDocuments_.review: It's OK. Don't expect "puzzle-puzzles"; it's mostly symmetry, counting and pattern finding. Color blind people might have difficulty with some levels. Too much UX is sacrificed for flavor; there should be a replay button for doing alternative solutions immediately during first play, and the animations and sluggish controls get old quick. I've lost count how many times I've had to nudge items to make them count. A bit expensive for the value, not much replayability (the daily puzzles seems like rehashes so far).

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left feels like is was made for me. As someone who habitually sorts their effects with purposeful direction, I found myself kicking my feet with glee upon sorting so many of the solutions in this puzzle game. It's hard to put into words, but this particular style of puzzle just makes my brain happy.Fortunately, puzzles are not constrained to orthodox or practical sorting solutions. Instead, you frequently must perceive overarching patterns in minute details. For example, a series of objects may form a continuous pattern when arranged properly. When properly arranged, the solutions are so satisfying I had trouble tearing myself away from the game.The puzzles strike a great balance of genuine headscratchers, and simpler yet still gratifying arrangements. A Little to the Left trusts you as a player, offering no tutorials or explanations for its puzzles. Inevitably, there will be the occasional alternate solution which leaves you stumped, and though rare, some of these are not altogether intuitive.The game wraps up in a surprisingly sweet and arresting ending, and its feline "antagonist" is such a cute little fella. Then the DLC presents more involved puzzles which utilize the recurring patterns seen in the base game in larger spaces, often utilizing multiple patterns for different series of objects.I adore A Little to the Left. No puzzle game has quite scratched the itch like this one, and I was joyous as I played through it. While its specific style is personally appealing, I also just think it's a tremendously charming puzzler all its own, and I encourage you to give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I want to like this game, I just can't. Some of the puzzles just have some hyper-specific answer it expects you to just know. I have had a good number of times something feels like it should've been a solution, but it was the game just misguiding you with design. While this might be seen as a feature to make it harder, it honestly just feels like a slap to the face because I paid attention to the wrong detail, and the only way you can tell it's the wrong trail is by following it.And other times, you're supposed to put objects in certain places they will just snap to, but you don't know that's what you're supposed to do until you try putting the objects all across the screen. Some kind of indicator would've been nice. And I had an issue when I "solved" a level correctly, it didn't complete. I had to restart the level and try the same exact solution again to complete it, which will make you feel like you're going insane if you didn't take a hint. Overall, the game is pretty and has a relaxing feel to it but poor UI choices, hyper specific solutions, and false solutions have just ruined the experience for me.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first "no" review for a game, but honestly its only 60% no and 40% yes, since the game is okay and I cannot give it a "mixed" or "meh" review. Why do I think it's more on the negative side is because the game keeps bugging in certain puzzles, like where I have to choose the leaves that I want to get rid off and it doesn't let me choose the ones I want but other ones that I shouldn't get rid off it lets me choose. I also thought the game would be more like "Unpacking" which would have been more satisfying because I love organizing, but it has more puzzles than I expected and some of them make no sense. Like the cat Polaroids, which makes me frustrated and not leaving me with a satisfied feeling. Now, I do love puzzles but there are plenty of those and sometimes you just want to organize things without having to do it in real life lol. I bought this game on sale, and I intend to buy the DLC because I do like the game enough to play it. But would I recommend it to other people? Not really. If there would be quality of life update in the game then I would turn my "no" into a "yes".
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I would probably give this game a 9/10 for people with neurodivergencies, a 7/10 for people who like cozy gaming, and a 6/10 for everyone else. Overall it's just extremely satisfying to arrange everything so tediously. I think sometimes it can become a bit picky with how EXACT it sometimes requires you to be (especially the Drawers DLC) but it's something you can relax into and use your brain for.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game. Having enjoyed Unpacking and Assemble with Care, I thought this would run in a similar vein. Unfortunately A Little to the Left - while it looks great - quickly becomes annoying and frustrating. What the game wants from you as a solution is often obscure and you have to rely on the hint (which gives you the solution right away. A gradual hint system would have been much better). Not to mention how finicky placement can be. On a particular level involving tools, the game would not accept my solution because one item was a pixel or two out of alignment, despite being where the damn thing needed to be.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles are very fun and engaging, with a lot of clever details hidden in the puzzles. Whilst the puzzles can be relatively challenging, some are quite easy, and most puzzles can be completed in under 10 minutes. It also features a nice looking art style and overall is well designed, The game is a bit pricey for the amount of content, at a bit over $20 AUD, and finished the base game in a bit under 5 hours. They do upload daily puzzles, but most of the ones I've seen are just repeats of puzzles from the base game, and aren't as engaging as you already know how to solve them. Overall still a good game, I thoroughly enjoyed playing it and recommend it to anyone looking for a puzzle game, especially those new to the genre.

Not at the beginning, not on the main menu, I couldn't find a help menu, etc. There is a "HINT" option, but I don't feel the hints are clear at all. I tried the hint twice, only when really needed, and it almost made it more confusing.I'm neurodivergent and really struggle when instructions/tasks aren't clearly explained...I ended up getting really overwhelmed after some levels. The first some puzzles I was able to work my way through, but once I hit a pattern I couldn't figure out even the hint felt not enough. It was so frustrating. I ended up more stressed and not relaxed.I know this may seem stupid to many, but I'm leaving this comment for the one person who may also feel this and need more clear instructions.The game is adorable, but I feel disappointed. _childDocuments_.review: I do love the idea, and was drawn to this game because of my frustration with the short length of Unpacking and how there were so many "wrong" ways to organize things. However, I wasn't expecting to encounter the idea that there are a bunch of wrong ways to organize things in this game as well. When there's a stack of books of the same height, I thought color and size was an appropriate way to organize. Apparently, you have to make the colors link in a way it wants as well. This carried on, and various other little things.Frustratingly, there's no words or anything that would tell you how the game works. Nothing that says "sometimes there is more than one way to organize this one" or "this one only has ONE correct way, despite how many ways you can think of."Maybe if you aren't going to be bothered by every organization idea you try being wrong, then this would work for you. For me, some of them are quite the stretch and the lack of information + possible time limit affecting my star score? It's confusing, if nothing else. I don't personally find it comforting to race and try as organize as fast as possible.

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is an interesting puzzle game about organization and getting things just right. The animation and music is very nice, and can result in hours and hours of fun while figuring out how to categorize and organize each level. I consider myself as someone with a bit of neat freak tendencies because I like order and things to be put in their proper place, or arranged in a certain way, so this game provided me with a bit of respite from reality. However, I also found the game annoying because certain levels required a certain kind of organization, and no matter how I would try to figure out how to solve it (without looking online for cheats or walkthroughs), nothing in that certain level really aided me in solving it. While with a lot of levels you can figure out how to organize it with a few trial and errors, certain levels felt so specific, as if it had to be by the developers definition of "organized". So is the game somewhat relaxing? Yes. Is the game also somewhat frustratingly annoying? Yes. This game is not as fun as some of the other organization games I've played, just because some levels leave no room for leeway. My suggestion is to buy this on sale, and not at full price. Also, don't buy the DLC unless you've tried the actual base game and decide you really like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game and its DLC on a whim after missing a good puzzle game in my life. _childDocuments_.review: a great game to unwind if you're a cozy gamer. each puzzle brings something new to the table and it's fun to figure out all the possible solutions. it also provides helpful hints that can help struggling players, and i like how you can choose to only erase part of the hint if you only need help with part of the puzzle. the base game campaign is tons of fun but i will say that it's a bit short. if you can afford it, then buy it full price, but if you can't, then i highly recommend buying it on sale <3the dlc is also very nice and simple. it didnt stray far from the original game and it really just felt like an add-on with more levels, just like you'd expect.my only criticism would be the daily tidy. i think the 100-day tidies is an excessive achievement. especially since the daily tidies are simply remakes of a handful of puzzles from the campaign (maybe 10 or so puzzles).  i understand the concept of the daily tidies and i like the idea of "doing something small each day," but it really just felt repetitive.  while the campaign is fresh and rewarding, the daily tidies are just monotonous and repetitive.a tip for any fellow completionists: you can simply change the time on your computer to skip to the next days' tidies. (there's a great guide by D.A.R.K. if you look at the community forum's guides!)as for anyone else who's read this far, i recommend time travelling to 12/27/2022 to try the five special holiday tidies! they were super fun and unique :) i hope they bring it back this year!and of course, thank you devs for all the work you put into this game <3 despite my criticism towards the daily tidies, i had an absolute blast!! i ended up 100%-ing the game in just 4 days haha

_childDocuments_.review: Just a cutesy time-passer with strong 'just one more puzzle' energy.- The cursor design and click detection are quite poor, especially when playing on a laptop track pad or the steam deck. I found myself getting a little frustrated with this.- There is a point in the game where you are unable to skip a 'cutscene' in order to continue on. It isn't long, but this would have been a nice feature. I wasn't a fan of the time it took to move from one puzzle to the next.- Many of the puzzles feel like pure 'filler' and are not challenging, nor interesting. For example there are countless 'symmetry' puzzles, where you're given some amount of shapes and need to create symmetry along a central Y axis.  This disappointed me, because there were many puzzles that felt quite cheeky/clever otherwise. At ~5 casual hours in length the game serves its purpose well, but I wouldn't classify it as  or a 'must buy' puzzler. I appreciate the trance the game put me in, and there's a lot of love put into this. So worth the $15, and even better if you can get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game didn't exactly live up to my expectations, and I wish that Steam had a Mixed review option.  In all fairness, I should of recognized the use of the word "cozy" in the game description as a red flag so I won't bash the game too much, but the description is still a bit misleading which is why I'm leaving a review at all.What drew me in was the promise of a puzzle game with multiple solutions.  This is technically true, but the puzzle aspect is very superficial.  Most of the puzzle solutions only involve ordering items smallest to largest, matching colors, creating a symmetrical pattern, etc.  Where the multiple solutions come into play is, for example, you'll order things by size and then you get to go back to the same puzzle and order things by color, etc.  Not a lot to it.  Also, the music is comprised of what feels like the shortest musical loops the devs could find, and it becomes annoying fast.  I kept playing at a leisurely pace in hopes of getting to some more clever puzzles but finished the game in about 4 hours without the puzzle quality improving.Given the release date and game's content, this feels like something that was put together by a few people who were stuck at home during the COVID lockdowns and decided to make a simple game based on what they could find around the house.  So it's got a lot of charm and you'll probably enjoy the game if you're looking for a casual experience.  If you're looking for an even remotely serious puzzle game though, then you'll be disappointed by this game compared to what the game description says.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun puzzle game.Not for someone who needs high levels of stimulation, this game is very relaxed and chilled out. Literally, you organise stuff on every level. The final level is a fun mix of the puzzle skills you've learned. It is fun to try and discover the different patterns and that some levels have multiple solves. I also love that when you play there is no time limit, no stress, just you and the puzzle, you also don't have to find all the solves when they have multi-solve levels which is a nice way to keep on moving through the game if you get stuck. The way clues are done is also very helpful, you rub out the page to show the solve meaning you decide just how much of a hint you get, a perfect mechanic for me when at times I just needed a little guidance and didn't want to spoil the fun of actually understanding the pattern.I'm especially grateful that the game is not traditional puzzle based, I get so stressed out by traditional puzzles, this is more about pattern recognition, something I adore!!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so satisfying! I played the demo a while back and was looking forward to the full release. So glad it's finally here. There are occasional puzzles that seem a bit convoluted. One or two I didn't understand even after using the "hint" mechanic to solve it. Most are pretty intuitive to solve without a hint, or by just uncovering one tiny portion of the hint screen to give you a place to start. I also like how there are visual and auditory clues when you get something right or wrong. Things snap into place and a tiny chime sounds when you get it right, for many puzzles. (Things can also snap or settle into the wrong place, but it doesn't chime in this case.) If something is in the wrong spot, it will often skew off-kilter so you  know it doesn't go there. Overall, I find this puzzle game to be calming and very enjoyable and I look forward to continuing. I am about to finish chapter 3 after just shy of 4 hours, and have unlocked 10/51 achievements. I am not specifically seeking achievements yet, but likely will go back for any I missed. I noticed you can go back and replay previous puzzles which I was grateful for because I accidentally skipped one I was having a tough time with, when I was trying to figure out if I had to save. (Note: the game seems to auto-save your progress.) Daily puzzles are a total mystery to me. Have not been able to solve one.*edited to correct the time played*Second edit: About 8.5 hours to get all solutions to all puzzles. Thank you to the reviewer who mentioned the "stars" as I hadn't even noticed them. I thought it was pretty fun to go back and think of another way to solve the same puzzle besides the first way that occurred to me. Overall I enjoyed this game a lot, and I'll probably go back to do the Daily Tidy occasionally as well.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Doing the bare minimum in A Little to the Left is the fun, relaxing organizing experience it makes itself out to be. Trying to 100% it, on the other hand, is sometimes like staring at one of those stereoscopic images where it looks like a bunch of TV static but it promises, allegedly, that if you look at it in juuuust the right way it'll become a bunny. I mean this in the best possible way.A Little to the Left has the amount of thought put into its concept (reflected in the multiple modalities of solving, the environmental story, and a well-crafted artsy aesthetic) that puts it beyond merely a novelty or oddity based in its particular appeal. It could have skirted by on its unique concept alone, but it didn’t – and for a game based on an observant, details-orientated mindset, it shows.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game didn't quite meet my expectations. I think the issue I have is that perhaps for the purpose of either minimalist aesthetics or streamlining the game there is no introduction to the rules of the puzzlesFor the most part this isn't a problem at all as most of the puzzles are simple and self explanatory enough to where it isn't challenging. However every once in a while I run into something so obtuse that it takes me out of the relaxing experience altogether and introduces frustration.An example is a puzzle with a clock where the only mechanic is moving the hands of the clock forward and backward. Seems simple, but I got quite stuck on it. The actual solution is that  Unfortunately there aren't any visual indicators of what this win condition is and it was significantly less intuitive than other puzzles in this game. In another game,  they would likely start you off by atleast introducing you to the rules, then gradually giving you increasingly difficult puzzles. However with this, the rule isnt obvious since each puzzle has a totally different "win" condition and once you do figure it out, instead of then ramping up the difficulty by adding complexity, it takes you immediately to a new puzzle with a different rulesetAs a puzzle game, I think its not super satisfying since most of the puzzles are a bit too easy. As a zen-like experience, I found the peace occasionally disrupted by a very unintuitive puzzle that left me frustrated

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is a game that is a little difficult to describe, but if you're part of the target audience, you'll just "get it" when you get in the game.Who is the target audience?  I really believe it's designed for those of us who like to fidget, those of us who compulsively organize things by some obvious or ambiguous set of standards.  Those of us who can look at any random stack of objects and feel that things aren't quite "right" until we fiddle with it a bit.As someone who absolutely fits this description, I cannot describe the pure, unadulterated joy of playing this game.  Stoking equal parts curiousity and comfort, every new puzzle made me giddy.  These "puzzles" are often an assortment of items which you then need to sort or organize or otherwise interact with in ways that may or may not feel instinctive to you.  What I like the most about this is that many puzzles have multiple "solutions".  I love going into one of those, and doing what feels instinctive to me and then trying to figure out how other people might see those objects and how they might interact with them that isn't so obvious to me.The art is beautiful and fun and the music is great.  This game is relaxing and also exciting to me.  I beat this game in 5 hours and played a handful of the "daily tidy" offerings.  At this price point, that was well worth it to me.  And there's still many puzzles left for me to discover their other solutions and the game offers a fresh new puzzle every day called a "daily tidy".  Worth every penny to me!  I strongly recommend A Little to the Left and I look forward to seeing whatever Max Inferno develops next.

You'll likely spend a bit of time pondering a few of them. _childDocuments_.review: This is the best money I have ever spent, possibly ever. The art design? Impeccable. The sound design? INCREDIBLE, MY GOODNESS. The hit boxes and subtle things as small as the way the little X twirls when you close out of the settings? WOW. Some of the puzzles are very easy, some are incredibly creative, some are just satisfying as HELL and sometimes they're almost a bit TOO out of the box. The hint design is extremely clever to where you only have to uncover the parts you want, should you want to keep the rest of the puzzle answer unspoiled. The music is also just really nice.I can't even begin to describe the joy I felt with how satisfying some of the organizing sections were. If you have autistic friends, I'm like 93% sure they will love you for the REST of their lives if you gift them this game. I was screensharing this game to mine and they practically came.I have never wanted to support a studio more than this one and really look forward to their future work. the DLC is COMPLETELY worth it, this is the first time since playing Outer Wilds where I was 100% confident in my need for the DLC. The only thing I have to complain about is the cat, man's is cute but a SABOTEUR and a NUISANCE and a harbinger of CHAOS. And I do think its a bit of a cop-out for some of the DLC levels to literally just be petting the cat by clicking once. But I'll let this one slide, even if the pin-up poses he makes on the moon is kinda weird.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. It was really cozy. It also works your brain and gets you problem solving. The levels were really creative, each level was unique so the game did not get boring or repetitive. Completing each level is really satisfying. The difficulty of the levels are just right. some are fairly easy others are challenging. Some of the levels have multiple ways to complete them.

_childDocuments_.review: I first got to know this game through a youtube video, and it seemed right up my alley and like a game I would love.And I did love it, it was quite enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: While I ultimately do not recommend this game, that advice is not without caveats. I think there is a lot to admire in what the creators have done. The organizational puzzles can be quite cathartic and the sense of accomplishment upon completion is worth noting. However, some of the puzzle solutions can feel subjective and arbitrary. I think this game will appeal to a very specific type of gamer and I certainly appreciated the low stakes, low stress level of the game. All that said, for all its charm, it did not quite scratch my puzzle itch. Your mileage may vary.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I think that A Little to the Left is an incredibly charming puzzle game, between its sound direction, art style, and the mundane setting/puzzles focused on organization and grouping. It is a really good casual zen game. I have played both the original game and the DLC, which took probably around 6.5 hours. This and the DLC are both great plays, and as a bonus there is an archive of seasonal/holiday puzzles. For what you pay for in this game, you get a polished game with unique style and puzzles.I have a few criticisms which do not change my enthusiastic recommendation of this game. As it is a puzzle game and each puzzle is highly memorable I have a harder time recapturing that initial experience where I am trying to solve something rather than remembering how to solve it, which diminishes the replay-ability for me. The controls/snapping into position can be a bit fiddly at times and I would occasionally go around the screen after completing a puzzle picking up and putting things down because one item was a few pixels out of place. I don't like the cat levels in the DLC where the puzzle is clicking the cat. There are too many of them and it inflates the level count without adding the challenge I want out of the game. I wish we could have the Daily Tidies that are new puzzles in an archive like the other holiday puzzles, untethered to achievements. When I want to play, I don't want to play for only one 5 minute puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This little game is so very cute and the puzzles are actually sometimes difficult! My only gripe is that MANY levels have multiple possible solves, and if I want to get all of them 100% before moving onto the next one, I have to go back to the level select and select it again rather than just 'redoing' the level. It's a pain in the ass.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: There are so many things I enjoyed about this game.  The art style, the amount of levels, the music, the environmental storytelling.... It was so fantastic to play.  I thoroughly enjoyed this game so much.One of  my favourite features of this game was the "Let It Be" feature.  The way it was worded and the fact that I could.... let a puzzle be as it was and move on was so nice.  I really enjoy puzzle games, but sometimes I really struggle solving them and with the frustration I would stop playing.  This feature allowed me to continue without feeling bad for continuing to another level.I thought, for me, the difficulty levels were pretty well balanced for me.  I am very much a novice puzzle enjoyer, so I found some puzzles challenging enough, and some more easy and I enjoy that a lot.This game was such a joy to play, and I am honestly so excited to go back and play through the whole thing again!

_childDocuments_.review: I was a pretty big fan of Gungrave Overdose back in the day. I loved the Nightow-styled visuals, the ridiculous characters, the way everything would be torn apart and riddled with bullets after a firefight. The first four levels of Gungrave GORE are alright. Grave can now pull enemies to him with a hook to use as meat shields and can throw them. There are finishers now too. Otherwise, Grave plays just as he did in Overdose. But it's been 18 years and Overdose was kind of clunky for 2004. And while Overdose was 9 stages long with three different characters, GORE has 31 stages. There are two other characters, but you play as them for a single level each. Grave's basic gameplay never changes.The game is extremely repetitive and is stretched insanely thin by the time the credits roll. As far as improvements, the camera isn't glued to Grave's back and you can aim with your mouse. But pretty much everything else is worse. The game's art style is hideous, with awful character designs in generic levels. The visuals are no longer manga-style and the game just looks like it could be anything. The story is a nonsensical mess that doesn't have entertaining dialogue exchanges like Overdose did. Instead, the two characters with the worst designs have long conversations about SEED. The levels are long corridors where you do nothing but shoot things most of the time. However, there's some platforming too, which is some of the worst platforming I've ever seen. If you're like me, you'll have an okay time for most of the first five levels until you find yourself on top of the train in level 5. Here, you have to dodge and jump over signs that kill you in a couple of hits. Think back to PS2-era Gungrave and remember how rigid the movement was now imagine platforming with those controls. Platforming rears its ugly head multiple times and falling can lead to dying instantly. There are a handful of sections where you have to do something other than shoot things and they're always nothing short of atrocious. But the worst thing is the enemy placement. Enemies feel thrown into the levels without any attention paid to balance. You walk through a door and get assaulted by a ton of rockets, sniper shots, flames, and a hail of bullets from enemies positioned behind foes with shields and ones with swords that deflect bullets. The enemy rockets are much like the ones in Ninja Gaiden 2. You'll be trying to fight only to have to deal with rocket after rocket slamming into you. And the stunlocking is nuts. So many enemy attacks stun you, so forget about standing in place and using Grave's awesome shoot-out mode. You'll just get stunlocked and have to either grab someone to use as a shield or spam demolition attacks to refill your health gauge. Grave feels as brittle as glass, but he also feels weak. The hit detection on his Grave Hauler is also poor and it barely feels like it even hits enemies. Oh, and you need currency to upgrade Grave, but it stays the same in every level. You'll need more and more to upgrade Grave's parameters but the amount you get for later levels doesn't increase.The gameplay is putrid. The basic shooting is still kind of fun, but this game lasts over 10 hours and you'll practically only be using Grave's pistols. You also can't unlock the other 2 characters for play after beating the game. You play as them in their individual levels and that's it. This game was delayed for three entire years and it's amazing that this is the best Iggymob could do. I wish we had a good new Gungrave game, but this one is just an insult to the franchise. That anyone expects you to play $50 for it is madness.
_childDocuments_.name: Gungrave G.O.R.E

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game at launch via game pass. I'm a huge Gungrave fan so I couldn't miss it, but despite me beating it at launch, I had a miserable time for most of my playthrough. However, Iggymob has been on point with listening to criticisms, because nearly every gameplay complaint I had at launch has been fixed in patches. I would now go so far as to say Gungrave GORE is a good game. It's still imperfect in many ways, and the game's budget was half a bag of Doritos and a dream (and it shows), but damn if they didn't turn an awful product into a good one, which is no small feat. And it's a miracle we even got a new Gungrave to begin with (the VR games don't count, trust me). If you're into aggressively 6-7/10 PS2-era action game schlock, Gungrave GORE is well worth it on a decent sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Gungrave G.O.R.E

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for the next triple A Devil May Cry style character action game, this isn't it. If you are looking for a simpler 3rd person shooter about a dead guy carrying around a coffin shooting crackheads, you'll get some enjoyment out of this. I once heard that the original Gungrave for the PS2 was designed around the idea that a drunk salary man, after getting home from a hard day of work, could play a game without having to focus and just have a good time. In this regard I feel like Gungrave G.O.R.E stays true to that formula. It's a simple and stylish game. That's the essence of the franchise and it doesn't have to be much else to be worthwhile.

_childDocuments_.review: "Kusoge", "So bad its good" and etc, are just lame excuses that represent the insecurities of many. If something is GOOD, then it is GOOD. You don't have to fit in with the rest of the hivemind that you feel inclined to justify your lack of self-thought by feeble means. What kind of statement is even "Best 7/10 game!", like why does everything have to be with scores? Why do we even measure our enjoyment? Everyone is quick to make assumptions and judgments, for this very reason we have games like Gungrave G.O.R.E totally overshadowed by such shallow remarks. G.O.R.E is not your typical action game, many commercialize it as such, but its highly different than the likes of Devil May Cry or Bayonetta. What you have here is pure, unfiltered Arcade Shoot Em' Up that has a heavy emphasis on scoring and utilizing your tools for effective Clears. If this doesn't seem like your cup of tea, that's no biggie. Gungrave series is definitely an acquired taste and if you want to see what you're getting yourself into, at least try playing the first game on the PS2 to have a clear idea. If you liked it, then congratulations on being part of the outcasts who think this series has just as much depth as the beloved "10/10" classics.Gungrave G.O.R.E is such a breath of fresh air in the Gaming industry whilst also being archaic in its values. Everything has to be modernized to appeal to the Status Quo for the Big Men in suits, even Nostalgia-baiting people with the "Olde" by remaking classics, and totally butchering them with microtransactions. Of course, the very same hivemind does not really mind this and is ready to have you impaled on a cross if you claim the "Resident Evil 4 Remake is a massive downgrade" but that's an entire issue of its own. P.S. I've played this game from start to finish on Hard on my first run, just git gud if you're crying about the Train stage. It really is not even an issue.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the strangest recommendation I've ever made.Gungrave G.O.R.E, which I will not be properly writing out again, feels exactly like playing a weirdo small-name game in the PS2 era. There were dozens of underrated gems back then, things that by and large slipped under the radar, and many of them never got to see the light of day again. Shinobi is dead forever, I might be the only person alive who loved Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams.Gungrave was a game I never managed to track down, and then one day I woke up to see that there was a sequel. Coming to Steam, of all things! I knew I had to give it a go once I had the chance.Well.Do I recommend this game to everyone? Yes, but only because it's been ages since I saw a game with this much heart and soul poured into it. I don't think the majority of players will enjoy this game - there are clunky controls (which I find tolerable because it's just like on the PS2), some lingering jank (which gives it charm), and the sound design in particular is constantly failing the visuals. The voice acting is PS2-era bad (which I love!), the gameplay is relatively simple (I enjoy it for it, it feels extremely arcadey) but the game just oozes heart.I've never heard of this studio before, but what I can tell you with absolute certainty is that they put their hearts and souls into making this game, and it's a really solid niche title for what it is. It's jank, it's fun, it's loud, it's flashy, it's completely ridiculous. This game would also legitimately gain 2 points on a 10 point scale if it had proper sound design, like, there has to be a sound library that's within budget they could use that contains sounds for 'chainsaw' and 'big laser powering up', right?unironically the only reason I don't record a bunch of foley myself and send it to the devs with full free license to use it is that I don't have access to the equipment I used to work with anymore :(And the fact I'd be willing to put in that work otherwise should tell you everything you need to know about this game and how I feel about it. This game is great fun. I recommend it. Statistically speaking you'll probably hate it. Buy it anyway. It's delightful 2000s edge.**UPDATE AUGUST 8 2023:**Whoa, I got a response from the developers! I never expected THAT!I kind of wrote this because I wanted to recommend this to my friends so I wrote it up as an easy way to share that, I never expected the devs would see it.I want to clarify a few things in light of that.1: I really genuinely do love this game, and I do recommend at least trying it to everyone who sees this. If you think you MIGHT like this game, you almost certainly will.2: I understand game development is super hard and I don't want you to think I was ragging overly much on the sound designer - it's difficult work, I've done stuff in that field before and people underestimate how challenging it can be. I just really think it's worth the effort, because the visuals are SO GOOD by and large that the underwhelming sound accompanying it undercuts them. This game could easily thrive off being loud and stylish with some more oomph to things like the railgun sniper shot at the end, the enemy attacks, etc.Grave's guns and Bunji's guns both sound fantastic, by the way. Very well done! And I find the voice acting fun and charming, this really does bring back nostalgia for the PS2 era in the best way.I genuinely look forward to any future work you guys put out!

_childDocuments_.review: Played the hell out of this on PS4.  A truly phenomenal action game that rewards tactical engagement with the level design with an awesome chaining system, and flashy combat feats with Art Score.  If you're just playing for completion, to "experience" the game, you're going to miss the point.  It flashes the scoring and ranking systems in your face for a reason, you're supposed to play it like an arcade game.  To actually engage with the game's mechanics and be rewarded for improving as a player, rather than just have its world and story presented to you.  You know?  To have fun playing a game?  Remember that?The PC port suffers from some of the usual UE4 gremlins, which do improve after first boot, but the game looks great on PC and has a good options menu.  Not played beyond the first level but can't imagine it gets any worse (or indeed better). Frame rate is good (even with RT and no FSR on a 6900 XT), which is the important thing.  Just remember to disable the Steam overlay, which causes massive hitches whenever it pops up.  You need to focus on the game anyway :) Oh, and the game crashes on startup if it doesn't have access to the audio stream, so you can't listen to bit-perfect CD quality music while playing, which is a mild shame for all 3 of us who give a ♥♥♥♥.  The sound design is great anyway so it's worth playing with all the sliders up.If you like playing games, buy the hell out of this, especially for £9.  If you like talking about/critiquing games, and their "immersive worlds", and call anything that constitutes actual game design or mechanics "dated", I hear there's a new Assassin's Creed out.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever played the other games, you would know that the stories and voice acting weren't the best thing in the entire world. Gungrave 2002 was incredibly bare bones plot wise and Overdose's story, while better by a long shot from its predecessor, was mediocre at best. GORE is, unfortunately, no different. Its story is, at points, difficult to follow and built shallow compared to other games. These new villains feel empty and a bit boring and they aren't as interesting or memorable compared to the first and second game. The voice acting is... atrocious and hard to listen to. Playing with the radio off is basically mandatory. But despite all of these negatives, I still would implore anyone with at least an interest in the franchise to try the game. Hell, try Overdose too, or at least watch the first two games if you can't play them. These games are made with love, care and attention and I can tell the people who work on these games LOVE what they do and what they work on. ESPECIALLY on GORE. I've listened and read a lot of the director's interviews and just listening to him speak about it, I can tell this game was a stressful labor of love that went through in the end.The developers, by the way, are amazing. It seems each month they actually listen to the fanbase and their critiques and make the game better with updates that make life so much easier. It feels rare nowadays to get developers who care and listen.I fell in love with the gameplay, which is just a fun mindless shoot-em-up that took a lot of inspiration from its predecessors. This game feels like it's stuck in the 2000s but has modern upgrades, which is a big relief since departing from the basic gameplay format would betray what these games have been built upon. It's flashy and spunky and fun to keep playing over and over again. The set dressing is also really nice to see too. The details you can stumble upon, such as a shooting range during the Vietnam stages, are small but lend to a sense of life in the stages that might be empty otherwise. If you like games with a sense of charm, nostalgia and a 2000s feel, try this game because you won't regret it. If you end up liking the characters, I'd recommend you to watch the anime. Actually, no watch the anime first, the games, and THEN play GORE because this game feels like a big love letter.

_childDocuments_.review: Gungrave G.O.R.E is frustrating. Not because I didn't enjoy the game, quite the contrary, I think its the most fun game I've played all year. It is frustrating because of how much I fundamentally disagree with the common consensus while simultaneously understanding where those frustrations are coming from.I think this game is a painfully misunderstood gem that highlights an era and style of game design that we never see a lot of these days, now that every game is polished to a mirror sheen and asks so little of its players. It is precisely because of how much Gungrave G.O.R.E asks of its players that I feel the game is misunderstood. Because the game has a steep difficulty and an even steeper learning curve. But at the same time, it is the mastery of that learning curve and skill that makes the game so satisfying.Not only that, but it is a lost art to see a game that is designed solely in favor of a satisfying gameplay loop and takes a scorched earth approach to any of the bells and whistles we've all come to expect from modern action games. Gungrave G.O.R.E has no dazzling cinematic sequences or environmental storytelling. What you see is what you get, which is a solidly designed hybrid between a shooter and a character action game. And for what its worth, the designers of the game have gone through a lot of effort, both during development and after through patches, to ensure that the basic gameplay loop of shooting and maintaining high scores is as satisfying as it can be. Contrary to popular belief, the level design, enemy design and combat design is built to make those moment to moment gameplay decisions challenging and satisfying. Experienced players that can master the game's mechanics will find a rewarding experience in ways that many recent games have not been able to quite match up to. But despite my praise to the game's core design and skillfully implemented core mechanics, I cannot deny that there is a massive lack of consistency in the quality of the level-to-level, moment-to-moment design of the game. Some parts are amazing at testing your skill while simultaneously giving you a good time. Some parts just feel like they weren't play-tested in any capacity. Still, with recent patches, I see that Iggymob has done the best job they can to smooth out the rough edges of development and ensure that the player experience is as rewarding as could be. Knowing the development history of this game, I can't help but root for Iggymob at the end of the day. They made one of the most unique games released in the past year and a true love letter to this genre and era of game design, all the while struggling to set up shop in a place where its even more difficult to secure funding while at the same time working with a very niche IP. The fact that the game is as polished as it is compared to more expensive AAA releases really says something about their passion.And despite all the parts that weren't fun to play, I've still played Gungrave G.O.R.E many times over because the good of what they gave us I think far outshines the few moments where it perhaps took me more time than I'd like to in order to adapt to the more difficult and downright unfair sections.But that does come with the territory. At the end of the day, I'd rather have a game that's this satisfying on a sheer mechanical level that has a handful of frustrating levels or portions, than a game that is polished to a mirror sheen and has nothing unique to say or offer.So I leave my review with this. If everything you hear and see about Gungrave G.O.R.E sounds appalling, if you would be instantly turned off by a game with a simple and repetitive gameplay loop because it doesn't have enough variety to satisfy you, if the game's lack of budget for cinematic sequences makes you bored, and if a game with intense difficulty frustrates you; then yeah, Gungrave G.O.R.E is probably not for you. You should probably not buy the game.If you like a game full of soul however and you have a strong interest in this genre, then go ahead and give it a try. I promise that it will be quite rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: Critiquing the critique.Saying that the game is something from a bygone era or PS2-like title is just lazy and uninspired. It's not a cinematic game filled with hubs & open world. It doesn't have any extra bloat like RPG elements or collectibles sprinkled around. You don't walk around aimlessly or explore. The whole framework of the gameplay and stages rely and are based on one thing, density. Gameplay density.It's an arcade game. You play for score, not for a story. You don't get a "break from the gameplay" during the stages, you fight tooth and nail all the way through. Just like in a SHMUP. Try playing the game like a SHMUP and it will click. Engage with the beat system, chain & link your combos, move around and utilize the space, don't hide behind corners or parry, you don't need to. The game will punish you for slugging around.Move, dodge, jump, shoot, keep that flame alive and most importantly, kick their ass.

_childDocuments_.review: Gungrave G.O.R.E. is the Gungrave game we wanted but not the one we deserved.I'll divide in chapters this whole thing so you'll know what are you going to keep reading.If you've never heard of Gungrave you will probably don't like this game or, at the very least, will not understand NOTHING of this by the story perspective...because there is absolutely no story here. It tries to be there but it's a fake, lazy and useless one.This game is like...you have TONS of money and buy the bestest oil colors, the best brushes, the best canvas...but you can only paint a stickman.No mocap in the cutscenes was fine in the old days or in low detailed video environments....with this level of detail (that is really good) makes the characters akward, visibly fake and altoghether ugly.I speak from the bottom of my heart, these cutscenes makes me wanna carve out my eyes.Now, the story: There is none. It starts abruptely out of nowhere and ends up nowhere.Usually in all Grave's games we have a precise motivation of why they are waking us up, a precise goal usually with Mika at our side that points us where to shoot and we always ends up saving her somehow developing ever further the love Grave kept for his family even after death."You have to like, Mika."In this game we follow an unknown brat that seems has been infected with SEED, we will never know why, how or anything...but this won't stop her from yelling at our ears every 30 seconds. She say to follow Mika and their "group" to get rid of SEED once and for all...for the third time. Point is that if you never played the previous games (last one from 2004) or seen the original anime you probably don't know what is happening or what SEED is and THIS GAME will not tell you nothing. So if you're a new or old fan of the series, do NOT look for some new engaging story here...you will end up starving and hoping your PS2 works again...Gameplay wise...it's Gungrave. It has a couple of new gimmiks but after all these updates it's the best Gungrave game I've played. Yeah, ok there are some minor issues like Putting Executuoner's Blood as a low level low damage Demolition shot but hey...at least you can use it much more...WAY much more since it hits like a peeshoter but those are details.-------If you don't know how Gungrave games works, here is a rundown:Gungrave is a linear corridor where you start shooting at the start of the stage, point at things that go *BOOM* or *SPLAT* and you stop because the level ended or you died. Seriously, if you stop keeping the shoot button pressed for longer than 2 seconds, you're playing it wrong. Just like the original game there are no secrets in the missions, no easter eggs, nothing. You just walk and shoot for 50 seconds to 8 minutes and then press a couple of buttons to start the next stage. They added some new stategies to make harder difficulties a little more tactical like the ability to take a hostage and use it as a shield but it is still one of those games where the absolute best defence is killing the enemies before they can hit you.All in all I really like the game. I really REALLY hate with all my might the cutscenes and the "story" they tried to came up with.Gungrave G.O.R.E. IS the game all Grave's Fans wanted...but it's not what we deserved after almost 20 years of cooking from the same developers. I know they can do marvels but seems like they either bite more than they could chew or got lazy...or they couldn't find the founds to do the story properly.I do NOT regret spending 60€ on this game...damn if they put more DLCs I will buy them just for the hope they will continue and do a better job next time.

_childDocuments_.review: I won't say that others concerns and criticism about the game isn't valid.The game has it's issues, as of currently writing this at least. Who knows if there'll be a balance pass or something in future. The game certainly has some levels with very odd difficulty spikes and not due to the difficulty setting you're on. No the difficulty comes in pure enemy composition. Even on Easy it's a ridiculously tough fight in places. Like I said, hopefully we get some tuning via a patch.But I also think a lot of the negativity here is from people that don't understand what kind of game this is.It is not a Stylish Action game like Devil May Cry. No, while GORE has brought in some Stylish elements.Gungrave is a Hallway Shooter. The whole idea was you don't look for cover, YOU ARE THE COVER. You tank your way down corridors blasting everything in sight. And yes it is repetitive. That's every Gungrave game. You mow down hordes of enemies with your oversized guns and then perform badass visually striking finishers with the coffin.And GORE? Is definitely a GUNGRAVE game. People might've been expecting more, hoping even, but this is on par with Overdose. With some different pros and cons between each. But if mowing down bad guys with big hefty guns is your thing? You're gonna enjoy it.If you're looking for another DMC? You will be disappointed.For those that have heard of Gungrave and want an in? This isn't optimal but the 'recap' movie in game does pretty well cover the plot and events of the first two games. At least enough for you to jump into the game here and enjoy the Anime-Level Storyline it contains. And I mean that entirely as a compliment.For those that wanna go full bore on Gungrave? I recommend the Anime then the games in order.
