_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this review first by saying; all of you praising OverDose (especially over this game) are wearing rose-tinted glasses and you need to get off of that copium. I have played the whole series before starting this game, and OverDose was one of the most miserable times with a game I had in recent memory. Awful silence most of the time, music stolen from the anime randomly, boring plot with annoying characters and cheap presentation, terrible boss design... I could go on, but this isn't an OverDose review. Point being, replay that, and try telling me with a straight face this isn't already a vast improvement over that right away.Lastly, if you are a fan of the anime; don't expect the game to be similar to that. Especially if you haven't played the first Gungrave either. It... Goes places. I love the anime, we all love the anime, believe me I know the devs do because you get one of the coolest unlockables ever if you beat the game on GORE difficulty; but the game series and the anime series have different priorities, so just bear that in mind.Now, onto the game itself. Well suffice to say that after reading most of the negative reviews I can only say that either they played on Hard and got immediately filtered (more on that later) or they're just immensely misunderstanding the type of game that this is, both newcomers and previous fans alike.About that Hard bit,  It feels to me like that's what the devs intended, as Hard can definitely bust your balls, especially with an unupgraded Grave. While I appreciate the choice of letting you choose it right from the get-go, I think the devs could've saved themselves a whole lot of flack by making you have to unlock  Hard instead. I do understand they've patched the game over the course of my playthrough to make certain bits easier, but I personally found Normal difficulty to be a good sweetspot of progression regardless, as the game can have a steep difficulty and learning curve. Salaryman-core like the first Gungrave, this is not.No, instead the game chooses to add a whole lot of depth by introducing new enemy types to the Gungrave formula (and fixing the ones imported from OverDose that sucked major bull manure) as well as expanding Grave's moveset by giving him new tools like the STORM BARRAGE, being able to take human shields, and much more as well as tweaking existing ones like improving Demolition Shot selection, variety and choice as well as making them regain your health; creating a satisfying loop of building Beat to earn demo-shots and using those to regain any health lost or clear a screen of enemies. I think saying "this is a character-action shooter" is overselling it a bit, but it is the spirit that the game is going for.While the story isn't anything to write home about--- The best part is, unlike OverDose, it simply doesn't get in the way. Whether you want to go full-hog marathon or just need a quick burst of action, it is very uninterrupted action in GORE and thus it remains addictive and well-paced. Stages don't overstay their welcome, with a nice length, and you get about 30 of them leading to a total playtime of 10 hours or so assuming you don't want to dig deeper. And while most stages are roughly "the same", you do get about 2 or three that try to do something different or change things up to keep your attention.As for PC-specific related stuff. I played this on a GTX1080, 16GB of DDR4 RAM, and an i7-7700k with the settings I had access to maxed out, and you do get some wiggle room with the game's settings, as well as playing with FSR enabled and set to "Ultra-Quality" mode. First few stages played on 16:9 1080p resolution, and the rest on 21:9 3440x1440 ultrawide resolution thanks to  And I encountered no performance issues during my playthrough, not even any shader compilation stutter or anything like that. You get options to rebind keys or any button on a controller, and the game supports simultaneous input.I can't speak about how exactly the game by default controls on Mouse and Keyboard as I played this game with controller (for the sake of consistency with my playthroughs of the older titles), but as I mentioned before, everything is rebindable so you should be at home whatever your chosen input method. And because the game supports simultaneous input, that means you can really go wild with any custom Steam Input configurations you might want to make. Flick stick, gyro mouse aiming, anything is possible.However, that said, I know a lot of people have been having trouble playing this with RTX cards due to what I assume bugged raytracing settings that enable/disable themselves, people being unable to play it on Deck, encountering other performance issues... Your mileage may vary, even with top of the line hardware.And I cannot deny that the game DOEs have its jank, whether you will find it amusing and a heartwarning throwback to the flourishing days of PS2 middleware or downright annoying or unsightly is up to you, but there is a varying degree of quality in the levels, both visually and mechanically. For example, the jump between beautifully pre-rendered CG cutscenes, to "fine" in-engine cinematics and cutscenes. Or playing sections of the game that are tightly designed (as much as they can be for this type of game) and then going to sections that felt like they weren't playtested with how unfair they can be.But I can't fault the developers too much. Motion capture is expensive, playtesting and QA is expensive, and at the end of the day this is a Gungrave title decades after the last one by a smaller studio; I know it sounds like an excuse, but there's a difference between that and just being aware of the context in which something was made in.It is simply a fun game to play, a game which you can get what you put in. If you're someone that enjoys seeking high scores and mastering a game's mechanics then this is definitely a game for you; but don't go into it expecting a gripping story or Capcom levels of polish. Me? I knew I was hooked when I actually cared about dropping my Beat score.But still, I wholeheartedly recommend it, and root for Iggymob's success. You can play it on gamepass for just a few dollars, or pick it up on sale if you're truly undecided. The game is a loveletter to the days of simpler game design, focusing solely satisfying gameplay loops and pushing for the player to dig deep and get progressively more skilled at the game. A game where just surviving is simple, but where you must be one with the character and the stage to chase those desired high scores and rankings.Plus, the devs have been very supportive and open to player feedback, actively patch and make adjustments in response to player feedback unlike most AAA devs, and their passion for the game and the series can be felt with all its moments of quality that shine through the jank. There's simply no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, no FOMO or scummy practices, no forced wallking segments, no narrative parroting and interrupting gameplay, nothing superflous and unneeded for just playin' and havin' a good time...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like that one friend who tries to be everything at once but ends up being hilarious for all the wrong reasons. Is an over-the-top, action-packed ride with a plot that's as coherent as a squirrel on an espresso binge.But here's the catch: Gungrave Gore is so ridiculously over-the-top that it becomes strangely endearing. It's like that cheesy '80s action movie that you can't help but enjoy because it's so bad, it's good. The gameplay is an insane ballet of bullets and explosions that'll make you feel like a one-man army on a sugar rush.So, is Gungrave Gore a masterpiece? Absolutely not. But is it a hilarious rollercoaster of mayhem and madness? You bet! If you're up for some mindless fun and a good laugh at the expense of its absurdity, this game might just be my guilty pleasure. Just don't expect any deep plot or character development - this one's all about the laughs and the carnage.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm past the 4 hr mark on this game, and I want to like it, but it makes it hard. Visually, there are some nicely rendered environments, and Grave himself looks great, but there is a randomness to all the enemies that feels like they were generic assets thrown into the game.  The cut scenes have parts that are cool, and then lots and lots of parts that suck, and that make no sense at all.  The story/dialogue in this game is probably some of the worst I've seen this year. The enemies say " ♥♥♥♥ you" "♥♥♥♥ off" "Get outta here" way too many times, it becomes grating to encounter enemies who are going to ramble random curses and nonsense.  Almost none of the cut scenes make sense, and it could have been written by a poor ai or words on dice. The concept is good, I have fond memories of the PS2 game with Grave, and some of the time the gunplay is fun. Unfortunately its almost 50/50 when its not fun. There are issues with hot detection when meleeing that is brutal, you can be trying to slam a giant coffin into a guy and get no detection for a long time before it kicks in.  Again, it feels like its thrown together in these moments as well. I got to mission 22/31, and I just don't want to finish it.  I still have fond memories of the PS2 version, but I can never see this character again now and be fine.

_childDocuments_.review: My playtime is mostly from the PS4 version and I recently bought it again on PC which is why my playtime is so low as of writing this.I was holding off on reviewing this game until they released all the Switch exclusive content on PC which as of now, they have just stealth dropped it all with new character DLCs at an affordable price.Now, this game is probably my favourite release from 2022, I am a big fan of the first two games and the anime adaptation. The combat is enjoyable and the game oozes with style. A lot of reviews against the combat or calling the game repetitive are very disingenuous as it is clear they did not explore the combat and systems in place (only 6% of the players have the achievement for using the Storm Barrage ability 500 times) which is one of the main bread and butter tools to use in the game to charge up your demolition shots. _childDocuments_.review: The gave devs clearly love Gungrave. You can tell they put a lot of heart into the game. His outfit reminds me of the first Gungrave and the pre-order bonus lets you play as Overdose Gungrave so I can deeply appreciate the love they have for Brandon Heat and the Gungrave franchise.The game looks beautiful. It's great to see Grave in modern gaming graphics. The core Gungrave (GG) mechanics are there from Overdose. Health, Shields, Coffin, Cerberus, Beats, Demolition shots, and even his bullet dance. They made it so you can upgrade Grave which I really appreciated. The only upgrades you could get from Overdose was new demolition shots so this feels much better to get overpowered. I see a lot of people complaining it's just "Shoot, melee, repeat" but I think those people never played GG before if that's your takeaway. Since both previous GG games were basically the same thing. It's just mindless fun.The devs definitely wanted to bombard you with mobs tho. You can get overran with enemies to the point where you're stuck in one spot surrounded by mobs. You can't just stand still and spam the melee button either like in Overdose. So I often got stuck surrounded by enemies to the point that I died. I hate BS deaths like that. The most notorious level so far was the train level and anyone who's played it will know that is the most BS level ever. Don't give players a time limit to traverse a train but then spam landmines and armored enemies that spam rockets and melees. Grave staggers way too much. Even with full shields you can get interrupted mid melee combo by a shielded enemy which is ridiculous. Shotgun mobs stagger Grave with every shot and it's infuriating. You basically can get stun locked A LOT. Conclusion: The game has a lot of heart into it. The devs clearly loved Gungrave and I can appreciate their dedication to reviving the game from the grave. There's a lot of game mechanics that would make the average player rage quit, but as someone who's played Overdose I can tell you this isn't new to the GG games. The final levels of Overdose made you want to quit the game at every death. I haven't beaten G.O.R.E. yet but I'm sure it'll make me want to quit many times before I've finished it. If you love Gungrave and you want to play a mindless shooting game pick this game up. If you rage easily then don't play it. TLDR; 4/10Edit: The Quartz level is hands down the worst level in this entire game. By far. This is some of the worst platforming I've ever experienced and playing as Quartz is absolutely infuriating. Bunji was fun to play as but this is ridiculous.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually reserve my reviews for when I complete the game, but seeing how I have essentially seen everything this game might have to offer after almost 5 hours of play, I think I can say that Gungrave G.O.R.E is just dumb fun. Admittedly I haven't played the previous games in the series, but I have seen the anime adaption of the first entry which I do recommend for people that are looking for a loose but faithful adaption of the source. To put it bluntly, this game has you playing as the most badass but edgy anime protagonist ever created, Beyond the Grave is his name and mulching goose-stepping punks is his game. Armed with his pistols, Cerberus, and lugging his coffin the Death Hauler, Grave is equal parts Desperado and Frankenstein, which is the highest honor you could give to a man like him. Throughout my almost 5 hours, the objective was simple. Kill everything or in this game's own words “Kick their Ass" which you will probably do with absolute glee. There is a story here but don't expect it to be some groundbreaking story with a moral lesson to learn, it's simple set dressing for Grave to kill thugs in droves and honestly that's all you really need. This game does feel dated and a little shoe string, but from what I've read that's always been the case for this series and if you can turn your brain off for a few hours I think you will find yourself having a lot of fun. The best description I can give is it's a hot brass ballet of bullets and carnage where the bad guys are locked in the room with you, not the other way around.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is jank, unpolished and just downright sloppy. It's also some of the most fun I've ever had with a video game.The story is... honestly not good and not what any of us are here for. If you aren't aware, this is the third game in the series. So it's gonna feel a odd, and honestly if you have played the original and Overdose you still would end up lost.One of the major step downs this game has from it's predecessors is art style. Yasahiro Nightow did the original character designs for Gungrave, but sadly few of those characters return. Grave, our main character, has a stellar model in game however.What really sells this game is the raw moment to moment gameplay. It's a spectacle fighter shoot em up. You are rewarded and expected to keep up a combo of shots to enemies with your pistols. Learning to start your gun katas or "burst mode" is honestly the biggest hurdle I had with the controls. This won't be Devil May Cry or Bayonetta, expect something more in line with the beautiful simplicity of Gunstar Super Heroes for the GBA. There is just the right amount of enemies and variations of them that combat remains engaging. You can keep up your combo by destroying objects in the environment.Sadly, the game has some issues with it's progression system. Your health, damage, shield and "demolition shot capacity" are all bought with points at the end of missions, but frankly speaking health should of been rewarded for points in the campaign... and most of this. Points can also be used to by Demolition Shots, super moves essentially. This should of been the main use of points, as well as some other abilities that augment your gun katas.It's short, and some of the levels can be kind of samey, but the actual encounters are pretty well thought out. The biggest issue with levels, especially the later ones (in fact mostly the later ones) is certain gaps that force you to drop your combos. Yes, levels are one big combat. it's great.I got this on sale and I'm glad I did because 80 CAD is a bit high for how short it was, but the studio is super small so at least I can rationalise it as "they need the cash". It's well worth your time if you try and engage it on it's level.Side note I have to dock this one points for the Vietnam Caves level where you control Quartz, iggymob I'm sorry I loved your game but please don't feature a playable character designed for the opposite of what your entire foundation is built on.

_childDocuments_.review: It may be a little rough around the edges but Gungrave G.O.R.E. definitely has a soul.Solid combat and mechanics, decent presentation with a kickass soundtrack and great action cutscenes (the pre-rendered ones). Ofc the game is not perfect and there are some issues with level design here and there, questionable balancing in some encounters and poor audio mixing that hinders the overall presentation.But I can't deny that learning how to chain combo an entire level ends up being super satisfying, there's an Arcade-like roots here that really makes it enjoyable if you're into that kind of stuff, you know, trying to figure out how mechanics works and actually engage with the game to beat your own high score.The gameplay loop is pretty much perfect, I can't stress enough how much fun it feels to chain combo everything on the screen while looking out for rockets to parry, stunned enemies to heal yourself, where to dodge, when to melee and when to retaliate with your arsenal of badass supers. Great game to play when everything clicks as intended, there's a solid foundation here that is held back at times by poor design choices, anyways I still feel like it's underrated as ♥♥♥♥, an instant cult classic in my book, it's a breath of fresh air from all the modern AAA open world cinematic copy and paste games of late.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on an anime based off a videogame IP, blast your way through 30-odd linear corridors, killing waves of drugged mafia henchmen, or mutant victims of experiments with the alien-derived drug, SEED. The game is a character-action title  that's mostly about shooting. Think Devil May Cry 2. Shoot goons, build up your meter for special attacks, dodge-roll away with guns akimbo (a la Max Payne), then shoot some more. Full disclaimer: I picked up the game with a very good discount. I do not think the game is worth the base asking price. There's 3 base game difficulties, and getting through the story on Normal took about 10 hours. Playing through each difficulty unlocks better guns (so you should play on Easy, to get guns that make Normal easier, etc). The game's story has some nice CGI cutscenes, which are incredibly anime, but it's fitting. There's a lot of upgrades to unlock (how much currency yu get is based on your rank at the end of each level, so it's possible to grind a bunch. I wouldn't say it's tedious, but... there's  not a lot of variety, as you move through neon-lit city streets, caves, or labs, smashing up stuff and trying to keep the combo meter high. There's a bunch of bosses, which are either giant mutants with AOE attacks to dodge, or humanoids with weird powers—where a bunch of dodging is also required. If you can get this game on a good sale (or play on GamePass)- it's got a high-production CGI story, an okay combat loop, and killing waves of mooks could be cathartic. But looking for depth, or elaborate game mechanics-- that's not really the place for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Full review having beaten the game:This game is very bad and is absolutely not worth $50. Many are saying this is a "cool PS2 throwback" but this would be shockingly bad for a Simple 2000 game... they called them that because they cost 2000 yen. Breaking down the problems into two categories:Bad basic gameplay. Frequently the game will just drop your input when you want to cancel from standing/walking shooting into dodge or melee. Difficult to use the charge shot. No way to tell where exactly you're going with the chain pull. Dodge feels too slow and short to avoid almost any attack in the game (or enemies track too quickly). The basic campaign is 8 hours longer than it has any right to be and no "extra modes." Extra characters barely exist and really shouldn't be in the game at all for as barebones as they are. Melee "combo" almost completely worthless because it doesn't reflect missiles, constantly getting staggered out of it, and it doesn't even kill the tanky endgame enemies.Bad level design. Poorly made encounters--almost no "normal" enemies and massive overuse of "special" enemies who do their special attack way too rapidly. Very rarely are the levels built with inanimate objects to shoot to extend your beat combo and often they have unshootable objects you can't identify at a glance. Too many empty monster closets that look like they might be the way to go, if you're not watching the objective marker. Unbelievably poor setpieces--anything involving jumping. Instant kill laser corridor. The whole train level.Just a lot of interlocking fundamental problems means it would be a LOT of work to make this game worth playing.edit: several issues apparently patched, to a satisfactory extent or not i cannot say. caveat emptor

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving it a thumbs up, but I wish I could leave a mixed score since I CANNOT recommend the game to most of the players.Don't expect a flashy DMC type hack n slash here, because Gungrave G.O.R.E. is a slow, methodical action shoot em up that panders to the fantasy of being 90's nigh indestructible gunsliger, think Desperado or Trigun.The game lacks serious polish, in-level cutscenes are half-assed (unlike the very few amazing cinematics) and half of the stuff in-game looks like stock assets, nothing compared to OG Gungrave (2002) game. But it's worth mentioning that the small studio tasked to make this game has been working overtime after game's premiere, carefully listening to player feedback to patch out bugs, smoothen player experience, and adding free bonus content - making the game MILES more enjoyable than it was on release. It shouldn't have been released in such sorry state to begin with, but nonetheless, kudos to Iggymob for doing their best.Gameplay? You stroll through levels gunning down EVERYTHING, shooting enemies and environment keeps your combo ("Beats") up. More Beats means you gain more Demolition Shots, special points you can spend on either Rage Mode for massive damage and stagger immunity buff (aggressive) or one of four `big panic button` type abilities that stylishly damage enemies and heal you up (defensive).To survive, you keep an eye on a blue bar, your regenerating shield. If it's down, incoming damage reduces health. To keep your shield up, keep your distance and position well to avoid being flanked and cornered, and use your hook on minor enemies to use em as a meat shield (with hook you also can pull yourself INTO enemies for a neat movement option). But keep in mind it can only hit enemies on horizontal axis, never an inch higher or lower. Weakened enemies are also open to execution which recovers a portion of your shield.While shooting ♥♥♥♥ up, always look for enemies that shoot rockets or throw explosives or snipe from afar, they're your high priority targets. Luckily, you can deflect rockets with your coffin swing which also doubles as your self-defense option when you're being jumped by melee enemies.There's Lab where you can spend points to purchase Demolition Shot Executions, skills, and upgrade stats. I personally detest the percent ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ because it takes too long investing in them to notice the changes later on. Also the prices are too high, credit gained from level is too low, and there are too many options for player to choose from (I recommend to follow a guide for it). Luckily you can reset credits and purchase desired stuff again between levels.There's a soul in this game that's being strongly held back by game's overall quality, and I hope Iggymob continues to improve on Gungrave G.O.R.E. so I can no longer be ashamed of enjoying it. I got mesmerised by the charm of the original from 2002, and I hope we could go back to that theme and atmosphere some day.

_childDocuments_.review: Gungrave G.O.R.E is the third main game in the Gungrave franchise created by Yasuhiro Nightow and Japanese developers Red Entertainment, and a long-awaited return after an 18 year hiatus.  Niche though this series is, it garnered a cult following, both due to how unapologetic the first two games were with their over-the-top stress-reliever design, and how fantastic the anime adaptation was purely on its own merits. So you can imagine my excitement that something as niche as Gungrave would be returning in glorious fashion. Despite the game being announced far too early (over 5 years ago), and my apprehension about the creative leads handing development over to overseas studio Iggymob (who might I add, created the terrible VR games), I liked what I'd seen so far, and was willing to meet the developers half-way, come November 22nd. And for better or worse, this is undoubtedly a Gungrave game. Gungrave G.O.R.E sees the return of Beyond the Grave, an undead hitman who lives to protect his only family; Mika, and eradicate the evil drug SEED and those who distribute it. This time, his enemy is the Raven Clan of Asia. The story has a decent premise to work with, and enough returning characters to bring a smile to any Gungrave fan's face, but where it falters is its presentation and lack of any true fanfair. Comparing this game to the anime would be unfair, so I'll instead compare it to Overdose, which despite its limited hardware and lower budget, managed to work around its limitations and allow its characters enough breathing room to grow and develop over the course of the story. With the exception of the pre-rendered cinematics, this game's cutscenes look awkward as hell. I would've been fine with the change in art direction from its more cell-shaded anime origins to this grittier, more realistic approach, if the developers made the necessary consessions for characters to properly express themselves and emote during cutscenes, but they don't. The animation during these cutscenes also have the impact of a limp ♥♥♥♥ on a chopping board, which, coupled with the lack of the main theme to accentuate these scenes, makes the boss-executions so devoid of catharsis or oomph. Doesn't help that the voice acting ranges from passable to bad. Grave, Bunji, Quartz, Big Wushen and Ganpo sound fine, but everyone else forgot to, y'know, ACT. Overdose's English voice acting wasn't perfect, but the quality standard was noticably higher, and they bothered to hire professionals like Quinton Flynn and Robert Atkin Downs.Moving onto the gameplay, while it has its fair share of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ moments and poorly-considered design choices, the core combat is the best it's ever been, and a genuine step forward from Overdose's improvements to the first game. Grave has more moves than before, and while he's still a slow, heavy powerhouse, he no longer moves like a tank thanks to full analogue movement and modernised third-person controls. All the moves you've come to expect are present and accounted for (shooting, more shooting, deflecting missiles with a swing of the coffin, and special Demolition Shot attack after gaining enough beats on an enemy, but now he can use one of four different Demolition Shots assigned to the face buttons, use his coffin to grapple enemies and use them as a meatshield while his own Shield system recovers, destroy shields with either a charge shot or one of three melee combos, and RIP execution attacks that recover Grave's shield in a similar fashion to Glory Kills from the modern DOOM games. Enemies tend to be thrown at the player strategically, so as to get them acclimated to G.O.R.E's mechanics and controls, and despite how typically-button mashy this game is, these mechanics manage to keep the game engaging, and make overcoming most of its challenges rewarding. Grave's moveset, stats and various Demolition Shots can be upgraded in a similar fashion to Devil May Cry, where the currency earned depending on how high your end-level rank is can be redeemed to strengthen the protagonist. Gungrave games encourage the player to keep their combo (Beats) going by constantly shooting enemies and destroying obstacles along their war path before it ends, which not only fills your Demolition Shots, but will help improve your end-of-level rank. My only issue with this is that some obstacles seem obviously-breakable, yet aren't, which is very deceptive. There's no universal tell. While the game's complexity and skill ceiling aren't comparable to character-action games like Devil May Cry and Bayonetta, this extra effort goes a long way in turning Gungrave from a simple button-masher to an action game with mechanics that can carry the experience for a longer duration than that of the past two games. It's a welcome evolution of the franchise, and Iggymob deserve credit for achieving this. Where the gameplay falters, however, is in portions of the level design, bossfights, other playable characters, and inconsistency. While levels do play to the game's strengths as an arcadey shooter, you'll eventually encounter some frustrating, poorly-considered segments with instant-deaths, such as the moving-train with no room for dodging or manoeuvring and little time to get to where you need to go, awful platforming segments that clearly weren't designed with Grave's (or Quartz') general movement in mind, and a series of laser obstacles that bring the action to a screeching halt. Bossfights are a mixed bag. While some of them do test the player on what they've learned so far, more often than not they lack in polish. They tend to serve as a trap for anyone who hasn't upgraded their bullet damage (which defeats the point in having options for what the player upgrades), and will inevitably pull some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ moves on the player after their health is low enough. The first boss of the game can be disabled based on the parts of its body you target, and the Zell bossfight makes good use of the human-shield mechanic as you use his soldiers to withstand the hales of bullets. So it's a shame that the other bossfights are either standard affair, really clunky in their execution and frustrating at times, or in the final boss's case, downright easy. And lastly, there are the other playable characters; Bunji Kugashira and Quartz. The game primarily focuses on Grave, unlike Overdose with its three playable characters from the start, so Gore's supporting cast don't get anywhere near as fleshed out. Bunji is a character any returning fan will be excited to finally play as, though in execution, he's passable at best. He's supposed to be a faster, more nimble answer to Grave, with two Demolition Shots based on his affinity with wolves. His dodge-while-firing feels clunky and unreliable, so I ended up just playing him in the most boring, safest way possible. Quartz was even worse. She's comparable to Juji in that her attacks are very melee-focused, but where she differs from Juji is in how fun she is to control and how satisfying her melee attack are; which is to say not at all. Melee attacks have ridiculously short range and rarely feel like they're connecting with an enemy, so instead of feeling like a badass hack'n'slash hero, you feel more like a character from a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ movie tie-in game. Very disappointing compared to what we got 18 years ago. Overall, Gungrave G.O.R.E is far from perfect, and in need of more polish, but its pros outweigh the cons just enough that I can comfortably call it a 7/10 game, with my own personal enjoyment fluctuating between 5 and 8. It shows growth and improvement in most areas that matter, while sorely lacking in areas it probably shouldn't. I hope we can see Iggymob or whoever else Red and Nightow choose to develop the next game learn from their mistakes with G.O.R.E, while carrying over every idea they successfully executed. While it's a tough sell to anyone unfamiliar with this franchise, I can recommend it to returning fans who know what to expect.

_childDocuments_.review: The first time I tried this game on Game Pass I really hated it. Got it in a cheap bundle again for Steam and apparently they really put some effort into fixing the shortcomings of the game. It plays and feels much better now and I had a good time reliving the simple PS2 times with Gungrave G.O.R.E. - they just don’t make many games like this these days. So what is Gungrave G.O.R.E.? It is basically Dynasty Warriors but with a gunslinging Anime protagonist. You walk through linear levels and mow down hordes of enemies without much effort. While some of the later stages and bosses can offer a little challenge the game is more on the easy side, fully playing into the power fantasy. There is a rating system which can be pretty tough. To get an S-Rank in each of the 31 levels you really need to understand the combo systems and level structures. For just enjoying the action and the story the rating system isn’t important though. Besides the main character Grave his brother Bunji can be unlocked half-way into the campaign and all levels can be replayed with that character. Each of the characters comes with his own set of special moves that can be unlocked by grinding experience points. So besides the rather short playtime of six hours to beat the campaign once, there is a good amount of replay value. The graphics are rather good for a lower budget game. The same goes for the heavy metal soundtrack. There are also some CGI cutscenes that look legit amazing. Besides some minor loading stutters I didn’t have any technical issues with the game. Overall a clear recommendation for everyone looking for some good old Japanese 3D arcade action.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very fun and well-made. I like the addition of extra coffin combos but find myself missing the ability to plant the coffin into the ground as a shield from OD. I have only encountered one game-play bug that forced me to reset to a checkpoint when I tried to do a special kill on someone as they died. Overall it's been a great walk of nostalgia and I am sure I will play it many more times after getting the last 3 achievements. It is a great game to just turn off your mind and kill large amounts of dudes. I hope to see another entry to finish the story! Great job Iggymob!

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I can honestly tell that there was genuine heart and effort put into this game, as well as an honest attention to the original source material that it is based off of.However, this game is simply far too padded with bloaty levels, an exhausting amount of enemies (with little variation to them) and just gets to be far too repetitive. 31 levels in a hack and slash is just too many. And while the game itself is pretty short and most of the levels can be completed in about 10 mins each, by the time you get to level 24 or 25 you kind of get exhausted of the same mechanics over and over.But, there are still brief flashes of greatness in this game. For one, the late game bosses are immensely better than the early game ones. Also, being given the ability to play as other characters in levels that have different playstyles was a breath of fresh air as well too. The CGI cutscenes are really well done, the soundtrack is really good, and this game DOES do a really good job at being a modern take of an edgy PS2 hack and slash.Was this game worth $50 on release? No. But at common sale prices of $9.99 or less, I'd say go ahead and grab it and enjoy it for the mindless callback to PS2 era hack and slashes that it is. All in all, this is a solid first attempt for being Studio IGGYMOB's first game.

_childDocuments_.review: In 2023, when talking about hyper-action games you tend to think of titles like DMC, Bayonetta, Yakuza, Ninja Gaiden. Anything but Gungrave. And so this game feels tailored for weird little people like me. People who crave nothing more but the clunky jank of old Japanese action games for the PS2/Xbox. This is Gungrave Gore. And because of it, I'm slightly conflicted. On one hand, this game feels nostalgic, all in the right spots. Like that feeling when you play a game and you just remember playing games exactly like that as a kid. This game feels like it came out in 2005 which is both a good and bad thing. Good for how there are no restrictions for it, it's jank but it's got soul. It has its fair share of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that makes you want to punch your wall but at the same time I couldn't stop playing it. It's ♥♥♥♥ but I love it. After playing this game all the way through I got everything I wanted in a Gungrave sequel. Let alone an action game. For that, I recommend this game to anyone like me who wants to play another Gungrave game. However, if you're looking just to try this out, I'd wait until this game goes on sale or if you have the Game Pass to give it a try there. Again, this game isn't for everyone. It has massive issues with gameplay. But that's just it, this is a Japanese AA game, not AAA action game. Don't expect DMC5 levels of polish. You'll be disappointed. For me though, I loved every second of this.*side note: if there is another game down the line, the ability to change Demolition shots mid-mission by cycling through a weapon wheel with it slowing or pausing the game when you go for a change, or by cycling through them in the pause menu like the original game would be the best change ever and would literally make this game 10x better. There's so many Demolition shots in this game that being restricted to only 4 per mission with no way to change them except after the mission feels like a hindrance to this game's potential

_childDocuments_.review: A very mixed bag of a game as someone who quite enjoyed the original 2. Tried this game at launch and gave up after the second area/chapter thought it was really disappointing and bad.  Saw a video saying it was better and they were patching it with lots of fixes, so decided to give it another shot. Now I would say it's pretty good, with a lot of issues though.It's a very one note, repetitive game that should have been like half as long. Too many stages fighting the same enemies, in very similar locations just to pad the runtime. The first Gungrave was around an hour long, the second around 2. They were like arcade games, and knew not to overstay their welcome.Also presentation is poor. Looks very generic UE4 (the added cel-shade filter makes it look worse), audio mix is weird with some sound effects way too quiet or missing, music is generic and forgettable. Story is also bad and poorly told, with weirdly paced cut-scenes and bad English VO. Also really bad shader compilation stutter here on PC.All that being said the base gameplay is good fun in short bursts, especially since they've altered some of the more frustrating parts and gave auto fire mode which is crazy that it wasn't in there from the start.Hopefully they can keep improving and bring the content from the switch version over once that releases.

_childDocuments_.review: G.O.R.E keeps and refines the satisfying Gungrave gameplay loop of shooting, exploding and killing everything while keeping the BEAT counter high and getting big ART scores with flashy Demolition Shots nicely as you go through multiple stages [31 to be exact] in various locations with a couple stages played as different characters like the melee focused newbie Quartz  and fan favorite Bunji the Wolf who just keeps conveniently reviving now.One thing G.O.R.E does change a lot from the earlier PS2 games is the overall style from timeless cel shaded look to a generic but passable Korean Unreal Engine graphics and music from funky/jazzy to metal and pretty good electronic with a couple original jazz tracks still being in.Story is pretty much a nothingburger like other Gungraves. A lot of earlier reviews are now outdated since Iggymob has given this game a surprising amount of post-launch love, for example they've made the game much easier by removing all platforming sections, made autofire a toggle, they added Bunji as a full character for all stages with his own demolition shots and made charge shots somewhat useful now.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely disappointed as a Gungrave fan. The graphics removed the charm and style of the original (even the cel shaded mode which I assume was added later doesn't make it any better and would have only been good if they designed the game with cel shading from the start), the music is abysmal (it really sounds generic in comparison to the older games that had a nice western/jazz/blues theme to it), and the gameplay is so clunky that it's a joke. I played it on hard and set my guns to auto and cleared the first stage with no effort that it was just boring and the only death I got was from the boss being cheap by boxing me into a corner that I couldn't jump/dodge my way out of afterwards. The demolition shots are so whack too and aren't as cool as the original. Once I shot that rocket there was little to no fanfare to it tbh it just felt like the equivalent to a charged shot with no flare to it. The execution style finishers for stunned enemies also felt really janky and weren't satisfying either. The grapple from afar is cool, but then afterwards you can't auto your gun anymore so I just ignored it. The coffin melee was so bad and slow that I often times didn't bother reflecting rockets and just auto-attacked them to death and moved along.After clearing that first stage I just immediately closed the game to write this review and shelve this game. I'll just stick to playing the originals because nothing about the original Gungrave made it to this game except for the name and the main character.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic and fun game, and a bit of a breath of fresh air after the last few I've played through!  The game picks up on the story from the previous Gungrave games (Gungrave, Overdose, VR, and VR:UN) as you continue to halt efforts to spread the drug SEED across the globe.  As a long time fan of the series I was looking forward to it and was elated with what was delivered.Gameplay: 9/10The gameplay is exactly as it is in the previous games, and allows you to jump right in and, as it says at the start of every stage, Kick Their Ass.  The controls are responsive and intuitive and the Demolition Shots provide varying ways to enact carnage upon your foes.  The dodging and jumping can be a bit dodgy at times, but there's only one 'jumping puzzle' in the game and it can be solved through direct application of force (killing enough enemies).  The only time it really even became an issue for me was on the hardest difficulty where some of the collision physics got me stuck on the terrain and caused a death, and even then that was a rarity.  The oft-maligned train level (Mission 5) isn't as bad as it's made out to be, especially since the last group of enemies can be dodged past with little difficulty.  There's a huge amount of things to unlock (You do have to complete the game on every difficulty to unlock all the various costume/weapon options) that make going back through and replaying on a higher difficulty much easier.  You also have the option of refunding your upgrades to spread them around if you wind up buying something that isn't working out, which was a wonderful touch.  You will get enough to upgrade everything as you play through the game, though you may have to play through 2 times if you don't grind it out in early missions.Story: 8/10The story is straightforward and could be seen as 'take it or leave it' on some level.  Your goal is to wipe out the people spreading SEED and take on the Raven Clan and eliminate their bosses.  It is more of a backdrop to the continuing carnage across various locations, and honestly that's what I signed up for.  The English voice acting is a bit cheesy and drawn out at times to match the Japanese language animations, but this was a quaint throwback for me and made me more nostalgic.  I will admit that this could be an issue for some because it is a bit jarring at some points, but I'm also aware that it's a second language for the developers so it's important to remember that too!Graphics: 8/10The graphics are beautiful and there's even an option to turn on Cel-Shading (as of the recent patch) to make it a more classic experience.  I'm not sure if it was my computer but sometimes textures did fail to load but as most of the time I was more focused on taking out enemies I didn't notice it all that much.  What stood out most to me was the wide variety of locations that span across a wide variety of locations around Asia, each with their own distinct look and feel to them.  It really makes you feel like you're traversing and taking out a far-reaching criminal syndicate in addition to having more game to actually play through!Sound: 10/10The soundtrack is one of the best parts of the game, there are tracks specific to each different location in game and they're responsive to entering and exiting combat.  The tone matches the wide variety of locations and makes each area feel distinct, which is an impressive feat combined with the lengthier game.Overall: 9/10This was a really fun game to play through and the huge variety of unlocks and upgrades made it worth it to play through the various difficulties to get all of the perks.  It definitely has some more 'retro' style gameplay but it delivers it with over the top action and aplomb.  For mindless action and egregious violence against an unrepentant crime syndicate look no further.  Get out there and Kick Their Ass!

_childDocuments_.review: So, full disclosure? I've never played a Gungrave game before GORE, therefore I have no real frame of reference to compare the quality of this title against the two PlayStation 2 entries. I did however, watch the 2003 anime series and had fond enough memories of that to give this game a shot. A modern day throwback to the aughts sounded like it could be a good time!Unfortunately, what I found is that Gungrave GORE is just a really shallow, undercooked game, that really does not have enough interesting ideas to justify its ten hour campaign. What you do during the opening stages is exactly what you'll do for the entire game, walking through rooms, shooting everyone inside and then walking into a new room to do it again. The game plays it safe, and because it does, all of its levels become forgettable, just a new backdrop for you to mash the right trigger in.On the other hand, considering the original design of the train stage and the cave container jumping section, maybe it was for the best that these developers decided to keep it simple. The game desperately needed variety, but it had to be done right. The inclusion of extra playable characters is a step in the right direction, but they are very underused.Even if the stages themselves were boring, that could've been forgiven if the combat itself were good enough to take your mind off of it (See, Devil May Cry V). Sadly Gungrave GORE doesn't make the grade here either. Grave's toolset just doesn't lend itself well to player expression, and the beats system forces the player to engage the game in one correct way if they want a chance of earning the coveted S rank. You have to play perfectly; dropping your beat combo means that you may as well just restart the stage from the beginning if you want to maximize your score.Well okay. The stages are boring and there's not much room for improvisation in the combat. That can be forgiven as long as the game's story is good enough to incentivize you to keep going. So how is the game's story?... It's a waste of time. Video game stories don't need to be high art, but this story in particular felt completely unneccessary. At no point was I invested in anything that was happening, or anything what's-her-face talked about on the comms. There were no characters, just cardboard cutouts doing the bare minimum to usher your onto the next round of mashing the right trigger. The voice acting is dreadful too, not even bad enough to be ironically endearing. Just, boringly bad.So Gungrave GORE is a game with boring levels, restrictive combat and a worthless plot with bad voice acting. Oh yeah, it's also a janktacular mess too. Objects that can be destroyed in some stages, and are invincible in others. Graffiti that stands out because it ignores the lighting of the stage around it. Ninjas that are invincible, but awkwardly go into their deflection animations seconds after you start shooting them. Enemies who aren't harmed by your laser attack because they're too close to you. Doors that close before you've fully entered them, making the stage unfinishable. QTEs that completely go away after the third stage of the game, likely because the developers saw how ridiculous they looked when you had any costume chosen for Grave besides the default. Just no QA testing at all......And you know what? Despite all of that? Despite the game's graphics looking like it more belonged in 2006 than 2022? Despite my better judgment, I STILL might have forgiven all of these problems and allowed the game a passing grade if it at least ran well on my PC. It absolutely does not. It is yet another in a growing list of poorly optimized Unreal Engine 4 games that are miserable to play on PC. Every time the game displays a new special effect for the first time, the game stutters. Every time the game loads in a new group of enemies or a new part of the map, the game stutters.I have an RTX 2080 Super and an Intel Core i9 10900K. Running the game with -dx11 in your launch options will stop the shader compilation stutter. Having the Nvidia Control Panel's Power Management Mode set to Prefer Maximum Performance will get rid of the stutter that happens when Grave twirls his guns at the start of a stage. Nothing I have tried has managed to solve the texture streaming stutter. Lowering the settings to rock bottom does nothing. Messing around with Engine.ini either has no effect or makes things worse. DXVK breaks the game's FMVs. Half of my playtime is just me trying to get this game to run at the bare minimum of acceptable quality! It's completely disgusting that I have to run myself ragged like this trying to solve a problem that any competent developers would have already solved themselves!So I ask you this, reader: Do you want to buy a game that you have to make excuses for? A game that can only be enjoyed by people who are caught in the throes of nostalgia for their childhoods, and the aughts? Or do you want to buy a game that is actually good on its own merits? A game that actually deserves your time and money? If you want the latter, then it ain't here, bro. You've been warned.TL;DR?- Yet another poorly optimized Unreal Engine 4 game. Absolute stuttergeddon.- Poor variety in gameplay. Very one note. The extra characters are barely used.- Dull level design. Enter a room, shoot everybody, door opens, enter new room. Wash, rinse, repeat.- Fever dream story with awful, paid intern level voice acting.- Graphics look like a remastered 7th generation game.- Jank everywhere that ranges from minor to game breaking.Not Recommended. Half-assed game. Half-assed PC port. Buy it on a large discount. Preferably on a console.Or just watch the anime instead. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Where do i even begin?At the very core of the gameplay, as in the way Grave himself plays, its Gungrave. The movement is essentially the samesince Overdose, with the added benefits of free-cam instead of the camera being glued to movement.You still have most of the basic Move-set; like Demolition Shots, Burst Mode, Storm Barrage, Funreal Strike etc. with the main changes being the button layout; most importantly putting the Shooting on the Trigger instead of a Face button which while very much a cute idea, tires out the finger even more than the original way and is also not rebindable in the in-game options menu.The newest addition to Graves move-set is a Chain which lets him grab enemies for Meat Shields or latch onto enemies to move across the Arena and the ability for instant kills called R.I.Ps which regenerate shields, both great additions that when they work really add to the gameplay flow.When they work, i must stress.The new flow of gameplay puts great emphasis on regaining shield in ways not prior available, either through Meat-Shielding or R.I.Ping enemies when possible, in the Original and especially in Overdose this was not possible, you had to rely on either using a Demolition Shot giving you some respite or just wait outside of a fight for your Shield to recharge;this is definitely an inspired decision, and mixed with the meat-shield slam attack would've heavily put the flow into the Players favour while still allowing for the huge wave of enemies the game throws at you to feel fair, but the chain just flat out feels unfinished. It either seems to be based on where the crosshair is, what enemy is currently R.I.Pable (sometimes) or if its right in front of you (sometimes), there is no real indication on what the chain will grab in most heated situations, if it even grabs something at all. Elevation is a huge issue for the chain to deal with, grabbing something on either side of a Staircase is a gamble and if there is even just a tiny box in front of your target the chain might just not bother at all, even if visually it would've connected. A major issue, one that has screwed me many times, is trying to chain Grabs from Meat-Shields, which you straight up can not do, at the very least not against the shield enemies. If you grab an enemy, slam them in front of a shielder to break their shield, and then tried to grab them, the chain goes through them; their shield break animation just flat out makes them immune. Considering this is an enemy type that is otherwise really a hassle to deal with in large firefights, with the only other methods available against them (not counting Fury Mode, as you wont always have it available and you still take damage) being to use the awkward charge shot (which doesn't let you charge unless you've already fired a shot) or the melee attack (which leaves you open to enemy fire, maybe even killing you on later difficulties), this is just plainly an annoyance and feels like a punishment for engaging in the games deeper mechanics.Not to mention, in the prior games you could shoot shielders and do just a little damage regardless,Speaking of enemy immunity, the Ninja: an enemy that deflects your bullets.Now that's fine, they exist in the prior games, and have the same weakness = Burst Mode fire overwhelms them eventually, killing them.But with this games expanded melee set, and the fact they don't activate the deflect when using it, it would seem hitting them with the melee is also an intended option. Just, it doesn't work: if you shoot them beforehand, leading into their deflect animation, they simply do not take damage from melee attacks making them completely immune to damage for a while. The Burst Mode strategy is not viable in the large scale firefights this game tasks of you, meaning you have an enemy type that now needs special treatment while there's Shielders with Shot-gunners, Snipers, Machine-gunners and Rocket Launcher (later with Homing Missles) running about, firing on you with full caliber. This simply wont do, once againit breaks any semblance of flow.Speaking of the Snipers, they're a little awkward. There's no real indication of when to properly dodge them besides timing it out; the laser disappearing might have been intended to be the cue for dodging but it seems the Snipers fire way too fast after it vanishes (maybe this was just me?) leading to frustration at their One-Shot shield destruction, especially during the city levels where they are stationed way higher than you can actually aim.The levels are another Topic entirely, its clear the designers where at best amateurs and at worst intentionally Malicious in their design. You will see many discussions and reviews mention the Platforming sections, especially on the Train, which feel completely out of place in a game like this. All guides for the train section will show you how to essentially outrun ever having to do the actual platforming parts, which should tell you from the get go how well liked the level is.Add this to the level where you jump between out of synch moving platforms and its really a mind boggler how they thought this was a good idea, though to be fair that one doesnt instantly kill you. Outside the other egregious level gimmick, the laser corridor that instantly kills you, the levels are otherwise the same; corridor shooter levels with the occasional cool backdrop like a church or a casino. These backdrops are few and far between however, as the game stretches its run time extremely thin with levels that feel like filler; perhaps in the fear that a shorter game would make the price-point sting even more. with 31 levels, of which TWO are not played as Grave, its hard not to get just a little tired of the never changing Gameplay among the repeating Sceneries, especially early on when its a lot of Labs and Sewers; the interesting locales don't appear until much later, leading me to think these might have been an afterthought.Of course, it doesn't help that the game goes for a less stylized look than its predecessors, though i wont blame the team too much here, its clear they reused and based a lot of assets on their prior VR title, making them stylized was not in their best interest as much as it pains me to say. On that note, the graphic settings don't work, at least for me and i've seen some other people with the same issue, so i didn't even get to see the "pretty" Unreal engine graphics, instead i looked at vaseline smeared concrete for most of my playthrough.The prior mentioned other Characters are odd additions, not as in multiple characters bad; Overdose had it too, more that one seems to fit the style while the other seems like a tech-demo for a different game entirely.Bunji is fine, he works, kind of even plays like Junji did in Overdose without the sword blades.Quartz is a melee focused character with a stun gimmick and her level features timed Platforming sections.I scratched my head a lot on that one, from both the prospect and the execution.Now her jump actually works, somewhat. She has an actual jump arc that's controllable and feels fine, the main issue being the delay on impact. You cant chain jumps making her platform section a pain in the ass, not to mention you cant chain any of her moves making her combat feel stilted.Why cant i jump out of my attacks, why cant i use the stun projectiles mid combo, why cant i use the dodge mid combo.She has a jump kick that feels completely useless because why would you ever risk it, you cant chain it into anything or chain anything into it!This game has many issues, and it pains me to say you cant fix all of them with patches; you can patch out the bugs, perhaps even an option to play the characters in other levels, but the fundamental issues like level designs remain. For the price it is right now, it's not worth it. There is clear passion, the devs were absolutely Fans of Gungrave, but that only takes you so far.Get it on a steep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this by saying that I have never played the original games in this series and thought I was getting a completely different product than what I bought. I figured this would be something similar to Bayonetta or DMC, but I can say I'm horribly let down and should have looked into this game more before I bought it. TL;DR: This game is so boring it literally almost put me to sleep. The main saving grace is that it has some very beautifully designed areas, but the combat is severely lacking in pretty much every aspect save for the ranged combat. It's very hard for me to find reasons to give this game a good rating. The combat will always consist of holding right trigger and backing up. Sometimes, if you're feeling spicy, you can perform executions, but they always look the same and honestly aren't really worth doing it unless you want the points from it. You have melee capability, but it's pretty useless unless you're knocking back rockets, which move so slow you can just slowly walk away from them. Enemies are pretty braindead and will always swarm you no matter where you are or what you're doing and don't react to being shot so it becomes this slog of being trapped in the middle of a room with 30 guys, half of which are shooting you and half of which are all up in your face. The bosses (the one's I've seen at least) are well designed bullet sponges. They aren't anything special and you'll probably be able to beat them the same way you can beat anything else. By constantly holding your fire button and either back peddling away form them or circle strafing. Sometimes, you might even have to dodge!The one and only saving grace is that this game looks beautiful. The environments look nice, but you don't really get to explore them, as this is essentially an on-rails shooter with extra steps. I can see where the majority of this games budget went, but when you sacrifice a very core component of your game (in this case, the combat), it really just doesn't make up for it. For what it is though, I can see people enjoying just turning their brains off to this for hours on end, but I don't think the vast majority of gamers want a game where you're made to play as braindead as the AI. Every single fight will play out almost the exact same.I think the funny thing is, if you look at the wiki for this game, it describes itself with "Stylish third-person shooting meets close-range martial arts, creating seamlessly flowing action as you crush your enemies in a gory ballet of bullets" and your melee combat is very rarely ever useful and is always forgone for your guns. I'm not sure if it's a bug or it's just how the game is designed, but when I swing the coffin, my attacks only ever connect with one person at a time, even if there are multiple people standing in front of me. Overall, I'm glad I picked this up from ♥♥♥ for like 10 bucks, because I truly don't think this game is worth the $50 price tag, and I can't recommend it to anyone at full price. Either wait for a sale or pick it up from a key reseller.

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm, this is a rough one! I really wanted to like this game, to the point of coming back to try it again after they patched it, and credit where it's due, they did fix some issues and added a lot of quality-of-life features like auto-fire. The game is certainly a unique third-person shooter experience that eschews the typical cover-based gameplay, and I liked how the levels were cleverly laid out that you could chain kills and environmental destruction to achieve a combo that lasts the entire level: reminded me a lot of other score-based shooters like "The Club". It just has a lot of dumb but lovable charm to it, and it can be loads of fun blasting goons to the awesome tune of "Time to Kill"!Unfortunately, as much as I loved that charm it had, it couldn't keep me engaged for long as the game has fundamental issues that kept getting in the way. There are loads of technical issues that range from major problems (softlocks from getting stuck in geometry, hard crashes) to lackluster elements that make the game feel bad (missing sounds, stiff animations, confusing hitboxes, limp feedback, etc). Even if you can brush those issues aside, the game also suffers from repetitive combat that doesn't evolve, a horrible upgrade system filled with boring stats and useless moves, and a confusing and unsatisfying story.Kudos to the devs for trying to revive this neat series: it certainly has a lot of potential but botched the execution for me. If you're able to get it on sale like I did and you enjoy exploring janky but unique games or are a diehard Gungrave fan, maybe give it a go, otherwise look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Loveable korean jank. I could bang on about the low budget look, the small stutters when first picking up the game, some really annoying levels or the padded skill tree, but the heart of this game is in its right place. Shamelessly trying to be a sequel for a PS2 game without a single shred of care, Gungrave G.O.R.E is one of those games where you can't help but like it because it's beyond saving. It knows exactly what it is, it appeals only to people like me, and it couldn't care less.We have a myriad of new abilities and QOL improvements, a second playable character and an expansive campaign that takes you at least 10 hours to finish, but in my opinion it's the inclusion of a forgiving normal/easy mode and an autofire option that makes the game significantly more enjoyable for people who just want to get in and start blasting like it's nothing. While I finished the game on hard and felt that the difficulty was just tight enough, some sections are definitely annoying.It's a testament to the love Iggymob put into the game however that several of the worst things about the launch version have been fixed, outright removed or rebalanced based on player feedback as well. As I just said, this is a dumb poor wrecking ball game, so expect it to be one of those titles that are kinda repetitive, stiff -and at times a bit ♥♥♥♥- but still love it. If you're the kind of person who likes every now and then to turn their brain off, this is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to know if you would enjoy this game, play the PS2 originals. Again, if you'd played them as a kid. Really *feel* what it's like to play a mid-PS2 action game.Did you enjoy the stylish combat, or did the control scheme feel too jank? Could you get into the over the top boss fights, or did the nonsensical plot make them just confusing nonsense? Did you get to grips with the surprisingly intricate scoring mechanics, or did you just get annoyed by platforming sequences in your third person shooter?Gungrave GORE feels like a PS2 game, and that's the highest compliment I can give it. Platforming feels terrible, the cutscene direction is a joke compared to the originals, enemy variety is lacking, and three of the bosses are basically palette swaps of each other. This is the sequel I hoped for way back when it was announced, and I'm actually disappointed I didn't get around to playing the game until now.

_childDocuments_.review: Gungrave G.O.R.E. is a exceptional traditional over the top arcade video action game, that captures the glory from the old days really well, yet remains very accessible to newcomers alike. It also comes with a massive soundtrack, that continuously delivers badass pumping beats. This game can be very stress releaving on a light difficulty mode.Its a triple A B game.(Eventhough i am not familiar with the roots of Gungrave, nor the previous games, nor the anime, this review is purely based on my experience with this installment.)A good thing to realise first, is that Gungrave G.O.R.E. is a traditional arcade video game, and traditional arcade games, can be very repetitive. And, well, so is this one.But nevertheless, it comes with the territory, yet to me, the repetitiveness is very well compensated by the great variety in level theme, and scenery design, the great use of the color palette, the badass soundtrack, the classic video game vibe, corny humor, and over the top badass special weapons / abillity's, with my personal favorite being the"Doom's Rain" ability :) This game really brings back that old school arcade cabinet atmosphere feeling, just like, when you would walk into a video arcade, back in the 80's / 90's. I personally just really love these games.This game can be a breath of fresh air, when you pick it up now and then, and can be very stress releaving. I found myself smiling on more then one occasion, while playing this game. I mean, don't you just wonder sometimes, how Grave can put all this mad, badass weaponry, into his coffin ? XDAlso, when you progress through the game, eventualy, there is also a bit of Max Payne flavour mixed into Gungrave. * Once you unlock Bunji ** But only a little bit of flavour though. ** Those who played the Max Payne series will recognise. *It might have some technical down sides for some, yes, there was some stuttering for me too in the beginning, when i first started playing this game, but they mostly fixed it eventually in my play through down the lane. And yes, the low res explosion animations, really can make you feel, like you where back in the 90's again. Yet i do believe, that people from back in the day, but also newcommers alike, yet also people with high and low end systems, might also be able to appreciate this game. (If you like the genre that is) Because, it will bring fun to the table. For me personally, this experience was a reminder about the days, when it was all about fun and gameplay, and games didn't took themselves all that seriously.It's a real good stress releaving classic arcade action video game, in an evolved form, with over the top madness, for oldschoolers and newcomers alike. So set your mind free, crank up the speakers, and enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Gungrave G.O.R.E. I love this game. I played Gungrave G.O.R.E for about 13 hours and I would like to speak about what I loved & what needs to be improved. Action games have been improving as generations passed by. Improving means actions games became better but at the same time more complicated and harder. In that sense, Gungrave G.O.R.E kept the fun that was there in the past. Less complicated and simple yet has this weird-ish attractiveness. I’d say I still comeback to it even though I am complaining at times.  So here goes my review.Pros:At first, I was like “What the F-!”. However, I found myself getting more and more immersed into the game. The game looked a janky but as I was beating the stages and equipped new skills, it got me thinking “What is this game? And I got to a point where I think the game is actually fun to play:” Here are my pros. #1. Nothing is stopping me. Nothing gets on my way and it destroys everything. It delivers that I am something special in-game very clearly. Maybe because we are fighting against drug cartel, there is no guilt trip by killing them all. Dual pistols don’t need to be reloaded. Bullet rain is the word. When I see the high numbers of enemies, I go “there are simply too many!” but I see myself getting rid of them all in no time. #2.Simple. You don’t have to think too much. Kill all if you see them. You can destroy objects as well and you are onto the next stage. Someone like me who doesn’t like when things are complicated, such a pleasure experience. #3. Cool looking character. Grave and Bunji are still cool. Silent Grave. Never seen a protagonist who doesn’t speak in modern games. I was expecting him to say something cool but nothing was there. However, Grave looks very unique and the design is cool so just looking at him shoot made Grave look cool #4.Playing time. Not too long, not too short. Maybe that is one of the reasons why I was so into the game. When a lot of enemies come out or when you face someone strong, you are so focused to a point you don’t even care about what’s around you. #5.Shield system really makes my palm sweaty.Very old yet classic method. You fight until the shield goes all the way down and when you destroy them all, you get excited by looking at the shield regenerating. That must be one of the attractiveness yet makes you complain at the same time? Cons:Studio said they inherited the pros of previous game but I can feel that cons were also inherited. I will write about the cons now. #1.Too loud. Too too loud. Shooting, exploding sound, and enemies’ sound effect are all mixed and very loud. I highly advise that you adjust the volume.  #2.Visuals were not so satisfactory. Comparing with likes of Call of Duty and God of War, they don’t look good at all. I mean we don’t even have to go there and compare since the visual quality isn’t really top notch anyway. Gungrave’s original version was not recognized by the visuals anyway so it is somewhat acceptable. #3. Crazy difficulty of some stages. The game is easy once you upgrade them but without upgrading your character, it will make you down. #4. Please add auto fire! Please!!I won’t explain further, you will know what I mean when you play the game. This game also pros and cons just like the other games but I find the game entertaining so I recommend playing this game. I am looking forward to the studio to patch the game to make the game better. I would like to see what studio Iggymob can do with their next move since they revived a title that was dead for a long time. _childDocuments_.review: Gungrave G.O.R.E is a game that doesn't pretend to be anything other than what it is...no side missions, pointless collectables, or secrets to be found here to pad out the content. Its a relatively short experience, having clocked in just over 8 hours on my first playthrough, where 75% of the game was done in normal difficulty and the rest on easy because it becomes entirely too ret*rded in terms of difficulty to a point where you'd probably have to go back and grind previous levels just to keep up with wtf is happening, and I just cannot be bothered to do that. Aimbotting NPCs, one shot shield busting attacks, constantly getting f*cking fire and poison gas dropped on you, weak special abilities and entirely too expensive upgrades that even getting an A rank on most missions can't afford. You don't get any more or less of a reward for playing other difficulties either so you just make the game harder for no reason other than to make it hard, to which most of it is just artificial difficulty...I really so no way of been able to out skill all the bullsh*t that comes at you half the time.Its an insanely repetitive game, and that fact sinks in quite quickly after the initial buzz of "oh this is awesome!" just annihilating bad guys in waves. Forgettable and annoying cast of characters, recycled voice lines spammed constantly as you move between rooms, a really convoluted story that I guess you'd have to have played the PS games and/or watched the anime to know wtf they're all flapping on about most of the time.Eh...a good concept of a game that I initially thought would be like Devil May Cry, but ultimately very poorly executed and just a bit boring unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing. This is a game targeted at a very specific niche audience; that is, those that played Gungrave and Gungrave O.D.I was not one of those people until recently. I can't in good conscience recommend anyone ever pay $50 for this thing, but it goes on sale every now and then. I got it for $10, but honestly think I would be willing to pay about $20, and that's as someone with an appreciation for its goofy edginess. It's REALLY niche; it feels like the PS2 games, and it looks like a PS3 game. Do yourself a favor and turn on the cel-shading option. It's more tolerable that way.I heard it was quite buggy at release: I'm happy to say that I have encountered no show-stoppers so far. Worst issues so far are lame cutscenes, nonsense story, and dear LORD please hire a native English speaker to proofread your English text. It's giving me conniptions, I'd do it for free but I can't be bothered to try and mod another UE4 game.Also, they got an entire Japanese dub but they didn't dub the mobsters in anything other than Korean and (poor) English. They speak like five generic lines, was it really that difficult?Here's some suggestions if you decide to play:1. TURN OFF THE RADIO VOICE. She's horrible, no matter the language. You're welcome. Unfortunately nothing can be done about the obnoxious holographic objective markers. The game is one long hallway, why are these even a thing?2. Upgrade your bullet damage. Hard is going to be a nightmare without it. Honestly, maybe don't play Hard until you've already upgraded your stats... it's tedious and unfun as hell if you don't.3. Just for fun, take a shot every time the game loads a cutscene and it's just Grave walking silently. It's hilarious. On second thought, don't do that, you'll get cirrhosis.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun game, certainly different then what the majority games offer today which is why it is worth playing on a sale. The core of the game is fun with honing in on the most dangerous targets, racking up combos and strategically deploying special skills. It is a shame then that the scoring system could use some tweaking. First of all it is difficult to tell if the amount of a measured metric tallied up at the end of the level you acquired enough of. Combo is one the components which is irritating to get right, to keep it going you have to be shooting either enemies or object in the environment. It takes a second of not shoot a correct object to lose it, losing it past the half way mark of the level means possibly losing out on a high score at the end of the level. This is annoying because the level design works not in your favour, levels are not always clear were to go next, the guidance from the game helps, but you have to be keeping a combo going at all times. Not all object are destructible which hinders your planning and routing thru the level, why couldn'tthe game geometry as bare bones as it is already be simplified in vein of God Hand to help with this?. A way to keep your combo going while being in a vunerable state as a trade-off would help a lot in this game.Overall there are other nitpicks, it is a fresh game in this gaming market, nowhere else you will find it, majority of it is janky, but you will enjoy it. A minus is the lackluster use of Gungrave IP which seems very bland in comparison to the manga, anime adaptation or even the 2002 game.
