_childDocuments_.review: I want to say this game is pretty dumb, but you know what? It's fun. It's hard to die, with constantly recharging shields if you can avoid damage and super moves that give you back health equal to the meter spent PLUS initializing an uninterruptable shield regen PLUS executions for some guys. But when you stick it on hard mode, the constant hail of bullets and little choices like "Now I'm going to melee these dudes, now I'm going to kite this group to do a giant rocket launcher volley" feels good. You COULD let your shield regen between gaps in encounters, but that would break your chain, which means your max chain rank suffers at end of level. You COULD just rapid fire everything, but that affects your style rank because you don't get style points for standard shot kills... you need to burn rage meter to do that. And how do you move from encounter to encounter without breaking chain? You shoot scenery. You should be moving into the middle of a room, looking for the big glowing "Go here next" arrow in the middle of the gunfight, and slaughtering your way towards that so you don't have to let your numbers go down. So, it's simple and addictive because of the simplicity. Kinda like Burnout games, it's a whole lot of flash and style, mostly just playing to beat your score. For the 10 bucks I got it for in late September 2023, perfect. Would NOT buy at 50, but it sounds like the devs are listening to issues and correcting them, so that might be worth supporting them for more dollarbucks. I'll probably pick up the cosmetic DLCs just to throw another couple bucks at em, something I don't usually do. Issues: - Sometimes the hit detection is real spotty when manual aim comes into play. The laser beam is this crazy thin hurtbox and you'll spend more time trying to get it to adjust to clip something than it doing real damage. Hits like a truck if you sweep it across minions, but worthless for bosses. - Buttons have a weird feel to them sometimes. You tap RB to pull an enemy to you, including for executions, and hold it to dash and execute, but if they're on a ledge and you see the execution prompt, do the chain pull, it'll pull you to them instead... and if there's a bottomless pit, you just died. It's weird. - Other button weirdness. There's a lag to confirm in the menus, so if you try to exit, for example, there's this awkward moment where you're not sure if the button registered. Minor, not really a thing that comes up much until you're bailing on the game, but it's strange that it happens. - Character models are like old women in mocap suits. Can't really see it until you watch cutscenes, but it's kinda like upscaled Dreamcast fidelity, back when they were still figuring out basic gestures.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this on Game Pass and I pretty much stopped when I bought Bunji in the shop towards, like, the middle of the game. I couldn't get the DLC at the time since they were preorder bonuses but now they're available for purchase. Which is great! Because the Death Ronin and Overdose Grave skins are SO COOL. Anyway, the game is equally as good as it is flawed. Shooting feels really good and the Demolition attacks are EASILY the best part about the combat. However, there really isn't much of a story which is a bummer but given how this is meant to emulate the mindless arcade shooters of yore, I can learn to live with it. I can live with the voice acting as well. I actually think it weirdly enhances the experience to some degree,When I played the game last year, there were quite a few gameplay issues that have largely been fixed. However, I still think that while the level design is okay at the beginning, it takes a HUGE hit in quality further in the game. Enemies also had a habit of REALLY crowding around you later on in the game where the only means of escape is to throw out the most crowd control-y move you have, which I found jarring even a game like Gungrave. Enemies can get pretty frustrating overall but they have gotten balance changes since the launch build, which is great. Also, the grind for DNA can get very time consuming. Upgrades and characters can get pretty expensive and as a result, I ended up having to grind for a considerably long time. I will give credit where credit is due. Iggymob has certainly been listening to complaints and have been releasing patches, regardless of the state of this game.And on a related note! Bunji. Thank you, Iggymob, for letting us play as Bunji. :) But I have one thing to say about it. Bunji feels very limited compared to the LARGE amount of tools in Grave's moveset. Granted, Bunji doesn't necessarily have to be as expansive with his loadout as Grave but I was always confused as to why he had 3 demolition moves instead of 4. That's probably my only complaint and I love playing as him regardless. This game has come a long way since its rough launch and I'm glad that Iggymob is willing to fix the game. Especially since the announcement for this game is how I got into Gungrave in the first place. The game is very easy to jump into without any knowledge of the game but I wanted to play the older games anyway because I thought they looked cool. Do I recommend this one though? Yes, but with caution. If you want to pretend like its 2008 again and experience this game for its strengths and weaknesses, be my guest. Up to you if you want to wait for a sale or not, it's your money. But, if you want a game with more depth than "shoot-everything-in-your-wake-with-little-regard-for-your-health-bar,' then this is definitely not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell in raising Brandon from the dead for one more genocide, Iggymob did it with love. Even if they got some things horribly wrong.I would criticize the game's art style, but to even call it an art style would be way too generous. They haphazardly dumped a big bucket of unreal engine onto their game without a shred of artistic vision. It's clean, bright, colorful, and utterly flavorless. It's all such a far cry from the slick and gritty anime style of the first 2 games, design that was exaggerated yet meaningful, characters and locations that could stick in your mind. This game, conversely, slaps a bunch of color on the screen without actually trying to paint a picture. It's downright criminal.The sterilized gruel Gore puts in your face almost invalidates the game for me, but beneath the plastic veneer, the soul of the franchise can still be felt.The man is very much the same tank you piloted back on the Ps2, but he's never been more responsive or had so many dance moves. Melee is far less rigid, with new situational combo enders. You can only bring four demolition shots on each stage, but you can whip them out at the drop of a hat without navigating a menu. In action, Grave is the best he has ever been, even if he does look like a goony doll now.While Gore is kind enough to put extra shootables in between arenas so you can keep your beat count high, level design is largely a miss compared to the older games. There are occasional hints of thought and structure to enemy placement in Gore, but it all typically devolves into a mess of random technicolor idiots marching directly toward you. Thankfully, lining them up and ripping through them all with a single massive bullet is always a pleasure.Bunji is an unlockable character, and he's functionally a quicker but simpler Grave. The other playable character, Quartz, you get for just one level. She has such a melee-centric approach that I guess the devs just couldn't figure out how to implement her in the main campaign where enemies start shooting and they just never stop shooting. It's a shame they couldn't manage to deliver a wildly new style to tackle each stage in a brand new way.I feel the places Gore falls short isn't for lack of passion, but money and/or talent. In animating his crazy demolition shots, in trying to cap off each stage with a cool cutscene finish, in putting in so many different enemy types and factions and surprisingly decent music, there were definitely people involved in this revival who really wanted to be there even if the budget was tight. Though the cover definitely looks rough, I think their effort still shows in a charming way.Nowadays, it's refreshing to have a game that plays straight with stupid edgy fun without having to submerge it in irony.

_childDocuments_.review: Gungrave G.O.R.E lives up to its name, especially the G.O.R.E part. It's fun, challenging and a lot more complex than your average hack-and-slash action RPG.Do I ram into the enemy, focus fire on them, grab someone to use as meat shield or dodge and kite like crazy? Do I use rage mode to mow down the enemy or a demolition shot to recover HP? The game feels challenging right from the start. Your character, Beyond the Grave, can feel clunky, but that's his character, and he makes up for it with his diverse and powerful kit. Two stages so far have felt like a DPS check that required me to either save up demolition shots in advance or straight up lower the difficulty, but I've been loving this game so far.The graphics are ok, then lighting is great, the rendering is pretty intense and it's even got ray tracing - a much welcomed addition after the game got delayed since before real time ray tracing was a thing - but the environment has a low and noticeable polygon count and it's stuttered like 1-2 times every 1-2 stages, which is a lot less common than haters say. Disabling v-sync might have helped some.I'm writing this review early to offset some of the hate the game's received. Gungrave G.O.R.E is not a marvel of engineering, but it still stands out as one of the most fun and challenging games of its genre. As someone who didn't get to play the PS2 original and having watched the masterpiece anime adaptation, I'm enjoying this game, and love the style.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a fan of the first two games and the anime. I have played multiple play through on those games as they have quite good re-playable value. I only play up to the train part and I really want to finish the game before writing the review but I want to do a preliminary review of what I feel thus far.Gameplay: it feels somewhat subpar, I really want to love it but it is not good for 2022 game. Combat system should be more fluid especially the way they throw in enemies at you. Melee is underwhelm but in the previous game it wasn't too bad as most of enemies use gun and it was GUNgrave afterall. While GORE has expand much more on the melee combat for Grave, it's not polish. The fluid between shooting and meleeing is not there at all. There's too many animation lag between swinging coffin and back to shooting. See that you can unlock more combos later but it strikes me a question that the animation lag decreases as the skill is increased in lvl. Demolition point feels cap out when you have max point and the gauge stops. The gauge should keeps filling like the old game and the extra point can use for something else like regen the shield or health. With how much enemies they throw at you, why can't Grave use Death Hauler as a shield? There are so many cool combos and transform of the Death Hauler into bunches of weapon but it can't block attacks?The train level is really annoying and it's hardly being called challenging. There's no balance in term of challenge, it's like the dev making it nearly impossible to beat and call challenge. It's like they tried to be Ninja Gaiden, Seikiro, and DMC hard but their combat and movement system is not great. Why trying to do platform and time sensitive challenge when the player can't even do combos and jump accurately. At least give the player an option to destroy the sign ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ through like what Grave would have done usually. He's not nimble and pretty much solve everything through destruction. Don't try to make him into Dante.I wish they would bring back the cinematic finish with cool music like the previous game. If I recalled, GGOD didn't do it neither but it was cool in the first game.Character design: I understand that this was done by Korean developer and you can tell by the art style. I don't really have problem with that but it feels like they have took out all the Nightow style from Gungrave. The "History" option to see the back story was nice but it was done so terribly where why bother? Like, it's better to just get the cutscene from the game and make it into little movies. It was already done in anime style and it was great! Though I like the costume design especially for Grave, it's throwback of the old one and mix with the new. I like it. I haven't seen all other character design but hopefully, I'll go back and get past that damn train and see all the other characters especially Bunji. Unfortunately, Juji and RB aren't in this game. It would be cool if they can be unlocked later or something.Music: In the previous game and anime, the music was done by Imahori Tsuneo. The style of the music was great and it was part of what makes it Gungrave. Gunlock Overdrive was used in the first two opening theme so why was it not in this one? I wish they would be a cinematic opening similar to the first two. Not having Tsuneo music feels let down as a fan.At beginning, I was going to leave positive review and not recommend to the non-GG fan. However, with everything I experience thus far, I feel that it might even make the fan feel let down like how I feel.PS: Where's my bloody pre-order bonus?!! I wanted to do a playthrough with OD outfit damnit.EDIT: I love how fast the patch and improvement is made and how the developer listen to community feedback. I changed the recommendation but leaving the original feedback.While I would love to have Tsuneo for music, the current music is great as well. I'm a fan of Monster Hunter and love music for that game too. I'm just biased toward original soundtrack from the old games.

_childDocuments_.review: In the first version of the game Gungrave G.O.R.E cemented itself as a worthy sequel to Overdose with level and boss design made to torture, infuriate and otherwise bring your patience to its edge with combat mechanics that, while they are distinct from its predecessors, brought a satisfying and fresh take on a formula that is not replicated in any of its contemporaries à la Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, etc. and this changed soon after with a couple of patches, in its current state I struggle to recommend this game anymore as they've removed essential components to its difficulty through rebalances of mechanics, area design and bosses that devalue the need of the mechanics they've iterated upon from Overdose and while patch 1.00 was the beginning of this feeling with a movement speed buff that allows you to outrun enemy bullets while shooting and the redesign of a few stages like the caves platforming section which now serves as an awkwardly paced intermediary section between kill rooms I still thought a lot of changes while ruining my own fun for the game were still a polished change to the experience that would allow it to be enjoyed by more people, but now we are on patch 1.01 where I truly feel they have killed the experience through a buff to Demolition Shot guage gain that makes it near impossible to die even on G.O.R.E difficulty, they also seemingly removed the generic enemies in condorbraves boss fight which I truly cannot fathom the need to do so as its the only thing that makes dodging his shots difficult I would've never first tried him on the previous patch and certainly not the first version of the game but now these and several other changes are making stages on the hardest difficulty barely something I have to pay attention to. I struggle to understand a lot of the other changes made as well such as 3 hit melee strings parrying rockets making death tornado a borderline useless attack and making the easier parry timing in this game feel completely unecessary, shield enemies having their shield health severely nerfed making them barely a consideration when fighting because you're likely to just break their shields regardless and even changes unrelated to balance like the weird camera angle change made during the executioners blood Demolition Shot.Overall they've stripped various aspects of the difficulty that felt carefully considered and well crafted to compensate for people that can't accept any form of jank in their video games, unfortunately the game is by nature janky so this is still in the game but without any of the difficulty that brings things together and you're left with a lack of challenge that makes many of the abilities in the game necessary and you're left with no depth to the games mechanics that while stylish in combination with the extensive length of the game I feel do not justify the purchase of G.O.R.E on their own.

name: Centipede: Recharged
detailed_description: The original bug-blasting arcade game is back! Centipede: Recharged has been reimagined for modern gameplay, with vibrant visuals designed for modern screens, a 16:9 field of play, and an original soundtrack from award-winning video game composer Megan McDuffee. Aim for a high score in the old school arcade mode and earn bragging rights with your name at the top of the leaderboard. Or test your skills and rank on the boards in one of 30 intensely creative challenges, which twist the gameplay in new and exciting ways. A dozen new power-ups can give you an edge by introducing abilities like screen-clearing explosions, rail guns, and even slowing down time. Every mode and level is playable in local co-op mode with a friend. _childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying that I love Centipede. I've been playing it for most of my life, and I've played it on a variety of platforms, both through emulations and ports. I've even played the original arcade game with the trackball (with a Millipede exterior, funnily enough). Needless to say, I know what I'm talking about when I say that Centipede: Recharged is a bit of a letdown.Now the most obvious thing you'll notice is the visuals, which have been altered from the original's raster graphics to look like vector graphics along the lines of other Atari arcade classics like Asteroids and Tempest, and while it looks stylish, the overall design looks better on paper than in actual gameplay. The game has been altered to take up the whole screen, which probably looks neater for a modern gamer raised on 16:9 games, but it means that the creatures have a lot more distance to travel, which hurts the speed and energy that make the original game so fun. Furthermore, a big part of the strategy is keeping an eye on the surroundings, and a larger playing field just makes it more of a pain, which isn't helped by the unnecessary (though thankfully optional, and not even default) option to zoom the screen onto the player.The redone sound also does more harm than good to the experience. In the original, Atari's proprietary POKEY sound chip, the same one used in their 8-bit computers and the infamous Atari 5200, is used to give the iconic sounds. Each of the enemies has a distinct sound, giving the player a cue to plan a strategy to deal with them. Recharged gives them more realistic sounds, which again, sound better in theory than in practice. The sounds are so subtle that I often barely notice when new enemies pop up. Making things worse is the generic, forgettable wavetable music, which often threaten to drown the sounds out.One thing I didn't mention in the original version of this review was that the shooting feels a bit slower than the original. Maybe it's just because of the larger playing field, but the Bug Blaster seems to fire more slowly than in the original, making it somewhat harder to time your moves unless you have a power-up.On that note, the addition of power-ups is a mixed bag. They can and do make the game a little more playable, but I consider them to be a bit of a gimmick; the original was fun without them. It's not like Arkanoid, where the power-ups added a genuinely enjoyable new layer to the gameplay. If anything, they wouldn't have been necessary if it weren't for the game's other flaws. It also doesn't help that the first time I shoot a spider in a given playthrough, the game momentarily freezes, though honestly that may just be down to my less-than-optimal computer setup.Another issue I have that I didn't previously mention was the removal of levels in the main arcade mode. The changing levels helped make the original more fun, as you had a sense of progression. In Recharged, I don't get that; for as long as I've played, everything seems to be the same difficulty.When I first wrote this review, the game was missing mouse control, which was a huge oversight in my opinion. Like I said at the beginning, the original arcade version used a trackball to control the Bug Blaster, and the resulting precise controls are a major part of what makes it so addicting. Admittedly, a lot of earlier ports had to port the game over without the ability to use a trackball, and the results, while usually still fun, do feel a bit more floaty than the original as a result, but in my experience, a mouse works just as well, if not better (then again, the vast majority of my experience with the game has been with a mouse, so I may be biased). Playing with a keyboard just doesn't cut it, and while an analog stick is more precise, it's just not the same. But the worst part is that playing with an Xbox or Xinput controller doesn't even work in my experience. I've gotten it to work perfectly literally once in my time playing, and every other time something goes wrong. When I turn on the game after turning off my computer, the game stops responding to the controller, even though it works with everything else. Unplugging and plugging it back in fixes the issue for the menus, but in the actual game, only the control stick works. The button that's supposed to fire does absolutely nothing, and I have to use the keyboard for firing. Of course, I did all of this before the addition of mouse support, so I imagine this has been fixed too, but honestly, I just don't have the motivation to test it out again, considering I can now play it using my preferred method.Back when I first reviewed this game, I was a lot more upset with the game due to the controls, but now they've been fixed, my opinion has definitely improved. At least now the game actually feels a bit more like the original. Still, considering the dull audio, questionable changes, and the poor intial launch, I'd be lying if I said I fully recommend it, not for $10 at least. Maybe it's my nostalgia and purist nature, but if given the choice between the original arcade classic and Recharged, I'd take the original in a heartbeat.I'm not familiar with the developer, Adamvision, but I've heard they've done great work elsewhere, and I do strongly commend them for their ability to address the more pressing complaints, especially regarding the controls. I'm certainly open to playing more of their product. It's just too bad that this game in particular didn't live up to my expectations. Still, at least now I can say it's playable, even if I do completely prefer the original, which is definitely a testament to the devs' dedication.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an update on an old classic.. Centipede, seen in the 80's on arcade machines. Your objective is to eliminate the various spiders, fleas, and centipedes that come crawling across your screen while trying to prevent or rid the area of certain effects like mushrooms that grow from various hazards - affecting and creating tight spaces from which dodging incoming attacks is limited. Various upgrades are to be had when killing a spider such as explosive bullets, bombs, and other neat and helpful upgrades to your standard shooting projectile.Graphics are, though generally simple, are colorful and dynamic. With satisfying area explosions from your projectiles to the unique animated ability of the general static screen.Sound is menacing and appropriate. Music is apropos to the genre.It is best played using a d-pad controller though you can control it with a mouse and keyboard.Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of Centipede, and was eagerly awaiting this game.I wish I could say good things about it, but it feels like it was a premature release orpossibly an earlier build that was never meant to go up.My Xbox one controller would not work, I tried both Bluetooth and the official dongle,although it would work in the menu options, it would not let me use it in game.There is zero mouse support, which is a criminal offense for Centipede.I gave in and used the WASD keyboard configuration, which made the gameplay very clunky and really - not enjoyable.The game itself seemed alright, but gone are the levels and any sense of progression,what you're left with is one everlasting level that just feels kind of stale.Blast the centipede, kill a spider, get a power-up, rinse and repeat, die once - end of game.There are some challenges, separate from the main game, that do seem cool.But I would have much more preferred seeing a classic version put in place of the challenges.All in all, it just feels like a very lazy attempt at a remake, now granted, I was crippled by the keyboard and technical issues, but for it to be launched in this state is insulting.Needless to say, it was an easy refund, I hope to revisit it again if they ever address the issues. In the time being, I'd give this one a pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: I have never actually not recommended a game on Steam so far, but this is the closest i've come to it. The actual game itself is a lot of fun and its another good addition to the Recharged series from Atari.The main issue is that a controller input is only recognised on the main menus and not in game so I have had to complete the game (all achievements) via the keyboard. Luckily this game is more than playable on a keyboard and you can still enjoy it. I cant play to the best of my ability without a controller though!I find it staggering that in 2021 a game can be released by such a huge Publisher, and there is no response from devs or anything a week from its release on the controller problems. Not a whisper! NOTHING!The game gets recommended on the caveat that there will be a fix at some point to get the controller working correctly, and that aside from that issue it is a really fun game to play.I hope there are more Recharged versions of other games in the future, and hopefully they will get a better UAT team and the controller will work correctly from launch!

_childDocuments_.review: Centipede is my all-time favorite arcade game. I built my own arcade cabinet with a classic trackball just to play it. So once I found out about this game, I had to try it. I will admit, I was put off by the large amount of negative reviews, but the game is at a fair price, so I figured I would try it out, and I'm happy I did. First off, just to be clear, this game is NOT the classic Centipede from 1981 and the game clearly doesn't try to be. I think the problem the reviewers are having with this game is they are expecting the classic game, but doesn't make a lot of sense to me because the promotional images and footage make that clear. If you want the classic arcade, go play it, there are multiple avenues to do so. This game is not going to give you the same classic experience.What this game does do is take the original idea of the classic arcade and gives it a modern twist. This game is not at all meant to replace the 1981 classic, instead it tries something new, which is what fans of other popular franchises often beg for. So, I don't understand why people are punishing this game for trying something new. The new ideas this game presents gives the original classic a fresh twist for players to try to master, and I applaud them for doing that.It took me a while to get used to the game, to be honest. I didn't know how I felt about it a first, but once I understand the true premise of the game, I started to get hooked. I was a little unwelcoming of the power-ups, but with so much going on at once on the larger playing field, you'll come to find that the power-ups are pretty essential. The other strategies used in the classic still work here but just on a larger scale, such as trying to keep your playing area clean, trying to manipulate the centipede for quick points, and reducing the poisonous mushrooms when you have an opportunity.The co-op mode is probably the best this game has to offer. This mode had us playing over and over again, and saying “one more” many more times than we should.The only issue I have with the game is the distracting visuals. That is certainly unnecessary and the only complaint I have. Sometimes I died because I couldn’t even tell there was something about to run into me. I wish I could turn them off. This becomes even more annoying when you are shooting down the centipede from the head up. You can’t tell if you are about it collide with it because the explosion animation completely covers what you're hitting.  Overall, an awesome experience and if you're willing to try out a new take of an old classic arcade, this might be worth a shot. No quarters necessary.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW #55Centipede: Recharged----------This was my first taste of Atari's recent "Recharged" series, and I'm pretty impressed by what's offered here. Atari has had a bad reputation in the past when it comes to remakes of their most popular classics, and Centipede has been among of the victims of Atari's remake meat grinder once or twice. However, Adamvision and Sneaky Box did a really good job at updating it in a way that feels new but still maintains the structure of the classic gameplay, resulting in a game that feels like a unique yet fun experience.For those unfamiliar with the classic, Centipede is a top-down shooter with the player being able to move around a large portion of the playfield's bottom half. At the top, various bugs and insects will begin to invade the play area while spiders will approach from the sides. Being a classic arcade game, the goal is simply to get the highest score that you can.Centipede: Recharged updates this formula in a couple of different ways, one of which is the addition of weapon power-ups. While this could easily end up being a gimmicky trope, the power-ups offered here are well-balanced and satisfying to use. There's 3 different variations of game play, each with its own unique leaderboard. Challenge stages and local co-op are also available, rounding out this rather robust package of a classic game remake.There really isn't anything bad to say about this title. Graphics and sound are great, music is pleasant and appropriate, controls are well-designed, and I've yet to encounter a technical issue. I will say that action can build up and get so frantic that it's easy to lose track of adversaries getting close to your position, resulting in a sudden "Game Over". However, I blame that more on my attention span than the game.NOTE: Co-op was not evaluated for this review.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game for as low of a price point as it is. All of the modes have a purpose and help add to the amount of value you get from this game; Recharged is good for when you don't want to devote a lot of time to the game, giving you a single life, as well as having power-ups like burst shot, worse burst shot, and explosive bullets, while also having disappointments that are still classified as power-ups for some reason, such as rotating bullets and side-shot. Classic, while probably the weakest of the bunch, (I'll get to why later) still gives you a relatively pure Centipede experience. Recharged Classic is just recharged with 3 lives which makes it  a longer experience, perfect for when you're just looking to see a high number when you die. Challenge mode is for when you get bored of the other three modes and you want to try out masochism. Now it's time for me to complain about Classic Mode. I like it, but I wish that it lived up to its name better. It's not level based like the original, so it feels more overwhelming, which I'm not opposed to, but with the name Classic, I kind of expected just the original Centipede but with upgraded graphics, but no. I do think the Classic mode that we have has value, but I kind of wish that we also had the original with updated graphics, or heck, even just an emulation of the original arcade version. So yeah, cool mode, but don't expect it to live up to its name. Also there is that one glitch where all the sound cuts out after a lot of sound plays, and I am not too fond of that, but I can live with that.Anyway, really good game, good price point, easy 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic! I've loved Centipede since the old days in the arcades and still like to play it occasionally on Mame. There was a good reworking of it on the Xbox 360 and I even occasionally considered digging out the old console just to play it. But this surpasses them all! It's the best retro-reworking I've seen, adding some nice touches (like the power-ups) and taking out some of the nastier elements of the original (fast spiders rushing in without warning from the sides). This is really well done and I would love to see similar reworkings of some of the other arcade greats (Defender, Robotron, Joust).Works with the Xbox elite controller but, unless I'm missing something, there seems no way to quite the game using the controller alone. Mouse control doesn't seem to be available in-game.Update: I find this game addictive but also frustrating. There is probably too much randomness in it and I would like to see the gameplay refined a bit further. Even though I've apparently got the 8th highest score ever (47,000), I can still play 10 games and not get above 20,000.Some suggestions:Multiple lives (with new lives every 10,000 points) would help offset some of the randomness. Infected mushrooms being consumed when a centipede hits them would also be good. At the moment, a scorpion creating some infected mushrooms in a bad spot can essentially wipe you out. Maybe letting the player move through the edge of the screen and come out the other side (Asteroids-style) would make it easier to get around.Some sort of smart bomb centred on the player might also be good.At the moment, explosions seem to obscure what is happening so you can't see centipede segments that are still active after you've done some shooting, meaning you can't know whether you have killed it off completely.

_childDocuments_.review: So some mobile devs saw  and said, hey, we've seen that "vaporwave" art the kids love, and Atari doesn't care what happens to their IPs nowadays, so let's churn out a knockoff! Whereas  &  iterated on and blew up the original's gameplay in supremely satisfying ways, though,  didn't really care about that "gameplay" thing and as such broke the original in several ways.  Namely: a) The playfield is way larger than the original, yet your shots have been slowed and take too long to travel the playfield to control the increased enemy hordes.  b) Aiming is  persnickety, and shots have to be pinpoint accurate to hit  -  good luck with that, given that one of the few ways this game is faithful to the original is the trackball mechanics and the attendant slipslidy movement (analog stick only here; sorry, no d-pad).  c) The mushrooms take more hits to kill and are  to get rid of given the slower shot speed and tiny hitboxes, leading to numerous scenarios where I am unloading and unloading into a centipede that's  of my face and not hitting it, because the first segment I hit turned into the Masada of mushrooms, the Krak des Chevaliers of mushrooms.  d) The playfield never clears out the garbage that accumulates, and the devs like to spawn scorpions every five seconds that spawn adamantium poison mushrooms that you're not able to hit reliably over the super-wide playfield.  Hey, everyone's favorite part of  is when all the enemies are bunched up on the bottom third of the screen, right?  That's what everyone loves.You do get power-ups  -  you pretty much  to be running a power-up constantly to survive  -  but they're not as fun or satisfying as, say, the screen-sweeping laser beams or giant ghost-squashing Pac-Men of .  By far the most useful are the explosive bullets, since their AoE nullifies the aiming/tiny hitbox problems and will help get rid of the 256,000 poison mushrooms littering your screen 60 seconds in.  Ditto the spread gun, though the smaller 3-shot variant still tends to miss a lot.  The railgun is useless.  Side cannons have potential but can't hit due to the aiming.  Rapid fire actually should have been default shot speed  -  see, that's the thing with these "'70s arcade games reimagined" projects: you have to go bigger & bolder, on both the enemy side  the player's.  You can't leave the player less equipped to deal with things than they were in the original. Also: the fun sound effects and changing palettes of the original are completely absent.  WTF?I used "mobile" at the top as shorthand for "cheap and thoughtless," but  really is designed for mobile sensibilities  -  given the length of the average game and content available, you're really not expected to be spending more than an hour & change on this.  I'll probably continue to screw around with , because I love  and will continue trying futilely to get mileage out of this broke-ass version and am fundamentally stupid.  Those smarter should just get  and hit up the rock-solid originals instead. Yeah, came to my senses and asked for a refund.  Every death is cheap.  This game just really frustrates attempts to have fun with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Centipede: Recharged is a genuine remake/remaster of the original arcade shooter, Centipede.  The graphics got a minor update, switching to neon style 2D vector art instead of the old pixelcrap (in fairness, pixels were the best the computers at the time were capable of, but no excuses today).  The big plus here is mouse control, giving you a way smoother and more responsive capability.  So another reason indie devs who fail to take advantage of PC hardware have no excuses. Anyway this is still a very shallow arcade game by today's standards (we've got games like Baldur's Gate 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 to compare this to), and the pricing is just an insult to fans of arcade games and modern PC gamers alike. On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was only 7 players.  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 120 million gamers on Steam and well over 50,000 games for gamers to choose from, the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected.Centipede: Recharged has the utterly unrealistic price of around $9 USD, it's not worth it given you can play Centipede and it's many clones for free on the web, especially considering the sheer number of completely free, much higher quality games on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: "Centipede: Recharged" is a neon-infused nostalgia trip that takes the classic bug-squishing action and cranks it up to eleven. Armed with a laser cannon, you blast through waves of centipedes and other creepy-crawlies in a dazzling, chaotic rave of color and sound.The gameplay is addictive and frantic, with power-ups dropping like candy from a piñata. Whether you're slowing down time or unleashing a spread shot, each power-up makes you feel like an insect-squashing demigod. The pulsating 80s synthwave soundtrack keeps your adrenaline pumping, and the zaps and booms of your laser are music to your ears.While the action can get overwhelmingly hectic, leading to moments of bewildered frustration, it's all part of the fun. "Centipede: Recharged" is a delightful, high-energy romp that will keep you glued to your screen and questioning your sanity. Happy hunting!Note:Overall my experience playing the game was good... but I did have some issues playing it on my SteamDeck.

_childDocuments_.review: Great sounds, crisp visuals, and addictive play. Exactly what you want out of a remake. You have all the feeling of an arcade cabinet (for us olds that used them) while having a fully modern SHMUP experience. The power-ups keep it interesting as it leads to different and more complex strategies. I am very addicted to the challenges as they really stretch your comfort with the game play and keep it fresh when you have a rough arcade run. It has probably been a decade since a not-RPG got me to rack up this many hours in a game so quickly. The added mouse support works really well and I appreciate the varied input options in general since it allows more people to play. Excited to see what else we will get out of the Atari Recharged series if this is our first taste.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, this was my favorite game in arcades and on my Atari growing up, so I am STOKED that it has been remade.  This version takes what is an amazing retro game and puts a "modern" feel to it, and I love it.  The mechanics are great and I love the different challenge modes it has too.  The music is also quite enjoyable to listen to, which is an amazing addition.  I have been putting timers up every time I play so that I don't just play it endlessly.  I can't wait for more games from this same group to be released.  I also love that you can reach out to the developer (Adamvision Studios) when you have issues and they get resolved quickly and without push-back.  It's always nice to have a developer that is so devoted to making sure their game(s) is working properly. 10/10 DO recommend for anyone that loves score chasing games.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: a Fun and Challenging throwback to the arcade days of Centipede in Pizza shops, arcades, skating rinks and bowling alleys.  the new challenges and powerups add a lot more to the game and the randomized powerup drops definitely can make the game more fun (or frustrating) the leaderboards also provide a good method of competing with your friends and random players worldwide.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: I find it so hard to understand why this game has so many negative reviews. I personally am loving it, I like the Modernised gameplay with the brutal push as far as you can go. I did originally experience issues with the controller, as described by other reviews, but then I remembered that this is steam and tried it in big picture mode (it was fine).
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more like Pac-Man DX Championship Edition with the retro neon look and gameplay changes that rewards completing challanges than playing long for a high score, so be warned if you're expecting this to be like the arcade original (it's not).It's decent to play but not as great as Tempest 4000, but for $10 I won't complain.  You only get one life so you must master the powerups obtained from the spider, especially when you quickly get swarmed by poisoned centipedes.If you like challanges and getting achivements then get this version, any purists who wants the original arcade gameplay would be better off playing the arcade version off Atari Vault which plays way faster.BTW... They finally added mouse support, but you have to enable it in the Settings menu AND unplug your gamepad.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Another fun game. I think I enjoyed the Recharged version of Missile Command just a little bit more, but this is still good. There's the expected arcade mode, and also a challenge mode with various tasks to complete (get X points, destroy X mushrooms, etc.). It also has local co-op.Overall, I enjoyed this and am looking forward to Black Widow: Recharged. I would love to see VR versions of this line of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Initiate insect extermination in this widescreen glow-up of one of the greatest arcade games of all time. The rules are the same as 1981: shoot the centipedes as they descend the playing field, and contend around the shot-blocking and path-altering mushrooms they leave behind. New to Centipede: Recharged are power-ups dropped by the spiders, such as explosive bullets, spread shots, and a devastating railgun. Fight for high scores in Arcade mode either solo or with a new simultaneous couch co-op feature. Tackle more than two dozen challenges that test bug-shooting prowess and introduce clever uses for the new powerups, with additional challenges exclusive to the Atari VCS. Take it to the next level with global leaderboards for the best records in the world, and earn more than 15 achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

name: Abyss
detailed_description: The earth is being invaded by foreign creatures, and you are the only one able to save the planet earth. Use the same technology as the invaders, against them, and work together with probably the world's dumbest scientists to save the entire planet. Receive the technology weapon from the scientists, and fight the invaders in a level-based, FPS (first-person shooter), 3D game, to protect the earth. But be careful, the invaders are pretty aggressive. In the level-based game mode, you can casually walk around on an invaded planet, earth. You can be unlucky and meet some invaders who will most likely destroy you, or you can take a nap in one of the buildings in the game. No pressure... It's only the entire planet depending on your fighting skills. May 1 2022 Update: New boss, unlimited levels, speedruns and much more.

short_description: Take on the greatest futuristic, apocalypse adventure with Abyss.Are you ready to save the world, from the invading creatures? Prove it in Abyss, by Axid Studios.

_childDocuments_.review:
Explore the abyss!

Earth, 3024.

Natural resources are scarce and the survival of the human race is in danger. Desperate to find new energy resources, the ASAN creates a biomechanical robot called Nep2no that is capable of withstanding extreme depths in the hope of finding new energy sources. After many years of exploration, a new energy source is found, code named "Gaia".

Your mission will be to find the "Gaia" energy stones by exploring the depths. To do so, you must control Nep2no by counteracting gravity and the surrounding darkness with the aid of a Light that will go out little by little.
_childDocuments_.name: Abyss

name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery
detailed_description: Feature List • Paint, sketch, and retouch your artwork to complete your masterpiece and your memories • Dive into and explore beautiful panoramic, hand-animated worlds inspired by Miyazaki/Studio Ghibli visuals • Experience an evocative story, through the eyes of a passionate artist • Step into a new painter’s artistic adventure - awaiting those who complete the main story About the Game Behind the Frame is a vivid, interactive fiction about an aspiring artist on the cusp of finishing the final piece of her gallery submission. A relaxing, eloquent experience that can be played at any pace. Become immersed in a panoramic world filled with resplendent colors, beautiful hand-animated visuals, and a smooth, easy-listening soundtrack. As a passionate artist, seek the missing colors that will bring your paintings to life - all while remembering to take the occasional coffee and breakfast breaks that keep you going. There is more than what meets the eye, for every painting has a story to tell.
about_the_game: Behind the Frame is a vivid, interactive fiction about an aspiring artist on the cusp of finishing the final piece of her gallery submission. There is more than what meets the eye, for every painting has a story to tell.
short_description: Guide brush strokes and solve a variety of puzzles to help an aspiring artist complete her masterpiece amid her brusque neighbor’s gaze and his pesky cat. As her painting starts to take shape, uncover an emotional tale of chance and artistry revealed behind unrelated yet familiar moments.

_childDocuments_.review: For a short game (I beat it in 1 hour) the game is beautiful and has beautiful music. The story of two people in love is told here, in a very different way than I have seen before! The puzzles are simple yet creative, and I was engrossed in the whole thing and didn't notice how I finished it.I highly recommend playing it yourself!
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This was a beautiful gaming experience, the music and relaxing atmosphere really soothed my mood and set a tone for my day. So, developers, thank you for that. Only note that I may leave is a very obvious one, I wish we could have had more say in the storytelling, as the player, but nothing that soured my play-through. The ending was unexpected but still nice. I would say definitely get the DLC for an interesting prospective, that sort of "finishes the scene off."  If the developers were to add more DLC to this game, I believe I would get those, as well. I am not so interested in just the music for DLC, but I am glad it is offered for anyone who may want it. The music really does set the tone for the game. Really? the audio period. Is an important element of the cozy feel to this particular experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Holy heck, this game gave me all the feels in such a beautiful and amazing way. Completely worth getting. I had seen this at the E3/Gameshow and knew I would want this game. If you love Studio Ghibli or Studio Ghibli inspired works/games, please play this. Absolutely worth every penny and then some. This game is short and sweet. There are a couple puzzles, but even if you aren't someone who enjoys puzzle games, I still recommend this game for the story and art alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: I will become the two thousand and fiftieth review, maybe, no idea how quickly stats update, which is also my first review on Steam so that's fun. Ignoring that and talking about the game itself it's very much more akin to a playable movie or art piece as you try to piece together the story as it evolves. The visuals are beautiful and the soundtrack compliments it with The Color You Love The Most being a very dazzling song while capturing the emotions of the game perfectly. It's a heartwarming experience with a bit of a bittersweet feel. Certainly something I feel is worth experiencing as the price is quite fair too. Though admittedly it's a short game roughly an hour maybe some more if you struggle with the light puzzle elements. You can wait for a slight sale, but also when you compare it to the price of a movie, which this is more a visual delight than a mechanic heavy game, I'd say it's not overly expensive.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, especially if you are a fan of things done in the style of studio Ghibli's works.  It's a reasonably simple puzzle game that you will likely be able to progress through without needing to look up solutions.  The story, music, and artwork are all wonderful.It took me approximately 90 minutes to full clear the game and achievements moving at a relaxed pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely beautiful game. I was looking for a comfy game to play and came across this gem. It's not normally my type of game but I gave it ago since it only takes just over an hour to finish and it was amazing. Beautiful art style, similar to Studio Ghibli. The animation was gorgeous.This game needs to be more recognised!Definitely pick it up and finish it. I had a bunch of theories on what was happening the more I played but the ending was, as with everything else in the game, beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Behind the frame is a fantastic game. The story is the game's star as it slowly unravels and you try to figure out what is happening. Despite the repetitiveness in certain spots, they somehow made those tasks like making breakfast fun. I shed a few tears at the end because it reminded me of my fiance and myself. While obviously not the same, there are many parallels. The moral of the story is never give up on someone you love, as Jack did. It's one of the few games I'm looking forward to playing again after fully understanding the story. Definitely a game everyone should play.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Narrative storytelling at it's absolute best! This is a stunning visual novel.  It's casual, simple, succinct, engaging, has fantastic music and spectacular art direction/animation. I downloaded this out of curiosity and to take a break from my heavier RPG oriented adventure gaming and was pleasantly surprised. While the puzzles are simple, what really grabs you is the story. No spoilers here, but suffice to say the desire for discovery drew me in to keep playing. The payoff on this is pure gold. Tightly written, meaningful and fun.  It will hit you in the feels. It is short and sweet in the best way. I recommend this to everyone. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only game to date that I have ever went back to 100% the achievements, partially because I loved the game so much I wanted to reach 2 hours so I could buy items from the point shop. The mechanics were easy to understand and straight forward. If you're a veteran to point and click games you'll understand it immediately, but bit of a learning curve that lasts ten seconds if you're new. The puzzles were at just a high enough difficulty that it makes you think but just easy enough to allow yourself to be engrossed into the visuals and metaphors laid ahead of you. Although a shorter game, I don't mind especially since they used that to polish the mechanics and coding to near perfection, runs beautifully and the transition to different sections of the game are smoother than waxed ceramic.Oh the art, oh my god THE ART! from the animated cutscenes to the backgrounds and interact-ables this game shows a type of perfection I like to call replicated nature. The rooms are messy and unkempt, the nature messy and wild, but you could clearly tell that it was all on purpose, the purpose being to represent life, people and mother earth. The details of rust on the sink, the color shift of the dried paint blended beautifully with digitally illustrated cell shaded characters. Everything goes together well and feels like a spiritual successor to ghibli's Howl's moving Castle. Which of course, showed the same methods of oil painted surroundings and cell shaded animation and color theory. I went out of my way to buy and download both of the art books' pdfs and the absolute GENIUS to make the background on a panorama! I'm unaware of current game develop technology and how it would work but I imagine that it was difficult to make such detailed work warp. Another comment about the art books is the how both   As a freelance artist myself this game hit hard. The mc is the type of person I aspire to be, in personality, life style and hope, this game may even inspire my next vtuber model design. I don't share her medium due to being a digital artist, and how oil painting is such an expensive endeavor it is if you don't make much and it isn't your true aspiration. When I played this and the dlc on my live stream it left such a mark in me I was utterly speechless. My brain stopped working and for a moment I was nor longer an entertainer. I had to stop my stream soon after to process my thoughts, never has a video game hit me like this. I MISSED small meaningful passion games that don't require 100 endings or tons of chores to keep track of. I miss how... humble...games could feel. If I had anyone in my life that cared about this type of media I would talk their ear off about this game. After I'm done writing this review I'm going to go check out what other games and media silver lining studios have in store. I know there won't be a sequel, the story is done and this doesn't feel like the type of game to need one. But I desperately want to find merch on this, I beg!art and creative direction 10/10Story 9.5/10   -0.5 premise was a llliiitttttlllleeee predictableMusic and Sound 9/10 -1 had to go back and edit my audio settings a few too many times due to how loud everything was.(i'm just a little salty dw dw)mechanics and game play- 9.5/10 -0.5 wish I could alter my audio settings mid game, and the painting had to be a little too exact for my taste.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: What looks like a simple phone game hits you right in the gut with its beautiful story. With a beautiful soundtrack and graphics, grab a cup of tea and get cozy. And bring a box of tissues. The puzzles are a perfect balance (at least for me) of difficulty, where they weren't too easy, but weren't so challenging that I was struggling too bad. While not a very long game, you'll enjoy every second of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so underrated! Very well thought out and the art style is super pretty, not to mention the soundtrack is one of the best I've heard and I'm in love with the ending song. It's a short game with a simple story but told in a way that tugs your heartstrings and makes you wonder what will and could have happened. Highly recommend!!
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is short, it effectively packs an emotional experience within its 1.5-hour length. The animation and scenery are beautifully done. The music fits every scene nicely. Lastly, the gameplay elements are charming, and none of the puzzles were annoying to solve.I highly recommend buying this game at full price. I am very excited to see more games from this developer. They are showing a lot of potential with this first title!
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to art, story, and atmosphere. I put on my headphones and just felt my anxieties melt away as my eyes and ears feasted on this beautiful, peaceful and inspired game. After years of botching stickpeople drawings, it was very satisfying to "create" beautiful art in this game. It's a short story with few achievements, but honestly the immersion was so well done that I have replayed it twice through already and will probably go for a third run in due course. In my opinion, if you enjoy peaceful, story-driven games with light puzzle elements, and like to replay games, this is worth the modest price tag, especially to support the team that brought us this game. I hope to see more in the future.Some tips for playing: I thought I was solving some puzzles incorrectly, but it turns out I had the right solution, I am just terrible at 'drawing' with a mouse and the game didn't properly register my terribly uneven lines. I recommend playing on a touchscreen device with your finger or a stylus to avoid any solution confusion. Definitely take your time with this game, it's best enjoyed when you allow yourself to soak in everything it has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful storytelling and illustrations albeit somewhat of short play through. The atmospheric music suited each chapter as the story progressed. I thoroughly enjoyed it and wanted more, but the Jack DLC (which is free) at the end of the main story was a very nice surprise. A slow-paced casual puzzle game - perfect for a lazy Sunday.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting little story focused adventure game about some painters. The story is much more important and fleshed out than the gameplay which is really simple. The story is actually really nice as you try to figure out who the characters are and why the world around you changes. It takes a simple narrative and twists it into a scenario where you really feel for the characters. The way the game messes with the environment also really helps a lot. The first half really has some ambiguity and interpretation of how you see the characters while the second half rounds the characters off. Overall, an actual good story in a decent game. Get it on sale since it's like 90 mins.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: I did not enjoy this game.It was too short (at least you're quickly done with it, not sure if it's a bad point) and the 'story' (if there was even one ?) relies on a single 'twist' that you can easily guess in the very first minutes you play the game.And that's pretty much all.. The 'gameplay' is tedious, the puzzles can barely be named as suchThe dialog is pointless and almost non-existent.At least there is something like 4 different tracks of music which are a bit cozy.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Even considering this is an "artistic game", the gameplay is just boring. The puzzles are toddler level and the painting parts are just a glorified version of A Little to the Left's hints. It's also extremely slow, as they force you to wait between each line before you can click to continue. If you're a fast reader, get ready to spam click impatiently.There's also a few bugs, it stopped playing cutscenes completely at some point and I had to restart.The story is cute I guess but very predictable yet doesn't make sense. You can see they tried to go into the supernatural but there is no explanation whatsoever. It ends up feeling like they're trying to trick you into believing it's more than just the most boring and cliché story, but they couldn't come up with anything original.The achievements make no sense at all, to the point where there is no way you could get them without a guide (why would you click 11 times on something that gives the same flavour text every time and have you wait a couple seconds between each click?)I finished it out of spite, but even if you have it because it was in a bundle or something, it's not even worth playing in my opinion. That's 2 hours I had to waste and I regret wasting it on this.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: That was... extremely underwhelming. The story was rather boring and didn't actually bring any answers? With the reviews this had gotten I would have thought the game would have been at least a little bit more interesting than this, but it really was... meh. Roughly an hour long and in my opinion not worth the price. Maybe if it's on super sale it could be worth buying but I honestly wouldn't recommend it to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: A terrific little vignette of an aspiring artist in the city. There's lots to love here. Great music, some interesting puzzles, amazing art that is both cozy and evocative, a well told story with lots of hidden depth. This is a pretty easygoing game to relax to and explore at your leisure. It's pretty short even for 9-10 bucks which might be the only shortfall, maybe an hour and a half, two if you want to find everything, but it's quality over quantity here. If you like artsy games, point and click, or just something very chill, this is a good one to pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Nice fun little game, story was intriguing and heartwarming and the music was delightful :3 I enjoyed it very muchAs a thought tho, I think it would be kinda fun if at the end of the play through there was a blank canvas for one to maybe choose to paint on freely :3 I feel like that could be used by the layers to have a bit of fun. Or make masterpieces with lols
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Regret is the sweet dream of things that were and could've been. Sometimes bitter, sometimes sour, sometimes salty, but always sweet until it isn't. Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery is an unexpectedly mature game. Not mature in the 'let's discuss dark topics' sense but mature in the wizened 'I intimately understand this topic' sense. I had my suspicions midway into the game but the free Jack DLC more or less confirmed it. Jack and Amber  Very brief game but well worth the time spent. Heartily recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Very unimaginative and underwhelming. An interactive movie at best. The story pretends to be deep but it's nothing more than an uninspired cliché with flat characters. For a painting-inspired game it feels like a cheap escape room with repetitive, boring mechanics and no room for creativity. The achievements are illogical and designed to extend the length of the game. On top of that, it's full of text bugs that cause the screen to freeze too often, turning a supposedly relaxing experience into a frustrating one.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into point and click adventure games from a mechanical point of view primarily, this might not be the game for you. The puzzles are not complex, the game is not long. However, the story is what makes this game and the technical work done to put the player into a Ghibli style animation/illustration story well worth the play through.I recommend play through this twice, play through it the first time, focus on just completing the game and finding out the story. Once you know the story, take a break, play again and take time to really look around. The enviroment is very impressive from a technical standpoint of seeing parts of the background move like you're living in that animation. There's also some enivromental storytelling you may miss because of lack of context to first time around.The story is really good, again it's not complex, but it's a story that I think a lot of people can relate with. A story about what-ifs and missed chances.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Behind the Frame is a very charming little game, not what I would usually consider my cup of coffee, but definitely worth the price (especially since the price is so ridiculously low). It is short, yes, but the experience you get is one of a kind, and considering the effort that had to be put into creating the visuals, I wouldn't blame the devs for asking more than that. And they don't.Admittedly, the story is rather predictible ("I got the twist before the game even started hinting at it and it's not because I'm so smart" kind of predictible) but it can squeeze some real emotions out of you.Lastly, if you buy it, finish it, and then refund it because it's so short - yes, you do not, in fact, have a soul :DBetter spend your days as best as you can, because when this is over, not even hell awaits you :D
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This is just like the Nancy Drew mystery PC games I used to grow up playing, but with a romantic storyline filled with gorgeous artwork and design. It may have been a short play to completion, but there was so much detail and thought put into the game. It's absolutely worth the purchase and playtime!
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art and animationBeautiful soundtrackBeautiful storyThis game made me feel something and made me think about life.Negatives: - Has a bug with german subtitles for every cinematic twice that lets the subtitle stay for like 30 seconds and freeze the game for that time where you're unable to click anything / progress. English subtitles seemed to be free of that.- No anti aliasing option, so the beautiful curtains swinging with the wind have ugly aliasing pixel stairs.- Cinematics are reused- You can't mix violet from blue and red in this artistic painting game- Unnecessary missable achievements like "click that thing for 11 times"However, I do recommend this game for a short heartfelt story session.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: I can't in full conscience not recommend this game, because it is beautiful and fun, but it's almost obscenely short and easy for this price. It's like something that would've been a free Flash project back in the day. Also, the more it happens, the more I dislike the tendency of everything having a darker twist or a hidden meaning to it these days. Can't I play a cozy, feel-good game for once, damn it?Actually, I got the feeling that this game is about  As an aside, I kind of see it working well as an Ib/Garry sequel to the original Ib. Oh well.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Saw this randomly in the store and loved the ghibli style I decided to pick it up. Its a cute game! I wish it was a little longer but it was only cheap so I don't think it would be fair to ask for more. A lovely story with beautiful animations and scenery and simple puzzles to keep you engaged. I really enjoyed winding down after work with this, I'd recommend it if you're looking for a relaxing short game before bed. The music is real nice too :)
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: I love the art style in the game and how the colors made the artwork come to life. The story was simple yet had emotion. The game did a good job at keeping you wondering what was going to happen next. Solving mini puzzles to advanced the story was also a nice touch. While the game is on the shorter side, the price did reflect that, which I appreciated. The devs also created a free chapter to the game without any additional cost to users that owned the game already which was a nice touch.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Behind the Frame is a bittersweet and cute little game. The art style is lovely and the puzzles are straightforward and easy to complete. This is more of an emotional story game than anything else. At first, I thought our protagonist was a slightly creepy voyeur who liked to peer into her elderly neighbor's window and draw him while watching him live his life, but really this story is about life, loss, and perhaps missed opportunities.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful,. A powerful story told by gorgeous art and cutscenes and a wonderful soundtrack! This game redefines just how visual a visual novel can be, and doesn't let the adventure of an adventure game get in the way of a good story. A bit on the easy side, but the gameplay is more for immersion than any sort of satisfaction you would get from a normal game. It is also a bit short but it is what it is and doesn't stay any longer than need be. Stellar work!
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This game was pretty... short. It's fine, I like how the environment was rendered. It's a 3D space but the art style gives it that 2d visual novel feel. The story, like all art, seems up for interpretation. I hit a bug near the end of the main story but going back to the home screen and going in again seemed to fix it. My main concerns were how sometimes the subtitles disappear before I finished reading them and the couple of minor bugs present. (And according to the guides I was looking at I should have all the achievements but something is still locked.) I still like the game overall, and it's up to the individual whether this short story game will be worth it to them.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Behind the Frame is the kind of game that makes me feel feelings... And I love it for thatI've always had a fondness of story's like the ones in this game. A choice not taken, A path not chosen. It makes me weak and makes me think of my own life.I can highly recommend the game to those that just want to relax and enjoy a story!It is not the most indepth gameplay, but the story and artstyle make it worth it. I highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: In 2020, during the heartache of the pandemic, I found myself contemplating the fleeting nature of memory more deeply than ever before. Days stretched long and lonely, filled with a sadness that seemed to permeate everything. In those moments, it was my books, my dear younger sister and mommy and the comforting presence of my former boyfriend who held me close. There lingered an anxious fear within me, a fear that the moments shared with loved ones might slip away into the ether of forgetfulness. The uncertainty of life weighed heavily on me, whispering doubts about my own worthiness, that I wasn't good enough, never capable enough, always falling short.From the days of my childhood to this very day, I've always kept a diary close at hand. Its pages became a sanctuary where I poured out my heart's troubles and joys, albeit I don't see myself writing as often as I used to. Though my artistic talents may be humble, I found solace in sketching alongside my written thoughts. These creations, both words and drawings, became etched into my heart. Nowadays, in quiet evenings, I find myself drawn back to those cherished pages, reliving moments through scents, sights, and the faded photographs I've collected over the years. It's easy to get caught up in the rush of life, but these memories anchor us, reminding us of who we are and where we've come from.Discovering "Behind the Frame" felt like stumbling upon a kindred spirit. Its gentle narrative, exploring the lives of two artists, resonated deeply with me. Despite its brief duration, the game left an indelible mark on my heart, a reminder of the beauty found in creation and connection. As I played, tears welled in my eyes. Yes, there was sadness in Amber's story, but it served as a poignant reminder. Our memories are treasures to be nurtured, for those we love remain with us always, guiding us from the unseen realms of heaven. Though they may be gone from our sight, their presence is felt in every beat of our hearts. So let us cherish each moment, for our memories are the threads that bind us to those we hold dear, now and forevermore.

I'd say give the full game a try even if you didn't like the demo. It gets better. Worst case scenario you can always refund it. But please don't, if you like the game. Some games I play for 100 hours and they do nothing.There is one issue with the game - all the story is told trough subtitles. But they appear while you're doing stuff, and during anime cutscenes. _childDocuments_.review: - I like that the game creates a cozy atmosphere with its laid-back music and hand-painted backgrounds (not a big surprise, considering that painting is the main theme here). It was also interesting to watch the story unfold, since even though it seems very simple, some unexpected things happen around the middle of the game.- It was rather short. It has six chapters but it can be finished in less than 90 minutes. Not a big issue however, if you look at the price of slightly above 8€.- The gameplay elements are REALLY basic. There are some tasks you do around the apartment like making coffee or writing up a CV, which you do multiple times over the first few chapters. Thankfully the game occasionally switches it up with painting-based puzzles, but then those are also rather easy. There is definitely more focus on the story than the gameplay and even that seems to only have a symbolic purpose- The ending felt a bit underwhelming. I'm not heartless enough to claim that it didn't make me feel happy for the main characted, but again it was a basic feeling, maybe summarized by saying "Oh, is that where this was going? Ok, good for you."Overall, if you are looking for a "game" game, you probably won't get much out of this, as it's basically a visual novel with some basic puzzles. However, if you have a free evening during which you want to relax and experience a short story that leaves you with a warm feeling inside, I'd say check it out, especially for this price.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing Puzzle ExperienceAs a puzzle game, this title has left me quite disappointed. Here are the main issues I encountered during my playthrough:1. Too Short for Its PriceFor a game priced like this, the gameplay is far too short. I was expecting a more substantial puzzle-solving experience, but I finished the game very quickly, making it feel not worth the cost.2. Clunky Screen Transitions and Hard-to-Reach CluesWhen searching for clues, the screen transitions are often not smooth, and some clues are extremely difficult to reach. This lack of smooth operation severely affects the game's immersion, making it seem like the game design lacks finesse and attention to detail.3. Unengaging StorylineWhile I can understand that the game attempts to convey a sense of regret and leaves some things to the imagination, the current execution is far from satisfactory. There is not enough buildup for the regrets of the main characters, making the story feel very disjointed. Players are left feeling confused and unable to empathize with the characters. This emotional disconnect makes the story bland and unengaging.4. Lack of Colorful VisualsConsidering that one of the game's selling points is its art, the use of color is insufficient. The color palette in the game did not meet my expectations; it felt very monotonous and lacked visual impact. I hope the development team will put more effort into this aspect and improve the game's visual quality.Overall, this game falls short in several areas and does not meet expectations. I hope the developers will take player feedback seriously and make improvements.
