_childDocuments_.review: Introduction:"Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery" is a beautifully crafted indie game that delves into the world of artistry, offering a unique blend of puzzle-solving and emotional storytelling. Developed by a talented team, this game invites players to step into the shoes of an aspiring artist and embark on a journey filled with creativity, mystery, and personal growth.Gameplay:At its core, "Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery" is a puzzle-adventure game where players guide the brush strokes of the protagonist while helping her navigate through various challenges. As you explore the artist's cozy apartment, you'll encounter a brusque neighbor and his mischievous cat, adding an element of intrigue and subtle humor to the experience.The gameplay primarily revolves around solving puzzles that range from simple logic challenges to more intricate tasks related to painting and artistic expression. These puzzles seamlessly integrate with the narrative, offering a sense of purpose and immersion. The controls are intuitive and responsive, making it easy to manipulate the artist's tools and interact with the environment.Artistic Expression and Narrative:What sets "Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery" apart is its emphasis on artistic expression and storytelling. As you progress through the game, the artist's painting gradually takes shape, representing her personal journey and emotions. This visual metaphor beautifully intertwines with the narrative, which unveils an emotional tale of chance encounters and hidden connections between unrelated yet familiar moments.The storytelling is poignant, evoking a range of emotions from joy and curiosity to introspection and empathy. The dialogue is well-written and engaging, effectively capturing the personalities of the characters and their evolving relationships. The game also cleverly uses environmental details and subtle visual cues to enhance the narrative, immersing players in the artist's world.Visuals and Sound Design:Visually, "Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery" is a treat for the eyes. The hand-painted art style exudes charm and elegance, reminiscent of traditional watercolor illustrations. The attention to detail in each scene is remarkable, creating a cozy atmosphere that draws players into the artist's surroundings. From the vibrant colors to the delicate brushwork, the game's visuals are a true work of art.Complementing the stunning visuals is a soothing soundtrack that captures the essence of the game's tranquil setting. The music gracefully accompanies the gameplay, immersing players in a serene and contemplative ambiance. Additionally, the sound effects and voice acting are of high quality, further enhancing the overall immersion.Conclusion:"Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery" is a captivating and introspective journey that seamlessly blends art, puzzles, and storytelling. Through its unique gameplay mechanics, players are invited to explore the world of an aspiring artist, unraveling a heartfelt narrative filled with emotion and personal growth. With its stunning visuals, engaging puzzles, and evocative soundtrack, this indie gem offers an experience that will leave a lasting impression on both art enthusiasts and gamers alike.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Roughly 2h to 100%, it's a beautifully short game. Obviously the references to Ghibli are pretty strong and mentioned quite often in other reviews, but it really does fall in line with that style. This game is very reminiscent of Hiromasa Yonebayashi's works and I absolutely love it for that.The gameplay is quite simple, point and click areas around the rooms and a painting minigame are the majority of what you need to do alongside a few simple puzzles. A few easy to miss achievements but not a hassle at all to replay for. For being such a short tale it still gives that punch-to-the-gut "who's cutting onions?" feeling, again akin to Maro's film work in the vein as Omoide no Marnie/When Marnie Was There - a highly impressive feat for this studio. I really hope this development studio creates more projects in the future as the storytelling and animation is absolutely beautiful. My only complaints is I wish it were so much longer; I am so sad that it's already over. Behind the Frame is an absolutely lovely game.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: During a few scenes I was afraid I'm going to cringe at the conclusion of the game, expecting it to get a bit too cliche, but the overall payoff was great. It's a very short, cute experience that starts cosy, then turns a bit surreal and dark, then once again wholesome. A tiny adventure.It's fascinating to observe the developers' decisions on how to use their limited budget and time. Some moments are meant to hit the hardest and have detailed highly stylized illustrations, properly timed ambient and music, fancy character animations, and a sense of style, while others are trying to just get things done as cheaply as they can without getting jarring. If the studio were to get a huge pile of money, I have no doubt they would turn it into a Visual Novel classic. That's why I really hope that the community actually keeps the game on their accounts instead of refunding it. Let's reward the artists for their effort.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so serene and ghibli-esque and an overall joy to play. The puzzles were simplistic and all colour/painting centred as it is the focal point of the game. I particularly enjoyed the references to artists throughout the game, mainly in the achievements. The art style is very reminiscent to that of Studio Ghibli and emulates the vibes perfectly. Many of the backdrops throughout the game could be interchangeable with Ghibli movies. The hues were vibrant and warm-toned to match many of the naturescapes. The actual plot of this game is so cute and well done for such a short game. Using paintings as plot devices was a very clever and fitting way of storytelling. The story itself is straight out of a ghibli movie with the ending being the best part of the game. The ending was perfectly done and encapsulates what many girls want. This is a perfect game for anyone who loves ghibli movies with the game itself sharing similarities to The Wind Rises (the good parts) and Howl's Moving Castle. The story is beautiful, the art and animation is absolutely stunning and the music is gorgeous. It’s a great story that definitely made me cry and I think if this was just a short animation film… I would’ve appreciated this so much more.The issue is that this is not a game. At best it’s an interactive film, and for the price and the amount of “gameplay” there is, it really isn’t worth it, especially because you can complete the whole story in less than 2 hours (maybe this was intentional so that people could instantly refund on steam as soon as they finished the story, jk pls don’t do this). The gameplay also consists of repetitive motions that are more mindless actions as opposed to actual gameplay, they are so tedious and personally, any “gameplay” I did ruined the flow of the story for me. I’d be invested in the story and trying to figure out what was going to happen next when bam, they threw in a random “puzzle”, if it can even be called that? The “puzzles” are so basic and easy even my dumba** with one brain cell was able to figure it out at 3am. They’re just more tedious tasks I need to finish in order to unlock more story and animations. The thing that honestly confirmed I couldn’t recommend this game was yet again another gameplay issue. SPOILER ALERT WARNING (not heavy, I’m just describing the “gameplay” and what frustrated me to no end):At one point in the game where  and I’m not even joking or exaggerating when I say that it legit took me 15 minutes to complete this “puzzle” because the margin for error was so low… I had to look up a walkthrough of the game just so I could find the correct placement and how exactly they wanted me to draw in order to get past this stupid part. This was at a super emotional point in the story as well and this just absolutely ruined any immersion I had in the story because I was frustrated and annoyed for 15 minutes with this stupid task that I couldn’t get past for the life of me. So, TLDR: If this was a short film I would have rated it an 11/10. As a game though, it’s like a 4/10 due to the horrendous “gameplay” and tedious tasks that brought no joy to my poor heart that just wanted to witness a beautiful story ;-;

_childDocuments_.review: It's a beautiful yet sad and emotional story mostly told by memories brought up by beautiful paintings. Definitely made my eyes tear up at the end. Also, don't forget to play Jack's DLC after you finish by clicking on his name under the title's name. I almost missed that.  All in all, a great story, simple enough "puzzles" to help you progress and beautiful animations very Ghibli-esque.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Cute Ghibli style, perfect atmosphere, visuals and music that tells a compelling and interactive story. The perfect unravelling of the primary story followed up by the dlc told a story that evoked two waterfalls down my eyes. It's a very linear game, that took about two hours, which propels the storytelling but doesn't present replay-ability other than achievement farming, but I definitely feel like I got my money's worth.But most importantly...THE CATS!! Best part of the game, hands down.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Even though this game is short, it's worthwhile. As soon as you press play, you know, you just do, that there is an emotional story happening on your screen. A deep human emotion. As soon as you can put the story together, it hits you. Very well done, with just an incredible graphic design choice. Yet another proof, that an indie game that keeps you busy for merely a few hours, can nourish your soul more than the most AAA titles that entertain you for a few hundred hours.Definitely a developer to keep an eye on.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Was gifted this through a humblebundle but would honestly have bought it. Well worth the price for the sweet short story. I'd have some tissues on hand if you find heartfelt bittersweet stories make you cry.  The art is beautiful. The puzzles were fun and fairly clever without being difficult.A sweet cozy game for a rainy afternoon.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that this game has overwhelmingly positive reviews truly baffles me. The only good thing about it are the visuals, as they are indeed quite lovely, but the rest is extremely weak; The puzzles (if can even be called such) are easy, the story is rather underwhelming and short, the music although nice is repetitive, game play is meh at best.This is an overpriced and overpraised mediocre mobile game that I would only recommend if you are into extremely effortless "puzzle" games, or if you are an achievement hunter. Otherwise, don't waste your money like I did; There are much better, engaging and cheaper games out there that will make your money and time worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Though it only took me around an hour to complete, I still enjoyed what was there.  I do think the sale price of $9.09 was still a little high considering the brevity of the game, but I do not regret buying it.  The team who made this is small, which is even more impressive.  The animation was well done, the mechanics worked well, and the story was beautiful.  The only reason you would buy this game is for the story, because there isn't much in terms of gameplay.  Nevertheless, I recommend this game for the story alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first review I've posted on Steam because of how much I enjoyed playing the game. I am a big ghibli fan, and was impressed by how beautiful the graphics were and enjoyed the touching story the game portrays. I started off playing the demo just to see if it would live up to the reviews, and it did! I loved how the music was very peaceful, and how interactive the items were in the home, from making coffee to cooking my own eggs with the ASMR included. It was a lovely 2 hours of game play on a sunny day when I was looking for something relaxing to do. I highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not only relaxing to play, the story itself is lovely. You've got puzzles to complete in order to advance the story. The music is amazing and the art style is just as good. This is definitely a shorter game, but for the price its worth it.P.S. It'll probably make you cry like it did with me
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely lovely. Beautiful art and music, easy but cute puzzles, a nice wholesome story, notably flawless translation and tiny smart Easter eggs about art history in the content, including the end titles. The first leisurely playthrough took me 1,5 hours but I think I'll tinker a little bit with the achievements yet. Considering there are much shorter games, this one is worth its price. And I bought the soundtrack, too. Should the same creators ever do anything along the lines again, I want it.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of those games that's hard to explain why it's so good without spoiling it. Suffice to say, I felt more emotional highs and surprises in the 90 minutes I spent with this than most games. It's like one of those animated art films from France or something, but you can play it. Really good stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: It's  lovely, sad, melancholic and beautiful.  The graphics though likened to studio Ghibli by others, would, in my opinion be more water colour painterly.  I guess the likening to Ghibli is the characters themselves.  I don't feel relaxed by the game. It fills me with a sense of melancholy and loss; not bad in itself if a game can stir these kinds of emotions in a player.  Life plays on even as we go about our daily life.  Art catches these moments and this game does the same with the  intimate story that is amber and Jack through actions, painting and music.  There are some puzzle aspects but overall it is a game that  you should play if you like art and definitely feeling with your story.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion it's a really boring game with way too easy "riddles". The atmosphere might be nice, but it really started to get on my nerves how monotonous the game is. The development of the game consists of doing breakfast (oh, egg and bread again, like the 3 days before too), making coffee (again and again), painting a picture, which looks like it was drawn by children. I cannot say it entertained me even a bit. It reminded me of old browser games where you can click through the whole flat story. But for 8 € it's definitely too much!
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Literally a scenery. Precious game. I feel like i watch a miyazaki movie but a little cheap version. (Spoiler)First i was taught we play as a amber but older and cant remember their past or something, than i play a bit and thinking maybe we are playing as their child, maybe we only a memory in a painting bla bla bla...And than BOM. Stupid girl married and left jack all alone. Even more bad than this jack fall in love with amber SO deeply like he never actually live his life full ! Im soooo sad and mad at this jack side ending.. I know amber want to live her life and dont have to love jack back BUT SHE CAN SAY IT TO HIM and he try to live a full life or atleast socialize with someone. He doesnt have to be die ALONE. Other than that, great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: feels like playing threw a ghibli movie; very pretty and chill game. love the overall vibe, wished I had coffee while playing xD seeing the character make coffee really made me want some. just sad that it was so short, I didn't realize how short it was. finished the entire game in 1 sitting (65 min) I wasn't even trying to play quickly or anything, I'm still kinda sad there isn't more. overall I liked it, just be aware that it is a pretty short game.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Really, REALLY wish I could I say I adored it. The art style, music, atmosphere and story are so up my alley that the extreme lack of content (I beat it in a hour with 20 minutes extra for achievements) and overly simple (If still effective and narratively fitting) gameplay hurts me and keep it from being something genuinely astounding like I wish it was.Despite its simplicity and length it was otherwise a wonderful little title that was absolutely worth its small price. I pray for a longer spiritual sequel.7
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fairly simple puzzle game. I'm pretty sure it was depressing, but I lost the plot somewhere (full honesty - I never had it) so I couldn't tell you exactly why it was depressing. I just know it is. Also, I've played through the entire story and only unlocked 30% of the Steam achievements...color me intrigued. I'm going to circle back eventually, probably.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Huh. All in all I really liked the feeling and the scenery this game has. It's a beautiful, relaxing thing to play and the art is just stunning. I loved finding out more about Amber and J (hopeless romantic here) and I liked that the game allowed for various theories to pop up while you were playing. HOWEVER.I am...not all that fond of the ending. Not because of the tone it had, but because it was utterly confusing. It was not exactly clear what had happened and it would have loved it to be a little less open. Not completely closed and well rounded but just a little more clear cut. The biggest question (   ) was really not answered all that well.  That left kind of a sour aftertaste, because it felt like a wasted opportunity.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a sweet, short game. It took me 1.7 hrs to complete, and part of that was it being open as I went and made myself eggs and toast (dangit game, you made me hungry!).I loved it, and it was incredibly relaxing for the most part and gets a little (tiny bit) spooky later on, but overall, just lovely. Made me realize I could definitely use a game where all you do is paint, drink coffee (tea for me, pls!) and make breakfast and look out the window. The third day - act? - was my favorite. The score was so beautiful. I loved when it rained. So cozy!If you want something that is relaxing, fun and interesting, highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Short and bittersweet like the story itself.It might have just been a case of me not fully understanding what I was buying, but this game was underwhelming. The art is quite pretty, however there just wasn't nearly enough substance to be worth even the $8 I paid for this game on sale, let alone full price. The "puzzle" tag especially feels misleading, as there is virtually no puzzling to be had, just matching pictures to other pictures.I completed the story in under 2 hours, it felt almost creepy in the middle which was not the vibe I expected, and the story wasn't exactly my cup of tea. I'm always hesitant to give a negative review, but I was disappointed and would like to prevent others from spending their money if they went in with similar expectations as me.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Lacks substance.Basically a very simple puzzle game which even I completed without any help where you have to collect different colour paint tubes in order to complete various artworks. A few of them require some cute puzzles, and the story has it's moments, but never becomes truly engaging. My trouble was that the characters are pretty detailed, but live in a world I don't, so it just never connected with me.The plot is simple, boy looses cat, starts canvassing neighbourhood; girl helps find cat. Boy then accidentally bumps into girl sometimes at coffee shop. It goes on from there quite a way, but I'm not going to spoil it for you. because it has a plot and trajectory, but it just never hit for me. I mean there are things for you to work out, and you build a picture of the timeline as you go, but I hope they release a DLC that fills in more of the timeline.I did find the game a relaxing play, but I would never pay the full price for it, it's too short, even with the JACK DLC. Mainly I liked it for the art style and the visuals which are great, but they are backed by a tired plot-line that does not hold it together. It's even fun to play the game a second time, just for the visuals. I am a bit partial so some paintbrush work myself, and found that although it's pretty easy to use a mouse to colour-by-numbers and paint inside the boxes. so anyone can play this game/story. But because it did not feel like it was hard enough to complete the "paint-by-numbers" style puzzles, each portrait lacked it's own sense of achievement. Perhaps if the images were "rendered" a bit cleaner and with more detail, it might have felt like something. No artistic skill required at all. Get it on the specials, but it's a short game.For more like it, click on my picture, or use this list
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this short story game, but it had a few areas that could be improved. The story was engaging and had a relaxing atmosphere, making it easy to get sucked in. However, I felt that the music was lacking in terms of memorability and motif. For a game that aims to evoke a certain emotional response, I think stronger music could help elevate the experience.At times, the game/animation took a little while to process, which occasionally made me feel frustrated or impatient. However, it was never long enough to significantly impact my enjoyment of the game.Overall, I would recommend this game on discount to anyone looking for a quick, relaxing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this Game at the beginning, but as it progresses Clues and direction get more muddled, no Clues, no information and trying to locate Paint Tubes has surpassed my abilities! Has taken 3 attempts and 4 hours play to arrive at a combination of Coloured arrows painted on objects and locations. Vital to crack  the Riddle and a Number Code but nothing interacts within areas available and info is zero. I hoped there may be access to a Walk through  option  or at least a Hint.  Its a no show. Too cryptic to understand
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't been truly affected by a game like I have with this one in a long time. Unpacking was a recent play that left me warm inside, but Behind the Frame is a beautiful, eloquent, well-crafted story that both makes you smile and makes you cry at the same time. I won't talk further on the plot because I feel it necessary anyone and everyone should play this as it will resonate with each individual separately. For me, I came out of this with a new appreciation for life and how I should cherish even the littlest of things; that I should live my life with my own dreams in mind and to live without regrets. I loved every second of this game even if a couple puzzles got tedious. This is up there with some of my favorite games from 2021 without question. Please, do yourself a favor and play this. Hell, tell me how it affected you as well. I want others to be able to share what the narrative left them thinking and feeling.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful short story game about 2 artists with some really simple puzzles and a stunning artstyle. Saying much more here would spoil it and I feel like it is better to just be experienced.With it only taking about an hour and half to finish with the free DLC included I would recommend picking it up from a sale/bundle as it is a pricey otherwise. I do appreciate it that they do not try to charge your for the DLC at least.Works without any issues on Linux with Proton (9.0-3).
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This is a two-hour game, made in Taiwan with Love. It has art, music, a love affair, and drama. The graphics are good, I found no bugs, and the controls were easy to use.I had to resort to a Steam Guide in one place because I couldn't find a clue which I'm sure was somewhere in the play area. In fact the Guide didn't help either, and I just clicked through various possibilities until I found the correct solution. Even having found it, it still makes no sense to me. Apart from that, the puzzles were simple and logical, and not difficult.I enjoyed the game. It is a little expensive at full price, given that it took me only two hours of play to finish it.  Replay value is limited, because much of the time taken is in figuring out the puzzles, and once you know the answers the game is just images and music.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This was a good game. Bright and colorful, Behind the Frame is a bittersweet, cozy slice of life game, that provides a warm and inviting sensory experience which kept me thoroughly engaged from start to finish. The puzzles were largely very intuitive and I was happy that I didn't need to consult a walkthrough to solve any of them - even if I did solve the hardest one by accident, lol. The story was a little predictable at times, but the journey was so immersive that I didn't really mind. I quite enjoyed this title.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: I can't even put to words how amazing this game was. Before you buy it, you should ask yourself what you expect and what you want. If you are looking for a tricky game with a lot of play-time, "Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery" might not be the right game for you. But if you're a fan of beautiful games with gorgeous graphics and a very touching story then this game is perfect for you. I enjoyed every second of it. The music, the storyline, the cat (who doesn't love cats?), THE GRAPHICS. I didn't feel like I was playing a game, I felt like I was a part of the story. That's why it was special to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: A simple and quick point-and-click game yet also a short tale of love and regret, "Behind the Frame" is lovingly crafted and perfectly captures the essence of why people make art - and how love can, in time, become a regret for actions not taken out of fear for not being good enough.Definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This one is my favorite game ever. I play this game and yoga master to be balance in real life, Relaxing after work. Very worth to have this game in collection. It make me love painting watercolor. Artwork so beautiful and music and story, everything perfect in this game, After you finished first story it's unlock man story. don't forget to complete :D
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Behind the Frame is a beautiful interactive story about an aspiring artist. As you progress you start recognising familiarity between certain objects and unlock an even deeper story.I thoroughly enjoyed this game. Perfect for relaxing, having a hot drink and being guided through the life of an artist. Art style and visuals were absolutely beautiful, the music- soothing and a well-written story which has you focused and constantly wondering what you will find next.The game is split into chapters, each with its own focus on a pinnacle part of the story. No dialogue (apart from letters), no voice acting - just a well written and well executed masterpiece. Game does not feel rushed, nor extended - with just about 2 hours of gameplay.Behind the Frame has you reflecting on your own personal life by the end of the game, ultimately hitting your emotions. Honestly, I enjoyed it so much - after completing the game, you unlock a new chapter in which the story is shown from a different perspective. This hit even harder.Overall, beautifully written and executed and would honestly recommend anyone try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I really enjoyed this game.  The music is really nice.  Very cozy and relaxing.  I also really enjoyed the art style.  The art in the cut scenes reminded me of Studio Ghibli films.  The story though, although good, could use some more clarity.  I played this on stream and we had a few questions.  I know the game is probably set up to where you have to assume and put the puzzle pieces of the story together yourself, but a little more clarity would have made this game perfect.  Overall, I'd say give this game a chance.  I completed it in a little over an hour.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: A smear and click game. People who had a stroke will love it. It´s an old hag believing that she´s still young and remembering her and another self-proclaimed "painter" - two entitled white gentiles that couldn´t be more white - painting kitsch pics and listening to kitsch music...until nepotism opened the door for her to go to wonderland.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: A very short, but also extremely beautiful game to play. The story is not so easy to follow as it seems... but with a dreamy atmosphere and very original, unexpected animations you don't really want to give up such cute game. The puzzles are creative, but very easy to solve, so this is really not the main thing in the game. In my opinion 8/10, because the story needs a little bit more words to explain and clear out things for everybody. All the other aspects are more then perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: It's visually and tonally appealing, but it wasn't robust enough, I guess, to enjoy. I understand that it's mainly a narrative game, I do enjoy those, this one just didn't feel like there was enough to it. It's very short and pretty easy to play, but feels like there's very little to do, and I don't think the ending is that well done, it's more confusing than anything really. Someone else said that it's more a work of art than a game which I agree with, very pretty for art, but not a really enjoyable game.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: The definition of a short but sweet game. It tells its story well and imparts what I consider to be a pretty nice life lesson to take home and think about. Not often does a game have decent puzzle gameplay and a heart tugging story. The puzzles were a bit easy but that is not the main objective of the game, just a nice side activity. Overall I give this a glowing review for a well thought out and nice indie game. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a game where you dont have to use too many braincells. Even though its a short (1-2 hours at most) game, its extremely relaxing and just a nice vibe overall (i LOOVEEEE the music and artstyle). Its perfect for those days where you feel like playing a game yet you dont have the energy to do alot of thinking. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This game is overpriced, be sure to get it on sale for a few dollars.This game is a simple point and click with simple puzzles and basic story, but it is lovely.If you prepare yourself to play it on a sunny afternoon, or a dreary wet day with a cup of your favorite beverage and maybe a biscuit, then you are sure to enjoy this slow paced, artsoaked love fest.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those "get it on sale" recommendations.The game is absolutely stunning and the story and gameplay hits that artsy whimsical spot for me.Yeah, let me paint, but also make coffee beforehand and scetch the neighbors cat by the window!The only downside is the length. I got through it in just over an hour, and that is REALLY short.Though I can't fully blame the game for it, because it's such a handcrafted experience, of course it's shorter if there is so much work put into tiny details, I suppose?I could have used more puzzles for padding, I guess.I had some slight "bugs" that padded the playtime too, sometimes you have to wait for dialogue to disappear on its own and it takes quite a while to do so and if  you're an impatient clicker like myself you run the risk of clicking the same prompt again, having to wait again... so yeah, it actually probably hit the sub one hour mark just because of those scenes.Still, it's a very beautiful and enjoyable little experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game if you like interactive visual novels but it isn't worth the asking price, I bought it in a bundle and you should do the same or wait for a deep sale.The game is ok if you are in the mood for a relaxing visual novel with some lite puzzles mixed in. The game looks nice, the sound is ok but the only problem I have is story related. For a game that you can beat in 1 to 2 hours I expect some level of...well I don't expect that the ending of the story is so obvious. Don't get me wrong the journey this game takes you on is nice but I expect some intrigue before the ending.Overall a good game to finish in one sitting on a rainy day. No chance it is worth the asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable puzzle game about a woman figuring out mysterious paintings. The story is enjoyable and the presentation matches the painterly qualities of the game. The music is a standout achievement which deserves praise, considering the length of the game, there is so much great music here. Unfortunately, the game is very short and takes place in mostly the same environment. I would love to see additional paintings and more done with the little mechanics set up here.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This is such beautiful game. From its vibrant atmosphere to the endearing gameplay, I enjoyed every moment of it. Without spoiling much of the story, Behind The Frame covers a story of a young female artist preparing her application for her New York exhibit. But as the story progresses it covers the story of two distant creatives that yearn for one another and the story behind how they influenced one another with their presence. I love how the game focuses on an implied love but leaves you to decide how their relationship lies.The game’s art style is heavily inspired by Studio Ghibli’s films and the cutscenes although short, always captured my attention. I found the visuals along with the wonderful soundtrack orchestrated such a wonderful and evocative story that pulled at my heart.The music across all six chapters brought about feelings of nostalgia and calm that contrasts with life in the big city. The story hooked me and the simple yet intricate detail that sits behind every puzzle provide a seamless and enjoyable experience. This is a laid-back visual novel that I found to be quite enrapturing. The title pf this game was something I never understood but as I completed the game it touched me. Paintings and photos are meant to hold a moment in time. It's beautiful how something as simple as an image can convey something really meaningful. This game truly shows with every work of art that there's a story... \
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: (Thanks for the game M...  I had fun covering every single item in paint/pencil dust.)Everyone in the reviews already pointed out everything that's wonderful about the game...  So I'll just do this:If you wish to feel an emotion called "sadness" ->  Play this game.For everything else...  There's smearing paint.v(u.u)v  Good, but sad.  Good though.  Good.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game! It's a rather short puzzle game with a very wholesome story (tears anyone? no? just me?), nice art and amazing music. It's the first game for which I actually seriously considered buying the soundtrack. I can't wait for the new content they will bring and honestly, even though it's short (~1h playtime) it's still worth the price. I bought it impulsively and it's one of my faves now. Just get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review:
Guide brush strokes and solve a variety of puzzles to help an aspiring artist complete her masterpiece amid her brusque neighbor's gaze and his pesky cat. As her painting starts to take shape, uncover an emotional tale of chance and artistry revealed behind unrelated yet familiar moments. 

Behind the Frame is a vivid, interactive fiction about an aspiring artist on the cusp of finishing the final piece of her gallery submission.

A relaxing, eloquent experience that can be played at any pace. Become immersed in a panoramic world filled with resplendent colors, beautiful hand-animated visuals, and a smooth, easy-listening soundtrack.

As a passionate artist, seek the missing colors that will bring your paintings to life - all while remembering to take the occasional coffee and breakfast breaks that keep you going. There is more than what meets the eye, for every painting has a story to tell.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

name: Minishoot' Adventures
detailed_description: THE UNCHOSEN HAS RETURNED... His minions have emerged from the underworld, your village has been destroyed, and all your friends are now trapped in corrupted crystal... Embark on a journey to save the world in this bullet-filled adventure, born from our desire to mix the joy of open-ended exploration with a top-down shooter's juicy game feel. ENGAGE WITH TIGHT COMBAT Take control of a swift and responsive spaceship, and shoot your way through handcrafted encounters supported by a crystal clear esthetic and crispy game feel. Overcome bosses in intense Bullet Hell battles, with difficulty options for both newcomers and veterans. VENTURE ON YOUR OWN Plunge into an entirely handcrafted world built with many interconnections to explore on your own. Lush caverns, ancient temples and sunken cities await you with their unique treasures, challenges and secrets. RECLAIM THE STOLEN POWERS Finding the Primordial Powers will improve your combat and exploration abilities while also opening up the map bit by bit as you unlock new paths and reveal shortcuts. _childDocuments_.review: Here to just echo the description of old-school Zelda / Metroid / bullet hell mashup. _childDocuments_.review: Minishoot' Adventures is a top-down bullet-hell Zelda-like metroidvania. I know this game counts as a metroidvania on a very loose term, but it has a connected world, lots of ability-gated areas, loads of hidden items, rewarding exploration, and everything else you can see in that genre. It is also one of the best metroidvania I've played. The game is consistent with its level design. The art style is clean and memorable. It really hard to not recommend this game.→: One thing I especially love about this game is how seamless you can travel from areas to areas. You can go anywhere on the open world map encountering no loading screen (well of course underground areas and dungeons still need loading). This design creates a sense of freedom which is common in other games feature open world design. Yet in Minishoot' Adventures, exploration and a pair of keen eyes are always rewarding. And as a metroidvania, it is always exciting to see how far you can go without acquiring the first ability.→: Because of the game's perspective, this metroidvania has some gating abilities unusual to other games in the same genre. Thus, double jump, air dash, etc are out of the equation. Instead we have abilities that benefit you with the bullet hell gameplay like explosion which can damage enemies and destroy projectiles and slowing down time for easier maneuver amidst the sea of bullets. Definitely something to look forward to if you're tired of the 2D side-scrolling design the metroidvanias are known for.→: Recently a lot of metroidvania just assume players will hit every wall they run into and try to get away with as little hints as possible for the items hidden across the world. This is a foul practice in my book, and I am glad Minishoot' Adventures does things right. Secret passages covered by unusually dense foliage, small cracks on the otherwise smooth walls, projectiles coming from seemingly out-of-bound places, button under a big lily-pad, just to name a few.→: I usually condemn too much arena-style fights as a lazy tactic to stall as much as time as possible, but the gameplay of Minishoot' Adventures makes me want to have more of this fights. Thanks to the bullet-hell, every arena fight feels hand-crafted and follows a specific pattern. It requires players to focus on dodging, repositioning, and shooting back so often time the fights feel more engaging.→Clean art style.→It's cute to see the little planes spinning around to express their emotion.→The little racing games with the spirits are fun.→You can see the lifespan of the projectiles indicated by the inner circle shrinking.→Breaking things are quite rewarding in this game.→More guns with different firing patterns Raiden-style to unlock would be lovely.→The order of recharging active abilities feels weird.中文小簡評→這款嚴格說起來不太算Metroidvania，但是他有太多這類型遊戲應有的特色，所以我說算就算！→做對了許多同期同類型遊戲欠缺的設計。→乾淨簡單的畫風。→無縫接軌大地圖，到哪裡幾乎不需要讀取。→跟其他Metroidvania不一樣的解鎖技能，玩膩2D橫向卷軸的可以試試這款。→隱藏道具的提示，給足線索讓玩家自己發現，而不是直接認定玩家會敲每一到牆。→難得有一款遊戲會讓我喜歡競技場行戰鬥，可能是因為子彈地獄的關係，打起來特別有感。→小飛機透過轉圈圈表達心情特別可愛。→與精靈賽跑很有趣。→敵人射的每發子彈都可以看的出何時會消失。→如果能像雷電那樣有多點射擊模式就好了。→技能充能的順序很奇怪。

_childDocuments_.review: "Zelda meets Galaga… and we get a beautiful little gem. It's a simple and straightforward game, with some secrets and a lot of exploration. The game's strength, in my opinion, is the exploration. The bosses aren't difficult, even on hard mode, but they became tedious for me. It felt like the fights would never end; on hard mode, the bosses are much faster and have much more health, so mistakes, especially early on, are heavily punished. However, the game is still not very demanding—you don’t lose anything if you die; you just have to redo the boss and return to the point where you died to resume exploring.Once you get enough upgrades, the game becomes much easier and, again, the most enjoyable part is the exploration: discovering secret areas and figuring out how to reach the items we see on the map.I only encountered one small bug, which was fixed by entering and exiting the game… several times. For some reason, a vendor wouldn't give me the option to buy the last item, even though I had what it was needed; but in the end, I was able to.Overall, a good game. I hope to see more from the developers ♥

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10. Absolutely recommended.The demo did a good job hyping this game up - and the full release delivered. I had an absolute blast for the 10h playthrough I just finished. 👍 The Good:- 🖥️ Cute, clean visuals- 🔊 Pleasant Soundscape- ♿ Accessibility options ON TOP of normal difficulty options- ⬆️ Satisfying upgrade system  - ♻️ Respec anytime - even in combat!- 🚿 Good bullet-hell gameplay (even though I'm not the biggest fan of that generally)- 🪙 Great implementation of secrets and collectibles in the game- 🕹️ Movement feels responsive- 📈 Upgrade pacing is well done - lots of games give you the cool stuff right before the end of the game, this game actually lets you play with the fun stuff from quite early.- 🕳️ Falling down a crevasse or into (deep) water doesn't cost health, so "platforming" sections are quite forgiving.🤏 The Neutral:- 🏎️ I kinda hate races. There are 8 races. Those are not mandatory for finishing the main story. You will need to complete them though for the true ending. Luckily I could just respec into move/boost and turn game speed down to 50% (Accessibility options), so they were ok.- ☠️ Dying in the overworld is kind of harsh since it respawns you at "town". It's located in the center (and there will be tons of shortcuts) so it's not too bad, but still annoying. Didn't happen often though.- ⏳ Strangely you can't pause the game at all (neither ESC or uprade menu) while the level-up animation plays; the game still runs normally (moving/shooting etc), you just can't pause it. 🤷👎 The Bad:- ⁉️ Sometimes progression through the map is not very clear. I got "stuck" twice in the game (separate occasions) and had to re-check quite a bit of the map to find where I needed to go

_childDocuments_.review: Minishoot' Adventures is a small team indie game that punches above its weight class due to its incredible attention to getting the core formula right: the result is a game where combat feels as intense as Enter the Gungeon (while being easier), and exploration is as intoxicating as the 2D Zelda / Metroidvania games you played as a child. Fresh and heartwarming ~10 hours fling :)(+)  is great at giving you hints to hidden secrets / new paths to explore after grabbing a new ability. This results in a game that's difficult to put down because you're constantly high on the urge to explore, looking for friends to save, shortcuts to unlock, heart pieces and powers to collect.(+)  that conveys all information you need without overloading the screen and giving you a lot of text explanations. Best examples are the character's wings showing Boost recharge status, the sound trigger when it fills up, the white dot in enemy projectiles which lets you know when they're about to fade. The color coding sky blue / red / black and reddish is clean. (+)  that are precise and responsive. (+) The arena / pantheon challenge was my favorite part of the game. The end game fully challenged my ability to play with advanced powers and it was pure joy.(+) There's flexibility in shooting and aiming modes that I enjoyed.(-) Infuriating one-shot bullets that are by far my least favorite feature of the platformer / puzzle sequences.(-) After falling into a pit, there's no indication of where you'll respawn, and no invincibility frames to protect you from damage. (-) Epilogue feels anticlimactic(-) Quite difficult to have smooth, high FPS despite having a good GPU. I was stuck at 40ish during exploration and often < 30 during combat. I'm not sure what causes this and there don't seem to be options to turn off to improve performance. (-) "Dodge roll" dash arrives quite late in the game: I would have preferred to have it earlier, and have combats requiring you to use it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic twin-stick shooter that's fun to explore and a joy to play.(++) Even better on Steam Deck(++) Great movement, great combat, great flow(++) Various types of enemies requiring different approaches(+) No skill gate-keeping: Offers different difficulties and adjustable auto-aim setting on top of it(+) Basic save-the-world story but it's delivered in a charming and fitting manner (and it's not much in the way)(+) Upgrading your abilities matters and you can feel the difference from the get-go(-) The art style is not the worst but the flash-like aspect where no two graphical elements blend together (due to strong outlines, odd color choices, round angles everywhere and flat lighting) makes the game look way too cheap(-) The whole environment (its every element) is placed on a grid and to no benefit whatsoever(-) Some mechanics can be tiresome: The metroidvania design is too strict and too much on the nose; some passages and bosses more frustrating than fun; the interconnected caves are just annoying and pain to navigate around

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. What a phenomenal game. If you were to take The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past and mix it with a relatively casual (but enjoyable) twin-stick shooter/shmup, Minishoot Adventures is exactly what you'd end up with. To find out that this game is the product of a two-person development team is astounding, especially considering the game is super polished and launching in a state that some AAA titles struggle to reach.First off, the GREAT:- Exploration is fun and intuitive; as the devs claim, it's a compelling mix of top-down action-adventure and Metroidvania. Map is huge and split into distinct biomes, each with their own unique enemy types and environmental hazards to overcome.- Progression feels smooth and is incredibly rewarding. You gain red gems that contribute toward an EXP total represented by a crystal, leveling up at specific intervals and then spending those level-up crystals on the game's various abilities. in addition, there are larger red gems that can be collected to spend on various upgrade items and "charms" that each have unique effects (revealing incomplete dungeons, bullets that stun enemies, etc.). There's almost always something worthwhile to work toward that makes character progression a consistently satisfying power creep.- The game's combat mixes some classic twin-stick shooting with careful maneuvering of the player's ship, and the boss enemies have distinct movement and bullet patterns to decipher that make these encounters one of the game's highlights.- Minishoot Adventures doesn't overstay its welcome, clocking in at about 6-8 hours depending on how much of a completionist you are. It's a perfectly paced and satisfying experience that never drags or loses steam.- The music. Was not expecting the soundtrack to this game to blow me away like it has. Very reminiscent of some of the best work of Disasterpiece. Expect to get similar vibes as both Fez and Hyper Light Drifter.The Not-So-Great:- The map fragments that you can collect really facilitate one of the game's strong points (exploitation and backtracking for upgrades), but the game gives no indication of where they're to be found or how to find them. Almost every biome has a different place where its map fragment is found, with some being purchasable and others being hidden/secret items you need to dig for. I get that it's part of the game's Zelda-like charm, and it's a small annoyance but one of the only missteps the game commits.Minishoot Adventures runs phenomenally on the Steam Deck, I experienced zero crashes or bugs my entire playthrough (again, kudos to the two-person dev team), and I loved every second of it. As someone who loves Metroidvanias, Zelda games, and shmups, this title was a unique genre hodgepodge I wasn't expecting. Arguably one of my favorite games of 2024 so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Minishoot Adventures is a straightforward story. Your little spaceship was woken up to save the land from a past calamity. This calamity saw your other spaceship pals imprisoned in crystal-like structures. During the journey you learn more about the world and who exactly put this state. Understanding history is key to not repeating it. Even though the story is straightforward, it is told subtly. Collectibles will be found around the world to fill the player in on that history (gameplay tools will assure that). In the end the story doesn’t hinder the rest of the game and is fine if you care to learn about it. For a ~10hr game, it is quick to pick up and understand  Minishoot Adventures is a straightforward story. Your little spaceship was woken up to save the land from a past calamity. This calamity saw your other spaceship pals imprisoned in crystal-like structures. During the journey you learn more about the world and who exactly put this state. Understanding history is key to not repeating it. Even though the story is straightforward, it is told subtly. Collectibles will be found around the world to fill the player in on that history (gameplay tools will assure that). In the end the story doesn’t hinder the rest of the game and is fine if you care to learn about it. For a ~10hr game, it is quick to pick up and understand   As stated above. Minishoot Adventure will always try to point you in the right direction. There are plenty of tools to make sure you explore every nook and cranny of the world. It’s very possible to 100% this game the first time around if you play on the top difficulty from the beginning. The various supplemental activities to do in the world further expand your spaceship’s kit and arsenal. Finding these supplemental activities starts with finding a map of the area. From there as long as you do some exploration, you’ll get tools that let you know where some secrets are and if you’ve fully completed them. Towards the end of the game, you’ll be introduced to challenge stages which are tough, but far from impossible. I recommend doing these, as they unlock the “True” ending to the game.  Minishoot Adventure is a beautiful game to play on the Steam Deck and should be lauded as a “must have” on it. It runs very well considering it pre-loads the whole world in the beginning for seamless transitions. Outside of it graphical crispiness, I didn’t pay much attention to music in the game outside of some solid boss music (final boss in particular). The art style is bubbly and colorful but knows how to instill the dread of the calamity by instituting  darkness. Enemy design was constantly changing, and environments were uniquely varied. I don’t know if the variation in the world design necessarily told a story non-verbally, but at least it was good looking

_childDocuments_.review: AVOID | LACKING | MAYBE | WORTHWHILE | COMPELLING | Minishoot' Adventure is a bullet hell metroidvania game with a heavy focus on exploration.In this game, you start as a little spaceship trying to save your friends and the world from corruption. Pretty early on, you can tell this game is going to be a delight; it has all the things you want you in a game like this - well-paced upgrades, distinct environments, lots of good quality of life aspects (nice map, you can buy an upgrade that tells you when you've completed a dungeon making for easy backtracking, you can downgrade abilities you have upgraded to fit various situations, easy to understand UI, etc), unique enemies, tough but fair boss fights (and lots of accessibility options to make it insanely difficult to literally being invincible), lots of secrets to discover, and the art is great to look at.The game took me ~9.5 hours to beat the "final" boss, at which point I had 100% in-game completion. It took another hour to beat the actual final boss, and then I took some time finishing the battle arenas to get the proper ending. By playing in advanced mode, finishing the battle arenas with at least 5 hears remaining, and getting 100% in-game completion, you will get all achievements.All in all, this game lit up my brain like Christmas tree - it hit every note I want in a game like this and delivered handsomely. It was pretty addicting to play, which isn't something I find is true with many games unless they're complete bangers. It's so easy to recommend. Like, do you enjoy having fun? Then you should buy this game lol. That's literally the only criterion I would use to base a recommendation of this game off of because it has so much going for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I find it strange I liked Minishoot so much. It's a very competent SHMUP being pushed through the filter of a simple Zelda-esque adventure game. You visit dungeons, find upgrades, and fight bosses. Standard stuff. Yet, thematically, the game doesn't work even a little. The story (whatever it might be) is completely out of place for a game about a spaceship doing pew pews, and it feels like the developers, ARGL and KUHO, had the skills to make a different game but a passion to make this one.The graphics are fine, and the sound is appropriate. It's easy to play and controls well. It feels simple, but moving around and shooting are engaging, so maybe it's not important that it doesn't make any sense. It's also the right length for its parts. That last part is a bit of a fib. The game has an ending, a true ending, and a more true ending. This annoys me a little because none of the endings are narratively interesting or satisfying; they are basically just more challenging fights to let you really put your skills to the test, and that's what the game does well, so... I guess I'm just annoyed that there isn't actually an ending that is worthwhile. You could stop when the credits roll, and it would be as narratively satisfying as doing the optional post-game boss fights.It also, importantly, has the right level of challenge. It's not easy, but it's also not frustratingly hard. It has secrets you might miss, but they aren't hard to find if you go looking for them. There are plenty of upgrades spread over your playtime, but not so many that it becomes a chore. The boss fights make you start over if you die, but they aren't long enough for it to feel like a punishment. It really just nails that sweet spot of being engaging without being tedious. Challenging but not infuriating. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Undoubtedly the most fun I've had with a game this year. And by that I mean the pure joy of sitting down for a session - a big grin on my face as I swoosh around, exploring a charming cartoon world that's one part 2D Zelda and one part twin-stick shooter bliss. Minishoot's controls are responsive, which is a must when the screen is dense with the firepower of your enemies. Being precise is better than just being quick. A whole slew of secondary quests and areas to explore entice beyond the main thrust of the game. Not quite powered up enough to face a certain arena or boss? No problem, there are a dozen other things to do that typically branch off into another set of fun adventures that'll loop back around to the main quest in ways that surprise and delight. There are a few obvious challenge bumps near the end that are a bit eye-rolling, and the final boss is the least interesting of the lot, but it's breezy enough, with plenty of post game potential to keep that keen sense of fun intact. All in all, my proverbial hat off to the two devs. They've done an incredible job on what could be one of the best of the year!

_childDocuments_.review: Clever and convenient in many ways:Projectiles show their lifespan, letting the player know how far they'll reach without memorization. Some bits, both important for navigation and not, are teased so the player knows where they are before reaching them. Not just hidden, but guaranteed things too serve as power progression catchups to decrease how much behind the power curve players are if they don't do side stuff/backtrack. Enemies have consistent and intuitive tells for how they're aiming and if they're aiming at all. The most immediate kind of power progression can be freely respecced, replacing regret with adaptation. This, having more than 1 way to go for most of the game and optional sources of power, combined with difficulty settings(which alone wouldn't achieve as much), allow players to always keep progressing or enlarge obstacles. Many collectible location spoilers require an intentional interaction to kick in, maybe too much for some, but most can have the best of both spoiled and not. Combat encounters tend to drop health pickups at the end, so getting hit little enough is the same for pacing as not at all. Overlookable things without indicators ever(except 1) are extras, not a permanent loss if overlooked. Some things are invisibly tutorialled, achieving knowledge without explicit anything. Some places have fun gimmecks that keep sameness down.I wouldn't be surprised if there's more clever/convenient stuff I don't see than I doA deliberate, but harder to agree with, decision is commiting a flowfire and making trees a lot bigger visually than they are for the purposes of collision detection, obstructing everything one needs to see to fight(stuff visible through them is everything except geometry, the player, enemies and all projectiles). Also, playing as if it was a gameplay-only game is not a valid pace to play the game at. Despite claims that everyone can play at their own pace, ~5 people can't due to forced downtime. Finite deceleration speed is frustrating in obstacle courses with instakill projectiles.Short flashes can be turned off, but longer walls of light can't. There are sound cues without visual equivalents. Don't play it without sound.

_childDocuments_.review: Usually my other reviews are nonsense, but I gave the other game by this developer a negative review. I feel obligated to make a serious review about this entry because I thoroughly enjoyed it.The movement of the main character is crisp, responsive, and natural. I played with keyboard - which is not recommended - but it still felt fine enough to maneuver through. The visuals are lovely, the animations and presentation are adorable, and the lore is intriguing while a little vague. The gameplay is also blazingly fun for what is a joystick bullet-hell shooter, and the metroidvania type of twist on it makes it very fun to go through and collect upgrades as you blast at stronger and stronger foes. If you are not too good at these types of games, it comes with a wide variety of difficulty and accessibility options - no one is left out.That said, I have a few gripes. Some of the arenas feel a bit overwhelming compared to the boss fights of the game, with spikes of difficulty feeling somewhat random or unpredictable at times. There is also a lack of variety within your weaponry; that is, you only get the basic gun attack you have at the beginning of the game and nothing else. You do get upgrades to that gun attack and some activated abilities, but I would have liked to see ways of modifying the gun into different weapons with different effects, including turning it into a bomb, making it a minigun, a laser, and more. Criticisms aside, I had a blast with the game, even if the longer section of my gripes with the game contrast with the short accolades I had given it. I feel like everything presented to you by the beginning of this review and the store page is all you need - go try it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a surprisingly delightful little blend of oldschool Zelda and the shoot-em-up genre, and I say that as someone who's never much enjoyed either class of game. I'd been looking for a game to tide over my Hollow Knight itch, and this fit the bill well: explore, find new upgrades that both apply in combat while unlocking new areas, and fight some challenging bosses. The secret sauce is how the game manages to constantly introduce new abilities and areas and enemies at such a steady pace that it never for a second loses your attention; I wouldn't be surprised if some people get sucked into this game and marathon it 'till they've finished every part of it.The most enjoyable content for me was after the true ending, where the game offers a hall of arena fights, re-mixing enemy encounters and bosses with your entire endgame skillset in mind. It was back-to-back high-octane encounters, and after clearing the first one I didn't want to take a break until I finished them all. As one point of constructive criticism, I do think this game is lacking a true 'mega endgame final challenge' that the likes of Hollow Knight had; the arenas and remixed bosses are difficult and enjoyable, but not a single one took me more than two tries... it would've been neat to really sink my teeth into a few fights (likely by making the enemies more aggressive/proactive and making it harder to simply back out of their range to mentally reset or get some free hits in), but then again I was only playing on 'normal' mode.I've completed the game entirely, and as you can see by my playtime it's rather short. It really is a no-fluff game; no padded downtime, 'boring parts', etc. Because of that, I think it's reasonably-priced. If you've been looking for a game to scratch that challenging/exploratory/charming itch, this may be the one for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: This has been such a phenomenal throwback to old SNES games combined with modern movement sensibilities. _childDocuments_.review: 1 / 2Minishoot Adventures reviewPlaytime – 18 hours, 100% save file and an additional playthrough on hardFor fans of – shmups, twin-stick shooters, light exploration & Puzzle solving  Straight off the top, I have to say I can’t help but recommend Minishoot Adventures, the Zelda-like Shmup developed by Soulgame Studio.  Controlling a nondescript ship, you are awoken by not-Navi and informed that the Unchosen has returned, destroying your village and imprisoning your friends & family.  With that, you are sent off into the map and very much left on your own to explore, save your friends and defeat the Unchosen.  If you go all the way to the true ending, there is a bit more plot & exposition but outside of that, the introductory context is all there is in way of plot.  Whilst virtually non-existent, the small amount of lore that there is plays with ‘The Chosen One’ narrative in an admittedly insignificant way, but one that still made me smile when all was said and done.I found the gameplay and exploration compelling, with XP and upgrades doled out to the player at a solid clip alongside stumbling across new caves & areas of the map at a consistently fast pace. The best way to describe it really is the original NES Zelda crossbred with Galaga, and some modern day quality of life improvements & accessibility on top.  Coming in with three difficulty options (which effectively dictate the speed of enemies and bullets) and a couple of additional settings pertaining to auto-aim and other assists mean that this game is approachable for people of all skill levels, without ever sacrificing the things that make it such a joy to play.  In terms of art design, Minishoot keeps it clean, simple, and incredibly readable even in the thick of the action.  Enemy ships all have simple, blocky designs which meant that no matter how intense the action gets I could still make out what was shooting at me and where from pretty much all the time.  This carries over to the light environmental puzzling, where it was always clear what could be interacted with and what couldn’t, and what walls may or may not conceal hidden paths.  Whilst I personally found myself stumped once or twice, thanks to the readability of the map it never devolved into just shooting and running into anything & everything looking for any tiny detail I may have missed.  I haven’t touched on sound design too much and admittedly don’t have much to add, as it was played without volume for the vast majority, which was an oversight.  I will go back and check out the audio design, but I don’t think it would impact my feelings towards this game even if there was no sound design at all!I did encounter one or two minor issues with my playthrough, those being some slowdown in the latter stages of the game when things get really hectic (I did play exclusively on deck so can’t really speak to how well the game runs on a proper pc) and also the game’s in-game map.  It is perfectly usable, and the QoL improvements in terms of the ways the game provides upgrades to the mapping system to show you what locations are unfinished/where hidden items are appreciated, but there are some spots of the map that just don’t do a good job of helping you understand some of the areas.  In places, it will imply there is no way forward when in fact there will be a path, and this led to one or two frustrations where the answer I wanted was somewhere I hadn’t looked because of what the in-game map led me to believe.As I said up top, I strongly recommend this one. Fairly short and sweet, Minishoot Adventures is a highly enjoyable adventure, with fun exploration and compelling combat scenarios.  It’s here for a good time and not for a long time, but boy was it a good time!  8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent indy developed game.  The game is advertised as a blend of of the Original Legend of Zelda with elements of shooter games such as Geometry Wars.  The game is incredibly engaging upon your initial play with excellent controls and a great atmospheric soundtrack.  My impression is that the game would be more appealing to fans of the classic Zelda games than it would be to a person who enjoys Geometry Wars or other bullet hell games, as there are portions of the game where things can drag on a bit, and it can take some real hunting to figure out how to get into certain areas.  In particular I would note the Dungeons that can really do need some sort of mapping system.   The overworld map and items that are designed to help you find the items for your adventure could use some polish too.  I mention these short comings only in hopes that they can be addressed or to service anyone who might want to improve on this excellent idea.  This an A+ game worth playing if you like classic Zelda.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Edit:The end game gauntlets had the pattern quality and challenge i expected from the regular game which is both sad and good. Buy this game its great.7/10This review contains minor spoilers!!!My only issues with the game so far(2 bosses down) are that first off the game is too easy even on hardest difficulty. You would expect that a bullet hell game would cater to a bullet hell playerbase. Secondly, when talking about a metroidvania, one of the biggest selling points of the game is atmosphere and worldbuilding for me. The areas feel very dull in this game. For example i really liked the huge open area of the desert with the worm ship but imagine if the worm ship was an actual worm like digger robot. And imagine if the desert area had sand that would spray around from the wind when you dashed. Stuff like this would make this game go up multiple notches for me. This also brings the topic to enemy variety. Most of the enemies i have seen in this game are very similar looking ships. They don't even have many different colors let alone textures. Overall although there is a lack of interesting world to explore in this game, the gameplay is spot on except for difficulty and the world design is not bad.(full of secrets)Edit: I also hate the inconsistency of ramp jumping (there is at least 1 ramp in the game that doesn't let you jump over the gap. For no reason other than the level being designed accordingly) I also hate the inconsistency with the water surf ability where some waters are just not surfable even if they are more shallow at times. This is also done for level design but its bad.After beating the game in 7 hours I stand by my point about difficulty in this game. I beat the final boss first try without using any abilites like time slow and blank and only got hit once. This game should have more difficulty options.

_childDocuments_.review: Here it goes,Exploration: What MINISHOOT does that I have not seen in most Metroidvania games, is how open the world is. How easy it is to navigate. I don't feel the claustrophobic sensation of reaching an end point at the end of a long corridor. But instead everything is open and if you find a blocked  access to a new area you can easily keep exploring the one you are already in. You just don't feel the frustration of backtracking. In addition, the level expansion is extremely well balanced: the bigger the world gets, the faster you can go and you get more items to orient yourself. Finally my favourite part: This game is full of hidden areas and secrets, everywhere !!! Combat: you start being a cuty little warrior and you end up being a cuty killer machine. The feeling of well deserved progression is always there. Never too easy, never too hard, just in the right fun spot. There are a ton of different enemies, patterns and combinations. And there are, of course, the boss fights. Which have a crazy soundtrack and crazy bullet patterns. I found myself screaming with excitement most of the time.    Sound: Most of the music and the sound effects of the game are simply over the top! Super evocative and magic. They really put me in a magic trance state. The game's environmental effects also add a lot to create that special atmosphere. And your character sound effects are just super cute <3Verdict: MINISHOOT has become one of my favourite games of all times for two reasons. One: because I simply love that feeling of freedom during the exploration and finding hidden secrets. Two: because all the combats and the evolution of your little buddy are so unique and crafted with detail and love.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 20/05 - There has been some recent updates to the Race section which addresses some of the concerns mentioned below.Recommended - For a bullet hell game this was a reasonably calm and relaxing affair. Exploring and discovering in this charming little game never felt like a tedious task, as I was genuinely intrigued to uncover what awaited me around each corner. Levelling up your skills was fluid and the upgrades were noticeable.However, the racing aspect of the game is quite disappointing due to several reasons. Firstly, if you happen to lose a race early on, there is no option to reset it, which can be frustrating considering the time it takes to fully get to grips with the race arenas/maps. Secondly, there needs to be some crystals available at each race location so as to boost your powers prior to a race. Lastly, it would greatly enhance the gameplay experience if races were clearly indicated on the map with a unique race icon. _childDocuments_.review: What could have been a great game was hampered from being able to ever reach its full potential thanks to its prevalence of horrendous euroshmup design mechanics, the most glaring and affecting of which is the heavy and painful inertia built into your ship's movement that poisons every facet of the game's mechanics design.  What am I referring to when I write about euroshmup design? What even is a "euroshmup" to begin with?  The term--a portmanteau of "European" and "shoot-em-up"--describes the design ethos for shoot-em-up/shmup games made (of the kind typically made by European developers) with experimental design goals completely at odds with classic shmup design (of the kind typically made by Japanese developers). Whereas classic shmups focus on responsive, arcadey, challenging, compact ("all killer, no filler", as they say), score-based game design, euroshmups try to blend classic shmup design recipes with foreign ingredients like RPG mechanics and simulator genre elements. This euroshmup design generally manifests in the following ways:  Considering that Minishoot' Adventure aimed to be a game in the same spirit as a Zelda title, you might think I'm being unfair to it by criticizing its euroshmup elements. After all, if your goal is to make an adventure game, you will need some kind of a progression system (like health upgrades), an emphasis on exploration with slower moments of soaking in the atmosphere of the environments you explore, and a somewhat longer game, won't you? All of this is true.  However, what I am criticizing is not the goal but rather the execution. Poor shmup mechanics implementation made the game suffer tremendously. It didn't need to suffer in the ways I am about to describe. You could have had a great adventure game without the unnecessary euroshmup mechanics problems that plague this game.  This game, most of all things, didn't need inertia. You can still play as a ship adventuring a vast world without having your ship feel like a hovercraft. Why is inertia a bad thing? Inertia doesn't just simply make your movement feel slippery. By its very nature, inertia negatively affects other aspects of game mechanics:  The game also didn't need to make your ship's default bullet speed, rate of fire and bullet reach to be so pitiful. Upgrade points could have been used for actually meaningful upgrades, like choices of different bullet shot patterns (just like how different playable ships in classic shmups had different shot patterns, like concentrated, spread and homing shots for use in different scenarios). The game also didn't need to make the player's secondary power shot take so long to regenerate and share the same resource as the player's boost ability (very euroshmuppy).  As you can see, euroshmup mechanics always end up coming at a price that negatively affects other gameplay elements. _childDocuments_.review: Is this even a finished product?I mean, it would've been fine if this was a demo. In fact, it would be a great demo but a full-fledged game? I don't think so. This game is very shallow in every aspect. Story, Upgrades/Progression, Explorations, Enemy designs, Combat.There is no choices to make in this game in terms of progression. You buy this then upgrade that in, and only in, a predetermined order. On top of that, upgrades are pretty lame and lazily designed. You shoot one bullet then two then three etc.etc. No variations to choose from. It's just that.Fighting enemies in this game feels very strange in a bad way. It's like you not only control yourself but you also control enemies too, not in a metaphorically way. For example, if you strafe left, the enemies turn accordingly in a synchronize fashion with you. If you wiggle, they wiggle as if you were controlling them. It's super weird, at least for me. Because of this, the trajectory of their projectiles is very predictable, well, you are the one who controlling them after all.I know that story isn't of concern for this kind of game but if you were to provide garbage narrative, you might as well not provide any at all. Just a world with a premise is enough, leave the rest for players. They know what to do.All in all, I regret buying this game and I'm sure that you will too. A big disappointment, considering all the positive reviews. A very big disappointment.1/5
