_childDocuments_.review: Game is super cute. The artstyle is really incredible. And the "top down twin stick shooter" seems a fresh approach to metroidvania, where the genrne is overwhelmed by 10000s of sidescroller/platformers. So that's nice! But...Not having map being recorded as you explore new regions was a terrible design decision. Game has 5 map collectables that are apparently very hard to find, as after playing for ~3 hours I have found only the starting one that is given to you at the start of the game. Now I have to somehow memorize every location.I simply don't have the time for that.Maybe the devs can take a page out of the newly released "Prince of Persia: Lost Crown". Map is autorecorded and the "maps" you find on your own unlock the regions you haven't explored yet and/or highlight unlocables you missed.There is also little variability in battle. You have one weapon, while you could instead be having so many different types of weapons. Your ship also has one fixed shape. While there is battle variability in terms of the bullet-hell enemy situation, I would like to have more agency as a player over how my ship looks like and fights in battle.  See Nova Drift for a counter example. Same space ship twin stick shooter battle setting, but with 8 or so hull designs and 100s of different type of weapons.So, while I could live with the little variability in ship shape and weapon type, I just can't afford to invest 10 extra hours to memorize the map. This game is simply not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: simply can not think of anything bad about this game. it excels in everything it goes for. even though it doesn't try anything particularly new, one area which really carries the game for me is the enemy variety. there's a massive number of little unique miniboss-type battles in the game that you see once and that's it. and even the basic enemies have a great variety and evolve over the course of the game. in addition to that, the exploration and progression is just perfect. there's a concise but challenging post-game section which leads to a true ending. even though this game doesn't have much of a story, the true ending still genuinely surprised me. did not expect this to become one of my favorites this year but here we are.

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:- Exploration is fun AND engaging. The game never enters this awkward late game state where you don't even look at enemies you come across while doing objectives. Here, you have to always be aware of bullets that might be coming from enemies off screen.- The upgrades to both the offensive and defensive combat powers feel great.- Bosses are challenging because of their unique phases with lots and lots of bullets to dodge.- I really liked that they went with spaceships as characters. They do beeps and boops and have a game meachnic, which is easy to understand (e.g. a shop or a heal). And the boost mechanic makes getting from A to B pretty fast.Neutral:- The dungeons are well designed and have a nice structure and progression. They often feature smaller arenas with waves of enemies and other challenges. For the game's mechanics, this is perfect, but the dungeons are missing a unique mechanic that makes them memorable.- Secrets or buttons are mostly just hidden in walls or under rocks. It's not that exciting to find one when the last dozen were in similar places.Negatives:- Single digit player health just doesn't work. If any bullet deals 1 damage, no matter if it's a random small enemy or the big boss charge up attack, then it also doesn't really matter what you pay attention to and taking a hit is sometimes the easy way to go.

_childDocuments_.review: A hybrid of TwinStick Shooter and Bullet Hell turns out to work pretty well.This is a very charming game. Your little craft has a few individual sprites for turning so it leans over more when making tight turns. It's also very expressive so when something surprises it, little squeals and sweat beads emanate from the cockpit, it'll spin happily when achieving something, and it generally conveys that quality of being alive well.The game has an open world with the interconnectedness of a metroidvania with gated-off areas opened by abilities, but is in essence a linear game with a lot of optional paths, unlike Metroid and more like Zelda I suppose.I'm still wrestling with the accuracy of an endorsement used in the trailer, that states the game is "A really neat fusion of Zelda and Metroidvania with Bullet Hell."I'm no expert at marketing copy, but I presume getting an quote that includes Zelda and metroidvania whilst mentioning Bullet Hell, all in one pithy statement, is gold because the Bullet Hell part is kinda-true, and people love metroidvanias and are desperate for Zelda-likes.The Steam tags are much more faithful to what the game actually is. You explore, you shoot with your sticks, there are some bullet hell encounters, there are some light RPG mechanics. They could have added 'female protagonist' if they wanted some more SEO. You'll note that metroidvania is missing from those tags - cos it really isn't one.To demonstrate the point that this isn't a metroidvania - a mild spoiler... (like, really mild)You have 4 abilities that open gates in the world. You cannot get ability 2 without ability 1. You can't get ability 3 without 2, and you can't get 4 without 3. In other words, you always get your abilities in the same order. I tried to sequence break; it can't be done.Additionally, if I mention Zelda, what comes to mind? Is your first thought puzzles? Challenges? Fishing? Unskippable dialog with annoying developer-insert Owl characters? If it was grid-based world design, congrats on being so special, and hey, you might enjoy how this game honours that super special appreciation you both have for grid-based dungeons (not the overworld though, that scrolls, and most of the dungeons too for that matter.)There are no puzzles in Minishoot' Adventures. At no point does the game throw down a room with a locked door and a bunch of switches, or have you rebounding light rays, moving blocks, shooting targets, or diverting the flow of water, or whatever else you could think up.There are a number of challenges, all of which are exploration or racing challenges. For instance, a lot of routes are locked until you find a switch to open the way, and a number of dungeons need you to navigate a trapped gauntlet.The Bullet Hell shooter-ness of the game is more generous, with tons of encounters throughout. These tend to be for bosses, minibosses and large ambushes, and they're great. It's very much babbies first bullet hell, and I don't mind saying I'm no veteran. The encounters are mostly fair and can be learnt and mastered. On slower difficulties, they can be reacted to. And they're fun too - I really enjoyed dancing from gap to gap between fields of projectiles (see the trailer/pics for the cruiser, bush-boss, and squid-boss for examples.)If you're wondering how a bullet-hell works in an open world setting - it kinda doesn't. The game likes to ambush you with spawns. These tend to work better if you are locked into a room as well, but they do tend to devolve into a melee with you trying to herd a group of mobs rather than a precise encounter. In the world at large, these spawn-in encounters are made much easier for your ability find a decent choke point or burst through weaker enemies so you can get to 1:1 against a bigger mob. I think the issue is, the world doesn't scroll automatically, so there's never a time when an enemy emerges on the horizon, holds position and throws out a field of projectiles leaving a specific gap at co-ordinates x,y, then after a brief interlude throws out a different attack leaving a different gap closeby. In the boss encounters, the enemies move slowly and deliberately to allow the bullet hell to take place. In the open world, the enemies tend to move erratically, shifting their position and staying within their desired ranges. Were they also to have complicated projectile field attacks it'd be nearly impossible to avoid attacks with them moving seemingly at random, not to mention attacking en masse. There is no swarm AI here, so there's no kinda rougelike synergy between enemy attack patterns. In essence, in the open world portions, and in most dungeons outside of fixed encounters, it's not fair to say this is a bullet hell, it's just a really good fun twin stick shooter.Going back to that marketing in the trailer, I do feel that IndieArk misled everyone with the Wanderbots' quote. This game is not a metroidvania, it's a linear game in an open world with a lot of backtracking for secrets; it's got more in common with Hob than Metroid or Castlevania: Symphony. It has even less in common with the Zelda series which has always had puzzle solving, skilful and tactical combat, and experimentation at it's core. It happens that a handful of games in the Zelda series have a top-down grid based dungeon layout that this game borrows from time to time. There's this really nice single screen directly south of your starting hub for instance. Otherwise it has about as much in common with Zelda as Skyrim's lockpicking does with Oblivion's.How did we get here? I'm going to speculate it was like this - two graduate computer science BAs looking to start their career in game development teamed up and respond to an online advert for "New Game Studio Talent Needed - Work from home - Good Yuan, err, I mean Euros to be earned!!!" They proceeded to make their first game and got setup as SoulGame Studios, subsidiary of IndieArk in all but name, both entities property of some nice Chinese fellas across the globe.The first game was a success, so they made another one. This time, they poured their hearts and souls into making it the best openworld action game they could conceive of, putting in a well fleshed out world, cool boss mechanics, and tons of charm. They took this masterpiece to their European-esque Mandarins and said "hey, here's our next game", to which the publishers said "you leave to us, we sell, you wait." PR set to work handing out keys to influencers and reviewers until one came back with the most perfect, the most sublimely misinformed quotation they could hope for; what was it? "oh, something about Zelda, Metriodvania, Bullet Hell, Fusion..." and, Who said it? "it doesn't matter, I scanned their YouTube channel - seems legit" came the assurance from PR, who added through a wall of toffee and nutmeg flavoured macchiato foam, "it was a good quote."Such was the fate of Minishoot' Adventures, which has an apostrophe in the title that doesn't do anything for no good reason. The trailer guy got the call to include the confusingly misinformed endorsement from Wanderbots, shrugged a shrug that can only be shrugged when you don't care who's paying the social credit bribes, and stuck it in the trailer alongside footage of the game doing it's wonderful thing.And here we are, some 8-9 months later, and some random guy on Steam (that's me) points it all out in a Steam review that's far too long and does the developers of this amazing game no service whatsoever because he gets hung up on poor marketing.9/10 btw, really good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that I highly recommend. Calls back to the old platformers like Banjo Kazooie, Mario, and Zelda (the top-down put me in mind of Link to the Past). Steam indicated that it was similar to Hyper Light Drifter, though, which I kind of get, but the art design couldn't be more different. Pros: -Fluid controls that make playing the game an absolute joy-Cutesy but affecting design of the levels-Very little hand-holding (which can be frustrating at first, but it's usually just a matter of checking your map and retracing your steps)-Great sound design-Satisfying combat that reminds me more of Enter the Gungeon -Great leveling concepts and attainable collector goals -Exceptional level design-My experience was bug-freeCons: -As I indicated above, the lack of direction at first can be frustrating, and will see you kind of aimlessly wandering when you start. -It's a tad short; it took me about 9 hours to beat. The price and the potential to 100% it without spending 100 hours kind of offsets that, though.

_childDocuments_.review: Runs phenomenally, with no stutters and a constant 144 FPS on the RTX 3090 in Linux. I didn't try this on my Steam Deck since I just played this over the weekend and finished it rather quickly.It harkens back to SNES Zelda: A Link to the Past in terms of game play and progression. There's a set number of dungeons that open up a final dungeon. There are unlockable abilities that slowly open up the map for exploration and there's an EXP system that makes your craft better in different ways. I did like that the upgrade points could be reassigned at any time. You can be strategic as to what to prioritize in different situations, whether it be movement or damage. It plays very similar to Zelda but mixed with a twin-stick bullet hell style of gameplay. You'll be dodging streams of bullets while firing back at the enemies. It's very fast-paced.The sound track isn't very memorable, but it does have a cool toccata track for one of the bosses. The secret unlocked sound effect sounds very similar to the Zelda sound effect.It's like if Zelda and Geometry Wars were smashed together. It doesn't overstay its welcome and can be run through over a weekend. The story isn't great, but the gameplay is perfect for what it is. The different abilities you unlock really make you feel stronger and able to take on armies of enemies. 2 thumb sticks up.

_childDocuments_.review: Great combination of bullet hell that adds interesting combat to typical metroidvania formula that is executed well. There’s basically no boring backtracking to find that last upgrade and traversing map is fun. New moves you unlock aren’t the most original ones but they are done right and add a lot of joy. Passive upgrades are again typical for twin stick shooter bullet hell but because you can at any point reassign points it leaves a lot of room for experimentation or adjusting to your current needs. There’s not many puzzles and those that are there aren’t hard. It’s more about agility and perceptivity than figuring out something. Game presentation has a little bit of cartoon for small children but it’s pleasant with nice attention to details so no real complaints here. If I would need to point out something that is the weakest is probably the world setting that has a very childish approach. Cute ships living in houses that fight with frog robots and bush monsters and collect keys and magic artifacts. And I’m not against less serious presentation. I would just expect to have it more coherent - swap houses with hangars, keys with nav data and artifacts with ship parts or something in that manner. Still a great game that I highly recommend.4/5Things good to know (no spoilers):- Works great on steam deck although sometimes camera can zoom out making your ship small but still playable- You can finish collecting stuff after reaching the ending- It took me to reach 100% 11h on Advanced difficulty and around extra 2h for additional stuff- Advanced difficulty isn’t super hard. Some bosses will require a few attempts to learn the patterns and rest shouldn’t be a problem for semi advanced player
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: What if top down Zelda, but also a twin stick shooter? That's Minishoot' Adventures in its simplest form, but there's a lot more to it than simply that.The world of this game is bright and expansive, with tons to find if you want to put in the time to 100% it. On its normal difficulty, it's not super challenging and I didn't have to nearly fully upgrade or find everything to be able to best the final boss. The combat uses well established twin stick shooter methods and strikes a good balance of being challenging when it needs to, but without feeling chaotic. The world is fairly large and you aren't led by the nose between objectives, but the game's very good about organically leading you in the direction you need. I only had one part where I could say I wasn't sure where to go next, but after only about a half hour of wandering, I came across what I needed, and picked up some upgrades along the way.My only gripe is that the game does have some bugs that will creep up sometimes. I had a crash that caused it to save without a quest item having spawned in a dungeon and I had to roll back to a backup save that lost about two hours of progress. There is a Bug Report button in the menu, but it just takes you to a forum the devs are completely ignoring. Not sure why they bothered. By and large though, it's polished and runs very well.If you like exploring and twin stick combat, with a simple story that's largely told without words, this is a good time, and will go on for much longer if you want to 100% it.

_childDocuments_.review: Minishoot' Adventures is a top-down adventure/exploration game combined with a twin stick shooter. There are 3 difficulties, 3 targeting modes and a slider than can slow down the speed of the game in the accessibility menu. All of this means the game can be basically played and enjoyed by anyone. The game is quite forgiving if you are defeated, simply reloading at what I'll call your "camp" or at a save point in many dungeons. Without mentioning any names it brings back awesome vibes of a super specific Japanese console entertainment system and one of their main IP's top-down games. I had a blast playing it and recommend it to anyone interested in top-down adventure/exploration games. Overall my first run on the middle difficulty took 8-9 hours. I will play it again some day but overall its replayability isn't great, it'll be something you want to play again every handful of years(maybe), especially after you earn all of the achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a near-perfect indie game from a small dev team, well worth your money and time especially if you enjoy twin-stick shooters and Zelda-like exploration. I played the game on normal difficulty and found it to be challenging without being punishing. The shooting feels tight and the exploration is fun -- only a couple of times was I unsure where to go. It's cool to dig for secrets between dungeons, and I was sure to collect everything before fighting the final boss. The game oozes polish, with nice UI/menus and bold/charming graphics. Pacing is also well done. Upgrades and leveling come at a steady clip up until the very end of the game. Average players will get 8-10 hours out of the main adventure depending on how many side objectives you want to complete. But there is also some post-game content, as well as the harder difficulty if your first playthrough is on normal. Sometimes you don't need an epic open world $70+ game with 100s of hours of content. In fact, I prefer smaller games with hand-crafted experiences, especially when they are polished to a shine like this one. Don't skip out on this delightful game! (Better chances for a sequel LOL.)

_childDocuments_.review: Played to true completion, normal difficulty entirely on Steam Deck. If you can believe it I did in the official dock at native 4K initially just to test but I don't think it ever dropped below 30fps except for one minor technical issue I will describe below.This is such a great idea for a Zelda-like. Taking the top down exploration and item collection of a Zelda game and merging it with a twin-stick (light) bullet hell. And it plays great with tight controls, good collectable powerups, and a flexible skill tree. As you fight you will level up which gives you points to invest in the tree and you are free to reallocate at any time which can be very useful in some scenarios, i.e. dumping points temporarily in speed for the race challenges.The art is simple but effective and the friendly ships are all charmingly animated. There is a very good visual design of all the elements making picking out enemies and their types easy and bullet trajectories, hit boxes and fade out very easy to read.The music is most ambient stuff that fits the mood but here and there it just hits you with this awesome stanky synth (in a good way) and I really liked it.As noted the experience was mostly smooth but I did encounter 3 instances where, after the game had been running for an hour or so, it appeared to freeze up even though the music was still playing. Turns out if I held a button long enough it would eventually respond like it was advancing one frame every 10 seconds or so. Even weirder if I managed to get it back to the main menu it would immediately fix itself without quitting the game. It's like there's some edge case where the game logic gets in a loop and it's weird. Either way, no progress was lost so for me this was a very minor point but I'm mostly noting it here so the devs might see it as a report.If you like Zelda and especially if you like twin-stick shooters then this one is a no brainer. And even if you're not a huge fan of the latter or not great at them then do know that not only is there an easy difficulty setting, there are also toggles for invincibility and infinite stamina if you get really stuck and need to get through a jam. This game was clearly a labor of love an oozes soul, and it's amazing it was made by just two people. Two thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 for what what a highest value indie game can be.Easily the most enjoyable and surprising game I have played in 2024.As a game designer myself I can't believe how 2 dev pulled off this little miracle - it is packed with brilliant ideas, great presentation, silky smooth control, expert level design and dozens of hours of non repetitive content.One word, KUDOS. I wish wholeheartedly that this gem will find a much larger audience.(PS. I will buy this game again on NS without hesitation)
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: I adored this game thoroughly. I was immediately sold from the demo, and bought it as something to play on my Steam Deck when I saw it got verified, but I got so engrossed in it that I never even booted it on the Deck.It somehow scratched the itch for a classic Zelda game and a bullet hell at the same time, and the amount of polish on this little game blew me away. The movement and combat feel extremely fluid, and that combined with the ability to upgrade and downgrade your abilities at any time made it exciting to explore different builds, even mid-combat. The visuals and UI are so dang smooth and appealing. The world has plenty of secrets to discover if you want to explore a little extra, even giving an item to help find everything for completionists. The main game took me just over 5 hours to 100%, and then there was a little bit of extra post-game content that was a fun little challenge.I never thought I'd be saying this, but Minishoot' Adventures has been one of my favorite games of the year, and I highly recommend checking it out. Looking forward to going back to replay it on the harder difficulty one day on my Deck. And looking forward to future games from these devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic blend of twin stick shooter and Metroidvania with a light coat of Zelda influence. _childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: WOWWOWWOWI don't even like bullet hells, but this is one of the best zelda-like adventure games of all time, period, full stop.What an awesome implementation of a genre fusion.A 10/10 must play for any classic adventure game or shoot em up enthusiast.Level design 10/10Controls 10/10Music 10/10Sound 10/10Story exists and not-quite-characters are super cuteYou won't be able to put it down!!

_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Just magnificent. Nothing big and flashy, but it sets out with a great, well-scoped concept and executes on it perfectly. Expertly designed. Every action feels great. _childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Better than expected! The right game at the right time for me. The difficulty adjustments are perfect, anyone can enjoy without needing trainers or cheats if you jsut wan tto breeze through.Excellent exploration and general desing.Is it me or there is the item sound from Rise of the Triad (1994) in this game?Will definitively complete this little gem! _childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: This is my personal GOTY. I enjoy it so much. A shoot'em up bullet hell combined with a Zelda adventure, I love it. It is so polished from the stylized graphics to the sound design. Shooting and destroying enemies and items in the levels feels so satisfying. There is exploration, puzzles, time based racing challenges, boss fights…What I highly appreciate in this game is what a lot of shoot'em ups do wrong: the auto collection of upgrade crystal. So when you destroy enemies, they leave behind crystal shards that you collect to upgrade your ship. You can fly over them to collect them or after a short time, they auto collect. Here comes what this game does right: they don't fly to your ship, they fly to your ruby shaped level up UI. In other shoot'em ups they fly to your ship, and when you are in the middle of a bullet hell battle it can get so confusing because bullets and collectibles fly towards your ship and you don’t know which one you need to avoid. But not in this game and I am so grateful for that design decision. Up to now there is not a single thing that bothers me. Thank you developers for this awesome game!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Shoot 'em up bullet hell style gameplay combines with a top-down Zelda-like approach to world design in this fantastic blend of genres. The movement is quick and snappy, the combat is frantic yet kinetic, and the core exploration adds a delightful layer of discovery on top. Easily one of my favorite games of the year!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: Simple but good 2D art. 7.9 out of 10Music: Good music with some memorable tracks. 8.5 out of 10Controls: Works well but since it's a twinstick shooter, having a controller with buttons on the back will help for easier access to some skills. Unfortunately since I don't have one of these controllers (played on a dualshock 4), using some skills during battles was a bit awkward, because I had to remove my thumb from the right analog stick to press some of the face buttons, which makes it impossible to aim. 8 out of 10.Gameplay: Really good most of the time, the player ship's movements are smooth and makes both exploration and combat fun. Not much to complain here except for two things:When you fall into the water or a pit, your ship respawns in some random place near where you fell off without any invincibility frames, and so falling off during combat usually means getting hit by some enemy or bullet as soon as you respawn.Another problem is that enemies shatter in pieces when they're destroyed, and they also leave some red crystal fragments on the floor. During chaotic fights against many enemies, it becomes difficult to quickly know exactly what is destroyed enemies' pieces, crystal fragments or enemies bullets.8.5 out of 10Story: Interesting story about ancient spaceships and holy scarabs. 7 out of 10Conclusion:Excellent game that combines twinstick shooter controls with metroidvania progression.Final rate: 8.2 out of 10
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: The most fun I have had in years, so well thought out, really well presented and super tight controls, generally just a super fun time.  Enjoyed it so much double dipped played through on my main PC, then played through again on the Steam Deck on advanced mode to 100% achievements.  One of those games you wish you could wipe your mind and do it again!Thank you for such a fun time, I salute the Devs, more please! take a bow Soul Game Studio.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game at an excellent price. Sale or no sale, it's worth the money by far. _childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: I am not normally someone who plays bullet hells -but this game was really designed so that all different player types could have fun! Sometimes on more challenging bosses I would use the assisted firing feature but for the most part I was able to play on my own. I prefer controller for the movement in this game. _childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastically addictive twin stick shooter. I picked it up thinking it would be a time filler, but I couldn't put it down.It is so easy to get sucked into seeing what is around the next corner and the combat is smooth and instinctive with just enough depth to be challenging. It's also not afraid to let you wander into challenges that you might not be ready for yet. From a two person dev team it's a real achievement. Strong recomendation!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a top-down bullet-hell game, with a map and screen layout which is reminiscent of OG Zelda.  It's even got some dungeons to explore, each with its own ability to unlock and use to then explore more of the map.  I enjoyed it a lot.  There are different levels of difficulty to help players (or make them hurt).  In about 8.5 hours, I'd completed the game on 'medium' difficulty and very nearly gotten everything.  Graphics are solid, game mechanics are good, the boss fights are generally well thought out, and overall it is a fun experience.If I had to complain about anything, I was troubled more than a couple times by screen transitions pulling back the view until your ship/character is about 60% of its regular size and that throws me every time.  One section in particular I very nearly always lose track of my ship amongst a sea of enemy fire, and that enemy fire is a one-shot.  I wish I had control over the zoom in/out, because in a bullet hell that inconsistency hasn't been very fun.  Thankfully, these transitions are very limited.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: I didn´t expect that i like this game so much. It is really fun. Exploration is fun and rewarding. Fighting ist accurat and so satisfaying. everything about this game is really polished and accurat. It took me around 12 h to complete the game 100 %. All doable in one Playthrough without guides. The Game guides you really well.  Im not a native speaker, so sry for any mistakes.Give this game a try, really.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend Minishoot' Adventures because it is a very finely tuned experience; it knows what it has to offer, executes it incredibly well, and doesn't overstay its welcome.Minishoot' Adventure is a 2D Zelda-style adventure where you play as a little ship. You move with the left stick and shoot with the right stick. You explore the not-too-large world, level up, defeat dungeon bosses, and gain new abilities. The controls and gameplay are very simple. What's unique is the blend of this type of adventure game with twin-stick shooting and how well they work together in this game.The strengths of this game are exploration and combat, both of which are very simple and satisfying. I really enjoyed exploring the world and finding all of the items. Every path has some kind of reward, and the reward felt appropriate for the effort. Movement in combat is tight. Enemy bullets rarely feel unavoidable. As you progress in the game, the enemies become more difficult to deal with and you gain more ability to work with. The pacing of the game was perfect for me. The world opens up as you progress but never reveals too much at once. The game expected me to get better but I never hit a wall that tested my skill and patience.Some features that I appreciated:What to expect:

A lot of games you upgrade your stuff and then fighting mobs feels less rewarding. Every mob gave me xp that I wanted til the very end. I'm not sure why they delete your save file when you finish... They do ask you 10 times if you are sure... but why still?? I don't really care b/c I was done with the game it just seemed odd.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: So what exactly is Minishoot' Adventures?Have you ever looked at the legend of Zelda and thought to yourself "Man, what if there was Zelda but as a twin stick shooter with a levelling system allowing us to upgrade or downgrade at will our abilities in a seemless world?" Me neither, and yet, this is pretty much what this game is.While the progress is mostly linear (you need to do the dungeon in a certain order), the between dungeon allow you to freely explore the world with the newer abilities that you unlocked with time to gain secret and other neat stuff.The game also got three difficulty options and even some option to make you only needing to hold down the button to shoot while the aiming is done automatically if you so wish it.Honestly, this game was truly delightful
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Minishoot' Adventures is a fun, relatively short game that deftly combines the dungeon exploration and connected overworld features of a Zelda game with twin stick shooter gameplay. It has a fair level of challenge but is not overly difficult in the way that a classic SHMUP is. If you are frustrated with a particular boss or section of the game, there is an upgrade tree that allows you to respec your points as needed. Overall, I had a really good time with this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Great game ! Tons of things to discover and the difficulty and the rythm of progression is perfectly tuned  - never too easy (in the harder difficulty mode), never too hard either (I failed many times, but not 10 times in a row). And there is always some progression made and some interesting new unlocks during every play session. Really well tuned so that it always feels great from beginning to end: even as the character become more powerful, the challenges encountered scale just right from beginning to end. As a bonus the music and soundscape are great too. Really worth playing this adventure !
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely good game.  As others have said it's a mix of a twin stick shooter and a Zelda game.  The game has a very good pace, I never once felt bored in my 8 hours, you're consistently getting new upgrades just once you have gotten used to your previous upgrade, all the way to the end at which point the post-game content gives you a good challenge where you have to utilize everything.  Music's good, art's great.  I am racking my brain trying to think of cons I can list here to have a balanced review but I am coming up empty, I only have positive feelings towards this game.  10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun Zelda-esque schmup game with a skill tree whose secrets was fun to attempt to find, and every powerup felt impactful. It offers plenty of challenging encounters, but I never felt it went  far, even at the very end of the game where most games usually do just that when they implement the same thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: A great adventure game with an unfortunate name XDAfter 10 minutes in the demo, I jumped out and bought it. I really enjoyed this game and recently finished it on normal difficulty. There's a nice progression with various upgrades, and the controls are sharp and responsive. The boss fights were fun, with some great 'bullet hell' moments.It's not story-heavy at all, but you'll slowly be given visual hints as to who you are and what you're doing.It's a great game that I'm looking forward to playing through again on hard. Minishoot Adventures has a great foundation/design that could be used for DLC and/or a sequel, which I'd happily pay for.Pros:- A unique mix of 2D Zelda and twin-stick/multidirectional shoot 'em ups- Polished game and interface, with cohesive art design and thoughtful settings/options- Well-balanced difficultyCons:A couple minor cons that come to mind, though nothing major..- The name is too generic. Sorry but "Minishoot' Adventure" sounds like the name of a crappy old 80s LCD game XDWhen I first saw the poster for the game on Steam, I almost dismissed it instantly. The apostrophe ' makes it even more weird.- I would've liked a little more variety with enemies. The bush enemies, for example, were great. - The south forest section of the map has very few enemies. I thought maybe it would fill up with enemies later in the game, but it didn't happen. Seemed a bit strange.Try the demo, see if you like it :)
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Couldn't put this one down. It oozes charm, is extremely well polished, and is an absolute blast to play. The main content is enough to justify the price and your time, but there's also a really nice endgame with additional challenges. It's one of only a few games I've played in the past few years that felt like the 100% experience was worth it. Congrats to the team; thanks for the amazing game, and I hope we get a sequel once you're proper rested!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said, this is a twinstick shooter combined with Zelda-like exploration. And it works really well! The sense of exploration is excellent, and the world is dense with secrets. You have to collect map pieces to fill in the world map, and since these are well hidden, you will often be forced to explore huge areas with no map. I really like this! It makes the world feel immense!The shooting and RPG elements also work well. I turned the difficulty up to its highest setting, and the so far it isn't too bad. I have to pay attention to the bullets, and sometimes I die, but it never seems impossible.The cute graphics, alien landscapes, and anthropomorphic ships remind me of Fantasy Zone, and I expect that is intentional on the part of the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic compact experience. All my playtime was on the Steam Deck and it played wonderfully. Boss fights were challenging, elite enemies were plentiful and also provided enough challenge of their own. My only gripe is I kept getting lost and going in circles and not completely sure where to go to next. I think the map could use a badge system to leave notes. Other than that when it clicks, exploring feels pretty good and finding how they scatter secrets around felt satisfying to find out.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Waited till I 100% this game before writing - it's an absolute brilliance of a game and one of my favorites to come out in years.The world design, bullet hell pattern complexity, and overall leveling mechanics and abilities are like nothing I've played before. The only negative thing I can say about this game is the bullet noise sfx - it's incredibly irritating and I wish they would have used another sound. Thankfully you can mute this in the settings, but just wish I didn't have to. Review time doesn't display correctly, but I put about 25-30 hours on this game for 100% on a single advanced difficulty playthrough. If you want all achievements just start from advanced and max out on your first play - there is no NG+; in the end game you wipe your save file as part of the story. Pick this one up, it's an absolute steal for $15.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful, 12 hour Zelda/bullet hell mashup. Minishoot Adventures' tight design propelled me ever forward, compelling me to keep playing to find one more secret before bed. There are so many fun upgrades and new ways to explore as you help rebuild a small, central HUB, with each rescued inhabitant adding some new way to spend currency, unlock lore, etc. With multiple endings, a post-game arena, and a story that is more heartfelt than I thought a purely ship-based cast of characters had any right to be, Minishoot Adventures is an absolute hidden gem and delight.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun game that combines twin-stick shooters and old-school Zelda-esque exploration. This game was a genre combination I honestly had never even considered, and the execution was essentially flawless. I spent just under 12 hours to 100% complete it, which normally falls under my general 2 hours per dollar spent metric, but it was so charming and well crafted that I am happy I was able to experience it. I recommend this to anyone who enjoys twinstick shooters or old-school exploration.Note: The game is relatively easy if you are a veteran of the genre, even on the hardest difficulty. And for exploration focused people, it is not super in depth, though there are some secrets to be found.Overall though, I give this a solid 10/10 on a good day, and a 8/10 if I am feeling more critical. Very much worth the price if you enjoy this type of game and can afford the cost, and 100% worth it on sale. Keep an eye on these devs, I think they will produce further gold for a long time to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a very pleasant surprise.First of all, it's a perfect Steam Deck game. Except at the very end, in the arena, where the performance is not as smooth. I also faced 2 freezes that forced me to shut down the game during my 9 hour journey. Fortunately I didn't lose much progress.Bit of a personal preference, but I also recommend turning off the lens filter.This game strikes a great balance between arcade and progression with its unique mix of genres. Creating something that feels this way, that is so easy to pick up and play but at the same time sets you on an adventure with such a progression is not easy to accomplish, so kudos to the devs.The biggest compliment I can give this game is that, even though I have a huge backlog, this game grabbed in such a way that I pretty much exclusively played it from start to end.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: I can't remember the last time I locked in on a game with zero distractions for 7+ hours in one sitting. The mechanics, the music, super intuitive exploration and discovery of new things, a cutesy but clearly Zelda-y storyline, secrets obvious enough that a W+M1 brute like me can figure out, all of it so satisfyingly clicks together. Difficulty is a little one-note at times and some bosses are a little too tanky (I've had a few instances of 'okay I solved the pattern can we move on' and early encounters with red/purple enemies take forever to finish) but I haven't had particular trouble with or disliked  anything in the first 2/3-3/4 of the game, or had to reset from super deep in any encounter yet. Overall it's great, probably a 95-97/100 game.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: A twin stick shooter with adventure elements reminiscent of the top down Zelda games. If that piques your interest at all, you should buy it. The twin stick shooter elements aren't too demanding though you can change the difficulty to meet your needs. It's a fair game though those bullets sure do follow you. This isn't a crazy twin stick shooter though, so don't think it's something like a Treasure game. But it's a fantastic game and full of polish and charm. Give the demo a shot and know it's more of that but even better.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Saw skurry playing and looked fun so I got it. Fun little game, well worth the price. It ran really smooth with the exception of the post game arenas which were nearly unplayably laggy. I run steam deck so it’s not the best hardware but considering I can run helldivers it seems like a top down shooter shouldn’t be an issue.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Very simple game with lots to love. A little on the easier side if you're familiar with bullet hells, but if you set the difficulty to advanced you'll still have a good time. _childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Minishoot Adventures was a game I had no prior knowledge of, it was just something I randomly found on Steam one day. Bullet hell boss fights and old-school Zelda exploration works really well, and I'd love to see even more unlikely genre combinations like this. The world and lore of this game was really interesting too, something I wasn't expecting being a cute lil' spaceship guy. A truly delightful game; would recommend easily!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Loving the game so far. It's a great mix of Zelda and twin stick shooting, but definitely has its own thing going for it. Bosses are great with some bullet hell action. The map is well design and traversing it is fun. Animations are great (how can an inanimate ship show so much emotion?), as is the sound. I'm a huge fan of the upgrade system as well. Haven't finished it yet, but I'm confident it will continue to be a great game. Playing on Steamdeck and it runs great.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: What it says in the box. It's well designed with pleasant presentation and a good soundtrack.It did feel a bit too clean and smooth to become one of my favorites. Probably because there's barely any plot and worldbuilding to speak of, and what there is was extremely garden-variety and unsurprising.Although it lacked that certain edge, it's easily worth the money. Especially for zelda/metroidvania fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: First review I have ever left on Steam. Picked this up during the Summer Sale, but even at full price this game is still worth it. Not a fan of bullet hell shooters in the slightest, but combining with Zelda-like exploration and upgrades has me hoping for a sequel. Complete joy to play, can really feel the passion that was put into this project. This has been by far my favorite gaming experience this year even though it took me less than seven hours to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Games like these are why we play indie games. It's a cute, unassuming game that absolutely delivers on gameplay. It has the excellent exploration of the early, top-down Zelda titles with twinstick shooter action. The world feels massive. The quality of life features are excellent and many are dripfed through unlockables, which makes your progress in the game feel super meaningful. _childDocuments_.review: A Refreshing Blend of Genres Done Well     This game is in many ways like the original Legend of Zelda except Link is now a spaceship and you get into fights with other ships that result in something closer to Galaga, Centipede, or some other '80's arcade top-down shooter game.  In essence, you are introduced to the world, and you head off in whatever direction you want (although some areas are gated by powers you gain along the way) not knowing what you may find in any given cave.  It does provide a slight bit of guidance by indicating the location of the next dungeon and its means of opening it on your map, but otherwise, you are on your own.The Good:-Controls are excellent, the twin-stick movement/aim works really well and you have firm control over your ships movement everywhere (except where you're not supposed to of course)-Visuals are nicely animated and even in the heaviest bullet storms you can still see yourself clearly enough without losing track of the fight-Audio is alright with decent music and sound fx-Doesn't overstay its welcome; I completed everything in the game (including the post-game) on the middle difficulty in about 11 hours and had a great time for about all of it.  I'd like more, but that's where you should be left at the end.The Bad:-Really just a technical issue.  The game crashed on me a few times when I entered a newly opened cave, and sometimes glitched if I tried to call up the map too quickly after exiting a cave, but everything worked fine again upon reloading it.The Bottomline:     This is a fantastic effort and result of a game by essentially 2 persons that is well-worth the time and efforts of the player.  Lots of optional upgrades and 'objects' to find, several cleverly designed dungeons, temples, and caves, and incredibly fun gameplay.  The game respects the player's time with minimal backtracking, and provides sufficient upgrade resources for you to proceed at your own pace without grinding.  I had a great time with it and compliment the developers on their results.  If you like Legend of Zelda and top-down shooter type games, odds are you'll have a good time here.  Be sure to check out the free demo if you are uncertain.  Good gaming to you all!

_childDocuments_.review: Minishoot Adventures is a really good game. Pretty basic, but absolutely polished where it needs to be.The game-play is pretty much perfect, at least in the Normal/Original difficulty. Hard, but manageable. No dodging, but the movement can always get you out of a situation, and if you get hit, it will be your fault. Never used the automatic shooting option, but hey, I can't complain about an accessibility option.The movement is probably the best aspect of the game. I found it so good to just roam through areas I've already been through because it really feels like gliding. Some areas are more slippery, but the game isn't too punishing, unless it's an area that uses one-shot bullets, but those only appear like 6 times max.This game is a Metroidvania, and about half of the power-ups completely change how the game is played. The others are pretty much only used to open up something, but are still incredibly useful in combatThere are a lot of extra power-ups that you don't have to obtain, but are incredibly satisfying. Some of them are default powers in other games, but going through most of the game without them makes it feel so rewarding. I will not go into detail, but the way you obtain one of them is such a video-game thing to do and also probably the most memorable part of the game. The power-up you get is also the most powerful one.The only issue I had was on my way to the second boss: The game lasted me for about 11 hours. I 100% the map, but still haven't done the post-game stuff. Maybe I'll even try to do the higher difficulty to get all of the achievements.8 or 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: HESITANT recommend. Too many reviews here are ignoring some really big problems this game has. I ultimately recommend it because there's plenty here to love, and I won't drone on about that since that's what every other review here does (and I agree with much of it) So for anyone looking for a slightly more critical review, here ya go:Color: there are only a couple types of projectiles, but they are all shades of orange and red. This is frankly unacceptable for even people without colorblindness, let alone anyone else. Even on explorer difficulty it becomes very very hard to track a lot of the action.Difficultly scaling: not sure I've ever played a wonkier game when it comes to this. I found myself playing the first half of the game on Advanced (I'm a geometry wars vet), but then I hit a completely inexplicable difficulty spike in the 3rd dungeon and popped back down to Original. No biggie there. Except now the game throws a ton of instakill projectiles (that are kinda pink?) and double damage projectiles. Not too crazy until they become overused in the last third of the game and suddenly it's more of a "ship dodger" than a shop shooter. Additionally, the difficulty levels are great QoL, except that they only control projectile and enemy speed. Please tell me why it takes an agonizingly long time to kill every darker tinted enemy even with max damage, rate, bullet speed, and supershot? The last monster closets of the game are just about as fun as a root canal. It's just locked section after section with instakill projectiles on narrow walkways. You don't die if you fall off, unless you respawn on the platform that's covered in instakill balls.This makes even the explorer difficultly level incredibly tedious to play. Additionally there are some big time low effort sections that were very disappointing. All 3 (not 4) of the dungeons look identical and could really be the same dungeon. All of the mini dungeon areas are visually distinct but the main dungeons are functionally identical. Very weird choice.Equally weird is the choice to crib one of the lamest Zelda game structures. So we get to the 4th dungeon and it's not a dungeon, we just get the unlock and move on. This is lazy as ♥♥♥♥ when Nintendo does it and was downright bizarre in a game like this. So I can recommend it because there's enough stuff to like (please see other reviews for the good stuff), but definitely know what to expect if any of the above sounds dicey to you.  I sincerely hope the dev team makes a sequel or spiritual successor and makes better UI and balance decisions.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to say after randomly coming across this game in my discovery queue, it's a really fantastic game among so many other indie games and deserves any recognition it gets. It was short but so sweet, and you guys did everything very well.The sound design is amazing, you really know how to reward people with great audio and visuals, puzzles are intuitive and encourage exploration, and having grown up with those old retro titles, this really feels like a spiritual successor to the sort of gaming that emerged from the late 80's and 90's and takes us back to a time where games weren't afraid to explore new ideas and game styles. It doesn't matter that it follows in the footsteps of a tried and true formula for a particular genre of gaming because it meshes unique gameplay with a fun story that's easy to digest for new and old players.If a Minishoot Adventures 2 ever comes out, I'll be there to get it because of how impressive this game was.This game features:- Gradual Power Ramp through XP earned by killing enemies. Spend on talents and re-talent as you see fit anytime.- Permanent Treasures which provide passive boosts to various aspects of gameplay found all over the map and in dungeons.- Fast Travel on the Overworld Map (Once you find a certain something which lets you do it.)- Mini Races! (Completely Optional, but worth doing. Trust me, I'm a Moose.)- Variable Difficulty, (I recommend Normal first and then trying it on Advanced, but there is an Easy Mode as well.)- A killer soundtrack, you will love it instantly.- Checkpoints at all areas of interest so you can try over and over should you fall in combat.- Intuitive and smooth controls, never felt janky or counterintuitive. The game does recommend a controller but keyboard and mouse works just fine, did not encounter any difficulty due to the setup.- Short and Sweet, to the point. The game can be completed very quickly if you only focus on the main story, but even with exploration and a little intuition I was able to complete the main story in 9 hours, with plenty still left to do. Great for someone who doesn't have a lot of time or a person who wants something new to plow through in a day. Won't elaborate so no spoilers. :)If you enjoy bullet hell type games, metroidvania style exploration and acquisition, and a classic story about being the hero, this is the game for you. Couldn't recommend it enough!

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful experience from start to finish!This game feels like a true oldschool video game where you can lose yourself in for a few hours to forget everything and just have fun, but enhanced with modern and fluid gameplay.A perfect blend between a Zelda-like adventure game and a shoot'em up with a little bullethell sprinkled on.I can recommend this game fully with nothing really negative to say!I can imagine this being a very forgiving entrypoint into the world of "shmups" and "bullet hell" games for some folks since even beginners to this genre should have no problem on the easy and normal difficulties.I played on "advanced" difficulty and found that it nails a perfect balance between challenge and fairness throughout the open-world campaign, with a nice steady ramp-up in difficulty.Nonetheless the difficulty can be adjusted on-the-fly if needed, however up to a certain point you'll need to stay on advanced difficulty to get a certain achievement for advanced mode.After that point there is also an arena-style gameplay which is not my cup of tea and was getting a little frustrating, but it is very doable with a handful of tries on normal difficulty.Moving around feels extremely fluid, satisfying and frankly even fun at times.The input feels direct and reacts instantly, any mistake I made while moving/dodging felt like I had only myself to blame and not the game.The artstyle is very nice and crisp, lots of color yet easy on the eyes.Enemies and bullets are recognizeable at a glance, even in busy situations.Level design and exploration is well done, reminiscent of classic Zelda games, many things to do and discover, and for all the completionists there are some helpful upgrades available later on to see if there is anything you missed.Top notch sound design, from the cute little reactions of your ship, to the impact and firing sounds and movement, everything has a little acoustic feedback that makes everything feel very "alive" for the lack of a better word.The music is pretty good, I wish there was a downloadable soundtrack on Steam or Bandcamp though.One curious point I want to mention though is that the Overworld/Town track is basically an altered version of Disasterpeace's "Adventure" track from the FEZ OST. The similarity is so blatant that I refuse to believe this is a mere coincidence. The track for the "Woods" area is also sounds very suspiciously similar to something I have heard in FEZ before.All the other tracks sounded "original" though and fit the overall theme really nicely, and those did not trigger such a massive "deja vu" for me.About 8,5 h for campaign completion (to trigger the achievements to complete the game) and collecting most upgrades and secrets.For full completion I'd say about 10-14h, I 100%ed the game at 16,7h but that is with some added hours AFK time.So, again, can fully recommend to anyone interested even slightly in Zelda-likes and/or shmups!

_childDocuments_.review: Highlights:Minishoot' Adventures offers a unique blend of genres, seamlessly integrating elements from metroidvania, bullet hell, and RPG mechanics into a cohesive and enjoyable experience. The fusion of these genres is surprisingly effective, creating a game that feels both fresh and familiar. Exploring the game world and finding upgrades is consistently rewarding, and the experience system, which allows players to strengthen their ship by defeating enemies, adds a satisfying layer of progression.One of the standout features is the flexibility in respeccing points. This allows players to adapt their ship’s abilities to different challenges on the fly. For example, I found myself boosting my ship’s movement speed to outrun a fairy, then shifting back to a more offensive build for combat encounters. This dynamic customization keeps the gameplay engaging and allows for creative problem-solving.Visuals and Combat:Visually, Minishoot' Adventures excels with its clear, hand-drawn graphics. The distinct separation between projectiles and the environment ensures that the action is easy to follow, even in the most hectic bullet hell scenarios. The smooth animation and detailed artwork enhance the overall aesthetic, making the game a pleasure to look at.Combat, while simple, is immensely satisfying. Enemies fire various bullet patterns that require the player to deftly navigate and avoid. The fast-paced encounters are well-designed, with enemies having reasonable health pools that keep fights from dragging on. The level design adds another layer of strategy, as every bit of cover can be used to dodge enemy fire. The precise controls for both movement and shooting contribute to the fluidity and responsiveness of the combat, making each skirmish feel rewarding.Player Agency:Minishoot' Adventures smartly incorporates player agency in determining the game’s difficulty. The ability to choose between manual, assisted, or automatic firing modes, along with adjusting the game's speed, allows players to tailor the experience to their preferences. This thoughtful design ensures that the game remains accessible to a wide audience without compromising on challenge for more experienced players.Drawbacks:One of the few downsides to Minishoot' Adventures is the presence of unskippable dialogue and brief cutscenes scattered throughout the game. While these elements contribute to the storytelling and atmosphere, the inability to skip them can disrupt the pacing and become an annoyance, especially on repeated playthroughs.Conclusion:Minishoot' Adventures is a delightful and innovative game that successfully merges multiple genres into a harmonious whole. Its engaging gameplay, visual clarity, and strategic combat are complemented by a flexible progression system and player-adjustable difficulty. Despite the minor inconvenience of unskippable dialogue and cutscenes, the game stands out as a unique and enjoyable experience. Whether you’re a fan of metroidvania, bullet hell, or RPG mechanics, Minishoot' Adventures has something to offer and is well worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Minishoot' Adventures is an absolute treat of a game, and one that hooked me even more than I thought it would. It’s a beautiful and charming game with a very good soundtrack, and it’s priced fairly. It can be relatively challenging at times, but it’s always fair. I never found myself really struggling with any areas, however, and the difficulty in general allows you to cruise casually through the game without getting frustrated.I found a lot to love in this game, and I had a great time playing it on my OLED Steam Deck. The only issue I had was that there were some pretty big FPS drops during the more intense scenes. That’s fine, as I know the Steam Deck is a relatively low-powered device, but keep it in mind if you plan on playing it there. I finished the game on the Steam Deck, clearing the whole map and (as of now) getting all but 3 achievements, and it was absolutely playable. I started with a locked 90 FPS and a 90 Hz refresh rate, but soon had to lower the refresh rate to 60 Hz and lock the FPS there. It stayed solid for most of the game, but towards the end I had a couple of areas dropping into the low 40s.I don’t want to finish this short review on a negative note, so I’ll say again how much fun I had playing it. There’s a demo, so there’s really nothing stopping you from at least giving it a go.
