I feel like this game is a gem robbed of a better soundtrack/FX, it has so much potential but gameplay feels "cheap" paired with the thin mystic atmosphere. Please don't take this as a harsh critic, it's quite the opposite, it does SO MANY THINGS well, it feels and plays amazingly, I highly recommend it but I'm leaving here a suggestion for improvement.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: A game that's just darn good at making you feel happy.You play as a little space fighter-type character, akin to Twinbee or Opa-Opa from Fantasy Zone, who exudes quite a bit of personality for a character who never speaks (or even has a face); just the happy little spin he does upon achieving a victory is tough to resist, and makes you eager to power up, track down his fellow sentient machines and fight off the baddies.Along the way there's a good amount to stick your nose cone into whilst you explore the world, as hidden paths, rooms and treasures abound; even when you find yourself a bit stuck every battle brings you closer to your next level-up, which gives you points that can be freely allocated (and re-allocated as the situation demands) across various stats to make you more formidable and better able to handle the threats you encounter as you venture off the beaten path.Exchanging hot lead with your opponents generally feels well-tuned, though when using a controller an analog stick isn't  as precise as a d-pad for micro-dodging; for most of the game it's not a huge deal, but some of the tougher fights can make your thumb well and truly tense up. Enemies and their shots can also sometimes be hidden by trees and other foreground elements, which can lead to some frustrating hits.Outside of that, though, exploring, discovering, battling, and learning feel like the proverbial warm blanket; rewards large and small arrive frequently and keep pressing you forward, shedding light onto previously-hazy mechanics and opening things up for even more engaging (mini)shooting. It's not likely to impress those who truly relish the raw challenge of an old-school arcade shmup 1CC or "how'd anyone do this without a guide?" puzzle, but there's definitely genuine love for the old guard present here, albeit repackaged with accessibility in mind.If any of this leaves a pleasant ringing in your internet ears, give that demo a try, chances are you'll want to see more.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Great game in many regards. You learn everything at a good pace so beginners can start easy and veterans can just proceed faster. The puzzles are not to hard but also not just there to stretch out the playtime. Backtracking is on a really nice level.Also a big plus are the different dificulties and special settings, giving everybody the best possible gaming experience. The Story is nothing special but still nice and also not the main focus of the game in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly what it presents itself as. The gameplay is solid and enjoyable, progression is fun and addicting, and it's short enough to not overstay its welcome. It's absolutely worth $15.The downside is that there's not much more to it. You're a spaceship in budget Hyrule, and though there is a little bit of worldbuilding, expect the framework of Zelda, not the magic.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Really had fun with this.  I don't really play bullet hell games, or even this is even considered one, but it blends really well with the metroidvania genre.  I wanted to get all the achievements so I played on the hardest difficulty and it was generally fine the whole way through.If I had one complaint is that the way the game handles tracking collectables is kind of odd.  If there is something you can find, but there are, say, eight different entrances to that area, all eight have an indicator for that one thing.  It gets really confusing one what and where you actually need to go.  If the indicator was only on the nearest entrance to that thing, it would have been better.  Specially when your looking for a hidden beetle that's also in a hidden room that's party of a dungeon with several entrances.Other than that, no notes, had a real fun time with this.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice and cute graphics and sounds, interesting bosses, each with individual bullet patterns, which are not that hard to remember. Good difficulty scaling throughout the game and when changing the game settings. Loved the map exploring and secret area finding. Sometimes the game gives you a glimpse of a hidden area with intriguing treasure (going through a tunnel under it while camera slows when above the area) which makes you excited of how to get there. Just the one weapon-upgrading twin-stick shooter I love! Will definitely play it again in the future and try to get that last achievement!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game beginning to end. It's a great combination of action and exploration, and has enough difficulty options for pretty much anyone to enjoy the game their way. The trailers may make the action seem a bit intimidating at first glance, but the game trains you slowly but steadily to deal with the bullet hell. The ship controls are very good and tight, which helps a lot in this regard. The boss encounters have fun mechanics, and while some are a bit tough they are definitely doable.This is hands down my favorite thing I've played all year. Kudos to the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Exploring the world in this game causes the same sorts of endorphin spikes I get exploring in Elden Ring. It's rare that I get that from a Metroidvania, but this one achieves it. Everything you do in the game is fun, from the battles which start out straightforward and eventually evolve into complicated dances with your enemy... again, much like a soulslike. Movement feels both believable and fun. Your ship has momentum, which means you're constantly engaged, even in a simple task like moving across the map. You'll be making microadjustments to keep your ship on track and "drifting" around corners just because it feels good.The length is perfect too. I'm going to end up doing everything in just about 12 hours... and it's incredibly rare that I even beat a game - even more so that I 100% a game. This game made it possible for me because of the aforementioned fun injected into every activity and the fact that it never wears out its welcome.I cannot wait to see what the developer does next!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: List form for my list of pros for this game cuz idk:- The gameplay is addictive. I see myself replaying this game in a way I struggle to get back into other games. The power scaling feels really good and every upgrade feels substantial.- I love the music, it sets the mood really well. (Special shout out to the  fight music, it's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good.) And the sound effects all feel super well-constructed and fitting. Just overall a great game to have the audio on for.- The difficulty for each area is precisely designed to encourage you to explore the area, because you know if you poke around in the areas you've got, you'll probably find a lil upgrade or some XP that will make you stronger.- As a chronic futzer who needs to poke around and find all of the little secrets, I very much appreciate the item that shows you where to find the collectibles you missed.There are a couple things that bother me a little.Even though the difficulty selection says you can change the difficulty at any time, the "finish the game on _ difficulty" achievements are limited by the lowest difficulty that you use, so if you know you're really gonna wanna go for the achievements, be mindful of that. Even just starting the game on a lower difficulty and then turning it up for a bigger challenge will disqualify you from the steam achievements for the higher difficulties....and why I think this is an issue that impacts how the ending hits. (major spoilers ahead)  Anyway. I know I don't interact with media in the same way as everyone else does. I just really liked the game, but honestly my experience of the true ending really effected how I felt about the game. I hope that a little warning about how the difficulty-based achievements work can be added. I think it'll really help re-enforce the themes of the . Otherwise, I'm very happy with my experience of the game, and I hope to get to see more from SoulGame Studio.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: This a great experience, especially for such a small team! It has great pacing, where every combat encounter is split up by exploration, dungeon crawling, and racing. As a fan of bullet hell games, I would recommend other hardcore fans to play on the highest difficulty and maybe not upgrade your maximum health to the full 10 hearts, as that did feel a little lenient for my taste.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute gem that blends the exploration of classic Zelda games with the frenetic action of twin-stick shooters, creating an irresistible and addictive gameplay experience! The bullet-hell inspired encounters are intense and satisfying. A fantastic indie title that deserves all the praise it's receiving.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: To start, the visuals and movement got me hooked haha - it felt good to move around and a lot of things looked very cute.As I played on, some aspects got me more interested: enemy variety with their own bullet patterns or behavior, exploring around without a map which you can find in their respective areas (the "map" vibrates as you close in on it, and different cute things like races, the noises when you find your friends/talk with them or buy things.In the end, what was really cool were:- some really good upgrades like dashing through and that divine scarab shot at full hp- changing stats without penalty to fit the situation (I max dmg for fights, and max speed for those spirit races)- the slow transition to these corrupted enemies that do more damage and have more hp- an item that showed areas that still had items you could find, very nice for completion/exploration- the final bosses (the unchosen) and in the arena... having these corrupted versions of the plot bosses we fought previously
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Strong recommendation here. Bullet-hell with some metroidvania stylings. The game has a really good flow, you often feel like you are getting stronger, the bullets can get wild but never gets unfair, you have a stack of customization options to make the game easier or more difficult. Exploration is solid. Abilities are fun. And the post game arena mode is a great way to top it off.Dont sleep on this. Its definitely worth your time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played a twinstick shooter game for a very long time and this game just reminded me how much I used to love this type of games! The control feels extremely smooth, making the dodging of bullet hells much more enjoyable. The exploration of the map feels seamless and fun, giving me a similar vibe to what zelda and animal well gave me. The ship upgrades feel significant enough but not overpowering, making my progression feeling very rewarding and satisfying. Anyways, if you like a topdown twinstick shooter and an airship that can drift, just play this game for a good time :)
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I’ve ever played. The combat and movement are so fluid and feel outstanding. The story is a nice nudge forward, but the game doesn’t weigh you down with it. The environments are FANTASTIC to navigate, the puzzles are great. I really liked the fair checkpoint system inside dungeons. This is easy to recommend to anyone that likes video games of whatever kind.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: It's rare that I find something that hits the game-feel of multiple genres and does it well. I love twin-stick shooters and I love 2D environmental adventure games with some story baked in. So, Geometry Wars and Legend of Zelda. This game blends them both excellently in a way that I just do not want to put it down. It feel balanced, it feels excellent. I will recommend this to any and everyone.Things I love about Minoshoot' Adventures- You can reallocate upgrade points on the fly whenever you want- There's a hidden story if you find the lore tablets- All the ships feel weirdly natural for their environment- All the noises the player and the NPC ships make are adorable- The bosses are huge and I feel like I genuinely have to work to survive those encounters. - None of the bullet hell stuff feels cheap. I always feel like I'm the one at fault when a mistake is made.- Minishoot is *adorable*Pick this game up. It's *excellent*
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great game! I loved every second of it! The controls are so fluent and movement is so much fun the entire time!I like medroidvanian games in general, but often times the basic moving-around in the world is tedious and no fun. It's a perfect mix of free exploration and shoot-em-up controls! I want more games with such a great movement.Also the presentation and exploration is great in this world. This is the best game I played the entire year!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo so I knew the devs provided an invincibility option. Otherwise I wouldn’t have purchased the game. I’m not a fan of bullet-hell games. Too stressful and I suck at them. But I do enjoy exploring, discovering, and unlocking things. I’m having a great time doing my thing in the game while virtually ignoring what the enemies are trying to do to me.I really appreciate when devs create a game and allow people to play it in whatever way suits them. They earned my money with gratitude. The game is a lot of fun no matter how you play it. I give it a big thumbs up!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Such a blast, I loved this game. It was the perfect amount of exploration and discovery, balanced with a simple but fun and rewarding upgrade and combat system. It was always fun getting to a new area and finding new secrets, and going back to old areas and finding those secrets, and seeing what it all would get me. I was never frustrated at the game design (I did die quite a few times though!), and I think this is the perfect little package of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - The gameplay here is very solid and fun. Don't expect any miracles, but you're going to enjoy the 10 hours or so you'll get out of the experience (more if you replay on a higher difficulty). The game has a lovely story, a tiny bit of lore, and great mechanics (plus, the music is pretty good).All in all, it took me about 10 hours-ish to 100% the game, and I feel like that's an absolutely solid playtime for a 10$ game without a lot of replay value. You'll keep unlocking more mechanics as you go.For the achievement hunters out there - very hard to miss any achievements and progress, but there are some hidden secrets that are very fun to discover. The "characters" are pretty cool and it's really nice to see your village take shape as you save more and more of them. The difficulty does spike a bit in the final mission of the game so you should be prepared for that. However, the achievement for finishing the game on a certain difficulty is actually unlocked before the final fight, so you can play on the highest difficulty and then lower it for the endgame to get the final achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Top-down Zelda meets twin-stick shooter.  As an enormous fan of the former but not much of one of the latter, I wasn't sure how well I'd vibe with this game.  I needn't have feared though, as this game is fantastic!  Few devs have ever managed to capture the spirit of the old-school Zelda formula so wonderfully, while also adding its own unique flair to the game.  That the game was made by just two people makes the feat all the more impressive.  It's a pretty short game, taking me around 8-9 hours to 100%, but every second of it was an absolute joy.  I cannot recommend this highly enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun! Great aesthetic that draws a lot from Link to the Past. Doesn't over stay it's welcome, I got to credits is around 10 hours. Plays and runs great on the Steam Deck. I'm not a big twin stick shooter/bullet hell fan, but this game feels great and is a lot of fun to dodge around all the bullets. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Minishoot is one of the rare instances where you start a game and it's instantly one of your favorites of all time.  This is a beautiful mashup of Zelda and a bullet hell.  It sounds daft, but it's so perfect and so polished time just floats away when you start the game.  If this sounds at all interesting to you, just download and try the demo.  Either you will fall in love like I did, or be able to say you tried an amazing game that did not hit for you for free.  Whats to lose?In general I'm not good at bullet hell games, but the difficulty here is at worst moderate, so if you are inexperienced with this style of game, don't worry you CAN do this one.  The flip side of that, is that hard core bullet hell junkies will likely be bored to tears.  The exploration is wonderful, and the world feels full of secrets, exactly like the A Link to the Past did when it first came out.  There are moments in this game that dropped my jaw and filled me with wonder.  I cant say enough about how much I enjoy playing this game.Normally in a review I like to offer a few critiques of games I play, but thus far I don't have any.  The graphics are simple, but that fits the game so I cant even fault it there.  The music is, again simple and a bit understated, but that fits. My only wish is a little more color in the world as the palate is often a bit too understated for my tastes.Minishoot is an instant classic for me.  I loved this game the moment I got into it's world, and my affection has only grown since more time in the game.  Thank you to the Devs for making such a great game!  Minishoot gets my highest recomedation.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, reminds me of old-school Zelda top-downs, with a very well implemented bullet hell gameplay. The overall length is on the shorter side, but the exploration and game progression is very well crafted. I also appreciated indicators for stuff missing on the minimap to achieve 100%. _childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE:I just finished the game with 100% and, wow... what can I say. Not only it's my GOTY so far, but it's among my favourite games in general.Amazing pacing from start to finish. Fantastic exploration (the true highlight of the game), wonderful atmosphere and the world... and the most important: it's an absolute joy to play.10/10Original review:Not done with it yet, but so far it's shaping up to become my GOTY.So charming and addicting.And I can't believe how much personality this little ship has.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Oh yeah, that was a ton of fun. It took me roughly 11 hours to beat it, and it didn't overstay its welcome. I really appreciated the combination of twin-stick shooting and Zelda-like levels and exploration. I've been a fan of this publisher's previous game (Swords & Souls), and am glad to say that this one lives up to my expectations. I plan on replaying it on hard mode after I beat the arena. If there's one con, the color scheme is quite samey throughout the whole game. Granted there was a forest area, most of the game is like a desert sand color and the dungeons are purple. I would have preferred a more diverse look to the game, like a fire realm, ice realm, and others. But, it's a small gripe. Great job on the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: I never knew I need a Zelda meets Shmup in my life. Thankfully the devs were aware of this crucial lack in my life. I had a blast playing it. One of my favorite games of 2024 for sure! The sound design was really charming (as everything in the game, really). I never would have thought that the mix of these genre would work, but they sure made it work extremely well.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: If you're on the fence about this game, just try the demo! I was pleasantly surprised with the generosity and play time that the demo allowed, and it hooked me in right away. On top of that, my progress transferred over without issue. I would call this game a smooth, very polished, adventure bullet hell. Extremely enjoyable if you like faster paced combat and shooting things via twin stick shooter. The creativity keeps coming with this one. Thank you devs for making such a fun game!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: It's Legend of Zelda, but a bullet hell where you're a cute little space ship. Honestly, I don't even usually like bullet hell games, but this one is fair, giving you all the tools you need to succeed. Upgrades earned over time give you a good sense of progression, and the game gives you the freedom to refund the upgrades if you like at any time.I'd definitely recommend this one to anyone, even if you don't care for bullet hell games. It's charming, full of secrets, and a genuinely fun experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever asked yourself a question, "What if Zelda was a spaceship?", then this game is definitely for you. Minishoot' Adventures is a charming indie game that offers a delightful blend of classic action-adventure, with bullet-hell combat, creating a unique and suprisingly accessible experience. With various difficulty options and customizable gameplay settings, it's approachable even for those who might not typically enjoy bullet-hell games.The game is a competent Zelda/Metroidvania clone, delivering a short and sweet experience (~10 hours). It is a nice dopamine rush, as you will be constantly moving from one intense bullet-hell combat gauntlet to the next, unlocking new areas, items, secrets etc. The synth soundtrack, with a sprinkle of C64 SID sounds, perfectly complements the game's retro vibe. Despite its relatively short length, Minishoot' Adventures provides a satisfying gameplay loop, with the option to grind for levels and ship upgrades.However, the game isn't without its frustrations. Some encounters can be quite challenging, especially multi-phase bossfights. Nevertheless, the combination of its engaging gameplay, charming presentation, quick restarts, and nostalgic music makes Minishoot' Adventures a must-play for fans of both retro games and modern indie titles.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: The game is simple but has enough difficulty to where completing it is super rewarding. It's a pretty unique game, not much story but it doesn't need it. It's gameplay is extremely fun and smooth. I'd highly recommend this game, one of the few games I've actually fully completed in awhile. I just wanted to play more of the game, and collecting anything in the game doesn't ever feel like a chore but a rewarding experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a game. This is one of my 3 favourite MVs alongside Hollow Knight & Ender Lillies, it's THAT good. The exploration is the best I've seen in an MV for ages, maybe ever. Only Hollow Knight might be better and I'm not certain about that, it's THAT good. Every thing you explore you find things and not just random upgrades but extra dungeouns with well-thought out designs, puzzles, minibosses, etc. Yes, it's a short game, but it's got content that games twice the length doesn't have. I'm not usually one for bullet hells, but this was great - amazing design and a variety of options to cater to people less into that genre (I choose normal difficulty with assisted aiming that slightly aims the ship towards the target). And the upgrade system is one of the best ever. Usually when you do stat upgrades you don't notice any single point, it's the accumulation, but here every single point is immediately noticeable. I could go on for ever, this game is a masterpiece - buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: This was the most fun I’ve had with a metroidvania since Hollow Knight.I played with auto aim on - I thought this might be too easy, but it was the perfect level of challenge that I wanted. Dodging enemy projectiles and timing special maneuvers during complex encounters is a lot of game on its own.Early game enemies would reappear later in new clusters and still be a threat. New upgrades made combat more complex and more interesting, while not cluttering the gameplay with too many frivolous toys.Every new enemy encounter was unique and creative. No filler or clone encounters. Enemy design paired perfectly with environments. The bosses were plentiful and exciting.Character movement is responsive and precise; whisper smooth. Sound effects like weapon impact were expressive and gratifying, never got tiresome.Basic quality of life things were appreciated like responsible checkpoint placement and automatic currency pickup.Rewarding progression. Smart level design. Cute characters. Evocative and transportive music.Game did crash on me one time but that may have had to do with me binging it for hours cause I couldn’t stop playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: This is a super cute, charming, and fun Zelda-like adventure with the twist that you're a spaceship that attacks like a twin stick shooter. The controls behave how you think they should, which is the most important thing in a shooter like this. The 2D graphics and game world are crisp and super clear in terms of where hidden goodies are. My only complaint there is the colors feel a little muted, but it is a ruined world, so that fits. The sound matches the world and the music is very enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: An overall great game, that's short enough to not overstay its welcome. The blend of zelda-esque map exploration with the bullet hell gameplay core is very interesting and something to explore more in the future.I feel there is a missed opportunity with the action and racing elements of the game, which are pretty much only a bonus, and could have been implemented more during the battle sequences (ramps and jumps). Enemy encounter variety is fairly low. Enemies are pretty much a few variations on a handful of skins, and the variety of bullets and behavioural patterns is very low. The game has two big problems: 1 - map exploration is very frustrating until you start unlocking map markers and map fragments to help with navigation. This is particularly true because the game just allows you to go deep into uncharted areas of the map and expects you to memorize all locations that you go through. It's confusing to know what you ought to do next, sometimes.2 - power-ups and bullet variety is very low. There's an overworld meta progression for your gun and its power-ups, but the main draw of bullet hell games is to have different kinds of bullet patterns, different kinds of guns, etc. In this sense, this game is very lacking.Regardless, Minishoot is a fun game, with a focus on exploration and strong indie charm. As a concept, I feel there's room to expand upon, but its competent gameplay and original concept are enough to stand on its feet as it is. Positives: competent gameplay; interesting concept; accessible and fun.Negatives: punishingly confusing navigation in the map for the first stages of the game; no power ups or weapon variations which is a staple of bullet hell shooters
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing in life is perfect, no matter how much we love it. But I want you to understand, "nothing in life is perfect" is the worst thing I can say about this game. Thank you for this, SoulGame. This game is a gem and I love playing it. The best thing about finishing this game is that you get to start again.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of bullet hell games and twin stick shooters this game is friggin' awesome. The controls are responsive, the gameplay tight and focused, the music and graphics are lovely, and the overall curve of the game's difficulty is perfect. I honestly can't say anything bad about this, I really can't. Steam needs more games like this. Seriously.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: A great little game, making me recall all the good parts of the original legend of Zelda, but in a shoot em up version of the happy-go-lucky exploring from my childhood.I'm happy that the difficulty sliders were there and also the accessibility options. That's for the arena because I couldn't be bothered, but I still wanted closure. I feel that the player should be given the option to end without finishing the arena. There was no real point to it. It could still be there for the people who want a challenge, but I just wanted the exploring and the 100%.Clean and neat looking and with great UX design.I would recommend this game to everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best game I've played this year. The whole concept of mixing the maze like exploration and dungeons of Zelda with a metroidvania style bullet-hell was executed perfectly. Even after finished it at just under 8 hours I couldn't stop and I rarely do that. You can get an item that shows you everything you missed on the map so collecting everything after finishing wasn't a chore like some games and was actually still fun, with plenty to still do that wasn't just simply collecting things. I liked that they utilised every aspect of this concept with even some racing elements since you're a ship.I'd really love to see a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: A twin-stick shooter inspired by Zelda 1. A super cute little game that combines Zelda-like exploration and dungeons with some basic RPG elements.Throughout its 5 hour playtime there was basically no downtime, and I've completed it in 3 sittings in the same day because I was so engrossed in it. The game completely understands what makes this type of gameplay good and despite being a little more linear than the original Zelda it has plenty to offer in terms of secrets and optional things you can find. The structure is familiar: find a dungeon, pick up an item within, kill the boss, explore further. It's nothing video games haven't done, yet I've never seen a twin-stick shooter follow this formula, which makes it feel very fresh and unique.There are a ton of pickups, from your basic pieces of heart, to unique new powers, which made exploration a blast throughout.If there's one thing I didn't really like is that if you're going for a 100% playthrough, the game becomes a little check-listy since you can buy an item that directs you towards any pick-ups that are still left in the world. It's not exactly possible to ignore and made maybe last 15 minutes or so of overworld progression a little basic.There's not much to say, the game doesn't really do anything truly new, but what it does is charming and easy to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: You could write thousands of words explaining to someone why this game is fantastic. And it would be incredibly worthwhile! _childDocuments_.review: I highly enjoy the Ori games along with Hollow Knight, and Minishoot Adventures is a great adventure game to add alongside them for me, being easily my most enjoyed game this year.Albeit smaller and a bit simpler in scope, and a clear difference from the former two by being a top down twin-stick shooter, it had very satisfying progression and exploration to it, and very fun combat to me with large enemy variety and also variety through non combat challenges with platforming like challenges, and races.As for cons, my only big complaint was the few instant kill sections towards the later part of the game, they did not learn from Ori the blind forest's mistakes on this one, who mostly got rid of instant kills for the sequel.Instant kills are not fun to me in general, and as someone who tries to play adventure games deathless they are terrible. Great challenge is welcome, but having some room for error and the ability to retreat to recuperate I value, and although being locked in fights is acceptable for the thrill as you get low and fight for your life, being instant killed is not thrilling to me, it was primarily used in non combat challenges, where I would have preferred it just teleported me back similar to falling off the map does, maybe combined with some dmg taken.Will also note that the races although enjoyable to me, felt a bit too simple and lacking in challenge. They seem inspired from ori's races, but fell short in excitement, still I consider the game better with them than without so not really a con, but not a clear strength either.With the cons mentioned, and although many words used for them, they ultimately didn't impact my fun much.Minishoot Adventure is a very easy game to recommend, and a game you can tell if it is for you or not within the steam refund window, since if you don't like it after the first hour it's a good chance it isn't your type of game.

The fact that I just kept coming back for more and thinking about it all day from the FREE demo really speaks volumes. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best games i've played in years. It's rare I come across a game that i can say is virtually flawless, but this is indeed one of them. It has a simple and charming art style that makes everything very easy to read and follow. The music isn't mind blowing, but it's atmospheric and catchy. But it's the gameplay that's really the star here. It's a combination of a twin-stick shooter and 2D Zelda game, and if that combo seems odd, in practice, it's incredible. The encounters are challenging, but with enough focus, always achievable. And the exploration is always fun and rewarding. There are SOOOO many option dungeons and areas where you can find truly helpful upgrades and items that truly feel rewarding to find and use. Can't say enough good things about it, i already beat it once on normal difficulty and am playing on hard mode now. Play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Who would have thought combining Zelda with a twin stick shmup would work like butter on bread?This game is way better than it might appear at first glance. The intense bullet hell combat adds an addicting layer of excitement to the more slow paced Zelda-style exploration. While the upgrades and abilities keep up a nice progression throughout the game. Best of all there's basically no filler - you just get to play the game. Highly recommended for anyone who feels the slightest interest in this formula. I don't even have a particular affinity for bullet hell shmups, it just works so damn well when broken up by slower paced exploration and puzzle solving.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. I have spent the whole month of May playing it, first on normal difficulty and then in "advanced" mode. It's a twin-stick shooter with Zelda exploration mechanics. My first impressions were that the art style is a little bland and the title is terrible, so if you have those same thoughts please push them to the back of your mind and play this wonderful game!You fly around in a cute little ship with the left thumbstick, and shoot with the right. The core loop of this game is:    Avoid bullets    Defeat enemies    Explore to find permanent ship power-ups    Defeat more and more powerful enemiesThere's a dazzling array of power-ups, and they're introduced slowly enough that it's not confusing at all. There's always somewhere new to explore. You're constantly discovering new areas, enemies, power-ups, secrets, races and boss battles. The world design is full of variety, and it's very clever - after reaching a new area there's usually way to open up a quick path back to/from the main base. As your ship gains new abilities, paths that were closed off before open up. This is all very normal for a metroidvania, but there's something about how polished this game is that makes it an absolute joy to play.Joy is the number one emotion I have when playing this game. The world is presented joyfully. The world is crafted to give the player a strong sense of progression & wonder. The characters are very cute and joyful little ships. The music is light and joyous. The sound effects are chirpy and adorable. The collision on the bullets is generously forgiving, and you even get a power up that negates their damage 15% of the time. Falling off the world triggers a playful Micro Machines style puff-of-smoke animation. It feels like the whole thing was crafted to answer the question "how can we spark joy in the player?"The game holds your hand just enough to get you where you want to be, then it lets you loose. It's like Tunic - there's a secret round every corner, except it's not so opaque and frustrating. If you're ever unsure about where to go next, the game finds ways to communicate the next objective. Or you can just go into the nearest cave and explore and have a great time.The world is densely packed with enemies and places to explore. But once you've cleared out an area, it generally stays that way. So it doesn't take long to traverse from one side to the other when backtracking. I love a compact world like this - it reminds me of The Witness. Yet it's not just a barren wasteland; some random enemies still appear while passing through old areas. If your ship is overpowered it's a nice opportunity to feel powerful as they pop like bubble wrap, or else it's a nice challenge that provides an opportunity to earn some more XP towards upgrades.The game feels a little bit like Traffic Department 2192. There's an immediate responsiveness to player controls, and a good weight to destroying opponents. They gradually turn a darker colour as you shoot them, so it's easy to see at a glance that you're making a dent amidst the bullet hell. Even the bullets change colour as they travel, so you can easily gauge when they will reach the end of their range.Some Steam users seem to not enjoy the races in the game. I love them. They provide a nice bit of variety amongst the bullet hell. Like an oasis of peace & quiet and competitiveness, away from all the noise outside the cave. To have the most success with these, you have to think laterally. Is there a shortcut available? Does the other racer take the most efficient line, or can I outpace them somewhere along the track? Should I take some upgrade points out of my gun and spend them on movement speed instead? (Yes). And the reward for completing all the races is a really cool powerup too, not to mention a step towards 100% completion.It's a great Steam Deck game. It's a little slow to load initially, but then it's super quick to pick it up & put it down. I will say there are some slowdown issues on the deck when there's a lot going on on screen. But that actually made some boss fights a little bit easier. The text is a little bit difficult to read.The story is very minimal. The game does make you wait for little cutscenes to play, but having played the whole game twice to 100% completion, and watching my girlfriend and two children play through it, I haven't found these to be annoying. The theme of the game is how power corrupts. As your ship becomes more powerful, it makes you feel really good to slice through huge waves of enemies more easily. Meanwhile the story warns against becoming drunk with power - skip the rest of this paragraph if you want to avoid spoilers - and at the end you are asked to give up those powers to complete the story. At which point the game erases your save file completely. I somehow found this incredibly satisfying and fitting. And then I jumped right back in and played the whole thing from the start again.And as if that's not all, when you've explored the overworld 100% and completed the story, there's a large set of challenge arenas. I somehow even got the achievement for beating each arena without losing more than half my ship's health.The normal difficulty level was perfect for me during my first run. I played it on advanced mode to get the final achievement, and I really think I needed the first run to gain the skills required to beat it at the harder difficulty level. It pulls no punches. But it still managed to spark almost as much joy the second time round and I couldn't stop playing until I reached the end again. I would advise playing with aim-assist on, even though sometimes it miscalculates and fires at where the enemy is, rather than where they're going to be. Speaking of which - the enemies in the game are very good at aiming at where you are going to be. It makes them feel very clever and always keeps you on your toes. You can't just mindlessly circle around them.Here's an obligatory paragraph about the sound design. Despite playing the game twice through, I never got tired of the music. It's got a nice gentle electronic feel in the overworld, and ramps it up really effectively for big fights and boss battles. I like the way the music crossfades when changing biomes. The sound effects communicate information to the player really well. For example, when the ship's energy runs out or I get hit by a bullet, there are special sound effects that I seem to be subconsciously attuned to. And it's all so cute, from the little chirps of the ships themselves to the chaingun-style clinking of the ship's main weapon.The only few negative things I have to say about the game are tiny nitpicks. It's difficult to see a checkmark/tick on a cave if your ship is sitting right next to it on the map. Sometimes I have to backtrack to find a crystal and recharge my special powers. There's the aim-assist issue I mentioned earlier. Negligible.I honestly could not get enough of playing this game. I think it'll easily be my top game of 2024. My kids both love it too - my six year old was able to complete the game fully. It's a joyously well designed game and I'd recommend it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best game I've played all year. Minishoot Adventures is basically Zelda: A Link to the Past, except you and all the enemies are spaceships, and the game is a bullet hell. It's incredibly well polished, well designed, a good length, and great fun throughout. _childDocuments_.review: A great game.Pros:The game feels very polished. The combat is fun and default difficulty seems nicely tuned.They do a good job of trying to keep things fresh across the 10 ish hours to completeCons:Lack of checkpoints. Pretty frequently a death will place you back in the main overworld and you need to do a boring trek back to where you were. This gets especially annoying in later part of the games where there are obstacle courses of hazards which are one hit kills. Not being able to retry quickly is annoying. I would have tried the higher difficulty if there were more checkpointsI think some of the dungeons could use some heal stations. There is no penalty for dying except for the boring punishment of the trek back so I think they could have added some heal stations to decrease the tediousness. Map - I wish the map was more detailed or kept track of where you were going. The areas are very same-y so it can be hard to remember if you had been to a place. I think if you took a break from the game you would have a hard time remembering what areas you had already explored

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic mix of the best from older, explorative RPGs and the good old bullet hells from the arcade. Combined with a timeless, cute style and buttersmooth gameplay, Minishoot Adventures is a must-play for lovers of top-down shooters. Don't let the cute graphics and soft tunes fool you though: the enemy in this game packs a punch. Especially if you choose one of the harder difficulties! The amount of game overs I have had are uncountable.The huge amount of collectibles, most of which give you unique perks within the game, is a huge plus for a completionist like myself. You often get rewarded for investigating that one suspicious, mysterious box, tree or coconut.Another big plus is that you can spec your ship as you wish, and you can always re-build too via downgrading for example your crit chance. Then you can spend those points on your fire rate instead, for example.

_childDocuments_.review: So I haven't finished / completed a game in a decade or more. Until Minishoot. This game is so compelling that it'll keep even the most jaded of gamers' hearts in the game until the very end. If that wasn't enough to convince you that Minishoot' Adventures is something special maybe this will: this game is so remarkable and one of a kind that it has convinced me -- an old school parent who's been gaming for 20 years -- to purchase the plushie of the main character. And yes, the protagonist is an aircraft, but it's sentient and adorable; you know the dev and designer have given us a masterclass in character design when they've managed to create an iconic gaming hero out of a spaceship, one of the most ubiquitously used avatars in the artform's history. Gameplay: masterpieceControls: masterpieceArt and art direction: MasterpieceNarrative: masterpieceCharacter (yes, character!) design: masterpieceWorld design: masterpieceAudio: masterpiece10's across the board. My previous review was for Hades II, where I named it my top game of 2024 so far; well it didn't take long for that title to be swept away by another contender: Minishoot' Adventures is the best game of 2024 and one of the best indie games - let alone Metroidvania or twin-stick shooter or bulet hell / shmup -- of the generation. The superlatives are thick here, I know, but they're well deserved. Keep an eye on this team and play this freaking game!*Recommended for everybody but particularly those who enjoy: Link's Awakening, Zelda II, Voidigo, Tunic, Cult of the Lamb, Nuclear Throne, Lone Fungus, Enter the Gungeon, Binding of Isaac, Star of Providence, Sky Force Reloaded, Hyper Light Drifter, Ember Knights, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: A unique blend of arcade shoot-em-up and Metroidvania that's fine-tuned to be as good as it can possibly be. It offers a satisfying challenge on the standard difficulty, with plenty of accessibility features for those that need them; and even the handful of little issues I ran into didn't stop it from being one of the most fun games I've played this year. Playing with a controller is strongly recommended.  is a game that takes inspiration from a bunch of different sources; but at its core, it's the combat of a top-down arcade shoot-em-up mixed with the non-linear exploration of a Metroidvania game. The story is your basic adventure game fare: a being called The Unchosen is spreading corruption across the land and imprisoning its inhabitants—a race of sentient spaceships appropriately referred to as Shiplings—and you're chosen by the powers that be to put a stop to it.Before going any further, a quick disclaimer: . On controller, it plays like a twin-stick shooter where the left stick moves your ship and the right stick determines your aim when firing. These controls are incredibly smooth, allowing for the snap movements needed for battles that can quickly turn into a segment straight out of a bullet hell. Playing with a mouse and keyboard is an available option, but you're stuck with the limitation of 8-directional movement, which can make some segments more difficult than intended. The developers have taken steps to make this control scheme work as best as possible, but even the store page makes it clear that it was designed with a controller in mind.Controller confusion aside, the rest of this game is just fantastic.  thanks to an abundance of secrets to find, often telegraphed through subtle changes in map design that can be easily missed if you're not paying attention, which just makes it all the more satisfying when you do eventually find it. , mainly because enemy encounters are carefully crafted to ensure that battles are exhilarating but never unfair, perhaps with a few minor exceptions. The environments have quite a bit of visual detail to them just to keep things looking pretty, but everything central to gameplay uses simple and consistent designs so you're losing as little visual clarity during combat as possible.If you're worried that your reflexes might not be good enough for this game, rest assured that . For starters, you have the standard difficulty settings that change the speed of enemies and their bullets; and you can set your aim to fully manual, assisted (orients you towards enemies if your aim is a little off), or automatic (automatically aim and shoot at nearby enemies to let you focus on dodging). As for true accessibility settings, you can change the game speed by any 5% increment between 50% and 100%, enable infinite energy for abilities like boost or super shots, or enable straight-up invincibility if you just want to focus on exploration. You also have a few features that can make parts of the game easier without being explicitly labelled as difficulty/accessibility options: stat points earned through leveling up can be reallocated at any time, which lets you better prep for specific challenges (e.g. increasing move speed for races) with less need to grind for XP; and exploration can be made easier through an NPC that reveals the location of caves and other points of interest, as well as optional purchases that more directly point you to any collectibles you've missed.As for the negatives, I have my gripes, but nothing significant. Earlier reviews and forum posts have mentioned trouble finding map pieces or the high difficulty of the racing minigames (especially on M&K controls), but these have since been addressed in post-launch updates and shouldn't be an issue anymore. As for what hasn't been addressed:Overall, , and the only achievement I missed is the one you get for playing on the highest difficulty. I found this game by randomly stumbling onto its demo, and I knew within 5 minutes of playing it that I wanted the full game. I'm happy to say that, despite the little issues here and there, it didn't disappoint.

_childDocuments_.review: What an gem! As others have said, this is basically a top down Zelda (Link's Awakening is the most obvious comparison) mixed with an arena shooter ala Geometry Wars. The visuals and controls are very clean and polished, and there's plenty of stuff to discover (the game makes it pretty easy to 100% everything even without a guide). The main game is pretty short - I beat it in about 5 or 6 hours. I wish it had a bit more in terms of movement/exploration based powerups but there are a number of optional areas and items. It's also very focused on the action side, so you're not really gonna be stumped by any of the puzzles here.Ultimately Minishoot Adventures is a very satisfying short adventure that I would love to have more of. It's not a game with a ton of variety, but the core gameplay loop is just so satisfying that it really doesn't matter.

_childDocuments_.review: I was intrigued by the fact that this game is a mixture of a Metroidvania and bullet hell shoot 'em up, but wasn't 100% sure if that combination would make for a good experience. However after beating the game, I've come to the conclusion that it does in fact make for a good experience! I, like probably most other people who've played this game, instantly felt as though I was playing a Zelda game - the way progression is handled with beating a certain amount of dungeons to access the final boss, dungeons that have you solving puzzles, engaging in combat trials to access a key item or upgrade and even the victory chime that plays whenever you finally "crack the code" - this is a Zelda game through and through.Some other aspects of the game that I like include the upgrade system and how you can add points to specific abilities, or take away points from one and add them to another. Also throughout the game, I also liked engaging in races against friendly NPCs and discovering one of the many well hidden secrets placed throughout the overworld and dungeons. On top of that, the game has a nice and sharp visuals, and great sound design (like how for example, shooting at certain items sounds like someone tapping on glass cups).There are a few things about the game that I don't like. For all of the similarities that this shares with Zelda, it's still a bullet hell shooter at the end of the day and can feel very overwhelming and frustrating at some points (even with me playing on this game's version of medium settings). Also, midway through the game, you get the ability to travel across water, but it felt like I was sliding on ice and constantly fighting the controls to keep the player character stable. The game's story is hard to follow due to the very minimal dialogue and not terribly interesting - I like to know why I'm doing what I'm doing in a game as that make it more engaging for me. Finally, there's the fact that quitting out of the game through the main menu takes way longer than expected (I played this on Steam Deck, so it could potentially be related to that)With that being said, I still think this is a great game and one that fans of Zelda, Metroidvania's or bullet hell games should try out. I'm very impressed that only two people made this game and can't wait to see what else they have to offer.My Score: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I hate bullet hell games.  Too stressful, and I'm slow and old now.  So I hesitated a bit before purchasing this.  But holy moly am I glad I did.Honestly the concept and gameplay design parts of this game are on par with a Nintendo-developed game, which is the highest praise I can think of.  By that I mean the game is rarely "hard," but is always engaging, surprising and delighting the player, while keeping forward momentum.  The puzzles and secrets are all super satisfying to crack, without ever being frustratingly esoteric.  Now, the characters, visuals and music are definitely not up to a Nintendo level of polish (it's a two-person dev team!), but they're perfectly fine and don't detract from the heart of the game at all.The way this game unfolds is extremely satisfying.  Progression is steady, and even when things become a bit difficult, it's never very punishing (no health lost if you slip off an edge, and you keep pretty much everything you've grabbed if you die).  The ability to respec your skill points literally at any point is fantastic, and means you never feel constrained by your choices.  The overall ramp up in difficulty, and corresponding progression of your abilities, feels great throughout the main quest (and beyond).There have been some outstanding "out of left field" indie games this year (Balatro, Animal Well etc), but this is my pick of the bunch so far.

_childDocuments_.review: First let me start with what so far has been the biggest negative after 2 dungeons and about half the overworld: There appears to be only one main weapon, as it evolves into its spreadshot form (it does have a tiny homing effect to it even on manual though). Even were there some later, it would still be far too long without options in this regard.That said.It's cute, the characters are adorable, the world itself well-contrasted and easy on the eyes.The sound's alright; like many dungeon-crawlers it's more an atmospheric background deal, so it's not particularly memorable but also never really bad either. This is no Zelda score, but far worse than this would still have been tolerable.Enemy abilities are generally quite clear at a glance; when you first see those little triangles without gunports begin to shake, your instincts know right then and there what you're facing. And in a world of skimmers, it's clear that those with spider-mech legs use them for something.Controls are tight and responsive, though given the arena shooting gameplay it would have been unacceptable for it NOT to be - it's a rather binary state of "works or doesn't" in this genre.The exploration's fine, the levelling does its job (if you're having trouble in the races, the first movement and booster speed upgrades should put a stop to that), there's tempting leaps (not that falling in water hurts) in lots of places that you may or may not be able to bridge with a little boosting and dodge-taps.I came out of my first night of this relaxed and eager to go search more.

_childDocuments_.review: Minishoot Adventures is a top down twin stick shooter that features an overworld that feels very similar to the other Zelda games, but with the combat making it feel completely unique in its own right. For a shooter game you'll also probably be surprised to know it's actually somewhat easy, with the middle difficulty hardly causing many deaths for me. The way the world is structured is pretty generous in terms of making shortcuts to travel places faster. For fast travel there's only a way to teleport back to tour home base, but I assure you this isn't much of an issue since you can get from one end of the map to another in less than a minute eventually. The game will encourage you to head to certain objectives which it'll mark on the map, but of course there are dozens of secrets to obtain everywhere. Even more generous of the game is the fact it offers upgrades that can mark secret items on the map, so anyone can be a true completionist here. The combat of course is what makes this game interesting you move your ship with one stick and shoot with the other. Eventually you get items that give a few new mechanics that will also let you explore more areas. There is also a level up system that gives you points to upgrade stats that can you respec at any time. On the other side of the coin are the enemies, and there's a good few of them that make sure the game never gets boring, alongside fun bosses that don't outstay their welcome. Overall, definitely a delightful game that certainly lives up to the name of adventure. The exploration aspect is fun, the combat is slick, and the storyline it has was also cute. Definitely a recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.review: There's something about Metroidvanias.  I'll just keep playing the same damn game every time, lol.The twists this time are that it's also got strong ties to Zelda: Link to the Past and bullet-hell shoot em ups.  It's not groundbreaking but combined with a cute, polished aesthetic and a lot of personality it'll make for a very pleasant ten hours of your life.  Really enjoyed it in a way that reminded me of another, older game, "Incredibly Twisted Shadow Planet" that I played on the Xbox 360 back in the day.Although you could describe it as "Zelda + bullet hell" and get an accurate overview, there's a lot of love put into this, clearly, and it shows in the little quality of life tweaks; the stuff they didn't have to put in, but did for the love of the game, so to speak.  The map is littered with powerups and bonuses that you don't *have* to find, but really give you a passive edge in a pinch.  Each area has its own distinct, refined style to it but they all flow into each other seamlessly; for the most part you know exactly where you are from what's on screen, it's THAT unique.  And another nice touch: levelling up gives chunky, satisfying upgrades, but you're not locked into them.  At all.  Going into a boss fight, you're completely free to reconfigure your ship and, say, upgrade your range at the expense of dodge speed, if you want to.  And by the end of the game you probably still won't have everything at top level; but you can shift stuff around to get two or three aspects maxed out and everything else where you need it.  It's a nice touch.Cheap and cheerful, yes, and doesn't waste your time; you'll be done with it in twelve hours.  But they'll be delightful.

_childDocuments_.review: Minishoot' Adventures has some good game design in it, from useful upgrades to interesting arenas to gratifying secrets. But what separates this game from any other top-down shmup is its presentation. The cute, cartoon-y aesthetic where spaceships gesture their way through an abridged, humor-tinged Legend of Zelda plot is appealing, but the the more important part is that this game is polished to a mirror shine. Every potential nuisance has been eliminated, making it very easy to get invested in finding the next upgrade or seeing the next gag or checking back on that one roadblock that isn't a bother anymore. This is one of the most frictionless games I have played, and that helps the everything else shine brighter.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Splendid graphics, very cute+ Progression systems feel well weighted+ Exploration always feels worthwhile, and getting 100% map completion feels well done with the tools provided+ Hitboxes are well set for enemies, player, and all projectiles in the game+ Can 100% (all achievements) in about 8 or 9 hours even on hardest, so good value versus money spentMy one minor suggestion, as I can't even call it a con to the game, would be that the developer could add a restart button to certain late game areas in place of quitting to menu, and then reloading the whole save. Exiting and loading is incredibly swift, however, so it really is just a small suggestion. Overall an incredibly solid game. Buy if you like the idea of an old era Zelda-ish style game with bullet hell combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Words cannot give praise enough to this game. If you've grown up in an era where A Link To The Past was a thing, you absolutely OWE IT TO YOURSELF TO PLAY THIS GAME.I have devoured this game in a single day and it is excellent from start to finish.Get it. Play it. Encourage the devs, they made a work of love and they deserve to have every single bit of support we can give them <3
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: as someone who adored its demo a few years ago, I am so glad to play Minishoot' Adventures now that it's fully out and has proven itself to be one of 2024's greatest releases.I mean, where to start on why that is? this game has such robust design. it melds together the classic Zelda-style dungeon crawling with the bullethell twinstick shooting so naturally that you could trick someone unfamiliar with either genre into thinking that is just how those genres have always been with how refined it is. so it's a genre fusion where the pieces just work together perfectly.then there's the fact that it looks and sounds amazing. I want to own its OST so bad. "Blue Spirit" alone would be worth whatever the asking price may be. simply sublime and euphoric tunes.but you also cannot ignore the handcraftedness. I love my fair share of action roguelites and suchlike, but there is always something so uniquely gratifying about engaging with something so artfully designed by hand, rather than procedurally generated or just regurgitated landmasses for any of the many vapid, Ubified open worlds.for more thoughtful recommendations of the best games on Steam, check out my curator, .
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic! I really enjoyed it. they did an excellent job with the level designs and game world and the gameplay is very fun! I enjoyed finding the secrets and unlocking everything. I played it on the easiest mode and thankfully didn't have too much trouble with it (I'm getting old). I don't finish many of the games I play these days but I finished this one! I can't wait for Minishoot' 2 with MORE of everything! great job!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Best indie game of the year so far.I was really impressed by the demo I tried during some steam fests ago.I usually do not buy anything at launch but this time I couldn't resist.As said by many reviews, this game is mix of a Zelda 2D game (like A Link to the Past) and a twin-stick shooter.The style is brilliant, even if sometimes it looks like a Flash games of the 2000s.In any case the style is simple, but in the good way.Level design is clever, difficulty well balanced and controls are very responsive.There are four main dungeons but the game is full of secrets.I haven't finished it at 100% ( I was around 80% ) but every hour I've spent with it was well worth.If I want to find some "bad" things I would say the design of bosses.They look and plays (more or less) all the same..If they were designed around the abilities you gain (like the ones you fight in a Zelda game for example) it would have been a masterpiece..Oh and the races too :(Anyway, for me, this is really a gem and absolutely worth at full price (even more I'd say, compared to other similar titles sold at a more expansive price and not even close to the quality of this one).I hope the devs will receive the success and the praise they deserve.8.5/10Good job!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: So far my experience with this game has been amazing.It has everything I wanted from it and more.The only bit of feedback I have currently is that it would be nice to be able to use a controller's joystick to move, while using the mouse to aim.As they both offer more precision than aiming with the joystick or moving with WASD for me.Though currently, it seems these two control schemes cannot be used in tandem, they override each other and eat each other's inputs if you try it.I'll probably stick with controller for now, which works perfectly fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Minishoot Adventures is one of the most pleasant gaming surprises ever!+ The gameplay mix of combat, exploration and racing/platforming sections works perfectly. The pacing of this game is great! I've done everything the game has to offer and left very satisfied.+ Movement is superb. Evading bullets and racing both feel perfect.+ Shooting is satisfying.+ The cutesy artstyle is a great contrast to the challenging gameplay. I loved rescuing little friend spaceships.+ Difficulty/Accessibility options are great! I can have a challenge in this game and so can my six year old. Absolutely commendable!Here's some improvements I'd like to see in the sequel (I want a sequel!):- Maps for the caves and dungeons. Half the game plays underground and we don't have a map for that half.- As much as I like the look, the overworld often feels bland. I often completely forgot in which biome a certain place was, which is something that never happened to me in A Link to the Past (which seems to be this games biggest artistic inspiration).- I hate how the game completely stops my movement when I hit an obstacle. I'd rather fall into a bottomless pit in this game than hit a slalom post or a door.- Active combat options could be more involved. 1. I'd like boost to do damage. I want to have to choose between using energy for super shot or going fast. 2. Charging up blue powers in combat should be more involved. Maybe place a chrystal or a charging pad in arenas. 3. The third blue power is boring. I'd enjoy a more involved option.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game purely because I was confused by the high reviews and BOY do I get it now!!Minishoot Adventures is basically a 2D Zelda game + Twin-stick combat + Metroidvania progression systems and it comes together perfectly. The combat is satisfying, the exploration is addicting, and the bosses are an event all on their own.It also has a number of accessibility features, including some tied into how your character targets enemies, which was SUPER helpful for me the Steam Deck!My only real critique is that enemies feel kind of bullet-sponge-y? To the extent that, in the postgame content, I ended up lowering the difficulty simply because constant aiming for so long was tiring for my wrist. However, that lowest difficulty setting felt really good to me, to the extent that I wish I had used it earlier!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game.  If you have any doubts, play the demo!This looks and feels a lot like an old school zelda game.  Sure, it's got some bullet-hell aspects to it, and you're shooting instead of swording - but the presentation is still very zelda.  Although it's marked as metroidvania, don't expect anything similar to the two namesakes, other than a bit of ability gating.The visuals are nice, the sound and music are satisfying, the exploration feels rewarding, and it's challenging enough to keep your attention.  Though i do wonder if the "normal" skill level will be too tough for people who have never played bullet hell games.  I felt like the game started out very easy, but the last couple bosses were much more challenging, even when i had my damage fully upgraded.Anyway - it was glorious.  Took me 9 hours to 100% the map - but there's apparently some new arena thing that has opened up.  So maybe i'll get a few more hours out of this.Play the demo and see if you don't quickly decide you should buy the full game...
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little game that nicely blends friendly bullet-hell and zeldavania.Relaxing difficulty even in hard for veterans of shmup and even more for bullet-hell afficionados even tho patterns and overall overworld/progression are well designed so give it a try ;)A bit short but it's bake by 2 developpers so let's see if there's some updates in the oven in the near future.Overall a nice (edges are a bit rough =P) little game that scratches those itches.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Without a doubt it's one of the most beautiful and colorful metroidvania game I've ever played. And moreover the game is smooth and captivating. I really had fun and joy playing it, exploring the world, seeking the secrets and so on. It's like Ori or Hollow Knight in terms of interest of exploring and finding treasures and secrets. And while playing you can really feel how the developers actually LOVE games, and it's really wonderful. Much respect for the devs, you are awesome guys. Thank you for this project ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal classic adventure game mixed with Asteroid-like shooter. Scratches A Link Between World style itch with excellent collectibles, dungeons, and just that sense of "I am lost and it is my fault, let me joyfully retrace my steps." Great design choices, like controller configs that can be changed mid game to match your actual button layout, this game really cares about the player and their time.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing little Zelda-like game with a twin-stick twist. Every time I picked this game up I found it very hard to put down. I ended up blasting through the main story in about 8 hours, but there seems to be even more after you complete the game in continue challenges to play through. Definitely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: The perfect blend between Zelda and twin-stick shooters.Minishoot's incredible tight level and world design, smooth controls, and great visual clarity in its design guarantee that the flow of exploration keeps consistently enjoyable. The artstyle is very charming and the animations are full of life, and the music is fantastic. Combat is fun and intuitive, and the items and abilities the player obtains along the way serve not only for traversal but for the combat as well.All in all, if you are a fan of Zelda, and you enjoy or don't mind shooters, this is a game that you can easily play for many hours straight and will be hard to put down.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome little game to scratch the Zelda itch that doesn't overstay its welcome. The world map is satisfying to explore and opens up organically as you gain new abilities while being easy to hop around despite no fast travel, items are there to guide you to the collectibles you may have missed (which are all satisfying to grab and are necessary for the true ending), and the respec ability is awesome. At literally any point you can reassign your skill points, so going up against a boss you probably want to focus on damage while finding one of the races around the map was always a time to kill my damage in favor of speed.My only real complaint is the frame rate chugged pretty heavily when things got super hectic, particularly in the post-game arena that's just a gauntlet of repeated fights. I bailed without finishing it after getting frustrated at both the repetition and unfair damage from the lag, but that was a tiny blemish on an otherwise delightful game.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable bullethell & metroidvania game, with good progression system, and good amount of challenging enemiesCute and beautiful visual with different biomes to explore, with lovely music for each of them, fit with the biome theme as wellLots of stuff to collect and secrets to find, and there is an item that can help you backtrack and find what you miss, so you won't forgot where you left off if you stop playing for a few days for whatever reasonFeels really good using keyboard and mouse with manual aiming (There are other aiming mode if you are not familiar with mouse aiming)Recommended for people who are looking to enjoy a simple bullethell / metroidvania game
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Immediately one of my top games I've played in a long time. I 100% it in around 9-10 hours with all achievements on Hard. Bullet-hell, zelda-like game that scratched all of the itches. Everything seemed well balanced and fair. Hard mode wasn't just enemy spam but faster enemies and their bullets. Small complaint about no instant death on races which made it a little annoying if you messed up early. But other than that everything seemed fair, intuitive, with essentially no dialog (a plus for me). I'm normally pretty harsh with ratings (not like IGN lol) but this is actually a 10/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Since the moment I played the demo to just finishing the game for the first time all I can say is this game will live with me forever. One of the best experiences of my life and I am so grateful the game exists. Such a fun and wonderful game. Exactly what I thought it would be from the demo and it is much more than even that!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: I saw someone else say "I love when devs remember to make the game fun". Perfectly describes this game. I played on Advanced difficulty and there were a handful of fights that I had to repeatedly retry, but for the most part I was cruising. The post-game has some special challenges that I'm finding push me to my limits.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic blend of twin-stick shmup action and Zelda-like exploration and progression. A great deal of care and expertise has clearly gone into the responsive game-feel and level design. It feels very satisfying to control and the pacing feels spot-on. In fact, it's surprisingly hard to stop playing. I found the difficulty level on the default settings to be perfect in that it's flexible and lenient. Allowing you to try out different upgrade paths without penalty. The tone is appropriately cheery, vibrant, positive and fun. Plus the soundtrack is so pleasing, it'll sit alongside Fez and Tunic as my go-to mellow work music. Brilliant game, and truly exceptional considering it's coming from a 2-person team.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: What a cool and smartly designed Zelda-like.. but as a Shmup! Dodging bullets is mandatory so expect this to be the core of the game. If you don't like that, stay away. Although I think it's not as hard as a traditional shoot 'em up, you get plenty of abilities to dodge or negate bullets. I think even as a none shmup guy (like me) you'll have a good time.As for the Zelda aspects: You got your heart pieces and batteries for your magic err.. energy bar and abilities gating different areas and secrets to eplore. What I really liked is the focus on movement, it's not just shooting and dodging bullets, it's also racing and different puzzles based on movement. Although it's nothing mind-bending, it's fun to explore the world and find everything.My game is pretty representative, I 100%ed the game in these 9 hours - if you're a better player and don't have to leave it on pause to watch for your daughter, you can probably do it in 6 hours on normal difficulty. Minor thing though: While the Shmup with Zelda combo is unique by itself, I'd have wished for some more unique abilities. When it comes to down to it, in the end you're still just shooting and dodging bullets in fights with 3 abilities that are nothing new in this genre. A bit more cerativity here would probably go a long way for a potential sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a really nice mix between LOZ:link's awakening and Touhou. so if you like those two kind of games then i definitely recommend this one.the OST is surprisingly mellow and easy on the ears, which is nice while you're exploring the world.i jumped right into the hardest difficulty and 100%'ed it. i feel it gave a decent amount of challenge.i would have liked to have maps for the dungeons though, sometimes i got a bit lost but i managed.the usage of colors was good and i never lost sight of where i was, which is CRITICAL in games like these, so good job devs!the bosses were fun and there was a fair share of enemy types to give variety. the controls were VERY smooth and satisfying.overall, a fun experience!I give it a solid 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures
