_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Twin-Stick Zelda. Game is loaded with charm, great pacing and progression make this game a satisfying and fun adventure. Feels more like Zelda than twin-stick shooter but can surprise with challenging bullet-hell gameplay and an interesting soundtrack. I nearly forgot to mention the design of this game, which is remarkably good and borrows from the best but also offers up it's own interesting mechanics as you boost and air dash your way through levels at fast pace. The demo is free and carries your save over to the full game so you have nothing to lose by giving the game's demo a try. I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, worth the price. puzzles and combat are not hard (played normal) but still fun and requires concentration. _childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice idea combining metroidvania with shoot em up :) The best part about this game was the great controls over the main character and how smooth it was. Boss fights we´re well balanced, although I think the power ups scale up a bit too high (I played with hardest difficulty the whole game). Just minor balancements tho. Visuals and music are also very nice. The game feels pleasing to watch and especially play.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: This is a perfect game for me. Everything just worked so well. The pacing of the game is perfect, balancing exploration, puzzles, and combat perfectly. The arena fights at the end, too, was the best way to end the game. The perfect challenge that scratched that itch for me. Didn't overstay its welcome in terms of play time and it didn't feel too short. It was just right.I'm very much looking forward to any future projects from this dev, especially if it's a sequel to this game! Good luck to the dev team for their future projects!(PS, switch version hopefully? a man can dream lol)
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun intersection between The Legend of Zelda and classic Bullet Hell Shooters.It has a mix of interesting enemies/bosses, adorably cute characters, and solid gameplay with few flaws.  (Jump ramps/races are a little squiffy, but are likely easier with a gamepad, and one of the abilities helps with races a LOT, especially since you can adjust your abilities on the fly.  Dodge/boost are bound to the same button, which caused a few issues.  Some areas are really tricky in the late game.  But nothing that dampens the fun too much.)  If bullet hell plus Legend of Zelda with adorable ship people sounds fun to you, or if you want an introduction to either style of those games, I recommend this.Heck, I recommend it just because the story is fun and the characters are adorable, with solid gameplay to tie it together.EDIT:  I just finished it again on Advanced Mode, and it's still fun, but a bit harder. (of course)I really hope there's a sequel that expands on the concept, and definitely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: I know I know, the statement Im about to say is to powerful, BUT, I put this up there with Hollow Knight. _childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of what I like. Twin stick shooting, bullet hell projectiles, metroidvania abilities, old school legend of zelda map, and shump-style upgrades. The art style and characters are charming and make cute noises. I think $15 for this game is such a good deal. There's even post final boss content! Props to these devs! This is an easy recommend from me.Btw I did play on the hardest difficulty from the get go and I think it's the best way to go if you like twin stick shooters and/or bullet hells.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Bloody amazing game. Terrible name. Makes it seem like a mobile cash grab game, but it's not in any way. Play the demo if you like, but if you're enjoying it, just get the full game as soon as you realise, as the save doesn't carry over.Less than 10 hours to beat and get most achievements, but so worth the pricetag!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: A really enjoyable metriodvania lite. Controls feel good, powers are fun. The bullet hell can be hard but isn't too truly hellish. Took me about 8 hours to do everything minus beating the game on hard mode and one other achievement so I'd say this one is well worth your money. Fun while it lasts and leaves you wanting more which is better than the myriad of overstuffed games focusing on length instead of quality. More fun ~8 hours games like this please!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not the biggest fan of bullet-hell style difficulties however I do greatly enjoy titles like Cuphead and Armored Core 6.For reference on preference so that everyone is aware of where I stand on gaming quality, here is the following.My favorite game of all time is Elden Ring. A game I personally consider close to perfection is Sekiro.I finished the game on Advanced.This game starts out very strong with addicting aspects that hooks very well. The sounds and premise reminds me of Spyro. I understand this game is advertised as a Zelda-like but I have never played a classic Zelda title because I played Castlevania instead growing up.The secrets are fine though I wish rest spots were implemented more with a designated warp system to make searching less tedious of an activity. The racing segments got old very fast and I wasn't motivated to finish them all just due to the lack of motivation. There's something that unlocks whenever you finish all of the races so I never got see what it was. I really loved the enemy locked arenas which forces the player to engage in battle and that was always engaging. The boss fights are very well crafted for the most part. I found the final fight mostly a rehash of what I already saw in previous battles which are aspects I analyze greatly on. There are four Purple Skulls on a door leading to the final boss and I was greatly disappointed that the fourth Purple Skull didn't even have a boss so I'm very confused on that design choice.My favorite part of the game however was the level design and venturing through each area that gradually became accessible through traversal tools earned. I do want to state that if you're going to implement Assist Features like invincibility, then make it a part of the world not hidden in a menu like the Invincibility Leaf from Super Mario 3D Land. I did experience one major game breaking bug and that was when a boss spawned and never attacked or could be attacked. To wrap up. I greatly enjoyed the game and for fourteen dollars it's not a bad deal at all for the amount of content it offers. I spent a lot of time doing challenge runs for boss fights and documenting them on my Youtube channel so I can remember the experience. Thanks for reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews often, but this game is so good I had to spread the word.- Metroid-like progression system? Check.- Old-school Zelda perspective, puzzles and secrets? Check.- Great twin-stick shooter gameplay? Check.This feels like a remaster of a lost SNES gem, with just the right features from modern games on top. This is a game that builds upon simple, easy-to-access gameplay mechanics, to explore new and interesting ideas until the credits roll (and even after!).I play ~40 games a year, yet I'm already sure I will keep fond memories of this one for a long time.Congrats to the team, and thank you :)
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: They took Star of Providence and turned it into A Link to the Past. I can't stop playing it. 100% done but still 4 achievements left. As soon as I'm done I'm just going to create a new game. This is going to be a problem. 10/10. Best game of the year.Edit: This is the only game I've ever gotten all achievements on. Really really really really fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Gotta give this game the praise and love it deserves! It's been some of the most pure and enjoyable gaming I've had in years. Exploration is fun and rewarding, without being painful.  Battles are great and challenging without ripping out your hair (i'm playing on default difficulty and don't really have much if any bullet hell experience).
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: I have played a few modern metroidvanias - Hollow Knight, the 2 Ori games, Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown. I can say that this game felt different from those, perhaps more it's Zelda like, but it gave me the same satisfaction on getting the abilities and being able to clean up the collectibles. The map is small enough that you can get from the hub location to the edge in under a minute once you unlock all the bridges/shortcuts, but it is very densely packed with content. I have never played a game before with this kind of checkpoint system, where only the central hub and the more hardcore dungeons have checkpoints. It was jarring at first but quickly got used to how it works and it was quite enjoyable. I would also like to say that the choice of art style is fantastic. I wish there are more titles with this kind of 2000s flash game art style.I played in the "Original" difficulty mode and must say it felt just right. Not too easy but also not too difficult. The only thing I would point out (not necessarily as a flaw) would be that I wish some of the powers were put to more use - mainly  and . I also found it a bit confusing how they recharged.One last thing I really appreciated was how polished and bug free the experience was. There was a noticable fps drop in the part where there was a lot of snow flakes at the end, but other than that the game felt pretty smooth on my mid-end hardware.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought a shooting game can be so much fun. I love the accessibility options provided. Don’t think I could have completed all races without setting the game speed at half the normal. I wish all games give such accommodations for people who are not adept but still want to enjoy the complete game. The map design is well thought out. I believe the dev’s put in a lot of hard work. I’d recommend even at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: The idea to combine the original Zelda NES game and a bullet hell shouldn't work, but this game is just so much fun and nostalgic feeling all at once. Doesn't seem overdone or cheesy. It feels really good. The ship controls really well and this game is just unbelievably amazing. I do not like bullet hells or SHMUPs, but this game is just straight up fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Great shmup-adventure mash-up that no one knew they needed.  Post-game arena mode is great for the die-hards looking to challenge themselves.  Adventure game is a great semi-short Zelda-like experience.  If a boss is too hard go grind some XP and power up the weapons more!  Want to prove your masochism? Keep all the power-ups at the minimum level!  The system is a great compromise between us filthy casuals and those battle maniacs who feel they aren't having fun unless their thumbs and eyes are bleeding.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Now I dont write reviews very often but this is without a doubt a great game. A beautiful and well done meshing of legend of zelda and top down twin stick shooter. The sounds, music and environments were really nice and great to experience. As for the enemies and boss fights, really well done. I will say though some enemy traps were straight up mean but very rewarding to conquer. Never once did I feel the game cheated a hit on me but rather I was being sloppy or wasnt respecting certain bullet patterns. All in all I fully recommend getting this game, you wont regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game, I don't think I have to add anything a better review hasn't yet. The only thing I like to say that I think that there is potential for so much more, but this would also be a complexer ame and less chill/more puzzly maybe. _childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Simple core mechanism executed extremely well! Did you get inspired by Zelda The Minish Cap and/or other 2D Zelda games? Dungeon design, boss fight design, overall map design that allows you to explore the same area in different way after unlocking new abilities. Thanks for building this simple but awesome game!
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: When I first played Hollow Knight, I was shocked at what someone could do to make a 2d side scroller so amazing and beautiful as a metroidvania.  Today I am amazed at what a top down game can do and can be in this genre.  Every aspect of the game is beautiful and satisfying.  Amazing work devs, this game deserves to be selling way more than it currently is.

_childDocuments_.review: Really love the atmosphere and the game itself is quite unique on todays market , but man , please give us a hp regeneration system , hp drops are so scarce and there is litteraly no other way of getting hp , its annoying when you get hit by an accident and practically have no way to get the hp back unless you are lucky , also , checkpoints , dying is just boringly punishing , like yea , progress isnt lost , but walking back to where i have to go feels like a task , myb an item sold in the shop could fix the issue , give it the ability to place a spawnpoint wherever you are by channeling it for a few secs . _childDocuments_.review: Not the biggest fan of bullet hells myself, but as a huge fan of metroidvanias, this one was an amazing surprise. I'm a bit tired of the same metroidvania formula, relying only on good visuals/fighting system/map design to determine a metroidvania game is great, and Minishoot' is such a fresh breath of air in that sense. Navigating through the world map is truly satisfying, you don't need fast travel because you smoothly go from an area to another. Every secret found and upgrade made feel super rewarding really. The progression is great and so is the general game feel when exploring and battling, definitely recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Minishoot Adventures is a fun and colorful bullet-hell metroidvania style game that's both easy to get into and play, and surprisingly relaxing and investing. There's plenty of secrets to discover and some challenging puzzles, but it never feels like a slog, and between the colorful world and the quick-pacing, charming writing, and fun game-play coupled with smooth controls it will suck you right in if you let it. Well worth the time and money I invested into playing it. c:
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: While the game definitely feels like it was made by a small team, it also feels like they poured their hearts and SOULS into it. The movement is very responsive, the sound design is on-point, and while the limited variety of enemies can make the game feel repetitive at times, the game doesn't suffer too much overall from this. My other main critique is the asset re-usage in certain areas can make pinpointing your location difficult without the map to guide you. A smaller issue I had was with the characters. The previous "Soul" art style in the developer's previous games, while simple, were much more expressive than the faceless ship characters. These are very minor gripes, and not at all reasons to ignore this game, though. Overall, the game play and exploration more than make up for it. Excited to see what the future holds for this game and Soul Game Studios' next project!

_childDocuments_.review: Played the demo some time ago, I think during a Next fest?, and was smitten. Picked up the game recently and dumped 6 hours into it already. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best zelda-likes I have ever played. While the game is rather short, its quality is excellent. The simplistic artstyle, the catchy soundtrack and the smooth gameplay all complement each other, creating a very enjoyable experience. As a bullet hell game, some fights can get really challenging, but there are none I would consider unfair. Even the final challenge - the arena - never makes you feel like the fights were impossible, simply that you need to focus more on dodging or that you need to obtain some upgrades.Speaking of upgrades, the game handles them really well. As this game is a zelda-like/metroidvania, the world gradually opens up as you gain new abilities. While there are only a few abilities you get throughout your journey, every single one feels impactful and allows you to both explore and aproach combat in new ways.In conclusion, if you enjoy zelda-likes, metroidvanias and bullet hells, this game is one of the best ones in that niche. I heavily recommend buying it, even without a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time Zelda fan, I loved this game.Minishoot Adventures is a breath of fresh air in the adventure gaming scene, highly recommended for all fans of The Legend of Zelda. The twin stick shooter combat system works flawlessly and integrates beautifully into the game's structure, offering an experience that leans more towards action than Nintendo's title. There is a certain lack of variety in the arsenal, justified nonetheless by the longevity of the product, which clocks in at around 11 hours. But for its price, Minishoot Adventures is a must-buy if you enjoy adventure games, the Zelda franchise, or if you simply want to support originality and creativity in the gaming industry.

_childDocuments_.review: Superb twin stick shooter with exploration evoking the best parts of Zelda 1. The pacing is tight and on point with a short main adventure but meaty side matters to dig up, unlocks are satisfying and the feeling of progression is palpable. The overworld is filled with secrets to discover, all leading to tangible upgrades, and the combat is fast paced with a heavy emphasis on positioning to survive the bullet hell patterns, yet accessible thanks to some generous difficulty options and additional tweaks available.Definitely one of the better genre mixes that's not only clever, but also extremely well done, with each part bettering the other. If you have any remote interest in twin stick shooting, old school top down adventuring or pretty bullet hell patterns, be sure to check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: A combination of twin-stick shooter and Zelda, Minishoot' Adventures puts a few unique twists on the genre and backs them up with slick gameplay, rewarding exploration and varied boss battles. The few points of friction early on are phased out as your toolset expands. You gain an appreciation for every skill and relic as your enemies evolve into more complex threats which demand more than just "fire rate" and "damage".
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just so fun, polished, and well designed. It reminds me a ton of Islets, another one of my favorite Metroidvanias. Every little detail, from player movement to map design, feels so well made and a delight to play.It is debatable if this is more of a Metroidvania or a Zelda-like. There are dungeons, but they act more like zones than isolated areas. You can leave, come back, etc. I only have tiny little bits of feedback I would leave. My main one - please add a purchasable upgrade to help locate map fragments. This was the only frustrating part of my playthrough (especially the blue forest one!) Also, not having maps for the dungeons is an interesting choice. Normally I would protest, but it didn’t really affect my playthrough or my ability to 100% the game.But ya, this is definitely in my top 3 Metroidvanias so far this year, along with Prince of Persia and Rebel Transmute. Absolute blast and I can’t imagine many people disliking this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great ~10 hour twin stick, metroidvania-zelda shooter. Extremely worth it, game is effectively underpriced for what you get. There really isn't much story, but it doesn't need it. The upgrades and exploration are paced excellently through the entire game, and it always felt like I had plenty of options on what I could be doing.Controls are extremely tight and NOTHING feels cheap. It is hard to say what exact style of area shooter it feels like, since it is a metroidvania and there is some progression and environmental impact on mobility. As a reference, early on in the game the controls and polish feel like Nuclear Throne. Later on, it feels much faster and movement floats more. This is actually quite nice, since the progression forces you to alter your playstyle as you improve - not just doing more damage, but requiring more from the player at the same time.High level of general polish, actually. No bugs or hiccups. Works great on Steam Deck. The "buggiest" thing that happened in my playthrough was... the camera wasn't exactly where I wanted it to be? One, single time? The devs should be extremely proud of both their UX and QA process.Other notes, this is definitely a twin stick shooter and not a bullet hell, it's much more approachable. Advancement is half metroidvania items, half experience/upgrade points. Map layout and dungeons are extremely 2D-Zelda inspired. There is a racing minigame for some kind of unlock, but I am terrible at racing and haven't done that.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine. It's bright and colourful, the feedback systems are neat, and the world is well realised with well-hidden secrets and well-placed challenges and treasures but it doesn't really push any boundaries and the gameplay, sadly, doesn't really evolve beyond how it starts. I wish the upgrades you got were more imaginative and transformed how you played the game beyond "point at the thing and shoot the thing until it dies".It's towards the end where my feelings slightly improve. The final dungeon is impressive in how it feels like an utterly warped and corrupted location that feels harmful to be inside. That, and the story about the Unchosen gets neat character tics towards the end. If the game leaned into its environmental storytelling and visual character personalities more, it would've elevated the whole experience. As it is, it's a decent eight hours to pass the time with if you have nothing better to do but, at the very least, I left feeling better than when I started.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is exactly as advertised. Zelda meets a Bullet Hell shooter (well more like Bullet Purgatory, as there are very few places where you can get insta-gibbed in one shot.) Overall, I can easily recommend this charming little hybrid, that only a tiny Indie team could release today.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute gem (pun intended). It's a quick and fun twin stick shooter and adventure game. The game is challenging, while having many options to mitigate said challenge. Although it doesn't do anything that hasn't been done before, it combines genres in a way that I've only seen once before, and executes it much better than the other, similar game (knight witch if anyone is wondering). The gameplay is sharp, responsive, and fast paced, although bullet hell veterans will likely find it easy, even on the hardest difficulty. The story is somewhat bland, but does not get in your way whatsoever (maybe like 2 minutes tops of cutscenes and dialogue). The adventure aspect is fun, with just enough map markers that you never feel completely lost (except for one area that doesn't give you a map until you've almost completed it) while still forcing you to figure most stuff out yourself. The playtime is a bit on the short side for the price (as of this review, I have 100%ed the game and gotten the true ending, playing on the hardest difficulty), but there is some postgame I have not yet played (it appears similar to the pantheons from Hollow Knight).Overall: 8/10(Note on playtime: I have about 2 hours on the demo)

name: Crossfire: Sierra Squad
detailed_description: Drop In and Feel the Impact of this Fierce Military Arcade Shooter in VR In Crossfire: Sierra Squad, you are the leader of an elite fireteam in the middle of a war. Be prepared for fierce resistance from all sides as you battle a variety of crafty enemies in a relentless search for the truth. 63 Campaign Missions Experience the high-quality characters, maps, and gameplay that Crossfire fans have become accustomed to, now in VR. Face fierce firefights between rival factions Black List and Global Risk in a variety of indoor and outdoor environments through 50 squad missions (single-player or 2 -player co-op), 13 campaign missions (single-player) and Horde Mode (up to 4-player co-op). 39 Different Weapons Master a large variety of weapons including pistols, rifles, throwable - and throwback-able - grenades, and sniper rifles with revolutionary scope mechanics that give you plenty of options to dispatch 17 types of enemies. 17 Types of Enemies Your adversaries are fearsome. In addition to soldiers with seemingly superhuman strength armed to the teeth with the finest weaponry available, you’ll face drones, bosses and vehicles brimming with mercs hell-bent on your destruction. Bring your A-game, because they’ll be bringing theirs. Play With Friends Clearing the enemies out won’t be easy. But if you need help, you can recruit a friend for co-op to conquer the squad missions or grab a few to take on the challenging Horde Mode as a fireteam of up to 4 players! Warning: Photosensitivity, Epilepsy and Seizure Warning A small percentage of individuals may experience epileptic seizures when exposed to certain light patterns or flashing lights. If you or anyone in your family have an epileptic condition, consult your physician before playing Sierra Squad. Also, if you or anyone around you experience dizziness, altered vision, migraine, loss of awareness, or seizure, immediately stop playing and consult your physician. Supported headsets: Valve Index, Oculus Rift S, Oculus Rift, Meta Quest Pro, Meta Quest 2, Meta Quest, HTC VIVE Pro, HTC VIVE Valve Index, Windows MR (Samsung Odyssey), PICO 4

name: METAL MAX Xeno Reborn
detailed_description: Humanity is on the brink of extinction and the last remaining survivors look to push back against the machines. Half a century ago of war against the mother computer NOA has reduced even Asia's largest metropolis, TOKIO, to rubble. Explore this desolate wasteland and battle your way through onslaughts of enemies. Salvage, modify and hit back using tanks, weaponry and faithful battle dog, Pochi, to reclaim a future for the human race! A Never-Ending Wasteland! - Set in a devastated world called Dystokio, Metal Max Xeno: Reborn is a nonlinear, open world, JRPG with real-time battle and vehicle combat elements. Take control of Talis and search for other survivors who wish to fight back against the machines of NOA. There are no limits to where you can go, no matter your progression in the game. Unite to Survive - The fate of the universe is in your hands! Hunt down your enemies with the helping hand from loved characters and your beloved battle dog, Pochi. Pochi can also level up and learn new skills and will join up as a fourth member. Help him earn skill points by feeding him at the base. And yes, you can also pet him. Hold Your Ground - Face NOA's forces with a party of three or four! Smash and blast across the vast desert and beyond to unite with remaining survivors and rise against the crazed machines in explosive missions. Strike your enemies from inside your tank, or disembark and explore dangerous dungeons on foot with your allies. Gear up for Victory! - Hone your skills to become more powerful than ever. Upgrade and learn skills of your choice from five general skill trees, which include “Drive,” “Repair,” “Medical,” “Militia,” and “Survive.” Light the Flame of the Hunter Spirit! Target your enemies using your tanks and weapons to unleash your powers to inflict massive damage. Salvage and Build! - Scavenge new tanks and customize them with fresh paint and the strongest firepower you can find. The tanks can range in design and scope. Freely customize your tanks and vehicles, swap out engines, upgrade the weaponry and bump them with special equipment. Enjoy endless possibilities with combinations. Please note: This game has been optimized for use with a controller

_childDocuments_.review: The incipit of MMXR is hardly novel: mankind created an AI to solve the crippling environmental issues of our planet. It worked quite too well, as it (rightly) concluded humans were the primary issue. In the consequent dystopian world you’ll wear the boots of Talis, one of the few surviving humans, hell-bent on destroying all the machines.Set in the aptly-named Dystokio, MMXR introduces you to a deserted world nearly-devoid of life, save for mutant abominations. The few remaining humans reside at Iron Base, Talis and crew’s main operations center. Between sandy expanses and crumbling bunkers, the post-apo feel is definitely there, but don’t expect an overly-realistic take on it. It’s sad that the visuals aren’t up-to-par with 2022 standards: at times it looks like a PS2 game!The side-characters aiding Talis’ endeavor will have distinct personalities, however don’t expect much elaboration on their backstories, nor great changes of character from them at any point - they’re sufficient sidekicks, nothing more. The lore itself is quite good, however the terrible translation often butchers it, rendering it less enjoyable.Is mainly performed using a variety of tanks and armored vehicles, however there are a good amount of sections where you’ll be forced to go on foot, as well. Dystokio is divided into five large sectors that you’ll progressively access as the story goes on - while the game promotes “non-linear open world”, this isn’t true since going too far will get you steamrolled by overpowered foes. Your minimap indicates all loot-crates, digging spots and respawning resource piles, so there won’t be any eye-squinting in the search for loot, which of course becomes better as areas become more advanced. Teleporting back to base and back again is something doable at any time, except during combat; a convenient feature that merges with Fast Travel Points, that act as ‘checkpoints’ of sorts across the five zones. Each square meter is littered with respawning enemies that will attack should you stay in their vision cone long enough - not immediately, so there’s some time to avoid trash encounters if you want.Is divided between ‘on foot’ and ‘on vehicles’, both of them using a turn-based mode with an optional auto-attack function that effectively makes it real-time until toggled. In the former, you’ll use Talis plus two sidekicks, and fight across tunnels, buildings, crevasses and whatever place is too narrow to reach by tank. Characters can be equipped with a variety of weapons, melee and ranged, with diverse firing patterns, ranges, AoEs and damage types. This becomes important later on, when many enemies will have specific resistances or weaknesses. Fights are your standard JRPG affair, with turns where you can use items, skills or simply attack. As XP is gathered (only for active party members), you’ll be able to spend Skill Points in one of the six specialization trees, each granting special passive and active abilities.Vehicle combat works in the same way, but with a twist: each tank has Armor instead of HP and won’t be destroyed when that reaches zero, instead Components (engine, cannons, etc.) will start taking damage, eventually disabling the tank completely and forcing the driver to fight on foot (usually a deadly proposition against vehicle-grade foes). Of course going back to base will repair everything, but also field fixing is possible, albeit in a slow way, since each item has a lengthy usage animation. Tanks will progressively become unrealistic, hulking monstrosities with five cannons, somehow operated by a single crewman; up to three can be brought with you on any sortie. Fighting on paper is complex, with many status effects, skills, passives and damage types - while these factors have to be accounted in the harder fights, most of the time simply building your tank platoon properly and setting auto-attack on will clear most scuffles without a hitch.Iron Base allows you to craft, improve and purchase a vast array of components and weapons for your crew and vehicles. Better engines will increase your tanks’ maximum weight limit, allowing them to carry heavier, better weaponry and armor without incurring in the heavy HP maluses derived from overweight. There’s no equipment limit, money does all the talking in MMXR and acts sort of like a ‘second XP’: get rich enough via selling, missions and enemy killing (bounties especially), and you’ll quickly get your hands on powerful gear. Individual weapons can as well be modified into 2.0 and 3.0 variants with the right materials, lightened or hardened to be more resilient in exchange for more weight cost, the latter also goes for vehicles. Chips unlock powerful abilities, like attacking with all cannons at the same time instead of one at a time, or perform other special moves, but they’re expensive and need to be installed with a specific strategy in mind, to obtain the best synergy, stack effects.

_childDocuments_.review: The description of Reborn can be summed up pretty succinctly in that it amounts to an extremely streamlined version of the console incarnation that it was wrenched out of. There is such a thing as trimming fat, but Reborn flays the meat right off the bones of the game, reducing content, complexity, challenge and even quality of life features on every front and simplifying the game to such an extent that I was able to "clear" it in just 9 hours with little to no significant thought or effort on my own part.My understanding is that this was done in, what I have to say, was a very misguided attempt to bring the game closer to its more "free form" cousins in the main series of numbered titles, but it simply does not have the world design to actually support this format whatsoever as it has virtually no points of interest or real exploratory potential, even severely cutting down on the number of indoor/on-foot environments present compared to the original game.Quite frankly, the only thing Reborn has going for it is bringing back series staple Pochi and making Po-M available as a playable character with the additional caveat of its general running performance due to some hiccups in the original version of Xeno on consoles, which suffered from inconsistent framerates even on the PS4. However, this is a caveat precisely because if you have a PS4 Pro or a PS5, these issues vanish.At this point, Metal Max Xeno can probably be had digitally on the Playstation Store for half the cost or less of Reborn (and given the package on offer here, 50 dollars as the price of admission is lunacy) and it is definitively a better game with a higher standard of quality, despite its rough reception among critics. I never encountered a bug or a translation error (or outright missing translation) my entire time playing it while I came across more than a dozen oddities/bugs (including the final boss suffering from repeated brain death allowing an effortless slaughter) and quite a lot of translation issues in Reborn.In short, Metal Max Xeno Reborn simply hasn't got a leg to stand on and its treads are all busted. Apply yourselves, guys. You can do far better than this and you have before.

_childDocuments_.review: Before we begin: A Note. The reason I officially rated this as 'Not Recommended' is because personally, I read negative reviews more than positive. Negative reviews give me a better idea of the cons of the game. Officially, I would rate this as 'Depending', and you'll see why as you read.I have to break this review down into two categories, for both my own sanity, and for fairness to the game. The first section will be looking at Xeno Reborn in a vacuum, judging the game on how it is when you only look at it. The second will be when compared to the very game it was spawned from, Metal Max Xeno. I do this because I am torn after playing Xeno, and I feel this is the only way to be fair.Metal Max Xeno Reborn; in Isolation:When studied by itself and without the added advantage of knowledge of previous entries in the series and without comparing it to previous titles, Metal Max Xeno Reborn is a solid game. The combat is a unique take on the turn-based combat of traditional RPGs allowing both freedom to build as you wish, as well as the ability to clean-sweep your foes if you're built properly. The ability to take the first shot, to get the drop on your enemies trivializes a lot of the combat in the game, but the combat that it doesn't outright trivialize (SoNs and Wanted Targets, for example) instead give you a much-needed edge in combat.The only real complain I have with the controls is how squirrely some of the tanks can be. Cresting a dune can cause you to spin out and re-orient yourself, which is only a real problem if you're attempting to flee combat. Early game is a bit tricky... you feel far too squishy than you think you should and the enemies feel far too durable. Hell, up until the third area of the game, avoidance is your best strategy.The plot is a bit... oh-ho ho ho... we'll get to you. But looking at it in isolation, Reborn's plot is a bit rushed, threadbare and it skips over far too many details for my liking... honestly, the plot is Reborn's weakest link.And now... the section I dread.Metal Max Xeno Reborn vs. Metal Max Xeno:I bought a playstation and a copy of the game, because I loved Reborn. I did. I had heard that if you liked Reborn, you'll love the original. I'm going to say this right now: If you like Metal Max Xeno Reborn and haven't played the original Xeno... don't. Do not play Metal Max Xeno if you enjoy Reborn... you will regret the decision. Why? Is it because the original one is so terrible? The... opposite, actually. Metal Max Xeno is leagues and bounds superior to Reborn, and as I play through the original, I feel my love for Reborn fading. There are no cutscenes in Reborn. No opening cutscenes, no ending cutscenes, no interim cutsenes. The entire beginning of the game, Talis' entire drive for doing what he does is IGNORED in Reborn. They drop you in, say 'have fun!' and let you struggle.Yes, tank modification is dumbed down in Reborn. Dumbed down, not 'simplified', but dumbed down. Aspects of the plot are wholly changed to speed things along. Honestly? Reborn feels like an Abridged version... and not a particularly good one, either. I'm eight hours into Xeno, and I haven't even seen Catastropus yet... and yet in Reborn, he's there from minute one. Enemies have personality in the original, the characters in Iron Base and your party are so much more vibrant... Why? Why did they feel the need to butcher the game?Censorship. It boils down to censorship. The topic of procreation is brought up a bit in the original, and all of that is gone in Reborn. Why? These people legitimately feel like they're the last people on earth! They're going to want to save their damn species, for once in my life, I found a game where the inclusion of sexual innuendo and sex talk MAKES SENSE.Do I recommend? If you've never played the original, yes. If you never plan on playing the original, GOD yes. Reborn is ... okay... for what it is. If you just wanna shoot machines in a tank like I did when I bought it, go the hell ahead and get it, you will love it! If you're a returning veteran and have played Metal Max Xeno... stay far away from it as you can. Please. You won't enjoy it... and that hurts to say.EDIT: I want to say that there is a lot Reborn did right. The change of traditional turn-based RPG combat to the psuedo real-time turn based did a lot for the series. Made combat easier when you know what you're doing and you're prepared, but more punishing if you're unprepared. The movement controls are far cleaner and more 'immersive' than in the original. But having said that, there's a lot it did wrong.♥♥♥♥ the Big Atrium.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I thought that MMXR was an action RPG game, like Divinity II. But I was wrong. In fact, this is a completely turn-based RPG game. If you find or encounter a monster, you can't fire at it directly. Instead, you must open a menu, select attack command from menu, then select a weapon and target. After these steps, you can begin a turn-based battle.Unlike other games from Metal Max series, player will not act as a weak hero who started from remote village with nothing. You can find a powerful tank and a huge support base at the first area. The base provides free re-supply and repair, shopping function, weapon and vehicle modification services. You can even manufacture some special weapons by using a lot of parts from monsters. If you have enough money, then you will get many ultimate weapons and equipment in the base store.Some of old players may dislike these designs. Because they want to experience a journey of growth. In the classic Metal Max games, the hero can't be got everything from the start. All best weapons, equipment and modification services should be found in the final city. I understand this mentality, but MMXR represents a new direction of Metal Max series. I'm sure that new players will enjoy it if they can master game mechanics.However, a lot of new players give this game a negative review just because they can't get their DLC. I always not buy any DLCs until I determined there were no bugs in them. So I don't have this problem.I must to say, the basic game is very good. Don't let yourself be fooled by those reviews with full of prejudice. Although there are some flaws in the current game, but it has more advantages.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fellow Metal Max simp, let me say first that each and every newer Metal Max game I play has found some way to leave me disappointed. Metal Max 1/Returns is the OG experience for Metal Max, you can't beat the feel of inventory management and terror of on-foot combat always being much riskier than in the safety of a tank. Metal Max 2 is also good, you can tell it was invented by the same genius mind that came up with the first game. Metal Saga just falls through completely on the fun factor by encouraging you to do one simple thing: buy a new engine in the next area so all challenge in the previous area is completely obsoleted, use previous area to fully level up, rinse, repeat. Metal Max 3 tries to go back to the roots but it's too eclectic and shell crafting is a major pain in the ass. This game, Xeno Reborn? It's hilariously broken to the point of if you have any knowledge of good strategies from previous games applying them here will see you absolutely murdering the last boss halfway through the game just by meeting him.Why is it broken? Two reasons. The first is that Machine Gun Rush is exploitable. If you have a Chaingun that shoots 12 times equipped in the first slot, all of the other guns shoot 12 times regardless of their actual attack pattern, so load up those extra Buster Flutes to watch the magic at work. The second is that Cannon Tube is completely OP. It's an aux gun so it's infinite use, it does in the realm of 1000 damage or more, and it always crits (er sorry, if I'm using this game's language it always makes affinity shots) which means it just about completely ignores defense. Cannon Tube wrecks anything at a 100 meter radius by itself, which includes aerial units. Combining these two facts means you do upwards of 8000 unblockable damage per turn just by using the Cannon Tube, and it only gets more broken when upgraded. Catastropus effectively got ♥♥♥♥ upon by a Metro Bus. So much for humanity's extinction. (Okay, so Cannon Rush helped too, but that's not as OP. Not without quite a bit more setup.)That said, there is way more to do in the game besides kill Catastropus for a fat bounty. Killing Catastropus unlocks a new difficulty every time he is killed on the newest available difficulty. Losing to Catastropus unlocks special monsters that upgrade the main character's special skill tree, which is never actually mentioned until you do but set up to be helpful to people who don't have enough common sense to know how to rush the last boss. Newer difficulties unlock new items to find, acquire, equip. There's a lot of world to explore and gather stuff in and conquer just by riding around in your tanks blasting away. And riding around in your tanks blasting away is, above all else, just plain fun. Maybe a bit cheap considering you can deal with a lot of issues just by Cannon Tubing things from afar, but if you're not careful other nearby enemies will join in, causing just the right amount of chaos for your party that later Metal Max games are known for. I think they absolutely nailed that part of the fun down. And on foot combat is spectacularly more balanced and interesting, and there are a number of on foot dungeons to try your hand at. Not scary like in previous games, but you are not overpowered and the right enemy can and will hand your ass back to you.The only really annoying thing this otherwise casual game has to offer is that items are used one at a time, and invoking them from inside of a tank can cause lengthy animations to play considering the character has to get out of the tank, use the item, then get back in. Recommend you disembark (alight?) before you use items repeatedly, which is still kind of annoying because you need to navigate the same menu every time to get back to the item you want to use. On top of that the localization is literal in most parts, lazy in others. There are rats in a parking garage whose description is a Japanese text dump. You get the impression from seeing some of these things that the budget ran out during late late development.Overall, I definitely believe it was worth my money. I'm just reviewing it now because I technically beat the game, but I totally expect to go back and find all of its little secrets. The achievements are mostly simply gained just by playing the game, aside from one or two hardcore accomplishments. If you like tanks, tank RPGs, and just plain fun, give this a try. It is a good look for the series, it just sorely needs a little more love and a counter for how much time you spend customizing your tanks at home base.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is the first negative review ive ever had to leave.  Let me preface it by stating, I love metal max and metal saga.  I have played every entry in the franchise.  I have imported where needed, and downloaded roms (legaly) with translation patches. I put well over 200 hours into metal saga on the PS2 and bought the first metal max xeno on day 1 and while it wasnt stellar, it was a decent approach to the series.THIS IS NOT THATThis version of metal max xeno is a travesty that should have never been made, and it upsets me to say that because i was very much looking forward to it, even now i watch the trailer as im typing this and part of me want to.. maaaaybe give it another go, such is my love for the franchise, but this pile of trash is broken in so many frustrating ways that I think even IF I ever try it again it will be at a massively reduced price.First off, the controls default to the Japanese playstyle of OX instead of the American playstyle of XO and there is no way to change them until you are actually in the game.  That is a mild annoyance by itself, what makes it so much worse is that even when you do change the control settings to the XO American playstyle it only changes the button requirements for SOME things, not all, menus still require the OX input style very confusing.  Secondly new characters and vehicles have to be named, great nothing new or bad there, except that even though the steam page states this game REQUIRES a controller to play, and you actually DO HAVE to use one, there is not softkeyboard for inputs, so you, like me, are playing on a TV and ur computer is at the other end of the room, you now have to get up and go type in the names because even though they game was built solely for controllers, a softkeyboard was too much work.Thirdly weird bugs in the name inputs. The default name of the first vehicle you get is something like Type10 Mk2.0 or somthing like that, the problem is you cant use the default, if you try it tells you "FORBIDDEN INPUT", any variation of that does the same thing, my guess is that they, for some ungodly reason, decided that numbers were not a valid input for vehicle names, as such any name with a numeric requires full retyping, queue having to go back to the keyboard because of lack of softkeyboard options (See complaint 2)Fourth, vehicle combat is actually annoying not fun... and thats sad.  So ground combat is odd because of the weird controls, but doable and i feel totally learnable.  Vehicle combat functions much the same way EXCEPT for a few key differences, for some reason the developers felt that when you choose to attack in a vehicle they need to transition to a load screen where you actually aim the vehicle weapon/turret.  You essentially just line up the reticle on the turret with a reticle that is superimposed on the enemy and click attack, there is no real functional reason for this other than maybe its supposed to look cool?, It actually has the opposite effect because once you click on it you then have to blink transition back out of aiming mode back to the vehicle combat view to watch the attack take place.  All told it only takes a second or 2, but it is jarring and disorienting enough to be very frustrating, particularly since there is no functional, actual, or necessary reason for it to be like this.Fifth, this is one i knew going in, but wanted to support the franchise anyway because i was very bummed to see the Metal Max Wild West got canceled but am still looking forward to Metal Saga Project Wolf, crappy action based combat replaced turn based.  To the developers... Why for the love of all that is holy, unholy, and unknown would you take a franchise thats bread and butter for almost 3 decades has been turnbased combat and decide to get rid of it? What this is IS NOT what fans want, and your reviews support that.  Honestly if Metal max wild west was gonna be more of this then im happy it was canceled, and if this is what Kadokawa Games has in store for Metal Max Project Wolf, then please save us the players alot of frustration and yourself the developer alot of embarrassment and just cancel it now and let the franchise die.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Metal Max Xeno Reborn with some hesitation, given the low Metascore and the negative reviews... But I'm actually really happy I've played it! And that's because this game is really unique, and it feels like a lot of passion was put into its creation. Two of the highlights of the game are the cool post-apocalyptic atmosphere (depressing but with a touch of hope) and the beautiful soundtrack by Satoshi Kadokura (with some really fascinating electronic pieces). Another really exciting aspect of the game are the tanks: finding tanks, collecting/building/fitting tank parts, driving the tanks around and fighting the enemies with them is really galvanising!Unfortunately, the game doesn't have a strong plot, and the dialogues are really brief and few. Because of this, I felt quite indifferent to the various objectives, and found the characters rather shallow. These limitations are also due to a lot of stuff being removed from the original version of this game (called Metal Max Xeno) - which I recommend giving a look at, on some YouTube videos (e.g. compare the Reborn intro with the original: Another issue is the uneven difficulty of the game: sometimes you destroy some enemies with one shot, and other times you get destroyed with one hit - this makes some parts very trial-and-error. Also, during the first playthrough, you have to avoid the very powerful Wanted Enemies, making a big part of the exploration just an escape. The game also doesn't make clear what you can do to become stronger, e.g. how to best customise your tanks or how to spend the characters' ability points. For this reason, I recommend reading this general guide before playing the game, as I found it suuuper useful: If you're a fan of JRPGs like me, and you care about a game atmosphere, originality and 'heart' more than graphics and level of polish, I really recommend this game, especially on discount!

_childDocuments_.review: -I have only ever played Returns, Reloaded, and 3Let's get the bad stuff out of the way first: no 1440p. Sucks, I half expect it from Japanese ports, but there it is. You need a controller. I use kb/m and controller equally so this doesn't bother me, but I know some people explode in violent rage if you even suggest they plug a controller into their PC (imagine not taking advantage of the PC having every peripheral you could dream of at your finger tips..). I've seen 1 or 2 monster flavor texts that are still in Japanese. Whatever.Game runs well, no dips bloops, crashes, or bops. Game looks like a Vita game but again, I'm not one to care. This game is not going to work out your 3080ti.  I see a lot of reviews crying about censorship and what have you, but the fact of the matter is that the original Xeno was not a very well received game. Fans of Metal Max were extremely unhappy with Xeno when it first came out, and Reborn is an attempt to address those things and bring the game closer to the older titles. The game we got is exactly the same as the Reborn the Japanese received. If you consider 'censorship' to be the owner of an IP attempting to make changes to a title to directly address fan backlash, then I guess this game IS censored and you can safely move on to something else (and for the record, I don't know if they succeeded). For everyone else though, there's a solid quasi-open world JRPG here for you. The game has received many changes and tweaks in gameplay from regular Xeno in return for the removal of others.  (you'll have to use Google Translate, but the Metal Max Wiki describes the changes under 'Other'). So far, it feels like a Metal Max game. Even more light on the story than the early games/remakes, you're just thrust into things with nary a spare word or idea why you're there, and off you go. It actually feels really abrupt compared to say, MM2R and I think they may have cut a little too much out. You can certainly tell things were cut or left out, and what little story there is left doesn't make much sense which is a BIG downgrade to older MM titles.  They too don't have much of a story, but they DID have one, and it wasn't so disjointed and random at times. So don't expect any kind of quality narrative really; you're there to survive, shoot guns, drive tanks,  kill bounties, and listen to the rocking song in the bar. That is your reason for living. That being said, it feels like Metal Max, looks like Metal Max, and while not as good 10 hours in as I found Returns and Reloaded, I am still having a good time and would recommend the game to anyone who liked them.  If you haven't played them, go find them! There are English patches for the three and they are completely worth the average JRPG fan's time. This game might be a good entry point for a new player as it has more modern conveniences like auto battle and the DOG System (teleport back to town) available right away. Edit: I have since finished the game. It is MUCH MUCH shorter than the other Metal Max games, and is basically a diet version of them. The game is solid, but if Metal Max R and 2R are 9/10s, this is a 6/10. Differences from the main series: You can buy lots of stuff from the vending machine at once now instead of one by one like MMR and MM2R which is the best change. Also, scrap no longer is loaded on your tank. Hell yes. Overall tank upgrading is a lot simpler, but there's some good QoL. Overall the upgrade and weapon systems you know are here, but perhaps not quite as richly as you'd like. It is kinda a bummer that tank patterns are no longer a thing and you just go buy whatever chip you want, but on the other side of the coin, it means all differences between the vehicles boils down to what you like to look at more or less. No more using a Wild Bus because it's awesome but feeling bad because it's just not as good as other vehicles.

_childDocuments_.review: The long-running post-apocalyptic RPG series finally makes an appearance on PC and unfortunately, it isn’t looking too good.Even speaking as a fan of turn-based strategy games - the combat here is just outright painful. It is far too slow, far too cumbersome, and has too many menus for its own good. Here you have a game where you’re rolling around in a tank and have to pause every single time you want to attack, select the weapon to attack with, slowly line up your aim, and then shoot it off only to repeat this whole process for each and every enemy in the area.It becomes this process of move, pause, menu, shoot, move, pause, menu shoot - it doesn’t flow well and is really just an odd fit for a game like this. The combat is far too simplistic to warrant needing the extra depth offered by a turn-based system, so I have to wonder what the goal was here. Because even when you do get in an extended fight, it really just boils down to sitting there and waiting until you’re able to shoot again. There is an auto-shoot function, but it can only be toggled once you are actually in combat, so it’s effectively useless because most of the time you’re just taking out enemies one by one or in small groups where usually one or two shots finishes the job. Really, the most depth you’ll get is from character skills and tank customization which allows you to equip weapons of different categories and elemental types, but the end result hardly feels any different.The normal enemies take like one shot to kill, but then bosses are these massive sponges that can easily two-shot you and have so much health that I’m hardly even sure if I am damaging them. A lot of the time, I would simply roll past them and move on to the next area where enemies became manageable again.To take down bosses, you got to do a good bit of grinding, both for XP and for materials to upgrade your stuff and honestly, the combat is so barebones and boring that the idea of doing that just is not appealing. I understand this is not a AAA title, but it’s also being sold for $40 and looks like a mobile game, with low-res textures across the board and the most static of environments. Yeah, it’s supposed to be some post-apocalyptic setting, but I personally don’t think that should excuse such lazy level design - it’s like something we would get from a Compile Heart game, complete with invisible walls everywhere.The story is there, but not a super big thing - and it is honestly better off this way because what is there may be even more barebones than the gameplay. Writing this review, I cannot name any character off the top of my head that isn’t the protagonist that I myself named - they are just that forgettable and hardly receive the development needed to make the story in any way interesting.I will give PQube - the publisher - some credit, it is better than some of their other PC ports, but still below satisfactory. For one, the keyboard and mouse controls. The Steam store page actually lists the game as having none, but keyboard controls do exist (and that’s just keyboard, no mouse). None of the buttons can be rebound though, so you’re stuck holding shift and the arrow keys to rotate the camera - so don’t even think of picking this one up if you don’t have a controller.There are also only three graphical settings: brightness, resolution choice between 720p/1080p, and fullscreen/window toggle. That’s it - it is the most barebones of ports and unfortunately comes with some technical issues on top of that. During my first two hours with the game, I had it freeze completely on me on two separate occasions. I didn’t have the issue past that two hour mark, but it’s worth mentioning regardless.A disappointing first showing for the series on PC, METAL MAX Xeno Reborn brings some good ideas to the table, but is bogged down by its numerous bizarre design choices and technical issues. The gameplay is slow and monotonous, the level design and graphics are mobile-game level, and the game freezing and lack of proper controls are not a good look either. It’s just a low effort port all around and unfortunate to see as a series I was excited to check out for the first time.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a review, this is a first-impressions write-up of the first 2.4 hours of the game.I've only played a little bit of the game. There are definitely issues. The game has all sorts of problems from gameplay to especially the PC port. It's not unplayable which is good enough for me (60fps, controller support works) but it isn't good. No keyboard prompts but you can use it, although I wouldn't recommend it since you don't have any prompts and mouse doesn't work at all (at least they were nice enough to mention that in big orange text on the store page though, so that's fair enough), barebones video options menu (1280x720 or 1920x1080p, fullscreen or borderless + brightness settings, that's it), there's an issue with monitor refresh rates. Despite the game being locked to 60fps, if my monitor is running at 144hz it looks like my character has an afterimage while running around, it looks super jittery. Not great. There's no way to change the gamepad bindings either. You're stuck with the default controls and prompts.The gameplay has its own problems. I wandered around for a bit wondering what exactly I was supposed to do. Through trial and error I explored and figured out everything I needed to know, mostly, only to find the game's main hub area and then get bombarded with tutorials regarding things I already knew about for over an hour (still going). Sometimes the tutorial would stop me dead while I cycled through its text boxes while enemies were about to attack me. There are numerous instances of bad design in this title and I can see why critics didn't shine to well to the non-reborn version which is apparently a lot worse if reviews are anything to go by. The combat and menus are a bit clunky, the map layout is absolutely stupid - why can't I see the overworld map AND the objective I'm trying to find on that same map? Why can I only see the objective marker on the freaking mini map where it's harder to figure out where it is + where I am???!?! The combat is initiated from the overworld but plays out in the overworld rather than being pulled to a different, isolated battlefield like other turn-based JRPGs. but aside from avoiding other wandering mobs, there really isn't anything added to the combat system by doing this. You can drive your tank or character around a group of enemies and even retreat but the combat isn't as good as it looks. You should be able to target weak points on larger enemies when you're in the tank and you moving around in a fight, by extension, your tank should have vulnerable spots for a risk vs reward playstayle where a frontal attack is the safest (that's where most tanks have all their armor, the front) but by trying to drive around the enemy to hit them in a theoretical weak point, your weak point would also in turn be exposed by that action. There's a lot of potential here and its a shame it just feels wasted at times....But... man it's nice to play something that's actually kinda different. I don't play JRPGs almost at all because they are so infuriating at times. I see people mentioning problems this game has slow combat or poor ui and yeah its a bit slow but... have you played Final Fantasy 7? That game runs at 24 frames per second, has slow battles with lengthy animations and yet that game is never criticized by anyone in the press, it's considered by everyone to be the greatest game of all time somehow. How many JRPGs did you play where the first 4-6 hours are nothing but cutscenes and tutorials? "it gets good 30 hours in bro" is a common phrase you hear, and sometimes it's true. But why can't a game give you the reigns earlier on and leave you to your own devices for a bit? At least this game didn't waste my time with endless menus and garbage, it was nice to be on my own for the first hour or so of the game without having to deal with that crap. And the combat here is fun enough. It's quick and fast. It's not great but the sound design and soundtrack help hold it together, not to mention the unique combat system of utilizing a freaking tank. It's fun to upgrade it and try out different weapons. It's fun to find new enemy types and blast through them. It's fun to level up while doing all of this and getting rewarded a little bit for everything you do thanks to the games main quest and micro quest system. And even though the tutorial bits are annoying, I was shocked at first that a JRPG would let me wander around freely with almost no instructions or directions. It was absolutely liberating and I wanted to stick with the game to see where it went, I still want to see where it goes.I think that's the main appeal I found. Good sound design, good music, and the exploration aspect of driving around and leveling up and finding new gear to equip you, your party and your tank with. They made the driving surprisingly enjoyable. I hate games that label themselves as "chill games" because they're so dull and unappealing to me but this one has my attention. It's got A TON of problems but it is something I think I can sink some more hours into when I have the time.I'd say if you're looking for something a bit more cozy but still engaging, this game is worth your time for a JRPG if you're okay with the main gameplay loop - that being driving around and doing basic quests and grinding. Sounds boring if you've played a lot of bad JRPGs but I enjoyed this one.. Maybe not at 40 bucks though, I do agree that it's pretty high-priced for what it is. But it still means I recommend the game (at least if it's on sale). Again, I've barely scratched the surface so maybe the game turns into complete crap later but I started having fun 30 minutes into the game and for a JRPG that is a rarity.If you liked this write-up, please consider checking out our curator page: Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: METAL MAX Xeno is a Hunting Rpg based around tank combat fighting strange Bio-Machine Monsters. The game only has one requirement to beat it: DEFEAT THE ULTIMATE HUMANITY DESTROYING WEAPON: CATASTROPUS.The Game itself is very Ps2 era Japanse game with a turn based combat system. It also has some translations problems and all voiced dialog is in Japanese.The Map is built like a race-track and consists of about 10-11 areas total.Your main gameplay will be trying to push deeper into the world to get better gear/tanks and fighting the many bounty/bosses. Alot of the original game has been cut and edited for the remake, they've removed several quests and the game itself has alot of glitches/edits that change the core gameplay. Its fun to play, but once you beat the game once you'll quickly start to see the cracks and how empty it is of gameplay.A 4/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a little rough, and obviously didn't the the attention it needed as a port to PC, but if you don't mind some odd translations, no keyboard/mouse rebindable keys (there are keys that work but no menu to rebind them), limited display options, and not super helpful tutorials (I know this is a big ask) it's a ton of fun. The series has never been one to be super deep or have a lot of plot, and metal max xeno reborn is very loyal in that fact. the entire basis of the game boils down to, you are a monster hunter go kill monsters, and boy does this game have a ton of monsters for you to kill. I highly recommend to gamers that are a little more willing to deal with more scuffed or less than polished games

_childDocuments_.review: Bloody fun time! It's a whole different experience to the original Metal Max Xeno from several years back, it's neither better nor worse, just... different. I enjoyed the combat quite a lot and the fact your gear construction options are now tied to exploration and item drops, rather than tech levels and character experience, actually makes the game feel whole lot more enjoyable and faster paced.Music was fine, serviceable, nothing really standing out, and the visuals were okay. Combat and crafting new gear is the true gameplay loop, along with tackling "WANTED" bounty monsters. Very fun game all in all, but I'm not playing through it all over again three times just to unlock the extra difficulty levels and more WANTED enemies. Once is enough :D

_childDocuments_.review:
Humanity is on the brink of extinction and the last remaining survivors look to push back against the machines.

Half a century ago of war against the mother computer NOA has reduced even Asia's largest metropolis, TOKIO, to rubble.

Explore this desolate wasteland and battle your way through onslaughts of enemies. Salvage, modify and hit back using tanks, weaponry and faithful battle dog, Pochi, to reclaim a future for the human race!

Set in a devastated world called Dystokio, Metal Max Xeno: Reborn is a nonlinear, open world, JRPG with real-time battle and vehicle combat elements. Take control of Talis and search for other survivors who wish to fight back against the machines of NOA. There are no limits to where you can go, no matter your progression in the game.
